It's definitely convenient when traveling to Busan or on a business trip to the provinces below. However, I don't know if the special room is worth the price. They provide spacious, simple cookies and an eye patch, but the regular room itself is too narrow to begin with, so there is no advantage to using the special room.

We took the KTX from Seoul to Pusan (Busan).  Our hosts paid for our tickets and we went 1st Class.  It was very spacious and comfortable.  There are great views of the Korean countryside, which is very pleasant, especially the rice paddy fields.  The train is quiet and you don't realise how fast you are going until you pass a train coming in the opposite direction.  With both trains travelling at close to 300 km/hr, a 200-metre long train flashes by in less than 1 second.

This is an express train between Seoul Station (B2) and Incheon Airport. Although it is only available on a limited number of airlines such as Korean Air and Asiana Airlines, you can complete the check-in procedure at the airport at the counter at Seoul Station. You can drop off your luggage and pick up your flight ticket here. If you already had a ticket to Incheon Airport, all you had to do was show your receipt and pay the difference. (If you buy from a ticket vending machine, we recommend that you get a receipt.) Once you arrive at the airport, you can head straight to customs. The fare was 8,000 won. The advantage was that I could skip the check-in line after arriving at the airport.

Book online and ride. I was told to print out my ticket and bring it with me, so I did so, but they didn't ask me to show it to them or read the code, so in conclusion, there was no need to print it out. It seemed like all the locals were making reservations through the app. The seats in newer cars can be rotated, so basically everyone can sit facing the direction of travel. The inside of the car is clean and comfortable, including the toilet. The price is also incredibly low considering the Japanese Shinkansen.

KTX in Korea is fast and convenient~ It is also very convenient to travel back and forth to Busan in one day with PASS available to foreigners~ Especially now that PASS is open, you can also book flights online~ It is more friendly and convenient for tourists traveling to Korea!
I enjoyed using the KTX to go from Seoul to Daegu.  It was a quick 2-hour ride in a clean and peaceful train car.  Will do every chance.

If you are going to Busan, do take this train which takes 2 hours & 40 minutes. I find that the flexi 2 day pass is useful & cheaper compared to purchase single trip. However, this is not a bullet train so it actually quite slow as compared to shinkansen.

I had taken the KORAIL Pass for tourists for 3 days as I on the first day itself I was travelling from Seoul to Gyeongju, next day from Gyenongju to Busan and then to Seoul. If you don't have KORAIL Pass, you can purchase the tickets. It is faster and the seats are comfortable.

I often use the Busan-Daegu section. It’s comfortable, fast, and I’m satisfied. I prefer KTX because it is easier to access the city center than by plane. I recommend KTX Sancheon more because the train space is wider and cleaner.
Comfortable, but old composition. The speed in some areas reaches 320 km/h. I advise you to take a ride.

The KTX is the best way to travel from Seoul to Busan. The fast speed train only takes 2.5 hours for the 330 km. The seats are not luxurious but comfortable enough. The train makes the most sense for this distance.
Traveling with this train is really fun. It is very comfortable and there is enough space. You are also offered a power socket and free WiFi. A good alternative to flying.

Even if you say you know about it, people who don't know about it probably don't know about Korea's proud high-speed railway (KTX). The vehicle looks exactly like the French TVG, and was the result of a competition between Japan and France for the order, with France winning. This time, I bought a ticket at Seoul Station from Seoul to Busan, but even though I wrote ``Special Room'' on the paper, it turned out to be ``General Seats, 2+2 across,'' so the fare was 6,000 yen per person, which was cheap. It was a two-and-a-half hour ride, stopping at five stations along the way. There are various types of trains running at different times, some early and some late. There are no checks at the KTX ticket gates at Seoul Station, and passengers ride on their own (this is called responsible boarding). I have a feeling that I will use it again next time, praying that there will be no accidents like the one in Taiwan.
I tend to use Seoul Station KTX often. Please note that it takes a while to get off at the center lane of the bus stop and get to the platform to board the train.
Comfortable.  Clean.  On time.  Limited staff.  Easy to use. Efficient.I would use the train system again.  Overall a good experience.  We traveled from Busan to Seoul with no issues.
Train on time slightly expensive, Seating arrangement is not realy spacious. Overall the distance is not far so its ok.

I booked the KTX first class from Busan to Seoul. You go to the platform 15-20 mins before departure. Basically no security checks whatsoever. When you book online, the tickets are immediately issued and you would have to print out a physical copy and save it as a softcopy for backup as they do not email a copy to you. There is no need to exchange the printout again at the station for another ticket. The pros are the trains leave on time and the first class has enough leg room, some cookies and water is provided. There are areas to store limited large baggages on either side of the car and smaller ones can go on top of the cabin seats. This is run like a lean machine, very few employees on board. There is free wifi but signals can be intermittent. Ride is smooth. The pleasant experience is somewhat marred by the behavior of some of the passengers. There are a few who will target foreigners and pressure them into thinking they have the wrong seats and to give it up. Finding your correct seat is idiot proof so there is no way one can sit in the wrong place unless it is deliberate.  Everything from the Train, Car and seat Number is stated clearly on the ticket so stand your ground if this happens even when they start to talk loudly or argue to embarrass you. I suspect many do not adhere to their asdigned seats or pay extra for a higher class seat and move around the train hoping they can get away with it. Other than this, it is a fast and pleasant way to get around major cities in Korea. I would give this 4.5 stars as a train service and 3 stars because of some minority passengers.

I use the KTX for business trips.  The trains are punctual.  Once in the train, the car seats are comfortable.  Would be great if they had charging stations.  Otherwise, the KTX is a great comfortable ride when traveling in Korea city to city.

The most convenient thing about ktx is that you don’t need to check in. You just need to remember your seat after buying the ticket. And getting on the train from the station is not like domestic high-speed rail stations, which sometimes take more than ten minutes to get there, which saves time.

I travelled on KTX from Busan to Seoul. The train departed on time and I was sitting in economy class which was comfort, smooth and quite nice. However, the train made 5-6 stops before approaching to its final destination at Seoul station. Hence, it arrived Seoul 32 minutes later than estimated.

I used A’REX from Incheon Airport to Seoul Station, and KTX from Seoul Station to Busan Station. When it comes to comfort, including facilities, KTX definitely wins. A’REX has a small number of buses, and there are no outlets inside the car. I think the cabin class was also 1 cabin. The seats were in a 2:2 arrangement. KTX was very comfortable in comparison. Maybe it was because I was flying first class, but compared to the 2:2 ratio of regular seats, the 1:2 ratio makes it very comfortable. We also provide unlimited water bottles and snacks. There were two types of sweets, and both were delicious. There is also an electrical outlet. It also supports USB, so you can use the internet without worrying about batteries while on the move. I will repeat first class if I have the opportunity to fly KTX again.
I took the KTX from Seoul to the Olympic village and again it was fast and efficient;  it will get you anywhere you need to go in Korea.

Definitely the way to go - buy tickets in advance online. Pros:- FAST (300kph) modern & comfortable trip. - Recommend 1st Class - roomy seats- GREAT scenery!!!- Both stations easy to maneuverCons:- NO WiFi - wasn’t working!!- No food - bring your own snacks, food & beer.

The train is comfortable and clean. A steward periodically walks by with a cart of snacks and drinks and offers to buy them for money. The carriage has a shelf under the ceiling for things, a folding table in the front seat, and a footrest at the bottom of the seat. In the vestibule of the car there is a small compartment for large things (such as suitcases and bags), and a toilet. The board shows the speed of the train and writes the name of the station where the train will have its next stop. Train tickets can be bought online or at the station ticket office.
We have used the high-speed train to go from Seoul to Busan and to Yeosu. Everything perfect. Fast, punctual, organized, quiet, competitively priced, comfortable and with free Wi-Fi.
Took the KTX from Seoul and Busan. Found it comfortable and it was a neat way to see South Korea. Didn't have much issue with luggage. Do recommend trying if traveling long distances.

I used it from Busan to Seoul. I made a reservation and purchased the ticket online, but when I got on the bus at Busan Station, I was confused because there was no ticket to open. I looked into it later and found out that KTX doesn't open tickets, and there's no ticket inspection unless you're sitting outside the designated area. This is convenient. The ride comfort was not as good as the Japanese Shinkansen, but the shaking didn't bother me too much. The inside of the car was also nice and clean. However, the seats are fixed across the middle of the vehicle, facing forward and backward in the direction of travel, so the middle seat will be arranged, so you should avoid this when making reservations.

If you're used to cheap train travel in many other parts of the world, the ticket prices in Korea may be a shock, but it was good value given the reliability, comfort, on-board wifi and speed to get all over the country.  When we accidentally left a shopping bag on one of the overhead racks, we were directed to lost & found where we showed out seat number & asked if they found it to send it to the train station in Busan where we were headed a few days later.  To my amazement when we went to lost & found on arrival in Busan a few days later, the lovely staff had our bag waiting for us!

Very convenient. But the seats are a little too small for an adult. In my opinion maybe they can make the seats larger about 50%. I am an Asian still think it is too small. Very convenient. But only the chair seemed too small. I personally think that maybe they could make the chair about 50% larger. As an Asian, I think the chair is a bit small.
I used it to travel from Busan to Seoul. The seats were more comfortable than I expected and I was able to travel comfortably without feeling fast, so I didn't even know when I arrived.

travel a few time with the ktx and i like it a lot, it cost a lot more then normal train but you are much faster at you destination. second class is realy good, enough legg space, ...toillets are clean, free wifi,i recoment it for sure if you travel far.
I travel 1st  class, it was more convenient with a baby and prices were 25 to 50% less expensive than in France. Services was good with water bottle free and a snack offer.

10 million people living in Seoul means the KTX underground rail system is used by a lot of people as an alternative to using cars and buses to get around this busy and vibrant city. Buy a re-loadable ticket at the subway (or I believe 7/11?), then load up on fare before you go in. Fares are reasonable. English can be selected on auto machines too. Easy to follow to load money.Subway is very busy esp in Peak hour. We were very frustrated when lifts and escalators were not working due to having a painful foot injury. Each stop is announced in Korean and English. Most trains have a screen to display upcoming stop too.Expect to stand up most times. KTX is a good reliable system to reach many places in Seoul and outlying areas. Good for tourists too.

From Incheon Airport, I headed to Bupyeong Station and then to Woninjae Station. It's hard to tell the difference between AREX and KORAIL, but this was Korean Railway (KORAIL). This is my first time staying outside of Seoul. It's good to go out and sightsee once in a while. I also used Korean Railway for my last trip to Suwon.

My journey from Guangneug to Seoul in first class went wonderfully! Ticket purchased 1 hour before departure for 40,000 won (around €30) for a two-hour journey. At this price the train is brand new and the free wifi offered has a speed of around 28 Mbps even at 300km. Small snack served on board (bottle of water and snack). Punctual train and service on board irreproachable.

I just have a thing for trains! I loved every minute of it! I loved that there weren't a lot of people during the time we went so it was quiet and I really had fun taking in the view! BUSAN was awesome! Better than my experience in Seoul! Must definitely take this train to experience its glory!

I used it to travel from Seoul to Incheon Airport. I was concerned that I had left something behind in my seat, so when I told her that my wife had left something behind near the airport, she told me that it was a priority seat for pregnant women, and when I looked closely, I saw that the same doll had been placed on the seat of the car next to me. I was very grateful for the kind consideration.

I rode from Seoul to Pohang. It was a push-pull configuration consisting of a locomotive and a passenger car, and although the seats were a little narrow, the journey was quiet and comfortable enough that it was hard to notice when the train was departing at the station. Looking out the train window, there was a huge gap between the urban area near the station and the rural and mountain scenery, which I enjoyed.

I took an early morning train from Seoul Station to Cheonan city. Train arrived on-time and it was a comfortable ride.Even it was more expensive than taking the underground train to Cheonan, it was worth to take KTX which provided much faster service.

We took KTX to go to Busan and also because of the legend of Train to Busan. We enjoyed the ride - it was fast, clean and efficient. We got our tickets few days before the date and on our way back we got the train from Shingyeongju, which looked like a relatively new station. Coming form a country with weak transportation systems, KTX blew our mind.

After sightseeing in Gyeongju, take a ride from Shin Gyeongju Station to Seoul. The ride time was approximately 2 hours and 10 minutes. The inside of the train was quieter than I expected, and there were almost no tunnels, so it was an exhilarating feeling to be driving through the land of Korea. The fare was 68,000 won for a first class car, which I think is cheaper compared to Japan's Shinkansen. There were no ticket gates, and the flight attendants didn't come in midway, so it was strange, but it was refreshing. If you are boarding from Shin-Gyeongju Station, you will probably need to take a taxi as it is far from major tourist spots. I took a taxi from Gyeongju National Museum and it cost about 20,000 won. As for tickets, I had heard that it would be crowded during the Korean Obon (Chuseok) season, so I made a reservation from the KORAIL website in Japan. I didn't get the impression that it was that crowded from Shin-Gyeongju, but flights from Seoul are said to be especially busy during this time of year, so I recommend that international travelers make reservations online. Before boarding, I had almost no power for my smartphone, so I frantically asked at the counter if there was a seat with an outlet, and I was able to change to a seat with an outlet. Just like in Japan, it seems that not everything has electrical outlets yet. In addition, the shape of the outlet plug is "SE" and a transformer is required. I was very grateful that I could charge it for 2 hours. There are many restaurants at Seoul Station, and I think it would be fun to check them out.
Clean, fast, reliable trains. The only issue is you get your single ticket deposit back of 500 won and I had 5 people, so I was constantly carrying around a pile of change.
A very comfortable ride to Busan. It was on time. If the tickte shows the departure time is 6am, the train's door will be closed at 6 am.

The train ride from seoul to Busan was fantastic. The trains were fast, clean and spacious. The windows were very clean which meant you got a good view of the scenery as you went past. I would highly recommend.The only thing worth flagging is that around the weekend and public holidays the train can book out so book early.
Went from Busan to Seoul on the KTX and found the ride to be smooth and quiet, internet access is provided. Get in early if you have a lot of luggage to secure.
Travel aboard this very pleasant and safe TGV, optimal comfort with very welcoming staff. Punctuality is essential, very appreciable.

For those who have a bit of nostalgia, the KTX looks exactly like the TGV. We can continue the comparison between the two transport systems and the services offered to passengers in France and Korea. Test and you will see.

KTX is South Korea's high-speed rail system. The seats are quite spacious, which is very convenient for transportation to and from Busan, Seoul. Each carriage has luggage racks to place suitcases. I bought a PASS ticket and it was very convenient to draw a seat. I highly recommend this method of transportation to South Korea.

Korea’s bullet trains get the job done. Gets you to any major city from Seoul within 2 hours-ish. Amenities are basic but that’s okay because you are never on the train for long enough.My one pet peeve is the lack of sitting room in Seoul station. Had to resort to sitting in McDonald’s to wait for my train.
The express train is practical and quick ticket at the counter or machine it allows you to reach the inchuan airport in seoul center
Fast, clean, and friendly staffs. I am shocked by the fact that the staff did not even check our tickets. I love how they easily believe in people. I feel so safe and welcome along the trip.

KTX is the best, quickest and most comfortable way to travel to Busan.A day trip is easily done, with leaving Seoul early and coming back the same evening/night. 1st class is worth the little extra, as it not only more comfortable, but also quieter.

A super easy way to travel far and fairly inexpensive. I was able to do a day trip from one end of the country to the other with ease. Just be careful if you fall e. The ride is smooth and you might miss your stop.
KTX is the pride of Korea. It is fast, comfortable, and the service is good. I use it every time I go from Seoul to Busan. I want to make memories here again later.

Efficient and very punctual, the equivalent of our TGV is truly a success, especially as it is very quiet. However, be careful with very large luggage, the lockers dedicated to them are quite limited. But it is still the ideal mode of travel to visit the country

I rode the Korean bullet train "KTX" from Seoul to Busan. First of all, the price. A green car in Japan costs 68,300 ₩ (approximately 6,800 yen), which is about half the price in Japan. Second, there are no ticket gates. That's strange. Europe, America, and South Korea don't have ticket gates, but is there a need for one in Japan?There is a lot of room for consideration. Furthermore, there are almost no announcements in the train, so you can relax. Coming to Korea and thinking about Japan's JR - I'm worried about the management, especially dJR Hokkaido JR Road...
Rook the KTX to Busan area. It was super easy and a pleasure to ride. Model of transportation. Great job Korea.

I went from Busan back to Seoul by KTX, the train was lovely and comfy as well as super quiet even though the carriage was full :') the train was super fast and only too around 2/2.5 hours to get back into the city the views of Korea were amazing seeing all the small villages and towns as well as the mounatins and green areas. so pretty!

I think it's a pretty good train. Seats will be assigned. I bought my ticket at the counter, but it wasn't difficult at all and I was able to speak English. Above all, the fare seems cheap. Seoul Station has many shops on the platform, including Japanese Hot Motte.
Totally smooth travel from Seoul to Daegu.it also provides wifi and power points.if you're going to daegu or seoul, the KTX is the way to go

Recently, as my business trips to local areas have increased, I take KTX approximately once or twice a month. If you leave early in the morning, you can do a day trip to Busan, so I think KTX is fast and good. Buying a lunch box before boarding the train in the morning is good because you can save time and not be bored on the train.
Runs on time. Roomy and comfy with free fast wi-fi. Clean toilets on board makes the trip to and from the airport a breeze. Ground staff are warm, polite and very helpful for any queries.

Because I had to travel from Seoul to Busan, I thought about several means of transportation, and finally chose KTX. It only took about three hours to travel to and from Seoul and Busan, which was very time-saving and comfortable.

You can take KTX from Seoul Station to different places in Korea, such as Daegu, Gyeongju, Busan, etc. It’s convenient for a lot of people! And if you are a tourist, you can have different discounts to choose from, so traveling to different places in Korea is by no means difficult!

You arrive at Seoul Metro Station and there you can take the KTX to the airport. fast, comfortable, very silent. It makes no intermediate stops. But the gem is undoubtedly the fact that if you fly with some airlines, such as Korean, at the station you will find an airport gate, where you can easily check in, send your hold luggage and arrive comfortably at the airport with your hands free and going directly to the boarding controls.

Although it was a short distance from Seoul Station to Suwon Station, I took the Mugunghwa train. There may be new cars now, but the combination of diesel cars and passenger cars gives a sense of nostalgia. At Seoul Station, I had my credit card kicked several times at the vending machine when purchasing a ticket, but when I looked at the display, it said I had bought a Domestic Card. There weren't many machines that accepted cash, but there was one near the corner, so I felt safe. The display is in English, but you can easily purchase by selecting your destination and time. The KTX boarding area has a modern, clean space and an open gate, giving it an open feel. People who were probably heading to faraway places were eating light meals purchased at the shop while waiting for the train. The smoke from the diesel engine, the slightly old-fashioned atmosphere of the passenger car, and the presence of footrests that distinguish it from regular cars are perfect for creating the atmosphere of an outing. The view from the train window, along the route from the city center of Seoul to the suburbs, is reminiscent of a city during a period of economic growth, and it even creates a nostalgic feeling. Still, it's an unbeatable price, so there's no reason not to take advantage of it.

Trains are always the best way to see a country as you travel long distance through it. We went from Seoul station to Gyeongju ( the meseum without walls) . Tickets booked in UK, no issues. Chose 1st class only £20 extra. Seats very comfortable with trays and recliners. Tip:  if you want to sit together ( the wife insists on this!!!!) seat B and C are together with A across the isle. In first class they do come round with a complimentary pack,containing.......bag of nuts, a cookie and a wipe. Suggest you buy provisions at Seoul station before getting on- prices normal. Train departed platform 6 from Seoul. Carriage numbers are on the platform floor and on side of carriage. Journey to Gyeongju was two hours, believe Busan is 2 hrs 40 mins. Taxi from station to the town Tumuli Park (  by the kings tombs) was 17000. Great tourist info centre at station people very helpful. Train has charging points, announcements in English as well as Korean

Tickets were booked in advance using the website exchanged real tickets at station. Trains are accurate even by seconds. Very clean, and the seats are super cool. Good leg space.And if you travel as a group two rows of seats can be turned to face each other.at middle there is a cafe cabin. Power sockets are available. Wifi is onboard
We went from Busan to Seul in the morning rush hour, and it was very easy to find our track and the train! Its a good choice if you are tired of airport procedures!!
A very fast precision train with a speed of up to 300 km/h. The train is clean, the onboard staff is nice and helpful. The price is very reasonable
I took the KTX to Gangneung and it went very quickly so I was satisfied. Clean and friendly service. ktx is the best. thank you ktx!! I will continue to use it often.

i am an asian and had to change to earlier train. my original train was scheduled at 10：00.i arrived at the desk 9：10. the lady told us we could catch the 9：35. when she was about to change the booking, two europeans came in and wanted to buy tickets for trains departing at 10：10. the staff chose to serve them first, while i was in a hurry to catch 9：35  train. it took them 10 mins to finish up, and it was 9：20, the staff said sorry for making me to wait.it was possible they could screw me up if it took 5 mins more. it was so rush because if the delay. i cannot accept the explaination from staff that changing tickets is more complex than buying. the time took her to change my tickets was just the same as serving that two europeans.this is discrimination. i hope staff could have some courage to tell every single customer to queue up, and make professional decisions at work.
Not much to say except that it did not disappoint. It was modern, clean and very efficient. If you get a chance to get on one, don't miss it.

Luckily I was still able to take the last train from Busan to Seoul. The train cabin was very nice, and seemed luxurious to me. The seating is also very spacious, the chairs are also comfortable. You will really enjoy your long journey using this fast train.
Just checked my online transactions and viola! they charged me around 200,000 KRW.  This is due to their erroneous and not so friendly website.  Note: I have purchased Korail Pass.

There are 2, 3, 5 high-speed trains departing hourly on the Seoul Busan route. Routes and number of stops vary. Travel time one way took 2h45m, the other 3h10 minutes.  For resale, you should indicate the desired date and you will be offered a printout with the pickup time, all that remains is to indicate the time and number of tickets. Our prices turned out to be $53 and $56 per ticket. If you forgot to say at the ticket office that you want to ride facing the direction of travel, and the ticket fell into seats located backwards, then it is enough to express your wish to the conductor.  As soon as she receives the necessary information, she will come and offer to change seats. There are vending machines in the carriages to buy bottled drinks and candy bars.

There are only two direct trains a day, so I had to transfer. Is it the Fix you transferred from KTX? The train was more beautiful (lol).The ride was comfortable and there was almost no shaking. For a while from Busan, we were only in tunnels, but we were able to enjoy the scenery along the way 🤗 It was similar to the scenery in Japan, so it was relaxing 👍
Great to book online, trains were good. Downside is that you still have to have the ticket printed at the station

Th train look like old generation French TGV (in fact they are!)  and are thus not the most comfortable but the comparison stops here: Clean, on time, ultra efficient (from online reservation to station indication, to boarding,. etc. The trip was very pleasant.  French technology and South Korean service quality seem to make for a good receipt!

Korean Shinkansen. For foreigners, there are convenient Rail passes available. There are passes for unlimited rides starting from 3 days, so please check with Korean Rail. There was also an ekiben (Korean food) at the Shinkansen platform, which I also enjoyed! Bibimbap was delicious. Although the seats on the Shinkansen are a bit cramped, you can relax enough, so traveling by train is also recommended. You can buy tickets in the morning, but if you buy them in advance (the day before), there may be no seats available on busy days. ! It seems that there is, so I recommend it.

Book tru changiwifi (SG) 3 day KTX Seoul to Busan. After confirmation, we reserved our date, time and seat no tru KTX direct website. We can straightaway print their train tickets(showing train no.)Actual day, 20 min before departure, check the station board which track is your train.(No need to go to KTX counter)Limited luggage rack. Best to travel light.On board staff never check our train tickets and depart on schedule.KTX train stop abt 5 station in between. It took 3 hr ride.Return to Seoul, we reserved 1 day in advance the date & time at KTX counter, paying about SGD15 for first class seat which more comfy/snack/drinks available (free). 30 min before departure, just check which track is your train no. on.Travel Light!!...

Although it is a bit pricey, it is a route that allows you to get to Munsi Station in a short time. It is a very convenient means of transportation as you can go from Seoul to Busan in less than three hours.

I had similar experiences with some of the other travelers here, which clearly shows that yes there is a problem with the KORAIL ONLINE TICKETING SYSTEM!We tried to book the tickets to Busan, and upon clicking payment, the system hang showing an error message. With no email notification, and no reservation number, we figured that the booking didnt went through, so we clicked to purchase the second time. After we show up at Seoul to exchange the tickets, the officer also didnt inform us that we had 2 tickets bought... It was only after we came back from our trip that I realized I was charged twice for the tickets! We tried to call their customer service hotline, but with their limited English, they couldnt really understand me. Also no email or online messenger to contact them, and the only way is to attempt to speak to their staff via the hotline. So after explaining everything, the stuff still didnt understand and just kept telling me no refund as it's pass the travel date already. Even after I explained that it was due to the error on their website, yet they still insist that there's no error on their website, so no refund. SERIOUSLY?!!!! The mistake was from your own website yet it has been incurred to so many customers innocently. For those traveling to Korea, I would suggest that you buy direct from the station and not from online. Also, good luck too as I remember that the staff could'nt really speak much English at the station too!
they speak english at the ticketcounter, so you can get easy to a ticket (seat number). Good connections Soeul to Busan.

It is accurate to say that money buys time. It is twice as expensive and twice as fast as a bus. If you visit a city larger than Daegu, I would definitely recommend the KTX. They say that economy class seats are narrow, but I think it is much more comfortable than airplane economy class. I hope that the price will come down a little more with rapid popularization.

Convenient, I don’t know about the benefits, we lived next to the train station, traveled from Seoul to Busan and back, convenient with a child and suitcases, the trip to the airport would have been longer and more tedious to go through all the registrations. In Busan, it is best to take the subway directly from the railway station; not everyone takes the buses in Busan with suitcases. On this website you can see the cost of tickets in letskorail won.
I rode from Yongsan when going to Namwon. If you haven't reserved a ticket, it's difficult to get a seat. I'll say it's OK because I have fond memories of riding the KTX.

There is a row of automatic ticket vending machines on the left hand side of the main entrance of Seoul Station. There are credit card and cash tickets. When I bought the ticket, I looked for a credit card at first. I found that I didn't have a credit card, so I bought cash. You may have to verify your mobile phone number. There was a handsome Korean guy next to me at the time who helped me enter his mobile phone number. There was no inspection when entering the station and no ticket inspection. Just arrive at the entrance on the second floor 15 minutes early.
First class is definitely better.Convenient and fast,would recommend, we left our large luggage behind,could be better with some food offering
Traveled from Seoul to Busan in 2 hours and 20 minutes. - the price is high though, you pay 60,000 KRW for the trip, but for the comfort it's worth it.

This time, I used it for sightseeing from Seoul to Suwon. There were other options, such as the subway, but I chose this one because it didn't require any transfers and seemed to be faster. It takes about 40 minutes to reach Suwon. The fare was very cheap, the inside of the car was clean, and it was a comfortable trip. I would like to use it again.

I took the Korail high-speed rail from Busan to Seoul and the A'REX Airport Railway. Both are fast, punctual and comfortable. KTX has a total of 6 lines, namely Gyeongbu Line, Gyeongjeon Line, Donghae Line, Honam Line, Jeolla Line and Gyeonggang Line, and the A'REX direct air train (direct from Incheon Airport to Seoul Station), which basically covers almost 80% of the main areas in South Korea. The trains are frequent. Passengers can buy one-way tickets or 2-5 day Korail Pass according to their needs; in addition to making reservations and purchasing on Korail's website, KTX You can also order online at Hanchao, but Klook and KKday only sell Korail Pass, not one-way tickets. Although the KTX high-speed rail is very convenient for long-distance transportation, because it really saves a lot of time, the fare is quite expensive. Therefore, if you use KTX to travel to long-distance areas, you really need to calculate the difference between the one-way fare and the Pass fare, otherwise you will lose your budget.
It has established itself as Korea's high-speed railway. I flew from Seoul to Incheon Airport. However, there are not many passengers on this route, so it will be discontinued.

Clean and fast is the only positives. But pointless WiFi. Pointless air conditioning and uncomfortable chairs. Honestly they say South Korea is the most wired country in the world!!! In most of Western Europe, China and Japan the availability of WiFi far passes Korea!!! Just a general warning.
I used it to go to the Winter Olympics. Very good! Like anything in Korea and Japan in terms of transportation.

The trains in Korea are always on time. The carriages are clean. You can buy tickets via a website before you travel, this is simple and clear. You will be assigned train, carriage and seat immediately. Stations are generally very clean. Seoul station is very spacious, so take some time to orient yourself where your train is!

There aren’t any areas to put your luggage if you are traveling with ones that cannot be placed in the over head compartments. (Only place is the back seat with the space behind so I suggest you quickly book those) You’ll have to deal with cramming it inside your seat area with no space to put your legs for hours.

It is really very tourist friendly, easy to get to, easy to get the ticket, easy to read the signs to take the train. Expeditious, clean, economical and its connectivity with the subway is great, if you want to travel to Seoul it will help you greatly.
Clean trains, but no services inside, also the guidance to buy ticket is not easi to find out. Price level is quite good.

Good afternoon! I really liked the express train - it’s quite easy to purchase a ticket (either from a machine or through an operator next to the machines), you select the departure time, the number of passengers, the final station and voila = the card is in your pocket (at the exit there are machines where you can exchange your card for 500 Won). From Incheon Airport to Seoul Station ~ 40 min. Price for two = 19,000 Won, 1,000 Won will be returned to you. I think it is the most convenient and cheapest transport.
The high speed train service of Korea.KTX connects major cities in the country.Seats aren't luxurious. But, fast and easy to use.I think this is the best way to travel Korea in case you don't drive.
we tried the first class from seoul to jeonju and it is much better. Comfortable seat but refreshment is not that good.

For our second visit to South Korea the best, fastest and easiest way to travel from Seoul to Jeonju and Busan to Seoul was to take the KTX.  The service was always on time, clean, seat comfortable and traveled in near silence.  As we were on a schedule I purchased our tickets online one week in-advance, an easy booking and payment process.  The ticket price never changes, always a fixed price not like in Europe.  I purchased second class tickets which are significantly cheaper to first class and just as comfortable for a 1.75 hour and a 3 hour journey respectfully.  Seats are assigned and tickets issued immediately online ready for printing at home.  We always take water and pick up snacks in the subway or nearby train station for the journeys, but you can purchase on-board.

Have ridden KTX's all over Korea, especially the Seoul-Daegu and Seoul-Ulsan, and Seoul-Busan route - all less than 3 hours. KTX gets you to big cities fast, and on time. The downsides: high cost (about $50 one-way Seoul-Busan), and lack of knee space. if you can spare the extra money, splurge on the First Class seats!

Quickly, it reaches an incredible 300 km. per hour, excellent transport, very comfortable, feeling of being in the clouds, without noise, without moving. The flight attendants are very attentive and helpful. The cost x benefit is excellent. Access to downtown Seoul.

Efficient, punctual, comfortable, wifi. Well-priced passes for foreigners that can be cheaply upgraded to first class. What's not to like? NOTE KTX is the long distance bullet train, NOT the airport train. The airport train is AREX.

busan - seoul in 2.5hours with comfortable seat. board 15-20min before departure time so you can find best spot to keep your luggage. there are limited spaces at the end of cabins for bigger luggage. the air conditioner is not working so well during summer. wifi and usb charging point available. toilet looked clean but no water for handwash.
We know the French TGV but this one has the particularity of being just as fast (+ 300 km/h) but it is punctual and twice as expensive. It changed us from France.

Overall, we had a good experience on the KTX. One ride the a/c wasn't working well so they gave everyone in our car a bottle of water.  The website takes a while to get use to and navigate. They could improve the website quite a bit.

KTX is an essential means of transportation when traveling from Seoul to the countryside. There are many convenient facilities nearby, so it's convenient to use the station and it's nice to be able to get to your desired destination safely and conveniently.

I often use KTX to travel from Busan, but lately I've mostly been taking the special seats: It's not that expensive, they give you free pet drinks, free WiFi, and sweets. Tickets can be purchased at booths or from vending machines, but many vending machines do not accept credit cards in Japan, so you can also purchase tickets with cash or online. SRT, which has many stops, also runs on the same tracks. Check the route and stops before using it.

Traveled from Busan to Seoul in about 2 hours.  Very quick and convenient.  You are given an assigned seat, and it is better to stay there, even if the car is half empty, or risk being rapped by the attendant and told to move.  Very interesting view of South Korea, mostly green mountains, fields and clusters of apartment buildings.  Less suburbanization than you would think.

The experience of riding KTX was because we got on the wrong way because there were no instructions in English or Mandarin, only Korean writing, this was our return journey from Nami Island to Seoul City. While on the train journey we were approached by an officer who asked for tickets, fortunately there were people who could speak English to help translate, we were helped to move stations to get on the correct train. The KXT ticket price was quite expensive for us but it was very comfortable, fast and clean and the officers were friendly enough to help.
It's a direct flight, so you can take your time. The seats are comfortable and it's close to the airport. There is also a staff member, so there is no need to worry. There's no reason not to use it.
Railroad is Korea’s representative means of transportation. There are reports of occasional breakdowns, but covering Seoul-Busan in under 2 hours is an incredible feat of technology.

Take the express to Seoul, rather than taking a taxi. You will save roughly $70 if you are alone. The KTX costs around $25-$30 per person (depending on exchange rate), so if you are more than 3, you may want to take a taxi. I still think the KTX is more convenient, faster and don't have to worry about traffic or getting into an accident. The train has Wifi, so you will be connected. Cool. There are no drinks or food on the train so if you want to eat something, buy it beforehand. Depending on where you will be actually staying in Seoul, it might be better to take the normal train (not the KTX). The normal train is far cheaper and it costs me only $2 to get to Seoul, instead of the KTX. Yes, it takes 20 minutes longer, but I would rather save $20 for the 20 minutes. :-) Now, there goes the tip. Once the KTX drops you off at Seoul STation, you will have to take a taxi or take the metro anyhow.... assuming you are not staying at Seoul Station area. I have made it to 155 countries. I have an extensive blog at pinchetravels.com, if you want to read more about my travels.

A convenient way to move to another city. There are express trains, the main thing is to be careful and not take a “long” train.  During the holidays, tickets can be difficult to purchase, so consider purchasing holiday tickets in advance. In general, I can say that traveling by train is extremely interesting.

Traveled from Busan to Seoul on the KTX. Price was approximately 80000.00 KRW P/person for first class. KORAIL was very helpful at the Busan station and obliged to change our tickets to an earlier train. The train trip was excellent and quick and within a very short time approx 2hr 42 minutes we had arrived at Seoul. Traveling at speeds to a maximum of 299 klm/hr. They are very efficient and punctual on timings. Easy trip!

All in all, it seems to me that a flight is more affordable, but less comfortable. We traveled from Busan to Seoul, and it cost about the same as a flight with luggage. The trip took about two hours, and was very comfortable. There are cell phone chargers, there is plenty of legroom, and you can load as much luggage as you want. I guess the view is amazing - we traveled at night, so I have no idea.

The train helps you reach your destination sooner, however the seats are not comfortable and it is not in the best conditions...here what you are paying for is the speed...It is worth it because you don't wait as long as on the plane and it is extremely punctual.
It takes less than 2 hours from Seoul to Daegu, and it's great because you can travel from the center of Seoul to the center of Daegu. There are many restaurants in Daegu Station and Seoul Station.
The train that can be used when moving from Seoul to another city. You can save time. The train facilities are clean and it is not difficult to buy a train ticket.
We took the train to Busan and then back to Seoul. It was fast, efficient, clean and quiet. Very easy 3-hour journey.

in 2017 my Family travel to Japan. and in this June 2018 we travel to Korea.KTX is OK. But in Japan people are quieter. In Korea, I found people talk louder and some people didn't bother to watch the mobile phone without earphone, which makes the train "noisy". Older people have reserved seat. But if the reserved seat is full, I don't find the younger people willing to give up their seat (unlike in Japan where all young people seems to right away give their seat to elderly / those in need). Also there are no Officer in Korea Station where we can ask question. The signage not as clear as Japan. In Japan there are officer who were very helpful to both local and tourist.

The most commonly used mode of transportation to Busan. It was super convenient - we purchased our tickets online (the site is in English thank goodness), printed a copy of our tickets and brought it along. On the day we only had to show the print out to enter and nothing else. As simple as that. Arrive 15-20 minutes before and you’re good to go.

I use this all the time in Korea. It is clean, safe, and affordable. I am the SRT and ITX are also available and sometimes necessary alternatives but generally speaking, the KTX is the way to go. Most Europeans and Japanese are fond of it and of course American have nothing to compare it too.
It was surely the most convenient train ride Ive ever experienced. It also offers a nice view of the country
Experience like no other.  You can even watch a movie and won´t feel that you are traveling. Very comfortable sits.

It was the optimal means of transportation without worrying about traveling long distances. You can travel a distance that would take 5 to 6 hours by car in 2 to 3 hours, and travel comfortably while riding a clean train.

Buying KTX high-speed rail tickets in South Korea is very simple. You just need to buy them at the counter or find a kiosk that accepts cash. To buy a ticket, you can speak to the conductor in English pronunciation, or you need to know how to spell the English pinyin of the destination when using the kiosk. It is also easy to catch a train. There are many trains a day between Seoul and Busan, so you don’t have to worry about not having a train; by the way, there is also a very convenient facility, that is, there is wifi on KTX, which is very convenient.
Ticket can pre-book via ktx website and it is very convenient and save a lot of time let you visit more places

This is a quick way to get around Korea in quickly.  I always spend the couple extra dollars to upgrade to first class for the added legroom and USB chargers.  It may be more expensive than taking the bus, but its often worth it.  You can book online at their English site, just search for KTX in google.

I did some research in advance and found that if you go out of customs and use the currency exchange office in front of the exit, you can get a discount coupon and it will be cheaper. If you have a JCB card, it will still be cheaper. On the way back, you can go through immigration formalities at Seoul Station, so you can leave your luggage there, which is very convenient. However, only on designated airlines. I was on Jeju Air.
My family and I took the KTX from Seoul to Busan. Purchasing tickets was extremely easy and convenient. The train ride itself was smooth and comfortable. A really wonderful way to travel to Busan.
If you want a faster way to go to seoul from incheon airport, hop on to ktx. It's very comfortable train going to the city.

While their website needs a LOT of work (or maybe I'm just getting old) - booking the KoRail Pass was really wonky. However, undaunted, I managed it. So glad I did.We travelled from Seoul to Gwangju, back to Seoul, then on to Busan, all via KTX. It was on time to the minute, clean, quiet and FAST! The stations were all modern, clean, and (mostly) with English signs. They've done a fantastic job with their infrastructure. If you're traveling by train in Korea, take KTX!

I used it from Dongdaegu to Busan. Japanese credit cards cannot be used at automatic ticket machines, but they can be used at counters. The price was 17,100w, more than 1.5 times the bus, but it was still fast and arrived at Busan in 48 minutes. Although it was more expensive than the bus, it was more comfortable.

Ticketless purchases can be made online. You can just ride the ticket at the counter without having to exchange it. Changes cannot be made and you will have to purchase a refund bond, but refunds are free until 24 hours in advance. After that, you can get a refund with a fee of KRW400 up to 1 hour before departure.

Whilst on business, I needed to travel from Seoul to Yesu for one of my meetings. Although I am an experienced traveller and have used the Janpanese and Chinese rail systems, this was my first time using the high-speed trains in South Korea.Great on-line booking system meant that I had my tickets ahead of arrivibg in Seoul & a great service on my journeys.Recommended.

Used the Busan to Seoul service and was happy with our experience. You have plenty of space in your seating, there are power outlet for charging and you can choose whether you want to sit facing the driving direction or backwards. The train left on time and arrived on the minute. Very efficient, only the price was the only concern. Same as flying, however, you end up in the city centre with the train which can be desirable for some.

We took KTX from Seoul to Busan and back so conveniently. For foreigners like us, we bought KTX Rail pass online, exchange the tickets and reserve seats when we arrive Seoul Station. All information is so easy. The train platform has all information. Trains arrives and departs quite on time. All seats are comfortable with phone chargers. It might not be as good as the bullet train in Japan as there is still noise but it is not too uncomfortable. You can visit many provinces of Korea through KTX.
Easy to purchase tickets for a necessary seat.. clean, quiet, and peaceful.  timely, punctual, and stress free
There's hardly any room for luggages, though passing staff were helpful and accommodating to help us place the luggages near the doors of the train.

It took about 43 minutes to get to Seoul Station, and since I wasn't traveling by car, there was no traffic jam and there were toilets, so it was comfortable. I think it's convenient for personal travel.

Although it is a high-speed train, it runs slowly until it leaves central Seoul. The regular seats are 4 seats in a row of 2 x 2, and the seats in the front and back are a little narrow. The biggest problem is that the seats are in different directions in the middle of each car, and if you sit in the front, you will be sitting facing backwards in the direction of travel, so be careful when choosing your seat.
It is my 3rd time to take KTX.Took 2hours 44mins from Seoul to Busan.It always punctual, fast and clean.You can have free wifi too.

I have completed 8 return trips from Busan to Seoul. Airlines more expensive and time consuming given travel to both airports and security. Booked on line and went to Busan Station to book days, easy, wrote travel days and time to give to staff. Busan has a info. desk to get timetable as would Seoul.Takes 2.5 hrs but delivers you in the center of both cities.Highly recommended.

After arriving at Incheon Airport, I took a train to go to Myeongdong. It runs every 40 minutes, and after leaving Terminal 1, the next stop is Seoul Central Station. I bought a ticket for subway line 4 to Myeong-dong at the ticket counter, and if I showed my Asiana Airlines boarding pass, I believe they would give me a 1,000 won discount.

We boarded the KTX in Gyeongju bound for Seoul, there were only first class tickets which was very nice. On board there are toilets and newspapers, you can also buy some snacks. I especially liked that during the tour I recognized the tunnels that were mentioned in the movie Zombie Station, Train to Busan, hehehe

I took a KTX from Seoul to Busan, and thanks to the speed I could did a day visit and get back in the same day. It´s an alternative if you don´t want to take an airplane. They have several trains during the day.

I have taken the KTX numerous times on different connections.  The trains are always punctual to the minute, they are always clean and very comfortable.  And nobody will use his cell phone in the compartment!!!

A comfortable 45-minute journey with a reserved seat. The suitcase storage area was full, but since it goes directly to Seoul Station, I placed it near the entrance. You can get discounts on Jeju Air tickets, or you can get discounted tickets when you exchange money at the exchange office at the airport. Tickets can be purchased at the counter or from a vending machine. Orange signs are direct trains. Your ticket includes a deposit of 5,000 won, so don't forget to refund it at the deposit return machine when you get off the train.
Transportation is very easy in Korea. Both the metro and suburban trains are very clean. Their hours are punctual. Trains are available to almost every city. In short, KTX is very good.

Coming from Australia I can only say our Government have a great deal to learn about public transport. We took the ITX to ChunCheon and for 7300 won each to travel each way it was not only cheap but comfortable and actually on time. The ride was so smooth you forgot you were on a train. Book online at least one day before and select your date and time and you will travel cheap. The Korea Travel Pass is also a great idea but about an 81000 won initial outlay (but you do get greater flexibility). We left ChunCheon earlier than expected (after gorging on Dak Galbi at Dak Galbi Street. and with the help of the wonderful young lady at the tourist information booth, were able to get on an earlier train at no cost. But be beware, if you buy at the station on the day you risk not getting a seat and standing room only.
In Europe you should be inspired by the speed, service and frequency of trains

On the way in from the airport i took the bus because i knew precisely where I was getting off - essential when the street names are so similar - but on the way back I took the train which was much easier and very efficient

I went back and forth between Seoul Station and Suwon Station. Since you have a reserved seat, you can move around very comfortably. It took about 30-40 minutes to get to Suwon Station. After buying tea and snacks, we boarded the train. It felt like an excursion. It also has a toilet, so you don't have to worry about it in case of an emergency. Next time I'll try going further afield.

My family went to Korea in late March. I didn't want to buy a Korail pass as we only needed a one way ride from Seoul to Busan.Ticket seat reservation opens only 1 month prior and navigating their site is easy enough but there is a difference.With the English page, you can't choose your car or seat number. It is randomly chosen by the system for you, which was a no go for me as I wanted seats near the luggage storage areas. The Korean page however is more comprehensive. I tried it out using google translate and it allowed for a wider range of options including choosing your car and seat number. Downside though is that you have to input a local Korean contact number to be able to reserve it. So in the end, I had our guide, TOP Korea, reserve it for me because I couldn't do it myself. Senior citizen discount was availed of for my parents because I booked thru Amy of TOP Korea thru the Korean page. The English page doesn't have this option.Things to note:1. You print out the ticket and that's it. You don't need to change it for any actual ticket like with other countries. Ours wasn't even checked while on board. Maybe because they could see we weren't local.2. Car and seat counting is in reverse for the Seoul to Busan trip. Car 20 is first and Car 1 is last. Same with seats, row 1 is the last per car.3. Luggage storage areas are limited for the economy cars. I was told by our guide they are generally located between cars 5-7. We took the KTX 251 for Seoul to Busan and we used up all the luggage storage area in between our car, for our luggage alone so yes, it's limited. Over head areas can store backpacks and a smaller sized luggage but was made of see through glass like material so it's better if it isn't too heavy. Their is no space to store luggage behind the last row of chairs per car on KTX 251. We checked out KTX 117 before it left and it seemed to have space. So it's different per train I guess unlike with Japan wherein you can store big luggage behind the last row.4. Arrive early if you have big luggage, the luggage storage areas are also used for product shipments as we saw on our trip. Our train was ready for boarding 30 minutes prior to our trip so we just boarded ahead of time to make sure we had luggage space.5. No food cart on KTX 251 so if you want food, buy at one of the food stalls before boarding the train. There are around 8 food stall stands at the top of the stairs before going down to the platform. More inside the station building itself.6. Navigating the station is clear cut, everything is marked clearly. Boards have announcements constantly updated with English. Boarding area of the KTX trains is pretty small and also clearly designated so you won't get lost. No problem at all even if the personnel don't understand or speak English.Overall, it was a clean, smooth, on time train ride.

I bought a pass for 7 days to go round South Korea and it was the best decision I ever made. It allowed me to go back and forward to the Busan, Seoul, Jeonju, Daegu, Yeosu and many other places cheaper than if you buy single trip on the spot. If I missed the time, I simply go to the ticket counter and ask for the next train without even paying again. It's fast and on time. You won't even feel you are in the train. Nice.

Seoul airport is a good 45 minute train ride away from the city centre so it is best to get the express train from the airport for a direct route to the city. Leave the airport departure and walk to the information centre to buy your tickets which at the end of your ride you put in a machine to help recycle your tickets and get some money back. The information desk is wonderful and directs you to the platform where you wait for your train to arrive near the door that will open according to the carriage number on your ticket. The trains arrive promptly and you need to get on promptly so don’t hang about! A great resource to enhance your travels

I took the train from Busan to Seoul, which took about 2 hours and cost about 5,000 yen. The impression is that it is very cheap compared to Japan's Shinkansen. Free WIFI was available in the car. The seats were a little small.
Traveled twice from Daejeon to Seoul and from Daegu to Seoul. I really liked it. Probably the most comfortable way to travel around Korea.
We took the KTX to Busan and had a great experience. It was easy to book tickets online, and then all we had to do when we got there was board the train. No lines, no problems. It was a great trip.

I've taken this to Busan as well as Masan now. Both times were comfortable, convenient and fast. Only problem is if you're lugging large luggages, you'd find places to store it a little hard. Price may be expensive but if you're looking to save time, then this is for you. Best is to head to Seoul Station or book online for KORAIL pass so you save up (esp on group bookings). Only drawback to the pass is you have to go the station to reserve tickets (cannot do that online).
Excellent experience. It was fast, clean and fuss free. But as we were travelling with large pieces of luggage, I found that we were not able to find allocation space to store it during our journey.

It's cheaper than Japan's Shinkansen, faster than buses, and airplanes have procedures such as check-in and boarding, but the KTX has the advantage of being able to get on and off quite quickly. It's close to the city center, so it's good. Note: The seat comfort and quietness of the train seem to be better on the KTX than on the KTX-Sancheon, but Sancheon has quite a few charging ports.

Took the KTX from Seoul to Busan. A 2:15 hours journey. The experience was great. A combination of speed and comport, its a great way to travel around South Korea.And the free WiFi on board was a plus!

30 minutes from Busan Station to Shin-Gyeongju. We arrived in no time. There are two types of seats: general seats and special rooms (like green seats). Generally, the seats are arranged in 4 seats: window side, aisle side, aisle side, and window side. Special seats are arranged in three seats: window, aisle, and window. We sat in the special seats. I didn't go there in general, so I don't know, but the special seats have footrests, folding tables, free bottled water (from a vending machine that comes out when you press the button for 3 seconds), moist cookies, nuts, and light snacks with towels. There was also a small bookshelf with picture books for children. Depending on where you sit, there are USB ports so you can charge your cell phone. We were able to charge it on the way home. The seats are wide and comfortable. The 30-minute journey to Shin-Gyeongju will be over in no time, but if you're going to Seoul, I think you'll be much less tired if you take a special seat. I bought the ticket online in Japan. The official website can be changed to Japanese. It seems that you can also cancel on that website. Even if you miss your flight, you can change to another flight or cancel at the station counter. Cancellation fees seem to vary depending on the amount of time that has passed since departure. I printed out my round-trip tickets and brought them with me, but they don't check them, so if you can check where you'll be sitting on your smartphone, you might not need to print them out. When I get on the train, there is no ticket gate, so I get nervous (lol).When I get on from Busan Station, it's the first train, so I'm at the platform about 20 minutes early, so I can get on the train early. It might be fine for the general public to get to Shin-Gyeongju, but since the one-way ticket price is just under 500 yen, I think it's worth a try. You can go to Seoul for just under 6,000 yen for regular tickets, and 8,000 yen for special seats, so I'd like to go to Seoul at least once. The return trip was on time. There doesn't seem to be an air-conditioned waiting room on the platform, so it might be best not to go up to the top.

It is very accessible and easy to get train tickets even at the very last moment. I bought my ticket to Busan on the day i was heading there. And I just need to wait for 30 minutes which is enough time for me to grab a quick lunch before boarding the train. The seats of the train is also very comfortable with enough leg room to stretch. The seat can even be shifted so that you are leaning slightly backward and comfortable enough for you to sleep. There is also a removable table for you to put your stuff. For some seats, there are even charging point for you to plug in to charge your electronics devices. Excellent transportation system. Would definitely go for it again when I head to other part of the South Korea.

The Airport Railroad, which connects Incheon Airport to Seoul Station via Gimpo Airport, is very convenient and comfortable as you can use a T-money card for regular trains. In both Gimpo and Seoul, the distance to the platform is frustrating, but transferring to the subway is relatively smooth.

Took an early train at 5.30am from Seoul Station to Busan to catch a bus ride to  Changwon city to visit cherry blossom boulevards. The KTX trip lasted 3 hours and each was allocated a comfortable seat. If you missed your breakfast, don’t worry you can buy fastfood at Seoul station and eat it on the express train. There are overhead racks to keep your belongings. Quite a nice experience.
After spending many years dealing with the UK rail system, it was an enjoyable experience to catch trains which seem to always run on time!   Easy and convenient, it made train travel pleasant!

I've only tried taking this train once, ordered tickets via online booking, the seats felt like they were in an airplane cabin, the road was smooth and fast, and you know, you just arrived at your destination.

I really like high-speed trains, so I was looking forward to riding the Korean one as well. Unfortunately, it is a train where the seats are too narrow and uncomfortable, the aisle between the seats is very small, you have a hard time avoiding someone. So a big disappointment for me.
Comfortable, convenient, easy to figure out, totally terrific mass transportation system.  We took it to the Olympics. You can turn the seats to face another pair, so our foursome could talk.

The trains were fast and comfortable. People were allotted seats, so no mess there. I wish the train had more amenities and stayed at the stops for maybe longer durations. Otherwise, very fast and convenient.
We traveled by subway the entire trip to Seoul, including from and to the airport. fast, convenient, inexpensive. By T-money from Seoul station to Incheon airport - 2900 local money.
With the addition of the east-west KTX lines, it is now possible to go between any major city in South Korea in about 3 hours.  The KTX lines have revolutionized how Koreans live and work in  Korea.

The train seats are clean and comfortable. However, the ticket system can be improved on. From Seoul Station subway, you need to buy a ticket for entry to the KTX terminal. Then when you arrive at the airport, you need to get a refund on the subway ticket. Not very friendly for tourists.

I bought the Korail Pass for foreigners as it offered unlimited rides for the day, which was cheaper and timings more flexible than 2 1-way tickets. There are discounts for groups of 2 pax and above. We had made ticket reservations a day in advance but missed our return train. No need to panic as trains between Seoul and Busan depart every 15 min or so. We were prepared to pay a penalty fee if needed, but maybe because we had the 1-day Korail Pass, which offered unlimited rides for the day, the staff only cancelled the departed train tics and gave new tics. No penalty fees! However as it was a last min reservation, we weren't able to sit together. At least it's better than standing tics for 2 hr 40 min!!There're no food bars on the train so be prepared to buy food for long journeys from the station's many food outlets. Luggage racks are available at the ends of each train carriage but it's small so best to go early to reserve spots for your luggage. Usually the train gets into the platform about 20 min before the departure time.

We travelled a lot by this amazing train, called KTX during our stay in South-Korea. It is very fast and comfortable seating, all clean washbasins. Staff is very polite and kind. (never asked for our tickets..) Wifi is awesome on board.Recommended.

We travelled from Seoul to Busan by KTX (Korean Train Express). It was a comfortable, time saving and fast journey. It just took us 2 hours 45 minutes.We pre-booked our tickets at Seoul station, if you don't do this in advance you risk not getting a seat and will have to stand for your journey. There were vending machines on board if you wanted refreshments and Seoul station had tons of coffee shops and restaurants if you want snacks for your journey. Pretty much all KTX trains to Busan depart from platform 6, the screens in the stations are clear so it should be obvious which platform is required.The seats were spacious and comfy and the views from Seoul to Busan were amazing! The TV screens in the carriages clearly display which stop is coming up.
The journeys between Seoul and Gangneug and Pyeongchang and Busan were most pleasant! Free WiFi! Beautiful landscapes of South Korea!!!

We took the KTX from Seoul to Daegu (and back) and thoroughly enjoyed our experience.  We chose first class to get a reserved seat.  They offer a small snack and free bottles of water in this section.  The high speed service was on time and is a great way to travel to the major cities in South Korea.
It takes about 45 minutes from the airport to reach Seoul Station. With the pick-up bus, we stopped at various places, and even though we had just arrived, we ended up stopping at a duty-free shop.

First of all, cocorico. The rolling stock is French designed and manufactured, the Korean TGV being one of the only TGVs sold outside France. Afterwards the comparison stops there with the SNCF. Here we are in a real class transport. Pleasant service, punctuality, impeccable on-board comfort. All this for a fairly high price (same as the plane).

This was a great train experience, fast, clean and on time.  I've taken trains in a lot of countries, so in comparison this rates among the best.  Of course it was new for the Olympics. The added stations, like Pyeongchang, were both functional and and a design delight.  Easy to make reservations even  in English!  You do need to plan ahead though for availability.

On early February 2018, I traveled from Busan to Seoul, Korea by KTX (Korean Train Express). It was a comfortable,  time saving and fast journey. All It take is 2 hr 45 min sitting in the comfortable seat for a scenery ride. Both Busan & Seoul station is located in the downtown of the city, convenience to connect to MTR, Buses and Airport Express line. The ticket price is reasonable, you can book it online in advance.
The best option for taking to/from Incheon Airport.  It cost less than any other options & is faster.

We took KTX from Seoul main station to Busan. It was hassle free, convenient and very user friendly. All the train staff speaks decent English and we have no trouble at all to secure tickets. There are overhead space to put your luggage bag but from observation - it might fit the Medium large luggage but Large size could be a bit darn heavy to lift. The seats are comfortable for the almost 3 hrs ride and they have free Wifi on board. Highly recommended.
Purchase tickets at the counter on the day. I headed for home after the train departed 5 minutes later, but KTX didn't have anything like a ticket gate on the way there or on the way back.

Since we wanted to spontaneously drive with a larger group from Seoul to Gangneung on the east coast for the Olympic ice hockey final, the KTX was just too obvious on the newly built route. With a journey time of around three hours from coast to coast and a fare of around 40 euros for the one-way route, the KTX is a cost-effective and fast means of transport. We were unable to make a (recommended) reservation due to time constraints, so we had to book standing room tickets, which are sold depending on the car. There are usually one or two jump seats in the car crossings and it is not uncommon to simply sit on the floor. Unreserved seats can of course also be used. However, it is advisable to make sure beforehand. The cars themselves are rather plain and functional. Larger luggage can be placed in luggage racks at the ends of the car.

This train has several routes throughout Korea 24 hours a day. It is essential if you plan to travel around the country. The price is much cheaper than taking a plane and the travel time (depending on the place of origin and destination) is short. The cleanliness of the carriages, the attention of the staff on board and the punctuality of the trains is a 10. In addition, it has free Wi-Fi, so you can enjoy the trip. Totally recommended. You don't have to travel first class to experience the best service.

We took the train from Seoul to Gangneung (and back) for the Winter Olympics. Modern, punctual, clean train. Wifi. Nothing to say. The only doubt was about the destination... in the sense that having made intermediate stops... we had the doubt of where to get off.
The KTX trains are high speed, and affordable to get from PyeongChang to the airport was 2.5 hours and only about $27 US for an economy seat.
Convenient, comfortable, goes to many locations but have to check the schedule beforehand because it stops early for some locations
It's a really comfortable and fast KTX. It's a bit pricey, but I'm very satisfied with the facility itself. I hope there are more sections.

I used it to travel to Jinbu and Gangneung during the Pyeongchang Olympics in February. Once I went directly from Incheon, and once I used KTX from Seoul Station. The direct flight from Incheon was very comfortable, as it was from Incheon Airport, passed through Seoul Station (actually took a different route without passing through Seoul Station), and then suddenly arrived at Jinbu Station, where the venue was located. However, since most of the trains departing from Seoul Station had to stay overnight at stations along the way, it took quite a while. Since KTX is a large express train, I thought it would be spacious inside, but it was actually quite cramped. The fatal thing is that there is almost no place to put the trunk. I wish they would have improved on that, even just for the Olympics. . Although it was cheaper than Japan's Shinkansen, I would rate it a 3, considering the slightly cramped seats, problems with the trunk, and timetable issues.
Took it to and from Seoul to the Olympics. Reliable, convenient, seats are pretty comfy. Just need a little better wifi, and maybe a little cheaper tickets.

KTX is a great train ride. If you get the right train with little scheduled stops, you can get from Seoul to Jinbu/Gangneung is just over an hour. It is fairly inexpensive and the first class ticket includes water and a snack. There is free wifi on the train and there is a lot of room in the seats.
Easy to book from the Netherlands, but also on site. trains run frequently and on time. clean and comfortable.

If you go to Korea it is essential that you travel at least once... there is an airport route that takes you to Seoul in an hour, which is basic to have this experience... comfortable, fast transportation, it is not so economical but you should use it... ahh it has wifi inside

We took the KTX in Seoul to attend the Olympic Games in Pyeongchang. The train system is very clean, including the washrooms. The trains were excellent value for the money we spent. They have seated tickets, as well as, standing room tickets that are less-expensive. These seats are located behind the last row of seats in each car or in the sections between train cars where there are two  bumper-type seats like the ones flight attendants often use on airplanes. The conductors are friendly and helpful. Be careful that you have the correct tickets for your journey because the conductor will issue a penalty ticket. The KTX was a wonderful experience for us, giving us the opportunity to travel quickly and efficiently to attend the Olympics.
Awesome new train service from Seoul to Gangneung on the coast. You can also take this directly to and from the airport. It's now only about 1 hour 40 mins from Seoul to Gangneung.

Decided to use KTX for my travel to southern port city of Yeosu.     My train left from Yongsan train station instead of the usual Seoul train station.     The trip takes a little over two hour and it is super comfortable.   Interior is fairly modern and they sell some snacks and drinks along the way.      I will certainly use KTX for all my future travels in Korea.

We used KTX for a trip from Seoul to Busan and back. We liked this type of transport! Convenient ticket purchasing process: you can buy at regular ticket offices (it was always crowded), you can also buy at ticket machines (there is an English menu, the purchasing process is very fast). I don’t know why people, even young Koreans, didn’t use machine guns. Perhaps there are some discounts. Although the machines provide discounts for people of retirement age. We took advantage of this discount, there were no complaints from the inspectors! It turned out cheaper by 10-15 percent! Also in the station building there are numerous cafes and shops with a large selection, toilets are free. I was also pleased with the presence of a tourist corner - you can take a map of the city and get information of interest, incl. in English. Next comes the exit to the platform. Everything is very thought out, there are arrows and signs everywhere in Korean and English. I was very pleased and surprised that the car numbers are indicated on the platform, so you can get to the right place in advance. It would be great if such a system was introduced at Russian train stations! The trip itself was very comfortable, the train moved quickly and silently. We took the right places. The carriage has two toilet stalls. During the trip, a waiter walks around with a food cart - this is paid. As far as I remember, the carriage also has a tank of drinking water - free of charge. Periodically, the controller enters the carriage and first...bows to the passengers. Then he very politely approaches the newly arrived passengers and asks to see their ticket. The level of service is excellent! The trip takes a couple of hours. During this time you can see the hidden corners of the country. I highly recommend it!
Drove from Seoul to Gangneung and back several times with the comfortable KTX. Well organised, always on time, trains super clean, staff very helpful and friendly.

I used KTX from Busan to Seoul. All you have to do is make a reservation in Japan, print out your ticket, and bring it with you. The train itself is similar to the Shinkansen in Japan, and is generally clean and comfortable to ride. The seats were arranged in three rows, one for two and one for one. There is a luggage storage area at the end of the vehicle, but it is small. I would like to use it again if I have a chance next time.

I used it 5 times during my 3 day stay at the Olympics. Although it was more convenient in terms of time compared to the conventional line, there was less space to store suitcases on the train, with only about 6 suitcases per car. It was very inconvenient. Is it because once the Olympics are over, the movement will be more about nationals than foreign tourists? I have no complaints about the seating comfort. What surprised me was that once I made a reservation, I didn't have a ticket, and it wasn't checked once when I got on, during the ride, and when I got off! Reservations can be easily made online or at the station. You said you increased the number of times at the Olympics, but I think the number was overwhelmingly low.

We always prefer taking KTX Train when traveling from Ulsan to Seoul reasons being It's fast, convenient, clean, spacious and very comfortable. It's fairly priced as well. They offer Free WiFi while and provide free bottled water machines for First Class ticket holders. Highly recommend for anyone looking to avoid airports and save some time!
