I think this is due to a difference in the ideology of railway operators.

if you are going somewhere the KTX will take you, I recommend it.  Smoother than air or car travel, easier than going to the airport because there's no security or really any boarding hassles to worry about, faster than car or bus, cheaper than plane, more comfortable than almost anything, it's worth it.  We bought first class tickets back and forth from Seoul to Busan and they were only about $80 apiece.  It took all of two or three minutes to get our tickets at Seoul and Busan stations, after reserving them online (website in English, takes American credit cards), and it took all of two or three minutes to board.  They never even checked out tickets; this operation is so efficient that they probably have a machine that reads your mind and knows whether or not you paid.  First class is very comfortable with a lot of leg room and free water, bathrooms that are a little nicer than airplane bathrooms, and drinks and beer and snacks for purchase.  The entire trip took only about 3.5 hours with three stops because the train gets up to almost 200mph.  But you don't feel a thing, it's much smoother and more comfortable than the Seoul metro or any other train I've ever been on, or an airplane or a car.  You could easily drop off to sleep.  We loved it.

I purchased three tickets online 1 month before I visited South Korea. I used KTX from Busan to Seoul. I payed 54.400 won and it's quite expensive for me (as a student college :D ) but I knew this would be my first time experience to try the fastest train in Korea. The journey took only less than 3 hr from Busan to Seoul.The train was so comfortable, with high-speed wifi in every car. You can see speed monitor on television above ( and I excited to see the speed reached 300 km/h, wow..)It was a smooth trip, even I didn't realize that now I was in train with high speed.Seats was so nice and comfy.
I visited south Korea for 3 days and used ktx it's well signed its good value and clean efficient service

It is very fast, you could transport from North Korea to its South in may be 3.30 hours and you couldn't feel boring because there is WiFi inside it, sure with youtubes and online videos your amount will finish quickly but if u didn't use videos you ll have amusements and it s very clean

From Busan, we went to Seoul via KTX. We bought our tickets 2 days ahead and we're lucky we did since seats and choice times sell out fast. Standard tickets cost 54,400 Won one-way (First class is around 80K Won). Standard seats are pretty comfortable with wide airline-like seats (only two in a row) and ample legroom.The train leaves on time so better get there early since it gets moving without much ceremonies. The ride is very comfortable and smooth. We were facing the opposite direction and we hardly noticed we were going backwards. Trains have WiFi but do seem have a time limit. Better check with someone who can read Korean if it does since the sign-in page is entirely in Hanggul.Travel time from Busan to Seoul (and vice versa) takes around a "short" 3 hours. Short since the ride is so comfortable it is sleep-inducing. An attendant with a cart sells refreshments and snacks in case you need it. There are restrooms inside the trains.

After an awesome holiday in Donghae, we decided to take this train back into Seoul at 1130 pm.  It was a very smooth ride.  I feel right to sleep.  The seat recline alllllll the way back when I took it with Girlfriend, co-worker, and his Girlfriend. It does get a bit chilly so bring a light jacket! Have Fun!!

The ride comfort is no different from Japan's Shinkansen. In fact, it may be better than Japan's Shinkansen trains because of the wider seat spacing. However, what is surprising is how cheap it is. The fare between Busan and Gyeongju was only 10,000 won.

KTX in Korea is easy, economic rapid ground transport with scenic view of both modern and more traditional Korea.  Korean rail system offered both one way ticket and pass program to explore the peninsula.  Having experienced the ICE in Europe and KTX in Korea, I must say they are two peas in a pod with two differentiable genetics to satisfy the host culture.  You will pleased with Korean courtesy and snack service carts.  Highly recommend this experience for those who want a cultural taste of people, place and things. Google KTX for info in several languages.  All rail info and announcements are in Korean and English.

Busan Station has restaurants and cafes on the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd floors, so you can eat there from early in the morning. Access the 1st floor platform from the open waiting area on the 2nd floor. There were no ticket gates, and the Korean style had separate entrances and exits to the platform.

We took tickets from Seoul to Busan. The ticket cost about 1.5 thousand rubles. economy class. We got there in three hours and forty minutes, with several stops. The train is equipped with toilets, free Wi-Fi, drinks are served, there are food vending machines at the entrance to the carriage, it seems there is even a cinema at the beginning of the train. You go through a lot of tunnels, but there is something to look out of the window, almost all the way there are picturesque views of local farmland.

Never go to the fish market when you’re full—you’ll lose a lot! In Korea, people visit the fish market in three cases: 1) fish auctions, where freshly caught fish is bought in bulk for restaurants and similar establishments (you need to get up at 4 am, stand in line before the auction opens, you may not get in if you come late, you understand - this is not my case, but writing about what I haven’t seen is not my topic! Although many enthusiastically share their impressions... 2) retail purchase for family needs: imagine the area of two football fields in a two-story building - the first floor has straight rows on both sides filled with aquariums and bathtubs with sea water, as well as many tiered shelves with ice (looking ahead, I will say there is no fishy stench, only the fresh smell of the sea and this is at 15 o'clock in the afternoon)... and all this is filled, filled and laid with Fish, Babyfish and Shrimp - everything is alive and wonderfully beautiful: tuna, salmon , trout, flounder and halibut, intertwined ropes of eels - this is a small list of what was seen and recognized, and then meter-long bright red crabs, king and tiger prawns lying in groups of ten, small items in piles and piles, lobsters and lobsters with tied claws sadly awaiting their fate, and next to them on the ice are oysters, scallops and mussels of all colors and sizes, plus all sea grass and vegetables...Odessa Privoz is resting!!! And at the end of the third, tourist Gourmet - the essence of the review: the market has a second floor equal in area to the first and consisting of 35-50 squares, each equipped with small, low tables for two or four people (they eat while sitting on mats, with chopsticks, if you ask they will give you forks, knives are not provided at all) in the corner there are a couple of grills and something on kerosene like a primus, only big! here! You leisurely admire all the splendor that I described above and curse the guide for dragging you into yet another pompous and very expensive restaurant and it’s hard for you to breathe after eating... lo and behold, you can’t even try such king prawns?!?... (they only sell for ten, without haggling, for 10 green, the lowest price!), and next to it is flounder, weighing somewhere over a kilo and scary, but not childishly delicious eel. Everything is in the basket and now the saleswoman quickly, shouting something, drags me to the second floor. to the best owner of the restaurant (your friend, sister, well, you understand...) Instant order and you are already at a small table with a bottle of beer and the thought:.. you need to send for whiskey... 10 minutes pass and here they are the first pair of shrimps when cooked on the grill: huge, once cut in the middle with the most tender meat, and you put it in melted butter and whiskey with beer.. Flounder and the eel simply couldn’t find a place after the shrimp! Please don’t go to the fish market in Korea full!!!

I enjoyed riding the KTX from Seoul to Busan. It was an enjoyable trip and I loved looking at the building and countryside as this fast train roared to Busan. The price is reasonable at about $50 USD each way for standard, and about $80 USD for first class seats, and I think it is a very fast and easy way to get to Busan from Seoul. I recommend buying your tickets in advance. Since I bought my ticket the morning of my trip, I was assigned an aisle seat though I wanted a window one, but the nice gentleman at the window seat willingly exchanged with me once I explained politely in broken Korean that I needed to take pictures as we go.  The train interior is clean and you can buy food and drinks on the train. Originally, I had planned to buy first class tickets for more quiet and privacy, but ended up with standard tickets. All in all, it did not matter since l enjoyed my trip.

No matter how old I get, I am still fascinated by trains. And bullet trains are as awesome as they get. OK maybe Maglev would be more awesome if I ever get to try that.For around $80 USD, we took the 07:30 KTX from Seoul to Singyeongju and took the return trip via the 20:58 train. The ride each way is barely over 2 hours. The trains reach 300 km/h in certain open stretches. That completely makes a day trip to Gyeongju manageable. Note that the Singyeongju (literally New Gyeongju) station is about 15 minutes outside of Gyeongju. A 1,500 KRW bus ride will take you into town or you can take the 700 bus directly to Bulguksa Temple if you want (we did). T-Money is accepted.Back to the KTX. The seats are comfortable and the 2-hour ride was not a problem. They even have wifi for every two train cars. Simply connect to the one that has the strongest signal.They will soon have new lines opening to the airport and to other regions of Korea. These high speed trains really make seeing more of the country easy, convenient, and fun.

the KTX from Seoul to Gyoengju or beyond is the way to get to the South East. Very fast, French trains by Alstom, very cheap...$44 reserved seat to Singyeongju... and exactly on time. We left Seoul after our driving friends by two hours and even after the 45 min bus ride from the station to the Gyeongju Hilton we arrived at the same time within a few minutes. As with the TGV recommend taking your own refreshments although they are available on board. Way to travel.

My visit to Seoul was made years ago, but let me tell you that I would love to go again, many times when you travel you say I have already seen enough, but Seoul is an impressive city, beautiful, very pleasant, it has many things, I would like to return and stay for about 6 months I think that this way I could get to know a large part of this beautiful city

The KTX I used from Busan to Seoul is a French vehicle. Once inside, there are fixed chairs and half of them face backwards. I think you should request this when you buy the ticket. What surprised me was that there were no ticket gates and you could go directly to the platform. Of course, there were no ticket gates in Seoul either. There was a conductor inside, but there was no ticket inspection.There is also wagon service and alcohol available on the train.If you want to enjoy traveling by train, there is a free pass for foreigners, which is a great deal.You can buy it cheaper than the round trip fare between Busan and Seoul, so it is also recommended for going to other places.

I asked a friend of mine who was local to place if they'd recommend taking the regular train which was around 3 or 4 hours, thinking I'd enjoy the view and the trip. He gave me a tired look and said ktx would be faster, and therew as not much to see. I was grateful I listened to his advice, as I saw myself there 30'minutes before the scheduled departure. The train was efficient, food and drinks served at a good price. For 53,300 won from Busan to Seoul I was expecting that maybe the seats were a little new, but seemed to be a little worn out. More than that, I couldn't complain more as to how efficient this was!

traveled from seoul to busan.comfortable seats.quiet during motion and braking.space for small luggage in rail above seats.compartments @ ends of each train car can hold larger luggages/packages.worth the extra money compared to bus fare or regular train tix.they sell snacks, soft drinks on train during travel.u can bring ur own food and drinks.safe.other passengers are generally respectful of others and not too loud during their conversations or phone calls.can reserve ticket @ Korail web site or go to KTX/Korail ticket counter to make your purchase.

The journey from Seoul Station to Busan Station on KTX001 takes 2 hours and 16 minutes. I wanted to say that, but I arrived 5 or 6 minutes late. I didn't have any instructions, but I wonder if it's something like this? I got on the train without realizing it was a non-stop train, so I was surprised that it didn't stop anywhere, but I was even more surprised that there were no ticket gates at Seoul Station, and there were no ticket inspections inside the train.

I have always wanted to go on a Bullett train. I was not disappointed. It was fast, and "clickety-clack" free. comfortable and even a cinema car, although it was not operational on the train i was on. The conductors and train manager make many trips up and down the train and bow when entering and leaving each carriage. Food service also available. Wifi was available, but I couldn't get it to work on my iPad. 2.30 hours from Busan to Seoul.

During my travel to Korea, I took KTX from Seoul to Busan (on Nov. 11 / Economy) and Busan to Seoul (on Nov. 12 / First Class).  It was my introduction to "high speed rail" travel.  As I was coming to Korea after trekking in Nepal, I had a GPS with me. The ride was so smooth and I was curious about how fast it was travelling.  So I checked my GPS and it was showing the speed as 280 km/h.  These days many people, especially Koreans, are shouting about "world class this", "world class that".  Without any reservation, my entire experience with KTX including ticket purchasing, boarding, on-board service, and departure / arrival punctuality was excellent.  KTX, yes, you can call yourself the World Class!     john / Vancouver Island, BC, Canada

It's cheap and very convenient. Regular vehicles are noisy with many children and people using cell phones, but special rooms are spacious and quiet. In the taxi on the way home, I made a big mistake by telling them it was Daegu Station! Please note that the KTX station is Dongdaegu Station.

I used it to travel from Seoul to Busan. The fare is about 4,000 yen, and it takes about 2 and a half hours to cover a distance of about 400 km. It's similar to Japan's Shinkansen, but the fare is much cheaper. I tried to buy tickets at Seoul Station using a vending machine, but I couldn't insert the bills properly, so I ended up buying them at the counter. At the counter, it was easy to communicate in broken English. The big difference from Japan was that there were no ticket gates or ticket inspections. The entrance to Seoul Station was completely open, and even when I went to the platform, there was no place to show my ticket on the train. When I left Busan Station, there was no place to issue a ticket. Maybe it was because I had a reserved seat, but I was surprised. The air conditioner's vents run from the window sill to the window like an air curtain, so the wind doesn't hit me directly, making it comfortable. I would like to use it again.

The KTX is an excellent way to get to the south west of Korea. I had a business meeting in Gumi and jumping on the KTX got us to the Gimcheon/Gumi station in a little over an hour. The downside was getting from there (the station is almost literally in the middle of nowhere) to Gumi proper. The taxi was cheap (by US standards) but added an additional 45 mins. The return leg had a similar wrinkle as the Seoul Station terminus is in the north of the city. If you're staying south of the river be prepared for a long subway or taxi ride.

I hadn't ridden KTX for a while, but this was my first time traveling back and forth on the line via Shin-Gyeongju. It incorporates France's TGV, but like in France, the track width is the same as the conventional track, so you can run on the old route as long as you reduce the speed. Construction costs can be saved, but if there are many sections where speeds are reduced, the time required cannot be reduced much. This time, it was about 430km and took 2 hours and 29 minutes. However, compared to Japan's Shinkansen trains, they produce slightly less noise and vibration when running at high speeds. Japanese-made cars usually have motors on all cars, which is quite noisy, but French-designed cars usually only have two motors, one in the lead car and the other in the back. He used to run 305 km, but now he seems to be holding back. It's true that the inside of the passenger car is quiet even though it must have been over 250km. I understand that this will probably sell better internationally. This is because the vehicle structure is simple. Japanese-made products require a very complex system, such as controlling the motors of each vehicle. It would be more advantageous from a business standpoint to not have to incur the extra expense of developing special vehicles like those for Japan's Nagasaki Shinkansen.

Traveling to the 2012 Yeosu International Expo I had the opportunity to travel on this fast train that offers comfort and convenience when traveling. Its facilities and accommodation are impeccable and truly hygienic. It is a very safe and fast means of transportation and the views of meadows and fields along the journey as well as the views of the cities and towns on the train route are wonderful and worth photographing. If the journey is very long there is the opportunity to visit the cafeteria or restaurant car and on short journeys there are carts in the cars that come to your seat offering coffee, tea and the odd snack. The price is a little more expensive than other trains but it is still cheaper than the air ticket and the complexity of going to the airport, check in, takeoff, landing, picking up suitcases, etc. and everything that air travel implies are eliminated, in my opinion, when using the train.

I used three sections: Seoul Station - Daejeon Station, Daejeon Station - Busan Station, and Shin Gyeongju - Seoul. The required times were 60 minutes, 90 minutes, and a little over 2 hours, respectively. I was driving slowly for quite a long time, probably because there are a lot of trains in the vicinity of Seoul. After a while, I got up to speed, but the rails were wide apart so I didn't feel any major shaking and it was comfortable. There are two classes of seats, like the Shinkansen in Japan, and I was able to secure a so-called green seat. These seats have a total of three rows of 2-1 rows across the vehicle, and the seats are wide in front and back. Although the seats recline enough, they are spacious and comfortable without bothering the rear seats. As soon as I boarded the vehicle, there was a place in front of the cabin to store large luggage such as the trunk, so I was able to use the spacious seats as they were. There is a staff member assigned to each vehicle in this trunk storage area, so you can feel safe leaving your luggage there. There are water vending machines between each vehicle. In addition, in-train sales are carried out in exactly the same way as you would imagine on a Japanese Shinkansen. Lastly, there are toilets in the car, but they are not separated by gender. Unfortunately, it wasn't very clean either.

The maximum speed is over 300KM. I enjoyed the 1 hour and 30 hour journey from Seoul to Kimcheon Gumi without making a reservation. There are only 3 stops to Kimcheon Gumi ^^ My friend and I are both beginners in Korean, so we were wondering if we could get off at the minor stations properly! ? I rode with such anxiety. (Moreover, since I didn't make a reservation, the cars were different.However, I was told that there would be an announcement so it was okay!) and got on the train.The one-way ticket cost only 34,500 won. I can't hear the announcements lol. There are some announcements, but like the Shinkansen in Japan, there's no music, and it's the end when I fall into a deep sleep. That's what it felt like. The only thing I was disappointed about when I went home was that there was a parent with a child next to me and it was noisy. . . But, thanks to you, I didn't have to sleep ^^; By the way, if you go from Incheon Airport to Seoul to KTX, if you tell the station staff that you want to use KTX for the non-stop train ticket from Incheon Airport to Seoul and show the ticket (possibly you can also buy it on the spot), it seems that you can buy it at a discounted price! !

Have lived in Seoul for 9 months. First trip on the KTX. Just like the Seoul Subway System the trains run on time (to the minute) and is a fast economical way to travel in Korea. You can purchase your tickets online, or at the station. We traveled in Economy to Busan, and First Class on the way back. First Class had more leg room, wider seats, free drinking water, newspapers (they did have English language newspapers available), crackers for a snack and free wifi. The price difference was about 20,000KRW one way between the two classes. There is plenty of food available to eat at both stations, and you can get almost anything to go, so don't worry about eating before you get to the station. Unlike Airports, the food is the same price in the station as it is on the street. I would be remiss not to mention that there is a great food court at Seoul Station. It is on the second level (one level above the main station and two levels above the tracks). It has 17 different food stations, with each station offering about 10 items each. Each order is prepared fresh and is a great way for everyone in your party to have their own type of Korean food.

We booked a seat in 1st class for about $46. It had outlets for your computer and plenty of leg room. If you are going on a long trip this is the only way to go. Also buy food at one of the restaurants at the station to bring on-board - better than the food you could buy on the train.

Typically, left on time, arrived on time. caught a nap.Seoul Station is easy to use BUT if you are expecting air conditioning in the station -not going to happen, bring a change of clothes if you are carry a lot of bags.

The KTX passes we purchased, which were a 10-day pass, came in very handy as we went from Seoul to Busan, Busan to Daegu, Daegu to Seoul, Seoul to Gwangju and Gwangju back to Seoul all within the 10 days. One thing to note is that bumping up to first class cost only 7000W if you already have the pass. It was worth it to us to bump to first class and have a larger and more relaxing seat. The economy seats were by no means uncomfortable or bad.  The trains were all very clean and quick. Its by far, the quickest way to get from coast to coast in Korea.  We saved a lot of money and hassle by having the KTX pass and look forward to coming back to Korea to ride the rails.

The KTX is the best way to travel in Korea, but don't talk.  My boyfriend and I were chatting in low voices, and were were told no talking, at all.   I could understand on a night train, but this was during the day.
Very organized, polite service, clean, good price, I liked it

Took the KTX from seoul to singyeongju. The train is very clean and has spacious leg room. It is very comfortable and does not delay in schedule. The average speed was about 300 km/h. Great way to get around korea.
Great Option for travelers to explore around korea with affordable price and worth choosing to go to BUSAN (only 3 hours).

Probably the best and definitely the fastest way to travel between the cities. The schedule is perfect - KTX trains leave every 10-15 minutes, no delays, and no problems. It takes less than 3 hrs and only 50,000 won to get from Seoul to Busan. The only minus is that you have to book ahead if you're planning to travel on the weekend - tickets are selling like fresh bread!

The KTX is clean, efficient and fairly economical. We traveled from Seoul Station to Busan Station and it took only 2 hours and 30 minutes. We experienced speeds of up to 301 kmh! A wonderful way to travel across South Korea!

I purchased a five day KORAIL pass from www.korail.com and on some of my journeys used it on the KTX, sometimes upgrading to first class for the minimal extra cost of KRW8500.Staff, punctuality,great frequency,seating, trolley service and a quiet environment to watch good scenery skimming by all contribute to an excellent travel experience.Well done KORAIL.  200 per cent better than flying!

I used KTX to go from Gyeongju to Busan. The KTX Gyeongju station is called Shin Gyeongju and is far away from Gyeongju Station. Busan departs from Busan Station. Both stations are relatively new and shiny. This section took less than 30 minutes, giving the impression that Busan and Gyeongju were very close. Busan Station has a lot of cafes and food shops, but Shin Gyeongju Station has only places to eat and souvenir shops, so it was refreshing. All you have to do is reserve your ticket online through KORAIL, sign it at the station counter, and pick it up. It was very easy. There are plenty of taxis outside Shin-Gyeongju Station, and there are buses right in front of the station, so you don't have to worry about that. I took bus number 700 from Bomun Complex to Shin Gyeongju Station, but was told it would take about 50 minutes. However, when I rode, it actually only took about 35 minutes.

I bought the 3 days KR pass travel from seoul to yeosu and back to Yongsan stationi started with online booking and the system is easy and friendly to use. Upon arrival to seoul station, i make payment and collected my KR passWith the KR pass, i made my train booking at the ticketing counterDuring travel day, i missed my train and the ground staff assisted me to make ticket change to the next fleet at no additional charges. Overall, it is a more comfortable experience to travel within korea as compare to bus. Travel and arrival time are accurate and punctual and this allow us to have a better control over the travel journey.
Is a fun filled ride from seoul to busan ! in less than 3 hrs. love the scenery on the way there n is fast traveling 300km/h. No delay and the train ride was stabled. comfy!
i loved using the train to travel all around South Korea. i used the bus to get from ICN to KTX my final destination was Daegu.
I really loved the convenience of schedule and the efficiency of this train. We should have these in North America too. I prefer traveling by train than plane.
It's more comfortable than the Japanese green cars. You can receive services such as water, sweets, eye masks, paper towels, etc. The free butter waffles are delicious!!
I rode from Suwon to Seoul. It took about 20 minutes to get there, which would have taken an hour on the subway. The seats were spacious and comfortable, and the cabin was quiet and very comfortable.

We went out to the countryside and it was easy to get a ticket and only $16 to go to the other side of South Korea.  The bus is very plush.  It fills up and then you must wait for the next one, so buy your ticket in advance if you have a particular time you want to travel, rather than just showing up to get a ticket.

If you take a taxi from Gimpo to Myeong-dong, it may take more than an hour due to traffic congestion. However, if you take this flight, you can arrive at your hotel within an hour of getting off the plane, so it's very comfortable. It's never full. Both the station and the inside of the train are clean. The drawback is that you have to walk a little while connecting at Gimpo Airport or Seoul Station. As a previous person has written, Seoul Station's platform is on the 7th basement floor, so it is more convenient to transfer to the elevator.

I went to Jeonju from Seoul (Yongsan Station). The trip took three and a half hours on the cheapest train, the Mugunghwa (about 1,100 yen). Even though it was a cheap Mugunghwa train, it was a very beautiful train. The ride was also comfortable. However, the water in the toilet wasn't flushing, which was a big problem (sweat).I was really tired on the way home, so I took the KTX. I was able to get home in 2 hours and 10 minutes for about 2100 yen. The seats were good and there was a table. Mugunghwa was good, but KTX was faster and more comfortable.

We used the KTX Train from Busan to Seoul. We booked the ticket on the internet, exactly a month before our travel date. The web site was very easy and quick. We picked the ticket up at the station and the seat number and wagon number were clear. We bought a sort of hot Bento Box at the station and found the platform easily. We boarded the train about 15 minutes before departure and had no problems in finding our seats. We had two large suitcases and there was ample space for luggage at the end of the wagon. The train was clean and the journey very smooth. The stops were well indicated and there was a trolley service with hot and cold drinks and snacks. The seats were comfortable and nice big windows to look at the view. The train departed and arrived exactly on time.

KR pass provides unlimited travel for foreigner for specific number of days. This save me a lot of money and time while travelling from Seoul to and from Busan. The train is very punctual and the interior is very clean and comfortable.

We went from Seoul to Yeosu to attend the World Expo. We booked tickets online about a month ago. It was very convenient to pick up the tickets when we arrived. We almost missed the bus, but the station staff were very enthusiastic to help us. The quality of KTX is really comfortable. The environment, seats and speed can be said to be great value for money.
The KTX is high speed rail as it should be.  They are on schedule right to the second.  Clean, efficient and friendly.  50000 won from Seoul to Busan at 300 km/h,  It is the way to travel in the ROK.

Fast, efficient and on time. Trains were clean and very comfortable. Only advice - BOOK ONLINE IN ADVANCE!!!!!!! We thought it would be easy to just buy a ticket at the station and because we weren't sure what time we would be leaving we just left it, however, I think because it was a Friday afternoon it was very difficult getting a ticket - ended up having to wait 2 hours and be seated on separate carriages - which we didn't mind since we got on the train - but in the future I would always book. KTX staff were very helpful.

We've traveled by KTX from Mokpo to Seoul. It all went smooth, on time and comfortable. And here's a useful tip for those traveling this year; because of 'Visit Korea Year', you can get a 30% discount coupon here: http://english.visitkoreayear.com/english/benefit/benefit_08_01_01.asp. (or simply Google, KTX 30% off)
Traveled from Seoul to Busan, 1st class, good value, on time, spotless, fast, quiet, wifi, just like train travel here in UK!!!!!!

I have used KTX many times, but this time I used it between Seoul and Dongdaegu to see a musical. For the same day ticket, there was only a general room where you couldn't rotate the seat facing the opposite direction of travel, so I took a special room. There are basically no automatic ticket gates, so once you buy your ticket, check the platform number before boarding. The journey to Dongdaegu was about 1 hour and 50 minutes and was very comfortable. I remember it being around 70,000 won (4,900 yen) for the weekend. We felt like traveling that day, but the other passengers were businessmen? Due to the wind, there were many passengers on board alone, and the flight attendants warned us to keep our conversations quiet. Wi-Fi won't connect normally in the KTX seats, so I was told that I should ask the flight attendant and purchase a usage card. In addition, the special room has free water vending machines and snacks. The seats are comfortable and can be rotated to face each other. The price is attractive compared to Japan's Shinkansen, so I would like to use it again.

Is it the Japanese Shinkansen? I used it on a tour, and it was a green car, so it was very spacious and nice. The restroom was a little dirty, but there was a water vending machine. You can get a free bottle of water! It was a short trip from Seoul to Gyeongju, but I think it was much more comfortable than by car. Next time I would like to try Seoul to Busan as well.

We had two trips on the KTX - Seoul to Busan (normal tickets) and Yeosu to Seoul (first class).  The KTX left on time and was fast - up to 300 Klms (190 m) per hour.  Clean and well staffed.  First class has bigger seats and for the price difference worth it if tall like me.   Buy your tickets in advance if you can.

This is a very impressive train service in South Korea.  It is very fast and very clean and convenient.  I recommend buying tickets online or in advance as the trains can fill up quickly, particular on Friday evenings.
Well it cannot be compared to shinkansen of japan, but is the best way to travel long distances.

I took the Saemaul and Mugunghwa trains between Seoul Station and Suwon Station. I was able to reserve my seat at the ticket vending machine, and there was also an English screen, so I was able to purchase my ticket without any difficulty. The seats were spacious, the fare was cheap, and I had a short but comfortable trip. However, it seems to be quite crowded on weekends, so we recommend purchasing tickets early.

Took the KTX several times, this time by myself. For non-Korean speakers, the friendliness of the staff and their English speaking abilities are a huge plus. Travelled first class, worth it in my opinion. The seats are spacious. There are power outlets, and in all carriages you have free wifi. Excellent.

This railway was taken by me quite regularly for business purposes while temporarily assigned to Daegu. I rode this line in excess of eight times and found the atmosphere to be extremely conducive to sleep, the use of laptops, tablets and other portable devices. The staff were deferential, professional and quite accomodating. All seats are assigned and staff go out of their way to ensure you are undisturbed throughout your trip.

You can ride the Shinkansen for less than half the price of Japan's Shinkansen. For long-distance travel, it is more cost-effective than airplanes. However, it shakes a lot and is not as comfortable as the Shinkansen in Japan. If you use it wisely, you can travel around Korea efficiently and cheaply.

I took the KTX round trip from Yeosu Expo to Seoul. Left exactly on-time. Boarding usually starts 15 mins before departure. First Class is wells worth the extra money. Comfy seats with a less crowded cabin. Travel time took 3 hours 27 minutes.... Not bad at all from city center to city center...

I took a local train from Incheon Airport Station (using a T-money card) and a direct train from Seoul Station (purchased a ticket at a cash machine). There was a station staff at the ticket gate who could speak English and Japanese, so I had no trouble getting on and off the train. This is a convenient train that allows you to accurately read the time between Incheon Airport and Seoul Station.
very stable and quiet... the speed shown on the overhead TV, it is just fast and easy, Free Wifi in train, i use google map and see my dot flying on the map... !!

i used KTX and check in in seoul station, then i have time to have my meal, went for Sunday Missal at Myeongdong Cathedral and did my last minute shopping (myeongdong or naedaemun)very expensive compared to commuter ( tripple the price) W11000 for KTX, only W3100 by commuter on airport line.
beats the pants off the trains in the UK for service, price and speed.

Both Seoul and Busan stations have English signs, so I was able to board without getting confused. There are also many places to eat and shops within the station, so I bought some drinks and other items before boarding the train. The inside of the train was comfortable and not much different from the Shinkansen in Japan. By the way, I reserved my seat online and had my ticket issued at the station counter.
Used KTX to get from Seoul to Ulsan and back.  Extremely smooth ride, and very fast.  Best way to get around Korea.
Took the train from Seoul to Yeosu to Expo 2012. Beautiful train, timely, and inexpensive (in 1st class).
Cheap alternative to get around. I just hope that some stairs have escalators.
A 3 hour bus ride was done in 59 minutes!  Inexpensive so would recommend first class!

Booking the tickets are easily done online from anywhere in the world. No problems with collecting the tickets from the ticketing counter at Seoul and Busan Stations. Departure and arrival are on time. The seats are comfortable, beverages and light refreshments are served on board. There is even free WiFi service. Announcements and screen displays are in Korean and English. The staffs are friendly and helpful. I highly recommend it but book a seat for convenience. The extra charge is worth it especially if you plan to board in between terminus or have problem travelling backwards. Well done KoRail.

I went on the KTX when visiting Busan from Seoul. It isn't like an attraction. Its just like an express train that is completely smooth and quiet. You will get to you destination in no time. I had a nice sleep while on it. On board, they sell food and drinks - people come around with carts full of them. But of course you have to pay. But only for the original price you would get them everywhere else. :)

To go to Suwon, I took a train bound for Busan at 8:45am. What's strange is that there are no boarding ticket gates, no ticket inspection inside the train, and no exiting ticket gates. Maybe this is because all seats are reserved, but it was pretty empty, so it doesn't seem like there were as many fraudulent rides as there were on Mugunghwa. The footrest and seat width were sufficient, so I was very comfortable for 30 minutes. At just 350 yen in Japanese yen, this elegance is highly recommended. The car next door has a coffee shop (dining car), so I would like to use it if I ever go to Busan, the last stop.

The Airport bus staff was so unhelpful and unpleasant that we chose the train. Not as good as Hong Kong's but fast, clean and spacious. The buses might take you to your hotel, but they are old,  cluttered, and the traffic can be awful.Take the train!

KTX, the so-called Korean version of the Shinkansen, connects Seoul to Busan. It is famous that ``If you use this, you can travel between Seoul and Busan in about 3 hours'', and this has made it possible to travel around the two cities in a short period of time. Moreover, the price is about 1/3 compared to Japan's Shinkansen. There's no reason not to use this. So here's some more useful information. That's KR Pass. In other words, it is a round trip pass exclusively for foreigners that allows you to ride the KTX, Saemaul, and Mugunghwa trains as you like, regardless of the number of times or sections you travel (however, subways and sightseeing trains are not included). Moreover, there are various types of tickets available, ranging from 1-day tickets to 10-day tickets, depending on the length of your trip. If you are traveling with two or more people, there will be further discounts. You can also take the Saemaul train to the airport and enjoy the view from the train window, and return by KTX. Please search for KR Pass for details.

Went from Busan to Seoul and back, no problems at all! Left on time, arrived on time, comfortable. Machines to book tickets are quite picky with notes and often credit cards don't work, so I suggest booking at the counter if you can.Other than that it is everything a train service should be.

This method of travel beats air travel hands down! The prices for a first class seat are reasonable, and there are no lines for security.  Buying a ticket online, even for an English speaking person, was an easy process. The Seoul Train Station is centrally located and there are taxis aplenty in that area.

I used KTX from Busan Station to Seoul. Since the yen is strong, I decided to take advantage of the special room. It was about 5000 yen per person! cheap. Make a reservation from Japan and receive your ticket before boarding. I got my ticket at Busan Station the day before boarding. The boarding entrance is a little high, so it's a little different from the image of the Japanese Shinkansen. (It's a little inconvenient if you have luggage.) If you choose a special room, you can get newspapers, snacks, and a small bottle of water for free near the boarding entrance. It seemed like the people in the general seats were also taking their snacks with them, so the sweets ran out quickly. The chairs were spacious and comfortable. Wifi is also available. I took the train from Busan at 9am, so I think there was a fairly high occupancy rate and the seats were full. Arrived in Seoul in less than 3 hours. If you leave early in the morning, you may be able to enjoy a late breakfast in Seoul. I ate breakfast in Busan before leaving, so I arrived in Seoul around noon and enjoyed lunch. There is almost no place to store large luggage (large suitcases). There was a little space to put it at the footwell of the seat or behind the seat at the very back of the vehicle. The special room has a lot of legroom, so I wonder if I can put it around my seat. I used a plane to go from Seoul to Busan, but considering various things, KTX might be more convenient. You can get off the plane quickly, and your seat is reserved, so if you get there a little before departure, you'll be on time. I thought it was better than going back and forth to the airport because it was easily accessible from the station.

This was my first time using the Korean High Speed ​​Rail. Up until now, I had only used the subway, which took a long time, but it is now very convenient as it saves time between Seoul and Gimpo Airport. However, if your luggage is heavy, such as a suitcase, you will have to take the escalator underground for a long time, so your luggage will get in the way.
The KTX is a great way to get to other cities in Korea but I am not sure why it is listed as an attraction.  I've taken the KTX many times and it is always on time and convenient.
Fast and efficient service to take me to cities outside Seoul.

My family (of 4) took KTX train to travel between Seoul and Busan. I was warned by my Korean friend that if we want to sit together we should book ahead using the Korail website.The economy class cars are normally full, so the advice about booking ahead was essential if you are travelling in a group.  I booked the train few days beforehand online, printed out the reservation page, went to Seoul Station and recieved the boarding pass at the counter. It was easy.The seats are a bit close together, the arm rest had to be shared. There are vending machines on the cars and toilets were average. We managed get on the train well before the recommended boarding time (15 mins before departure). We walked to the platform almost an hour beforehand and saw our train so we got in the train first. There aren't much luggage space on the train other than the overhead shelves, so I wouldn't recommend carrying large "airport" suitcases.Travelling at top speed of 304km/h, it had WiFi access and food carts. It took about 2 hours and 40 minutes to travel from Seoul to Busan.

The KTX trains are highly recommended. You can get from Seoul to Busan in just under three hours. The journey goes smoothly. On the train, a conductor will always come by where you can buy food and drinks. If possible, you should buy tickets early to ensure you get seats - for example, we couldn't get two consecutive seats when we got to the train station about 40 minutes before departure.

We recently caught the KTX from Seoul to Busan, it was a comfortable ride, we had not booked our seats in advance, rather purchasing on the day as we were not sure if our flight to Incheon international airport would be on time and how long it would take us to get Seoul Station, in fact it took us 2 hours from landing(@1410) to arriving at Seoul station (@1610). Once at Seoul station we tried to purchase our tickets at a ticket machine, there is the option for English, and we were able to get to selecting our tickets but in the end the machine refused to accept our notes, apparently this is a common flaw, and we had to head straight to a ticket office for our purchase.  We went first class on the next available train(@1700) only because we didn't want to wait one hour for the next available second class seats(@1800).On board the KTX to Busan, there is a food cart that comes through selling Korean snacks and drinks, but as we were unfamiliar with Korean food at this stage we did not purchase anything.  The announcements on board are in Korean and English.  Our journey took 2 hrs and 45 minutes, a great travel solution.

The underground rail system is super efficient and speedy. Sometimes a little confusing finding exits but usually someone around to help if you are completely flummoxed.If staying for a few days investigate the T/money card - worked really well for all of us.
Took the KTX from Busan to Seoul in January, excellent train!
I Went to Bubjusa of My.Sokli As Journey for True Awakening with my Dharma friends. Good Memories.

Wonderful connection from Gimpo to Seoul...except long walk in the underground from Gimpo Domestic Airport to board the express train with heavy luggage.  Heard that airport limousine bus was better without the long walk

If you don't make a reservation online in advance, you may not get a seat and may have to stand up and move around. Railway culture has not developed like in Japan, such as special bento boxes. Is it just convenient?
Very nice and clean train, fast, and comparatively cheap if you are used to European prices...
i love this train. the signboard is clear for travellers and it is easily accessed from the airport. It is considered cheap for me as conpared to taking a cab from the airport
i try the busan-seoul trip :) u can find wify, food, clean toilet, nice seat inside the train :) only take 2 hours from busan to seoul..

The train is fast and convenient, if you wanna travel from north to south of korea, ktx is the best choice for you. The price of the ktx might a bit expensive, but if you are a foreigner, go purchase a KR pass(only for foreigner), got 1 day pass, 3 day pass, 5 day and so on. You can travel how many time unlimited within the limit, and the price of Kr pass is really cheap if compare with 1 way pass.

Go to Busan or other terriories just easy and simple, but I recommend you should go online and check for your trip so you might get promotion ticket.The KTX provide you the food (selling), battery chager (fee), clean toilet , WiFI, and everything you need for a short trip.
I went to Seoul to Gyenogju. in just  2.30 hrs at 321km/hr. Amazing. I completly enjoyed spacious seat and no travel tiredness.

Train travel is excellent in Korea.  The KTX pluses are: fast, always on time, able to reserve on-line, only 40 cents if you cancel a trip and comfortable.  The negatives are no self serve kiosks so you have to wait in line to get your actual ticket and the price is moderately expensive.  While cheaper than Japan, it is comparable to Chinese trains, guess this really means they are reasonably priced ($US40 from Seoul to Gumi in first class).  First class offers three seats across vs. four and probably worth the slight extra cost.  You can book on-line at korail.com.

I used this very comfortable method of transportation and I must say that it is very worth it. The trains are really clean and there is the same service you would find on an airline. To travel the route that takes an hour on a bus without stops, it takes forty-five minutes by train. I highly recommend it!
We took the KTX from Seoul Station to Daejeon for a day trip.  It was very easy.  No problems at all!  The trains were clean and comfortable.  We'd definitely ride again.

I'm a huge fan of trains in general, so getting on the ktx was a must for me.  It was comparable to the kodama shinkansen we took in Japan, although the seats in the KTX were smaller (we took the green car in Japan, which is the equivalent of a business/first class).  The KTX is much cheaper than the shinkansen though (even the discount tickets we got for the kodama were comparably more expensive) so if you just want to try a high speed train this may be the one for you!If ever we go back to Korea I'm planning on taking one of the slower trains, the Saemaul(sp?).  It take a little less than twice as long as the KTX, but the seats are supposed to be much nicer, and it's also cheaper than the KTX.If you're coming departing or arriving from Busan station, you might like to try out the Bon Hola cafe.  It's got a great view of the port area and a salad/sashimi buffet for 13000 won each.
Super fast, lots of trains per day to lots of locations, and not too expensive. Snacks and drinks offered for sale on board. I've never had an unpleasant trip on the KTX.

KTX or the Korea Train Express is the fastest connection from Seoul to as far as Busan. Fast, comfortable and definitely a delightful experience, the KTX is South Korea's answer to the bullet trains.  Fare usually from Seoul to Busan (and vice versa) is approximately KRW75,000 for the economy seats. In spite being called economy, the seat is very roomy and comfy, perfect for the 2 and a half hour ride to Seul. The pretty and very poised train stewardesses were a delight to see. They look so pretty-- with their uniform and flower pins in their hair. You also don't have to worry should you get hungry during the trip. The train steward or stewardess usually roll out a tray containing coffee, goodies and even souvenirs available for purchase. I suggest you buy your tickets ahead (go to the Korail Website), especially if your trip will coincide with a major holiday. You have the option of buying economy or VIP tickets from the site and you just have to pay with your credit card. At the station, depending on your point of entry (Incheon International Airport or Gimhae International Airport in Busan), you just need to go to the KTX ticket counter to exchange your online booking to your actual ticket. No need to worry if you will miss your stop, since trains have announcements in English, Japanese, Chinese...and of course, Korean.Definitely, one of our most pleasant experience in South Korea.
We bought tickets from Seoul to Busan on the day of travel without problems. Train ride was quick and quiet. Food and drink trolleys passed by regularly.

If you arrive on a flight around 17:00 in the evening, buses and taxis will be stuck in traffic jams before entering the city. Also, even if you arrive early, South Korea can get very crowded when there are demonstrations or big events, so it's definitely convenient to arrive somewhere by a certain time. However, it may be a bit of a walk, and depending on the location of the hotel, the bus may be convenient, so you need to take that into account. Since it's a new line, no matter which station you get off at, you'll be deep underground. We recommend using different ones depending on the hotel you are staying at, your schedule, and your return flight.
Loved the fact that we could catch a train and travel at a reasonal rate and in good time!

I had never been on a high-speed train before. It was really easy, REALLY fast, and makes only one stop between Seoul and Busan. Don't even think about taking the "regular" train. You save so much time going this way, and it's WAY more comfortable.
u get free WIFI. The agents speak English on the train. There are bathrooms and food for sale. The train literally stops for 2 min. so don't be late!
Mega fast, many locations it goes to now. pretty expensive, a train to busan is similar to the cost of airfare to busan...
Better than flying when going to Busan since the train station in both cities are more central than the airports...it's also cool to see how fast you are going

KTX is marketed as comparable to Japan's Shikansen. NOT! We took the KTX to Shin-Gyeongju to visit Bulguksa and it was just like a regular train. Maybe the better trains run on other lines. The seats face backwards and forwards and the direction cannot be changed. Luckily, we had the forwards facing seats or I would have puked :-( The pitch of the seats was not spacious. Overall, it was kind of pricey for the quality you get.Seoul Station was also very disappointing. Again, cannot be compared with train stations in Japan. In Japan, there are all kinds of shops selling food and stuff. Even department stores! In Seoul, there was only Lotte. The food court was sucky too. Nothing nice to eat/see/buy.
i love travelling in KTX. my first ride was last year (in May) from Busan to Seoul. and this year also the same from Busan to Seoul. the service is superb and on time.
Waiting for the KTX train we tried one of the station restaurants with local cusine. It was way over what we expected
Travel from the North to South if the peninsula in less than 3hours... a bit pricey, but well worth it!
Very comfortable and quickest way to get to different parts of the country! It's more expensive than other trains but it's definitely worth it!

This one is fast.  You can go to the other end of Korea in 3 hours.  There are two other things I love about KTX:  (a) the Seoul KTX station has great restaurants on the upper floors and (b) you can download the KTX app from Apple Appstore and there is no need to physically carry the ticket -- your mobile phone is your ticket (btw, the app is so well made).

When I was traveling to Seoul with my kids and was wondering if there was a place that my kids would enjoy, I remembered KTX. The train is a Shinkansen (bullet train in Japan) that is meant to be used over long distances such as from Seoul to Busan, but you can also buy tickets at the counter to tour the train platform, so on the first day we spent a lot of time looking at the trains at the platform, and the next day we took a short round trip from Seoul to the next city. Last year, I watched a lot of news about KTX accidents, so I was a little reluctant to ride long distances, so I ended up riding short distances, but as long as it's safe, it's a very good option, so I'd like to use it again. I have made many round trips between Seoul and Busan in the past, and I was able to experience the different services and differences from Japanese trains, so I would like to have the opportunity to use them again. You can compare the difference between a special seat and a first class seat, so choosing a different seat for going and returning can be a fun way to travel.

We took the KTX from Seoul to Busan and back. Both trains left on time and arrived on time. The train was very clean and the carriages and seats were very easy to find. We would always choose this train over a plane trip. You can reach your destination in just over 2.5 to 3 hours. The only small drawback: the freely available internet is not always stable.

KTX is a high-speed rail service operated by Korea Railway Corporation. Among many routes, the Gyeongbu Line from Seoul to Busan is the most popular. The train has a maximum operating speed of 300 kilometers per hour and can quickly reach major cities, eliminating the need for cumbersome security checks and waiting when boarding flights. The carriages are divided into economy class with four seats in a row and first class with three seats in a row. The seats are comfortable, the facilities are complete, and the riding experience is excellent. Passengers can book tickets in advance online, and there is no need for security check or ticket check-in when entering the station. The process is simple and user-friendly. Getting on and off the bus was in good order, the cabin environment was quiet, and the overall ride experience was great.

This is a must in Korea, we went from Busan to Seoul on the KTX and it was awesome! The terminal is very well laid out at easy to navigate, and the train is smooth and comfortable. I recommend booking early as they fill up. We did ours 4 days in advance

I really disliked the experience. Honestly, it’s much better to take a bus than the KTX. Since we were in a hurry, we had to take standing seats, and I thought it would at least be manageable—but it was the complete opposite. It was overcrowded, congested, and even hard to breathe. As a foreigner or traveler, you expect at least a basic level of comfort, whether you’re in a seat or even in the standing area.

If you are a nerdy geek like myself and love a good high speed rail network, then this one is a beauty.Its based on the TGV of France and is just as good.It was very easy to buy tickets from Seoul main train station for the jaunt down to Busan. It took just about 2 & a 1/2 hrs for the trip.The pricing was so reasonable, it just made the experience better.Seoul main train station is fairly large, they have a train timetable board and it lets you know what platform its going from and when you can go down to it. They have the writing in both Korean and English so its very user friendly.We waited in the main concourse and then went through to the external waiting area above the platforms. We got our Bimibaps and drinks there for the trip.Boarding the train is easy. Id recommend trying to board first if you have large luggage as bag spots aren't at a premium. We were lucky to get on our carriage 1st and snag some of the limited bag spots. We had reserved our seats which were seated facing backwards for the trip, however, as the carriage wasn't full, we just moved down the carriage a little and got some forward facing spots.The train departed on time and arrived on schedule.The ride was super smooth and we comfortably watched the scenery blast past as we made our way to Busan.Its a jot for us to ride on such great trains as we don't have these high speed trains in Australia. If you want to get around in Korea, these trains are definitely the way to do it.Great service, smooth, clean, cheap and on time. AWESOME.
Comfortable, clean, on time, with good service…. Excellent! However, you must book directly on the Korail website without going through Ninja which doubles the prices.

For travellers visiting Korea for the first time and contemplating booking online for KTX (Korea Rail) between cities, beware the website Rail.Ninja. When researching beforehand, we read some reviews and mistakenly thought somehow it was an affiliated or approved reseller. We therefore booked with Rail.Ninja from Busan to Gyeongju and as we were staying quite near to Busan Station decided to go there to book for the leg between Gyeongju and Seoul and found that we paid almost double for the Busan to Gyeongju leg, and would have done so if we booked for the other leg. You will do well to book with Trip.com as the fare is the same (or slightly less even) as over the counter at the station.
Our trip going to Busan was facilitated by the travel agent. It was a smooth ride.  Lavatories well placed. Platform number indicating no confusion whatsoever.

It was my first family trip in 10 years, especially with my new foreign daughter-in-law, but the train I was supposed to take was suddenly canceled. To purchase this ticket, I bought the ticket a month in advance and made travel plans, but when I came to board the train, I was told that I had to ride the other train in standing room. Moreover, my family paid extra for a special room ticket rather than a regular seat. Normally, in cases like this, I think the rule is to provide a replacement vehicle in place of the accidental train. The actual train ride with standing seats was truly chaotic. Not only did I have to stand all the way from Busan to Seoul, but I was stuck in the narrow space between trains, barely able to move, and every time the train stopped, I had to avoid people getting on and off, making it feel like I was riding a train during a war. It was the worst travel experience I've ever had, and KORAIL's response was so incomprehensible.

I had the pleasure of using Korea's outstanding public transportation. You can easily book economy or first class in advance on your phone, though I recommend first class as it is much roomier and comfortable. If you run out of luck as I did and your timeslots are fully booked, ask the ticket desk for a standing car ticket!

Worst experience on a train ride so far. They made us stand for 2 hours on a KTX train although there were free seats available. Very rude stewardess and ticket officer. We booked standing seats because there were no other seats available for the next four hours- what kind of management is that- definetly can not recommend.

We travelled from Busan to Seoul on the KTX and had a fantastic experience. We booked first class seats, they were incredibly spacious, comfortable, and well worth the upgrade. The extra legroom and plush seating made the ride smooth and relaxing.A welcome snack and bottled water were available during boarding, which was a nice touch and made us feel well taken care of. The cabin was quiet and peaceful, making it easy to unwind, rest, or simply enjoy the scenery as we sped through the countryside.The train was exceptionally clean and well-maintained, with convenient storage areas for luggage and washrooms.Navigating the train station in Busan was also very simple. Just head to the second floor for the KTX departures, and watch the digital screen for your platform number—it’s released about 15 minutes before departure. Once it’s posted, take the stairs or elevator down to your platform and hop on. The whole process was straightforward and stress-free.The train departed and arrived exactly on time, travelling at which a high speed it was impressive how smooth and stable the ride felt.

We took the Seoul to Busan KTX first class booking on the Korail site a week before travel when it was almost full. Booking was easy - if you need to charge phones etc you can choose a seat next to a PowerPoint. There was plenty of luggage space either end of the carriage and racks on top for smaller bags. Seats were spacious though the backrest does not recline. We helped ourselves to Free bottled water and cookies (for first class passengers) though there was a machine for paid food and drinks as well. Screens show approaching stations and there are announcements as well. It was a quiet and comfortable journey. If you’ve travelled JapanRail you will note this is not quite there yet- however you are getting something similar for a lot less money. Recommended.

I've used the KTX twice so far: Seoul -> Busan and then again Busan -> Seoul. On the way there to Busan I took the old "classic" KTX in first class and had a single seat. The legroom was great and the journey was surprisingly quiet. On the return journey I took the new "KTX Cheong-ryong" (also 1st class again). The legroom was a little less, but it was like sitting there on an airplane. Each seat has its own window and a screen with an entertainment system in front of it (this is not available in 2nd class).

From paperless tickets to simply strolling on to the train (no gates barriers to deal with when running late. for the train), this is an amazing service. You can chose a slow ( ie many stops) or fast (only a few stops) service and in both cases it’s superb. Also, ‘first class’ is not that much extra in cost but well worth it .. free water, snacks, better seats with more room. I’d love to be able to take the JTX back to Australia!!!

If traveling to other cities in South Korea, I would recommend the train. It is easy to navigate and less hectic than air travel, plus you get to see the countryside. We took the train from Seoul to Busan and it took less than 3 hours. The ride was comfortable, the trains and train stations clean, and on board crew was friendly and helpful.
Fast, easy, get on from Seoul to Busan. One thing to mention, don’t buy ticket from rail ninja, double the ticket face value
The train was bumpy and service was horrible and wifi claims to be smooth but in reality is horrendous and it sometimes stops

Easy connection from Seoul Station to Dongdaegu Station.  Roughly $35 (US) for the one way trip.  Takes about an hour and a half to get there and is very foreigner friendly with all major signs in English.  Kind and professional staff.

There is little to say.... PERFECT. Very clean, punctual, comfortable and quiet, I have never traveled so well by train. The conductor who turned around and bowed to me every time he exited the carriage made me emotional.

I contacted them at 5 in the morning to modify my train ticket, which they did, even sending me a new ticket.Then 6 hours later they told me that the new ticket was cancelled and back to the initial time as they were not able to modify it, as it was already sold out (despite the fact I could have bought a ticket at 5am as seats were available, which I would have done even if it meant losing money).I couldn't book a flight as tickets were sold out.Yes, from now on, I will definitely fly: same price, quicker and good customer service.

During my trip to South Korea I used KTX fast trains for three routes, the first from Seoul to Busan, the second from Busan to Gyeongju and the third from Gyeongju to Seoul. Good prices. I booked the tickets a month before departure from the official KTX train website, booking from the site was very simple. They never asked us for tickets during the trip. The trains are quite comfortable even if we are not at the level of the Japanese ones. Those traveling with somewhat bulky luggage may find it difficult to find space to store it because the space outside the carriage is not very large.

Just sharing my experience. I have been booking KTX for the past two years. I could book train tickets one month in advance, but usually one week in advance is sufficient to choose the desired timing. Subsequent changes are allowed, use below-mentioned Help webpage for amendments and cancellations info.Do use their official website to get the best pricing. Third parties charges can be exorbitant. I wasn’t aware of this and paid much more for my first two trips because I couldn’t locate KTX official website in a rush. As an example, an economy seat from Seoul to Busan currently costs KRW59,400, while third party service provider may charge 70% more.Official Website: https://www.letskorail.com(Under ‘Travel Path’ selection, if ‘Direct’ selection throws up an error message, do select ‘Transfer’)Help/Info:https://www.letskorail.com/ebizbf/EbizBfHelp.doBefore you board the train, do take note of the train number stated outside the train even though you are on the correct train platform. Sometimes, for efficiency purposes, trains are coupled together for the initial distance and subsequently detached to go on different routes.

WARNING Main reason due writing this is to add to the voices of the scammed: DO NOT BOOK VIA RAIL NINJA. I discovered too late they are scammers who charge up to double the ticket price. They offer you two days before your Trip tickets on other days and times you Never asked for. They just want to get your cancellation fee, nothing else. When I emailed them about it their customer services replied immediately with just bla bla bla, no Problem solution offered. Book directly via KORAIL instead.

We travelled with KTX from Seoul to Busan and back, so I will point out our booking experience and the onboard experience on both journeys as we booked the Economy class to Busan and First class to Seoul.I strongly recommend using KTX in Korea as it takes you from center to center of both cities. Have in mind Incheon airport serving Seoul is 1 hour train ride away from the capital.- my first tip is to AVOID "Rail Ninja" website unless you like paying 50% or more for the same tickets. It usually appears on top of search pages, so doublecheck where you are. The official KTX webpage is letskorail and you have the English option,- book your tickets as early as you have your travel dates. Tickets DO sell fast, despite there are really many trains daily (around 3-4 per hour). We booked ours almost a month before actual travel,- there are NO return tickets - you buy your one way tickets by segment, destination and date you need,- prices are fairly reasonable - cheaper than Japan,- Likewise Japan they also offer the Korail Pass, but Korea is much smaller with two main cities to explore so we didn't find it economical to buy,- Similar to Japan, there are different kinds of bullet trains which vary in speed and number of stations they stop and so does the price. From Seoul to Busan you can travel between 2hrs15min up to 3 hours, so choose which best suites you.- you CANNOT choose your seats, but they're automatically assigned. BEFORE paying doublecheck the assigned seats for your party. We bought ours (party of 3) in the third attempt - in the first attempt we weren't assigned together but were in the same wagon, in the second attempt one seat was even in another wagon.- you can change your bought tickets for a fee (terms apply, read them). If you change online you must first cancel your entire order and then book again. It's easier at the railway station but be prepared for big queues. Considering the above tip we wanted to change our tickets 2 days before travel and there were NO tickets available but the late night (after 10 PM) tickets which didn't suite us.- no need to come earlier than 30 min before departure, as your train wont be even shown on which platform it is. Signposting on railway stations are excellent and you cannot be confused - just read the train number, destination and time. At the same time, officers on duty are very kind and will help you if you need.- Choosing between Economy and First class, I'd advise the First class as the price difference is not like in air industry. The nominal price difference is around 20$ pp, giving you greater comfort.- In Economy you have 4 seats in a row (2 at each side) while in First there are 3 (2 at one side, 1 seat at another). That single seat is for sure the best, but remember you cannot choose it - depends on your luck if you'll get it. Legroom is also bigger in First class.First class seats are in better fabric and wider and guaranteed to be forward oriented.In First class you get salted and sweet small snacks, along with water complimentary. They are at the wagon entrance and you can take as much as you want. None of that in Economy.WiFi is complimentary in both classes and is very good when you have signal. Beware, due to SK topography there're many many tunnels along the route where you loose the signal, so after some time I got bored reconnecting all the time. This applies for both classes.We paid 45 US$ per person for Economy for Seoul - Busan section, and 63 US$ for First class for Busan - Seoul. Price difference is around 40%, but considering the affordable price it wasn't that much.

KTX has its dedicated tracks or platforms in train stations across the Republic of Korea. We bought single-day tickets and took convenient KTX to travel by bullet train, criss-crossing the country. (Letskorail. com is more for people who want to buy multiday flex passes, and watch for sc ams!) The Korea Train Express or KTX runs before 7 a.m. from Seoul to Mokpo in Jeolla province, where the regular sea terminal or ferry to Jeju is also located. (Mugunghwa and S-train special for tourists from Haeundae or Bujeon may have bicycle racks, at least if a cafeteria car is attached.) Paying $50-$80 for an eSIM phone plan is necessary to book tickets online at Korea Railroad Corporation’s website; booking is only possible within 30 days of travel from Mokpo on the Honam line, or from Busan on the Gyeongbu express line. Before Busan’s biennial Wave event— happening until Nov 6, we travelled between this 2nd largest city on the East coast and Seoul. It would have been a 6-day (600 km) ride on the dedicated lanes of a river cycling route; but instead, it lasted less than three hours by train to reach our destination. In that way, we avoided the torrential path of Typhoon Hinnamnor. At the station’s ticket counter, we presented Visa cards to pay Korea Railroad (Korail), which operates the speedrail Korea Train Express (KTX). It can also be reached at (+822) 1544-8545 or 1544-7777 in the morning or noon hour, but with restrictions: especially Sept 8-12 with limited customer service an additional week, due to the annual holiday or Harvest Festival called Chusok. By checking on the overhead boards for the lit-up train number and departure time, it is possible to find the track number for KTX at the far right. Be sure to ask for KTX and carry a little cash ($4,$7,$10 equiv. Korean Won values, accepted by SK’s T-money pass), hopping onto a subway or transit; then between Seoul and Busan, the duration of your train ride will be cut to less than half or 2.5-hour duration (paying less than $60 for an economy KTX seat, e.g., $239 for a family of four). Seats can sell out fast, and there are no night trains past 10:30 pm. In Busan station, take the escalator up one level for ticketing and another level higher to purchase a filling meal for a good price ($10-12 at various restaurants). Tracks below are listed by groupings for regular Munghwa trains or S-trains for tourists. However, speed trains are behind the KTX gate with escalators descending to numbered platforms below, so watch the overhead signage. Even if someone forgets to pack anything, the electronic vending machine in-between KTX cars sells $1 beverages, snacks or $9 flash device and charging by credit card. Reclining row seats and family seating, each with a dining table, is available in economy train cars, listed on the car door and at the top of your KTX ticket. The convenience ontop of speed is unbeatable. Announcements are provided in English, Korean, Japanese and Chinese. Load Google Translate or at least Kakao Maps on your phone/loaner at Incheon Airport, and you’ll be set to travel Korea in a cinch!
