We bought the Korean rail Pass. It was difficult to use as several members of the KTX staff were not familiar with it. Try to make the reservations in advance or travel when there is not a holiday time. During the holidays, the trains are packed and you cannot find a seat. It is efficient. It is not as impressive as the trains in Japan. In addition, the Japan Rail Pass works much better.

I rode from Cheongryangri to Chuncheon. I've been hooked on short trips to South Korea lately, so I have a lot of opportunities to ride the KTX. I rode the ITX Seishun issue. When I boarded the train from Chuncheon, I was struck by the fact that the passengers were sitting normally on the floor. The teacher and students, who appeared to be on a social studies tour, were all sitting on the floor.

South Korea's Shinkansen. The 400km trip from Seoul to Busan costs about 60,000 won (6,000 yen), which feels cheaper than Japan. We have a large number of tickets, but they may be sold out during busy periods.

Travelled on KTX to Pyeongchang and the ride is very smooth and comfortable. The KTX App is available in english and it's easy to search and book for your tickets using the app. Book your tickets earlier if you are travelling during the peak season so that you can get a seat.
tried the train from Seoul to Busan around 330 KM where it was around 2 hours and 40 minutes which was really fast and first class cabins was wonderfull it was nice journey
You can quickly get to the Center. Other forms of transport are difficult to accept because the airport is outside the city.

There are no ticket gates. It may be confusing the first time, but if you ride without purchasing a ticket just because you don't have time, you will be judged as an unauthorized passenger at the ticket inspection and will have to pay more than usual. It's a little difficult to ride because there are steps.

I rode KTX for the first time. The journey from Yongsan Station to Ikusan Station takes approximately 2 hours. The reason why it takes so long to travel considering the distance is that the maximum speed is lower than that of the Shinkansen. The seats were normal and there were few passengers. Since the train departs suddenly without any guidance, we recommend waiting at the platform early.

If you can afford it, we recommend flying first class. You can purchase it from Japan through the KORAIL website. The difference with Japan's Shinkansen trains is that they depart on a reliable basis, so there is no bell and the broadcasts are in Korean, which can be difficult to hear, so it's a good idea to arrive at the station 20 minutes early. At Seoul Station, the first train, you can board the train once the interior has been cleaned, so please sit in the designated seat and wait. First Class has two rows of seats and one row of seats, making it perfect for solo travelers. Enjoy your train journey as there are amenities, newspapers you can read as much as you like, and some cars even have a mini library!

Timetable from Incheon Airport to Seoul Station and return from Seoul Station to Incheon Airport. It's easy to make a reservation through Conest. If you present a voucher at the counter and pay a compensation of 500 won per person, they will give you a transportation card and a receipt. The top of the receipt says seats 13A and 13B of car 5, so make sure you don't get it wrong. You can tell which car number it is by the orange plate. On the way back, I also left my suitcase at Seoul Station for the afternoon flight, went through immigration, and headed to the airport. You can enter from the side of Incheon Airport's immigration gates 2 to 5 and exit immediately, so please experience this stress-free and pleasant experience.
Excellent quality services both on trains and stations, pay attention to seat reservations in the direction of travel
Compare to Japanese train, KTX has room for improvement.  Luggage space is limited, toilet are not clean.

It is popularly nicknamed KTX. It felt like Japan's Shinkansen and limited express combined and divided by two. The vehicle I used had the direction of travel divided into left and right from the center, so please be careful when choosing a seat.

We woke up very early in the morning as we were heading towards Busan. Busan is a city that its located, literally on the lowest bottom of the South Korean Peninsula, meaning it will take a multitude of hours to reach through several types of transportation, except for a plane of course. But by taking a plane, one will miss some of the country side views and diverse cities we went through with the KTx Bullet Train Korea.We bought First Class as we wanted piece and quiet and yes, why not? we wished to experience the full comfort that a Super Train that travels at 300 Km per/hour = 187 miles per/hour, has to offer. We actually checked the speed on the Iphone and screen shot it for your convenience to see.We literally did not noticed when the train took off and it was not too long after that we reached the top speed mentioned above. It was like going on a feather, it felt as we were going 50 km per/hour a soft and unforgettable ride, that at that super fast speed took us to the lowest point of the peninsula in 3 to 4 hours only (counting several stops in some mayor cities along the way).They give you a small treat and cookies in First Class. nothing too fancy, but the seats are bigger, wider and you have lots of leg room with a huge table just for yourself.We did love the ride as we mentioned and we do recommend this experience as a Must See and Try when in Seoul and South Korea in general. First Class cost 80 dollars a piece and per trip, therefore making the math, me and my wife we spent some 300+ US$, almost the same price than going by plane minus the long ride to the airport which is costly (80 US$ a pop and per trip) and minus the hassle and security checks of airports and bumpy rides and nasty small seating space.Totally worth!!!!. Enjoy the pictures we shared for you.

KTX offer a pleasant travel between many cities in Korea. You can fully trust the time schedule and the ride is smooth. WiFi means you can work or leisure without problem. They don’t sell coffee though.

On this service the snack machines seem to take precedence over luggage storage space. The overhead space is very narrow and small so if you have large luggage get in quick because there is hardly any room. We ended up having to spread our luggage out over multiple carriages (and they were still not even in the proper luggage spaces) after being told to move them.

Because of the KTX, I arrived in Seoul from my city in 1 hour and 40 minutes. If I had taken a regular train, it would have taken about 4 hours. However, for those who are riding for the first time, please keep this in mind because the stopping brake sound is loud in the case of KTX-1 or the new Sancheon!!!

Good experience. Made easier by travelling with a local, who can communicate with most of the clerks, though some of them seem able to speak and understand some English. Trains are not as fast as to be worth describing them as bullet trains – 270 km/h is surely fast, but a Japanese Shinkansen is well above 300. Free Wi-fi works pretty well, allowing you to work while travelling. Every now and then the line drops, but it’s enough to re-connect to be back online. Seats are comfortable, each one has power plugs and USB ports to recharge your gadgets. Traveling is a quiet experience, thanks also to the good behavior of the passengers, who mostly refrain from speaking on the phone – less than ever loudly. Definitely much cheaper than the corresponding Shinkansen. A good alternative to flying if you go far. A very good alternative of driving, specially in winter time, when snow may be an unpredictable factor. And it definitely brings you to your destination much faster than a car. And more rested.

It is the fastest and best means of transportation to travel to regional areas such as Busan, Ulsan, Daejeon, and Daegu, and has the advantage of being able to buy food in advance and eat it on the go.

We travel from Incheon Airport and it just takes less than an hour to arrive Seoul town. The ticket is charging 500W deposit and it is refundable. Claim back your deposit when your arrival from the kiosk machine. Comfortable with spacious seats and there is a corner for your luggage. So, sit still and enjoy your view outside.

Used in April 2019. I used it to travel from Busan to Daejeon and from Daejeon to Seoul. The section connecting Seoul and Busan, like Japan's Shinkansen, has many frequent flights and is very convenient. You don't have to book in advance, just go to the station, buy a ticket and hop on. The high frequency of flights makes it convenient for individual travelers without time constraints.

Korea's representative high-speed railway. I always use it well. Compared to Japan, the seats are a bit more uncomfortable and the speed is a bit slower, but the price is much cheaper. It doesn't seem bad to just keep going like this without raising the price.

Travelling from Seoul Station to Busan Station in December 2019 on the first trip of the day was amazing. I slept the whole trip because the ride was very smooth. Took the KTX again two days later, from Busan to Seoul and the train was packed for the afternoon ride. We were given the seats with tables in between and I was able to work on revising our itineraries. Free and fast wifi was also provided on the train ride. Will ride this again. Highly recommended.

Used for sightseeing in Gyeongju on a day trip from Busan. I was able to buy tickets without lining up at Busan Station. It can be purchased online, but payment must be made by credit card. It takes about 30 minutes to get there, but most of it is inside a tunnel. Quite a lot of people come on board. There are no ticket gates at the boarding area, so you can get on even if it's just at the last minute.
Nothing to do with the SNCF. Very clean, fast train and never late. Costs around fifty euros to connect Seoul to Busan. No need to book except during holiday periods

Located near boarding gates 25 and 29 on the 3rd floor of Terminal 1. I've tried it 4 or 5 times now, and it's never been the same kit because it has so much content. Free is good. However, it sometimes takes time, so if you don't have more than 30 minutes to spare, you'll get anxious! You can check your boarding pass and ask the lady wearing a beautiful chimajeogori to decide whether it's OK or not. Available only to foreign passengers. (Most people don't know that it's free.) Even when I went there, it was empty. You can put your baggage inside the chair and enjoy the experience with peace of mind.
very comfortable, fast, silent, very convenient way of paying for travel using an electronic travel card
I used it to travel from Asan to Jeonju. It's fast, but I think the scenery was better on the old railway. I was told that only Korean credit cards can be used when purchasing tickets.

I always use this when going from Incheon Airport to the city. Connecting from Gimpo International Airport, it is a short distance to the city. The prices are low, the safety is good, and there are English and Japanese announcements for foreigners.

It took about 2 hours and 30 minutes to ride the KYX from Seoul to Dongdaegu.I bought a round trip ticket in advance from the KORAIL website.The atmosphere in Daegu was more local than Seoul, which was nice. There is also a subway system, so getting around the city is convenient. The market was also very fun, there was my favorite coffee shop, Sorubin, and I was able to buy a lot of strawberries cheaper than in Japan.

If you don’t like long lines at the airport and all the chaos then I highly recommend taking the KTX Train around Korea. It’s convenient, fast, clean and comfortable and priced just right. KTX is always my first choice ❤️🚄
nice n convenient to other town. ticket easily to purchase at ticket machine, english n chinese version display.

My sister and brother-in-law live in Gwangju City, so when I go to visit them, I use KTX, wonderful, comfortable, clean, punctual, you don't even notice that I've arrived at the destination, traveling on KTX is so good, one day it will exist in Brazil too.

The KTX is just fast, reaching 300kmph speed. Our trip from Seoul to Busan (and the return journey) left in time, calling at the stops as scheduled. Thats about it. Having travelled on the equally fast Eurostar, TGV, ICE and the Renfe trains, I rank KTX below them from the experience viewpoint. Seats are comfy enough but personally the interior could be better. I did not find any buffet car to enjoy the coffee and cakes and the scenery is not that great (of course I do not compare with the likes of the Glacier Express). If you are a train buff, “Man in seat 61” website would give you an insight for comparison.

Prior to my travels, I read that many people suggested to buy tickets beforehand. This depends on your timing of travel. I was easily able to buy tickets minutes prior to boarding the train. The trains are clean and comfortable, and they have electrical outlets and wifi! Also, all announcements are in several languages (Korean, English, Japanese, Chinese), so you are likely to understand and know when it is your time to depart the train. I do recommend taking your own drinks/snacks because there was minimal provided in the train's vending machines.

We took the Express train in First Class from Seoul Station to Busan on a day-trip and found the service to be comfortable with a fast and smooth ride.  2+15 enroute direct or 3+00 on the inner route through Ulsan.  The trains are SPOT-ON-TIME so do not be late.Once caution, there is no bar/snack/restaurant car at all.  There are a few snack/drink machines to purchase something small.  First Class passengers have free cold bottled water available in the F cabins and a very small cookie/pastry snack is offered (2 of each per bag).  So if you travel and want something enroute, be sure to pick it up at the train station before departure.Of note, I strongly recommend F class as the Coach seating is VERY compact and crowded and would be uncomfortable for the average American-Sized passenger.  Even at that, we had trouble finding F seats on some trains even mid-day.Booking on-line was impossible so we just bought our tickets at the station.  The agents have a good command of English. Seats are assigned at purchase.

I've experienced general seats, special seats, and standing seats, and I think it's not a bad option for domestic travel since there are a fair number of flights. It seems to be crowded on weekends, so early reservations are recommended. Considering the price difference, I think the special seats are better. In fact, even in Korea, it seems that the special class seats are filling up. If you have a Korail Pass, you can ride standing seats without a ticket. If you're lucky, you'll be able to sit on a simple folding seat next to the entrance.

Been on our own traveling to and fro Seoul and Busan. The train is well kept and have storage areas for large luggages. Clean toilets and comfortable seats. It takes us nearly  3 hours to go to Busan. There is am space for hand bags and also hanging our coats. The frequency of train is good . From11 am to 16:30, it is nearly every hour or event every 20 min per train. Train leaves punctually, so be at right platform 15 min before. Food bought outside can be consumed at the train.
Peaceful journey, reliable time frame, Less stops. Gives you the opportunity to see the view and take pictures or just sleep.

I took KTX trains all over the country and it made me wish this is what all travel was like. Seoul is an amazing city, but if you want to see the rest of Korea, have no fear of KTX trains or the KTX system.
Clean, on time, comfortable, good services. I have bought both way  ticket online from Pusan to Seoul. I have go to train station in Pusan to change to paper ticket. Every thing is OK.

Booked over the counter and asked for seats near luggage. Were given excellent seats, ample space for luggage and very spacious. If you have large suitcases, take 1st class and ask for seats near luggage.

It is so efficient and punctual! Bear in mind, if you are using KTX in Korea to travel long distance in short time. You have to be in time so that you won't miss your train. The train departs right as scheduled. So, always make sure you'd be at the platform (not waiting area) 15 mins before departure because your train is right there waiting. Board and have some books with you to kill the 2hours++ time. Enjoy your ride!
I got a discount when I showed my Asiana Airlines e-ticket. It's a good idea to write down on a piece of paper what time you want to take the train and show it to them.
Seoul to Busan and I slept through most of it.  Train is fast and quiet.  First class, they give you bottled water and cookies.  Free WiFi.
Fastest way to go to Busan. Clean and spacious inside with free WiFi. Do not expect the bulletin Train like in Japan.

Time taken to travel from one place to another was very fast! Pressure keeps building up in my ears. Instructions were clear. Information on train tickets and at railway stations are easy to understand for english. Train rides are very quiet despite being full. Some places need to book tickets earlier as they run out of seats e.g. from jeonju to busan (through osong) and trains from yongsan to jeonju. Some time slots were already fully booked when we tried to book about 4 days in advance.

It connects Seoul to Busan in 2 hours and 30 minutes with a maximum speed of 305km/h. The model was the French TGV, and the original vehicle was an imported vehicle. Since then, the trains have been domestically produced and are now operating on main routes such as Seoul-Busan, as well as throughout South Korea. This is because South Korea's conventional railway lines are international standard gauge (1.435mm) and can be used as is. The interior of the train is narrow compared to Japan's Shinkansen. By the way, conventional lines in Japan are narrow gauge (1067mm).

Booked the ticket online for Busan to Seoul sector, well in advance. The process was smooth as there were instructions in English. The train was punctual and the compartment was neat and clean. You can pick up packed food from counters at the station. There is a place at the entry point of the compartment where you can store your luggage
We travelled on the KTX service from Seoul to Busan and back. The journey was great, trains were punctual and, with a Korean rail pass, the fares were very reasonable.

I bought a ticket at Seoul Station to go to Suwon Hwaseong Fortress. Since I was able to buy a time slot that I could board immediately, I assumed there would be empty seats since it was a weekday, so I didn't worry about getting a return ticket. However, when I lined up at the ticket office around 17:00, I was told that I could only get tickets for around 7:00 pm, so I ended up leaving without being able to get there. It was a mess as I was heading back to work.

Great counter staff who assisted me even when I asked them which public wifi spot I could tap on, and they got us the front facing seats we wanted. The ride was super comfortable and toilets are decently clean. Definitely will take it again as it is a more convenient alternative to taking airplanes within korea.

I used it when returning from Seoul Station to Incheon Airport.The TV in front of me seemed to be showing information on weather, transportation, sightseeing, gourmet food, etc. in Korean or silently, but I didn't really watch it because I didn't understand Korean. I suddenly heard an English voice, so I looked at the screen and saw a PR video saying that an ancient document had been found showing that Dokdo was Korean territory. Since it is broadcast in English, it is clear that this PR is aimed at foreigners using the airport. People are free to advocate for their country, but I thought it would be inappropriate to show a political PR video in a place like this, so I left Korea with a bad feeling.
South Korea's high-speed train service is excellent. New trains, punctual and with an extremely friendly support team. I recommend.
I used it when I went to Busan. Compared to airplanes, it is cost-effective. The ride is a bit long, but it is convenient as there is no waiting time at the station.

Wow! Talk about efficient! We purchased tickets online to guarantee a seat and exchanged it at Seoul Station for printed tickets. Takes 2 hours to get to Gyeongju (seriously beautiful, btw) and the ride was smooth and comfortable. Our tour in Gyeongju ended a little earlier than anticipated and we were not able to get an earlier ride back to Seoul, they were sold out. We just chilled at Sin Gyeongju station. There's some shops and a couple of restaurants. KTX is awesome!

Great system for the price and quite fast as most have already noted.Also connected to major metro stations for easy access to subways.The average speed is about 300km/h or more between Seoul and Busan.However, there is always a strange slowdown around Sejong City.Probably would cut travel time by ~15m if this slowdown doesn't happen.

I tend to use it often as it is the fastest and most convenient means of transportation to Busan. In the case of 2nd class (general class), the seat spacing is too narrow. Also, it would be nice if the prices were a little cheaper through early bird reservations or promotions.

Fast, clean and efficient way to travel in Korea. Seoul to Daegu is about 2 hours. On a busy weekend, you might want to get a ticket in advance, or else you might end up with standing room only, which means standing in the area between the cars near the bathroom - not a fun way to spend a few hours.

Easy to find the train and the train is clean and the seat is comfortable.Ready your tickets early as i can see the train is fully booked.The ticket is not cheap but for me is an experience because of the movie - Train to Busan.

KTX is the best way to travel long distances in Korea. Its better than by air as it leaves from the middle of Seoul and lands in the middle of your destination in the city you are visiting. Very comfortable and free wi fi. Ideal if travelling to Busan
We bought the KR Pass, 4-day flexible pass. You can book one month in advance in their website.Went to Busan, Daegu, Daejeon and back to Seoul.It convenient, hassle-free and fast.

Traveling with KTX train is always one of my favorite public transport to Busan/Gyeongju and etc, Pros:- The train seating for second class is comfortable, and clean. Staff over the counter is helpful, as i need to change earlier train schedule from Pohang to Busan to avoid long waiting inside the station. They manage to help me change without any problem on the day itself.

Seoul airport is easy to get around. The automatic ticket machines are easy to use but there is a ticket desk near the entrance if you need help. It’s a quick trip into the city and you pay more for reserved seats. I used this service for my first trip and used the standard service for my other 3 trips.
My guess very cheep, in Japan 3-4 times more.also,much easy to use than metro in Korea.In Seoul is for me is nuts.

Korean trains are fast, easy to use, clean and safe. Tickets are bought at the various stations and come complete with train, carriage and seat number all in Korean & English. They run of time so make sure you get to the platform early rather than late.
Best way to get from Incheon Airport to Seoul. The CT pass was great for metro and bus lines. Best one stop mode for traveling to and from airport.
if going between Gimpo and Incheon this is the way to do it. Cheap, fast; not stuck in traffic. Be sure to collect rebate on turning in your ticket card.

Took the KTX train to Busan (no pun intended). The whole experience was like clock work. Tickets were easy to pre-purchase. Only suggestion would be to purchase the food on the platform rather than commercial options in the plaza.
The most convenient way to travel to Busan. Ride first class, free water and some mix nuts and cookies.

Nice and comfortable trains, but not all of them are as fast as the Seoul-Busan line. Actually even not all trains on the Seoul-Busan line are equally fast - at different hours they are different - some stop at more stations, some - at just a few. The Seoul-Jinju line is disappointingly slow - it takes over 3.5 hours to get to the final station, and the distance is actually smaller than Seoul-Busan, where the fastest train needs just over 2 hours to travel the whole distance with speeds of up to 300 km/h

We used the KTX from Seoul to Busan and it was enjoyable.  Get your ticket in advance as you really need to book a seat; it was a popular journey.  It took about two and a half hours.  Take a drink and snacks with you as I don’t think there is a refreshment area on board.

Easy to locate, system efficient. Some confusion on accepting card or cash at ticket counters but easily negated with easy access to atms. Trains on time and clean. Just do not use the toilets - terrible!

If you have taken the train from Seoul Station once or twice, there is no reason to hesitate, but if it is your first time, it would be a good idea to arrive early in advance of the departure time. It would be difficult if something embarrassing happened from the beginning of the trip. Especially for those coming via Seoul subway station, there is more time!!!

I took this train from Seoul Station to Dongdaegu and also to Busan. The entire system is easy to navigate with English signs and announcements. Trains are inexpensive, punctual, and there are places for you to put your luggage when you board. There are plenty of places to buy food in the terminals.

Took KTX from Seoul to Gumi Gimcheon, due to work. Bought VIP seat which is very comfortable and spacious. Snacks and water bottle are provided and the journey took about 1 hr 10mins. In the train you wont feel how fast it was traveling - 300km. Some more there is free WIFI.

You can take the KTX from Seoul Station, Korea's high-speed rail. Since most departures are on time, it is recommended to board in advance before the scheduled departure schedule. Tickets can be purchased at Seoul Station or by installing the KORAIL app.

All seats are reserved, and the seats are very spacious and comfortable. There's a luggage storage area for suitcases, there's no scaffolding to get in the way, there's free Wi-Fi, it's quiet, and you can get to Seoul Station in less than an hour. It's a great deal if you make a reservation at Conest when the won is cheap. However, since there are not many trains, I use the regular subway when I don't have much luggage.
I very much enjoyed my travel from Seoul to Daejeon by KTX. I was seated in the first class which was very comfortable. It felt nice to experience this super fast train.
The trains are just minutes away. The speed is stunning. (300 kmh) The cars are clean comfortable, full Wifi. I recommend everyone to give it a try. Great experience.
I took the KTX to go to Gwangju and... It's the same as in France! Everything is clearly indicated, no worries. I would say it's even better since there is a larger gap between the seats.

We took the KTX from Daegu to Seoul, but this time the one that made several local stops. It took 1 hour and 45’, but better to take the non-stop that takes only 1 hour and 15’. It is definitely faster than regular train and bus.

Since it can run at a maximum speed of 300 km/h, it seems that traveling within Korea has become faster. Since the seats don't rotate, half of the vehicle seems to be facing backwards. Because the car body is small, it is probably narrower than Japan's Shinkansen.

We travelled from Seoul to Busan, thankfully I watched a YouTube video and it gave me the heads up on checking boards and car number, the. Seat number. We travelled first class, which I recommend. You do not notice how fast the train is going.

We used KTX from Busan to Seoul, it was very convenient, fast and cheap. Get your ticket 1-2 hours in advance at the train station ticket office, no need for online booking hassle. The cabin overhead luggage fits up to middle sized checked baggage. Bigger luggage needs to put in between cabins.2 tickets from Busan to Seoul cost us ~110k KRW.Highly recommended.
Fast está way to go Airport and city, quik, efifcient, fast, best way to move, not to many people nows english
It's fast.  It's cheap.  It's Clean.  It's Convenient.  If you need to go is in the path of their tracks, by all means take it.
I took two trips on the KTX, one to Gwangju and the other to Daejeon. It was a very comfortable ride and they were always on time!

Suitable for people traveling outside of Seoul. To be sure, buy through the website. There are many styles and prices. The nest is comfortable. There is room to store large bags, but there are quite a few. Must hurry up first.

Unlike Japan's Shinkansen and China's high-speed trains, the train has a strange structure in which there are seats facing the direction of travel, and seats that always face away from the direction of travel, with seats facing each other in the center of the vehicle. This time I took four seats facing each other for a family, but it can be quite stressful to sit facing someone you don't know. There is WiFi inside the car, but it's a little slow and there's no power supply. Seats facing each other will be discounted and will be slightly cheaper.

I took the night train from Gwangmyeong Station to Busan Station at the fastest possible time, then took a taxi from Busan to my destination, and after paying my respects, I returned to Gwangmyeong Station by the first car in the morning and went to work. It is a very convenient means of transportation for people who lead busy lives.

Took this train from Seoul to Busan and vice versa. Ticketing was easy, although you might find the queue a little long if you decide to buy at the station. Not the most modern train, but fast, clean and comfortable. Definitely a more comfortable choice for traveling between the two cities (compared to airplane).
the train was from Seoul to Busan took about 2 hours but the train was fast and the riding was smooth

The good thing about the KTX is that its really easy to use. If you travel outside of peak days then you should have no trouble just show up at the station, buy your tickets and travel with the train. Worked like a charm for me landing at Incheon early, taking the Arex to Seoul station and just buy tickets. Grabbed a quick lunch and went to Busan. The train will depart at its scheduled time and it will be at the terminal stations 30 min before departure. Its the best way to get between major cities in Korea.I used the KTX for a round trip to Busan from Seoul.I thought I should go with first class to busan and back since Im on vacation and not on a budget. The train was easy to find and you just board the car and all is good for a relaxing ride to Busan... or that was what I thought.Its when you enter the train you realize that the standard on this train is sub par even on first class. The first class car was very shabby. the seats where torn and I found stains on them. Well some wear and tear should be expected but this was a bit too much when traveling on first class. When the train departed it was more or less full and thats when I saw the second drawback with first class on KTX. It started to feel like a commuter trains. People where walking back and forth all the time and others where switching seat after each station. There were also people standing in the area between cars blocking passage to toilette etc. Back from Busan to Seoul it was even worse and I had people standing right next to me in the first class car between some stations.I assume those were standing ticket passenger but why are they allowed into first class cars? Basically I bought first class tickets and it felt like I was riding a glorified subway train. The Arex Express trains turned out to be better than the KTX first class and the KTX is nothing even close to the Shinkansen.If you travel with the KTX dont bother with First class since you pay extra only to get a wider seat and a free bottle of water (which you cant get to because of people blocking the passage). Dont expect a calm and relaxing trip and prepare to have people walking by you constantly. Basically hope for window seat, put on some really good ANC headsets, try to ignore all the fuzz going on around you and pray you dont have to use the toilette.
We used the KTX a couple of times and in overall very satisfied with it. Be aware that if you try to get a last minute tickets you might not find it on rush hour.

If you're travelling with family with kids and luggages, this is the best option for you. It's fast, cheaper than taxi and easy. If you took Korean Air airline then you will get additional discount. Kids below 3 ride for free but they won't get a seat. KTX brings you from airport to Seoul Station which is 5 mins taxi away from Myeongdong.
Trains were on time and comfortable. We had friends who ordered our tickets so I can't say anything on that process, but finding the train and the everything was very simple.
We took the KTX from Seoul to Busan , inside is clean and comfortable and we are given some refreshment on board have really enjoy our 2.5 hour trip
We took the train to Busan. It was uncomplicated and there was a helping railway official available for every wagon.

KTX is one of the best train services in the world. They are punctual (not as good as Japenese), very comfortable, and very fast! I travelled in this train thrice from and to Seoul. Even when the train goest at 300 km/h, one will never notice the speed or jerk. It's very smooth. They do announce the stations in English so the tourists won't miss it. Travelling on this train is a must while in South Korea.

The KTX is an affordable and fast way to head down to the nether regions of Korea on the weekends. Here are some tips for getting around there. If you have a long layover, I would recommend using the coin operated lockers in the Lotte Supermarket next door. They have return coin lockers of various sizes and if your luggage doesn't fit, you can have the customer service desk store it away in the back room. They do it for shoppers so you should be polite to buy something small in the store before you retrieve your bags.Eateries in the train mall are limited by your typical franchises, many overpriced like the Paris Baquette, and Jason Krazur? bakeries- so expensive for some buns! Coffee is over priced except for in the fast food chains but then I've been told coffee here are very low quality and suspicious healthwise. Korean coffee is expensive because traditional people here sold coffee in salons where you paid for the place to meet people at a private table, not the coffee itself. Korean's don't meet people in their homes usually as homes are very small. I would shop for food to take with you at the Lotte Supermarket and eat on the train. Don't forget to get some tea or bottled water and maybe some cheaper pizza to go.Weekend rates (Fri-Sun) are 15% more than weekday rates. Tickets are a little difficult to read so be sure you know your train car and seat number in advance... And be on board 5 minutes before departure as last minute rush makes it crazy onboard at the last minute. Warning on seats though, if you are a large or tall foreigner, get the larger 1st class seats. You will be so uncomfortable in the regular cars as they are made for Korean-sized folks.

Took the KTX with my friend from Busan to Seoul last Feb 9.  Although there was a slight delay on arriving to Seoul for about 5 minutes, it was still fairly a comfortable ride for us.Refreshments were offered from time to time so if in case we get hungry, then we can just buy from the crew.All in all, we would not hesitate to take this train again given that the normal 6 hours or more ride from Busan to Seoul became 3 hours only.

We took the KTX train from Seoul to Ulsan January 20. We booked first class seats early as it was the lunar new year weekend, and seat were limited: good choice. The Korean staff were very respectful and helpful, bowing as they entered and left our train car. The total fare for two was around $100 USD. Top speed was around 200mph, and so smooth!Although the subway links with the KTX at the Seoul station, too many steps are involved if you have large suitcases, as we did. We took a taxi from the Metro hotel for about $5 and were dropped at the station entrance where sloped ramps lead right to the check-in/waiting area.We reserved and paid online, and picked up our tickets at the Korail  Dorasan Station near the DMZ to avoid the lines in Seoul: how convenient!

The most effective way to travel between SK's major cities.  It is also very cheap offering both economy and "first class" cabins.  It is also very clean and safe and services are very regular.  Ie between Seoul and Busan every 10 - 15 minutes depending upon the time of day.  Much faster than flying, and alot cheaper.

I've never seen a train more than 5 minutes off schedule, though I've heard of 10 minutes and that's considered a tragedy. The ride is smooth, the climate is controlled well, and the service carts come by regularly. Pay attention, though, because you're first mistake may be to end up 60km away from where you wanted to be.
It's fast and the service is good. You can get wifi on the train and enjoy a nap, but the price is a bit expensive.

We used the discount for foreigners to book tickets, but due to delays we could not complete the ticket collection within the time limit, so we had to send an e-mail to KTX 5 minutes before the end of office hours. When we arrived at KTX's office more than an hour after get off work, only the person on duty was left, and he actually asked us to answer the phone immediately. I was confused at first. How could there be a phone call? The service staff on the other end of the phone asked us to come back before departure to pick up the tickets and pay. We can still get 30% off the price, which is great! Also, there is no ticket inspection gate when taking KTX in South Korea. You can just get on the bus. The strange thing is that no one comes to check the ticket on the bus.

One of the easiest and inexpensive ways to see different parts of South Korea. If you have a short trip purchase a standing ticket for super cheap fares. The Bullet train from Seoul Station to Busan is only a short 3 and a half hour trip trip which would take about 6 hours via bus or regular train

Considering the outrageous cost of their neighbour's bullet trains in Japan, the KTX is a marvel.  It might not be breaking any speed records but it is very fast, very regular and extremely good value.  TIP:  If you are travelling in a group of 4, get a Korea person to use the Korea site to book you a group of 4 seats and save around 30%!!  For some reason this is not available on the English page.

If there is any dislike at all it is that the network is not extensive enough. We were trying to go to Andong from Gyeongju but cancel the idea after finding out that the KTX does not serve Andong.The KTX we experienced was fresh, onetime and convenient. To communicate try asking the Info desk to help write your destination and time of travel in Korean so you can show the sales person at the ticket counter.
i recommend public transportation for any travel in korea.  KTX is fast, safe.  Easy to use.  You can check schedule, purchase tickets @ their web site korail.com

KTX is Korea's express train and is especially worth it if you want to travel long distances (such as Seoul - Busan). You have to take your tickets before the start of the journey and seats will be assigned. These are nice and wide and can be set very low so that you can sleep comfortably. The journeys are quite cheap, but to be on the safe side you should always look at the many low-cost airlines, some of which offer even cheaper connections.
On time, comfortable, interesting information about speed etc.. Goes up to 400k/h..
Fast!! Highly recommended, and great value for money. No ear pressure problems, even in tunnels, due to sophisticated pressure systems. Loved it!

There could be one or two more trains per day at the smaller stations, but for the price, I am not going to complain too loudly.Treat yourself and go first class....Wifi was there, but I couldn't get online....All in all, a decent train at an incredible price.
Very fast and efficient way to see the country.  Trains are on time and clean but there is not much room for storing large cases.

It is an essential vehicle for traveling within Korea, especially between Seoul and Busan. If you plan on riding a certain amount, the KR Pass, which allows you to ride as much as you like, is a good deal. You can even get a moto on a simple round trip between Seoul and Busan. You can easily purchase it on the KORAIL website, and if you bring the printed voucher to the counter, it will be immediately exchanged for the actual KR Pass, and there is no charge for seat selection. Regular KTX seats are fixed, so you may be seated on the opposite side of the train (in that case, there will be a slight discount). All seats on KTX-Sancheon face the direction of travel, so you won't be seated on the opposite side. Although the number of trains is small, there are marks on the timetable, so if you want to ride, we recommend KTX-Yamakawa.

..and comfortable However, you should seek tickets beforehand on national holidays or weekends. They are almost always fully booked. The website also gives foreigners many discounts, happy rail is one of them.

When in Korea on bussiness, I travel extensively between Busan and Seoul... Before KTX you had to fly between the two cities and between taxi cabs, security lines, weather delay's luggage, etc. etc. the trip took up the entire day and also cost an arm and a leg.  Now for a fraction of the cost you can transverse the entire country in just a few hrs in exceptional  " No Hassle" comfort.KTX is so popular in Korea that there is a train leaving on the Seoul  / Busan route every 30 minutes like clockwork 7 days a week 365 days a year regardless of weather conditions, I can't say enough about about it. The online reservation process is as slick and painless as it possibly gets... you pay online and can cancel for free up to the day of travel, and for 400 won, ( aprox 35 cents US) up to 1 hr before travel which is unheard of anywhere else I have traveled in the world. Also free Wi Fi in all cars.The cost is about $50 - $55 each way for the regular cars, I always opt for the first class cars for aprox $20 - $25 more where you get bigger seats, more leg room, free snacks, and a much quieter trip. *** note they keep it quiet as a church mouse in first class, if you need to have a lengthly verbal cell phone conversation they will often ask you to to do so in the corridor between cars.A tip for foreigin nationals... you can often find discounts for foreigners of up to 30% off on the various  "Visit Korea" tourism sites, just click on the KTX icon... the discounts are not good during holiday periods and you often have to look for them carefully on the various websites, rarely are they on the first page so scroll down...

KTX trips are always quick and efficient. The train will arrive when stated and will depart when stated. The trains are clean, food and drink are available for purchase on board, some seating areas can even be manipulated to allow four travellers to sit facing each other. Can't really go wrong, unless you're looking for a cheaper option, KTX is great!

I took KTX from Seoul-Busan-Seoul in Dec 2011. The KTX arrives and departs at Seoul Station in Seoul. It costs around 42,000-45,000 Won for each trip. And it takes 3 hours each trip. Very comfy. I has bicycle storage and if you have big luggage you can store it near the entrance/exit door. They sell snacks/drinks/meals during the trip. Don't worry if you don't have time buying food or drink before departing.Note that the KTX is very on time. The train leaves at exact time as schedule unless there's something major going on.

I used it for a round trip from Seoul to Busan. Reserve the KTX 30% discount ticket for foreigners in advance from Japan, which is available until the end of December 2012. I went to the designated counter, but no one seemed to know me, so I had a hard time getting through. However, I called KORAIL Tourism Development and was able to purchase it without any problems. KTX does not have a ticket gate. The inside of the train is small, and the seats are fixed (TGV specifications), so don't forget to request a seat in the direction of travel.

Not enough space to put bulky luggages. KTX leave on time so don't be late. You can change the timing of the train tickets if you arrive too early at the station. Although it's pricy, it's worth it as it save alot of time. You can reserve the tickets online, and the credit card will only be charged when the tickets are issued in Korea. So you can reserve and cancel the online reservation anytime. Train is very clean and quiet. You can ask for middle seat (seat for 4 pax) or sear for 2 pax (regular seat)

I  really love this train as it makes Korea a smaller country by connecting Seoul and Busan within 2.5 hrs. It is reasonably comfortable although to save space the leg room and seat space has been compromised. Its my only dislike. Snack are available to purchase and one does not feel the 300km/hr that you are travelling.

The ``Shinkansen'' runs from Seoul to various regions in Korea. It takes about 3 hours to reach Busan. If you are a foreigner, you can purchase a KR Pass on the Korean National Railways website before leaving the country, which will give you unlimited rides on all lines.
The train, KTX is fast and convenience. It is not too new but not too old. Seats on first class are huge but not big space for suitcases. Accurate timing.

Not sure how this is an "attraction" but anyway, the KTX is a great way to travel around Korea -- only 90 minutes to Daejon, only 2 1/2 hours to get all the way across the country to Busan?  Why would you fly?

There weren't many people riding from Incheon, and the price was good. However, there is a long distance from the time you get off the plane to the boarding area. The platform was deserted and there were no station staff, so I was worried because I couldn't ask if this train was okay, but in the end it was fine. You will be able to see the scenery as you will be on the ground halfway.
We rode the KTX from Busan to Seoul and vice versa. Its very comfortable. They have discounted rate for those in tight budget. Its very accessible and the train is very clean.
I only used one station from Busan as an experience. Regular seats are a bit cramped, special seats are luxurious but still expensive, and if you have time, Saemaeul and Mugunghwa are more spacious!

Did the internet booking for our day trip from Seoul to Gyeongju.  Woke up too early so we decided to take a KTX much earlier one than the one we'd booked.  Ticketing staff at the Seoul station was very pleasant and changed our tickets in no time.  Took the first class seats as I wanted my old mother enjoys more leg rooms and comforts.  Coaches were clean and the very polite cabin attendant provided bottles of mineral water, biscuits, newspapers were given along the way.  Did not feel that KTX was going very fast (at least compared with Sinkansen in Japan) but it was one smooth ride!  There have been significant improvement in terms of maintenance, cleanliness, and overall services during the past few years.  Toilets were clean.  Loved the train ride.  Have to say, however, the new Gyeongju station is in the middle of nowhere.  We were welcome by strong stench of manures -- It was not a pleasant welcome to this magical place with rich history while it was a good reminder that Korea is well-known for livestock and agriculture.  The new Gyeongju station building was nice, clean but deserted.  Tourist information counter was closed and there was no maps or information available.  So those who arrive early in the morning, make sure you'd have some info ready.  For those who love sweet-potatoes, buy some sweet potato sweets at a small shop just going down to platforms at KTX Seoul Station.  It smells divine, so you can't miss it. --They were really lovely so much so that we bought some more upon our arrival back at Seoul in the evening.

We took the KTX train to Daegue and it was clean, fast and efficient. For this some  600 kilometre journey it only cost approxinately $20 per person. A tip is if there are four of you you can ask for discount as there are four seats together facing each other with a table in some of the carriages which are at a discount. Book early to get a good price and a seat.
korea's bullet train. took me 2 hours to get from seoul to singyeonju (gyeonju). cost was ~45 US
The ride were so smooth and fast, and so comfortable that you hardly noticed that you were actually on a train!

It is a ok way to travel, the train speed was most of the time about 270 km and very few times it went up to 305 km, but I can recomend it even though they say the train can go up 350 km per hour.The compartment was nice and clean and so where the restrooms.

For around 50,000 won you can travel the Seoul Busan route in 160 minutes with the KTX. The train runs very frequently but is usually quite fully booked. Therefore buy tickets beforehand. You can also reserve tickets online. The train has the technology of the French teacher TGV. It has (slow) WIFI but no sockets for computers? Otherwise the train is very comfortable. If you want to travel the route cheaper, you can either take the slow train or the bus. It takes about 4 hours and costs half as much
The trains are very clean and it is just a good way of travling from Seoul to Busan. For sure you can go to more places but I have only used the KTX from Seoul to Busan. Ticket price is OK.

The KTX is Korea's high-speed train, with which you can travel from Busan to Seoul in 3 hours, for example. A new track was built especially for the KTX, which can travel through the mountains using many tunnels and therefore the shortest route. Unfortunately, the pressure on the ears is quite strong when you drive in and out of the tunnels. On a longer route this can be quite unpleasant. Unfortunately, you can see less of the land from the KTX than from the other trains.
speed is 300 km per hour ., train is old and dirty

Korean version of Shinkansen "KTX". It connects cities such as Seoul, Busan, Daegu, and Gyeongju at high speed. It is convenient because there are many trains and the fares are cheap. There are many counters that speak both Japanese and English, so if you look at the crowd monitors (located at each counter) and let them know, it won't be difficult to buy a ticket. Facilities are divided into 1st and 2nd class. 1st class has seats in rows 1 and 2 and is comfortable, while 2nd class has seats in rows 2 and 2 that cannot be changed and is tight, and some seats have seats facing the opposite direction. Places that cannot be reached by KTX can be reached by the conventional lines Saemaeul and Mugunghwa. Night trains also run, so you'll be able to travel effectively.

Not sure why is a mode of transportation is listed as one of the places to visit in Seoul but I did try it for my journey from Busan to Seoul. A pretty fast and cheap way to travel as compared to the taking the flight. For a normal train ride, the journey takes about 5-6 hours whereas for KRX it took less than 2.5 hours. We took the first class seats as was only USD15-20 extra as compared to the next class seats. The train was punctual with comfy and spacious seats. The coaches are clean and well-maintained. For first class passengers, the fare included a bottle of mineral water and a packet of biscuits. A great way to see parts of Korea though we were asleep most of the time. You can book your tickets online.

I rode a high-speed train for the first time in August. Are you often late? There was a rumor, but there was no such thing and we departed on time. Announcements are also in Japanese, so even beginners can easily get on board. The ride comfort was almost the same as the Narita Express and Skyliner. Transferring at Seoul Station takes time and may be inconvenient for those with a lot of luggage. Overall, I thought the limousine bus was better.

I recently flew into Seoul Incheon Airport (International) and found that a connecting flight was not available that evening to Busan unless I was willing to transfer to the domestic airport 45 mintues away and wait several hours.  I looked into the KTX and found it to be a good alternative.  Although it requires a transfer from Incheon to the Seoul KTx station, it takes no more time than traveling to the other airport.  I was able to book a 1st class seat in advance (reserved) and easilty navigated the train station.  (There are restaurants in the building if you are hungry.)  Once onboard, there was a free water machine between cars and a person selling snacks came through the car several times.  The train stops 4-5 times between Seoul and Busan but the trip only took 2.5 hours.  The seats were comfortable, the train was quiet, and the trip flew by...literally.

Although it is a new high-speed railway that was built at the end of last year, it is very easy to use and convenient. It's fast after all! Of course, you can take the subway from the airport to central Seoul, but it takes a long time. In that respect, the high-speed train KTX is very useful because you can get to Hongik University or Seoul Station in a short time with just one train. If you are in Myeong-dong, just transfer to Line 2 from Hongdae-mae. I think it's good because it's new, the car is clean, and the price is not too high. If there is a drawback, it is that it is a little far from the platform at the airport. However, other subways are also far away, so it may not be that different. . Personally, I will definitely use KTX every time from now on.

We took the KTX from Seoul to Singyeongju (to the city of Gyeongju).  I love riding trains so was really looking forward to it. The cars are spacious and clean and have nice pull out trays. We had our kids (6 and 8) with us and this was their first international train ride. They loved it. They both said they preferred it over riding a plane because the loading was much quicker and less troublesome than a plane and they could look out the window as they went. The train goes something crazy fast - like 200 kph. The downside is that the train ride was only two hours! We rode it from Gyeongju to Busan (the Saemul, slower version)  and enjoyed it just as much.  We would totally do this again and only wish it went even more places.

I took the KTX from Ulsan Station, which is located above Busan, to Gumi Station. Both stations are new, having been built for about a year, but they are quite far from the downtown area and there is nothing around them, so they are not suitable for travelers to use as intermediate stations between Seoul and Busan. Also, although the train is made up of 18 cars, the distance between the seats is narrow, making it easier to travel by bus over long distances.

It's cheaper than Japan's Shinkansen. I used it on my way home, and the journey between Daegu and Seoul was about 1 hour and 45 minutes and cost 41,100 won. The outbound trip took about 5 hours and cost 34,100 won by express bus between Incheon and Daegu without any problems such as traffic jams. I think it would have been better to use KTX for both round trips. However, there were no ticket gates or inspections, so what does that mean? ?

I purchased an unlimited ride pass from the KORAIL website in Japan in advance and used it. Busan → Haeundae Haeundae → Gyeongju New Gyeongju → Seoul Seoul ⇔ Suwon Seoul → Busan Busan → Gupo It costs about 6,500 yen for 3 days!! KTX is fast, but the seats are narrow. It gets tiring because you can't bend it down very much, but Saemaeul Mugunghwa can recline quite a bit and the seat pitch is wide so it was comfortable ◎Please experience it all ☆
It is a railway that represents Korea. It runs parallel to Seoul Metro from Seoul Station to Cheonan. It is a means of transportation for Koreans.

KTX is also known as the Korean Shinkansen, but there are parts that run on dedicated tracks and parts that run on conventional lines. This is because the conventional lines in South Korea are standard gauge, which is fundamentally different from Shinkansen trains in Japan and Taiwan, which run on completely separate routes. So, KTX and Saemaeul Mugunghwa leave from the same station at Seoul Station. Although it seems to be considerably more expensive than the conventional express train, transportation fares in Korea are already very low, so for Japanese people it doesn't matter at all (in fact, it feels cheap). The most important thing to be aware of on KTX is that the seats are fixed in direction, so half are seats facing the direction of travel and half are seats facing the opposite direction. You can specify this at vending machines at stations (English is available), so I think it is better for Japanese people to purchase from vending machines rather than at the counter. This seems to be unpopular in China as well, but Westerners don't seem to mind, and Western-made trains often have it. It may be a cultural difference, but Koreans also seem to like seats that face forward, and I feel like those seats sell better.

South Korea's KTX is Japan's equivalent of the Shinkansen, and it connects major cities such as Seoul, Busan, and Mokpo, and although the speed is instantaneous between Seoul and Busan, it can reach speeds of 300 km/h, which is faster than the Shinkansen. The journey from Busan to Seoul used to be on conventional railway lines, but now the train will run entirely on high-speed rail via Gyeongju, further shortening the journey time.

I went back and forth from Seoul to Busan using KRPASS, which is sold only to foreigners. KRPASS is a free ticket that allows unlimited rides on KORAIL in Korea, and when I bought it, it cost about 7,500 yen in Japanese yen for 3 days. I used a regular KTX car on the way there, and a special class car on the way back, so I will write about the difference from now on. First of all, it's a regular car, but the seats are arranged in groups, so some seats face backwards, and the recline doesn't work. The seats are also small and uncomfortable. However, the special class seats are as spacious and reclining as Japanese green cars, and come with free bottled water and snacks. It also comes with audio so you can enjoy your stay more comfortably. If you use KRPASS, you can purchase this special upgrade at half price. I recommend it if you are in special class with KRPASS.

KTX is the Korean version of the Shinkansen. However, compared to Japan, transportation costs are cheaper in Korea, so KTX is also affordable. For travelers traveling particularly long distances, we recommend the KR PASS (Korean Railway Unlimited Pass for Travelers). According to the information at the time I used it, I was able to buy special seats for half the regular price. I also exchanged tickets and reserved seats at Incheon Airport, and was also able to buy a bus from Incheon Airport to Seoul Station at a discounted rate at the same counter. The most important thing is ride comfort, but I think it's comfortable. In the special seats, there was a TV in front of me, but the current speed was displayed in the corner of the screen. Even when I exceeded 300km, I didn't feel much shaking.

I think you'll probably get a better deal if you buy tickets online while you're in Japan. I realized I couldn't buy it the day before my departure, so I bought it locally. Still cheap! Although it was about the time between Tokyo and Osaka, it was almost half the price. Even the special room was cheap, so I didn't hesitate to get the special room. Actually, I didn't think about it because I had the impression that the general seats were small. Bottles of mineral water were distributed on the way there. Self-service on the way back ^^; There are no ticket gates like in Japan, but there are signs on the ground that say ``trust''. you” (lol) There was no ticket check and it was really about the ride. The ride was quite comfortable and it wasn't dirty. The scenery was the same as in Japan, or rather, it was more rural than Japan, so I was honestly bored. I was able to use the PC without having to pay anything. Security-wise I was worried about this, so I didn't look at any sites that required me to enter a password.My husband bought lunch boxes at the shop corner on the train.The coffee here was always Korean-style and weak, but I thought again that Japan is way too expensive.

Korean is written in kanji, so if you understand it, you'll be surprised how easy it is to read it. However, buying tickets is quite complicated. I think it would be faster to ask the station staff. Please be careful as 500 won will be taken as a deposit. Don't forget to come back after the ride! !

To go to Busan with a friend from Cheongju, I took a bus to Daejeon and took the KTX. Bus service is convenient in Korea, but I wanted to experience the KTX, so I took the KTX, but it costs about half the price of the Shinkansen.The train between Seoul and Busan connects Tokyo in about 2 and a half hours, so is it about the same time as between Tokyo and Osaka? I enjoyed traveling on the KR, which was completely different from the Seoul subway. The station was also nice and I took many commemorative photos. In-house sales are the same as the Shinkansen, and I thought it would be nice to travel on the KR instead of just the bus once in a while.

This time I traveled to South Korea and rode the Korean Shinkansen (KTX) from Busan to Seoul. It took about 3 hours from Busan Station to Seoul Station, and the view from the train window was good, comparable to the Shinkansen in Japan. It seems to be running on some conventional lines. There was no ticket inspection on the platform or inside the car. I wonder if it's okay.

I used KTX between Busan and Seoul. Travel time: 2 hours 50 minutes. If you decide to use it, we recommend a special room (green car, around 5000 yen one way)! I've never used the general seats, but they seem to have a bad reputation for being quite small. The special room allows you to stretch out your legs, the seats are quite spacious, and you can get free butter cookies, mineral water, and candy. However, if you don't pick it up as soon as you get on board, there may not be any, so be quick. I would like to use it again.

– We travelled by the Shinkansen “Bullet” Train between the cities of Tokyo Kyoto Hiroshima and Osaka – all in Green Class – equivalent to business class – all departed on time from carriage markers on the dedicated platforms – seated in a 2 x2 seating – big comfy seats with decent legroom – there were overhead storage spaces that could accommodate a medium suitcase and pre-bookable pre-paid space at the rear of the carriage for oversized cases – we had sent our larger suitcase by courier onto to our last hotel and therefore only had carry-on sized cases which presented no difficulties - whilst travelling at speed the ride was smooth and quiet – the carriages were never full – the toilets were clean – there was a trolley service and refuse collection – but on each of journeys we had bought snacks from the station shops – much higher quality than you find at UK stations with a greater choice – approaching stations you were encouraged to get ready for disembarkation well before we stopped as there was not much time to get off and on – announcements were given in English and Japanese and all the signing was dual language – the journeys were unremarkable – and we took little notice of the passing landscape except when Mount Fuji came into view – travelling by Shinkansen trains makes large areas of Japan easily accessible and given the central location of the stations a more convenient option to flying or travelling by road.

Positive aspects: punctuality, convenience of the stations, speed (still superior to the Frecciarossa by only 20 km/h). Negative aspects: high prices even with advance bookings, impossibility of doing everything online without printing a ticket at the station, terrible Wi Fi. I expected much better.
Impressive, shiny weather, requires a ticket, very frequent like an underground, operated for more than 15 years, quite comfortable, I have measured 297km/h speed by iPhone.

I was only in Tokyo for 2 days but I had to try the Bullet Train. I decided to go to Nagoya - only because that was the first big station at a reasonable distance, because all I was doing was coming straight back. I chose the Green Car which was quite plush and had plenty of leg room. The Ordinary Car looked quite spacious too. You don’t really get the full impact of the speed while on board although you do when it goes past you in a station. It is expensive (about £77 each way for me) but it’s definitely a “bucket-list” thing to do.

Attention. Unable to change your reservation. The staff at the station speak little or no English. We paid twice because it was impossible to change the schedule. You have to pay for your train plus the reservation. Don't forget your meal to buy before going up because there are only salty peanut cakes or cheese in cubes, ice cream in pots. Not really Japanese food and no choice. Otherwise train comparable to the TGV. Nothing exceptional! There are other fast and very comfortable trains in Japan. The reputation of this train is overrated.

Travelled on the Nozomi Shinkansen between Tokyo and Kyoto and again between Kyoto and Shin Osaka. To achieve the maximum speed of 300 kph, you have to travel between Osaka and Hiroshima but it was still very very quick and smooth. Most coaches are reserved but there are 2 unreserved coaches for passengers without reservations.We were lucky and got an uninterrupted view of Mount Fuji around 45 minutes from Tokyo. Sadly, not snow capped at present but still a magnificent sight.Seating comfortable and plenty of luggage space on the rack above. Note that luggage in excess of 160cm (HxWxD) has to be stored in the luggage area at each end of the coach or  behind the specific seats with luggage space - this has to be booked in advance. There is no food service on these trains currently, so ensure you pick up supplies before boarding.Any mobile devices have to be used with headphones or ear buds and not on loudspeaker and conversation is expected to be low volume for the comfort of other passengers - wish they would introduce these measures on UK trains!Overall, a brilliant experience.

There are more foreigners than in the past, but for Japanese people, services such as the elimination of green programs have been a pain. On the other hand, the extremely low price of the JR PASS (Japan Rail Pass), which has been pointed out for some time, is frustrating. To be frank, it's not up to date with the times and it's too cheap. It would be fine if all foreigners had good manners, but the bad manners of people from certain countries are alarming. Instead of putting all the trash in the trash can, they leave with trash in it, or they throw a plastic pot into the trash can without sorting the trash. Say it out loud in the car. There is no compromise of aisles. No, no. I feel that the price of the inferior pass of the extraterritorial jurisdiction should be increased further, such as by accounting for the cost of etiquette measures for foreigners.

A great way to expedite your travel across Japan.  Comfy seating a lots of room in the Green reserved car (first class) Something to note:  unlike the other trains, the storage behind the last seats of the green reserved car are reserved space for just the two seats in front.  We paid extra for this as we were not sure how much luggage we were bringing to Japan, just in case. Very smooth experience riding the Shinkansen from Tokyo - Kyoto and back. It was a little confusing when booking tickets specially when incorporating oversized baggage area, so I thought I'll pen down my experience so others can potentially benefit.- We were a family of 4, traveling with 3  suitcases that were 28" each (check-in luggage, larger than carry on)- Technically, as per Shinkansen guidelines, up to 30" suitcases can fit in the overhead space, but if it's heavy, lifting it up and bringing it down from the overhead space is a challenge, so better to book seats with oversized baggage area.- Seats with oversized baggage area / compartment tend to be the first and last rows in each car. So were were in row 18 going one-way, and in row 1 on the return. The oversize luggage area was right behind us. Very convenient. If you don't book seats with oversized baggage area, you have no choice but to fit luggage in overhead space, or cram it in front of your knees. Note there is NO extra charge for booking oversized baggage area!- Now, when I searched for 4 tickets with access to overhead baggage area, my choices seemed to be extremely limited. This is because the system assumes that you need oversized baggage access for all 4 seats! So here's what I had to do - run a search first for regular tickets without oversized baggage. This showed me which car had seats available that were together. I made a note of the car number and seat numbers. Then, I first booked 2 seats with oversized baggage area in this car, and subsequently booked 2 regular seats right next to them. All 4 tickets showed up in my app as separate reservations. No issues at all with the reservation.Hope this information helps!
