The lunch box I bought is called the ``Tokaido Shinkansen Bento'' and is filled with gourmet food along the line.It is the start of a fun journey on the Shinkansen that will get you excited and comfortable.
Super spacious seats, with superior luggage racks. Much better than cramped airplanes. Bathrooms, trash cans and sale of juices and snacks.

The other day on the news, it was said that wagon sales for the Nozomi and Hikari trains will end in October. It's true that many people, myself included, buy drinks and food before boarding the train, so it can't be helped.

We took the bullet train from Kyoto station to Odawara (Hakone). There were a number of really average features. Buying the tickets is needlessly complicated - we found online not to be an option. As such when lining up at the station we weren’t able to get 3 consecutive seats for our family… It’s a 20 minute wait to get the tickets. On board the train is spacious, the journey was smooth, however the on board free Wi-Fi is essentially useless. The journey seemed shorter because of the time taken struggling to connect to Wi-Fi.

I used it from Mishima Station to Shin-Osaka Station. In the Shizuoka Prefecture section, the Kodama train is the main train, and although there is a Hikari train that is stopped at Chidori, it was inconvenient to transfer between trains. Especially when it came to the Kodama train, there was a waiting list for the Nozomi train to pass at every station it stopped at, and it was easy to see why Shizuoka residents were so angry. The Kodama I took this time stopped at Nagoya Station, so I transferred to the following Hikari at Shizuoka Station, but I had to wait 20 minutes on the Shizuoka Station platform in the middle of the summer to connect, which was disappointing.
Best train in the world, on time, comfortable, best service, well organized, fast, clean, you can count on it

Shinkansen Hikari is the Japanese railway network of high-speed trains on which the so-called "bullet trains" travel. The term Shinkansen designates the line and not the single train and means "new railway section". The trains that run along it are called "Super Express". The nickname "bullet train" is due to their speed and the resemblance of the first locomotive design to the shape of a bullet.

What an amazing train the Shinkansen is! Go to one of the train museums and learn how the Shinkansen was developed and maintained daily. It blows your mind. It's always a pleasure to take the Shinkansen.

excellent service, cleaness , punctuality. It is necessary to reserve seats and luggage space (only large luggage), the rest can be placed in the space above your seat or between your legs and the seat.

We had tickets from Himeji to Hiroshima and were amazed at how everything was very structured and orderly. Also easy to understand for tourists. Punctuality is very important here. The high-speed train departs at the specified time, so there are no delays anywhere. Exemplary! However, there is very little space for luggage/suitcases. It was a great result for us.

The Japanese made a very good decision when introducing Shinkansen rapid transit: their own rail network, no use by other passenger and freight trains. It cost money and used up the landscape, but the result is great. There's no need to say anything more about the punctuality etc., it's unique. As far as trains are concerned, a German ICE does not do badly: more luggage options, better seats, more space, better catering. But: slower and more unreliable.

Well worth buying the JR pass in the country of origin. We used this pass to ride the Shinkansen several times during our two weeks stay in Japan. Very comfortable, on time and can save time when traveling between cities and even within the cities.

I had some business to do during Golden Week, so I took the Tokaido Shinkansen, and there were more people than I expected. Due to the coronavirus pandemic, it seems like I have gotten used to empty Shinkansen trains (lol)
We took the Shinkansen twice during our group trip to Japan. The train is comfortable.  On the Osaka-Tokyo route, it is possible to see Mount Fuji a little before arriving in Tokyo.

We used the Shinkansen trains from Yokohama to Hiroshima, then Hiroshima to Osaka, and finally a return trip Osaka to Kyoto & back.What a way to travel.  Staff are so efficient at the ticket counters, and take the time to explain to foreign travellers where to go, what the train number and time is, and what platform to go to.  If you have suitcases there is room for smaller cases to be put in front of your legs, but larger suitcases need seats booked at the rear of the carriage so you can put them behind the seat.The trains always left on time, and were extremely clean inside.  Very efficient Japanese system, that puts some countries to shame.

We went from Tokyo to Osaka by high-speed train in 2.5 hours. It is much more comfortable than the plane. You buy the ticket in advance, it is enough to be at the train station 10 minutes before. The seats are very comfortable, the toilets are clean. You do not feel any shaking when traveling at a speed of 270 km.

It's an experience worth trying. The train is not only very fast, but it has surprising punctuality: to the second.  Exceptional cleanliness and very polite staff, as all Japanese people will say, but on this train their kindness surpasses even the other activities. Every time they enter and exit a carriage they bow and the same goes when they check your ticket. The trains are cleaned frequently and therefore you will never find dirty carriages. The best way to travel in Japan, given the speed and above all punctuality.
It was a privilege to enjoy some train trips on this bullet train in Japan, the comfort, organization and punctuality make train trips in Japan something to remember.

When we booked our Shinkansen tickets for green car (first class reserved seating), we didn't reserve luggage storage space for our luggage as our luggage sizes were not considered oversized based on the measurements stated. We had read reviews that the space in front of the seats are big enough for luggage. It was a mistake. We did not know that there was a foot rest so that took up some space on the floor. We had to put our luggage in front of our legs as shown in the photos. We had 6 big luggage (28 inch). With my limited spoken Japanese, I managed to ask for assistance from a security staff who very kindly sought help from the train personnel. They managed to store 2 of our luggage in a storage compartment and 2 in front of unoccupied seats. We were very grateful for the great service from the Japanese crew of the train to help us. The ride would have been very comfortable without the luggage right in front of our legs.Tips:Please reserve luggage space (free of charge) for your luggage if you want a comfortable ride.If you are travelling in the direction of Kyoto to Tokyo like us, please book seats on the left so you could have awesome views of Mount Fuji.

We rode the Shinkansen 5 times to get from Tokyo to Odawara, Odawara to Nagoya, Nagoya to Himeji, Himeji to Hiroshima and Hiroshima to Kyoto. It has the reputation of being fast and on time and it is definitely both but it is also really comfortable, there is ample leg room so that even if you had to put a case in front of you, you still have space and loads of recline. If you book seats at the back of the carriage you get the luggage space behind meaning you can stretch out and enjoy zooming through Japan at up to 185mph. Honestly the best train network I've encountered by far.
Great ease of moving from city to city in Japan. Very clean, polite staff like all Japanese. To use without fear but reserve your places before

If you are traveling in Japan, riding on the Shinkansen bullet train is almost a must especially if you are traveling between cities and prefectures since it's fast and relatively economical if you possess a JR railpass. And my recent trip to Japan was no exception. We rode the Shinkansen bullet train from Nagoya to Kyoto (and of course to other prefectures/cities but not on the Tokaido line which I will review separately).From JR Nagoya station, it took about 34 mins by Hikari train (the 2nd fastest train covered by JR Pass as Nozomi, the fastest is not covered by the Pass) to reach the JR Kyoto station. Alternatively, you can also take the Kodama, but it's the slowest as it will stop at every station and is about 15-25mins behind Hikari.Riding on the Shinkansen was very comfortable, it's fast, safe and on time on the dot! We do enjoy the Shinkansen rides.However, in order to ensure your traveling pals are to be seated together and you want to travel on the specific date, it's advisable for you to make reservation on the seats. This is FREE service offered at the sales office in most JR train stations. In order to make a reservation, you will need to have the date, time of the train you are planning to take, the name and number of the train, starting and ending destination, and the staff will then proceed with the necessary work and then issue you with the train tickets on the spot! That's it. Of course, you will need to bring your JR rail pass along and passport for verification if required.So do not miss out the opportunity to experience the "bullet" train in Japan, one of the BEST in the world!

First ride since the coronavirus pandemic. Wifi was available and it was convenient. It was nice to be able to enjoy the scenery along the line when traveling during the day. If I travel at night, I just sleep.

Finally I get to experience the famous Japan rail’s creation, the bullet train. Felt like an aircraft inside with overhead storage. Personally I think Reserved seat is not necessary unless you are traveling in a big group. And without reserved seat, you won’t be in rush to chase after your train especially when they are running super on time. Simply just catch the next train. Use google map to plan your trip is a life saver as it will tell you every detail including your boarding platform. Buy a bento to bring on board with enhance your experience.

I rode the Kodama round trip between Tokyo and Mikawa Anjo on a tour. I went there in the morning and had a beautiful view of Mt. Fuji. Unfortunately, I couldn't see it on the way home at night. WIFI was available in the car, and the toilet was clean and comfortable. However, it was a shame that many cars were passed by Nozomi and Hikari.

For the first time in two years, I took the Tokaido/Sanyo Shinkansen to Himeji to celebrate my grandson's Shichigosan festival. Fuji was clearly visible, but perhaps because the temperature was high, there was no snow at all, so it felt a little lonely.
Took Tokaido Shinkansen with JR Pass in October and November.Mt. Fuji was viewed clearly from the Shinkansen both times.
There is no train service like the JR service , speed , punctuality , order , cleanness and funtionality are beyond compare

Used for business travel. JR Tokai's Hikari bound for Shin-Osaka. Although it was the beginning of August, it wasn't crowded and I was able to get a reserved seat even if I made a last-minute reservation 👍🚄 Of course 💳 AMEX is cashless 👍 👍

Business trip by Shinkansen. You can clearly see Lake Hamana and Mt. Fuji, and enjoy the wonderful scenery. It's a moment of relief. I took the Tokaido Shinkansen from Tokyo to Kyoto. Since there was no option to use the Shinkansen when going to Tokyo, I used the Tokaido Shinkansen for the first time in a long time. Fuji from the A seat, which I had hoped for, due to the weather. Travelled by coach to mt Fuji spent a couple of hours in awe of this sacred mountain,then a short coach ride to the nearest station ,where we saw several bullet trains speed through,then our train arrived and we set off to Tokyo station,train was so clean,comfortable, and warm,a real unforgettable experience,one of the many highlights of our trip to Japan that we'll never forget.

I used it during my trip to Kyoto in January. It was a trip of 2 nights in Kyoto and 1 night in Osaka. When I used the route between Shin-Yokohama and Kyoto, I was able to ride the "N700S" for both round trips. I bought a Plat Kodama ticket for the first time and used it to Shizuoka Station. After leaving Tokyo Station, I issued a ticket at the JR Tokaido ticket vending machine. "S" seen from Four Seasons Marunouchi! The "S" line that shines in gold is so cool that you can wait and take photos while waiting for the Shinkansen to depart!

I used the Hikari green car from Nagoya to Hiroshima. On the way back, I used a green car from Okayama to Nagoya, and the seats were thick and comfortable.

I took advantage of the go to travel campaign trip and went back and forth between Kokura Station and Tokyo Station in a green car. Both are 700A trains, which will soon be replaced by the 700S. Due to the coronavirus, there were few people and we had a relaxing time. This is a round trip between Shin-Osaka and Shin-Yokohama. After all, drinking beer on the Shinkansen is the best. Very convenient, quick and comfortable way to travel. It is 100% precise and departures every 10 minutes. You can buy food and drinks onboards, large legspace and clean toilets. A great experience!

We got the JR Green Pass, I recommend this for the larger people out there. The seats are very comfortable and the ride was very scenic during the day. The seats in the regular seating area are cramped and you may end up sitting close together with strangers.
In mid-July, I took the Nozomi train from Shin-Yokohama to Nagoya to visit Ise Shrine. On Friday afternoon, the car was relatively empty and I had a comfortable time.

There are 12 Nozomi, 2 Hikari, and 3 Kodama trains per hour. There are three world-class metropolises within 500km. A 16-car train with a maximum speed of 285 km/h runs around these three cities with a frequency similar to that of the Saikyo Line. It is the world's fastest commuter train.

Bullet train from Tokyo to Osaka. Precise, clean, silent. The speed impresses but does not disturb. the seats are very comfortable. It easily covers the tourist cities, the passage under the great Fuji volcano is exciting

Truly one of the most impressive technological experiences of my life. To travel to Tokyo, I went to Shin-Yokohama Station after 8 o'clock on weekdays with a non-reserved seat express ticket in hand, and Kodama, which had many non-reserved seats, was a little later. G car of the Shinkansen bound for Shin-Osaka at 7 o'clock. Although it had been crowded for the past two years due to the economic expansion, it was empty. I'm worried about the Japanese economy.

Very comfortable, with wifi and everything you need on board, it is the option to move between large cities, highly recommended

One of the best train systems in the world, extremely punctual and very fast. The cabin was very clean, the seat was roomy with functionalities including charger. It's highly recommended to get a JR pass and reserve the seat before travelling.

We travelled on the Shinkansen from Osaka to Tokyo. It was a great ride with the scenery whizzing past at a fast pace. The seats were comfortable and the ride was smooth. The shinkansen left Osaka and arrived 2 and one half hours later.She arrived on time. A bit expensive for a ticket and the staff need a little more help with their english and their attitude towards tourists, a bit more patience. Generally speaking I loved it-the streamliness of the train. You can choose whether you want to ride reserved (green seats) or unreserved. I could not see any difference in the carriages nor the seating for the priice difference. It is well worth the money just to say you have ridden on the Shinkansen
Highly recommended for traveling to other cities, arriving very quickly, it is punctual. I recommend bringing headphones for entertainment since in Japan people are very respectful of sounds.

We used this on two separate occasions on our tour, once on our trip to Nagano and then to Kyoto. Very impressive mode of transport, smooth, efficient and very clean. I was amazing to see that they can swivel the seats so that they can have each other if there are a group of you or ask just face forward. Bullet train was fantastic, we never needed to book as the train was near empty due to corona virus.We were only going to Osaka, so never got the jr pass as was cheaper (£250 return) to just pay.If you pay you get to go on the nozomi which is the fastest one.Train is spotless and guards walk up and down regularly, Bowing when leaving compartment.There’s toilets and a smoking room and you can purchase food and drink. A fantastic experience. The train is very accurate on the stations. No need for other transportation for the long hauls. If you look at the landscape near the train, its of no use. Too fast. I'm glad that Japan has such a fast, strict train service that runs to its destination accurately and safely.

Super fast, Super Slick sensation. This train is amazing, plenty of legroom, very comfortable reclining seating and trolly service.What more could you ask for ?

used on two occasions during the honeymoon, I don't have many comments to make as I was left speechless by the efficiency, cleanliness, precision, space, and I must say that also the price in proportion to the service is really very cheap, being very poorly accustomed to the Italian railways. Always on time, always clean, alway polite and helpful staff. Budget or promo airline fares can be cheaper but it is very hard to been the Shinkansen. Great way to travel thru the country and if you get some good weather, a wonderful veiw of Fuji san as you go rocketing past

I took Nozomi from Tokyo Station to Himeji. Lately, I've been going to Kansai a lot by plane, and it's been about 6 months since I've taken the Shinkansen. It's fast, it's punctual, and the inside of the company is clean...I've ridden several high-speed trains overseas, but I don't think any high-speed trains are as perfect as this one. My personal favorite is Sujata's ice cream! I sometimes miss the rich vanilla flavor.
Riding the bullet train was very exciting and cool! They are punctual, just like English clocks! You can get ahead, never be late!

I was delighted with the experiences I had traveling on the shinkansen. The quality, cleanliness and service on board is impressive. In addition, of course, safety, comfort and practicality. Extremely punctual and fast. It makes traveling between even distant cities much easier. Very good.
this is such a great way to travel around Japan and great value too. The trains are always on time and they are clean with clean toilets
