Live the convenience of the Shinkansen but after decades here I know it is far from the cheapest way to travel.
I usually use it when I go to Nagoya or Osaka. I always make reservations on Ekinet and it's convenient to ride, but I think the Wifi could be a little better.

I used it for the first time in several years. I took a day trip between Tokyo and Shin-Osaka. This was my first time using it since I stopped coming to check tickets. I arrived at the station 20 minutes early using the 9:00 Nozomi train, but the train I was going to board was already on the line, so I was able to get on the train right away.

In the past, there was something exciting about riding the Shinkansen! It used to be something to look forward to, but these days it feels like it's just a means of transportation, including for foreigners. I wish they would follow the example of the Kyushu Shinkansen. I guess the only option is "wagon sales". You can also buy limited edition items. I want you to do your best and stay forever.

I used it when I went on a trip to Nagoya. I was using the train on a Monday, and most of the passengers were businessmen, all working on their computers, so it felt like I was at work, and the train was full of tension.
Japan's main artery, the Tokaido Shinkansen. Most people travel between Tokyo and Osaka by plane, but the Shinkansen is the way to go between Osaka, Nagoya, and Tokyo.

If you are a visitor to Japan and hoping to go to Kyoto and Osaka and beyond, then the best mode of Transport is the Tokaido Shinkansen. If you are visiting Japan from overseas and plan to travel a lot in trains, shinkansen in particular, then note the following.1. Do not forget to get your JR Pass. These are worthwhile only if you plan to do several trips in Shinkansen and considerable amount of travel in JR trains.2. Plan your Shinkansen travel to fit the duration of the JR Pass.3. Book your seats in advance. This is most important if you travel with family or friends and would like to sit together. Seat booking is free with JR pass. You can book at any JR service centre and for as many trips as you like. You can change your booking later if you are unable to take the booked trip.4. make sure you cancel your booking if you are unable to take it. Ok, the train will go without you but it will allow someone else to use your seat - at peak times in particular.5. Pay attention to your baggage size and quantity. Most trains in Japan including Shinkansen do not have much room for large and heavy luggage. Medium to small bags can go in overhead racks and will do very well.6. Fastest Nasomi Shinkansen are not included in the JR pass. Hikari Shinkansen are almost as fast (has few more stops than Nasomi and therefore 10 or so minutes slower) and are included.7. Be on time. Shinkansen are hardly ever late.Enjoy. This is probably one of the best trains systems in the world.

I saw the information at Tokai Tours at Shin-Osaka Station. From May 2020, the space between the seat and the wall at the end of each vehicle can be used as a large luggage storage area by reservation. Large luggage is luggage that does not fit on the upper shelf. It also says that if you ride without making a reservation, you will be charged 1000 yen.

Even on weekend trips, the green cars are quiet and empty. Even if you recline it to its maximum, there is plenty of space in front and behind you, so you don't have to worry about it. There is a footrest, so it is safe for hygiene if you bring disposable slippers.

Excellent means of transport between cities in Japan, fast, safe, punctual transport. Recommended, if you make many trips between cities, purchasing the JR pass, just one trip from Tokyo to Hiroshima, may cost the price of a 7-day pass.
I used it when going from Tokyo to Nagoya. It's very convenient as you can travel in less than 2 hours. It is also helpful that you can make changes as many times as you like with the Express Card.

I went from Tokyo to Shin-Kobe to deal with work that suddenly arrived on the eve of the day. Is there a reserved seat available? My faint hopes were quickly dashed, and about 200% of the non-reserved seats were boarded. I had no choice but to stand on the deck of the reserved seat car for three hours, which was quite painful. I strongly reaffirm that you should not be able to make a same-day reservation during the holidays.

We have been travelling with the bullet train since we arrived Japan without realizing how fast The Shinkansen travel. We couldn't feel it unless it by pass us only at some non designated stations. The Shinkansen bullet train, with network of high-speed railway lines that connect the Japanese regions with the capital Tokyo for over 50+ years carrying billion of passengers. There has been not a single passenger fatality or injury due to train accidents. It is super amazing!Currently its maximum speeds is between 240–320 km/h. Test runs have reached 443 km/h and up to a world record 603 km/h

On a Friday night in mid-November, I wanted to get back from Tokyo Station to Shin-Yokohama early, but I had time at Kodama, so I took the Nozomi train. As expected, the non-reserved seats were full, and I stood on the deck with my daughter, but passengers who were boarding to Nagoya were also stationed on the deck with large luggage, so it was difficult for those who boarded at Shinagawa, and also difficult to get off at Shin-Yokohama. I would like them to follow the example of the Tohoku Shinkansen and remove the smoking room and create a luggage storage area.

I used it from Tokyo Station to Nagoya Station. Free Wi-Fi is now available on the Shinkansen, which can be a hassle as it disconnects every 30 minutes. There is also an outlet so you can move around comfortably. The ice cream sold in-house was delicious.

I used to take the Shinkansen to go back to my parents' house, but it was extremely crowded and I was unprepared, so it's my fault, but I couldn't get a reserved seat, so I had no choice but to stand in a non-reserved seat. It was painful. I thought that if possible, we should increase the number of flights during busy periods such as New Year's and Obon.

When traveling in Japan, riding on the Shinkansen is almost inevitable especially if you are traveling among cities. And my recent trip to Japan was no exception. Gotten a 7-day JR Pass, we took several rides on the Shinkansen. First from Tokyo to Nagoya and then from Nagoya to Osaka (and including the train services from Osaka to Kobe and back and the Osaka Loop Line and Yamanote Line in Tokyo are all covered by the JR Pass).Riding on the Shinkansen was extremely comfortable, it's fast, safe and on time on the dot! Besides enjoying the scenery outside, you could also eat your bento that you bought at the station before boarding or simply buy from the train crew, who will be pushing carts around.The line covers 3 types of trains, the Naomi, Hikari and Kodama. Do note that the JR Pass does not include Naomi, the fastest among all. But you can use it on the other two. Do note that Hikari is also fast and only about 10~20mins behind Naomi while Kodama is the slowest as it tends to stop at every station.We do enjoy every of the Shinkansen rides (including the year before, we took the Shinkansen from Fukuoka to Hiroshima and back, and then to Kumamoto and Kagoshima). Usually, we will opt for the Hikari or Sakura series trains. In order to ensure your traveling pals are to be seated together, it's advisable to make reservation on the seats, that is FREE service at the sales office in most train stations. In order to make reservation, you will need to have the date, time of the train you are taking, the name and number of the train, starting and ending destination, in which the staff will tend do the necessary work and then issue you with the train tickets on the spot! That's it.So do experience the "bullet" train in Japan, one of the BEST in the world!

I used the Hikari train from Tokyo Station to Toyohashi Station. Wi-Fi was available inside the car and it was comfortable. Please note that the Hikari train runs less frequently than the Nozomi train, so we recommend checking the timetable before using.

Unlike before, today there is also space for luggage. The car numbers are written on the ground in the station. There are some cars where you don't need to make a reservation. We always found space if you were at the platform 10 minutes beforehand.

Shinkansen is the best! We did a day trip from Ueno to Kanasawa and back and then took this train down to Kyoto and back.  Super fun and relaxing - and don't forget to grab a Bento or two from the Station before you get on!!

I was impressed to see that all seats on the Shinkansen were non-smoking, and there was a large restroom that could be used by parents and children and people with disabilities, which is common in Tokyo. I had two Chihuahuas with me and I always went home, so the bathroom was small and difficult, but I was impressed by how clean and new the vehicle was and how clean the bathroom was. There was a mother in front of me with a baby and a small child, and I thought it was a very good thing that the three of us could go inside and the children would feel safe. I took a reserved seat, but my Chihuahua wasn't there, so I ended up in front of the toilet, but since it was between Tokyo and Atami, it was right there. I took the local line from Atami to Shimoda, Izu. With Super View, all seats are reserved, which makes it difficult for people to bring their dogs.

We took the bullet train from Odawara (Hakone) to Kyoto, and it was an incredible experience, starting with the WOOSH of the trains before ours as we waited on the platform.  The trains are obviously very fast, and the amount of room in The Green Car is just amazing.  Food was nothing to write home about (particularly compared to the TGV) but we travelled right after breakfast, so getting a meal was not a priority.The fare was covered by our JR pass--which is a tremendous value if your are going to be in Japan for more that a few days,,,,,,,

We travelled this time from Tokyo to Osaka.  The trains are beautiful outside and in.  They are precisely on time and very comfortable inside. We FTA prefer taking the Shinkansen while traveling within Japan. Grab a bento and drink before you start and enjoy the lovely rid3e.

While on a sporting tour of Japan, we had 5 trips on the shinkansen. Wow, what a memorable experience! Staff cleaning the entire carriage in minutes before departure, superb service every trip, not a second late.  It’s an experience to relish in Tokyo and outside as this bullet train can get you 600 to 900 kms from central Tokyo in literally 2-3 hours!  I wish we had them in England and Ireland!

With the exception of Shin-Osaka Station, there are not many souvenir shops or restaurants inside the ticket gates at other stations. . . Tokyo Station, Nagoya Station, and Shizuoka Station are no exception. (Shin-Osaka Station is also under the jurisdiction of JR West, so it seems to be well stocked.) Tokyo Station has plenty of facilities inside the conventional line ticket gate, Nagoya has a station building, and Shizuoka Station has a mall in front of the ticket gate, so we recommend stocking up on drinks, souvenirs, bento boxes, etc. before passing through the Tokaido Shinkansen ticket gate.
I used the train from Tokyo Station to Okayama Station, and was surprised at how quickly I reached my destination. I thought Japanese technology was amazing.

For the residents it will be something common, one more trip, there are even people who take it every day to go to work, but for those who do not have a bullet train in their country, you see its speed, cleanliness, order and attention, and without a doubt a tear will fall... light years away from Argentina... if you are looking for the bathroom, there is... rest assured... between each long carriage, there are several... HIGHLY RECOMMENDED...

The train ride was smooth and comfortable with no delays. Customer service was fast and great. I lost my phone on the train and I was able to retrieve it back in less than 20 minutes. Great experience!

Although it has been more than 50 years since it opened, JR Tokai's Shinkansen seems to have had no accidents involving vehicles or tracks, as far as we know. Other companies have experienced derailment accidents on the Joetsu Shinkansen during earthquakes, and it is still fresh in our minds that the Sanyo Shinkansen was found to have poorly maintained vehicles. In some cases, the driver continued driving without noticing the accident that caused injuries in the tunnel. There was also a platform accident involving a high school student on the Tokaido Expressway, but this was due to human error. First of all, I would like to hope that there will be no major accidents until the Chuo Maglev opens (I don't know when this will happen).
It runs one after another just like a conventional line. I think the important thing is not to get the train time and boarding location wrong.

I used it for a round trip from Shin-Yokohama Station to Nagoya Station. I took the seat on the right side facing Nagoya. The view of Mt. Fuji from the window was moving. It was a quick and comfortable trip.

Nothing much to be said about the shinkansen. It is always on time, gets you to places fast. If you did not reserve a seat before hand go to the carriages that are not reserved. Also watch out for green carriages as these cost more.
When riding the Tokaido Shinkansen, some people may be looking forward to seeing Mt. Fuji, but at that time they are seated in the D seat. You can see it around Shin-Fuji Station.
I took this trip from Tokyo to Shin Osaka, it was wonderful to experience the high speed of a shinkansen

We pre-ordered the Japan Railway Pass and picked them up from the station upon our arrival.  This was the only instance where we had to wait 20-25 minutes and an opportunity for minor improvement.  Upon receipt of our passes every other step in the way from - reserving tickets (go the day before if you are able) to travelling were excellent!  And so quiet!

Really quite an experience! The seats are comfortable with ample leg room. Always on time, spotlessly clean and the most efficient way of getting around given that we had the 14 day JR pass. They have reserved and non-reserved coaches. Best to make a reservation as seats can run out (we were travelling during Obon week).

We traveled 3 times with the Shinkansen and all 3 times it was an experience to see how efficiently and comfortably it all worked. If we had similar trains in Europe, I think the railways would have crowned days.

The Shinkansen or Bullet Trains travels at 150-160 mph and feels as though you are hardly moving. It is composed of 15 cars and locomotive. Boarding is by waiting at the gate for your assigned car and you better be ready when the train arrives as you will have only minutes to board.

I used it when going to the Izu area. I took the Odoriko to go there, but on the way back I changed the route and took the Tokaido Shinkansen from Mishima. It was a non-reserved seat at Kodama on a weekday morning, but it was crowded and most of the seats were occupied. It was faster and more convenient than the dancer.

Honestly, it felt like being inside an airplane in seats that are nicer than economy. It was clean and comfortable. We booked through our travel agency and I discovered after the fact it would have cost a lot less to book ourselves at the window. Nice ride.
We took the 14 day Green Class JR Pass and it was a blessing. The trains on their own are not short of phenomenal. Not to mention effective.

I've been thinking about it a lot lately, but when I'm waiting, they don't come, and when they don't, they often come shortly after I get on the train, or the timing isn't right. Especially when I take the Shinkansen early in the morning, I often want to eat my fill early and get some sleep. This is no longer the time to increase the number of in-vehicle sales staff, and sales will not increase commensurate with the increase in staff. Instead of the old-fashioned sales method where one person drives a cart back and forth inside the car, I think there could be a service where the order is delivered to the seat using a smartphone or touch panel.What do you think?

It’s a real crime to visit Japan and not take a ride on the Shinkansen, so we decided to go to Kyoto from Tokyo for a few days. Our trip coincided with the arrival of a super typhoon, so some trains were canceled and some had their routes shortened, but information about this could easily be found at the station and on the official website. We bought tickets for the Hikari train, the ride is a little over 3 hours one way. It's the same speed as the Nozomi train, but with a couple of stops, the route takes longer, although this is compensated by the opportunity to save a few hundred yen.
Trains are on time, super clean, comfortable etc. The JR pass is the best way to travel around Japan. Bookings can be easily made in advance at any station.

We had heard so many good things about the Shinkansen, but even so were pleasantly surprised by our experience (we went on five altogether during our trip to Japan). Why anyone would bother with the green car, I don't know - the standard class carriages are as comfortable as first class in the UK, with wide, reclining seats, plenty of legroom, wide aisles and regular toilets between carriages. A snacks trolley will appear every so often, and you are given plenty of warning about the next station (in English and Chinese, I think, as well as Japanese). The ride is smooth, no matter how fast you are travelling. Punctuality is amazing too - again you hear about it, but experiencing it is another thing. We had had our seats reserved for us as part of our trip booking, but there are unreserved carriages anyway. Tip: it's definitely easier to use the luggage forwarding service provided at hotels, as there isn't a great deal of space for stowing large bags on the trains.
Enjoyed our ride on the Shinkansen. Amazing speed. Train was neat and clean. Professional approach and very nice.

I used Kodama from Shinagawa to Atami. There were far more seats in the unreserved seats, so the reserved seats were full and the unreserved seats were empty, making the unreserved seats more comfortable.

This may not be a problem for those who know, but when you leave Shin-Yokohama Station on the Shinkansen (from Tokyo to Shin-Osaka), the next station is Odawara Station, but just before Odawara Station, Mt. Fuji can already be seen on the right hand side in the direction of travel. Foreigners who are riding the Shinkansen for the first time will be happy if you tell them about it.

Bullet train that runs on various routes in Japan, particularly recommended for traveling between tourist cities (for example between Kyoto and Osaka there is one that takes 10 minutes to travel 40-odd km). Of course it isn't given to you as a gift but if you have the JR Pass don't hesitate to get one.
I used Plat Kodama from Tokyo to Nagoya. I was able to connect to the internet using free Wifi, and although it took two and a half hours, I felt like I arrived quite quickly.

It was my first time riding in a non-reserved seat. Information that you can board (sit) if it is the first train at Tokyo Station. I was able to sit down! From now on, it's an unreserved seat. However, two foreigners with large suitcases were sitting next to me (in the second row), so it was a bit cramped. Please stop extorting poverty.

The speed it reaches and being able to shorten distances that easily is amazing. Kyoto - Tokyo trip in 2 and a half hours. With the Japan Rail Pass it is super easy to take, and easy to reserve a seat. There are carriages for reserved seats and others without reservation that are usually reported on the screen. Very spacious and very clean train.
The Shinkansen was an amazing experience in itself, so smooth and comfortable. The only way to travel!
Clean, quite & pleasant way to travel around Much better than flying.... no check in, departure or landingAnd always on time

We purchased a 14 day pass. Our three year old rode for free.  If you want to stand in line to reserve seats, great.  If not, there are usually plenty of seats in the non-reserved cars (most often cars 1-3).  We always found seating for our family of four.  If you wish to purchase something to eat or drink you'll need cash. Credit cards are not accepted. We traveled from Narita-Tokyo, Tokyo-Kyoto, Kyoto-Nara, Kyoto-Hiroshima, and other places and always found seating.  Wait times were relatively short. If you have a long journey it is worth going to the ticket office to get a print-out of your itinerary so you'll know exactly where to change trains.  When we arrived we had a lot of luggage and finding space for large luggage can be problematic.  On the return we used a delivery service which collected our bags from our Kyoto Hotel and took them to our hotel near Narita airport.  Very convenient.  We enjoyed the bullet train experience but will try using a rental car on our next visit.

Be careful of letting the agents choose your tranfers.  Make sure to leave extra time for tranfers at Tokyo station since the trains are not as perfectly on time as you typically hear.  20 minute tranfer time is not sufficient when trains sometimes arrive 10 minutes late.Since most seats are reserved, you can be stuck without tranportation when one of your trains runs late.  Plan to leave an hour to transfer at Tokyo station to be safe.Also, they let non-reserved seat people stand over you and lean on your reserved seat, so try to get a window seat or use the 1st class green car if you don't want people leaning down on you, squeezing behind the furthest rear seat so you can't recline, etc.These standing people on any busy train also block use of the restrooms.Non reserved cars can be a little dirty (pee smell).Otherwise the trains are nice and ride smoothly.

The comfortable ride and stability are outstanding. Compared to airplanes, Shinkansen prices are less volatile, so if you make a last-minute reservation, the Shinkansen is often cheaper. I also like that it's punctual. It would be great if we could book things earlier like we do with planes, or get cheaper fares with higher discount rates.

What a fantastic service.  The whole experience is as an American put it 'awesome'.  The service is fast, efficient and comfortable.  The only small point I would say lets it down is the trolley service.  We manage four rail journeys on our travel across Japan.  It’s the way to get from a to b in style.

First of all, I had a very difficult finding this site.  So pardon me if I got it wrong. This review is of the Bullet Train that travels from Kyoto to Tokyo. Riding the Bullet Train was one of my main goals in going to Japan.  The others being seeing Geishas, Mt Fuji, and as many of the gorgeous gardens that I could.I wasn't displeased with any of them.  But I must admit that sometimes what you saw was different from what you expected.The Bullet Train WAS fast.  But deceivingly so as it didn't seem fast.  It was smooth and surprisingly quiet.  It also did not have the type of "services" I expected (a la the Chunnel between Paris and London).  You really need to send your baggage ahead of you when you use the Bullet Train.  And getting a drink (not just water) takes being forthright.I did get a nice Japanese Beer.  It took some effort but I succeeded.  And about a dozen others in my group immediately followed my lead.  In fact one of my companions was so excited she yelled out "now THIS is the way to travel!"  And it was very nice indeed.But the smooth countryside views and quiet were wonderful.  It was beyond my expectation and still wonderful but quite different from what I expected..Our tour guide prepped us on how to get on to the train.  She had us lined up in the correct order to QUICKLY board and sit down in our correct seats.  She made sure we understood that we only had ONE minute to board in the Kyoto station.  As the Bullet started to accelerate out of the station we gave ourselves a round of applause.  I still don't understand why they couldn't have allowed a little bit more time to board (2 minutes?) but Japan many times operates on frenetic paces.Candidly I don't know if it would be possible to board a family of four with your luggage in a minute.  You might lose a child or two in the process.  This train has a schedule to keep whether or not you are on it!  And on top of all that, we had to send our luggage by truck ... not on the train.  Given that fact I don't understand how one could travel by Bullet Train on an ad hoc basis.But it was fun ... and fast.
This super fast train or bullet train is on time. Prices are quite expensive.  Seats 3 and 2 in 1 row.   Wifi is free and there is electronic charging available. Leg room is quite spacious.

The experience of travelling on the Shinkansen trains is incredible, sleek, smooth ride and very fast, efficient and on time! Added bonus of seeing majestic Mount Fuji en-route made it extra special. Japan Rail Pass enables unlimited usage of the JR train network including most of the Shinkansen "Bullet Trains" this is an absolute essential to buy for anyone travelling to Japan.

Depending on the time, you can also sit in non-reserved seats. Seats are always reserved, but if you use the Express Card or use the annual fee-free option, you can reserve seats for the same price as non-reserved seats.

Surely you already bought your 7, 14 or 21 day Japan Rail Pass, so.... take advantage of it!!!! Traveler tip: The pass allows unlimited travel on all Japan Railways Group lines, including the Hikari and Kodama Shinkansen (but not the Nozomi and Mizuho) and on board their associated buses and ferries. Upon arriving at Narita International Airport, with our JRPass purchase ticket + passport in hand, you must go to the terminal where the pass coupon is exchanged for the definitive JR Pass, in the basement under exit B. When you present the coupon, they will ask from what day you want the pass to start running. Since they are consecutive days, it is best to start with the date of the first scheduled long trip. Keep in mind that for most long train trips you have to reserve and get a ticket at the JR ticket offices located in the main stations. In almost all cases you can get a ticket for the same day, although for greater security it is advisable to get the ticket the day before if you are going to a busy destination such as Kyoto, Hiroshima, etc. Use hyperdia to plan a train trip as it shows times and routes for any city, as well as transfers if any. Finally: travel light and compact, since there is practically no place to put your suitcases!!!

I ride the Tokaido Shinkansen several times a year. The number of Nozomi trains bound for Tokyo from Shin-Osaka has doubled (departs every few minutes during peak hours), and you can use your mobile phone throughout the journey, as well as wireless LAN, so you'll feel more comfortable every time you ride. The Tokaido Shinkansen is truly Japan's main artery and is proud of itself to the world. If the weather is good, you can even see Mt. Fuji and enjoy the view from the train window.

Japanese fast trains are the mirror of the country: efficient, very fast, very clean, punctual to the second, capable of connecting two wonderful cities such as Tokyo and Kyoto (about 600 km apart) in 2 hours, trains that travel at 300 km/h, pressurized due to their very high speed. Aside from the wonderful experience, they are an asset for Japan as well as very useful because they connect almost the entire country. Incredible!

I used it on my way back from going to Kyoto. It took quite a while to get there because I took a plane via Itami, but since Japan is a major railway nation, the Shinkansen is punctual, fast, and comfortable. Another advantage is that there are many trains and you can ride them quickly.

I used the Shinkansen service with some friends in September 2015 whilst travelling between Osaka and Himeji. It is a very comfortable and speedy way to get from A to B, the epitome of travelling in style! It is quite expensive, for our hour's journey, it cost around £40 return, but it was very high quality travel!

I used the Plat Kodama green car that someone else wrote about. I usually use regular seats, but the green car is really comfortable! ︎The legroom is wide, the seats are comfortable, and the inside of the car is quiet. It's a great way to travel at a leisurely pace as you can get a great deal. However, unlike on an airplane, the drawback is that you are gradually brought back to reality from the journey...
In Japan one must ride this train just to experience it.  Amtrak has lots to learn from the trains and buses in Japan. They are so very well run and clean.

The  Bullet Train (Shinkansen) travel to almost all parts of Japan and are always expanding. The shinkansen trains are comfortable, quiet, and smooth.The green class gives you a little more room than usual. The Gran class (if available) is expensive and is like business class on airfares. Service comes through carts with hot and cold drinks, bento boxes, snacks, souvenirs, etc.Even if you are a smoker stay in the non-smoking cabins, and just go and have a puff in the smoking cabin, when you feel the urge. You will understand what I mean when you're there, and experience the shinkansen.Tickets are available in Japan only and reservations can be hard to get on short notice.Enjoy the experience, and regardless of the cost, it is the way travel ought to be!IT'S AWESOME AND AMAZING, TRY IT YOURSELF AND FIND OUT =D

The seats even in ordinary class are comfy with lots of legroom. They turn to face direction of travel. If you have a JR pass make a free reservation so you are guaranteed a seat. Only issue is lack of baggage space so board early if you have suitcases.

The Shinkansen (bullet trains) go to almost all parts of the country and are ever expanding.  Trains are comfortable, quiet, and smooth riding.  Green class gives you a little more room.  Gran class (if available) is expensive and is comparable to business class on airlines.  There is no dining cars, but girls come through carts providing hot and cold drinks, bento boxes, snacks, souvenirs, etc.  Compare this with the U.S. and you realize how far behind we are when it comes to railroads!  Note that tickets are only available in Japan and reservations can be hard to get on short notice.

Anyone who visits Japan will be constantly amazed, and will never stop talking about your visit for years. Travel in Japan is also amazing, really efficient, clean and luxurious. however like everything in Japan its really confusing, the worst thing is trying to buy your ticket from a complicated machine, only written in Japanese, however some of them do "speak" English too ! then trying to find your way to the platform through a maze of underground passages, and stations with so many entrances and exits, with thousands of people all on the move. its a bit scary, but once you've got your confidence, being careful not to get lost, youre on your your way, some things are written in English, but not many, so you have to learn to read a bit of Japanese, on the trains there are different classes,the tickets will give you a seat and coach number, you queue for your coach on the platform, the trains will arrive exactly on time and arrive exactly on time. all trains are really clean and comfortable, the ride is quiet and smooth. you can buy meals on the train, called Bento. very polite staff come through the trains with trolleys like on aircraft, you don't realize the speed youre traveling. so once you've got over the language problems at the stations, travel in Japan is wonderful. like everything in Japan, its safe, clean, yes you will get lost, but that's part of the fun, learn to speak some Japanese before you go. and when you get lost, ask some school kids, or teenagers, most of them do learn some English in school, but they will probably be too shy and embarrassed to speak to you anyway. You can do it the easy way with a group tour, but much more fun to do it yourself, be extra polite to everyone and don't forget to bow all the time. its really appreciated.

We travelled with a JR pass from Tokyo to Kyoto on the Shinkansen, something I had always dreamt of doing. Negotiating the station wasn't easy so give yourself extra time to find the section of the station which serves the bullet train. Our hotel told us they would transport our luggage ahead for us (for an extra cost ) as that's quite common but we decided we'd rather take our luggage with us. However luggage storage on the bullet train is limited to the space behind the back row of seats on each carriage - consequently irrespective of what seat you've booked, if you have luggage stand at the part of the platform for the higher numbered seats - from memory the back row is numbered about row 20. Get on smartly and hopefully there will be room for your cases then go and find the numbered seats you've got for the trip.There is a trolley passing through the corridor with drinks and snacks but nothing very exciting. The train arrives and leaves on time to the second so don't be late! And after you leave Yokohama look out to the right and if you're in luck you will see mt Fuji in the distance and as you travel you'll pass within a few miles of it. It is majestic.

On my way back from a business trip from Nagoya, I took the Kodama green car to Tokyo. Since it stops at every station, the ride time is 2 and a half hours, an hour more than the Nozomi. I used "Plat Kodama" which allows reservations up to the day before boarding, so I was able to use a green car at a low price. It was an N700 series, and the seats, two on each side, were much wider in front and back than a regular car, and the seats were comfortable, neither too soft nor too hard, and I didn't get tired even after sitting for a long time. Additionally, there are charging outlets under the armrests of all seats, so I was able to use my PC and smartphone with confidence. It's much cheaper than using the Nozomi non-reserved seat, so if you have a little time to spare, we recommend using the Green Car of Plat Kodama.

I was in Japan for three weeks and used the rail system extensively. I had the JR rail pass and chose the Green Car option. There is not a great deal of difference between the ordinary and green cars. If you are traveling with luggage that easily fits overhead, you probably want to go with the ordinary. This was a segment of a two month trip, so with my heavy luggage, the less crowded green car was a real advantage. I never had anyone sitting next to me and so could easily accommodate my luggage. The Japanese rail system is wonderful.

I just recently took the Tokyo - Kyoto bullet train. It is amazing. Our trip only took 2:17h to go 230 miles. It is very comfortable, pretty luxurious, and quite spacious. I have the following advice if you are from abroad:First of all, I found the websites (for booking) not very user-friendly, and I am quite savvy with a computer. Therefore I suggest that you have the concierge (of your hotel) book the tickets. Second, if you're planning on eating during the train, I suggest that you buy food in the station beforehand. We found the food (that they served) on the train pretty substandard.  I am not a  fussy eater, but take my word for it. Solution: they sell Bento Boxes, snacks, etc. in the station. I noticed that on the way down I/we were the only ones that bought food from the trolley. Everybody else came in with their Bento boxes (and a beer) that they bought at the station. Third, make sure that you get to the platform on time. There is a bullet train every few minutes, but if your ticket is (for example) for the 12:00 train, and you miss that train, you cannot jump on the 12:05 train. Your 12:00 train ticket will be considered null and void and you will have to buy new tickets. Fourth, I suggest that you get a first-class ticket. The price difference between a regular ticket and a first class is very little. It's not the same as when you're flying (huge price difference). Also, do not forget to book your seats, more specifically if you're traveling with other people, and you want to sit together. Also, if you're planning to bring suitcases, it's not a problem. There is room behind the last seat of every carriage to leave your suitcases, and if all the luggage space is taken up, talk to the attendant, and they will find a space for your luggage.These are just a few points off the top of my head. I am writing this because I wish that somebody else had guided me accordingly.

My wife and I used a JR Rail pass for travel from Osaka to Hiroshima back to Kyoto and then to Nagano via Nagoya. It was sensational riding on the Shinkansen in great comfort, quiet and speed. You must get a pass certificate before you arrive in Japan and exchange it for a pass at one of the many JR ticket offices. You then use the pass to get tickets for reserved seats on the Shinkansen. For travel on JR metro trains and buses you just show your pass at the entry and exit gates. It was easy and convenient and value for money given the travel we undertook. The train and bus systems in Japan are second to none and the best way to get around.

To complete a rather dismal and rainy Mount Fuji Trip, we took the bullet train back to Tokyo Station. Timing was Saturday afternoon and there were plenty of seats available in the front of the train. Interestingly shaped train with impressive speeds though the trip we took was more 160mph rather than the 200+ mph potential. Choose a Mt Fuji trip wisely and the return on the bullet train may well be included within the price

It's a great way to travel long distances without getting tired and leaving on time. Isn't the cheapest way to purchase a set that includes a hotel and train ticket? However, there is no place to put a large suitcase, so I had to put it between the back seat and the wall, which is a shame. I request JR Tokai to improve so that my luggage does not cause trouble to other people!

The difference between a green car and a regular car is that the seats are spacious, the interior is chic and calm, the towel service is quiet, there are few passengers, and it is quiet.There are no special services such as blanket rentals, but if you ride a long distance like between Tokyo and Hakata, the feeling of fatigue is completely different. The seats in the N700 green car seem to have been created with a lot of research, which may help reduce fatigue.
quite fast, little bit jet-lag, with a simple android app, I can measure peak speed, sometimes reaching over 300kmph

If you are travelling in Japan I can't recommend the Shinkansen enough; fast, clean, efficient, and punctual, it is a million miles better than any other internal transport system I have ever used.The Shinkansen has specific platforms and rails, and if you are boarding at a terminus it is definitely worth getting to the platform early to see the train being cleaned and turned. The train itself is a funny duck-billed shape, and it's nice to have enough time to have a proper look at it. The cleaning crew on the train work with military precision and you can see them through the windows as they swoop along, turning the chairs round as they go. Both me and my husband were super impressed by this.You can book seats on the train for no extra charge at the stations, and it is well worth doing to guarantee your seat. If you book early enough you can choose your side of the train to maximise your chance of seeing Fujisan as you fly past. The service on the trains is fantastic, and you can get snacks and drinks from your train hostess as you travel, although we prefered to take our pick of the ekiben at the station.

On the Shinkansen section from Nagoya to Kyoto, on the right side in the direction of travel, you can see famous historical places such as the old battlefield of Sekigahara, the ruins of Azuchi Castle, Hikone Castle, a national treasure, and Mt. Kinka (Mt. Inaba) of Gifu Castle. I also learned from books about the Shinkansen that there are many historical things to see, but I was very impressed when I first saw Azuchiyama (there is a sign pointing towards Azuchiyama on the mountainside in the foreground so that you can see it from the Shinkansen) and Hikone Castle (it is small because it is far from the railroad tracks, but you can see it well). Due to the speed of the Shinkansen, the time will pass quickly, but for history buffs, this is a recommended way to enjoy the Tokaido Shinkansen.

A trip with the shinkansen is a special experience. First find the right train and departure at the huge Tokyo station. Then the futuristic train slides quietly onto the platform while the cleaning girls in pink uniforms give the train an overhaul. The "pilots" change and the train is boarded a few minutes before departure. We slide through the countryside at breakneck speed but completely quietly. A special pleasure are the delicious lunch boxes with all kinds of goodies that everyone has brought

It will be the world's first high-speed railway, connecting Tokyo and Shin-Osaka in 2.5 hours. Since its opening, there have been very few serious accidents, making it one of the safest high-speed trains to ride. There is little vibration and it is comfortable to ride for long periods of time.

If you go to Japan, it is a must that you travel on the shinkansen (bullet train).We took a short trip to Nagoya, some 300kms from Tokyo and travelled at 280kph. We were in Nagoya in a little over an hour.Comfortable, spacious and smooth.However, it is not a cheap ride.

Amazing experience to glide through Japan ... JR Rail Pass a must when travelling in Japan!!I loved travelling from Tokyo to Kyoto by bullet train ... it was very convenient and you just showed the JR Rail Pass everywhere and they helped guide you around.
Indeed, mobile, convenient and fast. The price tag for the JR Pass is a bit steep, but otherwise the most pleasant experience.

We used it between Tokyo and Osaka. The train is going very fast. In some areas it reaches 320km/h. Reserved and unreserved seat options are available. The reserved section costs around 350 TL per person between Osaka and Tokyo. The journey takes about 2 hours. Food and beverages are served on the train. There are designated smoking areas. Be sure to buy your ticket in advance. During busy periods, you may not be able to find a train at the time you want. Generally, there is a train every 15-20 minutes. Not every train stops at every stop. Some can be express.

I use the Shin-Osaka-Tokyo route more often for business purposes. I have the impression that it has become especially crowded recently. The number of foreigners has increased, and they are sitting here quite a bit. Running between Tokyo and Osaka in two and a half hours is just the right time, and I think it's the perfect time to read, sleep, and work on your own time.

It is the fastest and most punctual train in the world. Punctuality to the second, very clean and very quiet. A trip from Tokyo to Kyoto without practically noticing anything. Must try, if you are in Japan you can't miss it.

I used the shinkansen for the entire duration of my Japan Rail Pass (one week). I went from Tokyo to Kyoto, Nara, Hiroshima and Nagoya. Bearing in mind that I am a student used to traveling on regional trains, which are perpetually late and not very clean, getting on the shinkansen was an incredible experience. It has always been punctual, the interior is impeccably clean and the staff is really very kind. In conclusion, traveling in Japan using trains or any other public transport is highly recommended :-)

If you are going west from Tokyo on the Tokaido Shinkansen, it is best to take E seat on the right side in the direction of travel. Why? The purpose is to see the majesty of Mt. Fuji. This time, the weather was perfect and I was very happy. Shinkansen seats are spacious, quiet, punctual, and safe, so you're sure to have a comfortable journey.

Make sure you get your JR Rail Pass before entering Japan. The experience on the Shinkansen is amazing, and it starts already at Tokyo station!The 25% extra for the Green Car is worth it in our opinion: the reserved seats are great and you get additional service also. The green car also mostly stops very close to the stairs to the platforms, so all advantages you'll benefit off.

When customers come from overseas on business trips and their schedules include Saturdays and Sundays, they always ride Shinkansenn. "Shinkannsen" is a word that can be understood in any country, and engineers who are familiar with the Japanese era say that the railway is famous not only for its high speed but also for its safety. The other day, I used the bus to transport customers to Tokyo, and as we approached Fuji Station, Mt. Fuji appeared in the left window of the train, and while taking pictures of employees with their smartphones and digital cameras, they kept saying "amazing" in different languages.

We took a green car to go from Shin-Osaka to Tokyo in December 2015. The green cars (normally No 8, 9 and 10) are located in the middle of the train of more than 10 cars. There is a smoking area in  car No 10. So, if you are a non-smoker, it is better to reserve seats in car No 8 or 9. We were in car No 8, and there were not many people. There are 4 seats (2 x 2) in a row, and the seats are much more comfortable than in normal class, and a lady crew member distributes oshibori (hot wet towel and collects waste or garbage. You can request a blanket, if needed. There is not much space for luggage. So, travel light or book an airplane, if you have a lot of luggage. As on all Shinkansen in Japan, all the seats are in the running direction. (The seats change directions remotely or manually.)Our train left and arrived exactly on time. People get on and off very quickly. with no people blocking the way as in Europe. It is much better than TGV in France.

Well, when you think of Tokyo Station, you think of the Shinkansen. I've seen Dr. Yellow three times in the past few years, but strangely, I haven't seen it here at Tokyo Station (^^;But just seeing the Shinkansen lined up like this is exciting, isn't it?
I used it from Tokyo Station to Shin-Osaka. There are many trains running between Shin-Osaka and Tokyo, so it's convenient to be able to catch a train without worrying about the time.
It so nice to ride on this train, you don't even feel the speed of the bullet train, because it so smooth inside.

Traveling within Japan has been made easier with Shinkansen.  We took the Green Car Tokaido Shinkansen from Tokyo to Shin-Osaka via the Hikari.  It departed punctually from Tokyo station and arrived right on time in Shin-Osaka.  Note: For a nice view of Mt Fuji, take seat 'C' and 'D' towards Shin-Osaka. 'A' and 'B' will give you the coastal view.
Excellent way to travel between the major cities. Trains are precisely on time and there are a lot / hour !

Great way to travel internally in Japan. You get far, fast. Most impression made the extremely precise time table - we arrived at the time we were planned to arrive without really having to tjek whether it was our station. The cleaning team going through the train before start. Lines in front of each door on the station, exactly where the doors stop. And you can actually see the houses and mount Fuji lean a bit at the photos, you might take, because of the speed.

We used Shinkansen between Tokyo to Kyoto. We had JR passes, only had to get the reservations done from JR customer service, who were super helpful and spoke decent English. The ride itself was super smooth yet fast. The compartments were super clean and well maintained. The only issue we had was with our luggage, there was hardly any space to store the luggage, except behind the last seats in the compartment, which already had luggage stowed. Over all a great experience.

I visited Japan with an impression of an extremely efficient country. While I will not hesitate to compliment the organised  nature of affairs, I am a tad bit confused about the effectiveness.We used our Japan Rail Passes to travel Tokyo - Kyoto - Tokyo. There are trains every 20minutes or so on this route and as a Japan Rail Pass holder, we used the Hikari.While there was a huge excitement to experience the train, two elements stuck out like sore thumbs:1. For an extremely organised system, there was no indication of where you were expected to queue up. We had a train at 12:56PM and we were at the platform by 12:25PM. We stood right behind the person who was already at the platform. A queue formed behind us and another in the opposite direction. By about 12:50PM a railway officer tried to wave us off quite rudely and a few people joined him in support. There was no display of empathy or understanding by the railway officer.2. I understand that the Japanese travel light. The Shinkansen is obviously not very kind to international travelers on a holiday. You either have to eat up your leg space by holding up luggage in front of you or put it behind the rear seats.All in all, except for the speed of the Shinkansen, there isn't anything much to write home about. I have experienced the TGV and that one takes a cake in terms of a service being modelled for its customers.

I took the shinkansen to go from Tokyo to Kyoto, entering this super train the first thing that impressed me was the cleanliness and then the precision at the departure, not even a second late. The seats are comfortable, the maximum speed is impressive at around 340 km. Last surprise was the punctual arrival time of course. Finally, the kindness of the staff.

The accuracy of time, capacity, and frequency are just amazing. It is a vehicle that can be proud of around the world. The year-end and New Year holidays still get very crowded, but if you go to Nagoya, you don't have to take the Nozomi, but the Kodama, which runs at every station, is fast and comfortable enough.

I usually travel by plane, but this time I took the ride on the 4th of the New Year. It's been a while since I took the Shinkansen. It was so crowded that I couldn't get a reserved seat, so I took a seat in the middle of car 2. I wanted to put my luggage on top, but unfortunately I had a middle seat, so I gave up and put my bag on wheels at my feet. I thought it would be small, but I was impressed that there was still plenty of room and I was able to sit comfortably. However, the men next to me occupied both armrests and spread their legs, so I was a little dissatisfied. When we passed a place where we could see Mt. Fuji, there was an announcement in the hall, so I was happy to be able to see it for a little while.

I've been traveling a lot by plane lately, but it's been a while since I took the Shinkansen. It was very comfortable, with little shaking, plenty of legroom in the regular seats, and the fact that I could use my mobile phone line (instead of paying for Wi-Fi). I was able to reaffirm why the Shinkansen was so good.

There are more trains than the bad commuter lines, and they are faster. It depends on your final destination, but traveling from Osaka to Yokohama or Tokyo is faster than a plane. If you want to get around quickly and on time, I think it's the best means of transportation in Japan.
When I transferred from Nozomi to Hikari, my train was delayed by 20 minutes between Kyoto and Shin-Osaka due to the removal of flying objects.

I can't say enough about the JR Rail  System in Japan.  SIMPLY AMAZING!  NOTE: Foreign visitors must get a JR Rail Pass in their country before departing for Japan.  YOU CAN NOT get a rail pass in Japan.  Most recently i got a 1-week (7 DAYS) regular rail pass for about $230.00.  You can buy this through a Japanese Tour Operator such as JTB, H.I.S., etc.  You will  get a voucher which you exchange for a rail pass once you get in Japan.  You can exchange it at any major train station or even at the airport.  At Narita you will go down to the rail/train level and exchange it there.  This is also good for the Narita Express Train from the airport to the Tokyo Terminal Train Station as well.The rail pass is good on ANY JR TRAIN (EXCEPT THE NOZOMI SHINKANSEN), whether it's the Shinkansen (Bullet Train) or any of the express or commuter trains throughout Japan.  All you have to do it show it to one of the train station staff (at the electronic gates or entrance to the tracks) and they wave you right in.  Upon exiting you just show it to the exit attendant.On the Shinkansen (Bullet Train) you can also get reserved seats at NO ADDITIONAL cost.  You simply go into any JR station office and ask for reserved seating for the Shinkansen.  They will ask you when and where you are traveling. if you know the time and train number that would be helpful.  They will also ask if you want smoking or non-smoking.  All Shinkansen have either a smoking car or a car with a smoking room...but not alot.

Shinkansen is the best form of transportation in Japan, and the rest of the world. The system is simple and the service from the staff is outstanding, everything is now also in English. We had 12 trips with Shinkansen and only one trip was late, and it was only less the 60 seconds. Seats are comfortable even in second class. A true highlight of Japan
The seats are wider and more comfortable than on an airplane. Among them, the Tokaido Shinkansen is in a special category. It's fast and hardly shakes, but it's expensive.

From Tokyo to Kyoto in 2 hours and 40 minutes , no more or less, it was an enjoyable ride as one moves out from the city and into the countryside.Enough overhead space for small or big luggages, that was already enough to amaze me!The platforms were easy enough to find either at Kyoto or Tokyo train stations.It was certainly an experience getting on the second most fastest shinkansen , the Hikari, as the Nozomi being the fastest was not offered if you are holding a JR Pass. The seat was comfortable and leg room was so huge that you are able to stretch out your legs during the journey without any trouble. It was again an efficient most wonderful ride without any glitches whatsoever!

Whilst the JR line and the Subway are great in Tokyo, the only way to travel across the country is by Shinkansen Traveled from Shinagawa to Fuji in August and only took 40 mins. Great speed and the train also tilts on bends. Next time I would like to travel across to Osaka in it. Expensive but very much worth it.
Better than a plane trip - more room, better service, more punctual. Great views along the way of Mt Fuji and countryside. A reserved seat is the way to go via a JR pass bought overseas.

I use the Tokaido Line Shinkansen every month. Tokyo → Nagoya Nagoya → Shin-Osaka time is accurate. Lately I've been using EX cards. You can make reservations on your mobile phone and get cheaper fares. If you ride around 10 times, you will get points to ride the green car for free.

Japan Railways' Shinkansen services put the rest of the world's transportation systems to shame! Spotlessly clean, so smooth, punctual to the second, super-fast, comfortable, it's a massive Wow and OMG!  Even all the seats face forwards.We always travel in the Green Car for extra comfort, but this doesn't give you anything extra in the way of food or drink (available to purchase on board). Check out the way the train staff turn and bow to the carriage when they exit it.

Japanese transportation is so organised. People actually queue to go into the trains and follow the lines. We took the shinkansen from Osaka out but it gave us a bit of a headache. Not sure why but the shinkansen it definitely very convenient and saves you alot of time. Be sure to get reserved tickets to avoid not getting a seat!

The family decided we wanted to see as much of Japan as possible. The train is definitely the way to go. Some minor challenges including not able to book prior to arrival and converting our JR Pass. We exchanged our pass at Narita airport and was to late to reserve a seat. As we are travelling to Hakata over 1,000km away I was concerned. So we went to the ticket office first thing in the morning and it wasn't a problem. They worked through options to keep the family of five together.The train is brilliant ,fast ,clean and a great way to see a lot of Japan.

The Tokaido Shinkansen runs between Osaka and Tokyo, a distance of about 320 miles or 515 km. Trains leave every 5 to 10 minuites, trains are catagorized - Kodama - local/all stops- Hikari     - limited stops-Nozmoi   - express  ( Tokyo, Shinagawa, Yokohama, Nagoya, Kyoto & Osaka ) , not included in JR rail passFrom Osaka to Tokyo on the Nozomi cost about 14,500 JPY ( $120 USD ) depending on reserved or non-reserved seating and takes about 2.5 hours. Tickets can be bought via machine at JR stations or through ticketing offices. The trains run on a very tight schedule and leave on the dot, JR prides itself on this as well as their impeccable safety record. The original bullet train, the Tokaido Shinkansen has been in service since 1964. Since then railway technology such as tilting around bends, allow the N700 Series Shinkansen to operate at speeds up to 180 mph ziping through the country side, past the egde of the sea, & Mt Fuji ( on the left side if heading to Tokyo, right side if to Osaka. ) While to many riding the bullet trains as with flying on jetliners are nothing special and are no more than a form of transportation as one finds ways to past time whilst en route. To me its just cool riding on an engineering feat, its a lot of fun feeling like your barely moving while hearing all 17,000 hp of the electric motors whirring as you zoom past other trains and cars like they're standing still.

We went from Tokyo to Osaka in a blink of an eye and the smoothness of the whole operation made it more than worth the ticket price which per mile was a lot less than the  UK.The tickets were easy to purchase at Tokyo station and the trains run so frequently that there's plenty of choice.  On the platforms everything was clear and easy to understand, and in the carriage the leg room and noise levels made it a very comfortable journey.On a further trip to Japan we will plan to use the trains a lot more.

A boyhood dream fulfilled to travel on a bullet train. I went from Shinagawa to Shizuoka and back. I chose this for three reasons 1) The train really gets up to speed - 173mph2) It is only just over an hour there and back3) It goes past Mount Fuji (unfortunately it was a cloudy day so no great views or pictures)As no seats were left to resrevr in the normal car I upgfraded to the Green car whiich is like business class on a plane. Absolutely brilliant comfortThe train is astonishing in terms of smoothness, speed and luxury.I came back in standard class but that was still very comfortable and spacious.

We use it from Nagoya to Tokyo, round trip. Excellent means of transportation, super fast, clean and very friendly. The unmatched landscape. I heard people say it was expensive, but the truth is it seemed reasonable to me what you pay for the service you receive. To buy the tickets, make sure someone helps you, as they are like two different tickets that you have to enter the station with.

There wasn't one when I was going from Tokyo to Nagoya, but when I was returning from Nagoya to Tokyo, the conductor came around and asked me to take a look at my ticket. I'm nozomi on my way there and back. I thought the data would go to the conductor when I passed through the ticket gate, so I ended up having to look for a ticket in a hurry.

Probably one of the most famous trains in the world. From Kyoto to Tokyo it takes a little more than two hours. The carriages are comfortable - soft seats, plenty of legroom, clean toilets. There are tables for snacks. But the main thing, of course, is speed! However, tickets are not very cheap (especially compared to similar high-speed trains in China; however, the latter (with the exception of Maglev) have a slower speed). But in any case, it is cheaper and more convenient for traveling around Japan than a plane!

We used the Shinkansen from Kyoto to Tokyo. Tickets can be easily purchased at the Kyoto station in the "travel agency". Attention: There are 2 different types of counters there. There are switches for Japanese passengers in the front part. There are relatively long queues in front of it and the staff often only speak Japanese. There are two counters for tourists in the back. 1. There was nothing going on there and 2. the staff spoke good English. Our seats in the Nozomi (the fast option) were almost fully booked. In our experience, the seat should be booked early. The trip was very pleasant and relaxing. Legroom in abundance. Arrival and departure punctual to the minute.

The Tokaido Shinkansen serves the Osaka-Tokyo route and vice versa. If converted into rupiah, traveling by Shinkansen is considered very expensive but the experience provided is very interesting. This train can travel above 200 KM/hour. Even at that high speed, the comfort inside is far above trains in Indonesia, both in terms of sound and vibration. The toilets on this train are also very clean and are not dumped directly outside (unlike Indonesian trains). With the JR Pass we can travel as we like without additional costs (for certain trains). On this route there are Nozomi, Hikari, and Kodama trains, of the three only Nozomi cannot use the JR Pass (the advantage of Nozomi is that it does not stop at every station so the travel time is shorter).
The train was so fast that it took less than 30 minutes to go from Tokyo to Nagoya. The train is also super clean.

Have a good adventure with JR PASS. You must have and buy a JR Pass before going to Japan. JR Pass is available from 7 days to 14 days and you can choose green class or regular class. If you are on a budget, I recommend taking Green Class, it's very convenient. This JR Pass can be used to travel from Tokyo to Hokkaido and I bought a 14 day Green Class JR PASS and wow... next time I will use it again.

A trip to Japan is not complete without a ride on the Shinkansen -more commonly known as the Bullet train. It was quite an experience as they are so comfortable  and quick. They travel at 270 km /hr and the ride is so smooth( doesn't have the swing that the mag lev does) and they are so clean and seats have sooooo much leg room .Seats  are arranged in rows of 5  (3 one side of aisle and 2 the other) all facing front but the seats turn if you want to face your travel companions. When you buy your ticket it has the name of your train,carriage number and seat row with the exact set A,B,C,D,or E that you are allocated .( Typical Japanese precision!) AND... there is a sign on the platform that tells you where to stand to get on to your allocated seat!There is a buffet trolley service with snacks and drinks and they have a smoking area outwith the carriage.These are business trains so they don't take big luggage. We travelled from Hiroshima to Kyoto -journey time 1hour 40 minutes.   Great!

Got the green car JR Pass for the first time. It was so much more comfortable than the standard carriages. If you are travelling with check-in size luggage green car is highly recommended as you get more space for yourself and your belongings, quieter carriage to get some well needed rest and space to eat your "Eki-Ben" (station bento). They even provide you with wet napkins if they see you eating.We bought the 7 days pass and it only works out to be an average $20 or so extra each day which I think is well worth the money.

just spent a week in japan. bought a green (first class)  car 7 day pass. good value and well worth paying the extra. the first class cars are very nice. wide seats carpets plenty of room. you do need to reserve your seats which you must do at the station before travelling. the trains are amazing just to watch coming in and out of the station. the ride is great. fast and smooth. the jr pass can also be used on local trains and some ferries.i travelled from tokyo hiroshima okyama kyoto numazu tokyo had a great trip.

JR Pass is one of the best. Economical and make things very easy + enjoyable.Arrived to Tokyo Narita Airport. Used JR Pass to take the airport express to Shinagawa Station. Then took the Tokaido shinkasen to Osaka.I have a 7-days pass.Day 1 to 4 - stayed in Osaka, and travel/tour around Kyoto + Himeji + Kobe.Dat 5 to 7 - stayed in Tokyo. Travelled back to Tokyo from Osaka, and then when to Kawaguchiko to see Mt. Fuji.If only I have more time, I could have travelled further more.JR Pass - once you arrived, have it exchanged for your pass and if you have defined itinerary, request for a reserve seat on each train schedule.Very comfortable and easy. Reserve a seat so you can have a best view while travelling. You can also bring and eat/drink.

Our ride on the Shinkansen was from Tokyo to Kyoto. As long as you can figure out the underground passage to the JR Station, everything else is smooth. Although there are signboards in English, the place is a real maze. The boarding room clean and the train super clean. On board, they have toilets in Japanese, Western and standing style. People are friendly, very discipline and very quite. No worries about somebody screaming away on their phone as it is not allowed. Nice ride but sad to miss Mount Fuji as it was very cloudy. Except for major stations, the stop are very brief as short as 3 mins.You need to get ready before arrival. There be announcement.One more alert, you need to buy your tickets ahead.

It was a wonderful travel from Tokyo to Kyoto. Felt it a bit expensive, but a life time opportunity for travelers to experience the bullet train service. You will have an amazing view of Mount Fuji from this route. Keep your camera ready and enjoy the ride.

Japan has an extensive high-speed network, including between Tokyo and Osaka. Several trains depart per hour, so you never have to wait long for a spontaneous trip. The only disadvantage is the high price. Fortunately, a JR pass is available for tourists (but order in advance in your home country). Reservations are not necessary for this route, but are recommended. You make a reservation by going to a counter and booking the next train.

We didn't want to wait 30+ mins more to get a reserved seat so we didn't get one. Ended up standing for a good chunk of the trip, we weren't expecting standing room on the train.... So worth the 820 yen to get a reserved seat. And the view of Mount Fuji from the train is breath-taking, so take the inland-facing seats.

We travelled from Tokyo to Osaka with the Shinkansen and it was definitely a lifetime experience. The train speeds at 300km/h and everything inside the train is so smooth and stable. We reached Osaka after 2 hours+, we also ate the bento lunch which is sold by the attendant.The lavatory was clean and the train schedule is extremely right on time. Not forgetting that the frequency of train is high and need not rush.Although it is pricey but it is an experience of a lifetime.

First time you see one it will blow you away as they whip past you in the station line - nearly 300k per hour - can't wait to see the new one running on magnets projected at 600k+ per hour - amazing technology - just get on and sit down !!

It's an experience to ride the Shinkansen/bullet train in Japan.  It's an alternative to flying that may be a better choice.  We booked a Japan Rail Pass before traveling to Japan and that proved to be useful and economical when you want to transfer from one city to another.  If you intend to only stay in a city or two, it may not be the best option.  Regardless, this pass allows you to use the Shinkansen (except for a couple of trains) and virtually every JR line to your heart's content.  We took the train from Shinagawa station to Shin-Osaka and the trip took all of three hours.  Like every train in Japan, this one is efficient and always on time.  The trains are spotless and quiet.  The lavatory is always clean and the conductors are polite.  The next items are tips on utilizing your JR Pass with the Shinkansen.  It's advisable to book reserved seats at least a day before your trip using your JR Pass.  There is no fee associated with it.  The only time you will get charged in excess of your pass is when you take a Nozomi or Mizuho trains.  If you reserve your seat at the ticket station, this will allow you to avoid getting on the wrong train and you can ask the attendant to let you know which platform the train will be so you don't go around the getting lost.  You can opt not to reserve your seat, but each train only has a certain number of cars assigned for free-seating.  If there's not enough seats in a train, you can always wait for the next one.  Check train times for when the next train is.  Keep your ticket for inspection and never lose your JR Pass.  The train seats are relatively spacious and has enough space for a small luggage.  Otherwise, you can stow them in the overhead compartments.  Remember to go to the exit before the train stops at your station.  This way, you exit immediately and don't bother passengers getting in.  It's definitely an experience worth going through.  Taking the Shinkansen was like flying on land.  The scenery just go by you like the clouds do when you're up in the air.  Also, D & E seats from Tokyo to Nagoya gives you a view of Mt. Fuji.

Buying tickets and reserving seats was super easy on the Shinkansen ticket machines at Tokyo Station. Trains leave every 10ish minutes, are very quiet, clean and surprisingly spacious. We took the Nozomi Shinkansen from Tokyo to Kyoto (and back a few days later), and it was a very comfortable and fast train ride. Great experience!

[Points I would like to rate highly] - Accurate on time. It takes no ordinary effort to keep such a high-speed train running on time.・The inside of the car is clean. People often pay attention to the speed of the train, but the cleaning inside the train at Tokyo Station is impressive. - The seats are comfortable and you can enjoy various views. - All the conductors have been wonderful. Not a single person has ever felt uncomfortable. - Improved speed and vehicle performance. The efforts put into this improvement are also highly commendable. [Points I would like to rate low]・None. [Others] - [Kodama] does not have on-board sales.・On weekdays, there are more businessmen.・On holidays, there are many families, and children's voices can be heard inside the car.
These are the fastest and most luxurious trains anywhere ... On time an quiet while traveling at almost 200MPH ... What a thrill!

50 years old and knocks spots off anything in the Uk, if you visit Japan you have to experience the bullet train or Shinkansen as it is know, incredibly efficient and clean runs like clockwork and travels super fast

with the japan rail pass you can use all trains for 7-14-21 days with the only obligation to purchase it abroad... the high-speed rail network covers the main cities with unimaginable punctuality and comfort unique in the world... the kindness of the staff, the perfect cleanliness make this service a plus in Japan....

Tokyo-Kyoto is almost seven hundred kilometers. The Shinkansen covers this distance in two hours, making three or four stops. Very comfortable airplane seats and, most importantly, no matter where you go, you always sit facing the direction of travel.

This is the one and only bullet train that you gotta try if you are visiting Japan! It is a very nice, comfortable, fast and high class way of travel. It is not cheap but it is worth. The sits near the window are running out if you buy the tickets in the same day of your travel and even two sits together were kind of difficult to find so you should buy the ticket with a few days in advance if possible. The machines in the railway station have an English option as well so you can do that yourself or you could just ask the staff from the office, they will be very glad to help. The best Shinkansen and the fastest from the three existing is Nozomi.

We rode the Tokaido Shinkansen from Tokyo to Nagoya when we were traveling to Takayama and then again going from Nagoya to Kyoto on our further travels. The tourists' Rail Pass is invaluable, making travel so much easier.  The stations are signed well enough to figure out which platform you need to be lining up at and watching the cleaning crews tidy things up in record time is an eye-opener.  Electronic signs inside each car make announcements in Japanese and English.  Such a smooth ride, you hardly realise how fast you are going unless of course you try to read a sign close to the train or when another train going the opposite directions zooms past and the air pressure rocks the carriage.  Altogether very impressive and practical for distance traveling.

I have the opportunity to travel from Shin-Osaka to Hiroshima to the west and Nagoya to the east, and I often use it green. Aside from me, my wife is happy that all seats have electrical outlets (even in regular cars, the N700 series seems to have electrical outlets in the window seats...). However, the pitch of the green is wide, and I don't think there are many noisy customers (even during the busy season/hours, there were announcements like ``The aisles are also green. Customers standing should also move to regular cars...''). As expected, you'll have non-reserved seats between Shin-Kobe and Kyoto, but especially if you have something to do near Shin-Kobe, the Shinkansen is easier when you think about getting from Sannomiya to Shin-Kobe. When my wife takes European and American customers from Kobe (Kobe Port) to Kyoto, does it feel like one event if we use the Shinkansen? It seems that there are things that are appreciated as such.
The experience with the SHINKANSEN, the bullet train, was truly excellent. Timetables split to the second, obsessive cleanliness, order in access and exit, assistance.....EVERYTHING SPECTACULAR.

I arrived at Haneda Airport and used it from Shinagawa Station when moving to Shizuoka. I arrived on the Keikyu train and transferred there, so I had to walk a bit, but considering the days when I had to go to Tokyo Station and transfer, it was very convenient. It was just around noon, so I bought an ekiben and boarded the train, but the ekiben counter at the Shinkansen platform at Shinagawa Station was difficult to find and I almost missed it.

When in Japan you have to go on the bullet train! It is the fastest train in the world and the only place in the world you can go on it. We just went on it for the sake of doing it. Please bear in mind it is expensive! We wanted to go to Kyoto from Tokyo but worked out about £150 per person return, so instead we bought a 3 day pass which you can use on the JR as well which cost 8,300 yen which cost about £45 each. We got the bullet train to kuwasawa and ended up shopping in the most amazing shopping mall. It is best to reserve a ticket as on the way back the seats were full so we had to stand, but you don't have to reserve one.
Took the bullet train as I was so excited and it was really good .Good experience can,t go to Japan without going on it. It was cheap and really fast.A must do .

I am not sure what domestic flying is like in Japan because, frankly, for short hauls the Shinkansen 'bullet trains', are the way to go. No waiting for check in and security at the airport. Arrive 5 mins before departure (which is always on time) and get on.  Roomy comfortable seats and corridors.  Great views as you travel.  It's brilliant!

Tickets 1 way to Tokyo were 14450 yen per person which at current exchange on 12/10/15 is just about £78 per person and when you buy from the ticket office you are allocated a seat. The tickets state the platform number, time your train leaves, carriage number and seat number, it's easy to understand, I've attached a photo of my ticket for reference. Seat space is generous, I'm 6'2" and I had ample room for legs, the shelf above the seats also comfortably fits large suitcases and bags. There is free WiFi available and plug sockets to charge your devices. A snack cart comes up and down the aisles a number of times too but there are far more options at the train station, we picked up some bento boxes, drinks and onigiri from the shop called Kiosk. You are allowed to consume food and drink on the train. The train is nicely lit and feels very clean. Chairs can also be reclined for a snooze! There are pull out tray tables and a storage net for books/bottles etc in seats in front. Our entire journey took around 2 hours and 30 minsutes to travel the 320 miles or so. I'm not entirely sure but it may have been an extra fast limited service, it only made 4 stops on the way to Tokyo. It's super impressive! We had the green class (luxury) pass so we were in the nicer green car with more legroom and comfortable seats. We hop on the fastest shinkansen which is the Nozomi.. Try to book the seat beforehand to avoid not getting seat on unreserved seat cars..

This is a very nice way to travel fast and with no hazzel...take a reserved seat in the fastest delux train...like BC on a plane....a bit price bot worth every penny....see Japan from the train and just relax and enjoy good service and seats...

A train is a means of transport that takes you from A to B: well, no train - except perhaps the Orient Express - has accumulated over time as many legends, inaccuracies and fantasies as the Japanese Shinkansen. Contrary to popular belief, "Shinkansen" does not mean "bullet train", but rather "New Railway Section", a name that generally indicates all high-speed trains, whether state railways (JR, Japan Rail) or private. The expression "bullet train", from the English "Bullet train", was attributed to the first high-speed train, the Tokaido Series 0, the train that connected Tolyo to Osaka in 1964. As for speed, in the West it's up to whoever wants it the highest: 330, 350, over 400 kilometers per hour: in reality, the speed depends on the type of tractor used: the most frequent is the 700 model, which has a maximum speed of 285 kilometers per hour. However, it always travels at a speed close to peak speed, so it goes around 270 even when it passes through stations and cities. Stops at stations do not last longer than 3 minutes and this is made possible by the physiological respect for the rules inherent in Japanese culture: when a Shinkansen arrives, people arrange themselves to the right and left of a number that indicates the carriage that will stop in that place: as soon as the train is stopped, arriving travelers are let off, then those who are leaving get on board. All this, under the watchful eye of the train conductor who in the meantime leans out of his compartment to observe the operations. Furthermore, as you will notice when you are in Japan, only Westerners carry huge and cumbersome suitcases with them on trains: the Japanese send them cheaply to the destination. Although the gauge is the common one in the world (1,435 millimetres), the Shinkansen is significantly wider than our high-speed train and all the European ones: inside, in fact, each row includes 5 seats and not three, as here, and this significantly increases the number of passengers that can be transported.
