The cleanliness is, as always, like that of an operating room, a monitor indicates the stops in Japanese and Western characters, the staff on board wears impeccable uniforms, and is silent and efficient: it is a spectacle to observe how they validate the ticket, with their white-gloved hands repeating the same gesture always in the same way: their cold efficiency lets their pride in the role they hold shine through. The punctuality of the Shinkansen is legendary: on all lines in the entire country, they are never more than 10 seconds late in a year. Finally, an interesting note: airlines do not have flights to locations served by trains if the travel time by plane is longer. Usually, it is better to travel by plane for flights which take over three hours and ten minutes between check-in, flight and baggage claim: in the same time, you travel about 800 kilometers by train. Finally, safety: since 1964, only two accidents have been recorded on the Shinkansen: in both cases, no victims, only a few injuries. A journey with the Shinkansen is a spectacle to be experienced with admiring curiosity: don't miss it.
Fast and easy for foreigners to use and excellent value with the JR pass.Remember the bring some coins for the ladies with the serving carts as the food is a must have.
This train is awesome. So slick, so fast and quiet. Hardly any bumps or shakes. Even at high speed. A true technical marvel. Would use again for sure. A great way to see Japan.

We made our way from Tokyo to Kyoto by Shinkansen. Purchasing the JR pass made the fares so much more worth it. You absolutely have to get it!The ride was quick. It really FLEW past the rural areas, but good enough for some photos. The train was clean - no rubbish or vandalism. Most of all, it was comfortable, considering you'd be in the train for more than 2 hours.Pricey but worth every cent.

It has been 50 years since we connected Tokyo and Osaka. There have been five types of Shinkansen, and the train runs at high speed every 10 minutes from morning to night, and the fact that we have come this far without any accidents such as derailments is the result of hard work. You could say it's Japan's pride. Thank you for your help many times.
Punctuality, services on board, kindness of the staff, all at 330 km per hour!! A legend in rail transport, exactly 40 years after its creation. An experience to try.

We just completed 3 weeks in Japan on the JR Pass.   Shinkansen with the Ordinary (not Green) JR Pass was excellent.  I thought I'd highlight a few things that we learned:* JR Pass - Ordinary was all we ever thought was needed.  We never felt like we "should have" spent the money to get the upgrade to the green pass.  We were traveling outside the really heavy travel periods in Japan though.* For all but one leg we secured reserved seats for our trips.  There was one 15 minute short ride where we sat in the "non-reserved" cars.  Not a problem in this case.  We felt more comfortable though knowing where our seats would be.  Getting reserved seats required the investment of a few minutes at a JR Ticket Office to request a specific train and seats.* We were traveling with a party of 4, with luggage for 3 weeks (we travel kinda light - 1 suitcase/person) and one of our party in a wheelchair.  We selected trains in the late morning/early afternoon and never had a problem with luggage space or storage for the chair.  The wheelchair (folded) would fit behind the last row of seats in the car along with baggage.  When it didn't fit, the overhead shelf worked well.  We just had to be able to lift the luggage - there's no on train assistance with luggage.* Use the website Hyperdia.com or the Hyperdia smartphone app to plan your trip.  The smartphone app is probably the best as you can specifically request options that work with the JR Pass.  It provides several options and you can optimize for easiest transfers, total time, etc.* We traveled from Kyoto to Hiroshima.  It was a little annoying not to have access to the "Nozomi" trains - not included with Rail Pass.  That said, the transfer between trains was pretty easy.  It felt like a 10 minute change was the minimum necessary.  On one of our later changes, the train we transferred to actually was on the same track 10 minutes later.  We figured out that even a missed connection wasn't that big a deal since most trains operate regularly through the day.  We'd just catch the next one (typically 1 hour later).* Definitely take food/drink with you on the train.  Way more selection available.  What continues to amaze me is how the bento (box lunch) meals at the train stations were superior to the meals we have at Japanese restaurants in the U.S.* Finding elevators for our wheelchair transit was probably the most challenging part of the trip.  All the Shinkansen tracks we found were accessible.  Not so much all the subway stations, but that's another story.  We allowed extra time to find the elevators and never missed a train.  If you have large luggage you might also be looking for these elevators.* We learned to gather our luggage and wheelchair about 5 minutes before arrival at our station.  This made exiting crisply a lot easier.  Many stops are relatively short so exiting quickly is important.* There are markings on the train track waiting areas that show the location to wait for specific trains - i.e. a floor marking that says "Hikari Car #6".  There are also markings typically that show where to queue to wait.  It's frustrating to see mostly foreign riders (like us) skipping the line.  Make the effort to follow the etiquette.* We changed our plans once and returned to the JR Rail Ticket office and turned in our unused seat reservations and asked for new ones on a later train.  No problem, no fee.* Announcements on Shinkansen are in Japanese and English. There's also a sign at the front of the car that shows the next stop.  No worries about missing your station if you pay attention.Last but not least, if you have a chance to visit the JR SCMAGLEAV and Railway park museum in Nagoya, we recommend it.  It was fun to see a bit more about how these great trains work and what the future MAGLEV trains might be like.  If you're lucky you'll get the chance to drive the Shinkansen simulator.  Fun to ride the train again after seeing all of this.

Shinkansen are the best mode of transportation in Japan. Especially if you are going to multiple distant places and you don't have much time. JR pass covers all travel on Shinkansen for Hikari and below levels. Only Nozomi trains are not covered under this. However, it is not a great loss. The train has great leg room, you can actually tilt the seat back and it is fast. Use Hyperdia website to get the detailed timings - including platforms - so, you will know how to connect. I had it pat down and did not have to struggle at all. There is food available on many trains but get a bento box or some food before you board. Most platforms only have snacks so, get your fix before you go to platforms.

We took the bullet train from kyoto to tokyo in the morning. It was a great trip and sat in seats D and E so we could see mount fuji. It is a good idea to buy food and take it with you as the locals do.

A fast, comfortable and clean train. Thanks to the pass that we tourists can benefit from, we can use these trains without the need for a reservation since they have carriages for this. Above all, you have to highlight its punctuality and the ease of understanding its routes, platforms, location... with it you can travel most of the country.

Famous "latest generation" Japanese train. Too bad it was inaugurated 40 years ago so today it is not so latest generation. It should be tried because it is part of Japanese culture, even if it is not particularly special either in terms of speed or aesthetics of the interior.

Cramped and cramped seats (5 rows across these days?) Tiny windows that make it hard to see out (why are they so small?) Completely unusable wireless LAN (does anyone use it?) ``Ticket inspection'' that has long since been abolished on other railways (they come even during meals) High fares (there are almost no discount systems) b) There is no luggage storage (foreigners are often in trouble) Power is only available at some seats (I guess that's a good thing, right?) Online reservations can only be used by credit card members (only businessmen can use this) It's embarrassing for Japan's world-famous ``Shinkansen.''

It's like China's high-speed rail, fast and comfortable. The price is on the high side. If you buy a JR pass, you can't take the kind of car that only takes a few minutes. You have to wait for a fixed time. There are two types of tickets, reserved seat tickets and non-reserved seat tickets. Fewer people take the Shinkansen. When traveling temporarily, you can buy non-reserved seat tickets without worrying about being without a seat.

Punctual, fast, clean, pleasant control and comfort service, easy access to trains, look no further, the shinkansen has set the bar high for those who, like me, are used to the SNCF TGV!! For information we used it to go from Tokyo to Kyoto, the ticket is not that expensive if you take a Japan rail pass before your arrival in the land of the rising sun, you will quickly make the cost 400€ for me for a stay of 15 days but with unlimited access to a lot of public transport including the shinkansen, without that a return ticket Tokyo / Kyoto costs you more than 200€. The count is done quickly!!

The Shinkansen, which strictly adheres to safety and punctuality, which are the most important means of transportation, and carries a huge number of passengers every day, can truly be called the pride of Japan. The high quality of the crew and their appropriate response to emergencies was demonstrated during the recent incident near Odawara. Although it is the fate of mass transportation, there remain some inconveniences regarding the reservation system. Points that I would like to see improved include the fact that EX reservation members still have to pay and the online reservation process is complicated.
We made the Tokyo-Kyoto trip with JrPass, in just 2:30h and it was really good, lots of space between seats, you can recline, there is bar service like on the plane and it also has a plug. Perfect!!

Shinkansen is the best means of transportation invented by man! I admire everything about it: convenience, speed, accuracy, design. Tokaido is, I think, the busiest line, because... it connects the largest cities of Japan: Tokyo, Kyoto, Osaka. There are 3 types of trains on the line: Hikari, Kodama and the fastest of the high-speed ones - Nozomi. I rode Nozomi on the Shin-Osaka - Tokyo route, and on the other two - to Nagoya and Odawara. The complete feeling that you are on an airplane: the interior is very similar, the windows are portholes. But the Shinkansen is even more convenient: trains run very often all day long, you immediately get to the city center. The carriages come with reserved seats (for an additional fee or free of charge for JR Pass holders) and with non-reserved seats. I never reserved a seat - there was always a seat in non-reserved carriages. There is usually, but not always, space at the front of the cabin for suitcases. Some trains have a socket on each passenger seat - convenient for recharging gadgets. All stations are announced in Japanese and English, all signs are also duplicated in English. In general, solid advantages. The only downside is the high cost. But the benefits are worth it.

I have looked forward to travelling in the Shinkansen since primary school and it was great to finally do this and with my children.  We have travelled in Eurostar and TGV and I cannot say they are less than the bullet train but this was a special experience.  From the cleaning and announcements to the super fast boarding, everything was efficiently carried out.We were going to Kyoto from Tokyo for the second leg of our holiday. The train did it in about two and a half hours. This was the  Nozomi, the fastest of the lot. The views were fantastic, and food was sold in the train by independent vendors.

We travelled Tokyo to Kyoto on the first stage of a tour of Japan & loved the Shinkansen - from the cleaners bowing before we boarded to the comfort, speed and efficiency (we departed and arrived to the minute!), it was a fantastic experience. We chose to go First class which cost an extra A$500 for three of us over a two week pass but glad we paid extra - guaranteed seat reservations & slightly bigger seats. Don't forget to buy a bento box at the station to eat as you go...

I traveled by Shinkansen between Shinagawa and Hakata. Most of my travels involved round trips in my own car or by plane. This time, I boarded the train hoping to enjoy the view from the train window and the moment when I crossed from Honshu to Kyushu. The seat in the green car was similar to the seat in a passenger car, and it fit around my waist, so for someone like me who suffers from back pain, it was a big deal that affected my trip. There were spaces/persons that were not present on airplanes, and there were lights at the edge of the seat to illuminate personal areas. I am impressed by the rapid progress in technology. Perhaps because the train runs directly between JR West and JR East, I was given disposable towels again after boarding the train and after passing through Shin-Osaka. This is a great gift for traveling. When it comes to the view from the train window, the west side of Hiroshima is lined with tiled roofs, while the east side has a wide variety of distinct characteristics. Is this the Kanmon Strait? Before I knew it, I was passing through the tunnel (〃∇〃)I could also see the white Himeji Castle, which had undergone major renovations in the Heisei era. Until August 31, 2015, if you use the wagon service between Hakata and Shin-Osaka, you will receive a ``just show coupon.'' On the way home, I was able to get coffee and ice cream for 50 yen off each♪

For traveling from Tokyo to Osaka Traveling on the Tokaido Shinkansen is a very fast journey. The train runs very smoothly. The seats are comfortable. If you sit on the right side, you can see Mount Fuji clearly.  There is wide space between the legs. There is a folding dining table in front. There are clean bathrooms inside the train. During the trip, there will be employees selling food... Buying tickets, if you have a JR Pass, you can ride regular cars at no additional cost. which seats can be reserved Or if you don't have a reservation, you can choose to board a non-reserve carriage.

It's punctual and safe. Starting this spring, you can use transportation IC cards for sale onboard the train, making it even more convenient. Lately, I've had more opportunities to ride the Green Car, and I've been using it comfortably. If you're an Express Reservation member, you can ride at a slightly lower price, although there is an annual membership fee. It's an annual membership fee, but I'm satisfied with it.

We have now been traveling by train for almost a week and nothing beats the Shinkansen, you just have to use it. Easy to find the right departures and tracks, just make sure you have plenty of time, the train doesn't wait.

The Japanese TGV or excellence! The staff is attentive, ready to answer your slightest questions. In addition to being punctual (to the nearest second), it is super comfortable, ultra clean (nothing like our TGVs and the sickening smell that reigns there), silent and almost immobile compared to our TGVs where you are often forced to hold on to keep your balance. It is possible to buy a snack on the train directly. After having had the chance to take the Shinkansen (to go from Tokyo to Osaka), I will have difficulty getting back on the TGV in France.

Needless to say, the Shinkansen. When I was a child, I only used the Tokaido Sanyo Shinkansen, but with the opening of new Shinkansen lines one after another and soon the Hokkaido Shinkansen, it makes me realize that I am getting older. It is the lifeline of Japan that we cannot live without.
We use the Shinkansen from Tokyo to Kyoto and later back via Michima. We traveled very quietly at 270 km/h. A fascination for Germans: the train was on time ;-)

The Shinkansen works, and it works incredibly well.  My family and I took the Shinkansen on a day trip from Tokyo to Kyoto, a trip of approximately 260 miles.The Shinkansen leaves precisely on time, and stops for only 90-120 seconds at each stop (I'm not kidding about this).  It is an incredibly efficient process.  It is so efficient that they promise to refund your ticket if they are 2 hours late.  They never are.Our train was immaculate, quiet, and it sped through the Japanese countryside.  All of our stops were on time.I have ridden high speed trains in Italy, France, and the UK.  All were well run.  But the Shinkansen was the best high speed train I have ever had.

My wife and I visited Japan for our 30th Anniversary. One the third day, we took the Shinkansen from Tokyo Station to ShinFuji. It was a wonderful trip. The train was very clean, quiet, and the experience was well worth the ¥¥ we spent.
Fantastic train ride. Everything it's not in UK.Clean, fast, efficient, on time, a pleasure.Travel a hell of a speed!!!!

Japan is famous for many things and their high speed bullet trains are one of them. If in Japan, one must experience a ride on the shinkansen which is a very convenient and easy way to get between cities in Japan. Like all trains in Japan, they arrive on the minute. You've got 1 minute to quickly hop on because the trains depart quickly. After getting on, put your luggage at the back or on the overhead storage, find your seat, recline, and relax. Snacks and drinks are available for purchase. Enjoy the view, the smoothness of the ride, and in a jiffy, you'll be at your destination.

Fantastic Tokyo to Kyoto in about 2hrs 20 min wow wow wow . Although the TGV in France and the EuroStar from London are equaly as good there is just something about the bullet train.On time clean and easy.

We have all heard of the famed bullet train since when we were kids, and this is undoubtedly something truly amazing and truly Japanese that one must not miss while visiting Tokyo!The "Shinkansen" bullet trains connect various cities in Japan. For those looking for a short ride on the Shinkansen, I would recommend hopping on the Tokyo - Osaka bullet train and getting off after a 20 minute ride at Shin-Yokohama. This is the shortest ride one can catch on this train, but is just about long enough to experience the awesomeness of the bullet which picks up speed right outside Shingawa station. Take a 20 minute ride to Shin-Yokohama and catch a return Shinkansen from there back to Tokyo station.Trains run every 20-30 minutes and this would cost you about 3200 Yen. It's well-worth the money and a must-see in Tokyo!
We made the trip from Kyoto to Tokyo using the JR Rail Pass. It is fast, clean and punctual. You can't ask for more.

Efficient, clean, quiet, very quiet, and fast, fast, fast. I used it for traveling from Kyoto to Hiroshima, and from there to Tokyo. So much fun I didn't want to get off it. A great way to see the Japanese countryside.

There is a table behind the backrest, but you will notice that there is almost no level difference in the recess for drinks. It's great that your drink won't spill even on this step. After that, when I transferred to a conventional line, I was shocked at the difference in the shaking.

I took the train many times and was rarely late. The inside of the car is spacious and the ride is very comfortable. If I had to add anything, I would like to see more food and drink options on board.

A great experience! I was on a business trip and boarded the train at Shinagawa (Tokyo) for Kyoto. It is a very quick, comfortable train, which offers you a great sight seeing in the Japanese county-side. The tickets are not expensive, considering the efficiency and ease of journey.

We travelled on this from Yokohama to Kyoto and it was a great experience.  The train was clean and comfortable and so very smooth, it really didn't feel like we were travelling at c200mph.The tickets aren't cheap but it's worth it for the speed, efficiency and overall experience.

I was surprisingly able to sleep soundly. Once you ride it, you'll be addicted. It seems that if you have an EX card, you can ride it cheaper, but I haven't used it yet, so I'll consider it in the future.

Being the world's first high speed rail network, this is a great example of efficiency. Running more than 15 trains per hour, the system just amazes you. The comfort of the coaches and the service of the train staff is commendable. The route between Tokyo and Kyoto is scenic with a view of Mt. Fuji and the bay. Must do while in Japan.

Spent 2 wks in Japan June 13th until june 27th loved the Shinkansen trains been many years since last visited Japan.  so nice to go back to show the kids took my 3 kids we just loved the trains. Best trip from Hiroshima back to Tokyo  on the Hikari beautiful trip i didnt want to get off. The japan rail pass well worth the money we went to Kobe, Nara,, Hiroshima Kyoto, Osaka,  We did a day trip to Yokohama just paid regular ticket to have lunch in China town  which was wonderful.For anyone worried about rainy season go for it we had very little rain in two weeks only time we changed plans was last day in Kyoto missed going up the Kyoto  tower as very cloudy.Cant wait to go back hopefully March 2016.

I took Nozomi train number 216 from Kyoto to Tokyo. When I got to Tokyo I forgot my hat in the car. You can go to Tokyo Station to claim it within 7 days. If it's been more than 7 days, they will send it to the police. You have to go and get it from the police yourself. The important thing is to remember the details on the ticket well: what train, what time, etc. A good idea is to take a photo of yourself.

Travelled on the ''bullet train'' from Hiroshima to Kyoto. Wow the train arrived on the platform prompt and we were exactly opposite the carriage that our seats were booked  You stand in the area designated for each numbered carriage....what a fantastic system that really works. No sound to the train once we set off, just a slight hum and once up to speed, everything whizzes by......You have allocated seats on booking, just like in a plane, very very clean, bright and comfortable. The lady came with the refreshment trolley. On entering and leaving each carriage she would bow. She was so lovely, polite and interested in anyone who would talk to her.....The toilets had plenty of room and very clean. I stood at the door way to stretch my legs and to try and get a better view of the country side. Really fast efficient service, although I would say to many tunnels to really appreciate the country side. But efficiency is the demand and with little effort we had arrived in Kyoto. As each town/stop is shown on a message strip across the door of the carriage, you know where you are and how long it takes. better then voices over the speaker system that disturbs you. Disembarking the train was so fast and efficient,  the train will leave on time, prompt and you have to stay till the next stop if you don't have your wits about you. Super service, but then you are paying for the privilege......worth the experience, a real ....''must do''......

From Tokyo to Kyoto on the bullet train  Getting somewhere fast - the bullet train After we got all shook up by the earthquake, getting out of Tokyo for a bit seemed like a very good idea. Seismic activity is increasing in the whole region apparently and even the next day, after our big 8.5 earthquake, there were two smaller ones somewhere else in Japan. We set off in search of more solid ground and to buy tickets for the famous Japanese bullet train to Kyoto. In Britain, train travel is often a challenge. Different providers run different bits of the network with differing levels of indifferent service. UK tickets are the most expensive in Europe, punctuality is intermittent, and the journey is often crowded and uncomfortable, crammed in, facing the wrong way. Frequent loud and unnecessarily long announcements occasionally threaten you with fines if you don’t have exactly the right ticket, meaning that any snoozing is rarely an option.It’s not like that on the bullet train! Space age high speed trains called Shinkansen connect Tokyo with most of the country’s major cities. All the trains are operated by Japan railways (JR) and run at speeds of up to 320 km/h. Most trains depart every ten minutes and they are known for their punctuality (often to the second.) Carriages are very comfortable, spacious and silent. There have been no fatal accidents in the Shikansen’s history and all of the seats always face forward. This is astonishing to the British traveller who is often made to feel slightly sick in transit by facing away from the direction of travel. All seats can be turned by 180 degrees and are turned by staff at terminal stations or, you can turn them yourself if you fancy a foursome. Brilliant!During the two and a half hour journey you are asked very politely for your ticket by a smartly uniformed guard and you are served refreshments by a beautiful doll like lady who bows as she enters the carriage and then again as she leaves. We had delicious miniature egg sandwiches of the sort you may expect at a doll’s tea party, and the lady even told us exactly when to look out of the window so that we had the best chance of seeing Mount Fuji, the symbol of Japan. You can’t always see it if the weather is cloudy, but we did get quite a good look at this famous active stratovolcano.Love, love, loved the bullet train - check out my blog at Eccentric England for more info..
A great way to visit Kyoto using JR Rail Pass! Reserved your seats in advance if you want to be sure. Not much scenery to look at.
Whizzing along through the countryside the only sound was a little hum which put me right to sleep.  Go with the green car if it is tourist season.  Plenty of room for luggage.

Okay, my first thought after riding the Shinkansen was why the U.S. doesn't have these trains! The trains is FAST, smooth, clean, roomy, relaxing,  . . . I love it! Now, the Japanese are pretty clean people and that may part of the reason the train is so nice and clean. Nonetheless, it's a great ride and always on time! It's costly, too. It's about $100.00 from Tokyo to Kyoto.
I use the Shinkansen to commute from Kanagawa Prefecture to Tokyo, and I think the speed of the Shinkansen is amazing. The price is a little high, but I think it can't be helped since it saves time.
The ``Shinkansen'' is a name known all over the world. It's safe, comfortable, and fast, but I feel like the service is getting worse and worse. Safety, comfort, and speed may be enough, but...

Bullet trains are something fabulous... uniquely efficient, very punctual (they beat the second), very fast and very clean! We have never seen such an efficient transportation system! We took the Hikari train from Tokyo to Kyoto....stunning! As soon as it stops at the station (always perfectly in advance) each train is cleaned with astonishing meticulousness! And it starts again with not even a second late! We absolutely recommend the JR Pass taken from Italy....you will take all the trains simply by showing it to the controllers....saving time and money!

There are inspection vehicles that perform inspections while running on Shinkansen tracks and overhead wires. This test vehicle is called ``Doctor Yellow'' because it is painted yellow. Furthermore, because it is rarely seen, a legend was born that says, ``If you see it, you will be happy.'' Since it is an inspection vehicle, you cannot ride it, but this Dr. Yellow makes round trips between Tokyo and Hakata three times a month. The operating dates and times have not been announced, but if you can see it at a Shinkansen station or along the line, you might be happy. On the day of scheduled operation, parents and children can be seen pointing at cameras at major stations.
I like looking at Mt. Fuji from Madogiwa between Tokyo and Osaka. I think it's expensive, but it's comfortable and convenient.

The more I see of Japan the more I want to just send for my clothes in the USA, matter of fact, keep my clothes. The trains, subways, buses, and even the taxis put ours to shame, and that's a shame. Millions of people move flawlessly through the immaculate stations, the trains arrive on time, leave on time and do so with the precision of a fine Swiss watch.
Approximately 300km is the speed, it is expensive, it costs about 13,000 yen, which is about 110 dollars, but it is more lazy to go to the airport, wait, document, etc...

A really fast and safe ride. It is a wonderful vehicle that has received rave reviews from all over the world. If you are concerned about time, you should definitely use the Shinkansen as a means of transportation.

We traveled from Tokyo station to Shin Yokohama for Lunch on the Shinkansen (Bullet Train) . Travelling at just under 200 miles an hour we were there in 19 minutes. When you are travelling that fast you have no concept of speed. The train was exactly on time and was immaculately clean. We returned four hours later, glad to have had the experience of having traveled on the Bullet Train.

We travelled from Odawara Station to Tokyo Station on the Shinkansen. So smooth & quite. Super fast & efficient. Our trip was only for 50 minutes but the distancec travelled was huge. Another postive that was a negative to start with was that we accidently our day pack on the train at Tokyo Station & by the time we got off the train it was too late it had left. that was atg 8.00pm that night. We went back the next day to the JR Shinkansen Lost & found the next day & to our total amazement, the office person after filling pout the relevant forms walked out with our back pack. What an amazing surprise & it's just an example of the efficiency that you find in Japan. Our train trip was part of a day tour so it was relativly cheap.

Took the Shinkansen between Tokyo and Kyoto. Excellent and easy, realible and on time. Clean and friendly. Reccommend to buy Green Car (First Class) though it is more expensive than regular tickets. All tickets can be bought at the station from either a machine or the office (during office hours).

An adventure on its own.  I admit to cheating a bit by having the concierge at our hotel arrange green section tickets. As others have pointed out, this thing is always on time. The downside to this is that boarding takes almost military precision (which is a bit of a challenge for tourists with 5 pieces of luggage & 2 young kids). Seating in  green provided plenty of space (even for my 6'4 frame). I didn't catch onto this until our return trip but the seats rotate to give square seating for 4. I.e. you'll be assigned 9 a&b and 10 a&b. You hit a lever on 9 to swing the 2 seats to face 10.  I found it pretty neat.we were all issued wet naps (which seem to come with everything in Japan).Rather formal service. The ticket collector bows when taking the tickets with both hands. They also thank everyone & bow when leaving the car.Food carts come through several times per trip as does someone to collect the trash. Most people seemed to pack a meal with them versus buying from the cartThe trip itself was quite smooth & of course...fast... Nice views along the wayOverall the experience was neat & certainly worth experiencing. I'd happily take it again just for fun versus flying & would highly recommend it to anyone visiting Japan (esp. first timers).
My friend lives in Yokohama, so I went there to visit him. It's the best vehicle to save time.My son also loves trains, so he was very happy to ride them.

Not only is it a comfortable means of transportation, riding the Shinkansen is an event in itself, making it an enjoyable journey. Once you buy some tea and an ekiben and take a seat, you'll be in the mood for your trip. On a clear day, you can see Mt. Fuji clearly if you sit on the Mt. Fuji side.

I've taken the Shinkansen many times and it never ceases to amaze me that these bullet trains are clean, reliable, and very on-time.  My route was from Shinagawa to Hiroshima, a lttle under 4 hours on the Nozomi.  I bought my ticket at Shinagawa for same day travel and the staff was very helpful during my purchase.  Definitely recommend buying a reserved seat ticket, which costs an additional 1040 Yen.  Legroom on these bullet trains are amazing.  I thought I was in a green (1st class) car but was in just a reserved car.  Great way to travel in Japan.

I studied Japan in High School and have always hoped to travel to this amazing country. I was recently able to do exactly that and to ride the Shinkansen. I traveled between Tokyo and Kyoto (and back). With my pre-purchased JR Pass, ensuring a seat was simply a matter of arriving at a station the Shinkansen stops at, swinging by the ticket office and receiving a car and seat allocation. You can do this a day or two in advance or on the day. Trains are regular enough that there is not much wait time and if there is a half hour or so to kill, you can easily grab a coffee or snack. The best way to check the schedule is with the Hyperpedia app which is readily available. Put in your travel prefs and a host of options are provided.  I opted for the more spacious Green Car when purchasing the JR Pass. For the small extra cost it is worth it. The Shinkansen is fantastic. A must do!

I am writing the review while riding on the Shinkansen and it is quite a fantastic experience. Quick and punctual, this service can get you from Tokyo to Osaka in a bit over 3 hours. There are quite a few services but the Nozomi services are not available for Japan Rail Pass holders.Be sure to buy a Japan Rail Pass before you leave home as it cannot be bought in Japan. It essentially allows you to ride the shinkansen as many times as you like and is best used for inter city trips.

Don't buy internal flights in Japan. Take the Shinkansen instead. During our trip to Japan, we visited Osaka, Hiroshima, Kyoto and Tokyo, and we used the Shinkansen for all our internal travel between cities. If you're a tourist, you can get the JR rail pass which covers the cost of the shinkansen tickets, and if you're taking the shinkansen a few times during your stay it's 100% worth the cost. (The JR Pass also gives you a valid ticket for all JR subways, trains, buses and ferries.)The train was pretty compact, if you're travelling with luggage it can be a bit of a tight squeeze. There are small areas (read: tiny) at the back of each compartment where you can store your luggage. The train itself is smooth as, there were no bumps or unexpected shifts on the ride. This line will get you to a number of great places around central Japan. The JR staff are also incredibly helpful, we were able to find someone who spoke English at each of the major city stations we visited. Platforms are easy to navigate. Definitely the easiest, most efficient and fastest way to travel around Japan.

We took the Tokaido Shinkansen Bullet Train from JR Tokyo Station to JR Shin- Yokohama.  Travelling at 285k/m we arrived at our destination in 19 minutes.  After spending the afternoon in Shin-Yokohama we returned in 22 minutes.  The ride is extremely smooth and you have no conception how fast you are going.

The Shinkansen is a must experience when in Japan. If you can afford the cost the Green Car - first class is the way to experience it. Nozomi is the express service with the least number of stops. If taking luggage try and make it as small as possible - there are areas in the carriage where you can store it - but not a big area. Remember that the stops at stations are not long - so be ready to hop off with your luggage as soon as the train stopsWe had a large group travelling and the lady who ran the catering trolley kindly took our order for lunch bento boxes and called ahead to Nagoya to have them get them available for her to pick up when we stopped there - now that's service!

I used the Bullet trains to navigate my way across a large portion of Japan over the course of two weeks and I found the journeys an absolute pleasure because of the extremely high quality of service that the Shinkansen offers. High speed, clean, efficient, effortless. If only this service could be replicated in Europe or elsewhere!

I travelled from Tokyo to Sendai Japan on a return trip for business. Purchasing the ticket was easy and cost 11200 Yen or approx €85 one way. Navigating Tokyo central train station was easy as the signs are in English as well as of course Japanese. The train runs exactly on time so don't be late ! The seats are very comfortable with plenty of legroom & they recline nicely also. A lady with a refreshment trolly walks the train for the trip should you need anything. Considering the speed of the train (300kph) it is super smooth. Overall a very pleasant experience and comfortable journey.

We made sure we got to the station well ahead of schedule (something our taxi driver approved of) since the trains leave on time. The trip was fast, and very comfortable. We had a great time munching on snacks we got from the trolley, and watching the view outside the window swiftly transition from Tokyo, to stretches of countryside and small towns, and, soon enough, to Osaka.

Totally worth every cent you pay for the green pass in order to ride this baby. Super quick, clean, punctual and safe. Make sure you get to the station with plenty of time to spare because it really does leave exactly on time. You can see quick snippets of Japan through the Shinkansen windows, even better when another train goes past and you realise just how quickly you're going in comparison. Definitely not your average train trip at home. The only thing is that if you're on a longer trip, buy a warm meal/snacks from the station or convenience store beforehand. There wasn't much of a selection from the trolley on the train.

When I first bought our 7 day green passes in Australia  I thought they were a bit pricey but once in Japan, riding our first  shinkansen  leg to Fujisan I was won over.These trains are fast, VERY FAST ! They are just as efficient as air travel in Japan without all that downtime.The timetables are perfect and the comfort, service and amenities cannot be surpassed. After traveling from Tokyo to Mishima to Kobe to Kyoto back to Tokyo on this fantastic system I'm so impressed I want one ! Can the short-sighted planners  of Melbourne  please start saving up for one of these.....?

I love shinkansen. I love everything about it, although it is a bit pricey. But it's uber fast, uber comfortable, uber punctual, uber safe, uber clean and shashou-san are very very helpful. We usually reserve seats but for the Hamamatsu-Atami leg of our trip, we just went on the non-reserved car, and were standing. Shashou-san came and told us "the Car #1 is quite empty. Please go sit down there, if you like" - Aw so helpful and sweet. My husband loved watching the trains "pass" through the station - you could see how fast these trains really were! I just love the experience, every effin time. We go back to Japan once every 3 years or so, and we never fail to book a short trip within the country so we could ride on shinkansen :-) JR is awesome.

An excellent means of transportation in Japan, what can be said about a bullet train? I think it is more advisable to say that you should buy the Japan rail, before arriving in Japan, I recommend the ordinary one, really in my opinion there is no need to spend more, nor to waste time reserving seats, you can buy some food and consume it on your trip or buy it on the train itself, it is striking that the girl who was selling products once she changed cars bowed as a greeting and thanks

Based on my experience, i explore to anywhere in Japan with any Shinkansen and any local transport which a group with JR. I took JR Pass for 7 days. I paid one time only  28,300 Yen! About 283 USD. Amazing trip that i have. As i knew,this package only for tourist, unavailable for japanese.I suggest you to take this one, go to any where with the biggest transport network in Japan. You dont need to think any transport cost anymore. Much cheaper when we compare if we buy one ticket for every trip!
Excellent demonstration of efficiency! Great offer of trains, trains always perfectly clean and with all the services on board. Impeccable staff and punctuality to the second!

Quick comfortable clean simply fantastic! !!Used for the Tokyo Nara Tokyo Kyoto route ......with the JR PASS bought online it is certainly the best and cheapest way to get around the whole country.Obviously recommended!

Always wanted to go on this train.  And how often do those things you've longed for turn out a tad disappointing. Well not this, no way, no how. Bang on time. Clean as you could wish. But mainly, it's very, very, very fast. It's worth going out of your way to have a journey on board this baby.

I used it for the first time in several years. It takes less than 3 hours between Tokyo and Osaka. I usually prefer flying, but I found the Shinkansen to be very comfortable as well. I feel like it's becoming more convenient day by day. The ekiben is delicious, and the seat rotates, so you can have fun even when traveling with friends. Above all, I was surprised to find that power was available at almost all seats. Convenient for both business and sightseeing.

Unbeatable choice of transportation in Japan, we made a 320 km trip in one hour thirty, super comfortable and highly respected as users. It caught our attention when the guard entered the car to validate a passenger's ticket, and upon leaving it, upon reaching the door, he bowed slightly out of respect for us. Let us remember that the first bullet train began running in 1964, for the Olympic Games that year. Awesome.

We needed to go from Tokyo to Osaka, then to Kyoto and back to Tokyo, and the Shinkansen (Bullet Train) is the only way.  Why?  It is very fast - 200+ miles and hour.  Very punctual - a minute late for the train, sorry it has gone.  Extremely clean (like the rest of Japan).  Very comfortable, and limited food and drinks are served during the journey.Some tips: - There are 4 types of train - incredibly fast (Nozomi), extremely fast, very fast, and just fast. - You MUST reserve seats, which is easily done at any of the JR stations - You cannot use a Rail Pass on the Nozomi.The alternative is to fly - no thanks.

As if the punctuality of all mass transport options were not enough - trains and subways, in addition to buses, the Shinkansen (bullet train) follows the same pattern, offering comfort and agility, reaching up to 300 km/h,

Although it is not meant as an attraction but once you see the train pass in full speed and once you are on the train you realise what a technical development this is. It is very clear and you can get food etc. It is a pleasure to travel with the bullet train

Bullet train sounds flashy, but there is nothing flashy about this brilliant service. It is very understated, so typically Japanese. The carriages are noise free zones, except for the slight whistle of the outside world flashing past. The carriages are clean, the seats are comfortable, no sign anywhere of graffiti, a nice little hook to hang your coat, sit back and relax...Oh and you will be at your destination faster than any other transport type, on time every time. The railway staff are helpful, the ticket system is easy, even the food at the stations is delicious. After you have experienced this method of moving around it might leave you a little forlorn as to our train systems in much of the rest of the world... To the Japanese Railways: " arigato gozimas"

I don't know how I will ever be able to ride my local trains again after having visited Tokyo and Japan - lol.The shinkansen (Bullet trains) travel at up to 300km an hour and boy, do you feel the speed!!They are kept immaculately clean, warm, quiet. There are food carts so you can purchase food if you didn't bring your Bento box with you. There are powerpoints so your kids can surf the internet and keep themselves occupied whilst you sleep away the time.You must travel on these. We went from Tokyo, all the way down to Hiroshima and back over a two week period stopping at Kyoto, Osaka, Koyasan, Nagoya and up to Takayama.Do yourself a favour - it's mindblowing. Why the hell don't we have one of these in Melbourne! :)I almost cried when we got off of one for the last time. Yep it's expensive, but get a JR Rail pass and use that baby to travel everywhere you can. It's so worth it.

It operates between Tokyo and Shin-Osaka at a maximum speed of 285K/h (as of March 14, 2015). There are many sights to see along the line, including the World Heritage Site Mt. Fuji. These days, many people use the train from overseas, and it's not uncommon to run into foreign tourists when you get inside the train.

This station is said to have the largest number of platforms in Japan. It's large and always crowded, but even if you don't have any plans to travel by train, you can still enjoy gourmet food and shopping. When using Tokyo Station on the Keiyo Line, you can save 5 minutes by transferring from Yurakucho Station instead of getting off at JR Tokyo Station. It's far away.

Please take seat D or E. If you are traveling from Tokyo to Osaka, you will see it on the right, and in the opposite direction, you will see it on the left. Although it depends on the weather, you can sometimes see a divine sight.
It you are staying in Tokyo and want just to experience the train to say you have been on the Nozomi, take it to Shin Yokohama and return.

The absurd thing is that some phenomenon didn't give the highest rating... Absolutely the Ferrari of the world's trains. It doesn't miss a second, always on perfect time, comfortable, very fast, efficient, clean. It has no defects except perhaps the cost, but I'll never know, because you use it with the Jr Pass from Italy, valid for all the shinkansen in the country (as well as various local trains, metro, ferries). It saved our lives and a lot of our holiday time. God, how far ahead are the Japanese in rail transport!!!

No trip to Japan would be complete without a trip on the Shinkansen. We took it from Shin-Yokohama to Tokyo Central. It a bit expensive compared to the ordinary train but worth it as the speed is something else. You hardly know you are moving. Really great way to travel. Should be one of these in every city. Don't miss it.

Just what the other reviewers said, but let me mention the Pink Ladies who did the car clean up at the Tokyo and Kyoto stations just prior to our departure.  They did a good job and bowed just before stepping on to start their work.  Also, the ticket taker and snack cart woman bowed to the car just as they left to go to the next car.  Wow!  Do not miss travelling on the Bullet Train.

It's been a while since there were any smoking cars on the Tohoku Shinkansen that I always use. When I got on the Tokaido Shinkansen Kodama in Maibara, Nagoya, I was not in a smoking room, but in a smoking car. It felt very nostalgic. As a smoker, I'm happy. Also, I was surprised at how large the smoking area on the Shinkansen platform at Nagoya Station was. First of all, it's good to have a large entrance. I just wish the smoking area on the platform at Tokyo Station was like this. I got to Nagoya Maibara in less than 20 minutes, so I wish I had ridden a little longer. Even so, the Tokaido Shinkansen schedule, or rather the number of trains, is amazing. I'm often impressed by how the trains run on time without any accidents.

Shinkansen trains are an ideal to which railways around the world should strive! The most important thing is incredible accuracy, both in departure and arrival times! Comfortable chairs with tables, smoking areas in the vestibule, clean toilets, in the vestibule there are booths for talking on a mobile phone so as not to disturb other passengers. Some trains have separate carriages for smokers - you can take a ticket for such a carriage and smoke right in your seat. There are stewards on the trains from whom you can buy food and drinks.

Bullet train that connects the three largest metropolitan regions in Japan (Tokyo, Nagoya, Kyoto/Osaka), very quickly, comfortably and on time. If you have a JR pass, you can use the trains on this line (except the Nozomi super-express, as you need to pay a fare difference). Tip: there are cars for unreserved seats, which you can arrive and sit in if they are vacant. There are also carriages for reserved seats. If you want convenience, write down the trains and times you want to use and go to a Shinkansen ticket counter, at any JR station, and book in advance. Write down the information on paper as the attendants do not always speak English. It is worth it.
I walked this line several times, everything was perfect, always clean and fast, except for one that stopped at every station. I learned and only went by Expresso

While there are cheaper trains, this is a must do at least once while in Japan.  The travel time is a fraction of the slower trains, even while using the special rapid options.  The price can be 3-4 times higher, but it is an experience just taking the famous Shinkansen.  We took it from Kyoto to Osaka and it took only 10-15 minutes compared to the 30-40 minutes of the JR Special Rapid train.  They do accept major credit cards when purchasing tickets.

I can only say the best words and praises for the Tokaido Shinkansen. It allowed us to have day trips to Kyoto and Nagoya from Tokyo during our stay. We bought the JR (National) Pass and it was really great value for money, being able to use it anytime and anywhere for 7 consecutive days.The Hikari Superexpress Shinkansen on the way to Kyoto has a max speed of about 270 kph. It takes 2 hours and 45 minutes from Tokyo to Kyoto and same going back. The train was clean and have lots of legroom even for my husband's long legs (he is 6'3'). The crew were polite, always bowing when leaving the car once they've made their rounds. There was also a lady who makes her rounds with her cart of refreshments and snacks for those who would like to buy and eat while on board. She also bows when she leaves the car. I had a glimpse of Mt. Fuji. Make sure you're seated on the right on the way to Kyoto, to have this view. Next time we visit japan, we'll take the Shinkansen to Nagano, Kobe and Osaka! :)
This was expensive for a large family, but worth every cent. This was a great trip with kids. On time, quiet and smooth, very clean and lots of legroom. It was a fantastic way to travel!

We took the Tokaido Shinkansen from Tokyo to Shin-Osaka (New Osaka Railstation). With our JR Railpass we did not have to pay for the train nor for the seat reservation. The station staff was very friendly and booked us the earliest train. From the ticket office to the train track it took us 5 minutes fast walking / running, so make sure you have sufficient timr to board the train. On the track there are numerous signs in the air and on the floor showing you which gate is which train car. Very goos organized. Onboard all seats we saw faced the direction of travel which helps to avoid motion sickness. Also a train attendent went through with her push cart selling food, snacks, drinks, ice cream and beer (1 can Yebisu for 300yen). Every time again.

I traveled for the first time in 1995, I was 19 years old and I was enchanted, it goes from Nagoya to Tokyo in 1:40 h, and you don't have to unload suitcases and so on, clean, fast, accurate, 300km per hour, if you're a tourist, buy the JAPAN RAIL PASS ticket, buy it here in Brazil, you can choose for 7, 14 or 21 days, the ticket has single price however you can use the bullet train AS MANY times as you want, I've used it more than 10 times, today I no longer live in Japan but if I were there I would still definitely use it. Detail, it has been around since 1964, that is more than 50 years, extremely safe.

Fast (Tokyo-Kyoto in 2 hours), convenient, efficient. You can buy food - there is no restaurant, but there is a saleswoman with a cart, including bento and hot drinks. Tickets, if you don’t know Japanese, are better to take at the box office; although the machines have an English interface, there are too many options for the type of tickets. When buying a ticket from Tokyo to Kyoto, all the seats on the starboard side by the window are the first to go, because from them you can admire Fuji.

My first acquaintance with this rocket happened in 1998; there were no peregrine falcons or Eurostars yet. Simply a magnificent, clean, comfortable train. And having recently driven it, we can say that it remains the gold standard of quality.

Last week i made 4 journeys on the Tokaido Shinkansen Nozomi trains and 1 journey on the Hikari train and each departure and arrival was spot on time, not 1 minute late or 1 minute early but right on the allocated time. The cars are very clean and comfortable with plenty of leg room.The ticket inspectors and snack trolley girls are all very polite and always bow on entry and exit of the car. My longest trip was a day return to Hiroshima from Tokyo starting with the  06.30hrs Nozomi train a total round trip of 1111 miles in 7hrs 57minutes. All anouncements on the trains and at the stations are in Japanese and English the same goes for all the direction signs at the stations.Whilst waiting on the platform at Odawarra station for the Hikari to Tokyo a Nozomi express hurtled through at speed, breathtaking, blink and you would miss it.Buy a Tokaido Shinkansen pass for the Nozomi or a JR pass for the Hikari and Kodama trains before leaving the UK and upon arrival in Japan ride the best rail service in the world.

A spectacularly comfortable trip, very fast and agile. The seats are super wide and comfortable, which makes the trip very pleasant. It has services such as bathrooms, a smoking room and some girls who pass by with carts with food, coffee and drinks to buy. For internal transportation within Japan, it is undoubtedly much more comical and practical than by plane, since it always leaves and arrives at the train stations, where you can easily access almost all points of the city, both departure and arrival, however In the case of a plane, the airports are always far from any central point...

Japan's world-class high-speed railway. It is probably not well known that it has more passengers per day than any other subway in Tokyo. It runs frequently and is very convenient for traveling between Tokyo, Nagoya, and Osaka.

The Japanese TGV, high class, fast, a bit expensive, but it's worth it. Always extra clean (washed each time you arrive at the destination station, sisi!) I was only delayed once, due to an earthquake, and only 30 minutes, far from the SNCF in France ;-)
An indispensable means of transportation on business trips and trips around Japan. Fast, comfortable, reliable.

I use Nozomi between Tokyo and Nagoya about once a month for business or private purposes. During busy periods, if you reserve a seat, you will often end up in the middle seat of three people.On the other hand, you may have better luck with a non-reserved seat, but since you can often sit by the window or aisle, I use both reserved and non-reserved seats. I'm a smoker, so I'm grateful to be allowed to use the smoking room. The Nozomi train between Tokyo and Nagoya takes about 1 hour and 40 minutes, but it is a comfortable means of transportation.

Our 12-year-old daughter who loved almost everything about Japan was unimpressed with the shinkansen. What's the big deal? Sure, it is comfortable, and it doesn't take long to get to places but... When I thought about it, it made perfect sense. Bullet trains work so well, in such a discrete way, it is easy to take them for granted... until you realize how much they contribute to your trip, by cutting time, and allowing for less than perfect planning. You get your JR pass before arriving in Japan, check the schedule on hyperdia, show up 4 minutes before the departure, take an unreserved seat, and 2 hrs 20 minutes later, you are 600 km away, not tired at all. If you miss this one, you won't wait long for another one coming... Try that at the airport!If you are a train buff, little details will take your breath away - like the fact you can turn a set of seats around 180 degrees by pressing a pedal - nice for larger groups, when people want to face each other. Or the way the stations are announced, with perfect timing, and economy of words. Or the fact the 1/4 mile-long train stop within an inch of entrance spots marked on the platform... And the train station food is so tasty! For more technically inclined, wiki has great articles about these marvels, and their technical challenges (imagine: 2 trains pass each other within inches at 2/3 of the speed of sound!). So ride them to get to places, or ride them just for fun!

I had earlier travelled on a Shinkansen in 1997 and did not tire of sharing my amazing experience with friends and family.So on my latest trip to Japan I was mighty glad to take my family on Shinkansen between Kyoto and Tokyo and back although we traveled on the slower Kodama train after purchasing cheaper tickets from JR Tokai.The trains arrived at the station on the dot.We also got a free drink against our tickets.Since food is not sold on the Kodama train we had bought food at the station.In the station there are comfortable sitting enclosure for passengers on Shinkansen.The trains are extremely clean.The conductors are very polite and on the Tokyo-Kyoto sector the conductor made elaborate bows every time he walked accross the coach.The problem with Kodama train is that it stops at all stations and thus the trip between Kyoto to Tokyo took 4 hours.The top speed of the train was well over 250kmph.The toilets are very well maintained.However the disposal bins tend to get filled to the brim at the conclusion of journey.The electronic board inside the train gives you very factual and accurate information on the train stations enroute.At the end of the journey the seats are turned around by 180degree so that you face the direction of travel while journeying!A marvel of Japan.Do not miss the experience even though the tariff is high.
Traveling in it is impressive, but seeing it pass through the stations is even more so. It is striking that they still have smoking cars. But that is another hallmark of Japan.

We used the Shinkansen travelling from Toyko to Hiroshima and on our return journey stopped a couple of nights at Kyoto, back to Osaka, Odawarra (to go up to the Hakone area) and then Toyko.We reserved our tickets each time and learnt to try an get a seat at the front or back as we had suitcases.  We also did this especially if we were travelling on the weekend when it was a bit busier.  You can take your own food on the train, you can also buy some snacks too.  Our only bad experience (if you call it that) we had an elderly Japanese gentleman that was in one of our seats for the return journey from Odawarra to Toyko.  Despite showing him the ticket with the seat number on it he refused to move.  It was only a 40 min trip so my Husband sat in a spare seat.  We didnt want to whinging tourists to the conductor.  Pretty sure the guy understood us!

The Japanese TGV is expensive, it’s a reality, but what class!! Clean, fast, aesthetic, it will take you very quickly to Osaka in top comfort!! However, I recommend purchasing tickets in advance online.

Riding green class of nozomi shinkansen from shin osaka station to tokyo station. It's really on time (all of japanese trains do), my wife bought me a set of bento in the platfrom!! Took it inside the train and finished it up. The chair was really comfortable with huge space for legs. We even saw the mighty fujiyama (make sure u booked left sided seat to do so) from the seat window. The speed is 300 km/hour, no one talk inside and that makes the journey super comfortable. Restroom is clean enough and staffs are helpful. I put one of my large suitcase in the back of my car (1 shinkansen has 16 cars).

Compared to the Spanish high-speed train (AVE), the acceleration and braking times of the Shinkansen are minimal. The sensation of speed is greater. The vibrations are less than those of the AVE to Barcelona, ​​but perhaps greater than those of the AVE to Seville. I traveled on the Nozomi, which is the fastest. The level of comfort and exclusivity of green cars is exceptional. It does not have a bar car, but the hostesses frequently pass by with a paid bar cart. It is not equipped with video screens, but they offer a free selection of audiovisual content via WIFI to view on your own device (you have to fill out a form in Japanese, but the controllers or hostesses will be happy to help you with this). It is not possible to buy tickets for the Nozomi from outside Japan, but the train frequency is very high.

We made two trips between Tokyo and Osaka using Tokaido Shinkansen. On the express train, the journey lasts three hours, while the same journey can last an hour longer when it stops at all stations. For those who travel a lot, I recommend purchasing a Japan Rail-Pass in advance, which can be done at travel agencies in Brazil. Another attraction of train travel in Japan is the 'Ekiben', ready-made plates of typical food from each region.

The Shinkansen is a fast comfortable ride even in the cheap seats. I am usually wary of Japanese public transportation seating but I was pleasantly surprised by the amount of leg room in the Shinkansen.

We had the pleasure of going by this train between Tokyo - Kyoto, Kyoto - Hiroshima and Kyoto - Osaka on different occasions. Very pleasant travelling. The train was fast, it was comfortable and on time.The Japan Rail Pass was our key to cheap journeys.
I think it's the best train that Japan is proud of.It's comfortable, fast, has power, and the ekiben is delicious.I would definitely recommend it to anyone coming to Japan.

There are ways to travel within Japan such as the Shinkansen, plane, and bus, but if the distance is about 2 hours by plane, we recommend using the Shinkansen. It's punctual, easy to schedule, and above all, comfortable. It is also perfect for foreign travelers who want to check out Japan's hospitality and technical capabilities. Tokyo, Osaka, Kobe, and Hiroshima are the places most foreign tourists visit. You can use the Shinkansen at any point. Why not try riding one?

Travelling on Hikari train from Tokyo to Shin Osaka over three hour but did not feel like it. It went very fast and the journey was enjoyable. Reclining seat Foods trolley clean WC What more can you ask for. It simply the Best. Thanks to JR rail Pass. Station Master looks so attractive wearing white gloves whistle and lovely uniform. Safety is a high priority and never late.
On time, fast, comfortable, on schedule, clean, spacious, beautiful. Affordable thanks to the Japan Rail Pass. Anything more to add?
We took the fantastic bullet train, which reaches up to 300 km/hour, from Atami Station to Kyoto. Its front looks like a "duck's bill". Punctual, fast, comfortable and very clean!

Shinkansen, The Pride of Japan ! Efficiently right on time, stability and hygienic clean. Salute their culture of bow-ing, the politeness despite the super busy schedule of those trains. I took the Super Hikari Shinkansen, from Tokyo to Kyoto 3 hours of enjoyable ride. Recommended strongly should you travel to Japan.

The Bullet train - a mandatory experience in Japan. We caught a few, and after a while you become a little blasé about it all, but these things move very quickly...and frequently!!! There are a few varieties, but they are all super-quick. Having said that, even the normal subway trains accelerate very quickly, and are easy to use. Once again, its just another country showing me how inadequate the rail system is in Sydney. There are plenty of available seats, but id suggest you book your seats (free service) if you are travelling with youngsters...that way you can guarantee you all sit together. The trains run what seems like every 15mins or so between  most major cities, or connecting stations, so if you miss your train chances are there is another one not too far away. Ig you plan on using them frequently, or between major cities, best bet is to buy yourself a JR PASS. If you are a non-resident, THIS CAN ONLY BE DONE ONLINE BEFORE you get to Japan. You will save money overall with the pass, and it can be used on the JR Subway network, as well as JR Buses and ferries...very handy. It can be purchased in 7 day increments.

When travelling to and from Tokyo and Kyoto we used the Shinkansen through the JR Pass we bought prior to arriving to Japan.Not if you wish to use the Tokaido Shinkansen with the JR Pass you cannot use the Nozomi Bullet train which is the fastest.The Hikari can be travelled on for free with the JR Pass and you can visit any local JR ticket office to book seats.The trains have cabins for passengers that have pre reserved seats (which again can be done at a JR ticket office) and cabins for non-reserved passengers.Also another tip, ensure you know which carriage you seat is in as when waiting on the train platform they have specific areas to wait in for each carriage.The seats in regular cabins are great, the legroom is more than adequate (speaking as a 6'4 male) and each row have power sockets on either side to charge your appliances.The journey time between Tokyo and Kyoto was approximately 2hours and 50 minutes.There is a food cart lady, who will go down the carriage at least twice during the journey offering various snacks and 'bentos', as well as drinks and such. They also have an English menu in case you cannot read the Japanese menu.The trains are all extremely cleaned which you will immediately notice while you are there. Also another little thing to look out for, the ticket inspectors and food cart ladies will without fail bow upon leaving and entering the carriage. Just another example of Japanese manners!The Shinkansen is the most convenient way to cover the country of Japan, and with the JR Pass it is a must.

We booked trip from Tokyo to Kyoto by Shinkansen - Japanese famous bullet train. Just in case we had first class tickets to ensure full quality experience. The very first impression - this is the must during visiting of Japan. You don't feel the speed, you don't hear any noise typical for traveling by train. Only you can see so quick change of the countryside behind the window. Sometimes too fast.So the speed is one issue, another, what I consider as something amazing, is punctuality. In reality you can control your personal watch and adjust time according to the train performance. Later I jumped to their website - average delay for the whole network for the whole 2013 - below one minute!The difference between first class and the regular one is not so big. Ok, much more space for legs, less people in one car but the comfort, cleanliness and the service is the same.Definitely the best way of moving within Japan. Highly recommended.

We booked a package trip from Tokyo to Kyoto with the high speed train “Shinkansen”.The “Shinkansen” train itself is very clean, inside and out; onboard F&B service is very good; enough space to your seat neighbour; arrives on time in every destination.The train’s speed is in average 330km/h (205.05 mph) and you literally can “feel” the speed. Should you have the opportunity to travel to Japan you definitely should also book a trip with the “Shinkansen”. As the tickets are quite expensive I recommend to book the ticket together with a package.A lot of travel agencies have options for a train ticket incl. overnight stays in your desired japanese destination.

I had the opportunity to ride the famous & fastest bullet train in Japan, the Nozomi, from Tokyo to Osaka which took only 2 hrs & a half with short stops in Yokohama, Nagoya, & Kyoto. They leave on the dot & arrive on the dot as well. It is spotlessly clean, including the restroom, & the ride is smoother than in a plane sometimes. It's more or less like the MAGLEV in Shanghai. Some food & snacks are available on board which are reasonably priced and the staff are friendly & helpful.It tops in comfort with its ergonomic seats with plenty of legroom in between. Truly its the best & fastest way to get around Japan. However, it is more expensive than a plane.

It's best to be punctual and safe. I'm the type of person who tends to be stingy with slow trains when I'm nearby, but once in a while I'm impressed by the convenience of taking the Shinkansen. I feel that this is a vehicle that Japan can be proud of to the world.

The Tokaido Shinkansen is a transportation tool that is often used when traveling to Tokyo or Nagoya for business. There are unreserved seats, so it's convenient because you don't have to worry about departure time like you would on an airplane. I remember that it opened in 1964, the year of the Tokyo Olympics. This year marks 50 years of history. I think it is a safe means of transportation with no major accidents. I wish the price was a little lower.

Traveling via Shinkansen (or bullet train) is a must when visiting Japan. It's very convenient and the fastest way to travel. We took the train from Tokyo Station to Kyoto and purchased our tickets on the day of travel. Here is some useful info to make your travel easier:1. There are 3 classes of Shinkansen (Nozomi, Hikari, and Kodama). The difference between each is the number of stops the train makes. The Nozomi Shinkansen makes the fewest stops, and travel between Tokyo and Kyoto is around 2 hr 20 min.2. A JR rail pass is not valid on the Nozomi Shinkansen. This type of pass is usually bought in the US for longer visits (ex. 7, 14, 21 day passes).3. You can buy your ticket from a JR ticket machine at Tokyo Station; there are English instructions. However, if in doubt, there is a ticket counter where the staff knows enough English to help get you where you want to go. :)4. When buying from the JR ticket machine, a regular swipe & sign credit card does not work. You need a chip & PIN credit card, like those used in Europe. However, a regular debit card will work, since this requires you to enter a PIN. (We used our debit card.)5. Pricing is split into 2 costs, a basic fare plus a seat fare. Everyone pays the basic fare; then you either purchase a Reserved seat or an Unreserved seat. The price difference between a Reserved and Unreserved seat is minimal (830 JPY), so I'd suggest getting a Reserved seat for peace of mind (you'll have an assigned seat). My Nozomi ticket from Tokyo to Kyoto was 13,910 JPY (8,210 JPY basic fare + 5,700 JPY reserved seat).Travel on the Shinkansen was smooth and super fast. It's a great way to visit other parts of Japan from Tokyo. Enjoy the adventure! :)

I couldn't imagine how crowded it would be, so I rode from Hiroshima to Mikawa Anjo. Hiroshima is on the Sanyo Shinkansen section, but there are quite a few Nozomi trains that depart from Hiroshima, so I used them. The Tokaido Shinkansen refers to the line between Osaka and Tokyo. The Nozomi, which runs between Sanyo and Tokaido, has a 16-car train and only has unreserved seats up to the third car, but I was able to secure an unreserved seat without any difficulty by boarding from Hiroshima. After that, it was a little crowded, but it was still so crowded that I was able to go through the on-board sales. To go to Mikawa Anjo, you have to change trains once in Nagoya. At the first stop after transferring from Nagoya to Kodama, this Shinkansen was empty. This time I only rode the Kodama between Nagoya and Mikawa Anjo, but I was very surprised that it was empty even during the Obon peak.
I left for the famous Shinkansen, never late with on-board service for meals and drinks, in the end, ten minutes late and no one serving....

Caught the Bullet Train from Tokyo to Kyoto, and it was definitely an experience! Everything about the Shinkansens are so fast and efficient, from departure time to the cleaners. As soon as your train arrives you have about 30 seconds to board in order to keep in line with the departure times - so make sure you get to the station in plenty of time!!The seats are comfy, and have plenty of room. The ticket inspectors are polite and helpful too. Shame about their uniforms though.The stations also all sell various Shinkansen related souvenirs: Bullet Train scale models, Bullet Train clothes (mainly for small children), Bullet Train shaped biscuits, Bullet Train jigsaws etc.Expensive - but a once-in-a-lifetime experience.

I had the pleasure of using the Shinkansen (super-express trains) in Japan multiple times during my visit and I must admit that riding the Shinkansen was an experience by itself. It is by far more comfortable than any flight / airline I ever took, much roomier, splendidly clean, and organized – not to mention quite fast, comfortable, and an efficient method of travel. Beats all the other bullet trains I have seen in Europe.Food and beverages (alcohol included) are sold on board. It is also very quiet (i.e. inside) (people hardly talk loudly inside the train). I hardly recommend anyone visiting Japan to try it.

We took the Shinkansen "bullet train" from Hakone to Tokyo after a long day of sightseeing. I was so impressed with the comfort of the seats and lots of leg room even in the non-reserved section.  We knew we had to ride this train on our vacation and it didn't disappoint.  It was fast, punctual and comfortable.   We did have some difficulty when we got to the main station when we tried to figure out how to get to our subway. The train is a must!

We took a return trip from Tokyo to Kyoto, and this train is amazing!! We have a nice leg type, it's super fast and you feel like you're flying. Only the price slows down the desire to take it because it is quite expensive.

I made three very comfortable trips with super express trains of the “Shikansen” line from Tokyo to Nagoya (366 km in 1h 42’; price 11,090 yen ≈ 80,00 €), Kyoto to Hiroshima (380km 1h 40’;/ price 11,410 yen ≈ 83,00 €) and Hiroshima to Kyoto.  These “bullet” Japanese trains are punctual, fast, with broad seats and helpful personal.

The Japanese TGV!!!!We have lessons to learn regarding punctuality, cleanliness, courtesy of staff and quality of comfort. Nothing to do with "our TGV" which we can certainly be proud of, but it really is a class above. Arriving at the terminus station, the passengers get off and an army of people enter the cars to clean, change the headrests, prepare the train for the next journey. A dream.......Once on the train it's nothing but happiness, silence and the sweetness of life. THE BEST.....

Although the price was a little steep as compared to other modes of transport, it was worth it. The first high speed train in the world, was built in Japan so why would you not consider riding this. The only thing that I missed out on riding the Shinkansen from Tokyo to Odawara (Hakone), was getting myself a bento set for the ride.

Recently, I mostly use planes for business trips and trips, but depending on the destination, it may be more convenient to use the Shinkansen. Recently, I had the opportunity to ride the Shinkansen one after the other, so I would like to share my impressions in terms of comparison with airplanes. First of all, the good thing about the Shinkansen is that the seats have a wide front and back pitch and are very comfortable. I'm not talking about green cars, but ordinary seats, but they are far more comfortable than ordinary seats on airplanes. Also, unlike flying, where you have to make reservations in advance and get to the airport well in advance, it's great that you can hop on a train depending on the situation at the time. My first complaint is that there are too few benches on the platforms and inside the station. Although it doesn't matter if you arrive at the station a little early, there is no place to sit. The few benches are always full and you can't sit on them. On airplanes, there are usually enough seats at the boarding gate, so you can usually sit down. Is the biggest complaint about Shinkansen trains starting with the N700 series? It is the worst system that has been introduced, ``all seats are non-smoking''. To put it bluntly, this is nothing but an improvement. I don't smoke at all, and I'm a huge anti-smoker who doesn't want to inhale even an ounce of cigarette smoke. So what about the Shinkansen for me? It is true that all seats are non-smoking, but as soon as there are smokers sitting in front, rear, left, or right, it's The End. Every time that guy smokes in the smoking room and comes back, the passengers around him are exposed to second-hand smoke due to the cigarette smoke mixed in with his breath. I think JR is a complete idiot for coming up with such a careless system. From now on, even if it's a hassle, I'm going to fly.
this was an amazing experience cruzing at 300 kph speed, making it in a blink from Tokyo to Nagoya. Excellent seats, reserved. Nice japanies snacks to buy. Smooking cart available.

I have heard a lot on Japanese bullet train but one has to experience the journey to fully admire its speed, cleanliness and surprisingly always on time. I boarded this on Odawara station and a good 30 mins trip to the Tokyo Central Station as part of the Mt. Fuji Hakone tour. You don't feel the speed in the train, but when you look outside the window on trains moving past in opposite direction - its extremely fast. Close to the arriving at the Tokyo station, the train slows down until it comes to a complete stop. I then stayed in the platform for a good 15 minutes to view all the arrival and departure trains - the look of the train (the front) - as enjoyable as the journey itself. Its picks up fast on departing from the platform which I have never seen elsewhere. Next time in Tokyo, I shall go for a longer train journey.

The bullet train opened in Japan in 1964. I took the Tokyo-Kyoto route. If you are lucky and the day is clear, you will be able to see Mount Fuji. The train is very comfortable and the journey is pleasant. It is possible to have meals on board.

Used the shinkansen system for travel on a  total of 14 separate journeys from Tokyo to Nagasaki and return with numerous stops and side trips at cities along the way over a 21 day period. The JR pass was worth every penny.Tickets were easy to obtain from any JR office for our destinations and staff were happy to assist with any issues, including changing train times when we found ourselves either late or early for our service.The pre booked seating system meant we always knew where to stand on the platform to enter the carriage when the trains arrived.  Seating was comfortable and better than a lot of airplanes I have flown in.  Carriages were always clean and tidy.  On board staff were friendly and courteous at all times. Toilets and wash areas were clean and tidy also.Travelling with two large bags meant the overhead luggage racks became a small issue but we then discovered the luggage areas at the front & rear of the carriages so we had no further problems with lifting heavy bags etc onto the overhead rack.Power points fitted at each row meant we were able to charge phones, tablets etc while on the move.Travel was quiet, smooth, very fast and extremely efficient.This is the best way to travel in Japan but I suggest you ensure you reserve seats as some of the non reserved carriages I saw seemed to be very full.
