The Tokaido Shinkansen does not have many discounts and is expensive, but if you plan on staying overnight, we recommend traveling with Kodama as they are cheaper. I went to Kyoto using Kodama. It stops at all stations, but the speed between stations is the same as the Nozomi, so you can feel like you're riding a Shinkansen.
This was a superb experience. Very efficient service with very comfortable seats and ride quality. Much more comfortable than travelling by plane!

Travelled from Tokyo to Kyoto to Hiroshima and return via the Shinkansen. Rode on the "slower" units - "Hikari and Sakura" as we had a JR Pass. That was not an issue as they were only about 20 minutes slower to our final destinations and Japan being such a beautiful country - it gave us more time to appreciate the scenery and take photos of the countryside from the train.The pass is the best way to save money if making a number of longer journeys via the Shinkansen as it provides good value for money.What an amazing experience - clean, uncluttered, quiet, smooth, spacious, comfortable, relaxing and that was just the ordinary class. The seating configuration was 2 or 3 in this class. There was ample room to stretch out, the seats not only reclined but rotated a full 180 degrees to allow a larger party to have a face to face conversation. The inservice catering came through at least 2-3 times and was basic but welcome. As expected the washrooms and the toilets were spotless. There is ample space on the luggage racks above the seats on either side of the train. For larger bags you might need to consider the are  behind the seats of the last row of each carriage. We used both the reserved and non-reserved seating options. As there were 3 of us we were able to be seated together at least once with the reserved seating. It's great when you are in a hurry and you know exactly which car and seats are yours. However the non-reserved seating is just as good, but during peak or busy periods - if you want to be seated together as a family, you take your chance with where you sit. On this trip we did not have any problems in finding seats. The ride was so smooth and as others have noted - they are bang on time give or take seconds! In summary the most efficient and best way to travel between towns and major centres in Japan. Another great experience that is a must do in Japan.

I use it several times a year when going to Nagoya, Kyoto, and Osaka. When using Nozomi, there are many trains, so I decide on a flight after arriving at Tokyo Station, but Kodama only has two trains per hour, so it would be better to check the schedule in advance. Overcrowded timetables, efforts to shorten the travel time by several minutes (several seconds?) every time the timetable is revised are technologies that Japan is proud of. I was surprised to see that the time required from Tokyo to Kyoto was reduced to about 2 hours and 20 minutes.

It's a shame that you can't choose a seat from the seating chart, but it's fast and convenient. Seat B in the middle is 1.2 centimeters wider. It's a shame that on-board sales on the Kodama train are no longer available. It would be convenient if there were outlets at every seat, but the drawback is that there is only one on the wall.

Arrived at Tokyo Station at 20:33 → Keiyo Rapid from Tokyo Station at 20:37 I was able to take the B dash. . It might even be possible to transfer for 3 minutes. . Anyway, today I suddenly went to a castle country, but it feels further away than Osaka or a certain country. . Traveling by plane is so easy. . After all, you can definitely get a seat. . Bus from Sode → Haneda. I thought about this while riding the Keiyo train on my way home. Please come to Maglev soon. . Free seats on the Shinkansen both on the way there and on the way back. Surprisingly, coming from Nagoya, you can sit down. Nagoya has a wide variety of food specialties, and gourmet food is fun. .
If you reserve seats in advance on certain shinkasen trains you are likely to get allocated the better seats on the train. These are larger and provide more leg room.

Travelled from Hakone-Kyoto then Kyoto-Tokyo by Shinkansen. Most amazing way to travel - EXACTLY on time, very comfortable seats, super clean, especially the toilets, extremely polite train staff,WOW!There are three types of bullet trains - kodama, hikari and nozomi, with the kodama being the "slowest" with the most stops and the nozomi being the superexpress. Most seats are reserved and when travelling in groups, it is better to book reserved seats (for a small additional fee) if you want to ensure the group sits together. There are a few cars for non-reserved seat passengers. If you want to be near a smoking area, you can indicate this if buying the ticket from the counter staff and they will place you in a car near the designated smoking areas (about 3 - 4 smoking areas per train, each train is about 16 cars long).
A very comfortable mode of transport, impressive design, timetables ALWAYS respected, not to mention the possibility of very advantageous passes for foreigners, the Shinkansen is a real pleasure.

Travelled between Osaka - Hiroshima - Kyoto - Tokyo using the Shinkansen (bullet train) and it was amazing. Very efficient (stops for exactly 2 minutes), most carriages are pre book only, very spacious and amazingly clean.Great way to travel whilst in Japan

When we took the Full Moon trip many times before, we placed it in the gap at the back, but my wife and I, who are anxious people, were worried that someone would take it away. However, when I rode in a regular car this time, I placed it vertically between the seats so that the handle could be clipped between the seats, and found that it didn't move and worked very well. This was not possible in the green car because it had a footrest. Thanks to the fine weather, I was able to enjoy the wonderful view of Mt. Fuji from the train window.

Travelled from Kobe to Tokyo on the Shinkansen.  What a way to travel! Clean, frequent, on-time, fast and relaxing.  The seat was big, roomy, comfortable for work or a nap (which I did for an hour thanks to jet lag).    Great way to travel.  I wish the US had a train system like this.  Only downside was arriving during rush hour to Tokyo station.  Thankfully we had someone with us who knew their way around.

Shinkansen means new trunk line, referring to the high-speed rail line network. It is a network of high-speed railway lines in Japan. We used the Shinkansen out from Shinagawa Station (Tokyo) to Kyoto Station using a Japan Rail Pass. So fast and quiet. You find food service on the train, as every where in Japan polite and efficient. Girls pushing carts with snacks and drinks for sale up and down the train cars. Watch how they bow to the occupants when the girl enter and leave each train car, The trains are on time and the seats are very comfortable, All seats are revolving seats, always arranged in the direction of the way the train travel.

Shinagawa station(Tokyo) to Nagoya station in under 1hr 50 minutes. Used this link for more than 20 times now and 10 out of 10 they were punctual with time!! If you travel during lunch time and evening people eating their bento(packed lunch/dinner) but it is normal in Japan!! Ticket is always easy to buy and the Shinkansen is always clean like most of the Japanese cities!! When you are going to Nagoya direction then try to get a ticket on the right side then returning on the left side so that if you are lucky then you can see the beautiful mount Fuji. Bento boxes in various kiosk and at the station is very safe to eat!! They are slightly expensive but the quality is very good. If you want more variety of food then I advise you to travel from Tokyo station. You will be lost for choice!! I have used TGV before but each time they arrived at the destination 5 -10 minutes late!! You can not beat the japanese efficiencies!!

This time I used it from Tokyo to Shin-Osaka. I was carrying a large suitcase. I was worried about whether there would be a place to store it. There was quite a gap between the last seat of the vehicle and the wall, so I was able to get in safely. When I bought a reserved ticket, I told them that, and the ticket was issued smoothly, as is often the case.

Personally I feel every country should invest in one! It's reliable, fast, clean, spacious and comfortable way to get around. Used this train to travel between Kyoto and Tokyo. We reserved the seats a few hours before departure time to get the seat with Mt. Fuji view (right side of the train going from Tokyo to Kyoto). You will get a great view of Mt. Fuji from the big window. Eating is allowed inside the train and food is also sold on board. The train is a great piece of engineering; it moves very fast and it doesn't wobble at all. It also looks amazing on the outside (its nose looks like a plane). Very impressed and it was well worth the price. One thing to note is you need to be quiet inside as with all other transport in Japan.

It's a great, safe and secure vehicle. In any case, Japan is proud of the fact that no major accidents have occurred yet. The ride was comfortable, but if you were in the car behind the smoking seats, you could smell cigarettes even in the non-smoking seats. I would like it to be completely non-smoking, but at the very least I would like it to be only allowed to smoke in the last car. Also, I think it would be better if the stations along the way were interesting.

Used this for 3 weeks. Back home i miss them. fast, clean, and on time! used it with my JR pass. From Tokyo to Osaka, Kyoto and Hiroshima. if you visit japan, you really need to travel with these. reserve your seat, take your place on the platform and the train will stop in front of your nose. heavy suitcase are a small problem, but i used 2 heavy suitcaes on all my trains and i always found a solution (not all trains are fully booked)best way of transportation i used so far in all my traveling.

I had always heard about these trains, but imagined them to be overrated - I was wrong.  We had a Japan Rail Pass (Green Car status) and took the the Shinkansen several places in Japan.  The seats are very spacious and have plenty of room for luggage, coats, laptop, etc.  They also have usb pugs as each seat.  The trains run exactly on time, at top speeds.  The windows are very large and provide a great view of the countryside.  There is a great view of Mt. Fuji between Tokyo and Kyoto!  The trains were easy to use and easy to make reservations on in Japan, even for two people who speak NO Japanese.  A great traveling experience!

I wanted to get it cheap anyway, so I used it on my way back from Kyoto. Then I noticed that the Kodama wasn't slow, but that it was stopping for a long time. It will make 5-minute stops at Maibara, Toyohashi, Shinfuji, Mishima, Odawara, etc. By checking the timetable and making a list of local specialties, you can have an interesting and delicious trip.

I went on a trip to Kyoto with the 700 series Kodama, which seems to be nearing retirement, from Tokyo to Shin-Osaka due to the expansion of the N700 series. It's true that there are many hardware aspects that are inferior to the latest N700 series, but the green car was comfortable enough. I usually use it for work, but the Kodama is also great for private trips where you can enjoy the view from the train window. If your goal is simply to get around, then an express train would be better as it will take you as little time as possible, but the Kodama seemed to be well worth the effort if you were looking to enjoy the journey itself. I would like to see Kodama reinstate the discontinued in-car sales.

This is, by far, the only way to travel!!  We connected from the Narita Express from the airport and hopped on at Shinagawa.  A littler over 2 hours later we were in Nagoya.  Awesome.  Lots of room for luggage overhead.  Comfortable , roomy seating.  Reasonable price overall 26,000 Y for reserved seats for 2 from the airport.

As other reviewers have mentioned, this is the best way to travel in Japan.   You can only buy the 7, 14, 21 day JR Rail pass outside of Japan.   They're only available to foreigners.   I got the 7 day where I stayed in Shin-Yokohama, went to Tokyo in 20 minutes, then went down to Kyoto in less than 2.5 hours.   From Kyoto, you can go to Osaka in less than 15 minutes and to Kobe another 15 minutes.   Very convenient, clean and relaxing.   In Kyoto, you can also go to Nara Park by subway in 10 minutes and walk 10 minutes or by JR train which you can use this JR pass for 20 minutes.

The bullet train is very efficient, it arrives at the scheduled time without fail! Very quickly, as I didn't have much time I decided to take the Tokaido line and stop in Odawara to spend the night, it was really cool, we stayed in a very small hotel and got to know the local habits. It was very worth it.
I travelled kyoto-tokyo-kyoto(price: about 27000 JY)( time: 2h 28') nosomi trainVery amazing experience High tech,clean, notably on time , Neat,helpful,polite staffsNote: take reserved seat ticket

This time, I had a disabled child in a wheelchair traveling from Okayama to Tokyo, so I used the multipurpose room (reservation required). We used the N700 series multipurpose room. The multi-purpose room was relatively large, with plenty of room to move around even in a wheelchair, and the seats could accommodate two people, which could also be converted into a bed. It also has an outlet. There is also a toilet that can be used by wheelchair users right next to the multipurpose room, which was helpful. There was also a window in the room so we could enjoy the outside view.

Whether you're traveling or doing business, you can travel between Tokyo and Osaka in 2 hours and 15 minutes (Nozomi), which is amazing, and you can just sleep during that time...If the ride was comfortable and the price was a little cheaper, it would be the best. At Shinagawa Station, you'll also encounter four "Doctor Yellow" trains a day, so even though it's business, it's still fun!

We travelled from Kyoto to Tokyo but unfortunately we travelled in the evening and missed daylight views of Mount Fuji. The experience was still fantastic and experiencing the efficiency, cleanliness and speed of the train was second to none.  Make sure you pick up a bento box before embarking the journey and enjoy it with a nice cold 'Asahi'.

My first Shinkansen was the Hikari. I'll never forget the thrill I felt when I started running smoothly. I choose the Shinkansen from Tokyo to Osaka because there are no baggage restrictions like on an airplane, and you can easily board the train if you arrive 5 minutes before the departure time. The time is accurate, and the N700 series has a power outlet so you can charge your cell phone or PC (window seat only), so you'll be able to spend your business trip comfortably.

There are good value plans that include drinks, so unless I'm in a hurry I often ride Kodama. It's also very convenient that you can make reservations online, and tickets will be sent to you for an additional 200 yen. You can also choose a seat facing Mt. Fuji when making a reservation, so don't forget if you want to view the view from your seat.
Super fast, Super duper fast, and Super duper ultra fast.Those are the three speeds you'll get on the Tokaido Shinkansen and it services Tokyo all the Way to Kyoto and Osaka. Highly recommended.
The bullet train is very interesting, thanks to this transportation you can get to know Japan from north to south in a short travel time and the trip is very comfortable.

High speed, punctual, comfortable, reliable - what more do you need to you say about the Shinkansen between Nagoya and Tokyo? The Japanese are blessed with a narrow and long country, so a central rail line can serve a huge part of the population. The very different geography of Japan explains the heavy use and convenience of this rail line, while here in the U.S. we depend more on highways and air travel.Be aware that there are three levels of service on the Shinkansen, which in my words I'll call "express" (few stops and fastest time between major stations), "intermediate", and "local" (stopping at every station and adding significantly to travel time). The faster service comes with a higher price.You have the option of buying a reserved or unreserved seat, and taking your chances. I always opt for a reserved seat, and the added cost, so I'm not worried about finding a spot to settle in for the journey.

The speed is insane. 280 kim per hour although you would never feel it inside.  It:s comfortable and they sell snacks and drinks and all sorts.  It:s almost always on time, unless of emergency, like an earthquake (which in fact happened to me).  Gets you there fast!

We took the fastest bullet train Nozomi from Tokyo to Kyoto.The train frequency is every 30 minutes, ride time around 2 hrs. Th whole journey was superb, the train is fast, quiet and stable. i love the journey especially riding with the well mannered Japanese, they are so quiet and speak very softly, the train comes with 'chatting room' for someone who needs to takk on the mobile, so cool ! The train is well mintained, very clean and with comfortable seat. The stewardess serves food and drinks in the train (payable as not included in the fare)The train fare does not come cheap, around SG160 for our one way trip.We travelled with big luggages from hotel to metro station to the train station with little problem as the path is smooth and easy.

This is, by far, the best way to travel. The train is literally designed for speed (the front "nose" looks like something from a sci-fi film). It is comfortable, efficient, smooth and altogether a delight. Plus, there are food carts that come by a few times an hour. Take note of the ticket collectors who bow before and after they leave each car.When booking, be sure to request a window seat as parts of the countryside are just spectacular.

The high-speed train is an example in every sense. Fast, extremely clean and punctual. The impeccable staff. A pleasure to travel through the amazing Japan on this railway wonder that has celebrated 50 years of existence.

Travelled from Osaka to Hiroshima and to Tokyo, on time, fast, clean, silent and efficient.All Japanese Railways trains from Shinkansen to Express to Local trains were incredible as we're the staff who helped and guided us throughout our time in Japan

As other travellers have stated, it is definitely cheaper than flying. But we calculated that the JR Pass was actually more expensive. There are several independently owned train lines in Japan and JR is only one of them... The Shinknsen ticket (Osaka to Tokyo) can be bought from $130 to $150 for one way (if you are able to buy the tickets locally rather than from the train station. Train station cost is around $150). We travelled with a 2 year old, and didn't have to pay for him. We had reserved seats for ourselves (you book this at the train station)... The seating is 3 seats on one side and 2 on the other. We unfortunately did not have the 3rd seat free for the entire trip. There is plenty of room, but still a little uncomfortable.Also note there are different types of Shinkansen, and the Nozomi is the fastest (Osaka to Tokyo in 2hrs 30mins). It doesn't really feel like you are travelling that fast as it is so smooth and comfortable.There is no restaurant dining car, but a cart is pushed around regularly. Otherwise you can purchase a bento box on the platform before getting on the train.Another great way to get around and see some of the countryside.

Travelled from Tokyo to Osaka in 2.5 hrs. Its cheaper than flight and frequency is each 30 min. Convenient to catch from JR Tokyo station and get the ticket from counter itself. Occupency is hardly 30-40% so no co passanger in ur dual seat. Even for a first time travellor it was so convenient.

The “bullet train” or Shinkansen as it’s locally termed, is a symbol of Japanese pride. This train service is now celebrating 50yrs of services without accident, a remarkable achievement indeed.There are several services available depending on your travel destinations, and information can be found on the website. I travelled from Tokyo-Kyoto return on the “Nozomi” service, which is the super-express option for around $US 135 each way, taking only 2hrs20mins. There are two slower (cheaper) services with more stops taking 3 and 4hrs so make sure you get what you need.Seating layout is similar to economy or coach class airlies, although with a lot more leg room. Travelling with large suitcases would be problematic; the largest standard rollaboard suitcase for airlines is about as big as you want to go. There’s a smoking car for those so inclined, snacks and beverage options to purchase on the way. A very convenient and comfortable way to go far in a short space of time without the hassle of getting through airports.

as the other reviews demonstrate, this is a fantastic mode of rail travel. took this between Tokyo from Tokyo station and Kyoto. Definitely get the JR pass from outside Japan - especially if you are staying in Tokyo as the JR lines are a great alternative to the metro and if you have this pass you don't have to pay anything additional :)the staff were very helpful in converting our passes into tickets. the only thing i will warn you is - when we booked 5 days ahead of when we needed to be in Tokyo, there was only a single seat left in the non-smoking carriages. we figured, how bad could smoking section be? (we're both ex smokers too) - it was practically unbearable. ours might have had a faulty filtration system, but it was not a good experience. if you do not smoke currently, do not bother and take another train!other than that, and on the way back in the non-smoking section, it was a very quiet, comfortable and relaxing way to travel.

During our trip to Japan we often traveled on the JR Shinkansen.  The Shinkansen train runs between many of the larger Japanese cities.  The Japanese Rail System is an extremely efficient and organized railway.  Someone told us before we left that you could set your watch according to the trains scheduled arrival and departure times and after having traveled on many of the JR routes I would agree 100%.  The trains are supper clean, comfortable and very fast (top speed is 300 KPH!!).  It’s hard to get used to zipping along at 180 miles per hour while still on the ground.  What’s more amazing is that the passengers and staff move about the cars as if it was crawling along at 10 mph!!    The whole train travel experience in Japan is seamless.  Once you get used to the train station ticket dispensing machines they are quick and easy to use.  Directions to and from the various train platforms are well marked with overhead LED signs, which scroll in both Japanese and English.  And if you run into trouble you can usually find a friendly and helpful JR staff person to help you find your way.  The faster, larger Shinkansen trains connect to all of the smaller regional lines at most of the terminals/stations, so if you want to travel to some of the smaller rural areas this is easy to do.Train travel is by far the easiest and best way to travel in Japan.

First , before coming to Japan , get the JR Pass (Japan Rail Pass ) from selected tour firms in your country or the Japan Travel Bureau ( if there's one ) ( in Malaysia kat bangunan Amoda , kat jalan Imbi , belakang lowyat ) Goggle for easy reference .With the JR pass you can travel up and down Japan Shinkansen as many times as you want .That's what I did , from Tokyo to Nagoya - Kyoto - Osaka and back and stop along interesting stations / towns and get back on the next schedule.Its fast , clean , spacious , timely .The HIKARI express stops at selected stations while the KODAMA stops at every stations. Get down at Shin Fuji Station - to view Mt Fuji ( on a clear day )  and also get down at Odarama station if you want to join the ' tour ' to get closer view of Mt Fuji ( by normal train - Bus - Boat - RopeWalk - Cable car ) For Malaysian get your JR pass from the japan travel bureau , it cost around rm1,000 ( depend on rate) for a 7 days pass and your actual train rides cost more than rm2,000 Also can use the pass on any JR lines in tokyo,kyoto n osaka . Friendly and annoucements in the Shinkansen also in English.

The Tokaido Shinkansen is fast and convenient, but the drawback is that it is expensive. However, if you are not in a hurry and want to go to Kodama, it is better to use Plat Kodama. In addition to Kodama's reserved seats, a drink is included for 10,000 yen between Tokyo and Shin-Osaka. The speed of the Kodama train doesn't change much, and the stops at each station are long, so I enjoyed the ekiben as I rode.

The Shinkansen is widely used for work, travel, etc. It's been a while since I saw Yellow Doctor. That's cool. When I was waiting for Hikari at Odawara Station, I pulled up next to the platform and couldn't help but take a photo. The kids on the trip had a blast. The Shinkansen that is exported overseas is Japan's pride.

Known worldwide as the bullet train, it is very efficient and comfortable transport. Timetables are strictly adhered to, so much so that every year, the system records a delay of just 1 minute on all lines. very comfortable armchairs, you can eat inside the carriages, people take their bentô and or if they don't, they can buy it from the trolleys made available. The seats are numbered, very comfortable. People even prefer to go to distant cities on shinkanse, as the comfort is comparable to that of airplanes, without the famous hassles of checking in and checking bags.
Great way to travel. Be sure to confirm tickets for the seats you want days before travel.Green car was nice - uncrowded luxury.Would recommend this to anyone. The Japanese do train travel so well.

The trains are on time, the seats are comfortable, it's easy to purchase tickets, the staff is helpful, and the ride is smooth on the Shinkansen.  I'd recommend buying a bento box and a beer at the train station right before you board (and you don't need to get there too early before your train) and enjoying it on your trip.  Two small warnings: first, the ride is not very scenic.  You'll see some mountains and open grassland, but by and large you'll be zipping through small towns that all look the same.  (You can briefly see Mt. Fuji on a clear day if you look to the north, but look quick!)  Second - make sure you are on the right train!  They run so often and on a compressed schedule that you may make the mistake of getting on an earlier train.

Since much time Japan has no longer the exclusive of high-speed rail, so the experience of it can be more thoughtful. Compared to Italian and French HSR (the only ones of which I have experience) I see the following differences:- Maximum commercial speed a bit lower (270 km/h against 300 or even 320)- Exceptionally precise indication of the exact points of access to your coach- Greater distribution of the benefits of HSR in the territories, thanks to the co-existence of Shinkansen with very few stops (Nozomi) and Shinkansen with more stops- Revolving seats, always arranged in the direction of travel (which is not possible for example in Italy, because there are some stations where the train reverses). That gives great comfort to the ride, and also allows wider space between rows of seats.
Talk about train riding, fast as a cannonball but soft as a duvet. Comfortable travel in a nice design. Recommended to all, if only for a short distance.

This train service was a luxurious land travel experience and was a marvel even compared to the TGV. But if you have taken the Shanghai maglev and Beijing bullet trains, it is not as perfect anymore. We took it recently from Tokyo and Nagano and we found the train to be super packed with people having to stand up in between cars. Not much space to put in our luggage and the speed is of course slow compared to the maglev. We found the Narita express train to be a better transport and understandable since it is newer.

Took this train using a Japan Rail Pass from Shin-Yokohama to Kyoto and back while on vacation and was amazed how fast and quiet it was. We had reserved seats (not hard to get by using the JR ticketing office at the station - no extra cost with the Rail Pass and can be done virtually at the last minute) so we didn't have to worry about seat availability. Check the "Japan Rail Pass" website for particulars on obtaining/using the pass. The trains run regularly between major cities, though some cities have the "Shin" stations separate from the main stations because of the tracks the Shinkansen operate on, and you may have to take a connecting regular train to get into the city. We took the "Hikari", which are the moderately fast Shinkansen and for which the JR Pass is usable - they still go more than 125 mph and ride very smoothly. There is food service on the train; polite and efficient girls push carts with snacks and drinks for sale up and down the train cars (note how they bow to the occupants when they enter and leave each train car), and there are smoking areas on the train though not smoking cars. Restrooms are located about every other car, and are super clean. Each passenger's seat has a drop down tray in front of it to eat or work off of, and imprinted on the underside of the tray is a diagram of what car you are in, the relationship to the front of the train, and where the restrooms (Western and Japanese style) are located. There are overhead racks large enough to put your average roll-around luggage pieces. At the stations where you board your train, there are markings on the platform edges that denote the car number, and if you have a reserved seat in car number 10 for example, just look for the number 10 on the platform and Shinkansen car #10 will stop exactly there. The arrival/departure times of the Shinkansen are literally within seconds of the scheduled times, so if you are as much as a minute late you will miss your train. If you do not have a JR Pass, the ride can be expensive, and the down side of riding this train is that if you want to take photos of some of the amazing scenery, you will not be able to due to the speed you are moving.
We traveled to Kyoto, it felt like we were on a plane, comfortable, safe, clean, I recommend it to everyone who has the opportunity to travel on a Shinkansen.

I used train from Tokyo to Sendai, but unfortunately there was an earthquake during my ride to Sendai, the train 30mins late, but it's very rare for this train to be late, so still I could understand this. And when I arrived Sendai they cash-back 50% of ticket value.The seats are large, and plenty space to stretch legs, there is space for luggage, and clean toilates &  hand-wash. This overall very clean train, and the news & updates stream via LED screen inside the train, and most of automatic announcement comes in English & Japanese.Skinkansen is a symbol of modern Japan, so it's very liable and very effective, and highly recommend it for traveling cross Japan.

What great value a Japan Rail pass is. We used it for many journeys using local JR trains, but the main ones were Narita to Shinagawa return (Narita Express), Shinkansen from Tokyo to Kyoto, Kyoto to Hiroshima return, Kyoto to Kobe and Kobe to Shinagawa. We were in the Green Car which is like business class. The trains are incredibly punctual, fast and comfortable. It is so much better to travel by Shinkansen than air particularly if your hotels are located near the Shin stations. Smooth and stable the feeling as the train accelerates is like a land based Concorde! Do it!

I tried the bullet train as they call it in English and I can only compliment the entire organization. The customer I visited explained to me that the lines are managed by private companies, and everything could only work for the best. The train leaves very punctually and the one I had to take was a local because it stopped at all the stations.       Around here, use is so widespread that during a 25-minute wait to wait for mine, I saw at least a dozen trains passing by.     An indescribable thing. If you are traveling with bulky suitcases, these trains do not have an adequate location. The Japanese usually travel with very limited luggage. However, it is possible to put bulky ones behind the last seat depending on the direction of the train. Since each carriage has only one access door, I suggest the following carriages: if you are traveling from Tokyo to Osaka, then opt for carriage 8 with seats around row 17, while in the direction from Osaka in Tokyo ask for carriage 10 around row 1. All because the seats are turned 180 degrees depending on the direction, and the largest place to leave bulky suitcases is behind the last seat of each carriage. Have a good trip.

It is not straining to say that the Shinkansen is to Japan as the Cable car is to San Francisco or the Gondola is to Canal Grande in Venice. And the classic postcard from Japan is this fast, white train crossing a long bridge and the Mt Fuji with its perfect, snow capped cone, in the background. The distance from Tokyo to Kyoto (513,6 Km – 318,6 miles) is covered in 138 minutes which means, for example, that the Nozomi (the fastest train with very few stops) #207 leaves from Tokyo at 08.00 and reaches Kyoto at 10.18 am. The average speed is 250kmh (155mph) and the total, one way price, is 13320 Yen. Onboard we do not have the perception of such a great speed, probably because this train operates on a dedicated (larger gauge) railway line. There are 5 seat rows in the normal cars (3+2) and 4 rows (2+2) in the Green Cars (the 1st class, a bit more expensive). Ask for a window seat at the JR ticket office: on the left side if you want to see the Pacific Ocean (not a great view); on the right side if, just a few minutes after Yokohama station, you want to enjoy the exciting view of Mt Fuji (in summertime it will be harder, due to the hazy weather) or, near Nagoya, some hills with nice rural villages and some small tea plantations. Inside your train, enjoy the unusual (for westerners) view, like a ritual ceremony, of the train staff that, when they enter or exit your car, they curtsey respectfully. At the arrival in Kyoto, you cannot keep the green ticket as a souvenir because you’ve to drop it inside the machine to go out. Enter the main concourse and enjoy from below the view of the 15 storey futuristic building, full of shops, vending machines and, of course, crowds of busy people.A couple of tips: to organize with calm from home your trip, city to city, visit the web site of the Central Japan Railways http://english.jr-central.co.jp/info/timetable/index.html or, even better, the TrainRouteFinder http://www.jorudan.co.jp/english/norikae/ which gives immediate information from place to place, about the number of each train, schedules, prices, distances in Km, connecting stations, choice of type of trains etc. Once I had prepared my itinerary, I printed all these details, day by day, and showed the print at the JR ticket office because sometimes it’s tragic to try to be understood. They really try to do their best, but very few people speak English.

My first trip on the Shinkansen from Tokyo to Odawara. 100kms I think in 30mins. Very comforatble with plenty of leg room. You can BYO as many locals were enjoying a beer in the evening. What amazed me was the Tokyo-Nagoya shinkansen that roared passed at more than 250kmph. Next visit I am hopping on that train!!

We've visited Japan 3 times and each time we've bought the so-called Japan Rail Pass which offers you unlimited travel on nearly every train in Japan. The Shinkansen which is a high speed train connects all the big cities in the country and you can get access to other cities by using JR pass and changing to normal trains. In one word: a world class service, definitely the best public transportation on Earth.

Nearly 50 years have passed since the Tokaido Shinkansen opened, and Shin●● Station, which was once located in a remote area, has now become an open area with convenient transportation. I was surprised at how many station buildings were built at Shin-Yokohama Station in Kanagawa. Railway fares in Japan are expensive, but Shinkansen fares are even more expensive! If you buy a round-trip trip at the regular price, your wallet will remain loose, but if you buy a package sold by a travel agency, you'll save a lot of money because it includes the round-trip trip and local accommodation. Unlike airplanes, it's easy to use, and the best part is that the fares don't change much even during busy seasons. Diamonds are plentiful, accurate, and comfortable. Japan's proud THE SHINKANSEN!

The highlight of the Tokaido Shinkansen is the scenery from Tokyo to Osaka. You can enjoy many of Japan's famous places such as the Atami coast, Oigawa River, Odawara, Lake Hamana, Mt. Fuji, and more. Nozomi's reserved seats are spacious, so you can enjoy the scenery from the train window while eating your lunch. When I go on a business trip to Osaka, I take the train from Shin-Yokohama, and Shin-Yokohama Station is also a small gourmet town where you can buy a variety of bento boxes.

My husband and I bought the JR Rail ticket for 7 days in Italy. It is best to validate the voucher at Narita airport upon arrival, setting the date from when to start using the ticket. We used it for 3 long sections with the shinkansen. The pass is also valid for local trains and JR ferries. The Shinkansen is wonderful. It is advisable to book your seat in advance. The carriage number is written on the train track. The train is spotless, on perfect time and is an experience not to be missed
For a trip to Osaka, I took the Nozomi train from Shin-Yokohama Station to Shin-Osaka Station. I saw many businessmen in suits on Friday after 5pm.

Amazing.Japanese public transport (along with the toilets) is one of the things I miss the most.Punctual, fast and comfortable. I travelled from Tokyo to Osaka and I cannot believe the distance these trains cover in under three hours. We also travelled from Osaka to Kyoto - it took us 15 minutes on the Shinkansen compared to the 30+ minutes on other trains. If you have a JR pass, use the Shinkansen wherever possible.If you are travelling with suitcases like we were, I recommend taking a seat in the last row of the carriage. There is space behind those seats that is large enough to keep your luggage. I don't believe there were any other storage facilities as such?

It's really comfortable. Compared to overseas TGVs and high-speed trains, it is quieter, more comfortable, and more comfortable. Passengers are also nice and quiet. Seats are more spaced out and more comfortable than economy seats on airplanes. I don't think airplanes will ever reach this level.

We took it from Osaka to Kyoto (15 minute ride) and from Osaka to Tokyo (3 hour ride). We had the Japan Rail Pass (JR Pass). You must pay for your place and your seat reservation in addition. Everything is very simple with the JR Pass! We were able to rest for 3 hours after leaving our rental in Osaka and before looking for our new apartment in Tokyo.

There are many trains from Tokyo Station to Kyoto, so take a non-reserved seat. After staying in Kyoto for one night, we stayed around Lake Biwa in Shiga Prefecture, and since the Yone nuclear power plant Hikari train took a long time, we changed trains in Nagoya and headed home easily. It's convenient after all.

On busy days, the aisles are filled with people and I feel uncomfortable even if I sit there. If it's a free day, you can really relax and it's great. I thought I would be able to sit in the unreserved seats, but it seemed like there were other people thinking the same thing, so that wasn't the case. Well, to be honest, it's luck.

We purchased the Japan Rail pass and a Green 7 day pass which is the upper class coaches.  We used the bullet trains on several occasions Tokyo to Kyoto, Kyoto to Hiroshima and back again and the trains are amazing.However, I do have a gripe with the reservation system.  Why have some of the most sophisticated trains in the world.  An electronics system across all public transport which would be the envy of the world and then make you go to the ticket desk every-time you want to travel, as the green pass, which please remember is the upper or 1st class, is reservation only.  You cannot book a seat anywhere but the ticket office...... which often had queues two or three deep.There are even ticket lines only for today and if you don’t manage to book in advance you can turn up at these and the train and reservations are sold out!   I just don’t understand it why you cannot book a ticket online....Other than that, the trains are fabulous, always on time, clean and have all the facilities you could need.
Took the train from Kyoto to Tokyo. It was a fast and comfortable trip. I don’t speak Japanese, but found it easy to find my platform and train.

Recently travelled to 4 different destinations on the Shinkansen Bullett train, Tokyo,Osaka,Hiroshima,Nagoya, Kyoto, and every one was pleasant,super quick and a joy to travel. Very quiet travelling when on board, and the way to travel within Japan if possible.

The Tokaido Shinkansen has been used for many years. I've used it more times than I can count. At the time of writing this review, the last time I used the train was in November 2019, and this time I arrived at Nagoya while I was sleeping and rode to Osaka in a daze.

Bought a Japanese Rail pass, this gives you unlimited access apart from the two quickest trains. Not a massive issue, the ones we used, Hikari, was just as fast just a couple more stops from Tokyo to Kyoto. Very punctual and very clean. Seats were more comfortable than they at first appear.

The Shinkansen lets you travel Very comfortably. Very spaceous seats. Smaller bags can be stored overhead and there is even room for larger suitcases. They sell some snacks and coffe. We orderd our railpass vouchers before arriving in Tokyo. Once at Narita airport we picked up our passes and made seat reservations at the JR office for all our travells in Japan. Including for the Narita express. We had prior to arriving looked up timetables at Hyperdia, that made the reservations very smooth and in 10 minutes we had all our seats booked for our week stay.
when you want to travel in Japan, you must take the FAST bullet trains!  Fun, Fast, high quality, great seats, great bathrooms, clean!
I am grateful that the seats near the wall have power outlets. After Shin-Yokohama is Nagoya. You can travel from Tokyo to Nagoya in no time. If the weather is nice, you can see Mt. Fuji.

Our tour group travelled on the Shinkansen from Hakone to Tokyo and no-one should travel to Japan without experiencing this.  We arrived early and watched several trains flash through our Station at incredible speeds up to 320 kmh, before our train arrived to take us to Tokyo.  Their timing is perfect and during the trip several guards walked through our carriage, stopping before entering the next carriage to bow to the passengers.  A fantastic experience.

What a great way to see lots of Japan in a modest amount of time. Buy the week-long JR Pass and go through the side entrances, which will also reassure you that you are boarding to the correct platform. Get reserved seats. Yes, the Japanese do line up at the number painted on the sides. As mentioned earlier, train cars and facilities are squeaky clean and leg room is plentiful. We had been advised not to take luggage, but due to the typhoon our first hotel told us they could not guarantee delivery within two days, and we were were all aboard with our usual carry ons -- the same ones we had not checked on the flight over. There is plenty of overhead space -- as generous as an airline. Just don't try to take one of those mammoth hard sided cases. Settle in and be prepared to be amazed.

More often than not, we are forced to travel by air when abroad to maximize our time. However, in Japan's case, the Shinkansen was MUCH more convenient. Super easy to embark/disembark. Incredibly punctual (on all 3 journeys). The seating is comfortable and reclines much further than airplane's, has tons of leg room, there is a power outlet, and the windows provide great views (of Mount Fuji on the Tokaido line for example). Finally, everything is clean (incl bathrooms!)

Used on a business trip to Tokyo. Although it is from Osaka, it is convenient to take the Shinkansen to Tokyo. Since we use SmartEX, it is easy to make reservations, and you can change the time as many times as you like, so you can make early reservations.

My lovely wife and I took our first Shinkansen “bullet” train from Tokyo to Kyoto.  The train arrives at it departure station about 20 minutes before departure time. The cleaning crew then go to work - vacuuming, cleaning and tidying the train. Unbelievable efficiency and attention to detail. We boarded about 8 minutes before departure - overhead storage large enough for sizeable suitcases and large, comfortable seats with a power point. A food trolley does the rounds if you want something to eat or drink en route. The toilets as also clean and a pleasure to use. As expected we left exactly on time and arrived in Kyoto exactly on time. Wonderful experience all round.

The retirement of the 700 series Shinkansen, known as the Platypus, from the Tokyo exit is approaching. Recently, the number of temporary nozomi has decreased visibly. When using the Tokaido Shinkansen, for the past few years I have been going out of my way to use the 700 series whenever possible. Compared to the N700 series, it's noisy, shakes, doesn't have an outlet, and is obviously less comfortable. But...the 700 series is exactly the Shinkansen that I admired when I was a child. It's the gateway to something extraordinary, such as returning home or traveling. When I was a child, I remember the joy I felt when I was able to ride the Shinkansen, a rare opportunity. The same goes for the 0 series, 100 series, 300 series, and 500 series, but these have already been retired from the forefront (the 500 series remains, but only 8 cars). The N700 series is really comfortable and I have no doubt that I will continue to use it. Today I also saw the N700 Supreme for the first time and was excited. However, I would like to stay with the 700 series for a while longer and reminisce about the old days.

We used these trains a few times during our stay in Japan and were all very impressed. On time, clean, comfy seats with plenty of leg room, wi fi, food trolley with choice, pleasant staff. Coming from Britain this is all very new to us. Bought a Bento box to eat on the train as I read that's what everyone does - I was the only one !!! Oh well - I still enjoyed it. All sat together on the RHS and got good views and photos of Mt Fuji. Tried to reserve seats using out JR rail pass on several occasions but failed each time as they were all taken, even 6 days in advance were all gone, and from what I could make out this is quite normal so we gave up trying, especially when you see the queue at the JR ticket offices, they are all very busy all of the time

An amazing first time experience on the Tokaido Shinkansen this October. The trains were super punctual and clean, simply outstanding. Buying tickets was easier than expected as well, seat reservation advisable.

On my way back from a business trip to Shizuoka, I went to the Midori no Madoguchi ticket office to take the Hikari train back to Tokyo, but unfortunately all the reserved seats were occupied. I was tired and wanted to sit down and go home, so I decided to go back to the next Kodama. The station staff at the counter told me, ``It's going to be quite late,'' but I figured it wouldn't be a big deal and took a reserved seat on the Kodama for the same price as the Hikari. As I rode the train, I realized that the train stopped for a long time at each station. It took longer than I expected and was a huge failure.

Sp many bullet trains lead to Tokyo. I experienced seven or eight  trips, all of which were phenomenal. So fast  so smooth, so comfortable. They pull away from station's at a rate of knots.Makes British railways a total embarrassment.All very impressive.

The Japanese run their trains on-time and brilliantly.  Make sure you are ready to get on and off the trains on the posted schedule because they run their trains on-time.  Quick, safe and clean travel.

High-speed railways have been built all over Europe, but when you ride the Shinkansen, you'll be amazed at how many trains there are and how accurate the schedule is. It's amazing how easy it is to travel long distances without feeling special.
Fast, clean, punctual, nothing better to get around Japan than its impressive JR bullet trains. Recommended
This is Tokaido Shinkansen's famous ice cream. As a characteristic, it is hard and clapperboard. It doesn't dissolve easily.

A very comfortable ride. Get a seat on the right hand side for a view of Mt Fuji about 40 min into the trip. No snow on the summit in October 2019 but it was a long hot summer apparently. The seat were spacious in the green cars which are worth booking.

We took the Bullet train from Tokyo to Kyoto recently and were very impressed by the speed and comfort in our carriage. Tickets were easy to purchase a few days before travelling and cost about AU$250 each for about a 2 and a half hour trip which was ideal for travellers with limited time.

Obviously not cheap but worth doing once. My trip from Tokyo to Takasaki (about 50 minutes) cost about £40. They are very comfortable, smooth, and clearly very fast. You can easily book in a JR office on Tokyo station.

Worth the travel..We travelled from shin Osaka to Tokyo and vice versa..It was worth the trip..it was less than 3 hr  but I never get bored..Stunning views we saw ..If u want to see the majestic Mt Fuji.. reserve a seat by the window Stay at the left side..if travelling Osaka to Tokyo to view Mt Fuji👍Very clean train👍Very polite people👍
On the Shinkansen everything works fine. Punctuality, quality of service, comfort, cleanliness, speed. Great experience.

There are 4 types of Shinkansen classified according to their speed. The difference with our TGVs is that several of them run per hour. In addition, you can grab a last minute place at the vending machines. There are cars reserved for people who have not reserved a seat. But you risk traveling standing up...

Well, what can I say, you have not experienced Japan travel if you have not been on a bullet train. Train travel perfection on every trip. Comfortable seats, food onboard which comes to you - none of this walking the length of the train to find the buffet car! The bathrooms at the train stations must be the best train station toilets in the world...

I decided to go from Tokyo to Osaka with my mother-in-law, who is in her mid-80s, during Golden Week, so I registered with SmartEX. I was able to get a seat in the green car without any difficulty. It was only a few hundred yen, but it was cheaper. The inside of the train was very clean and the seats were spacious, so I was able to have a comfortable conversation and enjoy the view from the train window both on the round trip and back. My mother-in-law was worried because she had hurt her lower back and lower back, but she didn't seem to have any problems. To be honest, it's much cheaper to fly to Osaka with Saitoku, but it's surprisingly frequent, and unless there's a major emergency, the timing is accurate, which is something Japan is proud of.

Definitely the most convenient and quick way to reach Osaka from Tokyo and is well worth the trip. The trains are very clean and comfortable which makes your journey all the better and before you know it you've already reached Osaka. Japan is definitely excelling in providing the best transport!

reserve places before you go, so you can be sure you will have a seat. JR counters always in front of the entrance to the gates. Works perfectly, just check carefully at the stations which wagon and which train you need, there are several running at different times and those wagons do not always run at the same time!
Well worth a day out. Green car gives you first class travel and two seats across as opposed to three in the normal carriages. Pick your destination and enjoy.
Its really sad that Japan has done so well integrating trains into their transportation infrastructure and the US has no idea what's going on. The Shinkansen is truly remarkable. So fast, so easy.
Visited recently on a trip with teens from Australia studying Japanese. I was worried you would be impacted by the speeds of the Shinkansen but you hardly notice. Always clean and comfy and on time!!

We purchased JR Passes before leaving Australia, so shinkansen was the best way to travel around since all was covered. You cannot use Nozomi on JR Passes, but Hikari is the next best option and adds something like 20 min to your travel from Tokyo to Kyoto compared to Nozomi. We used it for Odawara and Kyoto (from Tokyo), and Kobe and Himeji (from Kyoto). Traveling with bags might be a bit tricky, but if you board at the end of the car, you can put your bags behind the last row of seats (if not already taken, quite often there is pram there and people do not fold it) and suitcases actually fit in the overhead compartment. The only odd thing was that they did not want to issue as reserved seats from Kyoto to Osaka, but I suppose this is only 12 min ride, so you can either stand or get into non-reserved car. All staff spoke adequate English and there was no problem with booking in advance, although you need to ask questions about different times of departures etc. If you say - I want to leave AROUND 10.30am, you sure will get a ticket for 10.32am or similar, although there might be a train at 10.10am, which suits as well. Just the usual Japanese sticking to rules and taking things literally.

We used this train to move around Japan for 3 weeks. It's fabulous. It's a good idea to get the JR pass, which isn't cheap. The transportation here is not, but it is of high quality. It can be taken out in Japan. It wasn't like that before. Consider that for 1, 2 or 3 weeks the cost is similar. The JR (Japan Rails) pass covers an estimated 80% of long-distance routes and 20% of short-distance routes. For short journeys there are local passes that are purchased at train or metro stations. There are no delays. The staff is super friendly. This happens everywhere. Although it is preferable to reserve seats for scheduled trips, there are always carriages that can be boarded without reservation. It is high speed. It exceeds 200 km/h and doesn't even move. It is the ideal means of getting around in Japan.

We were stunned at this train system. Incredible example of outstanding engineering.  Wow. Up to 300km/hr. Track is smooth and quiet inside. Funny that the track banks slightly when the train goes around a curve. I guess it has to at that speed. These are so convenient.  You don't even need to make a reservation although you can get a reserved seat when you buy a ticket  otherwise there are cars without reserved seats. We did it both ways. It's funny that you can just show up at the station and get on one as they are leaving the station almost every 10 to 15 min. Rivals a plane for sure to get somewhere in Japan as you just show up, don't need to wait or check a bag and you end up in the city centre. Note these don't seem to be included in Japan rail passes. Check. It may depend on which bullet train you ride. Some lines have a bunch of stops and some have almost none  these are the Express lines to get further faster. Completely impressed.
I loved traveling by shinkansen, we took them all over Japan, from the fastest north to Hokkaido, and down to Hiroshima. the US sure could use these!

We travelled from Hakone to Tokyo on the bullet train which was a great experience for the first time fast bullet train passenger.I have been on the fast train in China but first time for my wife which she enjoyed. Its comfortable, clean, plenty of leg room with all seats facing forward, you hardly know your travelling at 320 km/h except when your looking out the window, its fast especially when you see it flying past the station in front of you. We enjoyed the experience.

Japan's main transportation artery connecting Osaka and Tokyo. It is more convenient than Shinkansen trains in other regions, but the time available for cleaning the trains is also limited. The staff members are able to cope with the situation without sacrificing quality, and it is pleasant to watch. There is also space for employees at the bottom of the platform, which cannot be seen during normal use, and it is interesting to get a glimpse of the staff supporting the platform.

What mombogogo said, plus a few things. One minor error: stops are announced in Japanese, Korean, and English, with Kangi (Chinese) signage.I recommend reserved seats; you will know the car and the seat(s); wait at the proper place on the platform. There will also be a non-reserved car or 2. Your JR pass will get you a reserved seat, so use it for that. Also, should you have a ticket but decide to try for an earlier train, they will do that for you, depending on availability, at no charge.Luggage can go at the end of the car; some cars have (locking, sometimes) luggage racks; all have space behind the last row of seats).Bring snacks and/or purchase snacks at the station, and/or purchase snacks on the train. There will be a "map" on your seatback that tells you where the bathroom cars are and which end of the train is which. The trains do not turn around; they run one way towards Shin-Osaka and the other way towards Tokyo.If the planets align (i.e. if the weather on Fuji-san is perfect; this is rare), you might catch a glimpse of Mount Fuji.Clean, fast, and comfortable. Great way to travel.

Great experience traveling with the Shikansen. From Tokyo to Kyoto, the trains run at high frequency, the journey (cushioning, seat etc.) is comfortable. The trains are surprisingly spacious.  Street sale of snacks with a smile etc... It's not even necessary to talk about the legendary punctuality of this train. Only 4/5 because purchasing tickets through the terminals was, in our opinion, a bit complex and you have to understand that there are two tickets to buy, one for the train, the other for the seats. The 5C rule...It's C.. but It's Like ThatWhen in doubt, the station employees will help you buy what you need.No JR PASS not profitable for a single journey TOKYO KYOTO

Yep, bullet trains are fast.  But they're also very clean, comfortable and fun.  The way the trains are set up is very similar to the interior of an airplane, with luggage racks overhead, a bay at the front of each car for restrooms, and a hostess walks through with a snack cart every so often.  The seats offer plenty of legroom and have a nifty feature that, if you have a party of 4 or so, can be turned so that two rows can face each other.  At the front of each car is an electronic rolling banner that shows the next few train stations, in Japanese, Chinese and English. Destinations are also announced over the announcement system, so it's not a problem to figure out your stop.Using the JR Rail Pass is a great way to see Japan and get from city to city quickly and efficiently.  We particularly appreciated the ability to reserve seating prior to a trip; it's easy to walk into any JR Rail office in most stations (some of the much smaller ones sent us to the next closest station to reserve our seats), tell them what time you'd like to travel to whichever destination, and your seats are then reserved for a particular car and seat.  When you arrive for departure, you simply stand in line for your car and then seat yourself.  It all works on the honor system; no one ever checked or questioned our seat arrangements.  On a couple of our trips, we were unable to make reservations, but there are a few non-reserved cars.  On the marquees at the station platform, it's noted which cars are non-reserved.  These cars can get crowded quite quickly, so make sure you show up as early as possible to get a seat.  JR Rail offices can also help you find the most efficient and fastest way to any particular destination; they'll print out a list detailing station names, platform numbers, train times, etc..  In some of the smaller areas around the country, this was very useful and helpful!I'm very happy with the ease of using Shinkansen in Japan - it was one of my favorite ways to relax and enjoy the lovely Japanese countryside!
Took this from hakone to kyoto. Very fast and efficient. Reason for one star down is due to fact theres limited quality dining on board (used to have dining carts)

We travelled from Tokyo to Kyoto then Hiroshima back to Tokyo. Very limited luggage space if you have a large case, we travelled from Australia and brought a big case. Overhead can fit small cases/backpacks. There is space in the last row but get it quick as it only fits two luggages side by side, otherwise have them at your feet

This trip did not stay in the center of Tokyo, but in the Yokohama area. If you want to go to and from Tokyo Station, the Shinkansen is the best choice, it is fast and convenient. The price is quite reasonable, the seats are comfortable, and there are many free seats.

Riding the Shinkansen with the JR Railway Pass is extremely efficient and comfortable way of getting around Japan. There is almost no waiting necessary, and the train will ALWAYS be on time, it`s mesmerizing. The trains are completely clean, and if you don`t travel in rush hour there is no need for reservation. However, making a reservation at the JR office, only takes a few minutes, is free of charge and the friendly staff will help you plan your whole route if you are changing trains. The only inconvenience is that the WIFI service is not that reliable, and there is only one electricity outlet per three passengers (window seat), so if you are planning on working during your trip, make sure to claim that outlet!

You can make reservations in a variety of ways, and they are constantly evolving. You can see Mt. Fuji, the seats are spacious, it's clean, it's on time, and it's a very good means of transportation. Airplanes are cheap and fast, but I don't feel like traveling...
Efficient, comfortable and reliable. I wish we had such an amazing public transportation system in my hometown. Very painless to use with JR pass.

I booked our trip from Tokyo to Kyoto. I wanted to make sure we had reserved seats so I spent the extra $$$ for the green car. Turns out, it wasn't necessary. There were plenty of empty seats in the train. That said, it was a comfortable ride and they even have refreshment carts coming thru, with beer!!

Express reservations are convenient and convenient. It's a great service, but I think the price could be a little lower for off-peak seasons or for early reservations, like on the Tohoku Shinkansen. Since Tokyo and Shin-Osaka are cash cow routes, are there no commercial benefits?
It's noisy in Nishi-Magome, but the Shinkansen is always next to my apartment, and the other day I was on Dr. Yellow.It was a valuable experience.

One of many things that needs to be done while travelling in Japan is to travel with the one and only shinkansen. It only took us 2.5 hours from Tokyo Station to Shin-Osaka Station. It can be quite expensive to pay without the JR Pass but the experience itself is worth the price. You can reserve the ticket first or just directly buy it at the Midori no Madoguchi.The seating is comfortable, lots of legs space, even electric sockets on every aisle. The train is also very punctual and clean. It's really nice to see amazing view outside while relaxing on your seat, especially when it's sunny.

When we were choosing our format for traveling around Japan, we took into account when choosing MANDATORY travel around the country on the Shinkansen! And the best payment option in this case is to purchase a JR Pass. We took a weekly pass and, limiting ourselves to the inability to use Nozomi trains, saved almost 40,000 local tugris in a week. I started organizing the purchase of the travel card late, I came to my senses two days before departure. It turns out that this is not a quick thing ((three or four days... I was a little depressed, since the purchase can only be made outside of Japan, but I decided to try to make it and order delivery to our hotel in Tokyo. It worked! And at the reception upon arrival, they handed me two travel cards! Cool! Tickets with a travel card must be taken at the station ticket office. We traveled in early November and never stood in line for more than 10-15 minutes, the carriages are almost always We didn’t carry our suitcases with us in the evening, taking all the necessary things in our bag the next day and, having arrived in the next city and the next hotel, we got our suitcase, sorted out the things we needed, removed the extra ones and returned the suitcase again. It was very convenient and not very expensive! We had two suitcases in one that we had packed for a week-long cruise and we didn’t need it for a trip around the country. needed. To put it in a storage room for 8 days would cost more than 8,000 tugrs, but to send it from the Tokyo station to a hotel located 5 minutes from the station with the goal of receiving it at the reception in 8 days - less than 1,500 tugrs)) And the impressions about the trips on the Hikari and Kodama are the most excellent! Hikari is only minutes slower than Nozomi, which is not significant; Kodama is slightly behind here. The amenities on the trains are top notch, the toilets are clean, large and comfortable. The conductors are polite, they enter the hall, bow, go out into the vestibule, turn around, bow. And this happens ten times during the trip! Here's patience... They deliver drinks and snacks, but it's better to take them at the station, where the beer is colder and the selection of snacks is incomparably wider. In a word - a Shinkansen trip is a separate attraction of Japan, visiting which you will get a lot of positive emotions!

Because of its small size, the Shinkansen is the Tokaido Shinkansen. However, JR East is actually more convenient as the aisle seats also have outlets. I often travel between Tokyo and Kyoto, but I like to just take in the scenery from the train window. The Japanese countryside scenery has a seasonal feel and is very nice. Lately, it seems like there are announcements in English, but the live ones are so hard to read that I can't understand what they're saying.
Therefore, I think it is best to buy souvenirs from the shops located underground of the station (the passageway leading to Midosuji). I will definitely buy the 551.

You don't have to book in advance, the thing that not everyone knows: you can't put large suitcases in the train, buying the ticket is done quickly and efficiently. Every 20 minutes there is a train. When we traveled, most of the passengers were single men on what appeared to be a business trip. Very quiet, no one is talking
Travel comfortably from Tokyo to Sin Osaka. The trains are right on time and the reserved seats were comfortable. Only buying a ticket took quite a while (at the counter with live service)

We finally used the famous shinkansen to travel from Tokyo to Kanazawa using the JR pass. The only small inconvenience is that they gave us a ticket without a seat because perhaps we needed to add an extra and so at the beginning we occupied some free seats, then they made us get up and the conductor plus the on-board policemen pass by so frequently that in the end we were in the corridor without creating any arguments. On board the bathrooms are super technological, clean and comfortable. Separate compartment for brushing teeth compared to the toilet area. Fast and punctual travel without inconveniences

On the way to Odawara, when I was changing trains at Nagoya, I saw Dr. Yellow pull in and I couldn't help but take a photo. If you meet Dr. Yellow, happiness will come! There's an urban legend, but is it true?

First the good....easy to book using ticket machines in English (but not sure if there were any deals, so expected we paid the highest price) very smooth journey, comfortable seats (chose Green/First class), announcements in English, start/finish to schedule and clean cabins. But was maybe expected more from the famed Shinkansen. First the windows, being used to panoramic English train windows, felt very dark and dingy with the over-sized airplane style windows in the Shinkansen. Wifi did not work. Very limited space for luggage storage. 2+2 style seating  vs. 1 + 2 (table) in the UK. Overall, got to destination quickly and rested, but underwhelmed.

Starting next year, there will be a charge for bringing large baggage such as suitcases into the country. So I thought I'd make a place to store my luggage, but the place to store it was between the backmost seat and the wall! Even now, I sometimes have trouble not being able to recline, but it's extremely annoying. Nuisance spaces such as the several smoking rooms on trains should be quickly removed and converted into luggage storage areas. It is a transportation system that is completely unaware of the trends of the times and global trends. It's embarrassing for customers coming from overseas.

A staple of the Shinkansen. Surprisingly, the legroom is spacious even in the regular seats, which is nice. A good trick is that children can use unreserved seats for free. Might be better than a plane.

I rode this train from Shinagawa Station to Shin-Osaka on a business trip. “Nozomi 25” departing from Shinagawa at 10:37 and arriving at Shin-Osaka at 13:03 was comfortable. There is also a 100V power supply near the window of your seat, so you can charge your smartphone or PC. It was convenient for working on my PC on the Shinkansen.

We ordered three seven day pass exchange orders online via JTB travel in the UK and they arrived within 48 hours. Much easier than trying to get to a specialist booking agent. Exchanged them for passes easily at a JR office in Tokyo station. We used them for seven trains and one bus - great value for travelling around Japan. The ordinary class was fine, very comfortable with charging points, individual food tables etc. Excellent buffet trolley and lovely staff on the trains. Seat tickets can all be prebooked and indicate on the ticket which carriage/seat. Then can stand on the marked platform areas, ready to board. All trains leave promptly, so don't be late. Polite staff, perfect Japanese customer service, trains are clean and never late! Even have smoking rooms! Little storage area for over sized bags though. Some double seats turn around to make four facing each other if necessary for a group.

We always heard of the bullet trains.But taking one is something else. Unbelievably on time, you better get in fast or get out fast, otherwise, you are condemned!Inside, clean, comfortable, lots of space for legs and arms and civilised passengers.As for the speed, it is impressive, but for those who are used to France's TGV, it's the same speed, around 300 km / hour.
I always use Shinkansen when I visit in Japan. It easy to book at the ticket counter. They were very kind. The great things is Shinkansen is always on time!!!
The trains in Japan are incredible. Clean, on time and efficient. Take the time to travel in train. Tips: keep quiet and clean in the train. Be on time and use small luggage.
incredible service, punctuality, speed, frequency, highly recommended with the Japan Rail Pass. When returning you have to change with the pass, while there is a direct line
When comparing Shinkansen trains, I feel that the Tokaido Shinkansen ranks first in terms of overall points. Ride comfort, space, speed, number of rides. All in all, as expected.
The Hikari between Tokyo and Kyoto was always worth the price of the Japan Rail Pass, always punctual and clean and comfortable.

We travelled on the high speed train from odawara to Osaka. During the trip we inadvertently lost one ticket. We still had our receipt from that morning and one of our tickets, but they don’t let you leave the station without a ticket. We went to the staff and showed them evidence of our purchase of 2 tickets that morning, but clearly they are well-trained to not take any logical evidence. Their party line: you have to repurchase the exact same ticket to get out. Despite all evidence that we had two tickets and that we accidentally lost one, they made us pay for the same ticket again JUST TO LEAVE THE STATION! It was pure extortion and likely their way of taking advantage of travelers with bags who don’t realize how important it is to hold onto the tiny ticket stub. And when we tried to ask to just buy whatever the cheapest ticket option, they said that would be a crime and we had to buy the same ticket and same fare class.  Did the train get us where we needed to be? Yes. Was it comfortable? Yes. But were the staff completely unreasonable and did they extort us by not letting us leave the station unless we paid another $150 dollars (despite indisputable evidence that we had already purchased the ticket and ridden the train there)? Yes. Be warned— do not lose your ticket and do not hope or expect to be able to reason with any of their staff should you have any problems.

We took the Shinkansen from Tokyo to Nikko,we did not reserve the seat as this was an additional expense.High speed rail is one of the engineering advance you can experience here..Overall a great experience .Highly recommended .

We ordered from France via the internet 2 Ordinary Japan Rail Pass packages for 21 days for adults for a total price of €942. It may seem expensive but this mode of transport is fast, comfortable and the trains are always on time (to the minute). We stayed 6 days in Tokyo and we only activated the pass on the fourth day because we did not need it for the first 4 days. Reservations are recommended but are not obligatory in the latter case you will travel in compartments provided for this purpose. With the Pass you buy peace of mind. It is not only used for traveling between large cities, you can use it to travel on certain lines in various towns. However, in city centers, the metro or the bus remain the only means of transport and your pass will not be of use to you.

Our travels in Japan extend over 26 years and always involve travel on Shinkansen using the JR Pass. Most recently, the 14 day JR Green Pass was used extensively for both Shinkansen (5 trips) and numerous regional JR services.  The longest trip was the 11 hour journey from Sapporo, Hokkaido to Kyoto.  Time literally flies when travelling in such comfort.  Shinkasen is well patronised by the local population, with peak demand during festival and holiday seasons,, so "do your homework".  We would always recommend making reservations when travelling on Shinkasen.  For couples, consider the JR Green (First) Car Pass (reserved seats only). Extra comfort and less crowded.

High speed rail is one of the great engineering advances and there was no way we would go to Japan and NOT take the Bullet Train.   It's proper name is the Shinkansen and there are several types running on various lines all over Japan.   In fact, the Japanse have a very strong love of this train and all it's different versions. Ours was probably the busiest line, running from Tokyo to Osaka via Kyoto, which was where we were going.   I'm going to talk about a couple of things regading the Shinkansen and first is wether to reserve a seat or not.   We had advice from friends on this and the overwhealming repsonse was not to bother and get unreserved tickets.   This is pretty good advice with a couple of caveats.   First, if you get on at the terminus, you get a good choice of seats.   If you were like us and got on one or two stops into it's journey, then it's pot-luck for seating and we did end up split as finding three seats together is pretty hard.   If you want to guarentee keeping the faily together, you will have to reserve.  Finding luggage space can be hard as well.   You can place luggage in racks above the seats, but not large items such as a full size case.   Our experience was that it was a little awkward gettin in and seated with luggage stowed but overall not to bad.   On our return, we had to hunt through cars for space.Second thing is the whole JR pass thing.   If you've looked at the passes, you will have found that there is no one pass for all Japan and the way they have split them is...  difficult, so to speak.    When we worked out that we would do one return journey on the Shinkansen, we dropped the pass idea and bought our tickets over the counter.   For the three of us (2 adults, 1 kid) our ticlets were a third of the spend for JR passes!   Use the JR website to work out wether it's worth it for your needs.   And get the JR East train app!   This was absolute gold and covers just about everywhere including non-JR lines AND the Shinkansen.Now for the trip.    Unlike Europe, Shinkansen run almost as often as a metro train.   Around 15 minutes between trians in some cases.   So, if you're going unreserved and can't get on, chill!   Another will be along shortly.    The ride is smooth, quiet and you are kept well informed of stops bu electroninc displays in the carriage and announcements, made in Japanese and English.    There is a snack and beverage service that comes through the train and you can buy hot tea and coffee from them as well as soft drinks and snacks.   You're also welcome to bring your own snacks and drinks but remember to be polite and tidy with your eating and take your rubbish with you.     The seating is three on one side and two on the other, with lots of space for feet and legs and a seat back table.    The seats also recline if you want to snooze but how can you with Japan sliding by your window at 230 odd kph?    One thing that got me is that this train is flying, and it's a narrow guage!     In fact, a few times I felt myslef lift slightly from the seat as the track went from and uphill to a downhill gradient!We loved this train, it's speed, awesome looks and convenience and I am positive you will too.   Below are some hints to help you get the best out of it.;1. Work out if it's worth getting a pass or just pay-as-you-go.2. If you don't want to risk a split family, considder reserved tickets (more expensive).3. Luggage space can be hard to find, so you might want to use one of the luggage transfer services, like Yamato Transport.4. Find out where you need to be on the platform for the unreserved cars, or the car you're allocated to, before the train arrives.5. Stops are short and punctual, so get on and off in a timely manner.  Don't stuff around, they won't wait!6. If you're unreserved and can't get on, don't panic. Another train will be along shortly.7. Have fun!If we've managed to help you with this review, sweet!   Hit the helpful button so we know we're doing the right thing and read some of our other reviews.
Anyway, it's very convenient because there are a lot of them. This time, it was so cold everywhere that I regretted not having brought a layer of clothing.

Great train service - we went from Kyoto to Tokyo - took 2 hours - best to book the seats as they can get busy however, we brought our ticket with just 30 minutes before departure.
