You can buy the tickets at the JR Ticket counter (brought ours in one oft he smaller stations to avoid the queues at Tokyo). Very efficient and in time. They server some drinks and snacks on the train - but the 2 hours passed by fast - and we got to see Mount Fuji on the way !!
Tokaido Shinkansen bound for Nagoya. As expected. The seats are comfortable, there are a lot of them, and you can buy them cheaply from the website. I thoroughly enjoyed this route

If you want to travel long distances in Japan between the major cities, you should take the Shinkansen. It is expensive if you buy individual tickets. If you use this fast train a lot, you will have to buy a JR Railpass.
SO much fun with three little boys... they were completely in awe, not to mention it's a far easier trip than driving or a bus.
LCCs are currently cheaper, but considering the time and effort it takes to get to the airport, even if they are expensive, they are still convenient. You can buy tickets cheaply at the ticket shop.

I used the Nozomi train during the July holidays. The station was crowded with people, but I was still able to secure a reserved seat on the Shinkansen. To be honest, I feel like there isn't enough fun to be had, but I was once again impressed with the Tokaido Shinkansen, which is comfortable, runs at high speeds, and operates frequently.

Round trip ride from Tokyo to Yamaguchi. I thought about flying, but considering delays and cancellations due to weather, I felt more comfortable taking the Shinkansen, even if it took an extra hour. You can read, work, eat, drink, sleep, and do everything.

To return home, I rode between Tokyo (Shinagawa) and Nagoya several times. I always sit in a reserved seat, but most of the seats are occupied even on holidays and weekdays, which shows how many passengers there are. During the holidays, I went there without having to reserve a seat and it was very crowded, so I had to wait about 30 minutes to get a non-reserved seat. I think the Shinkansen is definitely more convenient than flying between Tokyo and Nagoya.

I took the Nozomi train between Hiroshima and Tokyo. They also sell tickets on the train in the Sanyo section, but it's the Tokaido section that makes you want to buy them. The ascent goes past Nagoya and ends in Yokohama. On the way down, the car sales time is the opposite. Speaking of the Shinkansen, it's Shinkansen ice cream. It's a little pricey at just under 300 yen, but it has a strangely firm texture and rich flavor. It's worth experiencing once.
Everything was easy to find at the train station. The staff is so adorable and helpful with tourists! I used the JR pass and I've been to multiple cities.

Nozomi has increased in frequency, while Hikari and Kodama have become less frequent, making it quite inconvenient to go to Shizuoka and intermediate stations in between. I wish they had built Shizuoka Airport Station anyway...
I often ride with my preschoolers. It gets busy during the holidays, so reservations are essential. The staff are polite and always take care of me.
I went to Nagoya on a business trip. On the way home, I rode in the green car. The seats were spacious and comfortable, with footrests and reading lights.

A business class like experience (Green Car!). The seats are comfortable (individually adjustable) offering ample leg space even for taller travelers. The cabin crew is very polite overing hand towels and for a small fee one could purchase many kinds of drinks, snacks or ice-cream.

The cabin is Like an aircraft without overhead bins, it’s smooth with no clickety clack and you don’t realise how fast your going until you pass one going in the opposite direction, puts our trains to shame.
What a pass! Speed, punctuality, comfort. These Japanese are centuries ahead of us.

Dunno why this has a TA listing, but as you'd expect, it will get you where you need to go very quickly. If you're not living here, the JR pass covers it as well. Just go into the station and book your tickets.

Japan's Shinkansen is so famous that you may be familiar with it, but in reality, there seems to be no better way to travel between Kanto and Kansai. Of course, airplanes take much less time, but when you think about the actual travel time to the airport, the time it takes to go through check-in, and the waiting time, I don't think there is a method as efficient as the Shinkansen. It is a mode of transportation that I like because of the wider seat spacing and faster speed than the KTX.

The Tokaido Shinkansen probably has the highest ridership among all Shinkansen trains. I enjoy riding the new Shinkansen, but after riding one for the first time in a while, I realized that Kodama has its own merits.

I am so glad that I took the "Bullet Train" from Tokyo Station to Osaka. I splurged for the Green Class (First Class) and so glad I did. It was a relaxing, peaceful and comfortable ride and I look forward to doing again. A bit pricey I think, but an experience.

This is the Shinkansen that connects Shin-Osaka to Tokyo. It seems that the fastest time is about 2 hours, but they are aiming to speed it up even more. Basically, it stops at Shin-Osaka, but I am reminded that it is quite a distance to be able to go directly to Hakata on the Sanyo Shinkansen. I used the service from Shin-Yamaguchi to Tokyo on my way back from a trip. It took four and a half hours, but if you're traveling more than 800km from Tokyo, it might be better to use a plane rather than the Shinkansen.

The Tokaido Shinkansen is over 50, that is.  Today's trains are so fast and comfortable and frequent it is really just an amazing experience (especially if you come from a no-high-speed-train country). We also booked using the JR app, impressive how you can book at short notice wherever you are and your seats are waiting for you.  Worth a ride.
Smooth and fast way to get around in Japan. The train will arrive in a minute. Comfortable chairs and good atmosphere

I go to Tokyo almost every month, and recently I found out that you can use WiFi on the Shinkansen, so I decided to try it out. I thought it was a little slow, but I was able to browse the Internet almost stress-free.

We had taken a JR pass for 7 days and used it for travel from Tokyo to Hiroshima and from Hiroshima to Jakarta. In addition to this, the pass gave us unlimited travel on JR trains within Tokyo and to Yokohama and on the JR ferry from Hiroshima to Miyajima island. Outstanding experience at every stage. The trains are spic and span, exactly on time and the staff courteous to a fault. The seats on the Hikari & Sakura trains were very comfortable with ample leg space. Do reserve seats on long distance trains. This can be done at no extra cost.

We took a train from Tokyo to Kyoto. It was exciting that we could go that fast on a train.  It was a smooth ride.  I was really surprised. About an hour out of Tokyo, you could observe Mt. Fuji from the train. It was certainly breathtaking, and I felt overwhelmed with the beauty I was surrounded by. I would actually like to take that trip again some time, and try to take in the sights once again. Not only was the train amazing, the service was really good as well.  The attendants were super nice.
Well, it is a fast train. Very clean and on time! I suggest getting JR rail passes to travel in and around Tokyo.

used to move from Tokyo to Kyoto, then to reach the ferry to Miyajima and finally to return from Hiroshima and Tokyo, having taken the validated JRP at Tokyo station it was very convenient to book seats, observe the timetables on HyperDia and enjoy the journey on these immaculate, fast, silent trains (phones must be silenced and it is advisable to speak in a low voice), obviously very punctual. Traveling with vehicles like this is not stressful at all, at the terminus a team of men and women with specific uniforms wait for the passengers to get off, then they greet them all with a bow and then they go up to clean, meanwhile the next passengers line up to get on and in a few minutes they get on and the train starts again, a marvel. obviously with the JRP you can take advantage of slower trains such as the HIKARI, while NOZOMI and MIZUHO are excluded, but believe us, there will be no hitch during your journey, in any case. used in July 2018

I always use it until Mishima. Usually we ride on Kodama, but depending on the time we use Hikari. Hikari stops at different stations depending on the time. There are times when it stops at Odawara, which is often used by foreigners, and times when it stops at Mishima. I don't ride beyond Mishima so I don't know the details. When I ride the Kodama, I often come across foreigners who are panicking because they think it's Hikari. When getting on a train, it's a good idea to look at the plate next to the door before getting on.

The Shinkansens are super clean and spacious.  We travelled to/from Tokyo and Kyoto.  It was easy to book seats in advance.  There were lots of room to store our luggage and everyone on board was quiet so if you need to nap, you can easily get a good nap.  People who work there were extremely polite; bowing when entering and leaving the trains.

Getting around in Japan is very easy since everything is designed with a hyper-practical mentality and even if you don't understand the language, the system in stations, trains, etc. is very friendly. The Shinkansen is essential to move long distances. You can get a pass for the days that are available, from the country of origin (it cannot be purchased in Japan) which enables you to use most trains and the Yamanote line in Tokyo. It is very convenient if you are going to visit more than two cities! It is not cheap, but in this way they have solved transportation in any corner of the country just by showing the card/pass. We did Tokyo, Kyoto, Himeji, Nara, Mount Fuji, Kamakura. And we use it in Tokyo every day, all the time.  The cost is taken away!!!!!
The only way to travel between cities in Japan.   Bullet trains offer really comfortable seating with plenty of leg room.  Adequate luggage storage and run to the minute.
It is a fast and comfortable way to travel quickly between cities. We had reserved seats, which is best. Very clean and smooth trip at 300km/hr. WE used it twice.

The regular seats are often so crowded that even the B seat in the middle is filled, and the trains coming from the Sanyo Shinkansen smell like bento boxes. Good points are that there are outlets and Wi-Fi. Green cars are always empty.
Fast, practical, comfortable transport with exact schedules, I highly recommend it as transport to discover the land of the rising sun.

The greatest train system  ive seen puts our Australian trains to shame .These trains enter the terminals fast no messing around.Rarely late and they apologize if even a few minutes late.Comfy seats and beer and snacks onboard or byo.Its great on Japanese trains no annoyign people with loud phones.

This ride from Kyoto to Osaka only takes 13 minutes, fast and comfortable... we bought a non-reserved seat ticket, it's cheap but if there are a lot of people the seats will be messy... so I suggest it's better to just buy a reserved seat so it's more comfortable
An experience to live: cleanliness, space, comfort. Remember to turn to the left (depending on whether you have reserved your seats or not) to see Mount Fuji from afar.

I used it for a round trip between Tokyo and Himeji. Lately, I've been flying to Kansai more often, and it's been a while since I've used the Shinkansen. I bought a boxed lunch outside Daimaru Tokyo Gourmet so I could have lunch on the train, and the trip took about 3 hours. My wife and I were aiming for Mt. Fuji on the right side of the descent, but the mountain remained hidden behind clouds on both trips and was too shy to show its face. Too bad!! Shinkansen trains are now equipped with free Wi-Fi, and people who look like businessmen board the trains with Mac bags and are glued to their computers the entire time they travel.

I was traveling down from Nagoya a little early for a weekday evening. It was more crowded than I expected, and there were always people gathered around the smoking room, which made it uncomfortable. If possible, I would like to use a plane to go anywhere.
The seats on the Tokaido Shinkansen are wide and comfortable, even on long journeys. The N700 series Shinkansen has electrical outlets so you can charge your computer or smartphone.
What can I say about the Shinkansen? It's as good as it gets as far as the trains go. Very punctual, safe, comfortable and fun! Love it.

The fastest way to get between the two stations, by far. Air-conditioned, comfy seats and not anywhere near as packed as the metro during rush hour. Both stations very large and rather confusing, but this was easy to find. Signs in English, as well as announcements on the PA system, so easy to use.
A route that represents Japan. There are many books and they are punctual. But the prices are high and stable, and it's always crowded. I want to move a little more slowly.

We went on the bullet train from Tokyo to Kyoto in about 3 hours. The train is clean, spacious, comfortable. There was free WiFi... and it’s one of the few public places where it is socially acceptable to bring food and drinks to. It was a nice opportunity to see the suburbs/ country side, even if it was just in passing. The train is fast, reaching 250mph at some times.

I used the train from Maibara Station to Tokyo Station on my way back from sightseeing in Fukui. I was worried that the express train going to Maibara Station was a little late, but I made it in time. Perhaps because it was the Hikari train, it was a little empty and no one sat next to me until the end, so I was able to relax.

Sightseeing in Japan with friends from overseas. My friend was impressed and impressed by the excellent quality of everything about the Shinkansen, and I was very happy as well. As a Japanese person, I'm really interested in the Tokaido Shinkansen's punctuality, safety, and friendly travel support system.

The Japanese Rail system is superb, on time, very comfortable, and the bullet trains zip you along at 200 mph, but are quiet, have food and drink service, and the Japanese Rail (JR) Rail Pass is definitely worth the investment, particularly if you want to see a lot of the country.

Once you have Japanese rail pass this is the only way to travel around Japan.you may have your coach but by the time you are out of the city by coach you are already at your next destination by Shinkansen .no need to worry about your suit cases you just wheel them like you do at the airport and use escolators or lifts.

We traveled from Hakodate to Aomori, with its 54km tunnel between the islands of Hokkaido and Honshu, then Sendai to Tokyo. Superb red or green oars, brilliant aerodynamics. The seats are honestly comfortable, but we have room and they turn around to always face the direction of travel. Impeccable space between two cars, with a hand sink, two men's or women's toilets and one for men exclusively (the door doesn't close, we see the gentleman standing, so we know it's busy; the ladies are supposed to look away!). Be careful, the stops are short, you should not hang around, neither on the way up nor on the way down! The controller bows when entering or leaving the carriage, the class. Much better than the French TGV, a little better than the German ICE.

The TGV in France and the ICE in Germany is way cheaper. The Maglav in China is way faster... I do not get what the hype is all about... Travelled in green class.. Costs more than a Flight and one had to carry ones own bag.... I don't get it.... But its famous, so all will travel in it... So let's go with the flow... Bhagwan..

I simply enjoyed riding the Tokaido Shinkansen (Hikari).  Although it's 10 minutes slower than the Nozomi, one can use the JR REGIONAL PASS to ride on it without additional cost (I bought the green pass).  Always make a reservation before riding it if you want to sit in the reserved sections to/from your destinations.  They are quite strict about this policy.

The fare may be high compare to other the local or even Rapid train in Japan, but if you plan to cover more places in a short duration, Shinkansen is the best. Able to travel Osaka, Kyoto, Tokyo, Nagano, Toyama, Hiroshima, Himeji using the Shinkansen (Bullet Train). The seats is even better than my flight. Most of the train I board have individual power socket for every seats to charge you electronic devices. Staff are polite and nice. Train schedule is frequent and on time. Really efficient.
After all, it's comfortable to move around. You can charge your batteries and most importantly, relax. The cleaning is perfect so it's great.

A stable Shinkansen. I fly a lot, but recently I've been reconsidering the Shinkansen. It takes about 40 minutes from Tokyo Station to Haneda Airport, but if you take the Shinkansen, you'll already pass Odawara. I feel anxious because I can never miss the baggage check. Airplanes where you are not allowed to leave your seat even if you have had too much to drink or are not feeling well. Itami Airport is quite far from Osaka city. If you're going as far as Kokura, the Shinkansen might be a better option if you think about it. You can buy reserved seat tickets individually for around 12,300 yen at ticket centers in front of Tokyo Station. You can buy it, put it in the ticket vending machine next to the Shinkansen ticket gate, and select it if the Shinkansen departs about 10 minutes before departure. It is best to avoid the Midori-no-Madoguchi counter as it gets crowded. Please note that the Cheap Ticket Center is open until 7pm and only accepts cash. If you buy it online, it's about 100 yen more expensive. If you want power, it's better to sit by the window. My airplane status is JAL_JGC/ANA_DIA, but I'm starting to think that the Shinkansen is more convenient. It's cheap and you can stand up and ride. Baggage inspection requires computers, water, and smartphones...it's a hassle.

From buying the ticket to getting off, everything is very structured, clearly written and easy to understand, even for foreigners. The train ride is very quiet. Unfortunately there is not much space for luggage.

We travelled from Tokyo to Kyoto with the Nozomi and it took about 2 hours and 20 minutes. The seats are good but when you travel with big suitcases there are not spaces to put them so we had to keep the suitcases in front of our legs. But I would recommend to travel with this Shinkansen.

Accurate, efficient, and safe, our lives are regulated in this way. This is Japanese life, and it makes you wonder whether that's why the Shinkansen is the way it is, or whether life is the way it is because of the Shinkansen.It's a transportation system that is so uniquely Japanese.
Reservations using Express Cards are very convenient. You can change your reservation until the last minute, so you don't have to worry about sudden changes in your schedule.

The bullet train has legroom of business class air-travel a decade ago. All this in the regular class of the bullet train. Our reserved seats from Tokyo to Osaka were near the front of the car. The downside to this location was a busy smoking room between the cars. The constant coming and going of desperate smokers was a tad disconcerting. For our next trip, we will reserve a seat in the middle of the car or choose a car without a smoking room. There’s no other train system in the world that operates as efficiently and reliably as the Japanese model.

I traveled yesterday from Tokyo to Kyoto and back to Tokyo I one day. This was my first time on the Shinkansen. Wonderful experience. I look forward to traveling again.Dr. Erick J Mann, PhDProfessor of History and Fulbright Scholar

I took the Hikari train 2 times, on the way from Tokyo to Osaka and back. It's not the fastest, but it's included in the JR Pass. A kind of train of the future. At the shinkansen you should definitely buy a bento - a set of food for the road. It’s an incredible thrill to feel like you’re in Japan, rushing on a high-speed train, devouring bento and drinking cold Japanese beer. Bento (and beer too) are sold at the stations where shinkansen depart. Drinking beer on the train is legal in Japan, so indulge yourself and you'll have one of the most memorable shinkansen rides of your life. The carriages have bathrooms. There is space for luggage at the beginning and end of the carriage, but even a fairly large suitcase fits normally near the feet (my height is 182). If you want a photo of Mount Fuji from the window, ask for a seat on the appropriate side when booking a seat (if I remember correctly, Tokyo-Osaka is on the right in the direction of travel, respectively, vice versa).

I had a meeting in Osaka, so I reserved a green car at Hayatoku and used it. Although the weather was rainy, I was able to travel comfortably in the comfortable seats. I mostly travel by plane, but I think the Shinkansen is convenient for Nagoya, Kyoto, and Osaka.
Took this Bullet train as part of Inspiring Vacations tour(Group 38).Certainly an experience.Just waiting at the station to board  with numerous trains bypassing every 3 mins was amazing!

Even if you're not going a long way, I recommend trying a short day-trip on the Shinkansen so you can experience the speed, cleanliness and precision of this marvellous means of transport.We decided to do a day-trip from Tokyo to Odawara – around forty minutes on the Shinkansen.From beginning to end, our experience did not disappoint. On our arrival at Tokyo Station, we saw the arrival of our train, watched the pink-uniformed ladies quickly enter, clean and leave before we could board. The train left on time, and only made a couple of stops before arriving in Odawara (Shinagawa and Shin-Yokohama).For our return, the train arrived at the station on time (to the minute), and the doors lined up exactly where the marks on the platform indicated we should stand.The ride was smooth, quiet and comfortable, and we were able to see so much of the scenery (city, suburbs and semi-rural areas).We did not reserve seats so our tickets were cheaper, and because we travelled on the Friday before Golden Week, we were lucky as the train wasn’t very full.Definitely a worthwhile experience.
Traveling by train is becoming so ennoble to me. The distance is so short and the comfort of the train is also relaxing.

I used it from Shin-Yokohama to Shin-Kobe considering time and cost. I booked a seat in the middle of car 5, which is farthest from the smoking room, but I noticed the smell of cigarettes several times. It must be said that JR Tokai, which still has smoking rooms installed in its train cars, either does not recognize or completely ignores the dangers of toxic tobacco smoke escaping from smoking rooms (second-hand smoke) and toxic tobacco substances emitted from smokers' breath and clothing (third-hand smoke). A complete ban on smoking indoors is also recommended by the World Health Organization (WHO).

Without a doubt the best means of transportation for long distances. His punctuality is exact. They are silent. Clean. They are very well signposted so not being familiar with Japanese is not a problem.  It is also not a problem not to get a seat reservation, the first cars are without reservation.

It is the ideal means of transportation between Tokyo and Kyoto. The train is comfortable and fast. (around 280km/h) There are different Shinkansen, more or less fast depending on the number of stops. The fastest and most frequent is the Nozomi around 2h20, then the Hikari around 2h40 and finally the Kodama around 4h00. If you have the Japan Rail Pass you can use the Hikari and Kodama but not the Nozomi. Hikari remains the best compromise. During our visit there were approximately every half hour. On the display panels the different trains Nozomi, Hikari... You also have the possibility to reserve your seat. We hadn't done it but we found space easily. It is necessary to locate the trains without reservation, often at the end of the train, it is indicated on the notice board on the platform and on the trains. During the journey the staff passes in the train and offers drinks or cakes for sale. Have a good trip.

It is very fast and the price is very high. It is suitable for people who have time requirements. Tourists with JrPass must be careful that some cars cannot be used and they will be fined. nozomi cannot.

We had a gift for our guess (maple syrup and ice wine) in a transparent plastic bag. The train employer toke the back but someone in our group cut it (at the same time we stop). I run and toke back the package and she looks like everything was normal. Becarefull you feel over safe in Japan !

The whole sensation is one of luxury travel. Reserved seats, lots of legroom, food and drink service, several charging points, spick and span toilets, in short the works. Worth every yen that we spent on buying the JR Pass with 7 day validity.

Took the nizomi Shinkansen from Tokyo to Kyoto.I chose to upgrade to green (first) class for greater comfort. Green class coaches are in 2-2 configuration as opposed to 2-1 in the uk. Arrived at Shinagawa Station in Tokyo. The booking staff speak some English and are very helpful. You need to choose your train times for your ticket. Note that you pay a price for the ticket. Then you pay extra for either an unreserved seat (normally coaches 1-3) a reserved seat or green class ( usually coaches 8-10) once you reach the platform , notices are in Japanese and English so you there is no misunderstanding. Boarding is through barriers onto the trains. On board the seating was very comfortable. Trains do get busy so I recommend reserving a seat. There is a trolley service on board but not restaurant, so I recommend getting food before you board. If you want to see Mount Fuji, sit on the right hand side of the train out of Tokyo. Service on board these trains is exceptional with plenty of staff around. The Nizomi train is the fastest of the bullet trains and reaches speeds of nearly 200mph. Really smooth ride though. Every train is on time and I didn’t see a cancellation on the departure board.This is a must do experience if you are in Japan.

You can’t beat these trains. They are clean. Fast. Quiet. The people who work in the JR offices and helpful and friendly. We did the JR Pass because we are traveling to 5 different cities. It came out as a big savings. Just a great way to travel. Can’t ask for anything more.
The world famous Shinkansen does not disappoint! As a foreign traveler, we bought the JR Rail Pass with our travel plan and found it clean, efficient and reliable. Every country should have it!

The Shinkansen is famous around the world for its speed and convenience. it is one of the fastest trains in the world and I highly recommend the shinkansen if you are travelling across Japan. I went from Tokyo to Osaka in about three hours. It is a great railway line.
I used Plat Kodama. Since it was an N700 series, there was an outlet and it was comfortable. However, there were no on-board sales.

Shinkansen was such a great way to travel across the country. The trains are clean, quiet, and fast. We purchased a JR pass for the Green cards and the exchange and reservation process was painless and well organized. The travel itself was pleasant, the seats are large and the service good.

Thrilling train ride via the super-express Bullet “Shinkansen” train headed for Nagoya. Here we transfered to a limited-express train for a scenic ride to Takayama, a delightful small town nestled in the majestic Japanese Alps. Hosted by Smartours. Another must do in Japan.

I am a member of ``Zipangu'', which is called ``Holiday for Adults'' in eastern Japan, and ``Zipangu'' in western Japan, and when I went to Tokyo, I went out on the Hikari. Although there are some restrictions (Nozomi cannot be used or there are periods when it cannot be used, etc.), it is a good way to travel slowly. Unlike airplanes, the Shinkansen runs frequently, so even if you miss your train, there's always another one, so it's easy.

We based ourself in Osaka and there is hardly any JR lines so we didn’t get a JR pass but we took the Shinkansen (bullet train) back from Kyoto to Osaka. Cost us 1400y or A$18 per person. Great experience and very fast as you would expect. That cost was an unreserved seat and a reserved seat is double the price for that leg at 3000y. We found the information office at the Shinkansen very helpful and booked our ticket easily .

I used it when going to Nagoya. If you book the Shinkansen online, you can change your reservation at the last minute, and there are quite a lot of trains between Osaka and Nagoya, which is helpful. There aren't many delays, and it's a good thing that you can get there in just 50 minutes.

The high class of this TGVWiFi, socket for charging phones, the seats are reclining and reversible in case you are a group of friends like this everyone can cope Surprisingly very stable given the speed at which it goesGood be careful between the wagons with reserved and non-reserved seats it is marked on the platform before getting on

This is exactly what we expected - fast, efficient and reliable.  Since we traveled light, we did not have any issues with our luggage that we stored on the shelf above the seats.  Our travel companions shipped their large suitcases using one of the delivery company recommended by our guide.  The journey was pleasant – plenty of legroom, electrical outlets, etc.  I wish they can offer a free WiFi…The boarding procedure was simple – all passengers formed the line according to their reassigned seat number and then quickly entered the train.

Despite large numbers of passengers, things move quickly for exit and enter.  Each car is well marked with identification and car number so you know which to enter from a well marked numbered gate.  Baggage space is limited to racks above the seats which are quite high.  If you have a large heavy bag it is a trick to hoist them up.  Alternatively large bags can be placed at the door way aisles leaving space for people to get by.  This works because there are only a few stops.

Used Shinkansen through my JR pass during my trip. Very easy to access. Accurate. Very clean and comfortable. I used Green Cars of Shinkansen which are more on the luxury side and requires seat reservation. It has enough space for luggage. Must to have and use during Japan visit.

We used the Shinkansen to travel in different cities in Japan.Arrived for a 3 weeks trip with big pieces of luggage.There is no designated space for big luggage in these trains, we had to hold it in the aisle , very difficult due to the fact that we had to remove it every time someone wanted to pass . The only space they have is for a small trolley - Lucky us that these trains are really speedy so the travel does not take too long...

I am actually on the train now. Yes it is smooth and quiet and on time, everyone knows that. However although we got a convenient pair of seats I find them a bit hard and not especially comfortable despite decent leg room and a bit of recline. Also the atmosphere STINKS of cigarette smoke because stupid design includes a smoking room as part of a non smoking carriage. And the air conditioning is not up to the job. Need to book a reserved seat in a carriage away from smoking areas, and wear expendable clothes. Note to otherwise grab a seat quickly in unreserved cars because locals are very nimble in getting seated quickly. Also give time to find your way through Tokyo station to the platforms as Shinkansen section is not as well signed as the metro. I like travel by fast train but European trains are much more pleasant
We travelled from Kyoto to Tokyo - it is a lovely experience, fast, efficient and very comfortable. Travel on the left hand side of the train (Kyoto to Tokyo) to see mount Fuji.

After watching the spring high school baseball selection, he always returns to Tokyo on the Kodama train, which runs at each station. It takes an hour longer than the Nozomi, but once you get on it, you'll be at Tokyo Station in no time. I also like that the price is low. With the money I saved, I upgraded to a green seat this time. Tokai Tours is the best.

A convenient way, we took the Nozomi train, it is the fastest, about 2 hours, it cost about 14 thousand yen per adult, cheaper for a child with a reservation. The only way to buy and reserve seats in advance is to install their Smart EX application, where you can pay with a credit card up to a month in advance and select seats. Then you can get the tickets yourself at the station ticket office. An important nuance - when receiving a ticket, you must present the exact credit card that was used for payment. In general, as with all Japanese railways, it is tedious and not obvious. If you see Fuji, you need to take the right lane on the way from Tokyo to Kyoto; in Nozomi there are two seats to the right of the aisle.

I guess they call it the fast train cause you have to have super powers to board in time!  We missed our booked shinkansen and had to board the next one - and had to stand for the 2.5 hour.  They need to consider older folk with heavy luggage and supply for lifts.

The two hour  “bullet train” journey from Odawara to Osaka not only was exceptionally swift, and on-time, but the quality of the experience also was exceptional. Comfortably spacious seating, impeccable standards of hygiene and cleanliness, courteous and efficient terminal and onboard service teams, and good-tasting coffee too. Wow!

Business trip to Osaka with Nozomi. It's a sunny May day with some clouds. Mt. Fuji that can be seen from Mishima and Shin-Fuji is beautiful. It feels like there's still a lot of snow this year, but what do you think? I like the window seat facing the mountain.
I look forward to seeing Mt. Fuji every time. The seats are comfortable so you can spend your time comfortably. It's a great time to eat ekiben on the train (buy it before you get on the train).
we travelled while coming back from mount fuji trip,noiseless,superfast,comfortable..dont know what else to say ..just fantastic experiance which should not be missed while in japan.

I only use the train about twice a month, but I always feel like a VIP every time I use it early in the morning, enjoying the view and the comfortable seating while drinking the coffee sold on the train. It has become my current boom.
To travel around Japan, the best thing is the JRpass, which allows you to take high-speed and commuter trains.
Gentlemen, what a great move. On time, clean, fast. When you sit inside you hardly notice the speed. No vibrations or other things.DB that's how rail travel and service works.

We took the Nozomi Shinkansen, from Tokyo to Kyoto. One of the fastest. Arriving at the station in Tokyo, two workers per carriage entered and, in 10 minutes, cleaned the trains, moving the seats with special mechanisms and changing all the headrests. After which the train left at 9:30 and arrived at 11:47, exactly as scheduled. Anyone who writes that Italian fast trains are the same as these lives on another planet. The difference lies above all in the fact that, in Japan, EVERY trip is like this, i.e. perfect, while in Italy if it goes well twice in a row, you can consider yourself lucky. I would add that the quantity and frequency of these trains, compared to those in Italy, will be 10 times as much, if not more. And I also say that the Shinkansen is the symbol of a much more polite, respectful, serious and upright society than ours. I'll add some information that seems trivial, but I had to do research to make sure I wasn't wrong. The Shinkansen leave from Tokyo Station, which on the Marunouchi subway line is signposted as the "Tokyo" stop. Hello.
Reservations are required before the holidays, but they are very convenient as they run in large numbers. Friday nights are often fully booked as well.

The online reservation system Express Reservation is very convenient. I often use the route between Tokyo and Nagoya, and there are a lot of trains, so using Express Reservation allows me to take a train earlier or later, making the most of my time, which I really appreciate.

apart from punctuality, cleanliness and silence, what is astonishing are the services on board. On a train I have never seen such a large bathroom (in which as an Italian traveler I noticed with a hint of emotion the presence of the toilet paper roll) and even equipped with a child seat for mothers who travel alone with small children and who certainly cannot place them on the floor in case of "need". In front of the bathrooms there are dressing tables with double mirrors, a shelf and a curtain for those who want to change and do their make-up before going down. And, finally, every three or four carriages there are smoking rooms with extractor hoods that don't let out a stink. All topped off with free wifi and a drinks and snack trolley that passes frequently. Applause!

This train epitomises so much of Japan’s way of life. On time within seconds, spotlessly clean, staff who make a polite bow on entering and leaving your compartment. The train is known world wide for its speed and punctuality and with good reason. Utterly reliable.

WEnt from Osaka to Kyoto in 14 minutes to discover the area. The train is on time, reservation of seats not really needed (double the price) as there are 3-5 waggons of non reserved seats. really you must do this train once in your life!

An amazing experience, travelling at 200 mph, with the train feeling surprisingly smooth.  Everything about this travel is remarkable!  It’s almost like travelling on a plane ...The trains run fastidiously to time, they are clean and comfortable, and they even have designated smoking zones !We’d had pre-booked tickets between Hiroshima and Kyoto, but were able to bring our departure forward by some three hours just 10 minutes before the next scheduled departure: an easy and quick exchange at the ticket office facilitated this.  Can you imagine doing the same for an airline ticket at the airport ?The on-board personnel, the guard and trolley lady, frequently walk the length of the train, and as they exit each carriage, they turn and undertake a bow.  Nice touch.The void between the rail services in the UK and those in Japan is unfortunately glaringly transparent across so many different aspects, so if you truly wish to experience exceptional rail travel, then this is a ‘must do’ !
the fastest and most efficient means of transport for three long distances. comfortable, there is room between each seat to stretch your legs.

In the month of April we took the Shinkansen seven times. The trains ran on time, were clean, no loud telephone conversations, no pressure, very good information in Japanese, Chinese and English, hardly any large pieces of luggage (this is usually transported from A to B by private companies) - that's how public transport works. And then there’s the speed! How would it be if the world took Japan as a role model in this regard?

We got to Japan with our routes defined at the beginning therefore, JR pass was a must. We got one for two weeks and it’s worth it especially if you travel between the cities. For us, just one ride to The northern part of the country and back was the price for Jr pass. It’s a very practical and comfortable way to travel, better to have a seat reserved that can be done within minutes before the ride but better one day before because on important routes in the early morning and late evening commuters go and it is full.As a bonus for our experience, i had the miss-fortune of losing my pass the first day running to catch the train. In matter of a couple of hours, they have found it, took it to lost and found and informed the staff on our final destination about this situation. With the help of a nice person, we got a ticket saying that i can ride free to get my pass back from Tokyo. It is better to keep it better and not loose it, but if it happens, it’s a better experience from the one you are used to in European countries.

My wife and I were here on a Gate1 tour with 34 others, leaving Tokyo and going to Osaka, where we stayed at the Courtyard Marriott near the train station.This was our first time on the bullet train.  We were very impressed.  Japan trains leave on time, extremely clean, quiet and smooth, and it took 2.5 hours to arrive at Osaka; a car would take about 6 hours.There were souvenir/food cart if you need it.  Some of the views were very nice, though many were partially blocked by a wall.Train seating was basically 3 seats, aisle 2 seats, and room overhead for carry-on.  Since we were with a tour, I am not sure how luggage would have been handled

The Shinkansen during Golden Week is very crowded, and all reserved seats are full. The non-reserved seats are filled with standing customers. It looks like the number of trains will increase, and the congestion shows no signs of slowing down.

I had some business to go to Ise during Golden Week, so I went to reserve a reserved seat a week in advance, but it was only possible to reserve a seat after 7:00 in the morning and after 2:00 in the afternoon. However, when I went to Tokyo Station on that day, I saw a sign saying, ``All reserved seats and green cars on today's Shinkansen are sold out.'' I thought the situation was terrible, but when I went to the non-reserved seats on the Shinkansen one train earlier than scheduled, I found that there was no one standing in the seats all the way to Nagoya. I thought something like this could happen. By the way, the next day's non-reserved seats from Nagoya to Tokyo were empty and you could sit anywhere.

Public transportation was a delight in Japan. Efficient. Clean. On-time, all the time, every time!! All you need to get around the country is transit cards.The Shinkansen (bullet train) was no exception to the amazing transit experiences.It uses a different ticketing system and it is more expensive, but we thought it was worth it for the experience. 280 km/hour so smooth and quiet you aren't even aware how fast you're going. Thumbs up!

It was amazing watching these bullet trains zoom in and out of the station. Our train arrived, we got on quickly and we were off!! We left the station fast and then gathered speed. Even so the train didn’t seem as fast as we’d expected.  The seats were basic but were upholstered and reasonably comfortable. In front of each seat was an information panel showing our carriage 14 – and those either side, 13 and 15 - and indicating where the doors and loos were. Overall we felt disappointed that the experience wasn’t as fantastic as we’d expected.

Very fast , 280km h and efficent to Osaka. This train is a delight to ride on and the views spectacular. Very quiet inside with good access to phone charges/power point. Seats were confortable and used jr pass. Glad i didn't book grren class pass and there were no seats. Normal class is more than fine.

An efficiency inconceivable for us Italians, the trains are perfect, very punctual, very clean and spacious. We traveled from Kyoto to Tokyo very quickly and smoothly. The price is very high but if you want to get there quickly it's a fantastic vehicle!
The best way to travel between Tokyo and Osaka ( send your luggage in advance to your hotel) and get a bento box to enjoy on the train

Before coming to Japan, I heard a lot about these trains, but seeing them in person, and especially traveling on them, is something amazing. The organization and logistics system of these trains is perfect. I don't know if something like this could be repeated in another country (without a culture of self-discipline). Certainly not with us.

Tokaido Shinkansen - the world's first high-speed railway was opened for the Olympic Games in Tokyo in 1964. It serves the largest metropolitan area in Japan with 6 million-plus cities Tokyo-Kawasaki-Yokohama-Nagoya-Kyoto-Osaka. There are three types of trains running (or rather, flying): Nozomi, Hikari and Kodama. The fastest is “Nozomi”: it covers the distance from Tokyo to Osaka in just 2.25. with an average (!!!) speed of 285 km/h. Kodama runs the same distance in 4 hours, because... has the most stops along the way. If you, as a prudent tourist, bought a JR Pass, you, like us, are on the road to Hikari, because... Nozomi is not owned by Japan Rail and passes are not valid on it. The Shinkansen runs like clockwork and is never late, but we were “lucky” - in July 2018 we were caught in the worst flood in Japan in decades (more than 200 dead). The Shinkansen was stopped on the Nagoya-Hiroshima line for the first time in many years and we had to return to Tokyo and take a roundabout route through Kanazawa. This would have cost a pretty penny if not for the JR Pass. By the way, the Shinkansen can also stop for seismic reasons, because... it is equipped with seismic sensors. Neither on the way to Nagoya nor back we were able to see Fuji in the Hakone area - everything was covered in clouds.
thank you always. This is the Tokaido Shinkansen. I wonder how many times I'll ride it before I die. I will continue riding even if the linear train is built.

For those of you fond of Amtrak or your local commuter railroads, prepare to be embarrassed after riding the Bullet Train. It arrives and departs on schedule (as did other Tokyo trains I took), the ride is incredibly smooth (no rail joints or shimmy) and quiet. I've risen US trains for decades and there is nothing that compares.
Comfortable, fast, punctual trip to central stations in each city. Simply impeccable.... Faster and cheaper than the plane to move within Japan....
Went on 2 week Japan trip woth family. Used Japan Rail Pass to travel on high speed Shiniaksen Bullitt Trains. Always on time, clean, fast but inside train car it is a smoother and gentle ride.
I took the shinkansen for visiting Osaka from Tokyo. It was a great experience. I felt like I am on an airplane, running on the ground.

Recently, in addition to JR, private railways have also installed special storage areas for large suitcases, etc. However, the Tokaido Shinkansen has not given any thought to storage areas, even though rolling stock improvements have been made since its opening. We often see tourists from overseas struggling to find a place to store their suitcases. In addition to speeding up trains and increasing the number of seats, we would like to see more passenger-friendly facility services.

We traveled from Tokyo to Kanazava and the trip was quick and efficient. The price is quite steep however.Make sure you know what station your train leave from (Tokyo has more than one) and be there with some time margin as the stations are huge and not always easy to find the right track...
Very punctual. This alone distinguishes them from our red arrows which travel at the same speed and are even more elegant. I was expecting who knows what...
Caught the train from Tokyo to Kyoto, just an amazing experience, on time , clean and efficient, not like the UK rail service. Great view of Mount Fuji as well.

The best way to see Japan. We ordered our Japan rail pass from the US. It was mailed to us and we had it on us when we landed in Japan. You need to convert the paper passes to actual rail passes once you land there at an actual Rail pass office.Once you get the passes you can decide to reserve specific tickets for specific trains or go without reserving tickets by getting into the unreserved compartments.Tickets with Japan rail passes cannot be obtained at ticket vending machines. They have to be bought at JR ticket offices. Also you need to flash these passes to a real officer instead of feeding them to a ticket machine in order to get in or out of the JR train lines. JR ticket offices are in almost every statsion. They can be crowded at times so plan accordingly.We travelled by the unreserved cars a few times and found that goign unrresered isn't difficult except that a seat is not gauranteed and you may not get to sit together if you are travelling as a group.

My wife and I picked up the JR Rail Pass in the USA and just returned from a month in Japan. The BULLET TRAIN is magnificent and so are the personal at JR Railways.  All the trains are safe, efficient, run on time, all the time and very, very fast. It is truly a great credit to Japan and its people.

It is very convenient for Japanese people to use it on a daily basis. However, it is very inconvenient for tourists from overseas to not be able to make reservations online. Also, there is not much space to put suitcases, etc., so it is difficult for individual travelers from overseas. If the number of overseas travelers increases in the future, I would be happy if they could take care of that.

Several things I’ve learned:1. Go to the ticket machine — there would be JR Railway staff who will assist you in booking your tickets (its easiest when you have cash in hand, or your credit card pin is active). 2. Make sure which train you want: there are three kinds of trains depending on speed. The Nozomi is fastest. Get the GreenCar to get better seats with better legroom.3. Before you leave the ticket counter: double check your trip number, the platform where you need to be, the car number and seat number (if you bought reserved seats).4. There are are two gates you need to enter (after you buy your ticket). Make sure to get your ticket after the first gate (as this is just the common entry point to the JR Lines), then use that ticket for the Shinkansen gantry. 5. Be there in time! Your trip time is LITERALLY the time the train will close its doors. So if your trip is 11:16AM, be there at least 10 minutes before.
The most famous Shinkansen. It connects Osaka and Tokyo, so there are a lot of trains. If you are going to Osaka, we recommend taking the Tokaido Shinkansen instead of flying.

Tokyo is a huge terminal station where people are always coming and going. The Tokaido Shinkansen, which departs from Tokyo Station, is used by many people for everything from sightseeing to business. There are too many people, especially around long holidays and in the morning and evening. Before entering the Shinkansen ticket gate, be sure to finish your shopping inside the Tokyo Station ticket gate.
I rode the Shinkansen and loved the smooth ride. Our seats were reserved! It reminded me of Amtrak in NY but was much quieter, smoother and comfortable.

I have been in Tokyo and traveled with the amazingly fast and clean Shinkansen train, when I went to Kyoto. These trains are the best way to travel when one is going to many different cities in Japan. They are always on time, very clean and the onboard atmosphere in calm and quiet, which I prefer. Very few - if any mobile phones, when someone wants to chat, they always leave the train compartment, just as the simple rules tell you to do. You should never show disrespect and be a loudmouth on Shinkansen trains. This is the friendly, polite and very respectfull way to travel, that is why I find Shinkansen so wonderful. It is easy to buy tickets in Tokyo Central Station and you can choose your seat. Very comfortable, clean seats too. On the way to Kyoto I looked out the window and saw the magnificent Fuji mountain, so beautiful. You can buy small things to eat on the Shinkansen trains, something to nibble on -  before you lean back and just relax.

Easy to follow signs will get you to your platform.  The staff at JR are friendly, a bit overwhelmed with tourists, but helpful.  Be punctual the trains leave on time.  Ok to bring your own food, but keep the trains clean.  Japan has a lack of garbage can no matter where you go.

Get the JR Pass BEFORE YOU LEAVE FOR JAPAN. Must be bought online before arrival and allows for almost limitless travel on the Shinkansen trains (check to make sure that your entire route is covered by the pass). Get an Bento box and a beer at the station or on the train, sit back and watch the scenery change.

loved using the shinkansen with the JR pass from Tokyo to Osaka and Kyoto.... the train was very clean, the staff were friendly...I pre booked all my seats and had no problems at all... great service.
Plat Kodama is good if you have time. I would like to see more discount services. Even Nagoya is too expensive.
I'm very grateful that the time is short, but the smell leaks from the smoking room, so I can't bring my children near it.

I have taken various shinkansen all over Japan.If you are a tourist and buy a JR pass, the shinkansen is the fastest and most cost effective way to travel between major cities in Japan. Train stations are generally centrally located in cities, so once you get to your desired location, there are lots of transportation options to take you where you want to go.Also, there are always good hotels and hostels in the vicinity of nearly every train station in the country, so if you do a bit of research you won't have to haul your luggage around too much. That is, if you don't take advantage of the excellent luggage transport options available to and from the airports to nearly all hotels + convenience stores in the country.Shinkansen are unwaveringly punctual, spotlessly clean, and very comfortable - especially if you opt for the (luxury) green cars. Most long haul (more than 1 hour) routes offer a food and beverage service - so you can enjoy a beer or Suntory cooler as you gaze at Mt. Fuji and the mandarin groves through your window on the way to Kyoto, for example. Otherwise, there are food (and shopping) options in most train stations so you can stock up before you get on the train.Check out Hyperdia for all the up-to-date schedules for pretty well every train in Japan (up to one year in advance).Love the trains in Japan - I just wish the rest of the world could build and run train systems the way the Japanese do.NOTE 1: It is best to reserve a seat on shinkansen and limited express trains with a reserved seat option the day before you plan to travel. You can get your reserved seat the day of your travel or take a chance on unreserved seats as well, but, you may not get a seat on the train of your choice especially if you are travelling during periods of high volume. Another option is to make seat reservations online on the JREAST website (up to one month in advance), but you have to pick up tickets at designated pick-up locations the day before your scheduled departure and pick up is not available at all train stations.NOTE 2: Train stations like Tokyo and Shinjuku are HUGE and CRAZY busy and can be intimidating and frustrating to navigate as there are wall to wall people pretty well all the time - moving fast - and signs are not always the clearest. More than 3.5 MILLION passengers pass through Shinjuku Station every day! To make matters more difficult, unless you speak Japanese - many of the station staff may not be able to help you as they do not all speak or understand English really well. However, a saving grace is that there is a LOT of information online regarding how to navigate these stations - with pictures - so if you just do a little reading before you tackle the stations - or bring the links on your smartphone - getting around can be a lot easier. Shinjuku Station even has its own navigation app. The MATCHA-JP website is a good one for getting all kinds of directions and recommendations, and not just for train stations.

This trip was on my partners bucket list and he was not disappointed. It was comfortable, fast and easy to use. Nothing cheap about it though. The train got up to 279km which is amazing. Happy to recommend this for everyone to try.

This was the easiest and quickest way to get from Tokyo to Kyoto and we even got views of  Mt Fuji on the ride (be sure to reserve a seat on the right going to Kyoto and left when going to Kyoto for best views).

No better way to get from city to city along the Tokyo and Osaka area.Slightly more costly than flying, but you are going city center to city center. When the cost and time to get to and from the  airport is considered, it beats flying.

There are three types of Shinkansen (Bullet Train):Nozomi = fastest, almost no stopsHikari = Fast, stops in a few places (See below)Kodama = slower, stops at most stations.A JR Pass will NOT allow you on the Nozomi, but the Hikari is fast enough.We boarded at Odawara (closest stop for Hakone etc) and went to Kyoto for a little day-trip. the journey was 2 hrs each way, and the 07:04 train from Odawara to Kyoto was excellent!  16:35 train back and all was well.  From Odawara it's a 1 hour ride to the first stop at Nagoya.  I think Tokyo to Odawara is about 30m on the Hikari Shinkansen, so you can do Kyoto from Tokyo in 2.5hrs  Amazing!.These trains are FAST!  I clocked it at 275kph (160mph) as it sped through the countryside.  Super smooth, you barely know you are moving.  The cars are more like airplanes than trains.  The cars all have signed scrolling in Japanese and English, so you will not get lost ;-)In the Green Car - First Class (cars 8 & 9), they give you hot towels and there is a snacks cart that comes by from time to time.If you have a JR Pass, remember (1) Exchange the JR Pass you buy outside Japan for the real JR Pass at the JR Offices in some stations (or airport) (takes about 30 mins dependant on queues), then (2) you can book your seats and get the ticket (NOT online! Why not, it's 2019!!!) and then (3) the first time you use the pass & Ticket you have to go through the gate with the attendant to get it stamped. Allow extra time for this and don't rush about!  The whole process takes a little time, but it's so worth it.It's an experience in it's own right, as well as a handy fast way to get from one part of Japan to another.

We took many Shinkansen rides during our travel in Japan using our 14 days JR Pass (Green Car) which is equivalent to first class. You have to go to a JR office at the starting station and obtain reservation tickets (free for JR pass holders). So, you have to budget some time between getting to the station and the train departure time. Usually, 20 minutes is good for that as some of the offices have lines. The ride from Kyoto to Odawara was spectacular, specially so as we got to get a ringside view of Mt Fuji near Shin-Fuji station. Unfortunately, we got tickets on the Kodama version of the train which has more stops and hence slower. And no food service at all. We were ravenous after the 3 hour journey when we reached Odawara.

Have travelled many times to and from Tokyo to Kyoto, Shin-Osaka, Kobe, Hiroshima ect. Have loved all the times on this train. Always on time. Always clean cars, toilets, seats. Great on board food service with nearly street level pricing. No talking on cellphones allowed in the cabins but between cars (most trains in Japan). Great value for distance travelled. A trip to Japan is not complete without experiencing a trip on the Shinkansen. SmartEX is their new app that allows you to book seats. Download before going and become familiar with it. Very convenient.

Great way to move larger distances around Japan . Make sure you reserve a seat (free of charge).If you have to change trains often it means you just stay at same platform but move to different car position for next train .Its all well signposted and staff will help you as best they can.

Took the train from Tokyo to Kyoto sitting on the right side on the outward journey and left side on the return in hope of seeing Mount Fuji.It's a sight to behold. The train pulls into the station about 30 minutes prior to departure. A small group of men dressed in blue and pink clad women enter the train and do a 10 minutes spruce up ready for passengers to board.Check your ticket for the coach number which is shown along with the seat number and place. The coach number is on the ground on the platform and you can queue there.The seats have generous proportions and can recline; there's an adjustable footrest and pull down table. The electronic board gives route information in Japanese and English; announcements are made in both languages too. Refreshments can be purchased from a trolley although the selection is fairly limited. Once passengers are aboard, the barrier  slides across to prevent access to the train as it picks up speed even as it's leaving the station, punctional to the minute. Travel is very smooth although you do have a sense of speed. Announcements are made prior to arriving at a station so passengers are ready to alight without delay.Unfortunately, Mount Fuji was shrouded in clouds on our outward trip but we were rewarded with a fantastic view of this iconic mountain on our return. It was a wow moment to savour.Highly recommended.

Buy your tickets ahead so you can get reserved seats from any JR station.  We bought one way tickets and we travelled with large suitcases with wheels but didn’t have any difficulties either in the station or on the train.

A delightful little train, of course, but the price is high. It's also interesting to watch the Shinkansen from the outside, but it doesn't last long. Like a bullet whistled) It’s good to take an o-bento with you in the carriage

A very comfortable way to travel between these 2 great cities and a must go do while in japan. Besides beeing fast and comfortable you have a good chance to see mount Fuji when sitting om the left side. Left side when riding the train from kyoto to Tokyo!Ny advice is to book the tickets at the shinkansen office and not the ticket machine. To be sure to get the right seats and if you prefer to pay by card! Ticketmachine accepts only cash.
Punctual..very clean..helpful and very smiling staff...perfect. Congratulations for the quality of service

It's convenient because there are a lot of them. If you are boarding from Tokyo Station, you can sit in a non-reserved seat if you line up. You can also charge your smartphone. It is said that Wi-Fi can be used, but I have never been able to use it.

We took this train to travel from Osaka to Tokyo, we booked our tickets in advance that is one day before and we booked our seats, we used our tickets to enter the train track, no one asked about the tickets in the train after that, the train was clean, quiet and fast, very nice experience.

I was able to move between Nagoya and Shin-Osaka comfortably. I was thinking of having a coffee in the car, but the time was too short. . . It's a luxurious story. The majority of people are men, so I wonder how women feel about it. .

I am impressed by the efficiency of the company's cleaning at Tokyo Station. The green car was spacious and I was able to enjoy the journey.
Took the bullet train back to Tokyo from our trip to Mr Fuji.  Easy and fast way to transit. Travel at rush hour was expectedly crowded, but your really not on the train for more than 30 minutes.

A must try ! Feeling it when i move is amazing ! Simple and convenient! Amazing, a little messy but when u undeestand how it works it is easy! We went from tokyo to osaka  it took 2 hours , 800 km/h

I used the Nozomi general reserved seat between Tokyo and Nagoya. It took us an hour and a half to get to Nagoya, and we were able to see Mt. Fuji as well. I also booked the hotel with JR Tokai Tours, so I don't know the price, but I thought it was a good deal. If you are going to Nagoya, we recommend taking the Shinkansen.

It is said that you are lucky if you see a yellow Shinkansen. It is said to be a special vehicle used for maintenance of the Shinkansen, so it is rarely seen, but it is a good feeling to see it. Really enjoyed taking a very fast shinkansen (bullet train) from Odawara (near Hakone) to Kyoto. It's not cheap, but a very pleasant mode of transportation. If you're going that direction, sit on the right side and get a view of Mt. Fuji as you fly by at 200mph+.

I bought the JR Pass (7 days), Green Car for my trip to Japan in Feb 2019.Firstly, the Green Car Pass costs about 30% more than its respective Ordinary Car Pass. It allows you to make reservations on the following: 1) Shinkansen Green Cars (Except Nozomi and Mizuno services), 2) Green seats on Limited Express trains, 3) any JR commuter trains. The Green Cars on Shinkansen (Cars 8, 9 and 10 for a 16-car train) are located in the middle of the station, which means it will be the nearest to the escalators, giving Green Car passengers better convenience. The seats are arranged in a 2+2 vs 3+2 in Ordinary cars, hence the wider seats with more leg room. The seats can be reclined electrically: with the push of a slider button, and each seat is equipped with a personal reading light. In addition, a leg-rest is also provided. Perks of Green Car: 1) Seats are more comfortable, wider, more leg room, 2) less crowded, hence a quieter cabin, 3) less queue when boarding, 4) free refreshment towel after boarding. Cons of Green Car: 1) JR Green Car Pass is 30% more expensive to Ordinary Car Pass, 2) All seats in Green Cars have to be reserved beforehandIf you're travelling alone and don't wish to squeeze with other passengers, I felt that it will be better to get the Green Car Pass.
So much more comfortable and easier than flying.  It is a great experience and if you can, take the green car and ride in style.
I used the Tokaido Shinkansen to go to Kyoto. It was convenient to be able to make reservations and seat assignments using my smartphone. I would like to go out on the Shinkansen again.

The fast train (aka Bullet Train) is only a bit faster than a normal train if you take from nearby cities to Tokyo (in my case, Odawara Station). Punctual, convenient and efficient. It costs a bit but saves time and is efficient. Good seats, smoking room and toilets.
The train was absolutely spotless as cleaners came on at every stop. The seats are comfortable and there is plenty of legroom. Great journey.

The best way to warp when you don't want to ride a crowded train is the Shinkansen. I use the Tokaido Shinkansen frequently, although it is only for one section. I use it for a business trip from Nagoya to Tokyo. If you are looking for non-reserved seating, we recommend Hikari. In particular, the trains that stop at one extra station are just a few minutes apart from the Nozomi and have 5 cars, so you can sit comfortably.
The seats are comfortable and the toilet is spacious. I think it's a comfortable ride. When I tried to charge it, I had to bend down to my feet...I almost forgot my charger.

Took a trip from Tokyo to Osaka. The train departed and arrived on schedule. The cabin was clean and comfortable. The announcements were clear. There was a food cart that passed by the cabin.

Travelled on the bulletin train from Motohakone to Tokyo Central Station, the journey was very comfortable, the train travelled at 200mph literally like a bullet!! Definitely recommended if visiting Japan and the bullet train experience can be included in many of the tours that visit Mount Fuji and the Hakone area.

I often use it to go from Tokyo to the Kansai area. There are many trains, and these routes are specialized for fast travel. This is inconvenient if you want to get off midway through the Nozomi-priority timetable. We used the Shinkansen train to travel between Tokyo and Kyoto. It took us a while to understand the ticketing system and how to get the best deal, we had to do quite a lot of research before, basically the tickets are express or non express and with seat reservation or without. We ended up paying around £180 return each by booking at the station in advance, to be honest it’s a lot more than I’d ever be prepared to pay in the UK or Europe, but to ride on the bullet train isn’t something I’ve done before so for me it was worth it.Arriving at the station there’s plenty to buy to take on board for breakfast and if you’ve not had time to buy something before there’s a trolley service onboard. For me as a vegetarian it was quite difficult as most of the breakfast options contain meat or fish so I had to go with some vegetable crisp/fingers and an orange juice, the prices onboard aren’t too bad. We booked ourselves onto the 2 seater on the right of the train so we would be able to get a view of Mt Fuji on the journey to Kyoto from Tokyo. Luckily for us we did manage to get a decent view for a brief few mins when the clouds cleared. The speed of the train is unlike any other I’ve used before but at the same time it’s very smooth so you don’t notice it so much, if you have long legs like me you’ll be pleased to know that you’ll receive a generous amount of legroom in the standards seats.On the return we missed our train back due to oversleeping, but we managed to get ourselves on the next train which was only a few mins after and we found ourselves a spare seat, the conductor was great and allowed us to travel with the ticket for the previous train which in the UK probably wouldn’t have happened and we’d have had to pay for it again.If you decide to spend a few days in Kyoto and return back to Tokyo afterwards I recommend leaving your luggage in a storage facility at one of the stations.
