Those non-reserved seats are very hard to book in the tourist season, such as viewing cherry blossoms or autumn leaves, and long vacation season. If you use non-reserved seats in the group, I recommend you to use Shinkansen at Tokyo station or Shin-Osaka station of departure point. Especially for Shinkansen from Shin-Osaka Station, station staffs will tell you at the ticket counter.The difference between the Tohoku Shinkansen and the Joetsu Shinkansen is that there is no exclusive storage space for large luggage such as suitcases, and Tokaido Shinkansen is weak against snow cover. If you have large, I recommend using the front seats or the back seats in the vehicle. If you use the bullet train in winter, you should check the weather in advance. Still, the delay will be negligible.

At this time of year, I am concerned about the weather in Sekigahara. The Tokaido Shinkansen is still sensitive to snow and is delayed when it snows. I would like them to follow the example of Hokuriku Shinkansen and Hokkaido Shinkansen.

The bullet train was convenient as was much public transportation experienced in Japan. The ticket counter staff often spoke English and were readily available to suggest travel routes and times upon request. It cost at least a hundred dollars  for a one way trip between Osaka to Tokyo and Tokyo to Kyoto.

I took a train to Shin-Osaka Station for the first time in a while. Although it was crowded due to the three-day holiday, it was a comfortable trip on the Nozomi. Ekinaka at Shin-Osaka Station is a lot of fun.
I wish we had bullet trains in the US. This is a great way to travel, so much better than flying, clean, comfortable and spacious. Highly recommend.

In the past, there was something called a "private room," which was very useful when traveling with children. Every time I go home, I think about it, but I wonder if we can at least set up priority vehicles for families with children, even just for the New Year holidays. I think everyone, both those with children and those without children, will be happy. The Shinkansen is very comfortable, and as someone who is now much lighter, I feel that this is because people with children are doing their best to cradle their children or move them to the colder decks. I regularly send my opinions to JR Tokai, but I thought I'd post here in hopes of calling attention to them.

I love train travel...this is the fastest in the world! If you go to Kyoto (5 hours) you will be able to see Mount Fuji from the window sitting on the right side. The price is high..but it's worth the experience. Advance reservations are generally required.

The Shinkansen is a comfortable means of transportation, but the green cars are especially comfortable. First of all, the seat is large and thick, so it provides a good grip and reduces fatigue. It's also nice to be able to take off your shoes and go barefoot. Also, the aisle seat is almost always empty, so you won't feel cramped and can keep your valuables close at hand. Also, the service where the crew comes to pick up the garbage is not very simple, but it is very helpful. Having a few blankets around the edges of the vehicle can be a blessing during the cold winter months, especially for women. Also, it doesn't matter if you have it or not, but we also give out free wet tissues and the monthly magazine Wedge.

With the Japan rail pass available to non-Japanese tourists, most shinkansen trains are free!  They are spacious and comfortable, and makes travelling between major cities an enjoyable activity on its own.My son listed the shinkansen trains and the ever-present drink vending machines as his two favorite things about Japan!

One of the important means of transportation. I ride it on business trips several times a month. Lately, Shinkansen trains departing from Tokyo Station in the evening have become extremely crowded. Being punctual in Japan seems like a normal thing, but that's not the case overseas, and it's actually amazing.

For anything that requires more than 3 hours by bus or regular train, the shinkansen is the best way to go.  Tickets can be bought right from the airport station itself and I would advise doing so there because it is not only convenient but also safest as there may be days that all reserved seats run out.
Has no parallel across the world and a trip to cherish. Fast, punctual, well maintained and iconic of Japan.

The greatest let down for foreigners. The Shinkansen tickets cannot be purchased from outside Japan but thousands of tourists need to use it. But once we arrive from other countries all the seats in all 4 types of Shinkansen trains are sold out for weeks in a row. What do they expect people to do? All to have a friend, relative or agent in Japan? We had to buy a same day flight ticket from Tokyo to Kyoto on 31 December and  it was extremely expensive. On the way back we paid the Yen equivalent of AUD$175 or USD $121 per person for a one-way ticket on 3rd January. This entitled us to nowhere to store suitcases and NO SEAT on the 2: hours and 40 minute journey STANDING all the way Kyoto-Tokyo (476 kms). We couldn’t believe any company could get away with putting hundreds of passengers at risk on every one of their train (one every 7 minutes) without sit belts or bars to hold on to, on a vehicle that moves at around 300 kms/hour. This is insane and would be illegal anywhere else in the world. I wondered if insurance companies would cover us for injuries sustained if there was an accident while travelling under these risky conditions. It’s like engaging in Bungy jumping! So forget about enjoying a view or having an exhilarating experience. This is the December-January holiday so be prepared to waste money on false hope and risk your safety and life if you need to travel by fast train inJapan.

Coming to Japan and not riding the Shinkansen is like eating bread without marmalade, or so I was told by a friend from Fiji. The trains are gloriously fast, perfectly punctual, fantastic service, efficient, and the JR staff handle passengers with class and dignity. Who would not want to travel this way? Consult with the JR ticket office to make sure that you get on the Shinkansen that suits your schedule best. Ride the fast rails of Japan! Get on the bullet train of Japan!

On this day, many people had large trunks, and they all rode with their trunks in front of their feet. I couldn't stretch my legs in the big trunk, and the person in front of me could only recline the seat a little. We both spent three hours in a cramped space, but was there somewhere we could put our trunks? If not, I would like them to create a trunk storage area somewhere in each vehicle.

There are many, they arrive quickly, and they are comfortable. I have the impression that the area, including the station, is safe even late at night, and I have even used the last train there. Although you often choose a reserved seat, you can save a little money by using a non-reserved seat, and there are benefits no matter which train you take. Recommended on days and times when it's not crowded.

I was traveling to Nagoya alone, and although I flew back, I took the Shinkansen to go there. It was easier to get there than by plane because you could get there from the station faster than I expected. I'm an airplane fan, so I don't think I'll use it much in the future.

Typically efficient, arrives and leaves when says it will.  Comfortable and easy to reserve seats at any station or machine.  We had a first class Japan Rail Pass which was definitely worth it.  Got wet towels once in our seats, staff all so friendly, polite and helpful and immaculately turned out.  Seat are all in direction of travel but there is a lever and you can turn them round which was helpful as there were 4 of us and meant we could face each other and chat. Very clean and you also get a bag for your rubbish when buying food from trolley and all rubbish collected regularly but bins at door if needed.  Definitely the way to get about and very user friendly for tourists.
Traveling in Shinkansen is a great expereince and is perfect for efficient travel to save time. Depart from Tokyo Central Station and arrive at Osaka Central Station in style.

They are punctual and have fewer accidents. Japan's pride. Some say there are gaps in security and that checks on carry-on luggage should be introduced, and I think that's correct, but if they were to be introduced, it would disrupt the smooth operation of the train. In a sense, I would like to see the pride of the peaceful and methodical Japanese people, and the continued service and technology they offer. Needless to say, Nozomi has outlets near the window and in the front and last rows for charging. I feel happy when I can see Mt. Fuji right next to me on a sunny day.

Tokaido Sinkansen is the original Shinkansen (Bullet train), which now runs through Japan. It has three categories, Nozomi (Hope), Hikari (Light) and Kodama (Echo). Very poetic that the hope travels faster than the light and the sound. Nozomi is the fastest of three express trains, followed by Hikari and Kodama. Nozomi stops only at selected stations. Kodama stops at all stations. Hikari is in-between, so one should check which station Hikari stops. For the express train which reaches the top speed of almost 190 mph, with 16 cars with more than 1000 seats, it is highly precise and punctual, departing every 5-10 minutes. In the train you really do not feel the strong vibration which you feel in high speed trains in other countries, the train ride is very smooth as well, thanks to the computerized tilt system to tilt cars slightly to go through curbs with higher speed. The car is very quiet, and extremely clean. In addition, car attendants with wagons come around avery 30 minutes or so, selling coffee, snacks, Bento boxes, souvenirs and amazing number of merchandize to meet your needs. To catch Shinkansen, you need just 10 minutes or so at the station. No security checks, and if you reserve a seat in advance, your ticket tells you exactly which car, which row and which seat, so you can go strait to the exact position of your car and wait for the train to arrive. Be in the position in advance, as Shinkansen train does not wait for you. Even at major stations they stop only for a minute or two, to unload and load passengers. You are supposed to know the exact spot you should wait for your assigned car to stop. Above all, it has amazing safety record. It has the system to automatically stop the train before the earthquake hits the track. Since starting operation in 1964, no one was killed in the Shinkansen train accident. For Tokyo - Osaka, Shinkansen probably has the competitive edge over flights, as stations are in the middle of the city. For longer distance (probably 4 hours and longer), flights tends to have more competitive edge. It is a must experience, which in many ways epitomizes the Japanese tradition of punctuality, self discipline, speed, precision, customer service and commitment to the quality.
Trains in Japan are amazing. Even if you dont have definite plans or maybe you have children (age 3-60) that like trains its worth the experience to witness the efficiency.

My children wanted to try the world famous shinkansen and they really liked it. We booked our tickets in advanced via Smart-Ex and got the tickets from the ticketing machine in 2 easy steps.Tokyo train station was huge but there are plenty of signage to guide us around besides the ever helpful staff.The Nozomi train was really fast and quiet. Great experience for my kids.
I use it often at work. It's an hour and a half from Nagoya, you can make online reservations, and you can use Suica, so it's quite convenient. You can also see Mt. Fuji on the way.

The Tokaido Shinkansen will take you to Nagoya, Kyoto, Osaka and in-between stops, like the resort town of Asami, depending on the train you take. The fastest shinkansen with the fewest stops is NOZOMI, followed by HIKARI. The train time to Kyoto from Tokyo is a little over 2 hours. It is sheer pleasure to splurge and take the green car. The only drawback: the shinkansen is relatively expensive unless you book a package deal that includes hotel accommodation. The Tokaido Shinkansen runs very frequently with waits of minutes in-between trains. It has never had an accident. The technology for the shinkansen was developed in the 1930's and the first 'bullet train' was introduced at the 1964 Tokyo Olympics. The time then from Tokyo to Kyoto was 5-6 hours. Within a few years that time was halved. Over subsequent years, the time has gradually been shaved further, so that on the NOZOMI the time from Shinagawa Station to Kyoto is 2 hours, 11 minutes. A beautiful travel experienceNote: if you are coming from overseas you can buy a pass on the Shinkansen traveling on the second fastest HIKARI speed. These passes must be purchased while in your home country.

40 years ago perhaps the shinkansen was a great novelty. In Spain we have had the AVE for 26 years and the difference is barely noticeable. Similar speed, similar comfort. If anything, the shinkansen has a First Class in which, by paying, you get comfort and luxury that is beyond what is offered on high-speed trains in the rest of the world.

I had to go to Tokyo for the first time in a while, so I used the Nozomi regular car for a round trip. It was impressive that there were many patrols by police officers. I have taken high-speed trains several times in Europe, and I always take first class. I've only used ordinary cars on the Shinkansen, so it's difficult to compare, but even ordinary cars are reasonably comfortable. I would like to ride in a green car once.

JR rail is one of many major rail lines used in Japan and friends recommended pre-purchasing a pass to save money. We thought we could travel by train using the JR line everywhere in Japan. This was not the case. We traveled 21 days in Japan and bought our JR Rail passes before our holiday. The cost was $700 AUD for each of us (family of 3) which we activated in Tokyo upon arrival to Japan. We had a fabulous round trip on the middle island from Tokyo down to Mt Fuji, across to Kanasawa through Matsumoto, and then down to Kyoto and Osaka and regions, back to Tokyo. We traveled to and through many small towns on the way either by train or bus - whichever was timely to our schedule.In Japan, there are numerous railway lines to travel by (the JR line is one of them). But as we traveled extensively, we found that often the JR rail or bus line did not go to parts of cities or towns where major attractions we wanted to see, were situated. When this happened, we could choose to get there by taxi or purchase tickets on other rail or bus lines that did go to the tourist sites. Traveling between some cities and towns we also needed to purchase regional bus tickets to get to major tourist sites on the dates and times that fitted into our schedule when JR line was not available. Despite trying to use JR Rail pass as much as possible, all in all, we paid $700AUD/person for pre-purchased passes and only used $500AUD/person during our trip. Additionally, we had to pay more money for all alternate rail lines and bus tickets that operated outside the JR pass when we couldn't use the JR line. As a family of three, we lost $600AUD of unused JR line travel, spending additional money on the  other modes of travel we did use.If we return to Japan we will not buy any pre-paid rail passes. Instead we will use the numerous rail and bus lines that are available to meet our needs. On the spot fares may be a little more than pre-paid passes but we will save heaps of money by paying fares that we actually need and use. All purchases of tickets for rail and bus are easily bought in any railway station around Japan. Staff were happy to help us.

Today I'm off to Osaka. Stayed the night before for tomorrow's meeting. As usual, I chose the green car today. Of course, you can make reservations using SmartEX. This allows you to easily make reservations and make changes at will. It's super convenient. On the other hand, the towels you get in the green car are very pleasant. Nowadays, you can use wifi for free, which is great.

These days, I often go before Osaka, so I often fly, but the best thing about the Shinkansen is that you can get on it right away, unlike a plane. If I get on the train after 6pm on the day before a holiday, I try to get a reserved seat. Even though the first train was from Tokyo Station, there were times when I couldn't get on many trains. .

We used this service to reach Kyoto from Tokyo and to reach Osaka airport. The service is quite expensive but it is worth it for the punctuality and comfort that all trains enjoy, the possibility of choosing carriages of absolute silence is excellent and the seats that rotate 360° so as to always face the direction of travel of the train are a spectacle. Highly recommended

This time I used the Tokyo Wide Area Pass to go to Karuizawa and Kusatsu Onsen. Several sections of transportation used the Tokaido Shinkansen. As long as you reserve a seat first, it is very convenient and comfortable.

We booked our tickets from a JR office at Shinagawa and the process was quite straightforward .Cost wise wasn't too bad considering the relatively fast ride. Around Y9000 return for each of us. Like all things Japanese,everything runs on time so get there early. We had a few stragglers getting on with luggage and they got the hurry up,which is fair enough. The ride is a great experience and the trains are clean neat and quiet.Our ride to Mishima is a short one so the Shinkansen doesn't really get up to maximum speed until it gets through the tunnels and it's quick alright.(didn't check speed)We got views of Mt Fuji on our journey as well.It's quite a smooth ride as we make our way out of the Tokyo area.Return journey was great as well. JR staff are really patient and helpful. Highly recommended .

Traveled by Shinkansen bullet train from Tokyo to OsakaFast and comfortable train.  Not cheap, but perfect means of transportation The train moves a lot of people and runs every 10 minutes Drinks served on board, but no food

I believe that Japanese railways have the best time accuracy in the world. Recently, security has been strengthened, and you can feel the security as you can often see security guards at Tokyo Station and Shinkansen offices.
It takes less than 2 hours from Tokyo to Nagoya. You can see Mt. Fuji and the sea. The legs are wide enough to charge your phone. After eating the ekiben, we arrived quickly.

For my business trip to Osaka, I have a reserved seat on the Nozomi, but for my business trip to Nagoya, I use the Hikari green car. However, ``Hikari'' is a train that does not have many stops. 5 minutes between Tokyo and Nagoya? There is only a difference in rank and the price is cheap.

I often use it when going to Nagoya or Osaka. There are definitely more people who go quickly on Nozomi than leisurely on Kodama. We recommend a window seat. This is because there is an electrical outlet below the seat, which is difficult to use if you are sitting in an aisle seat.

635874259 Our first experience on a bullet train. It was. Tokyo to Kyoto round trip. One way it took two hours 17 minutes. Extremely prompt. Seating is comfortable. It would be better with a foot rest in frontof the seat though. Seats are spacious and there is plenty of leg room to stretch. It would be nice if they had mood lighting instead of harsh fluorescent illumination. Surprisingly the shinhansen do not have wi fi currently but this may change in time for the summer Olympics that Tokyo will host in less than two years. There is wi fi on all other Japanese trains and metro cars. The speed of this train is great but you dont feel it except for some minor ear pressure. You may bring your food and drink aboard the train or purchase on board for a small mark up. Toilets are plenty and clean and each train has two enclosed smoking cabins with windows. Train personnel will answer questions briefly and politely but otherwise not engage with the passengers. Cost is about the same as the "high speed" lines of Amtrak in the Northeast corridor. All seats are reserved.no charge for seat reserations.
I used it until Shin-Kobe. There are many books and it is comfortable. The seats by the window are convenient as they have power outlets. We arrived at Shin-Kobe in less than 3 hours.

A convenient way to travel! We went from Hiroshima to Tokyo (about 90 miles) and arrived at the minute we were supposed to. They are very fresh trains and it is possible to buy drinks, something to munch on at each station or on board the train. Excellent!

A smooth ride from Tokyo to Kyoto in just over two hours. The only thing that could make this better is a gourmet bento box from Daimaru and some sake to have a feast on board! Regular car seats don't need to be reserved; if not reserving, it's a good idea to get there 20 minutes early or there's a chance you may have to stand. Japan Rail Pass users can't use the fastest Nozomi trains, in which case a ticket from Kyoto to Tokyo costs about 130 USD. Pricey for sure, but worth it IMO.

Punctuality, cleanliness, speed, smooth ride, all those elements make it a very enjoyable experience and a very convenient way to travel in Japan. Reservations advised if peak season. Try not to have too big suitcases, better to send them via your hotel to your next destination the day before.

The trains are always on time, departure are very frequent. The trip itself is very confortable and the space is definetely big.Comparing to high speed train in Europe at least I would say that Shinkansen experience was better.May be it is expensive but I recommend it for your trip inside Japan
Very civilized way to travel with the green ticket/first class.  Comfortable seats and you can bring your own food and booze!
Depart on time and arrive on time. This may seem obvious to Japanese people, but it is not normal in France, where I live. No strikes. There is also less shaking of the train. This is Japan's pride.
You can sit at the edge of the direction and get a good view of Mt. Fuji🗻. I've been riding it every week lately. Of course it's work. I often ride between Kyoto and Tokyo.
This is the view from the third floor terrace of Yurakucho Transportation Center. A Shinkansen passes by with the Tokyo International Forum in the background. Feel the aorta of Japan❗️

We took the Shinkansen from Tokyo to Osaka.  I must say, this was such a beautiful, scenic route.  Without knowing we were going to see it, we saw the snow capped Mt Fuji.  I was totally blown away at how close we were to that.  Spectacular sight.  We purchased a bento for the train ride, which took about 2.5 hours.  They did have a cart service (drinks) that came around to each box car twice.  If you have the opportunity to ride on the "bullet train," please take the opportunity to do so.  It was about $500.00 for two people (Tokyo~Osaka)

I'm currently sitting on the ICE from Frankfurt to the Ruhr area - it's easy for me to praise the Japanese railway company JR for their Shinkansen lines! No ticket without a seat! No delays and if there are, then only a few minutes, which are usually made up for! And for a distance of 550 KM, the fastest Shinkansen only takes 2.5 hours. And the costs are on a par with those in Germany with significantly greater comfort. However, some of the trains are now getting a bit old, which is fair to say. But the latter easily wins the DB - JR comparison!

There is an outlet (power source) at the seat next to the window, which is great for working on your PC, charging your smartphone, etc. When someone on the aisle side asks you to use a power source, the interaction feels very Japanese-like, which is nice.

The Shinkansen journey was relaxing, fast and the train cabin is very clean. However, this route is extremely populated with both locals and tourists, so make sure to book the seats early and buy the train ticket in advance.*If you seat at the correct side of the train on a clear day, you can see Mt. Fuji while travelling between Shin-Osaka and Tokyo.

The train operators have the authority to detain you, so it's very unlike western countries.  I once lost my seat ticket on JR lines from Ome to Shinagawa and they let me through. However my wife who is Japanese born took the Shinkansen from Osaka to Shinagawa and misplaced her seat ticket.  She showed the receipt, but they detained her anyways.  She had been a US citizen for over 10 years and there wasn't time to call the embassy.  Basically they forced her to pay twice or they wouldn't let her go.  This is Yakuza\Mafia type behavior.  I'm only flying down from now on and I've taken the trip about 10 times in the past 20 years for business with Microsoft.

Travelling by shinkansen is so much better than travelling by plane. We bought a JR pass and used it to travel extensively to various places in Japan for 3 weeks. We paid more for the green  pass as we had relatively large luggage - this proved to be a bit of a waste of money as it was so inexpensive to onsend our luggage, we weren't  burdened with it. The "ordinary" cars were also comfortable and the seats could be reserved. Toilets were clean and snacks were available to purchase. It was simply a fantastic experience. Don't miss it!

You have to go to Japan to realize how indispensable high-speed trains are. Here in the Shinkansen stations between Tokyo and Osaka trains leave every few minutes and are always full. Very fast trains that compete with the plane even over significant distances.

Used when traveling to Tokyo. My hotel was in Shinagawa, so I got off at Shinagawa station. It's wonderful to arrive at the station according to the schedule. Since there are many empty seats in the green cars, we should increase the number of private rooms to increase the occupancy rate.

Instead of getting to the airport early, checking your bag, going through security, sitting in a cramped seat, and taking a taxi to/from the airports, take the bullet train.  The ride is smooth, the train is fast (up to 200 mph), the stations are in the middle of the cities, the information is in Japanese and English, and it will in-the-end, probably save you time.  And the train stations have food and gifts available.  5 stars.

It was my first business trip to Tokyo in a while. Get off at Shinagawa Station for the first time. The conventional lines have an old-fashioned feel. Take the train one stop and get off at Shinbashi Station, a town for office workers. For lunch, everywhere was full, so we ended up having it at Yoshinoya.

The seats are also wide, so you can move more comfortably than on an airplane. There are many trains, and you can enjoy the scenery from the train window. If you want to see the ocean, the 3rd row is better, and if you want to see Mt. Fuji, the 2nd row is better.
Even more reliable than Swiss trains! Even a slight delay at the start is reported, and very often made up for. Comfortable and frequent trains
These trains are amazing!  Clean, quiet, fast, and OMG, on time!!  Notices are are in English as well as Japanese so it is easy to navigate.
An absolute must when in Japan go on a Bullet train, TRULY impressive.  It puts UK railways to shame.

Due to a signal problem, there was a significant delay and we were unable to make it in time for the last train on the conventional line. Even though the company was responsible for suspending operations due to no natural disaster, no alternate transportation was arranged, and the train was forced to stay at a train hotel set up at Shin-Osaka Station. A large number of passengers became angry at Kyoto Station, and the police were called to the scene. Even the taxi drivers were shocked at the huge difference in response from other railway companies, including JR.
This was a comfortable train ride and cheaper if you buy the JR pass before leaving home.  It was easy to access from Tokyo Station.

Don’t get me wrong, I love the Bullet Trains but increasingly for foreign tourist who purchase Green Car JR Rail Pass there is no available seats and so the options revert to Standard car and sometimes even non reserved. My group had almost half the journeys we had planned to do at an average time of year (not in holiday time) were taken in Standard car even though we had paid for the Green Car Pass.

We used JR pass for our Hikari Shinkansen trips. The train rides were really fast. Although the Shinkansen was travelling at such a high speed, the rides were so smooth compared to other Japanese trains that we took. Between our seats and the ones in front, there were a lot of space, big enough to put my big luggage in front of me. The cabins were also bright and clean. Staff will push a pushcart selling snacks in between meals. Do not be late because the train will only stop for a few minutes in between stations and they leave on time. Reach the platform earlier so that you will not miss your train.

The entire train and subway system is extraordinary. The bullet train is the best of all. Modern, punctual, clean, organized, shortens transfer times. There is the possibility of purchasing seats in the “green” category. The corresponding cabin is printed on the ticket, you have to stand on the platform where it is written where that cabin will stop and entry is super fast. Tip: travel only with carry on and if you have suitcases use a luggage transfer system that is contracted at the hotel you are in and that sends it to the hotel in the next city to visit, sensational!!!

maybe just that it is preatty expensive....  We used the bullet train for several rides so we came with the JR pass. Defenetly worth the cost.  The ride itself is amazing. The high speed is noticable and the most amazing part is on the turns. Like in an airplane you see the land on one side raising towords you and on the other side you see the sky. Amazing. Another nice technical thing is the ability to turn the sits backwords so a party of several people can sit with eye contact.

During my travels through Japan most of the time I am travelling on a Japan Rail Pass. Great feature, it brings you almost anywhere in great comfort and speed. Unfortunately as a JR Pass holder you are not allowed to ride the fastest Nozomi train. I never understood why not but OK if this is the rule I just have to accept it. Actually when you are on holidays in Japan the loss of time is of course not that dramatic.There are many sub-sections of the Shinkansen. Shinkansen is the overall name, but for instance when I went from Tokyo to Kyusho past summer I took the Tokaido Shinkansen from Tokyo to switch at Shin-Kobe to the Sanyo Shinkansen for Hakata. In Kyushu Japan Rail runs the Kyushu Shinkansen between Kagoshima and Hakata. The trains are basically the same: lot of room and large windows. However there is a small difference when you travel the Kyushu Shinkansen. Their carriages provide just 4 seats abreast instead of the 5 seat abreast in the other Shinkansen trains, so slightly more room. If you have bought a Japan Rail Pass the Shinkansen is probably the best option when travelling through the country.

We actually caught the Shinkansen from Fukuyama to Tokyo. These trains are fantastic. They are regular, very fast, smooth, comfortable, clean. Lots of room between seats and plenty of storage - really there is no need to upscale and pay extra for the green cars just book a reserve seat. The only surprising omission was no WiFi - lots of other JR trains have free WiFi but not the Shinkansen? The other overwhelming aspect is Tokyo station - trying to navigate it can be daunting.
Its efficiency is enviable, it allows you to travel in a short time from one city to another and its speed is not perceived, very comfortable and spacious.

It goes without saying that the Shinkansen is a well-known bullet train, but the ride comfort and speed are perfect, and the new trains are equipped with plenty of electrical outlets, so you can spend a comfortable time inside the train. Especially in places where you can see Mt. Fuji, everyone takes photos and enjoys the magnificent scenery.

The Shinkansen won my heart. Fast, silent and very clean, it is the type of transport that should be available everywhere in the world. Super punctual, with on-board service, space to accommodate luggage, super spacious and comfortable. Highly recommended!!!

The Japanese "bullet" train system is hands down the best in the world.  Fast, comfortable, perfectly safe, and ontime to the minute..  The volume of service is amazing.  From 5:00 to 6:00 p.m. eleven trains leave Tokyo.

Absolutely fantastic every time. So punctual its almost unbelievable. You do not watch for the time...just look for the train...haha! So smooth, so fast, quiet and clean. Lots of space. Can not ask for more out of a train. Would definitely recommend. Toursits normally need a JR rail card/pass from their home country before you get to Japan.

We mainly used the hikari included in the Japan Rail Pass and if I think of the journeys of hope I have taken in the past with the FS it seems third world to me. Comfortable and spacious seats and punctuality that splits the second. The only thing to complain about is that the bathrooms are not always clean.
We traveled by Shinkansen for a week and it was an unforgettable experience, cleanliness, punctuality, service, travel comfort at the highest level. I recommend it

You can ride it or see it. In fact, during a changeover in Tokyo, when I took a video of the cleaners greeting each other as they boarded the vehicle and cleaning smoothly as if dancing, I showed it to a foreign friend, and he was impressed. Japanese things. Recently, uniformed police officers have been patrolling Shinkansen trains, perhaps to prevent terrorism.
Fast and reliable transportation, with much more space than almost every plane out there.  With great service.

I use it occasionally for travel and business trips. I ride using the ticketless service, so I'm glad that it's easier than using a ticket. Even if you bring a large suitcase, you can put it in the back of the vehicle and there will be no extra charge, so it's safer than sending it from your home to your hotel by courier. Although express buses are cheaper, they take a lot of time, so I still prefer traveling by Shinkansen.
A fast, comfortable and extremely punctual bird. The trip was pleasant, quiet and with amenities to charge your cell phone.

When I went out to the platform to board the Hikari from Odawara Station, there was a lot of excitement as foreign tourists took pictures of the Shinkansen passing by. Even now, I realized how many foreign tourists there are. Although the train was crowded, it was a fast and comfortable journey.

Use Nozomi non-reserved seats between Tokyo and Shin-Osaka. The time is about 2 and a half hours. The seat pitch is also wide. There is also a power supply. Would you recommend both sides? It's near the entrance and exit, so there will be some people coming and going, but I think it's fine as long as it doesn't bother you.
We got a Japan Rail Pass and needed to be in Osaka for tours of southern Japan.  The train was clean and modern. The ride smooth and comfortable. Nice way to travel.

Traveling with the Shinkansen is really great: comfort, peace and quiet and super fast. It is wonderfully quiet because the Japanese attach great importance to standards and values ​​and telephone use is prohibited in the compartments (wonderful!).
This is how comfortable traveling is! Clean, punctual, functional trains.... it seems futuristic while it is everyday life!!!
I used it between Tokyo and Nagoya. Shinkansen trains are expensive, but they run frequently and the seats are spacious and can recline, making them quite comfortable.

I took the Tokaido Shinkansen to Osaka and it was comfortable. There were also on-board sales. The legroom was normal. The price is around 20,000 yen for a round trip, so the only drawback is that it is expensive compared to airplanes (LCC, etc.).
Traveling on this high-speed train is a pleasure (it has nothing to envy of any airline company). Shinkansen commercial speed approx. 300km/h

The Shinkansen is one of the world's most famous trains, but new metal cards such as those from Amex can no longer be used at Midori no Madoguchi counters. It seems like they changed it to a sliding type, but then almost 100% of metal cards cannot be read. Even though IC chips are the mainstream overseas, it is unthinkable to introduce a sliding type magnetic reader these days. Green is more expensive than an airplane, but I think the system that takes off and arrives in about 10 minutes or less is more convenient than an airplane. Free WiFi is now available, so I would like to continue using it, but I would like to be able to use metal cards such as AMEX.

We used the Shinkansen from Tokyo to Osaka and back to Tokyo. We reserved our seats so we didn't have to worry about anything. The train was very comfortable. There is great service on the train where there is beverages and food for sale. There is power outlets on the window side of the trains.
quiet, fast, and comfortable, you must try this train if you are there, In Japan without shinkansen so poor

Smoking is now completely prohibited on airplanes, even on long flights of half a day or more, but JR Central, West Japan and Kintetsu are going against global trends and leaving smoking cars and smoking rooms inside the closed spaces of trains. It seems that there are no plans to abolish smoking rooms even after the 2020 Tokyo Olympics, but smoking on trains, which is unprecedented in the world, should be prohibited by law as soon as possible.

If you live in Japan and are used to this line, anywhere else in the world will be somehow a discomfort in some way. Of course much has to do with the people in Japan being polite, still and clean, which adds to the cozyness. Oh, did I mention that there are no thefts? One thing to improve would be feee WIFI...

I arrived in Tokyo in about 2 and a half hours on this ride. It was fast and the seats were wide, so it was very comfortable. If possible, reserve a seat and travel comfortably. It is expensive, but I highly recommend it!!

If the vehicle is near a smoker or a smoking room, the odor will be present even in non-smoking seats. If it is impossible to eliminate it, I would like you to put it at the very end if possible. Everything else is fine. The seats are wider and more comfortable than airplanes.

Very cool, easy to use, definitely the way to move around Japan. Seats are comfy but lack of foot rest makes a little uncomfortable on long hauls. Don't be stupid, if you are going to move around get the JR Pass and save a bundle

We recommend Express Reservation, which even individuals can subscribe to. For an annual membership fee of around 1,000 yen, you can enjoy benefits such as early bird discounts and the ability to upgrade to a green car for each number of times you use the car. Depending on the time of day, such as Hikari, the annual fee can pay for itself with just one trip.

Accustomed to the arrogance of the Italian railways, arriving in Tokyo and getting on the Shinkansen is like projecting yourself into the future, savoring the unusual sensation of leaving and arriving at your destination on time. Remarkable speed even if the interior of the carriages is not particularly elegant, more like a commuter train. The fast cleaning system is interesting and makes the train available for the next journey in just a few minutes.
This route runs from Tokyo to Shin-Osaka. You can travel between Tokyo and Shin-Osaka in about 2 and a half hours. It is very convenient as there are many flights.
Quiet, clean, punctual and fast. That's all you can ask for from an intercity train. A credit to the transport system of Japan.

I would have given it 5 stars because it's super practical, we save more than 30 minutes on the Osaka-Kyoto-Tokyo journeys but the big problem is that we can't use the Railpass. Too bad because it's a great train with quality service.

Train was on time, impressive to watch coming into the station, was fast and comfortable to ride. Fastest way to travel across Japan, with lots if nice views from either side of the train. Saw tea fields in Shizuoka. Not sure where Mount Fuji was so missed it. It would be nice for tourists if there was a map somewhere to show what can be seen along the journey.
I often use it when going to Nagoya, Kyoto, and Osaka. It's very convenient. In particular, the Nozomi train offers fast and comfortable travel.

We took the green car and found that the seats are just that bit better and for us worth the additional price of guaranteeing two seats together. The trains run non stop and are a good alternative to flying. Note that the Shin-Osaka station is bit out of the center of the city, but easy to get to with the subway.

I used Nozomi to travel from Shin-Osaka to Nagoya. It connects Shin-Osaka and Nagoya in about an hour, and the ride is comfortable and has amazing technology. I think it's great that there is one every 10 minutes, depending on the time of day, and most of them are full.
An amazing way to travel.  Very fast and efficient.  We used the luggage forwarding service but there was sufficient space between your seat and the one in front for you to place a suitcase.

It's not the only high speed train in the world and it doesn't run at full speed for a lot of the journey. Very expensive tickets and not good value.It doesn't help that the Shinkansen part of Tokyo station appears to be dilapidated, chaotic and disorganised.

I used it when traveling on the Tokaido Line from Akashi City, Hyogo Prefecture to Hiratsuka City, Kanagawa Prefecture. I was able to travel smoothly to Toyohashi using the Shinkansen, but I had planned to use the Shinkansen for this section from the beginning because it took a long time to get around Shizuoka Prefecture and I was getting physically tired. I think it's a good value as it's a section where you can make the most of the limited express fare of 2,480 yen. After getting off at Atami, I took the rapid train again to the east.

there's nothing wrong with traveling around Japan by shinkansen. The ticket prices are high, but everything can be solved by buying a JR Pass with us and then you ride and ride and don't buy anything, just make a reservation. The service is always perfect, the staff is nice, the seating is comfortable.

Loved our numerous travels on the Shinkansen while in Japan. JR Pass most valuable (also very useful for suburban JR trains in cities we went to {Tokyo, Kyoto and Osaka}). Take a smaller suitcase so you can pop it in the luggage racks above you. For longer trips, grab a Ekiben ("station bento") from your departing station and enjoy while travelling (note: these bento boxes are not to be heated up; eat them as the come; great value for money). If your planning a few days in Osaka and Kyoto, stay in one city only and travel to the other as you want; the trip via Shinkansen is only 13 minutes!!
This train is gorgeous and super fast! You have to admire the engineering of this thing. But don't let it fool you: this ride is expensive.

If you have not tried travelling by bullet trains, you must ride the Shinkansen when in Japan. Buy a JR pass for unlimited travel. You can buy a 7, 14 or 21 day pass. We bought a 7-day pass and travelled many times on the shinkansen, sometimes for joy rides. You can even book your seats. Sometimes, we just get off at some stations to watch the shinkansen trains speeding past. The trains run like clockwork and are so on time. Unbelievable!

Having had flight from Osaka cancelled due to typhoon Jebi we were re-routed from Narita.Quickest way to Tokyo is Shinkansen and is it quick. Difficult to judge speed whilst on train but if one goes through a station then you get an idea. And they will have slowed down a bit for safety reasons!Comfortable seats, trolley food service and an enjoyable, quick and comfortable journey.

When going from Tokyo Station to the Kansai area, I use the Shinkansen. There are many trains and the seats are comfortable. If you're boarding from Tokyo Station, there's a good chance you'll be able to sit in a non-reserved seat after a short wait. If you are departing from Tokyo, the seat with a view of Mt. Fuji will be on the right side in the direction of travel. If you are heading to Shin-Osaka, the train bound for Shin-Osaka is relatively less crowded than the one bound for Hakata or Hiroshima.

I traveled from Nagoya to Tokyo to see Mr.Children's live performance. I decided to go there three days ago and only had one day off from work, but thanks to the Shinkansen, I was able to go there and come back without any problems. Using the Shinkansen this time made me realize once again that the Shinkansen is an amazing vehicle that can truly enrich your daily life, allowing you to travel to Tokyo, Shizuoka, Nagoya, Kyoto, and Osaka as soon as you want to go.
bullet train, what else! superfast and efficient, drinks and snacks on sale also provided, super clean

My family and I (Wife, children aged 15, 13 and 10) We were traveling for two weeks through the main cities of Japan and it is definitely the best way to do it, the order, punctuality and quality of the service is incredible. The only complicated thing is at first understanding the signs in Japanese, but there are many people willing to help you at all times, even if they don't speak your language.

For foreigners, get a JR Pass and you can ride any Hikari, Kodama, and Sakura trains. If you take 2-3 rides during your trip in Japan, it would already be worth the price.The train is super clean, seats are comfortable, and you can even eat inside the train. You can reserve seats which I recommend, otherwise you can get on the non-reserved sections where it's free-for-all. You usually will get seats though.And the timeliness of the train service - I can't even explain it. The way the trains come and go at the exact minute it's supposed to EVERY SINGLE TIME is just almost literally unbelievable to me.It's so pleasant and so amazing that riding a shinkansen itself becomes one of the highlights of my trip when I'm in Japan.

Our JR Passes were just the best buy ever for travelling in Japan, we traveled by bullet trains (Shinkansen), local trains and some buses. The bullet trains re bang on time, fast comfortable and simply a joy to travel on. Remeber to buy your pass here and activate it when you arrive in Japan.

So incredibly easy to book JRail passes on line.  Received within a few days via offered Express Mail.  You only need to activate at JRail office (we used the one at Narita Airport before heading to our hotel).  Taking one trip on the Shinkansen Hakari from Tokyo to Kyoto paid for the cost of the pass.  You can use JRail throughout Tokyo on an unlimited basis for the time period that you choose to book.  We chose to go Green Class which would be equivalent to first class.  Train cars clean, spacious and comfortable.  As with all trains and subways in Japan they run exactly on time!  You can make your Shinkansen reservations in advance at any JRail office.  The employees at the office at the Shibuya Station were so incredibly helpful with all of our transit needs.
Walla,,,,, Shinkansen is really that Fast... Express from Tokaido to Tokyo. What a wonderful experience after a long day of visiting Mt. Fuji, Hakone and Lake Ashi.

I have often ridden the Shinkansen for a long time, and I am always impressed by how many trains run on the Tokaido Shinkansen. Outside of the busy season, you can often find seats in the non-reserved seats. (Of course I think it depends on the time of day...) The Shinkansen is a little exciting for both work and play. I was so impressed when I saw Mt. Fuji from the window!

I don't know where the Shinkansen I should board departs from at Shin-Osaka Station. The directions to the platform are hidden behind souvenir shops, which may be fine for those who are familiar with the area, but for someone like me who is new to Osaka, I have no choice but to get lost.

It connects Tokyo to Osaka in two and a half hours. Tickets can be purchased immediately from reserved seat ticket vending machines, and there are also non-reserved seats, which is very convenient. During the busy season, the Nozomi train runs once every three minutes.

If you have taken the time to visit Japan then do not short change yourselves, ride the Bullet train.  This is the smoothest train I have ever experienced! We went from Osaka to Tokyo and it was fast, can`t wait for the ground breaking here in America.   A must do while visiting, get the reserved seat if you are riding during peak periods, or walk to the higher numbered cars.

We have taken this train and after recently flying between OSAKA & TOKYO we have come to the conclusion that the Tokaido Shinkansen is THE ONLY way to go...its fast, clean, and very easy to navigate.There are plenty of signs in english and uniformed station masters readily available if needed for more info.
Taking the Shinkansen from Nagoya to Kyoto is very frequent and the entire journey only takes about 35 minutes. It is the fastest among all means of transportation, but it is also the most expensive.

Extremely efficient transport system! Very punctual, spacious seats, slightly reclining seat and very quiet. I was impressed by seeing the operator who bowed and said hello every time she passed through the carriage. The only discordant note on the Tokyo-Kyoto Hikari train journey was the very fast passage of the food and drink trolley. In practice the operator quickly went straight ahead 2 times without giving the possibility of taking anything.

A nice experience of my trip to Japan was the ride on the Shinkansen, the ticket booking went smoothly online and the delivery of my ticket to my hotel also went well, the Shinkansen is characterized by punctual departures and cleanliness, you will find very friendly and helpful staff at the train station and on the train.

With a JR Rail Pass, it's a perfect way to travel between all cities in a fast and efficient way at nearly 300 km/h. When purchasing a Green card, you are guaranteed a perfect seat in their first-class carriages. Priority when entering and exiting the trains and very friendly staff on the trains.

This is how to take the train on time. I took the Tokaido Shinkansen from Tokyo to Osaka. The time required for this is just under 3 hours. Great experience. With the “Ordinary Class” you have enough legroom.

For foreigners buy yourself a JR rail pass 7/14/21 day and make full use. Your JR pass must be bought prior to arrival in Japan and allows unlimited use of their trains and reservations for the Shinkansen. There are 2 Shinkansens you can't use, the Nozomi and 1 more shown on the pass. However, these trains are 10-15 minutes quicker over a 2-3 hour journey length, so causes no major travel delays.The trains are bang on time and if you stand at the carriage number on the platform your carriage door will be directly in front when it stops. The seats are wide and comfy with good leg room and a recline facility. We also notice that the whole row of seats can be turned through 180 degrees so if there are 4 people travelling together you can face each other. There is a food/drink cart that rolls through the carriage at regular intervals and people take their rubbish off the train so it is a very impressive way to travel.
fast travel, in great comfort and incredible order and courtesy. The only surprise was one section where if we did not reserve seats had to travel like in Mexico, piled up as we could

Tip: if you are traveling to Tokyo from Osaka, ask to have seats on the window side that would allow you to see Mount Fuji when booking your ticket.  Note Mount Fuji may not always be visible but when she is, it’s quite a sight as you approach Fuji station.  That said the Shinkansen was always a joy to travel and we never get tired of it.  If you are a foreign visitor to Japan, make sure you buy the JR Pass before arrival.  It will cover all your Shinkansen rides, all train rides operated by JR and even other perks (for example it covered our JR operate boat ride to Miyajima while in Hiroshima)
It may have a non-negligible price but it is absolutely worth it. I recommend anyone to try it once in their life to realize that efficiency, punctuality and cleanliness are not just dreams.

The Japanese had this figured out with high-speed rail way back in the day, and it still continues to amaze - the shinkansens are a great way to get across Japan, and are super comfortable despite moving so fast. Great service and cleanliness as well!

I usually fly to and from Osaka, but since I stopped by Kyoto on the way home, I took the Shinkansen for the first time in a while. Since I was leaving Kyoto early and wasn't in a hurry, I chose Kodama, but it was a mistake. The train stops at every station, and Nozomi and Hikari will pass you at every station. Even though I had plenty of time, it was quite stressful. Even though the price was about 4000 yen cheaper, I just regretted it. Nozomi and Hikari are comfortable, but Kodama is harsh, so this time I gave it a 3.

For most of the trips during my trip to Japan I used the Shinkansen, bullet trains. Exceptional: super clean and always super punctual. Very spacious seats, certainly better than an economy class plane. I recommend booking your seats at the ticket office at least the day before. The risk of standing is high...Tickets are quite expensive but, if you plan to travel a lot, the Japan Rail Pass is very useful which, in addition to being a great convenience, saves a lot.

JR is said to be accurate to the world's hourly schedule, but Shinkansen trains are often delayed. It can't be helped because we are traveling at high speed, but wind, rain, people, etc. cause delays. Electrical system problems are also common. Additionally, security is lax, so I often fly by plane.

We took this train to Tokyo and booked our tickets at Universal city ticket booth that took us all the way from Universal City to right next door to our hotel in Tokyo with one payment and one ticket. Outstanding view of Mt. Fuji on the LEFT side of the train so pick your seats wisely.

We bought admission tickets at Shin-Osaka Station to pick up foreign tourists and met them on the platform. Since the train is long, it is necessary to check the car number in advance. Admission tickets can only be purchased with cash, as credit cards cannot be used.

I was a little apprehensive when i went on the Bullet Train for the first time but it was great, you dont even feel like you are going really fast and it was a great experience, Its a great way to get around japan very quickly with no fuss. The have food carts that come through the train and also have a smoking room on certain carriages. I enjoyed the ride.

Super organized, clean, very punctual and safe, it is one of the most surprising things about Japan. Very good way to move around at your leisure in a comfortable and easy way, following the directions
When you're tired or crowded, we recommend the green seats. The seats are spacious and it's quiet. You can do it comfortably.
Fast, smooth and comfortable travel in one of Japan's public transport engineering stars.
A green car that I managed to get out of the Obon crowd. I was able to get to my destination in a quiet space where I didn't feel that the occupancy rate was 200%.
In my travels in Japan I have always used the JR pass to travel with the Shinkansen and I have always had a good time. Punctual, clean and reliable.
If you choose a reserved seat because you think it will be crowded, the non-reserved seats are often empty. difficult. It's helpful because there is almost no delay.

The Shinkansen is a nice way to travel in comfort. They do have food carts but the menu sells out of the Bento. be sure to get your food before entering the train. The elevator is around car 8 and takes you directly near the exit for Taxis.

it is beautiful, I love the ritual of the controllers WHO GREET THE CUSTOMERS AT THE ENTRANCE AND EXIT OF THE WAGON... in white gloves I love THE CLEANLINESS... no customers leave anything lying around, when leaving their place, we straighten the backrest... luxurious and perfect toilets!!!

We had the 7-day rail passes and travel extensively with the rail pass.  Plan ahead and reserve your seats to make the trip enjoyable.  Trains are always on time but luggage space are limited. If you have big luggage, that might be a problem

I bought the JRPass from the website in Buenos Aires and they sent me a document via FEDEX that I then had to present in Japan. The exchange was super simple. What's more, you can activate the pass for a few days later if you buy a 7-day pass and stay for 9 days, for example. The train from the airport to Tokyo does not cost more than 500 yen, so it is not advisable to use it on the first/last day just to go from the airport to the center if your stay is longer. There are 5 cars that do not need reserved seats and if you arrive 15 minutes early you should never have a problem, obviously if you can reserve much better. Trains from Tokyo to Osaka/Kyoto are on the same road, leaving every 30 minutes. Average speed 260Km per hour. The same experience inside it is similar to what one lives on a plane.

I use it frequently throughout the year for business trips, etc. Occasionally, I think about taking a flight, but flights are often canceled due to typhoons, snow, etc. On the other hand, Shinkansen trains are extremely punctual and are not affected by weather conditions.

On my way back from a business trip to Osaka, all the reserved seats were full, probably because it was Obon. I got into the green car at my own expense. Since when? The width of the seat, the seat, the spaciousness, the wet towel service (lol) After a long business trip, I sank my tired body into the comfortable seat, had lunch, read, and slept... It was a comfortable 2 and a half hour journey.

A vehicle that Japan is proud of to the world. That's the Shinkansen! It's quiet, doesn't shake, and moves at super high speed, leaving you from Osaka to Tokyo in no time! It's a little expensive, but if you think of it as buying time, it might be worth it.

We went from Tokyo to Osaka with this train at 0900 on August 1, 2018. The journey was 550 km. It took 2 hours and 30 minutes. Very nice seats. Comfortable seats are wide. They can rotate 360°. People are polite. Food and beverages are sold. We couldn't understand how the paid journey was. The conductor greets people at the entrance and exit. Of course, it's expensive. $125 one way. It was a good experience for us.

Well what can I say.  It's AWESOME.  So fast and smooth.  You will enjoy the ride.  Just sit back and enjoy.  Take a nap or look at the scenery.  Seats are comfortable.  You can buy food or bring your own.  Bathrooms are clean.  Staff is great.  Fun, safe, and FAST!Everyone going to Japan should at least try to ride a Shinkansen once.If your doing alot of travel and JR Railpass is great to get.  However you can just pay as you go.ENJOY!
The train is fast ( some of them like the Nozomi) but unfortunately they dont accept Japan Rail Pass.Confortable seats.

Top comfort, plenty of legroom, super clean and punctual. In just a few minutes, the train is checked after a journey and, where necessary, all seats are turned in the direction of travel. Incredible service. AND super fast.

The Nozomi train connects Tokyo and Shin-Osaka in two and a half hours, and it's very convenient, with trains running approximately every 10 minutes. However, it also seems to be shaking a little as the speed increases. The price is still high.

This review is specific to JR’s (Japan Railways) practices when it comes to returning lost or forgotten items. The rest of its services are beyond satisfactory but when it comes to getting one’s lost/forgotten luggage back they are terrible. If I could rate JR’s luggage return service “0” I would.On a recent trip from Osaka to Shizuoka Prefecture, I left a bag on a Nozomi Shinkansen when I transferred to a slower service Kodama Shinkansen that I needed to take to reach my destination. I realized my mistake quickly but not quickly enough to get the bag off the train before it departed. JR’s website had adequate information on who to call on their website and the bag was located before the Nozomi reached its next stop. Unfortunately, this is where JR’s quality service ends and its stupidity reaches an extreme.I informed the lost and found operator that I was bound for a station a few stops down the line from where the Nozomi would next stop. Could they please send the bag back down the line to that station so I could collect it there?No. No. They couldn’t do that. But I could go 3 hours and additional train fare out of my way to go to Tokyo to pick it up, or they could send it COD to my home in Osaka, or perhaps to my accommodations if I was going to be there long enough. Useless and unacceptable.Fortunately for me, a friend of mine who is joining me on this trip will be able to pick up the bag for me from the lost and found center at Tokyo Station on his way. Other travelers may not be so fortunate, and the solution to the problem is simple: put the bag on a train that is bound for the area the customer is in, and create a system for that lost luggage to be returned quickly. Even if there is a (reasonable) fee involved with having luggage returned, that’s a far happier outcome than leaving someone without their belongings.Fix it JR!

There are many trains like commuter trains. The inside of the car is comfortable with little shaking. (If you get on a local train after riding the Shinkansen, you will feel a lot of shaking.) Tickets can also be easily purchased and changed online, which is convenient.

Punctuality, comfort and safety!! It’s a real joy to travel by train!! NOTHING TO DO with us!!  Here the quality of service borders on excellence, despite record attendance! The train is clean, at each terminus a whole team is working to clean everything in record time, it's amazing to see!! The Japanese who come to France and take the train there must surely remain silent in front of our organization!!! The only problem is that this excellent quality of service of course has a cost and therefore the ticket prices are expensive. The story of my trip on isaroadbook

Every time I ride, I think how many trains run and how punctual they are. Depending on the car model, power outlets are located near the windows and in the front seats of each car. It would be even better if wifi could be used freely.

Travelled on many Shinkansens using a 7 day JR Rail pass which I ordered in the U.K. then validated the day before, in the JR Ticket Office, I started my travelling. A few tips:1. You will need your passports to validate your JR Rail Pass so make sure everyone has theirs handy.2. The queues in the JR Ticket Office can be rather large so I found going just before it closed at 8pm was ideal as it was empty.  3. There’s separate foreigner desks where excellent English is spoken.4. You can book all of your seats at once for upcoming journeys. As long as you know the dates you wish to travel then the JR Ticket Office will help you with the times.5. There was never any problems with booked seats being taken or indeed finding a seat in the unreserved cars.The Shinkansens are amazingly comfortable. If you can, buy a ticket for the Green Car as the seats are much bigger, there’s a huge amount of leg room and the seats recline much further back than standard class. Free WiFi is not common on the trains so make sure you have sorted out your entertainment before you get on. Most longer distance Shinkansens have either a food carriage or a trolley that comes around but most people brought their own snacks. That being said, I have travelled standard class and the seats are great but if you can stretch to the Green car then do!

I took the train from Osaka to Tokyo and it was so easy. A few things that I found it a little hard to find out in advance: these bullet trains depart around every 15-20 minutes, and you do not have to have a reserved seat. If you want to travel on the fly, you can.The first few cars are reserved seats (not necessarily fancier, just promises a seat) and the rest are unreserved. So you just go into an unreserved car and take a seat.The ride is around 2.5hrs and made travel super easy. It's clean, super quiet and it's odd to be walking around while going that fast.

Fast, comfortable, clean and on time train.  It’s ideal for getting around, you can reserve places or not for free. You will always travel with the seat in the same direction as the train thanks to the rotating benches. Very pleasant trip!
Very fast and very clean. Next time I will try again to ride here. It saves time. Booking is easy and staff are helpful.

You can hop on trains anytime without reservation. However, you may reserve your seat if you go to the counters in the station before you do. They normally have seats available for the next train. Toilets in the train. On one trip they sold food; probably depends on the time of the day. The seats have plenty of legroom and recline way back. I barely got any cell phone signals along the route. So plan your entertainment off-line. It was two and a half hours trip from Osaka to Tokyo.

The organisation is outstanding and the quality of every aspect is near perfect. The trains run on time, are clean, quiet and the trip is amazingly smooth. A true example for every other train service to aspire to.

This is the second time I've ridden a Shinkansen as an adult, and I was surprised at how comfortable it was because it had power outlets like a night bus, the seats in front of me were wide, the backrests could be folded down, and I was able to eat local food sold on the train! !
we use a jr pass so we are free to ride this shinkanshen, during golden week, the reserved seats are full, but if we take it from shin-osaka station, the train is empty so we can get a seat
One of my favorite ways to travel. We took the train from Odawara to Kyoto. Clean, quiet, so much leg space and you can turn the seat the other direction.
Speedy, quiet and  efficient train ride. Views of rice paddies, lotus farms. Better experience than catching the plane.
The fastest train in the world. It took us 14 minutes from Kyoto to Osaka. Comfortable seats. Enough place for luggage.

On the evening of the last day of the three-day weekend, I took a non-reserved seat on the Nozomi train from Shin-Osaka. Despite being the first train to depart from Shin-Osaka, it was a great success as the non-reserved seats were almost full. I felt that reserved seats were advantageous during busy periods.

Love the transit system in Japan, and this is the best way to get from city to city. I have used Tokaido shinkansen on numerous occasions. On this trip it was all last minute bookings and all done with Nagoya as my starting point. I found the JR staff amazing. On board, it is just a pleasure to sit and relax and watch the world go by (admittedly at this speed - a little bit of a blur). Please note if you travel on this train, no using the phone (from your seat) and talk with your travelling companions quietly. And the other great thing? Always on time.

Read heard how good and efficient the bullet trains are in Japan but having experienced the rides , just fantastic...Comfortable, very good service and awesome train stations .... Worth the money without a doubt!!!

First time we had the pleasure of taking the Bullet Train. Never been on such a fast Train and it was an experience. Just watching them speed by at the station while we waited for Our Train was awesome. When we got on Ours it was extreemely comfortable and very fast. Worth the experience.
I'm thankful that the latest Shinkansen trains have toilets with washlets. Recently, there has been a bit of security, and the conductor has been patrolling the train closely.
Took the Shinkansen, Green Class, (reserved business Class seating), very comfortable and quiet ride to Osaka. Quick journey and spot on time, cant really ask for more. Train was exceptionally clean.

This is a difficult experience to rate.  I purchased non-reserved tickets through Japanican.com at 22% discount.  For 3 of us the price was about $600.  I thought it was a good option because we weren't sure exactly the time we'd want to travel, plus the discount is appealing.  We went to the Shinagawa station and waited in line for the train at #3 car (non-reserved is cars 1 through 3). When the train arrived we were shocked to see that the cars were completely full, even standing room.  People were packed in and we couldn't even get standing room.  We went to the Japanican office to see about exchanging our tickets for reserved seats.  We were told that there would be a $300 penalty, plus the new tickets would be $900.  We decided to try the next train.  We were able to get on but again it was standing room only.  We each had about one square foot to stand in.  When anyone needed to use the restroom they had to squeeze past everyone & luggage.  Elderly were standing and younger people paid no attention to their plight.  People with families who had babies and young children who could easily hold the kids on their laps were taking up a seat for infants and their diaper bags.  In hindsight, we would have gone to the Tokyo main station for a better chance at getting a seat.  Then as though things weren't bad enough, a Monsoon delayed out trip by 90 minutes.  So a 2.5 hour trip became 4 hours - standing.  The babies began to fuss and cry.  No one made a move to help the elderly who were standing.  I am 71 and I'm reasonably physically fit, but come on folks ... where's the fabled Japanese courtesy to elders?  On the return trip to Tokyo we were able to find seats, although not together.  There were some who did not have seats because they were trying to fit families together.  The return was on time and comfortable.  So I'm rating my trip 3 of 5 because the trip to Kyoto was a 1 and the return was a 4.  I would never again buy non-reserved tickets.

The bullet train is the pride and joy of Japan. It is a clean, efficient, comfortable and relatively inexpensive place that links several of Japan's major cities. In my view if far preferable to flying within the country. The cars are very comfortable, you have time and opportunity to work, read or relax. The food and beverages served are of the highest quality, and the train crosses some of the most beautiful terrain in the country.

We bought the Shinkansen ticket from Osaka to Tokyo some days prior our travel date. The officer at the ticket office was helpful. Wanted to actually get the Green Car seat, but we forgot all about it when purchasing. The officer did not also mention about it, I guess it is because the distance is not so far, so they offered you the most economical one. We got our reserved seat, but turned out it was as great. The train was clean, toilet clean, the ride smooth. We loved it, the kids didn't even realise that we have reached Tokyo in 2.5 hrs.

When I tried to buy takoyaki inside Shin-Osaka Station, there was a sticker on the package that said, ``Please refrain from eating on the Shinkansen train or inside the station.'' When I asked JR Tokai, they said that they had taken into consideration the smell from surrounding customers. On the other hand, however, the Tokaido/Sanyo Shinkansen has several smoking rooms throughout the train, and smokers who have just finished smoking can spread the smell of cigarettes inside the train. Although the smell of takoyaki may be unpleasant, it is not harmful to the human body, but cigarette smoke, even exhaled smoke and third-hand smoke, definitely poses a health hazard. Shinkansen passengers are mostly healthy people who are not smokers, and public transportation must never expose children and pregnant women to second-hand smoke. It seems that the new trains that are currently being tested will also have smoking rooms, but if we are asking people to refrain from eating takoyaki in the cars, it would be more helpful for many passengers to remove the smoking rooms, which spread damage from second-hand smoke from smokers' exhalation and third-hand smoke from clothing, etc., to all cars and turn them into luggage storage areas. There are no smoking rooms on trains such as the Hokuriku Shinkansen and Tohoku Shinkansen, let alone airplanes. The Tokaido and Sanyo Shinkansen trains should also promptly remove smoking rooms inside the trains.

Every time on the Shinkansen is just another experience. It does really fast and always safe except for the recent mishaps. The leg room is always good and the inclining. Indeed the Bullet train is a great Japanese Delicacy

After enjoying Namba, I was planning to ride the Shinkansen at Shin-Osaka. In between trips, I tried Smart EX for the first time. It's amazing that you can get your own reserved seat. Furthermore, I was so anxious that I entered my credit card and pin number at the automatic discovery counter. After passing through the long line at the Midori no Madoguchi counter, I completed the procedure and was issued my ticket. I didn't think it would be this convenient.

I definitely prefer the Shinkansen to the airplane when traveling from Tokyo to the Kansai area.    I like places where you can see the scenery, such as tea plantations and the city.     It's a shame that there aren't many discounts, but on this trip I bought a ticket called "Plat Kodama" that comes with a drink. If you can do all these things, your trip will be even more enjoyable.

Riding the Shinkansen is an otherworldly experience. The frequency of trains, their punctuality, speed and reliability are remarkable. Everything is very clean and efficient. Note that some Shinkansen services (like Nozomi) cannot be used with a JR pass.
Always punctual at the second, comfortable but expensive. Usually cars 6 to 15i for reserved seats and  1 to 5 for non reserved.

Driving at high speeds of 285km/h every few minutes has reached the realm of miracles, and is hard to believe in foreign countries. In addition, the high level of skill of the staff has been proven through their response to incidents and accidents, albeit unfortunate ones. Unfortunately, perhaps due to the pursuit of efficiency, the new vehicles lack appeal. Who would notice that the N700S is a completely new model?
