It is often used for business trips and travel. Despite some unfortunate incidents, high-speed rail is safe. I usually have reserved seats, but I was able to use the points and use the green car to get to Kyoto, which was very comfortable.
Excellent train. Very fast. Maybe hard to find non reserved seat during peak hour especially for family

It is the best way to get around Japan, it saves time. The difference between the first class seats, reserved and non-reserved, is not much in terms of service. First class seats have a higher cost but the difference in comfort is not great. I only recommend the reserved ones if you are traveling as a family and want to be together, otherwise save the difference and go in the non-reserved ones. Same service same time
I love the Nozomi 700 series Shinkansen and ride it when going to Kansai or Nagoya. I love green cars.
There are two tragic accidents that come to mind. However, it is extremely convenient and affordable. It's the best means of transportation.
No matter how many times I ride the Shinkansen, I get excited. Safe and secure! I often use the route between Nagoya and Kyoto, but sometimes it's too early to drink coffee. It's a luxury problem.

Convenient to move from a city to another. We used it twice. Thought it would be more comfortable as we booked first class tickets, but it was the train itself that was not 100% stable as another we tried.

A lot has happened recently, but I feel that it is superior to other high-speed railways around the world in terms of the convenience of getting on board, the comfort inside the train, etc., and it is one of the symbolic technologies and services that Japan is proud of to the world. Due to its accessibility with other routes, and its time accuracy, I still prefer the Shinkansen to the plane.
Despite its problems, I still think it's the best means of transportation. Ekinaka in Shin-Osaka has become very fulfilling.

Tokaido Shinkansen between Osaka and Tokyo (vv) is an experience in itself. At approximately 300 km per hour you will zoom silently through the landscape of Honshu. The seats are comfortable and there is a dining car so you can stretch your legs along the way

We’ve long hoped for a chance to try the Shinkansen /Bullet Train and a few days in Kobe gave us the opportunity to book a day trip to Kyoto.Fast, efficient, steady as a rock, clean and comfortable- what more can we say?At top speed, if I had had a cup of coffee on the pull-down table in front of my seat, the coffee would hardly have rippled.It’s amazing that trains travelling at these speeds can run so close together – and always bang on time.Apparently some time ago, Japan Rail had to apologise to passengers because a train left the station 45 seconds early...... Where practical, I’d choose the bullet train, rather than flying, between cities in Japan.

The Shinkansen is impressive.  There is a high speed train between Tokyo and Osaka every ten minutes.  The ride is smooth and comfortable.  You can choose either a reserved seat or ride in one of three unreserved cars.

We had heard from other travellers how confusing the trains and stations were in Japan for non-Japanese speakers.  Couldn't have been more different - the stations are well signposted in English as well as Japanese and all the station staff we did speak to were able to understand us and were extremely helpful.  We took the Shinkansen from Osaka (Shin-Osaka station) to Kyoto and arrived in about 15mins, a couple of days later from Osaka to Hakone in about 2 hours.  The trains are spotless, and I'm a fan of the ritual bow the train conductor does on entering and leaving a carriage!  I'm not sure this would ever make it's way on to UK trains, but I'd love to see it :)  On the longer trip, a snack cart was pushed around containing beer, highballs, coffee, tea and snacks so no need to obtain snacks before hand.  We used the JR Railpass extensively in Japan and it is valid on the Shinkansen as well.

As a frequent train traveler in Germany and Europe, it was of course a must for me to try out the Japanese long-distance trains. You hear a lot and wonder whether it can all really be as perfect as other travelers' reports suggest, and: Yes, it can! Due to a previous weekend trip to the countryside, our trip took us from Odawara to Shin-Osaka, for which we treated ourselves to a seat in first class ("Green Car") on the Hikari. This type of train roughly corresponds to a "normal" ICE in Germany and, in addition to the large junction stations, also stops at selected smaller stations, while the Nozomi trains (that would then be the ICE Sprinter) only serve the junction stations and the Kodama trains go to all stations (which is what you experience in Germany, for example, in the early morning or late evening). This train takes less than two and a half hours for the almost 500 km long route and, apart from saver prices, Also slightly cheaper than the ICE in Germany. In addition to the counter, tickets can also be obtained from long-distance ticket machines (not to be confused with the purely local transport machines that are also available!), and while the user interface sometimes seems a bit complicated, here, in contrast to Germany, it is also possible to select the seats to be reserved from a seat map at the machine. At the respective terminus, the seats are all turned in the direction of travel by the staff, and each row of seats has a window, so that choosing a seat is much easier than in the European high-speed network. When you are ready to leave, you go through the platform barriers to the separate Shinkansen tracks (the entire Shinkansen network, with the exception of a few feeder routes, is completely separated from the rest of the train traffic) and can immediately find the stopping place on the corresponding displays on the platform Locate the doors of the respective reserved cars. Boarding and disembarking are generally extremely civilized (certainly a factor in the high punctuality of the trains), and within seconds you are sitting in your reserved seat. In first class, the cars are seated in a 2+2 configuration (compared to 3+2 in second class) and offer approximately the seating comfort of an older regional business class product on most airlines. The legroom is excellent and the seats can be reclined very far back by European standards. When the journey starts (on time to the second, of course), a service employee first appears, at least in first class, who checks off the passengers who have boarded based on their seats (this eliminates the need for further ticket checks on the train, the conductors finally know who is boarding where - Deutsche Bahn also recently introduced this, although this still requires the passenger to interact via the DB app) and Hand out a damp cloth. The fact that all staff bow when entering and leaving a car may seem a bit strange, but this also contributes to a certain feeling of calm - hecticness would simply not suit this gesture. Speaking of peace: although our car was half full, there was absolute silence except for the driving noises. Nobody was on the phone, nobody had loud conversations. However, during the journey you can feel that the trains are traveling faster than the original design speed of the route - in some curves you can feel clear centrifugal forces, but this is not necessarily a negative impact. Otherwise, the trains are equipped with urinals, toilets and separate sinks, and there are several smoking cabins available for smoking passengers - these are quite narrow, but excellently ventilated. Announcements are also made before arrival at each station, that you should now go to the doors to get out (again a factor that contributes to punctuality) and all other stops will also be announced. It is really amazing how perfect organization, high discipline on the part of both passengers and staff, and a sophisticated operating concept with relatively old (but proven) technology can achieve such an excellent result, even though the trains on this route, at 280 km/h, are rather slow in European comparison. My journey Odawara to Osaka was definitely the most relaxing train journey of my life, and I would definitely give it a sixth point for “significantly exceeded expectations”.
I used Plat Kodama from Hamamatsu to Nagoya. Plat Kodama can be a bit of a hassle to make reservations, but if you use it wisely, you can use the Shinkansen at a very reasonable price.
The Shinkansen trains are unprecedented and remains a great way to travel a long distance in short time, but still have time to work and relax. Service and punctuality is of course great

- Trains depart on the dot, do not confuse the train you are supposed to take and the train that is on the platform a few minutes before. Look at the destination and train number. - You can reserve seats for free with the JR Pass, otherwise just proceed to the unreserved cars- You can consume ekiben in the train (best ones are purchased in the station, there are also some sold via the JR staff push carts, which are not too bad as well)- Circle and triangle marks on the station platform means where the door will be for the particular train you will be taking, look at the board for the shapes and queue accordingly, such an attention to detail!

The Shinkansen is really convenient to reach your destination quickly, and the seats are better and clean. There is a charging plug under the window seat. It is convenient for foreign tourists to buy a JR pass. There are quite a lot of buses, so you don’t have to spend time waiting for the bus.

I often use it between Tokyo and Osaka. I save up airline miles, so I often use JAL, but it's expensive. There is a strange phenomenon where airplanes are cheaper if you buy them early. If it were a little cheaper, I could skip the plane and just use the Shinkansen, but that's a shame. However, it is very attractive that there is no need to worry about going to the airport or wait too long. At least the non-reserved seat will cost around 10,000 yen...
This is the best way to travel across Japan, always on time, easy to work out which train and line to use, great service and help at the main stations where you can book and map out your trip.
The train is so smooth you don't even know that you are moving until you look out the window ad notice that you are speeding along at near 300kph and it leaves all others for dead.

We traveled from Shinagawa to Shin-Osaka on the Nozomi N700 train and it continues to be our favorite way of traveling Japan.We bought our tickets from a reservation agent instead of the machine in order to make sure that all of our were seated together.  I tried to get us tickets on the right side of the train (in order to see Mt. Fuji) but unfortunately none were available.  Reserved seating was only slightly more than non-reserved so this was the better choice since we had to lug our baggage with us.  For those of you with JR Pass, the Nozomi trains are not included.Arriving at Shinagawa and getting to our track was easy.  Shinkansen trains left from their own area in Shinagawa station so all we had to do was watch the monitors for our train number and then head through the automated ticket gates to our track.  Signage everywhere helps navigating.Once on board, our small hand carries went on top of the luggage racks while our larger suitcases stayed on the floor in front of our knees.  Bulkhead seats gave extra room and we also leveraged the empty seat next to us.  If space was still an issue then one could bring their bag to the back of the train and place them behind the seats in the last row.  however, I prefer to keep them nearby.Train left on time and smoothly accelerated out of the station.  Within the hour we caught a glimpse of Mt Fuji and for a short while engaged most of the passengers in our car.  Being the Nozomi train, there were only a couple stops before we got to Shin-Osaka.  Time flew by as well as the scenery along the route.  Seats were comfortable, more than some airplanes, and reclined.We brought our own meals on the train but there was also a person who periodically pushes a food cart through the car that you can buy food and drinks.Arrival into Shin-Osaka was on time.  It was an orderly exit of the train and then walk to the main station.  We were also able to connect with the local JR train to the Osaka station where our hotel was with no additional charge.

I have been using the Tokaido Shinkansen for many years, but it was very moving to meet Dr. Yellow for the first time. The moment suddenly came at Tokyo Station, and I was greeted by a crowd of people cheering on the platform next to me. As I was looking to see what was going on, I saw that yellow gliding in from the direction of Osaka. Take out your camera and take a look at the photos. It was truly [Happy Doctor Yellow].
I used it to travel to Shin-Yokohama. The seats on the Nozomi train were much more comfortable than the old Hikari seats, and although there was some shaking, I was able to enjoy a relaxing ride.
It runs more frequently than the average subway, so it is very convenient. If you take the Nozomi train, you can reach Tokyo and Osaka in no time.
helped by Hyperdia traveling by train in Japan is incredibly simple; the shinkansen network is important; the trains are very clean, the toilets too!
I used it when going to Kyoto for business. It's very convenient as you can get to Kyoto in about 2 hours. On the way back, I bought some wine at the in-house store and headed back to Tokyo.

When I was going back to Osaka from Kyoto today, although I had a free pass to take the train back directly, but... I didn't... I chose the Shinkansen. I must be curious why I had to take the Shinkansen. Isn't this a waste of money? There is only one answer. I want to experience the Shinkansen, which is available in Taiwan. What is the experience? I am very grateful to God for giving me the curious idea to take the Shinkansen because there is only one stop, so I bought a free seat. It is indeed very similar to the Painwan High-speed Railway... but I think the comfort and smoothness are better than the Taiwan High-speed Railway. On the Shinkansen, you can't hear any noise, even from the salesmen carrying products. Different from Taiwan's High-speed Railway, the Shinkansen has smoking rooms, wash basins, and seats with plugs, which really surprised me! I really recommend that when you come to Japan, you must take the Shinkansen once and experience the different feelings that the Shinkansen gives you.

I usually use reserved seats, but this time I took the green seat. I went to Shin-Osaka on a weekday morning, and there weren't many people, it was quiet, and the seats were comfortable. I decided to take the green car next time I take the Shinkansen.

My family traveled to Japan and were utilizing the JR Pass to get around. We traveled from Tokyo to Shin Osaka, then onto Nagoya before going onto Mishima and returning to Shinagawa. Get to the stations early reserved your seats at the ticket office and then hunt down the best bento/snacks in the world in preparation for your journey. The kiosk trolley on board is great for beers and other snacks/icecreams etc.Love that there is a smoking room for passengers that way inclined.
Do not forget to get the JR pass before you leave for Japan. If it is in your budget than go for the first class to get reserved seating

I rode from Shin-Osaka station to Tokyo station. I bought a non-reserved ticket for a Saturday travel and it was just over 13,000yen. My train stopped at a few stations before Tokyo including Kyoto, Nagoya, Yokohama and Shinagawa and took 3 hours. As far as I am aware there is trains that stop at less stations so get to Tokyo faster which, despite being able to understand the Japanese on the information boards, I went on the higher stopping train just because it left 2 minutes earlier, so big mistake there.Shinkansen is world famous so it felt wonderful to experience it first hand, however for me the ride was comfortable as I could not find an area to store my suitcase so I had limited legroom.

You simply must take the Shinkansen (Bullet Train) while in Japan!  But be ready -- while the trains almost always run exactly on time, you only have about a minute to get on board.  Great for travel between cities, but be prepared to travel light and not with huge duffels or roller boards!

This is the smoothest, quietest high-speed train ride you'll ever take, and at 2 hours 15 minutes from Tokyo Station to Kyoto Station it's by far the fastest means of transit between these cities. Overhead luggage space is modest, but can accommodate suitcases the size of airline carry-on bags. If you must take a large standard suitcase on board, there is a limited amount of floor space behind the last row of seats at the back end of the car. (This is space that allows them to pivot the seats to face in the opposite direction when the train reaches the end of a run.) If you intend to reserve seats on the Fujiyama side of the train, you would be advised to reserve them a couple of days in advance. We found that almost all the window seats on that side of the train were reserved 24 hours out from a mid-week, midday trip.

I used the "Kodama" train when traveling from Odawara Station to Nagoya Station. The speed was relatively slow as it was a stop at each stop. Thanks to this, I was able to enjoy the scenery outside. it was good! I used it around 9am on a weekday, and the car was empty and comfortable.
Namely the bullet train. Connecting the Shinkansen lines connecting Tokyo, Kyoto, Nagoya and Osaka, it is the first choice for traveling between Tokyo and Osaka. The drive takes just over two hours.

I LOVE how punctual it is. It's really clean despite allowing people to eat on the train. The toilets are clean as well and there is no smell even though there are smoking areas between cabins. It's super quiet too!

Initially, I didn't plan to take this super fast train considering the high price tag. But in the end I was tempted to try the short route, namely Osaka-Kyoto. The journey only takes 15 minutes with a ticket price of 1280 yen (around 180 thousand rupiah) for the non-reserved seat class. The train we used was Nozomi which doesn't stop at many stations. Even though it's short, the trip is quite enjoyable. The train is clean, comfortable and without vibrations even at high speeds. I've ridden the Shanghai-Beijing bullet train. In terms of quality, to be honest, there's not much difference. But what's wrong with trying out this famous Japanese technology? Hopefully one day a train like this will be available in my country. The only drawback of taking this train is that it is confusing when entering the platform at the station because there are so many platform doors with unclear instructions.

The Japan Rail Pass is fantastic, the staff is very attentive, with their assistance and good disposition they allowed me to tour and schedule the cities to visit and reserve the trains of my choice. I recommend the green class to travel comfortably, and buy the Suica card for the metro, buses and other lines.

Shinkansen is also convenient between Tokyo and Osaka. It takes about two and a half hours, and in some cases it can be faster by plane. The interior of the train is comfortable even in the standard seats. You can see Mt. Fuji and Lake Hamana from the train window. The prices sold on the train are high, but the nuts and cheese sweets are said to be popular. Although IC cards are now used for conventional lines, there are also cards specifically for the Tokaido Shinkansen, which are cheaper than buying them in general. However, there is an annual fee and it takes time for the card to arrive.
We took the Shinkansen from Osaka to Kyoto back and forth and it only took us less than 15 minutes to arrive at each place
It's no surprise that the name is bullet train, they are really very fast and as everything in Japan works with excellent punctuality, despite the price being a little high, it is very worth it.

Fantastic experience. I took it from Osaka to Hiroshima and it was a very peaceful journey. It only took 85 min, which is impressive.The train itself was clean and there was plenty of legroom.I did not reserve a seat but that was not a problem. There are many seats from carriages 1-3 (for non-reserved seats) so you do not need to worry about forking out a premium. To be honest, I felt as if the other carriages were more crowded than the non-reserved ones! Just try to avoid peak hours, though.

The Shinkansen (Shinkansen) is something Japan can be proud of as it is rarely late for anything (^^♪ The train runs between Shin-Osaka and Tokyo in no time. When the weather is nice, you can even enjoy Mt. Fuji.

Super fast train, super clean and super on time! (also because for us Italians having a train on time is a miracle). In just over 3 hours he made the Tokyo - Osaka route and we didn't hear any noise! plus the staff inside the train is very friendly!

I rode this train without my son unfortunately as he would have absolutely loved it. Clean, smooth and fast. Interestingly even though it was faster than trains in Europe or the U.S. it was hard to tell as it is so smooth. Depending on your plans a day pass was more economical but it was a little tough to figure that out at the ticket counter.

Day tour from Tokyo to Kyoto by Shinkansen was fantastic. We paid for first class because it was Golden Week and we knew nothing about the Tokyo Rail system. We were met at our specified meeting spot, escorted to and given a quick commentary and tour of Tokyo Central Station and put on Shinkansen. We were met in Kyoto and commenced our Kyoto after a lovely lunch in a first class hotel near station.First class travel was luxurious. Tour of Kyoto on the busiest day of year great as tour company was brilliant. We visited three shrines and temples Then escorted back to Kyoto Station in time for return trip. We were met again at Tokyo Station and put in a taxi to hotel. Day trip was expensive, especially first class, but so,so worth the experience of the fast train combined with no worry travel.
The Smart Express, which I use between Shin-Osaka ↔ Nagoya ↔ Tokyo, is very convenient. I also like that there is a 7-Eleven at the exit of the Shin-Osaka Station ticket gate. ‼

I used the Tokaido Shinkansen for the first time in a while. The in-vehicle ticket inspection system has finally been abolished, and the service, which had received a bad reputation, seems to have improved somewhat.
I used to ride from Tokyo to Osaka, but now Gifu Hashima is my limit. I don't like the continuous lateral movement. Today and beyond, we will be using a plane.

If the Tokaido Shinkansen suddenly disappeared from Japan, the country would be thrown into chaos. It is impossible for planes and other means of transportation to transport all the people who need to travel through the world-class metropolitan areas of Osaka, Nagoya, and Tokyo. Not only is it fast, but it's also incredibly comfortable to ride. The express fee is a little high, but...

Lots of leg room and very clean. The announcements are clear, both in spoken and the display (Japanese, Mandarin and English). Storage is a problem, as you have to lift your suitcase to store it above your head. Difficult to do when you're short and not strong enough lift your suitcase. We found it strange that for a bullet train, it makes so many stops between Osaka and Tokyo! You can purchase food and drinks on the car, but it more expensive than if you purchase your itmes on the station platform.

As I learnt that you can only buy shinkansen tickets in Japan, that was what I did after I landed in Haneda Airport International Terminal. I bought the tickets at the tourist counter in Haneda Airport.  The ticket from Kyoto to Tokyo cost ¥14110 per person reserved seat.  I was a bit nervous to buy ticket just 7 days before as it was the start of Golden Week.  But all went well.The train was on time (to the dot) and arrived on the dot too.  Clean and comfortable.Travel in May 2018.

A very fast and cheap means of transportation. There is nothing like this when traveling by express between Tokyo and Osaka. I recommend making a reservation online. Please refer to the internet for timetables.
It is now an indispensable means of transportation that connects Tokyo and Osaka. Nozomi is really fast. I wish it were a little cheaper.
I often use it when traveling from Yokohama to Kansai (Kyoto, Nara, Osaka, Kobe). It's very convenient. In particular, the Nozomi train arrives quickly and is very helpful.

I've been travelling through different areas of Japan, with a great service provided by JR.Since 2015 and six times to Japan, I've used the Shinkansen trains, to get me around various parts of Japan.When you get up to the ticket booth and you have your destination, as to where you want to go, the person at the ticket desk can help you.  Maybe a language barrier but between the both of you's, you get it figured out.  They have some staff that are pretty good in understanding English.They'll explain to you once you get your ticket, as to where to go, what time, and platform.  FYI.  The trains are leaving on time.  As to what it says on your ticket.  So make sure you're at your platform, before that time.The train itself is amazing to see when it rolls in.  Once you enter you put your small carry-on luggage above your seat, then sit and relax, to enjoy the ride.The seats are quite comfortable.  If you ask for a Green Car ticket, at the ticket booth, then the train cars are at certain spots on the platform, for where you wait, and the seating is a little wider/ more leg room. But it will cost you more.Make sure to have your ticket at the ready, in case the train conductor wants to see your ticket, for confirmation.  The trains are spotless.  The service of cleanliness is great.  They have stewardess that will come to you, when you first get on, and hand you a warm towel to wipe your hands.  They will also come by now and then, to see if you would like something to drink or eat.  And later on, to see if you have any garbage you'd like to dispose of.I have so much to say but I find it hard, to really put into words.They have the best service, for a train company, that I've ever experienced in my life.I always look forward, when I'm in Japan, and I have to use the Shinkansen.Because the level of service and comfort are just awesome.Keep up the great work JR and thank you.

Excellent and fast way to move between different cities. The best way to save time, and save money if you buy the Japon-rail and get the most out of it between the bullet trains and the subways of the respective cities you visit. For example, we took this train from Kyoto to Osaka and it only took 15 minutes!
An ideal option to get from one city to another. And relatively inexpensive. The carriages are perfectly clean, there is a toilet, and they serve snacks and drinks. Very fast and comfortable.

Ride Hikari/Kodama at Odawara → Shin-Osaka, Kyoto → Odawara. Driving on time is a given, but driving on time. The inside of the train is quiet and comfortable with about 60% occupancy. China's high-speed railways, which the Shinkansen is compared to, now depart on time. The occupancy rate is almost 100%, making it very noisy. It's just extremely cheap. If we keep thinking that Japan is the best, we are worried that our sales overseas will not go well.

I often travel to Osaka for business trips and often use the Shinkansen. A few years ago, there were renovations and the number of stores increased, so for example, I used to go to Kyoto to buy Yojiya's oil blotting paper, but now that there is a store, it's much more convenient.

We booked the Shinkansen Nozomi at Osaka station but had to go to Tokyo to catch it as it the the closest station. It only cost approximately $300 AUD for reserved seats for two people and not using the JR Pass. It is still possible to get onto the Bullet Train if you book it in advance as when we went it was full.  It was very comfortable as the seats were similar to airline seats which you could recline and enjoy a nap. There is some room for luggage if you sit at the back and there is room behind the seats for at least 3 bags. We departed Tokyo to go to Osaka but the closest station was Shinosaka the terminal but did not mind as wanted to experience the Bullet Train.  It went close to 300km/h and it was quite smooth with no bumps so you could fall asleep. If you were sitting on the right hand side could see Mt.Fuji and still take a photo but you had to be quick.
In just two and a half hours from Tokyo to Osaka, the Shikanzen literally slings you from one city to another. Better than the plane, even if the cost is quite high.

Well I need to visit Osaka when I was in Tokyo, an choose to use the Shinkansen, using a JR Rail Pass, the staff at JR Rail are great even when dealing with a none Japanese speaker. If you need to travel around Japan use the Shinkansen, for comfort and speed.

Although you have to transfer to the Kyoto Line or subway line to get to and from the city in Shin-Osaka, the station and platform are large, and you can shop inside the station before getting on the train. The lights at the station are sufficient, the toilets are clean, and there is everything you need to eat. However, Shinkansen tickets are very expensive, and many people would rather take the bus or plane. However, the Shinkansen has frequent flights, is not far from the city center, and is about the same speed as a plane. It takes 2 and a half hours to get to Tokyo. The seats are also comfortable, so you can have a good sleep.
The train has an old finish. It doesn't smell good inside. Small and wobbly table. No service offered and for wireless you need to get a subscription before leaving.

The Tokaido Shinkansen / Sanyo Shinkansen service between Tokyo and Hiroshima. I travelled between Shinkobe and Tokyo. Shinkansen services include the super express Nozomi, the Hikari. The travel time was roughly 2.5 hours for around 550 kilometers. The top speed reached was around 290 kmph.The journey is comfortable. The seating arrangements include reserved and non reserved with designated cars. The pricing is dependent on this. The onboard facilities include designated smoking zones, toilets as well as additional paid food services.Operations are spot on to the clock with absolutely no delays at all ( normal cases ). Advance reservations are possible in addition to reservations on day of journey.The route is Tokyo , Shinagawa, ShinYokohama, Nagoya, Kyoto, Shin Osaka, Shinkobe, Himeji , Okayama, Hiroshima.

Shin-Osaka to Tokyo in just 2 hours 57 minutes. Comfortable rides, and you can see Mt Fuji if you sit on DE’s seating. If you use JR Pass, don’t forget to reserve your seats at the counter. Bring your bento before departure.
Transportation osaka to tokyo and the train is comfortable but the ticket price little bit expensive.
SAmazing bullet train experience.  From the gleaming new Osaka Railroad station to Tokyo in under 2 /12 hours at 200 miles per hour.  Awesome.

We lose our bearings as a TGV traveler a little in the Nozomi (the name of the fastest train): single fare (and rather high because the Central JR company receives no public subsidy and provides an incredibly dense service), very fast ticket vending machine, very high frequency of trains (up to 10 per hour), no reservation necessary, seats in the direction of travel, perfectly well-kept Japanese staff (no pierced and tattooed conductors there), corners closed smokers, flawless punctuality, top cleanliness, ample legroom even in normal class, numerous power outlets, light catering service available on the train, spacious cabin, slightly dated decor (a surprise), "show" from the cleaning teams on arrival, etc. We are following in the footsteps of the historic Tokaido of 1964! Please note: the ticket includes a metro journey from the arrival station.

Took the Shinkansen from Tokyo to Kyoto and it was smooth and quiet.  There was plenty of room for suitcases. Plenty of leg room and you can recline your seat to take a nap. I fell asleep along with my partner and  we didn't wake up from a bumpy ride.
Nice journey with minimum inconvenience, good facilities and smooth journey. High speed noise proof, comfortable seats

I use it when going to Tokyo. If there is no one sitting next to you or someone is asleep, you can relax by eating your lunch or reading a book, but otherwise the space is small and you will feel cramped. Three hours alone is a long time to get to Tokyo.

On May 9, 2018, I took Nozomi No. 10 from Nagoya Station 1112. Both the window and aisle seats are full. The middle of the third row of seats was empty. There are no standing passengers. As always, the ride is comfortable and you can travel to Tokyo in about 1 hour and 40 minutes.

We got a 7 day JR Rail Green pass, which is the equivalent of first class - an excellent move - the pass and the train system were brilliant. The best way to get around Japan and see all that the wonderful country has to offer.

What a transport system. Trains run exactly on time, They are clean, no graffiti in Japan, and have seats as good as business class on a plane. There is food via a staffed trolley making the rounds with snacks. Only downside is luggage area is very small and you may have to send it via a truck to your next destination if you area a family.  Book a seat as its safer
Barely any legroom left if you have a large luggage. Fast transportation and best way to travel long distances in a short period of time.

No need to take first class (green) you will have access and plenty of room for your legs during your journey. On the other hand, during busy periods I recommend that you reserve your seats in advance (it's free with the jr pass), but this is often not necessary (be careful to get into the unreserved carriages in this case). The Shinkansen are very frequent so don't worry if you miss one. On this line we note the presence of Mount Fuji on your right going towards Osaka and on your left in the other direction. Really very polite and helpful staff.

We got a JR pass when we arrived in Japan and used the bullet train on a number of occasions to visit places like Osaka and Hiroshima.  Definitely the way to travel.The trains are always on time and immaculately clean. The seats are comfortable and there are luggage racks all the way along the carriage.  There are toilets and dedicated smoking rooms on the train.Whilst they are fast, you don't get the feeling of speed during the trip.  However watch on go by at high speed and you realise just how quick they are.A great way to travel and something you must experience in Japan.
I rode this line from Hiroshima to Shin-Osaka and the saved was well worth the fare. Most of the time these trains are covered on a Japan Rail Pass.

Among the various means of transportation available to travel between Tokyo and Osaka, the Shinkansen is considered the fastest and most comfortable. Taking into account various troublesome aspects such as travel time to the airport and security screening, Shinkansen can be said to be the fastest and most comfortable means of transportation. In fact, it boasts a very comfortable and fast speed, befitting the image given by the name Shinkansen. Compared to Korea's KTX, the space between the front and back seats is very generous, which I like. However, considering that the price is quite expensive, I have no choice but to use the JR Pass.
It was really fun to try the fast train from Tokyo to Osaka. The facilities are sophisticated and adequate and also very clean.

I used Hikari from Odawara to Shin-Osaka. By 8 o'clock on the first day of Golden Week, the place was full. However, there was plenty of legroom and the Shinkansen was a very stable and safe train. It was a pity that I didn't meet him and couldn't buy ice cream, probably because the in-car sales were asleep, or maybe because I went to the restroom. The toilet was quite crowded.

After travelling maglevs in China - we'd expected higher speed - but relatively "slow". Still - a very smooth comfortable ride. Excellent leg room and good space for luggage. Seat configuration not ideal - 2 seats one side of the aisle - 3 on the other - but the train wasn't full so easy enough to move around once we were on our way. Runs exactly to timetable - which is wonderful
certainly the most useful and comfortable means of transport to visit Japan, however choose the route with fewer stops, otherwise a two-hour journey can become a 4-hour journey. (happened personally)

Loved this train!.  Fast! Spacious and clean.  We had all the room for our luggage we wanted and it even came with a way to lock it if your seat isn’t by your bags.  The stops are pretty quick though so make sure you are ready to get off.

Last day of May 6th. You can reserve your seat at any time, including the green, which is fully booked all day long. I was prepared to wait an hour for the first train in Shin-Osaka, but I chose the Shinkansen 3 trains later and was seated safely. I rode around 9:00 to reduce the risk, but there were plenty of free rides.

I used it to travel from Odawara Station to Shin-Osaka in April. It's been a long time since I've transferred between Kodama and Hikari. I had accumulated EX card points so I upgraded to green. The seats were wide and I had a quiet and comfortable journey.

We too the Shinkansen from Kobe to Kyoto and back while our cruise ship was in port. It was amazing how smooth and fast the ride was. Getting tickets and boarding were also very easy too. Very convenient travel.

There is only something to learn from Japan regarding travel by rail. Speed, punctuality, cleanliness, friendliness. I have never been so enthusiastic about a means of getting around. Really fantastic.

This is an extraordinary travel experience. So fast yet doesn't seem it it until you look at time and distance. Effortless and relaxing to travel from Tokyo to Osaka. See lots of countryside without noticing the speed of the Shinkansen until you pass something up up close. Then, it's breathtaking and exciting and extraordinary. Buy your ticket outside Japan to save significant money on these trains. Try not to carry too much luggage with you as there's not a lot of space for it on board, though you will be able to manage with more just not easily.

Because this thing is just awesome!Only for the Japanese train saluting-culture on the platforms and in the traincabins it's worth trying this masterpiece of science. This invention makes the train finally a comfortable way of transportation, especially when you compare it to the inferior, smelly and cramped Dutch trains and our ridiculously failing attempt of making a high-speed train connection. Back home the difference is just bordering to medieval. Unbelievable that Japan just decide to make this thing work in their hilly and rough landscape with an average speed around 280 km/h. If there was a pooltable on board you can play without noticing you're in motion. It's just superb.

It had been on my husband's bucket list and so glad we ticked it off!Don't let Tokyo Station intimidate you, the majority of the signage is in English as well as Japanese and the staff more than happy to assist.Although it's not cheap (we paid 52,000 yen) for a return journey from Tokyo to Kyoto it was well worth it. The trains run every 10 mins so don't worry if you see big queues on the platform. You never have to wait long for the next one! The queues are orderly (like everywhere in Japan). The seat in in the carriages are all forward facing, they are turned by the staff before adjourned. There is lots of legroom and the overhead racks are quite spacious too.Only down thing is the windows are like airplanes not that big. The scenery is fantastic and depending on you route, and the weather you get great views of My. Fuji. The staff on board are great.So pleased we done it.

I'm a member of the Zipangu Club, so I can't use the Nozomi, but there are two trains per hour on the Hikari train, so I always use it from Shin-Yokohama to Kyoto and Shin-Osaka.This time, it was relatively empty on Friday morning in Shin-Yokohama and Saturday night in Shin-Osaka.

Shinkansen trains run on time. Of course, natural disasters (heavy rain, typhoons) are impossible. This is a recommended vehicle if you want to travel long distances throughout Japan. Food and drinks can be brought in. You can purchase it at the station. If you forget to buy one, there are on-board sales. Please purchase tickets from vending machines or at the counter. Of course, you can also make advance reservations. It takes about 2 hours and 30 minutes from Tokyo to Shin-Osaka (Osaka). On a clear day, you can see Japan's highest mountain, Mt. Fuji, around Shin-Fuji Station.
I took this train from Tokyo to Kyoto and this is the best way to go.  It takes about 3.5 hours and is roomy, nice and quite.  Much better than an airplane ride.
Punctuality, no fault in 40 years. Charming staff, clean trains, smoking rooms, clean toilets. The seats face the direction of travel. Lots of space and the seats are comfortable. An example.

Who is not fascinated by trains from childhood days? I dare say it would be every child's dream to one day be able to travel in one of the famed Japanese bullet trains. We got two such opportunities in the recent tour of Japan. This leg between Osaka city to Tokyo (we got off in shinagawa station), was the best as it covered the approximately 450 kms in 2 hours 30 minutes. On the last day of our conducted tour the whole day program was a boring bus travel from Osaka to Tokyo for 8 to 9 hour with frequent breaks. So the wisest thing to do was a break from the main group, catch a early morning Shinkansen to Tokyo which gave us the entire day for sight seeing all the places we had missed earlier!What a fantastic  journey it turned out to be!  We bought the tickets a few minutes before boarding the train and entire process was so swift and efficient. 18 of us travelled and took the tickets at 7.15 am and the fast Nozumi express was slated to leave at 7.20 am and gave us a few butterfly moments as we knew that the time on the clock may slow down or be erratic but the train would stop for none and leave at the exact minute, no make it second! Spotless cleanliness , hardly any discernible movement of the carriage , extra ordinarily well behaved japanese travellers, one of whom had forgotten to put his phone on silent mode and profusely apologised to co travellers before heading to the place between carriages to answer the call. The toilets were better than what one would see in good airlines and completely contactless operations. Suffice to say i have never travelled near about 500 kms in what ever mode of transport including air ( and I have travelled a far bit), with so less fatigue and more comfort! While a lot of people including me were critical of Indian Govt bringing in the shinkansen to India, i for one have now changed my opinion after travelling in it!

Travelling on the Shinkansen is a must for any visitor to Japan. It is an enjoyable, comfortable, and easy way to get between the big cities. A Japan Rail Pass is a must if you’ll be using the Shinkansen - they’re easy to order from your travel agent or by using JTB’s website in your country (if available) - saves a lot of money (can be used on other JR rail services as well - including the NXT from Narita airport to Tokyo), and it’s easy to book seats (go to a service centre or booking centre and just say where you want to go and what dates - unlimited travel for as long as your pass is valid!)Make sure you also buy a ekiben from the station so that you can enjoy a meal while smoothly speeding through Japan. There are carts that go through the train during the journey, but it’s so easy to stock up on drinks, snacks, and a meal before even arriving at the platform.

Although it is called the "Tokaido Shinkansen," it can be considered separately between the inside of Shin-Osaka Station and the area outside the ticket gate. The area inside the ticket gate is Tokai, and the area outside the ticket gate and conventional lines are operated by JR West. The same goes for Kyushu. The area inside the Hakata station ticket gate is JR West, and the area outside the ticket gate is JR Kyushu. So, for Shinkansen, Tokai is the main area, and West, East, and Kyushu are not the main areas. Tokai's head office is in Nagoya, and it holds the most cash in Shinkansen management.

What a fabulous experience! Took the Nozomi service from Tokyo Station to Shin-Osaka station.As someone who frequently experiences the horror of UK rail operators this was a stark reminder as to how rail travel should be. The train was spotlessly clean inside, including the toilets (an area that only the brave would venture into on a UK train...), smooth comfortable and very quiet. It goes with out saying that the train was perfectly on time.Buying the ticket was a simple process, l bought mine a couple of days before travelling from one of the machines at Tokyo Station. The machine had an English translation and it was easy to select the right ticket.Tip is to pick up a bento box lunch at the station before boarding the train, l picked up one from Ekibenya Matsuri and it was delicious.
Not suitable for sleeping. It's a boring time without family. Don't expect food. Let's buy it. But it's very comfortable to sit on.

Some trips for travelers. The station announcements and displays alternate between Japanese and English (also see Mandarin and Korean).  The express versions of the train (Nozomi) run approximately every 5 minutes in each direction.  You have to be ready.  The trains are 16 carriages long and their positions are marked on the platform and there are platform doors which open only when the train arrives. There is just 2 minutes for any passengers to alight and new ones to board. I traveled between Kyoto and Nagoya (146km in 35 minutes). The scenery was unremarkable and the journey over too soon. The high speed surcharge nearly doubles the price. There are less frequent and less fast versions (also using Shinkansen) that might give you more time to settle in.

To go from Tokyo to Tottori, I took Nozomi from Tokyo Station to Himeji Station. I was able to sit down because it was the first station. There is no entry procedure like on an airplane, so it is convenient to board immediately.

certainly an interesting experience. And not for the elegance or the design, these were not the objectives of the designers, but for the punctuality (incredible), for the practicality of the interiors, the courtesy of the traveling staff (the lady with the drinks trolley who bows, greets and thanks the passengers out loud), the organization in the stations (in 4 minutes of the clock the compartments are cleaned at each terminus!!). An unforgiving comparison with the FFSS

It was the best experience ever in my life. It is so easy to get anywhere with the JR. On some bullet trains, JR pass doesnt work but the people who work at the JR ticket office will find you an alternative so you dont have to pay anything extra if yoy hold a JR pass. Also, if you can afford, Green pass is far better than economy class. Its worth spending extra as the comfort is better than a business class of a plane
Depending on your seat, you can conveniently charge your smartphone on the Shinkansen. There was on-board sales (lunch boxes, drinks, etc.). Express booking was available.

First of all, foreign visitors can no longer purchase concession tickets in Japan. If you want to buy a Japan Rail ticket to incorporate the Shinkansen, you must purchase it from your home country. We had to pay full fare for our tickets as the rules changed only recently and websites have not been updated. Secondly, there is no where to store your luggage. If you are travelling first class (and it is worth it), book the last seats in the carriage as you can store your luggage behind the seats. Otherwise, you will struggle to find somewhere to put your suitcases while you are seated in your carriage. There are no trolleys nor porters so be aware that you will have to transport your own luggage through the station to your train. However, once you board, the train is comfortable and relaxing. It is not called the bullet train for nothing for it literally flies on the tracks and in just over two hours, you arrive in Osaka. Bring your own food and drinks for the amenities trolley has very limited selection and the coffee is disgusting. Highly recommended and just as fast as flying and definitely more fun!

Excellent can't fault the service. If you are taking the Shinkansen for the first remember to keep some time in your hand as you have to navigate through two barriers . Very helpful English speaking staff . You will never get lost

Not a first for me on the Shinkansen. But as always, a great experience. The train comes in time and makes it on time. The comport on board the train is perfect. Great reclining seats with power outlets.The only down side is there is no Wifi on board.Even thought its an expensive means of transportation in Japan. Its a great one and i highly recommend using it.

Punctuality is the key word. Service, Customer satisfaction oriented. The trains are at the platform 30' before departure, time for employees to change the headrest protectors and clean the seats and wagons. The seats are returned to the direction of travel. Suitcases can be padlocked in dedicated lockers. We're not going to the moon with it yet, but I'm totally satisfied with it to go to Kyoto.

I traveled between Hiroshima and Nagoya, Hikari between Nagoya and Odawara, and Kodama and all Tokaido Shinkansen trains between Odawara and Tokyo. I've only used Nozomi so far, but Nozomi has a smoking room, so it's a great means of transportation for smokers. I wasn't expecting it, but the Hikari is an N700 series train that has a smoking room like the Nozomi, and the Kodama train is also an N700 series train that allows smoking. Both the smoking room and the smoking vehicle were clean. Thank you to JR Tokai for being considerate to smokers!

As an Australia tourist I purchased a Japan rail pass as I was doing a far amount of travelling around Japan. The pass is great value for money and is a great and easy way to move around the country, especially if travelling to Kyoto, Osaka or Fukuoka! The bullet trains are very clean, have plenty of space, generous reclining seats and onboard snack and drink options!

I took the Kodama train from Shinagawa Station to Atami Station on Sunday around 7pm. I was able to sit down, but there were only a few empty seats. Even on the Kodama train, I found it difficult to get two seats next to each other from Shinagawa Station.

Ask for seat E (which is a window seat on the right side of the train) when making a reservation for the shinkansen from Tokyo to Kyoto to get a spectacular view of Mount Fuji. Also don't forget to buy a bento box at department store Daimaru (at Yaesu exit, Tokyo station) to enjoy while you taking in the view.

This is a great way to travel from Tokyo to Kyoto and back. It was really as smooth and effecient as I expected. I enjoyed watching the staff prepare the train before I got on. I queued, as one does, and watched a small army of cleaning ladies get on, clean rapidly and turn the chairs to face the new direction of travel. What wonderful Japanese efficiency. The journey is very smooth and you can watch Japan fly by. I had hoped to see Mount Fuji as the train passes close by, but the weather was too cloudy and I didn't. However, that was the only disappointment on an otherwise flawless journey. Oh, and it left and arrived precisely on time.

The bullet train is an absolute must when in Japan and it would be criminal not to go on it at least once. Last time I had the green card for first class and this time travelled second class and cannot say it was worse. There is loads of leg room, the delightful trolley lady comes around selling coffe and snacks and of course the punctuality of this train puts the train service in every other country to shame. To be on the safe side one should reserve seats but these trains travel very frequently so if you have not reserved and the train is full you hop onto the next one. They are an absolute eye catcher with their stream lined noses. One cannot go onto the platform to admire a Shinkansen as one needs a valid train ticket to enter the 'hallowed' platforms. This JR  Pass, as mentioned by other travellers,  must be purchased before one comes to Japan as it cannot be bought there.

What a ride!!  A trip to Japan was always a dream for us. There are a lot of sites to see and the people here are extremely cordial. A ride on the bullet train was never on our bucket list. (It should have been!) what an experience!!  Fast and smooth......that’s all I have to say about that!!  Make sure you are up-to-date with everything you need to do beforehand as far as rail goes. Planning our trip ahead of time helped us immensely. Good luck and safe travels!!

The Shinkansen, known outside Japan as the Bullet Train, is the world's best rail service. The Bullet Train runs on time, literally to the second. The train is very comfortable. The Osaka-Kyoto line has a train every 15 minutes, if you miss one train, get the next. Be sure to get your Japan Rail Pass before you go to Japan, you can't buy it once you have arrived. The Japan Rail Pass can be used on most railways, including most suburban railways and subway systems. The Japan Rail Pass is very convenient and it will save you a lot of money. The Shinkansen goes almost everywhere, it's very fast and very convenient. By the way, Shinkansen in Japanese means "main trunk line."

Riding the Shinkansen was a dream come true for me in Tokyo. Absolutely amazing was my journey from Tokyo - Odawara - Tokyo. This is the best ride if you have very little time , else u can do the Tokyo - Kyoto & visit Mt. Fuji with a day to spare - will do it next time.

If your travels call for it, enjoy the Shinkansen in Japan.  We booked “Green” car tickets and didn’t regret having wider, fewer seats in a row and far less crowds.  Quiet and smooth, it turned into a great, relaxing experience.  The real excitement was watching other Shinkansen flash through a station while awaiting our train.  Plenty of overhead space for even the largest of bagsBring your favorite snacks and drinks and sit back and enjoy the ride

After purchasing your ticket (get in line as they speak English and are very helpful), walk through the turnstile's and up the escalator to the platform.  Line up for your car and enter when allowed.  Some cars have room on  the ends for luggage but they are not designed for large bags.  The trip is fast and very comfortable.

I rode a Kodama for the first time in a while, and luckily it was a 700 series! Kodama has many non-reserved seats, but unlike the N700 series, there is no smoking room, and the only non-reserved smoking car is car No. 15. It's crowded, but if you sit in a non-smoking car, you won't be affected by second-hand smoke and can spend your time comfortably.

One of our bucket list items to tick off was to go on the Bullet train.OMG, this was just amazing. It is so smooth, and of course, so fast. The seats are comfortable and the scenery gorgeous.We even saw Mt Fuji!I do recommend a trip on this train if you can do it!
8 Shinkansen rides, eight times on time to the second. Very fast and feels like it runs every 5 minutes. No comparison to DB.

I booked my ticket from the JR Tourist Information at Shinjuku station, but you can either buy tickets on vending machines or book your JR pass (this need to be bought prior your Japan trip, since it is just for foreigners).In my case my ticket also covered the cost to get to Tokyo Station, where the train leaves. At Tokyo station just follow the signs for the Tokaido Line (blue bullet train sign).Before you pass make sure to get some snacks of Bento Box (traditional box with japanese food).There are cars that does not require reservation and when I went early in the morning there was a lot of spaces, but be mindful that if you take the train in busy times or along the way it might be good idea to get a reserved seat - (from Kyoto to Tokyo even the cars with reserved seats were full).Tip: To have a great view of Mount Fuji in a clear day make sure to seat at E seat (both direction - between Nagoya and Shin-Yokohama- since they turn the seats around in the end of line)Tip 2: If you have a reserved seat and want to get a train during the same day but at a different time, just go to JR Rail Customer Service. The attendant changed my reservation for an earlier train. Just to make sure that the time of the departure of original ticket is not past.They sell drinks and light snack in the train but they are not very cheap.

I'm not referring to luxury, but to functionality, in terms of speed, punctuality, courtesy, cleanliness and much more. In Italy we don't even know what a service like this means, because we've never seen it. It's a smart way to travel around Japan. Since the prices are high, I suggest the Japan Rail Pass.
For tourists, get a JRPass and board the shinkasen trains as per your will (depending upon the route and class ofcourse). They are fast and timely by seconds.

The downside to the Shinkansen, which is fast and comfortable, is that there aren't many discount tickets. For example, if you're flying between Tokyo and Osaka, early bird discounts are cheaper. This time, it was a short distance trip: Kyoto-Nagoya and Nagoya-Hamamatsu. I searched to see if there were any discount tickets and found JR Tokai's Plat Kodama. The fares above are 20-30% cheaper than usual. It also included tickets for drinks such as beer. Since it's a "Kodama", I don't think it's good for long distances, but I think it's good for short distances.

Traveling by bullet train is the most efficient way to cover multiple cities in Japan. Tokaido lines connect Tokyo, Kyoto and Osaka which is one of the most frequented tourist spots. The trains run at 250-300Km/hr but there is no vibrations or shaking felt inside the carriage. The trains are clean and always on time. JR pass is ideal to have if you are a tourist.

I have traveled over many countries using a train, in Canada, US, India, Thailand, Taiwan, Australia, New Zealand and European countries.However, nowadays, I have never experienced to hear the announcementto guide a smoking room or booth in a train.It might work as promoting a smoking during his train trip until a passenger arrives at the destination.In 2018, about 50 countries, including the above-mentioned countries, prohibit smoking inside of the train. It will put our people in Japan shamed at the coming 2020 Olympic game. When I was on the Shinkansen platform at Kyoto JR Station, which is the representative of Japan's old capital railway station, I heard a loud announce voice echoing in the ears just before the train entering to the station; Smoking rooms are located at the Car3, Car7, Car15 for regular vehicles, and Car10 for a Green Car.This action would cause discomfort for travelers from overseas! Such an excessive support of smoking behavior leads Japan as a country preferential to a smoker, and it counters the positive impression of Kyoto. A smoking booth which brings a health hazard to tourists should be abandoned. We plan to use Tokaido Shinkansen in the next April, although we definitely select seats in the vehicle 5, because it is relatively far from smoking rooms.
36 minutes from Nagoya to Kyoto. I can't even drink coffee slowly. JR Tokai's commercial, X'mas Express, is here from platform 16 of Nagoya Station.

It was a memorable experience. We took the green car on the Nozumi (fastest bullet train) from Shinagawa to Kyoto and booked the seats on Mount Fuji side. All staff were pleasant and it's worth going on. In the green car the seats can be turned around so if there were 4 of you you can face each other for the journey.

We took the bullet train from Shinagawa to Odawara. It was a great experience, the speed was really obvious when another train passed in the opposite direction. We bought our bullet train tickets at Shinjuku station, and took a local train to Shinagawa. Rail staff said we did not need a further ticket for the local train. Well, when we attempted to join the bullet train at Shinagawa, a loud and officious rail officer demanded to see our tickets for the local train. Fortunately, an older officer saw that we were not intending to rip-off Japan Rail, and let us through the gate. Be sure you obtain all the necessary tickets!We returned from Odawara direct to Shinjuku by slow train, which took three times longer.
Travelled from tokyo to kyoto. It really is an experience of a lifetime. Super comfy seats. The best part is to watch the velocity of the landscape moving.

This train system is amazing (depending of course where you come from!) The whole system for boarding is easy and very efficient.  Don't be late for it though, as you will miss it - they are on time to the second.  Signposting easy, once you get the hang of it, as it is also in English and colour coded. Fantastic.  Very comfortable seats.  Quick journeys.Even if you are not going anywhere in particular, try this bullet!

I used it to go to Nagoya Station. Since the train departs from Tokyo Station, you can sit in non-reserved seats unless it's a busy season. We also sell wagons, so you don't have to worry about drinks.

we used the rail system extensively during our trip. the "bullet train" is great, comfortable and like all other Japanese system, a model of cleanliness, order and courtesy.  My only caution is, there are some segments where there is the option of reserved seats TAKE THEM, otherwise you may find yourself, like we did, standing in a packed NYC metro car

We had a very bad experience in the shinkansen.The persons in the offices of the railway station don't speak a single Word of english.One of them did not understand the word «tomorrow» when we asked for the day of the booking of our tickets. The person fainted To understand and took tickets for one day before what we asked.The next day, we realized that our tickets were planned on the wrong date.We had To pay another ticket and we have lost almost 10000 yen... And nobody could (wanted) To help us and  To refund what we had to pay as extra charge for a mistake caused by a person who did not understand english. So the Shinkansen when we went to the JR station it was are last day so we got our tickets and got on the train.So then the train took off we were headed to Tokyo I was exited so on it there's the Green car which is like for first class so my dad took me to see the Green car.What we saw we saw foot resters but you couldn't put your chair all the way back like airplane first class economy is like well just like economy plane chairs.So ya that's what the Shinkansen is like.

Tokaido Shinkansen is the main fast train line in Japan, as it is the one that passes through the main cities of that country (Tokyo, Yokohama, Nagoya, Kyoto and Osaka). Nothing to say, punctual, fast, safe, and extremely comfortable trains to travel. The tickets are not cheap, so if you plan to make several trips, it is advisable to buy the Japan Rail Pass.

Because the Tokaido Shinkansen is used by many business travelers, regular ticket prices are higher than other means of transportation. It's fine for business trips where the expenses are low, but when I use it for private purposes such as traveling, I make good use of discount tickets. Express Hayatoku and Plat Kodama are also good options, and if you use JR Tokai Tours, there are round trip Kodama plans from Tokyo to Osaka that include a hotel for just over 20,000 yen. Even if you use it, it will be more expensive than LCC or express buses, but the cost performance will be better.

This route is often used for business and travel. After all, it runs as frequently as a commuter train, so it's very easy to use. I love flying, so I often fly between Tokyo and Osaka, but of course this is more convenient. The seat pitch is long, so you can put slightly large luggage in front of you, and I like the small details.

It has been a long held dream to travel on Shinkansen (Bullet train) and to see Mt Fuji on the journey. I finally realised that dream on a day trip from Tokyo to Shizuoka. It was an incredible experience and did not disappoint in any way. I purchased a return ticket at Tokyo Station (for a very reasonable $144 AUD) at around 8.00am for a train leaving in about an hour. They are very regular! The person at the counter was incredibly helpful and cheerful, arranging my tickets and giving me directions to the correct platform. Tokyo Station at that time of day is incredibly crowded and being so vast, can be confusing in the rush of the crowds, so the advice was much appreciated. Along the way I checked with a couple of staff who continued to point me in the right direction. The train left and arrived exactly on time. You can charge your phone at your seat, whilst you smoothly cruise past spectacular scenery, including the amazing Mt Fuji. There is a screen in every car (as well as announcements) with advice on upcoming stations - in both Japanese and English. An absolutely brilliant day trip! I'll be travelling on them a lot more often on my next, longer, trip to Japan.

If you want to visit Japan and you are going to travel through several cities, it is essential that you use the bullet train. It is very comfortable, quiet, the seats are very spacious and they also have plugs to recharge any device. You use very little time to move between cities. They are very punctual.

amazing transport always on time efficient and heads up UK you always get a seat. I used this transport to travel from Tokyo to Shizuoka. very impressed of the cleanliness and the timing of the trains. The speed is also amazing smooth and quiet very relaxing .

I travel all over Japan for work. For some reason, since the latter half of 2017, I have had to go to Shizuoka Prefecture for a lot of business, so I take the Nozomi from western Japan to Nagoya, and from Nagoya, I change to Kodama and go to the nearest station. During the snowy season, I often drive slowly around Sekigahara, so I thought I would have a hard time this year with the sudden cold and heavy snow, but surprisingly everything has always gone smoothly. I think it's the most reliable railway in the world.

I used Shinkansen several occasions last year for business travel. The frequency of the trains, timekeeping is simply impressive. With cleanliness and comfort of the travel makes it almost the best in the world. I would say, compared to other bullet trains the tickets are not that expensive. It's really an experience
The recent snow has caused some delays, and a while back there have been some cracks in the bogies, but it is still one of Japan's major highways.

I like reading books on the Shinkansen. When I thought about why I was able to calm down and concentrate, I realized that it's because I almost never stop. The route from Nagoya to Shin-Yokohama is especially long and easy to concentrate on. It's comfortable.

I'm just in awe!!  Smooth, quiet, fast and precise.  As a passenger, you will need to be equally precise: buy tickets in advance, arrive early, and find your platform. Keep your luggage organized and ready. Don't misplace your tickets! These trains are NEVER late, and only stay at each station briefly, so you must get on and get off quickly.  Most stations feature convenience stores with remarkably fresh, tasty and economical meals-to-go that you can take on the train. The seats are roomy, comfortable and clean (I wish I could have said the same about my Air Canada flight!). We saved by booking the train travel with hotels in a package deal.

How envious: punctuality, cleanliness, comfort. What is certainly appreciated is punctuality. A means of transport that allows you to reach Kyoto, Osaka, Hiroshima, Tokyo and other locations in a more than adequate time. Certainly our "Red Arrow" has also improved the service in our country but if we think that the fast train service has been running for many years!   in the sixties, high speed already existed. Furthermore, with Doctor yellow the railway network is checked every night. Congratulations!

The long journey felt very short by using this train. very comfortable clean, the food is also tasty and also very on time. if you are a little late will definitely miss. thats why the Japanese people are very fast way because they do not want to be late

I travelled from Hakodate to Ueno, Tokyo on the 1 Jan 2018 on Hayabusa Shinkansen, the standard carriage was clean and train was very fast. However I had one of worst service experience when I board the train. We travelled as family of 4 with 3 small cabin size and 1 large size bag, as the large size bag could not fit the overhead storage therefore I went to ask the staff for help, the time was around 5 mins before 1836pm Hayabusa 38 train took off. The younger girl could not speak or understand English and seek for help from an older lady staff. However the older lady could not speak much English too therefore I use my broken Japanese to indicated that I have a large bag need storage. She then shout No.1 and point to front carriage with very unhappy face. It was usual for Japanese to behalf this rude by pointing and shouting at customer, however I did not have much time to spare hence I ran to carriage 1 with the bag and later found out each carriage do have its own large storage. Japan is well known for its customer service and I had been to Japan few time but first time on shinkansen. Maybe just bad luck I guess.

The 25m x 16-car train is 400m long and runs at a maximum speed of 285km/h, so watching Nozomi pass by at places like Shin-Fuji is very impressive and is highly recommended. It has 16 cars with 1,332 seats, and has a maximum of 10 Nozomi, 2 Hikari, and 2 Kodama trains running on a regular schedule, making it extremely convenient. It is the world's strongest high-speed mass transit operation. Before I knew it, I had achieved faster speeds, and it took 2 hours and 22 minutes from Tokyo to Shin-Osaka, from 1 hour and 49 minutes from Shin-Yokohama to Kyoto, and about 2 hours from Kyoto to Mishima on the Hikari, so I always use the Shinkansen. If you register for EX reservations, you can not only make last-minute reservation changes from your smartphone, but you can also save up points and ride in a green car at the regular fare. On the other hand, when I returned home on January 3, 2014, my train was stopped for a long time due to a fire near Shinbashi, so I wasted half a day in the waiting room and was unable to attend my family's New Year's party. At a time when it would have been possible to cancel the service or turn around at a station along the way (in this case, Shinagawa), I feel that there was a lack of effort in stopping the train for half a day on the entire section to Shin-Osaka (although there is also a problem with the wiring, where only the middle 2 line can be used as a turnaround line on the Tokyo side). There is no increase or decrease in the number of trains depending on the number of passengers, and all trains, including the quiet Kodama during the day, have 16 cars and 1,332 seats, which can be understood as a measure aimed at businessmen, but it is cold and uninteresting. I sincerely hope that they will appeal to families and inbound tourists with more ``spaciousness'' and ``playfulness.'' Things like increasing the utilization rate of Kodama by having a car with a playroom exclusively for children, using half the rooms as a convenience store, introducing 2-2 rows for the reserved seats on Hikari, which has a lot of inbound passengers, and creating a luggage space similar to that of the Narita Express (the net rack is certainly large, but heavy luggage won't go up), a reservation system that assumes access from overseas, etc. I would like them to aim for a more attractive Shinkansen.

In comparison to its US counterparts, this high speed rail system is light years ahead. The trains run on time. They are immaculately clean. The ride is so smooth you can barely feel it moving. There are food and drinks served on board. We were most impressed.

It really is difficult to articulate just how impressive the Shinkansen network is. It puts the UK’s poor excuse of a rail network firmly in the dark ages. They are comfortable, fast, punctual and look amazing. We purchased a 14 Japanese Rail Pass for around £310. It was worth every penny and more. We traveled from Osaka to Nagasaki. Nagasaki to Hiroshima. Hiroshima to Tokyo. Tokyo to Mt Koya. Mt Koya to Kyoto, and then lastly to the airport. Most of the time we had three seats each to ourselves as we sped across the country. The Shinkansen Stations are very easy to navigate with all the signs in both Japanese and English. If in doubt the J.R. Staff are never far away to assist with any enquiries. You can pre book seats but we never bothered and we always had plenty of seats to choose from. It really is the way to travel. Our pass allowed us on the Shinkansen that travel up to 175mph. We did however go on the wrong train once, 199mph and where only told which trains to use in future to avoid any unnecessary surcharge. I haven’t calculated how many miles we traveled using these trains but it was many. So, get yourself a J.R. pass and see Japan.... it’s an amazing country.

We opt to travel by rail rather than by air from Tokyo to Osaka. It was a pleasant experience. Fast, clean, convenient are the words to describe our transportation to Shin Osaka. We purchased our one way ticket (at the JR office on the arrival floor of The Hanada Airport) at the same time we purchased the Suica Card (for mass transit on most major transit lines). It was a tad more than traveling by air.  However, talk about the convenience...a few stops away traveling on the Yamanote Green Line from our hotel in Shibuya to Tokyo Main Station, we boarded our Shinkansen train at the same Tokyo station. In a few hours we arrived in Shin Osaka where we boarded the local metro line toNambda Station where our hotel was.  Before boarding the Shinkansen, we were able to purchase bento boxes to eat on the train from many vendors and markets at the Tokyo Station.  What an experience!

So I didn't have the slightest idea that when you ride in  a bullet train you should also have the quick speed of a bullet.😂 We were all hyped up and ecstatic with our first shinkansen ride (the route would be Tokyo-Nagoya).After 2 speedy hours there was a vague, almost inaudible announcement that we are nearing  our destination. Of course we did not get up right away to get our luggage from the back compartment thinking just like a regular train there is enough time to do it. Little did I know that we have only 2 minutes to unload everything. So obviously enough we were not able to get off the platform in Nagoya and went all the way to Kyoto. Such a waste of time. From there we want back our track but this time we arranged all our luggage near the door and when the door opens, we literally throw everything out and faster than the speeding bullet whisk ourselves out the door.That being said we did not attempted to ride another shinkansen again. With the luggage we had in tow we're better off with a bus ride😆😆

The seating is comfortable. The distance to the front seat is far, so 1 small suitcase can be placed at the footrest and still be spacious. Chairs in a row of three. There is an electric socket for cellphones. Toilets are clean and spacious. Buying tickets is also easy and the operating schedule is 15 minutes apart. So there's no need to be afraid of being full.

As many have already written here, this is a relatively inexpensive and quick option to get from one city to another and at the same time, as noted here, feel like you’re on an airplane... -yes, I completely agree with these statements, but with reservations! – About them below!) These trains are divided into 3 categories, for example, I’ll write a time list for a trip from Tokyo to Kyoto (as it is especially popular, judging by the reviews) –1) -2h 11min – “Nozomi” - 4 trains per hour approximately 2) - 2h 36 min – “Hikari” - 4 trains per hour approximately 3) -3h – “Kodama” - these run 1 time per hour approximately In addition, as has also been written a lot, there is a division into “with reservation” (with a seat) and “without” (you can take any free one) - the division occurs “per carriage” - 1, 2, 3 - “without”, starting from the 4th - “with reservation”! The “notorious” JR Pass, which many here praise, is valid only for carriages “without reservation” and only for trains “Hikari” and “Kodami”... Accordingly, if you want to provide yourself with a “place”, you will have to pay extra!!! It’s clear that “without a reservation” costs a little less, and in fact I just want to save money, but!.. - for example, I went on December 29. and was in a hurry, so I took “without...” and honestly, I regretted it!!! - I don’t know why no one has written about this yet, but December 29 – “all of Japan” wants to get from Tokyo to Kyoto, so there are basically no empty seats in cars 1,2,3!!! And you begin to realize this as you approach the platform - there are quite a lot of people waiting for the next train in the hope of getting on, I repeat - “getting on” and not “sit on an empty seat”!!!)))... - ... I was going to Nozomi, which makes very few stops (fortunately!) and after about 1 hour 42 minutes it stops in Nagoya, where again “fortunately” a lot of people get off and so on. there is a chance for the “quick” to get the coveted “seat”!) – Believe me, after 1 hour and 42 minutes of standing, you begin to practically dream about it, spurred on by the fact that the ticket costs about 8 thousand rubles. with pennies!))) - There was a desire to return to Tokyo on January 3., and having been worried about the trip while standing and not “for not being expensive”, it was decided to buy a ticket “with a seat” in advance at the box office, “on line” tickets, by the way, are not sold at Shinkansen! (... So, what was my surprise when, having arrived at the box office on January 2.01., I received approximately the following answer from the cashier: “...Tickets with reserved seats have run out, eat without... - will you take it?...” - Another 8 rubles “for standing” and “moral” preparation in the form of an evening visit to bars to do this!)))... ...3.01. in the morning, “pretending to be a blonde,” I go back to the box office, just like in the advertisement: - “...What?!, - what if?...” - maybe the treasured tickets with “seats” appeared - in response to a pointed question at the box office, an unequivocal “sentence” was received: “There are NO tickets for today!” - Apparently my face “gave itself away somehow,” so the cashier added: “Go to the central office, maybe.” they will sell…”-…As is probably already clear from the above, 40 min. standing (to Nagoya)!!!, then “cheerfully jumping” to an empty seat (believe me, there are not many of the latter!) and now “happiness” - to Tokyo “sitting”!))) P.S. ...I saw that they write that: “...snacks and coffee are delivered to the carriages...” - this is, of course, true, but it only applies to carriages from the 4th onwards and does not in any way apply to carriages 1,2,3 “without seats”, at least not on dates associated with N.G. !!!
