The Shinkansen can take you quickly to Nagoya, Kyoto, Osaka, and beyond. Nozomi leaves about every 10 minutes and is very convenient (*^^*) I always take a seat by the window where you can see Mt. Fuji and enjoy the view (*≧∀≦*)

We took the Tokaido Shinkansen from Tokyo to Kyoto. It was spacious, comfortable, clean, fast and convenient. Overhead racks can fit up to a medium sized luggage. However, those with larger luggage on the train may have to either store it at their seat area or behind the last row of seats (where by it cannot obstruct chairs from reclining). This train does not have luggage racks for those with larger luggage unlike the much newer Hokuriku Shinkansen.
I traveled from Shizuoka to Nagoya and from Nagoya to Tokyo. It was on December 31st and New Year's Day, so we weren't sharing a table, so I was so relaxed that I fell asleep 〇
green car freserved seat, more expensive but for sure worth the money.spacy seat and legsspace.hardly chance on delay.

We booked a 7 day JR pass for our trip as we were travelling on the Shinkansen from Tokyo to Kyoto, Kyoto to Osaka, Osaka to Tokyo, with stop overs at each location to explore and discover.  Having the JR pass made our travel so much easier (and cheaper).  Although we had to line up for about 40 minutes to exchange our voucher at Haneda airport (if you have young children, find a comfy spot up at one of the cafes/eateries while someone lines up because they could be a while).Our JR Pass was a well used item both for the Shinkansen and also local JR lines.As for the Shinkansen itself, it was comfortable, efficient and clean.We pre-booked our seats from the JR office at the station the day we traveled which made traveling easier.We’d also pick up snacks or bento boxes from the train stations before we got on the train. It’s cheaper than the snack cart that comes around.The only trouble we had was that we lined up at the wrong car as the train was going in the opposite direction. This just meant we walked through 5 cars before we got to our seats.  Our luggage (including a stroller) fit nicely up in the racks above the seats.  Our tip here if you have luggage would be that rather than going straight to your seat, step aside into the section where to toilets are so that other passengers can find their seats.  Then make your way to your seat as the train gets moving and put your luggage up on the rack.  That was you’re not holding everyone else up in the aisle.The seats are spacious and recline nicely.  There’s a power point at the foot of the wall in each row to charge your devices if needed.The Shinkansen is absolutely a great way to travel.  And the JR Pass allows you to use multiple local trains at each location.  Definitely worth the investment.If your not from Japan you have to pre-purchase your JR pass before you enter the country.  A quick google will help you find multiple places to get one.   We found the cheapest price through Flight Centre Australia (who in turn purchased it from JTB.  But we paid less to Flight Centre than the JTB charge from their own website.  So do some research before you book.)  Top Tips:- prebook seats on the day you travel- get your food from the train station konbini stores (ie: 7 eleven, Lawson’s etc)- work out exactly where your car will be located. A station crew will help you.- put your luggage in the racks

We travelled from Australia to Japan and were unsure how easy it would be to use the Shinkansen Bullet Trains.It couldn't be easier, with the tickets waiting at our Hotel as planned and easy signage in English at the stations.Staff and locals were very helpful and approachable whilst we waited at the station for the train to arrive.All carriages are numbered, as is the platform, so easy to board.There is a secure space at thee end of each carriage big enough for two large suitcases, that lock into position as the train moves off.a fresh face towel was given to each traveler as we left the station, by a stewardess.overall an amazing experience, should not be missed if you get the chance.

I needed to travel from Osaka to Nagoya in a limited amount of time, so I had no choice but to use it. I chose a seat in the middle of car No. 12, farthest from the smoking room, so I didn't have to worry about exhaled smoke and it was empty, so I was comfortable. When we arrived at Nagoya, there was chaos inside the station, but surprisingly, the Nozomi trolley a few trains earlier had been damaged and nearly 1,000 passengers were being transferred. I shudder to think if I was on board. There is also a question mark about safety, and as long as there is a smoking room, you cannot use it with confidence.

I must say travelling on the high speed Shinkansen was something that can only be described as unbelievable. The speed and smoothness of the ride is amazing. Some 300Km plus an hour and you can't appreciate how fast you are traveling until you look down and out the window and the ground is a blur. Easily purchased tickets, you can do so at both the ticket counter or the self service machines. 13000¥ for Tokyo to Kyoto per person. Children under 6 free. Tokyo station is huge and has many different entrances to the trains however we were easily helped when asking questions. We purchased un reserved seats and scrambled aboard. 4 adult 2 children. Grabbed 2 rows of 3 seats stacked the luggage up top and away we went. Highly recommend a trip on the Shinkansen when visiting Japan.

We rode the tran back into town after an excursion to Mt. Fuji.  As we waited at our stop, a couple of express trains blew through the station.  Even taking a video of the experience doesn't capture how fast they move.Once we boarded I couldn't get over how smooth the ride was and how quiet it was.  I wished we'd been riding during daylight hours so I could get a better feel for how fast we were moving.This was definitely worth the extra money we paid to return this way rather than the motorcoach!

We took the Shinkansen Nozomi on two occasions. Both trains were exceptionally clean, quiet, there were clear announcements in English & we reached our destinations very quickly. The N700 sounded like we were on a plane & we could feel the speed.1. Tokyo to Kyoto via the Shinkansen Nozomi 29This departed from Platform 18, Tokyo Station at 1130 & arrived at Platform 13 Kyoto Station at 1348 – a total of 138 mins (2hrs 18 mins) to cover 513.6 kms.2. Kyoto to Hakata (Fukuoka) via the Shinkansen Nozomi 7This departed from Platform 13, Kyoto Station at 0913 & arrived at Platform 13 Hakata Station at 1158 – a total of 165 mins (2 hrs 45 mins) to cover 661.3 kms.Using the Hyperdia website we had worked out prior to leaving home which trains we intended to book, & did this at the JR Ticket Office at Narita.Even though this was the most expensive train option, it was more convenient than going through an airport & it was a more pleasant journey.

I stayed in Japan for 1 week and I bought the JR pass for 7 days, best desition ever! The JR in general is expensive, the friends traveling with me that did not buy the ticket ended up paying much more.  I went to Kyoto and Osaka, in Tokyo I always move in the JR which is easy to find! 100% Recommended. There is Free Wifi in all the stationas and in some trains.

In 2016, I rode Nozomi for a trip to Kansai. In November 2017, I took the Hikari train to go to Nagoya. In December 2017, I was going to Hakone, so I rode the Kodama. There is often information on the internet that says, ``Nozomi is crowded, but Hikari and Kodama are empty.'' Is that true? Last month, I rode the Hikari train that departs from Tokyo at 9:33. It was certainly crowded when we left Tokyo, but the number of passengers increased as we continued on to Shinagawa and Shin-Yokohama. Then, at Odawara, the conductor announced that so many people had boarded the train that not only the non-reserved seats but also the reserved seats and green cars were full. This day is a weekday. It turns out that contrary to rumors, Hikari is crowded on some days. On the other hand, when I rode the Kodama this month, it was pretty crowded both ways. Even though I had a non-reserved seat, I didn't feel like I was sharing a seat with anyone else. The progress is slow, but if you want a leisurely ride, Kodama is recommended.

Never regret buying the JR pass a few hours before leaving Melbourne. Have read thru in detail and was recommended by friends never go to Japan with out the JR pass.The exchange order or the passenger coupon has to be validated upon arrival at the airport  or your first point of using the JR pass, ideally at the JR exchange office ( At Narita airport Terminal  2-3 ). The train from Narita airport  to Tokyo & back is the JR NEX train with limited stops an hour each way.There is a space to store your luggage in each of the carriages and all ways book your seats prior to traveling.Its an amazing experience boarding the bullet train @ 320 K plus  Shkinkasen  Hikari  from Tokyo to Osaka in 2.45 hours each way and Tokyo to Kyoto in 2.5 hours each way. The JR entry & exit is via the service gate JR pass  is always good for extensive traveling in Japan. Inner city travelling in any city is mostly raging form Australian $1-5  each way in the most when you criss cross the city for site seeing. All trains are clean & on time all ways, hand luggage can be kept on the overhead storage and you jacket can be hung on the two coat hangers nest to your window. Power points to charge you laptops or phone is located below the window.Tokyo station is like a modern underground city all ways busy. Be early to board your train as most of the staff have limited English  and getting form one train to another train as this is one of the busiest railways station I have being.
How about WiFi that runs through the services of a specific company as Japan's leading means of transportation? I only scored this aspect.
It is an indispensable vehicle for comfortable transportation. If you want to see Mt. Fuji, get a window seat for two. If it's sunny, Mt. Fuji can be seen really beautifully.

The Tokaido Shinkansen runs between Tokyo and Shin-Osaka. Fares are expensive at regular prices, but if you use them in conjunction with an Express Card or a Tokyo Bookmark hotel package, you can save a lot of money. What's more, Tokyo Bookmark offers only high-quality hotels. Recommended.

Be sure to keep in mind that the queue for Shinkansen tickets is always at least half an hour. There are machines for purchasing, but they usually do not accept foreign bank cards. So buy early to avoid being late. Otherwise, everything is very convenient and fast. The train has a toilet and serves drinks, snacks and even ice cream (all for a fee). Garbage after yourself must be thrown into a special trash bin. There is a lot of legroom and the backrest reclines. Also keep in mind that only when you are abroad you can buy a special JR Pass (about 29,000 yen for a week), which also allows you to ride the Shinkansen unlimitedly.

At 10h00 we boarded the Shinkansen Nozomi , at Tokyo Station , destination Hakata . On the 11 of November this Nozomi voyage had the number 23 and we were destined to leave this Bullet Train at Kyoto station , som 800 and a few more km to the West, and a bit more than 2 hours of distance. The Green wagons for reserved 1st class seats are quite good, and the flight ... Sorry , the voyage is delightully serene at the speed of 318 Km/h . Just loved the view of Mount Fuji , while sipping a Coke purchased from the Hostess .Indeed we are delighted with the proficiency of the World Masters of Railways !

In the N700s, each seat has power only on the window side. None for N700. Only the front and last rows of vehicles are available. There is one toilet for every two cars. 2 large pieces and 1 small piece per location. There is only one multi-purpose toilet. Smoking rooms are only available for N700s. Maybe 3 places. The other day, when I got on the N700, car number 3 was all smoking cars! Surprised. There is almost no time delay. Tokyo ⇄ Nagoya 2 hours Tokyo ⇄ Kyoto/Osaka 2 and a half hours or more. Habuanasu Trip!

We purchased a 7 day rail pass which we used everyday as it can be also used on JR lines around any city or to Tori gates in Inari, to Nara, the hop on hop off bus in Hiroshima and the ferry to Miyajima Island.I recommend to reserve your seats for every trip as the train can get crowded and reserve them several days ahead.  We reserved all of our seats for the 7 days all at the same time.  Make sure you know the times and destinations of the trains you require as the staff have very limited English (our problem, not theirs) and do not give any advice, they just book your seats as you request.  Times of the trains can be found on HyperDia.  Window seats have power sockets on the floor next to the seat.Luggage - there are no end of carriage luggage storage that we could find, luggage must be lifted onto the overhead luggage racks or jammed in front of your feet, so pack lightly if travelling on these trains.This is a fabulous, very comfortable way to travel. Loved it.

What an amazing Railway system,trains every 10 minutes between Tokyo and Kyoto, beautiful trains very clean, and above all punctual service. Very helpful staff coupled with amazing Japanese politeness.

We found it quite difficult to work out whether it would be better to pre-purchase a rail pass or just buy tickets at the station. Finally found a helpful website which offered a calculator to enter trips you plan to take on your stay in Japan, and figure out is it is cost effective. One way from Tokyo to Kyoto, then down to Osaka worked out cheaper to get single tickets rather than rail pass. If you plan to do a round trip, get the rail pass. We paid 13,080 yen each one way from Tokyo to Kyoto on the fastest option, with un-reserved seating. The trains went every 10-15 minutes and un-reserved tickets mean you can take any train time. Seats D and E offer views of Mount Fuji on a clear day. The journey too 2 hours and 15 minutes, with approximately 4 stops in between. At top speed, the train was almost silent and super smooth. A must in Japan.

The English announcement on the train informs you that 'WiFi is available on this train'. This information is incorrect, they need to fix this misleading recorded announcement, as only a select few trains have Wi-Fi, for a prepaid price.

It is no doubt that everyone has heard about the Japanese bullet train called the "Shinkansen" as it was the first high speed train built for commercial use. It was first commissioned in 1964 just in time for the Tokyo Olympics and over  time the original design has been constantly improved to achieve a speed as high as 320 km per hour.The JR network of Tokaido shinkansen trains run extensively all over Japan from the central position of Tokyo to Kyushu in the southwest and Hokkaido in the northeast and because of its massive network, incredible speed and clockwork punctuality, it has always been preferred over air travel for domestic destinations by travellers, tourists and locals alike.The JR rail pass, which must be purchased outside Japan before arrival is a very good deal as it would cover all the bullet train travels on the JR network linking all the cities all over Japan, as individual trip tickets would be quite stiff for visitors to the country.Our trip from Tokyo to Shin-Osaka, a 515 km journey took just 2 hours plus to cover, and after you get the hang of it, going to Kyoto, Nara, Hiroshima or any other city connected by the shinkansen, was easy.If you go to Japan, this amazing high-speed experience is definitely a must-try.

what more can I say, the staff is numerous, charming, professional, the stations wonderfully organized, everything is simple, controlled. the trains are impeccable even in the standard class and they are on time to the minute ready,

The bullet train in Japan is a must try. If you are planning to visit Tokyo and Kyoto and Osaka, this is the best and cheapest way to get there. While traveling towards or away Tokyo, there is a chance for you to  pass and see Mount. Fuji. I recommend that you book your seat early . That way you don't have to hassle over the non reserve car or stand for an hour or so.Also, best to bring a snack and drink on board for maximum pleasure and comfort.

The UK could learn a lot from this fantastic, super efficient train service. We left Tokyo at 6:10pm and arrived in Osaka 2 1/2 hours later. I would recommend this service to anybody visiting Japan. As long as you arrive at the station with sufficient time to spare then the concourse is easily navigated.

We have been on many European high speed train lines in the past but nothing can compare to the "bullet train". (Named after the shape of the first Class 0 trains from 1964 and no longer in service)We were delighted to have several rides on the Tokaido Shinkansen, the 700 series trains are 16 carriages and station platforms almost half a mile long and efficiency is close to unbelievable with an amazing frequency on the dedicated lines. Most guide books to Japan have iconic images of a Shinkansen train with Mount Fuji in the background and we were fortunate to see Fuji twice, once with a snow cap and once without making excellent photographs.On this particular line maximum speed is around 285 Kph (some of the others can go a little faster) and comfort levels are simply exceptional. The "ordinary" blue class is far from ordinary and really the upper level "green" class is not really needed. Leg room is excellent and there are fold down trays for you to eat your food (best purchased at the fabulous and futuristic stations). Seats are always forward facing!  Frequency on the dedicated lines certainly puts anything in Europe to shame.We rode using the Japan Pass (purchased in advance in the UK) which permits travel on all but the "Nozomi" service (minimal stops) but it hardly matters. We cannot wait to go back and try some of the other lines. Pricing for individual journeys is not cheap but you get what you pay for here and on par with flying..If you go to Japan the Shinkansen is an absolute must.

This train is super cool, super fast and if your travelling from Tokyo to Osaka or Kyoto you may see Mount Fuji! 🗻Check for ticket prices in your home country, strangely enough sometimes these tickets are cheaper abroad. Do not buy one way or return ticket if you might be travelling more than once/twice, I made that mistake when it would have been cheaper to buy a weekly pass for that line.Hope this helps, enjoy 👍
A great experience to travel in a Bullet Train @ 320kmph. A must experience in Tokyo. Traveled from Shin to yokohama and back. very comfortable journey. very clean and class.

In my subjective opinion, no visit to Japan is ever complete without a ride on a high-speed bullet train – the Shinkansen. After all, how often do you see a tourist brochure on Japan that didn’t include an image of the bullet train? Like Mt Fuji, the Japanese Shinkansen is simply iconic. Japan has ten bullet train lines, of which the Tokaido Shinkansen is one. Being the rail connection between the capital of Tokyo and the country’s 3rd largest city of Osaka, the Tokaido is by far the busiest of all the shinkansen lines. Incidentally the term ‘shinkansen’ simply means ‘new trunk line’, but it is used as a reference to either the line/route or the train service, as the case may be.Tokaido Shinkansen refers to the line or route, and several bullet trains run on it, namely the Nozomi, Hikari, Kodama, Mizuho and Sakura Shinkansens. These range from full express and limited express to multiple-stops. While the multiple-stop bullet trains pause journey more frequently, they operate at the same high-speeds between stations. However their overall journeys are obviously longer in duration.Along the Tokaido line, the shinkansens run at three to seven minute intervals, with the expresses overtaking the multi-stop trains when stationary at stations. The precision in timing of these bullet trains is impressive.If you have the opportunity to alight/depart from an intermediate station, spend a few minutes waiting for the next express shinkansen to go by. A bullet train zooming by at maximum speed is absolutely thrilling! On the Tokaido line, the shinkansens run at a maximum operational velocity of 285 km/h (177 mph). Indeed, the velocity app on my smartphone clocked 281 km/h at several points on a journey on a Hikari Shinkansen. Even at maximum speed, the ride is so smooth that you hardly perceive movement unless you look out the window. It is as smooth as a Boeing 787. Comfort in Ordinary Class is far superior to airline Economy, and frankly, it is unnecessary to pay for a Green Class seat (supposedly equivalent to Business Class). There is yet another class, Gran (First) Class, but that isn’t available on the Tokaido line. Seat pitch and width in Ordinary Class is fantastic. In fact, it is long enough to allow a medium-sized luggage bag between your knees and the seat in front. The seat is as wide as a small armchair. Alternatively you can leave your luggage in the appropriate storage area or overhead. The seats are comfortable and can be reclined. Tray tables and power to charge your portable devices are available at all seats.A shinkansen ride is more than a high-speed train ride however. It is an experience. It starts with a troupe of cleaners who line up on the platforms ahead of the arrival of a shinkansen at a terminal station. They descend upon the train once passengers have alighted. Interior cleaning occurs over a mere five minutes but their cleaning is spotless and superior to that done by budget airlines. Seats are turned about to face the direction of travel, tray tables cleaned, etc. During this process, do not enter the carriage. We found this calmly frantic and efficient ‘ballet’ of cleaning rather amusing. The speed of their work is splendid.Then, only in Japan would you see a train conductor bow each and every time when entering or leaving the carriage. Only in Japan would you have bento boxes, sushi, various Japanese snacks and refreshments available for purchase from service stewards coming through the carriage with their trolleys. However a good option is to purchase meals (including hot meals) and refreshments from the kiosks on the departure platform. Food from the kiosk is typically good and prices economical, and JR has no issues with passengers bringing their own food and beverages onto shinkansens. But do not bring a carton of beer for a drinking party aboard as this is frowned upon.The Tokaido line traverses beautiful landscape and scenery, and arguably, the highlight of the journey is Mt Fuji. At its closest, the shinkansen line is something like 25km from the peak of the mountain; yet the volcano looms and is majestic on a clear day. For best views of Mt Fuji:(1) In the direction of Kyoto/Osaka (westbound), book seats on the right-hand-side of the train. Conversely, when heading towards Tokyo (eastbound), book seats on the left-hand-side. This will allow you to view Mt Fuji from the comfort of your seats.(2) If seats on the desired side is unavailable, stand at the door where you will still be able to see the volcano.(3) Mt Fuji will come into view 40-45 minutes into the journey from Tokyo, around the vicinity of Shin-Fuji Station (the 6th station from Tokyo if riding an all-stops train). Stations in order from Tokyo are Shinagawa / Shin-Yokohama / Odawara / Atami / Mishima / Shin-Fuji.(4) Obviously, travel on a clear day for best views.While you can purchase independent Shinkansen journeys, the best way to get your money’s worth is to purchase a Japan Rail (JR) rail pass. Japan Rail offers several rail pass options with different features and conditions, some for purchase in-country, some outside Japan. JR owns Japan’s largest rail network and operate the shinkansens. Arguably the best option is the JR National Rail Pass for tourists. These are available in certain countries and have to be purchased outside Japan from an authorised agent – e.g. JTB, H.I.S. & Sachi Tours. The agent will issue an exchange voucher made out in the traveller’s name. The spelling of your name must be identical to that on your Passport. JR will issue your rail pass in Japan on presentation of the exchange voucher and passport, provided all details are correct. The JR National Rail Pass is available in 7-, 14- or 21- consecutive day durations, and is valid for unlimited travel on all JR transport including Shinkansen bullet trains (except Nozomi & Mizuho services), express and limited express trains, local trains, local buses, Miyajima Ferry and the Tokyo Monorail.Given that there is a range of JR Passes available, do your research to ascertain which product best suits your needs; and at the same time, review their terms and conditions. As these Shinkansens are speedy, you can cover a lot of ground in Japan easily and quickly. For instance, Tokyo to Osaka is 2.5 and 3 hours on a Nozomi and Hikari respectively. You arrive at destinations well-rested. The line services major cities like Tokyo, Yokohama, Hamamatsu, Nagoya, Kyoto and Osaka. Recommendations:(1) Always book your shinkansen journey and seats, even if you have a JR Rail Pass.(2) Best to deal with JR’s Tourist Centers for passes, tickets and seat bookings as staff are used to tourists and speak English well. They are located in most major rail and subway stations. (3) Previously booked shinkansen journeys can be changed without penalty. Therefore book your journeys early to ensure you obtain seats.(4) Install a velocity app on your smartphone or device, and track the speed of the shinkansen. It’s fun!(5) Install the Hyperdia app on your smartphone. This app is excellent for train route searches and timetables including the shinkansens.Ride the shinkansens. We typically have several journeys on each trip to Japan!Thanks for reading this review and my gratitude should you rate it as helpful. Life is short... visit Japan today!
Punctual, fast and convenient. A very convenient way to travel in Japan. I wish you could find the equivalent in more countries.

The best and only way to travel around Japan. These trains run like clockwork are so comfortable and fast.Snack  food is served by a wandering hostess but there are plentiful shops on the main station to buy food for your journey. A truly memorable travel experience

Flawless punctuality, clean trains, plenty of legroom, reclining seat with tablet,...and separate male/female toilets!!!Rather high prices (230€/2) between Osaka and Tokyo but it is the ideal mode of transport between the 2 cities. High frequency of departures. No need to book!!!
It's like riding an airplane but on tracks. Seats are comfortable. Train is very much on time. Stops are so short, never attempt to go out if it's not your stop or you'll be left behind.
The best way to get around the city, they are super punctual, they have many lines so you will be connected with the entire city, the frequencies are constant, they are clean, fast, the best!

We were extremely impressed. It is possible to offer fast trains with comfortable seats, good service and punctuality. Entry and exit is cleverly solved, no crowding, instead discipline. The train is not expensive, rather reserving seats is expensive.

One of the reasons we came to Japan was to experience this train, and we were not disappointed. The seats are comfortable with plenty of leg room. Although it can travel At up to 320kms/hr, you still get a clear view of the passing country side. The ride is very smooth, the speed unreal! Highly recommend.

I use it 4-6 times a month. It's safe, accurate, and safe. As for accuracy, the annual average delay time is said to be a whopping 12 seconds, and this includes the effects of weather, etc., so there is usually no delay. As expected from Japan's JR!

The Shinkansen bullet train 700 series are a great experience in themselves, and so fast you can be transported from one big city, Tokyo to another big city, Kyoto, in a few hours, in comfort.I recommend getting the Japan Rail Pass. This enables you to travel without having to buy tickets at the station, where there is often a very long queue.Japan's Shinkansen network had the highest annual passenger ridership (a maximum of 353 million in 2007) of any high-speed rail network until 2011.Shinkansen also serves commuters who travel to work in metropolitan areas from outlying cities one or two stops removed from the main cities, and there are some services dedicated to this market.

I use it when going to the Kansai area. The inside of the N700 is clean and makes you feel like you're traveling. I guess the limit for traveling from Tokyo is to Kobe. If you are traveling from overseas, please try the Japan Rail Pass! You can't ride Nozomi, but it's a great deal.

Definitely the fastest and most comfortable solution for long journeys in Japan. I highly recommend getting the JR pass, but remember to reserve your seat every time, because the shinkansen are always full, peak and off-peak times. Simply go to any JR station the day before your planned trip and reserve your seat completely free of charge. For the shinkansen between Shin-osaka and Tokyo, ask which side is where you can enjoy the view of Mount Fuji on good weather days.

On JR Pass Hikari is quickest train to Kyoto. I recommend reserving a seat as trains non reserved cars fill up fast and I was forced to stand first few stops.  Non reserved cars in front (ours had 5 cars). Better to find it from outside rather than walking down aisles. Comfortable roomy seating 3 on one side and 2 on other. Need to prearrange wifi connection at ticket office. Power outlets at all seating rows. JR pass does not include access to green cars which are comparable to business or first class.

express train that goes up to 300 km, it goes fast and is super punctual, disembarkation takes place in 1-2 minutes. so make it ready in time for disembarkation the train does not wait! shopping trolley comes around in the train, there is ice cream, cafe, beer, drink water, snacks, etc. It's great to pay by card or cash or Suica card. good toilet on board.ps.paper is available.

Second class is OK but First Class is 10 times more comfortable and you get to sit next to the Grand Champion of Sumo if you are lucky!!!!  Such a wonderful way to travel.  Went from Tokyo to Kyoto and back (first way second class reserved and second way first class which was $100 more for 2 of us).  It is only 2 1/2 hours so if money is tight and you don't need lots of leg room then 1st class is not necessary.  We had wonderful time.  No dining car but a nice lady comes down aisle twice with drinks and snacks.
Travelled from Kyoto to Nagoya. Precise time schedule, clean, and fast. The Kyoto station is conveniently located across New Miyako hotel.

It's fast, clean and comfortable.  Much more room than trains in the UK. Luggage space is very limited on some services but overall a positive experience.  Buy a Japan Rail Pass before you leave the UK and remember to reserve seats as some services are very busy.  Please note that the Rail Pass is not for use on Nozomi or Mizuho services!

We purchased a JR pass for 7 days at a cost of about 450 Canadian $ and recouped our value very quickly.  The experience of traveling on a bullet train is a unique one.  You don't realize how quickly the train is moving.  one example - we rode from Kyoto to Hiroshima on a day trip.  It took 1 and 3\4 hrs compared to 4.5 hrs one way.The trains are super comfortable, the views for the most part are great except when going through tunnels and there are lots of them.The food and beverage service is limited and expensive so bring your own.

Yes, it is just a high-speed train, but the Japanese have organized it in such a way as to make it a very convenient experience. It is the best way to travel between Tokyo, Osaka, and Kyoto. There are many trains that travel back to back; so catching one is easy. You can use the automated kiosks for purchasing your tickets. Keep in mind, the stations can be a little confusing to navigate, and there are not as many signs in English as you might expect; so give yourself some time to find your platform when you have your ticket. Also, you can carry large luggage onto the train.

Used Nozumi service from Tokyo to Kyoto and return same day. Signage at both stations was excellent in both Japanese and English. Stations were very clean and we were impressed by the  safety gates between platform and train. The green car seats were very comfortable with only criticism being that the footrests got in the way for long limbed passengers. It was very hot in the carriage but a quick word with a staff member resulted in the air con being boosted. Announcements were bilingual and staff regularly walked by with a trolley carrying snacks and drinks. Whilst wifi was advertised it transpired it was not free and no one knew the password anyway!!Unlike UK trains, there was no noise or loud use of mobile phones allowing one to doze if required.Upon return to Tokyo we were greeted with a small army of bowing cleaners who, no doubt, ensured the train would soon be on its way south again devoid of any dirt and rubbish.

The N700A is JR Tokai's latest Shinkansen, but it has severe vibrations and high-temperature noise. JR East's Hayabusa E5 and Hakutaka E7 are extremely quiet with minimal vibrations. It's obvious which one makes your body tired more easily. If JR Tokai had a desire to be considerate to its users, they could have introduced the E5 series right away, but they don't. I can't help but feel that the users are being sacrificed to raise the huge costs of the linear motor car. JR Tokai will make the linear motor car the next generation Shinkansen. On the other hand, JR East seems to be considering increasing the rigidity of the conventional Shinkansen's body to achieve a speed of 400km to 500km/h and running it all the way to Sapporo. At first glance, the linear motor car seems to be a newer technology, but the basic technology was completed in the 1960s and is old. Commercial operation has already begun in China in 2002, so this is not the first time humankind has achieved this feat. JR East is competing with other countries to develop its conventional Shinkansen trains at speeds of 500km/h. This is a new technology because it can only be realized by developing an unknown material that is lighter and more rigid than metal. If successfully developed, it will have a wide range of applications, from rockets to skyscrapers to homes, and could completely change the landscape of cities. I watched the overseas news on NHK and was surprised by the Russian nightly news. The idea was to build a bridge across Sakhalin's Soya Strait and Mamiya Strait to connect Tokyo and Moscow by rail. Although it has not been reported at all in Japan, Russia seems to be moving forward. The terminal station of this railway was London. As you can see from the flight routes to Europe, the shortest distance from Japan is to fly over Russia. The same could be said for railways. It could be interesting if it comes true. It is said that there are currently 30 freight trains running between China and Germany each week. However, it seems that it will take a week to arrive because of the railway conditions in each country you pass through on the way. China's One Belt, One Road initiative probably means that they are trying to do something about this area with conventional Shinkansen trains. Japan and Russia are just two countries, so once the talks are over, all that's left to do is build a railway and it looks like it will soon be open to Europe. At 500km/h, it seems like you can reach Europe the next day. The world of logistics seems to be changing. What I want to say to JR Tokai is not to think about the world situation, but to consider the convenience of users. If you have time on your train, JR East will mark your ticket at the ticket gate and let you out. JR Tokai does not provide ticket gates. The only place to spend your time is to wait for an empty seat in the ``Shoboi waiting room.'' Even if you compare the staff, JR East treats you like a customer. JR Tokai has an arrogant attitude as if they are just giving passengers a ride. Your salary comes from us users. Every time I use the Tokaido Shinkansen, I can't help but feel more like a prisoner than a user. I have no expectations for the future of JR Tokai, which has good vehicles and good staff.

I did the journey Tokyo to Osaka and this is definitely a relaxing way to travel!Just three hours and the sights were great. We were lucky as Mt Fuyji was clearly visible.My tips:Don't book on the day, the lines are long. Do it in advance.If you have a rail pass. Go in to the station the day before and select your seats if in a group and want to remain together- or you are left with the unassigned seats.There is a trolley lady onboard selling coffee, bento boxes, sandwiches etc but she can run out if you are at the back of the train so bring some snacks.Suitcase space is limited so arrive early and line up.I definitely preferred this to flying!

Just returned from Japan (1st time). We would never buy JR  Rail pass again. Purchasing tickets there much cheaper, unless all your train travel is on JR you need to buy tickets anyway so it's extra costs. Sub stations are not included on JR rail pass. We got caught many times, as we used Google to help us get to A and B from our hotels. We bought 7 day pass used it for our booked seats (that you book when there) on Bullet train from  Kyoto to Tokyo incredible clean, fast and so comfortable. Station masters used crossed fingers no no not use here. But you learn from the experience though.

Most of the time, the Tokaido Shinkansen is comfortable, but things are different during the summer vacation period. The number of families, elderly people, and foreigners are increasing. It's a tough time for office workers because I'm so jealous and the unreserved seats are so crowded. That's probably why people like the Shinkansen so much.
Just waiting for the train is a experience and seeing the high speed trains go through. Then being on one is amazing, unforgettable experience.
The high-speed train is very spacious and also comfortably furnished; During the drive there is also friendly catering for smaller bags and drinks; Smokers can also retreat to a separate area
If you sit on the left side facing the direction of travel, you can see Mt. Fuji. Mt. Fuji was covered with a snow cap just in time for the season, and it looked as beautiful as a picture.
Japan is rapidly becoming more globalized in the run-up to the Olympics, and it would be better if Shinkansen trains had baggage inspection areas and IDs required as soon as possible.

What a great way to travel We purchased a 7 day pass in Australia before we departed You cannot buy this pass once you get to JapanYou are issued a voucher which you then must trade for rail passes at one of the JR stationsOnce this is done you can book individual seats for the date required We booked a green pass (first class) and would highly recommend itWe travelled from near Hakone to Hiroshima which was about four hours and then from Hiroshima to Kyoto. What a fantastic way to travel the country. Scenic views everywhere and travelling in absolute comfortThe JR pass also gave us free access to some other trains such as Kyoto to Osaka and in some cities their local bus toursNot cheap but worth every cent

Thank you for your help in various situations such as work, going home, private life, etc. If you use the Tokaido Shinkansen even a few times a year, we highly recommend using Express Reservation! It's so comfortable that you have to be careful not to oversleep (lol)

Fun to experience this "bullet train", but also has its drawbacks, e.g. was actually designed to be for businessmen, not tourists, so no baggage car.  If you have anything other than one small carry-on, you have to ship it ahead to your hotel and reclaim it there.  I traveled with an OAT tour group, so they handled all the arrangements, but I can see where this could be difficult and/or inconvenient for anyone traveling independently. Anyway, boarding is ultra-organized and very quick - the average stop is only 90 seconds, but handicapped assistance can be arranged in advance.  Seats recline, but do not have seat belts (optional or otherwise), which I found surprising since speeds of almost 200 mph can be reached on some stretches.  "Shinkansen" are very streamlined, and can run in either direction without need to turn around or change engines.

We made a number of journeys on the Shinkansen using the JR rail pass, which is fantastic value. The trains are easy to use - booked and located by train number and the seats in green ( first ) class are very comfortable and spacious. Oh and the trans run to the second, and they are so quiet.

I took a train from Shin-Yokohama to Tokyo, and passengers who had just smoked in the smoking room before getting off the train walked around the train incessantly, and I felt sick from their exhaled smoke and the smell of cigarettes. The echoes of the old smoking car I rode on the way home still didn't give me that unpleasant feeling. The half-hearted countermeasure against second-hand smoke by installing a smoking room is extremely malicious, as it spreads the damage caused by third-hand smoke, which was mostly limited to smoking cars, to all vehicles. Even though the number of foreigners visiting Japan is increasing, I think it's embarrassing that the public transportation system is one of the best in the world. There are also new trains coming, but I would like them to be completely non-smoking like on airplanes and the Hokkaido Shinkansen, and either have more seats for smoking rooms or use them as luggage storage.

We used this Shinkansen in reverse from Shin-Osaka to Tokyo and many other lines during our holiday. These are very fast and efficient and do not give you the impression that you are travelling at speed. We reserved our seats for all journey's at the JR travel centre. There was a trolley service throughout the journey.

A unique experience! Delay is a foreign concept for the Shinkansen, so you should be at the platform on time. The wagons are cleaned before the start of the journey and the seats are turned in the direction of travel. Our journey from Hiroshima to Osaka started exactly to the second, you don't even notice the high speed. The seats are comfortable and there is a lot of legroom. A dream! The staff is extremely polite and disciplined; the train attendant bows to the passengers when entering and leaving the carriage. You can purchase snacks and drinks during the trip.

I had the chance to ride the high speed 'bullet train' which took 2.5 hours with short stops in between. It is most comfortable ride and the seat is relaxing than a standard airplane seat. It has plenty or space to stretch and cross your legs. It does, however tend to be the most expensive mode of travel than air travel

Is unbelievable how fast this train goes. Between Tokyo and Kyoto it reached 320 km/h. You look out of the window and everything will look blury. Very confortable very quiet and a great option to travel long distances instead of a plane. Very expensive.
If the time matters to you, the bullet train or shinkansen is the solution!Try it at least once &  in spite of its high price  you will be the winner.

These fast speed trains are really neat, you can barely feel they are moving and they are going at really high speeds. We were in Japan and bought the 7-day pass, so we travelled everywhere with it with no problem. Totally worth it!

Although I made already many, many miles on the Shinkansen it still keeps amazing me each time I step on board this train. So efficient, smooth, clean and spacious Even the onboard service (coffee and snacks) is great. I love each and every ride I take with one and that includes all shinkansen trains not only the Tokaido trains.

Is it not possible to completely separate vehicles carrying smokers and children? There is no point in quitting smoking if a non-smoker smokes in a smoking room and comes near you. The same goes for bringing children. Smokers should use a smoker's vehicle, and children should use a vehicle exclusively for children!

I believe it is one of the points of reference in Japan, the service is impeccable, the carriages are very clean and the thing that leaves you amazed is the punctuality that splits the second. My advice, however, is not to listen to those who claim that outside peak times you can avoid booking a seat, it's not true, there are many periods of the year that without a reservation you risk being left stranded. If you have the JR Pass, simply go to the JR office at the station at least the day before and the reservation is free.
I usually fly by plane, but this time I was on a business trip to Nagoya, so I took the Tokaido Shinkansen. The seats are spacious, and they're punctual, which is nice sometimes.

There are a lot of trains, and it's extremely convenient, but for some reason, the inside of the train felt dark, perhaps due to the season. I have never experienced this on the Tohoku Shinkansen, which I often use.

If the tourist visiting Japan plans to visit several cities in the country, I think that using the bullet train is the most efficient way to do so. The train service in the country is excellent and in the case of the bullet train, in addition to its famous speed, the frequency of the services and the punctuality with which they depart from a station and arrive at their destination are astonishing. The seats are very comfortable and if you are not traveling with large luggage you will not have problems placing it in the space provided for this purpose above the seats. Yes, the common space at the beginning of each car is small for larger luggage. Although seat reservations are recommended for long journeys, each formation will always have three cars assigned (at the beginning or end of the formation) for those traveling without a seat reservation. There is no need to be scared to know when you arrive at your destination. Arrival at a station is announced by speakers in Japanese and English and also displayed in those languages ​​on screens located at the ends of each car. Furthermore, since arrival at a station is exact, at the scheduled time, knowing the preset times also helps to get off at the desired station. Two additional suggestions. If you decide to take the bullet train and plan to travel to more than two major cities, consider purchasing a Japan Rail Pass (JRP). By way of illustration, while a Tokyo-Kyoto ticket, with a seat reservation, costs ¥13,800 and a Kyoto-Hakata/Fukuoka ticket costs ¥15,840 (total cost ¥29,640), a seven-day JRP pass costs ¥29,110 (around USD 255) and can be purchased online and receive the voucher by mail. The JRP not only saves time and money but in many cities (Osaka, Hiroshima, etc.) it also allows the use (free, obviously) of other means of transportation associated with the JR company. The other suggestion is to plan any train trip based on the valuable information provided by the Hyperdia.com site (it is also in English). There you can find out, among other things, departure and arrival times and platforms, stops and/or transfers, type of train, cost, amenities, duration of the trip, distance to travel.

WHY do we not have bullet trains in the US? This was my first bullet train experience and it was super awesome! Oh my gosh, it's so much better than traveling by plane because the service and amenities here are so clean and well maintained. It's amazing. And it's so fast! If we could travel to nearby cities in less than half the time, wouldn't that be so convenient? Japan is extremely lucky. I'm so jealous.You MUST try these bullet trains for your travels. It's extremely convenient and comfortable. And less tiring than actually renting a car and trying to get to your destinations. Whether you're just visiting leisurely or here on business, these bullet trains will get the work done on getting to your destination safely and soundly. Try them out!NOTE: These bullet trains are just like planes. You are allowed to take in food and drinks you purchased from stores outside so no worries in bringing food in. They do sell snacks and packed lunches on board but they are a bit pricey for my tastes.

The Shinkansen is evolving, power is a given, and you can even use Wi-Fi. The Tokaido road goes all the way to Shin-Osaka, but you won't get tired even if you go beyond that by Nozomi. I am also impressed by the system, which does not stop for rare events and operates at short intervals without delays.

We caught the bullet train from Kyoto to a station that we could get to Mount Fuji from. The train ride was beautiful and we were there in less than two hours! There was plenty of leg room and it was a comfortable ride. We had preordered our lunch but a lady does come around selling snacks and drinks. Only thing, not so much room for luggage so pack lightly . Recommend you do this when in Japan !
I took a break and went to Kyoto. It's been a while since I rode the Shinkansen. I usually fly a lot, so it felt fresh. It was a comfortable 2 hour journey to Kyoto.

It's been a while since I've been on a train, but first of all, even compared to airplanes, the fares are extremely high considering it's a fast train, the hassle of buying tickets, the constant turnover of people, the expensive station lunches around you, the overall poor manners of passengers, and even though it's a hassle to get to the airport, I'd still choose to fly. I think the impression would change if it were cheaper.

We took the Shinkansen from Hiroshima to Osaka and were impressed: - by the smooth ride despite the high speed - by the punctuality; It is said to be extremely good (accurate to the second!) - seats were always given out - from the special "politeness" of the train attendants (bowing when entering and leaving the car!) - from the calm and discipline of Japanese travelers

Recently, in-car announcements on the Tokaido Shinkansen have added information to encourage the use of luggage racks, but it seems to have little effect. It is deplorable that Japanese people's manners have deteriorated, and it is common for many passengers to place bags with wheels at the feet of their seats, and it is disgusting to see passengers who put regular bags at the feet of their seats obstructing the entrance and exit of passengers sitting in the back seats.

There's no need to write a review.There's no competition, so the price between Tokyo and Nagoya is almost ridiculous.If you're on a business trip, you can fly, but at your own expense, fly from Narita to Chubu Centrair International Airport using LCC.The time will be several times as long.

Taking a Bullet Train is definitely something else! REMEMBER you can take food and drinks in the train. The stuff sold inside is expensive and they only take CASH. My advise? Buy yourself something yummy to eat at the station's "Seven Ereven" and enjoy while you QUICKLY travel everywhere.

It is very easy to take, in the big stations you can buy tickets at the ticket offices (they don't speak much English) or directly at the machines if you are clear about where you want to go (there is a menu in English, it is simple). The train is very fast, the Nozami Super Express takes only 2 hours 20 minutes between Tokyo and Kyoto. We travel in normal cars and in Green Cars, the difference is not very significant but in the latter all the seats are reserved. Be careful that there is very little space for large suitcases; They are placed behind the last row of seats in each car and recommend keeping an eye on them, not because they are going to be stolen, but because unattended luggage is considered suspicious and could be taken off the train at an intermediate station.

I used this train twice to go to Kyoto from Japan (3hrs) and to Hiroshima (4hrs) and they really are wonderful. You can buy a Rail Pass... which in Mexico costs about 250usd, and is used to travel for 7 days unlimitedly in Japan... what would cost only 1 trip you pay for the 7 days. You must be super punctual, very respectful when addressing it and when being there, because you cannot make noise... out of respect for others.  If you wanted to go to Kyoto it takes 6 or 7 hours by car, and on this train it only takes 3 hours. Truly a marvel

Mainly used for business trips. There are a lot of office workers there, and some people take off their shoes and put their legs up at night, so I would like to use planes as much as possible. Also, there are a lot of people drinking beer, so the vehicle itself is filled with the smell of alcohol, which I feel like I want to avoid in terms of space. If you leave Tokyo, you can see Mt. Fuji on the right side, and in the winter, the Mikawa Anjo area is covered in snow, so you can enjoy the scenery ☆ Also, the convenient location once you arrive at the station of Nagoya, Kyoto, Kobe, etc. is attractive ☆
We love using shinkansen when we cme to japan. Buy JRPass before. Eating ekiben, watching mount fuji. very comfortable train
We take a trip from Tokyo to Osaka by shinkansen. First, the train was very clean and smooth. Second, we enjoy the view from the window side with the beautiful scenery. Worth it.

After activating our JR passes our first train took us from Tokyo to Shin Osaka. All journeys were very comfortable, signage in English and lots of staff to help guide. Great views and can bring on food & drink (even alcohol). We were in the ordinary, not green, cars and they were very comfortable with plenty of space for all our baggage. Regarding the JR Pass, our needs were more than met with an ordinary pass.

We loved it, so cool, great experience. We travelled from Tokyo to Osaka. It was seamless. Caught local trains from Asakusa to Tokyo station. Found the Shinkansen ticket station area in Tokyo station, which was pretty easy, this is where you can buy your tickets on the Nozomi. Our attendant was very helpful and the transaction and trip were seamless. It is orderly, onetime, and awesome. We sat back and took photos the whole way, some were a bit blurry when we reached almost 300 kmh. You can take your food and drinks with you, but you can buy things but I don't know what as we took our own. When we bought our tickets there was a train arriving in 15 minutes, but we waited until the following train so we could get window seats, reserved which was worth it and allowed us time to look around, the trains were only 30 minutes apart anyway. Reserved cost a little extra but I thought worth it to sit together and have good seats. We had window tickets on the right had side of the train which were perfect, even saw today Mount Fuji from the train. If you have suitcases or luggage, they go at the back of your carriage and there is limited room with overhead storage for hand luggage.

The Shinkansen train is one of the coolest trains I've ever been on. The train was on time and travelled extremely fast. I recommend you wait for a few minutes after getting off the train to see another train pass and be amazed at how fast it travels.

Domestic travel is mostly done by train in Japan. The country has an extensive rail network which connects the big cities by high speed bullet trains. Today we travelled from Tokyo to Hakone by the Shinkansen 700. It is an amazing experience. The trains  departs perfectly on time, the train is clean inside and you hardly hear the noise from the train or other people. Even the regular class seats (which can recline) are very comfortable and the staff is really helpful. The speed is simply mind blowing as you never have the feeling the trains speeds up to over 230 km/h. We use the Japan Rail pass as we plan to travel more through Japan by rail

It was my first time seeing the Tokyo Station building. The red bricks give a sense of history and are very impressive. The modern buildings surrounding it make you feel like you've stepped back in time for a moment.

Took hikari from odawara to Kyoto and than Nozomi from Kyoto to Tokyo on a different day. Nozomi only takes 2 hours 20 min. Everything from ticket sales to signage to departure and announcements is well organized. Trains are spotless, but can get crowded. Trains arriving and leaving on the dot. Don't take Kodama trains, they are local. The only suggestion is to have more outlets/ charging stations. There is wifi on the trains.Highly recommend and well worth the cost, for busy times and destinations, get reserved ticket.

We utilized the Shinkansen on a 7 day JR pass. Well worth the cost and a huge saving made by purchasing early from our home country. This is the only way to travel long distances on mainland Japan. Tokyo to Hiroshima 1000km in 4 hours in perfect comfort. Grab a bento box sit back and relax, you'll be there before you know itTOP TIP: Book your seats at a JR office in advance, it doesn't cost you anything and reserves your seat in a dedicated car instead of chancing your luck on adjoining seats when traveling with a partner or friend.

Tohoku Shinkansen, Hokkaido Shinkansen, Yamagata Shinkansen, and Akita Shinkansen. Joetsu Shinkansen and Hokuriku Shinkansen. Sanyo Shinkansen and Kyushu Shinkansen. Nowadays, if we include the Hakata Minami Line on the Gala Yuzawa Line, which is equivalent to the Shinkansen, Shinkansen lines have begun to run throughout Japan. After all, the king of Shinkansen is the Tokaido Shinkansen. A magnificent 16-car train. For business such as Gran Class? However, it doesn't feel like a resort. As long as you are strictly business-oriented, that is the Tokaido Shinkansen. The view from the train window is always Mt. Fuji. In the past, vehicle operation was divided into Kodama, Hikari, and Nozomi, but now they are all the same. That's it when you consider efficiency. However, it is a shame that in-car sales have disappeared from Kodama. I loved that crunchy ice cream. This time I transferred from Odakyu Romance Car, so I was going from Odawara to Shizuoka. I got off the Shinkansen at Odawara because I was riding the Romance Car on the way back.

When foreigners come to visit, they usually request the bullet train, perhaps because they are used to flying. I'm having trouble traveling between Tokyo and Osaka or between Osaka and Fukuoka, and I'm not sure whether I should take a plane or not. The Shinkansen is likely to have no waiting time, but once you get on it, you'll be stuck for two and a half hours. troublesome.

Because of severe weather the nozumi we had booked on was 2 hours late leaving. However abellio take note JR railways flooded the station with assistants and information albeit in Japanese! They really know how to organise themselves to minimise customer disruption. Maybe the Scottish government should look further east than  abellio for scotrail franchises infuture. It's a rarity to run late and the Japanese travellers faces said it all !

It's really amazing to enjoy traveling on this super fast train. driving at a speed of 200 km per hour, you can barely hear the sound of the engine running or vibration when running. I can sit comfortably and enjoy the journey from Kyoto to Tokyo. The interior is clean and the toilets are also comfortable and clean.

I happened to come across it at Shin-Yokohama Station. This is the second time. The Tokai Shinkansen is amazing because it arrives on time. It is said that good things will happen to you when you see Doctor Yellow. There were a lot of photographers.

Took the bullet train to Odawara per another trip advisors recommendations.  Cost us $125NZ for X 2 adult tickets.  Plus $400¥ - $5.00 NZ, Shinjuku to Tokyo station.  Quite the challenge to know where to go as in how to buy the ticket, which platform (that was probably the easiest step).  Bullet train tickets are bought at different places to standard tickets.  We just wanted a close place to travel to, to have a look around without staying away a night.  This is a quaint seaside town with such an ambience about it.  Calm quiet peaceful.  Had lunch at a Tempura restaurant - fabulous, best meal in Japan yet.  Watched the bullet trains pass through as not all stop here so was brilliant viewing for train spotters.  Worth a day to go here.  Very relaxing.  One down side is that at the train stations there is very little English signs but enough however extremely little English assisting staff to be able to help you with directions.  I know we are in Japan......but for their tourism a bit more of the universal language wouldn't go a miss. Funnily enough there were many Japanese who couldn't really tell us what our tickets meant when we asked for assistance - they too were insure what ticket said.  The train map is a mazed in Tokyo, it is HUGE!  I like the fact I can say I've ridden the bullet train.  Fast, smooth, spectacular and extremely efficient.  Be on time! !!!!!!!

I was in Japan for a two week extravaganza, to see and do everything I possible could in that small amount of time. It was a no-brainer to take the Bullet Train (Nozomi) from Tokyo to Kyoto. My companions and I decided to go cheap and not buy tickets for reserved seats. These trains leave extremely fast once boarded, so be ready to move it! We left on a Sunday afternoon so it proved to be a little packed so we didn't end up with seats next to each other. The ride was as smooth as Mr. Clean's head. And I don't know how, but I swear this train can bend time because we got to Kyoto in what felt like two minutes rather than 2.5 hours. Maybe it was the fact that I really enjoyed being off my feet due to the miles and miles of walking we'd accumulated. This experience was well worth the money we paid. Travelling to Osaka we also ended up taking the Shinkansen back from Osaka to Tokyo and were able to admire the breathtaking views of Mt. Fuji.
Love it! Super fast and comfortable. Easy to use, easy to book tickets, easy to see a lot of the country

Nowadays, the Shinkansen has several routes from Kyushu to Hokkaido, but when it comes to Shinkansen, it is the Tokaido Shinkansen. In the past, there were times when the main part of a trip was simply riding the Shinkansen. Nowadays, it is mostly used as a means of transportation, but it is still a special vehicle as there are many sights to see, such as Mt. Fuji, Lake Hamana, and Sekigahara.

This is a must if visiting Tokyo or one of the other cities the Shinkansen runs through. Tried a trip from Tokyo to Kyoto. 520 km in 2 hours and 20 minutes. It's going fast. Order a ticket for 1st class, where you sit comfortably in large, wide seats and can enjoy the view and the speed.

Bought the 7-day JR railpass ahead of time and it paid for itself with just the round trip Shinkansen ride. The train was clearn and quiet, the seats were comfortable, and the view was great (we made sure we were on the Mt. Fuji side and caught a 20-second glimpse of it).

I lost count how many times I had been traveling using Shinkansen, visiting different cities in Japan since 1999, ever since one of my Japanese friend introduced JR Pass (green car) to us. I had traveled down to the south (Fukuoka) to as far as Sapporo in Hokkaido (north island) and many major and/or smaller cities in between in many different trips in the past 18 years.Yes, JR Pass is being considered as expensive for many foreigners if someone calculates the cost even for one week (7 days) travel especially in Green Cars (38,880 Yen vs. 29,110 Yen for Ordinary Cars). 14 days' JR Pass costs even more expensive than 7 days' pass (62,950 Yen for Green Car vs 46,390 Yen for Ordinary Cars). However, the total benefit and the experience of being able to make unlimited trips using Shinkansen has proven to outweigh the cost we have to spend.JR Pass Green car itself can even be more costly compare to round trip (economy) airfare from Jakarta to Tokyo (Narita/Haneda) by CX if someone buys his/her ticket months in advance. However, the feeling being inside Shinkansen was difficult to be described even after being on it for many years. I myself was fortunate enough to have traveling to many different cities at different times using bullet trains in Europe (ICE, TGV etc.) or even using slower trains (Renfe, Thalys etc.) but nothing really compares to the experience traveling with Shinkansen.The compartment and even all seats in Green Cars are super clean every time I was there. I could not really recall having a single issue with cleanliness inside a Green Car in the past 18 years. The seats in Green Cars are nicely design and extremely comfortable. They are definitely bigger in size than average seats in Business Class in many airlines today. It was really quiet and normally, it was not as crowded as the ones in Ordinary Cars. My suggestion : Try it for once if you can afford it. Even if you don't have a JR Pass, buying a Green Car ticket won't break your pocket although it is still costly (almost 19,000 Yen) for one way ticket from Tokyo - Osaka which will take approx. 3 hours. One more thing : Based on my past experience traveling with Shinkansen, they are strictly punctual when it comes to departure and arrival time not like ICE nor TGV in Europe. By using JR Pass, we won't be allowed traveling by using Nozomi which is faster than Hikari or Kodama Shinkansen.
Sometimes I want to ride for no reason. Unlike other Shinkansen trains, the platform position does not change depending on the train, making it easy to understand.

On the morning of the last day of Golden Week, I traveled from Shin-Osaka to Atami, and surprisingly there were a few empty seats. (The non-reserved seats may have been full.) It was great to see Mt. Fuji, but what really impressed me was the beautiful scenery of the tea plantations around Shizuoka.

I caught the Nozomi, the fastest of the bullet trains, from Tokyo to Kyoto. I did not buy a Japan Rail Pass before I left and this turned out to be a good decision as the rail pass does not alow for travel via the Nozomi. I went into the travel office at the Tokyo station and booked a seat as I did not want to have to risk not getting a seat; excellent decision! I booked ordinary class which was very comfortable. A refreshment trolley came through every half hour or so no need to worry about taking supplies with you.Great views of the countryside for the whole trip.Due to not much space for luggage, I used the terrific Luggage Forwarding system; I paid about A$15, handed in my suitcase by 5.00 pm on the eve of my departure and it was waiting for me in my hotel room when I arrived in Kyoto the next morning. This super idea should be universal; it takes all the hard work out of travelling!
I was expecting an avant-garde adventure, in fact it's nothing more and nothing less than a TGV with a little more space. I'm a little disappointed

We took the high-speed train twice. When we went from Odawara to Kyoto and when we returned from Nagoya to Tokyo. In both cases it seemed like an incredible experience to be able to move and cover a distance of 500 km. comfortably in just over 1.30 hours. Without a doubt, the best way to travel long distances within the island.

I recently visited Japan and used the Shinkansen bullet train numerous times in traveling between Tokyo, Kyoto, Osaka and Hiroshima - there's no use in gushing over the experience as it was wonderful and everyone has already commented about this.The one thing I wanted to caution travelers about is buying Shinkansen tickets directly from the ticket machines:  each time I tried it, the machine asked for a PIN code despite the fact that I was using a credit and not debit card (which obviously has no PIN).No matter what I did I couldn't get the machine to accept my card and I ended up either having to pay cash (which can be material, even a one-way unreserved seat on the Tokyo to Shin-Osaka runs around $125) or go to the ticket counter - which was fine except that there usually was a line of a dozen or two people and if you're counting on jumping on the train that's leaving in five minutes (which I was) you won't make it.Other than this minor nuisance, there's nothing about the Shinkansen that isn't spectacular.  I just wanted to caution others so that nobody has a last minute surprise like I did.

When visiting Japan in 2015, I loved the bullet train ride from Tokyo to Osaka.The train was immaculate; a cleaning crew cleaned shortly before we boarded. Refreshments were sold on board.  The ride was very smooth.  The train was on time.If you go to Japan, try the bullet train.

Always wanted to go on a bullet, so just couldn't resist booking my journey from Tokyo to Kyoto on the Shinkansen. The booking process was very conveniently done at the the JR station. The ride itself was great, very clean and efficient. Also find myself lucky enough to have a great view of Mt Fuji along the journey. A must try for anyone visiting Japan.

We used the Shinkansen twice. Once to get from Tokyo to Kyoto and the other time, from Kobe to Tokyo. The bullet train was very quick as it only took 2 hours to get to Kyoto & 3 hours to get to Tokyo. There was a lot of leg space too as I was able to fit a big luggage into that space with space leftover for my legs. I was kinda expecting the bullet train to be kind of lavish and luxurious, so I was kinda surprised at how regular it looked. Probably hyped up by the American media. Kinda expensive at about $150 USD from Kobe to Tokyo though. But it is efficient & quick!

What a fabulous experience. Fortunately a Tokyo based friend booked for us (Nozumi service) as we were travelling during a busy time and we were unable to book from Australia. As it turned out there was really no need for prior booking but it did ensure that we had prime seats for viewing Mt Fuji. As expected the service train was clean, efficient and fast! We were fortunate to view Fuji as we travelled in both directions - once with the peak covered by clouds and once with the peak visible in all its majesty. Definitely a must if you are travelling to Kyoto or beyond.

I was traveling Mishima to Osaka after finish my Mount Fuji tour. . Buy none reserved seat it's 11560 yen. It's was evening time so I was traveling standup until Shizuoka. After I got seat. Was very fast train. Mishima to Osaka 2 hours 07 mins. This train inside have smoking room, telephone both. Train arrive right time time. Great journey

Being a long suffering user of our railways it was so nice to travel on a network that runs on time who's staff are courteous and gets you to where you want to go on time.Seats are comfortable and carriages are clean with charge sockets for phones and laptops (that's work mr Branson ) Oh well back home now where's my southern rail pass 😥

No matter how many times you ride the Shinkansen, it's always exciting! Every time I ride, I feel like Japan is amazing. I'm on a day trip to Nagoya, and I'm looking forward to Mt. Fuji and beer on the way home. Hehehe

This is the first time I saw and rode on it. It's very amazing speed. It runs 320km/h. As compared to America trains, we are very behind Japan or Asia countries. The restrooms are very clean. Green car seats are very roomy and comfortable. I love it.
super fast train, impeccable cleanliness, punctual like clockwork, extremely courteous staff. Thanks to the shinkansen we saved a lot of time when traveling between one city and another in Japan.

We purchased the JR railpass for two weeks and explored city by city. Exchanging the pass and making the following reservations (green symbol) were possible without any problems. The space in the Shinkansen is great, very futuristic style. Great. There is even a smoking area every few cars. Reversing? There isn't, the seats are simply turned around.

We got the Japan Rail Pass, green car, which allowed us to move from city to city. Although there is no cost to reserve, it is advisable to do so in advance, because peak time trains usually fill up easily and then you cannot find a place. Cleanliness, excessive punctuality, service, speed, they go more than 300 km per hour. There are several types of shinkanzen. This pass DOES NOT COVER the fastest shinkanzen in Japan called Nozomi. But still, it covers others that are also very fast (we are talking about small time differences) because they make more stops. Not because the quality or the service changes. Delicious sandwiches that can be purchased on board. And cheap!

Very comfortable seats, lots of leg room as well as lots of storage space above your seats against the wall of the train. Also snack service is available. The train was very clean & the cleaning crew cleans the whole train & sanitizes the train before board the passengers. The train goes quite fast but you don't fell it as the ride is very smooth. Not crowded at all. Japanese people are very courteous & helpful. This was a Wonderful experience.
230-240 mph without a bump. Feels like you are not moving. Clean, roomy, food and drinks available. On precise time--we were told that only 36 seconds were lost over a span of several years.

A great experience to see one of these great trains going through a station at 225 MPH (360KPH). Really comfortable, clean and on time. reclining seats, good information boards, a great way to travel, lucky Japanese, 50 years ahead of us in the UK.
Traveling is pleasant. Good distance between seats. Space to store luggage. Punctuality and frequency are excellent.

So maybe im just used to trains in England but the efficiency of the train network in Japan is crazy. If you miss the train you wait for 3 minutes until the next one arrives. They are also very clean. I probably don't need to mention how fast the bullet train is, but I will, it's astounding!

The Nozomi Shinkansen is not cheap, but it is very convenient means to travel to and from Osaka and Tokyo.  The train cars are very clean and spacious.  We paid for the reserved seats.  You can buy snacks from the attendant with a trolley.  The train departed on time as most trains do in Japan.  The Shinkansen has several toilets and smoking room.  If you're holding a JR Pass, you won't be able to take this train.  On a clear day, you'll see the majestic Mt. Fuji on the left side.  The purser and attendant will be able to tell you the approximate time that the train will pass the area where you can see Mt. Fuji.

Not the most budget-friendly type of transport, but very fast and convenient, runs strictly on schedule, and there are several classes of carriages. We were in the simplest, sat down and fell asleep, generally a blunder. Navigation is not the easiest, but you can figure it out.
best train I've ever taken, fast, clean, punctual, professional and courteous staff, in short everything perfect! A little expensive but worth it

I always enjoy my journey with Shinkansen which not only time saving but also very comfortable. Inside the train is very clean and you can buy food from train stewards. Inside it has charger facilities. I enjoyed the speeeeeed........

Great clean and fast a total role reversal for what we Aussies are used to????Mt Fuji is speccy but you need to be on the right side of the train though. Don't worry about the crowds at the station though! I got a bit anxious as I'm a country boy!All good in the end. Staff at the ticket office very helpful tooAlthough there are other fast trains in the world.  These are very good although the speed wasn't indicated my app told me 269kmh was the fastest speed. Great travelling!
Writing from the trainGreen car luxuryFast Clean Courteous SafeTrain life doesn't get sweeterMy favorite travel in Japan

We vacationed in various cities in Japan and traveled locally on the railways, but to get from Tokyo to Osaka and then to Kyoto it was such a pleasure to use the Shinkansen.  We bought our tickets the day we were going to leave the city. There were some language issues, we couldn’t sit together, or they wouldn’t take our credit card, only cash, luckily we had enough cash to purchase our tickets, as they are not cheap.  Once we met up with our Japanese friend and he translated what we wanted, we were accommodated for our needs.  Traveling by the Bullet Train is seriously awesome. You can not tell that you are moving as fast as you are. It took us almost 3 hours to get from Kyoto to Tokyo, when it would take close to 6+ hours by normal railway. The bathrooms were very clean, they have charging units in each row. When the train arrives at a stop, a ‘cleaning team’ rush the train, and remove any debris, garbage and clean it so well, we felt like we were the very first passengers to travel the Bullet that day. Every where in Japan, it is so clean, the country employs very respectful people as they do a great job and it shows in its cleanliness.

We rode the Shinkansen from Shin-Kobe Station to Kyoto Station. While it was only two stops it only took 30 minutes and the ride by bus would normally be over 90 mins. It is fast, efficient, clean and on time! I wish we had such a great transportation in the states. It is a little pricey but a must do if visiting Japan!

It's like flying, but on rails. The trains stop in the station with typical Jappanese precision, eacactly at the spot indicated for the doors to open - no more guess work. The inside of the carriage is spacious with lots of legroom between seats and even comes with a hostess to serve drinks or snacks as she moves frequently down the aisle. Impeccably clean, undeniably super fast, quiet, with an unbelievably frequent timetable. Spoilt for choice of when to travel, but travel on the bullet train is a must!

If you plan to travel outside Tokyo please buy JR pass(buy online as its not possible to buy in Japan), it is worth the money. There are options of 10 days or more.We had planned to go Yokohama and Kyoto so every penny spend was worth.
The bullet train alone is an experience, it is worth it to get to know Japan, although it passes long stretches through tunnels you get an idea of ​​the rural areas of Japan
Took a short trip on the bullet train and all I can say is "WOW" we need this in Canada.As with everywhere in Tokyo it was clean,comfortable and fast, who needs planes with transportation like this.

We booked Green Car rail passes due to having a large amount of luggage to tour Japan with, and the Shinkansen trips were truly unforgettable! On most journeys, we had the carriage to ourselves, and the seats are huge and extremely comfortable, reclining to an almost laid-down position, whilst watching the countryside fly past! Because we had booked for the green car, seat reservations were mandatory, but as we had worked out the times and dates of our onward journeys, we only spent 1 hour at the JR station booking our seats (with a very helpful staff member who spoke good English). Avoid trying to exchange your rail pass voucher at the JR counter when you arrive at Hanaeda Airport, as the queues are very long and they only let you book 1 onward journey at a time. We booked our tickets at Mitaka Station  (about 20 mins from Tokyo on the JR East line) the following day,and there were no queues or limits.Many people have posted that there is no point in paying the extra for a green car pass, but I would say it is the best money we have ever spent, especially if you don't travel light! Punctual, clean, spacious, and an absolute pleasure to travel on. Highlight of my holiday!

On the Tokyo - Osaka route we took the JR Shinkasen from Mishima to Kyoto. After purchasing our tickets and reserving our seats, we waited at the designated wagon zone on the platform.
