Be sure to HAVE YOUR CAMERA OUT when you pass Mount Fuji because it flies by like everything else...yes, it's that fast.

Traveled on the Kodama after a blessful day seeing Mt. Fuji for the second time during our visit.  We found the Shinkansen to be a fast and efficient transit system, getting people from one place to another, from one connection to the next.Your ride is smooth, the seats are comfortable, and you are generally unaware of the speed you are traveling.  Most routes are frequent enough that you don't need to worry about rushing.  Be on time, the system has platform gates to prevent last minute dives into the cars.The majority of the cars are non-smoking.  Beware, not to occupy a car adjacent as the 2nd-hand smoke is dense and will travel to the adjacent non-smoking car.

The only way to travel Japan. Trains leave to the second on time. Carriages are super clean with airline seats. My tip is when using the JR Rail pass is to go their local office at Tokyo or Shinjuku a day or so before trip and reserve a seat. Costs no more and you're guaranteed a seat, especially important if travelling with a family group. Also on a longer trip buy a bento box from local shops to enjoy. Makes a difference when travelling with kids.

The best way to travel in Japan. The trains are clean and 99% on time. The staff is really friendly and in the GreenCars (1st class) the seats are heated, extra wide and there are wet towels to greet you. You should limit yourself to one suitcase per person.

Sujata's ice cream is sold on the Shinkansen train. It's hard and hard to eat right away, but it's rich. The recommended time to eat is about 5 minutes after purchase. Tokaido Shinkansen comes in three flavors: vanilla, matcha, and mandarin orange.

The Shinkansen is the most convenient way to get around Tokaido. It's early. My Tokaido route is such that every time I pass through Atami with my hair pulled back, I feel like I'm missing out if I can't see Mt. Fuji in Shizuoka.
Don't be late!  These trains leave on the dot and fly!  Clean interior and comfortable seats. Silence your cell!  Get to track early to watch the other trains blow through!

We travelled on the bullet train several times during our Japan tour. Each time it was a very comfortable experience despite busy stations and small window of time to board and alight from the train. The train punctuality is worth praising as one can set watch. It is said that annual average delay does not exceed one minute. The seats in standard class are in no way less comfortable than in green class. They can be rotated to face each other and travelling with friends can be real good experience. One needs to take care not to chat loudly else the conductor would often come and remind you to talk keeping voice low.A trolley refreshment service comes through at regular intervals serving hot and cold, including alcoholic, drinks and a selection of snacks and sandwiches. The eatables here are not as expensive as the ticket is.  The speed and smoothness of the ride has to be experienced to be believed. A two hour journey from Tokyo to Sendai was delightful as it is entirely on elevated track with great views of mountains and valleys. Must do if you visit Japan.Tip: Buy a japan rail pass if you want to move around in japan which is far cheaper than buying individual tickets

Stand on the platform based on your seat reservation. The train arrives exactly on the minute exactly where you are standing. You step directly into your seat. Maybe you're having a drink at the bar at 220km/h, no shakes at all. You see FUJI in the distance (a powerful experience. You arrive refreshed at exactly the right time.

The myth of Japanese bullet trains has also arrived in Italy, when probably the fastest train in our country was the intercity! A lot of water has passed under the bridge and now we too, in our own small way, do Rome-Milan in 3 hours... However, although the wow effect has waned a little, the Japanese shinkansen maintain a record that our trains will hardly be able to match or even come close to: punctuality. It is said that a shinkansen accumulates annual delays of the order of seconds and it is not science fiction!!! It is pure and simple reality, impressive. Just as impressive is the efficiency of the cleaning teams who "attack" the carriages at the terminus and with an all-Japanese precision and ghostbuster-style clothes, thoroughly clean the train in just a few minutes. Finally, the tapered design of the nose of these trains has a truly captivating charm for adults and children. Obviously only with JR pass!!!
Super fast train, I recommend getting the jr pass to take it. Also very convenient, food on the train is expensive however

I used it on a business trip to Tokyo. The train departs from Tokyo Station. It was early afternoon on a Monday, but it was pretty crowded, probably because it was the Monday after the last Saturday and Sunday of summer vacation.

We travelled on the bullet train several times during our Japan tour.  Each time it was a thrilling experience. The train arrives and leaves spot on time with a limited slot for disembarking passengers and new travellers to change over.The seats in standard class are very spacious (I am 6ft 2ins and had plenty of room) and comfortable, reclining sufficiently for you to sleep.  A trolley refreshment service comes through at regular intervals serving hot and cold, including alcoholic, drinks and a selection of snacks and sandwiches. The speed and smoothness of the ride has to be experienced to be believed.  A 2 hour journey from Tokyo to Osaka was one the delights of the trip with rice fields and villages speeding past. Must do if you visit Japan.

Before going to Japan we heard and read a lot about these super-fast trains. Obviously we couldn't not try them! Just looking at them, these long tapered "snouts" seem to have been built in a wind tunnel to cut through the air. Once we got on we noticed how clean it was like everything in Japan, once we left it didn't seem like we were going that fast, it's like going on a plane you seem to be almost at a standstill! As for punctuality, I don't even say that in Japan they are too far ahead!!!

It is the best way to travel around Japan in the fastest way, very comfortable, with excellent services. It is best to get a JR Pass to avoid the high prices of Shinkansen.I would recommend to travel with Shinkansen to arrive fresh at destination and visit your favourite places in Japan.

I was lucky enough to spend 3 weeks in Japan in May and trying the high-speed train was a fantastic experience. We traveled with it between Toyohashi and Kyoto and except that (like almost everything in Japan) it cost quite a lot, it will remain an eternal memory for me...

I used these trains when I went to Japan in September 2015 and I must say that I was truly amazed: from the punctuality, to the courtesy of the staff, to the cleanliness inside the train. The use of these trains, and in particular the Japan Rail Pass, is not recommended for those who limit their holiday to just one city but it is an essential subscription for those who want to move from city to city. The price of the subscription is absolutely convenient and the major cities are connected within a few hours (e.g. Tokyo - Kyoto is a route that takes approximately 2 hours).
Used between Tokyo and Kyoto. I traveled by Nozomi, so I arrived quickly. The seating area is spacious and comfortable. I tried the in-car sales several times, but I didn't use them.

It depends on the time, but I generally choose the Shinkansen over the plane. Trains are very crowded during the year-end and New Year holidays and Obon, so it is wise to reserve your seat as soon as you have decided on your trip (Nozomi, Hikari) On the other hand, I have never been unable to sit in a non-reserved seat on Kodama. The N700 series has an outlet near the window, so if you are interested, you may want to ask the staff at the counter.

For those who smoke, the 700 series is recommended! However, although there are few Nozomi, the probability of hitting Hikari is high. Check the timetable at the Midori-no-madoguchi ticket office before boarding. If you take a designated smoking seat, you can enjoy a cigarette while sitting in your seat until you get off the train. It takes about an hour longer than the Nozomi route between Nagoya and Tokyo, but it provides a very luxurious feeling. In the same car, the green car also has a smoking seat.

Last year I went by car and this year I went to see Mt. Fuji by Shinkansen. Last year I went to see it from the Pacific side, but unfortunately I couldn't see it. This year from the Yamanashi side. Take the Shinkansen from Kyoto to Mishima. Ride on the Hikari train. 700 series instead of N700 series. I thought it would be crowded because it was the last day of the Obon holiday, but the green cars were empty. Lucky❗

Get me to the next shinkansen! We just loved our travel by these trains. They are smooth and fast and just a joy to travel on them. There is plenty of leg room and they are very good value for money if you purchase a Japan rail pass BEFORE you leave for Japan as they are not available once you arrive. We spent £200 on our rail pass for one week which sounds expensive until you realise that this means unlimited travel (not the non-stop trains but all the others and local trains run by JR) on the shinkansen. Awesome!

I speak as an enthusiast.. It is neither the fastest train in the world nor the most modern one, but it has something that leaves us speechless especially for us Italians.. The punctuality, courtesy and gestures of all the people who revolve around it (e.g. the conductor who bows when exiting the carriage, the cleaning team with their rituals, etc..)
Fantastic smooth and comfortable way to travel. And fast! Kyoto - Tokyo in just over 2 hours. Also punctual and reliable like everything in Japan. Highest rating!
Ever on time, every 10 min, clean, damn fast, best travel means to travel far distances. You can choose the orientation of your seats , sit and relax, you are almost there.

The service is significantly inferior compared to ANA and JAL. Moreover, since there is no security check, there are many safety problems. This time I was assigned a standard seat, so it was stressful!

Yes it's great that you can travel at 180mph but you pay dearly for it. A short 30min ride was the equivalent of £30 each. I guess Japan is bloody expensive anyway but these other costs to the holiday really were a shock. On the plus side the trains are never late and seats have enough legroom for an large NBA player. Top tip is to travel when it's less busy - then you can buy an unreserved ticket and still get a seat without paying a hefty fee.

Tokaido Shinkansen has been in operation for many years.  This is the first time I tried the Green Car.  It was spacious, comfortable, and clean.  The washroom was also exceptionally clean and well equipped with travelers carrying babies.  The washroom is spacious enough to be the diapers changing room, with baby crib and diapers depository.  Either at Tokyo station or Shin Osaka station, there are numerous stores selling all kinds of food, drinks, snacks, souvenirs before or after you board the Shinkansen.  The 3 hours+ ride is never boring.  There is also a lady selling drinks and snacks with a trolley on board the train.With this service and comfort level, travelling within Japan is always a pleasure.

Just as legends say, Japanese punctuality and reliability are a solid reality. Trains that rock the second, very clean, large and comfortable. My bathroom is a dream! With the jrp you can use all the shinkansen except the mizuho and the nozomi, which make even fewer stops. A unique experience for us Italians.
I use it every week on business trips. The beer sold at platform kiosks at stations where only Kodama stops, such as Shin-Fuji and Kakegawa, is ice-cold and the best.

I used various Shinkansen trains for individual legs between Hiroshima and Yokohama in the second half of July. As already described in previous reports, the air-conditioned high-speed trains are very clean and you reach your destination very quickly (for example, the Nozomi only takes about 4 hours for the 900 km between Hiroshima and Tokyo - and you are already right in the center). The train sequence is also worth noting: on average, the Shinkansen leaves for Tokyo every 20 minutes! As a German train driver, you have to "adjust" to the following when using the Shinkansen: - don't arrive at the platform a second late. Delay is a foreign word for the Shinkansen. All information (written and spoken) is also in English and is also correct. - Friendliness is obviously the top priority for the train crew, even if the gestures sometimes seem artificial. For example, the train driver bows to the passengers every time he leaves the compartment. It makes sense to buy the tickets in the train station ticket office the day before your planned departure. You can also pay with your credit card here. It is also recommended that you print out the desired connection in advance via hyperDia.com to avoid possible misunderstandings (and the ticket itself should be written in English). The only downside: a ride on the Shinkansen definitely has its price.
Took the Shinkansen from Tokyo to Hiroshima and it was like I was flying on air. The trip was quick no fuss and provided a great view of the country. Highly recommend!

Comfortable, fast, perfectly on time... excellent then! However, there are some aspects that could be improved: the space for luggage (large suitcases) is only available above the seats; there is no power socket for the cell phone, there is no convenient catering service. However EXCELLENT and RECOMMENDED (with the JR Pass!).

If you travel by Shinkansen, you can be sure of the following things: 1. You will always drive exactly2. You will most likely drive at a speed you have never driven before3. The trip will definitely be your most expensive trip by train. Now, about the mistakes. But you also have to get off and get on in 3 minutes, and when the train is crowded and people are standing, it's not very easy, so before you get to the station, everyone is already getting off, and as quickly as possible, which is not very pleasant. It would be enough to limit the capacity of the carriage for passengers to be able to get off in peace. 3500 is not enough

If your 10 seconds late for the train don't bother rushing for it as its already departed. They are extremely punctual. We went for a day trip from Tokyo to Hiroshima. 4 hours on the express with 6 stops or there's an option for 6 hours where the train stops at every stop. The way I was told was why fire a bullet if you can see the bullet leave the barrel and travel. Pay the extra if it's an option in other words. They travel every 18 minutes the express are less regular. As for the experience as far as train journeys go it's a journey nothing really to report sorry to say. Very comfortable extremely clean. If I could improve anything I would want to know the speed of travel that could be advertised easily in the carriages. If your from foreign lands the JR pass is extremely useful (I didn't have this and it was costly) it will allow you to travel on the 6 hour service inclusive of your pass also will allow you to upgrade to the quicker service. GET THE JR PASS
Shinkanes is the most comfortable high speed train I used so far - it's extremely quiet, seats are very comfortable, lot of legroom and very polite train staff.

If you have to take a means of transport in Japan, it's the Shinkansen. The wagons are spacious, comfortable and very quiet. The smoking area is worth visiting, plus the train is punctual. We did the route from Tokyo to Kyoto, great. The SNCF should take example.

We are so glad there are so many revelers for “SHINKANSEN” as we really love to share our experiences too.. lolShinkansen are no ordinary trains but ‘bullet trains’ for good reason, JR’s shinkansen are the fastest and best-known services in Japan, the sight of just seeing one zip past is wow!. Especially useful when one travels long distance in Japan, they are much better than airplanes (and probably safer too!) w/o waste time going through all the checks.The Tokaido Shinkansen (東海道新幹線, Tōkaidō Shinkansen) is a shinkansen line that connects Japan's largest metropolitan areas of Tokyo/Yokohama, Nagoya and Osaka/Kyoto with each other.  We took the #522 Hikari from Shin-Osaka to Tokyo (Ikeburko).  Btw the Hikari class is the 2nd fastest speed train, only to Nozomi-category. We have to select the departure time well ahead, and NO change afterwhich.We checkin early to do some shopping inside the station and indeed much to grab as Osaka’s souvenirs, not to forget mentioning the unique station bento set!.   The bullet train arrived on the dot and as a hub we have slightly more time before it moves off to its next designation-stop.  It was a Reserved seat for Non-snoking.. It comes with far more legroom and much comfier chairs (recline a lot & footrest adjustable) than I’ve ever experienced on a flight. There are also toilets onboard. And the entire facilities are just great. Riding the shinkansen was indeed so relaxing as we alternate between reading and watching the Japanese countryside stream by outside the window.The whole journey was smooth and quiet, and only a couple of quick stops. It took just above  3hours where we alight at Shinagawa (JR Yamanote Line)Definitely recommended to at least try once.  We will try more often, if the cost can be lowered…..haha

There are three types of service: Nozomy, Kodama and Hikari. Depending on the name, they stop at more or fewer stations and cost more or less. They all have a Green Class category, which is our first class, but the price is significantly higher than the normal class. It is your usual transportation, therefore it is widely used and does not have many services added to the trip itself.  The best value is its frequency. Each train runs every 8/10 minutes and if you are not punctual you will miss it. When you get off, the same thing happens, they warn you about 2 minutes before getting off and you have 30 seconds. The queues at the station are rigorous and the entrances to the entrances where you must enter are drawn. Everything is very organized and it is not worth breaking the rules. It is quite an experience and no matter how much you use it, it will surprise you.  Shinkansen means "by another way" and they invented high speed.
What an amazing ride. Fast but extremely smooth. I hated our ride to end.  Train stations there run like clockwork.

I flew into Fukuoka international airport and took the shuttle bus to Hakata station.  Bought a ticket for the Shinkansen to Hiroshima.  Trains depart about every 20 mins in busy times. The trip took just over an hour.  A smooth, comfortable journey. On the return trip, I missed four bullet trains.  There is very little English at Hiroshima Station and by the time I found the right platform, two trains had already departed. My booked seat was invalid.  However, if you miss a bullet train booking, the front three carriages of any bullet train are for people with a ticket and no seat booking. I was able to use my ticket on a following train in carriages 1-3. Be warned - some of the bullet trains are so short in length, they do not reach the platform area marked for carriages 1-3. Two short trains flashed past before I could board the fifth one for Fukuoka. The bullet train is convenient but very expensive. Slower trains also operate on the tracks so it is worth enquiring about other options.

Travelled on the bullet train between Tokyo and Kyoto and also on a day trip from Kyoto to Hiroshima. I'm not the biggest fan of trains (as I travel on them every day in London!!), but this was an incredible experience. They are comfortable, efficient, clean and of course fast. One tip is to reserve your seats as if you don't you are not permitted to sit in one of the reserved carriages and they will charge you they find you sitting in one without a reservation.

From Toyohashi to Shinagawa, I used the Kodama non-reserved seat. It's not as good as Hikari/Nozomi, but I still thought it was fast enough and comfortable. And, depending on the section, it was quite crowded.

I travelled from Mishima to Kyoto and enjoyed the ride as it was smooth, silent and speedy.Definitely a must ride in Japan Bullet Train which is famous for it's punctuality(most trains depart on time to the second), Safety (only 2 incidents because of earthquake without any injury since 50+ years), comfort (relatively silent cars with spacious and always forward facing seats) and of coz operating speed with 320 km/h

If you love trains this is one amazing experience. Like the speed of light!!  So efficient, so clean. And, the conductor bows as he enters your compart,ment and again before he leaves.  Worth going all that way!!!

Rode the shinkansen from Tokyo to Kobe! The train itself is very fast, was able to reach my destination in less than 3hrs. Very comfortable, every seat has a huge space that you can just put your luggage in your area. Much more expensive than a plane ride but definitely a must try when in Japan! =)
I used it when going to Nagoya. There are some fun things to do, like looking at the scenery and eating Ekiben, but basically all you do is sleep.

An absolute must do while in Japan. If you are going alto a lot of places get the Japan Rail Pass to save money. Just google it. The train is so quiet and smooth. Signage is in English, and you wouldn't believe the amount of locals that will help you if you get lost. I highly recommend getting on the Shinkansen or Nozomi. Just go anywhere to experience it. You will be glad you did.
As always, when moving around Japan, I often use the Shinkansen, it’s much cheaper and faster than by car (unless of course you’re a company, and here you have to calculate)

I was able to make good use of the N700A series Hikari on a business trip from Osaka to Kyoto to Nagoya for 2 nights and 3 days. On the first day, I rode the nonstop Hikari 503 from Odawara to Nagoya, and transferred to the following Nozomi at Nagoya. On the evening of the second day, I took Hikari 478 from Kyoto and rode non-stop to Nagoya. On the last day, I rode Hikari 524, which was non-stop from Nagoya to Odawara. The Hikari train also uses the N700A series, making it possible to advance at the same speed as the following Nozomi train, making it more useful. There is also a Hikari train that stops at Odawara in the morning and evening, which is very convenient for me as I live along the Odakyu line.

We took the bullet train from Kyoto to Tokyo and were not disappointed!  The train ran bang on time and you would not know the speed it travelled at being quiet and comfortable throughout.  Train staff were so polite and it was a great pleasure to be with them

On time, efficient and comfortable ride from Tokyo to Toyota on the shinkansen, where there are push carts selling food , ice cream and drinks throughout the 3hrs ride. Remember to keep a lookout to the right of the train to have a glimpse of the beautiful Mount Fuji as we cruised by the area!
Very fast and pleasant way of moving. You can reserve your place(s) in advance or hope that there is room on the wagons that cannot be reserved.

We went from Tokyo (Shinagawa) to Kyoto using a ordinary JRPass on the Hikari. There are 2 classes ordinary and green. Green looks like business class on the plane and ordinary is like premium economy. There is plenty of leg room (twice as much as on the plane) and your chair goes right back without intruding on the person behind you too much. The seating configuration for ordinary is 3 x 2 and for green 2 x 2. They have phone/laptop chargers and pull down tray tables and a food cart came around twice with food to purchase. It took about 2.5 hours from Tokyo to Kyoto and the train was nice and smooth and quiet and did stop a couple of times along the way. There are also toilets onboard. The entire facilities are very clean.

I ride the Shinkansen several times a year, and it seems like Nozomi's time is getting shorter by a few minutes each year. On the other hand, Kodama takes longer to stop at each station. However, it is empty, so you can sit in non-reserved seats except during peak hours. Cars 1-7 are relatively crowded, so I always try to take cars 13-16.

Took the Hikari 467 bullet train from Tokyo JR station to Shin Osaka station with the JR green rail pass (reserved seating). Journey time was about 3 hours on a working day Tuesday morning so pretty empty and quiet which was good. Great to see the country side and train ride was smooth, fast and comfy although I sort of expected the train to go blurring fast being a bullet train but it didn't. Seats could recline, footrest adjustable, luggage rack above seats and all up hassle free ride next to window. It wasn't the non stop express train to Osaka (though that option was available) however there were loads of announcements to tell us where we were stopping, next stations etc so as not to miss our stop as the train was going further south to Okayama. Hostesses walk through carriage quite regularly offering food and drink at a price (and when you board hand out free hand wipes) though we had bought ours at Tokyo station kiosks on the platform prior to boarding. Loads of shops to stock up from inside the station as well. Separate carriages for reserved and non reserved seating passengers and all carriages are non smoking but there are designated smoking sections on few carriages. Overall good ride as expected though did pay quite a hefty price for the green pass.

We used the Shinkansen twice in our three weeks in Japan and it's the best way to travel long distances. Very smooth, fast and quiet. There's power outlets to use your laptop on the train. Great views as town after town fly past.
The title says it all. Dot on time, smooth ride, nice plush seats, availability of snacks during the trip were all superb.

Absolutely on time, clean and cozy - lots of space! Optimal way to explore Japan. With the Japan Rail Pass (order in Germany and redeem in Japan) it's also very cheap! It's best to reserve seats in advance at the JR counters in the train stations - it's free and staff usually speak very good English.

The Tokaido Shinkansen is punctual and has long operating hours, so I think it's more convenient to use than airplanes. The price is not much different than that of a plane, so if you want to save even a little bit, choose an unreserved seat. However, there are only a few seats available for non-reserved seats, so you may not be able to sit. If you want to sit down, it's better to think about lining up early or going outside during busy hours.

Who doesn't want to hurtle through Japan at extreme speeds?!? I loved the Shinkansen, it was comfortable, air conditioned and had power outlets. If you have a JR Rail Pass it is free. You can reserve seats which is great but you don't really need to! I highly recommend it!

The Tokaido Shinkansen connects the three major cities in Japan, Osaka-Nagoya-Tokyo. During your journey in Japan, you can go to different places. There are different types of trains. The location and frequency of each stop are different. Remember to check in advance.

We went on five different bullet trains during our trip. It is even better than I thought it would be. You have lots of leg room, the seats are comfortable and you can drink and eat as you whiz from city to city. We had a JR Rail Pass which was $462 for two weeks, arranged by our tour company. There are five speeds that certain bullet trains do. With the JR Pass you cannot go on the fastest. We did a variety but the Hikari 514 from Kyoto to Tokyo is apparently the second fastest. The trains glide into the stations with their long noses. Always on time to arrive and depart. You can buy many snacks at the station or even on the train. Each time then conductor enters and departs a rail car, they bow. Class!
Traveling on this train is great, an experience that everyone has to try. The trip is great. Punctuality and comfort. I loved the experience. We returned from Mount Fuji to Tokyo in 30 minutes.

Efficient, fast, quiet and comfortable - you couldn't ask for more!  Lining up at the station where your carriage number is printed on the ground, the train glides in to pick you up, matching carriage numbers exactly, and you just walk on and find your seat.  There is a smoking carriage on the train (yay!), or there is a smoking section in business class if you wish to pay extra.  A great way to travel in Japan.

Having an Express IC card allows you to reserve your seat online and make last-minute changes, which is very convenient. If you choose seat E, you can see Mt. Fuji. It depends on the weather that day.

Shinkansens - the perfect way to travel throughout Japan - the length and breadth, and even the height, if there was one! One takes the Japan Rail (JR) Pass and simply walks past the tailgates to board the trains. The JR Pass allows access to the Shinkansens which are your popular bullet trains and on regular JR specific trains. The bullet trains reach a speed of more than 350 kmph but don't seem so and are very comfortable and clean!

We travelled from Tokyo to Kanazawa.  The seats were comfortable and the journey pleasant.  We were disappointed that the windows were small and higher than we expected meaning that we could not see out so well.  This is surprising as most of the Japanese people are on the short side.  Also there are high barriers almost all along the train track - maybe to keep the noise in - which also impeded the view.  But it was still interesting to see Japan flying past the windows.  Quite flat heading out of Tokyo and LOADS of paddy fields.  Well worth the experience and of course you get to your destination very quickly!!!

It's a must do at least once in Japan! From the outside, the train speeds through the station at such a great speed! We almost had a shock the first time it sped past us. Once inside, it is a smooth and peaceful ride with great views to look at. There are smoking cabins so if you are sensitive to smoke, do take note and stay away from those cabins!

It's clean. It's fast. It goes from city centre to city centre without a two hour wait and security check. It's so punctual it is too good to be true. Stops are brief, at least that's what they say and believe me they are. And it is 50 years old. Who needs aircraft?

We took the Shinkansen from Osaka to Tokyo and then Tokyo to Kyoto. The train was very clean (they change the head covers/ aprons on each and every chair every time) and it arrives right on time.Just some quick tips: If you are using a Japan Rail Pass to ride the Shinkansen (bullet train), take note that you can only use cars 1 to 5 for unreserved seats, and if you are riding the Shinkansen from Tokyo to Kyoto, occupy the seats at the right hand side of the train to get the optimum view of Mt. Fuji. Conversely, take the seats on the left if you’re travelling from Kyoto to Tokyo.
A very comfortable ride you don't really have a sense of how fast you are travelling the train arrives and leaves bang on time

I have to admit to have been totally wowed by the Shinkansen train system in Japan. Being used to the UK rail network the Japanese train experience is something else completely. The train is spotless (as is Japan as a whole by the way) and when a train is due at a specific time it arrives at that time and leaves spot on time also.  Not a minute either way on time.  If you have a reserved seat - easy to do and recommended - the carriage door stops at the door marker on the platform where a small queue will have formed.  They stop exactly at the right spot every time.The journey is as smooth as flying in still air and again relating to the UK network one can easily have a coffee or tea at your seat with no spillage!Fast comfortable and a great way to travel around Japan.

Reserved seats are crowded at almost all times of the day, early in the morning, during the day, and in the evening. Early in the morning, you can use the IC Early Bird, so use the Green Car.There are 3 green cars, so if you take the Nozomi after 7am, or the temporary Nozomi even early in the morning, there will be fewer people, so it will be more comfortable.I definitely prefer the Shinkansen to the plane.

What a magical experience with the Shinkansen. We took it from Tokyo to Yokohama, again from Tokyo to Kyoto, from Kyoto to Himeji and all the way back, up to Takasaki and Utsunomiya. With the JR-Pass and a reservation for Green Car the experience cannot get better. Safe, fast and always on time.I fell in love with this super trains.
the trains are clean, spacious, and on time.  Quite a novelty for those of us in America with out third world rail system.  The ride from Tokyo to Kyoto was great.

Between Odawara and Yokohama. If you use the Tokaido Line, it will take you 60 minutes, but if you use the Shinkansen, it will take you about 20 minutes. It depends on where I'm going, but I like to travel this distance while standing in an unreserved seat.

Experiencing this punctuality, cleanliness and freedom of space in the ultra-modern Shinkasen trains makes me think of traveling by train in Germany with horror. Super organized processes that are second to none. Be sure to come along!

The N700A Shinkansen from Tokyo to Kyoto the Osaka to Tokyo was a MUST do trip and brought back fond memories of my one and only Concord flight from London to New York many years ago now. The Shinkansen is the Concord of the Railways. We reached almost the top speed of 300kph and the ride was very smooth and very quiet. In the past have been to Tokyo many times but never been prepared to spend the money on such a ride but was I glad I did this trip with my adult son. The trip has been special in many ways but this journey was really special and I felt like I was a kid again getting excited by the ride and taking video and pictures for my little grandson. I even went to a store and bought a mini shinkansen for him. Don't regret missing this just do it.  We just did reserved seats but next time we can try Green carriages (1st Class)

Great journey and very very glad to ride the Shinkansen! Reserving seats is easy. (Even when you don't speak Japanese.) there were English announcements too so you don't have to worry about missing your station. AND there is a trolley service that will sell you food and drinks (though it's cheaper to get the food at the stations).

My friends and I bought Shinkansen tickets at Osaka station at 2 pm. The train depart at 3:03 pm. 15 minutes before boarding the train, I found out that I had lost my ticket. I went back to the same booking clerk who I thought would be able to issue replacement with perhaps a small admin fee to pay. No such luck, I was obliged to buy a new ticket and had to pay the full fare of 14,550 yen. It's very easy to say "don't lose your ticket". Nobody wants to lose their tickets, but at least please be considerate. Moral of the story, don't lose your tickets in Japan.

Best option to go from one city to another! Comfortable and fast, it has on-board service (paid separately), spacious seats, sockets, bathrooms, bar. You have the option of purchasing the Japan Rail Pass where you just collect the ticket to go at the chosen time with assigned seats. There is also an option to buy individually and without reserved seats.
Very fast and worthwhile doing, however was very busy. Was great to do and am glad we have done it. Very fast.

Coming from the uk we are resigned to old cramped and dirty trains. The total opposite to the Shinkansen. So much space...so comfortable...so quiet...so clean. Oh yes and on time.Brilliant experience from Tokyo to Kyoto

Punctuality and speed from the airport. When you travel inside it it seems to go slowly but the moment another shinkansen passes by the train rocks and that's when you realize you're going very fast. The cost of the Jr pass is only convenient if your itinerary is full of trips outside Tokyo. It allowed us to do the Kyoto-Himenji return trip in a single day (for us the last day in Japan); Kyoto-Fuji inari shrine round trip; Kyoto-Tokyo. Crazy experience but thanks to the shinkansen.

The train from Nagasaki to Hakata was a beautiful older train with wooden floors and leather seats in the first class compartments. We took the train from Nagasaki to Tokyo and then on to Sapporo. It was a very nice way to see a bit more of Japan and not only Cities. We got a chance to watch the landscape change as each area is very different. We had 3 weeks to travel around Japan, if you have the time well worth it.

Coming from a city and country where public transport has never been a high priority for those in power, travelling on the shinkansen is an absolute joy.  Watching them glide into a station is a delight, especially as you know exactly where each door and carriage will be (particularly handy if you need a non-reserved carriage).Using a JR pass is the best way to get value out of using the shinkansen, as they are not cheap to pay for on their own.  I took several trips for no other reason than I wanted a spot to use my laptop and I didn't want to buy another coffee, so I got to see more of the Japanese countryside at the same time.The Tokaido line has shinkansen traversing it every few minutes, so it's incredibly easy (and quick) to travel from Tokyo westwards towards Shin-Osaka.  Depending on how much you've paid or which JR pass you have, most trains will have at least 6 carriages.  It's possible to have no luck finding a seat, as the trains are extremely popular.I am certain that on my next trip to Japan, I'll possess a JR pass and there will be many trips on the shinkansen, which make Australian trains feel like snails.

This was the fastest and most convenient option for me and my family to travel from Tokyo to Osaka. We chose the Nozomi Shinkansen as it had the least number of stops and only took 3 hours from Tokyo station to Shin Osaka station. The train was clean and the seats comfortable. Seats were arranged in a 3-2 configuration with overhead luggage space. Over-sized luggage were kept in the back of the car behind the last seats. There is no on train entertainment so be sure your gadgets are charged or have something to read. Also food options are limited and a bit expensive (I paid 900 yen for a coffee and a sandwich). Best to bring food for the trip (I suggest trying the sushi and bento boxes sold at the train station).Toilets, wash basins and, trash bins are located in between train cars.I got tickets on-line and had reserved seats weeks before my trip. However, it didn't seem like it would have been hard to purchase tickets on the day of our trip itself,even though it was smack in the middle of Japan's Golden week holidays.

A great train which is always on time, at high speed, journey times in "normal" trains are divided by 2, an impeccable mobile catering service offering bentos in particular, seats which can be adjusted and which allow you to sleep comfortably throughout the journey. You can visit Japan by shinkasen without problem and in complete safety for a completely affordable price thanks to the unlimited tourist pass! Recommended without the slightest hesitation!

We have booked Shinkansen from Kyoto to Tokyo (around 2 hours, 18.690JPY/ticket for reserved seats  in Green Car - First Class). Shinkansen is very quiet, comfortable and clean ! Don't forget to buy a Bento box to experiment Japanese style.It is also very convenient to deliver your big luggage from hotel to hotel to travel lighter (24H, around 1200JPY per luggage for finding it in your next hotel room).We did not find a way to buy tickets in advance from Europe, but it is so easy to buy it directly in Japan... (many trains from Kyoto to Tokyo, every 10 or 15 minutes at rush times).Green cars are very comfortable (Gran Class ticket not available on  the Tokyo/Kyoto line).
I took this train for about 1 hour from Hakone to Tokyo, a wonderful feeling, from a fast ride, there are also smoking boxes in the carriages
I use it often.I always drive the green car and it is stable and comfortable. I really like the hand towels you get when you ride.

Unlike the Netherlands, traveling by public transport in Japan is not a punishment. The Shinkansen always runs on time, is clean on the inside and you are not bothered by people calling or having to turn on their phone boxes if necessary. Impressive how many trains depart per hour. Please note that you do not take Nozomi trains if you have a Japan rail pass. You can use Kodama and Hikari trains.

If it's between Tokyo and Osaka, you'd be confused about flying. Airplanes are cheaper if you buy early. However, considering the boarding procedures and the need to arrive with plenty of time to board, it's hard to give up on the Shinkansen. You can also charge your smartphone. The Shinkansen is a great way to relax while eating your lunch.

Have you ever found yourself wasting your reserved seat ticket because the train you were on was delayed and you couldn't get on the connecting train? I learned for the first time that in such cases, if you apply at the station where you get off, you can receive a considerable amount of refund. Yesterday, Shirasagi No. 56 from Kanazawa stopped at Awara Onsen Station due to strong winds and its service was suspended for a while, resulting in a 20-minute delay in arriving at Maibara Station, making it impossible to board Hikari No. 516, which was a connecting train, and Hikari No. 464, which was connecting to Nagoya. Following the announcement inside the Shirasagi train, I boarded the following Kodama 650 from Maibara, but the reserved seats on the Kodama were full, so I decided to take a non-reserved seat. Nowadays, people tend to buy limited express trains with a reservation, but even though the reserved and green seats were full, the non-reserved seats on the Kodama were surprisingly empty, and we arrived safely at Hamamatsu Station with no standing seats. When exiting the ticket gate at Hamamatsu Station, I suddenly wondered what would happen to the difference in price for a reserved seat in such a case? I had a curious question, so I asked the station staff, and they asked me if I had to wait more than 10 minutes.They spread out a number of fax-like documents on the floor and continued to investigate.They told me that I could get a refund, and I was given a refund of 4,520 yen (I think it was) for my elementary school student. Since the delay was less than 2 hours, I was very surprised as I thought that at best I would have to pay the difference in price for a reserved seat. When I looked into it later, it seems that I was refunded half of the limited express fare for all sections of the Shirasagi Shinkansen + the equivalent of the Shinkansen reserved seat fare. At the counter, there was also a woman who had come on the same train from Kanazawa and was also waiting for a refund because she had asked the conductor or the station staff at Maibara Station. I was surprised that I was completely unaware of the fact that there was a system for such large refunds, and that if I didn't ask, my ticket would be taken back and I would be left with nothing. In this case, perhaps because it was a long holiday, I was able to get a refund even if I didn't have Shirasagi's delay certificate just by verbally telling them my departure time from Kanazawa Station, but I'm still worried that depending on the station (or depending on the station staff who happened to respond) they might not be able to give me a refund because I didn't have a delay certificate. Since there is no time to make individual inquiries at the counters at transit stations, I think it would be a good idea to automatically issue delay certificates to all transit passengers as soon as the transit train departs.What do you think? It was a rare opportunity, so I learned a lot. Both of them felt that it was unfair that when it comes to refunding money, whoever asks wins. If your train is delayed due to JR circumstances, it may be a good idea to ask first before handing over your ticket. By the way, in this case, I reserved the ticket in advance at JR West Japan's e5489 and issued it at the ticket vending machine at Kanazawa Station. Tickets purchased at travel agencies such as JTB or discount tickets may be handled differently. Also, there was a special situation where I was only able to get a non-reserved seat because the reserved seats on the following train were full.

We have been talking for a long time about this Japanese TGV which has reached almost 500 km/h Unfortunately on a "cruise" it hardly exceeds 300 km/h but what comfort, what silence You are a group, no problem, the seats rotate 180° for easy face to face 10 minutes at the station to clean and when I say clean, no joke, it's from top to bottom, even the headrests are changed, the seats dusted, the floors swept, the toilets disinfected. In addition, the staff who pass during the journey with a smile would teach many lessons to our sad SNCF
Shinkansen is a high-speed train. Convenient travel, fast travel time, save time, sit comfortably, enjoy the view along the road. Good service staff

We used the Shinkansen trains to travel to many destinations between Tokyo and Hiroshima. We had purchased a two week pass prior to our arrival in Japan and used this whenever possible in the cities that we visited. We took the cheapest option and found the trains to be clean, frequent and always on-time. We found it easy to use the Hyperdia website to plan our trips (particularly useful when linking connecting city trains with the Shinkansen - be aware that some stations are labelled Shin first eg. Shin-Osaka  when looking for routes). If you have a Japan Rail pass you can go into a JR station and book seats for free, however it is also ok to ride on the train without a reservation as long as you show your JR pass at the gate and only get onto the cars labelled as unreserved (often cars 1-3, or 1-5). This means that you may not get a seat, however that would be unusual. The advantage of choosing unreserved cars is that you can hop on the first train arriving at the platform and not waste time waiting in line for reserved tickets.Railway staff all over Japan tend to be very helpful and accommodating even if they don't speak much English. Information on train departures is provided on digital screens which rotate between English and Japanese. We worked out that you need to look for the shape (eg. Triangle, circle) on the sign to know where to stand and wait for your train (This system is used to allow for multiple trains arriving on the same track within a short space of time.) The trains have power sockets but no wifi yet. It is ok to eat on the train and toilets were very clean. The Shinkansen train stations in the major cities are huge with multiple shopping centres located nearby. All stations were wheelchair, luggage and stroller friendly with elevators and escalators everywhere. All stations we visited had coin lockers so you can deposit your luggage for a small fee and go and visit a tourist site en route to your next destination - of course the smaller the luggage the greater chance you have of obtaining a suitable sized locker. Whilst not as fast as other trains around the world now, all up we found the Shinkansen train system to be efficient and easy to use and would recommend it as an effective way of touring around Japan.

Domestic travel is basically by plane. When traveling from Tokyo to Nagoya, or if you have time, use the Shinkansen. The good thing is that the time is accurate and you can see the scenery around you while riding. Shinkansen usage increases during the cherry blossom season.

Took the Nozomi Shinkansen from Hiroshima to Tokyo on a bright sunday afternoon and reached Tokyo in 4 hours.  The ride was smooth and un-interrupted.   Tickets were easy to get at the station 20 minutes before the train departure.   Stations are clean.   Rode on the First Class Green Car.   This is where the novelty ends.  I rode bullet trains in other countries at similar speeds, efficiency and punctuality.   The punctuality is built in as the track is elevated with no obstructions.  There is no free meals or drinks in First class as in other countries.   The attendant walks around with refreshments and requires payments.  The is no attempt from the attendant to help you with purchases.   They always smile without trying to sell you anything.    Language is an issue too.   Even water is not free.  The seats in first class were clean but old.  The upholstery shows wear.   Now, with many countries having fresh bullet train systems being built, the shinkansen may turn out be a dinosaur.  Just the way things work out.   A new attraction needs to be discovered.

I have used it several times on business trips. I wanted to use my PC to create documents and check emails while I was on the move, so I designated a seat with a 100V outlet at the counter. The person at the counter was also happy to help me find it.

On time and fastYou can buy a week long or two week tick from outside country and then reserve seatsLoads of space to stretch legs, put suitcases upAnnouncements in Japanese and English - scrolling text about station is only English when at stationsNo free wifiToilets on boardSeats recline more than airplanes do!Space for wheelchair Power for laptop and mobile phones at every widow seatHave a rest and let the miles fly by
It is the Japanese bullet train, equivalent to the Spanish AVE. Clean, fast and very punctual. Recommended for traveling long distances, if you have a budget.

We bought our 7 day JR passes and used them extensively in our trip to Japan in April 2016. We travelled by the JR Shinkansen when we made a day trip visit to Kyoto and back to Tokyo in the evening and another time when we went to Hakone ( Mount Fuji ). We made reservations so we were in the carriage with confirmed seat numbers.  The trains are all very punctual, right to the minute. Inside, the trains are very clean and the seat comfortable with a lot of leg room. It was also good that they sell snacks and drinks. We bought some coffee and a pack of sandwich which was quite reasonably priced. If you need a full meal, would recommend that you pack a bento box from the convenient store in the train stations, where you would have more variety. The trains were very fast as we reached Kyoto which is more than 500 km away in about 2 hours 20 minutes.  This is better that taking a flight as it is far more comfortable. This nice experience is one of the highlights of our trip to Japan.

The journey to Platkodama takes time but is cheap. Recommended for people who want to enjoy their time on the go. You can also ride the green car for an additional 1,500 yen (Tokyo to Kyoto). The car bodies differ depending on the time of day, so if you want an outlet, you should aim for the N700 series. There are no on-board sales, so please purchase the necessary drinks and food before boarding.
Very clean, fast, comfortable, and very punctual trains. Especially interesting with the Japan rail pass.
Good way to travel, the station is clean and has clear signage. Recommended way to travel around Japan.

I took it 4 times for the return routes between Tokyo-Kyoto and Kyoto-Hiroshima and I had a great time on all occasions. Very punctual (small delay of 4 minutes for the last route but here in Italy it's pure science fiction), so much so that it splits the minute, they stop exactly in the right place on the platforms (like all trains in Japan) and have very comfortable and spacious seats. Whenever a crew member enters and exits a carriage, they also bow! Instructions on the stops to be made are given via loudspeaker in both Japanese and English.

seen the bullet train many times on TV, however this was my first journeys. Very helpful staff on the train, station signs on moving digital display in English (eventually, wait for the rotation).Bought a standard ticket from a manned booth at Narita airport. Very easy.on my return from Kyoto, I decided to use the Green car and buy a ticket a machine. Beware, as well as the green car ticket, you need to get a standard journey one as well (I didn't and got sent blocked by the ticket barrier)Green cars are much more comfortable, standard cars a bit basic, however you can change the seat angle in both

The bullet train is like flying on the ground. The best part is that you get to see lots on the way rather than just clouds. We splurged for green tickets which are larger seats and quieter but the unreserved seats looked pretty comfortable too. The carriages are clean and large and the seats very comfortable. There is a small food cart with drinks and snacks including very yummy sandwiches. We literally went from the airport by taxi to Shinagawa station where we purchased our tickets and got on. Despite many blogs saying we needed to book. All up a great experience

When one of these passes you it does so with a whoosh!  A starling whoosh.  The trains are very fast, very comfortable and clean with lots of leg room.  We did not reserve a seat and this did not present a problem on our sector.  One observation though, of all the fast trains, the TGV in France seems to quieter and smoother inside the cabin than the Shinkansen.

For our 10 day tour through Japan, we bought a rail pass (1st class) which probably the best choice for foreigners to getting around in Japan. We travelled between Tokyo, Kyoto and Osaka, (with a number of stops and other local trains in between). The trains (and stations) are always very tidy, and from the outside are absolutely high-tech. Entering the trains however, puts you back into the late 20th century, with the only amenity being a power socket. Even in 1st class, there is no Wi-Fi, no USB charger and no other amenity and we felt that the giant brown seats appeared strangely outdated. It would have been nice to be offered a drink or snacks, but it seems that this comes at an extra cost. There is no dining car on the trains, and luckily we just had bought our Bento box before boarding the train. On the plus side, travelling in these trains is very comfortable as the rails are extremely well balanced and there is nearly no vibration or shaking of the trains, even at highest speed (which I estimated at 300 km/h). I think the French TGV, the Italian Frecce rossa or the German ICE are ahead in terms of comfort and service. Technologically the Shinkansen may be ahead of the European counterpart

Tickets on the right side are more expensive going from Tokyo to Osaka, which we did.  The reason being that Fujijama is on that side.  Unfortunately we missed the holy mountain as it was shrouded in clouds that day.  2,5 hours from Tokyo to Osaka?  Yeah, anytime, thank you.  You can buy drinks and snacks on board.

We left our hotel at 1045, took the train at Maihama Station for our 1 pm train to Osaka. Ticket sales said it's an 18 min ride to Tokyostation. We planned to explore a bit at Tokyo City Station, sadly, due to strong winds, the JR train stopped for soooo long, as the winds were moving the train cars! We waited until it was safe for the train to go...we reached Tokyo station 1:15 pm and were advised that the 1:00 pm train has already left. We were told we can go to the non reserved seat train by 1:30.And good thing it was a Sunday...They have coffee and snacks sold inside the train...Toilets are cleanLeg room is more than sufficient. Luggages can be placed in an overhead rack...Yes, they (staff) understand English but they will answer you in Japanese but after that they will tell you the number of your (platform, car, gate) in English. So, take time to listen ...

Taken from Kyoto to Hiroshima and back. For this 380 km route there are two options with all or just some stops, so it takes either 1h 45m or 2h 20m. Wide seats and spaced rows make it very comfortable. Extremely punctual and rigorous in the stops at the station.

The Japanese bullet train is the equivalent of the Spanish AVE. They have several carriages without seat reservations, which allows you to skip the ticket office if you have Japan Rail (or if you want to save some money). If you have room, perfect. If not, you can go standing (it doesn't feel uncomfortable). "First come, first seat." On the platforms they give you marks so that you queue exactly at the door of the corresponding car. Extremely punctual, with very wide seats, even if there are rows of 3 seats. It reaches up to about 300 km/h. In any case, the AVE has nothing to send to these trains.

Between Tokyo and Shin-Osaka, I don't really want to ride during business hours for both non-reserved and reserved seats... It's fine as long as there are seats available, but when it's crowded, it feels like a chore to get up from your seat. The seats are as cramped as economy class on an airplane, so I find it difficult to settle down and hope that no one is sitting next to me...However, during business hours (especially on the last train), there are many passengers getting on and off at Nagoya, Kyoto, Shin-Osaka, and Okayama, so I can't say that. If you're looking for comfort, I think it's best to take a green car or during a free time, such as in the early afternoon. As for the green car, the seats are comfortable and the attendant's service is very relaxed, making you want to come back again and again! !

A nice station of the JR line. At this station in Tokyo, white roller coasters run for 300 km. They go up to speed. They do not reach this speed over short distances. The seats were comfortable and beautiful.

I experienced the Shinkansen from Tokyo to Kyoto (3 hours), and from Kyoto to Osaka (30mins). The trains were punctual, and clean with comfortable seats (plenty of leg room). Also, a thoughtful gesture was that there was a power socket at every seat, so you can charge your electrical devices while en route to your destination. The snack cart is reasonably well-stocked with mineral water, coffee, milk tea and light snacks. When the train conductor (I think) conducts his checks, he will first stand at the front of the car, make an announcement (in Japanese about what I assumed to be the train destination, and that he would be coming around to inspect your tickets), and bow deeply before proceeding to every seat to ask for your ticket. I found this a simple but very meaningful gesture, and made for a memorable experience. The Shinkansen tickets may be a little expensive, but saves on travel time. Use the JR pass. if you're on the Tokyo-Osaka route, be alert at about the halfway mark - you'll get to see the revered Mount Fuji out of the right hand window!

Having bought a return ticket on the Nozomi Toyko to Osaka express last week for about Yen 22,000, if you're visiting Japan and intending to travel around the country, it makes sense to get a Rail Pass. But which one do you get? The price of the one week Japan Rail pass is about Yen 29,000 for the Ordinary carriage and Yen 38,000 for the Green (effectively First Class) carriage (Apr 2016). Do you pay the extra for the extra comfort? Having bought both ordinary and green passes over the years, I'd suggest the following:-a) If you're just going on Shinkasen (bullet) trains, buy the Ordinary pass. In these carriages, the seat configuration is 2 seats and 3 seats either side of the aisle, which is good for a family of three. There is ample, really ample, leg room. The arm rests lift up and the seat pitch is excellent. This compares to the Green car which has the same ample leg room, the same pitch, but is a 2 seats 2 seats configuration. This may sound like more space but the seats have arm fixed rests which feel quite constrictive and they also have a foot rest, which gets in the way.b) The Green pass is really good when you catch the novelty trains or travel on routes outside the Shinkasen lines. I recall one train having fresh flowers in the aisle and a stewardess giving out refreshing hand towels.So, my suggestion is look at your intended route before deciding on what pass to get.

The Taiwan High Speed ​​Rail is essentially the little brother or sister of the Japanese high-speed rail network. Even though, strictly speaking, it is not even a "network", but only serves a single route (along the entire west coast of the country), only slightly modified Japanese technology is used (among other things, the route is served with modified N700 Shinkansen multiple units), and operationally, a lot has apparently been copied from the Japanese. It was probably the best decision by the Taiwan transport authority, instead of the European rail solution that was originally envisaged In the end, we have to resort to the offer from Japan, because in terms of operation and comfort, the level of Japanese high-speed trains is almost reached here. The trains are divided into 11 cars of the second class and one car of the first ("business") class, with 3+2 seating in the second and 2+2 seating in the first class. Each row of seats faces in the direction of travel (the rows of seats are rotated at the end stations) and also has its own window, making it easy to choose a good seat. 9 of the 12 cars per train can only be used with seat reservations (which can also be purchased shortly before one of the closely scheduled departures for a marginal surcharge), the remaining 3 cars have free choice of seats. The fact that the trains run on a similar level of punctuality as in Japan is not surprising given a very similar operating concept, and although the design and comfort of the interior are a little weaker than in Japan, there are two aspects in which the THSR is a little ahead of its Japanese model has: On the one hand, the fare for a given route is always the same, regardless of whether you use one of the express trains with few stops in between or one of the slower trains with stops at every station, and on the other hand, every first class passenger who boards is served a drink (coffee, tea, water, juice) and a small snack (pastries or salty nibbles). In addition, food and drinks can also be purchased from the on-board staff in all classes. What is also very positive is the fact that train tickets can be purchased not only at train stations, but also in practically all convenience stores (e.g. 7-Eleven) - this saves you a lot of walking if you want to buy your ticket in advance. Strangely, the ride back to Taipei felt bumpier and perhaps it was due to this that the train could not travel faster.On all sections, the trains were fully occupied and many passengers had luggage with them that they parked in the luggage area, which ensured the cabins were free of rolling or sliding bags. There were even vending machines and Nursing Rooms!With the HSR, I was able to make the trip from Taipei in the North all the way South to Kaohsiung and back in one day.  What an experience!I would recommend the HSR as an alternative to flying around Taiwan or even taking a coach.  It is quick and comfortable and certainly not expensive.
