Seats are super comfortable with plenty of legroom. If you have bigger pieces of luggage there is space at either end of each carriage for those items.As other fellow reviewers pointed out if you would like a reserved seat or a guaranteed spot on the HSR it might be safe to book ahead of time.All in all, I really love travelling by HSR and will do so again soon.

The HSR took over most of the regular train system in Taiwan for faster and much easier accessibility. The airport MTR linked directly to the HSR station in Taoyuan for easy transit to southern Taiwan. We took the very first train from Taoyuan to Chiayi on our most recent trip and had a pleasant ride without too much hassle. The only thing is that I wish the luggage racks are bigger to accommodate more large bags that the passengers are bringing on the train.

I went back and forth between Taipei and Kaohsiung. I couldn't choose my own reserved seat. There was little shaking, and there were many people eating lunch in their cars. There are also on-board sales. Apparently they use Japanese Shinkansen trains, and the inside of the train looked exactly like that. The legroom is also wide.

Took the HSR twice during our Taipei visit. Train is fast, smooth and clean. Note that if you aren't a regular commuter and don't reserve ahead, the same-day ticketing typically involves non-reserved seats (which meant sitting in cars 10-12). That's fine, but just be aware and to plant yourself at the right place when waiting to board.  Also, plan well your time to arrive/ticket/get to the platform. Will add to your efficiency. The HSR trains run regularly thru the day but not as regularly as the Metro Trains.

I took Taiwan HSR from Taoyuan to Kaohsiung. I travelled with business class carriage. The seats are wider than regular seats only 4 seats in a row instead of 6 seats ( in regular carriage). Train is clean, quiet and fast. There are power point fitted with each chair. There is compulsory light refreshments and drink. The only thing I would like to see is free wifi but unfortunately no service available. This is the easiest and quickest way to go between Taipei and Kaohsiung.

We took this train from Taichung to Nangang.  With senior discount, the fare was very reasonable and it was fast.  The seats were very comfortable for the distance traveled.  I cannot think of a better way to travel in Taiwan!

We took the High Speed Rail between Taipei and Zuoying, Kaohsiung. THSR is the Taiwan version of Japanese Shinkansen. The 700T is exactly the same as Shinkansen and Non-reserved seat is available so we don't have to rush for a designated train. Train runs every 15 minutes but some call at more stations, take a look at the passenger screen for detail. The whole journey only take 2 hours. Don't forget to grab an Ekiben (Station Bento) like you do in Japan, they are cheap (HKD$25), delicious, healthy and only sold between 1030 and 1300 and a few hours at night. Although TRA also sell bento but I prefer the HSR version. Fare is only half of the Shinkansen but the quality is same as Japan. Unlike China you don't have to pass through security check, waiting room, ticket checks and oversized station in Taiwan, stations are simple and easy to use just like taking a metro and people are well mannered. The only downside is most of the intermediate stations are quite far away from city centre and need a transfer to local trains or buses. Beware station names are different for TSA and HSR although they are the same station.

It takes about 2 hours from Taipei to Kaohsiung on the Taiwan High Speed ​​Rail. I don't feel any difference in the interior or ride comfort from the Japanese Shinkansen I'm used to riding. The room is also relatively quiet. Last time I came here on a business trip, I asked the local staff to arrange tickets for me, but this time I was sightseeing, so I tried to do it on my own. Since I used a foreign passport, I was able to travel cheaply, quickly, and comfortably.

The business class seats are large and have independent lighting and sockets, but unfortunately there is no USB power supply. Newspapers, simple snacks and tea are provided. It is recommended to drink hot coffee. The high-speed rail provides illy coffee.

It's difficult to buy tickets. I was finally able to buy it after being told about it by a local. It's also difficult to understand how to get on the train, there are no unreserved seats, and you don't have to have a reserved seat ticket to be seated. However, if the person you specified comes, you will have to give it up. It wasn't very pretty.

Compared with high-speed rail in other countries, Taiwan’s high-speed rail fares are indeed cheaper. If you don’t mind, you can spend a little more money to upgrade to business class, where the seats are larger and wider, and snacks and drinks are provided for free.

We took the HSR from Taipei to Taichung. Very good service Taipei main station clean with good facilities and comfortable waiting area. The HSR is also clean comfortable and convenient. A good way to travel

This was our first experience with High Speed Rail and I must say the experience is mind blowing. The station is very clean, staff is attentive, and schedule is on point. The train arrived as scheduled as would be expected. The interior is well kept, there was a place for your large luggage at the end of each car, and overhead storage is available for smaller carryons. The speed of travel was mesmerizing and you barely notice how fast you travel until you look out the window. Ticket cost was about $50 for adults and half for children. It was worth the experience and would do it again next time we visit Taipei.

This is one section from Banqiao to Taoyuan. It cost more than double what it would cost to live normally, but it was still around 1,500 yen. I took the opportunity to ride in business class, or what they call a green car in Japan. It's truly a green car. General trains have a 2+3 Shinkansen arrangement, while business trains have a 2+2 Shinkansen arrangement. It has a power source and is spacious enough. The room next door is empty and comfortable. Also, at the Shinkansen Green, you only get towels, but they also serve coffee and sweets. I'm a little happy. A long time ago, there was a free drink service on the Green express train in Hokkaido. Even in the first class of the Italian Shinkansen, sweets and water were provided. It's a bit of a luxurious time.
I went to Tainan using a 3-day tourist pass. Get off at Songshan Airport, take a taxi to Nangang, and then take a taxi from Tainan Station to the hotel. It took a lot of time and money.

Purchased ticket via klook. Very Efficient and we were able to save a lot of time from Taipei to Taoyuan Airport. You just have to show the voucher and claim the pass. Most convenient way to go back to the Airport

First time using Taiwan's Shinkansen from Taipei to Taichung. I was looking forward to riding the Japanese Shinkansen as it was introduced. Tickets can be reserved from Japan and can be booked at a discount, so it's a great deal. I booked with 20% discount. Since I made the reservation by entering my passport number, I will need to present my passport when issuing the ticket. This time, I didn't want to be tied to the return time, so I only reserved the ticket for Taichung, and on the way back, I bought it at the counter on the spot. It seemed to be quite popular and I was able to get a reserved seat on the Shinkansen, which departed in 40 minutes. I can't say enough about the Shinkansen that the ride is so comfortable! I wish I could ride it more (*^^*)

We took the train from the airport to the main station. Good signage and direction. The staff at the ticketing booth were very friendly and gave good advice so we got best value for money tickets. Easy to navigate and on time. The trains were Clean and the seats were quite comfortable. Friendly staff. Great value for money.

The Shinkansen cars are made in Japan (Kobe), and even though the distance between Taipei and Kaohsiung (Zuoying) is about the same as Tokyo and Nagoya (Tokaido Shinkansen), I felt that the Taiwan Shinkansen was faster. When the maximum speed was reached, the electronic display board inside the car displayed ``300 km/h,'' making it easy to tell.

Very convenient with fair price! You can enjoy the North to South Taiwan by HSR through west. It saves you tons of time and gives you a very comfortable trip. Much better than taking a train. Very convenient and affordable! You can take the high-speed rail from the west of Taiwan to travel from north to south. Taiwan's high-speed rail can save you a lot of time and provide you with a very comfortable journey. It's so much better than taking the train.
I was little worried how to go from Taipei to the south , but using it make it ease , the only thing I did not like I had to go on the bus from the airport to the station , which was not marked well

I used it from Taichung Station to Taipei Station in December last year. On the day of the event, the seats reserved for the evening were full and the non-reserved seats were extremely crowded. After that, I went to Grand Hyatt Taipei.
It took me 10min from hotel to high speed train station, then i went to Gaoxiong, and have a day trip back!

Don't choose a train that stops at every station, otherwise it will take a long time and be very tiring. Not every carriage of the high-speed train has a power socket. In addition, please turn off your mobile phone while riding the train and be polite.

Public transport in Taiwan is top notch and the HSR is no exception. If you're travelling on the western side of the country, this is the way to do it quickly and efficiently.  In the past couple of years, additions to the metro have been made so that you can hop onto the MRT right from the HSR if you need to head to the airport.   These changes have made travel around Taiwan very intuitive (even for English speakers).

In addition to 50% off coupons for company employees, some companies that cooperate with high-speed rail also provide 20% off coupons. As for the general public, if they can plan their itinerary in advance, they can also go to the official website to order early bird tickets at 40% off, 20% off, 10% off and other preferential prices to purchase travel tickets online. Foreign tourists can purchase two-day or three-day passes on kkday and klook to enjoy unlimited rides within the specified date.
On time, fast, very clean, and reasonable costGreat way to travel. Saves a lot of time when compared to traveling in a car.

Even though the interior layout and the feel and sound of the toilets are almost the same as the Shinkansen in Japan, the price is less than half the price for the same distance, so I'm not surprised or impressed, but it feels like a great deal. Still, to go from downtown Taipei to Taoyuan Airport, you need to change to the subway at Taoyuan Station, and this subway doesn't run very often, so I feel like it would be faster to take one subway from the beginning.

The usage is the same as the Shinkansen in Japan. The difference is that there is a baggage space and the seats are a little wider. Japan's Shinkansen trains have no baggage space, so inbound tourists have a hard time.

I went to Taipei for 2 nights and 3 days on a company trip. I wanted to go to Biryo Island subway station, which is said to be the second most beautiful station in the world, so I decided to use the convenient and reasonable 3-day free pass after planning a free plan. Although Beauty Island is located in Kaohsiung, it is also possible to get off at Taichung and sightsee, which was an effective way to efficiently enjoy Taiwan, which stretches from north to south. I booked a ticket in advance through JTB, and at the local ticket office, I was able to exchange and reserve a ride without having to speak broken English.Even though I'm a woman in my mid-50s, I was able to enjoy it without hesitation even on my own.

I hadn't thought about traveling from Taipei to Taichung or Tainan until now, but I bought a 3-day pass for foreigners at a local travel store and used it for 2 days, which was very convenient. I was able to sightsee without any problems while staying in Taipei. I thought it would take longer, but it arrived surprisingly quickly. I would like to use it again when I travel.

Every time in Taipei I use the high speed train, I always order the business class ticket:Coffee, wet towel, cookies are served during your trip. Power for chargers available too, comfortable seat as well. Super in time, just perfect.

There is a large shopping mall just outside the station, with convenient functions nearby. It is connected to the MRT/Taiwan Railway and other hubs. Shops, restaurants, and movie theaters are all available in the shopping mall. It is the northernmost high-speed rail station in Taiwan and you don’t have to worry about running out of seats if you buy free seats.

Took the HSR from Taipei to Tainan and back again. My husband and I did business class seating because we were coming from a long flight or going to one and wanted to be sure to stretch out. There certainly is a lot of room to do so. The conductors and staff are very friendly and fluent in English. Their snacks are diverse as well. Loved that it was fast and efficient way to travel.

This is my second time riding the Shinkansen, and it's as comfortable as the Shinkansen in Japan, and runs on time. It's a bit disappointing that there aren't many places to put your luggage. There are also on-board sales, so it's fun and makes you feel like you're on a journey.

Traveled by Taiwan's HSR on 11th September, a very satisfying experience. Am thoroughly impressed by its punctuality, cleanliness, and announcements. Even if it is a 2 hours ride to the destination, at the end of each journey, each and every  compartment, is cleaned, including the folding table. Helpful and friendly staff.

The High Speed Rail is THE way to travel Taiwan's west coast. Speedy, punctual and fun.Reservation can be made via internet prior to arriving in Taiwan. You may face some trouble when you are asked to type in your passport number: For foreign passports that to not fit the usual scheme, solution is to type in your passport number PLUS your birthdate in four digits (month/day). That information is a bit hidden on HRS's booking page. Once successfully reserved and paid, you need to get your ticket prior to departing. That can be done at the train station, or at any 7/11. But be aware: The 7/11 ticket machines work in Chinese only, not in English. So if you are not fluent in reading Chinese you may need someone to help you - or go to the train station.The train itself is excellent: Speedy, punctual, and great fun to get to the south so quickly. You may want to consider to go business class, as this makes the ride even more comfortable.In case you go from Taipei to Tainan: The Tainan HRS is a little out of town, but either the metro/train takes you to the city, or a taxi ride which is quick and not too expensive

Love how it saves my time in traveling between Taipei and Kaohsiung. Considering all aspects (WiFi, food service, restroom, cleaners, spacious seats), this is definitely a great transportion option to go for. Just wish that they will lower the ticket price soon...
It's excellent, but expensive. Fast, convenient. It's much too packed at times. At times tickets sold out.
Taiwan High Speed ​​Rail is reliable transportation in Taiwan. With this fast train, we can move cities quickly, saving a lot of time. The price is also cheap and very comfortable.

If you have never travelled on a high speed train, this is well worth the experience. The service was efficient and frequent. We travelled from Taipei to Tainan for a day trip, and it went smoothly. HSR also provided a free shuttle bus service through Tainan. A return ticket from Taipei to Tainan was NT&2700 for standard reserved seating. As there are services every 20 minutes probably no need to pre book, as tickets are cheaper if bought on demand. We took the Business class tickets for an additional NT$650 one way. It was well worth the extra cost for the extra wide seats and leg room.

We took a trip from Taipei to Tainan by HSR. We bought tickets online the day before our trip and had to go to a convenience store to print the tickets. It was also possible to go to the station before the train departed but we opted to print them the day before. Buying tickets online was easy.The train was punctual and boarding was organised and efficient. The train was clean and the journey fast.On our return journey we were early at the station and wanted to go on an earlier train and upgrade to business class. That was no problem at all. The customer service attendant could speak English and handled all this without fuss.The business class seats were so comfortable and had beverage and newspaper service. We were so impressed with the  travel experience and the staff were so polite as well.

From Taoyuan Airport, take a connecting bus and take about 5 minutes to the train station. It takes 30 minutes to get to Taipei Main Station, and if you buy a ticket in advance in Korea, the price is around 10,000 won. It's cheap, fast, and convenient~
Travelling all day in Taiwan makes you tired? Railway traffic in Taiwan is always crowded with people. You can take Taiwan High Speed Rail.

We took the high-speed train from Nangang to Taoyuan. First of all, it was very convenient to buy tickets. There were constant warm reminders from service staff at the station entrance and that we could take the vertical elevator with our suitcases in tow. There was a lunch sales point inside, which was moderately priced and seemed to be of high quality and cheap. When we boarded the train, it was very clean. The most important thing was that the service of the flight attendants was very warm and natural. It was a very pleasant travel experience!

This is Taiwan's version of the Shinkansen that traverses Taiwan. It connects Nangang Station to Zuoying Station in less than two hours, and the fare is extremely cheap. When I travel to Taiwan, I use this Shinkansen to plan an extensive itinerary.
We took the HSR from Nangan to Sun Moon Lake.  The ticket window staff were very helpful (we do not speak Chinese).  The trains are very clean.  The whole trip was easy to navigate.

We accidentally rode high speed rail…we wanted to go to Ruifang, got into the train bound for that direction and we found out it doesn’t stop till Yilan!! A conductor advised so kindly how to do after we get off at Yilan. There were other Japanese who made the same mistake. They didn’t charge us extra fee for coming to Yilan, that’s very kind of them.At Taipei station, please check which train goes and via. I don’t remember core but there wasn’t English sign to show destination.

Just as it arrived... it was already impressive.Looked like a train from the future.Spaceship.Awesome.Interiors were clean & spacious.Fresh.They say its almost 300kphbut you dont feel it.Recommended experience? Highly!!!Congratulations Taiwan

The HSR is truly the way to get around if you are simply moving from one destination to the other in Taiwan.  It is a great way to conserve time since transportation can eat up huge chunks of your visit!  The "slow train" and buses are better if you want to sightsee and are on a tighter budget.  In any case you want to make sure to get a reserved seat or you may be standing awhile.  The HSR does fill up quickly during holiday travel and weekends, so reservations are a must.

From Taipei Station to Kaohsiung Zuoying, Taipei Station is co-constructed by three railways, so you need to find a boarding location. However, if you need any help, you can always ask the station staff for immediate assistance. The trains are very punctual, the environment in the carriage is bright, clean and tidy, and the ride is very comfortable. The most important thing is that the traffic time is greatly reduced. If the budget allows, it is the best long-distance transportation in Taiwan.
As a railway fan, I love the Taiwan High Speed ​​Rail, which uses Japanese Shinkansen technology. It might be fun to look for the differences from Japan's Shinkansen.

I have taken the high-speed rail many times and found that the number of passengers is increasing. The convenience and comfort brought by high-speed rail have made it the first choice for people to take public transportation. The comfortable carriages, friendly service staff, and various kinds of food at the station.
Best high speed train in the world. Fast, on time, clean, high frequency, perfect service : all these make this train the best option for travelling between main cities in Taiwan.

I used it from Taoyuan to Kaohsiung as part of my Taiwan travel package. The fastest Shinkansen ride was 1:37 and cost 1,330 Taiwan dollars. The inside of the train is no different from the Japanese Shinkansen. No alcohol is sold on board. I was impressed that they came to collect the garbage after the sale.

I did a day trip on the THSR for business and it was fantastic. Pre-book reserved seat (helpfully arranged and assisted by the staff at Aloft Hotel). 4 hour round trip, 4 hours business including Taiwanese traditional lunch with customers. GREAT. Clean and efficient and some trolley service on board.

If you are traveling a little further from Taipei Main Station, the Taiwan High Speed ​​Rail is convenient. You can use Yuyu card, which is helpful. Perhaps because it was a weekday, we were able to sit down without making a reservation.

I used it when going from Taipei to Taichung. Taipei Main Station has a large waiting area, so you can arrive with plenty of time. The inside of the train was clean and comfortable, much like the Shinkansen trains in Japan. It was a little inconvenient that there were no power outlets next to the seats, and there was only a charging space in the middle of the vehicle.
I drove it really well, you drive and you don't feel the speed. super. you have to drive it...

I bought a three-day Shinkansen unlimited pass because it fit my travel schedule perfectly. I made a reservation through Beltra, presented my e-ticket and passport at the counter, and got a reserved seat without any problems. It's convenient. We spent the night in Taoyuan and then slowly moved to Kaohsiung the next day. Return to Tainan for sightseeing and stay in Kaohsiung for 2 nights. I was able to schedule a good schedule for Taipei.

I was planning to take a train from Banqiao to Hsinchu, but I accidentally took the express train and ended up in Taichung. It was my fault that I rode without checking. My plan to transfer in the opposite direction in Taichung and take the local train to Hsinchu failed again. To avoid repeating the same mistake, I have to decide whether to be a starter or a late starter. I looked at the signboard, but although it showed the destination, there was no indication of the stop. I asked four people in line and they all said that the train was stopping at Hsinchu. I believed it and got on the train, but the express train wouldn't stop again. I was stunned when I heard this from a conductor on company patrol. When I returned to Itabashi and looked at the signboard, I saw that the train stopped at this station. The signboard on the platform in Taichung is extremely unfriendly.

When it comes to high-speed rail, of course, we compare it with the Taiwan Railway, which is also a long-distance railway service, but it is basically compared to chicken legs. Taiwan Railway is characterized by slow, dirty, messy, inefficient, and dark and old station environments. High-speed rail is bright, clean and comfortable. On the contrary, only Taipei Station is dragged down and looks worse. Check that all stations are novel and comfortable at the airport level, and the service staff are polite. The efficiency is very high, and there is a big difference just when the trains are cleaned when they enter the station. On the high-speed rail, the whole team enters the carriage at once and cleans quickly, while the Taiwan Railway does not know if anyone is cleaning... Of course, comparing it to the Taiwan Railway is too much, because the Taiwan Railway has been bad for decades. Even if the high-speed railway is compared with foreign high-speed railways, it will never lose in accuracy and comfort. I give it five stars.

As expected, it was an export technology from Japan, and it operated at 700T, so it was almost like the Tokaido Shinkansen. The train was very clean and didn't feel like being overseas in a good way. We recommend KK day, where you can get a much cheaper ride if you make online reservations and payment in advance from Japan. The procedure for boarding the train is easy, just hand over your printed voucher at the ticket counter.

I used the round trip from Taoyuan to Nangang. It seems that Japanese Shinkansen technology has been introduced, and if there were no Chinese signs, it would be like riding a Japanese Shinkansen. When heading to the airport, it's quick to get to Taoyuan, but the MRT from Taoyuan has poor connections, so it's best to give yourself plenty of time.

The platforms, facilities, and restrooms at both Taipei Station and Taichung Station were clean. The seats were spacious in both the front and back, so even when reclined, I didn't have much trouble. It was quiet and the ride was comfortable. The famous bento box is available for a limited time only and sells out quickly. I was disappointed that I couldn't eat it. Taichung Station also had quite a lot of shops, including Japanese Loiho and Ootoya.
Bullet train that runs with the same speed as the Japanese ones. Very fast and comfortable. And the ticket can be purchased online or at the station itself.
When I rode the high-speed railway, I ate a high-speed railway bento. Available for purchase at noon and evening. It was very delicious. I want to eat it again.

Getting on the bus is very fast, and the cleaning staff will always patrol to see if there is any need to pick up the trash! It was my first time to use an ibon ticket, but the station staff didn’t provide any assistance when I entered the station. I didn’t know how to use it.
A TGV as easy to use as an RER, with added comfort. It is not essential to reserve your place, standing passengers are tolerated.

Taiwan does not have many infrastructures superior to Japan.  This one is an exception. Japanese tourists traveling along THSR would agree. It's Taiwan version of Japan's Shinkansen using Japanese systems and yet facility service is apparently better. With this  you can visit any of Taiwan's major cities within 2 hours. Trains depart every 20 minutes and local connection is smooth and comfortable.

Really easy and convenient to get to certain parts of Taiwan. Super comfy seats so you can just pass out for a nap until your destination. There are snacks being sold too so no worries if you forgot to eat!

For my last 2 trips to Taiwan, I used the High Speed Rail to ply between Taipei and Kaohsiung.  I took both the express and normal scheduled trains and the only difference is the timing.For express scheduled train, as they do skip a few stations, the travel time from Taipei to Kaohsiung took only 1.5hours versus the normal scheduled train of 2.5hours.The train is very clean and seats are comfortable with enough leg space to even put a hand-carry luggage.  On the several trips I made via the High Speed Rail, I noticed police presence - one officer will patrol through the carriage at least twice within the 1.5hours ride.The service staff are very friendly and helpful - on train and at the platform.  Hence, if you are lost or need travel advice, the staff generally will give very useful and good guide/assistance.The train allow passengers to consume food and beverages and during the journey, there is a service staff selling drinks and bento and there is another staff who will go round every half an hour to collect any trash that passengers need to dispose.  Hence, passengers are able to travel at ease and comfort.Overall, I enjoy all my trips on the High Speed Rail and I will recommend anyone who wants to travel across the island to use this mode of transport than by air as you get to see nice scenery along the way (unless you are travelling at night).

Taiwan HSR is a great option to travel in large distances in Taiwan. Very comfortable, affordable and quick too. It's also convenient as you can buy tickets on the spot, and pay with your foreign credit card.

I bought a 3-day ticket online in Japan and used it for sightseeing in Taiwan. . I used it to go from Taoyuan Airport to a hotel in the city and for a round trip between Taipei and Kaohsiung. The vehicle, the ride quality, and the cousin of Japan's Shinkansen were comfortable. English in-car announcements and in-car sales are also easy to understand. You can also take a day trip to Kaohsiung. However, you will need to transfer to a conventional line to reach Kaohsiung City.

There are many trains! Connecting various cities and towns in Taiwan! Basically, I’ve taken a few rides and I’ve never been late! But compared to other countries, the price seems too high! Very convenient!
The design, speed, and service are just like the Japanese Shinkansen. If you plan about a month in advance, you may get a 2-4% discount on ticket prices.

very good & modern rail service. the only problem was finding the ticket office to purchase our tickets as nobody spoke english & all the rail services were underground intermingled with shopping centers that run for miles.

Taking the high-speed rail shortens the distance between the north and south of Taiwan, and the riding environment is not noisy and very clean. On this trip to and from Beigao, I only had a lunch in the car and read a book. There are also many scenes of parents and children walking together.

You can make reservations in Japan, and of course you can also reserve your seat. There are a lot of them, and although they are convenient, I think the prices are quite low. It costs about 5000 yen for 2 hours from Taipei to Tainan. It's Japanese Shinkansen technology, so the ride is super comfortable! I would like to see the east side open as well.

Loved these trains - which I used to get to Taichung and to Fulong Beach. Seat allocations are made when you buy a ticket so you may not always get a desirable window. But the trains are comfortable, clean and fast. And the reasonable fares out the British rail system to shame.

Only if you can take the direct train to Taichung can you feel the speed of the high-speed train. Otherwise, as soon as you start to accelerate, you will have to slow down immediately, and you will not be able to truly experience the pleasure of hi speed.

From Chiayi to Taipei. I made the reservation from Japan, so I don't know how crowded the reserved seats would be, but it was actually full from the middle of the day. I thought it would be safer to make a reservation. I don't know if there is a Japanese reservation site from Japan. Reserved seats will also have coffee service.

The first time I took the bus, I wasn’t sure about the process. Fortunately, the signs and information on the website were clear, which effectively reduced my sense of uneasiness. However, the ticket price is really not cheap, and I don’t know why the ticket price shown online is different from the ticket price paid in person...

Taking the Taiwan High Speed ​​Rail has become a common thing. Even students, many people use the High Speed ​​Rail as a means of transportation. From Taichung to Taipei or Kaohsiung, it takes less than an hour if you take a direct train, and if you shop online in advance, you only need to arrive 10 minutes earlier, which is more convenient than taking a plane or bus!

There are few places to stop and there is no swaying, so the ride is perfect.In business class, sweets and coffee are provided, which is recommended. On the way back, it was a non-reserved seat, but I was glad I was able to sit.
fast, smooth, clean and always on time !!THSRC now provides free WIFI in the cabin, it's really the best way to visit Southern Taiwan from Taipei.

The indicators for the high-speed train are quite clear, and it is convenient to eat or use the toilet while waiting for the train. It just depends on the quality of the passengers in the same carriage. An aunt talking loudly on the phone or a noisy child will affect the ride quality. Otherwise, it is considered very good. Taiwan's high-speed rail is a clean and convenient means of transportation!
This is a huge asset for business travel. Book on your phone. Easy. Trains run punctually and are clean. Fast too.

Good, fast and not too expensive! The staff can usually speak English. It is the best way to travel from one big city to another. Don't even think of taking the plane: Taiwan is too small for that and the world is already too polluted.

Taipei Main Station is a three-rail co-construction. Basically, you must rely on road signs to avoid getting lost. As soon as you come out of Taipei High Speed ​​Rail Station, it is opposite the Taipei MRT. It is very convenient. If you walk to the left, you can also buy Taiwan Railway lunch boxes, C Eleven convenience stores and some convenient lunch shops.

It's a very convenient means of transportation. This time I used the route between Zuoying and Taipei. The last time I used it, I ate a bento box sold on the train, and it was warm, delicious, and reasonably priced. If you put banknotes into an automatic ticket vending machine and buy a ticket, your change may come out in 50 yuan coins.

the HSR is a wonderful means of transport to quickly cover large distances along the west coast of Taiwan between the major cities. Some HSRs serve some intermediate stations, others do not. The first one you can book is not always the fastest!

The ride was very nice, quiet and convenient.  Besides that, I left my backpack on the train in a hurry to get off with all my other bags.  They staff handled it right away and within a few hours, I had my backpack back. Nothing missing.

Very quickly delivers you from one end of the island to the other. The staff has always been courteous and professional. A great way to travel.

During your trip to Taipei, we recommend a day trip to Taichung, Tainan, or Kaohsiung!

The quality and service of the high-speed rail are first-class, and it saves tourists a lot of time in transportation. Although you can eat and drink in the high-speed rail, there is no dirty environment at all. Every user is very law-abiding, which I like very much!

On average, I take the high-speed rail once every six months. Most of the time I take the high-speed rail when I want to go abroad or travel with friends. The THSR is by far the best way to get into the city from the airport. Be advised that you do have to take a bus from the airport (this was not apparent to us until we asked) to get to the HSR station. But beyond that, it's an easy, fast, and affordable option to get downtown.

Taiwan's high-speed rail is a convenient and fast means of transportation, connecting Taipei to Tainan and other places. It saves a lot of travel time, but the tickets are a bit expensive, so you buy time with money.
I have used this service twice now while on holidays.  Found the service to be on time, clean, efficient, friendly staff, only negative is that it is very expensive

It uses Japanese Shinkansen technology, so it looks and feels like a Shinkansen. Despite being said to be in the red, the non-reserved seats are sometimes so crowded that you can't even sit in them. There are early bird discounts and time-of-day discounts, so if you take advantage of them, you can probably get a good deal. The online reservation system was also easy to use.
I often take the HSR to travel in Taiwan and it's always on time, clean and fast and the staff are super friendly. Thanks, Taiwan!

Taking the high-speed rail to Tainan was actually an unplanned trip. I thought it would be far away, but I didn’t expect that the high-speed rail only takes an hour and a half. I visited all the historical sites and ate a lot of Tainan snacks. It was so convenient to go back to Taipei from Tainan after visiting the night market in the evening!

Took the HSR from Taipei to Taichun and back. This is really the most efficient and quick way to travel within Taiwan I suppose, no traffic at all, regular schedules and comfortable. Check which trains go directly (or just with 1 stop) or the ones that stop regularly. Obviously the first one will go quicker. You can buy reserved seating tickets on the day of departure, until a few minutes before departure.

From Taichung to Taipei in less than an hour at 285 kilometers per hour. The stations are modern and even if this is your first time using the HSR, it is not difficult to buy a ticket at the station and find your train.

It saves a lot of traffic time. It is very convenient for people who have business affairs. The facilities are relatively new and usually very punctual. But I will buy early bird tickets which are cheaper

Fast, cheap and comfortable. Plenty of leg room for the taller members of our species, staff nice and polite. Only down side is there are no drinking stations on board, so you'll have to either purchase water at the vending machines or fill your bottle at the stations. But considering the travel time on HSR is usually quite short, you could just wait it out as I did. The platforms in Taipei though are quite narrow due to the platforms being added to Taipei Train station, stuffy as well. This is however due to the limitations of space and age of the stations, and nothing could be done. The new stations else where are quite nice though.
We travelled from Taipei to Hualien and found the trip quiet, comfortable with plenty of legroom to be able to recline your seat and relax.

From many perspectives, the CP value of high-speed rail is definitely not high. The stations are all in the suburbs, and the newly opened stations only have one train every hour. However, the high-speed rail makes up for these shortcomings with services. When I was at Taipei Station, because the stroller could not go up the escalator, the high-speed rail staff directly helped me move to the platform. The service staff on the car The staff looked at me taking the children and gave me an extra pack of snacks to appease them. Although it is only a short distance from Taichung to Taipei, it was still a pretty good experience. Even if you don’t need my recommendation, I believe that more than half of the people have taken the ride, but I still recommend it personally~
You can go to the airport by bus transfer. It saves time. The price is reasonable. I recommend.

The ticket purchase counter will be crowded, so it's best to give yourself plenty of time. Purchase tickets for foreigners with advance approval online from a local travel agency. However, you can only reserve your seat and exchange your ticket at the counter. You will also be asked to present your passport when making a purchase or passing through the ticket gate.
Traveling by Taiwan high speed rail is just a pleasure. Excellent space even for tall people. Clean and nice and the speed is just good. Great stations.
This time I headed from Tainan to Taipei. The feet are loose and comfortable. You can buy a ticket from Japan online and pick it up at a convenience store in Taiwan.

This is the way to travel for foreign travellers arranging your own  around the island itinerary. You need order online from the Taiwan high speed rail company website and show your short visit visa passport when picking up ticket to get a special package valid for 3 days to a week unlimited travel on high speed rail only or together with the regular railway system with a deeply discount. The advance reservation is only open 28 days ahead and seats are always available except for Friday and Sunday evening peak travel period.
This is the asset of Taiwan , really convenient , From Taoyuan to Tainan just take 80 minutes , save time , and you get the free shuttle from THSR station !
Best time to take the HSR going south would be around 9 AM or so because it’s after the rush hour and they offer a slight discount for this hour of travel!
We arrived from Taipei to Kaohsiung in no time. It's no different from Japan's Shinkansen, but the station in Taichung was modern and clean.
Be on time with your flights with hassle free transportation using the THSR. Affordable, clean and convenient train system.

HSR binds north with south very efficiently. Also reliably I may add. As its Japanese sister the Shinkansen, you can adjust your watch to it. Always on time!Comportable, fast and frequent. Can't ask for more. Tickets can be bought at the convenience stores or at the station. Easy and affordable.Two classes: economy class with random seating and economy with numbered seating; business class where coach 6 is dedicated, numbered seating only.Convenience trolly passes through for drinks and food, snacks and reading material.Some departures stops at all major cities. Other has max. 3 (I belive) stops between North and South. Travel time is about 1:30 hrs. Speed just below 300 km/hBusiness class ticket is approx. NTD 2,000 one way

Well sign-posted, easy to follow the rail map and very reasonably priced. Lots of staff available when one (we) got confused a couple of times and safely boarded us not only to our destination but how to find the attraction we were visiting. First class service, comfort, cleanliness and customer care.

This time, I used unlimited rides on two days of my choice out of seven days. The appeal of the Shinkansen is that it can shorten travel time. It is also possible to play in Kaohsiung, take a day trip, and return to Taipei. I like the Taipei Railway as it has a nice atmosphere, and long-distance buses are cheap and I don't mind sleeping in luxurious chairs at night, but this time I chose the time of day. The ride is comfortable and you can arrive at your destination while eating a delicious lunch. You can also reserve seats using the free pass you use!
This is just WOW. Looks like an aeroplane. Neat, clean and tidy. Very modern. I loved it taking this HSR from Taipei to Kaohsiung City and back. A great experience for me.
Speed, cleanness, always on time.  Very easy access.  Great value.  At-station transportation is also very convenient for most stations.
I used it on the way to the airport. It's an express, so it's fast and convenient! And it's neat, and there's a separate space for luggage next to the door.

Taoyuan MRT is very convenient. It's easy to understand, just follow the directions and you'll arrive at the station. It takes about 35 minutes from Taoyuan Airport to Taipei Main Station. It takes about 45 minutes to reach each station. I will definitely use it next time as I can easily go to Taipei.

Because of the high-speed rail, people who dare not take domestic flights have an option. It can reach their destination faster than the Taiwan Railway. Although it is quite expensive, time is money! If the wireless network could be smoother, I would give it one more star.

3 day free pass for foreigners is good. You can ride as much as you want, whether you're in a reserved seat or a non-reserved seat. It's annoying that you have to line up at the ticket counter and show your passport at the ticket gate, but you can get your money's worth by going back and forth from Kaohsiung to Taipei. I made a reservation with JTB from Japan using my PC. I printed out the application form and brought it to the counter, but for some reason I had to show them the screen on my iPad mini to get a pass issued. I bought the same pass a year ago, but it seems like the system has been improved and the ticketing time has become shorter. To reserve a reserved seat, all you had to do was print out the timetable and point to it. I will buy it again next time.

If you have never taken one, it means you don’t understand what Taiwan’s one-day life circle is. After Taiwan has high-speed rail, you can go anywhere in the western part of Taiwan to do errands and then return to Taipei in one day. There is absolutely no problem!

I have taken it several times from Taipei to Hsinchu, Taichung, and Kaohsiung, and it has saved a lot of traffic time. It is very convenient for business people. Because it is a brand new system, the facilities are relatively new and well maintained. There are not too many complicated car schedules, and they are usually very punctual.

From Taoyuan Airport, take a bus to Taiwan High Speed ​​Rail Taoyuan Station and take a business class bus to Xinzuoying, Kaohsiung City. Hot tea and cookies will be served along the way. The inside of the train is as comfortable as the Japanese Shinkansen.
Took a weekend trip to Kaohsiung. Easy to access rail at both ends and met a tour guide at Kaohsiung for a 1 day and a 1/2 day tour then back again on the train.

I took the Taiwan Shinkansen. I purchased it online while I was in Japan and had the ticket issued locally. Unlimited rides for 3 days. When boarding a train using a notebook-type passport, first go to a green counter and make a reservation. You need a Shinkansen passport and a real passport. When you say your destination, the Shinkansen number, date, seat number, etc. are written by hand on your Shinkansen passport. It takes a while, so if you're in a hurry, it might be faster to line up with the female staff. Everywhere, the male staff were always more restless. You will need your Shinkansen passport and passport to enter. Show it to the ticket gate staff before entering. I heard that Japan's Shinkansen is the 700 series, and the interior is very simple. It's like Hikari from a while ago. There are no electrical outlets. There is a suitcase storage area, but there are only about 4 spaces at the front and rear of each vehicle, so there is a high probability that you won't be able to store your suitcases. I have no choice but to place it at the foot of the seat, but it is quite tight for sizes M and above. There is in-car sales like in Japan. Ride comfort is ok. This time, I rode Taipei ⇒ Taichung ⇒ Tainan ⇒ Taichung ⇒ Kaohsiung. All seats reserved. I wasn't sure if it paid for itself, but I'm glad I was able to be active and not worry about it.

It took a while to read the credit card at the ticket vending machine. At a ticket vending machine at a certain station, the credit card itself got stuck in the reader and could not be returned. When I explained this to the staff over the intercom, the response was quick. I immediately took out my card from the backyard, and this time, I paid by credit card at the staff booth next to the automatic ticket gate and was issued a ticket. The company's human and software support was excellent.

Although it is Japan's Shinkansen, the business class (green car) is more luxurious than the Japanese one. Then, you can enjoy snacks such as biscuits and coffee. It's nice to sit on a comfortable seat and enjoy the scenery from the train window while drinking coffee. I also rode the regular designated train, which is the same as the Shinkansen in Japan. If you are going south from Taipei, depending on the time of day, it may be crowded with passengers from Taoyuan International Airport. On occasion, I think it would be a good idea to have a little luxury and enjoy traveling slowly.

There are more people in the business class than in the past and it is often full. However, the service staff can still maintain a certain level of service. They can also handle the situation smoothly when encountering passengers (who want this or that, watch videos on their mobile phones at high volume), which is worthy of praise.
So simple to get from Airport to the city and quick. Cheap also. Station staff are around to assist with any questions

The high-speed rail makes commuting between Beijing and Gaojiao very convenient. The seats and environment are kept quite clean, and the waiters are polite. However, you can't buy free seats online, which feels a bit troublesome!

Ticket reservations can be made online so that when you arrive at the station you can only collect the original ticket. The facilities at the station also provide English and Chinese so there are no language problems. the counter staff are also friendly and ready to help. The most important thing is that this train is clean, super fast and always on time. Travel time from Taoyuan THSR station to Taipe Main Station, which is 37km, is just under 10 minutes. that's something!

Taiwan is small enough that you can travel the entire length of the country in under 3 hours on the HSR. Taiwan's system is based on Japan's Shinkansen HSR.  The cars are clean, efficient and comfortable. Signs and announcement are in English as well as Mandarin and the other Taiwanese languages.  Seats are reservable. The HSR has a great online site where you can purchase tickets ahead of time.

I have been to Taiwan several times, but this was my first visit since the Taiwan High Speed ​​Rail was built. Since I was boarding from Narita Airport, I felt it was inconvenient to get around after getting off at Taoyuan Airport, but since the high-speed railway was built, it has become more convenient. You can travel from Taipei Main Station to Taoyuan Airport in just over 30 minutes. The fare is cheap and it's definitely better than spending over an hour in a taxi. The station and trains are still clean and comfortable. Airport check-in is also possible at Taipei Main Station, so we recommend using it.

I have taken the HSR (High Speed Rail) from North to South in Taiwan and it is always a very comfortable ride. The trains are very quiet and very smooth and it feels like you are floating on air.There are really 3 different tickets you can get: 1. Business Class with a Reserved Seat2. Standard Class with a Reserved Seat3. Standard Class with no Assign SeatIn Business class the seats are much wider and you get a drink (Water, Coffee, Tea, or Juice) and snack while you are on your way.  There are 2 seats on each side in the business class cabin.For the standard class, one side has 3 seats and the other side has 2 seats.  I have been on the train where it was standing room only so getting a reserved seat ahead of time is highly advised.I recommend using the app to book your tickets and to check availability.  I usually do a walk up ticket so when my taxi is almost to the station, I will pull up the app to book my ticket and then use the barcode on my phone as my ticket.  Saves paper and saves time.  If you buy more than 1 ticket, make sure the other people in the party have the app downloaded onto their phone so that they can access their ticket. To get around the island, High Speed Rail is the way to go.

I travel on this HSR once or twice a month, mostly for work. Just in case, i try to get the tickets in advance from 7-11. On some weekends and holidays, business class tickets are sold out, and in some cases, even economy classThe perks of business class are wider seats , "free" snack and most important for me, a charging port for iphoneAlways on time and reliable, so don't be late

I thought I would be able to sit in a non-reserved seat...I got on the train from Taipei Main Station, but when I thought I was leaving from there, there were already people on board and the seats were narrow.There were three people sitting across the aisle, so I thought it would be slow and comfortable, but it wasn't.

There are things like Nozomi, things like Hikari, and things like Kodama that stay overnight at each station. Of these, there are two types that perch in Taoyuan: the Hikari-like type and the Kodama-like type. There is a wagon service.

It was a little pricey but worth it to save half a day of travel and just to see what a super fast train is like (incredibly smooth).  I didn't book, but apparently at the busy times its essential if you don't want to stand for 3 hours. As you'd expect form all things Taiwanese it was very clean and efficient.

Taiwan's high-speed rail is a very convenient mode of transportation for business or short-term tourists. It only takes more than an hour to get there from the south to the north. Of course, you usually need to transfer from the high-speed rail station to enter the city, but if you do your homework, it shouldn't be difficult. If you don't understand, just ask any Taiwanese and they will tell you kindly.

Taiwan's high speed rail uses the best Japanese proven technology - and it shows.We used the high speed trains three times recently. Every train was no more than a minute late.Boarding is easy: no stupid Amtrak USA-like queuing for particular trains; instead, just show up at the platform at the right time.Platform and on train information is in English as well as Mandarin.The trains, even in economy, are comfortable.  Business class is available for a reasonable fare while local journeys such as Taipei to Taoyuan HSR station (for a local Purple line commuter train to the airport, or the Gloria Outlets huge luxury brands and factory outlets shopping centre) are great value.On board trolley service provides food and drinks while major stations such as Taichung have a railway outlet near the ticket office that sells an amazingly good quick takeaway lunch for just NT$80.As one speeds past the mountainous or city scenery, it's easy to reflect as to how far superior these high speed trains are to the former harried process of going through security at airports and waiting for a delayed plane in a boring environment.Every visitor to Taiwan should travel on these excellent high speed trains with their easy connections to local Taiwan Railway Administration or metro (underground) trains.

I'm very proud to be a Taiwanese as I've been living in Australia for the past 2 decades and I miss the public transportation system in Taiwan. Do yourself a favor, go to East coast of Taiwan, Hwa-Lein on the speed Rail. You will enjoy the ride, the view, and the excellent traditional food: bein-dong (the lunch box) is a must to have.

The high speed trains are well networked on Taiwan island from north to south. Well connected with trains to small cities or towns.May be a little pricey. However, consider the time saved, it is justified.

It's safe and fast, and the service is considerate! Thanks to the high-speed rail staff for helping me get home smoothly because I missed the high-speed rail train, and also for helping me with how to handle the large luggage...
I took the Hsr to Taichung. Very Impressed that it was a smooth ride. Train came on time and very spacious leg room.

I specially found a day to go to Taichung to meet friends, so I took the high-speed rail because I didn't have much time, but the fare was a bit expensive. But it’s really fast. It takes less than an hour to go from Taipei to Taichung, which is quite convenient.

It's comfortable. The goods sold inside the train are cute. Normally, you can buy a bento for 60 to 80 yuan, but if you buy it in the car, it will cost 100 yuan. However, the taste is average, so it might be better to buy it before riding. But the taste is delicious. The inside of the train is exactly the same as the Shinkansen in Japan. I haven't used the toilet, so I don't know what it looks like, but it's not that dirty, so I think it's good.

The best means of transportation connecting the north and south of Taiwan, with an average departure time of 30 minutes, it is as convenient as the MRT! Travelers who come to Taiwan for tourism or business can take advantage of this convenient and inexpensive means of transportation!

The high-speed rail has indeed shortened the time between the north and south of Taiwan to about 2 hours, so if you have to do business or meet with friends, you can take the high-speed rail to meet friends or negotiate. In addition to the high-speed train, the time is also very good, and we can also provide ordering services.

I took the train to Chiayi, Taichung and Taipei. Trains arrived on time and the arrival time at each station was also same as the ETA stated on their website. Buying tickets on line was a bit confusing at first but it wasn't that bad. After you've purchased tickets online, you'll receive booking number and other related details via email. Do take note, the physical ticket will still need to be collected. You can opt to change your tickets half an hour before departure, but you'll need to top up any difference if you had bought your tickets at a discounted price. (Early birds* will get 10%-35% discount)*5-28 days before departure.

We ride in a special trip which separates you from the crowded train. The seats are comfortable with snacks provided during the trip. The trip is very fast as we travelled from Taipei to Kaohsiung. Their service is very good, as my companion left his jacket in the train, we asked for their assistance and they easily located it and got it back to us the following morning.

Taipei is the main station, so the station is the same as the conventional line, but the other stations stop at different places from the conventional line, so it was a bit difficult to get to the conventional line station. The train was very comfortable to ride, and the cleaners came around frequently to keep the inside of the train clean, and there were occasional sales of bento boxes, sweets, and drinks, which made for a very pleasant journey.Also, most of the shops (restaurants, etc.) in Taichung stations were Japanese stores, so I didn't feel like I was in a foreign country.

Nowadays, the only fastest way to travel between the north and the south is the high-speed rail. There are few flights and it is not very convenient. There is an MRT available when the high-speed rail leaves the station. For office workers on business trips, it is easy to control their time.

Taiwan's high-speed rail. The train was imported from Japan and seems to be the same as the Shinkansen. The operation is stable, there is not much shaking, and it is comfortable. If you have a non-reserved seat ticket, you may be forced to stand because there are no seats available at some stations.

Taiwan's high-speed rail is fast and safe. I often take the high-speed rail to and from Chiayi, Taipei, mainly to visit my parents in the south. Sometimes I take the high-speed train to various cities in western Taiwan for meetings, which is really fast and convenient. I have taken Taiwan High Speed Rail many times. Its speed can reach 300km/hr. If you take direct train from Taipei to Kaohsiung, it is just one and half hours. With THSR, I can travel to west Taiwan cities within one day. Also it is safe because I do not need to drive in the heavy-traffic freeway. I always use it to visit my parents in Chia-Yi. It usually takes me 1 and half hours. Now free Wi-Fi is provided on the trains. THSR has already changed travel habits of many Taiwan people.

I have used various trains in Taiwan, such as MRT and Taiwan Railways, but this was my first time using the High Speed ​​Rail. Since I was returning from the Southern Branch of the National Palace Museum, I used a reserved seat on the section from Chiayi to Kaohsiung Zuoying. I bought my ticket from a vending machine at Chiayi Station, and the ticket was displayed in English, so the purchase process was smooth. Also, the inside of the train is almost the same as the Shinkansen in Japan, so there are no problems. However, is it surprisingly crowded? ? I would like to ride for a longer distance.

Since there is a high-speed rail station near my home, I find it very convenient. The distance between stations has become closer. It is a clean and comfortable riding space. There are also many restaurants and shops within the station. It is very convenient!

Taiwan high speed rail is no doubt the fastest and most convenient way to travel in Taiwan. Unfortunately their business class hardware are a little bit worn and may need replacement. Overall a very joyful ride and price is really not bad compared to other major cities around the world.
The seat was wide enough to store my luggage, so it wasn't a pain, but the toilet shook a lot. Please experience the toilet seat.
Take a ride from the city to Taoyuan International Airport. It's new so it's very clean and tidy. It took about 30 minutes to get to the airport, but it was a very comfortable trip.

At the end of August, I took the express train to Hualien (Taroko). The ride is not that different from Japan's limited express trains. However, the air conditioner inside the company is very strong, so if you are going to ride for several hours, it is better to bring a long-sleeved shirt.

The Taiwan Shinkansen connects Taipei Station and Zuoying Station (the gateway to Kaohsiung) in 1 hour and 36 minutes. Nangang Station has opened beyond Taipei Station, and there are also stops in major areas such as Banqiao, Taoyuan (there are MRT and buses to the airport), Hsinchu, Miaoli, Taichung, Changhua, Yunlin, Chiayi, and Tainan, making it convenient for rapid transit between major cities in western Taiwan. For Japanese (non-Japanese) people, there is a 3-day unlimited ``Tsutetsu Pass'' (purchased in advance in Japan and you can get the money back if you make one round trip), making it easy to enjoy sightseeing spots using the Shinkansen. The vehicle is based on the Japanese 700 series, and the interior of the regular car has the atmosphere of riding on a Japanese Shinkansen.

I have used the high-speed railway several times in the past, and since it uses Japan's 700-type Shinkansen and has the same operating system, it is very accurate and very comfortable. The big difference with Japan is that the fares are cheap, with a commercial vehicle from Taipei to Taichung costing just under 4,000 yen. Tea sweets and drinks were also provided, and some of the customers were able to speak Japanese.
As in Japan the high-speed rail is a very efficient and quite comfortable way to travel around Taiwan. Comfortable seating and pleasant catering.

With the high-speed rail, the travel time between the north and the south has been greatly shortened, making it very convenient whether traveling or working. It saves everyone a lot of time and gives you a lot more time to play or plan work. Furthermore, the punctuality feature of high-speed rail is really great, allowing people to grasp the time more accurately. The service staff are friendly and professional. It is really a great means of transportation and highly recommended.

Due to work, I need to take Taiwan's high-speed rail from south to north every week. For many years, unless there is a natural disaster, the trains run very fast and on time. It is easy for passengers to keep track of time and do not need to worry about unexpected delays. The high-speed rail carriages are quite clean and the service staff are courteous. The only drawback is that during consecutive holidays, the carriages are crowded with passengers. Even in the designated carriages, there will be many passengers standing in the carriage who are eager to return home but have no seats, making it quite crowded.
Amazing high-tech high-speed transportation system. Just make sure you choose the seats wisely otherwise you might end up sitting separate from your travel partner.

I was going to Hualien, so I made a reservation for the express train. It was a bit difficult to make a reservation, but I exchanged the booking number for a physical ticket at the machine at the main station. The spacious and comfortable indoor space has wide spacing between chairs. I traveled to and from Hualien very comfortably.

There are discounts for purchasing high-speed rail tickets online as a tourist. The price is cheaper than buying in person and is flexible. The carriages are very clean and spacious. It only takes about 1 hour to get there quickly from Tainan to Taichung or from Taichung to Taipei.

I have traveled between Taipei and Tainan, and between Taipei and Taichung. Tickets are purchased from automatic ticket vending machines. It's easy to understand and you can also use credit cards. The Shinkansen stations in Tainan and Taichung are located on the outskirts of the city center, and you will need to transfer to a regular train to get to Taichung/Tainan Station on the Taiwan Railway, which is located in the center. The time seemed to be organized well, so I was able to board the Taiwan Railway train without having to wait. The Taichung and Tainan Shinkansen stations are named Xinwuri Station and Shalun Station, respectively. Be careful not to miss it when returning to Taipei. The Shinkansen was comfortable, just like the ones in Japan.

I have to say that Taiwan's transportation construction is really well done. It is clean and bright, and the signage is very clear. It will definitely greatly improve the favorability of foreign tourists towards Taiwan.
Very fast and clean train  There are almost a train leaving every 10 to 15 minutes.  The price is very affordable as well.

Connect cities in a short time. I usually use the 20% discount ticket for foreigners or the 3-day tour ticket, so I go through the procedures at the counter. I can't speak Chinese. Since my English is only broken, I write down the train I want to ride and give it to him. This almost works. When boarding, you must show your ticket and passport to the staff near the ticket gate. The same applies when exiting from the ticket gate. The inside of the train is the same as the Shinkansen in Japan. The ride is also comfortable. In-vehicle sales frequently occur. It's not surprisingly expensive, but the language is often difficult to understand. High-speed rail stations and Taiwanese National Railways stations are often far apart, so you need to be careful about that as well. The transfer itself is not difficult. This is a convenient railway for both going south and north.

The High Speed Rail was clean and very comfortable.  The seats were roomy and you couldn't tell you were going as fast as you did since it was so smooth.  Definitely saved a lot of time and aggravation.
I used this for a worktrip and it was a very smooth trip, with good seats and a great view of the country side. Thoroughly enjoyed it.

If you need to go from Taipei to Hsinchu or Tainan - or anywhere in between - fast and safe, the High Speed Rail is your way. Speeds of almost 300 km/h in a perfectly calm and safe environment take you where you need to be. Only minor downside is food and beverage served in the trains, since sparkling water (for instance) is rare here, except at international restaurants. Price is fair and service is good. Trains are always on time and subway stations offer good connection alternatives.

This was my first time using the high speed train to go from Taipei to Taichung. Since I had already purchased a ticket with a foreigner discount, I lined up at the counter to get a reserved seat at Taipei High Speed ​​Rail Station. There are probably multiple counters within the station, but the female staff member at the counter where my family was lined up was very rude. Many Taiwanese people are pro-Japanese, and during my two trips there I had been treated very kindly, so I was surprised by the cold response from the female station staff. They couldn't help me in Japanese, and their English was fast and ruthless... In the end, we were able to resolve the issue even though we did not understand it. I felt sad that there are cold people everywhere. The station itself is modern and I thought it was a convenient station with many shops. The Shinkansen itself was clean and comfortable to ride.
These high speed trains are as good as they are in Japan, including the punctuality. There's 3 options: business class, normal tickets and the free seat option (could be a standing place when busy).

Took express train from Taipei to Hualien.  I booked and paid for the tickets online.  I collected tickets from counter at level 1 of the Taipei Main train station.  The seat was clean and had wide leg space.
