Since the high-speed rail started operating, traveling from south to north and within the island has become more convenient. The reduction of holiday traffic jams on highways has also increased the willingness to travel domestically!

The Taiwan High Speed ​​Rail is one of the most convenient means of transportation to go to Taichung, Tainan. The price is very affordable, the time is fast, the trains are frequent, and it is safe. You can find all the high speed rail timetables to and from Taiwan online. There is a post office in the Taipei High Speed ​​Rail Station where you can exchange Taiwan dollars.
Day trip on business to Tainan.  Trains are frequent and comfortable.  Not especially cheap, but very convenient and an easy way to get to and from cities on the east coast.

Highly recommended. Tickets can be bought in advance through their own site or through other agents with some discount. Unused ticket can be refunded with a minimal administrative cost. High speed train travels at 300mph +, tickets can be bought at the train station as well, early birds discount available. The service runs through the major cities in Taiwan and the routes can be found on their site. Seats are either reserved or non reserved.HSR stations are not necessarily in the city centre so for some cities, you have to take either a connecting bus or train to get to the station. Very convenient,economical and efficient way of travelling in Taiwan. Highly recommended .

College students can purchase college student discount tickets, save money and time provide early bird and free seat discounts, if the tickets can be a little more friendly to the people will be better The car is clean, the vehicle is running, very stable, not dizzy or unwell

There are taxis available at the high-speed rail station. You can take the high-speed rail to sightsee in the five major cities in western Taiwan, which saves a lot of time. You can also return from Taipei to Taichung on the same day. Compared with other modes of transportation, the high-speed rail is a good choice, and you can also use your credit card to upgrade your seat.

As the title suggests, it's comfortable and fast. Taiwan has good transportation, so it's easy to get around. It's a little more expensive than other transportation methods, but it's easy to use, so I recommend it.

It’s a good choice to travel from the beginning to the end of Taiwan. If you don’t get off the bus halfway, it will save a lot of time. If you can grasp the date of travel and buy discount tickets, the price sometimes varies a lot.

It was the first time I took my mother on the high-speed rail. She felt it was very refreshing to take her back to her hometown. She was so happy. I bought the ticket at a supermarket. Although it cost more than a thousand, there was a discount. My mother had the manual, so it was quite cheap. The overall feeling was pretty good.
It's very good way to get from North Taiwan to mid and South of Taiwan, you save time and comfortable carriage, plus reasonable/cheap train fair.

It's a little far from the basement of the airport, so you have to walk, but it's in an easy-to-find location. It's easier to charge your ticket first, leave it there, and enter like a Japanese watermelon. It was 160 yuan. There are two types of trains, and the purple one is the fastest.When I boarded the train from the airport, I took it all the way to Taipei, but when I went back, it didn't say whether I was going to take train 1 or 2, so I had to take it all the way to the end of train 1, then turn around and get off at train 2.It's better to know where I'm going to get off before I leave. The train is comfortable and takes you above ground midway through so you can enjoy the scenery outside.

Compared to Japan's Shinkansen trains, the outside of the train was not washed at all and was dirty.Also, probably because the trains were in the red in the beginning, the cars were old and the seats were not good.

Do yourself a favor, spend $50 and experience the THSR for yourself, 90 min from TPE to KHH. This time, I had the most incredible encounter with its passenger safety crew.So it finally happened, my rolling luggage got physical with the escalator while my mind was distracted. Knowing how there is very little room for amicable give-and-take, I usually paid EXTRA attention to make sure that each sits sideway on a flat tread, the big one below, the small one above, with me in the middle tread, and out of everyone else's way, all the way to the right, in the couple seconds before the treads went from flat to saw-tooth. But I was in a hurry, my bladder in need of relief, jet-legged from DC to HAM to TPE and ruminating over what a terrible son-in-law and son I have been these last few years when it came to the care of our widowed mothers, having just spent a day at my mother-in-law's flat, replacing 10 burnt bulbs & tubes and making note of plumbing deficiencies.When the big Rimowa on the upper tread tipped over and threw me off balance, I tumbled and fell towards the earth, thinking clearly to myself, "This is NOT going to be pretty" as I felt my body impacting another 2 bodies and thus taking 2 innocent passengers with me, my spectacles falling off my face and hearing the metal screeching sound, "O no these are my expensive progressive lenses but good thing I have brought a spare pair glasses for PC monitor...thank God I won't need to drive", and of course, "now there is no way that I am gonna make the 15:31 high speed train and my poor mom isn't gonna know why her son didn't show up at the nursing home on her birthday as promised to take her away with me."Instead, I found myself standing upright, as were my 2 luggage, the escalator stationary, and a young lady looking intensely and asking if I was injured, "Well no, but my glasses are broken." A young man in the same white shirt navy pants handed them back to me and said, "No sir, they are fine." What in the world! There were 3 scratch marks on my right pinky, for which they called the mobile nurse in with her first aide kit, which must have received the blunt of my fall, so why was I standing? If this had happened anywhere else in the world, like IAD or HAM or AMS or Xiamen, it would have been an ugly mess. But instead, the incredibly competent, efficacious, efficient staff at Taiwan HSR, I never even saw them waiting at the bottom of the escalator, hit the emergency stop (thus the breaking sound), rushed up the steps and held me in place or turned right side up, taking care not to step on my glasses or scratch my face (I bet they trim their nails short and filed smooth). I mean, does Taiwan train its mass transit staff like S.W.A.T. or Navy Seals? Seriously.I am definitely writing a formal letter of gratitude to the Taiwan HSR authority to express my amazement that their 6 highly train staff (2 who delivered me and my luggage from the escalator to my seat, 2 who inspected the escalator before restarting it shortly, the 1 nurse who anointed then bandaged my pinky after rattling off medical allergy list and gave me instruction on how to use the ice pack and care for my swollen pinky in the next few days, and the 1 record keeper who came by to write down my last name and cell number and inquire as to the cause of my pinky injury) dissipated a major disaster and disruption into a non-event. Now I picked up my ticket at the counter at 15:16, that's another amazing story of gracious and humble civil servant which will have to wait for another time, the bullet train took off at exactly 15:31. Consider that I had to figure out how to get pass the turn-stiles, the whole event transpired in less than 15 min. I have reservations about many things Taiwan (or Taiwanese), but this I must say,Taiwan HSR, your people ARE the BEST in the world! Bar none.

Since Tripadvisor don't let me select June 2015, I would mention it in advance. Family and i used this HSR train couple years go when we took a day trip to Kaohsiung to see the Fo Guang Shan Monastery. There were other ways(plane bus, taxi) to get there but we choose this method because it was the least stressful for us. He train is similar to one of the bullet train that we took when we were in Japan. Train was fast. We got there in about 2 hrs. On our return trip, we again took the train back to Taipei. If you want to see the Monastery, do take the train. And don't take taxi or bus like my friend. She took it and she got to spent about an hour at Fo Guang Shan before closing.

It is an indispensable part of transportation in western Taiwan. Although some extra stops will delay some time, it is still time-saving and fast overall. Early bird tickets or student tickets can save a lot.

We took the high-speed train from central Taiwan to Taipei, and all four of us were thoroughly impressed. It was the cleanest train I've ever seen anywhere. They have vending machines onboard, and even a room for mothers who are breastfeeding. The train was right on time, and the ride was so fast and smooth that we arrived at our destination in the wink of an eye. Outstanding. Why can't we have a system like this in the States?

Taiwan's Shinkansen. I used it when going to Kaohsiung and Taichung. HSR (High speed rail) means Shinkansen in Taiwan. Foreign tourists have a three-day unlimited ride ticket, which allows them to travel around Taiwan at a very reasonable price.

Compared with a few years ago, the hardware has not improved, but this may just be because mainland China is catching up. The highlight is still the service, the warm greetings with smiles, snacks and drinks, I am still satisfied.

I used the high-speed train from Taichung to Taipei Nangang Railway Station (which is the final stop, and were my hotel was located).This service is excellent, fast, safe, efficient and clean. And is by far faster than driving by car.

OK, first time on the high-speed train and it didn't disappoint.  The speed was well managed by the conductor so that you didn't feel any of the forces involved in traveling so fast.  Very roomy, and the food was awesome!

Easy purchase of tickets at Taipei Station and because of its speed you can choose many destinations for one-day travel. It flies.....in fact the interior is similar to being in a plain with comfortable seats and commuters clearly informed of their whereabouts on the chosen journey. A great experience!

I used it to travel from Taipei Main Station to Taoyuan International Airport. The station locations at Taipei Main Station are clearly marked and tickets are easy to purchase. Taoyuan Station, which is close to Taoyuan International Airport, is not directly connected to the airport, and it takes about 20 minutes to transfer to the airport by bus. Tickets are easy to buy and the inside of the train is clean.

It is faster than the regular subway and the distance between stations is long. It is also used when moving from the airport to Taipei City, but it can also be used just for transportation. Ground transportation is also a plus factor.

We used the HSR several times during our holiday. From north to south in 11/2 hours and at a speed of 300 km per hour, very normal. Buying tickets is very easy, people speak English. You can reserve the seats. Costs a little more, but when I left my bag on the train I had it back within 4 hours. Top shelf service.

Taiwan's Shinkansen, known as Taiwan High Speed ​​Rail. It is a vehicle similar to Japan's Shinkansen. The seats are also as wide as those on the Joetsu Shinkansen. This time I used the high speed railway 3-day pass. If you make a reservation from a certain website, print out the voucher and bring it to the counter, you can get an unlimited ride ticket for 3 days from the specified date. The ride is very comfortable and the time is accurate. The information about the home etc. is also easy to understand. Eating and drinking are prohibited on public transportation in Taiwan, but you can buy a bento box and bring it in to eat on the high-speed railway. We also sell them internally, so it's similar to the Shinkansen in Japan. It's kind of strange because even the music in the company was the same.

Most of my high speed rail travel is done in China. The stations are cavernous, overcrowded with long lines and overall the experience is worse and worse each year. The Taiwan system on the other hand is completely hassle free and clean. Quiet cars. Ticket lines are never long in my experience. Tickets can also be reserved online by foreigners which can be a challenge  in China. When boarding the train there is no pushing or shoving. Each station I have been too has enough food options even though they are fast food oriented. This system allows me to get to all of my business points in Taiwan clean and comfortably using a centralized location.
Efficient, it puts all the major cities on the island within two hours of Taipei. Value for money on-board catering which is a pleasant surprise for regulars of European trains.

Since moving to Beijing for work, the high-speed rail has become my best means of transportation to and from Beijing. No matter how far away I am from my home, as long as I take the high-speed train, I can rest assured because I know I will be home soon. High-speed rail has been equipped with many preferential programs in recent years. Although the increase in ticket prices is a bit alarming compared to a few years ago, if you make good use of these programs, you can still save some money. In the past few years, several points have been added, which has greatly extended the round-trip time between Beijing and Gaoyang with the number of stops at the stations. I hope that no more stations will be added and the high-speed rail will not become self-reliant. People in other areas can take other connecting public transportation to reach the nearest high-speed rail station. In addition, you may consider looking at the fares of high-speed rail in Europe. High-speed rail in many places in Europe carries farther distances, but the fares are cheaper and more affordable!

The so-called Taiwan Shinkansen is written as High Speed ​​Rail or HSR. I purposely took the train instead of the MRT to go from Taipei to Nangang. It takes 8 minutes and the entire line is underground, but the cheap price of NT$35 for an unreserved seat was enough for a test drive. By the way, non-reserved seats are displayed as "free seats". At Taipei Station, it was difficult to know how to get to the boarding gate, but the information desk kindly gave me directions, so I was able to board the train. I didn't understand it at first, but since ``Tsukidai'' means platform, it seems that we should aim for this display.
We took the Taiwan High Speed Rail several times during our visit. Clean, comfy seats, fast travel between Taipei-Kaohsiung, very on-time

You can go to many locations on the Taiwan Railway. However, if you have the opportunity to buy one, I suggest that when buying a flight, you can buy it more expensively so that you can sit on it. Basically, Taiwan Railway’s trains are very frequent, so it’s very convenient.
There is no difference from Japan's 700 series. I used it when traveling from Taipei to Kaohsiung. I slept the whole way.
Very clean, and the boarding process is always swift and orderly.   There are plenty of   ticketing machine, and  ticketing process very quick and easy.

It was clean, quiet, didn't rattle, and was very comfortable to ride. I thought it might be difficult to get on, but when I desperately typed the kanji of the station name into my smartphone and showed it to the station staff, she politely told me to go to the platform. Taiwanese people are really kind. I was also able to experience the kindness of people.

I used it from Taoyuan to Tainan and from Tainan to Taipei. At Taoyuan, I was able to buy tickets at the counter with a credit card without any problems. However, when I tried to pay by credit card at the ticket vending machine in Tainan, an error occurred, so I decided to pay in cash. All the change came out in coins, so why not double it? It became. The vehicles are the same as those in Japan and lack an exotic feel, but they are safe and secure. I like the greenery of the fields that I can see from the train window, which is typical of Taiwan.
easy to understand for tourist, the cabin was clean and a lot of leg room.. highly recommended for cheap point to point ride..

The fastest, most convenient and efficient but not the most economical mode of transportation. The only thing I would complain about is the cleanliness of the toilets, other facilities are good. The quality of personnel is indeed lacking in education.
I found out that there was a pass online so I bought it, and it was cheap and gave me unlimited rides for 3 days. It was really fast and good. I want to use it next time I travel to Taiwan.

The most convenient choice for traveling in Taiwan, especially for business purposes, the convenience has surpassed the advantages of flying. However, there are fewer direct trains or trains with fewer stops, and there are fewer discounts for frequent travelers.

From Taipei City to Taoyuan Airport, I specifically chose to take the Taiwan High Speed ​​Rail to Taoyuan Station and transfer to the shuttle minibus to the airport. Although the journey only lasted 20 minutes, I still felt the stability of the carriage. Next time I have the opportunity, I will try taking the high-speed rail from north to south.
Its fast, organized, there the railway bento that is a must try which cost NT$100, it taste better when you are travelling on the HSR
We loved it so much we went 3 times. By far the quickest way to get across Taiwan. Seats were spacious and trans left on time to various locations across the country.

Took the HSR from Taipei to Taichung (rtn). Reserved seats. Great way to travel. Most signs in English as well as Chinese.We topped out at 283 kph (~175 mph). The speed is displayed from time to time on the display. Was as smooth as you like. Toilets spotless.A good experience.

Apparently this is the world's fastest and most efficient HSR system. That being said, it was designed to cater more towards business people than tourists. I thought I could take a day trip to Lukang and Tainan, but the train stops about 20 miles from the city center, so you would have to make it an overnight thing and have a lot of money.We still ended up taking a day trip to Zuoying, as this is the only place where the HSR actually stops next to the main tourist attractions. But we ended up paying 200 USD for round trip tickets for 2 people. I would only recommend this train if you don't have a lot of time or money. If you actually want to do some decent site seeing, it's better to just take the TRA and overnight in each town.

If you're ever in Taiwan and looking at traveling around the country, I'd suggest to use the High Speed Rail system. It's quick, efficient and easy to use. I recently used the high speed rail from Taipei to Tainan City to work with one of our clients there for a few days. It's about 317kms and just over 3 hours by high speed rail. I bought the business class fare and the fare was $1780NT, about $60 USD. Traveling to Tainan you come past some scenic landscapes. After working with our client in Taiwan, I traveled to Kaohsiung which is around 40kms away to depart back home to Hong Kong as this city has an international airport conveniently for travelers leaving or entering Taiwan. Kaohsiung itself is another fantastic city to visit in Taiwan and another place I've worked with our another client whom  based there. I'll post my review of this city separately.

This is the second time we have used the Taiwan High Speed Train to travel around this beautiful country.The train is well laid out and very clean, travelling at around 290km per hour you can easily get from on place to another.A must if you want to travel by rail and beats any European train service.

I rode from Taipei to Kaohsiung. Please note that the automatic ticket gates are slightly different from those in Japan. The car body is based on the N700 series, and the seats are wide and comfortable. Announcements are made in three local languages ​​and English. The train windows along the way gave me the illusion that I was in Japan, with mountains, countryside, and city areas. There were many people eating Ekiben.
Clean fast and affordable.  If you want to get north to south or visa versa this is the best way.  HSR is a nice smooth ride with great views.

There's really nothing much to say. Its fast, it gets you there. Its not as crowded as people make it sound to be, on the contrary, maybe it was just us having great timing and luck, but when we rode it? we could see maybe a family, and 3-5 individual travellers.... that's about it.

Brilliant...perfectly on time. Super clean, very efficient and obviously super quick. Highly recommend reserving seats in advance especially if a public holiday. Bilingual displays on the train and announcements. Staff courteous and polite.

It's similar to Japan's Shinkansen. When you purchase your ticket, choose whether you want a non-reserved seat, a reserved seat, or a green car, and decide on a time when you purchase. Credit cards are also accepted. You can choose the English notation on the machine, so you can easily buy it even if you are not at the counter (＾◇＾) The inside is also clean and tidy. Just like in Japan, sweets are sold inside the train. What's different from Japan is that the customers seem to eat pretty much anything without worrying about it, and the person who happened to be sitting next to me was eating coco ichi curry and it smelled amazing, lol.

The fastest and easiest way to go from Taipei to Taichung or Kaoshiung and other stops on the way. You can get reserved and non reserved seats, I recommend the reserved especially during peak times. The cars are so clean and in such good repair that you forget you are on a public train. Sit back and enjoy, it's a great way to travel!

I used this Shinkansen to go from Taipei to Kaohsiung. You can ride with the same feeling as riding in Japan. You can enjoy the scenery quite a bit, so it is recommended for those who like photography.

A very fast moving public transport to central Taiwan. Customers use money to buy time. That is it. It is not cozy, not clean, rubbish on the floor. Be careful, you will get wet during a rainy day as you queue in Tai Chung station platform.

Previously, to get to Kaohsiung from Japan, you had the option of changing planes in Taipei, but after the Shinkansen opened, it seems that there is no longer a connecting flight in Taipei. The vehicle is an old Shinkansen. Both the ride and the contents are exactly like the Shinkansen from a long time ago. In-house advertisements are also advertisements for Japanese companies. Stores at the station include Family Mart, Mosba, Roiho, Ippudo, Yamazaki Pan, Ootoya, Marugame Seimen, etc. It's completely Japanese style. Of course, the ride is comfortable. I'm glad Taiwanese chose Japanese Shinkansen trains instead of European ICEs!

The business seats are naturally very comfortable, and there are newspapers, snacks, hot tea, coffee and mineral water. It is once again reflected that you get what you pay for. But what’s even more valuable is that the regular seats are also great! It will not make you feel like you have fallen from heaven to the bottom when you go from business class to ordinary seats. The spacious distance between the adjacent rows and the front row, comfortable seats, clean carriages and toilets, and excellent train punctuality - for this, all high-speed rail personnel must be given a warm embrace and applause. As far as public transportation is concerned, this is the most comfortable, fast and convenient choice for travel and business!
Convenient, fast, ALWAYS on time.  Handicapped accessible.  Great platform.  Comfy ride.  For business class you get a drink and a small pastry.

I was riding in a regular car using a reserved seat. I was traveling with a suitcase, but there was plenty of space to put my suitcase, and there was plenty of space in front and behind the seats, so it wouldn't be too cramped to put a small carry-on bag at the foot of the seat. It is said to be a Shinkansen made with Japanese technology.

It's just a high speed rail that you wanna have a long distance travel out of the city that you will use. You have to but eat and drink before you get on the rail but the stations in there has all kinds of convenience store and you can find almost everything in it.
In less than 2 hours I had traveled between Taipei to Taichung. The station in Taichung is slightly away from the city. Neat and clean + well maintained.

There is garbage! And there are a lot of people walking around. I don’t sit according to the seat, but the speed is very good. I have a ticket hole~ but I saw people eating in the car. I am not sure whether it is edible. I hope there will be more garbage cans and I think there shouldn’t be so many people walking around in the car!

It only takes 2 hours to get to Tainan, which really saves time and allows you to spend more time having fun. The environment is also very clean and comfortable, the seats are spacious, and the place for storing luggage is very good.

A common problem with high-speed railways is that [Taiwan and high-speed railway stations are far apart]. So was Chiayi Station. However, it is difficult to get to Taipei by Taiwan Railways, so I decided to take the High Speed ​​Rail instead. It took about 20 minutes by bus from Taiwan Railway Station to High Speed ​​Rail Station. Bus fare is free if you have a high speed train ticket. When I showed the screen of the app T-EX, it was OK. It took an hour and a half from Chiayi to Taipei.

I have taken the Taiwan High Speed ​​Rail several times. It has a clean and spacious environment. The lighting is soft and comfortable. It is very stable when driving. You can read a book or take a break on the train. The most important thing is that it saves me a lot of driving time and can get to Taichung or Kaohsiung. It is very convenient.

A very convenient way to travel to the South Taiwan.  You can go to the station via MRT or other public transportation.  Getting the ticket is also easy, you can go to the ticket station in any convenient store. The speed train is quiet and very comfortable. If you visit Taiwan, you should try this out.

1. The ticket sales and station staff are very professional and amiable, and willing to help passengers. 2. The seats are clean, and there are people patrolling the car to collect garbage. 3. Although the ticket price is expensive, you can go from Kaohsiung to Taipei in a short time.

It uses Japanese Shinkansen technology, so it doesn't feel exotic, but it's fast and comfortable. There are many books, and the display is easy to understand. I pre-purchased a discount ticket for foreigners online. It is recommended because it is easy to exchange at the counter (Kaohsiung Zuoying) and the price is reasonable.
The system is efficient and in expensive, It is easy to navigate, and runs till quite late at night.
From the airport into the city it takes less than an hour to get off at Taipei Main Station, Taipei's largest station. Conveniently connect to the subway to other stations or to other cities.

Taiwan's high speed train is one of fastest trains in world. All the high speed rail (HSR) stations are not less than an airport. They are clean, tidy and beautifully built. HSR has now several stations. From Taipei (north end) to Kaohsiung (south end) it just takes 90 minutes.   First,  how to reach there? If you are in Taipei,  you will have to go to Taipei main station. Metro is convenient and stations are connected. So,  you can get into HSR station without exiting out. Cabs are bit costly. Why not take bus if metro is not near!    If you are in Taichung, then you will have to travel to Xinwuri station which is 8 km from Taichung City. Cabs are too costly. Tell you the best travel which is free!  It's the city bus number 159. You need an electronic card which you use for 7/11, metro etc.   Inside the HSR you can get coffee,  tea, snacks and all eateries. So if you are rushing, no worries!  Grab your food inside the HSR.

The train arrives always on time - sometimes it is quite difficult to reserve a seating ticket, especially during rush hours and weekends, and mostly when your final destination is Taipei main station.People are not that noisy as in normal trains but they, sometimes, bring stinky food in the wagons. The connection with the Taoyen airport is a bit problematic as you need to ride a bus to the airport, but generally the service is better than the one offered with the normal train.

I've traveled on high speed rail in Japan and Europe, and the Taiwan HSR compares very well. We purchased vouchers for discount standard-car reserved-seat tickets (available to non-Taiwanese) on-line (through a 3rd party site) and presented the vouchers at the HSR ticket window in the beautiful Taipei Main Station. The HSR ticket agent was extremely helpful and efficient and we were quickly on our way to the platform with our tickets. I was surprised to see that the HSR platform was as well organized as the ticket counter. The location where each car will stop and each door will open is clearly marked on the floor of the platform, as are cue areas for each door - which are used by the locals so that cuing up and boarding is a very efficient process. (The Europeans could learn something from that system.) The train arrived on time, and the doors opened right where the painted indicators on the floor said they would. The seats were comfortable with lots of leg room, fold-down trays, etc.. The train is configured with three seats on one side and two seats on the other. All seats face the same direction. Like most such trains, a storage shelf runs the length of the car above the seats. Great views out the huge windows. The trip was smooth and fast. We took the express (1 stop) from Taipei to Zuoying station (Kaohsiung city) at the southern end of the island and the trip lasted about an hour. A cart came through the car a couple of times during the trip selling snacks (but we brought out own). A great way to see the Eastern mostly agricultural countryside of the island. Highly recommended.
I suggest to use the Hsr by buying tickets at the machibes thst are in English. At 7/11 mostly employees do.not speak English. Good experience, besides of the food smell.

I used it to travel from Taipei to Hualien on my first trip to Taiwan. I was worried about whether I would be able to easily find the ticket counter or boarding gate, but I was able to rely on the electronic signs and was able to do so without any problems. You can feel comfortable on the high-speed railway and time seems to pass quickly.

In the past, the round trip time from Beijing to Gaoyang was less than 4.5 hours. Since the opening of the high-speed rail, it has been shortened to 2 hours in an instant, which can be said to be a symbol of national progress. The ancients said that money can’t buy time. Now you can buy 3 hours of time by spending less than double the money. Isn’t it a good deal?

It only takes two hours from Taipei to Kaohsiung Zuoying, which is twice as fast as the Ziqiang train. It is also more convenient and cheaper than flying. You can also buy Taiwan Railway lunch boxes when you enter the station, and the carriage seats and toilets are very clean.
inexpensive, clean, fast and the network covers all major attractions of New Taipei; the new extension between Airport and Taipei Station offers best value for money.

It is the Japanese build system so close to Shinkan-sen in Japan. Comfortable and you find a train every 10-15 min (though the duration to the south is various because of number of stopping stations).

I used it for a round trip from Taipei to Taichung. You can make reservations online in advance and receive a small discount. The inside of the train was comfortable and felt exactly like a Japanese Shinkansen.
HSRs are Clean. they run on time. HSRs are comfortable / soundproof. They offer good food. (if u cant buy online) Better if u reach early and buy ticket of your choice.

It has been mentioned many times already, but unlike the Chinese Shinkansen, Japanese technology has been inherited, so you can ride with confidence. Although the body and interior coloring are different, the construction is exactly the same. I like that it's easier to read the time than on the expressway, and most importantly, it's cheaper. It is easily accessible from Songshan Airport and Taoyuan Airport, and my main mode of transportation is always the high-speed railway.

First ride to Hsinchu. From Taoyuan Airport, take MRT to Taoyuan High Speed ​​Rail Station. Thanks to the opening of the MRT, access to Hsinchu has become much better. Tickets were easy to buy by referring to blogs on how to buy high-speed railways. Please note that the ticket will be returned to you at the ticket gate at the station you arrive at, so you can receive a commemorative ticket as a souvenir. It takes 11 minutes between Taoyuan and Hsinchu, and non-reserved seats cost 125 yuan, so it's cheap. I got on the train at 8:30pm, but it was so crowded that I had to stand on the deck. It seems like you won't be able to get a free seat if it's this crowded at each stop. As expected, it doesn't shake. Eating and drinking is prohibited on the MRT, but it seems to be OK here, with many locals standing and eating on the station platform. It is a famous story, but the exterior of high-speed railways is extremely dirty. I once again realized how amazing Japan's always shiny Shinkansen trains are. By the way, it is interesting that it is 5 yuan cheaper to take the high-speed railway from Taoyuan to Taipei (non-reserved seat) than to take the Taoyuan MRT to Taipei. Aside from Taipei, people staying at the Courtyard Marriott in Nangang may also enjoy going via the high-speed railway.

You can go between the airport and Taipei without transferring. The price is 160 Taiwan Yuan, which is about 700 yen. There are about 4 flights per hour. If you take the rapid train, you will arrive in about 35 minutes. It just opened in the spring of this year, so both the cars and the station are clean.

I'm currently riding a high-speed train in Taiwan. After riding the train, I was able to understand anew what I had been hearing on the news. It is exactly the same as the Tokaido Shinkansen. I realized that the Shinkansen itself was an export of Japanese technology. I think the same person is speaking the English announcements as well. I was also surprised to see Japanese-made sweets for sale inside the train. The packages are written in Japanese, such as so-called Pocky and Koala March. It's comfortable and fast, so give it a try. thank you.

We took the High speed rail to Chiayi and wow what an experience. Train is clean and spacious. Seats in the train are turned around in the direction that the train is travelling, therefore for those that have a problem traveling backwards this will not happen. For bigger groups traveling together you can even turn the seats around so everyone can sit together. There is even a cart service on the train offering snacks and drinks.
We took high speend rail from taipei to kaoshuing. We book the ticket on line and went to taipei station to collect the ticket.The high speed rail is clean and on time

Just returning from a 10 day visit and cannot say one negative comment about the whole experience! The people are welcoming, friendly and helpful even when they have little English or none at all .The country is clean and easy to find your way around on the rail, metro , bus , bike or foot. The food is wonderful esp in the night markets! You can even buy beer at 7-11 which are everywhere . A very inexpensive trip that is really high quality !
Took the train from Taipei to Hualien, spacious, clean and fast.  The chairs inclined and you can take a nap in these comfortable chairs.

It is not easy to maintain a relationship between the south and the north. In my date with my old man, the high-speed rail plays a crucial role. The high-speed rail shortens transportation time and increases the time we spend together. The key point is...it is less likely that you will be discouraged from setting off because of the driving time. Sometimes you can even just leave!

We took the high speed train from Hualien( to see Taroko Gorge) back to Taipei. It took us only about 2 hours as opposed to the private van and driver from Taipei to Hualien which took us about 4 hours due to heavy traffic. There are portions of the ride with great views,i suggest to stay on the right side of the train. The train is immaculately clean and comfortable. Buy your tickets early when travelling on weekends or holidays.

It uses improved Japanese-made vehicles, and the ride quality is comparable to that of Japan's Shinkansen. I also rode the China Shinkansen, but the Taiwan Shinkansen is better in terms of cleanliness, service, and satisfaction. If you are going to Kaohsiung (Zuoying), we recommend purchasing a sightseeing pass. Although it does take some time to present your passport and pass at the ticket gate, you can receive a discount that more than makes up for it, and if you use a tour ticket, the more you ride, the more you save.
Relexing way to travel fast through Taiwan, close your eyes and before you know it your entering your destination station.

The seats are very comfortable to sit on, and the speed to and from the Beijing Expressway is fast and stable. There is also a personal dining rack similar to that of an airplane. Someone will pick up passengers’ garbage every one or two stops to keep the entire carriage clean. Although the price is a bit expensive and the discounted fare is very difficult to get, overall the service quality is worthy of the price.

There are 2 train stations in Tainan so make sure you are clear which one your ticket is for.The High Speed Rail station is around 40 mins from Tainan and there is a frequent free shuttle bus to the town centre (various stops on route).We arrived from Alishan at the local station which was in town .Took this on a late Sunday afternoon, fortunately we had reserved seats as it was very busy . We tried to catch an earlier train and stood in the unreserved line but it was so busy.( more flexiblity than UK. Stand in one of the unreserved queues and  if you can find a seat you can travel on an earlier train)Plenty of legroom and storage on the train.Announcements also in English.

This is not a bullet train like in Japan, and it frequently stops, but the seats are very comfortable (bring a sweater the air condition is extremely high) and the staff incredibly polite. Before the train arrives to Taipei, a member of staff takes all the rubbish (like in planes), wish we had the same service  in Europe

Usually there are mostly business people, so the car is mostly quiet. There are many ways to buy and sell tickets, and there is no need to queue at the window. Make good use of online ticket purchasing to save a lot of time.

You should reserve in advance to get a slightly cheaper price than usual. The high-speed train lives up to its name. Clean seats, bathrooms, and drinks dispensers available for use. On normal floors, along the way there will be employees selling beverages and snacks along the way.

I use it to travel to Taichung and have no complaints. The price is also cheap! (Taipei → Taichung 700 yuan) The inside of the train is mostly comfortable, but Taiwanese people usually talk on their cell phones. (lol)

I found the train clean and easy to buy tickets for. At one stop I had time on my hands and found that I could leave my luggage at the station for a small price and tour the area.  It is air conditioned.

The high-speed rail service is super considerate. If you can't catch the high-speed rail by plane, you can actually enter the high-speed rail station manually as long as you arrive on the same day. If possible, I really recommend that the high-speed rail can set up parent-child carriages. Otherwise, if there are children screaming and crying behind the seats, it will really be impossible to have a good rest.

This is almost the Nozomi of Japan's Tokaido Shinkansen. There is only a slight difference in design, but the sound while riding is also the same. I rode from Taichung to Taipei. I don't think it took an hour.
You can get from Taipei to Kaohsiung Zuoying Station in 94 minutes at the fastest time. The ride is comfortable and doesn't shake much. The office is also clean.
I was able to easily make a reservation in Japanese and travel to Taichung comfortably. This Shinkansen will take you to Kazutsu-tan in just over 2 hours. Recommended

The requirements for the public transportation system are nothing more than punctuality, comfort, convenience, cleanliness, and friendly service. So far, Taiwan's high-speed rail has performed fairly well in these points, giving Taiwan's pride a high rating.

I've only used it for a short trip (wanted to try it) from Taoyuan to the end of the line. Clean, punctual, decent space in the 2nd class. Ticket machines are a bit confusing. Advance tickets can be a lot cheaper.

I couldn't get on last time because it was full, so I made a reservation online this time. When I tried to go through the ticket gate an hour before departure to take a photo of the Shinkansen on the platform, it beeped, and when I asked an old man nearby why, he told me in Japanese that it was an hour early ♪(๑ᴖ◡ᴖ๑)♪ I had heard that the Shinkansen uses Japanese technology, but it was like riding a Shinkansen in Japan d(^_^o). It was safe, secure and comfortable!

The station is spacious and clean. Unlike the inside of a station in Japan, the train is not crowded with people. Just like the Shinkansen in Japan, the train is a space where you can relax. I was surprised that there was also on-board sales.

According to the guide's explanation, Japan's Shinkansen trains are being introduced through bidding. It's like being in Japan in a familiar office setting. The time was accurate, and it was neat and clean. In-house sales also came, but I didn't use them this time. I would like to try ekiben.

I bought a 3-day high speed rail pass, and even though I arrived in the evening, I made full use of it, including going to Hsinchu for dinner. The next day I made a round trip to Zuoying (the last station on the Kaohsiung side), and on the last day I went back to Tainan, so I was able to save enough money. The train cars are almost the same as the JR Tokaido Shinkansen, and there are also on-board sales, including coffee and Haagen-Dazs ice cream. Ekiben is also sold for NT$100 during lunch and dinner hours. The problem is that the stations, except for Taipei Station, are far from the city center. Hsinchu is 30 minutes away on the high speed train, but you need to take a 25 minute conventional line, and the same goes for Tainan. Zuoying is connected to Kaohsiung MRT, so it might be better if you can go there directly from downtown. Also, the toilets are not as good as those on the recent Tohoku Shinkansen trains, and there are no charging outlets.

Shinkansen imported from Japan. It is popular among tourists because it is cheap and allows you to get around quickly, but it is said to be in the red because it is being looked down upon by the locals...and there are rumors that its survival is in jeopardy as prices seem to go up frequently.

It is convenient for traveling around the west coast of Taiwan. The image is exactly what Japan's Shinkansen was like a little while ago. It was written that there would be on-board sales, but I didn't come across any. If you expect to be hungry or thirsty, we recommend that you prepare before riding. The timetable is almost accurate, and there are frequent trips between Taipei and Taipei.

I used it when going from Taipei Station to Tainan. The speed is reminiscent of Japan's Shinkansen, and you can get a nice view from the train window. If you can get tickets at a convenience store in advance, you can buy them cheaply. Passengers other than those on the train you are boarding are not allowed on the platform, so please check the timetable and be careful.

It's almost the same as Japan's Shinkansen, but Taiwan's doors were not sensor-operated, but opened by pressing a button. Business class? When you board the vehicle, you will receive free cookies and coffee.

If you are traveling between Taipei and Kaohsiung for work, I think it would be a good idea to arrange a 3-day high speed railway pass for overseas travelers in advance. It is also convenient to take the MRT from Taoyuan High Speed ​​Rail Station to the airport during this period. The station buildings for each station are also unique. Enjoy station and high-speed railway original souvenirs.

It is very convenient to book high-speed rail tickets online, and this time you get an early bird discount. With the confirmed number, when we arrived in Taiwan, we could print the tickets at the 7-11 near the hotel, which was very convenient and simple.
It is a great way to get around Taiwan.  There are people that come around and sell food and drinks or you can order before you leave.

Last night I booked a ticket on this and went to pay with my Amex, which I found out isn't accepted.  I emailed customer service immediately as you have three days or so to purchase a booked ticket.  They called me this a.m. at 7:45 my time to walk me through payment by VISA which is accepted regardless of bank location.  Very prompt and courteous, just like the trains themselves!

It was the first time i take high speed rail. It save 1/4 timing more normal and no need check-in or check-out. Great experience! Speed sometime become more 300km/h. It's easy to buy ticket & convenience directly or by automotive machine.

It is suitable for long-distance journeys in major cities in the north and south (for example: Taipei-Kaohsiung). It is very fast and convenient. Cleaning operations are carried out after every passenger ride, so the interior is clean and comfortable. During meal time, they sell high-speed rail bento boxes, which are quite hearty and well worth the money. Discount tickets include early bird tickets and college student tickets, which can save a lot of money. The only disadvantage is that the price is not cheap, and a few stations are far away from the city center and the transportation is inconvenient, so before booking a ticket, you must first confirm whether the place you want to reach is suitable for high-speed rail.
I took a round trip to Kaohsiung, and it took about 1 hour and 30 minutes at the earliest, so it was very convenient. The ekiben was delicious and just as comfortable as the Shinkansen in Japan.

Because of my credit card upgrade, I fly business class twice a month because it is very comfortable and spacious, and you can charge your phone. Every time I order a cup of hot tea and a bottle of mini mineral water, and then ask the lady to give me a copy of "Business Weekly", plus exquisite snacks. It is really the biggest reward of the trip. Often I have arrived at the station before I finish reading a magazine, and I have to get off the bus reluctantly. I often see celebrities in business class, such as: Li Changyu, Lian Shengwen, Chen Tingfei, Zhan Qixian... They are all newsmakers I meet. Although I don't disturb them, I also give myself a surprise. Another time I met Professor Hang Tai of Chengdu University and invited him to give a lecture on the spot. Isn’t it very convenient? You might as well fly business class next time!
Travelled from Taipei to Tainan and Kaoshiung and back to Taipei. The trains were clean, well lighted, airy, smooth and comfortable.
I was going from Taipei to Tainan to play a golf tournament.  I mistakenly bought a ticket that stop at every station, so it took me 40 min longer to get there.. which i almost missed the Tee time.

im from osaka, japan and i take the high speed train to tokyo all the time. this high speed train in taiwan is very reminiscent of the trains we have at home. they are comfortable, clean, and convenient. its costs a bit more but definitely a good way to travel from taipei to tainan then taichung.

It is the most convenient means of transportation to travel between the north and south of Taiwan. The seats are very comfortable. If you want to drink hot drinks or eat snacks, there are waiters on the bus at any time. The waiters at the station are also very enthusiastic to guide passengers~

It is a good means of transportation. It only takes half a day to travel between Taipei and Kaohsiung, which greatly shortens the commuting time. Although the fare is not cheap, it is a good experience to ride it occasionally. I look forward to the opening of the new station.
I was a little disappointed because the speed of the train only reached 295kph.  But this was fast enough.It was a smooth ride and the service was excellent.I'm glad I experienced the HSR service.

This will be my first option to go to Taipei from Tainan (comparing to trains or buses), Make sure you check the travel time as it's might be about 15 mins different of arrival time. It's comfortable and quiet while moving. You can buy a special package from the travel agent if holding overseas passport (better discount).
I would like to advise the Italo gentlemen to try this train once... so maybe they understand how a super-fast train should go!

It only takes 50 minutes to get to Taipei from Taichung. The seats are spacious and the trains are very frequent. There is a bus every 15 minutes. It’s quick to buy tickets while you wait, you can pay with a credit card, usually 700NT per ticket, there are discounts at Li Feng (OFF-PEAK HOUR)~

It is a very convenient means of transportation for people traveling between north and south. It can be reached within 2 hours one way, breaking the time limit of past transportation. However, the ticket price is very expensive, and I heard that the price will increase again recently.

Travelled from Taipei to Kaohsiung then to Taichung. I spent a week travelling around Taiwan and the bullet train was the most convenient and fastest form of transportation around the island. You can bring food onto the train or purchase food from the attendants on the train. There are two types of tickets: 1) pre-booked seats, or 2) regular tickets (no seat selection, first come first served)

The train speed is fast! The train speed is stable! The service staff is friendly! The fare is a bit expensive! Early bird tickets are not easy to buy!!! There are not many connections between trains and high-speed rail, which makes it difficult to control the time, so I always choose direct trains...
Comfortable and easy to book. Punctuality is the top priority and the willingness to help, as in the rest of Taiwan, is immense.

It is convenient to go back and forth in a short time. Only after the high-speed train, there is a transfer. It is very convenient and the time is short. The space is very large even for ordinary seats. You will not feel tired after taking a short time. Although the ticket price is a bit expensive, convenience still wins.

Obtaining tickets was a lot less tiresome with significantly less queues than for the normal railway (in the stations's main hallway on the ground floor).Train ride was smooth and comfortable, managed to get to Taichung in about 45 minutes on the express train.
not difficult to reach the train station from the airport, but it is far to walk in taipei station. Really easy to get lost in the subway.
Unlike Train service in my country, the service staff are very friendly and train are very nicely maintain, speed was fast and estimated time of arrival are very accurate!

There was no porter to take the escalator to the basement, so I had to carry large luggage by myself.It is recommended to carry less luggage.From Taoyuan to Chiayi 1 hour 15 minutes From Kaohsiung to Taipei 1 hour 30 minutes I took the green car No. 6. Drinks are all you can drink. All-you-can-eat cake, towels included, coffee, freshly made hot water, so I brought it back because it was a 250cc plastic bottle.One employee will clean the restroom, so you can use it comfortably.There are 2 seats in the green car.There are 2 seats.Groups will not be separated.No Wi-Fi.There is an outlet.You can charge your smartphone.We arrived while we were eating and drinking.It was very comfortable.By the way, there are 3 seats in the regular car, and 2 seats.It's the same as on the Shinkansen in Japan.

Took speed trains to both Hualien and Taichung for tour of Taroko Gorge and Sun Moon Lake. The trains are fast and clean and there's toilets on board the trains.The good thing is some of the trains have extra carriages at the back of the train meant for passengers with unreserved seats. This means one can take an earlier train back to Taipei as Long as one has a back to Taipei train ticket for the same day and as Long as their's empty seats in those "unreserved" seats carriages. That was exactly what we did when we returned from Taichung. Our scheduled departure was ard 7.30pm but we took the 6.32pm train back to Taipei and were seated in carriage 11. Our tickets were checked during the ride but we have no issue at all.
Travelled from Hsinchu to Taipei.Very efficient and on-time serviceClean & fastStaff at the station and on the platforms was very helpful

I used it to go from Taipei to Tainan. Since it was an overnight trip, I bought a 3-day high speed train tour ticket. It's as comfortable as the Japanese Shinkansen. There were also wagon sales inside the car.

"Take the high-speed train and eat lunch" is one of the traveling cultures of Taiwanese people. During our trip to Taiwan, we took the high-speed rail from Taipei to Kaohsiung and back. Haha, it was a complete experience of Taiwan's high-speed rail. The comfort level is good, but the maximum speed is only 200 kilometers. Maybe it’s because of the mountainous area~

Fastest transportation for travel between north end and south end of Taiwan, very well maintained and always on-time performance.Even though bit expensive tickets, we could save lot of travel time. Also, you can avail free shuttle bus service from HSR station to downtown in most of the stations.As most of the announcements / displays are in English, it will be convenient for foreigners too.

The Taiwanese high speed rail is great! From Taipei to Kaohsiung was like less than 50 USD for the business class, which is not much more than the regular class and the seat is HUGE and very comfortable and there's attendant comes over with little treats and drinks to choose from multiple times throughout the whole ride. Not to mention the ride is quiet, smooth and very fast of course.My picky husband is impressed as well, highly recommended!

I like to book at seven-11 (any convenient store is fine) using IBON machine as it's convenient and you get a Starbuck voucher. You can book early to get the Early Bird discount. Watch out for public holidays as tickets sell out very quickly

How long does it take to get from Taipei to Kaohsiung?! Taiwan's high-speed rail can help travelers move quickly and reach the farthest and most distant places in the least time. It is definitely suitable for travelers who need to rely on public transportation.

I went from Taoyuan to Hsinchu with an unreserved seat. At the ticket counter on the day of the event, reserved seats are sold out. I came every 15 to 20 minutes, and at the platform I waited in line just like in Japan. The first train that came was as crowded as during Japan's Obon holiday, with people standing up to the deck. The next one was at a station on the way, so I was able to get on it as it was empty.

My first night in Taoyuan and I noticed that I need to be in Ningxia Market by 9PM.  So I chose the 705 bus to Taoyuan Main Station and took the HSR to Taipei Main station.  For NTD180 it's just 30 minutes and I wanted to see more than wait on the bus.  This option was the best for me!

Traveled to and from Kaohsiung and Taipei.  The high speed rail ways are very fast, clean, and easy to navigate.  The cost was reasonable given the distance and time it took to travel.  The trains were always exactly on time.

I have taken high-speed rail in about 4 countries. Although my evaluation cannot be too comprehensive, based on the high evaluation of Taipei MRT, I think the overall quality of Taiwan's high-speed rail is not inferior to that of the MRT. Perhaps thanks to the overall quality of Taiwanese people, it is definitely the top public transportation in the world. I give it 5 stars and 93 points.

You can get advance tickets online to enjoy early bird discounts but if you are not sure of your timing, you can get them at the counter too. Very convenient to switch between different parts of Taiwan with this HSR system.

With the high-speed rail, my life has become more convenient. Whether I am working, traveling or going home, I cannot live without the high-speed rail. It increases my work opportunities and allows me to travel back and forth easily and conveniently in a short time. It increases my time to travel and hang out with friends. Thank you high speed rail

We started in Kaohsiung and 90 mins later got off in Taipei, a great trip. Very clean train and seats were good, big windows to watch the landscape fly buy. Snacks were sold on board and a light board explanaing where you were and how fast you were going (288kms). Get your tickets the day before travel for assigned seats.
It's very fast and saves a lot of traffic time. Although the cost is also more expensive. "However, some trains stop at unnecessary stations, causing a waste of time, so I cannot give five stars."

Whilst travelling from Taipei to Tainan in the south on the HSR, unintentionally I left this phone with which I am writing this review on the train. Realised it was missing after I left the station and had to return to report it. Within 5 hours, it was back in my hands and hence this review. Wonderful service, excellent interior comfort and condition. Fast travel from north to south. On time. Highly recommended. Well done to the staff of the HSR and the organisation and thank you very much.
Super convenient way to get to the Gloria Outlets in Taoyuan!Clean and efficient. We bought non reserved seats and it was totally okay. You can eat on the train.

Taiwan's HSR brings commuters to different locations around the country. Tickets can be purchased online in advance & you will enjoy a ''early bird discount'' subject to availability.  Mainly there are 3 types of tickets, non - reserved seats, reserved seats & business class.During a normal day, getting the non - reserved seats tickets would be sufficient. Their seats are very spacious & comfortable. You will be able to purchase a bento from most of their stations to bring along with you on board. Toilets & vending machines are available on selected train sections. On selected trains, there will be a trolley selling food & drinks going around.

An efficient and much quicker way of travelling than surface traffic.  Metro stations all have information booths at ticket office with someone who can help direct.  Trains are clean, speedy, and reach most of the central attractions.  Some of the stations are worthy of a look of how modern the city has become.
Very convenient mean of transportation. Fast. Comfortable. Tickets can be bought via Internet or at the station.

Whether you are visiting Taiwan for business or pleasure, the High Speed rail is the best choice for you to move around major cities. As an example, the High Speed Rail can take you from Taipei to Kaohsiung (300 kilometers) in less than 2 hours. It is fast, comfortable, and efficient. The ticket price is merely around US$50 for the trip. And if you are a senior citizen over 65 years of age, you get 50% off the ticket price. Highly recommended.

We took this train from Taipei to Kaohsiung at speeds up to 300kph its a must do experience. However, make sure you get the right ticket. We got the 3-day Unlimited but it's not quite so unlimited as it is restricted. The owners of the THSR must sort this out! All the brilliant technology this country uses on the trains etc. it's letting itself down by resorting to staff having to physically write down each of your journeys into a pass book. You also as a foreigner MUST have your passport with you, they check it every time you travel on this train. Surely they can get a fully automated booking system where you add your details once and travel around as often as you like on a single ticket that gets you through the ticket barriers over the 3-day or 5-day period. Other than that it's a once in a lifetime experience that everyone should do.

I took the THSR constantly during my last job. It's the fastest and most economic way to get from Taipei to Kaoshiung considering there are not many flights now. The interior is well maintained, and acceleration is smooth regardless of the high speed. Just remember to book the direct train (which stops only at 2 other stations before arriving at KS) and avoid rush hours (6:30-8:00 weekdays, slightly later on weekends) if possible. There are localized shops in each station, which are also fun to explore.

My colleague and I spent a couple of days visiting friends in Taipei before going to Taichung.  Traveled to Taichung in the HSR.  It was very nice.  We traveled business, since there were places in the car for the luggage we had.  The whole trip cost about $30 American to travel from Taipei to Taichung.
Convenient and super-fast for getting around Taiwan. Very punctual, in a few hours I reached Kaohsiung in the city center.

From Taoyuan Airport, you usually take a bus to Taoyuan Airport Railway Station, and then transfer to the high-speed rail to downtown Taipei. If you book your tickets in advance, the bus and high-speed rail fare only costs over a hundred New Taiwan dollars. The most important thing is that you can avoid traffic jams and make it easy to control your time.

I have been from Tai Chung to Taipei for less than an hour. I bought number seat and is not a really pleasant experience as I wish to be my friend side but there is no more seat. However I will prefer people to buy free seating ticket. Basically the rail is quite comfortable and is clear instruction to passenger where we are and when will reach. The only thing was the high speed rail is quite away from central of Tai Chung, you may need to take taxi to reach there. There will be another cost.

The Airport Railroad has just opened. You can take the express rail from the airport to Taipei Main Station. As of April 2017, it costs 160 won and can be used as an Easy Card. It may have been because it just opened, but it kept stopping along the way, but it was convenient to use. However, it was difficult because it was too far from Taipei Main Station to the platform.

Booking tickets through the mobile APP is convenient, punctual and efficient. Frequent shifts and many choices. The food, drinks and gifts sold on the bus are all reasonably priced. Friendly service, professional attentiveness, and clean high-speed rail carriages are the pride of Taiwan.
Best way to go north/south on the west coast of Taiwan...comfortable,good frequency,reliable schedule...business class is even nicer and worth the extra money ..freebees..

In the mainland, it is not that convenient to buy Taiwan Railway tickets. During Taiwan holidays, you need to buy Taiwan Railway tickets early. The Taiwan Railway's seat space is larger than that in China. The Taiwan Railway's bento is very cheap, only NT$80. The taste is just like an ordinary bento, which is quite good.

This is our family's first time travelling on the HSR so we thought we should try both the Business and Standard Class.We booked the tickets online more than a month before our scheduled trips which gave us better selection of the seats and timings, best of all, we could get discounted fares on Standard Class tickets.Business class, though no discount but we got better service, more leg room for the seats and shorter travel time like about 1.5 hour from Taipei to Zuoying. The travelling time was sufficient to enjoy the bento which we bought from the rail station.Standard Class, much cheaper with the discount, travelling time slightly longer but it didn't matter when we travelled from Zuoying to Taichung and from Taichung to Taipei which both trips were last than an hour.As for the baggage area, quite limited if you were to travel with many large ones. So it's better to book online to select the seats near the baggage area and queue earlier so you can secure a space for the bigger luggage. For smaller ones like 24" and below, the overhead compartment are available above the seats.The trains we took left and arrived on time.Overall, we had a pleasant experience and won't hesitate to take the HSR when in Taiwan.

Going by train through Taiwan offers you the best possibility to understand and enjoy the different type of landscape and culture. You swish by the Taiwanese “Silicon Valley” and in the next heartbeat; you are on the countryside looking at how farmers are cultivating their lands in the old traditional way. Moreover, you can do all this from a very comfortable rail service with wide seats, which you can turn around so that you can sit in a group of 4 face to face. The train is a high-speed train with all mod cons of course including a good food and drink service. Although it is not the cheapest way of transport (check out the bus transport network between cities) it is one of the most comfortable and enjoyable ways of travelling thru the country.
Fast, clean, safe. much cheaper than airplane and much more faster if door to door. And arriving in better shape.

Taipei high speed train system (HSR) of Taiwan is one of the best systems in the world. Service is very smooth, wonderful cleaning and announcing system is adapted. Stations are made with full facilities as airports.I am very happy. I suggest to others to use this facility.

It's very clean, quiet, fast, smooth train with not bad service. If you can make sure your date/time in advance, suggest you pick the direct line (less stops) train with same price.You may buy ticket through machine or at counter (many people in line) with cash or credit card, both very easy.

Just like Japan's Shinkansen, you can travel very comfortably. If you don't have many people, it's perfectly fine to buy them at the station on the day. But be careful. It is not as easy to get a reserved seat on Taiwan's regular trains as it is on high-speed trains. This is especially difficult on the eastbound route from Taipei. You might be surprised to think that everything can be done like a high-speed train, so be careful.
It is a easy and continence and fast travel tool for  travelling on the West Taiwan. But the price was a little bit high for economic traveler.

We took the shuttle from the airport and booking a ticket was simple at the station from machines or desk. $200 TWD got us to our destination which was great value for such a comfortable and quick journey. Train was on time, very clean, comfortable seats and easy to know when to get off.

My friends from South Africa arrived in Keelung (Taiwan) on 5th April by ship. The ship only docked here for one day and was scheduled to leave at 6 o' clock. Because I had to teach in the morning, I didn't have any time to waste when I left school. Well, what more I can say than:  Thank you Taiwan High Speed Rail for getting me to Tapei 101 in 21 MINUTES! It's CLEAN and so CONVENIENT. Yes, aren't we lucky to have a High Speed Rail? My country, where I come from doesn't have this luxury, therefore I definitely can appreciate it!

The HSR is the fastest andmost efficient way to travel around Tw. The tickets are a bit expensive but saves a lot of time. Food and bervages are sold on board. Cleaning lady will come collect your trash so it is fairly clean. Downside is they don't have USB charge outlet nor wifi.

Traveling in a new country can elevate stress levels, even for the most experienced international travelers. Recently, I had to make travel arrangements from Taipei to Kaoshiung, in the southern part of Taiwan. Having had a comical encounter with a Chinese language on-line ticket booking site, I decided to go to the main train station, in search of human assistance.A capable representative of the Taiwan High Speed Rail (THSR) quickly helped me to get my tickets. On the date of the departure, I arrived early to double-check which gate the train would be departing from, the train number and the time. Reassured that all was in order, I thanked the THSR representative and waited quietly for the train to come. It was a short wait. Other passengers and I boarded the train and off we went.However, it was not until four stops later, when other passengers were departing and others were getting on, that a young man, politely approached the seat that I was sitting in and showed me his ticket. I was in his seat.This was a surprise. Soon his friends and other passengers were gathering around to try to figure out what had happened. Train schedules were googled and it soon became apparent that I had been guided by very cordial representative back in Taipei to the wrong train.This young man, whose seat I had taken, quickly offered to stand until he reached his destination, some thirty minutes farther on down the rails. I offered to find another seat. Others quickly offered him their seat and then lo and behold, a kind lady found me a seat several rows back from where I had been sitting. People were so kind and even offered me a sandwich.This mix-up was handled calmly, with humor and good will. I continue to marvel at how kind the Taiwanese people on that train were to two complete strangers, a Taiwanese student and a lady from another country.in thinking about this experience, I would recommend having your travel details  written in Chinese. Otherwise, it was a smooth and cross-cultural travel adventure.

It was almost time to board the train, so we took out our mobile phones, opened the high-speed rail mobile app, and entered the gate using the ticket QR code on our mobile phones. In reality, it is a prime example of chronic time distortion. Trains arrive late, are canceled or don't even leave - and this happens as if it were part of the concept. The announcements sound like mockery: “Unfortunately the train is canceled today.” Unfortunately? This is not an unfortunate isolated case, this is the rule.📱 Digital offers - an app to break the habit The DB Navigator app is a masterpiece of digital frustration. Crashes, incorrect information, cryptic error messages - if you're looking for a connection here, you'll at best find one that causes your own inner despair. The user interface looks like it was designed by an IT intern who just figured out how to program buttons.🚽 Condition of the trains - rolling ruins with a toilet surprise The trains themselves are a mix of museum and construction site. Air conditioning only works when the outside temperature is below 5 degrees, the seats are sagging like the passengers' morale, and the toilets - well, anyone who uses them should make a will beforehand. Hygiene is a foreign word here, maintenance is apparently a myth.💰 Pricing policy - luxury prices for lottery experiences The ticket prices are absurd. You pay the equivalent of a flight to Barcelona for an ICE ticket, but in return you get a trip with an uncertain outcome. The railway is the only company that charges premium prices for gambling: Is the train coming? Is he driving through? Are there seats? Nobody knows. But you pay in advance.🎩 Management - an ivory tower of excuses and PowerPoint slides The railway's management level lives in a parallel reality in which delays are "operational challenges" and total failures are "customer-oriented optimizations". Responsibility is avoided like an empty train at rush hour. Instead of solutions there are PR phrases, instead of reforms there are strategy papers that nobody reads - probably not even the authors.🧱 Infrastructure - a patchwork of construction sites and excuses The rails are a puzzle of construction sites, closures and "technical disruptions". The train stations look like post-apocalyptic meeting places for commuters with broken dreams. And when construction happens, it does so at the speed of a sedated sloth. Their timetables are like a koan from Zen: seemingly contradictory, only understandable through deep meditation. Unfortunately, my body is not yet completely in nirvana, but stands freezing on platform 4, while my connecting train of course left without me - another precious lesson about impermanence and the absence of control. Ironically call the whole thing “rail comfort”. I call it a composition of incompetence, ignorance and innovative disinterest in the customer. Your app is like a digital oracle - it speaks in riddles, disappears when necessary and shows me trains that only exist in a parallel world. Don't get me wrong: I have compassion - even for your staff, who are often just as perplexed as the travelers. But at some point you have to ask yourself: Is this still a transport company or already a performance art project called “Waiting is Progress”? I don’t expect miracles. Just every now and then a train that works, a piece of information that's true, or an apology that doesn't sound like an autoresponder. With that in mind, may your company get back into balance soon - and if not, maybe I'll just start my own company. It will be called “The Line of the Dragon”, it runs on time, has warm seats - and no room for excuses. With determined composure, Mario San

Several large compartments were reserved exclusively for BahnBonus Gold and Platinum customers - in a short train! This meant that conflicts and arguments between the passengers were inevitable. Despite having a reservation and a paid ticket for the original train, you felt like a tolerated, annoying third-class passenger who had to make room for the premium passengers. What a "great" experience! What can the DB do better:> Use longer trains and replacement trains when it is already foreseeable that with such a high volume of bookings, the failure of a single ICE train will result in total chaos! > Introduce a reservation requirement in long-distance transport, such as with the Austrian Westbahn, this would create an effective instrument for the company for passenger management. Rebookings in the event of train cancellations could be controlled in a targeted manner and promptly communicated to those affected via an app.> Deploy additional staff to support stranded passengers at the train stations/platforms - we see this regularly in similar situations abroad and it seems to work excellently there (experienced by myself in: GB, AT, CH).> And there are no excuses here, such as: "poor planning; no running trains; lack of staff" etc. After all, you get your "service" from the customers pay handsomely!Other:Friendly and humorous train staff.For the unfortunate DB employees on the customer front, humor is probably the healthiest way to cope with everyday work in this - to a large extent dysfunctional - company. Conclusion for me/us:Despite having a BahnCard for all family members, it no longer makes sense to rely on the DB for long-distance transport. Added to this is the ever-worsening security situation at the train stations and in local transport. You can hardly be responsible to yourself and your family for voluntarily exposing yourself to such situations. We no longer have any hope that the DB will find a way to improve its disastrous situation in the foreseeable future. For us, from now on, our own vehicle will once again be the means of choice for getting around and traveling.

Deutsche Bahn disappoints across the board and doesn't even come close to justifying the prices it charges. Constant delays, lack of communication and chaotic processes are the rule, not the exception. Anyone traveling with Deutsche Bahn must always expect a high level of frustration and stress. Punctuality seems to be a foreign concept: trains either arrive late, early or are canceled completely. What's particularly bad is that even the published delays often seem glossed over - many connecting trains are missed, which leads to long waiting times. What's more, there are often no sensible alternatives. Replacement trains are inadequately provided and communication with passengers is disastrous. Announcements are incomprehensible or too late, and on-site employees are often overwhelmed. Another problem is chronic overcrowding on trains. Even if you have reserved a seat, this is no guarantee that you can actually use it, as the organization fails when the capacity is high. Deutsche Bahn's infrastructure also leaves a lot to be desired. Disruptions on the routes, technical defects and construction sites seem to be part of everyday life, which also leads to delays. Customer friendliness is a term that is apparently not a priority in the Deutsche Bahn system. Compensation for delayed trains is theoretically possible, but the process for doing so is so cumbersome that many people forego it. Overall, Deutsche Bahn is a prime example of inefficiency and poor customer management. Anyone who travels with them pays a lot of money for little performance and spends more time waiting than driving. As long as Deutsche Bahn does not fundamentally reform its system, it will remain an unreliable and disappointing transport provider. 0 out of 10 stars – deservedly.

For around 10 to 12 years, I have always donated the BahnBonus points I collected with the BahnCard to the Bahnhofsmission and then received a donation receipt from the Bahnhofsmission. Now there are "no" donation receipts anymore because the donations from rail customers are handed over to the recipients of the donations "in the name of Deutsche Bahn Fernverkehr AG". The DB justifies this by saying that since July 1, 2023 it has been responsible for flat-rate taxation in accordance with Section 37a of the Income Tax Act for the monetary benefit. For my donation of points worth 40 euros, the DB then has to pay 2.25% = 90 cents in taxes. From my point of view, the DB is enriching itself with the donations from rail customers and it can be assumed that the DB declares the donations in its own tax return as its own donation and, as a donor, receives a tax refund from the tax office, which in my case is certainly more than 90 cents! The DB will certainly not forego this tax advantage. I would like to advise all BahnCard customers not to donate the BahnBonus points they have collected to charitable purposes in the future if they value a donation receipt, which they can then use for their income tax return.
