Ticket officer told him that if he took a boat to Bingen he might get a train from there then he gave him a sheet showing the telephone number of a taxi firm. We got a taxi to Frankfurt which is forty miles away. I asked for compensation but the information desk officer said that as I had not got a ticket I could not get compensation. On previous occasions the toilets on the S bahn have been closed and pick pockets have robbed two of my friends at Koblenz and Mainz stations.

In terms of punctuality, the worst train company I have traveled with in my life. And yet I have traveled a lot. When the train is on time, it is an exception, not the rule. And the delays are often huge, when the train is simply not canceled. I work in Germany, this is 5 times in a row (in a row) that I have taken the train, and all of them have been late, with for the last case a delay of 3 hours (!) and the obligation to sleep in a hotel because no connections are possible. They offered a solution by reimbursing the room for a certain amount, but it was impossible to find a room at their price at midnight, so I had to take an expensive room on my own with a partial refund in the best case. Once again this is not an exception, it is systemic. And this is the sign of a company and perhaps even a country that is going through a major crisis.

The unreliability of this company threatens my existence, gets on my nerves and worst of all: LIFETIME. I am currently experiencing another unimaginable adventure on the drive home from work and am writing this review.
Not punctual or reliable. The trains don't show up at the station and there is no one who can give information. It is impossible to plan a trip/trip using Deutsche Bahn.

I traveled with the DB Bahn several times this month and not a single train came on time! In fact, it is no longer possible to get to an appointment on time if you don't leave hours beforehand. The conditions are really catastrophic! From now on I will no longer take the train and will cover all routes by car!

My train has currently a 90min delay, the board restaurant is closed, the tables at the seats are a disgrace and the carpet in the train looks like Jeffrey Dahmer and Hannibal Lector had dinner on it. At 170 EUR a pop - one way ticket - these people should be ashamed

Worst train system. In general, German trains are the worst. If you are tourist or decide to live in Germany, please start thinking about a car or car sharing. They simply do not care. They cancelled whenever they want (no concern for people who travel everyday for work), they are late. They just do not care. So if you want reliable transport, rent a car. You will pay a lot for this unpredictable service.

We used our train to flight tickets and were disappointed both on the outward and return journey. On the outward journey, it was only shortly before departure that the DB app showed that the train was cancelled. There was no corresponding announcement on the tracks and this fact was not communicated on the digital displays (time, information). Passengers without the app or even access to a smartphone are at a loss. On the return journey from Munich main station, the information came about 30 minutes before departure that the planned train had to be used elsewhere and therefore a different type of train would be used for the journey. All seat reservations were therefore no longer valid, the money was gone, the guests were dissatisfied and many were unable to use their paid reservations and even had to stand because the train now used had 300 fewer seats (100 in 1st class and 200 in 2nd class). Frustration from start to finish. Then it's better to drive by car...

Tickets purchased online cannot be purchased at the station. Much higher prices than Italian companies for a terrible service. The only carriage we found a seat in was the silent carriage: school groups talking loudly, the air conditioning doesn't work, the electricity doesn't work to charge cell phones, the bathrooms don't work. Never again

Always train cancellations. Book 4 days in advance and then receive a notification 1 day before departure that your planned trip is canceled. And that wasn't known at the time??? Earlier or later is possible free of charge, but those options are very limited. What to do with your seat reservation if you take another train? A big mess and it's not the 1st time. The NS in the Netherlands is not much better, by the way. If a ticket is cheap, but it is also ridiculously expensive.

I have no idea how much the DB cares about their own vehicles, but boy, over 40 minutes late on a Sunday because a door was stuck... Thanks for that. There is hardly a trip where DB doesn't shit in. I would switch to RB but surprise, they don't drive at all. Great club

For years I was a committed train traveler. For decades. Of course, I had numerous unpleasant experiences. But I always understood and defended the track. But now I'm fed up too. I can't take any more. The company must strike and the entire leadership, right down to middle management, must be replaced.

Never, ever book Deutsche Bahn. The absolute worst in customer service. I have never had a good experience. They change trains on you frequently, send no notification, and when they change the train you lose your seat reservation. So if you don’t notice until you arrive, you have to stand for your entire trip. And when they do these things to you, their agents on the train will say there’s nothing you can do except ask for a refund at the end of your trip, and the agents at the end will play dumb and say too bad, you already rode the train. Absolutely crazy!! DB is the last thing!! After a long 20 hour flight and drive from vacation. We only had to take the train from Frankfurt Airport to Frankfurt HBF in 10 minutes. There was already a delay of 10 minutes, 14 additional minutes. Now to Fulda. After just a few minutes there were problems on the tracks. You can then probably forget about the connecting train in Fulda. So it's really the last one!!

We booked tickets to see a Eurofoot match in Munich. 2 days before our trip our train was canceled due to damage to the track and no alternatives. We have been trying to recover the price of our tickets for 4 months now but I cannot explain to you the difficulties in contacting DB and finding the right contacts. No desire at all to reuse trains in Germany...
Most terrible company in the world, and as a customer you are completely powerless and have to put up with everything...

Dear Sir or Madam, I am turning to you to describe clearly my boundless disappointment with the catastrophic service provided by Deutsche Bahn. As someone who relies on the train for daily commuting and is willing to pay high ticket prices for this "service", it is unbearable to me that in over a year I have not experienced a single day without a delay or problem. I am a student and commute every day. Why? Because I think the train is an environmentally friendly and sensible alternative - at least that's what I once thought. I wanted to support the railway to make my contribution to sustainability. But after over a year of frustration, constant delays and countless glitches, I have come to realize that you are making it impossible to continue using the system. I simply cannot afford any more nerves and time to be wasted due to your unreliability. Since starting my studies, I have been confronted with a new problem at Deutsche Bahn every single day, without exception. I arrive late to lectures, exams and even home - often 2 to 5 hours late. I could ride a bike in that time and it would certainly be faster and more reliable! How can it be that a company that charges so much money for its tickets fails so consistently? I'm originally from Switzerland and I'm aware that SBB's service is hard to beat. But what Deutsche Bahn offers is not only far from an acceptable standard - it is an outrage. Their trains are dirty, ancient and belong in a museum, not on the tracks. I don't understand how anyone dares to ask for money for this impertinence. In any case, I have never seen anything about compensation for your shortcomings - in contrast to the SBB, which reacts immediately to every delay and accommodates its customers. And what should I think of your "customer service"? I've tried to reach someone more than 300 times over the last 15 months. Unsuccessful. If anyone sits at the counter at all, it's until 4 p.m. - after that, no one is there for the passengers. Announcements at train stations also seem to pose an insurmountable challenge for you. It's like you're intentionally trying to provide the worst possible experience. I'm angry and deeply disappointed. I always hoped that things would get better, but after so many months of daily horror, I no longer see any reason to believe in Deutsche Bahn. Instead, I now have to give up traveling by train with a heavy heart, even though it should be ecologically sensible and practical for me. But in reality it is pure horror for you. I sincerely hope that this message reaches you and that you think about how you want to get this absolute chaos under control. Other daily commute options seem increasingly more tempting to me than this constant nightmare. With extremely disappointed regards, Elena
Judging by the DB train services.. It would seem that Germany is a third world country.What ever happened to German rigor?
I just ate the BEST cinnamon roll of my life from the DB menu! Big praise to whoever ordered it! Cheers!
There have been unbearable delays on the Stuttgart - Münster route for months. There are also defective drink dispensers in the DB Lounge...

Train came later each time with a total delay of 2 hours. After the first stop the train was already at a standstill and we had to transfer to another train. Here we could not use our already paid seat reservations. Chaos and arguments broke out on this train. The train did not go any further and after standing still for an hour without air conditioning and half the people being thrown out, we continued. DB didn't even offer bottled water or a cookie, so ridiculous!

Waited on train in Hamburg for over an hour before the train was cancelled. Alternative route offered was replacement bus and 3 or 4 further changes. For that you were sent out to the airport for an SEV. Got to the airport along with 8 carriages worth of people to find chaotic scenes outside the airport where 2 (two) buses turned up. Pushing and shoving ensued with a few hundred people left stranded. Waited for more replacement transport to turn up but after over an hour at the airport, nothing turned up. There were no DB staff anywhere to be found so a lot of the stranded passengers had to make alternative plans. We decided to head back into the city centre and managed to find a ride on Flixbus, which was efficient, on time and very good value for money. DON'T USE BAHN.DE, APPALLING COMPANY, NON-EXISTENT CUSTOMER SERVICE, NO REPLY TO EMAILS OR FEEDBACK FORMS, NOTHING. If you want hassle free travel, use Flixbus or any other company.

I bought the Germany ticket for the month of September 2024 and noticed that the amount of 49 euros was debited twice. Despite numerous emails with proof and screenshots of my bank transactions, I have not received a refund. It is disappointing that my request was ignored and I feel betrayed. I hope this problem will be solved soon.

Price performance is not right at all. Totally overpriced. Permanent delay. Dirty trains and stations. No reliability. Little to no seats due to overcrowded trains. Too many unnecessary strikes from you... Shame on you!

DB is by far the most disorganised, poorly run, inept, incompetent and useless Organisation that I have ever encountered. 3 trains, over three days and they managed to screw up each one. Over 10 hours lost waiting, no notification of train delays, poorly informed staff (when you can find one) and a lack of care in the chaos caused by their incompetence that is totally unacceptable. Germany is a great country, the situation with the trains is totally unacceptable. Whomever is in charge should be replaced immediately.
Terrible terrible service, multiple cancellations and delays. Train are too full for anyone to get on!!!!! If you want to get to your destination DO NOT CHOOSE THEM.

It's a shame. I have seen some incompetent people in my life, but they are gems. Not a single train on time, never any seats and above all we miss all our connections. Worst train company ever! Highly suggest if you are looking to inter rail plan from the beginning to bus through Germany before you buy your pass. All of the ones I took were significantly delayed and multiple cancelled to the point where I got stuck in munich for an extra night and another time I had to book a bus out of hamburg. We had 2 separate rail trips with DB ICE and 1 with Regional with some very mixed experience across several contact points. My three journeys with DB rail in August 24  just got considerably worse as they went on. Of all the negative experiences I have had in Asia, Australia, India and Europe in my 40 years of travelling on rail, the three worst was with DB rail in one single month. Incompetence at a totally new level I have not experienced before. The staff have a strong contempt for anyone not German and are just plain rude to the passengers that are German. One would think that they were recruited by from the Stasi after the fall of the Berlin Wall. Not one of the trains had a working toilet, I bought 1st class tickets to no avail. On one journey the train stopped at an isolated station not on the itinerary and all the German passengers got off. Several american passengers and ourselves left on board. I asked the conductor what was happening. He informed me that the 1st class carriage had faulty brakes and was being left behind. I asked what would we have to do. He informed me that we would have to go to the first carriage at the other end of the train. My partner and myself ran to the first carriage with all our luggage and the train moved off as my partner was getting on the train. We have no idea what happened to the Americans.  If we had not of asked we would have been left on the carriage. On our last journey we missed the train that had  left 4 minutes early.  We missed it as the elevators were broken and we had to lug our  suitcases down three flights of stairs. My partner was needing to use the toilet. Another train was scheduled in 25 minutes so she went to find the toilet which was  closed. That train didn't come so we asked DB, who advised that they didn't know what happened to it and that is still could come, however advised catching another train. We caught another train which arrived on time but changed platforms. so up three flights of stairs and back down again.  The train has a toilet, happy days except it was out of order. Onwards to the airport, got on board with 20 minutes to spare. Best news  of the day, the airport had working free to use toilets. Who could believe that this would be the highlight of our day. NB: Germany is a great place and I loved it.
The train ran quickly and the tracks were newly equipped. Plus, some were clean. We didn't have to wait long for the train either.

Booked a first class seat from Krakow to Prague. DB trains overbooked the seats and when there were no seats left they told us too bad go find a seat in second class. People were standing in second class for over 6 hours. Horrible experience.

A lot of bad things are said about the train, because of delays, unpunctuality, etc. It was my first time taking the train and yes, I too was affected by delays. However, I have found that the train is not always to blame for the delays; sometimes it is also the fault of people who simply cannot break away from each other. When saying goodbye, three calls were made to clear the entrances, without any reaction from those affected; a train attendant first had to put an end to the separation. This could be seen not just once but at every train station. I think it's difficult to keep the times when no one is trying to support it.

Finally, the SNCF is not so bad....Last May, the German train leaving from Munich left late. It was announced that passengers with connections to France would miss the last train of the day. That we could either get off the train in Munich or in Frankfurt but that in any case we would not leave that evening. We are directed to the travel center. No help. They just tell me that there is no more room to leave the next day. That we'll just have to wait until Monday. Forced to take a hotel for 70 euros. And to pay 100 euros for a bus ticket for the next day to be able to return in time to return to work on Monday...No voucher. We have to manage. I am sending my request for compensation. And I was told that I would not be entitled to anything because the delay was due to a person on the tracks. We haven't been told anything about this... making us wonder if it's true or just a way of getting through customs. Ashamed.

I had an awful experience with Deutsche Bahn on the Munich to Berlin route. We had to wait for the next train, but with two previous trains also cancelled, it turned into a chaotic, overcrowded nightmare. Passengers were crammed into one train, making the journey unbearable. This disastrous service completely disrupted our travel plans. I strongly advise avoiding Deutsche Bahn—opt for a flight instead to save yourself the stress and frustration.

Best thing is timely info of service delays, etc. Bad: That info essential. Often late—sorry the old cliche about trains running on time in Germany is dead. We had what appears to be a rare positive experience based off the reviews here! I went to recognize Ms. C Dorsch for her excellent service in helping us book an earlier ticket than our original. Without any explanation, a train can stop in the middle of the tracks for an hour, or simply be canceled at the station so that it does not even appear on the display. I had the opportunity to travel across Europe by train, experiencing the varying levels of efficiency each country offers. Unfortunately, my train journeys within Germany were notably the least reliable. Over several months, regardless of whether I was on a Eurostar or an ICE train, delays were a constant issue — often exceeding an hour. It seemed that the moment we crossed into Germany, the likelihood of encountering delays surged. This became particularly problematic when I had tight schedules or connections to make. For those planning train travel in Germany, especially with critical timings or connections, I'd advise keeping this in mind. While the country has much to offer, its train system's punctuality didn't quite meet expectations during my travels.

It had been about 15 years since I last made trips with DB. Unfortunately I dismissed all of the complaints about the Bahn I had read and seen online because it didn't match my previous experience. My how things have changed in these years! I think my advice now is that you should never plan to *rely* on DB to take a specific route at a specific time. In fact, you may just get stranded. Twice in the same week going to and leaving from Munich, high speed trains were just cancelled because of some issue or another. The first happened while we were in route to Munich, intending to stop in Nuremberg and continue on later the same day, but the remaining trains of the day on to Munich were cancelled. Fortunately we were able just to continue on to Munich on the train we were already on. Two days later, intending to travel from Munich to Karlsruhe to continue on to Strasbourg with a TGV, we were 10 minutes from boarding our initial DB train when suddenly, it's canceled. The DB app informs you to select some other route, which I did -- a route to Zurich, Basel, and on to Strasbourg, but in very small print says  something like "make sure your fare is valid for this trip". OK -- how does one do that? So I stood in the 50 person deep line for the customer service at Munich Hbf where the agent told me "that's international so you can't take that route"; she then proceeded to get out a PAPER map of German rail lines to tell me that to get to Strasbourg, we'd have to take the "replacement" ICE to Karlsruhe which would be too late to get another ICE/TGV to Strasbourg, so we'd then need to board a bus to Baden-Baden, then a regional train to Offenburg, then another regional train to Strasbourg. Oh, and we'd need to pay another 25 euros for this itinerary on top of the 230 or so already paid for first class in what was supposed to be two high speed trains. Needless to say, all those transfers made for a hellish day. For the first cancellation, DB was "kind enough" to send two 10 euro vouchers, which by the way, had to be used for booking a trip in the next three months. Never mind I will be on the other side of the world. I tried submitting a refund request for the second botched trip, only to find out that you could only get another useless voucher, or get a refund, but only if you have a European bank. So I gave up. I'm a big proponent of taking rail, but if you need to get from city to city with DB, just save yourself the hassle and FLY.

Paid for two 5 day First Class Deutsche Bahn rail passes in Canada at a cost of €573 ( $846 CAD). We began using the passes on December 2nd, Berlin to Dresden. December 3rd, we boarded a high speed train to Munich. Everyone had to disembark the train at Leipzig as they were discontinuing service due to snow storm. Strangers we met on the train got us to our hotel in Munich. Tuesday, December 5th the trains were still not in service. We had plans to go to Neuschwanstein Tuesday and Salzburg the following day. We even had prepaid for reserved seats. On Tuesday, we went to the Munich Station to request a refund based on the trains we needed were not running. After waiting an hour in line with other stranded travelers, we were told “No, the passes were good for the month of December so we should just change our plans and stay longer to use them”. When we explained we were returning to Canada on Friday the 8th, their representative told us that is your problem. Nice! We did receive a refund of €26 for the reserved seats to Salzburg. On Wednesday, we found out that Deutsche Bahn was going on strike the following day. The trains were cancelled all week.We were able to get on the Lufthansa airport bus back to the airport as the trains were not running.  Another €26 out of pocket. We submitted a refund form as instructed by representative at Munich train station. It is nearly a year, despite hours spent of the phone, postage to send the original paperwork etc. we are constantly asked for more information, proof we were in Germany, our plans etc. always with the goal of delaying and not out right refusing compensation for no service. Master card will not reverse the charge and travel insurance will not reimburse for trip interruption because Deutsche Bahn is not putting their answer of no in writing. I believe their goal is to exhaust us so we stop pursuing this. All in all Deutsche Bahn made a bad situation worse by poor customer service. It appears there are no consumer rights for travelers in Germany. Please take this as a caution. If you prepay Deutsche Bahn, there is no guarantee that you will get what you paid for. We got one complete train trip for our money. A very expensive train ride. I am positive we would have paid a lot less had we just paid at the station in Germany. I would never purchase a train pass from Deutsche Bahn again.

Warning to Travelers wanting hassle free travel in Germany!There was a time, years ago, when you could count on DB Germany for on time schedules and good service. Nothing I loved more than traveling on DB, those days are long gone. On time departures and arrivals have been in a constant decline over the last years, however todays experience takes DB service to a new all time low. On our arrival on January 4th at Frankfurt airport we need to travel from Frankfurt to Karlsruhe, normally a little over an hour trip on average. We were informed buying our ticket that there was construction on the tracks and would have to take a bus from Frankfurt to Mannheim. Not ideal by a long shot, but I understand maintenance needs to be done. Where the problem lies is the seemingly lack of help in finding where those buses depart from. Little explanation by the DB employee selling tickets, and extreme lack of signage pointing you in the right direction of find the buses.To top it off DB is using local city buses for a long distance journey, no place for luggage, no room for the number of passengers, and rock hard seats to sit on for the 1 1/2 hour trip. Luggage rolling around on the floor, people without seats, those around us talking and scratching theirs heads, as we were, with the confusion in finding the buses, and chaos on the bus. To top it off they are charging normal prices for this terrible travel experience. Beware, we were told this is going on through February, and all summer of 2024. So when traveling in Germany, if you planning on using DB this summer make sure and give your self plenty of time, and be prepared to have trouble finding your bus if going on a long distance train. I'll give you the help DB does't, if long distance make sure and go the the long distance platforms 4 - 7, not level two where all other buses are departing from. DB here's a couple of suggestions: Have at least one, but better two DB people at the local bus stops to inform confused travelers this is not where the long distance (trains lol) buses depart from. Next, how about more signs! I was traveling with my German fiancé and we missed our bus, God forbid you don't understand German and try and figure it out.

When we did make it to our car, the luggage racks were full and we had to find a way to hoist two large, full suitcases onto the tiny luggage racks above the seats. This was frustrating but honestly the least stressful of the three rides.#3 The worst yet. Our train was changed but we received an email that our seat assignments were the same. Great. Then the platform was changed but wasn't updated on the digital itinerary. We eventually found the new platform. The train arrives, we find our car, and our two seats in a six-seat cabin are taken by a large group. Staff refuses to help us claim our seats, instead telling us to find different seats. There are NO remaining open seats in first class. The train they switched to is smaller than the original train and has less seats, so anyone who didn't get one is simply SOL - yes, even if you paid for seats and have reservations... We have to stand once more with our luggage as the train starts until the staff member can be convinced to vacate the seat hijackers and then only because the other group with valid tickets to the cabin shows up as well. But then, the icing on the cake: after removing the group that was squatting, the four other valid ticketholders for the cabin have FIVE adults and one child with them, so they take the entire cabin and the crew member tells us we're SOL again. She literally shrugged at us. We can't have our seats. Because apparently you don't have to buy a ticket for a child and can simply take another paying passenger's seat, and bring along another adult to steal a seat as well. Why not at this point? We were eventually able in our two hour ride to find vacated seats (after having to push three suitcases in the narrow aisles back and forth between cars multiple times).All three of these experiences were so ridiculous that we booked a rental car for the remainder of our trip as soon as we were able to do so. It's more expensive but at least we won't have to worry about unpredictable schedules; will have a guaranteed place for our luggage; and won't find random people sitting in the car's seats even though we paid for them.

I made the mistake of buying a monthly train ticket to get to work because theoretically the connection would be good and our company would be close to the destination station. Now the train has set up a construction site and announced a three-week duration. Consequence: the train that would take me to work on time has been canceled without replacement. An hour later I can take a replacement bus service. But the bus doesn't stop at the train station, but at the end of the world, so that I can walk 20 minutes to work from there. After the announced three weeks, they change the plan for the next 4 weeks in such a way that there is no train on three out of five days, but at least the previous one is running again on the remaining two days. However, the bus replacement service remains in place. Under these conditions, the monthly subscription is useless, but there is not even the option of canceling at short notice. So as a customer you are the last one again, paying for a service that is not provided and you cannot get out of it. As sorry as I am for the environment, I am now driving a car again, even if it costs me three times as much as the monthly ticket.

Hello, I am shocked and speechless about what happened today, September 23rd, 2021, at Rostock Central Station. I wanted to take the ICE 2275 to Berlin at 6:21 p.m. and then head towards Leipzig. I was at the platform an hour earlier to make sure I didn't miss it. I was sitting on platform 7 and then suddenly it was announced that there was a 30 minute (6:51 p.m.) delay and that the ICE was moving to platform 3. So I was on platform 3 and waited. I wait and wait then they came through again saying there were still delays. Suddenly another train came in and from that point on we didn't receive any more information for our ICE. Nothing, no announcement. I went to the next conductor who told me that the ICE left at 7:38 p.m. I and the other people stood there speechless and asked from where. Then the conductor from platform 3 said where they were standing. The ICE was standing there the whole time where it said please don't get on, our number wasn't there either. How can it be that there was no announcement that the ICE was late but in reality it was standing at the platform the whole time without informing us???????😡Then I went downstairs to ask what that meant. I was told that they couldn't help me because the ICE had already left. I said then please take a look. Then it just came, yes, it's gone, the next one will come at 8:21 p.m. Really great help. 👌🏻What happened next made me even more speechless...I was standing on platform 7 where the ICE was supposed to leave at 8:21 p.m. I waited and waited. At 8:08 p.m. I found out from two girls that the ICE was leaving from platform 4. Once again there was no say nothing, absolutely nothing. If the two girls hadn't said anything to me and the other passengers, we would have missed this ICE too. We sat in the cold the whole time and the ICE was already there. Crazy just speechless!!!

We booked three first class  trips on Deutsche Bahn so we could see Germany in July 2022.  Hmmm ... not sure DB  considers such fripperies as customers.  Let me explain ...  It started well - Hamburg to Berlin we had good seats in a six seat compartment with only one other passenger which was great.  (DB makes no allowance for luggage on the floor - everything is expected to be hoisted up on racks about 1.75 metres in the air - a bit of a stretch for most of us shortish persons on wrong side of sixty.  So a half empty compartment was excellent!)  Things went downhill from there.  Initially on the Berlin to Wurzburg trip (via Bamberg), we were allocated  side-by-side seats but no window; rather we looked on to  a large blank wall  .... The crew took pity on us and let us sit in special seats set aside for frequent DB travellers, otherwise our understanding of this rather  interesting stretch of German countryside would have been pretty small.  Then from Bamberg we had no allocated seats on a second class only regional train. It was crowded and we weren't fast enough to get great seats but it was ok.  I just don't understand how DB could charge 250 euros (especially given the availability of the wonderful summer offer of 9 euro tickets for second classs travel almost anywhere in Germany). Our booked tickets for Saarbrucken to Dusseldorf originally included a TGV to Mannheim,  then an  ICE for Mannheim to Dusseldorf. Within a few days of arriving in Germany, we were notified of cancellation of the TGV, and requested to change our bookings - somewhat of a challenge on an IPhone.  I tried to get help in Berlin in a big city station, but was waved away - the official would not countenance the ticket on my phone, and I hadn't thought to bring a paper ticket.  Finally I managed to change the booking in Saarbrucken itself.  However we were not given allocated seats, but I was assured it would be fine.  Wrong.  The train was packed and we found Saarbrucken to Koblenz (along the Saar and Moselle and surely one of the great short train journeys of the world) in an overheated carriage, very uncomfortable.  We had to sit several seats apart.  Neithe of us could sit comfortably as we had to sit squashed tightly to one side to make space for our suitcases. ( not quite cabin bags but not large).  The final leg from Koblenz to Dusseldorf was equally packed and without allocated seats we had no chance of seeing any of the country.  Poor mugs us - for assuming we could see Germany by train, for assuming careful pre booking and  several hundred euros would offer a chance to travel in comfort, for assuming DB had some interest in tourist  customers ....  Nup - when it comes to DB assume nothing!

Das aber die gesamte Reiseplanung auch mit möglichen Alternativrouten zu so erheblichen Verspätungen führt ist nicht nachvollziehbar und weiß aus meiner Sicht auf einen systemischen Fehler hin.- Wir haben Mitreisende gesprochen die den vollen Preis für die Zugreise bezahlten. Ich hoffe nur die Bahn ist kulant genug eine Rückzahlung zu leisten.- Selbst für einen Reisepreis von 9 Euro sind die gesamten Umstände so wie wir es erleben mussten nicht gerechtfertigt. Alle die darüber nachdenken als Nachfolgeprodukt einen höheren Preis zu veranschlagen muss ich entgegenrufen "Bringt zuerst das - Chaos und die Fahrpläne auf die Reihe bevor über höhere Preise gesprochen wird."- Wertvolle Informationen wie, "die beiden angezeigten Züge werden zusammengekoppelt" verbunden mit der Info das die zusätzlich angehängten Waggons "mit freien Plätzen sind" wären durchaus sinnvoll- Durchsagen mit einer laufenden Diesellok am Bahnsteig kann man getrost lassen. Es ist nichts zu verstehen. - Hut ab vor den Zugbegleitern. Ich hoffe die bekommen das Geld das sie verdienen. Ein harter Job solang die Serviceleistung Zugfahren so schlecht ist.- Die DB-App ist überlebenswichtig um Alternativen zu finden. Anzeigen zeigen nicht immer richtig an. Siehe Schwandorf. Durchsagen werden scheinbar nicht zuverlässig auf jeden Fall nicht mehr ausserhalb der Geschäftszeiten durchgeführt. Das Bahngleis zu verlassen um die Anzeigen der anderen Bahngleise zu prüfen oder die Großanzeige im Wartesaal oder davor zu prüfen kostet evtl. kostbare Zeit.- Ich möchte nicht alles schlecht reden. Zugfahren kann entspannend und interessant sein. Man hat interessante Begegnungen und Gespräche. Eine Bereicherung. Aber dazu gehört auch, dass eine geplante Reise mit der Bahn auch wie geplant abläuft.- Wichtiges Reiseutensil: Eine Powerbank Details:Abreise in Moosburg nach Landshut. Fast pünktlich können wir in Moosburg einsteigen. Ausreichend Zeit für den Umstieg bleibt. War eh knapp bemessen mit 7 Minuten. Aber angekommen in Landshut die erste Ernüchterung. Unser Anschlusszug nach Hof, im Flugverkehr würde man sagen, gecanceled. Ok, wir haben genügend Zeit, sind ja im Urlaub. Verlassen uns auf die Ansagen und die DB Bahn App. 11:29 geht der nächste Zug nach Hof. Wir nutzen die Zeit um ein Frühstück einzunehmen. Nicht zu vergessen den Alarm für diesen Zug in der App einzustellen. Wir genossen das Frühstück an einem schönen Plätzchen nähe des Bahnhofs um handlungsfähig zu bleiben. Rechtzeitig machen wir uns auf den Weg um unseren Anschlusszug nach Hof zu erreichen. Vor dem Bahnhof sehen wir schon hektische Betriebsamkeit an den Bushaltestellen vor dem Bahnhof in Landshut. Wir denken uns nichts denn die App hat ja noch keine Änderung angekündigt. Angekommen am Bahnhof kommt mit dem Blick auf die Anzeigetafel die nächste Ernüchterung. Auch der Zug nach Hof um 11:29 Uhr fällt aus. Es soll SEV (Schienenersatzverkehr) nach Wörth geben. Nun, wir nannten es Abenteuer hofften aber, dass es nicht gleich nach einer viertelstündigen Zugfahrt und einer ca. 2 Stündigen Frühstückspause beginnt. Zuversichtlich suchen wir die Bushaltestelle nach Wörth. Finden diese auch gleich vor dem Bahnhofsgelände. Wir sind richtig denn es stehen dort bereits sehr viele Reisende. Wir kommen sehr schnell ins Gespräch mit anderen Betroffenen und stellen fest, kein Bus sondern Taxi's stellen den SEV. Na ja, wenn schnell gehen muss sind Taxis eben schneller verfügbar. Als wir die die Taxifahrer frage wo diese hinfahren, bekommen die Antwort Neufahrt und die Fahrt muss bezahlt werden. Entspricht zum einen nicht den Informationen welche über die Anzeige vermittelt wurde. Und warum verlangen die Taxifahrer Geld für den doch durch die Bahn angekündigten SEV. Wir entscheiden uns die Glücksritter-Taxifahrer nicht zu unterstützen und warten weiter. Was sich nach kurzer Zeit bezahlt macht. Wir treffen auf einen sehr netten Taxifahrer der uns informiert über die Möglichkeiten der Weiterreise mit dem Zug und bestätigt das die Weiterreise mit ihm SEV sei und somit kostenfrei für die Reisenden. Es geht nach Neufahrn in Niederbayern. Ursprünglich nicht die Route die wir ausgewählt haben aber wenn diese über Regensburg nach Hof führt dann nehmen wir dieses Angebot gerne an. Puh, die Weiterreise nach Regensburg funktioniert ohne Probleme. Hoffentlich haben wir das Chaos, verursacht durch einen Oberleitungsschaden in Landshut, hinter uns gelassen. Ca. zwei Stunden Verspätung bei der Ankunft in Leipzig entspricht unserer Erwartungshaltung bei der Planung der Reise. Unsere Stimmung ist gut, wir hatten ja mit Verspätungen gerechnet. Regensburg nach Hof keine direkte Verbindung. Wir steigen ein in die Oberpfälzer Bahn nach Marktredwitz um Hof näher zu kommen. Freitag Mittag Heimreise vieler Pendler. Zumindest finden wir Platz. Der Zug ist hoffnungslos überfüllt. Aber wir sind froh Hof näher zu kommen. Angekommen in Marktredwitz scheint es, dass wir gut weiterkommen nach Hof. Es werden zwei Züge nach Hof angeboten. Der erste ist ebenfalls hoffnungslos überfüllt. Wir kommen mit unseren Rucksäcken nicht mehr hinein. Ist OK denn ein paar Minuten später kommt ja ein weiterer. Dieser kommt fast pünktlich wir steigen ein und sind happy Hof zeitnah zu erreichen. Fahrkartenkontrolle. Muss sein und ist vollkommen richtig. Wir haben das 9 Euro Ticket also kein Problem. Die Zugbegleiterin weist und darauf hin, dass wir mit diesem Zug und dem 9 Euroticket nicht nach Hof fahren können. Nachfrage: "Warum". Antwort: "Dieser Zug fährt über Tschechien dort gilt das 9 Euro Ticket nicht." Nun, das könnte man als erfahrener Zugfahrer aus der Gegend um Hof erahnen. Als unerfahrener nicht ortskundiger Zugfahrer hätte ich zumindest bei der Durchsage am Bahnsteig oder über die DB Bahn App die Info werwatetet,  das dieser Zug über Tschechien fährt und mit dem 9 Euro Ticket nicht befahren werden kann. Wir also in Schirnding raus. Sind nicht die Einzigen denen es so widerfährt. Das beruhigt ein wenig das Gemüt. Immer noch frohen Mutes warten wir 20 Minuten bis uns der Gegenzug wieder nach Marktredwitz fährt um dann in "den richtigen Zug" einzusteigen. Es gibt diesen Zug nach Hof und wir sind froh ohne weitere längere Wartezeit am Bahnsteig in Markredwitz nach Hof zu kommen. 16:54 unsere ursprünglich geplante Ankunftszeit in Leipzig und wir sitzen im Bahnhofscafe in Hof. Ein schöner Wartesaal der zeigt welche Wertschätzung den Zugreisenden entgegengebracht wurde. Ja, ein wenig Wehmut kommt auf und sehnt sich in diese Zeit zurück in der Zugfahren einfach und zuverlässig war. Wir haben die halbstündige Pause in diesen Räumlichkeiten genossen verbunden mit der Hoffnung, dass die letzen beiden Anschlußzüge Hof-Chemniz und Chemniz-Leipzig uns ohne weitern Verzug an unser Ziel bringen. Von Hof nach Chemnitz funktioniert gut. Umsteigezeit nach Leipzig ca 15 min. ist erträglich. Letzter Teilabschnitt unserer Reise von Chemnitz nach Leipzig. Wir steigen in einen wirklich sehr alten Waggon des Alex ein. Bedeutet für uns den nächsten Härtetest. Stickige Luft und Lautstärke. Das wären die eigentlichen Abenteuer die wir uns für die Reise vorgestellt haben. Alte Züge und Waggons die noch ihren Dienst tun. Plötzlich Vollbremsung. Ungeplanter Halt mitten auf der Streckt von unbekannter Dauer so die Durchsage. Wir verzweifeln. Kurz vor dem Ziel nochmal ein Halt der abzusitzen ist in einem unklimatisierten Zug. Der Gott sei Dank nicht überfüllt ist. Gedanklich richten wir uns schon zum Schafen in dem Abteil ein. Aufmunternd ist die Zugbegleiterin und ein Mitreisender mit dem wir uns gut unterhalten. Nach einer erneuten Durchsage, dass es doch noch etwas länger dauern wird geht es überraschend schnell weiter. 21:05 Uhr bei schönstem Sonnenuntergang fahren wir in den Bahnhof Leipzig ein. Geplante Ankunftszeit 15:05 Uhr. 6 Stunden Verspätung. Eingeleitet durch einen Oberleitungsschaden in Landshut. Wir freuen uns angekommen zu sein und auf ein leckeres Abendessen. Nächste Überraschung. Es gibt jede Menge an Restaurants am wunderschönen Leipziger Bahnhof. Nur schließen die Geschäfte und Restaurants um 21:00 Uhr. Dann eben Pizza Hut. Unbeschreiblich teuer. OK, dann Burger King. Service am Kunden definiere ich anders. Nachdem wir ca. 15 Minuten an einer Schlange anstehen und nichts weiter geht beschließen wir uns etwas auf dem Weg zum Hotel zu suchen. Wir sind ja sehr zentral und werden was finden. Aber auch hier ein ähnliches Bild. Restaurants schließen machen gegen 21:30 Uhr. Finden dann doch noch ein vietnamesisches Restaurant das bis 22:00 Uhr geöffnet sind. Werden zwar wie Ausserirdische beäugt als wir gegen 21:35 Uhr anfragen ob wir etwas zu Essen bekommen. Nach anfänglichen Missmut dürfen wir uns setzen. Werden aber schnell belohnt mit einem hervorragenden asiatischen Mahl was den gesamten Tag versöhnlich enden lässt.Aber jetzt schon kommen uns die Gedanken ob wir mit den heutigen Erlebnissen nach Hamburg weiterreisen. Wir könnten theoretisch noch drei Mal in diese chaotischen Umstände gelangen. 1x Weiterreise nach HH und weitere 2x bei der Rückreise mit Zwischenstopp in Göttingen nach Moosburg. Wir schlafen eine Nacht darüber. Samstagmorgen, die Entscheidung ist gefasst wir reisen nicht nach Hamburg. Verlängern dafür in Leipzig.Die Hoffnung ist groß, nachdem wir zwei wunderbare Tage in Leipzig verbrachten, dass die Heimreise planmäßig verläuft. Weit gefehlt. Der Start war wie erhofft. Unser Zug geht pünktlich von Leipzig nach Hof. Hurra. ein großes Stück der Heimreise (ca. 2,5 Std.) scheint zu funktionieren. Der Zug ist voll aber wir können uns einen guten Platz sichern. Kurz vor Hof ein ungeplanter Halt wegen eines Böschungsbrandes. Nun, dafür kann die Bahn nichts. Unseren Anschlusszug erreichen wir auf jeden Fall nicht. Die Bahn App zeigt auch schon SEV von Hof Richtung Schwandorf an. Liegt auf unserer Route nach Landshut. Na gut, die Odyssee scheint sich sich fort zu setzen. In Hof angekommen entscheiden wir uns den SEV (alter Bus ohne Klima) nach Schwandorf zu nehmen. 2 Stunden in einem vollbesetzten Bus. Ertragbar aus unseren Erfahrungen einer Albanienreise. Was die Bahn nicht sagt, es geht nicht direkt nach Schwandorf. Es werden nicht alle aber einige der mit der Bahn angefahrenen Haltepunkte angefahren. Somit machen sich 2 volle Busse mit Zwischenstopps auf den Weg nach Schwandorf. Verständlich auf der einen Seite aber wer hätte denn noch zusteigen können. Es war von Anfang an klar, dass alle Reisenden nach München wollen. Das hätte man klüger gestalten können in dem man einen der beiden Busse direkt nach Schwandorf schickt um die nach München reisenden schneller dort hin zubringen und die, die auf der Strecke aus- oder zusteigen in dem anderen Bus. Nach wirklich 3 unnötigen Zwischenstopps bei der eine Mitreisende ausgestiegen ist und ein Reisender eingestigen erreichen wir Schwandorf. Dort angekommen macht uns die Anzeige, Durchsage und die DB App Hoffnung, dass es mit den RB22 und den RB2 relativ schnell weiter geht Richtung München. Mit Verspätung zwar aber es geht weiter. Anfänglich 20 Minuten. Grund Polizeieinsatz. Es wird auch brav über jede Veränderung der Verspätung über die Anzeige und per Durchsage informiert. Aus 20 Min. wurden 40 Min. um kurz darauf wieder 20 Min. zu werden. Dann mit der letzten Durchsage bleibt es stabil bei 35 Minuten und einer technischen Störung. Alle nach München reisende verlassen sich auf die Anzeige welche brav die geplante Abfahrt, die Verspätung und das Gleis anzeigt. Ja, wir sind auf dem richtigen Gleis. Das wird immer wieder geprüft denn Gleisänderungen sind durchaus üblich. Warten also auf Gleis 2 auf unseren Zug inzwischen fährt auf dem Gleis 1 ein Alex ein. Klar erkennbar an den Aussenanzeigen der Waggons, Ziel München Hbf angezeigt wird. Unsere Anzeige auf Gleis 2 sagt weiterhin brav die geplante Abfahrt, die Verspätung und das Gleis an. Gleis 2. Kommend von Prag sind auch tschechische Waggons dazwischen. Vorne wird die Zugmaschine abgekoppelt hinten eine drangehängt ich denke es waren auch ein paar weitere Wagoons dabei. Die Anzeige auf Gleis 2 bleibt unverändert. Alle Reisenden verlassen sich auf die Anzeige. Ich denke mir, die Koppelungsaktion konnte wohl nur auf Gleis 1 erfolgen der Zug wird im Anschluss dann auf das Gleis 2 umsetzen. Die Anzeige auf Gleis 2 weiterhin unverändert. Zug nach München Hbf geplante Abfahrt, Verspätung und Gleis. Gleis 2. Hoffnungsvoll, wie auch die anderen Mitreisenden, blicken wir dem abfahrenden Zug auf Gleis 1 nach. Wir sind es nun ja gewohnt, dass es durchaus einige Minuten dauern kann. Doch den abfahrenden Zug nicht mehr im Auge verschwindet auch die Anzeige des RB2 und RB22 nach München Hbf von der Anzeige auf Gleis 2. Ohne Durchsage ohne weiteren Hinweis. Sekunden darauf informiert uns die Anzeige nächster Zug vom Gleis 2 nach München Hbf um 21.05 Uhr. Fassungslose Blicke aller Reisenden nach München Hbf. Die Bahn hat uns alle verarscht. Das erste Mal auf unserer Reise werde ich wütend. Ich und ein weiterer Mitreisender oder sollte ich besser Mitleidender sagen, machen uns auf den Weg irgendeinen Verantwortlichen der Bahn zu finden. Fehlanzeige. Im digitalen Zeitalter, in dem wir uns befinden, versuchen wir unser Glück telefonisch jemanden von der Bahn zu erreichen. Digitales Zeitalter ändert aber nichts an den Arbeitszeiten. Es war inzwischen nach 18 Uhr folglich kam von der Service-Hotline die Ansage, dass ich doch ausserhalb der Geschäftszeiten anrufe. Servicewüste Deutschland. Immer noch. Nachdem meine Frau und ich uns von diesem Schreck erholt haben ein erneuter Blick in die Bahn App um weiteren Verbindungsmöglichkeiten von Schwandorf aus zu überprüfen. Durchsagen waren ja jetzt ausserhalb der Geschäftszeiten. Anzeigen funktionierten aber noch. Ich möchte festhalten ohne die Bahn App wären wir aufgeschmissen gewesen. Was die App wirklich gut kann, ist Alternativen aufzuzeigen wenn diese dann auch bereitgestellt werden. Dank der DB App welche einen weiteren RB2 und RB22 auf Gleis 4 anzeigt und in Abstimmung mit den mitleidenden Mitreisenden begeben wir uns auf Gleis 4 wo um 19:05 Uhr die Reise weitergehen soll. In Schwandorf Bahnhof gibt es einen Kiosk und eine Bäckerei die auch nach 18 Uhr geöffnet bleiben (ein Schelm der böses dabei denk), dass hilft die erneute Wartezeit zu versüssen. Ein Wunder geschieht. Schon lange nicht mehr auf Pünktlichkeit achtend fährt auf Gleis 4 fährt ein Zug mit Ziel München Hbf ein. Keine Durchsage (wir befinden uns ja ausserhalb der Geschäftszeiten) kein Hinweis auf der Anzeigetafel, dass die beiden Züge RB2 und RB22 vereinigt werden. Ohne diesem Wissen laufen wir alle natürlich dem einfahrenden Zug nach. Dieser fährt bis ganz an den Anfang des Bahnsteigs. Im Zug erfahrenden wir von Reisenden, dass doch hinten Waggons zugekoppelt werden und diese leer seien. Also Platz zum sitzen bieten. Keine Ahnung wie lange der Zug noch am Bahngleis verweilt,  bleiben wir im vorderen Teil des Zuges. Wohlwissend, dass wir im hinteren Teil Sitzplätze hätten. Hauptsache wir kommen Richtung München weiter. Sitzen ist eh ungesund. Ein Stehplatz bei offenem Fenster in einem uralten Waggon hat etwas von Nostalgie. Wir genießen es Frischluft zu atmen und freuen uns auf Zuhause. Eine Zugbegleiterin kommt, wir zücken die Fahrkarten. Werden aber nur mit harschem Ton aufgefordert doch in den hinteren Teil des Zuges zu gehen welcher doch extra zugekoppelt wurde und somit genügend Platz bietet. Ich platze nach dieser Ansage fast vor Wut und schildere der Zugbegleiterin mit bestimmten Tonfall die Umstände und die fehlende Informationen am Bahnsteig. Sie ist einsichtig und wir einigen uns darauf, dass beim nächsten längeren Halt in Regensburg wir versuchen in den hinteren Teil zu kommen. Was dann, angekommen in Regensburg, nicht mehr nötig war da direkt Plätze frei wurden. Zu guter Letzt gilt es festzuhalten das der Umstieg in Landshut in Richtung Moosburg dann ohne Verzögerung und wie geplant funktionierte. Zusammenfassung der Rückreise. Abreise in Leipzig 10:55 geplante Ankunftszeit in Moosburg an der Isar 16:59 Uhr. Tatsächlich sind wir in Moosburg um 21.27 angekommen. 4,5 Stunden Verspätung. Was aber bei der Rückreise schwerer wiegt als die Verspätung ist die Verarsche in Schwandorf.Der Verkehrswandel ist notwendig dazu muss die Bahn wieder einen zuverlässigen und einfachen Service anbieten.Ich persönlich werde das 9 Euro Ticket auch noch im August nutzen. Meine Frau kann ich leider nicht mehr davon überzeugen das Bahnfahren als Alternative für Urlaubsreisen zu sehen.

Never again! Departure Berlin HBH: Totally overcrowded platform, it feels like all trains are being directed onto one track, late regional league teams delay the arrival of the ICE. Delay totaling 40 minutes - it's not that bad, I think. But then the train no longer travels across the border into Switzerland due to the delay. Announcement: "The train has stopped (it was difficult to remember). I don't know the reason. I'll let you know when I know more."

Horrible overall booking system, if you’re going to have reserved seats ONLY HAVE RESERVED SEATS. Getting on a train not know whether or not you’ll be able to find a seat to sit in, and having to scrounge around the whole train trying to find seats is ridiculous. And then because the booking system doesn’t work properly, you also have to give up your seat if someone shows up and says they’ve reserved it…

Paid an extra 50 euros for 'first class' which was just slightly more legroom.The onboard restaurant was understaffed and stocked, and so all I get was a crappy coffee, and the wifi kept dropping out throughout my 3 hour trip.What a rip. Was looking forward to a comfortable train journey with some great on board service after a 24 hour flight from Melbourne to Munich, but alas, it was not to be. Disappointing.

We were on a school trip and took the ICE. The chaos starts as soon as you get in: people simply get in wherever they want and block doors and corridors. Our seat reservation could only be clarified after a lengthy discussion with the other passengers. When we finally sat down we noticed that the floor was completely dirty and that the seats were incredibly uncomfortable. The view out of the window was very obscured by the dirty windows. Conclusion: Not suitable for longer journeys - I personally prefer the plane.

Dear ladies and gentlemen of Deutsche Bahn, do you actually know how embarrassing it is to have Germany, as an industrial country, represented by an association like you. I know you are not an association, but a corporation, but that can only be fake, because who would buy shares here? The contract execution would never come to an end. Or are you faster there? If it's about money, you might be able to hurry up; otherwise, you're in no way inferior to the infrastructure in some developing countries. Unfortunately, only one apt term: EMBARRASSING. We just wanted to drive from Hamburg to Bochum via Bremen. Well, the fact that the train was 50 minutes late can be ignored under normal law, it's always the same. We were almost satisfied, after all we would have caught the next train in Bremen. However, it was then announced that due to the delay, the stop in Bremen would be canceled today and instead it would be closing time in Rotenburg. Guess what? If I want to finish work early, I can go home. Then I get fired. That you give a raise instead. It's funny. That you are looking for support from the population. Shameless. That you believe you can continue to charge the prices they charge. Morbid. That you are, in a sense, a showcase project for Germany. Embarrassing for all of us. A crude joke that pretends to be a little more, which would make it even funnier if it weren't so sad. LG

The combination of the Munich transport company and the German railway is an absolute catastrophe and tax waste at the highest level. On the one hand, a non-resident customer can wait for 1 hour in front of the main train station to enter and almost miss the train. On the other hand, because of a strip that is not solved enough, you have to pay €60 for the S-Bahn ride to the main station, because it is supposedly hidden somewhere in the online app that a surcharge is charged for these rides. An objection is not possible because online chats lead you into a madhouse that beats Asterix books by far. Hello, so only clairvoyant people without time pressure are wanted as customers. Privatize! Immediately!

Deutsche Bahn has become a hellscape on earth. Total inferno. Absolute mess of a “system.” Complete disaster. A moving (but always delayed) dumpster fire. Came back to Germany 8 years after living here and am quite simply flabbergasted that this is what has become of their train system. A national shame and tragedy. Deutsche Bahn makes walking to the airport barefoot and buying a flight in cash day-of seem like a good alternative to the “service” they provide. It’s hard to fully capture all the reasons why DB is the trash of the trash, but here are a few:-Nothing is on time anymore. Forget any german stereotype you’ve heard about this-Connections rarely work (because nothing is on time)-Every single train is way overbooked beyond capacity. It’s like that movie where people are just stuck on the track perpetually (Snowpiercer?). Just people walking back and forth down the aisles looking for seats during the entirety of every ride. Lot of riff raff yelling and complaining. Extraordinarily unpleasant. -Trains are way dirtier and grimier than I remember-Trains just stop and split off randomly for no reason. So then you’re forced to get out occasionally and enter the battle royale for a seat on the other part of the train that still moves. Chance of success: 2%-You end up standing on long distance trains a lot. It’s very annoying-Cafe cars often inexplicably shut down-Seats cost extra and are often unavailable (a tell-tale sign of constant overbooking)-Website is confusing-Due to everything being delayed all the time, DB demolishes your inbox with notifications. It’s kind of funny how when you have a connection and your first train is inevitably delayed, DB sends you an email saying “You will miss your connection.” Then when your second connecting train is also delayed you get another email saying “You will now make your connection again.”DB’s motto should actually just be “good luck” with a side-eye and explosion emoji. That sums up how they think about their business. It’s hard for me to justify returning to germany due primarily to how u pleasant DB makes one’s life there. Otherwise nice people once you exit the train. If you’re debating, go somewhere else instead. It’s not worth it.
If I could give 0 stars I would. Embarrassing club. A bottomless impudence and a disgrace for Germany.

The trains never run on time. Today I was delayed 5 hours total. Never have seen one of these trains run on time. The delays cascade and result in HOURS of extra travel time. The incompetence is astounding - beyond belief.  And then they refuse to refund your ticket. This is one of the worst services I have had the displeasure of experiencing in my life.

I bought the 9 euro ticket for June via the RMV app. I couldn't show the ticket during a check because my cell phone battery was empty. On the piece of paper you receive you have 7 days to respond. Since I got sick, I completely forgot about it. Now I have received a reminder for €61.30. After consulting with DB Vertriebs GmbH, it is now no longer possible to show the ticket and only pay €7.00 processing fees instead of €61.30. So even if it is written on the slip, the ticket is no longer valid? Is this how DB earns its money? I find it very unfair and dubious and almost criminal! And that with constant train cancellations, being late, etc. Very bad!
Defective doors, which is why the trip is canceled. It's hard to beat cheapness and inability! Always been late but now nothing works at the dirty store.

Travelling in First Class on the ICE train services is definitely not as good or comfortable as Standard Premium on Eurostar.   The seats are not comfortable for a long journey though the service is certainly fast but connections are subject to change so you need to listen out for the onboard announcements which were sometimes a bit muddled and not always delivered with clarity.   Depending on the train, electronic signboards may be located behind you so not easily readable.   Food and drinks are not complimentary as advertised and service at your seat is sporadic, definitely not as advertised.   The two female crew whom I encountered were abrasive, bordering on rude.Eight hours thirty minutes from Zurich to Amsterdam became nine hours fifteen after several unexplained extended stops in northern Germany.   Expectations of a quiet comfortable journey were shattered by a German male passenger talking unnecessarily loudly on his phone directly behind me, another with a lengthy contribution to a Zoom conference call directly in front of me and a large young German female continuously rolling her foot on the squeaking footrest across the aisle from me, seemingly unaware of the nuisance factor.  More people poured onto the train at the stops in northern Germany than the train’s capacity so that there were passengers filling the carriage entrances as well as standing in the aisles.   There were no ticket inspectors other than immediately after leaving Zurich and no railway personnel on the platform at Basle to confirm the connection change.   Still better than airport chaos I guess!

Terrible experience with Deutsche Bahn. A round trip from Brussels to Hamburg with a connection to Cologne canceled on both the outward and return journeys, each time without prior communication. For the outward journey, I had to take 3 different trains (instead of 2), including a train from another company (with the risk of having to pay for another ticket) to succeed in making my connection only thanks to the train delay in Cologne. On the way back, I had to take another equivalent journey leaving 2 hours before, full and with assigned seats and therefore had to spend almost 7 hours sitting on the ground between 2 cars. Needless to say, I was not alone in this situation and we were crowded between the cars. In Cologne, at the Deutsche Bahn information point, the staff were unpleasant and very uncooperative, justifying that there was not a sufficient delay on the way out to request a refund. A refund should be made not for the delay but for the non-communication of cancellations and the (dearly) paid service which was not fulfilled, on the outward and return journeys. My interlocutor did not seem convinced of this... I filled out a reimbursement request document at this information point, I hope that my interlocutor will follow up, but his phlegm did not bode well. Scandalous Deutsche Bahn.
The nine euro ticket has mercilessly exposed the weaknesses of the railway. No train is on time anymore! What a crazy idea from politics...
Disaster, worst service ever, only train cancellations, no one can ever be reached by phone! Just embarrassing! And totally overpriced too!

Absolutely dirty club, never on time regardless of whether you are commuting or on long-distance transport. Always absolutely unfriendly, incompetent staff who are best never spoken to. Anyone who can should definitely avoid traveling with the DB!!!

They are unhelpful, rude and put the blame on the user. How come a developed country has such a terrible service and bunch of abussive workers? They have not refunded my money for a cancelled ticket more than a month back, and calling to their 'customer service' is a pain, everyone screams at you, they talk to you down and patronise you.

German efficiency? Joke! Overcrowded trains, outdated switches and constant train repairs. Worst train system in Europe. Rarely delay messages translated to English and out of 10 rail journeys in the last two months not 1 within an hour of on time if even completed at all. The Worst! Recommend multiple backups.

Unfortunately, I have been dependent on the German train for years and I don't know the last time it was on time. Why don't you work with replacement trains or buses? I've already traveled by train in Austria, Switzerland, Denmark and France and couldn't notice any delay(s) as extreme as with the DB. So why isn't it working here? A shame for our otherwise over-punctual and bureaucratic country. DB there is a lot of room for improvement!

Unreliable, always late, avoid if possible…. Plus overpriced. At the moment it feels like every train arrives at least 20 minutes late and the previous one is simply cancelled. In other words, you can leave hours in advance to get somewhere at a certain time... the excuses are always the same and the website always crashes if you complain

1st class from Kaiserslautern to Mannheim and no seat.....but not only that, no standing room either because everything is full with 9 € ticket holders, they even sat on the floor in the 1st class compartment....the worst thing is that no train attendant or conductor showed up during the entire journey.....I'm curious to see what DB's answer is because. Reclaim 1st class surcharge and compensation for pensioners and severely disabled people!

If I book 1 class ICE and services are also specified, these should also be adhered to. This is what happened on the ICE 611 and 714. No warm food or snacks from Hamburg (where the train was used) to Cologne, and no coffee. There were only cold drinks and sweets.

The train arrived on time but everything else was horrible. There is almost no information on how to navigate the train station or on the train. Also, we had booked a sleeping compartment but when we got on the train it said that they were all occupied, so we had to sleep on regular seats in a regular day compartment. Then the train made an extremely loud noise so it was basically impossible to sleep. It generally did not feel safe for that part. There was nowhere to put the bags except above the chairs, so even large suitcases had to hang outside the aisle. In addition, we ran into drug addicts on the train several times to ask for money in the middle of the night! The police arrived several times and lots of people who would hand out advertisements etc. Look at the picture below of a person who wanted to hand out advertising💩 Overall a bad railway company.

Why did Deutsche Bahn deliberately and massively worsen travel COMFORT in first class? In the newer ICE, the backrest of the seats can no longer be adjusted. The seat can be pulled forward about 5 cm. - But the point is null. Especially on longer journeys, this massive deterioration in comfort is particularly a hindrance to resting in a relaxed manner. Who would come up with such nonsense? It is well known that this goes against all ergonomic research and against all medical knowledge about the body's healthy resting position. Very bad performance!

Simply the worst in Europe. In the 15+ train I HAD to take the past 10 months, not a single one arrived with a delay less than 1h...Including on a 1h scheduled ride!A shame.That said, the staff is often trying their best to handle thousands of angry and stressed clients. Poor, really very poor: on the outward journey we booked a sleeper carriage, where a type of comfort was presented, completely different from the carriage we found ourselves on the Zurich Hamburg train. A rather old carriage and very rude staff on board. On the way back with ICE from Hamburg to Zurich, delayed by more than 40 minutes, in the end the train was stopped in Basel and we had to go to Zurich with another SBB (equally scandalous), with all connections missed

I bought a long-distance ticket on Deutsche Bahn from Hamburg, Germany to Amsterdam, the Netherlands with 4 transfers in total. The first train to Osnabrück (from Hamburg)  was supposed to be from FlixTrain but for some reason that was canceled. Since I had to take a train from Osnabrück, I ended up purchasing another train ticket to Osnabrück at Hamburg Central Station with additional cost. And luckily  this one came on time and I was able to make my way to Amsterdam.I then submitted a passenger right request to Deutsche Bahn thinking I could get a refund for the additional cost I paid to buy a ticket to Osnabrück. After a month and half of waiting, they sent me a post mail with the following message:Leider nimmt das von Ihnen angegebene Eisenbahnverkehrsunternehmen FlixTrain nicht am gemeinsamen Entschadigungsverfahren teil.This means Deutsche Bahn do sell FlixTrain tickets but are not at all accountable for anything in case of cancelation/delay. Instead, they asked me to contact FlixTrain. How can one sell a ticket without being accountable for anything?fyi: I also contacted FlixTrain but their reply was the same: Go talk to Deutsche Bahn.In case you ever have to buy a FlixTrain ticket on Deutsche Bahn, be mindful that none of them will be responsible for any issue.
Simply provide what is offered! Reservation without the paid seats! Dining car without food!

I never had so rude and unpolite interaction with stuff in all my adult life traveling everywhere. I know they do the job, but not necessary such attitude. I had ticket, but wrong train. Sure i will go out and change the right one. They are Like “YOU! OUT! UNDERSTAND?” But with really attitude like they are very important people (you are grown up women working in train).
