I used to collect decals and rubber figures, but today I collect excuses from the DB as to why trains are extremely late or canceled altogether

I would give -100 stars because 0 is still too many!!! It couldn't be more incompetent! Shameless, unpunctual, trains are constantly canceled and this is then announced at the station a minute before departure. Just a waste of time and money. Only good for building up and encouraging aggression, but since nobody needs that, the DB is completely trash.

Unreliable. 3 out of 4 trips have issues: train cancelled, delayed of anything from 30m to several hours or just unbearable conditions (e.g., overcroweded trains).If the train is in the afternoon and it is a trip longer than 3h, expect you could not make it on the same day. Potentially, you might need to find a way to spend the night if you change train during your trip.Don't rely on trains if you need to make it on time, e.g., to the airport.

Still wearing masks in 2022 on trains while some countries don't require it. I took an Ice train from Vienna to Nürnberg and the masks were not a problem until we entered Germany. Also the trains are quite late most of the time.

I have been living in Germany for the past two years … I used to travel in ICE every month . The reservation system sucks . If you do t reserve the seats it really sucks . They do overbooking and you have to literally stand after paying a lot of money. Last time  I travelled  from Frankfurt to Nürnberg. I was coming from Madrid and I have to reach early so I booked but the ICE got lasted more than 1.30 minutes and it reicht more two and half hours late If you guys want to travel with ICE you want luck , prior booking and patience ( a lot )
Berlin ubahn lighting did me dirty and gave me body dysmorphia but actually quite efficient so unsure would tolerate for travel

We were traveling from Basel to Viersen. Every single train was late. In total we were 2.5 hours late. Many trains were completely dirty and toilets were locked in many trains. A passenger who was sitting in a wheelchair could not get off where he actually wanted to because the platform was not suitable for people with disabilities. We had reserved seats, but this didn't work. Many trains were overcrowded so that people could no longer find space even in first class.  We have already traveled by train in many countries around the world, but nowhere was there such chaos as at Deutsche Bahn! It's a shame if people are willing to give up their cars and take the train, but the train doesn't take part. So many people are forced to switch back to cars.

I don't even know where to start. It has gotten worse instead of better over the years. In principle, all managers should train or, better yet, employ competent people. I now plan 2.5 hours for the train journey between Stuttgart and Frankfurt, but then I still have a 3-hour buffer at the airport. How often can a door be defective, how often can there be a signal malfunction, how often can the wrong train number appear on the ICE? DB employees grumble at people and rightly ask whether it's just the number that's wrong or whether it's really the wrong train. The app shows 2 different moves and nobody knows which is right. Old people are chased out of their seats because someone else has booked. An old man with a prosthetic arm would have to move twice with a suitcase... gag. This is just describing one trip and I'm so fed up with the club, maybe they're just completely overpaid and think they're stupid foot soldiers. sorry, but I can't find any other words for it. Every vacation starts with tension and only begins to become relaxing at the airport.
Simply repair the trains for the summer holidays. ...It's been a year... I've never traveled anywhere so bad and bad.

Bad, worse, Deutsche Bahn. The word to describe the catastrophic level of Deutsche Bahn has not yet been invented. Incredible. You couldn't even win customers with a €1 ticket, absolute ****** club. Remove the “GERMAN” from your name, you are insulting an entire nation!

It's bad that you have to pay money to reserve a seat (with long-distance Italian transport you are automatically assigned a seat when you book), but the fact that a free rebooking is not even possible due to a booking error is simply the last thing. For exactly these reasons and more, I don't usually take the train. Even Vodafone and Telekom are more customer-friendly.

I have been traveling regularly from Aachen to Leipzig and back for two years now and unfortunately I have only experienced the German train being on time once. Most of the time it is “just” delays and cancellations that lead to a delay of one to one and a half hours. (Regardless of the transfer time, you can add at least one hour to the journey time). Unfortunately, my last journey was that I was supposed to arrive at 6.03, but ultimately only arrived about 4 hours later, i.e. at 9.53. Of course, this often leads to missed appointments and opportunities. It's a shame that something so simple that every other country can do doesn't work in "modernized" Germany and probably won't work for the next 30 years. The prices that are then charged for it are more than audacious.
Unpunctual, unreliable & simply disgusting. Anyone who likes bumping into each other, crowds and all kinds of physical smells will get their money's worth!

Dirty shop. If you like tardiness, unreliability, stuffy air and canceled trains, this is the right place for you. Sad that nothing has changed all these years. Together with digitalization, one of the biggest disappointments in Germany and then our politicians wonder why so many people still drive. Very ironic.

Incredible! Holiday travel weekend, without a 9 euro ticket, so expensive too! Booking in 1st class, but the carriages are not included. We were supposed to go to second class, but it was already fully booked and until then there were no people and loads of suitcases, no way through the aisles. Hours of delay or entire train cancellations. Toilet broken, air conditioning hardly noticeable. Germany has been asleep here for decades. If we all really leave the car, then goodnight!! In contrast, Corona was a children's birthday!

At the weekend I took the train from Frankfurt to Bretten in BW and back. The return journey should take approx. 2 hours each. My journey there was still somewhat okay. It took 3.5 hours and we were stuck in a train station because the route was closed for several hours. There was no information. The train driver doesn't have any more information than the guests and can't say when it should start again. The return journey was chaotic. I decided not to go via Karlsruhe because, according to the app, the connecting train there was supposed to be 55 minutes late. So I didn't drive via Heidelberg. All the trains there were late, but this was not announced on displays or loudspeakers for the first 30 minutes. Only later did I find out that a train, which was also 1 hour late, had just left another track. Now things got chaotic. The loudspeaker announcements and displays contradicted each other and were constantly changing. In this heat yesterday it wouldn't have been great if a train had been 1 or 2 hours late. Then I could have sat down in the cafe with my book. But you never knew which train was coming from which platform and when, so you were just running around. I felt sorry for the disabled and old people who were exhausted in the heat. Ultimately I took the S-Bahn to Mannheim because the staff told me they didn't know when a train would leave for Frankfurt. They wouldn't know anything more than the app. According to the app, everything was fine. When I arrived in Mannheim it was even more chaotic, I had to run from platform to platform for almost 60 minutes, and the trains were delayed by dozens. When a train finally came, it was stormed, as if it was the last train to freedom. Hardly anyone wore a mask on the train. It wasn't checked anyway. I haven't taken a train for over a year now and wanted to try it again. That was definitely my last train journey. I was out for 2 days and I'm still groggy today. I would have easily driven 90 minutes by car. Trains may be canceled or delayed. What is most disgraceful, however, is the railway's information policy and how little the local staff is/is informed. It is absurd that those responsible are not held accountable. There are obviously completely overwhelmed managers at the railway.

The worst thermal travel experience of my life. A service that doesn't work, trains that are never on time, connections that are impossible to get, and trains that don't pass. Not to mention the employees who are as motivated as octopuses Never again the train in Germany

At first you are happy to get a seat with your severely disabled 8 year old son in the bicycle compartment with 3 bicycles, 3 people and 3 of us and 2 other passengers. The train attendant is overwhelmed and just shouts at everyone who doesn't have a bike to leave the compartment immediately. Conclusion: my son sat on the stairs from Rostock to Neustrelitz. I ask myself what counts more, bikes or people. Then also late because the door is broken.

A trip without delays, interruptions, failures or technical defects seems impossible for the operators. A shame for Germany! Czech Republic, Poland, Switzerland, Austria, Italy, Slovenia etc. - everyone can do it, except Deutsche Bahn. Next time you fly again, the Greens should clean up the railway rather than raise more unnecessary taxes... :)

You arrive at Cologne station, recovered from a wonderful cruise, where you find out that the train is missing, you take the train to the Dietz Cologne trade fair, you wait there for 1.5 hours and this train goes to Frankfurt and then you have to go to another compartment and the seat reservation and from Frankfurt to Munich you just stand and that with a mentally handicapped young person and no seat😡😡And the train employees are unfriendly 😡😡Train the last of the last why aren't you hanging there working carriages again😡😡😡😡????The tickets are getting more and more expensive and there is always something 😡😡😡😡😡

What a bad company ICE is! Every time I had to take the train from Gottingen to Cologne, there was always a delay, which gave me at least 90 minutes of extra travel time. If I had to give it a 0, I would! Far too expensive on board. Let them first make sure that they can make a train run on time. If you can do otherwise, do not drive the ICE unless you feel like an extra travel day
Nightmare journey from Mannheim to Trento! Overcrowded train, we traveled standing despite having paid 150 euros for two people. Dirt and neglect. Shameful.

High capacity utilization is announced for an ICE in July 2022 from Vienna to Nuremberg and seat reservations are recommended. Two clicks further you get: seat reservation not possible. Selected train for the outward journey, entered all details, at the end: purchase online not possible. Contact our counter. There: It wasn't possible because there was still a subway ride in Vienna. Shouldn't the online booking system have told you that? Because the rating system here is only intended for trips that have taken place, the July information here and June do not match.

The train dies in the middle of the prairie. Nobody knows anything. After 1 1/2 hours the announcement comes: The train is not moving any further! What should you do? Answer from the employees: no idea! We packed our things and set off on foot. Then take a taxi to Hamburg main station. DB information stand: 'no idea'. At some point the information: you get a hotel room paid for. Only there was no free room in Hamburg (information at the main station). AND NOW COMES THE HAMMER! Statement from the DB employee: "I don't care! ^After a long odyssey we finally arrived home (800 km to Augsburg). Conclusion: I can only warn everyone about taking the train!

Also today... from Berlin (use of the ICE) to Frankfurt, delay... the car in which I had reserved was locked, another car was completely missing. There was no information about this in advance. I had to look for a new seat in a different car. Angry guests and annoyed staff. Just embarrassing! WiFi is a luxury when it works. It can't work like that, I'm always amazed at how well things are going with our European neighbors, for example. Suggestion: just look over the fence and then get started with a realistic and customer-friendly concept! Greetings from Berlin

Deutsche Bahn is by far the most brazen means of transport of all. Actually, you should file a claim against them for psychological injuries. Punctuality is a foreign word. The only punctual thing is to increase the already exorbitant prices. If you want to arrive healthy and happy, take the car, taxi or plane but avoid the train!!

Get ready for delayed trains, inaccurate and conflicting messages form the time board and the app and long waiting times sitting in a full un-air conditioned train that is just staying at the train station for prolonged periods without a reason. With an 8h journey expect a 50 minute delay and any connecting trains with under 5 minutes to switch will be missed. (Even when the train claims to be on time) The poor organization and execution of the deutsche Bahn is the main factor keeping the public  from the desired ‚verkehrswende‘, (switching from cars to public transport)

Too expensive, always too late or they simply don't come at all and then don't even count it as an unpunctual train. Overall a huge joke but above all a really rude and impudent attitude towards the customers!

Unfortunately, I HAVE to take the train between Hamburg and Lübeck every day. Imponderables can arise, no question about it and it is certainly a mammoth task to ensure the coordination of all connections, but I still ask myself why a company with so many employees has such a deficient structure and this catastrophic communication policy. Outside of 9 euro times, this unreasonable cost me a whopping 270 euros a month. This is not a motivation to give up private transport.

Unfortunately, I had another very bad experience. My train connection from Munich to Düsseldorf was canceled without giving any reason and therefore the train connection was no longer available. Now I've been chasing a refund of the reservation fees for almost 2 months and no one is taking any responsibility. I asked directly at Munich Central Station and after a not inconsiderable waiting time, they explained to me that they would need my printed ticket. I then explained that I would need this for the journey home and that they would be welcome to make a copy. Either the will, the competence or the technical possibilities were missing. Ultimately, as is usual in the digital age, I sent the application by post on May 3rd. Since then I have been trying to achieve something for 6 weeks, partly by email and partly by telephone. However, so far without success. The case law that refunds for canceled flights does not seem to apply to Deutsche Bahn. Just as I pointed this out, I was put back on hold without saying anything. Thank you for nothing!!! Apparently Deutsche Bahn is doing so badly that it feels like they are trying to cheat customers out of a refund.

The brutal and impudent tone of the conductor on duty, who was accompanied by two other train attendants who seemed to be being trained. The lady in question also spoke to the foreign English-speaking guests in a commanding tone. The woman had just snapped at us again so much that we had to put the mask on properly. The tone itself was very presumptuous and she stood threateningly in front of us with her arms akimbo. When asked to tell us her name, she said even more cheekily that we didn't get it. After asking twice, she said: I am chief platoon leader 158, and she simply continued on. Such insolence has never happened to us before.
Tickets purchased and paid for. Official looked on. June 12, Arnhem Düsseldorf with bicycles. Total €46, there are no trains. Whistling for your money

I have never experienced such a catastrophe in my life. The DeutscheBahn is late every day! Every day! Sometimes I wait an hour for my train, which is late!!! How can such a large corporation have such a miserable organization? I'm honestly at a loss for words!

Absolute disaster. Gifted daughter a trip to Paris for her 18th birthday with a boyfriend. It should be an unforgettable experience. That was actually it. A few days before we received the news that the train we had booked was not running. An alternative was offered. No problem, but... seat reservation is gone, a complete disaster in the days of the 9 euro ticket. Reservations for the new train are not possible online. It has to be said that the nearest train station with a counter is 37 km away. So no seats. Of course the train was late, so the connecting train couldn't be made. But... alternative here too. Of course, no more seat reservations either. There were 6 minutes left for the next change, so I was worried that this train wouldn't be late. That worked. And what can I say, the same game on the way back a few days later. Again no seat reservation because there are other trains. There was a delay and I couldn't make the last connecting train, so I had to drive 37 km to pick up my daughter and her boyfriend at night. Otherwise she could have spent the night on the platform. And that wasn't a 9 euro ticket. I invested a few hundred euros on it. This is how vacation is fun. Thank you DB for this experience. I'd rather pay 500 euros for a flight, but with you no more, not even for free.

So with the EUR 9 ticket you can perhaps accept the constant delays, train cancellations, construction sites including very confusing announcements on the platforms. At least if you have a lot of time and patience. If regular prices were to be announced again in September, I wouldn't take part in something like that...I'm currently constantly observing that the trains with severe delays (RE/RB/Vlexx) are ultimately completely empty. To be honest, the 9 ticket seems more like a fake excuse from the train. Even the conductor couldn't understand today's wrong journey and everyone was happy to get there at some point - ugh... (I was the only one in the entire compartment)

I had to go from Basel Badischer Bahnhof to Frankfurt Airport and back. On the way there we couldn't go any further, shortly after Mannheim, we stood there for minutes, then the announcement came that we couldn't go any further because of construction work, we had to go back "a little" and then via Worms to Frankfurt, the whole thing ended up taking an hour. On the way back the train left without any delay. I was supposed to change in Karlsruhe and Freiburg. Shortly before Karlsruhe I found out about one Passenger, not through a loudspeaker announcement that the train is not going to Freiburg, but only to Offenburg??? It was Sunday night and so I called my employees who organized a hotel for me in Karlsruhe. The train to Basel was supposed to leave at 6:59 a.m. in the morning, which left at around 8:10 a.m., so about 2 hours late. The train was supposed to go to Chur, but at some point the announcement came that the last stop was in Basel Badischer Bahnhof, but that was no longer my problem since I only had to get to Basel. In the end, it took me an hour longer from Frankfurt to Basel than the day before from Singapore to Frankfurt. In addition, my ticket cost 177 €, but the cars were completely overcrowded with 9 € backpack tourists who, as far as I know, aren't allowed to take the ICE? But then I found a seat in the on-board restaurant. There was no checking (while I was there).

We're currently on the train EC 173 from Berlin to Prague. Unfortunately, we haven't reserved a seat but we paid for a ticket! Staying in the in between zone of the tracks for 3 something hours is very unsafe. The person who checked our tickets was very rude and "spoke very little english". But she was very willing to help other german passengers. Race and age discrimination in a very unsafe trip. Ps: DB if no reserved seats mean non seats at all, AT LEAST let us know in advance.

After hearing on every corner that almost everything at the DB is bullshit, I have to report a very pleasant incident for us based on my limited experience with DB travel. We were in Dresden at the main train station yesterday afternoon and wanted to inquire about the train connection for two trips with the €9 ticket. Because we are not very good at using the computer, where you can find out the train connections and also print them out. We asked a DB employee who happened to be at the machine for help. This employee, her name was Ms. Raue - I would definitely like to mention the name of this employee here, even though I was certainly circumventing the data protection regulations, helped us very patiently and gave us advice to our complete satisfaction. Our big thanks again for this. This is how we imagine good service. We would like to get rid of that here. So that everyone's criticism of the DB can be countered with a small positive thank you, the Läntzsch family from Dippoldiswalde

Time and time again, Deutsche Bahn manages to provide even worse service than before.   Disrupted trains are commonplace.  A while ago I returned from leave in Frankfurt and had to take the train to Mannheim. Luckily the train was delayed -we thought- so we wouldn't have to rush. At just after 8:00 PM we waited and waited... until just after twelve (where one train after another was canceled)... and just after one I took a taxi (130 Euro) to get home (and so as not to be late for work).   Will not be refunded, because you only get a taxi ticket after five o'clock or something like that. Spent a few days in Paris five weeks ago, the outward journey went normally, against all expectations.  On the return journey, only the electronic ticket stated that the train had been cancelled.  Without further explanation (even the French railway officials could not say much more).  Because the next train was fully booked, it was ultimately decided to divide everyone over different French trains.  A ride to Metz. A slow train with an hour delay to Saarbruecken and then another slow train to Mannheim.  Finally, after five weeks, I received a letter stating that I would get my money back.  But I do have to send my bank details in writing (they don't accept e-mail/fax at Deutsche Bahn).  So I also have to pay postage so I can get my own money back.

It's great that you wait for the train in Munich and then it just spontaneously goes to Pasing. Wait 30 minutes for the next train here we go. Last week it took twice as long as normal because nothing ever happens on time.

Luckily, not everything goes as wrong in Germany as it does on the German railway tracks. Even the “simplest” journeys are complicated to the maximum. There isn't even an apology for the customer. As we waited for our delayed train in Freiburg, one announcement followed the next. All trains were at least 40 minutes late. A complete disaster, especially for those who have to make particularly long journeys. It's a shame that there is no alternative here.

I travel at least once a week with Deutsche Bahn long-distance transport and several times a week with regional transport. So far this year I have had ONE ONLY train on time. This week and last week I was traveling a lot and honestly ALL my trains were about 2 hours late. If Deutsche Bahn is on time, it's nothing short of a miracle!!! It should be the norm! In addition, the tickets are way too expensive and the service is damn bad! Seat reservations are usually not possible and the WiFi on the train does not work reliably either. A single catastrophe!!!!

I wanted to give the 9 euro ticket a chance and protect my wallet and the environment at the same time. I've been traveling in the Frankfurt area for 8 days now. There was no train that was on time. The train stopped several times and didn't even move on. Every time a different excuse. I am at a loss for words
Telephone information was given up after 1.5 hours of waiting. The announcement “please wait a MOMENT” is simply ridiculous.

Deutsche Bahn is the last piece of trash. Rumor has it that there are people who would be in favor of it if for every insolence, every incompetence, every impudence, every five minutes late, every connection missed due to terrible coordination and every cancellation of journeys due to the railway's fault, the people responsible for it, as well as generally every loud-mouthed controller, would get a good slap in the face. I fully share the aversion to the points of criticism listed here and can also confirm their high frequency. I reserve my opinion on the "in your face" component...

Infinite need for improvement Hello, I am severely disabled (impaired walking) and travel by train a lot. I don't want to complain about delays and canceled trains. Others already do that enough. I'm annoyed by different prices when I access the DB offerings from other computers. That an expensive tariff is foisted on me when I have to book at very short notice. Apparently there is no more quota and the train is almost empty. Different information about the location of bus stops, which I can no longer reach because I have difficulty walking. The bullying of apparently homeless people at the train station in Nuremberg, then 7 station guards came up to throw a homeless person out of the train station and also insult me. My wife told me the same thing elsewhere. I hope that capable staff will come to the management levels of Deutsche Bahn at some point. There is a need for renovation at all levels. Expansion of railway lines, repairs, timing, service and humanity. Kind regards, Siegfried Ritter

Deutsche Bahn is and remains a catastrophe! Delay on the outward journey, and on the return journey too. It wouldn't be such a problem if it didn't happen so often and if you didn't have to worry about your connection every time! A piece of advice: it's better to wear sports shoes so that you can run fast enough!!

Bought a 9 Euro ticket for a short bidness trip this week.  Process online from the US was easy. Loaded the app, and combined with DB Navigator, used it to  plan my trips on local trains in Hesse.  That is where the fun stopped.  WTF with the 25 minute delay for no reason, to include a smoke break yesterday afternoon?  Oh, more prep for the fun at Biblis when the train stopped and we were to to dissembark, for NO reason.  Probably 200 of us, milling around, trying to get to Mannheim.  Ended up taking a taxi.  DB 9 Euro sux!

I went to the restaurant of ICE 722 NBG to Gießen to have a meal and sit down at a table; because my luggage is quite large I sat at a 4 person seat even though I was by myself. The restaurant was only half full and so there was plenty of space. I was told by the waiter that I had to sit at a table for two people because my table was to be used only by groups of four or moreAt two other tables there were groups of two and one yet they were able to enjoy a large table even though I was not.The waiter was very rude and used racially offensive language which I find to be intolerable. The waiter’s name is: Herr S. Schlopper.

Unfortunately there are always delays. Even though the trains sometimes leave on time, they are still late. The last time from Basel to Frankfurt there was a 50 minute delay around midnight. Every now and then the German trains wait for the German trains but if you have to change trains in Switzerland then they don't wait as they are usually on time.

I had booked a first class trip with the Zukunft company towards Bensersiel, return, for my over-80 mother and her over-80 girlfriend. Unfortunately, what the two women were then able to experience reflects exactly what one now expects from Deutsche Bahn. Exactly 2 trains “worked” on the trip without them being on time. Ultimately, the return journey was not in 1st class DB but in the middle of all the 9 euro ticketers on the Eurobahn. The fact that this company ultimately arrives at the destination station only 9 minutes later speaks for itself. Unfortunately, this service ultimately also ensures that passenger rights are rejected by the DB because the delay is less than 60 minutes. The fact that it was not possible to fill out the passenger rights form because the date cannot be entered exactly may be due to the general technical inadequacies of Deutsche Bahn. As a person who travels widely, I am familiar with customer service in Asia and other regions of the world. Managers would have to leave there and the customer would be reasonably compensated for services not provided. Here you will be harassed on the phone. With a single exception, which consists of a nice employee who doesn't speak German particularly well. This gentleman, to whom I was mistakenly linked, sincerely apologized for the inconvenience. This nice person deserves the salaries of bad management!

Never again by train!!!!!!!!The booked ICE train NR 77 including seat reservation Hamburg/Karlsruhe left 1.5 hours earlier without notifying the DB customer. We found out by chance and asking about the train at the counter. The train staff were cheeky and rude and the fact that we weren't expelled from the station was one thing. I've never experienced anything like that and it was definitely my last trip with the DB. An alternative (rental car) was unaffordable.

All prejudices were confirmed. I wanted to try out the 9 euro ticket. U 35 from Herne to Bochum onward journey to Aachen. From Bochum hbf U Bahn to the hbf platform no escalator worked, the train was delayed every 10 minutes for a total of 50 minutes. I didn't think I was going to Düsseldorf... the two trains were so full that I couldn't get in. Plan c was then we go to Essen..locomotive with 2 carriages...Plan d was then drawn. I went over the broken escalators to the u35 and went back to Herne. I lost about 2 hours of life and sat in my Fiesta st and drove to Münster. Clean city, no drunken redneck tourists and by chance I met Wilsberg, at least the antiquarian bookstore

9.-€ ticket + Pentecost. One could assume that one or two more passengers use the DB. Has DB management or logistics also asked themselves this question? Completely overcrowded train stations. Then the Konstanz-Karlsruhe regional train actually came with 3 carriages, within seconds they were completely overcrowded. Only after the federal police came and ordered passengers out of the carriage was the train able to set off late. Guests were unable to board at all stops. If management in the private sector worked like this, bankruptcy would be predictable.

Unfriendly staff, windows stay closed but masks should stay on, of course it makes sense. The conductor hisses at you if you take a quick drink and don't have a cloth in front of your face. So really not a compliment to Deutsche Bahn, as always. It's become a real juice shop since the state no longer has anything to say about you. And the Greens wonder why everyone is willing to pay €3 for gas.

This time I was really satisfied and both the outward journey and the return journey (long-distance train) worked wonderfully and without any delays. The staff was polite and the train was surprisingly clean. I've had a completely different experience on DB trains. Overall, this time everything was very good despite high seat occupancy.

just sad! the last 8-10 train journeys. all with complications and delays! Trips to the airport very risky! It's best to start with something else or a day in advance if you don't want to miss your flight.

Very unfriendly staff have no qualms about yelling at anyone for no reason. I think something like that doesn't work at all and is disrespectful. Such people shouldn't work in public but in the farthest corner in a basement! So you can see that some people don't know what to do with their lives other than complaining to others. Shameful service, traveled from Munich to Berlin (apart from the hour delay that may be there) but wi-fi not working, water in the bathroom taps not working in any bathroom, then the bar closes, I ask for a drink and they deny it... are you keeping me an extra hour because of you and you also deny me a drink? For €80 I think it's fair to expect better service! Shame

In Germany if you keep coming late to work you will be fired and if you are a foreigner you will have to get a new job or leave the country.Sadly, the Deutsche Bahn can contribute to this bad luck, big time. Your boss cannot stand the fact that your train is randomly delayed or broken, with additional 25 minutes to get another connection. Even if you leave home real early to catch train you will be surprised at the disappointments. Recently the S8 from Munich to the airport was delayed for a good 30 minutes, thankfully we planned to leave earlier and could make it 2 hours before flight departure. One will think that connection to airports ought to function without any delay in a city like Munich, but NO!The train system is often a disappointment and I will advice to always be on the look out for possible bus or tram. The underground train can also be delayed and canceled. Because I live in the city, I can look for alternatives faster but beware of the Deutsche Bahn and understand how this affects your official appointments or work hours.

The only absolutely positive thing about the German railway is the staff. I almost feel sorry for these people. Since I will be flying again from now on and I will advise everyone to do so. There is no journey that is not delayed, really none and I have been driving a lot lately. The delay would be bearable for me, but then not being able to offer an internet connection so that you can at least work is really an absolute shame.

For work I have to commute between Bavaria and Brandenburg every weekend. Travel time is over 8 hours if everything goes well. However, that never happens. Since the beginning of the Corona pandemic, the train has had the opportunity to show you that it is a good alternative to a car or plane. However, she can't do that. Constant technical problems, operational disruptions, etc. make every train journey a trip into the unknown. Transfer times of 15 minutes are regularly too short, as almost no long-distance train is even remotely on time. Especially in the evening hours, when connecting S Bahn or regional trains only run irregularly, small delays can often add up to delays of two hours or more. The railway fails because of everything: punctuality, service, reliability. I feel sorry for the train attendants who regularly get the justified anger of passengers. Conclusion: Cars and planes for traveling within Germany are significantly faster, less stressful and even cheaper.

Unfortunately you have to give at least one star. I can't remember the last time I took a train without it being late, canceled or something else. Now I had to travel a fairly short distance thanks to construction work at 6!! Take transfers (with enough time for all transfers according to the plan, mind you!). That was okay in itself. What's not ok - the first change was successful - is that the train arrived late for no good reason and just like that, it stands in the middle of the route for 20 minutes. As a result, pretty much everyone on the train in question missed their changes. The icing on the cake: the dear train driver couldn't give any information about alternatives for any of the connecting trains (around 4 as far as I could tell) (because there didn't seem to be any) and at the information desk I was told that I should take a later connection to the last stop on the train and from there pay for a taxi (about 20km remaining distance, which should be covered with a bus from another transport company. But since a later connection now has to be taken, no bus runs from there). They can't tell me whether I'll get the money back for the taxi. Thank you dear Bahn - I pay a lot of money for a ticket for a connection that is offered, but the way they work is unlikely to work even once. That's pretty sad. And on top of that, shell out another good €50 for a taxi. For me as a student, by the way, this is more than my entire weekly shopping - applause! Probably 11 hours of driving for a mere 350-400 km, that's a joke! Unfortunately I can't say it any other way, but here service, planning and implementation failed across the board.

The Deutsche Bahn and the GDL are the LAST THING!!! EVERY other company would go bankrupt but a monopoly remains a monopoly! Nothing works at this pig shop!! STOP SHITTING ON THE CUSTOMERS, it works DRIVING UNPUNCTUALLY OR NOT AT ALL, also works AND RAISE PRICES ON TIME, the gentlemen are also the elite!!! Ergo: This is the last dirty shop. You belong to the nationalized again

To Team DB:  You (and the related regional trains) made my last two trips to Germany a GREAT experience!  There was a sales agent named Angela who spent 30 minutes with me on the DB international phone line helping me plan my trip to Germany.  She was incredibly helpful and kind!  She should be the international ambassador for all of Team DB.  She represents DB well.  Also, Martin was very helpful in the international office.  Now, here is my review of the trains and train stations:  The Hamburg train station was very clean and user friendly.  The people in the station were very nice to me.  I am absolutely humbled by your patience.  Also, three cheers for HVV for helping me see Hamburg.After two days, I took DB to Berlin.  The train from Hamburg to Berlin was superb!  Wow, what an experience!  The hospitality on board the train was amazing.  I had a bike and everyone at DB made the trip so easy for me.  All of the employees went above and beyond to help me.  I could not have had such a great experience without their help!The Berlin HBF was amazing!  I love the place because EVERYONE WAS SO NICE.  I could find everything I needed in one place.  I stayed in Berlin four days.  IT IS ABSOLUTELY MY FAVORITE CITY IN EUROPE!  I LOVE THE PLACE AND WANT TO COME BACK OFTEN!  (See my trip advisor review of Berlin.)  My hotel was right across the street from the Berlin HBF.  The Tiergarten was nearly across the street.  How in the world can you not enjoy Berlin when you are staying right across the street from the Tiergarten?  After four incredible days in Berlin, I took the early morning DB to Munich today and the train and crew were fantastic!  This afternoon, I am enjoying a beer in the sun at the Chinese Temple in the English Garten?  Wow, this would not have been possible without DB!!  After reading the above, my only reaction is:“Way to go, Hamburg and DB!”“Way to go, Berlin and DB (with a special shout out to Angela and Martin at DB International)!”“Way to go, Munich and DB!”“Let’s hear it again!”“Way to go, Hamburg and DB!”“Way to go, Berlin and DB (with a special shout out to Angela and Martin at DB International)!”“Way to go, Munich and DB!”I LOVE GERMANY!  TEAM DB, YOUR HOSPITALITY, KINDNESS AND PATIENCE MAKES ME WANT TO COME BACK SOON!  Thank you for making my trip to Germany SO ENJOYABLE!

Impossible... you want to do something for the environment and travel by long-distance instead of plane, just 5 days after booking there is a strike AGAIN! The DB service hotline confirmed that our train would run as scheduled. 10 hours before the start of the journey, the travel information said “Stop canceled”. Thanks DB. You are by far the largest juice shop there is. A shame for Germany and then want to preach to people that they should pay more attention to the environment and take the train... NEVER AGAIN!!!
The German railway should pay its people better so that the damn train runs, damn MAACH ESSS
Constant problems and delays without notifying the passengers, and unfortunately no other reasonable options to travel in Germany

The DB is slowly becoming a big disappointment for me. My tip would be to listen to what people have to say more! I have one question: How often do you want to go on strike? At the beginning I slowly lost my understanding. There are people who are not mobile and have to go to work or have important surgery appointments. We would be happy if you didn't constantly think about money, but also about people.

Dear DB, today I would like to give a personal compliment to Ms. Constantinescu(n). Unfortunately, my trip to Paris had to be canceled because of the strike. I had a super saver ticket that legitimately cannot be canceled. Apart from the fact that I was given two options to either get the amount refunded or to postpone the trip, your colleague was more than friendly, professional and accommodating! The train drivers and the like are still on strike. So please don't dump your frustration on the DB's mostly very friendly employees! I would like to thank Ms. Constantinescu(n) and the DB for this goodwill!!

Terrible. Every year it’s the same thing, or even worse. Constant delays and train cancellations. They constantly fail to provide reliable information about when the train will arrive, and indeed whether it will arrive at all. Ticket prices are rising every year, and the service is falling lower and lower. Steadily, several times a week they have some problems that they cannot resolve for many hours. Today it took me 3 hours to get home instead of 30 minutes. No information, the application is buggy and shows trains where there are none. No alternative transport (bus) was provided so that people could get home after work. I can understand that there are different situations, but not EVERY week??!?!?!?! You can never rely on the timetable, you always have to take the train an hour or two earlier because you don’t know what will happen. If you need to get to the airport or have an important meeting, it is better to take a taxi. I don't recommend DB to anyone.

The worst transportation company ever! Horrible services! Ridiculous ticket prices! Not surprising, considering that they have a monopoly over Germany! Also horrible contract conditions (their whole BahnCard system) I hope other trains companies start operating too, because Deutsche Bahn does not deserve your money!

It wasn't the first time that the first class seats we had booked were already full. Last October from Cologne to Munich these seats were taken twice even though the car was almost empty. You could choose another place, okay. The trip from Munich to Bolzano on Wednesday, August 18th. with EC 81 at 7:34 a.m. was a fiasco. The first class was completely booked and the compartment we reserved was occupied and blocked by the drinks service. The train attendant who was summoned gave us a rude and impertinent message that we should stay at home if we were afraid. Friendly fellow travelers then offered us seats in their compartment, otherwise we, 73 and 77 years old, would have had to stand for four hours! You seriously ask yourself what the railway wants to achieve with such actions. We reported the incident to the railway and received a notification of receipt, but processing: Nothing reported so far! The strike and reassurance of the employees probably have priority over customer orientation, but be careful: the customer who orients himself otherwise does not put any money into the coffers!

Hello, the biggest son of a bitch club in Germany, we wanted to go from Wiesbaden to Flörsheim. We left at 12 p.m. and now we are in Frankfurt. So I have no idea what that's about. We pay money and precious time for this, when I could be doing more important things in the meantime, like counting grains of sand on the beach in Flörsheim, oh that's right, they still haven't arrived in Flörsheim. At least the replacement rail service was very pleasant with a sequence of villages where the bus driver thought we were bumper cars. Thanks but never again, I'd rather run for 5 hours instead of investing a cent in DB.

Just unbelievably bad!!! I had to change trains in Cologne Deutz with my wife and small children 5 years old and younger, one of them in a stroller. The train station looks like a construction site, which may be ok, but there are neither escalators in all directions nor elevators to be found anywhere. Individual stairs are completely blocked. As a non-resident, it is absolutely impossible to reach the appropriate connecting train within a few minutes in this constellation. Information about this can be found in the service center... how should I help you now??? Then you simply have to buy a new ticket and wait 1.5 hours for the next ice cream with your small children... if my children hadn't been there, I would have been even more unreasonable like him and would have gotten violent. Tickets are becoming more and more expensive, service and general service are getting massively worse... Next time I'll take the plane from Frankfurt to Cologne... or some other means of transport with which we can trample on environmental protection!!!

The trains usually leave on time and the conductors are mostly not really friendly. But the hammer was on the train .Munich Stuttgart ICE around 1800. The air conditioning and cooling didn't work, but the mask requirement in the sauna 35 degrees is important!!!! Actually, that should be forbidden!!!! Unfortunately there is no alternative

It is not for nothing that one of the train companies in Europe that has to complain about delays the most. Only Lithuania is worse in this respect. German punctuality is a virtue that certainly doesn't apply here! Unfortunately, I have to realize that I am unable to complete a single journey without being late. This is a catastrophe that is unparalleled. I would like to avoid having to take the car, but unfortunately I often have no other choice if I want to attend an appointment without stress. I'm angry and frustrated at the same time because it just doesn't get better over the years.

Can I give less than 1 starCan I give less than 1 star? That's how I feel after our "trip" today... we took the wrong S-Bahn from Munich east and actually wanted to go to Haar - the S6 usually goes there. Landed in Grafing - bought a ticket to Haar, selected the train and still had to buy a ticket again because apparently we didn't have a real ticket and the aver don't sell a ticket for the MVG either - pure rip-off, absolutely no empathy and their own machine probably doesn't work properly. Because of climate change we want an alternative - anything but the train!!! Damn company!!

LITERALLY TAKE ANY OTHER TRAIN. seats not comfy. The food sucks, there’s 2 options for breakfast…the workers are freaking clueless. They won’t offer you any water either. Seriously this is a piece of junk

Dramatically awful. Unfortunately my car broke down so I had no other option to get back home from the airport. First and definitely last time of my life trying to use German train transport. What would have taken 1,5 hours by car, now went as follows; First train; delayed by 10 minutes without any information anywhere about this. Fine, not too big of a deal. Second train I had to take; without any information just stood still for over half an hour after it should have left. After this long time it drove to the next station, where the whole train just shut off and went dark, again with no information. After 20 minutes someone said the train tracks were not working somehow and the trains were just not going to move anymore. At this point I have been trying to get home by German train for over 3 hours and I was not even half way yet!! Forcing me to have to to call people who had to drive to the station for over an hour to pick me up so I could FINALLY go home after a very long travel. So looking back at it I should've bothered someone to drive for me for hours right at the start. So yes, ridiculously hopeless and amateuristic 'organization'.

Today there is a strike again - which is understandable. But the railway still manages to misbehave 👏 you might think that it always wants to live up to its reputation! Because the train driver to Munich couldn't wait 5 minutes for the connecting train, all passengers now had to wait 2 hours. Was the train driver in question deaf, stupid or just a sadist? Apparently not a second thought. There's no justification for that. Then the station was kindly filled with the same announcements for 2 hours, very practical when waiting! After waiting for 2 hours, the next train simply arrived on a different track - but of course there was no announcement! Wow, that's an achievement, hats off to you. If the people on the platform hadn't communicated with each other, everything would have gone wrong - the next train would have arrived 3 hours later and would have taken 5 hours to travel. A dream for commuters, and especially people who depend on their job! Oh yes, and the railway hasn't been able to pay back the money for a canceled Bahncard for four weeks. What a mess! I'm happy to pay completely overpriced tickets for that!!!!

The punctuality of this company is indisputable.  I spent fifteen days traveling with her throughout Germany and I didn't have any problems.  Its biggest defect lies, for me, in that it has very old carriages as soon as you leave the areas most traveled by Germans by train (or the most important cities).

1st class with reservation to Berlin 1 hour late and no seat! Back to Berlin 2!!! Hours late (1st train late, connecting train missed, next possible train late). 1st class ticket with reservation - travel 2nd class WITHOUT A SEAT ON THE FLOOR for over 4 hours! Shame on you!
Bad company, bad service, app does not work. They take your money and you dont get a ticket. No service, no response.

I traveled for the first time on the train from Hamburg to Frankfurt airport, punctual and comfortable train, 3 and a quarter hours of decent travel I must say. In truth, I would have expected more about the modernity of these trains which are the equivalent of our high speed trains which in my opinion are much better and newer. However a good experience, I recommend it

If incompetence had a symbol, it would be Deutsche Bahn. First of all: Of course, this doesn't affect all employees, because there are some good ones among them. My conclusion after 4 years of intensive use of the train: About half of all my long-distance journeys (from 2 hours on fast connections) had a significant delay (more than 30 minutes). At least every second train used had a technical malfunction (air conditioning or heating broken, etc.). All of this would still be somewhat acceptable if the inflexibility and audacity of many employees and the company per se were not just as frustrating as their reliability. Our own mistakes are briefly excused, but occasional mistakes made by loyal customers are punished uninhibitedly. This is one of the rare cases where a foreign company takeover would be welcome.

I travel long distances with the DB every week - hardly any train is on time. There's always something... Train broken, air conditioning broken, no WiFi Complete inability in a country like Germany! China AND Japan do it perfectly - Germany is not able - how embarrassing!
It couldn't be worse. ICE has fun, NO TRAIN ON TIME, canceled trains aren't even shown online. You travel fun with your online ticket and get NO NOTIFICATION that the trains are all cancelled.

After 1.5 years, Corinna is going on a long-distance trip again, so we're going from Leipzig to Frankfurt Airport and back. The other years we've always been able to get to the airport parking lot without a hitch, including a transfer. This time I thought it would be more relaxed by taking the train to the flight. After boarding, I was told that the train wasn't going to the airport this time due to technical problems, but that you had to get off beforehand and look for a replacement with the S-Bahn or another train. As a result, changing, Stress, running around and being at the airport 1 hour later than planned. Of course you can get stuck in a traffic jam by car, but I don't know why in Germany you can't manage to rely on public transport. Just take a look at Asia and see how things are going there...
-5. Outrageous, train cancellations and delays without any consideration for customers. You should expect a delay of at least 6 hours for short journeys, regardless of the time of day.

The three of us traveled from Berlin to Amsterdam and back with German trains. We thought in advance that it would be relaxing to travel by train and bought tickets specifically for 1st class at the counter. You would think that you would get three seats together for a journey of 6.5 hours. But no - we were put into three different separate compartments 🤦‍♀️ Due to Corona, only a maximum of three people are currently allowed to sit in a compartment for six people. So it was stopped when we still wanted to sit down together. Exchanges with others were also not possible. In addition, the on-board bistro was closed for about half of the journey. However, apparently due to technical difficulties, the on-board staff simply got out. So much for the first trip. On the return trip (by the way, at the counter when we bought the tickets it was said that we were sitting together in a compartment) we were placed on two benches for two, but Corona suddenly no longer played a role because a fourth person was seated next to us 😡That's so ridiculous and just totally outrageous! In addition, there was completely incorrect communication when purchasing tickets and no attention was paid to it! Finally, I would like to mention that it is completely unnecessary to pay an extra charge for 1st class because the seats are in no way more comfortable and there are no other advantages at all. Thank you very much, dear Deutsche Bahn, for nothing! You definitely made our trip a little less pleasant!

I take the DB about 24 times a year and have a delay rate of 80%!!!!!! I'm not talking about 5 minute delays but ones that are 30 minutes or more. DB is the biggest dirty club and cares 0 about the satisfaction of its customers. If I had the opportunity I would use alternatives but which ones?
The staff is unbearable, rude, doesn't answer questions, and totally ruins a day of travel. THANKS.

Always late, bad WiFi. Just had another very bad experience: I was late again and rushed through the station with my suitcase and everything to catch the connecting train. There was a conductor on the platform who recognized my situation. Instead of helping me and a fellow passenger (5-10 seconds would have been enough), she did nothing. Result: I was still able to touch the train's door opener sensors (it hadn't started yet), but the doors no longer opened and the train drove away from under my nose.

I am very unnerved and very, very disappointed with Deutsche Bahn. I haven't traveled for a long time because of the lockdown and I forgot my username and password. I'm probably not the only one....Instead of sending me a link to reset it, DB suspended my account. Your phone number is unreachable. Yesterday I waited over 40 minutes to speak to someone and because I had another appointment I had to hang up.  The RobotVoice said the average wait time would be 7 minutes. Today I waited over 35 minutes and still didn't get anyone on the phone. I hung up again and created a new user account and booked my ticket. What annoys me the most is that the price has increased by more than 67% compared to yesterday. That's the DB business model I think. It's just outrageous to make people wait so long and then cheat them out of their money

Deutsche Bahn is a parody of a transport company and would not be able to survive in this form with competition on the market. Unpunctual trains, toilets with more syringes than in an intensive care unit (if they even work), annual steering gear failures and outsourced ticket controllers, 70% of whom are former bouncers who you wouldn't even want in a disco.

Terribly organized, delays that take hours for things they should Know and inform in advance. I wish they start paying attention to the terrible service they are providing. People should be able to make plans and not get regularly affected by the train problems

I have been in DB trains in past years. Nothing but wonderful experiences. Normally I always traveled in First class. Restaurants, seats, quality of food and service were just what you’d expect from the luxury class. Some years on I came back and obviously I longed for that first class. Began my dream trip from Munich to Hamburg!  Paid a high price and boy what a heartbreak and what a sad disappointment!  Restaurant now is more like a back door coffee shop. Service nonexistent, baggage storage lacking tracks need maintenance. Breakfast gone due to malfunction of cold storage. It simply was a super downer. DB stands for Deutsche Bahn but now it’s more like a Depleted Bahn. I feel for the workers but not for the management. Trains should fun rides, especially when one pays a steep price for first class. I sadly would not recommend any first class on DB. If your trip within Germany is more than a 5 hour train ride fly. Price are great and you’re sure to enjoy a less rocky ride.

The Deutsche Bahn is notoriously disliked, I was certain this notion was exaggerated until I experienced it myself. Dear reader, let me tell you, it does live up to its terrible reuputation. We were controlled by a very pushy train attendant, that told us that we had the wrong ticket - in German, of course. He took us out of the train - and explained that while he did have to fine us, the fine would, due to the insignificant amount of difference to the “correct” ticket, 0.70 € per person, the fine would be annulled once we got to the reisencentrum and spoke to DB-personnel. He assured us that he would write the circumstances, the insignificant amount and us doing our best to interpret the ticket-fares – and it would not be a problem.This illusion was shattered when we did get to the Reisecentrum and spoke to personnel there, as they told us that there was nothing they could do and that we had to pay 120€ due to the “incorrect” ticket, despite us showing the ticket and the attendant had assured us that it would not be a problem. (Please recall that the difference was 0,70€ ). We paid – but naturally feeling cheated and unfairly treated.With such dishonesty from the whole chain-of encounters with the DB, I am not certain that we had the wrong ticket to begin with. We felt as he was taking advantage of us not being German as we did not fully grasp what he was talking about. This suspicion reinforced when we later learned (from DB-personell, mind you) that the attendants have an economic incentive to issue fines as they receive a sort of “commission”. The attendands are (seemingly) free to lie all they want, and you have no way to appeal the fine - and non-German speakers make excellent targets for such predatory practices. Thank you for reading, and be careful!

I wanted to go from Bamberg to Fulda, but I couldn't even get on the train, even though I arrived at the train at 20 after 6. Departure would not have been until 6:25. The doors were closed and they didn't open them again in those 5 minutes. No railway employee in sight, so I sprinted forward to the driver. When I arrived, he looked at me, shook his head and drove off at 6:24. I wasn't the only one who had to get on that train. In the end I bought a train ticket for free and now I had to let myself go. In addition, the money is gone and you don't get a refund.

I've been on hold for over 40 minutes because you can't request a new password yourself online. It must be double verified. Just cause yourself a few more problems, Deutsche Bahn. Your reputation is going so well. Just bad.

I can only agree with the negative reviews. Especially when it comes to regional trains. I am a commuter and am forced to use regional trains regularly. Not only are there delays and train cancellations every day, the trains are dirty, the toilets are often unusable and the train staff, especially when problems arise, are either untraceable and sometimes unfriendly. No trace of adequate service. The railway makes a lot of money from commuters, but is treated most shabbily. The service is only ok on the ICE trains.

"Carefree travel with the DB" or "The DB makes you mobile" are baseless slogans. Through the DB controller Mr. S., on the Kempten-Augsburg route in the RE 3389, I had the personal experience of harassment, arbitrariness, discrimination, abuse of power, intimidation, self-righteous behavior in dealing with my medical certificate for mask exemption. My original certificate with the original stamp and original signature of the doctor should arbitrarily not be credible for this inspector. I am denied a (provable) severe disability. My justifications and questions were ignored by him. He deliberately sought out my proximity several times, led pressure-exerting, intimidating monologues ("You have to be careful, there are police officers on the platforms"), led minute-long monologues about fake certificates ("I heard that.....") and denied me (I was traveling with an acquaintance) a pleasant, unmolested trip. What is the company's goal? This was followed by my personal experience with a DB employee at the ServicePoint Augsburg, who, due to his incompetence (false statement: every passenger has to wear a mask despite a certificate) confirmed the cancellation of the trip. Does DB value competence and professionalism? Education certainly plays a key role. The journey continued by car. So much for the topic of “climate protection.” This was followed by my personal experience with the DB customer dialogue team. Here I have to notice that the DB is refusing to give a concrete statement (detailing the incidents I have described individually). This has little to do with customer dialogue: no apology for misconduct, no reimbursement for the fact that I was not allowed to continue my train journey. In my opinion, this represents unjustified enrichment without legal justification. Benevolent and solution-oriented dialogues took place between another DB ServicePoint employee and with the police. Understood.

We took the ICE from Augsburg to Hamburg and it started to happen that the air conditioning and ventilation failed in first class and it was unbearably hot for the entire seven hours... on the way back, strangely enough, it was too cold at night and you couldn't dim the lights. Likewise, the on-board restaurant was almost non-existent on both routes and there was a lot of fridge there... Of course, there was a triple delay on the way back due to technical problems and connecting trains were missed. It's really sad that everything seems to be getting worse and nothing is getting better. And as you can read, Deutsche Bahn is also dismantling route networks instead of properly preparing them... it's really bad

From Flensburg to Hamburg with an electric wheelchair. Staff very friendly and helpful. Registered with the MSZ days in advance, they will be available on the day of travel and will help you get to the train and the U/S-Bahn. Conductors and MSZ employees help with loading. Everything went smoothly. No delays, train compartment clean.
Really bad and sickening! Delays to the point of departure, missed connecting trains and price increases every year are really outrageous.

Oh man. I drove from Menges to Ulm on Saturday. The train stopped in Stuttgart (ice610). All passengers get off in the direction of Frankfurt and take ICE 598 to Mannheim. No sooner said than done. Missed the connection to Kiel. In Mannheim on ICE 108 to Cologne and also delayed in Cologne. Follow train path. No information on the train about what happens next. Went from Cologne to Hamburg at 4:27 p.m. But of all the ICEs, only one had an on-board bistro. Instead of 10 hours, 12.5 hours on the road. Home again today and the game started again. ICE from Hamburg due to PU diversion. That's okay, but there was no food or drinks there either. Only an emergency sale (sandwich and beer unrefrigerated) to Stuttgart. Took a different train from Stuttgart because the connection was delayed and the last train in Ulm couldn't be reached. You would think that there would be some decent food there! Nope, just another emergency sale (IC to Salzburg). I wonder what DB is thinking about treating their guests like this. You had long enough time to get your fleet ready. I'm extremely disappointed in you, and as a train driver who would understand a lot. You got rid of me as a Bahncard 100 customer. Thanks for nothing.

It's not about the journey, it's about the Schlebusch train station, platform 2. It's completely dirty, there are only stairs, no elevator, impossible for wheelchair users and strollers to reach. And I was born here in 1962 and nothing has changed. The track was made but not properly either. Wheelchair users can see how they get out of the RB 48 onto the platform. Should they jump down with the wheelchair? So people from the DB you should be really ashamed, the picture of NRW is sad.A.Budeus

The German railway is a disgrace for the country. Far too many delays and cancellations, it is impossible to plan reliably by train. It's expensive, I drive my BMW significantly cheaper, when I'm traveling with two people it's on average 50% cheaper! When there is a delay, the incompetent staff usually have no idea and are not only useless in finding alternatives, but are also happy to make the situation worse. It's just sad

Simply unbearable! Stuffing the ICE so full during Corona times! I assumed that the reservation requirement controls and aims to prevent 100% occupancy. Instead, people squeeze in close together. A woman sat next to me for 4 hours, coughing and sneezing while on tour. This is far from safe and relaxing travel!

Another trip with DB which deserves to be described as „absolut disaster“ due to delays (that’s what DB does best .. being delayed). From now onwards I rather pay 5 times the price for a flight and not having the stress. This company would be bankrupt without being backed up by the government.

The worst service, the most rude staff and you also paid a lot of money for a first class ticket. Apparently there have been signal errors for a long time on a simple railway line between Oldenburg and Bremen. That could have been said before we started. Missed the connection to Cologne. As a result, no air conditioning. Stop on the open road. When I asked what was going on, I was told what interested me. The railway can only be saved through privatization. Everything else is just junk. For our part, we will never take the train again in our lives. And I can only advise everyone to do the same.

After a fantastic bike tour on the "Isar Cycle Path" where we had one delay after another on the way there with the ICE from Würzburg to Munich, the trouble continued on the return journey from Plattling to Würzburg. An overzealous train attendant insisted that we hang our E-MTB on the much too narrow hooks on the bike racks, even though we had the appropriate lashing straps for level attachment and had done this in agreement with the respective train attendant x times before. The height of incompetence was evident in the demand to remove the batteries and take them into the train compartment. Hello,My name is Maryam. I am a master’s student specialized in neuroscience and currently living in Osnabruck. I am writing to detail my harrowing and shocking experience with Deutsch bahn, something that I would not wish upon anyone, especially a foreigner like myself. Earlier today, on my way back to Osnabruck from Berlin, I accidentally missed my stop and had no choice but to turn to the staff in charge of dealing with ticket issues for help. She advised me to go all the way to Rheine. later on and before 5 minutes of Rheine station she decided to suddenly demand that I showed her my tickets. I did as I was told but I was surprised because I mentioned before my ticket was to Osnabruck. Without hesitation, she slapped me with a ticket of 32 Euros and despite my concession that I was partially responsible for this mishap, my willingness to pay for my honest mistake, she kept hurling insults and snide remarks at me without batting an eyelash. After trying to reason with her about my lapse in focus that caused me to miss the train, I offered to pay her through my bank card, which according to Deutsche B site is listed as a perfectly valid means of payment, she flatly turned it down and clamored for cash, which I did not have with me at that moment. Then I had to resort to borrowing from the passenger next to me but still the issue wasn’t settled because she insisted that such a solution wasn’t allowed in this country of Germany, then I mentioned ok I will book online or I ask my friend to book for me (by the way I was explaining all in my broken German) but she refused. By then, I was at my wits’ end and asked her what she would expect me to do. To my dismay, she demanded that I should pay a heftier amount and show her my passport. I decided to cater to her obnoxious demand but what really offended me was her condescending attitude towards me throughout this whole incident. She made no effort to hide her contempt, disdain through her words, her tone and I became the sole target of her discrimination simply because of my skin color and heritage. She didn’t seem to take into consideration the fact that I am an educated individual and when I reasoned with her that this sort of thing could befall anyone, regardless of status or race, she rebuffed firmly by claiming that only someone like me would experience it as we’re both in German territory. Her racist words really pierced through my heart like a knife and shattered my dignity. To add insult to injury, she sneered at me when I kindly asked her if she could speak English, as if implying that anybody who isn’t fluent in German deserved to be treated like inferiors in Germany. What really shook me to my core and fueled my indignation in this incident wasn’t the 60 Euro fine but the saddening fact that I was treated with disrespect and rudeness and was made to feel like a lesser being for no other reason than my race. Therefore, I am taking my time to relay this story of outrageous discrimination to appeal to you to please weed out such racism from your organization and train your staff to respect foreigners who come to Germany for various purposes and contribute to the country’s prosperity.N.B: my student card from Osnabrück University allows me to take RB for free to Rheine so It was not my dream to be in Rheine it was just that I missed the train stop and which I have also informed her.

The train is the last resort and before I use their services again, I would rather walk or stay at home! I have never come across a more outrageous and inaccessible club like them!!!!

Unfortunately, I cannot start my train journey due to the short-term ban on overnight stays. Since I booked the super saver price (1st class), a refund is not possible according to DB. Here you should actively offer the traveler at least a voucher or a free rebooking.

THE indictment for Germany is the DB ICE 788 to Hamburg - once again. As is almost always late - Wi-Fi is incredibly bad...Where is this supposed to lead? You're ashamed - things are going better all over the world...

We bought 3 super saver tickets, just €280. It's normally a good thing if it weren't for Corona and you can't travel and you can't get accommodation. It probably goes into the salary payments of the board members. That's really a reason to say goodbye to the railway once and for all. Then we'll just drive a car again to protect the environment

Due to a family emergency, I took the train at 8 a.m. and because of the excitement I forgot that my annual ticket is only valid at 9 a.m. When I checked I got a 60 euro penalty ticket. Twice recently I took the train instead of the car. Twice terrible. Prices outrageous, e.g. 25€ for Krefeld - food and back. Solo travelers pay stupidly. Trains are canceled and late. No information at all or totally confusing. The platform displays contradict the ads on and in the train. The internet doesn't help either. Travel time is at least three times longer than by car. In the second case, 6 hours from Krefeld to Amsterdam. I'm glad that I have a car and don't have to rely on this shop.

If I can, I always try to fly. This is faster and cheaper. The prices on the train are unbelievable. Way too expensive for what you get. And nobody needs to talk about punctuality anyway. Even during the week or when there are no holidays, it feels like no train manages to be on time. Unfortunately, there is often no other option as an emergency solution. One should take Japan as an example.
Always technical difficulties or problems. I have taken many trips with Deutsche Bahn. Most of the trips are delayed.

Deutsche Bahn has strict policies in seat reservations and validation of tickets in time and place ... I love to travel with DB including first class seat reservations. During Covid-19 time it keeps me extra security in keeping distance and staying safe. I cannot understand how it is possible (today is just an example!) The employees are almost all unfriendly, there are rarely nice employees, I got a €60 fine even though I had a ticket and money because I was supposedly on the wrong train. Today I (forcibly) took the train again for the first time in over a year. 2 trips there, 2 trips back. Theater, delay or cancellation on ALL FOUR RIDES.
Berlin - Ústí nad Labem, the train journey is pleasant, you can go to the toilet and dining car. Only the price is quite high.

I'll NEVER INVEST A CENT IN DEUTSCHE BAHN AGAIN! I'm really incredibly annoyed by the quality of the employees and the advertised flexibility. Because the alleged customer loyalty does not exist. My request concerns a trip to Vienna. At the time of booking, Vienna was still far from being a risk area. Since this has unfortunately been the case for 2 weeks, my partner and I can no longer travel there for several reasons.1) Is my partner in the risk group with a chronic illness.2) Is it not possible for both of us to not show up at our workplaces due to a 2-week quarantine.3) We don't want to contribute to the spread of COVID-19 and endanger those around us. Next, I spoke to a customer service employee and he understood the situation and suggested that I submit an application To provide goodwill as these are super saver price tickets. I then followed this recommendation. In the application we explicitly mentioned that we did not want to get the money back, but would also like to receive a voucher for the amount. However, this was not addressed at all, but only pointed out that cancellation was not possible. Now I ask you, where does the railway want to retain its customers here? I am aware that this is a super saver ticket and that this is usually not possible, but it is a risk area. Airlines also accommodate their customers there. Why can't you react flexibly in these exceptional cases? Then Deutsche Bahn should keep the €200, but I will therefore never invest money in this company again and will instead switch to the competition with whom I have not had such problems yet. Then I still had a small spark of hope and thought that I would simply go to an information point and explain my concerns in person. I was there on Monday and spoke to an employee. She said to me: “Even if it is a risk area, I can go to Vienna.” Is it really in Deutsche Bahn’s interest that your customers act irresponsibly? I'm wondering if you and your employees are taking the situation seriously? I was also told that I could drive to one of the stopovers. I just don't want to spend 4 days in Nuremberg and Co. My needs were not taken into account at all. Finally, I was told that it was basically my own fault because during Corona times you should book the saver price and I could then cancel it. Why is the super savings price being offered? I even wrote to the complaint management, but they don't respond at all. The customers are simply left alone, but still receive a lot of tax money. Conclusion: THAT WAS THE LAST TIME AFTER COUNTLESS DISAPPOINTMENTS!

The worst trip ever,never on time,like an hour to two hours late,not reliable. They give u connections that looks possible until u are on the train and the delays starts. Zero star for me Took a 19 hour train to arrive at 23,now I will arrive at 5 in the morning No apology no nothing,bye my flight ticket SHAME

In the middle of the night, emails arrive saying that the booked trip cannot be started. The lady on the phone in the service center couldn't help either. She doesn't know why the trip isn't taking place. Incorrect information again in the railway's reply. And then the train is canceled at the platform 2 minutes before the start of the journey with the message "we're sorry". Very humorous. Standing at a train station in a small town at 7 a.m. on a Sunday and not knowing how to move forward. Broadcast national railway. Sensational service.

A couple we were friends with decided to visit the musical “The Lion King” in Hamburg in January. For ecological reasons we decided not to go by car, but instead on May 16th. - May 18th, 2020 with Deutsche Bahn. Then Corona came! The musical was canceled and postponed until later. The railway informed us that we can rebook our tickets, but we have to use them by October 31st, 2020 at the latest. In the letter (e-mail) I informed the railway at the time that there was a high-risk patient among the passengers and that a postponement to a much later date would seem to make more sense to us, especially since it was recommended by a doctor. This was rejected. So we decided to rebook to October 3rd, 2020. Now the musical was canceled again. The Corona numbers, especially in Hamburg, are increasing and I asked the train again (e-mail) for a customer-friendly rebooking. This was rejected! If we had planned the trip by car, everything wouldn't have been a problem because everything would have had to be canceled or rebooked. I'm also really disappointed, almost angry, because I/we are subsidizing the train with my/our tax money. As part of Corona, more payments will flow to the railway and yet the railway does not see the need to respond to customers. We will now start the journey in October, otherwise € 580 would be wasted. But it will definitely have been the last journey by train!! I am sorry for this because it would be a necessary alternative for our environment, but with such business conduct, *Deutsche Bahn* no longer has a right to exist from my side! I even assume to you that that you are currently supporting the spread of the pandemic with such behavior and are even consciously accepting physical harm, otherwise we would not go on the trip.

We planned to spend this weekend at the North Sea. Bought the tickets online from Deutsche Bahn, but booked the hotel directly.
