It's not our decision????The totally annoyed employee simply snapped at my girlfriend that she was so unreasonable as to want to travel when the travel warning was issued!!! They no longer offer goodwill regulations, simply outrageous!!! They receive funding from the state, collect money from customers, and with the incredibly high prices they offer terrible service!!!! I'm so disappointed!!!!
They are Embarrassment.   They know they are always late but still give you connections that you cant make.    What freakin joke.   No accountability.  Its the worst train service in world!.

DB must learn how to respect the foreign customers! Who bought a ticket for a canceled ride during the Coronavirus couldn't ask for a refund. Worst company ever!

I have already been disappointed too often in the run-up to it!

I regularly travel to business meetings with the DB ICE and there are also regular problems with the seats in 1st class - as was the case this time in car 37 from Hanover to Cologne: The seats are very uncomfortable because of the crooked backrest and this time the backrest angle cannot be adjusted. Connecting train recommended & noted - getting connecting train: of course not, information desk is slower than any online self-help including 45 minutes. Drunk people and drug junkies at the train station in the evening - wonderful

On August 30th with Ice 1005 from Berlin to Nuremberg, no information in the app or email that the train booked online does not stop in Nuremberg, no announcement, no information anywhere. 4 hours became 9 hours of travel time to Munich. The last, very last, most incompetent, overpriced club in Germany.

I contacted the Italian DB staff, who were rude and unprofessional. I tried to contact Germany, either they don't answer or you find staff who don't speak English. My train tickets purchased on their site never arrived, I find it unprofessional to compulsorily send the tickets by ordinary mail. Shame on you.

1) Ticket supplements unclearWe booked a online ticket via Deutsche Bahn from Hamburg to Amsterdam, and the tickets travelplan told us everything we needed to know. Yet the ticket said in very unclear washy language that sometimes a supplement is necessary, at the bottom of the ticket. So we had to pay a fine on the train. 1. last weekend Munich/Nuremberg: the car numbers are nowhere to be found: how am I supposed to find my reserved seat?2. just now: I'm expecting my husband Nuremberg/Munich: he's texting me: 30 minutes late... Unfortunately, this happens very often

Incredibly bad club. Delays, train cancellations, incompetent information.... And and and... I'm currently really exhausted again.... Künzelsau Berlin, estimated travel time 13 hours. Then just car and plane again, time, money and above all a lot of nerves saved. Many thanks to DB for the experience. I don't know of any company that delivers such unbelievably poor performance for a relatively high price, and has done so for what feels like forever.

A train delay also prevented us from continuing our journey with the required subsequent trains. An urgent appointment could therefore only be continued with a taxi, price: €86.00. Train 706 Munich-Berlin, dining car. Incredibly snotty employees in a Saxon tone tell guests to put their masks on immediately after putting down their coffee cups after drinking. I hereby invite the railway boss to a two-day train trip in Switzerland. There he learns how to travel by train.

The DB is the worst, most outrageous,...actually the shittiest company in Germany. I've been driving a 1 1/4 hour route once a week for 9 years; I can honestly say that punctuality has become a rarity on the railway. It's always been bad, but it's getting worse even though it's more expensive.

The trip itself was quite pleasant. This time I traveled first class with my son because the seats in second class are very uncomfortable and the price was only slightly higher. Normally I am used to polite service staff, but on our trip on August 9th, 2020 from St Pölten to Berlin, departure at 10:32 ICE 92, an employee at the counter in the dining car was so rude and snarky that I lost the desire to eat. This gentleman definitely didn't enjoy his job and shouldn't be working in the service in this manner.

We were traveling to Dresden with a change in Frankfurt. The train is about 3 minutes late in Mannheim, no problem with a transfer time of over 10 minutes. We arrived in Frankfurt 10 minutes late, the other train had strangely left on time. This confirms the suspicion that the delay was caused intentionally because our next train was perhaps overcrowded. I'm really thinking about being denied boarding. Everyone at the info point was very nice. The next train to Dresden only had one seat that could be reserved. The next train arrived in Dresden 2 hours late. It wasn't really clean. Many did not wear masks. The conductors didn't point this out. Ultimately, they are not vicarious agents of the respective state government, but rather have to ensure good transportation.

Had an appointment in Switzerland. Direct connection has failed. Super unfriendly at the information desk. Gives me a connection with 3x changes. Trains are full. Wanted to be in Bern 2 hours earlier. Still arrived too late. As a Swiss who travels around, I often have situations like this with the DB. What a son of a bitch club!
Deutsche Bahn; worst nightmare in my lifetime. Expensive, never been on time, toilets 1st class always locked, unfriendly employees. I changed to driving a car...

I'm actually someone who is always constructive in my criticism, but honestly, you are the biggest German juice shop!!! If you have any signal failures every second move then modernize your network or do something else. My condolences to everyone who has to travel with the German train. With any other company you wouldn't have a single customer left because of the poor service. That's just a joke, especially given the prices you pay. You probably won't do anything anyway, but I wouldn't be surprised. By the way, the DB Navigator app is also completely useless. If you want to buy a ticket, you sometimes come to a page where you can only pay directly without being able to select your BahnCard. Then you have the next problem that you have to go to a dilapidated ticket machine because you first have to get through 7 spiders and then when you pay you find out that the slot for the change doesn't open. By the way, I'm writing this review in the hour that I'm sitting at the train station again and hoping that the next train won't be canceled again. It's a miracle how your company can still survive.  In any case, I will only use the train if I have no alternative. And believe me, a bewitched donkey is a better alternative than you. It doesn't have any signal interference and I'll probably get to my destination quicker.

Incompetent and rude employees both in the Erlangen travel center and on the hotline. Trying to book a trip from Erlangen to the Baltic Sea was an odyssey like I have never experienced before. What this company allows itself to do with its customers can hardly be put into words, only a state-owned company that is kept alive by taxpayers' money can operate like this."Transportation turnaround"??? 25 minutes in the telephone hotline queue and then being thrown out DURING THE CONVERSATION THAT JUST BEGAN... The rest is known: hardly any information, hardly any service, poorly maintained, unkempt trains, unpunctual...

WiFi very unstable. Mostly dirty wagons. I don't even want to start with the toilets. When it comes to checking tickets, they're quick enough ✌🏼. There's probably no staff available to remove the garbage or wipe the weeks' worth of dust!? Absolute disaster!

For certain reasons I always take the train. After I got my BahnCard, I wanted to book a new one online. I would have to log in to do that. After the usual procedure: "unfortunately no match." Too expensive! A journey of about 3 stops 7.50 outrageous! Then you wonder why so many people drive fare

How nice it would be to have (at least) three train journeys in a row without delays or irregularities in the train arrangement, reservations or anything similar. Of course, the train is an alternative for traveling within Germany and is usually priced well, but more reliability and punctuality would be good. We recommend traveling in 1st class.

In contrast to hotels and airlines, from which I have not yet seen any refunds for services not provided, the refunds were credited to the account after just one week (group trip). Since I've been traveling by train again: empty trains, hardly any delays, pretty good. A highlight: EC Munich-Lindau with a double diesel locomotive through the green Allgäu directly to the Lake Constance island (soon to be history). Cheap bike transport, cheaper than a rental bike for a stay of just 2 days.
Since the Corona crisis, the train has been 100% more punctual! With seat reservations, there is enough distance between passengers.

Trip from Cologne to Berlin was 50 minutes late, the place wasn't clean, the table had to be disinfected yourself. On the return journey there was again a considerable delay, no consequences for guests who did not wear a mask, only a warning from the train attendant via announcement!!!!! There is no feeling of safety here in times of Corona.

I tried. 20 years without a car. I have always defended the railway because of the climate. And now... Corona... about full trains and shitty toilets... Unfriendly and no service as always... I'm buying a car this month... luckily I don't have any children (climate and stuff)

Booked trains were no longer offered; After weeks and many emails with requests for refunds without an answer, a voucher arrived with the words: "We hope this has served you!" Emails again with no response; The whole thing has been going on like this since April! Disgusting. Half of the people wear no face mask. Staff asks you to ask the people yourself to wear one. They are like: who the f... Are you talk to the staff if you are bothered. That's first class Ice. Not my taste. I have family. Some of them old I want to protect. So for the next one or two years: buy buy DB

You can get to other European countries quickly and comfortably by plane - and at reasonable prices.

As with my other railway reviews, first a disclaimer.  I'm a huge fan of travelling by train in Europe, and take every opportunity that I can to do that.  As a child growing up in Poland, then for many years by myself, and finally with my family, I’ve taken more train trips than I can remember.  Having said that, I try my best to be objective, and so I do find some negatives with Deutche Bahn.  But, for the most part, DB tries hard to do a good job.My first trip with Deutsche Bahn (called Deutsche Bundesbahn in those days) was in June 1983.  Coming from the relative backwardness of VIA Rail in Ontario, Canada, I was hugely impressed by the InterCity train that I took from Frankfurt to Hannover.  No High-Speed Rail in those days, just a very comfortable ride in First Class, with a delicious, cooked-to-order dinner in the full-service restaurant car.  The Inter City system in West Germany was an intertwined network of half a dozen lines, where cross-platform interchanges between trains coming from different origins several hundred kilometers apart and going to different destinations several hundred kilometers away were a routine that worked like magic.  It’s the first time ever that I experienced less than 10-minute train connections that I could actually rely on.  Since those days, I have travelled on DB trains countless times, observing progress and changes over the decades that weren’t always for the better.Traveling on a DB train today is vastly different than it was back in the early ‘80s.  The biggest change is that Germany is unified now and the entire network underwent a huge investment wave in infrastructure.  Many kilometers of High-Speed lines were built, so the travel times have decreased tremendously.  Journey times between main population centers have been halved.  And it’s not only the tracks that benefited, stations have been renewed or new ones build at a furious pace since the German re-unification.  The new and modernized stations such as Berlin Hauptbahnhof or Dresden Hauptbahnof are a joy to travel through.  And the number of trains and possible travel connections have increased by an order of magnitude, so that it’s possible to organize your trips in many different ways.The trains that were built to support this expansion are modern, comfortable, and pleasing to the eye.  The Inter City Express (ICE) brand has pretty much taken over the long-distance market, with the Inter City network filling in the gaps in the less populous areas.  There are several ICE train types, starting with the original design, the ICE-1.  The current, mass-produced ICE-4, is just the latest, with the ICE-2, ICE-3, ICE-T, and a few other series in between.  All these typically travel at speeds of 230 km/h and more for at least a part of the journey, feature First and Second-Class accommodation, a restaurant, and other areas such as a bar, a family compartment, quite cars, and bicycle space (only on the ICE-4).  I like the ICE fleets; it’s always a joy to get off the plane in Frankfurt and onto a spacious, comfortable ICE for our onward travels.Other train fleets have also benefited from investment in modernization.  The IC product now features the Bombardier TWINDEXX double deck coaches, which are still being delivered in large numbers.  These are prettied-up regional services vehicles, with nicer interiors and seats.  The improvements, however, are countered by lack of a Bistro area.  There is some form of catering available, but I was not able to sample it.  Whatever is there is a far-cry from a formal restaurant car, and even a self-service Bistro option sounds hugely better.  The regional trains as well have been modernized over the last couple of decades, with new EMUs and DMUs, and many, many, many TWINDEXX coaches.There are also new, rebuilt, and refurbished stations to welcome the traveler.  The showcase example is Berlin’s new Hauptbahnhof, the city’s main station.  Opened in 2006, it features five levels, with tracks and platforms on the bottom and top levels.  And, of course, numerous shops plus every conceivable facility for the traveler is there as well.But...  There are cracks in the armor.During my most recent travels by Deutsche Bahn, I perceived a noticeable decline in the quality of the trains and maintenance.  Frequently, components of, or entire bathrooms are locked out-of-service, entrance doors are not working, and the carpeting is well past its replacement time.  This is bad, but coupled with frequent overcrowding, is a big nuisance.  Since DB does not mandate reservations on its long-distance trains, I have experienced conditions where passengers are standing in the entry areas, or occupying the already diminished restaurant seating.  This is clearly the result of much increased ridership, without the accompanying increase in train length/frequency or maintenance effort.  I’m sure DB is happy about the added revenue, but I’m not, after paying the full price for a family of four, and having to go two cars over and wait in a queue for the bathroom, or wait for a table in the restaurant.And speaking of the restaurant, there is good news and bad here as well.  The good news is that on trains that offer gastronomy services, the selections are good, not overly expensive, reasonably tasty and healthy.  However, none of it is cooked on-board.  In the days when I started traveling in Germany by train, every main dish was made from scratch in the restaurant car kitchen.  The food was hot and delicious, and ultimately enjoyable as the scenery passed by.  This kind of experience is still possible, but not on DB trains.  You must travel east, and the best place to get a great meal on board a train restaurant car is in Poland.  PKP InterCity and WARS, it’s catering subsidiary, still make a cooked on-board from scratch culinary experience.At night too, DB has faltered.   After trying to run revamped night train services in the 1990's to the mid 2010's, DB gave up and killed the City Night Line brand altogether at the end of 2016, after first cancelling routes and cutting down on-board services.  Now, I’m a big proponent of night train travel.  It is the best way to cover longer distances in Europe.  While not as comfortable as hotel rooms, night train sleeping cars get you to your destination comfortably, without airports and the ultra-cramped quarters found on-board low-cost airline fleets.  When you combine the cost of a hotel room with an airline ticket, it is often less expensive to travel on a night train, and for me, it’s a fabulous experience to wake-up in a new country, have a hot shower in your compartment, followed by a delicious and copious breakfast, while admiring the passing scenery.  I was very saddened when DB announced the closure of the City Night Line network, but then overjoyed, when OBB, the Austrian Federal Railways, announced creation of a new night train product called Nightjet.  Some of the City Night Line routes were rescued by OBB, and I sampled their excellent services last summer (covered in a different review).And did DB offer something in exchange for their night trains?  Yes, some overnight services using the ICE fleet day trains.  This is definitely not a comfortable solution, just slightly better than a redeye flight in a cramped airplane.This new use of the ICE trainsets points out another issue with today’s DB:  more cookie cutter trains.  It used to be that a variety of train stock existed to provide the various services that Deutsche Bahn offered, from the local, short distance services, to the flagship InterCity services offering greater comfort and luxury.  Now, the trains are becoming very similar.  For example, the IC2 fleet of double deck trains isn’t that much different from the Regional Express (RE) double deck stock used for regional services.  Since there is neither a restaurant nor a bistro on-board the IC2 fleet, the travel experience is not very different.  The ICEs too are becoming more and more similar, as can be evidenced by the current ICE4 and the refurbishments of older ICE trainsets.  For the operator this is an advantage, I suppose, but for me, it’s a step towards making the DB equipment look like airplanes of different airlines, very similar.Despite some of the negatives, I still give DB a pretty high rating.  It’s the best way to get around Germany, period.  As long as things don’t deteriorate further, it should also remain the most pleasant way to see the country.

I am frankly quite shocked to see all the very negative reviews about DB. But really, during our stay we found it wonderful to be able to hop on a train in Regensburg, where we were staying, and easily get to a variety of destinations.  We frequently lamented that this isn't possible in the U.S.!  We used DB to get back and forth to Munich, Nuremberg, over to Plattling (to transfer onto the Waldbahn), to Passau, down to Salzburg, up to Leipzig, took an ICE from Halle/Saale to Regensburg, and my husband went to Innsbruck and back for work.  No trains were cancelled, a few were a little bit late, but never so much so as to miss a connection.  Our experience was that when only a 3-5 minute transfer was allowed as part of the trip, it was usually at a smaller station with five or fewer platforms, making a quick transfer possible.  For a family I definitely recommend the Bayern Ticket.  We were able to get very good ticket rates for our family of two adults and two children by leaving after 9:00 AM and you are not locked into a specific return train.  The Bayern Ticket also extends to non-rail transit in some of the cities that DB serves.  For instance in Passau we were able to use the Bayern Ticket we had taken the train with, to also ride a shuttle bus up to Veste Oberhaus and back.  The DB website is fairly user friendly to book through.  My husband also had the app on his phone.  Our "ticket" was often a QR code the conductors would scan. It's also possible to get tickets on the spot at train station kiosks or even on the trains.  For longer trips it is desirable to book ahead so that you are guaranteed a seat vs. standing.  Again, I'm puzzled by all the irate reviews.  We were so glad to be somewhere that we could so easily travel and sight see without renting a car.  Any inconveniences were of the minimal variety.  I fully anticipate using DB during any and all future trips to Germany!

The announcements here are almost only made in German and something else, which is perhaps 20% English/50% indefinable and 30% German (sänk ju vor träwelling wis Deutsche Bahn). At first he may not know where he is going, as there may be no information about replacement rail services, diversions or construction sites. In addition, a train journey in this country is so expensive that the average German earner has to think three times about whether he can afford the journey. I don't want to imply that all Indonesians are poor, but they would still be shocked. As far as the food on the long-distance trains is concerned, it is of course grossly overpriced, but it also tastes like the cheapest crackers from Netto. There's no point in sprinkling flour over burnt spots on pastries. My grandma also tried this with cakes, no, no, it doesn't help, you can taste the burnt stuff (sorry grandma, love you). At Deutsche Bahn, punctuality is always a matter of luck. Before every trip to the airport, my husband and I discuss how much time we should allow for the train so that we don't miss the flight. It's the same thing every time... You can't lump the staff together, some of them just do their job and some people are really very friendly. It's like that everywhere. At least I never go on the regional trains without my Sagrotan because the seats are disgusting, the floor sticks quite often and I never actually go to the toilet. Once I had a bladder infection and couldn't help it. What can I say, I survived it...As far as air conditioning and heating are concerned: It's no secret that it's catastrophic and in the summer it's really torture. You pay 30 peeps to drive from Aachen to Aldekerk and the DB can't even invest in sensible technology anymore. I have a dear friend, Kevin, who is a SHK master and would like to take care of it with his colleagues. I'm happy to mediate. I would say that I speak very good British English and offer to speak the announcements so that foreign tourists know where they are going. To be honest, DB, I want to contribute so much to environmental protection and travel a lot by train, but you really don't make it easy. So, now I'm going to go to the train station and pick up my brother. There was information about rail replacement services, but from where and how long that would take was nowhere to be found. But he'll definitely be here by Christmas. As you can see, I wrote the whole thing with a bit of humor and irony and the comparison can't be made 1 to 1, but the core of the matter should have been addressed. It's just the value for money that makes me angry. How can you charge so much money for tardiness, uncleanliness and a lack of information about construction sites etc.? Cheers...

I mainly use the train for work for distances between 150 and 500km, including driving cars and flying over them. First of all, there is a basic rule: if possible, don't change trains. A lot of time can be wasted here, especially if the transfer times are short. Otherwise, I can use the train journeys - usually in first class - ideally for many activities that I wouldn't otherwise be able to do. Since I always arrive the evening before for my professional appointments that are in the above-mentioned distances, it doesn't really matter to me whether the train is an hour or two late. Nevertheless, it hasn't escaped my attention that the train was ruined in the Mehdorn era with the crazy IPO plans between 2000 and 2009 (very bad when this unsuitable board of directors still knows everything better today). I know that the employees suffer the most from this and I generally refrain from commenting here; They can't be blamed for the delays and similar annoyances such as the failure of air conditioning systems.
One of my absolute worst travel experiences ever. Spent 125 euros from Salzburg to Munich. $125 didn’t even get me a seat. One and a half hours standing. Most rude staff even. Never again.

This is by far the worst transport company I ever encountered in my entire travel. It’s all about the staff attitude. The most rude I ever met. As soon as you ask questions, he will respond to you by yelling and insult you for unknown reason. He’s a driver by the way. No sympathy whatsoever. We were a family traveling from Zurich to Munich for a day. That means, we supposed to take the bus on the same day for return. We were denied boarding because we could not provide car seat for our almost 3 year old baby. That’s understandable because it’s their rules. However, the way they treated us and the other family with the same case, was just way too much. They ended up laughing as they were about to leave and we were left at the station. What a shame. We couldn’t get any information from the drivers or anyone from the bus station because everyone seems the same, all rude. Our hotel somehow provided us some information but it wasn’t enough though. If you can, try to look for other options. Swiss transport is still the best so far. I highly recommend SBB.

Today I was on the way to the train with my bike and my hibiscus pumpkin. I had to hurry because I was dawdling at home. I only transported the pumpkin in a paper bag which of course tore. My pumpkin rolled onto the street, but don't worry, I was able to save it! All sweaty from the grass, with the pumpkin under my arm, I arrived at the station and lo and behold, luckily! The train was, as always, 5 minutes late, so I still got my train despite the pumpkin accident. Thanks!
Really really bad transport.For my opinion this is the worst public transport in Europe. Allawys late also the cancellation of the train happen more often in one single day.

Already more than 10 minutes late at Aachen station, and that alone made me arrive at my destination 2 hours late at my destination in Austria. In Cologne, I encountered the most unpleasant conductor possible! the train, I am told that there is going to be AGAIN a delay (more than 1/2 hour) and that it is better if I stay on this train until Cologne and from there, take my connection to Aachen. I paid for a reservation for my 2 trips (10€ each time), and I did not benefit from the service! It is good because I am obliged to take these trains that I do so, but I would have the choice, it would not would be more my priority with the DB!

There is only one assessment for Deutsche Bahn - catastrophic!!! I drove from Zurich to Stuttgart today. Every connection (4) was delayed or canceled - no announcements - no information - no waiting for the connections - dirty trains (1st class). I would be ashamed. This is certainly not an advertisement for Germany. If you still want to go to Germany, take the car. After all, you will most likely experience a traffic jam.

As a BahnCard 100 owner, I use the train very regularly and have unfortunately noticed that problems are becoming more and more common on long-distance transport. In the last few months I have often used regional transport for work reasons - things are usually better here in terms of punctuality, and on some lines there are also quite new cars in which WiFi can also be used. This makes traveling by train more fun again.

We are in 1st class. We expect to be calm....But this is not the case. Noises, smells and phone calls (We are right next to the catering area - see photo - and the automatic door does not close). In addition, see photo, the luggage space above our head is squatted by I don't know which traveler....

take...The delays/failures of the DB are taking on proportions that are no longer acceptable in any way. I regularly drive a route that has a standard journey time of 3 hours, in the last few months my journey time has increased to 5 hours to 6 hours every time without exception. Such a situation is an absolute catastrophe when you consider that the train is supposed to be an environmentally friendly alternative to driving in the long term!! Unreasonable!

You are just making a fool of yourself!!! Unfortunately, I have NEVER been able to enjoy a train journey with the DB without having to get upset about the issue of punctuality. You wait 67 minutes for another train to take the staff??? Come on really???!!!

You pay for a seat but some people, for some unexplained reason do not get allocated a seat. It is therefore a total lottery whether your seat will eventually be taken by someone that has a reserved seat. This leads an abundance of people being forced to sit on the ground, I had to do this for 4 hours as they overbooked the train by a lot. Bizarre for a developed country like Germany! Would never, ever book again
Always late, sometimes entire trains are canceled, no comfort, unfriendly staff, overpriced tickets. No value for money
Deutsche Bahn - always always delays! No comfort and not very cheap. For such prices you expect at least on-time arrival, which is always impossible with DB!

I have seen Soviet train service, and even then I have not witnessed the total dusregard for customer service I recurrently see with DB. After having lived in Portugal, France and the UK, I can safely say that only in India have I seen these levels of bad service. Two points in case (among many):• Yesterday I had an American friend stay over in Hamburg, and then travel to Berlin to catch a flight there. Her ICE train got cancelled, and the station didn't even bother to announce it (luckily for her I was checking the DB app). When she went to ask for a refund and a new ticket, she was handed a form in German and no help whatsoever from the Harburg Banhof staff tat begrudgingly handed it. No warning for a cancellation, no immediate refund and a bad attitude?! Are you guys kidding?! And on top of that, the new train arrived in the wrong lane. The loudspeaker eventually announced it, everybody boarded - and five minutes later, everyone was told to get out of the train and catch another that had just arrived in the previous lane. This is the absurd incompetence that a foreigner is greeted with on her very first experience with German trains - and both her and I are huge fans of Germany and German culture!• Just now, on my way to the Hamburg Flughafen, two ticket masters walked in and very rudely asked for everyone's tickets. One pregnant Polish lady, struggling to understand, was shouted at. When she eventually produced the ticket, the ticket master shouted at her that she was lucky he even allowed her to be in that train. She was speechless, and he walked on, still shouting that only he decided who travels and who doesn't. These are just the two most recent examples of daily abuse and disregard I witness from DB staff to their customers. Obviously, not all are like that, but the blatant lack of care is not even acceptable in a third world country. Does the management simply not give a damn? Do you people realize that your passengers actually pay your salaries and allow you to exist? Shame on you! I have never written an angry review in my life, and it's sad that DB has to be the first one.
Delays on the same routes every day. Same thing every time. The DB has a lack of organization.

I bought my ticket online and downloaded the PDF. The controller still counted me as "Schwarzfahrer" (riding illegally) even though I have the ticket with my name on it and I have my ID with me. I went to complain and they told me it is the way it is, I have to print my ELECTRONIC ticket on paper for it to be valid, I was like, you guys serious? it is right here in PDF. What difference does it make whether it is on PDF or on paper? There is the QR code and everything. Best part of it all? I still had to pay the 7 Euro forgiveness fee even though I was not in the wrong. avoid buying the online ticket, just print it, and make sure to kill more trees in the process. And people still ask me why I insist on riding my bike even if it is a storm outside.

Without having read any reviews and thinking that German trains were the envy of the world we booked tickets for 6 of us (3 adults and 3 children) with Deutsche Bahn to travel from Bruges to Munich from where we travelling onwards to ZagrebWe travelled on Belgian Railways from Bruges to Brussels-North and all was well on our first leg. On arrival in Brussels we were told that our next train to Frankfurt Airport had been cancelled. The staff member from Belgian Railways said that we would need to catch a train to Welkenraedt and get off at Verviers-Central where buses would be waiting to take us to Aachen.The train to Verviers was really full with all of the additional passengers from the cancelled train so my wife and I had to stand for the duration of the journey. Whilst on the train to Verviers we both tried calling the Deutsche Bahn customer service helpline. A man took my details and said he’d need to speak to a colleague and then left me on hold for 30 minutes. In the end I gave up on the call. On arrival in Verviers we proceeded to the overcrowded buses where once again I had to stand for 30-40 minute bus journey to Aachen. On arrival in Aachen it was chaos in the station. There were two people trying to assist the tens if not hundreds of passengers stranded by the cancelled train. We managed to get details of trains to Munich and caught a regional service to Cologne. This was due to arrive in time for the next to train to Munich but was late arriving in Cologne and therefore we missed the next onward train. I went to the Customer Service Centre in Cologne. I explained that we were due to catch the train from Munich to Zagreb and that we were going to miss it. She said that on arrival in Munich we should attend the Customer Service Centre who would give us hotel vouchers as we wouldn’t be able to make our train. She told us which train to catch which left just before 8pm. We were due to be in Munich for 21:10!Our train eventually arrived in Munich in the early hours at approximately 1:30. We visited the Customer Service Centre just before it closed, and we were given a cancellation form/notice. However, there was no mention of hotel vouchers or how we were to get to Zagreb. Luckily we had already decided to book a Flixbus to Zagreb.Although we ultimately arrived on Deutsche Bahn trains in Munich it was over 4 hours after we were supposed to, and it was well after midnight. We were unable to use the tickets and seat reservations that we had paid for from Bruges to Munich. Due to our late arrival we were unable to use our tickets from Munich to Zagreb and finally we had to pay for Flixbus tickets to get us to our onward destination which cost so we have been financially inconvenienced by nearly €1000.At no point throughout were we offered any assistance or guidance by Deutsche Bahn staff on what we should do next. We were travelling for 12 hours and not once were we offered any food or drink or even somewhere to site. It was a massive disappointment and we were massively inconvenienced but nobody from Deutsche Bahn seemed to care.

After all, an ICE is a must-have if you want to move between several cities within Germany. You can reserve a seat and have a comfortable journey. Also, if your ride is long, if you sit in first class, they will bring you beer from the cafeteria. By the way, I'm surprised that the prices of coffee and beer are not that different.

Bad luck, 1 hour late on the outward journey, late for the appointment, train canceled on the return journey, stranded at night. The staff doesn't care that "you can't get anywhere today, you'll just have to interrupt your trip". Unfortunately, I had important appointments the next morning so I had to take a taxi!!! 436 €!!! “You get 25% of your ticket price back” - a nice consolation. Hands off the sh... club!!!!DB - Just a shadow of yourself!!!!Unpunctual, unreliable, extremely dirty and unfriendly!!!! And proud prices for that...

Here I rate the ICE route Berlin-Munich. The train was on time and things were going really quickly with the newly opened route. This time I was lucky and got a saver price. Unfortunately you rarely get it and otherwise it's just too expensive and I stick with the bus. The overhead compartments are also a disaster. Simply too small, you're lost with just one suitcase.

Catastrophic. A trip that we had been saving for forever was not possible thanks to Deutsche Bahn. Train delayed by 50 minutes!!!! The train started in Hanover and didn't manage to be on time in Herford for 100km. I will never trust the train again. I won't even capitalize them.

My wife and I treated ourselves to a first class ride from Hanover to Düsseldorf and back because the journey by car seemed too stressful for us. Unfortunately, I had to realize that the carriages were all open-plan compartments and, even though it was an ICE, they were very run down. Torn pillows, endless dirt, unmotivated staff and, last but not least, a 15-minute delay on the way put the crown on the whole thing. I decided that I would rather have a little more money to invest (the train journey was also very expensive.) and rather to take a plane. The DB will soon be able to do this at this level; other countries (Spain with the Alvia) can do much better.

Today I drove from Berlin with a change in Hanover to the IC to Amsterdam. OK, the on-board restaurant was closed, but the train arrived in Hanover on time. However, my booking was at an end. The DB app ignored this, as did the conductor, and so did the train announcement. On the platform in Hanover? There's no train. Checked the timetable on the noticeboard - everything was correct. Announcement? None. Accessing the Bundesbahn's WiFi is not possible. For information in the train station - queued - defended place in line. Employee? I shouldn't get upset, be very nice, or she won't talk to me. Then the confirmation - there is no train because there is construction work abroad. (but the train also comes from Berlin and goes to Venlo on German soil) But it's none of the employee's business. They also have no customer orientation.
Train arrives 8 minutes late, next to my seat: red bull can! Impudence! I didn't pay for it, 3 stars because I arrived at my destination!

Changing the station 15 minutes before departure is a no go. Every other train company can do this better. Never again Deutsche Bahn! No staff to explain things. Hectic and panic among the passengers is inevitable.

I moved to Germany a year ago. Since then, I don't exaggerate when I say about half of the trains I was meant to use were either more than 15 minutes late or cancelled. But the worst experience I had by far was today.My wife and I had booked a train from Frankfurt to Amsterdam. The day before departure, my wife checks the train status. To her surprise, it was written as cancelled; but we never received any notice, neither by phone, by mail or anything. We called DB and an alternative route was given to us, including reservations, and ultimately we would get in the train we were meant to take in Frankfurt, that was now departing from Köln.At our arrival in Köln, first disappointment (no surprise though): this train is said to be 25 minutes late. Whatever, we just wait... until a few minutes before said departure time, the train is purely and simply cancelled. And not only that, but nobody, nothing hints us an alternative route. Simply the voice saying we can take another train to Dortmund... But no hint on how to go to Amsterdam anymore.Awful and shameless national railways.

Devastating, the woman at the counter at the Freising train station was just busy with her cell phone and didn't want to give me any information. I should take a route timetable from the régal, everything I need is there. When I was told that I didn't know anything about it and that I would like to know when and which S-Bahn or train I should take and how much it would cost, the same message came as at the beginning. With such employees and such service, you shouldn't be surprised that there are still so many people who prefer to drive. For me personally it's done today, I'll go by car.

Passau to Munich. We had booked a ticket online. We took an earlier train than originally planned - without any problems. Later in the holiday we had booked a ticket with seat reservations from Munich to Berlin. The train was a little late but otherwise everything went fine. We like to travel with DB again.

We were to leave from Cologne at app. 1.00pm. At 1.55pm we were still sitting at the station. A train attendant advices us that we should leave that train and take the train behind as that train would get to the airport earlier. Following his advice we boarded the train as instructed only to find that this train also was delayed as well. In total we arrived at the airport 102 minutes late. Just late enough to be unable to check our luggage. At the airport DB office we were told that we would be entitled to compensation. Having started the process on our return home several letters were received from DB 2 of which asked for the same items. Although all the information was sent they continue sending request for the same information. Having phoned them to point out that all the information had been submitted I was told that nothing else was required. Nothing is done via email as part of their delay tactics is the use of snail mail. So far the time taken to get to the end is 13 weeks. I finally get a response to say that train delays are difficult to avoid in a complex rail network. No compensation is payable. Perhaps DB might like to take advice from Japan Rail as they seem to be able to run a complex rail network. On time every time. Having used DB numerous times I am totally disappointed and try to avoid wherever possible.

I really don't know of any company or institution with comparable substandard performance and constant failure to achieve goals. Everything is better than Deutsche Bahn (including all of its opaque companies, especially network operations). Even plague and cholera are more pleasant companions than these total failures!

If you purchase a 1st class travel, you are not guaranteed a seat and won’t get a refund if a seat isn’t available.  If there are current changes in your route the DB app will not notify you. Toilets at stations cost you 1 euro.

We travelled from Berlin - Dresden (& return) in mid June.The trains were on time, both times. Thankfully we had reserved our seats, I would recommend doing this every time. The train was full, people were moaning....no surprise there! The seats were quite comfortable with charging stations for phones/laptops etc. The toilet was not overly clean, but not unusable. The dining cart was reasonably priced, we grabbed a couple of beers.

I traveled to different cities several times with the Lower Saxony summer holiday ticket and realized that it couldn't have gone better. For €33 you can use regional transport in Lower Saxony, Bremen and Hamburg main station throughout the summer holidays. An unbeatable cheap offer! My trains were never more than 15 minutes late except for one time and I think that's a good rate for 5 trips there and back. As a "leisure traveler", I wasn't so concerned about punctuality to the minute as much as it was about seeing a lot of the country cheaply. But I think even with a large network it is definitely normal for delays to occur. For the price, the offer is unbeatable anyway, and every young person should take advantage of it as long as they can. I like taking the train, I've had good experiences with it before and it's usually very stress-free and environmentally friendly. Thank you dear Bahn for this great summer!

I'm currently sitting on the ICE1005 from Berlin to Munich. Expected delay of 45 minutes due to signal box malfunction. It's a joke. I don't need a sprinter on an incredibly expensive railway line. And the air conditioning in the back of the train failed. Just plain creepy.

On a trip on the ICE train from Amsterdam to Duisburg. Carriage 38 shut down. No aircon. Seats taped closed. All passengers for 1st class seats had to move to second class or the next first class carriage where the seats were already  reserved. Fun in a hot afternoon. Wasn’t their fault of course, an act of god. Probably best to be aware of what can happen on the Deutsche Bahn. You might not get what you paid for.

For many years I have travelled by train in Germany but over the past 2 years it has become worse and worse. Last week I travelled long distance twice. Both times 1st class wagons were closed without announcements, seat reservations were cancelled, no help with finding new seats. Incredible delays, no air-condition, no internet and no seats, cancelled trains and even the conductor was refusing to apologise as he had had enough as train was overbooked again. Food not available from restaurant.  Train personnel avoiding customers which I do understand. What has happened to service, decent equipment and simply a train systems  which functions. I have no choice but am dreading my next trip as I have given up arriving in time and having access to my reserved seat.

It was with much trepidation that we decided to travel on DB, in August, after reading some of these awful reviews.  However, our experience was very good!  The trains were all on time or at most just a few minutes late; nothing problematic. These were our routes/notes...we purchased all tix in advance via the website, from the US (sparpreis, first class, which includes seats):1. Prague to Berlin- starts as Czech RR (Ceske Drahy) and changes to DB staff at the German border. This was the only route that was a little behind schedule, by just 10 minutes.2. Kiel to Hamburg - very easy, short trip and no seat assignments for this.  I asked the helpful DB fellow at the Kiel info booth if we could take an earlier train than we booked and that was allowed with no ticket change. We simply got on the train we wanted.3. Hamburg to Hannover- another short trip, but the ICE train was quite nice and clean and comfortable and had air con and car attendants. Even in August on the travel day there were still 1st class seats available.4. Hannover to Frankfurt - also an ICE train and very clean/comfortable with ac and a car attendant. There were also several 1st class seats still available for this route on the day.96% of announcements and signage are in German Really any negative was our own fault - entering wrong cars with our luggage and then having to fret a moment about getting to the right car and our seats. Honestly if I hadn’t read all these bad reviews I think we’d have done better!! But we were so worried about having no car/no seats that we panicked a little on each run, only to NEVER have any problems. It was only our inexperience with trains at all and by our last trip we’d finally figured out how to get onto the right car immediately:), as indicated by our ticket and the signage on the platform.Ok, you might say well things were good because you had first class. Well no, the trains were still on time and there were seats to be had in all cars and I felt like just being about 30 minutes early to each station and taking time to read/understand the layout and platform assignments made all the difference (yes, platforms can change, but it is noted on signs). Also making sure you have a long enough connection will make DB train travel much more pleasant (on the web you can extend your connection time to whatever you want it to be, as long as there are other trains going to your destination).I also put the DB app on my phone and all our tickets were available in (mostly) English. The app shows the train car configuration at the station and along with the platform signage it was easy to stand at the right place for our car/seats.  Also handy for maps and S-bahn/U-bahn in all the cities we were in.Yes DB is a massive system and of course there are likely to be issues sometimes but I would definitely rely on DB again!!

Deutsche Bahn is simply an embarrassing impudence... Compared to other European countries, it may still be reasonable to charge such prices in a country like Germany, but here too we have long since moved beyond good and bad when it comes to delays. But the comparison gets much worse internationally. The best examples of this are Japan and China, where the respective countries have sovereignty over the route network and its administration. In China you can easily take the bullet train at 300 things in relation! across the country at affordable prices and arrive at your destination on time. No double seat bookings, proper announcements, both in the local language and in English and no embarrassing DB stammering. Japan not much different. DB is ashamed of you! You are a huge embarrassment to my homeland. Pooh!

August 8, 20191:45AMMy wife and I and I are finally in Leipzig. It took awhile. We started our morning in Amsterdam with plans to fly to Berlin and take a train to Leipzig. But it was not to be. As we were readying our bags I got an email from KLM saying our flight was cancelled. Then another saying we would be rerouted through Luxembourg - but arriving too late for our train to Leipzig. So we booked a DB train instead. It seemed like a good idea at the time.With just one change In Hanover we would arrive just an hour later than our previous plan. Things went smoothly through The Netherlands. At our first stop in Germany at Bad Bentheim (or as we now call it Bad Bad Bentheim) the train stopped at the station. They announced the train would go no further. (Neither did English announcements for the remainder of today’s journey.) Our train too was cancelled! Us and 200 unhappy passengers were tossed out into the rain.We have since found out that most Germans look upon them with a jaundiced eye. The conductor told us that nobody should ride DB in Germany. The conductor! After a three hour wait in Bad Bad Bentheim another train finally appeared. We finally got into Hanover far behind schedule. We missed our connections in Hanover and after two more potential but missed routes to Leipzig, we ended up in Magdeburg. The DB from Hanover to Leipzig fell behind schedule though and we missed the final connection to Leipzig. So off we went from Magdeburg in a taxi with a German-only speaking driver and two other passengers that spoke no English, hoping we would land somewhere in Leipzig. An hour or so later we did. After a bit of a walk, we were at our Leipzig hotel. As I sip my scotch at 1:45AM I’ll leave it to Anthony Bourdain to sum up; "Travel isn’t always pretty. It isn’t always comfortable. Sometimes it hurts, it even breaks your heart. But that’s okay. The journey changes you; it should change you. It leaves marks on your memory, on your consciousness, on your heart, and on your body. You take something with you. Hopefully, you leave something good behind."An Anthony probably would agree, DB REALLY sucks.

The once reliable DB system seems to have broken down. The excellent bahn.de website happily sells you an end-to-end return ticket, but the people running the services fail to match up. Outbound: 2hr30 delay. Homebound: 3hr25 delay - and lots of waiting around on platforms with scant information. Very sad to report. DB staff clearly equally unhappy, and sometimes downright unhelpful and unsympathetic.

Travelled First Class on the ICE650 from Berlin to Cologne and would like to give Deutsche Bahn a thumbs up!  Clean carriage...clean toilets (soap full, spare toilet paper & plenty of hand towels)...pleasant staff.  We had purchased sandwiches prior to departure and were glad of this as the restaurant car was closed, with only a limited drinks service available. One little bit of advice, buy a coffee before boarding as the coffee on board was awful 😝!

A true incredible disaster in the great Germany, we left Frankfurt and upon entering Holland in a remote place it stopped due to failures, they told us after a while that they would leave us at the next station and get ready, with the language barrier we ended up at the Amsterdam airport and from there to the central station who will pay us for the lost time, unfortunate

I have been trying for 4 months to get in touch with customer service to compensate me due to a train delay. The fact that they don't even have an email address to address in such cases is unacceptable. All over the phone and one employee sending me to another to no avail.

We drove from Hamburg to Amsterdam, through Osnabrück and back. On the platform in Hamburg, no one can really explain where the cars stop. Hired migrants in yellow vests are running around, not even speaking German. Everyone in the information pavilion is extinct. When the train arrives, people start running around the platform. There is no Internet in second grade. The stops are crowded with passengers without seats and simply free riders who constantly need to be driven from their seats. There are strange subjects lying around in the vestibule, so you can’t get past. When the controllers appear, the running begins. A half-car buffet with nothing on the menu. A couple of sandwiches and bottled drinks. You can forget about hot food, and there is nowhere to eat since there are passengers sitting everywhere without seats. There is a hubbub, screaming children and passengers, like on a “gypsy” train. On the way from Osnabrück, the air conditioner broke down and it was simply impossible to breathe, and then, half an hour late, in Holland, the train itself died. They offered to get there by train, without even telling us from which route or how. As a result, the nearest train was packed with people like sardines in a can, and there, too, everything was by class. She also stood there for a long time, they said there was a problem, but then we went. We were three hours late. On the way back we were about 40 minutes late; when crossing the border, German policemen wandered around the train for a long time and aimlessly. And this is Germany!? I remember the stall in Osnabrück on the platform. When the Asian girl took the hot dog and napkins, the saleswoman shouted “Ain napkin!” Literally snatched the excess from her. Immediately inspired by old war films.

I was trapped in this old train going from Amsterdam to Berlin  wishing that I had read these reviews before . I planned a multi country trip and thought it was going to be more relaxing traveling by train when possible. From London to Amsterdam it was First Class service, and a different company. It was a smooth and great experience With Deutsche Bahn it was not . I bought First Class tickets and when we arrived,at the Amsterdam train station ,they had sent a train without the  car where we were supposed to be seated. Which, by reading here, seems to be a suspiciously frequent occurrence  There was confusion as there were more people than seats. Like 12 extra peopleFirst we were told to grab any sit on First Class.  Later on , we were told that because other people already had those seats reserved to move to second class and just take any seat. Because, apparently, it was OK to inconvenience us and give us bad service, but it was not their problem to find a solution of providing the service that we had paid for .Was I in the mood of an argument, in a foreign country, with a not so friendly employee? Not worth it. The train looked like it had Second Class Premium seats in First Class and Second Class in Second Class. It was a 6 1/2 hr. Trip. As promised on their website...power by the seat. WiFi , Cell Phone signal that would not fade much...were not true.....3 hours into the trip, at a stop some old lady comes into the train and, the icing on the cake, had reserved the seat I was sitting on in Second Class. I swear she was the only soul in that train with a reserved seat in Second Class. So, I had to move again...They gave us a paper to go to customer service once we got to Berlin to “prove” that we were forced out of First Class . Of course, they count on people being tired and not wanting to deal with more incompetent service. And they were right. I just wanted to leave this old, not clean train, with substandard service, behind me. I was almost certain that what they were going to offer, if at all, was some credit. So my advice, if you can, avoid it . If you cannot, don’t waste money on First Class. Chances are high , based on all the similar stories I am reading now, that they will send you to Second Class anyway...and keep your hard earned money at the end.

My mom and I took DB from Mainz to Munich. We paid nearly $100 each for first class tickets. When boarding the train all the first class seats were taken. We asked an attendant for help and she said that because we did not reserve a seat in addition to booking the first class tickets we were not guaranteed a place to sit. She suggested we sit in the dining car, which was also full. We checked other cars outside of first class and they were totally full with no AC (at least first class had AC). Many people with first class tickets, including elderly ladies, ended up standing in the hallways. My mom and I stood the entire 4 hour train trip. Always make sure you have a seat reservation with your booking!
It was unbearably hot at forty degrees and we traveled breathlessly from Frankfurt to Amsterdam, stopping along the way without any explanation.

The doors of the train (RE 4238 from Ravensburg to Ulm on Sunday, August 18th, 2019 at 8:45 p.m.) closed in front of me, although people were still boarding in the front part of the train and the train driver was watching everything. So I ran to the front with my bag and luggage, past a carriage whose doors were out of order. While the train driver, who was leaning out of the window, was watching me, the last passenger in the front part of the train got on and closed the door, but before it was completely closed, I reached it and pressed the door button, but it no longer responded. I waved to the conductor, who was still looking out the train window but didn't react, just ducked his head in. Stressed, I pressed the button again as the train slowly started moving. I couldn't believe it! I am completely stunned and horrified by how rude the train is towards the passengers. The next train (IRE 3053) that I wanted to take was over 20 minutes late, meaning I would miss my connecting train. The railway is simply always disappointing, unreliable and incompetent. Also due to other small things for which the effort to file a complaint is far too great, so that many defects remain unmentioned (such as department doors that do not close tightly and keep banging open and shut during the journey; toilets that are out of order; ticket machines that do not work, etc.) Traveling by train is simply not attractive at all! Now more than ever I will take advantage of alternatives such as FlixBus, blablacar and Facebook MFG groups, which I would also like to recommend to everyone else. Have a good trip (without the train)!

In Italy things work much better, the vaunted German efficiency has completely disappeared from me, even after my stay in Berlin. Never again Germany and DB

Unfortunately spending a lot of time on the country side there is not much of an alternative to traveling with the Deutsche Bahn. Taking the train an hour earlier has become a habit due to spontaneous delays ranging anywhere from 5-45 minutes depending on god knows what. Whether or not these delay notifications are actually accurate is a whole other story. It has become a pleasant yet very rare surprise to have all connections and trains arrive and leave according to plan. Playing on the German cliché of efficiency and punctuality the Deutsche Bahn does not fit the box. My only positive experiences so far has been the bond I’ve created with strangers complaining about how horrible, beyond overpriced and tardy the DB is. Trip from Berlin to Amsterdam. We had booked first class WITH a seat reservation (people who don't do this save 14 Euro p.p. and make a dent!). Legroom and freedom in the coupe is of course OK, although you cannot recline the seats to sleep. Still 3 stars since the NS is only doing worse.

We travelled on an ICE train from Berlin to Amstersam for the firsf time but would never waste our money again! always a negative experience: you definitely can't rely on the German railways - always late, overcrowded trains, outdated rolling stock, inadequate information - so you never get drivers off the road!

unpunctual, disorganized, unreliable...!It's just tedious and the "best" ICE train is just about usable...

The train is ALWAYS really, ALWAYS late! 1h50 late in Berlin, 1h late in Munich, is it that difficult? 2nd class probably hard to bear, first class bad. Staff the only positive.

I made full use of the rail pass to travel within Germany and around cities. ICE is comfortable. Suburban trains are also frequent and convenient. The train journey was very nice.

Rode thrice for intercity transfers and got in IC second class and ICE First Class. Enjoyed rides in ICE First Class! I've only been driving for half a year...I've only been driving with the DB for half a year and I'm already really annoyed by the incompetent bunch. There are elevators but they are not working and locals indicated that they have not worked for some time. If one has mobility problems or, in our case, difficulty in carrying luggage up and down stairs, there is no way to travel to/from Weimar.

Traveling from Berlin to Leipzig or the other way around better make sure to have a seat reservation. (Though might sound like a good idea, but if the train is canceled and you'd have to take another-later one, the seat reservation will be expired). Obviously the staff is handing out more tickets than estimated for the train, so be prepared to be traveling either sitting on the suitcase or not sitting at all. Depending on which route taken that might differ from 1 hour and 10 minutes to almost 2 hours. If you consider to request a 25% refund (legible after 60 minutes delay) you will have to do all communication through mail (the real thing, with post office and stamps and so on) after filling out a form you are to receive on their website together with every inch of information you have. Better to actually be prepared and have the form printed together with your ticket. Because you also need to validate the delay on the train concerned with exactly that personnel.
85% of the trains are either delayed or cancelled. Deutsche Bahn is completely incompetent to operate the railway system. One cannot rely on Deutsche Bahn.

Every long-distance trip I've ever taken with Deutsche Bahn has been an absolute disaster. On public holidays like Ascension Day, it should now be common knowledge that several people are traveling and rely on the train. According to Deutsche Bahn, this is not the case. A construction site that has existed for months is viewed as a sudden and unforeseeable problem. To describe one of the numerous situations: We had to get off in Bernau, supposedly replacement rail transport was to be organized. We were previously sitting in a train with several carriages, and this train was a double-decker - so there were a lot of people on the train. When we arrived in Bernau everyone had to get off, there were no signs, more than a hundred people had to stand in the blazing sun without being sure that a bus would even come. When I asked the train over the phone they said, “The problem is known but we no longer have any buses” - perhaps Deutsche Bahn should have organized more buses from the outset, but no, that's not possible because otherwise they would have to spend money. In addition, this time I, like a few others, had to rely on forearm crutches, which the railway didn't respect. End of the song: Once again we arrived home with a lot of delay and stress, and of course the holiday feeling was completely gone. I really hope that we will at least get our money back from this horror trip. Based on my years of experience, I will now cancel my BahnCard 50. That's not how it works.

We bought first class tickets from Frankfurt to Berlin on an ICE. Although I reserved seats they disappeared a couple of days after booking. I tried in vain via email and phone calls to get seats reserved and was told repeatedly that the train was fully booked. As a result, we had to sit in 2nd class.Not one person at DB could have cared less than they did.Next time I will fly or drive...I recommend you do the same. (Airline tickets are almost the same exact price. We chose the train because we thought the countryside would be nice to see. Instead all I saw was the large sleeping person between me and the window.)

I've already done a lot with the train. That's enough for now: I forgot my ticket and was checked. The inspector said I had 2 weeks to show it. After 8 days I did that. Zack: 60€ - the deadline was only one week. I write to the fare collection staff and send them my ticket and the bank statement that proves that I had paid for the ticket. Then they pass my contact details on to a debt collection agency. Anyone who works on the railway has no soul or has sold it to the devil for hard money. I will cancel my tickets to Budapest today and fly there. Always. I'd rather buy a car than throw a dime down the insatiable throats of these cutthroats.

Berlin-Munich is a very decent DB route and can usually be done in 4-5 hours. This time, a well-known construction site in Berlin Südkreuz extended the journey time to 5 hours, but with a signal box malfunction in Schöneberg, Leipzig and a power car failure of the ICE709 in Erfurt, the accident took its course and ended in an overloaded train. Stress, planning chaos, overwhelmed staff and totally overloaded trains - it seems as if customers for this company simply come unplanned on the weekend. A masterpiece of lack of reliability and necessary infrastructure organization. Of course, the board bistro was almost sold out after 2 hours, but then the microwave exploded. That was the end of the hot meals. All in all, DB has upgraded and invested a lot in comfort in recent years. But most importantly, reliability, is severely lacking. The management seems to have lost control...which is actually a shame: the train is a very attractive means of transport.

Super trains, fast, punctual, nice helpful staff, the stations are organized, I traveled from Munich to Lermoos, I would go on this line anytime, despite several transfers. The quality/value ratio is excellent. Thanks

My wife and I have gone Vienna-Berlin 2/6-19 and ordered 1st class Panorama tickets, which we thought sounded luxurious. Well, the panorama was bad. It was a "quiet coupe" (of course 1st class), but with completely normal windows on the sides. The trip started at 10:15 and around 12:30 we went to the restaurant car for some lunch. It was completely packed with people with luggage, just sitting there with an empty coffee cup or a small bottle of water in front of them. Definitely a way to travel without having to buy seat tickets.  Actually, I think it should be that you can only sit there if you order something to eat! We wouldn't arrive until 6pm, so some food would have been good. Thought we'd buy some sandwiches then, (to balance dinner plates and glasses through two full trolleys is probably a bad idea) Yes, they had a sandwich....ONE!!  So we bought the last sandwich they had and a coke and went back to our "panoramic seats". The carriage was also hot as a sauna with non-existent ventilation. The tickets cost €250. (About SEK 2700) The train was also 20 minutes late. From now on, I choose flights for trips longer than three hours.
Always too late, no real proactive information, overpriced, too busy. Take the Danish railway as an example

If a train is delayed or cancelled no one will inform you what is going onFor example they won’t tell you If there will be another train or not and if there is another train they won’t give you the proper & correct information like telling you what time the next train will be, what platform to go to and which train to go on etcThere Is No Proper Customer ServiceVery Rude, Arrogant, Abusive & Unhelpful Avoid this train company at all coastsI would rather spend a bit more money to fly to my destination.

A delay of over 1 hour was displayed on the display board at Frankfurt Airport long-distance station. Then the train is cancelled. I received customer-unfriendly incorrect information at the DB information desk one floor up. There are also contradictory information about changing trains. Then we didn't receive any information from the conductors on the train because they simply ran away, annoyed by questions from other guests. All you can say is: it couldn't be worse!!

Used to travel from Frankfurt Airport to business destinations. I bought a first class Eurail pass, but I think it's cheaper than flying. It takes time though. I also used it on an excursion around Germany. I checked the itinerary and timetables on the online bahn.de site and reserved seats for the entire trip in advance. For almost the entire section, I specified a window seat in the compartment from the seat map. While traveling, I used the "DB Navigator" app to refer to online tickets and check the scheduled departure time, departure platform, and seat number. However, the boarding position may change, so I checked the display on the platform. You can also check delay information, current location, estimated time of arrival, etc. from the app. DB Navigator is useful. It may be inconvenient that some of the notations cannot be translated into English. Also, I couldn't do Komfort Check-in. Not being able to use the DB lounge was a mistake. The important train journey itself was comfortable. I'm not happy with the fact that the recline is shallow, the headrest tends to stand up, and the seat doesn't rotate, so I sometimes end up sitting in the opposite direction of travel. However, I am reminded once again that Japan's Shinkansen trains are well made. It's fast, doesn't shake, and is clean. I would like to fix the fact that the seats and storage space are small.

I'm absolutely not a train driver, so it's a new experience. Our train (TGV) seemed a bit old-fashioned and wasn't exactly new. Nevertheless, everything worked and it was fascinating to cover the Strasbourg - Paris section non-stop in just under two hours. Thank you SNCF, thank you TGV. The return journey was with DB and ICE. Modern train, great seats, 20 minutes delay on arrival, air conditioning works (everyone had their coats on on the train), toilets completely closed in all carriages (flooding). Thank you Deutsche Bahn, thank you ICE.
I see reviews giving the trains a rough deal. We had no problem at all. Seats were comfortable enough , toilets were clean and staff were helpful.

I'm ashamed of Deutsche Bahn! Current reason, the train has been changed - no more valid reservations, completely overbooked, dirty compartments with damaged seating, no air conditioning...Sooooo embarrassing! No other country has such chaotic conditions.  Not to mention the incompetent and unfriendly staff. Trip: Koblenz to Hamburg on MAY 26, 2019

I'm a 24-year-old student and have been using the German railways regularly for almost a month now because of a part-time job, and I have to say that I didn't expect such planned chaos... People give it a wide berth, no one here knows what's happening with the trains. Planning and overview are zero, cancellations and delays are part of the daily routine, which you simply can't understand at these prices, trains are overrun and dirty, staff are unfriendly or maybe just overworked, travel centers are at the most idiotic times closed, just Laos

Avoid DEUTSCHE BAHN unless no other transport method exists. They do not honour confirmed tickets despite their Website saying otherwise. DB trains- inefficient. German train efficiency is a Myth. As their website stated ‘booked seats was optional and you can travel without these still’, we were prepared to stand. They obviously overbook their trains and only give precedence to seats booked. A two train journey became a 4 train journey with a 3 hr delay.Subsequent DB compensation complaint made. Inefficient antiquated postal only procedure with refunds after much correspondence and 3 months later. This was only finally based upon one delayed train cost and not the whole journey as two separate tickets. This is not fair, as whole journey delayed by them.  Their Customer Service Dept were also informed but could not see anything wrong in us being expelled from the train. Told that the Website information only applies for ‘Standard Journeys’.

Schweinfurt-Würzburg-Essen. The feeder stops directly on the platform opposite the ICE. On time, comfortable, working WiFi, but the interior of the ICE was a bit worn out. If train journeys were the norm, the railway would have a great product.

Well, as opposed to recent reviews, we have travelled on four routes in the last two weeks on the ICE trains, first class and the service and timetabling has been excellent. Today was our final journey between Frankfurt and Paris and again, we arrived in comfort and on time. It was interesting to experience the high speed timetable once we were in France. We would not hesitate to use them again.
I booked a ticket and seat on an ICE train to Hamburg. Fast, comfortable and reliable. With better service it would have been perfect.

I bought a first class ticket plus paid for a specific seat, train IC 722 from Munich to Frankfurt, 16/05 at 9:51 am, it turned out that there was no carriage number 38 that day. Everyone with reservations for this particular carriage stood in a tight squeeze in the corridor in another carriage the entire journey!  It's definitely a pleasure having a ticket for 119 euros and having to stand in the corridor next to the toilet all the way. Strangely enough, the train staff, seeing what was happening, ran to the other end of the train! Of course, I will file an official complaint, but what's the point of complaining when I had to stand the whole way! Good luck with your continued DB!

BE CAREFUL WITH THIS COMPANY. Don’t buy through the website and make sure you receive your ticket at the time of purchase to avoid being scammed.I have bought international train tickets with BAHN and it has been a bad experience.I've bought two tickets from the website on February, but it said that e- ticket where not available so DB would send them by postal mail.The most incredible thing at this point is not that they don’t give you an e-ticket at the time of purchase, or a code with the possibility of printing the tickets on a machine at the same station. It's not that there is not even a BAHN person to help you at the main train station in a country where they provide service. The most incredible thing is that they sent two tickets crossing all the world by postal mail without TRACKING NUMBER, and they don’t even offer you the possibility of paying a little more for it but with the security of being able to know if your tickets are traveling, they were lost , or were delivered at the wrong address.I wrote an email TWO months after my purchase warning them that the tickets didn’t arrive and that it was almost time for me to leave my country and start my trip, and they responded that in that case I would have to buy new tickets locally and then I have to send to "online service" a letter to a post office box explaining the situation.It is interesting that the method that caused the problem is the same method that they propose to solve it, send a postal letter. I want to clarify that all this happened in 2019 and not in 1980.More than 70 days passed since I bought the tickets and left my country and they never arrived. I bought new tickets locally (there was no DB office in the entire Budapest terminal to get more information), and then I sent the tickets attached by email two days BEFORE taking the train.The answer didn’t arrive before I got on the train, I went to another country, then I went to another one, and then I went to another. It was not until I returned home and wrote on social media that they responded to me, saying that I need to send those original used tickets by postal mail. It sounds like a joke, but it's real.Two days before they had the ticket number, the schedule, the time of purchase, the amount I paid, the credit card I used, the QR code, the purchase code and many more data, they even knew in what seats we would sit.At the same time, with almost TWO MONTHS in advance, they had exactly the same information about the tickets that wouldn’t be used because we never received, and they knew which two seats we would NOT sit in.I repeat, it is real that in 2019 with all that I mentioned above, the only solution is to send a used ticket by postal mail, which of course has been lost among so many bus tickets, trains, subway and plane tickets that I used in my vacations and that I deludedly tried to plan with the maximum time in advance? Don’t really have any way to invalidate two tickets that I'm warning so long before they never arrived?It sounds much more like a bureaucratic obstacle than a goodwill to solve the problem.I'm not claiming the lost time during my vacations in which I had to go to a station to buy new tickets, I'm not claiming the calls to the post offices to try to find out if there was any way to track the tickets, I'm not claiming for the lost time writing this message and the many emails to the company. I only ask you to return the money for the tickets that I have never received.

This year in stead of flying to Berlin from Brabant-Holland (600km) I choose travel by train. Booked long in advance 1st class for reasonable price. Quite comfortable, but travel schemes should always be monitored because of maintenance works. DB-app works OK. Restaurant offers reasonable quality food and drinks, simple but practical. If you don't expect too much you'll have quite a relaxed travel. 1st class offers 220v but no USB (yet?). I travelled with IC / ICE.

On Easter Saturday, April 20, 2019, three of us took the ICE via Frankfurt and then took the regional express to Aschaffenburg. The ICE was very punctual and the regional express left 5 minutes later, which wasn't a problem for us. The trains were clean and the staff were very friendly. On April 23, 2019 we drove back the same route, both trains were on time, clean and the staff were very friendly. It was a relaxing journey and I would like to take the train again next time.

So i booked a ticket from a website online and printed it. I sat down on a random seat because my ticket didn't show any seat number.
