We drove from Stuttgart to Munich and 2 weeks later from Munich to Stuttgart again using Rail&Fly. And we were more than satisfied. Totally on time, clean. The seat reservation worked. It was very comfortable and you had WiFi and could charge your mobile devices. There was enough storage space for luggage and plenty of legroom. Also to mention, the toilets were really clean.

I have travelled with Deutsche Bahn for over 30 years and generally the services are fine with comfortable trains used. When the services run to time DB is a joy to use but if there are problems then it can be nightmarish. Automated announcements are multilingual but if there are last minute delays or issues then announcements tend to be in German only which is not helpful for non-Germans speakers. On my latest international journey from Brussels to Koeln Hbf the service whizzed through Belgium using the high-speed lines up to the border at Aachen. From Aachen the train was diverted via Rheydt near Mönchengladbach to Koeln which seemed to take forever. Deutsche Bahn can be comparable to some services in UK which are hit and miss so it is worth factoring in when booking a journey with them.

Booked ticket for "first class" ICE train journey on DB. When train arrived at station (25 mintes late), we couldn't find the car we were supposed to be in. Asked a DB employee  for assistance and was told 9 cars were left off the train. I pointed out we had reserved seats, and was told we would just have to try and find somewhere to sit. Barley got on the train standing in the doorway with our luggage for a 2 1/2 hour journey. Passengers were crowded onto the train sitting in the corridors on the floor, in the boarding stairs and in the space between cars. It was a third-world standard of service.No advance notice of this situation via DB app or email.

The charm of a train station can be debated, but this is where the journey begins. Hamburg Central Station seems to be a place for people with a lot of free time during the day, which could explain the number of non-travelers. Dirty and smelly, so not very charming.ICE Hamburg Munich actually arrives on time, many travelers try to stow their oversized luggage on the train, there are no regulations, the only thing missing is the chickens in cages. Crowding, pushing and irritability. When you finally get to your seat, you have to lower your hygiene standards. It's better not to open the table, because the accumulated dust, dirt and the sticky one-time experience are proof that this table hasn't been cleaned for a long time. Cleanliness at the seat was similar. I won't mention the carpet in detail. Departure and announcement: WiFi doesn't work. By the way, the screens don't work either. Must be a first generation train. Staff semi motivated. An employee even smiles once, probably accidentally. The only advantage: you can get to Würzburg in 4.5 hours. Conclusion: only by train, there is no good alternative. Otherwise the service is uncharming and bland, like the rest.

Apart from the ongoing delays, my wallet was stolen on the night train from Hamburg to Basel. But no one cared about that. I would simply be sent off and told to go to the railway police at the last stop. That's not important enough for you. I also don't feel like working at night, but you could still make a little effort. Never again Deutsche Bahn. I'd rather ride a tricycle!
frequent driver. very dissatisfied. bad company. unfortunately dependent on the train. is clearly getting worse.

When everything clicks it is a great way to travel.  But there seem to be ongoing issues with delays which impact connections.  And I have experienced two different strikes which halted much of the DB service.  On my latest trip I had reserved a window seat in a "quiet car".  What I  got was an obstructed view with two pair of neighbors who talked constantly.   If DB is going to offer these amenities then it needs to deliver them.

We had booked a trip from Cologne to Brussels. Almost as expected, the train was late when it left and it didn't even leave the starting station. So without comparing the data again in advance, you have no chance. However, the decision to counteract the unavailability of space was the best decision ever!  Nice service, delicious breakfast, great time!

At 6 a.m. in the morning there was already an hour delay, no alternative recommendations, no lounges, no service. On the ICE in 1st class, dingy seats, dirty toilets, bad-tempered employees, and all of that for a lot of money. Simply catastrophic!

The German railways make every effort to make traveling by train a nightmare experience. Train cancellations, train delays, train overtaking (even when the train is super full, with thousands of annoyed, late customers), trains being put somewhere else in the last few seconds where previously announced, platforms that have been nothing but a construction site for years (current example platform 1 in Bonn), trains stopping as far as possible from the stairs or elevator, etc... That's stupid, that's provocation, that's sadism! The German railway is Germany's biggest shame.

We were due for a transfer at Mainz to Darmstadt with 10 minutes to get to the same platform.The train was 14 minutes late and despite the conductor reassuring us the next train would wait it did not.When we approached him when we got off the train unable to see our connection he was very smug and disrepectful and gave us no further information. My friend is from Germany so there was no lost in translation problems just lack of communication.We then had to go upstairs to the information booth with two heavy suitcases. The elevator and escalator were both broken when we first arrived, luckily while trying to figure out how to get up the stairs with our 25kg bags the escalator was fixed. The information assistant told us we would have to wait for another hour for the next train, offered no alternatives or apologises.We are now arriving at our destination one hour late, after 9pm at night in the dark and have to call another taxi, very unhappy.We have taken trains all over Europe and this is the first time we have been so disappointed in every way. Disappointing staff, customer service and service.Just changed our next ticket from a ten minute transfer (which seems to be the default they cannot achieve) to a thirty minute transfer (hopefully this will be enough time!). Highly reccommend you give them time to screw it up because they will. We were meant to make it from platform 10 to platform 19 with suitcases in ten minutes... with the train most likely being late for our second train.

I have been travelling to Germany for over 30 years, and have always taken pleasure at using their rail system. I have just been to Berlin and Hannover, and used the trains everyday. SHOCKED is the only word I can think of to sum up my experience. I didn't travel on one train that either departed or arrived on time. We had a full breakdown with very little information given as to how to proceed. The trains were dirty, both outside and in, with uncleared food and drinks detritus. The boards were awash with delayed notices, each one being blamed on the preceding train. We prebooked a first class cabin, and the 'Wagon' had been completely missed off. The schematics on the platforms, informing you as to where to stand for your carriage were almost inevitably wrong (mad dashes down the platform from one end to the other). There was a single customer service receptionist in the Travel Centre who spoke no English, and had to use a Tablet to translate; I know it is in Germany, but really, a non-English speaker (the International language) in the biggest train station, in the Capital city of Germany?This past week has completely changed my perspective on German railways, never again can I say "this wouldn't happen in Germany" when I get a delay back home.I always took DB as the epitome of German efficiency, and a metaphor for what Germany is all about. If it still is, then someone needs to get this business by the scruff of it's neck and bring it back to it's glory days. Perhaps spending German money in Germany, rather than trying to prop up ailing EU partners for political reasons may serve the German population well.

The trains are always late and the staff is awful. I took  ticket but the train was late and I had to reach home so I took another one. I got fine for that while I had a ticket. The staff is condescending and rude particularly because I don't speak German. It is not acceptable to see that.

The Deutsche Bahn ist one of the most embarrassing things in Germany. I use it every day and the chances of it being on time are 50/50. Prepare to loose a lot of free time in its trains. You might not expect this in a country famous for its precision. Well in this case you will be disappointed. Politicians and bad managers mainly developed prestige projects instead of fulfilling the basic requirements of trains: arrive comfortably and on time at your destination.

I take the train about twice a month. Fed up!! I always arrive between 1h30 and 3h later. No comparison to our European neighbors!!! In the future we will face competition such as: Changing Flixbus even if that means being less flexible for me. I've had enough!!!

It's all well and good that a storm disrupts the entire train system, but it should be stated in the app that trains are canceled and not just afterwards. Instead of the train adding another car, most people have to stand all the way to Dresden. It's an outrage and the cost of cats is far too high for such actions that the German railways undertake. No wonder that most people take flixbus to their destinations.
Always LATE at least for 5 minutes, staff is typically RUDE, (especially on Magdeburg hbf). Ticket machines provide UNCLEAR RULES about the ticket validity! Have fun!
As a frequent traveler, my verdict: usually on time, clean and safe. Instead of hatred and malice, maybe try the pitfalls of a car ride or just drive a car. Nobody is forced to use the train.

Almost every time I use DB trains have some problem - delays about 20/30min are the expected and good ones. It's not unusual for trains get cancelled, stop in mid-way, change routes, have to go by bus, etc. Delays over 1 hour are quite usual. Sometimes delays are over 3 hours and you can miss a flight or have to take cab to do it. They don't care at all, and JUST SPEAK GERMAN at speakers and banhofs. That's the problem about monopoly (basically it's only them in Germany). If you have other way to do your trip, do it.
Always late, ALWAYS.If a train is actually on time, they probably fire the person driving the train.
Once again trains are canceled or late. You're lucky if it's only 10 minutes late! What customer service!

I have tickets for the trip and can provide any ticket information if necessary so that this person can be identified. We were in Germany for a few days and no one treated us like that, on the contrary, we were always treated well by everyone. This situation happened at the train station ticket counter, not on the train.
Quick and efficient service from the airport to the centre of Berlin then easy to navigate around the sights on the s/u bahn, tickets great value, 7euros for a day pass.

I regularly travel for work on plane and train. I booked a Super Sparpreis ticket. When I went to board the train earlier today, the scanner let me through (not all passengers the same), thus I assumed it was ok I was taking an earlier train than I had originally booked. When the ticket agent came by, he rudely informed me that I would have to buy an entirely new ticket. He described it just like Ryan Air, that is it is the cheapest and least flexible, etc. therefore, I paid full price for two tickets (not the difference in fares) even though their scanning system gave the green light that my ticket was valid. Zero flexibility. Not polite. Poor communication on terms and conditions. Not impressed Mr. Ferraro from DB. Not to mention there was only one unlocked and functional toliet amongst 5 passenger cars. Use only if you have to, and keep your expectations low for customer service.

One of the worst companies I have ever had the misfortune of having to use but sadly, also the monopoly on public transport here in Germany. Most recent encounters involved displaying platforms incorrectly in the main station, “cleaning” vomit up in a doorway by roping it off, leaving dried vomit on top of a bin so that it was still visible/the smell of it still lingered. Consistently dirty, late and unreliable, but remember to always have the correct ticket or you’ll get fined upwards of €60!

I traveled only on the international route Berlin - Amsterdam, in principle it was normal, the journey took 6 hours 30 minutes, departure and arrival were strictly on schedule, there was no service on the train. I can say that there is something to compare with from European railways, I traveled on Czech and Austrian ones, here are the five-point ratings, where 5 is the best: Austrian 5 Russian 4 + German 4 Czech 4 That's what I'm talking about international destinations, I haven’t traveled on domestic ones. And there, depending on your luck, the trains and carriages are different, and the mood of the employees “walks” in different directions... In all my European trips on trains, people sit on the floor if there are free seats in the carriage, and even with small children, including infants, I don’t understand them...

Long weekend in the snow. Three hours late. Stood in the cold forever. There was no more dinner in the hotel. Back the same. The train simply ended and I had to watch how I got on. Hundreds of people waiting, standing in the aisles etc. I was then informed that the train was allowed to run at 200% capacity!

Despite reading negative reviews, I had high expectations for my travel on DB trains.  Sadly, the reality of German trains is that they were (at least in my case) not on time, dirty, with poor on-board food/drink options, and most of all with disgusting stations (except for Frankfurt Airport) and mediocre first class lounges.I traveled in first class on three different trains, including one long-haul trip using ICE International.Some stations (Hamburg, for example) are simply disgusting in all respects.  Waiting any time at all inside most of the terminals was unpleasant.  The station at Frankfurt Airport (the station for long-distance ICE trains) was the only exception - it was quite nice.Not one of the trains I used departed on time, with delays ranging up to 25 minutes.The interior of the train-sets I traveled on showed their age.  The first class cars had seats and carpeting that were worn, filthy windows, and disgusting lavs.  This in stark contrast to the excellent condition of OBB RailJet and Swiss Rail trains which generally were as clean and comfortable as comparable Japanese trains.The condition of DB trains really became evident on a trip from Munich to Frankfurt.  The car shook and vibrated noisily the entire trip - it was as if the train were in the air experiencing constant "chop".The problem for travelers is that rail is by far the most economical and efficient way to travel around Europe.  My advice is to check schedules and alternatives carefully.  If you have the ability to choose a different carrier (e.g., TGV, Lyria, Thalys, OBB RailJet Business Class, or Swiss Rail) for a particular route, consider a carrier other than Bahn.I was very disappointed with my travel on Bahn IC and ICE trains, and I can't recommend it.

I did short Europe tour two years in a row. Last year was Amsterdam - Antwerp with a day trip to Aachen from Antwerp while this year was Frankfurt - Strasbourg. We moved intercity via DB ICE. Overall experience about DB has been positive even though some things like overcrowding and insufficient luggage space need to be rectified. In particular the train from Mannheim to Frankfurt Airport was so overcrowded we didn't bother to find a seat and just stood near the door so that we can get off the train quickly. It seemed we were not the only people who had the same idea.One thing that I like about DB is kids travel free as long as there are adults accompanying them. So DB was the cheapest way to move intercity in Germany. Otherwise I would have to rent an MPV to fit all in which daily rental costs much more than return tickets for 2 adults.On our trip between Frankfurt and Karlsruhe, en route to Strasbourg, we were given vouchers to claim toys at the buffet car. The kids were happy with the toys even though I would have wished the guy manning the cafe to be more considerate in asking all kids to present themselves to him to claim the toys. One of my kids was sleeping so I don't see the point of waking him up for a toy.

I've used this company for for 17 years! I have horror stories after horror stories about this company! Sadly there is no competitor so they rule in a way that can only be described as disgusting! Even loyal custom means absolutely nothing to this company! I had 15 years worth of Bahn Card Points saved up worth thousands of Euros, I was saving to take my children on a holiday! DB scrapped them over night with no warning to me, when I complained they did absolutely nothing and just claimed "it is so" The staff are also the rudest people you will ever wish to meet, they have zero manners or people skills. I treated myself and my child to a very expensive 1st class ticket due to the journey ahead being 7 hours, we had seat reservations. DB cancelled the train meaning my 8 year old son and me were forced to sit on the floor of a of the next available train for 8 hours which was full to the point nobody could breath! we were trampled for 8 hours by people squeezing through the train! The toilets were all broken and the buffet car out of use! and all for the price of a first class ticket!  This is a regular occurrence for users! I have travelled on trains in India and throughout SE Asia and I can honestly say with all my heart that DB is behind them in terms of customer service and compassion! The trains are modern but what use is a beautiful exterior if the heart is evil and the personality is rotten to the core!Disgusting vile company! I strongly strongly suggest you find an alternative way of travelling across Germany.
