My trips between different cities in Germany are made only with the Deutsche Bahn, ICE, IC for long distances and Regio trains for connections. There are all very clean and well maintained. Fast trains are very fast and reliable. Staff at the station, train contuctor, staff at the Bistro or diningcarriage are allways fiendly, helpfull in case of any doubt and with the propper answer. However, this last year I had bad experience with the scedule, sometimes for more than two hours, whitch was very anoying.Even those experiences in some ocation, Deutsche bahn is the best way to travel in Germany and neighbor countries. It is advisable to buy tickets in advance if you don't travel with Eurail Pass or any other pass.

Excellent experience on German high-speed trains, I used their Ice to go from Frankfurt to Brussels in various sections the speed was 300 kmh, silent praise for the railway network. The train inside was clean and the controllers were courteous. Nice experience.

Is there actually any route that is traveled on time? Basically, something is broken, breaks down, stops, is late... Looking back, I have never been happy with the train and avoid taking connecting trains, especially on long distances. Terrible is all I say 🤬

I find it embarrassing that one of the countries that was the first to operate railways is so incredibly unreliable. There is no shortage of experience. Trains are canceled or late every day. This no longer surprises anyone. This is the most natural reason for coming to work late. Of course there is always a reason for train cancellations. Line disturbances. Staff in traffic jams. Or something is broken on the train. I'm just wondering why does this all work in other countries? The trains are only serviced when they are broken. Speaking of broken... what exactly does the railway imagine if you sit on the train for hours and the toilets are broken, what should you do? Have you also had the situation where you had to get out to find a toilet and wait for another train? It's clear that the VW scandal is bad for Germany's reputation. But anyone who takes the train in Germany every now and then will laugh at the values ​​of reliability and punctuality in Germany. There is nothing that has frustrated my colleagues and friends more in everyday life than the unreliability of the train. In my opinion there should be no monopoly position for DB. It's a joke that long-distance buses were banned until a few years ago because of competition with trains.

Since I was traveling with an infant, I paid the specified price and reserved a family seat (private room). However, when we got on the train, there was another family sitting in our seats... Even though we told them that this was our seat, they just insisted that they had tickets, so we decided to tell the conductor (a young woman) and ask him to confirm. The family had been away for a while, and the train conductor was probably troublesome. In the end, they said, ``There are 5 of us (3 children) and you are 3 (1 child), so we'll give them 4 seats with a table and give you 2 seats with only chairs.'' I couldn't make a reservation on the way there, so it was a regular 4-person seat, so I was hoping that I'd be able to have some fun on the way back. . Why are those of us who have paid the specified fee being pushed to the margins, while those of us who have not paid and are traveling can have a more relaxing time? I can't help but feel angry at this brazen passenger, but I'm also disappointed at Deutsche Bahn's inability to manage the trouble.

First the positive: the friendly service employee made a real effort to explain the preparation time of the currywurst, which was almost 25 minutes. Why it takes 25 minutes to bring the elongated culinary work of art to room temperature is just as hard to understand as is the fact that the lukewarm sausage is pitch black on one side - so at least it must have been in contact with strong heat for a short time, but apparently too long. Unfortunately, the Tortilla Crunchys that were vehemently advertised in the railway newspaper did not find their way from the kitchen to the open-plan car, and the promised spiciness of the dish was replaced by the strong acidity of the red sauce, which can conjure up the sweat of heartburn on the faces of people with delicate stomachs. Conclusion: new quality in the railway kitchen? Not detectable. Even a simple currywurst deserves to be prepared in an edible way.

The only positive thing about the ICE trains is the speed and even that is not that great when you compare it with other countries. With which ones? Yes, Italy for example. There, express trains (Trenitalia and Italo) run through the country at a speed of over 300km and the 600km route from Rome to Milan takes less than 3 hours, while from Rome to Naples you can arrive in just one hour. Their trains are luxurious (especially the private company Italo) and very clean. On the other hand, the ICE that I used had compartments that still had a very annoying and unpleasant smell of smoke. This was unpleasant for me because it made you feel dirty and in fact the train was dirty and the floor carpet was stained and - especially in the corners - very dusty. On the return journey from Lippstadt to Nuremberg I sat in an open compartment and there was no way to stow my suitcase (which was relatively small). It didn't fit above the seat (too tight) and it didn't fit under or between the seats either. I would like to know who the genius was who invented a train that, like all trains, was used for traveling and didn't think about luggage storage options (he was probably paid for this misinvention of the ICE - a shame). In addition, the DB is far too expensive in terms of international comparison and the price-performance ratio (you can travel from Rome to Naples with the luxurious Italo for just 14.90 euros if you book well in advance). In addition, the trains are too full (in Italy, seat reservations from the Intercity upwards are included and a matter of course). Poor Germany.
ICE 849 Düsseldorf HannoverPunctual, clean, and decent service. Seat reservation this time via app. That worked too. Only in this ICE there are few storage options for suitcases.

Today we took the train from Kufstein (Austria) to Mannheim Hbf. This was part of a trip to Kitzbühel where we stayed over New Year's Eve. On the day of departure, January 2nd, 2019, we wanted to travel with the M79074 from Kufstein to Munich at 12:02 and the ICE516 from Munich to Mannheim at 1:28 p.m. The price of the ticket for 2 people was 168.80 euros. Due to snow chaos in Kitzbühel, we were stuck in traffic for over 1.5 hours on the way to Kufstein by car. At 10:45 am, when we had already been stuck in a traffic jam for over 30 minutes due to a traffic accident, I informed Deutsche Bahn that unfortunately I would not be able to make the connection in time. For the route of approx. 37 km from Kitzbühel to Kufstein we planned 2 hours 30 minutes because of the snowfall, with a normal duration of 45 minutes. Mr. Werner, who didn't want to give me his full name, told me that he couldn't help me and that we would have to pay again more than the amount we had already paid for the ticket. A recording of the conversation was consented to. As a frequent customer, I was more than disappointed. Mr. Werner also rejected a credit as a voucher or a discount. The ticket for the connection M79076 at 1:02 p.m. from Kufstein and ICE 594 from Munich Hbf for 2 people cost 191.80 euros. The receipts for all invoices are included. As a frequent customer of Deutsche Bahn, I am disappointed, especially since I have had to wait several times due to delays due to snowfall, among other things. So in the end: zero goodwill, unfriendly customer service and no understanding if you are late due to snow chaos.

New Year's Eve in Berlin, return trip on New Year's morning at 10:50 a.m. The train to Düsseldorf is canceled, everything should take the ICE to Cologne to Hanover, from there the ICE 640 should run, which was originally supposed to leave Berlin according to the plan. Train staff explain the possibility of changing trains in Hanover, but then they suddenly announce that the train is cancelled. Train totally overcrowded, no seat in the booked 1st class. Get off the train in Hanover, after 30 minutes the ad appears: ICE train to Düsseldorf is also canceled there, the next ICE 940 is also canceled. At the information desk it was advised to change the booking to IC 1 hour later, but what was not said was that there was suddenly a replacement train on the platform towards Düsseldorf that the information desk at Hannover HBF didn't even know about! By chance we took this replacement train, but the staff for the on-board bistro wasn't there, so there was no opportunity to buy drinks on the entire journey. Arrived in Bochum 3 hours late. Conclusion: Never again by train, enough is enough! Good thing I still have a car.

ICE 848 Hannover DüsseldorfOn time, seat reservation worked and the compartment was quite quiet and clean. Only the toilet looked really uncomfortable. I would always recommend seat reservations. Simply because the standing space in an ICE is rather limited. The number and size of the suitcase storage options is worth improving.

Rode a DB train for the four and a half hour trip from Graz to Salzburg. The snow and mountain scenery was lovely, but the train and railcars were tired and worn. Service was fine and the train was on time, but the rolling stock didn’t match the premium price.
We travelled with Deutsche Bahn and SNCF to and from Strasbourg and enjoyed the experience.Both trains were on time and the seats were really comfortable.

Today we took the ICE, albeit first class, and were very pleasantly surprised. The train was clean, as was the compartment, and the toilet was still in good condition even after 4 hours. The train staff was very friendly and they even handed out small chocolate bars. The staff in the on-board restaurant were also very personable and service-friendly. And last but not least, after almost 5 hours of driving, we reached our destination before the expected arrival time. So: It has to be praised sometimes!

I have lived in NRW and used the public transport system for three years now so I feel qualified to tell you how much Deutsche Bahn sucks. The busses are constantly late and overcrowded to the point where more than half of the passengers do not get seats. As with most large German companies, customer service doesn't exist and most drivers are rude and entirely un-empathetic. I have no choice but to pay them every six months because I attend Uni. I hate Deutsche Bahn but I am a customer because your government gives me no choice if I want to study here. As with ALL government imposed monopolies (e.g. Telekom), this company is a complete failure.

We did our round trip by train again in November. It started in Wuppertal and ended in Cuxhaven. Overall, everything went well and we almost always found a seat (even without a reservation). Only once on the route from Wuppertal to Cuxhaven were we delayed by 3 hours! With my Bahncard, weekend and cross-country tickets, we traveled quite cheaply!

We did 3 trips ranging from "almost local" to "regional" to "Intercity" and had issues with every one. First one a train change was required but ticket sellers didn't mention it when specifically asked which made me 2 hours late for a pre-booked appointment. The intercity (Frankfurt to Munich first class via ICE) has **NO** luggage storage **AT ALL** unless you want to lift your heavy suitcase over your head!! The conductor was less thank helpful - just told me to move my case but not where to move it to. Lucky for me there was a spare seat. You need to go to a ticket office and get them to print out your "plan" - on the day of travel, otherwise you could be completely wrong.Some trains have messages in English, others don't - oddly enough the "more local" trains had more English than the "more regional". I know we're in Germany and so we shouldn't expect English, but if the local trains can do it, why not the longer distance ones?Trains themselves are clean, comfortable and quiet. 2 out of 3 of ours were on time, the other was delayed by about 5 minutes each way.

I drive around 20,000 km by car every year. Every year I cover around twelve long distances of 500 - 800 km one way. Sometimes by car, sometimes by train, sometimes by plane. Just by car is individual and I have direct flexibility at my destination. With more than two people it gets tight. The costs are the same. I can take a lot of luggage with me - including bicycles. If I get into a traffic jam, it becomes incalculable - sometimes things go wrong in life. A real traffic jam happens to me once or twice a year. Comfort depends on the vehicle. The environment isn't really that great :-(.Just taking the train I have to choose one of the fares on offer. Sometimes a (short-term) BahnCard is worth it. In metropolitan areas I'm immediately flexible. It's sociable with more than one person and there's space if reserved. The costs increase accordingly. I can take a lot of luggage with me - including bicycles. If something happens on the route it becomes incalculable - things sometimes go wrong in life. It happens to me two to three times a year. The comfort depends on the car class. I can go to the bistro at any time on the way. The environment is smiling :-). For the plane alone, the price depends on the time of booking, the travel agency, the booking portal and what else. In metropolitan areas, the airports tend to be far out. It's just as tight with more than one person as it is alone. It doesn't take long either. The costs increase accordingly. I can take luggage with me. If it rains heavily or there is a problem with the undercarriage, things become unpredictable - things sometimes go wrong in life. It happens to me once or twice in five years. Comfort has little significance when it comes to travel time. I get a snack on the way. The environment screams loudly in pain :-((.Long story short - I'm taking the train more and more often. We'll become real friends :-).

Although the Bahncard was canceled immediately after completion (so that I don't forget the cancellation after the year was up), the railway claims that the cancellation was not received and has therefore extended it by a year... they must have really needed it...

It is difficult to judge Deutsche Bahn justly. Quite obviously, a lot of trains do not take the passengers to their destinations punctually. A lot of other trains do that. Some delays are caused for reasons of security. Regional trains are not much better than national ones. Recently it happened to me that I had to travel on a regional train in which one of the toilets was losing water Itself. There was a terrible stench in that compartment and nearby, due to the inundation in the corridor. DB had not even intended to park that waggon in a station and have it repaired. What a cheek!What you can say for sure is that the staff is much more friendly than in the past.

We drove across Germany for years, football Bundesliga away games Hamburg Berlin Cologne Stuttgart and so on, and were always very happy with the train. With the exception of a few delays through no fault of our own, the ICE journeys were all on time and pleasant. Gladly again, although the prices are now sometimes outrageously expensive. The last trip was the train to the flight in December and I was also very satisfied - I'm always looking forward to the currywurst in the on-board bistro :)!!!

We took InterCity Express (ICE) trains from Berlin Südkreuz to Wittenberg, round trip from Wittenberg to Eisenach, from Wittenberg to Vienna, and from Nürnberg back to Berlin.  This does not count S-Bahn trips in Berlin.The trains were on time, clean, and comfortable.  Where we had to change trains, delays were minimal.  We travelled First Class all the way, which gave us comfortable seating.We ate twice in the diner, and have no gripes at all.Thank you, DB.

I liked the trains, they were clean and tidy, there were no delays. I don’t recommend traveling without a reservation on a day off, the train was packed... fortunately we had paid for seats. The coffee was not the most delicious. For children, the controller gives a magazine and a toy. There is a children's compartment. Complete indignation is the luggage storage in BERLIN HBF and navigation at the station. The change machines don't work, there are cameras on different floors, there is absolutely nothing to breathe there. I didn’t like the station; navigation was absolutely inconvenient. You should definitely borrow a lot of things from ÖBB.

I often travel from Basel to Freiburg. Since the train is very often late, I am forced to take the train an hour in advance, so that if it is late, I have to take local transport as an alternative. However, I am convinced that Deutsche Bahn will never get the problem under control.

Due to DB, I missed not one but two trains in Frankfurt in my correspondance for Paris. The first missed train was the connection from Berlin with the TGV for Paris that - according to the personel on the ICE 373 from Berlin - should have waited for the Berlin train which was a few minutes late. The ticket inspector told me not to worry, he said the drivers were communicating. However the TGV for Paris didn’t even wait one minute. And the Berlin train driver didn’t say anything about the delay and the connections while rolling in to the Frankfurt station.After missing the Paris TGV, the Information desk gave me a reservation for a train from Frankfurt West at 18:00 (access only by subway because of construction work) to Karlsruhe to catch a TGV there which would leave for Paris at 19:00. The time was now 17:25. Just when I was about to run off for this connection, the guy in the information told me that before that, I had go to the Ticket Office to get a new seat for the TGV! According to my cue number in the Ticket office I had to wait 30 minutes. The train for Karlsruhe was leaving at 18:00 and of course I didn’t have the time to catch it. Hence I got a reservation for the TGV at 6:58 next morning and had to sleep in a hotel in a double bed with a woman I didn’t  know who was in the same case as me. The voucher reservation for the hotel was made by the personel in the Information desk, they said there were no single rooms. When we arrived at the hotel they said that they had single rooms but it was DB that should have fixed it.This problem could have been solved in such a smoother way. So much stress and frustration could have been avoided if I hadn’t been forced to wait 30 min (with people who were planning trips months ahead) for a seat reservation for the second train just to miss it. Also, the staff in the Ticket office (three masculin sellers sitting side by side, discussing my case in German which I don't understand) were all very unfriendly and arrogant. No excuses, no true effort to solve the situation. I later wrote to Deutsche Bahn to ask them for a refund for the dinner I had to buy in Frankfurt but the only answer I got was that they can't offer more service than this. I will never travel with this company again.

There is no DB journey that hasn’t a problem. At least not the ones I made.Delays, shut wagon, connections missed...And half the speed of the French SNCF!But you know the Peter Principle: the one who messed it up was promoted to the not yet constructed Berlin airport, where he surely failed...Of course, Germany is a bit bigger than Switzerland, and to make the railway function is very complicated; example USA, UK etc., so I give them a star for trying to do their best.

Yesterday (November 23rd, 2018) I took the RE 70 from Frankfurt Hbf (departure 6:12 p.m.) to Mannheim Hbf (arrival 7:19 p.m.), which this time consisted of two connected trains. This trip will remain in my memory and could no longer be surpassed in terms of incompetence, errors and carelessness when it comes to driving safety. I hope that similar cases can be avoided in the future through my criticism. Despite no overtaking maneuvers by other trains, the train to Lampertheim was delayed by 10 minutes, so that connecting trains in Mannheim main station could no longer be reached. This is very annoying, but you have to expect it when you travel with Deutsche Bahn. On the train this time it was different than usual, absolutely no information as to why we were running late. The highlight, however, was the fact that this train will never reach its destination station (Mannheim Hbf.). Shortly before the penultimate stop (Mannheim-Waldhof) it was announced that you should please change to the other train segment. Confusion spread. It was known that the train consisted of two parts, but no one could know whether the front part would move on or the rear part. Ultimately, all passengers get off from both parts of the train. An estimated 150-250 people at a stop called “Bahnhof” Mannheim-Waldhof. Despite a completely overcrowded platform, an ICE train rushed through at full speed on the neighboring track as if out of nowhere. This is absolutely reckless of your company and it was just luck that nothing happened. There was neither a loudspeaker announcement nor a warning signal from the ICE train driver. Absolutely dangerous because people with children also got out. Allowing an express train to pass at full speed on a crowded platform without warning has the potential to find itself in the headlines of a newspaper if someone is pulled onto the track. Then no one wants to know anything again. The conductor of our train got out and the passengers waited for him to tell us which of the two trains would continue. Without saying a word, he ran to the timetable and illuminated it with his flashlight. The information that everyone should go to platform 1, as a train was leaving from there to Mannheim main station in half an hour, caused the crowd to rebel. Protests against the individual employee became widespread as to why the train was not moving any further. We didn't get an answer. Such situations can turn sour very quickly if the wrong passengers take you to a train station without an illuminated timetable - without any help for the travelers who finance the whole thing. Really disappointing. People who didn't know their way around had to wait half an hour in the cold to get one station ahead. This was the most miserable train journey I have ever experienced.

For three years we used the German railways to get from Flughafen Berlin Schönefeld (a/p Schönefeld) to the Berlin Zoologischer Garten station (and in the opposite direction), these were trains - RE7 and RB14. There have never been any complaints about Deutsche Bahn, everything was clearly organized in this complex railway transport “mechanism”: from arrival/departure, information in the schedule and to the purchase of tickets. In the 4th year, an incident occurred: trains from Berlin Zoologischer Garten towards Flughafen Berlin Schönefeld (a/p Schönefeld) were listed on the schedule, but in fact they only went to the station - Berlin Hauptbahnhof. But there was no information about changes in train traffic anywhere! It’s good that we always plan all our trips with a reserve, otherwise we would have missed the plane this time! We had to take a taxi from Berlin Hauptbahnhof to Flughafen Berlin Schönefeld.

Today I dared to have breakfast in the dining car of the German railway. My low expectations were exceeded. The fried egg on my panino had a plastic-like consistency and was simply not edible. Afterwards I tried a few scrambled eggs, which were only slightly better. The best thing was the café, but you can't go wrong there. Too bad...
We had a very pleasant trip to Frankfurt. You often hear about unpunctuality, but in our case the ICE was more than punctual. We will use the DB again.

Saturday Berlin Hamburg with an EC / Czech State Railway from the Czech Republic (Prague-Hamburg) super punctually (only when entering the Hamburg main station there is a 5 minute standstill!! Why?) Sunday with an ICE of the DB back and..... of course late!!! So that all connections at Spandau station are lost and the waiting time is long. How does the train manage - despite being totally free!! Significant delays on the route from HH to Berlin with an ICE?

Never again German train! Small suitcase was packed normally on the luggage rack. If there is a jolt, it falls down and hits a passenger. Deutsche Bahn, why are we held responsible if you cannot guarantee safe deposits? The conductor said you weren't allowed to put your suitcase on the partition... Of course. Then please mark it that way and write it in the conditions of carriage (it's supposedly in there). Unbelievable!!! Plus completely overpriced prices. You also want a certain degree of security on the train (yes the suitcase was placed on top as normal, it was neither crooked nor was it protruding... A disgrace for such a company!!!

It's just embarrassing how poorly the railways work in Germany. You don't feel like you're in a country that is technically developed. Delays of more than 10 minutes are the rule rather than the exception.

I used short-distance or long-distance national trains or Sbhan several times. If it weren't for the discounted ticket, they would be too expensive for me. However, I must admit that the rolling stock is modern and quiet. It's very nice to travel by train in DE.

Unpunctual in bright sunshine. So it's not the weather's fault. Despite the long weekend, a car is missing. Reservations are no longer valid. Help is zero. Reservation displays broken. So you have to constantly hope that no one comes. Service is zero. This in first class. Fly better. I will now cancel my BahnCard.

I think the train is doing what it can to ensure guests have a pleasant journey. I've been taking the train a lot lately. We were always a little late, but it was never the train's fault. One time people were walking on the tracks, another time construction work was blocking train traffic. We were always compensated, even though the railway was not to blame. After all, if you're stuck in a traffic jam because there was an accident, you won't get any compensation like 20 euros per person or 50% of the fuel costs.

I've been living in Germany for a little bit more than one years, and i've been using Deutsche Bahn for travelling around the country itself. Normally, the service is punctual and there are not a lot of reasons to complain, but just have in mind, that sometimes "when something bad happens" the trains might be delayed or even cancelled, which is in my opinion a disaster. There are a lot of people giving very bad reviews to Deutsche Bahn because of that, but I give a 4 star because I know it works normally good.Also, it is quite expensive if you buy your tickets for high speed trains on the same day, so be sure to do that with at least a month in advance.With all that said, Deutsche Bahn also offers a lot of deals to make the train travelling in Germany more confortable and cheaper, like "Bayern-Ticket", Baden-Ticket, Schöneswochenende. And also, if you live here, get a 25% or 50% Bahncard which will help you to save a lot of money while travelling, but do it only if you think you are gonna travel periodically and DON'T forget to cancel the service if you are not planning to use it any longer.

Hm... what qualified contribution could I make here? The train was on time, so I had a stomach ache. On the way there, the connecting train was waiting in Mannheim. On the way back everything went well in Hanover. I don't know why we were denied the train without changing trains, because there was one, but it wasn't possible with our package trip. Funny. The train itself was probably from the first generation. One was completely renovated, the others were somehow no longer so great. There was WiFi, but it wasn't even enough for emails. Weak! Train toilets, another thing that I don't understand. This is antediluvian, in the truest sense of the word. It's not about people not leaving them clean - no, you feel like you're on a slow train from the 80s in the toilets. Modern is different. Staff was friendly, a plus. Flying wouldn't have been more expensive either. I have to think about it...

The railway often has problems with punctuality: It is therefore advisable to pay attention to a few things when planning your trip: It is better to build in some time buffer and not plan an arrival that is too short, and if possible, never take connections with a change. If you follow these two rules, you will usually arrive on time. Despite the lack of punctuality, the use of the railway is increasing. A few years ago, if you were lucky you had a lot of space on the train, but now all the seats are full - except at off-peak times (i.e. very early, very late). The other question is whether alternative travel options are better, i.e. flight or car. And in this comparison the train usually performs better (at least for me). Car is only worthwhile if you travel a lot in areas with poor rail connections.

So I’ve been told over and over how great bahn is so maybe I had high expectations... When I booked my ticket I found the website to be really annoying. Hard to understand if I need to buy a bahn card or not to get the best deal. Had to try three times before I could get it to work and each time took 10 minutes. Annoying but manageable.On my trip I enjoyed the app. This was likely the best thing DB has going for it. I highly suggest all travellers use it. It saved me hours.I travelled from Ghent to Munich. Sounds easy but was not. About two hours after leaving Brussels we stopped (not at a station). It was super hard to understand what was going on (I don’t speak German). Turns out there was a protest on the tracks so we had to go backwards all the way back to the next station. This caused me to miss my connecting train at Frankfurt by an hour. Train was dirty, bathrooms were gross (no water and sometimes no paper).Then when we tried to figure out what train to take the platform workers weren’t that helpful. Trains were late or left early.We ran for one platform and asked the attendant if it was the right one and she just yelled at us in German.The only help we got was from the passengers. While it was interesting, I’d likely not do it again with my family.

The railway has had significant problems with punctuality in recent months, but even before that there were some basic rules in place when dealing with trains. Above all, it's important to avoid connections that involve changing trains - the probability that it won't work is extremely high. Therefore, it is always better to take direct connections. Strangely enough, many trains are very full - the delays don't seem to be a deterrent. Otherwise, the train has improved a lot: WiFi in the ICEs, cleanliness could sometimes be better (although some passengers also have to wonder how they use the toilets - and whether they do the same at home). There is also a lounge at the larger train stations so that the waiting time can be spent more pleasantly. I've been a BahnCard 100 user for a few years now - so of course I have a certain sympathy for the railway, despite all the disadvantages.

Usually we hire a car to travel around Europe but this time we decided to do some by train. You hear how good the Europe trains are that we thought it would be simple. It turned out to be very stressful, more so than driving! We got the DB from Amsterdam to Hamburg which had one easy stop in Osnabruck. We decided to go first class thinking it would be nicer. Firstly, first class was a huge let down! No wifi, seats were uncomfortable & definitely not what I expected! No more luxurious than 2nd class just cost more! Then we discover due to rail issues our train was ending in some small town & we had to get off and get a local train to Osnabruck to get our Hamburg connection. The info given was very minimal but we were assured we would make our connection. Wrong! We missed our connection & had to wait for another which meant we also had no seat. The next train had no working air conditioner & it was a rather warm day. The food was very poor and had little to no choice. We got to Hamburg hours later than planned & other passengers had missed there connections to other places too. We got told that this is what German rail is like and it was nothing unexpected for locals to hear this. Next time, I will stick to driving!
I'm currently standing at the Düsseldorf Airport train station and I'm being smoked by smoking passengers. Fines and expulsions should be issued here so that this doesn't happen again in the future.

Frankly, it's not like before! It's been more than 10 years since I took the Deutsche Bahn to travel. Recently, I had to go to Cologne and I bought 1st class tickets. But there, big disappointment! Cars quite dirty and half of the seats turned against the direction of the train. But why?? It's quite unpleasant to be seated in the opposite direction of travel, haven't we finally understood that? on the return journey, no waiter from the restaurant came to ask us if we would like to drink or eat something, as was the case on the outward journey. Finally, I went to the restaurant myself and I was surprised to discover that the seats in the 2nd class carriages are just as comfortable as those in the 1st, ... and that many passengers had something to eat and drink. So it is no longer worth paying more to travel in 1st class!

I did not heed the advice of the previous reviewers before booking with this company and lived to regret that unwise decision.  What I found were dirty train cars, no curtain on window, disrupted schedules, no potable water on train (unless one can purchase water at the concession counter).  We attempted to do just that as we had a long trip but the credit card machine was broken so we had nothing to drink for hours.  This was a miserable trip and I wish I had taken the advice provided on this forum before booking- will not make the same mistake again.

Today I'm writing about the bistro on the ICE. After the LH plane (yes, the plane) was delayed again, there were only seats in the bistro on the train and that was a good thing. I ordered the Rioja. I'm not a particular wine connoisseur, but wine connoisseurs should also like it. Then a flatbread pulled pork. And that was really tasty. I hope the railway buys good meat (I just have a guilty conscience). The service was also good and the journey went very well looking out the window. And: on time!

Used the ICE trains from Brussels to Cologne and Berlin (and return) - Excellent service on board - comfortable - announcements in German and English. Main stations (Cologne and Berlin) are excellent - well laid out, easy to navigate with plenty of directions/information. Deutsch Bahn could teach the UK railways quite a lot!

September 11 at 11:30 a.m., on the platform of Offenburg station shortly before departure, announcement of a delay of more than 1/2 hour for the train to Frankfurt international airport due to technical problems with the train, then transfer to another train with a mandatory train change at Frankfurt main station, insufficient information. Finally 3 hours journey from Strasbourg! When will there be a direct, fast and quality train between Strasbourg/Kehl and Frankfurt airport? Strasbourg, the Capital of Europe is well worth it!
I traveled on the ICE flight for the first time. Precisely clean, silent and fast. I wish MÁV was like this in Hungary. 1 hour Nuremberg-Munich. It's a shame to mess with the car.

I have been travelling through many countries in the world (Vietnam, the Netherlands, Spain, Italy, Egypt, Tunis, Morocco, Japan, Hungary, Rumania, Norway, the UK, even the USA), but nothing has been ever as bad and unreliable as the #Deutsche Bahn. Moreover, never have I encountered such a lousy customer service. Last July we booked a train ticket for 45€ from Aachen to Frankfurt Main Flughafen, because we had a flight to Vietnam (which cost 1,000€ return). We booked a direct train to be at the airport 3 hours in advance. When we went to the station in Aachen, the train was cancelled, and the other alternatives available were slow trains, with which we could not possible make it on time for our flight. When we asked the person in the information/customer service office at the station, he shrugged his shoulders and said that we should just wait and see what happened (probably he never left Aachen, because otherwise he would have guessed how much a ticket to Vietnam costs!!!). As time passed, even the slow trains had like 1h delay, so we decided to take a taxi to Cologne, for which we paid 156€. Then from there, we were able to take the fast train to the airport. When we returned, we filed a complaint, where we kindly asked them to reimburse the price of the taxi or at least the train fee. They answered us by telling that we were only entitled to 25% of the train ticket, because it ‘only’ had one hour delay and we arrived 85 minutes later. Of course, it was only 85 minutes later, because we took a taxi. Otherwise we would probably still be waiting at Aachen train station. They had the nerve to say that they did not reimburse the taxi because we could have taken a later train (note that they said this after we sent them the flight tickets with the price of them). What is even more deplorable, is that this is not the first time that such situations have happened to us. This time, however, it was totally unacceptable. Considering the price that one has to pay for the Deutsche Bahn tickets (much more expensive than any neighbouring country and I would say most countries in Europe), their service and treatment to their customers is deplorable and shameful. I wonder why people do not complain more about this company, or just stop using it altogether. Probably walking one arrives faster and cheaper to their destiny. Avoid Deutsche Bahn like the plague.

I travelled many times with Deutsche Bahn on their ICE’s already and had various experiences with them. Most of them where negative! The biggest problem is, that they are unpunctual most of the time. Second thing is, the tickets, when not purchased far in advance, are too expensive for what they offer and compared to a flight booking! But the reason why I write this review about them is, that as soon it is summer everything is getting even worse! Even more delays and cancellations and the AC is almost not working in the cabin on hot days! Last week I took an ICE from Munich to Berlin and this week from Munich to Cologne. Usually I like sitting in the restaurant on their trains and have some food and drinks, but for what reason ever, they had drinks only, to Berlin even out of paper cups. For the same price! I noticed, that on more and more of their ICE routes they don‘t offer food any more and this for months now! And the staff is trying to explain the food situation by inventing flimsy reasons in my mind! All in all in need to say that the Deutsche Bahn is fully unreliable!

Deutsche Bahn has the unfriendly staff! It's disrespectful to passengers!  If your staff cannot work professionally, then please do not hire such people! They don't even deserve a star! Too bad! I enjoyed traveling with Deutsche Bahn every day for two years!

In order to make our trip from Basel to Frankfurt with our child (6 years old) pleasant, we booked 1st class with a seat reservation. The train is canceled, there is no replacement train and you can politely say thank you for being allowed on a much later train....🙄 seat reservation gone. The worst thing about the whole thing: I drove the route about 5 times and every time there were problems.... incompetent

On today's journey with the ICE 2541 from Essen to Frankfurt Hbf and with the ICE 579 from Frankfurt Hbf to Stuttgart, the onward journey was delayed three times, each by around 20 minutes, due to overcrowding on the trains. For me, missed connecting trains lead to an increase in travel time of at least 1.5 hours. The question that arises for me is whether selling more tickets than existing capacity is a method/intention to siphon off money as quickly as possible without taking the passengers into account or whether the planning/control is simply incompetent. I will definitely forego the train in the near future and use my own car.

The required trains on the way there and back were on time, there were still seats and the delay in the Munich S-Bahn area was foreseeable in advance, as there is construction going on here and there was also a terminal closure in the morning. The staff on the train was friendly.
One of the worse train service in Europe. Delays, standing travelling in intercity trains etc.. And obviusly it is not a cheap service
Train breaks down Replacement train is in Duisburg nobody knows what and then in Hamm 40 minutes +++ Deutsche Bahn company chaos and scrap

I've just come from a country where 2-3 hour delays are commonplace. The DB was 30 minutes late, which meant we missed our connection. The gentleman at the travel agency was very friendly and rescheduled us for free. Because our second train was 2 hours late, we got 50% back and every passenger got a free soft drink. For me it was a complete culture shock. The staff were always friendly and so were those traveling with us.

Started in München to find walls scuffed and cola stains on wall, carpets dirty and food crumbs all over. Two conductors loudly speaking to each other and impolite to US guests. Seats uncomfortable for a first-class product. Air conditioning not very good (though as it's Germany likely someone would complain they would die of a lung infection were it any colder). Lots of screaming kids in the car. Our train from Munich was suddenly re-routed while in motion, thus arriving 1/2 hour late. On the connecting train in Nürnberg just after departure a conductor was bellowing into his mobile phone extremely loudly. There is actually a glassed-in compartment where he could do that, but as with other conductors we encountered the passengers are largely irrelevant to them. And who can blame them, given pressure they are under by DB and their low salaries? The carpet was stained all over the first class car in this train as well. Three of the bathrooms in this half of the train were out of service; the condition of the bathroom that actually wasn't out of service was appalling. Absurd. Fortunately the dining car was semi-gemütlich, prices decent and food average. I took pity on the nice waitress and tipped her €5.But this is first class, seriously?!? If you've ever traveled by second class train in Switzerland then DB's ICE first class will shock you, as it feels so very much lower quality than even second class on literally any train in Switzerland. The first regional train to the final destination was as I remembered it from long ago: drunk footballers singing songs in second class and a dirty table covered with coffee stains in first class. Behind us in the final row in first class sat a DB employee in uniform, fast asleep. Again carpet stained all over. And our second and final regional train again full of drunk footballers, this time aggressively annoying passengers. The first-class compartment had eight seats, barely distinguishable from second class except separated by a glass door from which we could watch and hear the hooligans. Oh and the carpet again was filthy, final score: 4/4 dirty compartments in first class. Don't waste your money on this product; it clearly isn't worth it. Especially once you learn that under many conditions adults can bring children under 14 for free in first class. And then there are these cheap stickers on every row of seats that say ,,Bitte beurteilen Sie Ihre heutige Fahrt" with a QR Code. This literally looks like high school graffiti; it's done in poor taste and further underscores how DB has totally clueless management. Several days later I bought a second-class ticket for a regional train in Schleswig-Holstein and despite pressing all the right selections on the machine I got a ticket for the same day rather than the next day due to the fact a bus would be replacing the train due to track work that weekend. This then required going to a counter (the office was closed due to some reason that day) in Lübeck to beg the ticket be validated for the next day. Which it then was. Silly.  Verdict: Somehow DB feels like what the family used to call the Planwirtschaft der DDR. That was a failed country. This is quickly becoming a failed railway.

We heard that travelling by train was going to be easy in Europe, but it was not the case. My family (70-year-old mother, 31-year-old sister and myself) rode a Deutsche Bahn train from Amsterdam to Berlin. There were NO outlets to charge phones and the ride was quite long, so it was very inconvenient. Additionally, it was a hot summer day and the air conditioning was not circulating. The only way to feel any air was to place my arm directly on the vent but it then blocked the air from reaching the rest of my body. I would not recommend this train service as it was very uncomfortable.

Took the DB trains around Germany.  Inside of trains are plain, but okay.  The service is lacking.  At Munich main station, the person at the info desk was curt and slightly rude.  We waited for over 90 min to get a seat assignment, but our number was still far off, so we rushed to the train before it departed.  We bought tickets online and went to berlin station to get the system-generated seat assignment changed.  First desk agent said the seats cannot be changed.  When we asked several times why, she gave slightly different answers.  Then we left to eat and came back.  Another agent told us we can change the seat assignments and did so.   What kind of lying or incompetent service does DB tolerate among their employees?   French Rail staff may be just as lazy, but they don’t lie and the French trains are much nicer and faster.

Used for round trip between Frankfurt and Cologne. If you purchase the early bird discount from the DB site, you can get a great deal. The location of the vehicle scheduled to stop is posted on the platform, but even when I waited there, it was completely different. Since I took a first class train on my way back from Cologne, I was able to use the lounge at the station and have some snacks. It was very crowded in the evening, with people standing not only in the aisles but also on the deck. I think it depends on the route, but it was safer to reserve a seat.

We were 6 adults and four 5year kids. We decided for the trains to move around Germany. We took 3 trains.The first from Munich Airport to Munich Passing, all announcements only in German, we were kicked out at one station and fight our way into taxis to get transferred to another station, at 35°C, no water, 1 hour waiting, no one explaining anything just a lady shouting in German (the boys stated crying... ) horrible experience.The second, from Munich to Gunzburg, smelled horrible, all toilets were broken and one of the boys , 4 years old,was yelled at for 3 minutes, in German of course,  for having the tip of his shoe on the seat, the whole train heard it and actually a German lady in the train told him to stop it.The third train, a fast train IC from Gunzburg to Munich.. was cancelled! Never came! Again, no one to ask, everything only in German... We ended up taking a regional train that took for ever. Of course no refund.Worse decision ever, I lived in Germany for 2 years (16 years ago) and trains were so great! I never expected such awful service.

Very easy to use, we travelled from the airport to the city center by only buying a ticket from the DB app. It is clean in the station and also in the trains. All the trains and buses are exactly on time.
Fares are going up and the frustrated and long suffering frequent travelers are affected by seemingly never ending delays, cancellations and dirty trains.

We drove from Frankfurt to Berlin in the Sprinter on Thursday evening and arrived 40 minutes late. The return journey on Monday evening took 35 minutes. That's pretty intense. At the train station in Berlin I looked in vain for a currywurst or a boulette.

Today I got on the wrong regio Deeutsche Bahn train which meant I missed my last connection train from Wuerzburg to Hannover. In tears I ran up to one of the staff to get advise what I should do but the man reachted bired, desinterested and sad mocking me 'well you just missed your train' and when asking what I could do he said he didn't care. I didn't have a place to stay and was shocked by him.regusing to help at all.

It was a round trip within 2 days. Heat wave in Germany. 11 hours of air conditioning with green electricity. Despite all the justified criticism of Deutsche Bahn - important and necessary - the alternatives are no better and are actually more harmful to the environment. Remember again and again: the fellow travelers are sometimes annoying

In my honest opinion, never use the deutsche Bahn Service. On multiple occasions, these trains have been delayed by more than 2 hours and disrupted my subsequent plans. The tickets are also over priced.You are better off travelling via bus or renting a car. If I could, I would give them a 0/5 rating!

On Travel for work, with one meeting in Koln one day and one meeting in Hannover the next day with return the same day to Brussels, the train seemed to be the most appropriate transport... Well, what a naïve I was. First train : 2h30 of delay. Second train: because we were afraid of missing our correspondance in Düsseldorf, we bought new train tickets to take a train one hour un advance just in case...And luckily that we did! Again 54 minutes of delay. From what I have seen and understood this is common practice for this company (when looking at the announcement boards). And in addition, if you dare to ask,off course with politness (I exactly said "Hello Madam, excuse me to bother you, but would you know if we will have much more delay because we have a connection in Düsseldorf and we are afraid that we will miss it") you get shout at that they don't know what is going on! And that anyway they have only 50 min of delay (...!) Well, three things I know now: 1) if I can avoid it, never again a travel with the Bahn. 2) If I have no choice: plan 3 hours between connections. 3) At least, at next delay with the SNCB or SNCF (Belgian and French train company), I will always know that it could be worst, it could be as bad as with the Bahn...OMG! In fact I should say thank you to the Bahn!So, here I go: thank you Bahn for being the worst train company ever!!

Traveled by train from Copenhagen to St. Johann im Pongau. Had ordered 1st class, which was quite a bit more expensive than 2nd class. However, I would not recommend this if you expect better service or more peace of mind on the trip. The only thing you get for the money is a slightly wider seat. Nothing else. The German staff were rude, indifferent and slow. Maybe they should consider whether they are in the right jobs. Plugs for chargers didn't work in the entire carriage we were in (the journey from Freilassing to Hamburg takes 9 hours, so there were quite a few travelers who were unhappy with this), which several of the staff pretended they wanted to do something about. But you got no answer and if you asked again they were offended and ignored us. In Denmark, too many tickets had been sold from Hamburg to Copenhagen. So even in 1st class the aisles were full of passengers who didn't have a seat (but they had 1st class tickets).

I enjoyed a horror trip a few days ago. On a trip from Basel to Hanover that was supposed to last 6 hours and 20 minutes, there was a whopping delay of over 4 hours!!! The DB's "compensation": a maximum of 50% of the fare, and this through bureaucratic means (especially for passengers with tickets from abroad). The DB is the worst advertisement for Germany as a travel destination. And finally: if there is no good flight connection, then take the Flixbus!

Travelling from Amsterdam to Berlin, we were in our reserved seats and our air conditioning was not working. Admittedly we thought the train must not come with air conditioning. It was when the train was stopped that the staff discontinued the use of the two carriages. We were told to find seats in the other carriages and we lost our reserves seats and had to stand in between the carriages. Overall I had heard that Germany is proud of their trains, however this should not be one if their proudest moments.

What an absolute disaster of a service. €270 for my wife, our 4 year old and I, to travel from Berlin to our home near Frankfurt Hahn. Filthy cabin, littered from previous passengers. The first train left on time but arrived late to Cologne, our first stop. We were told our connection had already left and we had to find another train. The staff were so ignorant. Disgusting first and last experience of train travel in Germany.

I was unfortunate enough to have to travel with DB on a recent trip to Germany, and I have to say the experience was one of the worst I have ever had with any rail service.I had purchased tickets online to travel from Frankfurt Airport to Göttingen. My flight was delayed by three hours and I ended up being approximately 40 minutes late for my train. This obviously was not DB's fault but it did lead to perhaps the most appalling encounter I have ever had with someone whose job it is to deal with the public. I went to the travel centre to explain the situation and see what could be done about the ticket. When I entered, the man at the desk was staring intently at his computer so I decided not to interrupt him and waited for him to finish what he was doing. Some moments later he threw his hands into the air and gestured for me to get on with it. He had not, in fact, been working but was just too rude to muster a hello. I have not spoken German in so long it would have been useless to attempt it at that point so I began to explain in English, and had barely gotten a sentence out before he cut across me with, "I do not understand you!" shrugging his shoulders and gesturing with his hands. I attempted a second time and he interrupted me again, "What do you want?" This irritated me for numerous reasons, not only because this man sought employment in a train station at an airport where he would inevitably encounter tourists, but also because I spent over 10 years working in hospitality and although there were many times that my patience was stretched to its limit, and I often encountered people who did not have very good English, if any at all, I never took a tone with customers or demonstrated such blatant rudeness. Also, the woman at the next desk somehow managed to understand me and told her colleague IN English what I was attempting to convey to him, suggesting that his comprehension was quite good and/or I was easy enough to comprehend.He eventually deigned to deal with my ticket issue and attempted to sell me one for over €80. My sister, who is studying in Germany, has ended up having to get different trains on a few occasions, usually due to DB's notorious delays, and was often charged only the difference between the ticket she had purchased and the price of the ticket for the next train. In my country, if you want to travel at a different time than stated on the ticket, you pay a flat €10. Again, my plane delay was not DB's fault, but the ticket prices are scandalous, especially when you consider the fact that with DB, unlike other rail service providers, you are not purchasing a particular seat but merely a spot on that train. DB lost nothing due to my missing the train because they don't stop selling tickets when their seats are full, they proceed to pile people onto their trains like cattle, with no thought spared for passenger comfort or safety. I refused to pay €80 and miraculously he managed to conjure up a second ticket for €45, with an extremely surly reminder that it was merely a single and I would not be able to return on the ticket.My bad experience with DB did not end there and what transpired on my journey only served to further fuel my irritation. I had two changes of train, the second being one stop and a 10 minute trip on the ICE from my final destination. When I got to the station at 23:40 I assumed I only had a 15-minute wait. The train station was almost deserted: the shops and restaurants were closed, as were the toilets, and there was not a DB employee to be seen. I was waiting on the platform when an announcement was made - solely in German because DB don't believe in catering for people who may have little if any German - and thankfully, my German was good enough to understand that due to some vague technical issues - something which seems to occur to DB trains with frightening frequency - my train was going to be delayed by 3 hours. Needless to say, I was quite annoyed at this point, having been travelling for over 12 hours, and having been lambasted for my own 40-minute delay just a few hours prior. I was also stuck in an empty station, devoid of people or facilities, waiting for the last passenger train of the night with two other passengers, one of whom was a toddler. There was nowhere to seek assistance and this was more worrisome than it would have been with another train service due to DB's propensity for extending delays numerous times.When the train eventually arrived it was without an apology or an explanation from staff, which at this point did not surprise me as customer service or general manners does not appear to be something required of DB employees.I had to take the train every day of my trip, and there was not a time that I entered a station that there wasn't a notice of delay. I'm not exactly sure what causes these delays but I think it's unacceptable. Yes, delays happen, situations arise and trains can break down. But I wouldn't be allowed to take my car on the road if it was not fit for purpose and given the prices of DB's tickets, I would expect less 'technical issues' with the trains.Given that I had been delayed on almost every train I had been on, I was quite worried about my return journey to the airport, especially as I had three train changes. My DB app had the numbers of the trains I was to get, yet one train was a completely different number, which is disgraceful considering the train was serving three airports and would have passengers who would not be used to travelling with DB and would be expecting the number of the train to match what was on the ticket. Again, this train was delayed by half an hour, and again, there was no explanation given in English despite the destination being more than one airport.I will say that I encountered some nice conductors on the trains, but overall I think DB need to shadow their bus-driving colleagues to see how one should act when working with the public. I took four buses in Celle and the bus drivers were possibly some of the friendliest and most helpful individuals I have met, and certainly outshone the majority of DB I encountered.Advice to DB: have consistent policies. Don't let one ticket operator charge only the difference between tickets, or indeed refund if that is the case, and have others attempt to squeeze every last cent out that they can.If you're going to have trains delayed into the middle of the night, have some facilities open in the train stations, or at least an employee who can provide some assistance.Lower the prices: DB have the most expensive tickets of any rail service I have used and I'm quite confused about what exactly I paid for. It wasn't a particular seat or guarantee that I wouldn't be squashed between passengers and luggage and trying to find something to hold on to to ensure I managed to stay upright. It also wasn't punctuality, and it most certainly was not the outstanding customer service.It truly is a shame for customers that DB has a monopoly on nationwide train travel, but, I imagine, quite a relief for them as they would have to make major improvements to beat any competitor.

We spent a week in Germany in early July 2018 and here’s our experience and thoughts using the DB train system. Train times and delay:The trains were on time throughout most of our trip. Except for two days when it was raining,  we experienced nearly 30 minutes delay, but that was it. Fortunately, there is the DB Navigator App which updates in real time, providing information on the alternative trains you can take and the updated time of departure and arrival.DB Navigator App:I found this app very, very useful. Its user-interface is user-friendly, intuitive and loads information very quickly and smoothly. I used its Trip Planner feature before our trip to search which train schedule, transfers, ticket prices. Purchased some tickets in advance through the app. International credit card (VISA) worked without any problem. My favorite feature is the ‘Add to calendar’ function that saves all essential information of the train trips on my phone calendar (iOS), including departure and arrival times, station names, platform numbers. All this information accurately saved in my phone were quite convenient and enabled us to recheck our whole train schedule anytime even when offline. About transfers and connections:When planning our trip, our main concern was the transfer times. A lot of DB app’s schedule suggestions  included 3~5 minutes transfer duration. We weren’t sure if that would be enough or if we were bound to miss the connection. But, as it turns out, we were able to transfer trains as scheduled. Well, except during the rainy day, when we missed our connecting train because of the delays. It was an IC train and we had reserved seats. I’m not sure if I had to given the circumstances, but I changed our seat reservation for the next coming train through the app.Tickets:During our trip, we used both mobile tickets purchased on the app and paper tickets bought at the station. Mobile ticket (advance purchase)- After purchase, a ticket with a QR code is saved in the app and can also be saved in iPhone’s Wallet. You  have to show this to the conductor when they come to check your tickets. I opted the advance purchase of ticket for the trips that wasn’t covered by affordable day tickets. (Trips that start before 9am on a weekday, for example) It was much cheaper purchased in advance than during the actual day of your trip. Paper tickets (bought at the ticket machine in the station) - the ticket machine has various language options, English of course, so we were able to buy tickets easily. Used a VISA card with no problem. We bought tickets at the train station for trips that were covered by good-deal day tickets like the Bayern ticket. There was only one time when I hoped I rather bought it in advance. It was in Füssen station, there was only one ticket machine (the other one wasn’t working) there was a long line of people waiting for their turn to buy, and there was only like five minutes left before the train comes. We made it in time but it was quite a thrill. You have to write the names of your companions on the ticket. I only wrote my name as the representative passenger but the conductor said we have to write all names. Trains:They were clean, comfortable ride overall. Huge windows for taking in the views. Would’ve appreciated if they had blinds for when you’re at the side of sun because it could get quite bright and hot. We noticed the red trains (regional)  didn’t have blinds but the white and green ones (ODEG) had. We mostly took the RB and RE trains throughout our whole trip but also rode an IC and ICE train one time each. Seats in the IC/ICE train were clearly more comfortable than the regional trains. We reserved seats in the open saloon without table. The ones with tables had seats facing each other so they might be spacious but only if there are no other passengers sit across you. The compartment seats looked quite comfortable too and we thought it would be nice if you’re travelling with a large group.About the announcements inside the train— all in German for the most part, except for one time at the IC train, some info about the delay were announced in English. But then we didn’t find this to be a big problem because info on which station is next is displayed on the screen.Stations and platforms:We got to use a variety of stations, big and small. Some were very clean, some.. well, not so much. The big ones like Berlin Station have vending machines on the platform, great for a quick snack/drink shopping. We were impressed by Berlin Station, it was huge and modern. I read some reviews that it’s too big and one is sure to get lost in it but I found it to be very well signed and we found our way easily. We definitely appreciated that all stations have a big sign of the station name on the platform! (Can’t say the same for some railroad systems in Europe) One thing that surprised us was there was one train in a platform that was scheduled to split into two and go to different destinations! You have to pay attention to the destination displayed on the screen inside the train. Luckily, we noticed we boarded on the train that was going to another direction so we were able to get off and board the ‘right’ part of the train before it departed. OVERALL:We had an overall good experience using the German train system. It definitely helped that we’ve generally planned our trip beforehand. We had room for changes in schedule and the train system was flexible enough for that. We did hope that the fast trains (IC/ICE) would be slightly more affordable, but the day tickets for regional trains were of good deal and we’re glad we made good use of it.
What can you say...9 out of 10 trips with the DB are an unreasonable expectation. Delays are often not even the worst thing in this juice shop...

We eventually got on another train, but had to stand all the way even though we had paid for pre-booked seats. But the worst was yet to come. For the long-distance second trip, we made the transfer to the second train, but it was so overbooked we had to stand, along with some elderly people. Why not? The terrible part was when, 2 hours into the journey, a policeman and policewoman told all the standing passengers (without seat reservations, for which you pay extra) in our compartment to get off the train at the next stop. Just get off. We protested because we had paid for our tickets for that train and the policewoman said to my travel partner in German: "You have 2 choices. Either you get off the train or we will take you off." She actually threatened him with force. So they dumped us on some train station, and we had to try to finish our journey. The DB apparently doesn't see any need to show respect to anyone. They eagerly take your money (we spent over 400 euros on their trains) and then turf you out onto the station. Their complete disregard for their passengers is, quite frankly, shocking and it makes you feel degraded. I have spoken to people of many nationalities (including Germans) about their experiences on DB, and the stories are not good. Trains come late. Trains are cancelled. Trains just don't depart. You stand unless you pay extra for a seat. Trains are overcrowded. Yet the DB's modern booking system must be telling them how many people are travelling on which long-distance train. I can only conclude that the DB is making a lot of money at people's expense. The worst train service I have ever experienced by far.

The prices compared to other countries are okay. Unfortunately, the train is often late or even canceled and the cleanliness leaves a lot to be desired. The biggest drawback, however, is the unair-conditioned train, which is only ventilated or cooled through poorly designed windows... and therefore transporting customers is very inhumane. The conductors, who also served beverages, were very nice and helpful. Our seats were comfortable and, especially on the way back, peacefully quiet. We were there early precisely to avoid having to run for our train with my parents in their 70s and 8 pieces of luggage but that was exactly what happened. Many passengers were standing there, following the instructions not to get on  , and nearly missing the train. Great ride but unnerving boarding both ways.

during our stay in Berlin we used the S-bahn and U-bahn on numerous occasions and the trains were frequent, on time, rather clean and you could easily sit down and redeem your ticket on the platform but no access barriers; Be careful, the controllers are in civilian clothes!

We had to make an emergency and unplanned landing in Düsseldorf and had to be redirected to Deutsche Bahn to Hamburg because all Eurowings flights were fully booked. All trains were late. When the announcement of the departure of the next ICE came, masses of people streamed onto the train. On the train there was an announcement that two more trains were arriving, 5 minutes apart (if you can believe it!) and that the train would not move any further if the passengers, at least some of them, did not leave the train. I mean, the announcement could have been made at the train track. Management nil! And it is a permanent condition. Conditions like (without meaning to offend anyone) in India. Bravo to the German railway! To verify, the responsible person at the German railway can look at the delays on May 13th, 2018. It's true!

We rode the DB a couple of times in the past year when we've visited Germany.  I've personally found the entire system to be fantastic.  All of our trains were perfectly on-time, tickets were easy to buy, the train cabins were comfortable and clean.The staff we interacted with in purchasing our tickets were very helpful and gave great advice on which ticket was required and where to go to catch the train.When I visit Europe, I prefer to travel by train and the DB system has worked really well for me.

I wanted to warn all international travellers thinking of purchasing online tickets for train travel in Europe using Deutsche Bahn. I purchased tickets from Australia using Deutsche Bahn online for first class travel on the Bernina Express from Italy to Germany. I was told that my tickets would be sent to my address in Australia in 8 business days. I booked my tickets back on Feb 10th 2018 and I have still not received my tickets and it is now the 4th April 2018 and I’m still waiting for my tickets. I have tried emailing Deutsche Bahn Online to find out where my tickets are and was told that the tickets cannot be reissued or emailed to me because they are a “legal document of monetary value”. DB also do not have tracking on international “legal documents of monetary value” (tickets) that must be posted out. So how does the customer who bought them know where they are or if they were even sent. After much emailing and calling DB in Germany I was told that I should purchase a new set of tickets. Appalling service. I purchased another set from a friend in Germany who went into a DB office and received them over the counter. She sent them to Australia and I received them in just 7 days. Original tickets still are missing almost 80 days from purchase. How is this acceptable?! If you know someone in Germany to get DB tickets for you I suggest you ask them otherwise you will regret the online purchasing system DB have.

Only the Generation 3 ICEs were tested on the high-speed route; the Generation 1 ICEs received the new signaling system, but no tests were carried out. The Japanese and Swiss would be deeply ashamed. The managers of Deutsche Bahn are not ashamed. They should be fired.-----One can only pity the employees. Apart from two minor delays and some overcrowded trains from private providers (not DB), we always had a pleasant train journey and will use Deutsche Bahn again next time!

Incompetence coupled with rampant unfriendliness towards customers. Timetable accuracy is non-existent. Rebooking at the “friendly travel center” in Hanover was rudely rejected with the comment that it wasn’t really our problem. Presumably these employees all went through the excellent school of their works council chairman, who doesn't care about the customer anyway. All in all, I'm more than 2 hours late today, coupled with a standing room in the aisle despite a seat reservation in first class for good money, unbelievably dilapidated Federal Railway, technology & staff!!

You reserve a place on the ICE in the first class car from Frankfurt. The train arrives with a completely different order of cars and the announcement is unable to give the numbers of the cars. The ICE had been on the road since 0500 - we got on at 0951!

Of course, there is still something to improve: the punctuality, the quality of the information, some people get upset about the prices without having a reference point. And in fact there are many dilapidated train stations... still. I have traveled on trains in Russia (punctual and robust), Japan (super-punctual, overcrowded), China (great system!), USA (oh dear!), France (disappointing service), Switzerland (first-class timetable) and elsewhere, which are always presented as supposed role models. The railway can actually learn a few things from this. But: The DB is clearly in the top group in the world; there is no doubt about that. Quality and service are very good. And if you put 40,000 trains on the rails per day, you also have to expect failures. For example, I have also experienced people on the ICE who got upset because of “personal injury” when they were delayed. Someone had thrown themselves in front of the train. And? Should the train just keep going, you smart people? My favorite experience: Taking the train along the Rhine route, sitting in the dining car with good food (yes, I think it's good!) with a bottle of wine. Unsurpassed - worldwide. However, I remember with sadness the time when the DB still had beautiful sleeping cars and motorail trains.

Other than the train system cannot keep up with the heavy flow of passengers in keeping their trains clean, the German DB does a great job of providing service and product.  I typically went first class for more room and a seat reservation.  The only complaint is there is never enough room for luggage if one is traveling from one city to another.

This is an excellent and efficient way to get where you're going in Berlin. VERY EASY to navigate, routes are "color coded" similar to Paris and London however not as extensive. Ticket dispensers are very user friendly and offer multi language displays, single way, one and three day fares, cash only, they do not take credit or debit cards. Be fore warned the routes also have their share of pan handlers.

I've been taking the train regularly for two years. In about 20 trips from Hanover to Rostock and back alone, I couldn't find anything negative. I've been taking the train regularly for two years. Obviously nice if you don't have to wait for your train in the main hall or on the platform, but if you purchase a first class ticket, you'd expect a little more than just beverages. Wifi and newspapers available. Don't expect anything like an airport lounge though.

We are amazed by the efficiency and that almost all stations have an elevator. We found the metro (U-Bahn) better than that of other European cities (London, Paris, Barcelona).

I drove with my little dog. Since he was sitting in a basket, I didn't have to pay anything for him. We had a smooth train journey with no delays. So we were able to sleep on the way and arrived at our destination safe and refreshed. I will travel with Deutsche Bahn again!

Deutsche Bahn is a disaster. Germany is heading towards the abyss. Such a rich country will not be able to move trains over rails in 2024. If there were a competitor, the DB would have gone bankrupt long ago. And LH and Eurowings are also juice shops…
Unpunctual, unreliable. There's nothing more to say! Trains are canceled without notice. Delays are normal. Never experienced such a bad situation.

Return journey with 1x change: the 1st train is canceled, surprise! Of course, the subsequent ICE could no longer be reached and the booking was free, money wasted for nothing. Instead, change trains 3 times and arrive 4 hours late. Juice shop.

There is most of the time delay Any day, any season, any time… you must always calculate a delay.. it can easily be 30 minutes.. in 2024 I have never took a train and it was on time 😅 According to attached picture , the few minutes delay will make me waiting over one hour for the next connection!!!
