The trains could not run, although it was noted otherwise on the railway's official website. There was no information about a rail replacement service. The travelers were left at a loss. If you wanted to know something, you had to ask the locals on the street. There were only a few buses that went to Bremen-Oberneuland train station. These few buses were overcrowded. Many had to stay behind because they couldn't get on the bus. When we arrived at the train station, a railway employee assured us that we should get on the next train. But once we did that, everyone was immediately told to get out again. The train drove 100 meters further only to return on the same track. It's a shame that the railway is unable to pass on simple information to its guests. It is unacceptable that travelers are treated like a stupid flock of sheep. Ultimately, it is also a form of abuse of power if you do not address problems and improve them because you are sure of your monopoly. Deutsche Bahn has sunk to the level of an Italian provincial railway. Simply unfortunate and annoying at the same time!

Not only is it currently running between Frankfurt Airport and Arnhem at 4:40 a.m. instead of 2:25 a.m., but there is also a whopping 1:30 hour delay. Plus the staff who don't care about anything... Bad. Dilapidated infrastructure. Politics must act!

We wanted to take the e-bikes from Seeshaupt to the train to Starnberg on platform 2. The station only has stairs. So we drove about 500m to the other side. The train arrived on time....On platform 1......The stairs were too steep and the wheels were too heavy, so I drove around the tracks again and got into the first car. We were really shocked when we got out in Starnberg and realized that the door on the left side was broken and we couldn't get on. With the bikes through the narrow corridors, impossible. So we stayed on the train until we could finally get off in Munich. After an hour a train drove back to Starnberg. This time we checked whether the doors worked.
There is not a day without delays, regardless of local and long-distance traffic. You never know whether you will get to work or other appointments on time. Simply the very last thing

Sneaky, cynical and unhelpful. Terrible customer service. We bought Deutchlandticket in June, but were charged for two months! They want you to unsubscribe before the 10th, so if you buy the ticket and cancel it after that date, you will be charged for two months. 98€ instead of 49€. Customer service answers the e-mails exclusively on German and I was explained on the phone that they are not allowed to write/speak in English. Awful company!

I would like to write a review about the controller. My husband, daughter and our dog were traveling from Trier to Kobletz by train RE1. The controller came in, checked our tickets, and then gave out very tasty sweets to everyone, and took out and gave dog treats to the dog. It was very unexpected and pleasant. I talked to all the passengers, wished everyone well and gave everyone sweets. I wish we met people like this more often. pleasant controllers who love their work and bring creativity to it.

It's all in the title. When traveling with Interrail, we had to take a large number of trains. Two were chartered by the Deutsche Bahn, and I'll give it to you, they're the only two that screwed up. And according to the locals, it’s ritual. In short, if you can avoid it, avoid it.

Horror, according to DB train was defect but after 60 min in the middle of nowhere,  and later travelling slow...miracle happens and works again . Bs. More despicable is that because we were delays the personal in the train restaurant stopped working and was sitting in restaurant.  They told that in next station new personnel will come.  But but have to wait 50 until next station.  Terrible. Small cookies were offered. Additional very limited information in English about the whole problem. So far 93 min delay. No food  If you can,  do not use DB

In 2006 these trains ran like a Rolex. Excellent and without flaw.In 2024, run like a knockoff Rolex bought off Temu.Even the locals now say to take an earlier train if you actually want to get somewhere on time.Germany has fallen a long long long way.

My first "trip" in ICE on November 5, 2020: PARIS EST towards STRASBOURG. It's really different from a TGV to an ICE. The ICE is the German train on the left in the photo. Returnable in the event of derailment unlike our TGV which remains upright. And slower: 300 km/h maximum with an unpleasant noise (320 km/h for the TGV). Recently opened to competition, the national rail network welcomes sardine boxes like this one on our tracks. Paris Strasbourg by TGV, we don’t see the journey.  Whereas there the seats are hard as wood, with a constant muffled noise, white plastic walls, significant shaking from the slightest disturbance on the track. WC opened after 1/4 hour by ICE staff. No hand dryers in it, only paper that comes in confetti or bunches. At our seats: tiny trash cans placed on the table. Hello hygiene... . Staff who do not easily master the language of Voltaire "Bon Foyache". Anyway: can't wait to Strasbourg, this trip is torture.
What a juice shop, not a week goes by without there being a problem. Then you just get ripped off. Trains are canceled at random because a canceled train does not count towards the statistics.

Avoid German trains at alll cost: they are arguably the worst in Europe. And do not be fooled by the undeserved reputation of German efficiency. Their train system is a disgrace: technically obsolete, fragile and very poorly run. No care at all about passengers, in particular elderly ones. In our case, using the train to get from Switzerland to the Munich airport to take a flight and back, we had  terrible experiences both ways. In the first trip the train from the Munich station to the airport broke down. Messages (only in German, no English for passengers going to a supposedly international airport) promised replacement buses. We left the train at the station where it broke down, but there were no buses at all and the taxis refused to drive to the airport. We had to onvince on the spot an illegal driver with his private car! On the way back, the trains from Munich to Switzerland were stopped entirely for weeks because of some bad weather. However, similar (or worse) weather in Switzerland did not stop the trains for more than a few hours. So, we had to hire a limo!  One last word of caution: the train problems are particularly dramatic in Bavaria, like many other public infrastructures that are plagued by huge inefficiency even more than in the rest of Germany!

At the station it was announced that the train was 5 minutes late, then 10 minutes. Then we sat inside and the train driver didn't know at first why she wasn't getting clearance, then she called around and gradually found out that a train was probably routed incorrectly in the opposite direction and the train crossing (the route is partially single-track) would be moved. At least she clearly tried to inform us about the latest status with announcements, but it became clear that she had to gather the information herself. So after 35 minutes we were able to set off. I arrived hugely late and then had to pay 15EUR for a taxi to rush to an appointment at the last minute. Very poor performance again. The only bright spot was the openness and gallows humor of the train driver. The next day on the same route there was "only" a 15 minute delay and it was even announced in good time. You're almost relieved.

If I offer a service in my area of ​​work and knowingly do not provide it, this constitutes a form of fraud. But how does this work for a company like Deutsche Bahn (DB)? DB knowingly offers unpunctual services that are often canceled. No acceptable compensation will be offered for delays. For example, I was told: "If you don't reach your destination by tonight, you can claim a replacement or take a taxi." In my case that would have meant a delay of twelve hours; However, I ultimately reached my destination two hours later than planned. This led to a loss of earnings of 240 euros. Another employee just shrugged her shoulders and said: "I can't help you now." I would like to emphasize that I don't hold a grudge, but I travel regularly with the DB and unfortunately this tardiness is more the rule than the exception. This should make it clear what has become of the DB. The DB pays compensation for a delay of 120 minutes, but only in proportion to the ticket price. However, what do I do if I have a Germany ticket? My tip: If you have an urgent appointment, a subsequent flight or an important work appointment - in short, if punctuality is essential - you should take a plane, use the car or walk. These are based on experience and not slander.

6 hours late! For 13 years there have been only problems and no improvement in sight! Whether I had to go to vocational school, visit family or friends on vacation... I have never been able to rely on the German train and there are only problems with tickets, for example. The customer center is of no use either!

Bottom, there’s really nothing more to say about German railways and everything connected with it...absolutely everything is terrible, and it’s also expensive, not even a pleasure, but for the bad impressions

Train journey from Berlin to Sylt today, 1st class. The car was incredibly dirty. Feces on the floor, rubbish on the seats, windows dirty, toilet unusable, bistro closed, but travel price absurdly expensive. Railway staff on the train pushes responsibility far away (not responsible, other department, etc.). As a result, I canceled my BahnCard 50 1st class and no longer travel by train in line with the politically desired transport transition. The company is simply a disgrace for Germany as a location.

As always, too late. But don't disappoint because of that one star. Nothing expert across the board. I hope that every railway employee will be treated as a customer the same way they treat customers throughout their entire lives.

I should‘ve known better. Wanted to go from Frankfurt to Lyon with a stop in Basel. I planned 1h knowing that you can‘t rely on being on time with DB. It turned out this was far from enough. The train was supposed to leave at 2:45am. A time during which not a lot of trains drive. Nevertheless, the Deutsche Bahn totally made it possible to arrive with a delay of 1:30h. After asking at the information desk whether it‘s possible to gain back the 30 minutes I needed for my layover, the response was that this is realistic. Well, it wasn‘t. And instead we were going at turtle speed, waiting extremely long at every stop. We then arrived with a total delay of 2h. My connection was gone and I had to rebook the TGV in France. Luckily, this is super easy in France and you feel so relieved when you‘re there because you know the train will be on time. I‘ve never seen a TGV with a delay. The Deutsche Bahn literally is the biggest fraud you can imagine. It was my last time ever using it privately. Please, just take the car. For me, I can‘t wait until Terminal 3 at Frankfurt opens. The Deutsche Bahn won‘t even be able to compete with the prices airlines will offer. Faster, cleaner, better. Yes, cleaner. The whole train I was in (IC) was so utterly disgusting despite having a first class ticket. Nobody even worked there during the total time of 4h I was on board. Nobody said where we were at. The light was so bright, you couldn’t even try to sleep despite having a night connection. It‘s so sad that a rich country like Germany is unable to control a company that should be on top of their game. Never.Again.

I came back from Denmark to go to Switzerland. I had booked a night train. Arriving almost 1 hour late in Hamburg, I missed my first connection to Duisburg. Nothing serious, knowing the incompetence of the railway company, I could get a second connection. This was without counting on the qualities of the db to make the 2nd train leave 1 hour late. To make a journey through another Land than planned, and finally to be so late that we have to take a region to end up in Cologne to sleep in the station to wait for another train and return to Switzerland by another solution. Solution found, I go down to Frankfurt to take ICE to Basel... But 35 minutes late... Well, I just had a professional emergency. I had to return to Switzerland quite early... I was able to forget, especially with a 5-hour delay and a sleepless night. The saddest thing is that when it happens, you want to make everything shine. But it's illegal. But that's not the worst thing, it's that Germany is in the middle of Europe, and to go to "Scandinavia" you have to go through there. German quality they say! Germany is really not doing well, we can see that with its trains.
Over 10 of train that we took during Euro 2024, its either been cancel, heavily delayed. If you are on heavy luggage, please thinks other transportation. Its a mess, really bad.

By far the worst customer service you can imagine. What I experienced with the process of a so-called extraordinary cancellation of the Germany ticket is the worst example of how to deal with customers. I tried to explain the situation several times, by email and letter. No reaction, apart from stereotypical, machine-sounding reply letters that didn't respond at all to my explanations. Today the icing on the cake: a debt collection letter! It really couldn't be worse, 1 star is clearly too high... Actually, there shouldn't be a company that treats customers like that and doesn't realize that it is actually dependent on the customers.

Deutsche Bahn is probably the worst company in Germany and is known and hated for its notorious tardiness. Even the super sprinter from Munich to Berlin is sometimes two hours late at the planned 3:45 hours. The employees are just as annoyed as the travelers because they can't help the chaos. The current railway boss and the former railway bosses as well as a former transport minister are responsible, who wanted to take the railway on the stock exchange and saved money to do so.

Riding the D-Bahn is like riding a bike without handlebars. You don't know if or when you'll arrive. But one thing is certain: in the end it just hurts. Deutsche Bahn, a company that should have been gotten rid of years ago. But as you know, something new can only emerge from rubble.

Bad experience with Deutsche Bahn! But I had already heard negative experiences from relatives. After spending a few days with classmates and two teachers in Copenhagen, we were supposed to change trains in Hamburg central station. At first it only showed that the train was late. Then it showed that the stop in Hamburg Hbf was no longer necessary and therefore meant that we had to take the S-Bahn to Hamburg Harburg. It should be mentioned that time was short and we had to run in Harburg! That was stressful, especially for a school class! When we got to the track, we had to change tracks again and luckily we managed to get on the train. Yes, then there was a delay during the journey. Some things can't be avoided, but I found Deutsche Bahn's communication to be very poor!
What happened to punklichkeit?Absolut s...s...Delays between 50 - 100 minutes.Nobody at DB gives a f...Rent a car!!!

A big debacle! 1st class ticket + seat reservation from Düsseldorf to Oberstdorf. Train wagon from just after the war, air conditioning defective (33 degrees in the wagon), no luggage space, no dining car (checked in advance!) toilets clogged, doors closed after the locomotive was changed without first disconnecting the compressed air pipes, with a few exceptions, very unfriendly and rude staff! Return journey a week later on the same train, still no functioning air conditioning, clogged toilets and to top it all off, brakes that jammed and the fire alarm was activated... not a single employee on the train to lend a helping hand... panic, chaos and just figure out how to get home... DB is in financial ruin with 20,000 vacancies that they cannot fill!!! Advirs

To anyone unlucky enough to be forced to take German rail, plan ahead and leave plenty of “padding” in your timetable. We took/tried to take 3 trains in the last 16 days. One was cancelled outright; one 3 hours late, and the third sent us to a wrong track via announcement and App. When we finally got on the right train we were lucky not to be turned away like other passengers, because the train was missing six compartments due to “faulty planning.”Deutsche Bahn used to be the pride of the nation; now it is the shame of the nation! Truly abysmal!

Today on the IC from Hamburg to Zurich. The train was held up several times, and shortly before Basel we were informed that it would not go to Zurich due to the long delay and that everyone would have to get off in Basel Bad...no more DB!
All the trains were late, the DB app indicated the wrong platforms for trains and a lot of trains were stopped for repairs halfway through a journey.

I don't know what to say.  I was in Germany for Euro 2024.  The good - I took two night trains with DB and the service was wonderful, like being 1st class on a plane.  Plus the price was low having booked well in advance.  I also took several regional trains.The bad - the Customer Service.  You write in English to DB - you get a reply after months.  You write in Google translated German - you get a reply after a fortnight.  That is far too late for customers trying to book trains.My two night trains involved a change.  The train was shown on the platform notice board then disappeared.  No announcement.  After half an hour the train popped back onto the board and I caught it - but several passengers had wandered off and presumably missed their train.On two occasions in Gelenskirchen and in Dusseldorf every single train was late and it was a nightmare deciding which to take.DB - sort out the Customer Service!

Very bad service. I bought a ticket from Frankfurt to Copenhagen and it canceled after that, while when I check again the journey still run as normal and there's no cancellation. Tried to make phone calls and emails in every possibilities that I can but no replies. So because of they cancel it I might have to buy a new ticket with double price, regarding the same journey with the exact train??

1st class and a five and a half journey from Berlin to Garmisch-Partenkirchen with my dog. I follow the train map and board carriage 29 at the far end of the train. After five minutes a lady appears insisting she is in my seat. The screen in the carriage states 29. After a few minutes an announcement is made that says the carriages were labelled incorrectly and that passengers will have to move. I had to put my things away and rush the length of the train (16 carriages!)  along the platform. No apology from the train staff! I sit in my seat and go online to order food. 90% of the vast menu is unavailable, so I order a croissant and coffee. 1 hour later, my order has not arrived or been confirmed. There is no guard in sight and I had not seen her since five minutes after departure when she checked my ticket. I order again in case there was an error. The site says my order will be confirmed within 15 minutes.  Half an hour later and nothing. The guard comes through offering a complimentary biscuit. I ask about my order and she shrugs her shoulders and says there are two people working in the buffet car. I ask to order from her and she tells me I can go to the buffet car with my dog (not quite what DB say about ordering online or from a member of staff when in first class). Deutsch Bahn used to be known for good service and efficiency. What a joke! You should be ashamed of yourselves. Do you not have conscience about charging a lot of money for crap service? Aside from the service, the seat was comfortable with good leg room. Don't bother believing the sales pitch about onboard catering and service. Either eat well before travelling or bring a takeaway onboard. The staff behave like they are mightier than thou and don't have a clue about being polite or providing good service

Totally stupid. Trains are late 99% of the time. Often half an hour or even a whole hour. Often a train is canceled too. When there was flooding, a replacement bus was ordered for us on the way back, but it NEVER came. And then you get a voucher that doesn't work as compensation. Cobtactician sword too.

Huge delays occurring every time I used their 'services'. The trips are severly overpriced. The booking system is not working adequately. You freeze in the DB trains since the AC is turned on to maximum even when there are 16 degrees outside. The staff is very rigid and unable to adapt.DB is among the worst transportation companies in the world. Far worst then those from Eastern Europe.

Deutschebahn are an absolute joke, the trains are constantly late if the come at all, only 1.5 hours late for work today!. From now on I'll cycle the 20km because it's quicker than DB and more reliable

Unfortunately, it is the case today that you cannot take the DB under any circumstances if you are somehow dependent on arriving on time (planned with a 2-hour safety buffer!!!). Unfortunately, you're stupid enough to try again every two years only to be disappointed every time. I hope I last 3 or 4 years until the next attempt.

Our family of 4 boarded DB train from Prague to Dresden on June 21 st, 2024. We were soon to discover that there was no Carriage 254 and that we thus have no designated seats. Our group was split up and we were constantly chases off by other seat- assigned passengers. I will  try not to use DB again!!

We boarded EC 176 between Prague and Dresden, only to discover there to be no carriage 254. This left us stranded with no designated seats; splitt- up and being chased-off by seat assigned passengers as they got on.No apology, no assistance from staff to help us find new seats. I will try to avoid DB in future!

I've been driving the same Dresden-Zittau route every day for two years. I don't want to lie but at least every 3 trains are over 5 minutes late. Just ridiculous and a disgrace. And for 50€ I'm not even allowed to take a bike with me. Unbelievable. A construction site is extended by 5 months without explanation and is then not even finished on the specified date. Of course that too without explanation. (Ottendorf Okrilla-Königsbrück) It's sad that people are just watching and these idiots haven't been completely dispossessed long ago.

A nightmare. No train is ever on time. All coincidences are always lost. You must always allow for an hour's delay on short routes. On the long ones the delays are two, three, four hours. Perhaps the worst operator in the world. But aren't the managers ashamed?!?

It took me 3 different trains to do 60 km. All tree were late, and the first one got stuck for half an hour on a rail crossing and then stopped for for 15 minutes in the middle of nowhere. 2 of the trains I had to take were suppressed so I had to find an alternative and almost lost my flight even thought I planned my trip with a lot of spare time to be sure I don't have problems. All the trains are dirty and the S bans are even worse.

We travelled twice with the DB in the past two months:Once St Gallen (CH) to Vienna (booked 1st class), but the DB decided (without giving information) to cancel the train Munich to Vienna.  So we had to go via Salzburg arriving about 3 hours later than expected.  Our reservation of course was void and we had to take pot luck to find a seat in the overcrowded train!  We asked for a fare reduction but were told the train Munich to Vienna was "only" 2 hours late - so no refund! The return was also delayed about 2 hours.The second bad experience was a booking from Basel to Antwerp (again 1st class).  The train got as far as Cologne and we has to transfer to a bus (a regular uncomfortable bus - not a coach).  This bus ride lasted about 3 hours (non-stop) to Liege from where we could catch a train to Brussels.  The purpose of the trip was to attend a theatre festival - but we got in so late that we missed the first night of the festival completely.

Since I lice here, I've been using DB since childhood. Let me tell you, it's a horrible company.They are never on time, they cancel trips without telling you, without providing an alternative, you pay for the alternative then you still get fined cause you entered the wrong part of the train, the personal is unfriendly, they are CONSTANTLY demonstrating, which will lead to you not having access to public transport constantly, FOR YEARS.I'll probably start trying Uber etc, at least it's alot more reliable and goensrly not much more expensive.DB does not hold back from charging you 150 euro for a single station,bbe aware.

The train is over 3 hours late, I accidentally took out an annual subscription for a Bahncard which cannot be canceled. I've never been on time by train in my life. And should I agree to that now with the Bahncard? I wanted to cancel the Bahncard 2 weeks before it started, on the day I received the invoice for it. it does not work! In my opinion, this is not legal. But you have to get the money somehow, right? The same picture on all rating platforms. But unfortunately there are few alternative options in Germany. But you and your company ensure that people prefer to fly short-haul rather than travel with you.

The worst service in the world. Point 1, we were traveling from Frankfurt to Nuremberg, the canceled train told us to take any train, we took one and it was cheap for 2 hours at a station!!!! Point 2 trip from Amsterdam to Frankfurt ice105 paid for my seat for the most expensive ticket of the entire vacation. The car is not on the train, they tell us to choose any one and at the first stop people get on who need a seat. We had to separate with all the luggage, no one gives us solutions and they tell us that starting in Colonia, our car is almost arriving at its destination!!!! They are bad born. The worst company in the world! Never see this shit!!!

We used the train for several trips and found them to be clean and pleasant.  One of our trains was more than an hour late, but there were regular updates and one could rebook if desired. Would travel with DB again.
Cruel, it can't always be worse. The train is coming, just not to you. And if at some point or not at all. If you want to miss everything in life then book the train.

Worst transport ever. The word punctuality is unfamiliar to them. I have used it several times but I have never ever reached on time. Several times the train was cancelled or I was stuck somewhere on the way for 1-2 hours.

Dear ladies and gentlemen of Deutsche Bahn, I am writing to you to express my great dissatisfaction with your service. Unfortunately, in my experience I can only give 1 out of 5 stars. My main criticism is the unpunctuality of your trains. It is extremely frustrating that delays have become the norm at Deutsche Bahn. This not only affects my plans, but also those of many other passengers who rely on reliable transport. Added to this is the condition of your trains, which often leaves something to be desired. The cleanliness and maintenance are in many cases poor, which further detracts from the travel experience. Given that Deutsche Bahn is a central part of the public transport system in Germany, I find it shocking that such problems persist. It is particularly disappointing given that the German government is committed to a "green future" and that public transport should play a key role in this. I urgently appeal to you to take measures to improve the reliability and quality of your service. It is high time for Deutsche Bahn to live up to its obligations to passengers and meet the expectations of modern, efficient and environmentally friendly transport. Kind regards, T. Mujkanovic

So far, only once in my many journeys by train have I traveled exactly according to the timetable. The train was passing through. Today it should have been like that again. The ICE didn't run at all, it was completely canceled. It's nice that the information comes so promptly (sarcasm). Now you can select a new connection, said and done. This ICE619, also towards Munich, is currently 80 minutes overdue. I'm now stuck in Münster and I'm excited to see how much more time I have left. The announcements with dozens of delayed trains alone show the dire conditions at the DB. The planned trip in the afternoon turns into a fiasco. Normally I would be at my destination by now and comfortably on the sofa. Instead at the cold train station and wait in vain. The next scheduled train is a few minutes after 1 o'clock. The railway will therefore ensure that I exchange the electric car for a diesel...

Almost never on time, WiFi is non existing or not working and the list goes on...No rights whatsoever if the trains don't arrive or show up very late, if you have the Deutschlandticket. Thank you for nothing.

Worse journey ever and very very bad service! I live in Germany and 80% from my time driving with DB is a Katastrophe! I had to visit my family, it was a big event with my niece and we had hours of delay. We asked a DB worker  about some matters (our wagon was missing where we hat our seats) and he just yelled at us and say we should drive with something else) . So unrespectful people! No help, no sorry! They don’t deserve having a job. All my family plans were ruined. DB pretends they don’t have money to do this and that, but why do we have to pay that much the tickets if we get such a bad service? That’s not fair! We have families, we have lives, we can’t have our plans ruined so often because of them! Too bad we don’t have many options when is about long journeys to drive. And very sad we are not heard and not respected. 😒
It's just unbelievable and Deutsche Bahn should be ashamed! Unfortunately you have to give one star, but that's still too much!!

Deutsche Bahn is probably the worst company in Germany and an absolute joke. The punctuality is abysmal and the communication is simply not worth mentioning. They either say nothing at all or lie to the customers. In 90% of all trips I took in 2023/2024, I either didn't arrive at all (train cancellation + trip interrupted) or at least 30 or more minutes late. Unfortunately, nowadays delays of up to 20 minutes have to be considered punctual. In my experience, the railway is absolutely vulnerable, especially on the Munich - Berlin route. Every time I have to travel on this connection, I dread it. And while people still show understanding for reasons such as people on the tracks or flooding, other reasons are simply ridiculous. The best reason for being late I've ever heard was "...delay because the conductor is behind us on the train and therefore can't start the shift"... wtf. I can only advise everyone to give this company a wide berth and switch to alternative means of transport, even if it is unfortunately less environmentally friendly. At least then you have the fate in your own hands to arrive on time.

I went on a big trip in October 2023: in the first part I went from Düsseldorf with the ICE via Cologne to Brussels and then with the TGV to the airport in Paris Charles De Gaulle, then by plane from Paris via Muscat (Oman) to Dubai, then via Manama (Bahrain) to Singapore, after a few days of course again by plane from Singapore via Abu Dhabi to London, and then with the low-cost airline back to Düsseldorf. Why do I start all this like this? Because I did half a trip around the world, and to my surprise only one part didn't work: the first and apparently easiest and shortest part - the one with the German train! More precisely from Düsseldorf HBF to Cologne HBF - travel time about 25 minutes on the ICE - 10 minutes late on departure, another 25 minutes during the journey... ultimately my connection to Brussels MIDI was no longer possible. The train was gone, I had to wait 2 hours for the next ICE to Brussels, of which I was then allowed to wait 80 minutes in the service center in Cologne HBF for a new ticket WITHOUT my SEAT RESERVATIONS (booked through to Paris). As I said, I wanted to travel on the connections exactly as planned and paid for in the DB travel plan. The journey from Cologne to Brussels on the later ICE was fine, great train, great staff in the restaurant car (I only found a seat here), halfway on time, but there were no chilled drinks or food available. When I arrived in Brussels, the onward journey to Paris to Charles de Gaulle Airport with the later French TGV trains went smoothly (except that I didn't have a seat, which was gone due to the delay between Düsseldorf and Cologne); despite the 2 hour delay, I was still able to catch my flight to Muscat/Oman/Manama/Singapore etc. with a lot of racing and a high pulse and the great handling at the check-in counter in Paris. But the story doesn't end here, or it's not over yet: according to European law, I am entitled to compensation; The DB paid back the share ONLY to Belgium, the SNCF refuses to pay me a cent because it is all the DB's fault; After all, the train I originally booked from Brussels to Paris left on time, as did the subsequent connection that I had to take. It's now 2:2: 2 cancellations from DB, 2 cancellations from SNCF, and I'm the stupid one because I only received a fraction of the money. To be continued.... DB: what a disappointment - you can be late, even though in my case it was really tight and I would have missed a lot of flights and hotel bookings.....but asking me to get my refund here because of the over 2 hours and leaving me alone with the problem is real pathetic. Really bitter.

still trying to get reimbursed for a train that was cancelled in february. We re in june. They are trying to make me abandon and move on so they dont have to reimburse me. The customer service is a joke. The lady on the phone i had after 25 mins of waiting was sarcastical. Horrible horrible experience

As expected, the trip with Deutsche Bahn was full of disappointments and delays. The first train was already 13 minutes late, the journey hadn't even started yet, and the connecting train was a good 25 minutes late. Unfortunately, planning is a matter of luck on the railway. And great disappointment is inevitable. As always, unsatisfactory.

Buyer beware.  I read many articles before I left about DB and the need to stamp tickets.  However, not all tickets require a stamp and it’s not always clear when a stamp is required. Now I can hear from some people again what an environmental pig I am because I have to start my engine and that's only because there is a lack of incompetence and a lack of thinking at DB.
We can only advise everyone to drive. Train cancellations that are announced a quarter of an hour in advance and no information about what will happen next. Developing country Germany

What an amazing way to move between cities.  Worth the upgrade to first class(not pricey when booked in advice) to have a reserved seat.  Handed out chocolate.  Great views of countryside, clean and timely.  Overall pleasant experience.

DB gives world’s third class services. trains are never on time and always there is repairing work and always train cancellations. Government takes lots of money and does nothing. One of the shitties service always. For long journeys seats are not comfortable but prices are very nice and expensive for no reason.

It used to be the best company but lately the WORST in Europe. Frequent delays and cancellations of trains. Dirty trains with broken toilets. UNACCEPTABLE on a 3-4 hour trip that the toilets don't work in May. In September we paid for 4 seats from Copenhagen to Hamburg but the specific carriage was closed and we move from carriage to carriage without seats because they were reserved by other passengers at each station. There is no staff to help. But even now there is still dirt everywhere and broken toilets

So the DB can ruin your travel by train. Trip Linz Dresden. Everything went smoothly until Nuremberg except for the delay of >40 minutes. In Nuremberg we were asked to leave the train and change to another train on a different platform but with the same train number and carriage numbers because the original one was going back to Vienna! (you can understand it, but you don't have to) After we were undeterred, we were informed over the loudspeaker that this train was broken and we had to leave it again. When I asked a German railway service employee the succinct answer was "I don't know that either"! Ok, so off to the service center, a suitable train was found, but we were informed that it was completely overcrowded and our seat reservation was not valid! After a few carriages we finally found two separate seats. Result over 2 hours later, fought over and arrived in Dresden not relaxed. Riding the train is no fun. Next time by car!!

A sad end to an otherwise good journey. The trip from Denmark to Lübeck went well, despite the strike and uncertainty along the way as to how we got on. The journey home, where the strike was over, turned out to be even more uncertain and full of obstacles, in the form of canceled trains and rude staff

Unfortunately, the DB has declined significantly and it is now more of an imposition to travel long-distance with the DB than a joy. Either the ICE is late and you don't catch the connecting train, or you are on time and the connecting train is cancelled. Every time I have delays of around 2 hours on a journey of around 500 km. My patience is slowly running out. I think we as customers should go on strike because we shouldn't be satisfied with such "service". It's a shame that the DB doesn't have enough competition.

For God's sake, if you want to get to your destination then walk rather than take the DB. Hopefully I will never use this company's public transport service again. However, if you are homeless and would like to spend 1 night at the same train station then that's fine because with the DB you are already a few hours before you have to move on

I went on a cycling holiday in Germany with my partner. We traveled the return journey with the DB. Unfortunately, I accidentally didn't book a bike ticket (but reserved a spot in the bike compartment). Fine 163.40 euros!!!! The normal price for taking a bike is around 20 euros. Totally disproportionate for a mistake in booking!!!!! And twice. I will never travel with DB again, anti-social behavior on the part of DB!!!
Unfortunately, I wasn't able to take my train journey last weekend due to the weather. I applied for a refund of the tickets via the train app and the money was already in my account today.

Hotel booked from Monday to Friday. On Thursday my return trip was canceled due to a strike. Nevertheless, a connection was found with the regional train, which took an hour longer. At the first station there was a technical defect, the light went out, everyone was sitting in the dark and then it was said (about 30 minutes later) that the train was canceled due to a technical defect. Therefore, I will no longer take the train as far as possible and I will also advise against it. This is a disgrace for the German economy or service is simply embarrassing.

I traveled from Ingelheim to Cologne on the Middle Rhine Railway. You expect a nice travel experience. But the condition of the railway was deplorable. Dirt everywhere, sticky floors, dirty and flooded toilets, no toilet paper, paper and used tissues on the floor. A horror. Then another quarter of an hour late. Is that the special experience?
Do not use DB for any time dependent trips and do not use DB as an elderly person. It is frightening to see the level of incompetence and carelessness in this organisation.

We only stayed two days in Munich and unfortunately we used DB to get in and out of the city. For the first trip we took a train from Venice to Munich. We arrived on Dec 5th and we were informed that the train wouldn’t be able to go to Munich direct due to snow and we have to change trains in Salzburg. We did so but the DB train only went to Rosenheim. We were stranded there and they told us they had no ETA on when we can get on train to go to Munich. We ended up getting a taxi after three hours waiting. The second time we tried to go to Strasbourg from Munich. We had only one transfer and we paid more for the ICE. The train left on time but for no reason it was delayed 22 minutes and we missed our connection. We ended up changing four trains and again arrived two hours late at our destination. This is unacceptable and I don’t understand why they are still operating. Maybe Germany should go back to riding horses and donkeys instead of operating trains that is so complicated for them.

The reliability of the trains we took leaving and returning from Munich was bad. Admittedly snow caused much disruption on one day. But the worst was a strike causing our train to be cancelled. Strike was declared with only 24 hours notice. We could of risked it as a few trains were still scheduled to run but we could of ended up stranded. So we had to leave a day early. Unfortunately this is not our first experience of bad service- last year we were stuck on a train for 6 hours due to problems with signalling.Too stressful and risky to try using them again as part of our holiday arrangements.
Miserable. I can't think of anything else about it. I rarely catch a connecting train or the trains simply don't run.

Worst transport company I know. Even in Africa the trains run more punctually! I've arrived far too late so many times. I've never reached my destination on time. Entire carriages on the ICE are suddenly canceled even though all seats are reserved. I wonder how Germany is supposed to govern the EU as the strongest power when they don't even have public transport under control?!

I travel longer distances by train several times a month. I only book first class. 2nd class is no longer bearable. With very few exceptions, all of my trips in December alone have been significantly delayed. It is constant chaos, wagons and seat reservations are missing, trains are canceled and subsequent trains are extremely overcrowded. I use a rental car or plane more and more often.

Die DB - eine Schande für Deutschland und Europa - Menschentransport auf Zuchtviehniveau...Anspruch und Wirklichkeit bei der Deutschen Bahn am 1. Dezember 2023:Gekauftes Ticket : DNR : GVKPGHN ID3 – Nürnberg nach Luxemburg10:00 Nürnberg Hbf – 12:04 Frankfurt-Main Hbf – ICE 724 - 1.Klasse – Sitz 6212:56 Frankfurt Hbf – 15:02 Saarbrücken Hbf – TGV 9552 – 1. Klasse – Sitz 5315:15 Saarbrücken Hbf –  16:30 Luxemburg Hbf – Bus 131Preis 111,70 € inclusive reservierten Sitzplätzen im ICE und TGVDie gleiche Strecke von 450 km bin ich am Vortag mit einem Wohnmobil hingefahren und habe dafür 5 ½ Stunden benötigt.Und das hat die DB mir am 1.12.2023 gebotenStrecke Nürnberg – Frankfurt verlief normal – 10 Minuten Verspätung – alles gut.5 Minuten vor Abfahrt in Frankfurt wurde ich informiert, dass der TGV nicht in Saarbrücken halten würde – wegen Streiks.Ich wurde umgebucht – musste eine weitere Stunde warten bis es mit dem ICE 228  um 13:42 nach Koblenz ging. (Am Rande bemerkt – mein erster Zug wäre ebenfalls nach Koblenz gefahren)Der Zug nach Koblenz war überbucht und so voll, dass viele Reisende zwischen und in den Abteilen stehen mussten. Ich musste während der gesamten Fahrt, also fast zwei Stunden stehen bis der Zug mit 25 Minuten Verspätung in Koblenz ankam. Mein Anschlusszug (RE1- 5106) von Koblenz nach Luxemburg war bereits abgefahren – dachte ich.Am Infodesk wurde mir gesagt, dass alle Züge nach Luxemburg bis auf weiteres ausfallen würden, wegen Problemen an den Gleisen.Ich wurde zum Busbahnhof geschickt und sollte dort in den H-Bus nach Kobern-Gondorf einsteigen. Wie es danach weitergehen sollte und wann ich zu Hause sein würde konnte ab dem Zeitpunkt niemand mehr beantworten. Ab da hatte ich jegliche Orientierung verloren und eine Kommunikation mit der DB war während der gesamten Reise inexistent. Der DB-Mitarbeiter am Bus sagte als ich Fragen stellte: “Sie steigen besser ein, es sind nur noch 3 Plätze frei, sonst bleiben Sie hier stehen!”20-30 Minuten später mussten wir in Kobern-Gondorf wieder auf einen Bummelzug nach Bullay umsteigen. Am Bahnhof in Kobern-Gondorf warteten bereits hunderte Menschen auf unsere Busse um ihrerseits nach Koblenz gebracht zu werden. Die Strecke Luxemburg – Koblenz war ja ebenfalls gesperrt. Alle Menschen waren sehr aufgebracht, gestresst und die allermeisten hatten keine Ahnung was gerade passierte und wie es weiter gehen sollte. Informationen gab es keine!In Bullay war Endstation – alle Reisende mussten aussteigen (dank google maps wusste ich zumindest in etwa wo ich unterwegs war und konnte somit die verbleibende Strecke einschätzen).Überall fragende und ahnungslose Gesichter – was passiert jetzt, wie geht es weiter? Jeder lief dem Vordermann hinterher – viele Reisende kamen vom Frankfurter Flughafen und hatten Fluggepäck dabei – es gab in Bullay weder Rolltreppen noch Lifte. Auch die älteren Menschen mussten die schweren Reisekoffer die vielen Treppen von den Gleisen zum Busbahnhof runter und wieder hochschleppen. Da standen wir am Busbahnhof und niemand wusste was kommt – niemand war vor Ort den man hätte fragen können. Nach 15 Minuten in eisiger Kälte kam ein Bus mit der Aufschrift Trier. Was sich im Anschluss im Bus abspielte ist mit Worten nicht zu beschreiben. Die Leute drängten und schubsten und die allermeisten hatten sperriges Reisegepäck dabei, für das im normalen Linienbus überhaupt kein Platz war. Ein Flugkoffer im Mittelgang versperrte das Durchkommen nach hinten, Stau im Bus, der Busfahrer schrie – “Geht weiter durch nach hinten”! Das ältere Ehepaar war aber zu schwach um den großen Reisekoffer kurz hoch zu heben – ich übernahm dies, damit alle Menschen weiter nach hinten durchgehen konnten. Viele mussten während der darauffolgenden fast zweistündigen sehr kurvenreichen Fahrt an der Mosel entlang, hoch nach Wittlich, über Schweich bis nach Trier – im Bus stehen, überall standen riesen Gepäckteile, die Menschen hatten ihre Koffer auf dem Schoß oder zu Viert über den Knien liegend. Der Bus fuhr zügig die zahlreichen Kurven an der Mosel entlang, viele Menschen beklagten sich über Übelkeit. Alle Menschen an Bord dieses Busses beklagten sich über die unmenschlichen Zustände, über das Versagen der Deutschen Bahn in jeglicher Hinsicht. Die DB verkauft den Leuten eine Dienstleistung, welche so niemals stattfindet, die DB nimmt reichlich Geld für diese Dienstleistung und was liefert die DB in Wirklichkeit. Wie entschädigt die DB die Fahrgäste für dieses Versagen und die entstandenen Unannehmlichkeiten. Eine ältere Dame hinter mir kam aus Österreich, war seit über 12 Stunden unterwegs und war in Trier zu einem jährlichen Familientreffen eingeladen. Sie kam dort nicht rechtzeitig an.Es waren keine zufriedenen in sich ruhenden, reisenden Menschen mehr, es waren von A nach B transportierte Menschen. Das Bild vom Viehtransport schlich mehr als einmal durch meine Gedanken, es war in vielerlei Hinsicht ein Transportieren von Menschen unter Zuchtviehniveau, welche laut neuesten EU Regeln nun endlich auch mehr Rechte haben. So manche Kuh wird im LKW mehr Platz zur Verfügung haben, wie die Menschen die am 1. Dezember 2023 ihr Vertrauen und ihr Geld in die Hände der Deutschen Bahn gelegt hatten. Die DB ist eine wahre Katastrophe! Ihr schlechter Ruf geht zu Recht weit über die deutschen Grenzen hinaus. Ich war 12 Stunden unterwegs für knappe 400 km – meine Frau hat mich letztendlich mit dem Auto in Trier (100 km) abgeholt.Ist dies der viel gelobte öffentliche Transport ? Da lobe ich mir doch mein eigenes Auto. Danke für diese für mich gewinnbringende Erfahrung.

15-20 years ago the Deutsche Bahn (DB) used to be one of the best in Europe - fast trains, high frequency, good on-board service. But a great infrastructure requires regular on-going investment in maintenance and repair. This didn't happen and right now trains have to pass so much track repair work that few trains get to their destination on time. I recently travelled from Cologne to Salzburg. We arrived 60 minutes late in Munich where I of course missed my connection. Furthermore, track work between Munich and Salzburg resulted in many trains being cancelled and the one I eventually managed to get clocked up a 45-minute delay on a trip that should have taken 90 minutes. Even more infuriating: as I missed by booked connection I had to purchase another ticket. You have been warned.

We left a bag on a train and have gotten zero help from Deutsche Bahn. Yes it's our fault for leaving it on the train. We fortunately have it airtagged. It's been sitting in their train depot for three days now. We've done what they have asked and filed a report however they can not tell us when we can get the bag yet. There is no phone number for the depot, they don't know anyone who works in the depot, they just drop off the bags randomly. There is no one taking initiative or helping us in any sort of way. We can't be the first person to leave their bag on a train, there should be a system. At this point it feels like they have stolen our bag and the items in it for themselves. I don't have anything good to say about the company nor the people that work there.

An absolute disaster, people on the ground, drunk passengers messing with people, alcohol, drugs, a shame. The reviewers do nothing, it seems like the third world. Better not to take the train in Germany
Delay is part of the agenda, misinformation and excuses as well as compensation?? None!
I can't believe this exists!!! How I missed the NMBS. :) Taking Eurostar, not DB, will save you a lot of misery.

Delays, constant train cancellations, like today again. Disastrous German railway!!! Now we will switch back to our car! So much for the government's call that everyone should make a contribution to climate protection and, for example, take the train instead of a car...

Very bad! I bought my ticket two weeks before the trip. Without notification, my ICE train for the outward journey (Nuremberg-Frankfurt) simply disappeared. I only found out at the train station... standing in a queue, no seats for later trains, 1 hour later I was able to leave. The train back to Nbg was also canceled...a mess!!

On Sunday 11/26 we made a trip from Munich to Salzburg. According to what they said, due to road works, we had to take a bus to cover the sections under construction. It took us about 2.30 on the way out but almost 5 hours on the way back for 145km. And on the way back they canceled the train in Salzurgo and made us go by bus, but instead of taking a direct trip to Munich, they made us go to Worgl in Austria and from there, in theory, a train to Munich. But in reality they made us get off in Rosenheim because that train, which DB listed in the app, was an Austrian train. In Rosenheim we had to take another train to Munich which, of course, was half an hour late. A scandal!

I have booked a group tour. Unfortunately I now have Corona and I tried to change the name on the ticket. This is not possible. I was recommended to just get on the train with Corona. The illness wouldn't be so bad anymore. Alternatively, the group has to cancel completely. Here a company has absolutely not understood the situation. But complain about the lack of sick employees in public. What madness.

What a nightmare!! do not book first class with these guys, if the train you're catching broke down!! you will have to catch another train and  you will have to fight to get a seat, they won't refund you the extra money for first class tickets as they said its too late to cancel, after all its their faults for the broken train, it happened twice while we were here in Germany. should  have read all the reviews before we booked with them!! terrible customer service as well.. we were told to go and find an emty seat, and there were none as you got into the train. what a terrible experience, especially not in Germany, with their reputation of great minds, engineers etc..I think it's not a good reflection on Germany, esp with DB as they are international companies.STILL.we had the  worst experience with their broken-down trains. we still love Germany, just not DB trains

What a joke. Our trip with them started 45 minutes late, and somehow they managed to lose another hour on the trip from cologne to Brussels. Must have been really behind, cause they just ended the service 2 stops early and told us to take another train to the station we booked our trip to. We ended up about 2 hours behind, and missed our next train to London. Very frustrating. The employees were pretty rude about the whole thing to boot. I’d avoid this company if possible.

Last one year I have taken DB thrice.  All three times major problems.  The one I took today (nov 2023) has problems in changing from the Dutch power lines to the German ones at the border - so we are stranded for 2 hrs and need to take a local train thereafter!!!  I am amazed how every journey somehow becomes 2x to 4x longer when I travel with DB. I suppose there is no accountability mechanism.  Very sad state on German railways

As always, a disastrous experience. Trains are constantly canceled and late. It is always astonishing how boldly the German railway treats paying customers and in this way shamelessly exploits its own monopoly position.

WARNING!!!!!!!!!!!! Dont buy a Deutsche ticket after the 10th of every month. If you buy it on the 11th then you will have to pay for the next month too. You can't cancel anymore. This is totally stupid but thats how it works.
Unfortunately, unorganized, no proper communication, disastrous delays, running back and forth is typical for passengers, changing tracks at the last minute is also the epitome. Hope it gets better.

The trip it with Deutschlandticket was nice.  But the DB customer service is terrible .and the ABO team dishonest. We bought an ABO in the beginning of August. Cancelled it for August 31st. I sent several mails, no answer what so ever but received 2 letters threatening me of reporting me to a debt collection company if didn't pay before the next day. Still no answer and no money back. This ABO team is a catastrophe and a great shame for the Deutsche Bahn and the Deutschlandticket.

Shameful! At midnight only 5 students and us 2 teachers on the platform waiting for the train with the sign Bad Harzburg! The train doesn't even arrive before we get close and leaves after a minute!!!!! With the driver also making strange signs!!! Shame on you
12 hours for 422 km (Dresden-Rostock) corresponds to 38.5 km/h. The Germany Ticket is really fun.

They don't even bother to hide the fact that the DB passenger is passing by the ass. On the way from Saarbrücken to Krefeld to a funeral, the ridiculous chaos began! In Neudtadt we had to stop for 30 minutes because a signal box employee had to take his break. Consequence: missed connection to Mannheim. Replacement train drove to Frankfurt Airport.  There we were told we couldn't continue because the look guide wasn't coming and nobody knew when. On the recommendation of the train driver, everyone changed to another train, which in turn could not leave due to overcrowding. We had to take a later train and arrived in Krefeld almost 3 hours late. It's just pathetic what this company does!

Deutsche Bahn is broken up into individual divisions. The boss should be paid based on punctuality, so he would finally understand the drama. Sprinter from Berlin to Munich takes six hours instead of four hours. Compensation: 0.00 euros. It is by far the worst company in Germany, but somehow typical of the decline of Europe's largest economy.

During a five-hour journey from Berlin to Düsseldorf for a hefty €130 in second class without a seat reservation, I didn't expect the ICE to be overcrowded. After standing tired for an hour and slowly getting shaky legs and back, I continued to desperately look for a place to sit. I decided to take a seat in first class, which wasn't much different from one in second class. This was not occupied and so I did not deny or take away this space from anyone. In general, the first class was 70% occupied. During the ticket check, I was then expelled from the seat like a serious criminal in a way that I don't want to describe. It is incredibly ridiculous to act like that as a service provider in such a case. I never want to travel with Deutsche Bahn again. Afterwards I sat on the exit step like a poor soul for 4 hours. For 130€ without any comfort and subsequent back pain. I know that there are price differences but why are more tickets sold than there are seats? Why isn't there a better concept? The outward journey with Flixtrain for €49 was extremely well organized, every booking gets its automatic seat. Always like this from now on!!

The Deutsche Bahn is without a doubt the biggest joke of a company that can be found in Germany. Train delays occur so frequently that you can deem yourself lucky if you only miss one connecting train  in a given ride. And it does not stop here, the user information is so poorly managed on every level. The app is frequently malfunctioning, not updating information on a train ride, the speakers in the trains themselves are often broken so that you do not even get to hear the information and the information on the screens on the stations does not update. As a customer you are left in the dark and left to your own devices, clueless about which train to take. If you dare to ask for help, you will most likely be met with a resentful employee sick of his job in this terrible company, which is reflected in his customer service.If you choose to take a train with the DB make sure so plan in double the time it would actually take.I hope this company gets taken away from the hands of the CEO and shareholders who with the way to expensive prices are doing NOTHING for the welfare of their customers.It's just a matter of time until a massive DB emplyee manhunt will be manifesting from the condensed hate of millions of furuius innocent people that are fooled by this company on a daily bases.Kind regards,Your average DB traveler

Absolutely horrible experiences on every single DB train throughout Europe. Excessive delays on every trip, most without any reason for the delay. Our most recent trip of 25 minutes was delayed for an hour and a half. We sat at a train station whilst people smoked but no other explanation as to why we were delayed. This level of unreliability would not be acceptable in most other countries. In the future I will avoid all DB trains and will be recommending other travellers do the same. There is a huge problem within this train company.

Disaster. Train cancellations, delays, running and falling all over the station with small children plus luggage and strollers to connecting trains and falling, getting injured, wagons and seats that you have booked that don't exist, rebookings that go wrong, double debits in the app where cancellations no longer work and where you still pay money to the company for a train service that was not provided, even though you have sued them, (payment processes and rebookings also do not work on the Internet or by email). App, waiting for hours in the travel center), My wife is traveling 11 hours into the night to Flensburg with delays and broken trains and is freezing in a cold train station with zero security in Neumünster and comes back from her further training with a bad cold, air conditioning broken and trains too hot in summer, too cold in winter, unfriendly staff, expensive, expensive, expensive and no longer a real environmentally friendly alternative to the flexible car, short-term strikes during the holiday season with children, No thanks, unfortunately it's better to drive on the highway again, which is harmful to the environment, but at least get to your destination. Germany You're done with Deutsche Bahn and climate protection!!! Last year and this year I was on the verge of a heart attack due to Deutsche Bahn stress. In Vietnam the trains are all on time!!!

A nightmare!!! We are a family with two children. We take the train from Stuttgart to Viareggio with changes in Munchen, Bologna and Prato. We arrive in Munich, the train is delayed and makes us miss the connection to Bologna. We go to the information office, they change the train for the next one that goes to Verona, assuring us (in bad faith because we asked twice) that there is a connection after 22 minutes for Bologna (except that there wasn't one) so in a chain of events we missed the other connections. In short, we explain the problem to the conductor on the train and he reassures us that they will give us an alternative route instead. Once we arrive in Verona we go to the information office and I won't tell you how (laughing and not caring) they told us that if we want (paying) we have to travel to Rome and then the next day take the train to Viareggio (10 more hours of travel).. of course we refused such an absurd solution. Meanwhile we had to pay for a hotel, wait until the next day to repay the rest of the journey, arriving the following day. Liars, incompetents and thieves. A nightmare journey is an understatement. Never again!!!

I am a long-term commuter (Freising-Bamberg, twice a week) and therefore a victim of Deutsche Bahn. I don't need to explain why here. This is probably self-explanatory. Millions of people in Germany suffer because of this "company" - because it does NOT fulfill its services, even though it is a monopoly position for them, while the state does not intervene due to excessive demands and failure. CONTINUOUS STRESS, NERVOUS BREAKS, lack of oxygen, lack of seating - and now the lack of hygiene on the trains is suddenly turning what is actually a beautiful life into hell for almost every passenger. All of this has health consequences. I myself have developed a fear of confined spaces since taking trains regularly. Often the trains are so full that there are five people sitting on the stairs. CHILDREN, SENIOR PEOPLE, hard-working professionals and general family/couple relationships suffer greatly! "Why isn't daddy coming home today?" A young mother was trying to calm her baby on a crowded train while pushing through the masses of passengers in the hallway to the nearest functioning toilet (almost all of them were broken). I would like to say that this stress not only has psychological and physical effects on people but also economic consequences. There should finally be a meaningful study about this huge problem that (in-)directly affects everyone in this country. Society would certainly benefit in an incredible number of ways from a strong and reliable public transport network.
Trains are usually always late or canceled. I can't believe how disorganized this company is, the incidence rate must be over 90%. Unreliable, I would recommend any other type of trip

Please don't take the German train, they won't do anything. I missed my Ice connection because the regional train arrived 30 minutes late. And there was a strike on my way there. Every time I drive there is always something. Whether it's a construction site or a delay in another train, it's getting on my nerves and I'm starting to get absolutely tired of it. Now I'm supposed to take any train I want, but every train that's coming is completely booked, from which I conclude that it will be completely full. Next time I'll think three times whether I don't drive 5 regions earlier to actually get my ice cream...

I usually really enjoy traveling by train. But now it's absolute torture. You can actually no longer rely on 85% of the trains. Be it SBahn or ICE... trains are constantly canceled or late anyway. You have to take all of this into account when booking. Unfortunately, the German railway stands for Germany at the moment... Totally going down the drain

Dortmund to Berlin Worst experience ever. The trip has been many times postponed.You can't take your money back, and you have to search for alternative with DBahn 😩It took around 6 hour instead of 3:30 hours, and they told us many times that the journey will end in Hanover and we have to manage our trip from Hanover to Berlin. I tried to tell the employee in the information that and she was not cooperative.I reached Berlin at 3:00 o'clock instead of 23:00 o'clock. My conference started at 8 o'clock so I didn't have time to sleep.Berlin to Dortmund As usual train came late and there was 107 Min delay.This time they offered us bavarages but that didn't change the fact that the DBahn sucks

In addition to constant delays and hours-long waiting times, my criticism is particularly directed at the often incorrect timetable notifications from Deutsche Bahn. On the way to Düsseldorf airport, this was consistently announced as the "next stop" via advertisements and announcements. Since I didn't know the location before, I followed the instructions and after getting out I realized that I was at the main train station there. When I realized my mistake, the train had literally left and since an hour and a half wait until the next possible onward journey would have put me in a time crunch, I decided to switch to the taxi and pay 30 € in tuition. On the way back, the expected regional express arrived almost an hour late, but on a completely different track than indicated on the notice board and in the DB app. Even without heavy luggage, it would be a quick change over five platforms was a sporting undertaking during the train's short stay. If you only see the rear lights of the last wagon, the timetable correction that then occurs has very limited value. After another three quarters of an hour, I was finally on the right train. Due to repairs to the rail network, the journey here has ended abruptly halfway through several previous trips, even though the sign previously indicated the home station as the destination and the respective construction site had already existed for a long time. We traveled throughout souther Germany exclusively by rail using the DeuthceBhan Rail Pass. We utilized the seven day pass for our travels. Overall we had a pleasant experience using the train v. Car. Looking at the intensity of the roads and drivers using them, I was so glad not to be in that anxiety ridden mix. A few things that seemed mysterious to us before we arrived and I wish I knew ahead of time:We received the pass via mail from DB. It was a hard copy ticket that had seven blank—fill in dates printed on it. You fill it out once you arrive and have a train travel date. So let’s say you are in Germany and you want to travel on the train that day. You simply use an ink pen and fill in the date on your ticket and have that in your possession when on the train. There is no validating the ticket or anything you need to do before boarding. You just hop on your train. A conductor may or may not come by and verify your ticket and date. You do not want to be caught without the ticket dated. This may result in a hefty fine and being booted off the train. The ticket can be used on all DB trains and most DB busses. It cannot be used on local busses and local light rail. It also cannot be used if crossing into Austria. Use the trip planner in the DB app to figure your route and check it often. Things change. Contrary to popular perception,  stuff happens and the trains can be late. They can also cancel stops. The nice thing about the app is that it will update real time. Check it often to avoid issues as you travel with connecting trains. Don’t hesitate to ask the DB staff for help. We found them all very helpful and all we spoke to knew English well.
