I can recommend the cleanliness of the trains, but it stops there!  If you are thinking of buying a Deutschland ticket , please BEWARE!  My husband and I visited family in  Germany from 22nd to 26th June and we paid online for a Deutschland tickets, during the booking process I mentioned that I needed the ticket for 4 days, but these tickets are issued for one month, so it was dated from 1st June.  During the booking process, there was no mention that you need to cancel the ticket by the 10th of the Month, or  you will be charged for the next month, which is exactly what happened to us.  I cancelled the ticket on 26th June using their online webform. I heard nothing, so I wrote many emails, and had no replies. Then I tried calling them.  I got through twice and each time I spoke to someone, they just put the phone down. Their customer service is APPALLING.   I paid for the June tickets and then had a demand for the July tickets, which I could not use as I was back in UK.  Now they have debt collectors after me, and I have already paid for June and July tickets. I have written to the debt collectors and tried to phone them , and no response.  Please think twice if you want to book with DeutscheBahn, I am so stressed as I cannot find out what is happening. Needless to say I won't be using their services again!

A single catastrophe! There was a 1.5 hour delay from Frankfurt to Bochum on two consecutive days. From Bochum to Frankfurt over 2 hours late. It's a total disaster. This company should voluntarily file for bankruptcy and poach managers from SBB. Just embarrassing.

We took trains from Frankfort to Mannheim, did several day trips from there, then another long-distance trip to Basel. The Frankfort train was delayed an hour, our day trips were plagued by delays and cancellations, and the Basel train was 80 minutes delayed and then cancelled! We had to wait 20-30 minutes at the ticket office to get rebooked, then they gave us the wrong car number, and suddenly announced that the train was stopping at a suburban station and we would have to drag ourselves and suitcases across 6 tracks to catch another train to the main terminal in Basel! There was never any explanations in either German or English or any offer of help. We have traveled in Germany numerous times and always had good experience with German Rail but this time was terrible. Equipment is not being kept in good repair, lack of communication is rampant, and  trains are no longer reliable. Will not be back.

Sept 23 a disaster month for any one, in Germany who so ever travelled by DB.Many delays for hours,cancellations,disruptions,poor info display making passengers stranded.Had bad and harrowing experience last week . Berlin to Hannover trains delayed. Hannover To Berlin stranded at Hannover hbf for oblver 2.5 hours and added is no proper and No info dissemination, communication.  DB app is silent. Added is most data in german.Same story on last Saturday Berlin to Erding. Sudden cancellation at munich Hbf. How-to connect or go further to erding ,none gives answers. Even their Railway officials clueless.Sorry not expected out of Such an advanced country as Germany. Learnt many more such incidents all over.

On the journey from Cologne to Berlin, after a long odyssey in Berlin, we arrived at the train station at 3:30 a.m. Exhausted, tired, frustrated. As a woman alone, I decided to take a taxi instead. Logically, many people had the same opinion as me. Hardly any taxis in front of the Berlin train station, but there is a long queue of passengers. It was predictable when a train that should have been there shortly after 00:00 a.m. at the latest only arrived at 3:30 a.m. with the passengers from a total of 2 trains (ours didn't run any further in Hanover, bad luck). What finally ends the barrel is the unbelievable arrogance on the part of the railway customer service today, my suggestion to give information from the train to the taxi headquarters in such a case as complete It's absurd to say that a lot is expected of us, too much! And that is not our fault, but that of German railways! To at least take up a small suggestion on my part, to dismiss it so arrogantly by saying how unworldly, devoid of any logic it would be and that common sense would say that this would be complete nonsense, is simply outrageous. The customer service employee was arrogant, unfriendly, rude, rude and didn't care if I complained.

Worst train I have ever seen. They are not able to cope with the demand at all. 3rd time in a row my train was canceled and then no alternatives for 6 hours. The train before mine and after mine was also cancelled. Apparently this is normal. I guess thanks to DB people will be driving cars for a while in Germany
Train canceled. Replacement of other platform. Difficult to make announcements. Seat reservation no longer valid. This means there is no longer a group. No more meetings possible

We traveled as a family sitting in the corridor due to lack of space even though we had a first class ticket. This same train arrived more than 5 hours late causing us to miss our connection. After complaining to the DB we obtained a reimbursement of €110 for the delay but nothing for the tickets that we had to repurchase to continue our trip, i.e. more than €400. I am scandalized and I advise against the DB

Hello, good afternoon, on December 15, I was traveling with my husband and 5-year-old daughter on the DB Cologne train to Amsterdam airport to finally take a plane to Spain. The train had an incident and we had to get off in Düsseldorf (11:15). The solution was to wait for the next train at 1:08 p.m. and change trains in Utrech, final destination at Amsterdam airport. With this incident we had very little time on the plane. Even so, the train left late so we missed the Utrech airport destination, so we were forced to spend 130 euros on a taxi from Utrech to the airport, arriving 50 minutes early at check-in, so they didn't let us check in the suitcases, so we missed the plane and had to get new tickets, hotel, etc. An approximate total cost of 1700 euros. Can anyone help us file a claim? Fatal, a disappointment. They haven't taken care

Unfortunately, I have to rely on the ICE for work. I can only say good things about the train attendants, both long-distance and local. Unfortunately, the rest of the DB is absolutely inadequate. Outdated technology (from before the Second World War), things are promised and not kept (e.g. reimbursement in the event of a delay: you have to fill out forms, pay the postage yourself, and even if you have proof that the train was 5 hours late, you only get a rejection with the reason: "Too many requests of this kind", or something like that.) If you accidentally buy the wrong ticket because the machine is crazy and you don't pay the fine straight away, you are threatened with debt collection proceedings DB takes legal action and collects double or triple the amount. Long story short: the infantry can't help it and are nice, the rest is a nightmare.

DB is absolutely the worst train company in whole of Europe ! The train are always late, if you have more than one connection you will never manage to take it and I have already multiple times ended my trip with >5hrs of delay and even had to take multiple night trains to get to my destination. The service is an absolute disgrace. I wanted to do something for the environment by taking the train...well DB is the single reason why I'm taking the plane again !I cannot emphase enough how badly this company is organised and operated. A real disgrace for Germany.
After 7 hours delay on my trip from NL to Switserand, after taking a taxi to reach my goal the same day it's really impossible to get my money back.

Really bad service. Journey from Berlin to Duisburg. Once we got on the train for a night journey of about 6 hours we noticed that on all the seats there was an acronym containing the word "reserviert", when reserving seats was not mandatory for those who, for example, like us, are traveling with an Interrail ticket. We tried to ask a lady from the staff for information, but we immediately understood that we couldn't use these seats when she said to the kids in front of us in German "you can't sit randomly wherever you want" and we got confirmation when, while they were heading towards the exit to change carriages, she stopped us asking if we had reserved seats, but upon our negative response she implied that there was no room for us in "her carriage" then. After wandering among the carriages for about ten minutes, with heavy and tired backpacks (in the same situation as many others), we took advantage of the opportunity to ask two girls from the staff we met while walking for information. Let me start by saying that my German is scholastic (in any case I get along well), because I am a native Italian speaker, but nevertheless I made an effort to ask them the question in their language, however the response I received was hasty and hasty, so much so that I had to ask them to repeat it. I had never done it, because after that conversation I, like many other girls present there, learned that the seats with the writing "GGF RESERVIERT" on them, declared unusable by the first employee, were instead free seats at our disposal and that the reserved ones were indicated differently. I would add that I am sure these were her statements because to be sure I then repeated everything to her in my own words in German and received confirmation. We then looked for a seat, but at that point the train was almost full and it took us a while. As we passed the 2 girls we had previously asked for information on our way, we noticed that they were looking at us shaking their heads as if in a sign of disapproval. Now, I admit that none of us knew the meaning of the writing (in German, not even in English) above ALL the seats on the train, but precisely for this reason we tried to find out, but obtained conflicting indications from staff members of the same company. However, the worst came after 30 minutes of travel, when one of us had to get up because, contrary to what we had been told, all the seats had the same wording so it was impossible to distinguish the reserved ones from the free ones and when a gentleman arrived and claimed his seat, my friend had to move. This is not a professional way to work. If we had received clear information straight away we would have had a peaceful trip and maybe we would have even been close, given that it is not the aspiration of all girls to travel abroad for 6 hours at night separated from their traveling companions. A truly terrible experience, rude and unprepared staff, I strongly advise against the company.

Our train from Berlin to Amsterdam IC240 broke down on 15 September in the town of Rheine in Germany, effectively the middle of nowhere. There was an announcement that everyone should leave the train followed by virtually no information about the remainder of the trip. Passengers were left to fend for themselves and staff were either non existent, or unable to provide information. Passengers started joining up in groups Survivor-style to try to find a way to their destinations. We joined forces with a nice chap from Florida and we eventually took a Hail Mary train back to the previous stop where we were able to board another IC to Amsterdam we here we eventually arrived a few hours late thereby missing a long-planned museum visit. We later learned other passengers had taken a series of regional trains criss-crossing the countryside. A complete debacle. I rated 2 stars because the onboard conductor was friendly at least up until we were ejected on to the platform in Rheine.

It wasn't just my train that was completely canceled. (Frankfurt - Basel) The following train was also more than 30 minutes late. From now on I will only fly in Germany. It's really embarrassing. At every stop the staff had to apologize over the loudspeaker, which just makes me feel sorry for working in a company that has completely run into the wall. No thanks, I won't spend another cent on the DB.

1 hour delay because no one could allow the train to continue its journey due to a lack of staff. 🤦‍♂️ Even in third country regions, such processes are automated. With the Germany Ticket, the juice shop was sunk even further into a nasty, desolate planned economy. My time is valuable, I am needed in my family and at work. Therefore: never take the train again!

We were already warned about the delays (from Salzburg to Düsseldorf over an hour with tickets rebooked in Munich!!!) The vegan dishes on the menu were very tempting but in the end we were only offered a wrap (could have been bought at Aldi)) And all of that in 1st class !!!!! Shame on you, it was really a joke

Absolutely unreliable!!! It is unbelievable how they even dare to call this a transportation company! ALL, I mean ALL of the connections have delays, or cancellation, or problems with the service... it is absolutely disrespectful and unprofessional towards the customers time! It shows how low German infrastructure and efficiency has fallen. Absolut disgrace
If it were Japan and this train was late, the transport minister would resign. They made people wait for hours, they don't allow public travel, we would be tired enough.

Everyone complains about the train, but not us! We took the ICE from Bremen to Frankfurt without any complaints. Almost on time (3 minutes) and good, friendly seat service. On the way back we were 20 minutes late in Bremen. The train staff tried very hard to provide connecting journeys.

Past successes are certainly no guarantee for the future. Because we were delayed by more than 4 hours due to defective trains, we missed our connection to Switzerland. We had to book an extra night in Basel and could only continue the next day.

Our DB (train company) provided itinerary shows us ticketed on two trains going from Rothenburg to Munich Germany. Itinerary's second train going through to Munich. DB route maps in stations and on train shows second train going through to Munich. Turns out second train's terminus is many kilometers (50 to 75) from (before) Munich!! You must transfer to yet a third train, two stops before second trains terminus in order to get to Munich. There was no notice of this (no email before leaving USA, no signs, no DB employees informing us). Other passengers on second train heard us talking about going to Munich and informed us... Those kind folks turned out to be right. My best guess: our tickets/itinerary was printed weeks before travel, train routes changed, there was no notification to individuals and no update on route maps displayed in stations and trains. SO, doublecheck your DB train itinerary as close to travel date as possible.

Cologne - Basel: left more than 90 minutes late. Then a 30 minute compulsory break for the staff. In Frankfurt it was announced that the train would only run to Karlsruhe. No support from the staff present to re-plan the route to the destination - the staff at the information service were also extremely unfriendly. I expect more for the price, unfortunately the trust in Die Bahn is gone.
Every time we travel the train is late.Vienna to Cologne 4 hours lateNuremberg to Vienna 2 hours late.Takes at least 3 months to get a refund .Staff very nice. Rail system abysmal .

They don't allow you to reserve your seat when you buy tickets. I travel from Trento to Munich standing up, lots of people sitting on the floor or standing in the corridors, even many elderly people, I would say a terrible trip! If they don't have seats they shouldn't even sell tickets. Given the crowds, the ticket inspectors do not come to check the tickets.

The trains here run late often enough that entire trip plans have to be altered on the fly and often result in missing the event you set out for. No shade or seats even at remote stops meant to be small hubs with layovers. What makes things worse are the passengers. Videos and music without head phones. Kids running around, switching seats. People hogging seats with food bags and backpacks even at crowded times. No wonder I don't use my €49 ticket more often. The experience is unpleasant.

....I wanted to try out Deutsche Bahn....I've been sitting on the track in Düsseldorf for two hours. Not even seats here. The whole thing is simply unacceptable!!! Doesn’t anyone feel responsible here??? From now on SUV and highway again. Cheaper and more convenient...
Always a disaster. It's like a miracle when a train is on time. It should come as no surprise if you prefer to travel by car.

It‘s a joke of German transport. Never on time, never responsible, extremely chaotic. Just arrive to the station and a train that takes an hour to get to my destination was 50min late. All this for 55€ (for an 1h train to Leipzig!!!!) 1 star for most of the time pretty friendly and helpful stuff that needa to bend their back covering lack of professionalism in this company.Not recommended. Avoid at all cost.

I bought a Deutschland ticket for my wife, so she can go to work. The abo in DB Navigator disappeared few days before new month and there wasn't any update for it. My wife has to show the ticket everyday while using the piblic transport, so I had to buy her a new ticket. I wrote an email and described the situation. I was personally at DB customer service and described the situation again to the service worker and he told me to cancel the abo for the ticket and contact my bank to receive back my money for the ticket. Everything went smoothly until I got the letter from DB with description, that I have to pay the money for the ticket, which I cancelled on advice from DB customer worker, with penalty money for receiving the abo money from my bank. I sent them few other email and described it again and again. Yet no response from DB abo portal. Really shame from DB.
they charged me even though I unsubscribed.I can't cancel and keep charging month after month. please help, I've been emailing for weeks with no response
I commute with the ICE three times a week. Twice a MONTH I arrive on time. This is not how the transport transition will work.

Terrible Customer Service, Trains are never on time if they even go at all, even when you book first class on their highspeed trains you get treated like garbage, and after you want to cancel a subscription they take extra weeks to make sure they can bill you again. Avoid this company if you can and never let them debit you directly.

What else can you say? Left 15 minutes later. Then the train broke down and waited 45 minutes for a new train. At the station there was poor information about which train was the new one. + further delays and connection options all missed at the destination. Traveling by train is better everywhere than in Germany.

CAUTION !!When booking ICE trains ALWAYS book a reserved seat whatever the booking  site says.  Since we had a mildly complicated multi country itinerary, we booked through Rail Europe and there is no link to booking seats.  Crazy !!  "here is your rail ticket but good luck getting a seat".  It turns out that there is a separate DB website to book seat reservations for an adittional E10 fee.As far as the service goes.  Cologne to Berlin train was nice after we snagged the last two open seats in first class.  Between the Brussels to Cologne and Cologne to Berlin trains we arrived in Berlin an hour and a half late on a two hour journey.  The ICE train from Berlin to Prague is a joke.  First class compartments look like something left over from the 1930's. Small, no access to power. Seats don't recline, no food service.   And they let people sit in the corridors in first class which leads to ridiculous congestion.  Where is the vaunted German efficiency ??  Not at all what we expected.

We had booked Rail and Fly to Cologne Airport. We picked out the ICE and reserved seats. Then it turned out at the train station that the ICE was canceled. The following ICE train was overcrowded. People sat in the aisles. We had to stand from Frankfurt to Cologne-Deutz. We changed there. A train station with lots of stairs, no elevators, 4 large suitcases, 4 carry-on suitcases. Then continue with the S-Bahn. Luckily we got in with all our luggage and were at the airport on time. I wrote an email to the railway because we wanted to get the cost of the seat reservation back. After three weeks, a surprising answer came: "We are the wrong person to contact. Your tour operator should help you." However, the seats were booked directly with the railway, so the tour operator said that it was a directly booked service for which the organizer is not responsible. Since we had paid with a well-known payment service, we opened a buyer protection case. And we actually won! The railway had to pay back. But I would never book Rail and Fly again and would only fly from our home airport. The whole thing wasn't relaxing, like in the train advertising, but pure stress with subsequent anger.
It couldn't be worse! Delays and cancellations are not the exception but the rule. The whole world laughs at Deutsche Bahn. Leadership incompetence to the power of 100!

It's logical that the people at the depatte train are always late, the staff is just standing there smoking, you're not allowed to get on the train because it's being cleaned (because no one is there to clean) and the car for the on-board restaurant comes to refill 1 minute before the train has to leave, the train has been there for half an hour and at the last moment the track is changed and we have to wait half an hour again for the new train, I hate paying for German railways Always a lot of money for delayed diversions, trains that don't leave at all or simply stop when they want 🤬🤬🤬

After an outward journey to Cologne, although on time, stuck in an aisle, due to a train that was too full. Our return journey was hell. More than an hour and a half late. NO info, the train stayed on time on the app. No more paper in the toilet, while the train stopped in the middle of nowhere, and took an hour longer to go from Cologne to Aachen. I pity small bladders. We arrived at our destination 2h30 late, having traveled 100km. It was also an obstacle course to get compensation. The delay had to be confirmed by train staff, so we saw no one during this interminable journey. And anyway, the train was on time according to them. And if you still want to try, you will have to send a letter to Germany and hope. Let's not even talk about the excessive prices, an hour's journey (theoretical, of course) costing at least 40e per person. A company to avoid, take the car

I use the Leipzig S-Bahn almost every day. Last week it was permanently canceled. However, the message "S1 towards... departure... clock... canceled today" suggested that it was only this one train. It was only on the Internet that we found out that all S-Bahn trains on this route would be canceled for at least a week. Reason: The heat caused windows and air conditioning to break and some of the employees in the workshop fell ill. So you can't convince anyone of the benefits of public transport and tempt you to switch between car and public transport. The 49 euro ticket doesn't help either. But Deutsche Bahn obviously doesn't need any customers.
There was no stop in Mainz, I had to look for alternatives to Dresden in Frankfurt myself and arrived at my destination three hours later.

Deutsche Bahn can only be described in one word: DISASTER!!!! If I want to write about my bad experiences with Deutsche Bahn, it should be a book! Unpunctuality, unclear platform changes, high ticket prices, etc. If I had another option, I would NEVER take Deutsche Bahn again. NEVER AGAIN!!!!!!!!If they can't do their job properly, at least they shouldn't be allowed to sell tickets! Giving up isn't always a bad thing!

Traveling in 1st class on IC 2271 to Berlin was a bad experience. It started with the suitcase having to be dragged all the way up. Afterwards I cleaned the reserved seat of any leftover food. Empty cans and bottles rolled around on the top shelves. I couldn't sit for long. There was a cold draft in the open carriage, so I had to get an extra jacket from my suitcase. On the outward journey to Berlin on August 25th, 2023 with the IC 2270, I was able to buy a drink from the nice train attendant. Now on the return journey the staff were very unfriendly when checking the tickets. When I then asked if I could buy something to drink, the short answer was that there were no drinks on board. The reason became clear to me when I discovered that all the toilets were locked due to defects. There was already a sign on the platform saying that there was no disabled toilet on board. We didn't find out that there wasn't another one. Why do I pay the price to travel in first class when it doesn't exist? My suggestion: The money spent on advertising, which is far from reality, would be better spent on quality assurance.

The trains in Germany are invariably delayed , with no explanation given . Staff have a take it or leave it attitude . DB are pobably the worst in the EU for operating rail service (not even the Balkan nations are inept. If visiting Germany use any other transport option.
By far the worst company in Germany. Rarely have I seen such an incredibly unreliable company in years.

Look at the photo. Out of 12 trains, 4 are cancelled and 3 have delays. For one of them the delays keep increasing and increasing. I am traveling today and I had no chance as the flight was cancelled and Lufthansa gave me a train ticket, but I suggest to think twice, maybe three times before deciding to go for the Deutsche Bahn. Three days ago my wife and daughter took the train from Nuremberg to Duisburg. Sure thing, the train was cancelled.

I don't know how Germans put up with DB public transport. I'm Italian and I'm used to Trenitalia, but DB is surreal, we travelled all by train from Bologna to Munich, Berlin, Hamburg, Amsterdam, Cologne, Munich again and finally Bologna.Out of 7 journeys we had 6 problems, 3 of which were serious.On the outward journey, the journey, which was supposed to be direct, was divided into 3 parts (train, bus, train), the bus (or rather the 4 full buses) were delayed by 30 minutes due to traffic and the train did not wait for the 240+ people, as a result, we delayed our arrival by almost 3 hours (out of a 6 hour journey)On the journey from Hamburg to Amsterdam, with 10 minutes to go we were told the train would not arrive, a further 3 hours delay to change trains.But the most hallucinating thing was the journey from Amsterdam to Cologne, where DB thought to remove a carriage leaving everyone who had booked standing, I won't tell you the problems  between people arguing with eachorders. The other 3 problems were "just" delays from up to 2 hours.

My train was about an hour late for my connection. About 10 minutes before the transfer station, the conductor starts screaming at me about how I didn't put my bike correctly in the rack. Even though 3 previous conductors checked my tickets and passed my bike without saying anything. This is not the first time my train on DB was late. It's an ongoing issue. I am a older man in my 60s, I expect just a tiny bit of respect and manners.
It sounds exaggerated, but long-term commuters understand it. The train really NEVER comes! on time. I'm sometimes happy if it's only 20 minutes late and it comes at all. Can't you accuse them?

In the last days off I made a few trips with the DB. The IC long-distance service is still almost bearable. Reservations went well. Reached the destination in ONLY 15 minutes late. The ICE was at least a reliable DB vehicle. The delay was over an hour. Unfortunately, the DB regional transport took the cake. Unfortunately, punctuality is a completely foreign concept there. Consequently, half of all seats are occupied by bags. Unfortunately, the train crew is not interested in this. Consistency means standing in a train that is half full. Unfortunately, this is absolutely unprofessional for a transport service provider. If you consider that unfortunately every country around us can do the whole thing significantly better and significantly cheaper, this is more than worrying. Unfortunately, the train is and remains not an alternative that is even remotely worth mentioning.
Terrible customer service and ticket office in Bolzano station. Rudeness and conflicting information. The lady with the tail and glasses who curses her Trenitalia colleagues is the icing on the cake.

Never again Deutsche Bahn!22. August 2023, a completely ordinary Tuesday. Passau from: 11.37 - Nuremberg - Karlsruhe - Basel on: 18:36 From Passau to Nuremberg, the ICE 28 dragged itself at a snail's pace to Nuremberg, where it arrived 30 minutes late. Our connecting train to Karlsruhe was long gone. In front of the Nuremberg DB information desk, I patiently stood at the back of a long line of passengers seeking advice. All in vain, because I didn't receive the necessary information as expected, but was referred to the DB travel center. There I took a number in the entrance area so that I might get information and a new train connection with reserved seats at some point. Waiting time: 38 minutes in a hall without enough seats. Finally. I got a new connection and reserved seats to Basel, which later turned out to be pointless. We set off towards Karlsruhe almost as scheduled, two hours late. Once again the DB failed to maintain travel times. The delay became increasingly cumulative. Then the train driver probably had a mental, unforgivable blackout and stopped the train in Mühlacker-Rössleweg instead of in Mühlacker. I definitely knew then that we had chosen the wrong means of transport. When we finally arrived late in Karlsruhe and the passengers wanted to get off, the doors on the entire train didn't open. After minutes an announcement came that there was a door malfunction and that the staff was trying to fix it. At some point the doors opened. In the meantime, our connecting train towards Freiburg-Basel had of course left again and we only reached the following ICE 79 Berlin-Zurich because it was also 7 minutes late. At the Badischen Bahnhof Basel, there was renewed concern about our connecting train in Basel SBB. The ICE simply stopped there! The scheduled departure would be at 8:48 p.m. and he only moved to Basel SBB at 9:10 p.m. A sticker on the door of our car indicated that it was not possible to get out due to a defect. “Use another door,” it said. As a result, all the guests choked with their luggage through the transition into the neighboring car in order to be able to escape the DB. Once again, due to the DB's incompetence, we couldn't get to our train for the onward journey! We arrived home extremely late, from Basel at least with the SBB that runs on time! Keep dreaming, dear DB, but without me! Your beautiful words and promising advertising are nothing but lies!
The worst transportation ever !! I have been to sooo many countries and the worst Trains and bus system in the world is the German transportation

The most terrible experience! The train conductor from Berlin to Duisburg was a SUPER rude guy that was triggering pretty much every English-speaking passenger to get into some sort of argument for absolutely no reason and shouting at them 3 times with "DO YOU UNDERSTAND?". We looked at each other shocked and even reported to his supervisor, but unfortunately, this seems to be OK with DB otherwise he should have not been in charge!

One point and because it is mandatory to rate... train canceled without explanations, terrible organization to manage the change, zero information (passengers of SNCF, the French railway company, received notice of the cancellation hours before in their emails and mobile phones, with alternatives), and unfriendly staff with a more than questionable level of English. Summary: we had to travel the next day and without a fixed seat, so we had to move around the train until we found a free seat. Evaluating the experience as a whole, and taking into account that the price of the tickets is not exactly cheap (of which, with luck, we will recover 50%), the next time we travel to Germany we will try to do so using another means of transport, since the German state railway leaves a lot to be desired.

We travelled from Munich to Berlin and viceversa in August 2023 and the experience was terrible. First of all the Munich station is horrible, for an important city like Munich there should be a much better station like central station in Berlin. The car was a kind of bandwagon with very limited space, kids jumping all over, and if one happens to sit beside an extra large person, then its going to be tough. Will never use ICE trains in future for sure!

Disaster!! All the times I have taken trains and they have been around 5-7 times, they have ALWAYS been late, and they were 30 minutes late until the last time it was 2 hours. I have to say that the tickets are quite expensive for the terrible service they provide. The experience with DB was incredibly bad.

We had no issues with time keeping on our two journeys this summer. But on the first it was chaotic when we boarded. Many people without reservations were sat in reserved seats including ours (they were asleep and could not be woken until their stop!). Then we got our seats. But the carriages were all overcrowded.But the worst of it was the food service on both journeys. It was so slow and long queues built up each time. On each journey I spent 1/3 of the time trying to get food. The first time the restaurant service closed as I got to the front and I had to wait 20 mins until it re-opened. There is only one menu on the counter so you cannot make your choices in the queue. Lots of food was not available. It was very expensive. They ran out of cutlery. And had no change!But it was a comfortable enough ride, fast and air conditioned. If using ICE services again I'd make sure we had food before boarding!!

I've been driving long distances regularly for 2 years now and would be done quicker if I listed what worked. I'll still try to summarize: You have to be prepared for delays, 30 minutes is the rule, more than an hour can happen. Avoid connections if possible and pay attention to long transfer times if necessary. Railway employees, people on the track, technical problems etc are blamed. It never feels like the railway is to blame. The blame is always passed on, I would like to thank you as an employee...Generously, you often get the reservation costs back if the ICE breaks down again and you instead take the tourist train for twice as long standing up without air conditioning. The railway is really generous with its compensation.... By the way, there are no defibrillators on the trains either, but the railway knows how to make do and simply asks the guests if anyone has one with them in case of need. All in all, an experience that you wouldn't wish on anyone! I would also give it 0 if it could!

Booked 3 train journeys, 2 of which were disasters. 1/3 went according to plan, train only lasted 2/3 had 4 hours!!! Delay 3/3 was 1 hour late and changed tracks The app doesn't work "Error404" under "Help & Feedback". It's really embarrassing, economically uninteresting with the high ticket prices and then with the loss of time. Simply worthless

Never go to Germany on summer if you do not need to, specially using ICE or public transport. ICE is unorganized train. you reserved seats but they do not have indicator if it's reserved or not. Summer is not good idea to go to Germany!!!!! Currently seating on the floor infront of the WC's.

I wish I could give no stars.  I booked a train from Cologne to Liege at 9:42 on the 11.08.23.  The train left early, I wasn't notified, the later train was over crowded, staff were unfriendly and unhelpful, in fact utterly rude.  The train back that evening was an hour late.  Not once in our time in Germany did we get a train that ran when it was meant to.  A truly awful experience.

Disgusting. Due to an unscheduled transfer from one train to another (the reason was not explained), the train arrived in Berlin an hour late, which is why I missed the other train. In response to my questions at the information desk, they gave me a ticket for the other two trains (with a transfer, because there were no more direct ones). While waiting, it turned out that the first of the trains would arrive 2.5 hours late, which means I wouldn’t be able to catch the second one (despite it being the last one for the day). The information desk closed at five, all questions to the cashier. The lines are wild, there are a lot of late people. They offered to pay extra for a new ticket, despite the fact that we had to wait until tomorrow morning. Garbage and chaos is all that can be said.

Almost always unfriendly and sometimes even rude staff who mostly check tickets from foreigners but not from Germans and there’s no carriage for babies in the first class and in the second class it is allowed for people who don’t have children to sit in places meant for people with children. Staffs control nothing.Also based on my experience, trains are always delayed or late arrived!

Booked first class months in advance from Berlin to Heringsdorf. Timetable changed twice prior to trip and had to buy new tickets. The travel experience is horrific and is actually dangerous and a health risk for elderly people. Massively overbooked, Nowhere to sit, trains so crowded it's impossible to get to the toilet Nowhere to put luggage. Everybody's cases blocking the aisles,. Having to stand for a three hour journey in a first class cabin is a joke. Pressed together like sardines with coughing kids and crying babies. If there was one germ of Covid on our train then everyone must have it by now. Train was a Covid paradise.   No buffet car, No staff to sort things out. Just a complete and utter shambles. We love the North of Germany but won't be visiting again as travelling there by train ruins the experience. Such a shame because Germany does so much right. Unfortunately the railways system is a failure just now.
Constantly late, totally overpriced! Better drive a car! Never again DB! Zero reliability and we only advise against using DB in 2023.

We are on a trip from Amsterdam to Berlin on DB train. I understand there are some newer DB trains, unfortunately our train seemed to be an older version. However, it could still be kept clean. Highly disappointed as we boarded to see dirty bathroom, dirty cabin in first class car. Simple cleanliess should be the hall mark of any long distance train, specially in 1st class. Train never got cleaned in its international turnaroud service. Floor was dirty littered with debris, seat was covered with remnants of food from previous occupant I imagine, and of course, the dining car was not functioning due to lack of staff. Post covid, staff shortages are plaguing so many servie businesses, and DB seems to be no exception. Please be aware and keep your expectations low. Comparere to alternate modes of transportation. The train trips are no longer the delight restful trips they used to be. Aware of pick pockets. At least fortunately, the train seem to be running on time.

On the ICE train between Berlin and Amsterdam, you don't have anywhere to plug in a phone or laptop, even in first class. Outlets im the cafe wagon are covered with tape. Air conditioning not working in the wagon I was assigned and it was seriously 30+ degrees. You don't get a reserved seat unless you pay 4 euro extra so people just sit in the passage way because it's too full. Wifi doesn't work at all for most of the trip. 3+ euros for awful coffee in the cafe. Ridiculously bad service for the price.

Route Ulm - Augsburg - Munich, assessed by a commuter at different times. 1/10 trains arrive on time, but only if you're lucky. Is it perhaps time to adjust the timetable? Completely arbitrary, you can follow the concept in the same way as in the village with a bus: - You know sometimes a bus goes through, but you don't know exactly when. Same with the DB app: - Sometimes current, sometimes an hour late and no information, sometimes the train is canceled, you're standing on the track - DB app shows the train was running normally and just at its first stop - must be a classic ghost train... Just when you thought things couldn't get any worse, GoAhead comes along and since then It really couldn't get any more unpunctual. Even if GoAhead isn't late, which is extremely rare, the train has to wait at least 15 minutes to arrive shortly before Augsburg. I'm full of hate and have to buy a car for better or for worse, after all, you're not getting any younger and taking the train in Germany is now considered bodily harm.
Made in Germany. The worst train in Europe. German products are probably just as rubbish now,
Problems on every trip. Several experiences, very regularly, none positive. 3x I had to sleep in Mannheim and arrive at work late on Monday morning because of the DB. Null.

Customer service is poor verging on rude, the train we were on was expensive, but old, so no one was able to get in their correct seats because the car numbers weren't on the outside signs (broken). The car we ended up in had no climate control (broken) on a hot and humid day, so it was a three-hour ride in a sauna, with no offer of compensation for discomfort. Everyone, local and tourist alike, was sweating and miserable. At the very least, the dining car should have distributed water to the affected passengers.

It's not all bad about the train. But too much, and a lot of it unnecessary. Expensive prices for delayed trains in which you are then allowed to stand because the reservations don't work. Service was completely abolished and switched to non-functioning robotic processes. Any other service provider would be shown the bird. E.g. a hotel that charges money for reservations, but then has no rooms available and does not refund the reservation. I don't know...
What else can you say about that?! Unpunctual Unpunctual Unpunctual …… You can’t rely on anything, especially when it comes to important appointments.
Hello, as unpunctual as DB, I feel like I'm in a third country!!! Sad and you still have to pay for that!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

I’m on the 4th hour of this sh*t show while I write this. If zero were an option I’d have chosen it. 1st class my ass. This train service is the worst. Stinks. Filthy. Late. No staff. Thugs smoking in the cabin. People sitting wherever the hell they please, seat and section reservations be damned. Alarm sounding for an hour on an overnight trip. No TP in toilets. No to this hell train. I am literally fearing for my safety. Never, not ever, ever again. This train service is trash. Take a flight. Walk. Take a bus. Any other option. Please just do yourself a favor and do not take DB trains.

I was traveling from Wolfsburg to Munich (train to flight). I would have had to change trains 3 times for the trip. Of the 4 journeys, 3 were late. Only the rail replacement service from WOB to BS was on time because the MA said they'd better go now who knows what will happen. My seat reservation couldn't be canceled either. I'm curious whether I'll get my money back. In the end I was 1.5 hours late at the airport. Luckily I planned 3.5 hours more time because you know the DB. DB is the worst way of transport I have ever experienced.

I've recently been traveling by train for business because it's supposedly better for our environment and more expensive than traveling by car, but what the heck! I had to travel again from Leipzig to Frankfurt and from there to Stuttgart. Half an hour here, half an hour there... doesn't count as a delay... From Stuttgart back to Leipzig via Erfurt, Deutsche Bahn tops itself again. At 5:23 p.m. I was able to take the ICE in Stuttgart and was supposed to be in Leipzig at 10:10 p.m.! Since we were 50 minutes late because of a slice!!! has broken. OK. Missed the connecting train in Erfurt but the next one is supposed to arrive in 40 minutes at 10:40 p.m. Was the train there?? 11:40 p.m. still no train…only 12:10 a.m.! How can one rely on this incompetent organization? No company could afford something like that. The fact that DB even demands money from people for SOWAS is unbelievable. You can't plan an appointment with certainty or you have to arrive a day in advance. Even that doesn't always work with the DB. Since I started taking the train, I haven't even arrived on time and have always been between 2-4 hours late. DB has to pay for people to ride there. Also the 49€ ticket... Give people their money back and take a cue from progressive countries. Thank God there is a car & we should all just switch to it. Even the staff on board can no longer contain their frustration. It is also unreasonable for the DB employees who drive there or do the service part, etc.! These nice people deserve a good and reliable employer and not the miserable DB.

9 August 2023 train 205 from Frankfurt airport delayed to arrive to Mannheim, it was suppose to arrive at 22:23 but in fact on the screen it is shown 23:53 now, so I don't know even if we will reach Mannheim by this time, as still in train. Thing is I had a connection train to Heilbronn at 22:40, but obviously missed it, now the train will arrive at midnight, and I didn't even reach Mannheim, yet I need to go to Heilbronn! I have to.be tomorrow early morning there, so my husband who works as a doctor have work tomorrow morning as well and he has to drive one hour to Mannheim to collect me and then one hour back because of Deutsch bhan unorganized system! It is not a first or second or even third time I experience such delays with DB. And for such delays more then 60 min they refund only 25 percent of the ticket cost. Nowhere else I expirienced such unorganized work of a transport.

My experience seems pretty typical. Took an ICE to Hamburg, train was delayed by 2 hours, had to make an unexpected transfer in Köln, of course now can't reserve seats and had to switch seats 4 times so far so people with reservations can sit there. Either require everyone to have a seat reservation included in their printed ticket or don't require it at all!! This is the most anxiety-inducing train ride I have ever taken in my life.

As part of my trip within Central Europe and the use of the Eurail Pass, I went through Germany. Much tot my surprise, every single train I used encountered some time delays:_arrival to Saarbrucken from France: 15mns late_Mannheim to Munich: first delayed, the train was cancelled altogether. I had to run to get another train. Thankfully there was seat for everyone, but otherwise, I would paid a seat reservation for nothing! _Munich to Budapest: delayed for 15mns,then for another 15mns....We left with over an hour late. The trains are very comfortable, with free & fast wifi. But those are just bonus! Leaving and arriving on time is the least trains should do!  Very disappointed with German railways....s
Horrible. Deutch Bahn is worse than the SNCF, the trains are always late, no organization! I don't recommend.

Booked first class tickets for myself and wife well in advance (like 3 months).  Assigned seats were not together, seats were broken, cabin was filthy, no service offered, train was 20 minutes late (Paris East to Frankfurt).  A trip to the bar car and they had NO water, No sparkling water, No soda.  They had only lemonade (no ice).  THIS WAS NOT FIRST CLASS TRAVEL.  You’re better off with the treatment the airlines give you.Complained to DB and they ignored me.  I’ve been on many European high speed trains and this takes the title —-WORST!
Disastrous service, unreachable by phone! Lots of options at first, then you get stuck. Goodnight Germany
Shame on you double booking the first class on a 4-hour trip EC175 Berlin to Prague and your staff are so callous and rude. That is a 0 on customer service on top of the rip off.

The worst experience! Trains are either canceled or they are very late. I just can never get home properly at the scheduled time. It's arrogance with such prices! Hey! Government or whatever, do something!
Expensive, unfriendly staff, unreliable (we didn't catch our connecting train), never again.

Probably the worst train company in the world, and I've taken a few. It’s simple: in 22 train journeys with Deutsche Bahn this year, I have NEVER been on time. Often with delays of more than an hour. And trains that change tracks without it being announced. Not to mention the obnoxious staff, and the dirty stations full of junkies. And the app that never works, with boxes automatically checked to scam you. In short, if you don't like the SNCF (and it's true that it has faults), take the Deutsche Bahn one day. And you'll never complain about our trains again!

What they are good at is being unpunctual, unreliable and dirty... oh yeah and outrageously expensive. Furthermore, they are in a position to pay their talentless board members astronomical bonuses for failure. The passengers should receive money in order to be able to endure this cramp, even free rides would still be too expensive. The DB should be abolished or bought by someone who has what it takes... maybe the Nigerian State Railways, I think things are going better there

If I could put 0 stars I would because this is just the worst experience I had in my life with a train company.I took 5 times the DB company train in my life and not one time the train was on time and I’am not talking about small delays it’s always at least 30 minutes so your whole itinerary is ruined.Furthermore, first time in my life you buy a ticket but you don’t have a seat, you have to buy it or else you will have to stand up for 2 hours or sit on the floor and this causes people to sit just anywhere and even if you buy a seat it will probably be taken.Avoid at any cost !!!Take a Thalys or even Flixtrain/Flixbus

We have been traveling almost exclusively by train for our holidays for years, using Interrail to cross Europe. After being a reference for us in the past, Deutsche Bahn seems to have become one of the worst railway companies in Europe, with systematic delays, trains canceled or which do not start from the correct station, chaotic communication. I don't understand such a level of disorganization and such low consideration for customers. For our last trip, to Scandinavia, we spent a night running between different stations in Hamburg, with travel bags and children, before deciding to check into a hotel around 1am. The next day, we took a train to Copenhagen, the destination indicated from the platform was the wrong one. And I'm not talking about the opening to get reimbursed for tickets or reservations... In short, catastrophic service...

Absolutely lousy. Spontaneous train cancellations, no reasonable replacement. Every star is one too many. Unreliable to the point of not working anymore. If everyone worked like the German railways then the wheel wouldn't have been invented yet.

Worst train travel experience of my life, train cancelled multiple times during the same day, replacement train gets infinitely delayed, completely garbage management, worse than 3rd world, people responsible should be ashamed

Train from Berlin to Prague: horrible, price more than double the bus, and takes the same time. When you reserve a seat you can't choose, they give you separate ones and whoever they want. The overcrowding in the carriages seems like a train documentary in some remote region of India (hallways full of people standing, lying on the floor, smells...). I didn't expect it: hell at a very expensive price... We went in August, maybe there is a problem with massive interrail without prior reservation... I don't know, we all had to throw out people who were occupying our seats... everything was very, very bad.

We took three DB trains. The first one from Berlin to Dresden was so overbooked that dozens of travelers were sitting on the floor in the corridors, and worse, many passengers bound for Prague were ordered to take a bus due to lack of space on the train! For the other two trains we had reserved our seats (to avoid traveling sitting on the ground) and both times our seats had already been reserved, DB took (cash) the same reservation twice!
Very unreliable service, departure/arrival times are completely meaningless. It’s a good day if the train shows up

Unbelievable - save yourself the advertising! Traveling by train is NEITHER a pleasure for business travelers NOR for vacation trips, it's just annoying, stressful and frustrating - expensive tickets for ZERO service!

From Munich to Verona train in terrible conditions: very dirty, toilets impracticable to say the least. They sell tickets without the possibility of booking so people stand for hours. Improper train information. Strongly not recommended!

The regional one was 4 minutes late and the connecting train didn't wait. Missed the train from Basel to Lörrach with 2 children and had to wait 1 hour. I get back in the car and around. That just doesn't work with children.

We travelled from Berlin to Munich on the ICE train first class and it was an excellent experience.It was luxurious.  The seats were excellent, service,  comfort and reliability was without fault. I would strongly recommend these trains.  We loved visiting Germany and when we do come back, we would probably tour Germany using the ICE trains in preference to any other mode of transport.

I had my luggage stolen inside the train from Cologne to Utrecht today. No employee tried to help me at all. They just turn their back to me and pretend nothing was happening Be very aware of your luggage during the whole trip. In case anything bad happens, no employee from Deutsche Bahn will help. Horrible service and unsafe trip.

I've been traveling with the DE ticket since June - honestly, there isn't a trip where something hasn't happened. Even the shortest route doesn't drive as it should. And best of all; If a train is to connect with another train at the station, the doors will not open upon arrival until the trains are connected. The German railway is not interested in missing connecting trains as a result! The processes have been created very cleverly.

Just sad! If you have to be somewhere at a certain time, you can forget about taking the train to get there on time. After 15 years of taking the train, I switched back to the car and hope no one gets stuck on the road. DB 6-!!!

It's okay if you don't ask for anything. The moment a problem arises and you need assistance, a game of non-answers, rebounds, incomprehensible bureaucracy and the impossibility of solving the problem begins. The train was canceled due to construction issues on the line and it is not possible to get an answer on how to get a refund or voucher

Worse company in Germany.  Always late. Add 2-3 hours for your trip because you can garauntee that you WILL be late. Don't depend on it's time because they will steal all of your day. Your 1 hour ride will take at least 2. Your 2h ride will take 3. Your 3h ride will take 6h. So just use blablacar and you will reach your destination faster despite traffic on highways. I repeat, if you ever come to Germany, DO NOT USE DB FOR YOUR TRANSPORTATION.

Experiences since mid-April to date. 28 trips from Lindau-Reutin to Leipzig. Normally just over 8 hours with a 49 euro ticket. In general, except for 4 times, I was between 2 and 6 hours late. There is no compensation for the 49 euro ticket. So don't buy this. Pay normally and get the fare and compensation for every trip. Maybe the DB will get it then. IC, EC and ICE trains are generally delayed by an average of 20 minutes; from 16 minutes onwards, 25% will be refunded. And after 2 hours you get the full price back. So now I'm paying in advance because if I'm constantly delayed by 2 hours, I can travel for free with DB after requesting a refund and with IC EC and ICE, everyone does it like me! At some point the pseudo-intelligence bolts have to react. 98% of the time you make a lot of money for unfulfilled services.

Those being so critical of DB really do need to travel on a British train to get some perspective on what a bad rail service is. You spin the wheel if fortune every time you set foot on a train and the complex web of train operating companies collectively have nothing but absolute contempt for their customers. German railways are good standard by comparison

Absolutely the last dirty club. Always late no matter what day you go and the prices are way too expensive for the service. The train is still creeping around the area like a snail. You can also walk along part of it. I advise everyone to take a car or go with a carpool.

On the Husum-Sankt Peter Ording route. The train is late or doesn't come almost every day, so people are forced to use the bus, which also doesn't come. And we have to sit at the bus or train station for hours, which causes us to be late for work every day. Why do we buy tickets? Or is racism also being used here? Is the train not coming because only foreigners travel anyway?

I travel by train every day to get to work. At least 80% of the trains arrive late. Reach connecting trains? Wrong thought. You have to be prepared for the fact that a journey with Deutsche Bahn can take around 2 hours, if not longer, while by car it takes around 20 minutes. I cannot begin to describe how incompetent the management and the majority of their employees are.

We travelled on five days and on four days there were issues. On one occasion the train just didn't exist, on others they were late or cancelled before the destination. We were able to transfer to other trains straightforwardly. Plan ahead and keep evidence of your travel bookings. Allow time for connections or to get to your destination.
Deutsche Bahn, 1st class, of course the train was delayed... 9 out of 10 times the trains were delayed and on top if it to have that expereince on 1st class...

Do NOT ride this trainline. On our month-long backpacking trip we only rode it twice. The first time, on a (what was supposed to be) 3 hour train ride turned into four hours. We left on time but got to the station an hour late? Then our transfer train had a technical issue and we had to get out and switch to another train. They didn’t even tell us what was wrong until about 15 minutes after we were just stopped. So we got to our destination 2 hours and 30 minutes late. Now dreading the next train with this trainline. So then the second time we rode, it was late to the station. The second half of the train ends up having to detach meaning that even though you paid for a ticket, you had to stand since there weren’t enough seats. They didn’t get another train or anything. I will NEVER be going with this company again.
If I could leave 0 starts I would.Just the worst of the worst of Germany. Delays every day, cancelled trains, dirty trains…. It just sucks.
My train was canceled and I never receivzd any informations.I had to hitchhike from Cologne to Lyon (France).
This really was rubbish. 623 euros for supposedly 1st class service.Saw an attendant once in 4 hours.Don’t waste your money. We’re applying for a refund

First time in Europe. Amsterdam - Copenhagen. The trip was canceled a day before due to the impossibility of the connection in Hamburg Altona and the train leaving Amsterdam was also cancelled. I traveled to Hamburg Harburg where I could not board the delayed 0:30 night train. I was stranded with 20 other people. The station was unsafe and very cold. I had to take a taxi to Hamburg Altona and the 6:50 train didn't leave because there was a fire on the tracks. Then we took the S Bahn to Hamburg Hbf from where we took a replacement train, 7 Hours later! By that time I should have reached my destination. Horrible experience. The staff is not attentive to giving you the correct instructions. It's a waste of time traveling with DB. Anymore. If this is the image they give of German trains, it is completely different from what they had told me... Punctuality goes down their ass!

This year, like last year, I used Deutsche Bahn during a vacation. The result was catastrophic! I immediately canceled the Deutschlandticket and also the Probebahncard. Luckily, there are other travel options. Traveling by train in Germany means a loss of life, great inconvenience and is basically only possible for passengers without luggage! The Austrian Railway, on the other hand, was recommended!

Unfortunately, the train is still not an alternative to the car in 2023. Overpriced and overcrowded. If you decide to take the train, you won't even get a seat for exorbitant prices. The main thing is that the ICE's run the same routes, half empty, that the RE's also run and are overcrowded. Hardly anyone can afford to take the ICE.

Not worth it AT ALL. When the train arrived our wagon was closed off for repair reasons. Every person that had seats reserved there had to stand or sit on the aisles the whole trip from Berlin to Amsterdam. An eight hour trip! Worst experience of my life. No explanation or solution was ever given.

Nice weekend in Germany? Then definitely don't take the ice, on the way there the train was canceled at the last minute and we had to take intercity trains from Brussels (arrived 1h30m later). On the way back we had an ice on which we had no WiFi (we had first class tickets) so we couldn't order drinks at the seat which is included in first class, we had old seats, we had almost no view because we were sitting between two windows, no screen with information, not even decent lighting, we would have even had a better time in second class ( we sat behind the part where the driver sits, there are a number of chairs. We had 1 socket for 2 and so on. The only good thing was that we were on time and the bar is good quality, but that was not recommended
Wissing should be told to only use the train so that he can see how well it works.
The railway simply makes everything ~ It's possible!!!!!Most modern trains, exemplary track network and extremely friendly employees!!!!! ~ Chapeau!

Got an email: "Travel schedule no longer possible".  No other details, nothing!What does that mean? 45 minutes in the waiting queue for a customer support call to find out...No answer and still not sure how I will travel in just 5 days.

One star is given to Deutsche Bahn and German travellers. There were several quiet carriages on ICE train. They were no different to other carriages. Many people spoke loudly, used their mobile phones, kids played games, etc. It looks like DB themselves did not bother about it at all. You pay money to have a seat in what is supposed to be a quiet place where you can sleep and have a rest but finally find yourself in the middle of a noisy mess.

Worst trains. Always reaches very late. Always some repairs works or some issue. Not comfortable for sleeping. All lights will be on. Very difficult to travel with kid. No difference between 1st class and 2nd class but the charge will be double. Overall very worst experience nothing positive.

Not only the trains are outdated and hot with no AC, but also the employees are horrendous. They are how I imagine a prison officer. Just so angry, rude, screaming at you as if you are a begger not a paying customer. It’s from an experience of over tens of rides in Deutschebahn so I know it is the norm. I also wonder if they are allowed to run a train with no ac and no windows open in the summer heat of 30+. It seemed like it should be illegal. I literally couldn’t breathe from time to time.
No one from no one!!! Only delays of 1 hour, 2 hours, cancellations galore and even without warning. 1 in 10 trips go well! To flee at all costs

Unfortunately it's now the second time that I have real bad experience on this journey. DB.  There are no heads up on the delays an cancellation.  beside am sorry we don't how long . Dat doesn't solve the problems for passenger. Real disappointment.

15 years ago, I let 2 teenagers take the train from Geneva to Köln without having the slightest problem. Today, I have to plan a night in a hotel whenever we can't find a connection to get to my destination... Trains late: anyway... Trains canceled: very often... No more connections to get to my destination the same day, too often... It's really the Third World... And to think that Germany is subsidizing the Americans' war in Ukraine... I don't understand anything anymore...

Apart from train cancellations, delays and unfriendly employees (who are stroppy and ignorant), Deutsche Bahn simply offers nothing. There is no service there either. There is no justification for increasing ticket prices. The DB should simply be ashamed of itself and simply stop making comparisons with other countries, then it will be even more shameful!! Perhaps the decisions made so far should simply be monitored and examined. And the entire management team will be fired!

On Wednesday, July 5, my parents, over 80, went by train from Wilhelmshaven to Bremen for a day.  The trip went well, but the return trip was an ordeal that cost us €220. When we arrived at the Bremen train station to take the return train, they warned that the return trains were canceled due to inclement weather (80 km/h wind) and that buses would be made available to travelers as a substitute for the trains.  They told us over the loudspeaker that we should go to the square in front of the station, where buses are waiting.  When we arrived, there were none, but a lot of people. After waiting for more than an hour exposed to the wind and rain and without any possibility of seats for seniors, a bus finally arrived. The problem was that there were at least 200 people waiting, that is, many more than can fit on a bus.  The bus filled up immediately. There was no official from the responsible railway company, Deutsche Bahn. It was chaos. They did not warn that another bus might arrive. After waiting every half hour more, we decided to pay for a taxi to go home.  It is a shame how they treat older adults in the first place, then they do not offer any reward for the damage caused.  I think 80 km/h is no reason to cancel rail traffic.  In my opinion, sending passengers on a bus is much more dangerous. Furthermore, the responsible company does not show face and organizes the cancellation and replacement in a disastrous way. Germany is no longer what it used to be. It seemed more like a situation in an underdeveloped country.

Very bad experience. Bought what we thought was 2 return tickets from Frankfurt to Bad Homburg for a day visit. Just before getting off ticket was checked and it turned out to be only 1 ticket for the wrong date. 2nd of Aug instead of 6 July.  What wr thought was “2” adult tickets was “2 “ for the date. Paid 11Euro for this then fined 120 Euro ! And had to buy another return ticket which was11 Euro. Same amount we had payed. Ticket officer was very unfriendly and would not listen to any explanation of an honest mistake.The ticket machine was difficult to understand and took  multiple attempts for it to accept payment. Tried with visa and cash.Overall very frustrating and very tourist unfriendly.
Out of 4 trains, none on time! Change missed due to their delay: nothing planned, move on, there's nothing to see! Lamentable!

Now within 2 weeks I had to take the train twice after years. In addition to the dirty trains, there are also broken brakes.  .. and that with ICE traffic.  Travel time was over 2 hours late in each case! Close the store .Never again.

Racket! Paid 6 EUR for first class seat reservation on ICE train. Seat did not exist on the entire train.Conductor refused to offer any assistance. At minimum, I wanted the seat reservation money back. With this indifference and incompetence, they should go on the strike they threaten. Then hopefully all would be fired.

The railway, the mess of this nation. My daughter visits me by train every two months. From Ingolstadt to Saarbrücken. Every time chaos. Nothing works. It's a shame that there is no flight connection. I would pay any price not to have to travel with this mess

A catastrophe, our 15-year-old daughter with a valid driving license was checked a few months ago! Since this hasn't been necessary before, she didn't have a student ID card or ID card with her. She was treated like a felon. Then the letters from this company started. We have proven several times via the portal that she is a student and that we have been paying the excessive prices for both children every month for years. But it doesn't stop, you are too incapable of stopping the process. Always new letters and requests, we need this proof and then something new. Doesn't this company have other problems than dealing with bullshit like this? And constantly annoying families? Incredible, and the DB is not an open stock corporation, the only shareholder is the state and it shows. So the ARD's reporting is and was, as always, flawed and complete nonsense.

Cancellations and delays are the norm, but when it comes to refund, I got to know only about people with German last name who were refunded. My trip had 3 legs, the first was cancelled, there was no bus or any other means to reach my connection, so I took a taxi (also hard to find). They refunded me only the price of that leg, not the taxi. That was BEFORE 1st of May, they did not state any ground for such gall, only empty excuses. Every time, they agreed on the phone that I am entitled to a refund. Since there was no reason for the refusal, other than my foreign last name, they tried to make up one: the receipt was a carbon-copy (illegal reason, since this doesn't matter, AND it was the original). Not they are in the bargaining phase: they offered me a 10 euros voucher in the exchange of the refund claim, only to shut up. Meanwhile, I met a few other foreigners: a Polish woman fined like any other fare dodger, for using an identical train instead of the train she could not reach because the previous was too late; a British who was talked down to by the ticket collector because of his accent.All in all: DB is doing wrong by foreigners living and travelling in Germany. I have no doubt that their foreign employees are treated the same way. DB = one of the companies I would NEVER work for.
Terrible experience I am completely speechlessEverything everything went wrongInclusive the personal
It couldn't be worse! The only things that are reliable here are delays and total cancellations. My tip: If possible, avoid the train nationwide!
All trains are canceled. A one-hour trip can easily take four hours. Germany has to change something, otherwise the car-free future looks bleak!
Disastrous, especially the telephone support. I don't think it's worth the effort to go into detail. You could write entire essays.

On board a pm train from Zurich to Frankfurt. Train/trip was cancelled at Basel at 4pm without prior notice and all passengers had to run to find alternative trains. I could have missed all next trips due to this delay. Avoid it if you can!
The only company that did worse than SNCF. Horrible. 4 trains in two days, a missed connection always more than an hour late. It's scary.

Unfortunately reviews do not matter since this is the only train company in Germany. But I am so pissed and I don't know what else can be done except all of us stop buying tickets from this company.I travel for work once a month with DB and literally everything single time, I have to deal with delays or cancellations on their lines.what can I say, I can't even wrap my head around how they manage to stay in business with such an abysmal track record. And it's not just the service that's gone down the drain. The ticket prices are skyrocketing, while the quality of service hits rock bottom. If I forget to reserve a seat, I'm practically guaranteed to be left standing or, if I'm lucky, sitting on the floor.
