I would give negative points, but unfortunately that's not possible. It's late almost every day Can't brake pleasantlyDespite being late, people who are late announce that the train is lateOnly give out a note to prove the delay if it is 5 minutes late (the train was very clearly 9 minutes late)Sometimes come with only one part of the train in order to be even more late due to the train being blocked
Just bad. The German railway is a catastrophe and a collection of incompetence, incompetence and arrogance.

One star for this company is about 3 too many.Excuse the pun, but they're absolute train-wreck.  The term dumpster-fire was invented for this company.I'm British and have lived in Germany for many years.Warning for anyone booking with DB.  You absolutely CANNOT rely on them to be punctual enough to get any connecting train you have.  Leave AT LEAST 2 hours transfer time to account for inevitable delays.Also, don't expect to be helped by any one, or get any info as to why your train is delayed.  You more than likely won't get any.Also, the app is of little use.I have met ex employees of DB who informed me that they just don't care about customer service because they have the monopoly on train travel.Also, most regional trains' toilets are usually either out of order or filthy and don't have soap and water.If travelling in Germany, they can't really be avoided.  Just ensure you leave enough time for connections and expect at least a 30-60 minutes delay, regardless of where you're travelling.
Extremely bad. 28 degrees, no seats because the train is full. Delayed about one hour. In Denmark its bad but this tops it all.

We traveled from Koblenz to Lindau and booked the journey directly at the train station in Koblenz. We had to change trains 4 times as there was no availability on other trains.We arrived in Karlsruhe only to be told that our connecting train had been cancelled. We went straight away to the ticket office to see what our options are. The lady behind the desk tried to find other connections and finally found a connection which cost us an additional 138 €. We had to go back to Mannheim to catch an ICE to Ulm.The ICE 519, our connecting train, to Ulm was so full that the load of people prevented the train from moving. People where standing in the corridors or sitting on the floor. The train driver asked passengers voluntarily to leave the train to reduce the weight so that the train could continue his journey.Surely, the Deutsche Bahn has many „Baustellen“ but I would think that there is a better way to manage this kind of problems. Asking people, who in terms got a valid train ticket, to leave the train because it is totally overbooked is just a disgrace. The gentlemen next to me had to catch a flight from Stuttgart airport but missed it because the train was delayed. I always spoke highly about the German train system but this view has changed. Sorry Deutsche Bahn but you got a lot of work to do.

Deutsche Bahn is the first and only company where I feel 1 star is too much. Over the past 4 attempts to get from Frankfurt to Belgium not a single time they managed to get me there, due to consecutive cancellations and disproportionate delays  (ranging from “train too full” to obscure road blocks other companies like Thalys magically don’t seem to have at that same time). Each time my only rescue was to take Thalys who managed to be reliable at times deutsche bahn is not.There is no communication on getting you to your destination and the refund procedure seems designed to be so complex you don’t get it.In times where we try to shift people away from cars and planes DB is a creator of ambassadors for non public transport. I gave it 4 chances, so I can fairly advise people who need to know they arrive at destination that same day to search alternatives at all cost. It’s a dirty stain on Germany’s reputation for efficiency and reliability.DB is an expensive gamble, and you’re not the bank.

Please avoid DB at all costs. Absolutely awful. The personal, the trains and the website are atrocious in every way shape and form. If you think you're getting your money back when DB screws up, you are sorely mistaken. If you think the workers are going to help you out, I feel bad for you. If you for some outlandish reason believe that DB is the way to go let me know what where I can find whatever it is you're on because in no circumstance has DB ever been a positive experience for me. And this is coming from someone who consistently had to use it, to my misfortune and regret. This is a warning, if you can, avoid DB.

Train to flight, great thing I thought, it worked great a few years ago, but unfortunately it's no longer possible with the DB today. Despite carefully considered long transfer times and actually only 2 trains used (each for the return journey) and actually only 204 km, it was simply not possible. Even before I started the outward journey, I found out that the first train I used had already arrived at my starting station more than an hour late, so bye-bye to connecting trains. Looking for a new connection, first let the neighbor drive 60km by car, the train arrived on time yay, at the transfer station for the last train there was another delay of almost an hour, signal problems, signal box failure, oncoming train on the track, damage to the locomotive, I don't know what else. Luckily the last connecting train was an S-Bahn that took half an hour, yay plane made it. The return journey was the same fun, the last possible train that I could have used due to the delays of the first train was canceled from the start. So I ended up stranded at 11:30 p.m. in a completely run-down train station with no toilet but broken windows everywhere and then had a taxi drive me the last 25 km home. Conclusion: If I had taken the car straight away, it would have been cheaper even with parking fees at the airport and, above all, I would have saved nerves. So if you use the train to get to the flight, please leave 3 days in advance and possibly plan an overnight stay in a hotel, otherwise you could miss the plane, the same applies to the return journey, always have plan B in mind. And then I see DB advertising with the train to events, how long before the start of the event do I have to leave???

Tried to reserve a seat days before my journey but it wasn’t possible. The train was packed, at least 25 people standing just in our wagon. I found it very dangerous. Even the passengers who payed for their seats felt uncomfortable because people were standing next to them. How is this possible? Are they selling more tickets then the number of seats they have? Ridiculous!!! I was traveling from Zürich to Budapest, horrible experience! Toilets are also disgusting and stink

As always, we used (plan to use) Rail and Fly on our journey to the airport and back. The unpleasant experience began with the booking. In the past, a simple voucher was enough for the journeys, but now a comprehensive booking has to be made in the DB portal with infinitely long codes for each journey and each person, which is cumbersome. The specific rail connection is also booked at the same time. The result: on the outward journey there is a delay of over an hour when changing trains (at night at Essen main station - interesting experience -, unclear information about the onward journey, changing the platform 30 seconds before the train arrives, etc.) topped up by insufficient information about the remaining transport to the airport in the DB app (Skytrain didn't run, and as we continued the hectic journey via HBF, there was no S-Bahn connection to the airport for hours. As a result, we had to take a taxi for 30 €). The connection we had booked for the return journey was canceled without replacement, the diversion with replacement rail transport would have taken about 2 hours longer (for a total of barely 100 km. Basically, the experiences of the last few years were confirmed again, so no more Rail and Fly in the future.
Horrible service. Multiple delays and cancellations, it is impossible to plan a trip without losing the whole day

If you want to get stranded somewhere, the train is the right choice. You should try to get a connection on Saturday evening from Frankfurt Airport towards Hanover (Berlin is also in that direction). If you arrive there by plane on such an evening and haven't checked the timetable beforehand, you'll have a problem. But maybe I'm expecting too much.

DISASTER! On the verge of madness. Pure bullshit! Expensive ticket prices and endless delays. As long as the German railway is run by the state and there is no competition in the sense of public transport, nothing will change here. The monopoly position is mercilessly exploited at the expense of the citizens. The only alternative left is the car…

My family and I had a terrible experience on ICE 917 on 13 June 2023. We boarded the train at Frankfurt Airport and were shocked to see the train was full and there were people sitting on the train floor. What was worse was when we found out that the seats that we had reserved were occupied. Although we told them that we had reserved the seats, we were simply ignored and instead were told that it’s not their problem. The train staff was also not able to do anything after we sought their assistance. My husband had to stand for the almost 2 hours before there was an available seat. This could have been prevented if DB made their checks and insist that passengers are seated at the right seats. Staff should also be trained to handle this situation. It was unfair for paid passengers who made the seat reservations as recommended but did not get to sit at the seats that they have paid for.

The train that was supposed to be reserved for May 14-16 was canceled due to the strike. We had no choice but to travel by bus, and after that we tried to process a refund, but we were told that the trains were running and that the refund was not possible because the strike itself had been cancelled. This is an unfair treatment and I think Germans should be ashamed of themselves for pretending to be a developed country while using such public institutions.

I booked my train tickets in advance for my journey with Deutsche Bahn, but unfortunately, a few days before my trip, I received a notification of multiple train cancellations due to strikes. This sudden change disrupted my travel plans, causing inconvenience and frustration.I called their customer support and the representative confirmed the cancellation of my trains and provided guidance on obtaining a refund. They directed me to fill out the Passengers' Rights claim form and send it to fahrkartenservice email address. The customer care agent assured me that in case the train is cancelled, I won't have any issues with returning my funds.So after this call, I changed my trip plan and booked tickets for the bus. Additionally, I had to cancel one of my hotel bookings. After that, I filled out the Passengers' Rights claim form and sent it to the specified email address.However, on the day I was supposed to take the train that was initially canceled, I decided to check the Bahn DE app out of curiosity. To my surprise, I discovered that my trains were no longer canceled. The strikes had suddenly been called off, and the trains were running as planned. Regrettably, I only became aware of this while sitting on the bus, already en route.Since then, it has been a month since I submitted the refund request. Despite sending multiple emails and expressing my concerns, I have not received a single response from Deutsche Bahn. This lack of communication leaves me uncertain if they are even reviewing their emails at all. In my attempts to contact their customer service via phone, I have experienced prolonged wait times of over half an hour, with no resolution or assistance provided.I feel like a sucker who was bred by a gang of scammers for 200 euros. I would never have thought that the German railway was such a scam ...I am still waiting for Deutsche Bahn to respond to my refund request. I hope this review will make them take my claim seriously and address it promptly. It is unacceptable that they have ignored my emails and failed to provide the refund I am owed. I expect them to fulfill their responsibility to their customers and resolve this matter immediately.

DB is a shame and disgrace. Took an ICE train from Düsseldorf to Frankfurt and it nearly took 4 hrs?  The train personnel never sincerely apologized for the delay, kept using execuses that there were 2 regional train ahead of us. Isnt this a f***ing ICE?  Never trust DB and pls avoid it if possible
Unfortunately, it's always late and nothing is said when passengers behave like the ax in the forest. See photo. I've seen a lot of disgusting situations, but here I thought I was dreaming.

Do not use it! I have been living in Germany for 8 years and mainly use DB for transportation. It’s absolutely terrible! Try to use the alrernative like flixtrain. Yes, they aren’t as comfortable or fancy as the ICE, but at least they aren’t always late. For the past month I have been tracking my journeys with DB. 15 journeys , every single one of them late. 6/15 late over an hour. The rest between 20-45 minutes. They also changed the law so you can now only get a partial refund of 20% if the delay exceeds 60 minutes. It used to be a full refund

Today DB made me spend way too much time waiting, so in the meantime I wrote this opinion :)) I spent over 1.5 years living in different cities in Germany and used Deutsche Bahn a lot but... Unfortunately, it rarely happens that I arrive at my travel destination on time. Almost every train I travel with is either delayed, canceled (even a minute before departure), or doesn't stop at the planned station. It also happens that there is no working toilet on a train (you can hear a message that if you want to use a toilet, you can go to another train). Another situation that happens is that before your journey, the DB app informs you about the delay, so you can arrive at the station a bit later, but eventually, the train arrives on time and you miss it (so don't trust the app either). But the worst thing is when the train changes the final destination already during the travel. Moreover, when the travel is finished, no one from the staff checks if the train is empty - it happens that after the night travels there are people stuck in the train.Additionally, all the information they give from the loudspeaker is in German, so not every international traveler understands. The only good thing I can think about is that the trains are modern and in good condition, although the price for a ticket is relatively high, so I think it should be the norm.There are so many uncomfortable situations (some of them are scary) that DB caused me and my friends, I think that it is not acceptable in such a developed country as Germany. I know it is sometimes difficult to find an alternative for DB, but if you prioritize your time and comfort, I recommend choosing another means of transport.
All trains are late. If you think you will get a connection, think twice. You will have to check new connections before and during your trip.
Bad, worse, worst. Always late. You just can't trust the S-Bahn.

I had to deal with the trip, two carriages were packed with people, there was nothing to breathe, the seats were on the floor, on the steps, but one carriage was empty and closed! People were not allowed into this carriage, train E50, Nuremberg-Regensburg, why do people pay money for such a COMFORT???
There is no worse train line in all of Europe !!!! Prefer a bus If I could put 0 I would put Tragic

Train in time and I chose the quiet area. Problem is that women kept on talking  indiscriminately. I thought the German population respected the rules. It appears to be a myth.  Pretty exhausting. Vienna -Frankfurt train 28 Car 22. Nobody complains. Absurd! Where I live, either you’ll be quiet or you’ll be asked to move to the regular area.

It just doesn't get any better. I have been traveling the Bonn - Hanover route for work for over six years and I can advise everyone against traveling with Deutsche Bahn. I avoid arriving on the day of my scheduled appointments if possible because, even with a large time buffer, I often arrive stressed and on the last stretch or still late. Nowadays I usually leave a day earlier so that I can get to work on time. In principle, however, it doesn't matter when you drive and whether you are traveling from Bonn to Hanover or vice versa. I almost always arrive late at my destination station. Two weeks ago, for example, my return journey from Hanover to my home took over 7 hours and just today, during my journey, the journey with the RB 48, at 4:54 in the morning, is completely canceled again and I arrive an hour late again. If only the pricing of the train tickets were appropriate to the service. But it's exactly the other way around. The services are getting worse and the tickets are becoming more expensive.
“Always too late, no real proactive information, overpriced, too full. Take an example from the Danish railway” nothing has changed since then

I thought this was supposed to be an efficient network of trains and they would have figured stuff out by now. We set off at 9+. Train from Boppard to Bonn got stopped halfway because they simply decided to terminate the line. Train started moving backwards to our origin. We got off to get another connection which was then delayed twice. Given the delays+ infrequent trains  we got back to our city at 1+ without anything done. Gave up any ideas of the day trips after the exhaustion. I have much stronger words but cannot type them here. JUST DRIVE IF YOU ARE NOT IN THE BIG CITIES.

We booked tickets from Amsterdam to Basel, Switzerland in DB ICE 255.  Boarding at Amsterdam Central station was absolute chaos.  Absolutely zero security, no one checking tickets or directing passengers where to go.  People were getting in the wrong cars, sitting in the wrong seats etc.  I managed to get on and get our bags stowed.  Just before we departed, two men sitting in front of us, took their bags off the rack and got off the train.  Only after we departed did I realize that they had taken my wife's backpack.  I reported it to the conductor and he said he had seen them leave with a backpack but could not stop them because he didn't want to be accused of "profiling" people.  There was no cash or credit cards in the bag but she did lose her laptop computer.  The conductor told me it happens nearly every day.All this could have been avoided if tickets were checked as people boarded.  Passengers could have been directed to the proper car, non passengers could have been denied boarding and this huge chaotic situation could have been minimized.  At no time on this train were our tickets even checked.  I guess you don't even need a ticket to ride this train.We booked this train because it was direct to Basel - no changes.  About 2/3 of the way through Germany it was announced that the train would terminate at the next station.  We grabbed out bags and ran for the next train.  So much for reserved seats (that I had paid extra for) it was every person for themselves.  After working our way through 2 completely full cars (with our bags) we finally found seats.It would have been cheaper and quicker to fly, but we thought it would be nice to see Germany from the train and that it would be a relaxing day.  Hardly!I doubt I will consider riding DB again.

Incredibly bad company, a hopelessly overwhelmed railway boss Richard Lutz, constant delays, constantly changing train rows, constantly failing toilets, non-functioning software, purchased Germany tickets cannot be loaded into the train app. I've been driving Berlin-Munich every two weeks for years. There are always problems. The company should be broken up and rail operations in Germany should be completely re-tendered to private operators. Otherwise, transport to the European Football Championship in Germany in 2024 will be a disaster.

1 hour late arriving at wurzburg , missed connecting with train at Frankfurt to Strasbourg , got put on another ICE train 2 hours later but had lost our seat reservations so standing or sitting intermittently when there was a vacant seat , the staff at DB assistance counter( Frankfurt) just seemed to be going through the motions ( oh your train was late here’s the next available I can get ) just show them this paper I give you . I wanted to fill out a refund / compensation form there and then but he told me no just fill it out and mail it. No wonder they are loosing money hand over fist. Oh and the biggest issue was that this was another booking on top of one we already had for the same day because DB had failed to advise that the train we had previously booked from wurzburg to AnsBach / Strasbourg had been removed from their schedule so if I hadn’t of checked we would’ve rolled up to the station and No train. Unbelievable they just don’t care

The train is an absolute embarrassment for Germany. If you come from abroad you should be ashamed. Too late, broken, Luat, cancellations, dirty trains and stations...you can't have that many excuses...there's no hope...what are the French, Italians and Swiss doing right?

Germany ticket on May 13th bought. The ticket for €49 ends on May 31st. and from June 1st. 49€ will be collected again. You feel completely ripped off! Conclusion for all routes traveled so far, a good 80% of all departure dates are not kept. You constantly miss your connecting trains. Planning is completely impossible and compensation is practically non-existent. The DB is a disaster in terms of price-performance ratio. One star is still too much.

German train travel used to be marvelous. No more. Our group of 11 American college students and faculty suffered through late connections which forced us to resort to expensive taxis; were screamed at when we lodged a complaint; and froze on the night train from München to Berlin since the heating system was malfunctioning. If there were viable alternatives, l’d never ride another DB train, and I’ll definitely research plane fares for cross country travel.

Was traveling with the ICE from Augsburg to Berlin. I was very satisfied, everything worked out great, very friendly and courteous employees. Have to be honest, it's really a very pleasant way to travel. Gladly again!!!

Deutsche Bahn is simply very unreliable. Unfortunately, I am very dependent on the train and commute to work every day.  And there isn't a week where there are no delays or cancellations! Unfortunately, since I don't live in the city, it's always the case that when my train is canceled, nothing really runs! Not even a bus that was unfortunately discontinued. I take the Brenzbahn from Niederstotzingen to Ulm.  At least there used to be a bus if something went wrong.  Apart from the strike, I have to see how I get to work because then absolutely nothing will work on this route! Something absolutely has to happen!  Especially not only in the 10 km radius of Ulm but also for Niederstotzingen, for example, the 59 bus should definitely run directly from Ulm to Niederstotzingen again like before! Dear government, you want people to use public transport more, but my dear politics, that won't work! That scares people away even more and they will continue to drive their cars 🚗!!

Most recently I gave the track four stars because it had improved a lot. Unfortunately, two days ago both inspectors were very incompetent and hastily printed out an invoice for €60 because they didn't believe that I had a Germany ticket. I had just never used the train app before and was looking for a PDF file, as I usually do with train tickets. The inspector said I should let me know at the counter in Offenbach Marktplatz. "But I don't have to pay anything?!" I asked just to be on the safe side, and the inspector assured me that I didn't have to pay anything. Then I lost time waiting in line, only to find out that I had to pay €7 even though I had a Germany ticket with me. Even if I get the money back, I have lost enough time and therefore money just by having to wait in line for so long and now writing this review. Too bad. If at least the seven euros are not refunded, I will unfortunately have to downgrade one star.

Very interesting experience. I wanted to drive from Linz to Marburg (near Frankfurt). First there was a short delay of 10 minutes in Linz, then there were two technical problems until Passau. About 2 hours late. When everything was back in order with the towing vehicle, it turned out that there was a construction site going on on the planned route. Another 2 hour delay! From Nuremberg things took off and there were almost no more incidents. The only thing that stopped cooling the food was that it was no longer allowed to be sold for food. A real cabaret. Unless it's absolutely necessary, I'll definitely not take the German train again in the future. All in all, there is just too much going wrong. To Deutsche Bahn: Please work on your mistakes. That's not normal...!!!!!!!!!!!!

I haven't arrived anywhere on time yet. Even today I missed 2 consecutive trains, they were 40 minutes behind and instead of going straight to their destination, they still stayed at a stop for 40 minutes instead of catching up.
We waited for many hours because of delays, worst experience for everyone, many complaints and they did not help anyone!!!!!

The Nightmare ExperienceEurostar trains are perpetually delayed, yet EU law mandates compensation for disruptions over 60 minutes—up to 50-75% of your ticket price, no excuses.​After jumping through their torturously designed "claim portal" hoops—uploading scans, endless verification—they hit you with a wall of silence, no refund, no response, pure stonewalling.Avoid at All CostsThis isn't service; it's legalized theft of your time and money, barely skirting legal obligations with zero accountability. Better to walk the Channel Tunnel on foot than trust these crooks ever again!

I’ve travelled with Eurostar every year and love the service, but not the French staff.Rudest ever train conductor yesterday, Phillipe Boucheron: a nasty bully who should not be working on trains or in any public facing role. I asked to sit in the same carriage as my son for the beginning of the journey having booked on a busy service and been seated 4 carriages apart-  he tried to charge me for a new ticket at the same time as telling me that I couldn’t return to the seat I had booked as someone else was sitting there. He shouted at me/my son and threatened to have us taken off the train. When I asked him for his name, he covered his name badge and radioed Lille threatening to have me removed. An absolutely awful experience. Avoid him at all costs: dangerous and nasty. Eurostar, you must do better for your passengers.

I have not travelled on Eurostar for many years, so decided to pay for the Business Premier class - ridiculously, that is ridiculously, expensive. However at least we could avoid the hours long queues for security and the lack of seating waiting for the train. The Lounge is terrible, also crowded, the lift to go upstairs is broken, so good luck if you can't find a seat downstairs and have heavy suitcases. And the only food there are a couple of dry sliced cakes and the odd biscuit!The train to Amsterdam was delayed over an hour, and looking at other reviews, I do not think this was unusual. Coming back it was on time. The on train lunch was the standard we used to get in BA Economy decades ago - not very nice. The wines - Herault - had to look it up - used to be known as the European Wine Lake - are pretty undrinkable. But the worse thing is the lack of support for anyone older, or with a disability, or anyone mad enough to think you could go for a real holiday on Eurostar and not just a 3 day break only bringing hand luggage. There are 4 really high steps up and down from the small doorways, no offer of a ramp, and no-one able to help you carry your suitcase up and down the stairs. There is room at the end of carriages for about 6 suitcases maximum - again thank goodness we were in Premier, not sure what we would have done in Standard.  Our friends had madly planned a month's trip with 4 huge cases, including taking the Eurostar from Brussels to Paris. I have no idea how they did it, they just said the journey was interesting!  So no, I would absolutely never travel on Eurostar again.

We booked a return trip to Amsterdam with Euorostar, standard class seats. Also we booked a Hotel separately. Only four days prior to depature the return train was cancelled. When we tried to book an alternative return train the available prices  increased dramatically. No offers of a similar price let alone a discount for the disruption. What a shoddy way to treat customers. I WOULD NEVER TRUST THEM AGAIN.

First time using Eurostar at the weekend and unfortunately can’t see me using again.  Firstly the holding area is like a cattle pen.  Long queues at passport control, small outlets and nowhere to sit.  Next issue is the trains and lack of space.  We travelled to London in GWR and their trains are so much cleaner with more space.  Toilets were limited.  No point booking seats as they got reassigned both ways from forward facing to backward facing.  The product is dated and not fit for purpose.  When I raised with EUROSTAR got generic response quoting t&c’s and these things just happen.  Not a good experience

Took the Eurostar from Paris to London on a Monday in late September so we could say we'd experienced going through the Chunnel (which is really a ~25min ride through a long dark tunnel).  Loved the train from central Paris to Central London to avoid the hassle of going to/from airports.  We got regular class tickets which were fine and I'd equate to Economy Plus on the airlines.  Our train ran perfectly on time and goes impressively fast at times.  Only thing to be aware of is you go through passport control/customs in Paris before getting to waiting area so head the time they recommend to get to the station.

I’m now in the train from Brussels to Amsterdam. Left at 16:53, supposed to arrive  at 19:20. We just got announcements that we will arrive at 20:45. How great ! I’m an Etoile member for 7 years now and I use this train 6 times a week. Since 1 year the service has deteriorated immensely. It’s delayed every single time. And not by little. This trip costed me 180 euros back and forth , which is expensive and much more than the alternative of IC Direct. But as I need a reliable train I am willing to pay. Well, that is alas increasingly NOT the case anymore. Interestingly, my refund would be 30% should I go through the administrative Mount Olympus to claim it. I am constantly late at work, missing meetings or missing events in my personal life. My advise: if you can avoid Eurostar in any way, just do it. Eurostar Staff is always friendly though and it’s important to remind ourselves they have no blame in this matter.

Travelled to Rotterdam from London St Pancras in September 2025, Eurostar Plus.The train itself was great, spacious, nice seats and reasonable luggage storage.  Provided snack and drink was good (this is the middle of the three classes, the seat being the same as the first class).  Staff were friendly.The only downside was St Pancras Station, it was very busy and the line up for Eurostar was hard to find and very poorly organized with many people pushing in, lining up for the wrong train and so on.  Once in the line, we wound our way past shops and cafes and ultimately towards the check in area for a 15.05 departure.Check in, security and passport control out of the UK and into the EU was OK.  Waiting up in the below platform area was a nightmare, the Paris train was delayed and with two trainloads of passengers with their luggae in a relatively small area, it was uncomfortable and chaotic, when our platform was announced, there was a push through the waiting passengers - it all needs a big shake up.  Perhaps re-commissioning Ebbsfleet and Ashford stations for Eurostar would ease the St Pancras chaos and offer more flexibility for travelling passengers.

When we first traveled by Eurostar it was great but in the last few years the service has been abysmal. Trains are routinely late, some we have been on very, very late, waiting rooms too small, particularly when trains are baking up, and information/communication very poor.  This time we traveled on vouchers given in compensation for trains being very late in both directions in June. Our experience on the way out was much the same; when we arrived the waiting room was crammed as previous trains were late. Our train was late apparently due to the late running of the inbound train in Brussels. When the rescheduled time came along we were told it now had a technical issue and there would be a further delay!  We, as many others, missed our planned connection.  Amazingly the return from Brussels was on schedule.Many of the trains appear to have “technical issues” which suggests Eurostar is not maintaining the rolling stock adequately. The schedule appears to be unrealistic, too many trains, so they are constantly backing up. Although we would like to use the train instead of flying, the stress  of missed connections and expense of rearranging plans and having to use taxis etc means we no longer think it is worth travelling all the way to London for such a bad service.

This company is a nightmare. They are completely devoid of customer service. We were on a train from Paris to Amsterdam when they decided to cancel it in Brussels. We were told we could get another train an hour later. We spoke with the train master who advised us that the other trains were almost full, and we might not be able to get another train. Since we were going out and back on the same day, we had to return to London. The staff was rude and did not help us at all. I also was unable to go online and request a refund because the system is completely antiquated and in my opinion is meant to dissuade you from requesting your money back. You would be better off, walking to your location than riding this nightmare of a transportation system.

Just stop at Ashford International for goodness' sake. You go straight through it. Why should I get the Eurosta all the way to St Pancras just for the joy of getting a trin straightback down to Ashford. Do you realise how many people there are who would use you if you stopped in Kent again?? The whole thing is ridiculous

The outgoing journey was good and with Premier we missed all the queing but at a high cost. The food was ok on the way out too. However on the way back from Paris, OMG it was dreadful. The lounge was awful with hardly anything to eat and when I asked for ice the waiters said not until 11am. I kept saying its just ice but to no avail NOT until 11am ... really odd. The carpets etc were dirty too. The food on the train was awful with no menus so no one could really explain what the options were.  It was costly to go premier and would have expected better.
Ryanair on wheels, toilet dirty, smelly, but no problems with customs, just ticket out to Amsterdam 47 pounds, return 217 to London

We traveled from Paris back to London with euro star train as a family  of 12 people,  on 27 th of November. When we arrived at St Pancras station , I realized one of my luggages was left at the security check point in Paris. I reported this matter to euro star staff, they found my luggage and immediately brought it back to London for me with the next departure train from Paris. I was so grateful for the help from staff of euro star especially Ms Deepa. Their customer service was really amazing. Appreciate!

Eurostar is a great way to travel when the train leaves/arrives without delays.But, unfortunately, my train Rotterdam to London on the 26/10/25 at 19:28 got cancelled 30" before the scheduled departure. The Eurostar staff announced that we should simply re-book a later train on-line.So I tried to re-book online, but the website was down (see photo). So I tried to find Eurostar staff, but they had all left the station. I ended up calling the Eurostar help line: +443432186186, but the number only works until 7pm UK time. So, I booked myself a hotel room for the night and air travel to London for the next day.Afterwards, I tried to get compensated for these additional expenses. After several calls, emails and weeks, Eurostar compensated me for my hotel costs but NOT for my travel costs back to London (local train and flight). I don't think thats fair.

The biggest problem is that it is treated like cattle. On the way there earlier to be present in Rotterdam, but nothing happened there. Then why this instruction? Continuing with a delay changing trains in Brussels, I was yelled at 4 times that I was actually too late but was allowed to walk on for this time. Rather rude. By the way, arrived in the lounge there were still more than 30 minutes left and they say they close 30 minutes before time. The lounge is far too small for all passengers and you are driven like cattle to your platform. No boarding assistance. I wonder if fire safety isn't at stake in the lounge.The situation in London is almost worse. Be present at least 75 min in advance, for what?   The lounge here was completely full with every spot used to wait standing. Capacity really needs to be used differently. Is not safe.The conductors are friendly, food in plus was fine. The chair is ok with sockets.The total journey takes longer than by plane. And instead of waiting in a cattle hall, you can enjoy yourself at an airport.
A big thank you to Pamela for her kindness and welcome, which became so rare in 2025! And besides, a fast and efficient train ride: perfect from start to finish.

The commute from London St Pancras to Amsterdam is seamless. The food albeit small portions was very tasty. The red wine was sublime. (But let’s be honest, the French know there grapes!) . No delays, and a great use of time, to either relax, or work. IMO it is the least stressful way to travel and explore. I can’t wait to embark upon a new journey with these guys very soon.
An absolute shambles from start to finish, glad to get on board to get away from the mayhem. The whole operation is not scaled for the amount of passengers

Train tickets are expensive to get from Paris to Amsterdam. Eurostar sends us a train cancellation with no alternative except a telephone number without people and a website without solution. Then the director and all his staff will be fired by the end of the year for gross misconduct.

Our return trip from London with Eurostar Plus 9152 was a party, smooth trip, good food and extra drinks from Loic and An that made the trip even more enjoyable. See you next time! Greetings to Loic and An.

Took the Eurostar to Rotterdam from London on a business trip. Paid for the euro plus as this gave you a better seating area and food & drinks service. Whilst the travel was acceptable, with a minor delay on the way. The service for food and drinks was less than acceptable. As a pregnant women, there was nothing to accommodate me. The menu options didn’t have anything really suitable. They had no decaf tea or herbal drinks on offer. It just struck me as if the only frequent traveler's are business men who would like an alcoholic drink. The service cart only came around one during the 3hr 30 minute journey. Which when asked if I could get some fruit or water, they said wait for the next service and it never came around again. The staff on the way out didn’t seem to care. At least the staff on the way back did try to provide me some bread to eat. But only one glass of water the whole time.

My friends and I recently travelled on Eurostar (in Eurostar Plus) to Paris as part of my 60th birthday celebrations. All the lovely Eurostar onboard teams in our carriages on both our Paris-bound and London-bound trains could not have been more friendly, helpful and thoughtful.I would just like to personally thank Jean-Paul and Frank from our 9080 Paris-bound train on 31st October and also Kelly, Engracia, Kevin, Paul & Richard from our 9055 London-bound train on 2nd November.Thank you all for making our Eurostar experience so memorable and for making my birthday so special!

Great train service. Like being on a comfortable jet. More luggage space would help.Access is difficult it you have a bag. Elderly people and mums struggled with getting in at Paris and out at London. Poor design.Customs good. Escalator broken and NO to indicate lift 40 m away. Poor planning.Toilets on lower levels are pay at Paris end.
the cancellations and delays are excessive and not communicated well. very very very very very very very very very stupid.

First time using Eurostar as I usually drive. The actual onboard journey was seamless and on time, but the so called 'meal' was dire, if I ever take Eurostar again I will pack sandwiches,  but oh dear, the noise and the chaos at St Pancras, the check in system particularly when you are not used to it, the orders from the tannoy, you need three hands to hold everything, while putting coats, bags etc through the scan while holding your phone for the obligatory checks, and if you left an electronic device in your suitcase, well go to the back and start again!

Woke up at 0615 to see text message saying 0827 train was cancelled. Link provided was uninformative: only confirmed that train was cancelled, no information on options. Had to be back in London before 1100 so bought new, more expensive ticket for 0737 train, the only feasible alternative, and jumped in taxi to get to station. Informed customer service three days ago. Have heard nothing back. Interacted with useless chatbot for five minutes then tried calling. Was on hold for 27 minutes before I gave up. On top of that, the plug in my seat didn't work and the wifi is useless. Complacent, greedy, monopolist. I'll fly next time, at least there's competiion.

Why anybody would fly from London to Paris when the Eurostar runs nearly hourly service boggles the imagination. Whatever post-Brexit wrinkles once made for endless lines and schedule delays have long been ironed out -- except for the invariably crowded waiting area, with its paucity of restaurants and available seating. Once past that, though, the ride remains smooth and pleasant. Whatever small inconveniences you may find are paltry compared to the Dante's Inferno that is the Charles de Gaulle Airport.

The trains are a great way to travel — very fast and efficient. We took the route from Brussels to London. Boarding was a bit hectic, and the waiting area at the station was quite busy but offered food stations and a small duty free store.  Once onboard, the service was excellent, we were served a small meal and beverages. The staff were friendly and polite, and the seats were comfortable and spacious. We were even able to get some work done, and the internet connection was sufficient for our needs. The only downside was that the toilets could have been cleaner. Entering and departing the platforms was smooth, and everything was clearly labeled, which made the process easy.

First our train was cancelled, forcing us to change to a train at an inconvenient time. Then when we went through the gates we found our seats had been changed to table seats, making it difficult for me to stretch out my legs, something which is important to me as I have arthritis in both knees.

Cancelled my train day before departure forcing me to rebook (not straightforward) causing 5 hour delay.  Several failed attempts to claim compensation (which their website states I'm entitled to), 2 enquiry cases later and they're still trying to avoid the issue.   Cut and paste email responses from Lubniov, Oleg, and Vlad (so customer care is somewhere East of Berlin) totally avoid the issue of compensation.   Facebook Messenger interaction leads to more avoidance.  So the disregard for customer service is remarkable!

Far too little legroom for first class. Too narrow (with knees against trash can), too shallow (with knees against chair in front of me) and can't lower platform. Worst first class in all of Europe. And also way too expensive.

I would like to cancel my trip which is possible with the tickets I booked: Two hours of research on the EUROSTAR website, their help center, questin-ins asked on Google: how you can cancel your trip: no answer that gave a result. I filled out a contact form.It's not normal! Never again will I take EUROSTAR to go to Brussels or whatever!

Having booked our seats in 'Eurostar Plus' many weeks in advance in order to sit in a duo, Eurostar changed them one week before departure, meaning that we had to sit opposite other travellers. The so-called breakfast consisted of a choice of either 'a watercress, basil, tomato and cheddar swirl' or 'a chocolate and custard pastry', accompanied by orange juice poured out of a carton and either tea or coffee. We had the pastry and it was tasteless.The train was late arriving in Brussels, too late for anyone who had only allowed 20 minutes for their connecting Eurostar to Cologne.  Fortunately, we had allowed 80 minutes, but it was extremely confusing over how to get to it, as the allocated platform wasn't accessible because other trains were using it. It eventually left about 20 minutes behind schedule and arrived in Cologne even later.Tip - don't use Eurostar, we never will again. If you must use it, don't waste your money by upgrading to Eurostar Plus; take your own food and drink with you.

The smoothest experience ever! Can’t think about going on a plane from London to Paris after experiencing the Eurostar!The staff are also lovely! A big thank you to Philippe and Demba at St Pancras for looking after us, particularly as we were travelling for my mum’s birthday! Amazing service and will be back soon!

Super convenient and fast!Taking the Eurostar from Paris-Nord to London St Pancras, then again vice versa has been absolutely the right way to go!We had booked ferry tickets from Portsmouth to Caen, and were going to train down from London on Southern Railways. I'm so glad we decided to change the booking and go Eurostar! Easy access in Gare du Nord, there actually are a lot of amenities past border control. They have many cafés and to-go places, and boarding is quite easy from that station. Both Gare du Nord and St Pancras have automated border controls which are accessible from 10 years old. You cross both borders at your departure station.Eurostar seats are comfortable and offer more legroom than any plane or train I've ever been on! Definitely worth the little extra cost. From St Pancras, you can be in Central Paris in just 2 hours!On the train, amenities include an (extremely) overpriced café. Please pay in euros at the café, because this makes it cheaper.If you're planning to work or log in on the train, Eurostar WiFi has 1 hour free. Usually it's nice and fast, but sometimes it slows down. Don't let that full WiFi symbol stump you. It is wrong and it's designed to show this even in the tunnel (no WiFi or signal there!). So, if you're planning to use the WiFi, I recommend logging in immediately at boarding; then to take a pause in the tunnel; and continue on hotspot in the destination country.Here's a tip : fill up your water bottle before going! Water does go through security at both stations and that's way better than paying 5€ for a little can onboard.The entry process in Gare du Nord is simple if you arrive early enough to beat the queues. Make sure you have at least 2 hours in Paris before the train leaves.In ticketing process, you go through turnstile gates by scanning your boarding pass on your phone. This should be accessible via your confirmation email Eurostar sent you.At Gare du Nord, the departing hall is usually less crowded than St Pancras, which can have nowhere to sit, stand, or do really anything.Arrival at St Pancras is really easy and just includes a couple twists and turns through the station. All in all, I believe St Pancras is too small a station for its amount of trains.At Gare du Nord, the departing hall was spaced out and had a more secure, comfortable atmosphere. There were many benches but the bathrooms were not glamorous.At St Pancras, however, they even did extra luggage checks before boarding : and we had already cleared passport control! The bathrooms were dirty and uncomfortable.In summary, Eurostar is definitely the way to go if you're going from France to the UK or vice versa if you don't mind the cost.

I am a frequent Eurostar passenger and I am writing this as a direct warning to anyone considering travelling with them. After numerous trips, my experience has been consistently disappointing and, frankly, unacceptable given the premium prices charged.My repeated problems include:•Toilets frequently out of order. On multiple journeys the toilets were not functioning properly or were unusable, which is unacceptable for long-distance travel.•Carriages and compartments smell and are not thoroughly cleaned. I have repeatedly found compartments that smelled and showed obvious signs of poor cleaning; it did not feel hygienic.•Train managers’ behaviour: rude, unprofessional and at times aggressive. I have encountered several train managers who were dismissive, rude and unhelpful..•Apparent abuse of authority. From my point of view, some staff members seem to use their position to shut down passengers’ concerns rather than help them; I witnessed behaviour that felt like an unnecessary exertion of power.•First-class catering is far below expected standards. Food served in first class often appears and tastes not fresh — meats looked questionable, bread seemed stale, and the water used for tea sometimes appeared unclean. For the price of first class I expect basic food hygiene and quality, which I did not receive.•Overall impression: a company that markets itself as premium but repeatedly fails on cleanliness, customer service and basic onboard standards. After so many disappointing trips, I feel Eurostar gives the impression of caring for passengers while in practice passengers are regularly let down and their money is not respected.This is not a single isolated incident — these are repeated issues I have personally experienced. If you value cleanliness, respectful staff and decent onboard food, be cautious: my experience suggests you may be disappointed.To Eurostar: please take passengers’ reports seriously. Improve maintenance so toilets work, enforce higher cleaning standards, review and retrain staff on respectful customer service, and overhaul your first-class catering quality. Paying customers deserve consistency and basic respect

A disaster from start to finish. Seats already changed on departure: everyone scattered throughout the train. And left a little over an hour late, still 20 min standing still in Lille... on departure now the same - everyone changes places again so we are scattered again. The city is completely unhelpful and very rude... but there is no competition for sure...

Gote crowded the station.  St. Louis. Pancras. Long lines. Line for Paris was the same as the one for Amsterdam.40. mim in line until check in with ticket. Then sevurity, and passport control. Train was delayed by 1 hour and 15 minutes. There was too little seating, many people sat on the grunt for hours.,,For sometimes not the eurostar again.

Truly terrible customer experience.Bought a £350 travel voucher for my mum's birthday. She was unwell over the summer and couldn't get around to booking her trip. We accidentally let it get to 1 day over the expiry date. Tried to call to discuss with customer services - was on hold for 1h30 and gave up. Raised a ticket via their online form. It took them a full month to respond, and when they did, they just said "no chance" with some basic boilerplate. No attempt even to engage with the circumstances around the request, or offer any goodwill extension.I get that it was my own fault for letting the voucher lapse, but how can you have such uncontactable, inflexible customer service? Money wasted, lesson learned; don't buy vouchers from them and don't even think about attempting to contact their customer services.

Absolutely terrible experience. Delayed train, no working WiFi onboard, outdated train, no updates from staff. Appalling experience,  always take a plane instead or just stay at home and avoid the stress.

Stay in London, 1 hour delay on the way, no compensation, catastrophic return organization, we are made to wait to prioritize a train that leaves only 4min before ours. During our wait the sign shows that the door has just closed, the staff has no reaction and seems to be experiencing the events. Suffice to say that for Eurostar fares over 100th for just over 1h30 train the Service really leaves something to be desired. Next time it'll be the plane even if it means increasing the ecological footprint, at least I wouldn't feel like I'm being mistaken for a pigeon.
The ticket was not affordable.The cafe closed early and the guy just said it was too late. Long lines, so glad I came early.Next time I'll take small planes which are cheaper.

I love to travel by train when I am in Europe. The Eurostar is really the best way to get from London to Paris.  St Pancreas station is really clean with a lot of restaurants and retail stores, very clean and easy to find a place to sit-down. Check in is a breeze, there is always some to help if you have a problem with the passport machines. No need to take toilet articles out of your bag, just leave them in the bag and they send them thru the X-ray machines. Once pass security you have to wait for your platform to be available before they open the doors for you to enter, so you have to wait in a large waiting room with limited seating and a few fast food shops, they say if you travel first class their waiting room is much better, but the difference is the fare is hard to justify paying more.  The train seating is comfortable with large windows to view the landscape, I was seated at a table for four that I shared with 3 travelers from Australia. The trip took about 2 and a half hours, it was a comfortable ride and we arrived at Gare du Nord where I could easily catch a taxi to my hotel.

Our train was firstly cancelled,  then the alternative one 3.5 hours to get u back to London. This was due to the previous train hitting an animal, causing damage to the train and the track. Therefore  our train was stuck. The manager announced several times that we were entitled to compensation,  but upon applying the response said that we weren't eligible.  Absolutely outrageous.

We took the eurostar direct from St Pancras International to Amsterdam Central. Would recommend the eurostar. 4hrs direct. The food choice could be improved but the ham and cheese baguettes we had were really good. Good choice of drinks. Seats were okay.  The return was direct. Easy to get through security in the UK and in Amsterdam. Would definitely use again.

The Eurostar itself is wonderful - often runs on time, quick journey, comfortable, a joy! What drives me mad is the lack of Internet everywhere! I can't get the WiFi or my 5g to work in the London terminal, the WiFi on the train is a joke. So so frustrating as I can get excellent WiFi on a plane, but not on a train. Incredibly frustrating.
Travelled from Brussels South to London by Eurostar and back again. That went just fine. Good seats, the wifi on the train worked, as did the charging points.

Travelled from St Pancras to Gare du Nord, then on to Munich for Oktoberfest. Fairly long queue at check-in, but moved quickly, the Eurostar staff are good at keeping everyone moving. Security and passport control efficient, we had enough time for some tea in the departure lounge then onto the train. Departed and arrived on time. Getting to Brussels a few days later for our return journey was a nightmare thanks to DB’s dreadful timekeeping, we missed our booked train, but Eurostar staff put us on the next departure as soon as we arrived. Journey home fine. Well done Eurostar, as ever.

I had an incredibly frustrating and disappointing experience with Eurostar that not only disrupted my journey but also threw off my entire travel plans. I arrived at the station well ahead of my scheduled departure time, expecting a smooth process. Instead, I was met with chaotic and poorly managed queues that stretched throughout the terminal. There was no clear signage, no staff actively managing the lines, and no communication about delays or procedures.Despite arriving early, I spent an excessive amount of time stuck in queues for security and passport control, both severely understaffed and disorganised. There was no prioritisation for passengers with imminent departures, and no one available to assist those clearly at risk of missing their trains. It felt like a complete disarray.By the time I reached the gate, my train had already departed. A Eurostar staff member told me to go to the ticket desk and assured me that my ticket would be exchanged for the next available train free of charge due to the circumstances. That seemed fair and reasonable.However, when I got to the ticket desk, I was told I had to pay £44 to make the exchange. I explained what I had just been told, but the staff member refused to honor it. Even after a supervisor spoke to her directly, she still insisted I pay. There was no flexibility, no empathy, and no accountability for the conflicting information I had received from Eurostar’s own staff.This miscommunication and lack of coordination between staff members is unacceptable. What should have been a straightforward resolution turned into a costly and stressful ordeal. The delay caused me to miss a connecting appointment at my destination, which had knock-on effects for the rest of my day.Eurostar seriously needs to improve its customer service, staff training, and internal communication. Passengers deserve clear, consistent information and fair treatment especially when delays are caused by the company’s own operational issues.Given the circumstances and the misleading information I received, I trusted Eurostar to deliver a reliable service, and this experience fell far short of that expectation.
Checkin quiet, travel withBritish punctuality. It was a great family experience. Free shop not disappointed, perfumes and creams with great prices.

Paris to Amsterdam Central. An utter god awful experience. Train was late in a cold wind blasted Gare Du Nord for 30m. And then in Rotterdam, cancelled entirely and dropped into local trains with all the baggage, lack of info. Local trains naturally aren't equipment for luggage, or accessibility for all the Eurostar passengers that were abandoned into it, and added another hour to an already extended trip. The need to haul baggage to catch a train across unknown terminal injured my hand. So it trains were about the same, honestly didn't expect it to be as bad as it was.

Read the recent poor reviews,  but my experience of a London to Brussels return trip to visit friends was great. There was a big queue on arrival outside the terminal but it was well organised, staff made clear where to queue and despite its size, I only spent 15 minutes clearing the huge queue, security and passport control!. The  terminal inside is quite small for the number of trains served and there is only one Pret food outlet to get a coffee or snack, but my timing was good and there were lots of seats and no queue in Pret!. Journey itself was hassle free there and back. All this on a Eurostar promotional price of £70 return ..incredible value, and of course incredible to be in the centre of Brussels from London in only 2 hours…well done Eurostar and thanks.

My recommendation is to arrive 75 min EARLY. We arrived 75 min early and those who arrived an hour early were in an insanely long line.  I've read they stop allowing you to scan your tickets 30 min prior to boarding, so if you arrive 45 min in advance and the line is super long, you may not get through the first hurdle Stop #1 which is scanning your boarding pass. The first priority is making sure you are at the right train terminal in Brussels (which is called two different names for the same station, midi and zuid). Enter in the station on the Eurostar side by the taxi line. Walk inside about one min and on the right side there are ropes for the international Eurostar line. Stand in that line and stop #1 is to scan your boarding pass. Stop #2 is to have all of your luggage and belongings go through the 2 slow security lines (that took us 20 min alone). Stop #3 is to show your passports on the Belgium sideStop #4 is to show your passports on the London/UK side 5 min later. It took us 45 min to get through those 4 stops- then 5 min to walk to the waiting room for the train so 50 min in all and we arrived 75 min early. The line after we arrived was 10 x longer. Also, while it left on time, it was 30 min late into our station in London- Eurostar claimed there were speed reductions in the UK, so please take that into consideration if booking connections.

We were gifted a voucher for Eurostar so we booked London to Amsterdam. The train journey itself was fine, we paid the extra for Plus and glad we did. The meal was ok, nothing fancy but pleasant enough. Train was bang on time at all stations and arrived on time into Amsterdam. However, St Pancras is a disaster. The station itself was packed, no seats, toilets all closed at same time for cleaning. Check in for train was mad, long queues that did move relatively quickly I suppose but very  few staff to guide people. Once in the “lounge” after passport control the fun started. A lounge not fit for purpose. Packed beyond capacity, all seats taken and passengers everywhere and I mean everywhere. I’m sure it is a health and safety risk. Once a train was called there was literally a stampede for the platform up the travelator. The lounge was cleared briefly, you grabbed a seat and within minutes it filled up again. We were called for our train and joined the crush for the train, big gap between platform and train with 2 steps up, awkward to get a suitcase and yourself across and no one to help you. Then you have to work out for yourself where to put your luggage. As I’ve said the journey itself was pleasant enough but definitely not St Pancras and I would not recommend it

We traveled between Antwerp and Amsterdam and it was somewhat messed up.  The train before us was very late and when it arrived, we tried to board without checking and the Eurostar staff did not check out tickets;  they just let us board.  And of course our seats did not exist, so they had another passenger move to accommodate us.  Then they had run out of menu selections for the breakfast and what they served was worse than airplane food.  But the seat was comfortable.

Monopoly does not justify this abysmal CX. Eurostar take their customers for granted. Their pricing system is extortionate for the service. The experience in terminals is next to zero. Not to mention onboard when things go wrong. No fault on the staff. All on the management. People can’t wait until competition is introduced and when it happens it will be payback.

Never been treated with such contempt!Booked a table as we were travelling with young children.Less than a week before travelling we were bumped without warning to different seats.Tried in vain to contact Eurostar customer services however despite multiple contacts to get a resolution NEVER replied to!At the station discovered that Eurostar had changed the train to a smaller configuration, apparently for their own advantage!Hate being ignored but in addition hate being treated with such contempt when it's for their own advantage!The sooner this monopoly is broken up the better...

The Eurostar experience was much better than I had anticipated having read so many bad reviews. The outbound train was on time and the inbound from Brussels half an hour late. I paid for Premier travel and that was well worth it. It was good to have the lounge at St Pancras. Service on the train was efficient and friendly and meal good. The only aspects I didn't like were the crowds at boarding time - you have to join the crowds on leaving the lounge to find the platform and your coach on the train - and getting on and off the train with suitcases is not easy. There are two steps up and a gap between train and platform which I found awkward. The journey itself was smooth and fast. would use this service again.

If I could give it 0 stars, I would! Last time i used Eurostar was summer 2022 in standard premier (now Eurostar plus) both ways. The trip was wonderful on that occasion and I did not want to leave the train. Fast forward to August 2025 and I would like to get my money back although they have refused.Outbound journey to Paris was 8am on a Sunday from London. Huge queues to check in but they moved relatively quickly. On board was the issue as we travelled standard outbound. Cramped, (not a seat spare) and so noisy. The woman in front of me had a baby on her lap (not a separate seat) that kept kicking my legs, that’s how close the seating is. To make matters worse, another train ahead (although I think it was TGV) hit an animal so we were delayed by over an hour as the train sat on the tracks. Money was returned for the delay. However, on the way back we were on Eurostar plus. Again, that was busy. We were served a tasteless, cold pasta sort of dish with veg. My child with allergies couldn’t eat so we asked for a cheese sandwich and told we had to buy it despite paying hundreds more to sit in Plus. My child ended up eating nothing. Have been through an agency that helps to deal with Eurostar but they have still refused to refund on the meals. Eurostar is not what is was and people are betting off flying!

Return from London to Brussels, by the last train of the day one evening in November. Shortly after boarding the passengers, a delay of one hour is announced for a problem in the Euro tunnel. Delay which then lengthens to two hours before the train is completely removed.  More than 600 passengers disembarked, having to change their reservation online and find a place on a train the next day, and for many, search for a hotel room. As a previous train was cancelled, all hotels in the relative vicinity are fully booked. Of course, Eurostar staff cannot "invent" hotel rooms, but leave 600 passengers in decanters....? alternative solutions must be devised for this kind of situation, which is unfortunately no exception.

Used to be a weekly traveller on Eurostar. I cannot believe the decline in customer service. I tried to change tickets online. Not possible. Phone calls not being taken. Contact forms not replied to. Literally receiving a generic email in reply saying we assume your query dealt with so send another form. After sending about four forms I again received a general response saying they hadn’t had time to deal with them. Spent an hour and a half on the phone to obtain a refund. Not processed properly. Spent another almost an hour to again obtain the refund. Adviser said he could do nothing about my complaint and quite rude that I was complaining.  Even gave me an email address to send him info which didn’t even work. Complete waste of my time and Eurostar isn’t doing the basics. Sadly I would say fly if you can.

Took from Paris to London with my granddaughter. Paid to upgrade our seats to include a meal served at our table. When the staff got to our table we were informed that they had no more meat options and we were offered a left over gluten free vegetarian dish that was not appetizing at all and we declined. Ended up having to walk several cars through the train to purchase sandwiches and drinks. I did reach out to Eurostar and they offered me a small voucher to use in their trains in the next year, when I requested reimbursement for the lunches I had to buy. As I won’t be in Europe again for in the next year  this is totally useless. My advice is not to upgrade your ticket and just go regular status and bring your lunch with you.

It was a disappointing experience. Everything was fine at the St Pancras end, in fact itcwas very very good, but the journey itself was not as comfortable or special as I had imagined it would be. Long queue to get refreshments too  from an inadequate food outlet. The worst part was arriving in Paris, however, where the platform was old and tatty and the huge gap between train and platform was dangerous. Would not like to travel again on Eurostar.

What a bother to get up the stairs and wait for ever to cross a long bridge. Everything of an international service it is not. Tucked away, hidden in the rafters of a station. You have to bow your head to get through scanners, and why two of them ? For god’s sake. The only easy bit was getting a passport stamped, a kid would have taken more notice than the bloke at the desk - no wonder so many illegals get in by chancing it It's a cheap third world, hidden in the corner junk shop operation, what exactly is it that is meant to be international ? No information at all. Tried to ask to get into the office on ground floor, an ignorant French man simply refused me entry - stated I had to go upstairs - upstairs is packed due to very bad organisation and nowhere to put people - yet downstairs certainly had customers within as for duty free, our corner end shop has more to offer at cheaper pricesthe end security x-ray was screwed, of 6 or so available, another ignorant French man kept pushing the queue to the one that was working, the second out of service - whilst, the four the other side of the low steel work, were free flowing - you employ the dumbest of the dumb and steal good money from paying customers - employ competent people and manage the flow of people-this bloke simply didn't know what he was doing and compounded issue by simply doing the same, push all to one working x ray Far easier to get to an airport, clear regulates and jump on a plane, it's cheaper, far more efficient and much better service - their must not be returning customers who live outside of London or Paris - you would not travel to get on this train

A horrible experience with them. They have cancelled our group booking without any notification and don’t send any payment reminders. Be careful. They consider themselves fully in their right as they see this as policy. They forced us to pay 2300€ more for exactly the same seats. I have never been treated so badly by a company.

I have travelled many times on Eurostar. This time it was as always on time. The train is comfortable but always very full. The waiting areas as all stations are very poor. This time both security and pass port control were very quick and easy. I travelled Eurostar plus in the outward journey. Seats are large and more comfortable, particular if you are a couple and get the dried with just two seats facing each other. The food service was okay with free drinks, however the food itself was poor

Despite the delays, the trip went well!!! The flight crew is very friendly. Thanks to the controller who called the hotel for me, because I was afraid of losing my room reservation.Frankly top!Thank you and good luck

Absolute shambolic service, the CEO should resign.We booked Eurostar to Brussels outgoing trip was fine but the waiting for our train at St Pancras is totally shameful.People of all ages cattle forced into areas with no seating due to overcrowded departure areas.On the return from Brussels, the departure lounge was a building site ,no cafe for drinks, no water,no help either, the train itself was a disgrace, when we boarded and found our upgraded seats, we noticed the carriage door at the end next to our seats was broken.I challenged the train manager why we weren’t told, a shrug of shoulders is the reply.When the train departed the noise from the wheels and boogies was horrendous.The noise was extremely loud, added to this our seats at the end carriage had a toilet a few yards away so this meant while eating food the odours from the toilet was sickening.I did complain but they refused to move my wife and I to another carriage.I found out that the automated door was broken on the way out, and had been. for a long time and was not repaired.This carriage and passengers should have been warned.I sent in a complaint to the CEO, this has been ignored no reply or response.So much for the passenger charter they preach.An absolute disgrace the CEO should resign the amount of complaints are unbelievable, which Eurostar try to hide but not today.Check your seat near the end carriage and the automatic doors close.

My mum and I travelled on Eurostar plus to and from Amsterdam.  The check in at St Pancras was relatively swift but the waiting area to board is crowded with not enough seats.  The train itself was great although the cold food was a bit meh and my low salt offering was ok, but the panna cotta was just wet and horrible.  On the return journey the waiting area in Amsterdam was a bit crowded but not as bad as London.  They did not provide a low salt meal even though I had ordered it, so lucky I had brought my own sandwich.  It would be good if they offered decaf options for hot drinks too, which they didnt appear to do.  I wonder how chaotic it will be in December when the new post Brexit (what a stupid idea that was) finger printing checks etc are I operation.

Total chaos on St. Louis again. Pancras Int. In the Eurostar waiting area. Far too many travelers in a far too small space. Travellers are driven around like a long way. Disrespectful way of treating customers. For this reason, I'm taking a plane from now on.
Always mega mega chaos at waiting area at St Pancras. You’re reduced to cattle. It’s a disgrace! (I feel for the people who work there every single day🥺)

Eurostar is a mixed experience.On the positive side, the trains themselves are comfortable, reasonably clean, and our outbound journey to France ran on time. The actual travel once on board is smooth and pleasant.Unfortunately, the wider service leaves a lot to be desired. Our return was delayed entirely due to the disorganised and inadequate security setup at Gare du Nord. We had arrived 1.5 hours before departure, as instructed, but the queues were so poorly managed that we would have missed the train had it not been held back for the hundreds of passengers stuck in security.At both London and Paris, the waiting areas are completely insufficient for the number of travellers, leaving them overcrowded and uncomfortable.To add to the frustration, weeks later I am still chasing a £75 reimbursement from the purchase, with no meaningful response from Eurostar’s customer service other than being told they are 'dealing with a high number of complaints'. I can see why!In short, the trains are fine, but the service at either end and the lack of aftercare make the overall experience disappointing and not what you would expect for the price.

St. Pancras is a lovely station with a good selection of shops and cafés. However, once you go through security checks is when the real issues start. The waiting area is horribly over crowded. There are not enough seats to host anyone, in fact because so many people sit on the floor in the corridors it's nearly impossible to get through. I cannot imagine the overcrowding is compliant with fire safety regulations. If even one train is slightly delayed it becomes truly impossible. All these people together also means it becomes very hot and smelly. The trains themselves are fast and efficient. But for the cost of the tickets the waiting area over crowding needs to be sorted

NEVER AGAIN.  What a Terrible Bad Service this is. Train trip to London was cancelled last minute, now you could book a hotel up to €170, otherwise there was NO communication nothing. They simply cannot be reached by phone, and also via a contact form. On the night itself, the staff were super arrogant, helped nothing and quickly closed the door. More than 200 people at Rotterdam Central Station, no one knew what to do...... Really Bad Service. I'm still waiting for my compensation.

We took the Eurostar from Paris to London. The process was seamless. We booked online and picked our seats. Last minute, we decided to see if there were any available seats in an emptier car, and were able to switch our seats free of charge. When you get to the station, they only let you go through security up to 2 hours beforehand, so coming any earlier would be a waste of time. The security check line wasn't very long and moved quite quickly. If you have VAT refunds, you have to go through security first, as the refund machines + refund agents are located right after you pass security. The process for VAT refunds was also fast and seamless. After security, there's two cafes you could get food at, but everyone seemed to be lined up at the first one, but if you keep walking, there's another cafe further down. Our trip was delayed 30 minutes but it wasn't too much of a bother. The ride was smooth and quick. The cafe/bar car on the train didn't have much variety and there wasn't much to buy or eat, maybe a light snack? So that was disappointing.But overall, I think taking the Eurostar is much better and faster than flying because the Eurostar station is within the city and you don't have to waste time going further away to the airport, plus security is much more lax than an airport. Also, staff was super nice, friendly, and helpful.
The train was punctual, fast and looked after me with the priority boarding which I would recommend. Queuing was a pain but still quite civilised and not a scrum

Arrived early discovered our train was unfortunately cancelled , young lady bent over backwards to get us on the earlier train to accommodate our connections, return journey was as good as outward, food very good and seats very comfortable in premier

The check-in/security/passports at Gare du Nord is complicated, poorly signed and made worse by people like me who can't quite work out what's going on. I'm a very experienced traveller and if I find it tricky then others will be

Trip that went very well on the way (Paris-London). On the other hand the return was quite eventful due to our cancelled train, so rush to Pancras, to catch the train that left before ours we come across a very long queue but the staff is available and it goes quite fast (we do not struggle with the children) then on the train it is a whole different story.Cannot pay with his card at the bar because the machine was not working (weak network?). So after many refused attempts, I am still debited in deferred despite the amount that does not display on their TPE. To make me pay back an endless wait by the bar.Fortunately Albert and Jade from the Paris base (😉) were there to handle the situation and did everything possible to make this wait pleasant. They've been taking care of themselves and working out a solution with their managers so I can get my money back. Have Jade and Albert on your trains!Thanks again to them both.

We were travelling from Paris to London and I would say this would have to be the worst trave experience of all. The whole check-in & baggage check process was pathetic and getting on the train with baggage was almost impossible. A terrible experience overall, never again!
Horrible experience for disabled people. Be warned the facilities and services for passengers needing wheelchair assistance is non existent!
