Had a very pleasant train ride from London to Lille. All the staff were so lovely especially Nelly who made the trip so much more enjoyable with her kindness

If you value unreliable arrival times, and foul coffee, this is your train!Both our trip to the Netherlands, and back to London were an hour late, technical difficulties are common with this train apparently. And my word! Do NOT waste your money on the coffee, Yuck!!!

I used it for the London-Paris round trip, but I had an uncomfortable time on both trips. On the way, we had an awkward time with strangers sitting in four seats, with seats reserved in advance changed without prior notice. It got hotter as we got closer to Paris, but we had no choice but to stay muggy with no air conditioning. On the way back, I was able to sit in the seat I had booked, but I was very uncomfortable when a French passenger sat next to me extended himself to his seat. Internally, electronic message boards were telling us to have a comfortable trip with Wi-Fi, but Wi-Fi was rarely available for both trips. It was a really awful experience, like a game of punishment, except it was affordable.
Overpriced, and always late…. when then don’t cancel your train. I have had issues 6 times out of the last 8 times I used that service.We seriously need to have competition to Eurostar!!
For our visit to Paris booked with Eurostar. We could get from Aachen to Paris for a reasonable price. The trip took just over two hours and then we were in Gare du Nord. Definitely worth repeating.

Train delayed from 1201 hrs to 1731 hrs 'due to technical problem' in August 2025. Spent 5.5 hrs extra at St Pancras sitting on the floor as not enough seating available. Eurostar staff were unhelpful and rude. The place is like a Sunday market. Now they are offering me a voucher of less than 50% of the cost of that leg (calling it an exceptional gesture!) whereas their website states a 75% voucher compensation for the leg affected if the delay is more that 3 hours. Appalled and will never travel by Eurostar again!

Booked tickets in advance and had to make an amendment to tickets day before travel , price had increased by double resulting in me paying £192 one way London to Paris, certainly does not match their advertising of £44 one way..

Fast and clean, Eurostar to and from London is the best way to get between major European cities. St. Pancras station is easy to navigate and everyone proved to be friendly if directions were required. There is luggage storage available for quick side trips to see some sights before travelling onward.The Eurostar Premium lounge is on a par with any good airline lounge.The one issue is luggage handling; you must handle your own bags. No bag check-in is available, even in Premier, and the walks to your coach can be intimidatingly long.

Delay of 1h05 from Dusseldorf and 55min on arrival in Paris! For Eurostar this does not justify any compensation since the delay in arrival is less than 1 hour!Moreover, the train is really old, the “bar” reduced to a wheeled box! The proposed timetables between two major cities are worthy of a TER network in an abandoned region. It really feels like Eurostar is doing everything to discourage customers from choosing the train instead of the plane or the car! Yet another demonstration that Europe is not living up to its environmental commitments!

Overall a great trip. Even though the station was incredibly busy at St Pancras, the crowds were dealt with efficiently without drama and noise. The staff on the train are very curtious and friendly.  Lovely, tasty meal in Eurostar plus.  The toilet though is what we experience often on travel. Grimbsy docks smells better! The outside of the toilet bowl needs cleaning more than the inside! Grim. It’s an easy fix.

The train from Paris to London was great.  The train was clean, the staff was very friendly, and they met our dietary restrictions upon advance request.  It was well worth the money.  I docked them a star because they changed the departure time which messed up our transportation schedule to the depot in Paris, but mainly because an older couple was allowed to move to seats near us without having to pay extra.  They were real proud of themselves and staff did not want to create a problem.

Despite the fire incident on the train — which, shockingly, had also occurred the week before — my experience with your service was extremely disappointing.Not only did the journey take over 10 hours instead of the scheduled 3, with multiple stressful changes, but there was also no compensation offered for the lost time and inconvenience, only water during the wait when doors were locked and no fresh air access. Additionally:For the train affected by the fire, you only offered a 75% refund instead of 100%, which is unacceptable given the circumstances.For the return train, which deviated from the original itinerary and took 7 hours instead of 3, you only offered 25% back.After this, I had to chase your team for the refund, which still has not been received. The only response I get is to "contact my bank," but you have not provided any reference or proof of payment, leaving me unable to follow up with my bank.This experience has been beyond frustrating, and I will never travel with Eurostar again.

We recently travelled to Paris by Eurostar, and were lucky enough to go Business Premier. Security and other checks were streamlined, and the business lounges, both at St. Pancras and the Gare Du Nord, were pleasant. (The return trip from Paris took place on a public holiday, and the lounge at the Gare Du Nord, often crowded, was very quiet). The on- board staff were friendly and efficient, and the food (lunch on the way out, and dinner on the way back), was delicious. All in all, a pleasant way to travel (much more relaxed than flying), and a great way to start and end a holiday.

My train was cancelled with two hours' notice. I could possibly get a place on another train that day for a minimum of 270 pounds, though other trains that day were also cancelled, so there's no guarantee that even if I had paid, I would have been able to take the train. Trains were also cancelled the day before and the day after, so the service is very chancy. I was in the very fortunate position of being having friends in London I could stay with, but there was no compensation offered for the extra travel and meals;  if I had had to find a hotel room, at last minute (in London in August!) I don't know what I would have done. No help was offered by Eurostar. Arriving for my train the next day, the station was in chaos. I have mobility issues, and very little help was offered. Going through security, despite my issues (I have a cane so it's pretty obvious), the woman who was overseeing the process nearly knocked me over in trying to get trays out for other people, didn't leave me space to put my things on the trays, and snarled at me when I made a comment. The departures hall was also in chaos. They ask people to arrive two hours early but only post the departure quad 20 minutes before the train leaves. There are about 10 seats for hundreds, if not thousands, of people.

Book early for best rates and to seat 4 at a table, clean, comfy, & fun! Stations on each end are a bit chaotic, but they do their best. We saved over $2000 for our family of four travelling LA to Paris by flyng into London instead & taking EuroStar!

Booked on London to Aachen via Brussels. St Pancras was like a refugee camp with the queue stretching on forever.  Eventually got on the train to miss the connection at Brussels.  Crammed onto a later train (we had bought plus tickets). Return was similar with the first train late. No updates or apologies from staff. We had 15 minutes to sprint across the station. We try to travel less by plane to be reasonably eco friendly, but will not be enduring the hell of Eurostar ever again

We usually fly for our European city breaks but we thought we’d give Eurostar a go for a change. Never again. Both outbound and inbound journeys painfully slow and delayed, massive queues and overcrowding. Writing this whilst waiting in a makeshift waiting area I wouldn’t keep my dog in as our   Return Eurostar train journey has been delayed. Save yourself ALOT of money and time by flying.
Interesting prices and times. However, it was possible to go to the very unpleasant and unkind personal return.

We left two and never together scattered in the train on the way out, Train cancelled on the return , parked like animals at London station (Cannot sit for more than 1 hour) and again scattered in the train back. Inedible meal in 1st class. Oh yes!!!! it is well indicated free WI-Fi throughout the journey but do not dream it absolutely does not work!!!!! It was the first time in Eurostar and the last , Airplane for next times!!!!

Two days ago. You would think a two day trip to Paris on the Eurostar train would be the way to go. Worked well getting there but returning Paris to London was TERRIBLE. Never again. I was shunted from one queue to another. Standing for 2hrs, no seats, like cattle herded in small spaces. I don’t go often but this is the 3rd bad  time in a row so I’ll never go by train again.

Booked our ticket from London to Paris on Eurostar Plus, with specific seats as two of us have anxiety and similar travel related issues. The train was supposed to depart at 3:31pm. Until 3:15, there was no announcement, and then there was about a delay of 20 minutes. The delay then stretched to 40 minutes by the time the train actually started moving. Worst thing: they changed our seating and our coach and gave us backward facing, individual seats. We took it up with the steward Karl who refused to offer any help. Once the journey started, air conditioning in multiple coaches malfunctioned, so they had to adjust passengers from those coaches to other spots. We had requested Halal meal; it was a light quinoa slaad, with grilled chicken and harrissa. There was also some sort of chocolate dessert and drinks service. Better than expected. And then the train stopped, in the middle of nowhere, 1 hour from Paris, no airconditioning. 30 minutes, no reason given. we actually booked Eurostar for the experience but everything from the seats to the delays only made us never wanting to ever board a Eurostar train again!

St Pancras to Brussels outbound was asked to arrive 1:15h before our departure time. On arrival a lady spotted we were a large group of 6 with children and took us to a counter rather than go through the e-gates. There also appeared to be a double booking where another family had the same seats as us. The conductor resolved the issue fairly swiftly. Inbound Brussels was just chaotic from arrival at the station. The security check was fairly quick and once through passport control it was carnage. The waiting area was packed with not enough seating. The train before us boarded 20 minutes before their departure so we were standing for a little while. Our boarding was equally chaotic and only 20 minutes beforehand although the train departed exactly on time. Inbound Brussels staff were curt and rough. Once onboard it was peaceful both ways. We travel plus and had the breakfast service outbound and dinner service inbound. Both were okay. The inbound train toilets appeared to have a problem and the whole carriage had an awful smell for half of the journey. All trains were on time.

Amsterdam - Paris. They cancel our train 12 minutes before departure. They rebook the train but leave 5 hours later.  They don't answer the phone for 30 minutes, then when they answer they don't know how to help us or tell us what we're owed. (Compensation, Meals, Transportation) On board grumpy staff, first class totally FAKE (Premier mixed with Plus). Scarce food and drinks can only be had when they pass with the cart (on the site it says unlimited drinks) A scandal! DO NOT BOOK WITH EUROSTAR!!!!!

As one other reviewer mentioned the Eurostar experience has got much worse over the last few years - our train to Paris stopped at Lille due to technical problems on another train(?). We all had to get out, mill around the station before eventually getting on an old Eurostar train on the next platform from where we started. Chaos! The replacement train smaller than the one we set out on so no classes and no reserved seats. Total delay 1.5hrs so we missed our onward connection (luckily SNCF are used to Eurostar  delays so were very helpful!). On way back both our trains from Gare du Nord on different days were delayed and again chaos reigns. Paris station is even worse of course than St Pancras - and as ever no useful information or any staff available to give any! Where are all the Eurostar staff on these occasions - do they employ any?! Take the plane as at least there are options and most airports offer better facilities' such a shame...

I would like you thank Eurostar for the complete clustf%%%k that passed for a so called service on 27th and 28th August. You have become the "Ryanair " of train travel. Willie Walsh would be proud of you. How to provide a 3rd world service in 3 easy lessons.  As a retired railway engineer,  you excuses were as poor as the ones from our current government.  The board of directors should fall on their swords and resign, as you obviously have no idea how to run an efficient railway. Employ some people who know what they are doing. We are seriously considering going back to flying to Paris as it can't be any worse.

I experienced delays, then was left stranded on my own in Paris when they cancelled my train and those after. Over 1,000 passengers all trying to find somewhere to sleep for the night with no help from Eurostar. Told to claim for taxis, hotels, evening meals breakfast etc I tried that and I’m still waiting it’s now middle of August. When I finally got a train home a day later than I’d booked. I sat down and less than 5 minutes into my journey I was covered in water. The AC above my head leaked all over me. Rubbish customer service they really do not give a toss about people. I do not recommend them at all.

London to Paris: great check in process, clear signage and very well managed. Only poor point is the lack of seating in the waiting area. Paris to London; a total shambles! Huge queues, no sense to the queueing system. We were told to arrive at 2.40 for a 4.07 train and only boarded minutes after 4.07 due to a total lack of common sense in checking in passengers by train time. The staff are ridiculously incompetent and extremely rude providing absolutely zero information and repeatedly counting the number of passengers still in the queue for the 4.07 (well over 100 passengers). I cannot understand why the London side is so well organised (even having a separate queue for the those that choose to arrive 30 mins before - as advertised) whereas Paris is complete chaos. Reading reviews this has been the case for many years and my past experience of the Paris side has never been positive however today has been the worst. I will never travel by Eurostar again and do not recommend it (unless it is one way departing from London).
Rude staff, illogical processes, ran late and there was no information. As soon as delays happen everything falls apart and nobody is able to help

Went to Paris thinking it would be more pleasant than flying - it wasn’t. The facilities after going through security are not remotely close to adequate. The train journey was OK but spoiled by having a large piece of the carriage structure next to our heads rather than a window - part of the attraction of going by train was to be able to look at the view, which of course we did not have. Onboard refreshment facilities were poor and the seats were every bit as bad as a budget airline. To sum up I thought the whole experience was as poor as travelling by plane but without the cost and speed advantages.

It’s over ten years since I have traveled on Eurostar, and I was sad to experience the decline in service levels.  The check in at St Pancras is time consuming and the waiting room as unpleasant as being on the tube at rush hour.  Overall, worse than going through a busy airport.  Eurostar has totally given up the advantage they had over the airlines of being able to arrive at the station just 30 minutes before departure.  WiFi was very poor.  This also should be an area where they can do better than the airlines, but don’t seem to be bothered to do.  Train was 40 minutes late.  Even though I like trains I could not recommend Eurostar.

I regularly travel between Paris and London for work and this service is atrocious. Almost every train I take (at least biweekly) is delayed, several times they've been cancelled. They also have a pathetic delay compensation scheme where you get a measly 25% discount when it's well over an hour delayed....rivals and competitors can't come any sooner. Shockingly poor service.

Don’t wait for a comfortable and neat trip because your ticket cost you twice the price of an A/R by plane. The train is aging, from the time of the first TGV. As an added bonus, the delicacy of Welcoming staff, with a northern suburb accent, in the Gare du Nord who yell at customers in line to move the herd faster. Disappointing experience for what should be a pride.

Avoid!! Eurostar requires you to arrive 1.5hrs but offers inadequate space to wait. Older adults are having to stand as children occupy seats. God forbid there is ever an emergency because no one is getting out. Definitely fly instead!

Fantastic on board , the staff is charming , the meal very good , the comfort of the seats . we can hardly believe it is a train , and besides it goes underwater 😇 nothing to do with the sncf taking water

St Pancras waiting area is woefully small, if there was a fire, it would be horrendous, not enough seating or standing space, poor signage,  boiling hot, huge queue for small cafe.This would be helped if Ebbs fleet and Ashford International were open, as they would take a lot of pressure off St Pancras and  share the load.Once on the train it was fine, although due to the size and amount of luggage some passengers take the storage areas at the end of each carriage were overwhelmed, my suggestion would be a baggage car or an area where people with huge cases or lots of luggage pay a little more.It was actual quite difficult to find the carriage you needed the signage on the platform and the carriage numbers didn’t coincide.Cafe was frugal and one server struggled to get everything done quickly, although he tried and was friendly and cheerful.The journey back from Paris Gare du Noord was delayed and huge queues built up, communication was ok but same message repeated over and over again, better information would have been nice.Unlike St Pancras waiting area at Gare du Noord was expansive with a nice cafe and quite a lot of seating.I think Eurostar have become complacent as have their staff, some most unhelpful, they obvious think they are better than the alternatives, flying and ferry, and have stopped caring a bit.

We travelled to Rotterdam. The train was one hour late in to Brussells and then we were told we would need to go on a local train. We finally arrived 2.5 late. NO one from Eurostar made sure we were OK when we were turfed off the Eurostar at Brussels. The local train had just about standing room only, I was totally crushed for an hour and a half. There was no airconditioning either, so we arrived not only very late, but hot and dishevelled. Eurostars customer service was beyond appalling, patronising, rude, unhelpful and poor to the extent that I complained to the moderator and they have even ignored her advice and basically told her that refunding a pitiful amount and behaving as rudely and unhelpfully to customers as possible is perfectly OK and they have no intention of changing. I would therefore defintiely recommend flying!!  I would defintiely NOT recommend using Eurostar again!

Very poor service. They asked us to come to train station 1.5 hours ago. Guess what they have not enough seating capacity. People with kids like us and others or even older have to stand for a long time. Their ticket price is expensive but no facility.

Multiple delays from Bordeaux to Amsterdam. Initial delay from Bordeaux to Paris due to fire on tracks the day before, which meant we missed our Paris to Amsterdam train. Went to the customer service area. No help given at du nord station besides you can check with the train manager when the train arrives to see if you get a seat or not ((Very unreliable). Unable to give new seat allocation without buying new tickets. Had to pay €250 for 2 people. Was a hot day. Barely any air conditioner running on the train. Fabric seats made it unbearable. Train was also delayed. People sitting in carry holder areas. Would not recommend euro star.

We travelled between London and Paris in a large family group which included both my 94 year old mother and my 10 week old granddaughter, and at both ends of the age spectrum the station and onboard staff were extremely considerate and generally superb at assisting them and looking after them - many thanks!!

Travel on 11/08 from Paris to London, trains were late and some were even cancelled. Luckily I found the best employee, Mr. Xavier Jean, who had the Capacity (in covers) to listen to me, understand me and even more the kindness to change my ticket so that I could get on a train and get to London on time and take the plane. Infinite thanks to Sr XAVIER JEAN !!!!

Trains were on time and everything was rather organised. Toilets were conveniently located near the carriages. Cafe was a little far and the overall ride was not as smooth as I expected. However point A to B travel was quite convenient and efficient.
It was good . The terminal was overcrowded however the first class experience was good . The lunch was delicious and plenty of leg room , will travel again

Cafe has a terrible range, the poor one man operator was  underprepared for the rush. Coffee was ok but food was poor. For a 6-7am departure better options are needed. Seating was cramped. Couldn’t wait to get off.We booked 7 seats and were all split up. Disappointed.Expected more from European rail system.

One of the hottest days of the year, and Eurostar thinks it is acceptable to barely run the Aircon. Horrible conditions, both in the stations where announcements are completely inaccurate (boarding...followed by 20min of standing around and no train in sight), and on board, which became unpleasantly hot.

Eurostar: Despite a global Eurorail pass for one month had to pay for seat reservations for train from London to Brussels midi as all trains from London to Amsterdam was fully booked, no priority for Euro rail pass holders, This is how this rail company makes money and rips of their customers. Had no choice but to purchase seat reservations to Brussels midi and then take a regional train from Brussels midi to Amsterdam Centraal station. The station at Saint Pancras was intimidating, confusing, long queues for immigration and poor signage to coaches assigned on our tickets taking the Euro star. Poor air conditioning on 2nd class with the current heat wave of July in London, was hot inside the trains. Over rated trains and over crowded. So many seats was empty in 2nd class, didn’t realize that all trains were fully booked and the counter staff at Eurostar office had 2 seat on the train to Brussels but when we got on this train there were many seats empty, this is how the company rips of their customers and make money. Not impressed one bit by this rail service knowing how busy it gets in the summer they should have had every hour a train to Amsterdam and Belgium which is not the case so better take the domestic flight and go by air, avoid trains if possible knowing it’s much cheaper to take the train but because they are limited trains and so many disruptions daily in the summer, they are unreliable services and best to take the plane and use the airport instead of railway which is a mess and decaying each year. Zero upgrades of stations and platforms, so difficult to drag 4 wheel luggage on any Eurostar platforms, it’s a myth to reach in two hours when the entire trip takes door to door over 5 hours, keeping 90 min arrival at the Eurostar station before your train departure, so it actually takes 5 hours from Paris to London or London to Amsterdam or Brussels, I did the math. Not worth it, better take the plane next time if possible.

Despite the long wait to speak to a Francophone, the Customer Service is perfect, very attentive to the customera kind explanation and often an email to explain and confirm an expected answer 2 replies by email in case I had a problemThe result your concern goes away
Train space on the seats were good. Train on time. But not enough space for luggage.It was good to have people around to help out with where you have to go.

Travelled Eurostar from King's X to Amsterdam.  Smooth journey. Eurostar Plus seats were comfortable  . As the train was in the morning , they provided light breakfast as soon as we left Kings X , and then drinks + snacks  when when the train  left Brussels. Nice service. Comfortable  journey (personally l compared to flight . Waiting area in King's X was bit crowded , apart from thay all good.

We went Eurostar Premier - London to Paris.This is their "first" class and comes at a price - but we did take advantage of their summer 50% off offer.Big advantages are quicker transit through security/passport and lounges at both stations. Staff on train on way out were perfunctory - but on way back were great and engaged. Staff at lounges at both ends were great.Problems:The seats are uncomfortable and very far from luxurious (the old Eurostar seats were much more comfortable - this is more like siting on a chair in McDonalds)The food was awful - the hot chicken on the way out - had no indication in its description that is was heavily spiced - and was basically a very poor Indian dish. Very misleading. Overuse of fennel in starters and main - really lazy. Food was marginally better on way back but still way over-spiced.The wines and champagne were very poor - get a new sommelier - and Eurostar have replaced water bottles with one offering of a cup of water on the spurious grounds of environmental friendliness... surely it is more important to keep to your passengers hydrated in an air-conditioned environment....For us we would only use Eurostar if travelling in Premier - given all the hassles of boarding etc.....but it is not worth the normal £550 return price per person....

Mass handling, unfriendly staff who enjoy bossing and rushing everyone around. You almost have to undress at security and then you hardly get time to get dressed again. Degrading. Those who travel sustainably are punished this way. It's too bad. Understand all those who prefer to fly and seriously consider it for next time. Price-performance not given at Eurostar. Employees should urgently attend social education training.
Overcrowded waiting areas, uninformed staff giving ‘best guess’ information, repeated delays, overpriced. Not the experience I thought I’d be getting!

The waiting room was not fit to accommodate the number of people waiting for trains that carry 800+, and there were multiple of them departing during the same timeframe at that. There was hardly any room to sit or even stand without blocking walkways. Standing for 30 min. to an hour in such cramped quarters is very unpleasant. They need to expand their waiting rooms. That improvement alone would greatly improve things.

This was my first time taking Eurostar to Amsterdam. It's not the quickest trip at 4 hours, but to my surprise both the outward and return journey were on time. Coming back I came in premium economy for an extra £40, in mostly empty carriages, and well-supplied with wine by cheerful staff.As ever, Eurostar is let down by high prices (£300 economy return), inefficient check in (the barriers failed to read many people's barcodes), inattentive staff at check in (definitely a security issue), and badly timed departures leading to chronic overcrowding at St Pancras. Check in at Amsterdam was subject to unexplained delays.

Easy trip to and from Belgium. Checking in at both London and Belgium ends was simple, with lovely staff. Terminals can get quite busy and there aren't many shops either side once you pass security so I would suggest buying anything before passing this point.The train journey was on time, clean, and fast. We had standard seats on the way out, and purchased a drink from the cafe which was good. Toilets are ok for a train toilet - nothing special but acceptable. On the way back we had the upgrade to Eurostar plus. The extra space was much appreciated. The food was not to our taste though, but we were offered drinks including hot drinks and wine, which was a nice surprise.
ONE HOUR WAITING TO SPEAK TO CUSTOMER SERVICE AND THEY STILL DIDNT MANAGE TO PICK UP MY CALL - CONSIDERING THE PRICES IT'S DAYLIGHT ROBBERY

Checked in using app and had quite a wait to go through security at St Pancras as lots of people were trying to go through. Crowded waiting area with one cafe. Got on train which had comfortable seats and sufficient luggage space, be mindful of screens on ceiling of train which shows carriage number as can be easy to go on wrong carriage. Food/ drink offering on board is poor so take food/ drink on from station beforehand. On return at Lille, was much more straight forward security check and check in but again be mindful of carriage number as will be different location as signed on platform.  Would use again to go to Europe.

If I could give 0 stars I would. Just don’t do it. Based on the (false) advertising, we paid for the “best” package to round off a special trip to Disneyland Paris with our young daughter.Just appalling from start to finish. Not a single member of staff to show us, or anyone on the train, where to go on the platform, to welcome us onto the train, advise us about luggage or anything else. Very unclear where to sit on a full train and incredibly stressful getting on. When we finally sat down, to lots of eye rolls from the other passengers, we had our first interaction from a member of staff who promptly told us we had to immediately move our cases two full carriages along as they were in the way, even though there had been literally nowhere else to put them (they were in the luggage area) and no staff to tell us where to do so. No offer of help, just a telling off basically. This is on the supposed “first class”. A total joke.The staff’s only priority the whole journey seemed to be to throw the “luxury” (it really wasn’t) meal at you as quickly as possible so that was done, chuck half a perfunctory glass of champagne to you and then promptly disappear for the rest of the journey never to be seen again. The train itself is shabby, the day to day trains in London are much much nicer, this was actually held together with sellotape in places 🤦🏻‍♀️Seat spaces in first class are small and uncomfortable. It was hot on the train, despite it not being an especially hot day. During the journey we saw several passengers like us, unsure where to go, having lost luggage or generally struggling to get on and off. On the odd occasion a member of staff was around they just stood by and ignored the struggling customers. Honestly some of the worst and most  disinterested customer service I have ever experienced. The daily customer service on British Rail is kinder, friendlier and more efficient in every single way. If there actually is anyone in charge of customer service on Eurostar they should be truly ashamed. Like everyone on the train, we were churned off the train at the end (how ridiculous to have narrow steps and a single door for everyone to struggle with cases with, then a massive gap!)Obviously not a luxury or special end to the holiday in any way. First and last time on Eurostar, we will take the plane next time.Vous devriez avoir honte Eurostar!

I was on the Eurostar from London to Brussels and back. Great ride. Easy and quick process from entry to security check to immigration. I have a Plus ticket. The seats had a table, lights, a bit of storage, lots of feet and leg space, and they recline. Both trains were on time with their arrival and departure. We had 2 big bags and plenty of storage space.

Amazing train journey from London to Paris in Eurostar.  This is very good train journey experience with very fast and efficient train service.  We got upgraded to first class, so it doubled our good experience.  London train stations was good but Paris stations seemed not so good.
Absolutely disgraceful that ts and cs come above basic human interaction. Would not recommend, in this day and age some morales would not go amiss

We had standard seats from Paris to London. Seats were ok but the train was SO hot and stuffy. Felt like no air on at all.  We walked through other cars and they felt much better. Couldn’t find anyone to ask to turn on air for some relief.  Felt sick and nauseous when we arrived. Maybe standard seats don’t include air? Think twice before riding in summer especially.

My 1st time and thoroughly enjoyed it. Very quick, very quiet, very comfortable. Went 1st class, and the service and breakfast were great. The only downside was the waiting area at St Pancras after passport control. All herded into a small and dark waiting area with massive queues for food & drink. Paris on the return was so much better. Light, airy, and just a much better experience

My outward train was cancelled by eurostar the evening before I was due to travel. I received an email after 8pm, conveniently after their booking office and helpline were closed. I was told I could exchange my ticket but there were no available tickets due to the last minute nature of the cancellation. I was left with the only option but to buy a last minute flight at huge cost to myself, more than doubling the amount I had already spent on the train ticket.Despite being out of pocket over £200 I only received half of the value of my ticket back: less than £70. My return journey from Paris on eurostar, and was chaotic, badly organised, overcrowded and I was only able to board the train with 10 minutes to spare. I will never travel with eurostar in future and would recommend anyone using this service to have a back up plan for alternative travel!

Travelled from London to Paris, booked well in advance including our hotel, found the experience very good, no issues with security, passport control or delays, yes departure rooms can be busy at times but plenty of seats become available when a train boards. Found the pricing very good compared to flying when you include hold luggage, airport parking/taxi, and transfers from the airport, would not hesitate to book again, reason for only 4 stars, seats weren't that comfy and not much legroom but apart from that very satisfied

We took the Eurostar from London to Paris via coach. The train car and seats were comfortable and spacious. The train was fast, surprisingly quiet, and a very smooth ride. We did bring luggage on board and had no issue finding a place to put them. There is overhead space for the carry-ons, and a larger luggage area near the entrance of the car. We arrived at St. Pancreas Station 90 minutes before departure due to delays with the Tube (we were planning to arrive 2 hours early). The check-in at St. Pancreas was smooth and there were no lines when we went through. The boarding process itself was a little chaotic and hard to hear on the overhead. However, just following the masses took us to the right spot. Going through the Chunnel was a very cool experience. We will definitely travel on Eurostar again!
Very uncomfortable seats -Horrible.Expensive unless you book way in advance. They hold the monopoly so unlikely the price will become more sensible.

Really terrible. On the way, delay of 1h30 on the defined time and more transport to be able to return, so, taxi.On the way back, my train is cancelled 1h45 before departure. They find me another train and there, departure of this new train 30 minutes late for an arrival 1 hour late.And here too, a fairly late arrival. Frankly, it leaves something to be desired. The wifi works pretty badly and no bar Service on the way.

We had booked a journey from London to Amsterdam.We turned up at St Pancras an hour before boarding then whilst queuing at the ticket check I got a notification on my phone saying that the train was cancelled. I asked at the ticket desk as there were no staff to confirm the notification prior to this if the train was cancelled and the staff member said ignore the notification, the train is running as normal. We asked the staff member checking tickets at the carriage and she replied “I have no idea what you’re talking about” we boarded as usual. About an hour into the journey the tannoy announced that the train is terminating at Brussels and we had to find our way onward from there. The announcement carried on by saying we would have to purchase tickets for the journey and Eurostar would reimburse anyone who had. We paid another £100 for pre booked tickets onwards on board the train. Another announcement an hour later said that Eurostar tickets would be valid for any travel onwards from Brussels. We had a terrible follow on journey from Brussels with overcrowded trains and very little information. We arrived at our hotel 4 hours later than scheduled. The Eurostar refund system kept rejecting our claim for refunds through the app claiming our train isn’t cancelled.

None of rhe electronic gates at customs work. As a result huge queues. No space  overstretched staff. Kids screaming. Poor shops  be4 departure at har du nord. No magazines on board in business premier. Coach overcrowded. Food appalling

Ok, so the first thing to say is that clearly, eurostar has a complete monopoly on this journey, so really, there is no incentive to either respond to poor reviews or indeed provide any customer service. The thing to note is that while boarding at St. P is fairly straightforward, just rather unpleasant because the seating is so limited, boarding at GdN is pure chaos every time. The team in fairness to them is very very young, and instead of sorting passengers out up front as they do in StP, they hide out right by the passport counter, where by the time if they do call you forwards it's clearly too late anyways. This means that the main part of the queue is entirely unstaffed and can be particularly slow for families unable to use the automatic gates. There is also a culture of being abrupt/rude to passengers, i have seen countless passengers being berated for being confused in the chaos. Finally when there are delays or train cancellation there is very poor communication, and some poor person is sent out solo to try and speak to the crowd of 100s of angry passengers, who can't hear a thing they say anyway. So frankly, you can understand why they look so miserable.

What a fantastic experience. My wife and I travelled from London to Amsterdam and enjoyed every minute of the journey/experience, what a fantastic way to travel. We travelled Eurostar Plus and it was worth every penny. Without a doubt, we will travel with them again. *****
Eurostar not comfortable at all. Already in the driveway we were a little disappointed. But the return we were very disappointed by the comfort.Hard seats. Wrong seating.Back pain.

We have cancelled our Eurostar journey for business reasons by taking out the insurance. Even if we took out the insurance we lost more than 100 € on our tickets.It’s a real hiding machine and a scam, you have to know it and show everyone.

FAST, CLEAN, & SMOOTH RIDE!My fam and I recently took this high-speed train from London to Paris for a daytrip. The total time was 2 hours and 20 minutes.  The train left on time and we had clean, comfortable seats. I would highly recommend taking the Eurostar train to anyone wanting to travel between these 2 cities (or any other cities where Eurostar travels).  I was surpised how smooth ride is, even when traveling at 200 mph!  We caught the earliest train out of London (6am) and returned on the last train out of Paris (9pm). This gave us plenty of time to visit the Eiffel Tower and Notre-Dame.  This was a great trip!

These people are so bad at running a train service, they make British Rail look good. Do not use them if it matters to you in the slightest that you get close to your destination the same day as you ntend.  You will see I've done a small number of reviews over the years, all of them positive. I'm not a BOT and I don't write bad reviews for fun.You have been warned. Never use this service if you are a serious traveller.Eurostar. Please sue me if anything I write here is untrue. I booked a direct train London to Rotterdam.  By the time I got to St Pancras, I seriously believe they had no intention whatsoever of fulfilling this arrangement. I was given two tickets, splitting the journey in Brussels.The second ticket had printed Rotterdam as a destination and a train number.That train didn't go to Rotterdam, and I was instructed to leave it in Utrecht approaching midnight, hours after I was scheduled to be in Rotterdam.  I was told Eurostar weren't running any service to Rotterdam until the next morning. It was my problem what to do next.Throughout the saga that went on for hours, I received emails and SMSs explaining revised tines of my arrival in Rotterdam, all on a train that was never going to Rotterdam. Afterwards, the 'apology' started with an aggressive  instruction to check my Ts and Cs before trying to claim a refund. And the classic non -apology 'if you were inconvenienced, we are sorry ....".Never ever use this company. Eurostar, I told you I'd write this and it would be true. It's far too late to apologise. Just sue me if this is wrong.

We travelled from London to Paris on a Eurostar Plus ticket which we bought for £60 each (not a bad price), in fact, we could have bought the ticket for £50 but we  were slow off the mark.The seats were  comfortable enough and as we were sat one behind the other there was plenty of leg-room too. The meal provided was cold, as it was served no sooner than we had left London; what's the rush? Give it chance to reach room temperature - and what's with the cake - over the top we thought.The cake aside the journey was straight forward and the staff cheery enough and the train was only delayed by a matter of minutes.The return journey on a Eurostar Premier ticket was a completely different experience.We were not quite sure about the so called benefits of traveling Premier class. Eurostar explains it as:'A travel experience like no other' and they are so right. We must have missed something because it certainly was an 'experience like any other.'The booking in at Paris started well enough as we only have pass through the Premier ticket booth but after that, it was chaos. The dedicated priority lane must have been closed when we turned up as we never 'breezed through' anywhere and we certainly never 'breezed through' passport control or security.The so called 'exclusive lounge area' is situated at the top of the station and accessible by either lift or stairs. Once reached you are apparently offered  a 'top-class service'.Alas the daily papers, staff and the top-class service were missing, perhaps all three were stuck in the priority lane!Don't forget that when you leave the lounge to join your train you also join the crowd - you queue like every one else - £270 or not.We were looking forward to see and maybe taste the 'pioneering work of some of Europe's top chefs' but not on this trip.We were offered but declined the 'breakfast meal', in fact we were not the only one's either - not sure what it was suppose to be; perhaps the European chefs let their apprentices have a go and they had a day off!. No wine or champagne was offered and we were looking forward to our glass of champagne, alas it was not to be. The only drinks offered were tea, coffee and smoothie: what a scam.  The staff however, were first class which is more than we can say about the Premier 'experience'. Stick to Standard or if the price is right Eurostar Plus.

First class is an overstatement, the First class lounge and toilets could have been in any pub after 11pm. Disgusting and rude staff, maybe under paid and over worked. The Free drinks when they are available limited, maybe a good thing. Once on the train service improved slightly, then food was served, I have had better food from a takeaway.

Rotterdam/Brussels to London had hours of delays and cancellations with no warning, despite Eurostar knowing about the faults early that morning.We were left without any information on the 14th about the line cancellations. Why on earth when they found out about the problems on the track didn't they contact us!? we could have made alternative arrangements rather than deal with the hell that was our journey!By the time we got to Brussels there was queue 1000s of people just to get through customs because of the backlog from cancelled trains, all people who were not informed.We had to wait for hours in that queue with no apologies or information. We very barely made it on the train and were under stress for hours, ruining our holiday. Then I tried to process a partial refund the site has the audacity to say I'm not eligible. Will never ever use Eurostar again, I suspect neither with those other poor stressed people in that hellish queue!

I read the reviews for Eurostar and do agree with some points - the trains could do with some TLC, the food is not great (we took our own).  But the staff are really warm and welcoming. We got an upgrade to Premier through the bidding system and having access to the lounges made a big difference, especially with the heat. It's definitely less painful than flying.

I booked passenger assistance as my friend has mobility issues and uses a wheelchair  ( manual ) and I recently had a heart attack requiring surgery . 1st we got there too early ( had no idea that was possible ) . Then passenger assistance was sent . A guy over 60 , very abruptly told us to follow him and started to walk off . I asked how our luggage would get there . I was expected to push my friend in the wheelchair and carry 3 bags of luggage , I told him I'd just had a heart attack and wasn't able to do all that hence booking passenger assist.  He picked the bags up and huffed off , blatantly angry he had been asked to do that , leaving us feeling like our disabilities were a burden , it was horrible I wanted to cry . Paris staff where so understanding and helpful , completely the opposite of staff in London. I'd never travel with them again , London passenger assistance staff are rude & lazy and get angry that you dare ask for actual assistance.  As the companion, and with an invisible disability , staff expected me to do there job.It was exactly the same on the way back . Network rail is a fraction of the price but send 2 people to assist and couldn't be more helpful . Seriously consider flying if your in the same position I was . Eurostar really need to look into how it treats disabled passengers.

Notice for wise advice:- if you want to travel in Eurostar at an acceptable price, go for it as soon as the ticket office opens, otherwise the closer you get to the departure date and the more it stings!!!- no need to rush to check in, opening is an hour before departure so if your train is at 7pm, they open boarding not before 6pm.- if like us your ticket is cancelled (panic, panic) , no stress: the exchange is free, if link of the SMS only sends you on a paid exchange page, it is because their site is not up to date. So if as we exchange your ticket paying an extra cost, this is not normal (we should get refunded ... in 28 days ...). Either you take your trouble patiently and wait for their website to update ... or depending on the time you reach someone on the phone (count a good 20 minutes before you pick up) or you go to the ticket office. You can see that at Eurostar they never fill their trains completely to meet the unexpected (when you know that for the air it is the opposite...), and that at the station they always have emergency tickets that are not available on their website. Conclusion added 332€ for the penultimate evening train since the first morning, ours was cancelled; that I lost a day and had to make representations to hope to be reimbursed, all because their website is poorly managed when in absolute could have found me a free place on the next train ... it leaves dreamy!Since we couldn't find another train all day, we were upgraded to snack option on board. Yes Well we are no more or less on a charter equivalent in terms of Service Quality, free to you ...
Garbage old trains that break down now going to miss my connection in Brussels. Avoid at all costs euro star= hot garbage
Slow, late, cancelling trains all the time... Traveling from Amsterdam to Brussels 3 hours... That is only 200km...lame

Terrible service. Left stranded in Amsterdam with no trains due to industrial action which they must have known was likely but didn’t warn us. Impossible to get hold of to discuss alternative transport. Had to very stressfully book a flight home as everyone else was trying to at great cost. Once home Eurostar say they won’t cover the cost of a flight because it’s not “comparable” whereas apparently a 14 hour coach home is! Customer service are pointless at best, but usually just patronising. Do yourself a favour and fly. Had a similar experience with easyJet not long ago where a flight was delayed by 4.5 hours. Filled out one form and they provided compensation over the cost of the flight, no problems. Eurostar need to seriously look at their refund and compensation policies if they want to keep competing with low cost airlines. Avoid if you can!
A train that runs every hour from Paris North to Amsterdam is delayed by 50 minutes. Ridiculous, what a crappy service. Next time I better go by bicycle.

Arrive at London St Pancras and at check in my train seat number is changed so end up facing backwards (which makes me feel nauseous) on journey when I’d specifically requested forward facing. After going through security the waiting area was jam packed  with no where to sit. Kids sitting on priority seats. The journey back from Paris to London was horrendous with several queues, though not for any specific train, and a very long wait to go through check in and passport control. I’m nearly 70 and had to endure standing in the heat for nearly an hour with no seating provided. Packed like sardines and herded like animals.   Once through passport control there were no orderly queuing to go through security. The whole process was shambolic and the experience is one I won’t be repeating. The only reason I gave this one star was because the train left on time!

Customer service not good.  If you log a support ticket they don't do anything unless you open an ambiguous email and click through a link to say you still have a problem... obviously I still have a problem, i only logged my support ticket 12 seconds ago

Every time I was late, and the last time I went, I was entitled to compensation of 25% of the ticket price because there was more than an hour of delay. They are imposing compensation on me in a voucher, in breach of European law, and the intervention of the European Ombudsman has not changed that.Suffice to say that I will never go with them again and I strongly advise against this company!
Food decidedly poor. Service perfunctory. Ride smooth. Views so so. Delivery to Paris proper very nice. Security redundant.

On the way there, an hour and a half delay. The accompanying breakfast also comes after Brussels. On the way back, having to catch a train later due to delays. You don’t get new tickets for that, but a kind of ‘free pass’ without an assigned seat. So in a full train you sit among the luggage on the balcony.

Horrible customer service. Packed waiting rooms. And then when you get there you are stuck on the crowded, delayed, failed privatization British rail system. Do yourself a favor and just fly. Much cheaper and easier!

absolutely terriblefirst time using eurostar ,we came off orient express so it was nearbygetting through security is pandemonium no organisation ,no structureno one has a cluefull of rude employees then a train before ours was delayed so there must of been 2,000 people standingno announcemrnts,no staffterrible pure chaos train ride ok food terrible NEVER  again
Raze the building and start over from scratch. No air conditioning, no organization, late start time (2+ hours!!). Avoid this monstrosity unless you like beating yourself up for no reason.

The train journey was great but1) my wife and I were moved 4 times before we left. You can’t have a nice meal together if you’re in different carriages. When we asked if we could move the manager said ask if someone will swap with you. 2) return journey started with 2+ hours standing in a queue in a glass sunhouse in almost 30c heat with no seats. Some passengers were dropping out ill.  We tried to cancel the week before we left because of 1) but were told tough claim on travel insurance. We won’t be using Eurostar again, we’ll drive or fly.

I travelled Eurostar Premier from London to Paris.The lounge at St Pancras is a bit cramped but otherwise ok and the staff were friendly.The train left and arrived on time. The seat was adequately comfortable.The food was underwhelming. The dish was probably 50% peas. The desert tasted very strange.The wifi was non existent. Despite my devices saying they were connected nothing was functioning.I prefer this over flying, but I really dislike flying.

Horrendous experience.    At  Gare du Nord,   waited for a long time packed onto a boiling hot mezzanine level.    The staff had no idea of train times or how to organise people.    Then our passports could not be scanned as their scanners had IT glitches,   we queued for a long time  to have them manually checked.    The experience was so bad that whilst waiting both my husband and I looked up the TGV timetables,    if you don't need to go into London then avoid and simply book a TGV to a  port.    At least we did get on a train (albeit 40 mins late in leaving)  but many passengers around us had their journey cancelled with no chance of a seat on a later train.
Don’t do it I’m the summer!!!   Hot.  Crowded.  Delayed.  NO AIR conditioning. Disorganized.  Overall crappy.  Regret taking the trip.
Horrific on every level. And rude unsmiling service in premier. Delayed as usual, chaos as usual and rude staff who were most unhelpful and unfriendly.

Although the service was efficient, they do not cater for families with children under 4 very well. There is nowhere to safely store a buggy other than in the small luggage racks and trying to put the buggy down with cases, small children and a growing queue of passengers waiting to stow their bags is not ideal.There are no seating options available for under 4’s which is ridiculous as this means they have to sit on their parent’s laps for the whole journey. The chair spaces are small enough without adding a child to your lap. There is no room for the lap tray to be used in this situation either.I would not recommend Eurostar with those families with children under 4 for these reasons.

We travelled from St Pancras to Paris via Eurostar plus and were very pleased with the service and efficiency we experienced. Whilst the waiting area was busy, we expected this, as with airports, we fly from Manchester and it is busier than our Eurostar experience. The service we had on the train was professional and efficient. A smooth, on time journey. This was our first journey on the Eurostar but we are planning another l. I am glad we did not read the reviews prior to our trip as we would have been concerned, however no complaints and would recommend as an easy and quick way to travel to Paris.

I thought i had seen the worst of trains with British trains, but this was just unbelievably bad. Absolutely nothing about the journey Paris- london went right, from the moment we arrived 35 min before departure, got put in the sweltering heat in a long queue, to then by chance find out by forcing one of the staff passing by to talk to us, find out that we’d missed our train (that hadn’t left yet) because we were supposed to magically skip the queue and go to the front, through check in , 30 min BEFORE take off. They then change our ticket, then 10 members of staff kept sending us and the rest of the travellers back and forth between different queues, someone even tried to send us all the way back to the end of the queue (so we then definitely miss the new train too). Eventually, by fighting with every single staff member we make it through passport control, then security (all extremely disorganized, people queuing for 2:40pm train and 4pm train in the same queue). The were told the train has been delayed by 40min, there’s no cafe service on board and i’m still not sure i’m standing in the right queue. Not one member of the staff knew what was going on, worst organization ever (and i have travelled a lot) and to top it off, most staff was very rude and one lady completely ignored me speaking to her twice. People with kids, prefab at women, underage and old people all have no support or idea about what is going on.

Brussels-Paris: I bought 3 of Business Premier tickets (most expensive, 129 euros each): no meal provided, dirty and bad wifi connection. Terrible experience, not worth even one euro. Not even joking. False advertising about the quality.

Travelled to Amsterdam and back on Eurostar. Going was Business Premier and coming back was standard. Going journey was flawless as we did not need to change trains but coming back was a bit of a nightmare because when we got into Brussels to change to the London train we were told we weren’t going to be put on our booked train as a smaller train was operating. The way everything was done was very unprofessional to say the least. I was very disappointed and don’t think I will be using them again.

Needing to get from London to join my tour in Paris, I took the Eurostar rather than a short flight. I booked a premium seat which I guess is the equivalent to flying business class.  The train before mine was delayed so the Eurostar section of the station was packed and I wasn't allowed in too early. When I finally arrived at the Premium lounge, it was very small but I managed a snack and drink. When our train was ready to board we had to go up a travelator, with luggage and once on the platform find your carriage. Once you found your carriage, the luggage storage areas at the ends of the carriage were already quite full. On the trip I got a small hot meal which was ok. Getting off the train in Paris, the staff watched as passengers struggled with luggage. To travel on the Eurostar was an experience but the next time I travel between London and Paris I will fly.

The train back to London was cancelled with 30 minutes notice.  There was ZERO assistance to help us find a replacement train and all other trains that day were fully booked.We were eventually reimbursed for the cost of an extra night in Paris, but no extra payment for the new train fares in England, and no money for the trains that we missed due to the cancelled Eurostar.

I would recommend that you do not travel by Eurostar for the following reasons:- The departure lounge was so full of people that we had to stand. I cannot stand for prolonged periods due to medical issues. At one point they announced over the PA system that there had been a “security incident” in the street outside and they had had to evacuate the business lounge. No further clarification or reassurance was provided except to say that we were not going to be evacuated. I did not find this garbled announcement reassuring and looking around it appeared that a lot of people were also confused and stressed just like me.- The toilets in the departure lounge were filthy and the prices of food and drink were inflated.- The staff that we spoke to were stressed and dismissive. One or two of them were straight out rude.- They ask you to come 90 minutes early to go through Security. This means that a two hour train trip is now a four hour ordeal.- The seats in standard are not comfortable. The wifi doesn’t work and I could not find the charging port.- The arrival station in Paris was filthy and hot. The bins were overflowing and the buildings approaching the station were covered in graffiti. The general vibe is one of social decay.I recommend that you fly into Paris simply because it is faster, better organised and less stressful.

This company cannot run a railway and should lose its effective monopoly. It is totally unable to cope whenever there is an incident. Its staff seem incapable of organising anything and its customers are treated badly. Even the Wi-Fi is second-rate.

Abominable service. Something that could’ve been handled professionally and efficiently was turned into chaos thanks to the untrained staff at Gare du Nord.Yesterday, June 24th, afternoon and evening trains were canceled due to people jumping in front of them. It happens. However, what shouldn’t happen is for these incidents to paralyze the train services of an entire nation and beyond. People jump in front of trains all the time in London, NYC, Chicago. It takes couple of hours to clean up the mess and get on with it. In France they decide to cancel everything for the rest of the day and even into the next day leaving people stranded.Now one would think that a company like Eurostar would have a protocol in place for such events: have blocked rooms at hotels around the station for emergencies, food vouchers, hotel vouchers, customer service. These are basic things, but alas not in Europe where everything is running on Victorian time.And since Eurostar has a monopoly on the these trains, they could care less because they know most of us will continue to use their services.Last night after canceling the trains, waiting for two hours for a seat on the next available train, putting us on the said train, then telling us to get off, they told us to go rent a hotel room and we’d be reimbursed afterwards. Rooms were difficult to find and were running in the high hundreds low thousands. Cab services were charging outrageous amounts for short distances. None of this would be reimbursed. Although they do say they’d reimburse up to 250 euro. They also told us that we wouldn’t get on a train even tomorrow (today the 25th), so potentially incurring more expenses. They never gave us any options or kept us informed. At last at like 12 am when some of us were really angry, they told us they could put us on a train to shelter for the night from the dubious individuals roaming around the station.This was also done haphazardly 🙄Spent the night on the train, not the worst experience, went to wait in front of the gate as he said the night before to line up before 6am when they open. I go and there were people inside the gate. How did they get there if there’s no staff yet?Ah, the lifts…then what’s the point of the gate?!  People outside the gate trying to queue orderly until they were not. One would think the correct manner of going about this situation is to have staff there at 5 to direct people and reassure them. None of this was done even at 6 am !!!They opened the gates and everyone was rushing in, but the ironic thing was that the ticket office was closed…I mean, talk about coward behavior. They told us yesterday to come and that the ticket office would help us, but today they didn’t even have the decency to show up and help their customers.There were people in wheelchairs, other disable people, elderly people with health problems, young children, and Eurostar still could care less.I decided I’ve had enough being treated like cattle lining up here then there then,” oh none of you are getting on a train today. Maybe tomorrow.”One staff member even told me authoritatively that the easiest thing to do was to cancel my ticket and get refunded….but no alternative as to what I’m supposed to do next. I was even about to book a flight to Nice and then to London.I got in on the first train out though. But had to go twist some arms because I’ve had enough with them dicking around. It shouldn't be like this. Hope everyone else has a ticket out for today.

We travelled Amsterdam to London, and back again from London to Brussels and were really happy with the service in Eurostar Plus. Very nice service of food, beverage and snacks to our seats. Yes the waiting areas were crowded but we were not there long.  On time, comfortable - all good. However! Our service from Brussels to Amsterdam (a much shorter service) was so disappointing.  Altho waiting area was not an issue (staying within EU, no gate checks at all); the train ran late due to a problem with power at Schiphol (not their fault). But there was NO service whatsoever! We could understand no seat service on a shorter run, but the cafe was not open. So for 2 and a half hours there was nothing available at all. Sure a good thing we had a quick bite at the station, and had a couple protein bars in the bag.   Badly done, this stretch.

From London to Frankfurt, to Brussels with Eurostar. Ticket: Interrail Globe Pass. Reservation 1. Class via SNCB for 40 euros. In itself a nice train (similar to ICE) and a fast connection. If everything wasn't made so complicated. Cumbersome and complicated as well as quite expensive reservation for Interrailer only indirectly possible, weeks of advance recommended. The security checks take time, with me more than 1 hour (and were a farce, accidentally had knives and scissors in the backpack, but no one cared). Interesting: only the reservation was checked, not the Interrailpass. In the 1. Class was served free cold food and drinks (wine from plastic bottles) was satisfactory. Staff were friendly but overwhelmed by the lines at security checks.The train was on time, the 15-minute change in Brussels to the ICE to Frankfurt worked out just fine despite long train station distances. Conclusion: As a direct connection ok. If you have to go further inland, be it in the UK, France or even Germany, you are likely to fly better and less stressfully from any low-cost provincial airports close to your place of origin or destination.

I went on the eurostar from Amsterdam to London. The train itself was very efficient and comfortable. However, some of the staff particularly the staff in the food area could be quite rude and condescending making for a very uncomfortable experience. The food area also runs out of food quite quickly into the trip. While the Eurostar itself was great, be aware of the staff.

I'm fairly sure Eurostar is the worst company in the world. It reaches new lows in terms of its service, cleanliness, food standards, customer service, and value for money. This is what happens when one commercial organisation has a monopoly. There is talk of possible competition, please may that happen quickly and drive this outfit out of business!

This was a first time experience for us, so that made it fun! What took away from the fun was the long wait at the station. We were advised to get to the station hours before our train departure time which we did, check in was very fast, so that left us with hours to kill in a limited area. Shopping options were OK but not memorable, and the "waiting" areas are very small with limited seating.The train left on time, service was great, and it arrived at Paris Gare du Nord on time so no complaints there.

I wanted to be Eco so travel whenever I can buy a train  seems right.Thanks to the orange guy security is tight hence a two and not a one. It seemed okay that they grouped people in time columns.. then it went a bit sideways the staff controlling the columns was random in counting so one column moved twice and the others once. I politely asked the guy in charge and he went passive aggressive on me.. it's hot so I'm guessing he regretted his career choice.Got through to security as its Eurostar you get double dipped France security then UK. However the route from one to the other was like Hampton court maze.. you end up going back on yourself and across a stream from the Euro line. One positive my new passport worked first go. In summary can't organise a drinking session in a brewer. To the control guy no you don't know what your doing and self affirmation don't cut it negative reports by people who you've provided poor service do.

The train journey was great, I had a seat in ‘Plus’ which was spacious and quiet, with some food and drink. A relaxing way to travel between London and Paris. However - only 3 stars because the queuing and check-in process (both ends of journey) are terrible and spoil the whole experience. Could be so much better but it was like a grotty airport during the school holidays with temperatures over 30degs and no aircon. Wouldn’t hurt to put WiFi on the train either, people expect that kind of connectivity these days

Travelled to Brussells with a wheelchair user and everything was stress free.Staff were excellent and looked after us well. The journey was great, quiet carriage with plenty of legroom. Will certainly use again.

Awful- crowds, smell, staff - I’d rather fly from now on. Treated like cattle with no seating available.  I think that Eurostar treat their loyal customers badly. I have numerous trips planned but now will fly - Eurostar stop behaving like you have the monopoly……

Return trip from Amsterdam to London delay in Amsterdam Central was most stressful. Train cancelled and no information to get you to the destination. Email sent after we entered the station that the train was cancelled. We had to get to Brussels and then board the train. Eurostar knew they train would be cancelled well in advance.

While booking my tickets, the server failed to respond. When I tried again, the ticket price had gone up by €15 per person, adding an extra €45 to the total trip—through no fault of my own.Trying to file a complaint was a journey in itself: I only found a PDF form, and the link to the support email led straight to a 404 error page. After finally managing to send in my complaint, I received nothing more than a generic “Thank you for your feedback” response. Worse? The link provided in that email to follow up… also leads to a 404 page. And—brace yourself—the link on that 404 page, meant to report broken pages? Also broken.What a mess.Their Trustpilot score is currently 2.5. Based on my experience, that feels generous.

I am not sure whether it is because of lack of competition in the city center to city center market or because of lack of interest in customer expectations that this London to Paris service was so awful. Staff seem disinclined to be helpful, the terms and conditions mean no flexibility in terms of paying for upgrades, which means the the option isn’t offered but if asked for, can only be done on the day of travel and in person at the Station. The Premier lounge is an abomination, too small to accommodate demand, past its prime everything, a poor buffet offering and  a couple of  dirty bathrooms we would never have used. On the train bathrooms were at least as bad , first Class seats cramped, poor WiFi connectivity and minimal options for charging or powering up electronics. To add insult to injury, a security issue on our way back to London meant an indeterminate delay of multiple trains but Eurostar staff did not see communication to passengers as a priority. No information shared about the cause of the delay or whether trains would leave on time irrespective of the inability of passengers to go through security, passport control or baggage checks. Hundreds of customers were herded into a hot basement level space with no seating, offers of water or any other basic considerations.The train is fast and convenient but don’t expect a level of service or professionalism even close to budget airlines or indeed the TGV service in France.

Fantastic staff - we really enjoyed our journeys to and from Brussels. Well done to the staff - professional, friendly, helpful, faultless. Admittedly, we were travelling Eurostar Plus which was superb. Food, wine, quiet carriage. 100% worth the extra!

It's a mess.  The air conditioning does not work, we travel overcrowded and with a delay of more than 1 hour in a 3hs trip. And they didn't warn until after 30 minutes of the trip. Never again in this company disappoint

I was on the 19.11 from Paris today and the crew were fantastic.Stupidly left one of my earbuds on dinner tray. The crew had cleared away all the trays when I realised what I'd done. One member of the crew, Mohammed, went above and beyond the call of duty and went through all the trays to find the bud other crew members joined in the sesrch. Thanks Mohammed and rest of crew.

Used the Eurostar from Paris to London, London to Brussels & Brussels to Paris, highly recommend, way easier than flying especially when you have lots of luggage, I found it very convenient and easy to use & won’t hesitate to use again next time I’m Europe. Book as far in advance as possible for great deals

This beats flying! We booked online in advance ( tickets in Wallet). Pre Booked Business seats thinking it would ease the queueing at Euston St Pancras but we hadn’t booked Premium Business so had to queue but thankfully it moved quickly. Seats were great. Luggage storage good and near to our seats. The journey passed quickly and before we knew it we were in Paris. Queues there for a taxi were next level but moved fairly quickly. Generally a great experience.

5th trip on Eurostar Premier ticket. 0931 London to Paris 9/6/25. Inspite of high hopes & expectations based on previous customer experience, this was an unpleasant experience. Very poor refreshments: stale, chilled pain au chocolate or savoury pastry + mouthful of yogurt and fruit puree. Packet orange juice and awful coffee. No wine offered unlike all other Eurostar journeys.Lavatories dirty and extremely smelly. Kitchen a mess - had to be walked through to get to lavs. Staff ran out of Metro tickets! Not a quality, value for money or enjoyable start to a holiday.

Used Eurostar to go from London - Paris round-trip within a week. Tickets are not exactly cheap.  In both cities, the waiting area and boarding is a nightmare, it has poorly designed boarding areas and passport checks. In Paris, the French exit passport scanners didn’t work 80% of the time or were super-slow, causing huge bottlenecks. When descending onto the platform to find one’s carriage, there are no signs to show in which direction it is numbered. You can spot the carriage number on the door, but then you have to walk left or right to find yours. You’ll have no idea in which direction you should walk (with your heavy luggage)! Phone charging is a joke. You'd better bring a bag full of electrical adapters and cables. There is NO simple USB outlet (found on city buses in most cities nowadays!), even though when selecting your seats on the Eurostar site, it indicates UK and European electrical outlets and USB! Nope. No USB!

My previous journeys to DLP with Eurostar were fine, when they went direct that is.  I've have had the journey from hell and I'm currently writing this in a taxi into Paris as the returning train was cancelled last minute with no text or email to warn us. The Journey to Lilie was delayed for two hours as well. The connecting train was a nightmare too as we didn't have any seats. If you're doing to Disneyland I would suggest flying to save yourself this headache. Terrible company now.

We decided to give Eurostar a go as an alternative to flying to Paris, and in the main it is a decent alternative.I think the trouble is that Eurostar has probably outgrown its current terminals which causes the overcrowding described in other reviews.At St Pancras, everything was fine until we got into the lounge area, prior to boarding, which we found to be very overcrowded, and when boarding started it was a real "bum fight". At Paris as you go up the stairs prior to checking in, that area can only really be described as organised chaos. That said, once you are on the train, we found everything to be fab and we really enjoyed the journey. We were delayed by 45 mins on the return though.So, overall, are the problems with crowds, queues and delays any worse than at an airport, no. Would we use Eurostar again, definitely!
Late trains, rude staff at the station, food options poor, and price has gone up. Eurostar used to be a nice experience - it's just not anymore

Yesterday, on June 6, 2025 at 5.40 pm, I travelled with my partner on the Eurostar from Paris to Schiphol. Unfortunately, the experience was nothing short of disappointing. Earlier that day we had a long 4.5 hour train ride on a French high speed train from Pau to Paris. That train journey was surprisingly pleasant, comfortable, modern and without making me feel at all nauseous, despite the duration. Unfortunately, that was completely different in the Eurostar. The Eurostar train was outdated, smelled musty and it was extremely hot inside. There was hardly any ventilation and the overall condition of the train really left something to be desired. The comfort was completely lacking. The poor air circulation and shaking of the train made me very nauseous, similar to what I sometimes experience while driving. In short, it was not a pleasant trip. In addition, there was little space for luggage. Many passengers had difficulty getting rid of their bags, which led to a messy and uncomfortable situation on the train. On top of that, there were also warnings about pickpockets on board, which did not give a safe or relaxed feeling, something I did not experience at all on the French train earlier that day.Halfway through the ride, a Dutch conductor came on board who did make a difference. He was incredibly friendly and helpful, offered me a drink and even gave me some fruit sugar to make me feel a little better. I greatly appreciate his care, thanks to him the journey became at least a little more bearable, a big compliment to this conductor. But to Eurostar I really want to give this train is in urgent need of renewal. For an international connection like this, you can simply expect more in 2025.Until obvious improvements are made, you won't see me on this train anytime soon.

It is common a priori to close the gate before the requested arrival time in order to charge the whole family a ticket again. We arrived 15min before the closing time indicated, there was no one in front of us. Even the personnel on board told us that this was not normal but that it was a common practice of profitability. I should have recorded the conversation but I was so appalled that I didn't have the reflex!

We had no issues taking the Eurostar from London to Paris. We bought tickets about a month and a half before so they were relatively cheap. Even though plane tickets would have been around the same price, it was a bigger hassle for us to get to the airport. We took Uber to the train station and it only took about 10 minutes to go through immigration and security, even with our luggage. The train left on time at 9:30am, and the ride was smooth. I know sometimes Eurostar advertises 39 pound tickets to Paris, we couldn't find these for our dates. We paid about $336 for both of us.
