Eurostar is the best advertisement possible for flying to Amsterdam. The 11.04 from St Pancras finally left at 13.10. It reached Brussels at !5.50 where they told us they were terminating because they were so late. We should look for a scheduled train from Brussels to Amsterdam at 16.49, thank you and goodbye. The scheduled train was going to Amsterdam South not Central, was 20 minutes late and had no available seats. If you want a company that couldn’t give a stuff about their clients, cannot be trusted and provide appalling service then I suggest you choose Eurostar.

We wanted to experience Eurostar although it worked out much more expensive than flying. The checking in process at London and Brussels  were as complicated as any airports, slow and long queues. We opted for Plus, the cabin was clean and roomy. The food served was cold and rather tasteless. The dessert was so tiny and of laughable quality. We were offered some alcoholic drinks, wine and beer. Don't know if the extra charge was worth paying. However, the train was fast and reached destinations on time.

Today was my first experience onboard with Eurostar, and definitely will be my last. I had an extremely terrible experience.I booked 6 seats for Paris - Amsterdam trip. We were asked to come 20 mins before boarding time, but the line entering the coach was so long that we were asked to depart from another coach, then walked to our designated coach along the trip to make sure the train boards on time. We went onboard and found that all of our pre-booked seats have been taken. I reported this to the staff, but they were not helpful at ALL. They told me to wait until the departure time and see if I could sit on the seats later. I found out later that before my Paris - Amsterdam train, there should’ve been Paris - Brussels train that has been canceled. They squeezed in passengers from that train to Paris - Amsterdam train without any responsibility. As expected, many people did not get to sit in this 3 hour long trip. The price of Eurostar tickets were more expensive than other trains, yet I did not get to sit and have a comfortable journey. I had to talk to the passengers sitting our pre-booked seats that they took ours (they were supposed to be on the Paris - Brussels train). I think I should’ve not done it myself and that it should’ve been the staffs’ responsibilities to make sure I can sit on my seats. We managed to get 4 out of 6 seats back by talking to the passengers.I will definitely not recommend you to risk your money by traveling with Eurostar.

Our first experience with Eurostar and it couldn't have been better.  We travelled with Eurostar to Brussels and then on Belgium rail to Bruges.In Eurostar we were booked in "Eurostar Plus" which gave us very comfortable seats with plenty of leg room.  A light meal was provided in both directions which was pretty good and appropriate for the relatively short journey.On time in both directions.  Very pleasant and helpful staff on board and at the stations.  A very good fusion of rail and air travel type passenger management.

Find any other option you can instead of Eurostar. They are a complete scam. We’ve booked Premier class tickets well in advance and our train was canceled last minute. There was no notification of the cancellation and when we went to rebook, we were charged €200 for standard class (no Premier class available) and were not given a refund for the fare difference. The reason they gave is because we “chose” to book standard class and that they gave us the option to travel another day (as if we could re-book all of our other hotel reservations, and transfers around this stupid service). These people are complete garbage. You should do anything you can to not travel with Eurostar.

The 2. Traveled with Eurostar.Both times in London extremely unfriendly staff! Just barking at you, commanding. When I asked for help X times at the baggage checkpoint this time and emphasized having had a spinal surgery recently, it was ignored and barked further.

When the service runs on  time it’s great , but it seems to be every time I turn up on time now there are crap unexplained delays and no apologies : not acceptable for the money that is being charged.

Eurostar need to return to ebbsfleet and Ashford sooner than 2026 it’s getting ridiculous now I would actually use Eurostar if they stopped at Ashford but I’m not paying almost £40 to get up to London it’s ridiculous
Terrible bike service. 2 bikes boxed up permitted per train. £45 each. Wanted to take train back from Paris, how are you meant to carry a bike box with you as a cyclist. Ridiculous

We took the Eurostar from Paris to London. We booked Eurostar plus. The check in process was a very long wait and the entire thing took us about 40 min. The train interior in the plus carriage was very worn with stained carpet and worn looking seats. The bathroom had no water or soap to wash your hands. We were served what they called a breakfast meal. It was really just an appetizer in size. Our breakfast consisted of a small bowl of yogurt  and a tiny 2-3 bite chicken sandwich.   We were also served coffee, tea, water or juice. The passenger near us asked if it would be possible to have one more chicken sandwich. She was told that they were out. Our seats faced the galley and once the meals were all served we saw the two stewardesses with a plate each of about 3-4 of the chicken sandwiches eating away. I would have prioritized the passengers first since they paid for a plus seat with a meal rather than eating all of the extras if I were a stewardess. Other than that, it was average or below for seat comfort compared to other business class train seats we have paid extra for.

Be warned that you don't necessarily save time taking eurostar which is more expensive than flights in general.They advised everyone to arrive before the time stated in your ticket or risk yourself not getting on board, but if you arrived at their advised time you are "too early" - on both legs between London and Paris the check-in started late. Everyone just had no choice but cramped shoulder to shoulder waiting for the check in to open.It's an understatement to say this lucrative monopoly falls short in management - they designed the train schedule and they knew how many tickets are sold, yet they catastrophically cannot manage their own designed passenger volume and passengers are treated like cattle. Even budget airlines can do better than that (and way cheaper). On the journey from Paris to London, Eurostar changed their train model (not sure how last minute it was that they can't use their app to notify passengers and make changes), so hundreds of parents with their children were stranded in line patiently for over an hour without any movement, just to get the boarding pass reprinted to change their booked seats at the one and ONLY ONE manned Eurostar counter. It is the ONLY bottleneck which costed us 75mins min. - the Eurostar ticket counter 100% within their own control, not the french border control not the UK border control not the security scan. It could be more efficient by using hand written boarding passes than just one manned counter. It is clearly understaffed too so the earnings probably have gone to the yachts and huge payouts to their management. Proper scrutiny and probe urgently needed, or END its monopoly.Of course no doubt the train was delayed by long, as they cannot get everyone on board on time (surprise!).

There is nothing "plus" about eurostar plus. In fact, in the 10+ years I have been taking the Brussels/London return route myself and many fellow passengers have noticed the total collapse of Eurostar service in general. Constant: delays; degraded and sometimes near non-existant terminals; confusion in information to passengers; ridiculous prices for service and overall general collapse of in-transit service from staff that predominantly have no idea what they are doing. They barely look at passengers and seem now more interesting in attempting to solve the constant chaos around them. I don't blem them. It isnt there fault, there is clearly an overall total mismanagement and organisation from the top down.It's a total joke. Like Fawlty Towers but without the hotel or humour. While thier monopoly of the route continues there is little alternative but we shall be considering air options as much as possible from now on.
Horrible. Infinite waiting time, poor organization at the station and train delay of several tens of minutes. Shame on the price.

Terrible definitely won’t use again. 3 hour delay on the out going journey. 35 minute delay on the way back. The delay on the way back resulted in us having the extra expense of paying a further £100 for an additional train journey due to missing connection. Communication was awful! Did not get any emails until 24 hours after. Compensation is by way of 50% of the value of the affected leg of the journey if you want a cash refund, or 60% if you want an e-voucher. Diabolical.

We travelled to Paris from London today and was very disappointed with the service. An incident earlier in the day at paris had caused disruption to all of the trains, however, we were still called through passport control one hour before scheduled departure despite them knowing our train would be delayed, resulting in a very packed, overcrowded waiting room . The delay wasn't displayed on the board until 10 minutes before we were due to board and then even worse, the time kept changing. The tannoy system announced our train had arrived and was being cleaned and put a new departure time up, then changed again 5 minutes before. They then allowed the passengers on the train scheduled 1 hour after ours to board before us, I can only assume to avoid paying them compensation, which was extremely frustrating . We ended up boarding the train at 6pm for a scheduled departure of 3.30pm. Delays cannot be avoided sometimes but the management and information provided to customers was shocking, especially when travelling with 2 young children - we could have spent a couple of hours in London rather than being stuck in the small waiting room. Will be seeking a refund but already finding the system for claiming very unclear on the app.

If you treat this 2-hour train ride as no-frills flight, then your expectations will be met or even be exceeded. The train schedule is convenient and pretty reliable and you get more legroom than in a plane. The problem are the waiting room/lounge at the station, due security you have to arrive and spend 30+ minutes in a packed room, no windows, not enough seats and rip-off food and drinks. Worse than in any airport.

Was asked to be there 2hours before departure despite checkin not being open for another hour!! Filthy toilets. Train was full and luggage space was woefully inadequate. My first experience and hopefully my last

Eurostar are an absolute disgrace. Having had our homeward journey leg from Amsterdam to Brussels delayed by hours, we were told that when we got to Brussels Eurostar staff would sort us out hotels to stay in overnight as we would arrive too late to make our onward journey back to the UK. When we arrived at the station Eurostar had closed their desk and all staff including management had left. This meant that there were hundreds of passengers many of whom didn’t speak French abandoned in a foreign city at midnight. All the hotels were packed. I ended up with my partner and 5 other ladies including a teenage girl travelling on her own, walking around the area, which was very scary, begging establishments for a room. Finally after explaining our situation we managed to get accommodation.I have since attempted to get compensation but have been denied. I would advise nobody to travel by Eurostar. I certainly never will again.

We traveled between Paris and Brussels and the ride was fast and smooth.  It was quite comfortable.  Boarding and leaving were easy.  Friendly staff to help us.  Make sure you bring your food and drinks with you as they had almost nothing on board.

Incredible experience! We were travelling from St Pancras to Paris for my best friends birthday, she had a badge on and Reddah was simply walking through the train. Stopped and ensured we were having an enjoyable journey, later he showed up with a complimentary bottle of champagne for us to celebrate. Amazing customer service. He was amazing!

Eurostar Plus too expensive for what you get: tiny portions of food for the meal on board, cardboard cup for tiny initial fruit juice drink, the smallest desert you have ever seen, one teaspoon carried the cube of cake, cramped passenger facilities at Amsterdam terminus, one small cafe whose electricity signal caused the till to fail, long queues, two of the toilets outbound on board didn't work. Overall poor food, facilities,  overpriced.

For the first time with the EuroStar, easy boarding in Rotterdam and hassle-free to st.PancrasThe return trip there was a delay of 30 min. and idd it is quite busy in the waiting area But we would do it again with the train instead of flying

I took a standard class train from London to Paris. There are different types of seats, such as four- or two-seat seats, and some seats are difficult to see outside depending on the location of the windows, so be careful when making reservations.I thought that if I just wanted to ride and travel, the standard class would be enough. The speed is also over 300 kilometers, which is perfect. There is a wide range of prices depending on the time of day, so if you want to ride cheaply, you should go for the early hours. It's better to avoid late departures, even if they're cheaper for security reasons, as they'll be slower to arrive.

I would like to report my unpleasant experience regarding the journey from Rotterdam to London on 14.05.2025. My boyfriend and I arrived at the platform at around 19:10, after having already entered Rotterdam station and checked in with our ticket. After entering, we stayed on the lower level of the station because we saw that the train was delayed, and we bought something to eat. Then we went up to the platform, and the staff, in a very rude manner, told us that we would “definitely not be taking the train tonight,” because the passport control was already closed.We had no idea what they were talking about, and eventually received some explanation from a staff member who personally threatened to call security on me if I didn’t leave, when I was simply asking for information. He told us we couldn’t board anymore because the office was closed, and when we tried to speak to the woman inside the office (who was still there), she just walked away.We weren’t the only ones: another girl was in tears after being treated the same way, and another couple who arrived just after us ended up in the same situation. We tried in every way to speak to your staff, but the woman completely ignored us, while the station personnel kept insisting we had to leave. They were all there, the train arrived late, and then it left—without anyone even trying to help us.In the meantime, we checked all the numerous emails received from Eurostar and found that only in one of them it stated that check-in closes 30 minutes before departure. It didn’t even mention that passport control was involved, nor did it explain it properly. Such important information should be placed at the beginning of a message and clearly explained—not hidden at the bottom of one of many emails, without even clarifying its meaning.We arrived at the station on time, saw that the train was delayed, and didn’t worry about anything else because nothing was clearly indicated. We are extremely upset about our experience with Eurostar, which provided unclear information and whose staff, despite having the opportunity, did absolutely nothing to help us.The only person who eventually helped us was another member of the staff who, unlike all the others, took the time to provide a solution. It was extremely important for us to be in London tonight, and this change of plans caused us major inconvenience—especially considering the train was delayed, the staff was still present, and instead of treating us with kindness (as is expected when paying for a service), they could have simply taken two minutes to let us board. They absolutely could have done it. Very poor service.

Fantastic journey from London to Amsterdam on 9th May 6.15am . Return journey 12th May 13.40 .On time , efficient , clean , party of 10 , really enjoyed it . We did take our own food and soft drink and purchased coffee from the buffet car .

My wife and I were travelling from the Midlands to the Black Forest in Germany on the 9th of May taking the 1131 Eurostar from London to Paris. We left early to make sure that we would arrive at the station in time and took breakfast in Saint Pancras. The toilets there were absolutely filthy had never been cleaned. When we queued for the train, we were told that it was being delayed, and were ushered into the waiting area along with passengers of other delayed trains. We were all squashed in standing room only it was awful. Our train was delayed for more than an hour and a half it completely disrupted our whole journey and we got to our hotel very late. When I applied for compensation, I was awarded 63 points! The lowest price ticket on points is 800. That’s not compensation it’s an insult.
It's terrible. Delayed. No information given. Dirty toilets. Ludicrous queuing system. Cramped. Will never use it again.

Look - there’s a lot of positives to the Eurostar. I travel pretty frequently, the staff are usually pleasant, I usually get there on time enough. But my big gripe with the service is the food. I’m a pescatarian. We live in 2025. It’s not that hard! My experience (shared between standard premier and business class, goes as follows). Yes, they do a vegetarian main meal which is hot, but you always have to order 48 hours in advance, which is annoying as the Eurostar is a service which prides itself on a quick getaway. Yes, there’s a vegetarian salad, but it sells out before it reaches us. Yes if we hadn’t brought Pret we wouldn’t have eaten a main. I mean not that we would’ve wanted to eat the main because the food quality is always appalling. Stale rubbery bread, grim cake, a main which looks worse than school dinners. I’ve said it privately and now I’ll say it louder and hope that they listen. Eurostar. Your service is good. I’ll keep travelling. Your staff are lovely. Please. For the love of all things. Improve your food and your attitude to vegetarians. It’s 2025. How hard can it be!

Travel  in Premier Class for business on a regular basis. Expensive but worth it for ability to turn up very late when in a rush. Service generally pretty good but the food in Premier is consistently terrible so I recommend picking up Pret in the terminal first

Traveling with Eurostar from London to Paris in premier seating is a delightful experience, especially with the added perks that come along with it. As soon as you settle into your seat, the attentive staff treats you to a selection of fresh pastries and a light meal, elevating the journey right from the start. You also have the option to enjoy a warm cup of tea or coffee.The entire journey lasts approximately two hours, allowing you to relax and take in the views as the countryside. Additionally, right outside the station doors, there is a well-organized taxi queue, expertly managed by an attendant who ensures a swift and efficient flow of vehicles. This makes the transition from train to taxi seamless, allowing you to begin your Parisian adventure with ease. Overall, the combination of comfort, attentive service, and convenience makes traveling with Eurostar an excellent choice.

Travelling London to Amsterdam was no problem, but coming back, absolute shambles. Brand new terminal at Amsterdam Centraal, staff employed by an agency (G4S) who couldn't run a bath let alone a terminal. Queues galore and the time to departure was so close they opened (Eventually) another entry point only to be met by a load of stairs. As I'm partially disabled (And over 60) I pointed this out to the G4S operative and that I needed to use the one opposite as it had an escalator. This was flatly and RUDELY refused and was told in no uncertain terms to "Move Along". Fortunately some kind young guy offered to hellp take my case upstairs for me. The day before we came home our friends departed and reported that the cafe had totally run out of everything by the time they'd cleared security. This is a brand new terminal, why hasn't this been incorporated into the building plans? What sort of cafe, knowing there is problems thensays "We don't take cash?" Absolute Joke. The problems seriously need addressing and the G4S staff need customer service training

Pay for an over priced ticket to arrive to a crammed terminal to sit on the floor before taking the slowest 'fast train' experience, you might as well catch the channel barge and then ride a bicycle across the country. I thought maybe this one way experience was isolated. Surely not, the next trip was no different.Absolutely crammed terminal, 2 delay messages on the trip back home. ( 2 EXTRA HOURS DELAY.I recommend taking the risk of a delayed flight to avoid getting on this serviceDO NOT TAKE THE EUROSTAR UNTIL THIS COMPANY FIXES COMMUNICATION, PROCEDURE AND ADDS SEATS TO THEIR TERMINAL SO PEOPLE DOTN HAVE TO SIT ON A FILTHY FLOOR DURING THE NEVER ENDING DELAYS

We travelled with Eurostar from Amsterdam to Brussels and it was so quick. After seeking assistance at the train station for which platform (15) we found it very easy to travel. Seats were comfy  recommend

We had a great Eurostar journey from London to Brussels on Sat 19 Apr (~ 15:30pm) thanks to Malik. He was friendly, professional, and went above and beyond to ensure a smooth and comfortable trip. Excellent customer service !

Our first time using this service. We had a great time. Check in was easy, yes departure hall was busy but 2 trains left almost at the same time. Once called, made our way to the platform where we were greeted by a wonderful member of staff, sharing jokes and a smile with us. We used the Europlus service and breakfast was nice. The same member of staff (and a male) served us on this service. They were great. Attentive and relaxed, friendly. Sat in a comfy seat watching the countryside roll by at 300km. Can’t beat it. (We were 07:04, carriage 1, seats 33,34, London to Brussels) 💋❤️
The train was great but St Pancras station in London was chaotic. Disorganized and challenging with luggage.  Long lines and then nowhere to sit.

Terrible is the kindest word I can use to describe our Eurostar experience from London.  We were packed in like sardines in the departure lounge.  Far too small an area for the number of people waiting to board the train.  Staff were helpful when boarding. We traveled first class but cannot say the seats were very comfortable or a lot of space.  Be warned there are different levels of first class and not all allow access to the station first class lounge so check when booking your ticket.  Food was dreadful.  Good point was the speed of getting to Paris.  Eurostar need some competition as this is everything that is wrong with a monopoly situation
We decided to travel standard class to Paris, unfortunately the coaches in this class are beginning to look tired on our train, and not very clean, dust everywhere ,  shame really

Remember that if you can't go then you have to pay 25pp per trip cancellation fee really and top idea. And that money if you are 7 days in advance otherwise you are completely unlucky and you can not cancel.

This was one of the best services I’ve experienced in a long time—especially thanks to our driver, Guillaume Lebeuf (I hope I got his name right). The journey last Sunday from Paris to London was exceptional. Without a doubt, this is the finest way to travel between London and Paris—it’s simply unmatched. Keep up the outstanding work; you’ve set the bar incredibly high!

Absolutely disgusting organisation and putting thousands of people for no reason in.  Full waiting area I use a walking stick and my first and last time ever on Eurostar no brain cells used at all and not a care for anyone. Why tell you to go through when you have over 2 hrs to wait in a hell hole
eurostar is the best company the staff are really friendly and kind and loving and its the best customer service and the food is fantastic and really cool and i  love this company so much

Dear Eurostar Customer Service, I am writing to express my deep dissatisfaction and utter disbelief at the way I, along with approximately 35 other passengers, were treated on Eurostar train number 9348 of April 23, 2025 departed from Amsterdam Centraal to Paris Nord at 9.10am from platform 15b. First and foremost, the train we had originally been scheduled to take – as indicated on our tickets – was cancelled without any prior notification only for us to find out upon checking in. We were all transferred to this alternative train with no seats assigned, leaving us standing for the entire journey despite having each paid approximately €125 per ticket (that makes 250eu for me & my husband). I, like the rest, had expected a certain standard of service from Eurostar and instead received none. What made an already uncomfortable situation dramatically worse was the behavior of the train “manager.” I use that title loosely, as her conduct was not only unprofessional but outright hostile and unacceptable. I had overheard her being rude to another passenger even before boarding, but nothing could have prepared me for how shockingly she escalated things onboard.She made absolutely no effort to support or assist any of us standing passengers. When we raised complaints—rightfully so—she repeatedly interrupted us, spoke over people, raised her voice, and dismissed our concerns, besides the fact that having such a big group of people standing up next to eachother in the bar area like sardines is also a hazard. Hence my husband asked to at least be offered a complimentary coffee instead of water, given the circumstances, and even this was flatly denied because apparently Eurostar does not offer complimentary coffee for distressed passengers. When my husband calmly expressed his frustration (yes with a bit of a tone but nothing loud or violent) she threatened to call the police on him while also raising her voice. I stayed silent, looked down at my phone, and hushed “how stupid,” clearly referring to the absurdity of the situation, not to her personally. Suddenly, she began shouting, accusing me of calling her stupid. I attempted to clarify, but she wouldn’t hear a word and insisted that security would remove us from the train. And she followed through on that. At Antwerp, we were treated like criminals—escorted off the train by security simply because we complained about: a) Not receiving the service we paid forb) Being left to stand the entire journeyc) Requesting a basic gesture of goodwill like coffee This ordeal left me in tears, having a panic attack on the platform in Antwerp. I had a flight to catch from Brussels, and this experience jeopardized that connection, not to mention the emotional distress and public humiliation that I was put through. I occupy a C-Level position within an international company, with several years of experience within customer facing industries and I also travel extensively across the world. I have never, in all my travels, experienced such disgraceful treatment or been made to feel so humiliated. The woman clearly wanted to make a show out of us so nobody complains any longer. So, since when complaining has become a criminal offense? The only positive aspect of this situation was the calm, respectful handling by the Antwerp security staff and local train personnel—who, unlike your onboard manager, showed basic humanity.

Great train, let down by appalling infrastructure & stations.No seating in departure area for trip to Paris as the area isn't big enough for the number of passengers. Trip from London to Paris took 7 hour due to a fire near the tracks causing a 2-3 hour delay for leaving then everything else was slowed down by the number of trains already stuck on the track. At least in an airport you are stuck in a big departure lounge not in your seat.On they way back, we arrived an hour and a half before departure and only just made it to he train on time. We had 1.5 hours of standing in a queue either in the station with building work at 85 db or in security screamed at by private security!We will NEVER take this train again.Also, wifi is so slow its almost non existent and on some services you can only charge equipment if you have a French plug.

Overall fast and comfortable. However our outward journey was delayed by about 20 minutes. The customer service at the Gare du Nord was appalling: we were shouted at by one of the employees to get into pairs; he then demanded that my husband take his iPad out of his bag before the cases X-rays despite being told he didn’t have one. He even threatened to open the case himself although he had no such remit himself. Very stressful situation

We arrived at the station 20 minutes before our Eurostar train to Brussels, with plenty of time to board. The train had not departed. Yet, we were turned away — not for being late, but because Eurostar enforces a gate closure 30 minutes before departure, regardless of whether passengers could still board safely.We were then forced to pay £88 (for two missed departure fees) to be allowed on the next train. I work part-time on minimum wage, and this trip — our only holiday of the year — was paid for through months of saving.We had woken up at 3:45am to make this journey. Instead of compassion, we were met with a rigid policy and a complete lack of humanity. I was so shaken by the experience, I’ve been unwell ever since. It destroyed the beginning of our trip and cast a shadow over the entire experience.The worst part? Their customer service had no interest in our situation. Just a cold “policy is policy” email with no consideration for the real people behind the ticket.Eurostar’s policies are not about logistics or efficiency — they are about extracting more money from their customers. The station was overcrowded, poorly managed, and not even equipped to provide seats to the early arrival they demand.Avoid this company if you value dignity or decent treatment. I’ll never travel with them again.

Before booking on board attractive price that does not exist: after booking 3 times the advertised price paris amsterdam 169€ ticket taken a month and a half before the date! Delay 20 minutes to departure.  This airline is expensive with permanent delays...thalys was much better.

the Eurostar is a perfect way to travel. From my experience travelling Premier, everything is just so good. The lounge wasn’t overpacked, the food during the train service was spectacular and the staff and service was even better. Everyone knew fluent English, which was extremely helpful. Security was also a breeze.
We travel from St Pancras to Belgium Brussels. It was excellent experience. Seats were comfortable and if you have travel pillow then can sleep while sitting.

Poor service, long journey and way too expensive. Had booked Eurostar plus from Rotterdam to London and was 450 euros lost for a return. 3 times as expensive as plane. The trains were no longer running directly so had to change trains in Brussels and wait two hours for the next train to arrive and return. The extra service you pay for with Eurostar plus is only available on the Brussels - London route and not between Brussels and the Netherlands.Food is also very basic and you only get coffee or tea once.Brussels station is terrible and there are no seats anywhere so people are waiting on the ground.The staff is generally quite friendly but there are also some very unsympathetic figures among them.The train journey took me 5 hours on both outward and return journeys. Friends of mine who went by plane ended up in London an hour earlier.This was the last time for me this way.

Check in at both London and Paris is a shambles. Hopelessly under invested in space, long queues everywhere, herded and contained like cattle. Rude and officious staff at both ends making it an awful experience.Both trains were late setting off and arriving.We went Eurostar plus which gives no check in advantage. Cold unappetising food is served and the drinks service, both hot and cold is way substandard.Overall an unpleasant and very expensive experience.

I have used the Eurostar a number of times for business and leisure never having any major issues. However the first impression at the station (outside the beautiful architecture) is of a cattle market with people herded through an ever closing gap in London. The waiting area is crowded and messy, first impressions and all that. Lille and Paris not that much better. However the train and journey itself have always been excellent. This time was travelling for pleasure and had the same experience. My advice would be get the cheapest ticket you can as the upgrades are not like when travelling on a plane

We paid £800 for 2 seats one way to Paris, “FIRST CLASS” what a waste of money. Business lounge breakfast at 10.45, a choice of mixed crisps. No pastries in sight.  Disgusting. There was no hushed talking on board either blah blah blah…. Ruining the supposed ambiance…..the lunch, one floret of cauliflower….. what a rip off. Ive been mis-sold i want my money back, standard ticket is £39… how can they justify this…

Our first trip on Eurostar traveling Eurostar Plus - the waiting area in London was absolutely rammed with people and not a good first impression . Once onboard the train was clean - comfortable and staff helpful . The meal choice should tell them something - we wanted the chicken but when they got to us they only had the blue cheese option It was truly awful . Disembarkation was easy and we found our connecting train easily . Return journey was similar in that the waiting area in Brussels is inadequate but again train was good and on time . The disembarkation back in London was chaos - long queues and no staff in site .Once  on the train great - waiting areas poor with London the worst

I have previously written a review of Eurostar and not a very good one. Since its early days, the service has become overcrowded and quite frankly , overwhelming.It still is.But yesterday Eurostar came to our rescue. While travelling from Hull to London, not one but TWO of our trains broke down which resulted in a two hour delay and consequently missing our 13.04 Eurostar to Lille.We were looking at paying an extra £175 each.We called ahead of our arrival at Kings Cross and were assured that they would help. And they did.With a smile on their face we were given tickets for the next Eurostar. The service could not have been better. Thank you.

I traveled in premier standard from dres to Brussels at 13:05 pm, I have already traveled several times in this category by Eurostar and it is usually very good but this time I had a problem because, when starting the food service the attendant skipped and gave me nothing until the other attendant noticed and told his partner that he had not even attended me, the attendant did NOT apologize only saying that I was invisible and attended me in a bad way, I found his comment and his bad attitude very bad, what a shame that for one person your trip is not as comfortable as you expected.

Our experience of the Eurostar terminal was fairly horrendous; there were crowds standing shoulder-to-shoulder and enormous queues. It turned out this was because the train before ours had left very late. We had chosen to travel by train because I hate the ‘frisking’ at airport security; the scanner is always set off by my metal replacement knees. But it was just the same here; and they will not listen when you explain the knee replacements are the reason the alarm goes off. All very unpleasant.We had booked ‘Eurostar Plus’ tickets, but when we boarded the train we found we were in seats opposite two other people, whereas we had expected to be on our own. The seats were quite narrow compared with those in 1st class on the SCNF trains,  and there was no more legroom than we would have on a commuter train in England. A small salad was provided for lunch, which was quite acceptable; wine and soft drinks also available. But it wasn’t the enjoyable start to our holiday that I had anticipated.

The track changed at the last minute in Antwerp. I got on the Eurostar wrongly. I was ordered to buy a ticket of 144 Euro or I would be handed over to the Rotterdam police. I should read the name of the train he said! I felt treated like a criminal and also the reaction to a complaint showed little understanding and no waiver of the fine of 140 Euro. Bad experience.

A quick and comfortable trip after exploring your last day in Amsterdam. The train station is really central, and the train departed exactly at 18:08am, leaving travellers in a great area of Paris which is where the Paris Nord station is at 21:38. The train leaves on the exact timetable and arrives in the centre of Paris, with public transport at hand (from front of a metro station), which greatly facilitates the journey to other places. In our case we deliberately picked a hotel glued to Paris Nord Station, on Rue de Chabrol and even with the late arrival time, we moved on foot to the hotel. It was a good experience, which allowed us to explore another day from Paris, because our return from Charles De Gaulle was only in the evening. Being close to Gare do Nord was just to take the train to the airport and we arrived quickly for our boarding. We took advantage of two great cities in two days with a program to enjoy only the essential and enjoy them calmly. It's worth it.

We caught this from Brussels in Belgium to St Pancras in London. Told to arrive an hour before leaving time to allow for luggage scan and passport checks etc. The duty free area is a rip off as things are cheaper to buy away from the site, and as long as the container is sealed you can pack drink and cigarettes in your suitcase. The journey was smooth and fast but a lot more expensive than flying or catching a coach to or from Brussels.

Arrived around 6:30 for the 8:01 to Paris, security opened at 6:30. All went smoothly. Our train was delayed, started boarding around 8:10. Traveling with a disability, staff gave us priority for the lift to the platform. Smooth journey, arrived at Gare du Nord about 11:45. Had to travel to Gare St. Lazard to catch 12:59 for Bayeaux. At Taxi rank, staff gave us priority and we got to GSL by 12:15, cost ~12€. In GSL (first time there) stood with crowd in Blue Zone waiting for board to show platform. It did at 20 minutes before departure. Badged through with digital ticket in my iPhone wallet. Tickets said Coach 3 but coaches were 12 - 13. Staff member told us to take any seat in front car (1stClass). Train was not at all crowded, more than half of the seats were empty. No problem.

The trains and people on board themselves are very good. However, the amount of immigration and security measures and the pokey holding area ahead of boarding at St Pancras are not anywhere near world class. They are under dimensioned for the number of trains and passengers. This all results in a journey length that well exceeds flying, even through Heathrow if you live  up to 1,5 hours from - in this case - Amsterdam Airport. Security at the Eurotunnel for cars costs much less time than this.

Had a trip to Paris booked on Saturday 8th March, thankfully the trains started after the mess on the Friday. Thankfully we had no issues with checking in/boarding and using the train. The staff were really friendly and our seats were great. Bar was easy to get too/use and the toilets clean throughout the journey.Would definitely recommend.
John's train is now cancelled and can't make footy tonight. Absolutely shocking. Will be using different train in future. Thanks.

Left from St Pancreas. It was like living in a third world country. No enough seating and lots of people standing in walkways and corridors. If there had been an emergency it would have been a complete disaster and loss of life. Facilities for food and drink where like experiencing the hunger games. Is this the best Eurostar can do? Shame on you.

Standard Premier: very high prices. Website does not work well, so have to book Eurostar and then another website to book an onward journey in France. Lounges in both London an Paris are overcrowded, poor shops. Customs are worse than ever and worse than airport check-ins. Food and drink selection is, with a culinary consultant !, absolutely awful. The hot breakfast and hot dinners a congealed mess of whatever. Portions minuscule.

My adult daughter and I had rt tickets London to Brussels . I purchased premium seats that were pricey . Premium tix are said to include separate lines for check in which were non existent in both London & Brussels . I found the the security and passport control to be almost worse than some airports . Our seats were comfortable but hardly premium . All staff were attentive , friendly and helpful .Both lounges were well staffed , not much in food selection but very clean and comfortable . Our meals on the train were nothing special , more like sample sized portions of various foods. The journey went well , relaxing quiet ride . Again the staff at stations , lounges and on the trains were wonderful . The premium aspect is lacking imo.

The Eurostar booking process on their app is fairly straightforward, but I would not recommend their travel insurance partner, Allianz Assistance. I was one of those affected by train cancellations on 7th March 2025 due to the discovery of a suspected WWII bomb near the Gare du Nord station. The situation as St Pancras was fairly chaotic, with contradictory information and an initial lack of on-scene command. It almost seemed as if Eurostar lacked an effective contingency plan for such an event. However, useful information was eventually provided and Eurostar were quick to provide refunds or other options. However, the same cannot be said of Allianz Assistance. They refused my claim for reasonable trip cancellation costs citing an 'act of war' exclusion in their policy. They didn't even offer to reimburse my insurance premium despite the fact that the abrupt trip cancellation seemingly placed them under no risk whatsoever. In my view, Eurostar should consider selecting a more service-orientated insurance partner. In the meantime, I would recommend that you go elsewhere for your travel insurance.

PROS*  It is a famous an classic and  iconic name brand product*  The "nose trains" are sleek and smooth and massive and impressive* The famous name conjures luxury and a new era of train travel*  It is a major transportation method from London to Paris, Brussels, Rotterdam and Amsterdam*  The travel journey is directly from one city center tother city center*   It is the better and preferred way to travel than flying- convenience, location, hassle, etc... it is certainly greener and maybe it costs less too*  It is exciting to travel under the English Channel *  See the Dutch, Belgian, French and English countrysides with adequate sized picture windows*  There are reserved seats so one has a secured spot and a modicum of comfort*   Prices are very much less expensive months before departure, but there are sales sometimes*  "Frequent traveler" program; website and smartphone application*  Food available for purchase (I didn't do that)*  One can explore the large international urban train stations.*  It merged with Thalys which also has the sleek and beautiful nose trains.CONS*  The trains are always crowded and always busy and always full  *  Adequate baggage space might be a challenge*  Dynamic pricing is challenging*  Once customs is completed, there is not adequate places to sit nor anything to purchase to eat nor adequate restroom facilities XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX"I VISITED THIS PLACE​"...... because I traveled from St. Pancras London to Amsterdam Centraal.  I arrived after 0500H for the 0615 departure.  There were 200 people already there.  The line moved and the two border inspections passed OK.Since there were other trains departing at that hour, there was certainly no place to sit and barely any place to stand in the inadequate waiting area.  I purchased my ticket early foe the best fare and the best seat selection.  I had a window seat facing forward at the front of the train.  I slept from Britain to Belgium.  The part of the journey during which I was conscious was uneventful.This was my second Eurostar adventure- the first being a year and a half ago.  I had wanted to take this train journey ever since it started almost 20 years ago.  But I expected something epic and memorable and everlasting and meaningful- after all, the name Eurostar is iconic.  I found out then and again now that this is... a train.WAS IT WORTH THE COST?Yes!!  Buying early if you can is so worthwhile.WOULD "I VISIT THIS PLACE" AGAIN?Sure!!  I'm no longer obsessed with it as something that I absolutely must do, but it is efficient travel to and from London to the continent, and I'd definitely choose it againADVICES*  I highly recommend this mode of transport between those cities- it's preferred over flying*  Book early to get best price and seat*  Be prepared for passport controls and inadequate and crowded waiting areas

Pay 200€ in a trip of 1.5h total duration. In both directions the trip was delayed, in the first leg of 30 mins. Zero information or organization. Dirty, noisy wagons. 0 right to compensation. This used to be a good alternative to the plane but it is clearly no longer. Expensive, poor service and total lack of punctuality.

I booked 4 tickets, they gave me 4 places, in the end I didn't use one place and I was sitting alone, they made me move only that other two people can sit together!! To be honest I felt it was super racist and the woman moving me was extremely rude, totally not recommended!!

When traveling between London and Paris, Eurostar provides an excellent option for this journey.  However, St Pancras was heaving (not helped by all of the infrastructure being put in place for the new border checks that have now been postponed until October 2025; plus, many people with multiple large suitcases made boarding and finding one’s seat chaotic).  Once in Paris, it was only a couple of stops on Metro line D to Gare to Lyon where the hotel and conference centre were located. The return journey was very smooth with no queues for ticket, passport or security checks, plus very smooth boarding of the train.

Train ride was fine but don't bother even trying to use the wifi. It doesn't work. You might as well have no wifi. Do better Eurostar. I could not do anything on my computer the entire ride from London to Paris.

Avoid at all costs!! My Eurostar train was cancelled today Friday 7th March. Tried to call the company number, no reply tried to get on the website to get refund and rebook but it kept crashing. Had to make a new booking at £430 just to get home and a further £200 on a hotel room. Eurostar offered no help or support I will never travel with these amateurs again

St Pancras cannot cope with demand and is scrum to get on the train.Brussels end is even worse. Waiting area is like a dungeon with very few services. In fact, there's more area for duty free than seating. Food is VERY limited. Furthermore,  one has to queue back through the duty free to board. Chaotic!The train carriages are showing their age and one feels you need a good wash after alighting. Internet/WiFi is truly hopefully I would avoid if I could and not cheap
The driver helped us and was super nice! it was on train 9050. really top thank you sir you helped us!

Gare du nord chaos as usual. They separate off families with children but then don't let them through. Cue lots of crying children standing in long queue that doesn't move. There's no signs like in London, eventually just one members of staff trying to shout instructions. Once inside, complete mayhem, people sitting everywhere because train is delayed- why not display this earlier???- information boards all broken. We've not travelled through and it's not been chaos, in last few years. Clearly systematic problem. Once on train, drunk passenger was allowed to continue buying more and more alcohol from the train bar despite the fact chap can hardly stand up. He gets more disruptive and loud, on increasingly long delayed train. On board staff obviously aware, they can see him, just ignore. More crying children. Really poor even by eurostar standards

London - Belgium So it was our first trip on the Eurostar leaving from london to Belgium.  Check in was very smooth and easy. Staff were friendly and helpful. There's not much room when you go through but you are not there for long. The first train due to leave for Paris was delayed so they ended up boarding our train at the same time. I must say that having the two trains loading at the same time. Iwas okay but a little hectic.We got to our seats and in the rush I didn't notice that there was a stain and a wet patch on my seat. I only noticed it when my jeans became damp. It was clear that the stain had tried to be cleaned but had remained damp. I had to get tissue to soak up the remaining moisture and sat on tissues until my husband said he would switch and put more tissues down. I couldn't grab the attention of a guard so I messaged the Eurostar team via messenger. It didn't expect this sort of thing to happen to on a Eurostar. I would have expected that they would have taken the seat out of service. As I hadn't traveled on this service before I was not sure what the protocol was for moving or trying to find another seat on what was a busy service. So disappointed with this bit. However getting to Brussels-midi was so easy and the journey was so very quick and easy. We upgraded on the way back so I will review that separately. I would definitely go again and would feel far more confident about trying to move etc.

It is a fast and effective option for travel within Europe. He went out on schedule and everything was perfect. The only issue is the small space for bags of 23kgs and that you have to be controlling at each stop that no catch gets off with your bag.

Excellent experience, taking our daughter to Paris for her sixteenth birthday.  We opted for the middle service level and were quite astounded by the attentive, polite and helpful staff.  Truly first rate service.  Food was lovely, seats comfy, reclinable, spaciousness, magazines available, plenty of charging points for mobiles.  Couldn't have been any better.

The train itself is fine, as is the St Pancras terminal. But Paris Gare du Nord! What a nightmare!The security people are the most unpleasant I have ever come across. They get worse every time we travel. This time, as our bags emerged from the scanner, two people started shouting 'move the boxes' over and over again at us, while they just stood there doing nothing. When we didn't do it fast enough for them, the intensity of their shouting increased. Finally, when my husband was offended and let them know, they chased him through the hall shouting that he would be arrested. He's 76! They should be ashamed of themselves. Never again!Don't arrive early - there's nowhere to sit, and if you're lucky enough to find somewhere, it's decrepit.

We had never taken Eurostar as foot passengers only as car passengers which is an excellent service.  We decided to visit Paris and go on the train instead of flying.  Disappointed with the whole experience.  Travelling up to London from near the coast was a pain as we needed to drive  due to dropping off the dog on route so chose to drive to Morden underground and I used my parking app to park on a private drive 1 minute walk from the tube.  Much easier to drive to an airport and park for the duration.  Easy journey from Morden on the northern line to St Pancras. Tapped in and out with Oyster card.  We enjoyed a relaxed breakfast at one of the good restaurants before going to Eurostar. Then it all got very, very busy.  Crowds were crammed into the Eurostar terminal.  We were funnelled through both English and French passport control and the XRay security.  That is why you need to be at the station 90 minutes before your train.  Eventually once through security  there were not enough seats to accommodate all the travellers waiting.  It was a holding pen.  The train was comfortable and due to having paid extra for a ‘plus’ ticket food and drink were included.  We had booked a lovely hotel but took it for granted that metro/bus travel would be a simple tap in tap out system but not in Paris!  Having realised paper tickets were issued for all metro trips we queued at a ticket window and asked to buy a weeks travel card.  After much confusion we realised you had to have a photo attached to it so we were  sold a daily card instead with no photo requirement. However you don’t top up these cards when required, you have to top them up with the number of journeys you feel you might take at the beginning of each day which if not used, did not carry over to the next day.  Absolutely bizarre!We did try to use it on the bus but it wasn’t valid and we had to find cash.  It was like the U.K. system 30 odd years ago. To be honest the transport system is not integratedand not that simple to navigate.  Twice the ticket windows were closed and often at least one of the ticket machines were out of order with long queues forming as tourists struggled to use them. We gave up on day 3 and from then on used our Uber app and found this a quicker, easier and cheaper method of travelling round Paris.  The return trip from Gare du Nor station provided no comfortable restaurants for breakfast.  The concourse was cold and draughty and we eventually found seats in a Burritos food outlet that was warm and drank coffee listening to Mexican music at 08.30.  The Eurostar check in was even busier and more chaotic than in London.  The signage not clear - our information board told us the train was boarding then boarding had closed whilst all the passengers stood in a huge queue waiting to get access to the platform.  Lessons learned - fly to Paris and use Ubers to travel around.

I’ve seen other people have had unfortunate experiences and last year I was stuck in Italy for 36 hours because of an airline so after that, Eurostar was my first choice because if there are any delays, there is always another train.It worked perfectly for us, we had the upgrade and there was loads of space and we were served lunch with wine! The whole trip was the best rail journey I have ever experienced. There were families with Babies who were able to just leave their pushchairs parked. Stress free. Maybe only downside was when we arrived in Paris there was a long queue to leave the platform.I’m looking forward to the journey home!
Terrible company. On the way there cancelled the train, so we went on holiday a day later. On the way back the train was delayed considerably

We took the Eurostar my spouse, a couple of friends and me as part of our friend's surprise birthday and myself. The captain, found out and gave us very nice intentions throughout the trip. Furthermore, we had very good advice regarding London transport. It's been a great ride! Special thanks to Karine, JF and Mira for their welcome!

Rubbish. I've had 2 trips to Amsterdam this year, both badly delayed and resuting in my getting to bed at 2am. Got delayed from Amsterdam to Brussels, all made to run through the station and threatened with "check-in closing in 60 seconds" for the last train to London (supposed to be about 45 mins gap) only to find that the London train was delayed by 30 minutes anyway so there was no rush.London train was delayed by about 50 minutes, no communication at the station. It had apparently been at the station for 45 minutes before departure but they hadn't even cleared crisp packets off the tables. Many toilets out of order and staff clueless about what the delay was.Fed up of paying premium prices for a crap service.

On this occasion I won’t go with 5 Star and Excellent as we suffered a lengthy delay on our return journey from Paris to London, and then suffered numerous problems trying to make our Compensation Claim via their On-Line system.But on board the Train we were well looked after, food and drink good and information from staff on the delayed return can’t be faulted.Our Compensation Claim was however easily sorted by phone and the lady who resolved it, was exceptionally helpful and responded with an immediate email confirming what was agreed. She deserved a 5 Star + for assistance. Thanks.

My father and I took the 9117 from Brussels to London, from check in to boarding the train, everything went smoothly and rather quickly. The train manager K.Vanderheyden and her brown headed collègue were really helpful and made a commercial gesture to us which we truly appreciated.

The Eurostar from Brussels to St Pancras has gone downhill. Long, chaotic security and passport control at Brussels Midi, an uncomfortable waiting area, and frequent delays make the journey stressful. Onboard, WiFi barely works, legroom is tight, and food is overpriced. UK border checks are painfully slow, and arrival at St Pancras is chaotic. For the price, it should be much better. Only take it if you have no other choice.

Again I made the mistake of booking a seat that had a meal provided. The quality of the breakfast was very poor, on my return journey I had the lunch which was also very bad. Next time I’ll book a cheaper seat and take a packed lunch.

Had a delayed train leaving Amsterdam, was going to arrive in Brussels with very little time to make connection to London , the staff on the delayed train were so good, no drama, just answer’s for our situation! Made train to London . Just a big thank you for outstanding service from everyone on the Amsterdam to Brussels train

Just like SNCF, very bad service. After explaining them as well about the missed train to Paris due to sudden local train interruptions that hindered to be on time at the station to catch the Eurostar train, they just simply referred me back to SNCF since they provided the train ticket. Once again a company that doesn't take responsibility, doesn't care about customer satisfaction, refusing to offer a refund or sort of compensation like maybe a voucher and therewith losing loyal customers. Not interested to use Eurostar service any longer, will keep travelling just via flights then.

The train journeys to and from Brussels were fine; on time, stff were pleasant.  Food on the Eurostar plus was just about OK.  Carriages were clean BUT the toilets on board  were foul.  The one near our carriage was blocked and had no running water. A second toilet had no water or soap.   Was quite  disgusting feeling, especially as this was quite soon after departure.
A disastrous delay that just kept getting longer. Awful service, I am extremely disappointed and we will miss our museum entrance because of this.

I'm traveling often to Paris and London. Reservation process and app, it's fine. It's working and you receive live info.Rates: way too much expensive vs airlines but ok you don't get the help of the government (sustainability...)Wi-Fi : terrible... guys you have a majority of Business men, do something 🙄

Travelled from St Pancras to Lille. On hearing that it was my birthday, Brahim and Esther who were working on the train, produced a bottle of champagne and a card wishing me a happy birthday. All the staff wished me a happy birthday, a lovely thing to do and very much appreciated

Unfortunately, I have to come back to my previous experience. Customer service does not do what is expected. A lot of gross mistakes are made and if you don't stay extremely sharp yourself, it will cost you dearly. Always check your points after the trip. Usually they are not added. Train has a lot of delays and this is also not picked up correctly. Worst of all, the train crew on board are not customer-friendly either. All in all lousy service.
Eurostar brought forward time of departure meaning I couldn't travel. They then refused to refund ticket or even exchange for a voucher. Total scam. Never travel with them!!!

We travelled to Amsterdam by Eurostar last week. We thought we would use the train rather than fly. The trip was not cheap and we had upgraded to Eurostar Plus. The journey out was fine. It was a direct train. The return trip was terrible. We had to catch a train from Amsterdam to Brussels. It was showing on time up until 5 minutes before departure, then a 30 minute delay, and then a few minutes later it showed the Eurostar wasn’t leaving from Amsterdam but Rotterdam. There was no explanation and no help whatsoever so ever from Eurostar! The App was showing the train leaving as normal. The next few hours were horrendous. We were given wrong advice from station staff and many people boarded an incorrect train. We managed to get on an overcrowded train to Rotterdam. The Eurostar connection was due to leave well before we arrived but it did wait for us. Likewise the connection in Brussels did wait despite the App saying it was leaving on time. A terrible and stressful experience. The response from Eurostar was dreadful. A bland response saying we are not entitled to any compensation as we were not delayed for over an hour. An expensive mistake.

Fantastic excellent journey. Brilliant. Salmon lunch&wine also Wi-Fi wasn't bad made passing the time easier, 🤩🤩🤩🤩🤩

My trip to Brussels got cancelled an hour before departure! I have booked  an overnight trip for my daughters  birthday! We were waiting four our train to St Pancras when I received a message from Eurostar cancelling our trip! Very disappointed and would avoid in the future

The train itself was on time, it works.However the staff on Eurostar are simply awful - they treat passengers with utter contempt.The food they serve on your plus ticket is not fit for human consumption, the breakfast on the London to Paris leg was stale bread and some weird yoghurt.

We booked 5 days and 4 nights at Disneyland Paris taking the Eurostar from London. We were meant to come back in the evening on the last day but received a message from Walt Disney Travel Company on the 3rd day of our trip to say Eurostar had cancelled our train and we would have to travel in the morning instead. We agreed as we didn't want to spend the last day trying to secure alternative transport. When I asked who should we contract for compensation (Disney or Eurostar) they said we wouldn't receive any and that this happened all the time.  We pretty much lost a full day in the park.

5 out of 5.This was my first trip in the leshuttle and we were not disappointed, fro arrival to departure the operation was smooth and quick. The staff appeared to be well trained and helpful. The trip seemed to be over in the blink of an eye. Before we knew it, we where heading for Boulogne-sur-Mer and our weekend of exploring French culture. Would recommend using this service.

Absolute rip off. Mistakenly booked ticket for the following day, and was charged a whole other £100 on top of the £100 I'd already paid. Train was delayed 30 mins, and train was half empty. I will never travel on Eurostar ever again, it's a shambles of a service, when you can fly for 1/4 of the price. Absolutely ridiculous.

This is our first experience of the Eurostar and we love it. We are travelling Eurostar Plus from Paris to London. It is comfortable and the staff are friendly and helpful. Will definitely travel this way again. (Oh and the food was great!)

The London-Paris trip was fine. The Paris-Amsterdam trip was not great. The train left Paris late, it travelled slowly due to bad weather and then another train broke down on the fast line requiring we take the slow line, causing yet more delays. The scheduled travel time compared reasonably to a plane. The actual journey time compared poorly.

We travelled from London (St Pancras) to Paris (Gare du Nord) on the high-speed Eurostar. It was a straightforward and fairly easy journey that took 3 hrs 15 min. If like us, you are already staying in London and planning to stay in Paris, then it is awfully convenient.I can see very mixed reviews below but we did not have any delays or issues.We travelled in their Standard class which was fine for a short trip. It doesn’t include a meal but our seats were comfortable enough. There was a small, drop-down table top and our seats reclined slightly (only very slightly). Some seats were set face-to-face around a table for four but most were like ours, in rows and facing the one way. Overall, we were quite comfortable.POSITIVES:- Airport like security (our bags went through an X-ray machine and we had to pass through a metal detector) but the lines are quicker and shorter and we didn’t have to take off belts or shoes.- St Pancras Station has a good range of shops and cafes. We were early so we were able to kill some time here- Option to get cheaper seats by booking early (we booked last minute which was not ideal)- Plenty of space to store luggage and still keep it within eyesight- Arrived on time- Arrived in the heart of Paris at the Gare du Nord, making it easy to transfer to the Metro line to get to our hotelNEGATIVES:- You are told to be there 60 - 90 minutes beforehand. We were there 90 min before and spent a lot of time waiting around- Don’t expect a scenic train ride - this is more about getting from A to B- Seating once you move inside the departure lounge is limited and the area was very crowded

Honestly this was a remarkable experience and it relates exclusively to the Premier class. My family and I on New Year’s Eve took the train from London to Paris. I spent considerably more for Premier but the money could not be better spent. Check in was a breeze. It took five minutes. I spent so much time standing London lines this was a very welcome respite. The lounge which you have access to was fine. They served free champagne and it was quiet. I am not a decorator but it could use some freshening up. (A little spackle, a little paint, a little rhinestone…stole that from The Birdcage)  Once on the train the seats are great, the food they served was honestly perhaps the best I had on the trip. The staff was wonderful. Highly…highly… recommend spending the money and book Premier.

We had a terrible experience with Eurostar Premier.  Do not waste your money.  I took my wife to Brussels for her birthday and decided to splurge on Eurostar Premier.  The trip over was good but not "premier" -- a roomy and comfortable Premier carriage with pretentious but passable food.  The return trip was abysmal!! The train was old, without a Premier carriage.  They put us in an aging and worn Eurostar Plus carriage that wasn't especially clean or comfortable.  They ran out of the food on the menu, so they gave my wife a leftover dish from Plus.  They gave me a re-heated, day-old (it seemed) dish that gave me food poisoning.  Thankfully, I had only eaten a bite or two so I was only sick for a couple days following.  We complained to the train manager, who took our details and suggested that we would receive compensation.  However, three weeks later and we haven't even received an apology.  The whole experience was truly awful, especially considering the cost.  The lounge experience in London was crowded, with very cheap "snacks".  The lounge in Brussels was better, but still had poor quality food as well.  One bright spot is that the train staff were pleasant and friendly -- although clearly embarrassed by the poor quality.

Beware scam for the award of Eurostar club points. You are made to shimmer the award of one point for every euro spent... Lying!!!! Points are awarded ONLY to the club member for travel only.I spent 460 euros (for a family trip, Christmas gift) and was credited with 98 points (the price of my seat).

Eurostar Amsterdam-Bruxelles. Train with continuous departure delay, 35 minutes late and on arrival the car crew started chatting with the ground staff. They have shown their rudeness to our complaints about delays. Avoid them like the plague.

We took the train to Paris at Saint Pancras station on Sunday, January 05 we passed around 07:00 by a horribly unkind lady (with an Eastern European accent and a square cut) just before the police, she was not a police officer but basically she chewed the work of the police who recontrols behind her! We paid premier price for our trip from Germany to Brussels and at the last leg of the journey, the train broke down and we were forced to take a local train which was already full. The company offered no compensation for the trip for more than 1 hour of time we lost lugging around our luggage and taking coach class on a slower train and it was one of the worst journeys we had during our trip.

Fast efficient service but improvements could be made. App tells you to check in at least 1.5 hrs before, but staff won’t let you in at that time. Waiting area is too small and not enough seats for everyone. Train as clean and comfortable. With plenty of room for hand luggage and hooks for coats by window.

I travelled from London to Amsterdam on 2nd January, 2025 (Train 9126).  From arriving at London St Pancras and alighting at Amsterdam Central I was delighted by my experience.All station and Eurostar train staff were fantastic. Given it’s a heavy travel period, everything was seamless.

Honestly far more trouble than an airport. Lines out onto the concourse. Slower processing than an airport, scanning your own large bags, rudest bag search staff I’ve ever encountered, business tickets equivalent to a full service airline. And that was skipping the line with business premier tickets. I used this frequently when it opened, but it’s been some years and I’ll never do it again.  It’s sad, but I think the wonderful idea of connecting the Two Cities is going the way of the Concorde.
Overcrowded waiting area every single time and the boarding control staff are consistently rude and obnoxious. Makes the whole experience tremendously unpleasant.

Travelled from London to Paris via Lille. Great service, was given assistance on both legs of the journey. The Eurostar from London was delayed only by 20 minutes which we were kept informed about. The assistance at Lille was ok, although this isn’t provided by Eurostar staff. The return journey was the same, helpful and friendly staff at Eurostar. Someone from Eurostar was waiting on our return to St Pancreas with a ramp.

We took the Eurostar from Amsterdam to Brussels. Fabulous ride - the seats were very comfortable with USB connections at every seat. Easy to board, easy to stow suitcases with plenty of room. Very fast journey. Quick tip - find out where your carriage will stop by asking a railway attendent and stand there to aid boarding. Highly recommended

The best  relaxing easy way to travel to Paris from London is the Eurostar high speed train  , about  two and half hours  smooth ride , if you are not in any traveling  budget best buy  the Eurostar Premier or Eurostar Plus , it worth every penny !  complimentary light snake  and drink sever at your seat ,  super spacious and comfortable seat , also free wi-fi  onboard , depart London on early train and coming back  from  Paris  on the last train , plenty time for one day visit in Paris , you can easily seen what a different Paris Day and Night atmosphere and action !   but plan your trip well !

Eurostar continues to massively under perform. On Standard premier class No wifi available this has been the same for last 5 round trips. Food served is freezing cold and in editable. Cold broccoli and cold pasta served with dry Tiny chocolate attempt at Brownie. This time carriage is clean at least But overall the quality of service and customer service is terrible . All since the merge with TGV.

Recieved an email the day before travel with generic information about luggage requirements and asking us to check if times had changed by a couple of minutes etc. When I got online I saw the train was cancelled and was given the option for a refund or to rebook at an extra €90 per person for a less convenient time.Thankfully, after many hours of researching alternative options to reach my destination, I rechecked the Eurostar website again and the more expensive seats had sold out and the seat type I had booked had become available (meaning no additional cost). Never recieved any direct communication from the company letting me know my train had been cancelled. All communication indicated that everything was still going ahead.Will never use Eurostar again.*Did recieve an email from Eurostar, after the train had left, mentioning that some trains had been cancelled due to track work. Unhelpful timing.

We travelled from Cologne to Paris in the 1. Great.The outbound journey was delayed by around an hour due to a detour caused by the construction site (there had been an accident between Horrem and Düren weeks earlier).On the return journey, the journey ended in Aachen, instead of Cologne.We should take the Regional Express trains in Aachen (DB), but the Eurostar tickets were not valid. Im on a Eurostar train from Köln to Paris as I write this.  What a wretched experience. The train is dramatically oversold and passengers are sitting on their luggage in the aisles. The cafe car is filled with unseated passengers so food service is suspended. Luggage is crammed and strewn everywhere. The train is delayed. The communication before boarding was terrible. We paid for first class seats and got a horrible trip with no amenities and people crammed in the aisle next to and on top of us.  Just awful.

We booked a ticket from Cologne through to London. The first Eurostar train was late. In Brussels, Eurostar refused to let us on the train. No more trains that day. No hotel vouchers. Women with young children left alone at 10pm to search for a hotel room. 😡

We had to leave Paris to Brussels on 20-12-2024, return on 22-12-2024, due to a serious health problem that occurred on 17-12-2024, we had to cancel this trip, but “Eurostar” does not refund tickets 7 days before the departure date, it offers for a fee, a change of date, now the dates chosen corresponded to an event, so we are not interested in another choice. Following this cancellation, given the holiday period, it is obvious that Eurostar will have sold our seats, so we would have been better off not cancelling them! On the other hand, their rates are extremely high!!! There should be urgent competition. Next time we'll go by car.

We booked well in advance for brussels and cost £70 return which was cheaper than flying at the time we looked. Like how you don’t have to pay for baggage (can tell we usually fly ryanair!). We just did standard class and had no problems. Super quick through security and passports which was great as it meant we didn’t have to get up as early. No problems getting a seat at either station just get there slightly earlier than the ticket says. Trains are nice. Worked well for us, would use again, easier than flying!

Absolutely ridiculous that they won’t stop at Ashford International they can afford it they just can’t be bothered what is the point of having a station there if it’s just going to sit empty it’s ridiculous you have to travel to London which is very expensive after you have paid over £100 for a ticket and then have to pay for a return to london

Despite booking in 1st, carriages were dirty, staff scruffy, and it is ridiculous that a passenger boarding  in Rotterdam cannot choose to have the meal after Brussels.  All in all, a waste of money for a supposed premium cabin.

We traveled as two couples by First Class on EuroStar to Brussels and must agree with the vast majority of reviews in that it is very poor.We booked First Class as a treat and it was a complete let down on the outward journey. The Breakfast consisted of half an egg roll, small yogurt type dessert and one cup of Coffee!  The toilets were dirty, the seats slightly better then Standard Class but nothing else to differentiate between the two.  The homeward journey was slightly better in so much that you got a very small meal and some wine but again dirty toilets, with hand facilities broken and the overall cleanliness of the train lacking. The prices in the buffet are expensive and not many were using the facility. Also booking First Class does not allow you to use the lounge at St Pancras and anyone who has used the service know that the waiting areas in any of the Terminal (ST Pancras, Brussels or Paris) are very, very basic and shabby.  Passport control (whilst nothing to do with Eurostar) in Brussels is very unprofessional with the officers checking your documents talking and chatting to their colleagues whilst big queues build up.In saying all that, for us, the service is the most convenient way in getting to the centre of some European Capitals so we might use again Soley for that reason and that reason alone.  However, we will not be travelling first class and will be eating before we get on the train!!!

Very bad service Trains dirty Very limited staff for the percentage of customers They actually don’t care as there are no competition I think This service is very badLateness,Humans being treated like cattle.There should be another operator so they can compete

I will never use Eurostar again! A thoroughly unpleasant experience. Once we had passed customs, we had to wait for an hour and a half, standing the whole time. There were very few seats to sit on and not much standing room either! The trip door to door took 5 and a half hours. It would have been quicker and cheaper to fly from Gatwick! Eurostar has no regard or consideration for its passengers. They need to open Ashford station again to spread the load!

everyone now read the recent survey (December 20234) about Eurostar being on a  number of levels the worst European rail company. This is not surprising since I for one. - along with lots of other customers - have provided years of feed back, some very detailed and not one has been improved upon.
