All right, the trip, but on time. He didn’t leave or arrive on schedule, there were some children kicking the seat and no one corrected them. The rest is fine. Nice trains and good service.

If catching the first trains of the day be warned they do not open the check in process the advised 90mins that you are requested to get there before hand, more like 60mins before!This leads to a very long queue, and it ends in typical British fashion! Either get there really early or might as well wait till near the 30 min gate closure once the queue has shortened. Once through check in and security there isn’t really much to do apart from wait patiently is a small area with a coffee and stationary shop.The journey was fine, leaving and arriving on time.

We used to enjoy Eurostar. Not any more. St. Pancras end is quite frankly dangerous. Hugely overcrowded with NO signed fire exits. Paris is a huge mess, full of staff shouting and herding you about like a load of cattle, not fee paying customers. This is getting as stressful as flying. Hopefully competition may force smug Eurostar to think about the paying customer again. Shame on you Eurostar CEO.
Thank you so much Nasser for your kind service on my 50th birthday yesterday on the 9.01 from St pancras xx I look forward to seeing you again 😀

We booked a two day break in Brussels commencing on  a Tuesday, we pre-booked 'plus' tickets for the outbound journey and 'Premium' on the return. The 0901 train was the best for us. The terminal was very busy, but not an issue. Border control and customs straightforward and simple. Boarding the train was straightforward, the seats were large. Reclining and comfortable. The small snack and non alcoholic drinks provided were adequate. The journey was very quick and smooth, staff helpful. Leaving the train was equally simple.The return 'Premium' journey (2051hrs) was certainly a level up and worth the extra cost. We found signage at Brussels Midi Station was lacking and could be improved. Booking in was excellent and no queuing. The premium lounge was a great way to relax after a long day shopping in Brussels, complimentary nibbles and drinks were lovely. The onboard experience was excellent, enhanced by exceptionally helpful staff in particular 'Stefan'. The cuisine provided was small but adequate and excellent in quality again complimented by alcoholic and non alcoholic drinks. We arrived on time and relaxed for the manic of late evning underground travel across London.My only reservation was concerning the initial booking. We had booked early, But I could not see anywhere showing a seating diagram to enable me to book particular seats, this would have enhanced the experience considerably. It may have been me just not noticing the particular 'window' in the booking process. All in all a lovely way to travel

Took the Eurostar to Amsterdam, delayed outside Brussels for 2 hours, somebody had been hit on the track, not Eurostars fault but as the internet connection was very poor made it a very long trip. On the return Journey first problem is you have to change trains, no through travel. Major problem was the train from Amsterdam was cancelled. We we informed by test with no guidance on what to do or who to contact. After a long wait on the phone I spoke to a rep. who rebookecd me on a train 2 hours after the original. We finally arrived in London 3.5 hours after we had expected. On top of this because we 'rebooked' they are saying no compensation. Would have been quicker and cheaper to fly, never again on Eurostar, being delayed one way is bad look, delays in both directions looks like standard practice.Very disappointed.

we booked plus seats (mid range) on St Pancras - Brussels train at last minute changed seating, so not sat together. The food was really poor. On the return journey we were supposed to have a choice of meal but they had ran out of the chicken meal so we had a "take or leave it" stilton bake. I left it and so did my wife but the children ate it and were both violently ill during the night. Really poor.

We decided to go to Brussels on Eurostar a something different. The journey on the train was very good but the faffing both on departures on both ends was disappointing. The organisation and delivery of the entry service was very poor and not a pleasant experience and spoilt the journey, one attendant saying one thing and further down being sent back because the other member of staff is not on the same page. The waiting area before you get on the train is very poor and far too small for the people waiting for their journey. The whole experience was poor by the way it’s managed rather than the actual journey. Would we do it again, it has its pluses and minuses. One more issue, on the return journey from Brussels at 7.30pm, the cafe had very little of its menu available. Eurostar, we booked many months prior to our journey and you confirmed the package. One week before the journey, you sent us an email saying our train had been cancelled and you booked us on a later train. Why when we got to the station the original train was still running, we were told it would cost 4 of us €300 to go back on the train we were originally booked on, more importantly, if we could have booked our original train, there were seats. Very poor consideration to your customers and will put us off to use you gain.

I would like to say a big thank you to Lauren your call handler for Eurostar.   I was struggling to book 7 seats for me and my family to travel with Eurostar to Disneyland.   I called Eurostar and Lauren was absolutely amazing.   Who would know that a 25 year old passenger would be deemed an adolescent on the French leg of the Eurostar journey!!   Lauren was so helpful and booked my outward and return journeys selecting the best possible seats for us so we could be close together.   We have just returned from the most amazing trip to Disney and our travel arrangements arranged by Lauren helped to make this possible.   Lauren is an absolute credit to your call handling team.

The Eurostar business class is unworthy. An overpriced ticket , a lunch worthy of a bad canteen and narrow seats where it is almost impossible to put a PC and a phone . A shame. Add a noisy environment because not allowed for the small fee of 350€!

“Train delayed due to a train arriving late”. Not a good enough reason for a delay. Insane queues, same as the airport. Unfriendly at the Paris end. Passport screened not once but twice. Absolutely treated like cattle. Overpriced especially considering the bad service.

Train from Brussels to Amsterdam via Rotterdam and Schiphol airport was rerouted to Utrecht and never got to Schiphol or Rotterdam. I got to Schiphol eventually 1.5hr late by taking a regular train from Utrecht to Schiphol. The ticket cost 89EUR and no refund is possible.

We booked a hotel package with Eurostar for Cologne. We thought this would protect us better if we had any issues. We were very wrong. First the train that Eurostar selected for us coming back included long delays at Brussels. Perhaps we should have realised this was due to regular delays!We were delayed going out, and needed to run through Brussels station (I use a walking stick). No Eurostar people available to speak to on the train or on the platform or to direct people to the right train.Coming back there was a network delay in Germany, we had an email with an offer to cancel, but as we were on the hotel package we could only cancel both Cologne to Brussels and Brussels to London at the same time. This could have left us stranded in Brussels if the second leg of the journey was no longer available.Email communication was poor and for some people in accurate.Had we booked the Hotel elsewhere and just the trains with Eurostar we would have had far more flexibility. Our tickets stated we could change up to an hour before the train but as it was a Hotel package, this was not trueCustomer Service were difficult to contact and unhelpful. The Brussels Eurostar team on the way back were so friendly and kind. Alone, they would get 5 stars for the care on our return.

St.P. is deep in London and getting there with luggage is pretty easy but unpleasant. Taxi is ok and expensive, underground is good value but challenging. Every cafe, shop etc at the station is expensive but those I experienced were good. But VFM though, not so sure.Thanks to delays and cancellations the departure area was packed and uncomfortable and lots of confusion when trains were ready for loading.On board the seat was firm and uncomfortable. The power supply tricky to access and the wi-fi pretty poor.Saw some staff walk past but didn't see any engagement with passengers. If you're in the cheap seats that aren't really cheap the refreshment carriages 8 & 9 are a long walk away so best to bring your own food and drink. Buy a discounted ticket, take your own refreshments, don't expect much customer service, even less WiFi and prepare for some sort of delay,They'll get you safely from London to Paris, Brussels etc in around 120 mins and that's good. Everything else is pushing towards being just ok.
Treated like cattle from London- Paris and return trip - where are the humans? - service absolutely 💩 💩 💩 Just out for profit 😞

Excellent service, easy to use, great trip. Daniel looked after us. He made us feel extremely well cared for. We have never used Eurostar before, but we were so glad we got the chance to cross the fhannel this way. Thank you, Daniel, and the others who worked with you and made our trip so enjoyable.

This was our first experience on Eurostar. To give us the best chance we went Eurostar Premier. It was a wonderful experience and totally worth it. Daniel attended to us on the train and did a fabulous job. Thanks to Daniel and your fellow staff - perfect service.

On the way to paris I had a great experience, Catalina Caplea went above and beyond to ensure she delivered a high standard of service, she was very accommodating and kind and made the journey to paris smooth and enjoyable however on the way back Eurostar messed up our tickets, we were with 2 elderly individuals and were forced to walk all the way to our correct seats with 5 luggage’s whilst the train was moving! And the food wasn’t that great 😬 you’re better off buying from their cafe! Other than that the journey was fast and efficient
Luggage stolen from the racks where ypu are OBLIGED to leave your luggage. Response from one of the EuroStar employees "this happens all the time". Disgraceful

In short, that such a company is allowed to exist in this present day and age is a miracle. Truly a disgusting company run by a horrible bunch of amateurish people. Humanity and dignity are certainly not in the job description here. Our journey began last December 27. Three nights of London was the plan. This time not by plane but by train anyway. The problems that this ultimately caused are laughable in retrospect, and that is why I am happy to name them. So hopefully you won't run into the same problems by bypassing this company. It already started the outward journey, there was apparently a platform change that we had not been informed of. Well, this can happen. Eventually at check-in there appeared to be too many passengers for the train set. So an expensive paid seat became a folding seat at the toilets. Well, not nice but it's no different. We then had a wonderful 3 days in London and everything went perfectly. The return was supposed to take place on the 30th, but due to the flooded tunnels, no train left that day. We were told this via a text message on the way to the station. The text message had a link where you could see further options. Of course that link was immediately out and of course no one could be reached by phone. A great drama of course at the station, but this is also partly force majeure. Yet you were not really kindly addressed by employees. To ask for further information I asked a gentleman from Eurostar “What are we supposed to do now?”, to which I got a meaningless smart-ass remark “yeah unfortunately trains can’t swim can they?”. Of course I understood that myself and eventually he babbled a bit. That replacement transport is reimbursed up to 150,- per person, hotel accommodation is reimbursed, expenses incurred are also reimbursed. This is another windfall. In the meantime, people were piling up at the station and we quickly booked a next flight home. The train was not an option, because you could only book it from January 2. We wanted to celebrate New Year's Eve at home. The next flight was a day later, so we booked a hotel stay near Gatwick Airport. This all went fine and we were still home a day later. That's when the real trouble started! A week later, I mapped out all the charges with statements and the like, and put them in a file. I could not go to the eurostar compensation site, because my booking number of the return trip was not recognized. That's very strange, of course. After some vague mail contact I still didn't get a response after 2 months. I was just ignored. So pissed off that this made me, I put a lawyer on it. And so true, we get a response 2 days after a registered letter from a lawyer. What a laughable state of affairs. Long story short, many promises were made and nothing was carried out. Over 9 months it took me to get my money back for a small part. We have incurred 1000,- extra costs and a small 250,- was paid to this. Count out your profits... Apart from the fact that it cost a lot of extra money, it's mainly about being completely ignored. They assume that the average person will not make that much effort or yet does not have the means to prove his right. And in part, they succeed.. Even if I have to take the pedalo to England next time, I would rather take it and spend one euro on this *company.

This company is a total rip off avoid like the plague, the policy is tell the customers they can cancel with a full refund up until the day before then when when the customer tries to change the date due to illness if the new date is cheaper there is no refund but if its more expensive the customer has to pay and so when the customer tries to cancel and rebook charge them £100 and when they say "but it says 100% refundable" laugh at them and say "thats just the hotel you fool you didnt read the terms and conditions ha ha " . I will never use them again.

A huge thank you to Akim from Eurostar who took care of me with great patience at the help desks before checking and understanding! Thanks to him I will definitely take back the Eurostar!! Can't find his last name, but if the firm recognizes the potential of its agents, I recommend it 200% Pauline

I had my luggage stolen on the Eurostar from Amsterdam to London and the company have informed me that they do not have cameras and ‘can’t watch luggage and passengers all the time’ STAY AWAY IF YOU WANT TO KEEP YOUR VALUABLE LUGGAGE SAFE THERE IS A VERH BIG ONGOING THEFT ISSUE

Eurostar needs to get its act together. The tickets are hugely overpriced. I was travelling Eurostar plus to Paris. Nowhere to sit at St Pancras. Appallingly crowded. I am 78. No help with anything. Eurostar employee at carriage would not help me with case. Food ok as long as you like cold lentils and humous.  But Gare du nord is a nightmare .  20 mins to get from train to exit on packed tiny platform. Taxis also nightmare. Huge queues and rude aggressive employees pushing us around while waiting for cab. Return journey at gare du nord was dreadful. Passport control crazy - only one gate working. Rude aggressive staff at security. Train 30 mins late. Had to stand for over an hour. Nowhere to sit. Coffee machines broken!! Like herding cattle. How is it that they have allotted such a small space for at least two full train loads of waiting passengers. It’s a disgrace. The elderly in the know ordered assistance. They obviously knew what awaited them.  Customer service doesn’t exist .  They should be ashamed and they are coining it in. Looking at their website today the fares are beyond belief.  They should have competition. How is it they have the contract. Needless to say I missed a connection at St Pancras.  I will do my utmost to avoid in the future.

I take the Eurostar four to five times a year and travel in Standard Premier now called Eurostar Plus. It’s quite punctual and the seats are  very comfortable. The food served is more like a big snack than a regular meal portion but it’s well presented.  The negative points for me are firstly not enough seats in St Pancras while waiting and secondly the staff categorically refusing to help with the suitcase to get in and out of the wagon. The big gap between the steps and the platform is tricky for some people and a little bit of help would be appreciated.

You are overcharging everyone, this is ridiculous. I care about the environment but I can't afford 400 pounds train ride to Paris from London whileist the airplain is 100. So much for you sustainability, well done, enjoy your profits............... Disgusting.

From queueing to get in at St Pancras, to the overcrowded waiting area, to being cattle herded through passport and security, this was a thoroughly unpleasant experience. The trains themselves were not bad and were on time . The coffee however was disgusting and the meals left little option for special dietary needs. On the return journey from Paris the queue meant that you were left in a dangerous situation at the top of the escalator, struggling with baggage to get off. As a frequent traveller on Eurotunnel, where passport and security are at least dignified (and I can take my dog), nothing would induce me to switch to Eurostar on a regular basis.
Apart from the lack of space in the St Pancras waiting area, this is a good service which is punctual and smooth with no problems on board.

A regular user of the euro star and euro tunnel.They was I looking at all the advantages of being an  Advantage Star member , looking at all the advantages you get with this . Looking at the web site ohh if I ever need to take an earlier train it’s fee of charge before an hour. Never had to but today ohh finish work and away I go . The waiting area in Kings X is awful. Far too small, overcrowded. There are people with children sitting on the floor for God's sake, Eurostar sort this out. The WiFi cannot support the number of people waiting either, Internet access is

On October 25, 2024, we would take the Eurostar from Amsterdam to Brussels and then to London. Shortly before departure, we were informed that the train was cancelled due to a technical incident. Communication was very poor. Forty minutes later we took a Eurostar arranged train from the NS to Brussels. There we arrived too late for our connection to London. At the Eurostar counter the last seats on a train rebooked three hours later. So three hours later in London. We are entitled to a refund of half the ticket price, after all, more than 2 hours late, but Eurostar does not respond. It's about €300 anyway.

Horrendous customer service. Awful.We accidentally got bigger class seats not understand the HUGE price difference. We called long before the trip to fix it and get our original seats and get the difference reimbursed and they said, "our system doesn't do that." YEAH RIGHT.Then we tried another option: let's just cancel and rebook. They said even if we rebook we will have to pay $240 to cancel. That cancellation fee is bafflingly ridiculous. Especially considering we just need to return back to the seats we had ALREADY bought. Do better, Eurostar.

Traveling between St. Pancras Station in London to the Gare du Nord in Paris, the Eurostar takes about two-and-a-half hours to make the journey. To be sure, travel by high-speed rail is more expensive than flying, but there is the compensation of not having to go to and from the airport—and then, having landed, from the airport into town (and, eventually, back to the airport). The trip is made even more enjoyable when booking a table for two in expectation of the invariably delicious lunch (we had the rolled chicken breast and mushrooms).

You can't rely on the reliability of Eurostar. Recent trip to Brussels, 20mins late on the way out just under an hour on the way back, so no compensation available, but missed connections at both ends.I've travelled on Eurostar since the 90's. When it used to be a pleasure to travel on it, and have seen it's decline over the years. At St Pancras there was an old lady who could not lift her suitcase onto the belt. She asked the security guy if he could help but he just turned away.  I did it for her at both ends of the belt. The security people just seemed more interested in barking at the passengers.The terminal at St Pancras it too small with too few seats, and you end up packed in like sardines. Brussels has much more room.The trains are ok, but the airline style seats are uncomfortably hard, unlike the older trains.This time I travelled on Standard Premier, and the staff seemed completely uninterested in their jobs and made sure they got off the train before the passengers.The comparison with the Belgian  trains was stark. Nice comfortable trains ( on time ) and friendly conductors, who seemed to enjoy what they were doing. Eurostar - where did it go wrong, or don't you care about your passengers anymore?

Travelled Lon to Paris, train was clean really friendly staff at both sides, comfortable in and arrived and departed on time!Food on the outbound was lovely! did not have it in bound - great way to travel and avoid airports especially the giddy prices at LHR.

The W.C stinks that I wanted to vomit! We are paying hundreds of euro, Eurostar should do something as the passengers deserve a pleasant experience with them. We are here right now (premium seat) and still feel dizzy from holding my breath from the toilet.

Eurostar staff and rules are abusive, I was traveling for the first time with my dog and didn't know that I had to get an aproval because I have a small dog, so no seat needed to be reserved, because my dog always sit at my feet in every train in the world...to do this you have to wait 24h, but if you call customer services they can help you sooner, but they won't...they don't help you with the information, they don't give you anything, just an email...so why wait 24h, if my dog passport was ok and I already had a ticket, wich it was on the 27th when I booked...but on the 28th, they said that the worm treatment is expired...how can a treatment that you give a dog once a month can expire? Do they talk to a vet before they made this rules? No one would help me, they even laught at me and made fun of me wich is not profesional at all. They only have 1 person in charge of the animal control in Paris and desn't even know the rules, he just googled them and told me that I couldn't travel...so I tryed to get my money back, but they said that I have a standard ticket, wich was expensive to begin with...so i wasn't able to travel, and they wouldn't refund my ticket and I think this is abusive ...they could at least refund some of my ticket, I payed 250 euros, not 40 euros...the tickets have different prices depending on the time and date...like you are purchasing a plane ticket...but in the train I think it shouldn't be these big differences. Don't chose eurostar to travel with your dog or cat, there are other rutes available.

Not used Eurostar before. And I will not use it again. The number of seats in the waiting areas is woefully small meaning people of all ages sitting on the floor. The staff, generally speaking, were incompetent and rude with a fair amount of shouting at customers going on. There was a very nice Frenchman at Gare du Nord who smiled and I shook his hand to thank him for his politeness and good customer service, as did the man behind me. Do the Directors and managers of Eurostar ever use this service themselves? I would guess not.

I took Eurostar from London St Pancras station to Paris Gare du Nord station.I booked seats 13, 14 and 18. It has a shared table. Seats 13 and 14 face the forward direction when the train departs from London to Paris while Seat 18 faces the opposite direction to the travelling train which may be an issue for a passenger with motion sickness.

Having spent a hectic week in London, the Duchess and I took the Eurostar to  Paris. We were staying a short 15 minute taxi ride from St Pancras station so did not have to trek out to Heathrow - nor did we have to be there 2 1/2 hours before departure - just 1 hour.  We booked tickets in Standard Premium - about 40 Euros dearer than Standard - and paid a touch more than airfares - but we enjoyed a very comfortable, spacious and relaxing journey of 2 hours and 15 minutes.  The seats were extra spacious with a reading lamp and plenty of sockets to re-charge our devices.     The check-in at St Pancras station in London was painless with little waiting time as passengers moved quickly through security (very light by airport standards0 and then French passport control.   However the pre-boarding gate holding area was very packed and we were only able to get a seat when the earlier train to Brussels was called.  The small duty free shop was well stocked. - only complaint was that hey didn't take cash so we couldn't spend the last of our Stirling!  On board we were greeted by a very pleasant staff member who explained where to stow our bags and directed us to our seats.  A complimentary breakfast of juice, pastry, fresh fruit & yoghurt was served with tea/coffee as required.  Our train arrived right on schedule into Gare du Nord in central Paris so we were not faced with the hassle of getting transport in from CDG airport.  The Eurostar train is an incredibly quick and convenient way to get to mainland Europe from London. For us more convenient than flying.

Travel very fast and comfortable. The train leaves at the exact time and arrives in the centre of London, right in front of a subway station, which makes the journey to other places much easier. If you have a foreign passport, prepare to catch a queue to pass on immigration in Paris. It's good to arrive two and a half hours in advance. The queue goes very slow on immigration. Remember that your clock will be one hour late from Paris.
The service is horrible.  The tone used is unacceptable.  You get half-screamed at by people. And yet I took a first-class ticket to have a proper and polite service.
Train cancelled We had to travel standing on the next overcrowded train and when you request the refund online the site replies that your file is not admissible!

Travelled recently from St Pancras to Munich for Oktoberfest. Security and border checks were efficiently run, a bit busy in the departure area but we found somewhere to sit.Journeys to and from Paris on time, no complaints.
Speedy journey but you have to wait for ages in a lounge with only half the needed number of seats. Even EasyJet treat people better! Avoid.

We caught the Eurostar from Paris to London . We had to be there an hour earlier as we had to go through customs at the Paris train station . We only booked a standard ticket and it was a very comfortable trip . Plenty of room for our cases in the carriage near the entrance,free wifi and charging plugs in the seats . We have been on a few Eurostar trains on our trip through Europe and would definitely recommend this for travel . We travelled under the sea but it was so quick we hardly realised .

I have been a loyal Eurostar customer for years, but their recent handling of the loyalty program and customer service is nothing short of a disaster. Despite traveling with them 14 times a year, I’ve consistently had issues with missing status points. This isn't a minor oversight – I’ve been downgraded in status because Eurostar can't manage their own system properly, and they make it nearly impossible to resolve. Being downgraded after choosing them repeatedly, despite the fact they are easily three times more expensive than other options, is a complete disgrace.To make matters worse, the overall service has severely deteriorated. Stations are overcrowded, communication is nonexistent, and delays are frequent. The customer service team is clearly overwhelmed, unresponsive, and unable to offer any solutions.For a company that prides itself on being a premium travel option, Eurostar is failing on every level. If you value your time, your money, and expect even a shred of respect for your loyalty, I strongly urge you to consider other options. Eurostar has proven that they don’t care about regular customers, and I won’t be wasting my time with a company that treats their most frequent travelers so poorly.

Eurostar delayed by 1 hour at Check-out on the way, one of the cars, obviously ours, door blocked, forced to pass through the next car!!!Return train, deleted .... revalidation on another train, which ruined our program of the day in London!!! in St Pancras station, deplorable organization. the cars and seats allocated during the revalidation, changed during the control!!! because last minute change of train. Really experience from the most execrable .... Bravo EUROSTAR!!!!!

St Pancras International is quite a nice station, good shopping and food options, but the processing area for entry to the Eurostar does leave a lot to be desired. Long queues, limited seating, very crowded. We had no issue with the immigration check, that was smooth enough. The next issue is finding space on the train for your luggage, but that was OK. After that, it was just a relaxing trip on a normal high-speed train, with views of pretty French villages along the way. Food options on the train were pretty limited.

We have travelled with Eurostar several times, I think ive left a review before years ago..Our last trip was a week ago to Paris. UK side, pretty straight forward, usual passport control etc..lots of people waiting for the train though and no available seats we could find, or if there were , one add one between poeple..anyway, no problem for us, might be for others..Train, still the old trains, same lay out , same seats etc..I don't know if there are any new ones, but Ive not noticed any. The return, more hassle on the French side, seems to take ages to go through customs, chaotic for baggage check, queues and queues to grab food and drinks, otherwise, train ride as expected..means of getting from one place to another..find it easier than flying to Paris

After been a regular ‘commuter’ for approximately 20 years using the service every 3rd WE & spending £1500 a year, I have now been ‘demoted’ from Carte Blanche to Avantage.Since Eurostar have changed their tier system a year ago it has made it very difficult & unfair to stay in the same tier; as a result I urge all regular ‘commuter’ customers to boycott their service until they review their loyalty program; I shall from now on use VUELING airways to travel between London & Paris; it’s also costing me less to fly & to get to the airport than it was to the station.

Eurostar does not get enough hate. It is absolutely the worst train company operating in Europe. Things always go wrong and they are never prepared. People miss their transfers, late for meetings, exhausted by the wait and uncertainty.It doesn’t stop there. It is also expensive, poor at communicating with customers, has little to no food options and serves dirt water instead of coffee.

The set up at St Pancras is diabolical, entering the book in and bag check we were “ barked” at by one of the female staff, not a customer orientated individual by any stretch of the imagination. If the job is affecting you so badly, get another one ! Passenger seating in the lounge is woefully inadequate, given the prices the large amount of passengers pay this is very shoddy service.
