Not a great experience but it got the job done and on time.

Eurostar has the right to be 20 min late with no dommage reimbursement for the client. On the other side, when client is late 10 min before doors closing he is charged 100€ for 2 seats. Quite of a non sense and disrespectful for the client.

Boarder control is a complete chaos at Gare du Nord. For the forth time this month I travelled in Business Premier class. There is priority line until the French  larder control and then regardless of your trace class there is just one massive inefficient lane for British passport control. Staff shout at people. There is no space . Luggage screening is never fully manned and created massive delays with staff moving at the slowest possible pace. Nobody supervise the process. If you manage to make it to the lounge some rude staff in addition to your ticket ask you to show your Eurostar account ?! Only god knows why. And finally when boarding (the lounge is located at the opposite end from the business premier coaches) another rude member of staff ask for your name . The service seems to deteriorate even further every time I use Eurostar. Last but not least, don’t even ask for more coffee after they served it! The staff is busy doing nothing and bidding in the kitchen.

We have used Eurostar since it started 30 years ago. After the arduous rail and ferry travel if the 70s and 80s, it was a welcome - and efficient - change.Unfortunately it's turned into a monster. The check in facilities at both la Gare du Nord & St Pancras are completely inadequate as are the Border Controls. I've never understood why these people need to shout at travellers.Leaving boarding til only minutes before the train is okay for the strongest and youngest passengers but the weaker and older people find the rugby scrum impossible.Eurostar definitely need to limit the amount of luggage that passengers are allowed to take on as some people are taking multiple huge cases which they cannot carry.The ladies toilet at la Gare du Nord this morning was in a disgraceful state. No water, toilet rolls, soap. Rubbish all over the floor and poo on the floor of the toilets.The great Eurostar experience of 30 years ago is most definitely at an end.I don't suppose management care - they know people are still going to use their cattle truck.

Recently used EuroStar for a return journey between Paris and London. Have done this journey several times over the years but this was the first time since Brexit. Overall, not particularly memorable rail trips, similar to memory of using EuroStar in the past. Booking ticket online was fairly simple and standard. Check-in at Gare du Nord was somewhat chaotic. Hall B doesn't seem to have enough space for immigration/customs check-in and waiting area for outbound journeys. Check-in at St. Pancras was fine, managed better. Journeys were just fine, nothing particularly interesting in either direction. Would be fine to use EuroStar again in the future for trips between Paris and London. Note: Free internet on Eurostar. It was very slow and unstable in both directions. Best to use your own data plan if you need internet access during the 2.5 hour train trip.

Terrible experience and non-existent customer service. I got to St Pancras on time and was told my train would now only go to Brussels, not Amsterdam which I had paid for. I had non-refundable accommodation in Amsterdam and had minutes to make a decision. The Eurostaff staff assured me there would be lots of local trains and coaches going to Amsterdam from Brussels and I could send them the bill. When I got to Brussels the train manager informed me there was no way I could get to Amsterdam that evening. He said he would book me accommodation and to wait at the station for my reservation. I waited hours in the cold and wet and nothing came through. I looked for someone at Eurostar to help me but they just said it was nothing to do with them!!!!!!!!!! At midnight I got robbed as Brussels Midi station is full of pickpockets and bag snatchers. I was now stuck on my own in a foreign country at midnight with no passport, no luggage, no tickets and no phone charger. Eurostar hasn't offered a penny in compensation or refunded my fare which was for Amsterdam, not Brussels. Yes, when things go to plan, I'm sure everything is wonderful but when things go wrong, Eurostar won't help in any way. Will always fly in future and I strongly advise everyone to do likewise.

I have been a Eurostar customer for quite a long time, generally I am happy that they are there to offer an alternative to airlines and ferries and I did not think I would give a bad review. However, I do not think they are in anyway loyal to customers and in my and my friends position they were profiteering from our situation. We arrived late at Gare du Nord for a return to the UK due to late arrival by an SNCF train. Bear in mind that SNCF owns 55%+ of Eurostar. We had to pay again and were charged full fare for the return. Not only that but Eurostar then would not credit this trip on my customer account.  So ok, this is also how the airlines behave but it does show that there needs to be competition for Eurostar and their monopoly is making them arrogant.  Our group has decided not to travel with Eurostar for the same trip in 2025 as we are flying instead.
Had a lovely trip to and from Amsterdam. Very comfortable, great food, lovely staff. Would definitely do again. So less stressful than flying. Very good experience

Decided to upgrade at the Eurostar station and it was definitely a great idea. Really makes the two hour train ride way more enjoyable. With table service and upgraded seats the time just flew by at 160mph. The food was great and having a glass or two of wine really made for a luxurious little treat.

Clean train on time. But on the other hand very poor handling customs passport control. On the chain, the staff shouts as if we were on military manoeuvre, staff can smile. Were cold all the way hooded on a train and scarf it begs question...

First time using Eurostar. £1100 for 2 business premier seats. Return journey awful. Ripped headrests. Slack drink service, worn, tatty carpets. Broken crockery. I think I’ll stick to flying in future, this was unacceptable and embarrassing to be honest . Lounges offer a few crisps and drinks, absolutely nothing worth paying for.

Very unpleasant surprise 7 days before my Check-out when I ask for a refund of my tickets. The agent informs me that they are no longer refundable although indicated as “Refundable with a €25/£25/$40 fee per person/trip up to 7 days prior to Check-out. “ I am therefore asking to change my ticket to another destination, as “Tickets are exchangeable free of charge up to 1 hour before the original Check-out Time. If your new ticket is more expensive, you must pay the difference.”  I am told that it is not possible to change destination.This refund and exchange policy is a fraud.

Told to come back in 30 mins because too early. Came back in 30 mins and waited 1.5hrs in queue. Pushed to next train. Downgraded and not told so no food. Next train also an hour late. Nobody in sight to help. No apologies, no explanation Total sh*t
They say there’s free wifi. Well, there’s NONE. You cant even listen to a podcast or song. For the rest: no food. The fridge was broken… 🤔 Only chips and chocolade. I would recommend flying.

I'm beyond furious right now. I'm currently in the Business Lounge at Eurostar departures, a so-called "privilege" I've only received due to the absolutely terrible experience caused by the staff at St Pancras Euroatar. I missed my train to Lille because an employee, who clearly didn't know what they were talking about, told me to come back in an hour. Trusting their advice, I returned only to find the gates closed and my train gone.I had arrived 90 minutes early at the Eurostar terminal, only to be misled by their staff. Their incompetence has cost me my train. After standing there in disbelief and discussing the situation with the Departures Manager, I was told I was being "aggressive," and that she could prevent me from traveling. Since when did showing emotion become “aggressive”?After a long and stressful wait of about 45 minutes, I finally spoke with the station manager, Stefan, who, to his credit, expedited my passage through passport control, customs, and security in just 10 minutes. He even upgraded me to Business Class just to calm me down. I am incredibly upset; I had meticulously planned this trip to spend time with my husband, who is serving abroad in the Army. This situation has robbed me of precious moments with him, and I am utterly disgusted and enraged.
The air conditioning in the eurostar is so low that I think it's better outside... I think I'm gonna be sick because of this trip! Wifi is also to be reviewed...

I was lucky enough to take the Eurostar from Paris (Gare du Nord) to London and Rotterdam. Both Trips went well. Please Rating that to go to London there is a customs and security check in both directions. In the case of Rotterdam, there are no customs and security controls. In London, Eurostar enters St Pancras station. In Rotterdam, Eurostar enters Rotterdam Central station. It then continues on to Amsterdam. Please note that to get out of Rotterdam Station you only need to scan your train ticket. There's a snack car for food.

I am trying to consider my travel emissions so decided to travel from Rotterdam to London return. The entire experience was dreadful, truly dreadful. 1) Even if you have mobile phone data, the reception is up and down, so it is impossible  to work. Eurostar may have wifi, but it does not work at all.2) I was delayed both on the way there and back.3) The train varies from going 10km per hour to over 300km per hour, it drives you insane to be going fast, slow, fast slow, fast...4) The Eurostar Terminal in London is the most depressing place to travel from EVER. It is over-crowded, with people sitting on the floor, most people are standing and the staff does nothing to address the travellers that occupy more than one chair (one chair for them, one for their bag). The check-in time and process is so long, you may as well fly from London City to Rotterdam or just not travel.5) The staff are insanely rude and unkind.6) The seats are cramped.The tickets are more expensive than flying SO SORT YOURSELVES OUT EUROSTAR!!! It is actually inhumane to allow such a service.

Journey from France to England was disappointing. The train staff when getting on the train were rude causing my child to be upset. Once on the train was on a carriage that had no air conditioning while the train was hot and reduced breathing quality. One of the train staff offered some water, which was helpful. The staff told us we were able to get compensation under their policies and procedures. However customers services have refused to acknowledge what happened and refused to give any compensation.

Worst train experience you could possibly have… The train was 30 minutes late, however actually pulled up after just 20 minutes without warning or further updates. The train was fully overcrowded, leaving around 30 people to stand in our carriage and limiting the space for luggage. The wifi was off, not possible to connect at any time! (WiFi is included in the ticket price and should be an available). Board Restaurant could not be reached due to overcrowding, and then the train stopped for 20 minutes in the middle of a random tunnel… Overall everything you can do wrong they managed to do it wrong 😵‍💫 impressive

The trains are getting a bit dilapidated but it's still more convenient than air.Seats nowhere near as comfortable as French or Italian high speed trains and Eurostar has the slowest WiFi ( almost impossible to open a web site ) in Europe.Avoid if you can't live without WiFi for a couple of hours but otherwise OK

I was very disappointed with the Eurostar especially for the price. The seats are so uncomfortable. They have no cushion at all. The footrest is way too small. The boarding process was a nightmare. There simply ain’t enough room for everyone and the staff was very curt. I would not ride again. I rode from London to Brussels in the standard seat.

Disgusting dirty train from Brussels to Amsterdam Broke down half way Overcrowded limited air conditioning Do not travel with this company if you don’t have toPoor communication with stranded passengers A shocking experience!

London St Pancras to Brussells return- dissappointing experience, staff unhelpful (apart from lady in restaurant on return), not able to access any refreshments in the departure lounge, taps in train toilets not working, train poorly cleaned, internet does not work on board, very poor as on the continent trains are well connected. However plus point is trains ran to time on both journies, avoids chaos of flying, quick and easy way to get to the continent.Brussells to Cologne- very pleasant experience, and refreshingly efficient after my poor experience coming through the tunnel.

What a very civilised way to travel!  None of the hustle and bustle of an airport; Eurostar is much more relaxed.  Great trains, roomy seats with plenty of legroom, comfortable and fast.  We will defintely use it again.

Our first time using Eurostar, my wife and I took the train from St Pancras to Paris.. Getting through check in was not too bad, quite quick to get through passport control, but then the horror began. Felt like penned in cattle. The departures area is just too small with narrow walkways to navigate between seating completely packed with people and suitcases. It was so busy, hectic and claustrophobic, with no empty seats in the waiting area.  We stood for ages waiting, until finally some seats were vacated in the small cafe area, which we desperately charged for, but then had to purchase overpriced beverages from the cafe to remain sitting there. And then 20 minutes before our departure time the boarding was announced. Oh my god. The maniacal surge of people was horrendous, it was like the end of the world had just been announced. I think it's due in part to the boarding gate not being advised until just 20 mins to departure, with the majority assuming they may miss the train what with so little time left. So we joined this crazy frantic human exodus toward the boarding gate (narrow escalator to the platform) like a crazed herd of cattle. Where we boarded our carriage. We were in the cheap seats, the term 'cattle class' seemed so appropriate to how we were feeling by now. Cramped seating, hard and uncomfortable, and very little legroom for a tall person. It was as bad as being on a really bad bus or airplane.  Then, about an hour into the journey I had to put my coat on as it got so cold, and I mean really cold. Was glad to get off when we arrived in Paris. The station experience at Gare du Nord  was a bit better on the return. But again, the train got really cold after about an hour in. So in all, we didn't enjoy Eurostar, I expected so much better, we will not be doing it again.. Shame.

Great service, very quick and easy way to travel to France. The journey to Lille and back was comfortable and the staff at the station and on the train were very helpful and friendly. There was none of the hassle and stress that are at airports.
This review only concerns security screening staff who are unpleasant and aggressive! We were three cats but they stressed as if we were a thousand when we were more and more early. Nul!!!
Almost perfect, a super powerful air conditioner, the best way to catch a cold, a real duck cold. And global warming???
Perfect trip. Train on time. Clean. On time I'll be back from London to Paris. Recommended

Eurostar has nothing to do with Thalys!!! -Suck!Constant delays without any communication, comfort that is diminished, more opportunity to choose one's seat (and thus travel with a person who buys his ticket himself), more access to the waiting room (unless it is "premium"). Bref..Awards that went up for less service. And when the train is one hour late, we must be able to claim a refund. My train was over an hour late. And... his app to claim: no, not 60 minutes late. Liars!!!Little consideration for travelers...
The train was ok. The boarding arrangements are informed by the worst airport practice with people having to rush onto trains on a very tight timescale. This service could be improved.

Took Eurostar from London to Paris and highly recommend obtaining premier standard tickets.  It was non stop, food was great, beverages provided as well and service was great.Additionally days later took Eurostar to Amsterdam and had the same experience.  Easy transition with no issues on customs, passports or luggage checks.  Go Eurostar instead of airport transfers!!

Enjoyed trip as well settled, snack, friendly and available staff, tranquility preserved. Little tip: in Paris, we were able to take the front train thanks to the boarding staff. Downside: a lot of people in the waiting room.

What a great experience especially the return journey. We were upgraded to first class by a very lovely eurostar employee called Reddah, we were travelling from Paris back to London and he upgraded us for free. Lovely experience in first class, something that me and my partner could only dream of. Made our little holiday all the more enjoyable. Thanks Reddah! Top man!

The customer service on Eurostar rt between Paris and Brussels was awful and I won't provide any positive feedback. Our train travel had been delayed by an awful incident on another train line; but, what we faced on Eurostar, by its staff, bc of those delays left us with a profoundly negative opinion. I will not be using this train line again.

Excellent customer service, especially from my assisted travel assistant Marie who was pleasant and very helpful.I would def recommend assisted travel with Eutostar if you have any mobility issues.Thank you Marie for all your help, a credit to Eurostar

The London station needs a complete overhaul. The long queues created upon arrival are due to the lack of space in the boarding area, never mind having enough seats, particularly as the demographics using the Eurostar are elderly and with luggage. The whole experience is a hassle and stressful and boarding is so close to the departure time people stumble and run to the platform creating safety hazards. Vis a vis flying it is NOT a pleasant experience.
Just got the train from St Pancras to BrusselsPremium economyCheck in and passport process not badNot much space in departuresTrain trip and service was great Very smoothFriendly staff
Terrible. Booked special assistance and left to fend for ourselves. Two types of train. One is reasonably comfortable in standard class the other is awful . We suffered terrible pain when we arrived.

Just tried to get a refund form Eurostar for my train to Brussels  that was cancelled. They said that as I still GOT to Brussels they are non giving me ANY refund. Yes, I did get to Brussels, but I had to change 3 trains (with my luggage obviously), in one we had to stand because it was full of eurostar clients and there were no free seats. Instead of 2 hours the trip took me about 5. I had to leave Amsterdam in a rush cancelling all my plans for the day (it was my kids first trip to Amsterdam, thank you Eurostar for not letting them see the city!!)I bought eurostar tickets because it was direct and it was fast. I got nither and they tell me it's ok. I paid for their service that was cancelled and they think that if I somehow made it to Brussels they don't owe me anything. I think they owe me a refund and even a compensation for my trip beiyng ruined by their unexisting service (all other trains were NOT cancelled). "We hate to let you down" is written on their website, but it's exactly what they do!

Due to various circumstances we missed the train from St. Pancras to Amsterdam, but the staff were extremely helpful in reorganising our trip. They were so reassuring that they alleviated our anxiety, and were able to provide a relaxing journey.

Chris from Eurostar St Pancras gave above and beyond customer service to me in my hour of need. I’d promised to buy English newspapers for a friend living in France but having made rapid progress through check in and security, I quickly realised that newspapers are not available to buy first thing on a Saturday in the Duty Free Shop or the Business Premier lounge (weekdays only for some strange reason). So I tracked down Chris - supremely helpful and charming Customer Services Lead. He very kindly went back to the main St Pancras concourse bought the papers and then rushed to catch me in Coach 11 minutes before our train to Paris departed. Unbelievable. Brilliant. Restored my faith in humanity. Thank you.

Worst train experience ever despite the high price we paid for our tickets. The seat assignments for half of the passengers in our car was changed at the last minute. All passengers with paper copies were confused and uncooperative. The staff on the train was very slow to get things sorted out.

Extremely poor service for our return journey at Amsterdam station. No Eurostar staff at all to help and total confusion when the train arrived. Train staff shouting at passengers and we were unable to board because we couldn't get near the train.Absolutely disgusting!

Terrible and impersonal company deal with.For a month I have been trying to arrange to travel to Brussels with bicycles. Their booking system is a joke and they ignore requests for help. The baggage people cannot be spoken until 48 hours before travel (they are clearly working very hard doing anything but dealing with customers. You can't book a bike until you have booked a ticket and I do not want to book a ticket unless I can take a bike. This problem is too complex for them to deal with. Explore any other option if you can.

Travelling from Paris our train left with a fault and our journey was more than doubled.We travelled more than eight hours including the customs etc.Our ten yr old daughter by London was exhausted, it was late and we decided to stay in a hotel as another train after ten ay night was out of the question. We got 50% compensation for the train and non for the hotel.More than 3 hours later should be fully compensated at least for the ticket as in the UK. We had already travelled to Paris that day.
Nice trains, completely pathetic customer service and website. The site sucks, it technically doesn't work. Options for contact are limited. What a mess

Paid for first class premium tickets from Amsterdam to Paris. Food was finished before the server got to the middle of the cabin, we only had 1 option of vegetarian dish which tasted awful. Maybe a bit better planning especially if you're charging the customers premium prices?

The staff are so friendly and helpful as my husband uses a wheelchair for long distances. Even though our suitcase was over the limit they helped us get the suitcase on to the train,got the ramp out for my husband. The food was amazing and so choices in the business Premier lounge.

The train journey itself was a good experience in standard premier, but the terminal in St Pancras is far too small and there were no seats even when turning up and hour and half early. The seating and terminal really needs to be expanded as it was far too crowded and getting a coffee in pret was chaos

This was my first time travelling on Eurostar. My journey from London to Brussels was very underwhelming. The staff at St Pancras Station were quite surly as they herded us through to the overcrowded waiting area, which had insufficient seats. You had to stand around in the crowded waiting area for over 40 minutes before boarding your train.My return journey from Brussels was a very different experience. The staff were friendly, and there was sufficient seating for everyone.The actual train journey there and back was enjoyable. Would I travel on the Eurostar again? Absolutely yes!

First time Eurostar user; we travelled round trip between St Pancras and Gare du Nord.  Both trains ran on time; it was a smooth, quiet, comfortable ride -- a most convenient way to get from the heart of London to the heart of Paris without the hassle of flying. We had standard premier tickets, which provided some extra leg room and a meal.  There were enjoyable views of France's countryside along the way making the trip most enjoyable.We changed our return date after the initial booking; changing tickets was hassle free on the Eurostar website, although the ticket price increased since the time of the original booking, which is to be expected.Apart from the train, both London and Paris stations were overcrowded with a lack of seating -- we ended up standing or sitting on our luggage while waiting.  The passport and security checks went quickly and easily.  There was no need to arrive any earlier than what's indicated on the ticket.Overall, much easier than flying and we would definitely ride the Eurostar again.

Two trips, two long delays in two terrible waiting areas. Honestly rather be sitting in the train, even if it doesn’t move. The journey is fine, the trains are pleasant, but PLEASE Eurostar have a word with your terminals. The waiting areas are absolutely awful, with nowhere near enough seating. It costs next to nothing to make your passengers comfortable, Of course, get your delays sorted, but also fix your waiting areas at St Pancras and Gare du Nord.
No surprising most reviews of Eurostar are terrible. It's just beyond words in terms of shockingly bad customer service. Staff at Brussels Midi are useless.

I called Eurostar customer service in an absolute panic when our train to Paris was cancelled just hours before we were due to leave. We had been looking forward to this trip for the entire year to go and watch one of our dearest friends compete in the Paralympics (the one and only time he would be competing) and we were packed and ready to go when we received the cancellation alert. I immediately tried to rebook our tickets and was unable to find space on any alternative option that would get us to our friend's race on time, it was too late to get a refund for our accommodation and any viable flights were too expensive. I called Eurostar customer service and had a lovely lady named Karen try to help me find a solution. She was very attentive and sympathetic to our situation, but we seemed to be hitting dead ends. My partner and I had just about given up hope when I got a call back from Karen, who had taken it upon herself to go above and beyond to help us. She managed to escalate our case and get us on a train that put us on an even better position that we'd been in with our original booking. You absolutely saved the day and 2 Eurostar customers, Karen, we are so grateful!Give the woman a raise!

First time on Eurostar and not a good experience. Outward journey ok and St Pancras was fairly seamless and reasonably well organised. Train windows were dirty both ways making it difficult to see out. Catering is overpriced and poor quality. Terminal at Brussels Midi is disgusting. Cramped conditions , little seating  dirty choked toilets, one small info screen and limited catering facilities. Very disappointing for a so called premium service. Trains did run on time.

My husband and I travelled Eurostar from Paris to London in Business Premier.The ease and convenience from our hotel took the hassle away from going out to the airport.Chilled out in the lounge prior to the train departure and enjoyed coffee and some juice. There were also pastries on offer and cheeses.Although the train departed a few minutes late, it  made up some time and we arrived London close to schedule.The food and champagne onboard was sufficient for a two hour journey.Definitely recommend for an easy commute between the two cities.

Waiting here at Gare du Nord which, like St Pancras, is badly designed, ugly and cramped. This might not be a problem, except I noticed that the first two trains left late and the train I am on is now 40 minutes delayed. So...we built this phenomenally expensive tunnel so that trains could run at a very leisurely pace between London and Paris, and then, presumably because that isn't pitiful enough, Eurostar regularly delay their trains, which should run like clockwork. (Apparently a technical problem. Likely the "engineer" couldn't find his monkey wrench or some such nonsense.) It is always far more expensive (often considerably so) than flying, the trains are dirty and the seats uncomfortable. There are limited travelators in the station so the queue for the lift was 50 plus people long. Of course the lift only carries a couple of people with their suitcases. People always say "it's quicker / more direct", but you have to turn up 45 minutes in advance in any case (so that you can wait EVEN longer for your delayed train), so it's questionable whether this is quicker. All in all an unpleasant experience, but there is a captive audience, so Eurostar can afford to be lazy, complacent and incompetent.

90 minutes late leaving London. Almost an hour's delay at Lille waiting for a Belgian driver. So late at Brussels that we had to get a train 2 hours later than planned; hence no reserved seats. Chaos. Once in Frankfurt it was too late to eat. What a way to run a railway!

The staff were lovely, especially the French gals in Standard Premier on Aug 17th.  Food delicious, seats pretty comfy, very easy to navigate.  I highly recommend.If i could suggest an improvement, it would be to have an onboard "where is the train right now".  it would have been nice to know what cute town we were passing through.  There were so many times I wondered what cute little church steeple that was, in what town, and how old the buildings were.  Or what was xyzed farm was called.

This was our second trip using the Eurostar to get to Disneyland Paris and as such, we decided to go via Lille Europe instead as people had recommended it to be better and more calm than that of the Paris Gare du Nord. As expected the train was on time to arrive and leave St. Pancras international. It was the normal rush by all to the train and then trying to find our carriage and then seat. The journey is smooth and in essence, quick!One thing that we did notice as Brits, is that via Lille, there seemed to be more British families onboard than of the Gare du Nord train. This was helpful and more reassuring as it meant that we could all help each other and had the same goal without any potential language barrier issues., especially on the way home.We will be going this same route in the future, however, although, it is great to book the whole trip with Eurostar and have their protection of finding another train should your first one of the route be delayed, I wasn’t keen on the lack of time to arrive back in Lille on the SNCF train and get over to Hall 4 for the Eurostar without running like idiots! We also just had enough time to do the SkipTax refund before the train home started boarding. Therefore, the home journey, I would probably book separately to increase the time between the two trains to ease my anxiety!

Travelling on Eurostar was the best choice our family made for our summertime get away. From the moment we arrived at St Pancras the staff members ensured that we had the best, and more importantly stress free, journey. The whole journey from leaving our hotel in London to stepping out of Brussels-Midi railway station took 3.5 hours. In the past, going by plane this same journey has taken over 5 hours. Arriving at St Pancras for the 7.04 Eurostar train to Brussels we were immediately directed to a wider gate so that the whole family could proceed through to passport control without any delay and we made it through check-in/passport control within ten minutes. After this, we found our seats in the spacious departure lounge. Passengers aren't called to their train until 20 minutes before departure so there was plenty of time for the children to go into the small duty free shop. Getting onto the train couldn't have been easier. We chose to travel standard premier and there was another helpful Eurostar employee at the train door ready to help us get our bags and little people onto the train (it can be quite a big step up for little feet). Within minutes of boarding opening we were sat in our seats ready to go.  The same Eurostar employee who had met us at the door went through the carriage explaining to each customer what to expect during the journey. The extra attention to our children and their questions ensured they were ready for the journey and excited for the things to look out for along the way. Despite being standard premier you'd be forgiven for thinking you were in first class. From the very moment we stepped on the train we felt like VIPs, especially the children. Nothing at all was too much for the amazing staff members on board. Everything from the at seat service to the comfortable seats and wonderful attention to detail from the crew on board - who went out of their way to make our children's journey nothing short of magical - was exceptional. As we opted for the 7.04am train, we had breakfast included in our standard premier ticket, but even if we hadn't there are dining cars on the train serving excellent food and drink (which we took advantage of on the return journey). I can not express enough how wonderful the train manager and crew were on board the train. To top off our wonderful first trip on the Eurostar as a family, at the end of our journey, the wonderful train manager and carriage crew had between them arranged for my son to meet one of the Eurostar drivers who then gave him a private tour of the cab & power car. As a "future Eurostar driver" (his words) it really was the "best day of my life!" I'm now looking for our next family adventure and have already decided we will be going there by Eurostar.

Took Eurostar out of St Pancreas to Brussels Midi. 1st time Eurostar traveller and overall found it a very enjoyable travel experience.Couple of things I would note, check in at London was busy….queues not too bad on the day, but easy to see how this gets worse. Not enough sitting or restaurant options once in departures, this really needs improvement. Definitely book premium, not as busy, service fantastic in both directions. Would consider business class on future trips to gain use of the lounge. Although the value of this at Brussels is debateable, as it only appears to be an annex to the main waiting area.The ticket also included onwards travel to any Belgium train station. However, what wasn’t made clear is that STD Premium means you can travel 1st class. I googled this to find out but there is nothing on the emailed ticket info to advise this is the case.Which brings me to the only poor experience. That is the SNCB staff (who only seem to check 1st class anyway).On way back to Brussels Midi I showed the ticket man the ‘wallet ticket’ who wouldn’t accept this. As it turned out he needed to see the emailed ticket which showed the detail that onwards travel to any Belgium station included. (Presume there might be an option to buy a ticket without this?)His English wasn’t the best and my French ability meant this took a couple of goes to get to what he needed to see. All good in the end, but his attitude frankly was awful, very condescending, blatantly rude and quite nasty. Eurostar suggest you need to monitor your partners.I probably wouldn’t have mentioned this except the 2 foreign students who were checked after us had the third degree. I think perhaps they shouldn’t have been in 1st class for which they apologised, but they had a waiver for free travel on public transport as part of their student deal. They had only been in the country a few days, had university paperwork yet  2 ticket people laid into them…..it was awful, very disrespectful and threatening. Other than this incident, Eurostar albeit probably slower than flying is a very civilised way to get into Europe.

The crossing went well overall, but one of the staff members behaved scandalously. Me and my friend were in a hurry to get off the train, and one of the employees allowed himself insulting reflections “Lack of patience is a sign of lack of intelligence” before lecturing us “Listen to the youth, they seem to have lived longer than their father, a good war would not hurt” But what right is allowed to speak to us like this??? Doing repairs like that in front of the other passengers? Thank you but no thank you, sir, "Youth" will dispense with your contempt. If employees allow themselves this kind of thing, rest assured that I will fly next time. It might be more expensive but at least they'll talk to us properly.

I am so shocked Eurostar has some bad reviews, their service is absolutely BRILLIANT!! My partner and I travelled from London to Amsterdam in June, my partner is wheelchair bound and the service was excellent from start to finish.I booked special assistance with them over the phone, great service, super friendly, email confirmation straight away. When we arrived at St. Pancras staff was nothing but helpful and friendly. It’s very very busy but they helped us from start to finish. We especially want to thank Marie the special assistance lady who guided us through the entire station, explained everything to us, took us from gates to the train, so friendly, so helpful made us very comfortable. She was amazing!! The staff onboard are extremely helpful! Friendly, welcoming. Smooth journey, on the return, sadly our assistance didn’t turn up, however, we spoke to Kathrina who was the attendant on the train and she was FANTASTIC. I showed my assistance confirmation, she contacted them and dealt with everything, bless her, it was very stressful and busy but she handled it amazingly. We needed the ramp to get on and as no assistance turned up they worked out how to do it themselves so we were able to get on the train. She kept checking on us and made sure we were comfortable and sorted the ramp for the change in Brussels. I couldn’t of wished for a better person. All staff we dealt with were friendly, smiley, welcoming, assisted with all our needs. The food on board is superb!! Honestly, fantastic, even with a bit of a blip with no assistance on the return, it wa absolute amazing service and thank you to each and everyone of the staff that helped us. For wheelchair users we highly highly recommend the Eurostar! FANTASTIC!!

The whole experience was wonderful.  From the time we entered the Paris Gare du Nord Station until we arrived at St Pancras International Station in London everything went without a problem.  The carriage and seats were comfortable and the breakfast that was served was appetizing.  The whole journey was a very smooth ride.  I highly recommend the Eurostar as a form of transport to go from Paris to London (or vice versa).
Absolutely dreadful service. Hiked up prices for the summer and moved our seats to all sit separately, refusing to do anything about it. First and last time.

I had a very disappointing experience traveling with Eurostar recently. Despite booking in advance over the phone and requesting assistance, I was left to navigate security alone with my newborn baby, a pram, and a suitcase, which was extremely stressful. Onboard, there was no support, I wasn’t seated in the family section, and I was far from the baby changing facilities. There was also no space to store the pram. Overall, the lack of care and assistance made what should have been a manageable journey unnecessarily difficult. I expected much better service, especially when traveling with a newborn.

We usually fly from a local airport into Europe, but we thought we’d give Eurostar a try as much for the sake of the planet, and that we’re fed up with flight prices never actually being the final price to be paid. Eurostar pricing was very clear with no hidden extras and what could / could not be taken was clear from the outset.On arriving in London and the heat being in the high 20s, we decided to take a taxi from Paddington to St. Pancras as the underground would have been stifling. This turned out to be a wise choice, and for us, chatty cabbies are part of the tourist experience.St. Pancras is huge; the check-in is not very well signposted but is downstairs from the entrance and the Eurostar security is much less stressful than at airports in my experience. The French border guard was far too busy with a conversation on WhatsApp to pay much attention to me, but at least he didn’t walk off halfway through a queue of people, like his colleague!Outbound: We travelled at 17:04 in Standard Premiere as the price was not that much more in terms of cost from Standard and included a meal. The business class was far too expensive for us to justify, and this seemed a reasonable compromise.The carriage was attended to by two multilingual staff members, and greeting customers onto the carriage was a very nice touch indeed. This was very helpful as each carriage is not as easily identifiable as one might think. It was nice to be thanked as we left the carriage too.As the carriage only had about 8 people in it, we were offered more comfortable seats and had dinner comprising of a choice of wines and sweet potato falafels and Humus with a cheesecake, coffee and chocolates for dessert.The journey was very comfortable, and the two multi-lingual members of staff (Julie and Lauren) could not have been more helpful.We stopped at Lille and then carried onto Brussels Midi, which is one stop from Brussels Central (about 4 minutes) by underground. Your Eurostar ticket doubles as your ticket for the Brussels underground too.A great experience and a great start to our city break in Brussels, well done Eurostar and well-done Julie and Lauren!Inbound:  The Eurostar terminal is on the far left of Brussels Midi as you arrive from Brussels Central. We were travelling at 12:13 mid-day and the place was packed! We were kept waiting by French border guards for reasons that were not explained and it felt odd to just stand looking at the guards in the booths, looking at us.Entrance to the train is through the gift shop, which is also where the automatic tills are. This gave the impression that there was a huge queue for the tills, which wasn’t the case. Access to the Eurostar is up an escalator to the train and that’s it.It was nice to be welcomed aboard our carriage by a staff member who would look after us and thank us as we left.Lunch consisted of Salmon and Couscous with plum sponge and coffee for dessert, which was very nice indeed.Returning to London was equally as comfortable with more passengers on board this time.Eurostar made a welcome change to flying and we are now converts. The overall final price was for us comparable, and the experience (especially security) was much less stressful than flying in my experience.
Awful experience on both occasions I've used eurostar. Paid through the nose for first class, only to be kicked back to standard. No refund, no explaination. Unbelievable. Would not recommend.

Business premiere quite good but not worth the price charged.  The seats are nothing special, nor is the food and drink they serve.  The staff at Gare du Nord were great and very helpful, but the business premiere train service and overall experience appears to have declined in recent years.  Eurostar still remains probably the best way to commute Paris to London or vice-versa, but cannot recommend the business premiere product.

Travel from Aachen to London. Round trip was delayed. This means missing the connection in Brussels on the way out. The customs transfer in Brussels is adventurous. To drive one stop further on the return journey (instead of Aachen then Cologne) costs 30€. You already pay so much money and have to deal with a poor quality. Flights are therefore more attractive in comparison. Actually incredible in a time of climate change.

We took the Thalys, which has been taken over by Eurostar, from Schiphol to Paris. A clean seating area, although the toilets are filthy, but this is usually the case on toilets on trains unfortunately. Staff were friendly. Overall, it was a very good service.

I expect people working in the travel industry to be unhelpful and argumentative but the staff at Eurostar take it to a whole new level. Our train was cancelled. We were pushed from onecounter to another by the rudest people in London. We were eventually given tickets, not for the next train, but the one after that. We then waited in a hot and overcrowded area which must have been in breach of several health and safety requirements. Anyway, that train was delayed by over forty minutes. We eventually got to Paris over two hours late. When I applied for compensation I received an automated response declining the request. No explanation given. I'll be contacting the ombudsman. I would only ever travel with this dishonest company if there was no alternative. To be avoided.

Last June I bought 3 1st class tickets for travel from Brussels to Paris in August. When the train arrived, my seats were occupied by other passengers with correct tickets. We talked to employees and they told us they couldn’t do anything and to start a claim. So we traveled one part standing, the other in the folding seats between cars. When making the claim they answer that they give me 3 vouchers of 25 euros each (I paid 100 euros for each ticket), to be able to use within a year. We do not live in any of the countries where Eurostar operates, so we proceeded to request cash compensation for the difference between the contracted service and the one actually received. The answer has been that they already do enough with vouchers, and that their only obligation is to take passengers to destination. Legally it has a name: breach of contract or poor provision of a service.

If I could rate the Eurostar train a 0/5 I would. What a dreadful experience. We boarded our train into our assigned carriage and within 15-20mins of our departure it was evident that there was no air flow or air-conditioning in the cabin and it was only getting hotter and hotter. After spending half of the trip sitting in the adjoining toilet hallway to escape the heat - the multiple complaints in relation to the heat were heard by the train manager and our cabin was offered seats in another part of the train. Had it ended here my review would have been a lot more positive.  However the relief was short lived. There was no organisation of which seats we were to take - which meant we were being constantly moved as more passengers boarded the train! Each time having to move our luggage and with the staff being of no assistance and giving a rude unhelpful response that we are to vacate the seats for the people that booked them. Despite paying for the privilege of the Eurostar seat we were treated like an unwanted second class customer!

2 out of 2 journeys delayed. The refund of less than 20euros didn’t make up for missing connections, having to backtrack when they decided to make up time by not stopping at my station, having to pay extra for the next section of the journey. I chose this as an environmentally friendly choice but I’ll just fly in future.

First experience and the last. It sucks. The 12/08/24 train 9314 from 8.43 to Paris abolished. Next train taken. Train was full. We had to Trips upright for 2 hours. 34 degrees outside... and 37 degrees inside. Carriage no working air conditioning. Inside, I thought I was in an engine room instead of a high-speed train. A sweat lodge was nothing against it. Musty rooms far too hot. Annoying smell of sweat from people.  Staying away from people with a less pleasant body odor is unfortunately difficult, on a packed train.In short, much remains to be done to become an alternative to aircraft.What an uncomfortable journey from Brussels to Paris.Worthless experience Eurostar,

My train was canceled, and suddenly, they asked me to board the next train; once inside, they would assign us seats. It turns out that we traveled the whole time standing up. My mother is 80 years old, and she was exhausted.

Eurostar sold us seats that didn’t exist and when we complained, the travel assistant told us that they couldn’t do anything, that the car train was new and those numbers weren’t assigned… plop… In addition, the train was full because the previous train was delayed and Eurostar put some passengers from the previous journey on the new train… In other words, Eurostar transferred its problem on to its customers who had no other option than to travel standing up even with their children. Awful Note: Believe on TripAdvisor reviews, if customers say it is terrible, it is terrible…

I took the Eurostar to Brussels from London five years ago and it was exciting and fresh and affordable. This time it was the same price as a flight, the train was "tired"with some seats threadbare, the toilet was pretty gross and it was just not worth the £135 plus I paid. The seats seemed narrower with less leg room. I had to fumble to find the re-charging power- point between my seat mate's seat  (not a mate, but an unhappy stranger) and mine. Getting through security to board was relatively easy. But, I don't remember hearing any announcements or seeing staff onboard and the free wifi was pretty much non-exiatent. Tip: if you're travelling on a weekend, check flight costs before booking as the Eurostar has definitely slipped on comfort and class levels.
Service was fantastic and food was delicious! Laurinda was exceptional and a credit to the company - She provided better service than most restuarant staff and was very friendly and polite
Climate control & cooling was broken. Horrible odors from toilets in the cabins all allong the travel.Angry voyagers.

I booked 2 tickets to travel from Amsterdam to Paris Nord, the night before travel for a late evening train. Tickets were 298 Euro/ $325 US. When they came to scan tickets, I was told that our tickets were canceled by the company for unknown reason. I checked my account and sure enough the payment did go through.  The conductor told us there was nothing he could do because the booking code was showing cancelled. He provided no explanation ever after calling it in. We were told to either purchase 2 tickets on the spot or get off at the next stop. So we bought 2 more ticketsto get us to paris. Two days later when I got to the states I informed my bank of the situation. I contacted Eurostar through the online chat on NS international website and provided them the booking code and Explained that I was due a refund. I was told to wait to be connected to someone to help. No one ever replied. I reached out via the WhatsApp number that was provided and same thing happened. No one ever replied back after the booking code was given. I never received any emails or communication about the cancelation, and was never made aware of any problems before hand. This happened July 22, 2024 and it is now August 7, 2024 and still no contact. I now see why they have over 80 percent 1 star reviews. Horrible, non existant customer service is what they have. The train ride itself was comfortable and we arrived on time.

Our train Paris to London was delayed 30 minutes but we were only informed 8 minutes before scheduled departure.  As our French train was also delayed 30 minutes we had changed our booking over an hour before the departure in order to comply with Eurostar booking regulations at an additional cost of £105 each. Of course no refund from Eurostar for any of this unnecessary extra cost.

Travelling by train is so much more comfortable than flying. Security and passport control goes smoothly. We had booked extra legroom and that was lovely. The only downside is the waiting area in London St. Pancras. It's way too small.
Really poor customer service.  Very dissatisfied.  Had a death of a parent and I needed to cancel before my trip.  They are the only service provider who would not offer a credit.

Myself and a friend were doing a cycling trip around Belgium/France for 6 days. We got the ferry over to Calais and were going to get the Eurostar back to London from Brussels with our bikes at the end of the trip. First off there is no online bike booking facility. The information on the website directs you to book any train between Brussels and London and then email the team responsible to confirm the bikes as your cargo. No mention of a price or anything unusual. So we go ahead and book a train for £99. We get an instant auto email response that there is in fact an extra charge of €50ea bike and that only on certain trains can they be taken. Of course this did not include our train… why this information was not available prior to the booking step is nonsensical. Then they inform you that the team responsible for booking bikes has a 10 business day email turnaround. We were already within that to our trip. So we wait for a response from them, hear nothing… the day before the train is due to depart I call the customer service team and am advised that I have to move trains to accommodate the bikes and because it’s so close to travel that’s an extra £60pp. Even though the delay was caused by their own teams slowness… out of desperation we continue but all they can do is send an “urgent reminder” to the bike booking team and still can’t confirm our place to send this on the train. So we wait again. On the morning of the trip we call again and after 30 mins are informed to go to the station early and speak there to get the bikes added. So we do this and at the station are rudely told we are too early for our train and there are no bikes assigned to it… After some more explanation we finally get a manager who seems to understand what’s gone on and charges us for our bikes. THEN he says our original train did have capacity and if we wanted we can get on that one instead and save the wait time. So we do, but he will not return the extra money we were forced to pay to unnecessarily change train times. £120 in total. Total cost of the ticket therefore was £204pp… ridiculous, by comparison our ferry had online booking system and cost £27… will never recommend Eurostar to anyone. Still days later trying to get the partial is not full refund but losing hope at this point. Shocking service and flawed systems.

Mail received the day before for cancellation of the train of 16h31 with offer of free exchange but going further obliged to pay + 195 € because of space cheaper. so back to 85+195 €! The next day we learn that finally the original train is back on time but it is too late to cancel our change. In addition our train that was late left only 6 minutes before the one that was finally not cancelled. False publicity the change is not free in case of cancellation!!!
There were cancellations from London to Paris due to the Olympic madness. My train was cancelled and the staff were so lovely and made sure I got to Paris in time for the games! <3

Eurostar cancelled the train, tried to rebook but nothing available for 2 days, which was no good as we were going for the Olympics.  When I tried to book new seats, heypresto there were some available but only at £325 each one way.  I shall be taking this up with their customer services if I can get through to anyone.
Terrible, forst they cancelled our train, then made us wait 1 and a half hour for thhe next train that then didnt have any seats for us, even though we bought seats for the train.

Review of Eurostar Service to ParisAs a frequent traveler on Eurostar, I had high expectations for my recent journey to Paris. Unfortunately, my experience was marred by several significant issues that left me deeply dissatisfied.Lack of Direct Route to Disneyland ParisFirstly, one of the most glaring problems is the lack of a direct route to Disneyland Paris. Previously, Eurostar offered a convenient direct service from London to Marne-la-Vallée, the station for Disneyland Paris. This service was a favorite among families and Disney enthusiasts, saving time and the hassle of transfers. However, Eurostar has now discontinued this direct route, forcing travelers to endure inconvenient transfers, often through busy and unfamiliar stations. This change not only adds unnecessary stress but also significantly increases travel time, making the journey to the magical world of Disneyland far less magical.Non-Functioning WiFiAdding to the frustration was the consistently non-functional WiFi on board. Despite Eurostar's promises of reliable internet connectivity, I found it impossible to stay connected during the journey. In today's digital age, dependable WiFi is not just a luxury but a necessity for many passengers, whether they are trying to work, entertain their children, or simply pass the time. The lack of working WiFi is a significant letdown, especially for a service that markets itself as a premium travel experience.Cleanliness IssuesPerhaps the most disappointing aspect of the journey was the state of cleanliness on the train. Upon boarding, it was immediately apparent that the train had not been thoroughly cleaned. The floors were littered with crumbs and trash, the seats were stained, and the restrooms were in a deplorable state. Such conditions are unacceptable for any public transport service, let alone one that charges a premium for its tickets. Cleanliness should be a basic standard, and Eurostar's failure to maintain a clean environment is both unhygienic and unprofessional.ConclusionIn conclusion, my recent experience with Eurostar was far from satisfactory. The discontinuation of the direct route to Disneyland Paris, the non-functional WiFi, and the poor cleanliness of the trains all contributed to a deeply disappointing journey. Eurostar needs to address these issues urgently if it hopes to maintain its reputation and continue attracting passengers. Until these problems are resolved, I cannot in good conscience recommend Eurostar for travel to Disneyland Paris or any other destination.

The trip was perfect from Lille to London and back. The train is very fast and smooth, and departs near the center of London, which makes it a lot easier. The boarding and landing in Lille are quiet, while London is much more crowded (mainly for boarding). Immigration and waiting in the boarding room can be a problem, so it is good to prepare in advance and go calmly. Prices are high (at least for us who bought the day before the trip)

Thank you so much to Andre the customer service support at Paris Gare Du Nord. I lost my husband and he let me use his phone to call him.  He also helped us with a new train booking when we missed our train.  His kindness was so appreciated and he went above and beyond to help. Thank you. Nicola

They talked their way out of it. Although I sent proof that the train was over an hour late. Pay for no costs , although we did not start the trip because no announcement or further ad has been shown.

Eurostar to Disneyland Paris with a 2 year old. It's all good except for the passport control at St Pancras taking a while and not enough room to sit when you ate through. And then on the way back there are no facilities once through passport control. Train is good but don't understand why they don't stop at Ebbsfleet or Ashford now and why they are discontinuing the direct service to Disneyland!!

We had a Paris-London trip booked. We had to cancel. Their response to a request for a refund?Thanks, we have your money, &*%k off.Absolute S*&t customer service that discriminates against the average traveller since... if you have enough money to book business class they are happy to refund your money.We also had a Thalys train trip from Amsterdam-Paris booked. Had to cancel that one as well. Full refund, no questions asked.

Went on the eurostar to Amsterdam.Left London on time and very easy boarding.Arrived about 5 minutes late into Amsterdam but it's great to be straight in the city. The train was clean and very comfortable.The return was also straight forward no delay and Arrived on time back in London again very comfortable journey. What I would say is bring your own food and drinks if you can.Will happily travel again with eurostar

A stay planned in 2021, canceled by Eurostar 5 times, 5 times we accepted the solutions to discover London as a family (even going so far as to accept losing a day without financial compensation) The last departure was planned for December 26 but on December 19, 2022 they offered us yet another voucher because our train was canceled again which we accepted Unfortunately the prices have exploded and the only solution offered to us is to wait for the prices to drop or to complete to compensate. I put together a file made a written claim to be reimbursed the amount, on January 31 I received an email, they asked me to call them back! 17 minutes of waiting to hear me say the same thing... Deplorable One piece of advice: take the plane, it's ecologically irresponsible but it will save you from a stomach ulcer.

Travelling in Business Premier hoping for a good meal before arriving in Paris. Food was so vile it was inedible and even the bread roll was stale. Whoever chooses the menu needs to seriously get some advice.  Avoid paying the extra and take food with you.

I have been for weeks trying to intact Eurostar, it is impossible, there is no one to talk to or answer the phone. I am locked out of my Eurostar Carte Blanche account. This must be the worst customer service business that I have encountered. Terrible service.

Had a 5 hour delay on the way to London. There was no information given at all, we just had to figure out ourselves to get to Brussels with a Dutch intercity to get on the next Eurostar train. Once I tried to get a refund they told me at London that they couldn’t do anything and I had to go to the website; which didn’t work so I ended up calling them and I’ve been put on hold for 30 minutes.Never again.

We don't know who makes certain decisions but they are seriously having a joke, as someone in their infinite wisdom, sat behind a desk, has decided staff travel is now only standard whereas before we could pay the upgrade. Not now.So rather than sit with screaming children, noisy families and rowdy stag and hen parties we opted to pay full price for Standard Premier. The food provided was very limited and to be honest an absolut joke. Two options, Salmon Quiche (We don't eat fish) or Beetroot and Quinoa salad. (Urrggh!!, We're not Rabbits) What?? That's the choices?? No thanks. Disgraceful.So off to the buffet car located in Standard. (And not a bad selection of food) Bought Baguettes and Soup. Was given "cutlery" (Wooden). The so called knife wouldn't have cut through a piece of softened butter let alone a baguette. And as for the spoon for the soup, get this, it was a FLAT piece of wood. Take your own cutlery, take your own food or, (and we do not recommend), try SleasyJet, I'm sure the food would be a lot better quality. Absolute Idiots make these decisions that affect travellers but not themselves. Come on Eurostar, get your act together

No queues or problems at check-in. A short queue at the French border check. Departure from St Pancras had been put back by 10 minutes, but in the event we left at the original scheduled time. Arrived at Lille a few minutes early.Slightly annoying that, at 8 pm, no cafes or shops were open at Lille Europe. I could have done with a coffee or beer while waiting for the return train. Arrived back at St Pancras on time, a great day out thanks to Eurostar.
The toilets are utterly useless. Nothing works. The trains look old, the interior is tired in desperate need of serious updating. Not worth the money. Flying is cheaper!

At Amsterdam, if you arrive more than 90 minutes early for check-on, passengers have to wait outside the Eurostar terminal. In winter, this is horrible. Staff stay inside. The train was delayed, for people on tracks not Eurostar’s fault, but then later due to a technical issue, which is their responsibility. Train arrived in London 40 minutes late. Wifi on board was very unstable, to the point of frustrating. Toilets at St Pancras are dirty, to the point it made me feel sick from the smell just being inside the toilet area. Toilets inside Eurostar terminal at St Pancras on return are also disgraceful. I have used Eurostar for over 25 years, London - Brussels and recently Amsterdam - London. For me, it’s no longer proving to have any more value than flying. So I may have to start flying instead.

I've travelled twice in January on the Eurostar, and each time I have been extraordinarlly underwhelmed,One's disappointment starts when leaving the beautiful surroundings of St Pancras.  The surrounding area of shops, bars etc is wonderful, but once you "check in"and arrive in the Eurostar Waiting area / Departure lounge, the hororrs of Eurostar hit you pretty quickly.  The hall is rammed full.  The stench from the loos permeates everywhere, and it's all just really rather unpleasant.The trains are similarly crowded,The wifi is a joke - forget trying to work on the train.The food is appalling, as is the coffee.The trains aren't particularly smooth or comfortable.The carriages are either freezing cold or roasting hot.It's just a very disappointing, and unpleasant experience, and I will never do it again.  I rate it right up there with Ryanair as far as customer experience and satisfaction is concerned, and  haven't flown with them since 1999 on acount of how utterly appalling the experience was.I fear the Eurostar will be consignend to the same fate.It's a real shame because I work in sustainability, and was keen to reduce carbon footprint etc, but it's just so God Awful I refuse to use it again after my return trip later this week.   Goodbye and good riddance
I want to thank Mustafa who works in customer service at King's Cross international - he was helpful and patient to find my booking.

It’s 2023 and still no dogs are allowed. I get it, don’t do it in every carriage but have a few dog friendly carriages for a few services but NO dogs is just so backwards. You’re losing out on lots of business.
Both the London and Paris terminals were packed! Seriously overcrowded and no where near enough sitting. Check in, security and the train travel were all good though - no complaints.

Myself and my wife had a visit to Paris planned to go and watch the Paris Masters and decided to use Eurostar as we have done for the same journey on many occasions.The checking in process was very straight forward and comfortable seats were provided whilst waiting for the train to be ready. You are guided to your particular carriage and seats very clearly and the staff are always friendly and ready to offer help. We had plenty of leg room & comfort on both journies and really enjoyed the trip all round.

I tried to book for me and my 2 brothers one of them is in a wheelchair. I wanted to book a retour from Amsterdam to London. First of all, the information given is really unclear and limited. It is impossible to call the company and when I sent an email I got a reply only 2 weeks later. Their reply wasn’t nice and as I already booked tickets they did not care and did not offer any help. People in a wheelchair can only book a maximum of 2 tickets. It is weird whenever you are in a wheelchair you are not allowed to book with more than 2 people. So, I had to book a different ticket for myself and sit somewhere separate from them. Luckily, on the way to London the staff offered me a seat next to my brother. I had to pay extra but the employee gave me a 50% discount. I think there should be an option for people in a wheelchair to book tickets for more than 2 person even if it is not possible to sit together. It is weird that no one can be reached and that the assistance is not automatically fixed. I had to call a number for assistance but again no one picked up this phone. The staff in the train was nice and helpful. I hope that the managent will make travelling more accessible for everyone and might empathise with people in a wheelchair. Also, we couldn’t take the service dog and there is no clear information about bringing the service dog. Supposedly on the website it is stated that an extra ticket should be bought for the dog. However, I could’t find this ticket and we had to keep the dog and home and arrange shelter for the dog. Also the train could be directly entered with the wheelchair and a ramp has to be brought.I hope someone reads this and will try to make the Eurostar accesible for everyone.

I’ve always been a huge fan of rail travel in general and Eurostar in particular but I’m now going to avoid it if at all possible - because when it came to the crunch they lacked any interest in providing assistance - or even in fulfilling their contractual obligations. Last autumn the return leg of a trip to France was cancelled. None of the avenues supposedly available worked, whether rescheduling or refunding. It’s now three and a half months since the journey was supposed to have taken place and I’m significantly out of pocket - having had to extend my stay and buy an additional ticket. No refund, no compensation, no contact. This company has gone from hero to zero in a couple of years.

They do not adhere to the travel conditions. You should be able to rebook free of charge 7 days before departure, but you will simply have to pay for a new trip. They also don't give your money back once you pay! Very bad service and they sell lies! Next time just take the plane! They are also extremely difficult to reach.

Travelling on business to Paris I considered flying from Heathrow, compared to the Eurostar, which I had never used before.  Prices were comparable to flying, after considering additional costs.  I found Eurostar faster and more comfortable, arriving on central Paris more relaxed and with less hassle. Excellent trains, with comfortable seats, comfortable ride and far more luggage space than in a plane, easily fitted a larger bag in overhead storage.  Check in and security were completed in 5-10 minutes, far easier than at an airport.  Easy to change trains at both London St Pancras and Gare du Nord.Good departure lounges at each side.  Less choice than in an airport, but suitable cafe/sandwich restaurant at both London and Paris.Trains were on time and easy to book online.  Would definitely use Eurostar for future travels.
I would like to know from someone who has bought tickets (from Argentina) to travel from London to Brussels. On what page can they be obtained? Thank you!

This is a lie if it is the last train of the day since they like to go home early I guess.  Despite this and not living up to its own clearly stated rules on its website, they have not refunded us our ticket or any of our extra expenses incurred on this trip. I have received only negative responses so far as to our refund.  This would never happen in the anywhere else. When we told them our ticket said 801pm, one person said it left early and that  since it was the last train, if they didn't see anyone else in line, they probably just left early.No where did we read or see anything saying we needed to be there extra early or were we informed about the change in departure. We wasted a day spent on a hotel in Paris and had to book an extra night in London. We would like both or the tickets refunded for something that was not our fault.

After TWO cancellations through no fault of my own, one of which Eurostar didn't tell me about (I had to find out for myself when logging in to finalise plans just days before the trip), they will not refund me any of my money. The voucher they have offered as a gesture of "good will" (more nonsense) is not
Hire more staff and get rid of the one’s doing strikes.Alternative should be available. And at least 2 weeks notice should be provided.

Two round trips taken on the SNCF connect site in May 2022 to spend the New Year in London. So, I take insurance offered (Allianz). My partner's health problem at the end of December, so stay canceled. Impossible to have proof that we did not take the train. SNCF Connect washes its hands of this by referring to Eurostar whose customer service cannot be reached by telephone. No response by email... I've never seen that.. It's the worst company I know. In any case, next time it will be the plane!

1) Customer care is the worst ever. When you send an email, they do not reply except every 3 months to ask if your request is still valid.2) They make everything they can to avoid reimbursing you. This is completely crazy.3) If you make expenses, just try to ask them for a receipt with a price... You are going to love it :-)

It was a nightmare. Failure in the concatenation and 4 hours of delay. First 50 min, then 2 and finally 4!!!. They don't give you a bottle of water or a voucher to use the bathroom (1 euro). On top of that, they don't give you 1 cent back. Some scoundrels

I will start by saying that, once on the train, the 2.5 hr journey was smooth and comfortable.  However, I would never ever want to repeat the boarding at both St Pancras International and EuroDisney.   Treated like cattle is an understatement.  At St Pancras, the waiting area is too small.  Passengers for more than one train are herded into a small area with very few chairs.  We stood with our luggage in a group, only to be moved by Eurostar staff who managed to smash our bottle of duty free spirit over our cases and coats.  There is a coffee bar that also sells pastries but you are lucky to get back to your group with the food and drink intact.  There is nowhere to eat or drink other than where you are standing. We went by train to avoid the crowds at airports, this turns out to be unrealistic. The trip went well, despite a small delay due to weather and strikes in England. Checking in at St Pancras was a drama, certainly as bad as at the airports,

I have been on the Eurstar before  B.C (before corona)  to Paris but this time went to brussels Belgium. It was fast, comfy and  easier than going to and from the airports, It was very business like how you book on also like a plane

Departure from London, although busy is very efficient and stress free, a very nice departure lounge with plenty of amenities. On the other hand departure from Amsterdam is a bit of a shock to the system. The check in is at the very far end of the station- the end of the line, it the weather is unkind you will get cold and wet waiting in a queue. Inside there is only one ladies toilet cubicle and if you require any refreshments then it’s a vending machine. The departure area becomes rather cramped once everyone is in. A big let down after the spoils of London

Super easy way to travel as a family leaving from Kings Cross St Pancreas and arriving at Gard De Nour 2.5hrs later! Wifi was patchy, train was packed and the boarding a bit of a rabble but the real low point was the waiting area in London. Literally 100’s people crammed in, no social distancing and not even chairs. Eurostar needs to sort this out.
Stay booked months before and cancellation at the last moment of the return journey due to strikes but impossible to reimburse the rest of the stay...

I will NEVER travel with Eurostar again. On the R'dam platform they closed the glass doors right in front of me, while I arrived 1 minute before closing time (photo taken of the clock as proof). Without further understanding or apology, I was denied access to the check-in area, where people were still checking luggage. I could have easily caught the train. He was even standing almost next to me. Out of necessity, I had to take a plane for €440 to get to my appointment in London on time. After my complaint, my additional costs were not reimbursed. According to them I could have taken a train later. Which is nonsense because I would arrive in the middle of the night.  Shame on Eurostar!

Traveled on the Eurostar from London St Pancras to Paris on my first trip to Paris. I must confess I was very much looking forward to seeing what the hype was around the Eurostar and it certainly delivered. Comfortable, clean, quick and with fantastic facilities, the Eurostar is a great way to travel into Europe. The train goes through some amazing parts of the French countryside before it pulls into Gare Du Nord - ready for your trip around Paris. The price can be expensive if you book late but if you book early it is great value. 100% would do again!
Quite good and clean.However hardly any leg space after paying quite a lot and no wifi make this a bad option compare to flights.

Travelled back from Disneyland Paris on the 14th. We were one of the lucky ones who managed to get on the train home. However I was witness to almost 300 people including children, toddlers, disabled people and the elderly that did not get on the train home. Thankfully we did not listen to the Eurostar staff telling people the train was delayed and we were to go back to the park and return at 4pm. If we had we would also have been left stranded in Paris. The staff were directing people to ‘go over there’ and not to a particular queue. There were 4 queues. 1 - arriving customers, 2 - people trying to drop off luggage, 3 - people trying to collect luggage and 4 - people trying to leave that had their luggage. Everyone was just joining any queue creating a mass issue and ultimately the reason so many people were left behind. The problem could have so easily been avoided by having competent staff directing people to the right queue and by starting check in early. For us boarding started at 16:15 and ended at 16:50. There was no physical way 400-500 people could have been checked in on time. They knew this and still allowed it to continue. Once the train left, the staff went home and got the remaining customers thrown out by the police into the freezing cold. No hotel, no means of getting home. Just ‘try getting to Paris and see if you can get home from there’. No money to do this. Eurostar you are a disgrace and I will never travel with you again and I will share my experience with anyone that will listen!!And btw. There were hundreds of empty seats.

we were a group, family party of 7 , 3 generations - all of us part of the 300 ABANDONED by Eurostar ! No support, no information or advice ! We were told there was not enough customs staff to book us all in, so the train just left!!!! Armed police and dog handlers we brought in to ‘supervise’!!! It cost us Taxis, Hotel and dinner for overnight stay- then taxi to airport, and flight tickets to get home 28hrs later ! We were told we MAY get on a train the next day if we all went to Gar du Nord - no guarantees! Have left messages since getting home , no replies at all! Very  disappointed and Very Dissatisfied!

Decided on a European rail trip starting with the EuroStar to Amsterdam. Check in smooth, good coffee shop in departures. Easy to find seat on eurostar and great journey direct to Amsterdam Central Station in approx 4 hours.

Sadly disappointed using the Eurostar on Monday 19th December. Check in was ok but the waiting area before you go onto the platform was over crowded, extremely dirty, unorganised and all the bins were overflowing…..terrible place. The only saving grace was a Pret to grab a coffee. Not impressed.

Despite arriving early to the station and joining the check in queue on time, eurostar left over a hundred passengers stranded in Disneyland Paris with no further trains that evening (or confirmed the next day due to potential strike action). No help offered from staff and left to fend for ourselves. This included the elderly and families with young children.
