One of the most stressful experiences I’ve ever had and struggling now to even claim a refund as my train wasn’t “cancelled”. Never used before and never will again.

Tickets taken in July for December towards London. A week before departure, I learned that there was a strike on the day of my departure, so the train was cancelled. Their solution (exchange, refund or change the date of the ticket) knowing that the ticket taken a week before the holidays cost triple the price I paid. I find it shameful, no other solution proposed on their side. I had to request refunds for the accommodation and activities I had booked. Conclusion: trip canceled.

Consider with this service is really preferable to flying given flying costs no more and saves time and hassle. Flying may also be a better option for those in a position to use the Heathrow Express or Elizabeth Line, for example, to get to Heathrow. Having travelled on this service twice in the last 12 months some drawbacks have become apparent. Following Brexit, the time to go through the process at the station, especially at London St Pancras has been painfully slow. Also, the quality of service reflects an attitude that there is no competition so why bother. People are herded like cattle prior to boarding. There are virtually no Eurostar staff to be seen to help with problems that might arise. Trains are filthy and fully booked. One time we got bumped down a class with no explanation and a painful process extending over many months to obtain compensation, which was issued as a credit note in instead of a refund. In my experience the wifi doesn’t work most of the time. This is especially a problem at Kings Cross at there is also very poor mobile reception at the station.

I had a problem with my passport, and I couldn't go to London. I informed the Eurostar where I got my tickets. They make no effort or commercial gesture. I am really very disappointed with this company, I do not recommend it at all. Furthermore, I have sent emails without responses, and it is extremely difficult to contact them. On the other hand, to take your money in less than 24 hours, they are very fast...

Eurostar has the worst customer service. They will answer to your requests/ questions. After 5 calls of 2 hours 30 minutes and several mails, I still didn’t answer. And obviously, they always hung up my calls. Avoid Eurostar.
When buying tickets the price changed during the transaction, adding £35 per ticket only to be reduced back to the original value after the tickets were bought.

The news clearly states Mitie are on strike, however, Eurostar say the train is still scheduled and to make changes I will need to pay. Their website is still alllowing you to book travel for 16th December!!!Already need to book a hotel for 15th in London due to National rail strike on 16th, now hotels booked in Amsterdam are near collecting payment unless cancelled, and Eurostar want to charge me as it cant move the tickets to next Christmas as too early, so to split to 3 separate trips I need to change names (from 3 couples to 1 couple having 3 different trips) and they want to charge me £60 for this.(Not sure if that is per trip or once). Can't speak to a Supervisor for 3 days, which is after the dealine to change the tickets for free.RMT have just confirmed strike is still going ahead, clearly Eurostar dont believe the strike will happen or are happy to cancel their service and leave customers in the lurch at the last minute - which is it Eurostar?
train Rotterdam London booked transfer Brussels.  transfer much too tight, train a little late.  arrived Brussels.  and could no longer participate.

Both the trip to London and the return were horrible. On the way, we left Amsterdam, connecting in Brussels. As the connection is with another company, Eurostar doesn't even have a team in Amsterdam. It's very confusing. And to make matters worse, the departure time from Amsterdam was wrong. Arrival in Brussels is chaos. You have 10 minutes to get from arrivals to the Eurostar check-in location. Don't even think about going to the bathroom, you'll miss the time. When you know the path it is easy. It wasn't my case. Check-in for the train was a big hassle. We arrived around 35-40 before the train left and the queues for RX and immigration were huge.  And, of course, the train left 20 minutes late. The way back was another tumult. They organize check-in by train timetable. But all the trains were late, so the boarding space was full. We stayed around 30 minutes after the RX to do immigration. They stopped answering because the room was full. I ended up sitting on the floor to wait for immigration to open. Our train was 3 hours late. And we were still stuck for 30-40 minutes in Lillie due to the Belgian railway workers' strike. And on the train, there wasn't even toilet paper in the bathroom. The Wi-Fi network doesn't work. We had to arrive in Brussels to find another connection and hotel option.  There is compensation for delays of more than 60 minutes, but it is in the form of a voucher and is only useful if you are going to use the train again, which is not my case. Eurostar, I hope to never travel with this company again.

What an appalling service! First of all in Brussels where Eurostar blames the Belgian custom officers (4) to slow down the enormous queue (we had a 30mn delay) when they themselves only have 2 X-Rays open for a whole train and refuse to open the empty business class ticket check-in to speed up the process. Second in London where due to power outage we had a 2,5 hour delay. No one came in the train as promised to help us with connections, no annoucement made to let us know if the last thalys to Amsterdam would wait for us. We ran like mad in Brussels to catch it, no elderly person, handicapped or mum with young children could have made it. No one in Brussels to help with platform change. I am SO disgusted with this company it’s unbelievable!!! Poor customer service, shocking management, gross inability to manage gigantic queues at St Pancras. Honestly! Tickets are far from cheap, what are you guys paid for??????

I have written to customer services to complain about the service we received on 25th  November Train to Lille, only to have a standard reply, not addressing the problem at all.  Would be very grateful if someone could actually read the email and respond properly, not only did you cause undue stress and some of our holiday time( and we were not the only passengers who had a bad experience) but you cost us a lot of money.   Hopefully this can be sorted and I can amend my review but at the moment I would not recommend Eurostar to my worst enemy
No information when trains are delayed. Shameful. I am often disappointed by the customer service, and a 4 month wait time for a refund.

The Eurostar trip from London St. Pancras to Paris was great. My wife and parents went recently for a day trip while staying in London. The train was fast and efficient. Seating in economy section was tight but not unbearable (if you’re used to flying economy on flights in the US, this is similar). Nice food car onboard with knowledgeable staff. Pro Tip: buy your Paris Metro passes on the Eurostar from the Food Bar ahead of time to save time in Paris (especially if you are only going for a short period of time as I was). Customs both in St. Pancras and Gare de Nord was quick and easy. The only negative was that there was not enough seating at either location (London or Paris) so you had a lot of folks standing around waiting without an area to sit.

Took the Eurostar to London for the first time to limit emissions from flying and avoid long check-in times at Schiphol. Unfortunately only two connections per day from Amsterdam and therefore getting up very early. We had booked Business Premier Class and were able to check in and clear customs later, but that did mean that there was no room to sit in the small waiting room. One closed men's toilet and a urinal that overflows. Guests and staff must make use of this. It's really a shame. The outward journey was delayed by an hour and a half due to problems on the Dutch route, and was therefore diverted over the normal railway lines. Mediocre breakfast under the supervision of Mr. Raymond Blanc, three-star chef! In the meantime, one announcement after another is being made. So bring headphones. Things went better on the way back from London St. Pancras. The departure was 6:16 am!!! Otherwise you could go directly again around 6 p.m. No problems or delays here. Here a larger lounge, even a separate one for premier travelers, where only one coffee machine worked so everyone queued endlessly. The same breakfast again and a grumpy train steward. To Amsterdam in four hours. That was fantastic. Next time we will just reserve standard class.

Service at St. Pancras station was below average, signs are not clear for check in process and international departures. However, there was one super star at Euro star boarding I had the pleasure of meeting. His name was Pedro.I can not praise him enough for turning our herendeous experience at St. Pancras in to the most satisfying one.Thank you Pedro.

I cannot thank Eurostar enough and specifically Mr D Gutierrez-Sierra in the terminal services team at Kings Cross. As a charity who travel with large groups of terminally ill children the station is one of our most daunting times and he made things as smooth as simple as they could be. So many families were made to feel at ease. in what i appreciate is a high pressured environment he really took the time to help and nothing was too much. thankyou !

There are loads of things France does better than England… bread, boulevards, revolutions… but getting onto the Eurostar is not one of them. The queues are huge and completely disorganised, there’s not enough room so random gluts of people hold up those behind them, the passport control seems designed to punish British people going back to Britain (don’t get me started- I voted remain!). It took double the length of time to get through to the platforms than it did in Kings Cross. It’s pretty embarrassing and could be sorted with some rudimentary space planning and organisational change. Add that this completely disregards anyone with mobility issues or chronic pain: everyone stands for over an hour, including children and elderly people. The train was actually delayed because people couldn’t get onto it on time, and about 9 couples were arguing and stressed. Terrible and needs a rethink.
First experience of Eurostar, check in and security far smoother than any airport, more room is an advantage as is the speed to exit into the centre of Paris

I was travelling from Brussels to London, it's about 6 years since I last made this journey and the last time I did this was when the UK was still part of the European Union.Sadly through the acts of narrow minded people the UK is no longer part of the EU and this now means there are extra security checks that need to be carried out before you can travel. (I bet the people that voted leave did not think about this)There was quite a queue of people but once check in started we were all dealt with quite quickly and professionally.The departure lounge at Brussels Midi has a very big area for purchasing things like sweets and perfume as well as snacks for your journey. We were called to get on board the train and it was not long before we were leaving Belgium. The train ran non-stop from Brussels to London and it runs on a purpose built High Speed line all the way which is really impressive.The train was clean and comfortable and the staff were all friendly and polite.It's quite amazing that you can get from Brussels to London in just over 2 hours. WOW!

the WORST service, I had bought a dar ticket in EURAIL and reserved a ticket to travel from United Kingdom to France with Aural. the online page didn't work and they didn't answer my e mail or anything before the dar so because in the app says that you can do the reservation on the train station I intended to do that ant arrived 2 hours early to the station, but the men that atended told me that with Aural I could not make it, that he didn't kew why if I had the ticket in my cell phone but if I wanted to travel I had to buy again the ticket with them, and because I had to leave I did, Wasting a lot of money just because the companies aren't efficient

Such horrendous customer service. I'm still in shock that I have paid so much money to a company that values people so little. I have spent over a month trying to contact customer service regarding 3 tickets to Belgium - my booking reference was not recognised on my account. In the end I had to go to Kings Cross to actually speak to someone, who told me the case was closed. Even though I had no response! I would recommend that anyone wanting to book a Eurostar train think twice. I will fly from now on.

I was traveling on the Eurostar from Paris Gare Du Nord to London St Pancras on 5 August and during the X ray security scanner, my bag was caught in the conjoining conveyor belt and destroyed the leather strap on my bag. Eurostar are now refusing to compensate me for the FULL damage of the bag only part of it - which is absurd! NOTE: Eurostar staff say this is an everyday occurrence so my complaint will not come to a surprise. Their conveyor belt is designed for industrial purposes not for everyday passenger bag use. Ladies - be aware of your expensive bags!

GENERAL: Usually the service is fine so giving 3 stars average.THALYS ISSUES: However, not so when I booked a Eurostar ticket Ams->Lon. The Thalys train (ticket provided by Eurostar) was cancelled and no information provided anywhere. Eurostar guided us to international train information where they didn't know what to do. When arriving at Brussels we had to buy new tickets for the slower IC service from our own pocket. There was no information then or now, and the Eurostar website says there is no compensation. I emailed Eurostar and after a very long time received an automated response asking if my query was somehow resolved now considering they had not taken any action... After another response I received a personal email, saying they could only refund the ticket Brussels-Ams that I paid out of my own pocket. This is unacceptable.TIP: Take care when booking a ticket for Amsterdam, make sure you have a DIRECT connection without Thalys as they get cancelled frequently - this is not very clear on the Eurostar website when booking.

Just unbearable.  Delay of more than 45 minutes. No information. Totally random and with a stunning feeling of amateurism. With a price much higher than the plane, you really have the impression of being robbed. And no hope of reimbursement. Pitiful.

Took Eurostar from Lille, France to London, England.  Check in and Customs moved quickly. The ride from France to London was on time with no delay.However, the reception hall in Lille looked drab and run down as if it had not been touched since the hall was established.  The interior of the coaches also looked in need of a serious updating or refresh. Dirt and dust had accumulated on the grill of an air intake. Upon exiting at London, noticed a Eurostar consist which was in serious need of a wash.  Either new equipment is in the wings or Eurostar is tight fisted.

Tips is horrible! Unbelievable bad! They cancelled without any notications and made me wait 2 hrs for changing the tickets. In the end, I forced to change my day off my trip and all booking of hotels etc was wasted! They also allow people jump into the line and there is no control

Amsterdam/London Although I've lived in Amsterdam for more than twenty years, this was my first Eurostar experience. I flew Easy Jet once, and the experience on Eurostar was very similar in terms of cramped spaces and seats, unexplained delays, ridiculous distances between trains/gates, and a deep understanding of just what you give up by flying with a low cost carrier. A lot! I like trains and prefer them to flying when traveling around Europe.... Just to be clear. Had problems and delays too... But not the stress and hassle of Eurostar. From beginning to end it was one problem after the other. One delay after the other. Although I never was saw an actual employee of Eurostar on the train, I did experience terrible internet service, confused passengers who had others sitting in their seats and a mad dash to make the connections.... Arriving breathless at our connections, like all of my fellow passengers... Interesting to me that Trust Pilot has a 1.5 star rating and your site a 3 star. Makes me wonder why?The security check and waiting lounge at St.Pancras is beyond belief..... Like a Netflix reality show demonstrating how many unhappy and delayed passengers can be crammed and shoved into one space, with many, many people having to stand. Actually, the whole experience felt like some sort of endless bus journey in a developing country. Wow! Actually.... Gross.Do yourself a favor and fly. It is probably cheaper, definitely quicker and if you have a delay, there's probably at least a place for you to sit!

Eurostar arrival from Amsterdam at St Pancras on 29/09/2022 was chaotic.Too many people trying to use the escalator led to people being jammed and pushed at the bottom of the escalator. There were at least 3 doors into the customs hall but only 1 was open. No staff to be seen.Sent a complaint to St Pancras Eurostar. Received a review case number on 30/09 but nothing since then despite several attempts

Departure from Paris early in the morning. Gare du Nord terminal opens at 6:15 a.m. Several points for eating. Departure from London at the end of the afternoon, Smooth and well-managed journey: PAF / British police / Security filter Two points for eating. Please note, the small duty free only accepts credit cards, no cash... Trains on time in both directions. Fast journey. Clean train. A little cool inside, don't hesitate to cover up...Buffet bar available. You can buy the OYSTER card to travel around London. Ideal means of transport to reach the two capitals.

Best be prepared. St Pancras is currently the only station serving all destinations so is extremely busy. Totally understand the baggage scan but having not traveled for a few years we were not prepared for it, coupled with how busy it was made our journey stressful. A number of cancellations meant three trains worth of folk were crammed into the waiting lounge, most of us standing, which is not a problem for me, but my wife can’t stand for too long.  It says a lot about our rail network that you can travel Brussels in 2 hours, but it takes nearly four hours to travel from st Pancras to Eastbourne.

I was extremely disappointed with my experience of the Eurostar service and would avoid travelling to Paris with children on this service and instead fly in the future. The journey from London to Paris was fine we were on the first journey and were able to get through no problems. The journey back was probably the worst travelling experience I’ve had. We arrived to the Paris station and the queues were awful, it was packed and there was a lot of pushing, 3 adults were travelling with 4 children and we ended up getting split up multiple times because of bad management of the queues. There was also no access to toilets or drinks, and no air conditioning on a very hot day.  We queued for 2 & 1/2 hours to even get through security and in to the waiting area. 10 minutes after our train was meant to leave there was an announcement of a delay as the train we were meant to be in had broken down and they were sending a new one from London so it would be another hour at least.  As we were delayed over a certain amount of time, we were to get a 25% refund on our return tickets.  I had re-arranged my journey to travel with friends and had paid £800 in total before doing so. The time I re-booked for said £0 extra to pay, as my original tickets were more expensive than the ones I was re booking onto (I knew this as my friends had only paid £350)- they didn’t give the difference back, I just didn’t have extra to pay (lucky me). When I got my 25% refund it wasn’t based on the rate I actually paid- it was based on the price for the journey I re-booked onto. So I got £60 back, I was actually disgusted when I realised that’s what they had done. If it was like the journey from London- Paris then I would have been happy with the experience, but Paris- London was horrible.

The Eurostar service is good one. Unfortunately its web site has the worst functionality I have ever come across. I booked my wife and I on a trip to Paris. For health reasons I had to reschedule her trip. This website could not cope with me splitting the booking - and the site started showing a lot of nonsense information for my ongoing tickets. It also prevented me managing any of my tickets. In the end this cost me £175 on a ticket I could not use or change. In the end I had to book a flight from Orly to London which was a similar price. By the way Orly is good alternative because of the short coach transfer from there to Paris. I often go to France and will probably choose this option in future, This is a shame because I still think Eurostar is a good way to travel to Paris. Pity to see a great service let down by a shockingly bad website - what are the IT people doing there? No apology or compensation from the company. To phone them is near impossible and response time long and then with wrong information - no doubt due to their internal systems. What a shame!

Journey from London to Paris, and return a few days later went very smoothly. No queues to check in, passport control and security swift and efficient. Trains departed and arrived on time. The departure of my outward train was put back an hour because of a train strike in the UK, and Eurostar staff stamped my ticket so that I could book on a later onward train in Paris. Remember to print out your tickets as well as having them on your phone!

Eurostar from Brussels to London. 15h56 Cattle ClassI can only repeat what I wrote 3 years ago with an addition: filthy seats (see pic, some king of chocolate goo).Agreed, it's much less hassle than flying and the longer journey in your seat & reasonably quiet coaches allow some sleep despite the same endless & loud blabla on the speaker (welcome blabla at each stop,blablafor the bar coach, blabla I’m François your train manager, blabla for just saying hello...).On the minus side, the seat in the new Siemens trains look inviting but are hard as a concrete slab, legroom in Standard Class is just sufficient, poor food choice in the 'Café Métropolé (and you need to walk several coaches) and not nice to eat on site, you need to go to your seat with your little bag (no seating).Experience at the Brussels Gare du Midi nearly as awful as in St Pancras with only a ghasty & crowded seating area, overpriced & difficult to access parking, unfriendly Belgian police (security staff nice & helpful, UK Passport control manned by robots) and overpriced ´tax free’ shop.Last but not least and amazingly, this time the train left on time (fingers crossed for the return).Useless & superslow 'free WiFi' and, what would you expect ?, filthy & smelly toilets.All in all, Eurostar is somewhat better than flying (less hassle) but it is trying very hard to be just as annoying. If you need to go to London from Belgium, not much choice left since the demise of VLM.

Travelled to Paris for Oct half term by Eurostar, I’ll fly next time! Trains both ways were delayed, queues are huge in London and Paris and you are herded around like cattle and crammed in with everyone until the last minute before boarding. Once you arrive at Gard Du Nord expect more queues to escape (over 1 hour for taxi or 30mins for an underground ticket as machines not working). Overall a very unpleasant experience vs airport. The trains aren’t clean - toilets were a disgrace. Eurostar doesn’t deserve the business, book a flight instead….

I travelled on the 0755 service today London to Paris.  The ticket processing was fairly efficient...following the correct line by signs and verbal instructions. It was however between ticketing and border security near on a crowd crush.  There was literally no room to move. EU and EEA passport holders were able to be fast tracked however because of the lack of signage, direction, or room to move they were lost in the crowd. As an Australian passport holder I managed to find a spot in a line with people of similar nationalities and progress through the crush. Absolutely dangerous and ridiculous way of processing the large crowds...One suggestion would be to stop processing tickets until border security can catch up. On the return trip Paris Gate Du Nord train station was much more organised and civilised.  I appreciated the staff speaking English as I am not able to speak French. The check in process is on the next floor up....use the escalator near gate  17.  This is not clear at all....better signage would help.....dare I say it...perhaps signs in English would help too. On the whole, this trip is good value for money....not sure whether I would bother again visiting Paris this way again as it certainly was not relaxing.

Eurostar is a great way to travel from Paris to London, but you have to take extra time to get there, the station on the street has people waiting for the opportunity to steal, so you have to be very attentive.  The immigration area is well organized but it takes time. The trains can change and the rooms too so you will have to be very careful.  The train is good, fast and does its job.

Overall the reservation procedure and the two trips went well Where the problem is the communication Customer service unreachable by telephone and email more than a month to obtain a response which does not answer the questions. The icing on the cake, all post-trip communication concerning the satisfaction survey is done exclusively in Dutch. I remind you that Belgium has 3 national languages including French, the language with which I made my reservation. I conclude that certain services are managed by flamingo extremists who hate the French language to the point of excluding it from all communication

First of all, I had been looking forward to “taking the train that connects England and France” since I was much younger but when I finally tried “the Chunnel”, I was so disappointed that It almost ruined my time in Paris!I paid more than $400 to ride in first class because it was supposed to enhance the experience… but in reality… you are still moving like cattle with the unbridled crowd at St Pancras rather than being permitted into the lounge!!!The food on the train consisted of two cold buns, a tiny container of yogurt, coffee or tea, and water!The saddest part of the whole experience was that THERE IS NO TOUR GUIDE type of announcement or anything which informs you when you’re underground and going through the channel! It is difficult to tell because the windows of the Eurostar start out as black… Overall, I hope the Eurostar goes out of business; treating people like they don’t matter… is not worthy of profits! If you wanna get to France…. FLY! Listen carefully: other reviews told me that it is easier to travel via Eurostar because of the “ easy” security check!! Pure lies! I’m sure those reviews were written by shareholders because the security at Eurostar even told me to take my watch off and then I was scanned over and over again for NO REASON! They said, “Random”!Just fly… forget the train!

Had a trip booked for April 2020 which was cancelled due to covid lockdown. Eurostar have been the only company not to offer a refund and only offer postponing the trip. We have since paid an extra £180 each for the new dates we have booked. Have just now received an email to say our seats have been changed due to a train change. There was no option to change them online but we have been changed from forward facing to backward facing seats, which isn’t suitable as I get bad motion sickness. Phoned customer service to try and get help with this, was on hold for 30 minutes then the agent who answered was very short and made me feel like I was inconveniencing her by phoning. Only thing she could offer was putting a note on our booking for the train manager to look at on the day. No guarantee this would be resolved despite us making this booking a year ago. Very disappointed with the whole process and now feeling really anxious that I may have to stand or sit on the floor to avoid sitting backwards the whole way and getting sick.

They delayed the train both legs of the journey, with 4 hours delay in total. This was after having moved my booking to an earlier train with no explanation for the return journey. The compensation and attitude of the company is dreadful and after almost two weeks I have still heard nothing back from them. I have sent three emails now explaining my disappointment but to no avail. They only offer one avenue of contacting them now as they are ‘extremely busy and this will ensure they respond as fast as possible’. What a joke that is. Just another example of a company in todays world taking no responsibility for their handling of the service they claim to provide. I will continue to contact Eurostar directly until I receive a response and we come to a conclusion we are both happy with but I won’t hold my breath on that. My advice for travelling would be, unfortunately it’s out of your hands if there are changes and there will be little to no explanation or compensation for it if you choose to travel with them and it goes adrift. If travel goes as planned I would imagine it’s quite easy and smooth sailing. It’s a coin flip you’d be taking with your holiday/business travel plans.
Don’t leave people stranded in another country.Be warned Eurostar can text you that they’ve cancelled your train with no support. At least they ‘apologise for inconvenience caused’

Stuck on the train for 4 HOURS (technical problem (((((strike)))) at Gare du Nord aka the station from hell for not changing), we are only allowed a small glass of water. Forced to go BUY a mini packet of 5-ball chips. I'm waiting to see the compensation which I think will be execrable but better than nothing.

Booked a package deal through Eurostar, they left two women (one who is 6 months pregnant) without a hotel as they apparently “relocated us” according to the email they sent the hotel. Wouldn’t answer the phone which resulted in us having to find a new hotel and pay again. Haven’t had a reply from customer services want my refund urgently. Booking reference- NHNJDQ.
Had 1st class tickets but didn't even get a seat. Had to stand the whole journey. If you are going to travel with this company, there is no value in upgrading the cabin

They cancelled my return train to London in the last minute without any reason at all and claiming I should choose a different date time but there was NO AVAILABILITY for that day or any of the other days. Hence my only option is to claim an e voucher. So not even a refund although it is absolutely their fault and they refuse to claim responsibility for their errors. On top of that you cannot reach them as they are "too busy"! Absolute scam!!!!!! This is the worst service ever, destroyed a wonderful holiday for our anniversary....

I travel on the Eurostar a couple of times every year, and thought to finally write a review.   Travelling on the Eurostar is easy, convenient and relaxing, except for St. Pancras station, but I will come to that.  Purchasing tickets and downloading/electronic tickets is convenient.  Very easy and reliable.  The cars and seats are comfortable with plenty of room.  From Brussels to London in two hours, nice.   Arriving in central London is also nice instead at one of the airports.  However, the return from St. Pancras station.  Every time, the waiting area is over crowded.  Only enough seating for half the travelers and they want you there 120-90 minutes before your departure.  Premier Lounge is at times full and turn away passengers or you have to wait to enter.  They need to do something about St. Pancras.

Have used Eurostar a few times before in both directions and have never had a problem but using it but this time on the 2nd June 2022 was a different experience. A couple of days before my journey I went past St Pancras station in a bus and saw this huge line of people stretching out of the building and around the block and hoped that it was a one off situation, bomb scare or water leak or similar.Having seen this I arrived at the station around noon for my 2.31pm departure the line didn’t look too bad at the entrance to the security and passport area only to be told that the line was actually around the corner and there was a gap where I was to allow people to get to the other side of the station and the line did actually stretch around the station and outside onto the street but not as far as it was the other day plus they wont even let you join the line until they call your train which is usually about an hour before the scheduled departure. Around 1.15pm which I did and it took well over two hours to get to security and passport control and finally the platform which worked out well as the train was delayed by over an hour due to some incident on the line in France but worked out well as if it hadn’t been delayed I think it would have been an empty train.Once finally on the train it was back to what seemed like normal service with a meal provided shortly after leaving and it was a comfortable trip in the premiere carriage with its 1-2 seating which gives a good choice of seating options for singles, couples and groups. A bonus at the end of the trip was an announcement advising that as we were 72 minutes late we were entitled to compensation and would get an email probably 24 hours later which I did get. Hopefully the mess at London St Pancras will be fixed by the time I have to travel again but the actual train ride was fine and I really think it is a much better way to travel between the two cities than flying.

We booked forward facing seats as one of us gets travel sick and we were given backward facing seats.  There were no seats to move to.  My friend tried sitting sidewards with her back to the window and had one foot up on her other knee.  I went to check for spare seats, when I got back my friend had been told off by the Eurostar personnel who told her it would be £75 fine for putting her foot on the seat.  She explained why she was sitting sidewards and he shouted at her and said "it isnt funny - did she want to pay the fine".  He was so rude.  I have now complained to Eurostar twice and they have not even had the courtesy to respond to me.  I paid over £400 for our tickets and will not be travelling on Eurostar again.  Terrible customer service.

Really crappy customer service: you have to be there 30 minutes in advance. Communicated very briefly (somewhere in a footnote in an email). Arrive 20 minutes in advance. Train doors are still open, but no: they refuse you access to the platform until the train has left. We were with all kinds of tourists who also did not know that you have to be there 30 minutes in advance. Then something goes wrong in the communication if this was not clear to so many travelers. Then we visited the Eurostar office. Refers to NS International, which in turn refers to Eurostar. They can't do anything at the office at CS, you can only call. Eurostar selection menu not working. In other words: customer service with a baseball bat. Flight tickets booked. Never again with this hopeless organization.

Great trip apart from the passenger lounges at St Pancras. The staff were very helpful in giving us priority because my disabled wife  cannot stand for long. The terminal at St Pancras was rammed and just can't cope with the passenger numbers; you wonder why they cannot reopen Ebbsfleet and Ashford. The train ride was lovely and good to see passing the passing the scenery in each country. On the way back we were once again at Amsterdam given assistance at the Eurostar terminal. The terminal is no more than a shed and once again rammed. My wife said there was only one Ladies toilet for all these people. At both ends we had to queue for security checks, emmigration and immigration checks; apparently it's got worse since Brexit but we did get nice stamps on our passports. The staff were actually friendly. So all in all a lovely trip. It does seem silly to have to go all the way to London and then come back through Kent. The terminals need substantial improvements to the infrastructure to copw the number of passengers

Customer Service is non existent ….. my train was delayed 3 months ago and resulted in me missing my booked connections. Eurostar emailed me the very next day saying I was due compensation….. im still waiting…… they don’t respond by email, you can’t phone as they have closed their phone lines and they havent responded on Social Media…… Really shocking for such a well known company!Whilst I am sure Brexit has caused a lot of issues , this has absolutely nothing to do with Brexit but everything to do with  some unhelpful staff , terrible Customer Service and a management team that clearly don’t care about their customers!

I feel a lot of services have gone to the dogs recently and Eurostar is no exception to this rule. We purchased 2 first class tickets for $1,000 AUD. Lounge was dirty and overcrowded. Food offering in the lounge  was about as flavoursome as an IKEA hotdog. No help with luggage upon boarding into first class. Food on board was not as described “Raymond Blanc inspired”, more like “Ronald McDonald inspired”. Toilets were overflowing with water everywhere and to cap it all off they “ran out of Champaign”. Do yourself a favour and fly!

Would recommend euro star its so fast there paris in no time ,checking in so simple nice bars in check in area and the trains are comfy  and can get drinks and stuff from the middle carriages ,get yourself to paris

never better than mediocre...efforts have been made to speed up the horrendous queues at gar Du Nord. It helps when one (stupendously expensive) has a business premier ticket and. a non UK European passport. This time endless queues but bearable. Electronic tickets appear not to be in use. VIP lounge very little food, no water and overcrowded. On board no magazines, cabin not clean, food very very poor and getting worse.

I booked on line ahead of departure a free of charge special assistance service for my elderly mother who was travelling on her own and was recovering from a knee operation.  I received a very kind/personal and explanatory email a few days before departure explaining what to expect when arriving at St Pancras. The staff was brilliant! As soon as we arrived, we were directed to a different check in desk therefore avoiding queues.  There were chairs in front of the check in desk where my mother could sit whilst the staff promptly dealt with her passport & check in papers.  I left her there to buy her a drink and when I returned she had been transferred onto a wheelchair where a member of staff was patiently waiting for my return with her suitcase and paperwork in hand. She was transferred to a waiting room until 1/2 hr before the train departure and was wheeled down all the way to her carriage before any other passengers. Her suitcase was carried for her onto the train.  The same had been organised when she arrived in Paris.  There was a member of staff waiting with a wheelchair at her carriage who unloaded her suitcase and wheeled her all the way to the taxi rank.  She is used to travelling with Eurostar but has never used the special assistance before.  She was very happy as was I with the fantastic service and kindness  she received from the staff both at St Pancras and Paris as she did not have to worry about stairs, escalators, carrying suitcases or busy platforms.  I cannot thank the Eurostar staff enough for the 5 star service we have received.

We went to Paris and back as business class customers and had a very smooth outward journey, although the breakfast wasn’t that great. It was a good lounge experience at St Pancras. Our return was delayed and there were huge queues, but the French staff managed then well by grouping different queues and cordoning them off. The business lounge is again good, with mini madeleines, vegetable crisps and lots of drink options. However, we were told we had to walk down the stairs to the train and this was very difficult for me as I had a huge heavy case - staff offered no assistance. I’m grateful to the staff for rushing us business class passengers through. The meal was terrible coming back - some kind of chicken sliced on Bulgari wheat that tasted like petrol, but we enjoyed the dessert tart and the drinks. Don’t forget to use the tax refund machines just by the duty free department in order to claim back tax on purchases over 100 euros. You just scan your tax invoice and it does it in seconds. Also, be careful when going to the toilet on the train as it’s high speed and I kept falling over.

We took the Eurostar from London to Paris the last week in September. From what I've heard we got lucky - no strikes and no delays. The trip was easy and on time and the ride was comfortable despite the fact that the train was full. There's a food car in the train, but there was only one person behind the counter, so there was a long line to get food and a glass of wine. Other than that it was an enjoyable trip and fun to cruise through the England and France countryside at 180+ mph. By the way - we got to London St. Pancras station an hour before our train left and it was more than enough time to go through customs and figure out where we should go - it's a big station but we found it easy to navigate.

To avoid taking the plane and go for a more environment-friendly alternative, I planned to go from Brussels to London via Eurostar. Bad idea! Due to delays of a previous train (which were out of my control), I arrived at the Eurostar terminal a few minutes after check-in for "ordinary people" like me had closed. I needed to be in the upcoming departure as a national strike in Great Britain would have made it impossible to reach my ultimate travel destination. So I asked if it was possible to still get on the train, that was not leaving for nearly another half an hour. The staff suggested that I buy a business premier ticket for 370€, because IT IS POSSIBLE TO CHECK IN WITHIN 15 MINUTES OF DEPARTURE FOR BUSINESS CUSTOMERS, BUT STRICTLY ONLY WITHIN 30 MINUTES FOR STANDARD CLASS TRAVELLERS. So I was emotionally blackmailed to spend what is close to a month's salary for many people to get on a train that had obviously still seats available and for which I had purchased a ticket. I had to cancel my entire holiday due to bone-headed Eurostar staff. Never again! From now on I will always take the plane or long-distance coach to get to the UK. Fun fact: Business premier tickets include a champagne reception and a lunch option "designed by Raymond Blanc".

Hands off! For environmental reasons, I wanted to take a train instead of a plane. Once the vacation failed in Brussels thanks to Eurostar - with the corresponding additional costs for a new journey/cancellation fees at the destination. I couldn't rebook or cancel the ticket for the return trip, so I made a second attempt. Extremely rude employees (probably underpaid and you can hardly blame them) who want to control the hustle and bustle. The security checks are a horror. No room to form a group, just a big group of people. A paradise for pickpockets and viruses of all kinds. Once in the security area, things continue. No space for the many people and their luggage. Crowds everywhere and people squatting on the floor for lack of alternatives. Although there wasn't time for that later. First a bag check was carried out like at the airport and then we were packed together so that evacuation would not be possible. This is how security works. Because of the chaos at the security checkpoint, I would also recommend allowing about 5 hours of transfer time to be on the safe side. As we all know, a lot goes wrong on the train, but somehow you always get to your destination in the end. It's different with the Eurostar

Travelling Paris to London. They kept saying there’s a delay for a few minutes, but ended up  with leaving with an hr delay as they needed to exchange the trains (which I understand it could happen). The queue was an absolute mess and there was no effort to organize the line and to accommodate the passengers with heavy luggages as many of them ended up taking the stairs with their large luggages while there were escalators available from another gate. At the train, the attendants were verbally pushing the people to enter the train hastily. Awful experience!

Arrived for my train 25 minutes before departure and gate was closed. Waited in a queue for 20 minutes to change my ticket to the next train. I went through security in less than 5 minutes and was through on time to hear my original train being called. Closing gates before departure is just money grabbing. There’s no good reason to do it. I wanted to take the train because it’s more environmentally friendly and less hassle than flying but what is the point if companies like Eurostar are looking for any opportunity to shake you down? Really makes travelling a misery.

Very concerned after reading so many negative reviews but our first experience was faultless, even travelling in economy.Check in at Paris was swift with friendly staff, the train was on time, clean and well prepared. Didn’t use the cafe carriage as the queue for Paul in the station was short. The only negative is the price, nearly €200 each for one way to London. (This may be due to threat of ATC strike) But way less hassle than flying and we had loads of heavy luggage after touring France, none of which was questioned and plenty of space on board.
Can't contact customer service for any problems you may have. Don't answer phone or emails, even ticket office is closed. I have been trying for weeks.

LONDON TO PARIS------overall good the wait before boarding is TOO long-----waiting area too small---not enough seats------on site catering take away style by Pret was good.Train journey quick/smooth -------limited refreshments but to a good standard.Gare Du Nord--------this has always been a VERY bad part of Paris------dirty/crime ridden------VERY long waiting time for Taxis with bullying Security staff treating passengers like sheep.PARIS TO LONDON-----train journey was as before ----BUT the Gd N check in area and facilities very poor---badly sign posted and hard to find-------the whole area was dirty ---rubbish everywhere-----refreshment area  PAUL----although providing some good food and drink was filthy and adjacent toilets even more so------smelly and not cleaned in a long time.The area PAUL had rubbish piled up at every litter bin and the tables------the staff I assume are NOT responsible because they made NO effort to come front of house to clear up------come on France---this is a premier transport system with many things to reccomend it------CLEAN IT UP!
Terrible sums it sums it up quite well. Nothing worked. The service was no help at all. Spent 3 hours waiting

If you have an issue there is no telephone support - you need to write a form and they will get back to you in 28 days! 28 days???? It seem like Ryanair in 2007 but tickets are not cheap!  Disgraceful.

I traveled from London St. Pancras to Bruxelles Midi. The Eurostar terminal was a nightmare. Two trains for Paris were delayed, but they kept on allowing people to go through security. There were so many people that it was impossible to walk, let alone find a seat. The train was jam-packed and dirty. Irrespective of the current Covid protocols, and the clear reminders on the train, almost no one wore masks. I paid almost 200 euros for a one-way ticket of a dreadful trip.

The trains are dirty, old, freezing cold, and seriously need to renovated. The seats have crumbs tucked into the crevices and the tables were dirty. Very old fashioned and poor quality for the extortionate prices the Eurostar charges these days. The seats were also awkwardly very large and uncomfortable.

Just back from a golfing trip in Belgium, taking golf clubs on Eurostar was very simple (apart from carrying them in the queues). When you pass through security in St. Pancreas they give you a tray insert to place your clubs on, but coming back they go straight on the rollers. Once you board the train there is a luggage area which you can lie your clubs down in, we just had cart bags and there’s no real need for a travel bag.The train journey is simple and smooth, with toilets and buffet car not far away from any seat. On seating, you get allocated a seat but you can then change it via the app or website without any charge. There are plugs by most seats for charging phones etc. we didn’t use them so can’t really say which type of plug you need.

The journey on the train was lovely and relaxed both ways.  Here are the extras:London to Paris: great service, departure lounge and check in procedure.  Helpful staff and on time.  Unfortunately, when arriving in Paris we were made to wait on the platform for 10 minutes or so before being allowed to leave.  What was that about?Paris to London: had to wait for ages in queues to check in, go through passport and security.  No time to relax in departure lounge.  Train was late, too.  It is not even high season.  Again, what was that about?

Overcharged for travel insurance by Eurostar 7 months ago and still haven’t been refunded. London to Paris trip on 31 May was completely shoddy. Trains delayed, no info at King’s Cross, lounge filthy and no water in basin in loo. (Staff member said “It’s been like that for months”) Cold food on train. Arrived late, missed connection.No help or response from Eurostar since.

My wife and myself travelled to Paris this morning on Eurostar and - besides the long queues at St Pancras (any future travellers are advised to add an additional hour to their arrival plans to avoid disappointment! - it was a very smooth journey.We left on time, arrived on time and - as we were travelling Standard Premier (very comfortable seating) - enjoyed a Continental  breakfast en route. Service was also very good and,  as such, any future trips to Paris are likely to be by Eurostar - a view clearly shared by many others as the average Eurostar journey accommodates upto  850 passengers and there weren’t many empty seats on our train!

Typical Eurostar. We were at the Amsterdam station. Always looks like they expect 20 people to get on the train. Huge long lines, 1 or 2 members of staff, very limited food and drink at station. Packed in like sardines until the train time and then the train itself is filthy. They always leave on time in my experience and you can get to your destination. All the in-between bits are poor.

The train journeys themselves were perfect, both outbound and return. The security and border procedures at St Pancras outbound were well handled, if busy. The return trip from Paris GdN was poor, with passport scanners failing, consequent lengthy queues and a thoroughly inept security scanning procedure. The staff were ill-informed and unhelpful throughout. It was the airport experience I had hoped to avoid.
We travelled standard premier to Amsterdam. Seats, journey and food & drink at seats very good. Altogether, a very civilised way to travel.

On the whole the train and staff from London to Amsterdam were very good; where I find that improvement is required is when the return train is “cancelled” due to Dutch railways industrial action and we were left with almost no assistance in getting home. We were told we could transfer our tickets to a service on another day but the next available train was fully booked. It turns out the service was not actually cancelled but would be running from Brussels Midi instead of Amsterdam (we found this out after we had cancelled our return trip, booked an extra night’s accommodation and booked a Thalys TGV to Paris and the Eurostar from Paris to London). Why could Eurostar not provide a coach service from Amsterdam to Brussels for those that required it? I’m sure the cost of our tickets would have covered this. I emailed Eurostar with these concerns but they have not yet replied after two weeks.

Re-review after an understandable gap! The Britishend is still fine witha relatively smootyh transition from station to train and a generally pleasant experience. However as with some otherParis entrance points - notably Gare du Nord and Charles de Gaule airport the French endhas bombed in the past three years with a preponderance of rude (to the Brits) staff and a geerally sub standard service. Unless we have to go throughParis we now use Brussels.

A shame! They cancel your train, promise you a solution and then leave you stranded as a family with a young child to find your own way back for the next day! Obliged to take a hotel at your own expense. You lose your working day. Eurostar promises compensation. Pure utopia. Nothing after three months! Not even a response to the email and registered mail

very overpriced and disorganized.  the internet didnt work on the british leg. the tea and coffee machines were out of action in both cafes. both cafes had one person serving with probably 800 on the train so the ques were half hour.the french end is even worse . arrive at gare de nord at least hour before or you miss the train. the whole french side has just 6 passport booths and the helpers are clue less and dont speak english.  will be worse next year when fingerprints will need to be taken so allow 1 and half hours and that shud put it on a par with flying.  so lessons to be learnedbuy food before you get board- allow at least one hour arrival time otherwise you will miss it. but tickets at least 2 months in advancedont speak with the clueless attendentsor just fly.

Easy site for booking we also booked the hotel ED Amsterdam which was really good for value and location.Trip information was good as was boarding and comfort.Only negative was the very limited refreshments at Amsterdam one you have gone through passport control. No café just one vending machine and one coffee machine and considering your asked to arrive 90 mins before departure its not great.

Our trip from London to Paris went well with an on time train. Went through the accessibility request process by email with blind husband.  Timely email told us exactly what to do at St. Pancras to move quickly with a short walk and no wait through passport checks both British and French.  Arrived 70 minutes early as instructed.   Took early train so we were  delighted that there were two food shops open  for coffee before  7am in the passenger lounge.  We sat in the accessibility waiting area and were escorted to the elevator when it was time to board our train.  There was a little communication problem while waiting in the disabled area before the staff understood we were not waiting for a wheel chair but could walk short distances, First class was comfortable with a simple breakfast service.  Small cups of coffee and no refill when the attendant was asked.  Difficult three steps for blind person to get on to train at St Pancras and off train onto platform at Gare du Nord.   We were continuing on but booked the French train separately with ample time to travel to St Lazare in case we had some issues.

I'm a bit of a train fan so all new experiences are eagerly looked forward to.  On this first ride on the Eurostar from St Pancras to Gare du Nord, things thankfully ran fairly smoothly.  The train was fairly full for a morning departure but the train left on time and arrived in Paris on time slightly over two hours later.  To be frank, this isn't a train ride with much to see out the windows due to the lengthy barriers that keep the noise down in the areas neighbouring the train tracks.  Going through the Eurostar tunnel was interesting although, naturally, there was nothing to see either.  I do agree with other reviewers that the cost of a Eurostar ticket is fairly steep but if convenience is foremost, there's not much of a better option.

May be fine if all goes well but they don't take calls and don't reply to forms submissions so any issues and you're on your own. Literally the worst customer service imaginable. They should be ashamed

Eurostar was booked as part of a package tour to Disneyland Paris. As a group of two families we wanted to sit together and although, initially we were sited in different carriages for both journeys, changing seats via the website was an absolute breeze. Booking in at St Pancras was simple with the the only hold-ups being border control and security. The train was on time and very comfortable. On board service was great both ways and the food provided (Standard Premier booking) fine. It’s worth noting that there is a time difference in breakfast service when travelling to Disneyland. The return trip was more relaxed as the Disneyland station at Chessy is smaller and less crowded. This is the first time that we have travelled by Eurostar and I would not hesitate to use the service again.

Travelled by Eurostar from St Pancras to Brussels. Booked our tickets a long time before I had a serious injury and ended up having to have surgery on my leg, so by the time it came to travelling I was using crutches. A quick few minutes filling out their online form to explain my situation a couple of weeks before we travelled and they had arranged some special assistance for me.As soon as I booked I checked to see where our allocated seats were - no window! Quickly chose new seats at no extra cost so that we had a window to look out of on our journey. Would suggest everyone does this.Arrived at St Pancras to be greeted by very long queues. The queues to check in were that bad they were shouting out for passengers for the train that was due to depart. As we had booked the special assistance we were able to bypass the queues and were swiftly checked in. The next step was security. I knew that either my crutches or the metal plate in my leg would set off the security scanner and they did, so was taken to one side and patted down and hand scanned. Quick check over and I was on my way.I was under the impression that once we had checked in, that was the end of the assistance. I was wrong. When queueing for passport control we were also pulled out of the queue to bypass that queue and go straight to the next available passport desk, where the Eurostar staff waited with us until our passports were checked. Such a smooth process and put me at ease.One downside of the special assistance was that for some reason only one of us had been checked in through the special assistance gate (we were told we were both checked in) as my partner was showing on their system as a no-show when they were walking through the train to make sure all the passengers were on board. A quick conversation to explain that we had gone through special assistance and had been told that we had both been checked in and it was resolved (thank goodness for printing out our tickets and not relying on technology!).Arriving at Brussels I didn't think I was going to make it off the train! We were in the last coach, coach 16, and the curvature of the platform meant there was a very large gap between the last stair of the train and the platform. Had to give my partner 1 of my crutches to hold, while I held onto the train to try to step off sideways! Something to be aware of next time as we will make sure we book a seat on the front of the train arriving into Brussels as that is straight.We were travelling onwards to Bruges, and just managed to get a train 25 minutes after arriving into Brussels.Return journey was just as good. Brussels don't have a dedicted special assistance desk so I just mentioned to the woman at the entrance who was directing everyone that I had special assistance booked and we were shown to the Business check in. Turns out they had a wheelchair waiting for me! After much insistance that I really didn't need the wheelchair and was happy to carry on with my crutches, we were through check in, a separate security line to the standard passengers, and straight through passport control. There was also a dedicated assistance waiting area in Brussels which I didn't notice in London (maybe because we were lucky enough to find some standard seats in London), and we were one of the first to be let up onto the platform, up a ramp so we didn't have to walk through the duty free area. We travelled Standard Premier, purely for the extra space. The food that came with it wasn't really to our taste. The breakfast on our outbound journey of yogurt, croissant and bread roll was ok, but the return journey was either salmon quiche or falafel. I chose falafel (which I had never had before but I really don't like salmon) and my partner didn't eat as he didn't like either choices. As we knew the food wasn't part of our choice for booking these seats, and we didn't know what the food would have been until about a week before we travelled, this has no affect to this review as it is personal choice.Arrival back into St Pancras was ok, the travelator wasn't working so I had to ease my way down it on the crutches as we couldn't see a lift that was in action, but that was probably the only issue on arrival.Both journeys were pretty much on time, trains were smooth, and despite the initial hiccup on the outbound journey with them missing checking in a passenger I'd be happy to travel again.

Received email saying my train had been cancelled due to British strikes.  I have disabilities and was in France already.  They closed their phone lines and no response to my online contact forms. The option to exchange my ticket didn’t work recommending me to phone them lol!I ended up having to buy another ticket. 2 weeks later still nothing from customer services but somehow the money has been refunded. But this doesn’t compensate for the anxiety they caused me or any notification of them paying me. Avoid Avoid AVOID
The prices became outrageous. They have reduced the number of trains and raised the tariff. It's often over €400 for a return ticket during the week. It is a rip-off!!

On 1st August my husband and I caught the Eurostar from St Pancras, London to Gare du Nord, Paris. The train departed London on time at 12.31 and arrived in Paris roughly on time ~15.48. As part of this booking we had a connection to catch from Paris Gare de Lyon to Avignon TGV, departing Paris at 16:38, i.e. a maximum connection time of 48 minutes, as the TGV doors are locked 2 minutes prior to departure.  As we had booked the entire journey via the Eurostar website, we assumed that the connection time across Paris from Gare du Nord to Gare de Lyon would be sufficient, however it certainly was not and we therefore missed our connecting train.Issues that contributed to this – •	Eurostar suggests to connect via the RER Line D. This requires buying a Ticket+ from Gare du Nord. The queues are very long and exceedingly slow at the ticket machines and kiosk – this took a good deal of time.•	Once the RER was located, the Ticket+ would not allow my husband to pass through the barrier. •	Once on the RER platform, there was a wait of ~10 minutes before a train arrived•	On attempting to exit the RER, my Ticket+ would not permit me to leave and I was trapped behind the barrier•	We then ran to the TGV platform only to see our booked train departing without us.•	The station staff at Gare de Lyon told us we could get tickets for the next service (an hour later) from a kiosk. However the queue was again very long and very slow moving and time passed with nothing happening. I decided to check via a ticket machine to see if there were tickets for the next train ( 17.38) and found that there were none left. Equally the service 2 hours later was fully booked other than a small number of tickets in 1st class. In order to avoid being stranded in Paris, I bought 2 tickets for this train at 18.39 at a cost of 244 Euro. We therefore arrive in Avignon 2 hours later than expected, this caused a huge amount of stress and worry, not to mention the additional cost of having to buy new tickets.All of this could have been avoided if Eurostar had sold us tickets with a reasonable and achievable connection time in Paris. The website states the connection time is around 30 minutes, however fails to include time to orientate oneself at each (large) station, purchase RER ticket+ and wait for a train to turn up. Please consider that you should allow at least 60 minutes for such a connection. We feel that we have been mis-sold the TGV tickets – it was simply not possible to have made the connection.With regard to the planned connection for our return journey on 5th August. The planned journey (again booked as a complete journey from Eurostar website) was to arrive at Gare de Lyon, Paris at 15.35, from Avignon TGV; with the Eurostar back to London leaving Paris Gare du Nord at 17.13. Given that Eurostar recommends check-in 90 minutes before departure (i.e. suggested check in at 15. 43) it is difficult to see how we could possibly have achieved that connection? When we realised this was going to be an issue, I attempted to amend the booking online, only to find that only the entire journey could be amended, when I really just needed to amend the time of the TGV tickets in order to arrive in Paris earlier. Why is this not possible? I then had to decide to again purchase new TGV tickets, at a cost of 124 Euro, in order to avoid missing the connection again.Prpspective Eurostar customers - please consider the actual required connection time for this journey, which should have been at least 2 hours, given the need to check in for Eurostar and the lengthy queues and border checks etc. Do not buy tickets from Eurostar for onward conmnections - they don't leave enough time and it's not possible to amend 1 leg of the journey independent of the whole.I have complained to Eurostar twice so far via their online form, but no response to date, not even an acknowledgement.

Visited Paris with my partner in May and we took the Eurostar from Kings across/ St Pancras to Gare De Nord.The whole booking/checking in process was quick and smooth and the staff members at the station were very friendly and accommodating. Once through the check in/security there is limited options for food and drink such as Prett or a coffee shop however there is a small duty free store.The journey itself was quick, smooth and fine, however the seating on the train is a pain if your allocated a table for four people as the leg room underneath is very small and my partner had to sit sideways due to the guy opposite her stretching his legs out to underneath our chair! The only other issue aswell is that I feel more staff could be present at the arrival destination as Paris De Nord is notorious for scams, thefts and your unwanted individuals being around and it can be quite intimidating, especially when not know where to go or who to.I do recommend using these, and Eurostar please re open at Ebbsfleet or Ashford!!

Last minute train cancellation with no alternatives leaving us stranded and incurring significant extra cost and inconvenience Tried to process refund for the train they cancelled but this wouldn’t go through and no one available to speak to Shambles

We took the Eurostar for the first time as a family, the adventure was great. Especially when we returned to France. Our pick-up from St Pancras station by Maud was great. Many thanks to you Madam. She was able to resolve our problem with kindness and kindness. Train on time, journey without problems.
Boarding in Brussels Midi is a challenge. Difficult to reach by car. Waiting area too small. Better find another station. Train was fine because it was too late, Brussels airport strike.

Train from Paris to London was on time. Long lines for check in and immigration but moved along well. I would not recommend arriving earlier than the latest suggested time. They have you wait to go through immigration anyway and then wait again in a crowded boarding area. The Standard Premier seats were well worth the upgrade--comfy seats and decent meal option with drink. Once on board, very smooth and pleasant journey and would recommend.

What a shambles Eurostar has become. Massive queues, so 2 hours check-in. Departure pen, like a refugee camp, with insufficient seats. Seats on the train misaligned with the windows...so luck-of-the-draw whether you can see anything at all. Nowhere to sit in the "buffet" car. 50 euros extra pp, if you get through the queues in time, and there's space on the earlier train. Once was enough for me...a great engineering triumph, ruined by incompetent management, contemptuous of its customers.

I traveled practically every week on business to Paris from Ashford close to home. I stopped during the pandemic and now Ashford like Ebbsfleet are probably definitely closed. Since the pandemic and the Ashford closure I have taken Eurostar ponly twice using the thousands of points I have accumulated over the years. My Carte Blanche was soon cancelled and the travelling experience of waiting for both the delayed trains at Gare du Nord and St.  Pancras has been awful in cramped waiting room.  I now prefer Easy Jet from Gatwick which I'd much cheaper or take the car!
Always enjoyed Eurostar before the pandemic but noticed that the café onboard now pathetic. Only instant coffee and if you want to by water it’s in tiny one use cans. A complete rip off.

Simply awful experience. With Ashford inexplicably close due to Covid!!! All passengers who would have used Ashford have to go to London and then the train goes back through Ashford. Absolutely crazy. The result is lots of additional time added to the journey, large queues in London and an altogether stressful time getting on board

I am a frequent traveller on Eurostar. It used to be really good, but now I experience problems with about 1 train in 2. My last trip back from Paris was a bad one. Train was shown as on time.  Huge queue for immigration, as usual, but went through OK. Train still shown as on time, but the departure time came and went with no announcement.  A large crowd gathered around the boarding area in the heat. But still no boarding and still no announcement. Then finally they announce  a "small" delay and boarding in a few minutes, which turned about to be twenty minutes. Then a mad scramble to get on the train, since everyone's seat had been cancelled and it was now free seating.  The situation was very badly handled and the absence of information caused physical distress to older passengers who  stood waiting  in the heat for forty minutes to try to board first and get seats near their families. Train finally arrived over an hour late in London. A few days later I got a message inviting me to apply for compensation  but the Eurostar system won't recognise the ticket number they gave me in the very same email inviting me to ask for compensation. Their call centre is unreachable and they don't respond to requests for help from their online forms.  All in all, it is a company that needs new management and a sense of customers service.

We loved our trip from Paris to London on the Eurostar!  No hassle at all.  Took the 10:13 train, which left at 10:13 on a Tuesday morning in July.  UK customs had its own line out of Gare du Nord, we were in the line for USA passports.  Ran into no delay with our paperwork or bags.  Bought the Standard Premiere vs. Business Premiere tickets on recommendation from Trip Advisor posters and it was the perfect choice!  Eurostar kept us posted about departure information on their mobile app. We arrived at the station 80 minutes before departure.The seats were more like first class airline seats with a table to work and eat on.  Brought our own coffee and had more on the train.  Really pretty trip - we saw beautiful farms and country side along the way.  Our train was full - we were able to stow our luggage in our train car (we even had a very large suitcase).  We arrived at St. Pancras, in downtown London, just a few minutes early.  Had heard how horrible the crowds were at both CDG and Heathrow, we had such a smooth and easy crossing.  So grateful!  Highly recommended and we'll definitely ride with Eurostar again.

I was really worried after reading all the bad reviews, but I have to admit I was surprised how quick and smooth it went. There was a line for a few trains from London St Pancras to different locations, but nothing too crazy, it was pretty much the same as in the pre pandemic times. It has litteraly taken us half an hour to go through luggage and passport control. The only difference is that there was way more staff than I remember from previous years.

We took the Eurostar from London Pacreas Station to Paris-Gare du Nord.  There was a line that formed when we arrived ~ 1 hr. before departure time. The line was orderly and the the check-in took quite some time as it was a slow process. Make sure you allow enough time.  After checking in with your boarding passes, there is another line for checking your Covid vaccine status and finally another line to check and stamp your passport before heading up the elevator to the Eurostar Train.  You may purchase food at the stands there as well as use the restrooms before boarding.  They are absolutely on time in departure and seats are reserved when you purchase your tickets online.  The train ride was very smooth and quick. Before we knew it, we had arrived in Paris- a few minutes before our scheduled time.  Great way to get from London to Paris in less than 2 1/2 hours. Oh, also, there is a time change of one hour ahead in Paris, so make sure you make a note of that before boarding the Eurostar.  Worth the ride!  Also, Eurostar was also very helpful in refunding us the tickets we purchased pre-pandemic in 2020 when we were unable to go.

Used to travel on Eurostar all the time before the pandemic - it was marvelous then.. but now -  we wont be bothering again.  Hughly expesive return trip from Lille to St Pancras (we live 50% of time in France) for a meeting we needed to attend in London...  as Calais Frethun is now closed 'for the foreseeable future' - Calais was great for us as the car park is free and it is much closer to our house.. but thats an aside. The 'lounge' in Lille Europe is a disgrace. There is nothing there at all. no bar, no shops - nothing . A vending machine if you want some crap - but other that that - nothing. On our return from st Pancras the waiting 'lounge' was packed to capacity - standing room only after a 40 minute delay to our train. Bar staff at St Pancras were surley and uninterested . It was chaos, hot and frankly not worth it. £595 for two return. Standard class. A disgrace. The trians in both directions were also packed. We'll be using Eurotunnel from here on in - sadly. Eurostar is not as convenient as they make it sound , its totally inflexible (Eurotunnel is VERY flexible ) and the whole experience is simply not worth the money. I rather sit in my airconditioned car and drive to France than go through the meyhem that is Eurostar again.
Honestly you should just fly. They are rude and expensive. I really regret not flying. They need more trains, their booking system is awful. Really, do yourself a favor and book a plane ticket.

We took the 7:01 train from St Pancras to Paris on Monday 8th August. As this was my first time on the Eurostar I was a little anxious about travelling after reading some of the terrible reviews. I have to say though that our outward journey couldn’t have gone any more smoothly.We arrived at St Pancras before the recommended 90 minutes (around 1 hr 45 mins before) and the check in had already opened. The staff were polite and there were no queues for ticket checks or security, which meant that we were through security and in the departure area within 5 minutes of arriving. The train left for Paris on time and all was well!Our journey coming back from Gare du Nord was also good overall. We queued for around 30 minutes when we arrived at the station and then were told that the 9:12 train we were due to travel on was delayed, so they were putting us on the delayed 7:43 train, which arrived slightly after 9:00.Because we had been asked to go on a different train, us (and many other passengers) no longer had a seat allocation and were told to sit in any available seat.This resulted in chaos with people rushing to get on the train and then blocking the l aisles whilst they found space for their luggage and a seat.Although it was a little stressful It wasn’t a massive inconvenience and we arrived back at St Pancras slightly earlier than we would have on the 9:12 train. Overall we had a really good experience on the Eurostar.

Can’t fault the train journey itself but it’s completely let down by the organisation at St. Pancras which is best described as a shambles. Queues are to be expected but there is completely inadequate signage, unhelpful, stressed members of staff (at one point a crowd of passengers were shouted at because they were waiting in the wrong place - the exact place  another staff member told them to wait). Passengers were being turned away having queued for ages and reached the front but the random queue they’d joined was for a different train. We used the train to avoid the problems being reported at airports. What a mistake that was! On the plus side, the return journey from Gare du Nord was the complete opposite. A slight delay but we were kept updated, signage was clear and staff helpful!

Never book directly with Eurostar but always via NS International. Tickets can then still be changed if, as in our case, the planned outward journey is cancelled. Eurostar is completely inaccessible. Phone is not answered, emails are not responded to and rebooking via the site/app is not possible. Now I was forced to buy a plane ticket for the outward journey. Fingers crossed that the return journey will continue and that we will receive money back for the outward journey. Suspect not.

Took the Eurostar from London to Paris in the early morning - it was absolutely packed. The security lines moved fairly quickly, but the lounge was insanity. No where to sit, many people standing, can barely get past anyone. The staff, especially with security, is BEYOND rude and disrespectful. I understand they may be overwhelmed, but the way they spoke and yelled at every person was disgusting. I am hearing impaired (100% deaf actually) and couldn’t hear what one staff member was saying to me - I spoke up and nicely said I am hearing impaired, and she gave me a disgusting attitude over it and purposely tried to make things harder and more difficult for me. She tried to back-talk me and would give the most dirty looks. She made this first-time experience miserable for me, causing me to feel embarrassed and very upset. She should be ashamed of herself. I’ve never had such an awful experience with customer service and I highly doubt they were trained to be incredibly aggressive and rude. The security staff needs major training and learn how to have patience. Many of the travelers are new to this system, while I’m sure many others have done it before, yet they were extremely rude to everyone. I will never use this company again.
