There is a first time for everything, and sadly this was the worst experience for something I was excited for and doing for the first time. Disability discrimination at its finest!
I don’t know if I should laugh or cry. What a mess. Paris to London. Complete fail lol you couldn’t make it up lol miraculously I got back to London. Brilliant outcome!

Stations out of control. Queues out of the station. A holding pen system used with no sign posting at all. Confusion reigns and violence and sharp elbows help you make progress in the queue. Truly awful.

train cancelled 2 hours before departure , no explanations, , holidays ruined,  we cant contact anyone, refund is impossible as it says as it says refund can only be made if the train is confirmed cancelled !!!!!!!!!! useless, eurostar, never again, , anyone and everyone just take a plane and avoid eurostar

Eurostar has lost some of the excellent features which used to make it a desirable cross-channel experience. First the check in time has increased, almost doubled - without telling us; I printed tickets 5 months earlier - lucky I checked!The lounge is massively overcrowded, people sitting on the floor etc, toilets dirty. Queue control is now a shambles, with false announcements and people walking around shouting. Hold up was NOT French passports but British (should I write to PrettiP?) Covid checks were nominal.Began to get that "cattletruck" feeling which was why we left airlines.

We booked the Eurostar as a group of 8. (4 adults, 4 children - 14, 12, 6 & 2). The trip was from London St Pancras to Marne-La-Valle (Disneyland Paris) direct. We booked Standard Premier and chose our seats months before travel.We booked the trip around 6 months before travel - this was important as the prices were rising almost every few days. We paid more than what we could have, but almost half of what it would have been had we left it until we paid the holiday off. The station in London was crammed and really busy. There was no real direction and there were queues for about 4 trains all mixed in together with no advice or direction apart from when you got to the front of the queue you were asked what train you were on - if it was the wrong one, you were sent out to queue again. This was real bad in my opinion especially as one of the group has accessibility needs - while there are services for this, it wouldn't have worked with our group - although I am not exactly sure what services they provide for accessibility.The journey was great though. Once through check in, we were kept informed. The train was on time, the seats we chose were booked correctly. The snack they provided helped get through the day. It didn't seem like 2 1/2 hours and it was a nice start to the holiday. (Same as usual, this was our 3rd Eurostar to Disney, and always good service!) The toilet however was showing as engaged the whole trip and when we were about to stop, one of the staff forced the door and there was no-one inside, so this was a slight negative as the kids had to walk through 2 carriages to use the bathroom.The return journey was the same for the travelling - top notch! (And the toilet was working fine this time too!) The station in Paris was much calmer and no massive queues so was much better on the return.If not for the masses of people (I don't know why they don't open the other stations in the UK) this would have been 5 stars.

Total disorganisation. Massive, massive queue. No sufficient signage. Very confusing. Standing up for a long time not really knowing what’s happening. Been asked to queue up again as this queue was for earlier train. Fed up with lack of organisation.

The ride is smooth and peaceful.  If only the operators realized that there are modern systems and processes in place to substitute their archaic boarding procedures, the experience could be so much better.  Standing in line for hours is a nightmare. Both trains left considerably late. The purpose of saving time by not flying is throughly defeated.  Will NEVER ride again and will tell anyone thinking about it to avoid it at all costs.

Terribly rude staff at St. Pancras International, yelling and screaming at people. It was very busy, staff were obviously overwhelmed and had no idea of crowd management. People were sent outside to wait for check-in. I was among them. At some point, after waiting outside for quite long, a staff member said we could come into the building. When I was there, another staff member started shouting at me, asking what I was doing there and seriously wanted me to go back outside and to the end of the queue! At that point some other passengers came to my rescue and said I had actually been waiting outside. The staff member then proceeded to yell and scream at others and I could finally get in line for check-in……Incredible how unprofessional the Eurostar staff are at St. Pancras. Unacceptable behaviour! They were not at all helpful. I can’t imagine they learn this kind of aggressive and intimidating behaviour during their training. It was my first time using the Eurostar. I thought I might give it a try. Never again! I might as well wait in queues at airports. Airport staff are always courteous.

We opted for standard seats on the Paris to London stretch.  Totally comfortable for the two and a half hour journey.   Check in and customs went like clockwork.  Real advantage in entering the UK prior to boarding so when you arrive there is literally nothing to do but hop off.  A couple of tips:Book your trip as as early as possible to lock in a cheap ticket.  If you have big bags get to the front of the boarding queue to make sure there is room to store your bags in the luggage area in your carriage.Basic snacks and drinks are available for sale in the cafe carriage.

So we traveled on the Eurostar we caught the 0600 from st pancras on Monday the 25 July I keep hearing about Brexit and long queues but in my experience it was the people in charge of getting you through the doors at the beginning they called only 0600 then put the later travelers in a different queue only to then mix you all up we then ended up having to be hurried through by some very helpful lady from the french side of the boarder control in my view those in charge of the doors need only 1 person in charge what I saw they all wanted to be in charge and cause chaos the French how ever more organized by far the train itself was amazing Eurostar please sort those sub contractors out

This service seems to have been designed 20 years ago and hasn’t been updated. It probably works quite well if only 4 people travel on each train. Our train broke down and then returned to London. From the moment it stopped until about 14 hours later when we arrived in Paris, nobody in the company was equipped to help anyone. There was minimal communication about what to do, confusion about queues, staff totally overwhelmed, no ownership from the company in helping hundreds of travellers with ruined travel plans. The website and app crashed and is not fit for purpose. The service needs a complete overhaul top to bottom. Where is the plan when things go wrong, who is in charge, why are there are only about 3 people at the station to help, why are those people not trained in what to do? The terminal building itself is too small, too hot and ill equipped. The customer service line does not appear to take calls. The shame of it is that we, like many, wanted to try Eurostar as an alternative “green” option to flying. I doubt anyone who travelled when we did (12th July) would bother again….it isn’t worth the pain. I’m nearly £1,000 out of pocket due to rebooking travel and hotels and attempting to get my money back through insurance. My refund request from Eurostar might come through after 28 days! A joke of a service, but it isn’t funny really.
Arrogant shop. Booked train canceled due to strikes, promised exchange is boycotted by the website, promised refund not received, communication refused. Sometimes you just want legal insurance.

Went business so skipped the absolutely enormous queues in London (it was chaos) that would put an airport to shame. Business lounge over crowded, lack of seating and under stocked. Train was smooth. Terrible food. Warm wine and champagne (due to 15 min delay apparently). I’d love to see Raymond I Blanc giving it the thumbs up Back from Paris to London, we were delayed 5 hours. No food other than peanuts and snacks in the lounge. At least there was AC, economy passengers had to wait in a stuffy hot hall on the ground for 5 hours. Train itself was over 3 hours back. Food was pretty poor again, dessert was three tasteless peaches. Inspired by Raymond Blanc, give me a break. Train arrived into London 2:30am. Online claims push you to a voucher, you can get a cash refund. We will never ever travel Eurostar again.

Our train was canceled a few days before our trip and when we tried to exchange it none of the options they gave us worked. We tried to contact eurostar via Twitter, email, their website, phone and nothing. They won't take responsibility for anything and for all of the trouble they costed our trip.

Our train from brussels to london was delayed 97 minutes. we then got an email about compensation in which they gave us a 9 euro voucher. I then emailed customer support as we missed our bus back because of this delay and im not planning on using the eurostar anytime soon. Never got a reply. terrbible train service and terrible customer service
What an horrible experience ! My train arrived 3 hours late and the queue was 1.5 hours if you arrived very early. A snail would have been quicker

Use the Eurostar regularly but first time to Brussels. Travelled out on the so called hottest day ever with delays and cancellations galore. Train was packed but everything from check in to passport and boarding was excellent. Return journey the same in a comfortable environment

I took a Eurostar train from London to Paris in the evening, taking advantage of bargain fares thanks to the Eurail pass I had purchased before going on my Europe trip. My experience was (as the Brits say) brilliant, and per les français, super ! Checking in was hectic with the intense summer crowds, and I often felt claustrophobic while going through security and passport control (just SO many people!). However, the staff on hand were wonderful and gave me decent assistance as a disabled customer. You go through customs in London in order to enter the Schengen area, which means no immigration or security procedures once you arrive in Paris. The company really has it all sorted out. They were generous enough to grant me complimentary access to the business lounge to wait for my train, and the snacks and atmosphere there is amazing. If you obtain access, use it!The train itself arrived on time and left on time. Since I was traveling in my electric wheelchair, the disability assistance received was above average for already-low European standards. They were able to efficiently accommodate me within an hour’s notice. The interior of each car is clean, modern-looking, and felt smooth while on the tracks. Dinner service is free for all passengers, and my chicken was super scrumptious. You had a choice between two meals, if I recall correctly, plus a vegetarian option.I will enthusiastically pick Eurostar again on my next European journey in the future. Their level of service and operation is among the best on the continent. Thank you et merci !

I think this is the only way to travel from London to Paris....so quick, so easy, no cancelled flights or airports to deal with.  Nice to have customs all taken care of right before you board and then in Paris you just get off the train and go right into the city.   Our seats were comfortable, the cars very clean, charging ports for devices...took just about 2 hours and 15 minutes and this train MOVES...like around 160 mph.  I looked it up and found out you are 75 meters below sea level when traveling through the Channel Tunnel.The only negative I have is the waiting area before you board...very, very crowded and not nearly enough seats while you wait to board your train....but hey, much better than going through airport security and waiting at some crowded gate for a plane.We will definitely take this train again.

We had a great experience at Eurostar in London. The service was superb and a man named Mo was extremely understanding and helpful. He aided us with kindness and respect, and quickly resolved all of our queries. We will definitely be using Eurostar London again.

Taking the 4hr train from Rotterdam to London sounded more preferable than flying. The check-in/passport  control went smoothly. The train was clean and comfortable but in Brussels we had to change trains due to technical issues. The transfer was smooth (though inconvenient). Due to a passenger health emergency, we also had to make a stop in Ashford so we were about an hour late. Overall not bad except plan some leeway for the occasional delays.

I travel by plane regularly and this time I wanted to take the train to England. I was very disappointed with boarding at Gare du Nord. Flow management sucks. I understand that in this confined space it is not easy but then there should be more competent staff to help customers. It's always difficult to understand how large companies like Eurostar, run by high-level executives, are able to deliver such a poor quality customer experience. Is this a resignation or simply a lack of interest in passengers? Otherwise the train is great.
Long lines, overcrowded stations. We will never use Eurostar again, flying to Paris is a better, cheaper experience.

I actually can’t even be bothered to go into why I wouldn’t use this service again.Flying to France is much quicker, cheaper and actually more comfortable, and that’s how I will travel to France in the future. I will never use Eurostar again,

Eurostar provides a great opportunity to connect into Paris and France however the level of service is still questionable after all these years of operation.Regional airlines provide just as good connectivity and a competitive price.The facilities and experience at Gare du Nord are ok but could be better. St Pancras is an embarrassment with station architecture seriously constraining movement, amenity and comfort. Such a shame as the rest of St Pancras is amazing.Surely the need to socially distant provides an incentive to improve these facilities - why not use more space at the front of the station for processing and open up the vault for more retail and seats.Will think twice before coming again.

I love the Eurostar and I think it is such a useful service. However, recently on trying to travel from Brussels to London I was refused entry because of having a bike in a bike bag. I was told this had to do with Covid although neither I nor the staff could understand how bikes were now linked with Covid restrictions. I was then also told that the new post-Covid prohibition on bikes was clearly laid out on the website. This is true if by “clearly laid out” one means buried deep within the website if one follows 4 links and then ignores the “Bikes on Board” logo and reads the fine print where they tell you bikes are welcome but they must be kiddie bikes. Given bikes are allowed on the TGV and BE train services, this seems to be an arbitrary rule and one that really should be more prominent when booking. Belgium and France are after all particularly well known for their love of cycling. Needless to say insult was added to injury with no offer of help, no alternatives and no refund. As a protection against future arbitrary rules emerging I would from now on always recommend travel insurance when using the Eurostar.
Queues and more queues, delayed trains and everyone packed in like sardines. A dreadful experience made worse by only seating in the waiting area for less than half the people.

This is a review of two halves.Onboard the trains, on both outward and return journeys, the trains and staff were superb. Plenty of room for baggage, staff friendly and helpful, both journeys left and arrived on time. Exactly what you want.St Pancras check-in was atrocious with queues snaking the full length of the station. Eurostar advised arrive 90mins before departure and we did that, and we were finally processed just in time for boarding.Eurostar blamed Covid checks and extra security as the reasons for the delay. The Covid check consisted on someone asking your destination. If it was France (or NL), you provided Covid vax status. If it was Belgium you were waived through. However this check was done in-line and unless you didn;t have the paperwork, there was no delay. I think the delays were due to the passport checks and the fact that not all security and check-in desks were open. We didn't have the same delay in Brussels. I suspect UK operations can no longer handle the volume of passengers and it is slowly eroding the benefits of train travel vs,. air travel.Shame really, as it was a bad start to a great trip.

I was on the 10.22am train from London to Paris on Tuesday 12 July 2022. Half way through the journey the Train broke down with no electricity or air con.Eurostar then had to tow the train all the way back to St Pancras.Urgently had to rebook 7.00pm train, that was was also delayed. Now it’s after 1am in Paris and I am walking the streets alone trying to find my air B and B accomodation. F””” you Eurostar.

Eurostar delay due to understaffing caused me to miss my following train from Belgium which was a first class ICE to Germany, instead I had to take a Thalys train that was overcrowded (due to everyone missing the ICE) and had to stand 4 hours with my little children, Eurostar left with a delay of 55mins, of course because 60mins means refunds. Yet due to Eurostar incompetence I was delayed by 3 hours in total to arrive at my final destination. Eurostar had only 2 counters out of 8 open during checking and the queues went around St Pancras station. Last time me and my family will take a Eurostar.

Very dirty. Passport queue management, chaotic check-in and security. Very bad experience. Very low quality business class seat, sharing a table with other passengers, with hardly any space, and uncomfortable without any option to recline the seat.

Recently we had a trip to Paris using Eurostar on the way from London to Paris we were delayed a couple of hours. Coming from Paris to London we were delayed 7 hours. We spent money on breakfast and lunch.  We were told we would have a partial refund by email. We had two emails just offering evouchers. Because we didn’t realise we could then still have a refund we clicked for evouchers which are of no use to us whatever. I have tried repeatedly requested a cash refund but this is not possible. I feel this company is so very disorganised and extremely unfair and would never ever use this train company again.

I have travelled all around the world and stayed at Airbnb which are great but if you like to cook often have blunt knives. Consequently I carry in my suitcase a pocket knife to cook with. Sticking my knife in the hold on planes has never been a problem but it is to travel on Eurostar. As you can gain access to the knife on the train it is not allowed the customs guy said in Brussels and that  isn’t the case on a plane. So if you’re aim is to attack people with a pocket knife do so on the normal train service Eurostar. I lost a knife which had huge sentimental value. As far as the train service is concerned it’s Ryan Air with British Airways prices and was an hour late leaving Brussels.

From Rotterdam to London very relaxed, no long queues for passports and check-in. No food except from a vending machine after check-in so keep an eye on that. From London to Rotterdam it is very busy. Long line and 2 small eateries that are of course very busy. The journey itself is too cramped and noisy in 2nd class. The class above (premium standard) is spacious and quiet. Wonderful travelling. The major disadvantage is that the WiFi continuously dropped out. I will use Eurostar again next time, but at least premium standard.

Very expensive business class trip from Paris to uk.  At the last minute Eurostar split our group up they had changed trains, many other said the the same, passengers swapped seats about themselves, so why couldn’t Eurostar have done the same? The food was vile and the Far Eastern waitresses rude.  However saving the day was the purser Sebastian, what a credit to the company he is, don’t lose him whatever you do.  He was the only good thing about the journey.

BEWARE! Worst company ever!!!! They have a habit of Canceling  trains with little to no notice. Then No one at the company  will respond to calls, messages,Emails nor chat. The only way to get in touch with them, especially, when you’re in a panic to either exchange your ticket from a train that’s been canceled to one that isn’t or get a refund, is by way of a  DM via twitter. Really people?!!!! After trying all of the above, I finally received a response  and got a refund 2 days before my European trip was to begin. My first leg of my trip was to arrive in Paris via London by way of Eurostar. . . Nope! Now what?? Thank goodness for British Airways coming to the rescue that same day of the mass train cancellations  which was only 4 days before my trip was to begin. Otherwise, the trip that I have been planning for two years would have been totally wrecked.

Trip from London was fine.However chaotic onParis.Check in was poor.Train is late but no warning.Gaye has changed.Onlu found this out by askingToilets down a long staircase.I cannot do this with a bad back.Not enough seating and sitting on the floor.No more train trips,just going by car

The service I received from this company It's terrible!! The worst service of all my life!! I thought I was dealing with a serious company!!! And I was wrong!! Eurostar have just cancelled my train and it's too late to book any flights instead, and there are no alternative trains offered by Eurostar on the day I was intending to travel.

A very useful service so as to avoid flying. BUT, it should be so much better. Check in is disorganised and customs facilities poor. Customer service is non existent and it is impossible to contact anyone.Our return train was cancelled and whilst it gave an option to rebook, get a voucher or ask for a refund, the website crashed. Also the phone lines do not work. Both of these appear to be known and ongoing. Only option was to rebook and attempt to request a refund. This appears to be pending but did not give to the option to specify which part of the journey. We’re not sure that our tickets would be valid until we actually checked in. A good competitor is required to give Eurostar incentive to improve.

Now I can't review Eurostar completely as I haven't used the service, but below is my journey from booking, to trying and being denied a refund. I booked a last minute journey to Paris over the Christmas period. It was expensive but I can't fault them for that due to the time of year (roughly £300 for the return journey). The day before my outbound journey, a Saturday, France declared no British tourists due to COVID levels in the UK, just one of those things that can't be helped. Since it was over the weekend, Eurostars call centre wasn't open and so I was unsure whether it was best to cancel the journey at my end, and let it appear as if I'd missed the train and call them Monday. I'll also note that the outbound train was still running, but the return train had been cancelled already by Eurostar. I decided to cancel the outbound train myself and while going through the process online, was only given the option for a voucher. I thought that's fine, I'll call on Monday and explain the situation and hopefully they'll be understanding. Maybe Eurostar would have been, but I could not for the life of me get through. No call queue, at all, just an automated message that would say they're busy and hang up. I kept trying every few hours, everyday for about a week until I tried Eurostars online enquiry form. I didn't get a response from them until 2 weeks after saying they're busy and will extend the vouchers (which actually was a sooner expiry date than given initially) and if I still wanted my request looking into, to click a button within the email they sent. Obviously I did which took me to a standard "we will look into it and contact you" page on their website. I'd lost faith in Eurostars online presence and proceeded to try calling again. Now, if I were reading this I'd find it hard to believe, but fast forward 5 months to May, after weeks and weeks, hours upon hours of just trying to speak to a real human I finally did! I couldn't believe it as I'd started to think there were no customer facing personnel at Eurostar. Anyway I explained the situation, and the lady on the line was very nice and empathetic so thank you Rachael. She ultimately couldn't do anything herself which was fine and passed my case onto the refund department. A week later Rachael emails me saying since I cancelled the initial journey myself they can't provide a refund (despite explaining it was my only option when cancelling), and since the return journey they cancelled was after the 22nd Dec 2021 (my return was booked for the 23rd), that couldn't give a refund for that. I'll admit I've not read the Ts&C's myself, but that last part seemed suspiciously coincidental to me.I'm left exhausted of the situation and have strong doubts I'll ever see a refund but I will hopefully update in the future.
Fast and Clean! Boarding is a little daunting because they use the festival seating methods. It's very fast, very clean and it gets you to your destination.

Delayed for some reason. Absolutely NO information from staff, no announcements and absolutely no help at the information desk. The only updates we got was when the delay changed from 15 to 30 mins then to 45 mins and so on.The next announcement was when the train arrived. Until, that is, when the buffet bars ran out of drinks and snacks.
Dreadful. Appalling service. Slow, inefficient and arrogant staff. Will not use again. Very expensive too. Cannot recommend.
2h long queues, extremely overpriced, rude customer service. I can’t wait for a competitor to start operating on the London-Paris line.

Travelled by Eurostar to Amsterdam, no complaints about our departure point of St Pancras.But our departure back to London was horrendous, the facilities at the Eurostar terminal in Amsterdam was like a cattle shed, no facilities to buy or eat and only one toilet in the Gents and Ladies. This experience spoilt an otherwise great journey back home.

Overall, we had a pleasant experience going on the Eurostar. The trip from London to Disney was easy and comfortable. However, the Eurostar station was overcrowded though and didn't have enough seats nor places to eat to accomodate everyone within the terminal. We got on the the train with no issues and the staff on the way to Disney were very friendly. The experience on the way back was good as well although the staff on train were nowhere to be seen and the officer in passport control was extremely rude. He yelled at me and didn't even look at us to verify our identity for passport. Security at Lille Eurostar was very poor. It felt like that London was taking safety and security more seriously whereas Lille staff couldn't be bothered. I did feel that using Eurostar was much easier than flying and going through an airport. It's a shame that Eurostar doesn't provide a service from Disneyland directly to St Pancras as it would avoid the stress of changing trains with so little time to get to the connecting train in Lille.

As a disabled customer, I can honestly say that me and my family have never had such a worse experience, let alone the way we got treated! Firstly, getting through to them is a nightmare trying to book the tickets and organising assistance at the train station took literally an two hours to speak to someone, then when we got there, that was a different story all together! Secondly, we asked where the gate was to the platform, and majority of the staff there didn’t know what they were doing! There was one staff member who was extremely rude to my mum, then another who was unsure of where the gate actually was, so this made the experience even more confusing! Thirdly, when we finally got to the security area, it was even more chaos! The staff at the Passport area thought that a man who’ve we’ve never met before was with part of our family, when it was just me, my mum and my auntie. They told us to go and stop how many times I couldn’t even count, to one point where I got really fed up and just wanted to look in Duty Free! Finally once we got to the waiting area to board, me and my family were told to wait there for assistance and somebody would come and get the pieces of luggage and help us and because it didn’t happen, me and my family had to put on the pieces of luggage on ourselves… until a nice man helped us to carry the luggage on the train for us. However, we nearly missed the train, because of this and we were the last to board, surely if we had assistance we would have avoided all this hassle? I’d honestly say that at the Paris station, they were more on board with helping us out! Meanwhile, on the way back was so much easier and it was a completely different story, we managed to get some assistance at Paris Gare De Nord station, who were really on board with helping us out, even though we’d waited for two hours, but honestly I can say, that they were more on board with helping us out! My family then phoned Eurostar about our experience with the assistance with Eurostar to which the lady said “They were probably just having a busy day”. The moral of this story is don’t bother travelling with Eurostar if your planning to go to Paris as a disabled customer! To be honest, your rather much better of flying!

I wrote a very long detailed report on my Eurostar experience to the Exec office. To be fair, the lady who responded replied in detail to every point and it’s clear that not everything is Eurostar’s fault. However, a lot of it is, and the execs at Eurostar need to go undercover to some of their terminals and see exactly how bad things are…I travelled from St Pancras to Amsterdam. I’d not used Eurostar for several years and recall the unpleasant, overcrowded and poor facilities of the terminal. I’d high hopes that after all that time that it would be vastly improved. Well, no it wasn’t … in fact if anything it was worseThe first experience which the majority of reviewers on here comment on is the horrendously rude and unprofessional security staff. I’ve been advised these are contracted out so I’d suggest Eurostar urgently review the contract of the company responsible. Staff do nothing to help … trays were building up after the scanner and a male member of staff, rather than proactively clear the trays just started yelling at customers. In general all the staff on the baggage area were rude and had clearly had no customer service training at all. The French border control … actually ok, though the customs guy spent more time chatting to his mate.Next the worst bit. The waiting area. No where near enough seating for the number of customers. Eurostar tried to tell me this was due to a delayed train …that didn’t help, but there’s still not enough seats for the number of trains due to depart. The whole area was dirty and spillages not being cleaned up (this apparently due to a cleaners strike - if this was the case, Eurostar should have got someone in). Toilets … vile. Two restaurant/coffee outlets woefully inadequate for the number of customers and both struggling to deal with the amount of people. Queues were massive for both adding to the general chaos of the waiting room. The one ‘shop’ is a tiny duty free outlet with very little on offer yet still had five staff mostly standing about chatting….Train boarding wasn’t too bad and the tiny breakfast was served efficiently … but it really was tiny. As the journey time was over four hours, I’d assumed you’d also be served the main meal. You aren’t. The journey was then delayed by an hour yet no further refreshments were offered - I was told by the exec office that they do serve extra refreshments in this instance if any are left - there were plenty left yet not even extra water was offeredWe just went over the hour needed to get compensation. This is a meagre 25% of the cost of that leg of the journey … the email I received only offered the option of a voucher or Eurostar points even though cash refunds are available (my return journey was also delayed and that time I did get the offer of a cash refund)Unlike other reviewers, the refund form did work for me and the tiny amount of cash was credited my account within two days. I’m still waiting for an explanation as to why no cash refund offer was available for the outward journeyComing back was hideous … no border force staff at Amsterdam so whole train had to disembark at Brussels. Again not Eurostar’s fault but they do little to make the process as painless as possibleStaff on the train were mostly pleasant, but service standard have clearly dropped along with meal quality since my last journeySenior staff and execs need to get off their backsides and start doing something … getting cheap contractors in clearly isn’t working as their staff are dreadful and are costing you revenue as so many never travel with you againAlas, it’s back to flying for me next time

Due to British Airways canceling our flight from Brussels to London with only 6 hours notice, we had to arrange for train transportation to make our connection from London to Boston later in the day. We had taken several trains throughout Europe for the previous 10 days without issue, and were feeling confident. When I first checked for the tickets online about three hours in advance of the departure time, the price was 184 euro each. After speaking on the phone with BA and realizing they had no intention of actually helping me reschedule our flight, I ordered the tickets online about 45 minutes advance of the train departure. Within those two hours, the ticket price had risen by €50 each. My husband and I arrived at the train station about 25 minutes early for the train, looked at the screen to see which track it was running on, and saw a notification that the boarding had closed. We went to customer service to see if they could help us and there was an angry line of disgruntled customers demanding to be let on the train. The employees were yelling at the customers that boarding had closed and that they would be arrested if they did not obey. It was a scary scene to an American traveler, for sure. We were directed in an extremely gruff fashion to stand in a different queue as we were somehow in the wrong for purchasing these train tickets. After waiting our turn, we were told we would be put on the next train 4 hours later, but that we would have to pay €109 for a change fee since “missing” the train was our fault. I politely explained to the customer service agent with the very tiny mustache at the very center of his upper lip that we were actually 25 minutes early for the train and that the Eurostar website says that changes are always free. He sneered at me and told me that I should go online and try to change the tickets myself then. I explained that I had no confidence in the website after this experience and that he could go ahead and charge the money, but I felt like that’s what the whole purpose of shutting down the boarding to the train was all about. Basically, this train company is scamming people by capitalizing upon the fact that airlines continue canceling flights, and they are doing it in an extremely aggressive, threatening, rude and downright nasty manner. Next time I return to Europe I will stick with the train companies like Thalys and TVG INOUI who sometimes experienced delays but always provided adequate customer service.

Excellent connection between Amsterdam and London. First time to London with the Eurostar. Great experience. The train left Amsterdam on time and arrived in London on time. It should be stated more clearly that you have to go through a check! Including suitcase check and passport control by both the Dutch and English military police. Sufficient space for suitcases. Great alternative to a flight.

A trip from Amsterdam to London was horrendous.The person whose job it was to serve food missed the train and as a result the meal was not served until the very end of the journey .  Hot drinks were ‘not available ‘ and ‘no white wine available’ !The charging points adjacent to seats did not work and the crew were surly and rude .  Unacceptable for a return trip price of over £300.

Entering St Pancras station,  the first thing Eurostar needs to do is employ less rude staff at the security conveyor area. I was struggling to hear the woman shouting instructions at us through her mask and the loud clatter of the large plastic trays we put our cases and personal items into. I was trying to get everything into it including a heavy case to keep up and she shouted " HELLOOO" I explained that I am hard of hearing and do not shout halloo at me like that, She retorted, " YOU HEARD THAT DID'NT YOU?We were instructed to arrive 90minutes early and sat around until our train was ready.The staff on the train were just the opposite, polite and helpful, however the seats are not fit for a four hour journey. My leg had a job getting blood flow back.On our return journey from Amsterdam for the 18.47 to London on Friday 17 June 2022, we were herded into a large modern shed on platform 15b. It was a very warm evening with full sun on the platform. The air con was not working and there was only 1 urinal for the men and 1 toilet for the ladies to cater for about 3 to 4 hundred people crammed together in this hot shed with no air movement. I requested a supervisor to open a large emergency escape door to get some air movement, I explained that we are in a Covid incubator here and a health risk, but he was a jobs worth and did nothing.The odd thing is that, if they had designed the building with vented windows and roof vents and with the sea right next to the station platform, there would have been enough fresh air blowing in without the need for air con (which did not work).On boarding the train, there is no one to help with our cases on the station, we are getting to be older travellers now and the high step up to the coach is a struggle trying to lift them clear of the gap. The staff on the train were really helpful and friendly. Well done the train staff! A shame about being let down by the staff both sides of the channel !Eurostar, you need to get a grip! Us travellers will go by ferry next time!
Trip was cancelled due to a strike.Refunded within five days. Which is excellent compared to many other companies so I can't complain.Hope to travel with Eurostar one day.
Very expensive tickets, long lines, rude staff, no refunds… Extremely disappointed in this service all around and will never book with them again.

St Pancras to Rotterdam, we where due to changed at Brussels, but the train was cancelled , no information nothing on the boards , had to take local crowed train absolutely packed , got into Rotterdam 2.5 hours late , spoke to a frequent traveler he said that train is always cancelled, they refund him 50% automatically as he is a frequent traveler. I send them emails , no replies they won’t answer the phone, seems no way to get hold of them , the app just rejects refund, will not use this service again . Even the return journey was a mess , all very stressful.

Terrible service even if you book business tickets Ticket flexibility is highly restricted and you are at the mercy of strikes and delays without possibility to cancel your trip and get a refund. Never again, ever.

Like many others who have expressed their justified negativity, I had opted to do the ‘environmentally responsible’ thing and take Eurostar to Paris for a 2-day visit.My first - and LAST - such trip.First off the ridiculous price: £225 for a Standard class return. Easily comparable to or regularly cheaper than an airfare.Complete lack of seating at St Pancras; usual over-inflated prices for basic necessities such as coffee. Queues a total melee to embark.WiFi totally useless on board a very crowded train.Return through Gare du Nord considerably worse: rude staff making gibes about Brexit and deliberate routing of UK customers - inc me - through even longer queues.Security cursory, passport control totally inadequate with no access to e-gates (which I am able to use elsewhere in Europe and almost everywhere else in the world!!)1.5 hours from arrival to sitting down just prior to boarding.Pathetic. I can’t even be bothered to complain based on others’ comments re Customer Service.It may be trying to recoup cost post-pandemic but Eurostar simply don’t deserve to run this monopoly.

Overall the travel experience is fine, however if you need to get hold of anyone at Eurostar- forget it. On our return journey from Amsterdam our carriage was the only one that did not have ANY air conditioning for the entire trip back to the UK. We were advised that we could raise a refund/compensation request after 24 hour via the Eurostar website, however the form throws up and error EVERY SINGLE TIME. And when we have tried to speak with anyone, the phone lines are essentially shut down, the message tells you that they are not accepting any calls. I have reached out via the email form multiple times without any response or reply and we have even posted to them directly on facebook, with a generic response advising they are busy. So in short, Eurostar customer support is no existent.

Everything from booking your trip to travelling in is annoying.  Voucher codes they send that don't work, payment options that don't work, boarding is absolute chaos... I just hope different companies get to use the Eurotunnel soon.

The queues are extremely long at St Pancras. The staff are rude and were shouting unnecessarily at passengers. The train was late in leaving.They are blaming COVID for the delays however they have had years to sort this out. We will never use Eurostar again

Don’t bother. Queuing worse than an airport. Poor queue management. Staff shouting at everyone at every stage. Treated worse than prisoners. More time spent trapped in various queues than at airports, just dire. Avoid.

Incoherent and abrupt ground staff who use angry hand gestures rather than any decent level of the English language, and who made the whole experience worse than it already was. We became so stressed that we accidentally left one of our cases in the line and upon realising only moments later was told it was taken to lost property and we wouldn’t be able to get it back for out trip as they couldn’t get it until the next day - we then realised he had the case behind him!! On scanning our tickets, which we’d organised months earlier for our 25th anniversary, we were given new seats which were in separate cars!! We politely requested new tickets from the information desk after waiting 10 mins for her attention to be met with huffs and tuts. The scramble for the train was confused by a last minute explanation that different cars could be accessed by different travel actors on different sides of the platform. One of the worst, if not the worst travel experiences I’ve ever had.I love train travel but this has out me off using Eurostar again - next time, I’ll just fly to Paris!

Trains are clean, normally run to time, it’s just so convenient. Heart of London to heart of Paris in 2:15. I use the service several times a year and could not be happier. On the rare occasions there is an issue they resolve the issue and actually chase you to file a compensation claim!

Travelled to Disneyland at Marne-la-Vallée. Enjoyable journey on way out, very busy as school holiday but hasslefree. Return journey would have been fine except the most horrendous smell of a fish smell but the next level up. Noticed it before we got on the train as walking along platform it was coming from one of the doorways. When we got to our carriage the smell of fish prevailed wafting through from the toilet. Absolutely disgusting, it was there for the whole journey and we were sat near the toilets. Everyone was commenting on it. They obviously had some drainage issue but made for a very uncomfortable and unpleasant journey home. Have emailed Eurostar but as yet they have not bothered to reply.

Just avoid. They randomly cancelled our train last week and then provided no support. Asked us to find a way back to London from Paris. An airline can't do that. This company should be banned or should be brought under proper regulation.  Eurostar can't be trusted.

We travelled from St Pancras to Brussels on a midday Friday train and returned the following Monday afternoon. Initially, I was delighted that we were travelling with Eurostar. Having seen all the queues recently at the airports, I thought this would be a much more civilised option. However the queues at St Pancras were horrendous. They snaked round the station, then doubled back on itself. Part of the problem was advice from Eurostar to arrive 90 minutes from departure. So I guess that was what most people had done, joining the interminable queue to queue even to get into the departures hall. Station Announcements then asked people not on the next train to leave the queue, and rejoin later. It was all a bit chaotic. In Brussels for the return, things were much smoother. You clear passport control for Belgium in the U.K., and vice versa,  so at least when you arrive you are free to go. And of course no waiting  for luggage as you take it with you from the train. Once you’re on Eurostar, it’s a pleasant service, although the advertised wifi didn’t work in either direction - just be prepared to queue.

For years I have wanted to use the Eurostar, but living in Devon, this has not been practical/easy. But after flying to Faro a few months ago and enduring endless checks and queues, I decided to use Eurostar to get to Paris.Well, it was nothing like I imagined. At both St Pancras and Gare du nord, the queues were horrendous. They moved at a snail's pace, and no-one seemed interested in making things comfortable for travellers. I always imagined that Eurostar would be totally separate from the rest of the concourse, but that only happens when you are finally allowed through. In the meantime, you have to wait in both station with hordes of other rail users, in high temperatures and lack of seats. Gare du Nord is marginally worse. Why you could not progress to departures earlier or on to the platform, I fail to understand. It was just like cattle being horded! Then the train coaches are numbered with about 100 seats each. There is nothing on the outside to indicate where to enter the carriage based on your allocated seat number. So people are inside pushing past each with suitcases trying to get to their correct seat, which is generally the opposite end from where they entered.The train itself left and arrived on time, which was a bonus. The seats were comfortable and the storage was good. But the food and drink on board was virtually non-existent, and the toilet facilities were terrible!With the state of the airlines and the flying experience in general, I really thought we had made a good choice using Eurostar. What a massive mistake. I will never use this service again. Stressful and unpleasant experience. Disappointing, is a massive under statement!

Travelled return London to Amsterdam.  Queueing in London was out the door into the street, though the queue moved reasonably promptly and was well signposted.  Boarding in Amsterdam much simpler - with only one Eurostar to accommodate, not several to different destinations.Service was on time but on the European side of the Channel the train was really slow. This rolling stock is capable of going much faster than this.  Even allowing for stops in Rotterdam, Brussels and Lille, the train never really got up speed.   Why is the service not being run to reach its full potential?

More than half the Eurostars I've been on have been half an hour late or more. Once 2 hours late and I got a measly £7.50 refund! Wifi is terrible - can't even send text emails most of the time. In 4 out of 5 trains the toilets are disgusting. Twice I've had to queue for well over an hour, and particularly at Gare du Nord this can be very badly managed - once we were all stuffed on the concourse, maybe 1000 people, old people really struggling, unable to get water or go to the toilet. Also I wanted to change seat reservations (which I couldn't do online because that trip was through Interrail) and tried calling 6 times and could never get through. Last week I went on the French TGV and, in stark contrast, it was fabulous. Quiet, excellent wifi, online live tracking so you could see where you were and how fast you were going, large tables with places to put things, ample foot space. Why can't the Eurostar be like that? Plus it's so expensive compared to flying. A tragedy for climate change.

Delayed one hour in London. In a snake queue but ok. Delayed over 4 hrs in Paris. Disgusting, packed in departure hall. No information, assistance, water. Families with young children. Passengers delayed on earlier and later trains all packed in together. Earlier everyone directed up the escalator. At the top no where to go. People falling over each other and their baggage. Chaotic with no help. Went Premium but never again. Got home at 2am, at work 8am. Thank you Eurostar for ruining our only break this year and the last 2 years

Deplorable and shameful customer service whenever there is a delay!
