Clearly Eurostar doesn't care about its customers and their well-being. A shame.

Totally disappointed with Eurostar. I have tried everything to get in touch with them.My daughter has spent hours trying to get hold of them and no one answers the phones. Filled out the form on line nearly a month again and still no one as responded. Tried online chat and says please call.Eurostar is providing a shocking service and are useless to date with customer servicesHad to write a date but never been still waiting on someone to answer emails messages or anything in factUseless

It is super busy and can be overwhelming, but I would not necessarily agree with all the reviews that say you're better off to fly.  Are there TONS of people there all trying to catch their trains? Yes, but ultimately I found it to be an OK experience. If you set your expectations and understand what you're doing.  You'll be happier that way. They had many employees helping direct traffic for upcoming trains. What they are trying to accomplish is to only have people in line who are at or within 90 mins of their scheduled departure. So, you'll see the Eurostar employees at many spots in the super long line around the terminal holding signs that say "Paris 12:31" and unless you are on that train, then they tell you not to get in line. Yes, it was a huge line and ultimately they will get everyone through the line and on their train, but you will take 60-90 mins to get through it.  Security and passport lines at airports aren't any better. Really, it's UK's fault. If they would just be part of the European Union, it would make life for tourists MUCH easier. :-)

My experience has been horrible. I do not intend to use Eurostar ever again. I hope that all users do the same because it is a shame how they are treating us. More than two hours waiting in line without being able to sit down or buy drinks. (Both on the way out and back). They could now distribute bottles of water and offer a rest area. Between 45 and 60 minutes late. No explanation. On top of that, when you finally get on the train hungry and thirsty, you find that there are almost no items left in the cafeteria. A stale sandwich for £5 and on top of that they refused to charge me the menu price because there were no drinks left that I liked and I wanted tea. A shame. Pay £12 for two stale sandwiches and a tea after being on your feet for over two hours. I don't know what kind of compensation they're going to give me but if it's a Boucher they can keep it because I won't even get on another train for free.

All I can say is that this was our first time on Eurostar and we won’t be doing it again !Delayed by 30 mins leaving St Pancras as incoming train late due to an animal on the line. This we learnt from the internet……not Eurostar.Delay caused over crowding in the departure area.Return journey even worse. Delayed by 40 minutes. It was absolute chaos getting through check in. Long disorderly queues, lots of staff talking to each other but not explaining anything.EU travellers selected and allowed through first !! Then when they realised that most people were non EU they let us through the same area. What an insult ! Took approx an hour to clear check in. Air travel is far superior to this even with its current problems. Flying may have its disadvantages but definitely not as bad as this service.

Recently took the train from London to Paris. It was the same day as the big soccer game (Liverpool vs Madrid) in Paris so the train was sold out. We had a delay boarding due to the large number of riders, but the line moved quickly. The ride was comfortable, and we had plenty of room for our bags. Our porter was named Sebastian, and he took good care of us. Although we were delayed over 30 minutes leaving, the conductor made up all but 8 minutes of the delay. Arrival into Gare du Nord went well, and we were able to get a taxi within 10 minutes of arriving.

The Eurostar just had a 4 hour delay that experienced for its customers (including myself): virtually no updates on what was happening, no updates on when we were going to move, no snacks or food offered for free (and they actually ran out of food for the entire train), no full refund of the ticket offered, etc...

TWO DAYS tryng to purchase a Paris London ticket,  for travel  in a couple of days' time. Computer throwing me a message indicating tickets have not yet been released?  30 MINUTES  WAITING onEurostar phone line . No oone picking up15 MINUTES TRYING THE ST PANCRAS TELEPHONE number... NO joy either. It rings a few times then the engaged tone..I HAVE HAD BETTER SERVICE FROM BUS COMPANIES IN AFRICA AND MEXICOILL CONSIDER FLYING.

On the way to Paris we had Liverpool fans screaming swearing and chanting all the way and I told staff but they said if you can move but nothing they can do. On the way back I had to stand for 2 and half hours with a heavy travel bag on my back in agony. I suffer with chronic pain and I tried to get advice at start of the queue but the man just said I am busy and would not talk to me then I was stuck in queues of people so could not ask anyone else. I was crying at passport control but all they cared about was a festival tattoo I had. Then I was told to go to the furthest point away to go through luggage control again to another queue. I finally got to a member of staff who allowed me to sit down while I wait as I couldn’t get to priority seating for disabled as it was closed off so she needed to open it for me to sit down. Then I had to go through more hordes of people to get on the train! I chose to go through Eurostar instead of fly as thought it would be easier than going through all the queues at the airport. I will never again pay £800 for this privilege absolutely disgusting service. Also after all that I couldn’t even get any lunch as the staff on strike so no food or drink available. Absolutely exhausted hungry and upset as well as in agonising pain

We took the Eurostar and I think we would have been better off flying. If you don’t buy the expensive Business Premier ticket you will wait in a very long line so you beed to get there 1.5 to 2 hours ahead. Luckily we did have the Business class ticket so it made checking in much faster. The lounge is really nothing special and the on train meal was also not great. Also if you a nut allergy I would recommend bringing your own food.  There we no nut free snacks or meals.

The boarding process in london was disgraceful. Disorganized,; no organized line; escalator up to waiting area (standing room only) became dangerously crowded; long wait time to Board train; inefficient immigrant and customs clearance; no assistance (carts/trolleys) for luggage. I would consider going by air. It was much better pre-Brexit.

I travel very regularly with Eurostar between Paris and London and I am scandalized by the mediocrity of this line and the services offered both at the station and during the journey. Saint Pancras: Terrible tail! At least an hour of meandering while standing. Absolutely avoid the double departure Paris + Disneyland (10 hours from Saint Pancras). Incompetent and unpleasant staff at the restaurant. Journey: Systematic delay! It's unbearable! The wifi never works! Paris: Better organized than Saint Pancras but which suffers from underinvestment and a chronic lack of maintenance.
252 minutes late and impossible to get a refund. customer service unreachable and the internet link to get a refund tells me that I am not entitled to it!!!! Does anyone have a solution? THANKS.

Poor customer service once you have scanned your ticket. Crowded no help with luggage and unhelpful staff who stand around and show let everyone struggle with their luggage on the conveyor belt.Border and passport control are like robots and don't expect them to even acknowledge you.Waiting room needs more seats particular if 2 trains are due to leave. Overall disappointing experience. Better off leaving check in until as late as possible.Once train platform was called only one door was opened and again over crowded.Shame because once on the train it was a great experience

I arrived at Paris Station with plenty of time to spare, an hour before the 7:43am departure from Paris to London. . . At immigration (*because the UK left the EU) there was a huge line on the French side, and then on the British side. It's not progressing at all. The time is getting closer and closer...oh no! ! Everyone around me, including me, was getting impatient from around 7:30 and told the guide, but everyone else around us was at the same time. Yes, yes, I feel like that. Ah! I was worried that I might not be able to keep to the departure times unique to Europe, so I went through French immigration, British immigration, and completed the baggage security check. The time was 8:05. I trotted towards the train in question. immigration! How about we do something about it? ? I'm tired of it. Inside the car, there was only simple bread and coffee, no need to put it on a huge tray. Needs improvement! !

Passing though security & passport control was quick with only short queues being manged well and moving quickly at both ends. Waiting area was clean & presentable, although very full when the majority of passengers had arrived. Queues for coffee were extremely long, I think I waited longer than 30 minutes at Pret, so you might be better off waiting until your on the train. Train itself also pleasant, clean & presentable with WiFi provided, staff were friendly & helpful. Little café on board is useful. Arrival painless as can walk straight out though the boarder controls.

252 minutes late. Compensation 55 euros on a 125 euro ticket in voucher, what's more! eurostar is getting back to health on the backs of travelers! For such a significant delay, the SNCF, which is not a model, reimburses in full
How is such an unprofessional company allowed to trade? It's lamentable

This was our first time using Eurostar.Good going through passport control, queues move quite quickly, not much seating in the waiting area. Once our train was ready to board just walked through the station and headed towards our train -and carriage. Comfortable seats, and charging point for your mobile etc. The station is Paris is just vile and  dirty and outside is even worse. We were glad we arranged transportation to our hotel, not having to find a taxi. When returning not a very good waiting area. The train back to London seemed older than the the train to Paris. Quick journey, no delays. Would use again as better than the airport,

As a British ex-pat living near Rotterdam, this is my go-to method of getting to central London or SE England. Greener and quicker than flying (though not always as cheap), it's a much nicer way to travel. I often pay the up-lift for Premium Economy to get a better seat and service - worth doing if you can be flexible about your dates & times.However, 2 big complaints...1) These trains may be very modern (300 kph is super fast!), but their toilets are constantly breaking down. On 4 journeys to date, the train has started with all toilets operational, but by the end, a significant number are out of action. One of the train staff told me that he's been with trains where only 3 are working (on an 18-carriage train!). And the train manager I spoke with blamed people for throwing things in that they shouldn't and blocking them (though this problem isn't something airlines suffer from). They really need to sort this out - it's shocking for a 3.5 hours journey.2) Check-in at St Pancras is woefully under-staffed by customs officials. Admittedly this isn't Eurostar's fault (though perhaps it is?). On my last journey, it took 1h20m start to finish and a lot of snaking around long queues in a hot airless space. This is particularly odd as Eurostar used to pride itself on it's short and simple check-in and in the past I've turned up 30-minutes before departure. Of course, Brexit (bless it!) has changed this for the worse, but it doesn't need to be this bad! And please turn up the Air-Co - it's stifling in the customs hall!I'll continue to use this train but it's rapidly turning into the miserable experience that is modern flying.

I will be avoiding travelling from Paris to London on the Eurostar if I can. To begin with there were no clear signs as to which line was for which train, which there was from London to Paris. The staff were generally rude and dismissive, and the difference a particular lady treated standard versus business premier passengers would be hilarious if it wasn't shocking. I understand business premier pay more, but it shouldn't be "bonjour Madame/Monsieur" smiley smiley and polite, and on the other hand shouting at people to get there passports ready and physically stopping them if they don't. What are we boarding the Titanic?? Our train was delayed due to electrical failures, fine they can't control that. But there was NO explanation as to why from the staff and we were left standing there dumbfounded for hours. When a lady asked when we would be boarding, she was completely ignored. Finally they changed our tickets to an earlier train (still massively delayed), but it wasn't clear as to why we were getting our tickets changed and to what train. When I panicked a bit (I think understandably), she LAUGHED at me and shook her head. Appalling behaviour and the staff should be ashamed of themselves for the way they "handled" the situation. I understand you can't control technical issues, but for the love of God there should be some contingency plan that doesn't include being flippant and extremely rude to people who have PAYED to board your service. I can only give two stars because the London to Paris side was very well organised and the staff were very polite and lovely.

I traveled with Eurostar in May 2022 from Paris to London. First of all staff responsible for organising passengers in queues for passport control is one of the rudest I have ever experienced. Imo the create more mess and disorder than anything else. All in all, it took us an hour to pass passport and security control.Then when we got to the actual waiting area we were told that the train will be 30 min late. In reality we were 50 min late on departure and when the train started they told us we will be arriving to St.Pancras at 8pm instead at 6pm. To put the cherry on top there was no food on the train, apart from snacks.In short I will never, ever be using Eurostar again.
Refund policy is pretty meaningless. They can take your money for a booking in seconds but if they cancel the setvice the refund will take 3 months , if it ever arrives. No justification.
Recently travelled to Brussels. Departure 40 minutes late and carriage toilets blocked and overflowing. Disgusting.

What an excellent experience. All of the Eurostar staff were amazing. Everybody was very helpful and friendly and all were smiling ( behind their masks of course). We travelled Business Premier and  were looked after handsomely all the way to Amsterdam. This is definitely the only way to travel to Europe. The only gripe is that the directions  to the terminal are not very good in Amsterdam, but once on the train this is soon forgotten. Keep it up Eurostar.

My train was cancelled. The website does not work to rebook a ticket or claim a refund and their call center had me wait over an hour before hanging up and telling me to check the website again. My friends who were supposed to take this train are in the same boat, and they too waited over an hour in the call center queue before being hung up on. Basically, I was scammed out of 50 pounds. Do not take Eurostar, it is not worth it. Flying is comparable in price and you will not have to deal with this mess because airlines actually have to compete with each other.

Ticket prices are rediculously expensive and overpriced. I would assume the train would be a good alternative to save money on flight tickets, but it's the other way around. Guess they're only aming at wannabe world-savers with a bad conscious.To be fair, the ride itself is as conevient as a flight, if not more convenient. However it is much slower and can't compete in any way with flying. Other than the environment.

The train service is good - comfortable and on time. However the check-in experience on both sides was awful. The waiting space in Paddington is like an overcrowded cattle shed, and the passport control was very slow. It was even worse in Paris - 1 hour waiting in disorganised queues for passport control. Even Ryanair seems preferable. Very disappointed.
Get rid of these stupid mouth masks, now! Just like the rest of the world.Plus start serving some decent portions that suffice during a four-hour trip.

Good:  convenient way of travel, St Pancras is a lovely station with lots of food options and shopping.  Train delivers you to the centre of Amsterdam.  The Standard Premium seats were spaciousNot so Good:  ran out of choice of food options on the return journey - not a great choice in the first place.  Amsterdam Eurostar - after check in there is only a vending machine, very squashed waiting area, long queues to check in and some of it outside - buy food before you check in.  Cafe on the train had very long queues and very limited food options. Allow plenty of time as both stations are very large. Didn't seem to get the seating we had booked so double check the configuration.
Comfortable and exciting. The only thing I would say is that the waiting area is not that comfy. Views were good, too.

Eurostar, for all its faults gets you from London to Paris (or visa versa) quickly and quite comfortably. The formalities are unfortunately reminiscent of an airport but much less unpleasant. It seems expensive but the fact that it takes you from city centre to city centre is worth a lot. Charles de Gaul airport and the train into Paris are very unpleasant by comparison. Taking the metro in Paris to the Eurostar terminal in Gare du Nord involves a baffling succession of gates and repeat presentations of your metro ticket. Instead take the sortie at Gare du Nord signposted Rue de Dunkirque and re-enter the station from the street.

Absolutely not worth it for Amsterdam to London. We took the train as we’d never done so before and want to fly less. Went with my family - ticket cost around 1.5 x as much as a flight. Journey time ~4 x longer with three intermediate stops. Eurostar “platform” at Amsterdam hidden in a remote corner of the station like an afterthought, and the worst bit was - once through security, almost nowhere to sit down apart from some uncomfortable stools in overcrowded departure lounge whilst we had to wait around an hour for our train, very unpleasant for my parents both over 60. Arriving at St Pancras - only then did I think this was a nice terminal befitting of the “Eurostar” brand. I feel guilty posting this review as I also want to take the train more and fly less to reduce carbon footprint. However I’m penalising myself by doing so (to Amsterdam anyway) when I have so many options to fly, many more convenient times / London airports to choose from, tickets cheaper, and 1/4 the journey time, by air. I did a search on flights and trains to Amsterdam in June, every single day that I searched there was a flight option that was cheaper than a corresponding train journey for the same day.Eurostar may be worth it to Paris / Brussels but DEFINITELY not for me to Amsterdam. Above all my own OPINION.
Overcrowded overpriced no loos working and no help at all. Not enough seatscat terminus. Nothing else to  say as very disappointed and annoyed

The departure lounge in Amsterdam is very basic, if you want food for the journey between Amsterdam and Belgium/France/London make sure you get it before you go through Eurostar customs, the baguettes they sell on board are shocking, couldn’t break with my hands let alone teeth, must have been at least 3 days old and you pay ridiculous money for the pleasure!Train journey is quite painless though, no problems either end.

Made the mistake of getting the Eurostar from Brussels to London. Don’t try and go through security any more than 70 minutes before the train leaves - they won’t let you through and there is no where to wait. The waiting area is horrible too when you finally do get through - no cafes just terrible duty free style shop (we’ll done on the refurb guys!)Got on the train which was a few minutes late. The door then got stuck shut between coach 1 and 2 and they couldn’t fix it - so at Lille they had us change seats and move from coach 2 to coach 14 at the other end of the train causing more delay and a long walk.We were then told we couldn’t get food or drink in coach 14 due to a ‘technical problem’, yet all the people in coach 14 had clearly had food before we got there. An absolute shambles and the staff don’t care. Don’t use this until these jokers learn how to run a railway. I suspect everyone any good left during the pandemic.Finally got to London 20 minutes late.

Thousands of people queuing at gar do nord in vert small space . Insufficient staff. Electronic passport controls keep breaking down. Waiting area overcrowded. Vip lounge overcrowded. Train delayed by over an hour... this ticket cost me near 400 pounds !

Surprised at how good the London terminal is. Plenty of facilities & organisation. Even a duty free shop. Continual announcements in multiple languages & scrolling updates on arrivals & departures.Compare this to the departure lounge in Amsterdam. Had to queue outside on the platform, uncovered  until the doors were opened. Yes there is a waiting area with chairs, stools & sofas aswell as plugs to charge electricals. Apart from that there is only a small vending machine with snacks. The screens don't update with travel information and the speaker announcements are very last minute. No duty free either. You need to make your food & beverage  purchases before getting through to departures.At both ends you go through passport control to leave the country & then almost immediately through arrival passport control.Such a difference between the two ends of the service.

Poor customer service. My mother purchased flexible tickets but could not change the dates not via email, phone or website for over a week due to EURO STAR technical issues.I managed to contact them via Facebook. They then insisted on adding extra costs according to prices today and not according to the date of my mother's initial request for amendments.EURO STAR never answered my mother, only to me. I found it very discriminatory as their service should be accessible to all ages, especially for the elderly.It seems like these technical issues are the perfect way to make money, and I found the way they handle it to be very unsettling.
Don't bother travelling on Eurostar, queue forever! Packed out in station area. Worse than an airport!!!! Staff try hard but to many passengers or the facilities are not sized right.SOS

Abysmal!  Queues snaking round and round into to shopping areas at Kings Cross while 2 of the 5 entry gates were closed. The return at Gard du Nord was also extremely bad. 2 hour + and delays of 40 minutes on departure.If you can’t provide the service don’t sell the tickets…
Cancelled our trip from Bruxelles to London. No compensation. Just a blant reply. Poor service. Had it been a flight, yoy would have been fully compensated.

Both London and Paris - chaos and very badly organised. Queues merging and demerging, too few staff and border force. Not sure why they bother with security screening, absolutely useless and just another bottleneck. Such a shame.

There were sooo many people at Gare du Nord that we queued for 1 1/2 hours to check-in.  That's on top of the 20 mins that we'd patiently waited as we were told our train check-in hadn't begun.   In the end we decided we shouldn't wait for the train information to appear as from comments we'd heard we knew people on our train were already queuing.  The queuing system (if there was one) was appalling.  Four queues into 2 or 3.  Then within each of those people were directed to different booths for French Border Control.  Because of the 'system' you were likely to be even further back in the queue to British Border Control as others filtered in in front of you!  It led to  trains being delayed (tempers being very frayed) and some people missing the train they'd booked on!  It was difficult to find up to date information about trains once through border controls.  Once onboard the announcements weren't clear.  They were mumbled and the English was not very clear.   We've used Eurostar before, to/from Lille and Disneyland Paris, but this experience has made us decide never to use Eurostar from Gare du Nord again.
Costumer service is complete 0. Have no idea why they put that number there, when no one is going to answer it. Poor service, no way to get in touch with someone

Arriving 1 hour early at Gare du Nord, we waited 1 hour in the cold to go through security and almost missed our train. There were very few people at passport control on the British side. Obviously, it's always like this and it doesn't shock the Eurostar staff at all, who explain that during busy periods, passengers regularly miss their train because of waiting to go through customs.

I don’t understand why the name on vouchers issued cannot be changed. It should be as easy as changing the name on a plane ticket. My partner had vouchers in her name and was unable to travel with me because the vouchers were in her name and Eurostar refused to change the name on the ticket. Therefore we would need to buy completely new tickets in order for me to travel.

I travelled from London to Paris. Give this exclusive line only the price was a thrill.Board bistro: sandwiches with bread like dry paperWLAN on the train: Probably weakest in EuropeBoard entertainment: ZeroI travel a lot on train and had some expectations that all were not fullfilled except coming from A to B.You could do so much more of it. It's a shame.

Very poor costumer service very very very rude staff shouting and smacking the luggage fromOur hand …reported to the manager been said that they will talk to the staff but no bothered to ask who was the staff actually…the service is like once u paid dont bother us treated like animal

I wondered whether to leave a negative review because, for carbon reasons, I'm supportive of people taking the train rather than flying. However, I guess more people will take the train if the people at Eurostar read feedback on Tripadvisor and improve the service as a result, so here goes .... My recent experience with Eurostar was pretty poor. I stood in a massive queue at St. Pancras for well over an hour (it seemed to me that the delay was caused by an insufficient number of French immigration officials and a check-in /security area that's just too small). As a result, the train left 20 mins late, and was further delayed by a fault on the line in Belgium, meaning I missed my connecting train to Frankfurt, adding an extra two hours to my journey. On the way back my German train was cancelled, meaning I missed my Eurostar back. To give Eurostar credit they simply moved my ticket to a later train with no additional cost. However, trying to contact customer support following the journey has been painful. Ten days after sending an email nobody has responded; and I have tried to call them unsuccessfully a number of times, being cut off regularly. It's almost as though they DON'T WANT to talk to their customers. I feel I am owed money by Eurostar, but trying to speak to anyone to sort it out seems impossible. Really disappointing customer service. In short, it's disappointing: for those of us who don't want to do short haul flights in Europe Eurostar seems to offer the perfect solution. But the service offered could be much better.

Vacation ruined because the mention of the compulsory passport for children was not indicated. No refund. But an exchange for tickets 3 times cheaper, without any reimbursement of the price difference. Eurostar = dishonest company! First and last time we are taken in by fraudulent commercial methods. Thank you to your site for circulating the information.
Not organized, racist, rude nothing was good they don't even deserve a star. Bad language with customers.

In reading other reviews, I feel that I got lucky.  My travel mates and I travelled down to Paris on the 7am train and back by 6pm that night.  Appreciated seeing the countryside and that we could buy Paris Metro tickets on board.  We did not have any delays even though they warned of one near the Chunnel.  It did take longer to get through the lines on the Paris side but we made sure to give ourselves lots of time beforehand.

I'm a little confused with all the negative reviews I have been reading about poor service etc on Eurostar. We and I have to be totally honest had the best experience for our day trip to Brussels, we left on the 9.01 departure from St Pancras and returned the same day on the 18.56, arriving back at 19.58. We did (as it was a special occasion our 60th Birthday) book Business class, on our way out we were seated in coach 16 and looked after superbly by 2 lovely ladies. Now being 60, I forgot to ask their names, so apologies for that. the service, journey and experience went far to quick and in less than 2 hours we were in Brussels. We had a lovely day exploring the Grand Market area, had lunch in the square, purchased some Belgium Chocolates.On arrival back at Midi, we checked in and with our ticket were allowed to use the Business Lounge. Excellent experience, nice staff and the drinks flowed. The time went very quickly, then it was time to board our train for the return trip to London. This time we were in Coach 1, at the other end of the 16 coach train. The staff were not the same as the one on the way out, but the service was the same high standard. The meal was enjoyable and of course served with wine. The trip went far to quick. The staff, from the train manager through to all others were friendly and professional. We had a super experience and would recommend Eurostar anytime, as a day out the memories will remain for a long while, thanks you to all the staff we met in coach 16 and coach 1, who made our day and made us feel very specialAs for customer service, we didn't have a problem

Inexcusably badly designed terminal, terrible check-in process, poorly trained staff. Must be terrifying for people who are tired, elderly, disabled in any way or are travelling with children. Be prepared to be confused and shouted at in some un-identifiable language. All round a very unpleasant travel experience. No one should put up with this. Just fly and use the cost saving to offset the carbon.

I won’t be travelling on the ski train again until the alcohol ban is lifted.Could I suggest rather than punishing the passengers and having a complete alcohol ban, you stop passengers bringing their own alcohol on board and train / educate staff more thoroughly as to what a drunk person is, and then refuse service, or put security on the train.Your company should be able to deal with this situation and prevent people from drinking further, as does every other licensed venue like / premises in the country.If you cannot do that and control it, you shouldn’t hold an alcohol license full stop.It also makes no sense to get us all here 2 hours before departure, to then have us sitting in the crowded lobby with masks on for 90 minutes without anything to drink.Stupid rules made probably as a result of Brexit bitterness again.

We bought a trip to Paris. London to Paris very enjoyable. Quick boarding, fast departure and after over two hours, Paris. However, two days before returning to London I have received email to download new boarding tickets coz our seats has changed. Done, not a problem. We arrived to GdN we were given new seats where our 7 year old daughter has been allocated to different carriage. I have rise an issue with staff in response I have been told that my wife can seat with a child so I can take different carriage seat. No problem however my question is how come Eurostar is able to separate seats from parents and kids. Shame Eurostar. Definitely I will consider other options next time.
Extremely expensive, disorganized, wifi never works so impossible to work during the journey. Last time, I will take the plane from now on

Impossible to speak to someone. Phone lines have been down for 18 months, nobody responds to you over email. The worst customer experience experience I’ve ever encountered…customers should complain to London Watch their ombudsman. Trying to manage your booking online doesn’t work and asks you call their number - number doesn’t work - ‘unprecedented demand’ but it’s been 18 months.

I wanted a quick and comfortable trip to Paris to meet up with my brother so we could go on holiday. The queues at St Pancras International where horrendous. I waited in line , shuffling along for 2 hours. When I finally got to my seat it was comfortable and just what I booked but it did not compensate for the long queuing and 35 minute  departure delays.I upgraded to business class on my return which was a mistake as feeling under the weather after a long night flight all I wanted was a cup of tea not (champagne)which I had to wait for until everyone's meal had been served and eaten .The business lounge at Gare du Nord was pleasant though and I thankfully did not have to queue in Paris at all. I live close to Ashford International train station so ended up going through it without being able to stop twice. When are you going to provide this service again ?

As a train enthusiast, I started traveling with the Eurostar in 2007, in that case coming from Berlin and taking the ES to Brussels.  Everything was perfect. To date I have traveled the Eurotunnel another 6 times, often return trips within the same day from Paris. The last time was in 2019. I would like to know now which documents I might need, as I had a cerclage done on my kneecap on 15.3.22 and I wouldn't want to have problems with the metal detector. I will try to translate the resignation certificate to use as justification. Thank you

more than an hour and a half waiting on the phone to request a credit of €150 on a ticket that I had to change 4 times due to Covid, request refused for me but accepted for a friend with whom I had to leave for London 2 hours before, total inconsistency, total inequity, absolutely lamentable for this company which generates millions, INADMISSIBLE!!!

The pandemic has impacted all areas of life including travel but I think Eurostar need to improve the flow and process. Check in is pretty chaotic and not a great experience as the first part of your holiday / break. The queues are not acceptable. Period. This is compounded by a la knot staff which would make it more bearable. On board food is terrible. Sandwich and coffee and even orange juice from a renoun brand is not good. Service is good onboard when buying food but the food itself is bad quality
the queue at st pancras is simply unnaceptable. i used the service a lit pre pandemic and a bit during.  its hopeless standing in a mile and a half long queue for 2 hours.

Worst service ever! Train broke down halfway between Amsterdam and London (which may happen), but what followed was pure disregard for all passengers: over 100 passengers were left in Brussels to their own luck, having to hope to get on the last train of the day. The company refused to attempt having these passengers relocated to an earlier train, and ultimately after a lot of stress we all arrived in London over 6 hours later than expected. If that was not enough absurd, the company also claims the total delay (to be considered for refund) was only 66 minutes - which is basically only the delay that happened before the train broke down in Brussels. All that without mentioning the ticket costs twice as much as a plane ticket. In summary: I will never travel with them again!

We had to queue for more than two hours to have our passports checked. It was a very stressful experience and the train departed with a 55 minutes delay, enough time to avoid paying for a partial reimbursement. We spent a fortune for the tickets, thinking we would be traveling in full comfort. We were completely wrong. Far from a Eurostar experience.
Think I will go back to flying. The train bit is fine but security, passport and departure areas are far from enjoyable and reduce the whole experience to a shambolic mess

I have been using Eurostar off and on for many years. Sometimes excellent, but sadly now a zero star experience. Never did I expect to queue for over TWO hours to pass French passport control. One gentleman in the queue collapsed..once on the very late running train the buffet car ran out of snacks even BEFORE leaving the station, the loos were overflowing....but almost worst of all the staff (all French) were abrupt and unfriendly. The product could be an amazing experience.but I suspect that this is all a little payback for the politicians game playing. Lets have a little competition on the route....or even better strip Eurostar of its license to operate to the UK.

The queues are extraordinary. People are asked to wait for over 1h (!) in a line to check in. The operation is so unprofessional. They act as if it is the first day of service. Never take that train to Paris! Take a plane and you will be much happier.

Spent two plus hours in a que  at St Pancras which apparently is  very normal. This meant the train departed late. So all is forgiven Easyjet and Ryan Air . It is actually cheaper to fly and  quicker and the only real  advantage of Eurostar is that you can take luggage and bottles  but the hassle with   x- ray machines, passport control and security delays is exactly the same on the train if not  worse . So when you see Ryan air fights for £18 why would you get the train . Our trip cost £150 return to Brussels each . Managed to buy the wrong ticket so had to pay another 40 euro return for  Brussels to Bruges sector.  which is included as long as you buy the right type of ticket Make sure you select  "Any Belgian station" - easy mistake  to make.

I made a complaint about very rude and unfriendly check-in staff more than three weeks ago, 2nd March, and I have not received an acknowledgement let alone a reply. I makes me think that Eurostar does not care what the public think. I certainly will not use your company again.
If I had known I would have to stand in a queue for 2 hours, waiting to get on the train, I would have travelled by another means, and will do so next time.

Very bad service.In the website it says to be at the station 120 before departure time so we made sure to be there 2 hours earlier.There was a very long queue and we joined it. Then as the queue started moving the staff told us to step outside of the queue to let passengers travelling earlier to go ahead.We had to wait by the side (not able to go somewhere else as we would have to join the end of the line) for an hour before we were let in the queue again.Basically they encourage people to come late as the people who come late get fast tracked. Then the train was delayed for over an hour without any specific announcement on how long. They only said due to high number of passengers the delay is known! Which only means bad management.

Impossible to get through to Eurostar. Waste of time ringing their number whether English or French, doesn't matter if Club or regular. Sooner or later the phone goes dead.I need to change my booking, but when I try to do so online, it says I need to ring their number. What am I supposed to do ? It is outrageous.Yesterday I tried but waiting time was 25 mins so I decided to try today. Silly me !

On our return trip from Paris to London, the Covid measures in place, namely mask wearing and more specifically the excessive air conditioning on board had negative effects on our journey. My wife developed a cough during the journey due to the excessive cold air being circulated and it was also noticed that other passengers were being effected in a similar way. For example, a passenger one seat in front started sneezing. Another passenger was heard coughing also. Also in the terminal itself on departure, the recorded voice emphasised the requirement to wear masks when this is no longer a legal requirement and members of staff were observed not wearing masks. Going through passport control on departure was OK and my wife and I were able to stay together. On return due to my wife being French we were forced to separate. The staff were also quite authoritarian in their attitude, snapping orders out to passengers. Unacceptable. Eurostar really needs to move on from Covid in this respect. Thankfully for our next trip to France we will be taking Brittany Ferries and will only be using Eurostar when absolutely necessary.  It should also be noted that the number of email alerts relating to Covid requirements was excessive and that for our return journey, despite coming prepared with all documentation in this respect, none was requested. Seat changes were also an issue being advised at the very last minute.Once again, unacceptable. At the Paris side when going through passport control, there was a failure of several terminals and the number of photos taken automatically was ridiculous. Very much a dystopian experience although I imagine that such criticism will fall on deaf ears.On board the train there appeared to be no place to deposit rubbish. What has happened to Eurostar? Covid has obviously had a negative impact and those high in the management structure of the company appear all to keen to impose non mandatory measures on passengers which then has unintended consequences on the health of passengers such as was the case with the excessive air conditioning/air circulation. Another point: once again, aspects of non-covid related cleanliness procedures appear to have been placed on the backfoot. My wife reported that when she flushed one of the toilets there were unpleasant smells emanating from the toilet. Also when descending the excalator onto the platform on the Paris side, I looked at my hand which had been placed on the rail and it was covered in some form of oily residue.
32 minutes on the phone for 2 days and no one picks up! Impossible to reserve for an electric wheelchair!!!!

I used this Eurostar service during the last few days to attend the 6 Nations Rugby Final in Paris. I am not a frequent user but I was impressed by this wonderful, comfortable and swift train service on Eurostar.   My experience was somewhat spoiled by the fact that you felt like a captive traveler being offered terrible food and drinks at Exhorbitant prices ! On my return from Paris I ordered the Breakfast deal of a Croissant , coffee and orange. After a short way into the journey they had run out of Croissants ! They therefore sent me the most awful Chocolate Brownie, a coffee that needed condemning as not fit for human consumption and a bottle of orange juice. Despite not having any Croissants left they still charged full price for the deal. So you pay full price for something that is majorly sub standard, not what you ordered and something I would not feed to my dog ! But why spoil a most magnificent feat of engineering, a super service, pleasant staff by ripping people off ? ? I don't get it. If they charged reasonably for a good standard of food and drink  they would increase the number of customers wanting food and drinks and would make more money and would not be getting reviews like mine.

When travelling from London to Europe you need to arrive 90 mins to 2 hours before the train departs to cross the “French Border” which was one man for our queue and took an hour, travelling from Brussels to the Uk the advice as 45 mins to 6 before departure, the Brussels exit stamp was quick but again the UK border check was poor 3 of 6 machines working and although plenty of imkigartuon officer in booths as well a very officious UK border guard made us queue for machines and let her colleagues have an easy life waiting for the odd US of non EU passenger!!  Hmmm come On Eurostar the border procedures reflect badly on you! The actual train service is brilliant hence you escaped a 1 star rating!
Awful dystopian travel experience, haven’t moved on from Covid like many other travel companies, like travelling in lockdown. Very rude, unhelpful staff at check I /security. Avoid!
Eurostar ha cancelado mis trenes dos veces y ha decidido darme un voucher en vez de devolverme mis billetes. Not only does it ruin our vacation but it makes us waste time and money. Terrible job

Avoid at all costs. Refused to refund my money despite changes in COVID restrictions when this was clearly stated as a reason for refund in the insurance documents. Months later I got a gift voucher instead, only to not be able to get into my account due to password reset emails not working. They don't pick up the phone. Customer service is non-existent. Absolute waste of time.

Some of the worst customer service I have ever encountered in the travel industry. I have travelled with Eurostar a lot since I live in paris and my family live in the UK and had no problems until there was an issue with one of my bookings. The phone number that they provide does not work (it just says they are too busy and hangs up) and I have sent several emails and not received a single reply.Over my trips I have also collected quite a few points which I was saving to use on one big trip but there were lots of restrictions on how and where I could use them, so eventually I had to use them on separately costing me a lot more in the process. It’s not all negative though - the trains are very convenient and for the most part leave on time. I have never had any issues at security and the lounges/duty free have food, cafes etc. as well as lots of space to sit while you wait.
Terrible, badly prepared system and staff that are unhelpful; it is like going through an airport in a previous century!

annoying when people use tripadviser to be vent frustrations about customer service that don’t specifically relate to Eurostar experience. Ok, so the customer service call centres could be better and a few covid issues could be improved but if you separate  these from the actual Eurostar product, it’s really pretty good.check in and customs experience is pretty efficient, (albeit would highlight delays on the Paris side, a consequence of brexit and us Brits wanting to do things in a less efficient way, but let’s not rerun that debate)The train carriages are very comfortable, the trains left and arrived on time and the whole experience is far more comfortable and stress free than flying! Taking more luggage on board is another great benefit of rail travel.

Eurostar is not without its faults - such as poor information when things go wrong - but it is so much nicer to relax for a couple of hours in a comfortable train to get from London to Paris or vice versa than it is to struggle to and from the airports in order to be crammed into a noisy fuselage.  The less pleasant aspects of the trip are the same as one gets by air - "security" and the horrible British xenophobia writ large on the scowling faces of the Border Force at St. Pancras. Tips - go "Leisure Select" if you can afford it. Extra comfort and a small meal - be very careful on arrival at the Gare du Nord. Many pickpockets and scam artists work here and on the metro.

I wish there was a zero stars option. No customer service for anyone that doesn't pay business class fares, in the middle of a pandemic! Not to mention they don't answer calls, I would rather walk and swim to France rather than using Eurostar again. Avoid, avoid, avoid!
Horrendous organization with terrible customer service. All the negative comments here are true. Stealing money from tourists in the middle of a pandemic. Find alternative means of travel.

Passenger locator form nightmare. We arrived at station one and half hours before departure to London. Rude women demanding the form to be completed. Difficult stressful code wouldn’t scan even though we both vaccinated. Finally did form. Then my passport scan of face didn’t work. Sent to police control. Husband ahead had lost him. Finally after begging to be let through had two mins to run for the train. Absolute nightmare. I could see other passengers same stress. Terrible. Paying for the experience. Not enough help and guidance. Shameful. Ruined end of our ski holiday.

My train would in principle depart from Rotterdam central station. This train was canceled 2 hours in advance, after which I tried to rebook the train. I then waited in line twice for a full 120 minutes (so a total of 240 minutes!!!!!), after which the line was disconnected after 120 minutes both times. I tried to rebook online, but the site crashed. So this didn't work either. I texted, no response. I emailed, no response. Finally applied for an e-voucher. This went up to €80, while a new ticket cost €200. Then I tried to book a new ticket, but the e-voucher code was not usable. Ultimately had to book a new ticket; the next morning at 09.00 from Brussels. This meant I had to get up at 5 a.m. because it was a three-hour drive for me. Received no help whatsoever, worst service I have experienced in a long time.

Booked and paid from Australia in 2020.  Business class seats.  Worldwide pandemic.  Unable to travel.  Emailed voucher.  Attempted refund over a two year period.  Got stonewalled at every attempt.  Voucher has now expired on the eve of Australians being allowed to travel overseas again.  Dishonest company.  Making money from tourists without offering any service.  Warning to all users, buy your ticket on the your day of travel, or fly.

I booked a packet train with hotel. Because was during the pandemic was cancelled.Got a voucher and i rebook my trip after some time. I had extra for less days and in worst hotel. I have never seen such deplorable and incompetent customer service as that of Eurostar! Given the prices you were offered I think it is a scandal to have such catastrophic customer service. A horror

Worst customer service ever , their phone line doesn’t work and hangs up automatically, they do not respond to their emails or will take more than a month . I had an issue with my ticket and tried contacting them over a month before my departure to resolve this Im still waiting for someone to get back to me . Very annoying considering the price of the ticket!
Both train journeys canceled without informing us. Unreachable customer service. Never received a response to complaints

My original train was cancelled and there were no later alternative trains that day which meant I had to change my incoming flight to catch the earlier train. This was overcrowded. It took an hour to get through immigration. My seat was open to just a third of a window and was as cramped as an airline economy seat. One does not expect this on a train. It was just horrible! It’s high time there was some competition for Eurostar. For a longer but much more pleasant travel experience go by SNCF and catch a ferry.

Customer service is simply unreachable and an invitation to contact them via a digital journey worthy of Monty Python (closed questions leading to inconsistencies). Worst customer experience of 2021, well done there were only a few days left. Pros: the train is eco-friendly and fast, Cons: no customer service, poor customer consideration, customer frustration. AVOID

We've been trying to contact Eurostar for days after they cancelled our train from Paris to London. The link they sent to change your ticket is for an e voucher and can take up to 28 days to process! We are trying to get home next week. Completely understand the need to cancel trains but should have something in place that will allow the customer to change their reservations OR should have someone at the other end of the phone/email/text/FB etc. etc. We have tried to contact them multiple times in multiple ways and have not heard back. We were impressed with their handling of paperwork/covid restrictions on the way out of London. This latest situation however has made us never want to use them again.
Could not travel due to covid restrictions. Could not even refund my ticket. Absolutely disgusting practice in these pandemic times. Honestly how the government has not stepped in is beyond me.

Frequent Eurostar travelers, this company is a disaster. The trains are systematically late, they sometimes cancel the trip a week in advance, they are unreachable by phone or email... the customer service is deplorable, not to mention the organization at Saint-Pancras which is simply disastrous (only one queue for all the trains). Add to all the incredibly high prices for a 2 hour train journey... Avoid at ALL costs

Businesses Premier Experience:London -> ParisParis -> LondonWhen you arrive to the station is nice to see that you get some priority is some of the queues and passport checks but police will often move people around to speed up the non priority lines. I understand.The lounge is very luxurious and offers hot drinks and cold drinks with some salty snacks, but that’s all. Apart from wifi and restrooms you won’t find any food, bakery or any other types of snacks so you are basically just there for coffee, tea or a bottled beer. Finally the train.Seats: This is the nice part, the seats are very comfortable and more spacious than non business coaches, which means less people and most of the people in the business coach tend to be respectful and will try to behave. Food: as expected, just like in the lounge, only drinks are offered apart from the breakfast/lunch/dinner include, so no snacks, not even a bag of chips. The dinner platter service will always be cold food, either salads, vegetables or chicken. From what I understand they don’t appear to have any microwave or coffee brewer so don’t expect anything hot or more than just coffee with milk. Finally, what made come here to write is that when I asked what do you offer they said that only that and if I wanted more I could go the cafeteria and buy other snacks. For a ticket that you pay +4x the price of a normal ticket (my case was £250 vs £57) is not normal that you get told that you have to go and buy a bag of chips because they don’t have any.In the end, for a 1hr 30min journey unless you really dislike the noise and the seating in non premium seats, is not worth.
I have just had to cancel my trip to Paris because of Covid restrictions. Eurostar was fantastic and gave me an e-voucher immediately so that I haven't lost out financially. Very impressed.

15/12/2021Had a horrendous trip home from Gare du Nord to St Pancris, last night. The train was delayed by 4 hours, still in the station for 3 hours while passengers were stuck waiting for any kind of updates on when the train will leave, me and my partner were unable to leave the station to get food and the food kart had no food only chocolate which we would have to pay for. After leaving the station we were re routed which made us that extra hour delayed taking us to 4 hours. When speaking with the train manager we were offered an agreed paid for taxi of £130 to get me and my partner home. We were told the cab driver would be waiting at the station for us, when we arrived and directed out of the station, by Eurostar staff, there was no cab waiting for us. 30 minutes later at 2 in the morning we were notified by a member of staff from St Pancris that they have been told by Eurostar our cabs won't be coming and we would need to find our own way home and that there were no Eurostar staff at the station to communicate with. So very tired and hungry we were forced to pay £130 out of our own pockets to get home at 2 in the morning.
After years, they still won’t allow pets and they still aren’t part of the pet passport scheme. Shameful! Are we stuck in the 1800s or what??
I want to change my train ticket but the customer service is non-existent. You cannot reach them unless you wait for at least 45minutes (and you are not even sure to reach them after 45min)
very disappointed that the tunnel is in fact made of bricks, and not glass, so there was no view of all the fish swimming around! Is this because I didn’t choose first class?

Had a trip booked to travel to Europe for an interment services for a close friend.  The date of the service was postponed due to pandemic restrictions.  When trying to request a credit note to be used for future travel once the new service dates was known, I could only get through to a support team for UK bookings.  This team told me I was at the wrong department, they could not redirect me to the EU support team and advised they were not allowed to contact the department themselves.I am left with the only option to use the trainline website contact us form.  This I have used and it is yet another trainline black hole.Recommend booking direct with EU train operator rather than trainline
I was in a car next to a very loud group of people in the bar. The staff did not do anything to make them keep it down.

I use Eurostar as the only train service that can go into Europe - and don't they know it. There's nothing they do to make a good customer experience, and they can get away with it because there's no one who can do it any better.The train itself is fine. They ask you arrive 90-120 minutes in advance, which is unnecessary and means the train takes longer than just flying.Once you've got a ticket, you're stuck with it. I wanted to cancel last minute because I was visiting a friend who came down with a cold last minute. I couldn't refund the tickets at all (which cost a huge amount), and moving them cost £30 per ticket (there and back) - I'm actually better off just buying new tickets closer to the time.I'm currently 70 minutes into a phone call with customer service to try and get some money back, even as credit. I've never had anyone put me on hold this long. The first 3 minutes of the call is reiterating the information on their website about travel restrictions. Please stop wasting my life, Eurostar.I'm tired of supporting this terrible service as the only alternative to flying. Despite my objections on environmental grounds, I'll be flying from now on. It's faster, cheaper, and has better customer service.

Coffee in the standard class is literally undrinkable, with uht milk. Wifi wasn’t working and no plug points at our seats. Carriage was poorly ventilated. I wouldn’t mind if it wasn’t also far more expensive than flying. An easyJet experience at premium prices.
Good experience. However, it was too cold during the trip due to the air conditioner and the view under the see is not what I expected !

The last time I used Eurostar was an offer to go Business Class to Brussels with my wife, it was a lovely experience. Today I travelled to Paris in the premium cabin and the whole experience has put me off using Eurostar againThe lounge at St Pancras is very tired with badly worn seating. Drinks are very limited, snacks too, most of it still appears closedPassport control was slow despite few people being there, very disappointing, no fast track option eitherWhilst the train itself was fast and on time, the service was terrible for a premium price. I can only describe it as economy airline food serve in an economy way. Yes, they do offer champagne, two very small glasses and if you ask for more they don't seem to like it (customer service?)In summary, badly stocked, tired lounge, really poor food and miserly drinks.It has made my mind up to do the LHR-CDG run again, it's actually less hassle and for the same service you pay a fraction of the price
Travelled to Lille from St Pancs. On time, easy check in and comfortable. Less trains at present but less people travelling.

Traveled Eurostar London St Pancras to Brussels. Eurostar terminal is on ground floor of St Pancras Station very easy to find and well signed from Underground and all station entrances. Travelling to Belgium, checks to see if you have completed the Belgium government COVID Locator form before you enter queue area. Unbelievable amount of people turned away because they hadn’t despite many emails and text from Eurostar clearly showing what documents you need…not Eurostar’s fault. Only 10 minutes to get through security and passport and vaccination checking. The departure waiting area has always been tight for space and was no worse than before due to COVID checks. Good enforcement of mask wearing. There is only one food outlet inside the terminal (a Pret a’ Manger) at time of visit, so may want to use the many excellent food outlets and restaurants in the magnificent St Pancras station complex beforehand. The whole loading process was super efficient and friendly. Worth paying extra for the premium economy with larger seats and an acceptable continental breakfast with friendly and efficient service by the train staff throughout. Service arrived  on time and efficient/quick transition through documents check on arrival in Brussels. For me this was still a quick, relaxing and enjoyable way to travel to Brussels from London. Well done.

Hugely disappointing experience travelling from Amsterdam to London.  A wait in a cramped departure "lounge" in Amsterdam with appalling toilets and no refreshments (unless you want to use a vending machine).A train that stops for what seems an age at Rotterdam.  And a buffet car out of food after the first stop.  Poor.  Better going by plane.  A

On 5 November, I used Eurostar's services for the first time, travelling from London back to Germany. It explicitly says on the ticket to get to St. Pancras International 120 minutes before departure, because of intensified checks related to Brexit and Covid. I arrived on time and went through the checks in less than 30 minutes. Apparently, other travelers didn't consider the extra time and arrived too late. Instead of Eurostar considering it these people's responsibility to be on time, we *waited* for all guests to pass the checks, resulting in a 19 minute delayed departure and a 27 delayed arrival in Brussels. A whole group of people, myself included, missed the connecting ICE to Cologne/Frankfurt - it was announced that the ICE would wait for us, but this turned out to be untrue. Why does Eurostar reward latecomers, thereby causing problems for people who have to travel farther? At least Eurostar booked me a hotel room in Brussels, as there were no more available connecting trains that day.
A canceled train No text message to warn 4 hours of delay Obnoxious and lamentable serviceUseless first standard class Filthy compartmentThe SNCF IS BOKING UP

Very antiquated non assistance dog policy. Discriminative against dog owners on this vital travel link .  This would be the only realistic way for non car drivers to travel to the continent with a dog.

Gare du Nord is unsuitable for travelers waiting for the Eurostar for London or Brussels and even less so when departures to the two destinations are almost together. There are not enough seats to sit, there are souvenir or cosmetics stores which are already flooding Paris while we have to queue on average 15 minutes for a coffee. There is only one poor Relay and one Paul, it's really fair when we are asked to come very early and we wait sitting on the ground while the price of the ticket is on average 3 times more expensive than the plane. The luggage belt is not practical and there is nothing to put the coats which are placed on the carpet with the suitcases which roll on the floors of dirty cities. I am not commenting on the Gare du Nord itself or the people who hang out there. Nothing to do with St Pancras, a true reflection of a dynamic and organized city such as London

I am writing you a review here because I have already alerted your customer service by email of the very bad experience I had on October 13 at St Pancras but I have not received any feedback from your services. Here are the facts, one of your employees was extremely unpleasant and aggressive towards me that day. My ticket did not pass through the turnstile. Instead of helping me, this person looked at me without doing anything (while her role is to help the passengers I suppose, especially since she was doing nothing at the time) Then, she walked towards me, seeing that I was stressed because I had my train very soon, so I asked her for help and she replied with a superior air "I won't help you before you calm down!" uh, that is to say that I had already been trying to get my ticket for 3 minutes, that she did nothing to help me and she told me that. So I calmly ask him again “Could you help me please?” and she tells me "No" and leaves. Another British hostess at another station had seen the scene and helped me straight away. But the other employee wasn't happy about that and she kept muttering about me from afar. She suddenly arrived at the counter while the hostess apologized on her behalf, was affable, empathetic and printed my ticket. Obviously, she didn't like me being helped at all and she was looking for a confrontation. She then says to me in French, “You know, I have the possibility of banning you from taking this train?” Um, sorry? There, I just told him to leave me alone once and for all, to shut up and leave me alone, that I only wanted my train! In addition to refusing to help me, she literally came to my head at the counter and was not happy that another hostess was taking over. I must have lost almost 10 minutes in total because of her and another security agent told me that I was really going to be short on time for the train because there was a queue at the passport check. I showed him my disabled badge and he told me to show it in order to be given priority, which I did and the passengers agreed. It was without imagining that a person from the staff visibly warned by walkie talkie by the same ill-intentioned person would stop me and tell me to go see the manager. So I explain to the manager what happened just before and he calls the person in question who says in English that she categorically refuses to speak with me by being confrontational. So he leaves for 7-8 minutes (still lost for me) and comes back saying text to me "You apologize to her right away or I will forbid you from taking this train!" Surreal but true. I wanted my train and so I apologize flatly to this person while thinking that I am experiencing something profoundly unfair and abnormal. I finally got through security but I was shocked. Not to mention that I have a back condition, a condition that prevents me from being up for too long and there, in this case with my luggage and bags. I informed these people of my disability by showing my disabled priority badge but they didn't care which is also very serious and made me wait (the manager) I have never been treated like this, I had to apologize to a person who was super aggressive with me, under the threat and blackmail of not being able to take my train, and that is not normal at all. I should have alerted the authorities who were not far away but at the time, I was mainly thinking about getting my train. I can give you the exact description of this employee as well as the manager who was not at all fair play in the end but I am still extremely shocked to have been treated like that. Not to mention that this bad experience may be repeated with other customers received by the same team at the station.  I therefore really wanted to write this testimony because it could have gone much further if I had not chosen to apologize to put out the fire given the pugnacity and stubbornness of this woman. I'm still shocked and not at all ready to take a Eurostar again anytime soon. To this day, following my email, I have still not received any apology from the group. Obvious gaps in the training of your teams in customer contact.

When did Eurostar become so bad?  We used to travel Business Premier to Paris etc and it was a lovely, comfy quality experience, nice seating and lighting, good food. Now it's as if a bucket airline was running it.I purchased top price tickets partly due to they offer hot food options. 12 days later I still had no confirmation of my booking and I was was locked out of my online account. Repeatedly we tried to reset the password, but no emails came through to let us set a new password. I now see on Tripadvisor other people have had the same issues. Totally stressful. Tried phoning Eurostar and they claim they are busy and cannot take calls, call back later. Called back later for 3 days in a row. Finally got my tickets 3 days before travel.We skipped breakfast as we knew we would be using the Premier Business Lounge at St. Pancras, but there was nothing. Just a bowl of crisps and nuts anyone could put their hand in. What happened to the snacks ? Now you have to spend more money by leaving the lounge and buying something from Pret A Manger.We are in the time of Covid. We need to be washing our hands. But in the Business Premier Lounge there was no running water in the bathrooms.We then went to our train carriage. I believed my partner had got the wrong one. The seating has changed to economy flight style seats, many all facing the same way. Bight lighting, ugly colour scheme. All cheap and nasty. The carriage wasn't even clean. There was food debris on the seats. And the seats are hard, no better than a regular low priced train ticket. The Eurostar website states Premier Business = Extra Spacious Seats. Nonsense. It was a bucket airline seat.Then came the food. There is only ONE hot food option despite the Eurostar website saying HOT MEALS. It's not MEALS, it's ONE HOT MEAL option. A curry. Is anyone really desiring a curry midday on their way to Paris ? And the cold starter was Arabic. Is that what people want midday? This is a train going from London to Paris. The menu is apparently by Raymond Blanc, a French man living in the UK. What's with the Arabic and Indian menu? There are better meals on offer on a plane economy ticket. And just one offer of a coffee or tea in a silly little cup. Toilet on board. Staff had loaded the toilet rolls wrong. Impossible to get hold of any paper.Obviously no expections for the return journey. Dirty seats again. Wiped off someone else's food debris before sitting down. And my seat was broken. It would not lock in place, so constantly moved. Staff aren't trained to fix the seats.Served drinks, and within minutes the clumsy waitress knocked mine on the floor and stupidly asked if I would like another one? Of course I want another one, I've not even started to drink the one I've just poured.Entering France you're supposed to have what's called "Honesty" paperwork for the French authorities where you state you've had no health issues, etc. No one asked for it.On the return to the UK you're supposed to have filled out the Government Passenger Locator Forms. Even when you arrive back at St Pancras there are signs "Have you got your Passenger Locator Forms?". At Border Force no once asked to see proof. Everyone off that train sailed into the U.K. with no checks at all.

My wife asked me to make a booking for her as she is finding it IMPOSSIBLE to actually make a booking at all.Firstly, there is no actual phone service : if you try calling them to make a booking you just get disconnected.   Second : if you forget your password and you ask to reset the password the system doesn't actually send you a reset email : so you are permanently locked out.Thirdly, if you write them an email to their support team asking for them to reset your password you get a reply saying they are receiving 1000s of emails and it could be many weeks until your email will be answered.So, unless you are prepared to set up a whole new email account every time you forget your password ... its actually impossible.What sort of a company is this ?Probably the worst company in the world.
Lot of bad reviews but we enjoyed our journey. why would you fly when you can get to london from paris so quickly. we were thrilled with the experience. fast comfortable and easy.

The Eurostar experience: Book Paris for two July 2021, trains get cancelled due to COVID, e-vouchers sent (that expire 31 Dec 2021). Rebook Paris for two Nov 2021; when applying e-voucher at checkout, error code says, ‘Sorry we can’t complete your checkout’ and provides phone number. This was our first trip on the Eurostar and were very impressed. Very comfortable seats and a lovely smooth ride. We went First Class but sadly the food included was not to my taste, so if you are a fussy eater (like me) then it would be advisable to take along your own food with you. Having only just received notification 24 hours before our departure that we had to get antigen tests for our two 16 year old children, panic levels were at their highest. The WORST experience of my life. They give you no information ahead of time about COVID restriction changes to the UK. I love the Eurostar and so hope it survives this pandemic. It's a brilliiant way to travel and the best way to arrive in Brussels as it takes you right to the heart of the city in barely more than 2 hours. Your ticket includes onward travel to a variety of other Brussels stations via rail services which are easy to navigate.The process at both ends is really so easy - although that has no doubt changed since we left the EU (don't blame me, I voted remain!). There are strict measures in place at all stages of the journey with the wearing of masks mandatory and you will always be seated with only those you are actually travelling with - for solo travellers like me that means you get an empty seat next to you. The only issue is of course the lack of catering - you know this though when you book and it's easy to take stuff with you as unlike airlines there are no restrictions on liquids. The wifi was for some reason switched off as well but for us Brits who still have access to roaming within the EU this is not such as issue either - it makes it a little slower that's all and cuts out when you go through the tunnel. I would definately travel this way again as to me it's so much quicker and easier than flying - and feels a lot safer as well.
