To be frank Eurostar has done a poor job accomodating it's customers whilst adhering to social distancing measures.Promotional advertising even that shown onboard is still aimed at BC times but the price we paid for a day trip to Paris was definitely more than the from £54 return; three times more and for that you receive nothing more than the train ride.All catering onboard has ceased from the buffet car to the meals served in Premier/Business class.Announcements strongly advise you to bring your own food and drink, which is all well and good but when catching the last train back from Gare Du Nord. The only shops open in the station are mainly selling sweets and in the Eurostar lounge it's a choice between the vending machine and Hotel Chocolat.Although if you want to drink spirits the whole way, Duty Free is open.Onboard also no reason is given for the wifi being unavailable.At St Pancras you're made to complete what looks like a hastily typed up and then photocopied form solely in French asking for your details and a declaration that you don't have any of the listed symptoms.The form is useless as no one asks for it at any point of the journey and most likely a purely reactionary move to the online form you have to complete for the UK government.This is also pointless as at Gare Du Nord when asked to show the form the immigration officer says that's fine as you go to show it and hands you a piece of paper that basically says you've shown it.Don't loose this as it's collected at St Pancras.Seating wise you may end up with a piece of paper as you check in saying your seat number has been changed. This is to ensure social distancing. But when a couple who have booked together are separated as we were, the member of staff we asked at St Pancras simply said to move sests once the train leaves.At Gare Du Nord it wasn't only our seats that were different but also our carriages. In typical French style the member of staff said, "what is the problem".Apart from all this palaver you'll also be regularly shouted at to maintain social distancing but at Gare Du Nord you can forget this as the announcement to board unlike at St Pancras whereby it's opposite carriages one at a time; is basically every man/woman unto him/herself and you all pile down to the platform en masse. Trying to avoid bumping into each other as you realise your carriage is behind you.Last but not least, hoping to join the train at Ashford, well, you can't. Direct service only from London to Paris.

One member of gate staff at London was a bit rude with a passive-aggressive “Can I help you?!” bellowed at me as I struggled to retrieve my passport within the requisite 15 seconds, but apart from her I found the staff there to be fairly helpful.It’s a shame the same cannot be said for the Border Control and security staff, who I found quite rude and arrogant, with an attitude that suggests they’re somehow doing you a favour by letting you proceed beyond their little glass cubicle (after waiting in a long, snaking queue with little regard for social distancing for 20 minutes because they can only be bothered to put two staff on, despite knowing the passenger numbers in advance). A "please" and "thank you" would be a nice touch. However, I do understand there’s probably not much Eurostar can do about this.The journey itself was pleasant, smooth and quick through to Lille and back to London. The tickets are quite pricey, but fairly reasonable considering the trains can only run at a limited capacity at the moment.It was a similar experience on the way back, with two polite and helpful Eurostar staff on arrival at the terminal, an extremely rude and shouty English border control woman, a very polite and friendly one and a really rude and an arrogant French cop.Note that you have to bring your completed 'Passenger Locator Form' with you and present it at the UK Border Control cubicle, not on the train as I’d expected, something that is not made clear. (They may ask some questions, the answers to which you’ve already provided on the form but they don't bother to read beyond your name and address.) It would be helpful to have a clear sign advising passengers to have this ready, along with their ticket and passport.Social distancing isn’t really enforced at either end but there was an announcement reminding people to wear face coverings whilst onboard.One really irritating thing at Lille was the inability to easily find the train formation so you can be in the right place to board your carriage, and the lack of platform staff to assist. There were a couple of confusing electronic signs I found eventually but I still ended up getting on carriage 10 instead 4. It was fairly empty so I stayed there for entire journey.Another annoying thing was that the WiFi didn’t work on either the outbound or return journey, regardless of whether or not we were in a tunnel.Oh, and of course the travelator and escalators weren't working at St Pancras on our return.I did find the Eurostar app pretty handy, however. It keeps details of your booking including tickets, seat reservations etc.All in all I was fairly happy with the service provided by Eurostar but there is certainly room for improvement. And don’t expect check-in to be a pleasant experience. Be prepared to queue for ages and be treated with utter contempt, like you’re a total inconvenience by the border and security people. Nice once you’re on the train though.

The Euro-Star is in a class of its own. We took the train from our hometown via Frankfurt to Brussels and then got on the Eurostar there. The speed is noticeable, but not unpleasant. Everything is clean, very comfortable and well air-conditioned (absolutely important, especially in summer). We arrived in London in no time and our return journey was easy and uncomplicated. Gladly again!

Having flown to Paris I wanted my 9 year old son and myself to experience the Eurostar to London.  It leaves from Gare do Nord when you have to clear French and UK immigration / customs. This means there are no further checks once you arrive in London. The pre is airport style security which moved pretty quickly. Once you have cleared immigration you are in the departure area which is like an airport with shops and cafes.  You then go downstairs to board the train and this process was very efficient. The train  itself was bright clean and modern. The seats were comfortable and there was a 3 pin and 2 pin charging sockets below each seat. These would allowing phones, tablets and laptops to be charged. Toilets were also clean. A screen provided useful information and kept you updated on the progress of your journey. There as a catering area further along the carriage which provided snacks, sandwiches and drinks. The train was very comfortable and made for a very pleasant journey. The Eurostar arrives Into the fantastic London St Pancras station where you can open joy others playing the piano on the concourse or have a go yourself. A very pleasant and relaxing journey from central Paris to central London.

So far, most in the travel industry have been sympathetic or we are awaiting an answer to our cancellation refunds as many reservations were non-refundable back when the world was normal. All have been courteous and sympathetic. Eurostar has lashed back at everyone I see on social media, travel sites, their own site (their FB site totally ignores the Pandemic like it doesn't exist), etc They are only offering waiver of change of date fees and from what I see on the travel sites, etc is a customer service department told to hold the line and be rude to all their customers. I wrote to customer service, got a long winded business as usual response from their FB Messenge as well as their email. Their CEO issued a ridiculous inconsiderate statement as if they were doing everyone a favor, on their website. In the current situation, who knows when we would be able to re-book and they were only giving to the end of the year despite most of Europe closed for business for the foreseeable future. We were so looking forward to doing the high speed Chunnel thing but I will make sure everyone knows about our experience with Eurostar. Obviously Eurostar believes in the business model of Profits Before People. In the long run, they will pay dearly for this.Poor business decisions and practices.

Travelled to Disney Paris last week with my family, usually we get the ferry over from Newhaven and I drive us to Disney, it's not my favourite drive, it takes about 3 plus hours and driving through the outskirts of Paris really puts you off Paris itself as it looks like a war zone and they have a big problem with gangs racing on the roads.This year my wife suggested the Eurostar, which I scoffed at because it changes my routine, which I don't like, even if it does mean avoiding my Baghdad bumper car journey.We all drove up to Ebbsfleet at 7am, clear roads on the Sunday all the way there, parked up, got some food at the MnS café, had a nice wait, kids playing and then the easiest train ride I've had into Disney.Luggage went straight to the hotel, we went straight to the park. On the way back it was just as easy despite some train delays.I don't usually like to change my routine ever, but now I won't travel to Disney Paris by any other means than the Eurostar.It's a shame it's getting some negative reviews due to Coronavirus, you'd think people would be understanding that the world is in chaos and negative energy and moaning miserable gits help no one.

Their lack of flexibility regarding their refund policy is outrageous and utterly disgusting. They refuse to refund bookings despite the fact that both France and Belgium are in lockdown, everything is closed and governments basically deemed it illegal to travel witout serious motives. First and last time I am using their services. Rude and useless customer service which ignores all customers.

In these times of "health war" Eurostar prices are exploding like frost!!! €224 for a one-way ticket obviously purchased the day before but given the health situation which is evolving from day to day it was impossible to anticipate the purchase of a ticket and some students preferred to return as quickly as possible. Great solidarity from such a company.

ZYR-QQS. My most recent journey was from Brussels-Midi to St Pancras on a Saturday Evening. I booked a standard ticket and I was allocated a seat in Standard Premium, at weekends some premium carriages can be used by standard ticket holders but without the premium extras offered.Check in and boarding was the usual mess at Brussels Midi, the departure lounge is clearly not big enough to cope with departing trains and it is not a pleasant experience. The journey in Standard Premium was nice but the ride quality on the new E320 is not as good as the original E300 train.I have used Eurostar services since they first started from London Waterloo and I was a huge fan but now I will only use Eurostar if I really need to. The fares are often quite pricey, there are deals available but there is only ever a small window of opportunity to bag the bargains. I often either fly or use the coach as using Eurostar is not quite as seamless or enjoyable as it is often portrayed.

My wife and I intended to celebrate our 1 year wedding anniversary in London / Paris. As of last night, due to COVID-19, President Trump has imposed travels bans for most of Europe. Due to this, and the risk of not being able to return to the US at the end of our trip, we made the difficult decision to cancel our plans. It has been heartbreaking for both of us, as we have been planning and looking forward to this for months. I immediately began calling travel providers and explaining the situation. American Airlines, Southwest Airlines, AirBnb, Holiday Inn have ALL been wonderful to work with, providing credits or refunds for nearly all of our costs. Eurostar on the other hand, has consistently been rude and direct in saying they will do nothing to help. As their service isn't impacted, that dictates they can't do anything for their customers. I haven't even gotten an apology or an offer to look into it more closely. We are going to lose a significant amount of money because we aren't able to go on this trip - they won't provide credit, a refund, a partial refund, nothing. If we do finally get to take this trip, you can believe we'll fly direct to Paris and/or use flight to travel between London and Paris, and I will continue to share Eurostar's terrible customer service with everyone that will listen.

I booked a train ticket from London to Paris for April about a month ago. As an addition to a work trip, I planned to visit Paris while in Europe. Due to coronavirus, many businesses are cancelling trips and encouraging less travel. Airlines have been very accommodating in waiving change fees and providing refunds during this uncertain time, especially for international trips. I will no longer be making the trip due to the virus spreading, and following CDC and WHO advise to stay home whenever possible. I gave Eurostar a call and asked if they would be granting any accommodations due to the spreading pandemic and they told me no. Given the US has also placed a travel ban on outbound flights from Paris, I find it ridiculous they still expected me to make the trip. Most major airlines understand the severity and are waiving change fees for flights, seemingly the train system would do the same.

All things considered the Eurostar from London to Amsterdam was a nice experience. I purchased Standard Premier tickets well in advance of the journey after tracking prices. Less expensive that business class flights and intra-Euro flights are crap for business class anyway (economy seat pitch with a blocked center seat). The train was spacious in the 1-2 seating, seat was wide and comfy with power port, and advance selection got a 1+1 with a full window to share with my travel partner. St. Pancreas London station signage and staff made my first trip a breeze to navigate checkin, security, and passport control then find my way to the platform. The on board staff was excellent. Light meal with beverage was served early then beverage/snack later. Train was clean and everything worked. Free Wi-Fi was okay speed. Much like flying there were delays and arrival was 20 minutes late, at least I could see my luggage the entire time, and go to the toilet anytime. All things considered this route and this journey was good for us. Unlike my Euro friends who must commute by train I find this a relaxing way to travel and the train station is right in the city center which is where I’m staying.

London to Brussels review only.Arrived to find the seat/carriage I chose was re-assigned. A real rush to get to the new carriage as the woman at the gate had said it’s a sit anywhere policy.Luckily I got another solo seat, though facing backwards. No consideration for whether this is a problem for me, as it is with some people.Late leaving, late arriving at destination.An announcement as to why was made after we entered France, by the driver, not the staff onboard who said they didn’t know.I ordered a special dietary meal, which never arrived, as it was served to the original seat I chose, and they couldn’t get me anything except a mini smoothie bottle, about 100ml.So arrived at Brussels very hungry, having been up at 5 am and travelled to London.A noisy carriage but that’s just people with no manners these days, can’t blame Eurostar for that.But at nearly £400 for a Standard Premier return ticket, I expect more. I have not given Eurostar great reviews but the service experience hasn’t improved for me, so I have to take notice of that or keep putting up with hit & miss service.

What is the point to have customer service if they can’t help you with changing destination time or date? I’m not upset about people working in customer service for Eurostar but the people that made the rules. It is really unfair because they really don’t care if you make a mistake in your booking. For some reason when I booked my return ticket it booked it twice from the same destination in my case was London Amsterdam twice instead of London Amsterdam return. So I called the customer service and they said that they couldn’t change it. So I asked if I could cancel or get a refund and no you cannot do nothing you can’t even resell a ticket so that sit is going to be there empty for nobody to use. I don’t understand what is the point of this if I am not going to use that seat why can I not give it to somebody else to use? And if the website made a mistake why can’t you help me to change the destination? if you are really that cheap and customer service is not your priority then I don’t see the point to have a customer service office in the first place. I travel a lot with Eurostar so now that I know that their customer service is so bad I don’t think I’m gonna be traveling with you anymore so you just lost a customer. Honestly if I can travel with a different train company or a plane I will do that. It’s unfair to give money to people they don’t care about others.

Best way to travel around Europe. Went to Paris with my mum recently and it was just easier then flying there. Very accessible and comfortable. The staff we were amazing too.Wish it travelled to more parts of Europe.

After booking tickets in December, Eurostar came back to me to cancel them due to strikes. Either. A refund was therefore planned within several days. However, after more than a month, I was forced to send more than 4 different emails to customer service to find out the status of my refund. Once the refund was made, I was once again forced to resend an email due to the incorrect refund amount. I travel very often with Eurostar and I have never had any problems but from now on I can tell you that their customer service is truly useless and inefficient. After several months of exchanges by email, we are now in March and I still do not have the right amount for a refund of tickets canceled by the company itself. I am very disappointed.

Eurostar's schedule was perfect for a day-trip to Paris. We left London in the early AM and were able to see many of the must see sites in Paris  and were back in time for dinner. Not the ideal way to see Paris, but with our schedule it was the only way to do it. The train was very fast and comfortable.
Wonderful service to go from the heart of London to the heart of Paris with ease.  Cost and time effective.  No issues with anything.  Very timely.

Went to London from Amsterdam by Eurostar. It's fine in one day.  You have approximately 4.5 hours to spend. An hour will be added from April because you will no longer have to change trains in Brussels

More than 25 minutes late in Paris Nord. Very fair to take a TGV at Gare de Lyon when only an hour was initially planned. In addition, in second class, many toilets are out of service or in a pitiful state. A blatant lack of maintenance despite a fairly high price. To be preferred especially without connecting with another train.

Pleasant trip. However the seats are small. In Brussels at noon, very poorly indicated and poorly organized, in addition the staff was unpleasant, on the other hand in London everything was well organized and very friendly staff.

We were taking a train for the first time, three of us.  It was recommended that we choose first class.  The only snag was not initially knowing that section 3 was the top floor of the train, so we were lost for a bit looking around.  Spacious, comfortable, friendly passengers and personnel, and breakfast.  That was a surprise to us, and it was a good breakfast.  Croissant, pastry, orange juice, yogurt, butter, jam.  The train was amazingly smooth and stable, like you almost weren't even moving.  Outlets for computers and charging phones.  Easy to sleep.  Private "cabins" available.  It's necessary to walk up/down stairs to get to the upper deck.  The upper classes are the way to go.  Spend the extra money to be packed in like a sardine.  Magazines available to read.  Interesting scenes.

Service exceeded my expectations but meal was so so, very attentive hosts on board , quick and easy ride and arrival , was rushed though at st pancras , herded through the checkin and immigration process and in the end had to wait 1 hour to board .....

Earlier this month we travelled by Eurostar, standard class, from London to Brussels and back.In view of worries about coronavirus we took Dettol cleaning antibacterial wipes and used them on our table, the back of the seat, and especially the seat arms. All the wipes were absolutely filthy, even though the carriage looked superficially clean.If Eurostar wants to avoid being a vector for an epidemic in needs to clean its carriages properly.Eurostar, you can do better than this!

single ticket to Paris, nearly 300.00 pounds. VIP lounge small, poor choice of breakfast, poor coffee. Train uncomfortable seats,unappealing colour scheme, brown, red, black, poor choice of magazines (only French), coffee poor, breakfast not changed for nearly a decade. WIFI barely working. Too much use of plastic. toilets hot air dryer not working, no paper. This is an attempt the emulate first class air travel and whilst the ambition is there, this has failed for nearly a decade, despite the same customer complaints
My first experience of traveling with Eurostar on my trip to Belgium. I found it straightforward and good value for money. Quicker than getting a plane and good value. Will definitely use again.

I have got to say that I am very disappointed and disgusted by Eurostar customer services.   My daughter lives in Paris so we use the service regularly as does my husband for regular travel.  NOT ANY MORE !!! My daughter wanted to surprise me and come home for Mothers Day and her brothers birthday.  She paid for fare out of her student loan as she is in Paris completing her 3rd year uni degree. She made a mistake on the journey requesting from london to paris (return) rather than Paris to London.  We I approached them about paying extra to amend them they inform me that this cannot be done,  THEY ONLY MAKE CHANGES TO BOOKINGS WITHIN 24 HOURS AND THEN IT IS ONLY DONE IF THEY FEEL LIKE GIVING YOU IT AS A GESTURE OF GOODWILL.  They will not even change the travellers name.  I am absolutely outraged by such a big companies response and lack of compassion.  I WILL NOT BE TRAVELLING EUROSTAR AGAIN AND WILL BE TELLING EVERYONE TO BEWARE AS THEY HAVE 0 CUSTOMER SERVICE AND COMPASSION.  I have a very sad daughter.

This is a convenient way to travel from St. Pancras Station to Paris, Brussels and Amsterdam. It's a little inconvenient because it's close to the plane and you have to clear baggage inspection and immigration inspection at least 30 minutes before departure, but the train is comfortable and you can travel from city center to city center, so I think it's convenient. Also, we occasionally have sales, so be sure to subscribe to our email newsletter to keep up with the situation.

Was slightly late for my train and they wouldn’t let me through even though there was enough time to board the train. Had to pay €49 to change my train ticket, not much of a choice considering the expensive ticket price. Obviously they understand this and see it as a way of making an easy buck, very disgusting way to treat customers!Have seen other stories of similar rigidity. Poor customer service along with expensive tickets make Eurostar the epitome Bureaucratic ugliness!

As has been pointed out by many others be extremely careful when making online bookings with Eurostar, Im usually pretty clued up but I also fell foul of just this mistake. When booking it is so easy to not get your days and times lined up correctly and then when you go ahead with the booking you suddenly notice you got the wrong date or time. I accept this was my fault but it was a genuine error, there is however a nice little button onscreen that says 'we know sometimes things change' and you click it to alter your booking. I did this within THREE MINUTES of making the mistake, because there are 4 people in my party I instantly clocked up £240 in fees to change my error. No problem I thought, it was a genuine mistake and it took only 3 minutes so Eurostar havent lost anything or had to do anything, I contacted them and had a reply 4 days later, and yep you guessed it...its my own fault and they wont give back even a single penny of the £240 fees charged on my day trip. Let me say again it is my fault for not double and triple checking but seriously I feel thats one of the cruelest things any company has ever done to me, be careful.....it has ruined our trip which is yet to come.

Great service.time table was a bit changed , but always were informed. At the end arrived on time . Service on train station was good , attendants on a train ,Fanny and Leila,  were polite and smiley . Food was ok .

No problem with this service at all.  The waiting area was very manic, probably more so than an airport, but being in central London, it worked really well for us.  I wasn't so keen on the prospect of being "under water", but the trip seemed to pass pretty quickly.I'd certainly use it again.

Eurostar has a mixed press, but I have to admit it works well for us. We have used the service on a number of occasions without serious time delays and travelling Standard Premier, enjoy the extra legroom. We are not big eaters and the meal provided suits us well, others with a bigger appetite may be looking for additional food. Our only disappointment is that with First Class understandably closest to the exit at destination arrival, it seems harsh that the standard premier always seem to be the furthest from the exit.

The service on the train is excellent. Unquestionable punctuality. Security control is not good in London, because the attention is quite poor. The immigration people are very attentive. The waiting room in London was full of people, people from different trains gathered together and there was no place to be, very uncomfortable. The train is spectacular, you can't feel the speed, the Wi-Fi is excellent even in the tunnel. The arrival in Paris was also excellent.

For the first time I tried the direct train from London to Amsterdam. Departure at 7.11am, you must pass the customs check at least half an hour in advance. I was surprised at how long this took: over half an hour. A long line shuffles through gates first for ticket control, then for baggage control, then passport control through British customs, and finally French customs. Since it was so early, everyone had left their hotel without breakfast, so there were also endless lines at Pret-a-Manger and another similar place (I couldn't find anything else). So make sure you get something to eat and drink before the checks. There is something available on the train, but there is not much choice. The train was on time. I was in 2nd class by default. I found everyone sitting close together, there was little leg room. Lots of very noisy Americans, who were already drinking vodka shots at 9 o'clock for the extra volume. Including the trip from the hotel (near St. Pancras) to the station and being there in advance, the journey to my front door took 6 hours for me, flying took me 4 hours. As far as I'm concerned, not a great success, next time I'll first check the prices for 1st class tickets and then make the decision, also in the context of the environment.

This review relates to the Eurostar ski train - outward travel on the 1st February 2020 and our return journey on the 8th.We don’t really enjoy air travel so thought we would give Eurostar a try. Big Mistake!The queues for Security and Passport control at St Pancras are every bit as bad as at any airport and when we had passed through these there was nowhere to sit when waiting for our train. The facilities at St Pancras were inadequate. At one point there were 35 people in a queue for one of the (few) food outlets. Toilets were poorly maintained (worse than any UK airport) with queues here as well.Then to our dismay our train was delayed and delayed… Eventually 1hr 45 mins late (again we thought we might avoid this kind of thing when travelling by train!)Getting on the train was complete chaos. It was clear from the outset that there was not enough room for the amount of luggage people had with them. There were four seats in our carriage which had been reserved for luggage, but the labels on the seats indicating this were tiny and no one noticed them. Also these seats were not pointed out during any announcements. It was only when staff (eventually) came through that they advised about using these seats for luggage. Even with these seats the luggage was straying into the aisle, bags containing skis fell over several times, on one occasion nearly hitting someone and I had to move a Ski bag which ended up obstructing a door. I would think that another 4 to 8 seats would be needed to safely stow all the luggage that was on our carriage.The toilets on the train were very poor. There seemed to be an issue with loo paper dispensing – pull out one sheet and dozen would fall on the floor, making quite a mess but also meaning no loo paper at all by the end of the journey. On the return journey I found one loo covering in stains (sorry for the photo but it was just disgusting and Eurostar need to be shamed).One consistent issue was refuse. To say refuse collection was inadequate does not really paint the picture. There is clearly no system for dealing with the amount of refuse generated and I now realise this is in no way limited to the service we travelled on. I was wondering on our outward journey why so many passenger groups had bin liners with them. These it transpires were the seasoned travellers who know about the refuse collection inadequacies on Eurostar. My other photo is of the nearest bin one hour after leaving Moutiers on the return journey and this bin was not emptied for the remaining 7 hours of the journey. Yes there were a couple of occasions when crew came through the carriage with bin liners but they seemed more intent on getting from one end of the train to the other than with collecting any rubbish. We even found uncollected rubbish in the seat pocket in front of us when we got on the train at Moutiers.So Eurostar – rubbish is dealt with very effectively on cramped aircraft. There is no excuse for not dealing with it on a train. We conclude you just don’t care because your seasoned customers have just learned to live with it.We will not be joining them again.

I haven't even started my journey yet.. but I have booked my tickets 5mths in advance. Unfortunately I booked my train to Paris a day later than I wanted (or did I ? As there are plenty of complaints about Eurostars booking process on their website and I was double checking everything I did with my wife!)I went back to the site the next day, I realized, there was going to be a fee (obviously) for changing days. My booking was for 2:20pm to leave for Paris so I clicked the correct day (strangley 2:20pm when we wanted to travel had jumped up by £20 as well as the fee of £30 per passenger and the train is still empty). I may be wrong but I think this was a deliberate extortion of an additional £20 from us to travel at the same time (all other non peak times were the same price). Decided to write this as a warning to other passengers (TRIPLE CHECK YOUR BOOKING BUT EITHER WAY YOU WILL BE STUFFED IF THEIR SITE GETS IT WRONG). Reviews are showing that Eurostar is performing very badly 1.5 stars.. I am really looking forward to my trip now!!!!

Decided to take the Eurostar on its newish route to Amsterdam. Being my first experience by High-Speed rail I was impressed with the level of customer service on the outbound. Especially as it was my first trip with Eurostar.Sadly the return was a bit longer than anticipated due to the weather delaying the Thalys connection back to Brussels.  If it wasn't for that, this journey would have been seamless from start to finish.  Even though it wasn't, Eurostar booked me onto the next available service; and unlike airlines such as British Airways, the process was stress-free and overall great.

Fri 14 Feb 2020 / Sun 16 Feb 2020, x2, Valentine's weekend in BrusselsOLD stock has comfy seating; NEW stock is cheaper/nastier than new Sleazyjet seats!Fri 14 Feb - London/Brussels - Standard Premier (same seats as BUSINESS, just lesser food/drink!)Seats were comfy, and reclined well, but we had facing seats, with table in between, so our legs/seat-posts/table-posts etc all made for 2 pairs of less-than-rested legs!  However, we then checked out the other seats, especially the facing-someone's-back seats, and they reclined same, but you actually had far more legroom, so we changed our return seating for those, so that we could have a good sleep on the way back on Sunday evening!  The journey itself is very smooth, quiet, and flashes by in 2 hours!  Food was good.  Service good.Sun 16 Feb - Brussels/London - Standard Premier (same seats as BUSINESS, just lesser food/drink!)Alas, these seats were clearly far newer style, similar to how Sleazyjet has modernised their seats - sleeker, but far less padding, and seats only recline an inch or two!  ARRGGGHHHH!!!!  Our plan to sleep on the way back was thwarted, as these new-style seats have non-existent padding, so we both had a numb-bum and achy legs before we got halfway - I am 6'1" and chunky, missus is 5'6" and slim, so it should have suited at least ONE of us...  NOPE!!!On outward journey, we were talking of using again for PARIS,and from April 2020 to  AMSTERDAM...  but on the basis of the DIS-comfort of the NEW seats, we would never use Eurostar again!!!Food was CRAP on return leg too, and staff in too much of a rush to get home to provide service!

Took Eurostar from Brussels to London and return. Amazing. Simple passport control and security, smooth, effortless journey. Plenty of seats, so could move around from the allocated seat number (to avoid the person sitting beside me eating a large, smelly dinner very loudly....why is eating on train carriages even allowed?). Plenty of luggage space, fast journey. On the way back to Brussels, a storm had hit with many cancelled sea and air crossings, so I was doubly grateful to be going on Eurostar. Convenient as it takes you straight into the heart of London, rather than having to travel across London from Heathrow. Same in Brussels, connections to the central business areas are super-easy.  Everything good.

Many will say that they prefer a flight between Paris and London than taking the Eurostar. For me Eurostar is the best way to connect cities, from center to center. Time savings, similar cost, no worries about luggage (quantity and weight) are some benefits. We have taken it several times and always on time.  Sometimes there are bottlenecks in migrations but the train always leaves on time. I recommend

02/15/2030 No queues at check-in and customs at Gare du Nord.  Surprise trip for my twins' birthday with a gift from a Eurostar employee. Traveling in standard first class, it's really pleasant and they are very professional in terms of service. Thanks again for the little extra ;)

Everything worked out great.  The train was on time and fast. The carriages were largely clean. The staff very friendly. The prices in the bistro were a little more expensive, but not overpriced for a train bistro.

Use the Eurostar 3/4 times a year and so far excellent. This trip the check in and boarding was really quick and trouble free. Comfortable seating with plenty of space as only half full, maybe time of the year

We were surprised at the high standard of service and food was well above our expectation. The train took just 2.5 hours and traveled smoothly. We enjoyed the champagne and the wine with our meal although airline style had the flavours and taste.The lounges at both ends were comfortable
Quick convenient journey to Brussels. Painless security and passport control, convenient access and exit on both sides. Eurostar Business Premier lounge also worth a diversion if you have access.
We travelled from London to Brussels at the weekend. All on time and a smooth and comfortable journey.

Looking for a Hotel in Paris, worrying about where how etc  - book through Eurostar - Tim Hotel - 1 stop from Gare du nord (on the metro -lots of people dressed in red in the Metro downstairs in Gare du nord giving travel  information in english) to Gare de l'est, the Tim hotel is 5 minutes walk .or walk  from Gare du nord if you want....20 minutes .with cases not so easy , ruck sacks . easy easy , the Hotel not 4 star - but very clean - and a very good price with a good accessible location , the breakfast outside the hotel  is less expensive - mac dons and burger king if your on a budget - nearby there are many moderate priced restaurants walking distance - many nationalities - nothing to even concern about .. i have more concern in london .

My husband booked Eurostar for Xmas pressie to go to Bruges - everything was booked including interconnecting trains and then three days before we were due to travel he received a text saying Eurostar was cancelling due to strike action. Text went on to say he could get full refund but to this date have received nothing & there's only  a two month window for claiming refunds. Will never book again.

Don’t suggest you travel via Eurostar to Switzerland for a ski holiday from Ebbsfleet International. The left hand doesn’t know what the right hand is doing. We were able to take our skis on board with us heading south, but on returning they made us “check” the skis for an additional €46 and wouldn’t allow them to be offloaded at Ebbsfleet so we hVe to go to St Pancras to collect and travel back to Ebbsfleet at further additional cost. Just fly - easier, quicker, better all round experience.

We travelled to Paris from London on Eurostar and back and found the experience to be excellent - far, far better than flying. - check in - quick and efficient - we were through to the departure lounge within minutes, very little queuing and none of the hassle of airport security- journey - bang on time, and you walk straight off the train into Paris, having done all the Border checks back in London (and vice eras on the return leg)- departure lounge clean and comfortable at both ends, with decent catering available (Paris end better)- standard class was fine - you're only on for 2 and a half hours anyway, so not convinced the superior classes would be worth it, although I might give it a try just to see.- very good value.

Used from St. Pancras Station in London to Rotterdam in the Netherlands. Travel while enjoying the view from the train window that you can't enjoy on a plane. I've experienced train delays in many places, so I was glad that the train departed and arrived on time. Initially, I was planning to book a trip to Brussels, Belgium, but for some reason the fares were cheaper in Rotterdam, which is far away, so I changed my itinerary to Holland and then Belgium. If you are planning to travel to both countries, you may want to check the prices for both before making your plans.

We've taken 2 trips on the Eurostar in the past month, one in standard from London to Paris and the other in standard premium from Brussels to London.There's an enormous difference between the 2 classes with the latter far superior in the comfort and service received.On the latter, service was warm, friendly, with food and drinks at a superior level and plentiful for the trip.Seat comfort was far superior too, with far more space than economy, making the journey an overall much superior experience than its less expensive counterpart.We cannot fault the service, the food, the comfort, the space nor the wonderful crew who were always attentive and extremely pleasant.Overall it's worth every cent/penny to be in this class rather than the cheapest option.

I took a day trip from London to Brussels on Standard Premier. Check-in is easier than on a plane. The train departed on time. It was comfortable. I reserved two seats facing each other online in advance, so I was able to board without any hesitation. The morning meal in the car was bread and yogurt. I thought it would be something like this because it was mentioned in the reviews. The bread is delicious. How about a whole apple after your meal? He was handing it out. I was wondering how they were going to eat it, and one of them got an apple, bit into it, and threw the core in the trash. By the way, there is one set of trash cans in the car next to the passenger seats. In the evening, on the train, I was surprised by the small amount of food I had, comparable to an in-flight meal. There's also wine, which makes me happy. You can't see the view on the Eurostar, but it might be better at night. I couldn't see anything inside the tunnel, but when I watched the TV in the car, I thought it was like this. It took some time, but it was very enjoyable and comfortable. .

We traveled on a Sunday morning to Paris and we bought tickets for carriage 12 on a table. They changed the place at last time and we stayed on carriage 16 without a table. When we showed the tickets to this worker, after she called all people there that arrived AFTER us, she was really unhappy and not nice to us and being ironic sending us to carriage 16. When we said that we were waiting there first than the others she said “you’re not on this carriage you’re on carriage 16, thank you” very ironically. Very rude . Apart of that the train is really comfortable and the trip was enjoyable.

Going from Paris Gare du Nord: correct except for the waiting time at the endless customs control service, machine only working half way. Clean and new train but 20 minutes late arriving in London.  Return to departure from Saint Pancras: change of place and car 1 hour before departure. Old, dirty and uncomfortable train. Fast customs inspection service

Departure from Paris Gare du Nord, long or even very long control service, Eurostar late by 20 minutes. Pleasant comfort of the paddle on the outward journey. Saint pancreas return, fast control service, no waiting. Eurostar is on time with last minute seat changes at check-in. Old generation oar, impossibility of reclining the seats.

My family and I took the Eurostar from St Pancras London to Gare du Nord Paris. The security check, waiting area, custom clearance, boarding time all went very well. The ground staff and announcements were very helpful. You can buy the train tickets at St Pancras but I bought mine in advance online. If you download the Eurostar app they give you daily updates on the train schedule. This was helpful as there were train and metro strikes during our visit to Paris. The app gives you updates 3-5 days in advance of any train cancellations and give you option to switch to earlier or later trains so your travel plans are not affected. The train ride was very smooth and comfortable. You can buy food and drinks and eat onboard. They give useful information on display as the journey proceeds. There is sufficient space for luggage’s and there is toilets for your convenience. Overall 5 star thumbs customer focus Eurostar service.

I am extremely disappointed with my most recent Eurostar experience. I’d traveled on Eurostar a few times before (years ago) and had really enjoyed the journeys to Paris and Brussels. So when the new direct route to Amsterdam was announced, I was excited to go there by train - a bit more costly, but more environmentally friendly, avoids the faff at the airport and lots to see on the way, right?!? Could not have been more wrong! Firstly, on the way to Amsterdam, our train was delayed by over 40 minutes. No apology or explanation from staff, and of course no compensation at all, as you only qualify for that if your train is delayed by an hour or more.Secondly, on the way back, the booking system managed to reserve us seats on a non-existent train from Amsterdam to Brussels (because it turns out the direct London to Amsterdam service only exists during the week, you need to change if travelling on a weekend). Arriving at a station to find that the train on your ticket doesn’t exist isn’t a great way to end your holiday. After much panic and assistance from staff (not Eurostar staff, but local station staff), it turned out the train did exist, but was scheduled at a different time to what it said on our tickets. Thankfully the new departure time was not hugely different and we didn’t miss the train, especially as we needed to catch our connection in Brussels.Thirdly, arriving in Brussels to change onto the Eurostar, we found that information provided on signs and screens in the Eurostar departure lounge was extremely confusing and unhelpful. Many of our fellow passengers appeared equally confused. For example, when already inside the departure lounge (so AFTER check in and border security etc.) the screens displayed check in times (at that point completely irrelevant as passengers in the lounge had already completed check in) and no boarding times. Furthermore, we all were funnelled into the waiting area for platform 3 when the screens said our train would be from platform 1 and there was only one single tiny sign to platforms 1&2 which were both cordoned off. This would have been fine if there had been information for passengers, reassuring us to just wait for announcements and giving us a boarding time on the screens, but there wasn’t very much of that. We ended up asking staff at the info desk, who (judging by their bored and slightly annoyed expression and response) had already provided this information to pretty much all passengers, as everyone was confused and unsure.Fourthly, when we finally did board the Eurostar back home, we found that for the THIRD time (i.e. for three out of three trains booked via EuroStar), we had been allocated seats with no window or view, right next to the sections between windows. Given that most seats on a carriage have access to windows, getting seats without a view on all three journeys - when one of the reasons for taking the train was to see more of Europe - was extremely upsetting and disappointing. You’d think there’d be an algorithm in the system to prevent that from happening...Overall, this was a terrible and upsetting experience that it was definitely not worth paying the extra money for, especially when planes are cheaper and faster. Given the climate crisis, it’s extremely disappointing that a company that should encourage people to choose the train over planes is offering such an atrocious and awful service that they have rendered themselves a non-alternative to flying.

I've taken Eurostar a number of times to Brussels and to Paris. It's an efficient easy way of travelling without having to have the stress of air travel. The ticket ordering process is easily completed online and tickets can be held on your handheld device or if you prefer printed out.The terminal at St Pancras is clean and nicely laid out, the trains are modern with good facilities. Overall it's the better more environmentally conscious way for travelling to the continent. I would definitely recommend

I'm taking Eurostar for the second time this year, checking out at Gare du. North are nightmarish, with incompetent staff and very unpleasant with customers. Having arrived almost 2 hours before departure, we were not able to take the planned train because the queues were poorly managed. What a shame! However, it was perfect in London for our return. Not better the second time. Now I will take the plane.

This is how the journey to London by Eurostar begins. Two days during which I tried, without success, to buy tickets via the Eurostar website. “We are trying to connect to your bank”… and nothing. 10 times, 20 times, nothing. I removed all protections such as firewalls, VPNs... Nothing. Customer service on the phone, 17 minutes wait, “international rate”?? Then a gentleman, laconic, feeling guilty. "All our customers get there", it's my fault. No solution offered, except to pay 14 euros to buy over the phone. On the OuiSNCF website, the same tickets are much more expensive. London, you have to deserve it! But Eurostar does not deserve our congratulations. Bad picture! But the company has a train monopoly. Damage.

After a nightmare journey from home to St Pancras where my partner managed to leave his bag with his passport on the train! I spoke to an excellent member of staff that told us if we were able to retrieve the bag with the tickets in he would be able to put us on a later Eurostar free of charge. So after a very stressful morning with lots of tears, we got the bag back (it had travelled all the way to Bedford!) We spoke to the nice gentleman again, didn't catch his name but he had a beard and he put us on the next train to Paris. We eventually got to our destination, Disneyland Paris only a few hours later than planned. Would love to thank the kind staff who were very helpful and calm in dealing with two very stressed out passengers!
Great experience, first class from the waiting area in St. Pancras to entire journey. Highly recommend...clean, fast and great views along the way

We have used Eurostar to Paris three times in the past year, both standard and premier class. Check in is fast and efficient though it will be interesting to see if it passes the strains of 31st January It is pleasant to have the extra legroom and  meal with wine of premier class but I am not sure it is worth the £85 extra for such a comparatively short journey.

A game of two halves. On the way out, changes in train set caused all reservations to be void and chaos. We eventually got a seat but it was not ideal. On the way back, the services was faultless. It did seem very busy but there had been cancelled trains due to the French General Strike.

It's a very fast train and the ride took a bit more than 2 hours. It really does feel like flying... The security and the boarding in London were done very fast and it was an excellent experience!In the train you have designated seats, so if you are unlucky, you'll be riding backwards... The train was full, so no way to change seats.

Leaving in Switzerland I planned to combine a trip to London and Paris, using a flight to London, then Eurostar to Paris and TGV back to Switzerland.Bought a 1st class ticket on Eurostar (standard premiere).When it became obvious that my stay in Paris was going to be disrupted by the strikes (no metro, TGV back to Switzerland xxl) I was able to cancel my TGV ticket with a full refund without any issue.For Eurostar, I guess a 1st class standard is not enough, since I was offered a change of date (which unfortunately I can not use since no plans to travel again to London and Paris during the same trip) or I have to go through a request with my travel insurance (which means asking TGV for a letter confirming the cancellation).Well to make a story short, I can only regret that EUROSTAR does look at the situation in overall instead of just pointing that THEIR train is not xxl!I understand the strikes in France is not their fault but flexibility can be appreciated.

I traveled with my wife and two teenage sons from London (Standard Premier Class) to Paris and back (Standard Class) despite the December transit strikes.  While premier class gives you a nicer seat, quieter seating area and meal service, I'm not sure its worth the extra fare.  The journey is not long and standard gives you a decent seat and access to the buffet car.  That said; the masses do standard so expect a crowded car.  The Eurostar experience is more like flying than traveling by train with a similiar check in, baggage screening and passport inspection.  Can be more expensive than flying depending on when you buy your tickets.

We travelled as a small group. The outward train to Brussels was packed and the departure hall was most unpleasantly crowded.  The travellator to the platform was broken and boarding was a scrum. The train itself was - as said - full and while there were announcements they were incomprehensible.   The train arrived on time and took the allotted 2 hours; it seemed more!  On the return there was again a scrum to check in and board but once boarded there was a delay. Again some sort of incomprehensible announcement. The train arrived just 55min late. [Had it been an hour we could have got compensation].  There is food available to cattle class travellers in two buffets and while the staff were friendly and helpful the food could best be described as dull.

We were hesitating between flying and the Eurostar from Brussels to London. At first glance the Eurostar seemed more expensive and slower. But if you include the paid parking for the car/train to Brussels South, transport from airport to central London / N/A with Eurostar because you arrive straight in the center of London, check-in and check-out time / N/A with Eurostar. Changed the picture. In addition, you have much more certainty that the Eurostar will depart compared to an airplane. We definitely recommend the Eurostar!

Me and my family were planning to go to England for Christmas and were looking forward to it.We knew about the strike going on in France and turns out our train was to be cancelled because of the strike.We had booked that ticket a long time ago for only 50€ per person.At the last minute we tried to look for cheap and good tickets however Eurostar kindly wrote us an email giving us a ticket for a different train.We are very happy to be travelling with them and we trust them to give us good assistance in the future.
It was the first time with the Eurostar to London and it was not too bad. Train left on time and everything went smoothly.

I used it to go from London to Paris. It was a friend's birthday, so I went for a bit of luxury with the Standard Premier. Everything was comfortable, including the seats, tables, Wi-Fi, and the hot drinks they served us.
Loved the Eurostar experience.  Just wish I had booked earlier so it would have been more affordable.  Traveled comfortably and quickly to Paris!

Love these eurostar trains.  1 hour 59 minutes London to Brussels. I use once per month  As others have Standard premier (1st class) is great. especially if you get a free upgrade or upgrade for 10 euros which happens quite often.  Not sure it's worth the full 45 euros normal price!"?  Only negative is the way they do the seat allocations.  You get four single people seated in the 4 group seats with a table and a family separated.  Happened yesterday.  a lady sat next to me with two very young children in separate seats whilst 4 unconnected people had the 4 group seats with table.  I'm often sat next to someone in a seat with my back to the direction of travel when there are loads of double empty seats facing the direction of travel.  Top Tip on this route:  London to Brussels,  change to a better seat if you can. (You might have to give it up when the train stops at Lille but it's only another 30 mins to Brussels).  Brussels to London, wait until 10 mins after Lille and then change seat.  Bar/cafe - seems much cheaper to pay in £ rather than Euros.

Thoroughly enjoyed taking the Eurostar to Paris from London and return.  Far better than taking a flight and much more enjoyable with teens.  Peace was about the same as flying but far less stress, more room and just a better way to go.  Loved it!!!
Left on time. Arrived on time. Going to Paris and back. Comfortable seats. Despite the problems in France everthing was running on time.

I travelled on the Eurostar at Ebbsfleet to Brussels Midi for work on the 12th December. This is my first time using the star as oppose to the Eurotunnel by car. I couldn't have been more happy and relieved with the service I got from the staff at Ebsfleet, London and again at Brussels Midi. My boss had booked the wheelchair seats for myself and my husband who accompanied me and when I booked in the staff member instantly acknowledged the fact that I was a wheelchair user and told me what would happen without me having to find out for myself, which is pretty much the norm! She took me to passport control and told me that I could use the business lounge because there was more space for me. As we waited for our train, my anxiety began to increase because more and more people arrived in the terminal and trying to find where you need to go from a lower height than everyone else and trying to access a lift that everyone else thinks they should use before you, is somewhat daunting! I didn't need to worry because a staff member came and found me and said that as one of the toilets in my carriage wasn't working so they were moving me to the other disabled seating where I would be able to use the toilet facilities, again, I couldn't believe how much care goes into making sure that I was OK, she escorted me to the lift, so no battling crowds of people and waiting for a lift that a whole host of able bodied people pile into knowing that you simply don't have the luxury of making an alternative choice. I was greeted on the platform and told where I needed to be for the ramp.  This ramp was not what I was expecting, I'd actually laid awake the night before hoping that it wouldn't be some tiny flimsy ramp that would make my heart palpatate! Again, needn't have worried, this was a huge ramp that more than safely covered the gap and I was assisted by a member of staff who ASKED me whether he could help me, so respectful. The carriage had plenty of room and I was right next to the accessible toilet, which had been really well thought out. All this was done again in Belgium, the staff at book in acknowledged my wheelchair status and explained how things would work, a member of staff came to find me 10 minutes before everyone else was called and was given a member of staff who took me to the train and boarded me with the ramp. Once back in Blighty I was greeted by a really cheery man who asked me if I needed some help to disembark the train and told us exactly where we could access the lift to exit the station. All in all, what a great experience for someone who can't just make these journey's without others playing their part to assist. I can not wait to go back again because it took the stress away and made travelling on wheels as normal as on foot, which is a total rarety! Thank you to all at Eurostar, you were all amazing 😊

Me, el s lips and senior thereof popped on the Euro(don’t bloomin’) start for a day trip to the Brussels market.Using the service reasonably regularly expectations weren’t high as the service is functional rather than a particularly good experience. This lot have a habit of changing your seat on departure if the stock used is different than planned. You go to a lot of effort to make sure you’re sat with your compadres only for them to reallocate you seat miles away by being issued a yellow ticket upon going through boarding gates. Thankfully this didn’t happen but be wary of these snake oil whatit’s  as you don’t always get Ronsealed as it were.This journey was overcrowded and there were too many cases and bags you could barely move. They should really restrict baggage or charge for more than two bags as I don’t care for Francois’s life laundry blocking my corridor to the waterfront hole.The new train we got is less comfortable than the old stock with quite hard seats and barely any windows. It feels a bit like a prison but at least at Belmarsh your cell mate is probably more affable than the Eurostar riff raff. Cue (or should I say queue) heading to the cafe bar where a queue snaked round the whole area only to be told there was no coffee and go to the other facility.No word of a lie we went to the cafe bar around Stratford and weren’t served until we entered the Channel Tunnel with only one person serving at each bar. The fact they serve generic tut as their selection of microwave food and prepackaged nonsense there’s no excuse for the poor service. The train was quite quick reaching the Belgian capital in a rizla paper over two hours. However these new trains were more bouncy than a trampoline down at the Fountain Leisure Centre in trusty old Brentford (citation needed - confirmation on whether they have trampolines required).All in all Eurostar is a pack em in and move em on service with little focus on the customer experience. If flying was less of a pain that would be my recommendation although I may get a piercing glance from old Greta who is more bitter than a pint of ESB, although my annual carbon footprint is equivalent to a Chinese factory producing a single waving cat. THINK ABOUT IT.Buenos tardes.

I do like Eurostar’s, and Standard Premier, if you can upgrade at a reasonable price is worth it.What does annoy me, is that i always see a price promotion of say £29 each way to Paris , etc, but I can NEVER find that price. To me it’s false advertising and should be looked  into.The train itself is comfortable, the check in ( at Ebbsfleet) was fast and efficient, and the staff, very helpful.Again, my only gripe is their pricing policy. Don’t advertise a “ bargain”, when no bargain exists .If Eurostar don’t look into this, promotion policy,then the  Advertising Standards Agency ( or whatever it’s called) should, as in my opinion it is totally false advertising.

Irvine; Jean Paul and Rachid took the best care of my mother and I.This was our first time traveling out of Country (London & Paris getaway) and we booked Standard Premier tickets from London to Paris. I didn't realize that the seats I booked were "backwards" and my 72 year old mom found it very disorienting.  They immediatly helped us move to forward facing seats which really helped.  The cars and restrooms were well tended/clean and the food was great.  The service was fantastic and scenery just lovely.  *Be sure to get a photo on the platform at the London station, they have a beautiful statue of a soldier and his lady saying good-bye and a neon sign below a large clock that reads "I want my time with you"
We had a horrible Experience with David and Sara at Eurostar in St Pancras. They were very rude, not understanding, and basically stole our money. Never want to travel Eurostar again.

The Eurostar is an efficient way to get from London to Paris and which is less stressful than flying. Seats are comfortable and there is plenty of room for luggage. The boarding and disembarking process is very smooth.

Booked 4 months ahead and paid £99 for standard premium seats. The booking web site is straightforward nevertheless I managed to mess it up! A quick phone call to a very helpful man at Eurostar  secured great seats for  two with a table between us. Seats reclined and were comfortable, the carriage was quiet,  well ventilated and we were served orange juice,  yogurt, coffee, bread, jam and a croissant . Perfectly adequate.The Premium carriages are a big step up from standard.  I  took a walk through the train and thought the standard carriages were dark, cramped  and the air very stuffy. Book ahead for best prices.

Check at St Pancras Station is efficient and quick.The area for waiting is crowded and there’s not enough seating.It’s better than most train departure points but not as good as an airport.The trains are fine. Boarding is quite speedy to your assigned seat. The seat pitch was less than expected and no adjustment possible to the seat back. The train left punctually and travels at high speed at around 180 mph across the countryside very smoothly. It slows down for the channel tunnel but you wouldn’t know and ends up in central Paris Nord only 136 minutes from London.Book in advance to get best prices otherwise expect it to be pricey at the last minute.
Travelled normal service, was not a comfortable journey by any means. Seats far to shallow and hard, no leg room as on a table seat setting.Will try again but upgrade and hope that's better.

The train was on time and comfortable but I have only given it 3 stars because of the boarding at Brussels.  The first call to board at Brussels was also the last call so everyone was in a big rush along the concourse and up the slope to the train.  No explanation or other announcements.  Why are we treated as cattle when the experience could have been much more civilised?
Take this train a few times, AWAYS good. Slower this time because of the Brexit going on. Great ride not long under the ground. Very good system for boarding trains. Get there early at least a hour.

I went from the Netherlands to London by train and because I was going to live there I had to take quite a few suitcases with me. The nice thing is that when you go by train you are automatically allowed to take 2 large suitcases and 1 piece of hand luggage. You also have no problems with the weight of the suitcase because it does not matter how heavy it is. I prefer traveling by train than by plane.

In September 2019 I travelled by Eurostar from London St Pancras to Brussells. When checking in to security at this station, one is required to lift one's suitcase onto a roller conveyer which is approximately 2'6" in height. There is a notice at the end of the conveyer that states "If you have difficulty lifting your suitcase ask a member of staff for assistance". As I am in my eighties I asked a member of staff for help but help was refused. Not only was I refused help but the refusal was made in an extremely rude and offensive manner. I asked several other members of staff for help but again help was refused on each occasion. I lifted the case myself with great difficulty. Moving on to the waiting area, I found this to be very crowded with nowhere to sit down due to the overcrowding. Finally, in order to reach the platform one has to board a steeply sloped travellator. If you are not prepared for the slope you are liable to fall backwards as some travellers did. I wrote to both the Head of Security and Head of Customer Service outlining the problems experienced, and mailed the letters by recorded delivery. After three months I have yet to receive a reply from either official. If you are elderly or infirm I suggest you travel to the continent by other means.
A great way from London to Paris. The train is comfortable and the journey is fast. Beautiful scenery alternates with driving in the tunnel.

I have been warned that people in Paris won’t be friendly with you if you don’t speak French. My experience here with Paris Nord today totally changed that impression! Sany ( apologise if I spelled it in a wrong way) from the Eurostar ticket office helped me a lot to sort my reservation problems, all the nervousness just gone! Then when I was running towards the train in the high heels with my suitcase ( yeah, it was really embarrassing), Marcel the porter at the Paris Nord saved my life! I definitely was running out of breath! He carried my suitcase for me and managed to help me to jump in the train at the last minute. No words could explain how much I appreciate their great help! Without them, I won’t make it home safely and on time. I’m amazed by the hospitality of Paris Nord( Eurostar) vía Sany and Marcel, big thanks to you!

Fantastic experience on the Eurostar from London to Brussels.  Incredible how fast that thing moves.  Didn't know about the stops outside of London, going over to Brussels, but coming home it was a straight shot...under 2 hours!

First time using the Eurostar and was very impressed.All staff we met in the UK were very friendly and polite. Getting through security and passport control took no time at all.The waiting area seemed crowded when we first got in but as soon as the next train announced they were boarding it was easy to find a seat. There are only 2 shops in the terminal so take drinks with you.No delays and so much more space. The seats can recline without affecting the person behind you. Power supply's for UK and EU plugs under the seat. Very comfortable to get to Brussels.Brussels terminal was pretty much the same as London. A poor guy did fall ill in the priority boarding section but this didn't delay our trip back.Would definitely use again

So pleased that this option now goes from Rotterdam to Brussels. It’s 70 min each way. The old regular train service was over three hours (plus delays). It was crowded and unpleasant. In contrast Eurostar is fast, quiet and efficient. I used the premier option which included a vegetarian snack and drinks on this short journey and electricity for gadgets and internet.

Traveled to Paris and had access to the Business Premier Lounge.  I was really looking forward to experiencing this, however greatly disappointed.  It was 11.30 so maybe it was in between breakfast and lunch but no proper food apart from crisps, peanuts and biscuits, reminded me of a Delta Airlines lounge in the states.  There was a great selection of alcohol but unfortunately a bit early for me.

We went to Strasbourg on Eurostar on Premier and found a couple of things very annoying. On the way out the "information" desk at St. Pancras told us that he could not give us any detail but a strike in Paris could make it difficult to complete the second part of our journey. This caused us some concern and  worry, and we found this distressing for the next hour until we checked online and again with his colleague who assured us that there was no strike.On the return journey a very old train was used with no wifi (but advertised). This train also felt incredibly dirty and despite a ticket showing a table of 4 we were allocated airplane type seats. in 2's.(couples in front of us had been allocated the 4 seat tables, kindly swapped with us)Staff on the trains were fine, and the food served was better than airline food , but the land side experience needs to be improved greatly and staff much better attuned to customer service .On a good note the hotel booked thru' Eurostar  - Courdu corbeau was excellent. see separate review

Myself and two adult children flew Air France from London to Paris, an unpleasant experience. Returning to London we went Eurostar, and now I would ALWAYS recommend the train. Easier to board, quicker Customs clearance, more comfortable, more direct access to the stations either end. And cheaper.Kim W, Gippsland, Australia

A weekend in London. From the Netherlands it is not yet possible to travel directly to London with Eurostar, so first go to Brussels with the Thalys. When we arrived in Brussels, we went to the business premier lounge, had a nice cup of coffee and something to eat. They don't have sandwiches or croissants, but they do have small fruit yogurts and some small snacks like peanuts. Half an hour before departure, an announcement is made that they have started boarding and if you would please grab your things and walk towards the train. Took a seat on the train, very comfortable, 1st class. I sat at a table of 4 and each chair had a charging point under the backrest, both with a power cord and with a USB. There is WiFi on the train, which is easy to do. Entertainment on the train is available via the Eurostar application, for which you need WiFi, Eurostar Connect. Back I sat at a table for two which was also very nice. Just plenty of space and you don't have to argue with your neighbor because the table can be extended with an extendable table. In 1st class you get a small meal, which is quite manageable, but if you don't think it's enough, make sure you have something with you as an extra. Overall: good train, good connection and comfortable seating.
Much better than flying! More comfortable and spacious. Very easy check in and boarding process and good drink & meal options onboard.

We booked these tickets in advance on the Eurostar website, which was extremely easy to navigate. Great value and easier than trying to get one way flight from Paris to London. Leave yourself time for customs before gaining access to the terminal for the Eurostar. Also, bathroom at Gare du Nord are pay bathrooms until you are past customs for the Eurostar. Those are complimentary for customers with tickets.The train ride was comfortable and on time. Lovely experience and would absolutely take this again!

This is the worst form of European transport I have taken, you have to check in and they close the doors to board as if it is a flight, this takes away the convenience of traveling by train... very disorganized as there were more passengers having problems with their tickets and access to the train as well as some passengers not being able to arrive 1 minute after the check in deadline.  In summary, I don't recommend the Eurostar at all, which is very expensive.

I was travelling to Paris and when I’m on my way back from Paris to London. The train was 2-3 hours late, which result in me missing my domestic last train home. What do i get in return? a simple £27 compensation refund for being 2-3 hours late. I had to sleep at Victoria Coach Station because I couldn't book a hotel or check in after 12am and get a coach home which took me 4-5 hours. The train was ridiculously expensive due to peak hours in the morning. Next journey i am coming back from Paris to London, i was 5 mins upon checking in time, guest what ? 45 euros for ticket exchange. Pathetic they sucked the life out of you when it’s your fault, but never take the full responsible for theirs. Avoid at all costs! Cheaper to travel by flight and more reliable service!

Having traveled last year in a better class, the wifi worked very well and we traveled very well. However this year, the wifi no longer worked, the toilets were not clean, the electrical outlets were not easy to access and the staff were not attentive. In summary, very disappointed with this trip
Having decided to go to Paris for a long weekend we thought it would be better by train and it turned out to be excellent. Train, food all excellent.  Picture of beloved waiting for the train

The train lived up to all and every expectation our small, family group had for our trip from St. Pancras to Belgium. We were touring three countries to celebrate my husband's retirement and on our way to Bruges. We thoroughly enjoyed ourselves on the train and found it comfortable. Would love to go again.

I was lucky enough to be booked onto what was described as more or less a premium economy trip to Paris and back.  Here is a summary of my experience there and back.1) The Eurostar terminal in St Pancras, after you've gone through security, is like a shed with few chairs and a foreboding atmosphere.2) There's nothing special about being in premium economy.  In fact, the quality of the food is/was dreadful.3) My dad said to me when I was a kid that you should always inspect the toilets before you eat. The toilets in premium economy were dreadful. It was obvious that they hadn't been cleaned properly for a matter of days. I'm not talking about the inevitable consequences of people visiting the loos - it's that no one had taken care to clean the whole of the toilet for, perhaps, weeks.  4) I can't fault the staff. They were all wonderful.5) When I arrived at the Gare du Nord, it was easy peasy.  On my return journey from Paris to London, I was super impressed by the quality of the waiting area, the notifications for boarding, and everything else.6) The food on the return trip was equally disgusting.  I would recommend to travellers that a) they buy a standard trip located near to the buffet usually in coaches seven and eight, and b) rather than waste money in premium economy but sandwiches in Euston and in Paris.

I would highly recommend Eurostar for traveling in Europe. There are places Eurostar doesn't go, but there are places where you can connect to other places. First tip, please book ahead of time so you would get a great price and a seat as well. If you know your dates, go ahead and get a ticket. Secondly, get there at least one hour ahead of time so you can get something to eat etc. We didn't get there on time and we couldn't go to the shop and buy something. 3rd tip, The lines are long, so be patient. 4th, have your things ready to go through the security check. 5th tip after passing the security, check your train timing, our train was late more than an hour for Brussels. 6th tip, when you are passing through the international security check point, please try to go through as smooth as possible, it is slow, very slow, long and just time consuming, that is why I suggest getting there early. It is a crazy process and they take all their time to check and ask questions etc. Thank God our train was delayed because with those people checking...The good part, the train is very efficient, fast and get you where you need to go. Also, they will accommodate you and your needs. The surprising part, we received a voucher because of the delay, it was a surprise and very nice. That is why I recommend highly Eurostar. I hope to see more Eurostar connections in the future. My last tip is Don't wait buy your ticket and have a piece of mind because the prices do go up and very high... For example, the ticket I bought was 3 times the value afterwards....Enjoy your travel!... Next stop Brussels!

The passport control people and the staff aboard the trains are great. With an upgrade the journey was very comfortable and the meal served was very acceptable. So what' s my problem? The terminal itself. The security staff are vile: bullying and devoid of any people skills whatsoever. Jobsworths with attitude sums them up. And the over-crowding was dreadful. It seemed routine and hadn't arisen because of any cancellations or unforeseen circumstances.  So many people were crammed in that there was not enough seating and passengers had to sit on the floor. This seemed dangerous as well as uncomfortable, especially when bored little children were trying to have races on their scooters. Eurostar may claim to be victims of their own success but they really need to sort out their terminal before someone comes a cropper.

I went with my family from London to Paris, but we paid an absurd price, as we left to buy 3 days before! Anyone interested in going, buy in advance! So that what happened to me doesn't happen!!!! And the season is too hot, as they are not prepared for the heat!

Did Paris in a day on our own from London.  Eurostar was fast easy and very comfortable.  TIP:  Tickets can get expensive, especially last minute, we checked out tour companies and bought "Paris on your own" package, which included TGV, Paris boat tour and Paris transit pass for less than TGV tickets alone on eurostar website.

The Eurostar is a comfortable TGV, allow 30 minutes to go through controls on the French side (not very well organized), less on the English side, note the smallness of the Gare du Nord boarding hall, which is really not practical.

Used Euro Star to go to Brussels for a birthday treat and it felt like as soon as you had settled in your seat, that you were at the destination.Comfortable seating but wi-fi is very intermittent despite being on the Euro Star own system, so every thing buffed or dropped out.
Such a quick way of getting around. Great service and comfortable seating. I would highly recommend taking a trip on the Eurostar.

Booking process was good with the chance to change your seat beforehand online. The check-in and boarding procedure was like a cheap charter flight - overcrowded departure lounge with no seats and expensive food options. At least there was a water bottle refill available at the London end. The train journey was quick. Coming back I tried to order a 'meal deal'.
