There was very few meal options and even though I bought one of the meal deal options offered in the on-board magazine, I had to pay the full price.

Short vesrion: do not help actual help from EUROSAR unless it is with you spending money.  LONG VERSION Travelled Standard Premier to Paris and managed to leave my glasses on the train.  Looked at the lost property page and rang the number, told to complete a form on line by the SNCF call handler.  What web page, what link?  Well this was not information she was privy too.  Complained to Eurostar, got a nice e-mail back from a chap called Adam which amounted to "sorry chum contact SNCF, can I help you with something else".  Well for more zero-help, no thanks!  You would expect for an international service they could at least have furnished a link to the right page.  UPDATE - a link has magically appeared in the last couple of day.  Interestingly "Adam" neglected to mention this

Not having to deal with airports really appealed to me when trying to get from Paris to London. It was easy to check in. Easy to board. No hassle at all. Seats were comfortable and roomy. Dont stare out the window to much you will get sick due to the things going by too quickly by your window. The trip seemed to go by so quickly and was very smooth.. only bad thing was that there was no food service on the train due to some strike. We got food before we boarded at the terminal

I would definitely recommend it as a means of travel to Paris, Brussels, Amsterdam , Much less hassle than flying.  Two hours from city center London to city center Brussels. Comfortable, quiet.  Pay the extra for standard premiere. The carriage was nice, very comfortable seat - a single by a window. The light meal and complementary drinks provided all made for a lovely train journey.  Came back to London the same way. Same excellent results.

Caught the Eurostar from London to Paris and the trip was a delight.Check in and security were a little tedious, but less so than most airports.The trip itself was smooth, on time and I watched a movie in their wifi and it worked well.Everything worked the way I needed it to.

I found the service on my recent Eurostar journey acceptable. On the outbound journey boarding was delayed about 20 minutes. No information or announcements were provided until after the booked departure time. The waiting area at London St Pancras was very crowded (considering there were only 2 departures left that evening). There was nowhere to sit, people were standing around and lying on the floor. The outbound journey was comfortable and uneventful, with useful announcements made. The same was true of the return journey.The waiting area in Paris was even more crowded than the one in London! Nowhere to sit, hardly anywhere to stand.Although the journey is fine, they need to look at facilities in the terminals in London and Paris. I found all staff I encountered pleasant and courteous.

We took this from London to Amsterdam and it was a nice, smooth ride.  I fell asleep, even.  You need to be there an hour or 90 mins prior to departure.  We arrived about 20 mins before they opened our gate and there were several folks for our train as well as others already there.  When they opened our gate, we had to go thru security, as you would at the aiport, and check your ticket and passport.  It took maybe 10 mins max.  However, as we sat on the other side, we could see the line had grown quite a bit and I couild see how getting there later would be stressful.  Once on the train, it was good, quiet and arrived on time.

I took the train from Paris to London. It left at the scheduled time, and arrived exactly at the agreed time. It is more expensive than low-cost airlines, but it leaves and arrives at central train stations.

We travelled back from Paris on the 20th October and found the Gard du Nord in chaos because of delayed and cancelled trains.The train that should have left an hour before our scheduled departure was still being loaded after our departure time and there was incorrect information on the screens, nowhere to sit and abusive staff shouting at us. We eventually left an hour and 20 minutes late and there were several announcements made on the train telling us we could claim compensation for the delay.It hadn’t occurred to us to do this but at home we tried numerous times to claim on the website and sent several emails which were ignored. When I eventually got through on the phone I was told that the train arrived only 59 minutes late and we weren’t entitled to compensation. Fine!I made a complaint about the poor service we had received but was just told why there was no compensation. This was not my point. I wanted an apology and explanation for the delay, an apology for the poor level of customer service,  and an acknowledgement that if we hadn’t been told to ask for compensation we wouldn’t have wasted any more time.Quite frankly this was worse than any low cost budget flight I’ve been on and much more expensive with customer care is not fit for purpose.

Maybe I’m a little harsh here, as we had just got off a TGV from Basel to Paris that was as smooth a train ride as I have ever experienced at speed The Eurostar we caught to London was the exact opposite You seemed to be constantly jolted in your seat and yes I understand that this train travels at slightly higher speeds than the TGV, but I don’t remember it being as bumpy as thisHaving said this, the service was excellent and we arrived in London on timeThis will not deter me from using Eurostar again as air travel is twice as bad

I recently rode the Eurostar from London St. Pancras station to Paris Gare du Nord station and then returned.  I went outbound on Standard service and returned via Standard Premier service.  Here are my observations:1)   It is really fast.  Speeds were over 150 mph much of the way.  It takes about 2 hours to get from London to Paris or the reverse.  Except perhaps by plane, this is the fastest way to get to France.  The last time I did the ferry it took me 16 hours to get to London starting from Aachen.2)   The tunnel works really well but it is a non-event.  It is all dark so you can't see anything inside.  Your ears don't even pop.3)   Standard Premier is much nicer than Standard if you can afford it.  In Standard, I was crammed in a space about the same size as an airline seat with no added services.  In Standard Premier I had a Window-Aisle seat, a table of my own, a good meal, and some pretty good wine.  Standard Premier had good power connections.4)   For internet you should have Google Chrome or Firefox on your laptop, or you need an iPhone or Google phone.  Don't count on having internet.  Outbound it worked intermittently.  Returning it did not work at all.5)   Security is pretty intense.  It is comparable to airport security, and you have to clear customs.  Note that this was before Brexit.  Post Brexit I suspect it will be worse.6)   Handicap access is not obvious.  You go up an escalator to get to the departure lounge, then down stairs to get to the train, then up stairs to get into your car.  Elevators may be there somewhere.  I saw no one with a wheelchair.  If you are handicapped, I'd call ahead to find out about access before booking.7)   The departure lounge is not all that large and has limited facilities.  It has restrooms, currency exchange, and some restaurant counters.  The restaurants aren't bad; I had a pretty good baguette at one of them.  Selection is pretty limited.  A much greater selection exists outside security at both train stations, particularly St. Pancras.8)   Get a window seat.  The scenery is worth watching, except of course in the tunnel.9)   Swaying on the last car of the train is much more pronounced than on the center cars.  If you get car sick, consider this when making your seat selection.In summary, this was a nice train trip, comparable to traveling on Thalys, the German  ICE trains, or the high speed train from Madrid to Barcelona.  The main difference is higher security and bad internet.

Outward journey from Paris to London rather good except for the queue for formalities, recent and comfortable trains; on the return, smooth formalities in London but old rotten train: seats that sink, no sockets, poorly soundproofed, old trains and lots of groups (it would be nice not to mix individual travelers and groups! Trains on time on the outward and return journeys.

Recently went to Paris for 5 days and the mode of travel there and back was, EUROSTAR. The whole set up from beginning to end was fabulous. Passenger assist made our passage through passport and border control painless. The guy pushing my wheelchair was very informative, obviously proud of his company. On board the seats were comfy and the toilets extremely roomy and well set out. We were offered a meal the minute we set off and the standard of catering excellent. I had never ending tea on the way back. It's an experience I shall remember forever.

I have travelled on Eurostar to Paris a number of times, and always enjoyed it. From London to Paris in less than 2.5 hours, and the ride is so smooth. Travelling at 180 mph across the French countryside is just fantastic. It is an incredibly positive travel experience.

Searching for a quick, convenient way to travel from London to Paris, our family reserved economy seats on Eurostar. We had reserved tickets at home online for discounted rates. After getting through French customs in London at St Pancras Station, we waited for embarking. The train was delayed about an hour.  It seems to be fairly common for a Eurostar voyage to be delayed or sometimes cancelled from what I’ve discovered. Once embarking began, we found the correct car number and seat numbers. Our large bags were put in a holding area and the small bags were put overhead. The train soon departed. Most of the time, there was no great view out the window as we passed train tracks, fields, or the darkness of the Channel Tunnel. Other times we had fallen asleep and missed it all. Not a big deal, though. In just over 2 hours, we arrived rested at Paris Gare du Nord station. We definitely recommend taking advantage of Eurostar when travelling between London, Paris and other European cities as long as tickets are reserved in advance for a reduced rate.

Eurostar is certainly not the cheapest way to get to France but arriving in Paris was convenient. We opted to skip the upgrade from London to Paris but decided to upgrade at Gare du Nord on the way back. The upgrade was €40. I was upset at myself for not opting for the €19 upgrade when booking the trip. The food in business/first class was acceptable. My only complaint was that we were on a very old train and the wifi wasn’t working. Standard ticket passengers had to pass through our business class car to get to the food car that had wifi, which made for a very busy car. Overall, acceptable and better than Amtrak in the states!

We booked for a family of 6 in standard premier . To go from Ebbsfleet to Disneyland Paris direct route on the Eurostar .Going out no problems.Coming back told to be at the train station 1 hour and 30 mins before departure, No update from anyone that our train had broken down .the passages building up at the gate but No one fromEurostar around to help or tell us What was happening eventually by looking on our mobile found out it was delayed.we were then let through and told a replacement train has been sent , and now we would  have to sit wherever and not in our allocated seat so it was a free for all , anyone could sit anywhere our party was split up , in all parts of the train and no meal as this wasn’t loaded onto the train , we were then told we could claim compensation from Eurostar, but all they are offering is a 8 pound e-ticket for Eurostar, we only use Eurostar once a year .my concern is firstly we booked for premier standard seating and didn’t get this , on the phone I was told by Customer Service there is no record of this happening on the 19/10/2019 train from Disneyland Paris only that it was late . What a surprise this was never documented that anyone could sit anywhere and that everyone who had booked Premier Standard on the train would get a refund .The manager on the Eurostar  had told us all we would get a refund for not sitting in standard Premier. Eurostar will take your money for seats you don’t get and  you will then not get a refund and just basically be told it didn’t happen . And the train was only late so I’m the one who loses money not Eurostar.
It was our first time taking the Eurostar and it was a treat, going from Paris to London.  Check in was fast and efficient.  There train was a bit late but everything was orderly.
There wasn't anything more than an "Oh, I'm so sorry about that." Miserable train maintenance regarding the toilet. The one toilet that worked was out of paper. NO euroSTAR - absolutely not

Travelling by the Eurostar was such a relief and a welcome change after the recent air flights. The seats were spacious and comfortable, with lots of leg room, and good views out the large windows. Easy to board, and easy to store hand luggage in the racks provided too. A civilised way to travel to France.

I said to my boyfriend taking the train is less of a hassle then the plane. Boy was I wrong. It started with the line that went all the way to the train station rush through security to be felt up worse the at the airport. We ran to for the train. The train before us had a malfunction we we're suppose to arrive on Amsterdam at 22:30 its now 02:17 we are still not there. All they gave us was half a glass of water at a kitkat bar. The toilets are a complete mess. No staff in sight the only came by once. Take the plane at least if there is a delay there are alternatives and you not stuck in the middle of nowhere.

We are trapped the Eurostar outside Calais. For now 2 hrs. There has been no communication the staff don’t care and the trains are heating up.I have traveled twenty times in the kay year but this is the worst. I will be into London for 12.00 instead of 9.30 have to work in the morning and look after my children. Eurostar don’t seem to care!  Don’t book this fly it’s better
This is a great train journey. We have travelled from Paris to London, then London to Brussels and could not fault it. The food was great and the service the best I have seen.
Booked a duo table in Standard Premier. Could not fault the service by the wonderful crew who were all helpful and friendly.Comfortable and clean train. Plenty of food and snacks.

Nightmare! Sent away twice with an hour before our train. No one knew what was going on. Stopped people going up the escalator. Still no info. No screen info. Nothing. We now have 20 minutes before it leaves and no on has been let through. We are not going to make the train and still haven’t a clue was us going on.

For those of us who don't know how to use the train for long journeys, this is a great option. In the app it shows the speed, which varies between 280 and 315 km/h. Don't sit down. Only when you are on the side of a highway do you notice cars quickly falling behind. A spectacle. Small meals and drinks can be purchased in the central cars.

As said because of lack of time visited London for a few days as we decided visiting Paris too.Thus we decided to use Eurostar connection between both cities.Incredible really, We knew Kings Cross St Pancras station, but not the international area.First thing I must admit is how amazed we were when noticed how many people used the Eurostar for every single connection, the station was totally crowded and our train, towards Paris, if not complete, almost. And we were talking about a Wednesday in the middle of September.The trip really confortable, the experience fantastic, the only but was that the train was a bit balancing compared to Spanish AVE trains.

We enjoyed the quiet comfort. The service was very good. Our maximum speed was 324 km/hr. The customs formalities through French border security (at Paddington) were painless. While the 54 km traverse of the chunnel (at 75 m below the English Channel is not scenic, it was a very interesting experience. The scenery until departing the UK and and after arriving at Calais was quite pleasant. We would definitely do this again.

Arrived one hour before departure to discover that our travel agent never fully confirmed the trip. Louise at premiere check in was fantastic, she calmly rebooked us and provided a lot of great advice.Go find Louise when you check in - she’s the one with the big smile.

My wife and I travelled to Brussels planning to go out on the Monday early and return on the Friday early evening. Due to a medical condition whereby my immune system is compromised I had been checking prices over a couple of weeks. Eventually I booked tickets as I thought for the correct dates and duly arrived at St Pancras early on the Monday morning. Going through security was easy and trouble free the train departed on time although it was not easy to see the carriage numbers when boarding. What a disappointment once in the carriage. The carpets were dirty the seats old and saggy and resembled an old 70's sofa. There was an uderlying smell in the carriage which just smelt of dirty people. Not what I expected. but that said we had a pleasant journey and arrived on schedule. The return journey however was not a great experience. We arrived in good time and went to go through check in only to find that due to the foibles of Eurostar's website I had accidentally booked to return on the evening of our outbound journey. We then had to re book and were charged £462.00 for return tickets on the train we thought we had booked on in the first place. Now I expected to pay for my mistake (although reading others experiences of the website I am not alone in this) but to hit us with such a punitive charge was disgraceful in my opinion. We were told to speak to Eurostar on our return which we did and got a paltry £118.00 back and told that we were lucky to get that. Back to the return journey the carriage on this occasion was much cleaner and more comfortable although as previously stated no WiFi. On balance it isn't a bad option if you don't want to fly but I won't be using them again which is a pity.

We travelled from London to BrusselsThe seats were very comfortable, better than airlines seats! We were able to choose our seats at booking which was greatWe were slightly delayed at the Eurotunnel and whilst that did not affect our plans, other passengers missed connections but the staff tried their best to sort this out with other train companies etc. The food was a little expensive but pleasant. Some of the deals were good value!

Traveled from London to Paris for one day. Probably best to get tickets in advance to get better price. Purchased ticket the night before to Paris for £169. Returned on late train for £59.Overall, train was a smooth, quiet, and relaxing ride.

Brussels South to St Pancras was a very pleasant way to travel. the stewart who offered coffee and sandwiches was very friendly but his coffee was almost undrinkable. Too bad... now with the security measures and Brexit around the corner, you now also have to queue at least an hour in advance for double pass checks B and GB and checking your luggage, no advantage of quickly taking the train.

We traveled from London to Paris for one day- ambitious but doable if you only pick a couple of things to see while i Paris.  Take the first and last departing trains.   Signs well mark where to go for eurostar departures in St Pancras station.   Allow an hour to get through security and French customs and still have time to pick up some snacks at Pret a Manger.  Standard business was nice- breakfast included coffee/tea, orange juice, a small yogurt and two rolls.  We had a table as well.  Standard class did not have a table or snacks.  Service was prompt . The train was clean and the bathroom roomy (though roomier in standard premier than standard)

Train on time, but dirty, why reserve a seat when booking when it is changed at the time of check-in, I had asked for a window and found myself with an aisle seat close to the bar car and therefore everyone jostles you during the numerous trips. Why make us arrive between 60 and 75 minutes before the departure of the train, does that make no sense?!, especially when the departure is early in the morning, it is not justified and no longer allows us to compete with the plane

it really defeats me how a Raymond Blanc allows himself to be associated with the food served in Business Premier; overcooked, tasteless chicken, a lump of butter with a bread roll, beetroot portion the size of a postage stamp and, well. The rest of the journey was without reliable WiFI (always reliable on the continental trains), poor selection of magazines and an overcrowded lounge at Gar Du Nord. 370 euros ???

Eurostar didn't care how the journey continued. The connecting train from Brussels to Cologne was no longer available that day. No information or help during the trip, no compensation after the trip. No more Eurostar!

I bought a return ticket London-Brussels for 22/08/19 on the first and last trains of the day. However, when I went to scan my return ticket on that day I was told the ticket was for the last train the next day on 23/08/19. I felt gutted and ashamed and being extremely tired because of the very long day trip, with no much battery left on my mobile and with the pressure building up because time was running fast to get the train I wanted, I decided to exchange my ticket for the one I needed and paid 182.50 euros. This was a huge blast to my poor economy as my original ticket was £29.I thought about it and concluded that this wasn't my mistake because when I booked the tickets around 21.05.19 I was looking for the cheapest and earliest journey available and I first checked on 4th August being one day after my birthday, however it was more expensive and at the end I had to take the 22nd August for being the one fitting with those plans. However, I decided to double check because I had seen some prices changed at one point on my search and I went back to check 04.08.19. To my surprise the price was what I wanted; £58 and after double checking everything I clicked on buying.When I received the confirmation email the date booked had changed to the 22.08.19 and I thought 'oh, there must have been a system problem', however, I left it there because I had already tried all possible dates and the first available one for the price I wanted after 04.08 was 22.08. I never checked the return date thinking of course that it had gone back to what I had chosen first; to go and come back on 22.08.19. I never wanted to stay the night in Brussels because I didn't want to pay for accommodation.Under these circumstances I don't feel is fair I had to pay for this ticket, I'm very sure I never made a mistake as I'm very careful when I book tickets, I double check every piece of information I need to fill or confirm. As I say above I booked for 04.08.19 and I received an email with a ticket for 22.08.19 and returning on 23.08.19, I never looked at any return ticket after the 22.08.19, so how could I have got such a ticket?After complaining to the company and London Travel Watch they refuse to offer any refund or compensation, there are other people in this page that have experienced similar issues in August. How does Eurostar defend themselves when there have been so many glitches on their system on those dates.They argue that as I got an email with the confirmed dates I am the one to blame, but how good is that when the problem is that their booking system doesn't work properly and makes mistakes?

Loved our train journey to Paris. Clean trains, very comfortable seats. We did book in economy and I was disappointed to be seated facing the wrong direction. However it was a lovely fast trip and then we caught trains all over Europe. Wonderful way to travel.
Frankly, train transport to London is good. Yes there are rules to respect! But overall nothing to say. Comfort is good but nothing more. And you arrive in the heart of London.

I traveled form London to Paris via the Eurostar train last month, and it was fantastic. The seats were comfortable. The meal was nice. The staff was pleasant. It was fast and smooth and civilized! It's great to go from downtown to downtown vs airport to airport.

more recently staff on the London-Paris route are much less efficient than in previous years, Some food (shame on you Raymond Blanc !) hasn't been changed in year, such as the breakfast. Uninspiring, bland, small portions. Magazine racks frequently out of magazines and few in English.WIFI not working. Extremely expensive

When I tried to book tickets for my return to the UK on Sunday 22nd September I was told there were no trains and no alternatives (really!!!!).I therefore had no alternative but to book a hotel in Brussels and a more expensive Monday am Eurostar back home.Imagine my surprise when I turned up at Brussels to discover that trains were running but that the last one had gone.when I contacted Eurostar customer services to at least get some of the extra cost of my ticket reimbursed they were entirely unwilling to offer any compensation.There response as follows:"I am afraid if there were engineering works due to take place we do not release the tickets for sale until the timetable is updated. In this case I believe they were cancelled and we then advertised tickets for sale. I am afraid we are unable to reimburse the extra costs due to this"

We first travelled on tge Eurostar last year and found that the help we received both in the UK and France getting to and on and off the train was brilliant. Everything was waiting and my husband just wheeled up the ramp and into the train.The access on the train was also good and it was a surprise to be in a carriage where the wheelchair was not stuck next to the toilet. We have raved and recommended travelling this way to everyone since, so you can imagine our surprise this time when our view changed.Firstly we did not get the help with directions that we had on the first trip, the ramp was not there so we were left waiting around for someone to get it, when on the train however we found it was still as pleased as last time. On arrival in Brussels again we had to wait a long time for the ramp to be bought so we could get off.The return journey was awful again we had to wait for ramp and also found we were on a new train,  my husband struggled to actually turn the chair to even get in the corridor to the cabin because it is smaller than on the original one, once in the cabin the tables and wheelchair seating have been changed and he couldn't get under the table, the wheelchair space is right next to a automatic door that is constantly opening and closing loudly and every time someone uses the toilet you get the noise and smell from that.Talking of the toilet that has also changed and is still supposed to be accessible but you cannot even get a wheelchair in there so basically the wheelchair user has to spend 2 hours on the train with no access to toilet facilities.The first train journey we had on Eurostar was also very smooth but the return journey was so bumpy you spilt everything and could not walk without losing balance.The whole return journey was stressful and uncomfortable and caused my husband anxiety. The only positive was the ramp was there waiting when we got off.We thought we had found a wheelchair friendly way to travel with Eurostar for a wheelchair user but now I will definitely not recommending it to anyone else or using it again.A new teain

Took the Eurostar from Gare du Nord to St Pancras station in London and the ride was smooth, comfortable and at 170 USD a great option to flying.  My only issues were around bathroom cleanliness and the awful lunch provided.  Pack your own sandwich and careful of those auto flush toilets. Both stations have plenty of food available and signage is very clear

From Sheffield to Lille in 6 hours- easy throughout. Plenty of luggage space on train. Easy Checkin. No charging places for phones on our train though, so carry a battery charger if you need to charge.

...the announcements in Dutch !!!!I am referring to train 9133; car 3; 27 SEP 2019.If you cannot do better than that (I did not understand a single word), better not do any announcement at all. It is an affront to all Dutch speakers !Sorry to be so harsh.

I've always been very pleased with the level of service I get from Eurostar, but this time they went above and beyond. I was away on business in Brussels when I suddenly got a call from my wife telling me that our daughter had to be taken to the A&E. I rushed over to Gare Midi to see if I could jump on an earlier train and they swiftly booked me onto the next one with no charge. They were very understanding with my situation and showed a level of empathy that was greatly appreciated given the circumstances. I look forward to travelling with Eurostar again!

Just returned from London. On the outward journey the train was 20 minutes late. On the return trip I arrived 2 1/2 hours late. My train was canceled due to an accident. This was announced and everyone had to make sure they exchanged their ticket for the next train. Complete chaos. The next train (officially an hour later) was also delayed by 75 minutes. I had a Standard Premier ticket, which normally includes a light meal. But there was no food, and we only got a drink and a tiny bag of peanuts. The compensation I was offered was 25 euros. Completely ridiculous! Unfortunately, you can only protest via chat and hope that someone will contact you. I'm still waiting. I think this is very bad for Eurostar's reputation.

I’ve just travelled to Belgium and back on my own and I’m in a wheelchair. Eurostar on the whole were excellent and helped and looked after me well. Brussels was very busy with a few people needing assistance but they got me through security and passport check and got me on the train in good time. I would definitely use Eurostar again because I felt safe and got the help I needed.

We used Eurostar, leaving on the first train in the morning and returning on the last train at night for a day trip to Paris. Booked standard coach going and the premium  class returning. No real difference other than some food that wasn't that great. The trip went really fast - both trains were on time and a very pleasant experience. Although we booked fairly last minute and paid a lot. Definitely book more in advance if you can.

We went on a trip to Disneyland in June 2018. I was quite weary about it any way as I wasn't sat with my 3 and 5 year old. luckily they managed to sit us together on the way there. on the way back, I had my son on my knee and daughter in front which was a pain as I'd paid for my 3 yo so there was a spare seat in a different carriage that I'd paid for. However, that wasn't the huge problem. on the way back, we all got taken off due to a random on the train and were waiting for 2hr before getting back on. ok.. can't be helped. better safe than sorry. when we got back to London we had missed our transport back and were told to rebook a train and we'd get paid back. Every time we've tried to get the money back they've put it off. I've lost out on over £200 thanks to them and it's put me off for life. Never ever using the Eurostar again!!
We booked the cheapest tickets yet still had a great view, very quick and comfortable trip from London to Paris at a very reasonable price.  great experience - Would do it again

First time using the Eurostar with my family and it was great! Check-in was super easy. Just scan in your e-ticket, walk through the gates to border control and then you’re through to the departure lounge. The Eurostar departed on time for Paris and I found the cabin to be spacious and perfectly lit. The ride to France was quick and smooth. Same thing for the return journey back to London. We sat on coach 8 and had the whole coach to ourselves which was a blessing. The price of some of the items in the cafe on board the train is a bit high, 3.75€ for water. Nonetheless, we arrived in London on time. There was also wifi on board which was great! Plenty of space for luggage too! HIGHLY RECOMMEND EUROSTAR!

Went on the Eurostar to Paris.  Would definitely recommend it.  It’s pretty simple and the train left on time both to and from Paris.  It’s extremely busy and was full on both journeys.  There is a beverage and bar facility available on the train.   Both stations are fairly easy to go through. The tunnel journey is about 25 minutes and overall its a lovely ride.

From St Pancras station to Gare du Nord station. Immigration inspection was similar to that at an airport, but I didn't have to check in my luggage, the lines weren't that long, and the inspection process was quick, which was great for traveling with children. Even though I was in second class, it was a short flight, so I had no problems at all and had a comfortable time. The scenery of England and France that spread out from the train window was interesting because even though they are both in Europe, they were somehow different (the shapes and colors of the buildings, the vegetation?).

My husband and I took this trip St Pancras station in London to Paris. I do all the planning and booking for our trips. As an experienced business and leisure traveler - I do my homework.  I leave the reviews to hubby and occasionally like to leave a tidbit for inexperienced — or better stated — less frequent travelers. This was a wonderfully easy trip - albeit research is in your best interest. 3 levels of tickets are offered based on your budget.  1. Standard2. Standard Premier3.  Business PremierThe first 2 tiers require one to be there a good 60 minutes prior to departure - and the waiting area is a bit cramped as more people arrive. We splurged this round and booked the Business Premier tickets. As long as we were there 10 minutes prior to departure (gates close 10 minutes before departure) - we were fine.  But - out of habit, we were there within half an hour which allowed us ample time to go through customs, security and on to the far end of the platform where our coach was. Our tickets included complimentary meal and beverage service.  They gave us 2 options and both were as satisfactory as airplane food. Hot and edible - nothing to get excited about but certainly not terribly disappointing.  I ate all of mine and was pleasantly satisfied.  I’m also not too terribly picky.  Take that with a grain of salt. The England side of the trip - wobbly and rocky and yet pleasingly relaxing. Once in France — ZOOOOOOM! You’re coasting along at high speeds on smooth rails through the countryside. This was a lovely experience and we’ll be doing this again!  My husband used the lavatory and did not complain of cleanliness or lacking any necessities. Prior to arrival - they offered to arrange a meet and greet taxi service where the driver meets you at the end of the platform with your name on a device screen or paper.  We took up the offer and found our driver waiting for us in Paris.  This made arriving at our final destination in Paris that much easier! Good luck to future travelers of Eurostar. I found their service and offerings to be most excellent overall.

First time on the Eurostar. Very pleased with everything. Train arrived on time at Ebbsfleet International, ride was smooth and straightforward. Staff all so polite and friendly. Information constantly given over tanoy. Will definitely use again.

Used the Eurostar from London to Belgium  and found its fairly average.Although the seats where comfortable, the toilets were disgusting for an early start, there was a toilet that was leaking into the the walk way, no toilet roll in another and one what was overall very unclean. The food was overpriced with very little to choose from and felt rushed making an order.

We found Eurostar an easy alternative to flying.  We breezed through the station & customs, to the platform, and to our easily identifiable car.We were served a nice lunch and beverages.  The staff was friendly and courteous.  Our car & it’s lavatory were clean.Will def use again!

The staff demonstrate a living example of how bad customer service should be... and they do that with arrogance. I have paid nearly double the price of a plane ticket to try Eurostar but it is highly not recommended.
First time on the train from London to Paris and was pleasantly surprised. Train was clean, comfortable and quiet.

Going out to Avignon was great. Coming back was everything Eurostar say doesn't happen no queues in immigration and customs.16 September saw us queue for one hour ten minutes. We had to get off the train with all our luggage and slowly shuffle through the system.Unlikely to use Eurostar again.

I bought a ticket to Amsterdam, departure was today September 16 at 7:16 a.m. I arrived 20 minutes before departure at St-Pancras and was already told that I could not take the train: I could have understood 5 or 10 minutes before departure but 20 minutes knowing that the queue was not huge, it would not have been a "death of man" to have me go straight to check-in, knowing that I only had a 30l backpack and a small bag. Your hosts are not trying to understand that I could not do earlier than 20 minutes and tell me that it is too late and that I must change my ticket when from experience the boarding of your trains is 10-15 minutes before departure. After talking with your hosts to try to make them understand the situation, they sent me directly to the ticket counter even though it was 7:10 a.m.! That's not all, I found myself paying £44 more! For a train at 5:16 p.m., I have to spend a night in Amsterdam which was not planned to pick up my bike and buy another train ticket for the city of Zwolle where I was supposed to be today... Even more money to spend, I can't afford to take a £200 business class to arrive earlier! I find it unacceptable for a team of around ten people not to be able to adapt and be immediately impartial, your hosts do not don't even try to understand! For a company that wants to satisfy its customers! Again 20min (6:56am) I don't think it was your rush hour this morning. I took the Eurostar the day before for Paris-London and it took me 15min to get through check-in and customs. I already had to wait 30min for your trains, even an hour longer, 3 hours during the customs strike! And I didn't complain. This morning I find myself exasperated waiting for the next train at 10 a.m. that I am asked to pay £44 extra even though I did not arrive late, hoping that it is early enough for your service which has no flexibility. I do not agree at all with one of your hostesses who told me that it is like at the airport, it is because it is supposed to be faster than the airport I go through your service. A dissatisfied customer with a ruined vacation.

We took this from London the Paris with Standard Premier Class.   It's worth the extra money.  The cabin felt almost empty.  The best seats on the train are 61 and 65.  They are singles facing each other with a great window.  The toilet on the car is huge.  The food was amazing.  A must if you are travelling in Europe.

As my wife has limited mobility I phoned customer services to ask for advice. At Ashford they seemed to know we we coming. Absolutely wonderful staff from arriving to boarding the train. Perfect. On the train we were approached by a man with a hand held device who asked us what we would need at Avignon. We told him. We were impressed.. Then...... We arrived at Avignon. No assistance whatsoever. No trolleys even!!!! No lift working What. A young woman, nothing to do with Eurostar, saw how distressed my wife was so she helped us down the ramps with our luggage. A slow journey because of my poor wife.No, we didn't take the return journey. We flew. Couldn't face the fiasco at Lille.

I was THAT guy! Four ladies told me “sorry you are too late” and the fifth one I asked said likewise until I pleaded...”I know you are a Very Important Person & can escort me thru” and that is when my Guardian Angel named Farah worked her unbelievable magic! So very grateful to her. All I can say is: Thank you Thank you Thank you. On my way to Amsterdam & in style. Nice trains, stellar service and a comfortable way to travel to the mainland. Bravo Eurostar!

As part of a business trip, I visited London St. Pancras International to board the Eurostar to Brussels. All the signage was clearly marked with the directions to the EuroStar Terminal.The security, similar to airport security but without the liquids problem, & passport control were relatively easy to navigate except it was a little chaotic.As an American Express Platinum card hoder, I was allowed access to the Lounge & narrowly missed the breakfast cerals but caught the pastries. Lunch was being put out as I was about to leave for my train and this consisted of peanuts, baked breads and chocolate coffee beans.The queue for the train, up a travelator, can be long but once on the platform, I was quick to board.I had upgraded to the intermediate ticket Standard Premium, which for £15 extra entitled me to a better seat, cold lunch and wine. OK but not really worth the money.Qucik journey with intermittent Wi-Fi & I was soon getting off at Brussels Midi.Better than the plan any day.I took in the loverly historical train station and its many, many shops and restaurants.

What a great way to travel to Brussels from London, it's hassle free and overall a very enjoyable experience. For us we were able to walk to our hotel from Brussels Centrale which you need to take a local train to from Brussels Midi to when you arrive. For the uninitiated and English speaking only this may present some initial concerns when you arrive at Brussels Midi but if you head to an info desk you will find getting to Centrale quite easy and this leg is also included in your ticket.The trains are clean, staff friendly and the overall experience is quite unique especially when you realise how fast you are going (I will let you find out). Would I recommend this over taking a plane, oh yeah any day. Firstly no long and boring waits at the departure lounge and getting off at the end takes a few minutes as compared to the often long waits once you land when flying. Oh and you get to see some scenery too instead of clouds, that's a plus for starters. It is reasonably priced too so for us it really was worth every cent.

First time on Eurostar, we wanted to try it out for a while.Travelled down from Edinburgh to Kings Cross, the terminal for Eurostar is next door at St Pancras, so a short walk away.We paid for Business Premier , which enabled us to skip the big lines and allows you to check in ten minutes before departure with a dedicated check in We had arrived around an hour and a half before our departure but were able to check in and go through security.The security is similar to an Airport as is passport control.With business premier you get access to the lounge which is very useful and gives you the chance to relax , work or just enjoy some peace and quiet away from the noise hubbub of the rest of the place. The ground level was very busy and so we went upstairs and was much quieter and  more space.Everything we found was self service, coffee, tea, juice, croissants pain au chocolat  and other pastries and beverages. The staff were very helpful, albeit there seemed to be some confusion about the time of serving of alcoholic beverages? My travel buddy wanted to have a bloody Mary, but it appeared alcoholic drinks weren`t served until after 1000am? The lounge itself is nice enough, with enough seating but it is starting to look a bit dated and some of the seats were looking frayed and it could do with a bit of a facelift.We travelled to Amsterdam direct. The train itself was comfortable enough. The seats could do with more cushioning, something like LNER have in their first class carriages. For a journey of over four hours you do want to be comfortable.The food onboard and the service was impeccable and professional and all the staff are to be congragulated on doing such a great job. Friendly and good humoured it was a very pleasent experience.

Hassle-free London to Paris direct from St Pancras International to Gare du Nord. Arrive 60 mins before at St Pancras with ticket & passport. Waiting area after clearance is small with limited food options. Actual boarding is very quick and seats/travel is comfortable with WiFi. Totally ok to bring your own food onboard (loved the M&S store at St Pancras for the options available). If you're not tied to a specific time for departure, leverage snap dot Eurostar dot com to get really good pricing on your tickets (from ~ 25 pounds one way). Else purchasing from Eurostar site was fast and easy, e-tickets arrived within minutes that could be added to eWallets. Return trip was easy as well, but plan to arrive 90 mins before departure and post-customs, the waiting area has lots of food options as well. Tip: Paris public toilets require payment/ coins before use, so definitely use the train toilets before you get off the train.

Be careful, you should not arrive at the station 30 minutes before the departure time as indicated on the ticket, but at the boarding gate, which is not the same thing. Do not listen to the advice of the staff at the station! We were sent in the wrong direction, so we arrived 3 minutes late at the gate, due to Eurostar staff. We were forced to pay €200 to be able to board! Bad faith and incompetent after-sales service. Bad food on board, discomfort, exorbitant prices. Choose any other means of transport.

An excellent option to travel from London to Paris, avoiding travel times and costs at airports, you leave very quickly from St. Pancras Station, which you arrive by metro, and you arrive at the Gare de Nord in Paris in two hours. The immigration process at the station is similar to that at the airport so it is best to arrive at least one hour in advance. If you go as a family, reserve a place for 4 with a table and Wi-Fi connection in advance, the children really enjoy it. To get better prices than an air ticket, book them months in advance and live the experience of a high-speed train.

First the good bit. The train itself was clean, quiet, smooth and very fast! London to Paris in under two and a half hours.The parts before you get on the train are awkward. At the London end the automatic passport readers at the french border control all failed simultaneously.There was some chaos, but we made the train.On the return leg the french border control was working faster than the British. This caused a mass muddle which suddenly resulted in them opening the biometric readers and redirecting the queue. Needless to say my passport couldn’t be read so I was sent back to where I came from!The train immediately before ours was half hour delayed. That meant we we allowed very little time to get on the train. In fact, not enough for my aged mother in law to get to the correct carriage.Don’t know if we were just unlucky at both ends?

It’s good not having to fly to a destination and ticket and passport checks are very quick in London. St Pancras is a fabulous station with lots to see and do.  Unfortunately once through security the area to wait for your train is very small and there is insufficient seating. This is the same in Brussels which is very small and not very clean. I fully appreciate you’re not there long but it is exceptionally cramped at both locations.  A majority of staff in London are walking around chewing gum.  We travelled Standard Premier which was lovely.  Plenty of room for luggage and staff were very polite and friendly.  I fully appreciate the food served to Standard Premier is cold but would appreciate it being at room temperature.  Everything including the cutlery felt as if it had just been taken out of the freezer.  Arrival at Amsterdam was easy and efficient arrival at London was as expected.  Cramped with long queues to leave the platform.

We decided to use Eurostar (followed by a TGV) to get to the South of France (with a change in Paris).  We booked four months in advance and found the cost (with luggage) was cheaper than flying.  Ticket gates opened 90 minutes before departure and we were soon through security, passport control was slightly slower. Unfortunately we arrived at the departure lounge prior to three trains leaving, so the place was very busy for the first half-an hour, we then had a short while of space before our train started to board 30 minutes before departure.Transfer in Paris from Gare du Nord to Gare du Lyon was simple (€1.90, via RER line D).The train was clean, departed and arrived on time, and was so much more a relaxing experience than flying.  Just one thing to note: in the buffet car it is a lot cheaper to pay in sterling than euros.
First time that I have travelled on Eurostar and would recommend it to everyone hassle free travel to Europe

We took the Eurostar from St Pancras to Lille Europe and then onto Marne La Vallee. The Eurostar going to France was lovely.  We was in Standard Premium and it was worth the money! If you can afford to upgrade to, do so. Once you're seated and the Eurostar starts moving, you're served free food. You get a choice between a meat or vegetarian meal. You also get complimentary water and wine. The seats are comfortable and you have more than enough leg room. There's space to hang your bags above your seat for easy access. The staff are nice and seemed to always have a smile on their faces. There are plug holes by every seat so if you need to charge any of your electrics, you can easily do so - you can either use a USB port or an actual charger plug as they have both by your seat.

Whenever you are running a bit late in Paris for your check in, and you are denied entrance within like 15 minutes to departure time. Pray to God so that you can fall on a kind staff to pardon you and give you access. I was refused to check in 15 minutes to departure time by one of the young female staff, whom from  the look didn't liked me, while her colleagues on the other sides were letting other passengers in, with the same departure times as me. So I  was forced to pay €49 extra to  get another ticket! I fell so sad during that trip!
I traveled to Paris and back with my family, the trip was hassle free and very comfortable, seats comfy and carriages very clean

Our family of four quite enjoyed the Eurostar train trip from London to Paris. The train was on time, seats clean and comfortable and the food OK. We were a little amused at the lack of information as to where the train was during the trip. Certainly no fan fare when you arrive in France. Ultimately a cost effect way to travel between London and Paris.

This ride is a must for anyone who have a love of trains.  The ride was as smooth as ever and the seats were extremely comfortable.  We were served a full meal with choice of beverages that was actually pleasant to eat.  Highly recommend this versus taking the plane as you don't have to worry about baggage weight, etc.

The great thing with the Eurostar is that it's so boringly effiicient and predictable. The scenery isn't great on the journey, there isn't the excitement of Easyjet (will the flight actually take off? will we be able to get our bag on the flight without hassle?) and it just runs!The seats are slightly less industrial than they used to be, which helps. Apparently it's better for the environment, per passenger kilometer, even than other trains.

Definitely the way to go when traveling between London and Paris. Saves you time have to drive out of the city and back into the city from each airport. Be sure to buy tickets 6 months out, as the further out the better the price typically.

We took the TGV to Paris to change stations and go to London on the Eurostar today.  All in all it wasn't bad.  It surprised me to have a meal served at my seat on a train if you remember 1980's airline food well I can tell you where it went.  The station experience in Paris was horrible, hunting all over the station because there were no signs until you got close, I had to find two station employees to ask where to go.  I had booked a newer Eurostar train and their was an equipment change and we ended up being in a set of four seats.  The newer train according to the crew ended up being one of the first Eurostar trains built.  I remember coming to London in 2000 and riding Eurostar to Brussels as far as I could tell this could have been the same non updated train.  But what's important is it left on time and arrived in London early, can't beat that.  I love the high speed trains in Europe.

We returned from Lille Europe to St Pancras on Eurostar train 9141 on 28th August after staying at our French holiday house. Whilst on the train a Eurostar guard approached our grand daughter and asked her name and also to check if she had her UK passport.It turns out she had dropped it in the departure lounge and a message had been sent to train staff.At first it appeared she may have to return to Lille on her Australian passport or have it brought over by courier.The train employer asked us to wait at St Pancras with him while he telephoned friends to see if they could bring the passport over for her. It arrived at St Pancras lost property later that evening and our grand daughter collected her passport the next day.What really impressed us was the time spent trying to find a solution and the kindness and assistance demonstrated by the Eurostar staff member. A credit to the company in every way.

As a family of four we went to Brussels for the day. We traveled standard going to Brussels and Standard Premier on the way back which was 40 pound each extra. The terminal at St Pancras was clean and busy, the drinks and shops expensive as would expect in these captive market businesses. Then came the rallying cry the train is now boarding and the rush began, horrendous when remembering that everyone had a seat allocated as far as I am aware. I had to pick our seats when booking on-line. the journey itself was new and whilst a little noisy from a chap having what seemed to be a meeting on his mobile for a vast portion of the time, and after a few attempts following the loss of service he thankfully resorted to e-mail as he stated to the caller at the other end. Would be nice if there were a few more announcements like we are entering the tunnel or something along those lines. The trip was just over two hours and comfortable enough for us. On the way back we were in Standard Premier and the difference was immense, we were greeted onto the train and had food served almost as soon as we set off, albeit 10 minutes late because of one passenger time was made up and we got into London 3 minutes late. The food and the team serving us was we found to be excellent. The seats were very comfortable but the downside for us was that the wi-fi was awful, very intermittent which does not go down well with two teenagers. Brussels terminal signage was confusing sending you all around the place when if you went the opposite direction would have been quicker and easier. The helpers as you come off the Eurostar were not that helpful to be honest which was disappointing but others around the terminal were very helpful but they were attached to the metro.The ticket scan, bag checks then border control where they change shifts when passengers are being ushered through, then the UK border control is a slow painful process. Then you wait and wait with not enough seats for all the passengers. I would however consider doing this again, but not again this year.

We had a lovely journey from London to Paris (and return a couple of weeks later). Checking in was quick and easy, and everything moved efficiently.Standard premier was comfortable, the staff were very friendly and helpful. The train was quiet, and we were able to enjoy our journey peacefully.It was great to be given the option to pick a vegan breakfast for my journey, but the one star was lost as this turned out to only be a few pieces of melon and a cereal bar (while my husband who isn't vegan had a large muselli with yogurt, 2 croissants, bread with jam, a danish roll). Great to be given the option, but there are many more vegan foods available these days so this was quite poor in comparison to what is out there. I had half expecting this however, so ate before we travelled. It wasn't a big problem.

They will try and make you pay out of your nose for anything and everything. Should you use this service, make sure you arrive 1hr before your train departs. While you may have no seats to sit in and wait, if you arrive early enough and have the misfortune of being stuck behind people waiting to check in, you'll be forking out an extra 49 euros per person for the unforgivable crime or getting to the ticket check 3 minutes after the posted time. NB: even if the information board says checking in and boarding doesn't begin till 20 minutes before departure, for those 3 minutes you're stuck behind passengers, you'll pay 49 euros on top of your ticket.

This is a really comfortable and fast way to travel from Brussels to London. We used it as the last leg of our train trip from Stuttgart to London. The German railways were late and delayed (not what you might expect). The only part of the journey not to be delayed was Eurostar!!Because of the delays we missed our original reservation on Eurostar but the staff quickly rebooked is onto the last train to London. Check in was as unpleasant as an airport with baggage scans, people scans and two passport controls. The waiting terminal is miserable with terrible lighting and badly designed spaces. Some parts looked like displays had been removed and the walls not repaired or repainted. There is a caffe/ bar which doesn’t look too bad but, on the whole the entire terminal feels tired and neglected. Perhaps they are waiting to see if it is worth renovating after Brexit. The actual Eurostar train is spacious and comfortable. The table seats (4 together) have foldout table sections if you need extra room to spread out. The luggage areas near the doors are generous as is the overhead storage. They also have recycling bins to separate out your rubbish which you don’t often find on trains. The bar is expensive!  Three small bottles of Prosecco and a can of beer for £20.45!  And you get to drink your Prosecco out of a plastic beaker!!A really fast and comfortable way of travelling to and from the heart of Brussels.We must have been lucky judging by the negative reviews here.

We took Eurostar from London to Brussels in August and arrived at 730 am for the 9 am train.  It took 90 mins to get through the line and we almost missed the train.  The waiting area before security and immigration was overcrowded and chaotic.  The staffs were not able to manage the volume of passengers.  The staffs did not give priority to passengers on the 9 am train.  If you take Eurostar, I strongly recommend you arrive 2 hours before the departure time.
Train was clean, modern and on time. We enjoyed the travel from London to Amsterdam and also Paris to London. Train was clean, modern and on time. WiFi worked perfect as well.

We arrived 5 minutes late (half an hour early) and were turned away abruptly. Which I can understand for the timing, less for the reception. We therefore had to get tickets from the ticket counters, which all had a large queue for the same request. (90€) Arriving in front of (French) customs, my son presents his identity card and the customs officer perfectly in his role, begins to stare straight into his eyes for more than 1 minute then asks him (sitting behind a window without activating the microphone) for his address. We barely heard him, the customs officer started to get angry between 2 text messages that he was obviously sending to his partner (smile hearts and other explicit emojis). He returns the card then when my son passes. He calls him back and starts the same most destabilizing circus again. In short... he was obviously looking for something, without success, having no answer despite his provocations. Once installed on board, I went to the toilets which were in a terrible state. Rather surprising for a departing train. The chatter of the staff on the microphone then becomes ridiculous. The backs of the chairs are so high, you feel a little suffocated (I don't know why). Only one piece of advice: take the plane!

I am a student, I am going by electric bike with my boyfriend from Brussels to London and we want to take the Eurostar with our bikes for the return. From 1: the price for a bike on board = 60 euros which is totally impossible From 2: impossible mission to reserve a place for our bikes, by chat, 2 conversations cut off by them, they reference an email address which is simply not valid. Result, only solution?? Call a toll number! I am very disappointed with their behavior and the abuse of their monopoly position because obviously we have no other options.

Travelling to France from London we decided to catch the Eurostar rather than flying to experience the Channel crossing. From the very beginning the trip was a disappointment. Our train was delayed by an hour, as was one other, and the waiting area was an overcrowded circus. When we finally boarded there were no service personnel to assist with luggage onto the train. Luggage racks are insufficient for the number of passengers. Once seated my partner and I were in different rows- despite having booked months before and with no opportunity to choose our seats. Only the kindness of an obliging passenger allowed us to exchange seats. In this day of modern technology failure to provide USB charging outlets at each seat, unless seated in business, is symptomatic of Eurostar’s failure to keep up with the times. The power plugs that are provided are under the seat and require one to be a contortionist to use them. In addition, many of them appeared not to work. The train manager provided information on the train stops in three languages but there was no digital representation for those who didn’t speak those languages. There is no information provided for customers about available food and beverage options. On arrival at Lille again there was no assistance with luggage. Altogether a disappointing experience. Eurostar needs to provide a more modern, customer friendly experience.

I traveled London to Paris mid May. My train was at 3:30 pm. I found St Pancras station to be well organized with well-marked lines for the various departures, both to London or Brussels. You go thru British passport control, then a few steps later, French passport control.  Security is similar to Airport security,  but you can keep your water bottle,  no taking out a liquids baggie, etc.There were a lot (!) of passengers in the waiting area, and not a lot of seating for everyone. Some food counters,  news shops.Once the boarding started, everything proceeded well.I was booked in first class. The seats were very comfortable,  and easy access to luggage storage. The journey was fast and easy. This was my first trip to UK, so I don't know how to compare cost/time to flying,  but I can only imagine the train is nicer.My complaint was with the food service. Due to it being mid-afternoon,  I wasn't expecting a full meal. Believe it or not, the train was helping to celebrate National Vegetarian Week. Well, Ok. But there were no non-vegetarian choices. Two choices for your sandwich. I chose the tomato basil pesto,  with a dinner roll, slice of cheese,  and a little mousse tart. The  red wine was very good. However, my sandwich bun was dry and inedible. The spread was thin and couldn't be scraped off to eat it. You could've done that with ham and cheese,  though. The "crust" of the little mousse tart, I swear was made of birdseed. When the steward came around to clear the tray, he inquired if something was wrong. I told him, and he thanked me for my feedback. No offer to bring me something else, nothing. Great disappointment for first class service and probably the only time I'll be able to take the trip. So I arrived in Paris pretty hungry. Wish I had gotten lunch at St Pancras.

In July, 2019, we took the Eurostar direct from Ashford International train station to Disneyland Paris.We were in Standard Premier class, which includes a meal served to you at your seat.There were 9 in our group, including grandparents, parents and toddlers.All were very pleased with the service.Both the station and train were clean and comfortable.The station even included a play area that the toddlers in our group very much enjoyed.The food served on board was far tastier than we had expected.All in all, a very nice way to travel between the UK and DLP.

Our first time on the Eurostar and found it really good. We traveled standard premier on the Way there and standard on the way back. Service very good and friendly staff. Comfortable seats. The only thing I would say is when you go through security you have to lift the cases up yourself on to the scanner and they were heavy. Other than that an enjoyable journey and great going in to the tunnel.

A tried to book a journey from Birmingham International all the way through to Brugge. It looked simple enough on the website. Got the times that suited me went all the way through the booked process and at the end told "Error 706", so tried three times, in the end had alive chat with the web assistant. After a long time she told me to call customer services. In the meantime I have three sets of emails telling me my insurance was booked then cancelled.Called Customer Services and eventually someone answered. Told her the problem, she checked and as calmly as anything said, "Oh yes we have charged your credit card three times" Over £1,000 pounds. She said it was a common problem when booking a connecting journey through Eurostar. Eventually managed to get a refund on two of the bookings. She sent a confirmation email which when I opened only had the Eurostar tickets and not the connection train tickets. When I questioned this 20 minutes later I was told that I had to go to a Train Station to print these tickets of. I then had to book my own insurance as they had cancelled the Insurance and couldn't add it again. Took over 4 hours to get one train ticket booked.Rubbish website, rubbish customer service, rubbish booking system.Dont try and book anything other than a standard journey on Eurostar only through them.

The train was delayed, which is no exception. But this time the delay was so long that we received compensation. However, I never saw any of the compensation back. Normally I always book online, but... 'Due to a technical error, several vouchers were registered but not sent. The voucher with a value of € 16.50 each has been made and we can redeem it for you. If you know when you want to travel, it is possible to call us so that we can make your booking and use your voucher for this.' But compensation could not be given when booking by telephone. We also had to wait a terribly long time when we arrived in Brussels to be able to go home. There were no more trains running, so they had to find an alternative. Most of them went home on their own, because it took hours before they came up with a solution. We went to a strict school just the way they treated us. The staff is not very friendly and incompetent.

Why would anyone fly between London and Paris when they can ride in style and comfort midtown to midtown??  We were provided Standard Premium tickets through our travel broker.  The coach was very comfortable with a table and power outlets.  A light meal with free drinks was a pleasant surprise.  Only drawback was the overcrowded waiting room in St. Pancras Station.  This was after going through the security check so my suggestion is to wait until shortly before departure to enter that area.

We went to Disneyland Paris in June 2019 and we travelled by Eurostar.   We stayed overnight in London the night before as our local train wouldn't get us there in time. St Pancras has a dedicated departure area for the Eurostar, although we didn't find the signage very clear, we walked past all the queues, but had no idea where we were supposed to go or what train to be on.   Information informed us kindly, that as long as we follow the train number, no matter what time it changes to, it will be the right train.    There are loads of different shops in the departure terminal, we went into M&S to buy some nice pastries and snacks for the journey.     They wouldn't allow us to queue until they had cleared the earlier train, which made sense, then they started 2 queues for the next trains.   We were booked onto the direct train to Disneyland, so went to join that queue.  The guards started to put out queuing barriers as it built up.   As we got to near the front , the attendant pulled us out of the queue and put us through the Premier line.  I queried this, but it was due to my mum's stick.    Sadly she didn't make it quite clear to us what we were supposed to do, but never mind.We went through the Premier line which was of course a lot faster, then rejoined the Standard line after the suitcase scanning , as we thought that was what we had to do,  but then saw other disabled passengers going through Premier so I think that we should have stayed there.   It was quite hard on my mum standing for so long in the queue for Passport Control.  It all felt a bit like cattle herding.Once through Passport Control it is a bit of a free for all, and we had absolutely no idea what to do next.   No signs, no assistance, but we did spot a guard in front of an escalator, who told us that the screens would tell us which escalator according to the coach that we were in.    This happened to be coach A on the way out.     Once the gates opened for boarding, we all piled on the escalator up to the platform and jumped on the train.The guard was a bit rude and unhelpful.  She came on and started shouting that the train was full and that we all needed to move our suitcases onto the overhead.   She pulled them out and asked people to put them up.   She pulled out my mums, shouted for it to go up and I told her that I couldn't lift it over my head.   She then demanded that somebody else in my party did , so I told her that my 72yo disabled mother and my 11yo child couldn't do it either!    Another passenger then kindly did it and said they would lift it down when we got there. It was all for nothing as our carriage was half empty all the way there.....    We were seated together on the way out.   We were seated in Standard, there was a power socket and a pull down tray and some legroom.We got into DLP on time and the guard put out messages along the way keeping us informed of speed, time etc.On the way back, we had to queue in a totally chaotic fashion at DLP station, people were coming up the stairs and jumping straight into the queue when we had been queueing for ages.   I think that due to my mum's mobility issues, she could have probably waited near the front and slotted in, as when we got near there, they again pulled her out and put us through a wider area with less people.    My suitcase got scanned, travel tip for you, never ever take a square box of batteries in your suitcase ....  it triggered every security that I went through!   We got a lift down to the platform , and found the area that our coach would stop in, it was all clearly marked.    A couple kindly gave up their seats for us, as seating was very limited.We had a slightly bigger train on the way back, with more leg room.  There was power socket again.   Sadly we weren't seated together on the way home, but I was sat behind my child and could see her at all times and my mum was also behind her.    The train was packed right out this time.I did go to the buffet car this time.   It was as expected, extremely expensive, but worth it as we were hungry.   I bought coffee, Pringles and chocolate and it came to around 24e.Getting off at the other end was good, again security let us go through to the lift so that my mum wasn't in a pushing scrum for the escalators.I am now looking at Eurostar for other trips, such as Amsterdam or Bruge or a quick trip to France.I would like to try Premier next time, just to avoid the queues so badly and to get the free drinks and food served at your seat.   On some trains it doesn't cost much to upgrade, I have seen it for as little as £9It is an amazingly easy way to travel and it was nice to see the French countryside as we travelled through.   The last time I went on Eurotunnel in a bus, so couldn't see a thing.

When my 13 yr old son took I’ll before boarding the train in Paris the staff couldn’t have been more helpful. They quickly booked us onto the next train and called medical staff to check him over. The trains themselves are great. Great service in first class

Taken this train service many times from London to Lille, and never had any major issues. The trains are clean, fast, and a lot more spacious and comfortable then most train services in the uk. My only complaint is it can be a bit stressful getting through security before boarding if it’s a busy day, but staff are generally helpful.

The Eurostar is an easy way to get between London & Paris, but it's expensive for what one gets. It is fast, has panoramic windows, and is convenient. Seats were somewhat comfortable, but plenty of legroom. The bathrooms (both on the train & in the terminal) were dirty, not enough seats in the waiting room, and some staff could be friendlier. I would use it again, but they could see some improvements in their service.

Eurostar is the way to travel from London to Paris. We purchased standard premier tickets allowing for assigned seating to ensure our party of 5 sat together.The train cars are clean, air conditioned, and quiet. The large windows allow you to view the beautiful English and French Countryside as the train speeds along the tracks. Each high backed seat features the ability to recline, a USB charging port, a seat back tray and even a seat back mirror.A meal is included with your ticket. After I had finished eating, I wished I would have taken a photo. We were offered the choice of two entrees, a side, a beverage and desert. I chose the curry chicken which was served with a vegetable quinoa both of which were surprisingly delicious. The perfect light little meal. To drink, a bottled water is offered in addition to your choice of soda juice or wine. To finish coffee and hot tea are offered with all of the fixings. The only downside was the condition of the restrooms. Much like an airplane bathroom, for some reason it seems as though passengers forget all of their manners when using the facilities. The woman in front of us in line did not have any consideration for other passengers or Eurostar employees that would have to clean up after her.If you can avoid the restroom during your two and a half hour journey, you will have a very pleasant and enjoyable journey.

We decided to travel form London to Paris by Eurostar and were not disappointed.  Travel time was 2.5 hours by this high speed train.  Service was excellent and we were served breakfast.  The seats were spacious and comfortable, more than you get on a plane.  Plenty of bathrooms and snack cars available.

Return trip to Avignon in standard premier. The trip to Avignon was first rate, new train, nice food and excellent service from the crew. The return was awful. Old train, noisy and uncomfortable.. It took almost an hour to get a glass of water, despite boarding on a boiling hot day. Crew were not very good, slow and a bit surly. The temperature on board was way to high. All in all a really uncomfortable journey and a complete contrast to the way out. Maybe next time, train there, fly back?

London to Paris Booked and paid for Standard Premier with the expectation of being able to provide power to my laptop on this work trip.Power socket was broken. Staff response; have n't you brought more adaptors? Problem was not the adaptor but one of the pin sockets was jammed so all the adaptors in the world would not have helped. Staff response; can't help you / can't relocate you / can't give a sh*t. In fact I know you've been polite but sod it, I'm going to walk off and ignore a passenger. Did I just hear other passengers say they (staff) don't give a sh*t? Oh well. Solution would have been; we can upgrade you for free / a partial fee / give you some or a total refund for the journey.Minimum would have been to apologise on behalf / thanks for politely bringing this to our attention / note the seat so another passenger won't be inconvenienced. Then maybe engage one the aforementioned solutions.I used my time to later provide customer feedback and complete their lengthy survey.I had one response from Customer Service weeks later. No replies since.Yes the journey is great and fun way if traveling. Is it expensive? Certainly. Is their customer service utter sh*t? Definitely.

Did a return to Paris, on the way there, we had a slight delay, which didn't really delay us. But we were kept informed of the situation whilst in London, and there wasn't much disruption caused. On the way back was plain sailing, can't fault the train at all. If you're getting a standard ticket (cheapest) you will not get any plug sockets to charge your devices, so be warned about that. The food and drink is pretty expensive, which you should expect to be fair. Bring your own food and drink, you can go through with it. But I'd definitely recommend using the Eurostar for moving between London, Brussels, Paris and Amsterdam.
Lovely and clear, you don’t have to have your euros for the toilet as it’s free. Staff very helpful and friendly

Worst train experience in my life. We took the train from London to Brussels and wanted to reach a connecting train to Germany. The Eurostar was late and the crew made a wrong announcement about changes to the subsequent connecting ICE during the ride so that around 150 people were not able to reach the ICE. My girlfriend even went to the train staff to double check their information as there was other information on Deutsche Bahn App. Instead of taking any measures to help the stranded people, including families and children, Eurostar didn't do anything, changed their arguments of defense several times, and called instead the police staff to help closing their terminal. Finally they did blame Deutsche Bahn for not being able to communicate properly and one of the managers even shouted at the crowd of 50-60 people to shut up. The only help was to advise to book an hotel on our own cost and to take any train the next day. Thanks for nothing. Never again

Booked seats months in advance from Australia, found to be an easy process.Getting through security took some time, but finally boarded and found our seats.Very comfortable and loved being able to look out at the countryside.  Food available for purchase was ok nothing special.

Didn't find the booking service an easy process.  My booking (London to Brussels) kept locking up. After hours of trying, learnt from customer service it's probably due to using a private tab on my browser, so that is something to bear in mind when booking.  Very quick process, getting off the tube in Kings X and walking through the station to the Eurostar.
