The queuing system for the trains could be easier - basically one line for all journeys and times, so have to be careful to line up at the correct time.  Quick pass through UK passport security check and luggage screening, then have to show passport again two steps away to EU passport control.  The Eurostar was quick and smooth.Chose to go with the Deluxe service to have a meal served at the seat and it was very useful having my own charging points.  The staff were courteous and it felt as comfortable as travelling on an airline economy plus service.There are no monitors for entertainment, but they have an app that can be downloaded for that, however chose not to go for that.  I will definitely consider travelling Eurostar again, but probably not during school holidays, as it was very expensive.

We travelled from Ebbsfleet to Eurodisney and back with a party of 10 and found this a great way to travel.  Getting on and off the train, with young children and lots of baggage was the most challenging part but still less than many other forms of travelDirections were clear as to where to go and stand and the train stops directly in front of you for your carriage and seats, if your in the right placeThe seats are comfortable and spacious, unlike flights.  The luggage express option is excellent and I would highly recommend for allThe buffet car was the biggest let down but it is a train so still had adequate provision but the queues are long and the prion list short.  What they do have is quality food and drink provision but stressed staff working in the area as it is constant and busyWe would definitely travel this way again. Almost stress free. I would upgrade next time though, not a. Option I was aware of when we booked

I have used the Eurostar a few times to go to Paris. It is a great way to get straight to the heart of Paris.I have always found it queues to be well organised and staff informative.It can be really busy in the terminal and hard to get a seat but once on the train it is quite comfortable.It is better to book far in advance for the best priced tickets.

Business trip to Paris - chose Eurostar over Flights, and it made the whole journey much easier (and much more comfortable) - not real difference in time, but having leg room, being able to take drinks etc through passport control, simply makes the whole thing a more pleasant experience.

Very comfortable way to travel. Oysterkaar for public transport is sold on board. Definitely make use of this because I had experience that ordering via the Internet does not always go smoothly. Unfortunately, the seat covers on many chairs were dirty and broken, as was the floor covering.

found a cheap flight to London, but our vacation started in Paris. I figured it would be easy to just take Eurostar train to Gare du Nord, but it was a major pain in the neck. In hindsight, we should have just flown to Paris. 1) it was a hassle getting from LHR to St. Pancras. Took Tube, which took an hour. 2) train station is nice, but boarding was an absolute cattle call. Not nearly enough room for everyone to sit in crowded and hot boarding area. Boarding is disorganized and must battle a sea of people (not ideal with luggage and small kids), 3) Not enough space for luggage on the train, leaving some luggage stacked in the aisles. 4) seating was confusing and uncomfortable on train, 5) Gare du Nord has same issues with crowds, and not ideal transportation from there.

We waited we'll in excess of an hour whilst a power problem in the tunnel was resolved. Eventually arriving in Gard du Nord much later than we wanted to. Would l travel on this service again... Probably even if it was just for the lovely meal and the bottle of wine...

Two trips on Eurostar this week. Both on time. Clean comfortable trains and a good journey, mostly. Three things to think about though. It is a real scrum getting on the train at Gare du Nord. I travelled standard and had screeming kids both ways. People moved out of the carriage on the way back. Can't blame this on Eurostar, however next time I'll upgrade. Finally when you get on the train remember that there is good luggage storage at both ends of the carriage. People didn't look for that!
eurostarexcellent organized ticket website, and easy to find in Paris, super wait facilities, easy customs,  train seats comfy good space. Why did I wait so long before trying, will be back.
Shortly after the gates closed we arrived at ticket control. Afterwards we had to pay almost double the reservation fee (44 pounds) as a fee to rebook in order to be able to take the next train.

Be careful, the gates close half before departure and you can no longer get on the train. That's not in the app! Since we bought the tickets online, we didn't know this and got to the train station 20 minutes before departure. There we had to be rebooked onto the next train, which cost around €50 and the WiFi didn't even work on the train. The info screens also kept crashing.

Booked a short break in Bruges and as not a great lover of flying thought I would try Eurostar. Waiting at St Pancras, got involved in the stampede for the train, bags and wheelie cases galore. Crammed in like sardines, toilets dirty, buffet car mega expensive. Then had to repeat the experience on the return today. Never again, I will fly next time.

Travelled standard premier to Brussels and back for a weekend break. Fast and efficient check in at both London and Brussels, helpful staff, and trains on time. Impressed with the onboard staff who were friendly. The seats could be a little more comfortable, but a good experience compared to air travel. Long walk to taxis and buses from the train at St Pancras which could be a problem for the elderly.

Book in advance for more reasonably priced tickets!! We chose this route because it was faster and cheaper than flying with all our bags (we booked about 3 weeks in advance). On the way back we upgraded to first class and this was definitely worth it: more space, a meal, quiet car. Trip back to London was absolutely better than the trip to Paris.

Decided to try Eurostar standard premier to Paris and have to admit we were disappointed. Checking in and the actual journey was great but the state of the train and food was awful! Dirty seats, broken seat (luckily they were able to move us) and hard, bland food. Breakfast was a hard croissant, rock hard roll and juice. Return journey, cold salmon and rice with hard roll again. Just expected it to be more plush or atleast clean for the price you pay so will probably drive or fly next time.

We decided to have a trip Brussels with an overnight stay so we booked the Eurostar fast train.  The journey out was OK; much the same as any other train and it got us to Brussels without any fuss and on time.  But on the way back we booed the Standard Premium option and we were so glad we did.  The carriage was spacious with tilting tables, power sockets for the phone or laptop and tilt back seats.  But the icing on the cake was the fresh food, wine and soft drinks. Unlike airline food, this was fresh and tasty  The service from Pascale, Brigitte and Amel was excellent.  They made the trip fun and carefree and before we knew it we were getting off of the train.  We would highly recommend Eurostar especially the upgrade to standard Premium and we can't wait to book our next trip.

I took the Eurostar between London and Paris, return. The queue tended to be long, but organized very well. It was travellers who were not understanding instructions that they were to "line up here" or "wait here", and "this line is for Paris only"... The employees I saw had the patience of saints, answering multiple travellers questions over and over. The train itself is fast and confortable. The employees on the train were all polite and the food was quite delicious. I would recommend taking the Eurostar over flying; either way you have to deal with long queues to get to your gate/platform.

we traveled From London ( St PANCRAS International Station)To Paris (  Gare du Nord ) 🇫🇷 France And back to London.EUROSTAR is a fast TRAIN 🚂 with a maximum speed of 300 kms per hour. This Train travels in under Water Tunnel. This is a Engineering Marvel.as its 75meters under Sea..( this train reaches destination in just 2 hours 16 minutes.)With lots of legroom and space to unwind, seats are designed for a comfortable  journey, Has Café Métropole, For onboard cafe drinks, snacks and meals for any time of dayImmigration is completed at starting point of journey.
We traveled Standard Premier class on a train from Brussels to London.  Wonderful 2 hour experience, efficient, on time.

The absolute worst staff ever.  They were rude, even shouting at people at times.  They gave us no information, instead opting to insult passengers.  I expect better treatment for such a premium price. The actual train was fine (nothing special), and we arrived on time.  However, save your money and just take a cheap flight.  You're more likely to be treated decently by an airline.

Used Eurostar to travel from Ashford to Disneyland Paris.The journey out was straightforward,but the journey back was awful.We got the the station two and a half hours before departure at which time the queue was already building. By an hour and a half before,when check out was due to open,there was absolute chaos with the top floor of the station full of families as well as all of the neighbouring stairways. Other than a few Eurostar staff wandering around,there was no attempt to start checking in despite their sign saying check in would start 90 minutes before departure and no notification as to what as happening. Eventually with less than an hour to go,2 check ins opened to serve hundreds of people. It was then Identified that their systems were unable to check passengers in, and it wasn’t for another 20 minutes that the first person was checked in. Things were so slow that the Eurostar staff started diverting people to the priority access,but instead of dealing with the passengers who had queued for hours,started directing people who had just arrived into the queue. The train eventually left nearly 90 minutes late,and was dirty as they had been unable to get cleaners to clean the train.The reason given by the staff for the delay was ‘additional security checks’-nothing to do with them opening the check in late then! To top it all,despite having paid to go direct to Ashford,the train was not suited for that station and we ended up going to Ebbsfleet to then catch a packed train back to Ashford where we had parked adding an extra hour to our journey.We had mistakenly thought this would be easier to travel than by air,but never again.
The train was clean and on time. Very good and fast way to go from London to central Paris. (It's faster than the plane). Seats were comfortable and there is a bar on board for snacks and drinks.

Swift check-in, despite the number of travellers. Dealt with quickly, politely and efficiently by staff. More pleasant than airport security and passport control since there is no need to remove electronic devices or liquids from your luggage.Plenty of seats in the terminal for the first train of the day, the 7.15am to Marseille on a July Sunday morning. A friendly goodbye from the staff member in the terminal as we were boarding.I have plenty of experience of Standard Premier from frequent business trips to Aachen via Brussels. It’s always pleasant but with the 6.5 hour trip to Marseille it’s even better. A light breakfast was served whilst in the tunnel. Then south of Paris, a hot lunch is served, with a choice of 2 mains for adults and a nice children’s meal. Service was friendly and top ups for coffee/tea were offered.The space in Standard Premier is great and this service to Marseille is in my view a much nicer experience than flying to nearby airports in the south of France.

Had the 07:19 from London to Marseille booked on a Monday in late July.  Arrived at the station at 06:20 and was shocked at what I saw; the queue was endless.  It went back and forth in front of the ticket gates and then around all the way back towards the Northwest end of the lobby.  But it moved fairly fast.  I scanned my ticket at around 06:50 but then it took me until almost departure time to get through security and passport control, walk up the ramp, and find my seat.  Not sure if I'd have made it had I arrived at 06:30.  The train was on time.  The legroom in standard class was just about adequate; I'm 1.9m tall.  2nd class on the German ICE is far better.

A good way to travel from London to Paris if you don’t like flying but this time we were delayed due to track work. Eurostar offered a credit which is useful if you can plan another trip within 12 months. The food in first class was edible and the wine was just ok but maybe you should eat the bread roll and book a table at a French bistro.

We booked the train direct in March and picked out our seats towards the front of the train and facing the front of the train. A month before we were due to leave were advised that they changed trains and we were allocated new seats, this time towards the back of the train. Complained but was ignored. I think is is totally wrong if you book a seat on one end of the train and facing forward to be allocated a seat opposite to our request.  ok early to get the best price as they go 4 fold towards the end.
We traveled from London to Paris.  Fast, convenient and quick customs clearance.  We traveled business class it it was roomy and comfortable.

Just travelled from London to Paris on Eurostar 9022. The train took off and arrived on time. The train was clean and comfortable. We booked Standard Premier and the included lunch was very tasty. The red wine wasn't too bad either. There was a lot of leg room and the staff were quite friendly.

I like travelling with the Eurostar.  I travelled with my mother who needed some assistance and this was perfectly organised.  Checkin and passport control was easily done.  Appreciat that a lot.There is room for improvement though.  Wifi on board doesn't really work.  The waiting room in London can barely hold all the passengers that are waiting to board.  If trains are running late, it would be nice to offer an extra drink especially with the tropical temperatures from last week.I usually travel from Lille. Checkin there is quick since only a limited amounts of passengers board from there.

I was subjected to major delays on the 24/0711:04 train from London to Brussels. I was told that in fact my train will not be stopping at at my destination (Brussels) and will terminate at Lille. Completely understand that these things happen, but the lack of communication was appalling and I was also told conflicting information of where I can get my connecting train! Which had me walking aimlessly round Lille for over 2 hours. I have received a email informing me that I will receive a partial refund has my train was 132 minutes late. Even though this was the case, they have not taken into account I arrived into Brussels FIVE hours later then planned!! Which surely should be taken into account as the service I paid for ( which was not cheap) was a direct train from London to Brussels!!!
We had an excellent trip between London and Brussels. Super fast train, clean, comfortable... lots of people in July.

The Eurostar train is a fast and a eco friendly way to travel. But there are so many delays. Expect a lot of waiting stranding in line or in the terminal where maybe 1/3 can sit. The rest have to stand. For hours. With all your luggage.

We travelled from Ebbsfleet to Disney on 14th July. The train was on time, clean and the staff were very helpful. There were individual plugs and USB ports along with an entertainment channel on the trains WiFi playing films and music. The food arrived in plenty of time and was a good snack. It contained a small bread roll and croissant with buttter, jam and a yoghurt. There was water, orange juice and tea or coffee to drink. I will say that if you are looking for something to keep you going around Disney get something else before you board or when you get there. We did the express luggage service through Disney and the member of staff that brought all of our things went through everything so we knew where we needed to be and where everything important was. Overall going out was a good trip.However, the return journey was not so good. The train was actually early so we could get in and sit down but in comparison to the train coming out it was like stepping back 20 years. The inside of the carriage looked old and worn there was one European and one UK plug between 4 of us and the plug sockets didn’t work properly as they kept on over heating and turning off, which isn’t great at 7pm when you’ve been in the park all day and everything is low on battery. But the main problem was that despite calling Eurostar twice before going on our trip once at home and once in our travel agents they hadn’t recorded my dietary requirements. This meant that all I had to eat from the meal was a bread roll and a mousse. Sadly this wasn’t a surprise given how very unhelpful the staff on the phone had been. It seems according to the first man we spoke to that there is no way to put allergies on to dietary requirements only a specific selection of alternative meals that you can’t guarantee will not contain the allergens as they won’t actually tell you what the ingredients of those meals are. I have never had this problem that not one person had a menu or list of ingredients before having travelled many times and eating in many places. The second person was more helpful and said that there was a way to record and there would be a note on the booking. However, when the food arrived there was no note on the booking and no possible alternative meal as it was the last train of the day and they had no spare meals. The hostess on the train was very good and did manage to find me extra bread rolls and butter so I had something to eat so she saved the day but this was very poor customer service from the booking team.

Nothing to compare with other bullet/ fast trains in the world, the customer service and the cost is ridiculous. My family used thinking it would be an easier and cheaper option to travel between London and Paris. It worked out to be a very expensive and was worst than flying had to be at the platform 30mins before. In actual fact with an airlines you can walk through if you had no check in luggage until 5mins prior to flying. Please do not consider Eurostar. We then took many other trains in Europe i.e. Thalys, SNCF, DB and have been on the Japanese rail. There was nothing so good about Eurostar. Do not take any customers post 30mins, but when you are in they take their time to check all tickets and many times the trains do not depart on time unlike the other bullet train companies in the world. So reconsider other options, DO NOT TRAVEL EUROSTAR as it is gauging customer money with poor service across the board.

The train was meant to be leaving at 8:12 pm yet there was one person checking all the tickets for 1000 people delaying it and making us leave at 10 because the lady was sat there making phone calls. It’s disgusting, we left at 11 ruining plans. Never taking it again and do not recommend it the staff are awful and the system is horrendous.

Normal trip, without any surprises. We booked a ticket on Eurostar to give the children the experience of a fast train trip. I don't know if it's worth it compared to low-cost flights, only because of the shorter notice you have to get to the station and because it leaves and arrives in a 'central' area of ​​the city, but the value is much higher than a flight.

Booked hotel plus train via their website for 3 days in London. Price was quite good and train ride quite ok except for a few long waiting times at check in. However, on the return journey the train was delayed by more than 1h15, meaning we missed the last bus and train home. No problem, the Eurostar staff said, we will arrange everything because the train was delayed for more than an hour and public transport is no longer an option, you can take a taxi and Eurostar will refund everything. So I took the taxi with the peace of mind that everything was fine and Eurostar would reimburse me for the taxi. However, when I asked Eurostar to refund me the next day, they said the following: The train was only delayed by 59 minutes and we only reimburse for 60 minutes. I don't know how they arrived at the 59 minutes, they didn't want to tell me, maybe they count from when you arrive in the arrival zone and not when the train actually stops and you can get off. But what bothered me most is that the staff lied to us that everything would be refunded. If they had been honest from the start it would have been different, but lying that they pay for the taxi and then saying later that they didn't is just misleading and sad that they play the game that way.

If the ticket price is right, this is way better than airports. You save the price of the train to and from airports, plus you can be at the station just 45 mins before, instead of 2 hours. The train was comfortable and we arrived as planned to Paris.
First rate travel experience, on time, clean, efficient, and pricey.  Worth the price if you want a sure thing for first rate travel each and every trip.  Eurostar is indeed a notch above.

Eurostar Ticket holders from London to Lyon beware! Eurostar will dump you at a different Paris train station than the one you will need to get to Lyon. Your only choices from there are to arrange a taxi for a 30 min trip or travel on a dangerous commuter line.   My family of 5 spent close to $800 to book Eurostar travel from London (St Pancras) to Lyon. With no warning of a need to make additional transportation arrangements or face dangerous criminals my family was deposited in Paris Gare Du Nord, a 30 minute drive to Paris Gare De Lyon for the second leg of our trip. The fastest way to get across Paris to the connecting station is by RER (D) a notoriously crime infested commuter line out of Gare Du Nord. With all of our luggage in tow we were prime targets. My husband was surrounded by men who began bumping into him creating chaos so they could grab his wallet, then jump off the train and run. We would never have put our family through this trauma had we known of the danger. We would have made our own safe transportation arrangements between stations had Eurostar given us any information about this connection. We ended up missing our connection and after two police stations, several taxis and purchase of a new set of tickets my family was seemingly robbed by criminals and then again by Eurostar for requiring us to repurchase tickets. If you are traveling from London to Lyon - DO NOT USE EUROSTAR!!!!

This is, by far, the most fun way to travel from London to Paris.   The ride is fun and you get to see a bit of the countryside, plus traveling under the Channel is fascinating.  The food in Standard Premier is excellent, and the service all around was really good.

Really fast, even on the UK side, quiet, this is the way to travel.We booked standard premier so the seats are very comfortable and breakfast served at your seat after a 7.16 departure time was very handy.Be very careful with your seat selection, many, even in premier, have restricted views.

I travelled with my wife and son from paris gare du nordcto london kings cross with eurostar on the 21st of july. The check in process at Gare du nord was fast as we all had european biometric passports and passed through security and into the waiting rooms in less than 15 minutes. On board the train i noticed that the baggage storage was not adequate for all the passengers luggage as its small . Our seats were facing towards the train route. The trip was nice. The seats were comfortable. We arrived at London Kings Cross on schedule. Over all we had a good journey that lasts for 2 hours and 20 minutes. I will for sure use Eurosrar again on my next trip  from London to mainland europe

What frustrates me about Eurostar is not how bad it is, but how much better it could be. It should be the Concorde of the 21st century, but instead you get two holding pens linked by a tube train. Cocooned by their monopoly position, Eurostar can charge what they want for whatever they want, and you get the feeling that they want you to know it. I paid for standard premiere class, but we were on one of the old, tatty trains, and I wasn't really sure it was worth the money. I suppose there was a bit more leg room, but spacious it was not - and I am no Goliath. Our electric socket didn't work either, so I couldn't even electrocute myself. Standard premiere is supposed to come with a meal. Now, I've been luckier with meals in the past, but this train was due to arrive in London at 11:43 (or 12:43 French time) so our bean-counting chums at Eurostar decided that they could get away with charging for a meal and then serving up a couple of croissants and a cup of coffee. It wasn't terrible, but it wasn't a meal. Had they wanted to impress, they could have done a full English, or a brunch, or thrown in a glass of bubbly to take the edges off the pain. They did not.Service was good throughout. Occasionally the mask slipped and you could tell that the crew were dreaming of working in a more welcoming environment, like Belmarsh. But to their credit they didn't take it out on the passengers. We were fellow sufferers rolling through purgatory together; we formed a bond.But it's not the train that really gets you down, it's the check in. Paris is worse than London, but both are bad. This time was no exception. Grim-faced, we stood, dragooned in stationary lines. Then shuffling, defeated through shifting serpentines governed by rules beyond understanding, or perhaps by none. Finally we were herded into the tiny detention block of a departure lounge, where a lucky few gained the brief mercy of a misericord and a coffee in a paper cup. The glamour of rail travel lives on with Eurostar.In the end, we got from Paris to London. It was quick, and it was on time. I know we will continue to use Eurostar, but I also know that if there was any halfway reasonable alternative, then we wouldn't.

We had already been poorly received by the Eurostar staff when we made our reservation over the phone. The train staff finally convinced us. They are all very very unpleasant. However, clean train and on time.

Took a trip to Lille for 2 nights on Eurostar.Delay on train outbound but in the end only about 20 minutes. Train was newer train and all good.Return journey 2 and a half our delay! They called us to departure lounge at correct time but told us as we went through that there would be a 1 and a half hour delay! As there are only vending machines in the departure lounge and the train time was 12.35 pm, over lunch time it would have been very helpful to advise customers before so that they could buy food in the station.We did get a box of “food”, however they did not announce this, it just so happened that I noticed another traveller going up to the desk and coming back with white boxes! We finally boarded the train and were hassled by the guard to hurry up and board! We were stuck behind a family with masses of luggage so not our fault and there was no one on the train assisting with boarding. The train was a disgrace. I think it must have been running since the tunnel opened! The carpets were filthy and the seats were saggy and filthy too.We ventured to the buffet car through about 5 carriages and had to hold our breath to avoid the stench of the toilets between carriages. I don’t know how the people coped who were sat close to them as the carriages stank as well. I was only able to stomach a toilet because a lady had just come out and had sprayed loads of perfume to disguise the smell. In the buffet car there was no queuing issue, however there were 2 staff standing chatting along from the counter who ignored us and the one lady who was serving a customer, not with food but Oyster Cards for London (presumably there was a commission involved) she took at least 5-10 mins and just ignored us! Eurostar clearly have a captive clientele as they have the monopoly, but come on surely you can do better than this.I would say that St Pancras is lovely but Lille Europe is old and tired.

My wife and I took the Eurostar from London to Amsterdam.  We had not previously traveled across any of the route and were looking forward to seeing the landscape as the train crossed the countryside.  The train was clean initially and comfortable, and the ride was smooth and fast.  The problem was that we were booked for seats among 8 British teenagers who were completely out of control.  They were drinking beer the entire time, throwing trash and food on the floor and seats.  Every sentence was laced with profanity, and the more they drank the louder they became. The conversation focused on using drugs, strippers, visiting prostitutes, drinking and how to use their mum's credit cards without revealing where they'd been.  As the trip progressed they started amusing themselves by spraying water on each other and around the car. Eurostar employees came through the car a couple times but other than telling the guys to get out of their way in the aisle so they could get past they did nothing.   It was a miserable trip for us.  We had no idea this kind of conduct was condoned on trains - we'd traveled on several trains during the previous two weeks in England and experienced nothing approaching this kind of behavior on rail in the UK.  Next time we'll fly - a flight was less expensive but we wanted to see the countryside.  Never again.  The only good thing about this trip was that the train remained on the rails.  I can not say the same thing about the passengers.

This is the perfect way to travel from London to Paris. High speed and very convenient. The staff could be friendlier, but we arrive in Paris with a lot of energy and we were very excited to arrive in the center of Paris.
London to Paris - It was great. Very comfortable and it was on time. Fares were reasonable and cannot expect more than that.

Took the start for a route and first to Paris.I’ll give 5 star for their service. Well information in the station, polite and courteous immigration and staffs and pleasant journey.Comfortable seats and smooth. Will use for my next trip without hesitation

booked a return tripmfrom Calais over the weekend. Outward leg booked standard premiere as the upgrade only cost 10 euros each, the seats are a lot more comfortable with more leg room than standard class we travelled at 21:30 and had a light evening meal with a hot drink incuded in the price.Inward legtravelled standard class as the upgrade was a lot more expensive, you notice the difference between the two but not sure the price hike is worth it, on a longer trip probably so.Considering the amount of people who travel  by Eurostar the terminal at Saint Pancras is not up to doing the job.There are far too few seats in the terminal in relation to how many people were waiting for the trains , I would say at least 50 % of the people had to stand whilst waiting for their train , as Eurostar say you should be at the terminal at least one hour before, this is a long time to stand.
Not helpful, not friendly, greedy money stealers. Getting in touch with them costs a fee even. DON’T
We traveled first class and the employees on the train were more than just unfriendly. I would never take this train again. I don't even want to know how other people are treated.

Signage at the train station was a bit lacking.  The ticketing / passport control was very smoothly run.  We upgraded so we could have more leg room, but the seats were facing two other seats with a table in between.  I feel like the leg room would have been more if we didn't upgrade and didn't have seats facing others.  We did get a nice breakfast.  This was still a very convenient way to travel from London to the rest of Europe.
Huge roomy seats with lots of legroomComplimentary meal of chicken salad, roll and butter, and dessert of cake and cream and wine

This place has the worst service I’ve ever experienced from any company ever.  Our flights were delayed so we called them ahead of time to let them know we were going to need to change our train reservations.  The representatives on the phone were useless, as well as the customer service in London.  Not only would they not exchange our tickets that we told them about ahead of time, but we had to pay another thousand dollars for new tickets while getting berated and insulted by the employees in the office.  I wouldn’t recommend this service to my worst enemy.  If you want o go between Paris and London, I would recommend flying or some other form of transportation instead of using these criminals.

Travelled from Liverpool Lime Street to London Euston, 10 minute walk along Euston Road to St Pancras and checked in for Gard du Nord, Paris. Booked Eurostar Standard Premier which is similar to Virgin First Class but the train is faster, cleaner, food and wine is better and the toilets don't smell.  Considering I hadn't travelled with Eurostar previously, check in was stress free and easy at St Pancras.  The return at Gard du Nord was overcrowded and chaotic but, hey, this is France!  Travelling on this train was a pleasure - in contrast to the misery of Ryanair, Easyjet, Manchester and De Gaulle airports which I will never use if there is an alternative.

For the outward journey on 06/26/19 we had no problems: the siskin was on time, the cabin crew pleasant and correct, cleanliness also, aperitif, decent meal and no worries (we were in premium business) On the other hand, the return on 06/30/19: more than 2 hours late; the abominable business lounge toilets, the unpleasant cabin crew, no aperitif, the train was not cleaned, there were crumbs left on the floor. I told the person serving us that the service on the way out included an aperitif, she replied that they were told to hurry up and therefore minimum service. We learned over the intercom that we are entitled to compensation for the delay on the site: compensation.eurostar.com, unfortunately by filling out the form correctly, we were not entitled to compensation!!!! a real scam.

On the London-Paris route, the biggest advantages of Eurostar over air travel are reliability, comfort and convenience. The train left St Pancras punctually at 1:31pm and arrived at Gare du Nord at 4:47pm (Paris is an hour ahead). We opted for the Business Premier class, which offers priority passage through immigration (the process is already done in advance before entering France, which saves even more time), a comfortable lounge (with good seats, snacks and drinks, much better than standing in the boarding area), more space in the carriage (in configuration 1-2) and a full meal (of a reasonable standard). Getting to and from cities is also very convenient, with direct access to mass public transport (or saving several minutes in car traffic).

Our family of 4 needed to get from London to Paris during our summer vacation. After comparing air vs train we decided this would be the more interesting way to travel.  We were told to arrive 2 hours early as customs and security could take a long time.  While it was crowded they moved people through in a quick and orderly manner and we had plenty of time to spare.  We opted for the Standard Premier ticket which afforded us more space plus a meal and drink on board.  The service was exceptional, the food was quite good and it was nice to enjoy a beer while traveling through the English & French countryside.  The train is very fast, very quiet and very comfortable.  The WiFi wasn't great but we weren't working so it didn't bother us.  Arrival in France was very easy and you can get anywhere in the city from Gare du Nord via metro or taxi.  We would definitely travel by train again, would recommend the upgrade to Standard Premier and really enjoyed our experience with Eurostar.

We took the Eurostar from London to Lille and from Paris to London. The route from London was much easier to navigate at St. Pancras, but Gare du Nord in Paris was disorganized. We were in premium seating from London, and we enjoyed the service and breakfast. We would travel by train again simply because it's easier than flying; however, it would be nice to get some order into the boarding process in Paris.

London to Brussells rt with the wife. Excellent boarding and departure right on time. Very clean and comfortable ride and way less than flying as far as both time and money considering the hassle at airports anymore. Highly recommended.

It's the worst thing that happened to me in Europe. The train left with a delay of more than 2 hours due to a problem, according to them, beyond the company's control. Once it left London for Amsterdam everything went very well until it arrived in Brussels. In Brussels they left us stranded, the train officer refused to continue the trip because he had gone past his schedule due to the delay in leaving. They left us at the Brussels station and told us to take a train that was going to Amsterdam, that train was not of the same characteristics as the Eurostar, it was a local train that stopped at all stations, it did not have the amenities that I had contracted, traveling with the suitcases on the seats, not to mention that I was traveling with my 11-month-old baby plus her stroller. But it didn't end there, the train that was supposed to leave us in Amsterdam ended up in Rotterdam, they changed trains for us again, well, we had to change trains without any information from anyone. Once the next train was located, we had to change trains again to reach the final destination in Amsterdam, where we arrived more than 5 hours late, no one gave us any explanation, and they never gave us the corresponding refund. They barely reimbursed us for a ticket for having left late, the company never took care of dropping us off in Brussels. A shame.

Booked Eurostar from London to paris. Traffic was terrible like all in Europe.  But once inside..very organized and staff there are very nice and helpful.  Train was smooth and clean and comfortable.. would DEFINITELY book it again if we go back.

Rather than flying to Paris for a quick trip, we opted to take the speed train.  We did not go premium or business class and instead purchased "economy fares" which was still more than perfect.  The rail is clean and comfortable and quick. The hardest part of the travel was merely the lines (crowds) into either rail station of both locations.
Main trains are clean and comfortable.  When connecting to a regional city trains are less so.  Cost is good for service provided.  Outside of large city terminals not may bilingual staff.
If you go to London by train, it's fine, the train journey is also very good. but wifi is completely crappy. and check-in only takes 45 minutes, so be sure to be on time. otherwise you are seen

The ride from Brussels to London St Pancras International was a smooth and comfortable ride in the standard class. We boarded and departed about 5 minutes late. The terminal at Brussels was quite full with people filling the isles in between chairs ready to race on and board. There were no issues with the train service, except there was no wifi after we excited the English Channel tunnel in the UK until the end of the train ride. The wifi was working intermittently and at reasonably slow speeds most of the time I tried using it, however it went out in the tunnel (as one could expect) and never returned. I would recommend the Eurostar as an alternative to flying across the channel depending on the points you are using it to and from.

Check-in/security and loading were chaotic and time-consuming. Maybe this was accentuated by being a chaperone of a large group, but I saw plenty of individual/paired travelers in similar distress and staff were militant. On the train was relatively comfortable, but wifi was little better than nothing and charging ports were inconvenient. Ability to pay for food in both sterling and euro was a good way to empty the coin purse of unused currency of one type before switching to the other. Good luck accessing toilet paper if you don't have the small hands of a Parisian subway pickpocket...

We missed our first train to Paris due to our train beforehand being cancelled. We did get another ticket and seat on the next available train to Paris which was great however the man we dealt with was very rude and didn’t listen to what we were saying but apart from that it’s a great way to travel to Paris.Get to the train station at least an hour early before your train due to all the security you need to go through.You can take your own food and drinks on the train which is good although you can purchase food and drinks on the train. Good amount of storage to put your suitcases in. The wifi on the train was really fast and easy to connect to.We did find that our carriage was awful warm and the seats do not have any where you can charge your phone or laptop.

Pleased be advised, this is s long review!Boarded at Gare du Nord after a stressful trip from pretty much “ guess where you are going if you can trip” from Gare du Lyon on a Metro “Sauna” At GDN you need to head for Platform 1 but it’s not where you are sent next to platform 2 - it opposites and upstairs on an elevator. There it is down the end of a long concourse where you will meet a multitude of people trying to literally squeeze into the “time saving” passport machines through disney queues into two doors - no not two - one - but wait as a nice French official is asking you to wave at the Sensor to open the second door as he’s locked out! When you succeed he nips inside and locks it and you are frustratingly back to one. Eventually getting through to the passport machine in which you have to remove glasses and hats and hold all your baggage and try to squeeze through the stupid gap, have your face scanned and pass no more than 10 feet and do it all again with your passport!!! Then it’s onto baggage security where as there are no trays provided  to place your items,you have to shove everything you have into your already stuffed bag to get it through the scanner! By this time there’s a serious delay and your train leaves in minutes. Of course if you’re second class that’s at least car 5 and further. Now you could get on and fight your way past people in earlier carriages or just hope you’ve got time to board your own carriage several miles away. I’m all for security but like one previous reviewer said it’s not helped by officious staff keeping you from moving forward because you’re not the requisite 30 inches away from the next person and don’t forget that’s your train about to leave for which you have an allocated seat- paid for!! This was not a pleasant experience and even more farcical when the lady at the gate entrance at the top of the non operating supermarket trolley ramp asks you which train you’re trying to catch!! ****^!!**😮Seats unable to tilt forward but you can move them back but awkward with tray down. Charging sockets difficult to reach and poor free wifi most of the way!  The app mentioned about having seat service as standard and a two part meal being brought to your seat - not sure how that works - drinks cart times once only on trip. This was meant to be s special end to our 45 anniversary holiday - well it was certainly memorable for sure- I don’t know about EURO STAR??? More like EUROJOKE! I’m like one other one star reviewer - Just fly its easier, quicker and way cheaper too- even on Easy Jet!😮

Have travelled with them several times and the service is always good but today they showed their true colours.I was returning from Germany and unfortunately delays meant that I missed my planned train in Cologne making me late in Brussels and therefor missed the Eurostar that I was booked on.They charged 49 Euros each to change us onto the next train, one which had plenty of empty seats when it left.Sorry but this is just profiteering at its worst.

The Eurostar train is a great way to commute to Paris. You can purchase seats in advance so that you are sitting where you want to. The cars have very comfortable seats and ride very quietly while moving very fast. The trip takes about 2 1/2 hours. There are also washrooms on board. The step up to the train is quite high and some people might need help with their luggage. There are luggage bins on board but fill up quite quickly. A very enjoyable trip to Paris.

Went Business Class to Paris--with a lot of luggage thought it would make things easier. Keep in mind the Business Class price was many multiples of the standard fare--maybe 5 times. First the good: you could jump the massive security queue and it was massive. The lounge was fine. But then it fell apart. First off while there is an elevator to the platform, it was not available for Business patrons. So from that point on you had to join the massive throng of people. Then the carriage. It's the same layout as the one up from Standard--that is, 3 not f 4 abreast. Alas, no real luggage space defeating the rationale for going Business. Service was shaky--they forgot my meal and I had to hunt them down in the galley to get it. They said they would book a taxi to wait for us at Gare du Nord. Alas, no taxi appeared. So they offer a lot and deliver very little.

Had a horrible journey in March. My train was cancelled so I needed to spent extra night in Paris. Eurostar offered free stay in hotel as a compensation. However, at the end I ended up paying my hotel bill as the hotel said that had no arraignment with Eurostar. On the top of that in order to take my train back to UK I waited over 1h30m for passport checks and the train was delayed with over than hour. Moreover, trying to contact customer support is more than impossible. Waited over 2 weeks for a response on email and up to today I didn't recieved any answer to my query.

I travelled on a Saturday morning from London and it was quite chaotic, lots of people asking to go through security ahead of us because their train was leaving in "2 minutes." Security was fairly quick, you have to take off belts and put phones in a tray but all liquids are fine and they even offer cardboard trays for your coffee etc!The train I got took me to Lille Europe and you then have to go across a car park to get the SCNF train from Lille Flandres direct to the Disney station. On the way back there is no security or passport control at Disney station because its effectively a regional station. However once at Lille Europe, head towards Hall Londres. You go through French passport control then directly onto UK passport control! Then through security again and into a lovely lounge. I was offered a free bottle of water!There is a cafe type place, newspapers for sale and tables and chairs. People queued up kind of like they do at an airline gate and then we were taken down an escalator to the platform. There are signs on the platform indicating where to stand for your coach numberI'd definitely travel this way again, less stressful than airports!

Stayed in London three days decided to take the Eurostar to Paris for the day and get the HOHO bus. Very easy, I watched u-tube vidios, which helped. Get tickets as far ahead a possible for cheapest price. Also no need to by up grades on seats the cheapest worked out fine. You need to scan ticket to get in gate, then go through security, then to waiting room. You will be told when to board train. When you get off in Paris take a look around where you get off, because that is where you will go to get back on. To get to HOHO bus walk straight out door and go straight for 2 blocks over and across the street  That is the Blue route, in a stop of two you will get off and get on the Red route. That is the route you want for all the sites. FYI If you miss the blue route getting back to the Eurostar, And you are pressed for time, go across the street from the main HOHO bus excange and catch a bus!!  Very cheap.

Very good travel experience, connecting two countries by crossing the English Channel. It is recommended, given that you are going from the center of one city to another, avoiding wasted time getting to the airports that are generally outside the cities, and it is always at least 2 hours in advance that you have to be there.

I am not sure what happened to Eurostar, it used to be great but it is now awful. Security and passport control is worse than any airport I use and seems to just break down. Station facilities are very cramped especially if operational problems cause trains to backup. The new trains have a horrible unsettled ride quality, uncomfortable seating and appear to be shoddily built. On board WiFi is a joke. It didn't used to be like this, I used to love travelling by Eurostar but now it is just awful. Things are that bad I would rather fly.

While it's still the most comfortable way of traveling from Europe to the UK, they've been consistently bad getting their trains on time.If you depend on any connections make sure to account for at least a one hour margin.For the price, the service is disappointing.

I realise that travelling by Eurostar to France is international travel and involves security checks and passport control but there must be a more efficient way. However, I can understand that space in London limits allowing passengers to pass through customs too early.The train ride was smooth and efficient - it left on time and arrived on time. There is a power point for charging but the seats are uncomfortable.The customs’ process for the return journey from Paris was smoother but that was because we were there when check in opened and the station has a departure lounge.

You can’t go wrong with traveling on the Eurostar! We took the Eurostar from London to Paris and loved every moment.  We made the decision to upgrade to business class.  They served us a meal with wine, soft drinks, and coffee/tea.  It was delicious! We were relieved to have USB ports to charge our phones and excellent WiFi.  Looking forward to our return trip to London!

We took the Piccadilly tube train to the Eurostar station in London, after getting off the train at the King’s Cros/St Pancras tube station it was convenient to find our way to the Eurostar then rain check in and departure section as there was signages showing the way. The Eurostar station is huge, we arrived early and had our lunch here before checking in, it’s best to arrive early as there can be a large crowd due to immigration clearance which we experienced during our check in. The train departure was on time, the seats were comfortable and we had a pleasant trip to Paris.

Excuse me but your adverts are at least mis-leading if not, and I use the legal term carefully, mis presentative. Myself and my partner want to travel from Ashford International to Paris, out on July 14, back July 21. Your cost over £500 for the two. £546 I think...er not quite the £116 implied on the advert BUT on the same day I have booked with Trainline from Calais Frethun to Paris Nord, TGV both ways £116 return for two. So, yes, I have to get to Calais and back - but I can easily to that for £200. you are failing the residents of Kent..so OK your London customer base have a greater propensity to pay? or, you need more capacity, or you no to re-negotiate your franchise? how long does that last for by the way. All ways Eurostar is overpriced...simple

This was our second trip on the Eurostar from London to Paris - but it's been years.We ride trains in Germany and Italy when visiting from the states and it is a totally different experience. You can no show up here 15-20 minutes before the train and expect to get on.Getting on in London --Passport checks, security screening, boarding passes (not tickets) then you wait for your train to be called and travel up a long escalator to board.Cars are nice - with comfortable seats, electrical outlets, a/c (not controlled at seat), carry-on baggage storage right above your head, and window shades.There is a food car, but you can also bring food/drinks on board.Train does not travel through any areas that you will feel a need to take pictures. It goes fast, but you can still see all the landscape around you. But not much to see.Getting off in Paris --Be careful of Gare du Nord as there are alot of shady types hanging around outside, UBER cannot get close to station so have to walk to meet them near, and absolutely everyone you ask "do you speak english" say no. Still better than taking a flight between the two cities.

If you're travelling with standard luggage, there should be no issues.If you need to use Eurodespatch for any 'unusual' items then expect to have to make 30 phone calls to get through and then wait nearly 2 hours to get connected to an advisor.A truly abysmal state of affairs.
First timer on Eurostar ,staff very welcoming ,can't wait till I go again , assistant for wheelchair top notch as I had to be in one last minute ,💖💖

The train itself was o k and we soon got to Paris but the queues to get on were chaos ; o k this was Xmas but the passport control and customs were a bottleneck that made our departure an hour and a half late and not much better coming home ; So be sure to give yourself plenty of time and don’t arrange any tight connection times

very basic, poor poor service (apart from a couple of nice staff members ) to and from Paris.the staff will not help you with a pram and say it's not their issue.on the way to Paris, I was moved to carriage 14 due to having a pram. they first told me they would not offer me my business meal which was paid for. a manager came later to tell me he would offer it to me but I did not receive a drink.the toilets near business class did not work on the way to Paris and all toilets were extremely filthy.Even with a pram on business class, it took them a while to let me through the special access way as I waited in que for over 10 mins.The only thing that made the trip bearable was the other passengers who helped me get on and off the train. it is very sad that euro star can charge 700 euros!!!!!! for a return for such a poor quality service.on the way home our train was delayed by 75 mins!! They asked us to get onto the train next to us as there was a fault with our train. this was very stressful and the manager from coach 1 (blond, older lady) refused to help me with my pram on the broken down train). they dont seem to care if people book economy or business class. my sister who traveled via Eurostar before me said when she traveled they had over booked their business class tickets and tried to make her sit in economy for 300. ( their excuse was they were overbooked so would she mind, and if she did move she would not get the business class service) I have never heard of this, such bad service or how cheeky they are. not sure if this is all legal or day light robbery.  I would not recommend Eurostar, especially business class. if you like wasting money and bad service then you'll find Eurostar a good deal!!

Travel a number of times and following is an overview. Journey out good with quick security. Arrive on time. Comfortable journey even though very busy. Return journey again busy but Lille side not so great (Brussels better) Easy check in and boarding. WIFI all round is rubbish even when not undergroundNewer trains are more comfortableCancellations in winter as not so busyFood is rubbish

The ride took about 2 hours from London St. Pancras Station to Brussels South Station. It was a normal class, but I didn't have any pain at all. However, it cannot be reclined. By the way, to get to Brussels Central Station, where the Grand Place is located, you need to change trains once at Gare du South. No need to buy additional tickets.

The journey from London to Paris was great. Was travelling business so all very pleasant in the lounge and also on the train. Great breakfast and great service. Everyone super-polite (my only small gripe was that i could not get the breakfast and my laptop on the tray at the same time - which i can just about do on the plane).So the outbound was all hunky-dory. For the return leg I arrived probably 50 minutes before departure at Gare du Nord. Basically there was a massive queue caused by the French customs only having two machines/scanners going. There seemed to be no urgency but this meant everything backed up to the extent they could not let people use the automated passport barriers because even if you got thru there was no space the other side. The speed was SO SLOW it was unbelievable.The French chap in front of me was so embarrassed and kept apologising.Finally got thru and legged it to the train with a couple of minutes to spare.Don't want to sound like my grandfather (bless him) - but totally unacceptable. There were old people who had to queue for ages and were seriously fretting about whether they would catch the train. Just took the edge of the whole experience.The service on the train and the food, again, was very good but i'm afraid that queuing killed it for me.Next time I will fly.

Train was fine from London, return venture was a joke. After arriving an hour in advance, I ultimately missed my train. Firstly I was refused through passport control with the coffee I bought at the entrance to the Eurostar.. Not because of some liquids rule, no because I might 'throw it at the machine' and then the attendant would 'lose my job'.. Anyhow after being told to just sit and relax drink it then come through, I ultimately left most of my (4 euro machine made) coffee to ensure I'd make the train. After plodding through security, I was eventually ushered through with the group needing to catch the next train - Turned out to be a pointless endeavour. Despite apparently being in a rush, the security guard still decided he needed to leave at least 30 seconds between people going throughm for reasons I am yet to fathom. In any case I made the gate with 10 minutes to spare, ahead of most of the group sent through, thinking nothing but a minor annoyance at the various hold-ups. But no, I was not allowed on - I was 'late'. Indeed droves of us were turned away. What an absolute joke. I've been later for planes and allowed on. I arrived far later to London for the outbound journey, and made it comfortably. The following train was then late to add insult to injury.Ultimately I was left with the impression that the staff who care only about themselves, and couldn't care less if I have to sit around for another hour. What's that to them. Will think twice before booking again.And if you are going, make sure you're ready to board the train before it stops on the platform.
Good experience, quick and comfortable. Much better than flying. No long waiting at luggage control. Arriving in the heart of London
Travelled home , last evening and the state of the train and toilets , lots were closed , lots were dirty and horrible to use , toilets over flowing , it was awful

Had an excellent ride on the Eurostar this morning. We used Standard Premier, meal and ride was awesome. Seats and comfort were also good. Toilets clean and spacious. Only complaint was getting through security where you had to lift your suit onto the conveyor belt to X-ray the bags. Okay for me, but someone may find it difficult. The train was awesome, staff and meal onboard were very good, wine and a bottle of water included.

The new rolling stock is very good and the journey time to Brussels from London is amazing but here's the end of the positives. Well, apart from the premier class food, which was ace.The London terminal is chaotic and clearly too small to handle the security and passenger numbers. The London staff need some customer service training and many need help with their English. The signage once  checked in is poor and the whole place needs a rethink.

We wanted to travel from London to Provence, a region in the south of France. Eurostar trains run from their terminal at St. Pancras in London to Marseille, once a day on certain days in the season, stopping at Lille, Lyon, Avignon and Marseille. We alighted at Avignon.This was a very comfortable journey: smooth, quiet, and a great alternative to what would have been much more complicated by air, with travel to and from airports. Customs and passport controls were very efficiently done at St. Pancras, although on the return journey you have to detrain with luggage at Lille.Altogether a highly impressive experience -  strongly recommended.

Caught the lunchtime departure to Brussels travelling in Standard Premier. All the staff were very polite and efficient and as usual the “snack” lunch sufficed. Seats are very comfortable and luggage stowage is also good, with large/heavy bags having a separate space near the exit doors. It was also punctual allowing for a stress free connection at Brussels Midi.

But when it goes wrong.... omg.(Brussels --> Ashford since May 2018)I have no idea why Ashford International and the Eurostar trains are STILL not compatible. The problem seems to be exacerbated 80% of the times I decide to travel. It's annoying.... if I wanted it to take me 3 hours to get home, I'd work in London.As it goes, when I do call, members are now much more helpful and understanding than they were 6 months ago which is half an improvement.Back in December, the train from Brussels to London decided it wasn't stopping at Ashford despite me booking the precise start and end points and I had to pay out of my own pocket for the train to go 20 minutes past where I live and back which ruined my whole weekend.This time... half the same story... got some sympathy as I've missed an appointment a stopping train would have made. And it means more weekend time spent travelling.90% of the time I go premium. Except at breakfast times... not a big fan of continental breakfasts when everything is freezing cold. Meal services are erratic: Sometimes you don't get fed until Lille and then have to rush... other times you get fed just out of Brussels and woe betide you if you've not finished your meal before Lille... the tray will be yours until you get to wherever you are going...Not being rude... I do appreciate the convenience of Eurostar. A suggestion... on their virgin voyage, there was probably excitement and precision and exceptional customer service. Stick to those values and BRE or any other type of exit won't matter.

I have been using Eurostar to go to Paris, Brussels and beyond since the service started. I accept that it cannot be as much of an amazing thing as it was at the start but I wonder if it is now getting tired. The journeys are still fast of course. However, at St. Pancras seating is hard to find when you wait to board. That is not so at Brussels Midi. Boarding and leaving still works well. However, luggage space is more limited than it should be. The toilets lacked toilet paper and water and that was not at the end of the journey. As a user of the AVE in Spain this service is not as good.

We waited for 8 hours in line without food or water in Gare du Nord.  It was so bad that our Premier class tickets were worthless and they seated folks wherever they could.  Eurostar then makes it the traveler's problem to seek refunds and handle all of that. I am flying from now on. Big mistake to do this. I get that it was a disruption, but this is happening constantly all over France. With Brexit on the horizon, I see this getting worse and not better.

The journey itself was fine, transfer in Brussels to London: waiting room capacity completely insufficient, no seats to be found, a really chaotic situation, delay of 30 minutes because the train had arrived at the wrong platform, boarding well arranged on the return journey, but the train turned out to have a power connection problem, 45 minutes delay

We took the train to go from Paris to London as my husband loves trains. It was a great trip. You go through immigration for the UK in Paris so when you arrive you can go right out and start your day in London. Most times the train went about 185 MPH so the trip was quick at just over 2 hours. We booked the standard tickets and they were fine for this trip. No need for food on such a quick trip. And if you need a snack there are snack/drink counters in some cars.

My son and I decided to make a quick trip to Paris on this high speed train.  From London to Paris in just over 2 hours.Great train stations at both ends of the journey and a truly memorable experience

My wife and I traveled from London to Paris in a little more than two hours on the Eurostar at the St. Pancras station in London.  We bought tickets in advance online.  After clearing customs, we boarded the train and whizzed along toward Paris at speeds in excess of 100 MPH.  A food car was available to get snacks, and the restrooms were easily accessible.  Watching the countryside as we passed, the trip went by quickly and before we knew it we were at the Paris station at Gare Nord.  We then took the local metro two stops to Notre Dame.  EZ PZ.

I booked my Standard Premier seat online - very easy and I could change my seat online using the seating plan. Standard Premier is the same seat and carriage as Business Premier but doesn't get a 3 course meal and would have cost me A$300 more. For breakfast my one course with juice, tea or coffee, croissant and fruit was more than enough. They also give passengers dietary options! The ride itself was smooth and all announcements were in French and English. There was even an announcement prior to entering the Chunnel. Very quick and enjoyable journey.However: A few days before I was due to travel, I received a text message and an email advising me to arrive at the Gare du Nord on time because of increased passenger numbers. I arrived there 2 hours before my 9.10am train was due to depart. It was chaos. No customer service to advise which queue to join; and then when I found someone to ask they all refused to speak English. The hold-up was the Eurostar ticketing checks, not the passport checks with the French Police and UK Customs or even the baggage xrays. I finally boarded my train 10 minutes after it was due to depart, and it departed 25 minutes late. My colleague was on the next train to London and he texted me that his train departed 20 minutes late.I was appalled that regular services to London from Paris Gare du Nord (there are no other Eurostar services from that station) would be so chaotic and non-EU passengers would be treated so badly. There were some recorded messages in French and English but no signage and what staff that were there appeared to not understand English. I was chatting to an American lady in the queue and it was her first time on Eurostar too - both of us agreed we would never do this again.

I have used Eurostar quite a few times. My trains were ontime. We could see the seat map and choose our own seats but u couldn't if travelling on Thalys. Also better seats, lower fare, newer train than Thalys. The only downside of was the toilets. I found few of them were out of use sometimes but not end of the world. I will use Eurostar again anyway.

Using Eurostar is convenient but they are definitely not friendly when it comes to rebooking. I asked to move our train to London early after we made it from Italy early. To move the train up four hours was insanely expensive (370 euros). Plenty of seats she said but can’t move it because of some dumb reasoning. Even flying most Airlines we get same day changes for free. I’m not a fan of the gouging and not being remotely flexible when it’s clearly no one will be taking the seats.
Took the train from paris to london and this is a nice ride similar to the ones in asia. I didn’t even sit in business class and my standard premier was pretty good

For my birthday, I treated my grown up family (6) to lunch in Paris at a cost of £1180 on the Eurostar. (An Easyjet flight was half the price!) Having left in what we thought was plenty of time to catch our train home, due to numerous road, bridge and metro closures because of the Gilet Jaune protesters, we missed our booked train by minutes. I was then charged a penalty fare of €300 to catch the next train one hour later, which was half empty. I wrote to customer service on my return asking whether they would reconsider this rather harsh penalty, considering the amount I’d already spent and perhaps issue me with a credit voucher for another trip, if not a refund. Their very helpful reply was:   ‘Moving forward, I would advise you to ensure you arrive within the check in time to avoid any further costs.‘ Top marks for stating the obvious, bottom marks (and hence 2 stars) for customer service. The train itself was fine, although the older style train coming back was far more comfortable than the newer carriages on the way out and Ebbsfleet is great!

Recall that when we learned of the opening of the Anglo-French Tunnel, the press from various countries scrambled to report it as a political, engineering and transportation feat. When I was studying, I always wanted to experience the Eurostar train to Paris, but always, I live in Manchester in the northwest of England, and it was always the most convenient to go to Paris by plane. Until 2009, that time I stayed at a friend's house in London, and I encountered the Eurostar offer early in the morning, so I experienced a Eurostar trip, back and forth to Brussels, Belgium. In 2018, after visiting Paris with my wife, in order to accompany her to experience "Eurostar", we once again boarded this international train spanning Britain, France and Belgium. In order, the 2009 one. That day, arrive at S. Pancras early in the morning to catch the 5:53 a.m. shuttle bus heading directly to Brussels Midi/Brussels Zuid. I started from my friend's home on Old Street and luckily there was a bus so early in the morning, otherwise, I would have had to leave half an hour early. Back then, still not with using electronic tickets, I had to get to the train station early by going to the ticket machine to get a physical ticket. Nowadays, if you book a ticket online, you can scan the page with the QR Code to enter the gate. However, nowadays, it is still necessary to arrive at the station early because of the additional security check and two checks in the same place. "Eurostar", is the setting of the high-speed rail. In the UK sections are rare international trains, so there are dedicated railway sections. In 2009 there was still no tedious security process. After checking the ticket, you can enter the platform directly, the flight attendant will greet you are correct car, door boarding. The seats are wide enough and leg room is good. But the whole trunk feels very cramped. However, sitting in the seat, its sense of space is sufficient. In short, comfortable enough. On the UK sections, the speeds were not fast because some sections were shared with local trains (back then). Now, there is a dedicated railway from Dover to St. Pancras, which saves a lot of time. After crossing the Anglo-French Tunnel, the speed started to get faster. Pieces of farmland and huts disappeared quickly before our eyes. And, slowly, I saw the dawn of the rising sun, counted the time difference, and was able to start my Brussels trip after 9 o'clock. Moreover, in those days, the flight attendants were responsible for checking documents and handling entry and exit in the car, which saved a lot of time. Just like taking a regular long-distance Inter City train, more than two hours in the basket, you arrive at Brussels South Station, where you can immediately embark on a two-day and one-night trip to Brussels. Time jumps, it's 2018. This time, we were traveling with my wife, departing from Paris to London, and chose "Eurostar" as our means of transportation. The boarding point for Paris is the Gare du Nord, one of the busiest train stations in Paris. According to my experience in 2009, if you have a ticket in hand, you can get on the bus directly. However, it is now 2018, and many things are different. As it turns out, there is now an additional one-country-two-checks procedure for boarding the train in Paris. In Paris, covered a stamp leaving the Schengen region of the European Union from Paris Nord. Two more steps ahead, there is the UK immigration counter. After the immigration personnel sent from the UK briefly asked a few questions about the reasons for coming to the UK, they were covered with a UK entry stamp with Paris entry, which was very special. After passing the immigration office, you can board the bus immediately. I thought I could get on the new train, but the two trains on the platform were Class 373 that started in Pangu. A small feature of Class 373 is that the train’s wheel bogie adopts the “articulated bogie” (Jacobs Bogie) commonly used by the French TGV. Looking at the relevant website, it turns out that this design favors reducing noise and making it easier for trains to pass through more curved railways. After another two hours or so drive, we returned to the familiar London, the familiar St. Pancras Station. On the platform, at the same time saw the old and new two “Eurostar”, the new car (Class 374) is more streamlined and feels more fashionable, in the near future, the old Class 373 (yellow train), ready to complete their mission. When in Paris, the carriage we were in was located at the rear of the car, so we had to slowly manage the platform to the station room. The empty, half-dome station design is very British and very traditional. In 2009, I was very touched when I saw the bronze statue of a pick-up and a kiss. In 2017, this bronze statue that seems to have become the ground, named "The Meeting Place" is still there, adding a very unique romantic feeling to the station. The Eurostar trains, which are very convenient, especially to and from London, Paris, and Brussels, are more direct and faster than planes and cross-border buses. In addition, they have seasonal Disney Paris and several popular ski resort routes in France, which are also very popular. In 2019, Eurostar also commissioned routes to and from Amsterdam.

We traveled from Brussels to London and had a very nice time. We reserved seats with a table which worked out very nice with the kids. Being able to walk around and get food is the best way to travel!
We thoroughly enjoyed our journey from Paris to London on Eurostar.  Very clean, comfortable and fast. Good value too. Much better than flying.

Usually cheaper to fly than to take the Eurostar so beware, but the train is definitely more comfortable than a flight!Make sure you arrive at least an hour early for your train to ensure you have enough time to get through customs and security.Overall, a very confortable and reliable service, make ensure you book well in advance (months) to get a better price.

The high-speed train is very good, it connects you to the continent in just 2 hours, the train has a buffet to eat or drink whatever you like. In addition to being very comfortable. It is recommended to arrive one hour before departure to avoid inconveniences due to immigration and luggage controls.

I usually only leave reviews if there’s something really good or bad. In this case, sadly, it’s terrible. This is my first trip to Paris using the Eurostar. But my God...the seat in the ‘regular’, poor people class is extremely uncomfortable. I never thought I’d say this...but plane seats are better! Unbelievable. Eurostar need to make the seats 100% more comfortable. They need to recline more, be less bulky so one's head actually feels the upper edge of it...which enables passengers to relax. The current seats make you seat up straight for hours....it’s impossible to relax and enjoy the ride.

Awful customer service. We were running a few minutes late to our train because of delays with public transport in Paris. Upon arrival to the station the staff denied our access to the train despite being there before our train left the station. They forced us to change to a later train and pay a $100 fee to do so. The train they switched us to ended up arriving to London 30 min after it was scheduled to which was over an hour and a half later than we were originally supposed to get in - which made us miss another tour we had booked for the day. On top of this the staff asked me how I was able to afford such a trip to Europe (after explaining that I was a student from America) which was pretty rude.

As you are enjoying your trip through the French countryside at 183 mph here are a few tips to make your journey smoother.Register with the Eurostar app and have it on your mobile so that you are informed when future seats are on offer as considerable savings can be made during the sales.  Even after booking your ticket you can change the seats using your app.  The quietist seats are in the centre of the train away from the engines - although these are not particularly noisy at all.  However in the centre you will be closer to the cafes.  You will need to decide whether you want to be forwards or backwards facing and also if you want a seat facing others with a table in between (there are 2 in each carriage).  Also note that some of the “window” seats are largely next to a wall. These are marked on the seating diagram but it is not completely accurate.  You can usually move to an empty seat after the train starts.  However when coming from St Pancras remember that passengers also get on at Ashford International.  Trains to Lyons and the South of France only disembark passengers in France so the train gets less crowded as the journey progresses.  Conversely if you get on in Marseille then more passengers will join at each station.  You are told to arrive at St Pancras 45 - 60 minutes before departure and the trains to the South of France usually leave around 7.20am.  You have to go through security and also UK and French border control.  You will have about 20 minutes in the departure lounge which is a crowded and miserable place.  There are 2 cafes but if you are looking for provisions then note that the food may be over twice the price of that outside in the station.  The food on the train is not very good (standard railway fare) so prepare yourself a picnic for the 7 hour journey.  There is a Little Waitrose in Kings Cross Station across the road from the Eurostar entrance.  It opens at 6.00am but unfortunately will not sell wine at that time.   However you can buy croissants and a lunch for the journey.  Your ticket will state that you should arrive at Marseille Station for the return journey again 45 - 60 minutes before departure.  This is totally unnecessary as there are no passport or security checks and you just show your ticket and get on.  Obviously you should allow a reasonable time as the train is very long if you have to walk to the front.  Whilst Marseille Station has a number of bars and stalls the surrounding area is quite rough.  Avignon TGV Station is outside the city (note there is free transfer to the city centre for Eurostar ticket holders) and is bland and hot with few places to relax.  Best to minimise your time at the stations. On the return journey from the South of France you must be prepared for a diabolical security and customs arrangement at Lille.  Everyone on the train has to get off, with all luggage, to go through ticket validation, French passport control, British passport control and security.
