There is a lot of waiting in queues and the whole process can take up to 90 minutes.  It is the one major disadvantage of the whole journey.  The staff on the train are very helpful and friendly but why there is a need to have someone sitting in each carriage is strange!Overall despite minor flaws it is a fantastic journey and usually on time. Great value too at around £99 in the sale.

The Eurostar itself is great, definitely the most relaxing way to get to Paris especially if you go by Standard Premier. However, the booking process can be disappointing and costly if you're not careful.I was halfway through my transaction, having put in all my details including payment card details, when their system crashed. Starting again, the site showed the tickets had gone up from £112 each to £134. The Live Chat agent said that it was because all the £112 tickets had sold out and that even though it was their system error, I would now have to pay the higher price. According to the agent their "dynamic" system automatically updates the prices, sometimes while you are in the process of making a booking, and once those prices have gone up they can't roll them back. I then accessed the site from a different computer and, what do you know, those same tickets were available at £112 each. It seems to me that the "dynamic" system as described by the agent is simply an underhanded way of fleecing their customers. I wonder how many other people have had to pay extra because Euorstar's system decided to "dynamically update the prices" halfway through their transactions. You should be ashamed of yourselves Eurostar.

I use Eurostar every week from Paris to London. Over the past 5 months, the service has deteriorated very clearly. Due to the nature of my job, I sometimes have to change my tickets a week or a few days before my departure. Last problem with Eurostar: they ask me 274 euros to change my Paris - London ticket while a new one-way ticket is offered on their site for 140 euros! No reasonable explanation by telephone: you have to change the outward and return journeys. However, the site suggests changing only the outward or return journey. The supervisor is not available.

I live in the UK, my partner in Belgium, we both travel every few weeks to eachother and now only use the eurostar as it is such an enjoyable, easy experience. Most of the staff are lovely and friendly, they have great accessibility especially as I have a disability which limits my mobility. They're always helpful and it's nearly always a positive experience. If booked in advance it's not too expensive, and you only have to be there 45/60 mins before the train leaves. Honestly could not recommend enough, especially as a frequent traveller as you get points which add up to free trips after a while. You're always informed of any (very rare) delays and compensation is easy if things are delayed dramatically. Will never fly to Belgium /France /Amsterdam again.

We traveled to Brussels by Eurostar and were very satisfied with the journey and ease with which we checked in and boarded the train. The location and lack of signage of the Eurostar station in Brussels isn’t easy to find but once there the trip is very good.

I have two bits of advice for Eurostar travellers. First, no matter what the signs in the train say, there is no WiFi inside. Theoretically, it works, but in reality it is either not available or is so slow that you cannot do anything online. Second, if you are travelling from Amsterdam to London, you have to transfer at Brussels Midi. That is what the ticket will say. In reality, you need to get off at Brussels Zuid. It is the same stop, but the name on the platform that you will see from the window is the latter, not the former. I almost went straight to France thinking Midi and Zuid are different...

If you are in London and want to go to Amsterdam, Brussels or Paris, taking the train could be a good option. It's not cheaper than going by plane, but it's worth it as a travel experience. But be careful with reservations and delays. Eurostar may cancel your trip at short notice, so check the status of your itinerary regularly. And if you are a day late, be prepared to face long disorganized queues (at least it was like that for me in Paris: disorganization).

Did four days in Paris and four days in London. Landed in CDG. Train to Agg 19. Then boarded the Eurostar to London. In Detroit, trains are laughed at. In Europe they are a life line for survival. Aside from having to remain outside the Eurostar waiting area until 2 hours prior to our departure, this was an excellent experience. The train was clean. Service was good and did I say fast? We boarded at night, so the scenery wasn't much. At 180MPH, you could hardly tell we were moving, although the lights outside were flying by like a blur. 2 hours later we were there. Did I say it was fast?

On Amsterdam route this morning. Security were quite bossy in my view. The chairs in waiting area are all mechanically connected so someone moving at one end jogs everyone else - very unpleasant experience. Noisy crowded and stressful. I generally want to see the positive in everything but this needs to be massively redesigned.

Booked the train from London St-Pancras to Amsterdam in Standard Premier. Everything was good until we got to Brussels.  The train did not go on for over one hour, they announced an issue with new crew not available. Finally someone told the passengers in the rear of our car that this train will not go anywhere tonight!  There are two Thalia,s trains that will leave in the next few minutes for Amsterdam and we should  try the get on one of them. The one train had 45 seats and the last train had 75 seats. Our train had 600 passengers. Luckily we got on the second train, my wife got a seat but I had to stand in the luggage area. Got to Amsterdam 2 hours late after midnight. During the whole time in Brussels not a single Eurostar representative was helping any of us stranded passengers. The original crew also abandoned the train and was nowhere to be seen. Still looking to get a refund from Eurostar but all emails get ignored.Terrible customer service!

I have been traveling on this line for years, the service is continually deteriorating, both for delays, cancellations, treatment of passengers, etc. To be avoided if possible, plane journeys are safer, shorter and cheaper

We used the direct Eurostar service Disneyland Paris via St. Pancras . It was a 10-14 departure so we had to be there fairly early for check in.We had printed off our tickets previously via the Eurostar app and this was very helpful in checking in. We simply scanned the print offs and entered the customs /security area.This area is manic and gets extremely busy. Tip 1...get there early, do your check in early and reduce the stress levels or it will almost certainly rise. Security was slow but a necessity. Every piece of baggage ,including hand luggage has to be checked. Tip 2..travel as light as you can.After that customs and passport control. Then on to be photos scanned. Tip 3 ..make sure you stand on the yellow feet marked on the floor or nothing happens. Then its the wait. You get called for the train about twenty minutes before it is due to leave. Your luggage comes with you.As for seating choose the best class of seating that is affordable. Our Disneyland train was full of young kids so be prepared for noise and mess. Hence go for the upgrade if you want a quiet journey. On the normal Eurostar services this is unlikely to occur.The journey was fast and comfortable and the cafe prices onboard were not to bad. 3 Euros for a cup of coffee. Reasonable selection of food ,drinks and snacks.The return journey was similar, however The Disneyland Paris Eurostar terminal offers no facilities once you are directed to the platform. On the day we left it was absolutely freezing so if its a bit chilly ,dress up warm. So if you need to take food or drinks , get them at before you check in.Eurostar is a good experience , but again to get the best try to go for the upgraded coaches. It is a very long train with some 17 coaches so-be prepared for a long walk .On leaving the train at St, Pancras you have to clear immigration and customs once again. Be prepared for a long wait here. Customs are the same the whole world over. They simply do not rush.

Quick trip to Paris for the weekend, pre booked tickets on the Eurostar fro St Pancras Station in London to Garde de Nord Station in Paris.  Arrived at St Pancras Station via a taxi from Kensington, but could have easily taken the tube....we were fortunate to not have our trip thwarted by strike on the French side..as the train before ours and the one after were cancelled.Once aboard it was a smooth 2.5 hrs and we arrived in Paris, caught an Uber to our Hotel and viola we had a great 3 day weekend!

We took the Eurostar on 04/30/19 9:04 a.m.... what can I say, more than 1h30 of trampling down a staircase with our luggage to end up separated even though we had reserved a family square since November 2018... My children being minors, I still managed to travel in the same carriage, it's the minimum. The driver explained to us that the inconvenience was due to the slow passage through customs. You only need to return from London-St Pancras to understand that it is especially very poorly organized on the French side where all travelers are allowed to access controls regardless of the time of their train and where only two ticket scanners are available despite a large number of travelers. Although we arrived more than an hour early, we almost missed the train and what a surprise to see travelers relaxing at duty free while waiting for the next trains, there was a real organizational problem.  It's time to seriously modernize the Eurostar departure hall at Gare du Nord! The return was perfect: train on time, pleasant staff, efficient organization.
Why take the train when the queue is like a cattle truck. Staff screaming, massive waits, it’s horrible all round. Completely spoils the point of the train. Easier and better on plane unfortunately

I traveled on the Eurostar from London St Pancras station to Brussels South station. Although the train was a little delayed, it was a comfortable ride, and although we couldn't see anything in the Strait of Dover due to the underwater tunnel, we arrived at Brussels Midi Station in about 2 and a half hours. I had a reserved seat in a regular car, but there was no problem.

We are at the end of our journey to London after more than 90 minutes of waiting. Here is the beginning of my comment in order to make you understand all the dissatisfaction with this Eurostar Paris London organization. We have organized a family trip since November 2018; namely 4 places reserved at the price of €54 and one place added at €103 in February 2019. We arrived this morning at 8 a.m., 60 minutes before (as marked on the ticket) and we still had to wait in a huge queue just to scan the tickets, so we had to pass two checks - French customs and of course English - and finally a baggage check. In short, 36 minutes of delays on our train, family divided (passengers in different cars), old train, without WiFi and clogged toilet, without forgetting the stress of our elderly parents not used to this type of pressure for a simple train trip! Before saying that the fault is London, it has now been 3 years since the United Kingdom left Brexit and you have had plenty of time to better organize yourself given the size of the Gare du Nord station and given the number of people who travel every day to London from Paris. I have already read your refund policy and find it despicable. I am therefore asking for a commercial gesture for the mental and physical damage suffered (lunch reservation in London canceled due to the delay). Train 9015 from 9:04 a.m. Paris-London 04/30/19 Reserve number SQTJGD

Last year Eurostar set up a London to Amsterdam service.  I'd wanted to go through the Chunnel, and a short break in Amsterdam after visiting my grandkids in London looked attractive.   Eurostar offered two trips a day from London St. Pancras to Amsterdam-one in the morning at 0816 arriving in Amsterdam mid day, and one in the evening. My wife and I opted forthe 0816 departure--which meant that we spent the night in the St. Pancras Renaissance hotel (no way to spend it at our daughter's home in London and get to St. Pancras in time).  We were told to allocate 45 minutes to clear security and border control to get on the train. In fact we arrived at 0715 and had just 8 minutes to spare to get on the train.  That was as much of a hassle as  security at Heathrow. That said, the ride to Amsterdam was fine.  We were travelling Standard Premium and got a light meal that was fine.  But coming back from Amsterdam to London is a bit of a hassle. You have to change trains in  Brussels (high speed Thalys train from Amsterdam to Brussels--then Eurostar to London).  It's not perfect yet.    But I suspect I may take it again next year--maybe Eurostar to Paris, then a high speed train to somewhere else in Europe.

Took the first train to London from Brussels. Then more than 9 hours to discover London before taking the last train home. The train journey is relaxed, there is ample legroom and the arrival at San Pancras is very easy.

First=it is pretty expensive. For the price I paid I can get half of it and take the flight to CDG. On board service is not really what I was expected. First if our coach is in 1 or 16/17/18... you will have to walk to coach 6 or 13 to get your drinks. Secondly, our ticket cost £243 rtn for 2 hrs route...let think again...For an emergency yes will do it but if you have time to take alternative option I suggest you do so...In Paris our flight was 15mn delayed...OK.. not problem but they only told us at 1825 for departure at 1834...Staff more showing off with their bilingual than doing the job. Most of them are on their phone. Passport checking took their times as if they were in a pub - again UK or USA Officers they don't give damn %£^$%^*& as they take their time checking your passport.

Travelling on Eurostar and informed that they had cancelled my return trip and apologise for the inconvenience. What they did not do was offer any assistance 'Last Man In Lifeboat' you are ON YOUR OWN.I bought an airticket home and off hired a car at the airport rather than train station and my car was at Ashford and I arrived late at night at Gatwick. Tried to recoup my expenses and was told by EUROSTAR to go away .GREAT leave you dumped and then do not help in any way. I dare not state what my impression is of them!!!!
Slow degeadation in the 25 years I've been taking it. Date. Constantly delayed every time. Unsuitable for its time. To flee.

Very unorganised company, not helpful, change my seat without informing me, when you try to contact customer service they are very impolite, useless, not ready to help, seat wasn’t clean in our way to Paris, in way back we had to wait for 2:30 queuing in Paris, train was late for 47 minutes no one trying to help or give you correct or accurate information, very bad experience they didn’t care about if you have any children they only care about the money, today I received email from customer service telling me that we cannot give a compensation as we give only for one hour 60 minutes so if I’m late by another 13 minutes I can have a compensation what a company! Have a look at the pictures of the chewingum on the table in our way to Paris.

I've used eurostar multiple over the year cause of the lack of other options but this time they completely missed the plot. I would rather swim to the UK next time than give them anymore money. Don't expect any help ever if anything happens

I took Eurostar for the first time with a friend for a day trip to Pairs from London. The trip there was very pleasent and relaxing. On our return we ran into delays due to customs. Eurostar couldn't have handled the situation better. The staff was friendly and helpful. Since we missed our train as everyone else did, Eurostar made it easy and simple to get the next train. After this was all said and done Eurostar gave us a small refund for something that wasn't their fault. Overall a wonderful company and will defiantly travel with them again.

I and my wife travelled to Paris during the customs go slow on March 6/7/8th 2019. On the advice of  Eurostar-I re-booked a journey cutting short a non refundable city break. Wrong advice it was. Queues in Paris were unimaginable and to lessen the crush we were told that the dispute was not in Lille and that we would be taken there to clear customs prior to travelling through the tunnel. This was not the case- 18 carriages of passengers and all of their luggage were disembarked late at night in Lille to be processed through two security check points. Eurostar staff were totally disinterested at the distress and cold suffered by people processed on the platform in Lille. We arrived in St.Pancras early the following morning. We were advised to submit a claim through the Eurostar website-which would amount to a grand total of £28 for two travellers. Various complaints for hardship and additional expenses incurred have been firmly refused.They claim it was my decision to cut short the city break. Eurostar messages were for information only. This company has no interest in client care. That much is obvious. The service is convenient when it functions but throw something at them that is unexpected and they revert to the party line. Minimum allowable compensation. In future fthere will be further customs disruption. I strongly advise travellers that have flying options not to use Eurostar.They  discount fares, cram passengers in with huge amounts of luggage, are crowded and grubby.

We are in the departure lounge in Gare du Nord. Absolutely boiling, there appears to be no air con.  My father tells me there is only one functional toilet and that is a stand up one, which is impossible is you're 83 years old, which he is. There departure lounge is hopelessly overcrowded, we are lucky enough to be perched on a bench but that is agony for my mother, aged 84, with a bad back.  Not good enough.

This was my first trip using Eurostar to Amsterdam and was very good experience. The train was very clean and the service excellent. However the return trip from Amsterdam via Brussels to London was good, however not without challenges. First of return journey Amsterdam to Brussels was fine. Brussels to London found it bit challenging when one doesn’t know European language but English. Not very many signs in English when one is looking for Eurostar platform, by chance noticed the opposite board showed Eurostar platform 2. Check-in, going through security and thereafter immigration found it to be time critical. Not much time left as one has to rush given only 45minutes to go through all this points. Reached the train for London 7 minutes to spare, one needs to re-visit how the passengers are processed, I appreciate the challenges faced by the different arms of the law. Only disappointing experience on the return journey yesterday (17/04/19 at 18.56 departure from Brussels) was that on requesting one latte and 2 cups of hot water 💧 and was told only one cup of hotel was allowed as it was free, somehow I don’t understand the logic behind the thinking 🤔 or the policy. Otherwise the journey was flawless without any further disappointments. Need to add one observation is that the pick up from the station 🚉 is very challenging and needs to be re-visited allocating for taxis or private cars can do the pick up with ease as it can be daunting. London Mayor should re-visit the policy as it is used mainly used for Eurostar passengers, as it family and others are bit tired and to add to the stress is the pick up are, please do something about this mess, otherwise great 👍

Travelled on the train from London to Paris. The train itself is clean, fast and comfortable and is a great way to get to Europe.The check in process was however a different story! London not so bad but in Paris we waited 2 and a half hours in the line to cross the border before we could board the train. There was no order to the system with passengers from later trains allowed through whilst passengers from imminently departing trains waited. So much so that the train was 30 mins late departing. Make sure you allow yourself plenty of time to clear immigration and security. Seats are pre allocated so once through you are good to go. Shop, toilets, wifi and phone charging on board.
always on time enough space at an affordable price very quickly on site free clean definitely recommended

The experience was unreal. No sooner do we arrive at our seats than do I experience more than I ever imagined. They give you food and water, is this real. I still can’t get over how fun my experience on the Eurostar was, in fact it was better than the actual holiday in Paris spent in a budget heat trap under a motorway flyover. I wished I could have spent more time on Eurostar.

Great way to get from London to Brussels, 2 hour journey and you're there. The seats are comfy enough for a 2 hour journey.Check in much better than a plane and you can take you're own drink aboard Would definitely travel with them again

The seats are more comfortable than buses of course. It is also a good choice for those coming back from Disneyland Paris so they don't have to go back to the city centre. However there were so delays both at the start and also midway. But the trip was smooth overall

Excellent means of transport between London and Paris. You only have to be 1 hour early at the station (St. Pancreas), they accept more luggage than on an airline and you arrive at Garé Du Nord in Paris in 2 hours. Clean, fast, if you get hungry there is food to buy in the carts. I would repeat it without hesitation! The closer you are to the travel date, the more expensive the ticket costs. I suggest you buy the ticket online in advance. You can also purchase them at the St. Pancreas office; If you use the machines that are set up for that, you get the same price as the internet; If you buy it in the office with the assistance of a person, they charge you a surcharge. St. Pancreas station has an elevator to reach Eurostar, so you can get there by metro without any problem.

Can’t say enough about how easy this trip was. Booked online - very straightforward. Arrived St. Pancras station early, had a delicious breakfast at Le Pain Quotidien - adjacent to the entry gates. Swiped my printed ticket at the gate, proceeded to security, in which all gear and coats have to be run through the X-ray machine, then off to the British exit agent and straight into the line for French passport control. Once through, we were in a large lounge with access to food and currency exchange shops. Twenty minutes before our train was scheduled to leave, an announcement and the electronic boards directed us to board, and two escalators directed passengers to the correct location of their respective coaches. Hopped on board, with plenty of storage for our luggage and, a little more than two hours later, we were at Gare du Nord. Very smooth ride and, from someone who hates going through tunnels, not a worry. Twenty minutes in the Chunnel went by unremarkably.

We left London from the St Pancras Station. The window is open 1hour before departure. There they scan your ticket and the next stop is security. you don’t have to worry about liquids,  it you do need to remove belts, shoes, watches etc. once you are through there you enter a large departure hall with a nice Pret A Manger, tables and restrooms. When they call your track, follow the crowd and ask someone for directions to your assigned car. On both occasions we picked a car at the end requiring a long walk. There are little diagrams along the way telling you how close you are to your car. Just keep asking as it’s quite a long walk. The ride was very nice, they served beverages including alcoholic ones In Our class including breakfast . Very nice trip!

Rode the Eurostar train from London to Paris. Train was clean and seats were comfortable with free power ports and free WiFi.  Train goes up to 180mph and made it in about 4.5 hours. They had bathrooms and food in other cars.

Traveling from Ashford to Avignon I receive a text as the train is arriving in Paris telling me there is no return train. Why was I not informed before boarding at Ashford I would not have got on. Next day I receive a text saying do not come no offer at all of any help though!! So I am in Avignon my car is in Ashford and I need to get home on a Saturday night! ABANDONED great eh! I flew home from Montpellier dropping my hire car off at the airport (extra charges) fly to Gatwick on Easy Jet (extra cost) Arrive Gatwick Saturday night and my car is in Ashford. Great eh!! Put in a claim to Eurostar and three weeks later not a peep. Fantastic customer service eh??  Absolute rubbish no service at all you are on your own and the The Sound of Silence.

Don’t travel this way- treated VERY VERY badly, worst than I have ever experienced.Herded into concrete corridors Disney Paris end. Advised to arrive 75-60 minutes before train departure.After passport control, 1 lift down to a very cold platform, with seating for 16 people per 2 carriage area( carriage holds 30 ). Knowing that this is the Disney train back to uk , very little help with families with young children, 1 lift down straight on to station platform(health and safety non existent ).Train finally arrives - on time but carriage numbers all wrong adding confusion.Arrival at Ebbsfleet- 1 lift + 1 escalated up to a very slow passport control.Passengers made to wait on station( very cold wind tunnel effect) allowing 6 families at a time up escalator  as no room in passport control for full train load.Heard a comment from one security/ station employee- maybe it’s 1/2 term?NO ITS EASTER WEEK - and Euro star charge twice as much as norm for the privilege!Surely they should lay on extra staff knowing full well they have a very FULL TRAINNOT A HAPPY END TO A DISNEY EXPERIENCE- DISNEY NEED TO RETHINK THERE INVOLMENT WITH THIS ROUTE At least it’s made the family realise that it’s Florida next time!

We have booked a direct trip from Amsterdam to London. It was advertised and that it would take 3 to 4 hours. On the day of departure we arrived at Amsterdam Central Station 1 hour in advance, but there was no Eurostar in sight. At the counter we were told that we had to change trains in Brussels and that the departure time was therefore from Brussels. Yes, it is there in small letters and yes, also "from every train station in NL", but because we had booked Amsterdam CS - London directly, we never thought for a moment that the departure time would not be Amsterdam. Very misleading information! So we missed our train in Brussels and had to buy a new Brussels - London ticket worth 240 euros per person. Ridiculously expensive! And a total of 8 hours on the road. When we returned from our trip, we filed a complaint with Eurostar, but as expected, we did not receive a cent back. We really feel cheated and treated unfairly!

Our experience of travelling from London to Paris and back was quite positive, thankfully, but there have been complaints of delays on the return journeys. We were only required check in 45 minutes prior to departure, which is a considerable improvement over the 2 hours necessary at most busy airports. We find that taking the Eurostar instead of travelling by plane out of Heathrow saves both time and money. Getting through security and EU immigration is much quicker than at airports, and there is then a brief wait for a few minutes inside the waiting room before boarding the Eurostar train. There is a decent amount of food vendors and places to get drinks and snacks. The train itself is very comfortable especially if upgraded to premium (at GBP50) as this option includes bigger chairs and a light lunch with drinks. The compartments were clean and the A/C properly working. The experience of going through the tunnel is interesting - it is dark inside of course but it only It takes around 35 minutes to travel the length of the Channel Tunnel before you exit into the flat landscape of Northern France on the way to Paris. All going well it takes about two and half hours before arrive right in the heart of the city of Paris at Gare du Nord. It’s definitely not the most glamorous part of Paris the conditions in Gare du Nord Eurostar are not so good as in St. Pancras. At present going through security in the International station in St. Pancras is usually here quick and straightforward, but, unfortunately this may change if/when the full force of Brexit hits home.

We travelled from London to Paris via the Eurostar.  Our departure was delayed almost an hour but did not hamper our plans very much.  The trip was easy and pleasant and very affordable compared to airfare.  We would use it again in the future.

It’s 2019 and I would guess that 99.9% of travellers departing from Brussels on the Eurostar have some sort of mobile device, many of which need charging. Airports take this into account admirably and have charging points all over the place. How many are at the ES departure lounge at Brussels?  Well there are two, and those are linked to bike machines which have to be pedalled to produce power. Pathetic is the only word that comes to mind. I wrote to Eurostar and they blamed the station. Sorry to say that but that is an unacceptable and, again, a pathetic answer.
Stay away from Eurostar, do yourself a favor a travel another way. We spent 8 hours waiting for a train, missed a tour and what did Eurostar offer $57 for future travel.

Had to cancel a eurostar trip through ill health. As I did not know when I would be fit to travel I requested a voucher or similar so I could re-book when I was fit.They made absolutely no effort to help me and were the only company that I dealt with that gave the impression that they didn't give a damn about you.So disheartening that companies like this still exist.
Went from London to Paris and it was quick, comfortable and it was nice to look out at the countryside. Son liked the speed, I liked the lunch, and husband liked the bar :)

There is no doubt this is the easiest way to travel from London to Paris!  The train was awesome- we were in standard premier and had both meal and tea service.  The trains were clean and very easy to navigate. When traveling in Europe, I would not hesitate to use Eurostar again. Highly recommend.

Even if you buy the ticket that is flexible, Eurostar has a way to change the "pricing" of the current ticket. A train can be completely empty and the ticket would be 300 euro, making sure you pay the large differences. You are better of flying!
This has been an absolute dream to travel on. Quickest, most comfortable and easy way to get somewhere. No luggage problems, no long queues and before I knew it we had arrived.

St Pancras Station is easy to get to has dining options available and getting on the Train was easy.  Train is very comfortable, I upgraded.   Had Lunch and a couple glasses of wine on the Journey.  Gare du Nord station in Paris is convenient to all the attractions and ground transport is waiting right out side the door.  Did I mention this train is fast.  180MPH  what a fun way to travel and less hassle than going by air.

We have used Eurostar on a few occasions. Twice to Paris and once to Brussels (then onto Bruges). First time from St. Pancras which was a hassle getting to from mid Essex. But we now found that Ebbsfleet was a better bet for us and, an extra, Ebbsfleet is easier and quicker through security. Parking is easy and very close by. When travelling to France or Belgium we will always use this fast, clean, and friendly service. Hopefully they will sort out the return journey from Amsterdam. Then we will give that a try.

This was an awesome experience for us. We upgraded our travel to Coach 2. The seats are very comfortable and the food served was surprisingly good: goat cheese stuffed chicken with couscous; bread; carrot cake; white and red wines. Love that they keep serving you wine too :) There is also a virtual reality tour on your phone that you can look at when you are in the tunnel. It's a cartoon so mostly for kids but we kind of enjoyed it. Would definitely book again.
Went to Amsterdam on Eurostar.  Left on time and was not too full.  Managed to get a table seat as our reserved seats were taken over by a family.

Relaxed way to travel from London to Amsterdam. The other way around doesn't work yet. You get on in the heart of London, being there 30-40 minutes in advance is enough. Don't come too early, the waiting area is hopelessly too small.

After a delay which was not Eurostar’s doing , although their communication was awful about reopening the check in, we headed off for Amsterdam. Except we were told our train was now going to terminate in Brussels.... we had a connection in an hr. that connection ended up standing room only for almost 3 hrs then it still didn’t get us to Amsterdam, we had to change at Rotterdam then wait another 40 mins and get a train and tickets to arrive 6 hours late. I’ve just had a compensatory email £20 e voucher for my next travel?!?! I don’t think so. I’m going to ATOL with this.

We had no problem on this trip. Best to get to St Pancras early for check in and passport control. Watch the monitors for platform information.  Train trip was uneventful, just a hint beware of overpriced taxis at Amsterdam station, we only needed trip of under 2 kilometers and he was charging 40 Euro!. We ended up taking an UBER for around 15 Euro.

For the third year in a row my train is canceled at the last minute due to strikes. Eurostar is not recommended for travel between March and April. In addition, their telephone contact is always busy and the staff is not informed. Very bad experiences. Too bad I'll go by plane from now on.

I booked a trip from London to Paris for my wife and I. It was our first time on Eurostar and the business premier upgrade looked appealing, no wait times, drinks and meal included, along with a larger more comfortable seat. We skipped the que to get into the security checkpoint, so good so far. Once we got past that point, we were lumped in with everyone else and it took about 15min to get through to the gate. Eurostar claims you can arrive up to 10min before the train departs, but there is no way you would make it to the train if you did. Luckily we came 40 min before hand. The business class rail car was nice but the seats felt like sitting on cardboard. Nothing close to any business class seat I have been on. The WiFi onboard might as well not even been there because by the time an email goes through you will be at your destination. I downloaded their app to watch movies on board, but the movies wouldn’t play. We opted out of the meal, but the food looked ok. Just book a regular ticket, the upgrades are not worth anything close to what they charge.

I took the Eurostar train from Brussels to London. The one-way ticket was awfully expensive, but it was still the most convenient way to get to London. The check in though was painful. the line was very long and I missed my train. So for next time, I'll make sure I arrive to the train station with lots of time.

We were traveling from Paris to London to catch a flight back to New York with our 8 month old daughter.Thirty minutes into our journey, the train stopped for ninety minutes. No updates, no AC, no electricity, no lights even, no water. It was terrible. The toilets stank and our infant daughter was miserable. It was a terrible afternoon that I wouldn’t wish for my enemies.When a new train came to take us to London we had to move our luggage into the new train ourself and that took an extra three hours. All in all - even though I built in an extra 5 hrs of cushion it wasn’t enough and it took us over SEVEN hours to get to London.I was charged $1800 because I missed my flight. I took it up with Eurostar and virgin air for months and no one would help me. Can you believe that Eurostar wouldn’t even give u a full refund??? They only offered half even after I escalated apparently to the highest level of “customer care.”Our family now has $2k in credit card debt because of Eurostar. Also- all around terrible customer service. Never using them again.

Due to a 'go slow' by French authroities in Paris, my train to London was delayed by 1.5hrs. This meant I missed my connection from Euston to Manchester and I was forced to spend £90 on a new ticket. Eurostar refuse to compensate me for this cost. Disgraceful.

We booked on the train from London St Pancras to Paris Gare Du Nord online!Check in was incredibly easy, we scanned our tickets at the automated gates, went through security (same as an airport, bag scan and metal detector) and through Passport Control. There is a small duty free shop and a few food outlets and several information screens which keep you informed of the departures of trains and the platform your train is going from.One Gripe is that St Pancras is a bit of a mission to get to on the underground, I traveled Eurostar before and it went from London Waterloo which was much easier. We boarded the train on time but were delayed leaving due to the Customs Strike on the French side the driver of our train was delayed coming in, however we were kept well informed by the train crew.The journey itself was comfortable however the free onboard wifi is incredibly slow. Sadly the return journey from Paris to London was not as smooth but this is in no way Eurostars fault! Due to the French Customs Strikes all Eurostar services were subject to delay or cancellation so we arrived at Gare Du Nord far earlier than we usually would have done, when we arrived there was already a huge queue snaking around the station, this queue was incredibly slow moving but eventually after 4 hours we got through security and 2 lots of passport control and ended up getting the (late leaving) train we were originally booked on! Due to the number of cancelled trains bookings did not count for anything and people were being given boarding passes for whichever train was the next to depart, you were assigned a coach to go to but not a seat, we ended up in the seats opposite the ones we booked.I really cannot fault Eurostar as their staff were taking a lot of abuse from passengers for a situation what was completely beyond their control, however they remained friendly and professional and kept people as informed as they could and were giving out free bottles of water to people in the queue.I would not hesitate to travel Eurostar again in the future.

I am change business travel habits : using more train, planes only when really necessary. Beside the environmental advantage, the fact the you can really work on a train makes this switch easy.Recent train services from Lille to Lyon by Thalys (3hr, only 2 stops), Berlin to Neurenberg by German high speed services supported a reasonable Internet signal though WiFi.  The Internet on the Eurostar, especially the UK part of the trip is just a disaster. Tried to follow a web-based meeting, but could only catch like 2minutes out of the 30 min meeting.It’s a pitty that no investments are made yet to support decent Internet.

On our way to catch the Eurostar to Paris we had to pass through the lovely central London Victorian Saint Pancras railway station, now known as St Pancras International, home to Eurostar with its direct high-speed train link to the Tunnel and Amsterdam, Avignon, Brussels, Lille, Lyon, Marseille, Paris, and Rotterdam.  We had arranged to meet friends in Paris for a week-long adventure, and what better way to get there from London was on the Eurostar, with all its modern-day amenities like Free Films & TV, Usb Sockets, and on-board entertainment. It is stress free and really fast, no standing in long lines like at the airport, and very convenient to the city centers. We had a coffee at Le Pain Quotidien bakery at the London station, two bottles of wine on the train and a short time later a glass of very smooth wine in a Paris bistro. The station is very clean, bright and airy.TIP: Check Eurostar deals before you book, you might get a deal.

it was the first time i used that train, from St Pancras to Brussels Midithe price of a low cost plane, but for a train which starts and let you in the middle of the two citieswe had two big luggage, easy to transport with that train, costly to do it by planeabout the travel itself, it was very pleasant - we spent some time to the little bar, for a coffee and bang, France!; another short time to speak, and we reach Brussels, etcno delay, by the wayit is a very good alternative to plane, with good connections to local inner city public transports

TerribleThree hour delay on my way out from London to Paris. Cancelled on the return and no availability to travel the same day. The most terrible service due to French industrial action. The most hopeless county in Europe for business! Avoid!

The Eurostar is probably the worst high speed train in Europe. I traveled in business class from Paris to London and almost everything is disappointing. The cabin and seats are old and badly kept, food is really terrible but the worst of all are toilets, they work very bad and there was no water even in business class! Terrible experience for a train in Europe!

Travelling on the Eurostar should be a great way to travel to Paris.  Once you are on the train it is comfortable and relaxing.  It is a great pity therefore that the whole experience was totally ruined by the gross inefficiency, incompetence and crass bureaucracy of the St Pancras Eurostar staff.  Overwhelmed by high traveller numbers, the staff appeared incapable of moving people through the airport style security checks at anything other than a snail's pace.  As a consequence many of the passangers were forced to miss their booked trains. If you think airports are slow, St Pancras is far worse.  In my frustration I had to resort to assisted passage through the checks.  Thank goodness the calm and efficiency of the journey once on the Eurostar train was a welcome contrast.  I also noted that the return journey through Paris Eurostar was relatively painless.  I will probably fly next time.

Booking well in advance we bagged a one way ticket from Brussels Midi to London St Pancras for 35.00 Euros 💶 Check In and Security took at least 15 minutes and there after we grabbed a snack for the train and boarded 10 minutes later making ourselves comfortable for the 2 hour journeyThe train left on time at 1251 and arrived into a London 1406hOn board Food & Drinks were available and staff made clear announcements in Flemish , French & English Overall a great service & bargain .....

I travel to Paris almost every week and occasionally to Brussels and had a wonderful service from Ashford International until about 3 years ago. As I travel regularly I have a White Card which gives me some appreciable privilidge although with the prices of the tickets I feel I pay for themUnfortunately today the service is reduced drastically and is very unreliable. The privilidges like free parking have been scrapped and none of the staff appear to be able to do anything.Now on top of unreliability there are long delays because of operational problems and French customs officials. East jet to Gatwick is looking like a much more attractive alternative.

I had booked a package deal below yesterday and when creating my package it was advertised as £343. However, when checking out (no further amendments made) this price increased to £391. I have also checked the same deal today and it is also £343 for the exact same deal. I have also taken photos of the prices as proof and have been told that this price cannot be honoured which is very disappointing as Eurostar should not be changing the price when checking out, especially without informing customers that the price has now increased in the space of 15 minutes!

Travelled Ashford Internationl to Paris early morning in a Standard seat and it was comfortable enough. No food or drink, just a gaggle of middle aged women drinking champagne on a 6:20am train which only allowed them to get louder and louder as the journey progressed. It might have been a stress free journey had it not been for the disregard for others. Return trip I booked us standard premier to gauge the difference between this and standard and it certainly was worth the extra bit, more comfortable seats and good food served by very friendly and professional staff. Having read the bad reviews prior to our journey I was pleasantly surprised to find that this wasnt the case. I did check out the Business permier coach and quite honestly say that I couldnt see the difference in seating from standard premier. The only differenc would be the Business Permier Lounge prior to departure - certainly not worth the 300% increase in price. Return trip was serene, no drunk cackling middle aged birds on a mid life crisis trip, just people wanting tranqulity like us. Very impressed.

I am a wheelchair user, and I’d like to commend Eurostar for their exceptional customer service.  It was wonderful to travel in business class for a standard class price, and the included food was quite tasty.  I travel with two companions, and the second companion had to buy a standard ticket sitting separately from us, because of our budget.  But on our outward journey, the check-in staff upgraded her to business for free - and on our return trip, the train staff let her join us in business anyway.  As a wheelchair user, it was very easy to travel on the Eurostar.  The newer train model especially had lots of room to maneuver and a very large bathroom.  Definitely easier than flying.

I had a meeting in Paris so decided to take the train as I thought I could spend the travel time working. The check-in was tedious, their use of technology is a massive fail, in this case passport control which was slow and error-ridden, unlike the automatic barriers one finds at airports. The journey itself was pleasant, especially on the return journey as I had paid for an upgrade: the service, food, and wine were delightful. The big issue also concerns technology: the slow speed signal frequently dropped out. They warn you of the variability asking travellers to excuse this because the signal is supplied by 3G and 4G networks, a poor excuse in the 21st century. Personally I don’t believe the cost of this service is justified for business travellers without a decent internet connection, unless you are a business traveller who has time on their hands to enjoy what is almost stress-free travel.

I would never recommend eurostar. I got two tickets for almost 200dolars from london to paris, but i got them from a company named goeuro, i biught the tickets the 1st of january travelling the 3rd of march 2019, the 22nd of february i got an email from eurostar saying that they had a disruption and had to cancelled my ticket, the offered me to exchange or get a refund for my ticket, they never answered my exchange request, and the told me i had to ask goeuro for the refund. But eurostar had to cancelled their trains because of a disruption they had, go euro didn’t cancelled my tickets. I had to buy  two more tickets for 500dolars because eurostar didn’t reply to my exchange request, and now is the 1st of march and i couldn’t get any refund from neither of the two companies and i’m out of 700dolars

We bought tickets to travel from Paris to London, the trip was good, the problem is the dirt in the bathrooms and carriages. In my car the 2 bathrooms (men's and women's) were out of service and the bathroom in the next car did not have toilet paper, the other bathroom was covered. It is a very expensive train to have such poor toilet service.

We are a familly of 4 people. We baught some tickets to go to London for some holliday from next monday, in 3 days.My husband learned yesterday evening that his hollidays are cancelled because his company urgently need him to work on an important technical problem.We tried to reorganise our holidays to spend some good time with my children without their father. Having left for a weekend in London, we are well settled in the Eurostar. Customs clearance was well carried out and boarding was impeccable. The trip started off well

The seats were comfortable but the legroom is not that good in Standard class compared with the same class on GWR. The wifi is far from good. difficult to get onto it and when on it either kicks you out or breaks up.

Appalling will never use again. I refer to a Delayed journey of 74min from King's Cross to Paris.First of all, the service is atrocious. When we arrived at King's Cross at 1.00am from Coventry for the 5.40 train (later train not possible due to lack of overnight services) we found no waiting area and it was probably one of the coldest nights this year. This is unacceptable to 65 and 66year olds waiting on a metal bench in the freezing cold for 4hours. We both ended up with severe colds and flu for our holiday. Then we missed all our connections down to Genova in Italy and ended up staying overnight in Turin thanks to SNCF who ensured our safety, as there was no other train to Genova until the following day. Then when we went to book our return with Eurostar the prices were ridiculously high so we took the ferry from Calais which was a delight. Needless to say our experience of the Eurostar will not happen again as we won't be using it!Not only should they refund the entire ticket but they should pay compensation for the stress we endured.

We travelled to Bruges for a weekend celebration. Train from London was on time and comfortable  and the connection at Brussels was easy and quick. Not a lot of room in the seats but it was only 2 hours to Brussels. The Wi-fi was so slow as to be useless. On the return we could not access it at all which was bad for a business service.There isn’t enough room for all the luggage, it feels as if more seats have been crammed in. However it’s quicker than flying and easy.

I recently bought first class tickets Paris to London on Eurostar. I bought them through Raileurope for approx A$100 each less than if bought directly from Eurostar.Raileuroe automatically allocate seats which cannot be changed. Eurostar allows selection of seats.The seats we were allocated are next to a bulkhead and we have little chance of seeing anything from our seats.It appears to me that the seats are offered at discounted prices simply because there are not good seats.Has anyone else had this experience.

to avoid taking my car, in London, the train is great...But customer service non-existent Difficult departure, be careful train canceled at the last minute with children,...Super - Great They don't need us, until the day!!!!
Good transport to London. Comfortable seats. Sockets for recharging the batteries.

We booked our trip 6 months in advance. Family of 4, 2 adults and 2 children in standard seats travelling from Ebbsfleet to Disneyland Paris.  Very surprised on the ease of parking Ebbsfleet. Literally 1 minute walk from car to station. Only shop to purchase food and drinks, M&S go. Eurostar staff really helpful with information and guidance for first time travellers of the Eurostar. Arrived 1 hour prior to departure as advised and little ques through security. Nicely surprised with a newly refurbished train. Plenty of leg room in standard seats with plug sockets (UK & EU). Very well organised and child friendly! Will definitely travel via Eurostar again.

My family of 4 recently took the Eurostar from London to Paris and back on a standard premier ticket.  We did this several years ago and it was lovely, but they have definitely "cut back".  The snack from london to paris was terrible and on the way back our train was delayed- no weather issue, just some sort of train maintenance issue.  After being assured we were being rebooked in same standard premier class in same configuration by 2 different agents, we got on the train and soon discovered they had elected to go with a smaller train with no standard premier and had seated us separately.  Never were we asked if we wanted to keep our same class and go on a later train.  Fortunately other customers were also misassigned seats and we all traded so we could sit as originally planned and we all regretted not stopping to bring our own "snack" since what we paid for on the train was not being provided.  After the trip, I asked for a refund- we had paid over $300 for the upgrade in class.  I was told my original ticket receipt was not good enough for a refund, I had to find the ticket I was reassigned. Do they not keep track of train issues?  After finding the 4 reassigned tickets, scanning and sending I was told a refund was not possible.  They offered me an evoucher of $320.  I have no plans to be in Europe so they suggested I give them to a "friend". I feel like I was completely scammed and will never take Eurostar again.  If you still elect to take Eurostar don't waste your money on an upgrade.  Its not worth it and you may get scammed like us.  Consumer rights in Europe must be terrible if this is allowable.

Great value if booked ahead and very easy to use.  No problems with the customs or security at either end and no need to bother with very small quantities of liquids or very small carry on cases for a weekend away.Seats were clean and comfortable.All in all I will use again as I had not used them for around 10 years, but the cheapo offer was just such great value for money.Service on the train is good as well, however the buffet car only had a limited selection, hence I think that you may be better off taking your own food with you.

If you create an account with Eurostar, you can book further ahead than the website otherwise allows. Usually you can book about 180 days before, but I booked 203 days before when I created an account first. The difference in prices if you get one of the early bookings is huge! In 2019, the lowest price is 50.50.
My wife and I travelled from London to Paris in a business class seat and were both very impressed. Clean, OK food, great service and on schedule.

This is a simple and straight forward service and is so easy to use, will recommend anyone to use this instead of flying, we went premier and the service was excellent, the return from Paris to London was fab and were looked after by the staff so well! Annabelle looked after us and is an asset to the company!

There is plenty to be positive about Eurostar. It gets you from the centre of London to the centre of Paris, Brussels, and now Amsterdam, quicker and more conveniently than any air travel can. If you book ahead, and choose your travel dates and times carefully, you can do it as cheaply as any budget airline (once you factor-in the cost of reaching a city centre from an airport). On the whole, the staff are professional and polite. the trains are comfortable, and there is none of the security hassles surrounding liquids. If you need to bring some pickled onions, some Marmite and a few pints of English bitter back home to the European mainland, there's no need to check-in your hand luggage. So far so good.If it's busy, there are too few passport booths at Brussels Midi (both Belgian and British) and St Pancras isn't much better. This can cause unwelcome congestion in the check-in area. On the trains, wifi can be unreliable, too. Not all trains have electric charging points in standard class. Interestingly, when there's no internet connection in standard carriages, just move along the train and try it in Business Premier where you may find that your problems are solved!The difficulty I have with Eurostar (compared to the excellent Thalys service between Paris, Brussels and Amsterdam, which I use a lot, and the incomparable French TGV services which I use more or less weekly) is that it cuts too many corners - not least on customer service. There are far too many delays on Eurostar, and these delays are compounded by the superior attitude of the staff who seem to delight in not providing information. I may be completely wrong, but I get the impression that Eurostar is not a great company to work for, and its treatment of its staff is evident in the attitude of the staff towards customers. The moment a train arrives at its destination, the staff are the first off the train, and head for the terminal at the speed of lightening, which means there is absolutely no-one on the platform to help or advise if there are delays or difficulties. If you are unlucky enough (as I have been on several occasions) to be on a train where the journey is cut short late at night (e.g. at Lille or Calais) you try finding Eurostar staff to help with the onward journey! You are left to cope as best you can.Compare this to a delay caused by stormy weather on the TGV to Boredaux recently, where we were diverted to Angouleme and held for just over an hour. The moment we stepped off the train, not only was there an army of SNCF staff to answer questions, but a stall with free drinks and a doggy bag containing salads, chocolate and biscuits for each passenger.The other issue is cancellations. A couple of weeks ago, we were notified about the cancellation of specific trains 'due to weather conditions' in Brussels and Paris. As I looked out of the window of my Brussels office, on a dry day with blue skies and no immediate forecast of snow, I was baffled. As I was when looking at the forecast on Meteo France. When I mentioned this to a regular fellow passenger in Brussels Midi later that day, she said that an informed source had told her that Eurostar are prone to cancel services that are not fully booked. That's worth bearing in mind if you absolutely have to be on a specific train. A service with cheaper tickets available close to the date of travel is always a tell-tale sign.If you are planning to travel from St Pancras to Amsterdam, the return journey to London is not direct (you still have to change in Brussels). Try taking the first part of the return journey on the Thalys service as far as Brussels and you will get a good idea of the difference.Of course, Eurostar is a monopoly for direct services between London, Paris and Brussels. A bit of competition on the same routes would certainly shake it out of its complacency.
Took the Eurostar from London to Brussels and everything ran perfectly- to the minute. Security was quick and smooth and the train itself was very comfortable (even in standard class).

I take Eurostar on a monthly basis and I am fed up! First of all, the prices are outrageous for a train ticket (sometimes £200+ for a one way) and the service is extremely poor. Trains are late once every other time, and sometimes even canceled. There is a huge queue to pass the security and customs barriers which causes delays and inconvenience. The Eurostar staff is aware of this because it happens all the time but do not do anything to solve it. The worse is probably the French side, where the security machines STILL DON'T HAVE TRAYS meaning you have to put your coat and bags on the dirty treadmill. I don't understand why they just can't provide trays.

I travelled Paris to London on Eurostar and the experience was amazing. The Seats of train were comfy, had Wifi facility and had cleaned washroom. I was feeling like travelling in business class plane and I reached London on time without any delay,However when I was retiring from London To Paris, my train was delayed by 2 hour and I got the compensation for waiting at station. The staff was so good . Once in lifetime, one must experience to travel via this train that is to one country to another counter via underground English Channel. I give a big thumbs up👍🏻

So much easier getting the train than flying,  going through security was a breeze not busy no hassles.. Train  was comfortable  myself and my partner was in standard which was very comfortable, train left on time and arrived at Gare Du Nord at the time stated , ok Gar due Nord station is a bit of a minefield, we  needed to connect to the Metro, but once we found it  was all ok... seats on the train  was very comfy shame planes are not like this.. only thing Id say the buffet  not that much selection and a little overpriced.. other than a good journey... only probs we had was waiting at St. Pancreas Eurostar to board  was the services in the cafe  absolutely rip off and service dire....

Really mixed thoughts. Travelled to Lille on business. London side:Fantastic old upgraded station. Really modern comfortable feel. Warm throughout with quick boarding. Comfortable journey. Good buffet carLille side:Freezing cold platform with long queues. Bag check slow and arrogant. Platform and boarding chaos. Train packed due to cancellations. Train was freezing through the whole journey

Were due to travel on 7th Feb as a birthday treat for my wife.About 36 hours before departure they cancel with a standard email and a link to re-book or cancel the trip. Link does not work as all it does is takes you to a compensation page. Can't change the train time by loging in to my account and Cant phone as office is shut.Book flights instead at double the Eurostar price.Then phone the next day only to spend 15 minutes getting the refund sorted out after being questioned a number of times and asking if we want to re-book. This despite me telling them in the first place that it was a treat for my wife for her birthday, so why would I want to go at another date. Refund takes about 3 weeks she said.Customer service need massive improvements as does the IT. No womder they never made any money for such a long time.

I travel on the Eurostar regularly. Overall it is fairly good. They make a bit too much of a song and dance about getting on the train with seemingly unecessary queues all the time. It is however a fairly smooth operation from once central location to another. Sometimes depending on my schedule and activity I do or don't get the insurance. Last time I did and I wanted to make a claim.......impossible!!I had MONDIAL-ASSISTANCE. This is the default insurer that appears at the bottom of the purchasing exercise. It may vary as to where you buy your ticket from. Anyway DON'T GET THIS INSURANCE - THEY WILL NEVER PAY. They also have one of the worst online Customer ratings of any product I have ever seen.As I said travelling on Eurostar is ok but the purchasing agreement is terrible. Minimum of 40 euros to change a ticket and buying a ticket close to the date of travel is very very expensive. Book in advance, don't miss your train and get some insurance that you can actually trust. Bon voyage!

We booked a Holiday package deal through Eurostar from London to Paris for a 3 day weekend. We received a text message 2 days before departing stating our train had been cancelled due to maintenance as a result of severe weather. We requested a refund as the text message said we could, directly with Eurostar. As we were meeting friends in Paris for the weekend we booked flights and accommodation with another company. 7 hours later, we received another text message from Eurostar apologising for the confusion but our Eurostar train is running and have a nice trip. We contacted Eurostar and told them we had requested a refund. We also informed them we had re-booked our trip through another company after being notified of the cancellation. We have been in battle trying to get a FULL refund. The Train Tickets are being refunded. The accommodation is not. Please be aware that on Holiday Deals/Packages offered by Eurostar there is NO refund on the accommodation portion of the trip if your train is cancelled. This was our first experience with Eurostar and we are not impressed.
Regular traveller with business commute and totally fed up with the promise of Wi-Fi. I have never got it to work properly. Choice of on board snacks are dismal

As part of a surprise visit to Paris, this was my inaugural use of the Eurostar, before this I would not have thought of using this, I’d have flown, this trip has changed my mind, it was efficient, on time and delightful.The staff were very helpful and courteous. The train was more comfortable than envisaged. The amenities of board worked and it was an enjoyable and quick trip from central London to the centre of Paris for a night out and an overnight break.It was a special birthday and a message was played over the PA system to my embarrassment and joy. The staff were great and then found me to wish me a nice time. It is the little touches that you remember and I am so grateful to you. Cannot wait to travel again.Please note that the return leg the following day was also enjoyable, efficient, clean, relaxing and comfortable. This journey was again to time and the staff were still helpful and nice without it needing to be my birthday. This was still great, without the bells and whistles

Travelled in Standard Premier Class which was very comfortable.There was adequate luggage space in the train.The service was very good, we had lunch which was served cold, I would have appreciated a hot lunch. I had the same meal (vegan) on both outward and inward journey which was a bit disappointing!On the outward journey there was no Wifi available on that train!

I first travelled with Eurostar in 1995. Since then I have made hundreds of trips between Brussels - London, Paris - London, and recently London - Rotterdam. I like the service. However, I think it would be far better if the Eurostar made a stopat Schiphol before Amsterdam, this would attract a lot more passengers. Also, the speed of the train between Brussels - Rotterdam/Amsterdam is unnervingly slow. Speed up this leg to the same speed as London - Brussels, and make a stopat Schiphol and you will have a winner of a service that airlines cannot compete with.
From Brussels to central London in about two hours! Significant time saving compared to the plane! You travel comfortably and in a relaxed environment, with excellent Wi-Fi and other amenities.

My girlfriend and I caught the train to London from Brussels before Christmas. When we got to security we were told that her ice skates (small as they are) needed to be "registered". Weird, but if they want to "register" ice skates I guess that is their issue. The problems were that: 1. this "process" took a ridiculous length of time - enough (after already waiting in a long queue) that we were told we had missed our train (we had not) and then we were told that we had to run to catch it (during which process other property of ours was damaged); 2. we were made to pay €20 for a "service" that obviously should be free (it is their problem, not ours, if they need to "register" ice skates); 3. the security staff member we had the misfortune to deal with was most unhelpful (he boasted that he did not care about customer service because, as he was proud to tell us, he is not employed by Eurostar) and 4. the security staff member in question was not wearing his ID, in distinction to all the other security staff (I gather from what he said to us that many complaints have been levelled against him - he seems to be some kind of rogue employee). None of this is acceptable. We trusted Eurostar with our travel arrangements. Our trust was misplaced. Eurostar contracts security staff and they are responsible for this part of the service too. If there are idiosyncratic luggage requirements these need to be notified beforehand. The signs at the station listing proscribed hand luggage do not mention skates and everyone we have discussed this with has been surprised. I travelled a great deal on Eurostar before this event (and am a great fan of trains). I have not used Eurostar since. I will revise this review should I receive a satisfactory response from the company. It's never too late for people to do the right thing.

Our Eurostar train changed so we got given different carriage and seat numbers when we checked in, no big deal at all as the service was still spot on and speedy. On the way back however it was complete opposite, the security and staff at Lille Europe was absolutely useless, we only had 30 minute window to get our Eurostar to London from Lille EU and no one seemed to know where we should be queuing to get through passport control! We got sent to the ticket office but this was wrong so had to rejoin the long queue. We now had only 10 minutes left to board our train and were still in security section. Then on board the WiFi was not working at all so it felt even longer to get to London!

Eurostar from Brussels to London. OK, agreed, it's much less hassle than flying and the longer journey in your seat allows some sleep despite the same endless & loud blabla on the speaker (welcome blabla at each stop,blablafor the bar coach, blabla for saying hello...).On the minus side, the seat in the new Siemens trains look inviting but are hard as a concrete slab, legroom in Standard Class is just sufficient, poor food choice in the 'bar' and not nice to eat on site, you need to go to your seat with your little bag (no seating).Last but not least, PUNCTUALITY is very poor, our outbound train was cancelled 'because of the weather' (very light snow that day in Belgium) so we arrived with then next train in London late in the evening. Our inbound train was delayed for more than one hour (unspecified 'technical problems' delaying all Eurostart trains at St Pancras).Useless & superslow 'free WiFi' and, what would you expect ?, filthy toilets.All in all, Eurostar is somewhat better than flying (less hassle) but it is trying very hard to be just as annoying. If you need to go to London from Belgium, not much choice left since the demise of VLM.

We have travelled from Lodon or Ashford to Paris many times over the years, and I love it. The seats are comfortable, and the train is not only very fast, but very quiet too. We took advantage of a special offer this time, which made the cost incredibly reasonable.

First ever time travelling on the Eurostar, would definitely recommend it as a means of travel to Paris, Brussels, Amsterdam , so much less hassle than flying, and made for a very pleasant travel experience. Somehow managed to book standard premier tickets, which was very pleasant, the carriage was nice and comfortable and the light meal and complementary drinks provided all made for a lovely train journey .

We used Eurostar round trip between London and Paris on a recent vacation (that began in America).  We paid - for two adults traveling on weekdays in early January - slightly more than $115 round trip for each of us.  That's less that a quarter of the walk-up fare.The trick, for us, was to determine our dates and times of travel and then stick to them.  We also booked more than 30 days in advance and spent a fair amount of time on the (easy to use) Eurostar website ensuring we had the best price.  The boarding and ride are exactly as advertised: quick and comfortable.  We were even able to purchase a carnet of Metro tickets, saving us the time of navigating a machine at Gare du Nord.Last tip: Gare du Nord is also a Metro and RER hub.  For two Metro tickets (total price: $3.20), we took the RER Blue Line two stops to St. Michel.  That's a substantial saving over the 45 Euro ($56) cab ride paid the same day by another traveler at our hotel.

My trip was from Cologne to London. Thanks to long-term travel planning, I was able to purchase cheap tickets in 1st class. I found checking in and the security check in Brussels stressful and the staff at the security checkpoints extremely unfriendly and rude. I traveled alone with 2 suitcases, a handbag and a small backpack and a winter coat. Everything had to be lifted onto the conveyor belt for the security check, and people were then pushing from behind. As I was going through the security check, it beeped and I was checked for metal with a hand-held device. Meanwhile, my luggage and also my handbag with my wallet and passport were lying unattended and out of my sight. I found that unacceptable. In addition, the extremely unfriendly staff...You then have to sit in the waiting area for 30-45 minutes until the train leaves, but there are also toilets there and an opportunity to organize something to eat or drink. The call is then made and you are allowed to go onto the platform for the train. On both journeys I had a single seat in an open-plan compartment in first class. There was enough space to put my suitcases on a shelf at the end of the compartment. I found the seats very worn and shabby, WiFi was only available when we were in the tunnel. The staff on the train were very friendly and helpful given. Plus a drink, water, soft drink, wine or beer and then coffee or tea. Plus a small dessert and a cookie. The train drove quite quietly, unfortunately you couldn't see much of the landscape behind the tunnel in England. The train was on time both on the outward journey and on the return journey. It then arrived in London at St. Pancras station. From there you can easily reach all corners of London by subway. The journey itself was fine, just like the train, but checking in with luggage was really bad, so I'd rather take the plane again next time. A note for the return journey: if you have to continue from Brussels towards Germany, you shouldn't take too short a changeover time. I had just under 20 minutes, but I had already moved so far forward on the train that when I got off I was immediately at the place on the platform where you can leave the platform via stairs. So I managed to catch my connecting train to Cologne. You should definitely plan 10 minutes as pure walking time. The ICE tracks are a short distance away. I arrived in Brussels on Friday afternoon (on the train that leaves London at around 3 p.m.) and if I hadn't reached my ICE connection there would have been no connection to Cologne or Frankfurt or Düsseldorf that day.

Hello,We arrive in front of the tail, the hostess closes the passage before us pretending that there are only 28 minutes!Forcing us to take a penalty of 44 pounds per person (about 400 euros for our group ???) and we recommend taking the Eurolines (bus) if we were not happy ??Very good stays in the English capital. However, the Eurostar company only seeks profit without any empathy or commercial spirit. Pity.

Ebbsfleet (kent) to Paris in 2 hours and 6 minutes, travelling comfortably but the best is the service provided on board  by a very experienced and friendly Crew. The journey did not seem as long as it took, as we were in company of a very enthusiastic team members who made sure we were satisfied with the Eurostar experience. Bravo EuroStar and Thank you.

Hello, I have not traveled by this train yet, but I plan to do so in June. I would only like to ask if I should be at the platform for at least two hours before boarding the train? I heard that there is a check-in like when you go to a plane?

My children and I took the Eurostar from London to Paris. The lines were ridiculously long (as expected), but surprisingly moved along steadily. Employees held up signs with destinations and times and helped direct passengers into the right lines.The ride to Paris was smooth and we were able to catch a few naps. When we reached the outskirts of Paris, however, we were unable to get off the train for a while as someone had reportedly placed an object in the tracks. I am grateful that the safety of the passengers was a priority and the delayed arrival time was no problem at all for us.Instructions were spoken and displayed on monitors in English and French. I would definitely use Eurostar for other trips between European countries for the affordability, efficiency, and comfort.

Thursday January 10 departure from Paris scheduled for 9:13 a.m. Departure 45 minutes late Saturday January 12 return from London with departure scheduled for 4:31 p.m. Departure 45 minutes late. Simply SCANDALOUS. Having travelers come between 45 and 60 minutes to register what is the point??? Considering where the tickets are sold it's not giving a damn about the world.

This is not so much as the Eurostar journey itself but the customer service. You can't knock travelling from the centre of London to the centre of Paris. In principal. I'll find out in a few months how that rates as I get my first eurostar for a few years. As for the costumer service. OK I made a mistake. I booked a train from London to Paris instead of London to Lille. It was a silly mistake. I had been booking different journeys and making different searches and I got mixed up. As soon as I pressed the button to buy I realised my mistake and FOUR (yes four) minutes later I called Eurostar hoping to get a simple rectification.Would the customer services person issue a simple refund so that I could go back in (online) and make the same transaction a few minutes later? No chance. I was told that I would have to pay a £10 fee and they would rebook my train and any difference in fare would NOT be refunded.The rebooking took forever. Now this is NOT the first time I have done this. 80% of my purchases are done online so I am bound to make a mistake here and there. But every other company I have dealt with has, without flinching, refunded my money immediately if I have called then within the house and I have gone back in and purchased the correct fare straight away. And Im talking the likes of Virgin Trains. British Airways. German Trains dB. Even LOT airways (who have some pretty terrible customer service). But not Eurostar. It took an email to customer services, their press department and some top bod a few days AFTER I had paid the fees to get my money back. The way the letter was written, I was meant to feel grateful that they had made an exception. Blimey.And to be honest, it wasn't really the money. It was the principal. I vaguely remember reading somewhere that there is a cooling off period for online purchases. However, forgetting that, surely all companies should put into place a 'common sense' period. If a customer calls up four minutes (or even an hour or so) after mistakenly booking a product online (eg a ticket), it is obvious it is a mistake and common sense should prevail. It wasn't until i saw eurostar's 82% terrible customer service score on trustpilot did I realise that many others were no happy with the way the company deals with its customers. Maybe they should have a serious rethink. Or maybe they need competition on the cross channel rails to wake them out of their slightly arrogant customer service slumber
The trip from Paris to London in premier standard was sensational. It was worth paying a little more for the extra comfort.

The EuroStar is the most efficient way travel from one country to another with ease. This was the first time we used Eurostar train traveling from Paris to London. We left Paris and aboard the train at the Gare du Nord station. I suggest booking your ticket online months in advance from the traveling date as the rates can fluctuate.  The app is helpful to use as you can purchase tickets on your mobile device.  Arrive about 1 ½ hour before the scheduled time the train departs from the station.  Upon entering the station the Eurostar entrance is located upstairs as the company has own section that includes checking in with your ticket and passport in hand.  We did fill out the form provided to give to customs.  The form must be completed before you get to the customs desk.
