Once we went through customs, the securities check point was the last step before heading to board the train. The train is modern and sleek. Warning! Make sure you look on the side of the train to match the cabin you number on your ticket. The conductors of the train will be outside to assist you to the correct cabin number. We stepped up into the cabin and found our seats inside the train. I must say this train was clean and very simplistic. Once entering the train they’re sections to place the luggage and large items. The sliding doors will open to the seating area.  The train also has an executive suite and tickets can be purchased to seat in that section but will cost more money.  The standard areas seats can be reclined back and the feet can extend for more comfort. Seats range from two seats to four with a table in between. If you get two seats like we did the tray in front of you can be folded down. Storage is also available under the seat in front of you.  Outlets are available for both passengers and overhead storage is available as well. If your hungry don’t worry the train does have a café in the six cabin of the train. The speed is fast and the scenery is simply breath taking when you look outside. I suggest making sure you wear comfortable shoes when walking through the cabins as the train is moving a fast speeds it is best to great stance when moving. The café had a verity sandwiches, soups, snacks and an array of beverages to choice from. I’m not sure if it depends when your train is departing if the food options change. We both enjoyed the experienced and fell asleep heading to London. A two-hour ride on the Eurostar was smooth and we had no issues taking it back to Paris as well. The train does have televisions with informational detail about the country you are heading to as well advertisements for other trips you can on the Eurostar.
Great way to travel on a girls weekend. Loved that you can take your bottle of fizz and nibbles and just relax. Your At your destination before you know it!

despite the many many customer complaints and negative reviews don't hold your breath for improvements. Customers are not well regarded, their needs or value for money. Breakfast on Business Premier is poor and has not changed for many years now, no English papers or journals, no WIFI... the list is endless. Waiting areas at the stations are poorly served with shops, VIP lounges same repetitive food-fare, rat infestations continue...

1 - expensive - E220 Ashford to Paris2- unhelpful and expensive - wanted E200 to change my return time to an earlier train4 -totally confusion - would they stop or not at Ashford, my return station. Contradiction between their staff. 5 - no stop at Ashford - so then apologize with same apology 6 times in half an hour - maddening.6 - they changed trains and reallocated seat numbers - and completely screwed that up. Duplications all over the place.7 - outward wifi did not workAll in all a complete S show - after all these years you would think it would be better than this.

Got on at Ebbsfleet to Brugge, as usual it was on time, simple and dropped us right in the heart of Brussels which made it easy to get to Brugge and makes it our favourite way to get to the continent.
It was good and fast trip from London to Amsterdam. Staff on board was very nice and courteous. Service was good. Definitely worthy. Just make sure to buy your tickets early for a better fare.

If you need to travel last minute it is extremely expensive. If you want to change your ticket it is impossible. You just need to rebook your ticket at an enormous rate. 410 euro for a return ticket are not normal rates. Above all you are in a not so nice train, really not worth the money. TGV is much more luxurious and much cheaper.

This was a nice alternative way to travel from London to Paris.  We’d been on a number of long flights in the past 12 months and our family felt like trying something different.The tickets were a good price (at the time we booked it was almost the same price as a plane ticket).Check in was so easy.  Scanned our ticked, went through baggage check and customs without a fuss.Found our carriage easily, and then our seats.  The only interruption in this whole process up to this point was the fact that other passengers don’t know how to play Tetris.  What I mean is that people put their small bags down on the bottom of the luggage racks and don’t consider others with bigger bags.  But it’s ok.  My OCD kicked in and I rearranged the baggage in a more sensible order.Then the train wouldn’t start and we were delayed over an hour and had to swap trains.  But this wasn’t a big pro alien for us because of 2 reasons:1) it got to play luggage Tetris again2) we got a financial compensation refund credited back to us.As for the train journey, everything went smoothly from that point and we arrived without a fuss or bother.The kids enjoyed being able to move around a little more freely and not having to be restrained to their seats.  We took our own entertainment; colouring in, books, snack and iPads.Our return trip back went off even better because we were familiar with the system and how things worked.  We’d defiantly travel the Eurostar again.

The trip was very good. Everything is very organised at St Pancras station and there is a lot of food options. Staff were telling everyone to buy food and take it on if they wanted to. Great service and the train ran on time.

Compared to flying, the Eurostar is more convenient as you only need to arrive about an hour before departure and you can pass through French immigration at St. Pancras Station. However, there were many passengers at the end of the year, so it took a long time to go through the automatic ticket gates, security check, and immigration. Once you get on it, it's pretty comfortable. After driving through the English countryside for a while, we passed through a tunnel and headed into France. Announcements will be made before entering and after exiting the tunnel. When you arrive at Gare du Nord, you walk straight to the concourse, which gives you the strange feeling of suddenly being thrown into the hustle and bustle of Paris.

We opted to travel from Paris to London on New Years eve on the Eurostar.We paid a high price for the ticket as we booked in only days before we departed and it was New Year's eve our departure day.   My recommendation is, if you are considering travelling on the Eurostar service from Paris to London, book the tickets well in advance to get a cheaper deal.The service was good.  We arrived at the Gard de Nord station about 2 hours ahead of time,  this is highly recommended as checkin was a lengthy process of us.  You clear customs in both France and the UK in the same location, before boarding the train.Once on board, the trip is pleasant and fast compared to the other options such as bus or flying.   We recommend the Eurostar, but make sure you book well in advance to get a cheaper rate rather than waiting for any last minute deals.  The seats are comfortable, and we had a table.  Coffee and pastries etc. can be purchased and taken on board, plus there is also a buffet car on board.

For such an expensive form of transport this train was beyond shabby. Seats dirty with crumbs of bread and stuff over the seats and tray tables. The carriages and a terrible odour and frankly a rip off at £245.00. Better to fly at half the price. Customs is slow at Ashford international and they seem disorganised, especially at 6am in the morning. Journey back from Paris is better in terms of train, although customs is a mind numbing experience at almost an hour!! This is before Brexit!! No information as to what platform when you get through, just lots of people asking which gate do we need to board from. They need to up their game at such extortionate costs.

The Eurostar is a great way to travel from London to Paris. The train departs from London St Pancras and arrives at Paris Gare Du Nord. Standard Premier class provides comfortable seating options and meals are included.

The Eurostar offers good service to Paris at a price less than an airline ticket and at a trip duration not much different than airlines considering commute time and congestion at London area airports. St Pancras station is well organized to handle departures. The only slight negative is the need to lift a full-sized suitcase waist high to get it onto the conveyor for luggage screening at security. The processing through ticket control, passport control and security were well set up and the lines moved well. The train was comfortable. We departed and arrived on time. Overall it is a good service but you do have to watch out for last minute coach and seat changes as train configuration is a moving target (we had two such changes - one a week before and the other at the station).

We made the trip from Rotterdam. On the outward journey there was a transfer from the Tallys to the Eurostar in Brussels. It took some time to find where the Eurostar departed and the security check took some time. That is why it is advisable to go there immediately. The Eurostar also left a few minutes early. On the way back we left London at 6:15 PM and arrived at Rotterdam Central Station at 9:30 PM without a transfer. Fine! If you want to eat something at the station before leaving London, if it is very busy on the ground floor you can also go to the upper ring, where it is much quieter. If you want to buy an Oyster card for public transport in London on the outward journey, it is better not to do so on the Eurostar, because it is much more expensive there than at the machine in the metro station. On the Eurostar you do not get the normal Oyster card, but the visitors card, which also gives discounts on attractions. You will not get the purchase value back later, but you will get that of the normal card.
We went in the Standard Premium class and it is worth paying a little extra for comfort, a wonderful meal and VIP service. Super comfortable armchairs and very polite and helpful staff!
We had a lovely journey from London to Brussels on our way to Brugge. Unfortunately the train was 59 minutes late, but we were well looked after once we got on board. A nice way to travel

Took Eurostar from Paris to London. Very impressed all around. Painless way to travel between the two capitals. Just over two hours. We chose Premier Standard, which included a light snack and drinks (including wine). Comfortable seats with a wide table to spread out. And check-in / customs was a breeze. Very fast and efficient. And unlike airports, no need to check-in hours early.

Being a new route and my daughter not being a fan of flying we opted for the Eurostar. I had bought my tickets early so received a great price for the 6 people travelling. Overall we had a very positive experience, the staff were helpful, train was on time and food/drinks were available.Free WiFi was a bit hit and miss. Arriving into the center of Amsterdam also means there is no need to transfer from the airport and you are soon at your hotel.I would definitely recommend this mode of travel.

recently had to travel to eastern france for a meeting, as flights didn’t get us near to the venue we went by trainst pancras to paris was oka new train, even bearable in cattle class!the food car isn’t anything to write home about but when your travelling to paris you might as well wait for a meal when you arrivegenerally clean on board and the garde du nord station was excellentonly improvement would be food, and perhaps the trains would run as fast as the rer trains down to strasbourg

We traveled in standard first, Paris/London on Friday December 14, London/Paris on December 15. . Why are the wagons in this category the last in the train, which requires the entire train to be reassembled upon arrival at the station and therefore to arrive last at the taxi ranks? We can logically think that paying a more expensive ticket implies additional comfort. Does anyone have an answer? Furthermore, on the way out, our carriage was so uncomfortable that we felt all the bumps, to the point that the staff spontaneously offered us to change carriages. Apart from all this, the staff themselves are very friendly and helpful.

We we due to depart on the Eurostar from London on 11th December at about 9am which was nearly a hour leaving causing problems with our European connections. In addition the toilets in our carriage were faulty and very smelly!! On our return today (15th Dec) the train stopped at Ebbsfleet and it took the driver a hour to get it started again, apparently he had to reboot it (I guess it’s running on Windows95!). We were over a hour late back. This time also the toilets were faulty and in addition the power sockets were not working.This was our first and possibly last journey on Eurostar.
We traveled as a family with the children from London to Paris Everything was amazing and in perfect detail A train different from the others but with many pros A must if you get the chance to travel

I needed to catch an earlier train home to London, so spoke with the online team. They told me this was easy and to speak with the team at the station.  Did this and was charged €450 for two fresh tickets (assistant told me it was cheaper that getting a refund on my existing tickets!).What that pricing is about I have no idea, but it's a total rip off which I had to accept as I needed to return home urgently.Although there is wi-fi, it is so slow as to be totally pointless, so like everyone else I saw, we used 4gAs a train service I guess it's ok, I rarely use trains but the pricing leaves a bad taste, I will not be travelling on Eurostar ever again

We drove from Amsterdam to London with a direct connection. Just over 4 hours later in the heart of London. Great. Better than flying and more comfortable. You can get a small snack on the train along the way. Arrive wonderfully rested.

Took the Eurostar train from St Pancras to Paris.  Overall this was an excellent experience. I had a business premier ticket so had access to the lounge for both journeys so I had somewhere very comfortable to wait with food, drink, newspapers and so on.  Staff on and off the train were very pleasant and helpful - I needed wheelchair access and this was arranged very efficiently at both stations.  The only problem I had was at Gare du Nord.  Unlike St Pancras (and Brussels which I’ve used in the past) the Eurostar departure area wasn’t clearly signposted and I struggled to find it.  I’d recommend allowing plenty of time to check in for your return journey in case you have the same problem.

Very impressed with the ride from London to Paris.  We were on the 7pm train, so the entire trip was dark.  Being our first time... and the train so smooth... it was hard to tell when we were in the tunnel and NOT in the tunnel!  Service was impeccable and the First Class food service was surprisingly good.  Hot meal came with choice of wine and served on china with REAL silverware!!!  Table trays were roomy and lots of electrical connections.  WIFI was iffy, and eventually gave up on it.

As a disabled passenger, I was rather apprehensive about using Eurostar to Paris,especially at this busy time of the year. However, the help and kindness I received from staff was exceptional. The organisation for less mobile passengers was excellent,and seamless, they helped my daughter with luggage,and were never too busy,or made it seem like a chore. I would thoroughly recommend it. Thankyou.

This was our 1st trip.We went Economy (2 hours) from London to Brussels. Had no complaints apart from no service staff entered the area during the trip (not sure how it would go if travellers were less disciplined).Security is laxDoubt that it is wheelchair accessible without considerable help.

First time on Eurostar to Brussels. On the positive side the journey on the train was reasonable. But facilities at St Pancras miserable - a bit like the actual boarding gate at airport, very limited cafe facilities. The train itself was scruffy - seat covers dirty and badly worn (the return train much better),  Then no facilities for rubbish disposal - stupid!

Booked a Eurostar journey for my partner and I from London to Brussels in December 2018.At the last minute - when I checked our booking on-line - I was alerted to the fact that our preferred seating had been changed as the trains had been switched.No problem - same journey - different seats.However, on the return leg, the train had also been switched but this time the re-seating did not put us together. We are now 4 rows apart and facing opposite directions.So - after 11/2 hours on the 'on line chat' and 'customer service' phone line - this is what I know.Eurostar do not guarantee your preferred seating (I was aware of that). If I wanted to upgrade to the next level of service there was a charge of £460. If I wanted to transfer to another train the charge would be £65 - each.The advice I was given was to negotiate with other passengers once I was on the train to see if any were prepared to move seats.Before I get a barrage of 'Read the T's and C's' - what I would say is this. Despite it being written in the T's and C's - it does not make customers very happy if they are not treated reasonably. We booked seats together for a reason. Surely it is possible for Eurostar to use an algorithm that re-seats  passengers together - after all we can land a probe on Mars - surely we can seat two passengers on a train. (and before anyone says anything - I realise this makes no sense - but it just felt good to say it).So - my message to Eurostar - if you don't want people to talk about poor experiences - then treat your customers a little better!

Booked a train & hotel break to Bruges - train out was Standard Premium which was great, very comfortable, nice food and drinks - all good. Hotel excellent (Pand Hotel).Decided to upgrade from Standard to Standard Premium coming back and this is where the poor service really took over !If you book a hotel/train package YOU WONT be able to Manage your Booking via the app or online, so no way of upgrading there. - their live chat also wont be able to help - although they told me I could upgrade for £60 per person. I had to phone because of the agent they use for any hotel/train packages isnt them, it's farmed out somewhere so their systems cant process it!. When I phoned I was told it would be £300 + for an upgrade - NOT a new ticket, just the upgrade, same train etc. When I questioned that, they said it was a mistake and it was £200. Asked about the £60 I was told, they said that was wrong.Having bought the £200 upgrade I arrived at Brussels station to find upgrades advertised for just 45 euros !!!!!!!! Not impressed - tried to get some form of refund from their customer services - not interested, dont care, tough, move on.Lesson learnt, make sure you decide and book the correct ticket or failing that just upgrade at the station. Dont book the hotel & train package via Eurostar and they move you on to a 'hidden' agent/3rd party who doesn't link their systems well at all. It's no cheaper and makes any app or website booking management fail badly.All such a shame because the actual train journey etc was excellent ! Great trains, great stations, quick and clean. I was delighted with that, but the feeling of being ripped off and being taken advantage of is how Eurostar have made me feel. Noticed a few others feeling the eurostar poor service/rip off on here too - live and learn I guess!

We traveled from London to Brussels for the Christmas market, and Eurostar is the way forward. Check in was a bit manic as the Paris train was leaving 3 mins before. We had standard premier tickets which is worth doing. Comfy, plenty of room and a lite meal. 2 hrs later Brussels in comfort. The return was as enjoyable, the check in was easier as it was only the London train. I’ll be using this again.

Took the Eurostar to Brussels from St Pancras, firstly St Pancras is a superb station, very clean and easy to use, the train was very nice, smooth and the journey was fast. Coming back however they changed our seats and we were facing backwards which gives my wife travel sickness. Very annoying when you've picked forward facing seats. If you travel to Brussels on Sunday and plan on getting a taxi from the station, the traffic getting out is terrible due to a huge market which runs on Sundays. Over all the Eurostar was great though.
The  train was nice and  friendly and  the food was was OK. I we didn't enjoy the the food and the water in the toilet didn't work when you wash your heads
Upgraded seats - worth it as train is busyOnly one train out of Ashford 7.30amAnd one train back 5.30No other trains stop at AshfordFood not very good on the train

My husband and I took the Eurostar to and from Paris for the day while we were in London.  It was on time, comfortable, clean and a much more efficient way of travel. The French countryside was beautiful as we passed it in the morning. We were very happy with our mode of transportation. We recommend and would choose Eurostar again.

We were comfortable in our Eurostar train to Brussels, although there wasn't a lot of room between seats. When we arrived at Brussels Zuid, it would have been good to read in English that we could travel to Brussels Central, which was much closer to our hotel. We'll know next time!

What a treat to finish work in London and be able to go to Rotterdam via Eurostar rather than heading out to Heathrow / Amsterdam train to Rotterdam. Travelled in standard Premier and was delighted. Great service and the meal including wine with follow up drinks a few hours later was perfect. Seats well spaced and comfortable each with USB points. Have seen comments about the lines at St Pancras and would agree that really was the only major down point for the trip although at 5pm on a week day it still took no more than perhaps 30-40 minutes from check in  - security and passport control so not really a major problem but suspect could be improved significantly - space in the station may be major limiting factor.

We were booking same day roundtrip, London to Paris. Somehow the ticket for return ended up coming next day. To change it so we could return home, Eurostar charged us $400 to change the 2 tickets at the desk. They did this because they could. When we boarded the train, it was less than half full. In our moment of need, they were unwilling to yield and give us any help. Instead, they took advantage of us. We will never travel Eurostar again. With the security and check-in delays at the train station, flying is just as easy and costs less... (and quicker).
Last Friday returning from Germany I purchased a Stella Artois but served in a floppy plastic glass instead of a proper glass. Why was this please?

Very disappointed by the service: train more than 30 minutes late, wagons dating from the Stalinist era, without any comfort, no power outlet and completely blocked toilets. Better to choose the ferry or the plane or at least ask yourself the question.

I haven't booked a Eurostar train/hotel package for a while and won't be doing so again after my recent experience. In short, I thought that I'd booked a package to Lille last night only to be instructed by a Eurostar standard message to phone the service centre to confirm. The service centre knew nothing and advised me to clear my cookies and try again. I discovered that the price had been hiked by nearly £100 but went ahead anyhow only to receive the same message and the same advice from the service centre who also told me that there wasn't necessarily any price advantage to booking a package. So I booked the hotel with those nice people at Hotels.com for something closer to the original Eurostar price!

We really like to take this mode of travel rather than flying when we have time to do so. We see the landscapes and it’s very relaxing. The seats are comfortable and we can go to the café if we are a little hungry.

I've used the Eurostar twice to travel from Brussels to London and back.In comparison with the Belgium railroad company NMBS, there were hardly any delays and staff was professional and friendly. Ordering tickets on the official Eurostar website is easy and swift. Just make sure you compare prices, because these can differ quite a lot depending on the hour and season.The usual ritual of passing the security checkpoint and border control was a breeze. The only reason why the line is sometimes slower than it could be is due to travellers who do not follow the safety instructions and try to pass the metal detector wearing a metal belt or other stuff you're expected to put on the conveyor belt.The only reason why I can't give it 5-stars is because the WiFi-signal is quite undependable, so don't bother trying to watch a movie on the Eurostar multimedia platform, because the signal is interrupted several times. At best it's good for quickly checking your e-mails or FB, but the technology to watch streaming isn't quite there yet.

I recently travelled on Eurostar from Paris to London with my son. We arrived about an hour before the train was due to depart. There was  a huge number of people at the checkin and security area. Unfortunately no attempt was made to prioritise the passengers according to the train they were booked on. As a result we got through security to discover our train had left without us.There was a large group off other passengers in the same position.We were allocated a seat on a later train and did receive an upgrade. However I missed my train connection in London.

We booked a trip to London planning to end in and fly home from Paris! We thought the EuroStar would add to the fun of our journey and it did! We were right beside the bar car which was super convenient! We had seats facing each other and were able to enjoy the lovely countryside during our journey as well as play cards to make the time fly by! The trip was fast and comfortable! Our customs experience was speedy and seamless! All-in-all I would travel by EuroStar if making this crossing again in a heartbeat!!

I decided to opt for Premium Standard to Bruges recently, instead of standard  in the sale at a much reduced amount,  so that we could have a table for 2 and a much more comfortable journey, supposedly. Our seats were not as booked due to a change of carriage at the last minute so we were seated behind each other in single seats. I was most upset at the time. It was difficult getting the chef de train to see us as well. Eurostar Customer Relations will not give any compensation.  I will think twice about booking Premium next time and just book standard where, even with a train change, we would still be sitting together. It seems we lost out by booking the seats we did. What a difference on the return when we had the seats we had booked.

Love Eurostar.  This is the best way to get from London to Paris or Brussels.  I have even used to connect to Frankfurt on Thalys Train.  Once went from London to Brussels for a cheap lunch with my wife, we left after breakfast, has Croc Monsieur (Grilled Cheese Sandwich) in Brussels and were back in London for dinner.

We drove from Brussels to London and back. The check-in is stressful, but the journey is pleasant. For the return journey we also got the 3D glasses for our cell phone from the machine for 3 pounds, unfortunately the WiFy is not available on the entire return journey. So the fish couldn't be seen. Unfortunately, the request for a refund of the purchase price falls on deaf ears. Tip: better not buy it.

these are new trains but when travelling this weekend it was the first time in many a trip that i found it very un comfortable and the staff not very Professionalthe seating space is less than b4 and gives the feeling of being on  Ryan air very cramped and had to walk 2 train cars to find a toilet that was working and the air condition was stuck on freezing and several people asked for it to b turned off but the staff member just shrugged and repied we will soon b in brussels

Good way to travel and arrive directly into central London. Clean, comfortable, room for legs, friendly and caring staff. Departure in standard class first hearty breakfast on return unfortunately 2 hours late due to a problem with a freight train in the tunnel. Small meal served which was welcome as we arrived at 9:50 p.m. at Gare du Nord. More expensive than standard places but it's worth it.

Good connection to London. Smooth but there are differences when checking in. In Brussels I thought it was just a heap in a dark, unpleasant station, while in London it is a super beautiful and very organized station. The trains themselves are clean and equipped with all the needs, personally a lot better than Thalys.

you can't beat the train itself, and going from paris to london clearances were easy. however the queueing, immigration, and security clearances are ridiculously poorly organized and executed, for heavens sake. it was bedlam on a simple weekday morning. this is such a popular route, can't they dedicate and area and do this right? it is kind of an insult to pay pretty good money for this then be herded far worse than cattle in disorganized lines. please have an efficiency expert straighten this out.

We had traveled around France on SNCF TGV trains for a few weeks without a hitch  they were always on time and with out any dramas and with excellent wifi when the trains had it. Now for Eurostar, the train left on time and we were traveling Premiere class the wifi was erratic and the train not as smooth as the TGV's in France. In Premier class the ticket includes a meal  which is served at your seat a little like airline food only taster. Then came the announcement that the train was making an unscheduled stop at Callias due to technical difficulties, this where everything  turned into chaos. As the entire train travellers had already cleared imagraton in Paris, we technically were not in France so we weren't allowed into the station or back on the train and thus had to stand out on the platform in 7 degrees for approximately 2.5 hours with no toilet facilities.There was no communication from the Eurostar staff as to what's happening and when asked they said 'they don't know?' We were told that there was another train coming in half an hour which eventually did arrive to the applause of the passengers waiting, then one of the station staff told us that when the doors open to go board the second  train we were to a find a seat if there is one (this train was delayed leaving Paris by over 1/2 an hour so we found out) so all the passengers from our train ended up in second class and luggage everywhere.Now I do understand that things break down but 'what got up my nose'  was the lack of communication by the Eurostar staff to us,  the passengers  on the platform - in other words total organised chaos and a massive communication breakdown to customer service.

First time using Eurostar to get to Paris from London as hate airport check in and St Pancras is a very easy commute for me. Disorganised and security workers at St Pancras slow down the entire process. They need to be automated out asap to help improve the passenger experience otherwise it’s back to flying.

Comfy and fast train, which means efficient in time, truly efficient. Start from St Pancras in the centre of London, where passengers can use different type of public transport, such as tube and busses to come here, relax and spacious station at St Pancras, simple and very quick immigration process, and straightaway you are in the train and ready to go. Smooth riding, no bumpy along the way at all, then not too long you approaching the tunnel at the coast of Britain and then entering the tunnel, a 50.45 km tunnel below the Strait of Dover, and emerged at Europa land travelling to Paris, to the last station Gare du Nord, and no immigration and custom processes. The maximum train speed at that day is 316 km at Britain side and 304 km at Paris side. Comfy and relax seats, nice interior, really quiet, efficient, less than 3 hours London - Paris, and affordable tickets, brilliant. What else are you looking for.

This trip from London to Paris and back ranged from excellent to shocking.The outbound trip was fine - we sailed through St Pancras into the waiting area and onto the train. In Paris, you are in the heart of the city at the Gare du Nord, with access to the metro etc.The train itself was new, well appointed and nicely designed. The seats could have been more comfortable perhaps, but overall a good journey.The return trip could not have been more different. We arrived at the station to a massive queue at the bottom of the escalator up to the Eurostar area. There were then further queues at check-in and security. Organisation was non existent, queues huge, no messages were delivered, all trains were at least 45 minutes late - ours left 78 minutes late. The train manager let slip the reason for the delay - the clocks had changed the night before, and this had led to chaos and not enough staff! Unbelievable! The train itself was old and tired, which rounded off an awful return journey. I'm not sure which  journey is more representative - hopefully the outbound one!

The Eurostar was included as part of our holiday package to Brussels and we were incredibly impressed at the organisation that goes into the booking process and delivery of the service.Checking in was similar to the airport having to put your bags through the scanner then passport control, all of which were very quick and efficient.  Any problems were quickly addressed by staff.There was plenty of seating in the checkin area as well as a cafe, shop and toilets.Your carriage and seat are allocated and it was easy to find your way.  We were pleased with the size, comfort and leg room offered by the seats as well as a table.  Best of all a proper area to store cases during the journey.The journey itself was quick and smooth with plenty of information about the tunnel and speed of the train.Overall a very good experience and we look forward to traveling on the Eurostar again soon.

From check in to arrival in Europe, there is a professional approach, helpful staff make security more speedy than the airports, but still have to take off the belt!  The journey is faster than flying to Brussels and Paris, just over 2h15 in total from London to the continent. The trains left on time, were quiet and smooth, we had a table as there were 3 of us, so we could spread out, read a book, have a chat and recharge the phones! The crossing of the channel tunnel comes quickly, then comes Lille and soon afterwards we arrived in Brussels-Midi.On the return journey there can be extra stops at Ebbsfleet, the journey took an extra 10 minutes but was not delayed much.

The Eurostar is a good alternative to those that don’t want to fly from London to Paris, Bruxelles or Amsterdam. Be prepared to arrive 60 mins before departure time at St. Pancras Station because check-in ends 35 mins before the depature time and if you need to print your tickets and queue for check-in you will need the extra 25-30 mins.Journey itself is so-so, wifi was not working and windows were dirty. We have arrived on time in Paris but we did not feel that it was a special journey. I will think twice before booking again Eurostar.

It was surprisingly comfortable and didn't shake. However, it is not as good as Japan's Shinkansen. There seems to be a big delay at times, but I arrived almost on time, about a minute late. There are steps when getting on and off, which can be difficult if you have large luggage. Also, there is a long way to go to see the first car in a 20-car train.

Paid £75 extra for one way upgrade to Std. Premier. from Gare de Nord to London.What waste of money.  I was seated next to galley and there was constant banging as staff opened & closed fridges etc.  Also draught. Staff refused to close door between galley & carriage. Do cold I had to put on extra layers & wrap coat around me. Girls were only interested in business men, asking them if they would like drinks.  Women were ignored.  Definitely terrible service and not worth the money. Wine undrinkable.

The experience is first class its a pity the train exterior was very dirty. Hard to see the passing countryside. Would have liked to see a camera view from the drivers compartment to give a good insight at the speed of the train. The free wifi they offer doesn't work many were upset by that and if you plan to recharge equipment, you need a power plug as there is no USB connection.

I traveled with my 2 daughters on the Eurostar Train, from Paris to London. We bought the tickets almost 3 months in advance of the trip, through their own website, paying 56 euros each. We booked tickets on train 9063, car 10, standard class, choosing seats 14, 17 and 18 with a small table in between. We depart from the Gare du Nord station on October 2, 2017 at 9:13 p.m., and we arrive at 10:39 p.m. on the same day to St. Pancras station. Check-in is similar to that of an airport, with freeshop included. Getting on this train was quite an experience, super punctual, clean, comfortable, with exclusive space for suitcases, there is even space to store luggage between the seats. It also has a cafeteria where you can buy something to eat and drink. Its ride is so smooth that you don't realize the high speed at which it is traveling. The duration of the journey was about 2.30 hours, but the crossing through the Eurotunnel was so fast that before we realized it, we were already in England. Without a doubt, for this route it is a better option than an air trip.

I thought that the Shinkansen trains in Europe would not run on time, but surprisingly they did run on time. After passing through immigration at St. Pancras Station in London, I opened my ticket and boarded the train 15 minutes before departure. After departing on time, we entered the Eurotunnel in about 30 minutes and exited to France in 20 minutes. From there, we continued on through the plains until we saw a plane landing at Charles de Gaulle Airport, and then we arrived at the last stop, Gare du Nord. Although there was a slight delay, it was a comfortable journey of 2 hours and 20 minutes.

Well, that was fun! After a hectic day in London, it was time to head back to Amsterdam on the Eurostar.Check-in at St. Pancras International Terminal was busy and congested. There was a delay before going through French Immigration but once it started it was fast and easy. I recommend check-in minimum 90 minutes early and sit towards the gates entrances to immigration/customs to avoid getting behind travellers who need more time.Onboard the train, it was comfortable and quiet. Standard Class was full and I was happy I selected my window seat towards the back of the carriage - I got a little privacy and didn't have another passenger facing me.The bathroom facilities are good but locating it was a bit confusing and a slight step down. Be prepared - some travellers will be lugging lots of big suitcases - I recommend trying to pack light!I booked two months in advance and got an amazing rate! If your dates are flexible, you can find a very good deal on this route (going to Paris is generally more expensive because of demand). Riding under the English Channel after crossing on the Channel early on the Stena Ferry was a memorable adventure.

I have travelled a lot and generally put bad experiences to isolated incidents, but Eurostar just can't seem to stop giving bad experiences. From their shockingly bad service (with the exception of a few), this is probably the worst form of travel I have ever had. During the hottest summer this year, on one trip I was refused ice for my drink and the reason "No sir, we need to keep that for those who order alcohol". Another incident there was a 3hr delay, in the same summer, with no explanation other than "Sir, it's delayed, what do you want me to do?". During this 3hr delay, no refreshments, nowhere to sit, because you were not allowed in the waiting area and to top it off, I was provided with a £20 refund on the ticket. UK you would be entitled to the full amount. Most recently, I had an issue with booking a return ticket. Arriving in Paris at 9:20am with the return on the same day at 10am. In other words I people travel 2hrs 30mins from London on a train for a visit to Paris for to wait for 30mins and head back. Regardless of whether this was human or computer error, you would think common sense would prevail.....not with this idiotic company. "Buy a new ticket it's full price last minute £240". What is worse, you don't get any response from their customer service, try email, tweet, phone (if you can find one), mail (if you can find one), pigeon, smoke signals. It seems that Eurostar doesn't need to adhere to any laws and are run by morons which are approved by even bigger morons. So much for EU law, I've almost converted to being glad to be leaving the EU!!STAY AWAY. FLYING ACTUALLY TAKES ABOUT THE SAME TIME AND IT'S SOOOOO MUCH CHEAPER. I'm certainly done with this pathetic excuse for service company. I'd like to apologies to the Airline industry that I left you and would graciously appreciate if you could welcome me back!!

First time to ride the fastest train in Europe. If your ticket says 1:15 be there at 1:15, you won’t be allowed to check in earlier. Staff is friendly, check in & passport control is smoothly. There are shops & cafes inside to purchase souvenirs & food. Our seats were comfortable and you can buy coffe & sandwiches in the train cafe. The train is fast but you hardly feel it, we enjoyed our ride from & to London to Paris
Title says it all. Best part is no luggage fees and any other extra fees like the airlines. Although around 2 hours plus travel it was very convinient.

Our first time, and definitely not the last. don't know why we have been flying budget airlines on short hops to Europe all these years. Easy  customs, no airport shuttles, short queues, and dropped in the heart of Paris.

Three hours late. A huge line formed, and we were not given any information beyond ``technical trouble'' and ``30 minutes late,'' and we were forced to stand in the queue. Fortunately, my route departed, but the flight before and after it seemed to have been canceled, and I couldn't even get to the ticket office for a replacement (I didn't receive any notification that my route could be canceled, so it may have been bad luck for passengers who wanted to switch to a flight). The official page did not update the information properly, and sometimes the delayed route was supposed to have departed. The situation with so many customers standing around on the 1st and 2nd floors was a hell of a scene (Twitter was pretty active and people were posting photos).According to the people around me in line, it wasn't usually this bad even if there was a delay (in fact, when I went there too, the delay was only about 15 minutes at most). However, the response was so bad that I think it should be recognized as a possible risk.

I paid for a Business seat, but due to technical issues the train from London was delayed  then replaced and we ended up in a lower cabin class.  The train captain assured us that we'd be compensated, but I subsequently needed to contact customer services for them to start looking into this (they needed a picture of the ticket to start investigating, so keep that if any issues).  They then only offered me a percentage of the original ticket cost, rather than the difference in classes - they've continued to quote policy, rather than understanding of why this leaves me out of pocket.  To make things worse, they insisted they could only offer a voucher rather than a refund, which isn't helpful as I'm in HK and so may not travel with them again in the next year.  Boarding issues haven't improved since we last travelled Eurostar - especially disappointing at the supposedly purpose-built St Pancras, with the whole train squeezed onto two escalators.

Took the train from St Pancras to Gare de Nord, Paris. A great experience, beats taking the plane hands down and only takes 2hrs 15mins. Comfortable and convenient service. Get to St Pancras early and look around the revamped area behind Kings Cross Station, Granary Square and the canal.

We think it is a perfect and relaxed way of transport. Certainly better than by plane. You get on at Amsterdam or Rotterdam and before you know it you are in the heart of London. Just be careful when you buy something, don't pay with euros, they have a very bad exchange rate, pay with pounds.

Booked Eurostar to see family in Amsterdam.  I had business premier ticket.  To say it was great would be an understatement.  We left London at the very minute we were scheduled to leave.  The staff were friendly and attentive.  I had breakfast, which was small but very good.  The staff checked with me many times.  The train was smooth and not track noise at all.  We arrived into Amsterdam 2-3 minutes ahead of schedule.  I wouold take this again in a heartbeat.

First trip - got reassigned seats from a table for 4 to individual seats with no view - just watch out - my 1st french experience  for 30 years and its a bad one.  Thanks for a bad intro to europe - hope tbe italians have more respect.Wont be using this service again.

We did London to Bruges via Brussels Midi. The waiting area at both ends can be a bit of a crowded scrum and quite tatty but we went Premier and the carriages were roomy and quiet. The lunch food on the way back was much better than the breakfast on the way out but the service efficient and friendly. The at seat plugs were a benefit. If you are connecting back from other trains at Brussels, note the dual language means that Brussels Midi (French) is also called Brussels Zuid (South Flemish). Can be confusing! Also if going to Bruges, watch which train you get on. The way out was very crowded old rolling stock. Wait until the next train in ten minutes which is a much better double decker and a totally different experience.

Turned up to Paris station on time for check in and waited in a queue. Was getting close to the half hour check in time so informed staff of this and were told there is plenty of time to get us through so to wait in the queue.Got to the front and were then informed we were 10 mins too late ! made to buy another ticket for a later train.When complained about this the email response was to point out terms which state they have to charge for a new ticket !No concern over the rudeness of their staff, no concern over the fact they have no signage in Paris as to where they are located.AVOID USING IF POSSIBLE ! SERVICE IS A DISGRACE AND STAFF CLEARLY DONT WANT TO WORK HERE, HENCE WHY THEY ARE SO RUDE !

We recently took the Eurostar train from London to Paris.  This was a nice change of pace from flying.  The passport check and security check at the St Pancras rail station was very quick and effortless.  Train was very comfortable and smooth. I would highly recommend traveling to Paris this way.

The direct trains on the way to Amsterdam are brilliant. You clear all customs at St Pancras and get straight off the train at the other end.  On the way back is a little more complicated as you get on a high speed train at Amsterdam then change to the Eurostar at Brussels where you go through customs. There is another passport control at st Pancras. The trains were all comfortable and the checks all seemed to work quite smoothly. The Wi-fi is a bit hit and miss though.  I would definitely use it again.

We bought our eurostar ticket from home a couple months before the trip. The seats were comfortable and it was all very organized. We felt like the price was fair. But, We were riding on the train seated backwards. I don’t know how it happened  or how we could’ve got a seat facing in the proper direction. Anyway, if anyone is interested it might be a good thing to search before buying a ticket. I did buy the cheapest ticket so maybe that is why.

At least over 90% of the time the WiFi doesn’t work. The seats are cramped and rock hard. If you are traveling between Paris and London don’t get their hotel package deals. The hotels they will put you in are horrible. You can stay at those hotels yourself for a lot less. Just get the cheapest possible train tickets. Good luck.

From Paris, Lille or Brussel, this is the best way to reach London. From centre to centre, not too much time to waste before travel. True, it is not cheaper compared to the plane, but it can be faster in terms of total duration of the trip. Comfort ok, very poor wifi and enterntaiment.

We recently visited Europe and used a few trains along.  We travelled from London to Paris via Eurostar.  The boarding process T St Pancras was quick and efficient however an earlier train to Brussels was running late resulting on an overcrowded waiting area with no available seats.The train was comfortable however the WIFI did not work at all.Overall a good service.

Annoyed by the air transport, I chose to take a Eurostar train from London to Paris (return).Two hours is not bad and all this space and comfort compared to the plane . . . How wrong I was. The train is more expensive than the airplane. It's been delayed on both legs by 45 and 17 minutes, respectively. From London to Paris the wifi did not work for technical fault. On the way back it did work but - contrary to what the in-train leaflet says - most of the time one gets the speeds that are well beyond anything usable. Very poor mobile signal coverage of most of the rural landscape in France, it is fair to say this route is connection-free. In summary, the train connection between London and Paris (or Brussels) has got all the chances to be really good. But the excessive price, no punctuality and low level of connectivity make it unattractive. Next time, I will fly again.

We took the Eurostar to Paris from London. We were told that our golf clubs must be sent via registered luggage by EuroDespatch. That costed 30 Euro. When we arrived at Gare du Nord we were told the golf clubs needed to be picked up from the EuroDespatch counterpart in Paris. You would guess that it would be somewhere with a clear sign like Oversized Luggage in airports. Sorry no. That was too easy for visitors to Paris. I walked from the concourse back along the platform, past some security offices behind closed doors, dodging luggage trolleys being pulled by mini trucks along a narrow lane of no more than 3 metres wide. The collection point was in another building further and hidden behind trolleys and carts. Then I have to pull the bags back to the concourse. Another 500 metres or so. So golfers who are travelling on Eurostar. Beware.

The train to Paris on 9/27 was great and it went very fast. The ride was very enjoyable except the line for the cafe was very long. Our seats in standard were pretty comfortable and the Odyssey game on my phone was cool. The ride on the way back to London was a little uncomfortable as the temperature was very cold.

I could not make my train to Bruges on Monday because I needed urgent surgery. Customer services refused to give me any compensation/refund. My only option was to transfer my train tickets to a different date and charge me an extortionate amount of money to do so. I will never be booking with Eurostar again after loosing £200 worth of tickets.

Clean trains, on time, smiling staff. The check on is a little heavy at first. Several barriers to show passports, x-rays to pass... In short. Once past that, we are well settled!! And what's more, we arrive directly in London, it's great!

The smell of the filthy toilets is so disgusting and pungent it is notable throughout the seating area. My fourth return trip on the Eurostar to Paris and the same problem every time even in the business coach. Surely this is not a difficult problem to fix. It’s a shame because the service is efficient.

I purchased standard premiere seating, was downgraded to standard seating without prior notice and Eurostar refuse to refund stating they are within their rights to do this.I wonder how many times they charge customers for upgraded seating, don't provide and refuse to refund? Premiere seating was full so implies they sold the seats at a higher rate twice.

What a great experience was ride this fast train. We go to St Pancras station, it was amazingly clean with many shops and restaurants. An hour before the schedule departure of our train we went to the appropriate platform and pass the security and customs. The checks were orderly and quick, then we reach the waiting area for our platform. Comfortable seated we await to have access. With British punctuality the Platform doors open and we could access the train.The coaches were spotless clean and very comfortable, - obviously we depart right on time.Once in movement we experience a very steady and quiet ride. The electronic sign inside was continuously showing the speed, - incredible 347 Km/h (210 mph). This causes the trip duration to be only 2 hr 10 min. After a while the lunch was served. It was very good. We arrive to Paris (Gare du Nord) on time. It was a great experience and, in this case, faster than a flight.

I am a student of military matters (mainly naval) and a railway enthusiast, remembering that railways were invented by the British. Ever since the Channel Tunnel was built and turned over to traffic, I've always wanted to travel from London to Paris by train. We bought the tickets months ago and, on 25/08/2018, my wife, daughter and I boarded train number 9036 at 15:31 at the beautiful St. Pancras Station, in London. The train left at the scheduled time and, precisely 2:16 hours later, arrived at Gare du Nord, in Paris, also on time. The journey was very peaceful, you couldn't hear people talking loudly (great for seeing the beautiful British and French countryside, or resting), the train in fact barely rocks and the Eurostar services are excellent. It was very worth it. I want to repeat the trip in the future, it really is another world.

Whatever mode of international travel you pick, you can’t get away from queuing somewhere and Eurostar is no exception. Though the staff are very helpful, directing you where to go.The train itself left on time and we quickly sped our way to Ebbsfleet and then on to Paris with no fuss. Being served our continental breakfast without issue in Standard Premiere class. Would use Eurostar  again for over flying or ferry if possible.

Eurostar trains are a great way to travel to the continent with little fuss, but the wi-fi network is non existent. So slow it’s not worth even trying. Still, nice to see the world go by and get a glimpse of the rural areas you don’t normally visit.

The new trains have carriages with far too many seats, which makes for a very cramped journey.  When running to time this is OK but the toilets were out of order (this seems to be very common) and it left over an hour late, which caused a number of people to abandon their journey and get off before the train left.  There was no indication that the delay would be that long.  When the journey finally started, the very small children who by that time had already been couped up for too long in a hot, small space understandably went into meltdown and a poor elderly passenger vomited over themselves due to the high vibrations, possibly exacerbated by the new rigid seats and not helped by the toilets being closed as well as the by now humid, smelly carriage.  All in, the journey was very delayed, the carriage stunk of vomit and there was ample screaming for what is marketed as a business service.  Onboard there was an announcement that compensation would be made, when requested later, it was refused as though it left very late, several minutes were made up so that the journey was just under an hour late by a few seconds.  The general tone from Eurostar is officious and unhelpful, which is surprising as the staff generally seem keen and open.

My beautiful wife and I thoroughly enjoyed and l traveled to Paris on this fast and efficient train. Very smooth and comfortable.Beats flying and a lot more cost effective.Service was good along with available snacks you can purchase.No disappointments here.Good value for your money spent.

As a traveller from Australia I couldn't book far ahead due to alleged track works scheduled for the time of my travel, so not only missed cheaper early-bird fares, but had to book separate single journeys (rather than a return) which cost more. It is ridiculously expensive, and as we wanted to alight at Ebbsfleet, choice of trains was limited and no cheaper despite not going the full distance. The on-line chat facility was useless (totally unable to tell when tickets would be available) telling me to subscribe to their newsletter. This gave no information either and I have since had great difficulty to "unsubscribe."The trains themselves are uncomfortable and unsafe, i.e. seats are plasticky, the internet doesn't work, the information TV's gave NO information but just run self-promotion all the time, there are no conductors passing through the carriages to ask questions of, - and unsafe due to not nearly sufficient places for suitcases. On our journey, many 25kg suitcases had to be hauled up onto overhead luggage racks (built for small cases) but appallingly many were also in the aisles (no where else to put them) making even trips to the refreshment car hazardous.Boarding the train in London was a manic and crushing experience, but even worse at Gare du Nord! No organisation, people pushing in, a creepy and horrid station full of touts and drunkards that security seemed uninterested in moving on.So Eurostar may be a convenient city to city option, but it needs to lift its game hugely - conductors moving through the train would be a good starting point, and please clean up Paris station. In its present state we would not use it again even though other transport options between London and Paris are less convenient.

I travelled by Eurostar to lille . I had brought the ticket at the last minute so was prepared for the worse. I was in carriage 001 which turned out to be right at the end . However once I got on board I was surprised at how spacious it was particularly when I was then offered breakfast . I walked down the carriages to my friends and then realised I was in premier class ....what a difference ...I had got a last minute cheap city break . If you can afford it then pay for it  ...also look at weekend breaks ...I used lastminute.com. One gripe ...if I had paid the full amount for that ticket I would not be pleased with the location of the carriage . It should be at the front of the train. On my return the train was late and I did not have time to get down there so had to walk through all the carriages plus the kitchen ! Eurostar get it right for business travellers

Having used Eurostar when it first began many years ago, I recall a sleek pleasant experience in above average trains..whisking you under the sea to the continent with excellent standards of catering and plush seatsVery disappointed to see what this service has become.Scruffy dated TINY seating, almost non existent wi-fi, being herded like sheep when it’s time to board with no organisation either end The usual security queues snaking for miles Just awful. On the other hand, the connecting Belgian train between Brussels and Bruges was great. Huge comfortable seats, clean plentiful toilet facilities - most impressive.

The London traffic was bad and the taxi driver assured us we would have plenty of time to make the train to Paris as it was very simple and easy to check in. At the main gate the staff were only letting through people for the next 2 trains. The queues for check in and passport control were a bit haphazard but moved reasonably quickly and we flew through the French passport control. As we weren't allowed to go up to the platform there was a mass of people in a rather confined area (hate to think what would happen in an emergency) but power and USB ports were available. Once the gates were opened it was a total bun fight to get up to the platform. Boarding the train was simple and efficient and the staff helpful. The train was clean, seats ok and they did have power and USB connections.Once we were on our way we were given "breakfast" which was cheap and the coffee (how can they call it that) was disgusting. We sped through the countryside at 300km and were in France in no time at all. Pretty much the whole way the WiFi was none existent but as the trip was so quick it didn't seem to matter to me but for others was causing great disruption. We were late into Paris (15min) due to congestion but received many apologies. Again the bun fight to disembark and get off the platform but once in the taxi queue it moved rather efficiently. Would do it again at the drop of a hat and if you can watch out for the special deals.

I am a former frequent traveler on Eurostar and am just completing a round trip journey from Paris to London in Standard Premiere. “New” Eurostar coaches look like the Paris RER or local British Rail trains: hard seats everything in plastic. The so called Wifi, when available, isn’t even strong enough to run internet on an iPad or iPhone. Really? The Saint Pancras Station personnel at the Lounge refused me entry with two different American Express Platinum cards. Since when is  place of issue a criterion? I have a French Card, not good enough. Neither was my US issued Platinum. And did it really require a wall of five scowling employees to convince me? Guess I look like a criminal? One crew member on board was exasperated every time I got up looking for the WC or a trash bin and ended up near the galley. I hadn’t realised we were in an airplane, required to stay seated? Perhaps an airline industry reject thinking he was on a fantasy flight?  As I write, the trip back is going to take four hours due to repairs on the TGV tracks in France. Sorry, then why did my ticket still cost more than €450? Was it for the abysmal cold quiche platter? It’s become a cattle class affair all around. The security wait at Saint Pancras station was enough to dissuade me already. Disorganized, people blatantly jumping the queue without regard for anyone else and zero enforcement of rules (except for the Lounge of course). I’ll fly next time for sure. Eurostar is selling an overpriced dream that has long ago ceased to exist. I’ve been taking it for over 20 years so am well placed to say it. Shameful, sad but true.
It was a real treat to ride Eurostar from London to Paris.  The train was on time, comfortable and clean.  I will chose this mode of transport again.

Travelling between London and Paris can be a pain if you travel by one of the budget airlines and are not an EU citizen. We walked on to the train with a minimum of fuss and it was close to the city. The train was clean and crowded. Our seats were a lot more spacious than flying. Getting off in Paris at Gar de Nord was easy and just near our hotel. Don't buy food or drink on the train as the prices are very high. It was a pleasant journey though the countryside. There is no need to go first class for such a short journey.

Used Eurostar for the first time in quite a few years, and for the very first time from St. Pancras, for a trip to Brussels. At 0710 the queue for check-in started halfway down the main concourse, a roped area, and huge queue of people, being the only clue. No signage. Clueless, unhelpful Eurostar staff wander around with pieces of paper held in the air. No idea why. People duck under the rope, go straight to the front, push in and generally queue jump. No one from Eurostar intervenes. It took 45 minutes for me to get through check-in, security and passport control. Way too long, makes airport security seem fast and luxurious. The departure lounge is cramped and over-crowded. Once on board, I travelled Standard Premier, the staff were fantastic, the train comfortable, clean and well-appointed, the service excellent with a basic breakfast, juice and coffee FOC. On my return trip, check-in, security and passport control took five minutes, the lounge was much more comfortable although six out of seven urinals in the gent’s loo were out of order. The same great service from pleasant staff, once on board, but the train was ancient, the Standard Premier carriage and seats being completely different to my outbound train and no where near as good. Surprised at this difference in quality. All in all, a great train journey but a dire customer experience. Avoid St. Pancras and travel from Ebbsfleet or Ashford.

My review is not so much about the Eurostar journey - after all, it’s just a train, admittedly one that gets you from A to B very, very quickly, but about the pre-journey experience. I don’t know if there’s a railway equivalent of the word ‘airside’, but the Eurostar version at St. Pancras and, especially at Brussels Zuid leave a lot to be desired (I can’t comment on Paris). Bearing in mind each Eurostar train can carry around 750 passengers the facilities are just not up to catering for that number of passengers compared to airports. At St. Pancras there could be a train leaving every 30 minutes at busy times and basically the departure area is just too small to cope. When I was there this week at 5pm I should think there must have been well over 1000 passengers in the (single) departure area. There are enough seats but it pretty crowded. There is one shop selling booze and souvenirs, and a bar. Regarding the bar I have one comment on the draught beer they have on offer. German, Belgian and Irish. Considering there are around 1,200 breweries in the UK this is nothing short of a scandal. Of course the beer is supplied by mega multinationals who only care about profit and not quality, as do the people who run such bars. Moving on to Brussels the departure lounge there is simply abysmal. As there is only one train departing there is enough seating but only a small cafe and no shop. Want to charge up a mobile device? Forget it - there are no sockets on the lounge, just a few by the cafe. This is simply outrageous in 2018!The toilet facilities are worth a mention as the day I was there six of the seven urinals were broken and covered with plastic bags. Basically airports have got is right with plenty of space and great facilities for the departing passenger. Eurostar passengers on the other hand, are treated like cattle.

This is my preferred way to go to London: -no airport type hassle, - you arrive to London- St Pancras station is a good location for further commute.From one hand, if you are early enough, you can get the tickets for quite a reasonable price.From another hand, if you want to go in a bit more “exclusive” way, you have a choice to get a 1st class ticket. The lounge in Brussels Midi is quite ok. Also the lounge in London is a convenient location to pass your time in case if you have to wait for the train to leave.

We didn't think it was a cheap travel for the 2 and so hours.  We went from London to Paris and then did the return trip some days later.It is quick travel.  Fairly clean on board and the food and refreshments are reasonably priced.I guess when you look at all the costs in running such a train i can understand thete is a profit to be made.Take the teain for sure.

The most appauling customer service I've ever eperienced in my life. I'll never travel with EuroStar again. I'd rather walk!!A few weeks ago I suffered a *SIX AND A HALF HOUR DELAY* with EuroStar. Arriving into London at ***03:30am***. The conditions were awful. It was hot and uncomfortable.Customer service at the time was shocking. I only saw the Train Manager once during his single walk through the carriages, and he could bearly take the time to speak to me. What did we get during the ordeal? A *CUP* of water (not even a bottle) if we walked to the cafe cart ourselves, and a fun-size twix each!That was shocking enough, but the customer service afterwards was even more appauling. So there's a sliding scale for compensation in this type of case right? Between an hour and two+ delay. But when something goes catastrophically wrong do you think the company should maybe take that into consideration? A six and a half hour delay is exceptional and something deserving of a special handling. EuroStar don't seem to think so.I had to contact EuroStar multiple times to get my claim paid out as well. They only paid the percentage of the tickets originally, even though they had promised to refund our taxis.The biggest insult...get this... Whilst I put my Mum into a taxi, I took the night tube home. The train manager even suggested we do this. I thought I'd be considerate and do it, since I could get home that way. It felt like travelling home with zoo animals, it was horrendous. So, I don't get indoors til gone 5am right. EuroStar refuse to pay my *****£2.80***** tube fare!! WTF?!!Compassion?Customer Service?Alien terms to these corporate jobsworthsThis is an excetional circumstance, I get that. For that exact reason alone EuroStar should be grovelling, saying 'usually we're really good, here, let me do anything to prove to you that when things go catastrophically wrong you can count on us. Please ride with us again'.This type of handling would be a stroke of genius, promoting word of mouth recommendations of admiration that whilst it was an ordeal, they make sure you're sorted if something really off the scale from a nomal delay happens.Instead, they're quoting rules of carriage to me and making me waste my time, and producing the most annoyed and frustrated customer ever.I literally tell anyone and everyone about how crap the trip was, how bad the service has been, and go into every single detail and communication I've had; there's not been a single person not shocked and appauled. I don't think I'm the only person that'll be put off ever using EuroStar after hearing my story.For a company that spends millions of pounds on advertising, they can't even spare £2.80 of good-will for someone that's been so put out.You couldn't pay me to go on EuroStar again. They don't deserve my money!

When it was decided that I would travel to France on the Eurostar it was no big deal but then when I heard the train passes under the English Channel then I was really excited.  When we arrived at St. Pancras Train Station we made our way to the Eurostar line.  We were early so we had the wait for the passengers with earlier tickets to get on.When it was time for us, we had to scan our boarding passes to enter the area for passport control.  My pass was not scanning but it was easily rectified by a staff member.  Then we had to go through airport type security - sending bags and jackets through scanner, etc. This process was quick.  Then we had to have our passports checked by the French border police.  Then sit and wait for the train.The train got delayed for about ten minutes but then we were called.  You have to take the "conveyor belt" up the to ramp then go to your respective coach.  Once inside there are spaces available for your luggage.  Then we were on our way.We travelled at night so didn't see much of the landscape.  During the ride we were given an update on the speed of the train, arrival time at Gare du Nord, progress of the journey and depth below the sea.  Once we arrived we exited the train and made a long trek to meet our cab.The experience was okay but not that spectacular.  The seats were comfortable enough and thankfully there were no emergencies.  It is a great option for travel between London and Paris.

We naively thought that taking the train to Paris from London would be a much nicer experience than flying. Wrong!The queues were worse than an airport and our departure was delayed by an hour with constant mis-information given over the PA system on the length of the delay by a very unsympathetic announcer who would be more suitable working in a Gulag!This will be the first and last time that Eurostar get my money!

Plenty of room, enough area to store carry on's and plenty of sights to see. This is a great way to get to Paris from London! It really is less time than going to airport, having to wait  a couple of hours before getting on the plane then the trip itself. The train was clean, quiet, and had a snack and sandwich shop aboard. I think it was well worth the money.

Have frequently used Eurostar to travel to Brussels and Paris. This review was a return trip to Brussels.Travelled in business class. Comfy seats and plenty of space if you have a table for 4. Charging points for laptop and phone.Food is good and staff make sure you are offered plenty of drinks. Champagne as an aperitif is a must.

It was a pleasant train ride even though you are under the English channel. The seating was comfortable, there are cafeterias on the train offering great snacks and drinks. Train speeds in the UK and EU are somewhat faster than in Aussie.

The trains are old and some of the seats are completely stained. The check-in was catastrophic, especially in London. Two trains ran in quick succession. The baggage check was still relatively quick - the staff seemed annoyed, stressed and unfriendly. The customs check went incredibly wrong - only one counter was manned per country - which of course meant that things moved in slow motion. At least the Eurostar was waiting - otherwise dozens of people would have missed the train. The friendliness of the staff on the train is very positive. We were late and the train boss took a long time to find a solution with us that worked really well. The food was also good and very friendly (1st class)
hard to cope with the stress of travelling to paris but in the ame time, it is better than plane.customer service is ok but not so flexible.eurostar experience could be improved

We have just made our first trip on Eurostar and will definitely be using it again.My husband is in a wheelchair so we were unsure of how it would go but from the moment you arrive you are guided through security, customs and to the lift you need to use by friendly helpful staff.When you get to the train the ramp is there waiting. Once on board unlike most trains here it is easy to get to your seat and luggage is not allowed to be left in the aisles.Depending on what time of day you travel you get food and drinks bought to you which was very nice.We seemed to arrive in Brussels in no time attall.I would highly recommend this to everyone who doesn't want to fly or drive

My wife and I are lucky to travel a lot and with that comes a lot of airports, something which I usually dread due to the time spent queuing. So when we take a trip on the Eurostar we are always impressed with how smooth and efficient everything is. We have used Eurostar 3 times so far, twice from St Pancras and the last time from Ebbsfleet. St Pancras was good but due to living outside of London it’s a mission getting there and expensive (train prices). Ebbsfleet was amazing! Easy to get to off the M25 and parking was so simple. We paid for parking on the internet months ago, £17.40 for 3days in car park D, when we drove up to the gates it opened and recognized our plate. If you have no walking difficulties then don’t pay for any of the other car parks, D is the farthest away but still less than 10mins. The bit we love the most about Eurostar is the checkin, security and passport control. It literally takes longer to take my belt off to go through the scanner than to do all of those things. So much quicker and more efficient than airports. The sitting in economy on the trains is great, good amount of leg room and descent size table trays. You load your own luggage on to the racks and keep you’re handheld stuff with you. Another good point is that due to it being a train and not a plane, you can bring food and drink in from outside the station, a money saver. If you’ve never been with Eurostar definitely give it a go, it’s expensive but once you’ve done it you’ll go back.

Dreadful experience. We booked a train from Ashford to Paris which was cancelled and Eurostar never informed us. Our ticket was still downloadable in the morning for a train which no longer existed that day! All our travel plans were disrupted, we'd wasted money on a hotel for the previous night in Ashford, and by the time we got to Paris we were frustrated and exhausted. And Eurostar are refusing to take responsibility or even consider any level of compensation or gesture of goodwill. Shocking customer service. Never again. I'd rather fly.

Easy to use to get to Paris.  Reasonable prices and no hassles like when traveling through an airport.  You do need to get there early enough to queue for security, but it's nothing as crazy as an airport.  Scenic ride and a nice meal served on board.

After being delayed 3 hours on a previous train from Milan, my wife and two 13 year old children arrived at the Eurostar booking office. Because we had valid tickets we were expecting to simply travel on a later train, but oh no. At first we were informed that it would cost 49€ each to purchase new tickets, but then they realised we were greater than 2 hours delayed so we would have to pay even more 236€ EACH!!!!!!I have no idea where the logic is that says because you have been delayed longer than someone else you then have to pay more for your ticket!!!!! To add insult to injury we also had to pay 236€ for our two 13 year old passenger's as they told us they had no children's seats left, which is strange because I had never noticed before that Eurostar had special children's seats. How does a train with available seats run out of children's seats!!!!! I have traveled for many years on Eurostar but not any more, back to flying for me I'm afraid.

Recently traveled via Eurostar from London to Paris. Train was about 15 minutes late, not a big deal. Seat was comfortable, trip was uneventful. Easy way to travel, but a little pricier than I was expecting. Probably would have been cheaper if it was booked far in advance. Overall a good experience.

Worst experience ever if you have the misfortune of having to deal with the call centre staff.  They do not listen to you, their communication skills when handling a complaint is inept.  They display disinterest and demonstrate continual lack of care.  They apparently have no knowledge on how to contact Eurostar office in another country saying they dont have their phone number or any contact details to be able to communicate to them.  Due to French rail strike, which also impacted Eurostar trains being cancelled (still dont know why), we had no option other than abort our French travel plans and transfer our ticket Paris to London via Eurostar to an earlier day.  An hour on the phone to the call centre staff who had no expertise on how to help us was the first episode of atrocious customer service.  The only thing they appeared to be good at was trying to fob you off saying "it should be running, you should be able to get your ticket" after following their advice that only way to change ticket over was online assuring us that the train we were transferring to was definitely still running.  Upon transferring over it stated that our train was cancelled and therefore we had effectively NO ticket after just paying an opportunistic inflated transfer cost of over 250 pounds.  Over an hour on chat line which was useless and couldnt offer any assistance.  Would not arrange for a callback next day.  Asked to escalate and they wouldnt.  Closed then for the night.
