Next day another hour on phone.  Eurostar's website down, app down, no way to obtain ticket which was apparently, according to the untrustworthy staff, still running despite their website saying the contrary.  Staff said they have no contact information for them to consult Amsterdam Eurostar office to see if we could print off tickets there.  Even Team Leader beheld no customer service skills or mannerism in customer's concerns.  If you were travelling on the day of the strike on Eurostar you did not have to pay exhorbitant transfer costs however if you were still effected, in same way, as we were and had to cancel our entire French travel leg of the trip, because we were travelling a day outside the strike we were stung for Eurostar's selfish opportunistic unjustified costs.  They were very defensive and unapologetic for the poor experience and for their website and app down, nor were they even aware of it at first and negleted to pass on the information as the next morning they still were not aware it had gone down previous evening and was still down.  They ignored any inconvenience that we were enduring. We had already paid for our initial ticket but forced to pay ridiculous extra amount of money and no one in Eurostar showed any empathy, concern or consideration.  An appalling experience and reveals the mismanagement, poor culture and unprofessionism behind the scenes.  As long as you dont have to deal with them directly you consider to be lucky.  We too have travelled numerous times on Eurostar in past but beware if you actually need assistance.  Upon requesting to lodge a complaint and did not want to repeat everything again as we had been on phone for over an hour, an additional hour of documented conversation with their chatline outlining the nature of our concerns clearly however staff, including Team Leader, said the only way you can lodge a complaint was online and then waiting a unrealistic timeframe for a response.  We since found clearly on their website that you can lodge a complaint by calling them.  Yet another example of their ignorance, unprofessionalism, lack of knowledge and determination not to want to help and assist customers in their customer service focused role.  A real disgrace.

Well the biggest advantage of taking these trains as compared to flights is that you move from one city center to another. It was my first experience with Euro star when I travelled to Paris and it was a pretty good one.

I booked tickets in July and had to change  at the last minute had to pay nearly a hundred quid in change fees and Standard tickets are non transferrable. So money lost there I think Eurostar should realise that people can have change of plans so after a change fee there should be a refund option.My trip from London to Paris was marred by the fact that i was sitting near the luggage rack which was behind the toilets so every time someone used the toilet a foul smell reeked into the cabin which was a nightmare. So basically i paid 200 quid to sit in foul smell for 2 hrs 15 mins. Be careful and not choose seats near luggage racks and toilets.Immigration was easy but Gare Du Nord section of Eurostar is v small and takes ages to move along lines. Train was delayed by nearly 35 minutes on the way back. On the whole not much cheaper than flights so for a first time experience I am not impressed.

Seats comfortable , train very clean and staff were brilliant . Lovely continental breakfast with lots of coffee . Time passed very quickly . Be warned to use the bathroom on the train as once you get to Paris unless you have euros and in small denomination you cannot use the bathrooms at the train station . Finally found the atm that dispensed large euros then the bureau of exchange refused to break the more into something smaller . But none of that has anything to do with the train itself that was excellent would do it again

We booked standard premier. It was my friends birthday so I’d ordered a bottle of champagne to have on the way. When it arrived it was warm so consequently when opened it soaked all of us and surrounding passengers, seats, windows etc. Not a great experience. Breakfast was terrible. Dry roll and croissant with orange juice, tea or coffee. Very disappointing. Our trip back was better however. Meal and wine was very good.

Staff is absolutely friendly , when travelled to Paris , station was overpacked and queue was huge ,was around 30 min in queue and thought would miss my train . But than member of staff went through queue and asked who is going on that particular train , I raised hand and she moved me up front of queue. Service on a train was immaculate. Staff is really friendly , food was ok.
Easy and comfortable was to travel from London to Brussels. Allow plenty of time for check-in at St Pancras.

I took the Eurostar train for the first time, From London St Pancras to Paris Gare Du Nord.I used the standard ticket, and it was very comfortable, clean, and perfectly on time in departure but we arrived 35 minutes late for some reason . First at the station in London there was passport check and security check, which is important in these days, but it was very fast and easy. The people there were really helpful and friendly.I booked my ticket on line and all the details was there, the train number, the coach number and the seat number plus of course the ticket number.And when arrived Paris every thing was very easy and smooth.The price was high because I booked in the peak season ( August ),almost triple the normal price.But all in all I loved the experience.

A relaxing journey to Brussels. The train left on time and was comfortable throughout. Pleased that there were no interruptions from staff trying to sell stuff and there was plenty of space overhead for our luggage. A much nicer experience than flying!

Booked standard premier on line and used mobile tickets. Easy check in at london and onto the train. Nice journey, albeit its not as comfortable as the TGV trains.Only warning is be prepared for Gare du Nord and if you are trying to connect to Gare de Lyon.They are both very busy stations. Watch out for the pick pockets who roam around in very orgainsed groups

Great trip - so easy!  You board and clear customs in London and just get off in Paris!  I didn't even realize we were properly in the tunnel and all of a sudden you pop up in France!  So smooth and quick!  We traveled in the first class carriage and it was roomy and service was great - nice food too!  You store your luggage in the train compartment with you and there is plenty of room. Big seats with USB charges and clean toilets!

We again travelled on Eurostar to Belgium from St. Pancras London and as always it was quick and easy.  Our travel Agent had booked tickets on business plus for us, which meant we could spent some relaxing time in the club room prior to boarding however, she had booked first class on our return and don't ask me to explain because I really can't even though I checked with them at the station, but this meant  we didn't have access to the club room but had a pretty good meal with wine on board the train, whereas business plus although we had the club room we didn't get a meal and drink included on the train.  Sorry but it makes no sense to me?   However, each way the trip was relaxing and fast so have no complaints, don't know what we ever did without Eurostar:  Well yes I do, we flew to Europe or went by ferry!

We have used the Eurostar a few times now for weekend breaks in Lille and Paris and have always been impressed. The journey time from centre to centre is seriously fast and the lack of long airport waits makes it the ideal choice for a weekend break. The journey goes by in a heartbeat, which makes it seem like France is just around the corner. It’s a good idea to look out for deals on tickets as they can be quite expensive otherwise.

Travel from St. Pancras station - London to Gare du Nord-Paris on Eurostar, buy at Business Premier, the tickets are the most expensive on Eurostar but it is worth it, the service was very good. It includes two meals and they will get you a taxi if you need it. You can also find a small cafe where you can shop at any time. If you want to change the time of your tickets, they do not charge you any penalties. Travel time is approximately two hours. Advisable! Super service!

Me and my family took the train from London to visit Paris and back to London. It was great! We had assigned seats in the train which was good and there was no need to rush to get in. Security was easy and quick. It was far more better experience than an airport and long queues. We had eaten lunch before our trip back to London and so the meal they provided was sufficient (It was more of a snack and not lunch) The train ride experience was excellent! Good option cheaper than a flight and no hassle going thro crowded airport. There were USB ports to charge the cell phones which was good also. The train was clean and had enough space to put our luggage also.

My wife and had spent a significant amount of time traveling Europe. We did our research, and the Eurostar came up and we booked. Unfortunately we do not catch our train, which is totally our fault. A gentleman named Mo at the service desk, bent over backwards to accommodate our misfortune. The train, staff, and experience are top-notch. Again hats off to Mo for helping us out in that pinch! A truly humbling experience, I couldn't have had a better experience! Thank you!

This is my first time giving a bad review.To be honest, Eurostar from London to Paris was so bad from the very beginning. The staff are all lack of training. None of them have any idea of how to service for passengers. They can not give you any advice, assist nor directions. I have paid US$1000 for 2 return tickets from London to Paris. And I think by far, this is the worse payment I have made my entire life. I have arrived at London St Pancras station one hour and 30 mins. And I have been told by their staff that I came too early. I can not join the line which is 500 metres long. All I can do is wait for the call to join the line. I am a father of 2 years old toddler. And the staff ask me to join an hour   line whenever they feel like to. There was no priority check in line or what so ever.The staff was always rude and will only give you instructions in an aggressive tone(as if we were in the army). After we walked through the check-in, there was a luggage control spot. Where they will scan your luggages and belongings. Here also another 30 mins waiting time. The staff here was also not helpful and impolite. Of course, you might get asked to strip down at the airport. But it will be done in a much better manner. Then the passport check. Here you wouldn't find any troubles. Because it will be done by the border security not the Eurostar staff.Lastly, you will get through to the train. I have spent a total of 2 and a half hour from the time I arrived at the station.Please do avoid Eurostar and use the budget airline. Do not make the same mistake I've made. You will only feel sorry for your companion and above all, yourself, for using the most unprofessional, non-systematic, disgusting transportation service in the entire Europe. Use budget airline while you will only pay 35% cheaper for a ticket. Eurostar does not give you the great train experience you deservePs.I would have give zero rating if I could

I don't even consider another way of travelling to London anymore.  I usually take the train in Lille.  1h and 20 min later I am in London.  No need to travel to and from the airport.  No need to be hours ahead of departure time.  Though... it can be busy in London. The train is not only fast but also comfortable and almost always ontime.  Last trip the return train was 1 hour 15 min late.  The next day Eurostar gave some compensation.  Even though I hated the delay, I would travel with Eurostar again.

The Eurostar journey is good. It's quick and inexpensive if you book in advance. For our journey, the departure and arrival times were respected. The car was not very clean, the wifi is not great because it works with the external mobile phone network. The staff is pleasant. For the outward journey we traveled in Standard, I, who have long legs, touched the seat opposite. For the return we traveled in Standard Premier, so that’s the best!! First of all, the reception on the platform is done by a dedicated person. The carriage is spacious, the seats are spaced further apart from each other. A small meal is served on board during the journey, with drinks and coffee to finish. Staff regularly stop by the aisle to ask if everything is okay. We loved it, and I recommend this little upgrade which has a cost but is great. The toilets in Standard Premier were very clean, but the carriage was like the one on the outward journey, that is to say not very clean.

Apart from the queues at St. Pancras, xray machinery tray rollers broken on our queue and then just one French immigration officer slowing the whole process.....the train left on time and it was plain sailing from then on. Not the most comfortable of our pre booked seats but better than some airlines and it was only 3.5 hours so doable. So 3 countries later we're at our destination bang on time....doing 299km per hour at the fastest shown today. Destination Amsterdam Central.....very easy to negotiate station.

This was my 6th Eurostar trip from London to Eurodisney and I honestly can’t find a sing,e good thing about th trip.1.It started with a 2 hour sanding queue at St Pancras( with th children!!), the queue was all around the station and you can see families struggling, one parents goes to get food then the other taking kids to bathroom, it was horrible, The system is so bad and old it takes that long to check people in.2. The train so old and feels filthy, and very uncomfortable, I even got carsick, which is new to me on a train.3. The queue on thw cafe on the train is more than 30 minutes, and one person serving every one.  4.we used the Disney express where our bags are taken returned to the hotel, but the system is so bad an unorganized, that it took 30 minutes to drop the bag and 1 hour to take on the way back, ver unorganized and chaotic, is easier to drop the stuff at the hotel ourselves. 5. On the way back at St Pancras, passport control took an a hour,  again very unorganized.6. Tickets for 2 adults and 3 childen cost 1000pounds, it is defiantly cheaper and more comfortable to use th train, even adding the airport trips ....

We travelled between St. Pancras and Gare du Nord and what a difference between the check in at the two stations.St. Pancras was an absolute breeze.  It was very busy, but the lines moved smoothly and quickly and there never seemed to be major delays in the process.However, Gare du Nord was so different.  We arrived in good time to check in, but it seemed that people for the train an hour before us were still muddled up at the check in.  None of the scanners were working on the ticket barriers, but the staff still insisted that you put your ticket through to scan - only for it not to be accepted. Of the six automatic passport scanning booths, only two were working.  Then, when we got through to the manned passport control, only two of those were manned.  There was a third but they couldn't get their pc and other equipment to work so weren't able to help.  This all meant that everyone was held up and getting more and more frustrated.That said, the journey itself was excellent and the seats really comfortable.  Certainly more space than being cramped up on a plane.

Used Eurostar as means of travel for a birthday celebration trip.  We had booked three seats together but at St Pancreas, one of our three was told that his seat had been changed and he was moved right to the other end of the carriage.  We objected  and pointed out this was a special trip for a birthday celebration, but was told that sometimes it is necessary to change reserved seats.There were people travelling on their own that were seated near to my wife and I and I questioned why one of those was not moved instead.  The answer from Eurostar was "the re-allocation of seats is an automatic process so does not always group people together".There was no check on age so presumably this means that minors or elderly persons needing assistance could also be moved away from the rest of their travelling companions.

Check in en passport check  went smoothly. We were the two  last persons . So we didnt have to wait long. Our Business Premier Class seats were changed. We did not ask why, because at the check in they said we were still sitting next to each other and next to a window, in the same class.. Boarding was also perfect  and the train left excatly on time at 12.53pm. With a speed of 300 km phr we went through Belgium and later through France towards England. Not long after departure the hostess came along with the lunch. I had salmon with herbs and Kinoa a small bun a seven up and a bottle of water. My friend had  a small vegetable quiche  and a lentils salad a small bun and a small bottle of wine. You could ask for more if you wanted. As desert we got a small bun filled with whipcream. Covered with suger. The food wasnt that great.When we departed the train was not full but many people got on along the way. Seat width is good. You cant stretch your legs properly because we were sitting at a table of four and other travelers were sitting opposite us, The seat can be inclined to a comfortable position. There are also reading lights on the left side of your seat. On the side just above the table there are english sockets to charge your devices. The train also had wifi. The train had train entertainment but you can/ could only enjoy it if you download the eurostar app or on eurostar.com. There were overhead screens in the train but they realy didnt give any info. It would be good if info was provided about the position, the speed, remaining travel time etc etc. The biggest part of the journey went smoothly.. We arrived with a delay of 30 minutes at Sint Pancras Station.  We had a delay of 20 minutes in Calais. Because of security reasons. I could not figure out what those security reasons were.The return journey five days later was almost the same. But without a delay. Again we had a seat change without any explanation. But now it was changed from Business Premier class seats for seats into The Standard premier Class. The lady at the check in said the service was the same. But the seats were smaller. The train left on time at 10.58am. It was in the morning so we got breakfast. luckily It wasnt english breakfast. (i dont like it).The breakfast was not great but not that bad either. The croissants were not warm. It was an older train than the one we came with. It has no wifi. The journy went smoothly and we arrived at Brussel South/ Midi Station exactly on time at 14.05. This was a realy nice experience. Nice clean and fast trains. Friendly and helpful staff.In 2007  Sint Pancras Station became the terminal station of this train in London. Before that it was Waterloo Station.

Great idea, lousy execution.  Go business or first class if you can.  Economy is a real cattle call.  Crowd management on both ends poor, no place to sit if you are early.  Staff indifferent or rude.  In St. Pancras, not enough seating so three trains worth of people were stuffed into the waiting room.  Delays a big problem on both trips; 90 mins + when we returned.  The UK border force agent in Paris was unprofessional and brusque; I filed a complaint about it.  Pay the money and get the lounge.  Service in the bar car was glacially slow; very understaffed.

We travelled to Bruges by Eurostar we caught the 08.54 service, on the paperwork it said to give yourself 45 minutes to get through the checks, we gave over an hour and still only just made the train sitting in our seats at 08.51!We queued to scan our tickets, then we queued to go through security, the scanner seemed to have a moment where it stoped working with our bags in it, then when we went through passport checks I asked an operative if there was a quicker way as I feared we would miss our train, he said he was in charge of the queue....well let’s just say he was doing a CRAP JOB! It was carnage in the end two girls in front of us had to push through the queue and get us all to the front, then we were rushed through by the staff like we were idiots for being late and to add insult to injury we had to run at full pelt up a travelator that wasn’t working dragging heavy cases behind us, the whole experience from start to finish was shambolic. It was only after we were told that we could have gone through the electronic passport gates which were much quicker but obviously we were told that by other passengers and not Eurostar staff!!!! if they had one person calling for people on the 08.54 to come to the front of the queue it would have been so much better, instead the useless staff members were just stood around not being any use other than ornamental! All these points considered I would give yourself at least 1-1/2 hours to check in, on a positive note coming back from Brussels was an absolute dream so at least one side of the tunnel have got it right!!!!!

Center to center, with Wifi all the way.  We'd done this before, but it's gotten faster now that the London terminus is St. Pancras.  Give yourself plenty of time to get through security plus passport checks.

Yes, yes it is a very nice train. The front end is very modern and aerodynamic looking.  The inside was nice...high quality seats, enough leg room (I’m 6’4”), better-than-airplane  food and friendly staff.  It was not the Orient Express nor was it Amtrak (if you’ve been to the U.S.)...my Grandson and I were comfortable.  However, BEWARE of the windowless seats! I carefully chose our seat, using all of my 50 years of International travel experiences, so that my Grandson would have a great view of the passing scenery.  And, of great importance, we were taking a very fast train to be able to experience the relative movement of going >150 MPH. However, there was no window. Two seats...one aisle and one not window...just a bulkhead or blank wall, nada view to anything.  So, we sat there in full-on befuddlement.  We would not be able to have the experience we had so anticipated for so many months.  What to do? I found a Eurostar steward (ess?) attendant. She was not very helpful even though there were ten vacant sets of seats in our car...telling us that they were “reserved.” We then left the station as she was telling me that all the seats were taken. I did not want to cause any further negativity on our trip...so I opted for a “make the best of it” attitude and moved my Grandson and I to a full window seat on our return trip to London.  Here’s a hint for getting the feeling of speed (as long as your smart phone has video capability): Using a vertical edge of the window for a framing effect on one side of your image with focus on the window frame.....wait until there are shrubs/bushes/trees flying by as close to the train as possible and start your video.  Let it run for at least two minutes and provide your own narration if you wish. Next: using the same window frame make your focus on the greenery that is flashing by and not on the frame.   Also shoot for at least two minutes.  Depending on how the sun light is hitting the shrubs you will get a strong feeling of very rapid movement.  (BTW this only works with lensing that can be focused)...other wise just shoot with whatever equipment you have and you will still get your “Need For Speed” fix.  My Grandson and I certainly did on our return trip to London.  One last thing, they do not announce anything about the tunnel...like, it’s “coming up in a few minutes” or “ don’t worry, we have not entered a black hole” or “how do you like having no frame of reference with which to gauge your speed?”  or, “What was that?” Or, finally, “Tunnel, what tunnel? I didn’t see a tunnel.”  All in all it was an amazing experience to go really, really fast on the ground! Go for it! Cheers!

We traveled from London to Paris with the Eurostar and it went pretty smoothly. St. Pancras was very crowded and there were some long lines going through security. Once we got onto the train, the ride was so smooth, and fast! No problems at all through the trip to Paris. We certainly enjoyed our trip on the Eurostar.

Have taken 3 trips this month, all of them delayed with issues. They bill themselves as faster than flying with less hassles. They have similar if not worse delays, you still have to go through security procedures and wait in long queues. I think you are better off flying now. Overall a massive disappointment

As a forty-something, I saw a world in which crossing the English Channel with a tunnel was one of Engineering's greatest challenges. I remember crying when the French and English engineers exchanged flags as they drilled the last part of the stretch. I decided to visit Paris from London, and I recognize that the trip has nothing special other than the convenience of leaving in the center of Paris, at Gare du Nord. The Eurostar is uncomfortable, with children crying, and that terrible interval to wait for the branch to be released, horrible. You fly at 350 km per hour for leagues, and a few kilometers from Pancras or Gare du Nord, it gets into an annoying row.

Good points:train is fast, food is not bad, service on the train very friendly and efficient. You can walk about, lots of space. You go straight into the heart of London/Paris.Bad points:Awful check in, long queues, long delays and then terrible customer service when it comes to claiming compensation.  They basically pretend to offer compensation to you but make it impossible to claim back.

it is very nice to be communicated between paris and London as fast as eurostar does. I dont give the 5 stars because is always very expensive. if they decrease the price can be one of the best trains ever.

We are resident in France but decided that as we are in our 70s a nice peaceful train journey to London might be preferable to crowded airports...big big mistake!  The first leg for us was Angouleme to Lille Flanders and any “easy stroll” between Lille Flanders and Lille Europe - across vast rebuilding and road schemes with luggage. The heat wasn’t Eurostar’s fault!  Crowded check in, up and down staircases, no food available except vending machines, zero help. Everyone was travelling with luggage, some masses of it. No trolleys, more stairs and onto crowded Eurostar to London. Average comfort in non upgraded carriages and endless incomprehensible announcements.  The return was worse. St Pancras made Terminal 5 Heathrow  look like paradise.  A nice Eurostar guy rescued us, let us sit down precheckin and put us and our luggage thru security quickly. Again, huge amounts of chaos, luggage and confusion, overcrowded wait area and more ramps!  Very very disappointed and will never ever use this again. Late both ways and who designed the platforms to be almost 2 feet down from the trains? It was a hazardous manoeuvre getting off both trains, more so in Lille Flanders.  Great idea very poorly executed. 12 hours door to door....

This was a nice change from flying (comparing business class to business class) for a short haul. The airports are such a pain and the business class seats are just coach with an empty middle seat. This was extremely pleasant (although our bus diver got lost and we missed our first booking, LOL). The airport not so crowded with plenty of shops and restaurants and there is a very nice business lounge. The train itself is very comfortable with plenty of leg room.

Booked standard premier London to Paris.Checkin and security is a shambles.Boarding was ok.The luggage space is a bit limited for international.Our seats were terrible, two facing backwards with no window. Just an awful experience and so disappointing to not be able to see any of the countryside.The train is fast and smooth, but what sort of moron designs an interior with no views???I was deeply disappointed especially in view of the premium price we paid.
checking in is a nightmare during holidays but once you're on it, is is so conveinient to go from city to city . price is a bit steeo though

I took the Eurostar from Brussels to London. To purchase tickets at a low price, book directly online on the first day of sale six months in advance. It was 56 euros per person in second class. There was only one ticket left after two months, so it's better to book early. Seats can be determined on My Page after making a reservation. The orientation of the seat cannot be changed, so be careful when choosing. There is immigration control for the UK in Brussels, so you can move immediately after arriving in London. The Eurostar departed and arrived on time. There was a table, and the seats and legroom were wide and comfortable. There are two toilets in each vehicle. The cafeteria is in cars 8 and 9 and sells the same items. You can use pounds and euros (although expensive). I was worried about where to store my luggage since I had a suitcase, but the locals had small suitcases so there was plenty of space. There was no announcement across the International Date Line, and the time on the monitor was changing suddenly. Before leaving, I tried to take a photo at the front (in front of the staff), but my husband was told not to take a photo...

Occasional travelers such as we are, we have no complaints about the Eurostar service itself, just a complaint about the on line seat booking... The seat maps are inaccurate where window positions in concerned, so be warned, you think you booked a seat by the window and end up with a six inch view of 200 mile an hour countryside.Other than that, all good.

We arrived at St. Pancras Station with plenty of lead time to get through customs and relax with a coffee. What we didn’t know was they don’t allow you to “check in” until just more than an hour before departure. That’s both good and bad. On the one hand, there are plenty of places to get coffee & people watch before checking in.  On the other hand, once you get through U.K. customs and French customs, there aren’t many places to sit around waiting to board. Our train TO Paris was quite comfortable and we arrived at Gare du Nord on time.The return trip was a bit different... the train was older and the seats a bit more worn and less comfortable... we arrived back in London on time.

We waited in line for over an hour to get to the first of 2 immigration check points.  After clearing British immigration we had to wait in a lengthy line for French immigration.  Next was a lengthy line for bag screening, which meant lifting a regular size suitcase up on a conveyer belt.  After that was the line for body screening.  With minutes left before departure everyone was running for the train.  No time to go to any shops for food or drink.  Half an hour into the journey we stopped and sat for almost 2 hours because of an incident on the tracks.  Food car had nothing but chips and a few other junk foods.  You get off at Gare du Nord and are immediately surrounded by gypsies.  Avoid the taxi line, use the G7 app to get a safe, economical, honest car in minutes.  There were over 200 people in the taxi line and no taxis.  Mysteriously mini van taxis kept showing up which security escorted groups of 3 or more into, leaving the regular line just standing.  Something not right going on!  More expensive than flying and an absolute nightmare.  I do not have an EU passport but after Brexit neither will the British.  Have no idea how that will be handled.  Avoid the Eurostar!!!!

Someone once wrote that rail companies are now trying to combine the disadvantages of traveling by train with those of flying. That's certainly not entirely true, as there are actually no rail-specific disadvantages with the Eurostar. The bottom line is that getting from city center to city center is certainly no slower than taking a plane, and other amenities of flying such as a certain exclusivity or meals included in the price have not been around for a long time. However, the Eurostar has taken over some of the disadvantages of flying, such as booking a specific train in good time, having to be at the train station a long time before departure and the security check. We had planned our trip long-term and were therefore able to book a cheap fare. In the meantime there had been a minor change to the timetable, which we were informed about by email when it came into effect and again by SMS a few days before departure. You should be at the station 60 to 45 minutes before departure (access closes 30 minutes before departure). First, if there is an automatic barrier (which does not always work) or a busy counter, the ticket must be scanned and if the seats assigned during booking have changed, you will receive a boarding pass with the new seat number. Then all the luggage goes to a security check, because as is usual with the train, the luggage is not checked in, but taken onto the train. During our trip, the security personnel were extremely unfriendly. You can find out which items are prohibited on the Eurostar website. They are slightly different from those on the plane. Then the passport is checked by a friendly Belgian police officer (Schengenland is left) and then there is British immigration control in Brussels (automations like those at British airports). Then you have to wait until the train is released for boarding. There are luggage compartments at the ends of the train on the train. Suitcases and bags that are not too large can also be stored in the luggage rack above the seats. The seats are comfortable (for me more comfortable than in the Railjet or ICE), WiFi works as usual in railway trains. Ultimately, it was a very pleasant train journey that lasted about two hours.

First time on Eurostar from London to Paris, loved it.  Premium class ticket was very comfortable, good on board service with free WiFi.   Going through security was also smooth & easy.Highly recommended

Travelled by Eurostar from Ebbsfleet to Brussels. Fast and efficient service. Parking at Ebbsfleet is easy and reasonably priced and the terminal staff were all very helpful. I arrived very early and was able to change my ticket to an earlier train. I also needed a ramp to get on/off the train and this was supplied efficiently and with no fuss at both stations for both outward and return journeys.  Meals were supplied by friendly staff on the train and the time passed very quickly. Will definitely use this service again

We booked a month back but there were limited choices for seating so my recommendation is to book even earlier. It meant we were unable to get four seats facing a table so we’re left with two behind the other two which wasn’t so bad, but they are fairly cramped in economy. Make sure you get to St Pancras station nice and early as there are literally thousands and thousands of people running everywhere and it appears like chaos! Luckily we were prepared for that to a certain extent because we  had picked up a rental car from St Pancras a few days earlier so knew our way around. The day we were travelling to Paris the toilets were completely out of order in the entire station and you had to go across the square to Kings Cross where they were massive queues for the toilets. This made us a little late joining the queue for the train and there was a huge mass of humanity trying to get through the gates, border control etc. The LCD screen started flashing that the gate for our train was closing which made us anxious until I spoke to one of the staff and she said not to worry. Makes me wonder why they have the thing flashing because it just causes everybody anxiety! This was obviously a bit stressful but we got on board in the end. Seats were a little cramped but it was not a big deal as the trip is only two hours 20 minutes - awesome way to travel and it’s hard to believe you are in Paris so quickly. Picked up an Uber at the other end to take us to our airbnb apartment in Paris. Eurostar recommended and would do it again.

Used Eurostar to travel from London to Brussels in June 2018. Booked the First Class ticket. Awesome experience, great on-board service. Plenty of space for our 2 suitcases. The coach was very comfortable and quiet. Well worth the extra expense.Check-in was easy, security was excellent.

We were 2 couples traveling together from England to France. We had reserved a table for 4 in Standard Premier class several months in advance. Arriving at St Pancras station about 1-1/2 hours in advance we received our first shock - the check in process was utter chaos. The trains appear to be scheduled too closely together and seem to be overbooked. Think of the worst security lines in airports where everyone has all of the luggage - not just carryons. They were pulling people out of line who were going to miss there trains overwise. When we finally made it to the gate to scan our tickets, 3 out of our party were given new seats, not together and my ticket was rejected all together. I was sent to another long line to look into the problem. After finally getting to talk to someone I was given a new seat assignment. Only after this do you go through security! It turns out that the car we had been ticketed for was totally eliminated from the train that day! No announcement as to what was going on - just shuttling and shoving from line to line. We were finally all in seats with just 5 minutes to spare. No one on the railroad staff cared at all and were just plain rude. The ride itself was fine and the food was good, but the overall experience is definitely colored by the check in process!

Took a trip from London to Paris through the Chunnel Via Eurostar.  The lines in London were quiet long but the staff was extremely organized and for the amount of people the process was efficient. We took Standard premier and the service, seats, and accommodations were great.  Every seat on the train was full but it was quiet.  They serve a meal along the way and there is a beverage cart you can also visit for drinks and snacks.  The trip through the Chunnel was very quick and the view from the train was great.  The only negative part was that we were stuck on the tracks for two hours due to a faulty rail line, but I am not sure how much of that was Eurostars fault.  The attendant in the beverage cart (Sebastian?) was a hard worker and very welcoming.  Overall great experience and easy travel London to Paris!

We booked our Eurostar train from London to Paris a few months in advance and we were able to pick seats for the four of us around a table (which is great as long as two people don't mind riding backwards). The tickets said to arrive 45-60 minutes early. We arrived at least an hour early at St Pancras. This is still international travel, so you need to go through security and a passport check before arriving in the waiting room for the train. Boarding was very easy. We were booked in Standard class. The train was very clean and comfortable. We weren't sure what the food would be like on board, so we had bought some sandwiches for lunch before we arrived at St Pancras. The travel was very smooth and it was nice to see the English and French countryside. Overall, an easy way to get between the two cities.

Recently enjoyed EuroStar high speed train service from London Saint Pancras to Paris Gare du Nord station. I had done some preliminary online and personal research and decided to book Standard Premier class. Eurostar offers three classes of service:  standard, standard premier, and business premier. The biggest difference between standard and standard premier is the level of spaciousness of the cabin, meal service with wine offerings, and overall increased comfort. The next class of business premier offers access to business premier lounge with pre-departure amenities offering refreshments and food and a nice, relaxing space to await your departure. After much research we opted to book Standard Premier. The cabins did not appear to be any nicer in comparison and the online research did not indicate any difference in level of service while on the train. The major difference seemed to be the access to the lounge and early boarding through a dedicated entry, which we thought unnecessary. Also the cost for the business premier was substantially more expensive than compared to standard premier. We thoroughly enjoyed the service in standard premier. We were offered a nice lunch with refreshments, including a nice glass of red wine, all served on china with silver. Very nice!  The train was so comfortable and smooth. We actually slept through the Chunnel crossing!!  2:15 ride to Paris was such a comfortable experience. I would highly recommend! Comfortable, efficient way to get from London to Paris.
Very convenient connection without taking off ground. worth taking first class. online booking works perfectly.

We bought the executive and we don't regret it. Good waiting lounge and some queue to board Very spacious executive carriages with good service and food. I really enjoyed coming from Brussels to London!

Took the Eurostar from Paris to London. How cool is it to go BENEATH the English Channel in the Chunnel in a comfortable and fast train. Better than Treni service in Italy in that the Wifi internet was free and the cars are more plush. This was booked through Costco as a 5 days in Paris and 5 days in London package. You must go through both French and English customs at either end of the journey (if you go from London to Paris or you go from Paris to London) so make sure you leave yourself some extra time to do that as it does take a while.

We were booked on a morning train in June 24 that was cancelled and resulted in a 6 hour wait until the next available train. Now, July 5 we have a minimum 2 hour delay. Terrible customer service. People wall to wall. Miserable.

I recently had a wonderful trip to Europe.  It was only marred by one thing: Eurostar.I purchased a First-Class Eurostar ticket in Australia before I left for England.When I boarded at St Pancras I was not afforded any of the entitlements of the ticket except for the relevant seat on the train.I was made to queue in the Standard queue – I was not re-directed to the Business Premier queue.  I was pushed and jostled through Security.  The whole episode was very disorganised.I was not directed to the lounge, where I was entitled to wait before the train departed.The stairs up to the train carriage were very narrow and steep which made it awkward with a heavy bag.  No assistance was offered.The announcements were inaudible and we were not given any idea of the layout of the train.  Were there toilets on board?  I don't know....The food was cold and horrible and not nicely served.  The whole experience was distressing.From now on, when moving between France and the UK, I will fly.

Other than check-in at St Pancras International, which was somewhat disorganized, my round trip from London to Paris was a very enjoyable ride.The train was very clean and the seats were comfortable. My daughter had a croissant from the snack car and enjoyed it, and the price was reasonable. They accept British pounds and Euros. They might accept credit cards, but I am unsure on this on as I paid in Euros.As I mentioned to a TripAdvisor member, I purchased my round-trip tickets a couple of months in advance directly from the Eurostar website. We traveled in Standard class, and the price was very good. We could have upgraded to Standard Premium, but the seats were comfortable that we felt we didn't need to spend the extra $100 each just for a bit more legroom and included snack brought to your seat.All-in-all, a very enjoyable ride. I'd definitely travel Eurostar again, and I would highly recommend this way to travel to Paris, if you want a comfortable ride with great views of both the English and French countryside.I wish I could provide pictures from the train, but I was too busy relaxing.

A relaxing way to travel pleasantly, efficiently and environmentally friendly. Early booking is very affordable, and you can also choose your seat preference. Unfortunately, a different type of wagon had been used on the outward journey, so this was incorrect. By the way, this was resolved as best as possible. Therefore, just before departure, check whether the layout is correct. Sometimes the Thalys is also used for connecting routes. Bookings can therefore be made directly via Eurostar instead of NS International

Since I don't like flying, this time we chose the option of traveling to England by train instead of the ferry. The Eurostar is more than an emergency solution. This train is extremely fast and comfortable. You also save yourself the lengthy process of checking in at the airport. Really great!
Went to buy a snack a little over half an hour into journey to Paris but nothing left.Buy something from the station concourse before boarding.Toilets were dreadful. Ashamed to be British.

Travelled to Paris on Eurostar just for one day, went from Ebbsfleet which was very convenient, easy check in and customs clearance.Decided to go Business Premium, the seats and compartment were excellent but on way out the hot breakfast was cold, on way back food was better, I did expect a little more as the price was expensive.Still it was a good service on time both ways and the perfect way to travel to Paris for business for a short trip.

High speed train was on my bucket list!  Arrived about an hour early - the Terminal was a zoo!  Check-in line, security line, UK Exit Customs, French Entry Customs.  I think there had been earlier trains cancelled that morning, so it took a while.  Once inside the terminal, it was calm and I had a snack at the French bakery.  The short ride was very nice and comfortable, I bought a drink in the Cafe.  Arrived in Lille to find a huge shopping mall next to the train station!  Spent a few hours shopping and returned to London the same day.Overall, I enjoyed it very much and will do it again!  Message me if you have any questions!

If one wants to travel between London and Brussels or Paris, the EuroStar train is an attractive alternative to taking an airplane or a car. It covers the distance from downtown to downtown in 3 1/2 hours, so it can beat a plane (it is also probably far more reliable than a plane).The train is famous for the ride through the long tunnel under the English channel, but I found that part of the trip rather unspectacular.Since we were on family vacation, we treated ourselves to first class tickets. We felt that the additional space and comfort were worth the money. It turned out that we hadn't factored in another benefit: they served us a nice little lunch on the train that was very tasty. It was included in the price of the ticket.Many people have to travel a lot by airplane these days, mostly for business reasons. That is true for me also, to some extent at least. Let's say, I have to travel more than I would like to.The airplane industry is under such tremendous pressure to keep the cost in check that nobody really can enjoy traveling by airplane, except perhaps the select few who can afford first class tickets. When I hear travelers exchange their experiences, it is rarely positive what they have to say about traveling by plane.The space is limited, the food is lousy, comfort is really non-existent, it is noisy, the reliability could be better, the prices are too high, and so on.In contrast, our travel experience with the EuroStar train was 100% positive. This is a great way to get around. There is space and comfort. The four of us got to sit at a table. There was space for laptop computers, newspapers, card games. I can only recommend you try it out.

This was my first time riding a high speed train. I spent a week in Paris and needed a fast and less expensive way of getting to London for another week. I ended up comparing prices between airlines and Eurostar train rides. I happened to find a train ride for 161 euros and most flights were over 200 so I decided to try the train. I will forever take the train between Paris & London any time I go to or from...what a great overall experience! :)

I was riding in a comfortable seat on the "EuroStar" high-speed train. Among the nearly a thousand passengers in more than ten carriages on this train, my wife and I were the only ones from the East. The whole journey only takes 2.5 hours, which is really convenient. The quality of the passengers is good, and I didn’t see any tour groups!

It's a quick and easy way. You don't have to fly into the sky, just sit comfortably on your home and you can reach your destination in more than two hours. Except for a section of the road under the sea, you can see the scenery the rest of the way, which is different from the sky.

We had a weekend in Paris. We paid for the wider seats and are so much better than the standard ones. We got breakfast included going there and lunch coming back. The food is lovely and they ask you on several occasions throughout your travel if you would like tea or coffee. The staff are very helpful and professional in their job

Can not complain.  The service was excellent.  The food was excellent.  It was quick and of course you were able to take in the scenery in the UK and France.  The seats were comfortable and with 5 of us we could all still talk to each other.

We went to Eurostar.com at St.Pancras Station. I am in a wheelchair, so going anywhere is not that simple. I was told that Eurostar had some good package deals (Trains and hotels) to Amsterdam, and, if you try to look these deals up on the internet, the Eurostar website suddenly clamps down, saying ‘Oops, something went wrong’ and ‘sorry, we can’t complete your search (Error: BPA)’; simple, we’ll go to their U.K. London office in St.Pancras Station. Could we please know about your deals? ‘We don’t know’.Could we know the cost of your train fares? ‘That’s not easy’. Could we have a copy of your train time tables? ‘We will have to go and find them’. Do you offer help for the disabled? ‘We are not sure about that’. Not great.

My Train to Brussels was cancelled. I was told to rebook on a trerminal at St Pancras. I tried to book for the next train which was 2 hours later. The system didn't work and the terminal told me to "Seek Assistance". I asked a member of staff and was told to join a queue. I then got an email telling me of the cancellation and saying I could book on line. I tried it, it failed to work. It also had a phone number to call, I tried it, they refused to answer and the call just kept hanging up! Absolutely no customer service!!! I queued for an hour. I finally got to talk to someone. She was useless and didn't have a clue what she was doing. She had to call a supervisor to help her. Eventually she gave me boarding passes for the train which was 4 hours later. I asked about the one that was 2 hours later and she said there were no seats left. I asked if they were in the same class (I originally booked premium Economy). She said "no, there were no seats left". I walked away, disgusted. I then looked at the boarding passes, she had stamped them with "voluntarily downgraded". Nothing voluntary about it at all, if I hadn't have asked her I wouldn't have known until I got on the train. I went to check in after hanging around St Pandras for 3 hours. The boarding passes wouldn't work in the automatic barrier. Someone took them from me and scanned then at a desk and let me through. I hung around for an hour, in the stiflling heat and packed out waiting area, with nowhere to sit. I then boarded the train, and there was already someone else in my allocated seats! I hung around at the end of the carriage and eventually collared someone on the platform who told me to go to coach 15. The train then left and I had to struggle through 5 coaches to get to coach 15. There was a member of staff with an iPad, she asked for our boarding passes, but couldn't find us on her system, so told us to just sit anywhere! This turned out to be a premium coach. We were not offered anything in terms of food or drink that we were suppose to have recieved on a premium service. The staff were notable by their absence. The train was then delayed about 30 mins and I eventually got to the hotel I had booked about 5 hours later than expected. I have been in dispute about compensation for this shambles. They just keep quoting terms and conditions at me. I booked the trip as a package, including an hotel, and I didn't get a breakdown of the individual costs. They are claiming the train fare was £113 and they will refund 50% (or 75% if I take vouchers against a future ticket). Looking at the booking system on the internet the cost for the same train, any day at 1pm, is always over £200. The company is a total disgrace and will rip you off when you try to claim compensation. They know they can always sell the seats as, on the face of it, is a very convenient way to travel. So they have you over a barrel once you click to accept the T&Cs.
90£ extra for round trip only for one bike and on the way back we find the bikes even ribbed!! Mai fidarsi per servizio bici !!!

Ah, the Eurostar, the majestic iron worm that gracefully slithers from Brussels to London in a mere 2 hours. Because who needs wings when you can glide on tracks? Alright, let's dive into this rollercoaster of a review.The Green Appeal 🌱First off, let's give a round of applause for the environment-friendly aspect. While jetting through the skies on a plane might seem like the epitome of cool, Eurostar is here to remind us that going green isn't just for hippies. It's a train that leaves a smaller carbon footprint, which means you can smugly sip your overpriced coffee knowing you're saving the planet, one train ride at a time.The Luggage Conundrum 🎒Now, onto the fun stuff. If you're someone who enjoys a good workout – and by workout, I mean lugging around your own baggage – then this train is right up your alley. Forget those fancy smug plane porters. No sir, it’s all you and your biceps here. Think of it as a free gym session.Cleanliness? Meh 🧽Ever wanted to experience the thrill of uncertainty? Eurostar’s cleanliness is a bit like playing Russian roulette. Will the train be spotless, or will you find remnants of someone’s snack from 1999? It’s a mystery! So strap in and hope for the best.Speed Demon? Not Quite 🚄Sure, flying might shave off some time, but where's the fun in that? On Eurostar, you get to enjoy 2 hours of scenic views, questionable cleanliness, and the satisfaction of knowing you’re marginally better than everyone else who chose to fly.Verdict 🎉Despite the minor inconveniences – like having to be your own bellhop and enduring the occasional grime – Eurostar offers a solid, planet-friendly alternative to flying. Plus, think of all the stories you'll have.So, if you're up for a bit of adventure and environmental bragging rights, hop on the Eurostar. Just maybe bring some hand sanitizer. Totally can recommend it.Safe travels, eco-warriors! 🌍🚆✨
Never ever again!!! An absolute catastrophe!!! It’s a shame for the company to employ a train manager like we had on our trip. We will never travel again with Eurostar!

It is rare that we travel by train as we usually fly.  We had 4 large bags and kids… so normally it is a bit of a hassle to get from A to B.  We found the overall experience to be better than flying… the St Pancras station was near where we were staying in London, we followed the guidance of being there 90m before departure and followed the signs.  We did note that it was very busy because of another train departing just before ours, so security was queued and the departure hall was packed.  Once that train loaded, the hall was relatively empty.There were staff everywhere that we could ask questions to, clearing French customs was straightforward, and boarding was also pretty simple all things considered.  The best part was that we arrived in Paris in the core rather out in the boonies… so getting to our hotel didn’t take any where near as long as flying.The only criticism I have was that the WiFi on board is unusable.  Whomever is responsible for the IT infrastructure doesn’t know what he is doing.We would use Eurostar again if we had the choice.Note that ticket prices go up and down based on demand… so you could save a few $ if you watch prices to get an idea how they move beforehand.

Having traveled from Barcelona to Paris on the TGV, which I rated 5 star, experiencing a high degree of comfort / cleanliness in an almost silent (train / track noise) environment for 5.5 hours.  There was no comparison with the very tired / shabby and noisy confines of the Eurostar to London. The French owners need to invest in this service.
Poor quality PMR assistance, they often forget about people coming to pick up in wheelchairs, so you may miss your Eurostar because of incompetent staff or behaving weirdly with old people.
Refused to board the train 30 minutes before. Instruction written very small. 50€ per person extra. Staff not friendly. Might as well take the plane if it is to arrive 1 hour before the train!

I booked a Eurostar 1st class, direct trip from Amsterdam to Paris for my family 3 months in advance for $377 only to find out that it had been cancelled.  I happened to login to the eurostar site 2 nights before leaving, and there was a message saying the train was cancelled and that I needed to re-book a different eurostar train or request a refund.  NO eurostar trains were available since it was 2 days before departure, and in discussing it with eurostar they admitted that they had failed to notify me via email or text of the cancellation.The only thing I could find was an IC (InterCity) train to Brussels in 2nd class with no assigned seating that transferred to a eurostar train for the Brussels to Paris leg of the trip.  The trip was longer and not as nice as originally planned because of these changes, which we could live with...  The infuriating part of the whole situation is that I had to pay $611 for the new booking since it was 2 days before departure.  While eurostar did refund the $377, they denied my request to refund the difference.  Again...  THEY cancelled my train without telling me and admitted that they failed to tell me.  My whole family could have very easily showed up at Amsterdam Central with all of our luggage and no path to Paris.  It was by chance that I even found out about the cancellation.  At a minimum, eurostar should cover the difference in my ticket costs.  I have reached out to them multiple times over the past few days after speaking with 1 individual on the phone that actually showed some compassion and desire to help, but now I get no response to any of my email inquiries.  This is one of the worst customer experiences of my life considering the company admitted their mistake and refuses to make it right.  My costs almost doubled for their mistake.To top things off, my son is in a wheelchair because of a broken leg 18 days before I trip began.  The IC Train and transfer in Brussels only made that part of our situation more difficult.

Hello, I booked a ticket, my booking number is YPTJK2 my train was at 18h13 on 09/07/2024 and the employee refused me access. He didn't even look at my ticket. I was waiting in line to have my ticket scanned and being the last in line because I got passed by everyone, I arrived last and the gentleman told me no I close I want to know nothing. What a poor and unacceptable quality of service! Buying a €100 ticket to make me disrespect that I receive no consideration is gross... I will certainly forward this message with a Google notice and tell everyone about it. It is a scandal and all the employees I have spoken to agree with me. It was car 15 and if I knew who refused me access, I would mention his name. Eurostar has changed badly and humans remain insensitive and devious. I am making this comment because I want a return to justify this attitude which was disrespectful.

I made a mistake during the reservation process. I was forced to buy a new ticket for 250 euro. The costumer service was polite but unwilling to help me. Recommend checking three times before booking.

Unfortunately dogs are not allowed on the route to London.Many Europeans have dogs and would like to spend their holidays with their dog in dog-friendly England. Eurostar's decision prevents environmentally friendly arrivals and departures and encourages driving and flying.And in times of climate change.When I asked for the reason, I received no reply. Only confirmation that dogs are not allowed. We booked tickets with Lufthansa today.Not environmentally friendly, but completely problem-free.

What a great experience - from arriving at Kings Cross St Pancras, through customs and on board - then whisked along in comfort, to arrive at Gare du Nord for easy access to anywhere in Paris!  We were travelling with friends and late to book, so had the 'airline' seats, but they were spacious and we were still able to socialise. Highly recommend - we wouldn't travel any other way London to Paris.
I bought three tickets, Rotterdam / Paris...on the day of departure one of those who was with me sick very badly so we had to cancel the trip...ZERO returned me for my tickets, no solution.

Went to Lille in France. Everything went wonderfully well. Train was clean and trip was very relaxing. Seats comfortable and plenty of room and cafe on board served very nice coffee at reasonable price. Will definitely travel again by Eurostar

It's actually worse than Deutsche Bahn! The Eurostar was untimely - not in Germany, but only in Belgium! - and lacks various comfort features:- Little legroom, an ICE is much more comfortable- Very poor Wi-Fi, practically unusable- Announcement so quietly that nothing is understood- There is no reasonable catering (contrary to the announcement on the homepage and in the app), but only unhealthy junk such as chips and hard waffles. The presence of an on-board restaurant must not be relied upon, it is probably a gamble whether the train used has one. The machines installed apparently do not accept German cards, cash insertion is not possible- Constantly interrupts the power supply so that the charging process stops. Surely totally good for the phone battery.- Dirty toilets- nowhere are there waste containersDespite everything, the trains are totally crowded and you wonder why they don’t just run more frequently. A joke in itself is also the boarding process in Paris: Only shortly before the departure is the track announced, then hundreds of people storm onto the platform at the same time and it cuddles massively...Unfortunately, there is no alternative to getting to Paris by train from the Rhineland!

The only public transportation I know that penalizes those who arrive in advance. We arrived 2.5 hours in advance because we needed to pass the Tax Refound. First surprise: You can only enter the queue 2 hours in advance. We wait 30’ and we enter. We stayed one hour in line before the customs. We were only in line for the train at 11:12 and our train was at 12:12. In other words, it did not make sense to arrive sooner. Complete disrespect for children and the elderly. A complete lack of organization, of management.

Eurostar experience was fabulousWe did two cross border trips in Europe We loved every minute of itThe service is second to noneAmazing all round experienceEasy to find your designated seats Well organized crew at every stop And service desk at every major capital city station were so helpful tooComfortable seats, plenty of space and leg room Highly recommend We will be back for more!
Juliana was fantastic. Really took care of our every need and want. Can’t wait to enjoy her service again. We were very well looked after.

Long queues for check-in and very hot. Passport e-gates worked randomly which delayed us getting through. Then the departure lounge was stuffed, no seats, very hot and long queues to get a drink and food. Staff at customer service couldn't answer our basic question about buying Metro tickets on the train (yes you can). For a change Gare du Nord in Paris was a much better experience on the way back.

Avoid Eurostar at all costs. We were told a week before but we ignored the warning and took a train from Rotterdam to London with a transfer in Brussels. We arrived on time at the station but the departure kept getting delayed . When we were on the train it was not clean. We were told during this leg that the next train we had to catch will wait for us in Brussels. Everyone rushed to customs entrance to line up only to be told that it had departed and we would have to wait2hrs for the next train. They announced we would get a food voucher to compensate. Well we had our turn at the counter and the man just handed us the new tickets and no voucher , he just called the next person in line. We paid for our own food while we waited and then were told to board . Again everyone lined up only to be told to wait 5 mins, then another 5 mins , then 15 mins. In the end we stood in que 40mins before we could board.Again a dirty train and the air conditioning was not working well.Then we waited 20mins toget moving as they announced they didn’t have permission to travel yet.We arrived 3 hrs late and behind schedule , it means we had to drive in peak hour traffic.Very Disappointed. The worst part was that the  lady behind us catches it regularly and said it is the same every time she travels,  it’s normal? Next time best to fly .

Eurostar is fine. Some seats aren't so roomy but overall it's better than flying! Brexit has slowed down the process. It was very efficient in the UK but in the Paris it seemed like organised chaos. We arrived in the queue at 2:45 for 4:12 train and made it onto the train about 8 minutes before scheduled departure. There appeared to be no logic as to the queue shifting and staff did little to communicate. You just constantly felt like everyone was moving along faster. I personally started to feel a bit faint as we hadn't expected to be in the queue that long. But I have to say while I didn't understand the logic, there was no point in complaining, I've never missed a Eurostar train because of the security process. But I do have to call out one ridiculous passenger. Part of the obvious challenge was that at the hour we were travelling there were A LOT of families with babies, infants and young children. All of which slow down the process. One woman in the security queue was huffing and puffing that if they made her take her baby out of the pram she would refuse to get on the train. (wish she had). On the train she was rather loudly proclaiming that Eurostar staff have no clue and had no customer service abilities as they had made her take her baby out of the pram. Dear lady, it's for all of our safety. People take note. FRANCE has raised the TERROR alert to its highest. The Olympics are starting. The day this woman was ranting was the first round of ELECTIONS. There were different levels of security walking the train stations from armed national guard to security etc. To keep everyone safe, NOBODY gets special treatment. I'm sure a crying baby is a minor inconvenience in the grand scheme of keeping all of us safe. So while she thinks because the people at security let her baby stay in the pram in London doesn't make them right - it means they were less vigilant. And as a mother, I'm abhorred by people who are so selfish when travelling. This woman was also complaining that Eurostar is awful because they sold all the seats and everything was too crowded. Seriosusly, this lady had no sense at all. She's going on about Eurostar being a monopoly (she should read up on the history of how the tunnel came to be). Anyway, obviously it's convenient for passengers when things are less crowded but it makes no business sense NOT to sell as many seats as possible! Also there are other ways to get from London to Paris - on Eurostar you can PAY to have more space in Standard Premier or Business. And if that doesn't appease you, you can take a plane which will be far more inconvenient than the Eurostar security. Or you can take a ferry and other modes of transportation including driving or taking other trains. But there's no way to avoid immigration and security. I've taken Eurostar countless times from London to Paris and back since 2007. It's the fastest and most efficient way form city centre to city centre.

I had booked a seat on the Eurostar from Brussels to London.We departed one hour late.There was no catering on board.Nothing moved in the cues.No announcements were made structurally.When we were finally waiting in the waiting area, all of a sudden the crowd moved through the shopping area to board. Not the slightest announcement was made still. The security agents spoke French only.Once on board, the train responsible, a certain Simon, addressed his messages in French and occasionally in English with a strong accent. Not one single word in Flemish/Dutch (which is by the way the most spoken language in Belgium).A caricature of Belgian servicing and a shameful image for foreigners.Please recruit Professionals and communicate professionally in the future to avoid such a bad experience!
Station is very clean and safe.  Eurostar cabins are comfortable and there are food and drink available as well as many bathrooms.  Would recommend for your travel needs.

Our train was cancelled at very short notice. We were initially directed to the next departure, felt though if all five in the family would get seats when our tickets were not updated. Shortly before this departure, the train is cancelled and we are directed to another company's departure to Brussels and from there continue to Paris. That train is becoming overcrowded and a considerable police force is being called in to evict all Eurostar passengers who have been informed in writing to take this train. Again, reference is made to a later departure and then overnight stay in Brussels. Never again Eurostar!

The worst experience you could imagine,our trip to Amsterdam 2.5 hours late.We are now turning around and told we have make our own way to Amsterdam from Rotterdam, beyond a joke,just dumped in the middle of nowhere.

Literally THE WORST. The train got delayed 2 hours and a half. Communication was poor to non-existent. We had to wait "in line", meaning all cramped together in the heat with no information whatsoever. Because of this delay, we lost a whole day in London and all the tickets we had for activities. The management at the Paris train station was mediocre and disorganized.
My family and I took the Eurostar train from London to Paris through the chunnel.  This was a fast and efficient way to travel.
Great first experience on Eurostar check in straight forward. The train was clean and tidy fast and effiecient way to travel to Europe much more relaxed than flying.

Used Eurostar from St Pancras for first time. Great experience.  Security checks and passport control well organised and quick, unlike airport security.  Train was clean and comfy. Looking forward to an opportunity to use Eurostar again!
Terrible, clowns, unprofessional, rubbish, ridiculous, disrespectful, without credibility, shit, rotten, rubbish

I booked a comfort ticket with the option to change the ticket (free of charge) as long as I can do it one hour before the train departure. 1,5 hours before departure, I tried to do it online, impossible. Tried to do it in the office, they told me to go to the train.  The train manager, was in a bad mood and charged me 50 € or I stay in the station. My surprise was that the train had several (really several) seats available, so there was not shortage of places. Why paying a much more comfort ticket? What about the misleading information in the ticket booking? Very disappointed with Eurostar and Thalys, I will consider other traveling arrangements from now on.

Terrible customer service. Denied boarding without reason with reference to "rules" (even though I clearly followed ALL rules as stipulated on the website). Incompetent and unhelpful customer service employees (for example, Daniel from Brussels). If you ever need anything from them, best to avoid this Eurostar at all

A great experience with the help of good people: I want to thank the Eurostar company and its employees and the security workers on both the French side and English side of Gare de Lion North. We took the 9:12 train from Paris to London. We passed all the passport checks and the security, and my husband Eli realized that he did not have  his cellphone. I called his cell and surprisingly it was not in the deep pocket of the bag but in someone’s hands. And he replied. It was the taxi driver who was standing outside the station where he dropped us off. Eli talked to the security people and immediately someone walked with him through the English passport and French passport controls. He found the taxi driver and went back through the two passport controls and security.Another official woman was walking among the standing passengers and asked who was waiting for the 9:12 train. At this very moment my husband came back through security. She transferred us to another official person to show us the path to the train. When we came to our coach, number 11, there was standing the same pleasant person that checked us when we boarded the train three days prior. It was a great experience to have security people so helpful, and I want to thank them for doing a great job.

I travelled from St Pancras to Brussels today, and due to excessive delays in the ticketing and passport checks in the past I was there when checkin opened for my train. There was no queue after all of the checks I was met with a crammed full departure lounge, no seats and almost no standing room.The information on the timing of the trains was very last minute and meant that no one had a clue how long to boarding, when their train would leave.In terms of running a railway Amateur Hour would be my summary. Treat your passengers with respect and give them information that is real and credible.Eurostar is definitely not a nice experience in the departure hall.The actual train journey was very comfortable, allowing me to relax after the 2.5 hour wait to leave in St Pancras.

Environmentally friendly it maybe, but a lousy experience. Crowded waiting room - highly unfriendly and aggressive  immigration staff  - uncomfortable seating - awful food.  As bad as any airport.  Our first - and last time travelling Eurostar!
Wait times are terrible. Swimming is better than the Eurostar. They cannot handle the crowds going thru security etc. Be prepared to stand .

Disgusted and disappointed! Eurostar cancelled my train 10 before departure! Because of the short notice I can’t get refunds on the tours I rebooked!! I’ve been planning this trip for weeks!! Shame on you Eurostar!!

Very arrogant staff at the baggage screening desk.A staff who looked like an Indian was behaving as if he owned the Eurostar.just finding fault with whatever we did .I felt  he was trying to showoff his position which he thought was superior.Shame on him.It was his job to clear the empty trays and he had the audacity to tell me to clear them if I wanted my bag.Never again will I travel by eurostar.wish I could give zero rating

Morning train from Paris to London delayed 55 minutes. The prior train departed almost 90 minutes late. Boarding was very stressful. Our seats were purchased together but they were not honored because of the delay. Instead Eurostar had free boarding which means every person fends for herself/himself. So, our family of 7 was forced to split into seats in  three separate cars. I did not expect Eurostar to be so far off schedule and service to be so poor. I hope I will be able to avoid Eurostar in the future.

Not good. The journey out from London was fine but the facilities are minimal. However Paris Gare du Nord was chaotic, staff were inefficient and rude. They need more signs to keep customers updated eg boarding pass check coming up. They certainly need customer service training. Awful experience- and I note that they rarely bother to respond to reviews. My advice: let the plane take the strain

Technical delay!!Ridiculous! One of the worst managed train services in the world! The entire management board at Eurostar should be terminated!! They do not know how to manage a train service. Utter disgrace

It’s fast! Nice way to travel. Down side…the advertised fares turned out to be higher than advertised (depends on your travel date and time, so double check). The food on board was good but VERY expensive. Also, the seats could use a shampooing.

Eurostar should be an excellent service. Everything is going for it. In comparison to flying to and from UK airports from Brussels, it’s a no brainer. And yet, it consistently fails to achieve its potential. The trains are filthy, the service is regularly delayed and disrupted and passengers are treated with utter contempt. The Eurostar hub in Brussels is a disgrace. After the overhaul, the majority of space was dedicated to a so-called duty free retail outlet that is outrageously overpriced. In the tight space for over 700 passengers there are two dispensing machines that are always out of order. In the old days, there was a cafe and bar with a bit of food , coffee and a final Belgian beer. It’s an insult to fare paying passengers. And to cap it all, the fares are constantly on the rise. Come on Eurostar. You really can do better!

Quick and easy transition through passport control in London. The area we waited in to board our train to Paris was extremely crowded. But we didn’t wait long until boarding and our train to Paris was fantastic.

If you want to walk across from kings cross station and into st pancreas and onto a train to Paris or Amsterdam, instead of the trek to the airport and get there 3 hours early then this is it. Clear Uk and Paris immigration right after you scan your bags - then buy some euros and wait for your platform to be announced - Amsterdam in 4 hours, Paris in 2. It’s a breeze!

Return trip from St Pancras to Brussels, and it was effortless and smooth. Our seats had uk plugs and we visited the cafe. All the staff were so friendly.  I cannot praise the Eurostar staff in Brussels enough they explained we could use our tickets on the train to take us into the centre. They also exchanged our tickets on the return as we missed our train, free of charge. The whole experience exceeded my expectations and so much easier than flying..

This is unforgivable.Hello, today I am writing my opinion on basic Eurostar.
