I am not the type of person who is the type to write opinions but hey, it was necessary because after having paid full price for my Eurostar return tickets like everyone else, we stops me because supposedly they think I'm going there to do dirty things, in short I don't need to specify just because I have 2 big bags and I'm a foreigner they stop you for nothing so that you miss your eurostar and like that you pay 50€ more fortunately there was someone who knew how to speak French so I didn't pay anything extra because it's serious it's a sketch in short be careful if you are foreigners because we will surely arrest you because you have the misfortune olalala of looking like a thief dealer how to turn your trip into a nightmare for your whole family who are dying of worry 0 compensation of course "screw yourself" I had a premium seat I find myself in standard in the next train because "why did you miss the other train" but you're srx where you're really cool idiots eh come on the sketch is over it was funny to make fun of me and Well, let's show you.Kind regards, A former loyal customer.

Outbound service from St Pancras to Gare do Nord was excellent. My wife is a wheelchair user and we had booked premier Business class tickets. At St Pancras we were met by a customer assistant who took us through to the departure lounge, and then we were boarded before the main group of passengers. All very efficient and friendly.By contrast at Gare du Nord on the return journey the experience was less impressive. - We couldn't go through to the departure lounge when we arrived (we were a bit early admittedly, but would have thought a wheelchair user would have been permitted)- We waited nearly 30 mins in the assistance area for someone to "confirm that there would be a lift to get us onto the train", why was it necessary to keep us there as Eurostar already knew we had a wheelchair and which seats we were in??- eventually I had to insist that we be allowed to go through to the lounge that we had paid for as my wife needed to use the toilet - even though this was "against procedure"- the lounge itself was almost empty (why couldn't we have been admitted when we first arrived?) and the food / snacks underwhelming (croissants available in St Pancras, but not Paris!)- the final straw was Eurostar not loading any food onto the train so we didn't get the meal that is part of the package. On-board staff said we would get a refund from Eurostar, but nothing happened until I contacted Eurostar, and even then we were only offered an e-voucher which we would be highly unlikely to use (seems this is standard Eurostar Ts & Cs - very difficult to get a meaningful refund ).I have had good experiences travelling to Brussels on Eurostar in the past and would like to use the train more for travel, but was not impressed by this experience.

Amsterdam station seems to have made the distance to the platform as far as they can. Then the actual platform is very long. The Waiting are is poor and yesterday had only one functioning lavatory for male and one for female.. That is just one cubicle for a potential 1000+ passengers.  Very limited refreshments available ! Not enough seats!  Tatty and not properly clean. The station has hardly any level paving and so using a wheeled case is very difficult.   Limited lifts so cases have to taken on escalators the occasional one falling from an old person's grip down to the bottom. Where there is  level paving, special strips have been laid to halt the easy path of a wheeled case.  After to lack of decent snacks in the waiting room, join the train to find just as little at very inflated prices.   Also found the same seats double booked !   Fortunately there were two spares available,. Arrival at St Pancras the way out seems to have been selected to give maximum excercise off walking after sitting still.   Not a good experience.
Bad sevice never on time, had to wait half way through the trip for  hoursbecause of some unknown reason, they didnt explain what the actual problem is just made us wait for hours

Another fantastic trip with Eurostar!We travelled as a group of 7 adults, all of which have various disabilities and I'm a wheelchair user.As usual the Eurostar team were faultless on their assistance and customer service. It couldn't have gone better (other than the toilet breaking half way home)

I have taken the Eurostar from Paris to London and back more than a dozen times in the last one year. Finally had enough with Eurostar trashy service to overcome the inertia of writing a review. Was denied boarding on Business Premier when I scanned my boarding pass at 1516 hours at the St Pancraa gates. Called the staff over and the time showed 1517 hours on my iPhone. Staff said gates closed 20 min before departure. Wasn't it ten minutes for Business Premier I said? Checked the website and it turns out the cut off is now changed recently to 15 minutes. Asked the staff if they could let me through as my wife had just entered a couple minutes before me. Staff refused and walked away, ignoring my pleas for assistance. Lots of poor service here. No clear updates from Eurostar wjebever they changed their business premier check in times. Then even if it were 15 min, the staff could easily have let me through at 14 min but clearly loved the power tripping. Also, I would not be as annoyed if not for the fact that multiple Eurostar trains I were on in the last year had to stop on the tracks midway for more than 30 min, bunching up my onwards schedule. No compensation from Eurostar, just th usual apologies for th delay. But one minute after the cut off time and all the power tripping absurdity. Not the first power tripping rubbish I had at Eurostar. On another trip from Paris to London, I was stopped by a Karenish British lady at the security checks who hollered at me. My crime? Not stopping and standing still (in her ridiculous words) and replying her (like some high school kid I guess) when she asked me what passport mine was. Answered her but continued walking and apparently that was a really bad thing to do.

Great ride from London to Paris. Business class is the way to go. Very organized and easy if you travel business class. It’s worth the extra money. No crowds.  Private dining in the train station. Food and drinks in the train car.

I was travelling with my son from Paris to London using a voucher from my previous trip which had been delayed by a few hours because of strike action.A couple of hours before our trip, we had a message that there was an IT problem with a supplier and our train was likely to be delayed.  There were huge queues again with people trying to get through security with the limited number of Eurostar staff doing their best to keep the queue moving and organised, whilst keeping people updated. After two and a bit hours queuing we got up the stairs and were able to join the next queue to get through security.  Once we did that, we got to the departure area.  There are duty free shops and a couple of cafes, but given we were a couple of hours late by this stage some of the shops were closing and the cafes were low on stock.  We got on the train - the carriages are spacious and comfortable with chargers available by each seat - and headed to the cafe.  Again, there was almost no stock and no hot foods, sandwiches or baguettes available, so we were limited to a packet of crisps and a chocolate bar.  There is wifi on board but it's slow and frequently almost unusable. The service was quick and efficient when it did move and the arrival into London was smooth and we were quickly through arrivals. I know that neither delay I experienced was directly because of Eurostar, but the processes for dealing with the delay are poor and stressful for those waiting.  The long queues often filled with children on their way to and from Disney make it hard for passengers to use toilets if travelling alone with children, and no water or other refreshments are offered during the delay.  The staff work hard to keep passengers up to date and what to do, but there are not enough staff to do that and signage is not clear in these situations.  The actual service is great when it works, but delays are too common.
Just queued over 30 minutes for a coffee many things sold out.  One person serving the whole train. 2 bars but only one open. For the price they should be bringing it to your seats.

Amazing experience for wheelchair travel! I am a wheelchair passenger and just wanted to say how grateful I am to have the Eurostar to facilitate my travel needs. You have the most competent staff on the phone lines who handled my booking with ease, as I had not booked a wheelchair ticket originally. These days, customer service is no longer a priority with jobs being off shored, frustrating the customer experience which is why I am so impressed. The the entire service when onboarding was great. Typically waiting in tight queues is a source of anxiety which is why I was very happy with the attentiveness of staff to get to through the check in process efficiently. It's comforting to know I can count on Eurostar as flying is simply not an option as they are ill-equipped to deal with electric wheelchairs and the whole process is laborious and really taxing. I cannot stress how easy and enjoyable the entire process is

Rate 1 or 0Eurostar is the worst possible way to travel to France or UK. Crowds of people, confused staff, hours of waiting in lines, elderly people and children standing for 3 hours without water or access to toilets in France. If you want to experience chaos, travel with Eurostar. All this because some underpaid employees deliberately delay passenger check-ins. Eurostar should compensate for the service - I do not recommend it. Punctual trains with delays of 4-5 hours joke.

Horrible and fine print rules that hold them unaccountable or understanding of anything for their customer.  As a first time (and last time) rider, I booked from Paris to London round trip for me and my husbands 14th year wedding anniversary. Due to delays on the metro I showed up just inside of their fine print 45 mins arrival before departure to board my train that was still in dock.  Had to pay $124 to change my two tickets to the next train. Then on return train they were late in leaving by an hour for the train before ours causing us to be 16 mins late getting back to Paris.  Me and my husband with his bad knees had to RUN through the metro to try to catch any train to get back to our night plans and hotel before we’d have to buy another day pass on the metro.  Then when I wrote Eurostar, they didn’t offer anything for our horrible experience. Nothing …not even accountability of their own lateness.  I will not be a repeat return business for them.

On returning from a day trip to Amsterdam on May 23rd our train came to a halt outside Rotterdam. After a few hours we were then transferred across the track to an adjacent train and shuttled to Rotterdam. An announcement was made on this train to seek advice from the NS (Dutch railways) counter at Rotterdam. On arrival at Rotterdam the counter was closed. Station staff at Rotterdam were disinterested in our plight saying it was a Eurostar problem and nothing to do with them. Around 400 people were left stranded at Rotterdam Central at 1 1pm at night with no help or advice. Those with internet access were sent an e-mail telling them to rebook on a subsequent service, however the site was down and they couldn't do so. There were no staff or representatives present to advise or assist their stranded passengers. We were not keen on spending the night on a station with many down and outs and drug users about so decided to head to the Hoek and try to return by ferry. We were fortunate in not having any luggage and for many people this wasn't an option. We managed to find a hotel in the Hoek and return to England by ferry. Only a fraction of those who stayed at Rotterdam were able to get a place on the first train in the morning and faced a disjointed journey after spending a rather unpleasant night on a station populated by many undesirables.   Trying to recoup the additional expenditure incurred and a refund on the service they failed to provide is also becoming a pain with their website sending you round in ever increasing circles leading to a dead end. The customer "care" Ashford phone number on the Eurostar site is 'no longer recognised' and a visit to St.Pancras in person only results in staff advising you to claim online. Even Ryanair and Easyjet don't treat their passengers this disgracefully and they're faster and cheaper. EUROSTAR ? NEVER AGAIN !!!

following on from my own and many others) customer reviews - fairly awful overall - I really wonder what the point is in providing feed back, since there is never any improvement. the seats remain the same, hard in all types of tickets including Business Premier, few bits of reading material, the food gets worse and worse ( shame on you Raymond Blanc for calling a congealed mass 'fine dining") the departure lounges are overcrowded, staff not particularly competent .This is for near 1000 popguns return London to France
We are still entitled to a refund for a ticket but the customer service does not respond or writes to us that we should contact customer service - a disaster for this company

I have been a few times on the Eurostar and it’s a wonderful fast way to travel. This time we started in London and went economy class to Paris. Quick trip. Smooth ride. No delays. You can pre order what kind of meal. We ordered vegetarian. On our return we went standard premium so we had a meal and sat in a quieter carriage. Delicious meal, lovely man serving food and the carriage was less busy. Was a lovely way to travel. Book tickets in advance to get the best rate.

I recently caught the Eurostar with my sister. We travelled on economy London to Paris and premium economy Paris to London. Economy is great - clean, comfortable seats, charging ports and lovely clean spacious bathrooms.The premium economy comes with a meal which was super delicious- we were quite surprised! It’s also quieter in there.Overall a fabulous way to travel and super easy going through security on both the English and French side!

I only travel by this means because my husband loves trains. I'd rather fly if given the choice. However, this was the route for our group rail excursion. That said, the very early mornings to catch an early morning train to Paris leaves one weary.By the time you get through security and wait in a packed waiting room without sufficient seating or services, heating up and then having to rush on board a train that is usually just sitting there is unnecessary. There definitely needs to be an expansion of the lounge area and services offered. The time for our boarding announcement came and went and then we were told that the train would be late due to a technical issue. We ended up leaving late and then missed our connection to Barcelona. We then had to get new tickets to Perpignan and then a coach. This ended up being a very long day thanks to this delay and we didn't get into our hotel in Spain until minutes to midnight. The Eurostar service in reverse is honestly no better. The moving escalator was not working and so we had a very very long walk along the platform to our coach. Revamp is needed all around.
Extra space,which is nice , but the foods not 5* awful !  Went to the cafe to buy a panni ,  but they sold out 🤬🥲 . That’s all I have to say , but says I need to write minimum words
Abysmal.  Train arrived at Lille 90 minutes late.  No one in the locked Eurostar office at Lille.  Missed connection for onward train.  No compensation.

Comfortable and clean ride, except for the prices that cost more than a flight journey would. You can expect arrival/departure to be on time/delayed by hours, same as flights. The security and immigration check queues at St. Pancras International can be organized in a better way to avoid clutter.

I booked a train/hotel deal for Paris. Its my sons 4th birthday and mummy wanted us to celebrate with a weekend to Paris. It cost £340 per person, Mum, Dad, Child, £340 each. Booked it. Hotel told me we all have to share one bed. Complained and they said to speak to Eurostar. Eurostar said there was some small print on payment page to say children don't get their own bed. They said the per person price doesn't mean per person it means the full price devided by total of travellers. Ive had to pay an additional £100 for my sons bed. Eurostar Customer Care told me, if you don't like it, cancel your trip and you can have a voucher not a refund. Its a little boys 4th birthday, you money hungry monsters.

My wife and I are travelling around Europe for 6 weeks and this was definitely an easy way to get from London to Paris. Heaps of friendly staff to get tickets scanned and passports stamped and then boarding was simple and easy. Train left right on time and there was plenty of storage for large suitcases on a storage rack and also backpacks, handbags on shelves above the seats. There was also an onboard cafe where the food was good. At this cafe you could purchase metro tickets for Paris to save time. We had a great experience on the Eurostar!
Easy, direct, the way to travel between Lille and London. Really easy to do and if you choose your tickets well, not too pricey.

Dreadful! Whilst in the tunnel, we lost power and sat intermittently in the dark and without aircon. The whole time with no information apart from 1 or 2 very basic (text book/robotic) apologies over the intercom. When we finally made it out the tunnel, we then had to wait 1 hour on the train for the replacement train. There was an offer of…. Water…. And yet again no information. The changeover of trains is where I lost my patience, carrying very heavy luggage, we were swept up by a crowd leaving the train station as there were no attendants to direct us to the new train. My 11 year old daughter and I were in the car park before we realised we had gone wrong.Another hour waiting on the new train and we are finally en route to Paris. I wouldn’t be surprised if their compensation is no more than £50 per person (Eurostar vouchers!) I will not be travelling with the Eurostar in a hurry again!
The whole journey ran like clockwork.  All facilities were as expected.  Reasonable value for money.  I would recommend the service.

We travelled business premier back from Paris to London on 5th May on the 18.12. The srevice on the train was excellent and  we must thank Morgan and Victor in particular. Nothing was too much trouble and they were both professional and welcoming and had a great sense of humour which really added to our return journey and made it a fun and relaxing experience. The drink quality was exceelent as was the food we were served which came as a welcome surprise. We will be travelling business premier again!! Thank you.

After flying in Heathrow, our driver took us to St. Pancras train station to board for a delightful trip to Paris.  As always, it is an efficient, lovely way to travel and arrive refreshed after a delicious on board lunch. Once at Gare du Nord, be advised there is construction on the adjacent streets so be prepared for a longer walk to the taxi stand.

If I could leave a zero I would.  Absolutely embarrassing!I booked two tickets for my mum and I, my first time using so I had to make an account, I put all my details and her details into the system, few days later I download the tickets and they're both under my name?? So I call up and ask to check because I input her details and they said the ticket must have automatically updated itself when I made the account to both being my name so I asked for a name change and they told me that because I made an account I can't change it and I'll have to just waste the ticket or use it for a different day!?! I asked if they had a name change policy and they said yes they do, it's £15 to change the name and you can do it up to 7 days before you depart but I can't have one because I registed an account. Absolute scam!!!

Purchased first class seats & received less than coach. Before getting on I went to the help desk to make sure the amount of luggage I had was ok. She said it was fine no problem at all. Well I go with my family to get on and there was absolutely no space for our luggage. We had people in our assigned seats. The woman seemed like she spoke English until I said your in our seats (there was no more available). She turned away and ignored me. There was no other options but to sit on the floor, the stairs, and one like jump seat that folded up along with all my luggage. Wendy (Eurostar employee on the train) asked for my tickets (3rd time I was asked) & said it wasn’t safe to sit the way we were. I explained the situation yet again (a manager was suppose to come help with the situation- never did). So Wendy went to talk to the family. Their response was “I have kids & a lot of luggage”. So while I was asked three separate times for my tickets, I never saw anyone ask the family to see theirs. No idea if they had any first class seats or just purchased for the parents and allowed the other 4 children to sit?? Not sure. They all got breakfast, coffee, whatever- I was never even asked. What I got was a seat that had actual poop on the back, a horrible view of the smelly bathroom, and a kid that vomitted on the floor inches away from me. I did message Eurostar…. Absolutely nothing back. They act like they are better than the rest but this absolutely was the worst experience I’ve ever had on a train. I feel I’m well traveled & have been on tons of trains. Never had such an experience like this before. I purchased the first class seats because I had too much luggage. We’ve been traveling for 5 weeks at this point & had purchased 2 new large luggage to accommodate all of our purchases. I will never use Eurostar again willingly. I paid almost €500 for these first class seats when I could have paid €189 for coach.
Awful customer service. Staff are not help at all. Travelled on May 2024, bad experience getting tickets and checking in.

We travelled from London to Amsterdam on a train and hotel package with business premier tickets. The facilities and service at St Pancras and on the train were excellent and we thoroughly enjoyed the first part of our journey. Unfortunately at Brussels there was a problem and after being held for ages were told we couldn’t continue for “operational reasons” and everyone was ordered off the train and just told to get the next one. There was no help or assistance. After several platform changes which are problem when you are travelling with a disabled person with mobility problems, the train arrived and everyone was told we were not allowed on and staff aggressively blocked anyone from getting on. They told us they couldn’t help, we were on our own and we just had to go to the Eurostar desk. Obviously a train full of angry passengers meant it was chaos at the desk and no help anyway, we were told we had to arrange getting booked on another train ourselves. Instead of enjoying ourselves in Amsterdam we wasted hours of our holiday stuck in Brussels station. I understand problems can and do happen, but to not have a comprehensive recovery procedure, clearly communicated to both passengers and staff, with full support for passengers is completely unacceptable. Despite the train being initially being labelled as cancelled, when it comes to compensation they have now reclassified it as only delayed not cancelled. If abandoning a train full of passengers in an entirely different country to the one they paid to get to is not a cancellation, I don’t know what is. On our return 5 days later we were held again at Brussels for over 3 hours. This time entirely beyond Eurostar’s control and we got to stay on the train, but it was an anxious wait fearing history was repeating. I thought travelling by train would be less hassle than flying, it seems not.

Taking their customers for granted, the joy of being a monopoly!Outrageously priced tickets, rude and inconsiderate staff, a point and reward system that changes from one day to another and a stinky lounge! That’s how regular customers are rewarded! After countless disappointments i need to call them out!

Not the best experience:- The train was late departing and arriving.- We were prevented boarding when the train arrived so that it could be cleaned.  An attendant shooed a couple of people out of the train, then left.  No one walked through the car again, ever.  Once the conductor shouted from the end of the train that we could board, we entered to find trash strewn across the floor, empty crisp bags on the tables and general disarray.  Obviously no cleaning was done.- The wc was so small that I had to turn around twice to find a way to open the door so that I could get out.- The café car consisted of a vending machine and four standing tables.- The wi-fi was no more reliable than Amtrak on the Northeast Corridor route.  High latency, low bandwidth, and frequent dropouts.  It disappeared entirely for the last 50km into Rotterdam where it reset once we reached the station there.  It took about an hour to do five minutes of light work that I could have done faster with my phone.- There were times when leaving Amsterdam when the Intercity local train passed the Eurostar.  The Eurostar only gained the advantage when the local train had to stop.  It was a half-hour after departure before the train exceeded 100km/hr.- The experience felt more comparable to Amtrak Acela than to the Shinkansen.  The only point of comparability with the latter is the max speed of the train.
At best staff are indifferent. But mainly rude and why do you they make you check your passport twice?? But you have no choice obviously

Check-in Eurostar to London. Track (3) was open and I was there 45 minutes before departure (surprised that there was no ID check). 20 minutes before departure I was turned away by security (red shirts). They showed the way to the check-in desk. Lady at the reception initially explained to me in French that I was late. I then explained to her in Dutch - although irritated - that I was not late at the track and that I was waiting there quietly. According to the reception lady, who now also spoke Dutch, I was far too rude - in my opinion, just as rude as she was to me.She called the person in charge of Eurostar and gave her an (hyped up) version of the facts in French.The person in charge made it clear to me 1. that I was late 2. that I was lucky that the train was delayed. 3. And instructed baggage control not to let me through UNLESS I HUMBLELY apologized to her colleague.I had to do that twice - for this power-hungry lady (Eurostar manager) and the first reception lady. The way in which the person in charge spoke to me very loudly and made HUMBLE apologies twice - even stunned the people at the baggage check (they even felt sorry...).I'm lucky that I get to travel...on Eurostar.And at Brussels South station I would recommend CLEARLY reporting to the EUROSTAR platform that you are allowed on here without checking in - why not just close this platform in advance?Next time I'll take the plane againto London from a friendly airport?And I recommend that Eurostar teach its staff how to deal with a well-founded complaint.

A Bucket List birthday present - careful what you wish for. Starting with the lifting your own suitcases onto the security trays followed by the horrible experience in the waiting area where there were not enough seats with people packed in like sardines. Then the joy, approx. 15 minutes before departure when they announce the “gate” which instigates a huge rush as people push and shove to get up the travelator first. Once on the train ( we travelled Standard Premium ) the seats were fine and you get some refreshments but it’s all a bit basic for the cost.. overall not the quality experience I had expected for the price. Why you would prefer that instead of flying in terms of total time and cost I really don’t know.

The staff called Summer and Laqueta are absolutely rude set of people.Having people like this on thr Frontline is a disgrace to Eurostar.They made me look like I was a fool and told lies to their manager just because I said I didn't want a rude member of their staff jointly dealing with me.Avoid these 2 staff..Shame on this carrier .

I’d rather not fly, so this was a good option for me. Expensive at $90/person one way to Lille in a standard seat. The standard seat was fine, the trip took about 1.5 hours, though once is enough. Lots of empty seats, so maybe last minute fares are the way to go. 20 minutes under the channel can be nerve racking for some.

This was our first trip abroad together since my diagnosis 2 years ago and my first on Eurostar. The thought of travelling anywhere new is not something I look forward to these days, with the physical limitations of my condition and all its side effectsMy partner (carer) and I decided to travel by Eurostar, as I no longer feel comfortable flying with all its restrictions and the train goes directly from London to Amsterdam. Plus, my luggage needs are not small anymore with the extra clothes, incontinence supplies and various safety items I know need to travel with, but luckily, we managed to squeeze it all into a single large suitcase. We spoke to Eurostar passenger assistance to establish what type of assistance we could get on our journey. They were very quick and helpful in explaining what they can provide in the UK and what to expect at other stations in Europe - which is a big difference, and I had a dedicated person that answered all my questions in the many emails that followedThe upshot was that the only assistance we can get at Amsterdam Centraal station is a wheelchair lift if I take my own wheelchair. Given that there is very limited assisted help in Amsterdam, we decided to be brave and go it aloneWhilst my mobility is not good - I cannot walk safely without assistance and rest stops, I am not yet dependent on a wheelchair, so had already decided I would tackle this holiday on 2 legs rather than 2 wheelsWe also decided to pay the extra for Business Premium, in the hope this would reduce the amount of queuing/standing and allow access to seated lounges at both ends. Also, rather than try to travel across London to St Pancras on the same day, it would be easier to split this outward journey over 2 days and stay at the Premier Inn at St Pancras the night before our Eurostar outbound journey. And I hoped the added champagne/food on board would help make our journey more romantic for my partnerWe arrived on the day much earlier than we needed to, after a slow walk from the Hotel to the check-in desks, having already scoped out the layout of the station the night before. The Eurostar staff on the Business Premier check-in were super helpful and allowed us through straight away it was then quick and easy going through security and both border controls (much easier and quicker than an airport)We then stepped into the departure lounge and it hit home how glad we were to have upgraded to Business Premier as the departure lounge was completely rammed everywhere. This made moving to the Business lounge - which is to your right after you clear border control, a little challenging but once we entered the lounge the helpful Eurostar staff explained the layout of the lounge and found us some seats for me to recover and my partner to enjoy the complimentary food/drink. We arrived in the lounge just before 10 am hoping for some breakfast but unlike airport lounges, there was no hot food just a limited range of cold snacks - like a continental breakfast, along with different hot/cold beveragesOur train boarding was announced 20 minutes before departure and we made our way back out into the general departure lounge which seemed even busier. With each train holding 800+ passengers and multiple trains leaving so closely the number of people and all their luggage reaches a big number very quicklyWhat we had not thought about and so not planned for, was the location of our coach on the train, I spent a long time selecting the right seats for both journeys but neglected to consider the coach number. On a standard Eurostar train Business Premier coaches are at either end of the train with everything else in between and these trains are very long. Also, coach numbering does not always indicate the direction of travel nor always start at 1 in EuropeYou guessed it, our coach was at the front of the train and the ramps/lifts to the platforms above were at the other end of the train. It was a challenge getting onto the platform trying to keep hold of my case whilst going up the travelator – not easy when you have no sense of balance (should have joined the queue for the lift) and then a very stressful trek down the long platform with my partner trying to control 2 suitcases as well as holding onto me, but we just made it before the doors closed and I could now relax for the next 4 hoursThe things that were important to me; the seats were comfortable and though the designated disabled toilet was not near our coach the nearest toilet did have grab handles and was big enough to squeeze 2 people in if needed, which was all I needed. The service and friendliness of the onboard staff were good, and we enjoyed the food (which started once we cleared the channel tunnel), champagne (which started flowing as soon as the train left the station) and views as we sped through Europe until we reached BrusselsWe were stationary at a platform in Brussels station for about an hour, just listening to various onboard announcements telling us the delay was due to a missing member of the crew. Then came another onboard announcement telling us our train was now cancelled and would not continue onto Amsterdam. All passengers were to disembark with all their belongings onto the platform and wait for the next train.Referring back to the earlier mention of the advice given 'to travel in my own wheelchair' - if we had there was no one left on the train or platform from Eurostar to help get off the train so I might have easily been stuck, but luckily, we managed with the help of other passengers to disembark onto the platform with all our luggageThere then followed what can only be described as something out of a comedy sketch, as we were all repeatedly sent to the wrong platforms over the next hour - again none of which were easy to navigate to and from, only to finally be on the right platform as another Eurostar train pulled bound for Amsterdam Centraal but no one was allowed to board the trainStill no sight of any Eurostar staff, it was left to Brussels security to deal with a now increasingly angry group of about 200 passengers. We were all finally told - by a helpful Brussels ticket inspector, to go to the Eurostar desk on the station concourseBy the time my partner located and I made the journey to the Eurostar desk the queues were very long as everyone tried to find out how to continue their journeys. Whilst queuing, other passengers began to share the current info they got at the front of the queue, and it became apparent there was no replacement train only a few spare tickets still available on later Eurostar trains which were being grabbed by everyoneBy the time we realised this, we looked at the ticket availability - using our phone, on later trains and managed to book 2 new tickets on a much later Eurostar train heading to Amsterdam Centraal, but we had nearly 4 hours to wait for the train, so in desperate need to find somewhere to recover we headed for the Eurostar lounge to hopefully find somewhere to sit, relax and recoverWe encountered our first member of Eurostar staff at the lounge front desk, and after explaining to him what had happened, he very kindly allowed us entry despite our new ticket departure time being well outside of the lounge entry rules - thank you, kind sir, you will never know much this very little concession made so much difference to usThe trip to and from the station/lounge is not an easy one for anyone with disabilities, due to the excessive use of cobbles and high curbs, but we made it back to the station to meet the 20:22 to Amsterdam CentraalThankfully the Brussels station staff we encountered back at the station, were extremely helpful in making sure we got to the right platform and more importantly the correct position on the platform to board our coach (I learnt from earlier) and our journey continued onwards - only lacking in the champagneWe finally arrived at Amsterdam Centraal at 22:30 feeling very exhausted and weary and you guessed it a long slow trek down a very long platform in the darkOur accommodation - which we also booked through Eurostar, was excellent and despite the terrible weather, we both had a lovely stay having put all our travel woes behind us - so we thought...The journey home started OK having learnt a lot about how to make sure you are at the correct platform location for your coach, which thankfully was at the same end as the boarding gatesFinding the Eurostar terminal at Amsterdam Centraal is a little bit of a challenge, given that unlike St Pancras the station wasn’t built with the service in mind. You have to go through the gate line at the station and up to platform 15b. Once level with the trains you need to trek all the way down the platform until you see the Eurostar building at the very end of the platformSecurity and board control are immediately as you enter, with fast-track on the left. If it is raining, and there is a queue, you will get wet. Once past security you go past Dutch and British board control, before being ejected into the departure lounge. This is for ALL passengers – there is no Business Premier lounge located this side of security, the lounge is on the opposite side of the station next to platform 2, which means you have to navigate multiple lifts/escalators along with all your luggage and allow enough time to go through security and border control - not something I was willing to try given our luck on the outbound journey. As the Eurostar terminal is built on one of the platforms the lounge is very long and thin. Your only food and drink options are these vending machines and an out-of-service coffee machine. Note that you cannot leave the terminal until it is time to board the train.A small observation/question - why are all the passenger departure lounges so small at all the stations we visited on this trip; none seem to have anywhere near the 800+ seats needed for just one full trainThe journey started well until we got to Belgium - again! And the train in front of us broke down and we were again stuck albeit just outside Brussels this time!Our previous journey experiences came flashing back to us, initially thinking we would face the same problems, but no not this time, as we had a Eurostar train manager on board who came around and spoke to everyone, explaining in person what the issue was, that we needed to reverse our train back to the previous station, then take an alternative route to Brussels. This turned out not to be quick nor easy and took 3 hours before we were finally able to leave Brussels station, but we were kept refreshed and fed throughout, and more importantly no tour of Brussels station againUnlike last time it was a great comfort to experience a level of service we would expect on such a journey and despite arriving back in London 3 hours later than expected I was mentally and physically up for the long trek all the way down the platform - yet again!I have learnt a lot from this first trip on Eurostar - not least to be better prepared regarding the coach we choose our seats in and maybe not be so quick to not accept some assistance at the stations it is available atUpdate: Having contacted Eurostar about our travel issues once we got home, they have kindly refunded 50% of both of our tickets on both legs of the journey, as we had been delayed for over 120 minutes on both. Along with also getting a full refund for the additional tickets we had to purchase to continue our outbound journeyThis is not meant as a complaint about our experience on Eurostar but more of an observation of how close things came to going disastrously wrong had we not had the strength, resources (money) and the luck to encounter a few very exceptional members of Eurostar staff at key moments on our journey, and we especially want to draw attention these helpful staffWe will certainly be better prepared should we travel by Eurostar again someday

We had our flight cancelled from London to Paris so had to book last minute on the Eurostar. The only tickets left were Business Premier for the 4 of us. This is the highest service they had and on the site they advertised as a first class service. Let me start from the beginning of our trip and tell you why this is no where near first class. When we arrived at the gate we had to wait a bit to get to the gate as they let you in about 1.5 hours before boarding. When they called us to the gate we asked if there were two lines as we had purchased the business premier, the not so nice women told us there was just one line. As we made our way up in the line i heard another women ask where the BP line was and she was also told there was none and that was only on the train service. when we got a little further in the line my wife noticed some people going through another line with no people, we asked another attendant what that was and she said business premier, we told her that was what we were and she let us under the rope to get in. This was super frustrating and clearly not all attendant's were trained. we did get to the lounge early and it was wonderful, we had some light breakfast and drinks and relaxed, this was the only good part of the trip. since we booked late our grown kids were in different cars than us which was ok however we expected that there would be attendants in BP that would help with baggage, there were none. The bags were packed poorly and some fell down when the train started, for the amount we paid we expected some assistance here. The BP cars looked in need of updating and there were no wireless charge pads like advertised on the website. The food was ok but not as good as advertised either. My son wanted a coke and was told he would have to pay 5 pounds for it, how ridiculous.  we paid roughly 50% more for what we thought was a premium experience but it was far from it. Save your money and go couch and get food from the food car,  not worth the extra money.

We were 30 min in advance and they didn’t even let us check in, the staff was terrible with every customers, they are such a joke, I’ll never forget their pitiful smile when I was crying my eyes out because I had to pay charges to get another ticket, when I could literally see the passengers check in and I could’ve easily went!Also the woman at the ticket reception literally said when I explained to her why I was late, which was for a very unfortunate incident, « aw that’s sweet of you but you could tell me anything and it still wouldn’t change a thing » When people didn’t even change in yet…

I haven't travelled in years and a bit OCD about cleanliness. Yes Eurostar is looking a bit tired, but it's still easier than flying. I went for Business Premier as a treat - yes its pricey, but considering what happened today I am so glad. Outbound to Paris went smoothly (by the way the bathroom in the London lounge is ok - though the Paris ones are nicer). OMG on the way back from Paris to London there was some failure of all the  passport control barriers...delays from 4.30pm onwards, which meant EVERYONE on the 4.30/5.10/6.10pm trains were being held in Gare du Nord for an hour or so. Christ if it wasn't for the Business Premier lounge where you could get a comfy seat, a decent bathroom, free snacks and drinks, I would be totally shredded . The french crew on the train back were so lovely and we got a nice hot meal and plenty of drinks on the journey back to London.  And that is why Business Premier is worth it!

2 hours late on the way out (departure at 11:12 p.m. instead of 9:12 p.m.), 40 minutes late on the way back.Overheated hall at Gare du Nord, no toilet paper, no more catering sales, non-dimmable light in the carriage, no taxi on arrival at Saint Pancras station (12:30 a.m. instead of 10:30 p.m.).Compensation of 25% of the one-way ticket only (€23.50) due to 115 minutes of delay according to customer service (compensation of 50% beyond 120 minutes).

I was a little anxious as I had never been on Eurostar before.I was very pleasantly surprised. The seats are very comfortable and the train is not at all claustrophobic. I was shocked at how quickly the journeys were over. I loved it.

We traveled from Paris to London on the Eurostar, an economic trip under the sea. The trip was very smooth, and the arrangements were surprisingly efficient. This passenger train began operation in 1994; the trip is 50 km (30 miles) between Paris and London.   We traveled First Class; we had a restaurant-standard meal with wine, it was a remarkably good meal. We had previously traveled between England and Europe, traveling between   Dover and Zeebrugge; the Eurostar is far more comfortable than a ferry when you cross the English Channel.

Going LON-PAR wasn't bad....checkin went relatively fast, boarded quickly, Standard Premier was OK.  Food was fine (roll, quinoa/lentil salad with salmon, apple tart for dessert) and trip went quickly.Return (PAR-LON) was a disaster.  Something was happening with the automated passport gates, so most people had to go manual passport checks.  Even then....it was incredibly slow, lots of casual chatter among the passport agents, leisurely placing the passport on the reader, etc.  Train was delayed 30 minutes due to the backlog and I'm not sure everyone even made it.   Meal was OK (cheese bread roll, fresh pineapple, yoghurt).  WIFI is abysmal....cannot stay connected on either side of the Channel.  Standard Premier service was good, attendants were friendly and efficient.  Tea is awful. Not sure it is more efficient than flying and might not bother next time.

Absolutely disappointed with Eurostar's service. While in Paris, we received a sudden notification that our train was canceled, causing immense panic and distress. In a frenzy, we hastily booked a flight back to Bristol, only to receive an email moments later acknowledging their error – our train was never canceled. This gross incompetence cost us precious time, money, and ruined the remainder of our day in Paris. Despite eventually receiving a refund for the return fare, the damage was already done. Our trip was marred by unnecessary stress and uncertainty, leaving us deeply dissatisfied with Eurostar's reliability and customer care. Additionally, we were appalled to witness Eurostar's willingness to leave a disabled man in a wheelchair and his family stranded in Paris with no refund for at least 3 days, and no accommodation provided. Furthermore, their exorbitant charge of £150 more per person to change our train to the following hour was outrageous, especially when compared to the £90 flight with EasyJet per person that we ultimately took. Eurostar's disregard for the well-being of its passengers and their families is unacceptable, and I cannot in good conscience recommend their services to anyone.

The Eurostar terminal at St Pancras is far too small when the trains are full - but check-in is well regulated and the staff are perfectly civil and helpful. I queued for a few minutes only and then went through security and passport control without any problem. Train arrived in Paris on time. Gare du Nord on the other hand - chaos. Apparently 'too many passengers' to blame for the very very long queues on 22 April - doesn't its operational business plan work when the trains are full?! After standing in a long queue for 45 minutes, and being corralled in a totally random manner BEFORE I even got to check in, I was worried I would miss the train - but no, the trains are just delayed!!  Then they get stuck behind slower trains near Lille.  Passport control and security was just manic, staff shouting all the time. And constant ads for WiFi on the train but nothing that my phone could find. If its going to be like that may as well fly cattle class for far less money.
London to ParisAggressive train manager when no service due to strike.Threatening behaviour and unpleasant Apparently that is the best they can manage

This could have been such a wonderful service but it feels barely more comfortable than taking the London Underground.  The check in at Gare du Nord is a particularly harrowing experience.  Everything is cramped and small.  No announcement to advise us of a delay and rude staff literally screaming at passengers.  It’s still the quickest way to get to Paris but the service overall has lost it.  You can even see that with the trains being dirty and the platforms full of rubbish.  Such a shame.

We were travelling to Disneyland Paris. Unfortunately Euro Star doesn’t go direct we went via Lille which is an absolute nightmare. But I’m reviewing actual EuroStar which we all loved. Family of five . Two toddlers 2 & 4. Plenty of language space . Large comfy seats . Table for 4 . Lovely breakfast going and dinner on return. All staff were kind and pleasant. Especially on the return journey which was yesterday 18th April. Christophe was our steward. What an asset to your company . Excellent five star service. He was a joy!! I think he will remember us . We was the only family in our carriage. The business men must have thought there worst night mare. But my Grandchildren were very good! We all laughed together as we got off. Hope to travel again soon. Please go back to a direct service to Disneyland

Average waiting area at St. Pancras, with a very limited Duty Free. There is a small bar there, but is really over-priced (£6.60 for a can of beer, £9.20 for a 'lunchbox bottle' of wine). so bring food and drink with you. Security and passport control was a doddle and quick. Train itself was immaculate. Carriages were clearly numbered and everyone found their seat quickly. Comfortable seats, with UK and EU charging sockets. We all got sat together at no extra cost. Train was so comfortable, and the buffet car was reasonable and friendly. Sat there with a glass of wine speeding through Kent at 180mph (the best way to experience some areas of Kent) was a way better experience than flying. Clear announcements, clean toilets. Absolute pleasure, would recommend.

A truly awful experience, and not for the first time!Despite being there over an hour before check in, I was told the train was full and would have to get another ticket. This happened on two occasions, and at £240 a ticket it was getting stupidly expensive. The trains had been over booked and I felt this was something they do regularly in order to get more money out of people in buying alternative tickets. French staff in check were extremely rude and unhelpful.Was offered no apology or refund!I will not be travelling by Eurostar again!

It's been 4 years since I took the Eurostar... Very complicated customer journey. No explanation from staff about the route and waiting times. Over 60 minutes needed from start to "boarding" hall. Staff replaced by security guards who have no goal of customer satisfaction. HS passport control gates. No emotion from employees... Customers seem to be considered like cattle... What happened to get to this point? I'm not talking about prices...

First time on Eurostar from Paris  -London; underwhelming and very disappointing 30 minutes late into London -no explanation /reason given at all and very little apology -resulting in rush to make connection for onward journey  Not enough seating in Paris Gard du Nord Eurostar area Filthy train  windows couldn’t see much out of themOnboard Cafe out of stock of many items Only decaf coffee available was instant coffee which was  horrible Most  importantly train  late by considerable minutes - Poor

I booked my £700+ return ticket from London to Cannes because I hate flying. Arriving into London there is absolutely NO where to sit and whilst I have a Platinum Amex which gets you into the business lounges, unfortunately as my card was for business, rather than personal I wasn’t allowed. What a ridiculous rule. Huffing and puffing, I then had to stand for an hour because there were absolutely no seats in the waiting area. In board, premier seats are pretty standard and the Food is absolutely MINGING. And the real reason why I am spending time writing this is because of the RUDE French staff on the Paris side on the way back.There’s even a sign that says “paid for by the European Union” if that’s not an FU to Brits, I don’t know what is. Anyway, My train from Cannes was delayed and therefore I missed my Eurostar connection by a few minutes. I was shouted at to go to the office like a naughty school boy to get a new ticket. I was then told it was 50 euros to change tickets - even although clearly this wasn’t my fault and I had booked it via the Eurostar app. Luckily I kicked up a fuss and the 50 euros was cleared. Moral of the story is - always complain…. I read online it really depends who you get on whether they will charge you or not.Arriving Staff on the ground are pretty rubbish

The Gare du Nord Eurostar concourse is a disaster. No air conditioning. No space to sit, lines for the police at the chaotic borders. Simply a shame. And having us come an hour early to solve your organizational problems is really taking your customers for fools. And of course 30 minutes late on 19.58 number 9053.

We travelled business premier as I was taking my 70 year old mother for the her first time in Paris, I wanted her to experience 1st class travel. I traveled eurostar business class once before in 2011 and it was exceptional. Both lounges felt so classy and peaceful and both had fully stocked bars and great complimentary food.The lounges sadly have been greatly scaled back. The lounge at St.pancras is still quite nice but the decor is getting tired. The bar upstairs im glad to see is still manned. We traveled in the morning and they were service freshly made smoothies. However we are now at gard du nord. The queues even for business premier cannot be avoided (you're ok if you have a European passport though. But sadly uk is no longer in the EU so very very long queues for us.) once you're through to busness is not the quiet professional space it once was. It seems many people travel business with young children now and the space is quite echoy. The sunken bar lays empty and unused. We are traveling at lunchtime and I would have expected it to be manned.The sorry selection of complimentary snacks is limited to crisps and pretzels. Basic alcohol selection and tea and coffee. The food and drink area is full of people asking where the non existent sandwiches are and faces of disappointed expectation.

We specifically flew from Glasgow to Gatwick to catch the Eurostar to Brussels… yes.. yes… people asked why, but I used to live in SE England and loved the Eurostar when I lived there and my partner had never been on it, as many people living in Scotland haven’t..’ Can’t really fault it, but there simply isn’t enough room at St Pancras, nor Brussels for holding people-then it’s a dangerous walk along the congested platform (Brussels Midi) to find the correct part of the train. This wasn’t clear.It also isn’t clear at Brussels Midi where to check in for Eurostar until you are actually there! It is signposted as ‘Intra Schengen…’ why not ‘Eurostar vers le Royaume- Uni..?’  Or a flag???

The train is very good, very comfortable in what they call “first class” but they should URGENTLY review the staff they hire, given that throughout the trip a girl in charge of serving lunch on the train from London to Brussels (15:04 ) is extremely unfriendly, unpleasant and unprofessional. Not only did she make snide comments towards us during the trip but she basically treated us badly for stacking the two trays since we wanted to use one of the tables and that apparently made her job horribly difficult. Totally rude, I don't know if she thinks she's the queen of England but she should lower her smoke.

What a disorganized s**t show at Gare du Nord! Felt like we were being herded into pens like cows awaiting slaughter. Lines and lines of people waiting with virtually no guidance or communication. Had to go through passport control twice which undoubtedly contributed to delays. The whole awful experience made traveling by air seem well-organized, pleasant, and stress-free. Never again!

The only arrogant company that allows itself to ask you to respect the conditions on their site but which does not respect them itself, clean up your managers, the company will only be better off because the rest of the staff is good to it, respectful and not trying to show off!!

Paris to Brussels on April 10 on business premier - train was on time, comfort reasonable, but cleanliness could be better.Booked business premier partly due to complementary meal service. Compartment was less that half full but they were all out of food (!) when they got to my seat and I was offered nuts or chips instead. Filed a complaint and was subsequently not allowed to have a complementary sandwich from the onboard bistro instead. Mistakes happen but there were not really any real efforts to redeem. It is very unfortunate that Eurostar  runs a monopoly between Paris and Brussels, would not choose them if there was a choice of carriers.

Took the Eurostar from London to Paris, rather than have the hassle of a plane trip and airports! We were not disappointed.  Other than a rather crowded waiting room at St Pancras, it was superb.  We booked Standard Premier, and were served a delicious lunch, accompanied by a very enjoyable wine.  So much easier than fighting through airport crowds!!

Pretty disappointing. Got the plane to Brussels (cheaper) and the Eurostar back due to more choice of timings. Wish I’d got the plane back.Train was just under an hour late with no real explanation and barely an apology. Not directly Eurostar’s fault but the departure lounge at Midi is abysmal. No natural light or cafe and not nearly enough space for a whole train of people. Extremely overpriced cold snacks only. Told delay of 15 minutes when it was clearly much later. We had onward connections to catch so accurate information and a proper explanation would have been really helpful. Once all on the train, it took another 15 minutes to actually depart. Actual train was fine though very few sandwiches left in the cafe shortly after departure. Only good thing is despite missing our connection, thanks to an agreement between Eurostar and British train companies we were allowed to get the next one despite having advance (fixed) tickets. Unless you specifically need to get to central London, flying is sadly a better plan.
At least the one that touched me is punctual. Very basic and a little run down in terms of cleanliness, it has no comfort and the free wifi never works.

Travelled to Brussels on 11.05 train 5th April Business Premier. Hugely disappointing - I suspect we had old rolling stock as the BP carriage (just the one of 16) was  drab and dirty. No attempt whatsoever at identifying it as premier, and our seat did not have a window view. The food was bland and too cold: I had goats cheese mousse and a bread roll to start with followed by beetroot and roasted parsnip salad. Offering individual bottles of champagne may be a good idea as, at 11.15am, I was not in the mood for alcohol, ‘free’ or not. I was very underwhelmed, sad to say as travelling ‘first class’ on Eurostar has been on my bucket list for years. I’ve travelled 1st class by plane to the US several times, and the service and ‘extras’ were remarkable. No comparison on this journey and I doubt I’ll be checking out business premier on Eurostar again.

Our return train was cancelled, which I found out two days before our return. I was promised a refund if we took a different train back and stayed overnight in Brussels en-route, but after 12 calls and 2 lengthy visits to the Eurostar desk, I am still waiting for a refund dating back to Feb (it's now April). This is my first and only experience on the Eurostar. I am out of pocket and they don't compensate for the hastle, the extra hotel room or the extra train trip despite having all the receipts. Utterly dismal customer service

Worst system that Ive ever seen, avoid this and just take a flight instead. With the trains and booking they dont tell you where to go and they also dont help direct you to find where to go with 0 app support or any live human to speak to.
Very convenient with teens , we got a booth and kids manGed to do lots of homework before we arrived to Amsterdam. Comfortable sitting and table

Still a good alternative to flying but the prices vary so book in advance where possible. We used to travel from Ebbsfleet which is no longer available so St Pancras is the only station left. The 1st class travel isn't good value anymore as it also gets crowded and the menu plus wine has gradually all diminished over the years. Overall it is just a normal train journey. The windows on our carriage were dirty so we didn't get much of a view of the countryside. Wi-fi is free and there are chargers and a slot where you can place your book when not reading. You can take your own drinks on board and food. You are only allowed into the departure lounges around 60-90 minutes beforehand, probably for safety reasons. Food and drink places are few and far between once you get through to the lounge areas, but there are plenty of places in the station areas and also at Kings Cross station, across the road.The sooner Ebbsfleet and Ashford return the better but sadly first class is never going to be the same as it was when the Eurostar first opened. Halcyon days of 3 course meals and a wine with each course.

A crazy world this Monday, April 1A long queue and few explanationsFew seats available and the price despite a purchase made more than a month ago is very high: 4 times the price of the planeBut the car, even 2nd class, is correct and traveling by train to the city center is appreciable
Brilliant experience. Such a well organised experience from beginning to end, so much smoother than airports. Will definitely do again. 2 hours 1 minute and we were in Brussels- fab

I would wholeheartedly recommend Eurostar for anyone requiring special assistance and more generally anyone wanting a quick and hassle-free trip to Paris. Prior to my trip the team assisting people requiring special assistance were helpful and thorough and facilitated a comfortable and faultless journey. I purchased a standard ticket, but I could wait in the lounge and once on the train, my seat was in Standard Premier where I was served  a meal during the journey which I hadn’t realised I would get prior to my journey. The accessible toilet In my coach was spacious and clean. Thumbs up, a great experience. I would choose that over getting a plane.

Very mixed reviews must obviously mean many different experiences. But when you count the dozens of Eurostar services to & from any of the destinations serviced, on any given day, I guess that’s understandable.We took the train from London to Brussels (and onto Bruges), and return.It’s international travel, so customs & immigration are a fact of life and in our experience, both were handled well at both ends. Trains were on time, clean and comfortable.  Certainly favourably comparable to an equivalent experience flying economy.What did disappoint quite a bit were the waiting areas, at both ends, between immigration/customs and boarding the trains.  And on the trains themselves, a total lack of USB charging points in the seats - come on, it’s 2024.But overall, far, far more relaxing than flying and the associated dehumanising that has become. Would happily do it all again, but with more battery packs.Let’s hope that the talk of new competition on the service brings a better experience.

Do not take the Eurostar from Paris to London, there are buses and trains the same price or cheaper. You have to show up an hour early and will get treated absolutely horrendously by the staff. The train was delayed, and it was overbooked because the train prior didn’t arrive. A person further up in line had my luggage and they made her carry it the whole trip. For the price their service is awful, it’s not on time, and the journey was terrible.

Get there at least 1.5 hrs before. You will queue but that is international travel.Buy your food before you board. You never get good food on a train.Charge your phone cos you can’t on board the train. It’s quick and staff were polite.

If this is how they treat business class customers I would hate to see how they treat people who haven’t paid such an exorbitant price! Unhelpful and rude staff, particularly at Paris, where the food offer is nonexistent and the facilities are very poor and much in need of refurbishment.

Terrible customer service, outrageous policies, unclear and misleading advertising. Also face unnecessary rejection at the gate because I was 5 minutes late due to a train cancellation. Then the service was also delayed. Ridiculous. Change to next available train for free is rubbish too, they charged me £44. Second time I’ve used Eurostar and it’s the second time I’m having issues, will fly from now, it’s usually cheaper anyway!

Fantastic price to travel from London to Paris. The trip itself was comfortable and on time.I was a bit disappointed that having spent time picking out a seat with a good view, the style of train was changed and we were reseated with not the best of views.My wife had this forethought of packing a bottle of champagne that we sipped whilst we travelled at speed through the countryside. Eurostar are fine with passengers, bringing a bottle of wine or four cans of beer each.

I paid for cancellation insurance and found that I did have to cancel. I had a cardiac ct scan that revealed significant calcification and I may need a heart by- pass. Unfortantely my insurance, arranged through Eurostar, is operated by a company of their choice, Allianz, so it’s not a straight forward procedure. I have to wait for a letter from Eurostar. I was told this can take some time due to staff levels. I then have to send this to Allianz who will decide if my insurance is valid for this cancellation. Fortunately I booked the hotel with booking.com who cancelled immediately with no problems at all.

Arriving at Amsterdam Central Station, it turned out that the departure platform had changed. We were not informed of this. We found the right platform and were able to leave for Brussels. We had to change there. There was a half hour delay. We were waiting with all the passengers in the duty free shop, which was a bit strange.  Be sure to arrive on time, for both the outward and return journey. Otherwise had a great trip.
very good experience.the train was on time in both directions, the reception agents were professional and kind.Next time I have to go to London, I think the train will be my priority.

Journey: AMS-BRU-LDN // LDN-AMSI had expected my train ride to be more comfortable than airplanes, and with the thought of less " waiting "  with regards to boarding etc., I was expecting a less stressful journey compared to plane trips. Well... I was wrong. I would even prefer Ryanair over Eurostar.In short:- WiFi NOT WORKING properly in any of the three trains I took. So my plan to work in the train- Toilets are gross, look like train-station toilets that are being cleaned once a year.- Even on 4 hour trips, not even free water is provided.- Seats are VERY UNCOMFORTABLE. Dutch NS trains and airplanes have better seats.- Leg room equals Ryanair economy class.- Sockets were not providing power reliably.On top of this, but this was partly our own bad, you have to "check in" for trips to UK 60-90 min before departure for passport and bag checks. In Brussels, this check took only 3 minutes, and the train arrived like 5 minutes before departure, so the 60 minutes seem a bit overkill. We were 8 minutes late for these checks, and they did not allow us to check in: we had to wait for 2 hours for the next train, even though they could have checked our bags and passports and we still would have had plenty of time to kill before having to enter the train... Anyways, would not recommend, especially not on a work trip when expecting to be able to do some work in the train.

Standard premier terrible quality, no working power and no WIFI Ripped seats and broken fixtures. Advised by nice staff old trains are not repaired and no wifi in board for months. Eurostar trading on lies about quality and facilities on board. Staff all know no wifi and no power at seats nothing they can do. Seriously over priced seats and no customer care difference between economy and Standard Premier. Don’t waste your money

I accompanied  someone living with dementia from paris to london and was unpleasantly surprised by the poor quality of the assistance service in Paris. It was an awful experience. There were other disable people on wheelchair near us who experienced the same issue. The assistance staff has not been trained on hidden disabilities . They brought the wheeelchairs to the platform but did not bring the ramp . We had to wait in the cold for them  finally decide to go and look for the ramp. The list of issues is too long. The staff was impatient, not considerate and careless. We forgot the scarf of the person needed assistance who was cold at the custom, I asked  3 different member of staff including the train manager  to help me get it as I could not leave her alone. None of them bother to try to call their colleagues to assist of find a solution so she does not stay in the cold waiting. The staff need training. They are not ready for the para Olympic . Awful and tearful experience .

The FIRST PROBLEM we encountered was the POOR FACILITIES which are provided when using the EUROSTAR TRAIN from Amsterdam to London. We purchased Business Premier and found the extra cost from Standard was DEFINITELY NOT WORTH IT.  We travelled on a Saturday at 08:15am and found that the LOUNGE that is supposed to be available for Business Premier ticket holders was CLOSED till 10:00am and it's on Platform 2 and we departed on Platform 15. No service and too far away to use. Also there was no Priority Boarding, which is a part of the Business Premier Ticket.The SECOND PROBLEM was the food which was suppose to be a hot meal, turned out to be a ROLL with HAM & CHEESE in a PAPER BAG with a bottle of water, because their fridge was broken and that's the best they could do and this was given to us just before disembarking in London. The trip takes around 4hrs and 15min. so having an early start, you expect the correct food to be distributed about midway through the journey, but because of the fridge problem they had to find an alternative food source. Very disappointing for the EXTREME EXTRA COST. As you could understand, this journey was a part of our holiday travel experience and it turned out to be too expensive for our trip, which could have easily been taken cheaper and quicker by flying. I would NOT RECOMMEND anyone to pay the extra cost from STANDARD TICKET when travelling, if you still want to travel by rail. This was my last way to complain as EUROSTAR was not interested in direct response, when I contacted them by email, twice, before giving this review.I WOULD DEFINITELY RECOMMEND THAT YOU PURCHASE "STANDARD" AND NOT BUSINESS PREMIER, WHEN TRAVELLING BY RAIL. BETTER STILL, TRAVEL BY PLANE.

I have been using the Eurostar for 10 years and I can confirm after hundreds of trips that there is no WiFi in the train. I have had different laptops/phones over the years and I can confirm there is no WiFi in the sense of a WiFi that can be used and Eurostar has been lying to passengers face for a very long time. The tickets are always expensive when compared to plane (3 to 5 times). I still take the train to reduce my carbon footprint but the overall service/price is very bad.

What an amazing train ride! Gorgeous station in London to start. Had a first class ticket for upcoming cruise. Food was perfect and set for my dietary restrictions. In the tunnel I think we hit about 180mph. Rode to Brussels Midi station in Belgium, another great station. Return trip was just as fast, good food again, and amazing views on both sides of the tunnel.

Train late on the way out and back. Display problem, indicate one platform then another then you find yourself running with your suitcase to get your train on time. On the train it is very cold despite low temperatures outside. Very slow train are you sure it is a TGV?

The waiting area was thronged, far more than seating capacity. The only toilets have long queues as they  are at half capacity with males having to share female toilet section as male section is closed. We had to sit on the floor for an hour. Why do they insist on arriving 90 minutes beforehand when the waiting area is so dismal and uncomfortable. Thoroughly unpleasant experience and it's far cheaper to fly!

Very unfriendly conductor.Train is delayed and the conductor is talking on the platform.His colleague wants to close the door, so I enter the train behind the conductor.He turns around and snaps at me that he wants to see m. Ticket.I say 'please?' to remind him that it is also allowed in a friendly manner.Then he snapped further. I asked for his name and he wouldn't give it.After boarding, his colleague called him 'Michel'.The delay is of course not a problem, but normal behavior is appreciated.Travel7-3-24 8:30 PM (8:42 PM) Antwerp-Amsterdam.And then you want to report this discreetly via the response form..., the WiFi on the train does not work. So on to your own data, the form does not work (up to 3 times).
Trip from London St Pancras to Paris. Great train with plenty of legroom ar seating and good luggage space plus attentive staff and a lovely light lunch. Great way to travel.

Disappointment in the management of passenger flows. Departure scheduled for 9:02 a.m. for London.... Actual departure 30 minutes late.When you pay expensive prices, when you come to spend 24 hours in London with appointments set... it's not up to the level of service expected.Regrets.

Was a more pleasant experience than the plane and for a few weeks in early spring it is about the same price as flying. Rest of year is 3x more expensive by eurostar, at least the London to amsterdam route is.I was interested to get a feedback form from eurostar but only for the amsterdam to London part which was on time rather than the London amsterdam part which arrived 25mins late. I wonder if this influences overall scores for their reviews.There is still the pack at security and at amsterdam end a long queue in the rain but the train itself nice and smooth.

Went out to Paris for a meeting, returning the following day. The way out was ok. Got through security in about 15 minutes and then was able to work from the lounge until the train departed. Only negative was there isn't any lounge food - just peanuts. I'm not expecting a meal, but would have been nice to have something a bit more than just peanuts.The train trip was good - decent seats, places to put things and reasonably quiet. Meal was ok - it's pre-made but not too bad.The return journey was worse because there is no separate passport/customs gate for Business Premier. You have to queue with everyone else to get through a handful of gates which takes time. Lounge is similar in scope to the London one - a few drinks and peanuts. But at least it's quiet and can get work done. Then you get onto boarding and when we went the gangway for the front of the train is closed. Of course they don't tell you this so you walk there, find out it's closed and have to walk back to the queue with everyone else to get down to the platform.So in summary, London outwards isn't too bad, but the return from Paris really needs sorting out.

An advice.. think twice before you buy their ticket , 10 mnts after I bought a ticket for my daughter she told me it didn't suite her school program, I wanted to change the ticket for a day earlier (both ways Brussels London- London Brusselschoose exchage ( which was written  it was possible before 7 days -and the departure was ju. st 7 days , it first wanted to charge me 150 GBP ( the ticket it self was 170 GBP ) Than tried to call , write .. nothing today I did find out all with their answer underneath   """Yes you will need to pay £152 to change this ticket. Eurostar tickets can be chaged up to 7 dats before the date/time of departure which in this case was 18:51pm. "" So their days do not end up at midnight like in the rest of the world ! I have bought the main ticket around 7 pm and tried to change it after 10 mnts ,their day calculation is not explained at their web site and for sure they lack any good intentions ! I will try my best to avoid them in the future , simple flights to London airport do cost almost the same and they treat their clients way better

My husband & I visited Amsterdam for my birthday. After a lovely trip the 18.45 train home was cancelled. The staff casually said the train is cancelled & you will have to come back tomorrow!! They turfed everyone out & said re book on the link on email. The link never worked, the customer service lines were shut. We had to book in to a hotel & decided to get up early & try & get re booked ASAP. The staff were not interested & said they couldn't re book till 18.45 causing us a lot of stress with childcare at home! The staff were very dismissive & uninterested I'm our predicament due to their cancellation.The saving grace was when I finally got through to customer service the lady was very helpful & booked us on 14.45.It was a shame as we had a good journey in & this stress spoilt a good few days.

On the way out, the train was a little less than 30 minutes late, no compensation. On the way back, we were right on schedule (you have to be there at least 30 minutes before departure) and we arrived 33 minutes early. However, the person at the ticket check refused to let us pass and directed us to a ticket office to take the next train. There were 5 of us (a couple with 3 children) and had to pay an extra 200 euros to take the next train even though we were at the station on time! The staff didn't want to hear anything, not even after our return when we made a complaint asking for a check of our arrival time with the video surveillance camera and at least a commercial gesture. We received a standard response to our first email, not at all personalized or taking our situation into account. For the second email, same type of response and no action taken! We had the impression of an all-powerful form of Eurostar, a company that acts as it suits it and calls into question our honesty. In addition, the Eurostar agents in London during all the checks were generally unpleasant, not a smile, we really had the feeling of being treated like cattle!The only advantage of the train is that it arrives in the center of London otherwise the service is deplorable and it is very difficult, if not impossible, to communicate directly with the after-sales service. We will no longer take Eurostar.
