They cancelled last train from Amsterdam to London Kings Cross today at 18.45 leaving the people without any accomodation, help or chance to book train for the next day They offered refund of the return of the ticket. I had to book flight back to London for £200 plus train from Gatwick to London. I will never use the service. Shame on yoy

Travel from Amsterdam to London with transfer in Brussels. Amsterdam Brussels had an overrun and arrived in Brussels about 10 minutes late. At the gate to the Brussels London train there was still 26 minutes to board. I wasn't allowed in anymore. Computer says 'no'. You can fill in a complaint form on the website... this is hopeless.

First time on Eurostar for many years and I was not disappointed Easy  check in online, easy security and passport control in London, train was on time, clean, and staff were very helpful. even experienced a breakfast going out and an evening meal coming home!Everything work very well, so definitely recommend this option of travel to the continent ( vs airports!) and I would definitely be using this service more often going forward😀

Not a great experience. We were frustrated they have stopped the direct London - Disney service but was promised the change at Lille was easy when boking.It was not as easy as it should of been. Half the train disembarking at Lille with no details of connecting train on display nor any staff to ask. hundreds of lost people franticly trying to find where to do. Even he French people lost trying to find where to go!. London departure lounge is also far to small for number of people they are trying to have pass through it. On board the food was poor, far worse the aircraft food. Coaches were clean on way out but on way back they were filthy. Will look to fly next time we travel

I travelled as a group with Rail Discoveries from Paris to London. We already had our tickets and seat numbers, but on arrival at the Paris all our seat numbers had been altered. Also could they not keep the windows cleaner??

We are on premiere class Eurostar train from Antwerp to Paris ( 2/22, train number 9328, coach 11 ) The Asian attendant intentionally skip us to serve deserts/ light meal to us , when we confronted him, he first said “ I asked you, you said no”, which was a complete lie.  Then he said“ you did not ask me”,  but he was extra nice to the white guy sitting next to us  (check with him all the time, ask him need anything, and offer drink and deserts ). I don’t know  if this is because we are Asians. But the incidents made us very uncomfortable. And his behavior is totally unacceptable, discrimination against race should never be tolerated!!!!

I would like to use the train for work travel more often but Eurostar's inflexible rebooking policies will make it that I won't be doing so in future! I wanted to rebook trips between London and Rotterdam twice now and Eurostar will not let me rebook an indirect ticket (via Brussels for example) to a direct one (even though ticket prices are similar). The only option is to buy a new ticket! This should be more clearly communicated before purchasing the ticket. Now it looks as if there are 6 trips per day that you can take on this route, but for rebooking you're limited to 3. All 6 are seemingly operated by Eurostar, so why this is, is a wild mystery to me. I certainly won't be traveling to or from London using Eurostar for work again.

Bought their tickets online. Plans to fly to Europe changed last minute because infant got sick. Instead of refunding even partially, they kept all the money and blamed it on the purchase policy I signed up for. Didn’t even agree to provide a voucher for future use instead of refund. Never spending a penny on them again.

Going out to Paris from St. Pancras was fine. Coming back was diabolical. The train was cancelled  at very short notice because of a strike.  We were told we could rebook at no extra cost, but there were no available trains for 4 days. We therefore booked a flight at 200 euros each. This was cheaper than staying in a hotel for 4 days, but Eurostar will not pay for alternative travel. The family also needed to get back for school and work and we received no support from Eurostar, so had to make a quick decision. I am appalled by Eurostar's customer service. Don't touch them, unless you are prepared to put up with a lot of frustration and lost money. It's a shame, I've travelled with Eurostar in the past, when it was a quality service rather than a rip-off.

In first class, the hostesses are unpleasant, speak only English and refuse to speak French. Eurostar 9369 - car 11 - 5:25 p.m. train. This Monday, February 19. At this price, when leaving France and arriving in Brussels, they could choose people who speak French and who are a little more pleasant!

Extremely bad costumer service. Don't do the ALLIANZ ticket cancellation option as it is A SCAM! The person from the call centre even told he never heard anyone cancelling only the return ticket in HIS ENTIRE CAREER and that an insurance letter could possibly not be produced. SCAM! Not even refunded for medical reason. Very disappointed
Shocking. Terrible queue. Not enough staff. Trains delayed. Separated from my wife completely due to barrier getting closed. Depressing and sad.

what a disaster! they like to brag that it's better than flying but it's far from the truth. horrible line ups (2 of them) before boarding. not enough space to sit down while waiting (saw old people walking around because they couldnt sit). you basically go throught security check like in an airport. wont do again

Certainly easier than getting to the airport even though you still had to go through customs. The trains themselves were comfortable and very quick. The only issue was at Gare du Nord station in Paris, where our eSIM for our phones didn't work. Finding where to get a physical SIM card quickly was a bit difficult but sorted it out in the end.
London to Paris. Super easy transport option. Train left on time. Super friendly staff. Prompt food service and coffee. Train was clean. Would travel Eurostar again

We took the train from St Pancras to Amsterdam Centraal and back on their Standard Premier basis. Checking in at both ends was straightforward whilst the standards & service on-board were top quality. Snacks, light meals & drinks were served regularly while we eased our way through North Central Europe. A much more relaxed journey than by plane and you get to travel between the hearts of the cities, rather than having a long connecting train journey at either end. No baggage reclaim to navigate, either.
I've never seen such a filthy seat. The toilet was awful and flush did not work. Utterly disgusting and appalling that Eurostar doesn't care

Our trip home from the Netherlands was cancelled. There were no representative from Eurostar at the station explaining what can be done to arrange alternatives. The customer services were unavailable for 3 days. The website didn’t recognise my booking so we couldn’t re-book for the next available journey. There were no additional trains put on and as such there was no availability for us to pay again for our journey home. When we tried to claim £800 in compensations for our hotel costs, food costs and alternative transport. Eurostar were only prepared to consider hotel costs and selected few food costs. The process of compensation was dragged out, I feel deliberately as the Eurostar website was having digital issues and they also lost my emails. I’ve still not received compensation over a month later despite me stressing to them I have a young family and times are hard.

Upon the train's arrival in Paris Gare Du Nor at 17.12pm on the 10-02-2024, I want to express my gratitude for the exceptional kindness and assistance provided by both staff members in coach 9. Their interaction with my autistic children was truly remarkable, and they remained helpful throughout the journey. Despite a seat booking error, with seat 31 being duplicated, the staff swiftly resolved the issue without hesitation, ultimately benefiting our family. On behalf of my family, a heartfelt thank you (MERCI) to both members of staff. Exceptional customer service fromNesser and Sophie.

So I have spent 160€ to not reach my destination, I had to stay an extra night in Belgium. At the next day I was allowed to get a train at anytime, so I did it, but there was no space for myself, so I had to travel 2.5h on my feet with all my baggage in my hands. NEVER EVER AGAIN!!!

Hesitating between Eurostar and air travel for brussels-london trip? Choose air travel! Eurostar = longer waiting times, lousy service, no information, very frequent delays, lounge with bus station atmosphere

We traveled from Paris to London on the 8th of February, on the 20:10 and the staff were absolutely fantastic, there was a problem with mine and my daughters ticket but not my partners , this was my first  travelling and I found the situation very overwhelming, the staff were beyond helpful and made every effort to sort the situation as quickly as they could , I wish I could thank them for everything, would 100% travel on the Eurostar again just because of them , if there is any chance they see this , thank you so much for getting me and my family home , you have no idea how much your efforts made me feel at ease with our situation, keep up the good work , it’s very appreciated !
The train was a great and efficient experience. The customs officials, however, were beyond grumpy. So unreasonable and totally unnecessary.

Absolutely terrible service. We had significant delay due to a train issue and sat without information, electricity, or toilets for nearly 8 hours. The management of the situation was atrocious and the response to the disruption was disorganized and pathetic. Upon returning to London (our departure not our destination) end of day there was no process or alignment among station staff to rebook the trip and it descended into an utter mess. Clearly a lack of leadership, commitment to traveler care and safety, and overall a pathetic excuse for a guest-centric company. We are still going back and forth with support trying to recoup our money after having to rebook multiple trains, hotel for the evening, and spend added costs on food. The support team is slow, poor at communication, and not guest friendly. Recommend avoiding Eurostar if peace of mind, care, and trust are of high importance to you.
It is recommended to arrive 2 hours in advance, it is better to wait inside the departure lounge than in the X-ray queue and at the two passport controls
St Pancras station is beautiful and spacious, but the boarding procedures are long, tiring and take place in very small spaces!Pure madness!

Surprised my partner and his mum with Day tickets to Paris, and was also surprised myself with the amazing customer Service! Having travelled on the Eurostar multiple times, I was starred as a frequent traveler and the lovely Dominic was waiting to take us three to business class. What a lovely, added touch to our day trip! Food was amazing, staff were very attentive (even before this while boarding!). Positive and friendly the whole time. Have travelled multiple times and each time is a great experience.

Easy to book tickets and get to via thameslink train. Swift check in and security and a comfortable seat on train. Only things that let it down are rising ticket prices and first come first serve bag storage.

We took Eurostar for a return trip from London to Paris. On both the journeys the train could not get us there in time. In the first journey the schedule was randomly delayed by 15 minutes and the train arrived further 20 minutes later than the changed schedule. On the second journey there was horrible management at the checkin and security making us wait for over an hour in queue. Even after waiting for over an hour we missed our train for no fault of ours and the Eurostar staff forced us to take a later train. Even the later train was delayed. So we ended up arriving 1 hour 15 minutes later than our planned schedule.As compared to LNER, Avanti, SWR in the UK, Eurostar is poorly managed. What’s the point of a train operation that can’t get you there in time on any of the journey? Even the checkin experience is horrible if you compare it to taking a flight.
0 trains, 0 New Year's Eve weekend with family in London, 0 reimbursement of my expenses (including our accommodation which was necessarily canceled the same day) and 0 excuses... it's heartbreaking!

I've never been compelled to write a bad review before but this was a terrible experience. I was on the 11:04 departure from London to Rotterdam (train 9126) on January 28th, it started out great. The staff in London were lovely, helpful and we departed on time. Everything on the trip was great until about 10 minutes after we left Brussels. We stopped at Michelin station however the doors remained closed and we sat there for 30 minutes before we received any communication. When we did receive communication all that was said is that they didn't know what was going on or how long it would be just that there was a serious delay. After a five-minute google search on the Belgium Train Line website, I found that there was a downed overhead power line and initially they did not know how long it would be. We continued to sit there for 2 and a half additional hours and then they announced that we would be returning to Brussels and then this train would be canceled. They also said that upon arrival we would be given other train options and if none were available a credit for a taxi or a hotel room for the night. We were also informed we would receive a full refund. This sounded great to everyone on board however to our surprise on returning to the station there was no staff anywhere to be seen. At this point I had collaborated with two other solo travelers and luckily between the three of us we had English, French and Dutch so we found a security guard who told us where the Eurostar desk was. When we got to the Eurostar desk the staff member told us there would be no refunds, hotel or taxis and to run to platform 14 as a train was going to go to Rotterdam from there however when we arrived at platform 14 we were told the train would not be running, the platform was closed and we had to leave. We asked him where to go and if there would be another train and he said go to platform 6 there should be one arriving at 6:52pm.  We then went to platform 6 and attempted to speak to the uniformed Eurostar staff however they said they couldn't help us and walked away. At this point we found a non Eurostar uniformed member of station staff and asked if he could help. He was lovely and told us to wait until the train arrived and get on no problem, our tickets would be valid. We also double checked this statement with security and he also said it was fine. With how crazy the day had been we wanted to double-check this information with a Eurostar staff member and we finally found a group of them standing together that would talk to us. They said we could get on but that the train was full so we would have to stand, if we did not manage to get on we would have to wait until the next service running at 9:30. We luckily managed to get on the train and stood in the bar cart. At least 50 other people from our original train made it on and spread out across the train. There was about 10 of us in the bar cart and we went and asked the train manager if there were any seats available as it was still at least another two-hour journey pending no more delays. We were then yelled at by the train manager of the new service because "This is a red line train, you only paid to be on a blue line train, you didn't pay for this level of service" We attempted to explain the situation to him and that his own companies staff had informed us we were allowed on. He replied harshly that we were not allowed on however he would have to let us stay as we had already started moving. So the group of us stood for the entire journey and received glares from the train manager everytime he walked by. I understand that the delay was out of Eurostars control but the communication and customer service was completely in their control and needs to be handled better. I also sent a message to their Instagram direct message and received a great reply from a lady named Kate (Thank you Kate) then this afternoon I received a quite unhelpful  reply from someone named Jude who told me we were unauthorized to be on that train and although he shouldn't have raised his voice he was in the right. We were apparently supposed to wait for an email from Eurostar inviting us on a new train... well considering its been 24 hours I don't think anyone got those emails. In the end we arrived in Rotterdam 6 hours after we were supposed to and I can't even begin to imagine how much longer it would have been had we not gotten on the train we did. Never again, I'll fly next time, its cheaper anyways.

Last Saturday we were travelling across France to get the 3.12 Eurostar from Paris to London. Our TGV was delayed over an hour and we weren't going to make it. I phoned Eurostar and was told only 8 seats available on the 5 and none on the 7 o'clock I was strongly advised to take 4 tickets at £ 650!!!! as if Not they would go and we'd be stuck in Paris with 2 young children until the next day. She told me if I go to the stations Eurostar office they would charge me around £ 50 each to go on the next available train which wouldn't be until the next day, I was about to pay when I lost signal. I got through about 10 minutes later to be told only 5 seats available and now £ 1050.00. Again as no other option I was going to pay, lost signal again. We went to the Eurostar office at the Gard du Nord where we we're given 4 seats together on a table FOR FREE as there was plenty of seats available, I asked and yes plenty of space on the 7 o'clock also. On return to the UK I phoned Eurostar and complained, was told someone would come straight back to me with an explanation, they didn't. I phoned the next day, explained again. Was told they would escalate and come back to me, they didn't. Phoned again, guaranteed someone would contact me within 72 hours. They didn't. I phoned again, not at any time did anyone I spoke to know what I was talking about, no one took any notes, no one had any intention of getting back to me. At every opportunity when I phoned from the TGV I was lied to and would have been ripped off, apparently according to the person I spoke to today none of the 3 staff knew about 'hotnat' where they should have transferred for free. However, the lad I spoke to earlier, after the event knew all about it in detail.. they had me at a disadvantage, took every opportunity to try and rip me off and when I complained had no intention of ever getting back to me. Have been told basically, oh well nothing we can do about that. rubbish.

Euro star has gone down hill in the last few years, but still be sure to book the larger seats in standard premier as they are worth the extra price. There is no more welcome drink (bubbly) as they used to serve, and no hot food :(   Sadly the food has taken a real hit and is now a tiny portion of cold rabbit food.  The buffet cart in standard class has better food than standard premier which makes no sense. Dont't book business unless your company is paying, its not worth the extra price as the seat is the same as standard premier, but with slightly better food. Instead, be sure to stock up on M&S food at the station before your journey and enjoy on the train. M&S food will be 100 times better than the food they serve you on the train. Too be honest, they should just ditch the food altogerther or raise the price a bit and serve something hot and half decent, as at the moment they have just got it wrong wrong wrong.They also rush the service now. Instead of a nice two hour slow service, you get your wine, water, tea/ coffee and all your food in the first 30 minuets of the journey. For the next few hours of the journey, you get nothing. No service, drinks or food. Its so so bad compared to how it used to be, but can still be enjoyed with the above advice.

The trip from Rotterdam went well enough. Okay, we were delayed by an hour, but it didn't matter to us whether you arrived at 6 p.m. or 7 p.m. And we got a refund. In vouchers or simply in money.The only problem, of course, is that you have to queue for customs for half an hour at T. Pancras, but that's what the British wanted.And the Eurostar staff made sure we were on the train on time.A trip to or from Heathrow or Stansted to Amsterdam or Eindhoven would not have even been possible on our day due to the weather.

Took 90 minutes to check in at St Pancras, in disorganised chaos, not enough room for the queues and a complete shambles.Coming back from Paris was actually worse - 2+ hours standing in unorganised queues, 90+ minutes late arrival, 2 in my group got bumped onto the following train. NEVER AGAIN

My return journey from AMS to LON was due to depart on 19 January at 18.45 and arrive into LON at 21.57.I arrived today at 12.32..........The journey took 14 and a half hours.The train left AMS on time and went to Rotterdam. Next stop Brussels........The train broke down outside BRU and we had to wait for a "rescue locomotive" to tow us about 10 miles into Brussels Midi station. Announcements and information was very limited and illogical and staff need to be trained how to deal with situations like this.We finally arrived at 03.15 in Brussels. We had been on the train 8 and a half hours. Nobody from Eurostar on arrival and told to book a hotel or sleep in the station. It was below zero and snow on the ground..........You may want to Google "customer service."Nothing was done by Eurostar to assist people and it was basically just get on with it.I spent 4 hours in a hotel room at Midi station and returned to the station in the hope of getting to London before Easter! I was starting to understand why there was a murder on The Orient Express!The train journey this morning to London was of course delayed. The on board staff were just a disgrace and if you were "the people from last night" they refused to serve you a meal in Premium. The staff member working in my area was a most unpleasant, aggressive, unprofessional woman who clearly hated her job! She put a meal tray down in front of me........then looked again and recognised me from last night's horrors.Apparently I was not entitled to anything because I was not originally due to be on this train. She took the meal away from in front of me and told me she would talk to her Train Manager about me.......why?? What was already a totally horrible journey and experience was now so much worse. Instead of trying to placate people who were displaced and exhausted, they did the exact opposite. Only one word at this point.....disgusting.Finally arrived in London at 12.32....half an hour late of course!14 and a half hours from AMS to LON.Paid out about £150 for food and hotel room.4 hours sleep.Verbally abused by a staff member for absolutely no reason. Beyond a disgrace. The worst travel experience in many, many years and I travel a lot for work. Customer service......minus 10. Untrained and thoroughly unpleasant staff.Thanks for reading.

The trip to London was canceled due to a defective trainYou are told at 10:00 PM after standing still for 1.5 hours that yes, you can eat for €40 in the evening and you will be reimbursed for that tomorrow morning. Unfortunately, they have no solution for still being on the train at 2 am.There is a canteen but the only thing handed out were kitkats. No food is arranged. No drinks arranged. Even the Red Cross that brings water doesn't understand it.They don't know yet whether there is room on tomorrow's train. Probably. London in ruins all weekend.Once but never again...

250 pounds per person for a standard premier seatEvery step of the travel- sheer shocking disappointment1. Eurostar lounge - a pathetic , dirty ,  poorly maintained area with fingerprints on almost everything from cutlery to bathroom .2. Train - stained seats , muddy windows, no bins3. Food service- Almost equivalent to no food , small portions served with broken chipped glasses and stained cutlery. Poor condition. Average taste , cold food4. Almost every train from and to London has been delayed for more than 2 hours ., late or no information, technical faults , excess stoppages , no heating between stops , lights going out , electrical out , no Wi-FiStay away to stay safe from Eurostar

1.5 hours delay on departure and now 45 minutes delay and counting on the way back. You are asked to be there 90-60 minutes in advance and you then have to sit on the floor among all the stranded travelers, which is not easy at my age. You will then receive a voucher as compensation, which is of no use to me personally.

Train delayed had to make an unexpected stop and switch platforms but employees kept sending us in opposite directions. Employees vests say "here to help" they should say "I would rather not do my job don't bother." Horrible experience.
Amsterdam-Paris seats are dirty full of dust everywhere, toilets stinky  for only 250€, ns thank you

To flee ! Never again ! Disgusted!Eurostar train returning to France canceled at 10:30 p.m. As a result we have to find a hotel to stay and possibly return the next day. No more hotels available! The captain tells us that he will be reimbursed £300 per person for the hotel night. We have never had any help from Eurostar! No writing… We found a hotel at the price at midnight! Result Eurostar reimburses us £300 per room and not per person!!! Something absolutely not said orally 4 times throughout the train! Unacceptable! Ashamed ! So we find ourselves a month and a half later still not reimbursed! Let's not talk about returning the next day... never again for us! Inhuman! Even the staff told us this.

This is a great service. It has been for 30 years. It’s a train that links two of the finest cities in the world. If you’re a grown up who has been on a train in either country before, you know that the food might be pricy, the toilets not always immaculate, there will be queues and for one reason or another it won’t always run on time. That’s life. You get on in London, you get off in the middle of Paris. You’re on the train for less than three hours, you’ve the option to bring your own food and drink on if you’re watching the pennies, and they’ll get you there. So ignore the whining on here; you know what you’re getting, so sit back and enjoy it.

What a service by Premium Economy! Fast, roomy and clean, with excellent service from both Otillia (sorry if that’s not quite how her name is spelled) and her English colleague whose name we cannot recall but served great English Breakfast tea! This is the way to travel, fantastic.

Decided to use Eurostar via Rotterdam to Venlo in the Netherlands to visit family.The journey from London was seamless and very comfortable. The journey from Rotterdam to Brussels, where we had to change, less so. The train had a different colour livery and the cabins appeared far more cramped.In addition, we were told to arrive at least 45 minutes before the departure for no reason. It was not clear at all whether we could go through passport control at Rotterdam (not), so hanging around Rotterdam station in the bitterly cold wind wasn't enjoyable. Plus the train was late.

Compared to an airline flight, Eurostar is a good financial deal, mainly because Eurostar has a generous baggage allowance. However, it's really bothersome that Eurostar "deals" seem to be available only several months in advance. The closer you book to your travel date, the more cost prohibitive it becomes. I understand charging a lot more for a trip booked within a week or so of one's travel date; however, I would expect a more reasonable price when booking a ticket about a month in advance. In terms of the actual trip, the check-in process is lengthy, yet no more so than an airline flight. After check-in, you need to wait in an incredibly crowded holding area until about 20 minutes before your train's departure. On the train, the attendants were attentive and helpful. Lastly, our train was on time.

Reservation 7WVPGGI wanted to take a "train+hotel" package to visit the Harry Potter studios for my child's birthday.Once the order corresponding to my dates has been validated on the Eurostar website.I book tickets for the Harry Potter studio thinking that everything is OK except that Eurostar tells me that my order is canceled due to lack of space in the hotel.Why did you charge me when you are not able to honor my request.I find this unacceptable, I must wait to be recredited for the amount you owe me before I can take anything back.Not everyone.de can afford to place several orders at the same time.I also risk losing my Harry Potter tickets (366 euros) ifOnce recredited there are no longer the desired dates.I do not recommend your site at all.No star would correspond more rather than one!

I had hoped this would be a better experience than Network Rail in the UK but it was nearly as grubby and the seats in Standard had even less knee room. Same old security hassle as the airport, in fact rather more given some airports are using improved screening. Crowds of people, inadequate toilets (men and women had to share when we travelled). Immigration was efficient though. Gare du Nord is tired and bleak and we had to queue 15 minutes to get a Metro ticket , number of machines wholly inadequate -  when will the Metro use touch and go like everyone else? Given the prices Eurostar is hardly competitive with flying which is a pity, OK if you live in London I suppose.

I paid 445 euros to be firstI made the same trip with friends a few years ago and it was impeccable: good seats, impeccable service, careful meals at a reasonable price.This time, the comfort of the chairs was mediocre, it was cold, and the meals were terrible.For what ?

I booked a Eurostar package rather last minute ie return journey London to Paris inclusive of hotel with breakfast. The price was great, and the hotel was as described on reviews. It ticked all the boxes ie location, cleanliness, quiet non smoking room, breakfast, wifi, 24 hr front desk service, room nice and warm.
The toilets are a disgrace in the departure lounge - too few and must they be communal first men and women- utterly filthy!! Need to get whoever is supposed to clean them proper training
This is the way to travel!  So much better than air travel.  Staff are friendly ( and they don't treat you like a terrorist), it runs smoothly and you are straight into Paris.

The staff and organisation at the London end was faultless, efficient, polite and helpful staff. We left on time and arrived in Paris on time. However the return journey from Paris was awful. I was travelling with my family who had come from New Zealand to experience French  joi de Vivie I can’t believe how rude and unhelpful the staff were. I tried to explain to the woman marshalling us and blocking off all routes that the children with me had New Zealand passports and she had blocked them off from their parents but no she just shouted move, move. Eventually we managed to get back together as a group only to find ourselves in the freezing cold waiting for passport control the line wasn’t moving but the people in the booths were having a wonderful time playing on their mobile phones and laughing at the idiots waiting for them to take any notice. Then when there was only a little time to get to the train we finally got through passport control only to find that the lady had once again blocked off any routes leaving everyone confused and unable to move. Do they call this service because we certainly didn’t . Sorry Eurostar we won’t be using you again and it’s such a shame when the London end service was impeccable. They certainly won’t be recommended in New Zealand when the family return.

We were among the 40,000 potential passengers that had our trip to Paris cancelled at the last moment.  We milled around in the St Pancras station, frantically trying to get to Paris another way, but were unable to get flights as we were unwilling to spend another 2,000 pounds for a flight to Ireland with a 9-hour layover.  Because of this, we lost expensive hotel bookings and tours that we could not cancel in time for a refund.   We also we out the money we spent to take the train/tube from Oxford to St Pancras, around $500 for our group of 4.    This basically spoiled out whole trip, as we had to get to a certain point in Paris at a specified time.  We did receive refunds from Eurostar for the train trip itself, but lost thousands of dollars on other portions of the Paris visit- non-refundable hotel reservations and tours.  Advice:  don't even think about this wretched train.  It was even cancelled earlier in the same week for a French workers strike.   Only book same-day, if at all....

Travelled 20th December for birthday celebrations, getting the 1st train out of London & last one back. Five stars go to the 9080 Team, especially Pierre, together with Sarah & Gina. They made the start of a fabulous day absolutely wonderful. An absolute credit to Eurostar, top class service  -  Thank you so much!!! -x-x-x-

First trip in December 2022, outbound train canceledSecond trip to spend New Year's Eve, train was canceledAs I had a voucher for €314 at the first cancellation, it is impossible to obtain a refund, balance sheet of lost costs, the hotel which was not reimbursed to us €400, nor the Lion King show , 330€ or more than 1000€ and the customer service replies "these are the conditions", I regret having trusted Eurostar because the conditions are incredibly unfavorable for users
Easy trip with great staff who helped us find our way. We would highly recommend. Love comfort class!
Eurostar disappoints: delays, discomfort, and poor service; an overall unpleasant travel experience.

Traveling by train is nice. For this reason we went by the Eurostar fromBrussels to Amsterdam. First impression was good; easy boarding, departure  on time, comfortable seats etc. However, the total amateurish service onboard destroyed our experience and travel moods. Breakfast arrived very late, the coffee was cold and there was nothing to serve!!! Only one tray remained and since the expiry date had passed it could not be served. We will take the car next time.

Hello everyoneWarning regarding your journey with Eurostar.Let me tell you that we had booked at standard rate and that's where the problems startedI have been trying to cancel our trip for some time now due to my wife's serious health problems. They direct you to the insurance taken out online but the latter asks you for a cancellation certificate which cannot be given to you because we booked at the standard rate... so no trip and therefore no refund... .only a change of date is planned but again you have to pay.... too bad... this stay promised to be wonderful... happy holidays to all

First and last time with Eurostar.On the way back from London all trains were cancelled. Without communication and/or help from Eurostar, I was able to obtain a new ticket for the 31st with pain and difficulty. Now we have been standing still at Lille station for 45 minutes on New Year's Eve. With the message that we have to be patient.Well, I'll just take the plane again!Very very very bad

Awful- flying far more reliable. Travelling using vouchers from a cancelled train last year (cancelled on morning of departure). This year outbound train was delayed by over two hours and current delay for return is at 20min (held in awful conditions in Gare du Nord - made worse as boarding gate b is closed for maintenance). Never again!!

Like many others, if zero stars was an option I would have chosen it. Last minute cancellation on all trains. No refund, no compensation, no apology. Stranded in London without accommodation, lost our hotel in Paris and the Moulin Rouge booking we had saved for and arranged as a new year treat. Hundreds of pounds out of pocket. They cancel when they like and you have no rights apparently. Utterly disgusting. They have a monopoly on the London-Paris journey and are clearly making a lot of money for some very rich people whilst treating the public with contempt.I personally will never use EurNOstar again and would certainly advise others not to. Be careful people.

By far the worst company in history. They don’t help you at all. They canceled my train ride and didn’t  reschedule me. I got stuck in Brussels with which ruined all of my New Year’s Eve plans in London. The tickets to go London are fully booked for 3 days. They only offered to give me  the refund amount of the ticket and up to $170 euros for hotel loss but this is Christmas time and hotels are at a premium. I’ve lost 2 nights of hotel stay which is $500/a night plus a river new years cruise which I paid $600 for. A total of $1600 USD. In my opinion run from this company it’s better to just fly and avoid them all together. P.S. their Staff barely knows who to speak English and Spanish and have poor customer/service communication skills.

I have booked twice for a holiday to London during the end of December. In 2022 there was a strike of the union. All trains from Europe were canceled. This year, I I tried again and this time, they canceled the trains 1 hour before departure due to flooding in a tunnel under the Thames. Of course they can't help it but when you try to reach them, there is no one able to help. Rebooked everything and they gave me seats scattered over 4 different carts. I am traveling with kids, so how am I supposed to look after themThey only gave you the option to change seats after you booked the new tickets. But there are no seats left. No telephone number you could reach, just a lousy form. I wonder if they will respond before my departure date. I am so disappointed and will never use the Eurostar again. Buying a plane ticket is maybe more expensive, but at least I can be sure that I arrive on time at my destination. Eurostar, please get your act together. I have only experienced chaos with this company. So please avoid this company unless you want to take the risks.

I loved this journey. It went very smoothly and the staff where great. Food and drink was nice. I was lucky to travel first class so lots of space and comfort. Highly recommended. Although no delays for me - no idea what it is like when delayed

An absolute shame, they have canceled all the trains for the day and have not given notice, we have realized when we arrived at the station that we had to make a living because they have not given any solution.The trip and New Year's Eve have destroyed my family and hundreds of other travelers.If you want a 100% calm and safe trip, save yourself from possible mishaps like ours and book a plane, you won't have so many problems.

Terrible!!! Canceled all trains two hours before our departure.. We had to stay an extra day in Paris, plus by a very expensive flight the next day to London. We originally booked the train (even though more expensive than flying) to give our kids a new experience .. never again.. Complete joke!
Efficient que management.Quickly processed through security and passport.Easy waiting area.Prompt boarding.Very efficient and pleasant staff.

We travel from Amsterdam central to  Paris-Nord and back to Amsterdam central on 12/25/2023. International train like euro star, not letting us pick our on seats for premier class, what a shame. Train runs very slow and noisy compare to other same class/Type international trains. Baths room one that i tried to use have water spilling all over the floor. nothing but DISAPPOINTMENT,  by the way this was my First ride in euro star and for now  and not willing to give it a try again.
Little delay for December 26 and a very efficient service on the train with a hostess (Tourya) who did everything to make our trip pleasant

A disgraceful experience. Waited 2 hours in the multiple queues despite arriving earlier than the directed time. The excuse given was "strict border controls". Then had small kitchen (pairing) knives purchased in Switzerland confiscated despite not being listed as prohibited items. The train left 40 minutes late. Never again. I'd recommend flying.

PROS*  It's iconic and sleek and classic- I love it*  The famous name conjures luxury and a new era of train travel*  The sleek smooth nose trains are incredible and look so shiny and massive and impressive*  The train is smooth and silent*  Major transportation method from London to Paris and Amsterdam*  Travel directly from one city center tother city center *  It's a better way to travel than flying- convenience, location, hassle, etc... it is certainly greener and maybe it costs less too*  Traversing  under the English Channel is a big perk*  Enjoy whizzing past the Dutch, Belgian, French and English countrysides with adequate sized picture windows*  Reserved seat only provides a secure spot and a modicum of comfort*  Passport controls (at least in Amsterdam and London) seem to move efficiently and smoothly*  Prices are very much less expensive months before departure, but there are sales sometimes*  "Frequent traveler" program; website and smartphone application*  Food available for purchase (I didn't do that)*  For train enthusiasts (present company included), there is the extra tourist adventure of exploring the large international urban train stations.*  I understand that it is merging with Thalys which provides service between France, Belgium and the Netherlands- I know nothing and have no experience about that except to say that Thalys also has the sleek and beautiful nose trains.CONS*  The trains are crowded and full (but everyone has an assigned seat)- adequate baggage space might be a challenge*  The website sometimes had journeys not posted*  Dynamic pricing is confusing and aggravating*  Once customs is completed, there is not adequate places to sit nor anything to purchase to eat nor adequate restroom facilities (I understand that passport controls only became required with Brexit two years ago; I hope that there are plans for upgrading and improvements"I VISITED THIS PLACE​"... ... because I've wanted to take this train journey ever since it started almost 20 years ago.  I expected something epic and memorable and everlasting and meaningful- after all, the name Eurostar is iconic.  I found out that this is... a train.I enjoyed every part of my experience.  I bought my ticket at least three months in advance, and not long after that, the price was double what I paid.  The passport control was smooth and not overly long nor tedious.  The waiting area was crowded and unpleasant.  Boarding was OK- I loved the long walk past all the attached carriages.  I had reserved a forward facing window seat and enjoyed the view every minute of my journey.  The 20+ minutes under the English Cannel was uneventful- I had hoped that it would be a triumphal amazing experience... except for total dark, how does one know that one is under the water?WAS IT WORTH THE COST?Yes!!  Buying early if you can is so worthwhile.WOULD "I VISIT THIS PLACE" AGAIN?Sure!!  I'm no longer obsessed with it as something that I absolutely must do, but it is efficient travel to and from London to the continent, and I'd definitely choose it againADVICES* I highly recommend this mode of transport between those cities- it's preferred over flying*  Book early to get best price and seat*  Be prepared for passport controls and crowded waiting areaFULL DISCLOSURE"I visited this place" with the intention and plan to write a thorough complete and "helpful" review of EuroStar and ​I have attach​ed and submit​ed many "helpful" photos here on tripadvisor, so if these did "help" you, please indicate that by tik​king the "thumbs up" 👍​ symbol.  Thanks.  --

French customs system down. Waiting with no explanation as train departure approaches. This follows on from strike by eurotunnel employees a couple of days earlier when my train was turned back. Very few explanations. Chaotic. Missed connecting train and had to rebook. Lost cost of connecting trains.

Trains were cancelled two days in a row with no communication beyond a text and email. Their contact centre was overwhelmed and could not take further calls - the lines also remained open strictly within their stated business hours.The website provided no live updates on the cancellations and in fact stated that the trains were running.Essentially you are trapped in the city until the trains run again with little to no information. Details of their compensation policy are also vague - they do not explicitly state what the limits to compensation are so you will likely be hit with additional costs that they will refuse to cover.

There was a strike on 21st December. These things happen, it's how you deal with it. The website and app offered a refund or e-voucher (both useless if you want to get home) or to book next day. Only you couldn't book the next day as all was blocked. So, misinformation which cost valuable time in re-loading and trying. The staff at Brussels Midi were entirely unhelpful and simply told me "bad luck". So, I cancelled my ticket and booked a hotel and flight for 22nd. On my way back through Brussels midi I noticed that a Eurostar was running. When I enquired, I was told that it was full but that I'd be reimbursed up to £170 for a hotel and for sure there would be space the next morning. Completely different information to that I received when I needed it. In summary. Eurostar don't care for passengers. They have a monopoly on the line so don't need to give a helpful or fair service.
Gathering from the SNCF platform at Gare du Nord, no line is organized so people push and pass in front. It’s really a mess… We arrive 1h30 early but leave late without being informed of course.

Went to the station in Paris trains cancelled. No notifations and when we asked the staff the response was "look on the web" Cost 700 euros to get to England with no chance to recoup money.Do yourself a huge favour and fly or get a ferry It will cost less and is more reliable

Upset with Eurostar's inability to email clients about the potential French strike. No information when my husband and I arrived to the station. I did not have a clue for my next steps. I had a prepaid reservation in Brussels. I was more upset when I had to miss checking in with the Marriott in Brussels. I will request for a refund for the departure ride and expenses lost due to rescheduling. I had to book a next day flight that cost 400.00 one way. I am hoping my Eurostar return will be better. If not, then I will request a refund. An awful day!

We were stuck in France and they cancelled all trains just before getting on. Had to spend way more on a late ferry. Would have been better if they said about the cancellation earlier but next to Christmas it is not fun (21,12,23)

They cancelled the train 40 minutes before departure time. Passengers stuck in the departure lounge with no way out.In general eurostar is much more expensive than flying, is slower and now they just cancel trains after passengers have been through passport control. No staff to let passengers out of departure lounger in Rotterdam. TERRIBLE company.

SCANDALOUS. Impossible to trust with these 3 delays of one hour in 1 month + 2 trains canceled at the last moment without being warned! And the icing on the cake: impossible to request compensation on their website which says that I am not entitled to it each time despite the delays or disappearance of trains, impossible to write to Eurostar, impossible to get information . SCANDALOUS.

Great trip. Super nice priority in Brussels with our 7m daughter. Everything very well arranged. Unfortunately, the return journey is not a priority for babies, etc. The station itself is also very different than in Brussels. So from Brussels great and back ok. Toilets on the train are dirty and very small. I don't understand how people can/do change their babies in that. Bad...

An experience not to be repeated ! From booking in onwards it was terrible. The waiting area is grossly inadequate for the amount of people booked onto trains with no seats available until the first train departed but still over an hour stood around ! Coffee outlet very slow and a somewhat mediocre product. Train was filthy on the outside, not able to see much through windows when sun was on them. On board the seating is not great with barely enough legroom for tall people. Cafe/ bar service very limited with one not having any hot water for drinks and other one unable to process payments. Glad to get off in Rotterdam! I was under the misguided impression that this was somewhat of a slick, well run service . .  .  .  . Not at all !  No better than British Rail tbh

Compassion and understanding is non existent. Before you book any tickets make 100% sure that no one in your family gets Acute Myeloid Leukaemia, which will require a stem cell transplant, making it impossible for you to travel for at least 12 months. I did not ask for my money back, just a voucher so I can book when all this if over. NO was the answer. I am still reeling, our future is already so uncertain, you don't expect such harsh unkindness from a big company. I was told I can move the dates. So on top of all the hospital appointments and all the stress, I have to remember to keep moving the dates of travel  I guess Eurostar has no clue just how much this changes everyone who is connected lives. Maybe I am extra sensitive because I don't know if my partner will survive this ordeal. But really, it does not cost you any money to reverse my payment to a voucher to be used. granted I will only know by 3rd quarter of 2025. Welcome to our world were nothing is the same and nothing is guaranteed. Note the travel date is for August 24, but this review does not allow a date in the future.

While the seats are reasonably comfortable, the space to actually work on the train is limited and not suitable for extended (i.e. more than, say 1/2 hour) of work. This is exacerbated by the non-existent internet from getting into the train (why no connection at St. Pancras?!?) and all the way through the UK. Now that England is no longer a part of the EU, getting from London to other parts of Europe has some new challenges. The good news is there are a lot of options, and depending on your time, physical constraints, and budget, you can get across the channel without worries at all.FIRST THINGS FIRSTCrossing from England into the EU does require you to clear border security on both sides of your journey. I realize this is a no-brainer, but you do need to make allowances for your time and arrive early in order to move through what can be a staggeringly long line at airports and train stations. Here are a few ways to get across the channel.THE EUROSTARLeaving from London St Pancras Station, the Eurostar is absolutely the best way to cross the channel, and they know it. Your best friend when it comes to buying a ticket on the Eurostar is time. The Star uses dynamic pricing, so the sooner you can buy your ticket, the better and the cheaper. Walking up and grabbing a ticket on the same day can be very expensive.Arrive early at the train station and clear border security as soon as you can. I arrived a few hours early simply because I would much rather sit and have a coffee before the trip than stress wondering if I will make my train. There is food on the other side of the crossing in the station, along with a huge waiting area.The EuroStar is absolutely a premium experience and a well-run machine. I recommend this experience to everyone, even if it is a little more expensive. The train will take you directly to the city center station with your baggage in hand, thus no need for transportation, airport transfers, or waiting around. If you are on a time crunch and want to maximize your time, take the EuroStar.THE AIRPLANEThere are some great deals from London to your destination city in the EU, many under $100 one way. Again, time is your friend; buy early if you know your schedule in advance. Waiting will cost you more. Speaking of additional costs, these low-cost airlines make their money by charging you extra fees for everything from baggage to a soft drink. Make sure you check your baggage allowance before you buy a ticket; by the time the final bill arrives, you may not be too happy. I would also keep in mind the amount of time you will spend waiting for baggage, clearing border security, and finding your way into the city center. If you are on a weekend trip to Paris from London, the EuroStar is the play.THE BUSThis is an interesting option but usually reserved for backpackers on a budget. If you have the time and are looking for more of an experience on the cheap, this is your route. There are a number of different bus companies that run from the EU to London; I usually ride the FlixBus. I was traveling from Antwerp, Belgium to London, and I bought the ticket the day before my ride and paid about $40.Expert Tip: Buy a sandwich, some chips, water, and a few cookies to share with a friend for this trip. The bus does have a bathroom on it but only makes one quick coffee break stop for this ride (15 minutes). Euro truck stops are not like the massive American stops; they are small with not a lot of options. Even getting that coffee in fifteen minutes is a hassle, and you DO NOT want to get left behind.I actually had time and really enjoyed cruising through the European countryside. I like the idea of slowing down on trips and having a look. The bus stops in a few towns to load and offload passengers; the key is not to worry and sit back and enjoy the ride.Eventually you will arrive at your crossing point for The Channel train; this is where things got interesting. Like any crossing, you have to clear border security, the same on a bus.Expert Tip: The traffic line at the crossing might be extremely long, and I have heard of people having to wait up to FOUR HOURS to be loaded onto the train. Keep this in mind and know it’s not the driver's fault; if anything, I would buy him/her a coffee because they have to do this wait all the time.The bus receives a number that is its place in line for the train. When it’s time to go, the bus pulls through a massive scanner (scanning for what, I don’t know) and then pulls over for border security. At this point, everyone has to come off the bus with passports in hand and get cleared. The driver has to wait for everyone, so if someone is having a problem, the bus will wait as long as it can for that person. I personally pulled up a chair outside the station and enjoyed the fresh air.Eventually, the bus is loaded onto a train car. THIS was a fascinating experience. If you have a problem with small spaces, maybe this route is not for you. The train car is more like a boxcar, and the bus cannot run its engines inside the car, THUS no air conditioning for a bit. When loading is complete, you can exit the bus (on the train car) and enjoy the train car's air conditioning, but it can be tricky for people who have a problem with confined small spaces.The ride took about an hour or so; I found it fascinating and made a few new friends outside the bus on the crossing. When you arrive in England, you go through the same procedures, but in reverse. The bus unloads and eventually finds its way to the freedom of the highway system and into London.Expert Tip: Traffic into London is horrible; by this time, you may be feeling a little stressed. The trip (for me) took about eight hours, but just try to endure, especially when you hit the traffic in London; you can be so close to the final station and just be sitting there, it grinds on you.Final thoughts on the bus route under The Channel: I don’t think I would do it again if I had the choice. It was definitely an experience, it was cheap, and works if you are not on any kind of schedule, like you woke up that day and wanted to go to England. Otherwise, you will lose a full day, and maybe that’s not worth it. Up to you. :)OTHER OPTIONSThe other option I found was to take the ferry across The Channel. I would assume this would be a lot like the bus as far as time constraints and hauling your stuff around, but above the water. I didn’t take this route this time, but I would say it’s worth a Google search to see if it works for you. I would say if you have much more than one roller bag or a backpack, it would not be worth the hassle, but who knows?CONCLUSION:The Eurostar is the best ride, but buy your tickets early; the price can double the closer you get to your departure date. The plane is a good idea; again, buy your tickets early, look for hidden fees, and consider the costs of ground transportation to the city center. The bus is cheap and an adventure, but be prepared to lose the day. The ferry is another adventure that looks fun, but be prepared to lose a day and drag your stuff to

The Second time I have taken the Eurostar train from Amsterdam Schiphol to Brussels snd both time it has been terrible in terms of both finding the right train and right seating, and both times I have been told that even though I have my ticket that says my seat number on it, I don’t have this seat and I have to give it up when the person who «actually» has this seat comes. We have travelled with euro star twice in twenty years. It has been delayed each time. Last month we were excited to go all the way to Aix en Provence. Dirty seats , chewy gum ,cramped up luggage , smelly passengers with BO. Terrible terrible terrible rather fly then use this overly priced crap train . REFUND ME NOW

Never travelled by Eurostar before, personal experience our train from St Pancras to Brussels Midi was on time both ways, the train itself was comfortable with enough legroom. Travelled business class. On checking in, told our seats had been reallocated and that my wife and I were now seated in separate carriages. Not a word of apology.Never again.

worthless company, cancels a train to Paris at the last minute, while the hotels can no longer be canceled and that cancellation happens without demonstrable reason. I suspect the train is not full enough, smacks of deception!

The Eurostar departures area (at St Pancras) is a disgrace, basically because it is too small.  The seating provided is totally inadequate for the volume of travellers.  Most people have to stand or sit on their bags.  Refreshments are limited.  The toilets are poorly ventilated (hot and smelly).  So avoid checking in early, and do all your shopping and loo breaks in the main station (which is very pleasant), before check-in.Embarkation is chaotic.  This is made worse by the facts that A) travellers have to manage their own luggage (unlike at an airport where there is a separate baggage handling process) and B) the Eurostar carriages are built with only one door to each carriage.  So you have a significant number of passengers with multiple heavy cases who can barely lift them onto the train.  Then they have to negotiate the entire length of the carriage to find their seats through the melee.  It makes for an unnecessarily frustrating experience for everyone.The train itself is pretty comfortable.  On the other hand, the selection of refreshments is pitiful, and on my train the Café Metropole were already running out of stock within 20 mins of leaving London.  So either bring something from home or buy before check-in at St Pancras. Finally, if you are connecting to another rail service, either book open tickets or allow a long changeover time.   On my trip the outbound Eurostar was 40 mins late and the return Deutschebahn train was 60 mins late and decided to terminate short of the Eurostar station!

Quite mixed opinion on this Eurostar,As for boarding in France, nothing to report with smooth check-in and decent staff.The travel part is quite comfortable, the seats have sockets, the toilets are clean and the trains are on time.Disappointment sets in upon departure from London St Pancras station, notably by the staff who were absolutely detestable throughout check-in:- Arrival for check-in is separated by different lines to access the different trains (so far the logic is good), but these lines finally join into one for checking the suitcases: immense crowds and waiting .- When checking the suitcases and going through the security gates, the staff failed to show any ounce of patience or understanding towards their non-Anglo-Saxon passengers: they yell at you to put your suitcases down and separate your luggage! If you understand English well, good for you, if not, too bad for you!- Once this stage has passed, you access passport controls... Always the two lines which join into one to create even more waiting and supervised by staff who are always detestable and overwhelmed by the world. Second incomprehensible logic: only one gate for European passports and the rest for non-Europeans (and very poorly indicated)?? For a EUROstar, this seems complicated to me.- You finally land in a tiny waiting hall where you have to jostle to find a seat while the rest of the cattle wait standing for the platform display only 20 minutes before departure while we are summoned for at least an hour in advance !To summarize this experience, the gentlemen are ultimately French and definitely not English, with also an organization that absolutely needs to be reviewed across the Channel.

Brussels London was perfect. The way back was a disaster with no WiFi, invisible staff and no reliable information as connections from Brussels to Cologne are limited in the evening. Not recommended!!

When we arrived in the Eurostar terminal waiting area, it was severely crowded with many passengers having to stand. The mens toilets smelled terrible. Not a great way to start your journey and they could learn something from the terminal at Gare du Nord, Paris which was a pleasant environment.  The rest of the Eurostar journey was efficient and enjoyable.

I would not recommend Eurostar as a way to get between London and the continent when cheaper and faster short-haul flights are available.- The price booked months in advance was $125, which is more than many round-trip airfares in standard economy.- The cars are basic commuter stock with a few luggage racks added. They are cramped and uncomfortable for such a long ride. Seat pitch is a few inches better than standard economy on an airplane, but certainly not enough for the person by the window to get in and out without disturbing the rider on the aisle. (It seems like one advantage of trains over planes would be less need to pack in passengers to cover costs.)- The wifi is almost completely useless. Internet was unavailable for at least half the journey, and it was unreliable and slow for the rest of the time. Worse, availability was intermittent: it would often work one minute, and then not the next. Certainly don't expect to do work on the train.- The journey from London to Amsterdam and back was slow, except for the stretch between London and Brussels. I estimate 1/2 the distance took 3/4 of the time: north of Brussels, it runs about as fast as normal (i.e., not high-speed) regional rail.- Maybe the worst part is that you are required to get to the boarding area almost an hour before boarding, and the waiting area is *terrible*: cramped, insufficient seating, uncomfortable, and with insufficient air flow or cooling, and with nowhere to escape to and nothing to do. Contrast with needing to get to an airport prior to boarding, and being able to wander a large airside terminal with shops and restaurants. And pray your train isn't delayed: my outbound trip left 45 minutes late, meaning that I spent nearly two hours standing in the hot, cramped, and uncomfortable waiting area in St. Pancras.- Remember that Heathrow is only a 15 minute ride on Heathrow Express from Paddington, rendering dubious any comparative value from having the departure point be in the city center.My conclusion is that it has all the inconvenience of flying, including security theater and long passport control queues, the actual transit is far slower (compare the 4 hour trip to under an hour in the air to most of Western Europe), and it's not even cheaper to compensate. In short: Eurostar is something I have done once, and found zero redeeming value compared to flying.

Security was quite speedy but the train was delayed by 40 minutes. We had changed our kings cross tickets to be there earlier which cost us an extra £50 which we need not have done as the train was late

I travelled on the Eurostar after 19 years!  I travelled on the E320 from London to Paris where we changed to the high speed French train, the TGV, to Montpellier.We travelled on 2 September and bought our tickets about 4-5 weeks before travel via Rail Europe’s website and paid £141~ for a one way ticket.  You can watch the full review and a detailed overview of the Eurostar train and experience on YouTube at Luxury Vegan Travel.St Pancras station has something called ‘The Market’ which essentially  a shopping hall with M&S, Boots, Pret and many more options!  There is a WHSmith for reading/puzzles and a Holland & Barratt for healthy snack options.Unlike flying, there is no need to do an online check in.  It is just a case of packing your bags and heading to the train station.  Note, you need to arrive early.  Eurostar advise to arrive early, at least 60 minutes before departure and 90 minutes early if you pre-booked special assistance.Check in and collecting our tickets were easy!  After booking via Rail Europe we had QR code tickets which the desk clerk scanned and confirmed that all was okay.  We even managed to change our seats last minute to ones that included a table!  You will then pass through security and immigration.  You are permitted to pack liquids such as perfume, water and so on.  However, if you are taking alcohol then there are some restrictions.  Again, I have put links in the description of my video which tells you what you can and cannot take on board, I cover luggage allowances and what you need to do if you have excess or oversized luggage.We were sitting in Standard Class (cheapest).  There is also Standard Premier and Business Premier – which I cover in the YouTube video.  We were very happy with the Standard Class and we had also picked up some goodies beforehand!Standard Class is in a 2-2 configuration.  There are luggage racks at the beginning of the carriage for large suitcases and luggage and smaller items can be stored above the seat.  The seats dimensions are more generous than many economy airline seats!  There are (quite spacious) lavatories on board and a café with some meal deals and options for those with dietary requirements like me – vegan!The journey takes 2 hours and 16 minutes or so to get to Paris.  It is a very smooth and pleasant journey.  When we reached Paris, we were in a mad rush as we didn’t have a lot of time to get to our next station which required us taking the metro for two stops to Paris Lyon where we hopped on board the TGV to Montpellier.  The journey to Montpellier was equally smooth and pleasant.  The TGV is a duplex train with two decks – an upper and lower.  We were on the upper deck and had some beautiful views!Both trains had free WIFI and a café.I would definitely choose this option again as it is very enjoyable with beautiful scenery. In Montpellier, we stayed at the Courtyard By Marriott.  At the time of our stay, I am a Titanium member on the Marriott Bonvoy loyalty program.  Be sure to check this review out on YouTube at Luxury Vegan Travel which will be posted on 22 September 2023.Thanks for reading and hope this was helpful.

Eurostar Train Journey          AMS- Lon                           08 Sep 2023                           07:47 > 11:00                          We were on this train, we arrived as requested at Amsterdam Centraal Station at 06:42,The Eurostar train arrived at 07:45 eventually leaving at 08:05, we travelled relatively slowly to Rotterdam Centraal arriving in Rotterdam some 30 minutes late.The Eurostar train left Rotterdam, after some time the train manager announced that there were some problems with the train and its power supply. The train made various stops on the line eventually arriving in Antwerpen Luchbal at around 11:00. The train manager then advised that the train had lost total power but was able to maintain the air conditioning. At 11:30 the train manager advised that a train would be arriving across the platform to take us to Brussels Midi/zuid and we would be able to catch the 12:56 Eurostar to London St Pancras, and that the train would wait for all of the passengers from our train. At 11:40 a local running Belgium Railways train arrived which were able to board, this train made a number of stops eventually arriving at Brussels Midi/zuid at 13:15. There was an announcement on the Belgium Train that all passengers from the Eurostar train should on arrival at Brussels Midi/zuid make their way to the Eurostar Gate. My wife and then join the queue for the Eurostar train to London to be told that our existing tickets will be reissued at the Eurostar desk. We then stand in the queue until 14:15 when we reach the Eurostar desk and we are the issued at ticket for the 15:56 train to London:-                       Train 09145                       Brussels Midi - London St Pancras                       08 Sep 2023                       15:56 > 16:57                      These new tickets replaced TNPHCW tickets at this point we are given two food vouchers to the value of €9.00 each to spend within the Brussels Midi station, eventually we found an outlet willing to accept these.We boarded the 15:56 train 09145 and left Brussels Midi on time, as we progressed on our journey The Train manager announced that we would not be able to enter the Channel Tunnel due to a malfunction on the train. At 17:30 the train stopped on the line between Ruminghem and Audruicq. The train manager then announced that the driver would be leaving the train and may be seen on the left side of the train as the driver would be trying to locate and correct the problem. There was a further announcement around twenty minutes later stating the driver had not been able to resolve the problem.The train then moved again and stopped at Les Fontinettes, the announcement given advised the driver and the engineer would try resolve the problem, after about 15 minutes it was announced that the driver had been able to resolve the problem and we could continue our journey to London. Following this the remainder of our journey between Les Fontinettes and London St Pancras was uneventful arriving 1.5 hours behind schedule at 18:30 local time.Our Eurostar Journey between Amsterdam Centraal and London St Pancras should have taken in the order of 4 hours, our journey took almost 11 hours. This journey has been the absolute worst train journey we have ever undertaken, we missed a family dinner that had been booked in Hertfordshire for 18:00 we did not arrive until almost 20:00.While there is an acceptance that on occasions there will be some breakdowns or problems two Eurostar train malfunctions on the same journey beggar belief.Now we have contacted Eurostar for compensation we are offered a voucher for a journey between Amsterdam and London or if we wish a cash refund we will be given 50% of the original cost of that part of the journey.It would appear that Eurostar are much more interested in saving money in compensation that caring for their customers. A further and of greater concern is the conditions of the Eurostar trains, are the trains being maintained correctly and to a acceptable safe standard.
