They also were not able to provide a meat option on the way back to London which I think is rediculous given you pay so much for the ticket. We also arrived 25 min late on the way home which meant we had to run with 4 suitcases to get our connecting train. Worst customer service I've experienced in a long time.

Just constant minor annoyances. Long lines for security and customs. Crowded to the point of unsafe waiting area. Very limited food options. And for a 3 hour semi-luxury train journey is it too much to ask for some water? Apparently so!Please do better Eurostar.

We booked well in advance, Premium Economy and two weeks before the same seats were twice the price = book early.Well worth the additional money from economy.Half the time the train is above ground, so the scenery is great.

We have travelled on the Eurostar a few times London to Paris and also to Brussels and enjoyed the journeys however this trip Amsterdam to London was an absolute disaster. Train was due to leave at 7.47am and was cancelled that morning. Notification came through at 7am. Supposedly an operational reason, even the staff had no idea what the issue was. We were told to get on the next Thalys train that was going to Paris & get off at Brussels. As it was then a double capacity train the Eurostar passengers had to stand from Amsterdam to Brussels (if they couldn’t get a spare seat). If a seat was reserved the passenger was entitled to that seat so the Eurostar passengers had to stand or “get off” the train & wait for another train. We had upgraded due to our age 67 & 73 & and as a result of both having major surgery during the year so standing for hours was ridiculous and not just for us. Finally boarded a train to London in Brussels & for breakfast which we should have had on the booked train journey we were handed a paper bag with an orange juice, muesli bar & a croissant. If we wanted coffee we were told to go to the dining car. The girl said they had no idea where our breakfast was. Finally arrived in London late & missed our next connection. We were told the Dutch train service is known for having problems.

The trip for children traveling alone is really great, the staff takes care of everything really well! I was able to get off five minutes before the other passengers to be able to find my seat more easily. They accompanied me throughout my journey.

I am really disappointed with the service, I had the train at 6:35 p.m. I was at the station at 5:30 p.m. Arrival at the ticket counters to beep the ticket, Eurostar services. They told me it’s closed. I paid for a second return ticket

Train was cancelled from Amsterdam to London.  No announcement, email, or phone call made.  Station had no instructions.  Sent us to the wrong gate. Herded onto a train to Brussels hoping we could rebook it.  Sitting on the floor of that train now.  Worst service ever.  I will never do this again and I’ve taken trains for travel including Eurostar many times.

The worst non-experience. We were unable to make our trip due to an injury/medical emergency in the family, so we had to cancel our trip. I called a week prior to our booking date and time- maybe an hour before our future departing time. However, I was told because it was outside of the 7- day period, they could not cancel and refund us the money. They are extremely uncooperative and do not care at all about an hour difference of being outside of their “seven day period” for cancellations. We even had insurance, to which the claim couldn’t be made and was said to take 6-8 weeks anyway. Something that could have been cancelled in minutes ended up with us at a loss of $992 and a trip we couldn’t even make. Very unhelpful. Zero customer service consideration. I guess everyone should clearly “read the fine print” beforehand if they ever happen to get into an accident or injury or other emergency that prevents their trip.

Travelled on your service of 14:43 in carriage nr 1 from Gare du Nord to St Pancras at Business premier on 21/08/2023.We are regular travellers and usualy enjoying a good service and hospitality. But this journey the servise was not up to tha standard. Regards.

I was concerned by some of the reviews before we travelled but it turned out to be a far better experience than I'd read about. We'd had to change our booking from March to August because of industrial action but the process was easy and there was no additional cost to us. St Pancras is busy and yes the waiting room is cramped. This is because after Brexit they had to install both French and UK border control in the same hall which resulted in a significant loss of space and it wouldn't be fair to blame Eurostar for this. Bad scanning the same as at most airports - a little manic but if you relax and  just go with the flow its fine. On board the train was a great experience. Standard Premier loads of leg room and space for cases. Lovely smooth ride compared with the journey down from Yorkshire! Meals provided - not quite to my taste but the parts I did like were good quality with wine and coffee. Travelled to Lille and trains there and back punctual with the same level of service both ways. Same waiting issues at Lille as London with two sets of border control but not an issue. Generally seemed well organised. Would be more than happy to travel with Eurostar again based on this experience and for us it works fine - it's just not like walking up for a UK internal train journey and you can't expect it to be. We've had plenty of queuing at airports and the Eurostar experience seemed a lot less stressful than some of those! Glad we did it.

We traveled from Rotterdam to London. And return. Check-in in Rotterdam went quick however the waiting area is way to small and very inconvenient.  In London it was even worse as there were more trains and it was so busy.  We had to stand and wait for quite a bit, as you are asked to come one hour in advance.  Inside the train is what I expected.  It is a shame that we were traveling backwards.  But don't do this trip if you think it is a scenic trip.  Best this was the travel time and arriving in the middle of London.  And for us Rotterdam was easy and quick to get to too.  Price wise it was also a better option than flying.

All I want to say is that other reviewers nailed that when they mentioned the lack of station seating and overcrowded trains. You simply must get your tickets in advance and then remain committed to your time because they demand 50 euros if you want to change your schedule. The trains themselves are clean and well maintained and I don't think in America we can ride the rails at 150 miles an hour.

What is the F’ing point? After arriving 5 minutes late thanks to the rubbish tube system in London, we were told we had to wait 7.5 hours for the next departure and pay more. After hanging around in front of the London Library all day because they don’t allow luggage inside, we returned for our departure 90 minutes early only to find no seats available in the waiting areas, kids everywhere because they travel free on Eurostar, and no bars, shops or restaurants (only fast food). What a disaster and should have flown.

You should be able to put a note for the outward journey and one for the return journey.In Paris, access to trains has improved considerably with queues well organized by departure time.On the London side, it’s a disaster! We don't know where to go. Whether you arrive 30 minutes or 2 hours early, you queue in complete disorder, traveling for miles. And we end up running to catch our train!!! Arriving 1 hour early, I almost missed my train (there were several of us in this case…). Stress, fatigue, annoyance… it’s very damaging to the quality of the trip and the image of Eurostar.It’s all the more a shame as the train journey itself is rather pleasant (after the hour of stress of standing around).

I had hotel at Baker Street with 7 min walk. All reviews said to get early for train London -Paris. Our train 8:01am. So, we reserved 2 hours, and....it took us 30 min from hotel to waiting area for train... Included 7 min walk from hotel to Baker St Tube Station - 10 min metro 🚇 ride- walk 6 min to ticket/passport control and 7-10 min all process to waiting area....now stuck in waiting area for 1.5 hour.... have to apologize to my kids that wake them so early....maybe it is early morning 6:30am and it different from other reviews and videos that recommend 2 hours arrived early. It's packed with people, but 20 min before 7am train people were gone and we had plenty of seats.

It's okay. If you live in or near London then sure it might be a good idea, however we travelled from South Yorkshire and I wish we'd just flown. I've travelled eurostar many moons ago and my memory was a good one. Since then though, Eurostar have got new trains, and unfortunately like the rest of the UK, they've decided we like sitting on ironing boards. We travelled to Amsterdam and after an hour, we were both so uncomfortable. The seats are relatively narrow, lack cushioning and legroom or any creature comforts for long journeys. The old trains used to have such comfy homely seats. EasyJet and Ryanair both have comfier seats. We had a cheeky nosey at the Premier seats too and they didn't seem much better. Certainly not hundreds of pounds better! All in all, meh really
Traveled from Brussels to London v.v.Security and passport control went smoothly. Waiting areas on both sides of the Channel were too cramped, but the journey was otherwise very comfortable.

The most overrated transportation option in Europe?? Old trains, not even remotely refurbished. Ears popping continuously, dirty windows, dirty interior. Honestly they sell as an option to flying? Barely. Prices aren't cheap either. An experience thats it. And stop advertising you have wi-fi. You don't and thats ok cause the train is going 300 km/h, just stop saying it's there, it's not.  Waiting area was packed, standing room only.   NOT a premier level of service all around.

Absolute chaos  - insanely crowded - both at London and Amsterdam stations - not enough seats elbow to elbow.  I heard from family in uk that it’s much more pleasant to fly and that Eurostar has gone downhill. I believe it.
From Brussels to London. The train was running almost on time. No problems for the rest.Because there were 4 of us reserving, we were automatically put in a Carré, which was nice.

I’ve travelled several times with Eurostar and on this occasion I opted for the Standard Premier service. There is no difference in service to Standard until you are actually on the train. The seats are considerably different with comfort factors of very spacious legroom, adjustable foot rest, reclining function on the seat. There is also a reading lamp built into each seat located on the left hand side of the seat and a light located in the drinks holder adjacent to the drop down table. The seats were incredibly comfortable including a fantastic adjustable headrest.The morning outboard journey from St Pancreas the breakfast consisted of a slice each of fresh melon and pineapple, a Classic French Pain Aux Raisin that seemed fresh, a chilled carton of orange juice and a Yeo Valley organic raspberry yogurt. Fresh tea and coffee was served several times if required. All served with glass, porcelain crockery and metal cutlery. Overall a very good service. The crew were very calm, professional yet attentive.The evening inbound journey from Brussels the light snack consisted of 2 choices. I opted for the chickpea and feta quiche (this was absolutely delicious even though I’m not a vegetarian). This was served with hummus and a couscous with Moroccan spices, a baked roll, a portion of butter, an apple flan/cake with a sweetened crème. At the time of serving a choice of wines including dry white, rose, sparkling and red were available or soft drinks. The white wine was dry. However, it was palatable. Again the crew were phenomenal and extremely professional and throughout the journey they continued to serve additional drinks and hot drinks to those whom required. The carriage was very clean and presentable and when boarding being met and explained where my allocated seat is was a nice welcome and the crew member used an iPad device with each customers name and seating plan, very efficient. It’s a shame the UK mainline train operators did something similar.I would say the lounges after check in both in St Pancreas and Brussels looked outdated and I felt there needed something to jazz it up. Maybe some very large TV screens located around with some slick promotional footage promoting the Eurostar routes and the different services available to both give passengers something to watch and to show passengers the differences with even live time screens of the trains like you can see with aeroplanes. Would I recommend Eurostar? Absolutely because it’s very convenient from central London to the heart of a European city without the need of transfers. Would I recommend Standard Premier? 100% if you want a more spacious seating with a very professional crew.

Actually, it's THE alternative to flying! But I've never experienced such stress. Changing stations in Paris was catastrophic. No signposts, overcrowded metro. Then the Eurostar: customs and baggage checks underground. Long, narrow lines, bad air, hot. Then the train is delayed. No working WiFi on the train, even though it's advertised on the monitors. Making phone calls is impossible. BEWARE of pickpockets in Paris and London who take advantage of the Eurostar chaos. And then there's the outrageous price.

They left me stranded in Amsterdan after asking us to vacate the train to London.No communication and no-one from the company at the desks to help the passengers. Unacceptable customer care, not even compensating me for the day's work lost.
Lovely train journey! A big thankyou to Ingrid who was working the bar/cafe.... thankyou for being so helpful and giving me your pen! 😃

Had a very different experience to recent reviewers. Online booking process is easy with good follow up updates and travel essentials. Long queue on arrival at St Pancras but well  organised and through ticket entry, security and passport in 15 minutes. When there are lots of trains the seating area is limited but it’s not a long wait. Premium economy and service excellent experience and value. Just a simple and enjoyable way to travel London to Brussels in 2 hours…don’t even think about taking the plane!.

The main advantage of Business Premier is that you skip the long lines for security and passport control. Especially useful during peak times like the summer. You can also board a different train from the one you booked very easily.The use of the lounges is another way to avoid the crowds while you wait for boarding, but they don’t compare well with good airport lounges. Same for the meals. They may be supervised by Raymond Blanc but are nothing special and nothing like a good BC meal on a plane.The reason I give two stars is really that service in the carriage is almost absent and not really different from Standard Premier. For the very high price you pay, Eurostar does not offer an experience comparing well with Business (or for sure First) on a plane. Ok if money is no issue and you want to skip the lines.

On the 5th July we boarded the Eurostar in London to our paid destination being Amsterdam. We'll into our trip I received an SMS and email stating the train will not be going to Amsterdam due to storms and we had to get off in Brussels. No one from Eurostar assisted us in how to get to our final destination. Which travel company notifies you well into your journey that service is cancelled and just dumps you in a location without any further assistance. We had to find our own way there. Eventually we did after another 2 trains, bus and taxi. How dare you Eurostar charge us for a service you never delivered on and even after you emailed me saying I am entitled to a full refund you only refunded us 50%. Absolutely disgraceful. If you are thinking of using the Eurostar don't. They wouldn't know the meaning of fulfilling their travel commitments or assisting customers.

Eurostar has the monopoly over passenger journeys through the tunnel but for how long?! With talks of other operators potentially joining the market, Eurostar need to up their game. The Eurostar terminal at St Pancras always feels so chaotic and crushed, it does not make for a pleasant start to a trip. There's a few reasons for this....1. The demand has simply outgrown the terminal.2. The scheduling of services is too close together for the size the terminal.3. Now that ES are not stopping at either of the Kent stations it means those passengers are having to come in to London. Arriving at the ES terminal in St Pancras is quite embarrassing to us Brits, the queues snake through the station making it look totally and utterly unorganised. This also means that the retail area prior to check-in becomes crowded and exceptionally busy. Talking of retail, the offer in the departure lounge is quite frankly an embarrassment. The duty free is now in what was the tiny WHSmith, any more than 5 people in here and it's a squeeze. There are two coffee shops which again are way, way to small for the number of passengers. Every time I have used ES the passenger numbers have exceeded the seating on offer meaning thoroughfares are blocked by people sitting down. I'd question the safety of the terminal pre-departure if there was a fire or other emergency as people will quite frankly be crushed. As boarding is announced the clambering for the escalator to the platform is feral. Yet when you do get to the platforms it feel spacious and able to accommodate all passengers comfortably. Of course St Pancras is a beautiful Grade I listed building so expansion is difficult but this is not the same for Kings Cross just across the road. Currently East Midlands services stop at St Pancras adjacent to the Eurostar platforms yet these services could do to Kings Cross as per other Eastern / North Eastern services. That way more space would be created for the Eurostar trains. Onboard Eurostar in my opinion has lost its zing. Whilst the pandemic and inflation have of course impacted finances, visitors number are showing a significant return, yet what incentive is there to retain the loyalty of returning or new customers!More often than not I travel Standard Premier, more so for the extra leg room and generally less people. I have previously travelled in both Standard and Business Premier (more on these shortly). Standard Premier is laid out in a 2:1 configuration with some extra leg room. However the leg room is only particularly noticeable IF nobody is sat opposite you, if they are then it is often a case of knee on knee. Seats are.comfortable and have a small recline to them, however nothing which presents a significant benefit than completely upright.This cabin class can sometimes be c.£10 more than standard in which case it may be better value for money, more often however the price difference is between £30-£60. For this extra cost you have the minimal benefit of some extra room (if nobody is opposite) and a 'light meal'. When Eurostar say light meal they really, really mean light meal. Breakfast consists of 2 small slices each of melon and pineapple, a yogurt, small carton of orange juice and a small pastry. You also receive a bottle of water and offered a small (espresso size) tea or coffee. In my opinion this light meal is not value for money over standard class especially as drinks are only usually offered once per trip! In fact if you sat in Standard and ordered from the Cafe onboard you'd get more food for £10, larger drinks but less.lwg room, although again it's pretty similar to standard Premier if someone was sat opposite. Standard class does not include at seat service and there are more seats within these carriages making it seem a lot more crowded but the seats are quite comfortable. In Business Premier (usually c.£250 each way) you have access to a lounge (utterly pointless and lacking). The seats are the same as Standard Premier but with a 'three course meal' instead of a light option. There is also champagne provided. This class is by far the least value for money due to the size of the dishes. The Business Premier food is designed by Raymond Blanc OBE which therefore comes with a premium but the sizes are basically 3 of those you receive in Standard Premier for an extra c.£125. This really is where Eurostar are taking advantage of its customers. If Eurostar want to continue growing their passenger numbers and compete more with low cost airlines it MUST give passengers a point of difference. Rail travel used to have some glass and glamour but the 60's through to the present have pretty much obliterated that class and style. But the railway market is becoming increasingly competitive between operators especially with sleeper services. Now that Eurostar has merged with Thalys it has an opportunity but I have no faith that will use it. Thalys' fleet is old, much older than many other international operators so they are already behind. However they still have the only access to the tunnel between the UK and Europe. • Staff need retraining in customer service and etiquette. Eurostar is essential the rail version of Air France and as such a flag carrier. Staff need to reflect this in how they present themselves in both their uniform and manner when serving customers. • The uniform needs changing to present luxury regardless of class. The polo shirts for some are not a good representation of the brand. • The catering needs a complete overhaul to provide better value for money and again reflect the quality of the brand and the nation's it serves. • Whilst the interiors of the Eurostar trains are adequate they too should reflect quality and represent the brand. Other European international operators have better interiors such as Db Ice.• The terminals in London, Paris and Amsterdam need reconfiguring for both safety and passenger comfort. Brussels is more better for seating availability and quality of retail. I might sound like I've given Eurostar a hard time, perhaps I have but it's because I love the notion of direct UK to Europe rail travel. The who travel aspect is so much better than air travel. Sadly I feel as though customer experience and satisfaction are less priority than profit due to the need of 're-balancing the books' post Covid. Eurostar need to think like Emirates on rails.

Check-in on the CS Amsterdam platform is bad: at the end of platform 15 there is a kind of construction shed where up to 800 passengers can check in when the train is full. This means that there are a lot of queues and especially when it rains (in our case too) you have to wait outside.Train was delayed by 60 minutes (no announcement was made) and there were not enough seats to keep everyone waiting (also no point of sale for extra drinks, etc.).On the train you could not immediately go to the catering, they were also delayed, so there was also a queue here when the buffet car was open.On the way back to A'dam, the checkin at St Pancras station was a real hell, 3 (X 800 people) trains check in at the same time, while the capacity is calculated at a maximum of 1 train (800 people).Eurostar does capture the turnover but does not provide service. Staff on the floor were not very pleasant, were tired and reported that it was 'holiday crowds'. My bad experience was even confirmed that this situation happens regularly. Will I book Eurostar again? I would really like to because of the environment, but I refuse if the handling is so bad.

Having not been on Eurostar for over 10 years, what a shock! We thought travelling by Eurostar to Paris would be better than flying! oh were we wrong. The check in Process at London Kingscross is an absolute shambles. We arrived 1.5 hours before departure and still needed to be called forward for our train from the ridiculous que. The waiting area does not have enough seating and the toilets in the waiting area are disgusting, two cleaners were chatting outside and I mentioned to them that it was disgusting, the response was, go and tell customer services, come on guys your were outside the toilets and the smell was overpowering!   We paid premium seating but the seats were dirty and train on whole was just not cleaned. We ordered Gluten free meals and never got them! Again many excuses. Why would anyone want to travel in these conditions. Back to flying for us. I would say this is just corporate greed, maximise profit over customer experience. The only reason why I did not give them one star was the fact the Paris Eurostar was great, easy well organised check in. Clean holding area and lots of seats, just felt better. Unfortunately the UK side as always is slow and lacks any ownership for pride or customer focus.

I am traveling with Eurostar once a month approximately. When I book my trip, it is always mentioned that my Eurostar points will be added after my journey. However, I checked my account and what a surprise to see that my point have not been added to my Club Eurostar Points that could allow me to get free return tickets or other perks. I called Eurostar's customer service this morning and had the most inconsiderate person on the phone. I was explaining calmly that this is not fair because points should have been added "automatically" and what has been answered to me is that "you have to take responsibility over your Club Eurostar membership and connect once in a while to see if points have been added or not". For an "automatic process", this is quite a joke and I was expecting far better given the usual great service we have at the station and in the train. Also, as a recurring traveller, I am choosing Eurostar for ecological reasons but I will now consider taking the plane more often.

Yeah, we did it. no issues. Traveled back and forth from London to Paris at the height of the tourist season in July. One of our adult kids (a female), couldn't travel with us, so we took someone else (an underage, i.e., minor, teen male friend of the family with us). Never even bothered to ask Eurostar for a name change since we knew they wouldn't do it. And I wasn't about to spend $450 for another ticket. So, I did it myself using Adobe Acrobat (which of course is purely cosmetic). Strictly optional step here. There are agents around the ticket gates before passport control to help and do crowd control, but no one is hovering around right at the gate to check any names. And no, it doesn't flash your name up on any screens in big letters when you scan in. We just scanned our 'home-made' screen shots of the ticket bar code using our phones for the outbound journey (we don't use the app) and scanned the paper tickets for the return journey. Easy peasy. Passport control doesn't want to see your tickets and doesn't ask for them. Your tickets are not checked on the train. Good luck to you and enjoy your journey!

A connecting train was delayed to Brussels. We arrived with 30 mins until departure but Eurostar refused to let any non-business class through. There was plenty of time for people to go through. This is pure laziness by eurostar. As a result everyone was delayed over two hours and a half empty train left on time.

I used the Eurostar to go from London to Amsterdam, I was due to visit Rotterdam and Paris before taking the Eurostar back home. While in Amsterdam however my pregnant wife experienced a medical emergency and we had to rush home to a specialist hospital. I purchased separate Eurostar tickets from Amsterdam to London at a premium rate as they were purchased on the day for £430 for both of us. I contacted Eurostar well before I was due to train back to London from Paris to request a refund on the much lower £99 tickets I had purchased for this journey. Given the exceptional circumstances and that I had spent an additional £430 with them this seemed like a fair request, but all I was offered was a short term voucher, so short term it would be unusable in our current situation.

Fantastic experience apart from check in. Arrived 2 hours early to go through UK customs. If I had my time over I would have gone 75-90 minutes early. The process is fairly easy with a few passport checks and a screen scan. Passengers then wait for their train which is boarded about half an hour before departure. There was a host at each carriage who assisted with directions and luggage storage. There is an area in each carriage for large bags with medium and small bags stored above the seats. There was no issue with storage capability. The hosts serve free refreshments and are friendly and helpful (merci Raquel). The trip is about 2.5 hours and is smooth. Wifi can be patchy. Whilst waiting to board there is a food and coffee shop which has long queues. Also refunds of sales tax and some duty free shopping is available. There are escalators to the carriages.Don't panic if you are at the end of the boarding queue as the process is quite smooth. Disembarkation at St Pancras was also ok and it didn't take long to get to the underground trains.

Eurostar from St Pancras to Paris then return 5 days later. Waiting areas in both locations were over crowded and no seating available. It’s pretty obvious that the waiting areas are not big enough and the layout is in adequate. I found that the condition of the interior of the train has dis improved with staining on seats and carpets. The food provided is poor and again has dis improved over time. This used to be an iconic service and my recent trip was really disappointing. Eurostar need to up their service delivery especially the waiting areas.

Took the Eurostar from London St Pancras to Amsterdam. Traveling with the kids and going through the security line with no AC and then standing there for 45 min while we waited to run to the train was a bit annoying.I was fine with everything else aside from the most irritating thing. The internet was advertised as free and would be available point to point.Well after 15 minutes of burning up my battery with no success I asked an officer on the rail line about it. He said “ it’s no good in the UK, but will be better in France.” I can tell you that my family of 4 had access to the internet for about 30 min in total during our 4 hour train ride. This is super annoying because I had planned on doing work, catching up on some things -and do some research. I was only able to text a few pictures and write this review because I was so annoyed.The trip was fine, but no internet? Come on

Lousy service, overpriced. The train stations are not air-conditioned, the waiting area is too small, and there is insufficient seating for waiting passengers.  But they want you to show up 90 minutes in advance.  The train seats themselves are tightly packed and uncomfortable.  Lounge access is restricted to business premium, so beware, booking premium is not sufficient to get you to the lounge, which is air conditioned.The free meal included in premium class is inedible.Delays are frequent.  Our outbound train was delayed 1.5 hours. They offered a refund but required international wire transfer instructions without details on how much of a refund they would provide. Air travel is cheaper, faster, and more comfortable.
Good smooth ride. Comfortable seats. Took train from London to Paris. Went under the English Channel.

We had a great experience with Eurostar this month. Traveled by train from Edinburgh to London, then Eurostar to Paris. I nearly made the mistake of making our transfer in London too short - I thought 40 mins was plenty time for it. But the email I received when I booked my tickets said to allow up to 90 minutes to clear security and customs, and that check-in closes 30mins before the train leaves. So I allowed a transfer of 90 minutes at London. And this would have been fine, had our train from Edinburgh not hit a deer and sat on the line for an hour, before limping to a station and having to get another train to London.I thought about trying to rebook the Eurostar for later in the day, but I would have to pay all over again. I called Eurostar and a lovely lady calmed me and advised me to just get there as soon as I could, explain what happened, and they would help us.We arrived to a huge security queue exactly 30 minutes before departure. I found another lovely lady at the 'first class' entry who was most sympathetic to our situation and whisked us straight to the front to get our bags scanned.Our final lovely lady of the day was at the passport control, she ushered us through the crowd, straight to the front, and told us to run.We did. Bottoms on seats with 3 minutes to spare. Everybody went above and beyond on this occasion to ensure I didn't have a nervous breakdown and we made it on our family holiday. I cannot thank you enough.The journey was great. So fast. I hate airports and the whole experience of feeling like cattle when you travel by air. I loved getting the train.

We took the train from Paris to London.It was extremely well organised, and  very simple to go through French and English customs on the French side.I would recommend getting the “Premium” fare as you get a table between 2, as well as a light meal, and the experience is much improved.I would recommend getting this train every time as you save so much in airport transport, such as taxis.(the train goes from the heart of Paris to St Pancreas station in London)

Arrived 30min before departure but the queue was huge, When I scanned my ticket , it says that I was too late. I travelled Eurostar a lot of times, I never had that before, as long as the train was there, they could always let you in. In the new post Covid world, company like Eurostar wants to recover as many others which is affecting the attention to customer. The Eurostar agents were rude and said in the queue (where everyone was in the same situation) that we should have arrived 1h before and it was our fault that we missed the train. Poor world and poor planet! Next time I will rather fly as same constraints with the train now and much more expensive. Of course for this price wifi does not work in the 21st century between the 2 largest city in Europe. Avoid Eurostar, they don’t deserve to have you on board.

We really enjoyed our trip with the Eurostar to Paris. There was a delay on the way back but we received a partial refund. I highly recommend the business class ticket. There was a minimal queue for security and border control. The lounge was stocked with treats, drinks, and magazines. The service onboard was phenomenal.

Was told train was cancelled due to a strike and given a refund. had to book an expensive flight alternative. Whilst in London I checked at the station and the train was still running stuff very puzzled said never affected by the strike.
The seats are cramped when you have a seat with 4 seaters around a table. It's awful. Who designed the seats around the tables? People under 5' for children? It's ridiculous.

Our trip was booked months in advance. Before we had even arrived at the station we were having notifications from Eurostar that we would no longer have our initial chosen seats in the preferred quiet carriages, several times having to re choose. We were fortunate to still be able to sit together but I see others are not always so lucky. But the over riding issue with Eurostar is that they cannot cope - in London or Paris - when things go wrong. St Pancras and Gare du Nord have no space for queuing passengers for multiple trains. I was told by a passenger that in Amsterdam you have to wait outside - come rain or shine. At least we were under cover. Eurostar ask for 45-60 min arrival before departure on the ticket while also asking for 90 mins on their website.The departures area at St Pancras is halfway along the shopping concourse. We arrived about two hours before departure - our choice due to inbound travel timings to the station and we happy to sit for an hour on the concourse with a coffee from one of the many retail outlets and croissants from M&S. There is a very small easy to miss departures information screen at eye level outside a zig zag holding area for passengers. Fine if it isn’t busy, not so when busy as everyone is crowding trying to see. Or simply standing in front of it. When we arrived, mid-morning for an 1131 departure, departure timings were an average of about thirty minutes apart. The issue was they were already running late. You could not get into the holding area until your train number was called. I say called - but it is a member of staff holding up an A4 laminated card with the train time on it. The screen said we could enter the zig zag at 10am. Then it was pushed back to 1015, then 1030. There were no announcements, just the small screen. Eventually someone held up a card and started yelling 1131, follow me, and walked a train full of passengers off down the concourse to start a queue. Not only did this block off shop entryways, but you then had another snaking zig zag queue outside of Eurostars own departure area.  Clearly this is a routine thing as barriers were already in place to facilitate this. For a moment it felt a bit more organised and the queue slowly moved forward eventually joining the tail end of the snaking queue in Eurostars own departure area. 1046. After the snake you scan your ticket and proceed into the security check hall. You expect security halls to be lots of shouting with the emphasis on getting through. This one was, but with lots of stop starting to the lack of trays for the belts, and lots of peacocking managers and blaring walkie-talkies. On to top of that there were staff walking around yelling ‘anyone for the 1104’ - the train before ours. Eurostar won’t leave until they are loaded with all the scanned in passengers. Unlike an airline. Into passport control, still the yelling for missing passengers for the 1104. And then up onto the platform and settled in to our seats at 1146. Relief. There is nowhere to sit down all the way through the queuing system. The journey itself was uneventful and we finally felt able to relax. We travelled Standard Premier, which comes with a meal and dessert, bottle of water, and soft drink or wine or lager. Having a table seat certainly made a difference. It was all very pleasant from that point on, with attentive staff, and we arrived roughly twenty minutes late into Paris. After an amazing break of extravagance and indulgence, we knew what was coming - the return journey. We purposely chose to arrive closer to the 45-60 minute guidance and arrived at Gare du Nord a few minutes outside that window. We ascended the escalator to Eurostar’s departure point to find the train prior to ours was still not able to start going through. Their train was running 50 minutes later. Meanwhile more and more passengers were arriving for our train and the small holding area very quickly started sardining. Staff were yelling trying to keep the two trains apart, while also trying to keep a walkway clear for the group bookings - large parties of school kids - that needed frogmarching through. Priority was given to groups who then clogged passport control. All of this under a glass roof where the outside temperature was in the high twenties and the sun was out. We spent just under 90 exhausting minutes in this area, no one able to sit down, no water, were there were children and pregnant women, those struggling with the heat, all crammed in together. We then went into small holding queues that really made no sense in terms of how they were released, before being ushered forward a batch at a time toward passport control. Asked to show we had a UK passport, we were directed toward biometric gates. My passport refused to scan on one of the gates - a member of staff saying it did not accept UK passports, despite it was open for EU, UK, Swiss and EEA. She ushered me to the next one along. My wife who’d struggled with the same issue followed to the same gate I eventually passed through, to find her passport would not scan - to be told this gate does not work with UK passports..! She had to try four different gates. That was the French border control. We then has another set of biometric gates for the UK which were way more efficient. Security was way easier than the UK, almost instantly through, no messing about with trays. A simple efficient conveyor belt. And then into the departures hall with much welcomed air-con and over priced shops selling water. Our gate opened and we all sardined off toward it - to find a belt stopping us going further. After a ten minute wait we released. A moving walkway took us down to the platform level, which was interesting as the door to the platform was still closed. Mild panic ensued on the walkway with shouts of ‘get out the way’. Once on the train, we settled on it again became a pleasant experience. Despite leaving over an hour later than scheduled - which means we can claim compensation - we arrived back in St Pancras just 19 minutes late. Don’t get me wrong, the train itself is great. 180+ mph. Fab. It’s the bit before it that was just utter rubbish. We came home, from what had been a beautiful and relaxing few days, feeling utterly exhausted and in desperate need of a shower. Would I travel Eurostar again… highly unlikely.  It’s a real gamble I reckon. Once a train gets delayed it impacts every service after it as they have no way to segregate between the different departures.  They just do not have the space.  You have to wait for the train before you to be fully serviced before you can start your own journey. And that’s just not conducive to good customer service. Or experience. [Photos St Pancras, 5 July 2023. Return journey was made 9 July]

Everything about eurostar is one big disappointment from start to finish.The conditions are always unfavorable for the passenger and always very favorable for the company.Due to riots in Paris, passengers plans have changes and later journeys were cancelled. I would expect more understanding regarding ticket changes from the company. Unless you bought a horrendously expensive ticket ( Business Premium) there is not much what you can do.An untrustworthy company that is focused only on profits.I'd rather spend 10 hours on a bus than be taken advantage of again.

The journey from London to Paris was efficient and ran on time. The return from Paris to London was an absolute nightmare. All trains were running an hour late but the station signs indicated they were on time. Huge crowds built up in stifling heat in the Gare du Nord. There were no announcements. Absolute carnage travelling from Paris to London. Endless, disorganised, delayed cues with powerless staff unable to provide information to navigate the chaos. Triple the price of a flight, yet zero star rating! Avoid!

My adult children took me on a trip to Paris on the Eurostar train. We left London on time and enjoyed an incredibly smooth and quiet ride all the way arriving in Paris ahead of time. Eurostar successfully killed my life-long love of train travel. In June, I was stuck in London for hours with no communication from Eurostar as to issues related to my train. There were literally thousands of people at St. Pancras looking for help. None to be found. After hours of delay, Eurostar cancelled several trains. We have ridden the Eurostar a couple of times. Once in 2018 and again in June 2023. When we rode the Eurostar in 2018, there was a virtual aquarium as you went thru the Chunnel(perhaps meant for kids)-but cool nonetheless. We noticed they did not have it this last time so I asked one of the attendents if they still did this. She said she remembers the virtual aquarium but they have since stopped. Check in experience at St Pancras was easy and pleasant, well signposted and although busy, not chaotic. Departure lounge was comfortable and well serviced.Train itself was a bit cramped, not much in the way of leg room but luckily it's only just over 2 hours from London to Paris so it wasn't too much of a concern for me. Someone taller or with longer legs may think differently.Buffet carriage was a bit pricey.There was supposed to be onboard Wifi throughout the journey but the connection was terrible and I kept losing it.Announcements were in English, French and Spanish and kept us informed of progress along with safety announcements etc etc.Having come from the north of England first to London, it wasn't a quick way to get to Paris, but we were conscious of carbon footprint and are trying to cut down on unnecessary flying.

Waiting areas are dirty, toilets smell awful and too many people packed in a small place. Train comfort is ok but cannot match the comfort of the Thalys. Long queues for security and passport. Overpriced compared to flying. Staff is very friendly.

Winston who works on eurostar had the most patience during rush hour I could of ever imagined. Thank you so much for being ever so lovely and trying to help everyone (including myself). ❤️❤️❤️ Got me on the right track safe back home - what more could I ask for?

Customer service is diabolical.Two days before travelling, I received an email from Eurostar stating they have changed the seating plan.  When I checked I found that me and my partner were no longer sitting together - in fact we were seated 3 coaches apart.  I immediately contacted Eurostar- no reply.  I contacted again and was fobbed off by email saying - that’s the way it is.  I tried calling - they don’t answer.I asked at the information desk at the train station.  Bizarrely was offered a change of seating but still not anywhere near.Of course there was an offer of a different train at a cost of 100 euros.Whilst I can understand that there may need to be changes made due to logistical reasons, the terrible experience is trying to communicate and deal with Eurostar who clearly have very little regard for their customers. They have a real talent for letting you know that they absolutely don’t care.I cannot recommend using Eurostar and would advise you to explore all possible alternatives before placing yourself at their mercy.
Trip was great. Only problem was long wait checking in. We booked in months in advance to save a huge amount of money

Disorganized and chaotic and this is a Wednesday, arrive 60-90 minutes before is nonsense as they only let you board if your train is an immediate one, ques are massive leaving you possibly missing your train, staff are aggressively shouting at anyone they can and just pushed a guys wheely suitcase out of the que because he stopped to answer back, more stressful than an airport, will fly next time.

I haven’t gotten on the train yet and already unhappy with customer service. The journey is comfortable and scenic, and I was lucky to not be in a loud or packed carriage. Staff were friendly and helpful. The the journey is more expensive and less efficient than flying, but I am glad I tried it once.

Reasonably fast, but delayed. Back Brussels Amsterdam just canceled one day in advance. We'll have to figure out for ourselves how we can get back from Brussels. 09:30 in London in line to check in 17:00 in Eindhoven. Not that you say a quick trip. So we do more

I Love the Eurostar these trains are superb compared the the first trains I love the sleek design and the loyalty program I was in business class which was empty I was the only person in this class outward and return although the train was superb I was a bit let down by the lounge which was just dirty with no staff around but nevertheless I would travel business class again

My first trip on Eurostar.  Travelled from St Pancras to Disneyland Paris (Marne-la-Vallée), in standard premier.  Was impressed and the journey both ways was enjoyable and relaxing.  The staff were smartly dressed and pleasant.  It was a morning trip out and early evening trip back, so we had complimentary breakfast on the way out (croissant, yoghurt, apple juice and water) and a cold light meal on the way back.  Both were fine.  We'd chosen our seats online beforehand so we could get seats for two facing each other with a table, but on both journeys the trains were changed and seats reallocated to non-table seats.  As it turned out, on the way out we were allocated single seats, one behind the other, in a carriage which was primarily for disabled passengers, but it also had a few seats for non-disabled, and there was a whole unoccupied table for 4 which we moved to.  Nice quiet journey as there were only 3 other passengers in our carriage.  On the way back our seating had been changed to seats beside each other (no table) but we could have found table seats to move to.  As it was our first time on Eurostar I wasn't sure if there would be bar service on the way back so went off to find the bar/cafe.  I had to negotiate many carriages to get to it and then there was a long queue, with one man serving.  The problem being that obviously the aisles can only accommodate one person at a time but passengers had to queue back into the carriage before the bar, so there were people trying to get to it whilst others coming the other way trying to exit the bar.  All rather chaotic and the standard class carriages seemed very crowded/full compared to the relative calmness and space in standard premier.  The other thing that surprised me was that it was very difficult to walk when the train was in motion without stumbling and nearly falling onto passengers, so you wouldn't want to be carrying much in the way of drinks.  (By the time I eventually got back to my seat the bar service had been and gone but a drink had been purchased for me anyway, so there was no need to have made the perilous trip to the bar, but it served to show me that I wouldn't want to travel in standard class, and how annoying it must be for those seated near the bar with all the coming and going.)  So standatd premier definitely made the journey enjoyable as we appreciate space, peace and quiet.  The worst part of the whole experience was the appaling lack of seating space in the departure lounge at St Pancras.  One of us had to stand the whole time, whilst the other managed to find a high stool to perch on, which wasn't very comfortable.  In fact, so cramped were the conditions, passengers were even finding it hard to find places to stand without blocking walkways or access to the small disabled seating area.  Very poor indeed!  On the way back waiting was on the platform at Marne-la-Vallée, where again seating was very limited and it was unpleasant as one of us was in pain and really needed to sit down but couldn't.  When we reached St Pancras there was a long slow queue for immigration.So to sum up, the train and service was good in standard premier and we enjoyed the journey, but the station operations/facilities in both countries let it down.  I feel sorry for people who cannot stand at the stations.

I was unable to find my tickets and the reset password link never arrived. After hours of trying to find tickets I read on the internet that you need to sign up again. I used the same password and it actually worked. I downloaded the app and triple checked the ticket. Very frustrating.

Very expensive for a train journey. Eurostar have had it for too long.

I do like the fact though, that both border checks are done at departure so you just walk straight out on arrival.Departure waiting area at St Pancras is far too small for the amount of people, and the toilets are disgusting (felt very sorry for the guy at the Bureau de Change opposite as smell was horrendous). Not very reliable and totally overpriced, they have a monopoly and take advantage of it, completely outrageous
Holy balls it is fast. Also very clean, semi-reasonably priced beer, and if the train has empty seats they don’t hassle you for switching to a better spot

Why is Eurostar such a disaster? It is totally unreliable and overpriced. If you are lucky enough to get on a train out of London, there is no guarantee you will get a train coming back.  It is the most unpredictable way of traveling to the EU.

The organisation was a bit chaotic from start to finish. It looks staff need more training by contrast the journey back from Paris went very smoothly.

A comfortable journey.  Seats in premium  were 2x3 as opposed to standard ( in which we returned from Paris to London)  having a 3x3 configuration . Though the same narrow tables in both classes. Staff was scrambling around to try and get people on and sadly some didnt make it both times. Overpriced service but only way to go between cities.   Don't use taxi services outside if Paris station. Be careful of taxi scams at Paris station. We waited in line like others outside station at taxi station. Once we got in our taxi he stated he only accepted cash which was a scam. He tried telling us it would cost over 100 euro and suggested we stop at an atm. I told him to drop us off at the nearest corner. Clearly this taxi driver was a scammer. I used Freenow driver services and cost us 30 euro to hotel.

Unfortunately we were travelling at a Bank Holiday weekend, so it was really busy, but the staff worked hard to get everyone to queue, [and to be in the correct queue], and it all worked well.Plenty of eateries and food outlets in the station, for you to pick up some snacks to eat on the train, though the train does have a cafe facility, for you to buy items on board, including hot drinks.Boarding was quick, plenty of room for bags and even a decent amount of space for storing large casess, [but suggest you get on early, to make sure you can grab a space for large luggage.]Seats are spacious, good arm rests, temperature was comfortable, and you have the option of facing forward, or backwards, and also having a seat with a table between 4, rather than an individual small table.First time using Eurostar, but a very good experience.

I book early 6 months before my summer holiday and then Eurostar tells me 4 months later, 7 weeks before departure, that my trip has been canceled due to work. Leaving later is not possible because all hotels and apartments are now packed and what is left is twice as expensive. Now I have to fly, which has become extremely expensive so close to departure. This now costs me around 700 euros in additional travel costs. Ridiculous. Thanks Eurostar.

Not particularly well organised.  There is an ‘air of chaos’ surrounding the check in procedure. Everyone herded though passport, baggage and check to wait in a holding area until the platform is announced.  Check in staff seem often confused as to who is doing what,  what is actually required and the process just isn’t smooth or efficient.
Great way to travel from London to Amsterdam. Superkind professional staff on board. Thanks to Mrs Palmers I travelled worry-free...I'm disabled....much better than flying....simply love Eurostar!

The outward journey was 'only' rickety and poorly organised, the return journey was cancelled. How you get back home with your children is then your problem. There are no alternative train rides, they are all fully booked days in advance. So then you can either cancel your entire trip (with hotels and tickets already booked), or stay days longer and book extra hotel nights, or look for another way to get home (boat or plane). Eurostar doesn't lift a finger and the bill is yours anyway; they don't even refund the booking costs, let alone the extra costs you incur. So it's an expensive gamble to buy such a ticket from Eurostar. For those who want to go to England, the night boat is a safer, cheaper and more comfortable alternative.

The train left on time from St. Pancras station, London. We took the train to Amsterdam. The outgoing ride was fine. The seats are not very comfortable. There were  3 of us in our group and we were seated at a table. Good idea right? Not really, it wasn't comfortable at all. No leg room. There were so many people crammed into a small space. The Amsterdam station didn't have working elevators & escalators. This made hauling luggage difficult. The vending machines in the Amsterdam station were not working. The tickets seemed a bit high.
Delayed train for 30 minutes, everyone cramped up, the train that was supposed to leave after mine boarded before us...I wish Eurolines was back and I could take a bus because this was awful.

What an amazing experience - everything from the booking process to the actual train ride was perfect!  Special mention to O Efunsile for his tremendous service helping us out of St Pancras - he was a life saver as my husband has massive back injuries and he help us with our luggage and to direct us to the Uber rank, can’t thank him enough!

I have had the Eurostar probably 40 times over the last 8 years and I feel as though it has got worse.  Departing from London is mayhem.  Once through security and passport control you are met with a waiting area with not enough seats, people sprawled all over the place.  Rubbish abandoned all over the floor.  Toilets are filthy and smell.  Boarded a train just today - and the seat hadn’t been cleaned and there were dirty tissues under the tray.  The train I caught last week had the remains of someone’s sandwich.  Yes it is convenient - but for the price there is major room for improvement.  Basic things could and should be done.
This is not worth it at all, chose a plane instead. More comfort, cleaner, cheaper and more used friendly (even with the popular carriers). Eurostar was a disappointment,

I haven't been on my journey yet so my review is not about the train service itself. When I booked a return trip for July 2023, I was comforted by their new T&C's which allow for change of dates before you start your first leg of travel.  The website says you only pay the difference in fare. So basically there is NO DIFFERENCE in the fare, but Eurostar is asking me to pay GBP75 per person.  Ridiculous!I reached out for hep via their online contact form 5 days ago, and am still waiting to hear back.  I am now not even hopeful anyone will ever get back to me.  And I've read about the long waiting times in departure lounges with very few seats. I am dreading my trip.  I wish I had come on here to see these reviews before I made my booking.

Starting with the good points. The trains were fast and reasonably comfortable and both ran on time.However, we arrived at St Pancras with 90 minutes to spare before departure (as advised on the website and following warnings of chaos at check in). We got through check in and security quickly to be left standing around for ages in a crowded departure lounge. Maybe not so bad.At Bruxelles Midi, on the return journey, we were advised ro arrive 2 hours before departure before being told that we had to wait an hour for check in. By then, we joined the end of a long queue. Once through check in, we again waited in the departure lounge before being allowed up onto an empty platform. When the empty train arrived, there was a nad scaramble for everyone to get on the trainMy son's return journey two days later seems to have been even more chaotic!

Traveling by train in Europe, at least Paris/London/Paris, top. Train on time to leave and arrive, snack on the train normal price, good seat for a 2 hour journey. It is worth it. Just buy your ticket in advance for the best price.
