I really don't recommend travelling with this train service any longer. First, they have overloaded their St Pancras departure hall to the point that they ask you to arrive 90 mins early. The hall is jam packed to overflowing - on a weekday no less - and the toilets stink to high heavens. Second, while they are very eager to sell you alcohol on the train they will not provide free water. Not to refill a child's water bottle, not when trains are stuck or delayed. NOTHING. We opted for a slower trip with a change at Brussels and I could not be happier about this. Thalys is everything Eurostar isn't. Courteous, on time and staffed with lovely people. Oh and they refilled my child's water bottle.

My last review concentrated on their business practices. This one is on the actual service which we got to finally used after Eurostar relented and allowed anytime use of tickets unused because of Covid. The ride was uneventful and the seats were adequate, There was sufficient room for the luggage. The trains appear worse for wear and were not very clean.  The hassle to get on the train at the station was probably not Eurostar's fault but it was dreadful. It was a quick ride but make sure you have enough time to get to the train. It was not the best train ride I have had inEurope but I would say it isn't the worst either.

Check in was painless both ends, although Gare du Nord needs to put more seating into their waiting area.  Both trains were on time.  The Standard Premium meals served both ways were surprisingly good and coming home we were even offered extra small bottles of wine.  All in all a vety good experience, will certainly be using the service again.

Eurostar is - of course - the passenger service between Paris and London.   The terminal in Paris is OK but crowded.  It is - I suppose - better than boarding at Kings Cross.  It was sad in that when the train arrived the windows were dirty.  Security is - in general - poor both at check in and when waiting to board the train.  I was booked on the 1913 train but could simply have walked onto the 1813 as there was no ticket checking.  The announcements in the terminal were poor and inaudible [something about the "Aero" in the first class catering].  The train did run to time [how boring Northern France is]. There is a lot of negative comment both here and on Trustpilot and it is perhaps indicative that there is never any response from managaemnt

Was expecting a slick and professional experience not standing room only in departure area, not not being contacted and rebooked for a cancelled train, nor being waitlisted on a premium ticket - you’ve a lot of catching up to do on Customer service Eurostar here’s one customer you won’t be seeing again anytime soon . The service could be great but you are so wide of the mark currently you need a revamp - do you any of your Board actually use the service?
didn’t let us onto train because of strikes. literally just pay your workers its not that hard. lost hundreds of euros

It seems all slick and cool - I bought the insurance provided by Allianz because the ticket said it was not refundable. So they suggested I buy insurance in case I have to cancel. So I bought it. Then sadly had to cancel and they say it’s not refundable … so why did I pay for insurance ?  I don’t mind paying. But I hate scammers and  líars. It really cheapens the brand. Next time I’ll fly over.

We took the train from Paris Gare du Nord to London St. Pancras. We paid for Business Premier and I think that's worth it for three reasons:1.Security and passport control for Business Premier are in a separate Q than the other passengers, so faster2.There's a large lounge with snacks (limited), coffee, booze etc and plenty of outlets, seating space, and OKish wifi3.On the train itself, the seats are a reasonable size and there's drinks and meal serviceThe ride was smooth, the train clean and the staff (unlike on the TGV we took from Avignon to Paris) were helpful especially when they saw us having a bit of a struggle with our 3 yr old, stroller, and extra bags with his stuff.While I prefer NOT to have to repack and lug bags from hotel/Airbnb to taxi to train and then off train, in taxi to next place but rather keep a vehicle for the whole trip, getting from France to UK with a vehicle can be a pain from what I understand.Would take Eurostar again.

Shame on you Eurostar! Tickets purchased for almost $1000 totaled. A family of four. This was supposed to be a treat! Purchased months in advance, so in eligible for promotions and discounts. Happy to pay. Received multiple unusual emails, but all were followed with “ignore that previous email.“ Well, fast forward until two weeks before departure… My family is not seated together. My children are alone. They are in different coaches. I contacted customer service as directed for “special assistance,“ but was told that the train was full and they could not help. I was instructed to contact the manager on the day of departure ?! When I look online, there are in fact seats available, but because they are not in the same coach, neither the mobile nor full website nor app will allow me to move my passengers. Instead, it says “it’s better to be together,“ “kindly book all your passengers in one coach.“ imagine the irony of that 😞 I am too embarrassed to tell my husband what has happened. Our children will be traveling alone. We booked for Stander premier, food because we’re going over lunchtime, going to where they do not speak the language, and wanted to sit at a table together. This was a wonderful experience in 2000 but over the last 20 years it seems Eurostar has forgotten it’s call to service. This is a plea for help. I have a couple of weeks, Eurostar please do the right thing and put the family together.

We recently travelled to Amsterdam with Eurostar, travelling Business Premier. We were frequent users of Eurostar before the pandemic, but this was the first trip since then.  Apart from a slight delay on the homeward journey and a degree of congestion on the  platform at St Pancras on the return leg due to a failed escalator (both matters outside Eurostar's control), all the arrangements went smoothly, the journey was comfortable, and the food was pleasant. The staff were welcoming and efficient.  Given that we were lucky enough to be travelling Business Premier, the check-in procedures were streamlined, and I'd certainly choose to do that again whenever possible.   A far pleasanter and more straightforward experience than flying.

I would like to shout out to Kaizin at Eurostar. I had a situation and spoke to several representatives all of whom were unwilling to help out.  She took her time, found a solution for me, and implemented it seamlessly.  I would use Eurostar again because of her excellent service.  Thanks so much Kaizin!!!

First trip to Brussels on Eurostar and we found the whole experience very good.Much less hassle than flying, comfortable trains bang on time.St Pancras was much busier than Brussels but really pain free process getting through customs etc.Plenty of connections to Bruges.Highly Recommend

Amsterdam - London 1 May 2023.People waiting on the floor at Amsterdam, not enough seats. 5 toilets in a row on the train didn't work, the 6th had no paper. The destination displays were continuously wrong, so London arrival was Lille. Delayed half an hour at Brussels, no explanation.A poor way to treat customers, I mean passengers !
Smooth and easy trip from Paris to London. Train was clean and there was lots of communication with signage and announcements.

We had the direct train to DisneyParis and back with Grand children..overal good going out except for waiting area packed out with no seats available then scrum to board train. Disney Express luggage service first class.We were told that we could get to station for return 2 hours before departure... what a joke no seats/no food/basic toilets!... a sad end to a good/expensive holidayBest advice we can give is avoid Eurostar.. hence one star

St Pancras terminal needs to be twice as big as it is to cope with the number of passengers. Heading out we had to join a long queue that went way outside the Eurostar terminal and into the shopping area. Having eventually got in the terminal there were long queues for border checks etc. Then there was another wait until we could board the train and more queues to get escalators. Gents loo stank. No sign of cleaning staff. On the train there was a screen in the carriage but it never changed or gave any information whatsoever. Onboard food used old bread and very little choice on offer. Internet connection was extremely iffy until we arrived in France. Brussels terminal even worse. Everywhere crowded. No instructions given re the passport scanners. Staff extremely unhelpful. Very hard to get any decent food. Train at least had a working screen. Long queues to get off train and out of St Pancras. Alltogether a very uncomfortable and frustrating experience.
4 seats purchased at the same time and we were not seated together while other people did not know each other, were seated in the side of the 4 seats!
on arrival at Saint Pancras, the platforms are wide and clean... in short, easy to get around, lots of shops in the station before boarding

I was supposed to take the 9:01 to Brussels and arrived within the advised timetable posted on line by Eurotunnel. So, arrived at 7:30 to find ridiculous long line for boarding  at St Pancras and passengers treated like cattle. Spent the next 120 minutes queuing to get to the train by 9:28. Clearly the amount of passengers and the problem in the lounge were excuses for an appalling service and disregard of the comfort of the passengers. People piled like cattle , forced to queue from the outside of the station and treated like cattle: ‘hurry up! Move on! Use all available space! This is ridiculous . If you gave no capacity to board in a normal civilised way so many passengers then you should sell less tickets. I believe that the service is the worse I had to face and I have already endured the Easy Jet customer care. Train left 32 minutes late. Lady on speakers insists on the volume of passengers. If there is too many people, it means that they sold too many tickets and so is about being greedy more than caring for the quality of service.

On our way to London from Paris we were on route to a flight home and they told us we couldn’t board the train 30 Minutes before departure. They told us to wait for the next train which was an hour later, but we didn’t have ensured seats because the whole train was booked.

Having read a number of negative reviews and, as advised, arriving 90 minutes in advance to cover delays with security and passport checks, we found the Eurostar experience both efficient and friendly throughout. Despite the trains being full, check-in procedures at St Pancras and the Gare du Nord took less than 30 minutes.  The staff were both welcoming and helpful and the terminals well appointed - albeit expensive.Onboard we were in "economy" but the buffet car was adequate, the wi-fi worked thoughout and the journey effortless -we reached 180 mph at one stage - just as well it was quick as the seats were a little uncomfortable.We would use this servce again

The trip from London to Paris was quick and smooth, but the process of getting on the train felt very stressful. You are recommended to arrive 45 minutes to 1 hour early, but I would say you need to get there closer to 1.5 hours ahead of time. The queues were long and staff was rude. It was almost like they didn't have enough lanes open to accomodate everyone.

We love Eurostar. But Gare du Nord is a serious problem, its plain awful whether arriving (aggressive taxi touts at the usual taxi exit, there are poor signposts to the official taxi rank up a ong walk over a building site, no police around which there always were) to departure (long queues - there being only one working escalator to the train which had just about everyone with a suitcase and then mayhem on the platform as the various groups had to cross each other). And there was seating for maybe 10% of the travellers, I don't expect to sit on the floor when I have paid for Premium. It was the same in February 2022 when I last went through. No progress made, Eurostar need to consider another station, just like when it shifted from Waterloo (awful) to St Pancras (fine). And there was nowhere to get a last drink on the station without going outside to the horrifically expensive bar opposite. They are number one in a field of one, so that place will deal with any left over Euro's. Wake up Eurostar we need a better experience pretty quickly.

I am very disappointed with the staff at the English border who are very unfriendly and threatening under the pretext that we want to understand certain things compared to a small Swiss army knife which hardly cuts anything. The manager was not at all into dialogue and kindness. He even called us terrorists.

i took Eurostar from London to Amsterdam and then again on my return trip from Paris to London. My general experience was very good. Train is fast, clean and efficient, maintains time. Since this was an international travel, the immigration process both at London St Pancras and Gare du Nord , Paris were very simple and efficient unlike many airports. And since the immigration process is completed for both the countries at starting point, upon arrival at destination, there is no waiting in queue. Just take the luggage and walk out of station. Since I traveled in economy class, food was not included in my ticket. So I packed it from Stations. The only disappointment was the  Channel tunnel. I expected a spectacular experience. But , since the train enters the tunnel may be a couple of Kilometers before English channel, the feel of under water tunnel travel is not there. It is just like any other rail tunnel , except that this tunnel travel is of around 20 minutes in total darkness. And from London side, there are a few smaller tunnels before the Chunnel, you will realize it only after a few minutes of travel. So this was a bit of anti climax.

Eurostar Business Premium meal and complimentary alcohol travelling London to Paris. Travelled as a family of 4 adults. Booked in advance. Ample room for our four suitcases. Checking in went as smooth as it could with the amount of people coming through. Seamless process through security to train. Although not enough seating provided prior to boarding on London side. Great service onboard. The steward was very pleasant. Carriages were clean and tidy. Phone charging available onboard.

We went to London for the West Ham - KAAG match. Check-in and baggage check went very smoothly. The train left perfectly on time. The seats were comfortable and there was enough leg room. The ride took 2 hours, which is a fast connection. You get off in St. Pancras, which is in the heart of London. The return trip also went without any problems. For me, this remains a very good alternative to flying.

Overall disastrous No internet on the way out or back. An insane price A completely overloaded boarding hall in London with no place to sit for 45 minutes. Bad food as standard first on the way back. In short we see that it is a public "service", no attention to the customer who is the least of their worries. Setting up a competing line is the only way to improve the service and in the meantime it is better to take the plane or we are treated better.

tl;dr Eurostar ignores customers messages, does not provide bicycle transportation anymore – with a non-sense excuse of covid (!?) –, has mediocre usability on both site and app, and has serious capacity issues on their boarding station at St. Pancras.Long story:I am a huge advocate for trains-instead-of-planes, and as such I expected a much better offering than what Eurostar do today. 1) Sent Eurostar a message through 'Contact us' 2 weeks before my trip, was completely ignored/have never answered.2) Purchased my ticket after joining the Eurostar Club and informed my member number during the purchase, which was done while logged in. Nevertheless, Club page/app says "You have no upcoming bookings".3) The Contact Us section on the website also says "We can't recognize the current booking reference". It's like I had no bookings, while I actually do.4) Eurostar removed the ability of carrying non-foldable bicycles "because of COVID" (never heard of viruses hazards caused by bikes) and never brought it back, which is a move towards the past.5) During the purchase process, at the seat map there was no indication of 4-seats arrangement (when people face each other), and I got assigned to one of those seats to my surprise.6) At the seat map there is no clear indication of the direction the train takes (from the seat's perspective). I was seated backwards, which is fine for me, but a huge nausea problem for some people.7) St. Pancras station has a TERRIBLE arrangement for security and especially for the two passport checks. It is clearly not roomy enough for the demand. Plus, the queue space was designed for people with no luggages at all. It's a train, so you don't check them, hefty ones come with you all the way; it is hard to move them zig-zag all around in a crowded and disorganised line.8) St. Pancras boarding area was clearly underestimated: there is no enough seating space for the number of passengers waiting to board a train, even when it is not completely booked.9) On the train, the seat reclines almost nothing. Some of the plug sockets do not work.Advice:- If a customer contact you, answer it. Improve your communication channels. You should be on phone, WhatsApp, social networks.- Improve your website/app, especially the Club/bookings system information exchange + the seat map.- Bring back the ability of carrying non-foldable bicycles on the train!- St. Pancras boarding process is very far from reasonable. That really needs to be rethought/expanded/modernised from scratch, from security to waiting area.

Garbage is an understatement. Forced me to pay for a ticket change and take a train 3 hours later because I arrived 30min before my train exactly. "You are late you should be here 30min before your train" and refused to listen when I showed my watch telling me oh its already a minute late. The gates were completly empty with no que as shown in the picture. I usually don't arrive at the last moment but sadly a connecting train was delayed but neither company will take responsibility. The sad state of having no competition meens you will receive terrible service and get charged the absolute premium for it. Just take a plane.

More than competent customer service from Laura and Ethel at the Gare du Nord ticket counter. They were able to respond to my request and were remarkably efficient! The service on board Maximilien as a first standard should also be highlighted.

Had a last minute seat change despite booking weeks in advance.Already had one email telling me the seating had changed then an email straight after telling me to ignore the email.Food served was not of the usual standard. Spoon had old food encrusted on it which put me off. Had a pastry that was quite hard. This is my 5th time on Eurostar and service standards appear to be slipping.

Our trip went well. The train was on time at departure and arrival. We were a little afraid that it would be canceled because of the strikes but that was not the case. For once a train is on time... Decent on-board service. Fast boarding.

After reading the many negative reviews, I had mixed feelings about the Eurostar trip. The tickets were already booked so we just went on Good Friday, despite all the bad reviews. What a wonderful experience it turned out to be! From Brussels Midi the entire trip went perfectly, quiet check-in and security control, large waiting area. The journey itself was uneventful and quick. Same comfort as in Dutch trains. Enough legroom for my husband (1.96m) in standard class, seats are adjustable for more or less legroom. Sockets for charging telephones, etc. are available everywhere at the seats. WIFI is bad but not a problem for us, you are more or less forced to do something other than aimlessly look at a screen for 2 hours (reading, staring into space in peace, etc.). You'll disembark in the heart of London with a direct, interconnecting service between St. Pancrass and King's Cross. Luggage can be stored in the compartment, no hassle at a baggage carousel and transfer from the airport. Oister Visitors Card (20 GBP) can be purchased on the train at the bar/kiosk in carriage 8, ideal for getting straight from the Eurostar onto the metro. Return journey from London was busier in the waiting area, but nothing compared to an airport. Absolutely recommended!! In addition to the fast connection, you also travel in a climate-friendly way ;)

RUDE CONDUCTOR + Arbitrary new seats attribution because of train changeNew seat attribution because of a train change on our way back to Brussels from London forced us to have seats in standard premier irrelevant to our costly reservation of two face to face seats (paid rather dearly for - more than 600 EUR-and reserved very well in advance) while the rude conductor insisted that he would not accept our "conditions" (!?!?) for seating. So much for customer rights, service and care! :-(...

The journey is the destination. Despite the strike in France, everything went well! Friendly employees. Basel - Paris - London. With a coffee break on the Ile in Paris. Five hours between arrival and departure. Sounds like a lot, but it was just right for us. Allow at least 1 hour for the change of station (Lyon - North). So that you stay relaxed. Rush hour is also added. With the regional train on the lower floors (RER). We had no queues at the Eurostar check in. Nevertheless, it's worth getting there 60 to 90 minutes beforehand. Eurostar trains well staffed, a little tighter than TGV. Cleanliness okay. On the return journey to St. Pancras, the waiting room before boarding was packed (Maundy Thursday). The atmosphere is peaceful and the employees are supportive and patient.

Bit wary about catching the Eurostar after reading such  bad reviews.    However, I have no complaints about my Business Premier Paris - London (return) trip.    Check in at Gare du Nord was efficient and the Eurostar  Lounge well stocked for breakfast.    Food on the train both ways was decent and the staff very friendly.   Trains ran on time and no problem getting an earlier train back from St Pancras, although lounge at St Pancras not as well generous for food  as Paris and check in not as organised.

Transfer in Paris was a disaster, never again. Chaos because the passport controls take forever, instead of opening all the control gates, only 2 of the 8 are occupied. Waiting room completely overcrowded, very warm, very bad air, hardly any seating, ...holidays like Easter always come so suddenly 🙄, what a shame. We wanted to travel in a climate-friendly way, but it's not worth the stress of such a 4-day short trip!

The Eurostar is easy to find and access via the London underground.Ok so we had not read the literature and did not realise that you needed to allow a certain amount of time before departure ( to get through customs etc). However we were luckily saved by a worker who rushed us through so that we didn't miss our train.On the outward journey we had pre-booked Standard Premier which included a little meal (you will need to prebook dietary requirements)  and alcoholic/non alcoholic drinks. The seats were comfortable and we were  all (3) seated together- enough space to easily store luggage- and plug sockets to charge mobile phones.The staff in premier were lovely!.To be honest it was a great journey- relaxed -We had hoped to swop the return journey to standard premier too however if we were to alter /upgrade  at that stage there would have been a big cost per person so we declined.We travelled direct to Paris and I would use i the Eurostar ,if we were to travel to France another time.(On a side line-be warned if you use the metro in Paris- there are pickpockets and we did get targeted !)

A bad experience.  The trip was supposed to be 4 hours, but it took us 15.   After Bruges, there was a fault on the line. We waited for an hour or so and the poor train staff were not being told anything,   The then decided to reverse to Bruges, but there were no parking place for the train.    After another hour,  they went to Lille for another hour's wait. Finally got into Lille station and we were told that we could get lunch but to take our luggage with us as they couldn't guarantee they would be here when we got back.  Still no foof and no water. They finally got us to Brussels and told us to ask where we could get the intercity to Amsterdam.  Unfortunately there was no one to ask.  200 people milling around but we finally got a intercity, which stopped at every cowshed between Brussels and Amsterdam.   Got into the hotel at 10:30, and of course the kitchen was closed.  (The staff did get us some soup and a beer, though.)   Next time we will fly.

We expected a trip to Lille to be trouble free, but our train was run by british people, who want to be paid, but not do any satisfactory work. First disappointment was the way eurostar make you wait until the last second before letting you onto the train, crammed into an unsuitable space with hundreds of other passengers, with no places to sit. Perfect for transmitting covid and very uncomfortable. Just as bad as the airport experience. The next disappointment was realising that we were sharing the train with Disney travellers, mainly loads of children and their annoying noise. I asked a eurostar advisor why it isnt advertised that the Lille train is also the Disney train. Her reply was, 'I thought that everyone new that'  A typical response from an idiot employed by eurostar. What she should have explained to us was that if they did advertise the trip to Lille, banged up for 90 mins with the Disney multitude, they wouldnt get any bookings. Never again will we use eurostar.  Its just a very bad experience.
Very bad, all tickets are non refundable and inflexible. Please take flight instead of taking train via Eurostar, it won’t be a good experience taking Eurostar

Not even left and so far disgusted with service. I booked and paid for seats to Paris back in October 22 and booked all five seats together. This week we leave and received an email saying check your tickets only to find out that they have split my family of five people up to five different seats in different  carriages including my mum aged 80 and my 14 year daughter who is now sitting in a carriage all by herself. I called to asked what can be done as this is unacceptable and they said nothing cause the train was full. I can’t believe they can just split up a family. My daughter is so upset and bloody scared of travelling now. They say that seats can change but there must be other family’s travelling who are split up, it just seems to be my family. I sent a email complaint and I get a response thank you for you feedback !!! Absolutely disgusted by there system

The train itself is fine. Legroom for people over 1.90m slightly less ideal (knees against the seat). Information about the trip was disappointing. After the reservation I received a confirmation, but a day before the return journey I received a seat change. This information could not be viewed via the app and the website due to a malfunction. When we asked for information at the station, we were told that the seat had remained the same and that the email was probably sent by mistake. Once we arrived on the train, it turned out that the seat was already occupied by a passenger who had reserved exactly the same seat. Very strange. We were able to exchange places with another passenger, but this is absolutely not the way you would want to travel. The travel information is poorly indicated. Our trip was extremely delayed due to a malfunction. Information about the delay was given piecemeal and nothing could be found online (app/website). For us this was the first and unfortunately also the last time. No stars for Eurostar. Hopefully the journey with this train will be better for others.

Eurostar have succeeded in making boarding one of their trains more unpleasant than going to an airport. The e-ticket says turn up 90 minutes before your train, the paper ticket 45-60 minutes, but on arrival you are greeted with queues, inadequate facilities, and not enough seating. It is a wonder how they have  managed to make it so unpleasant. The train itself is fine.

We chose the Eurostar for a day trip to Paris while visiting London for a week.  Tickets were bought in advance so price was fair. Our trains were on time and got us terminal to terminal in less than 2.5 hours.Trains were clean, comfortable, and power sockets in working order.  Wi-Fi was a bit slow but I brought a book as I wasn't expecting to depend on it.I was a bit suprised that the London terminal was more chaotic with less available seats than the Paris side - but it could have been time or day or the fact that another train or two was delayed in London.  I'd choose this over flying if I was doing this again - not sure I'd be so eager to do a fast-pace day trip with my wife and 9-year-old son if this was via air.

Unfortunately we had an 80 minute delay on our outward leg to Paris. We were on one of the older trains and they were extremely spacious with 2 buffet cars and lots of storage room. We returned on a new train and had a very different experience. They have obviously learnt from budget airlines to cram in as many people as possible, and it felt very claustrophobic. Given the choice I’d go for an older (E300) train every time.

I love trains but Eurostar experience has been awful. Preventing you to enter 30min before and to have airport's like checks is not the best but, the most awful thing, is the fact that train tracks are not indicated properly and on a timely fashion in Amsterdam. Furthermore, personell was more busy to chat than try to compensate for that.Long story short I needed to buy another ticket for almost 300€ and the operator told me to try not to lose the train again.Since the only train I have lost so far is Eurostar, I think I will achieve that by not taking it anymore.Much better to take the airplane with a service like that.

For the price you pay for the Eurostar, trains are frequently cancelled or rescheduled. We're booked on to Brussels this weekend, our outbound train is cancelled due to French strikes. Now I understand this is out of the train lines control however, we're having to travel a day later than our planned visit shortening our trip and no compensation is offered whatsoever.  Additionally, considering we're all trying to reduce our carbon footprints the train line needs to find a way to remain competitive with the cheaper flights alternatives. Even booking several months in advance the Eurostar is usually 20% more than flying.

Traveled from Amsterdam to London by Eurostar. Made the same trip by plane before. We liked the Eurostar better than Easyjet. Security and douna went smoothly. The journey itself is longer, but you get out of the center of London and that is a big advantage. Comfort on board is excellent. The WiFi connection is a bit slow but it works. Great alternative to the plane. Booking directly via Eurostar also went well. The only downside: on the way back we had seats 3+4, which means you have little or no view outside. That wasn't really clear when choosing the seats in advance. Everything else is fine!

Easy smooth check in. Friendly polite staff. Plenty of room to wait on seats before boarding the Eurostar to Paris. Train clean and easy to store luggage. All on time. Our return journey was equally smooth and effortless.

Do not even consider going to Amsterdam by Eurostar if it means changing in Brussels. Our train left St Pancras late which meant we missed our connection and so we were dumped on 3 different SLOW trains, and arrived hours late. We then had exactly the same experience on the way back - the train from Amsterdam was cancelled and we had to get 3 SLOW trains to Brussels. All the time we were stressed as it looked like we would miss the train in Brussels. They in fact held the train so we managed to avoid an overnight in Brussels.When I applied for compensation I was expecting Eurostar Customer Services to be apologetic and helpful. Not a bit of it.First of all they tried to fob me off saying the trains were only 30 and 50 minutes late. A total lie. When challenged they admitted they didn't have the info and asked me what my arrival times were. When I told them they then challenged me again, saying they DID have the info! So in summary - avoid any journeys that are not direct, and if you have to deal with customer services, don't be put off when they try to tell you there is no compensation!!

The experience on the train was fine although the French SNCF trains are nicer, to be honest. The worst part was in the waiting lounge/hall. Two trains were scheduled to depart within half an hour of each other so the seating (which is ample) was not enough for the amount of waiting passengers. Having been told to arrive 45 mins to 1 hour before departure meant standing around for an hour, and though I am essentially healthy that was a long and uncomfortable hour. Also (not attributable to Eurostar) the passengers were impolite or rude, saving seats for “somebody in the toilet” while using the seating as a luggage rack. The downside of travel on the train was being in a carriage with a very loud and borish English family who seemed to be eating the entire journey - again not attributable to Eurostar. (And I am English and was embarrassed by these people). I had thought Eurostar would be a genteel and comfortable experience but it was not, unfortunately.

Excellent connection to London. Very quickly and easily from Rotterdam Central Station. Good seats and enough legroom. We could also easily store suitcases. Due to strike in France (what's new) slight delay. The only disadvantage on the return journey was that there was far too little space in the lounge of St. Pancras Station for all the travelers returning on the same train.

We took a Tuesday to Friday trip to Amsterdam from the UK on a direct train. Was a great experience from checking in through to our arrival home. Everything worked like clockwork, no delays, comfortable seats and friendly staff. Would definitely recommend.

Excellent connection to London. Smooth and easy, good seats and enough legroom. Everyone is also quickly seated, which is always a lot of hassle on an airplane. The disadvantage is that the phones of fellow travelers are used frequently and noisily. More noise than in an airplane.

Booking process straight forward. Tiickets provided on the App. Checking in 90 minutes in advance in UK & 60 minutes in Lille. Enough security side watering holes. Never waited too long at any stage despite the early trains full of skiers. On schedule trup despite the French national strike. This train would have carried on to Brussels.Useful to know there is a secure bag drop at the far end of the station at 5.50 Euro per item for 2-10 hours. This was good for final day when we left the cases early on a returned later to collect to save carting around all day.Some food options on station BUT there is also Euralille - Westfield shopping centre next door for eats & drinks when returning home which is quick & easy to use.There is a huge Carrefour if you want to stock up with supplies aswell.

Abysmal experience. Due to strikes in France, out train was cancelled for days in a row. Reaching out via Twitter gave a response 3 days later, in which they were unhelpful. I have already traveled alone twice with the Frecciarossa 1000 - in September 2024 from Milano Centrale to Napoli and in October 2025 from Bologna Centrale to Roma Termini. I was absolutely thrilled with both train journeys! The Frecciarossa 1000 is considered the fastest high-speed train in Europe. On my routes, speeds of over 250-300 km/h were reached at times - really impressive! The train staff on the train and at Roma Termini station were very friendly and helpful. On my last trip from Bologna Centrale to Roma Termini, I reserved a seat in advance online when booking. Unfortunately, after this was accidentally awarded twice, I received a FREE one! Upgraded to Business Class even though I booked Standard Economy! I thought that was really great! Hospitality is included in business class and it was excellent: there were good snacks as well as coffee and cappuccino. The Trenitalia employees in Roma Termini were very friendly, helpful, courteous and always helped me with questions and minor problems (e.g. station display boards) at the train station! The Frecciarossa trains are very modern and attractively designed inside and out. The carriages are clean, there are 2 toilets at the ends of the carriages - practical on longer train journeys! Several screens on the ceiling show the route, the current location and the current speed. The ride comfort in standard economy and business class is very good. The seats are very comfortable, offer plenty of space and wide armrests. Between the seats there is a USB port and a socket (Euro socket) for each seat - perfect for charging your laptop and power bank at the same time! The journeys were pleasantly quiet, with almost no driving noise. Booking train tickets online was also smooth and easy every time. Conclusion: When traveling in Italy, forget about the airports - this is the way to go!

After trying the "Standard", "Premium" and "Executive" tariffs, I can say for sure: I do not recommend it. Even the "Executive", despite the astronomical price, is anything but a flight into the clouds: the seats are spaced awkwardly apart (so no decent conversations), the Wi-Fi barely works, the staff is sometimes less than courteous and the service is, to put it kindly, "football". This year we tried the "Premium" class and found ourselves in a ten-hour night's hell. First of all, the definition of "comfortable seats with reclining backrests" is a complete lie. The backrests don't recline because they simply don't have room: there are plastic screens behind them. With a lot of luck, you might find the mechanism that makes the seat slide forward slightly, but your back won't feel any improvement, while your legs will... banging against the knees of the passenger in front. The seats are cramped, and if you're over a size 50, the Freccia Rossa is not your transporter. Plus, the armrests don't raise and will dig into your thighs so much that you'll have marks for hours after the trip. If you're traveling overnight, be aware that there's no comfortable head support—bring an airplane pillow. And yes, the lights will stay on all night, so don't forget your eye mask if you want to sleep. As for dinner, here too an absolute disappointment: "Premium" passengers are kindly given a chocolate, a bag of peanuts and a measly bottle of water. Thank you very much, truly.Conclusion: Red Arrow does not care about your comfort, only about its own profit. Behind the nice words of the fares lies a cruel reality: they pack you in like sardines and you also have to say thank you for arriving alive. That's it. Never again.

Great way to avoid highway traffic.  Pleasant experience to have assigned seat, ability to plug in laptop and recharge phone.  Temperature was comfortable, bottle of water in business class. nice train with bar service, clean and large bathrooms. comfortable armchairs. courteous and kind staff. left and arrived on time.

I had previously enjoyed traveling twice with the Frecciarossa 1000 from Rome to Naples and Milan to Bologna in business class. This time we went in Executive Class from Paris Gare de Lyon to Milano Centrale. There is nothing better in high-speed trains: the car only has 10 leather seats in a 1-1 configuration. Each seat can be rotated 180 degrees and the backrest can be folded back. The fare includes full board, which you can choose à la carte. Since the train left Paris at 6:35 a.m., breakfast was served first. Later a lunch was served which was good. Everything is prepared in the car itself and does not have to be brought from the dining car. There is a service person who is only responsible for the Executive Class. The only thing that was a bit lacking in style was that the coffee was served from paper cups. At my request, I got the coffee from cups. The ticket is available flexibly from €165 (for comparison: a flexible 1st class Nuremberg-Berlin costs €214 without a BahnCard). I got the last available seat for €205. Although the train was 20 minutes late due to a technical problem on the way, it reached Milan one minute early! Conclusion: With the Executive Class, Trenitalia offers a standard that DB customers can only dream of and which is absolutely unique among European high-speed trains. The trip was an experience! P.S. Dear Trenitalia, the advertising film that was stuck over the entire car including the window should be gone! This is apparently only used on the Paris-Milan route. The foil obstructs the view of the guests who pay the most for the ride! But this is also a nuisance for passengers in Standard Class!
