Changing your reservation is not possible online, you have to call the paid telephone number (very expensive!). These pay off your phone bills!

This was my first ever fast train trip. We took the Italo train from Venice to Florence. I was a bit apprehensive as I suffer from motion sickness, however I found that it was smooth and pleasant once I got used to the speed at which the scenery goes by. If you don't look out the window, you would hardly notice the speed but on my first ever European trip I didn't want to miss a thing! I found that if I concentrated on looking into the distance, my eyes coped better with the speed. The seats were very comfortable in first class. I have a bad back and I had no problems with the seat. The staff were pleasant and we were even served an included drink and snack. The train was very clean and the whole service was most efficient.
Its a fast train that is privately owned.  We took it Rome -> Florence and Florence -> Venice.  It was great.  The train was clean, fast and cheap. I would take this train again.

Во время поездки по Италии воспользовались услугами Italo дважды. Билеты бронировали заранее через сайт перевозчика.Первый переезд был из Рима во Флоренцию, сам поезд шел по маршруту Рим - Милан. Поезд на вокзал Термини пришел минут за 20 до отъезда, однако, в течение 15 минут в него не пускали - проводили поверхностную уборку, стряхивали мусор с сидений, заправляли воду и т.п. Людей стали запускать за 5 минут до отъезда, чего в принципе вполне хватило. Поезд выехал вовремя. На маршруте поезд делает несколько остановок в основных крупных городах; собственно, Флоренция является следующей остановкой после Рима, затем до Милана есть ещё пару остановок. Во Флоренцию поезд пришел вовремя.Второй наш переезд был из Флоренции в Венецию, маршрут поезда Неаполь - Венеция. Во Флоренцию поезд пришел с опозданием минут на 10, остановка составила также чуть дольше положенного, в итоге поезд отправился дальше по маршруту уже с задержкой минут на 15. До Венеции он делает несколько остановок, и в самой Венеции останавливается в двух местах - на материковой части и на островной. Мы долго стояли на станции материковой Венеции, объявляли о каких-то проблемах с очередностью доступа на вокзал островной части. В итоге общая задержка приезда в конечный пункт составила около часа, однако не уверена, что последнее время задержки было виной именно перевозчика, а не логистики ж/д вокзала.Что же до основных аспектах поездки с Italo. На входе билеты не проверяют - их проверяет контролёр примерно спустя 15 минут поездки. Для проверки билетов достаточно иметь файл билета в телефоне, распечатка не требуется, что очень удобно. Пытались воспользоваться мобильным приложением, но оно почему-то не показывает билетов, так что его использование можно считать бессмысленным. При покупке билетов ставили галочку об sms-уведомлениях о прибытии поезда, но ничего такого не приходило. Ошиблись с маршрутом при покупке одного из билетов, в итоге с удержанием неплохой комиссии (у нас она составила около 35% от стоимости билета) за пару дней до поездки часть денег оказалось возможно вернуть, деньги пришли в течение 2-3 дней.Сами поезда крайне комфортные, в России их можно сравнить с тем же Сапсаном. Высокой скорости не чувствуется, ход плавный. Очень удобные кресла, большое пространство между рядами. Каждое место оборудовано крепким металлическим столиком, вешалками, розетками и usb-интерфейсом для зарядки электронных устройств, сеточкой для мелких вещей и маленькой урной. Розетки могут быть расположены либо между своих кресел, либо между передних кресел. Также в поезде работает бесплатный wi-fi, правда скорость и качество связи не самые лучшие - полагаю, это может быть связано с тем, что половина ж/д маршрутов в Италии пролегает по туннелям, где связь в принципе ловит плохо. В каждом вагоне есть туалет, также вполне удобный и хорошо оборудованный. Для размещения вещей и чемоданов в вагонах предусмотрены небольшие отделения в начале вагона, за 0.5€ можно "закрыть" там свой чемодан. Однако багаж всех желающих в этих отделениях явно не поместится, поэтому в основном чемоданы размещают на верхних полках над сидениями, и стоит заметить, что полки эти крайне вместительны и подходят даже для достаточно больших чемоданов.Во время поездки после контроля билетов предлагают различные закуски (бутерброды, шоколадки) и напитки, по цене сказать не могу - не интересовались.В целом впечатление от поездок с Italo вполне положительные. С сотрудниками компании особо не общались, проблем во время поездок не возникало. Хороший перевозчик с хорошими ценами.

Attendant said we were in the wrong seat. We showed her our ticket twice as she appeared confused as if she didn’t understand the ticket. She then realized her mistake and did apologize but it was an awkward 5 minutes. Italo Website claimed wine and beer could be purchased however we were told we could not (along with numerous other people also sitting in car #1 Prima section). Do not pay extra for this section it’s not worth it. Attendants on train aren’t the friendliest either. That said, scenery was beautiful and train was on time.

First fast train ride in Italy. Great smooth ride. Train reached 300 kph on numerous sections of track. Seats were very comfortable. We were served a drink and a small snack as complimentary, which was a nice touch. Staff were very friendly on this service. Train was slightly delayed due to traffic in station, but it didn’t cause us any great concern. Messages were given in Italian and then in English, which was very helpful. There was also a digital display of information in both these languages to assist. Would happily ride this train on to any destination in Rome.

Our family just used Italo for our transportation from Rome to Venice.  The train was smooth, clean, quiet, comfortable and the fares are very reasonable!  We booked first class so our seats were wider and more comfortable than usual.  There were power outlets in each row and  plenty of room for carry-on baggage.  Italo has a large presence in the train stations so you can get help or information quite easily.  The complimentary drinks and snacks were quite welcomed!  We will use Italo on our next trip to Italy!

Really enjoyed this train journey, the train is comfortable and modern with plug sockets, the toilets are good for a train and the ride went quite quickly. We were delayed, although it wasn't the fault of Italo and we were offered compensation back on the ticket, which I thought was very good. Would use them again!
Italo is a privately held company that operates numerous long-distance services connecting various points on the Italian peninsula. It is a good alternative for Trenitalia. Highly recommending
Took Italo trains three times on my recent trip to Italy and every time they were one time. The trains are smooth, quiet, and offer spacious bathrooms and vending machines.

The manager was extremely rude. A woman around her 30s with short hair. We were a group of 8 people but with different times on trains. My family doesn’t speak English or Italian. I told that to her and she screamed at me saying she was the manager and if I didn’t get on the train I’d miss my ticket (48€). First of all, she shouldn’t  talk to anyone like this, and we’re paying a pretty expensive ticket to be treat treat this way. Really upset and disappointed with this situation.
We traveled between Rome and Florence. On both the outward and return journeys, the train was punctual. Nothing to complain about comfort and cleanliness.
Train on time, comfortable, staff available throughout the station for any type of information, cleanliness at the meeting, snacks during the journey! NOTHING TO SAY! I recommend this company :)

For the next stage of our Italy visit we needed to travel from Florence to Naples, in order to get to the Amalfi coast. My wife had booked us on an Italo train. We had reserved seats but could not get all our seats together. Also, we didn’t have the nice seating setup with small table that we had on the Tren Italia trip from Rome to Venice. The trains were running about 10 mins late into the Florence station. It was a bit warm waiting around in the main section of the Florence station. To get some AC, for part of the time we were in a cafe and for another portion of time we stood inside the small reception area for Italo - but since we were not members, we could not access the lounge waiting area. Upon boarding the train, the overhead spots large enough for our small luggage,  were taken by the time we got to our seats. However, there was room available at the storage areas at the end of the train carriage (car) - but we would have felt more comfortable with the luggage where we could see it. The AC on the train had trouble at times keeping the carriage cool enough in the 90 degree temps of central/southern Italy. There were electrical outlets available at the seats. WiFi was also available but the performance was quite poor. I eventually gave up trying to do any serious email or web based work. The train stats showed that at times the train was traveling at 250kmh (about 150mph). There was some nice scenery to be experienced along the route of our roughly 4 hour ride. Farms, towns, homes and mountains.

On July 22, 2019, my boyfriend and I went to Milano Centrale station to catch our train to Rome at 11 am. When we arrived at the station we saw that the train was canceled and we went to the company counter, which had a huge queue. As we waited in line, we saw the Italo sign indicating the new timetable and were reassured that we would be relocated. However, after hours in line, the attendant informed us that the only solutions would be: refunding the money or being relocated to a train THE NEXT DAY. At this point I had already read on the European Union website that in this case the railway company should provide us with accommodation or reimbursement of the money spent. But that didn't happen. We told the attendant that we had already checked out of our accommodation and that we had accommodation in Rome, and we asked if she could do anything and she said NO. We soon had the loss of the extra night in Milan and the lost night in Rome. The company did nothing to mitigate the damage caused by the incident.

I like this train line.  I have taken it three times. Rome to Milan and Florence and back and to Lake Como.  They have a good website to buy your tickets.  I don’t use the machines or counter.  Always buy flex so you can change your ticket with no problem.  I never buy round trip tickets since I like to change plans.  Will always use them for trips between the big cities.  You ca buy a pass too to travel but that does not reserve you a seat.  The only time the train was packed was to Milan from Rome.

I had the absolute worst experience with them. I purchased a ticket to Venice (round trip) and all trains were cancelled due to an electrical issue outside Florence. I was refunded for my ticket purchased on Tren Italia but Italo wouldn’t refund the return ticket because “the train is still leaving Venice”. I couldn’t EVEN GET TO VENICE! They didn’t care - one rep even said that I could fly there 🙄. After two hours of waiting in line at the station to speak to a rep they suggested I call the customer service number. They kept the money knowing that I didn’t use the ticket and I provided proof of such. I have never been so mad or frustrated at a company. I tried everything - they wouldn’t credit me, let me travel elsewhere, nothing. What a waste of $200euro. DO NOT USE ITALO EVER. They are the worst.

I booked a high-speed train seat to go from Venice to Florence the 22nd of July, 2019, leaving at 13:00. Apparently there was a fire in one of the power plants near Florence early in the morning, and the train was canceled. I went to the Italo consumer service office at Venice's train station, where they told me there were no other trains they could transfer me to, and that the only option was to give a refund and get on a bus. And so I did.I went to a ticket post office. Before arriving there, a Italo worker told me that all trains bound to Florence had been canceled, so I started to think that I was actually going to have to go by bus.I searched with my mobile to see what other transport methods I could use, and found that there were actually not only regional, but high-speed trains going towards Florence. But instead of going with Italo, I had to go with Tren Italia. I then spotted the guy who had told me that there were no services going to Florence, and admitted that he had lied to me only because the trains going there were from Tren Italia and not from his company, Italo.If I had done what Italo's staff told me to do, I would have either had gotten in a bus, arriving 5 hours later; or booked a hotel room and pay it all by myself.Defenetly never getting on those trains again, they have very pretty trains, but when there are delays and cancelations they do everything they can do for you not to get on another company's train.

My son left a small case with his Nintendo Switch in it under his seat, when we realized he left it the train had already been cleared and back out enroute. The Italo customer service agent said there is nothing they could do and gave us a number to call. The problem is the number can only be called on a local phone and they don’t have phones there, my cel would not work. When we finally were able to get a hold of someone at the call centre they said they would contact the train manager and he would get back to us if they found it. We told them exactly where he left it, under a seat, gave the seat number in executive class against a wall. No one called back, numerous visits to the station and calls to customer service with the same run around. It is ridiculous that they don’t have a better system to deal with lost items, especially with the amount of information given to them and the short timeline. Never again.

We tavelled on Italo trains twice during our 3 weeks in Italy.  The first was from Rome to Naples  The train was well-appointed, the seats were very comfortable and there was plenty of room to store our bags.  There was a display in the front of  our car that indicated the train was going over 300 kph!  Amazing.  The 2nd trip was from Milan to Venice, and again the ride was near perfect!  It was on time and service aboard was superb.

It is the competitor of TRENITALIA. It has private capital different from Treni, which is state-owned. The trains are great, they stop more and yet the travel time is the same due to the speed. There is a luggage rack on top of the seat. Travel from Venice to Rome in Italo in Prima class. Very hard seat, back pain starts to be felt after 2 hours of travel, the hard plastic armrests hurt your back if you try to turn over to sleep. The socket is a USB socket so be careful if you want to plug in your computer it is impossible. Frankly disappointed with the comfort, especially with your back blocked for a simple journey of less than 3 hours. A low-end high-speed train in terms of comfort.

We used the train from Rome to Florence and from Florence to Rome.. we had booked the tickets online and found them very economical. The train was spotless and quite fast and we arrived without any delays.. would definitely choose it again
I made a reservation online in advance. I think it would be a good idea to compare prices with Trenitalia. Even in the same section, time etc.? The amount will change. Class, of course.
Saturday and Sunday Rome Milan and return. Very pleasant experience. Time flew by. Train very punctual for both routes. Clean and comfortable. No mobile food service

The trains are lovely and comfortable I will give them that. But I had the unfortunate bad luck of confusing what train to be on and ended up going the wrong way. You'd assume that I could just explain the mistake and get on the right train. Nope. After disembarking I was told to go speak to someone about the transfer. The transfer they spoke of was me having to buy a completely brand new ticket. The person who was supposed to be helping me gave me a choice of a brand new ticket or 100 euro upgrade. That was the only option presented to me. With no other  choice I bought my 20 euro new ticket (that a travelling student really couldn't afford) and took myself away from them to cry on the platform. So all in all they took an already very stressful and upsetting situation and made it 100x worse for me. 0/10 would never use again. Terrible service when in a crisis. If you're a perfect human being who never makes any mistakes then you'll be fine using them.
Very fast without being annoying, well soundproofed with good services. Comfortable seats and very attentive staff.

Took this train to go from Rome to Milan and return (about 3h). Train was a bit delayed on the way to Milan but they informed us of the issue during the trip. Tickets were cheaper with Italo than the other company. You get free wifi and you can buy drinks and snacks on the train. Overall good experience.

.Italo are modern high-speed red trains accelerating up to 300 km/h. They go almost on schedule, and it’s clear that it’s difficult to be accurate at such distances and at such speed. The carriages are comfortable for any budget, with a choice of 4 classes: Smart (standard), Comfort, Prima (premium) and Club Executive (VIP). The seats are adjustable with backrest tilt, tables, footrests, 220v sockets, and there is also free WiFi on board. Each train has vending machines with food and drinks, cars 3 and 7, and there is even a CINEMA Car. Tickets are sold in separate machines, but it is better to buy them at the box office. A guy helped us change the tickets we bought from the machine for different seats in one car - for paired ones in another. In general: SERVICE, COMFORT, SPEED and reasonable prices, although sometimes the ears get blocked, especially in tunnels

Trenitalia also runs between Florence and Bologna, but it takes about 30 minutes, and tickets for Italo are cheaper if you buy them in advance on the website. There was one running every 30 minutes. There was a 10 minute delay at the train station in Florence.

Trains much more advanced than in France... Very comfortable seats with compatible charger sockets! Great for our 3:30 hour trip. All that's missing is a bar car, there are vending machines inside the train but plan to have some cash and go early because at 10:00 there's already not much inside. Value for money more than good. €88 for two for a ROME/MILAN one-way ticket.

After having read variable reviews about high speed train travel in Italy, there being two company choices, I want to offer my very positive experience with two trips that I recently took on Italo Treno in September, one from Rome to Florence, the other from Florence to Venice.  The website for online booking is excellent, and when looking at choices, a "12 box matrix" of three cost levels in four seating categories comes up. This allows for easy comparison of relative value for available choices, and one can easily look at those options in other time selections.  Given the choices available at the time of my booking a month in advance, with the comfort level option sold out, I chose the prima ticket because it was offered at just 2 euros more than the smart ticket, which effectively paid for itself with free beverage and snack service.   That also allowed us faster track entry at Rome Termini.  Both trains were very clean and comfortable.  WiFi was good.  There was a lot of space for luggage at the end storage area, and the overhead racks readily fit large suitcases.  The one train was delayed by 15 minutes, the other on time.  A very positive experience from choosing the tickets online to the arrival at destination.  For the best prices, the earlier you can make your reservations, even weeks/months in advance, the better.

We used Italo to get from Rome to Florence to Venice to Milan and all the trips were wonderful.  It all started off with going into the ticket office in Rome; the young man helping us was friendly and handled all the bookings quickly.  They had a special promotion going on where we paid economy fares for "Prima" service.  That mean more space for seating and, I assume, the complimentary water/juice and snacks.  The trains reached a top speed of 250 kph and were quiet and smooth with just a few exceptions.  the service was great and easy to use.
Such a great train service.  Travels at up to 300km an hour.  Great value, helpful staff and a really good App so you can check prices and buy tickets

Italo Treno is a private train company in Italy that offers service between cities. We rode this train, in first class seats, from Rome to Florence. Highly recommend!

I have read a lot of very negative reviews from travelers who have taken a TGV. Well, maybe I had a mixed opinion before leaving, but the result of my trip was pretty decent but not disappointing. So I took the TGV INOUI 8755 in first class from Paris Montparnasse to Lorient in Brittany, leaving at 9:10 p.m. The journey is in the TGV version to Rennes directly, with peak speeds of 315 km/h in quite remarkable silence. Then, the train uses a normal track from Rennes to Lorient, with multiple stops, a total of 3 hours of time, which is OK for me. The comfort of the seats is certainly not exceptional but adequate. Everything worked on board, courteous staff! We left 10 minutes late as already announced, good! On board, the services work, electrical outlet and free WIFI but not secure, practical removable work tablet. The car bar is right next door and the service is good, with a choice of cold and hot drinks and snacks. Prices not excessive. It is pleasant to sit on a seat, although not very comfortable, to observe the landscape, which passes through panoramic bays, with a changing decor. Arrival in Lorient was late at past midnight. The station is modern with an elevator and escalator to access the footbridge to the main exit. The hotel is close by, an 8-minute walk away, in an almost deserted Lorient at this time. The return is in the same style, early departure, first train to Paris departing 8:21 a.m.; The station only opens at 8 a.m. but not the toilets which are closed!! The TGV INOUI 8708 train, which comes from Vannes, is on time, the car numbers are indicated on the platform to facilitate boarding without searching. Tain without stopping from Lorient to Rennes which saves time, compared to the outward journey. Signaling problems, which slowed us down a little with arrival in Paris almost on time.

My wife and I opted for first class on the TGV INOUI for the Lille Europe-La Rochelle journey (round trip €546) imagining we would benefit from a more comfortable journey...what a disappointment. Following my complaint about a defective chair, you royally awarded me €6.75. You're talking about ridiculous compensation when I traveled 1 hour 48 minutes (Marne La Vallée - Lille Europe 1 hour 38 minutes + 10 minutes late) in a half-lying position and sideways in an armchair whose back could not be straightened and one side of which was collapsed... my back still hurts. There was a free seat in the row in front of me. As I was planning to sit there, the lady sitting on the seat next to me could only advise me against it, her husband had also just changed seats because the seat in question was also defective. When, out of conscience, I checked ours during the journey, I found them stuck between the steps and the exit door of the carriage. Without this, they would have fallen on the station steps at the first stop when the doors opened. You can keep your alms, I don't want it. You can invest it in suitable rolling stock. In the future, we will fly… faster and cheaper. Yours sincerely,

Is it from having lost three hours of sleep? is it being taken for...? Is this incompetence?  The 3 my captains who wrote this review. This morning, I woke up at 4:15 a.m. for a commuter train leaving at 5:28 a.m. and having to drop me off at St Lazare at 6:10 a.m. to reach Gare Montparnasse by metro. TGV departing at 7:03 a.m. towards Bordeaux, arrival scheduled for 9:14 a.m. then TER connection scheduled for 9:53 a.m. (i.e. 39 minutes of travel time) for Lesparre where I am expected. First pitfall arrival St Lazare (SNCF portion) 6min late, no explanatory message. Fortunately I took a good margin and the metro did the job without any problem. Departure from the TGV on time and for the first time in my life (I'm approaching 50) I discover first class, a cheap upgraded ticket that I bought myself thanks to...the SNCF compensation vouchers accumulated for delays. And unattractive schedule, I understand why. The awakening stings. Objective to have a quiet trip to compensate for the short night. Oh that I was going to get my money's worth: not even 10 minutes after departure, an unplanned stop at the Massy TGV station, the train conductor announced: a train in front of us had broken down in the St Pierre des Corps sector and that our train had to "park to let the tow truck pass". We leave with an announced delay of 17 minutes. Ten minutes later receipt of a text message from the SNCF with a completely different reason: work on the tracks, expected delay of 30 minutes. Two more stops followed and we continued to be told the story about the train breaking down. At the same time, the text messages follow one another, always mentioning work on the tracks. The delay announced in the text messages increases to 40 minutes then drops to 35 minutes. The suspense is therefore at its height for the connections and in fact the announcement is only made about 15 minutes before arrival: yay the 9:53 a.m. connection is maintained. The conductor goes into the cars and informs us that the train will leave from track B and will wait for us. She still invites us “not to hang around the station”. Everyone is therefore in the starting blocks when the train arrives, which finally arrives in Bordeaux 36 minutes late, at 9:50 a.m. What follows is a run in the station (personally at the risk of waking up an Achilles tendon injury), I even see an elderly gentleman stumble in front of me. I reach the platform at 9:55 a.m. and there: SURPRISE THE TRAIN HAS LEFT. We are about fifteen castaways in disbelief. A gentleman confirms to us that he had time to see the train leave at 9:53 a.m. without waiting for us even a minute. Of course, no agent is there to give us information, we are sent to the ticket office which is obviously at the other end of the station. Barely compassionate reception “yes yes we are aware of it, there are a few of you, we will report the dysfunction”. We were told on the train that in the event of an unguaranteed connection a new ticket would be sent by text message? “ah no you have to use the same one” The next train? “Well, it’s at 11:52 a.m..” 2 hours of waiting at Bordeaux station in the rain, which is compared to the five hours spent more or less on the same date two years ago in the same station on a heatwave day following a torn catenary. My mom who had planned me for lunch? Well...we'll heat it up this evening.And long live the holidays, right?At least the man from Bordeaux won't have wasted 1 minute going to work this morning for these...Parigots who have the presumption to take a vacation...And for all that the SNCF will royally offer me compensation of 15 euros in vouchers so that I can once again suffer from their services. Opinion written on 08/20/2025 in the old jalopy which has always taken 1h30 to connect Bourdeau and Lesparre (80kms)…crossing your fingers

TGV inOui 9862 from Lille to Brussels on 28 Jun 25 2nd class was an entirely different experience however. My wife and I spent the entire journey standing in the lobby of a carriage. We booked 4 seats on a Turin to Paris TGV to connect with a Eurostar to London.In summary: The train was cancelled and we were told to make our own alternative travel arrangements.  We had to book new trains on a different, more expensive route (because the trains on the Turin-Paris route were fully booked for the next 3 days). We also had to rebook the Eurostar (at more cost).  We arrived back in the UK 36 hours delayed.  We filled in all the forms for compensation and have been told we'll get 25% of the original ticket price + £30 expenses!!!  That's all...In more detail:  The train had to turn back because of bad weather in the Alps.  We were put up in a hotel in Turin and told that the train would run the next day, 24 hours late, and a transfer was arranged to collect us from the hotel.  A bit annoying they didn't just do a bus replacement around the problem bit of line and quite frustrating, but so far fair enough.  But later that day we were then told the transfer was cancelled and so was the train.  We were told we needed to make our own alternative arrangements instead.  As said above, the direct route was fully booked for the next 3 days so we booked new tickets via Nice and paid to change our Eurostar tickets.  We also needed to book another night in a hotel in Paris as the Nice route did not connect the same day with the Eurostar.  We had the impression that we would receive compensation to pay for the new tickets (also TGV) and just needed to apply for it.  However after filling in all the forms, we've been told we will only get 25% of the original ticket price back plus £30 to cover expenses!  As well as being delayed 36 hours we are very badly out-of-pocket.  What compensation would you expect for a cancelled train requiring alternative travel to be bought and badly missed connections?  In Germany when a 2 hour delay caused us to miss a connection we had all our costs covered for alternative (non-German) trains.  In the UK, you'd get a full (100%) refund on the original tickets, PLUS all other consequential expenses paid for.Incidentally, if we had chosen to fly instead of travel by train, the airline would be required to fly us on the next available flight and pay all expenses to look after us while we waited.This treatment by TVG is simply shocking.

BUYER BEWARE!  THINK TWICE BEFORE YOU BOOK WITH Ouigo!We were working in France in Dec 2024, and we hub at the Sheraton CDG instead of going down into Paris center. The first ticket was sent to my email almost immediately.  I waited until we were about to leave for Lille, when I realized that I still had not received the tickets for the return trip.  I had an email with both trips and the booking reference codes, but only the first ticket (QR code) was sent to me via email.I found out the hard way that Ouigo is only online, and even though inOui is technically the same SCNF connect operation, the folks at the inOui kiosk were the first to tell me that Ouigo can only be managed online.My email confirmation stated that I could find my ticket in the SCNF connect app, but even with my email and booking reference, there was an error message.I was not interested in leaving for Lille without a return ticket, so I booked a second return ticket for both of us (through inOui; it was the same train as the original ticket).As we made our way to Lille, we found a chat and provided our complaint to Ouigo, and they said that they couldnt understand what happened, but after another check, I found that my original return ticket was now available in the SCNF connect app.  So, I had purchased two return tickets.  Coincidence?!?The cost was 66 Euros, so it wasnt about the money.  But, I will never make the mistake of booking a train with Ouigo, and I deleted the app.Everyone should make sure to be very careful if they choose to use this service, and I use the term "service" loosely.  You can use inQui without worry, except that the staff will be rude to you, but if you travel in Paris, you should expect this sort of behavior.

Horrible customer service. Cost us lots of $ in changed car rentals when we had to switch at last minute.

All trains Paris - London today November 15 almost one hour delayed since at least 13.30. The boarding process is absolute chaos. That announced the 15.06 departure to be 45 mins late and it didn’t leave the platform until after 16. TAKE THE PLANE. This is wasting your time. If possible I would have given MINUS STARS

I regularly take the tgv on the Paris - Lyon line, morning and evening. I notice a delay of 15 minutes on average. As this lasts, I tell myself that it suits everyone except me. If the train is more than 30 minutes late (1/4 of the trip) I am reimbursed 5 euros (approximately 1/20th of the fare) and only have enough that will allow me... to take another late train. Apart from that the places are small and not comfortable. The wifi is not good. 1st class is much better but reserved for the very rich. The tgv in France is a bad experience and it lasts, you shouldn't expect much from it, you will come out less disappointed knowing that.

Not very user-friendly site for booking. Impossible to book in the direction of travel. Use the 220 Volt socket between the two seats. Coffee and pastries/savories service… quite slow when there are too many people. Work on the track adding 2 hours to the journey. In short… average and too expensive.

During our trip in Europe we needed to travel from Barcelona to Paris, and as we wanted to experience the train insteqd of a plane we chose for the TGV. Two months in advance we booked our tickets for the TGV inOui on the SNCF Connect website, from Barcelona Sants to Paris Gare de Lyon. The booking process went easy and the e-ticket could be downloaded to the phone. On our departure day we arrived just 15 minutes in advance to the station, did the security check and could board the train. We had comfortable seats and the 6 of us all sat together (4 at 1 side and 2 at the other side). Luggage was stored in the beginning of the carriage and our smaller backpack above our heads. Compared with a plane this is a way better method of getting from A to B. You have plenty of space and can enjoy the views outside. Our trip took 7 hours and 14 minutes but went smooth and we arrived on time in Paris. The only comment is that we stopped a lot at stations in France. We did not try the restaurant on board as we brought our own food and drinks. I’ve seen a lot of negative comments but for us the trip went as planned and we didn’t regret we took the train instead of a plane.

Horrible Experience with the TGV!I’m writing this message from the TGV right now, and it’s an absurd situation. I bought a ticket to go to Milan and specified that I’d be traveling with a dog. When purchasing, you’re only asked whether the dog will be in a carrier or on a leash—there’s no question about the dog’s size or any other details. I’m in a two-seat space, with a stranger beside me, and obviously NO room for my dog.I can’t even put my feet on the floor without taking away the only space my dog has, and my dog is medium-sized. If I had a Golden Retriever or a Doberman, what would I have done? Would I have had to stand by the doors for the entire trip? Or sit on the floor? I asked the conductor if I could move to another seat, but he said no. When I asked if he could report this issue, he replied with resignation: “It won’t change anyway.”I find this absolutely outrageous!

Nice subscription at first glance and often practical, especially for the fairly simple and crowded Lille - Paris journey. On the other hand, the availability of trains remains to be desired for one of the most used journeys in France (therefore many trains) which is serious! Trains whose seats are sometimes available (numerous) but always paying despite the subscription even 2-3 hours before departure??? The icing on the cake, when we have managed to secure our tickets in advance, we have to re-confirm the day before that we are taking this train, seeming to say I'm going to book this train in advance to be sure of having it so as not to take it on the day, really I don't understand... So you don't have to do anything on the weekend or really put reminders all over the place to avoid forgetting, and therefore losing your place on the train, which I have to validate on my MAX space a ticket that I DELIBERATELY chose in order to make a trip THAT I WILL make on the day I want to go home or go to school during the week, in short, I can't wait for it to improve! It’s a shame for the flagship of French industry to have such a lack of practicality and offers accessible in particular to young people…

Groups of tourists scammed out of €35 by SNCF. Validated my Zou card at Antibes station and jumped on the first SNCF train to nice. Immediately a team of inspectors boarded and quickly scammed four different groups of tourists for €35 a piece. This all happened within minutes. We were told the Zou card isn’t valid on the SNCF TGV as it is a different company from the SNCF TER service. They are both SNCF. We were told at Nice Station that the Zou card is valid on all public transport. It’s not. At Antibes station they managed to shakedown at least 4 sets of tourists with fines because they said SNCF TGV is ‘a different company’ to SNCF TER. Who knew? It’s such a blatant horrible way to cheat people. It’s the same route on the same line just different letters on the train. I’d say the shakedown is worth thousands of euro a day to SNCF judging by the financial haul carried out faster than a pickpocket. It’s clearly a scam because of the way it was carried out with such ease, speed and efficiency. The Zou card does not work on all public transport on the French Riviera. So read the letters carefully before you board the train or you’ll be the next victim. The guy said he was doing me a favour by only scamming €35; he said he was doing me a solid by not charging €70. I have more respect for the pickpockets at the station than the SNCF shirts and caps fleecing tourists. Horrible way to treat visitors to your country.

Saint-Raphaël station, 16-10-2024. We are accompanying our 2 friends, aged 88 and 87 respectively, to the Paris TGV, each with one piece of luggage. One of the two who is very ill must go to the emergency room tomorrow in Paris. A controller prevents us from accessing the platform, we don't have a ticket, that's the rule...we still try to show her the usefulness of helping our friends transport and put their luggage in the carriage...no question of deviating from the rule because the SNCF is trying to IMPROVE ITS IMAGE...we could get on the train without a ticket...we are over 70 years old...did she understand her role? We don't thank her for her lack of humanity!

TGV max subscription to avoid!!! I do not receive emails to confirm the reservation of my tickets 48 hours before departure and the tickets, which are canceled because they are not confirmed, remain displayed as if the trip was still valid until the train arrives at the station. The perfect recipe for getting fined. We would like to deceive people that we would not otherwise do... Furthermore, very few trains available at acceptable times. In short, a dirty story.

TGV incredible discomfort: very narrow seats, sitting in them almost straight like poles to put as many seats as possible per car, in order to earn more money on tickets which can go up, depending on the destination, to 100€ in normal fare, soon we will eat on our knees to make even more room; dusty cars too, I no longer count the number of times I have sneezed while being near the ventilation; ridiculous luggage storage space considering, once again, the number of travelers...Always more beautiful slogans, despite ever more numerous train delays, ever higher prices and ever more enormous discomfort, I no longer count the number of trips during which you have to stay up for 1 hour having paid 30 to 50€ for the ticket or the toilet which has a problem, not to mention the reimbursements which vary depending on the time of delay because 30min, 45min, 1 hour late for a trip to work or missing an appointment is nothing! For the few rare times that they refund tickets, it is on a percentage of the price; while for travelers, the price of the ticket rises in a few minutes, depending on the number of people having views on the same trip, thank you bots!!! The SNCF is in the image of the public service: paying more for a service of less and less quality

Travelled 2nd Class in Coach 17. Zurich to Paris. Pros: - Quick to reach destination- Lot's of room for luggageCons:- WiFi doesn't work- Power point gets turned off and on at every station arrival- Broken and stuck seat tray- Not clean and maintained- Announcement in French mostly

Recent holder of a Max Jeune subscription, I am informing you of the questionable practices of the SNCF. Having reserved a ticket via the Max Jeune subscription, I wanted to modify it because on the MaxPlanner site (of the SNCF dedicated to TGV Max Jeune subscriptions), I had found another more relevant route with plenty of places available. I therefore had to cancel my previous reservation to make the new reservation. So far, everything is normal. But in fact, the site MaxPlanner was bugged and all the information on the trains available was false, which was later confirmed by a message: "The MAX PLANNER is under technical maintenance. Please do not take the results of this into account. A return to normal is planned for xxx. Thank you for your understanding." But the site was still accessible. And yes, instead of pointing to a simple page "under maintenance", the SNCF prefers to leave false information visible, while knowing that it is false. Bottom line, I canceled my initial reservations and I cannot make new reservations on these dates, either by internet or by telephone, indicating my good faith. My vacation is ruined. Thank you SNCF for this contempt for customers and for this management of a deliberately buggy site that is visible. This is unworthy of a large company in 2024.
The trip from Geneva to Paris was a disaster. Instead of 3.15 hours, the journey took over 6 hours due to a technical defect. The Schwazwald Bimmelbahn is faster!!!

OUIGO is awful, avoid booking with them if possible. Omio app is awful also, together they made my life hell over a booking. There is no customer service, and each just points to the other. they should both be banned from trading. By contrast I found IRYO great to deal with, when booking a train from Barcelona to Madrid, with the terrible french company Ouigo
Worst experience ever. First they charge 38 € for a 9 minutes ride, and then they charge 20€ for the suitcase. They are so greedy that I get sick. Disgusting company. Hope the go bankrupt.

TGV is the worst train company I’ve ever traveled with. Not only do they price their seat reservations ridiculously high, but they also charge you 50 euros if you activate your Interrail pass after the departure time from the train station. In our case, we activated our Interrail passes 2 and 3 minutes after the scheduled departure time, and three hours later, when they showed up to control our tickets, they required us to pay 50 euros each because we activated our passes too late. And they threatened us with calling the police in Paris if we refused to pay.

In mid-August, I called on the access plus service in Paris, for people with disabilities. I'm leaving for several weeks, so more than one suitcase, declared to the SNCF. And upon arriving, a deplorable reception in Paris at the access plus service. I understand that this service is not a moving service, but when you have more than one declared suitcase, this service should provide a luggage trolley, in order to help disabled people. From the moment I got off the train to the access desk, I heard myself being reproached, this attitude is inexcusable.  This service does not have the attitude to take care of disabled people and their luggage. On the other hand, Rennes and Quimper, the access plus service is at the top. I met caring, friendly people, which is sorely lacking at Accès plus Paris. If taking care of disabled people does not suit Accès plus Paris, I recommend that its staff take another job, as humanity is sorely lacking in these people. WE DO NOT CHOOSE TO BE DISABLED, this service should be aware of this.

Wanted to travel from Zurich to Paris. Due to a technical issue we came about 15 driving minutes far from Zurich and then turned around. Was told we should take a train to Basel and there would be a replacement train. Arriving in Basel was nothing. The Swiss citizen were told to get home and make a refund. No Alternative travel. Go and look yourself… Best customer service I ever experienced. Hope at least I get a refund of the hotel, train and the concert i missed due to no bookable trains the following day.

Always thought of the TGVs as better than UK trains. But currently delayed by 150 mins on the Lyria service from Geneva to Paris and the customer service is foul. Poor comms.  No apology. Zippo assistance.

The train that left Lyon at 2:04 pm and was scheduled to arrive in Paris at 4:10 pm was STOPPED for more than TWO hours due to problems on the railway lines. Chaos among passengers. I, with a schedule responsibility, felt very disadvantaged.

Unlike the station in Paris, the train station in Provence made our train ride from Provence to Paris a nightmare.  Three of us traveled from Provence to Paris, including a senior citizen, 90 years old.  We received Zippo assistance to help us navigate us to our train.   Had we not found someone speaking English, we would never have made it.  1) No porter service2) The train announcement systems was only in French3) The station does not have any signage indicating where each coach stops4) The train itself does not have markings on the cars. I DO NOT recommend this trip unless you have received very thorough instructions in advance.
Only two stars because the train was very dirty. No cleanliness. Sunday September 22, 2 hours journey from La Baule to le Main, TGV INOUI.

The SNCF is a machine for ripping off its customers, with a total lack of transparency on prices.   Compensation of 25% for delays of up to two hours, cancellation or change at a cost of 19 euros while the operation costs the SNCF nothing… on the contrary since it sells the tickets more expensive. The public service mission is no longer its horizon, only the desire to make money on the backs of users motivates its action.

I have walking problems. I chose the TGV Turin Paris and return because it was sold to me as a direct train. Instead, only after payment was I informed that, due to the landslide that occurred more than a year ago, we would have to travel by coach and stop for more than an hour while waiting for a new TGV. The stop on the way out was in a deserted land without a bar, toilets or seats to sit on, just low concrete walls. On the way back stop at Ulzio...new TGV on the second track, BROKEN ELEVATOR. The promised assistance when boarding the bus was not seen. A shameful scam. It was enough to be informed of these HABITUAL malfunctions to choose another travel method, more suitable for A PERSON WITH A MOTOR DISABILITY. SO A REAL SCAM. COMPLIMENTS!!!

The train journey from Paris to Barcelona was disappointing. The trip felt like it took an eternity when it could have been much shorter with fewer stops. I chose this option for its ecological benefits over flying, but unless the service improves and becomes more affordable (first class cost around €180 with no added perks), I'll likely return to flying. This service desperately needs competition to drive improvements and make customer satisfaction a priority. Overall, it was an unfortunate experience.
There is very little space for luggage, so we had to put it in the middle of the hallway, people were very awkward and it was much too hot.

First class-haha! Took the Paris to Lyon train. Left on time, arrived on time, clean. “First class” unfortunately had minimal AC, a stinky bathroom by the end of the trip, no ice, zero help with luggage and we rode backwards. If you can find a better train, take it! Or take some nausea medicine with you!

The staff of the TGV train are the most Racist and rude we have encountered for any service worldwide. Marie Pierre was not pleased to see us African Americans in our paid  1st class seats and was rude to us Only from the minute we boarded. As we came on the train she demanded that we get out of her way. We held global EURAIL passes for which we paid €1,500 and had seat reservations for an additional €150 but she still demanded that we pay an additional €175. We had a named trip in the EURAIL APP as well. When we eventually give in and paid she charged a child as an adult and ignored my question as to why. Her rudeness and racism was so surreal we had to get it on record.

First class is no longer up to the standard it was a few years ago, sometimes it is very good but often the seats are dirty, the corridors the same for certain trains. Too bad because this train transports us quickly and it is more ecological.

It is a horrible train company ever!! The tickets cannot be refunded even though with an exceptional case (i.e death / illness). The customer service was bad. We had billions of emails and phone call. First, they transferred my call to SNCF, then SNCF asked me to contact OUIGO. As well, no one speak English beside French at OUIGO customer service phone line. We lost 200 EUR tickets and couldn't get any refund due to my partner's cancer situation. They don't have sympathy. We are very disappointed and never travel with them again!!!!!!

Awful experience. No direction at Saint Raphael train station. We paid for first and sat in second class bc we were waiting on the opposite side of where the train pulled up. Had to run with our bags. Awful terrible unorganized experience. Would never do this again.

Placed on the stairs because of dog allergies. I paid €89 for a ticket to take a trip seated on the stairs of the TGV because the woman next to me had 2 dogs with her and I am allergic. The conductor told me that he had no other solution than to place me there, due to lack of space on the train. Not once did he ask another passenger if they would be willing to change seats. As a result, I only have a refund of €13 out of the €89 paid because it is the “maximum they can do”. No ! I took an entire trip without air conditioning on stairs in a passage. You can do better
A nice Paris early in the morning and already dirty! The train did not see the cleaning staff! We pay a lot (150) and with a reduction too!

Shameful!!! I was doing a Lorient Toulon. Arriving at Paris Montparnasse I was told to go to Gare d’Austerlitz to take the night train. Arriving there, I was told that I didn't show. Lamentable, overpriced trains, incompetent service on all levels....I was stuck in Paris for the night. We are told, traveling by train is more eco-friendly but it lasts 2 days. I would have taken the plane, it would have been much simpler. France and this new world where no one is able to help you out. We are all customers and the SNCF has forgotten that! Date of experience: August 17, 2024
We travelled from Zurich to Paris but for some reasing the train made a 30 minute stop in Basel on the way there and on the return journey which basically nullified the train's speed of 320 km/h

Lyon Part dieu to Montpellier St. Roch. The train was delayed 45 minutes.. however the issue is much bigger. Noone checked our tiquets and no seats were available in the train. The result is that we traveled standing, at the luggage point, as many other passengers.  So, we payed for a seat that never existed and for a tiquet that was never checked. Don't bother paying for tgv..after all is free and extremely uncomfortable.
Repulsively filthy train in 1st class, non-functional toilets, ticket price disproportionate to the service

0 stars if possible, blatant harassment and corruption. Absolutely disgusting, especially while hosting the Olympics. Disgrace and embarrassment of a nation.My friend and I were returning from Cannes on our way to Nice.  He bought two tickets but we were separated in the throng of people boarding the train and ended up sitting in different cars.  When the conductor came to me I showed my ticket, which he said had already been scanned.  I explained that my friend probably just sent me the wrong ticket that he had already scanned.  My friend sent me the other, and then the hostility began.  The train official kept badgering me saying that I was not Jon, whom I’m obviously not.  I kept reiterating that my friend had purchased two tickets and he was in a different car.  He said I don’t care.I kept asking to just buy another ticket on the app or pay in cash for another ticket.  He said because I had already shown a ticket with a different name, it was a fine of €70.  That fine then fluctuated over the course of the conversation to €100 then €150, then eventually back to €70.  Keep in mind these tickets were €9.He then brought over a military cop who said nothing but whose presence was clearly meant to intimidate me.  As a young female traveler sitting alone away from my friend, I felt incredibly unsafe and violated and paid the fine for fear of being detained otherwise.  This would absolutely never happen in America nor most other “first world” countries.  I find this particularly disgraceful and quite honestly embarrassing for the Olympics host country.As a French Canadian by parentage I’d always loved France and the language and culture.  This completely destroyed any positive view of the country and affirmed that the social media perspectives of its poorly managed public service are indeed unfortunately true.I sent a complaint to the US Embassy but hopes are low of any resolution.  The SNCF likely will continue being able to enjoy taking advantage of young tourists and their willingness to pay rather than face foreign detention.  Shame on France.

Travelled return from Paris to Nice for a quick Olympic visit. Train was easy to locate at Gare Lyonand Nice. Train seating was comfortable. Ride was very smooth and ontime. WIFI was great gave me the ability to connect with the outside world Refreshments and food were plentiful and served with a smile Onboard and boarding staff did everything possible to make this ride seamless Bought tickets in North America with ease. Fantastic way to travel through Europe. Well done. !!!

Ouch ouch, I wanted to get my ticket refunded because I missed my train due to an accident on the road, and then I suspected it was a scam when I started to fill out a long, tedious file where they ask us for references that they already have in order to make us stop the reimbursement process. And I receive a very gloomy email without the possibility of revising my file explaining to me that they will not reimburse me without really a valid explanation, it would have been necessary that I call a number to continue my trip, something that you obviously need to know if this has never happened to you. It's simple, it's a scam, don't take out insurance with your ticket, the same goes for additional luggage or large suitcases, they never check, at worst it's €20.

OUIGO = help! Never again! Journey Valence - Antibes Uneducated young people who take your place without apologizing, who smoke in the car! No, but where are we there??? Apparently other very drunk "travelers" were also caught smoking and were fined. Not the young people in my car... Speaking with the train controller, he informs me that he can do nothing: neither make them get off the train, nor make them stop. That some people even get on without paying...I will now have to opt only for classic TGVs or the plane so as not to be hassled but it's not the same price eh. So sad for low-income households, who are forced to endure this degradation of our society. It's high time to do something!

OUIGO = never again. Always delays. We never refund you the right amount. It is indicated on the train that you will receive a refund, but in reality it is much less! You pay for things you don't have style taken etc.Frankly lousy at c****

The sncf is execrable, the control staff must be excessively frustrated in their daily lives to demonstrate such wickedness, a scumbag company, I put 1 point because we cannot give 0. Favor other transport services, this one is only good for greasing its hands with your money and is not capable of respecting punctuality, simply shameful!

We really wanted to take the TGV on our holiday in France. The joy began in the holiday resort of Argèles sur Mer: the extremely diligent young lady at the counter checked various connections to Lyon for us. Thank you very much for that! Then the actual journey from Narbonne to Lyon Part Dieu: punctual to the minute! (Unthinkable in Germany these days) Seating comfort as comfortable as on grandma's sofa, extremely disciplined passengers, whisper sound - in 2nd class!

We traveled on TGV in 1st class from Basel to Paris, the journey was comfortable and pleasant, especially on time. Unfortunately, nothing is offered at the table, but only available in the restaurant car. Not very affordable rates, considering you booked 5 months in advance.

Deplorable service, luggage surcharge, impossibility of changing the ticket without paying at best 19 euros, also impossible to put your ticket back on sale as announced in the scandalous false ad "OUIGO SWAP"... in short, don't let yourself be fooled by this monumental scam.

Pathetic. No room for suitcases larger than cabin suitcases. And even there. On the way, the suitcase was knee-deep, on the way back, I was left standing between two carriages. For the price... So take the plane. Cheaper and more comfortable

“1st class”? Seats without windows, poorly numbered, broken seat, headrest at shoulder level, torn and unable to move, no room for legs, 0 service, not even a glass of water. Brussels-Paris section of a transatlantic trip with Air France, paid 4,000 euros in business class, flight!

Catastrophic!!! The SNCF is very expensive and is no longer able to provide its service…delays, last-minute cancellations…. “We’re going to make you love the car” should be its slogan… can’t wait for the competition

To travel from Barcelona or Girona to Paris it is an excellent option since the total journey time is equal or better than by plane, since there are no transfers, you do not have to pick up suitcases... We traveled with 2 children and they gave us seats with a table on the second floor of the car both on the way there and on the way back. On both trips people complained about how poorly marked the carriages are. Errors occur at all stops and there are people who have to stand in the bar car or at the entrance because they cannot go through the entire train inside and they have made a mistake. On the way back there were many stewards who guided you on the platform but in Girona we were almost lucky to get it right. In Girona we found a woman in one of our seats because she didn't know how to find hers and in Paris a foreign woman with her children took the wrong car and sat in our seats. It was a continuum. It would not cost anything to put large numbers on the outside of the car. You can carry several suitcases, but the shelf that in Spain fits cabin suitcases, on the TGV is very narrow and only fits small briefcases and bags. There are plugs but not in each seat. The journey could be faster, but between Perpignan and I think Montpellier, it goes very slow, I think on a normal route, which makes the trip longer. The coffee bar service is very correct, not so much the slightly inflated prices, but the quality of all the products. All the people on the train were very friendly. The train was clean and so were the toilets. The only thing missing is for the night trains with sleeping cars to return. It would be even more comfortable.

thanks a lot SCNF! had to get a train from Marseilles to Macon for a VERY important event. gave plenty of time to spare, planning to arrive in macon at 12:13 when the event was at 1:35. But no, the train was extremely delayed (although why i don’t know) and once it finally arrived it took forever to leave the station. We are now so so late for this event, ruining the whole day and causing repercussions with connecting trains too. Something must be done about this horrible situation

we took the TGV from Paris Gare du lyon to Nice, getting to the train was super easy, we found our seats fast, enough space for our luggage,  generally the sears were comfortable, WIFI and food were OK, the trip took about 6 hours and was on time, it is a very efficient way to travel without going through airport hassle

The air conditioning makes you SICK. However, it's nice outside. Why? The train even arrived early. It's exceptional especially when he is not able to simply arrive on time. Either late or early Thank you

I travelled few times Barcelona- París first class. I think is over priced for what it is. First of all no wify, almost at all so no way to work on the train. Second of all , most of the bathroom have no soap. It has often delay on the way. On a good side, the first class seats are pretty comfortable and the food on the train is price but pretty good which is unusual.

An agent who wanted to let off steam attacked me because I had misunderstood the train announcement. Firstly there is a delay, Secondly I pay for a direct and even less for a service like this.Lyon -> Montpellier

Not enough room for XL luggage. Cabin baggage locations above the seats are very small. It seems like everything is done to purposely annoy people. I travel a lot by train throughout Europe. The least functional trains are on the French network. Everywhere else there is room for everyone's luggage. Armored trains on every journey. We save money by piling ourselves together like cattle. We have centralized bins in each car and therefore more space for luggage. I wonder who the engineers are to have such catastrophic ideas. The lamps on each seat are placed on the armrest, therefore very annoying and come on unexpectedly throughout the journey. Inspectors often intolerant with a lack of discernment because the more fines there are, the more personal commissions there are. And in terms of recruitment, we must not be at the top of the basket. Not to mention the delays / exorbitant prices etc…..I try to find positive things but not obvious ones.
The worst possible train experience? Look no further, it's OUIGO. Old and dirty train. No travel pleasure. Scary.

My wife and I went to Paris for a few days at the end of May. I chose two 1 class tickets and it was a wonderful travel experience from A to Z. Everything was just right, from the friendly train staff, the seating and the delicious food with a glass of champagne. We are already looking forward to the next trip and thank you for it.

I was traveling in first class on the TGV from Lyon to Paris. The train was a two-story car with seats arranged in rows of 1 and 2. The seats were certainly spacious, but their orientation was fixed and could not be changed in the direction of travel, and they faced each other in the middle of the vehicle. The luggage storage area is also on the second floor, so you may have to lift heavy luggage. We shouldn't compare it to Japan's Shinkansen, but France is an advanced country, so I think there is room for a little more consideration in terms of design and functionality. I ate at the buffet on the way there, and it was fun, bright and open, with a lot of friendly passengers.

Email from the SNCF received a few days before the trip telling me that my place had been changed. Once seated, a lady presents herself with the same seat number. She suggests going to the conductor to find a solution (crowded train). And there, the controller treats him like a delinquent in front of the other passengers, even after showing him the email. When he understood that I was acting in good faith (SNCF error), no excuse for his attitude. I'm shocked.
Bad smell, poor food options, no AC on first class. For 700 eur for a family pf 3 one would expect a bit more. Tried to complain over their website and all you get is a lousy chatbot experience

,If I could give OUIGO a negative 1 I would. Absolutely the worst transportation of have ever taken. I’ve taken OUIGO multiple times while I lived in Paris and I have never had a clean experience. From late arrivals (9-10, the train is late). To air conditioning issues, to dirty toilets. I would never recommend this service to anyone. In fact if possible I would rather walk from Paris to the south of France than use OUIGO. -1 from me.

I took a day trip from Paris to Geneva. It's my first time riding the TGV and I'm very satisfied. The view from the train window is beautiful, but I don't feel like taking pictures because the windows aren't cleaned well. I had a fixed seat, so I was riding backwards. Japan's Shinkansen trains are quieter. The rail joints are noisy. It was nice to have power and WiFi available.

It’s a shame! always a problem, always a delay, always m…!!!!! the price at which we pay for the tickets? more and more expensive but more and more problems during the trip! in this case lower the prices it will go with the quality of the service! shame on the sncf

Female staff member with curly, shoulder length hair and glasses on gate at  Disneyland Paris  (to Charles de Gualle Airport) TGV was horrible. Rude, unhelpful, a bit of a megalomaniac. Told us our tickets weren’t valid and we had to but new ones online. No courtesy. This is discriminatory, as not everyone has a smartphone or can use one, plus the wifi/signal is non existent in the station. I had the opportunity to make a trip to Paris Lyon in TGV Inouï 1st class and the return in Frecciarossa business Verdict: the Italian train crushes its French competitor all along the line! - Frecciarossa welcome: with a smile on the Italian side - TGV welcome: it's almost a nuisance on the French side when you ask for your train (display broken on the TGV doors) - Frecciarossa seat and comfort: wide and very comfortable space on the Italian side electrical and USB sockets for each seat small, very practical trash can on each table - TGV seat and comfort: broken seats and our 4 faulty electrical sockets in the TGV (you will say it can happen of course but it happens a little too often in TGV I think) - Frecciarossa on-board service: table service snack with drink and real Italian coffee - TGV on-board service: no table service, bar prices prohibitive for average and rather industrial quality - Frecciarossa toilets: clean and everything works perfectly (soap, water and hand dryer) - TGV toilets: effort made on cleanliness in recent times but regular soap and hand dryer malfunctions (soap is hard I find especially in 1st supposed to be more "comfortable" - Frecciarossa prices: very competitive (maybe still in the launch phase so I imagine will increase in the future) - TGV prices: more and more expensive for a service rendered less and less qualitative (see the comparison above) - Punctuality and reimbursement Frecciarossa: train on time and good compensation policy also displayed on the screens in the train - Punctuality and reimbursement TGV: although efforts are made on punctuality, delays are quite frequent and compensation is increasingly difficult to obtain (submission of a tedious complaint file via a chatbot and good luck...) In short, I hope that opening up to competition will allow a real dusting off of this old SNCF house A company which certainly has good assets but must now stop behaving in “public service” mode in a monopoly situation

A zero for SNCF.

Firstly I had the same ticket as another person because of their overbooking technique to make more profits but that's nothing! Time for checks arrive and I therefore present my tickets to a ticket inspector who also asks me for a card to prove that it is really me. So I naturally show my vital card which contains name/first name/date of birth/photo of me… all the information necessary to prove that I am not a usurper. She would not hear anything, giving me a fine and in your opinion how much was this fine? €160, €160 even though I am 20 years old and I eat 2 meals a day consisting of of noodles to be able to pay my rent. All this so that I pay 160€ because of a company that does not respect its passengers and a controller who needs a vacation... Thank you for your compassion, if you want to help me pay the rent it would be with great pleasure. More seriously, expect an immediate refund. A shame!!

I take the TGV INOUI every week between PAU and PARIS. Their WOFI is a gigantic Joke, and they brag about it. Maybe you should think about changing operator or doing an upgrade. It's really disgusting. Ultra slow connection, regular disconnections, in short, hell when you have a 4.5 hour journey and want to work. Pay for 1st class and did not get it also NO Wi-Fi for all the 6hrs, complete rip off never again will I use this service

Delay of 1 hour 20 minutes at departure.  The train was not ready. Of course nothing to sit on. Once again the SNCF has demonstrated its inability to manage its trains. Indifferent staff. All of this is paid for through our taxes.

Please note: on these trains you have a 50% chance that it will smell like urine during your entire journey, because the stench from the toilets reaches halfway through the carriages. The journey was good, the only thing is that when we were returning from Paris to Barcelona they changed us at the Montpellier station due to technical problems. Bedbug bites, according to my doctor. During my 2.5 hour journey in a TER from Angoulême to Royan, I felt itchy. I figured there were mosquitoes on the train. The seats of these new unheard of cars are uncomfortable, hard seating, and above all the table is too long and impossible to lower without traumatizing your abdomen. In short, undoubtedly an effect of public call for tender, that would be the only excuse. Otherwise, it is much more serious for France.

Very good for us... train exactly on time, comfort inside... only downside but the SNCF can't do anything about it: in the TGV Lyria, the Swiss are without any embarrassment and scream throughout the train... if you want to rest, forget it, they are infernal and unmanageable.

High speed train (Train à Grande Vitesse) or low speed train (Train à basse vitesse) 850 km from Perpignan to Paris in 5 hours, leaving an average of 170km. Where is the high speed? Furthermore, without any type of security to get on and with their toilets very dirty.
Great and very comfortable family space to go with children: plugs to charge cell phones and a table for games or eating.

Mannheim - Avignon TGV 9580 in September 2023. Already driven this route several times. Since Corona, trains have been slightly overcrowded, especially 1st class. EC speed from Mannheim to Lyon, then top speed. As usual: seat direction changes from Strasbourg and if the dining car is missing, 6 hours can be very long.

First of all, I like the SNCF. I would have liked it to remain a public service. My comment concerns the Océane range TGVs and their seats. Dear SNCF member, I've had enough! enough of your disrespect towards us travelers! Fast train between Paris and marseille booked via Trainline but no air conditioning in our compartment with the temperature around 33degrees. Unfortunately not recommended
The SNCF is really crap, the train times change all the time, for one trip the arrival time has to change at least 4 times, it's scandalous, it's nonsense

We purchased these tickets through SNCF to take the Lyria from Paris to Lausanne. The train itself is fine, the train is efficient, first class is relatively spacious,  but the lack of air conditioning is appalling. I don't think I will ever ride with TGV again.  Outside it is 91 degrees (34 C) and I'm convinced if a window were opened it would be cooler than the temperature of the car right now.  I assume this is a ploy to drive up business in the cafe car since that is the only car with a temperature below 80 on the train.  Older people look sick and I have had to take medicine due to nausea from the heat.  The bottom cars are slightly cooler, but not by more than a couple degrees.  I'm incredibly disappointed with nearly every experience with the trip.  Please consider flying instead or taking another train.

It's perfect! With the TGV from Hendaye to Paris it takes us less time to go to Paris than to go to Madrid or Barcelona, ​​that says a lot. In addition, with the annual discount cards that exist in France you have very good rates that include two adults and several children.

Horrible experience. 30 hours (thirty) to return from Paris to Turin. Delays, technical problems, little information, we are in the third world. No type of assistance, little education from the French railway staff.

The big disappointment for the first and last time we are 3 hours late and we are not yet at Cannes Lyon station 9 hours and we have not yet arrived in Nice 1 hour stops no matter we are elderly people at least respect us.

20 years ago I absolutely loved traveling by TGV in France, regularly using the Paris-Lyons route for both business and personal travel.  On a recent business trip, I elected to use trains to get from London to Munich - Eurostar to Paris, then TGV to Munich.  NEVER AGAIN.  The Eurostar was great, but TGV is simply no longer the jewel of Europe's train travel that it used to be.  Service was non-existent (in 1st Class), food options were worse than a cheap vending machine, the coaches were worn-down and beat-up, and most of the WCs on the train did not function and were closed off.  The only part of the TGV experience remaining is the speed - and I can use a plane for that.

I'm still traveling with my family, gone and already thinking about the return, we are in first class, dilapidated carriage, dirty with a bad smell. Leaving aside the fact that I, a celiac sufferer, was unable to eat lunch because, although some gluten free dishes were indicated on the menu, I was told that they were finished (at 11.30am!) Could this be the organization of the French railway?

No power outlet, wifi that doesn't work, no bar car (phantom car 14) non-refundable ticket, no concession possible to just look for your phone with the controller on a Sunday morning between Angers and Paris. Change jobs 💋

I took the OUIFI which guaranteed me internet during the trip. What a scam! Pay 3 euros to get nothing! Nothing worked!!!Never again

Excellent connection from Amsterdam to Paris; fast and enough space. I thought the WiFi was very poor and the air conditioning was also not optimal. It was very hot on board. Otherwise just okay, convenient to the heart of Paris.

Everything is lost! the SNCF is proof! getting worse and worse! It's expensive, now the TGVs are all double, even short distances. We are crowded together like animals at the start, and whether up or down, there is less space. The seat cannot be extended. All this to save space and more money. The height of it! We are like animals for very high prices.
Clocked at over 300km.  Fantastic eco travel experience.  Comfortable and convenient.  Nice cafe, luggage stow and bathrooms.

Great way to travel from CDG to Disneyland. Only takes 9 minutes and costs €18 pp. The Magic shuttle which is so heavily advertised is €25 pp and takes more than an hour. TGV is under Terminal 2. Not easy to get a seat but for the 9 min journey we just stayed by the doors. Great speedy way to get from airport to Disney.

Dispute with SNCF since October 2022! Following cancellation by Sncf at 3 a.m. for a departure of our TGV at 5:50 a.m. on 08/22/2022 from Part Dieu station in Lyon. There are 4 of us and we had booked a trip to the USA and we had to take a plane to Roissy, taking off at 11am. All we have to do now is jump in our car to try to get to the airport on time. Airport parking reserved along the way (195.80 euros), return tolls (73 euros), full return fuel (166.47) or 435.27 euros! Not to mention the stress!! We are asking for the rbt of our tickets, i.e. 195 euros, and the costs caused by this TGV cancellation. We therefore provide the corresponding invoices. Finally we thought so...Our file remains pending for months before having a first offer of 80 euros......we refuse and ask again for the rbt of the 4 tickets, i.e. 195 euros + the costs incurred. After a few more weeks the SNCF "grand seigneur" reimburses us the 195 euros but for the rest....we must send the file to the mediator. What we do. In July 2023, we receive the result from the mediator!!! And there, the final bouquet! He is missing the parking exit day, the invoices for the 2 full tanks, the plane tickets. In short, at no time are we asked for the missing parts that we had!! As a result, the mediator offers 57 euros in compensation that the SNCF carrier can accept or....refuse....and if we are not OK with that we can refuse but we can no longer contact the mediator to send her the missing parts. We must initiate proceedings before the competent court!!!!And leave again for 1 year of procedure and this time at our expense ????I don't know anything about it and then Fed up😡 Suffice to say that the SNCF is calm, there will not be many complaints after our files have passed into the hands of a mediator!!! Long live the SNCF, as efficient as ever!!! I couldn't give zero stars but it's worth a zero point!!!

Where to start... 50' late on the Limoges-Gare d'Austerlitz intercity, a breakdown could happen. Gare d'Austerlitz to Gare de l'Est is metro line 5, well marked on the ground, you can't go wrong. So next time for the same price and the same duration I'll take my good car and I'll transfer the SNCF Connect app as soon as I get back It's not over!!! In second class there is no power on the sockets...
The trains are wonderful. Everything perfect. They are not cheap, but they are worth the investment. Very fast and very comfortable.
do not take out the insurance that the SNCF offers you as “cancellation - reimbursement of 100 if you cannot travel”. it's a lie, there are conditions

TGV canceled and well you won't believe it but I had to pay for a new ticket (130 euros) because there was supposedly a strike notice and in this case the SNCF does not reimburse!! Yesterday I wanted to visit Versailles with my friend we needed to buy metro ticket to go there but there was anyyy workers to ask which ticket we should buy so we bought 4 tickets to Paris (because we thought it's correct one and there was not any one for verifying) for going and coming back and it worked so we thought it was the correct ticket But when we got in Versailles the controller check our ticket and he said it's the wrong ticket and you should pay 70 Euros as the fine , I was like WHATTTTT?!?! he forced us to pay 70 Euros for a ticket that cost only 4 or 3 euros and that was an honest mistake,Don't use this train and use other options even if it seems more expensive.

….the beautiful French railway of the past! Milan-Paris train from times gone by, service just sufficient, I expected better despite the good expectations considering that the French were the first to apply high speed in Europe...

Unheard of discomfort in the new TGV wagons. In the old ones, the second class was correct and the first class was very comfortable. In the new ones, back pain is guaranteed in both. What. Unacceptable regression. Upcoming plane trips.

We traveled with tgv air from Nantes/roissy Charles de Gaulle to and from our vacation!
