That awful smell from overflowing lavatory. Nasty. There seems to be too many staffs who simply do not care about cleanliness or service Trash
Lamentable 👎. The SNCF trains never arrive on time. Today August 1, 2023 Aix Paris Gare de Lyon 40 minutes late.

The train arrived 2 hours late into the final destination, meaning I missed my very vital connection. Fortunately, the train conductor was making regular announcements about how late we would be, unfortunately, they were only in french, so good luck if you are a tourist. By the time we arrived to Paris, all ticket offices were of course closed (around 20:45) so I just had to buy a new ticket for a later train. So of course they make it super easy for you to actually get some money back. Anyway, safe to say I will not be traveling to France any time soon again.

We traveled with TGV InOui from Milan to Paris and then back. Everything was fine, friendly staff, clean carriage, punctual. Excellent price. Only note: both on the outward and return journey the bar-restaurant was deactivated for a short stretch of the route.

We thought we'd take a relaxing train ride through the French countryside to take in the sights. Instead, we found old, disgusting train cars with no air conditioning on a  ride that was meant to be less than 6 hours (spoiler alert: it was more).

Absolutely shameful to provide such uncomfortable seats for passengers. impossible to find a minimally comfortable position, no room for the legs. places for luggage we don't even talk about it. It's been years since I took the train and not sure to repeat

Very practical because you can reach the center in just 35 minutes from Lille and it is not too expensive, the connections to Brussels are free with the SNCB. On the other hand, the trains are starting to age and are no longer very comfortable and increasingly late. I was 50 minutes late on my last trip and for 50 minutes neither the SNCF nor the SNCB managed to give reliable information.

After three years of using this high-speed service weekly, I cannot be positive at all. They are often late without a proper update. Staff is very often stressed out and aggressive in tone. In total, I arrived around 10 times more than two hours later at my destination causing a lot of frustration for people on the train. When addressing these long and unacceptable delays due to poor reasoning, how can one be satisfied after seeing so much better examples but far less expensive? One example was so hilarious: the train left a half hour later, the train and station notification was that there were "issues" with the train, however that staff were discussing that a member overslept his alarm?!?!?" Often heard other "real reasons" instead of the mentioned ones through official communication, which is very unprofessional. One should expect more for a high-end train service as during Corona, the local and slower national train service caused a higher service level with fewer delays and friendlier more professional staff.

The French invented high speed, now it's time to upgrade or step aside. Delays seem to be normal, this can depend on many factors, but dilapidated first class carriages have no excuse! Clogged bathroom, air conditioning once necessary to wear a sweater for freezing temperatures, other times to suffocate in the heat. No air conditioning on a 5.5 hour trip better Paris and Nice.  Very stuffy, hot, humid and uncomfortable the enite ride.

strange experience: train stops in the middle of nowhere ( small village station) after communication that a sick person has to be taken of the train and waiting for an ambulance (" sapeurs pompiers")starts. I’d taken trains in France and other European countries and never found them to be like this.  When I purchased my tickets I knew this was the low-cost version but I thought it just had less services and everything was ala Carte. I didn’t expect to be packed like sardines in an enclosed room with little air.
Avoid the « food » served on the TGVinoui! We paid €28 for a soggy “burger” which was disgusting, an old salad and 2 soft drinks.
Taxi provided via Inouï to be avoided at all costs. Monsieur leaves before time Attempt to change the flexible ticket fails... Lack of professionalism

Thalys is easy with onboarding, no queues or long security lines like at the airport. High comfort seats and friendly people. Clean toilets. A great alternative for air travel.

We had paid for the overpriced seating tickets. We had bought the railpass but activated the trip in the app a couple of minutes after boarding the train. Because of this the staff demanded we paid a 50€ fine per person. Unbelievable.

The OUIGO company is a SCAM! I tried several times to exchange my tickets before my train left and the process did not work on the website. So they kept my 128 euros and now "invited me" to buy new tickets for the new date, which will now cost 200 euros! Such a SCAM!

Will never again use this service, here's why;1) Had reservation for Nice to Paris Jun 2023 booked months in advance. 2) Train cancelled by email less than 4hrs notice due to technical failures. If your journey includes more than 1 leg we suggest you contact station personnel"3) Went to Nice Ville station ...no Ouigo personnel. Let the controllers do their job, no worries... However, there is no need to be aggressive at the start even if the remark is justified... But above all, paying for a defined seat and being ordered, on the basis of being full when you have 2 allocated seats, to spend 3 hours on a wet floor in front of an out-of-service toilet is more than inappropriate. I love trains and so do my children. We took TGV from Lille to Paris for a day trip. Let's start with the booking process via SNCF Connect. It saved me €40 as opposed to NS International, the website and app are nightmares. The user interface is terrible. I booked first class tickets for my wife, two young children and I. For some reason the booking got split in two, with two separate booking codes for me and my wife and my two small children. Then I decided to change our train for our inbound journey, which was possible according to my fare conditions. But I had to do it twice with, in theory, the situation that my 1 and 3 year old could be sitting somewhere else as I had to change seating for them and my wife and I.High speed train travel is coined as 'the alternative for flying', but I'd prefer the plane anytime as it comes with a more hassle free travel experience.  Our train was not busy, but check-in sees all the passengers trying to storm to a couple of narrow gates that do not accommodate travellers with buggy's. Luckily, there was a traveller receiving assistance. We could follow through the gates for wheelchair users, but don't think any member of staff will do anything when they see you approach with a buggy and a child in it.As said, we only travelled with two buggy's and a diaper bag. Our double decker train was not step free from the entrance. No problem for us, but if you travel with anything more than a small bag you will be having a very hard time getting your luggage in the train. There are no luggage carts. Luggage storage is minimal and only accommodates really small bags. With our buggy's, the rack was full. So what if the train would be at full capacity and there is no more storage for your luggage?Although our train ride was smooth, the air-con was not working when we boarded and only kicked in while we were moving. It was 34 degrees outside and other coaches where cooler than ours. Toilet on board was smelly. The train guard, however, was a very friendly guy. Then you arrive at Paris Gare du Nord. Trash and litter on the tracks. Lifts not working. Toilets filthy. Imagine yourself transferring to the TGV to Southern France where you will stay for three weeks. Travelling with two children and three suitcases (which is on the light side when you're travelling with two adults and two small children for a three week holiday. No luggage carts, you need to wiggle your way through heaps of people and probably need a taxi and will be stuck in Paris traffic and risk missing your train if your connection is tight.All in all fun if you're on a  short leisure trip like us. But certainly not an alternative to flying.
TGV INOUI 🥇I read the reviews after booking.....nothing true! Perfect return trip from Paris. Everything on time, not a minute late.

Worried by the reviews I was fearful but between the return journey 5 minutes late in total. Courteous staff carriages and second class seats with nothing to complain about. Bar service working and messages also in Italian, what can I say a nice surprise in this sea of ​​terrible reviews. TGV Inoui 🔝

Travelled first class with family from Luxembourg to Paris Est on Friday, June 02, 2023. Had the privilege to be yelled at by a offensively impolite conductor! Boorishly, at the top of his voice! Third class experience in first class!
Wifi on the train, pitiful and uninteresting, is of absolutely no use. Paying for a service that doesn't work is pathetic

When everything goes well, nothing to say, but beware once a train gets cancelled for the 100th strike in Paris, be prepared to wait almost a year to get a refund...still waiting for mine and still not replying to my mails. Horrible after sales !
Wonderful and perfect trip. Always on schedule with explanations and safe travel.  Excellent service without a doubt.

Three hours sitting, on the ground in a big detour, In front of the latrines, an experience of heavy distress. One hundred and fifteen crowns spent, but for what purpose? Bathroom was overflowing by the time we boarded, not cleaned or emptied for the entire 3.5 hour ride.  A/C was not working the first 1.5 hours.  No attendant to verify seating, our train was filled with people in the wrong seats.   Just an overall poor experience.  Also, WIFI didn't work.

Worst train service ever. I had to take it for an year between Zurich and Paris and regretted every single time. They take so much advantage of the fact that they're a monopoly by delivering a terrible service at a stupidly high price. Starting from the price, the algorithm makes it so random that you never have any certainty of what you're going to pay, making the whole booking experience only anxiety-inducing. Sometimes it gets high in the evening and back lower the morning after. Speaking of predictability, sometimes the times of scheduled trains changes for no reason (I lost one on a Friday because that only Friday of the year it started 10 minutes earlier), sometimes trains are cancelled and you aren't notified of it even if you have a ticket. Inside, the train is always so full that there is no space for the luggage, the wifi works poorly and the trash bins are always full. The toilet is rarely clean. For a train that expensive, it's totally unacceptable. Only the even more incredibly expensive French highway and a monopolistic position keeps it in business.
The train is a turtle and an accumulator of delays. Milan Paris in 10 hours. Terrible service (complete with train changes).
Getting worse and worse. Trains rarely on time. Even the TGVs. Terrible customer service. Exorbitant prices. We make fun of customers.

I just took one of the new Thalys trains between Amsterdam and Paris, and I am horrified.With its popular bar coach, comfortable seats, and warm-coloured decoration, the Thalys used to provide a pleasant journey, almost a luxurious experience if one compared it with taking the plane. Not anymore. The bar coach has been reduced to half its original size and its not really a bar anymore. Rather, it looks now like the sad coffee corner of a budget company’s offices. I also wonder -- was it technically necessary to wall the windows on one side of the bar, or was this only done to add to its sadness?The comfortable seats are anything but comfortable. They are hard as a rock and my lower back, which although fragile was perfectly fine in the old trains, now starts aching after half an hour. I still have three hours to go. The footrest is gone so you don’t have that extra support anymore. To put it in few words, Ryanair’s seats are more comfortable than Thalys’. Another thing about the seats, this one about their appearance. When you sit down and look at the back of the seat in front of you, you can appreciate the finesse of the seam. It looks like a five-year-old did it. In fact, it looks so bad that I don’t know whether to laugh or to cry. Every seat is the same. Pleas, who did this? And why?As to the decoration, I used to love the soothing effect of the warm colours in the old trains. Those colours invited passengers to relax, they conveyed the message “enjoy your trip”. The new colours, on the other hand, with their violent contrast and rather boring (if not plainly ugly) tones, make me feel like I am on a dentist’s waiting room. I want my old Thalys back.

A very comfortable and hassle-free trip to Paris from Amsterdam. The newly designed cabins in Premium class are very clean and spacious. As a couple, we reserved the duo facing seats - seating at the window facing each other with a table in the center. It offered slightly more room compared to the side-by-side seating. The overhead storage was good for backpacks and small bags, but getting heavier carry-on luggage above is difficult - especially for seniors. I would recommend to be one of the first to board so that you can use the limited luggage racks as you enter the compartment. Service is very good, but the food is nothing to write home about (included with a premium class ticket). You save a few dollars by traveling Comfort class which has the same premium seating without the food. Access at Amsterdam Centraal is easy through gate 15A at the end of the station. If you enter through the back of the station, gate 15A is right there and will save time walking the entire length of the station. Even with the potential transportations strikes in Paris during April/May, our train was only delayed 10 minutes. I would recommend Thalys but be sure to check their website for updates about travel times and cancellations so you are not surprised when you get to the station.

TGV train INOUI Paris GDL - MILAN Porta Garibaldi, 4 June 2023. Two hours late. ALL toilets are unusable (clogged or closed). Train conductor nowhere to be found, Cost of first class tickets: 189 euros. Scandalous.

Disappointed by the recent experience I had with the SNCF. The problems encountered during my travels were numerous and seriously damaged my confidence in this railway company. The recurring delays have become a real source of frustration. What was announced as a simple 5 minute delay often turned into a wait of an hour or more. This imprecision in the information communicated creates considerable confusion and discomfort among travelers. The SNCF appears to have difficulty ensuring connections in the event of delays. I have experienced situations on several occasions where my train arrived late and I found myself with a missed connection. There was then no guarantee of having a seat on the other trains offered as replacements, passengers with "broken" connections not being given priority.  Unacceptable given the high price of tickets. The SNCF should also review its G30 guarantee and offer fairer and more adequate compensation in the event of delays and especially missed connections. Travelers deserve to be adequately compensated for the (increasingly numerous) inconveniences suffered and the consequences caused. On my last journey from Toulouse to Nantes with a connection in Bordeaux, I experienced an initial delay of 35 minutes in Bordeaux but this then led to a delay of 4 hours in Nantes due to the missed connection and the difficulty in finding a replacement train. As a result, I was entitled to a €7 voucher, which reinforces the feeling of contempt towards travelers and gives them the impression of not being taken into consideration. The SNCF also seems to lack an adequate reception service in certain stations.  Only two employees present to inform more than a hundred dissatisfied travelers. This situation is simply unacceptable. I strongly recommend that the SNCF review its practices and put in place measures to guarantee a reliable, punctual and respectful service.

Never before seen: the removal of armrests and other wonders! Yesterday my husband arrived at his destination 1 hour late. Today I also went on an ouigo which started 20 minutes late. Yesterday it was someone on the rail, we said. Today: “suspicious baggage”. But what is suspicious is this new way of low-cost, starting with the fact that it is not all about “low-cost”. 49 euros to go to Marseille?, okay. But more than €200 to get to Marseille or Cannes? No, I will not walk up the steps on the red carpet. Big surprise this time. Un cerveau a machiné un truc incroyable dans notre monde amoral ilibéral : on a retiré les accoudoirs pour mettre une rangée de plus dans chaque wagon ! Not only can you not recline your seat but you are stuck to others without this essential separation which separates you from the body of others and keeps you in a moderately comfortable position when it is not the scheduled bus you take daily. I paid the "extra" to carry normal luggage, that is to say where you put a toiletry bag, a change of underwear, two pairs of pants and a second pair of shoes or sneakers. But the microspace intended for normal luggage was already taken and no one was controlling this situation. I paid and put my suitcase anywhere I could, standing at each stop to make sure it wasn't considered "suspicious baggage". Having been born in a developing country I have never seen the removal of armrests, the minimum comfort of a medium and long distance service has been maintained despite the difficulties. What limit is there to the greed of groups who impose new ways of traveling, to pile up to make more profits? Date of experience: May 16, 2023

Resumen: Terrible company, terrible customer service, always on strike.They are likely to cancel your train at the last moment and leave you stranded - which is what happened to us, family of 6, with 4 young children.We had planned a trip to Paris and Disney for the children over the Easter break, getting the train from Barcelona to Paris. Unfortunately Renfe (the spanish rail company) no longer operate crossing into France (I can only image what they had to deal with, once over the border into the mess that is modern-day France).So we opted for the train with SNCF, thinking that it would be less hassle on the train, with 4 children, than getting a flight - terrible mistake.We were due to travel on Saturday April 29th - and had booked the tickets since Janauary.On Thursday April 27th at 8pm we received a text message just saying simply:"We inform you, your train is cancelled due to personnel issues"Nothing else. Then an email arrived some time later, stating that there was no train on our departure date, we had the option for a refund, or a change of date. Unfortunately, we opted for the change of date - to not disappoint the children by saying there was no Disney trip. A big mistake.So, we had to frantically call around, cancelling the hotel, the Disney tickets, and everything else that we booked - losing money on non-refundable things such as entry to the Eiffel tower, bus tours, etc.But we were happy as the big costs were Disney, and the hotel and both eventually agreed to changing the date to the weekend of May 1st, the date we decided to travel on, as it was a public holiday and the children would just miss one day of schoolSo, for the next month we just were kept thinking that at any time SNCF would again cancel, last minute like we had just experienced.Finally departure day came, and we headed to the station. Until then, we hadn't received any cancellation message, so we felt "it was a once off, let's go to the station". We arrived at the station and realised they had put one of our kids in a totally different carriage, (in the stations on Spanish side of the border, there are no SNCF representatives to be found - you can only get in contact via their helpline). So we just ignored the seat number and sat together.The train ride was on the low-end of acceptable, the trains are old, not modern, very warm, no air conditioning and minimal services. But, we were just happy to on our way. Then on the last 5 mins, entering into Paris, Gare de Lyon, we received the dreaded text:"Your (return) train is cancelled for personnel issues".As you can imagine, we flipped. We go to the station and then queued with all the other disgruntled passengers for 90 min to see an agent to see what our options were. No one had a clue about anything, as said before - completely useless customer service in Gare de Lyon and in the company as a whole.In the end, the agent told us that there was an alternative train leaving on the Monday at 09:38 (or train's departure was supposed to be at 14:58).She told us, that they were obliged to get us on the train, so to return on Monday at 08:30 to talk again and get us on the train. So, all weekend, that was the only thought on our mind, being stranded in Paris, we couldn't enjoy the trip.Then came Monday, waking up the family at 7am, to go to Gare de Lyon to try and escape the filthy mess that Paris has become. On arrival, the agent working informed us there was no space on this train at 9:38, that we would have to wait until Wednesday to depart (2 days later). We appealed to her to try something, here we were in the station, with 4 young children, suitcases, etc and waiting around for 2 days wasn't an option. She then went to get the station master, or whatever other silly title they give the manager. This was the most ignorant, rudest person I've every had the displeasure of dealing with. No sympathy or empathy at all, he was almost smiling as he informed us that "the law in France does not have to provide us with hotel or food cost compensation for the time we are stuck here due to the cancellation" (All other EU/civilised countries do this).He said we had only 2 options:1. Take a refund and try get a flightor2. Wait 2 days for the next train departure (if of course, this doesn't get cancelled as well).After lots of arguing, someone in the queue pointed out to him, that the train that was destined to go to Barcelona was still departing and going as far as the border town of Perpignan, it just wasn't crossing the border (for some silly reason that it needs 2 extra staff to cross the border, and it was these 2 that were on strike). The person recommended us to get to there, then to get a bus for the final part of the journey, which is what we did.So, if you're thinking of coming to Paris for the Olympics 24, then I'd advise not to - and if you do go, then avoid SNCF at all costs.

The four star rating is for the TGV train only and not SNCF.We rode the Train à Grande Vitesse-Lyria on March 7 from Gare de Lyon to Geneva. This was not our original plan. The tickets we had purchased in advance were for TGV-Lyria 9269 to Lausanne. But with March 7, being the start of the latest round of social unrest in France that train was cancelled and I had to scramble to find another train that was running to Switzerland. That led us to TGV-Lyria 9765 (Gare de Lyon – Geneva). This sucked as the tickets from Paris to Lausanne (purchased well in advance) were €59 each and when I had to reschedule the cost jumped to €107 each. Seems that SNCF would honor the original price as it was not my choice to change trains but was forced by SNCF cancellation of the original train. We boarded and departed Gare de Lyon on time and arrived in Geneva on-time. A very smooth and fast trip to Geneva in just over 3 hours. By car it would take 5 ½ hours.Dealing with SNCF is a pain when the trains are cancelled, but doing it online was not that hard. Overall the trip was a very pleasant ride and the added benefit of traveling in 1st class allowed us to utilize the Le Salon Grand Voyageur prior to departure.

trip which went well, train on time, staff who come to collect any waste in the aisle however ridiculously small toilets, compared to those of the eurostar are a palace!

Commuti g with It from Zurich to Basel, After a business eventi in Zurich was a Nightmare.No seats in the normale wagons only in the small Bar area, sitting like a parrot for One hour

I had a train booked from Stuttgart to Paris on April 17, 2023 which was scheduled to leave at 9:11am. I splurged for First Class seats as my wife and I had heavy suitcases.  We learned on the way to Stuttgart that the train was cancelled. When we arrived at Stuttgart HBF, we went immediately to the information desk for the train company. We were coldly told we had to get on another train changing in Mannheim that was leaving in less than 10 minutes and we would grab another train in Mannheim to get to Paris. We were told there were no seats available on either train and we would have to sit on the floor or wherever we could find a place to sit on either train. We asked if we could get a seat on a later train but were coldly told NO. We then ran to catch the train to Mannheim. We fortunately entered at the door next to the bar car so we sat there for the approximately 40 min ride. The waiter said we had to order something. We said we were only sitting there because our train was cancelled and we had no seats and were told to sit wherever we would on this train.  Too bad said the waiter, you have to order something-so we ordered waters. We arrived at Mannheim and got on the train to Paris where we sat on the floor in the baggage compartment with other passengers that had been on our original train for the next 3 hours.  I have since filed a claim on the SNCF TGV website to try to get some refund considering I paid for First Class tickets and sat on the floor for the duration of the trip.  The website makes it hard to do so. Choosing reasons such as "cancellation" or "delay" causes the website to freeze. I was able to get a complaint in under "fares" considering i paid for a much higher fare. I got a confirmation email that says I can check on the status of my claim with a claim number, but there does not appear to be anyway to do it-as the link simply takes you to the home page.  I expect I will never receive any form of reimbursement for the experience. I recognize that I was able to get to Paris, but I wonder why I still need to pay for a First Class Ticket when I clearly did not ride First Class and the train was not cancelled for any unforeseeable reason (weather etc).   Keep this all in mind when you decide to book a train with these folks.

A first class TGV fare used to mean food service, functioning bathrooms, clean cars, and well-maintained coaches.  Unfortunately, the only good part of TGV that remains today is the speed.  Food service is no longer part of a first class fare, and the trains are simply not maintained.  On today's trip from Strasbourg to Lilles, I found no food service and fewer items for sale in the club car than I would expect in a half-empty vending machine, none of which were appetizing.  A bag of crisps is not a substitute for breakfast.  Half of the cars' bathrooms do not function, and I had to go 5 cars down the train to find any water to wash my hands.  Finally, there  is no headrest on my "first class" seat - that's broken and tossed into the luggage space above.First class train travel?  Hardly.  Eurostar may be the only remaining example of acceptable train travel in the area.  Outside of London-based trains, I think I'll just take a plane.
The worst train service I have ever seen in the world.Easily get cancelled, but difficult to ask for a refund.

I bought tickets through Trainline with the provider being OUIGO. OUIGO’s service commitment is that tickets will be delivered 4 days in advanced. They sent me a confirmation email but when I tried to access the tickets on their website the confirmation code came up saying it was invalid and I got an error message for two days. I ended up buying a new set of tickets at the train station because the train was boarding and they hadn’t arrived. When I contacted OUIGO they said they delivered them 14 minutes before the train left. FOURTEEN MINUTES! After two days of getting an error message on their website. Who would trust that? Who would put faith in the fact that their tickets would arrive. They refused to give me a refund or help me in any way. Customer service means you try to assist your customer when you realized your company messed up and didn’t deliver a product the way you promised. They either don’t understand that concept or just refuse accountability. When I contacted Trainline they agreed that it was all OUIGO’s fault. Oh and OUIGO doesn’t have a customer service number or email on their confirmation emails so the only way you can contact them is to go through their social media which is weird and sketchy at best.WARNING DO NOT BUY TICKETS THROUGH OUIGO!

They gave us a free train for the next day, losing a paid hotel night, which seemed unacceptable to us, if it wasn't because we had the option of taking a flixbus, we would be left without a trip. They should offer the possibility of relocating passengers to other trains instead of leaving 0 options, I understand that it is an exceptional strike situation in France, but the price of the ticket is excessively clear (just the one way to Carcassonne from Barcelona has cost more than 100 euros per person), with that price I expect exquisite service and treatment. It doesn't matter to me that they give me a refund option if I have the hotel and everything has already been paid for.

We are a family with two children aged 2 and 8 years old, we went by train TGV Milan Paris, the train makes many stops, (it seems like a regional one) the bar was closed from Turin to Modane, it also caused a delay of 40 minutes or more. Not very recommended for those traveling with children and for those who don't have much patience

The SNCF has been making fun of users for years with constantly disrupted and overpriced trains. Reimbursements and services at the station or online are worthy of a Chevalier and Laspales sketch. And our taxes help maintain this charade.

It's all in the titles. Trains either late or canceled. Incredible!! Being so incapable is unheard of! I don't understand why such a bad society can continue to operate like this! It's not disappointing, it's disastrous. They never mind if we're late or stuck somewhere.
Fast and convenient. On time, comfortable, stations at great locations. Better than flying or driving.

Airport to Disneyland Paris. Worth getting a first class ticket! Comfy seats and quiet carriage. Unfortunately faced some delays due to signal issues. This was only announced over the tannoid in French not English. Overall easy enough way to get to Disney.
Disastrous company. They canceled my train due to a strike 48 hours before and they did not give me the option of another train at another time, or another means of transportation.

On the 12th of March 2023 at approximately 7:25 pm, we embarked on a journey with Thalys, the high-speed train service, from Paris to Amsterdam. During the course of the journey, a regrettable incident occurred wherein our backpack, which was of blue The North Face brand, was stolen/robbed, with trickery/physical interactions having taken place.Upon careful recollection, it appears that the incident must have taken place at the Schipol stop at around 10:30 pm. We were seated in coach 12 when a person approached and dropped a key. We observed the individual during the exchange, and it was at this time that an accomplice of theirs removed the backpack from the top drawer, which was where we had placed our luggage.The backpack, which was located in the top drawer above our seats, contained valuables worth approximately 3500 EURO. We must stress that the luggage was never left alone at any point during the journey, and we had taken utmost care to ensure its security.We attempted to seek the assistance of service personnel at the station in question; however, none were available. We also made contact with Thalys to report the incident, but to our dismay, our efforts were met with no response. The phonelines were dysfunctional, and the chatbot was insufficient, thereby adding to our distress and sense of helplessness.It is with great disappointment that we must conclude our highly unsatisfactory experience with Thalys, and we have no choice but to file a complaint. We urge caution and recommend against traveling first-class with Thalys, as our experience has demonstrated that the service may be unsafe and provides easy entry to criminals on their trains outside of France.We kindly request that our complaint be addressed with utmost urgency, and we would appreciate prompt redressal of our grievances. Our reference number for the incident in question is TSBNET. We trust that Thalys will take swift and effective action to prevent such incidents from occurring in the future.

The most incompetent company in the world with employees who only think about striking and who don't care about the travelers they leave in trouble. TGV booked 4 months before and canceled the day before our departure. The same goes for the return for our stay with children. And I'm not talking about the superior blow due to the solutions found urgently. In short, avoid the SNCF at all costs, the least reliable service in France.
No choice. Bad site. In short, a site of civil servants who make fun of their clients. We are cash cows, not customers. To be privatized asap

The experience of rushing through the countryside with 300 kilometres an hour is fantastic. The delays and boarding experience are not. Rail traffic on this route is clearly very congested. Creating knock-on effects if things are not going according to schedule. Departing from Rotterdam was smooth, departing from Brussels Gare du Midi is a nightmare, with the train information not being accurate (numbers of the coaching switching all the time). As with every high speed train, luggage space is insufficient. If you are a family and are travelling with luggage (say suitcases and a pram, goo luck with finding space. On longer distances I would still rather take the plane.

We were lucky enough to travel 1st class (repatriation), it was very quiet and comfortable. The bar car on the other hand: a croque-monsieur served cold (well, so it's a ham and cheese toastie, right???), 3 items missing from the order... in short! And obviously, very expensive but we know that, for food that remains chemical and industrial, at the same time we don't expect anything else in a TGV...

I once saw a report that TGV beats the ICE by far. Especially compared to 1st class. But now my opinion. Absolute nonsense, the TGV Mannheim to Saarbrücken was the worst train on my tour to Munich and back. The arrival alone was a disaster: entry area A for reserved seats on the train didn't work. We fought our way to A so that we could get on a train that was almost fully booked without any stress. No, the train continues two sections. Walk 100 meters with a bunch of wild passengers with luggage to reach the train, which was almost 12 minutes late. These delays are normal at DB, so they say. But I didn't have that experience. On my tour, all trips with ICE (1st CLASS) were TIP TOP and Just in Time. After the train reached the kuddel muddel, I immediately noticed the narrow corridors (staircase first floor). Larger suitcases are difficult to lift, so small suitcases won't fit on the shelves. My suitcase fit on every ICE/RE/RB. Ok, at the beginning of a car there are places to put suitcases, but on a busy route heading quickly towards Paris, these 10 to 12 places to put things are far from enough. Ok, my little suitcase under the seat went. But with big problems storing my feet. My seat adjustment was defective. My back, which is plagued with neck and intervertebral discs, complained bitterly. In particular, I sat with my butt on the seams of the upholstery. Absolutely uncomfortable! If some people think that I could simply change seats, that's only partly true, because the train was unfortunately full. I wasn't able to select my reservation exactly as I could with the ICE. I had to come to terms with the space that was allocated when I made the reservation. Unfortunately, the reservation notices were broken, so I had to assert my claim before starting my trip, first with a mother with a child. I find that impossible for 1st class. So when it comes to TGV compared to ICE, the ICE is way ahead. From the feeling, the train we used has reached its operating time. The train was very bumpy, rickety and smelly. No infotainment on board, so you had to trust the German-French gibberish of the train driver. But what doesn't work at all are the doors; every time someone used them, it sounded like a soda can being opened right next to your ear. Very uncomfortable if you at least try to doze a little when your back is bothering you.

The ride was smooth, not bumpy ,and very fast. The wifi is great, restrooms were clean and organized,everything was great. However the bar didn’t have large varieties. Also for clients upstairs, it’s quite hard for them to transport their luggage around, especially moving them from downstairs to upstairs or upstairs to downstairs. Moreover, the trip was pleasant, and I would recommend it.

I think the TGV is absolutely overrated. Fantastic service for first class is advertised, English-speaking staff, a good on-board kitchen. However, I met staff who didn't speak English. We drove from Barcelona to Paris, a 7-hour journey. It's normal to get hungry after a while. But the bistro is far too expensive. I think a small menu for around €15 is unreasonable. Compared to other trains, I paid a lot for a reservation and received the same or much better service elsewhere. By service I mean, as is the case in other countries and even Germany, that the service takes care of the needs of the passengers. This was not the case here. Instead, staff came through the wagon every 10 minutes with a garbage bag.

Unfortunately, the high expectations of using the big-name TGV simply disappointed me. I had to use the train with a friend on an Interrail trip, as unfortunately there is no way around France when traveling to Spain. The expensive surcharge is not justified. There wasn't even a meal or drink for such an expensive price. I would recommend every traveler to avoid using the TGV if they can. The performance here in first classes can be compared with a normal regional train. Furthermore, the expensive staff isn't even able to speak reasonable English, which doesn't make things any easier.
Luggage space can not hold enough baggage of train passengers. Seats are uncomfortable. Good luck finding platform in Gare Montparnasse.

I am very disappointed, I never had a problem until yesterday!! There are no controllers on the platforms of small stations, this is unacceptable. There is very little time between two trains so when we have to change stations it's too tight given that I missed my train because of a train that was late! The controllers don't care even depending on your situation. I am very surprised and very disappointed.  It's scandalous. You have to communicate between trains when some are late.

absolutely terrible ride. Almost two hours late (100 minutes!!!!!), constant technical problems, above-average WiFi (compared to other public WiFi), sometimes runs almost at walking pace, terrible service for such a price!

There is no direct train to Cologne. Transfer in Brussels. Filthy first class, 4 hours to get to Brussels. I lost connection. Punctually the German ICE left at 16:22, clean, silent, fast. TGV should be TBV!

Our first experience of the TGV was our trip in summer from Paris to Milan. We had travelled from Gare du Nord from Gare de Lyon using the RER and when we arrived it wasn’t really clear which platform our train departed from. Eventually the gate opened and there was a bit of a scrum to get onto the train. Make sure that you get onto the correct part of the train, part of it disappears off somewhere else in Southern France. We had prebooked 4 seats with a table but unfortunately our allocated seats were in what seemed to be shabbiest carriage on the train. When I wandered through to the café bar the other carriages looked more modern. Our seats were also next to the exit to the toilets which already smelled of ammonia when we got onto the train. To compound that the electronic doors were not working so every time someone came through they either didn’t know how to open the door or forgot to close it as they went through. Then when it wasn’t closed we could smell the toilets through the open door. That gets a bit frustrating after 7 hours, especially when even the staff didn’t try and do anything about it.We had quite a delay at the French/Italian border when the Italian police boarded and started checking passports. When we travelled back using the Frecciarossa we didn’t have the same checks. We also had the farcical situation of being forced to put masks on once we reached the border, this is after having been in the carriage with the same people for 4 hours already so the masks seemed a bit pointless. Still rules are rules and the train staff do wander up and down reminding people to put a mask but others were allowed to sit there without them on throughout the remainder of the journey. The scenery towards the border and into the northern part of Italy is well worth waking up for even if the rest isn’t particularly scenic. We arrived into Milano Porta-Garibaldi (the Frecciarossa goes all the way to the more convenient Centrale) later than scheduled and then struggled to find a taxi, I think it was because we left via a side entrance rather than the main station exit. As we were late I was invited to claim compensation via the SNCF app. There was an option to claim it in cash which then inexplicably disappeared so I thought I was settling for a journey credit. I was told by a livechat assistant on the app that I could change it but my messages went unanswered until late November (I started the claim in mid-August) when I was told I could have a bank transfer and if I provided my details it would take 20-30 days! I sent my details and expected the payment by Christmas. When I didn’t receive it after more than 30 days I chased it and was told there had been an issue so the payment would be sent again and would take 20-30 days again. It seems that they are determined to hold on to my money for as long as possible.If, like us, you are travelling from Paris to Milan I would definitely suggest that Frecciarossa rather than the TGV is the better option.

January 2023, bitterly cold, cold air comes out of the vents, the windows are full of drafts. Really tight seating. Excellent cleanliness, punctuality too but really too cold and too narrow. The red arrow is more comfortable and warmer. Know this

Just to say that in the history of incompetent and disrespectful staff I have rarely seen better!!! There are many agents and if you have a problem, for example like me, getting the device to read a simple QR Code on your phone, don't wait for someone to offer you help!!!! They are there in front of you, repeating the obvious, namely presenting the phone for the scan (thank you really for the added value of human presence compared to the simple device!) in an increasingly friendly tone of course and what's more afterwards they comment on your passage by saying: "I've told him 3 times! ". We're not even addressing you, no we're leaving a very appreciable and public comment, that's always a pleasure, rather than trying to help you when you're struggling!!! This is what I increasingly tend to call “French service”!!! I don't want to fall into generalities but by going abroad regularly the observation is clear and cruel for us! But the OUIGO staff still wins the prize in this area!!! For me it was the last time in any case because there is no need to mention that this is not the first time that I have faced disrespect from the staff! Until then I hadn't said anything but now it's one time too many. OUIGO is a big NO!!!!!!!!!!
Unprofessional.. marketing online some good prices when you try to book they come up drastically.. the workers are really bad and aggressive..

Once again, the TGV train is late: more than 90 minutes!! I’ve lost my next connection, will arrive home over 1 am and can only make it home paying a taxi or uber. Thanks TGV, you never miss a chance to disappoint your customers.

On December 29, we took TGV 6608, which leaves Lyon la Pardieu and arrives at Paris Gare de Lyon, at Creusot TGV station at 8:46 a.m. We installed our 2 suitcases in the compartments reserved for this purpose upstairs because there was no more room downstairs. The train started while we were waiting in the toilet next door. we got our seats and upon arrival at Lyon station, we had the unpleasant surprise of finding that one of our suitcases had disappeared. Arriving at the hotel near the station we discovered that the other suitcase had been forced and our tablets had been stolen. This theft occurred during the journey, of course the SNCF declines all responsibility since there is a PAID baggage support system.

The seats!!! But who is the fool who designed these horrors?!! Always more expensive for always less comfort, the ouigo are more comfortable than the new inoui it's a shame, impossible to rest, sleep let's not even talk about it, less space, inclination is as ergonomic as possible, padding as hard as a bench, ultra aggressive lighting with the addition of individual lighting whose button is... against the passenger inside the armrest, so you turn it on without intention when you move (i.e. a lot seen the discomfort of these seats to try to relieve a bruised back or buttocks), removal of the nets to place some items on them. Add to this the reduction in luggage racks, and try the experience on a busy day, it is in your interest to have some knowledge of climbing to pass over the suitcases in the corridor. Conclusion: nothing is going well, you arrive at your destination in pain everywhere and with raw nerves. The line is becoming very thin between the ouigo cattle truck with the smell of piss and the inoui with its deplorable comfort. The plague or cholera but whatever happens a m**** experience and a very light wallet. Between the strikes, the delays, the yield management on prices, the lousy app and now this: the only thing where the SNCF excels is in the art of taking people for big Cs.

THALYS train from Paris to Amsterdam , staff is very helpful and professional, very clean, I love riding in trains and THALYS provides a great experience every time, the breakfast was great, a lot of food and they came back to see if I wanted more. People say it’s expensive but I think it’s worth the money, the train is fast , food is good, staff is great. All together it adds value to my experience

The best staff..I was on a TGV train from Paris to Milan with my family. I placed my laptop bag underneath my seat and forgot to retrieve it. We were already in a different station when I remembered. I ran back to Porta Garibaldi but the train already went back to the depot. I ran to the TGV office and they informed me that the person who checks the train at the depot will not be in for the next hour. If ever they find the bag in the train, they will not be able to return it to me until the next day because the depot is inaccessible to the public and I had to wait for the train to come back to the station. I had another train to catch to Florenze in 2 hours. I was already crying because it was my work laptop.I roamed around the station for an hour while waiting for news. I was already hopeless, devastated, extremely worried. I went back to the TGV office and they told me that they found it! What’s more, the guy who found it was willing to drive to the station to give it to me!! When the guy arrived, I thanked all of them for helping me, gave them a tip for their trouble, and ran outside to catch an uber to Milano Centrale.Alas, my troubles were far from over. I couldn’t find the uber. Thankfully, the guy who returned my bag saw mestruggling. He offered to give me a ride to Milano Centrale and I gladly agreed. I gave him money for the fare and caught my train to Florence.I am in disbelief, first, for my stupidity and second, for the seemingly miraculous help I received from the universe. Any second of delay or a different TGV personnel on duty and I would not have been reunited with my bag. Thank you TGV! Thank you Lord. Thank you to the kidness of strangers 🤍🤍🤍

Get to the wrong train station, miss your train by the time you get to the right station?Forget about exchanging tickets or getting a refund. You're better off flying. Do yourself the favor and fly. - Still fighting to get a refund for a service unused, would've saved myself the nightmare had we just flown.

Wifi = 0Service = 0Friendliness of the controllers = 0Train on time = 0Paris -> Nantes = €120The SNCF service for the price is shameful, not a train goes well, wifi is impossible, nothing is going well... getting worse and worse!
A shame these strikes in the middle of Christmas.... Unreliable company, strikes at least 4 times a year and regular increases to make up for these strike movements....

In France, SNCF strikers have the right to cancel your expensive train trips!! Christmas is coming? Well, count on SNCF employees to spoil your end-of-year celebrations by preventing you from joining your families and friends! This country is incredible! The Atlantic TGVs are still the most affected in addition to their dilapidation and filthy seats! As for the cramped toilets (be small and skinny to get in and out!!) often out of order: clogged, no water, no soap, no paper... and very dirty, smelling bad because they were poorly cleaned. Welcome to France!

Standing an entire trip from Paris to Milan. The servicemen passed by and ignored passengers. Our two booked seats were taken and the passengers refused to get up, the servicemen did not help with this. Tickets were very expensive. There were not enough seats for the people so a seat is not guaranteed even if prebooked, please save yourself the trouble and find another service.

It can be improved, avoiding continuous delays and making the services work, you cannot travel 7 hours on the train without a bar or refreshment, things that you pay for in the ticket, I buy this ticket because I have these services, I would have chosen something else. Broken seat, total disservice

On December 17 I should have made a Marseille-Paris trip on the TGV OUIGO, after having taken my ticket and seeing that potentially, like every year, the SNCF will strike, I wanted to cancel the latter (a few days later) (like possibly at TGV INOUÏ for example). Except NO, refund impossible and cancellation either, only an exchange (well why didn't you think I took the TGV all the time you) so currently I was able to cancel my TER that I had before this TGV but the OUIGO I can't I have to wait for a person to buy the seat to have the extraordinary right to have a voucher for 80% of the total value of my ticket. But lol (how to steal money from people 💁🏼‍♀️). I am willing that there is the notion of low cost at OUIGO but at a given moment if we are looking to take the cheapest trains, we are also looking to be reimbursed when we cancel like at INOUI and TER. On top of that it's their fault for going on strike all the time, there's no PTN train running every time it's things like (adhesion to the rails, too much wind, too much rain, too much sun eh ftg) not able to work properly always a problem. That’s good!

Booked in October 2022 first class, SNCF INOUI with departure Paris G. du Nord 12.47 and expected arrival Milan Porta Garibaldi 19.49. Total price 2 adults plus a 4 year old child, 330 euros (130x2+70). Technical fault at the first stop but we set off again and a new prolonged stop for attempted repairs in Modane. For these reasons I arrive in Milan at 8.45pm. The real reason for the poor rating is the poor quality of the first class carriages (I would say 70s without cleaning, with the numbering of seats incomprehensible) and above all, right from the start, the Chiusa bar carriage, which for a journey of almost 7 hours (in the end almost 8) is INOUI (in French unheard of, incredible). Long live Trenitalia!!!

Delay due to a poor display of the cars, on the speakers in the wagon a person seems to be drunk making us hear an incomprehensible message, 3 times. So inversion of passengers on two adjacent TGVs, they from the front must go to the rear, which takes 20 minutes. A little later I received an SMS saying that the TGV delay was due to the breakdown of another train on a track.... Take responsibility for your mistakes and stop taking travelers for idiots. When you don't strike, you are in bad faith, there is always a pretext. Tired of depending on the SNCF, I hope for a call for tenders to have better service providers

Zurich - Paris I was thinking: come on, let's go by train, only 4 and a half hours... We had to change the ticket because they canceled the train we were supposed to take, due to the strike. So €52 more per person ok than the price already paid then we had to change in Basel. While in Basel we were on the platform waiting they told us to change tickets... then go to the other side of the station... we thought come on at least everything will be fine on the way back. No, the road back didn't go well either... strike over, but thirty minutes late then they only warned at the last moment that we had to change in Basel... but at the start they didn't say anything... the train had to be direct... and go from one part of the Basel station to the whole other part... at least the Swiss train conductor ❤️ didn't cause any problems because we had tickets for the other train... never again with the TGV

Never think about buying tickets with the SNCF TGV company, they have canceled our train on 12/4/2022 due to a strike and they refuse to refund the money!!! I have lost a hotel night, and they are not responsible for anything
OUIGO, the new concept from the SNCF to make you travel in cattle wagons...I didn't dare go to the toilet...

We used the TGV and departed from  Strasbourg and arrived at Marne La Vallee on a first class fare. We found the Railjet Austrian train much better. They serve meals at your table (notTGV) and overall the trains were in much better condition.As far as space and comfort quite similar.Storage for large suitcases is limited and there should be better facilities for luggage and getting luggage off the train.

You can't call this food first class service: a bland pretzel roll (not really fresh) and applesauce...the drinks are limited...2 bottles of champagne for the entire (fully booked) compartment! I recommend taking a picnic with you at Sprüngli in ZH for half the price and skipping the gastro service...it's cheaper and tastes better!

If I could give a zero, it doesn't deserve a star... Reliability of customer service 0Cleanliness of the wagons 0Communication 0Customer service misled me, they are thieves and crooks!!! Incompetent people hiding behind their screens, it's impossible to reach them by phone. Be careful even if it says "exchangeable under conditions" that's not true, they're liars, they're taking your money. If you ever wish to cancel your trip at first they tell you we are studying your file a confirmation by email will be sent to you. Once the date of the trip has passed they tell you that your ticket has not been resold so we can do nothing for you. If I had been warned before I would have I would have changed plans and taken this train. In addition if you are late by more than 30 minutes thanks to them you missed your connection no compassion is given. We really take customers for cash cows!!

Monday, Nov 21, 2022, I took train No. 9820 1st class to St Pierre des Corps, so far so good, quiet journey, my descent is announced for Massy... When collecting my suitcase in the location provided for this purpose, NO MORE SUITCASE, a passenger had the "bad taste" to move my suitcase to put his own. My suitcase was moved to the next carriage. Lack of civility on the part of this person, in addition in 1st class.Bravo France.Being used to traveling in Quebec I can tell you that respect there is favorable +++.Fortunately my traveling neighbor was very obliging and assisted me in this action.I thank him very sincerely for his services.Micheline Robineau 37300

The service around the TGVs is definitely getting worse and worse. After the catastrophic SNCF website, we are being given the new double-decker cars in the South East. The affair turns into a nightmare: highly uncomfortable seats (guaranteed back pain), toilets out of order (this evening there are only three working for our entire train...), unfriendly controllers....Long live the SNCF!!!!

I made a quick return trip from Strasbourg to Paris from November 18 to 20 with the TGV and a ticket purchased via OuiGo. I was lucky enough to grab my place for €19, or €38 for the round trip. It's exceptional value for money since it didn't even fill up half my tank of gas. The TGV left on time, arrived on time on every trip and that's all I wanted. Everything else doesn't matter. Well done SNCF because the commitment has been kept so if you offer other operations at a reduced rate I will be the first to take it.

TGV have been running in France for many years now and have yet to experience them until now.I was travelling from Paris to Frankfurt and they run services from Paris to various different cities in Germany. I purchased my ticket in advance and it was 10 Euros extra to purchase a ticket in First Class so as this was a special occasion and I was going to be on the train for 4 hours I took advantage of this.The TGV I travelled on was from Gare De L'Est and was a double decker train. I showed my ticket at the gate and it was easy to find my carriage and get on board. We left on time and once we left the city the train picked up speed and for quite some time was going at over 300 kph on the high speed line.Once we came off this line it was a bit slower but still very good. We ended up arriving in Frankfurt 10 minutes late but this was due to engineering works near Mannheim.A very pleasurable experience.Au revoir!

I ordered tickets on the SNCF connect site yesterday, it's pitiful, very unclear, to get an explanation you have to go through the robot which runs in a loop for 10 minutes before giving a completely useless telephone number since we end up with a robot which sends us back to the site. It's really bad

It had been a long time since I had taken the train, and I must admit that I was stunned by the filth and dilapidation inside and out of these superb machines, at least they were at the beginning... The tickets are prohibitive, and quickly make you want to forget about ecology when you get back into your car, and then at that price you still expect a vehicle as clean as a plane for example, but no, it's clearly very very dirty, marks on the seats, on the ceiling, accessories that don't work (USB sockets and others) and I'm not talking about the wifi, which in my opinion has never been turned on. Where has the SNCF prestige gone...??!, is it due, as in many companies, a question solely of profitability where we transport livestock? My next trip will be by car or plane, cheaper, cleaner even if it remains less clean for the planet. I am willing to make financial efforts for ecology, but the service provider must do so too.

We landed at Charles de Gaulle Terminal 2, and it was a bit of a walk to the TGV terminal. We queued at the ticket office for tickets. You can probably get tickets from the machines but we  were unfamiliar with the whole thing. It was a slow queue! When we got the tickets I asked the lady what was the destination of the train and she said there was a number on the ticket and there would be a number on the train. We came out of the office. The entrance to the platforms is on the right, we couldn’t see where it was. When we did go through I asked the ticket checker what platform the train was on. He just kept saying ‘Allez, allez’ which I know means ‘Go’. We ran down to the platforms and a train was coming in. We couldn’t see any number on it or on the screen or on the ticket. I asked a passenger getting on if it was going to Marne le Vallee ( the Disney stop) and she said it was.It’s only about a twenty minute trip, we had to stand up. People taking the train further had booked seats. I found the whole thing quite stressful. At Marne le Vallee we walked the few minutes to the Rer station to take us the one stop to our hotel at Val d’europe . When retiring to Charles de Gaulle we were coming from Paris city so we took the RER there rather than the TGV.

Incompetent OUIGO staff who don't care about travelers. On the platform, 2 trains are waiting, one of which is leaving very soon, but no, we let the passengers of the 2nd train, which leaves later, pass without worrying about anything. As a result, we miss our train even though we are in the queue on time. You don't even deserve to receive the minimum wage given your commitment to your work.

Took these trains from Paris to Arles [with one change] and Nimes to Paris. The Arles leg was in what I would call second class; the Nimes’ leg, first class. Neither class had any service, lunches or bought food breaking out on both trips. Both were rather full, the French fully embracing the ‘go slow’ approach to travel. Luggage storage might mean it is not necessarily close to you. For a bit more time you save a good deal of money and can enjoy the countryside.

We absolutely love train travel in france mostly on time, good value and incredibly fast, we love the easy check-in, and the luggage allowance is awesome, we had two big bags each and a carry-on, no problems, storage is a premium, advise to get there early. The trip was smooth and the seating, (first class) is comfoartable.

The TGV maintenance worker smells very bad! He passed by me twice, it's an infection, I want to vomit. This poor man may not be able to wash himself, but the SNCF should provide him with a shower. For your information, I am on the TGV Inoui 8707 between Paris and Rennes (departure from Montparnasse station at 8:56 a.m.). Fortunately I'm going back by car, this TGV is horrible :(

We expected a lot from the TGV since it is a modern train. Unfortunately, the carriages are really small, with hardly any space for larger suitcases and narrow aisles. It's best to travel with hand luggage only (small backpack or handbag). This can be stored directly above the seat. So Deutsche Bahn and ÖBB are more comfortable.

I wish I could leave less than one star. They cancelled both of my trains on two consecutive weekends from Brussels to Paris. One time they cancelled hours before departure and the other the day before. When trying to get my money back or change the booking, the only option is to call them. No one answers I have tried several times and the longest I have waited is 34 min with no reply. They take your money, then cancel your train for some made up reasons. And then make it impossible to contact them, so that you can not get your money back. They are basically a scam. Would never recommend no matter how conveniently fast they might be. I am talking here about the TGV Inoui. The seats are C-shaped, so you spend the journey hunched over, your neck craned forward. It's more expensive than ouigos for less comfort and less space. And the application is just as uncomfortable.

I never miss a chance to use the TGV in our frequent trips to France.It defines the what we call Bullet Trains.Our most recent trip was Paris Lyon in October 2022. We left Paris about 6:30 AM and arrived on time in 1 hour and 56 minutes, a distance of 243 miles. The trains run up to 186 miles per hour or higher in more recent versions. The ride is smooth and quiet. Acceleration is smooth and fast as is slowing for arrival.The ride is quiet and comfortable. The timing on our last trip allowed us to spend a long day in Lyon and return to Paris and go out that night. This is a trip we’ve made many times on other trips. We watched on another recent trip as they rolled up a second 10 car TGV Duplex set one morning set that linked to a similar unit already in the station for the early morning run to Paris. It was filled with as I recall just under 2,000 passengers on the train. Not on the roads, not in traffic James, reliably on time. We’ve had similar experiences in our travel in France and beyond where the German High Speed Rail offers a similar experience and convenience. Is it practical? More than that. You go city center to city center which is ideal for doing business or for most other purposes. Good public transit and the usual options make it easy to get around once you’re there. A friend who lived in Metz was faced for a time with the prospect his tech company would have to move to Paris for multiple reasons and him with it A home town guy, he helped push to speed up the Metz link to the TGV which let him keep his company loyal and he could be at the Paris Office in just over two hours, put in a full day and arrive home at a decent hour. At one time I commuted between NYC and Washington. I drove, flew, and took the train. Both flying and the train were competitive. You could walk on the Eastern Shuttle and pay on board. Trains were a little more involved in terms of location and worked well, not as fast. Today. It’s vastly superior although it’s not much faster. Essential security in today’s situation makes the train competitive in speed and it dominates the airlines in the essential Northeast Corridor. It is not yet up to TGV standards and its profits are siphoned off to pay for other rail service, valuable but not profitable. Investment in a broader rail system would more effectively tie the regions together with an economic impact. The TGV has enhanced the value and importance of regional capitals rather than diminish them.

The quickest and safest way to get to Marseille with a wide choice of timetables is without reservation the TGV. There is a TGV every hour from Gare de Lyon and some departures from Roissy airport and the journey takes between 3h10 and 3h20 thanks to the direct line to Marseille which does not pass through Lyon. Prices depend on the period and time between 50 and 120 euros in second class, first class being on average 15 to 20% more expensive. So I took a first class ticket from Paris to Marseille for 80 euros and with prior choice of seats. The train is long and it is recommended to arrive well before the timetable to have time to find your seat. Reclining and comfortable armchairs with removable shelves, electrical and USB sockets. Wifi is available on the train. At high speed, only the rapid scrolling of the landscape gives you the impression of going fast. In the wagon it is quite silent unless there are children... . At the entrance to each double-decker carriage, you have places for luggage but these are often insufficient, hence the benefit of arriving early if you have suitcases. Each train has its own snack car with drinks and snacks service. The setting is really pleasant with panoramic windows that let you admire the landscape. The punctuality of the SNCF when I take the train has not yet been faulted.

Since November 2020, my wife has had to use the TGV three times between Agen and Paris. Now, this is a service that it is difficult to find fault with. I runs on time. Is fast, comfortable and reasonably priced.However, during the Covid emergency it is a nightmare. The most recent journey in February of this year was the worst so far.My wife's journey continues from Paris to the UK via Eurostar. Very clean and one passenger to each group of four seats. Social distancing very well managed.The stations at Paris and Agen are well marked with signs reminding you to wear a mask and to keep your distance. On the train that all goes out of the window. The train arrived with three people travelling by the entrance doors. Two were sitting on the stairs to the upper deck.In the coach every seat was taken. So, for three hours, people were packed together with no regard for social distancing. For a company that is Government owned, that is not a good thing. No wonder France currently has a very high rate of infection.Something needs to be done about it.

For years it has been a pain to have to deal with this unfriendly company. Don't warn of delays... 1 hour anyway, don't reimburse for journeys, lousy telephone service try to get someone to help you good luck, the opening hours are a joke, and so on, such incompetence is tiring. On the other hand, there are a lot of people when it comes to imposing fines. I really hope that there will be more talk about the privatization of railway companies. The customer deserves better treatment, and better prices for public transport! This service is simply a shame.

From beginning to end this was a smooth experience. The only thing I would say is that they could have improved their covid measures when going through the check point as there were often crowds of people trying to get through. All in all I would definitely recommend.

22.12.2020 Paris-Milan. Without any warning, as soon as we got off the train on the platform at Garibaldi station, 30 policemen attacked us, surrounding us and shouting customs control (in Milan?). I soon found myself crushed, between the train and a police line, by other passengers who were scared because we didn't understand what they were doing. They ask us for documents which they scan with a mobile phone and don't give any details of what they are doing and then they push you to leave one by one. I don't expect a red carpet on arrival but a warning from TGV about this operation would have been appropriate. The check could have been carried out easily while we were on the train by asking us to stay seated for an extra minute and not as if we were incarcerated. I have been traveling between Milan and Paris for 3 years and I have never seen anything like this.

I have just paid 20€ for my luggage which did not have the dimensions for free 11 people are in the same situation as me on this trip at no time are the prices displayed at the stations the controllers verbally recognize the business of the SNCF.

In my entire life as an SNCF traveler, and among all the trains and classes that I have been able to use, it was on a first class seat on the beautiful, incredible TGV that I had the most uncomfortable journey! Lack of space, hard seat, backrest too straight, headrest at shoulder level, no more foot rests and no tilt adjustment. The second class of all other SNCF trains are much more comfortable! Another great success for this company that we are obliged to use... When will there be competition from passenger trains???!!!!!

Ouigo tourcoing montpellier September 11 On-board controllers do not require the wearing of a mask over the nose and mouth, no comments to travelers who endanger others. First trip on the OuiGo tgv, my impressions are negative. Frankly Sncf, Unheard of worse than insurers, it’s really nonsense. Valencia Paris awful. The croque monsieur is excellent even if its price is slightly high, this one easily earns its fourth stars.

In the middle of COVID-19, we are put through all kinds of health measures before getting on the train and then find ourselves on a train piling one on top of the other... incredible. No social distancing, not even from a bench!!!! We find ourselves with the leg directly crossing those of the neighbor. I took the TGV last year to go to Toulouse. Result, dismal service on board unworthy of the price of the ticket, and an hour and a half delay which opens up to compensation.
