Let it be said, next time I will take the plane.

On Sunday 13th September I took a trip with my son from Milan to Nice at a certain point the train stopped saying there was a problem with the doors, So they made all the passengers get off, Then they made us get back on Then they made us get off, then they made us get back on and so far everything was ok then we left again 70 minutes late, so I couldn't visit the market, then I thought it was just something on the outward journey but instead the train was an hour and thirty minutes late for the return, they also said that it wasn't something from that day but that with them there are always and always problems, I'm very sorry because it was so comfortable it's nice, with helpful and friendly staff, find a solution thanks

Super disappointed !!!  They are purely out to make money, have no sympothy for any Corona restrictions ! This was my first and surely my LAST time I made use of there services.... Do not waste your money with these people !!!

GO and pick up a person at ROISSY TGV STATION, you are on time, the person you need to pick up is at the TGV station. No possibility of waiting, we take parking for 7 euros. The person cannot join us: no boarding pass. We try on our side, we are stuck!!! I get angry and they agree to let us pass. Phew!!! To go back to SENLIS, very poorly signposted, we go in circles. 3 hours TGV 1 HOUR to Roissy CDG!!!!

I am from the 40-year-old generation. So the train, and in particular the SNCF, is quite a symbol for us: it's our 2nd means of transport after the car, it's the memory of vacations, of grandpa and grandma... This is the reason why I have always defended this company, and I have passed over all its little faults (except the deportation in 39-45, because that's not possible). But here, what just happened to me today... I took a ticket to Angers. The site directs me to Ouigo - because do you know the ouigo segmentations, yes, what else do I know? Do you know what each thing corresponds to? Because I don't know, I just want a train ticket that takes me from Paris to Angers, that's all! The waiter offers me a 19-buck ticket leaving from Massy. So yes the price is interesting, so I take it. I still say to myself: hum, massy, ​​I don't know, I hope I don't get lost...I had a nose! Because, even if I arrived 30 minutes early, well, I missed my train! Yes ma’am! And you know why? Because the signage is so rotten in this station that you even wonder if it's not done on purpose so that you miss your train. I come out of the RER B platform. I look up at a sign. There is information on the right side of the panel, and on the left side. I look to the right and I see: RER C, and TGV PAR QUAI RER C. Well I see TGV, so I go to the right. There I arrive at some doors. So I pass them on. And there I see 2 signs: TGV by platform 5377, and TGV by platform 5316. Nothing else. I go down to the platforms to read the illuminated signs. No trace of Angers... I then say to myself that okay, well I'll wait, I'll see a TGV train arrive and I'll get off where it is. I'm starting to freak out because it's 2:35 p.m., my train being announced at 2:39 p.m. So I decide to make the emergency call on the door. The guy tells me to read the light signs. But there isn't one. He then says to check with an agent. There aren't any either. He tells me he can't help me. I insist, almost desperate. I ask him to tell me on which platform the train for Angers arrives. He doesn't know. He can't help me. I insist. He hangs up, promising to call me back (nice). He tells me after 2 minutes that I was wrong and that I have to go to the RER B platform where I come from, because the “real” station is there!!! I run and run but hey, can you imagine that I miss my train! What do you think will happen? The agent at the counter not empathetic for 2 cents, because you understand ma'am, yes, it's not refundable! So the guy charges me €78 for the ticket to Angers that I have to go and get in Montparnasse. Oh yes ! And of course you have to pay for an RER B ticket again, because yours is no longer valid! Here, ma'am, is your ticket to Nantes! I said ANGERS!!!  Oh sorry, well it costs €2 more! Well yes, why deprive yourself??? I'll point out to you anyway, I tell him, that it's because of your poorly designed signage which misleads people... But no ma'am, our signage is perfect, ouigo is even advertised on the signs at the top of the RER B platform. Well no my guy, scammer and incompetent... or a liar? I took the photos, there is no trace of ouigo. And then ouigo is for the technocrats of the SNCF, because I just wanted a train ticket to Angers. Morality: after what happened with the Hendaye trains, frankly the SNCF is pitiful. Tomorrow is not the day before the railway revolution! Sad.And above all: avoid MASSY!!!

the Ouigo train (SNCF) suffered a technical problem. we waited at the station for 2 hours. despite this inconvenience which can occur... SNCF reactively informed us of the problems encountered, the progress of the troubleshooting. They provided water, details for ticket refunds and a balanced and complete meal tray! really great.Thank you :)

Null. I thought I would have peace of mind in 1st class to work but it's no better than Ouigo, which is already pitiful. It’s shabby (see photo). Impossible to choose your place. I asked for downstairs and only in the direction of the road, I got up and in the opposite direction. But I have motion sickness. What's more, next to another passenger who I have to ask to get up and wait until he's finished sleeping to buy dinner. If you are a professional, don't think this is business class! If you are there for the holidays, beware of unpleasant surprises! Run away!

Unfortunately it's very expensive and even though 4 hours is really quick for a train ride to Paris, I don't understand how this will be made more attractive than flying in the foreseeable future. Unfortunately there is no working WiFi. I thought it should be possible to achieve this given the time we are in. Buying tickets online is very difficult or almost impossible so you are almost forced to buy the expensive tickets at the BH. First and last time.

Wanted to take the train to Lyon, but hopped (by mistake) on the wrong one (to Gare du Lyon, Paris). We addressed our mistake to the train manager and all he did was charging us this extra expensive ticket (130 euros???). At the same time we couldn't cancel our totally useless ticket from Lyon to Brussels. It's a total rip-off.

We traveled from Valence TGV station to Paris passing by Lyon for summer holiday. At arrival we could not find any luggage put in the luggage storage between two wagons. The TGV staffs completely ignored our claims. The SNCF Security team explained that could be a thief’s. The National Police gently refused our official claims because there is no proof of thief. Inside the wagon there is no room for large luggage. The SNCF ask you to keep all time the luggage with you without blocking the circulation. And because of Covid19 you are asked to limit your mouvements. So there is no way to keep your luggage safely. And be aware that your luggage have no chance with any insurance. This experience is truly a nightmare. Unless you travel only with a hand bag, avoid the trains of SNCF!

The trip was pleasant, but travelers remain stupid. They allow themselves to take the place of others and this seems not to pose a problem for them. The prices of the mini-bar are rather high in my opinion. Paying €6.40 for a simple club sandwich I find it much too expensive.

Previously, there were direct Geneva-Nice connections that I took regularly. These connections disappeared and were replaced by Geneva-Marseille connections, which involves a change in Marseille. Then, the Geneva-Marseille connections were replaced by a single trip early in the morning, which requires using, if one wants to travel at a decent time, or simply connect at Geneva, a Geneva-Lyon connection provided using equipment older than 40 years (VTU75 type cars formerly called Corail), involving a change in Lyon. I would like to point out that access to these cars presents enormous difficulties when you are the holder of a disabled card, because without being obliged to travel in a wheelchair, a disabled person is not specially trained to practice climbing on antique equipment. The icing on the cake, when you have managed to get into these antediluvian cars and get out of them, the TGV equipment to destination of Nice is also 40 years old, since they are old single-level PSE type trainsets put into service in 1981. So again there are difficulties in accessing these trainsets, while the other two-level trainsets have full-level access which does not require training for the "Handisport" games. The SNCF and its subsidiary Lyria make no fun of their customers and the comments made. dissuasive "services", the arrival of competition is impatiently awaited, because I think that Vinci, DB or Trenitalia will be keen to offer a passenger service worthy of the name and not a caricature of public service..

Regarding the comfort of the TGV, I haven't yet tested the new 1st class seats, but in 2nd it's really not great. The backrests no longer lower and you feel like you have a bar in your back. You have to put your suitcase under your seat because there is less luggage space and it no longer fits on the shelves above. As a result, the person behind can no longer stretch their legs. Just like there are no more private trash cans but small trash cans that quickly fill up in the hallway. In short, it feels like a low-cost plane. I'm not ready to go on vacation in 2nd class.

Terrible seat comfort. No other words. I'm 1m95 tall and the seat backs are curved forward... more than 2 hours of travel changing positions every 10-15 minutes. The Intercités train is much more comfortable, fortunately my first 2 hours of travel were OK...I don't necessarily understand the designer's idea.

Even if there are improvements (WiFi, power socket and USB). There is not much room for large suitcases (2 places for a train at the bottom) there is mainly room for cabin type luggage (under the seat - not practical). In terms of comfort, increasingly stiff seats even in first class. There is also no longer an individual trash can at the passenger seats (top during the COVID 19 crisis) etc... In principle the TGV INOUI should be the premium of the TGV range we do not have the same notion of premium...

Having used the Thalys with great satisfaction every week for several years between 1995 and 2007 on the return journey from Paris to Brussels, I must admit that it has changed a lot.....Pleasure trip from Paris to Amsterdam that the SNCF without warning stops in Brussels as a terminus on the way out (waiting 2 hours to take the next one), on the return dirty toilets without water... it stinks 😷. Controllers without a professional soul! Indeed, it seems that men have degraded this flagship whose speed remains intact.

Deplorable quality of service and significant delays, as always in the end. No control relating to simple barrier gestures or the wearing of a mask. A simple announcement of apology will be enough for them.

Arriving at Gare de Lyon, when scanning the tickets to access the platform, it does not work (as is often the case). An SNCF agent comes and scans the tickets on his device. He then tells us that our suitcase is too bulky and that we must pay extra. We therefore pay an extra €20. And surprise, once we arrived in our car, there was no room for our suitcase... We wonder what the point is in paying extra for a service that doesn't exist!!! As always, the SNCF takes advantage of its monopoly to scam people! 👏 Looking forward to opening up to competition!

I used the access plus service for mother who has difficulty walking no problem In Morlaix the station manager was great with a person of a certain age and even took the time to reassure her In Paris tb except the service had forgotten to bring a wheelchair but immediately remedied the problem Bravo for this service which allowed my mother to come and spend time with the family I highly recommend it in Morlaix Paris

The SNCF canceled a return train for me over Christmas for 2 people. They're giving me a credit. I recently bought a return ticket for 2 people and they partially deducted the credit, saying that it was only valid for one person and I had to pay the extra. It's a scam. While the credit was valid for 2 people. So I still have a credit for the same deadline as before. This is not normal.  At Christmas I had to extend my stay by 2 nights at the hotel because I did not have the means to return. I had to pay again for a flixbus.  Thank you SNCF!

Tried the Thalys from Schiphol to Paris for the first time this month. Already a lot of experience with NS International via ICE and IC Berlin connections to Germany. The carriage order is neatly indicated on the signs. First class carriages look neat and tidy. Due to COVID-19 measures, the dining car was unfortunately closed. From Schiphol, the train runs quickly to Rotterdam, where speeds of 300 km/h are sometimes reached in the Netherlands. Then you will be in Antwerp and Brussels South before you know it. The next section is almost exclusively on high-speed rail, so we drove from Schiphol to Paris in just over three hours.

The train was on time, which goes to show that miracles exist. 7 hour journey so I took a 1st ticket. That said, I have a little difficulty seeing the difference between 1st and 2nd. Because of your air conditioning system from the bottom to the top you are allowed to turn it on so use it there or change the system. It is just as hot on the train as it is outside.  I appreciated having my sweaty back in contact with the carpet that covers your seats, which by the way are nests for mites. It's really time that the SNCF is privatized and that we get what we pay for. Prices are changing, train lines are disappearing and we continue to pay high prices for our tickets.

Dirty train. Cakes on the floor. Sticky tablets. We can clearly doubt the covid disinfection at the sight of the train. Lamentable. No electrical outlet either even though my ticket expressly provides for one.
With what's happening at the moment I don't find it normal at all to have someone next to me, shouldn't it be every other seat normally? Phew!

Booked Karlsruhe-Paris round trip.. uncomfortable seats, zero wifi, zero distance between seats despite the COVID situation.. mandatory masks on board but people do what they like.. zero checks on board.. truly pitiful!!!
always late!! It’s really too much!! you never anticipate problems! on the other hand level of price increase there are people! be on time dammit!

I can't write about taking the train,  because, due to COVD-19, our flight to Paris was cancelled and we couldn't go.  I can comment on THALYS' Customer Service though, because I was able to easily get through by phone, explain the situation, and received my refund in one day. Thank you THALYS for making  a unpleasant situation a little bit better by your prompt, cheerful and efficient customer service.

Angers-Paris Montparnasse travel in 1st class on the new TGV InOui. Very pleasant, refined and neat cabin. The seats are very wide and can even recline up to a certain slope. No problem with legroom. Many details in the seat (storage, light, etc.) which make the difference with 2nd class. There are also screens in the cabin where it is possible to follow the location of the TGV in relation to the journey. Departure from Angers on time and arrival slightly early in Paris.
Fascinating journey on a super fast and comfortable train.  Just your hours of travel at a very reasonable cost. First class travel with little difference to 2nd class.  It is worth it!

The worst customer services ever. They canceled the trip due to their strike that they organized and they kept my reimbursement claim for 3 months in order to tell me that they will forward it to Belgian railways because I've bought the tickets via the internet and apparently the Belgian railways should deal with my claim, even if everywhere on my tickets it was mentioned SNCF France. The problem is that I called them 2 times and asked if my claim was ok. Both times they told me that there are no problems with the claim and I should wait for the reimbursement for at least 3 months. I waited for 3 months and then they just told me that is not their business to reimburse me and they told me to hire a mediator if I want my money back. They just don't care at all about customers there. They could easily tell me when I called them - instead of this they kept my claim for 3 months. Very disappointing and very unprofessional services. I will never use their services again. I prefer to travel by bus or another company, but SNCF was definitely the worst decision. I would never recommend them even to my worst enemies. And 1 star is too much for them.

I am for the TGV but regret the problem of paid parking in the provinces. In my personal case, I use the TGV towards Paris from Chalon sur Saône. To go faster, I take the TGV to “Le Creusot” because it takes 1 hour 30 minutes to get to Paris.  It goes very quickly but you have to add costs, in particular the distance from Chalon sur Saône to Le Creusot by car, then, the parking costs at "Le Creusot" (Montchanin station) What I regret about the TGV is the parking costs, knowing that for "Le Creusot", the parking is out of the city!!!!  The station is isolated!!  Plus, it’s a shame the TGV doesn’t leave earlier in the morning! Otherwise, the big advantage is that it always arrives on time

It takes approximately 4 hours to get to Paris Lyon Station. It was possible to use it with a Eurail Pass, but it costs extra to reserve seats in advance. I used the SNCF app, but it was disappointing that I couldn't select a seat.

Took the TGV from Paris Gare de Lyon to Dijon. Great views of the Ile de France wheat growing region of France. The train zips through the open countryside, then runs about the same speed as the North East Regional (USA) from Montbard (the only stop) to Dijon. Dijon train station is a bit confusing as one has to go back to the main hall to find the quai for your next train. For a few Euros more definitely go First Class, especially if you have long legs or any luggage!

Following yesterday's announcements of school closures in France and after having informed health priorities since the start of the virus, today Friday March 13 in the Aix en Provence tgv taken at 12:18 p.m. towards Paris, no liquid soaps either in the sink or in the one near the toilet, being close to the bar I informed the bartender while having a coffee who said to me, you are right it must be said, ironically of course because he did not take the trouble to inform the maintenance staff, after 20 minutes I go back to check and still no soap, well done SNCF.

For our train ticket, which was booked for February 28th from Mannheim to Paris and back on March 1st, 2020, no working email / web refund option can be found on the SNCF website. The international telephone number provided is no longer valid and the new number is only announced in French. The train to Paris, including the following 3 trains over a 4-hour journey from Mannheim to Paris, were canceled - so a trip could no longer be carried out in a meaningful way. We have not received an answer to the contact entry on the SNCF.COM website for 6 days. We are very disappointed in the ease of processing problems - booking and paying were of course easy and the ticket email arrived immediately. What should we do now? We are very disappointed and frustrated :-(

From the center of Barcelona to the center of Paris (and vice versa) in six and a half hours. A time that is excessive, although if there is no rush the experience is pleasant. An excess of stops slows down the trip. The price is reasonable, although without the possibility of choosing a seat.

When you arrive at the platform in R'dam, it says at the front (2a) to Paris and at the back (2b) to CDG. But according to our ticket and the letters on the platform, we have to sit at the back while we go to Paris. A friendly employee told me that the designation 2a and 2b is never correct! So we go to the end of the platform. The train comes and it stops somewhere completely different, so we leave the platform again. When boarding it turns out that everyone just has to sit somewhere and it doesn't matter because an earlier train has canceled. Then tell Thalys staff immediately! Back almost two hours delayed because our train was also canceled at that time. And the next train was 40 minutes late. And again not good information at all! And also dirty toilets without water. OUIGO... or not... frankly so-called low-cost travel... when I do the math... we are far from it. I left with my daughter but we returned by two different trains. I had kept the luggage. Took the red train from Paris Gare de Nord to Brussels Midi the ride is 1:20 the ride is smooth and comfortable first class seats are wide and comfort, there is free wifi and power charge for mobiles and appliances. The train departed and arrived on time. Staff were friendly and helpful. The tickets are on the expensive side if you don't book well in advance.Overall recommended

First class from CDG to Strasbourg and from Strasbourg to Paris. First of all, at the time of making the reservation, I didn't know the direction of travel of the vehicle from CDG to Strasbourg, so it was a do-or-die decision as to which direction the seat should be facing. As a result, the sheet ended up facing the wrong way. Next, inside the car. The seat is wide and easy to use. It is also equipped with a USB power source, making it a mobile environment. In-car wifi is also available. But it's dirty. Trash remains scattered. The window glass also lacks transparency. Maybe it's a problem with the manners of the French people, or maybe it's the railroad's negligence in not cleaning the inside of the train, but either way, it feels like France. As it is a European express train, it is faster than a bus and allows you to reach your destination without having to worry about traffic jams. Well, it's cheaper than the Shinkansen in Japan, and it's kind of like that.

We took the TGV from Disneyland Paris to Charles de Gaulle airport and it was super easy and straightforward. If your under 25 it’s free to take. We bought tickets online before we left and used our phones as tickets. The ride was about 10min from Disney to the airport and direct. Our original train was delayed 45 min, so we asked the information guy if there was another train we could hop on instead. He said when your train is delayed more than 20min your free to hop on any other train to your destination. Overall the ride was comfortable and clean and lets you off in terminal 2.

I travelled with my young boy from Basel to Paris and back. On our onward journey buffet was closed. There were free bottles of water left but no food. It's a three hour plus journey. Sad. On our way back from Paris we were delayed for nearly two hours for different reasons. Both toilets on our coach were out of order. It is fun when it's traveling 320 Kmh but overall, very, very disappointing. Get a plain if you can. Or even a bus.

the city is always beautiful even if it shows some signs of neglect, perhaps due to the economic crisis, I ate well in Montmartre, look carefully for restaurants, the French are like all other restaurateurs, I will return

The TGV offered us a connection that connects Karlsruhe and Paris in just about two and a half hours and is also on time. The space could be a little larger, but otherwise there is absolutely nothing to complain about. Highly recommended.

We travelled first class to make sure it would ne clean. And it was not really dirty. But going to the bathroom is not a picnic. And try to get some decent food there (not clean)! Luckily we brought some sandwiches.

Thief !   The MR527 controller gave me a fine of 39 euros for using my "Illico-liberté" card in the PACA region, telling me without even having verified that I could use it in this area...! We got delayed for 90 minutes at Bordeaux. All announcements only in French. If I did not ask fellow passengers I would not have known that I had to get off since we are going to miss our Renfe (Sudexpress), Hendaye to Lisbon connection and they do not have hotels for us in Hendaye. I had a first class ticket and was thrown into this dump with no TV, no wi-fi, no room service, no breakfast, terrible bed. It was 27 Dec and I had to make emergency plans to join friends in Lisbon for new years. The next day I was told that we will be transported to Lisbon from Hendaye by bus, appox 24hour journey! I had to make my own way from Hendaye to Bilbao. Again I was given wrong information about no trains from Hendaye to Bilbao. A fellow passenger I met by chance told me about the Euskotren. I paid for hotel in Bilbao on 28 Dec, not part of my initial budget. the whole experience ruined a holiday of a lifetime. ( I am from South Africa and traveled half way round the world to experience this trip.) Back home now and still struggling to get any feedback or compensation. I do not have any hope at this stage that I will get a cent from SNCF. My best advice to anyone is stay away from SNCF and stay the hell away from France!

If you are into delays, bad service and overpriced trips - you will love sncf. Well I say money, they will give you sncf vouchers. Although if there is ever an issue on your side - here there is no merci, you either pay extra or get out.And then they strike because they think they deserve to have some special right for doing such a terrible job.
Very punctual. Super comfortable,  Specially first class. Super fast. Easy to buy tickets online or at the station.
Unreliable service.Trains are often late,cancelled or broken down. Not forgetting the predictable yearly strikes every holiday season.

The boarding information is not displayed easily, and when the platform information is displayed, the escalators and elevators to the platform are very crowded in order to secure a seat.

We travelled from Schipol to Antwerp and back again. This thing goes like the hammers. We got up to 186mph, and it was very smooth. Would have liked to have the train staff being a bit more visible. It could have had anything in it. And I did not want my fingerprints on a potentially hazardous item. The train staff should have been there to deal with the incident, but no one came. It did inconvenience to passengers walking through the carriage. But not my problem unfortunately.

The TGV is not specific to anywhere in France. It is a fast and efficient means of getting from A to B in modern comfort. Since its introduction into service in 1981, the TGV has transported well over 2 billion passengers. The TGV, especially its original orange PSE version, has become an icon of French technology, arguably equivalent in stature to the Eiffel Tower. Travelling at up to 320km/h (200mph), the TGV has shrunk journey times significantly, sometimes by half or more.

Very easy online booking. Cheaper than Deutsche Bahn. First class is very spacious. Wide seats, free WIFI, sofa bed. Very cozy, clean and quiet. In 2 hours you can be in Disneyland. Great. Very nice conductor, too service. We will definitely book again.

Me and my girlfriend can fly from paris to geneva for 60euro round trip 1 way train to geneva or anywhere over 500km is 60euro 1 way.So, we are paying 4 times as much to train. After rushing to be on time my friend found himself stuck behind the security barriers because his luggage was too big.. Impossible to leave Paris and arrive in Montpellier in the middle of a strike. Long live humanity! the money above all is disgusting. Of course the ticket is not refundable!!

Even though there were strikes, the TGV, given the excellent service both at the station and via the app, replaced the return train for us and we left for the return without a hitch. We took the incredible Paris Perrache tgv and are very satisfied with it. The seats are comfortable and clean. Everyone has their own socket for their laptop or tablet

The THALYS staff that “welcomed” me at Gare du Nord was unbelievably rude. The train inside looked disgusting and was late. There was an awful smell in Comfort Class But mostly, I can’t get over the terrible staff you have at Paris that treated me like dirt!

Avoid if possible. Thalys is a total disgrace. They canceled the train I was booked on without notice due to a strike in Paris. I get that. But what happened consequently is very poor customer service, making me run around in circles, and gave me different conflicting instructions.  They don’t care about their customers.

I should have travelled, but due to the strike the train was canceled and it was impossible to make a change as SNCF would have you believe. It's the second time in a year that this has happened to me! Customer service non-existent and unprepared. I have been trying to contact them for many days and IT IS IMPOSSIBLE. They did not refund my money for return tickets from Paris (having canceled my outbound tickets due to the strike). I'm waiting for a response, otherwise it would seem embarrassing to me.

The announcements on trains are all untimely, too loud, uninteresting, redundant. They only disturb and make noise when we try in vain to try to be calm when no one and nothing favors it. It is an additional ordeal of the trip.

Travelled ‘first class’ from Lausanne to Paris Gare de Nord.  The TGV service arrived in Lausanne with carriage numbers that did not match anything booked by any passengers.  There are no staff to ask where our assigned carriages are on the platform - and confusion reigns.  The wifi doesn’t work (as usual for French trains) so no use trying the TGV website for guidance.On board the train, passengers who have boarded are arguing about seating with no one certain if they’re in the right seats/carriage.The carriage is divided into upstairs and downstairs compartments, making changing seats all the more difficult.  There is a small space for storing luggage at the end of the carriage which was entirely full before we left Lausanne - and unfortunately the overhead racks are only really big enough for a coat or handbag, so larger suitcases are just shoved wherever.At the second stop, Geneva, the circus continued as more boarding passengers find people sitting in their booked seats. A harried looking conductor finally appears and says the train has ‘a big problem’ with the numbering of the carriages.  He advises travellers to just sit wherever they can.Disorganised and disappointing, especially since passengers have paid to book reserved seats on this service.

Our trip was cancelled due to a planned strike and we were notified it would affect us a day before our journey. They are impossible to get hold of online or by phone for a refund with the only forms being in French. Their actual website informs me to contact them by post for information... in this day in age. They simply want you to get frustrated and give up. AVOID!

We booked our tickets online. Although the travel experience in itself was comfortable and nice, the issue was the strike and the incompetent, and unfriendly staff.I was informed by email that the train I booked was cancelled, due to national strike and that I should change my ticket to a different train.I tried to do it on the sncf app, but it kept giving me an error. Then I went to the counter at gare de Lyon. After 1h30m standing in line, the lady at the counter said that my train isn't marked as cancelled and that I don't have to do anything. I showed her the email I received,but she said I shouldn't worry,as all customers received this email.I didn't believe her but she refused to change my ticket unless I wanted to pay EU 200+!2 days later (1 day before my trip) I received another email notifying me again that my train is cancelled and that I should change my ticket. So I tried again on the app, with an error again.Then I went to to the machine at the station but it wanted to charge me again.Finally I had to go to the counter again, and despite me explaining that I have already been here, waiting 1h30m in line without having been helped, the clerk rudly explained to me that I would have to stay in line again like everyone else. (the same clerk was however more helpful to a young beautiful lady that came later... Wonder why...)When I finally made it to the counter I was helped competently, however there was no apology, nothing.

comfortable fast train. Be careful quickly full, you have to remember in advance. For my case, had to take the bisness class because train full. For return offer of a sandwich. Pass several to offer drinks. Few Ankara speaks another language unlike Istanbul.

We used this train to get around Paris without flying. The trains are beautiful and ours left and arrived on time. The on-board staff is courteous even if a little cold. We are more or less at the level of our high-speed trains, although everyone may have their own opinion on the matter, in our opinion we are on the same level.

Three things we have come to expect from these guys, we love train travel, and do it every chance we get, we really look forward to our trips with these guys the trains are so smooth no clickity clack, just whoosh, at around three hundred k’s, amazing.

May the government have the courage to permanently eliminate the status of these wealthy people! Salaries doubled by bonuses and various expenses, more than reduced hours and retirement at 50!!! Last year we took the TGV to Bordeaux, this journey took 5 hours. This year we went to Lyon which only took 3 hours. These trains run punctually and are very comfortable, the wagons are also neat. This is a good and fast way to travel. There is also plenty of choice of food and drinks in the dining car. Prices are on the high side. I now have 2 experiences with the TGV and they were both very good.

Train is the best way to travel, and I love it! We had a blast in Brussels. The Air bnb, the bus pass, cooking food in the Air bnb, we saved a lot and we even saved more by traveling using the Thalys train. It is very comfortable and even much better if you get a great price. Yes, Thalys is the way or TGV, I highly recommend it. Ah one important tip, as I wrote before, if you know your dates of travel buy your tickets ahead of time, don't wait, they get very but very expensive. I bought my tickets around November and I was traveling in August, I found them for $40 for two people one way. If you think that is a good price then do that... Last year I found the same tickets for $32 one way for two. So if you are on a budget, then that is they way to go. I would love to travel to other parts using TGV like Zurich, etc. Enjoy your travel, ah another tip, I just remembered: If you are traveling with kids, I highly recommend buying tickets ahead of time.

I took out an SNCF card with my wife for the sake of sustainable development. Very often late or canceled so we are going to take the plane again which does not necessarily cost more. Roll on privatization

Paris-Nice on December 2 - departure delay 20 minutes - endless queue at boarding (how to manage to create bottlenecks - the SNCF has undoubtedly filed a patent for this!) - excitement at its height which generates panic and benefits pickpockets - the police intervene - the excitement goes up a notch - an exhibitionist lets loose - the police intervene again - the train ends up leaving but that's without counting the breakdowns South-East signaling station - the non-maintenance technicians probably live there! - in short, we are told of a traffic jam - 1h30 late in the end. A round trip from Paris to Brussels during the day allowed me to verify that this train still had the same quality Certainly the trains are a little old but they are comfortable the service in first class is good and friendly Nothing to do with our usual TGVs where only the fares are .. 1st class
Travelled 2nd class from Paris to Strasbourg. The ride was smooth, comfortable & roomy. The luggage space was very generous.
I like this Train, but the oui.sncf page to reserve a seat never works. For years I have been trying to post this through this page, without success. There are always "technical problems" :-(.

Comfortable, consistent and efficient. Paris to Zurich in 4 hours. NO hassles. Clean and fast. First-class provides access to a very comfortable cocktail lounge. Sit back and enjoy the scenery and avoid the auto rental. Eurorail is a  great value! Easy to understand and easy to transfer.

My train from Antwerp to Amsterdam got canceled. I wonder what kind of service is this? next time it'll be easier to just walk all the way to Amsterdam

We took the train to Paris today.  No one checked our tickets. We had to remove some people who were squatting in our seats like gypsies. Other than that nice ride. Only other issue was the wifi app was not working which sucked. Our TGV experience last week was excellent.

I took the Thalys for a return trip in 1st Premium class to Brussels this weekend. I was once again disgusted and annoyed by this company which unfortunately has a monopoly. The condition of the seats was deplorable on the way out and the journey lasted 2.5 hours; in fact the train obviously recorded a delay (the daily batch) on a timetable already announced as extended due to works (which were not the work of Thalys). On the way back, on the train leaving at 11:04 a.m., the service was lousy (and that's nice); unfriendly on-board staff and a complete scam in terms of "Premium" catering (compare the photo claimed on the site with that of reality...). All in all, a sandwich wrapped in a sheet of kitchen paper.... a real scandal. From a legal point of view, is it normal to allow this type of shamefully misleading advertising to continue? The smallest restaurateur would have the worst problems with Fraud... It is urgent to open these lines to competition!!!!!!

Null ! Never use! Absolutely avoid! Scandalous! A disaster! 20 minutes late Saturday 9/11 missed connection, and certainly 2 hours today for the return! Stupid and false announcements and emails. A boarding like cattle. The value for money is very bad. Prefer a bla-bla because it is more reliable and more pleasant.

The website goes round in circles when you search for refund/cancellation etc.  Appalling.Be warned!
Until now the tgv was comfortable, but the new inoui version is horrible, whether in 1st or 2nd. Looking forward to opening up to competition

Paris-Lyon, which is equivalent to Tokyo-Osaka, starts at 59 euros, so it's cheap. There seems to be a cheaper brand called Ouigo, which is cheaper, but unfortunately you can't buy it with a Japanese credit card. LCCs in Europe are cheap, but I like trains because you can see the scenery. There are no paper tickets, so if you have an app called Oui sncf on your smartphone, you can easily purchase, change reservations, and board the train.
Very comfortable trip. well-stocked bar and spacious, clean facilities. Arrival in the center of Paris. No problems with children.
Nice station from an architectural point of view, integrated with the airport. However, the windows were lacking in cleanliness, dirty and full of cobwebs.

Traveling by TGV can turn out to be an obstacle course...Sunday 27/10 I bought a Bordeaux/Paris for 27.45 euros in first class. If you are making a tourist trip and what you want is to get to the center of a city as quickly as possible, then this means of transportation is ideal: fast, comfortable, punctual, efficient. We arrived to London, from Paris, on a comfortable and very fast TGV (Train à Grande Vitesse, for its acronym in French) called Eurostar. The Paris-London route is completed in just three hours, crossing the tunnel under the English Channel. The trip is simply wonderful. Better than the plane. To get around Europe, it is an excellent alternative.
Accident 2h50 reimbursed. and ter deleted great I take a train two days later deleted. Great waste of time I had to take another more expensive one. SNCF strikes great week

They can’t tell time and are too strict, but if you get stuck in their terrible check in system at least when you go to the info desk, they’ll compare themselves to an airline with a check in desk and security. Also watching the train, on their strict schedule, leave early and then not be able to do anything. Save your money
Travelling from Zürich to Paris with the TGV is very easy and comfortable. Need to reserve far in advance though.

Thalysthecard gold member and frequent traveler. After yesterday's unprofessional answers from the customer care and the outdated tickets on thalys.com when changing a ticket according to support advise I don't recommend this company. I switched to comfort1 prices are similar somehow and seats are of bad quality. WC is dirty not as before. Not sure what happened to this company over the years. After more than 20 years of using these services, it really must be said that the French public service at this level does not offer the slightest service. Always held hostage by strikes, we all pay for substandard service and unpleasant staff. Late trains, reservations in 1st to end up in 2nd with a free seat, no smile, in short. It's a shame.

I was returning by train from Montelimar... And at Bolieau, near Nice, the railway police entered. I noticed that they were asking everyone for tickets... they fined one boy but left him on the train. Just back from a trip around France and Italy by train and the contrast between train services is stark. Supprimé became our new feared word as many french trains were cancelled at short notice ( citing a social movement by drivers protesting at safety, strikes, “planned” maintenance etc)No online or in-station systems worked when rerouting tried. Staff withheld options for alternate travel...yes, Marseille, I’m talking about you! You can jump on any other train on the same day without penalty if you are aware of this right. The toilets at both ends of our carriage malfunctioned half an hour into a seven hour run ( Paris to Milan). Squalid. This isn’t how it used to be. It’s sad to see. I love train travel, but alas in France it’ll be car travel for me from now on. It’s a trade off between my carbon footprint and my coronary arteries.By contrast Italian railways emailed me several days before a journey from Florence to Milan. My initial reflex was heart sink. It seemed to be alerting me to a change in itinerary. It was. There’d be a five minute later arrival in Milan!!! They were accurate.Italy’s rail system, which I’ve booked via Trenitalia over the years,is a joy.Just as well as since their car drivers are all crazed, it’s the one European country I’m afraid to drive in!

Very good service in punctuality, schedules and conditions. I totally recommend it. I bought the tickets at the offices because there were always some problems with the website on the Internet. I highlight the comfort for traveling and the punctuality of the services.
impossible to rely only on trains! the state has been very kind to penalize the car and encourage people to take public transport but there should already be a minimum of competent companies

We are travelling first class today from Zürich to Paris. Disgusting, smelly, toilet is so filled up with paper and caca... i cant believe it. I suppose its the french standards. But to have to cope with this also in First class is a no go!!Never again!

In the spring the booking worked out perfectly for my fellow travelers and I from Freiburg/Br. to Paris & back: 5 stars for that. I received notification of the debit and a link to print out the tickets by email, as well as the note that this email would not replace the tickets. Because the link didn't work, I turned to help. I'm now waiting for an answer and help to get the tickets! If printing is not yet possible, this should be noted when booking and also when and with which link you can print the tickets!

Please avoid using the SNCF app. It would not allow us to book 7 passengers. We had to go in twice to book a 4 and a 3. While doing so the prices were going up (popular February  half term week). every day, I take the train back to Paris Normandy to go to work I pay 192 euros per month for transport at the moment the controllers decide at the last moment if they are going to work or not (so-called social movement following an attack) of course I do not condone violence, but they only have to blame the management instead of ruining the day of those who work it is shameful but the SNCF doesn't really care as long as they are sitting behind a desk

Before going to Europe, I had a very high expectation about the trip as it’s the first time I bring my wife for a one-week holidays, but I end up in horrible experience while taking Thalys train from Amsterdam to Brussels. I do search several options before decided to book & paid a train ticket online, instead of purchase the airline ticket as we wanted to experience the Europe’s countryside scenic view. We purchased the first class wagon seat as we wanted to ensure things are pretty organize & safe. But, but, once the train about to arrive the Brussels Midi-Station, our bag was swiped by a thief and all our passports, money & other important travel documents were gone. I’m traveling many countries around the world and I never had this kind of experience; and I would like to recommend Asian Travellers - DO NOT take train in Europe across the counties as Thief is everywhere & they are targeting Asian Tourists the most. France in a nutshell:Train is on time, fast and very quiet.On the other hand: cleanliness gets a "C-", seats are worn out, insufficient room for luggage: there are suitcases in the aisle, luggage by the doors and getting on/off is a scramble of suitcases and people trying to move through.  It feels a bit like a vegetable market in the countryside: colorful but not very efficient,Ticket price is ok.

We got the TGV SNCF train from Lyon to Paris. It was quite clean and comfortable. Although I did think the two Italian trains we used - Italo and Frecciabianca - were a lot better overall. However, the TGV train was punctual and efficient. It was not as smooth as I had expected and I did have trouble walking around. Perhaps the upstairs part of the carriages experiences more movement than the downstairs section. My main issue with TGV is their online presence comprising a poor website, lack of communication and big price hikes. Despite being signed up to receive email alerts for special prices, I never did receive any till it was too late. The prices were always increasing on their website and the only time they did a promotion, they just advertised it on Facebook which I missed because it only went for about 8 hours!

Absolute joke of a train service. Not worth the money and unreliability.Next time will definitely be flying rather than taking a TGV.If I could, I would Give it 0/5.Firstly. I am on TGV InOui, which is supposedly the “new updated” TGV. The seats are filthy and looks like from early 2000’s. There is no WIFI. Even though, when I booked, it told me there was WiFi on board AND there are signs all over the train saying there is WiFi. When I asked the staff, they told me the WiFi is 6 months away and they have advertised with stickers before they even installed it. FALSE ADVERTISING!!The train appears to be so old it can’t even reach the quoted 300km/h. It just rattles around the tracks at normal regional train speeds.The toilets are not cleaned and stink.Just please don’t make the same mistake we did!

Took the train from Paris to Berlin in 1st class and the ride was great, then had to change trains which is where the problems started as the TGV was held up which caused use to miss connecting train to Berlin on GB train. Was easy to change trains but no seat allocated there had to find a seat on a 5 hrs ride which was no easy

Strongly recommend potential SNCF train customers avoid SNCF at all costs. Find another way to your destination. We pre-purchased a two round trips from Paris Nord to Chantilly for ~ 50 euros. On the way back, we boarded the wrong train due to our own mistake, and had to disembark at the next stop and reboard the next train to Paris. When conductor checked our ticket, we were shocked that he not only would not accept our original pre-bought tickets, but charged us an additional 100 euros in total for “boarding a train without a ticket”. 100 euros – for a one way, 20 minute ride that was already paid for!!! We think he price-gouged us because we were Americans.When arriving back in Paris Nord, we explained the situation to the SNCF office in Paris Nord, but they did not even offer a partial refund. When we politely pressed the issue further with logic and reasoning, we were again shocked at how they treated us – calling us “rude and arrogant Americans that have no place in Paris”, and motioned for security to escort us out. Security never came, so maybe it was a bluff – regardless, we left by our own will anyway (no refund, of course).But there’s plenty of other reasons to avoid SNCF as well – signage on actual trains and platforms is poor or nonexistent, central boards at stations don’t always list the platform you’re train is leaving from, and if a train is late (which SNCF trains are frequently) and you miss your connection to another SNCF you pre-bought, you’re out of luck.  Finally, compared to Italy & Austria, the interior of the trains is filthy and neglected. Long story short – avoid them like the plague – look for other alternatives like other train operators that run to and from Paris, local/regional bus lines, Uber/Lyft, or even rent a car.

Terrible trip from Basel to Paris with TGV. Firstly, train was 65 minutes late departing due to 'a coupling problem', so we were sitting on this grubby, urine scented train for longer than we should have. No redeeming qualities that I can report. Felt in need of a hot shower after  what should have been (and definitely was not) a pleasant trip in 1st Class. Will not waste money on these guys again!

It was my first time on the TGV.  We went from Paris to Lourdes and back.  The seats were very comfy in 1st class.  The 5 hour train ride went by so quickly.  Staff on the train were friendly and helpful.  Food was like on any other european trains.  Right on schedule which is the norm in Europe anyway.  One doesn't really feel the high speed during the travel so people should not be concerned about getting motion sickness.
I had a lot of problems paying for tickets on Rail Europe and ended up on Loco 2.  It was fast, had a more navigable website and no problems with purchasing.

I got an email today that said I bought a RT ticket from Paris to Amsterdam through Thalys. I have not bought any ticket nor am I planning to buy one. I have tried calling (they do not answer phones). I have emailed and online chat to no avail. I then called all my credit cards to put in a fraud alert. Why do they not answer phones or respond to a serious fraud problem. BEWARE!!!!  Oh, I finally got a number and they charge 50 cents a minute to talk to you and I was put on hold never got a person. Terrible!!

received email at 19.11 on 22 sept 06.29 train cancelled to milan went to gare de lyon at 20.00harassed and aggressed by sncf staff as disabled passenger refused to let us in to find out options to change ticket to next train departing 4 hours later. was only told i would have to pay difference in cost to change ticket!?! and to come back another time. this is outrageous. i stated i could not physically come back as i am disabled and the cancellation of the train was causing me undue stress and anxiety and there would be no reason we should have to pay a supplement of the difference in cost for a train cancelled by sncf for the next express train to milan. sncf staffwould not let us in stating they were closing at 21.00?!? unable to reach anyone on phone at 33184 94 3635 after 30 minutes on hold or to change ticket on sncf.com as option states cancel or change ticket but no option to change only to cancel. had to book last minute flights at great expense plus taxi to paris orly. receipts available. wish to be reimbursed for train tickets cancelled by sncf and reimbursement for additional expenses to get to milan and explanation as to why i was harassed as a disabled person at gare de lyon ticket office by sncf staff as witnessed by my travelling companion/aide.

We arrived at CDG and made our way to TGV station. Our train tickets were part of a air/rail deal with Air France to reach Brussels. We just went to the Air France counter at the train station, showed the boarding passes and the lady in the office immediately issued the boarding passes for the TGV train. 20 minutes before departure,  the platform showed up on the display signpost. The number of our carriage correlated with a letter on the platform. We waited there and the teain stopped so the the correct door was right in front of us. Train was clean and the seats comfortable. The ride was smooth and fast. Neat rest room and free wifi. The TGV arrived at Brussels Midi (South) but we used the same ticket to catch a local train to Central station.

I just bought with a credit card an international ticket with a portion of the ticket in Switzerland. They sell it through their site but cannot send it to you via electronic form because they are not allowed to send electronically ticket for countries outside France. In addition, they cannot send regular mail to countries outside France even though they say they will. So you will NEVER get your ticket and you will never get a reimbursement! Just a rip off!!!
First TGV experience and certainly not the last. On time. Comfortable. Very smooth!

TGV N° 9240 at 7.36am to Turin Porta Susa, booked through an agency fifteen days in advance. Presented at the station three quarters of an hour before departure, twenty minutes before departure a single announcement informs us of the cancellation of the train due to strike in France and that, perhaps, (given the chaos of the station and the terrible loudspeaker system of Torino Porta Susa, we are not sure we have understood correctly...) we could have taken the next train at 10.11 or 16.11. No explanation as to where we would sit since the seats were all booked and the seats on the next train could have already been taken. At the various ticket offices at the station no one was able to give us any information, telling us that since it was a French train they didn't know anything about it. They didn't even know who had made the only (!) announcement on the station's loudspeaker, as if it had been made by another station or by some alien passing by... Simply put, to summarize, make do: SNCF telephone number either hung up immediately or responded with a few very quick words in English and then hung up. At 9.30, the agency's opening time, we managed to speak to our travel agent who did his best to get some information and called us back telling us that the SNCF advised us to "TRY TO GET ON" the next train and to try to sit on the first free seat we found (!) and to ask the conductor (who we DID NOT see for the entire journey to Paris!). We went up to first class hoping that there would be a better chance of finding free seats and, fortunately, that was the case. But I would have liked to see if we had occupied places already booked by someone else! The train managed to arrive almost three quarters of an hour late from Milan, a delay which it managed to maintain until Paris. The three toilets we visited (then we gave up on finding others in decent conditions) were already clogged before leaving Italy with imaginable scents in the surrounding areas, and the regulars on this train confirmed to us that this was a usual condition... On the return the TGV train left Paris on time, we were visited, as long as the train remained at 300km/h, before Lyon, both by the conductor to check the tickets with his helper, then by the customs guards who blocked the passengers in various points of the carriages for checks, and then when the train transformed into the swaying snail that it becomes from Lyon to Italy they all disappeared: we understood why when, thanks to the swaying and the usual scents coming from the again clogged toilets, someone felt ill and vomited in the passage between the seats... Obviously none of the staff showed up again and the passengers had to make do with cleaning as best they could... But he arrived on time... How envious we were of those who were on the Italian high speed trains...

I've heard many anecdotal stories about "bad' French Railways.  Lot of nonsense.  Immaculate double decker train.  Left on time and arrived on time in super fast comfort.  Buffet car was handy and not too expensive (think British Rail rip off!).  We paid an extra 16 Euros total for 1st class returns (on a two hour journey).  Don't see that happening in Britain.

The 3 1/2 hour literally seemed like an hour with 1st class service throughout the trip.  We just sat back and enjoyed the food and drink as we look at our window at the beautiful French countryside.  The seats were also comfortable for the whole family.

We booked first class tickets Lyon to Paris with reserved seats only to find the train cancelled. We were told to get on thr next one and find a seat. The conductor on that train told us there were no seats as we were not booked on his train. Stood the whole two hours. Scumbags!

Making new TGVs with much lower quality.. Old and uncomfortable seats, no power outlet.. And a 20th surcharge for luggage! For a simple suitcase. I don't pay for my suitcase on ordinary SNCF TGV trains. This 5-hour journey is going to be long and painful.

There is no wireless connection, impossible to do any useful activity. Either sleep or die. Poor services even in first class. Italo has a far superior level of seriousness and professionalism. Better hitchhiking.

Trying to give the most useful review possible, I can say that the journey from Paris to Milan Garibaldi went well, nothing more, nothing less than what one might expect from a normal train journey. Given that I am a type of person who doesn't expect anything and that I traveled in second class, I found the carriages mostly clean, they are certainly not new, but I have seen much worse, the seats in my opinion are more uncomfortable than those of an Italo or a FrecciaRossa. Train conductor and girl at the bar (both French I think) very kind and helpful, the menu is quite assorted. The journey went a little beyond my endurance limit in terms of duration, despite this we arrived in Milan ten minutes earlier than the established time, however I believe that the reverse journey from Italy to France could be subject to more delays due to border controls (if this were not the case I would be happy for someone to comment), which is not the case when coming towards Italy. Since short-haul plane trips are the most polluting, I try to take trains so as not to impact the climate with my holidays, but I believe that to encourage others to do this the prices should be drastically lowered, it is not possible that given a seven-hour journey (to go to Paris) I have to pay the ticket at that price. That's the most terrible thing about the trip.
Comfortable and relatively clean. Good seating and plenty of storage for your luggage. Prices ok if booked in advance.
The ROISSY-BORDEAUX train was very dirty. It's not normal to have people travel in this state of lamentable cleanliness... Avoid if you have other alternatives. For me, the SNCF is over.

First class seats were booked on the upper level, for journey from Barcelona to Paris. We were allocated these seats without being able to choose. Fortunately it was to our liking. Although it was quite a mission to get our bags up the stairs as there’s not enough room to leave them on the lower level.The biggest gripe was the condition of the toilets. No toilet paper in the one toilet after two hours into the journey. Flushing was problematic as well!View from above was very good. Passed  lots of dam areas with wind surfers. Passing Talabot offered views of balconied old buildings with beautiful wrought iron balustrades. All in all a pleasant journey. However, there was a long queue for taxis at the Paris station and unexpected slow moving traffic to our hotel, on a Sunday afternoon.

The very special part of this trip for us was landing at 7:30 AM at CDG Airport from YVR Vancouver Airport after a 9 hour journey and then a layover for 4 hours till be boarded The TGV Train To Nantes for a duration of 3 hours... we went 1st Class for the extra space and totally enjoyed the ease of this journey..
Run down, slightly grubby and very expensive train. Delays are usual; occasionally running on time. Unfortunately no alternative for travel by train Amsterdam - Brussels - Paris.

Used for holidays: on the way to the 1st class bathroom no water came out of the tap while on the way back (always in 1st class) no water came out of the drain (imagine the conditions of the bathroom...), the mite-attracting seats retain the residues of the various meals consumed over time; let's say that hygiene and cleanliness are not really the strong point. Every time it's a little late. On the way back, he could have arrived at Porta Garibaldi a couple of minutes early but instead he slowed down to a stop and lost 10 minutes near the station. I read that from June 2020 the Milan-Paris route will be covered by our Frecciarossa 1000 in just 6 hours (compared to the current 7.20-7.30), with a higher speed and at competitive prices.

Having to travel from Paris to Bayonne, I find myself in the unbelievable....What is unheard of (I didn't even know it was possible) is the extreme discomfort of the seats!!! And I was in 1st grade! I used to take the "classic" TGV and I was always comfortably seated, I enjoyed making long train journeys... but here the discomfort of the seat is unprecedented... after 30 minutes you are squirming in all directions, your lumbar and back feeling loose... REALLY ATROGIC

I’m on the 08.15 from Narbone to Paris in first class.Toilet out or order, not enough legroom ( I’m only 161cms )tall and a 20minute Q for anything to eat or drink.  After 1 hr the buffet had run out of most things. Not impressed, the only good thing is the train appears to be on time .

An extremely mediocre meal in a TGV, we are more in the habitual, the common, even the obligatory, we tell ourselves that it has been going on for thirty years and inevitably, when we fall into the trap, when we order the thing, we do not even have the right to be disappointed, we tell ourselves that it is well done, we had nothing to do.  On the other hand, when the SNCF hides this mediocrity behind a Michelin star, it is truly shameful. Recent experience: we read the menu offered on glossy paper and we say to ourselves, why not, perhaps there has been a questioning and paradigm shift in the search for quality. Nope. After 20 minutes of waiting, a hamburger in a cardboard box just warm on the outside, cold on the inside, devoid of the slightest taste quality, bordering on nauseating, a bag of pseudo-dehydrated fries like a food shortage meal, a so-called industrial chocolate fondant in cellophane, all for a slow and very painful digestion, that's it for the Michelin macaroné, shame on him for having endorsed such a sub-cantoche mess.

My train ticket had a mistake in it, it was telling me that I had to switch train, which is wrong, I had to stay in the train. And even though I paid the same price as my friends they were in first class "luxury" and I was in first class "comfort". I wanted to go talk to them to make sure they knew we had to stay in the trains but the Thalys crew just stopped me from going to talk to them. I was treated like a criminal who was going to disturb the passengers of  ultimate 1st class. This is absolutely scandalous, I couldn't even go tell them there was a mistake and because of this extreme and severe policy we almost missed our stop.

A nice way to travel and sure beats dealing with airport crowds and security. However,Booked 1st Class Paris to Girona for the experience. For the money we paid it was a let down. No food or beverage service to your seat (compare London-Paris on Eurostar) and on this trip the food ran out and there was no coffee or hot drink available from about half way through. The catering staff just yelled in french, and spanish if asked, to the long queue that there was no food and that was that. The carriages are tired and not what I would call First Class. The ride is quiet however and reasonably comfortable in large seats.I have to say the whole event was a waste of time and money. Aside from the lovely country side wizzing past at near 300 kph there was nothing to support the cost outlay.We should have flown which would have given us more time in Girona for some sight seeing.Give it a miss or just go 2nd class and take your own food and drink.

The train itself is nice and is quiet.  However, all the bathroom sinks don’t have running water on this trip.  Not sure how a 7 hour train ride doesn’t mandate that their sinks work.  Basically had to buy bottled water in order to wash my hands.

In late May, when I tried to take the TGV from France's Manure-la-Vallée station to Charles de Gaulle Airport, the train was suddenly closed due to information that an explosive device had been planted at the station. We were all forced out of the station, and the police were staring at us with guns. I was told I was waiting for an inspection, but I don't know when it will be restored. To make matters worse, it was Sunday, and the buses were stopped because we couldn't get into Paris due to the weekly strike. If I don't go to the airport in two hours, I won't be able to catch my flight to Italy in time. However, I was lucky enough to catch a taxi as it was a little far away. I was on the move because I could get to the airport without having to go through Paris. When I inquired about a refund later, I received a coupon that was valid for one year and could be used on all French railway lines. I'm disappointed that I couldn't get a refund.

I took the TGV from Turin to Paris in August. The train arrived on time (only 10 minutes late but it's a tolerable time). The convoy is not brand new but, all things considered, in fair condition. Each station has an electrical socket (one socket for 2 armchairs therefore to be shared between 2 people), a small rubbish bin under the armchairs, a table and a footrest. However, I found the bathroom in pitiful conditions: dirty and smelly. I understand that it also depends on the education of the passengers but, on a journey of almost 6 hours, perhaps it would be appropriate to clean the toilets more often! There is also a carriage used as a bar but the prices, obviously, are not so convenient. So overall I can say that the trip was pleasant. However, what absolutely needs to be improved is the Italian customer support service. In fact, in the weeks before leaving, due to a landslide, it was not certain that there would be trains in August. I really struggled to receive safe information. No one ever (and I mean never!!) answers the Italian telephone number that appears on the site. I tried calling for weeks at all times but no one ever answered. When I tried to call the French phone number, an automatic voice answered and then the call was cut off. In any case, it is not always the case that everyone can hold a telephone conversation in French (or English). So if tickets are also sold in Italy it is necessary to create an assistance telephone number in Italian. The information on the site was never secure. I wrote an email and after 2 days they replied that they still didn't know for sure if there would be trains in August (after the landslide on the tracks). But how can you, a few weeks before departure when everything is organized for the holidays, not know whether you will be able to leave or not? So the assistance service in Italy is really bad and should be reviewed. The journey, however, was pleasant.

We prebooked this train trip from Zurich to Paris Gare Lyon…A better option for us than flying into CDG. We booked first class to get better seating and seat numbers. It was quite comfortable.  It was early around 7.30 am. A trolley service came through - selling coffee, drinks, sandwiches and croissants. The coffee was surprisingly OK, but the food was very ordinary - should have purchased food at Zurich station and taken it with us.  There was storage for our cases and a toilet. It was smooth ride however the announcements were  not good - the volume, diction and interference made it impossible to hear. Still it was an experience, and convenient for us.  We would probably train a similar journey in Europe again.

We missed two connections due to the Thello train delay from Ventimiglia to Voghera! And it made us waste 2 hours for nothing when one is tired and wants to get home early! We kindly ask Thello train stuff to be more organized!

I really was impressed by the speed of this train. I arrived in Paris in less than two hours from Strasbourg, which is nearly 500 kilometers away, without an intermediate stop. The comfort of the train is even in the second class better than in an aircraft (economy class). I also used the bistro. The quality and prices of food are OK, especially when you are short of time and don't have time for a meal before departure or after arrival. The timetable has some reserves. We left with 15 minutes delay, but reduced the delay to 5 minutes up to the arrival in Paris. It is a comfortable alternative to an air travel, especially when you avoid the security controls and strict baggage regulations.

Traveling from Barcelona to Paris. I have to say the speed is very good however they have far too many first class carriages. I was forced into one of these due to them having no ‘normal’ seats left (likely because they have so many 1st class seats). This meant that even though I had the interail pass I had no choice but to pay 70 Euros for the ticket. At least I thought I could experience first class. Not that I cared. Then I found out that first class effectively just means you sit in purple seats rather than blue. There is no free food for the entire journey, only a catering carriage with extortionate prices. No extras. The seats are a tiny bit larger and there was no WiFi. I have therefore come to the conclusion that SNCF create there 1st class carriages to artificially reduce the space they have for normal customers. This thus allows them to force those booking late to pay effectively a fine. (The first class price). Instead, if they haven’t provided enough seats for normal paying customers they should upgrade you to first class for free as that is their problem. They should get rid of all their first class spaces. When I tried to sort the WiFi with staff they were dismissive and rude. This should be a 1 mark review but felt I had to put 3 solely because the train is going nice and quick. SNCF STOP ROBBING PEOPLE

In July, for an AIX-LILLE trip my companion and I took the paid option to have a socket each (because yes, you have to pay extra). When we were getting in, the captain changed our car because there was an air conditioning problem in the initial car. We were put back in places that did not have sockets. The captain told us that the reimbursement would be done automatically and that she would provide the information. I never received the refund and despite efforts by emails and telephones, they refuse to reimburse the option!!! There were around fifteen of us passengers who were reseated, that's a profit of around €150 for ouigo on the backs of their customers!!!

7 hour train ride from Paris to Milan first class. First class means NO WiFi (even for purchase), no meal included at all (only a very skimp overpriced  bistro menu for purchase), and worst of all.... no water. For seven hours I had to buy bottles of water. Even the standard seats have the same menu and bar cart as first and it’s very limited. The only difference Between regular and first class is in first class you have the option of having a server bring your food TO you from the same bar cart that u can walk a couple of feet to yourself. Also they call the seats “berth” which means sleeper but they’re not. They don’t lean any further than an economy class plane seat and there’s nowhere to elevate your legs besides a kickstand. Just fly... it’s cheaper and they give you free water. We did this for the train experience but it ended up being worse than a economy flight experience. the bar cart is cool because you can stand and stretch your legs.
We enjoyed our 2 hour train ride from Lyon to Paris.  It was on August 15th so service was a little limited.  Not much of a selection in the food area.

I took this train from Amsterdam to MARNE-LA-VALLÉE DISNEYLAND® PARIS and boy I was put down by the way a conductor was behaving . He was so rude . I don’t think Thalys will ever care about the public perceive them . I rather take a flight than be subjected to this rudeness .

Tgv 6:07 a.m. Marseilles. Late arrival of catering staff. 10 minutes after departure... Start of product placement...impossible to get a coffee without waiting for the end of placement. The controller, out of union spirit, finds this absolutely normal and announces on the train microphone the opening of the bar with a delay of 30 minutes.. In front of the customers present. Come on, with a little luck, the TGV will be on time
The only positive note was the punctuality, but otherwise a disaster: old train, uncomfortable seats, one socket for two, non-existent Wi-Fi, we're just not there.

We were very happy to make a Paris / Les Sables d'Olonne / Paris return trip aboard a TGV (and TER) which was pleasant, comfortable and on time. The journeys were remarkably smooth and the TGV driver + extra controller.

Travelled Antwerp to Paris. Second class. Train was noisy, not clean and the baggage area was totally inadequate. Toilets stank. Wifi didn’t work. Not impressed! By comparison we caught a Eurostar Paris to London three days after second class and it was like first class compared to Thayles. Quiet, clean, comfortable with plenty of luggage space. Wifi great. The Thayles mgt could do with learning from Eurostar how to provide a decent service!! There really is no comparison!

We took the TGV several times this summer and bottom line is that TGV need to get their act together and provide their PAYING CUSTOMERS with cleaner trains. It is not rocket science to clean a train and having functioning washrooms with soap and water. It is not just about travelling at 250-300Km/ HOUR. especially when CUSTOMERS are paying a lot of money to use the service. Also we noticed that the TGV stations in France are run-down and the bloody elevators in Grenoble, Tours and Paris Charles De Gaulle do not function efficiently enough, nor do they work properly. I am guessing that TGV will not take responsibility, but they should because this is where the trains depart and arrive from. Oh yes and the TGV 20 Euro reservation fee for Interail 1st class pass holders is unacceptable as well, especially for train cabins that have wore out seats, dirty floors, non-functioning bathrooms, poor AC (air conditioning) et cetera et cetera.

This was my first time using the TGV for a round trip between Zurich Central Station in Switzerland and Gare de Lyon in Paris. I made a reservation online and got a first class seat, but when I boarded the train at the station, I couldn't find a sign telling me which car number I was in, so I couldn't find my seat until departure. Even at Gare de Lyon, the train numbers are not displayed until 20 minutes before departure, so I would like to be contacted in advance for reservation information. The first class seats were spacious and comfortable, and the train was very comfortable with no shaking or vibrations. However, it was a shame that the seats faced backwards in the direction of travel and could not be changed. I will make sure to check the orientation of the seats when making reservations in the future. Cash was only accepted in euros and Swiss francs were not accepted at the on-board sales or kiosks.

Calling it a fast train is an understatement, a filthy jumble of carriages without services with uncaring staff, no Wifi, a restaurant car that doesn't have hot meals but only coffee and bagged snacks. Unprofessional staff, workers stolen from agriculture. The first class is the same as the second, no difference.

We took the TGV inOui from Stuttgart to Paris and back. Everything went great and smoothly. If booked in good time, the tickets were also inexpensive. The ride was very pleasant and very fast! We felt very comfortable on board - in the double-decker car upstairs!

I will remember my trip on the OuiGo tgv. This formula is perhaps designed to find trips at a lower price and can actually allow many people to travel at a lower cost, but after having tested the formula today, I strongly advise against it. I find it shameful to make people travel in these conditions: each wagon is allocated a greater number of seats than in classic TGvs. The reason is obvious: to allow the SNCF to transport more people by train and therefore earn more money. So far nothing shocks me. Except that the conditions in which you are traveling are Spartan: it is better not to be too big because the space with the front seats has been reduced, no armrest, and especially no space for bulky luggage!! If you did not take the €5 (I think) option for large luggage when booking your tickets, then it will cost you €20/bag at the station on the day of boarding. So don't come and tell me that Ouigo is made for cheaper travel...if that was really what the SNCF wanted, they would penalize you with a lower surcharge...To that, you add the absence of a trash can. Like in airplanes you might say! Except that there, I didn't see anyone from the SNCF passing through the wagons to collect any waste you might have, as is the case on a plane. Before boarding, no one from the SNCF to tell you where your car is. At Gare de Lyon in Paris, you must access via hall 3, therefore under the tracks. You have to take Escalators to get to the platform, but not at the beginning of the platform, that would be too simple. Right in the middle! So when you have two TGvs hooked up for the trip, you are with two young children, a large suitcase and everyone arrives AT THE SAME TIME on the platform (since this is how the principle of boarding in OuiGo works, you don't know if you should go to the right or to the left!!!! Obviously, I didn't take the right side. Well, turn back with a large suitcase and two children, with several hundred people on the platform, it is not a pure pleasure. In short, offering trips at lower prices for its travelers must not drastically replace the quality of the service provided. I understand that we cannot have everything (high quality service and low price). But here, I have the feeling of being considered not as a person but as cattle. even less the case.
