I think that this is a false pretext for the SNCF to simply allow it to increase its profitability (which does not bother me at all personally) but to the detriment of the well-being of its travelers (and this really bothers me) on each trip made by making more volume, by taxing you as soon as you are not in the nails (bulky baggage), with less flight crew (invisible controllers, invisible cleaning staff), comfort Spartan, car bar absent, trash cans absent). I know that this formula will satisfy some people, and so much the better! but to others, at least be warned of what awaits you because in my opinion, the sncf does not warn you enough. For me, OuiGo is now NoGo, jsute NoWay!!!!

Been a fan of TGV trains in the past, but it seems the ratio of quality of service vs. cost went down lately.Pros: travel on a ~300 km/h train with a fair degree of comfort, avoiding the hassle of airports and jets. More environmentally friendly transport. Free wi-fi.Cons: expensive - 120 eur for a 2nd class 6-hour trip from Paris to Nice; interior such as seats etc. saw better days; no included meal; no soap in bathrooms (we even checked in two bathrooms - seriously, no soap to wash your hands on a 120 eur TGV ride is a disgrace).All in all, will consider flying next time unless they improve the quality.

Overcrowded.  Luggage Racks full.  Both bathrooms for the coach (LOL) - out of order for entire trip.  Free WiFi - also out of order (you can connect fine but there’s no internet).  This was a second class ticket - try first class maybe you’ll have better luck than I did (or not).

Simple, fast, inexpensive and oh so easy. With car parks in Lille close to the stations. It is an alternative way to travel to Paris and children find it an experience. Definitely recommended in terms of convenience and price. First class is sometimes almost the same price as second class.

In August 2019 I took the TGV Lyria from Basel to Paris and back. We booked our tickets online a few months in advance. The booking process went smoothly and the operator's website was available in several languages. The ticket price was absolutely right. However, children pay the full price and are not free, as is the case with Deutsche Bahn, when traveling with their parents. We were assigned a seat right when we booked. On the day of the trip to Paris, everything went wonderfully. The train was on time and we quickly found our seats. However, the train was very full. The luggage racks became scarce or insufficient and one or two passengers found it difficult to find a place. Although it was mandatory to reserve a seat when we booked, tickets were sold without a reservation a few days before the trip. Perhaps in the assumption that not everyone will make the trip and that these seats can then be sold again? In this situation, it is not particularly helpful that the reservations are not marked on the seats. The trip was definitely great. 600 km in 3 hours is simply great. The train staff was friendly and accommodating. The return journey was similar, but it was a bit tighter here. Conclusion: Switzerland - Paris with the TGV was simply great. Ticket prices very attractive. But it can also get tight and a bit chaotic.
Best way to travel around France.  The connection from CDG to Southern France is outstanding.  But, there are limited elevators at CDG, so best to use the elevators.

This is easily the worst experience with train travel I've had in my life. We arrived at the station (Amsterdam Centraal) with 2 hours spare as we like to be prepared. We get to the platform quickly fine, but after waiting 15 minutes, we are told it's the other end of the platform. We walk to that end (All 4 of us with heavy cases and bags), then board. A minute or so later we are told we're on the wrong train and get off. They then send us back to the other side of the station and we board. Everything fine now? Of course not. There is someone in our seats, only because the staff have put us on the wrong train. We are told to RUN to the one behind it, and don't make the sprint down the ENTIRE station in the 30 seconds we had. As we'll miss the train otherwise, we hop onto the wrong one (they're connected) and decide to swap carriages upon arrival to Schiphol Airport. We lug our luggage along and make it in time, lift our cases onto the racks and sit down and try to relax. Time passes and we all get drinks / food, before being told seconds later that suprise! We have to change trains, AGAIN. We repeat running with our luggage, trying to disembark one train and get to another along with an entire train of people who all have no idea where they are supposed to be. The staff overall weren't very friendly are were fairly abrupt and rude to be honest. Sitting down in the apparently correct train a loud, repetetive beeping noise kept blaring on and on, stopping and starting 4 times.Overall, staff were blunt, communication was AWFUL, not especially fast, food was mediocre and everyone was very stressed out.Passengers around us shared the same concerns as we ended up chatting to them as we all went through the same problems. Thank god I don't have to experience this nightmare of a train with any kind of regular frequency, otherwise I would lose my mind. If I wanted 4 trains, I would book 4 trains.I strongly don't recommend this train.

Nothing changes over the years: the trains are dirty, the toilets stink and are filthy (remember to take your own paper, there is never any), the air conditioning regularly breaks down, the bar is overpriced (I'll spare you the friendliness of the staff). Some wise advice? Take the plane!
We travelled from Brussels to Paris and back, excellent journey, no delays, only 1h22 minutes to cover 300 km. Book it as early as possible, it's not at all cheap.

Booked 3 first class tickets on OUI.sncf from Carcassonne to Toulouse. When we got to our seats, squatters had taken them. No conductor to be seen. After much back and forth, the squatters grudgingly left. Two of them (teenage girls) plunked themselves down on the floor at the end of the first class car. The other (middle aged man) locked himself in the toilet for the duration of the trip (45 minutes). We arrived in Toulouse (about 20 minutes late) and departed without anybody ever asking us for our tickets. No wonder the squatters are so pervasive. They know they can get away with it because there is no enforcement. Incredible.
The train is fast, comfortable and safe. The only thing that was annoying was seeing that the train ran over a lot of animals, as you can see the blood in the photo.

Niles & I decided to begin our trip from Frankfurt, taking the TGV to Strasbourg.  The first half of the trip was comfortable and uneventful.  The second half was completely different.  Although we had first class tickets, we ended up having to stand, cramped like cattle to the slaughter house, with the smell of sweaty passengers who were caught in the similar predicament.  The change in the adventure was due to a cancellation of one of the trains which resulted in having at least twice as many people boarding a train which was not sufficient to handle everyone, not to mention that the train was late.   It felt like the scene from a movie of India in the 1950’s or 60’s.  (Niles:  at least they did not ask us to climb on top of the train - LoL).We have travelled throughout Europe and had never experienced issues when travelling in First Class.  However, this is the first time we travel in France by train.  Although Niles recommended that we take the “insurance” while purchasing our tickets, I laughed at the thought because of past experience which has always been great and on time.Most of our travels were completed by car, and this morning we are on our second train ride which was also late, taking us from Nimes to Carcassonne.  Hearing the complaints of other passengers, it appears that this is a common occurrence.  Nevertheless, the seats are comfortable and the service very pleasant.  The score given in this review is for the trip to Strasbourg where everyone felt and smelled like canned sardines (not that we would eat that). Nous avons débuté notree voyage a partir de Frankfurt en direction de Strasbourg par train.  La première moitiée du voyage était comfortable et sans évênement.  Cependant et magré des billets de première classe, nous avons parcouru le reste du trajet debout, complètement coincé entre des gens qui étaient pris dans la même situation et ce durant une canicule.  L’odeur était absolument suffocante du à la transpiration de centaines de gens qui étaient grimpées partout à l’intérieur du wagon.   Notre premíère expérience avec SNCF-TGV fut un grand désapointement puisqu’on s’attendait à un meilleur service.  Aucune information n`a été  fournie.  Il faut mentionner que le traject avec DB était très bien.  Nous avons voyager à travers l’Europe sans soucis auparavent.  Ayant completer la partie conduite de notre voyage, nous sommes présentement abord du train en direction de Carcassonne.  Et sans surprise, le train était en retard, ce qui semble être commun selon certains passagers.  Nous ne sommes pas en Suisse, bien sûr.

Great experience from Paris to Avignon. The train was on time, clean, comfortable and easy overall. My kids enjoyed the comfy seats and clean bathrooms. I was happy with the comfy seats, ease on on/off and cleanliness.

Took the train from Paris Gare de Lyon to Barcelona in 6 hours 19 minutes.  It is quite a long journey but very civilised - comfortable seats, buffet car and wifi, along with great views along the way (more details of the journey can be found on the excellent seat61.com website).As an international train the announcements are given in French, Spanish and also English.A wide selection of things available from the buffet car, the usual sandwiches and cold things plus also a number of hot dishes. Photo of menu attached.A very civilised way of getting from A to B plus plenty of time to catch up on reading or in my case a number of episodes of the Crown I’d downloaded to my phone.One small point is that the overhead luggage racks are quite small, due to the fact these trains are double-deckers though there is plenty of space for cases as the ends of the carriages.Photos attached showing buffet menu (has English translations after the French and Spanish), the double-deck nature of the train, the view of Bezier’s 13th century cathedral taken from the train and an outside shot of the train at Barcelona showing the double decks.

Departure at 6:22 a.m. the air conditioning is on even though there is no need for it. It's almost cold in the car. Surprise, the toilets are devoid of soap... Paying for 1st class even for second class when there is no soap I find this deplorable. Positive points: - Comfortable seats - Sufficient space - Quiet
Yesterday We took the train from Pairis to Calais and there was No water,no elettricity for charge the phone,and no wifi...

I have recently travelled from Paris - Avignon - Lourde -Paris through TGV and overall experience was comfortable and worth for money paid. Lourde - Paris wifi service was excellent and easy to use. The train reached sharp on time though it was a 5 hours journey. I would recommend to book as early as possible before you travel date and get best rate !

The wifi is non-existent, my phone is well connected but it doesn't work. I don't understand the point of having air conditioning at 7 a.m. when even outside it's a little cold. The heatwave is over. I paid 45 euros for the trip to be really cold and have almost no internet. And I had to take the train at 6:30 in the morning to get this price since the others are not even affordable, impossible to sleep in this coolness. In short, please remove this air conditioning/ventilation when it is not hot outside.

I would like to remind everyone that the TGV is an SNCF train and deals with the Milan Porta Garibaldi - Modane route. The others, the Thellos, are from Trenitalia and obviously they don't get anything right with the TGV

The overall experience was a comfortable journey, but it didn’t start that way.  We were told we could sit anywhere so we did.  Only to have someone 10 minutes later we were sitting in their seat.  So we moved trying to figure out where to sit, so it didn’t happen again.  After a short while we spotted a small spot above the seats that indicated which seats were vacant or reserved.  This would have saved us some embarrassment if there was a staff member that could have explain how it all worked instead of just saying sit anywhere.  From there the trip was comfortable and was on time.  This is a great affordable way to travel in France.

We spent 75 euros each one to go from Aix en Provence to Paris. We were supposed to go in a high velocity train, but we didn't. The official version is because of the fire, but actually they didn't have any kind of organization. They just got more than 800 people with no train and we had to go back to Marseille with no seats because the train was much smaller than the number of passengers!About the time that we were supposed to arrive to Paris, we hadn't arrived to Lyon even!!!FINALLY ARRIVED WITH 4 HOURS DELAYED.So problem wasn't the fire, was the fact that they took us around the whole France in a train that wasn't faster than 100 km/h.When we arrived to Paris we stopped 20min in the airport before going to the Gare de Lyon (the station) and before arriving to the Gare they stopped again 15min because of the circulation. We took half an hour to make less than 10km.When we arrived some people asked where could we make a complaint and the workers where saying on kind words something like "it's late and it's not our business, go to wherever tomorrow and complain tomorrow".No email from the company, the train on the app wasn't canceled as it was (on the internet it was like if nothing had just happened!).So the worst experience that I've ever have in a train, has been with this company in France, from Aix en Provence to Paris.

Very comfortable & relaxing - great way to travel rural France. We went to Avignon & back.Only downside is lack of space for big cases as people put small cases in luggage rack when there are other options. It is impossible to lug big cases upstairs. Fix that .........and it is world class & beats airlines hand down

What a stress to take the train... never on time (no more chance of winning the Euromillion jackpot), random wifi, crappy phone application (you're still on the train late so it tells you that you've arrived...). And even in the toilets there is always something missing (water, paper, hand dryer or all 3). Frankly, it's an ordeal to have to take the train... privatize all that for me and where's the competition...
The TGV was fairly crowded although the seating was reasonably comfortable.  The best part about it was that it was quick.  Loved the sensation of traveling over the ground at 300 plus kph.

We really enjoyed our experience of travelling on the TGV as we don't get to travel by trains at home, and certainly not ones as fast as this!  As this trip was part of a post-river cruise visit to Paris, the tickets had been reserved ahead for the small group of us, luggage was handled for us, and we had someone accompanying us to the station, assisting us to find the right train, seats, etc, so all went smoothly.  The first class cabin was roomy and comfortable, reclining seats.  WiFi was fine.  The train moved so quickly we could barely enjoy the passing landscape! The train left and arrived on time. I gather from looking at the prices of tickets at the station that they are a bit pricey.  Certainly convenient to arrive right in the middle of Paris!

I travelled with my wife with tgv from frankfurt to paris est on the 19th morning . I book 1st class 3 months ago. On the wagon most of travellers were quiet but there was a family with 3 kids that did not stop to cry from the begining of the journey until the end (almost 4 hours) . I beleive that is a mistake from the company s site to allow small children to travel 1st as most of the travellers were business travellers heading for work and needed quiet. Other from that the trip was good the train was very fast going at some point up to 295 km per hour the time i noticed and arrived in paris on scheduled time. I will use again tgv on my next trip to europe .

These new cars are of very unequal quality. Go to second. We only had a small suitcase and a backpack. No more places in the luggage racks. The small backpack does not fit in the overhead racks. If you leave the luggage in the aisles because you cannot do anything with it, a dragon arrives and threatens you with a fine of 150 euros. Return to first, same problem for the luggage. The seats in second are unimaginably uncomfortable. Two hours of travel and I was good for a session at the osteo. Back to first grade. A little more space but the arch in the lumbar area is terribly unpleasant... 60 euros of osteoarthritis to be expected in addition to the price of the ticket.
First class travel at a price, very comfortable, and on time.  Recommended, but on the pricey side if you are traveling with a group requiring multiple tickets.
Unfortunately, all that remains is to take the PLANE or the carNo Train possible today by trainIn FranceNeither Ouigo Nor InouiReturn the old TGVs, much more comfortable Please...

The online booking with seat reservation worked easily. The train was comfortable and on time. The only thing that was a bit tedious was changing from one train station to another in Paris using the metro. Conclusion: TGV is significantly better than Air France - I've had problems with that in recent years. The staff at TGVIST was also much friendlier than the staff at AIR France.

I often travel the Milan-Nice route and unfortunately I use this train. I decided to write to the newspapers! It is no longer possible to stay silent. This line is a rip-off! Three-hour delays very often. Two times out of three. Let's leave aside the dirt and the state of the trains. But at least arrive on time....Please let's unite. It is not possible to accept such treatment. IT IS OFFENSIVE

We took the TGV from Paris Lyon to Avignon TGV. We had no problems and the 3 hours went by quickly. The train itself was quite comfortable. Taking trains in Europe are always a scramble ... especially with luggage...this was not too painful.

When traveling from Avignon TGV station to Paris. I got a first class seat, so when I waited on the platform as instructed, the train that came in late showed a completely different car number. I panicked and ran to the last car, but this time I couldn't find the seat number. It seems that the train I was supposed to ride on was thinned out and ended up with a later train. Thanks to that I was able to sit on the door step until I got to the next station. There is France. I guess it can't be helped...

Personally, I had really high expectations. The seats are comfortable, like an old American car, and the seat width and cushion are like an American car.The reclining is also comfortable.It's different from the Japanese Shinkansen.If anything, it felt like a Kintetsu express train, but it was fun.

I take the thello 4/5 times a month, having an office in Savona. The service is poor, carriages often not very clean, smelly bathrooms, perpetually late. In the last 3 round trips, average delay 38 minutes each way. But does this seem normal to you? Today we are in a carriage with bad AC, hot, crowded, and more than half an hour late! LONG LIVE THELO, LONG LIVE US PASSENGERS WHO PAY TO TRAVEL IN A CATTLE CAR!

We had pre booked for the grand journey of 500 km to be completed in four hoursWe were quite early to arrive at Gard e Lyon and waited in a huge areaAt 1005 the train platform was announcedAfter swiping all four tickets we entered the coach 15 and took our reserved seatsWe had just 4 stops in betweenWe started at 10/26 am as plannedSoon the Paris city was behind us and we started enjoying the lunch green land outside A bar a restaurant a play area and a crèche is all offered in same trainThe fastest speed was 305 kmph that time

I purchased a ticket for 10/07. Due to the landslide, my train was canceled but at Garibaldi station I found the assistance staff very helpful in giving us all the necessary information and alternative solutions to continue my journey the next day. Not being able to blame anyone other than Mother Nature, I thank these guys who were smiling, thoughtful and extremely kind to us travellers. An event like this certainly won't stop me from returning to the Tgv!

Had a terrible service. Sat on thalys and sat on right seat number but the wrong cabin as I turned right instead of left. Got a nasty reaction and fined an amount nearly same as what I paid for ticket. Terrible and they refused to listen.

SNCF has the WORST customer service EVER!!! Not helpful at all!!!I booked 2 TGV tickets from Paris to Tours and 2 bus Tickest from Trous to Paris through their website, I received a cancellation email after the money was already withdrawn from my account!!! After several emails and several attempts to contact them, NO cooperation AT ALL from their side although I have proof!!! This is called a theft!!! SHAME on them!!!

We were in the first-class top. The air was not working and they could have cared less. We were going from Paris to Barcelona. It was dangerously hot. Some of the other cars were cool but everyone in our car was dripping with perspiration. Rent a car and drive or fly. Stay off these trains. We got off at the first stop, my granddaughter passed out. She just needed cooling down which I did by lying her on the cool tile floor and pouring water on her. A stop was Valencia and no one there was helpful either. I have heard that the Parisians don't like American well I believe it now. The car rental people at the train stop just pretended to not understand English and wouldn't even check if cars were available downtown. My son and his smartphone found a car downtown and we drove rest of trip. The people in town were very helpful.

I had planned a trip with the TGV for August 3rd. Since it was not my travel destination and therefore I would then have to change to another train, I had already planned everything. Yesterday, by pure chance, I discovered that trains were canceled until August 15th. Now I wonder if I hadn't looked, what would have happened to me... After numerous requests for assistance, he finally answers me. He tells me that I will be reimbursed with a deduction of €5/ticket. (As per normal cancellation) because the trains "COULD" run that day (but then who knows...) Now I have requested a refund, given away €20 and who knows if I will see the remainder again. Never again TGV. the seriousness underfoot.

From Tuesday 2 July 2019 the Milan-Paris TGV line is interrupted due to a landslide on the route, until the end of July. For years, tickets can only be purchased online, so SNCF had our contact details but we were informed of the cancellation of trains only 2 days before departure. However, having found the news online in real time, we had already gone to the Milan-Porta Garibaldi station where a couple of SNCF staff were present only a few tens of minutes before the departure of the trains, to inform of a (possible, not certain) single daily train-coach service, but with no guarantee of return!! They were pushing for a refund request. Luckily we were able to move the holiday, but many tourists, especially foreigners, were in a panic because they didn't know anything about it. We asked for a refund (attention: NOT on the sncf.com website, as their email indicates, but on oui.sncf). Naturally, while the debit was made in real time, I have now already been waiting for 48 hours for the credit.

If i could give -10 i would . This is the first negative review i have ever written but sitting on the floor for the entire paris to Brussels train ride has me soo pissed off. After paying €69 for a seat on the train, given a ticket with  a seat number that morning, arriving to the station to find no information on where my train was, asked multiple people and was told to board the other train that was leaving at the same time. Got to that train and was told that i didnt have a seat and to wait until everyone else had boarded and hopefully get a seat because my train was cancelled. So guess what no seats availiable and im sitting on the floor and im not the only one. No communication from staff at all. Would  rather pay extra and pay for baggage to fly or even the bus than go with thalys again.

I purchased tickets for the TURIN TO PARIS route....trip planned down to the smallest detail for the summer holidays with the family. 2 days before departure I receive an email informing that the train for both the outward and return journeys has been cancelled. For 2 days I have had no assistance or support regarding the amount to be reimbursed or in any case reconverted to make another route. Nothing at all...truly scandalous....at the time of purchasing the tickets, the money is taken in a second... when there is a need for assistance, some people don't show up.

I took the TGV at least 4 times this past month - starting from CGV all the way West to Bretagne.  For the most part, the trip was uneventful.  The train departed on time and arrived on time.  However, the 3-star is for the 3 hour track issue outside of LeMans with all the information just in French -- very typical French.  And the abhorrent supposedly world-class TGV station at CGV that had no AC and no free toilets -- very stereotypical French.  And oh, the WiFi didn't always work which is consistent w/ the lowly Amtrak that we have at home.  As of this writing, I'm still waiting on my reimbursement from OUI.sncf for the failed trip to Rennes as a result of the 3-hour track issue.  I'm not holding my breath due to the laissez-faire attitude of the French.
We had a great trainride incl breakfast served on train 1. class. Merci beaucoup to our train attemdant !

Unfortunately, due to so much luggage, I was forced to take this train, from Paris to Milan, Porta Garibaldi. After 2 hours of travel, they let us off (after waiting for almost an hour) to take another train: infernal heat between June and July 2019. People getting off from one train to another with relative discomfort and crowds. Delay of an hour and a half. No wifi and non-working sockets. If it weren't for the company, it would have been more horrible than it already was! Never again... Obviously I don't recommend it.

High Quality transport, European quality and security. Fast and Safe, reliable. Scan the deals and for only 6 euros you might have a Premium Class. I am frequent traveller on the Eurostar and Thalys and proud to travel on this unique European Project. Go to London, Amsterdam, Brussels, Paris and the South of France faster then taking a plane.

Hi! I agree with Hongkong8787; don't even bother trying to email SNCF TGV inoui; they don't email you back, even if you write in French. My issue was finding out if I had to pay an extra 5 euros for my suitcase(because their website said so) but my French ami kindly called them and confirmed that you can bring 1 suitcase for yourself without any extra charge. It was very easy to clarify over the phone verbally.  OUIGO was better; at least you can pay the extra 5 euros online(they say if you pay at the station it's 20 euros) through OUIGO. OUIGO had small, crampy trains though. There are NO announcements in English AT ALL so unless your French listening skills are up to par it can be difficult to travel. No one helps you either. They are eager to say 'I don't speak English'(whether they can or not), SLAMMING the door of communication shut. You'll be lucky if you don't get pushed around. In the US everyone says excuse me or sorry when they come in proximity; I only heard one lady say 'Pardon'(after she had nugged/pushed me 5 times, I am not kidding), the rest, none. Do not be surprised (esp if you are coming from the US) with the INTRUSION of personal space. And don't forget your wee-wee money at the toilets in the station; 80 centimes.

We booked 1st class tickets for our family travelling from Paris to Milan after flying from Australia. The cost was quite high but it was my 50th birthday so we thought let’s treat ourselves to something special As soon as we arrived at the train station we could see the taxi drop off area was a shambles. Cars lined up 3 to 4 wide and our taxi was unable to get anywhere near the entrance When we entered the train station the heat was unbearable.  The place looked and felt like a giant glasshouse. Do they not have air conditioning?? We then lined up at our gate and asked the employee where our carriage was or was there a number we need to look for? We were abruptly told “over there”. We had to figure out which one of 20 carriages was ours with zero signage or assistance. We thought we found it and took our seats only to be told by a rather unpleasant passenger that we were sitting in their seat.  After 20 minutes of searching we were told by a railway employee to get on our carriage before the train departs and at this stage they actually took us to it. Upon entering we could see our seats were taken and no polite request was going to move the passengers from our seats. A train employee entered and said seat numbers don’t matter and take whichever seat you want. To top it off we arrived in Milan 1.5 hours late Will fly next time
Travelled from Amsterdam to Brussels with no issues or concerns. Comfortable train with amble storage for baggage.

Traveled from Amsterdam to Brussels with no issues. The train was on time and it was easy to find our carriage and seats. The train was air conditioned, the seats were comfortable and there was limited (250mb) free wifi which enabled some basic email checking and a few websites. I ran out of my limit about 3/4 if the way through the trip but that was ok. No food or drink was provided but this was expected as per the ticket we purchased. We would happily travel with Thalys again in the future.

Boarding took place 10 minutes before departure, despite the request made to us to come 30 minutes in advance. 20 minutes before boarding the trains were not ready and we did not have access to the platforms on the pretext that it is “cooler” down there. Despite having paid 20€ there was barely space for our luggage, our suitcases were placed in another car. No possibility to buy food or drinks on board even though it is a 6 hour journey. Don't take these trains, go somewhere else!!!
Terrible customer service due to a monopoly situation. Inconsistent internal communication (station loudspeakers, SNCF agents, website, complaints service, etc.). Hope that changes one day.

I used it from Rennes Station to Montparnasse Station and from Paris Gare de l'Est to Strasbourg Station. Both are second class seats. I made a reservation from Japan. The interior of the train is much smaller than the Japanese Shinkansen. The seats are in two rows and two rows, but both the parlor and the aisle felt cramped. There was a space to put your suitcase, but since most people use it, it was also placed in the aisle. Next time I would like to use the first class seat.

Travelling from Paris to Geneva.  What a rude and obnoxious way to treat passengers.  It's probably ok for people who know how your system works but for everyone best of luck to you.  There is zero service anywhere except one lousy obnoxious attempt from one lady on the train platform who waved us down towards the end of the train because we couldn't find our carriage.  Why couldn't we find our carriage?  Because they aren't numbered.  Carriage 15 is miles away and with my mother in tow with mobility issues and 2 large suitcases between us we barely made it with no time to spare, these trains don't give a hoot if you're on or not and neither does this company.  Between TVG and Gare De Lyon station our experience was stressful and awful.  I do not recommend this company for anyone with mobility or requires assistance of any shape or form cause they don't care in the slightest. And wifi doesn't work either.  Well done on delivering some of the worst customer service ever, you must be so proud.

I thank the French bar clerk who refused to heat up ready-made baby food for an 8-month-old baby, making him continue to cry. I have traveled half the world, but the rudeness and arrogance of these people found on this train has exceeded all limits. Unfortunately there are no words to describe what happened, but at least I hope that our described experience can be of help to those who are thinking of taking the TGV with newborn children.

This opinion does not concern the train itself, but the SNCF and in particular that of La Rochelle...Shameful..!.My wife, 74 years old, and myself, 75 years old, experienced an SNCF episode that unfortunately many other users suffering from age had to experience as well: After a long 11-hour air journey, arrival at 6 a.m. at Roissy; recovery of the 2 hold suitcases of 20 and 21kg (let's add the cabin baggage of 10 and 12kg). - complete crossing of Charles de Gaulle Roissy to access (without trolley) the platform nominated for the destination Poitiers for the TGV...Arrival in Poitiers for a change of train - (wait 2 hours)..here is our TER (no reservable seats) which will take us through the Niort countryside and charentaise to La Rochelle...and there, a new nightmare: two platforms separate us from the station exit and above all two infamous staircases going down then up: the suitcases suffer on steps devoid of "levelling tracks" (filling the gaps between steps). Faced with our difficulty and our near helplessness in rolling and carrying this luggage, only a young girl of around twelve years old will come to our aid (let us thank her again). this did not seem to concern him..! In addition: outward journey La Rochelle - Roissy: TGV 80e for two people. - return journey: Tgv Roissy-Poitiers then Ter Poitiers-La Rochelle: 160e for two people. Goodbye SNCF, from now on we will use the Greater Region Buses.

Allianz train delay insurance, cost: €12, reimbursement: €10 I took out this insurance for a TGV Avignon/Paris trip. The contract clearly specifies that this insurance is made for a train delay greater than 30 minutes on departure and 1 hour on arrival. My train was 2 hours late at departure (2h05mns at arrival). I absolutely had to be on time, so I took another train ticket believing that I was insured! After several emails and phone calls to Allianz, I finally got a refund of €10 for an insurance cost of €12. I call it THEFT, so flee Allianz: KING OF SCAM.
We were attracted by the prices which were very attractive but the journey was really not pleasant, the carriage dirty, people on top of each other, luggage everywhere..

We used this train which is really very fast and relatively comfortable. It is clear that the carriages and seats are old, but preserved.... I recommend arriving in advance to carry out the boarding process calmly. The internal bar has a good variety of food and drinks. Another tip is if you have a lot of luggage, be well positioned in the place where your carriage will stop to place your luggage first because some compartments are small.
Great trip, much better then dealing with airports. View is great from the top deck. 1st class is worth the extra money.

Travel from Bordeaux to Poitiers in 1st class. There is no justification for paying a 1st class fare because the cleanliness in the cars leaves something to be desired. Worn seats and armrests. Dirty cup holders. Let's not talk about the toilets. A shame.  Nothing to do with the cleanliness of trains in Japan for example. Too bad for a big country like France. It's time to privatize the SNCF

Narrow seats, high price but worse than anything is that there’s no customer service. They don’t seem to care about customers. Our train was cancelled, we were told to move to a different train and nothing else. There is no information available, no air conditioning. There is no train number anywhere and no one to help. We do not know at what time we will departure or arrive. My first and certainly last SNFC trip.

Paris Gare de LyonDelay announced of 30 minutes. Come on, let's be patient, the journey has only just begun :-|The train left without us and other disciplined travelers: we were waiting for the track number to be displayed in front of the big size screen, but it was never displayed. INADMISSIBLE!!!!We had to buy full price tickets. Special thought for the student in the same problem, who could not make up for it... Used to trains and planes, this is the first time I have seen such management! I inform travelers thanks to the screens but only half: delay but no track number! You shouldn't exaggerate!

I took the paris to stuttgart train earlier this week and was happy with the comfort and service. I was a bit surprised that 1st class tickets do not include food. the food is nice and cheap enough anyway but would have been a nice addition to the trip to have this included. charging points available at every table and the seats were very comfortable

The TGV is so comfortable and the speed of the journey really is something.However, the trip form Paris to Clisson cost me €200. As I said, the service is great but you could fly to two, maybe three countries for that much. I live in Ireland and yeah, the public transport isn't great and it can be expensive but this really knocked me back.

Following my first trip on an incredible train, in which I traveled in 1st, I am outraged, seat not very comfortable, dirty and dusty, design and color of the seats just horrible, (the impression of this found at Mami), corect reception bar a little more spacious than in a classic TGV the only positive point, unfortunately poor value for money.. I have just read an article which tells me that the project is to replace all the classic TGVs with its TGVs for me very low end knowing that I traveled in 1st I wonder what the 2nd looks like for this 300 million project? It's a joke, let's leave our good old tgv or the 1st and very pleasant, the 2nd also.. ah I almost forgot there's no wifi woupiii it doesn't work lol 😂. I can't stand the SNCF anymore, unfortunately I'm dependent on it.

Had an excellent ride on this iconic train for France. The tickets are available at a kiosk, ticket counter or on line. They can be linked to your phone or simply print them out. We rode in Class 1, your tickets are clearly marked what carriage and seat you have allocated. Heaps of rooms for suitcases and smaller one can go in the overhead. On time, efficient, clean and you can get snacks in the car.
We took TGV from Paris to Rennes, a distance of 220 miles. Then Regional bus to  mont St. Michele.It was great. We

Recently my wife and an other couple took the high speed train from Paris to Toulon. It was our first time using the train. It awesome...if you have never ridden a high speed train you should! We topped out at 296km/hr!!I booked tickets online from Canada and it was easy(I'm a bit of a techno-moron😁) and everything was perfect. The train was east to find at the Gare du Lyon in Paris using the information provided n the ticket. These people get it right and now i would not hesitate to use trains...we have ways rented car. The experience was one of several highlights of our trip. Seriously if you have never used the train you should try it.

We travelled from Paris to Bordeaux- the 1st class ticket which allowed us a quieter seating area. Wifi access was excellent and the food down table and charging option for your phone was great. Very clean and tidy. 👍🏼
I tried to book tickets from Strasbourg to Paris using a Visa and then a Mastercard. Both were declined but the money was still debited from my account. The customer service is refusing to help.

I'm absolutely not a train driver, so it's a new experience. Our train seemed a bit old-fashioned and wasn't exactly new. Nevertheless, everything worked and it was fascinating to cover the Strasbourg - Paris section non-stop in just under two hours. Thank you SNCF, thank you TGV. The return journey was with DB and ICE. Modern train, great seats, 20 minutes delay on arrival, air conditioning works (everyone had their coats on on the train), toilets completely closed in all carriages (flooding). Thank you Deutsche Bahn, thank you ICE.

I can't say whether the problem affects only my carriage (7) or not, but the famous free Wi-Fi is not present and the only socket present is not working. Bear in mind if you plan to spend the hours on board working....

We took Thalys from Amsterdam Central to Brussels Midi on Monday night. Our train was ontime. Staff were nice. Train was bit old. The ticket fare was way too expensive. Eurostar was definitely a lot better.

“Pan-fried shrimp” from chef XXX (its name is not worth remembering): tasteless, without salt too. Who are we kidding? The SNCF service provider does thunderous marketing. Its most expensive menu is, quite simply, dismal (except the dessert which is... ok).

Very old and poorly cleaned trains. I find it absurd that on Sundays there are only 2 timetables (trains without changes and therefore with shorter duration) to choose from. The service could definitely be improved.
Very good experience and good option for families. Offers reduced price for children. The prices are very competitive

I took the Thalys between Brussels and Paris 2 days in a row. The first day the train was 2.5 hours late and the second the train was simply canceled. Fortunately, the conductor of the 2nd day was exceptionally kind (train 9358 at 4:13 p.m. between Brussels midday and Paris).

Hello everyone, I rebel against this charade! All this cinema cc wifi in this high-speed train! Why spend so much money on this project with purely catastrophic results? I take this train often and I have never been able to have a connection worthy of the name. It is purely a shame to dare to offer this to travelers at the price of the ticket! Kind regards...

I took the TGV from Charles de Gualle Airport to Strasbourg, France, and from Basel, Switzerland to Gare de Lyon, Paris. Because the trip to Strasbourg was on Easter weekend, there were very few seats available, even though I purchased my tickets a week ahead of time. These tickets were very expensive. If you want to pay less, reserve your seats early! My tickets from Basel to Paris were purchased online 2 weeks before traveling. These were a very good price, but they were absolutely non-refundable if we missed our train. This could be stressful, so just plan ahead. The ride was smooth, easy, and comfortable on both occasions.

Recently travelled on the Thalys from Rotterdam to Paris.  Very comfortable seats with good room ( economy) , smooth ride, very quiet, clean facilities, power sockets to charge devices at your seat,  food good for a train, prices at the cafe/bar were good and the attendant very pleasant. Only negative was the WiFi had poor connectivity...  I dont know why train services bother to say they provide wifi as I have yet to encounter one that has any decent connection - airports too..!! We had an issue with our ticket which was bought online through SNCF from Eindhoven through to Paris while we were in Morrocco.  The website did not make it clear that the ticket could only be uplifted from a French railway station and as we could not access France due to air traffic controllers strike we had some difficulty  getting from Eindhoven (where we flew to )to Rotterdam and had to purchase two new tickets for this sector ( am claiming refund so fingers crossed) As the train from Eindhoven was a little late we had to go directly to the Thalys where the Train Manager was extremely helpful, confirming he had us booked and allowing us to board without printed tickets.  Could not have been more accommodating.  Top marks to the team onboard.

the train was on time ,  it is quite comfy , i did it on both line ( via Bordeau & Lyon) can get real good price booking online  at ouigo , just make sure to bring an off drinks & food for the ride as it is €2.50 for a small bottle of water .
the speed allowed us to visit "relatives" far away geographically, .... with added comfort, more risks on the roads, no more serious fatigue......

Damn it: riding this train is fun. We drove from Emmendingen (near Freiburg) to Paris in 2:58 hours, arriving to the minute, both there and home. It's MUCH MORE fun than flying, or even driving. A GREAT EXPERIENCE for the whole family, and very stress-free!
Recommended option. From Sants to Gare de Lyon in 5.5 hours. Very comfortable seats. Ideal for traveling with children. Beautiful landscapes. Great option.

We were waiting to start our quiet weekend... The train arrives at the station in Vercelli... it stops announcing the position of the first and second class... I head to get on... DOORS CLOSED!!! I try again insistently but nothing, the doors don't open and the very kind conductor immediately gives the starting signal...!! Moral frantic race to be opened without any sign... train that leaves without loading us... what can I say experience not to be repeated and money wasted...!! non-existent competence!!!

I paid twice as much for the same ICE trip here. It's on a weekday (Sunday return trip to Germany), but it's actually not worth the extra charge. The seats are comfortable, everything was clean, therefore average
There were two of us and we took the TGV from Bern to Paris. At 4.5 hours, this type of fishing is definitely preferable to a flight. Have fun!

We reserved online and everything went very well. On the outward journey we were in a four-person compartment, so we could choose who went forward and who went backwards, which was very good! However, on the return trip we had two rows. Both driving backwards, that was really annoying.

We took the TGV between Paris and Bordeaux and both trips were smooth. The staff are helpful and the trains were punctual. Seating is a bit cramped, in terms of legroom but otherwise comfortable. Toilets are clean

already used other times on the Milan/Paris route, this time I made a return trip from Milan/Lyon. Very punctual both on the outward and return journey and information on board also transmitted in Italian. However, the SNCF office at Porta Garibaldi station no longer exists. Some time ago I had received an advertising email in which there was talk of renewed trains, but I traveled on the ones I already knew, which were rather dated and with room for improvement (Frecce and Italo are of a higher level). Having the possibility to book well in advance you can find good rates. I spent, with outward journey 18/4 and return 22/4, a total of 330 euros for 3 people with a partially refundable or removable reservation (the non-changeable one was not available with which it would have been possible to spend less). I read about a user who is having difficulty getting a refund following a delay. Last year, for a 40 minute delay, I received a bonus of the expected amount valid for one year directly online and within 3/4 days; I remember that during the trip communications were issued numerous times reminding people of their right to compensation and how to request it. The only time a similar case happened to me with a Frecciarossa, I had to submit a formal complaint because at the counters they found that the delay had been 29 minutes and not 39 as detected not only by my watch and those of the station, but also by all the monitors on the carriage....

I have heard it from many people, Thalys is everything but reliable! If you have time enough that you can take the risk, will it go, will it not go ... that's the big question! The trains itself are also old and not as comfortable as what you may expect from such an expensive way of traveling! No food, no drinks ... although, for a ticket of almost 300 euros Brussels Paris and back I would expect a free drink! And on top of it, after waiting almost 90 minutes we finally left Paris! As good it was in the past, so bad is it today!

making this trip for the first time, the trip begins on time friends from the first stop at the TGV Lorraine station we are told of a problem on the previous TGV and a delay of one hour, an hour later we are told another hour and still no more explanations and no controller in sight, at least we are at the station and not in the open countryside. we arrive in Lille Europe 125 minutes late, no announcement on the platform, no controller or SNCF staff to welcome us. Sorry! Back home, I decided to complain to the SNCF who told me that because of this delay, I was reimbursed 50%. I then receive an email offering me a credit on a future purchase valid for 1 year (funny refund) I wrote asking for a REFUND, and I'm waiting to see the SNCF has not changed (apart from the name)

I have taken then THALYS a few times as to avoid airport delays and stress.  You do not avoid delays and stress by not using the airport systems.  Arrived into Amsterdam from Paris on a major delay due to “track maintenance” (on a holiday Sunday).  Literally sat on tracks more then moving.  Move 50kms, sit, move 50kms, sit, and on and on.  If this is normal they need to buffer in sit times in schedules.  From what I hear from colleagues this is not abnormal.   Very frustrating to pay what I paid to save time to see cars flying by you on the highway while your traveling at 25kph.
Hello, I took out missed departure insurance and my file was refused after several weeks of waiting. This is a scam, never take out this insurance.

We wanted to go to Le Havre Brest by train with our bicycles!! well it is impossible to leave together in the same train...because the sncf does not take more than three bicycles per tgv train.and to top it off when you book a trip on a ter he gives you a wagon without a hook to put the bicycle on "it's up to you to check with the conductor to have a place in the right wagon😈😈😈😈
As a tourist we took this train to experience the high speed train but the experience was not great as the the speed was average and doubted if it ever touched 150 KMPH.

Very good trip on the Inoui Paris Bordeaux tgv. The train was on time, taken, comfortable seat (in 2nd class) and restaurant car which offers quite a few choices and not bad at all! Friendly staff. Small downside, the wifi doesn't work very well.

Booked this train online through OUI.SNCF  with no issues. Took the TGV SNCF train from Brussels Midi Station to Disneyland Paris. Somewhat confusing to figure out what coach to get on. I think there was an extra number. However I found it and boarded with my luggage. Have to find a spot where it fits. It was around a two hour train ride.  It was crowded however I had a comfortable seat and the ride was great. Arrive at Marne-la-Vallee Chessy, walk out of the train station and your at Disneyland Paris.
We did Geneva - Paris in less than 3 hours. Very comfortable, with bar car and landscapes of the French countryside. I recommend.

During a business trip from Aix to Paris, my partner and I had the opportunity to test the new TGV Ouigo formula. It was so atrocious that I swore to recount this experience here. It is clear that there has been a deplorable disappearance of customer services (or withdrawal of their free services) for a ticket price which has not fallen! Total scam. Here are a few examples: no luggage rack in the wagon, external luggage racks for a fee (!), disappearance of the reading light beams above the seats (!!!), no individual trash can at the seats (we are now doing the job of the maintenance workers by carrying our own waste to the outdoor trash bin), reduced size of the shelves in front of the seats, disappearance of the magazine nets, very noisy wagons (howling babies, very poorly behaved customers who chatter very loud, who answer the telephone as if they were at home, who park in the central corridor, therefore impossible to read or rest even with earplugs), choice of quiet carriages made for a fee (!!!!!), disappearance of free sockets near the seats, no bar to admire the landscape and chat...Here is a MAGISTRAL FAILURE of the SNCF for which the customer pays at great expense. Next time, we will travel by plane while waiting for the welcome opening to competition from this Soviet company with totalitarian methods.

We had a good trip on the TGV and also the SNCF part as well. The only problem is the getting down from the platform which is very bad for people with a walking mobility problem. the other problem is that getting from one station in Paris in the required time can be a bit of a problem due to lack of taxis. We just made our connection with 11 minutes to spare. we would still use the service as it makes it easier to travel long distances.

First time on a TGV and it was pretty good, although the toilet was something to be avoided!! Wider seats than the UK but the WIFI still dodgy....... Good views from the top deck as you are quite high up and the speed is great gets you to where you want to go quickly and quietly.A few delays to be fair but this didnt make me late.

Since the TGV takes just over 2 hours from Paris to Bordeaux, we never fail to take the train, thus avoiding having to take the car. It completely changes our life, especially since we know that we can travel in very safe conditions.

If you are hoping to be able to get a refund thanks to Allianz travel's refund/cancellation insurance, you are wrong. By reading the contract more carefully (3-4 hours of reading) you will realize that your case is not taken into account by the insurance (regardless of the reason). As a student, classes were moved and I had to cancel my tickets. After 1 week of looking for all the documents requested by the insurance company, they sent me a brief email saying "no, we will not reimburse". For what ? because it said "Refundable for cancellation or rescheduling of """leave"""" and not "vacation".One case among many others...In short, a shame...

I enjoyed my ride from Charles De Gaulle airport to Marseille on TGV first class seating.  The price of first class was only a few Euros more than second class. I had a separate window seat, it was wide enough and reclined slightly for a comfortable position.   The French countryside is pretty to view and good for taking pictures.  There are a few stops along the way, main one is in Lyon.  It is a big city famous for food.   The conductor does come once to check for tickets.  What is interesting is that the was no one to check tickets past Lyon.   The compartment  basically emptied after the Lyon stop.   I noticed many passengers just come and take the first best seat.   So, it may be that the train is open seating past certain stations.   The station in Marseille is right downtown, close to all the attractions.  One can walk to the old port and have a nice lunch.   It seemed possible that if one had around 11 hours transit in Paris and the times were right, one can chance a trip to Marseille during this time, take the hop on hop off bus in Marseille and be back for the flight from CDG.
how disgusting, 3 hours late and I can't get a refund, they wrote to me that they will reply within 30 days?

Getting to Mont Saint Michel is easier than you think. The arrival time was accurate, and I was surprised at how polite the signs on the train were compared to those in Japan, such as being 5 minutes late. The fares for 1st and 2nd class are not that different, so I recommend 1st class for Japanese people. I think it has a warmer feel than the inorganic Japanese Shinkansen.
The counters close one after the other in the Paris region, the Gare de Lyon ticket store is always full, we must thank Monsieur Pipi for his vision on SNCF services.

Impossible to travel with your bike not dismantled! And what do we do if we go hiking for several days? Why not provide a car for all the bikes or a place in each car with hooks to hang the bikes from the ceiling...as is done on many trains?

Sometimes we use high-speed TGVs. This time we made a round trip from Paris to Reims in second class. Right on time. Fast - 50 minutes. Comfortable. The seats are comfortable. The high-speed train runs smoothly and softly. A pleasure.

Excellent value for money, comfortable TGV, quite clean...apart from a tablet full of coffee stains...the only downside is the lack of contact, no one passes on the train, checks are carried out on the platform before boarding and a bag is provided for the waste there. There is only a small bin at the entrance to the carriage...

I traveled on the TGV from Paris to Italy, and then returned on the TGV Lyria.  In both cases, the journey itself was quite nice - beautiful scenery, helpful staff, large wheelchair spaces and lifts for easy access between the platform and the train.  However, booking the tickets ahead was very difficult.  Because I was traveling between different countries, I could not book wheelchair spaces online.  But when I called the provided number to make my booking, I was told that they did not accept American credit cards other than American Express (which I don’t have).  The “English line” also presented a language barrier, with a worker who could speak English but not quite enough for her job requirements.  I was able to get around this difficulty by contacting an acquaintance in Paris who was able to call and purchase tickets on my behalf.  However, that is not an option open to everyone, and the TGV booking system is sadly unequipped to handle international wheelchair users who want to book international journeys in advance.  I’d also note that the wheelchair booking system opens a few weeks later than the regular booking system, which prevents wheelchair users from taking advantage of the cheapest advance fares.

Did a hassle-free booking at Trainline’s website from Morges-GVA-Gare de Lyon-Lausanne-Morges. Departed Morges on Friday around 7:48pm and arrived Paris around 11:00pm.The ride was smooth with no issues. Better option than flying as I arrived in 10mins to the Latin Quarter.

This is more about the website, it is very easy to use and book the train tickets. Exactly 3 months prior to the date booking open with discounted price. The ouigo trains cost 1/3 of other trains and one can book extra luggage for mere 5 euros. So the luggage problem gets solved.     Remember our can pay only with some countries issued credit cards .This information you don’t get on website.  Otherwise it takes you through all way to final payment and shows payment failure. Go through the pics down which provides list of credit cards from the countries issued are listed.

Paris Toulouse in a little over 4 hours, a real progress except that the new tgv which is unheard of as the name is a lie, is even in first class uncomfortable: the non-ergonomic seat seems to have been designed to create back pain! When booking on the site: ask for a high room window and you find yourself in a low room Isolated in the first car.. this half-room in the basement looks more like a pile of seats than a first class carriage! Long live the Paris Marseille tgv: space and comfort Why invent new trains to the detriment of passenger comfort when those already designed provide satisfaction. It's good advertising and marketing but not to the detriment of the SNCF's missions which is to transport passengers in good condition! And the icing on the cake, train stopped in the middle of the countryside! In short, the SNCF must evolve but not to the detriment of its users and by increasing prices!
A bar in the back for passengers over 1.75 m tall. The power socket/USB box with protruding angles designed to catch passengers' knees....Avoid the new incredible trains while there is still time!!!

Train not comfortable, you can't straighten the seat backs which in my opinion are too tilted, impossible to have a coffee on board when you cross the border, also drunk English people in the bar, disgusting toilet, oasis of water to wash your hands, so I only had to stay there for two and a half hours to go through the controls..... Now I find myself stuck in London czr all (??) The trains are apparently full to bursting for all the week?? I'm going home by bus.....

238 Euros (or dollars) for the Paris to Chamonix trip is too much.(1) Was I charged TWICE when I called to simply change the day of departure and the agent cancelled, then rebooked me?(2) They assigned me to a seat... BUT, I was never given a choice to ride (a) in the upper level coaches with a view, or, (b) closer to the "food" car... Perhaps not so important, but not given the choice.(3) In general, modern planes and trains provide announcements in at least two languages: the non-TGV train for the last segment of the journey certanly did.Why can't the TGV be bothered to be modern?(3a) Also, why couldn't the TGV employee be bothered to direct me in the correct direction back to my seat (from standing in a long food line two cars away) even after looking at my ticket?First class? Not by any standard I've ever experienced. In general, the TGV ride I looked forward to for so long was a disappointing sub-standard trip.To add insult to mediocrity by being charged 238 for it is absurd.I wish my interaction with TGV had lived up to the hype and promises of its video advertising.It absolutely does not.

Cannot believe the state of the amenities on the French trains. The toilets were absolutely disgusting. Eurostar was fine from London but after that went down hill. Went to Switzerland, back into Paris and up to Lille and return. We paid extra for first class so hate to think what they were like in economy ...windows filthy ..whilst I prefer this train travel after a long haul flight I would not use them again.

This week I went to Paris by train for the first time, previously I always went by plane. In terms of costs, it is certainly much cheaper than a flight, but in terms of duration (perhaps depending on where you need to be in Paris), slightly less. But the peace and quiet of simply boarding and being able to stay in the heart of Paris, but also being able to sit comfortably during the journey and also being able to work well (excellent WiFi) certainly makes it interesting. However, the experience of the Thalys is outdated....I was in 1st class Comfort on the way there and 1st Premium on the way back. The seats are spacious but cannot be adjusted very well, the upholstery/color scheme looks quite 1980s. In Comfort you just have to go to the restaurant where there is a reasonable range of drinks, snacks and snacks, but it all seems very 'cheap'. The toilets were also a bit dingy. In Premium, the offer is actually not worth it. The food is just mediocre and the service without any class (EasyJet has even more charisma). Too bad, because for the tired business traveler, a little bit of comfort is just that extra thing that could make the Thalys really interesting. I'm now considering flying economy again.

A good 45 minutes of waiting at the bar for a coffee is still excessive!!! With a waitress of unspeakable friendliness who seems to have nothing to do with customers - oh sorry users - waiting for a long time and archaic equipment to make the coffees (she doesn't have any help!), this is the result!!! Fortunately we are going on vacation and we are relaxed!!!! But what the hell!!!! It’s pitiful!!!

Disappointed by the comfort of 1st class of this incredible generation - hard seats, no room for legs, a mini tablet just enough to put your phone on... the only positive point is the friendliness of the captain!

What to say? An unpleasant journey from start to finish. In the end, the feeling of having been ripped off with these low-cost tickets and ready to pay more to no longer travel in these conditions. The train is not that different from regular trains. BUT:- Absolutely messy boarding....an endless queue in an isolated Gare de Lyon hall, travelers in panic. In the end we do not understand why a low-cost implies such rotten boarding given that it requires SNCF staff and that the train leaves on the platforms of Hall 1....accompanists are not allowed: women with strollers, elderly people are not entitled to be accompanied by a loved one to the train. You can imagine the panic....On board: normal comfort, although the cleanliness leaves something to be desired. You have to put your luggage under your seat otherwise you have to pay (nonsense or even a scam). A horrible jingle that makes you jump every hour. A flight attendant who wakes you up (even though he sees that you are sleeping) by asking you for your trash....I regret the early tickets. In short, ouigo maybe works when you go outside of school holidays, when you are young and without children. Otherwise, it's better to forget!

Paris - Geneva by business class TGV. But who are we kidding??? More amateur than this performance, it’s not possible! Friendly but incompetent staff, absolutely mediocre cuisine, only passable wines. We dreamed of a moment with a minimum of attention but what a disappointment. Everything needs to be reviewed or better removed, this service which is a bad joke. Do not take this class during this trip!!!

Departure 6:30 a.m. from Lyon Depart arrival scheduled for 8:30 a.m. in Massy. It’s 1:28 p.m. we’re still on the TGV. It’s incredible like the train!!! Long live the sncf. I'm not even talking about the flight that we had to take at 11:20 a.m. obviously the plane is already far away the next one scheduled for tomorrow at 11:20 a.m. is 24 hours late 🤮🤮🤮

Do not take out insurance on the SNCF site with Allianz, they process files as follows: incomplete file, file being processed then file closed...it lasts weeks or months if you want to fight.  Everything is tied up so that the customer abandons and is not reimbursed. This is what I did after spending a lot of time with obviously bad people who were very well trained to make the subscriber give up.

For the first time I took the TGV Turin/Paris and I chose first class to have the best. The carriages are old and run down, armrests detached, two lights burnt out. Toilet without toilet paper and with faulty flushing. Cold air from the slits under the windows (c'est normal, the controller told us...). There is no Wi-Fi!!!  Fairly varied catering service, served at your seat, acceptable prices. No restaurant car, just a rather poor bar. "Technical" stops caused a 40 minute delay. Everything the same as the return, except that it arrived on time.

The SNF has therefore obviously decided to transform the TGV experience into an incredible ordeal for its customers. Surprising! But why so much hatred? Already boarding at Montparnasse station: obligation to use hall 1. Renovated at great expense, the rents must be visibly profitable (or at least made to believe in a greater possibility of income for the tenants). No more question of going through hall 2. So, obligation to use a hall less accessible by car, with many more people, where it is difficult to move around, ... in short, gone is the calm and tranquility of hall 2 (which in addition, arrived in the middle of the train, and therefore did not require running all the way along the 2 trains to reach your carriage). Ultimately, it is mainly the discomfort of the seats that is unheard of. Indeed, for these trains: - If you are in a lower room, surprise, there is no consistency in the numbering of seats. Example: seats 24 and 26 are each on the opposite side of the wagon even though their numbering suggests that they should be close to each other. It's complicated to find your place peacefully with this numbering worthy of Kafka! - The space allocated to luggage in these trains has been further reduced: it was already insufficient in previous versions, it's worse now: installation of recycling bins which take the place of suitcases, storage area reduced to a minimum in the carriage (towards the end). All this to increase the number of seats? Isn't the TGV supposed to transport people traveling for several days and therefore with suitcases? Why not have corrected the problem rather than accentuate it? - So, the SNCF implemented a brilliant idea: storing your luggage under your seat. An idea that may seem excellent, but once again, it is the comfort of the passengers that suffers. Under your seat means in front of the feet of the passenger in front of you. Result for this passenger: impossible to extend his legs. He finds himself in a constrained position often unable to move his feet. - Once seated, one could say that this is enough. Well no. Obviously, the SNCF has designed a seat for passengers up to 1m75 tall. I'm 1m80 and I find myself with the headrest of the seat in my shoulder blades (curiously, in the previous version of the layout, the headrest was well positioned, but it must have been too comfortable for the passengers). This might not necessarily be a big problem, but this headrest is harder than the seat back and especially shifted a few cm forward. Result: I find myself in a position where it is impossible to have my upper back straight. Mandatory bent position. And presto, a good back and neck pain upon arrival in addition to knee pain. Did the designers of these seats test them before their implementation? What does SNCF intend to do to remedy this problem? Answer: nothing, we don't care, because our trains are more comfortable as we tell you so in our advertisements. So the SNCF promises a much more comfortable journey, but has ultimately put in place all the ingredients to ruin the journey for its customers. But what is the objective of such a strategy? Especially with the price of the journey (Paris – Rennes) increasing!

We've been riding fast transfer decades in Europe. The TGV was a pioneer in genuine high speed and by now they've been at it a long time. The standard speed is 186 miles per hour, but that's been true for a long time. Some trains routinely go 200 mph or a bit more if the track ahead is clear of other trains.We took the TGV Duplex from Paris to Lyon for a three night side trip. Our journey time from the Gare de Lyon in Paris to Lyon was 2 hours. The Duplex is a two level train with an upstairs and downstairs. Either is great and comfortable.The trains are usually made up of two power units and 10 trailers. That was the case for our train to Lyon. and that provides for  passenger load of about 600 passengers. Coming back to Paris, we watched them couple two such trains together, opening the noses of two power units to connect them. So our train capacity was about 1,200 passengers. They routinely adjust the train lengths this way to accommodate peak travel. The double level train has only about 4 percent more wind drag than a single level. As for stability, you can read and write or hold a drink or leave a glass of win on the table in front of you on either level. We've done this on trains all over France. A TGV Duplex set a world speed record for a commercial train on steel wheels in 2007 of 357.2 miles per hour. The train was specially prepared for the record run and it had only three trailers - but that is very fast. The system could tolerate more speed and would not require major modifications. But there is a point where significantly higher speeds would increase maintenance requirements. The French have determined that current speeds are okay as things are. But they are continually adding capacity and higher speeds can help relieve traffic. We've taken high speed trains in Spain (the largest high speed network in Europe), in Italy (where they're about to begin operating high speed freight rail). in Germany and the Eurostar from London St. Pancras through the Chunnel to Paris and to Brussels. My wife's work before she retired frequently required her to be in the UK and France on the same trips. It is a great time saver. At one time, we had to make some of these trips by air and that's increasingly not making sense. Between the long tedious trips to the airports, then the endless delays at security etc and then the same thing on the other end, the TGV is a life saver. A friend who lives in Metz,  France was facing a move to Paris because of his business needs. But the TGV let him stay where he was without sacrificing anything. All I know is that the Acela is currently our only sort of high speed rail. We've used in between Connecticut and D.C. and for trips to Boston. On the last trip from DC, the poor rail condition made it very difficult to hold a drink in my hand or to read a book. It is still better in many ways than air, but we should be embarrassed by the great superiority of the European Rail System, especially the TGV.

Need to make customer appointments in Paris, a 1st class on the way out and an ouigo from Massy on the return, perfect both in terms of time and comfort. Wifi to work, silence in the car, space for luggage. The toilets on the other hand are always a dreaded and vomit-inducing moment and the bar, I never want to go there because it's so expensive and it's not very good

I crossed France starting from Nice early in the morning and reaching Paris in time for my connection. The journey was comfortable, relatively quiet, the food on board was reasonable. The queue of taxis outside the train station is endless so I chose the metro and took my second train of the day to Troyes. In the following days I crossed Champagne and the Marne. A rolling landscape dotted with small villages with ancient churches, I recommend it in spring and summer.

If you go to Europe, one of the most impressive things is the use of the bullet train. Advice, if you go from Charles de Gaulle to Disney, don't settle too much. It's 10 minutes. But the view is unbeatable.

I took second class seats from Montparnasse in Paris to Rennes. I was satisfied with the on-time departure and arrival, but there were stains on the seats from spilled drinks, and the air conditioner near the window was full of dust, so I wish they would improve the cleanliness. When you think about it, you realize once again how clean, punctual, and comfortable Japan's Shinkansen trains are.

Paris Marseille tgv archi full. 20 minutes after departure, want a coffee. 15 minutes of waiting at the bar, only one waitress (still with a little smile but for how long?...). No more pastries...almost empty, dirty window. Alongside this, we highlight products from star chefs. And if we went back to basics...Simple, good products, available and served quickly.

Traveling by Train from Paris to Reims was comfortable and easy. We left from the Gard de Est station and the process was quite easy. Once the train arrived in the station the Platform that the train was departing was posted. After showing our electronic boarding pass it was a easy walk to our train car and to our seats. I was just getting comfortable when the train was slowing down to the approach to our destination. I highly recommend booking via the web app and paying for a First Class Ticket.

I really looked forward to this trip but the staff managed to ruin it almost before it started. Probably because of poor maintenance of kitchen appliances, part of the menu was not available. Not possible to serve hot soup or pasta. Went for the pre prepared Italian platter with some meat and some cheese but then they were out of the focaccia that was a part of this item on the menu even before the trip started.Next attempt was a burger, only needed to be heated. The lady who did the heating was more busy with her own mobile and the sandwich she was eating while preparing meals for the customers and it more or less killed the rest of my appetite. All in all, a very good example of the worst possible customer service. I just hope the trip itself will be good. At least the weather is fine.My advice will be to bring your own food.

Decided to leave the hussel and bussel of Prais behind for the day and take the TGV to Riemes for they day,being only 50 minutes from Paris by Train it was certainly do able there and back in one day.The train is quick and efficient and with seats in first class being allocated we did have worry about seating.

The cars are new. However, there is less space, less comfort. It's cramped and the electrical equipment fails half the time. The first of the old TGVs were in velvet with plenty of space and comfortable.
Sandwich club poulet. I would cry if it wasn’t so funny. Plenty of dry bread and not much in between

We decided to take the train from Paris to Biarritz instead of flying.  Thought it would be fun to see the countryside.  The train itself was very nice.  Clean and comfortable. There is no space for luggage near your seats.  There is a small area for luggage at the back of each car.  We were a bit worried about theft at each stop, and watched our bags.  The train travels very fast but the ride is super smooth on the lower level.  We went upstairs to get food and the motion is much more pronounced up there.As for the "views of the countryside"- we learned that this is not a particularly scenic route!  For most of the way, we only saw the high foliage along the tracks.  From the upstairs, the views were better but still not especially scenic.  So- take the train to save money, but not for the scenery on this particular route.

Japan's Shinkansen is more comfortable. Time is delayed. You won't know the station platform until 20 minutes before departure. The inside of the train is not cleaned, so if you expect it to be like the Shinkansen, you will be disappointed.

Excellent for speed and very competitive ticket prices, compared to those of Italian railways, especially if you take advantage of the many promotions. Clean and comfortable, with numerous daily connections. Unfortunately it doesn't always arrive on time, especially on cross-border connections.

After flying to Paris we took the train to Bordeaux. Due to a mix-up in our tickets, we wound up in "second class." Terrible experience but we had no time to correct the mistake. On subsequent legs (Bordeaux to Biarritz, Biarritz to Bordeaux and Bordeaux to Paris) we traveling first class on the TGV and it was delightful. The cars were clean and roomy with desktops for working and plenty of legroom. If we had this mode of travel in the US, I would use it all the time. In France we truly enjoyed our train experience and aside from a lack of adequate space for luggage, the experience was very enjoyable. I will say that the food offerings and service in the dining car was underwhelming so I would recommend taking your own food on the train with you. If you have an opportunity to travel via train, do not miss the opportunity to travel on the TGV.
Beautiful trip on the high-speed train bordering the entire blue coast of the Mediterranean... highly recommended.

Unfortunately, and from what other people tell me, a problem of the size that I suffered is not unusual. After the first train, a TER, was delayed, I missed the TGV connection. The attention at the connection station, unable due to lack of staff in the face of the avalanche of people asking for a solution (everyone very polite, by the way, without a single high-sounding word) They offered me a combination of two TGV with connection, without a seat because they were full, which were also late. Nothing to complain about, they tell me in the end...

Flixbus is cheap, it's an almost guaranteed schedule for 10 hours of travel on the TGV, the luxury of paying a lot for a non-existent service, if you want to miss your connections, take it, it's guaranteed, it's like a Pepy in the Apple
