If you are wondering what is inYes?   1. It's the same train with a big inOui sticker.       (Now we're not kidding) 2. The Bar car is simply closed.       (It's just to go from Strasbourg to Marseille so nothing to worry about) 3. No power on the sockets (this is normal, we're still in 1st) 4. I gave it 1 out of 5 because the Wifi works.       (But only intermittently otherwise it's not funny.)Conclusion: it's still just as "good" but what's more (this is the extra thing that makes it inYes) they take you for an idiot (a real idiot) by making you believe that you are going to travel on Business! So it's not inYes?

Unless you want less people in your train car, it's not worth paying extra for 1st class. Yes, the train is on- time and fast (Paris- Bordeaux and Toulouse- Paris), and the WCs are in good shape, but the seats are horribly uncomfortable, poorly designed. My neck and back were miserable from the rigid, inhumanly-shaped seatbacks. Also, the windows are filthy, even in 1st class, so you can barely see out of them. Paris- Bordeaux train was better here.)It was disappointing, especially compared to the Eurostar.

I really like the convenieince of getting to the train station 20 minutes before you leave, having a reserved seat, relaxing and having a snack and a beverage for a simple 2 hour journey at a reasonable price with Free WiFi.  This is a very nice option if you are returning to Paris CDG for departure to avoid going through the center of Paris and/or changing trains. Our train left on time and arrived on tie, can't beat that.Book your trip in advance directly on their website  -- it will save you money and it's easy.

We decided to take the high-speed train from Paris. After some research we determined which Paris train station to board the train from - Gare de l'Est. Although railway stations have a long history, they have managed to develop high-speed train operations. Instead, China's old train stations are being demolished and replaced with cold, modern buildings. It takes almost 6 hours to get from Paris to Nice. It is one of 11 services running throughout the day. We found the carriage easily - we went first class. The seats are very comfortable. The carriage is quiet. Because a high-speed train must travel on both dedicated and non-dedicated tracks, it must occasionally slow down. In China, dedicated tracks are built only for high-speed trains, so there is huge waste. As our train approached Nice we saw the beach and sea from our seats. One note of note: The train is able to tilt as it moves around curves. Again, China's high-speed trains don't have that feature. We saw a dog arrive as a passenger. Generally speaking, Europe's public transportation systems are pet-friendly. Finally, I read from the Internet: The route of high-speed trains is extended to surrounding countries - Germany, the Netherlands, the United Kingdom, Spain, Switzerland, Italy, and other countries. It makes money every year. On the contrary, China's high-speed trains are only domestic, and the profits are different.
Even in 1st class, it’s dirty, it smells like old socks 🧦! At the price of the ticket, a shame!!! For information Angers-Lille on October 6

Terrible..I put my luggage on top my seat someone just took it,I lost 10 thousand Europe my camera.the train and the police do nothing.on the day 15 people lost the luggage.abd they told us is normal.

TGV = OMG!!!!!A beer and a wine and a meal at 300kph The French TGV is very comfortable with good food and refreshments from a well equipped cafe which allows you to 'dine in' or take away to your seat. Do Your Self A Favour - for 10 Euro upgrade to first class. The seats are big, you get wifi free, charging ports for phone/camera and computers a great dining car and room for the luggage.Paris to Montpellier in just over 2 hours :)
I enjoyed train travel more than I have ever before . I love Paris & travel by train is the easiest & most affordable way to go anywhere.

If you are traveling with a large suitcase, be sure to get to the platform early. The baggage storage area inside the car is not that big, so it fills up from the bottom, where it's easier for everyone. It is quite difficult to put heavy items on top of it. Especially girls. If there is someone kind nearby, they can help. Also, if you choose a seat when making a reservation, there are seats in the middle that have a luggage storage area, so be sure to check that out. It would be helpful if the luggage storage area was close to the seats. Since there is a luggage storage area near the entrance, we cannot guarantee that there will be no theft. Also, you need to check which platform the train will arrive at frequently. You may be confused if the platform changes just before you arrive. It's fine if you're at the starting station, but if you're boarding from a station along the way, the stopping time may be extremely short, so be sure to give yourself plenty of time. If you're driving a long distance, they may even come to sell your items in your car.

Slight delay, but arrived in Paris only 10 mins late. Travelled in first class as we did in Austria and Switzerland and glad we paid the extra on our Eurail ticket. Food wasn’t great however I wouldn’t expect much more, best to pack your own snacks.My big complaint was the toilet, I opened the door and shut it immediately as I could stand the smell, I waited until we arrived instead.While still a pleasant trip, the trains in Austria and Switzerland were better.

We traveled from Barcelona to Paris by high-speed train since the prices were much cheaper than traveling by plane. The good thing about traveling to France from Spain by train is that there are often very tempting and affordable offers. Extreme punctuality both at arrival and departure times at destinations. It is a fairly large train with two floors, with quite a bit of comfort, the cafeteria is spacious and well attended with polite staff, comfortable seats, the only drawbacks that I would have are the stops that it has in certain French cities but they are not long and they get tiresome and the trip would be more enjoyable if the monitors in the carriages could show a movie since the trip lasts about 6 hours and 35 minutes or so. Usually perfect. I will repeat.

We chose to go from Lyon to Turin with the TGV to experience the thrill of an excellent train of the French railways - albeit on a stretch where there is no high speed - also allowing ourselves first class for the occasion. The experience, however, was quite disappointing: when we boarded the train at the Lyon station our seats were occupied by others, so a brief moment to make them free. For some kind of comfort, we have to wait for the passage of the obsolete "trolley", with prices however quite high. The cleanliness left something to be desired, particularly in the bathroom (but why is the toilet flush button so well hidden under the toilet paper? well...). Finally, even the punctuality we were hoping for was lacking.

We traveled first class. It's not great, but it's acceptable. The train appears old. Both on the outward journey and on the return journey there was an abundant delay (which, on the return to Milan, also made us miss our connection). Bar service on the way out, but not on the way back

The slogan: “stay connected to the earth from your armchair”. The good joke. I want to watch a movie. In 10 minutes, I only saw 15 seconds of credits. On the other hand, I can see the spinning spinner clearly. Come on, I give up. Especially since there is only one socket for two... Madame Rachel Picard, on your Inoui flyers, you should write: "Be very, very patient... rather than "Travel with your time". Did you know that in cozy buses, there is a socket for each traveler? At the end of the rail, the light will come, but when?

We usually travel from Madrid to Paris and vice versa because we don't like the plane at all. Through Barcelona it costs on average three times as much as through Hendaye. So even if it takes a little longer, we always go through Hendaye. The last trip cost us €65.60 for the complete trip Madrid - Paris, which through Barcelona cost about €170.

Never again with SFIGA-THELLO! Locomotive broken on 5/8/2018 on an afternoon train from Albenga to Milan. A 3 hour journey which instead lasted 7 hours!!! Hostage without any information from the staff (at large) and only with precise electronic announcements that reminded us of the accumulation of minutes of delay! A survival basket arrived in Genoa (1 bottle of hot water and 1 tart). The only positive note: the air conditioning remained active for the entire 7 hours of slow progress!!!! Hoax: reimbursement (if it ever arrives) of only 50% of the ticket..... We would need compensation for damages! And apparently the delays of this train are the rule!!! Scandalous that it can still remain in service!

Started well but ended up over 3 hours late. So why the 4 stars. Well it left on time. Plenty of space for everyone’s luggage...comfy seats, very clean and modern car... about 15 minutes into the trip, the electrics on the train failed. We actually were able to get out because our car was on a station. There were police, fire brigade and SNCF personnel everywhere. After a bit, the water was being handed around to customers... luckily, although sunny, there was a nice breeze so it wasn’t too uncomfortable.. I had a little snooze on the train.Then after about three hours, we took off again. Constant info over the speakers, more water, and a dinner box with a meal, sweets, drinks, juice, biscuits etc. some info about compensation I think over the speaker but not sure as my French is very poor.  The trip , once going was very quiet and smooth. The view along the waterfront from Nice was stunning ..thanks SNCF

Worn out grubby train, omg the toilets rang out of water to wash your hands, the smell of urine was awful, (even when we disembarked off the train) the power did not work in 1st class,coach 1 to charge your mob phones.We noticed the grub in the window sill as someone else had taken a picture of this. Paid €118 for this trip for 2 adults. I'm glad we took our own lunch and drinks, we did buy a cafe @ €2.50 each very small cup. Very disappointing, the only thing that was good was the slightly comfy chairs and extra leg room on a regional train.
as usual no problem; travel in 1st for €4 more on the journey. Why deprive yourself. Departure and arrival on time.

Been to Europe many times for businessI am used to train delays within 60mins. Used to be better back in the days but I’m not complaining.I never go through France and this was my first time taking the TGV. I can’t believe how inefficient it was. My first time experiencing a 2hours+ delay.Good experience, now I know I will avoid this country at all cost. Nothing goes as planned here.

I have been taking the train for 7 years and I found the people who openly criticized the SNCF quite exaggerated. But today I in turn express my dissatisfaction and my exasperation. The trains are often full and it feels cramped. I have a subscription in which I use my bike but I always have to play Tetris with the 10 others, due to lack of space. I met railway workers who were very kind and very professional. But that doesn't make up for it with far too many others who barely listen to you and respond like a dog. (especially TER controllers)At the moment, some trains are 4 hours late. Almost none of them are on time....In short, it's nonsense!

I took Thello in September 2018 to get to and from Nice and same thing last year. The service is not bad, apart from some aspects that could be improved, the big problem is the delay, which is never less than 40-45 minutes and creates problems in particular for those who would then have to take another connecting train...
The first class was far worse than the second class of Italo and Frecciarossa... grandeur on trains remains in the dreams of the French!

With a degree of apprehension we booked train travel from Paris St Lazare to Bayeux and eventually on though to St Malo. Train travel was quiet efficient and we were impressed with our experience. Taxis  were not always available at our destinations but we made out o/k. Overall a very good experience

TGV Lyon to Brussels. First class but zero service. I mean zero. Dirty, old and worn chairs. The buffet car is a disaster. Nothing substantial to eat, nothing for vegetarians. TGV is an example of service that has declined through cost cutting but still expensive for travellers. Avoid so called first class. Very poor.
On time service and the ride was smooth but I could not help notice that the 2nd class car did not seem as nice as our last trip four years ago.  Bathrooms were bad. Very disappointed.

I travel frequently with this company for business as there is no alternative. I always book premium to give me flexibility to change tickets and times. In order to change anything you have to call a helpline that can only be described as unhelpful, they offer to sell you tickets that are not available and explain that is not their fault, it is just "the system". Their website also sells tickets that you cannot buy. It amazes me that with the price of the tickets their website functions like it was put together by an enthusiastic toddler who just completed the hello world excercise for Javascript. The train itself is poor overall; the seats are decent, the food is terrible, the bathroom smells horrible, and the wifi is unusable from business perspective. Some of their staff are also quite rude. Not all are like that, but enough for me to make a comment on it. I really do wish there was an alternative way to travel from Amsterdam to Paris quicker. Thalys is a painful experience.

For 15 years, 8 to 10 times a year, I have made the Lyon-Lille Europe journey during the week for professional reasons, generally in second class (frequency subscription): This time, I am writing an opinion (which I hope will be read by the staff and managers of the SNCF) because my limit has been reached. Let's move on to the strikes for 15 years... This Lyon-Lille Europe train has been regularly late for 15 years (really). Today 09/17/18 (2 p.m. train) we are 30 minutes late. We had to change platforms when boarding: no announcement in English. There were many panicked tourists who naturally didn't understand what was happening. It’s shameful for the image of our country. We're lucky that they come to travel in France and we treat them very badly. I'm not talking about our veterans who can't carry their luggage (door H escalator broken down at Part Dieu station). The worst is the battle to get to the train. It’s amazing in terms of service. Is there no solution to organize this in terms of queuing? Once on the train (in 2nd: on seats of 4 which you cannot avoid when booking) you travel knee to knee. It's very uncomfortable for 3 hours. I really hope that this opinion will be read by the SNCF.

Got first class ticket.  Nice seats.  Bathrooms absolutely disgusting.  And no food on board.  Went to food car and looked at menu for awhile, lady standing behind the counter, we ask for a sandwich. She replies oh we don’t have anymore...none.  They had 2 packs of m & M’s 1 granola bar and 1 waffle.  That’s it!!

20 min late as usual, bar doesn't work with card or cash. To order meals online you have to use mobile network, because wifi also does not work. Disgusting ! They could at least make the trip cheaper as the service doesn't deserve the price.

We were staying in Paris, and a day trip to Mont Saint-Michel was in our plans. So we caught the Rennes TGV from Gare Montparnesse and had an extremely comfortable and fast trip.There were some “slow down areas” where I assume our train had to slow to avoid bumping into traffic, but most of the time, the car “status screen” showed that we were moving along at 280 to 300 kilometers per hour.There was plenty of room in our car, course we started very early in the day so that we could get to Mont Saint-Michel as early as possible.At Rennes, we had to depart the TGV for a ride on the TER to Pontorson - but that is another review.90 minutes and we were in Rennes, less expensive than renting a car and parking would have been dreadful at Mont Saint-Michel.I have read various reviews herein about cleanliness, our car was very clean, no odors and the seats were comfortable.

Had the tub from Switzerland to Paris. It’s a smooth ride and departure and arrival was on time. The cleanliness inside the train could be better. The tablet of my partner was not even existing anymore. How can that happen all seats pay the same price! The audio system is horrible the announcements can not be heard! That needs improvement!

We are told about investments for TGVs without drivers but: we don't care!! (To be polite). Make investments in equipment and track renovation!!!!!!. 3 hours late on my return from vacation due to a switching problem....I am impatiently awaiting the opening to competition because at the moment we are caught in a storm by the SNCF but as soon as competing trains are put in place I would have no qualms about no longer taking your trains.

Overall, the trip with the TGV was okay, we only drove 10 minutes for a distance of about 40km, which we thought was great (Disneyland - CDG airport). The price is... well... for 10 minutes, but the TGV is the fastest means of transport for this route and is therefore portable. Overall, the train is a bit dingy.

I was at Gare Montparnasse on the day of the fire, July 27, 2018. Unable to take the train to Royan for a short week of vacation, I fell back on my car. My daughter and I left the station quickly because it was packed with people. The important thing was to leave as a priority. I inquired and the red vests told me that I would be reimbursed for my trip but that I would have to go to the SNCF store. It doesn't matter, it can wait. So I went to the store (rue de Belleville) to assert my rights to reimbursement and came across a very unfriendly person who told me that they couldn't do anything and to manage either with the internet or by postal mail. Internet: impossible because there was a correspondence. So I went by registered mail which left on 08/23 and received on 08/24. 3 weeks later I started to worry about not having a response and so I sent a simple request on messenger: how to proceed to find out where my reimbursement is at? Here is the response from the SNCF: Hello Corinne, I understand your expectation, however, due to a large number of requests, the processing time for requests by mail is currently more than 3 months. I invite you to be patient. And yes, it is a public service!!!!! This is unacceptable. How, in such circumstances, can we trust these people. Until my request is lost, there are no miles. I am appalled by this type of response. Privatization is going to be very funny to them: they will have to work and much faster than that. I work in a commercial department in the private sector: this kind of response would not be accepted either by my management or by my clients. This is just a stab in the void but I needed as many people as possible to read this post

My husband and I took the train from Paris to Barcelona and back booking first class both ways. On the upper deck you see so much more and we were sat at a table for two with plenty leg room. Plenty of space for luggage although it's not easy hauling your luggage up to the top deck.Downside, both ways there was no water in the toilets to wash your hands on both journeys. Once, maybe, but twice!! Really not good enough.Thank goodness for hand gel.

It's quite comfortable, it's fast. But the experience can still be improved: why leave Amsterdam CS on platform 15b? There is no seating, there is no kiosk, there is nothing at all. What a 'disgrace'. Moreover: why is there no check on suitcases here, but on the way back at Gare du Nord in Paris, there is? There is no room for large suitcases in the wagons, but you only find out once you are inside; the 'steward' at the door does not point this out (and will not help lift the luggage in either). The luggage rack above the seats is a dark cave: no idea if there is a rack at all, let alone how big. The seat (1st class) is not overly spacious, and there is a waste bin and a footrest that get in the way. The table can also only be unfolded as a whole (= large). Some rates include coffee and something tasty and lunch. The goodies had already been reduced to one choice halfway through the wagon, the same at lunch. By the way: which chef would think of serving grapefruit segments (unthinkable with cholesterol medicines) and nuts (allergies) for this target group (50+)? The toilets are also not kept clean, so you can hope that the other travelers don't splash and splash too much. Unfortunately. More must and can be done to get air and car travelers onto the train.

We traveled from Milan to Paris and days after from Paris to Barcelona.   We did both first class. The Italian Frecchia Rosa equivalents are far superior.  The TGV seats are uncomfortable. They don't have Wi Fi. Bad air conditioning... Only one bathroom per car, which after a short drive was very dirty.   The implacable Italians; with good A/C and good, comfortable seats. On the TGV they don't even give water to drink.   Everything is paid.  And what they take to eat is of average quality.  Finally, with both TGV trains we arrived a little over an hour late.  No explanations.  Just warning about the delay times, and how they increased as we progressed. I don't recommend it. Only use if you have no other alternative.   Yes, I recommend the Italian and Spanish equivalents.

I recently traveled on a high-speed line between Paris and Strasbourg with a ticket previously purchased through the SNCF online channel. My ticket indicated seat 83, but the assigned car only had seats numbered up to 70 or so. I checked the cars before and after the one assigned and I noticed that in all the cars the seats ended with the number 70 or so. Our luck was that we were able to travel in seats that had not been sold. Honestly, I don't understand how such a prestigious company can make these mistakes.

I took two round trips from Montparnasse to Brittany in August. You can easily make reservations and issue tickets using the smartphone app called "OUI." It's extremely convenient to be able to choose seat attributes, but I can't get a receipt. (In terms of the sweat cars themselves, I think Italy's high-speed trains are cleaner. (I didn't have a chance to ride the new double-decker cars.) The toilet in the car I rode on was collapsed. Vacations are extremely crowded. The difference between 1st and 2nd class is the difference between 3rd or 4th rows, and I think 2nd class is enough. Like in Italy, 1st class is served with drink service. There was no in-car ticket sales either. However, buying tea and snacks at the kiosk is a fun experience that you don't get in Japan. There are some people who don't have tickets in the train, but you can check them by showing the barcode on the smartphone app.

I go to Paris for work once a year and this year I decided to try the return trip by TGV... out of curiosity because I am generally a lover of train travel. However, my enthusiasm faded very quickly ... the train was literally disgusting ... stains everywhere and certainly not from the same day, indeed certainly dated ... there were various encrustations, dried pieces of brioche between the seats and endless crumbs ... the bathroom was filthy and had a terrible smell ... I had to work and so I opened the table and it too was all dirty and sticky ... I really had the impression that the train hadn't been cleaned for a long time. And that's not all. My seat was broken .. in the sense that it only remained lying down (ah.. I was in first class!). The only positive note was the very kind conductor who found me another free place up to Milan. The train... the icing on the cake... it also arrived 40 minutes late. Finally, I would like to point out that the train I had initially booked was canceled like 3 days before for unclear reasons and I had to purchase a new ticket because making a change and/or asking for a refund for the canceled train proved to be an impossible task (in 2018 I would say that they should have provided an alternative solution or at least allowed me to change trains online without costs!). Experience not to be repeated!

Disappointment. The Turin-Paris journey is at high speed only in the Lyon-Paris section while from Turin to Lyon it proceeds at normal speed. The train was very dirty both on the way there and on the way back. The obscenely dirty and smelly bathrooms. Virtually no service staff. Non-working electrical outlets. Much below the level of our Frecciarossa. Next time we will definitely travel by plane.

After a trip from Brussels to Amsterdam which went well, the return was much more disappointing. An employee who distributes breakfast as unpleasant as possible. She made very unpleasant remarks to us because we told her no for breakfast then yes a few seconds later. Then, we remained stuck on the train for 2 hours and 20 minutes with the only information: the company had no information to give us and that the train was stopped for an indefinite period! In the end we pile into the next train which is already crowded. In our luck, we got off at Brussels Midi station. Passengers who were going to Paris were invited to get off and wait 1 hour 45 minutes before taking another train to Paris, obviously without any further information. We requested a refund...we have no return...

Excellent transport, booked in first class. On the way out we were delayed by an hour for customs control in Modane. Then it was partially recovered, only 25 minutes longer. Dated carriages, indecent bathrooms, smelly and dirty already at the beginning of the journey. Exaggerated prices at the bar. A coffee for 2.50 euros and if you wanted to add a drop of milk, the price rises to 3 euros... Dirty seats and carpet ditto. A first class public service was unusable because it was closed from the start of the journey. On the way back, I travel on time, same dirt, very annoyed and arrogant Italian barmaid, always an unusable bathroom. For a first class the service is poor. There is no WiFi which is advertised on the TGV website

Always fascinating what others see as high quality and modern. The TGV was dirty on our trip, the windows were uncleaned, there were small remains on the seats and there was dust and old, moldy dirt everywhere. We traveled 1st class. To this day I don't know what the difference should be compared to the 2nd class (which we looked at). The seats were narrow and had nothing special. A normal regional train, which we used during our stay, was much cleaner and more comfortable.

Scam, More and more expensive, and Never reimburse you! Yes, because they always have an excuse or they end the conversation by saying “I can't do anything for you”. Second time this has happened in a month and a half. What a service! It is certain that I would not use their service again. Today, I just arrived in Charles de Gaule, I took a ticket to Rennes, the ticket office indicated a stop at Massy. The screen also indicated Rennes with the track number. While going to the indicated track, another train was announced. I then asked the staff and they didn't even know. We actually had to take the train from Bordeaux. Bordeaux was not indicated anywhere when the ticket was purchased. The lady then told me that she would make me a commercial gesture for the second train, telling me that this was not my fault. Then she gave me my new train ticket without giving me back the difference. She told me no, I can't do anything for you because you should have seen that there was a stop at Massy. (Turnaround) I had seen the stop at Massy but everything pointed to Rennes and not Bordeaux. I lose €100 and have to wait 4 hours. She also told me that Montparnasse would not take my ticket, that they would not do anything for me. This is RIDICULOUS knowing that it is the same group: the SCNF. Waste of money, it's over. I wouldn't travel with them again.

Due to the scheduled Ryanair strikes during the month of August, whose tickets we had purchased last March, we opted to make our trip to Paris on the TGV-AVE, which did not displease us either since the duration of the trip, about 6 hours, is comparatively similar to the plane trip: if we add the trip to the airport of origin, the check-in time, the duration of the flight, the inexplicable and inevitable delays, the luggage collection and the transfer from the airport destination to the center of Paris. The price is very expensive, even though you have the Renfe gold card with a 40% discount, the amount is still very high. For the outward journey we bought tourist tickets and for the return trip, for a small increase of €20, we opted for 1st class, which we do not regret due to its greater comfort and spaciousness of seats. We thought that we would make the trip on the modern Renfe series 100 AVE trains, but on both routes we had to use the SNCF 2-story Euroduplexes, clearly older and without the comforts of the Spanish AVE, of which we had fond memories of a Madrid-Barcelona trip some years ago. The lower floors are intended for the tourist class, the seats are not as comfortable and spacious, the visibility through the windows is quite fair, and the air conditioning is not very Good, because it was quite hot during the entire trip. At the BCN-Sants station, she received very correct information, identification with the DNI and inspection of the luggage through the security arch. The destination station, Gare de Lyon, is unworthy for an international trip, since you arrive and get off on a narrow platform, without information of any kind, without information personnel at the exit of the train; We located an underground exit that linked to the subway, but it was amazing: without escalators or elevator, carrying our suitcases. The return trip is another story. We arrived at the station well in advance and spent time having a drink in a bar near the platforms, then we remembered that with 1st class tickets we could access a VIP waiting room: very small and with few seats. From the information screens we realized that our train was coming with 40 minutes. of delay. The public address system at the station leaves a lot to be desired, as it is barely audible and incomprehensibly only in French and the staff at the information desk only spoke French and English, don't miss it...... Despite paying attention to the information on the screens, we found out by chance that the train was already on the platform and would leave shortly. We went to the corresponding platform and we couldn't believe it: there was no security arch to check the luggage, nor personnel of any kind controlling and verifying the tickets or the ID, and look for the life to find the car that corresponded to us, once inside and during the entire journey no one asked us for the tickets, we could have snuck them in without paying for the tickets.  Again it was SNCF's 2-story TGV, this time when we went in 1st class we were assigned to the upper floor, which you have to access via a small spiral staircase and carrying your suitcases. On this floor the materials are of higher quality, the seats are very spacious and comfortable, but the electrical outlets in the entire car did not work; Furthermore, there was no background music, no movies or drinks as we remembered from the Spanish AVE. Anyway, since in the end we arrived in Sants with a delay of 60 minutes, they paid us 25% of the tickets. The truth is that the amount is very expensive for what they offer, although the trip is more enjoyable and pleasant than on the plane, due to the small price difference it is worth purchasing 1st class tickets.

I took the TV with my little girl both to and from Paris. Ok the cars are narrower, the seats seem dirtier but the journeys went well, in France it flies on the high speed section, in Italy it operates an intercity service. Of course the bathrooms are not cleaned by anyone during the journey, as happens on the Freccia Rossa. Careful checks at the French border on the outward journey, no one was seen on the return home. If you organize yourself, 7 hours pass and at least you arrive in the center of Paris.

For a country that is justifiably proud of it’s TGV, there something very wrong about the acceptance of such low standards of hygiene that welcome you on board. The smell from the toilets is all pervading as you get on the train. When the call of nature eventually beckons and you reluctantly need to use the facilities, the smell is enough to dissolve you nasal hair. We made a return trip from Paris to Turin and tried a number of toilets on both trains and sadly they were all the same. Come on SNCF, get you act together, passengers deserve better. Other than the issue with the toilets, the journey was punctual, comfortable and the price was very reasonable.
Our train trip through Europe was very nice. Clean trains. On time schedule as well as beautiful scenery as we traveled throughout France and Italy

I'm currently on the TGV 9247 Paris-Milan train, of the Trainline and SHAME......a very strong smell of pee all over the carriage, let alone inside the toilet. Furthermore, there is also no water, in the other toilet there is a smell of ammonia which makes the air unbreathable. This in the first class... let alone in the second... If it were at least a cheap price, instead it is also expensive!!!!! On the first leg we were on a French train and it was a completely different thing.....LEARN!!!!!

I took the TGV from Montparnasse station to Rennes station. From the station, we took a bus to Mont Saint Michel. I applied for TGV from Japan through a site called Rail Europe. Since the site is in Japanese, I was able to easily arrange tickets. Unlike the Japanese Shinkansen, you cannot reserve seats. However, if there are seats available, two people will be seated next to each other or across from each other. All you have to do is print out your e-ticket and bring it with you when you receive an email. I wouldn't trade it for anything more. The train number is displayed on the electronic bulletin board next to the entrance of each car, so check it before boarding. The platform will be displayed on the electronic bulletin board in the concourse 20 minutes before departure, so look at it and go to the platform. The platform numbers are displayed in large numbers, so you won't have to worry about getting lost. When we boarded the train, there was no checking of tickets on the train. The toilet was also fairly clean.

I took TGV Milan Paris, the bathrooms had no water to wash your hands, they smelled disgusting and the stench even extended to the carriage. The icing on the cake on the return was a serious fault in the electricity line, 7 hours of waiting and return with a replacement bus. To be avoided carefully!

I will never travel with SNCF again. Nightmare. They sent my changed booking ticket to me in Australia, but I am in France, unable to receive it. I have an email confirmation and receipt to show proof of purchase but that wasn't good enough. So got my family back in Australia to open the mail and take a picture of the ticket with barcode to email me. Still not good enough for them they wanted me to buy a whole new ticket. Had to buy an additional ticket for a different route also which saw me going back and forth to their ticket office because apparently that also needed to be finalized. Although my.money had already been taken by them, so then I found out,luckily, I needed to validate that ticket before getting on the train or risk a fine. Absolute confusing nightmare for a traveller, that was not customer friendly or straightforward. I will not be using them again. It actually took hours of my travel time to just buy a ticket, when it should be so easy.

Forced to travel by train to return to Italy due to a car accident, we took two lines with the TGV: Brest-Paris and Paris-Milan. Crazy price around 450 euros for a first class that doesn't exist! To say dirty is to pay a compliment! It is indecent, as are the bathrooms, dirty and indeed impracticable from the moment you leave! Never seen anything like it. On the red arrow they continuously pass by to check them!!  Not to mention the service, terrible. They don't offer you anything (other than sparkling wine, water and newspaper!!!!) there is no restaurant car in theory they should stop by to book or sandwiches or something else, but you have to call them because no one stops. But to collect the dirt......best wishes!!!! In short w the red arrow and Italo !!!!!!!

We were involved in an accident on the TGV from Paris to Milan on August 20th. An electrical fault before Modane. We remained stopped for 5 hours with news given in dribs and drabs by the staff. Two hours with light and three hours in dark. No assistance just a little water towards the end. I would like to point out that there was also the border police on board who, as usual, took it out on the usual black man who, however, they did not "arrest". Finally they towed us to the next small station and "unloaded" us onto buses, again without saying anything and without help, especially for mothers, children and the elderly. They just watched us go by. There were some cartons on the floor with food inside but it wasn't easy to understand. We passengers were very good, I didn't hear anyone complaining more than necessary. We arrived in Milan at a quarter past five, exactly as announced by the bus driver. At least he spoke. Today I went to the station to ask for a refund and they told me that it can only be done via the SNCF website which however did not accept my IBAN. Luckily I live near Porta Garibaldi and so I returned to their ticket office where they kindly helped me. However, the refund will only be 75%. In this case of bad assistance it should have been total. And I'm not going to tell you about the bathrooms that are already ridiculous but in this case have become a nightmare.

Anyone who complains about Italian trains has never taken the TGV. Obsolete interiors, complete with the smell of cigarettes left over from the 90s, narrow seats, unusable bathrooms and inconceivable slowness for a train that connects Milan to Paris. The train makes too many useless stops, some sections are single track, therefore having to wait for the connection to be able to pass: a return to the past. Bottom line, if you have to go to Paris find another way. Never again.

We took a tgv yes Go For a long time we have not taken the train for various reasons. This is an opportunity to spend a few days in Avignon and we are thinking of the train to save time, not to have the fatigue of driving and also a surprising cost. Oui Go A total surprise the train is comfortable, clean, on time and after 3 hours of travel we arrived very happy and satisfied with it. To do again if possible (opportunity). Excellent price and service.

We booked 1st Class tickets from Paris to Bordeaux a month or so before our trip. A few days before our departure there was a fire at the station and strike action which was threatening to reduce the number of trains. We arrived at the station early to try and mitigate any of these challenges and were pleasantly surprised.The information staff were very patient; polite and helpful. Platform staff as well were helpful and polite. Once you figure out the system (really the same as any other major station in the world) it was easy. We found our platform and train; our coach and our seats easily; stowed our luggage and had a very efficient ride to Bordeaux.Some of the reviews we had read before bemoaned the quality of 1st Class and the space for luggage. In the middle of a European summer we could complain about neither. This is a train after all and 1st Class is not expected (nor promised) to be that of an airline. Luggage space was ample with a little re-arrangement. It would appear everyone grabbed the first racks whilst there were racks mid-carriage and at the opposite end.Seats and tables are equipped with power connections for charging. There is free pretty-good wifi too. Upper deck views are worth the extra cost and the seats were comfortable; with reclining settings more than adeuate to sleep in should one wish. The bar carriage served snacks and light meals as well as some not-so-bad plastic bottled wine!Overall we were very impressed with the efficient of TGV; SCNF generally and for the value for money which we received.

I have traveled through France many times by TGV, the French high-speed electric passenger train, and have rarely experienced hiccoughs. My most recent trips, however, took place in April 2018 from Paris to Aix-en-Provence and back again during a period when rail workers were striking on dates announced in advance. Two fell on my travel days. I had to scramble in France to change one reservation to a non-strike day and the departure time of the other. SNCF, which operates TGV, ensured that this happened quickly, efficiently and without any additional cost, though I held non-refundable tickets. I was very impressed with how well the process went during a high-stress period for staff and passengers and how customer-focused the company remained.I traveled first-class to Aix and returned to Paris in a second-class car. My first-class seat proved to be a tad more comfortable with more legroom. But I do not think the difference between the two classes is enough to pay a lot more for a first-class ticket. Sometimes, for an unknown reason to me, the tickets are almost priced the same and then I will opt for first-class. Going to Aix, I sat for the first time on the upper level of a duplex car, which I will not do again when traveling with a heavy suitcase. I found it quite difficult to ascend the myriad narrow stairs with my bag.In Paris, I found the boarding process to be somewhat disorderly in the terribly crowded Gare de Lyon. There was no formal line, just a mass of humanity inching along to the machine that scans the ticket bar code. Much jostling occurred. I experienced the opposite at the small Aix station for my return, simply validating the ticket, with no other passengers nearby. I then waited on the platform for the train to arrive. This time, I had ensured that my seat would be on the bottom level.On both trips, the train departed and left on time. Inside, the cars were clean and appeared to be well maintained. I did not use the toilets during each 3-hour trip so cannot comment on their condition. I also did not buy any food. Overhead space for storing suitcases was limited, and luggage racks at the end of the cars became full quickly. I recommend taking only one small bag, if possible, on the TGV, though the luggage limit is higher. I always enjoy my TGV rides. They are quiet, and I find it exhilarating to zip through the countryside at speeds up to 200 mph. All the TGV staff with whom I have interacted have been friendly and helpful.When searching for tickets, I have always found Rail Europe to have higher prices than other agencies. For my April travel, I got the best deal through Trainline on-line. Regardless of agency, the best prices -- up to 60 percent less -- generally occur three months in advance of departure. Prices then start to increase the closer it gets to the travel day.

The TGV is a very comfortable way to travel to the south of france. However, thats the good bit. The not so good bit is the delays, the toilets (a familar story in france) and the crazy busy stations at paris nord and de lyon.But the actual journey is very relaxing and 1st class gives you more space than you could dream of compared to plane.Tip - take your own food, drink and loo paper

We booked our train tickets from Bordeaux to Paris (and back) with Rail Europe.  When we arrived at the station, we found out that our train had been cancelled.  We got a ticket to talk to someone at the counter and waited for our number to be called.  When we got to the desk, we were told that we could get tickets on the next train that left 2 hours after our scheduled train - at that point, it was only a little over an hour until it would depart.  We took it.  We had paid the extra for first class (not to much over the regular price).  Once we boarded the train, we noticed that there didn't seem to be any rhyme or reason to the seat numbering.  Be sure to get on the car that is and whether you are upstairs or downstairs.  Then wallah - you'll find your seats.The train was very fast (up to almost 300 KM/Hr - whatever that is in MPH) and we made it in 2 hours.  Yeah!On our return trip, we had to wait and wait and wait until our train was assigned a track number.  Many of us were waiting for the same train.  Once the number was posted, it seemed that everyone who was waiting was also headed for our same train.  This time, we knew what we were doing any found our seats without any issues.  2 hours later, we were back in Bordeaux.  I'm glad that our trains weren't late or cancelled like other reviewers mentioned.  I guess that we lucked out.

A round trip in 1st class (Marseille-Paris): armchairs with dubious covers which struggle to recline, rubbish which overflows from row bins, tired air conditioning, lamps which never go out (frustrating on a journey where it is still dark) and toilets which are dirty and flooded as soon as the train leaves... When will there be a real alignment between the prices which are so high and the comfort sought after? As for the Wi-Fi, I received it well but it never allowed me to browse the Internet, so weak that I quickly gave up! What's the point of booking 1st class? Too expensive for the service, I'm thinking of taking the plane next time.

I keep seeing reviews of the TGV. Unfortunately, I have to point out again that many users have published a review on an ordinary train, convinced that it was a TGV. The most widespread confusion is that between TGV and Thello. Many people travel on the Thello convinced that it is a TGV, a high-speed train. In reality, the Thello is a very common Italian Intercity train, of a rather old generation... It was taken, painted red for the second class cars and green for the first class ones. class. Internally a rather cheap restyling has been done. In short, the Thello is a somewhat clever way to charge more for a journey that could be done at a lower expense... and with travel conditions that aren't that different. For example... the Thello Milan/Marseille-St-Charles. It makes several stops in the Ligurian section, a few less in the French section. But overall I don't know if it's worth paying double for a travel time that's not too different from a train normal. The TGV lines in France are well defined, only on some routes. The trains are of an excellent standard, with the exception of some models still dating back to the nineties (for example some models of the TGV Lyria). But going so far as to say (as I have read in some reviews) that the TGV is an old train that is falling to pieces... well... the only explanation I can give is that a train that is not the TGV has been reviewed. I usually travel to France, I have season tickets for normal lines, Intercitees lines, TGV lines, and I can confidently state that the standard is high. I am not writing this out of xenophilia, but out of simple and necessary objectivity.

I'm writing this review after a almost 3 hour delay (and counting). There was an accident between Mechelen and Antwerpen Centraal (Belgium) on Wednesday August 15, 2018. The rail was closed. Ok. This is not the company's fault. But the horrible service provided is. The attendants didn't seem to know what they were doing. They are not prepared for this kind of incident at all. We were carrying big bags and they sent us to a wagon where there was no space for our luggage (and they did this for no reason). If you need to go from Amsterdam to Brussels, go by plane if possible.

On a recent trip to France, I purchased a roundtrip Train Pass on reference number XXXXXX , Customer reference number XXX. The trip was to originate in Paris MONT 1ET2 on 29/07, returning from Bordeaux St. Jean on 03/08.Due to a fire in the station, the outgoing train was cancelled. Your company did not notify me of any changes, I found out via the news media and our hotel. Because of the lack of attention to this matter, and my not finding out until the evening before our trip, I was forced to Buy a plane ticket one way for my wife and I to Bordeaux. I made attempts to contact you via phone, but nobody answered or called me back. I am looking for reimbursement of not only my train ticket, but the plane ticket I was forced to buy because of your lack of customer service and options. I am posting this on social media today, and a recommendation not to ever use your services due to poor customer service, and lack of ability to contact during emergencies. my plane reservations were $609.14 Euros.

Don't fool yourself into thinking that on the TGVs you will find the same level of quality, cleanliness, comfort and punctuality as the Italian high-speed train. We took 2: from Milan to Paris and from Paris to Tours. They are old, dirty to the limit of decency, always late, the interiors are dilapidated, they also accept standing passengers. The Milan in Paris is scandalous, built in 1992, filthy, with suffocating and impracticable bathrooms right from the start and it doesn't proceed at high speed until the last hour of the journey from Lyon onwards. First it also travels on the normal network from Milan to Turin where there is a fast connection. It stops at numerous unknown locations in the French Alps like any regional train. I also traveled on the normal French network and it is scandalous, delays are a constant, cleanliness a pipe dream. If you can avoid SNCF. Italian railways are a thousand times better.

Trains are always late although they need to be more than a certain amount of time late before they count as late. Even with this piece of fiddling one train in ten is late. Delays of thirty minutes are standard. If you need to make a connection then play safe and give yourself a margin. Delays and missed trains turned a seven hours journey into a near twelve hours journey. Anyone who claims the airlines are worse timekeepers must fly with aeroflot. For every twelve counters at a train station you will do well to find five open. The queues at Gare Du Nord are something to behold- security gets put on to keep the fifty metre long queue in check. Would be better to have more staff on at stations. When you do get on a train be prepared to sit in aisles and stairs because they are so overcrowded. France also seems to allow a far higher proportion of passengers to be unseated than would be tolerated in any other developed country. Travel in France is cheap for a reason; it's not reliable in any way for timing or for seating

First time on the legendary TGV...a total disappointment. We are still on the road and there will be a delay of over half an hour. The numerous stops are annoying. Some in remote stations or in the open countryside. It looks like a club.

This country is deteriorating, hygiene and services non-existent, prices are high, which can only be justified by the talent of our engineers, for the rest, hygiene, services are deteriorating, we should take an example from Japan, nostalgic for the past

I am an absolute train fanatic and just love the sight of a TGV roaring through the countryside at full speed. Yet I'm sorry to say I still find air travel to be a better alternative than the high speed train.Tickets are very expensive and need to be booked month in advance to get a good price on tickets. That's just not realistic when planning trips. The ticketing system is uncomprensible. A first class ticket from brussels to Paris would've vost me €138, meal service included. Second class was €155. That's just not logical. Quite disappointingly, trains are very old, seats uncomfortable. I wouldn't want to be sitting for hours on end in a seat that makes by back and bum hurts as much.As we already where in Brussels, we took the TGV for a short day trip to Lille. Tempted by the short travel time (just over 30 minutes) and cheap tickets (that seemed to be fixed priced at €19). Our train was a service to Montpelier and even though it arrived on time, we departed with almost 20 minutes delay without a clear reason given. The announcements on the PA where inaudible. The boarding process was chaos, with only one door per coach.The journey itself was very cool. Reaching top speed. Loved it.Unfortunately, the train for our return journey was delayed again for 30 minutes. The train came from Nice and was absolutely packed. Luckily we had reserved seats. I noticed the lack of luggage space in the train. Something which truly amazed me as environmentalists are trying to sell TGV as a viable alternative for air plane travel. But it isn't. I'd rather check my suitcase in to an air plane and sit spacious and hassle free than zigzagging passed luggage left in and around  a cramped TGV. There is virtually no room for big suitcases, so you must be lucky to find space to store them. And finally, all TGV's in France draw 75% of their electricity from nuclear power plants. Which is smart, as it is a very sustainable power source. But deemed non sustainable by the same environmentalists that coerce you in taking the train in stead of an air plane. That's downright hypocritical. Concluding: it was fun to sit in TGV for a short high speed trip. Despite al the delays . But as long as a TGV ticket set's me back five times more than price of a plane ticket (in this case to London, for two persons, same travel period) I will be flying. And from The Hague to Paris, I'd rather go by car. The inflexibility and discomfort is just to big.

I went from Paris to London for the first time using the TGV and it was quite peaceful. From immigration to waiting for the train to arrive and boarding, everything worked well. The only detail is that on one side the seats are facing forward and, on the other side of the aisle, they are facing backwards. If you don't like traveling backwards, pay attention when purchasing tickets. I recommend purchasing in advance.

If you're traveling from Paris to anywhere in the south (Avignon, Marseilles, Nimes, etc.) the TGV is the only way to go.  It's a super fast, smooth and comfortable ride that will get you to your destination in less than half the time it takes to drive.  If you're adventurous and want to save on the ticket cost, take the RER from Paris to Marne-la-Vallee.  This is the site if EuroDisney and the same train from this station to the south can cost as little as 24 Euros.Highly recommended.

The trains are always late. When you miss your train because this one is late they send you to another village. When you arrive at that village they Just tell you that you won't be able to go to your final destination, so you loose your week end. When you as for reimboursement, you Will wait for 1 month before getting an answer...Terrible experience. Never take the train in France, go by plane or car.

Unreliable train, first class carriage without air conditioning, even if it were in second class it wouldn't change. We have been stopped in Genoa for more than an hour due to a fault with the doors, but they have yet to find someone to fix them. If I think that I will have to return with this train I cry. Never again

I'm still traveling and can't wait to get off the train. First class, it makes me laugh...... Disgusting. Filthy carriages, I cleaned the seats and tables before sitting down. But dirt is everywhere. What a difference between Italo and the tgv. Furthermore, you're dying from the heat, the air conditioning doesn't work, you have to pay for everything, not like Italo who offer you free drinks and snacks every half hour or so. I can't imagine the bathrooms that I haven't used yet!! But according to other reviews they don't promise anything good. Next time I'm going to Paris by plane. I prefer to overcome the fear of flying rather than travel like this. I think the time has come to demolish these trains or at least CLEAN THEM.

30 minutes late, without any message at Bellegarde station on Valserine. Service at the bar lousy, an incompetent person with no concept of service, barely able to collect by credit card or cash. The second does what she can with her colleague.
This was our second time on the Eurostar to paris. Competent and Efficient, well worth the money spent.

7:22 a.m. train. I ask for a 'wake up plan' but at 8 a.m. the pastries are finished. They offered me bread and butter instead. I receive a micro-loaf and the addition of 4E80 instead of 3E90 in the formula... I have the misfortune of asking for a glass of water. I am given a glass with 2cm of water. I have the misfortune of asking for more water. The saleswoman is indignant: we are being asked to give you little! Imagine everyone asking for water, etc. What greed, what shame!

Taking the 5 hour ride to Hedaye from Montparnasse was good, maybe perhaps I booked a 1st class seat. Less crowded with 2-and-1 configuration, but the luggage rack was completely full...I had to set our luggage on the floor and wait for Bordeaux passengers to get off for a vacant spot. Seats were wide and sufficient, reclining with foot step. Wi-Fi is good, but i ended up using my own pocket Wi-Fi.

I purchased tickets for my family and entered the wrong date somehow. I immediately (within 5mins) noticed this and contacted Rail Europe to try and change the dates and have been provided with an arrogant response that the refund policy that is associated with my booking would apply. Which meant we were pretty much charged the full amount. My mistake I know, but disappointing response. Won’t use them again!!

I bought a train ticket in April and was signed up (unwillingly) for their email lists. I've tried to unsubscribe for months since I started receiving the emails, but the unsubscribe button on all emails is broken, and has been broken since I started. I've contacted customer service 10 times since April and they say they will unsubscribe me from the lists, but I am still receiving the unwanted emails, 5 months later. This is a violation of privacy and against the Canspam law. They are breaking the law by sending these unsolicited emails! If you are having the same issues, see if you can get through to customer service! The email comes from OUI.sncf.

The French TGV used to be the best in the world. Although the network is still admirable in terms of coverage, it’s no longer the fastest, and the looks and comfort of trains now lag behind many others. Second-class seats in high-speed trains in China are now more comfortable than the TGV’s first-class seats, and Chinese first-class seats are LIE-FLAT beds as on planes; and they all offer WiFi! Japanese bullet trains have better service, eg. food (including sushi bento boxes) in push-carts, and their Shinkansen network is as good as France’s! There are at least three operator apps for buying train tickets in France: SNCF, OUI.sncf, and TGVPro. The problem is they are not integrated with one another; you can buy mobile tickets on all 3, but you can only exchange tickets on the last 2, and only the third will issue you an exchanged mobile ticket! A typically-French problem !

To make my girls happy we traveled by train... never again!! Endless journey, train stopped at every station up to Lyon... very, very smelly bathrooms on the way out and incredibly dirty on the way back... 6 hours of travel trying not to pee... an experience you don't want to repeat...

After reading a lot of negative reviews, these are my impressions: incredible smell from the toilets that spread in the carriage, dated but still acceptable train with fairly wide seats. Sockets worked but only after 3 hours did I understand where to throw the waste. (There is a seat in the middle). Arrived 15 minutes late due to police control. Air conditioning which sometimes worked and sometimes didn't. Friendly staff but no free drinks or newspapers.

I have been traveling between Paris and Brussels since March now....1 train out of 2 has been delayed by more than 20 minutes! ...and when it happens twice in the same day, you can imagine the inconvenience! I find this unacceptable!

Service from Montpernasse left exactly on time. Three quarters of the way th rough the 2-hour journey and still on time. The unfortunate fact though? No air conditioning in car 15. Daym it's sticky. We'll get to Bordeaux on tiume at the very least.

We needed to get to Paris quickly from Avignon and the TGV was a lifesaver. The train was very decent. However, we had also used the TGV to get to the center of Paris from the airport. Ticketing was an easy experience but the trains themselves were dirty and smelly. The seating wasn’t comfortable and it was packed. It was an economical way to get into the city without paying extreme taxi prices but if I had a large family, I wouldn’t think of using this service. We also used this service to get to Disneyland. The trains were a little better here but still not ideal.

The TGV is fast, comfortable and a great way to get around France but despite what you may have heard, the onboard catering is terrible. On our train, they ran out of food very quickly and what there was, was pretty grim. Take the TGV but buy your food in the station before boarding.

Our TGV train was cancelled due to the strike and we were rebooked onto another train which was then also cancelled.  The online refund system has not worked.  After waiting in a long line at Montparnesse Station for a refund, the rude SNCF representative said we were owed the refund but he couldn't give it to us because we booked online and paid via PayPal.  He insisted that he added information to the computer that would allow us to easily receive our refund online.  It didn't work.  Email to SNCF customer service has not helped.  Two letters to SNCF customer service with copies of all our tickets have, so far, yielded no refund and no response.  I recognize that SNCF is not directly responsible for the strike, but their customer service in handling the refunds is poor.  Ironically, we continue to receive frequent emails from SNCF advertising their services.

Out of all the trains that got cancelled back in May, I was able to get assistance and ultimately refund for the tickets I booked via Trainline. The experience with oui sncf has been impossible - I've had no luck in person or their website. I finally called up customer service but they were unwilling to reach out to claims. I called up claims with a friend who spoke French but it was just an unmanned line.

Love travelling by train & with so many airline strikes/delays in France nowadays we had no issues with our trip. Short journey from Paris to Amsterdam. High speed & quiet travel. Luggage space can get full quickly so be ready to board on time. We had a table seat booked which is good for this distance. Food was ok from the dining car. Not great but not terrible. Easier boarding & unboarding as compared to flying.

Okay, that's good. Only, here’s a strike....The flag is RED in their hands, but let them return 180 euros to me because of the canceled train for two. And, they will apologize for ruining my vacation!!! Let them fulfill their obligations, and then they can shove the flag out of their hands into.....

My 14 year old son and I took the train from Paris - Nice one way. It took 6 hours. I booked at home in Sweden before we went on oui's website. It cost us SEK 2,000. I only booked 2 years before we left and if you book earlier it is cheaper. The train left in the morning at 8.20. It was a lovely train journey, a very quiet train. Didn't hear much. A lovely trip. The conductor was nice.
The level of air conditioning on the train is embarrassing. You die from the cold. I got strep throat in mid-July, horrible trip, never again.

I traveled with my family on the 6th of July from Paris to London. We were more than 2 hours early. There was an endless queue to have the ticket validated. I had purchased the tickets online but the barcode did not pass, mine and my son's. That of the other members of the family did not cause any problems. Mysteries... They gave us 2 new tickets saying that the train was now full. That is, my son and I leave on the next train to the rest of the family. We waited, we informed ourselves and they gave us other tickets for a third time. In fact I have 3 tickets for the same train which also left one hour and 40 minutes late. Waiting in line for the updates to be made. A terrible organization that surprised me.

I bought a preferential train ticket to return from Paris to Barcelona, ​​thinking that it would be more or less like the bird, since the ticket is not cheap, much less than traveling in a clean, comfortable and why not safe carriage. Well, when you arrive at the Lyon station you find a chaos of people entering, some are looking for the number of their car and seat but with no luck because no one here informs you of anything. You enter and you already think that you have taken the wrong train and that it is a rodalies or something like that, because it is dirty, old and neglected. There is no space for suitcases, anarchy reigns, a woman traveling on the upper floor has had her purse stolen. I had planned to walk to the bar but I lost the desire. That they don't steal more from us and that they don't charge an arm and a leg for traveling in "preferential" waiting for minimally decent service, a total disappointment, these 7 hours are going to feel like forever.
Absolutely catastrophic... ordered a ticket via the internet... the TGV drove away from under our noses... it is impossible to change trains in one minute...
A Paris -> Perpignan for €227..But when will they stop increasing their prices?? It's beyond comprehension...

I booked our trip from Le Have To Paris St Lazare and back before leaving the US. You book on line and the people helping me were patient and extremely helpful. Which I really appreciated. You can chat with them on line any time. We rode first class but I think except for extra leg room, coach would be fine. They we’re on time and so much better than a stuffy bus. They were having a train strike when we were there and I was a little nervous about booking, they answered all my question know matter how small. Also, gave me a 50% off senior promotion. Nice way to see France

TGV Bordeaux-Paris in a short 2 hours 10 minutes - a fast 180-200 miles/hr does not feel uncomfortable, train is on time, comfortable, fast, clean, even the food is decent. If only we had trains like this in the US

We took the TGV from Basel, Switzerland to Paris.  The trip was fast and efficient. We booked first class tickets and enjoyed comfortable wide seats.  However, we almost missed the train when they changed the platform with little or no notice (I think there might have been an announcement but I couldn't understand it as it was very muffled).  Luckily, I realized something was wrong and rushed my husband and 2 kids with luggage in tow over to the correct platform with about 4 minutes to spare.No soap in a smelly bathroom.

This train used to be one of the worlds best but has been let down by their militant unions. Cancelled trains , long delays , poor service have been recent features. Still beats flying when it works but very hit & miss these days thanks to the unions.

As usual there's always something wrong 90% of the time they're on strike and if not something always pops up: we took one train from Paris to Bordeaux on June 30 where there has been an error in the train referral and a 35 minutes delay. we are at the moment on another train from Biarritz to Paris and we are stuck between Dax and Bordeaux coz there's an ongoing police operation and we don't know how long it will last! I think we will refrain from using any sncf means of transportation from now on and will advice our contacts against it

Booked well in advance for our trip from Geneva to Paris, got to the station only to find that our train had been cancelled.. we booked first class tickets, yet even though they had our details there was no notification by email of our train being cancelled. Went to the ticket desk in Geneva, and was told that the next train is full, “you could get on it, but you might have to stand”.We were put on the train after that, with allocated seating, but got to Paris 8 hours later than we should have, and missed our trip up the Eiffel Tower, for which we couldn’t get any money back from the tickets, but that’s another story..I wouldn’t waste my money again paying for 1st class tickets, because at the end of the day, all you really get is a bigger seat, nothing else...Also it is the slowest fast train I have ever been on, totally ridiculous, I wouldn’t waste my money again going by train. I know flights get cancelled too, but there are usually more options than what there was today...Customer service is terrible, do yourself a favour and skip this company if you can!!

Oui.sncf and sncf do not communicate with each other, impossible to get help to get the promised full refund after the train strikes. Only the staff at the stations are helpful, but even after one month still did not receive a refund, had to ask the credit card company for a charge back.Worst customer service ever! Will never buy a ticket again.
To strike they are the first in the Parcontre ranking at the personal level, and the service offered is the last. Can't wait for the competition to arrive! Outside the SNCF

Totally disrespectful and extremely rude staff! A shame in 2018!!! Simple frustrated civil servants who, in addition to going from strike to strike, feel superior! A means of transport to avoid as much as possible!!!!! Incredible but true!
Tgv Paris Turin PS, second class, 50 minutes late, disgusting bathrooms and usurious prices for restaurant service. Please do something to return the splendor of the past!

The TGV Lyria from Zurich to Paris is in the meantime not anymore up to date.The seats in first class are ok, but the rest is from the last century. No Wifi-serviceThe so-called “restaurant” is a jokeThe toilets are by far the most dirty and horrible place in the world, and I mean all of them. No in-seat-service whatsoeverIt is mindboggling how a company has so little clue about on-board services nowadays. Maybe we should all be just happy that there is a train service in France.

Paris-Milan train of 1 July 2018. Two carriages without air conditioners with a temperature of around 35 degrees and without working sockets. The train conductor says that it is dangerous to travel like this and that they would have had a technician pick up in Chambery. Obviously nothing changes. Unbearable journey, we ran away to the other carriages to look for some free seats. Sitting a little and on the floor a little. It's a shame because the first leg went well.
TGV Paris Milan. Train delayed, air conditioning not working. A terrible service. Other travel options to consider
High-speed train recommended for medium or long-distance journeys from France to Europe or vice versa.

Traveling to Paris from Barcelona by train is an option to consider. You leave from Sants station (center of Barcelona) and arrive at Gare de Lyon (center of Paris). But I warn you that it is officially a 6 hour journey or what is the same, 6:28 minutes in reality. Arrive late to Paris but never exceed 30 minutes to avoid having to pay part of the ticket price. The trains have two floors. All services are offered on the upper floor, so I recommend that if you travel on this train you choose this floor. If you are wondering which is better, traveling in economy class or first class? My answer is tourist. First class you pay more and it is exactly the same. Unlike Spanish high-speed trains, this French train offers you nothing.  Because it doesn't offer, it doesn't even offer movies. The trains are neglected, dirty. And if like me, you choose your seats on the lower deck, forget about seeing the cabin crew. What caught my attention was the informative announcements of the different stops during the journey. They are in Spanish, Catalan, French and English in Spanish territory and only in French in French territory. The cafeteria services are quite correct and their prices are similar to any other route. For me, expensive. The luggage areas are small. If like me you choose the lower floor, you will see how little civility we travelers have since travelers on the second floor leave their suitcases in the lower area to avoid climbing stairs with them and they end up piling up without order in the narrow exit.  I would like to highlight the difference in train access control. En la estación de Sants deberás pasar un control de seguridad de tu equipaje y el control de billetes antes de bajar al andén.  At Gare de Lyon, there is no baggage security check or ticket control. The conductor stops by your car already on the journey, if not almost when you are about to cross the border. Anyone can access the train and even get on it without anyone checking if they have a ticket, so be very careful with your belongings since “friends of others” get on the train with impunity. What's more, they go up two by two, one entertains you by asking you for a signature to support some solidarity initiative while another takes everything he can and more.

Booked several months in advance from Paris to Bayeux/Caen.  6 people hooking up with a special tour (over $500 tour) of Normany beaches.  Got to train station, 2 taxis, only to find train on strike.  No way to meet tour with short notice.  Filled claim, got future credit for ticket price only.  Expires in 12 months.  Do not live in France, at my age, almost 80, probably may never get back.

TGV Paris to Geneva and Turin to ParisApart from extra leg room, no other extra features, no WiFi, no snack trolley available,no restaurant car, buffet bar poorly stocked with only a limited array of snacks - for a six hour journey this is unacceptable. Toilets dirty. Similar lack of facilities were evident on outward leg from Paris to Geneva
Took the TGV to travel for CDG Airport in Paris. It can hot inside the train. Ride was good overall.

Friends and I caught the TGV from Paris to Avignon, then Avignon to Lille (Belgium) and from there back to Paris. An economical and fantastic way to travel across the country and see the scenery. We bought first class tickets for each of the trips - well worth it and still cheaper than flights and more convenient than trying to get to a nearby airport. It was great to see the cities and towns and the surrounding landscape which you cant do if you take flights all the time. Australians just need to understand that you buy two tickets - one to get onto the train and then one for the seat. Going first class is also a better option - comfier, wider seats with a table, access to a good sized bathroom (more than just a toilet) and of course a buffet car. There is also much more space for luggage. Have also caught a TGV from Vienna to Zurich - we went economy; trip was great but travelling first class is infinitely better..

We have traveled from Hendaye to Paris and the comfort of the TGV is spectacular. With table, plug, USB, and Wi-Fi, perfect for connecting to the computer. It is a shame that on the Hendaye-Bordeaux section it cannot develop the cruising speed of the TGV.

Upon arrival in the carriage, reception by a typical SNCF perfume (it stinks!). Stained carpet, blocked seat, toilet.....no comment!!!   I forgot to tell you that the train was at its departure station, which would have made us hope that it was clean. Last oversight, we were in 1st class.  Shame on France
Traveled to zurich from paris ona 320 KMPH ride, comfortable and fast. Be sure to check the calendar before hand as french strike might play a spoil sport.

on June 21, 2018, I took the Cherbourg train to Guinganp, being disabled, I was offered the service (access plus) and the surprise I didn't believe it, I was accompanied at each train change, because you should know that on this line 2 changes, so each time someone came to carry my luggage, and in times of strike not obvious for the SNCF staff, I say well done to them they have been at the top, I wanted to say it because for me I saw it as impossible thank you to the staff for their kindness and once again well done it's still free Veronique

- Staff is unfriendly - Credit card payment not possible on the train Restaurant - Seats rattle and are outdated - Very bad 1st class - Long delays - Always affected by strikes - Price / performance (1st class) very poor

Even with the sncf app installed and a moderate understanding of the language, it is difficult to find out whether the desired train is running or not. In addition, with a ticket more expensive than a plane ticket, it was really difficult to sit in a seat that was designed for children. I also found out in advance that there is a restaurant on the train, but of course there was no service. As compensation, the fastest ones got a bottle of water. Well, besides, the ticket exchange process was easy after first trying all possible combinations, why couldn't my ticket be found in the system. But everyone has their own way of filling the trains to the limit and raising extra money at the last minute.

Hello everyone, do not take out insurance on the SNCF site with Allianz, they process the files as follows: incomplete file, then in processing then closed file. No explanation, no refund, for insurance purchased for missed train. All this for a plane delay with Air Caraibes, ticket purchased in direct flight Sint Maarten / Paris and NO.... kerosene refueling in Pointe à Pitre, hence a significant delay in Paris to take the TGV......

Hello, my connection being canceled I cannot make my trip, Allianz asks me for proof of NON-responsibility of the SNCF which of course I cannot obtain despite what is written on the sites. There is also a telephone number but when I call the answering machine tells me to go on the internet! In short the SNCF is over for me I will take Blablacar or similar.

I travelled from Brussels to Le Mans. From Brussels to Paris, I took a Thalys in premium class. In this class your meal is included like in an airplane and the food is served at your seat. Wine comes with it too. Unfortunately, only the vegetarian menu was left for me. Because of travel delay I missed my train to le mans in Paris. Because it was the last train I got a good hotel room for free.

The SNCF announces that it reimburses trains on strike days: this is false. Impossible to access the claim forms, impossible to claim at the station, impossible to claim from Eurostar which says that it is from the SNCF that you must be reimbursed. Avoid the SNCF until it disappears. No competition and real professionals

Ticket reserved 15 days in advance and confirmed by SNCF; On the day of departure, places are no longer numbered. Free placement, a real mess. The controller hides. Technical outage lasting 30 minutes in Metz. Wagons in a deplorable state of cleanliness, dilapidated and dirty As they say: we don't stick our thumbs, "we stick together, but that doesn't make things move forward, quite the contrary
