this is a far better way to travel to the Costa Brava than stuck in airports. if you are lucky enough to be on the top deck the views are stunning

A weekend in Paris, this time taking the Thalys. A disappointing experience. The train sets are very outdated and not very comfortable. I press my knees against the hard back of the seat in front of me. No USB ports for your mobile devices (there is a power socket, but it doesn't work), no catering in second class and general chaos when boarding. I could only book a ticket without a guaranteed seat, which means that you give up your possible seat at every stop and then have to look for another seat. For me, next time it's the plane again; same price (or cheaper, if you book wisely, faster and no musical chairs. Unfortunately more polluting, but in my opinion Thalys is not an alternative
No TGV office at ZURICH main station. Limited displays and lack of information will make it difficult to board. Overall average cleanliness and just ok service

Gare de Lyon - Lausanne (Switzerland)The advantages compared to the plane are that the TGV Lyria generally leaves on time and takes you inside Paris. The disadvantages are that: - the cars are quite busy, armchairs not very comfortable, vibration, even in first class. - even with a reservation, there is always someone to occupy your seat - no drinks or snacks offered

Took Thalys from Paris Gare Du Nord to Amsterdam Centraal. US$220+@ on goeuro.com. Got to our seats to discover them occupied by non-English and non-French speaking individuals. After we showed them our tickets, they stood up and left. Later we saw them and a couple of others hanging out in the dining car, sitting on the floor with their bags. Unsure whether these passengers actually had tickets.Good wifi, very polite lady bartender, working outlets, common space to store luggage, but the toilets were tiny, dimly-lit and smelly. Plus everything was just so RED.

In March 2018 I took a tour of different European cities (start and end in Milan) and traveled via TGV from Nice to Marseille, Marseille to Lyon and Lyon to Brussels as a stopover to arrive in Bruges. I found the first class excellent (Wi Fi on board always included) and what makes it highly recommended for me is the sales and after-sales service. I bought all my tickets online and always had an online chat service on hand to resolve any type of question immediately to my satisfaction.

Boccolini menu developed by chefs...... Very bad image for the chefs... I took the chicken lemon menu of the day, not too horrible but nothing crazy but above all NOTHING to eat!!! For 17 euros 3 mini pieces of chicken..... And the worst, dessert! Chocolate ganache... A horrible taste! Above all, avoid these overpriced and mediocre menus....
More and more dirty, more and more expensive, more and more run down, more and more late even when there are no real reasons.

We booked tickets for the Strasbourg-Paris route in advance, the train was always on time and the seat reservation was perfect, unfortunately all announcements are only made in French, it would also be good in English, but that's the only thing we have to criticize. Clean train and clean toilets on the train. Will travel with the TGV again

My wife and I decided to take the train from Paris to Amsterdam instead of flying.  We booked it online several weeks prior.  It was a Monday train and it was quite full.  We managed to book Comfort Class with a table (facing each other) which was very nice.  The journey itself was smooth and issue-free.  All all-around good experience and would recommend it as an alternative to driving/flying.

We took Thallys from Amsterdam to Paris. On time. It was very comfortable, good wifi, a cable coupler in the middle, under the retractable table in front of you. You can work with your laptop if you need it.
We missed the Le Havre-Paris train because of the railway workers' strike. We had to take the bus. What a loss. Let's not be alarmed, there will be more railway workers' strikes.

Train departing from Milan Porta Garibaldi to Chambery (250 km - like Florence - Rome approx.) price 60 euros second class. Really embarrassing. Very dirty train, sockets not working, only 1 train conductor/chief, smell in the carriage of dirty old upholstery (like when you enter a room closed for a long time with a dusty sofa inside), seats to report.. In Italy I would have defamed the train conductor if I had found this disgusting thing, here I seemed to be the strange one.. bhooo.. look at the photos and judge for yourself.

In Paris Marseille I pass right behind a toilet cleaner. I tell myself that there is progress, but once inside there are no hand towels and soap, and the dryer does not work. Which left him unfazed! Anything.

Like all high-speed train systems in Europe, first of all you have to take into account what these services offer and what they do not offer. It is not practical if it is full of suitcases or with many children or very distant destinations. In the first case, choose a micro (bus) and, in the second, a plane. I have never had problems with reservations or punctuality.

I took the TGV (train grand vitesse) from Paris to Lyon, it is a semi-fast train (no more than 200 km/h) the first one does not have WiFi, the seats are very close to each other and to really compare them with the Italian ones, they have no chance

Elevators out of action, mega queues. No assistance readily available. Add to that TGV trains delayed so much that we missed our connection and ended up stranded at 2 am. Ticket cost 179 Euro. After months of waiting, they deign to refund 44.50 Euro. BUT we have to send the ticket registered post. Cost £6. Definite - give TGV, Interrail and Gard de North a wide berth.

Our travel agent in Australia booked us on a 9am train and when we got there, we discovered that our train had been cancelled due to a strike. So we found an official who directed us to an office (what turned out to be a ticketing office), an another staff member who spoke English, helped us transfer to a later train which was four hours later. We were not happy but the time passed quickly at the station, which is huge, and we eventually left for Hendaye.  There are shops for coffee and food. The bad thing about this was, we had booked and paid for first class tickets but none were available on the later train. In hindsight, I think we should of known how to check the train schedule the day before because we could of changed to the later train then and had a better chance of scoring a first class seat again. Another tip is to get on the train early if you have luggage as the baggage compartments may be full by the time you get on and this ill mean you have to store yours in another carriage out of sight. We did find navigating our way around th station to the platforms daunting when we first arrived. But the staff were helpful and all over the station. S

We were lucky that our trains were the only ones that ran, despite the strike. Railtour Suisse provided good support regarding the strike. The trip was good, fast and comfortable (1st class, Zurich - Paris). But don't expect too much from the on-board service or infrastructure. (Food, toilets, etc.) TGV is a really good alternative to the plane, as it arrives quickly and directly in the center.

We took the TGV first class from Gare de Lyon to Avignon as a 3 hr train ride seemed a much better option than a 7+ hr drive. Still happy with the choice but SNCF employees really need to spend less time going on strike and more time cleaning and maintaining their equipment.The ride was smooth and although 10 min delayed still a better option than driving but lots of things could be improved:1. The tray table was dirty. Not only dirty that you can see the dirt when you wipe it but food crumb collected on the tray on both my seat and my wife’s.  We wiped down the trays with wet  tissue before we used them and the tissue was black afterward. Nasty, huh!?2. The seat back holder made of cords on my seat had broken cords and a hole in the bottom. Was obvious and had this been any airline I fly, I know it would have been spotted and replaced.3. The toilet didn’t have any soap. The part of the soap dispenser that normally contains the soap was missing.I’d still recommend the TGV instead of a long drive but bring something to wipe down the area around you and some soap or hand sanitiser. Pretty sad comment on ‘first class’ travel huh?SNCF, Air France ... less striking, more doing the basics of the job would be a big step forward.

I'm literally on the train now in 1er carriage. The interior is dated but in the least it is clean. Everything is quite basic, most notably the business seat. It resembles an airline premium economy seat (at best). I passed on lunch, but I am quite disappointed (in 2018) to find the drinks served in plastic cups. It's barely excusable in 2ieme but reprehensible and pedestrian for a 1er service. On the positive side, the internet is remarkably fast and consistent.

I loved this experience.  6 hours from Gare de Lyon to Barcelona Sants beats extra transit time from central Paris to an airport, getting there 1.5-2 hrs early, the hassle of checkin and security, inevitable delays in boarding and taking off, waiting for luggage at destination, and the rather long ride from Barcelona airport to the city center.Instead, you show up to Gare de Lyon 10-20 minutes early, find your seat without any hassle, and not long after you are cruising along at 260-300 km/hr with a nice view of the French countryside.  You don't have to keep your seat belt on, the WC are plentiful, you can walk around, there's wi-fi (!!), and when you get to Barcelona, you are right in the thick of the city, not 30 minutes away by their (admittedly very nice) special airport transit line.It was my first time seeing the Mediterranean and the Pyrenees, all from the comfort of my seat.

With a stop in Rotterdam, Antwerp and Brussels South, you can be in the middle of Paris in about 3.5 hours by Thalys. Comfortable with an average of 250 km/h. Reservations are required and you will have your own seat. There is a restaurant, toilet and a rack for large suitcases.

65 euros each for a 2 hour trip that lasted 3 hours due to delays. We were in first class. The train had a 30 minute delay, proceeded very slowly and made a noise that resembled that of a hungry beast. In addition our car had no toilet paper. I told the attendant and she said she already knew that but they had no paper on the train so I would just have to find another coach with a bathroom that did have it. Inexcusable!

Business trip - book first/business class. Was very busy (due to imminent strikes). Seats were OK - was expecting more but plenty of space. Power socket and WiFi available though lost connection many times. Drinks bar was crowded but fine. Trip itself was flawless. Best to order & confirm well in advance

We traveled very early in December from Marne la Valee (Disneyland) to Brussels, my considerations are the following. In the equation, speed and simplicity to reach the destination is unmatched, it beats the plane, the punctuality is optimal, the seats are comfortable and they have a practical table, its ride is very quiet and the high speed it develops is not felt in the slightest. On the other hand, I could say that it is difficult to travel with a lot of luggage, since the racks available per car are very few, and on the seats with a lot of luck you can locate a carry.on. Another detail that I had on my trip was that by decision of the company the planned stopover in Lille became a transfer to another train, it was not so serious except that the announcement on board the train was only made in French so we were fasting until we saw the general movement of the passengers and one of them noticed our situation and informed us in English what was happening.

The TGV Lyria is a most underwhelming experience. I upgraded at a discount to FC. The only thing FC about it was the seat, and even that didn't have working electricity, to OR from! Many of the seat's garbage bins were missing, and the bathrooms were tiny, sticky, and smelled of urine from the outset. There's no WiFi, even if you wanted to buy the option ( that blew my mind).To top it all off, I was ripped off by the employee manning the restaurant who overcharged me €10 for a pack of Metro tickets (my fault for not getting receipt, ugh!). Train travel is certainly relaxing, but annoying when your books on your phone to save space, and you can't even charge it during a 4-5 hour trip. Poor experience.

They sold me $1080 euros for 4 tickets without seats. Horrible company that only wants to make money from first time travelers going on the train. Who would have thought they would sell 4 tickets for $1080 euros WITHOUT SEATS. I would NEVER recommend this train for anyone...

Used from Charles de Gaulle Airport to Avignon. As I was about to leave Japan and the strike began, I had booked a night bus from Haneda to Avignon because I really wanted to get there on the same day. I thought about repurchasing the TGV ticket departing from Gare de Lyon for about 7,000 yen cheaper, but in the end I decided to take the TGV from the airport. It was my first TGV so I had high expectations, but even the first class seats were not very clean and were average. The exterior was also quite dirty. German DB is much prettier. Arrived on time.

The TGVs are incredible... Unbelievable in discomfort! Fortunately it goes faster and faster because your lower back will quickly ask you to finish them. The ideal would be to return to 3rd class carriages with wooden benches. You took the path with the 5-person bench at the back of the lower rooms in second

We used the TGV from Gare du Nord Paris , to Amsterdam .All precooked and prepaid on line in Sydney Australia, and tickets with reserved seating all printed at home . Despite the late arrival of the train from its inbound journey , we left only ten minutes late , and the train was clean quiet and problem free . Highly recommended

Really terrible service, they made me book a train and hotel to Paris a month in advance, reassuring me that strikes DO NOT EXIST for them, and then one day before departure, as if nothing had happened, they sent me an email canceling my trip!!!!  AND NOW WHO WILL REFUND MY HOTEL????  In Italy something like this could never have happened!!! THANK YOU OUI.SNCF, THANK YOU FRANCE!!!!!!!!!!!

Thello Milan-Paris P6QUY reservation made in March for 2 adults and two children in a sleeping car. Today, looking around on some websites, I see that on 27,28,29 April there is a strike on the French railways and then on the Thello website that the Thello train will be replaced by a coach. 12 hour night trip sitting in the coach instead of 12 hours lying in the sleeping cabin, big difference. But the problem is that I have not received any information from Thello, I am registered and they know my reservation, email and telephone, but they have never heard from me, good service to their customers, given that the strike is announced by law 30 days in advance. After a phone call to Paris (there is no telephone number in Italy) they tell me that I can request the SIC refund or take the coach. Thanks to they......I made a request for a refund on the Thello website and I received news that I will have a response (not a refund) within 30 working days. It seems like a company of incapable, badly organized and other things that I don't write. Better to choose alternatives. Think VERY carefully before booking with Thello!!!!! Solved by yourself with a Vueling flight. Avoid people, avoid

Beware!!!! If you purchase tickets in advance, online from the Oui/sncf.com, make sure you get insurance. They have a no refund policy and they don't budge. I had to cancel my trip to Europe due to an unplanned hip replacement surgery, and they told me there is nothing they can do about it, absolutely no refunds!!! What a rip-off!!!! Horrible customer service, SHAME!

I'm a regular, I've always traveled 2nd class, I wonder if I shouldn't continue to do so. First time in 1st class today, I was thinking of a peaceful and peaceful journey: anything but! People constantly getting up from their seats, children shouting from one side to the other in the corridors, people talking and shouting as if they were at home... Rather than taking the airplane which would mean going to the airport, check-in, security check, then at Paris waiting for your luggage, transferring from the airport to the center, we’ve decided to take the train: „center to center“. It’s a six hour trip if you take the French high speed train TGV.Coming from Munich, Augsburg, Ulm, Stuttgart or Karlsruhe, you don’t need to change trains, because the TGV will stop there (same in the opposite direction of course).Some technical information:They use French double deck high speed trains. Maximum speed is 320 km/h on the French high speed line between Strasbourg and Paris. In Germany the highest speed is reached between Stuttgart and Karlsruhe (250 km/h). On all other tracks within Germany the trains runs at the the same speed as IC and ICE trains as it shares their tracks.We booked seats in the First Class (Sparpreis Europa Ticket). Seats are very comfortable with table lights at club seats (seats facing each other). The seating is 2 / 1 (two seats on one side of the aisle and one seat on the other side). All center aisle coaches (saloon coaches).The coach with the bar is located between the first and second class coaches. Additionally a mini bar service will pass by as well. In the first class area you can order snacks or meals from the bar at your seat. There are several luggage areas (due to the limited space in double deck coaches the overhead compartments can only be used for very small luggage. 220 V AC power outlets can be found at each seat.Free wifi is available for the entire trip. Although I was not able to access with my reservation number you can click on „foreign ticket“ to get „limited“ access that will be renewed every hour. In both directions our train was delayed for a few minutes: on the way to Paris due to a technical problem after being connected with another TGV at Strasbourg that was coming from Colmar (it seemed that the train driver had to reset all systems) and on the way back to Munich due to abandoned luggage at Paris.Customer information (in German, French and English) is very good; in my opinion much better than on German trains.In both directions the train seemed to be fully booked but as seat reservation is mandatory there was no chaos on the train.

It was dirty, no toilet paper, a free-for-all on seating (even though our previous ticket had been first class, and a family of five sat across and next to us and the toddler screamed and threw toys the entire trip. What should have been an hour long train ride was three plus hours, and then there was a three hour delay because our original train was cancelled and we had to wait on this one instead. If we were to have hired a driver or gotten a taxi, we would have saved five hours today and paid about the same amount. We are only in Paris a short time and an entire half day wasted is a big deal. Don't use the train. Do uber or lyft or a taxi or even hire a private driver with a nice big Mercedes. It will be more cost effective and you won't sit in a cold terminal for hours and then stare out the window hours more wondering why the train keeps slowing and stopping.
We traveled from Marseille to Paris. Fast, ultra-quiet and considerably comfortable train. Departure and arrival on time.

What was supposed to be a 3 hour travel from Switzerland to Paris took us more than 5 hours. The food sold is bad and the toilet is so disgusting. For tourists like me, if you intend to going to Paris and taking the train and arriving in Paris Gare Lyon, I would suggest that you just fly. The train ride and train station are both horrible experiences.

The TGV is a good solution for long distance trips inside France. As its name says, it is a very fast train. But.Delays are very frequent, change of timetables and of course the extremely high prices for their service. As far as the rest (not TGV) of the trains -connections are concerned, avoid it if you can. Rural railways are dirty and smelly, very frequently dalayed or cancelled without notice, in some lines you will have to travel standing up (more than 45 minutes) because they're always overcrowded.And pray not to have a trip planned on a day the SNCF decides to go on strike...Since it is the only train company in France they rely on this monopoly to be as horrible as possible. If you have a cancellation or delay due to them, you have no right to anything (RER etc). If on the other hand you get on an earlier train than yours (even without seat) you pay a fine. Actually, beware, you could pay a fine for everything that you can imagine on a SNCF  train (French Railway Society) according to their need to collect money.Avoid it

we chose the TGV line to move from Paris to Amsterdam, in about two hours. Few stops at some stations. Not very friendly staff at baggage check-in, which took place in pouring rain. It is not permitted to board other carriages other than the one marked on the ticket, which is scrupulously checked individually with the ID. Cleaning ok.
Less than an hour and a half METZ - PARIS EST in first class, it's really the capital at your fingertips

What a disappointing experience - paid for first class as we departed at 18.23 for a 3 hour journey. Given the website referenced meals, had expected a meal would be served. No such luck. About 60 mins we got served a quarter sandwich and a pudding cup. That was dinner! I'm sorry but the service was clearly over dinner time and if you don't get dinner at this time then when does it kick in??Add to that toilets that rivalled those I'd used on trains in Sri Lanka. Floor covered in urine and the stench! I resorted to rolling up my jeans. Seat was comfortable. Had expected wifi too but no on that front too. I should have stuck with plan A of flying instead.

We barely had our train, so no time to buy food beforehand. So we chose the restaurant car (no choice either😊). Our train left at 12:27 p.m., meal time, hence the hour-long wait for an industrial sandwich. Just one person to take orders, cash, prepare and serve. An experience that should definitely not be repeated...

The train is a fast and comfortable way to get to Milan.  But be warned that the big number on the side of the train is not the carriage number.  The carriage number is on the tiny electronic sign in the window that you don't even notice.Many people must be getting in the right carriage just be chance.  Or are right enough that it doesn't matter.  I got on the carriage for the train that split off at Grenoble, and had 4 minutes to get myself and my luggage on the correct train so I wasn't stranded in France.If you get stuck in this situation don't panic (like I did).  You only need to get to the back of the first train, and there's time for that if not enough to get to your carriage.  You can push your luggage through with some effort.The staff are not helpful at all in this situation.  There are no officials checking tickets or directing passengers.  You don't find out until it's too late.  The ticket collector didn't explain and it was only by googling that I found out how little time I had to get my stuff together and make a run for it.  Fellow passengers were very helpful, letting know the situation and helping me find my carriage.  I feel like this error is mostly on me, but also that some information regarding carriage signs (on TGV or Gare de Lyon website) could avoid this sort of thing from happening.

Working for the railway in Canada I always tell my wife that I have no interest in travelling by train.  Quite honestly I'm just tired of being on trains.  As this was the high speed version I relented to travelling this one time by train.  We travelled this time from Paris to Amsterdam.  The total trip took about three hours.  I would say my overall experience was a complete surprise.  We travelled second class as we heard that the difference was minimal.  The seating and ride itself were great.  My one complaint would be the aisles in the coach were a bit narrow.  This lack of room made it hard to get our luggage to our seats.  Probably not a big deal if you are travelling with small suitcases but we were travelling to three countries over a couple weeks.  I would absolutely recommend this service to get you around Europe.

I bought my tgv ticket as I landed. It was easy enough to find the station, the service to buy a ticket was great and then the travel was easy . The train clean and has wifi charging spots if anything a vending machine for water would have been nice . I will definitely travel like this again the train made my trip so easy !!

Traveled to straussburg, and any other option would have taken a lot longer. Just a few tips if you are not from the country...Buy tickets early, you will get an signed seat. Use the mobile app, the website tries to guess at your location and sucks if you aren't from the EU. The Paris station is a little walk from the airport, so plan for it.The coach numbers aren't obviously posted - look for an LCD screen on the coach to confirm. Better still look up the expected location on the screens as you walk into the platform.Get a window seat. It is fun to watch the world fly by.

We were taking two river cruises, one on the Seine and the other on the Rhone river.  To get to Lyon, Viking cruises made arrangements for us to travel on the TGV.  Aside from Viking doing an excellent job in shepherding us from the Le Pecq port to Paris TGV train station, making sure we were on the correct train, in the appropriate class coaches, and telling us which Lyon station to get off of, the TGV is an incredible way to travel over 280 miles in 2 hours 10 minutes.  The train was very clean, comfortable, quiet, with wifi.  Of course, Viking transported our luggage separately so we didn't have to deal with any luggage.  And of course we were met at the Lyon station by Viking reps to take us to our ship.  Needless to say, I would definitely travel by TGV again - so much nicer than going through the airport.  If you found this review helpful, please click on the thank button below.

I have used Sncf on previous trips ... but it seemed much easier to make arrangements on line this time... what I found the best!!! They offer booking a cab to pick you up at wherever you are staying taking you to train station and the same at destination... so on ... you pay up front... they text the day before and driver texts you on his way & when the cab arrives! Excellently & you can cancel online or rearrange... very impressed!Thank you...you French are the best!!!
It was narrow but clean, and since you just pile your suitcases in the aisle, there are no pickpockets in the winter, so I was a little scared, but I was relieved.

clean train, functional air conditioning, very decent 2nd class seats, discreet clientele, functional wifi, affable and courteous, even pleasant controller, overpriced drinks, that's the only downside...train on time, PARIS STRASBOURG swallowed in less time than it took me to read 1 newspaper and 1 automobile magazine... in short, it remains the best current high-speed train in Europe, whatever people say!!!

We used thello going from Verona to Paris on November 1st and returning on the 5th. The carriages are of low quality and poor maintenance: in one the heating didn't work and in another the night lights. Toilets are insufficient and poorly served. The restaurant service is of the lowest quality. Friendly and helpful staff. Given the price and the quality provided by the overall service, we strongly advise against using this mode of transport.

- Trains, old vehicles, WI-FI NOT WORKING, there are no screens in the carriages EVEN in 1st class; average cleanliness of trains, There are no screens in the carriages, Limited bar serviceMilan C. Monaco, Monte-Carlo routeIt is possible that more modern trains are in circulation but in all cases not on the Milan-Nice route

October 20: The delivery men had been waiting in front of the car for 40 minutes. Their elevator was not working. And since the head wasn't working either(!) they didn't move even though a working elevator was available 10m away! A more resourceful employee gave them a lecture but 3 minutes before the train left...all this at 8 p.m. on a big departure day on a train that costs a lot!!! (Bordeaux Tgv) The other day: a 3 km queue, an unspeakable mess because of the inappropriate online ordering service, which only serves to annoy everyone, the waiter who is always alone and who cannot prepare his orders given that the forklift....(see first case or any other case of logical negligence) the customers who have ordered online and who blush to be served before other customers who have been waiting for a hour.The other day again: strikeThe other day: oven breakdownThe other day again: no coffee on a morning train. it sucks! And often: disgusting dishes (the shredded beef is to vomit), staff on the verge of a nervous breakdown (we understand them!), a bar that is neither done nor made. Don't hesitate to complete and share. Maybe that will stir them up. We can always dream. When are they going to put two competitors on the same train? It would perhaps work better. There I was complaining, it's better but what's wrong with me!!!
Choose ''IDZEN" option while booking your train ticket if you prefer a journey in a serene environment. Enjoy your read or music with absolute no disturbance!

From Ländle quickly to Paris, then only with TGV. From Stuttgart to the French border it zips comfortably through the countryside; unfortunately the existing track infrastructure does not allow for high speeds. But then it accelerates properly. Before you know it you are in the city of Paris, no airport stress, no too much squeezing, everything is fine. If you book in time you will also get a good price for the ticket.
What  a way to travel , the french certainly have got trains sorted , i would quite happily travel on these train everyday especially at the speed they go bravo

The first time on the TGV dates back to more than 20 years ago: excellent. A few days ago, together with my husband, we traveled on this historic train from Turin P.Susa to Paris: comfortable and spacious seats but not exactly clean, barely adequate catering service (everything served very cold) saved by the kindness of the attendant. ABSOLUTELY sore point: the toilets. Simply DISGUSTING, DIRTY, SMELLY. Their use is justified by pure and simple need: 5 and a half hours of travel necessarily imply a visit to the toilet even if one would gladly do without it. I don't think I will repeat the experience.
For people sensitive to the direction of travel, it is important to note that the train changes direction after Marseille.

Just returned from Paris after we finished our extended Viking Rhone River Cruise. Utilized TGV, booked by Viking, for a TOTALLY smooth and FAST ride ( though you don't feel you're traveling about 190 mph) fom Lyon to Paris.It's a totally positive experience and it was all managed by Viking Reps. Best yet....we the travelers didn't need to drag our luggage to and from the train! You can't believe the relief of the cruise company handling the baggage. How wonderful! We needed to do this on our own previously and what a pleasant difference.Enjoy the experience......Take the TGV.

The best means of transportation between Paris and London. We had no problems other than experiencing the vacuum effect while crossing the English Channel. Apart from the breathtaking views while passing through the plains of France, the comfort and service were also very pleasing. When you buy your ticket early, you can get this pleasure and fast transportation at very reasonable prices. The only difference is that you will pass through customs when boarding the train, so proceed accordingly.

Family trip (with three girls) on Thalys, Paris-Amsterdam section, departing from Gare du Nord. The trip was super comfortable and on time. Traveling with two teenagers and a girl can be complicated, but in this case the comfort of the train and especially the access to WiFi, made this round trip an excellent family experience. Totally recommended.
Trip from Nice to Paris and back on time. The carriages were clean, the seats comfortable. Absolutely AVOID the catering service inside the train

TGV Lyria is a French-Swiss railway company, belonging to the French SNCF group and SBB Switzerland. The TGV Lyria trains connect France and Switzerland, the carriages are good and the journey is quick. I bought my ticket in advance online, ticket cost from Paris to Zuerich €64.00. Boarding was via Gare de Lyon, TGV Lyria 9213 at 12:23 pm and arrival in Zuerich at 4:26 pm, covering a distance of 610 KM in 4:03 am, with stops in the cities of Dijon, Mulhouse and Basel. Very good

traveled from Paris to Milan with final destination Padua. Preferred over the plane because we also had two large and practically empty suitcases, as well as the advantage of having the Gare De Lyon two metro stops from us. hotel and avoid all the hassles of the airport (checks - waiting for baggage). Rather dated train, with slightly narrow seats (2nd class) and cleanliness that could be improved. Our "arrows" are definitely better. Very slow route, although at times with pleasant scenery, from Grenoble to Turin. Partiti puntuali e arrivati con 10 minuti di ritardo . Did not use the restaurant service.  We paid, booking more than a month in advance, 118 euros for two.

The ouigo trains departing from Marne la Vallée towards Bordeaux are clean and the staff at reception and on the train are top notch. To avoid spoiling anything, the price at certain periods defies all competition.

This is a scenic train - not a fast train-- with some really remarkable views of the Alps. The cars are on the small side with almost no dining facilities for a lengthy trip and questionable toilet facilities. The train starts out as one long train and the splits apart with a very few car arriving in Milan.

Trains are generally old and the interior worn out.Bathrooms though available are unusable because of the filth and smell.I had a quiet car, yet the couple behind had a very noisy child and the conductor never showed.Computer assigns seats that are NOT changeable and splits families or groups.!I would choose alternative whenever possible.

After a week in Paris we took the day high speed train to Milan. We purchased the tickets direct rather than through an agent and therefore at a more discounted rate. Likewise, we purchased second class not first after reading reviews and realising that for a lot more you didn't get much. The second class seats were excellent and we packed wine and nibbles and before boarding purchased a light lunch. It made for a fun day watching the beautiful and changing French countryside pass by. Overall highly recommended although internet on the trains would have been a bonus. We found that even on trains which advertised wifi it didn't work anyway. This is one of the many hit/miss things you will find define travel in Europe. The great advantage is that you can get up and walk around and even spend time in the dining car.

Neither of us have ever traveled by train in Europe, but when it came to going from Paris to Aix en Provence, we decided the TGV made sense. We are now so happy we unlocked this way of travel for us. Fast, really fast and with little to no hassle. Of course, when we say little to no hassle, we did had a driver to the station and an escort when we arrived to help with directions and luggage. Now, that we understand the logistics, we would not need all that service in the future. We enjoyed our downstairs seating across from each other. Next time we go from city to city, it is a train for us.

I rode from Toulouse to Montparnasse in Paris. Purchase tickets at Rail Europe. The ticket was changeable, but I was told that changes could only be made on-site. That's quite unkind. TGV was better than I expected. 4 hours and 19 minutes to Paris. It ran at the same speed as other express trains to Bordeaux, but traveled 320 km from Bordeaux to Montparnasse. Relax and enjoy the local scenery of France. Although it was a first class car, it also had a USB power source, power outlet, and WIFI. Although WIFI sometimes doesn't connect in rural areas, it worked well enough. I was told that there were coin lockers in Montparnasse, but they were closed due to renovations.

The first time I used the TGV I was surprised by the low level of passenger service but they explained to me that in France the use of this type of railway service is much more rooted than in Italy, as if to say that they use it like we use a regional train. It's an interesting point of view, but spending many hours on a train would probably require better comfort.

We traveled from Paris to Brussels and back. The journey is beyond praise! Twenty hours at a speed of 300 km/h and you’re there! The seats are large and comfortable. Before we had time to leave the station, we were fed a delicious and hearty breakfast, and dinner on the way back! I recommend it to everyone for traveling around France and Europe! It is better to buy tickets in advance and online. It turns out significantly cheaper.

The trip from Munich to Paris was comfortable, great legroom and good storage options. The service was also quick and friendly. The WiFi didn't work on the outward or return journey. If you advertise it, it should work.

The railways of France are at their best. When planning the trip, I bought all the tickets online on the TGV website 3 months in advance - 2 or even 3 times cheaper than directly at the station. We even managed to take the Paris-Nice night train. Everyone is on the level, everyone is happy. I have been traveling by rail in France for several years now, and I am very pleased.

The ride was from Geneva to Gare de Lyon in Paris. Although it has a sense of speed, I am concerned about some vibration and noise. Swiss National Railways was so quiet and comfortable that you couldn't tell when it started moving. Of course, you can't compare them because the train speeds are different. The atmosphere inside the train is like a country train. My expectations were betrayed.

We took the TaGV train from Paris to Nantes and the trip was on time and went without a hitch. Nice, clean train with comfy seats and space in each car for luggage.couldn't make use of the bar car as the line was too long. On our return, we took the Ouigo train, which is similar to the TGV, only much cheaper at 10 Euro, plus 5 Euro for bags. Book our tickets online through trainline.com. Smooth, no problems.The problem with Ouigo is all emails are in French, but I had the hotel translate when I received my tickets via email. With Ouigo you must show up at least 30 minutes early to check in. A real bonus was we could take the train from Nantes directly to Charl de Gaule airport with having to change trains in Paris. Nice feature as the airport has it's own train station next to terminal 2.

One would expect Wi-Fi (no way), one would expect service from the train team (forget it, they are French), one would expect quality working seat (no - under repair), one would expect a smooth ride (the last 40 minutes after Bourg en Bresse are simply horrible)All in all for an experienced non-tourist traveler an unacceptable solution.The same applies for the Paris - Vallorbe - Lausanne train.

Everyone envy us French cuisine. Everyone envy us the TGV. But, no one should objectively envy us "French cuisine" in the TGV! The whole concept needs to be reviewed: endless waiting in the service corridor, the very metallic, very noisy, disconcertingly sad "kitchen" corner, the role of the service heater, the "food" and its presentation. In short, on the Richter scale of junk food and bad taste, we are at the maximum! This splendid achievement that is the TGV really deserves much better...

In September 2017 we made a pilgrimage to Lourdes and took the TGV from Paris to Lourdes. The journey was very pleasant and very quick. No “fighting” for a seat, as a seat is allocated with every booking. We drove the almost 900 km in 4 1/2 hours. The cleanliness of our two trains (including the return journey) was excellent. WiFi was available free of charge the entire route. The only "complaint": The announcements were only in French, no German, no English. Tip 1: There is a price calendar on the TGV website. If you are flexible with your time, really great special prices are possible. Tip 2: Book seats on the upper level so you can see more of the country.

I took the train to go to Paris and it was dirty, you couldn't enter the bathrooms at all and the conductor behaved very badly towards me and other passengers, saying "I'm the conductor, if you don't like it, get off" and this was because we complained about how the train was.

Smiling and friendly staff. Train clean and in good condition. The TGV was on time. Breakfast was free and of very good quality. The price was very good, considering that tickets were purchased 3 months in advance. For me, flawless. THANKS.

It was my first time experience to really ride one of the fasted train the world, and then TGB indeed was one the best rated bullet service train. I ride the train from Paris to Toulouse, there was only one issue though, it became bit tricky to find the railway platform sometime, arrive at least half an hour early.

We travelled as part of a large group using the TGV to travel between Paris and Milan, and the return journey. Even leaving Paris where SNCF have direct control the train was filthy internally, 30 years ago the TGV was 'cutting edge' now it's worn and uncared for, the return from Italy was even worse with no water to flush the toilets or wash your hands (as seasoned travellers we carry baby wipes for such contingencies) and half way through the journey no more toilet paper (removed as no water to flush?). We were considering another venture to Italy with the same organisation, but following this trip and the TGV experience we'd rather fly.

I travelled from Loches to Paris.  An SNCF coach and not a train is provided fro Loches to Tours.  SNCF do not allow adequately for the connection.  It was late getting in and I had 90 seconds to run from outside of the station, find the platform to get a connecting shuttle train from Tours to St Pierre des Corps.  Why do don't they stop the coach at St Pierre des Corps, it stops at places that didn't even have a station?  At St Pierre des Corps the TGV to Gare Montparnasse was 2 and half hours late.  I got aboard a slow InterCite train to Gare Austerlitz, which took 2 and half hours, despite having paid a premium for TGV. Trains Grandes Vitesses, Trains Grandes Merdes more like. SNCF should be an example to the UK as to why re-nationalising rail would not provide a solution to poor service.

I traveled from Milan to Paris on the TGV in second class: comfortable and clean seats, perhaps a little narrow. The train starts using high speed only from Lyon station so up to there you travel as on a normal regional train. Ideal for those who love traveling by train like me, otherwise the almost eight hours will never pass. Characteristic restaurant car, good quality food but quite expensive as expected. Negative note in the bathrooms, in terrible condition.

1st class - departure from Basel. The tables were still covered in dirt from the guests who had disembarked. When we pointed this out, the train attendant simply said that the cleaning was already done. The food is a real pain and the service couldn't be worse. It won't help that a new provider will now be responsible for catering. After a 50 minute late departure from Paris, we only received coffee 90 minutes after departure and only when we asked. The food was still on the table, even though there were barely 10 seats occupied. If I owned this company, I would fire the management on the spot.

We have some experience with the TGV or Thalys. As far as travel conditions are concerned, we have always been satisfied even if sometimes we find certain prices uncompetitive. On the other hand, the catering is deplorable and for several years we have preferred to have a light meal to take away before boarding.

We did the Lyon-Paris route. Overall, the option ends up being faster and more affordable than taking a plane. Cons: little space for luggage; poor air conditioning system; the selection of seat numbers is automatic. If you are purchasing for two people who want to sit together, purchase the seats in a single order, or the system may assign different chairs and carriages.

We took the train from Paris to Brussels. This service is good. There was a long queue for security prior to boarding the train. One is forbidden to take knives, guns on the train. I had purchased a set of kitchen knives which was in my case. I told the attendant at security as I thought I would have to forfeit them. Strangely enough she just smiled and said it didn't matter and motioned me to come through!I thought this was very puzzling!

Did I just pay for a first class ticket ? Hadn't done the Geneva-Paris journey for several years, the train was utterly filthy when I got on in Geneva, and I had to put some garbage near my seat into the bin. They offered a minute sandwich, cold tea and coffee which came back at the same temperature when I asked for a change, and the toilets... OMG !!!! Looked like they hadn't been cleaned in days, no toilet paper, the floor was full of urine and a wretched stench nearly made me vomit. Did you say Swiss quality and hygiene ? Come on guys, this is inadmissible !!!

The crew on Swiss segment zurich to Paris refuse even give you a newspaper or waterYou need wait till it cross frontier go FranceTo get any service !!This is unacceptable- on eurostar you are offered drink newspaper on British soil. The crew were not friendly and told me to write to SNCF complainDon't bother go on first class as no free wifi even Good quality is also lacking !!
Super connection from Rotterdam CS to Paris GDN. In 2.5 hours with excellent service, cheap (also the most expensive ticket), low CO2 emissions, comfortable. Don't fly, travel by train!
TGV is on time as always but the catering... My god. 10€ for a GREAT microwave hamburger and a bottle of water.

Recently travelled from Lille to Montpellier and back. Then from Lille to London. Despite a late start on the way home SNCF and Eurostar did brilliantly well to get all passengers back to London even though the last train had theoretically left.The only issue I have is that when booking your seats could there be a place to request a seat facing forward or backwards.Otherwise very good experience even though the trains were packed. Staff were delightful and Security simple. Trains leave a central London station, at civilised times of the day, unlike their winged rivals!!!!!

Puts Australia to shame. While we talk about how lovely our trains are doing 120 or so, the one we got from Paris to Dijon got up to 300. Smooth and quiet, yes a little old and grimey but they've been around a while now. On time. Just a really good rail system here in France compared to many other places. Certainly not cheap but you don't use the TGV everyday I suppose. Dunno why people complain about the staff having no French, we spoke to a number of staff and they all spoke excellent English, but I suppose how dare they speak only their own language in their own country. Besides who can't read a timetable? Free wifi, hear that British rail?

Travelling by train in France can be a challenge unless you speak fluent French. You may be lucky to find a fellow passenger who speaks english but be prepared to be a bit flustered.  Although I had a ticket on the TGV with carriage and seat number, everything happens so quickly I was at the wrong end of the platform, not knowing how the carriages are numbered, couldnt even find the number on the carriage and leapt on any carriage hoping for the best.  At quieter times of year this is probably not an issue, but I certainly was in someone else's seat that happily didnt matter at this shoulder travel time of year.Some of the luggage racks were full so I'd advise to take minimal luggage or certainly no more than mid size suitcases as getting on and off can be a bit of a jump too. A nice way to travel when things go smoothly and Id previously been fine, but do also prepare for delays and if you think you have enough time for connections, think again...i had allowed a good 45 minutes but didnt count on every train I had booked being delayed or 'retarde' which threw every connection into chaos.  My four hour trip turned into nine hours, so plan for an early train with a good gap between. At some stations there are ticket offices but finding a staff member who can speak english can be difficult.  I had to have my tickets changed to later travel and needed assistance. Luckily managed to do this but it was a stressful experience.  Still its all part of the experience!

Oh, if only we had something like this!!! The journey to Paris took about 2 hours. Comfortable carriages. Everything is for the convenience of passengers, there are sockets nearby for charging your gadgets, comfortable tables. Clean, comfortable.  The speed is not felt at all, although it is constantly displayed on the display in each car.  There you can see the route and travel time. Very convenient transport.

A little apprehension at the start to make 6 trains with 3 children 2 years old, 7 years old and 17 years old. My husband and I chose to only take 4 places. To my great surprise we had plenty of space for my 2 daughters and me on 2 seats, opposite there was my husband and my son. There is plenty of space, tablets are available for you to use with phone sockets.  The girls were able to play (drawings, modeling clay... we have room for lunch). The staff on board are friendly and competent. The wagons are clean, as are the toilets. We didn't see the time passing...

A few days ago I made my first trip from Turin P.Susa to Paris with the TGV, return trip always in 1st class and with a dog in tow. With the dog, if we don't want to travel by car, the train is a good and comfortable alternative, good bar-restaurant service, friendly staff, but how dirty!!! my seat on the return trip was truly gross. Closed or dirty bathrooms. Something really needs to change.

The train was on time and efficient.  However, the cars were quite dirty.  In addition, the bathrooms were in teriible shape.  No toilet paper, trash all over the floor.  For the price of tickets for the train they could have someone cleaning up since it was a six hour train ride.

We took the THV 1st class upper deck from CDG Terminal 2 to Avignon. What would have taken 7 hrs to drive took 3 hrs on a very smooth train.There's a cafe car with basic food and drinks and the seats are relatively comfortable. The wifi is about 2Ms which is ok.If you're holidaying in the south of France and flying into CDG and want to avoid the long lines, security checks of airports or the long hours driving, TGV 1st class a good way to go.

Undoubtedly interesting for the timing and departures and arrivals in "central" areas.  I have traveled first class several times.  Milan - Paris and vice versa. You can sense that the cars are a few years old......no comparison with our Freccia Rossa, both in terms of comfort and cleanliness. By the way, bring some wet wipes to clean the table and I hope you don't need the toilets.

The TGV from CDG to Lyon has two train numbers. The reason is that the two cars are connected because there are so many passengers. Don't worry, the destination is the same. At CDG, there is a TGV ticket purchase counter on the far right as you face the platform. There are many tourists on board the train, and they will be carrying huge luggage, so it is safe to assume that they will not be able to put it in the luggage storage area. Is it faster than the Shinkansen? Since it runs on land, it feels more stable than the Shinkansen. I highly recommend traveling by TGV.

These trains might be fast and the seats comfortable but that's about where it ends.  We have been in quarter full 1st Class carriages and there is simply not enough luggage space.  The overhead luggage racks are ridiculous - you can't even fit a small backpack up there and the space for luggage bags is not sufficient for the small number of passengers on board.  I would hate to see what happens if it is full!  The Italian trains leave them for dead.  Back to back seating allowing for bags to be stowed between the seats is brilliant - were the French to proud to copy somebody else's great idea?

I paid for 1st class for the family to travel from Zurich to Paris at 1334 on the 15th August.Unfortunately the seat opposite had a flickering fluorescent light in our eye line. I mentioned this to the two guards. The one with the French uniform was sympathetic and tried to restart the lights without success. The one in the Swiss uniform remarked (assuming I don't speak French) "They can close their eyes!". For four hours?Not what you'd expect from a premium fare service.

I had bought my TGV Tickets on-line and had to go to the Gare de Lyon part Dieu in Lyon to collect the physical tickets.   Excellent service provided by the ticket help desks.  The trip on the TGV itself between Lyon and Geneva was excellent.....comfortable seats, plenty of legroom and plenty of room to keep my luggage.  Very impressed with this Rail-line.

We traveled from Lyon to Paris mid week. The service was on time and the journey was less than 2 hours. We picked up the cheapest tickets available which happened to be in first class. The seats and big and comfortable, it was a good way to catch up on some sleep after travelling for nearly a month.

1 hour delay.... and then the dishes with dubious tastes at full price. A bitter vegetarian rice salad filled with turmeric and not even the flavor of saffron. €5.90 for 3 mouthfuls... rice not cooked. Vegetable steak sandwich for €6.90, even not heated, really shabby. And when I tell myself that before leaving I looked to see if they had sandwiches and that on the SNCF website they said that they had them from 3.60... in reality the cheapest is 5.90€ and so above all don't look for taste. 23€ for an adult + child lunch while remaining hungry and with a bitter taste....

Our first time on the TGV. Gare de Lyon is well organised; we managed to get a decent cup of coffee and sit down waiting; only complaint was that the platform wasn't shown until 10 mins before departure - it takes that long to walk the length of the train! The speed of the train is impressive, although it slows right down crossing into Italy - but the views compensate.

Waiting for TGV to St.Malo from Montparnasse - train simply cancelled leaving us with just one option of catching another train 2 hours later.Customer Service just didn't seem to care stating we should just take the next train.When the train arrived it was just a total mad scramble with all other commuters rushing to get on board. We ended up having to stand in cramped conditions for 1/12 hours to our next train stop off at Rennes. I was told we could complain & receive refund - however this is a laborious form filling process which you cannot do online & have to print out providing original tickets etc etc then post to them. Seems like they want to make it as difficult as possible to pay any compensation.Personally I will NEVER use the TGV again.
Unfriendly staff who talk to you like a dog, still no connection and an hour late.

After the TGV finally reached Strasbourg at a snail's pace from Munich via Augsburg-Ulm-Stuttgart-Karlsruhe, things really got going. If the infrastructure in Autoland Germany were better, you could reach Paris from Bavaria in 4 hours. Seats in EK ok, quiet travel, no on-board program but socket, WiFi works well at times. First Class is with waiting staff, menus and good service, the sanitary facilities could perhaps use better water and paper supplies. Anyway, clean. The announcements are multilingual and not annoying, speed and route (stops) are clearly displayed. Delay was minor on the return journey. TGV promises a waiting lounge, but doesn't have one in Paris L'Est.

I regularly take the TGV in the morning around 7:40 a.m. to travel from Geneva to Paris in 1st class. In the vast majority of cases, the train is on time, the restaurant service is efficient, even if the food is not always excellent. Once is not usual, I decide to leave in the evening by taking the 7:41 p.m. Instead of a 3h05 journey, the train took 7h30 to arrive around 3h30 in the morning at Paris Gare de Lyon (this was due to a personal accident and violent storms in the Paris region during the day). In short, all this to say that the SNCF reacted very well and organized the trip as well as possible, ordered enough taxis and also gave a €20 voucher. Given the delay, we were able to get our tickets refunded. People complain and complain easily when something goes wrong, so for my part I salute the staff's ability to react and their professionalism on this occasion, hats off.
Great view of the country side. The seats are comfortable... toilets are clean and over all pleasant experience!

I used it from Bordeaux to Paris. I was originally thinking of taking a plane, but since I had time, I decided to take the TGV. I took the first TGV from Bordeaux (around 6am) and headed to Paris. As a result, considering the waiting time for boarding the plane, I was able to get to Paris early and use my time in Paris effectively. Perhaps because it was early in the morning, there weren't many passengers, so I was able to enjoy the train journey very comfortably. If you want to travel efficiently, TGV may be better than planes, so please give it a try.

Took the TGV from Paris Montparnasse to Bordeaux St Jean in first class as a solo traveler. Had a brand new train, which was fun! Was happy with the seat and the silence of the cabin (no screaming kids, yay!), but 1) the plug with the seat didn't work, but the USB connection did so that wasn't a big issue 2) Way too little luggage space particularly for big bags, but was fortunate to find some. Would do it again as it is much more relaxing than flying. My train was also right on time.A shuttle from Gare du Nord to Gare Montparnasse would be nice as Paris' subway system is... not the best.

Several times I have made the stupid mistake of going to "eat" at the bar car of the TGV Montpellier-Paris. I should have understood from the first time that the dishes offered could only be suitable for farm animals (pink in color)...and even then!!! I can't believe that such food can be sold in a country so proud of its gastronomy! The height of horror (or comedy): I noticed that certain "dishes" (I stick to the quotation marks) were sold under the signature of star chefs. I won't mention any names, of course. I am sorry that the lure of profit can lead to such contempt for travelers.

We took out the Thalys tickets to do the Paris-Amsterdam section, departing from Paris Nord, more than two months in advance. Firstly, we paid 114 euros for each one. The first thing that is worth highlighting is punctuality. It is advisable to go with a little time as there is a queue to put the suitcases through the scanner. The service on board the train, which travels at 320 km per hour, is very correct, both for the treatment of the hostesses and for the quality of the food they served us. Without a doubt I would take it again.

The new LGV makes it from Bordeaux to Paris in 2 hours and 4 minutes, we did it in the morning in exact 2 hours, amazing. Service on board has not changed, slow, quality of food mediocre,  sandwiches and croissants at best. I am talking first class now. The offered lounges at both ends are crowded and only coffee is available. Return trip back home same day took 20 minutes longer.Seat comfort below par for 1st class. Overall disappointing service.
bordeaux lille 5 hours. the tgv bar new fresh dishes. very friendly barmaid. dishes to take away or on site with beautiful view of the landscape. price a little high anyway.

I have a problem to understand the official punctuality statistics for the TGV train, which according to SNCF was about 90% for the whole year 2016 (trains arriving exactly on time or within 5 minutes delay). I stayed in France for two weeks in July and i used the TGV ten times (i am a great fan of high-speed train traveling in general). 4 out of 10 times the train was delayed (for 30, 25, 10 and 40 minutes respectively). I picked up the fastest train from Marseille to Paris (3 hours 5 minutes) and it was 25 minutes late (we stopped to a complete halt for about 10 minutes just after Lyon Airport Station due to an alarm notification from a forward train, according to the information we received from our driver). The delay of 40 minutes was at a journey from Paris Est to Champagne - Ardennes TGV station, which is a distance covered in about 40 minutes actually!! (We departed Paris Est some minutes later than the scheduled arrival time!!!). Regarding the 6 other journeys (Paris - Bordeaux and return, Paris - Rennes and return, Marseille - Avignon), the train was not exactly on time, but within the 5-minute delay margin. On the contrary i used the slower Intercites service four times (Paris - Orleans and return, Paris - Bayeux and return) and it was always on time without even one minute delay.So be careful if you are planning using the service and having connections involved.Reliability and punctuality of TGV are the main problems for this otherwise excellent technological marvel and in my opinion the French have to learn a lot from the reliability of the Japanese Shinkansen, which has a punctuality of one minute delay on average for the whole system.

I rode the TGV from Geneva to Paris for the first time. Compared to Japan's Shinkansen, it was a bit more thrilling because of the railroad crossings. The in-car service is different from Japan, as food is served just like on an airplane. If you want to travel long distances while seeing the land of Europe, I think it's a good idea to try riding one at least once.

TGVs provide you with the speed and safety to travel when you want to arrive quickly and without having to travel by plane. Their speed and attention make them different from other trains. The Thalís company is one of the best in this concept.

Be carefull if you book tickets for destination outside France. Overpriced if your journey include a train not part of their 'group'. In my experience, for travelling from Paris to Italy, the ticket in Italy was sold at 29EUR on their website but available at 12.90 by buying directly from Trenitalia.

Excellent train for travel between Stuttgart and Paris, speeds of over 320kmph displayed, consistently over 310-315kmph after Strasbourg. Very busy route, 2 levels and has capacity to handle large bags for storage. Left Stuttgart at 8:54am and arrived on time in Paris at 12:15pm.
For a journey of more than two hours, no bar service either at the square or in the dedicated car. And for all Dunkirk Paris journeys it's the same......
I think the Shinkansen is more comfortable to ride. I think it's better to go early and check the platform before boarding. Don't forget to stamp your ticket before boarding.

Superb service and amazingly smooth considering the speed of over 300km/h. The food was excellent in first class. we were fortunate enough to get one of the superb double decker TGVs to Zurich via Dijon and Basel - just 4 hrs it is faster than flying city centre to city centre and it was bang on time. A truly marvellous experience - and it's a nationalised industry too - UK Gov take note!

You can cross the entire country quickly and conveniently using the services of TGV and SNCF. They go according to a schedule, it is better to book tickets 3 months in advance - it will be cheaper. The carriages have a clean, used toilet for a fee.
Return journey from Zurich Extremely comfortable journey Tasty lunch served and ran to schedule Always good aspects to every journey

Even if we left Geneva at 7:41 p.m....sorry, an hour late and arrived in Paris after more than 7 hours and 30 minutes of travel, i.e. 3:20 in the morning, I cannot blame the SNCF because there was a personal accident in the first place (suicide in general) and our route was diverted by another route. And on the way back, tree on the tracks, loss of 30 minutes. But in the end, a comfortable train (1st class), a small meal tray and no disturbance. Communications about the delay, timing and reasons have been clear and consistent. Boxes were offered with drinks and salads, biscuits....The ticket will be fully refunded and we were offered a 20 EUR voucher for a taxi. Correct given the circumstances and appreciable. A great evolution of the rail system.

WOW - if you are waiting for a TGV and it is supposed to arrive at 3:02 (they inevitably have odd times), do not look for it at 3:01 or even 3:01:40. It will be there at 3:02 - oh, and if you are smart everything will be ready to go because if it says it leaves at 3:08 it will, with you or all your suitcases or not. A true pleasure to ride, the journey is smooth and there is usually a club car where you can get a drink or a snack. If you do not want to drive, and still want to see the countryside, this is the way to go.

Attendants, in addition to not helping, respond rudely to customers. I will give preference to airlines in the future. I was with my brother and sister-in-law getting on the TVG Lyria in Lausanne bound for Paris. There was no space for luggage and one of the attendants indicated an empty space behind some benches. Unfortunately, the space was already occupied by a wheelchair belonging to a wheelchair user who they themselves helped board. I asked if there was another space available, and the answer was that he couldn't do anything, it wasn't his fault that people came with luggage. And it didn't move an inch... Well, isn't that the idea of ​​traveling using the TGV? What kind of answer is that? TGV never again.
First time on a speed train, really relaxing, pleasant, AC, scenic and the station was clean, open, interesting.

I wish everyone in America could take one ride on a TGV!   You board in the center of one city (say Paris) and in a few hours (2 for Bordeaux, for instance) you are whisked to the center of another city.  This city-center to city-center mode of travel is addictive-- no standing in airport lines waiting for a cab, etc.The train ride is smooth, comfortable and FAST.  I'm talking 180 mph fast!  The French scenery flies by and the views are enhanced by big windows.  A club car has drinks and snacks and you can wander around if you get bored.  The newer versions of TGV have internet access as well!! You can buy sandwiches, desserts and drinks at the departing train station if you choose.  The train stations themselves are architecturally interesting as a bonus!

I made the trip from Milan to Paris on the TGV in 1st class, last June 17th and returned in 2nd class. The value for money is very good, good bar-restaurant service (maybe an alternative menu), comfortable seating, well air conditioned, quiet and punctual, time passes well in company, I also recommend it for the landscapes.

This is a fast train although Sundays can be a bit slower timetable and even delayed trains..You can book tickets online at a cheaper rate or get your tickets at the train gare station although make sure its the TGV train station office and not the RER train office as its much slower,as there in the same building..opposite each other..Their is also RER TICKET machines self service which you can choose a language first then click on how many tickets needed..Some of the staff are friendly and it helps to know some french before hand..Also pick up a map at the station always good..Also make sure your on the right train line for TGV or RER train..The TGV train has two levels on the train with there is more comfortable seats on the upper level as these are the pre booked reserved seats..It can get very busy at peak times..Its a great service fast train from the normal train ..and costs more..but its great if your in a hurry to get there...

Booked first class from Zurich through Paris to Amsterdam.  TGV provided the Zurich to Paris leg.  Well maintained, comfortable trains with helpful staff.  Food was nice and free flowing drinks was a welcomed addition on the afternoon trip.  Difficult to believe that the train is traveling 180 mph during trek across French plains.  Wish I had made the booking at a seat with a table, but will know to do that on next booking.

I used the TGV instead of the plane, 5 hours and 30 minutes from Turin Porta Susa, convenience, speed, and direct arrival in the city! The TGV is always very punctual, and I underline fairly comfortable.

A week has passed, I have returned to a “working” state and am ready to tell you my personal “adventures”. Flight St. Petersburg-Munich-Lyon. Work in Lyon. HP, as always, does not finish speaking. There is no point in criticizing, they need to sell...For me personally, Lyon is a friendly city for tourists. Friday, pre-weekend day. Travel by 1st class DVT on the Lyon-Nice route.
