We need to´go from Zurich to Paris and it took us a while to decide whether to go by train or by plane. The fare was a little bit higher by train, and the travel time much shorter, but then we started adding the time sitting on an airport, the long lines for security checks, the time waiting for the luggage; it ended up being the same time and the same price but much more confortable on the train, with a nice seat, no lines, really beautiful sight seeing, electricity outlet for the computer or the phone (traveling coach), confortable table. The so called restaurant, really expensive, but it is there if you need it, and you can also bring your own snack. And you arrive in Paris at the very beautiful Gare de Lyon, walking distance to La Bastille, even with bags. You can also buy your ticket make stops on the way and visit nice locations like Alsacia for some hours without increasing the cost of the ticket. The cars are not as nice as the Swiss SBB but better than the Italian. The train at full speed is really fast but even the totally comfortable, surprisingly you don´t go at fast speed must of the time, during our trips (one round trip) it was never on fast speed while in Switzerland.
spend the extra for first class! comfy seats and a quiet ride. 175 mph got me from Paris to Arass in no time, well an hour. Nice views of the country side and a no stress way to get around

Dream about the service levels of our Frecce Rossa or Italo. It's a big train. I took it from Paris to Turin. The toilets are dirty, and even have writing on the walls. On the other hand, it arrived on time, which was strange. I was in first class, but it's like economy on Italian trains. The concept of a reserved seat is very complicated. Nobody explains it to you, I was convinced I was in the right place, then a lady who came to Lyon said that that place was hers, and she was right. The restaurant service is not bad, and I must say at not high prices. Attention: the TGV is TGV from Paris to Lion, then after the border it is an accelerated one, and arrives in Turin, and then in Milan, on the normal route. They explained to me that the French refused to pay the Italian railways for transit on the Italian high-speed line, so the train travels on the old Turin/Milan line, and stops in Vercelli, Novara, etc.

Puts ours trains to shame. Quick and comfortable, non  stop to the south of France then skirts the coast down to Barcelona .... Really nice trip with amazing views. First Class is only slighter dearer and really comfortable

The Turin - Paris route is increasingly slow, 8 years ago it now took 5 hours and 40 minutes, now even up to 6 and a half hours! The carriages are dilapidated and dirty even in first class, there are no free snacks, there is no wi-fi, the entire journey is always in the midst of ringing phones and people shouting on the phone (this last point, I recognize, is not the fault of the SNCF but of the widespread rudeness of the people who ignore it they don't care about anyone else). But the last straw was that after the last trip I received an email from the SNCF asking me for my review: I explained what was said above and after a few days they wrote to me that my review had been rejected... in the same email they warned me, however, that they care about the customers' opinion! crazy, if you don't write a review that they like they won't publish it!!! after something like this I would give zero stars if only I could...
Even if I find the price to be high, it is still less than alone in a car with the costs that go with it. In this hot period, the air conditioning is appreciated.

I got the train from Paris to Avignon, you should be in the station only 1 minutes before departure, the trains are big enough for all your luggage, there is a variety of food and drink in trains. tilets are clean.TGV in France is the best way for transportation even easier and relax than aircraft.

We travelled from Gare d' Paris Est to Strasbourg in Class 2 on a train going on into Germany. The seats were comfortable however since there were so many travellers with suitcases storage was a  problem. It was unfortunate the direction like on the Shinkansen in Japan. The train left exactly on time at 3.55pm and arrived on time at 5.41pm.

travelled from Genève to Paris & back with a friend..train is excellent...I bought ticket online about a month earlier so I got great fare (just €34 one way)...one bad side though... I selected seats "face forwarding" on both journeys and when we boarded the train, our seats were facing backwards... this could be a problem for people who get slightly dizzy facing backward in a high speed train !!
I traveled in 2nd class on upper deck from paris to antibes. Comfortable seats, good leg space, separate racks for big luggage. Clean toilet and nice cafeteria.

We decided to go to Marseille for a weekend. So, we took a TGV from Lyon to Marseille on a Friday. The train arrived from Basel with 10 minutes delay, and 15 minutes after leaving Lyon, there was an announcement saying that the train was diverted to classical tracks instead of high speed tracks because of an overhead cable problem. So, the train was not anymore a TGV (Train a Grande Vitesse), but was a normal slow train. Althongh the train was back on high speed tracks just before Aix-en-Provence, and the announcement said now  we could run at 300 km/hour, it was too late, and the train arrived at Marseille with 55 munutes delay, which is enormous for a normal traveling time of a little more than 1 hour and half. On our return trip on Sunday, the train was almost on time, but still arrived with 15 munites delay. Our seats were facing backwards on our return. In fact on TGV you have 50 % chance that you face the wrong way, as half of the seats are facing the wrong way.The folding table of my 1st class seat was broken and did not exist (was removed), which was not practical at all. On either way, there was no Wifi available in the train. The toilet was clean but there was no water in the toilet to wash hands in either way. By the way, we wanted to buy some souvenir on our return at Marseille station, but there were no open souvenir shops. Except that you cannot change seat directions (like on a Japanese Shinkansen).,the design of the car and seats are good and cosy, but the punctuality and maintenance leave a lot to be desired.

Traveled by TGV from Turin - Porta Susa to Paris - Gare de Lyon and back and even in 1st class the disgust is unimaginable, dirty and uncomfortable seats (crumbs), waste paper and various waste already present in the designated compartment!!!, wi fi not present!!!, despite being halfway through the carriage, every time the dividing door between the carriages in which the toilet is located was opened there was an unimaginable smell of piss (journey return) now I wonder about keeping costs low (if we can talk about low costs 240 euros return for 2) to the detriment of the quality of the trip itself it seems like a suicidal policy to me, the only positive thing is the duration of the trip which allows you to be in Paris in about 5 hours and a half on time and moreover on time but as I repeat in first class the situation was this and perhaps you expect something more.

Thursday May 18 TGV 9761 car 15 seat 38 - TGV 9780 car 18 seat 68 in both trains the electrical outlets were without power. The flight attendants said they were sorry and couldn't do anything. I was traveling for work and I wasn't able to use the travel time to work on my computer. Does SNCF ever maintain the cars????

travelled 1. class. Our seats were in the upper deck, very comfortable and spacy, lots of space on the table. Steward came by with newspapers and coffee. Took only a litte more than 3 hours to Karlsruhe, Tain went very fast and the ride was very quiet. Took 1/2 h less than on teh way out with the ICE III. Will choose TGV again. Very pleased.
If you book a train trip, TGV is the way to go! Seats are comfortable and friendly staff. Clean and easy to find assigned seating.

Last year we were in Chambéry (and on the return in Valence the train was replaced by another that came later and they offered me to go in first class due to the loss of the hour that we had been waiting too long). Coming from Paris we were assisted by the conductor when we had a difficulty, now this year we have gone to Bordeaux and last Monday on the way out the transfer from Narbonne-Tolouse was 15 minutes late and the conductor before arriving in Tolouse He passed one by one to those of us who had a transfer to Bordeaux and who were missing the train, to tell us that when we got off platform 1 we should go directly to platform 1-A because ours left in 10 minutes so that we could all get on and they were waiting for us asking for information on the same platform to make sure that we had understood it and that we didn't lose it. . .a ten for the company that works alongside the AVE in Spain because the year we went to Strasbourg, the train from Barcelona to Lyon was AVE and in Lyon it was changed to TGV - meaning there is international cooperation to serve all passengers. - I recommend getting the tickets three months in advance and if it can be the same day they go on sale, there are interesting offers like last year 75 one way to Paris from Barcelona or this year one way to Bordeaux for 150 euros from Barcelona.- (the return trip is the same, of course).- By car to Paris or Bordeaux it would cost much more, the garage in Paris or Bordeaux at the Hotel was 15 euros a day.-In addition, the train always leaves you at "CENTER VILLE" that is, in the city center you are going to and this is another important saving. . .to keep in mind.-I recommend 100%

Scandalous. I have been tricked several times but I will never buy anything at the TGV bar again (here Strasbourg Lyon but it's the same on all journeys). How can we dare to serve this tasteless food for €17 per menu! (supposed to have been concocted by star chefs!!! Is that humor??) Next time I'll buy sandwiches from Mr Paul! before getting on the train!!

Bought tickets online at Renfe (Spanish railways) for the Paris - Barcelona route and at Thalys for Amsterdam - Paris. Paris - Barcelona was on offer for €29 each way. You will be on the road for a total of twelve hours. Departure 8.25 from CS and 8.40 arrival Barcelona Sants. In Paris you have two hours to transfer with the RER (regional train) from Gare de Nord to Gare du Lyon. You can already buy a metro card on the Thalys that is also valid on the RER. Unfortunately, you cannot buy a metro card on the TGV, so you can buy it from the machine on the way back at the metro station. You follow the green signs with RER D (both there and back) and then it is quite easy to find. You can take any train that comes, it's only two stops, 10 minutes in total. These trains can be very busy. Comfort in the Thalys is good and the internet speed is reasonable. On the other hand, the TGV/AVE has no internet and there was no socket on the return journey. There is also very little space for your luggage on the TGV. There is no space at all above your seat, so if you travel with a large suitcase it will be a problem if you enter the train late. It is very strange that there is no security check at all from Amsterdam to Barcelona, ​​but there is on the return journey, both in Barcelona and Paris.

We have done several branches at SNCF, which is the company that manages the railways in Franica. We went from Figueres to Paris, then to Strasbourg, to Colmar and back to Strasbourg and to Paris. We had tickets purchased long in advance. When from Strasbourg we wanted to change the departure, moving it forward 4 hours (it was raining and we wanted to arrive in Paris earlier) they wanted to penalize us with a cost of 140.00 euros for two paid tickets (the total round trip in first class was 308 euros). There was no way. We had to wait four hours and then the train was almost empty. Bad way to attract passengers. We will try NOT TO USE SNCF-TGV ANYMORE.

We have traveled many times on different routes. In one of the last ones, we booked first class because there were no regular tickets. We had the idea of ​​eating on the same train, as we were in first class.... our surprise was to see that there is no meal service included in the ticket as is the case on the Ave. Apart from that, everything was fine, train on time as usual.

Departing from Novara at 6.30am for Paris, the TGV appears to be dated with comfortable but creased seats, the smelly toilet already early in the morning! First class travel has no associated service....water coffee tea biscuits sweets all for a fee....oh dear my red arrow...you sure make us travel better!!!!
Traveling to / from Paris and Lyon was great. The train is nice and comfortable - very clean.  The trip is around 2 hours.  It was a great way to get to Lyon.

It was the first time at night on this route so I can say that the positive notes were the punctuality both on the way there and on the way back, the kindness of the staff, the (incredible) cleanliness of the functioning bathrooms. On the other hand, the negatives can be summarized in the air conditioning always on on the way out at our request, we were told that unfortunately it was not manually adjustable while on the way back the opposite was the case: high temperature and the same reason! Personally, the plane is better.

Travel dated 02/05 between Poitiers -Strasbourg, departure at 9:17 a.m. (bar in car 14). The person at the tgv bar lacked professionalism. After waiting about fifteen minutes, the waiter offers a coffee to the person in front of me, just after throwing this person's dessert into their lunch bag. And when my turn comes, I ask him for coffee. And there, the waiter tells me that he is overwhelmed and that he doesn't have time to make coffee. Thank you for reviewing the commercial aspect of their role with this person.

I used the codeshare flight with Air France from Charles de Gaulle to Brussels South. The transfer was convenient. However, Charles de Gaulle Station cannot be directly connected to the outside world, so please be careful when leaving the airport and avoid taking long detours. Additionally, in France, where there are many union strikes, whether Air France or SNCF goes on strike will affect flight operations, so special care must be taken with AF codeshares. When I used this service, even though the train was running on time, I had to wait over 30 minutes to collect my luggage at the arrival station due to the luggage union strike.

Route Strasbourg - Lyon and back. The trains were on time both on the outward and return journeys. The interior was a bit older, but comfortable with plenty of space (2nd class). The space for luggage is very rare and sometimes a little further away. Nevertheless, the journey of around 4 hours was pleasant.

24 April 2017 outbound and 28 April 2017 return: dilapidated and smelly trains, sleeper cabins with incredibly small spaces, impossible to move even if you are size 38/40 with the expectation, during border checks, that travelers are in "cabins" in which they can only lie down in their assigned seat. Restaurant service that promises excellent dishes that are not served. Cost not adequate for the service promised on the Thello website. Thank you never see us again!

Its was my first time to travel by train, it a nice experience as everything went smoothly, the people working there are friendly and experienced, the train is fast clean and comfortable.What i hate is the. Cashier who told us that the trip will take 3 hours with non-stop but it took 5 hours as we stopped in 5 stations.

I traveled on the TGV from Milan to Chambéry (it's the TGV Milan-Paris Gare de Lyon) and it was a shocking experience. Rude and arrogant staff right from the ticket booth (where they even prevented me from sitting on an armchair, declaring that "it's not a waiting room" and inviting me to leave), a dilapidated TGV SNCF train from thirty years ago, probably taken from a scrapyard, dirty and deteriorated, a nightmare journey: the so-called "high-speed" TGV between Milan and Turin travels at the speed of a train on the conventional line (to avoid paying the toll of the superfast train at the FS), with enormous inconvenience for travelers who hoped to find rapid and efficient transport. I was in first class, but no specific service is guaranteed to the traveller, unlike what happens on the Italian "Frecce": not a drink, not even a glass of water, nor a pretzels or a sweet. Third world stuff now. Last but not least, on the return journey the TGV broke down before Modane: we all had to get off, in the cold, and wait over an hour for the replacement TGV without counting on any assistance at the station in Modane. If this is the service that the French railways are able to provide, next time I hope to travel to Burundi.
Every week... I take it... lovely staff but more and more often late... too bad... otherwise I feel at home there
A symbol of French know-how So much criticized...Imitated and exported by many other countries With the help of SNCF know-how Today in free fall...What a shame!!

Trip London/Paris in second class 130 euros. Poor service: no Wi-Fi, dirty bathrooms, listless staff at the bar, the only kind person was the boy with the food trolley. Zero leg space, too many people, slow train with just 4/5 stops where you can't even get off for a moment if not just one. Delay of almost half an hour.

Paid about 80 Euros to ride from Paris to Zurich. I booked my tickets ahead of time online. Trip was under 4 hours. My seat was power plug equipped and the train had free wifi. Bathrooms were clean and they sold drinks and snacks. This train gets up and goes. One stretch we must have been rolling close to 200kph. Lots of scenery to admire along the way, including bright splashes of canola fields. A great way to relax and spend free time vagabonding across Europe. An interesting way to see the world. I would take this train again.

I took a first class train from Paris Gare de l'Est to Reims, a journey of about 55 minutes. One row on one side, two rows on the other. The ride comfort is not bad. I didn't use it because it was a short trip, but the food and drink pamphlets in the car looked delicious. The return trip was on the second floor of a two-story building, but since it was night, I couldn't enjoy the view.

We travelled from Basel to Paris in first class on TGV.  Nothing about the ride was first class, not meriting the higher price.The shabby train cars did not have WiFi.The food service was coffee, a croissant, and a piece of fruit for a four-hour train ride over lunchtime.For the last 1.5 hours from Dijon, second class passengers flooded into first class and took the empty seats.All announcements over the PA system were fuzzy and hard to hear.The English was read with such a strong accent that it was indistinguishable from the French.***Nothing*** first class at all about this train ride.

We traveled from Paris to Lyon on the TGV and were very happy with the short, two-hour trip.  The train was smooth, I mean no clickity-clack like most American trains, and had almost no sway.  My only complaint, is the sudden pressure changes when entering tunnels or passing other trains.  Perhaps this was more noticeable for me, since I have hearing aids?  Anyway, I was able to catch-up on email with the complementary WiFi and my Wife was able to doze, no small feat.
No delays, staff present, quick but thorough checks, presence of law enforcement in the two stations (London and Paris) including dogs. Clean train, good wifi access, low prices

I first used it when I traveled to Europe using a Eurail Pass about 17 years ago, and since then I have loved traveling by train in Europe, not just the TGV, but I have used it often when traveling to France. It wasn't even a train at that time, but it was super cool compared to Japan's Shinkansen! I was so excited. In recent years, there have been various types of trains, and there are many trains that don't have the cleanliness of Shinkansen trains in Japan, and are obsolete.The windows are so dirty that you can't tell when they were last cleaned, so you can't enjoy the scenery. . . However, now you can make reservations online, and you can easily buy tickets from vending machines at stations, so you can use them instead of having to buy them at a counter or at a counter in French, which is very convenient. It's hard to decide on your itinerary, but if you book early, you can find regular cheap seats, so be sure to look for them! It was a ticket that could not be changed, but I asked at the counter to change to an earlier flight without looking like a stranger, and they accommodated me. Maybe it was because I was obviously a tourist...Please note that if you get a ticket at the station, you must stamp it with the punching button next to the platform. The 1st CL has many 2 x 1 seats, and the seats are spacious and the luggage storage space is also spacious, and in some cases you can put your suitcase behind or next to your seat, so you can sit without worrying about your luggage. The 2nd CL has 2 x 2 seats and is a Japanese Shinkansen regular car type. Space for suitcases is limited and it is difficult to store them near the seats. I once rode on a two-story TGV train with extremely low ceilings and narrow spaces between seats, and there was hardly any space for luggage, so I learned a lot from it, so I've been using the 1st train ever since. However, this depends on the type of train, and you may be lucky as there are some trains that have a comfortable ride even on the 2nd train.There is no problem if your suitcase is large and heavy enough to be placed on the rack.However, there is no dining car depending on the train. It is clearly displayed on the timetable. It's fun because you can easily use cafes etc. Not only domestic flights but also international flights, especially sleeper trains, are really fun! Compartments also vary depending on the amount. You can travel to Paris, Germany, Italy, Spain, etc. while sleeping. You can enjoy a journey that you cannot experience by plane. In the compartment, the conductor will skillfully make your bed and provide snacks. Don't worry, the two-person compartment will be assigned to people of the same gender. The 6-person compartment had triple bunk beds on both sides.I was a little surprised because I shared a room with a person of the opposite sex. This was a long time ago, so what about now? By the way, please come to roll call in the morning and evening. As for the Tegeve, it is very old, but traveling by train in Europe is really fun. Also, I think this is often the case in Japan as well, but I think that even though the people at the station counters and conductors are busy, they are kind and gentle. I'm sure people who work for railway companies love trains.

Traveled by rail from Germany to Paris first class.  I cannot compare other classes of travel.  First class is awesome.  Large comfortable seats.    Dining car.  Euros required in the food car as they don't accept US cash.Train is fast, smooth and quiet.  The French countryside is quaint.  Small groups of houses surrounding a church steeple.  This is a great way to travel.
Excellent Turin/Paris return trip. In less than 6 hours you arrive in the heart of Paris, then just go down one floor to use the metro and move quickly throughout the city

There is no denying that this remains the most successful means of transport in France but unfortunately at high prices and with still quite a few holes in the racket, in the provinces certain connections are still missing such as from the east to the south....
Best train in the world French touch, french service, french speed You have to try this train at 300 km per hour. Good Seats, comfort and silence

I went from Paris Gare Lyon to Marseilles St. Charles. And the 800 Km journey took me exactly 3 hours and 17 minutes. That is really high speed and the seats are very comfortable too. I enjoyed the journey and looked at the beautiful countryside through the glass window but it is difficult to take good pictures because of the speed and he reflection of the glass window.

for the Paris-Milan route the prices are excellent. Perhaps to the detriment of the services offered to the traveler. there is no WIFI coverage; seats that are rather uncomfortable and do not fit with the windows (some seats are between one window and another); there is no free snack service for the customer, but only paid service with little choice and few staff to serve you; there is no bathroom cleaning service on board. Italian trains are a hundred times better!

TGV with disabled personNever again. Wrong booking from France. Disabled people have first class cabins and instead France has blocked numbers 5 and 6 where wheelchairs cannot pass. Notified by my trusted agency and the response was an email confirming cabins 5-6 instead of first class. On the outward journey, problem resolved by the train conductor and on the return, problem resolved by Italy which blocked the train after 4 hours to let the disabled person off and then get him back on again in first class. In Italy 100% assistance, while in France we leave it at that. We will certainly never take the TGV again. Long sentence to you.

for the Bern - Paris trip by tgv everything was impeccable, a table between 3 other travelers, sockets for recharging cell phones... on the way back, no table and no sockets since I was seated in wagon 11 on seat 21 or 26... a row of 4 seats on the aisle side!

With my length of 197 centimeters, I was curious about the legroom - I've never been more relaxed when traveling. Compared to the living room armchair at home, you can sit here really comfortably. There's enough space for luggage. The staff of the DB and the French railways - friendly and helpful. Since we took the TGV to Paris in order to change to the Eurostar to London on the same day, we were able to compare directly. TGV is clearly ahead when it comes to cleanliness, legroom and service.

Just horrible! I wanted to try the Provencal stew and gnocchi by Vincent Ferniot. Terrible texture of the pasta! The taste of the meat is just horrible! I regret the double cheese that I thought I would have when I arrived at Le Mans! The dessert "brioche pudding and strawberry compote from Christophe, half halal, raised the bar... but a dessert is not worth 17€!!! In short, to absolutely avoid as far as the stew is concerned... which ultimately lives up to its name.

We arrived in Paris on a girl's trip by plane after 11 o'clock at night and just boarded the TGV, which took us to the city center. It being summer, I sat on the "train" in a t-shirt and shorts, of course everyone was dressed normally. The journey was very comfortable!
Sometimes a little late, sometimes a lot and still on time Sometimes expensive, sometimes very expensive and also good deals for cheap travel

We planned ahead so we got first class tickets at a great price which helped make the trip from Amsterdam to Paris was delightful...smooth and quiet. Service was great and breakfast and snacks were much better than I expected.
faster than flying, cheaper, see the region first hand, computer access, food and alcohol on board for purchase! Reservations a must!

THINK if you taking TVG to bring your own hand sanitiser,if you care about health and cross contamination!To my shocking finding TGV from Nancy to Paris On Jan 2017 No Soap provided on 4 toilets of 5! The restaurant was operating ,how the restaurant staff wash their hands or? I was luck to borrow some sanitiser to dig in my home made sandwich! Complained to Train colector who limit him self to take note!! For routes with Italian destination and departure, SNCF uses the oldest and most run-down trains, reserving the new ones for internal routes, but despite this the standard is always good: fast, comfortable and silent train, almost always on time, which only aesthetically shows its age. On-board staff always friendly and helpful. Bar service to be used only as a last resort, given the very high prices. Today it is competitive compared to the plane only due to the excessive prices of flights from Turin charged by the Alitalia - Air France cartel, but once the fast Turin - Lyon route is active it will be unbeatable.
4 out of 5 only for the friendliness, availability and courtesy of the bar staff. Guys eager to work and it shows! They are always open at night and the breakfasts are excellent.
Fast train over, 300kmh throughout. Friendly staff and priced fair. Can't ask for more than that really.

This is very fast and comfortable mode of travel. It took just 2 hours to cover a distances over 350 KM. The cabin is very quiet and cost. Excellent seating.  Simply loved it. Booking of tickets was also very easy on sncf.com.  Will recommend for fast and peaceful travels.

The TGV trains are fine but be very wary of the customer service, and above all, do not rely upon their punctuality.After our connection from Paris to Barcelona was cancelled, we really had to struggle to get transferred the next train instead of being put on a bus from Perpignan. But this was a minor upset compared to the nightmare with the tickets. We booked tickets to be delivered by post via voyages-sncf.com; however the tickets arrived extremely late (DAYS after the booked day of travel, and indeed after we had left home!). Rather than re-print the tickets, they billed us AGAIN for replacement tickets before they would allow us to board the train. They promised to replace our original unused, and unusable tickets if we sent them those originals. Indeed, we sent them the originals and the replacements, but weeks later, there is no sign of a refund and we are hundreds of euros out of pocket. They claim the tickets we sent them have vanished in the the post, and we were stupid enough not to pay extra for registered post - so who knows, perhaps the tickets are lost in the post. Nonetheless, we have emailed them photographs of the cursed tickets, and sent them letters and the entire rigmarole is completely pointless by now, as the tickets have long since expired - indeed the tickets had _already_ expired before they even arrived in my post box, and I suspect before they were ever sent from the offices.Document every communication you have with these people, photocopy everything and be very very cautious when dealing with their internal bureaucracy. Their staff are polite - indeed, so polite that I feel guilty writing reviews such as this; but the politeness and apologies do you no good when their rules are set up to deny you basic refunds even when the ground for that refund is a mistake made by their ponderous internal bureaucracy.

Excellent.  Study fare choice sites before you hit ok as you can get the same seat much cheaper on some sites versus others.  The tgv is below terminal two.  We went first class and those coaches are double decker.  You can store your luggage up or down.  There also is a bar car.  Seats are really nice, train is super quiet, staircase is very wide, overall a great way to travel.

Very fast and comforteble way to travel relativly large distances in a short time. The direct TGV between BE and Lyon (and further to Marseille) circumvents Paris, saving lots of transfer time. The journey took only 3,5 hours (no check in, luggage waiting etc which you endure with airtravel) making a short weekend trip of two nights to Lyon from BE/South of the Netherlands, interesting. Seats are spacy (in first) and it is nice to see the scenery go by at 300 km/h. Only downside is, no complementary meal/drink in first-class, which you do get on the Thalys (same kind of train, but other destinations). Coffee was bad to, but there is time enough to drink some at your destination.

5 of us were travelling on 1st class from Paris to Marseille. The train departed on time, we have enjoyed the comfort (without wi-fi !!!) and our arrival was even 2-3 minutes earlier than the schedule.A week later on our return from Marseille we were travelling on 2nd class. Due to some technical problems our train stopped in the countryside. There were regular announcements in French only .... 10 min....15 min...30 min ......  1h 50min delay. Finally we arrived to Paris with 75 min delay only. On the next day each of us received a 25% reduction voucher by email for our next TGV booking, that can be used during one year.
Only had a short journey from CDG to Disney, but wow every fast and efficient, the best service in Paris. Would certainly use TGV next time whilst in Paris,
The trip was very good, but there is a lack of clarity in the signage at the Gare de Lyon station. You have to go early to avoid missing the train.

Having been left stranded by EasyJet cancelling the Gatwick flight on December 30th 2016 we had to take 3 trains from Berlin to St Pancras. The best by far was the TGV, the one train I have always wanted to travel on and I was not disappointed. This train is better than flying and we will be planning a trip to southern France on this train. Cannot wait
We had train tickets to get to Bayeux. We found this very comfortable & easy toget around. The train was very clean and well kept:
France has a good network of high-speed trains, which make the distances between cities insignificant.

We got on and the nightmare began. There was no place for the suitcases, of the 3 bathrooms I tried to go to, 2 were interdicted. Cars unbearable due to the human stench. On the other hand, punctual. Next time I will do the Camino de Santiago before getting on this 150 euro train. Disgusting.

Comfortable and with good facilities TGV gives a great experience for the money you pay. I used TGV to travel from Paris to Belgium and views are amazing. Train goes directly inside the Brussels airport. A must have experience when in Europe

Having traveled in the Thello from Paris to Venice here are some inconveniences that we noticed: unworthy bed sheets (paper) - the restaurant car did not work despite an advertisement touting its merits... dirty compartment floors and toilets... only the staff was welcoming and competent... few positive things in fact... Enjoyed travelling in TGV. Good connections and friendly staff and service. Fast and prompt service.

An excellent means of transportation throughout France. I hope someday we will also have such fast and clean trains. You can easily get to almost anywhere in the country comfortably and without any problems.

After the last post in August referring to the suppression of the TGV (for those who haven't read it, I invite you to do so...) nothing has changed. Deep hatred for train travel on my part. This time it went well. No mishaps, no delays. Excellent service on board.

Traveling between Lausanne and Paris for a professional trip, the journey went well despite a delay of 55 minutes on the way out and a delay of 40 minutes on the return. The punctuality guarantee allows you to be compensated for these delays. There is enough space for everyone. The presence of individual 230V sockets (European plugs) allows you to plug in your smartphone or computer for the duration of the journey.
Delayed train ended up missing Eurostar transfer first and last time using tgv i think i'll fly and coach it in future
Departure from Geneva and 3h30 after Paris we arrive at Lyon station, a metro ride to the hotel. 62€ per person round trip great.

Strasbourg, a major city in the Alsace region, can be reached from Gare de l'Est. The line also extends to Germany, so I started from Stuttgart, a city famous for its car industry in southwestern Germany, got off at Strasbourg, toured the towns of Alsace, and then headed from Strasbourg to Paris. Where do we put the luggage? This is not the first time that I have had to go to Roissy CDG airport. Each time it is the same inconvenience: There is no room for the suitcases! For years, the SNCF has still not understood that people taking the plane need a sufficient volume of luggage racks on this train serving an airport. I have experienced (almost every time) anarchic stackings of suitcases in the entrance airlock with the impossibility of gaining my reserved seat. Reflection of the controller, while I was sitting stuck on a sort of folding seat in the airlock filled with passengers and baggage: “You have a reserved seat, why don’t you occupy it? ". Answer: “How do I get there, traffic is blocked everywhere? »Returning (for the second time) from Japan where I used the Japan Rail Pass for 2 weeks to travel the country from south to north) I can testify that the fast Shinkansen trains are comfortable, well soundproofed, always on time, without unpleasant surprises from repeated strikes, with space and absolutely impeccable on-board service (2nd class). As for toilets and sinks, there are more of them, more modern and better sized. In comparison, we can judge that our SNCF is very mediocre. Sending SNCF executives on an internship with their Japanese colleagues would open their eyes and draw inspiration from what is best in terms of rail transport. I recently saw in the press that in Normandy, because of the dead leaves, the Paris – Granville trains leave late or early and that they are sometimes replaced by coaches. We think we're dreaming. There is also the fall of the leaves from the trees in Japan, but their trains do not slip and are as punctual as possible. We understand that French users are exasperated. Coming back to the Japanese Shinkansens, judge their layout and the space on board: On one side a row of 3 armchairs; on the other a row of 2 armchairs and between the two a wide aisle with a constant service of snacks, and ekiben (railway bento) hot and cold drinks by exceptionally courteous staff. We obviously have a tablet and a cup holder. As a bonus, sockets allow you to power a computer or smartphone.... and there is room to put your suitcases! When a conductor or a person from the catering service enters a carriage, he begins by greeting (by bowing) all the passengers and he does the same (by turning around) when he leaves the carriage. The doors separating the carriages open with a touch of the hand and do not have the annoying habit of closing prematurely. Another innovation: each row of armchairs (3 and 2) has a pedal allowing you to unlock the base to arrange the seats in the direction of travel or vice versa. The maneuver requires no effort; a child being able to return the rows alone. We were a family of 3 adults traveling with 3 children. For long journeys, we could choose to face each other to play cards, or converse for example. As for the trains (monorail for Tokyo Haneda airport) which go to the airports, large luggage spaces are provided and circulation is easy. The level of the platforms is perfectly flat with the threshold of the train door and the gap between platform and carriage is reduced for safety. The suitcases pass without difficulty from the platform to the floor of the carriage, whereas in the low-loaded (double-decker) SNCF wagons you have to go through steps that go down. The signage on the ground for the different trains is perfect and the legendary politeness of the Japanese means that getting off and on is done without anarchy, even at peak times. Yes, the Japanese are "the lords of the rail". They have everything to teach us. On this subject I read in Claude Leblanc's guide: "Japan seen from the train" this (page 59): "in 50 years of operation the Shinkansen has never experienced a fatal accident" and again this (page 62): "During the earthquake-tsunami of March 11, 2011, none of the trains came off their tracks with passengers on board despite the extreme violence of the shock. It must be said that considerable progress has been made by Japanese engineers. Even the high-speed trains that were traveling at the time of the earthquake managed to stop without incident. ... The only time a Shinkansen was derailed during an earthquake was in 2004 during the earthquake which shook the Nigata region 350 kilometers north of Tokyo, but without causing any casualties. Japan and its people, we return more humble to France.

How 21st century France cannot provide a correct and continuous internet connection (we go through all the statuses...) on its Avignon-Brussels TGV line for which we paid €140.00. A real shame and last experience for me.

We went from CDG airport to Marne-la-Vallé/Chessy (Disney station) and it was a 10 minute journey. We were allowed to purchase tickets in advance online and when we got there we just put the codes into a machine and it provided us with round trip tickets. On the way back, the TGV was delayed by half an hour (it was supposed to be at 9:01 am and was going to be at 9:31 am) and it was going to make it difficult for us to catch the flight, but the TGV conductor at 8:53 am allowed us to travel on this TGV even without the correct ticket just so we wouldn't miss the plane. they were very friendly! clean and silent carriages.

Such a fast way to get anywhere book trip in advance as they say . We waited the morning not thinking and prices and possible time you want wont be  available comfortable seats clean wonderful views . Restrooms as well food cart as well seats have table no wifi

Taking a TGV or Eurostar through European capitals is an attraction that you cannot miss when traveling in Europe. Moving at more than 300 km/h in several sections, it is possible to move quickly between nearby cities, enjoying stunning landscapes and aboard one of the most modern vehicles in the world. The sumptuousness of the train’s facilities is a spectacle in itself. Care must be taken, however, for those who suffer from vertigo or labyrinthitis, as pressure fluctuations due to small changes in level during the journey as well as entering tunnels cause minor discomfort in the ears of some people, such as the elderly and children.

I always find the TGV from Porta Susa to Paris very convenient, the price varies greatly depending on how far in advance you book and also when. I spent from 25 euros (historical minimum for this last stay, October 2016) to 200 euros with a supplement of 15 as I purchased a ticket on board. By the way, I would like to point out that it is therefore possible to purchase a ticket on board, when there are no more tickets available at the ticket office, for the TGV always keeps reserve seats which it sells for 15 euros more on board. You need to immediately look for the conductor on the ground, he usually gets off towards the middle of the train, and make sure there is a seat (sometimes they have even run out of reserves).

The TGV is still as fast and efficient, but it doesn't feel as good as a few years ago. And often the fault of the travelers themselves, who speak loudly, who let their cell phones ring when they are asked to put them in silent mode with vibration, who listen to loud music coming from their headphones. And who speak loudly when they are in a group, especially in squares. No criticism at the bar level, where the service is good, even if the quality of the "dishes" is quite average. One thing though: "Voyages SNCF" dares to sell seats where you travel standing up, on the website. Fortunately the controllers are friendly and find you a seat, even if it means putting you in first with a second ticket. Be aware that the mention "unallocated seat" means "traveling standing"... the site counts on absenteeism (quite logical, as in planes which overbook) of a certain percentage of travelers. The toilets are what they are, it is often also ugly on planes, at the end of the flight! But the technology is still there, the TGV sometimes reaches 310 km/h between Avignon and Saint-Exupery, some trains have speed displays.

I was surprised to see a two-story vehicle. Unfortunately, I made a reservation on the first floor, but the seats were relatively spacious and nice. However, although there was an outlet, I was a little disappointed that I couldn't use it and that I couldn't recline the seat.

I went on a few trips: To Chenonceaux, Amboise and Rennes during these last holidays. Rennes to go to Saint MICHEL. The train service in France is enviable! The organization and support on the platforms by the Sncf staff is impressive. They are always helpful in resolving doubts. With rare exceptions, delays occur, well justified by works on the railway network.

Took the TGV from Gard Lyon to Avignon 2 weeks ago and Avignon to CDG airport today. Really liked it!Very fast. Very quiet. Ticket purchase easy. First class is worth the very nominal extra cost. Only disappointment was food choices. Eat beforehand you go. Basically just snacks and minimal food. Great way to get from Paris to the country.
If the service is 1st class! It would be wise to think about cleaning the toilets from time to time... And the rest too! Tablet and floor full of crumbs from the previous traveler!

Reservation of 14 berths in 1st class, therefore higher price, which is normal! What is less so is that they are identical berths to the second ones (only 4 are open) which are very uncomfortable, with dirty pillows (we don't dare grab them to put them in covers) and duvets which have not seen a wash for a long time! They are in non-airtight nylon bags, and you have to install a kind of non-woven sheet that is folded over the end of the feet, not the foot really! No comfort, but who cares, when you have a monopoly, you don't care about the customer! The SNCF trains were much more welcoming!

I think trains are the best means of transport. More comfortable than planes (economy class, which is the most used). The TGV are there, it's wonderful. Comfortable, fast. Easy disembarkation and always central. It's not always cheap. But if the reservation is made in advance, we will find good ones.

Since the journey time is 1h50 to make the Strasbourg-Paris journey it is a treat. For my part, my trip went without incident. The TGV was on time at departure and arrival for both journeys that day. I always travel in 1st class but I don't find the seats very comfortable, it must be said that I am rather tall, 1.90 m. fortunately with less than two hours of travel it is bearable even if I find the ticket a little expensive for a return trip during the day.

This is, simply put, a very fast train with fairly comfortable seats.  It does get crowded quickly.  It is a nice smooth ride.  I have used the TGV 5 years in a row for various travels with students from or to Paris from various towns in France.   With a lot of students, luggage space can be difficult to find, so by the same token, if there is a large group on your train, you might want to get on early to get luggage space.Good service.  Friendly staff who check tickets and roam with the snack cart.

A very convenient of traveling inter-cities via the TGV! Comfortable seats and food vendor inside train but the toilets are not very clean for some trains. Better than driving as you can sit back relax and enjoy the views outside.

We took the TGV train from CDG to Beaune (via Lyon) and from Dijon to Paris Gare de Lyon. Traveled first class from CDG, and second class from Dijon. Wasn't much difference between first and second class, hence the change on the second journey. It was fine, not particularly fast (several delays) and not enough places for luggage on the second route. Still far better than driving!
An overbooking in 1st on the St Exupéry Lyon/Paris Gare de Lyon route is also that. The photo is edifying...Thank you for the removal of double-decker trains on this line...

Do not, under any circumstances, book your French rail travel with SNCF Voyages. We made this mistake in July.  They were to send us our rail tickets from Montpelier to Argeles, and failed to do so.  At Montpeleier station an appallingly rude and self-righteous official told us that the tickets had certainly been sent.  It turned out within minutes that they had not: SNCF Voyages had recorded meaningless words and numbers instead of our email and telephone. The rude official did not apologise, but forced us to pay for our tickets again, and claim.  We claimed; the process required us to send vast amounts of information, as well as the original tickets, by recorded delivery to an address in Spain, at enormous expense.  No one bothered to acknowledge them,  After several enquiries, I was told that my claim had been "been sent to level 2 who are responsible for the last stage in claims."  Today, just under three months after we were forced to pay twice for our tickets becausse of an SNCF Voyages mistake, nothing has been received, not even an apology.
In general, it is better maintained than the subway, for example. But even so, it has its flaws. Of course, if you need agility above all else, it's the best option.

Ok.  I am in France to BE in France.  Vueling or Easyjet are ok, I am well versed at air travel; so even though I am NOT fluent, (in anything really), I believe that good manners, enthusiasm, & sincere attempts to butcher someone else's native  language go a long way (as well as some skill at charades, a very strong sense of humor, and willingness for self-deprecation) to assist you in doing anything that makes you uncomfortable but allows you to immerse yourself in your experience.  Although I humiliate my tween daughter consistently, I have accomplished many, many goals, and not yet been banned from France.  Buy your tickets in France.  Talk to the conductors.  Talk to the passengers.  People are lovely and they will help you.  Those experiences will make your trip.  Smile.  Get out there. It makes the journey worthwhile.

Unfortunately, apart from the friendly train staff, there isn't much positive to say about my trip to Paris. After all, I was traveling first class and found the seating to be comfortable, but still a lot of groped. The food was poor. There was no water in the toilet, without notice. Way back: Coffee machine broken, oh well. Unfortunately, the way back was also delayed. Conclusion: The short journey/distance ratio has to make up for the whole miserable rest.

It was my first time experiencing TGV. When the platform number is displayed on the electronic bulletin board, it is interesting to see the passengers start moving all at once and move to that platform. As written in many travel books, regular tickets must be stamped by passing them through a ticket gate (engraving machine) located at the end of the platform. However, if you book your train online and print your E-TICKET, there is no need to stamp it. When I headed to my destination car, the staff at the entrance read the barcode on my E-TICKET and confirmed it. After we started running, the conductor came to check on us even after we took our seats. Surprisingly, he was very strict! As soon as I feel it. The ride was very comfortable. Is this the TGV while driving around Paris? It was so slow that I thought it was, but by the time I got out of the suburbs and saw the countryside, I had picked up speed and exceeded 300km/h. It was a second class seat, but it was equipped with an outlet and a table. Next time, I would like to ride a German ICE.

TGV is a well-known success story in France, the 300 km/h speed has completely changed the destiny of many French cities in the 80’s and 90’s. The majority of them are now 2 or 3 hours away from Paris’ centre. You can catch it directly in Paris CDG or Lyon LYS airport to avoid the high fees to reach the busy centres of Paris or Lyon in case you don’t need to go there. The train itself is modern, quiet, and efficient. It could be cleaner with friendlier staff at the stations but Hey- you’re in France! For most national destinations, the time door-to-door is shorter and the trip much more peaceful than when using the plane, but the logic for the ticket prices is now as messy as for planes. Go directly to the official web site –look for voyages sncf available in many languages – you may get a good discount on tickets like “Prems” or “IDTGV” which you will probably not get if using a travel agents or a travel package. The electronic ticket works great, you don’t even need to print it.
Nothing to say about this journey. Train clean and in very good condition. Small problem: the power outlet doesn't work!!

A little daunting finding platforms and cars.  Use the yellow ticket machines and don't get flustered. From CDG seemed a little less confusing, the main thing to know is Disneyland is not listed on the machine use the "Marne De Valle Chessey" stop and on the way back to CDG asking questions is almost futile watch the screens and check them all you only have a few minutes from the platform announcement until the train comes.Just like a rip-current keep your cool.
Pleasant trip, pleasant staff. Very expensive ticket (TGV) 120€. Wifi is still missing, connection at each stop :).

Our first class tickets were booked in Australia, ten days prior to departure. Tickets were sent via email. Having caught trains in Germany, Austria and Switzerland, we were interested to see the comparison. Gare de Lyon is insane, even at 630am. There is no notification of which platform your train will depart, however if you ask nicely even in broken French, they will tell you. My feeling is that if you are local, you just know, the TGV a Nice is dix- sept (17).The section Paris to Marseille is super fast and once beyond that, going east along the more coastal areas, it is a little slower. It was very disappointing that for the whole journey there was no wifi (not sure if that was a password or access issue). Again, there is no notification of which stations, when or where so it does pay to do some research on their routes via the website. TIP: make two photocopies of your tickets, in separate bags and take a screen shot or save to iBooks.TIP: do pick up supplies before your journey. It surprised me that not even a quality baguette was available on board and the queue was horrendous to purchase very average fare. Boulangerie Paul or Brioche D'or is the best choice here and if you are organised, a later train will allow you to have brunch at "Le Train Bleu", upstairs.TIP: 20 minutes prior to boarding, be prepared to run with your luggage, you must pack light! There will be a scramble for seats and luggage hold and people walk up and down the car confused thinking you have their seat - even with reserved tickets, it will not be marked (unlike in the UK).TIP: 1 or 2 marked in colour on the car is the "classe" while the carriage or "voiture" is marked in digital closer to the door.Nonetheless, this was a good journey and saved us having to transit to CDG or Paris Orly Airport and at the other end, transit to Cannes (45-60min by car).Conclusion: convenient but when compared to other countries, service is lacking. Our early departure got us there just on time for hotel check in.
This is the fastest way to get from the airport to the park.  Only 10 minutes. It is 24Euro each way.  Make a reservation for the way back as the trains do sell out in advance.

I really love the fact that, when you are travelling to Paris by TGV, you already arrive in the city itself! From the Gare de Lyon it only takes you 20mins to get to La Defense (compared to the almost 2h you spend in transit if you arrive by plane at CDG!).the train ride itself takes about 3.5-4 h which just fly by if you are working or reading a book. And so far, all my train connections have been quite on time, no lengthy delays. just make sure you book your tickets in advance, especially if you want to travel 1st class. There are usually some special rates, which actually are not that much more expensive than 2nd class tickets.
I traveled there from Turin to Paris, climbing up you immediately have the sensation of dealing with the Transalpe and with a culture different from the Italian one.

A delay on our originally booked Eurorail train royally screwed us. We had to get off in Cologne and grab the subway to the main station where the next Eurorail to Brussels wouldn't be leaving in time. Our only option was to ask Thalys- a privately owned company if we could catch their train. They were able to put us on their train at a discounted fee at the very last minute. We were very grateful. Comfortable train and free wifi, so no complaints!Thank you staff of 16:43 from Cologne to Brussels, September 24th.

Inadmissible delay. I was late for an exam. the cost of the ticket is too high compared to such a poor service! I do not recommend to everyone! Rather use blabla car which is certainly better than the services offered by thello.

The trip to Hendaye/Paris was tough due to the limited legroom if you travel with a stranger in the seat in front of you. The first part of the trip, when your knee doesn't hurt yet, is not bad because at least there was free Wi-Fi, but there comes a time when you no longer know how to sit. The return trip was worse, since one of the two tickets we had stated that we did not have an assigned seat, something that was downplayed at the station because "the conductor would solve it for us." Well, here we are, on the Paris/Hendaye train, one sitting and the other standing in the gaps between carriages, having paid (at all times) for a first class ticket... sharing sorrows with a multitude of passengers in the same condition... the conductors do not dare to make an appearance and also on the way back there is no wifi, the queues at the bar stretch across carriages... Is this the best they have in France? I must say that in Paris we took a German train to a German city, and the difference is very notable. The next trip we will organize to go by AVE, it is clear. This transport is highly not recommended, since the price is not up to the service.
The service is very good. Reliable and sometimes expensive. But it is possible to find good prices too. Arrive early so you don't get lost.

I am from Canada and booked and paid for tickets in advance. Planned trip from Nice to Paris but realized 3 days before trip I had mistakenly booked Paris to Nice.  I emailed the company asking to change this and there was only 1 person that could speak/write in English (fare enough)...and she told me there would be additional fees to change the tickets plus I would have to pay an additional €18 per person at the station because I would not have printed tickets.  When I challenged this-she simply reiterated the company policy and stated I could call her that day only to make the changes.  I didn't receive the email until the following day (because we were in transit) so I called the following day.  The first person I attempted to speak to didn't speak English and simply hung up. I called right back and the person said nobody in the office spoke English.  I than left a follow up email requesting to change the tickets with the person I had been emailing-no reply.Arrived at the train station and low and behold the changes had not been made.  I called the company and the person said it was past the 5 hour deadline and there was nothing he could do.  Unbelievable! Subsequently, we had to purchase 2 new train tickets from SFN which meant the entire trip cost us double.I had a friend that is fluent in French email the original person( in French) had been communicating with and they have never replies to either of us.   BUYER BEWARE once they have your money they don't care whatsoever if the customer needs help or wants to make changes.For the record-I have never written a review before this and appreciate mistakes happen (including when I make them) but this was beyond unacceptable customer service. I decided to write this to help others avoid a similar situation.
I have visited many places, I don't remember where this place was, what was TGV, anyway, Paris is generally very nice, worth visiting.

We travelled on the TGV service from Niort to Paris Montparnesse in First class accommodation.  Journey was as ever very speedy, but we did not like our seats in the Club4 compartments, which seem to be a new addition from SNCF.  It felt claustrophobic and not at all spacious, with little leg room and minimal luggage space in the overhead lockers.  If we use this service again, we will be avoiding and choosing separate seats for two.

Living in Japan, where we often travel on bullet trains, I was eager to have a first-time experience on the TGV, travelling from Basle/Switzerland to Paris.While in Japan we usually choose to travel in second class, mainly due to cost reasons, for this particular 3-hour trip we had decided to book first class seats.What we noticed straight away was that it is actually not so easy to find your carriage, as I felt that the carriage numbers could be a bit more prominently displayed on the cars, especially as there isn't any indication on the platform as to where which carriage number will come to a stop. A bit of a nuisance if you have a lot of luggage. That luggage then presented us with another issue: Where to put it? Unfortunately the baggage rack was already full and, in my view, a bit smallish, especially for a train that is used for tourists and business travellers staying at least a few nights in their destination. So we had to leave our suitcases in the spot reserved for wheelchair users. Lucky for us, I guess, that there were no wheelchair travellers on board.The seating has some plus and minus points compared to what we are used to in Japan. The footrest is very good to have, but we felt that legroom was rather limited, especially when considering that we were travelling in first class.We found the complimentary food and drink service a rather nice feature, although it turned out that it apparently only extends to passengers with an international ticket (i.e. travelling from Switzerland). Some passengers boarding the train in Mulhouse, not far from the Swiss border, were not offered any drinks, although the journey for them was almost as long as for us.The toilet was very much "French style", with the floor all wet. Not sure why.The journey on the whole was OK, but 3 hours is quite enough, as it - despite first class - kind of felt a bit "cramped".Admittedly, the price is rather attractive, and as the whole journey (door-to-door) takes hardly more than if taking the plane, the TGV is surely a very viable alternative.
I travelled down South to Toulouse and enjoyed the TGV service tremendously. Its is a great way too see the French countryside.
On the Milan-Paris stretch, both on the outward and return journey, there was a pungent and persistent smell coming from the bathrooms and very little cleanliness.

Ahhhhh the SNCF, or how to charge 70€ for a Bordeaux - Paris without WiFi and without an electrical outlet (hello, it's 2016...) the second class is a kind of dormitory train, I find these companies shameful which allow themselves to do anything because of a monopoly, don't forget for the SNCF you are not a customer but "users" it immediately shows their vision of things... in short, go 2 stars because it only had 10 minutes late...

Shader than the bar car?? Dishes concocted by star chefs?? These chefs took their fees... good for them... on the other hand it would have to compromise their reputation! I would never eat the M again... which they serve at prohibitive prices... I don't even dare imagine or try to calculate the selling price per kilo of this vile food. I didn't have time to buy my sandwich before getting on the TGV... it was very bad for me. Being hungry, I added a croque monsieur to my order.. 6€40 for them. two pieces of bread covered in cream.. (not even 1€ at Metro) My neighbor took the Maxi Burger.. The box is maxi, the cooking in the microwave too, the price too, the disappointment is maxi XL effect

Looked forward to the journey for months and it did not disappoint,traveled 1st class great seats and first class service from the crew.Started with breakfast at 7:30 as the train left on time at 6:22 the steward was meticulous when he served the meal everything was spot on, It was exactly the same when he served our lunch. You have to arrive 20 min before departure, more than enough time to check out which hall the train goes from.No problem as the station system is easy to navigate. This is my first time on the TGV and it will not be the last, this train is streets ahead of Virgin east coast  1st class. Richard Branson should give it a try and see how trains can run.

Hello everyone. I tell you my experience with SNCF. Back in June I bought 3 tickets to make the trip from Metz to Luxembourg. The page did not give me the option to print at home, it only gave me the option to send it to my home by postal mail. Well, when there was a week left before the trip I began to complain that I had not received them. The answers seemed predetermined, they didn't leave anything clear to me. I asked about how to solve the incident or about the possibility of them being sent to me by email and they answered "you chose postal delivery" (of course, it left me no other option), without further ado, without giving me a solution. The day of the trip arrived. We showed up at the station with enough time because according to what we read we were sure they weren't going to easily put it on us. Well, we arrived at the ticket office with our locator, our email in which the 3 seats were reflected, the amount paid and even the name of the passengers. Operator's response: I cannot give you the tickets because they were sent by postal mail. If you want to ride the train you have to buy another 3 tickets and file a claim to see why you didn't receive them. A question for those who defend the SNCF, is this an answer worthy of a serious company? I was identifying myself, I had the card with which I had made the payment, the car number, the seat number, with my name and surname accompanied by my identification document.... and you can't give me my ticket? Well, to avoid having our trip cut short, we proceeded as we were told. We bought the tickets again at the ticket office and kept them so we could claim them when we returned. Well then. On my return, I send by email the details of the first tickets with the locator, those that we never received, we attach the new tickets, the ones we used, and the payment made at the station. Now comes the best part: they tell us that to file our claim we have to do it in writing by postal mail to an address in France, to a town north of Paris. Certified shipping only costs 18 euros, which if we take into account that the return would be 31 euros makes it almost useless to complain. That's just to open the claim, after they don't come with more letters and nonsense with no guarantee that they will refund the amount. Come on, in my country this is called SCAM. They have this set up so that you pay twice and you lose the desire to complain. If anyone knows how to put a package in them, please tell me. Thank you so much. All the best.

TGV, the original technology of Korea's KTX, is a high-speed train that runs throughout France. I boarded it on the way from Karlsruhe to Strasbourg and on the way back. The interior was two-story, and the seats were good.

to sum up, paid dearly, it was a failure!!! : 5 hours late on the dirty train, not air-conditioned in the heat (cattle wagon), fault not attributable to the sncf therefore no refund, missed plane, accommodation at our expense for the evening (not reimbursed of course) = thank you sncf, to be avoided at all costs

From a transportation standpoint the TGV is still an outstanding way to get around after all these years. However navigating the stations can be a bit of a challenge if you don't do it all the time. At CDG in Paris you need to catch a shuttle train over to the terminal but signs are sorely lacking to direct you there in the airport. Once you're there you have to wait until 20 minutes before departure to know which side of the station to use and which track. If you make it through all of that then the trains are comfortable and fast. If you travel 1st class, for not a lot more than 2nd class, you have room to relax though 1st class accommodations vary based on destination and train set. It's still a great way to get around France quickly without the hassles of flying today. Recommended despite the confusion. Cheers!

The train is a great way to go to barcelona from paris.  I went first class in an individual seat so plenty of space even though the train was busy.  It goes through some great scenary. It arrived on time,  so much more reissuing than flying. Had my own food with me.  The only surprise and disappointment was that there is no wifi hence the 4 stars.

Secure your first class seat from Paris to Zurich by booking online in advance. Since I was traveling alone, I had planned to sit in a quiet solo seat, but there were a lot of groups of Indian families with small children on board, so it was noisy. When I went to the next car to use the toilet, there was a Chinese group. SNCF seems to separate vehicles by race. Since it was around noon, there was a lunch service (a cold version of the airplane meal). All the food was cold and not tasty.

We traveled on the TGV to go from Turin to Paris and back. On both occasions we found dirty and dilapidated carriages, no Wi-Fi on board, cramped and smelly toilets. We Italians are used to always complaining about our services and the grass always seems greener on the other side... but if this is the flagship of the French railways, they too are not much better off than us, on the contrary... The only advantages are the price and punctuality

looked forward to this journey but  the seats were dirty grafiti on stairwells and gangs of youths blocked toilet entrances as they where using them to smoke illegal substances.we love train travel but will not be going this way agein

Especially the Atlantic with the La Rochelle/Montparnasse line, what delays due to its slowness with constant work, also evoking problems of overcrowding using this line, resulting in too long luggage loading time. (message on board).The grandeur of the TGV and these former speed records are replaced by its great non-punctuality! An aging and increasingly dirty train, it is high time to open up once and for all the competition on the rails as it exists in the air!!!

These trains are excellent. They are efficient, fast and the the staff very helpful. I had my stuff stolen in Brussels including my ticket and they were very helpful indeed in getting me on the next available train at no extra cost. U.K. Of course was the opposite. They couldn't care less about my stolen ticket and lack of credit cards to pay for new one even when I showed them my email booking. "You have to buy a new one" was the ambivalent response from the uncaring fat man behind the desk.

Not given enough time to find our car. 2 officials misdirected us. At the last moment we jumped on the last car, where my friend was pick pocketed by a " helpful" person. Paid for first class seats which had no more space than second class and were encumbered by tables in the middle of the foot space. Over priced food. Trip  took just about as long as the drive. Only good thing was the helpful conductor who finally used a manifest to find our car and the delightful man in the snack bar.

Very comfortable trip from Paris (Gard su Nord) to Amsterdam. We paid a tourist ticket but they gave us a place in first class cars, without breakfast service. An employee told us that in summer they usually do this. Delicious coffee in the bar car. They sold us tickets for public transport. Excellent. I recommend it and would repeat it.
I often use this transport between Amsterdam and Brussels. Highly professional staff, excellent catering.Book well in advance and you'll find a good deal.

Traveled from Brussels to Nice 1st class in very comfortable, spacious seats that were adjustable. The sockets were also very much appreciated by the children. You don't notice that you are going so fast.  Unfortunately, we had to transfer from Marseille to the front train due to an accident earlier that day and it was overcrowded, so we stood in the passageway with our suitcases. To our surprise, after about 30 minutes two employees came to pick us up and escorted us to still empty seats. Although not first class, it was very nice that we could sit and our suitcases were carried. Great service

Caught this train from Bordeaux to Paris. Was easy booking & changing tickets online, and then used bar code on smart phone on board. Very fast, 300kph on stretch from Tours to Paris. Extremely impressive, would use again, great!

Traveling from Cologne to Paris in second class is a reasonable 35 euros. The vehicle happened to have a shop, so I bought a coffee and enjoyed the journey, which took just under three and a half hours. On the way back, it was the 20th anniversary of THALYS, so I sang Happy birthday THALYS♪ with my son and daughter and a video was taken. I hope it gets selected.
In terms of arrival times, duration 3h03 at terminal 2. August holiday fare €116 return in First class. The seats are adjustable and allow those returning from a long haul to be able to sleep.

The fast train of France or TGV, is a good option for traveling, a little expensive but it has the advantage that you do not have to be at the station for a long time, and the train stations are usually relatively close to the center of the cities you visit.

I don't understand why a mean of transportation can be an attraction. Also how a mean of transportation has a location and the location is in Paris at a certain train station.It is not the greatest train in the world, and because my experience with it on some of the trips in the last 12 months is bad i gave it 2 stars. If the SNCF will improve their services then maybe I will change my review, until then is TGV is not worth more.

TGV,Train a Grande Vitesse is one of the best options in France to travel across..We bought the Euro rail pass & Traveled across the Europe by trains.Among all,the TGV was a great experience.As we were euro rail pass holders,our bookings always were in 1st class.We traveled Paris to Colmar(the french Venice)by TGV Duplex,then Paris to Brussels & Brussels to Amsterdam by Thalys service.Thalys has on board wifi & it was pretty fast.Trains were on time & pretty comfortable.some cabin attendants were with some freaking attitude though,overall it was a nice experience!
reaching the Ville Lumiere with the TGV is a great pleasure, the Gare de Lyon that receives us is magnificent even with the modern improvements it is always a great pleasure to see it.

the new trains in the central region are a disaster!!!, no comfort for people after an hour on the train your back hurts since the seats are uncomfortable, no equipment, in short it feels like you're in a cattle truck!!!! a shame when we know that in other regions, the trains have been put on the high end with all the necessary equipment for people!

Family trip for 4 people, to Paris, the cost of second class is around 300 euros, the carriages are a bit old but in the 4 seater lounge you travel better than on a low cost plane. The train is not very clean and is quite used. Our high speed trains are better.  Punctual takes less than 6 hours from Turin. Ultimately convenient for going to Paris. Without praise or infamy.

From Stuttgart the TGV takes 3:25 hours to reach Paris. At the prices and with this time there is nothing better on this route. There has been a delay once so far, but otherwise everything was on time.

Forget the driving and flying to the South of France and to AVignon take the TGV, relaxed, fast and trouble free. We left from the Gare de Lyon and down to Avignon in just over 2 hours and arrived fresh at the TGV station, little tip if you need to go to the Avignon central station the TGV ticket covers that short journey. We will use the TGV for every trip in future.

Too bad about the lies on the websites where tickets are sold. "There are only 2 places available for this price", while the TGV was less than a third full. For the rest it is pleasant and calm, the staff is always friendly.

We have requested a refund for the two Avignon-Paris tickets we were unnecessarily made to purchase today, August 7, 2016 at gare Avignon.  We were sold the tickets when we arrived a couple of minutes late for the 10:01 train.  After we exited the sales office we noticed that our original train had been delayed (Not announced on the Internet because we had checked) and was up on the platform. We raced to the platform only to have the doors close as we were steps away.  When the ticket agent (I didn't get her name) sold us tickets for the next train, she didn't bother to let us know that we hadn't missed our original train.  When I went back and to complain she said she is just a ticket seller and doesn't watch the schedule. I find that very hard to believe. And if true, extremely poor service. The two additional tickets cost 232 Euro or 116 eachWe have receipts for everything.We have written the Gare d'Avignon and are awaiting their response. It would be nice to have a happy ending to our trip rather than a bad taste.

Viajamos de Stutgart Alemania a Paris en el tren TGV, es una gran experiencia, nunca habia viajado en tren en europa, los asientos son comodos, no tiene suficiente espacio para guardar maletas grandes, lo recomendable es llevar maletas medianas, el recorrido fue de 4 hrs aprox, y hay una pantalla donde indica el tiempo recorrido, alcanza una velocidad de 300 km/hr son bastante eficientes y tienen salon comedor donde se puede disfrutar de un crossaint y cafe, es una experiencia fascinante, I recommend it!

We were debating on flying from Paris to Nice on Easyjet or Ryanair since it is cheap and only takes an hour, but decided on the TGV for the experience.  It was comfortable, air conditioned and clean.  The best part was seeing the French countryside - the vineyards of Burgundy and Beaujolais, the little stone villages on the hills, the lavender and sunflower fields of Provence, and the beautiful Cote d' azur.  This turned out to be one of the favorite we did in France.

We took the TGV from Avignon to Paris.  We had First Class seating.  Based upon that experience, from now on, if there is a option to take a high speed train vs an airplane, I would take the train.As I see it, there are many benefits to taking the TGV.  First of all the train departed and arrived on schedule.  The seats are spacious and comfortable with lots of leg room. The ambient noise level seemed hushed when compared to the constant roar on an airplane which made the ride more relaxing. There was great entertainment value watching the scenery zip by.  Finally, the TGV is fast and departed from the center of Avignon and arrived in the middle of Paris so the total hotel to hotel transit time was probably not much different from traveling by air.Dealing with luggage was a minor issue. We had to carry our luggage up and down long sets of stairs.  (There were elevators available but they were small and inconvenient). We didn't have issues storing our luggage but others getting on at later stops did.. All stops were announced in French which could have caused us a problem if we had to get off at a station before Paris.
You like adventure and the unexpected...you will be served by traveling with the SNCF and its famous TGV..."everything is possible" it's true but above all the worst...

86 euros for a Paris CDG - Nantes... without even paying the exorbitant price. They could at least use part of the price to pay for some cleaning. Frankly disgusting seats covered in food or greasy and black window sills.
