So wish we had high speed train travel in USA. Took the train from Paris to Marseille. Arrived early as it was our first time through the station. Booked the top level. Not first class, but the level below. The train was awesome. Very comfortable. Got to see some countryside. Great trip. Recommend bringing food onboard for the ride. Limited options on the train. Arrived refreshed and relaxed.
I used the train system to Paris from Milan. The system is efficient, the train I took seemed a little old, but it served perfectly. It's totally approved.
Trip to Paris from Italy with the thello euronight white arrow combination. Cheap trips thanks to promotions but with long transport times. Good accommodation

The high speed rail is the ideal way to get from point A to point B in the shortest amount of time.  The trains are very clean and even when you are traveling on a train with 20+ 3rd graders you'd be amazed at how well behaved these children are.  They were actually a delight to travel with and made our journey from Paris to Nice fly by!  Everything you need is available.  Seats are comfortable and offer plenty of space.  Food and drinks are available should you have forgotten to pack you own.  The biggest plus - TGV was always on time!

What can I say!! Nothing new that everyone knows...! Just recounting a conversation: Me: "hello sir, I missed my connection following the delay of my train. I would like to know where I can sit? "The agent/controller: (no hello!) "ah but I'm not going to seat you!" (Thank you for the welcome and politeness) Me: "I'm not asking you to seat me, I'm asking you to advise me to know if you have unreserved seats? "The agent / the controller: "well... you get on the train and you'll see..." Me: "ok! I understand, I'm managing!!! Thank you sir!!"Conclusion: A perfect service!!! Top notch customer relations!!! Well done training!!! And a trip between two cars in the heat while my dear controllers chat in good comfortable seats in 1st!!! I looooove it!!!!  WELL DONE!!
Stinky sweaty first class cabinDirty exterior railway carsDusty cabinWorn upholsteryNoisy brakesOn time departure.

Compared to Italian trains, the ones in France suck! We had to take it twice and we were deeply disappointed. Dirty and smelly and absolutely horrible. Just take a ride on ANY Italian train and lear from them how to treat customers.

One thing i've learned, it is better to book your ticket online ahead of time. The benefit is really great -- you get to choose a good seat and the possibility of booking a much cheaper price. Train are on time!
Very fast, very clean, very quiet. A great way to travel at least in 1st class. The trip from Paris to Lyon was the best. Recommend that you travel the French country side this way.
TGV is sweet but be very prepared to board and disembark.....all done very rapidly. Montparrsse station easy to navigate...have taxi drop you off on the 2nd floor.
Seat okay, NO internet service as advertised.  Coach attendants were friendly.  Toilet (as expected) was very smelly.....

We traveled to and from Paris to Geneva on TGV Lyria. It was fantastic. None of the stress of driving or flying. So easy. And we could nap comfortably, get a snack at the bar car, or watch the beautiful countryside go by. It was definitely worth the price. I believe we paid about $280 euro for 2 adults and 1 child one way.

I had a problem with my ticket that I was not aware of until it got checked on the train. The guy didn't know what to do and couldn't answer any of my questions. So I asked the SNCF and got 2 different answers from 2 different people and in the end ended paying a ridiculous fine. Between the incompetency of the personnel and an unreliable service (strikes and being stuck for 3 hours with no info and the train manager deciding to close the bar so there was nothing available to drink), I'm pretty fed up. Take a TGV at your own risk!

There is not a ticket collection machine at every station it would seem (Sallanches didn't have one) so you have to go to the ticket office anyway.  The confirmation email for ordering gave no indication of this but could do quite easily.The journey itself was fine and on time throughout. On the train, the first class cabin was busy but not noisy. The individual seat was quite comfortable and it's good to have the plug socket for the long journeys. The toilets are disappointing and got in quite a state quite quickly. Sat in the seat nearest them, it did become a little smelly after a while but it was mainly the cleaning product I could smell. There's little luggage space for big bags and I had to rearrange some of the storage so I could get mine in.

I am writing this review because I am returning from JAPAN. I took the Shinkansen (Japanese TGV) for 3 weeks straight. Unfailing punctuality!!!! I hallucinated. To the minute... But not only the trains, the metros, the buses too. So on my return to France, I took the TGV from Paris to Hyères and there!!! Boom! Welcome back to France ^^30 min late at departure. No update of arrival time in Hyères then ultimately 50 minutes late on arrival. It's not that it bothers me a lot, but there's a lot of neglect in this society. What to say? At least the SNCF represents the French well: always on strike, never punctual LOL

TeGeVe, French-style, perhaps one of the first European high-speed trains. And it shows! In fact I had the impression that they are a little dated. Not very comfortable seats, no Wi Fi. The Milan-Paris section with speeds worthy of being defined as HIGH are in the Milan-Turin and Chambery-Paris sections. The Val Susa stretch is practically regional style. Past Modane... too! On the other hand it is expensive! Positive and quality service. The staff speaks both Italian and French very well. The announcements are the same in both languages. The fact that we get off at the Gare de Lyon is positive. In the heart of Paris. And that's no small thing...
We travel at 300 km per hour from Brussels to Paris. Awesome. Comfortable and super fast. Highly recommended.

Booked to travel 1st Class on the TGV high speed train to Cannes from Paris, only announce the platform 15 minutes prior to departure then an absolute shambolic stampede as everyone tries to get on the train with big pieces of luggage, during all if this no conductor in sight, when one is located he proceeds to scream in French and then ignore your ticket and pushed you into a carriage with no seating left and then everyone sits for 5 hours in the stairwell next to the WC ... WonderfulThe trains do not interconnect all the way so we could not walk further down the train.Clearly no safety concerns on this high speed train...
The train's clothing is torn and the carpet is very dirty, for the price of the ticket they could do with maintenance. You must arrive 2 hours in advance to pass all immigration and security checks.

We traveled from Hendaye to Disney. In second class the outward and in first class the return. A very pleasant, comfortable trip. The worst thing about the trip is the two transfers, it gets tiresome. In Bordeaux it is only fifteen minutes, so you have to be alive, but it gives you time. On the way back, it takes ten minutes, but it also gives you time. It is expensive, 600 euros round trip Hendaye Disneyland Paris, for two adults and two children. There were better prices but the times that interested me, first thing in the morning and last thing in the morning, are what there was. In my case, the first class of the return, departure included, was cheaper than the second. I'm talking about five euros. But it is worth it, the wider and more reclined seats. There is no WiFi, which could already be done for the price. You have a plug to charge your devices. They have a cafeteria, a cafe for almost three euros. French price.
That's the one and primary advantage of tgv trains. And also the safest way to travel.Access from platforms is too congested though, and tickets still expensive.

We took TGV from nice to paris, it was 80 minutes latte and at no time information was given in english, only in french and on screens there was no info about delay either, and we had to catch next train... No wi fi.
despite booking well in advance, I didn't enjoy the trip the Eurostar was dirty smelled of beer very little space

I took the TGV from Rennes to Paris, as it was on sale, I chose to give a little more and go first class. The journey is really quick and the train is comfortable. But I didn't like that all the seats were facing each other, it meant there was little privacy and little space to stretch your legs. The train was old-fashioned, already a little old. And no internet access. In Portugal we don't have a TGV but we have the Alfa commuter which I consider to be quite comfortable and spacious, even in the tourist class. By comparison I consider it to be better. I also realized that there are different trains depending on the destination, perhaps this line is less profitable for the company. I confess that my expectations were high, even based on the comments I had read here. Maybe that was the problem 😉The advantage is speed!!!

We did Paris, Avignon, Barcelona, ​​everything connected and much more. Comfortable trains, silent, at times very fast, at other times fast compared to the ones we have in Latin America. They were not as punctual as they say on the tickets (that 9.03 or 15.17) it was not so like that either, they are not Swiss, but in general punctual. It is part of the experience and you enjoy the landscape.

Traveled on the TGV "fast train" from Lille to Lyon no second class seats left so had to pay for "First class" firstly this was an absolute rip off there was barely anywhere to put your luggage tickets were not checked once people whom hadn't paid for first class were sitting in our seats which caused a lot of hassle on more than one occasion. The train was delayed on several occasions to be fair the kitchen provided free food as compensation but it was disgusting. The train was anything but fast I'd be willing to pay for a flight next time.Would not recommend this train at all considering it was supposed to be first class there was no wifi use of phones in first class is prohibited a complete waste of money.

So as a member of the Irish green army (football fan) I needed to get from Lille to Lyon so we decided we would go on the TGV and to treat ourselves to first Class.First I would really like to compliment Michel our booking agent at Lille Europe who was a thorough gentleman and did all that he could to help us!However the train itself was a complete disappointment, there was a stale smell in the cabin, it felt old and musky, and the lighting was dim and the air conditioning was intermittent on a very warm trip to Lyon.Maybe we are blessed in Ireland but there was no Wifi aboard the train which I could not believe, as it is on every train and bus in Ireland.Our train was delayed for over 2 hours in Charles de Gaul and we were given no explanation only an emergency ration box containing biscuits pasta and apple purée!! Overall I was rather disappointed by the train journey but more than that totally shocked by the lack of first class. Similarly I wouldn't fancy seeing what the economy was like

We travelled by train from London to Varenna on Lake Como last week. The majority of the journey was excellent - Eurostar was great and Italian first class train travel always fantastic. Unfortunately the leg between Paris Gare de Lyon and Zurich was in the TGV. We had booked first class but it was more third class than first. It felt old, tired and dirty with broken seats and no air conditioning. We were delayed before boarding at the station with no explanation, no idea what was happening, no where to sit down and very hot station at Gare de Lyon. While I would recommend travelling to Italy by train from London which was a real adventure the TGV was a complete let down.

The TGV in France was clean, relatively inexpensive, on time and extremely quick.Would recommend this as the premier mode of transpo for your visit in France, offers multiple destinations, packages and varied travel schedules. Staff was qualified and pleasant and the views through the large windows beautiful.Made for great people watching and fun conversations with fellow travelers.
We took the TGV to go from Lourdes to Paris and the entire trip was very good: clean train, comfortable seats and good punctuality. Of course, you have to buy tickets in advance to get better prices.
Luxury for low cost price and wifi. Love the TGV in France, ensure that you book the idtgv to benefit from reduced costs

Unfortunately, having missed the TGV from Paris, we were directed to the 'boutique' of Thello Gare de Lyon. We had never heard of it. Seeing the 'hostesses' at the ticket counter, and hearing the prices ($120 per person, second class only!), we thought of a new company, like our Italo. Maybe! Real rubbish! RUBBISH! Six-berth cabin, all very cramped, uncomfortable, dirty. The bathrooms on the entire train remained closed for hours! Lying on my very uncomfortable and shaking bunk I felt like I was in a niche. Zero Security. Luckily I was with my husband. I scored a dot but it would be unspeakable. HIGHLY NOT RECOMMENDED! Too bad because the idea of ​​traveling at night would be positive.

My experience on the TGV was very short as I used the service to quickly travel from CDG airport to Disneyland Paris (Chessy). From what I could see, the service is very punctual, the carriages are spotless, the on-board staff are very helpful. Even if the cost of the ticket is not exactly cheap, I recommend it to those who want to travel quickly.

On 01/05/2016 I purchased the TGV9242 Milan-Lyon online (2 people, 1st class, Euro 39x2), on 26/05 I received an email from SNCF indicating the CANCELLATION of the train due to works on the affected railway section. I visited the SNCF website and on the blog I read comments from users from three months earlier (February) who asked about the cancellation of the train (but works of this type which involve diversions and abolition of trains are not known well in advance...???). I went to the SNCF boutique in Milan-Garibaldi for clarifications but having purchased the tickets online, I had to send an email to request a refund; the operator on site could only sell me an alternative route (which involved two changes) but "clearly" the difference in price of the two changes would have been at my expense (in addition to having canceled the trip, I also had to pay more for it). On 30/05 I requested an online refund of the tickets, and only after 19 days (against the 48 hours indicated on the SNCF website for the response) they asked me for a copy of the email that the SNCF itself sent me indicating the cancellation of the train (...they ask me to prove that the train was really cancelled...?!?!). Well, I still kept it and sent it, asking for a quick settlement of the matter. (I think they are playing on the fact that the email may have been trashed...). I hope that they have speeded up the refund procedures and that the timescales are not as long as a couple of years ago, when I requested a refund for a TGV delay, the refund arriving after 8 months. I use other European train companies but I find that, of all, SNCF is the worst. In the future I will avoid traveling with SNCF, preferring other companies and I will advise anyone I know to do the same. TO AVOID - SHAMEFUL ZERO SERIOUSNESS AND PROFESSIONALISM!!!

Nothing to say, top flight Geneva-Paris-Geneva in 1st class. Booked well in advance, price of 175.-- round trip. Departure and return on time and luckily no strike. Duration 3h07. Meals on board included with a nice tray, to my great astonishment, including wine or other alcohols. Generous with second passage for drinks and for chips or sweets especially on the way out. In addition, efficient and smiling staff. Pleasant.Very convenient arrival at Lyon station.Recommended.

Departure from Toulon on time, even though the train was announced to be late... the staff at the station very good... The TGV arrives from Nice and it is full... no room for my suitcase (nor for the suitcases of the other passengers who get on in Toulon). it is clean... and during the trip a cleaning agent comes by for the toilets!!! only one stop and direct to Paris... so only 3.5 hours... Great... The bar, in the center of the normal train... Good... but they are all identical in the TGVs... Arrival Paris Gare de Lyon on time... For the return the same and on time...

I booked a round-trip ticket from Zurich to Paris online from Japan. When I arrived at the Zurich station that morning, there was no train. When I asked the station staff, I was told that there were no trains going to Paris because the French National Railways was on strike. In the end, my trip to Paris was canceled and I returned home. When I contacted them later to claim the ticket cost and cancellation fee for the hotel in Paris, I was told that unless I received a ``certification of non-boarding'' at the station on the day I boarded the train, I would not be refunded a single yen.If I am not satisfied, I am told that some people will file a lawsuit (in Paris), but most cases end in failure. It's true that proof of non-boarding was written in the terms and conditions at the time of reservation, but was it my fault that I didn't understand that it also applies in the case of a strike? When you add in the cost of first-class tickets, hotel cancellation fees, concert tickets, and restaurant reservations, it's quite a loss, but I think I'll be in tears.
Absolutely worth trying - comfort - practical and above all available for all schedules. Both stations are exceptional

This is my second time travelling with France's TGV. twice I almost couldn't travel due to the strikes... I got on my Lyria from geneve to nice... paid 1st class.. to be honest,  very bad service. Everything that is advertised in TGV Lyria page does not exist.If I had the chance I would travel with other companies  (Austrian railjet or German ICE).The trip was good though.. we arrived on time and safe.

Dirty, old, noisy train that you can't sleep a wink of sleep. Non-existent service, they come by twice to ask for documents without knowing if they have already passed. Restaurant car and food not classifiable.

We took the TGV Lyria 1st Class from Paris Gare Lyon to Basel and now prefer this mode of travel between F and CH.  It departed on time from the very accessible Gare Lyon and arrive within a minute of the scheduled arrival time.  Food served in FC was acceptable and the seats were very comfortable.  If you have a small rolling luggage there is ample space to store near by your seat.  However, if your luggage, no matter the size is a bit heavy opt for a lower level seat as wrestling the bag upstairs can be a bit of a chore for weak-armed folks.

Wife and I took the TGV from Paris (Gare de l'Est) to Reims on 31-12-2015.  Went 1st class there in the morning, then took an evening train back to Paris in 2nd class.  Overall we had a wonderful trip - very comfortable, on-time, and FAST.  If American had this option in the Northeast Corridor, it would be my mode of travel!  Looking forward to the next time I am in Europe to travel on TGV.

The TGV Lyria ride was smoother and quieter than expected. Paris to Lausanne in 3 1/2 hour.  We had a good view about half the time, at other times it was below grade, in tunnels or screened by taller treesThe station is reasonably organized and some shops if you have a few extra minutesHalf the seats face frontwards and half backwards. Some also have much better views and a bit more space - those 8  at the each end of the car typically.So if you don't want to ride backwards chose carefullyFood available at an increased price in the dining car.Since no tickets are checked until it is rolling, freeloaders are not uncommon

I booked my train from Lyon TGV to Avignon and it took about 4hour plus to reach my destination as the train kept stoping in the way for non reason . Be careful for those traveler who is going to chase their next flight as this train will seriously cause you a big loss !!!

We took a TGV bullet train from Paris to Reims, France which was very convenient with a comfortable ride. I try to always take these TGVs in France since we have always enjoyed the speedy ride. France has trains that can take you almost anywhere you want.  All have been on time, clean and up to date too. If you have lot of  bags or small children I would go by plane perhaps as the is better choice. Once in a lifetime kind of fun to experience if you want to travel by TGV speedy trains!
I travelled from Basel SBB and the double French deck TGV was excellent A trolley came by with two Stuart's offering from champagne to water They were very friendly and helpful
The TGV is a great means of transport. Super comfortable, fast and good. I like to travel first class, with the comfort of first class.

Very convenient and comfortable ride. I have been on several TGVs in France and have always enjoyed the ride. They are punctual, clean and comfortable. If you have baggages to cart then probably plane is a better choice. However its an experience if you want to travel by TGV.
on the way back from Paris we traveled with the TGV to Milan, the same as other trains in terms of service and cleanliness. Excellent in respecting its always perfect timetable

We go to Saint-Etienne quite often. comfortable, quite clean, first class is generally great. Sometimes there is not enough space for luggage. rides smoothly and quickly, although I like high-speed trains in Switzerland better...
Good trip down to Nice though if sitting in seats with table between there is very little leg room. Go for airline seats unless travelling with young children

Very pleasant experience. I stayed in a 1st class salon. People repeatedly offered coffee, tea, sandwiches and pastries. Very good care. Great sound. Wifi works. I was able to continue working wonderfully.

We traveled with the TGV Duplex in 1st class from Munich to Paris and back. Including a 30 minute stay in Stuttgart, we were at the Gare de L'Est on time in 6 hours and 10 minutes. Between Strasbourg and Paris it drove without stopping at a top speed of 320 km/h and, to our delight, it did so absolutely quietly. The ride comfort is good, wide seats with plenty of legroom. However, there is no Wi-Fi, but there is a socket for charging cell phones and laptops. The food in the spartan bistro is average, but expensive. It's best to bring something with you.
Unforgettable first-time experience travelling on this modern, high-speed train with my wife from Paris to Geneva and back. It was convenient, comfortable, and overall relaxing.

I took the flight from Brussels to Charles de Gaulle Airport. There are several points that are different from Japan's Shinkansen. [1] Advance purchase discounts are advantageous. Especially outside of the morning and evening peak hours, it is common for fares to be less than half the normal fare. However, you will not be able to change the time. [2] If you purchase on a website or app (English or French) and download/print a barcode ticket, you don't have to go to the station counter or ticket vending machine. [3] People say that there will be delays, but the official website is more kind than the Shinkansen, as the delay status for the past two months is published. [4] The seat orientation is fixed. You cannot specify whether you want an independent seat or a box seat on the website (although it appears you can do this at the counter or at Rail Europe). On some routes, the direction of travel changes at a station along the way. [5] Ticket gates are random. At Gare du Nord and Gare de Lyon, you show your ticket to the staff on the platform, but in Brussels, even though it's an international flight, there was no check at the station or at the ticket gate. [6] It seems that renovations have started recently, but the vehicle is old. However, there is plenty of luggage space and power outlets.
How simple can traveling in Europe be.  Relax with a drink and appropriate reading material or drive your iPad through the French landscape. Blessed

I took a train from Paris Montparnasse to Rennes station and went to Mont Saint Michel. The idTGV is like a sibling that runs alongside the TGV, but I was able to purchase it for 19 euros by purchasing it online in advance. Purchasing with a credit card issued outside of France is a bit more complicated, but it's a great deal compared to regular TGV fares. The vehicles are exactly the same as regular TGVs, and bar trains are also connected. However, you cannot travel to and from regular TGV vehicles. Also, not all TGVs are connected. If there is a setting, you can find it by searching on the SNCF web. There was no setting for the TGV on the way back, and the Prem's fare for the same section was 35 euros.

We travel with Europass and  book 1st class coach on TVG Lyria for our trips from Basel to Paris.The staff intentionally ignore to service us during 3 hours journey. He just pass our seat and do serve others customer, this happen 2-3 times so I'm sure this is by intention. Notice on we are only Asian group on this coach. I'm immediately send feedback to TGV Lyria customer support website and they request a copy of our ticket for verify. After sent all prove evident and 3 times weekly follow up by ail,  I don't get any response back from them. Rude on-board service, inattentive customer support. This is the worst service for our whole journey. not recommend.Note : We also use 1st class service from Trenitalia and Thalys for our trips, both staff are polite, well educated and have good service mind, Thalys is the best.

We Took the TGV from Paris to Avignon.  Train was great Taxi dropped us off at Gare Lyon Paris walked through the doors stamped tickets and on to the train we went, Quick and no problems.  In Avignon station was very modern and easy to make our way out to find a taxi.

Even if the price is high, the comfort is pleasant and the train is punctual. No strike, for once! Only 2 hours and 40 minutes of travel, just enough time to read a few chapters of a good book. The only problem is the people on the phone that can be heard throughout the car, even though it's forbidden! No ticket checks during the journey, is this normal? Means of transport to recommend for zen travel.

We were originally booked last month but had to reschedule because of a strike (that's the reason not a 5 score). Took SNCF TGV train from Bordeaux to Paris. Initially not too fast but final hour was amazing. This thing flies. Tried to remember driving as fast in Germany but way faster. Like in an aircraft just before it takes off. But much smoother.

The ride from Lyon to Paris was fast with only a few snags.  Do wish the elevator to the platform was more clearly marked = lots of luggage up two flights of stairs.  We purchased our tickets on-line weeks before the journey.  That may have been the easiest part.

I think the journey from Milan to Nice is just over 300 kilometres..the journey lasts 5 hours!!..come on..does the train that connects Milan to the Côte d'Azur make 13 stops? The train itself is of decent quality, there is an appreciable bar service...but the stops are too many and some of them are of long duration...absolutely needs improvement..
To be used when your ticket is refunded... otherwise there are other ways that are much cheaper... and certainly quieter, the bus, carpooling, the plane (yes, cheaper!)
An extremely pleasant journey in the TGV Lyria, both journeys on time to the second. The selection in the dining car isn't huge, but it's decent and fairly priced.
Train station beneath Charles de Gaulle is a dump. Want to change ticket ps for an earlier train 40 euros. They charge you to use the bathroom. Place is dirty. Train is nice and it runs regularly.

Perhaps for locals, this trip [Paris to Nimes/Montpellier] is passe, for me it was amazing. There was a bit of a scramble for available luggage towage space as we all boarded (in the end we all fitted in as not many had luggage) but after that the only problem was that the train was so fast that it was impossible to take any photos! The seats were lovely and comfortable, well spaced, and the journey smoother than I ever thought possible for a train, let alone one at 300kph. We did not use the refreshment car. One tip for first time travellers: your platform will be announced at Gare de Lyon only 20 mins before departure. Then be prepared for the rush.

Don't book this night train to Paris, you would start your holiday in the worst possible way. A train from 30 years ago. Dirty, uncomfortable, everything half-broken, toilets unpresentable and indescribable. Noisy and very badly air conditioned. Sleeping is almost impossible in the "loculi" offered. Wi-Fi? Unthinkable on board. Rather, leave the night before by plane and sleep in Paris, you certainly wouldn't spend more!

We went from Hendaye to Paris. 6 hours of very comfortable travel. Silent train, "High speed" debatable but the trip is pleasant. Nobody shouts in the car and thanks each other, even if they talk on the phone! Neither do the children. You can read in peace, or fall asleep or see the landscape...The return trip from Paris to Hendaye is just as calm and pleasant. It is worth taking the trip on the TGV,

This is the first time I have travelled on the TGV through France and found it very comfortable. I booked a few weeks in advance and got a good price and it was cheaper than getting a plane taking about the same time if you include the time you need to be at an airport before a flight. I was able to view the countryside and didn't feel I was travelling so fast as the train was so smooth. Would certainly compare prices with planes and use again.
Great experience of this fast Train. Traveled at 319 kmph at some parts of the journey.Traveled between Stuttgart and Paris. Nice Restaurant aboard - not expensive.
Very good way to travel to Paris without being humiliated at any airport. Comfortable and relatively fast. Of course, the AVE is more modern. Double-decker cars, the upper level is better.

Outward journey 16 April at 8.45am Tgv 9244 Milan P.Garibaldi/Paris Gare de Lyon. Return journey 20 April at 2.27pm. Tgv 9249, same line, the one that passes through Chambery and Aix les bain, certainly not fast. In several places it is very slow, over seven and a half hours of travel, at least five of which you travel at a snail's pace... I'm not exaggerating. I feel like I'm a young girl again on so-called "accelerated" trains... anything but High Speed.... Both trains in question are dated, old carriages, I don't know how old they could be, discolored and worn seats, the power sockets don't work, there are no coat hangers. On three 1st class carriages, on the outward journey, only 2 toilets are functioning (because you can't get into the other two...) damned smelly. On the return journey, always 1st class, same situation as the carriages, but, AS SOON AS WE LEAVE, we go to the toilet and wait patiently for the conductor to come and unlock the door...we are the first! but the smell is suffocating.. But do the workers know that you have to use soap and water to wash it? or didn't they do it at all? Among the countless trips I've taken, this was certainly the worst. And thank goodness we were in 1st class!!! Our Arrows are better, more comfortable and above all cleaner!!! Trains to be strongly discouraged!!!
wow... I always want to travel like this, with that comfort, tranquility... the dining room is all super clean. a single word.    Flawless !!

I frequently take the TGV on the Milan-Lyon route and then continue towards other destinations. The train is always on time, a maximum of ten minutes late, the person on board is very kind and extremely helpful, the problems are of a different nature. It is a train that is now dated, the seats are old, both in 1st and 2nd class, the restaurant/snack service does not excel, there is no surplus of any kind. These considerations apply to almost every French TGV train, our Italian high-speed trains are much more cutting-edge.

Were with the TGV Lyria in "1st class!?" over the weekend in Paris! On the way there, the air conditioning was running at the highest level and this with outside temperatures of 8-10°!?! When we asked why that was like that and what that meant, we only got the answer: "Sorry! But this car you're sitting in has a defect that we can't fix and we don't have enough money for new cars!?" After arriving in Paris I had a stiff neck and pain! That's supposed to be the more expensive and better 1st class????On that The best thing happened on the way back: 1. The train wasn't shown at the station until shortly before departure where we could get back on and then it was wrong where it could come! So we had to rush through the entire Gare De Lyon to catch the train in time!2. When we arrived on the train and found our reserved seat in the so-called 1st class, we had to go to the toilet due to the stress beforehand and the lack of time! But this was closed!?! When I asked one of the train staff a decent question, I got the answer: "The toilet will only be opened by the train manager after departure at some point, BUT I CAN GIVE YOU A BOTTLE SO YOU CAN PICK IN IT!??????What the heck is a statement like that supposed to be from a first class employee???3. When I asked the employee for his name after this statement, he bitchily refused and gave me the Train number! Plus he said more than arrogantly that from now on he would NOT SERVE me anymore!! From then on he just ignored me the whole way! 1st class offer for my money! I hope none of you reading this will ever be offered the same!?
Huge station with connection to metro lines, it is a great experience to travel in Europe by TGV. I highly recommend it!

Excellent mode of travel from Paris to Milan.  Train is super comfortable and a wonderful opportunity to view the countryside.Having said that......Staff taking orders and serving food were incredibly rube and only interested to attend to French people even though they had good command of English.  Completely ignored our part of 4 mature adults, never once asking us if we would like to purchase food, coffee etc.Had to actually chase girl doing service.....she eventually brought down 4 x sandwiches which were incidentally dated made 10th April - our date of travel 13th April, so 3 days old.  Cost of 24 euros or $37 Aussie dollars.  Absolutely disgusting.If travelling on the train ensure you pick up food in town prior to your trip.

We took the TGV from Paris Charles de Gaul Airport to Brussels.  The trip was easy, the service was nonexistent.  After the first leg of our trip I wanted to purchase drinks but the concession car was closed.  I asked and was told we weren't in France anymore and the staff was gone.  I guess you only need to buy bottled water while in France on a two hour train ride.  In 30 years of running this train you would think they would have figured out how to pay staff to work the entire trip.  Bring your own food and drinks.

I don't know if we were particularly unlucky given the period of terror we went through but, every time we took a train, we had problems. The first time going to Disneyland it stopped 3 stops from the terminus and we had to get off. They put a replacement bus which was packed with people and left us (after a shocking 20 minute journey) in the middle of nowhere. After almost an hour waiting we quickly stopped a 7-seater taxi and managed to get taken to Disneyland for the modest sum of €70! On the way to Versailles it stopped for quite a while but then we managed to arrive luckily. The last time was when we had to go to the airport that everything stopped and we were forced to take a subway ride so as not to miss the plane! Really terrible rating!

traveling by train across Europe is something different, I was impressed by the efficiency of the system, the comfort of the trains, and the quality of the service. Whenever I can, I will travel by train around Europe

First class and not the slightest kinder surprise. Big big disappointment for me and my family. Plus it's impossible to go out at the end of the meal, and we end up in another city. The height of the scam, we even have to pay a second time to hope to return. And grandma was no longer hungry. Gray isn't my favorite color either. Strongly advise against it but not that much.

I used it from Paris Gare Montparnasse to Mont Saint-Michel, and from Gare de Lyon to Avignon. In addition, routes are being extended from Gare du Nord to Belgium, the Netherlands, and Germany. The trains I took from Gare de Lyon were all double-decker cars. Compared to Japan's Shinkansen trains, the passenger cars are not missionaries, so the sound when running is quieter, but the car body is narrower and I felt a little cramped even in first class. In addition, the flight attendants told us to be careful about pickpockets and pickpockets in second class (although it seems that this happens even in first class).

I travelled from Turin to Paris with this TGV and the journey itself was relaxing and comfortable. It was way better than catching a plane as all I had to do was getting on the train, sit back and relax. Make sure you book as far in advance as possible as prices could really be unbelievably good. Set up an email alert on the website for the date you would like to travel, in order to be able to get the best price! Bon voyage!

On these super-fast and punctual trains you can travel to many European cities, but make reservations in advance. They are not as economical and not as comfortable if you have seats in the back... but it is the best alternative to having to drive more than 6 hours, while here we go at 300 km per hour (attached photo).   Adolfo V.B

IDTGV Paris / Béziers.. I booked in 1st class in the IDZEN wagon After the Nîmes stop, an unpleasant smell, quite simply the staff passing by pulling a large garbage bag filled with garbage, the travelers are seated and during this time this person who empties all the garbage bins from the locations while there is more than an hour of travel left, I have never seen that.. BRAVO THE SNCF!...

I was forced to take the Paris-Venice train on March 20, 2016, because due to the strike of French air traffic controllers, my flight to Venice was cancelled. We left at 7.15pm and arrived at the Venice Mestre station around 1pm the following day. 17 hours by train. We were stopped in Switzerland for about 3.5 hours due to works on the Swiss railway network. Aside from this non-Thello-related inconvenience, the rest of the trip was a pain. In 17 hours on the train no attendant came to clean the toilets or collect the sheets that are offered for the night. Try to imagine with the train practically full. Not to mention the restaurant car, which quickly ran out of what little it was supplied with. Dated carriages, without wifi. I felt like I had gone back 20 years. All for the "modest" sum of 130 euros. A shame. - ABSOLUTELY NOT RECOMMENDED
Wonderful train, very fast, we bought a europass and traveled first class through several countries, it was perfect!
The TGV has reduced distances in France and near Europe since 1981 when it came into service. A Paris-Brussels in 1h20 and a Paris-Lyon in 1h54. Book well in advance to get a good price.

These high-speed trains from SNCF (French railway) are comfortable, safe and fast. You can use it for trips in France or to other European countries. As it only stops in the main cities in each region, you save time. Very good, I recommend it despite it being the most expensive type of train trip.
If you want to move quickly and comfortably around France, I recommend TGV. Tickets are not cheap but I think it is worth paying.
The most pleasant train ride so far: From Ulm to Paris in 3.5 hours!!! The speed at times is more than 300 km/h. Clean, cozy and only 2 stops!

On March 8th I took the train from Milan to Nice. I usually go by car but having to take it to the mechanic, I decided to try this new experience. I left Milan at 11.10 and to my amazement I discovered that these trains are very welcoming, clean and comfortable and the on-board staff are friendly and helpful. Then they announced the possibility of going to the bar car, I wanted a coffee, but in practice I discovered a small restaurant, the walls are covered with prints representing their products and I let myself be teased by the image of the lasagne, I ate very well, they have an excellent choice of wines, and Illy coffee. The guy at the bar was kind and very nice. Once I finished lunch I returned to my seat, I was relaxing and another guy passed by with a bar cart, also polite and very nice, from whom I purchased a chocolate snack. I think I will avoid using the car for my weekly trip to Nice from now on
We left Paris for Amsterdam on the bullet train, it was one of the best parts of the trip, unmissable! Everyone should travel on these trains to know the feeling.

This TGV train, the service from staff and seat comfort is great. If you are travelling in France and you have the opportunity to travel on the TGV, no matter what class you choose, you will get to your destination fast and in comfort.

The TGV (High Speed Train) is the best way to travel around France, well between Paris and another major city! For example, it takes a bit more than 3 hours to reach Marseille or Aix-en-Provence. However, note that it is not because you're on a TGV that it's going to be fast all the way! For example, as of today, if you're travelling from Paris to Bordeaux, the service will be high speed only between Paris and Tours, mostly because the section between Tours and Bordeaux is not a LGV (High Speed Line) and cannot support high speed services!Anyways, high speed or not, travelling by train is the best :p
Reservation without problem. Fair price for late booking. Price paid 107 euros. Per the SNCF website, the price was 170 euros.
This train is AMAZING. At 300km/h and hardly feel like you're moving. It's quiet and efficient. We came from London to Paris on this and only took about 3 hours.
The trip from Rotterdam to Paris was only €40 for the outward journey and €40 for the return journey. In addition, we were in Paris quickly, ideal for traveling with this!

A punctual transportation may be a little expensive, but the service is very good, the luggage is located in the aisles of each car and they do not charge extra charges. When looking for a price for this service, there are several possibilities in terms of schedules and days, average €189 per person.

Departed Turin 7.39am arrived Paris GdL at 13.31. Lyon to Paris in about 2 hours. Pleasant views through the Alps. Comfortable journey in 1st Class. Very economical and food on the train very reasonably priced. Would have given 5/5 but a bit grubby in places.

Left a wet Turin and travel through the snowy Alps before entering France. Lyon - Paris in under 2hr. Overall journey 5hrs 40min. Great experience, even the food and drink was a reasonable price. Two business class singles about €150 well worth it. Only critics is a bit dirty in places hence the rating not being excellent

TGV allows you to travel around France conveniently and quickly. If you buy it at the same time as it goes on sale or buy it quickly, you can get it at a much cheaper price. Sometimes the price difference between first class and second class is not that much, so compare carefully before purchasing.

Departure at 7 a.m. from the center of Paris by taxi. 7:20 a.m., arrival at Lyon station. 7:40 a.m., departure of the Tgv 12:20 p.m., arrival at Cannes station 12:30 p.m. arrival at Cannes town hall. eternal daily traffic jams. And I'm not comparing the significant difference in cost!
A wonderful way to travel around France and Europe. Used it for trips to Belgium and the South of France. Very pleased.

It promises to get you to Paris from Turin in less than six hours and delivers perfectly. Up to Lyon it goes like a normal train, it makes a lot of stops, then it goes wild and in an hour and fifty minutes it travels the route to Paris. The negative points are the discomfort of the seats and the poor cleanliness. There were also some "Portuguese" on board, which is incomprehensible given that the seats should be booked by Pablera

I went back and forth from Paris to Bordeaux and Bordeaux to Paris. I had a large suitcase and was planning to buy a lot of wine on the way home, so I booked a first class train this time. Last time I went to Rennes, I took a second class train, but the crowd was different. There were no children or young people, there were mostly businessmen and old people. The layout is 3 rows, [1 row - aisle - 2 rows]. I made a reservation in the direction of travel, but it was a bit difficult because it was a coach type and there was a person across from me. It is a long journey to Bordeaux, taking over 3 hours. On the way there, we were greeted by a gentle elderly couple who were kind to us, but on the way back, a very fat person came along. It was better because it was a cool season so there was no smell yet. There is a dining car that no longer exists on the Shinkansen in Japan, so I went to see it. However, it is not restaurant style, just a shop and chairs. It seems that some trains are not coach type, but it was a failure.

We had a great ride on the train from Paris to Brussels. We sat down in Amsterdam. Promotional tickets open, it seems, 2 months before departure. 2nd class is quite a decent level. Travel time flies by

After many years of travelling with budget airlines and feeling like herded cattle we decided to be one of the first travellers on the new  southern high speed TGV train line. It enables  direct travel from London to Marseilles in the south of France in nearly as quick a time as flying. We thoroughly enjoyed the experience, we booked early treated ourselves to first class on the way down to our destination of Avignon, and returned by standard class to get a feel for our future trips. Both classes were very good but the first takes it for the delicious food and drink served which was included in the ticket price. What a great view of the french countryside at 200mph sipping your wine.Everything was timed to the minute as we rolled into Avignon bang on time. It was a shame that on the return trip we were delayed by three hours due to a train fire but the staff were fantastic re organising peoples onward travel or hotels etc. As compensation all travellers received  free return tickets to be taken within the next year delivered by email within 2 days of our return. First class service unlike some airlines I could mention. And we have booked for 2016.

There were six of us friends leaving for an exhibition in Paris. Ticket purchased in December and all in all not very cheap (€135 return with 1 and a half months of presale is quite high). Train arriving from Venice late but leaving on time. Very old and very dirty train. Inside the cabin there was a bottle of water for each but there were no sheets, pillows and blankets for everyone; reported to the carriage manager but obtained nothing. The comfort is obviously that of an old compartment in which there are 6 berths, so almost zero. I arrive about 30 minutes late in Paris which, considering the length of the journey and the absence of stops (apart from Dijon), is no small thing. On the return, I leave Paris on time; cleaner train overall impression; on the other hand, here too the bed kits were not complete (but this time they completed them immediately); However, two mats were so old that you could feel all the iron bars underneath (a wooden board would have been better). I even arrived early in Milan but in one of the two bathrooms there was no more water to wash. On both trips, despite having turned off the heating in the carriage it was too hot. All in all we left with the idea of ​​a gypsy trip and so it was; we also had fun because we are adaptable but the cattle wagons are probably more comfortable and cleaner. The Thello website is misleading in its advertising and does not correspond to the real state of the Venice-Paris trains

A must do, better than flying or driving!We traveled from Barcelona to Paris and then onto London. We traveled first class which was great. Very comfy.Food and drinks on board were also good considering.

A great train journey is a combination of the scenery outside the train, dramatic mountains, picturesque coastlines and sparkling lakes, experience inside the train, drinking a glass of good wine, bearing in mind one can bring one's own bottle on board, getting to know the locals and the chance to just sit back, relax and catch up on emails.From its first service in 1981 the TGV has set the pace in European high-speed rail operations. These beautiful trains are capable of running at an operational speed of  320 kmph although the experience on board feels anything but frantic in fact it is  smooth and enjoyable. The trip from Tarbes, frequently featuring on the Tour schedule, to Montparnasse bang in the middle of Paris is a truly memorable experience giving glimpses of  classic Gallic  countryside right throughout the journey. Do not forget a corkscrew and if in need of help remember the man in seat 61.
Very fast train. Punctual. Always arrives on time. Nice trains and cover many miles at no time. Some of the trains have Cafe also available.
Quite pleasant trip, in 2nd class, but prices can explode depending on timetables. Still available a cafeteria but lacks wifi.

Travelling in TGV through the country is one of the best travel experiences one can have. It's so convenient, easy to book, so well connected across the nation and then with the entire continent through its partner railways (just like a spider web), that you instantly fall in love with TGV. Moreover you will get so many offers round the year.

The TGV undoubtedly derives its raison d'être from its speed. Strasbourg - Paris in just over 2 hours is almost sensational by European standards. However, you have to accept narrow aisles and, above all, a lousy selection of food. The German ICE is way better. But since the TGV is so fast, this disadvantage is hardly significant...

From Turin to Paris it is quite comfortable. High speed only exists from Lyon to Paris, otherwise it travels normally. On the positive side, punctuality and silence, friendly staff. Sandwiches are quite good but expensive. Otherwise it is quite filthy, dirty carpet, so-so toilets. Quite old-fashioned carriages. No Wi-Fi and not even a snack or newspaper in first class. Our Red Arrows are definitely better.

Still super disappointed with the Monop daily restaurant (yes crime): expensive, mediocre and industrial sold with a lot of marketing: the Boco chefs, one or 2 organic products to enhance the image... Real business restaurants that display Smart meals (not for the customer, nor for the gourmet) Great disappointment for 2 years: the formula no longer includes the starter but remains at the same price, or even more expensive and loses flavor. Worse, that morning, 2 out of 4 items were missing from the breakfast formula (yogurt and orange juice absent). I order, the waiter warns me that nothing can be replaced and when paying asks me the price of the complete package, ha ha ha. And to argue “I can’t do anything about it, it’s the price of the formula”. That's the spirit of SNCF catering, no one can do anything about it!

A great way to get around Europe and France. Trains run from Germany via Belgium to Paris, plus they have a large network of roads throughout France. Fast and convenient. The most important thing is to buy tickets in advance for promotions. Although on some sections of the road the speed is high, this speed is not felt at all. A good dining car with normal prices, not as inflated as in Russia. The case when it is made for people!
We took the TGV from Valenciennes to Paris in first class. The transportation was pleasant and very quiet. The spacious seating areas. Appreciable transport.

One of the trips was from Brussels to Amsterdam. I forgot a backpack inside the carriage. About 10 minutes after disembarking, I returned and the backpack had been broken into (torn), as it had padlocks on it. Two employees were getting out of the carriage when I was returning, I suspect the employees did it themselves. So don't neglect your belongings.
One of the alternative when you want travel around Europe. This train also connected with Paris Charles de Gaulle airport. Always on time & fast so this train efficient way to travel.

I had the misfortune of traveling on the Thello night train on the Milan-Paris route. Advertised as a new TGV, in reality it was a very old coal-fired Euronight with dilapidated, dirty carriages, broken air conditioning (it was June with unbearable heat), bathrooms out of order. Arriving in Milan an hour and a half late without any news or assistance, we found ourselves traveling in disastrous conditions, unable to sleep a wink due to the suffocating heat and the terribly dangerous unprotected cots that they assigned to us. Furthermore, I had booked a 4-berth vagon lit and found myself in an unpresentable 6-berth carriage. Absolutely to be avoided.
Traveling on TGV trains is very good. Punctuality, comfort and ease of going to different places without airport stress. I highly recommend it.

business trip, for a product presentation at the Poitiers theme park. comfortable train, good service both when accessing the train (reservations required) and on board. really quick, trivially in the sense that by car or plane it would have taken us much longer to reach the destination.

that the train is not at the announced departure time no longer shocks anyone but the journey is carried out in a pleasant way that we forget it. Food still questionable (we should sue the distributors of these products or force them to eat them at the price sold) comfortable seat, coffee and mineral water, correct wifi? but electrical outlets, esoteric price lists and timetables (really for those in the know)
Great service that is always on time and will take you all over France, excellent service  that allows you to have a glass of wine while the sights go by at great speed.

very bad experience we traveled from IRUN TO PARIS we had the worst seats at the end of the car there was a table in the middle to be divided between 4 very uncomfortable seats and on the way back it was the same but with the misfortune that the train that was ahead broke down and we arrived 1 hour and a half late we were going at 30 an hour and what I liked least about the PARIS station we went for information and they only knew how to speak French for being an international station others did not know how or did not want to speak languages of shame
Fast and efficient way to travel around France - no frills and a little dated but who cares - quite economical -

When it first debuted, it had a bright orange color and a linear design that was different from Japan's stubby Shinkansen trains, but as you would expect from a French high-speed railway! I used to look at it with envy, but even though the car has been repainted many years since its introduction, I can't help but feel a little tired. The exterior doesn't look clean at all and looks dirty with soot.

Our Last trip to France we traveled from Paris to Reims for the day. We traveled the 144klms via TGV. We travelled off peak for 18 euros each each way, sounds expensive but so what the trip took 45 minutes from go to whoa. We hit 330kms per hour, that is an experience. Here in Australia a similar distance Sydney to Newcastle is like two and a half hours  its a must do trip and an experience.
I traveled on several occasions, none really different from the other... quite a few lines to buy a ticket, as is usual.

Start Hendaye, next stop Saint-Jean-de-Luz, next Biarritz, next Baiona, next Dax, next Bordeaux and this is where you acquire TGV speed to Paris. If it happened in Spain they would have already been eliminated. We do not defend what is ours.

For Americans trains in general and the TGV in particular, are a pleasant upgrade from Amtrak. 300kmh (200mph), departing and leaving from city centers for under €100 is amazing to us. At these speeds we don't need fancy dining or luxury, we'll be there soon enough. That said, I enjoy the comfort of 1st class, but the price value is clearly in coach
I heard that North Station is not very safe. I think it will be easier if you have some level of English ability. The signboard is in French and English.

Turin-Paris TGV journey, convenient to get off in Paris and already be in the centre, the journey was less tiring than other shorter ones made by plane. Sufficiently comfortable and smooth, you can stay seated in the seat almost all the time. Interiors a little outdated, especially first class (in which I traveled), I didn't use the restaurant service because I wasn't attracted to it. Cleanliness to improve.

On the La Rochelle-Paris journey, I tested the new “Boco” meal designed by star chefs.  These are dishes presented in glass jars including a revisited duck confit with mashed beans that is really very good. The strawberry crème brûlée dessert was also very good. A good point for the SNCF!

I decided to use the TGV to go from Milan to Paris. It was a question of convenience given that low-cost travel requires constant ups and downs on public transport as well as a significant time commitment. In any case, I decided on the TGV from Milan Porta Garibaldi to Gare de Lyon. Positive: departure and arrival perfectly on time. Negative: dirty train, broken seats, filthy toilets, expensive and pre-packaged food offered, horrendous. Shady characters who slip between the (first class) seats, sitting down to eat and fleeing as soon as the conductor arrives. I don't understand, I thought the TGV was a luxury train with which to travel in peace, but instead a voice in Turin informs us that it is possible that pickpockets get on the train! but how, and where are the police or controllers? In fact, the journey is less tiring than flying. Choosing a hotel near the station (NOVOTEL which I will review shortly) was excellent. However, it is a shame that the railways do not pay attention to those who favor their vehicles.

Stunningly efficient mode of transport and such an easy way to go from Paris to the south.We bought our tickets on line through Rail Europe - 63 Euros for the two of us.Caught the metro to Gare du Lyon.  It is a large station and you have to find the hall your train departs from.  There is a large board you have to stand and watch until they put your platform number up and then there is a stampede to the platform.The train left on time 10.37 and arrived on time 13.21 in Avignon.  No stops, no hassles - just a very quiet trip with plenty to watch out the window.There wasn't even a conductor coming through to look at our tickets.
The cleaning level is not good lol Well, of course it's probably fast. I took a first class train from Paris to Lyon, but it was nothing compared to the green car.

To cross France it's the quickest solution... provided you don't trust the SNCF site which always wants you to go through Paris with a change of station. Whereas, even on a non-direct journey, you can change trains elsewhere without having to change stations. Obviously Massy is not a place to visit, but it's better to have a quiet coffee in a not-so-great bar, rather than rushing in the metro with your suitcase from one station to another.

I travel every years on first class TGV'S when visiting my Family in France from Australia.Cannot compare trains in Australia that are very bearely existent slow and old with TGV'S but what I can do is to compare TGV'S SNCF with Trenitalia Frecciarossa offering Coach 1: Executive (dominant colour - brown)Coach 2 Business (dominant colour - blue)Coach 3: Business + BistroCoach 4: Premiumand SNCF has only economy and first class no restaurant just a snack bar carriage..with very mediocre food... best not eating. Well what a different in service. SNC TGV"S do desperately in need of total change of standardVery well TGV"S are extremely fast but that is all they have to offer even the equivalent trains in Spain and luxurious to full meal service in first with wine included in your tickets.I travel executive and that was stunning on Trenitalia So SNCF time to review your services.

As an American one is used to slow, noisy, not on time, uncomfortable trains.  The TGV is is fast, quiet, on time and very comfortable.  The prices are good.  This is a civilized way to travel around France.

So the TGV, like its German counterpart ICE, is a high-speed train. I'm not a train enthusiast and couldn't get anything special out of it. It's comfortable and clean, but I think that's what the ICE is too

Have you ever driven over 300 km/h? it's very exhilarating, and at the same time, you don't feel like you're going at that speed. 7Making a journey, such as Tours-Paris, or Tours-Roissy at this speed, means shortening time in an accelerated manner. In fact, it takes about 1 hour to cover the 240km that separate Tours from Paris. Just enough to rest a little! We don't have time to take out our snack and start devouring it, when we're already told we're approaching Montparnasse station. Enough to drastically reduce distances...and the country! The TGV is a beautiful technological gem, capable of transporting you...time to talk about your transport!
Stuttgart - Paris in less than four hours. It couldn't be quicker or more convenient. However, the included snack is inedible

We traveled from Dijon to Paris on the TGV train.  Very comfortable trip with nice seats.  Very modern and clean.  I think the speed was around 200 miles per hour or the equivalent of 320 kilometers per hour.  The fastest I ever moved.  Very quiet ride.  You can see the scenery going by but there's no sense of going fast.  You cannot feel the speed.  It's amazing because we knew we were traveling very fast.  The scenery all along was spectacular.  It was a sunny day with blue skies, white clouds, and greenery all over.
A very convenient and fast way to get from the very center of Paris to Brussels. If you buy a ticket in advance, you can significantly save on the ticket price.

Forget the ease of D-Bahn and SNCB ticketing because in France they work in a different way. In many cases tickets bought and reserved online, will have to be printed out at the station. The instructions are likely to be in French and in the bustle and noise its not a nice way to begin your journey.  You may consider that the new Voyager programme, which they say is open to all, will circumvent this hassle, but upon filling in the online application form you discover that it will not accept non French mobile numbers. And so it goes on....

I used the 1st class toilet yesterday, 16.12.2015, I was in the 2nd class saloon. Big surprise, I sat down after wiping and putting paper all around. (I'm a man) and the toilet is too low, and the bowl is not round enough so, my private part was touching the inside of the bowl. (yet while resting). I had to clean myself with their blue product, taking the time to redo the toilet at home. The 2nd class toilets are higher up, so it works. I'm surprised that people in 1st class don't complain. The small tables are dirty, never cleaned with water, just a wipe. Time is running out. this is the observation that I made, the time to cover the 400 m which separates the TGV queue and the center of the Montparnasse station. The hygiene is deplorable. PS: the same day a first customer before the departure of the TGV presents himself to the conductor, he would like to take this train because his train leaves in 1 hour, is it early. Ok says the conductor, you will have to pay 20 euros extra, but you would travel standing up for more than place. Who is the crook in this affair? Even honest people are fed up.

What can I say, NEVER AGAIN NEVER AGAIN I'm currently returning from Gare de Lyon.... I travel both there and back in a 3-seater bunk. Tropical temperatures even after telling the train manager about the problem we had on the way out. Miseries. I confirm the bagged and stained cushions and the non-cleaning of the compartments... how disgusting.

We travelled from Barcelona to Paris and a few days later returned.  Everything from boarding at each of the stations to the ride in the huge comfortable seats was wonderful.  One thing that struck us was how quiet the train and the travelers were.  Very enjoyable!

For a Canadian, who took the train in Canada (slow) the first time I took the tgv, my surprise was the fluidity and smoothness, I had left Paris for Chamonix, the prices on board for food are extremely expensive......
efficient for long distance travel, clean, fast, secure...I took the TGV to go from Paris to Toulouse, it was the first time I took a TGV in my life, the speed is remarkable.

(-_-;) I didn't enjoy the "train journey"... Thalys was no good... Even if it can't be helped that the cars are old, what do you think about the lack of cleanliness of the seats? ( ? _ ? ) How about French National Railways go to Italy for an inspection tour... Don't call it a "Shinkansen" anymore, I think a "regular local express" is fine.

If you are on vacation, book and get your tickets on line. The site is very good and works smoothly. The benefit is that SNCF uses a dynamic pricing model and the same route can cost much less depending on the time of day. We went Paris to Reims, 144 km (90 mi) in about 45 mins in total comfort. The speed is posted on the screen ..the fastest I saw was 325 kph ... pretty neat! Quiet absolute comfort and tranquility.Going back to CDG we took a local train to the town of Champagne Ardenes. The station, although quite large was some what isolated in the fields, so I guess it was mainly a transfer station.So while sitting in the grey of dawn we saw a light approaching on the middle track. With in 10 seconds that train was thundering by at 325 KPH! The it was gone ...Our train arrived a few minutes later and we were advised to stand back from the platform ... I wonder why?The train was smooth, fast and comfortable. I was in the bar getting coffee when when we passed another coming the other way. The shock wave was so strong it nearly blew the coffee from my hand. These trains are long but they pass in about 2 seconds.Going somewhere in France? Give yourself a thrill ... take the TGV. It is probably faster than flying and a lot more fun.

The itinerary for the trip to France is to pull a train from Lyon to Paris. I think the Bullet Train (T.G.V.) is comparable to the high-speed train in Taiwan, but the train body is an upper and lower double-decker carriage. The interior of the carriage is clean, comfortable, cool and has no odor. I also feel its stability and safety while driving at high speed. I have complete trust in it~ After stopping at two stops, we entered the suburbs. Galloping at high speed in the district...I finally realized his powerful explosive power! What's even more charming is the natural scenery along the way. It couldn't be more beautiful. On the open grassland, there are dots of cows, horses, and hay like cake rolls... coupled with listening to local radio music, wow~ It's really a top-notch sensory feast~ A great experience~

The Thello train from Milan to Paris looks much closer to a Milan-Villa San Giovanni carriage from the 1970s rather than a Frecciarossa. The cleanliness is miserable, the maintenance is approximate: missing lights, heating not working (at night, in December, in the middle of the mountains), cut seals. The sheets are made of disposable paper, while the blankets, presented in plastic bags that would mean they have been cleaned, have stains that are best not investigated. Anyway, with the cold weather, you have to use them anyway. There is no cleaning of the bathrooms during the journey, so upon arrival they are almost unusable. On the return the carriage is new, the blankets almost clean, on the other hand the paper pillowcases for the pillows are missing. The train leaves more than 2 hours late, after having been stopped at the station for more than 1 hour without information and with the toilets locked (the children are grateful). Cleaning, maintenance and service to be reviewed. The advantage, delays permitting, is the timetable: you travel at night and compared to the plane you save two days which can be dedicated to visiting Paris.

Took TGV from CDG to Lyon. Took 1 hour from landing to collect baggage. 15 minute rail shuttle from Term 1 to Term 2 where the rail hub is located. The rail hub was a chaotic mess. Be aware that there are North and South gates with identical numbers. Be aware that not all itermediate stops are shown on the teain board. The platform is very cramped and chaotic. The train cars are just ok. For first class and first class prices,  I expected more. The entire journey was on tracks laid in a railcut, so if you are one the car lower level, you have no scenic view, just the side of a ditch.Cars were clean and in relatively good shape. The train left on time and arrived on time.

We drove from Gruissan to Paris, about 4 hours. I must say that they were practically not felt. There is quite a lot of space for accommodation, it is very comfortable, your back does not hurt, and you can even take a nap (those who never sleep on trains will understand me).

As the title suggests, it won't be the Orient Express, but for what it costs it's more than good as a train and as a journey. If you don't want to make a quick trip between Venice and Paris then it's the best solution. I used this train last week and I traveled comfortably and peacefully. On the outward journey (Vicenza-Paris route) only 40 minutes of delay caused by border controls between France and Switzerland; it must be said that the train arrived in Vicenza 50 minutes late due to problems in preparing for the train, but in Domodossola it had already recovered everything. On the return instead I leave with +10 but arrived in Vicenza 1 minute early. The carriages may also be UIC-X cucdettes from the 70s/80s, but they are not that bad. Too bad the bathrooms were not cleaned during the journey. However, to go to Paris directly in the center this is the solution better.
Having rarely had the opportunity to travel by train, a business trip to Paris is always an opportunity to look forward to taking the TGV. What a pleasure to only take 1h30 to reach the capital.

It may have been the flagship of the French railways until some time ago, but today it absolutely does not reflect the service expected from a high-speed train, both in terms of cleanliness and the quality of the food.
I rode the TGV several times, but I believe it was better in its early days. I once took it from Lyon to Paris CDG and it was like riding a comfortable bullet.

TGV is a French high-speed train. Even though it runs very fast, there is no body discomfort or jerking due to acceleration. It's great because you can get to even the farthest countryside quickly from Paris. Prices are also very cheap in the off season. Also, it is not very expensive even during the peak season, so it would be a good experience to try it at least once.

Booked cheap tix from Paris to Bordeaux for just $20 each online. This may be stated elsewhere, but I want to mention that at Gare Montparnasse the Gate for embarkation does not show until 20 minutes prior to departure. It is on a large board above your head in the center of the station.

Took the trip from Paris to Lille and found it very good for what it is; a very fast train, more comfortable than modern air transport, and economical.I fully recommend this if you don't mind taking a little longer to get to where you're going.You don't even mind if the person in front reclines.

The train never ever made it to the destination. It doesn't get much worse than that. Well actually it does. The train only got as far as Perpignan. It was meant to go from Paris to Barcelona. When the train stopped at Perpignan, an announcement was made in French and Spanish, that due to technical problems, the train was not going any further and we would need to catch a bus the rest of the way. The train crew all got off the train and disappeared. Unfortunately they had not told any of the non French or Spanish travellers what was going on. Various English, Japanese and Mandarin speaking travellers sat happily looking out the window while the rest of the train where loaded onto buses. I nice Indian man pointed out to me what was about to happen. I went around the train and told the others. The staff had all disappeared. We all made it to the bus just in time. The bus was not what I would call "flash". The bus susquently got lost in Barcelona. This resulted in lots of people giving the driver advice in different languages.  The bus stopped at two points along the way, where the driver attempted to drive off with passengers not on the bus, as they had gone to the toilet. The TGV is a relatively expensive way to travel, and for this level of "dodginess"it was really quite poor.

Train frequented by 90% of immigrants and illegal immigrants, insecurity and anarchy reigns. Old 1960s train, dirty, bad smells, toilet always closed, very uncomfortable bunks. If you want to experience the illegal immigrants' route, take it.

What was meant to be an enjoyable and relaxing journey in a 1st Class TGV Lyria,Turned out to be the worst journey I ever had.Especially that I paid for 1st Class and did not receive the service.I asked for compensation due to the fact that we had to travel by bus instead until just over the border of France.What was disappointing that the SNCF did not give us a reason. And when we boarded the train in France,no one checked our tickets and we did not stop at the connecting station.When I approached a conductor, he said we are now going direct express to Paris.Due to the delay because we travelled by bus, we missed the connection that would of went to Belfort.I demanded the conductor needed to stop the next station that had a connection to Belfort. About 10 people even had to go by van taxi to another station whereby there was a connection.Even at that station they gave us the wrong tickets to go on the wrong carriage.Luckily we knew the direction between one destination and the other.After I completed a form for compensation,for paying extra - 1st Class and not receiving the service, SNCF replied by saying that they are not liable.I am convinced that they have robbed us.And advise others not to travel with this company as apparently this happens often.

Our TGV departed from Gare de Lyon on time. We travelled as part of a group in 2nd Class which for us was something we had not done for some time. We were pleasantly surprised at the comfort of the seats and the smooth journey. It was wonderful seeing how the countryside changed from city to arable to dairy and forests. Food and drink is available on the journey.

This train TGV or AGV is an extremely convenient way to travel between cities in France and whole of Europe. These trains have beautiful interior ambience, comfort, food and drinks on board. The speed of travel could be 300 KMPH. Very punctual and good frequency to travel if you are looking for an economic way to travel in Europe. First class and second class, two categories are options to choose from comfort levels.

We returned from Paris to Frankfurt aboard TGV.  First Class was worth the few extra dollars if you can do it.  We were not expecting the meal and drinks so we were quite pleased to chow down on something other than chips.  And soda.  How often are you served wine on a train in the US?  Amazing the speed!!

So we had booked our tickets in advance and we got for a rather price, tickets from Strasbourg to Paris. The journey was uneventful - however the space to keep bags is a little restricted. Most people were single business bags - larger luggage can be kept in the stowaway at the entrance of the coach. Food is slightly more expensive than maybe some of the other trains.The route was beautiful and it is a pleasure seeing the quaint little towns speed past on the Paris.

We caught the train from Dijon to Paris, after our overnight train from Venice was cancelled at Dijon.Since we bought tickets on the train itself, we paid quite a bit (probably twice as much as if we had pre-booked).  We ended up spending the whole trip in the dining car, but the seats there weren't bad.The staff were relatively friendly and helpful.  Seems like a reasonable way to get around France.

Normally the easy way to get to Strasbourg. Direct (or 1 stop, 2h19m). Beware of the cheap tickets which have more than one stop and can extend the journey to 3h. Comofrtable. Go online. The 'prems' (first tarifs) in 1st can often be cheaper than a full price 2nd class. TGV is a great way to travel.
here's the big surprise, late, average services for average service, the big quality is the speed of travel, that's all.

A great way to zip around Europe. We took the morning train from Paris to Barcelona. The TGV is quick and efficient, and could catch up to the world and install WiFi. They don't serve food like other trains but did have a basic bar food car that ensures you wont shrivel up from starvation (takes 6 hours to do this trip). The train was clean and the seats were comfortable, but gets boring with no internet. I guess I am spoiled?Next time I'd get seats with a table and on the top level to better see the country side.

From Rotterdam to Paris in about two hours. Very good. And free Wifi. If it works,.which seems to be a problem quite often.Otherwise a very comfortable way to travel to Paris. I have no actual experience but travelling onwards looks like a bit of a issue, since you have to change stations when you want to go further down south, meaning Metro or other means of transport in between, No fun when you are having additional luggage.But I like the TGV, beats planes depending on where you go,

One of my favourite parts of traveling with the TGV is that you don't have all the fuss of the airport. No checks, no lines, no security (good thing??) and you can arrive 5 min before departure. On the negative side there is no internet on the train and cell phone reception is very 3 world quality. This they could easily improve. Ill be back though, just gonna bring more books.
Compared to Shinkansen which is a lot better than tgv. The trains are newer, faster and quieter. Also the seat are wider and more comfortable.

We took the TGV from Paris to Annecy in 1st class for 3,5 hours. Booking was done over the web a month in advance. Everything went so smooth, directions at the station were more than clear. Quite an experience. Will take the TGV again with pleasure.

We took the TGV (tres grand vitesse  - very fast) train from Paris to Lyon. The trip was two hours travelling at over 200 mph. Beautiful views of the country whizzing past and very comfortable. It was easy to board, easy to get tickets, and easy to pass through the the stations. This the way to travel in Europe!
We use it to go from Luxembourg to Paris. It has super comfortable seats. It goes really, really fast. They claim it reaches 560 km/hour, but I don't know if it reached that speed on our trip.
