We really enjoyed our TGV train ride to Arras to see Vimy Ridge. It was a nice change to see some countryside and farmland, after spending days in downtown Paris. We had no trouble locating our train (they post the platform numbers on the overhead monitors 15 minutes before departure), and the conductors were very helpful as well. After the train was underway, the conductors came around to scan our tickets. We bought first-class seats because we booked so early (about three months ahead), that the first-class tickets were the same price as the second-class tickets. I am not sure there is any difference in quality between first-class and second-class cars, but we did notice that it was very quiet in our cars as we had mainly business people around us.There is a choice of seats: pairs facing forward, pairs facing backward, pairs facing each other across a table, and the same choices for single seats (forward, backward, or facing one another across a table). We had heard that the website's seat plans were incorrect, but we had no trouble selecting the seats that we wanted. The only thing that you can't tell from the diagram is whether you have a full window to look out of, or a partial window. We were in seats 15 & 16 in car 12 going there, and in seats 15 & 16 in car 2 coming back, and we had a partial window both ways.  Not that it really mattered, as we enjoyed ourselves anyway.The seats are roomy and comfortable, with a hook on the wall to hang your coat, a sturdy metal fold-up tray available to you, swing-down footrests, and overhead racks to store your luggage and personal items. Tip: If booking tickets online, use the Capitaine Train website, not the SNCF website, which kept redirecting us and was very confusing. We had absolutely no trouble booking through Capitaine Train.  Also, order months in advance, as soon as the tickets go on sale, to get the best price.

This is a very fast and efficient service.  The train staff were very pleasant and attentive and we noticed that our toilet was cleaned at least 3 times during the trip.  The day we left Paris it was 4 degrees and we passed through lovely scenery including a lot of snow covered land.  The journey ended with spectacular views of the Mediterranean Sea and sunshine scenery in Nice.  The journey from Paris to Nice was almost 6 hours but as we had quite a lot of heavy luggage and as there are stairs leading to upper and lower decks on the trains we found it very difficult to handle the cases.  Normally there are platform attendants to direct passengers at each carriage.  On this occasion there was not one attendant present and we got on the wrong carriage which caused further stress when we were asked to move.  Also when we arrived at Nice Ville station there are a lot of stairs to negotiate to exit - no lifts and again we found it quite stressful.  However if you are travelling with just light luggage it wouldn't be a problem.  Also the food on the train is not the best and very expensive so it is wise to buy food at the station before boarding.  One thing about French trains is that they do not announce the platform number until 20 minutes before departure time.  This involves several hundred people milling around the announcement board waiting for the  number to appear and when it does several hundred people then rush to the platform and board the train.  It is bedlam as the train will leave absolutely on time whether everyone is on board or not.  However I would definitely recommend it as a fast, efficient and much cheaper alternative to air travel if you get in early to purchase your ticket.  Note, all announcements are in French.

We used it to go to Paris from Turin, the first Turin-Lyon route is not covered at high speed, so it takes almost 4 hours, but unlike the car you can work and rest, while the Lyon-Paris route (520 km) approximately takes just 2 hours. The only flaw... The cleanliness of the seats..... A little maintenance wouldn't hurt
Traveling between London and Paris was fast, smooth and quiet. If we went by jet, wee would have to be at the airport 3 hours early and wish I took the TGV. So easy and comfortable.
Railway Station Luxembourg (1907-1913), since 2007 main station of the fast Train TGV-Est,Central Railway station, with his high clock tower are in Moselle Barock.From Luxemborg to Paris in 1h 45.

TGV Milan-Paris... the first class of the train absolutely does not reflect its standard, really dirty rooms and seats, non-working electrical sockets, no control over passengers who spend the entire journey on the phone in a loud voice or disturbing in other ways, nor over unsavory people who get on without tickets at the stations to harass passengers. The food prices on board are absurd: €8.50 for a fixed breakfast (hot drink, croissant, sandwich with butter and jam, and juice) €3.80 for a coke, €6.00 for a sandwich, €7.00 for toast, €2.40 for 35g of chips... we didn't dare ask for lunch... the on-board staff who served the 1st class seat were in some cases very kind and in others very rude and unsympathetic. The journey itself is "comfortable" until the French railway begins, that is, the last 4.30 hours, where the train begins to zigzag without stopping, due to air disturbance, making it really difficult even to rest, let alone read... I also don't understand how they can call it high speed given that it makes so many stops, even close together, and the travel speed is regional... it covers a distance in 7h22 that a real high speed travels in 5h/5h.30... It will also go from the center of Milan to that of Paris but the service offered is truly disappointing. Terrible value for money.

I took the train from Paris to Marseille, and the train at the station was so dirty that my first impression, perhaps because I'm used to seeing the Shinkansen's shiny appearance, was, "Is this the Shinkansen's rival, the TGV?" I rode in both first class and second class, and I think second class is enough, but first class is more empty, so I thought there was a difference in fare. . Personally, I prefer German ICE.

Accustomed to traveling by plane, the simplicity and lack of obstacles is surprising (on the outward journey they didn't even ask us for tickets). The punctuality also caught our attention. As a negative aspect, the lack of cleanliness and the bad smell of the toilets.
I loved riding the TGV. It goes so fast and it is a relaxing ride. You barely feel that you're going fast.

Having travelled many times on the TGV we are now convinced that where such travel is available we will never fly again.  From Paris to the South of France and to Zurich,both trips being around 4 hours city centre to city centre. When you look at all the hassles of getting to airports and then from them to a city centre there is just no comparison.   We used the Euro Star from London to Paris 2 hours. We compared this to flying where you write off almost a whole day not to mention the wear and tear on your body and there is no going back.  Not only time but comfort and the pleasure of seeing the passing scenery is amazing.

On a recent trip to France, took the TGV from Gare Montparnasse to Bordeaux.  What a rush! Comfy accommodations in first class. compartments for 4 with tables and plugs for electronics.  Dining, Bar car but we shopped in Paris and brought a picnic of wine, baguette, cheeses and charcuterie.  Very smooth ride and no real sense of the immense speed until you look out the windows!

I rode from Brussels to Lyon and from Lyon to Paris. I rode in both 1st class and 2nd class, but I recommend the single seat in 1st class. A two-story vehicle is even more recommended. Both 1st and 2nd class cars had power outlets at their seats, but they could only be used in 1st class.
these high-speed trains can take you to every corner of France and Europe. Very convenient and fast. However, this is not a cheap pleasure, especially considering the current ruble exchange rate.

In early September, I used the routes between Paris and Aix-en-Provence and between Paris and Rennes. As a Japanese person, I can't help but compare it to the Shinkansen, but the differences are that second-class cars feel smaller than the Shinkansen (especially double-decker cars), and the seats don't rotate. The speed and quietness are on par with the Shinkansen. As for the regular schedule, I get the impression that I am usually about 5 to 10 minutes late. However, compared to when I used the TGV a long time ago, it has become much easier to use. Another attractive feature is that it is now possible to purchase tickets directly in Japan over the Internet, even for dates far in the future.

There's no better way to capture the natural landscape of Italy and France than the TGV. Although train tickets get a bit pricey during the summer, it's more or less the same with any air ticket. (Milan to Paris) It wasn't very fast than I thought. Having booked through voyages-SNCF.com in advance, I boarded the train in 1st Class front-facing single-seat comfort. I never slept the whole time I was travelling. I must have taken lots of photos and videos.Have your ticket and passport ready whenever checkings are conducted.A crew comes to you for your meals. You can also check some items at a bar (near the 1st Class section) and meet some people.

I have taken the TGV Barcelona Paris many times in both directions since it was inaugurated. Every time I think about the magnificent service of the birds from Barcelona to Madrid, with friendly guys and girls who serve you breakfast, snacks, meals and drinks with a smile. In general, the French railway system, which was exemplary in every way, has degenerated over the years. Access to the train in French territory is every man for himself. Since there is no control, thieves get on and take suitcases from the platforms. They give absolutely nothing to drink or eat in first class. There is a pitiful bar and a pitiful cart that circulates tirelessly on the upper floor. French prices and Spanish employees in the cafeteria, generally friendly, except for one unspeakable edge. Throughout the south of France the roads are conventional and old, which causes slow movement, incidents and delays very often. No one helps carry the suitcases to the upper floor. Many elderly people have to ask for help halfway up the stairs. The 6 and a half hours of the trip seem eternal. Despite everything, I like trains so much that I take them whenever I can.

Travelling from Paris to Quimper for 6 hours I thought was going to be difficult, but it was quite the opposite when i used the TGV from Gare Montparnasse to Quimper. I booked my tickets online and with their deals all the time I was lucky to get first class seats for a very good price. The seats were comfortable with their own foldable tray. Washrooms were clean and the cafe had an ok selection. Prices are not cheap so it is always good to bring your own meal if you are budget conscious.
So we love the TGV. We rarely had any problems (delays or otherwise). We take the family square and it's very nice for traveling. We always make the same Valencia-Paris route.

The intercity train service in France is great... you can get from anywhere to anywhere but you need the help of someone with experience as there is no one on the train or at the stations to assist you... you can  easily get on the wrong train... the trains though are comfortable and very fast... power to charge your mobile devices but free wifi like the ferry and English trains would have been great

The train is comfortable in first class BUT the journey took over 7 hours   Food is quite expensive but to be expected and there is no wifi on the train, not even in first class   From other reviews our delay of 2 hours (40 mins at one station) is a common issue.  Could have got here in just over 3 hours door to door if we flew and the cost was likely the same.   There are a few nice views from the window but for the sake of 3 to 5 hours I would fly next time.   This seems to be a TGV issue as train from Amsterdam to Paris was terrific

The TGV Bullet train from Paris to Lourdes(Southern tip of France) sped at 300 km/hr and was so comfortable...However. ...we wish all the announcements on board were bilingual and not only in French...Air conditioning can sometimes be in adequate. ..

Ride from Lyon to Charles de Gaulle Airport! Arrived in two hours! It's convenient. The automatic ticket machine is a little difficult to understand, so we recommend purchasing e-tickets from a computer. The luggage storage space is small and it was full when we arrived at Lyon Station! I ended up leaving it in the aisle. Please be careful as there seem to be a lot of pickpockets.

Well, for a start, today 30 Sep 2015, while waiting for the 9:50 train from Avignon to Paris, about 20 minutes before the scheduled departure the screens said it was running 10 minutes late. That got to 30 minutes late before we departed and then to cut a long story short, it finally arrived at the CDG Airport station Paris 3 hours and 5 minutes late, heaven help those folk who had an airport connection. The only announcement on the train  in English about the expected arrival time was made around 3pm, I.e. 2 hours after the scheduled arrival time. I know that there was some sort of accident, but the French TGV communication to passengers was pathetic.We travelled first class, toilets disgusting, carriages old and scruffy, with dirty carpets and scuffed ceilings.Will try to avoid TGV in future. In my experience, the TGV is 10 years behind the Deutsche ICE train service.

Avoid booking through Rail  Europe. Try to book through idtvg website (using 060000000 phone number instead of a U.S. Line). Otherwise book through sncf English site using UK as home country. If you book through the sncf or rail Europe sites :Don't prepay for meals. No need to. Don't pay for premium class at Cdg in order to have a lounge. It is far away in the airport, not near the trains If you book through idtvg, it is the same train but there are discounted seats. Everything is done online. Rail Europe is a more expensive option for USA with awful long waits for any refunds or customer service

This train ride is to me the best I've ever done. There's a unique feeling to wake up in London, board the train and then be in Paris in time to have Breakfast. It's fast and impressive when you think about logistics.. Not to mention how much better it is to choose the train before air transportation in terms of sustainable travels. A must on the bucket list !

I was very happy to have chosen this means of transport, comfortable, fast, friendly staff. I left from the center of Milan and arrived right on time in the center of Paris, no changes, no waiting time, of course the train is a little dated and not perfectly clean (or perhaps I was expecting a train like our Freccia or Italo). What I definitely didn't like was having booked the trip in the direction of travel and finding myself in exactly the opposite direction!! The very kind train conductor did his best to find a replacement seat, but there was still inconvenience.

this fast train is spectacular --punctual , clean , well maintained & nothing to fault --also great to arrive in the centre of Paris & leave from the centre of Lyon hence avoiding all the hassle & time delays of airports ---no graffiti like our own Australian trains always seem to have.Unfortunately next journey from Paris to Amsterdam was a disgrace. Toilets filthy in first class , taps not working , staff disinterested , very old trains. Complained to staff who acknowledged there was a problem -same owner apparently (sncf) & have advised management often with no results.

The TGV Barcelona Paris thing has been a terrible disappointment to me with all the talk about the Ave train direct from Barcelona to Paris. It seemed that with this air travel was going to end. Well, nothing could be further from the truth! For now, the train does not have (even remotely) the comfort of the AVE in Spain. The problems begin as soon as you start (that is, before climbing) because there is not a single operator to, at least, tell you where you have to go. If we add to that the fact that the train has two floors and that you have to carry your suitcases by hand, you can imagine that at that moment I remembered the gym I was skipping. But the absence of personnel is missing even throughout the trip. Don't let anything happen to you because no one shows up for hours! I'm not going to be the one to point out the security flaws here because it's even scary. If we add to that the fact that cleaning and maintenance is poor with broken trash cans and bad smells and armchairs of different colors (in first class!) I'm not saying anything about the cafeteria service where you can only take 4 things (literally) for a trip that lasts half a day. Because, here comes the good thing, the train is not an AVE "always". That is, from Valence until almost reaching the Spanish border it goes on conventional roads and, sometimes, slower than a powerful car. The hours, you can imagine, become unbearable turning around the tablet without even a bad movie to put into your mouth (and I don't like TV). Furthermore, to top it all off, it is very expensive for what you get and, when you arrive in Paris, it seems like you haven't arrived at the station. They leave you on a platform. All of that was at night, raining heavily, with two suitcases and alone with a 6-year-old girl. I'm going back to the plane!

I recently traveled to the upper level of a TGV. Fortunately, Rennes was the terminus. But during rush periods, particularly July-August, with full wagons, there is a risk of getting stuck in the narrow staircase (with around 3 minutes to leave the train before it leaves...) In addition, in these new trains, the seat signage is almost illegible (tiny numbers). I noticed that on the upper floor, it is impossible to drag a suitcase up high (the space only allows for a few things). This could be a problem during peak periods in summer. The planned locations will probably not be sufficient. In short, I prefer the current trains but it seems that these "dupleix" trains will be more and more numerous. note that they are also much shorter (8 cars instead of 20).

Dated but clean train......right on time, fast on the Lyon-Paris section...a little slower on the Alpine section...friendly staff, police control both in Italy and France...which doesn't hurt and reassures......given the times......positive experience to be repeated for sure.....if you book in advance you will save money.

I used it to go from Montparnasse station to La Rochelle station. I loved trains when I was a kid, so I got excited when I heard about the TGV, but now that I'm used to riding the Shinkansen, I'm a little disappointed that I can only think of it as a ``fast and convenient vehicle.'' The TGV is fast on dedicated lines, but when you go to rural areas, you have to use conventional lines, so it may not be that fast.

I am writing this review on board one of these trains from the fast Paris-Milan route. I am stunned by the ignorant arrogance of certain people who review Thello as TGV. The first is a train operated by the Italian state railways, the second by the French ones. Let's continue to confuse ma... with chocolate. Having said that, the train was very punctual both on the outward and return journey. Restaurant service on board, very courteous staff. I would also like to point out that I was traveling with a Labrador. At the time of online/telephone booking, the staff told me that I could easily purchase the ticket for my dog ​​on board the train (the SNCF ticket office is closed at six in the morning) without a surcharge. And so it was!!!!

Have had the opportunity to use TGV many times and every time they were on time, clean, and very helpful. Whether traveling alone travel with family Travel across England If you don't make it in time, there is an employee who can give you advice and find a new seat for the next round. It is truly a very worthwhile way to travel.
TGV IS THE BEST SERVICE I HAVE BEEN TO IN A TRAIN.Its quick on time and bang on services in train related to comfort and food

The worst method of transport on earth, other than Ryanair. You board the LATE train to find there is NO ROOM FOR YOUR LUGGAGE. Then each seat has two numbers which causes chaos. Then you find your seat and there is a family of grumpy french people squatting in your seats. After finally getting them out, you sit on a rattly train that gets you to your destination late causing stress, pressure and lots more chaos as you nearly miss your Eurostar connection. Somebody French needs to go on holiday to China and find out how to run a high speed train network - this experience was terrible!

Traveled on Thello trains on 9 June 2015 on the Milan-Paris route, and on 14 June 2015 on the Paris-Milan route. The first journey in a sleeper carriage was acceptable, the return in a sleeper carriage was shameful... especially due to the conditions of the bathrooms, dirty and smelly. If you consider the price of these trips, whoever manages this route deserves a complaint. A real shame, because the train always remains an excellent alternative to the plane, a different way of traveling and those who choose it deserve more respect.

My mother & I got the chance to travel with TGV in 1st class TGV's train on September 2015 from:1) Brussel Midi - Paris Nord = meals and drinks are provided. Unfortunately the AC broken down within 30 minutes of our trip. They had to stop in the border of Paris and Brussel to fix it for 1 hour but didn't work. So we had to continue our 1 hour trip in sweat. But the TGV staff was great, they apologize through the speaker and in person too. Because of the delay, TGV provided free water bottle and biscuits at Paris Nord. 2) Paris Nord - Rotterdam = snacks and drinks are provided repeatedly. Although we were expecting a full meal like our first trip.

Here I am reviewing it after a month and I'm still shocked!! My departure (Paris-Milan) was scheduled for 8.00 pm. Well you know, after 5, 10, 20 minutes of spending there wondering why we aren't leaving you go and inform yourself, I asked a gentleman for explanations who told me that the train had a problem with the locomotive (It's nice that I had to ask a gentleman why no one warned us) and nothing we had decided to wait also because what to do otherwise. At 9.00 pm more or less, we we were asked to get off the train but to leave our luggage on it because the locomotive had to be replaced in Bercy station and then the train leaves and we are there. After a wait of more or less 3 and a half hours in which everything happened, in particular I remember the arguments between the passengers and the conductors, in which a female conductor claimed not to let the train start and insulted the passengers (I'm not joking, I understand the pressure but don't insult the passengers) making even the children cry. The train however arrived at 00.30 and left around 1. Thus causing all the people who had it (including me) to miss their connections. We thought we would now be safe...but no!! The air conditioning wasn't working in our cabin, I woke up in the middle of the night (3.00 am) because I wasn't breathing, you see... I had to go into the corridor and didn't find a conductor until 5 in the morning, then the brilliant solution was to open the window... I fell back asleep but every time a train passed I got sick. Really the last time.. speechless.
fast and clean and efficient, would ride anytime, it is often better that flying, faster and cheaper
Took to Avignon. Smooth ride. Clean. Quiet. Easiest way to get from Paris to other locations. It's so easy, we've heard that people travel from Paris to Lyon just for dinner.

I paid for 2 tickets at Thello, one from Savona to Milan and the other from Milan to Paris. due to a shameful delay of the train from Savona to Milan, I missed the connection from Milan to Paris. I therefore had to stay overnight in Milan (at the expense of the state railways) and pay for another train to Paris the following morning. since July I've been trying in vain to get a refund (or at least an answer with an apology!!), but it's not possible to reach "thello" in any way!! by email: no response for 2 months. via registered mail: no response! via express courier of the Italian post office: address non-existent!!! a shame, a real scam!! and the deadline for complaints expires in 2 days! luckily I have receipts for all the registered letters and couriers sent, but who might be interested? NEVER THELLO AGAIN!!!

We paid $185 each to travel from nice to Paris, first class . as foreigners you get overcharged. Turns out no one ever checks your  ticket, so all the seats around us and the restaurant on board was filled with free loaders. This is not a fair system. Next time I will fly. Note; you can literally hop on and ride this train in 1 at class for free!

We took the 2nd class car from Paris CDG to Lyon and it was a terrible trip. There was baggage everywhere, in the aisles on our laps under the tables, and on the shelves. The train was supposed to take a bit over 2 hours to Lyone and it took over 3.5 hours. We ended up in Perrache station instead of Part Dieu. Pretty miserable all the way. Going back to Paris, it was much better with bags only in the baggage areas and on time. So if you want to travel from CDG, consider 1st class or be prepared for living amongst piles of baggage.

TGV. Fast and punctual. The service on board was good. We used it From Paris to Turin, booking it three months in advance and the price was incredibly low, €29. The problem comes when we talk about the carriages, old and poorly maintained with parts that were falling off. Overall, however, I am satisfied

First Class tickets got us a ride from CDG to Bordeaux in a coach that was filthy inside and out with worn floors uncomfortable seats. The stench from the toilet was as bad as we ever smelt even worse than overcrowded trains in Asia. Food selection poor. Would not do it again
This is a great way to travel which I did from Paris to Provence and back. The speed  was fantastic and iy certainly arrived on time. A great way to travel.
The high-speed train to Marseille-Paris is comfortable, but it always has difficulty keeping to its schedule....
It's worth it... For me it was a mystery to take this trip across the English Channel, I always dreamed of it, I sat in the armchair and drank in every second of this trip,,,Wonderful!

Terrific way of going between Paris and Lyon.  Faster than flying when one takes into consideration the traffic to and from both airports.  Downside:  It is almost impossible to walk around the train while holding a cup of coffee or a glass of water.  The motion is far too pronounced.
This is the fast train that gets you to and from Paris. It is maintained at average levels and is on time mostly

We were honestly very worried after reading the many negative opinions about the Thello and instead we were lucky. The bunk was comfortable and had a socket to charge your phone, courtesy light at each bunk and enough space for luggage. Reading the various opinions we equipped ourselves with noise plugs and inflatable pillows since they don't provide them. There were 3 of us and therefore we shared the cabin with 3 other people who did not cause any kind of inconvenience. The toilets were like other trains. In short, we armed ourselves with a lot of patience and adaptability and it went well. As for the negative points, they are the staff on board who spoke loudly in the corridor in the middle of the night and the bar which has high prices and very low quality. We had a big problem when purchasing tickets online, the system incorrectly assigned us 3 different cabins (with a minor). The paid calls were of no use and not even going to the ticket office because it is a different sales channel. Only the complaint email allowed all 3 of us to travel in the same cabin

Padua-Paris journey. The train was quite punctual, the only positive side. Thello is a very old train, carriages from 30 years ago. It has nothing of a modern train suitable for an international route. Among the TGVs it is the worst. The toilets are never washed during the journey, with all the imaginable consequences. Before lying down on the bunks I disinfected them. The floor of the compartment was filthy (I ran a damp handkerchief over the floor and pulled it up black). It is not possible to regulate the air conditioning. Very noisy and jolting journey. The train stops for an hour in Switzerland for document checks. The journey lasts a grueling 13 hours in total. I had chosen it because it was very cheap and for the convenience of going up to Padua and then being in the center of Paris, in the hope of using the night hours to sleep. Next time I will definitely choose the plane.

The (dirty) train had significant delays both on the outward and return journey... I asked for the expected refund months ago as at least partial compensation for the damage suffered. Still nothing. I recommend, in this case, issuing a certificate of delay at Paris Gare de Lyon at the Thello point for any cause. In Italy at least they did their utmost to immediately issue me a new replacement ticket for the missed connection. In Paris, however, forget about an additional service... on the contrary.

I have travelled on trains around the world and finally had a chance to travel on the famed TGV. But frankly, it is outdated. There is no service in first class and limited baggage space and for first class the seat were rather cramped. There is a dining car but the whole experience is that what would be expected in second class. However, the train left on time and arrived at the Gare du Lyon on time, so good for a shuttle service.

I took a round trip when I traveled from Paris to Lyon. I chose 1st prize. I was seated on the lower floor on the way there, and on the second floor on the way back. This can be specified at the time of purchase. I have used Gare de Lyon in Paris before, but this is my first time using the TGV. I have already purchased an e-ticket from the French National Railways website. I had a little trouble finding the train platform. The TGV is fast and can get you to Lyon's Part-Dieu station in 2 hours. I'm glad I arrived on time this time. All the customers are quiet and have good manners. However, the toilets are generally inferior to those on Japan's Shinkansen and limited express trains, so I'm a little disappointed.

I chose thello to go to Paris because I thought the journey was particularly fascinating, convenient for reaching the city center, certain of arriving rested and thus being able to save time on the day of arrival as well as on the day of departure to visit Paris. The plane wouldn't allow it. I then considered that we would have also saved a night in a hotel. Well, some of these things were confirmed, but not the poor quality of the trip. Toilets and in general very bad. Dirty. Broken sheets and bunks. Travel companions not always recommendable. I give two stars only for the rationality of the choice and for the gain in time and savings compared to flying.... But otherwise a great disappointment. It's a shame, because if it were well managed they would make tons of money.

Out of all the trains I have ever rode on worldwide, this is THE BEST train ride I have ever taken anywhere!  I took this train from Charles de Gaulle airport to Montpellier, then transferred to the TER for my final leg from Montpellier to Agde and back the same route a week later.  In total, I must have rode close to 1,600km on this train alone.In fact, riding on this train is very much like riding on a cushion of air and, if you spend most of the time taking in an enjoying the scenery off in the distance, the time will fly quite quickly.

Comfortable seats even in second class. Cars have large numbers on the side indicating 1st, 2nd class, etc. Marquis screen on each car indicates which car number each one has, easy to find your seat. Conductors are friendly. Be aware that the train WILL leave on time, not late like airlines do.

Novara-Paris Gare de Lyon trip with TGV, no changes, very convenient for those who live in the province. Train clearly from the 80s, only a little worn, but clean and functional, the services were also in order and remained so until Paris. The online booking was clear and convenient, and the seats obtained were exactly those booked, both on the outward and return journey. For those who haven't remembered to prepare them, it is not essential to put the label with the name. The seats have the availability of an electrical socket for cell charging, but the socket has 2 holes, the ones from the 70s/80s for only two plugs without earth, luckily mine was like that; if your plug is a 3, get a reducer. The hotel also had the same type of outlet, which I think is common in France. The food on the train has a good choice, but it is expensive, in line with other trains: coffee for 2.40 euros; we brought a small snack. There is room for large luggage in some dedicated spaces, and there is a convenient hat rack for bags and backpacks. Departures on time, with a slight delay on the outward journey only on the Turin-Bardonecchia route. Then without a hitch, at 290 km/h from Lyon St. Exupery to Paris: checked the speed with the satellite app and the geographical point with the Here map. For checks in Italy the polfer passed once, and in France the gendarmerie.
Italian pasta on the menu.  Ashamed. You can see the photo. The menu is 14.90. Tgv Paris Luxembourg from August 21. Honestly the worst I have eaten on a TGV.

We went to Paris from Milan P.ta Garibaldi, left on time and arrived in Paris 5 minutes early at 1.15pm. Overall a comfortable journey, certainly the strong point is the absolute punctuality. Some doubts about the bar, the food and drinks are decidedly expensive (as on all trains), seven hours pass without discomfort. The cars and bathrooms are clean, the fastest route is between Lyon and Paris, almost 300 km per hour ( This is what the application I downloaded said.)

The worst high speed train ever!!! 1, the train was delayed for 40 minutes. 2, the seats was duplicated and we didn't have seats. 3, when the train arrived in Geneva the door couldn't opened becoz of the technical problems therefore we waited for 20 mins. 4, my luggage has been stolen in the train and from the TVG management no one was really care they said wasn't their problem. My experience was bad bad bad and sad!!
Very fast but still expensive. The seats are comfortable and the cars are quiet, the only downside is the prices and quality of the products at the car bar.
We used the TGV to reach Paris, the train is very comfortable. Clean bathrooms (although unfortunately on the way back many bathrooms ran out of water). I recommend buying food and drinks on land.

After reading the reviews we almost didn't want to leave but we had a great time. Train very punctual both on the outward and return journey. Even on the way back we arrived in central Milan early. Very courteous on-board staff, many speak perfect Italian. Clean train and well-organised bar-restaurant car. Great trip!

If you want to reach Milan from Nice or Marseille I suggest you take a plane, whatever the cost, and avoid this fetid cart at all costs! The train is late, the staff is unprofessional, the toilets are unusable (real LATRINES to be ashamed of) and the cost is not justified. Having arrived in Milan Lambrate, one step away from Centrale and the end of the journey, already 30 minutes late we were informed that a serious fault forced us to stop and that the delay could not be calculated. Stop. No other communication to the entire train of tired people who have been traveling for 5 hours and who are expressly forbidden to get off at the rest station. HORRIBLE.

To travel from Paris to Bruges, I recently obtained the high-speed train tickets through the website from Argentina. I find it interesting to say that my experience was very positive, both for having sent an email with some doubts about the journey, and regarding the stopovers, which were resolved within 48 hours, meeting my expectations. Then I paid with the credit card and in approximately 12 days I had the tickets at home. The page was that of sncf, which was in Spanish and is very clear to search for dates and alternatives.  I recommend doing it more than 60 days before the trip and you will get a better rate and peace of mind for receiving the tickets. I am making these comments because I saw many doubts regarding these topics in the forum.

The TGV was a great technological advance; but today, it exports poorly unlike other high-speed trains like the ICE 3 and the shinkansen. Just compare the Thalys and Eurostar offers which are more qualitative than the TGV for almost similar trains and it is without counting if we compare with the German, Chinese and Japanese offers. It is also not innocent if the Chinese market has not developed its TGV train offer. Having used different high-speed lines, the TGV remains good, but it is no longer the best and the arrival of competition from 2019 could hurt.

We traveled from Paris Gare de Lyon to Perpignan on the TGV.  Comfortable spacious seats with foot rests and panoramic views from the large windows.  The journey took 5 and a half hours and there was free wi-fi in the designated space on the upper level of this double decked train.  Only one gripe about the experience was when visiting the buffet car on the upper level of the train the assistant who served me couldn't get my debit card to work (even when holding the machine to the external window and I was without cash but apart from this we were satisfied with this quiet train both going and on the return journey.

I really don't know how to start. The carriages had a smell that was very reminiscent of that of the chemical toilets outside the stations, the seats do not seem to be the cleanest (but fortunately they were not very uncomfortable) and they do not have any electrical sockets. The wi-fi doesn't exist, the train goes far from fast, and it's basically dirty. Luckily there was air conditioning. One last thing that annoyed me was that although I had specified in the reservation (made months before) two seats that faced the same direction as the train's journey, I found myself two seats in the opposite direction. I won't take it back!

Scared by previous reviews we tried THELLO. Online booking Verona/Paris full compartment for 3 people and Paris/Verona compartment for 4 (there could be an extra person). Once the train arrived right on time I went to an employee to ask for information, she only spoke French!!!! it tells me that from the reservation two people are in one cabin and the other is in another. But how is this possible if I have an exclusive cabin on the reservation?? A colleague arrives who fortunately speaks English, she immediately shows herself willing to join the family in the three-person cabin, she bends over backwards and after a few tens of minutes from the train's departure we are assigned our three-person cabin. Small premise on the train, there are 80s FS carriages with one, two or three fairly large bunks and a small sink inside equipped with a clean duvet and pillow and a small bathroom kit including a towel, toothbrush with single-use toothpaste, night mask, soap and earplugs, then there are the Thello (French) bunks where there are four, five and six bunks (to be clear, those from the 80s on trains Italian long-distance trains) of recent construction but where the bunks are short, hard and narrow, there are no cushions but there is a kind of sheet that also functions as a non-woven blanket. The bathrooms.... painful service, nauseating-vomiting in the morning and that's all I'll say (for a cost of around €700....) so even if they're old I recommend the bunks for up to three people. The best thing is that we leave in the evening and in the morning after sleeping, for those who can sleep, we arrive in the center of Paris. Dining car present but not tested.

You are spoiled in first class😄 We had comfortable seats with enough leg room. Zurich --> Paris in 4 hours It's really super fast. I say it's even faster than flying. Breakfast is included in the price and is served on site. We were lucky to leave on time and arrive on time👏 That's the only way I'll travel to Paris👍

We booked the train months in advance as there were 5 of us. Ages 16, 19, 23, 39 and 62. We were travelling from Paris to Barcelona so 6 and a half hours in total. I found the station relatively easy to navigate our way to the train. Similar to the airport they have departure screens which will tell you which hall to go to and then about 20 minutes before departure time they will update with the track number. The train was very comfortable and there was plenty of space for luggage ( though we were the first stop so not sure if people picked up at later stations they might not have found the same). There was plenty of room. I am 5ft 10 and I had plenty of leg room so pretty spacious which is a bonus.If you can try and get the upper deck (especially for long distances) as the view is gorgeous. There is a café on the train though as you would expect quite expensive so bring your own if you can.My tip would be keep checking their website for the release of tickets for your date of travel as the cheapest ones sell out fast as do the ones on the upper deck.
Excellent connection to get to the heart of Paris in the fastest way. A (fairly) expensive way to travel, but extremely comfortable!

Where to start? 1. If you have bought tickets online and have to print at the station make sure you get there well in advance. Our resi number didn't work at the print out mach. and we had to wait 30+ mins to talk to an agent. 2. there is no wifi on board and 3G is very spotty. 3. it was very hot on board. 4. the food on board is terrible. 5 the beer was warm.

We took the high-speed Thalys train from Brussels to Paris and back. It was really fast (only took about an hour and fifteen minutes each way), clean, comfortable, and on time. Prices are very reasonable if you book in advance. Highly recommended.
Trains in Europe are great. We had so many to catch in our trip and without exception all were a comfortable pleasant experience

It was my first trip on TGV Barcelona - Nimmes, and the truth is I was a little disappointed... I was traveling in first class, the seats were wide and comfortable.    On the way there I traveled on the ground floor, it was a little hot, and the ground floor is a little oppressive with the ceiling so low; The windows were so dirty that I couldn't even take a photo. The cleanliness of the carriage was a bit "fair".. The return was on the upper floor, I recommend it, more comfortable, but... two surprises... - The bar service in the carriages, and only on the upper floor, understandable because of the stairs, high was announced repeatedly but never arrived... not even in first class.   - At the bar... they informed me that in Paris they DON'T CARRY ICE... can someone figure it out-... For the rest it's normal, except that from Nimes to Gerona many times.    The AVE is more than good...
Left Malpensa airport... from a return trip from Brazil. we decide to return to Paris for a few days... super fast, clean train and a valid alternative to the plane.
wonderful technology at a time when there are too many vehicles on the roads ideal means of transport (former TGV driver)
I enjoyed traveling on these high speed trains, very clean and very quiet. The only complaint is they dont speak english to notify people which I think should be looked into.

Anyone reading this review do not take Thello. Old and obsolete cars - old and smelly bathrooms. Very narrow spaces (you are on the train for several hours). And to say that we were in a sleeping cabin. We saw the bunk arrangements: practically a cattle car. These things shouldn't exist in 2015, especially with those prices!!

I have often had to take a high-speed train, notably Paris-Lille (1 hour drive) and Paris-Strasbourg (2.5 hours drive). The last time I used the TGV was to go to Angers to visit the Saint-Louis exhibition.
If you are under 26, pay 15 euros and get a Carte ZOU! and receive (great) discounts when purchasing your ticket and that of your companions!

First off I'd like to say the TGV has the worst first class of all the high speed trains I've been to. La frecca Rossa in Italy's is outstanding and la fressa rossa in Spain is a close second. The TGV is also extremely overpriced, one beer can run you from 3-5 euros! The food was expensive especially for the crummy stuff they had. I would recommend it obviously because it's faster way to get around France, (other than flying) if you can fly spend your money on a flight instead.

TGV is easy to book on the (SNCF site). We booked multi trips together and printed them out. Do check when you get to the station if you have to pick up tickets at the information desk and there can be ques at some stations. This year we travelled around France on the TGV. We flew into Paris and got TGV to Nice. Be prepared for a 6 hour journey( 2 trains). The train was nice a comfortable, make sure to reserve your seats. On the ticket it shows you your coach number and seat before the train comes it shows you on the bill board where exactly your coach will stop so you not running up and down the train with suitcases trying to find your seat. Next train we took was up to Avignon it take about 3hours these trains have upstairs so try book one of them cause you can take in the scenery along the way. when you arrive you can get a local train into Avignon it takes about 7minutes and if you are only staying for the day you can leave your luggage at the station for 7euro per day. Next train we took was the TGV to Paris same as before took about 3hours. There is a snack bar on the train. We would recommend using TGV getting around France.

We recently travelled between Paris and Cannes on the TGV and found this to be a memorable experience. The trains were comfy, fast and ran on time. The buffet car was reasonably priced and had an adequate range of food/drinks.The views of the French countryside and coastline were stunning.We will certainly use the train again when travelling in France/Europe and would highly recommend this mode of transport to others.

We had the unfortunate idea of ​​taking the thello train from Milan to Nice. We had opted for first class since the journey was very long. Surprised at the station the first class carriage is missing, passengers start arguing about which seats are the Italian Trenitalia controllers and train conductors say verbatim, you can get a refund by going to the Thello boutique in Nice. At the shop in question we find absolutely incompetent staff who obviously deny the refund and the responsibility lies between Trenitalia and Thello. We have also asked for a refund on the company's website for 10 days and we are still waiting for a response.

Before departure: Thello offices at Gare de Lyon closed during the train's departure time. During the journey: 1- Compartment curtain broken, to remedy this an on-board manager gave us a sheet to act as a curtain and thus protect us from the gazes of passengers passing through the corridor. 2- At departure there were 2 usable bathrooms in the compartment, upon arrival only one (the other had been closed) and without water. 3- During the night I was stung on my arms, the only areas uncovered, by I don't know which insects. Even today after 4 days the bites are red and itchy.4- They no longer give pillows and they don't even warn you about this so you have to make do with rolled up clothes.5- I wonder why there are no European standards and if there are why they are not applied regarding hygiene and cleanliness on trains. Why aren't surprise checks carried out by swabbing the dust present on the seats and floors at departure when in theory the train should be clean?

It is fast but needs a few extra bells and whistles. We picked up this train from Paris, our coach driver couldn't get into the car park because the barriers were down and he couldn't get anyone to open them, he had to reverse back out and go through the out lane. The train carraige wasn't anything special, I was expecting wifi there wasn't any. I was expecting a power socket there wasn't one. If you go on this train take your own food and have a wee before you set off. British Rail is better than French rail.

When I traveled to Brittany, I traveled in both 1st and 2nd class. First class seats are in three rows, and sometimes all the seats are in the direction of travel, but sometimes they are seated facing each other. There were 4 rows in 2nd class, and there was space inside the train to store luggage. I think the windows often have to be a little dirty to enjoy the view from the train. There are various sites, but you can purchase tickets in English on the French National Railways website, and I think the price is good value.

We had chance o to experience this famous train known under the name TGV ( Train a grande vitesse ). It was nice experience to be on it, we took the first train from Nantes to Lyon and the second from Chamberry to Paris. It was very fast but pricy train

On May 28th, with my wife and 2 children, we took the Tello train from Milan central 11.00pm to Paris 10.15am. Left on time and arrived on time. Unfortunately we chose the wrong day because the day before arrived at 9.15am. 80's train, noisy with a lot of vibrations especially if you have the highest bunk, but ear plugs are enough. We found impeccable service, friendly staff, clean compartments and bathrooms (but this depends on who frequents them), bottle of water for each person, set of sheets and pillowcase sealed in a transparent bag... Of course, it takes a bit of adaptability, and luck, but it went well for us!
Fast, comfortable and stylish, good experience, worth the extra for your journey, extensive network.

Incredible experience. The TGV is super comfortable and reaches high speeds. It's surprising. The best way to travel to more distant places, taking half the time it would take with another type of transport.

As newcomers to travelling on the TGV, we were not aware of the convoluted carriage numbering system on the TGV. Unlike most trains which start with 1 at one end, then follow sequentially to the other end, the TGV starts with 1 in the middle proceeds to about 6 or 7 at the rear, then continues forward from 1 to the front of the train. This results from two trains being coupled together.We had booked Bordeaux to Paris travelling first class.  Much of our problems resulted from the Bordeaux platform being a construction site, so the signs explaining the strange numbering system were largely obscured. When the train arrived we could find no numbering on the outside of the carriages. We only observed one first class carriage towards the front of the train, so raced for this. I could find no seats matching our tickets, so as the train started moving I finally located a conductor, who explained that our seats were at the rear of the train, and as there were no stops, and a locomotive in the middle of the train, we would not be able to access them. He pointed to three fold down jump seats between two carriages we could sit on, then just walked off. So there we sat, in cramped conditions, for 3 hours 15 minutes. So much for first class. The crowning moment came when I discovered that in the confusion of trying to find our seats, some thieving mongrel had taken off with my camera.....

I went to Grenoble to visit friends and took the famous TGV from Turin. Price paid 67 euros for a commuter train. Let's keep our Red Arrow!!!! TGV or Train Grand Vitesse!!! But please! Maybe from Lyon to Paris! It's better to draw a veil over cleanliness. First and last time. Au nous pas revoir !
The fastest conventional train in the world... what to add. It is very good experience to try to travel with this train.
I took TGV several times. I recommend Talys, which is a better company, although TGV is for making certain routes. It does not have free WIFI.
Why can't we do this in the United States? What a way to get long distances quickly without the hassles of flying. If only...

Although trains are delayed quite frequently and strikes recur annually, the customer service is very good. If you decide to cancel the trip, or change the date, it is very easy. If your train is cancelled, refunds are quick.

TGV Gare Lyon was very crowded and very unhelpful to English speaking tourists. Be ready to pay to pee and be insulted in the process. Paul's likewise was insulting and not up to standard. Very unhelpful train attendants mis directed us three times onto the wrong car. Not happy at all.

We took the TGV from Paris to Dijon and then from Dijon to Charles DeGaule Airport.  Both times, the train was on time for departure and arrival.  The seats in first class were large and very comfortable.  The train is quiet and the ride is smooth.  The cost was good value for our travels.  It was an overall excellent experience.

The comfort, ease, access, everything about the TGV is perfect. High speed is something that attracts me. Riding a TGV is a unique experience. There is a bar inside the train. The attendant spoke Spanish, English and French. Walking 500 km in 3 hours just shows us how far ahead of our time they are.

We took the 6am TGV on July 18th to Paris. Disturbing journey, from Sestriere onwards there was no air conditioning, we arrived in Paris on time but in a pitiful state! for the record it must be said that the conductor came by twice to bring us free bottles of water... the return was better, with the air conditioning working but half an hour late.... First and only experience.

Purchased RailEurope passes through Rick Steves Web site.  They forward you to a questions format that helps you determine if purchasing pass vs. point to point is best.  We were steered to the passes and I purchased 4 passes for my family.  On arrival to Frankfurt I went to train station office to validate passes after an 11 hour flight.  I made the unforgiveable error of writing starting date month/day/year instead of date/month/year as is the custom in Europe. They would not allow me to switch the numbers and re-issued tickets for myself, wife and oldest son.  They could not issue a new ticket for my youngest son since it was part a package and had face value of zero.  Eurail could not fix pass since they did not issue pass.  I contacted RailErope and they said since I was already in Europe, there was nothing they could do and wrote "I hope it works out"!!!! In the same email they said we want to provide the best customer service???I tried 5 train station offices and Eurail offices without sucess This was a complete hassle with every train ride and we still needed reservations for all the trains with supplement payment for the high-speed trains worth about 300 extra Euros for the family on a 3 week trip.I would NEVER use or recommend this pass to anyone or family.

I took the Thello train last month in June 2015. Train was horribly dirty, sleeping compartment that my wife and I shared was very cramped (but still cost 400 euros). We boarded at 1100 PM and were told to wait to sleep until they can get our passports. The attendant was very flaky and we were nervous to give him our passports. Took him about an hour to finally return so we could finally sleep. I asked him for a pillow and he said he was busy and would return in ten minutes.....never did, so I slept all night on a shirt for a pillow....when I say slept, I laid awake all night. In the middle of the night the train stopped and didn't begin moving for at least three hours. When the train stops, the AC also stops, so we were stuck in the heat wondering what the heck is going on. Unfortunately Thello has no overhead system so you can't get updates without finding an attendant, which are few and far between. Breakfast was due to be served early in the morning, but since there was a delay we were told there would be no food until we got to Milan. The food on the train was horrible! Basically just TV dinners, if you can even call them that. We were due to arrive in Venice at 0900 AM, but didn't get there until 1600 (0400 PM) that evening. Missed tours that we had booked. I would highly recommend not using Thello. They are supposed to give us a refund of 1/2 our ticket price due to being delayed over 120 minutes. I have submitted my application for the refund twice now and still haven't heard back from them. DONT TAKE THELLO!!! Fly, take another type of train...drive if you have too! Worst experience of our trip, horrible customer service.

If you are in Paris and want to go to the south of France, with TGV trains you have several destinations and there is always a promotion to pay cheaper for these trips. If you want to change the date of your trip, do so on the same day so you don't have to pay the 12 euro fee.

Awful, filthy, horrible food, train travel describes this hell ride from Paris to Milan on the Thello train. We boarded what we thought would be a romantic journey on an overnight train through the alps. It was anything but that. Many hours are spent in tunnels. Our 3 sleeper cabin for just two of us was like getting into a closet. No porter help available. We had to hoist our bags up onto racks three feet above our heads in order to fit into the cabin. The train and our cabin was so filthy dirty no amount of purell could make us feel we were not sitting in a germ infested jail cell. Our room was over 33c when we boarded and only after several hours with the AC on high did it cool down. It was advertised as having a bathroom. It doesn't. It's a cupboard with a sink and a plastic mirror. A few toiletries are provided. The toilets are at either ends of the car and after two hours were unbearable to enter. Never cleaned during ten hour trip. No toilet paper etc. The dining car consisted of boxed food at a counter. Only one person serving with huge lines of people. Drinks were warm and cold food was too. Bring your own food on this train. Our breakfast was included but we never bothered to collect it from the dining car for all of the above reasons.  They come by to fold down your beds at ten pm. After that there is no sitting up! So you try to sleep. The sheets seemed clean but the 12x12 inch pillow half full is not enough to cushion the bed of steel you're forced to sleep on. We do not suffer from motion sickness but this ride was somewhat unsettling. We were two in the cabin and could barely climb in and out of our bunks via a small ladder. Cannot imagine a third person sleeping on top bunk with the luggage. After taking many types of trains throughout Europe this by far was the worse. We felt like we were in a bad dream. Oh but hold on we never fell asleep as it was noisy bumpy and hot. To top it off it was very expensive too. We are thinking of complaining but do not think this company would care.

Our train experience wasn't what we expected. We went from Mannheim, Germany to Paris, France. It was a 3 hour ride with no a/c and the temperature outside was over 90 degrees and it was hotter on the train. We were completely drained when we arrived in Paris. The ride was slow in Germany with many stops, but fast in France. Would have been a nice ride if it wasn't so hot.

Our American Airlines flight PHL-CDG was 2.5 hours late (weather delayed takeoff), so we arrived too late for the E-ticket ticketed seats, booked on Rail Europe Booking. SNCF ticket agents at the CDG station refused to exchange or give any value for the $250 E-tickets documents, Paris to Avignon. The agent did sell us tickets for another train, at the price discounted for 60+. But the conductor on the train refused to honor those tickets, because we didn't have a "Carte" document, which he said had to have been purchased at least a week before the tickets were purchased, which the SNCF agent knew or should have known. So we had to then buy tickets on the train. Our advice to Americans planning to use TGV: Do Not buy your tickets until you are in France and ready to board. Those ticket are specific and valid only for the person named, date, class and route of the ticket. Caveat emptor. SCNF's advice to go to the American counter for a remedy has gotten no remedy, either. American says they will not refund the price of a rail ticket, even through they caused the delay. Another piece of advice: use the same carrier from departure location to ultimate destination, so they are responsible for the results of delays. Changing the mode of transportation in the middle of the trip can be very costly.

Moving from one big city to another on these trains is a sum of benefits. We traveled from Frankfurt to Paris. Super modern trains, quiet, comfortable, strictly punctual with their departure and arrival times and at convenient prices, is the sum of ideal adjectives to not hesitate to use this service. I advise paying a minimum difference and traveling in first class, where the comfort is greater, less movement of people through the corridors and food service in the car. Great experience.
Very fast train. Clean interior! It accelerates to 300-400 km/h. You can get from one end of France to the other very quickly!
What a delight is the french rail system.  Imagine what life would be like with it in North America... It's timely, it's clean and it's fast.

Fast and comfortable even in economy class, what more could you ask for? We left and arrived on time which is the main thing here, the train was clean. I never hesitate to use the TGV for my trips to Paris, whether tourist or professional.

We were on tgv lyria to basel and although it started on time it was very slow, it never looked like an express train and we were delayed by 2 hours to our final destination basel. Date of travel 1st july 2015
We took the TGV from Paris to Rennes and return. Business Class seats were comfortable and made the journey a pleasure. Easy access and minmum time to bbaord unlike air travel

This year we gave up on the driving in favor of the TGV. We used the TGV from Brussels to Avignon where there is a relatively new TGV-only station, Avignon-Paris-Brest and Brest-Paris. First class cabins are the way to travel.  This coupled with using the Spanish TGV last year and we're sold on the comfort of this mode of transportation.  Sit back in a comfortable seat, plug in your laptop and watch movies, read books or work as beautiful and varied terrain passes by. Luggage storage can be an adventure but even with far more luggage than we should have had, we always managed.  The only minor flaw was that on the Paris to Brest route,  the train only travels at TGV speeds about a quarter of the distance but you still get the comfort of the TGV carriages.  Travelled on four different types of carriages all with their own special features. Even taxi transfers between stations in Paris was easier and faster than anticipated.
Very comfortable way of travelling. when going to France it's not much slower or sometimes faster (including check-in and transport to and from airport) than airplane and it's a lot cheaper.
It's very worth it. We used Versailles windshield and it was very fast, comfortable and safe, I really recommend it
Very good, satisfactory service. Much better than law cost flights.. comfortable seats and smooth journey. We had no problems. I highly recommend

I made a round trip from Bari/Montparnasse to Rennes to go to Mont Saint Michel. The trip was on the day of the French National Railways strike, and although the train I had booked moved, the previous two trains were canceled, but I arrived on time. On the way back, when I went to the counter to change my reserved train to the previous train, I just made the corrections with a ballpoint pen and there was no seat reservation, so I had to choose an auxiliary seat near the door. I sat down in the seat that had become vacant after the train moved, and I arrived without being told anything. The 2nd class seats cannot be oriented or reclined, but they were comfortable.
Clean, modern, extremely fast and punctual train. The guards were helpful and helped me in Paris. Great means of transport.

Quiet and fast travel at 330 KPh you don't even feel it moving.  Reasonably priced, good service and quicker than the plane, just taking 2 and a half hours from London to Paris with no airport hastles.

Fairly well enough organized building wherein the trains dock and depart. There are signs in English so you wont be lost. I did not notice any beggars or pickpockets at that time. You will need to fill out some forms if you are leaving the country. The train ride itself was quiet and smooth, no problems.

I took the route London - Paris. It took around 2:20 h. It's a little difficult to walk around the train, especially going to the restaurant car. But it's a cool experience. I recommend trying to get seats in the direction of travel. I didn't take care and traveled backwards. It's not so cool.
Whether it is orange like the first ones or now gray and blue with or without floors, this train is truly a blessing to travel. We don't even realize how fast we're going. Damage.

fast and smooth train travel from barcelona to paris today. fast: 300 kilometres per hour at maximum speed. smooth: reclined seat and slept for some of journey. kids also slept without problem.  six hour trip but generally comfortable and supportive seating and beautiful countryside made the experience worthwhile.

We used the train in July from Basel to Paris. The 2nd class was overcrowded and chaotic as it appeared that some of the passengers had tickets without seat assignment. Furhermore, seat numbers were totally messed up in location and noone of the train company was available to assist. It took us about 20 minutes to find our seat in an overcrowded train as nothing moved due to too many people. On the way back, booked 1st calss. "Lyria Lounge" in Gare de Lyon is dramatically different from the advertisement. The receptionist had no time for us (chatting with a lounge vistor for several minutes, small talk it seems without caring for her customers otherwise) and then seated us on plastic chairs in a windy corner full of smoke odeur in the restaurant, with the single question "Cheese cake or sandwich". No service at all beyond that, no hint to journals, wlan, or a friendly apology (however, a snippy "You cannot get there its full"), no kind invitation later as there was space in the lounge a few minutes later. The lady left 40 mins before lounge closure and did not contact us again, neither for track assignment nor as lounge guests. The restrooms of the Lyria corner are absent, those of the restaurant were not as clean as appropriate for a first class comfort. No privacy for redressing or the like. The 1st class trip in the train on the way back to Basel was ok, the usual inflight menu (cold) and a friendly service.

The TGV is the flagship of French industry with its speed records and its national network. All routes are now practically served by high-speed train from Paris. The first was the service to the city of Lyon. These trains are comfortable and allow rapid travel to major cities in France and neighboring countries.

The windows were dirty. Although the chair didn't seem to be able to recline, it was very comfortable and I was able to take a nice nap from Rennes Station to Paris Montparnasse Station, reviving my stamina for the trip.

For someone who comes from Brazil, where trains are almost all the time in "out of order" status or simply don't exist, TGV is a dream come true. We could enjoy it many times between December (2014) to January (2015) going to North France from South France, including Côte d'Azur and it was punctual, organized and nice way to travel. I have only one complaint: I traveled from Marseille to Strasbourg by train and we had an ice problem when we were about to enter Strasbourg, which is normal in December, but we had "un retard" of 2 hours in our "arrivée" in Strasbourg and we were afraid that our hotel would not consider our reservation. We couldn't get a compensation because there are no options for foreigners (maybe foreigners out of Europe only?), although we had filled the document to get the compensation. We tried to write to SNCF and we gave our BIC number but apparently it was not enough. A very kind person from SNCF sent me a letter asking me about my BIC number beacuse apparently it was wrong. I went to my bank and they confirmed that my BIC number was ok and yet I didn't receive any answer from SNCF after I confirmed again my BIC number. Still waiting...

We decided for an adventure to take Eurostar to Paris and then connect TGV Paris to NiceWe arrived at Gare de Lyon in plenty of time but on one of the hottest days of the year.  The departure was announced and immediately mayhem, but this is France! Made it to our coach to find we were sitting upstairs, no sign of anyone to help with bags unlike very helpful Eurostar people at Ashford InternationalTrain is full and my seat is broken so it only reclines and there is no table3 hours to Aix very smooth 3 hours onward to Nice aargh! I could have walked the last part fasterArrived at Nice 19:55 to find no porters and no lifts or escalators.  ( I know there are indications they are upgrading station but still!)Overall an adventure we won't repeat next time Easyjet!
From London to Paris... Very fast, smooth trip. Tip: Don't reserve seats with tables facing each other. Unless they are all your acquaintances.

Me and my husband took the TGV train from Zurich to Paris,4 hrs ride.We had an amazing time,we got first class tickets,I bought them online a week before.We got a lot of snacks and unlimited drinks.The people who work on the train were very nice,we had the tickets on the phone,no paper;)The train was very nice,smooth,not new but decent.A lot of leg room,enought space to put bags any size.The views were amazing,a lot of green:mountains,villages,cities.We loved everything about this trip,we will do it again.

The TGV is an excellent way to get around France and to CdG, our last trip shuttling between Paris and Disneyland (that's another review... TL;DR, stay in Paris unless you have young kids). There's a lot of grief about the TGV but I still find the first class to be better than the Amtrack service in the States, but not as nice as the service and comfort of the Eurostar (London to Paris) or the high speed Shinkansen in Japan. With the TGV you'll

Caught the train at 11:01am to Paris and arrived at 2:26pm.  Ride was smooth and effortless, toughest part was getting the bags stowed.  We were 4 traveling to France to get on 2wk river cruise and bags were usual size suitcases...area to pack not easy to find.  We did however manage to get them stowed and we were on the train in cheap seats thanks to Joe's diligence on tickets $58 US each....worked out great.  In Paris caught a taxi to river cruise and had a great cab driver who gave use good sightseeing tour at the same time....saw where Princess Di met her demise, but also other very interesting sights as well.  We would definitely take the train again, so easy and we can se how one could just day trip from London or vis-versa.

Modernity that unfortunately we won't see in Brazil anytime soon. Fast and comfortable train, bar with somewhat expensive soft drinks. Board at Gare du Nord calmly, despite passing through the English immigration post being a bit hectic (and not very friendly).

The TGV is more and more expensive... It is better to buy a reduction card if you take it several times a year in order to benefit from the advantages. Delay level I think it's correct. Comfort level as well, especially first class which is very quiet. A TGV trip is pleasant.

In one word, DON'T - fly instead.  Our "first class" cabin was run down and grubby, there was one small sink in a cupboard blocked by the ladder leading to top bunk.  The ladies toilet at end of carriage was sealed because it did not work - the men's next door was in a dilapidated state, with the toilet paper soaked through and no replacement.  We had to make up our own bunks, and the air-conditioning was patchy.  The train broke down for three hours in Switzerland, and because it was late getting into Venice, we missed our booked guided tour.  The so-called breakfast was shoved at us in the restaurant car - a small bottle of juice, a small container of apple puree and a rather stale "croissant" in a brown paper bag, and NO COFFEE - the machine had broken down!!!  Never again.
There is no better way to get to Disneyland when arriving at Paris CDG airport. It is reasonable in price and takes between 9 and 10 minutes. Wow! At the same price it takes c45 minutes by coach.
Coming from Nice, the high-speed portion to Marseille is still missing but we believe it will eventually arrive.

TGV is an acronym for Train Grande Vittesse, and in the French alphabet, it is pronounced as "tejeve". There is no problem even if you pronounce it in English because the other person will understand it, but I think it would be good to know it so that when the other person (French) says tegeve, they can understand it.

The TGV system is truly impressive, racing across huge swaths of France at speeds of 200 and more kmh quietly and comfortably in both first and second class.  In no time, passengers arrive at their destination in clean, comfortable cars.   THere are few delays so don't be late, get on the train quickly and get off just as quickly.  Restaraunt cars are on most routes.  The biggest drawback of the TGV are the stations themselves which most often require hiking up, up, up and down again, far too many stairs.  Some stations have elevators that operate slowly or are placed at some distance on the platform.  With heavy luggage it is a huge distraction to the otherwise train system, not to mention the inconvenience.  TGV stations are much like the Paris metro system (too many stairs, few escalators and elevators), poorly designed for the elderly, very young, disabled or people with too much luggage.     Book tickets early and walk away with great prices and savings.

Decide to travel to Geneva for a day during our Paris holiday.Finding the ticket selling area at Gare de Leon was a bit difficult but was successful after a long wait.The cost was high as we only booklet two days ahead. (550Euro for two return first class tickets)The trip was fantastic, the scenery wonderful, especially entering the Swiss Alps.We missed out on a meal as they had booked us into the wrong carriage but were very apologetic and gave us a drink one knibbles.Geneva was beautiful although it was hot, very clean compared with Paris.Our only complaint was the railway station. Very little seating (compared with Gare de Leon) and very hot.Getting on the return train was a shambles. No one seemed to know wher we should sit as it was a double decker train In lieu of single deck.In the end we were told to sit upstairs wherever we liked.We got a free meal, just OK but plenty of beer.All in all a pleasant way to spend a day away from the bustle of Paris

Better standard of train than in the UK The seats are larger and toilets user friendly We used this service from Paris to champagne The only criticism is that they aren't as regular as I would like on a Saturday. As a train service though it is good and reliable
I have experienced best ever train time from Swiss to paris. It was very quick, neat and clean and best wa yo travel. They have also assisted me in booking cab in paris from within the train

I booked the TGV-Lyria online from Paris to Zurich. The train was really comfortable. Though we booked second class in TGV Lyria, still we found sufficient place to keep our 2 heavy big boxes in the luggage area.Seats were really comfortable.  Train was absolutely on time. Definitely , I will recommend anyone who is planning a trip from paris to zurich , to book on it.

Excellent means of transport. The modernity of these trains and the cleanliness of their interiors is incredible, given that many people pass through them every day. I loved riding the TGV in France...

We did the Milan-Paris return trip at night in couchettes. On the way out the air conditioning didn't work, so there was no air in the compartment and we couldn't breathe. After going around half the train we managed to find the manager, who didn't know a word of Italian (but is it possible that a manager only knows French on the Milan-Paris line?). With the help of a train conductor who translated, he told us that he could put us in first class (it was almost all free) but by paying the relevant supplement: yes, we actually had to pay 70 euros more for a disruption caused by them! We obviously remained in the same airless compartment. The train left 1 hour late and arrived 45 minutes late. I would like to point out that the carriages are at least 30/40 years old, so the noise is truly deafening and being able to sleep is very difficult. On the return (Paris-Milan) the train left on time and arrived on time, some toilets were without water in the toilet and one wonders how it is possible to start a train that has to face 10 hours of travel without water: it is clear that no checks are carried out, which I hope will instead be carried out at a technical safety level... I would also point out that from the middle in June, to save money, they don't even provide pillows, so you have to organize yourself by balling up your jackets and sweaters to be able to rest your head.

We mostly enjoyed our trip from Paris to Avignon, travelling amongst a group of musicians and other tourists. We were pleased that our online booking with Rail Europe has been so easy. Negatives included poor food and a surprise in the form of a tiny dog travelling (? hidden) in the bag of a fellow traveller. The dog created the most disgusting miasma over the carriage each time it "went to the toilet" in the said bag. The owner seemed quite oblivious and unapologetic much to the disgust of other travellers.  If we had known that animals may be travelling on this train, then we may have reconsidered our mode of travel.

I had taken the TGV 25 years ago and it seemed like a cutting-edge train to me... it's a shame that today it's the same train: no renovations. The carriages are quite shabby, the seats are cramped, there is no Wi-Fi (which might have been fine 25 years ago, not today when we are all equipped with electronic media and perhaps choose the train to stay connected, navigate and perhaps plan our stay in the place we are about to reach). There are no monitors to know where we are Yes, the speed is that of a local and it is more stationary than in motion. The bar service is very expensive: 2.40 euros for an instant coffee!
The train is really fast, leaves the station on time and I found it very easy to locate the platform. It's really worth taking the trip, very beautiful landscapes.

Our first TGV trip was from Paris to Dijon in 1990. We were astonished then. We're astonished now. Our own country embarrasses itself when it comes to mass transit of even the most basic sorts, but this high-end replacement for airplanes makes us look even more pathetic. Fast trains, when and where there are trains, are France's slow ones.So, we were almost as excited about the ride as about reaching our destination.
