That, too, remains a theme as we continue to travel in France. We were traveling as a family of three generations—eight of us. Somehow it didn't occur to us that the sleek engine with its nose aimed at the boarding area was one of two and would soon be the the "caboose." And we were looking backward, too, as we shot through incredible countryside at speed.We'd figured it out by the next trip, which meant we had the same film in reverse. But even backward, it's superb. When we switch to more utilitarian milk runs, and then to buses, we are only slightly less impressed. Obviously, that deeper infrastructure makes the TGV possible.

beautiful, and also comfortable, shame about the inconveniences: we left Paris headed for Milan, and our train stopped at the border with great delay and we were forced to continue the journey by coach because that TGV didn't have permission to travel outside France, I don't know who to blame, but the journey became very bad, considering that I suffer from car sickness and had chosen to travel by train on purpose, booking first class tickets...

The worlds fasted train. I always love to travel on the TGV LIRA when it comes to visiting Paris from Zurich. They are very fast and very comfortable for travel. They make your travel tiredless.. Even when the train clocks above 350kms/hour, you will never feel any discomfort. Always my best when it comes to fast trains.

I took a TGV from Paris to Tours. My plan was to take the train directly from CDG but as I had not booked the ticket in advance the train was full. So, I needed to take a train and metro to Montparnasse and get the next train from there. So, for the next time I will buy the ticket in advance. Much easier. The train journey itself was very comfortable and went very quickly - it is amazing how fast the train goes and you do not actually even notice this. A fantastic way to travel.
Taking the TGCV from Stuttgart to Paris is always great. Comfortable seats, enough space and since everyone has a reserved seat, no crowds or crowds like on the ICE.
Excellent connection to the Netherlands Excellent service Comfortable Good transfer options Clear signage Please order tickets in advance

For a trip between Paris and London, the TGV is essential: it leaves punctually at the top of Gare du Nord. As it is a little complicated for those who don't know the station, I recommend arriving at least 45 minutes in advance to find the location, fill out the immigration forms and answer questions similar to any port of entry. Leave return tickets and accommodation ready if you are staying for more than 24 hours. The train is nothing special, and people strive for silence, especially on early morning trips. Buy your coffee, which will be much better than the one served in the restaurant car. Depending on your bad luck, you may end up going with a group of students. Take your ear plugs.
Excellent quality and punctuality of service. Clean platforms and equal trains. Convenience and speed that exceeds expectations.

On the West line (Paris/Bordeaux) Tight like sardines in the carriages with positions called "square", power outlets missing, still no wifi, chair heads still uncomfortable... Pragmatism, comfort don't exist at the SNCF?

I have had a couple of occasions to travel with the TGV and I must say that it is a decent but not extraordinary train. The image is meant to be of an extraordinary, fast, punctual train: it is actually a decent train but the quality does not excel, the speed is there but the punctuality is a little less so. Italian railways have an image of poor quality and delays but all in all...

Love a fast train.   Get on in Paris and next thing you know you are in NICE!  (my destination this March...but did Avignon to Paris last year)   The only complaint is that it could be cleaner.     But can't complain about the schedules and the ease of use.  One complaint is that it is hard to book it from the US without paying extra ...if you go to TheManInSeat61  the guy who writes that blog has a work around so you can book on the regular site and pay in euros.
Amazing train system that gets you all over France more quickly than imaginable......with a frequent schedule, and modern seating, amenities......very impressive.

For the first time with the TGV-Lyria from Zurich to Paris and back again on the 4th day. An unforgettable experience.Extract from Wikipedia: << The Paris-Basel-Zurich route via Strasbourg was in operation from June 10, 2007. The travel time from Basel and Zurich to Paris was reduced to 3 and 4 hours 34 minutes respectively. The TGV Rhin-Rhône route has been in operation since December 2011, and for the route via Basel this means: in three hours from Basel and in four hours from Zurich; All trains from Switzerland use the Gare de Lyon since the TGV Rhin-Rhône route in Paris went into operation. All connections to Switzerland are now offered by TGV Lyria, a joint subsidiary of SNCF and SBB. A special feature is the Jakobs bogies, in which two abutting middle cars rest together on one bogie and therefore cannot be separated. They give the train a low weight, particularly smooth running and reduce the likelihood of derailment. >>The upgrade from 2nd to 1st class was worth it. There was something to eat and drink and we were well looked after. The vehicle technology is striking in its smoothness. You don't even notice that you're traveling so fast. No bumping, no rumbling. Great. I recommend the iPhone app “GPS Speed” (see photo). The top speed was 340 km/h. Hey - that was fascinating. The masts whiz past, a typical noise tells the passenger that the speed must be very high. And yet - the calm and the suppleness were totally new to me. Absolutely comfortable.The service was very attentive and pleasant. There were two offerings of food. Non-alcoholic drinks and wine were included in the price. We chose Chardonnay. The food was delicious and left us completely satisfied. The train attendants and the service staff were all friendly and in a good mood. What we will do differently next time: Taxi booking on the train is offered, but is very expensive because the taximeter is already running while the taxi driver is waiting for the passengers at the train station and meets the guests at the arrival gate. Now we know that the metro or a taxi outside the Gare de Lyon train station are available. Another detail: there is a free offer from the SBB for international tickets like the one from Zurich-Paris. The SBB lounge is available to all passengers free of charge. Alcoholic drinks are at the passenger’s expense. Apparently the same offer is available in Paris, but we fortified ourselves with a drink at Le Train Bleu. But just take a look at the photos and form your own opinion. A “like” or a “helpful” always makes me happy. Thanks for your timePidu

I took the TGV Lyria as part of a railtour holiday from Paris Gare de Lyon to Lausanne and a return a week later.With a journey time of a little more than three and half hours, this was an amazing trip. Travelling first class, the journey was extremely comfortable.  The outward complimentary refreshments left a little to be desired but the return breakfast was excellent.For a fast and relaxed transit across Europe, this is hard to beat !

The TGV Milan Paris (and return...) is a fast train, comfortable but very often not particularly clean. Furthermore, its punctuality is often affected by long stops for which the reason is unknown! A positive side is the reimbursement punctuality of the French Railways. Record-breaking.
It's true that the TGV is a good alternative when you don't have a flight connection! The journey, Roissy/Montpellier does not seem too long despite a few stops. We are overall satisfied.

I was really excited to take the TGV train from Paris to Milan. The train left on time from Paris and really flew at an amazing speed to Lyon. Unfortunately, that was the end of the 'high speed' trip. After Lyon, the TGV turned into a regular inter-city train making at least a dozen stops and going no more than 80 MPH as far as I can tell. The worst part however was the torturous seating - just barely larger than an airplane! I am not a large person, and I was cramped up as if I were in the Gemini capsule. Even later on with no one beside me, I was still uncomfortable, and the air conditioning hardly works at all - I was sweating the entire trip wearing just a T-shirt. The train arrived in Milan 30 minutes late. At least the trip was cost effective - only 58 Euro's, so that was the bright side.

experience not to be repeated, dilapidated carriages, both on the outward and return journey the restaurant carriage was closed, making an 11 hour journey without being able to get a coffee is really hard. No air conditioning on the way back and too high on the way out, lack of blankets, sheets and pillows. The staff were kind but helpless. Broken bunk door, very dirty bathrooms and 2 and a half hours late on the return so missed the connection to Rome booked 2 hours after the supposed arrival. Too bad because the service would have been convenient but there is nothing positive. Ruined holiday

My daughter and I traveled Calais to Paris.  The lady in the ticket booth was too busy chatting on the phone to help.  We wanted first class (only $20 more), she gave us second.  We asked her to change it, she said no changes allowed.  We wanted reserved seats.  When we got on the train, we saw that we had actually only ONE reserved seat.  At that point, the train was full and I had to ride standing in the cattle car.  I tried to get help from one of the ticket takers, even tried to upgrade to first class again (where seats were available).  No one was remotely interested in resolving the issue.  Oh, and the standing car had no air and was approximately 127 degrees (I can joke now ...).  Overall an awful experience and for the bargain price of about 130 euros.  I wish I could give a 0 rating.  I would walk before riding TGV again.

Excellent! Certainly not very affordable, these menus are however value for money out of all proportion to the rest of the dishes offered. Every day a different menu, every day great signatures of French cuisine. Frankly, the 5/7 euros difference with the rest is really worth spending. Well done SNCF for this great innovation!

The French railways TGV train allows you to go from Milan to Paris (and vice versa) comfortably, without changes, and very quickly. It is an excellent alternative to the plane, for more relaxing and ecological tourism.

Traveling by train in Europe is fun and convenient. The TGV is particularly useful when traveling from Paris to anywhere else, or from anywhere else to Paris. When I traveled during Golden Week, I used it to travel from Gare de Lyon in Paris to Marseille in the south of France, and from Schiphol in the Netherlands to Gare du Nord in Paris. (Schiphol is a flight from Marseille.) From Japan, reservations can be made from the Rail Europe Japan site (http://www.raileurope-japan.com/). If you book early, you can get cheaper tickets.

Outward journey from Milan with a surprise, the bunk was occupied and the staff didn't bother to come and check. When we finally entered the dirty bunk with a nauseating smell left by the person who slept there. The worst surprise was yet to come, the occupant (male) saw fit to urinate in the waste bag between the tables. We called the staff who told us they couldn't do anything. The whole trip with scented company. It was disgusting.
Traveling by train in Europe is a true pleasure and doing so on the TGV is an experience that must be had.

Had the experience of riding the TGV from Paris to Germany. The inside of the train was clean and comfortable. But that time, the train was quite late. TGV had them write a claim for compensation. It was considered a satisfactory experience.
Paris Gare de Lyon... Magnificent station with two halls. Beware of uncaring people! Lots of security on site...

What can I say. We travelled from Nice to Paris 1st class. The train was quite reasonable but the Nice station was dreadful. The waiting area was very crowded with uncomfortable metal seating. When it was time to get onto the train it was all for himself. People rushed to take the escalator down to change platform the the same crowd.Had to drag heavy bags up a number of steps to the platform. There were no lifts. The platform is quite low leaving quite a big step onto the train with heavy bags. The first class seats were comfortable and clean and the train was fast. Toilet facilities were good and there was limited food available. At the Paris  end it was again a scramble.
I used the tvg to get from frankfurt to paris. It was on time and comfortable. Not anythoing to rave about neither anything to critisize. It was fine and wouldnt mind using it again

◇Background France/Turkey pack costs 29,500 yen (Actually 113,000 yen including fuel surcharges, taxes, etc. and extra charge for a single room) Free sightseeing in Paris🚅Used in Rennes👉Day trip to Mont Saint Michel◇ How to purchase tickets It seems like you can buy tickets in Japan if you have a card on the SNCF (French National Railways) website, but I'm not sure about my language skills, so I decided to buy them locally...However, you can check the admission status of each train on the website, so it's a good idea to check. ◇There is no central station in Paris until the day's station, and there are several stations depending on the area. This line becomes Paris Montparnasse station. Of course there is a subway, but like Tokyo Station, you have to walk for about 10 minutes (quite scary) through a maze-like place, so you'll need plenty of time. By the way, most of the displays are in French, and there is no basic English! ◇There are vending machines at Montparnasse Station in Paris, but the machines are scary, so I buy at the counter. English OK. The staff members were very polite and the process of buying tickets was similar to checking in for an airplane. Of course, credit cards are also accepted◇French railways (preliminary knowledge) do not have ticket gates. Therefore, in order to stamp the ticket, each person must enter the yellow numbered ticket issuing machine on the premises and stamp it themselves. ◇TVG...Unfortunately, it's fairly modern, cool, and comfortable, but it's not as interesting as the Shinkansen or China's high-speed railways. There's no car sales either. There is a buffet, but nothing that will make you want to eat. Rome, Italy🚄The dining car of the Milan conventional line was much better. However, the seats are more comfortable than second-class cars in China and ordinary Shinkansen cars (excluding Sakura)...but they remain fixed! On a weekday in January, the descending area around 7 o'clock was pretty empty. Recommended because it is comfortable. ◇The 2 hours and 10 minutes I spent on the train was quite enjoyable in the countryside of this agricultural powerhouse. ◇ Impressions/Conclusion The price is probably more expensive than the Mont Saint Michel bus tour. Even if you include a layover, it will probably be 1-2 hours faster. I think €61 is a little high. Although it's not very interesting, it's worth riding the TGV at least once. It's fast and comfortable...

High Speed ​​Train, from French, Train à Grande Vitesse or TGV is a series of high-speed TGV trains connecting Paris with other cities in France and with neighboring countries. The TGV is one of the fastest conventional trains in the world; In some sections it operates at speeds of up to 320 km/h. I knew the station but I didn't travel, very, very nice train!!
Comfortable high-speed train, although it could be better if the seats reclined... there is a cafeteria on board, it is a quiet trip.

Interesting trip but they need to keep the cars cleaner. Seat stains needed attention and trash containers needed emptying. Temperature in the car was far too hot to enjoy anything. I'd fly if they aren't going to keep it clean and comfortable. We paid first class fares for a lees than economy experience ( and hot).

I used it to go from Montparnasse to Rennes and to Mont Saint Michel. Although my seat was facing the opposite direction to the direction of travel, it was quite comfortable and the ride was smooth despite the speed. Although I was in a 2nd class train, I didn't feel inconvenienced and there were no strange people around, so I didn't feel unsafe. (I don't think you should let your guard down no matter where you are.) There is a power source at your seat, so you can charge your cell phone. When I bought coffee in the car, it came with a small barrhona chocolate. It was refreshing to see the scenery of the French countryside, and while I was looking out the window, I arrived in Rennes in no time. Next time I would like to go to southern France.

Took the TGV from Paris CDG to Bordeaux Gare St Jean. First class compartments are not really a marked improvement, and it was more the non-intrusivness of the other passengers that impressed me more than anything else. We were seated in coach 11, which made it impossible to take advantage of the snack bar. Odd that first class passengers aren't even afforded this convenience.Be warned that it's a good 1 km walk from Gare St Jean to the car rental companies, with absolutely no cover.

This is the French version of the Shinkansen. The red high-speed train Thalys runs not only in France, but also in Belgium and the Netherlands. It is true that trains run at high speed, but their schedules are regularly disrupted, making their arrival times unreliable. When I lived in the Netherlands, I often traveled to Paris from Amsterdam or Rotterdam, but I was never sure when I would arrive. Also, if you are boarding Thalys, don't forget to use a lock with a wire at the suitcase storage area. It seems that you may encounter theft.

On the journey from Milan to Paris, we took seats in first class for an excellent experience, combining the landscape of the journey, combined with the comfort of the service provided, but not!  The landscapes are very beautiful and the train is very punctual! As for the rest, the carriage was simply filthy and carpeted, imagine the dust mite party (for those with allergies, I recommend taking an aleggra beforehand). It felt like I hadn't seen a vacuum cleaner in about 100 years. There is no Wi-Fi service and all snacks and even coffee are paid for. I had a vision of modern trains in France and was very disappointed.

we have used the TGV to get from Paris to Lourdes. it's a long trip of around 7 hours but the train is clean, punctual, the seats are fine.. it was good but it took a long time to get there. there's also a cafe at the last wagon where u can buy food and drinks.
I took the TGV from London  to Paris  and found it a great introduction to the France Train arrived on time like swiss watch.I almost  sh.t my pants when trains reached 200mph ;-)Could not be better,
Up at 5 a.m. for 6:34 a.m. TGV. TGV delay at departure of a quarter of an hour. Illy catering not yet open at 6:40 a.m. despite a 10 meter queue... Still the same circus
I used the TGV 1*class train to go to Rennes, Reims, Strasbourg, Munich and Paris (TGV duplex). Comfortable seats, several luggage racks and quality service.

I had booked the Thello night train from Venice to Paris for 2nd May. I received an email on 1st when i was in Venice that seats would be re-arranged since the number of coaches would be reduced. So i landed up in the Santa Lucia station 30 mins before the departure time to find out that the train will run only till Milan and then afterwards we would need to go on bus to Paris (Milan to Paris is roughly about 850 kilometers)The train that had arrived in the station had only seater coaches and no sleeper coaches as i had booked. I felt quite cheated at this. This was the first shock (When i had booked the train i had got the coach no as 86 which seemed to be quite absurd as well. I have traveled by Thalys, Frecciarossa, Eurostar and all these train tickets mention the actual coach numbers in tickets)Second shock - I was asked to seat anywhere in the train. I had a family with a small kid who was tired and wanted to sleep properly. That was not possibleThird shock - We had to wait for sometime in the Milan station for the buses to come in. Buses were not ready. Had to wait at a entrance where people were drunk and blabberingFourth shock - The buses that were booked and the comfort is quite shocking. I could not sit properly. I had back pain and since i had a kid i had booked the Thello sleeper class to relax. Instead what i got was pain, pain and more pain.It was a harrowing time that night. Hope no other passenger goes through such experience

I decided to travel from Annecy to Paris by TGI Buoy, and when I bought the ticket online three months before it went on sale, I was surprised at how cheap it was. Well, when I checked the service status the night before I boarded the train, I found that there was no service from Annecy to the next station. In the end, I took the bus 30 minutes earlier than the scheduled departure time to the next station and was able to safely board the T-G buoy I had booked. It was a comfortable ride for about 3 hours.

The thello train is actually much less than a Eurocity night as they call it, it is to be clear the old express that was once used at night to reach Southern Italy, a Crotone-Milan or similar which now no longer exists and they have moved it to the French line. The train to Paris at night would be comfortable with the right adaptation to carriages that are not exactly new and do not correspond to the price you pay which let's face it is not exactly cheap (more than 200 euros per person return in sleeper) because you arrive directly in the center and if it were on time you could enjoy your time in Paris right away considering that the scheduled time is 9.30. The problem is that apparently this train is almost never on time, for us it was 2 hours late on the outward journey with arrival at 11.30 and a good 4.20 hours late on the return with arrival in Milan at 10.20 instead of 6 with all the inconveniences related to it. Plus having subtracted some from the train carriages, including the restaurant both on the outward and return journey, due to problems on the Swiss line or at least that's what they told us; they distributed all the travelers in cabins of 6 without distinction of reservation, therefore we who were traveling in 4 and had booked and paid for a compartment of 4 had to travel in 6. Of course in Milan they took care to assign us other seats on another red connecting arrow for Bologna and said that we could obtain a refund for the difference on the price paid, and this seems to me the minimum, but it was truly an interminable journey and certainly an experience not to be recommended, at least until the managers of Thello (assuming it resists) they do not change their travel mentality and are able to provide more appropriate service guarantees.

We took the TGV from Paris to Dijon to start our river cruise and found it a great introduction to the French  countryside (so much better than flying).  The train was fast and smooth (wish we had those in Australia!) and we were able to watch the scenery flashing by.  Just a note to those with limited mobility - as others have mentioned, the train is a duplex with stairs to reach the upper level.  Those who would find this a problem need to try and get a lower-deck seat when booking (if this is possible).

Could not be better, 1st class from Avignon to Paris with a prepayed taxi with driver at the end of the platform. He looks after the luggage, explains the drive through the city and got us to our hotel in perfect time. Please use this service option, it costs 11e and adds class to the trip. I think that it is only on idtgv with tickets that you print at home, just like Ryan.

On the TGV Paris Valence, the bar and restaurant service is of some interest. ..except that the person behind the counter is just unpleasant and even contemptuous. An exchange between an American couple unfortunately confirms this observation Boycott?! Journey of May 2, 2015 train no. 6065

The train ride itself wasn't too bad. Thello sent an email at noon on the day of departure to say that the 8 PM train would depart 1 hour late, with an offer to refund if that was not acceptable. We didn't have any alternatives so we waited. And waited. It actually departed 1.5 hours late and arrived in Venice 3 Hours Late!!!  Not sure how they pulled that off, but they managed to. The sleeper car made things more comfortable, it would be hard to imagine riding for 15 hours in an open seat. The attendant that came to our cabin was pleasant, but other than being greeted at the beginning of our journey, any other service was pretty much non-existent. Upon arrival in Venice, we waited for an attendant to open the portal door so we could leave but apparently that is not part of their job description. Knowing what I know now, I would skip the Thello and find a better form of transport for this route. 180 Euros per person is no bargain with no service and 3 hours late!

We travelled from Monaco to Nice. At the entrance to the station there were ticket automats from SNCF and nothing else. There were no way to buy tickets for other companies and no sign that tickets bought on this machine were not valid on othe than SNCF trains, When we boarded the thello train our tickets were not accepted, and we had to pay thrice the price of the now defunct SNCF tickets. The thello ticketor on board the train had no sympathy for our view, and was adamant that the rather excessive amount of 15 Euro for two pensioners (instead of 6 E) had to be paid. The train was BTW late on arrival, and was far from luxurious. We will try our best to avoid this compny on future travels.

Yes, it is quite expensive to travel by TGV but what a pleasure to arrive at your destination without being the least bit tired! Paris-Marseille in 3h20.... top we traveled in 1st class ZEN atmosphere.... it's great! Room for the legs, 220 V sockets for portable devices, comfortable seats and above all, almost silence. What more can I say except that the trains we took were on time and that the controllers were in both cases very friendly. 2 trips without incident.

It is very convenient as you can go radially from Paris to major domestic and international cities. On the other hand, not all lines are high-speed, and some lines, like the mini-Shinkansen in Japan, connect to conventional lines midway through, so some lines do not have high-speed delivery considering their distance.

One of the top rail companies worldwide and certainly the best in Europe. Comfortable, fast, and in my experience, always on time. If you`re planning to visit France (or neighbouring countries), there are lot of offers and many cheap tickets to be bought throughout the year.

Every year, I plan my end-of-year vacation, usually after Christmas, and I go to a different place with my wife. This year I decided to visit the famous Trem Bala. I bought a Europass in Brazil to be used in 15 days, traced the route and went to see 5 countries. I left Paris heading to Brussels in Belgium, then headed to Frankfurt in Germany, Vienna in Austria, Zurich in Switzerland and back to Paris. It was a wonderful trip, super punctual trains and as I traveled first class the comfort was total, onboard service, optional restaurant and one thing that fascinated me, free Wi-Fi. During the trip I was able to post my photos on Facebook. Without check-inAs with most European trains, TGV trains do not require check-in. This means that the passenger can board the train they have booked without any preamble as soon as it arrives at the station. Carrying luggageThere is no official limit on the weight of luggage, so each passenger is expected to carry what they can reasonably take with them. As you can take your luggage with you, to place it in the carriage, you just have to leave it in any of the luggage racks closest to your seat.  You travel with your suitcase without the fear of it being lost. Modern stationsThe stations are more like a shopping mall, they have everything, shops, restaurants, souvenirs, ATMs, escalators, etc. The TGV (Train à Grande Vitesse) or high-speed train) is the French fast train, which can reach 300 kph on main routes, and up to 320 kph on newer routes in eastern France. It is the best and most effective way to get around Europe. You can enjoy the landscapes, work, rest, without the stress of planes and airports. I traveled through 5 countries, I didn't show my passport once, not even to get on the train. THOSE WHO DON'T KNOW, MAKE YOUR ROUTE. NOTE: The photos published are from different cities and different seasons.

This is a train equivalent to the Shinkansen in France. I used it between Paris and Geneva. I rode in first class, and the seats were in rows 2+1, and I also got a cold plate meal. I bought it in advance from the website, so it cost about 60 euros. It's a great deal if you have your itinerary decided in advance. Unlike the Shinkansen, the train is pulled by the leading locomotive, so there is little shaking even at high speeds, and I think the ride is extremely comfortable.
I traveled on this train (4/2015) on the Milan-Nice route; cold, slow train (too many stops to be in Eurocity) and 20' delay both on the outward and return journey.

We booked a premium cabin for two for the journey with some expectation that it would be better than a standard coach. (1) Cabin was extremely hot and A/C did not work properly. (2) Windows opened all night which created a very noisy, windy and smelly ride. (3) Food was honestly some of the worst we've ever experienced during travel. (4) Cabin could not be locked from the outside without an attendant, and they are very difficult to locate. Plan on wandering up & down the aisles until you find someone while your partner remains in the cabin for security. No partner? You have to leave the cabin unlocked whilst looking for an attendant. (5) Beds were okay although you must be able to climb a very narrow & rickety ladder for the top bunk...no options there. All in all, a very disappointing and excrutiating train ride that we will never repeat. We booked it because we usually fly and wanted an alternate experience. Well, it was alternate all right. We flew home, by the way...

20 min. delay in Paris l'est at the departure. Locomotive damage ... although it wasn't exchanged ... maybe it was something else ;-) no final train in D was waiting for the TGV. End of the song ... 2 hours total delay.

We buy the tickets online, and we print them in Buenos Aires. We made the trip from Paris to Colmar. Both departure and arrival super-punctual. The trip was very comfortable. Since there are many trains and the frequency, you have to pay attention to the signs at the station to know which platform and what time the train leaves, then on the ticket there is the indication of the car. Inside the train there is sometimes not much space to store suitcases, so whoever boards first always has the possibility of storing their bags in the place of their choice.

What can I say... it's true that the return train from Paris to Turin broke down after Lyon, with a consequent delay that foreshadowed an odyssey... ended up with 11 hours of travel... but one thing must be said... during the journey we were given the letter requesting a refund and after 4 months, the refund arrived, and even more than what one could normally expect... of course, you pay more for the TGV than the normal train, but if this is the guarantee... gentlemen... I challenge you to do something like this in Italy...

We took metro line 5 to the Gare du Nord, which we only saw from below. In the international sector we took a TGV from the SNCF company, the Eurostar, to London. We did the immigration procedures with very friendly employees (coincidence?), we went down the escalator to the platform and found the car easily because everything is well signposted. The train is ugly on the outside, but on the inside it is much better and comfortable, even though it was tourist class. The trip was pleasant without any problems and we arrived in approximately 2 hours at the beautiful St. Pancras Station.

We used the Thello for a 5-day stay in Paris: departure from Vicenza. We booked four months in advance and this allowed us to take advantage of very advantageous rates (€70 each return). The fact that we were traveling with six people (including two children) allowed us to have a compartment just for us. As the main positive aspect, I would point out the convenience of the solution (arriving in Paris in the morning and leaving in the evening allow you to make full use of all the days of your stay). Both on the outward and return journey the train was punctual and the staff very courteous. However, I consider the quality of the carriages, compartments and services to be very poor. Bathroom doors that are difficult to close, toilet lids that come off their hinges, lack of hangers, clogged sinks. In the compartment the reading lights did not work (except one), the possibility of regulating the temperature in the compartments is non-existent, the pillows were terrible and there were many other things to criticize. It is true that the carriages are at least thirty years old but a little maintenance is essential.

I left by TGV from Lyon station towards Nice for a first class return trip. Very disappointed by the lack of hygiene on the windows. I also went to the bar to buy a meal for €17.90 in glasses; the piece of bread given to me contained apricot jam. So I went to see the very unpleasant, unprofessional waiter, he had absolutely nothing to do with it. I do not recommend taking the TGV towards Nice, which is very expensive for the lack of service and quality that is provided. . . From a very disappointed customer

The trip takes around 2:15 hours between Paris and London. There can be delays at departures or problems during the ride. But it is usually on time. The coaches are comfortable. Depending on the season and how early you book your tickets (preferably on the Eurostar or the SNCF websites).It is so much faster and cheaper than by plane (if you don't fly with Rynair which lands in an inconvenient airport so far away from Paris).The Paris Gare du Nord is old and dirty. The first floor area for Eurostar passenger is better, but it still takes sometimes a few long minutes to pass emigration and police security checks. Then, the waiting area before boarding the train is quite small and crowded.Saint Pancras station is London is so much more attractive, spacious, efficient.

We were in Paris for several days and then had to travel to Lille & Lyon and then back to Paris. The TGV was the only way to travel, hop aboard, relax in comfy seats and zoom to the next town! Very nice way to travel.

Brescia - Paris trip, luckily one way (return by plane). We didn't experience any faults but the 3-seater sleeping cabins were below expectations and above all not adequate for the price paid. Very cramped, not exactly clean, breakfast to forget, not soundproofed at all, staff not up to par. It's a shame because traveling by train is beautiful and at least the last part towards Paris we enjoyed the scenery
I did a Lille - Montpellier on April 7 and everything went well. The staff was friendly, the TGV was on time, cleanliness was OK. The food is good but a bit expensive.

We love Paris and we don't mind reaching it by train at all. We take the Thello sleeper train from Milan in a double sleeper cabin and vice versa from Gare de Lyon usually once a year. We have always found punctuality, extreme cleanliness and comfort in the beds and in general in the cabins, always well equipped even in the toilet department. The staff were courteous and helpful. The shared bathrooms have always been supplied with water and paper, but use and maintenance by users is another thing... The bar-restaurant service is more than acceptable. The last time then (on the evening of April 6th when we left Paris) we particularly enjoyed the dinner and the kindness of the lady who served it. We can only thank you.

I have been traveling by TGV for years, generally in 1st class. I make at least 3 or 4 return trips per month, which earns me the “frequent flyer” card. I can no longer count the problems: - Dirty car, even in first gear - Delays for aberrant reasons, such as "preparing the train" - Connection breaks sometimes within 1 minute.... Once in Marseille the passengers of a TER ran towards the TGV connection still at the platform; However, the staff closed the entry barriers to the platform, preventing customers from accessing a TGV which was still on the platform for 2 minutes! - The controllers are not very courteous or even downright rude towards customers. - Many journeys standing (with a 1st ticket!) due to overload/broken connections. Not to mention the strikes... Ultimately, the SNCF never provides compensation for the services it sells but does not provide. On the other hand, when I forget my reduction card (which I have and is valid), I am systematically "regularized" at the full price, with a €10 deduction. Suffice it to say that the customer is just good to pay and shut up. I recently tried to obtain compensation after a rather lousy journey (broken connection, standing in 1st gear, late arrival), but I was brushed off by customer service. Since then I have favored carpooling and flying as much as possible.

Getting on this train is quite an experience. Check-in is similar to that of an airport, with a free shop included. Super punctual, comfortable and with a ride so smooth that you don't even feel the speed. The Eurotunnel passed so quickly that it was only when I saw the GPS that I realized I was already in England... Excellent... without a doubt, for this route it is a better option than a plane.

It will cover more than 800km in 3 hours and 17 minutes. There are two stops along the way: Avignon and Aix-en-Provence in southern France. Even when the maximum speed of 320 km/h is displayed, there is no shaking and the seats are spacious and comfortable.

We took the train with my family to reach Paris and despite not being a regular on trains I found this solution quite convenient. For us who, living in Mantua, had to travel to Milan to pick it up, it wasn't very convenient because we had to arrive by car and park, the time involved was quite considerable but the journey itself was quite comfortable. The train left right on time and even arrived 10 minutes early. We made the outward journey in first class and the return journey in second class and I must say that apart from the slightly more spacious seats in first class we didn't find much difference, so to save some money you can opt to both go and return in second class.

I traveled from Paris to Lyon by TGV, the train was on time, the quality of the carriages is satisfactory, that said the seats are starting to look old and the carpet is not dusted enough. it's still better than the plane so to do

We are Canadians living in the ME.  We tried to book tickests on TGV for travel within France this summer.  RailEurope demanded that my wife send via fax photocopies of her passport and both sides of her credit card used to purchase the tickets before they even attempted to use the card to actually get paid for the tickets!  A call to our bank confirmed that RailEurope had never even attempted to use the card to pay for the rail tickets.  Smells like a scam to me.We told them to cancel our reservation and that we would never, ever, ever recommend that anyone ever use RailEurope.  Mission complete.We went on the SNCF site, called the reservation line and was helped by a very friendly representative, tickets were booked with no issues.I would give NEGATIVE 5 STAR rating if I could .......

we left Vicenza for Paris on 31/3/15 in the evening with 4 adults, very dirty bunks, bathrooms that were dirty to say the least, very smelly and without water!!!!, dusty linen, stained blankets: terrible experience. Upon returning from Paris on the 5th/4th evening our berths booked at least a month before had also been assigned to other people.... NEVER A SIMILAR INDECENCE AGAIN

We bought tickets from Reims to Paris and back, and following the information provided in various places, we took the Reims tram to the outskirts to the TGV station officially called Champagne-Ardenne.  There we were told that our train was from the station in the centre of Reims.  So the first tip is - check your stations very carefully!  The guard at Champagne-Ardenne station was excellent and arranged for us to go on the next TGV from there which was only 15 minutes later.  Our journey was comfortable, pleasant and impressively fast.  If only other rail systems could be like this.

The rating I give to this train is unacceptable. We left for a few days on a family trip to Paris. We booked the four-seater sleeping carriage (at a cost comparable to that of the plane ticket). We found a train with old, badly damaged and very noisy carriages, but what is absolutely unacceptable is the general disrepair of the carriage and the dirtiness of the bed linen. In conclusion, I urge the managers of the Thello train to examine their consciences (or take a ride on their train to understand its condition) and to completely rethink the service, given that the idea of the train, which uses the night for transfers, is very good and very competitive compared to the plane, making it easier for Italians to visit Paris and vice versa.

tgv Turin/Paris and return1 class assigned seats, booked online a month ago with a really convenient rate. Nothing to complain about: perfect time both on the outward and return journey. It's true it may be a little dated but the seats are comfortable, wide and reclining. Possibility of having breakfast or lunch either at your seat or in the restaurant car. Checks and police on board, which isn't a bad thing!! I'm more than satisfied and if I were to return to Paris, I'd go with the TGV without a shadow of a doubt... But do you want to have the convenience of avoiding check-ins and booking transport to the city center??Take it easy: here you arrive at the Gare de Lyon from where the main metro or RER depart...👍

I used the TGV and the THALYS, they are both the same. Very good speed and easy movement between countries. I went in second class and it was super quiet. If you buy with a better tariff category the WIFI is free.

A very convenient and inexpensive (especially if you buy tickets in advance) form of transport. Many years ago I traveled from Lyon to Paris, my memories are vague... But in June 2014 we took a ride from Paris to Saint-Malo and back. Very comfortable and fast! I bought the ticket online 3 months in advance and paid by card. The ticket cost 30 euros; closer to the travel date there are more expensive tickets (other fares) - about 80 euros. I would be happy to use the TGV for other trips around France!

My wife and I took the Eurostar from London to Paris in August.First time on the train and it was great. The trip took about two hours. The train itself travelled about 200mph until we hit the tunnel and then it slowed down. I hadn't even realized we had gone through tunnel. Mainly because the train goes under so many bridges and underpasses it didn't dawn on me. I didn't know we had reached Paris either until the train stopped at the station. Once the train passes into France, overhead announcements were made in French.Immigration was a bit confusing. Passport was stamped at St Pancreas as we boarded. So when you get to Paris, you just take your things and leave. Which to me was a little confusing as I expected to have to show my passport when I arrived in France not before. Returning wasn't too bad but did take bit longer though. My wife and I were questioned why we were coming back into UK. But it was all just formalities. One lady in front of us I think was denied entry because of a Visa or passport issue so that actually held up the line.Make sure you fill out the declaration card before approaching the checkin desk. It will save time. Gare du Nord isn't a very spectacular place to hang around. A lot of it seemed dated and old. The Eurostar checkin was upstairs and easiest way to get to it was by a Lift tucked away in the back of the station.
It's almost like a plane (exaggeration), but it's very fast, unique comfort, extremely high-quality service, breathtaking landscapes along the way.

I took the train from Paris last night 03/26/2015 to return to Milan. Departure scheduled for 7.59pm, arrival in Milan at 6.00am. The train still hadn't left at 10pm. They make us all get out on the platform in the cold around 10.30pm and tell us that they have to replace the locomotive. Not even a bench to sit on or the possibility of indoor shelter. The cold in the bones! The train finally arrives at 1am and leaves at 1.15am. It arrives in Milan at 12.00pm with 6 hours of delay. I queue for more than an hour at the Trenitalia ticket office for the refund of the ticket, which was done on the Trenitalia website, and they give me a thello form telling me to go to the agency which is close to the central station where I am.....maybe I haven't complained enough if they have the courage to do this to me proposal....

This review concerns  TGV Lyria from Paris Gare de Lyon to Mulhouse.Part of the problem is that the TGV is held out as a great service - and this really wasn't. In one day we travelled from Sunderland to London via Grand Central, London to Paris via Eurostar and then this trip on the TGV. And the only one that was late was ? Yep, the TGV.But there were other things too. We were travelling first class where food was included, and the announcements at the start of the journey advised us that light snacks would be served at our seats. We are still waiting. I had read other reviews saying that TGV Lyria had a habit of either 'forgetting' the meals or claiming that the time was wrong. My advice is to take sandwiches.First class seats are very comfortable, but the carriages themselves are nothing special in  terms of décor or comfort. It's nothing better than you'd get anywhere else in Europe. To my mind is a train that is let down by comparison to its reputation rather than by matching or even approaching it. The trip was no better than average and that's me being generous.
We really enjoyed the trip as it was fast and comfortable. Only downside was the flat, French countryside as we are used to the mountains and valleys of Wales.

(Normally) We board the aircraft, see clouds, get off the other side.  Assuming the airport is efficient, it's generally the quickest mode of transport for international travel.  BUT if you fly, you don't see the country(s) you're travelling through.  So we thought we'd try a trip across France by high-speed train.  The TGV is in a different league to our trains here in the UK (and believe me, I know how crappy our trains are, having commuted 4 hours a day for 5 years). The TGV cruises at c.180MPH (I checked the GPS - very satisfying), it's smooth, roomy and surprisingly quiet.   And people behave themselves; they actually go out of the main carriage to make those annoying phone calls.Worth a try if you want to see more of the journey.

The TGV (High Speed ​​Trains) operate mainly within French territory. TGV's leave from all over France to the main cities in continental Europe. The detail is that, while traveling along the French tracks, trains can reach speeds of up to 300km/h. However, once they cross the borders, they slow down a little. This is due to the fact that the tracks in countries outside of France are not yet fully adapted to the TGV system. For example, a trip I took by train from Madrid, Spain, to Paris. From Madrid to Hyundai, on the border with France, the trip was quite boring, tiring and jolting, due to the traditional Spanish trails. From Hyundai we took the French TGV. Honestly, there is no comparison!!! In addition to being fast, it is much more "soft" and comfortable.....without those "jolts" of common trains. It is still the best way to travel between France and other European countries (except for the United Kingdom, of course, which has the Eurostar, which is much faster). Tickets are not cheap. Prices are charged according to the mileage to be covered. Still, if purchased well in advance it is possible to get very affordable prices. And for young people up to 26 years old and adults over 60 years old, there are special prices, that is, much more affordable!

So if it is worth traveling by train, it is like a bullet, it leaves at the indicated time exactly. I took the Paris Lyon trip with incredible comfort but it has other routes. Very well cared for and maintained, it goes on air mattresses.
Last October on first class TGV between Nice and Paris NO WIFI. Today we are on a bus between Essaouira and Marrakech in Morocco WITH WIFI. Which is the most sophisticated?
The rest of the world could learn a lot from this most pleasurable way to travel within France. The only way to travel.

Round trip in 1st Class for a Paris Lyon. On the way there, no heating in the carriage (broken). I'm not naturally cold, but I spent the entire trip with my jacket as a blanket. Maintaining a train without heating in winter...On the way back, a repulsively dirty carriage, I hesitated to sit on the seat. Incidentally, I had never seen this type of seat which was totally uncomfortable. Incidentally, having access to the internet in the 21st century seems impossible for the SNCF... The days of "SNCF is possible" and the French technological flagship are long gone! In short, I think I'm going to stop paying for a 1st class which isn't one and stop the TGV altogether.

The worst train trip I've ever taken, which is no small feat considering I often travel with Trenitalia. However, the TGV taken in January 2015 has no space for luggage, much less for strollers, it is always full as they accept people without a seat so you really don't know where to put your luggage. It's slow rather than a fast train, I use less by car on the same route and it's always late.

I took the Paris-Milan route leaving Gare de Lyon. The route is fast and reaches high speeds in the French countryside. It slows down only when crossing the Alps. Little difference between first and second class.

I was in first class and had Duo seats (single seats or facing each other). It was quieter than I expected, with little shaking, and although the train was fairly full, it was quiet and comfortable. Also, each seat has a power source, so I was able to charge my tablet and cell phone, which was helpful. However, the sink in the toilet didn't seem to flush, and the overflowing water flowed into the hallway, flooding the area.

We were driving from Mannheim, Germany to Paris, France and back from there to Karlsruhe, Germany. Prices were okay, but we booked a little bit too late so they could have been less expensive. You have your own pre-reserved seat and they are very comfortable, too.Very fast-going and silent and also punctually.Recommend.

I have wanted to try a TGV for decades, so when we wanted to visit Paris from Frankfurt it was a no-brainer to go by TGV.  The train we took was clean and solid, with huge windows so we did not miss a thing. I was surprised to find we were moving, as it was smooth and silent.  In fact, it remained soundless (except for people chatting, and the occasional noise of the air-conditioning fans) even when we were doing well over 100 miles per hour.  I took a video, and as the scenery flashed by, I could clearly hear the crinkling sound as my wife opened a paper bag six feet away. Eerie and delightful, especially when contrasted with the oppressive thunder of a jet aircraft. Much more relaxing.When we entered France, the ride got a bit less smooth, but remained very quiet due to the magnetic suspension used. The broad grain fields reminded me of the Canadian prairies, except for the big stone church spires in stead of grain elevators.We got to Gare de L'Est on time, relaxed and happy. It was much nicer than a flight would have been, although our first class tickets may have been a bit more expensive than a bargain airline.We enjoyed the ability to just walk on and walk off, with no security hassles at either end.Highly recommended!

We did the Amsterdam-Paris route, a trip of just over 3 hours. The journey was peaceful, with beautiful landscapes. The ticket price was cheap, in addition to boarding/disembarking access being much easier and faster than on a plane trip, with the advantage of boarding/disembarking in the city center. Great option for transport between not so distant countries in Europe.

The route we took was Paris Bordeaux and Bordeaux Paris, all in just one day, despite the distance it was very comfortable, I would just recommend a restaurant with more options, as we left at dinner time, but despite few options, dinner was great.

The service was very reliable, super efficient checking in, very fast. Couple of things like wifi, much faster buffet service would make the journey better. Seats looking a bit tired, but comfortable, clever design on headrests so can sleep. Not so cheap at £270 for two people short stay in Paris but much quicker than flying. Being organised and booking ahead is the way.

We took the routes Amsterdam/Paris (35.00 euros per pax) and Paris/London (50.00 euros per pax) in TGV. We have already left Brazil with all tickets guaranteed through the official raileurope website. It is synonymous with comfort, practicality and safety. An excellent service. It's much better than taking the air journey, as the view is very beautiful. Highly recommended.

Japanese people think that the Shinkansen is the best in the world, and I thought so too, but even though it is faster than the Shinkansen, there is almost no shaking. TGV might be better for driving. The sheets were a little dirty though.

On my wish list was a journey to Nice by train 1st class from Edinburgh .We began the journey with tremendous help and support as I was suffering from a spinal condition and the staff on the Caledonian sleeper where fantastic . Again Eurostar couldn't have given us more attention , loading luggage and ensuring I was comfortable . Unfortunately at the Gare de Lyon there were no attendants to assist and my wife had to manage our cases to the upper deck of the Duplex . There are no complimentaries inspite of the 180 euros you pay for first class apart from having an upper level seat . The on-board 'snack-bar' was very limited and run out of stock before Lyon. I would never recommend 1st class ,a complete waste of money
Fast, clean, and incredibly convenient, almost like in Japan! And if you don’t take 1st grade, then you can do it on a budget.

If you have ever ridden in a Japanese bullet train or any Japanese train you would laugh at these trains. I really have nothing good to say about them aside that we didn't die In a crash. The trains are filthy inside and out, black soot and pealing paint. Seats are thread bare and mismatched colors. We had "first class" tickets from Paris to Milan via Geneve. The first leg was TGV and cost  $600 for two adults. As I said dirty thread bare mismatched seats. Your service consisted of a bag of dried fruit and a drink in a plastic cup. Be aware that not all window seats actually have a window or only about 6" of window and the remaining is wall. The TGV toilets are small and dirty. The train from Geneve to Milan was cleaner but service was mediocre at best. For $580 USD for two you might expect something. Also, why did I pay almost $600 for tickets and have two coach class passengers come up and take two seats. No train crew to fix this issue. We are the only two passengers in first class, these two came up between stops and after they punched the tickets. One of the bathroom doors didn't lock. The announcements stopped being bilingual for some weird reason as well. When it was in French it was a 1-2 minute dialog, English about 5 seconds. What gives to lazy to do your job correctly?  Also, as far as "bullet" train is concerned we hit 180mph for less then an hour, the rest was much slower. Rode on a Italian Trenitalia over night train, that's a whole other story and review to come.
I love French railways)) Honestly! We traveled all over the country by train. I really liked it. Tickets were purchased through the website and paid by card. Comfortable.
We have always had a good time. Fairly on time, and with good prices if booked in advance. For the rest we are fine

It was the first time I took the TGV from Turin to go to Paris, the experience didn't start well because it arrived 20 minutes late but once on I found the seats and cleanliness satisfactory. For a high-speed train it makes too many stops and was unable to make up for the delay, in fact it accumulated even more delays, arriving 40 minutes after the scheduled time but the convenience of arriving directly in the city center is certainly the strong point of using the TGV compared to the plane.

The TGV (Train a Grande Vitesse) is the high speed train network that allows you to travel across France in comfort, fast and in an affordable manner. Highly recommended for trips between cities when you visit France. More reliable than the flights, with more time options on schedule as well.

We recently took the tgv from Munich to Paris and it was amazing, as a Canadian it was my first time on a high speed train and they didn't disappoint at all. We opted for the first class option which I highly recommend for the small increase in price, the seats and space rival most Airlines and were very comfortable and spacious. The food was decent as well. We really enjoyed the scenery and how smooth the train was. Will for sure use this service again
A pleasure to travel on these trains, they leave on time, they are very fast, clean, there is space for suitcases, the truth is that we are light years away from this...

A luxury, departure on time, very fast, clean, large space for suitcases, used to the San Martín line with the train full, with people traveling hanging and smoking joint and drinking wine in the bike car, this is a luxury.

This was Awesome. Our party of four traveled from Paris Gare de Lyon through to Nice. Total travel time was 4.5HRS & enjoyed every minute of it. We booked & paid for our tickets in Australia before we left with Rail Europe & each passenger was only 15 Euros. ???? So cheap. Couldn't even drive a car down there for that Price. TGV 6175 was our service & had  seats 95,96,97,98 which where upstairs. Excellent views of the French countryside & although it probably took 3 times as long as flying, it was so much better. Food & beverages available fro purchase on board the train as well as bathroom facilities. We had four backpacks, four day packs & a walking aid & there was ample room to store it. Didn't seem to have any indication of theft but, it was the cooler part of the year so not as busy. Clean & tidy carriages & seats are very comfortable. The trip back from Nice was just as good & the weather was a little bit better so got to see a little bit more scenery. If you book in your home country the price is heaps cheaper & I even got two prepaid SIM cards each time I booked :) If you have walking difficulties, make sure you advise of it when booking. This will ensure you are in the lower section of the carriage & not up in the second level as there is stairs to climb( see photos)

Wonderful train, which really runs on time, is clean, arrives on time, travels at an incredible speed, it's worth the trip, but depending on whether you leave it to buy at the last minute, it can be quite expensive.

I have traveled on high-speed trains in France many times.  I would like to immediately note that trains to the UK are called Eurostar, and trains from the North Station to Belgium, Holland and Germany are called Talis.  And TGVs cover distances throughout France.  I recommend registering in advance on the TGV website; you can receive notifications about discounts and promotions by email.  I aimed to buy tickets 90 days in advance as soon as the sale opens.  Then you can grab tickets at the lowest price.  It is worth considering that such tickets cannot be returned or changed.  But if you have clear travel plans, as I had, then feel free to buy tickets.  On the day of departure, prices may be several times higher.
First class left a little to be desired..., old carriage structure and a little noisy with old finishes, but overall functional.
TGV is probably one of the fastest and best ways to travel between cities in France. No problem, free to relax or work if you want to.

One of the best options for traveling! Good prices, fast and comfortable trips! High-speed trains (TGV-Tren grand vitesse) are the best options for traveling in France. My experience with this means of transport was wonderful. It has a restaurant, comfortable bathroom, small but comfortable, accommodation for luggage and great service! It's worth trying

TGV was a first hand experience for me. Traveled in 2nd class, which was great and very comfortable. Everyone in our group fell asleep on the ride because the seats were really that comfortable.Passing the beautiful country side of Belgium and France, this was one of the most memorable trips.TIP : Book well in advance, you might be lucky to get a 1st class fare for price of regular 2nd class...

Excellent, speedy service. However, when we got to our *reserved* seats, they were occupied by 4 men who were dressed like businessmen.  Underneath the nice clothes, however, they were pigs.  We showed them that they were sitting in our seats and they just sneered.  Luckily, the conductor came by and asked what the problem was and after seeing our tickets and the men's lack of tickets for those seats, he kicked them out of our seats.  Otherwise, the trip was very nice.
My two sons enjoyed this train journey from Lyons to Paris after changing from Eurostar. It was a smooth, quiet and comfortable journey and we had no complaints at all.

We booked tickets from Rome to Paris with a brief stop in Milan to change trains. The first leg was on an Italian Trenitalia Frecciarossa train in business class. It was quite comfortable with big leather seats, free Wifi, etc.The second leg however, from Milan to Paris, was on a French TGV train in First Class (they didn't offer business class). We were incredibly disappointed! The seats were fabric and looked about like you would expect fabric seats would look on public transportation. They were worn, filthy and threadbare. The seats had plenty of room but they were disgustingly dirty and incredibly uncomfortable. We took the train because we thought it would be a great way to see the countryside and try out the famous European railway system. We were happy with the Trenitalia train but the TGV was a major disappointment. Certainly a train ticket is less expensive and you have ample room to move around, but they really don't have a First Class experience to offer on the TGV trains.Even more disappointing were the restrooms. They were as small as an aircraft toilet and about as clean as a parking lot Port O' John at a football game.I am not saying that it is a bad way to travel, just that you should temper your expectations of the level of "Luxury" you expect in First Class. Luxury and service, really don't exist on these trains. It is really just a question of "do you want a bigger nasty seat (first class) or a smaller nasty seat (coach)".

I don't understand why the reviews of Thello and Tgv are mixed here and there is a risk of confusion.  In fact I was a little scared before leaving. I took the TGV from Turin, return price, 110 euros per person. The train certainly aesthetically and also internally does not give that feeling of a latest generation high-speed train. But the data speaks clearly. We left Turin right on time and in less than 6 hours we arrived split second in the center of Paris. Inside, despite being full, it was clean, comfortable and quiet. Same thing on the way back. Punctuality as on the outward journey, in fact we arrived 4 minutes early, something that, as a daily Trenitalia customer (which ALWAYS accumulates delays for infinitely shorter journeys), I wasn't really used to. Nothing to say...

I traveled with my wife on January 1st to go to Paris, first class and seats 51.52 Face to Face, the train is now dated, the upholstery and seats are very worn and cleaning takes a little time, the reduced speed and too many stops, even unexpected ones, lead to a bit of boredom even if it must be said that after Lyon you "fly" at over three hundred an hour, the bar service although a little expensive ( 5.40 euros for two hot teas) highlights a very kind and competent staff. The ticket price is a little expensive even if booked more than a month in advance, on the return on January 5th it was even early. I chose the TGV as an alternative to the plane to get to Paris directly in the heart of the city and all in all there are more pros than cons, with hindsight we realize that by getting on this means of transport we enter, accepting it or not, into the philosophy of life of Grandeur...which sometimes does not reflect ours

Riding the train is the best way to get around Europe, and if you can, be sure to opt for first class. From Paris/London, vice versa or any other destination is much more practical than facing the stress of airports.
The TVG would have to be the better way to travel with comfort an speed.  The catering car too offers great coffee to enjoy while watching the French countryside pass by.

The TGV is one of the great railroads of the world for its reliability, speed, comfort, technological sophistication, and safety.  If you live in America where train travel is thought to be for the other people, take a ride on the TGV and ask yourself if you would like to have such a system in the US.  For certain distances it sure beats flying or driving.  Go first class if you can, but second is nice, too.

we must clearly distinguish between tgv and thello, about which I read many negative comments. I'm from Turin and we're lucky enough that the actual TGV leaves from us. Punctual, convenient, 5.20 and you're in Paris. A little expensive in the bar car, but kind. I traveled with an 11 month old baby and I didn't have any problems.

We took the TGV from Paris to Annecy, a eastern town in France adjoining Switzerland. I think it is the BEST way to travel across France, travels at amzing speed and very comfortable and very quite inside.

Smooth journey from Paris to Strasbourg, very good first class carriage, compared to the Talys, from Amsterdam to Paris, the quality is lower. There is no wi-fi, they do not serve appetizers or snacks in first class. And I had the misfortune to get the last chair, with little space to recline.

Great travel experience!   I wanted to go from Paris to Barcelona when I had a free weekend on a trip for work.   Loved it!   I got to see a lot of French and some Spanish countryside.  The train stations have connections to the metro and bus, so makes it easy to continue to one's final destaination.
Absolutely not to be repeated! Dirty and old trains, unusable floors. Tickets too expensive for the service offered.

Only 2.5 hours from Nimes (this is Languedoc, the very south of France) - it’s wonderful! With gorgeous views, a power outlet, wide armchairs, and if you’re lucky, Wi-Fi for a little money. And this is just one example. Moreover, if you bother in advance, you can buy euros for 30 (I bought for 38, but for first class). In general, the railways of France are gorgeous.

I Took the TGV from Paris to Lillie.  Booked trip on line in advance for approximately €45 per person. Very pleasant and quick trip, about 50.minutes.  Paris nortd station was within walking distance of our Paris hotel, and lille station was near shops and restaurants.  The TGV made a one day trip very doable.

I took the TGV in 2nd class from Turin to Paris for the first time because it cost less than the plane and had the timetable I needed. I paid around 70 euros for the outward journey (excellent) and I enjoyed reasonable comfort on board although I was disappointed by the lack of a wireless network and the quality of the bar which offers sandwiches for 7 euros that seem to be made of rubber. I could understand the price but at least they are excellent, otherwise ... This trip however made me understand the need for the high-speed railway as in the Turin - Lyon section the train travels almost at the speed of a local. I imagine that with the high-speed railway you would get to Paris in about 1.5 hours less, which is no small thing
The train is quiet and safe, as well as being punctual. For trips of up to medium distances, it is undoubtedly the best option. Easy to get on and off. Buy in advance online, it is more advantageous.

shameful, dirty carriages, torn seats, filthy and smelly carpets. Plus you buy tickets online, choose your seat facing forward.... But you find yourself positioned exactly opposite to the one you purchased. Prices not adequate for the service, to pay for high speed from Paris to Lyon and the rest from Lyon to Milan similar to a regional one! Compliments !

Seventies carriages, seats for six which then become four and also not too comfortable, air conditioning stuck on the cold in December, dilapidated and unusable bathrooms. The real problem is the passengers who also illegally occupy the rest of the carriage. A mix of the worst that can be found among Algerians and Tunisians (it is not racism but a factual observation given that all you have to do is go to the platform at the start which seems to be in the worst suburbs among drug dealers and street sellers of contraband cigarettes and other things) often smelly, who smoke in the carriage despite the ban. Two hours late due to various gendarmerie checks for cigarette smuggling and so on..... Too bad... With two small girls I would have preferred another company on board but despite everything they were enthusiastic about the experience, they slept well and had fun and for me this is the best. Of course it wasn't a peaceful couple of nights for us parents but anyway if you like adventure, book thello two days before leaving, spend 700 euros and good luck.....

The TGV offers a fast and pleasant way to cross Europe. The train no longer has the modern charm of a few years ago, but it guarantees that you arrive on time for appointments and enjoy a beautiful panorama of Central Europe.

In the USA passenger train transportation is not common.  However, if the TGV came to the USA then I think our mentality would change.  This was the second time I have used the TGV, and both experiences have been wonderful.  The first time we traveled 2nd class, which was great and very comfortable.  This time we upgraded to first class, and talk about really comfortable seats!  For a longer journey, this is a fine upgrade.  Almost everyone in our group fell asleep on the ride because the seats were really that comfortable.I did not fall asleep because I was looking at my GPS logger hitting 200 mph!  The fun part is that you don’t even feel like you are traveling that fast, the train is so smooth.If you want to get from one city to next, don’t bother booking a city hopper flight and definitely don’t rent a car if you are planning on staying in city centers.  This is the most effective way to get around France.

Something has really happened at the French Railways. The new TGV Lyria from Basel to Paris is more pleasant than the plane. Overall, it is the fastest connection. The prices, however, vary greatly. In 1st class you get daily newspapers, magazines and a menu served at your seat. The food is cold but surprisingly good. You can choose between 3 menus (vegi, fish, meat) and even wine and non-alcoholic drinks are included. The service is very accommodating, better than on some planes. The seats are comfortable and offer enough space even for tall people. You also have the option of using your cell phone etc. at your place. to load. After 3 hours you arrive completely relaxed, fed and on time in the middle of the city.

For me the best means of transport in France. The train is very comfortable and super fast in addition to the fact that you are already in the city center and do not need to travel from airports to the center.
We can only envy the technique... unfortunately we have a pendolino but it won't reach the same speed as this miracle... it's worth a ride... I recommend it

TGV is the acronym for Train a Grande Vitesse. A super advance and in addition to being comfortable, they are definitely fast. I remember when they opened the line to the French northeast, the journey took 5h20 to 1h10. Impressive. Sometimes first class is 1 euro or even 10 euros more. Sometimes traveling by plane is cheaper, but the advantage is that airports are usually not central and stations are. Safety, comfort and speed
I loved it, very quickly. I went from Paris to Aix. Travel quickly and comfortably. There are several destinations in France

We travelled from Paris to Biarritz.  Although it was a 5 hour journey, it was much cheaper than flying and when you don't have check-in, flight delays and transfers to and from the city it seems much faster.  We booked early in 1st class.  It wasn't that much more expensive than 2nd class, and seemed much more comfortable.  Had no problems with staff or people in reserved seats.At Paris there were two trains leaving together (maybe the trains split further down the track).  So the first carriages were numbered 11, 12 etc.  We were a bit confused when looking for car no.3, but it was in the second part of the train up front. This might help you if you encounter the same problem.

4 of us leave Milan for Paris at 6am on Monday 13 November. we've been there since 5, the doors open at 5.45. The return is scheduled for Thursday 13th at 2.41pm from Gare di Lyon. On day 13 we take a taxi to Paris just before 2pm, 10 minutes from the station. But there is a demonstration and we find ourselves in a traffic jam. The taxi driver tries an alternative route and at 2.30 pm we are in front of the station. We run, loaded with luggage, the 300 meters that separate us from platform 13, the departure point of our train. At 2.39pm we are on platform 13 but our train is not the first we come across because there is another one parked there along its entire length, so to get to ours we still have to travel the entire length of the parked train. I tell my son-in-law and my daughter, who are much younger and fitter, to speed up and go and explain to the controllers that we are coming. Meanwhile, the people waiting on another platform encourage us to run! I see my son arrive at an open door while the speaker announces that the train is about to leave. My daughter also comes in, after 15 seconds I arrive while a very insensitive attendant signals to me that it's too late. I press the button while my daughter screams and cries from the window. I scream at these inhuman little men dressed as railway soldiers, but nothing, they don't seem to want to hear of it. I kick against the door as my wife arrives in pitiful condition. I yell at my daughter to pull the emergency brake, the alarm, something, then a little man in uniform signals to me that the door of the next carriage is still open, telling me 'fast italien'. We enter the compartment and, exhausted, drenched in sweat, we collapse on the ground. My daughter joins us shortly afterwards. We made it, but you are total blockheads, inhumane and insensitive, just to leave perfectly on time. For the record, we arrived in Milan 30 minutes late, so, in addition to having demonstrated a humanity equal to Hitler, you were also incompetent at work. To conclude, I want to let you know that you put me through a very sad moment in my life. I will remember you for this. Gianluca Salvietti
1st class travel: Very uncomfortable seats, no on-site catering service (unlike the Spanish TGV), and more than questionable toilets, no cleaning of seats, aisles etc.
It was an unobstructed trip and I only made one change of trains during the route from CDG to Remis, I recommend you for trips within France as well as going to the north of France: Benelux.
One of the charms of Europe, riding one of the most efficient means of transport available in the modern world.

From the reviews I had read I was really expecting a cattle truck, but this was not the case. I traveled at night, Venice-Paris route in a T3 sleeper car: the cabin was small, sure, but clean even if old. The service includes welcome cocktail (juice or champagne) and free breakfast for those staying in sleeping cars. The breakfast was good and plentiful, the staff was mainly French but kind and helpful. The journey takes quite a while but it is totally liveable, I slept many hours peacefully. The only delay was on the outward journey, about an hour and a half. Overall good service, advisable for those who prefer not to take the plane.

I took a non-stop train from the TGV station on the outskirts of Avignon to Gare de Lyon in Paris. The flight departs at 17:40 and arrives at Gare de Lyon in Paris at 8:00 pm. The required time is 2 hours and 40 minutes. Avignon TGV station was built in 2001, and up until then the main way to travel to Paris was by plane, but now there has been a big shift to traveling by TGV. It is a TGV-only station with a modern design, and there are no transfers to conventional lines, so most people are heading to Paris or Marseille or Nice in the opposite direction. After arriving in Paris, I didn't have the energy to go out to eat, so I bought a sandwich and a cake for dessert at the station shop before getting on the train. The sandwiches were sold by Eric Kaiser and we were able to enjoy them in the car. Many French people were eating sandwiches in their cars, and of course they were eating with open bottles of wine. In France, where dogs have citizenship, dogs are not confined to cages, but rather lay quietly at their owners' feet, even while their owners are eating. There were no loud conversations involving alcohol, which you sometimes see in Japan, and everyone was talking in hushed tones, and the car was quiet. Of course, there were also vehicles selling sandwiches, drinks (alcohol, coffee), and sweets, so it was quite busy.
very cheap and quick alternative; right in the center; for €80.00 H/R from Cologne is an unbeatable price! Always my pleasure...

I made a reservation online in Japan, printed out an e-ticket, and brought it with me. It is very convenient as there is no need to spend time and effort to purchase at a local counter. I arrived at Gare de Lyon 30 minutes before departure, but the departure platform number did not appear on the electronic display board, so many people were waiting under the electronic display board. When it is displayed 10 minutes ago, people are moving all at once. I took the train from Gare de Lyon to Gare de Lyon in Paris and it was very comfortable.

We were traveling from Germany to Paris and the TGV was more stylish inside than the German trains. The landscape through the window merges due to speed. It is better to buy tickets for long distances several months in advance, there will be significant savings.
