I took the TGV from Dijon to Paris and reserved two first class seats as we had big luggage and thought it would be more convenient to pay a bit more for the comfort.  To our surprise, when we boarded, our seats were occupied and there was no conductor to enforce seating.  We ended up having to stand the entire trip which was extremely disappointing as we have travelled on similar train services in Spain, Italy and Portugal without encountering this kind of incompetence.  I strongly recommend not wasting money on anything other than 2nd class.PS:  when we lodged a complaint we were simply told that we had already taken the trip.  Don't expect anything resembling decent customer service from SNCF

we took the TGV from Basel to Paris. Clean and efficient train (but we were used to super clean swiss rail system by then, so TGV was not that special). Seats will have 2 numbers displayed. The one where the light is on is the actual number for the seat (for this visit). The compartment number is again displayed in a tiny panel near the door. Given that TGV stops only for few minutes, please be there where your coach is likely to stop - as displayed in the platform. Booked the seat using Capitaine site. Got it for Euros 23 one way for adult.

Excellent trip. We bought first class in advance so the price was very similar to the second class ticket. We reserved seats on the second floor. We carried our suitcases up without any problem, there is plenty of space to leave them, even between the seats. The seats are comfortable and spacious and the tables have a lamp that even makes the trip romantic. They serve a snack - lunch with the possibility of having wine or beer (I wasn't hungry, but it was a light lunch) and there is a dining car where you can buy more things. A top fact: They sell metro tickets in the dining car, so that when you arrive in Paris you don't have to go buy tickets but you already have them in your hand. Save time and hassle, excellent!

we go to Paris 3 to 4 times a year, always taking the TGV. Excellent means of transport which takes us from the French-speaking Switzerland border to Paris in 3 hours. In 2nd class we are a little cramped, but the seats are comfortable, with PC sockets. In 1st class a menu is served instead, not extraordinary but correct, price of the meal included in the ticket. The seats are more comfortable as is the space. If you buy your tickets well in advance, the prices are very attractive.

My experience was good, the train was on time. Obviously the journey is longer than the plane but I wanted to try this experience because as a child the TGV train was one of my favorite toys... :-)And by booking 4 months in advance I was only able to pay 29 euros for the ticket.

we travelled from Paris to Perpignan and our bag got stolen , someone had got off with our bag and there is no much help from staf or information given in advanced on the security system or cctv because ther is non. All the answer from staf was that the bag was gone and ther was not anything they could do. At least warn people about this because it seems to be feequent as other passengers told us. althougth it was a good journey I will recommend to keep your stuff with you, because if you put them in the lugagge rack they will be stolen and no one to help. Finding your seat is not easy a bit complicated.

A little skeptical, I had to book a trip for me and my family to Paris, on the motte train. Unfortunately, my father doesn't want to know about the plane and therefore, 12 hours were waiting for me, and I was expecting hell... Instead... We arrived at the station in Venice at 8, changed trains, got on the TGV, left our documents with a ticket inspector so that during the checks in Switzerland we could sleep peacefully while they checked our documents. Once we got on the train, our berth was for 6 people but booked all for us, at a gift price (€100 return each). As soon as we entered we sat down, each of us had a bottle of still water. The bunk was clean, there were sealed sheets for each of us. We sat down, the journey began. We were very comfortable, little noise. When it was time to sleep, we made the beds and lay down. First of all we locked the door, but not only with the key integrated into the door which can be easily tampered with from the outside, but with some wire... and we did well! Around Switzerland, the train suddenly stopped in the middle of nowhere: three guys, after having cleaned the bunks, stopped the train by pulling the lever and ran away into the middle of the fields. Here, this is the only flaw, but if you get some wire and close the curtains so that they don't see you from the stopping stations and point at you, you can sleep peacefully... At 7.15am they woke us up by knocking on the door and handing us back our documents, at 7.45 I began to see the tower: really fantastic! I RECOMMEND IT

My husband and I had to celebrate our wedding anniversary and we booked this train to Paris Gare de Lion, paid 240 euros...Arrived at Milan Central two hours late, already packed with people, non-EU citizens with suitcases and bags that were probably moving from Italy...Dirty, smelly and impossible to get on board!The berth booked by me and my husband occupied by 20 suitcases and bags of these people displaced in short. We had to get off and we gave up going to Paris. Anniversary ruined and 450 euros thrown away. We asked for a refund from Thello von letter from my lawyer. SUPPRESS THIS INDECENT TRAIN because it is not in a condition to travel.

We chose to make our way to Venice from Scotland by rail - and enjoyed every minute of the trip. Having stayed in Paris after the first leg (Edinburgh-London, Eurostar to Paris), we made our way to Gare du Lyon to take the 6.41am to Milan.  We travelled First Class, having booked well in advance the difference between the price of First and Standard was minimal.  The train left on time; the journey was very comfortable with plenty of leg-room; adequate luggage storage; purchased coffee from the café-bar (very good); was offered at-seat breakfast, which we declined but opted for the at-seat lunch.  For Euro14 we had a delicious Caprese salad, bread sticks, apricot mousse and a third-bottle of wine - plenty of choices had we wanted something else.  Most importantly - the scenery outside the window was fantastic and we arrived in Milan on time!   Highly recommended.

We chose to go to Paris by train, via the TGV which leaves from Milan. First of all, the work of SNCF in resolving the emergency that had arisen due to a landslide on the line near Modane was commendable. Given the problem, they quickly put us on a bus from Milan to Modane, so considering the unexpected situation, we arrived in Parigni less than an hour late. I challenge you to know what would have happened if such an emergency had been managed by Trenitalia... The journey overall is relaxing and interesting for those who love to savor the landscapes they pass through and don't want to find themselves simply catapulted from point A to point B by plane. The train is very comfortable, especially in first class. Unfortunately, the effectiveness of the TGV is only evident in French territory, where the distance from Lyon to Paris is covered in 1h50m with an average of around 300km/h compared to the average of 110km/h on Italian territory. The problem is not the train, it's the railway... Ultimately, if we kept up like the French, we could get to Paris by train in 4 or 5 hours versus the current 7.5 hours.

Took the TGV from Lille to Nice. Thought it would make a pleasant change from flying. Confusion over finding correct coach and seats (even the French were struggling). People had huge amounts of luggage, which spilled into the aisles. The windows were filthy. Some seats have virtually no window space anyway. Immediately the sun came out the regular customers pulled down the blinds, so any views were lost. The train broke down and we switched to another and grabbed First Class seats. What a difference. Comfortable seats and clean windows. Return journey was better but still luggage blocked every area near the doors. All in all, not an experience I would repeat.
On board the TGV Paris Bordeaux boco meal apparently prepared by chefs, in any case appreciable and above all better than station sandwiches

we took Brussels-Marseille return TGV tickets in 1st class: never again! Is this what 1st class is?: no meals on board for a journey of more than 5 hours, no wifi connection... nothing that one would expect from 1st class. We are warned at the start of the trip that the espresso machine does not work (same on the way back), according to the steward, it never works. Departing from the Brussels Midi terminus, the toilets are in a terrible state; the same on the way back from the Marseille terminus at Saint Charles station and there not only are the toilets dirty but there is also no soap and the hand dryer is broken. Strictly not recommended!

We took the TGV from Paris to Barcelona we had booked first class tickets and our seats where on the upper deck which gave us a perfect view of the passing scenery. The seats are very comfortable and they recline. The catering facilities on board are very good with a wide choice of reasonably priced food and drink (Although you can take your own food and drink on board) Although we had a major delay of three hours in Paris and Montpelier the speed of the train if phenomenal and surpassed 300 kph. Definitely well worth doing instead of flying and the price we payed was great.

I love the TGV experience!.. I traveled First Class to Bergerac and then back to Paris...the trains were on time, clean and the seats were very comfortable. In First Class they come around with a drink cart, which is free except the alcohol beverages and pass out small snack packs of nuts or cookies. I purchased my tickets on line, had 1 set mailed to me, which I received right away and had the other confirmation emailed, which I printed out and carried with me for my return trip to Paris. I purchased lunch tickets as well...I found the lunches options to be jsut fine...not a fine dining experience but certainly fine for train travel. What you see of the countryside during your fast ride is a neat way to see parts of France you certainly don't see from the miles high up airplane travel....I would take the train again, when this type of travel is appropriate...it was a great experience...just be aware that when in the station for connecting trains, you need to plan on paying for the restroom.

Took it for a round trip to lille (actually went on from there to Bruges). It was on time & fast. Definitely would use again.  The seats were a bit worn down. There is not much of a view. About half the trip eye level is below ground level . When there is a view i got a bit dizzy.

High-speed trains that make it convenient to travel around the city. We drove from the airport to Disneyland in 9 minutes. You can book a ticket online on the company’s website, this will be better due to queues and non-working windows or breaks.

We took several TGV services between; Nice and Avignon; Avignon and Lyon; Lyon and Paris. We travelled in First class, we found that if you purchase your tickets as soon as the fares become available you can pick up tickets for around 70 Euros for 2 people one way.The location of the stations are within easy access of each city, we walked or took the metro to most of the stations. We only travelled to the station by taxi in 2 cases as we were unfamiliar the city or the station location was not within walking distance.We had two large suitcases and as we were seated on the upper deck made it a challenge to get the bags up the staircase but there is a baggage rack just inside the door so it was easy enough to stow your luggage and take your seat.Can thoroughly recommend using TGV for travelling around France as the service are quick and efficient and you can save time as you only need to arrive just before the train time allowing you to spend more time sight seeing or sleeping/eating.We used the TGV trains on previous visits and have never had any problems with our journey.

My wife and I took our first TGV trip from Paris Gare de Lyon to Nice on the Mediteranean. It was quite an experience speeding across France in comfort. The train travelled at about 180 mph or 290 kph. You can see the countryside unlike in a plane. There were plenty of restrooms and a food car which made the trip more comfortable. I did watch bags in the stations to make sure they weren't taken. Otherwise really no worries. Imagine if we had these in the USA and could travel coast to coast in less than 24 hours unlike the 3 days it takes now.

TGV is THE means of transport London-Paris or vice versa. I did London-Paris and it was very peaceful. St. Pancras station is beautiful, close, efficient, boarding is quick, comfortable seats, quick journey. The station in Paris is also very close to the center. Much better than going to the airports. I highly recommend it!

Getting around France can be accomplished via the TGV. It is actually easy, clean, and efficient. It is pricey though and you must watch your bags as they can easily be stolen. Multiple languages are spoken and you can easily find help. The people were very friendly there and willing to help.

We took the TGV from Paris to Munich with a change in Stuttgart. We booked 1st class tickets and it was very nice. We were served a full lunch with drinks and the staff were very pleasant. The train was comfortable, smooth and our top speed was 319k/h. The booking was done online and there were no problems at all. If you are planning a holiday and this route is part of your trip, book the nice seats - not that much more and very nice experience.

We took the TGV to go from Brussels to Paris airport, so with quite a bit of luggage.  We didn't have much room for our hand luggage and we had to leave the large suitcases unattended at an exit.  Not really a comfortable feeling.  So if there is another way, we will no longer take the TGV for a long trip.

The journey was a quiet yet cold journey. We were taking the train from Barcelona and stopping at Montpellier. Reserving the train took over an hour as the system in Barcelona wasn't the best and had to pay 10€ pp with an Interrail pass.The journey was smooth yet the air conditioning was way too cold and the draft was really uncomfortable.Overall there was nothin special about this train besides an over-priced bar service; which had friendly customer service may I add!

First the good.. The train was on time and the price wasn't bad. Also, the seats were large enough and comfortable.The not so good.. No sign of any buffet service in the carriage itself despite this being premium class. We had to go to a dedicated carriage where the offerings weren't exactly mouth watering.Compared to Eurostar where we got a snack served at the seat in standard class it was a poor second. The train itself was starting to look a little tired and the toilet itself was a disgrace.. Stil, having grown up with UK trains I felt right at home..

Although the systems at first seem rather strange, they work.  When arriving at station you won't know until 20 mins before ) which platform the train will depart from.  In large stations you need to be alert.   You will notice people standing under the announcement board waiting. When the platform is announced a mad rush is made for the train.  If you are boarding on a station between the termini of the train, you will see a board showing the layout of the carriages.  Check your ticket as to which carriage you are on then compare with the board.  You will then be advised where to stand on the station and when the train arrives, your carriage will be in front of you.  This doesn't happen until just before the train arrives.  You will have tops 5 mins to get on with your luggage, store it and find your seat before it departs.  Storage is very limited. Don't delay in getting on the train it waits for no one.  If you can't get to your carriage in time, get on anywhere and find it after the train departs.  Trouble with reserved seats is that someone else may already be in them, and often they won't get up even knowing they are not their seats.  Conductors don't seem to really care either.  We purchased a month rail pass for 4 days travel - travelling on 6 different trains.  The last ride was a hiccup.  Being instruction by the company selling us the pass, to check in at the machine on the station proved to be the problem.  The machine wouldn't accept our numbers and we had to go to the SCNF ticket office who refused to confirm our seats telling us we had no tickets/had not paid.  Showing the pass to staff made no difference.  We had paid for reserved seats on a specific train via this pass and via a company in Australia only to find that we then had to buy new tickets as the system in Australia let us down.  By doing this we discovered having a rail pass was not necessarily the cheapest way to go.  Next time we will buy tickets at the station when we need them and not purchase a pass.  Just food for thought.
So we travel at super high speed on the top deck of a clean and spacious train. So WHERE IS THE WIFI????????  Come on SNCF let's get into the 21st century.
Bought our tickets online.  Really easy.  Luggage was a bit if a squeeze but it all fitted in the end.  I bought 1st class tickets from Paris to Nice. Top speed was 297km/hr.
I didn't find the service I expected.... Nothing better than Italian trains, on the contrary: no power socket and no wifi available!

I used it for a round trip between Montparnasse and Rennes to go to Mont Saint Michel. Tickets can be purchased at the counter at Montparnasse station. It was my first time on a TGV, and the first thing I noticed was that the face of the vehicle was dirty (lol), and the seats were just like that. It's really like an express train. The departure from Montparnasse was completed accurately, but the return trip was extremely delayed and I had to wait on the platform for over 30 minutes in the heat. You need to be mentally and physically prepared. I also found it strange that there were other people on board when I got on the train from Rennes, even though it was a reserved seat for some reason. (Although he quickly left...) It was also strange to see so many customers standing in the aisle. Wasn't it like all seats were reserved? I don't care though.

I rode 2nd class from Geneva, Switzerland to Paris, France. In Japan, I often ride the Shinkansen for business, so I was looking forward to seeing what the French version would be like. However, I was completely betrayed. First of all, Geneva station is dirty. In particular, the women's restroom in the departure waiting room was out of order, and the women were in tears because of the smell and filth. There was a gap in my body as I had just come down from the beautiful mountains of Switzerland. Also, TGV is slow... I had high expectations after leaving Geneva, so I was blown away by the slow pace of the ride and the scenery along Lake Geneva. I finished "Lake Geneva View" and thought it was time to go. But it doesn't get any faster. On the contrary, the train stopped every time it arrived at the station. After all, it takes about 5 and a half hours to cover 500km... The maximum speed is probably around 250KM. It was about the last 30 minutes (it was quite fast). Was this train a "Kodama" type? Even a "Kodama" is fairly fast... The seat pitch was about 75% of that of the Shinkansen, which was too narrow even for me, who is 175cm tall. The table in front of the seat was dirty and covered with some kind of sauce. The wash water in the toilet had an unusually chemical smell that made my nose crawl. I don't want to ride it anymore!!

I took the TGV from Paris to Zurich. The first one in the morning. I slept the whooooole way. The served a nice tidy breakfast. Nothing much to say except for the fact that I forgot a backpack in the train and left. I realised and went back running, got onto the train again, but could not find it! My first thought was "damn thieves!". Nevertheless, when I got off the train again, I saw in the distance a stewardess with the back pack coming towards me! She gave it to me and told me she was taking it to their office. Nice experience! Train was on time.If you plan to travel on advance, be sure to get the discounts and you´ll be able to get the same price for coach or first class!!!

TGV offer a fabulous company, Navendis, as their car transfer company in Paris. You can also book directly with the company for any transfer by registering with them online. This is a brilliant and affordable service. Each time we have used them, the driver is there right on time and will take your luggage to their vehicle for your transfer. As you have paid in full at the time of booking, it makes no difference if traffic is bad - unlike a taxi. I cannot recommend this company highly enough! Don't risk taking a taxi - ever!!!!
Experience to forget: very old train, scary noises, unexplained stops, small sheets so you touch the seat of the train, tiny cot on the floor, no a/c, etc. thello never again

I went from Paris to Nice. I chose to travel on the TGV. I bought it 3 months before and got a first price the same as the second one and much cheaper than buying it at the last minute. The trip was lovely. It was through the French countryside and the last stretch along the entire French Riviera: super delicious trip and also the seats were huge and very comfortable seats. I recommend them.

Be very careful booking online, at least from Australia. I went back a screen to check the price and found after I had paid that I had been charged twice and had two sets of tickets for the same people on the same train! So far, the Australian booking agency, after two weeks of email exchanges, has not provided any assistance and it looks as if I will not be refunded the price of the second lot of tickets. I am clever but not able to occupy two seats at opposite ends of the carriage at the same time! So even if the trip is pleasant it is ruined for me. I only gave one star because you can't complete the review without it. It's a no star for me.

Used between Lille and Paris. Compared to Japan's Shinkansen, it is designed to make traveling more enjoyable. The seats are wide even in second class. There were family seats facing each other, and families were happily playing games with a table in the middle. The interior is also colorful. The speed is not as fast as in Japan. It also connects to Charles de Gaulle Airport, making it convenient.

from Stuttgart to Paris in just under 4 hours at a sensationally low price. The advantage of flying is obvious: no lengthy airport check and arrival in the middle of the city. Only the board restaurant leaves a lot to be desired and unfortunately doesn't offer any real seating and the service was quite unfriendly.

TRAIN OLD, dirty, dusty, bedding and cushions infested with bedbugs - see photo below - undrinkable coffee reheated in the microwave. Young and friendly but completely inexperienced staff. 450 euros per person round trip for a 2 cabin. Avoid ABSOLUTELY. Fly five times cleaner.

An amazing experience. But first, a suggestion: Unless traveling in peak season (we were not), I don't see the need to purchase your tickets in advance. If your flight is delayed (and ours was) and you arrive after the train you bought tickets for has left (as ours had), you have to buy new tickets (and we did). And they are not cheap.That out of the way, let me just say that the TGV "bullet" train is just the best way to get from De Gaulle airport to Disney Paris. The distance of 43.8km ( 27.2 miles) takes 10 minutes, non-stop. If you've never moved at 200mph (322km/hr), it is an experience you will not forget. The trains are clean, bright, well lit, and, in the off season, sparsely populated. The ride is smooth and disturbingly stable given the speed at which you are moving. There are numerous web sites that can guide you through the process of purchasing tickets, boarding the train, etc. ( see "Paris by Train" for an overall guide to mass transit in and around Paris). The station at Disney (officially "Marne-la-Vallée") is dead center in the Disney resort complex. As we exited the station, the Disney Village was directly in front of us and the entrances to the Disney theme parks were to our right and behind us. Bus connections to the outlying hotels (Disney and otherwise) as well to the surrounding communities was to our left. While websites will describe the station as being at Disney's front door, the security protocols are such that you will have a bit of walk to clear the station and then wend your way to the theme parks and/or the Disneyland Hotel.The Marne-la-Vallée station not only accommodates the TGV train but also the RER commuter lines. As my wife and I had decided to avoid renting a car this was great convenience in terms of commuting into Paris as a local would. And that had it own benefits and features.At the end of our stay, we walked from the hotel to the train station, waited for the train (it was running late. Ironic?), and ten minutes later we were at the airport. Brilliant system.

My wife and I took the TGV from Paris to Stuttgart, and it was a wonderful train ride. At times, we travelled at in excess of 320 k/h, but it felt as if we were barely moving. The train seats were comfortable, our carriage was quiet, and the service was excellent. It's a great way to travel in Europe.

After several trips on board the TGV Milan-Paris/Paris-Milan, even at different times but all always in 1st class, we have come to the conclusion that we will no longer make even one. The last trip in chronological order is the Paris-Milan of 26/08, which arrived at Garibaldi station one hour late. The price of the 1st class ticket is not at all adequate for the quality of the journey nor for the services offered: in our entire 1st class carriage there was no working power socket, the seats deserved adequate sanitisation (they were smelly) and the bathroom in our carriage was almost unusable as the waste water produced a weak jet and the drain cover did not open... therefore it did not drain. I would like to point out that the previous day we took another SNCF high-speed train (always in 1st) and the conditions were almost similar: bathrooms to avoid, sockets not working but which, upon request from the on-board staff, worked in another carriage....(?). After this terrible experience, I really don't think we will travel with SNCF again.

To leave the French country and reach our destination, the famous city of London, we use the train that passes under the ocean. I thought the trip was fantastic and very quick, you don't even feel like you're on a bullet train. This means of transport is very well structured, it’s worth it.

I used the Milan-Paris service with night departure to enjoy the convenience of arriving in the city center the next morning. Thello is the only operator that offers this service and evidently takes advantage of its monopoly position: old and worn carriages, rather uncomfortable and short berths, impossibility of finding a position to place glasses or an alarm clock/telephone, very dirty bathrooms already in Milan, suffocating heat in the berth alternating with sporadic switching on of the air conditioning system at polar temperatures. Maximum solidarity with the kind and exhausted staff who have to suffer this ordeal on a daily basis!
We traveled from Paris to the south in 4 and a half hours. The service was very good and worked perfectly. We travel very comfortable!
Wonder! We went from Frankfurt to Paris, it is comfortable and spacious, but the place to put our bags is a bit complicated. It's worth using this means of transport!

fast and punctual! what many don't know is that it quickly connects de gaulle airport with disneyland paris at the same price or perhaps less than the vea shuttles given that children under the age of 4 don't pay!

We didn't use the TGV on this most recent trip but had a very good experience on an earlier trip. We took the train from Avignon to Paris and were very pleased with the ride, the train and the personnel.  It was an interesting experience, particularly when two trains pass each other.

when I see the devastation caused by the passage of the new Paris Rennes tgv line, both ecological and landscaped to save a quarter of an hour between Paris and Rennes, I find it a dear price for our countryside

We traveled on the THELLO train from Italy to Paris and back. The trains used are very old intercity trains, very noisy and uncomfortable. He advised against the journey first of all because, given the antiquity of the vehicle, it was impossible to sleep amidst the terrifying noises and jolts. The journey was still acceptable because, having booked the cabin with two berths, we at least had a little more space and attention. The return was a nightmare: despite having always booked the cabin for two, for "technical" reasons, when we had already boarded the train, they made us get off together with all the passengers of our carriage and distributed us in second class, occupying the holes in the six-sleeper compartments, thus finding us sleeping with strangers in cars that were dilapidated to say the least: neither the compartment door nor the window closed, dusty seats and dirty bathrooms, staff annoyed and strange noises and creaks everywhere. A nightmare of over twelve hours. An experience absolutely not to be repeated.

A very average trip from Paris to Bordeaux in so called 1st class not a patch on Eurostar which we had just got off of . The signs are poor if you don't know what your doing which we do … please research as much as you can it will make transfers smooth.The buffet was terrible considering your on the train for 3 1/2 hours and your captive,COULD BE SO MUCH BETTER i have had better food from a French transport caféThe only up side was plenty of room.Getting on and off is tricky even for the able……..
A great quick trip to Paris 3 hours. Better than the return trip with ICE. Comfortable seats, best service.

I used the TGV for a trip with my family in the week of August to go to Paris and the main reason for this choice was the price because by plane it would have cost double while with the Italian train it would have been a good 30% more: so the price was ok, the punctuality as well, the call center assistance was superb with kind and trained operators. But let's get to the defects which are the prices of the bar (a freeze-dried coffee costs 2.80 euros not to mention drinks and food) and the cleanliness of the carriages which leaves a lot to be desired: on the ground there is a carpet that has seen better times and between the seats there are still crumbs from the First World War. Last tip: bring a sweatshirt even if it's 50º C outside because the air conditioning is very high.

TGV, 1st class ...... This was one of the worst train rides ever. I thought I treat my family during our Europe trip to one of these wonderful train rides, using the TGV . To make sure ( I thought) we have a marvelous experience, I bought first class tickets.  To make the story short, after having to stay around with hundreds of other people, waiting for the time table to reveal the platform of our train, 15 minutes before the train arrived, finding no working escalator and to have to log our heavy luggage up some very steep stairs (including our two small children), fighting our way into a wagon that barely offered space for our suitcases, we found our seats in a wagon that had a NO WORKING AIR CONDITIONING system. IMAGINE THE WAGON WAS AIRTIGHT, the temperature was between 90-100 Fahrenheit, AND WE WERE TRAPPED IN THERE FOR 3 HOURS. We complained to the conductor without any effect. We arrived like overcooked shrimps, and swore never again to step a foot into a French train.After our return, we complaint to RailEurope. I copied the response below for those who might consider to use this service. Good luck with getting the required documentation if one does not speak the language .Quote.....Please be advised that unless the tickets are endorsed by the conductor verifying your claim, the European Railroads will not provide any compensation. However, if your tickets are endorsed by the rail official verifying your claim, please send your original documents along with a letter via traceable mail to the following address. Rail EuropeAttn: Customer Relations/Claims9450 W. Bryn Mawr Ave. Suite 400Rosemont IL 60018Shipping phone number: 847-916-1001UnquoteBy the way, we traveled also in Switzerland and Germany, there only second class. We felt in heaven in comparison.

I used it for a round trip between Montparnasse and Rennes.・I made reservations and tickets in advance on a Japanese website before traveling, and if I booked early, I was able to get a 1st class seat that was cheaper than 2nd class. Tickets can also be issued at ticket vending machines at National Railways stations in Paris, so I thought it would have been better to just make a reservation in Japan.・The ticket stamping machine before boarding the train did not work properly, so I had to ask a local person for help. Tickets issued in France are stamped when you insert the barcode side, but tickets issued in Japan are stamped not on the barcode side, but on the opposite side.・The first class seat you reserved is a semi-compartment for 4 people, so if you don't want to be with people you don't know, you may want to avoid it. Inside the compartment, the seats are facing each other with a folding table in the center, but the table is large so eating and drinking inside the car is no problem. There's also a trash can by the window, which comes in handy. However, if you are in a compartment, you cannot see the entire vehicle, so it is not suitable for enjoying the view from the window. It's a plain rural area, so the view from the train window may not be enough to enjoy it.・I also went out to the bar car, which is no longer on the Shinkansen, and had a beer. It's a standing bar, there are no seats, and the prices are expensive, but it's perfect for a change of pace. It is also convenient that credit cards can be used.・When boarding a train, you must be careful. If the train has two formations connected, you cannot go back and forth between the formations, and if you make a mistake when boarding, you will not be able to take it back. If your train is stopped at a station platform, there will be a sign telling you which formation you are boarding, but you need to be careful as it may be the wrong car or the train number. The same may be true for departure information boards at stations.・The water system in the washroom and toilet in the car may be incomplete. There are cases where the toilet compartment is dirty or the water does not come out, and the vehicle is not properly maintained, so if it is poorly maintained, it is better to move to another vehicle immediately.・I don't know if there is a strike, but this time the round trip was on time, and I was able to connect to the connecting bus from Rennes to Mont Saint Michel without any problems.

This for me is the best means of transport in France, sometimes they can be more expensive than an economical plane ticket, but the practicality, comfort and accessibility of the TGV is unmatched. I have already traveled to Reims, Bordeaux and Marseille from Paris. Modern and comfortable trains and most importantly, punctuality. I recommend everyone to travel by TGV around France.

I have always preferred the TGV to the plane, we can work there, walk there, make calls, all without having to go through security checks, check-in queues, prohibitive parking costs, wider seats, etc. Subscribe to the professional area first, silence in the dedicated car, everyone can work but it exasperates me to be disturbed by the controllers themselves who still have not understood, for some, that they represent a service company. The airline service will never accept seeing a steward eat in place of a customer, in business. the sncf knows how to do it! And yes, why not, no one except the customers to see them and even if it means reading the newspaper, taking out the sausage, you might as well do it in the quietest and empty compartment, forgetting that travelers like moin pay 800 euros per year to benefit from them... How can we not receive the disapproval of hard workers or simply customers whose company pays this type of benefit, who work even while traveling who see these controllers, comfortably seated, eating, drinking, chatting in an ID Zen wagon, pedantic to their working time....what legitimacy when they are in the street to demonstrate afterwards. I remain a fan of the TGV, many efforts are made but the bad apples must be trained, removed from customer service so that the TGV takes the commercial upper hand over the plane.
A wonderful journey, completely relaxing, crossing the Alps and then enjoying the typical French landscape. Comfortable and fast trip. The Bar cabin was our favorite room :)

Took the TGV from Paris to Reims in order to visit Clicquot Champaign house.  Booked trip on line in advance for approximately $100 per person. Very pleasant and quick trip, about 45.minutes.  Paris Est station was within walking distance of our Paris hotel, and Reims station was near shops and restaurants.  The TGV made a one day trip very doable, with lots of time for Reims attractions.

Its sad, but the French dont seem to maintain the trains as they used to do several years ago. Now, they are completely dirty and smelly. My wife travelled from Zurich to Paris some months ago, and she already has a horrible experience on a smelly and dirty train. Today a cousing left from Zurich, while we help her to place the luggage, it was inevitable to notice the smell and how the floors where completely dirty. You can check the pictures I will upload now.

I rode from Montparnasse to Rennes to go to Mont Saint Michel. I made a reservation from the official website more than two months in advance, so it was quite cheap. As the boarding date approaches, only the higher seats remain, so it is important to make reservations as early as possible once the date is decided. Cheaper tickets cannot be canceled or changed. I took 1st class on the way out and 2nd class on the way back, but I found that 1st class had more room. However, the day before, I took a day trip to Brussels by Thalys, and the 1st class seats on Thalys are more luxurious than the green cars on Japan's Shinkansen trains, so I honestly think the TGV is just average. As I felt when I went to Versailles with SNCF, it's a tourist city, so I wish the vehicles were a little more clean and neat.

This is one of the easiest ways to get to Paris from the south of France. The trains are comfortable. As a rule, there are two classes of service, but the difference between them is small. You can book tickets on the sncf website. During my entire TGV trip I traveled 4 times, but I also used Intercity and Ter. Among all other types of high-speed trains, the TGV is the fastest and most comfortable. Seats are given to you at the time of booking. The speed of the train sometimes exceeds 300 km/h. The train has a buffet. Unfortunately, the TGV has a minus - the price. Sometimes it reaches 100-150 euros. You have to pay for comfort. Only once we had a 3-hour delay due to the weather. The thunderstorm knocked down the trees and they fell onto the tracks. We were given dry rations (applesauce, cookies, water) and kept apologizing. As they say, a stone can fall on anyone))) Travel with TGV!
Fiz duas viagens de TGV. A primeira de Lucerna-Paris e a segunda de Paris-Lourdes. Recomendo!!! É pontual e confortável.
took it from bern to paris.it is not super fast in switzerland, but once your enter france it uses special tracks and runs at 300 kmph.not many options available for food on board, so stock up.

En pleine grève sncf, je dois prendre tgv. Retard et absences de communication, une image une fois de, plus écornée. La premiere classe, est quand meme confortable. Les controleurs, étaient pas bien loquaces...

Sempre é bom viajar de trem pela Europa, uma vez que as estações ficam próximas aos centros das cidades ao contrário dos aeroportos, quando viajei de TGV, não percebi tanta velocidade, mas vale a pena pela pontualidade e eficiência desse transporte.

We travelled from Amsterdam to Paris and then a week later from Paris to Avignon, booking first class seats in advance. We haven't travelled much by train before and certainly not a longer journey. We both found that the experience was a lot less time consuming and stressful than flying. What a great service and it's traveling at 300km per hour. There are places for luggage and the reserved seating is excellent. in fact we went onto travel by train through Italy as well and their system is excellent also. I had read about rail strikes and no doubt if that occurred it would be a challenge but I guess planes get cancelled as well from time to time. Recommended!

Nous avions choisi de voyager de Paris a Barcelonne en TGV samedi 5 juillet a 7h15, en premiere classe, quelle mauvaise idee.D'abord la grande vitesse ne concerne qu'une partie du voyage, la moitie, le reste du lent, du tres lent avec des arrets un peu partout. Donc TGV,non pas vraimentPar ailleurs nous voyagions on voiture 1. Des le depart les toilettes sentaient tres mauvais comme si elles n'avaient jamais ete nettoyees. Il est incroyable de lire que le personnel passe regulierement pour s'assurer de la proprete des lieux. C'est juste un mensonge.Quand la porte des toilettes s'est bloquee toute la voiture a eu a supporter cette odeur pestilentielle, et je vous jure que je n'exagere pas.Honte a la SNCF, seule une entreprise publique peut se permettre une telle absence de service sans faire faillite. C'est une honte pour le pays quand on voit le nombre d'etrangers qui etaient dans le train.Evitez ce faux tgv avec de vraies mauvaises odeurs

How comfortable was this to travel through the French and German countryside. Luggage stored in the racks at the end of the cabin comfortable seats loads of room and up to 320km/h. Maybe the bullet train from Osaka to Kyoto was smoother but this was smooth.Would definitely do this again, more pleasurable than air travel.

Our family, with a baby in arms and 2 yr old, took Eurostar to Lille and picked up the TGV at Lille, saving ourselves a trip across Paris, as at Lille we needed only to change a platform.  I found there to be little choice of food at Lille, wished we had bought picnic at St. Pancras Marks and Spencer Food for the journey.  Needed all our water bottles.  Seats pretty comfortable, and lovely to have no smoking.  Gap between train and platform, had to be very careful with 2 year old. Plenty of luggage storage either at end of carriage, between seat backs, or on racks above head for small things.  They stupidly moved our seats without informing us on return journey, and put us in four across instead of facing each other.  Stations are NOT good for handicapped as elevator not working and escalator very crowded and actually had to do emergency stop, not gentle on the back.  Don't know how wheelchair would cope.  No adequate seating on platforms but a waiting room with seats. Toilets clean and adequate. Wish we'd been able to eat properly on way down as it was a long trip.  But still better than cattle class on airline and all that airline hassle.

Non facciamo confusione. Non ho mai usato Thello ma spesso il TGV. Non direttamente dall’Italia ma, lavorando spesso sia a Parigi che nella zona di Lione, ho scoperto da un quarto di secolo come è comodo volare su una delle due città e raggiungere l’altra con il TGV lavorando, telefonando… come ormai abbiamo imparato a fare anche in Italia tra Milano e Roma. Certo, il progetto ha i suoi anni e qualche treno lo dimostra ma questo proprio perché è stato il primo dopo lo Shinkansen ed è ancora il più veloce. Comodo.
TVG  самое удобное средство транспорта по Франции. Мы из аэропорта  Шарль Де Голль до Северного вокзала ехали на RER  за 9,50 евро, а в Фонтембло за 15евро. Рекомендую всем.

My husband was excited about his trip on the tgv. Personally I think it's overrated. The train was packed with people standing over each other and on exiting in nice there are too many people for the exit stairs provided. What on earth would happen if there was some kind of emergency??

I used the train between Paris and Milan, longing for the view from the train window. My thoughts are...I think it's good enough. It was a long way, and it took about 7 hours. I regret that I should have gone by air without hesitation. However, I didn't see much of the rural scenery in the French suburbs along the way, so it was a good thing. As for the vehicle itself, well, you could say it's European-style, but it hasn't been cleaned. I guess Japan's Shinkansen trains are too beautiful. Now, the problem I had on my way back from Milan to Paris was that there was no car with the car number on my ticket. I was a little nervous, but since the number of cars will increase due to the addition of connections at stations along the way, this is the car with the one's number. Other foreigners have also come and gone, so be careful. Many European trains do not have ticket gates, so outsiders can enter the train until just before departure. There are a lot of pickpockets at Milan stations, so be careful.

First class train between Lausanne and Paris. As soon as you pass through Switzerland, the speed increases and the track shakes less, making for a more comfortable ride. The seats in the vehicle are basically 2+1 rows, with 4 seats facing each other for group use and sideways sofa seats. The light meal service consists of a choice of meat or fish, a plate of cheese, bread, vegetables, etc., and drinks (soft drinks, wine, beer), etc. are served at the customer's seats. The taste is at the same level as in-flight food, but as expected from France, the cheese and wine are good. The toilets were small and I didn't feel clean.There were times when I thought it was a first class train, such as seeing people who were not seated with their bicycles in the aisle, but overall it was comfortable. Perhaps because the Swiss section was slow, the speed felt somewhat like a Japanese express train.

When returning home from my final destination, Mont Saint-Michel, I used the route between Rennes and Charles de Gaulle. I took the opportunity to arrange a first-class flight through HIS. I think it was about 6,000 yen per person. What I thought was better than the Shinkansen was the spaciousness of the seats. It was spacious with 2+1 rows. Well, their physiques are different. Many people wrote that the toilet was dirty, but I was lucky that I didn't have to go to get it. Unlike Japan's Shinkansen, there are sections where the speed is reduced in urban areas, so it takes a long time compared to the distance. I don't think it was 400km, but it took about 3 hours. Japan's Shinkansen trains have an image of being clean and shiny, but trains in Europe, including the TGV, are quite dirty, probably because they are not washed very often. The tip of the lead vehicle is quite dirty with crushed insects and other things that it hit.

It’s an attraction in itself! The TGV is legendary and its design, elegance and speed are a pleasure. Very pleasant for short distances but not for crossing France because the train is always a little less pleasant beyond 2 hours.

When I go to Europe, my first priority is to travel by train and TGV. I have already walked and still travel a lot by train. It is a peaceful, pleasant journey without waiting because they are punctual. I love it and recommend it whenever you can go by train because it is wonderful. Comfort, quality space. Well, it's like being in a relaxed room. I find it fascinating. Now from May to June we made 4 train trips.
I left Gare de l'est in business class to Germany. I loved! You don't even realize it's a train journey. Comfortable, fast and practical. There is a free snack for those in first class.

TGV .. Paris de L'Est to Mannheim .. First Class. We had a brilliant trip. Upper deck seating, food (salmon main course) and drink service (albeit limited) was excellent. We always have had great service on TGV and this trip didn't disappoint (even with the strike causing problems for some). Coach was very clean, in great condition and very comfortable. If your travel budget allows, this is the way to travel in France.

We traveled from Paris to La Rochelle, booked a ticket in advance via the Internet, then received it from a machine at the station by simply entering the reservation code. Everything is simple, accessible, convenient, comfortable, and the price at a distance greater than from St. Petersburg to Moscow is 3 times cheaper than on SAPSAN - this is not Russian Railways - where only prices rise and the well-being of the manager.

TGV is the worst train corporation In Europe. We are in our honeymoon and was honing from Paris to Milan.The workers went on strike and they told no one. We had a reserved seat so they had our details. But no call or email came.Tried to book another train but it was fully booked. Had to buy plane tickets which cost us 600€. And one of our bags ended up getting lost. Worst experience ever.

We used the train system from Amsterdam to Paris and again to London. What a way to go. Forget flights this is efficient, comfortable and there is even a buffet car for coffee and food. Interesting people to talk to and very very fast. Try it as it is great value for money.

We only had to go from Amsterdam to Paris and had to make three changes with TGV, one with 3 mins to change, one with only 9 mins and had to run, and I mean all the way, from track 23 to 3, and even when we got there the conductor told us we couldn't get on. Of course we did, we have tickets, but when we asked for our seat locations we were waved away. When my wife had to move some luggage the conductor stood and watched her struggle, and laughed. We ended up renting a car and loving it.
You can find spaces at comfortable prices if everything is done in advance, scheduling the trip, it is not that expensive. The food on the train is not the best, but it is the least of it.

The TGV is the bullet train, which is faster than the regular train. We pre-booked our tickets about a month in advance from Paris to the Loire Valley (Tours- St Pierre des Corps station). It's a 1 1/2 hour direct train ride rom Gare Montparnasse in Paris. The trains are clean, modern, very efficient and smooth ride. Depending on destination, different TGV trains depart from different train stations in Paris. We arrived early to the train station. Usually, the track number for the proper train will be announced 20 minutes prior to departure as the train arrives to the station. Everybody is pending looking at the departure board to see when the train arrives. Need to board train fairly quick, as some of the cars may be quite far back requiring more walking, especially if travelling second class.  We strongly recommend to pre-book the tickets, although you can buy tickets the same day.  We booked online and noticed that the price goes up as it gets closer. Is like plane tickets. They first sell off the cheapest ones and then goes up to next price bracket.  When purchasing the tickets, there are first and second class tickets. For our trip, we left early and got a very good price in second class tickets, but for the return we found that the first class tickets were cheaper than second class tickets. Therefore, we recommend to check both classes and see what option works best. During the booking, we were able to choose our seats which was included in our price. It  also indicated which car we needed to board. The second class cars are further back and will require more walking, while the first class cars are closer to the front.  The seats in first class are wider and more comfortable than second class. But second class seats are still comfortable. In each car there are area for storing suitcases/luggages and there is overhead storage for smaller items.   When looking for the car number, each train car has the number on an electronic panel near the door.Something to note, if you would like to snack or something to eat, we were allowed to bring food and beverage on the train.Another thing to consider if you bring too much luggage, it may be a challenge to move around. At Gare Montparnasse we were dropped off at the entrance with the escalator that was going to second level, but it was not working. Therefore, we had to lug our luggage up. Fortunately our suitcases were carry on size.

We took the TGV directly from CDG to Reims (easy transfer at Champagne-Ardenne) and then non-stop back to Paris East Station. All trains were on-time and about a half hour. First class has bigger seats but not much else.The only issue I have is probably my own fault, and that is too much luggage. You have to get it on and off the train in somewhat of a hurry and you need to go up/down three steps. There are luggage racks however, and since the train is non-stop you don't have to worry too much about them disappearing.I used a site called capitainetrain.com (no affiliation to me) to make my reservations. I found it easy to use and the lowest fares of any of the so called "euro-train" sites that you get linked to. The earlier you book, the cheaper the fares. I paid 15 Euros each as soon as the dates became available (about three months out, I think), while others in my group booked later and paid a lot more. US Credit cards welcome and you get your actual tickets either electronically or using a kiosk when you arrive in France. Seat assignments are included at no extra cost.

I'm riding something. Well, don't compare it to Japan's Shinkansen. The toilet...it's dirty. It was clogged and I couldn't use it. Vehicle...it's dirty. There probably aren't any cleaning staff like on the Tokaido Shinkansen. Above all, the graffiti and scratches on the car body are still intact. Meal...I couldn't find a dining car this time. Even so, the staff is unfriendly.　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　〇　　　　　　　　　　　It seems that there are no French people who talk while eating something gooey. Conductor...Maybe because it was a group tour, there was no "ticket inspection".　　　　　　　When I travel alone, they come to check if I have checked the ticket properly and if I have an e-ticket. However, the atmosphere you see from the train window is still that of a foreign country, so it's good to experience it. However, train stations are full of pickpockets, and you may find someone sneaking right up to you without you even realizing it, so you need to be extremely careful.

Fast, on time, great way to be moving around France. Beats driving for sure. I love watching the cars going slowly along the motorway as we speed past at 280 kph. But I find the trains are warm and very stuffy. Food on board is limited; we buy filled baguettes at the station before departure. And you MUST get a seat reservation - the first trip will show you why. And the platform is only announced just before departure - you really have to move quickly when it is announced - the trains can be hundreds of metres long.

Passengers were so quiet that I couldn't believe there were people who took the train from Paris and Montparnasse to Rennes. The reason you can't hear people talking even though most of the seats are occupied is not only because the seats are compartmentalized, but also because public places in France are like movie theaters in Japan, so the voices are very quiet. It's hard to tell what other countries are connected, but you can soothe the fatigue of your trip while looking at the scenery outside. You can feel the difference between Europe and Asia because the train moves slowly like the Shinkansen in Japan, and there are no people talking in a loud voice.

Coming from Australia, with our sad, old rattlers (romantic in their own way though) we had heard a lot about the famous trains of France that travel at 300k/p/hr.  I can't say there was a lot - some, but not a lot -  of help on the Paris metro.... but I found the central railway (PARIS MONTPARNASSE) much the same as Central Railway - familiar layout, the same general organised chaos.  Once I got over my (sacre-bleu) inability to speak or understand the language and started to look at the inner city railway as the same as Sydney's, I was able to orient myself a whole heap better.  My bad.But nothing was better than flying across the countryside (all of it new and beautiful) on the TGV.  We travelled up, down, across and did the jump off/jump on again after visiting little places just for the heck of it.Wifi, electrical outlets, comfort, stand up bars, clean.... and did I mention 300k/p/hr?  Who'd fly? and who would catch a bus?  This was living.  Must do - just for the heck of it, but definitely for the value for money, convenience and wow factor.

I find that the SNCF has really “let loose” on prices recently without the services being improved: wow, that really hurts the wallet. In addition, their system is not completely up to date when you want to exchange or cancel a ticket and you are far from an SNCF station; Unfortunately, I have paid the price on many occasions without the (totally useless and ineffective) customer service of the SNCF offering me an adequate response/solution. However, it is good to point out that the TGV allows you to quickly reach several cities in France and is therefore very practical. Furthermore, the wagons are rather comfortable and pleasant.Conclusion:- A well-deserved zero for "all the work" of the customer service and their number 3635 with which you can NEVER reach a soul (basically the SNCF tells you to manage and abandons you on the side of the road; they shouldn't be respectful towards their customers either...).- A 4/5 for the TGV itself which is very practical, and for the train sets which are often comfortable (especially in 1st class of course). - Basically, if you take the TGV and you don't have to exchange your ticket or cancel it, everything will be fine for you. On the other hand, otherwise, do not count on the SNCF to help you or be cooperative. Usually you will only have your eyes to cry...
Convenient location at CDG.  A bit confusing for those of us that don't speak French, but help is always available.  Get a first class ticket with seat reservation
Fantastic transport in France. The trains are clean, extremely punctual and the rear staff are highly trained to offer an excellent quality service.

Be warned!! The TGV is infested with pick pockets who jump on the TGV at a station. They try to assist people and in the process they are targeting you or someone close to you.I was putting my luggage away when a guy started to try to assist trying to get my bag in a space it wouldn't fit and in the process getting as close as he could to me.It was only when the TGV started on its way from Avignon to Paris that I realised I was missing my wallet. A few minutes later I heard an announcement saying my name. The staff had found my wallet on the platform minus 300 Euros.When we arrived in Paris I saw exactly the same thing happening. A guy causing chaos. I approached the TGV staff which you could see were in a tizz about getting the TGV going and when I pointed to the pick pocket holding things up and said in a loud voice pick pocket. They just shrugged their shoulders.They couldn't give a stuff. This is the TGV in France a service that does everything it can in ensuring the pick pockets have a good income.If you travel watch out for them as they are a major problem and keep your hand on your wallet.

I used it when going from Paris to Mont Saint Michel. I took the plunge and bought a first class ticket online. However, when you actually get on board, the seats are box seats (seats facing each other), so if there is another passenger across from you, you won't be able to stretch your legs or cross your legs. Also, the scenery was only through rice fields, so I couldn't enjoy the change in scenery. I think it's not as good as Japan's Shinkansen.

A nightmare, Milan - Paris, treated like beasts without air conditioning, crammed into dilapidated carriages, with arrogant staff, unusable bathrooms, it seemed like a journey for displaced people... and I was traveling in first class.

Made a trip from Girona > Paris > Girona, in first class. I still think that the level of an AVE is much better, especially in Preferente. The TGV does not have good service, the food is terrible (12 euros for a menu of very poor quality), only on the upper floor do they serve food/drinks, you do not have an audio system with headphones, you do not have television screens. So a trip like ours of 6 hours is very long. Looking at, for example, our second part of the trip on Thalys from Paris to Amsterdam, how good! A menu in your place, very good quality, wines, other drinks as you want, very very good.

Recently I took the TGV from Paris to Zurich.  I booked it & paid online.  The  TGV was cheaper & no long bus ride to CDG or ORY for a flight, no security to go through.  The train station is center city in Zurich, so it's just a short walk to a variety of hotels.

It must have been luck...but both the outward and return journey went more than well for us. On the outward journey the wait was worse...the train arrived in Milan only 10 minutes late but the people waiting to get on were really worrying.....but then on the platform there was a group of more than 10 policemen who created a barrier and who, one by one, checked documents, tickets and residence permits, rejecting more than half of them to the sender. of people. In the end the trip was perfect. We had the cabin for 4 which we were supposed to share with 2 Sicilian/Parisian gentlemen who instead went to sleep in another bunk with a friend... so we were also alone. The sheets were clean and packed, the bathrooms always clean and stocked with paper. The return was worse, but nothing groundbreaking. We shared the cabin with a lady who was coming to visit Italy and an Italian boy who works in Paris. On this route no strange people but a trip by French students who, predictably, made enough noise to keep the train awake until late. We didn't even have time to go back to sleep before the Italian financial police came knocking and were carrying out random checks... and unfortunately the boy in the cabin with us had "won"... consequently everyone was awake again. Moral of the story: we slept little but the thello had nothing to do with it. Even on the way back everything was clean, including the bathrooms. The nice staff and even the bar area for a snack, although not excellent, doesn't leave you with an empty stomach in case you arrived in a hurry, like us, without having time to get dinner.
First class, Basel Paris , nothing really impressive, plus 2 phone charger are now broken because of the train plug.Expensive for no reason.

TGV to anywhere is much better than Amtrak. Fast, clean, reliable and THE way to get around France.There is a station at CDG so connecting to the train is actually sometimes faster to get to yon or Nice than waiting for a flight.

We bought tickets in advance (3 months in advance) on the website. We traveled from Brussels to the suburbs of Paris (to Disneyland) for an adult about 25 euros, if we had bought it at the ticket office at the station before leaving, we would have paid about 100 euros per person. There are constantly sales on the website, the ticket was paid for by card, printed out - no one really checked. comfortable inside even in 2nd class, clean toilets, space for luggage.

after 25 years I take the TGV again which I only knew in second class due to lack of means. there in 1st class, annoyed to see that people paying a second ticket allow themselves to walk around in 1st, to use the spaces reserved for 1st suitcases, and even better to use the WC...which results in limited maintenance and cleanliness, too bad otherwise it's just as quick a ride.

On the train from Paris to Venice I had the bad luck of forgetting my wallet in the cabin when I went to get breakfast. When I got off the train and went to pay the ticket for the bus, I saw that they had stolen every last ticket from my wallet. They left cards, but they didn't even leave me a tip. Be careful!

This was our first experience of SCNF TGV trains. From our use of the booking online service in Australia (printing off the tickets online was really good) to the TGV service made this a pleasure all the way.  We travelled from Paris Charles De Gaulle airport to Bordeaux and Agen to Paris was a simple and comfortable service. Trains were on time, clean and comfortable. We have had experience of the German long distance high speed train and there is little between the two.  Well done to SNCF TGV for a well run and efficient service.

We took thello for the May 1st long weekend and we traveled really well, punctual, clean as usual (it's a train) and our traveling companions were courteous, we were in berths for 6 but we slept peacefully, honestly from the reviews we read we feared who knows what... a good trip, and a good opportunity to meet other travelers and see the landscape. Very recommended.

A very painful experience returning from Avignon to Brussels. Crowded, “overbooked” train, controller absolutely powerless to do anything other than check tickets. No room for suitcases. Why didn't we plan that anyway? Well yes, people travel with suitcases. Some even have strollers for children. I had to travel standing while waiting for the next stop. So I was able to take a first place, paying extra of course. Fast train but still the door handle did not work except from the outside. In the event of an accident, what do we do? The toilets don't close either, but that's a detail. I am attaching a photo which shows what it will be like in a while.

We took the night train on April 30th from Milan Centrale at 11pm and arrived at the Lyon station at 9.30am, returning on the 3rd night arriving at the station at 6am. I recommend this means of transport for the convenience of timetables. We were in a 4-berth, the space was comfortable, they provided a sleeping kit (sheets, blankets, pillow and pillowcase). Clean.

Reading the previous reviews I was a little scared, but I have to say that it went well for me. Left Milan on perfect time both on the outward and return journey, the bunk was clean, the bathrooms too, of course it's not the bathroom at home, it's still a train toilet, the blankets had a few stains yes, but they were washed and perfumed and you just need to sleep in your clothes. I didn't sleep well because the bunk is actually uncomfortable, it's not the bed at home, but you know! For the rest, the staff were kind and efficient, even in the cabin with us there were calm and respectable French couples, in fact in the entire carriage they were 90% French, so no problems even during the night.

from Karlsruhe to Paris.  This is not what we are used to from the DB anymore. And there’s no comparison to flying either.  No queuing or check-in stress at the airport (don't I have anything "forbidden" in my hand luggage?!). Just be at the platform 10 minutes before departure, get on and you're good.  We booked first class on the return journey to test it out and were thrilled.

I used it from Geneva to Paris. I feel that it is inferior to the Shinkansen in all respects. The inside of the train is not very clean, and the train does not run according to the schedule. The staff are also not very attentive. It came with a meal, but that was probably the only good thing. However, if you have a dream of traveling through Europe by train, I think you should give it a try. It should be educational in many ways.

I used it between Paris and Lyon. Compared to Japan's Shinkansen, I feel that there are many sections where the train runs slowly. As a result, it took a surprisingly long time, and I was later than the scheduled arrival time, and the time was not accurate. What bothered me the most was the lack of cleanliness inside the car. The windows are quite dirty, and the toilet in particular is okay if it's not dirty, but sometimes it's clogged and malfunctioning, so I don't feel like using it. The restrooms at the station aren't clean either, but I think it's better to use the restroom beforehand.

I took the Thello train from Verona (8.50pm) to Paris. I was quite apprehensive given the previous reviews. Instead I found myself quite well. I chose a compartment for 4 people and perhaps this made the difference, because in fact the compartments set up with 6 berths seemed less comfortable. As far as cleanliness is concerned, it is always a problem, but the sheets supplied allow you to rest in acceptable conditions. I had the impression that the bathroom was cleaned during the night because I always found it tidy. The staff on board spoke good Italian and everyone was kind. We arrived in Paris on time, among other things at the Gare de Lyon, so not as far from the center as when arriving by plane.
Not being used to trains that run on time, and are quick, this was a great experience! Comfortable trips to and from the center of cities that ran on time, the TGV was brilliant!
Great experience, quick, secure clean. If not a bit expensive, but well what can you do!! Worth it!!
Took the TGV from Turin to Gare de Lyon. I must say that the first part of France is a bit slow, but otherwise it's a clean train. everything tidy and organised. Arrived on time

I did the round trip from Paris to Cannes on iDTGV. I chose the silent carriages: no cell phones, no music, low-voice conversations. It was a tremendous experience. Second and first class are equally recommended. The best, the landscape. I missed having wifi.
Extremely recommended trip. Comfortable, fast and practical. There is no waiting for the train, as punctuality is respected. Take gum, as there is pressure in your ears when you enter the tunnel.

We decided to have a romantic weekend in Paris, going there by train - first class - from Rome: 360 Euros for a two-seater cabin. Apart from the annoyance of having to transfer to Milan with the Frecciarossa (Thello no longer leaves from the capital), at the departure station, the discovery: the convoy is a set of old, smelly, noisy, dirty carriages, with real barracks latrines. We are not picky but, believe me, at this price everything is absolutely unacceptable. Some details: we had to open the upstairs bunk ourselves (the attendant didn't even make the gesture); no toilet paper in the latrines; between noises and jolts, we would have slept maybe two hours; the arrival in Paris was an hour and a half late, which, as it turns out, is absolutely normal. Never again. NEVER AGAIN.
Highly recommended, cheap tickets in advance. I recommend it to everyone for its cleanliness, punctuality, etc.

I purchased TGV PRO 1ere tickets (First Class Professional) to travel from grenoble to paris and back this week. The online blurb says that all first class TGVs that travel to Paris have electrical sockets and Wifi. So I paid 150 euros (instead of the 80 euros second class price) for this service. Liars. Neither train had either service.They should not sell tickets at this price if they do not provide the service. But this is France... 'Customer service' ? What's that ?!

From France to neighboring countries? TGV, don't hesitate. You save all the headaches, the time before boarding and a lot of money when compared to a commercial flight. Plus I find it more entertaining.

I recommend! Comfortable, fast and practical. Great way to travel. There is no waiting for planes and you can still see the landscape through the window. Suggestion: take gum, you may feel some pressure in your ears during the trip

Used for round trip from Paris to Mont Saint Michel. You can enjoy a peaceful view from the train window. At night it's pitch black and you can hardly see anything. Tickets can be purchased from ticket vending machines at stations, offices around town, or online. The vehicle number is not written on the vehicle itself, so be sure to check it at the platform.

Thello they put in that place!!! I traveled on Thello on 12/25/13 in the evening, I should have arrived in Paris in the morning at 9.30...I got there around 1 in the morning on 12/27 by BUS!!!! We spent the whole night stopped in Domodossola, due to snow, we couldn't proceed, but the manager who had to decide whether to let the train return didn't show up! he was probably in bed scratching himself, warm. The train conductors disappeared throughout the night, only in the morning after a 10 hour stop did they warn us that perhaps we would return to Milan. Once back in Milan the journey of hope began via BUS to reach Paris. I am still fighting, after 3 months, to have at least a 50% refund of the ticket, which they should give to all passengers only to apologize for the mess made. Instead they are attacking useless scams, on procedures, original tickets, purchase methods, etc. so as not to refund anything! NEVER TAKE THE THELLOAh, not to mention the trains: dirty, smelly, water gets in, narrow, uncomfortable...If I could vote negative I would!!!

From the moment we saw him arrive at the Milan station where we left, we knew it would be a nightmare! Intercity train, old, dilapidated and noisy. We had a double berth, paid an exaggerated amount, but the space available is non-existent, not to mention the pseudo-sink which leaked water on the way back. Sin!

We traveled from Munich to Paris 1st class at a sensationally low price (Europe Special) and were thrilled. Super comfortable seats, very reasonable menu, best service at your place (all included in the price). 6 hours from Munich main station to Paris l'Est, the journey goes by incredibly quickly, the speed is not really noticeable, it can only be noticed by the seemingly stationary cars on the motorway parallel to the tracks. The disadvantage on the return journey: The TGV has to wait in Stuttgart for an ICE from Berlin, because the TGV is never allowed to arrive in Munich before the ICE... unfortunately the ICE was late...

One of the great joys of travelling in Europe is high speed train travel (something we really need in Australia). It's a great way to get between cities and in most cases, saves time rather than flying. The TGV is a great service. Comfortable and efficient you can cruise between major cities in only a few hours. We travelled in first class and the only downside is that unlike the Dutch Thalys service, there is no wifi available on board. I hope it's something that's added as a service soon. We just missed the introduction of the train service from Paris to Barcelona, but 6 hours from city centre to city centre is a great service that I look forward to using next time I'm in Europe!

A meal taken on the TGV Lyon - Paris at lunchtime. I am attracted by the BOCO menu prepared under the aegis of great chefs. €17. Dishes by A. PIC and dessert by C. MICHALACK. Very good surprise. The dish was reheated in the microwave very well (no overcooking of the fish) and the dessert had character. In short, for the price, the catering on the TGV has become very decent.
We went from London to Paris in July 2013, very comfortable, no queues, wonderful, next time I'm going in 1st class, we simply loved it

Took TGV from CDG to Marne la Valee (Eurodisney), turn up and go prices make UK prices look bargain basement. Second class from 18 euro to 30 euro depending on time of day for a 9 minute trip and children pay full price at age of 11. Also being TGV have to book seat so very inflexible.

We traveled at night in a 6-berth... to forget! We wanted to have this experience, also given the price of the trip (35 Euros) in order to travel at night and earn a day...mmmhh...the bunk mates (strangers) were very kind, but obviously you don't know who you can find. During the night, many braking and many stops... moments when it was shockingly hot and others cold... the bunks are a bit dated, the blanket and sheet were clean, but really microscopic. We left from Milan for Paris and the train was really packed... from the trip of French children to the Turkish pizza chefs looking for work... the bathroom was quite clean (in the first hour of travel). The plane was much better, even if you have to waste time going to the airport first.
We went by train from Paris to London on the Eurotrain. The trip was excellent and the 2 hours between the two cities passed quickly in the comfort of first class.

The cost of the 1st class ticket is a bit high compared to the services offered: none other than a spacious seat, no cinema screens with film programmes, and the carriages are not exactly modern. The bathroom is kept constantly clean (and fortunately I would say... also because the duration of the trip is not short). I, who have benefited from RENFE's high-speed business for years, find the TGV really poor in comparison.

I took this train for a few times from Paris to Angers. The economy class is clean but if you are traveling with some bigger luggage it should be quite problem. There is a small luggage compartment in each of the coach but it can not be locked. Also TGV is quite expensive and do not forget to book a seat (often comes with a ticket)!

It turns out that my train from Paris to Bordeaux turned out to be a design train! Economy and business class carriages of such destinations as TGV Atlantique and Paris Est were designed by the famous French fashion designer CHRISTIAN LACROIX. And I was lucky enough to ride in one of these. A comfortable carriage with rich purple and orange-red seats, with sockets at every seat, a cafe with dark glass tabletops, bionic shape, entertainment for children - all this can be called a club train. Very nice!

Used TGV from Paris to Dijon. Train left both paris and Dijon on time but they were 2-4 minutes late arrival. Not punctual as the Japanese bullet trains!! To Dijon the train was new-ish and even in the economy class the seat size is good enough and just enough leg room. It was clean and comfortable. Returning to Paris the train was the old type but still good. reached 297kph on stage but it didn't shake very much and smooth ride. Bought some food on the train but it is the normal British snack level food. It is better to buy some food from outside the station!! I was able to buy return ticket for London-Paris-Dijon from the Eurostar website. It was easy and hassle free purchase. Will use again.

Very expensive and without services worthy of its fame (it stopped years and years ago...): first class almost identical to second class, a railway after-work bar, cleanliness at the limits of decency, and almost non-existent heating.

Hello, according to the latest comments from members, it is very obvious that they have never experienced the transport of forty years ago and more. What would they have said about steam locomotives, the soot which seeps into the compartments, the luggage racks where you have to carry the suitcases at arm's length to install them, in the event of sudden braking certain suitcases fall on the heads of those below, etc, etc... Every time I take the TGV, it's bliss, no clang, clang, at each section of rails. Speed, silence, you have to plan activities to pass the time, reading or otherwise.
