It turns out that, in the past, I worked in a company under contract for the initial construction of the TGVs. First there is the design office, the 3D designers and I created the full-size prototype of the TGV for passenger and freight transport, then come those who determine the panels, make the molds for each of them and the production: laminators, finishers, etc... So I know the TGVs very well.

I'll start by saying that I don't have great needs when I travel but taking the Turin-Paris round trip I would have some complaints. positive aspects, the interiors are very beautiful, more so than other high-speed trains, very silent carriages and always very friendly conductors who also speak Italian. However, it's ok that up to Lyon you have to go slowly but not at the levels of a regional train, a little more sprint wouldn't be bad. at customs in modane they look at your document on the way out, the Italians and the French on the way back (at least that's what happened to me) but they do it while you're traveling so it doesn't slow things down much. on the way back, however, you have to be careful because they reverse the seat numbers two seconds before leaving. each seat has two numbers, one high and one low (e.g. 12 and 98) and the number to refer to is illuminated. well as soon as I got on the first carriage because I had the low number I didn't even have time to put down my suitcase and the light of the other number came on. so we all got off and went to the opposite side of the train. In any case, a pleasant journey, from Turin it is certainly more comfortable than the plane. the prices are also affordable, 50 euros return.

Let's say first of all that we need to distinguish between Thello and Tgv. Here we are only talking about Tgv. The train stopped at the Milan Rogoredo station makes a bit of sense. It seems old (its production dates back to the 80s if I'm not mistaken) and looking at the interior it makes even more sense (old-fashioned carpet, honestly not very clean) which however is very "France"... very nineteenth century. However, comfort on board is not lacking. I liked the backrest especially in the headrest part which can fold up thus allowing for a good nap. The seats for two are comfortable. Do you put the suitcase there? and you can be sure that you will find it turned upside down over there! So those who have delicate material in their suitcase should be careful. The most beautiful and perhaps most romantic route is the one that crosses the Alps. For the rest, from Lyon onwards there is a lot of walking. Both on the outward and return journey the French police (and why not the Italian ones? well..) came on board, asked for the documents and above all the drug-sniffing dog (always the French police) also came on board. There is a trilingual staff on board (French, Italian and English) I would say is helpful. Go through the catering service... there are the bathrooms... In my opinion the 7 hours aren't even that long, for me they passed quickly also given the service and the fact of being able to rest. And you wake up in Paris. What more could you want?
Excellent train, quality, comfort, speed, neatness and accessible... use the service to go from London (st Pancras) to Paris (gare du nord) and I would do it again.

I hadn't used the TGV train from Turin to Paris for 22 years and I consider the experience I had this time with my family to be just enough. The trains are worn and cleanliness almost non-existent. Cleanliness of bathrooms completely unsatisfactory. The train arrived about 20 minutes late both on the outward and return journey. High speed is only from Lyon to Paris.

We travelled First Class from Milan to Paris. The SNCF TGV train was very disappointing. The carriage was dirty and needed to be thoroughly cleaned. There was no Wi Fi service which I think is unacceptable in this day and age. Furthermore no food or drink was offered as part of the service - it had to be paid for on top of the ticket; this is very poor compared to similar services such as EuroStar. There was also very little food on offer to purchase for an 8-hour train ride. Finally the lady who served us looked a state with tatty clothing and unkempt hair which was completely bizarre, further demonstrating very little interest on customer service for Premium travellers.

We have just returned from Paris by train...in 4-berths there is no living space...let alone 6-berths...and maybe with strangers! The train is very dirty and cold... the carriage flooded and no one was able to do anything... at every station people get off and on with relative confusion... it's an eternal journey... if you consider that 2 more were added due to an inexplicable delay... I wanted to give the children this new experience but it was a failure... very dirty seats covered cushions!

As someone has already said, this is the first TGV, so certain shortcomings are also acceptable. You also have to deal with the low speed and the stops in the stretch between Turin and Lyon, but in terms of cleanliness and temperature it competes with our TrenItalia Intercity trains. Departure from Vercelli. First class with face-to-face seats...vents under the window blowing cold air. The staff proceeded to raise the temperature... as if nothing had happened. Then we understood: only the ventilation was running, so the whole trip was with the jacket on (and not just us). As for cleanliness, between the seats we gave up asking any more questions: it was dirty! This train has a big advantage compared to the plane: you arrive immediately in Paris and with a metro or a surface RER you can go where you need to go, but for the rest it is below mediocre
Travelled across France to Switzerland by TGV, 1st class. Great food, drinks and service - all at a great yet somehow very smooth speed.

on Christmas Eve 2013 I took the Milan-Paris trip in a Thello 6-berth: a more than decent trip! certainly the train left Milan an hour late but he had collected everything at the Lyon station. The staff, certainly precarious (but no more than that of RyanAir or Easyjet?) were courteous, I don't know their level of Italian (I'm French), but helpful. The bathroom remained clean almost until we arrived (air problem coming from below with the risk of sucking in feces and urine!). Sheets, blanket and pillow were clean. My 5 traveling companions, a Chinese family who spoke only English, were disciplined and calm. A good trip therefore, which I would definitely recommend: when my children and boyfriend thought of going from Paris to Venice they rightly thought of the Thello train.

Reading the reviews regarding the thello train I was almost scared! It is definitely not a nice train considering the route is quite long and considering that traveling at night it should offer some more comfort.. In my case it was still punctual both on the outward and return journey and not excessively dirty! Being able to travel at night allows you to arrive in Paris in the early morning and enjoy the whole day!

A disaster. Departed from Paris more than two hours late, arrived in Brescia 3.5 hours late. I add a dirty train with ASL intervention toilets. Ticket cost €180.00, I have submitted a 50% refund request and I hope to get it. I believe that Thello needs to review its policies on service management if it does not want to lose its customers.

The trip from Paris to Grenoble took just over 3 hours. A very comfortable train, and most importantly, you can get there quickly. Air, unfortunately, if it flies, it is not with the same frequency as trains. As for the cost, the principle is the same as ours - if you buy a ticket in advance, you get a discount. Tickets go on sale 3 months in advance. If you buy in advance, a one-way ticket costs 25-30 euros (!!!), 1st class can be bought for 50!!! A week before the trip, a ticket for less than 80 euros one way, 2nd class, is almost impossible to buy! Tickets can be smoked on the website. The booking system will also offer the best options: en.voyages-sncf.com

In reading some reviews, I noticed that there is little emphasis (in some cases even omission) to distinguish between two different railway services. Many users attack Thello, mistakenly passing it off as a TGV. In reality, things are different. To clarify: Thello is a set of long-distance railway services, designed to connect Italy and France, carried out by the Trenitalia-Veolia Transdev (TVT) consortium. TVT rents the carriages from Trenitalia, while only the locomotive is rented from Akiem, a subsidiary of the SNCF group. Therefore, do not make the mistake of making the equation Thello=French railways. The level of the TGV transport service in France (precisely carried out by the SNCF) is of decidedly excellent quality, at the level of the most advanced European standards. I have personally been using the TGV for about 20 years, that is to say since our "evolved" Italy insisted on having the ETR trains (progenitors of the current Frecciarossa) travel on the tracks where steam locomotives ran until a few decades earlier. In short, the usual Italian things were done; only with the Frecciarossa project did we finally understand that it is not logical to design a "railway Ferrari" and then have it run on a dirt road. But we got there in a structural way only starting from 2005, while in the rest of Europe high speed has already been a consolidated reality for decades. Then obviously no railway system is free from defects. This is obviously not intended to be an official defense of the French railways (which are also not free from flaws) but only a clarification. Furthermore, the fact that the homeland of the fake nationalized and decadent Trenitalia is throwing itself into acting as judge on other railway systems... definitely makes you smile.

We decided to get to Paris by high-speed TGV. From Strasbourg to Paris about 3 hours. The train is comfortable - in the 2nd class carriage there are 4 seats, and in the 1st class there are 3 seats in one row, but both have comfortable seats, the carriage is spacious, there are shelves for luggage. The carriage has good sound insulation, the train flies quickly and smoothly. If you buy tickets in advance, there are additional discounts, you can choose good seats, we had seats in a 2-story carriage - on the second floor. Large tables. In 1st class there are sockets near each seat, but the Internet was paid. It was quiet in the carriages; people came out of the cabin with mobile phones to talk, so as not to disturb others. There was a trolley with tea, coffee, etc. - food at an additional cost, even in 1st class. It’s fast and convenient, and if you buy a ticket in advance, it will be cheaper. The train met our expectations.
Basel to Paris within 3 hours is fine. But the train is old, dirty and the toilets probably give you motion sickness. The advantage over flying is of course that you are directly in the city.

Absolutely to be avoided! Taken (fortunately) for the outward journey on December 5th with 1 hour delay, dilapidated bunks and very dirty bathrooms; I wonder how it is possible that certain trains are still running! Luckily we made the return trip with the TGV: very punctual, clean bathrooms and they also gave our little girl a coloring kit.

My friend and I were traveling from Paris to Poitiers on the TGV, I saw it for the first time, it felt as if there was a spaceship in front of you))))) we got into the carriage, it was so clean, cozy, the seats were large and comfortable. We got there very quickly, I just dozed off and already arrived. A great way to save time, although not exactly cheap.

This is the first TGV born in France, far away in terms of comfort and performance from our AV, not to mention Italo. The obsolescence of the train, however, does not affect the convenience of the route since the arrival (gare de Lion) is in the center of Paris. 1st class has only three seats, so these are wide and comfortable. There is an employee who comes by to offer (non-alcoholic) drinks or to sell snacks and even packaged dishes: to be avoided like poison, as they are worthy of the worst airlines. Clean bathrooms, also because the train was not full, but there were empty seats. The biggest regret is the enormous waste of time in the section from Turin (with strange stops in Oulx and Bardonecchia) to Lyon (stops in Modane, St Jean de Maurienne and Chambery) due to the very low speed, in addition to the aforementioned stops. The final stretch, from Lyon, is really short (two and a half hours). However, everything is faster and more comfortable than the car and than the plane, as well as being cheaper (1st class, return 110 euros).

Avoid!!!!!! Horrible !!!!!! And yet on the train bed (the best quality!!! :() It's an old train that smells bad, noisy, very dirty. I wonder how it is possible that a train in such poor condition can have authorization to run....(broken electrical panel held together with tape, the neon on the ceiling flashes constantly, the cupboard door slams all night because it cannot be locked, the height between two beds is very low +/- 40 cm, not adjustable because it is stuck ) At breakfast (included in the price of the ticket) there were no more croissants at 8:00! Late arrival and no information!

my review concerns the TURIN Porta Susa - PARIS Gare de Lyon route, I must say that my opinion is more than positive, especially when compared to the flight. In fact, it took me about the same time, obviously considering the departure from home and the arrival at the hotel, but I didn't get tired and I spent less than half, despite traveling in first class, without the additional time and costs of the transfer to and from the airport. The TGV proved to be a very punctual, clean, silent means of transport, with very comfortable reclining seats. I suffered a bit of motion sickness, but it's a personal problem, perhaps reducible by choosing a forward-facing seat when booking online.
We did the Munich Paris route and everything was perfect. Easy access without queues, you simply enter the password at your seat and wait until you reach 320km. Great onboard service. Go first class.

I used it on a tour from Geneva to Paris. I was assigned a seat on the first floor of a two-story building, but the view wasn't particularly good, the glass was dirty, the train was shaking violently, and compared to Japan's Shinkansen trains, the ride wasn't very comfortable. There are two rows of seats on each side, and there is a box seat in the center of each car where four people can sit facing each other, but half of the seats around this are fixed facing opposite to the direction of travel. I had envisioned riding it at least once, but it was a disappointment. I think it's a faster and more comfortable means of transportation than the bus.
With the TGV in Paris in 6 hours. 39 euros per nose with the Europe saver price. Back for 59 euros. Much more relaxing than flying!

Allow a day to recover! you can't sleep, noisy train, people shouting (but this is the rudeness of the passengers!!) heating at the limit of bearable, there's absolutely no air! As for the bathrooms... they are what the bathroom of a packed train can become after 12 hours of travel! The staff is friendly. I paid 100 euros for a return trip from Bologna to Paris in a 6-berth berth. I recommend using it only if you can get a low-cost reservation for 30 euros (booking 3 months in advance). Consider arriving at Gare de Lyon at least an hour early... it's huge and you risk missing the train trying to find where it leaves from! half an hour delay both on the way there and on the way back!

My wife and I took the TGV from Paris to Lyon and back last week.  We LOVED it.  The seats were very comfortable and the ride was smooth!  We flew into CDG airport on American Airlines, and it was only a 5 minute walk from customs to the TGV station.  (The station is actually in the airport.)  The station in Lyon was very convenient also.    On the return trip I visited the bar car and got some wine to enjoy as we glided smoothly toward Paris.  WHY can't we have train service like this in America!!!!

My husband and I have been going to Paris every year for more than 30 years now, and during the first few years, we always went by train, leaving late in the evening from Florence and finding ourselves in the morning at Gare de LYon, ...how beautiful!!!!. Then the low cost flights arrived and we converted to the plane, also because the sleeper carriage was really expensive. After many years, I felt the desire to try the sleeper carriage again, encouraged also by the not so negative opinions that I found and, despite the cost, I would say exorbitant, I let myself be tempted by the convenience of taking the train home in the evening and getting off in the city of Paris fresh and rested as a rose. I had never done it!!!!!. We arrived at the station Florence Campo di Marte at 9.30pm, a Trenitalia employee passes by on the platform asking "Who goes to Paris?". She tells us that the train has been cancelled. (It's useful to know that they were still selling the ticket on the Trenitalia website and at a high price, even though the train hadn't even left Rome and therefore they knew very well that it wouldn't be there.) So my husband, I and another thirty unfortunate people of all nationalities were boarded on the FLORENCE-MILAN Frecciarossa, where we would have found a connection with the VENICE-PARIS train at midnight. (We were all already tired since we wanted to go to sleep in our expensively booked bed at 10.) The Trenitalia staff had guaranteed us the same treatment for which we had paid "of course" the young lady had said, instead, we saw ourselves on board, tired and [--] on very dirty, uncomfortable bunks, and in the carriage where we were the sink was missing the door.......yes the closing door, ..how nice to wash in the corridor.... We spend our stay in Paris, and, we find ourselves on the platform at the time set for the return and.... no train. After a while, some unhelpful guys arrive and tell us that there are technical problems and that the train will leave two hours late. In reality the conductor was missing, and we had to wait for him to arrive from Dijon, not just around the corner. This time the bed was there, although without any shock absorber. However, there was no food in the restaurant car, there weren't even croissants, which had to be saved for breakfast the next morning, the coffees were only freeze-dried and counted, we took the last two, the others made do. A scandalous treatment, given the prices paid. They gave us a flyer with instructions to ask for compensation, but I doubt I will have an answer, also because some French gentlemen told us that a consumer consortium has even been established in France for the protests against the THELLO company. What can I say,,,,, never again in life.

First class upper deck Paris to Beziers - great service, comfy seats, excellent service, fabulous food, quiet, peaceful, on time...need I go on?  The way to travel.  Something British Rail (or whatever its called these days) need to look at.

Personally, I had a great time both on the outward and return journey. My wife and I left Bologna on the night of 10/23/2013 and returned on 10/27/2013. The train was punctual and clean, bathrooms in excellent condition, very kind staff. For 70 euros per person return it is perfect. Definitely an experience to repeat. To enjoy Paris I recommend the month of October and to avoid weekends so as to find few people and what's more the climate is still mild.

Carriages not very clean, carpet everywhere and also visibly dusty. The route from Milan almost before Lyon is very slow. Overall punctual, the offers are ok but 7/8 of the journey then the plane is better.

We traveled from Paris to Nice last month with the express TGV, and I was impressed by the speed and comfort. The train experience feels so good, compared to the hassles of air travel. Gare de Lyon is accessible by metro, and from the Nice station, you can walk to most central hotels. This is definitely my favorite mode of transport within Europe. E tickets were bought on line, and printed at home. Trains were on time, and arrived on time. I did not find the cost prohibitive.I recommend this method over airlines.

We took the TGV from Paris to London and i have to say it was so relaxing, I pre booked 2nd class with a meal and a couple of drinks,storeyour bags in the racks as you board no problems ,plenty of space in the cabins, bigger seats than aircraft and you can what the French country side go past  have a nap and before you know it ..thru the tunnel and out the other side..highly recommend this form of transport.we arrived at St Pancras straight out of the station grabbed a cab and off to our hotel...tickety boo..easy as pie...loved it!!!

...it is worth getting to Paris by TGV. The prices are very affordable and the trip is fast and comfortable. TGV convoys have become somewhat outdated. They do not offer catering in any of their categories, you have to pay for it in the cafeteria, although they do take it to the first seats. The speed in some areas is high speed (more than 300km/h), although in others it is lower (160km/h). The trip between Spain and Paris lasts just over five hours, leaving us at the Montparnasse station, a few metro stations from the heart of the Parisian capital.

(This review is on a TGV trip between Marseille and Paris.)Most travelers seem to expect four essential qualities from a "high speed" train: Speed, comfort, cleanliness and a reasonable price. The TGV meets all four nicely. When you pass cars on a parallel major highway in a wink, and you know they're doing 120km +, that's fast. And the other three "musts" are well met, too.I spent the few extra euros for 1st Class. The big (only?) difference is that the seats are wider: it's 2 + 1 seating rather than the 2 + 2 in 2nd Class. (The leg room looks to be the same.)A few tips and things to be aware of:- If you want to buy food or drink on board, bring cash. No credit cards are accepted.- There's no wi-fi aboard. (This omission, and the preceding above, resulted in my docking one star.)- When you reserve, you can choose between regular and 'quiet' cars, the latter meaning that cell phone use is prohibited. (I almost gave them that star back for this one!)- If you plan to do some sightseeing en route -- and it's wonderful! -- try to book a seat on the opposite side from the rising or setting sun.- Although the sightseeing's obviously better from the upper level, if you've got really bulky or heavy luggage, remember that you'll probably have to horse it up the stairs with you.- There's a very small boarding time window: it opens about 20 minutes prior to departure and closes promptly at 5 minutes before. Be warned!If you're debating the train vs. flying, at least between Paris and Marseille, it's no contest. The TGV wins, hands down.

Dated 24 October 2013. Night round trip from Milan to Paris and back. Luckily we were in a cabin for six with children in tow among friends. Disturbing journey with sudden braking, unusable and smelly bathrooms...cabin door that wouldn't close. Dilapidated train. No operator spoke Italian even though I admit they were kind. Nobody was able to tell us if the arrival time in Milan would have taken into account the time change. Absolutely never negative again! Given the prices and inconveniences, next time I fly!

We took the fast TGV deluxe train from Marseilles to Paris.  We had a rental car and arrived at the rail station near downtown Marseilles where we dropped the car off and walked 5 minutes to the train station.  We had our tickets pre-ordered and printed. The info desk there was helpful and told us to wait and watch the screens to see at which platform our train would arrive.  This was posted.  The signage train cars was not superb but when we asked, we were provided with the information.  The train was two-storey. We were on the lower floor.  There was plenty of room for luggage.  The train was indeed very fast.  Our GPS device measured speeds up to 260 km/hr.  There were 4 or 5 stops between Marseilles and Paris.  The train was quiet and steady.  It arrived at exactly the minute it was supposed to.  We were amazed.  Travel time was about 3.5 hours.  In a car, this distance would take about 8.5 hours.  With the gas prices in Europe, the 100 Euro ticket was a great deal, especially considering the reduced travel time.  There was a snack bar in one of the cars but we didn't try it.

Booked TGV Frankfurt - Avignon that week. First  class was really cheap by using early booking conditions. Train left on time and arrived on time. First class compartment (sat upper deck) provides vrey comfortable seats with recline, good light etc. Toilets clean as well. Anyhow the included snack was a cold ( from fridge) chese sandwich and only rose wine available. Not an issue but SNCF advertises to be top of the top !!!! So what ? Internet does not work. Maybe mistaken by me or in fact not available. As Sunday eve the train became really full people with 2nd class just entered the coach and took place in 1st class. It took a while untill the conductor identified them and ask them to relocate. Some sectors only are accesable with high speed. Others as usual old SNCF conditiones like old rails, small curves etc limiting the speed. at Avignon TGV station in the evening only 2 taxis waiting. Clear info about the convenient bus to downtown is missing. Maybe taxis ask to stop infomation to earn 15 Euro for the down town trip if they are available. TGV has to learn that first class service does not end by leaving the coach!

Traveled from Brussels to Paris CDG Airport;train arrives just below the air-port. And then on to Lausanne and back to Paris,all in II class..Seats were  firm and comfortable enough for the shorter journeys we did. Did not use catering facilities. Trip was short so did not try the catering. Though going by what is available on trains, best either to eat or get something packed beforehandUnfortunately,on Lausanne section,window glass was very dirty and spotted,so could not photograph the scenery  properly,.Trip from Brussels was at high speed,while the trip to Lausanne was 'slower' in the inclines.Trains were absolutely punctual and its a good idea for visitors to reach the station well before departure.Be very sure from which exact station the train is supposed to leave as TGVs can originate from different stations in the same city ,as in Paris.Locating the departure platforms can take time as certain main stations have platforms at different orientations and locations.Make allowance for that.Coach numbers are on small  electronic displays near the coach doors,and seat numbers to are at the top side of the head rest in electronic display.Door auto-shut and interim stops are very brief.So do not step  out the train mid-stop.Watch out for announcements of up-coming destination,to enable yourself to gather your stuff and reach the exit before hand.That will avoid a last minute scramble.If one plans accommodation near TGV stations,it really is a quick and convenient way to get around France and adjoining Europe.Fast,convenient and well recommended.Book early if possible to get better prices.

We traveled by TGV from Paris (from Gare de Lyon) to Avignon and from Dijon to Paris this trip. Last time, we traveled by TGV from Paris to Bordeau and back.  We have previously traveled from Paris to Milan on TGV.If you are traveling in France and do not need to stop, this is the way to go. We went first class, and it was clean, quiet and comfortable.  The dining facilities are basic but work (not catering for gluten free other than chips.The only hassle is the bags.  As we are traveling internationally, we have a substantial bag each and hand luggage.  Leaving our bags near the door unattended is a bit of a leap of faith, but it has never been a problem.

Our first class trip on the TGV from Gare de Lyon to Turino Porta Susa was not a good start to our journey to Milan. We booked in Australia via RailEurope. It was not possible to choose the seats and not only were we travelling backwards but the view was obscured by the window pillar.  Additionally there were two trains on the platform and ours was the front train. There was nothing explaining this and no-one nearby to help.  We had to dash to the beginning of the platform to find some help.  There were no porters or coach attendants to help get the luggage onto the train and no indication of which end of the coach had the luggage racks. To top it off, the young woman who takes food orders completely ignored our section of the carriage.  We were glad to get on the Frecciarossa for the trip to Milan which was in complete contrast to our TGV experience.

We had to make our way from Paris to Frankfurt and decided not to fly but caught the TGV from Gare de Est. It was one off the best decisions I made for our European holiday. In worked out extremely cheaper than flying and catching taxis to and from airports plus it was more comfortable.I did book on the Bahn network which is the German site and it cost EUR69 for first class. The train is quite luxurious with comfortable seats. The seats were in the upper deck and you had beautiful views all the way. It was great being able to get up and walk around and not confined like you are in a airplane. A cold breakfast was served which was very delicious. It was incredible seeing on the screen the train reaching speeds of up to 320 kilometres per hour. The railway station in Frankfurt was only 500 metres from our apartment so that was a bonus as well. All in all a very pleasant experience and great way between point A and point B.

To catch the TGV in route Paris/Milano is a wonderful experience:Paris Gare de Lyon to Milano Porta Garibaldi. Gare de Lyon is one  of the most beautiful train stations in Europe, and if you take the train ver early in the morning, is like seeing paris waking up.We took the TGV in wintertime, first class coach.Its a lovely, classie  and speedy journey through the snowie fields in France.About lunch time you will be crossing the Alps and the villages, from the french side to the italian one.Being a train lover, TGV represents one of the highest train experiences. Enjoy the ride!

Took the TGV from Calais Frethun to Paris which was very quick and arrived exactly on time,but with a 20 minutes or so wait in Lille. The real adventure began with the Duplex service to Barcelona. We had first class seats on the upper deck,(not as expensive as you might think),all the way to Figeres in Spain. I couldn't believe it when we reached Valence in the Rhone Alps in about 2 hours. From then on the scenery is fantastic as you cross and recross the Rhone all the way to the the Riviera. It slows a bit then but that's good because there's lots to look at. At FIgeres you leave the French train and walk across the platform onto the Spanish train to Girona and Barcelona. A great journey and much more relaxing than flying.

Both journeys were overcrowded and hot, no snacks/drinks on the way as the bar was closed but now thankful of that as the return journey snacks/drinks were dismal. If you can sleep all the way its a fast way to travel.
These trains are very comfortable and fast, when we are in them it feels like we are standing still and they reach an incredible 320km/h. A good choice for Europe.
Thought it would be a long trip (more than 50 km) from Paris to Geneva but it was over sooner than we expected. Very smooth journey. Meal on board the train was served quite promptly.

I used it for the Paris-Nantes-Paris route and it was very peaceful. The train is reasonably comfortable, but it doesn't compare to the Russian Sapsan. The station at CDG airport is convenient, within the airport, but you should be very careful because they only announce the platform 15 minutes in advance. At this station it is common to have two trains stopped facing each other on the same platform, so it is recommended to enter as soon as the train arrives to avoid surprises.

Took THELLO 8 weeks. to Bologna for Paris, return Thello 21 September Paris Bologna. Worse than the worst of the old Palatines. Same carriages even more run down, toilets unusable since departure from both Bologna and Paris, usual, painful bed kit, increasingly precarious and uncourteous staff Roberta Pesaro
The high and medium speed TGV trains are very good, comfortable, fast and, above all, punctual. Never be late, otherwise you will miss your train. seats must respect the timetable.

I took thello to and from Paris. It's convenient because you can sleep on it at night and then you have two almost full days in Paris more. The train is recovered from 40 years ago: it's the slightly modernized Milan-Sicily workers' train. If you travel alone, you have to be lucky in finding the right travel companions, who in any case are mostly foreigners or students. I found nice people as well as hateful people. 6 berths per compartment, 10 compartments per carriage: the compartments were clean, but the bathroom is better used in the station! the "adjustable" heating: either hot or cold or off. The sheets and blankets provided were clean, the pillows a little less so. the staff is very helpful, even if they mostly only speak English and French. Remember to always give all the necessary documents to the staff: identity card, passport, visa, residence permit, if you don't want to be woken up at 5 in the morning by the customs officers. Only half an hour's delay between Venice and Paris: I thought worse. A great experience for those who want to try to take a dive into the past of night rail transport!

We took the TGV from Frankfurt to Paris to board the night train to Barcelona. In short: the journey with the TGV was a great experience. At least from the German-French border you can go to Paris at 320 km/h without making a stopover. We booked 1st class for a really cheap price. A delicious menu was served at the table and drinks were constantly available. TGV: simply recommended and time-saving!!

From past reviews I thought I would get on an animal carriage, but instead I found clean bunks, all the bedding that was mentioned on the site and the person in charge of my carriage, even though he didn't speak Italian, was very nice and willing to help us, we communicated in English!! Sore point is that the bathrooms are cholera-like after a few hours!!! In our carriage there were all 4-berths and it was crowded but I saw terrible scenes in the carriages with 6-berths, entire caravans of Arab and North African families with lots of children... It must have been a horrible experience traveling there!!

I haven't traveled by train since university and unfortunately I see that things haven't improved: Thello's price is attractive compared to other means of transport but unfortunately the quality of service is mediocre. The carriages are very old and not clean, the linen provided is not adequately sanitized, the air conditioning is very noisy on the way out and not working on the way back, however it is not adjustable. The staff, who were kind to us, only speak French or English. The journey wasn't comfortable and sleeping wasn't easy either... next time we'll change the means of transport.

When you live in France, you must take your kids to Paris on a TGV.  That's what we did and they thoroughly enjoyed the five hour ride from Cannes without having to change trains.  Make sure to book first class as being stuck in crowded second class can be a bit of a pain, even on a fancy TGV.  It was a smooth and convenient ride into the center of Paris (Gare de Lyon) without the hassle of having to drive to an airport, deal with luggage & security and painful airport transfers in Paris.  TGV vs. EasyJet.  My vote goes to SNCF.  They are friendly and there are no hidden fees!

I'm traveling with my family, my husband has problems with the plane so I train: - on the outward journey Milan Paris 2 hours late at departure and no one gives you clear explanations, we go up and very dirty berths - cabin for 4: identical to the one for 6, horrible pillows (if you can call them that) and terrible paper sheets, everything to prepare and no one asks you if you need help... broken window and air conditioning not working properly... but they give you a bottle of water - but the real thing the bathrooms are terrible, very dirty, unhygienic and inadequate for the number of people present in the carriage. THEY ARE VERY OLD TRAINS (the same ones I took 40 years ago to go to Sicily) WHICH OFFER UNACEPTABLE ACCOMMODATIONS TODAY. Furthermore, even in the 4-person cabin I spent more than I would have spent on the plane, let alone with the two/three or single cabins which cost more than double!!!!

Fast, safe and punctual. The TGV is one of the best ways to get around Europe. It has an affordable cost, comfort and speed. When I went from Paris to Brussels I found the onboard service to be bad and very slow when entering Belgium. Other than that it was very good.

Three weeks ago I took the TGV from Turin to Paris, because my mother has a crazy fear of flying. I bought the tickets in April (yes, by phone, so I was sure of the super prices: 25 EUR each for the outward journey in second class, 45 EUR for the return journey in first class :-) My father carries a cane and is 80 years old, we had 3 suitcases. The train arrived on time, it was clean, the seats were excellent, comfortable and spacious. I imagined ending up in the usual cattle wagon typical for this time of year (on certain Trenitalia trains throughout the year!) but instead the 5 hours flew by, we were also lucky enough to have very kind and polite neighbors. We arrived early on both the outward and return journeys. Personally I prefer the plane, but if I were to return to Paris I think I will repeat the experience with TGV.

We took the TGV from Basel to Antibes, then Antibes to Paris and Paris to Basel. After reading so much about the French TGV service we were looking forward to these trips. In short the service is poor (over booked trains, French passangers who are reluctant to moved from reserved seats, poor food, trains are old and dirty and the service is slow) and compared to other high speed European rail services the TGV ranks pretty close to a last. We were stuck on-board during a 5 hour delay near St Raphael and all they offered was water, no explanations or reasons and air con is average at best. Save your money and fly...

This is the second occasion I have used the TGV from Paris to Nice on this occasion I became particularly aware of the poor quality of the food and its service. This never ceases to amaze me,we are constantly bombarded in the UK by the  fact that France and the French are the Masters of Cuisine. Not on this occasion,it is at best similar to the catering offered in the lower divisions of the English Football League.On a 6 to 8 hour journey buy your food in the Gard de Lyon.Oh and the train.Traveled first class.In relation to rail travel in the UK it's cheaper it's far more comfortable and is definitely Premier League

When we left Milan for Paris they changed our compartment because one bed wouldn't go down. First class!! We saw the welcome kit in the photo, we had to ask for the pillows and towel from the carriage manager who, kindly tried to solve the various problems, much more important than ours, of other passengers, in the end he managed to find us 2 pillows out of 3 towels 1 out of 3. Cleanliness, let's spread a merciful veil!! The only positive side is the 80 x 190 cm bunks, which are quite comfortable. I don't even want to think what second class might be like. Next time by car!!! Or rather on a scooter.

We were in Paris the week of August, traveling with Thello on the way out and with the TGV on the way back. The TGV is as good as Thello is bad. THELLO: I definitely can't comment on the company. The train arrived an hour late. The on-board staff spoke exclusively French and a little English, saying they did not understand Italian. The sleeping cabin was old and dirty, the air conditioning had no intermediate settings (either hot or cold), the power sockets didn't work and the door didn't close well. Travel bag and slippers were not provided. The bathroom was dirty and in very poor condition. For the sum of €288 for two I expected much more. I also believe that misleading advertising is being done on the company's website. TGV: excellent train, comfortable, quiet and above all clean. The staff was friendly and also spoke Italian.

The TGV connects Milan Porta Garibaldi to Paris Gare de Lyon in just over seven hours. If at first it seems like a lot, it should be calculated that there are no waiting times at check-in and check-out, but above all that you start from the center of Milan and arrive in the center of Paris. Another important thing not to be underestimated is freedom regarding luggage. Since we can then decide the dates in advance (as in our case), the prices are competitive (€70 per person return trip in 2nd class and €140 per person return trip in 1st class). The train is quiet and the journey comfortable. Importantly, avoid the bar-restaurant carriage, since for a snack (sandwich-drink-coffee) you risk spending more than the ticket. The cleanliness of the carriages is good and the toilets are cleaned during the journey.

The Thello is a train that is too expensive for the service it offers. I had the bad idea to take it last July. It's dirty, old, and stinks. The air conditioning doesn't work in all carriages and that's why I think not only the cleaning is rough but also the maintenance. I absolutely do not recommend it.

We traveled with Thello on 19 August 2013 from Paris to Milan with 6 of us occupying a single compartment. Once we got into the carriage and reached our compartment, in order to sit, we had to clean and disinfect the seats and the compartment where we would place our suitcases with sanitizing wipes because everything was dirty and full of dust. A towel falls on the floor and as we crawled across it to pick it up we noticed that it had changed color from uniform matte black to its original shiny blue. You can't imagine the disgust, but it's okay, after all it's only about ten hours. But the worst has not yet arrived!!. Once the children have been settled, we proceed to prepare the beds for the adults, we open a blanket, stuffed into the bag with the pillow, and we immediately notice that it was SPOILED WITH ANIMAL EXCREMENTS, smelly and dirty. I then ask the service staff, given that upon departure they recommended via loudspeaker that they were available for every need, and in an unkind manner they replied that they had no other blankets available for replacement. The air conditioning, which they pass off as ADJUSTABLE, is a lie. The button doesn't work and the temperature is decided on the general panel of the carriage by the service staff. At customs we were stopped for about 40 minutes and the air was turned off. Imagine that sauna, windows closed and people gasping for a breath of fresh air, plus, what a boost to your health when you turn it back on!!! I understand that the cost of the trip is low compared to other means of transport, the idea is excellent but does the traveler buy cleanliness and hygiene by paying for the ticket or not? It's a shame because it's a winning idea but the management, as usual, is rubbish. It would be enough to DO the necessary cleaning to make travelers travel with dignity and it would be a very comfortable train to reach Paris.

I set out with great enthusiasm to travel by train from Rome to Paris with Thellò but already at Termini station the enthusiasm gave way to disappointment. The train is the old Palatine put back on the tracks, the carriages are positioned with an unknown criterion so you have to walk along the entire platform to find the right one and don't ask for the staff because they won't help you. The interior (two-seater sleeper) is spartan to say the least with a mini sink where I found soap and a towel on the way out but not on the way back. I asked the staff the reason for this lack and I was told... IF IT IS NOT THERE IT IS NOT THERE... The common bathrooms on the carriage become impracticable after a couple of hours of travel and the bad smell spreads along the entire corridor. Considering the cost, you can expect much more.

The train is comfortable, punctual. The only problem are the steps for those who want to climb with heavy suitcases. The steps are high and a person who traveled alone like me needs someone to help them climb up with their bags.

We have just returned from Paris: the journey was made by Thello train from Milan Centrale: never again!!!! The train was very crowded, almost all non-EU citizens carrying packed suitcases with them. You get on the train and you can't sit down, you have to already lie down on the "berths". We had the most infamous ones, that is, the low ones, which have the armrests of the backrest transformed into a second bunk bed above the head and feet. we practically had 5 cm. of space from the flea-filled arm. We spread the provided sheet on the seat and amen, we tried to sleep. The bunk had 6 seats; luckily only two other Pakistani boys were sleeping on the other open bunks. During the journey we were brutally woken up three times: the first for the tickets and the identity card, the second by the financial police who came in with the dogs and the third because they were looking for a certain guy who was in another compartment. The train has a very narrow corridor, if you meet another person it's a problem, if they have luggage it's impossible to pass. The restaurant car was 10 cars ahead of ours and once we arrived it didn't have coffee. I'm not talking about the bathrooms... the sink and a person standing there didn't fit.. This is not having respect for the people who pay for a ticket (among other things not even cheap!!!) an elderly person or with even a small physical defect is unable to travel on this train!1! Never again!!!!

Milan Paris by TGV is not to be discarded a priori, the train is comparable to the red arrow therefore excellent soundproofing and good comfort, the problem is that it travels at high speed only from Lyon onwards as there are not yet suitable rails in the construction phase. 7 hours from Milan to Paris with three trains a day throughout the year ensure excellent route coverage. I would like to recommend it to everyone, suggesting that you book in advance (€25) starting price.

I repeat what I have read in the other reviews: the thello is a very expensive train, dirty beyond belief, smelly blankets and pillows, dirty and sticky floors. the hostess service is practically non-existent, I was more than an hour late both on the way there and on the way back... It's not a train, it's a traveling dustbin!

We regularly take the TGV (and also its twins, Thalys and Eurostar). Fantastic means of transport (in first class) to Paris and beyond, Germany, the Netherlands, Great Britain,...Relaxed trips at 300 km/h, drinks and snacks in 1st class, comfort, in short, we are fans.

We took the TGV Duplex from Frankfurt to Paris for the first time, about 7 hours in total, but the time flew by. The SNCF offers in 1st class are surprisingly inexpensive for a total of 156.00 euros there and back. Very punctual departures and arrivals, the comfort in first class is excellent, bilingual support during the journey and a beautiful landscape that rushes past at speeds of 300 km/h. From my point of view, the so-called on-board bistro is negative with a ridiculously meager selection of food, slow service and high prices. On the way back it was from Marseille to Mulhouse, so it wasn't open at all for 4 hours because the staff supposedly showed up at night. This is reminiscent of the worst level of Federal Railway service that one occasionally experiences. Otherwise highly recommended.

As soon as I got on the train I didn't have a good impression as the carpet on the floor was very dirty and so were the seats, but the best was yet to come! when we arrived in modane they made us get off due to a technical problem and left us there for more than an hour without anyone bothering to give us information. The staff was very rude and when I went to ask for information, the conductor told me in a less than polite tone not to disturb him because he was angry!!! Him!!!!!!!! they also say they sell Paris metro tickets but they have increased prices: a real steal considering that it is always public transport!! Ps our train was delayed for almost three hours!!! Shame!!!!!!!
A squalid train delayed by 4 hours both on the outward and return journey, indecent service, not even the air conditioning worked

Just returned from a return TGV trip Paris - Perpignan. The train rides were great - had upstairs seats giving us great views going through France. Booked early so got good pricesOn the trip out we stayed in Paris after getting there by Eurostar for a sight seeing day and night. On the way home I' m thinking I should have gone to Lille rather than go back to Paris and have to cross from Gare de Lyon to Gare du Nord.On the return home our engine packed up at Montpelier and we had to wait an hour for them to reattach us to a new engine. Luckily I had allowed for delays when booking my connection to Eurostar.Food on the train is poor and vastly overpriced but overall the TGV is a great option.

We caught the high speed train from Strasbourg to Paris and found it a comfortable and easy way to cross the country.Boarding the train at Strasbourg was a bit hectic because this was our first time using the syem and the locals do not like lining up at all. After waiting for others to board so as not to hold up people while figuring out where to store our luggage, we were the second last group to get on. Stowing luggage was a breeze with plenty of room in both the lower and upper decks.I was looking forward to feeling the train get up to 300 kmh but thought at first we were not going to reach top speed as the display was only showing route and not speeds. Due to the smoothness and quiet of the train I was estimating we were only travelling around 100 kmh when suddenly the speed was displayed on the screen. Topping 318kmh and easily cruising along at 300 we were into Paris in no time.

Going from Milan Garibaldi to Paris Gare de Lyon with 29 euros and a clean and comfortable train frankly you can't ask for more. Well done to the SNCF. On the other hand, I went to Zurich with an ex-Cisalpine etr460 of our railways and I found it really dirty and noisy with four toilets out of order and I had to go to the 1st class toilets to relieve myself.

The TGV out of Paris to Geneva was awesome!  The train inside was super clean and the ride smooth and FAST!  Here in the U.S. we have Amtrak but it pales in comparison to the TGV!  If we had more time for the trip, most likely I would have preferred a chartered bus to appreciate the surrounding landscape(s) but since we were on a short trip, the TGV served us well and delivered us safely to Geneva!

We use the Paris-Montpellier TGV line more often than the others (Bordeaux, Brest, Lille, London or Amsterdam) but it is still a marvel of technology. First class is a cozy little nest that allows you to travel without any fatigue, but second class is also very pleasant. If you are a foreign tourist, know that you can visit France very easily thanks to this high-speed train (TGV) network of French technology. You often save more time than going to an airport to catch a plane and the network of high-speed trains allows you to go almost anywhere in France. For those who like to travel light, you can have your luggage delivered to your destination the day after it is collected (count 35€ for the first bag and 17€ for subsequent bags). In addition, you can enjoy the French landscapes which is hardly possible by plane. For the record, this high-speed train obtained a world speed record at 574.8 km/h in 2007. I promise, I don't work at the SNCF (Société Nationale des Chemins de Fer français) but we French are proud of this train ;-)

We wanted to leave at 9.34pm on 7 July 2013 from Florence Campo di Marte to Paris but the "train" arrived almost 5 hours late without any night arrangements!!! In other words all piled into seven normal carriages for a 12 hour journey! No refreshments on board: the aim was probably to crash us before arriving in Paris! Train arriving from Rome Termini LURIDO with bathrooms already in Florence without running water. Similar problems for the return from Paris arriving two hours late. The bunks were dirty, with broken and tattered headboards, compartment doors that struggled to close and bathrooms with a foul smell. The only thing clean and sterilized are the sheets!

My luggage was stolen from the train. It was a gray and black trolley bag did not remain. It contained jewelry, clothes and lots of personal effects. The train left central Naploli bound for Rome Termini at 8.17pm and was delayed by 10 minutes. I train my luggage in the luggage prep room and then when I arrived at my destination my luggage was gone. There is no security around the train to make sure this didn't happen. I am outraged by this event as a tourist.

We left at 11.38pm, departing Milan and going to Paris. Once we got on the train, we immediately noticed the carriages used by Trenitalia in the 80s and which had been modernized in a hurry. We risked being robbed by a non-EU citizen, we reported the case to the inspector, who did nothing. We go to sleep and... surprise, at 00:30 they knock to ask for the boarding pass and documents which will be returned upon arrival. Then, to make matters worse, the financiers show up at 1.30 am asking us questions about the trip, the cash in their possession, etc. While the petty thief goes unpunished. Sunbeds measuring 1.80m long and 60cm wide, a delight! I strongly advise against it, better to take the TGV first class during the day!

We booked three months in advance, and the seats were going fast! After checking the departure times and prices, we decided to get the 1st Class as it was just slightly more expensive than the 2nd Class.We had wider seats that reclined, and were served a welcome drink immediately. Then we were served a full breakfast which was quite filling (only for passengers going to Switzerland though - it did stop twice in SE France). We were served one more drink before arriving in Geneva.Not crowded, quiet and fast. Best way to go from Paris to Geneva.

After finishing a week in Paris, we chose to get the TGV to Cannes for a week in the French Riveria (around a 4 hour journey).The train was beautiful, comfy and clean (especially compared to English trains) and it was quite easy to sleep the journey away. The train was mostly filled with french people but there were some other English people. All announcements were in french, however, it was pretty simple to translate what the driver was saying.The carriages were quite, even people with babies took them out if they started crying. The journey was fast and took us straight into the centre of Cannes - couldn't have been better! Wish there was a similar service of such standard in the UK.

A nightmare to travel with this incompetent company. On Friday 15th July my family, made up of me, my wife and an 11 year old daughter together with a family of friends with two children, a classmate of mine and a 7 year old child, went to the Florence Campo di Marte station with regular reservations for Paris destination Disneyland. The first train is announced with 15 min. then late with 25, but so far everything is normal. Finally it arrives we split up as we have two different carriages and we get on and as soon as I enter the sleeper carriage I receive a phone call from my friend who tells me that they are on the ground and cannot get on because two carriages left in Rome are missing due to a breakdown, not even having time to realize the fact that the train is leaving again with our friends and other people on the tracks without any assistance or explanations. Only after many minutes, prompted by our innumerable complaints towards the train conductor, who was also absolutely indignant at how the situation had been handled, given that the problem had existed since the departure from Rome, a person appeared on the platforms saying that a replacement bus had been organized without knowing what time it would arrive. It should be noted that at one o'clock he had not yet arrived and the station toilets closed at 9.30 pm, at which point our disappointed and desperate friends returned home and organized themselves for a flight from Pisa which fortunately was available on the morning of the 16th with an additional cost of €600. Among other things, our trip was also a disaster, the air conditioning did not work, the cell phone could not be charged because there was no electricity and, finally, blankets, sheets and pillows untouchables. If I were you I would avoid it.

This time I used it from Geneva to Paris/Lyon station. It's enough if you only need to travel for a little over 3 hours. I don't know how fast it is, but first of all, the vehicle is old and poor quality. It's still the same as the car I rode about 10 years ago, with the seats being narrow and narrow. Of course, you cannot change the direction of the seats, and half of the seats face the opposite direction of travel. When I rode it before, I thought it was a quiet vehicle, but I also noticed some noise and shaking, probably due to the age of the vehicle. Japan's Shinkansen trains don't shake much, and the seats are spacious and I thought they were good overall. I think it's good if you're just using it because it's cheap and there's no passport check.

We live in Surrey and so a journey into Central London is not a first choice. We chose to drive to Ebbsfleet, park the car there for a week (cost £57.00) and take the Eurostar to Lille and change onto the TGV to Montpellier. So incredibly easy! Left Ebbsfleet at 11.30 and even with a 1.5 hour stopover in Lille arrived in Montpellier at 20.00, French time. Return journey was even shorter:Left Montpellier at 13.30 - arrived in Ebbsfleet 19.30! Collected the car (a short 10 minute walk) and were back in Surrey by 20.30.  The fares were £70 per person each way (we booked ahead and benefitted from "senior discounts") - but no airport hassle, no hanging around for 2 hours in Gatwick, Stanstead etc each way! Thoroughly recommended, relaxing and pleasant. One note of warning - food on the TGV is non-existent -or fairly awful - take provisions with you! It is also pointless booking first class on the TGV as it is really no better than the standard seating. We booked through the London office of SNCF - extrremely helpful and pleasant staff

We paid the extra for 1st class on the Zurich-Paris route, as a treat on our way back from holiday. We expected more room, which we got, a welcome drink and food served at our seats, as described on the website. What we got was miserable cabin crew, a tiny plastic cup of Luke-warm Coke and 1/2 a sandwich. We only saw the on board crew once in 31/2 hours and then the poor lad was really harassed as he handed out our meagre rations. If we had known that was all we were getting, we could have headed to the buffet and bought something. The only good thing was we arrived at the right time to Gare Du Nord, so we could get off and find something to eat!

We booked to take the train from Nice to Paris and were looking forward to a fast comfortable ride.We were to board at Nice at 6:55am. We arrive at 6:30 to be told that there was track work and the trains would not be running for 4 days. We asked to speak to management who advised us to take the bus to Cannes then pick up the rail. We did this but were then told that we would miss our booked fast train to Paris.  After a harrowing journey we arrived at Marseille RS. As we had missed our train to Paris we took the regional train it was so packed we had to stand crushed in by our other weary travellers - this did not help the anxiety levels. We realized that we would not make our paid and  booked hotel in time, we got off early in Dijon and booked another. Arriving at the Dijon RS to catch the 9:30 am train we were advised that due to track work there would be no trains. Luckily I had a friend staying in Clamecy who picked us up in their car.  After spending two relaxing weeks with our friends we went to the Clamecy RS the day before to book our train to the airport. We were advised that the trains had been cancelled but if we took the 5:00 am bus we could get there. We did and arrived 14 hours early - what a relief. The rail staff were extremely helpful and friendly.

Nothing wrong with the TGV trains - fast and reasonably comfortable - being on the top deck is great for the views but .........  steep spiral staircase and luggage coupled with a three minute stop with 30+ to get on or off a train  means a frightening nightmare!!   Lyon and Avignon stations on the Brussles/Marseilles route.Luggage space restricted and jump seats in doorways (often occupied).The train guards are insistent that the train will not wait so those boarding are trying to push on whilst you are trying to get off.  We ended up running the length of a carriage (at the insistance of the station guard) for another door and then carrying all our luggage through the carriage to get to our place. It may be fine in ones and twos but I will never use this method again as I'd spend all my time worrying.

We took the TGV from Nice to Paris.  The cost was about 50% of what it would have cost to fly and we found it more convenient--just go to the station, tote and stow your own luggage and hop on!  The trip between cities on the Riviera was at a slower speed which gave us a chance to catch glimpses of the various towns and villages along the way as well as the beautiful Mediterranean.  Once we finished picking up passengers, the car was completely full and we sped to Paris, all in all the trip took about 5 1/2 hours but it was definitely a unique experience as we have nothing like it in the USA.  You don't realize how fast you are going until you pass another train.  The seats were comfortable but we didn't take advantage of the food; we both fell asleep!  It was a pleasant and enjoyable trip and we're so glad we experienced the TGV!

Travelling London/Paris?  Forget airports and planes, in 2hr 15m you can travel centre to centre of these two great cities.  It took me 90 minutes from CDG airport to Gare du Nord by taxi just this week, so for stress free travel, it's TGV for me!

My 85 year old Mother and I caught the TGV from Lyon to Paris (Gare de Lyon). It was a bit tricky to find the actual station from where our taxi dropped us off but once we were there it was easy. There is a waiting room and the toilets are downstairs. As usual, you have to pay to use the toilets. I had thought I would have to exchange our Australian-issued paper tickets (a bit like those old airline tickets with the multiple carbon copies) for electronic tickets at the station, but not so. You have to "composter" each ticket before getting on the train, this means to validate it and there are little machines, yellow as I recall, where you put the ticket in. The machine stamps it and then you remove the ticket and keep it to show the ticket-checker person on the train. Do check that the machine has typed something on the ticket and if it hasn't, have another go. The TGV itself is double-decker train and you leave your suitcases on the lower level unless you want to hump them up the stairs to the upper level. Our tickets had allocated seats which were on the top level so we had great views, when it wasn't raining. There seemed to be plenty toilets on board and you can buy food. The seats were comfortable with more leg room than some airlines have. We would definitely travel by TGV again.

Reader friends if you are from France you know it as well as the SNCF and these strange prices like for a plane' friends tourists it is to discover 300 or 360 km/h in a silent train it is incredible and seen nowhere else except perhaps now in China and Japan. But for example in Canada via rail is very slow, the same in the USA if you have the choice take the upper floor for a better view.  Dear tourist enjoy speed train with 300 or 360 km/h near s’en In Canada or USA

My wife and I took the TGV trip from Lyon to Paris as part of our tour of France in May. Being aware of the problems with luggage, we only carried two each (one small and one medium). However, they were already heavy with the half-dozen bottles of wine we had bought in the Rhone region. When we had to go to the departure platform at Part Dieu station, to our surprise, we had to carry our bags up the stairs because there was no escalator available for that track! On top of that, it was difficult to carry luggage up the narrow and steep stairs to the upper level where our seats were. Conclusion: once we boarded it was wonderful, but until we got settled it was a sacrifice. Advice to travelers: only use this means of transport if your luggage is light and easy to transport.

We returned today, just the worst reviews. They are practically trampling on all the strengths of traveling by train compared to other means of transport. These trains (at least the sleepers) are expensive, old, dirty, uncomfortable, there is no customer service (in an Italy-France train the staff many times say they don't know Italian or even English) adopting various justifications they are not direct and on time.

Using French booking facilities, I grabbed a special offer of first-class at second-class price from Paris Gare de Lyon to Besancon.I dreamed of free food and drink, brought round on baroque trolleys by waitresses in black and white uniform after boarding from a luxury lounge.Well...At Gare de Lyon we left the station briefly in search of a pre-travel cafe, but it looked like the exercise yard at  Alcatraz and there were guys swigging from beer cans hanging around. Best idea at Gare De Lyon is the "Logan's Run" technique of staying on the premises and using the facilities provided.Once aboard our seats were reasonably comfortable and wide enough, though facing backwards in the "Spectrum Pursuit Vehicle" style for a high-speed ride.I cannot fault the smooth and super-fast ride. Very efficient indeed.After a while the guard unlocked the toilets and in I went. I almost regretted leaving my crash helmet at home because the mirror was swinging loose from some unit behind it and it just missed my head. Anyhow, I survived and went back to await refreshments.Well.... at least the buffet car was nearby. No trolley service to our seats.But it got us to our destination quickly and smoothly and that's the main thing. I wish we had them over here because anything's better than flying.

I was very disappointed in our journey from Paris to Zurich on the TGV. Firstly the positives: it was on time; it was clean and it was inexpensive, we booked early and got good fares.Now the negatives:- we booked forward facing seats but got backward facing seats and we had another couple facing us who either could not or would not converse- we were in the very front seat of the very front compartment and had other people's luggage piled high next to the seat so it was very difficult to move.- right across the length of the window is a metal strip that blocked my view. I had to stretch up to see over it or crouch down to see under it. What a terrible design flaw.- I asked if we could be upgraded to a couple of the many empty 1st Class seats and was asked for a ridiculously high price that was much higher than the Internet price, even though I had already paid the economy price.Overall it was a disappointing and uncomfortable journey. Compare this to my Bernina Express report.

I regularly do Paris-Montpellier and Paris-Marseille. If the TGV from Marseille is direct, it is 3h05min. The one from Montpellier always stops in Nîmes, and most often in Valence. So 3:15 or 20. I take the metro and line 14 puts me at the foot of the TGV. From home, 30 min. If I went to Orly, it would take 1 hour, I would have to arrive at least 30 min before, plus 1h30 of flight and to leave the airport. So it's almost the same. Well, it tires me a lot less and makes me less stressed to take the train. I just have time to read the newspaper, do a little crossword or read a little, and I arrive, straight into the city center. I have more space, I can choose a solo seat if I am alone or a duo if I am accompanied. It is only the catering that can be improved. But on Air France's domestic flights, it's worse, there's no more food, nothing but a small packet of crackers. So long live the TGV.

I liked the Thalys which cost me around 100 euro for a return (early travel to and late travel from) from Amsterdam. Trip took about 3,5 hours from my doorstep which is great without the hassle of airport security checks or driving yourself.

prices are sometimes expensive but you get everywhere, conveniently and quickly. Reserved seats, speed, cleanliness and generally punctuality...above all it's a choice if you can't find the RER or you have time problems with other means of transport
Great value and really impressive for cleanliness and punctuality. The views of the countryside are great and the service was very friendly.

On March 26th at 7.59pm I left Paris on train 221 Thello Euronight. The next morning I found myself still in Paris. The train had turned back due to a breakdown. The staff was totally unprepared, they made us wait standing in the freezing cold for hours for an alternative journey: The passengers were not even offered a hot drink and were told numerous lies by the staff. The alternative trip I was offered was the longest and least expensive they could find. I arrived at my destination more than 12 hours late. Compensation? Only 50% of the ticket cost: ridiculous and not yet received!
A superb invention, this brings us closer to the furthest distances, today train travel has become a pleasure

Monday 15th April my wife and I travelled onboard the great TGV from Nice to Paris. It was a really great experience; it is simply the best way to travel. The train departed from Nice at 11:34 hrs, and we arrived at the station “Gare de Lyon” in Paris at 17:11 hrs, i.e. the whole trip lasted for around 5 ½ hours. The first approx. 260 kilometers (160 miles) journey from Nice to Aix-de-Provence lasted for around 3 hours (only the old rails were available…though, we enjoyed very beautiful scenery along the Mediterranean coastline in Provence). However, during the next part of the journey (from Aix-de-Provence to Paris), a distance of around 800 kilometers (500 miles), the train went up to the max speed of 320 km/hour (198,8 mph)…and that distance was finished in approx 2 ½ hour !!!  We had booked 1st class seating a couple of months in advance (through the homepage www.idtgv.com). The internet rate we paid was Euro 55:-/person. The wagon was almost empty, and we had a very nice seating at the top floor, 2+2 seats towards each other with a table between us. The large windows gave us a marvelous experience, having the possibility to enjoy the beautiful scenery (the Mediterranean coastline, the cruise ships in the harbor of Marseille, the many small cities, wine yards, agricultural areas with cows and other animals, mountains, creeks and rivers, the approach to the city centre of Paris…..)   Some 15 minutes ahead of the departure from Nice, after we had found our seats and when I went outside, along the platform, towards the “locomotive” to take some photos  –  I was invited by the driver (“the pilot”) in to the “cockpit”.  He showed me the interior with all the computers and buttons in front of his seat and in the rest of the cabin…not very unlike a cockpit in an airplane. He informed me that the maximum speed for the upcoming journey would be 320 kilometer/hour (198,8 mph). Even though we had big communication problems due to his French- and my English language (he couldn’t speak English; and the little French I learned in school 40 years ago was forgotten a long time ago), it was really great to visit the “locomotive”. I appreciated it very much, and it is surely a nice memory. There was a café onboard where you may buy coffee, wine, beer, soda…..and something to eat (sandwiches etc.) Ourselves, we had bought some really good sandwiches and salad in Nice (ahead of the journey), which we enjoyed while the train passed through the great landscape.Finally! This was great – and it is the very best way of traveling!

Fast, furiously good train. We were in Paris city from CDG airport in no time. We took the same train to go to the Disney Park too and the system was still up and running efficiently until late in the night too. Quite dependable, inexpensive and good transportation system. Every successful city must have a good transportation system and Paris has TGV

It's an old, dirty train with half doors that didn't work. In the middle of the night they had to move us (around Lausanne while the doors to enter the wagon in Milan were already not working!) due to a technical fault in another wagon and 6-bed while we had paid the sum of 140 euros for 3 T-women. We left after 2 and a half hours of being stuck (18-5-2013) in Lausanne station. The return other breakdowns (25-5-2013), it was very cold and in the wagone rest. for breakfast the heating didn't work. In short, quite a nightmare! Joanna/Trieste
7 hours goes by pretty quickly on this train. Excellent cleanliness and courtesy of the people who work on it make it a delightful train.

Took the TGV from Paris to Zurich and back again, and this is the way to travel. On-time. Super clean. Able to view the countryside and read my book while traveling. No hassle in getting to train station. What's not to like about this? Wish we had TGV in the USA.

we travelled on April from Strasbourg to Paris with Tgv on 1st class and return on 2nd class on a double - deck train.Both trips were wonderful, the view was nothing special but the train itself was a great experience!Comfortable, clean,modern,kids frienldly.Such a great way to travel!

Let me start by saying that I paid 720 euros for 2 people return Rome/Paris. The journey would be nice but the train is one of the worst intercity trains I've ever taken. Very old, dirty, inefficient carriages, noisy due to the windows that closed badly (the sink was leaking water, there was no electricity in the sockets, dirty bathrooms), the food was terrible and the bar was always closed. For that sum I would have asked for more: aren't we ashamed with similar trains around Europe?

After a failed booking out of Heathrow, we jumped on the eurostar to paris to catch the TGV to Geneva.Not knowing the standard of the train, we prepared for the unexpected.We had booked seats and found ourselves on the top deck of the 2 tier train, speeding through France, fantastic views, so ask to go upstairs.We packed some food and of course some wine, but when we went to borrow a corkscrew from the buffet car, which they did without question. We bought other bits from French snacks to Creem Brulee. A much better selection than other trains and good value!The train was clean with carpet, which was a nice change.So a high speed picnic with scenic views from Paris to Geneve, we would do the journey again just for the entertainment.

I took the train to go to Paris with my two daughters, mindful of the beautiful memories left to me in my youth by the legendary Palatine. Never a more wrong choice, we left two hours late, nothing was known about the train, not even any information, until Florence the carriage had no electricity, bathrooms the same as 30 years ago with an unacceptable smell and cleanliness, finally we arrived in Paris 4 hours late with a simple announcement that they apologized ABSURD .The return was better only an hour and a half late but with the same dirt. THINK ABOUT IT!!!!!!!! even if like me you keep a good memory of the train

Loved the speed and efficiency of this train - recommended for any journey when you are in a hurry!   This reflects France at its best - great technology and good public transport come together in a high quality experience.

I was most impressed with a day train from Gare de Lyon [Paris] tp Lyon.  It is about 600 km and it only took about 2 hours and 10 minutes and it was smooth that it was hard to believe that we were doing 300 kph most of the time. It is much more convenient than flying since you do not waste time at an airport and depart and arrive in mid city. The train had double decker carriages with comfotable seats and table. Food and drinks can be purchased.

We booked our seats from Paris to Brittany and back to Charles de Gaulle airport sitting at home in South Africa. We paid online with the minimum of fuss.Our return journey was partially on the regional railway in Brittany, so our ticket had to be validated at a SNCF station prior to travel - the station staff couldn't have been more helpful.The staff we encountered on the TGV were all friendly and helpful - language barrier permitting (and for heaven's sake, do try to use some French. It will be greatly appreciated). The rolling stock is starting to age, but our seats were clean and comfortable.Still loving the TGV.

comfortable. red some reviews here before, and worried a bit if we can have a decent sleep on a moving carriage, luckily I did had a great sleep.we booked this online-internationalrail.com.au, can not tell if we booked a triple cabin or not, after 1-2 emails, found out it is not a private triple cabin. so when we board found another gentleman already in the cabin, we are 3 ladies, luckily he is quite gentleman, trouble free. I had a good sleep, no wake up at all until about 1 hour before we arrived at venice. Half hour after we board the train the inspector took all of our passports and left the receipt, that gentleman got off at milan got his passport back before off-was told by my friend, as i did not wake up during this. there are drinks and snack for sale-a bit expensive if you need them.if it is your first time to take this train from paris, try give yourself a bit more time at gare de lyon. we  stayed at a hotel near gare du nord, took metro-easy short trip to gare de lyon, but after got gare de lyon, could not find any sign point to the right dirction for this train, had to asked around more than 3 people, when i asked one security guard and showed our ticket, he told us definitely we were at wrong station, luckily did not follow his guide, asked another 2, finally found out this train leaving at hall 3, we need wait at hall 3 and watching a board continueslly to find out which platform for boarding.

Used the TGV to get from DeGaulle airport to Nimes.  The agent could not book me on the next train out, but booked me on the next one after that, and I had to pay first class fare, as that was the only option available.  It turns out that May 7th is VE day (a holiday) and the next day was Ascension Thursday, another holiday.  A lot of people were heading south.  Beware of the difficulty of trying to travel on French holidays.

Used the TGV for getting from CDG to Disney (Val d'Europe station) and back, the journey takes about 10 minutes. Ordered tickets online and had a problem to pick them up from the automatic ticket machines at the CDG station.
