However, I got escorted to the customer service who managed to print out the tickets for me. Since then, everything went very smoothly.

Her's one thing the French do really well! Heavy subsidies bankrupt the state, but it offers a fast efficient service in very comfortable surroundings and if you book sufficiently far in advance - very reasonable prices!
WHenever I use the trains in Europe, I am crestfallen that we do not have these in the United States!  They are efficient, clean, and very fast.  A wonderful way to travel.
TGV means "Train à grande vitesse": High speed train.To resume the experience (and after comparision with other occidental high speed trains), I would say:Very sureVery fastVery confortableVery cheap

Really great way to travel, specifically when you consider the rains generally drop you in the centre of the city.  When flying taking the 4 hours into account for getting to the airport, checking in, boarding procedures, then collecting your luggage and finding your way into the city, it is great.

We use the TGV to travel between the Languedoc and London on a regular basis. For us, it is a balance between Ryanair and the train.  For comfort and stress, the TGV/EuroStar wins every time. The cost varies with both methods of transport and depends on timing, how long before the journey I book, time of year, whether we are carrying suitcases etc.  i also take into account the cost of getting to/from the station or airport. Your seat on the TGV and EuroStar is reserved with the TGV seats  being more spacious than the EuroStar and much more spacious than Ryainair. You can walk around and there is a bar on board serving food and drinks. We travel as a couple of over 60s and I book on the voyages SNCF website.  Tickets are delivered by post within a day or two. We have been delayed on the TGV where we were in danger of missing our connection to the EuroStar. On that occasion, train staff came throughout the carriage, reassuring us that EuroStar were aware and would honour our tickets. We were also given a voucher for future travel.We usually travel via Paris, but via Lille is also an option and is an easier change.

Used the Eurostar for the first time this month.  It is a very efficient way to travel between Paris and London, and is comfortable instead of having to go through the airport hassles.The waiting lounge for passengers to board the train is too small, overcrowded, and lacks seating, so next time I think I will pay the money and get a business/executive ticket.
great prem'son tickets can go far for nothing, too bad there are people who don't respect their cell phones

We left Paris at 7.50 am with TGV and arrived in Milan Garibaldi at 3.20 pm with a whopping 30' delay: 7.5 hours for 850 km. Not bad for a TGV. Average: 113 k/m hour. Lots of stops in very small villages. We stopped for almost half an hour in Modane to wait for the convenience of the French Police who got on the carriages for a parade of policemen who limited themselves to looking at us seated passengers. During the journey only some information on the speakers about the stops made. No screen with the indication of the travel speed (pitiful and just omission).W the Freccia Rossa Milan Rome with its screen indicating the instantaneous speed and a journey of over 600 km in exactly 2 hours and 55 minutes: average of around 207 k/m per hour!!

If you consider having to pay all the tolls, parking fees, and fuel prices, if you're coming from outside France, the TGV is absolutely the best way to travel to Paris.  Not only that, driving in Paris is a nightmare and not recommended if you value your vehicle.

I took the Thello train at the beginning of April to Paris, if you book in advance the prices are more than convenient (but they are in limited quantities you have to be among the first to book!) €35 each in a 6-berth compartment, of course there are other types of comfort in first class with free toilet kit and sink but the price is higher. The comfort is classic, the trains are Italian trains that are not very young but nothing terrible and they were clean. The staff is very kind and very welcoming, both we arrived on time on the way there and on the way back, I also had alicizia with my traveling companions. A bit of a wait at the restaurant car but the food was good (good pasta and salad) I can recommend this train

Folks have been reviewing the Thello train under the TGV classification. Thello is a separate company not affiliated with SNCF that runs the TGV service.  Thello is a revival of an older overnight service from Paris to Rome and uses old cars and not so fast rail lines most of the way.  It seems to serve groups of students and the adventuresome who are not worried about luxury.  The Florence station (Camp di Marte--not the central station) is very popular for those going to Paris.  The cost is fairly reasonable for the distance covered and the cost of a night in a hotel avoided.  BUT, the train is slow and has a certain old-timey sway and rattle.  Nevertheless it is relatively clean but makes use of technology of the 1960s and 1970s when toilets were, well, a hole in the bottom of the car under the porcelain--My trip in April, 2013 was very reminiscent of train journeys I took a that time in Europe.  The dining car is very basic and the food best avoided.  Bring your own food and manage in the small compartments.  They do try a bit to act like a better than basic train service, but the staff are quite young and really not attuned to service.  It does seem to run on time.
It's a comfortable train, which from the feeling I had on board the train is faster than the Freccia Rossa, even if it goes like a snail between Switzerland and Italy...

I traveled from Avignon to Geneva in a TGV. Comfort and speed, with bar service and other conveniences, in certain sections, the train exceeds 300 km/h. On the Geneva-Paris route, I went to collect my ticket in Switzerland and the attendant did not accept my online reservation. I had to pay a lot more. If you are going to ride the TGV between France and other countries, I suggest doing the "retrait" in France.
The TGV is pleasant, and Paris-Strasbourg in 2h30 saves a lot of time. The only downside still concerns the insecurity felt in Parisian stations.
Soo practical, just the time to read some and tchat and you are there, no hassle, no parking, no boring autoroute.

Took the overnight Thelo train from Paris to Venice in October/1212 with must excitement and anticipation. My wife and I had the 2 person 1 class sleeper car that was comfortable. To give you a primer, anyone can board the train, even people with no tickets because tickets are not checked until long after departure. The reason I mention this is, unwanted characters the locals called "gypsies" board the trains and offer to help you with your luggage. Now mind you this is right in front of train personnel, so you almost mistake these people for train personnel. Now these friendly helpful people help pull your heavy luggage onto the train, or to your seat (they even offer to store your luggage at the entrance of the train way out of your sight). As soon as you get to your seat they demand money. The locals jumped in with my helper after he was quite loud and was escorted him from the train. At departure the "helpers" scurry off the train and go to the next departing train to pray on the next commuter. Sorry for my diversion but no where in the train postings does it mention these "helpers", and there all over Europe. Back to the train ride. Our overhead compartment light was out and we lit our cabin with the reading light. The bathrooms are located in the common hallway. The women bathroom had no toilet seat, and the mens bathroom had no light (so good luck with you aim at night on a swaying train in the dark). I reported these problems to the conductor who showed up about 2 hrs after departure and he was quite unconcerned. The dinner car was first come-first serve with tables that seated 4, so you set with anyone you can. In the morning the train smelled like toilet chemicals and urine. If your looking for adventure, this is it.

Don't travel by car, travel by train across Europe. I left Paris (Gare de Lyon) heading to Geneva with a change of train in Lyon, southern France. From Paris to Lyon the train is a bullet train, travels at more than 300km/h and you don't feel any vibration, it's fantastic. From Lyon to Geneva the train is a little simpler and slower, but it is a much higher level train than the Brazilian subways, for example. A tip is to board immediately and arrange your suitcases at the ends of the cars or between the seats (as one seat faces the back of the other, this place in /\ is a place for suitcases /x\). Don't worry, your suitcase at the end of the carriage, close to the door, won't be stolen or anything like that. Tickets can be purchased in advance on the website www.raileurope.com and the tickets will arrive at your home, here in Brazil, via HDL transport company. So buy well in advance! I bought my tickets from Paris to Geneva, Geneva to Montreux (return) and Geneva to Venice (there are different trains, even though they are good, they are inferior to TGVs). Don't drive from Paris to another place that has train lines, go by train, the experience is fantastic.
Easy & fast ! Had lots of help with purchasing tix and then switching train times, even speaking the worst french !

The TGV website exhibits major suckage. First, they try to divert you to Raileurope, where you will pay a booking fee. Then they reject credit cards the bank confirms are perfectly fine. So I had no alternative than to use raileurope.com.au, which isn't the fastest site & where you first get an email booking confirmation, then an email with tickets 'within 1 business day', so you sit around waiting for them to get their act into gear & wondering if they will send you the second email. Not ideal.  TGV trains are great, but the booking kerfuffle not so much. TGV has much to learn from Deutsche Bahn, Thalys, Trenitalia & even Cesky Drahy, which enable users to register & pay with no drama. But first world problems, eh?

Hello everyone.. we have just returned from a nice trip to Paris by train, we have online tickets with e-ticket which was a great idea because you don't have to do anything just enjoy the journey without disturbances, get on the train and take the seats you had chosen, in our case there were three. The departure journey was very punctual, we left Porta Garibaldi at 8.50am and arrived at 4.05pm... there were no problems of any kind even after reading other reviews I understood that there were delays due to checks for illegal immigrants, but the checks were there but they didn't stop the train to do them and this continued without stopping, even if they found some unfortunate people without documents but they let them off at the following stations without any kind of problem.  The return journey was a little more complicated because we left Paris a little late but in the end we arrived in Milan on time. I made the journey with my sixty-year-old parents and even though it's a seven-hour journey and it's a bit heavy, for us it's always better than going in a small plane and arriving straight away in the city.

As I regularly book the journey Perpignan to London and back via Paris, I spend some time looking at al the options. Here are two tips that might interest travellers on the Eurostar and TGV.1) Booking on-line the Eurostar and TGV from London to Perpignan (and to several other destinations such as Marseille and Girona or Barcelona) as one trip means SNCF sells you a package. This package might contain a lengthy wait at Montpelier to change trains. See (2) below for how to avoid this !2) The "through journey" package from London to Perpignan in May 2013 proves quite expensive. Booking the Eurostar from London to Paris and the TGV from Paris to Perpignan as separate journeys brought up an "over 60 years old" option for the TGV NOT shown on the continuous journey which was then €80 cheaper. There was also the possibility of waiting 40 minutes at Paris (have a meal in the Tren Bleu restaurant) and taking a later train which doesn't involve changing at Montpelier.My suggestion: spend some time on the internet and check prices of "through journies booked as one" versus "journeys split into segments and booked separately".

Boy, do we look backwards compared to Europe in many ways (health care, animals pumped full of steroids, our obsessions with cars and guns). Ride high-speed rail in Europe and you will be advocating some changes back home.

We took the train that connects the Gare Lyon, in Paris, with P. Garibaldi, in Milan. We found the service excellent, very comfortable and with a bar car with more than adequate prices. The landscape is very beautiful, and we were greatly rewarded for having taken the train option over the plane. On the other hand, it connects the center of Paris with the center of Milan, an advantage to take into account. The only unpleasant thing, but it no longer corresponds to the TGV itself, but to the SNCF, is the sordidness of the place where you get off the taxis, with people sleeping on the floors and not very satisfactory lighting. It could also happen that they encounter mistreatment by the caretaker of the bathrooms on the last platform. Otherwise, a trip to repeat, without a doubt.

Most of the time the roll is stuck in and you can't get the beginning out because the paper tears off too easily, so it's best to bring paper with you. The bistro offering is also very weak and expensive and is not worth the money.

The TGV is a fast way to get around France, although there is a very big gap in using the TGV to get to the middle of France currently, but it is super fast and very nice way to get to the south of France in a relaxed manner in order to see the country side.
When it's on time, the TGV is excellent: speed, service, cleanliness, speed! To dream! Too bad it's not automatic.... the "human factor" can ruin everything.....)))))

There we waited for three hours for another TGV which picked us up; settled back and sat down, while we were preparing to eat the dinner package offered as "compensation", the new train arrived at the border... and stopped there. At this point they let us off again and we had to take buses which luckily had already arrived to pick us up. We arrived in Turin 5 hours late, after having changed a multitude of means of transport. There is a 13 hour journey on the way there and the arrival was on time. Only 12 for the return, then in fact the train was an hour late and therefore here are the same 13 as the outward journey! The sore point is the temperature of the compartments: on the outward journey, a suffocating heat that was almost unbearable while on the return journey, freezing cold so much so that in order to take off my coat I slept with 2 duvets, shoes and a scarf on. There is a duvet, sheet, pillow and pillowcase, all clean and closed in plastic bags. cellophane that every traveler opens and uses. The inspector collects the identity card upon departure and returns it upon arrival so as not to wake the traveler during border controls (Italy, France, Switzerland in, Switzerland out, France). Of course in the morning after a night on the tracks you are not at your best but at least on the train you don't have the checks that are done at the airport so you can bring the jars of sauce and jam to your daughter in Paris with an overweight suitcase without problems or extra charges!!

My wife and I traveled from Canada to Paris where we spent a week before heading to Provence for a two-week self-driven tour of the region in a rented car.  We decided to travel south by train, just to give it a try.  Over the years, we had heard a lot of comments from friends about how fast and efficient the TGV (Très Grande Vitesse) was and our overall impression from those comments was that it was a great way to travel.  So, we were anxious to try it for ourselves.  To make it more of a memorable experience, we bought a couple of Premier class tickets for the three-hour ride from Paris to Grenoble where we picked up our rental.  At about 150 EUR each, Premier Class fares are more than 2.5 times the cost of Economy Class tickets. The big question:  Is Premier worth the extra cost?  I would say NO without hesitation.  You do get into a separate car, but that car is not appreciably more luxurious or comfortable than the Economy class cars.  And you certainly don't get to your destination any faster!  Lunch was also a big disappointment.  It was more like a snack that came in a paper bag that we had to pick up at a counter in another car – the same place for everybody – and bring back to our seat.  It was not included in the price of the tickets and it was very expensive for what you got.  Anyway, we had to try it; now, at least, we have the experience and we can talk about it!  Our recommendation: don't waste your money on the Premier class fares.  Economy is fine, much cheaper, and it will get you to your destination at the same time!

Traveled with my young daughter and decided to take the overnight train from Venice to Paris.  First, you need to manage your expectations.  It's not a high end luxury train but generally everything is very good.  Though we had 2 people, we booked a private 3 cabin sleeper to make sure we didn't have any unexpected guest - booked directly on Thello site.  The room was clean with a small sink basin that included some slippers, toothbrush, and mouthwash.  There's no TV and wifi (though I did hear some trains do have wifi).  We traveled in April and it was a very quiet train and not full.  Food was ok but a bit expensive.  Though it was neat just being able to dine in one of the cars - they do take credit cards.  You can also purchase a few things a la carte or just bring your own food, drinks, sandwiches, etc.  With the sleeper tix, you do get a small continental type of breakfast (coffee & danish) but make sure you don't go at the end when they start to wrap things up. They key reason I'd use Thello for this same trip again is the convenience.  We stayed less than a 2 minute walk from Santa Lucia termini so we didn't have to pull our luggage across Venice.  Plus all you need to do is literally get there 2 minutes before the train takes off.  They handle customs/passport during the night.  Much better than taking the Chunnel where you have to be there 1 hour before departure.  This was an overnight train so there's not a lot to see as it is dark - summer might be better.  Did have a few incidents late a night with people trying to board the train, but the attendants were totally on top of it and still felt safe in the end. You figure instead of paying for a flight, going to Venice airport, taxi, and additional room night in Venice or Paris, your cost on the Thello is a bargain.  You board at 8pm and arrive in Paris at Gare de Lyon at 9am, and from there can catch the Metro to anywhere in Paris.  The ride is a bit rough at times, not quite as smooth as the TGV or similar overnight trains in China. Overall a great experience.  A great resource is the website seat61.com, for all train travel info in Europe.

It's easy to travel from Granada to Algeciras by train, and it's nice to be able to get off in Ronda, but trains tend to be delayed, and there are only three direct trains a day between Granada and Algeciras, so be sure to check the departure times.

Renfe train is a good way to explore Spain.  Took the train from Barcelona to Seville to Cordoba, back to Seville and then to Madrid. Bought the Spain pass train ticket online using Rail Europe website which was easy.  Once you booked the ticket, you have to go to Renfe website to validate and then book your train trip.  Online tickets are accepted, no need to print hard copy. They will need to validate your Spain pass and ticket for the first trip, after that only need the tickets to board.  If you select preferente class ticket, you can enjoy the Sala club before you board the train. It was easy to find and board the train, there are display signs that tells you which gate to board.

We really enjoyed using the trains to get around Spain. Easy to use and reliable. Just be aware no sharp objects can be carried in luggage. I bought some kitchen shears at a cooking class and they were confiscated after being spotted in the scanner. I had trouble with the Renfe site to book so I used Loco2 for the booking and that worked great and seemed to be the best price.  They also showed me the longer journey options broken into two legs. Which on other sites I tried and they just showed no option available.  Stress free way to travel for the most part, when we had a second leg of the journey to we would send one to ask where our next train was so all 4 of us didn’t need to run around. Sometimes it was almost right where we got off and other times we had to go through security again and go to another area. Just be prepared to get to your connection asap. We took 5 trains and had no problem with any of them. We bought tickets that couldn’t be changed and that worked fine too.

Wonderful experience. Went from Barcelona to Madrid in the afternoon. It was impressively fast and absolutely on time. The seats were great. Wish I had the option of taking a single seat across the aisle. Was there in 2h 50 m. Would highly recommend it. However for cheap rates book early. I made the mistake of booking just a day earlier and ended up paying 108 euro.

Yesterday I traveled by AVE towards Atocha to Seville, departure at 6 pm. We took the Renfe train from Granada to Madrid on Oct 3, 2019. Tickets were easy to book online through Eurorail. In the Preferente Class, a meal was served including wine and other beverages.A very civilized way to travel. Thanks Renfe.

We travelled from Barcelona to Madrid on the AVE fast train. The 2 hours or so passed quickly and the seats were quite comfortable. Trains depart Barcelona almost every hour and cost approximately 30 Euros. The only issue is the lack of space for suitcases and the crush of people wanting to take a advantage of the limited space when we first got on the train. Not an issue for us as our luggage went on the bus to Madrid. The fast train network in Spain is definitely the way to go and much cheaper than flying. Would recommend.

Train from Madrid to Granada. I was unable to purchase the ticket from the automatic machines in the station. I got it with the Renfe App. Very expensive price, €85. Train delayed 35 minutes. I got there an hour early, which is best & got there 30 minutes early & almost missed the train! My rides: Madrid to Barcelona, Barcelona to Granada & Granada to Madrid.

Early flight into Malaga Airport from John Lennon Airport Liverpool, through passport control in no time ,walked over to train station in the airport grounds,used ticket machine which is easy to use,got tickets to Benalmedena area ,trains on time,comfortable seats,clean train,on time and air conditioned, beats a coach or taxi transfer and a lot cheaper .While on holiday we jumped the RENFE down to Malaga for a day out and also to Los Boliches for days out,again super efficient. A great train system and if your planning a holiday to Spain well worth checking out.

Excellent transportation option, due to travel time and comfort. You go from the center to the center of the cities. Spacious seats (nothing to do with a plane) Exquisite punctuality. Renfe is the national rail services of Spain and you can say it is a monopoly so you must use it. I used my Interrail pass first class version and booked AVE bullet train from Barcelona to Madrid and from Madrid to Sevilla. Although the train used was the same as Germany ICE but the whole experience is completely different. First of all, you need to pass through luggage security checkpoint to enter the waiting area, and then wait at that area until 20 minutes prior to departure, unlike other European countries or Japan you can just hope on the train a minute before the train departure time. Most of the AVE trains are on time and first class passengers are allowed to use the lounge. Note that some stations are located after security (Madrid) and some are outside (Barcelona). On trains passengers are served with Spanish newspaper, snacks and a meal, which are the dishes from spain. The trains run on dedicated high speed track unlike Germany so most of the time the trains run with 300 km/h.Wifi is not tourist friendly as actual phone number is required.However the local commuter train services need to be improved. Interrail pass / Eurail pass holders are required to go to the service counter to get a ticket for entering the ticket gate, my ticket was not working to exit in some stations and some stations didn’t have service counter so it was frustrating. Cimmuter trains are always at least 5 minutes late and services are poor. Better to pay for the metro.

It usually makes its journey with delays and malfunctions. It is very useful and necessary for daily travelers and tourists. The website and the speed of responses and attention should be improved. That the use of this service is up to the taste and need of each person.

When booking train tickets in Spain on the internet, NEVER EVER USE RAIL NINJA AND/OR RUSSIAN TRAINS.  THIS IS A SCAM.  When you book through Rail Ninja, they divert you to Russian Trains.  Russian Trains then tried to sell me tickets at inflated prices and tried the good old "bait and switch" trick where they sold Premium tickets on special, took my money and then emailed me a few days later saying that only Economy tickets were available at the same price or else I have to pay an extra 105 EUROs to upgrade to the Premium tickets that I had already paid for!  Russian Trains are SCAMMERS.  When I went direct to Renfe (the Spanish national rail company) I got the tickets I wanted with no problems.  The trick here is the Rail Ninja web site is actually much easier to use and looks much better than the RENFE site but don't let appearances fool you!  Book directly with the rail company and not re-sellers.

Usually decent staff would come in and see through the lies of the people that cut in line, but not the staff at renfe.

Absolutely disgusting behaviour from the supervisor. The whole time we were yelled and screamed at because we could not place our suitcases in the racks and we had to put them up! I am travelling with a school group with adults and the supervisor was screaming at the head teacher and no letting her speak. He was yelling, I don’t want to listen to you!! With the little spanish I have I can safely assume how rudely he was speaking to me when I wanted to know where to put mine and the children’s bags. I am so appalled and have never seen such behaviour. I wish to never step foot on these trains again because of the trauma I have endured. I would not wish this unfair treatment on anyone!

The online purchasing service is terrible, not all available trains appear. Also for some destinations there could be more train connections if they wanted, if they allowed a minimum waiting time between one train and another, but it seems that they are not interested in travelers...

I make a lot of trips Madrid Alicante, Alicante Madrid, they are putting very good prices on prefente that includes food, not in Alvia and it is really worth it. I am celiac and the only shame is that if you don't let me know when you buy the ticket it becomes impossible to let me know. On the phone, they do not answer your request and you have to waste time in an office. In these times it is a setback

Shameful, I'm from Madrid and I can't go visit my family, I have to go to Jerez or Malaga to take the train, we have been without tracks for many months, without a train, in a space as popular as the Straits crossing, a shame.

We have had a difficult year 2019 in: punctuality, cleanliness, service, attention, treatment and punctuality again. But they continue to charge us money and pay no attention to the complaints. Horrible. Thank goodness I have read that two more companies are entering the lines. Renfe has to make more of an effort to offer what it charges!

Trains are nice, clean and fast, but the website hardly ever works. Went from Barcelona to Madrid and the ride was crazy shaky, it’s like the constructors we’re drunk when putting down the train tracks.

After a 10 hour and 40 minute flight from Los Angeles to Madrid with terrible service from the airline, which I don't want to mention because it's relevant. I want to say that the service I received from Renfe was impeccable, from the state of the hotel to the food. Many airlines should take the example of Renfe.
Travel round trip Madrid Barcelona on the high-speed train. I recommend it. A sensational trip
We have traveled with a dog and everything has been facilities and attention. The staff on board did everything possible to make our trip comfortable.

Spent 200 on a train from Mardrid to Barcelona on a Premium only train. Very comfortable space, tray table, jacket hook, wifi, snacks, meal and drinks all included. Would definitely use again, much more comfortable and quicker in total journey time than flying

Valencia to Malaga trip. Left precisely on time.Very comfortable seating and so very smooth, you couldn't spill a drink on this train. At one point we reached 300kph and you would not have known it if it weren't for the speed meter in your carriage. Nice buffet car for drinks and nibbles reasonable priced. The change of trains at Cordoba was so easy, off the train on one side of the platform and a short wait of a few mins and the AVE  to Malaga was on the opposite side,  no hassles of changing platforms. Overall a great service at reasonable cost IF YOU BOOK EARLY enough on line. RegardsAdrian & Anna (NZ)

I took the Seville-Madrid train on 7/4/2019. A few minutes after our departure, an explosion was heard and smoke was seen coming from a carriage. I was in the last carriage and the carriage from which the explosion came was the one connected to mine. Taken by agitation, we got up trying to change carriages causing further disturbances. I remained in the smoke-filled carriage for an infinite time without knowing what had happened. Not even the staff, who went back and forth, were able to explain the fact. After about an hour of fear and agitation I received an email from the company apologizing for the technical failure. As if an email could reassure me. Now, without any information received, we set off again. We don't know if we will change trains or if we will continue with this.

With the autumn rains we were left without a train. There was a landslide and since the track must be from the 19th century, we were left without a train to Madrid, to Granada... We are in the 21st century and we have a track layout from Algeciras to Granada that is absolutely outdated, very slow trains and with the rains we were left without a track. We have been waiting for the settlement for four months.
Very clean, comfortable, spacious, quiet and punctual trains. Too high price. If they were a little cheaper they would have 5 stars.
We travelled from Malaga to Córdoba and I have to say that it was the smoothest, fastest train journey I have ever taken. It was a fast and on time journey which makes travelling in Spain a joy.
I travel with my wife often from Alicante to Barcelona and we always do it on the Euromed train because of its comfort and the attention they give us, newspapers, soft drinks, snacks, lunch, etc.

We were travelling as a group of three from Madrid to Toledo. The train is an easy, fast affordable way to get to Toledo from Madrid. We tried to purchase tickets from the ticket kiosk in the train station but the kiosk instructed us to see a teller. We went as a group to the ticket counter and requested three return tickets to Toledo. We clearly indicated that we were together but we paid for the tickets separately. The agent processed our tickets and we were on our way. That night when we returned to the station - we were being processed to board the train after security and my ticket wouldn't clear. The agent had put two of us on an earlier train. At no point did she draw our attention to the fact that we weren't purchasing tickets together. We had no idea that she had switched times on us. We were really flexible with our timing and could have taken a later train together. There was no communication at all that she had changed times. We had missed our train because we weren't aware she had switched the return trip on us. We had to purchase new tickets at the train station in Toledo. What an expensive mistake. Don't leave the counter without confirming what the agent has booked - they may put you on a train you didn't request without any indication. We were all adults but can you imagine if they had done this to a family with children! Very poor service.

Our experience with buying Renfe tickets has been a mixed bag. We bought tickets online and printed them before we left the states for specific side trips. For the most part, this worked well and the cost was reasonable for us.On the other hand, we were unable to buy tickets easily after we arrived in Spain except by going to the counter. The counter tickets were double the online cost.  We were unable to purchase tickets using the Renfe app because it requires a payment code which we don’t have. When we tried Renfe.com, Renfe rejected our credit card. After an hour of fiddling with the Renfe site, we gave up and went to the counter. Does anyone have a solution? How can we use the Renfe app or website given these limitations?

Train line C1 runs between Malaga city center and Fuengirola. The line also stops at Malaga airport. In February 2019, the prices were:-Alameda (Malaga center and terminal station) - Malaga airport €1.80 approx. 20 min-Malaga airport - Fuengirola €2.70 approx. 40 min-Fuengirola - Malaga center €3.60, less than an hour. 40 minutes, so it might be good to check the schedule in advance. The ticket can be bought from the machine at the station, with cash or with a card. The ticket should be saved for the entire journey, because it will be stamped at the gate also when leaving.

I contacted customer service as I tried purchasing tickets online with 4 different credit and debit cards and none went through and delivering a pop-up that it was the bank's fault. I wrote a complaint asking for help with this issue in order to buy my tickets, their answer was literally this "Renfe dispone de varios canales de venta de billetes, es responsabilidad del cliente determinar a través de cuál de ellos realizara las compras, asumiendo los gastos en concepto de tramitación establecidos en cada uno. En la actualidad no existe la obligatoriedad de disponer de una vía telemática para gestionar el despacho de los mismo"Which basically translates to Renfe saying that it is the customer's responsibility to chose where they buy their tickets from and because they have different channels, I guess buying at the station is one of them other than online, they do not have the obligation of keeping the online service running.Are you serious?!?!Completely disappointed! Especially as there is not much you can do about it as they are the main railway company in Spain!! I just cannot believe this, instead of offering their help they honestly tell me that it is not their problem because keeping their website running is not their responsibility!!!!
Easy to and from the airport by train! Fast and also cheap, only cost €1.80 for a single ride to the center of Malaga. Simply wonderful!

Yesterday I left a bag with all my documentation inside it on one of the trains. Today I called them, first they told me that they don't have a lost and found section and second, that if they don't find it no one will let me know. WHAT THE FUCK???? So how do I know that someone has gone to check that my bag was there???? I THINK RENFE IS PAINFUL, PENSOUS first because of the treatment you give to the client over the phone and second because you demonstrate that you have zero involvement and responsibility with the client. A SHAME......

I went to the Santa Justa station (Seville) because the website did not work to buy a ticket, I do not understand why a person facing the public, dedicated to customer service, can be so dull and condescending, the treatment did not seem adequate to me... I mentioned that the website did not work and he told me "it's punctual" (let's see, sir... I've been trying all afternoon... If not, believe me, I'm not going to the station to see it)... I don't understand why every time I go there a person helps me no desire to work...
This is the most unreliable transportation in the world, period! Hardly ever did it come on time; but surely it would send you to the wrong place!

My last 3 trips on the Renfe have been soap operas, all 3 late, one of them 45 minutes, the other sold my duplicate ticket, so when I arrived I found another person with my same seat number. The conductor's solution (in a rude and cool attitude) was for me to sit on the floor, the last one was 10 minutes ago, another delay. The trip from Madrid to my town cost 12 euros, in 2 years it went to 16.70. I recommend trying to use another transportation service, this one is rubbish, although if you have to use the train you have no other choice. I hope they get competition soon and maybe they get their act together.

Easy ride - high speed and efficient. Booked the first car but ended up in the second car which was fine. Easy to catch a taxi at the train station to bring us to our hotel. We are traveling on vacation with our college-aged young adults.

Today, January 23, I bought a ticket to Córdoba. At 11:45, by mistake, I boarded the train to Almería number 13922. I asked Mrs. Capotroneno if it was the correct train, she, rudely, replied that she had other things to do and did not look at my ticket. When the train left he said the train was wrong without giving us any explanation or help. All without a minimum of education and respect. This attitude wasn't just for us. Because of this lady, we now have to wait two hours to reach the destination with a regional train and not a direct one. I hope that this complaint helps you improve the service, because I trust the professionalism of other people who work with you. If possible, I would also like to have a contact for a manager. Thank you

Terrible customer service. I called last week for a seat change to the silence car. Solved in 2 minutes, I waited to take the survey and rate the operator excellently. My surprise is when I get to the train and see that the silence car is nothing at all. I call again and they tell me that they can no longer change my seat. Pathetic experience. Also, there is no wifi on the train so you can't work if you need to. I have ever found a network but it doesn't work. It's not like we were in the 19th century.

As a citizen of the city of Algeciras, he regretted to say that the days go by and here in the first port of Spain and in a city with a unique geographical position and link between two continents we are abandoned by RENFE! The work to repair the tracks after the rain is delayed and day after day the port of Algeciras is suffocated by the containers that cannot leave by rail! Sincerely, a very dissatisfied customer Javier bersabe Reberdito
........... Renfe's service is pitiful compared to many countries. There is a lot to improve.         ....................

But not these trains.  Old, slow and cramped unless they are the new high speed lines. If you do get on these things make sure not to be in seats 1 and 2 or the last row as there are large metal parts from tables that were removed.  Just take the bus.  Nicer, cheaper, more frequent and almost as fast.

There are supposedly 2 trains a day from Algeciras to Madrid. They are Altaries from the year of the polka that do not have a silent car or anything similar. By train without 5h 30 min and by car 6h, but hey... at least it was a comfortable option to go to Madrid. However, since last winter no trains leave or arrive at the Algeciras Station because the rain flooded the road so they take you to Antequera by bus and you take the train there.  Third worldist...

Well, the same as always with the Algeciras train, an old altar that needs adaptation of the gauge to reach Madrid and with prices of a bird in the center of London. It's fine for one person, but when two people go, it makes more sense to share car expenses.

In general, I don't usually write badly about Renfe, but I didn't know where to send my complaint today. It seemed incredible to me that on the dates we are leaving the T4 airport to take the train there were only two ticket vending machines. Two huge queues have formed and it was not rush hour.  In addition, people who come to Spain and don't know how it works get together with those here who have changed our ticket from one day to the next for recharges and neither do they. To say that there was a worker helping and they helped us in front if you paid in cash but only because we asked, otherwise we had to wait 15 minutes

On 12/29/2018 we take Alvia in Orense bound for Barcelona Sants, we wait at the station more than an hour late, it arrives more than half an hour late and you go to complain and they say that it's 28 minutes, I'm fed up with the train minutes, they put what they want so as not to return part of the ticket... I missed the last connection that left and I had to pay for a hotel... Since I didn't have a connection ticket, they won't solve anything for you but maybe they would have solved it In the event that I have it... I DON'T BELIEVE IT... when they are scratching for minutes to not return the money... Well, it is easy for me to have my ticket stamped by the conductor when I get off the train and that way we will know how late the train is... Not what they say
It seems shameful to me that the "Spanish high speed" and in the year we are in does not have WIFI to offer its clients after paying a fortune for tickets.

When we got off the train at Antequerra we did not know and we're not told there was no train to Ronda. Hundreds of traveller's were in the same situation, milling around the station entrance while bases came and went, in some cases empty,. Staff had no idea what was happening and gave conflicting advice sentence to sentence. One very rude staff person constantly screamed at Asian passenger. She berated them even though, like everyone else,  they had no idea of what was happening. When we asked one staff where to wait he said jst wait where we were but many others started getting on the bus, we asked again and they said, get on. We hardly found space for our luggage underneath.  There was no luggage control. We  got the last 2 seats on the bus but not together like our ticket said.  So the train might not be running but why do rude, panicked nasty Renfe staff make the situation worse.? Chaos and poor service.  Get your actions together Renfe

What happens at the Oropesa del Mar station is shameful, they increase the number of trains for greater comfort but if you want to take any train in Oropesa you must get on the train without a ticket since the sale at the ticket office does not work and the ticket vending machine has been broken for several days and Renfe does not provide any solution. Why do we want many more trains available to travel if we cannot get the tickets at the Oropesa station due to a problem with the Renfe computer systems breaking down? don't they solve? 😞

It was so full of suitcases that I had to go the whole way with mine between my legs. A lot of movement of people coming and going all the time and the bathroom was very dirty. It was a tourist plus ticket and I paid 90 euros. The only good thing is the speed of arrival.

On our few days in Spain we travelled numerous times on the Renfe trains. Some were slow, a little crowded but all comfortable. Getting on at Pl Cataluna, for example, was exceptionally busy during early and late evenings.Tickets can be purchased using the multi-lingual machines or from the station attendant. We bought our from the ticket booth and asked for and was given the seniors discount travel.
The trains are old and are waste from other areas, the tracks are unstable and there are sections where the speed does not exceed 20 km/h, a shame, now there are closed sections and travel is by bus

The Spanish train company RENFE is very successful, I would definitely recommend it to those who will travel by train, especially long distance trains are very comfortable (AVE / AVANT trains), but buying your tickets 2 months before your travel date provides a significant price advantage. If you buy tickets at the last minute, you may pay very high prices. Buying tickets online is very easy and reliable. Wi-Fi connection on the train is only available in the cafeteria and cannot be used outside of that.
very poorly signposted airport exit.  round trip ticket from the platform vending machine, but surprise on the way back the ticket is only valid on the same day (great for tourists) a heresy.

We traveled on a Saturday afternoon by train. We leave Barcelona at 4:00 p.m. We didn't have time to eat but since we were traveling in business class we knew that they always serve you something to eat. Well, what would be our surprise that on Saturdays they don't serve any food. This doesn't seem right to me. One pays the same price on Saturday as the other days of the week. One travels in business class because one expects a little better service. This does not speak very well of Renfe. At least it should be warned.

Because I want to go from Madrid to Barcelona, ​​I chose to take the Renfe AVE high-speed train. The online ticket purchase should have been on sale 60 days ago, but it has not been seen yet. I went to Check every day and finally saw it was on sale. It is really cheaper to buy it immediately. It only costs EUR41.62. Use PAYPAL when paying, no problem. The interior of the train is clean, and it takes 2.5 hours to reach Barcelona. It is really convenient and fast.

My husband and I traveled to Malaga in October but we wanted to spend time in Seville primarily. This was looking to be really expensive by plane, so I looked into going by train  We had used Renfe trains in previous trips to Spain.So we traveled by plane to Malaga, stayed a few days, then booked a train to go to Seville.We were so pleased we did this. One,it worked out to be far more economical, and 2, we were able to see the magnificent mountains, gorges, fields, countryside of Andalucia, out of the window.The trains are clean, spacious, air conditioned and comfortable. But most importantly, the system is very well organised, extremely punctual (actually early) when the tickets are booked, you are allotted a seat number so there is absolutely no confusion, and no one has to stand!All very civilised...lolI say this because as a Londoner, our tubes often have delays as do the trains, are hugely overcrowded and many do not have air conditioning.So well done Spain....it was a pleasure to travel on Renfe.Would definitely recommend....Nearly forgot, there are plenty of sockets under the seats where you can charge phones or laptops.

Punctual and precise, Madrid-Barcelona route approximately 7.20-10.50am. Safe and clean station and train. Socket to charge your mobile phone. Check at the metal detector before entering the station. Purchased the ticket via the website, no need to stamp it. Excellent choice.

RENFE has always been an excellent service, but just beware of keeping any travel card near your phone! When staying in Fuengirola, we bought a 10 trip card, which after a few trips would not let us out through the barriers, but as someone was around to help there was no problem. The following day we went to the ticket office, and an extremely helpful agent told us that keeping the card next to a mobile caused the problem, he immediately re-validated the card and all was well, but the card was kept separately where there would be no magnetic influence.

I took RENFE from Malaga Airport to Malaga-Maria Zambrano Station. There was also an electronic display board inside the car, which made me feel safe. It was around 10pm when I arrived at the station. I hadn't eaten dinner, but since I had a suitcase, I bought a sandwich at a convenience store at the station and ate it at the hotel. The station had everything you could want, and there was even a cafe that was open early in the morning.
Impossible to book by telephone with a foreign credit card, the same from the site... insufficient service.

What a way to travel!  Lovely seats  and comfortable surroundings mean you can just relax and watch the Spanish county side wizz past. They allocate the seats with your ticket and the whole experience is a good one.  Feels like being in an aeroplane but with loads of room. They show a movie if you want to be entertained but I was happy to look out of my window seat. Train left on time and arrived in Valencia early.

If you want to avoid the queue, waiting for your luggage to arrive with you, the more than an hour waiting at a gate for a flight... then the train is your best option and RENFE does a good job. Some of the trains need charging stations for your devices and also some look quite old but in general for a short of medium distance it takes you from A to B with not much hassle.You can also take in some of the trains a bicycle with you for a little as extra 3EUR.

Málaga Barcelona - I was in a very old talgo, the seats were dirty and they didn't recline and what's worse is that they sell very expensive tickets. This journey was 12 hours, €60 and they didn't even have enough to charge the cell phone. Miniature and neglected bathrooms. Be careful if you have a long trip in a talgo, don't take it. Barcelona - MálagaAve €399070 Yes, everything is very good until you enter the bathrooms. Disgustingly dirty and they smell terrible. The faucet doesn't work and the toilet doesn't work either. You don't have to look for other nañps either. Each one is worse than the other. The truth is unfortunate. With what you pay and the bathrooms are in those conditions. Appalling. There is no choice but to travel by plane (same cost) for fewer hours of travel. More comfort.

A comfortable pre allocated seat in a spacious clean carriage with ample luggage and legroom, on time hassle free departure and only 3 minutes late arriving in Alicante after a 2 hour and 35 minute journey and all for €24.95!Fantastic value.Some of the UK train operators could certainly learn from RENFE.The entire experience was so smooth [well, apart from the online booking process, but the glitch was my fault as I inadvertently entered a telephone prefix of 34 instead of 44!].The Madrid Atocha rail station is large and on different levels and can be daunting at first, but I soon got my bearings courtesy of the most friendly and helpful staff.There are only three stops en route to Alicante; Cuenca, Albacete Los Llanos and Villena Alta Volicidad and the comfortable seat, rolling countryside and lovely coffee priced at €2.10 served by a very smartly dressed stewardess made the journey most pleasant and in no time we arrived at Alicante station.One thing to remember, the cases must be labelled with your name.

I don't know if we are going with the attitude of "they are going to let us down once again" but the truth is that except for one very kind lady who is always at the ticket office and is a huge professional, the rest are just "following orders." A thousand adventures, two thousand delays...and the passenger is never right. Renfe has a thousand and one internal laws so that you stay like the rooster of Morón. What are we going to do to him!!!

Of course, Renfe in Algeciras has a lot to improve. It is true that there have been some updates to the modern world since a few years here, such as the chargers in each seat for electronic devices that are great for so many hours of travel. Even so, I still do not understand why we have these trains that are so old and slow, why, for example, the AVE does not reach Algeciras, and why the prices are so high. On the other hand, in this case my disappointment comes from the fact that I had to travel with my pet, a dog. 5kg. The thing is that you have to pay a separate ticket for her, and then she has no rights whatsoever. To begin with, there is no space for her, she has to be put in a carrier, thank God my pet is small and I was able to put her at the foot of my seat, which left no space for me to put my feet in and enclosed my seatmate. I had to go the whole way with my legs open, and a trip of almost 6 hours in that position ends up being very annoying. On the other hand, they don't let you take her out of the carrier, at one point I had her asleep in my legs and she threw a donut and they caught my attention. I understand that she should not leave her carrier, but that they provide a space to deposit her where she can be close to me and not force me to be crouched and my seatmate completely enclosed, since I have paid a ticket for my pet independent of mine... where is her seat? I don't know if I'm explaining myself correctly, but I was very disappointed with the conditions for pets, because you pay for a place for them that doesn't exist, you have to juggle to fit it on your feet... as I said mine is small, but what if it becomes a little bigger? Where do you put the animal?

This unique line from Algeciras to Ronda was built by British engineers working for a British company. The stations on the line are all the same pattern, British colonial, and all the fittings were manufactured in Britain. It also passes through some of the most spectacular countryside in S.W. Spain.
The train was smooth and easy to get to.  Seats are comfortable and the train is very modern, especially when compared to the US Amtrak system.

Today it comes 30 minutes late, advances 50 meters and they say over the train's public address system that it has broken down. Send eggs. Users who were already inside say that it is the third breakdown. Then to claim insurance you need the dragon balls, a mermaid tear, a unicorn horn and dust from a shooting star. . Gentlemen of Renfe, please renew your trains and improve your services. I'm going to see my newborn godson in the hospital and at this rate I'll arrive for his first communion.

Paid £67 for my journey and expected high quality service but reality was far from this expectation. Despite the train being delayed by 1.5 hours there was no advance information of this for passengers so all of us had to just stand in the departures hall staring at the screen for the info to appear. Once on the train, I was surprised by how powerful the air conditioning was - it was so strong that even after changing from a dress to trousers, wrapping up with a shawl and sticking my bare feet in flip flops underneath my bag,  I was uncomfortably cold. A fellow traveller - a mother with a baby in her arms enquired to a member of staff why the tenperature was so low but there was no change after this intervention. I have to say toilets and other areas of the train were very clean and staff courteous in their tone in which they conversed with passengers. For this I give renfe 2 stars. However, overall it was a very poor experience and would not recommend renfe. Next time I will book a bla bla car at half the price.

Malaga Airport to Cordoba needs two trains, the local from the airport station just outside the terminal building to Malaga Maria Zambrano then the express to Cordoba.Large ticket office in the RENFE station section complex of the Malaga terminal and easy enough queueing system where you take a ticket from the machine and can specify for travel today or in the future. We were done and dusted with our tickets within 10 minutes. From Malaga to Cordoba there seems to be two trains an hour, one to Madrid and one to Seville , but the Seville one come in 20 Euro’s cheaper at 27Euro per person and seems to just take 5 minutes longer from what we could see.  Anyway both directions were sweet as a nut and hassle free with the journey on time and taking 65 minutes each way with two short stops at other stations.
Fast and smooth ride on Preferente (1st Class). Great Service while enjoying the  beautiful countryside. Breakfast and reading material served. A great experience while in Spain.

I have been to several cities and towns by the trains Renfe. This time one of my friends travelled with me by this train to Setenil de las Bodegas. It was the first time for her travel on this train. She is impressed on the facilities provided onboard. The train is always punctual, clean and comfy. There is air conditioning, Canteen, Vending machines and toilets onboard. Before approaching to the next station there will be an announcement both in Spanish and English.To purchase the train ticket, you can get it from the sales office or DIY machine from every station or order the ticket online. Alternatively, you can pay for the ticket to a conductor who works on board.

I loved the train service in Spain ,on our 10 day holiday in Fuengurola we used the train service several times including from Malaga airport to Torreblanca there and back.Trains were air conditioned, seats comfy,price superb and there fast and efficient. We used the trains to get to Malaga City,Benilmadina ,couldn't complain in the least.A great train service and if your planning visiting other towns and cities in this great country a great way to travel.

Nothing to say about the trains, punctuality and cleanliness: excellent. But don't buy tickets on the RENFE website: you will no longer be able to make an exchange. In fact, it is not possible at the station, the system does not communicate with that of the site, while the site asks you for a myriad of information (passport, telephone number, residence, codes, passwords, etc.) without accomplishing anything. Result: bought tickets from Segovia to Madrid again. Take them straight, always.

Many things to comment on Renfe:1. I am from Granada and I live in Valencia, so when I want to go see my family it is an impossible mission. The train station has been closed for years and what they do is put a train from Valencia to Antequera and from there a bus to Granada. It turns out that you can only take this line Monday, Friday and Sunday, when in reality the trains from Valencia to Antequera leave every day, they are not able to provide a sad one-hour bus every day. And to top it off, the train that goes to Antequera is usually AVE but if you buy the Valencia-Granada route, the train that does exactly the same route (Valencia-Antequera+bus) is LD. Turning out to be an 8 hour trip. 2.Other times I take the Valencia-Malaga or Cordoba AVE. They put on the oldest trains they have, they go slower, they don't have a bar (they pass the cart), and some of them without even being able to plug in the headphones. 3.Not to mention the sky-high prices they charge for traveling on worse trains. They charge me more for worse conditions. It costs me to travel to Andalusia for generally between 100-120 euros. Prices that are nothing like European ones. They take advantage of the fact that there is no other train company. Of course, if I can avoid them, I do.

Come to Barcelona for a holiday witty the kids, and decided to take them to Portaventura a couple of times. Getting out of Barcelona wasn’t so bad, both trains late (only 10 mins), both over crowded, and one changed platform without much notice. It was the return journies that were awful, the first was late by 3/4 hour and then broke down. We got to Barcelona 2 hours late. The train for the second journey was cancelled without warning. This left me and the kids in 28 degrees heat with no way of getting water for about 2 hours. Needless to say the train over crowded again. We eventually got to Barcelona several hours later then expected, dehydrated and famished. This has left me with a very bad opinion of Spanish public transport, apart from the Barcelona Metro. I found Sri Lanka had a more reliable train service.

On Aug 14 I used the renfe to travel from Barcelona to Valencia. My train was due to arrive at 3:30 but is was delayed for HALF an hour without a notice.On my way back on August 18th. They announced a half an hour delay but the actual delay was an HOUR. I could’ve missed my plane if I didn’t have some buffer time. They offer a trip to the airport in Barcelona but I was afraid I won’t make it on time. Very stressful experience, I don’t recommend it if you have an appointment to make. Seems like the usual delay is between 30 minutes and an hour. Worth mentioning as well that luggage space is limited so it’s better to be among the first comers to find a space for your bag (if you have a big bag that doesn’t fit in the upper compartments).

Round trip on the same day by Ave from Barcelona to Madrid and vice versa... the trip was very good, everything was very controlled... the return trip hit me and it's not Renfe's fault, a tribe of people who spent the entire trip laughing without rhyme or reason, filthy children shouting... it hurts... the worst thing about the trip, apart from the tribe, .the headphone music is a shame... I bought the ticket over the Internet and it was very good.... I came to the conclusion that the Renfe staff are unmotivated, it seems that everything doesn't matter to them... expensive prices for a bottle of water 2.10, but also the user is getting lost in the forest of dirt and lack of style, people barefoot, legs crossed and so they have a disgusting and dirty foot half a meter short!!, eating and without caring about dirtying the floor...children (over 9 years old) on top of the seats...talking on the phone (it is indicated to do so from the platforms)..I don't agree with Renfe, it needs a washed and very thoroughly of its organization... there are many inept, irresponsible and corrupt people in its ranks..... shame... it will never be achieved.........

Very poorly educated stewardess...Ave 5191 Valencia-Madrid on 8/12/2018: trip back home with an 8-month-old baby, folding cart, a large backpack and an umbrella. My seat was at the end of the car and the next one was in the cafeteria; Since the car does not fit down the aisle to exit on the other side of the car, I ask the long-haired brunette stewardess for permission to exit through the cafeteria door. He tells me no because it is the loading door of the cafeteria (at that moment there is no one loading anything).  When I explained to him that I couldn't fit the car down the hallway to get to the other door, he told me: "Well, do whatever you want." Another stewardess, a blonde with curly hair, sees the scene and immediately comes over to help me... one of them is very poorly educated and how nice the other is! And on top of that, when I tell him to speak to me with respect, he answers me wrong again... with the amount of people who want to work and they have that girl there...

Horrible service and extremely rude.  Renfe  does not care about the customer.  They would not let me take an earlier train than what was on my ticket so I had to wait 6 hours in the train station with no a/c in August.  They told me I had to buy a new ticket for 70€.  They had available seats on earlier trains, but their greed outshines their customer service by a long shot.  Its a shame that I will have to find other alternatives for travelling.  Reading all of the negative reviews only confirms that I am not alone and that there is a real problem with this company.  I think they should think about it or they will lose more customers.

Good morning, I just traveled with you yesterday, August 3, from Cartagena to Madrid, Altaria product and Madrid Vigo train hotel, and I am going to tell you about my experience, which has been quite unpleasant. On July 13, at 10:17, I am heading to the train station in Cartagena with my two children, ages 5 and 8, to buy 3 combined round-trip tickets departing on August 3 from Cartagena to Madrid. And one hour later HOTEL TRAIN madrid—ch Vigo guíx with return on August 13, the employee tells me that the return ticket will no longer be by hotel train since it will be during the day and I accept since it is something I knew, I buy the tickets and I check them over the date and time of departure and the altaria and hotel trains, we started the trip and I honestly expected something more from the train, I thought it would be a little more modern and not so old since the trays came loose on their own every time. two by three and there was no way to be able to hear the television since the headphones could not be connected and the seats so what to say........but hey one is positive and trying not to let this influence us, we arrived in Madrid 45 minutes before the next boarding, we make time, we buy something to drink and we smile because we are going to take a sleeper train some bunk beds to sleep in and what is our surprise! Wow! The car that we have had is not one with bunk beds but we are sitting with two children wanting to take the sleeper, how is it possible that when buying the tickets they have not informed us that we are not going on the sleeper train? Couldn't the employee have informed me of that? Wasn't it important to him? He knew what he was selling me and for me it was the first time I traveled by train. I didn't know that there was the option of a seat and not a bed. Can you imagine the cries of the two children? Can you imagine the night we spent? It seems incredible to me that an employee did not correctly report what he was selling, and finally, do you know how this service is that has not been cleaned at any time during the journey? Do you know that the seats are very difficult to slide? The trays go down by themselves, in short, very upset with the trip and knowing that I have the returned one, I am sorry to tell you that my trip was very negative and that I will not travel with you again, greetings

15 March 2018 we reserved two Renfe Spain Passes, each for 6 journeys.Then we booked hotels in six cities.We then tried to reserve seats on Renfe website, but the website demanded payment before we could continue the process.  We had already paid for the Renfe Spain Pass.The website was a challenge, e.g. instructions reverted to Spanish after the first page in English, which was frustrating. So we had to go to the station at each of the cities we visited, as soon as we arrived, to book the next leg. This worked well in Barcelona and San Sebastián, but when we arrived in Madrid the trains were all full. We had to pay for a bus ride to Granada,  In Granada we had to find the Renfe station (not easy with many people telling us that it was closed) and reserved seats to Madrid (partly on bus because of construction works). The bus was fine, but when we transferred to the train the seats allocated were double booked. So we were standing in the aisle with our suitcases for some time, while the staff tried to find two seats in a very full train.  Then a kind Mexican family moved around and we two were sitting in the same coach (no thanks to Renfe).We wanted to visit Córdoba but it was just too hard to find train/bus information so we gave up.In Madrid we reserved seats to Toledo, and two days later back to Madrid. In a train about one quarter full we were given seats at the opposite end of the train. Why ?  I am 80 and wish to stay with my companion.  We would not have used our Pass on these short journeys if we had been able to go to Córdoba.  Such a waste, and we still only used five of our six journeys.The trains were clean punctual and so comfortable and the scenery great, but the Renfe service, signage and information access was the worst I have had in fifty years of travel in Europe. With the exception of a helpful man in Barcelona, the Renfe staff seemed to regard us as a nuisance in their day.  Our pass was a waste of money and time.

Definitely This is NOT an express train, but rather a 12 hour ride with stops. Having traveled using Renfe between Madrid, Valencia and Barcelona, the train used is old. Seats are worn out and the bathroom overflowed. The overhead screen monitors were not working, it was tough to see what station we are about to arrive...nor any announcements. Conductor was inattentive, can’t even suggest where to put our luggage since there were no more space in the rack & too big overhead. Next time I will just fly from SS to Lisbon...spare myself the agony of such long trip and hear incessant chattering all night from some passengers.

We traveled by train Madrid to Algeciras. It was comfortable, clean and fast. The ticket price was fair and we were able to see Spain along the way. The attendants were friendly and came through with service often. There was a cafeteria onboard with really good coffee and sandwiches. They provided a movie and music with complementary headphones. The bathrooms were clean and the ride was smooth. Would definitely travel renfe anytime!

We took it in Malaga to Barcelona because Vueling canceled us 12' before checking in the luggage. The trip is on time, the train is clean, the dining room is expensive. The only observation is that it does not have Wi-Fi, although the logo is on the train, the service is not provided

We were greatly disappointed when we contracted the preferential rate that had access to the Renfe Club room where they only offered water, coffee and infusions, it is not worth paying more for this “upgrade.”

Our family travelled all over Spain on Renfe trains, high-speed and first class when we could, fabulous -- smooth, great service, good food and wine.BEWARE OF EURAIL PASS, however!  For non-Europeans at least, it is not worth it unless you know exactly when and where you will be traveling and can book these well in advance.  A big headache to book reservations for trains, you need to additionally complete forms once you're at the train station, no exchanges available unless each ticket is >25euros which is rare so our family lost 23euros x4 twice because we changed one travel leg, NO PHONE NUMBER, NO PHYSICAL OFFICE, NO CUSTOMER SERVICE (email took >2wks to respond!!).  I don't understand how a company is legally allowed to operate without these components.

We bought four passes for two adults - ran us over $400 but we were able to travel from Madrid, Barcelona, Malaga, and back to Madrid.Pro tip: book early and reserve seats in the silence car.This is the most inexpensive and nicest way to travel through Spain. We got to each location in 3 hours or less. The train travels 194mph!

Very comfortable train, smooth journey and enough room for the luggage however terrible service for English speaking travellers at the train station. I have given three star because of customer service at Attocha station (Midrid). It seems like they hate English speaking travellers.  Automatic ticket kiosk of Renfe wasn't working and online service was only for the travellers with renfe card holders so we had no option other than stay in three different lines (3 times) for 45 minutes in order to purchase tickets. Also, you have to pay for pee :) at train station so make sure to keep change. Good luck.

My wife and I recently stayed in Algeciras, Spain while on vacation and I had the time to visit the Renfe Train Station. I walked around the platform at the station taking pictures of the station, and the older historic station which is not in use and the passenger train that had just pulled up to the platformIt was a Renfe train and I spoke to the engineer  named  Juan, and he offered to give me a tour of his train. The coaches are very modern, clean, and comfortable. Everything about this train says "take a ride".The Renfe train set that I toured was a  real pleasure to see how Spain regards their passenger trains...And their stations too....And I could tell how proud of his train Juan was....

We planned a morning trip from Barcelona to Madrid.  Two days in advance we attempted to purchase tickets online.  Their website refused to valid MasterCards and a Visa card.  We telephoned them, and the person who answered attempted with all 3 valid cards (working everywhere else) to complete the purchase.  We went to the station, and the machines and the clerk both failed to accept our cards.  We were told we would have to buy the tickets from the machines on the day of travel.  We went early, and the machines did not work, and the clerk could not complete the purchase as well.  We were told we would have to pay cash, but the clerk could not sell us a ticket, only the train manager who could, who rode aboard the train.  He would come up from the tracks as soon as the train arrived.  There were on average trains running that route about every 45 minutes.  The first manager to arrive told us he only had 1st class tickets, and that instead of $112 Euros, we would have to pay more than 400 Euros each.  We waited for the next train, and it had no room.  We began this process en the early morning, and finally were able to purchase expensive tickets for the 2 PM departure, getting us there at the supper hour rather than before noon, as we had planned.SCAM!!Fly, it's quicker and cheaper.

Lately they don't allow you to select your seat online and frankly the assignment leaves a lot to be desired. And it's not about a window or aisle, but you are automatically assigned a table and they are so happy. For long distances, table seats are horrible because you can't stretch your feet without hitting the one in front of you and I don't understand how people who haven't specifically asked for it are assigned without further ado.

I would give this a minus rating if there were one.  A word of warning if you are planning on any train travel with Renfe please book well ahead on line!!!!!!!  We wanted to travel  from Barcelona to Madrid, thinking we could get the tickets when we were in Barcelona.   I tried two days before travel and was told that 3 different credit cards were not acceptable.  I went to the train station the day before travel and was told I could only purchase tickets on the day of travel.  After going to the train station the next day again our credit cards would not work and we would have to pay cash.  Unfortunately there were no tickets available except for first class seats, the price in effect more than doubling, and they insisted on cash.  We waited for several hours as the supervisor from each train comes 1/2 hr before that train leaves and lets you know if there are seats available on that train.   This is my worst moment of travel in Europe and if you are planning train travel in Spain book ahead, and check out other web sites to get tickets.  A friend got his ticket only through the site of a third party re-seller after failing to at the official website.

I booked online with trainline, 21 days before I travelled, return tickets from Seville to Cordoba. I booked the mid distance train, instead of the express, saving myself lot's of Euros. O.K. it took one hour twenty minutes, each way, but I was in no rush, being on holiday. Two night's In Cordoba, then returning to Seville. It worked great for me, reserved seats, 21Euros return ticket. Thank you Renfe. I'll do it again.

Taking the overnight train from Madrid to Lisbon looked like a fabulous adventure.  Websites described the lovely dining and breakfast experience (free to grand class customers).  THIS NO LONGER EXISTS.There is an uninviting cafe car which was poorly stocked.  The staff were lacklustre.  The train and cabin was old, very loud and very uncomfortable.  The toilet/shower was passable but in need of updating.  If you want a relaxing journey and a good night's sleep, don't bother.  However, if you like a train journey rather than the plane, this is the one for you - just be aware of the facilities available

One of the worst train I have seen in my Europ tripTrain was stuck at Albacete Los Llanos station  for more than two hours with no one to share the update with passengers For 11 hrs journey they don’t have phone charging options , I mean I was completely shocked 😮 Headphone provided dose not workSeats are dirtyNone of the announcement were made in English

My experience is that the services are terrible and very expensive, the cleanliness is poor, and kindness is conspicuous by its absence. It also cannot be that the prices are more expensive at the station than on the website. Also the website does not work well

Got the train from Malaga to Ronda. Not an easy place to get to. Only 2 hours by train and station 5 mins from city center. Great way to get there....Something changes with the train just after Bobadillo, it takes you a few minuets to put your finger on it?????

This train/metro is extremely convenient for airport-stay transfer. You pay only €1.80 for a single ticket, which you can buy at the machine (several languages ​​available), with cash (coins or notes up to €20) or with the card. You must keep this ticket to get through the gates (both when leaving and when arriving). The train runs every 20 minutes (May 2018), line C1.

I easily bought numerous Renfe trickets at the Loco2 website. A great site that explains everything and allows you to purchase tickets in assorted European countries. The site is full of interesting and usual information and the staff is responsive to all enquired.The Spanish trains are punctual, comfortable and quiet. But one major drawback of the quiet mechanics of the train is that you most often have to listen to people speaking loudly on their cell phones for the entire journey. It would be good if Renfe would either provide quiet cars or require people to go between cars whenever they use their cell phones. The media-distance trains were my favorite as the media screens show you a map of the train’s route and the next destination. It also make clear audible announcements in both Spanish and English, so you don’t have to worry about missing your stop, which could be easy to do as the trains remain only a minute or two at each station.

Their website wouldn’t take my American credit card and their iPhone app wouldn’t either.In Valencia’s train station there is NO seating for those going Barcelona.And there’s no WI-FI on the “Preferente” fast trains between Madrid / València  / Barcelona!!!!!!!!!  What is this, the dark ages?  I’d even pay for the service if offered.

We took the AVE train from Madrid to Seville and it was a very pleasant experience.  The seats were comfortable and the staff were pleasant and helpful.  The stations were a little tricky - we had some trouble finding our way around the Madrid Atocha station.  Signage could definitely be improved. We had booked 60 days before the trip and prices were very reasonable.

I am trying to book tickets for trains for my family in early June. The Renfe website shows that the price of the time I would like is 49.55E. However, when I add more people to the reservation, the price of the ticket inflates to 62.70E. Why is this? We are travelling with 7 adults, and 2 children (age 6 and 3). My 6 year old is being charged a full fare like the adults. Is this typical. I have priced the route via multiple website (Loco2/Renfe/Trainline) and all have the same results. Why is the price of the ticket inflated as the size of the group is larger??

Travelled from Barcelona to Madrid. Even though the website was in Spanish, Google translate translated the entire page to English for us, which made things a lot easier.
