Seats were comfy, food was great and free flow of drinks (including cava) for business class section. The only thing is if you are travelling with tons of luggages, do try to board early as there are limited luggage space available (we were seated at Coach 1).

Used the AVE to travel from Madrid to Malaga. We treated ourselves to Business Class which cost about €80 each, one way. The carriage wasn’t new but provided large and comfortable seats. Breakfast was offered along with drinks which we didn’t try. The train reached speeds of 290km/h and took a little more that two and a half hours to reach Malaga. All in all a great experience at what felt like a sensible price.
There are no other options than Renfe in this country for the railway. In the province of Barcelona, ​​the service is disastrous, slow, with breakdowns and delays, expensive and without alternatives.

Today I missed a train, it was at the time it said on my ticket, but even so, they didn't let me access it. The fact is that the train left at 6:20 a.m., so when I arrived at the station and tried to enter through the usual door, I found that it was closed... I went all the way around the station, until I managed to get in and had to go back to the first floor, where the access to my train was... When I arrived at the checkpoint, the girl who checks the tickets is talking on the phone... When she finishes her conversation, she reads my ticket with a little machine. I put my backpack in that lightning tunnel, and a security girl who talks and laughs with another... She tells me that I also have to carry the jacket... I turn around, put the jacket in, the jacket comes out and I run to the counter, where a lady, with bad manners, tells me that the train is closed... It is, on her watch, 6:20 a.m. He informs me that the train closes its doors two minutes early, that another one leaves at 7:00 a.m., that I should go to the counter in front and they will change it. So I do it, and they send me to someone else... When I arrive, I explain the situation to him... On his watch... It's still 6:20 a.m., it seems that at that time time stops on the Atocha clocks. They send me to the ticket office on the ground floor, where they tell me that they have computers without a network, to go to customer service, where a man alone and on the phone tells me that there is no other option than to travel at 9:00 p.m. on this same day... Unless I buy another ticket paid in cash... Look, I don't usually go with too much cash in my pockets... So for a machine, I have had to change another ticket again. , without any help, empathy, kindness, attention or good work for any of these people. Very dissatisfied, so it's better to tell it, in case anyone doesn't want to be surprised. I have it clear, my next trip by bla bla car, much cheaper and at least, I will know what to expect...
In andalusia I used a lot this bus service to move from a city to another one. Usually the buses is on time and with comfortable seat
Fast, efficient, clean, economical.  Left wishing our US trains could be like this.  There is no better way to travel in Spain.

I really enjoyed the train, we booked first class and it was very comfortable. We took the train to Barcelona and it $210.00 A which I thought was pretty steep but we wanted the expierence.  Future reference book at the station not on line from the states it cheap and there were plenty of seats . You had to purchase a drink or food on the train and for the cost of the trip should be provided in my opinion  The Renfe station in Madrid is really beautiful so if you arrive early walk around it's really nice.  First class was really comfortable and the country side is spectacular.  Would definitely do this again.
I have used it to go to Madrid several times. tranquillity. few stops. The journey is not long... I take advantage of the offers if you get them in advance. good price.

Used Ave Renfe for this route. Excellent. first of all safety, then the services (film, music, restaurant, free earphones, socket for charging cell phones, etc.) a journey of 2 hours and 50 minutes.... flown in complete relaxation

The trains are the fastes mode of transport here and the operators will always keep an eye out for tourists and give you a friendly nudge to make sure you’re getting off at the right place.Also an economical form of transport.

We had a horrible experience with Renfe today when travelling to Girona from Barcelona. The train departure was at 9:45 and we were by the gate at 9:43 but they did not let us on the train. Needless to say, we were not informed about this (except for a Spanish note on the ticket). At 9:45 we were in the office to exchange the tickets for a later train but after waiting for 10 minutes they only abruptly said ‘not possible’ and we were not helped with our issue anymore. The person who sold us the tickets was really helpful originally, but the Renfe office was the opposite, even though they had the power to do so as we later found out. There goes our 60€... thank you Renfe for the special help not provided!My recommendation is don’t even bother going into the Renfe office at Barcelona Sants, as you won’t be helped, but going there is really beneficial should you want to wait in a sauna for 10+ minutes with no one noticing you for a while. :(

I really thought that paying preferential would give me a decent service for me and my family... to begin with, the suitcase locker is full, I almost have nowhere to put mine and I'm surprised that those who can't store them have to put them in the doors building the exits... Zero cleaning, the toilet doesn't smell STINKS.. what a disappointment!! I was thinking about the tourist class that was also packed... about the obstruction with the luggage... the bad smells... total disappointment... however I previously took the MD Figueres Barcelona train... it was empty, much more modern for a 1 hour and a half journey... clean and leagues modern... and the 7 hour journey is sad...

We travelled from Barcelona to Girona and back and had a fast, punctual, comfortable journey; the train clocked 130mph for much of the time.A couple of points to watch:Check the seat and carriage numbers on your ticket and don't try to sit anywhere else.When you buy a return you have to specify the times of both the outgoing and return trains; tickets are not valid on any train.You can change the time of your return trip at no cost if you ask at the customer service office at your destination; the lady at the Girona office was very helpful with this.We were seated in a Quiet carriage on the return trip; not a problem for us but  if you want to talk it might be worth mentioning this when buying the tickets.

We took Ave to go from Madrid to Lleida. The train departured 3 minutes late from Atocha station when Renfe and the Spanish goverment always are bragging of its punctuality.In our carriage it was full of people shouting instead of talk like normal persons. Please, I've paid an amount of money to enjoy a quiet trip.The train is unconfortable, noisy and expensive for its service. This company is a shame in general

We booked online prior to our Andalucía trip that included many cities including Seville, Malaga,Ronda,Granada and Granada in early April. The Medium Distance trains are sleek looking, clean and relatively quiet. The Seville to Malaga train departed Estacion San Justa, a clean modern station right on time. It made many stops along the way. Then half way to Malaga the conductor announced in Spanish (he held up iPad with English translation) that due to technical issue we had to switch trains in Osana. Turned out as soon we exited they used the same train to take another group of passengers back to Seville while we scrambled with our luggage crossing the track to the south bound platform and board another train. That was puzzling. The Malaga Maria Zambrano station was even more impressive. We took s day trip train to Ronda. Apparently only 1 daily round trip. 1000-1600. We finished our sightseeing in much less time but ended sitting the Ronda station cafeteria. We will try renfe again in the future.

We used Renfe (Spanish train operator) for travel to and from Barcelona-Madrid and quite unlike the trains I took from Holland-Germany - these were the best! The seats were comfortable and plenty of leg room (premium turista) and of course the high speed ensures you get to and fro the major cities fast! It is relatively easy to figure out your cabin and the service staff are fantastic help even if you don't understand Spanish. FANTASTIC!

I traveled the Valencia-Barcelona route first class!!!! I must say a perfect trip... we had dinner on board (all free) pampered in everything... from the pretzels... to the complete dinner with dessert and dark chocolate to finish... kind and friendly!!!!! FS ITALIA... take an example!!!

I used Renfe, the Spanish train operator to travel from Cordoba to Seville at the beginning of March. Knowing that the best deals are available in advance booking online I chose to do this. The Renfe website was a little confusing though so I booked via Loco2 instead who offer tickets all across Europe. For the time that I wanted the high speed option seemed the best so this was the one I chose. It didn't cost that much more than the regular service and got me there a lot quicker so as to optimise the time I had. Finding my way around the station was easy with the platforms all signposted with large boards displaying train times and platforms. The practise of having to X-ray luggage did though seem strange to me, although I guess after the Madrid bombing I can understand this. Either way it was quick and painless and I was soon on my way. These high speed trains travel at 186 mph so the countryside literally whizzed past and it seemed that in no time (45 minutes in fact) I was there. For such a short journey refreshments are not needed, but the train did have toilets I noticed, not that I needed that either. Other than that the layout was pretty much the same as any long distance  British train, with tables and plugs for you to recharge phones and so on and plenty of space for luggage. One thing I will say is that the trains did seem considerably cleaner than their British counterparts, and are considerably less crowded which always makes for a more pleasant trip. Last time I travelled this way at home the carriages were crowded full of annoying people playing noisy games with their bags blocking the gangway - not so here. Perhaps that would be different in the height of summer, I don't intend to find out as the heat would be too much for me.This for me was overwhelmingly the best way to travel. Having tried Alsa as well, the Spanish bus company trains are an altogether faster, more comfortable and more civilised way to get around - in my opinion - and far more convenient as well!

The trains are very clean, they are VERY PUNCTUAL in their departures, they arrive at their destination on time. During the journey there is a bar service, TV, personal headphones. The seats are spacious and quite comfortable. Excellent security in the train stations. The only flaw is the high cost and the journey time is a little excessive, almost like a bus.

This was my first visit to Madrid Spain.  We wanted to go to Barcelona, so we took the RENFE.  We booked it on line and everything went smoothy.  The seats were comfortable.  They even gave us a complimentary breakfast on our morning trip.  It took almost 3 hours from Madrid to Barcelona, but the 3 hours flew by.  It was very pleasant and I will definitely use RENFE again when in the area.

Most travellers will tell you to take the bus, but I took the train, and I’m glad I did. I spent a night in Sevilla, had a good dinner, and left at about midday on the media distancia the next day, (a very civilized time!) with a brief stop in Antequera de Santa Ana.  After a few days in Ronda, took the Altaria to Algeciras, the rail line follows a route through the Parque Natural, with amazing vistas around every bend. I took advantage of my Tarjeta Dorada  (seniors card) which made the journey very affordable. The train offers great comfort, and the on board and station staff were all very helpful and courteous. Not as direct, but much more comfortable and scenic than the bus!

The electric train is good and fast, since it reaches 180km, but due to repairs they change the locomotive to diesel in the last 100km, and there it gets slower. The attention of the waitress is good, and also of the lounge bar, and the toilets. They are clean. There isn't much to complain about, the movie and music help with the 5 and a half hour trip from Madrid.

This appears to have become a general review site for all RENFE journeys. Whilst responses are varied, we enjoyed an excellent day return from Valencia to Madrid. Comfortable seats ( Much better than our local trains in the U.K. ) in standard class and trains running on time. A great way to travel whilst enjoying views of the Spanish countryside.

We crossed the Straits of Gibraltar from Tangier Med to Algeciras Ferry Terminal and took a taxi to Algeciras Train Station, which is a 5-min ride.  Tickets were purchased a day earlier through Loco2, a reliable online booking service. As we have a wheelchair elderly with us, we have to specify it during booking as the train staff will help us during boarding and alighting and even during stop at Antequera Santa Ana, where we have to change to a bus to continue to Granada. We were impressed by their extra careful service towards the less mobility. This route has a very scenic views that some panoramas look like paintings with your naked eyes. Superbly amazing.

The Lisbon-Madrid night train was a 4-star journey for me. It was a perfectly pleasant and  functional way to do the trip and arrived in Madrid at a good time and place to do a half day sightseeing trip. I imagine that it might get lower scores from people hoping for an Orient Express-style luxury experience though. It was a bit rattly, but I got to sleep OK. The cabin and bedding were fine, and the bunk comfortable enough. The bar-restaurant was open to everyone (i.e. not restricted to the Gran Classe ticket holders), and the meal was quite nice and the atmosphere was very convivial (but again the meal might not have satisfied a gourmet; it is not a special culinary experience). I just took one star off because they do a ticket check in the middle of the night. I think this is because the same guy doubles up with ticket and bar work, so he can only check the tickets once the bar has closed - it's a pity both for him and the sleeping passengers that Renfe don't hire one extra person, As a UK card holder and non-Spainish speaker, it was easier for me to get the ticket from loco2.com (who were very helpful) than the Renfe site. All in all, I was pretty happy and the biggest single advantage is that the hour of leaving Lisbon and that for arriving Madrid make it like a cheap and cheerful hotel that shifts you between places at times that fit conveniently with maximizing trip time in both cities.

I had booked a train from Salamanca to Madrid, we realised when we go to the station that we booked for the wrong month but when we got to the desk the lady said no worries  you can pay on board for 20 euros, a similar price to booking online. We boarded the train and took a seat. The man who we’d confirmed this price with earlier approached us. We had minimal cash on us for emergencies and for our accommodation at our destination. He informed us he had to calculate the cost and concluded it was 41.30 euros each to Madrid. We did not have enough cash on us for this price, as we were not told we needed this amount before boarded the train. The Renfe employee was very rude and refused to help us solve the issue in anyway and just kept repeated the price. . My associate could converse with him as her Spanish is reasonably good but he refused to listen and made us feel very threatened and he used a very intimidating manner in the way he spoke to us. Everyone else in the cabin also seemed to feel very uncomfortable but nobody interfered most likely due to his rude tone. I was astounded by the terrible service by Renfe. I personally will not be using the service again and would recommend to anyone that is considering it to not do so!

This train journey was punctual and quite comfortable. No surprises just a good way to get from Malaga to Seville. It was not as fast as I thought it would be but it was comfortable and I would certainly use it again.
Went by bus to Ronda and returned by train. Fabulous countryside. Occasional white villages. Smooth and very comfortable train journey. Highly recommended.

Going by AVE is a good experience, especially for long distances. The mid-distance are comfortable. The best way to travel with a place to stretch your legs, with a toilet, bar and outlet to recharge your cell phone or whatever you want.

The train in terms of price, speed, cleanliness of the seats is very good, but the cafeteria is not! Horrible price quality! But the worst thing is the waiter's dislike, his job may not be his aspiration, the salary may be shit, but since you're here, why not have a good time? Why not be kind? Why not have a smile and say hello? If it bothers you so much to serve, then do something! Meanwhile, for the people who pay their ticket and who consume, make their trip pleasant, at least with the minimum, a good day, a thank you, a greeting. Bcn-Seville train 3940 8:30 a.m.

They give schedule options and do not comply with any. As if that were not enough, they do not provide solutions of any kind, and they defend their task by being completely rude. We leave Barcelona Sants at 12 noon and arrive in Murcia at 9 pm. Being that the ticket said that we would arrive exactly 6:57 p.m. We asked for some explanation about it and we were only ignored (they told us that when we arrived we would see what we were doing). We had a ticket integrated with another trip to Cartagena and we lost it. We approached to ask for a solution because there was no way to get to a city at 1am, they were waiting for us. In fact we paid more to arrive earlier and we found the cheapest train in Murcia but not the time we could arrive.  We had to wait 2 more hours at the train station, which has absolutely nothing in Murcia, without any solution. We even thought of a taxi to Cartagena that costs €70. The train arrives at the station surprisingly. We sat down and had to wait 1 hour for the driver to arrive because we had to take a taxi to be able to leave. I am ashamed of the problem and the treatment with which a gray-haired man addressed me, treating me as a liar in front of “his passengers” as if I were not one. I am supposed to be able to demand a full refund of the ticket when I don't take that train. The information they had just given me. The only thing I can rescue is the sales manager who put herself in the place of a student who comes to a city to live at ONE IN THE MORNING, and had compassion. But from then on they are terrible. I prefer the plane 🖕🏼
The station is small, without many services but totally adequate for the waiting times of a small station. Around there is the bus station and you can use that cafeteria.

Since the connection possibilities are scarce, it is inevitably a small station, very close to the bus station and close to the port, making it feasible to walk if you don't have a lot of luggage. It is also close to a hotel and the city center.

I use Renfe long distance quite often. It can be expensive, but if you are over sixty, which I am, you can buy a gold discount card (tarjeta dorada) and get up to forty percent discount. The card costs just six euros and is valid for a year. And the card is active the minute you buy it. What’s more you do not have to be SPANISH to get it. All you need is your passport for proof of birth. You can also use it when you buy your tickets on line. I got my six euros back and more on my first ticket. Jerez to Madrid should have been 75 euros, cost me 48, plus. 6,.....54 euros in total ! As for the trains, clean, fast, comfortable, on time. Some routes have a very high demand,, so book as early as you can. Also, as the trains head towards a sell out the price can go up quite a lot. Food wise, better to prep something to go with you before you set off, or buy something outside of the station. Think Ryanair food because that is what you get, expensive and non nutritional. At a push it’ll do I suppose.

The building is in the lower area of ​​the city in front of the old Hotel Octavio building where the bus station is located. They have the possibility of using the train to reach Madrid, Ronda and Granada. The latter with stops at almost all the stations along the route and arriving in Madrid at Antequera-Santa Ana via the AVE railway line. The building has no artistic value. It does not have a cafeteria. There is parking and the possibility of renting a car (EUROPCAR). In a straight line you can access the Passenger and Merchandise Port in just 10'.

On the line from Madrid and Cordoba to Algeciras, the quality of the track deteriorates as you pass Ronda, the speed suddenly slows down, and the train starts to shake a lot. In addition, since it is a single line, it will be directly affected by the delays of up and down lines. You need to plan with plenty of time.
Qualified personnel who are attentive to any passenger who needs help with information or who needs personnel because they have a disability.

We booked renfe train from Toulouse in France to Cordoba Spain in advance. Total amount was €511 for 3 person. 3 transits from Toulouse to Narbonne to Madrid Atocha and finally Cordoba. The train from Toulouse to Narborne was just a normal slow train with no sitting. It cost us €71.50. Then we had to get down to another train from Narbonne to Madrid costing us €252.The train was not high speed as claimed. Seats were not comfortable. Aisle narrow and no free wifi. I had a seat facing another passengers and I could not stretch my legs without kicking her.Finally we need to get down the train and board another train from Madrid to Cordoba. Long way to walk from one station to the other. The tickets cost us €188.10.If you have travel by Kiwirail from Wellington to Auckland which offers so much cheaper tickets you will see the differences. Luggages check in and you do not need to carry or run from one station to another. Service is tip top. Seats are very comfortable. Or if you talk about high speed train try Japan Shinkansen.Overall we were very disappointed with Renfe. Expensive yet not up to standard.This is my first and last time taking Renfe train

For us it was a very pleasant experience. Punctuality, cleanliness, attention on a modern train, and at a highly appreciable value. With breakfast service we travel very comfortable and feel safe. The Spanish landscape is very particular and is worth seeing. Just one detail is that (strange) the bathroom at the end of the route had a strange smell (it was not dirty), which caught our attention.

Terrible service. Slow and old trains, you either die of cold or are roasted by heat, with hardly any space for your suitcases, very uncomfortable seats, the televisions are from the 18th century and high prices for the service they provide. They always arrive late, they are never on time. In addition, it makes too many stops. For a journey like this (more than 5 hours) there should be another type of train that makes the trip more enjoyable. Renfe will take very good care of all AVE, but with regard to Talgo, Alvia, Euromed, etc. that travel along the Mediterranean coast, it seems that the trains have not yet changed the century.
We traveled from Seville to Barcelona by AVE. Punctual departure and arrival, car with a pleasant temperature, and comfortable seats. I would repeat the experience.

For about 3 months, every, EVERY time I have taken the AVE to go to Madrid, three times, and to Burgos, once, I have arrived late. Obviously they have compensated me, but it is a pain to be late for a meeting due to... I actually don't know what it was due to because on none of the occasions have they said anything over the public address system.
Took the high speed (almost express) from Gerona to Madrid. it was just about three hours. Comfortable seating. Clean restrooms. Club car for snacks. A spanish movie for fun. 110EHighly recommended

False and misleading punctuality commitment. Train from Madrid to Córdoba more than 35 minutes late and they do not compensate, hiding behind the fact that it is a ticket purchased at a promotional rate (difference to the normal price 4e per ticket) misleading advertising in which they inform absolutely nothing. A shame.
I find it sad that for a few years there has not been a train that goes directly from Granada to Algeciras. When will they finish the work?

A good choice we made when taking the AVE to go to Madrid. Punctual, comfortable and fast. We were debating whether to go by train or by car and in the end we decided on the train and one of the best journeys we have ever made. You don't even notice the time or the train, it's pure comfort. It should be noted that the price is not cheap, but even so, we would repeat.
Cheap way to travel, from Fuengirola to Malaga airport €2.70. Trains run in 20 minutes. at intervals and the schedules can be trusted.

I use the train from Madrid to Toledo. The train was comfortable and really fast. To board in Madrid I would suggest to arrive earlier because of the lines to check the tickets and the security area, specially on Summer.
This is RENFE of the Spanish National Railways. Algeciras station is a very lonely station with only a few trains arriving and departing each day.

Dear users, as a commuter, as soon as I saw all the well-organized and safe systems active in the train stations of Spain, my eyes opened wide. And this also applies to the excellent service offered by Renfe used for the Seville-Cordoba route; 45 minutes of pure relaxation admiring the Andalusian landscape.

I recently travelled on various journeys using the high speed trains, 2 of my journeys were from Barcelona to Madrid then Madrid to Valencia, they are the most modern, comfortable trains I’ve ever been on and I can’t wait to travel other parts of Spain, I never had any issues with the Renfe website and it was easy enough to find the right platforms, however especially in Barcelona allow yourself a spare 30mins to get to the actual platform, very busy route, the earlier you book tickets the cheaper they are, I only purchased the tourist class tickets and the seats + carriage were great, plenty leg room, so relaxing, can’t wait to do this again...puts UK trains to shame, they are an utter disgrace compared to Spain

On two different trips through Spain, we used the Internet to choose routes, times and prices. Then with these choices displayed in Notes or other app, so that they can be shown to the Ticket office for a quick and easy method of telling the Agent if you do not speak the same language. Saves time, too!

We travelled from Seville Santa Justa to Jerez de La Frontera on a Renfe mid distance train, and were very impressed. It only cost about £32. return for two of us (just over an hour each way) and the train was clean comfortable, very punctual and a very smooth ride. There is lots of room and a good size tray table with a cup holder. First time using a Spanish train and after our experience it won't be the last.
Good punctuality, comfortable but without Wi Fi. With the prices they charge they should have internet at least. Fastest way to travel in Spain.

I just returned from PortugalI just returned from Portugal, a beautiful country experiencing a great tragedy with the fires, something that prevented me from selfishly thinking like 500 more Renfe travelers, who trapped us in Coimbra on a Talgo Altaria hotel train, on 10/16/2017, we should never have left Lisbon, the communication routes being on fire, but they took us out, locked us in a road for 12 hours, without food nor drink nor any communication, we tried to speak with the Spanish consulates and there was no response, much less from Renfe, they are totally incompetent, is it that no one works there?, no one is responsible for anything there?, no one has an action protocol in cases like this?, Renfe does not deserve any respect from me, especially after having crossed Portugal in flames, by bus, in Madrid, "trip Lisbon-Madrid, 24 hours", no one provided us with the passes to our house, they misinformed us where we had to go, for this we pay taxes in the provinces?, so that some gentlemen can sit in the court of Madrid?, to all those who are not scandalized by these, I hope they do not have to go through what we have gone through, Renfe does not have qualified personnel to handle extraordinary situations, Spain is a country that at this moment only cares about the 155 and they care nothing about their citizens, something that I must underline in capital letters, YOUR CITIZENS DO NOT CARE ABOUT ANYTHING

The train system is good however they have a lot of room for improvement. Took a lot of trains during my trip in Spain and here are my observations: -Employees at the Toledo train station are very rude and not helpful at all. We arrived to the train station on time to take a previous train and even when there was room they did not allow us to take that one. They said we could leave and come back which we did but unfortunately lose cause they said the train was leaving. When we asked for help for a later time they were rude and said "take a taxi". -On the train from Madrid to Cordoba when arriving Cordoba they asked everyone to wait until they could complete an exchange and then leave without notifying when people staying at Cordoba could get out of the train. We ended up having to go Seville and back to Cordoba but unfortunately lose our tour. Spain is very disorganized in general, lot of people is rude and have no idea of what customer service means. Sincerely, hope to not come back ever again!

We travelled from Barcelona to Madrid Tourist class, was a fantastic trip. Then we went from Madrid to Avignon, about seven hours in first class. Awesome comfy train and good service from the staff onboard. Our last trip on RENFE was Avignon back to Barcelona, another hassle free comfy ride. Awesome to bet able to charge iPhone & iPad at your seat as you travel along. We had pre purchased our tickets from RailPlus in NZ before leaving, took all the hassle out of trying to speak Spanish & French at the counters.

This High Speed AVE train is a little bit more expensive that an airline ticket for the same route; however it is well worth it.  First of all the time you save by not having to drive to airports and wait 2 hours before your flight.  Same in the arrival city, the train station is in the heart of Barcelona and it took a very inexpensive taxi ride to our hotel.  We bought the premium class and we got a lunch and a drink which was really good.   The only drawback is that the cars do not have enough space for luggage.   Overall it was a great experience.
We arrived 4 minutes before the train started and even though it was stopped, they didn't let us get on and made us pay the full fare for the ticket from Toledo to Madrid and wait another hour.

We just finished our second trip on the RENFE trains-the first from Madrid to Valencia, the second from  Valencia to Cartagena (with an easy change at Albacete).The booking process was easy to do on line (and we don't speak Spanish). The car and your seat are clearly marked and the Valencia North Station was especially easy to navigate.The trains are clean and comfortable and we loved being able to buy a glass of wine as we travelled.A couple of negatives RENFE-get with the times and allow us to use our mobile phones to check in and provide more space for large luggage.

We read a lot of mixed reviews about the train. But my friend and I decided to try it out to save time and money, plus we just like trains. The website is bizarre. I had paragraphs in English and other paragraphs in Spanish. Luckily I'm bilingual by even with that we found it difficult to properly book 2 tickets. Somehow we ended up booking for for a cheaper rate than the original two so we listed the names of our alter egos. Some things really work out. We ended up with a nice 4 seat table right by the bar where you can definitely by snacks and beers. They also come through the cabin multiple times with a little food and drink cart. As the train filled up more at each stop we were happy we had accidentally booked all 4 seats. I'd highly recommend this mode of transportation. Only critiques I'd have is to add wifi and a better website.

we booked late as we didn't know exactly when we would be travelling so we were forced into getting a seat in the club car. Now this is a weird experience. It's like on a plane but bigger and better seats. You get food and alcohol for free in the price. Why is beyond me. We were only going Malaga to Madrid, so not a huge trip at 275 kmh. Suppose they had to do something to justify the price, so unless like us it's the only ticket left, don't waste your money. Don't get me wrong it was really nice, but unnecessary. Always liked the fast trains so I rate them highly, absolutely nothing wrong with the trip. Booking, well that can be another matter, but, trains themselves, spot on.

My 13 year old son and me traveled from Madrid to Barcelona. After waiting in a long line to board the train we finally got the access to the platform. The boarding and the train was delayed so everybody was in hurry. After finding our car number 6 we seat and prepared for the ride. But it comes out that we are occupying the wrong seats. Actually it was the car number 16 as it was seen inside the car. And the outside indication of the car number 6 was wrong. Ok, we started to look for the car num 6. Unfortunately, there was no car num 6 in this train. Only cars 11 to 19. Sorry.  And there is no one to help or to ask the question. After a while, renfe's employee started to hand out the earphones and asked him. He explained that there is actually two trains connected one to another. One of them, has cars numbers 11-19 and the second one has 1-10. But there is no passage between them inside the train. We should exit on the next stop and run (with our luggage) to the another train. We better do it fast because the stop is no more than 2 minutes. Finnally, we decided to continue our ride on the coach in the inter-car space,  not taking the risk. Thanks at least that train got to Barcelona. The train was late for 40 minutes after all

We took overnight trains, fast trains, lots of trains during our Spain adventure. It was great.  Sometimes the trains had buskers. Some bad, some fair, some good, some great.  But they disturbed the monotony and added artistic joy  to our journeys

Where to begin?  We used the Renfre Train Service many times during our 13 days in Spain.  First from Madrid to Jerez, where we initially stayed.  Then Jerez to Sevilla for a day trip.  Also, Cadiz to Jerez. Then finally back to Madrid, where we used more local lines out of Fuenlabrada, first having to go to Atocha then switch lines to Plaza del Sol.  We also took a trip to San Lorenzo de El Escorial, which was an hour long.  That was the worst because on the way home (the bathroom was broken or Out of Service on the train and there was no place to go!).  TERRIBLE JOB to put a train in service for a long trek with out of order facilities!!!   Also horrible, are the ticket machines.  The Renfre ticket dispensers ARE THE ONLY service in all of Spain that denied mine, and another family member's Global Credit Card by two different banks!  Those cards worked EVERYWHERE else in Spain but at the Renfre Machines, meaning we had to scramble Euros together to get back.  UNLESS, there was a ticket operator available, and then the Cards went right through.  BUT, due to BAD CUSTOMER PHYSICAL SERVICE, many stations don't have anyone there or even willing to help if you can find them.   I can't believe that I am touting how great the Boston and NYC train service is when compared to these folks?  We also had a conductor on a train strip all our rides from our purchased tickets that we received from an agent at a station, when he told us it was a mistake and we were out of zone.  So, he made up the difference for the 11 of us (we all bought tickets), and drained our multi-tickets on the train because he said we didn't pay.  Meanwhile, security (they are on every train, and that's a good thing) watched in case they had to throw us off.  Unbelievable how this service operates!?!  Buses seem to be better in the Madrid area.  And, walking is always an option.  We had some successful rides, but we also had our problems with a faulty system.  This service really needs review and revamping by officials.  By the way, the issues were not related to language, as we had several fluent speakers in our group, including someone born in Madrid.
They are new trains but very slow, they cannot take 5 hours for 475km and if you take the promo fare you are 1 hour late to get a bonus

We got a day return from Algeciras to Ronda on the train. It takes about the same time as the drive and it is a lot prettier and more relaxing. The trains we took have us about 4 hours in Ronda which is about right to see the town and have lunch. The train service to and from is great. The cars are clean, spacious and light with panoramic views of the wonderful countryside. All together a great day out and very relaxing
Their commitment to punctuality gets worse, more and more delays, more expensive, worse service... Year after year it gets worse and worse.

Great and cheap. On time and well worth it even with luggage and family. From Malaga airport you do have to go outside but you're on the same level as the ticket office. Only €1.80 adult single to torremolinos. See the website for all zone info for C1 train and others.

The truth is that it is a great trip to travel on the bird, I usually use it regularly to go from Malaga to Madrid and I have to say that the trip is very calm, comfortable and the trains are very punctual. The downside is that trips are expensive unless you find promotions and it usually works out cheaper. Without a doubt the best way to travel. For me it is more comfortable than the plane.  That's why I always recommend using the bird.
This is an excellent and affordable means of traveling! Great service and clean. Friendly staff and even wifi!

With Renfe you travel well from Algeciras to Madrid and vice versa, the station lacks a cafeteria and newspapers since it was renovated, a shame because they did exist before. The waiting time becomes boring in the meantime. Wishing that the Ave arrives here and the journey takes less and less time.
Third World Station. It doesn't even have a measly bar. Disgusting bathrooms. Two trips to Madrid a day. One in the morning and another at noon. Talgo train type. Super slow trip to Antequera.

We returned to Madrid from Algeciras, the truth is that the tickets are somewhat expensive but it has good comfort and views that are worth it. You have cafeteria toilets. Everything is very good, the truth is we will repeat it. Greetings.

Last weekend a group of friends traveled to Malaga. The bus was 55 minutes late and they refunded the full amount of the ticket. It's wonderful to travel like this and know that no matter what happens, they take responsibility.

It is clear that if you want to have something to drink when you travel by train, you only have the cafeteria, but they have outrageous prices. It's embarrassing that for a bottle of Coca-Cola that costs 58 cents they charge you 2.5 euros, but it's like lentils: take it or leave it.

This has to be the worst service I've ever experienced while travelling. We lost our stop in Valdepeñas because the door closed to early. I found some staff and was met with lies from them saying "tranquilo" and that we'll get another train to go back to our stop.That did not happen however. The rude old man at the stop in Manzanares just laughed at us and offered no compensation or help.I can also add that the trains are old, dirty and have unsafe luggage storage.

The ticket clearly states that the doors will be open for 2 minutes during stops but only held open for half a minute causing us to lose our stop. The representative from the business at the next stop assumed no responsibility and suggested we take a bus without offering any form of compensation. If this is representative of the transportation system in Spain, stay away.
I've been trying to see my ticket and have exhausted all sources; website, email, app, smoke-signals. Absolutely frustrating in every way.
Very good food. In general, all the services are quite well cared for, but it would need some reform. Close to the beach, although it is made of stone and quite bad

We traveled from Granada to Barcelona, ​​the first section we went by bus to the Santa Ana Antequera station and from there we took the AVE to Barcelona. In tourist class you travel comfortably and the trip is very pleasant. You can go to the car that is the dining room and buy something to drink and eat. Very good option for traveling between cities.

At the RENFE station in A Coruña, trying to make a claim, they sent me from one place to another until I ended up at the advance sales window, which was out of service at seven in the afternoon. I couldn't file the claim. At the station there is no information posted anywhere visible on how to file complaints. I suppose it is the company's policy: to make the user dizzy in such a way that in the end they manage, out of boredom, to reduce the number of them. Next time we will have to call 092 and have them record that the company refuses to provide a complaints book.

Positive experience, the tourist trip was good and comfortable. But the cafeteria is expensive, 3 breakfasts €20. We moved back 4 hours early but there was no place in tourist (there would have been no cost in tourist) and we took priority. Although it cost us €50 extra p. Person it was a pleasant experience from the VIP room on the platform with free drinks and snacks, air conditioning, plugs to charge mobile phones. On the train, wider seats, better air conditioning, better movie. Newspapers. Hot towels before lunch and a lemon towel afterwards. Coffee and drink. Attentive and pleasant staff. A good experience.

We traveled on the train from Barcelona to Madrid. It was a beautiful experience, the landscapes are incredible and the attention of the staff was wonderful. We were stopping at a hotel 3 blocks from Plaza Cataluña and we arrived at Sants station in 10 minutes (by taxi which cost us 8 euros at 6 am - without traffic -). We arrived an hour before the train departure, but they only let us enter the platform 15 minutes before (that is, it is not necessary to go much earlier). We traveled in preferential class for a few euros difference and they gave us a great breakfast and the seats are very comfortable. I recommend it!

First train trip in Spain.  A lesson for younger players.We went to the station to buy a ticket to travel from Madrid to Córdoba ( at Toledo ) Plenty of advanced warning. We asked for the cheapest ticket in the afternoon of the preferred future day of travel. A particular train not required. Our ticket was the most expensive in the history of world travel ( it cost Christopher Columbus less in relative terms to take his fleet to the Americas ). We challenged the chap who seemed to speak and understand English well - he seemed to check other options but no, that was as cheap as it comes. We resigned ourselves to use said tickets  ( it said carriage 12 so we figured it was at the back ) only to find that they were the most expensive seats on the train and were at the front - we checked and there were plenty of spare seats further back.On arrival at Córdoba we asked the 'customer service man ' to assist us. When asked ( in Spanish) if he spoke English he just shrugged his shoulders - I tried to explain my issue in broken Spanish and English - he feigned ignorance - I asked to speak to his supervisor - he too decide he couldn't understand English - we left and found the complaints office ( the then 6 or so staff and supervisor who had gathered to bid us Bon voyage were discussing something in great earnest - obviously trying as best they could to comprehend my English - perhaps next time they can contact the chap in Toledo who sold us the tickets and he can assist their comprehension. I'm sure if I had told them I would like nothing more than to see them roasted on a slow turning spit like at the Spanish Inquisition they would have understood very well to the point of outrage.The complaints person smiled at least once - I understand my Spanish isn't great but she at least was prepared to acknowledge she understood English... After an extended struggle trying to understand my Spanish. It turns out her English was really quite good and I complemented her for same.She gave me a form to fill in. Call me stupid but in customer service land given it was going to be read by someone in Renfe ( or not ) who wouldn't understand English ( as clearly no-one seems to ) I should have thought she may have translated my words into Spanish - but perhaps she recognised my literary talent and didnt feel capable of doing by words justice. She assured me that 'they' would write to me at my Australian address in due course - I felt that my issue had been listened to and acted on. I will frame that letter if it ever arrives in acknowledgement of Renfe customer service.As for the train - great trip, on time and very efficient - pity the humans in the organisation aren't like the trains.

Purchased the tickets about 45 days in advance online from the U.S., using my credit card and had no problems. Had decided to use the train, given the hour plus wait on both ends of an airport trip. BobbiTraveled Salamanca to Madrid, and Madrid to Barcelona. Check in was simple, we stored our luggage in the back and had a comfortable, uneventful trip. I would use them again.

We had a car from the beginning of the last century last. With such a sudden movement that we got dizzy a metal door that opened (I don't know what it was) but the conductor closed it every moment. Generally the Algeciras/Madrid trip is five hours with an obsolete train. But better than BUS. We have no choice but to continue holding on. Because RENFE has no regard for these customers to make the trip more enjoyable. Comment positive cafeteria good Israel breakfast or snak Clean toilets👍

I'm a Spanish speaker but I would like to write this review in English so everybody can understand. If you need to take the train obligatorily take it but, if there's other way for you to take another mean of transport, don't hesitate  to do so as the service is anything but good. Firstly, renfe consists of a monopoly. There's no other train company here in Spain operating which I think it's the main problem for its lack of competence and professionalism. Secondly, not only the staff is not friendly at all but they are also not good at problem solving. I cannot understand how people who work facing the public can be so rude and so little empathetic as these people can be. Finally, and this is my last and only recommendation as a person who has frequently taken the train, avoid using one of the renfe's trains. There are other affordable options such as blablacars and buses which can offer you the same thing for a more affordable price and a more friendly service.

Arrived early to Madrid Atocha station to in order to upgrade ticket from economy to first class ie pay RENFE more money. Rude staff who pretended no English; bounced from "Customer Service" to "Tickets"; then from one queue to another. Watched the cousins from the USA get a similar run around trying to validate their Eurail passes. Only the onboard experience recovered the travel experience - train clean, fast, on time and staff pleasant. Gave up on first class ....

The Alicante Valencia journey, of just 160 km, takes almost 2 hours....then from Valencia to Barcelona 3 more hours....honestly it is a very slow journey....it is not competitive, the plane is preferable

I had planned my travel itinerary across Spain several months before my trip and key to my travel plans was use of the Renfe high speed trains.  We had traveled using Renfe from Barcelona to Madrid, Madrid to Toledo and back, Madrid to Granada (including a free bus transfer/ride as Granada's tracks are under renovation), Sevilla to Cordoba and Cordoba to Madrid.Please note that your train tickets might not be available to purchase until 50-60 days before your travel date so you might have to keep checking if you've made your travel plans early like we did.  (It was a bit nerve wracking for me because I had all of my hotels, plane tickets, tickets to various attractions months ahead of time but no train tickets connecting between until they became available).  Their website was also seemingly undergoing renovation and updating because I had to use google translate while trying to get tickets in some parts as the English portion was not always ready.  Also, like some of the other traveler's have mentioned there are problems at times trying to process the transactions with my American Express but had no problems once I switched to my Visa.  I'm enrolled in the Verified by Visa program so it required opening up another page and verifying with them during the transaction but otherwise I had no issues with buying tickets.Thankfully any annoyances with Renfe was during my planning stage but after buying my tickets, printing them out and taking them with me on my trip everything else with Renfe was very enjoyable.  The tickets I bought were Turista class and had assigned seating so I simply arrived 25 minutes before my train, went through security and sat down comfortably on my way.NOTE: FREE AIRPORT TRANSFER.  If you happen to be leaving from Madrid you can use your printed ticket to get on the train for free to the airport.  You simply go to the machine (look for a complimentary/combination option to the airport) and you simply scan the QR code on your ticket and you get a free pass to ride the train to the airport.  We did so and it took about 25 minutes to the airport saving us the $30 taxi ride.

Booked my ticket online the day before travelling (book earlier so save more money) - and got terrified when I realised they only accepted paper tickets. In 2017 I would really assume a reference number or a code on your cell phone would be enough. Make sure you show up at least 20 minutes before due to luggage and ticket scanning.

We boarded at Toledo for Madrid, it was fully booked however just after leaving the station we noticed it was getting very hot. Understandably considering it was 40oC outside. However the heat quickly became unbearable as these trains have no ventilation and rely on airconditioning 100%. We looked up at the temperature display which read 46oC and was switched off withing seconds, now reading 0oC. Several passengers feom all carriages started passing and looking for a conductor with no one to be found. Finally got to Madrid and everyone piled off the train, went to the driver's cabin and he too was not visible. A train in this condition should not have taken passengers. On compliant at the service desk we where told to hi on the cue of around 40 and fill out a form. What a joke, be warned.
We traveled in first class from Madrid to Algeciras. The comfort offered on the train was very good. The train moved quickly and the landscape passing by is worth seeing.

Seeing some of the other reviews about purchasing tickets ..... my wife had no problem purchasing multiple tickets from RENFE on their website, using her American credit card, from her computer in Panama. We did have to wait on their email in order to download/print the tickets, but that was no problem.  The boarding process itself is easy and the comfort of the train ride was great.  The trains are clean, safe and offer an affordable way to get around.

I must say travelling on my own from malaga to airport I was a little apprehensive as I don't speak much Spanish. However the desk staff were helpful and the trains efficient and quick. Felt safe. Trains were clean. Easy and affordable travel. Definitely do again on my own.

The purpose of this review is to make people aware of the perils and pitfalls of trying to buy Renfe tickets. Basically their web site flat does not work to buy tickets with an American credit card and by PayPal unless you have cell service in the location where you are trying to buy a ticket. And forget buying a ticket in a train station in a major city, you can be in line for literally hours. Our experience - we waited to buy train tickets until we were in Spain. Everything worked fine on the website until we were ready to purchase. When we tried to purchase via credit card we got an error message over and over. When we tried to purchase via PayPal they now have 2 factor identification but the only option is to have a text sent to a mobile phone. While we have an iPhone we do not bother buying a European SIM card, rather we just use the ubiquitous wi-fi and messaging. The people at our hotel reception told us that they tell all tourists to go to the station to buy tickets, because the problems with the Renfe web site are well known. So we tried. They do not sell advance tickets on Sundays for a starter. Weekdays, the windows only open at 10 am. When we strode into the station around 11:30 we took a number - 299. They were up to 81. In 30 minutes they got up to 119. So we left.Eventually we were tipped to a solution. The big department store, El Corte Ingles, has travel agents in many of their stores, at least in Barcelona and Madrid. They were able to sell us tickets in about 15 minutes and charged us all of 4 euros.

It is terribly frustrating to try to book a train ticket with Renfe's website. Alvia's trips simply don't show up on the website. Their website hasn't worked properly since I can remember. It's amazing how problems linger in this company. I am from Spain I can only imagine how confusing and difficult would be for tourists to deal with this broken system.
Contrary to what they had told me, that is, they gave a good breakfast, they charged me €4.20 for a water and an instant coffee!! It doesn't seem right to me!

When we stay in Spain, we often bridge the distance between 2 cities by train. This year we traveled from Algeciras to Ronda (Madrid Atocha terminal station) with the Altaria to enjoy the beautiful landscape in a relaxed way. The passengers and their luggage were checked well in advance and everyone could take their pre-designated place. In the station building, in addition to the ticket offices, there is a cafeteria and a vending machine with snacks.

We used this transportation in Malaga, we used the regional one several times to different destinations, no problem getting your tickets either at a booth station or machine. There was always someone to help us out .the trains are clean, reasonably priced and very punctual.

Used the service to get from the Airport to Torromolinos, was abit nervous at first but it so quick, 10 minutes to resort, then used it to go up and down the coast from Malaga to Fuengirola. The Station is at the airport just a 2 minute walk out of the Airport Terminal. Cheap, reliable and clean.

Good transport. I got the wrong ticket though. I ended up getting the day rider I used when I was in Barcelona. I was heading towards tarragona. I had to pay the inspector the right ticket on the train. However, it has been a nice trip. Very similar to the national rail services we have in the UK

This is the best way to get about along this coastline. The trains arrive when they should. They are clean & efficient. There is a station inside Malaga airport so we used it to get to our hotel in La Carihuela and we arrived within ten minutes and it was only 3 euros for us both. Better than any transfer or taxi.I would highly recommend using the trains wherever possible. They could teach the UK a thing or two

Malaga Maria Zambrano Station is the 1st stop after taking the RENFE suburban line from Malaga Airport for 8 minutes. Tickets can be easily purchased from a vending machine at the airport (I think they cost about 1.5 euros). The station building also houses a supermarket and a hotel. There is a bus terminal right next door, and buses to various places arrive and depart. Easy access and convenient.

I am sorry to say that we did not catch our train from Madrid to Valencia Saturday the 8. April 2017 because of delays with the Iberia flight from Copenhagen to Madrid. We drove around in the airport with the flight for 30 minutes after landing.In the airport we called the Renfe office 5 times to change our tickets to a later departure. This was 30 minutes before the train was supposed to leave from Atoche.  This was in good time according to Renfes regulation on cancellation as printed on their web-site.The staff at the office hung up, even when we had a Spanish woman from the tourist office in the airport to call them.At the Renfe office in the airport they could not change the tickets and told us to do that in Atoche. We still had more than 40 minutes to do that according to Renfe regulation, they told us not to worry . The train from the airport to Atoche was delayed and stopped with out any notice 2 stations before Atoche and went out of service. Nobody gave us any information. The passengers slowly began to leave the train not understanding what was going on. We did the same and found another train to Atoche with more stops of course (line C7).At Atoche station we found the Renfe customer service office and stood and waited for about 30 minutes. They could not change the tickets but referred us both to your office and to another Renfe office in the station.We found the other Renfe office but the said they could not help us since nobody could speak English and the time was now 20.40. So we bought new tickets to Valencia for 124.20 euros with the Ave train at 21.10.I bought the original tickets as flexible in the case there would be some kind of delay. But actually nobody in Renfe where prepared to change the tickets even when we phoned them from the airport or stood in line at the offices in Atoche.The phon e numbers to Renfe that we used was+34 902 320 320 and +34 902 109 420 as stated on their web-site.I think it would be fair if Renfe reimbursed our tickets from Madrid to Valencia since Renfe did not provide us for what we paid for.Arriving home we filled out Renfe complaint form and asked for at refund. As documentation Renfe asked for copy of our used and not used tickets, witch we provided.The answer we recived is the following:"It is important that unused tickets are NOT REFUNDABLE. You bought train tickets through a Virtual travel Agency and as commercial rules; changes or cancelations are only possible through the same point of sale. Only the Virtual travel agency can change or cancel that train tickets.To this respect, it is necessary to point out that the refund of the not used tickets is not allowed if its have not been changed or cancelled previously to the departure of the origin train, in this case only through the travel agency.If customers, in Spain, want to change or cancel a ticket bought at a Virtual Agency, they can do it, only, contacting to Travel agency, and only that way can you cancel or change tickets. For these reasons, we inform you that we can not accept your request refund."I don't have the energy or time to check whether this answer is in accordance with Spanish regulation. So let this just be a warning to travellers with a need for costumer service from Renfe: forget it!

I used Renfe for the trip from Málaga to Seville. I ordered the train ticket through the GoEuro app. The return ticket cost around 1000 CZK. It's not exactly the cheapest, but the train journey was comfortable. Everything was fine

Fortunately, when we arrived, the underground train had already reopened.  the indications, the information offices, the machines to purchase tickets, all at the service of tourists. For only 2.50 Eu and in half an hour without any difficulty you can get from Barajas to Atocha in the heart of the center. In our case 2, 3 blocks from our hotel. Fantastic. The carriages are clean, silent, and with audible information about the name of the stations. More than recommended. As in the great capitals of the world. In Istanbul it is identical.  without a doubt to use it again and again. Unfortunately we didn't have time to do it on the bird.
Amazing  scenic journey from Ronda to Algeciras, train modern , on time , no refreshments on train , but buffet bar at Ronda
A trip from Malaga to Torremolinos at €2.05 is not expensive and it’s every half hour. It's better than the bus.
I have travelled by train substantially in Spain. The trains are punctual, efficient and spotlessly clean.The staff by and large speak good English and are helpful and friendly.

I have used it a couple of times and it is truly a very good experience. One time we used the seats and another time we were in the bar area. I think they would have to find another option, to go in the bar area, which is standing, and by not using a seat, it would be more economical. The criticism I make is the theft in the cost of car parking.

First of all the pluses. Renfe is clean and comfortable in Spain. The big plus is the scenery ! There are some spectacular sites to be enjoyed from the comfort of the train.BUT......the big drawback for me is tge cost ! I recently had to go to Alicante from Gibraltar. The cost by bus was €55 and the train......€244 !!!!! The bus took 9 hours but was comfortable, had washroom and wifi. The train made complicated ststion changes.Your choice......mine was easy.

Traveling from Algeciras to Madrid, the restaurant in Algeciras station has been closed for some time so we thought we could have breakfast on the train but there is no food, drink not even a bottle of water for the 5hr 4in journey. Very poor!
Comfortable/On time/the best way to relax an see Spain Honestly.We have traveled Spain to various locations and really enjoyed it.
A small station, near the port and in front of the bus station. There is a bar, parking.

Frankly, since the AVE has been spreading throughout the Spanish geography, I like going by train more and more every day.  It is a comfortable and fast means of transportation.  I still remember that donkey train to Seville and how in 1992 the trip passed in the blink of an eye.  Frankly, it has allowed the possibility of taking previously unthinkable day trips (unless you paid a million dollars by plane) and expanding the sightseeing options.  It is also true that the opposite process is being experienced since very long distances are achieved and, on the other hand, smaller distances are farther away because it is more tedious to go to them in the same time or longer than the new options.

Renfe is the best train service to travel through Spain. All the units are very good and clean and the AVE is really spectacular, very comfortable. I have traveled several times and the preference service is very good!!!!

It's easy to get around and the in-flight meals are very good. If you can use first class at a low price during a promotion when making a reservation, you can travel conveniently in a spacious and comfortable space and seat.

We need much better service, we have a laugh track, it takes us a while here in Cadiz until we get to Seville or Malaga. It's a shame that they don't worry about putting it in good condition. If it were like that, surely more ordinary people would take it.

I bought a 3 day Spain Renfe pass, tourist class. I traveled from Madrid to Algeciras on the first day and from Algeciras to Barcelona on day 2 and from Barcelona back to Madrid on day 3. The 3 days of travel in one month met my needs for this trip. I traveled from Madrid to Toledo but it was only 10 Euros each way, which was cheaper than buying a 5 day pass. I don't believe they offer a 4 day. But in any case, a full day is more than 20 euros. I did regret not spending the extra bucks for first class. The car I was in from Algeciras was filled with families and was quite noisy. I had planned to rest on the train but this was not to be.I arrrived in Barcelona at 830pm and had to take a taxi to my hotel, which was within walking distance, but I didn't want to walk after dark. The taxi ripped me off and charged me 25euros. I didn't realize til the next day how close the train station was. When I left Barcelona I took a taxi to train station for 6 euros. I still had a good time and tried not to focus on negative stuff.

The public transport is absolutely Fantastic in Spain it is a well drooled operation and runs to the minute we have yet been late leaving either by train or bus . The fairs are very reasonable indeed compared to the U.K. . Inside the station is a shopping complex and places to get that quick coffee fix and cossiont . There are ample taxis waiting outside to whisk you to your destination.

RENFE helped us getting from Ronda to Malaga, a very nice journey. Also a good option for the airport. We experienced the trains to be punctual, reliable and service friendly. Easy to get tickets and so on.
Renfre is the train provider of Spain. The website is somewhat challenging- but the trains are decent and comfortable.

Travel with Eurail pass for 3 days through Spain in 1st class. AVE trains Barcelona to Madrid, Madrid-Toledo. Segovia-Madrid, Madrid Alicante. Euromed Valencia Barcelona. Very good service (food and staff attention) and very punctual. They refunded us the value of the reservation for the Segovia-Madrid trip due to the train delay and we made it on time to take the train before the scheduled one.

Good longer-distance service on the few occasions used and the local service was very good and inexpensive. Bags scanned. Sale of tickets in advance is a plus although on-line it was found to be difficult. Trains were punctual,fast and clean.

Travelling from Barca to Madrid for football and check all types of travel (hire car, bus, plane and train). The train is the best in all waysWatched Barca game and two days later took train to Madrid. Could not buy tickets online for Madrid so needed to be there early. Train departs just after 6 and takes just over 3 hours. No delays, service on train good and seats comfortableTop speed was 300km per hour but felt safe and comfortable

We journeyed from Ronda to Algeciras by train & enjoyed the scenery & villages/towns it passes as it goes from mountains to coast.  Later we journeyed some way up the line from Algeciras & did a station to station walk which was most enjoyable.
Very comfortable, clean, punctual and efficient means of transport. Thank you Renfe for excellent service and guidance.

Hello, I often travel Madrid-Algeciras and vice versa and the combination there is is very very poor, we only have two trains, one in the morning and one at noon, they are always full, I do not understand why the offer does not increase, and that the price of the ticket is even more expensive than the Ave Malaga-Madrid (which takes two and a half hours) when half of the journey is made by conventional route and the rest by fast track (it takes 5 and a half hours to arrive) it makes sense to someone that it has more or less the amount equal to or greater than the AVE?  To me, of course, NOOOO. It would be fair if the amount were lowered and the offer increased.

The train we have in the 21st century is regrettable; The Algeciras-Bobadilla railway line was inaugurated in 1890 and, apart from some repairs, we are still the same. Being the southern border of Europe, we do not have a good connection with anywhere and the Port of Algeciras is one of the best...More than 5 hours Algeciras/Madrid - and two trains a day. The transfer in Antequera is like a movie!

ok so due to it being xmas week and having a made late booking to Spain from Perth couldn't get flight from Madrid to Alicante so decided train was the next best thing ,BEST DECISION MADE , got taxi from airport to station 30 euros and 20 mins trip , got to Madrid with 25 mins spare to catch train ( you do need that amount of time ) purchase ticket it is well worth the extra 20 euros to book 1st class , the seats were great , leather , only 2 wide on one side and single on other and full size table we were served lunch including wine, great staff that once they realized we only spoke English spoke to us in English all the time , we had a relaxed comfortable 2.5 hour trip to Alicante arriving fairly refreshed. Return journey was a bit different arrived at Alicante to get the 12.40 train and it was full !!!!! so had to wait till 2.40 for next fast train , paid again for first class , on boarding the seats were defiantly closer together  and narrower more like plane seats , fabric not leather , and a pull down tray like a plane , good leg room though (unlike a plane !!) also no food on this trip only orange juice and a biscuit , same cost though (80 euro ) it also was a longer trip with about 5 stops but still arrived in Madrid by 5.30, then10 min taxi ride ( 10 euro ) to Madrid center and hotel for the night before trip back to Perth. defiantly better then flying but make sure you get the fast train when booking , and also as previous reviews tried to book on line it was useless as couldn't get page to translate .
There aren't family discounts and children pay almost like an adult. The toilets in the weren't very clean. The only good thing was that we could arrive from Malaga to Cordoba in 1 hour.

I had a Malaga-Madrid ticket which I have tried to change or cancel and it has been impossible due to the disastrous website they have.  In the end I didn't even change the ticket and I lost the money. More than an hour trying to solve it both online and by phone and in the end nothing. Both online service and customer service are disastrous services.

Our route was from Madrid Malaga!! Everything was great!! Above all, punctuality! The train leaves at the correct time!! Not a minute late!  The seats are very good and quite spacious!! I wouldn't change anything!! Very happy in general with everything!! Excellent price quality!!!

Trip Barcelona-Seville round trip by AVE, everything good, price, comfort and time, with the exception of the toilets that are clean when you enter and halfway through the journey they are dirty and no one cleans them throughout the journey

Many years ago my father, mother and I drove from Madrid to Malaga - it took us two days!Our trip from Madrid to Malaga took 2 hours and 40 minutes!We had spent two nights in Madrid arriving from Miami and our train left from Atocha Station which is easy to navigate our ay through to the platforms for the AVE. But do bear in mind that you and your suitcases have to go through a security check and there can be longish lines so allow a bit of time before the trip to get through security. We had decided to buy 1st class tickets as they were cheaper at the time of the year we were traveling - October. We departed on time and the cabin staff were very attentive. Lunch was served including cocktails and wine and was delicious.The countryside literally 'flew' by as we traveled at over 300 kilometers per hour yet one wouldn't have known as the ride was very smoothWe arrived a little early in to Malaga. Congratulations on a great journey and excellent service from the on-board staff. Thank you!
Algeciras railway station, a hub in southern Europe with good connections to the rest of Spain.

It is sad that a population like that of Gibraltar and Ceuta has these trains in the 21st century. Slow, with very few schedules to choose from. The train route to Antequera dates back to the 19th century, and it is not an exaggeration, it is real. Very few reforms have been made. After Antequera it already uses a more modern route and goes faster. It is noisy and the rattling continues in the first section. High bar prices. A disaster. It seems incredible how little interest all administrations and all parties have in connecting this area with the rest of Spain since it is not just with Madrid.

I travel several times a month to go from Marseille to Perpignan in France (train which goes to Madrid). It's really the best. The SNCF has everything to learn from the staff who are very, very warm, welcoming, smiling and helpful. Now I only travel with them.

Good experience. In 2h45 you are from the center of one city to the center of another. Very punctual. I recommend the silent car if you want to go quietly without noise. It would be very useful if the train's WIFI worked, because there were wifi advertisements but it never worked.

We booked our train tickets through RailEurope and payed a service fee of $7.95 but got a fabulous price on the tickets because we booked early.If you can, book first class which we did from Madrid to Barcelona.  The day that we traveled, we got a delicious pasta dish, salad and cake. They also give you plenty to drink.The train car that we were in was very quiet and the ride even though high speed at over 180 miles per hour was very smooth.Luggage was not a problem.  Upon entering the train there is a huge rack to put your luggage plus additional space above the seats.The seating is singles on one side and doubles on the other.  They are very spacious and comfortable with trays if you need them.Wonderful way to travel!

The Renfe high speed train system is as good as any of the European trains. They travel at 300 kph (180 mph) so it is much faster than driving. Pay the extra for first class; seating is two seats on one side and one on the other with lots of space, electrical outlets and a big table. The service is good and most of the staff speaks. English. I took the train from Barcelona and back and was very pleased. The only negative is that the train leaves Barcelona from the Sants station, which is 15 minutes [and 25 EUR) from the airport. You can buy tickets in advanced on-line, but you have to select a departure. You can also buy at the station. I did this on both legs and waited just a few minutes in line each time.
For the number of travelers who pass through Algeciras. They could put better trains. From Córdoba to Algeciras it seems endless.
On time, very comfortable way to travel around Spain.   The trains are modern, spacious and offer more than most airlines.   I highly recommend high speed train travel.

Very beautiful station, lots of light and good indications, many commercial premises, which you need something, you have almost everything, including a Mercadona. Let the people of Adif in Zaragoza learn that it is sad to have such facilities that are always empty.

We traveled from Madrid to Toledo return. Very clean trains. Very efficient. Both on time. Booked tickets by app GoEuro which was good although renfe insisted on printing the tickets at the Atocha station which was a little annoying. Good security. Great experience.
The trip was very good. Everything went as we planned. We traveled from Barcelona to Malaga (round trip to Barcelona) we traveled on the AVE, high-speed train. Everything is excellent
I travelled SPECIAL ASSISTANCE from Malaga to Madrid. Lots of legroom. Better than the plane. Courteous staff. If over 65, for E6 you can buy a Carta Dorada. Just show your passport.

If your in a wheelchair or cannot use steps DO NOT and I mean DO NOT use this company. I travelled from Salou to Barcelona on the 21st of Sept after buying our tickets we where informed that there was no ramp to get on the train so we had to ask the help of other customers which one Scottish man help us,when we got to Barcelona station there was a lady that came with a ramp to help me off.I informed her that we where returning the next day and was told that the ramp would be there.on returning the next day we where informed that we needed to give the office 24 hours notice when I explained that I told the member of staff the day before it did not matter. We decide to board the train anyway with the help of other passengers I managed to get on the train on arriving at Salou station we had to depart the train on the middle platform so there fore we had to cross the train tracks there was a ramp at one side but when we got to the other side there was a 300mm step to get back up onto the platform.The attitude towards disabled people from Renfe is Disgracful.DO NOT use this company if you

Good luck purchasing Renfe AVE tickets on line.In March/April 2015 my husband and I travelled around Spain by train. Gave up buying Renfe AVE tickets online, so as we were staying in each city for 2-3 days I would purchase tickets for our next leg of the journey as soon as we got there. The ticket machines at the stations would not accept overseas credit cards but were handy for checking timetables (in english).Over 4 weeks we visited Madrid, Avila, Salamanca, Toledo, Seville, Cadiz, Gibraltar, Granada, Valencia, Barcelona and then back to Madrid.  All via train except Granada to Valencia by bus.  We would always take the AVE if possible (check online or via ticket machines for pricing).  We also visited during the Easter Semanta Santa but never had issues with purchasing tickets and all cities have the Hop on Hop off buses, so there was no need to hire a car at all.Hope the above helps you to plan your adventurous trip around Spain.Sybil.

Britain could learn a lot from Spain.  We always use public transport when on holiday and often take a train direct from the airport to where we are staying.  Renfe has this spot on.  From Barcelona to costa brava or Malaga to Costa del sol it is just so easy and cheap.  The train stations are within the airport grounds and generally take about half an hour to the coastal resorts.  Announcements on each train are in both Spanish and English with clear displays of each stop on TV screens in each carriage.  Timetables are always accurate and tickets so reasonably priced.  Even going further afield from your holiday resort if you fancy a trip inland is easy.  We have used Spanish trains to travel to Figueres from Barcelona to see the Dhali museum, Malaga to Granada and have always been amazed at the reasonable cost of tickets and excellent conditions on the trains including air condition which is a must when travelling in Spanish temperatures.  As my husband drives everyday for work it means he can fully enjoy his holiday without having to think about driving.  The website is reasonably easy to navigate and you can do any research before you fly.As I said at the beginning the UK should take a leaf out of Spain's book when it comes to travelling by train.
Yes, that's 140 km covered in 40-45 minutes. The trains were on-time and clean, no wifi though. Perfect for a day trip to Córdoba from Sevilla, or vice versa.

Bought 4 returning tickets for Barcelona - Madrid. 11 days before the trip I realised that i bought tickets in wrong direction. I sent email to customer service, but they did not respond with a single letter.Never again

I took the Renfe hi speed train from Barcelona to Madrid in a first class car.
