Ticket cost me 150 euro.The seat was comfortable and the car was pretty quiet and conducive to getting some work done (without wifi).Food they served was not good, but there was a food car if you wanted to buy something else.  Train left on the dot when it was supposed to.Would use again.
Nice clean station in the middle of nowhere... Was surprised to have purchased Eurail tickets only to stop here and get on a bus 1.1/4 to Granada... And the same thing  returning to go to Malaga

I took this from Madrid to Valencia, then Valencia to Barcelona.The food was great when I paid for a higher class (I'd gotten a deal online.)  No wifi is no helpful.  And I was early arriving so I asked if I could switch trains (it was quiet) and they were not having it.  Seemed odd to be so inflexible.

Renfe is a good train service, although my tickets were purchased through Iberia, meaning that I had 3 hours to get from the airport to station which is NOT enough time. Missed the train and got a fine.

Hello from Seville, but the thing is that the suburban area of ​​Seville is bad around the clock, why can't it be that during the day there is approximately every quarter of an hour there is one and around 10 there from 45 to 45 minutes there one that I think could be changed because it is bad for people who leave a later time I don't know if I'm talking to the Renfe operator in Seville but please pass it on to him
It was a very long way without any accommodation or else in the train. The crew was wierd and very disappointing. We'll never take this train again
The trains are clean and precise. The only flaw is the fairly high cost for short routes and in any case it takes almost an hour from Malga to Fuengirola for 40 km.

Renfe Cercanías are buses that, combined with the subway network, can take you to almost any place in Madrid and its surroundings. The service is efficient and the buses are good and in perfect condition. In my opinion, the information provided is somewhat confusing to know which train to take or which route is appropriate. Electronic signs and boards with clear information for tourists that coincide with what one sees in the app would be needed. of the telephone. In Spanish speaking it is confusing, I can't imagine other tourists. There is also no one to ask. Something to improve!!! I experienced this in Nuevos Ministerios and Atocha to travel to Alcalá. Good luck!!

We took the train from Madrid to Malaga. Both stations were very busy. The train itself although we thought we had first class  tickets there was no service and we had to go to the buffet to but drinks and the queue there was very long. There is no wifi on the trains and it was quite a long trip . On the way back we tried to change our train time but the staff at the station in Malaga were very unhelpful. We had leather seats on he way back that were a little more comfy but still no service except for a drinks trolley that went though but did charge for drinks.
It is a small station like any other station, the treatment is normal because I didn't have to deal with anyone either.

The trains are good, few trips and limited schedules but within reason, what is super sad is the gallery of the station, it is scary to arrive at dawn and stay there just waiting for your train to arrive, only one cafeteria that opens during the day...they should give that a little life.

The railways of Spain are distinguished by their great organization, speed and convenience. It is more convenient to purchase tickets for long-distance trains on the website renfe.com. Their prices gradually increase closer to the trip. We took the morning Euromed train. The duration of the trip is 5 hours. Price (in advance, but not from the moment of sale) is about 22 euros. Standard fast comfortable train. I walked exactly on schedule, arrived at the intermediate station (there was only one) 10 minutes ahead of time. They gave out free headphones, but they were very simple; we prefer to use the more expensive ones. The seats are comfortable. They “recline” by sliding the seat (and lower backrest) forward. There are tables. Luggage space. The bathrooms are in perfect condition. Due to the quality of the trains and rails, they travel quite quietly. As for the speed of 400 km/h, this is probably an exaggeration, but they travel more than 200 km/h.

I have made this trip before and before it was long, now it is less so. This time I wanted to send my niece who understands Spanish poorly with a minor escort service advertised by RENFE, and they did nothing but create obstacles. In defense of RENFE I will say that being the summer months I understand that it is complicated, but the Customer Service was still disastrous. We called twice to get information, and on both occasions they gave us different information. So we stood at the Chamartin station, and they informed us of other different conditions (e.g. that you only contract if you buy a ticket online), but they forgot to mention other important information. Of course it couldn't be done online, only for advance sales (and only with more than 48 hours in advance) and only for preferential tickets (for a child under 12!!). We return to Chamartin and it turns out that advance sales on the weekend can only be purchased in Atocha, so we are going to Atocha, on the other side of where we live. And there they inform us that you can only book this service if you make the entire journey to Algeciras!!! And if you want to get off in Ronda, can't you? Of course, no one had informed us about this until that moment!! To try to guarantee that they assist her at least in getting on the correct train and not getting lost, we spoke to Atendo, for adults, to see if they can help. They say they are overwhelmed but long distance Customer Service exceptionally gives authorizations to be able to accompany her to the train. As my daughter is doing, I understand that they would let both of us in to accompany her, but no! I have to leave my youngest daughter outside the ticket control while I take my niece to the train!! I understand that they are security measures, but it was only a 12-year-old girl, not a criminal who is going to sneak in!! I find the lack of flexibility and humanity impressive, as well as the lack of knowledge of the Customer Service, which does not know how to give a unified response about a service.

Trip from Madrid to Algeciras. so good in preferential than tourist. Before, RENFE offered food and drinks on a preferential basis. Today you don't pay the same as before and without being able to charge your cell phone in the seat. Very expensive cafeteria food. Friendly staff. Algeciras station very small but clean. Bus station 50 meters away. Paid parking next door. Place to eat around.

Superb! Upgraded to first class for approx 10 Euro each when booking online. You get very comfortable reclining seats with oceans of space and good quality food included served on trays like on airliners.  Drinks come with the food and further drinks are offered later, also included in the price.The train is modern and fast 300kmh at times so journey time only 1h45. Staff are friendly and spoke English.

We travelled between Madrid and Barcelona on an evening AVE high-speed service.  The train was clean and seating was of course pre-allocated, so it was easy to settle-in.  The journey was punctual and non-stop.  The train was indeed high speed, seeming to reach a peak of about 302 Km/ H (187 MPH), with it rarely dropping below 290 Km/ H.  The ride was very smooth, allowing some pleasant time to be spent in the buffet car, where drink and service was good.This is of course not the cheapest way to travel, but the speed and technology of this train system makes it worth spending more.  Although darkness was falling, the first hour allowed exceptionally magical views of the Spanish countryside at sunset.

Train left on time but arrived 10m late, very friendly attendants, very comfortable seats (and several of them free), air conditioning at the right point, cleanliness, arrived more than 10m early (which avoids stress and rushing to get on), sockets available, very large space to place luggage on the chairs (avoiding worry about theft) (on top of that they are beautiful glass with silver details). moving and making noise in one section). Note: I managed to get a very good promotion to go in the preferred class (their executive class) I paid cheaper than the tourist class! It's definitely worth checking when buying.

Before we purchased our tickets for AVE train from Madrid to Barcelona, I think I read pretty much all there was to read about how and when to do it, so I was prepared. There were numerous recommendations instructing people to buy 60 or 62 days prior to travel to get the best prices. I spent about 2 months watching the prices and exploring Renfe site before the time to buy our tickets came. There was a specific time we wanted to travel (10:30 a.m.). The long anticipated day (62 days prior to departure) came and the tickets went down by only about 10 Euros (from about 85 to 74.70). We did not buy in hope of them going down a little bit more (as I wanted to buy them for about 60-65 Euros). The next day (61 days out) the prices were the same, but my husband started warning me, that tickets for the same train for dates that were 2-3 days before our travel day went back to 84 and over 90 Euros, so it looked like the discounted rate was selling quickly. Next day, (60 days out), we just bit the bullet and bought the tickets for 74.70 and upgraded to Promo+, just in case we need to cancel, so we don't lose all the money. The upgrade was about 5 Euros--no big deal. In the end, we ended up paying 160.10 Euros for 2 Promo+ tickets. I checked back couple days later (58 days out) and found the same tickets for 66.15 Promo (or 71.50 for Promo+), so obviously, the best time to buy in our case was not 60 or 62 days prior to travel but 58 days! So, we paid about $20 more, which may not seem as a big deal, but considering the amount of time and effort I put into this, it was disappointing.We originally wanted to buy from Renfe site to get the best price, but we noticed that the site was not showing us what seats we would get, which we found quite annoying. We will have large suitcases and need to be close to the end of the car, so we can put them in the luggage area and be able to be close to our suitcases. Fortunately, we found French site Captaintrain.com that was in English, very easy to navigate, worked like a charm, and sold tickets for the same price as Renfe--no extra fees. You cannot select your seats if you buy Promo or Promo+ tickets, seats are assigned to you. However, at Captaintrain.com, they show you the seat numbers before you buy and if you google the right train, you can find the seating chart and see if you like the assigned seats.This is what I did--put 2 tickets in my cart and once it showed me the seat numbers, I went back and did the search again and added another 2 tickets to my cart without deleting the first ones. I was able to do this several times and after about 8-10 sets of tickets placed in my cart, I started getting errors. At that point, I went to my cart, selected the tickets that had the seats that were closest to what we wanted and deleted the rest. Then, I proceeded to payment and since we contacted our CC company (Chase) before this purchase, the purchase went through immediately without any issues. Then, I saved the tickets as pdf. files and also printed them.If you live in the USA, make sure you use a card with no foreign transaction fee as both, Captaintrain and Renfe will charge you in Euros. Also, if you play with the seat assignments, don't forget to delete the tickets you don't want before you check out. Good luck. I will post another review after our trip.

We left the car at San Roque - La Línea Station (several kilometers from both towns), where there was ample parking, to save driving into Algeciras. We traveled in comfortable, modern, air-conditioned trains to & from Ronda. Shortly after leaving San Roque there were lots of storks' nests on top of the electricity pylons.  The second half of the journey was the more spectacular, the line winding its way through mountains, often nowhere near a road.  Ronda, approached by rail on a zig-zag to gain height, was well worth the visit.
Hot and nice, good beer, last of places to see. Good bus service and the train from Malaga, super. I recommend it to everyone, a city to visit, very hot but there are bars everywhere.

It is clear that it is a calm and fast service. But the cost is excessive, they don't give even a single piece of water during the tour. I paid 115 Euros per person for the service which seemed extremely expensive to me. I traveled with my partner so the total expense was 230 euros.

Really comfortable seating, cost around 26 euro each for a 2 1/2 hour journey from Seville Santa Justa to Malaga central, train was on time, was very clean and all the necessary information was on board, I will certainly use it again, although it is only 15 mins quicker than the coach time, it went through some lovely area including the Kings Walk which is certainly worth a visit

The train from Barcelona to Madrid took us 2 hours and 40 minutes because we arrived early. Please note that they leave on the second and its a great way to travel. Convenient seats, a cafeteria cart on board and some snacks for sale on carts. Loved seeing the countryside and zoomfrom ng sometimes at 300km past everything. I will do this again.

Booking Renfe AVE train tickets for local trips around Spain is not as complicated as you think despite its webpage being in Spanish. I just followed the steps and tips in the Tripadvisor page (Buying Renfe Tickets Online - Revised Feb. 11, 2016). Booking was fast as i used the Tripadvisor trip as my guide but it took a while for my payment to get through though as Renfe's website seem to decline non-Spain issued credit cards. My Paypal account took seven failed attempts before my payment finally got through so be patient.Took a taxi from Gran Via to Madrid's Puerta de Atocha station which cost around €7 for a 10-minute journey. The gates of Renfe trains are located one floor down the station. You should arrive here an hour earlier than your travel time if you would like to grab a bite. You will also pass through a X-ray machine.There is a help desk if you like to ask for directions though they can only speak a little english. I just showed my ticket and asked for directions. Trains to Barcelona were said to be anywhere within 1 to 5. There are also various tv screens that list all train schedules and departure times. The gate number will only be flashed 15 minutes before your train departure so be alert. As soon as it flashes, people will start to quickly line up the gate entrance. You may or may not need to print out your tickets as long as you save the copy of your ticket on your mobile phone as long as their scanner can validate the QR code.Beware that if you have big luggages with you, you have to fall in line early to be able to place your luggages in your train coach's luggage storage area. Our coach can only accommodate a maximum of about 10 to 12 big luggages, see photo. Otherwise, you will have to store your luggage in other coaches. Hand carry luggages can be stored at the top shelf of your seats. Having booked a month in advance, i was able to get a discounted fare on the Turista Plus coach. This is the slightly upgraded Turista (Economy) seats with wider seats and leg room. Since I'm travelling with three other friends, i booked the Tarifa 4 Mesa seats so we could sit together and four of us could face each other. It is also cheaper and cost us €51.20 each compared to pricier tickets from other English websites selling Spain AVE train tickets. The cheapest fare I've seen at the time of booking was €30+ and the most expensive was €100+ roundtrip so do your research to get more value for money. Legroom and space was not bad despite having a table in the middle of our seats. You can get a bit dizzy though if your seat is facing the opposite site of the journey. You can transfer to other seats if the coach is not full.Our train travelled at 291kmh. Travel time from Madrid to Barcelona is around 2 hrs and 45 mins with several stops in between. Check your luggages from time to time to see if it's still safely stored as there were said to be incidents of stolen luggages. For our safety, we fastened our luggage handles with cable ties in between the rails. The train departed exactly on time and travel was relatively smooth. It was a good and comfortable way to travel. My only complain though was the smelly water closet. Overall, my Renfe experience was good, I'd recommend it to those planning a trip to Spain.
This station is luxurious, it lacks nothing boutique restaurants super markets newspapers ATMs parking everything brand new and very clean bravo.

Not sure if this is fraud, wondered if anyone else affected.Bought tickets for a RENFE Mid Distance train journey from Flaca Station near Girona, Spain, to Barcelona.Attempted to pay for them with a credit card but as transaction was being processed, the ticket office woman, who incidentally  was exceptionally surly, said the machine had crashed. She switched it off and on again, but it still didn't appear to be working, so I paid for the tickets with cash. On returning home and checking credit card, the transaction did in fact go through. I had assumed as the machine had been switched off, this was not possible. Am now raising this with RENFE and my bank but for anyone making a similar purchase at this station (Flaca), please be aware of our experience.

We booked the Preferente Class through Rail Europe for €108.87 each (€99.8 + 10%vat €9.07). It's slightly more expensive than if you were to book directly at Renfe website. However since it was not easy booking through Renfe website as it is always not working on the various browsers we used or most of the texts are in Spanish, we decided to go for Rail Europe website - at least we know what we are booking for. With Rail Europe, I was not able to select a Gran Clase though. The First Class mentioned in their website means Preferente Class.We were not given a choice of cabin to choose from but were booked automatically at Plaza 031 & 035 - don't be mislead by the number as both of these is a bunk bed in one private cabin. The space is small just like most night train. If one person is standing or walking, then the other person should sit on the bed.The room is clean and there is a washing basin. The water that flows out of the washing basin is much better than the Caledonian Sleeper  train I took in August 2015. At least we can brush our teeth and wash our face properly. There are other amenities like lighting, power socket and coat hanger. Bed and pillow are comfortable. The bed faces the window in the cabin - so you can see sunrise and beautiful scenery live from the comfort of your bed. There are bottled water and toiletries pack in the compartment  near the sink - it's all yours to keep so don't miss that as I don't remember seeing a signage about this item being here. It was the lovely service staff that told us about this.The train is well maintained and the shared toilet was clean. There are food services on board very close to the cabin but they are of course more expensive than what you normally pay for outside. My suggestion is buy something to eat / drink before you board the train if you want to save money. Service is excellent and the staff are friendly.Overall, we had a very pleasant journey and definitely recommend Renfe Night Train.

We traveled from Barcelona to Madrid in mid April - purchased three first class tickets in advance over the internet with no issues.  There were lots of trains, times, options to choose from.  Since we don't travel by train very much, we splurged for first class tickets - they were nice - seats large and roomy with Wi-Fi, food service and drinks included in ticket price plus reserved seats.  We were going to fly, but my son suggested the train because it is so near the city center.  The airport is quite a ways out, plus it requires going through security, etc - much easier just to take the train.  Glad we did.  Next time I would be tempted to go with a mid or economy ticket for comparison, but very happy with the overall experience.

We took the Ave 2212 train from Madrid to Seville - and what a delight it was.A two and a half hour smooth journey from Madrid's Atocha Renfe station to Seville, through beautiful if not spectacular Spanish countryside. We raced by towns and cities,  green fields and farms, castles in the distance, all spied through wide clean windows. Our carriage wasn't 1st class, but the second class ‘preferente aperitivo’ was more than comfortable - new, shiny and clean, with large glass windows, very confortable seats, wide tray to fit snacks and a laptop, or to play cards, audio in your seat, complimentary snack, wine, juice, served by very friendly bilingual staff. I couldn’t think of a better way to go from the Capital to one of Spain’s most beautiful cities.

Let me preface this review with the fact that try to resolve these issues with companies privately, and almost never give a negative review, because I know how important they are to the traveler. I know I use them constantly to help me decide how to travel/what to see/where to go. So I will do my best to avoid ranting unnecessarily and just provide details I would like to have known as a traveler. TL; DR version: Find a different way to travel through Spain. We had an extremely terrible experience with Renfe from the moment we bought our tickets. The ticket buying process was confusing. We bought Euro Rail passes for Spain for three days, and we bought two first class tickets because they weren't much more than the Coach tickets. It appeared to be the more economical option, since we were traveling to multiple cities. When I went to reserve our seats, however, I realized that in addition to the Euro Rail Pass, you have to pay to reserve a seat on a train as well. There were almost no options available without paying another $150+ dollars to reserve a seat (coach or preferred). This was almost three weeks ahead of time, and we only had options to travel before 10am from Sevilla to Madrid, and Madrid to Barcelona, both very popular routes with lots of options. If you're looking to travel the most affordable way, don't buy the Euro Rail Pass, it tricked us into paying more than we would have by buying the separate tickets. I purchased reservations for seats at the inconvenient times, and the next day got a phone call that not even those reservations were no longer available, so I had to choose different times. The times were still extremely limited, and it felt like a rip off to pay the money for first class tickets and have almost no options to choose from. Next, we actually got to the Sevilla >> Madrid train. Someone was sitting in our First Class, club seats, and he was not moving because we actually both had tickets for the same seats. The stewardess moved us up to the next train car where there were open seats. The supervisor then came and told us we would have to move again when we got to Cordoba because we were sitting in someone else's seats. I asked if he spoke English, because my Spanish is not excellent, and he just said no and continued to speak quickly in Spanish, making no attempt to help us or even find someone that spoke a little English (the stewardess I spoke with earlier did speak English). The seats he wanted to move us to were facing backwards in the direction of travel, which always makes me nauseous. I tried to explain this to him (and the new passengers in Cordoba), and he refused to listen and openly blamed the problem on us. The problem that started with our seats being double-booked in the first place! Also, the train car was extremely loud, with people talking constantly on their phones. We were not the only people in the train car bothered by this, but nobody did anything to try to help the situation, even after several people asked for help. Additionally, the train did not have WiFi. None of the trains we rode had WiFi.Now, we sit in Barcelona. We arrived a couple hours early, so I asked the ticket counter if we could exchange our tickets for an earlier train. Several were showing open seats. The first counter said they couldn't exchange it because it was paid for in US dollars, so I had to go downstairs. The counter downstairs said they couldn't exchange it so I had to go to the ticket office outside the station. The ticket office outside the station said they couldn't exchange it because it was purchased through a different company, and that I'd have to go to customer service. Customer service said it was impossible to exchange because it was purchased in US dollars. This was unbelievably frustrating to be dismissed at every ticket counter and told nothing helpful. They just said it was impossible to help me and didn't know how to help in any way. Now I sit in the "first class club room" in the Barcelona train station. There is no WiFi, the bathroom is out or order, and the service is extremely unhelpful and unfriendly. Our train gate opens up, so we go to check-in. Keep in mind, at this point we have already ridden from Seville to Madrid, on the same train service with the exact same tickets. We get to the ticket counter, and they say we cannot board without a special stamp from the ticket counter, which is outside of security. I tell them we already used the train without this stamp, so it's not actually required, since we got through security in Seville without it. The supervisor tells me I have to get it, and he will not come with me to help, and he will not hold the train as I run back to the ticket counter to get this stamp. So I run to the ticket counter, wait in line, get the stamp, and come back. He then proceeds to publicly (and loudly) walk me through what we did wrong, chastising us for not reading directions. Seemed unnecessary and spiteful for him to do that at that point, and left us feeling embarrassed and angry. I expected more based on how expensive these tickets are. We were hoping for a comfortable, enjoyable way to travel that would make this trip special. The entire trip was extremely stressful, and we felt ripped off. They take your money and do nothing to earn it.

The train station is a 10 minute walk from the port. There are trains running to places like Madrid and Malaga, but they don't run very often, so the area is empty except when trains arrive and depart. There is only a small shop, so you cannot buy food.

Despite 10+ page of instructions/warnings on another Trip Advisor blog site, I just booked 1-way tickets for 6 of us in about 15 minutes on the RENFE website. Could not have been easier. Contrary to what you read elsewhere, they DID take my Visa-bank texted me to make certain it was legitimate charge, then put it through. Got our seats all together, discounted rate, pdf print outs and we' re all set. Site was all in English (look for English prompt on top left) and super easy. Don't pay consolidators to book for you.

The Algeciras Renfe station is very well located, in front of the "COMES" bus station and also very close to the passenger port. It is a modern station with good facilities and very busy. It could be improved for the transport of Containers, so important for our great port of goods, but it seems that this is not of much interest to our politicians.
I find it incredible that the bird does not have Wi-Fi, since in the rest of Europe and even on Alsa buses you enjoy this completely free service.

Let's say it straight away, comfort is not the strong point of the trains which connect Algeciras to Granada. In exchange, we are surprised to find that they are much more punctual than in France, within 5 minutes. They are also much cheaper. At the start of 2016, when it was planned that the AVE (Spanish TGV) would go from Granada to Antequera, unfortunately we still have to make this journey by bus. That said, this Algeciras-Granada line is very pleasant and allows us to discover landscapes invisible by car.

It is almost impossible to purchase the train tickets using the website from USA. It does not accept Credit Card. You can spend whole day and still not get your reservation.There are other website such as LOCO2.COM.- Excellent way to purchase your ticket.ACPRail.COM - DO NOT USE THIS. It is a Ripoff. They charge me $60 extra.

We traveled Barcelona to Madrid. Return tickets are over 620 US. Ouch. Flights were half that price. In Canada we have no high speed rail, but we do offer wifi. Renfe has no wifi and charges 3 bucks for a can of coke. Love the train experience as we boarded with 10 mins to spare. Traveling at 300 kph is cool.
Lovely trip to Ronda from Algeciras.  The all stops train is worth doing as each station is interesting with proper station masters in uniforms!   Very clean all the way up to Ronda.

We rode the train from Madrid Puerta de Atocha to Seville. We bought our tickets using the machines at the station. My husband was using a corporate card & I had my own credit card, so we were on 2 different machines. I found the touch screen to be glitchy & not smooth. You are able to select English, so at least we understood the screens, but my machine had a ticket printing issue. Right after the ticket printed, the screen gave me an error message & said the transaction hadn't gone through (I never got the printed receipt), yet I had a ticket in hand that looked normal. There are no real people on this main level of the building (where security is), so we proceeded through security to the entrance to go down to the platform & my ticket wouldn't scan. NO ONE speaks English, so they were motioning that my ticket was no good, & pointing me back toward the machines. I couldn't even figure out how to get back out there (I eventually just went back out through the security area). This time I got flustered, as we were 15min out from the departure that my husband now had his ticket for, & I was doubting my credit pin code. That's another thing. If you're American, you will need your credit card pin# to use these machines. We never use the pins in the US, so I was doubting myself, & thought maybe that's why it didn't go through, although I should have known that it wasn't the pin, but rather the machine, since it didn't give me any message about it being a payment problem. I eventually got frustrated & went back through security to try to find a person to help. I went to 1 counter (only to find out that I needed to go to the bottom floor of the station to get customer service). I had no time for this, so I found another office that I'm not sure what they did, but 1 young gal spoke English. I explained I had issues buying the ticket, & she was able to help me. My card worked & she was able to run it without the Pin #. Just know that at Atocha, it's a huge station & allow lots of time for machine errors & possibility of needing human help (& that almost no one speaks English). Once on the train, we were in the normal "tourista" class. It was ok. Nothing special. You have assigned seats in a certain "coche" # on your ticket. The cafeteria car was a couple cars up, & they served snacks & beverages. A cart comes through that you can buy from too. The norm seems to be to eat the food in the food car. There are also norms to talk on the cell phones only in the between car area. The train is super fast, & was right on time, so no complaints there.On our return trip from Seville back to Madrid, we had another ticket issue. I had asked our hotel desk staff if they thought I needed to buy advance tickets (as in, do the trains sell out?). The trains run every hour, & the one going from Madrid to Seville wasn't crowded at all, but I was anxious since I noticed the line to get on the train in Seville when we arrived was long. The lady at the hotel said no, that the trains don't sell out. She was WRONG!! I should have bought our tickets in advance, although I wasn't sure when we'd be able to leave, due to my husbands meeting, although I heard that you can buy a "flex" ticket. I have no idea how that works. I also heard that the website has major issues & isn't user friendly. When I arrived at the station in Seville, I went to the 1st machine & selected English & only 1/2 the screen text was in English! I proceeded to the next machine over & tried to select the ticket to Madrid & noticed that all the hourly slots said "sold out" I started to panic, as we had a flight out of Madrid the next morning. I got into the actual real person ticket line (after the "Information" desk person couldn't speak english & pointed me to that line). The ticket seller didn't speak English either, so in my broken Spanish I explained that I needed 2 Madrid tickets & I understood him to say "no" that there were no trains out for the next 3 days. I waived my credit card stating "Puedo pagar mas" He wrote down 280Euros on a paper & I clarified that this was for 2 tickets on 1645 train. I had no idea what I had paid for, but it turned out it was the "preferente" class. I don't speak enough English to ask how many of these tickets were left & so although my husband should have used his corporate card for his, I purchased both personally, since he was still on his way to the station. Once my husband got there, he wanted to refund the 1 ticket & repurchase it on his card. We went to 3 different counters, & no one would help us. The ticket agent said "terminado" which I understood to mean, we were screwed & there were no refunds, even though we just needed to repurchase it with a different credit card. Once on the train, it is a very nice way to travel in this class. Included meal, snack, alcoholic beverage & the car was much nicer than the "tourista" class. The train was on time & the service was great in this class. In the future, I would research pre-purchasing a flex ticket if possible & make sure that you allow a ton of time for machine/ticket errors. Good luck!
Traveling by train in Spain using Renfe is very practical. The price is fair and the trains leave on time. Bathrooms could be cleaned more frequently.

We used Renfe to travel from Avignon to Barcelona twice. The trains are clean and comfortable, with headphones to follow a film...Far be it from us to want to compare, but the prices are much more advantageous and the comfort is there.

My advice for renfe travellors is to upgrade to tourist plus for a little extra cost, where you'll have more room to spread out on long journeys. Book as afrin advance as you can for cheap tickets. If you have a long journey, take a picnic because catering is quite limited.. If you have an onward connection to make, leave plenty of time because the trains in Spain seem to be routinely late, especially the medium distance trains.The long distance trains are v fast. Customer service on these is very poor. Ticket inspectors can be rude and patronising. Don't take it personally....it's the same service for everyone.

Render revises their prices based on bookings so it is a good idea to check for the trains and routes you want ahead of time.  Also they show movies on the trains (in Spanish) and pass out ear buds for long distance travel.

We always travel on our own, but we don’t have a car. Therefore, RENFE is an indispensable way to move throughout the country. It is especially profitable to buy tickets from them online and in advance.
Spain's high-speed rail system deserves all the praise it deserves. Convenient schedule, low fare. And most importantly - quickly, the speed in some areas exceeds 300 kilometers per hour.
We took a day trip to Ronda and had to queue for 25 minutes for tickets. So, either go early, or book in advance. Clean station with helpful staff.

We bought Spain Passes over the internet before leaving the U.S. In Madrid (Atocha station) we managed to spend 3 hours, visiting 4 different offices within the station trying to get our Rail Passes and to make reservations and get tickets to Cordoba. Finally, we ended up with reservations, and one rail pass printed on a sheet of white paper and the other printed on a piece of cardstock (think airline ticket.)  When we arrived in Cordoba we decided to get the NEXT leg of our trip before leaving the Cordoba station. The pass printed on white paper (with a square bar code) had been a problem in Madrid and it was a problem in Cordoba. 2 hours and 3 offices later, the very helpful staff ended up CANCELLING the paper pass, then reissuing it correctly. Supposedly they worked....but from then on, we decided to spend our time on vacation instead of on dealing with Renfe Spain Pass. We could See the Train Schedules using the Phone App 'Rail Planner' (*NOT* the Renfe App), and we just went to the station and bought tickets from the machines. Less hassle....worth it to just chuck the Renfe Spain Pass in the trash 1/2 used.Except for the high speed lines from Madrid to Cordoba to Seville, all our travel was on smaller trains...so we'd bought second class passes.  When we switched to paying cash, we found that it was cheaper to buy 2nd class tickets, anyway.  Next trip to Spain: NO RAIL PASS.

Renfe station, exit to all places, restaurant, cafeteria, everything at your fingertips, two hundred meters from the city, one hundred meters from the Florida Theater, Chapel of La Caridad, Cristo de la Buena Muerte and street, commercial tariff, food market built and subject to coluna, the only food market in Andalusia.
We used this facility to access Ronda using the old railway line up into the mountains. We didn't try the catering facilities at either end so cannot comment on them.

I have done this Journey from Algeciras to Madrid several times. Although not the modern Madrid - Barcelona trains. Still very comfortable, and First class is so affordable it is well worth the few extra euros for a journey of this length
We have just used Renfe trains for the first time. Caught the train from Cordoba to Madrid. Beautiful, quiet and comfortable.  We found the staff to be very helpful.

We have the worst railway line in all of Spain. The train that connects Algeciras and Madrid has a section that goes on an old-fashioned track with a winding route that prevents speed on said train. The interior of the carriages in terrible condition. Quite decadent service.

In addition to the long-distance AVE line, RENFE suburban lines also depart from this station. You can take a suburban line to Malaga Airport. By the way, tickets for suburban lines cannot be purchased at the counter, but from automatic ticket vending machines.

The service prior to getting on the train was unfriendly and confusing, but once we found our seats the ride from Madrid to Barcelona was smooth and comfortable. The windows were clear and clean, I just wish the view was more scenic. Take something to read.
Also went to Segovia it is highly recommended, what a beautiful town with lots to see and do young or old. plenty of good bars and restaurants.

I used RAÍL EUROPE to buy the tickets and I really felt scammed, they sold me 4 round trip tickets Madrid - Barcelona in first class and it turns out that that does not exist, what is on Renfe is preferential and current or standard, and they told us that with the users of their portal they always had the same problem, they treated us very badly for requesting that they place us in preferential and we lost the additional payment for a better level service, I will never use it again, additionally the train staff It's not very friendly, the train on the other hand is great

Instead of expensive plane tickets, we bought a RENFE train ticket for 28 euros, which took us to Malaga station from Madrid Atocha in just 3 hours. From there we got to Algeciras by bus. True, we bought tickets very well in advance. The train is comfortable, the seats are located on both sides of the aisle, two at a time. There are several stops along the way. But everything is only for disembarking and boarding passengers - two minutes each. On the way, the train reaches speeds of up to 400 km/h.

Think of a top train!!! It doesn't change anything very quickly, we went from Barcelona to Madrid, it took very little time!! Tip: don't go on Sunday as it's the only day that doesn't have an open bar

I bought the Spain Pass but was struggling with the reservation of the tickets. I managed to reserve my tickets at the Barcelona station to Madrid as one helpful attendant helped by referring me to the automated ticket machine where he also helped me to enter all my details. I was advised that tickets can be only issued on the day of travel and I have decided to reserve my tickets from Madrid to Sevilla when I reached the Atocha Station at Madrid. Upon reaching Atocha Station, I took my spain pass to the ticketing counter for reservation. However, the ticket counter was unable to print the ticket and referred me to the customer service office (as the queue behind me has also built up). I took my spain pass to the customer service office (no queue at all as it was very early in the morning) and requested for help. The customer service officer look at us and shrugged and referred us back to the ticket office although we politely told her that we have been referred by the ticket office to them. Same reaction and she pointed us back to the ticket counter. I would have wish that the customer service officer can be more helpful (and what's the point of having a customer service office when there's absolutely no help provided?). Desperate, we tried the automated machine and it worked!! We decided not to take any chance when we reached Seville and to get our tickets reserved in advance for our return trip to Barcelona. When we reached Seville, we tried the Automated Machine...it turns out that all tickets are fully booked. We went to the ticket office for help. The ticketing officer at Seville - Santa Justa has been extremely patient...told us that we can pay a small fee for an upgrade in train class but he too encountered the same issue where tickets cannot be printed/issued. He patiently referred to his manager and finally advised us that the reason why is because we booked our Spain Pass through the internet and reservation has to be done through the same way, ie. the internet (WOW, this is enlightening and finally a reason why we had so much difficulty!) We went to the Seville Station customer service office and decided to enquire how to make reservation on the internet and she kindly went through with us by showing us on the screen (Another GREAT experience at the Seville Santa Justa Station). What a difference in experience this makes! My recommendation to RENFE is to perhaps review if they REALLY need that customer service office in Madrid (Which i guess they should given that it is the main train hub in SPAIN) and to review the Service Level at that particular office.

I want to alert fellow travellers to the worthlessness of the Renfe punctuality promise and their poor customer service. The punctuality promise refers to some of their high speed trains whereby they offer a full refund if the traveller is late....sometimes only by 5mins. Renfe publicise this promise massively. It is a big advertising promotion for them. By the way I'm a big fan of train travel and have loved travelling all over Spain by train over the last decade and personally I'm not interested if my train from Madrid to Seville is 5 mins late but I do expect a Renfe to fulfil its commient to a full refund if I arrive 2hr 25 mins late on a high speed train from Madrid to Cadiz! The first we knew our train was cancelled was less than 15 mins before departure when the departure platform was indicated on screen ( even at that moment we thought we were still going to catch the train we had booked, on time) only to arrive at the gate and have a mute (and later haughty) Renfe attendant simply take our tickets, cross out the time and reassign us to a train 2hr 25 min later. No apology, no explanation, no word. Nothing! She even managed to separate myself and my partner from each other on the replacement train rather than sit us next to each other ...as we had planned for the 4 hour journey . Unfortunately the Renfe staff have been trained at (or possibly have been selected for their natural talent for) fobbing the traveller off. We tried both at Cadiz and Madrid to obtain the promised refund but at both places were treated extremely rudely by staff who were totally disinterested. For example, in Madrid Atocha Customer Services Desk the woman didn't even look at my me or my ticket before she brusquely said 'you need to wait 24hrs before you apply'. I told her it was 5 days since the journey. She then tried to fob me off saying the train was cancelled due to a strike and that we didn't qualify for a refund. The website clearly states that only in cases of ..., is the punctuality promise not valid. In Cadiz we were told ' but you got here didn't you?' 'The train you came on was on time'. Both were seemingly correct statements but we were severely delayed, massively inconvenienced ( late for major social event) and cheated. We bought the Preferente tickets on the basis of the punctuality promise but now appear to have no prospects of a refund. The worst thing however is the really poor customer service from Renfe. Even in the UK the staff would have been much more kind to the customer. An apology at any (or every) stage would have made me feel better and I probably wouldn't have sought the refund which I now feel duty bound to pursue. Renfe get your act together, keep your promises and most of all improve your customer service!
The MD train had a very good journey and its facilities were well maintained... although a bird that arrived in Barcelona directly would not go amiss.

Fast, cheap. Today I was driving from Blanes to Barcelona in the first direction, everything was fine, but in the other direction there was about a 15-minute delay, some accident or something. The worst thing was that the only toilet on the train was unfortunately out of order. The ticket cost €6.15 one way, so not that bad.

I will share my experience of communicating with the RENFE company and I, maybe. our travelers will find this useful when planning their trips on the trains of this company. On September 18, my wife and I made a one-day trip from Lloret de Mar to Madrid. [Tickets for Sarfa buses (Lloret-Barcelona-Lloret) and AVE trains (Barcelona-Madrid-Barcelona) were purchased 2 months before the trip.] The trip in the forward direction was punctual in time and brought a lot of positive impressions (cool Sarfa car and high-speed AVE train, landscapes, etc.). Our return journey from Madrid to Lloret de Mar was timed fit into the following scheme: at 18:00 on AVE 03181 we leave Atocha http://s26.postimg.org/tyxcczyw9/renfe_1.jpg, at 20:30 we are already at Barcelona Sants, and with time to spare at 21:45 with Barcelona Nord the last Sarfa bus we leave for Lloret http://s26.postimg.org/vta6uqlwp/sarfa_1.jpg. But, as they say, “it was smooth on paper, but they forgot about the ravines.” RENFE presents us with a “gift” that could give elderly tourists a heart attack. The departure time of AVE 03181 is approaching, but there is no information about flight 03181 on the radio or on the board. And only five minutes before the train departs (at 17:55) boarding is announced. Upon presentation of the tickets http://s26.postimg.org/tyxcczyw9/renfe_1.jpg we were given this boarding pass http://s26.postimg.org/qglcgly09/renfe_2.jpg, and, as it turned out later, it was not our AVE at all, but on AVE 03183, which left Atocha at 18:30, i.e. 30 minutes later than the canceled flight AVE 03181. Moreover, AVE 03183 to Barcelona went with two intermediate stops in Zaragoza and Terragon and arrived in Barcelona only at 21:20. Of course, we were late for the last Sarfa bus to Lloret, with our tickets in hand. This is the “surprise” that the RENFE company presented to us, not only without compensating for the additional expenses of passengers, but without even apologizing to them for the incident.

We took this train from Barcelona to Madrid. First we got hot towels then a choice of beverage alcoholic or nonalcoholic  then two small sandwiches and a piece of chocolate more towels. The seats were very comfortable with plenty of legroom.

Took a train from Cadiz to Asturias with a change in Madrid.  Had to go from Madrid Atocha to Madrid Chamartin.  Booked direct with RENFE.40 mins to go from one station to the next and as that is 3 stops on a busy line no problem you would think.  Well ...At Atocha a guy was on the platform to gather Gijon passengers. Well pleased it was organised. 4 mins we stood but not all were off the train when the guy uttered his first and only word "vamos" .  He set off at great pace leaving stragglers behind as we marched I'd say 150 meters to the far end of the platform.  One older couple (they could walk ok) were soon well behind and had no chance.  At the top of an escalator we were suddenly in a mass of commuters and soon lost site of the guy.Knowing Madrid well we made our way to cercanias (local trains) but had to persuade a RENFE official that we needed to get to Chamartin.  He said no as he said the train left from Atocha which it didn't; but eventually let us get to the platform.  We waited 6 minutes and arrived at Chamartin 9 minutes later.  There we made our way from I'd say platform 8 (more or less) to platform 21.  Passed ticket inspection and security with 3 minutes to spare.We looked for the older couple both on the train and in Gijon more out of hope but they had no chance.  There are no more trains so I guess a night in a hotel and hopefully a train in the morning.Always found RENFE about a century behind any modern western world railway but delightful for that.  But this was the worst customer service and human behaviour I've ever seen.Be warned if you need to change in Madrid.

I just returned from Santander on the Alvia and I must say that it is a disaster, the punctuality is very good, but the service itself is fatal. Dirty, smelly cars. I get out in business class and when I go to my seat it was broken, I complain and they tell me (after half an hour) that unfortunately they can't change me because the train was full, so I had to endure the entire trip to Albacete with the broken seat. It's a shame, I think the cuts did a lot, but as a travel agent, I believe you have to offer the client the best or at least try. Believe me, when I say poor, that's how it is.

The train station is located in the south of town. There is also a bus terminal near the station. The station is new. There are few trains from this station. There was also luggage tech. Please board the train with plenty of time to spare.

To begin with, trips on the Madrid-Barcelona Ave are becoming more and more expensive. If prices were lowered, customers like me would use it more than we do to travel on a normal weekend and Renfe would earn much more. I can understand that on long weekends they raise prices a little more but for a normal weekend it is not worth spending 200 Euros for 2 days because it is crazy. It cannot be used as a competitor to gasoline because whoever wants to travel to distant places or does not have a car will use the bird as a means of transportation, otherwise people will end up opting for the car because in price they are becoming more and more similar. On the other hand, comment that yesterday my boyfriend and I were traveling on 2 different trains and we tried to overtake my train that was passing an hour before, according to the ticket office employee the train was full and there was not a single space, however, I traveled with no one in the seat next to me. to Madrid having stopped at 3 stations during the trip. I thought it was a shame because apart from the place on my right, there were many others free in my car, let's see if they secure themselves better and improve their applications and programs because they don't work very well and with the cost of the tickets they could make things easier.
I took a first class ticket for the Barcelona-Valencia route: punctuality at departure and arrival, nice lunch included in the price and kindness of the staff. 10 and praise.

Planning a trip to Spain and are over 65.  Don't get overheated if you've missed out on cheap Internet offers on RENFE (Spanish Rail System).  As soon as you land in Spain get yourself a 'targetta dorada ' otherwise known as a half price seniors card from the nearest RENFE ticket office.  It's valid for around a year and costs in the vicinity of €6.  With this in hand you're  eligible for half price train travel on the AVE which hoots along at around 300 kms an hour and gets you there in no time at all.  You can also use it on any service operated by the Spanish Rail system and its worthwhile flashing it on coach tours...you never never know.

Booked a train from Coimbra to Paris via Renfe - it was hours later - they claim they offer a 50% return but when I tried to claim it they claimed it was a force majeure that caused the train to be late and so no compensation was forthcoming.  The trip was the worse I had ever experienced and I arrived back TWO DAYS late having had to spend time in train stations and ferry ports.  The first train to the Spanish borer was nearly two hours late with no explanation as to why. I would never use Renfe again and advise you to use another system if you can.

Extremely poor customer service! If you have a complaint about the train/bus combination in Barcelona because someone behind the counter made a mistake, this will not be resolved and there will even be no communication anymore. You may then do one more thing and that is fill out a complaint form that you will then never hear from again. Even the reception who called afterwards to translate it was fobbed off with...fill in a form! Their own Spanish people say about this company that it is a scandal for Spain that they leave tourists to their fate.

My wife and I recently had some great experiences riding the train in Spain thanks to the Atendo service. Anyone who has ridden trains in Europe, knows the feeling when your  platform isn't announced until 15 minutes before departure time and then you have to rush to the correct platform. Now imagine if you have reduced mobility what a challenge that is. After our first train ride in Spain, where we struggled to make connections, we found out about the Atendo service and the folks with the orange vests. And thanks to them, we never had to worry about making our train even when the platform was changed at the last minute. They were always there with a wheelchair, smiling and helping my wife enjoy her trip. A huge "THANK YOU" to all the people who work in Atendo.

The Renfe trains were great: on-time, clean, with many options.  However, thinking we needed to book ahead of time, we booked our tickets on-line from the States before traveling to Spain.  Even though our tickets were "flexible," once you are in Spain, if you want to make a change, it is impossible.  So, just know that once you book your ticket through Renfe's American agent, you are stuck with THAT train and time.  You won't be able to change your reservation.

I have traveled more than once on Renfe Rodalies trains from Calella to Barcelona. The compositions are different, there are old ones and there are more modern ones, all of them are equipped with air conditioning. The main disadvantage is that they are regularly late; the train has never arrived at its destination on time. Therefore, planning connections is very difficult.

If you are referring to the station cafeteria... It has been closed for a long time! Which further increases the abandonment suffered by the traveler...not even having a luggage storage! Shameful for a city whose basic source is tourism!!!
great for getting to know other places. You can go at night and save on hotels. depending on the beginning and end of the trip
I go in business class and the truth is that it is uncomfortable because there is no food. Only the staff who are friendly are saved

First world stuff! We buy on the spot! Clean train! Comfortable ! Everyone in their place! If you're going near (Toledo....) or far (Barcelona! Paris! Amsterdam....) go by train, it's worth every euro. Brazuca is the envy of Europeans here! This is quality

Travel on the AVE between Barcelona and Madrid. I recommend doing it in executive category for very little difference. The perfect service, the comfort too and the trip super fast. Only 2:45 from the center of one city to the other. Better than the plane!!! They would only need to add Wifi on the train. Luck !

My wife and I took Renfe train from Malaga to Cordoba for a day trip.  Ran on time and was reasonably clean.  That said, the online experience was terrible!  I had to spend 20 minutes getting all the info onto the site, and when I fanlly got to the last point to pay, it kept bumping me, saying the phone number was in the requested format- but none was requested, and no combination of dashes, spaces worked!  I also had issues getting my payment made so many tries, that Key Bank locked my accounts, thinking it might be a fraud attempt.  So using my charge plates became a nightmare, and I had to walk to the actual station just to get my tickets, and then pay in CASH $150 because they got my charge plates locked!

Travelled by RENFE from Algeciras to Ronda. The start of the journey provides excellent views of nesting storks on pylons, etc. Sit on the right for best views. Then passes through forested and mountainous area until emerging towards Ronda which is a must for a visit. The seats were OK but not friendly for anyone with back problems. I suffered a little towards the end of the journey and I noticed one middle-aged lady standing up holding the seat in front for the last few miles. My wife also began to get fidgety towards the end. The service was good albeit 20 mins late on the return journey. Purchase your tickets the day before if possible or turn up early if travelling the same day as queues can be encountered at the ticket office. We waited 30 mins.

Bought a tourist plus flexible ticket. Website says use of club lounge at station is allowed however staff at club lounge insisted it was only for first class passengers. Got to train station early and no one at customer service was willing to change my ticket for a train that was leaving one hour earlier. All the  customer service reps are lazy and not willing to help. Train ride itself was fine. No point wasting money in tourist plus. Go regular tourist class and spend the money you save on having some great tapas in seville.

We have recently travelled around Spain using trains. The booking process on their website was straight forward and we were able to book our tickets well in advance. The trains were very clean and comfortable - we travelled in first class and tourist class ( no real difference) and always left on time. The even have movies (provided you can understand Spanish) and we found the staff always helpful and polite. The only minor issue is that sometimes they don't announce the platform the train is leaving from until about 5 minutes before departure - which creates a bit of a mad rush.

The most abandoned station in the world, if you get robbed there is no security at all and the services are somewhat poor. Little control and little security being at the crossing of the strait. It makes me sad to see that they do not change it for the better.

safe, practical and very comfortable! the train is punctual, clean and quiet. Films and music are shown on board. There is a snack bar with prices the same as in the season! Don't even buy snacks at the station thinking it's cheaper inside, it's the same price!

My partners and I planned a five-night stay in Córdoba, flying to Málaga and staying two nights there before proceeding to Córdoba. I had great difficulty trying to reserve train tickets on the RENFE website and instead used Loco2, who processed my order efficiently and sent PDF files of the tickets in the same way as airlines send boarding passes for online check-in. The A4 print-outs were accepted without question at the security scanning entrances to the platforms. We considered buying the tickets from an authorised UK agency, but they appeared to charge a considerable handling fee. You do need to know, however, that Loco2 has no customer telephone number, although it does answer emails reasonably quickly. We had brought no laptop or smartphone with us and when a strike was threatened on the TV we could get advice only from the authorised UK agency (which does have a phone number). Fortunately no strike occurred to disrupt our travel but there was a cleaners' strike at Córdoba station and it was indescribably filthy when we arrived, but had been cleaned when we left. The train ride was punctual and the seats spacious and comfortable. Highly recommended. The missing star on our assessment is because of RENFE's website and the mess at the station, not the wonderful trains.

This station, to call it that, because it lacks everything and I mean everything, because the trains are a shame to go to Madrid, we still have to wait to get to Bobadilla to see a modern and electrified line. I do not understand this political caste that having the largest port in Spain and that Algeciras is the gateway to southern Europe, to have this poor station, without trains, without roads and without equipment.

I often travel with Renfe trains to move around Spain, especially for the Lleida-Barcelona Sants route and then with Rodalies from Sants to the airport. I've always had a great time, the trains are super clean, very quiet and comfortable. There is plenty of space for suitcases and backpacks, the seats are comfortable, the staff comes by at every stop to offer earphones that you can use to listen to music or watch films projected on the televisions. I only once arrived at my destination about ten minutes late, all the other trips were flawless!

We had a lovely ride to Rhonda and then were able to have lunch and proceed by train through the gorge at El Chorro and the lakes, it was a great day with beautiful views. The historical value, was that it was built by the British for the servicemen and their families to go into the mountains for a break.

The Algeciras station is characterized by being very poor in services, it seems incredible that it is the gateway to southern Europe, but to know more we would have to see why the tracks from Bobadilla are from the third world. Lack of investment. To say something good, it has the bus stop in front and the maritime station a few meters away.

Horrible service! I've used AVE trains several times. The AVE bullet trains are really nice, specially the Siemens trains which are very comfortable. This review is for the overall service experience.Renfe's online portal to purchase tickets is not at all user friendly and does not work very well with credit cards from outside Spain. At best, Renfe's online portal is a reminiscence of the early days of e-commerce during the .com boomPurchasing tickets at Barcelona Sants station is also a major nightmare, after standing in line for 15 min at a ticket window that was labeled "long distance", I was told to go to another window and wait another 15 min in line. The people at the window tend to be rude, unhelpful and may only speak Spanish (and may not understand gringo Spanish). While I'm sure that working at a ticket window  is probably not one of the most fulfilling jobs, Renfe's window employees must really hate their jobs or have little or no training in customer relations. In general my impression is that European customer service standards are well below those of US companies. I would say Renfe is well below the lower European standard.On my last trip to Spain, I bought the tickets from the US using Renfe's authorized US portal raileurope.com I paid extra to purchased flexible tickets so I could try to board an earlier train when returning from Madrid to Barcelona. At Madrid's Puerta Atocha station I was sent from one service desk to another for some 20 minutes, only to be told at check-in that the flexible ticket I paid for couldn't be changed for an earlier train. Perhaps the earlier train was full? Not the case, in fact there was plenty of availability I was told. However, if you purchase the tickets outside Spain, even though the tickets look just like any AVE Renfe issued ticket and the contract is exactly the same, they just can't honor any changes on it (even if it's a flexible ticket). They will tell you so, of course in a very rude and unhelpful way. After insisting, the only solution offered was to go to a travel agency. If it weren't that I know Spain well, from that answer I would have concluded Spain has not been part of planet earth in the last 20 years.I do recommend riding the AVE, that is if you can get a ticket.

If you wonder how to get to the city from Barcelona airport, the train is so convenient and cheap.  if you buy a book (T10) of 10 tickets which cost 10.9 Euros, the cost come out about 1.1 Euro each way.  The taxi I heard would cost about 40 Euro.  These same tickets could be used for all the other subway lines in the city.  The train goes from the Terminal 2 at the airport.  If you get down from the international flight at Terminal 1, you need to take the airport bus, which is free in the front, to go to Terminal 2 then walk to the train station to go to the city.  When you get to the city, you would get off at the main station (SANTS Estacio) and then take the metro, green line to go to Las Ramblas, or you can also get off at the next station at the Passeig de Gracia if you stay near the Sagrida Familia.  The metro is convenient and can take you anywhere.  The local people are very nice and helpful.  You do, however, want to keep an eyes on your valuables as like any other big cities.  The ride takes about 25 minutes and there will be music on the train to enjoy.  if you like, give those people some change.

We traveled a lot by train in Spain, bought tickets in advance on the Internet, printed them on a printer (although you can also print them from ticket machines). The best trains are, of course, those that go from Madrid to Barcelona, ​​the German Siemens, an analogue of the German ICE. But other varieties of AVE are also good. But I don’t really like alvias (up to 250 km/h). AVE, by the way, was never late when we rode on them, but Alvia was regularly delayed by 30-40 minutes. From Madrid to Algeciras it is not Ave or even Alvia, but Altaria - a simpler, slower train, although closer to Madrid it also runs quickly. But closer to Algeciras it is very slow - the road is bad and winding.

It is amazing that a city like Algeciras, with one of the most important ports in the world, has such a mediocre train station. The traveler who approaches it, and I was there today because I came from Granada, will see that it only has a couple of ticket offices and a large waiting room. The station's services ended there. No cafeteria, no newspaper shop, no tourist office, no nothing. It is unfortunate that a city like Algeciras, through which hundreds of thousands of people pass each year, does not have something better.
on time, clean,and cheap way to travel to places like Ronda, Cordob and Seville. Very easy to find the  train station in algeciras
nothing to dislike about the train journey seating on train too was good but you have to reserve but not busy when we went in october
Good train services to Madrid, Rhonda and other places. The carriages are good and clean. Refreshment service and good clean stations with refreshments
Very clean  , discounted tickets for pensioners, trains run on time , Superb views  - look out for the storks. Read the article on the Andalusia website for historical details

I love Renfe Trains but i hate dealing with their people. Ticket officers at Atocha this morning were like 1950s Public servants: slow, not even remotely aware of urgency, and happy to chat endlessly with people in front of them instead of moving the queue along. Here's a tip for free, Renfe customer service management: tell your "i couldn't care less about timetables" staff to get some sense of the industry that pays their bills or tell them to get off that fat cabooses and give their job to one of the 48% unemployed Madrid youth who would love to help a tourist get on their train on time. You shame Spain, you really do.

Terrible organisation, both for high speed and medium distance. The staff speaks only Spanish, they don't even know what English is. And this already bodes badly for a tourist who wants to move around Spain. Among other things, after having canceled our high-speed train for unknown reasons, an assistant proposed a solution that was decidedly longer and more tiring than the planned journey, making us wait for almost 3 hours at the station while just a few minutes later one was leaving for our destination (which was not full, among other things). Get around by car or plane, Italian high-speed and intercity trains are definitely superior!!

Once you're actually on the train, the experience is fine--it took us where we wanted to go safely and efficiently.  But here are things that Americans MUST know in advance:1.  The automated ticket machines at the stations WILL NOT accept your U.S. credit cards.  European credit cards have a chip in them for added protection; American ones eventually will, too, but they don't have them yet.  This means that the machine will ask you for a PIN number, which you probably won't know.  Even if you do have a PIN associated with your credit card, don't use it!  The transaction will be processed as a cash advance, not as a regular charge.2.  The Renfe employees at the train stations are rude and do not give one flip about you.  This is true whether you speak Spanish or English.  At the Atocha station, the ticket agents will tell you that the ONLY way you can use your credit card to buy tickets through them is to use your PIN.  This is a lie.  Any merchant displaying the MasterCard logo must accept your MC credit card; all they have to do is manually enter the data from your card, including expiration date, and the system will accept it.  Other merchants will do this for you in Spain--Renfe will not.  (I got this information straight from Capital One.  I assume it applies to Visa and American Express, as well.)3.  Don't bother traveling in a class other than Tourist.  There's no real difference other than the fact that they sell you sandwiches in Business Class.  The price is too high, but worse, the food is inedible.  I mean this sincerely.  Whatever the mystery goo filling was on our sandwich, we couldn't get it down.If you know these things ahead of time, go ahead and travel on Renfe.  We took round-trips  from Madrid to Segovia, Salamanca, and Barcelona, and the ride was comfortable.  Just educate yourself, be savvy, and don't expect any help from Renfe employees.comfortable

I was hoping that there would be a restaurant where I could get breakfast, but the station was really empty except for vending machines, and it was deserted with no one around until just before the train was about to depart. There wasn't anything nearby, so I bought bread, ham, and cheese at a supermarket near Plaza Alta, made a sandwich, and ate it on the station platform.

There seems to be a bit of criticism related to Renfe, however, I can merely say my experiences have only been excellent - Madrid to El Puerto de Santa Maria; El Puerto de Santa Maria to Seville and return; and, Madrid to Narbonne via Barcelona and Figueres Villafant. In fact, my view is that they are better than SNCF in general. When things go wrong of course, one expects people to be unhappy and even angry if things are not handled well, however, in my experience, all was perfect.

During our trip to Spain, we used various trains and electric trains of the renfe railway network. From Barcelona to Madrid and back we traveled on high-speed AVE trains, very convenient. The travel time is only about 3 hours, the cost is slightly lower than by plane (I paid about 9,000 rubles for 2 adults round trip), and in the end, the train turns out to be more profitable in terms of time, since you do not need to go to the airport in advance, then wait for baggage collection, and the railway stations also have access to the metro, which is also convenient. We were very pleased with the convenience and service on the Ave trains. Since we lived in Pineda da Mar, renfe were our friend on regional and suburban trips to Barcelona, ​​Montserrat, Girona, Figueres. During commuter trips, various beggars (musicians, singers, clowns) often ran into the carriage. On the one hand, during our frequent trips, we got pretty tired of the beggars, on the other hand, at least they beg beautifully, I was amazed by the sound quality in their portable equipment; in our villages, some of them would be installed in clubs! Another incident happened once, the train stopped for some reason, all the passengers were thrown onto another train. As a result, instead of our station, we only got to the nearest one 2 minutes before it, and then we had to take a taxi, which led to additional expenses and interesting adventures. The renfe website is a little inconvenient to use, the Spanish and English versions are different, it’s difficult to figure out, but it’s possible.

Train from Madrid to benidorm , train breaks down , they don't inform us whilst on the train about what's going on , they make us wait 2 hours before telling us anything then proceed to get another train to finish the journey to alicante but it gets there too late and we are left stranded in alicante and cannot get to benidorm which is what we paid for , they did nothing to help , we had no means of getting back to benidorm , their advice was to sleep on a bench and catch a train in the morning , worst train service in Europe hands down .

The train from Algeciras to Granada via Ronda is well worth while. The stage to Ronda was built in the 1880s and links some 20 villages. It passes through lovely countryside as it climbs, taking about 1 hr 50 min to Ronda. The trains are new and comfortable - the seats are automatically allocated on buying the tickets and they face in both directions. It may be possible to specify facing or back to the front, but I did not know to ask. One can go both ways in a day, but take the oppoertunity to have a good look at Ronda.

I used RENFE a lot to get to know other cities in Spain. Very good service. Ease of purchasing the ticket. A good value for money. Punctuality with schedules. Comfortable accents. I used a night high speed one and it was very good too.
One of the best trains in Europe to travel on...punctual and always a clean environment with good service.

Having stayed for the Easter holidays in a hotel (Golden Taurus Park Resort) in Pineda de Mar, the proximity of the RENFE station to the hotel made us want, like last year, to spend an afternoon in Barcelona. We could certainly have gone there by car, but good luck finding parking. Brief. So we take a Regional train, which stops at all the seaside stations. The journey takes about an hour or a little more. Comfort is acceptable. What do you want, it can't be super comfortable on regional trains. Schedules are respected, no delays (within one or two minutes). The price is very affordable, 33 euros for a 10-trip card (being 4 people, we used 8 trips). Cards are available for sale in train stations as well as on the website of Renfe, the Spanish rail transport company. All timetables for all lines are displayed in the stations, you can also ask for a leaflet containing the timetables for a line (you can ask for several if you want to know the timetables for several lines). Here we remain on very positive grounds, and we are surprised to see that the timetables are respected in Spain, with significantly less delay than with the SNCF in France. Indeed, in all the holidays we have come to Spain (that is to say almost all of them), the biggest delay we have encountered either while being on board the train or consulting the illuminated display panels at the stations announcing the departures and arrivals of the trains was 7 minutes! Impressive! For any other questions or if you would like more details, do not hesitate to contact me via TripAdvisor.

Have used RENFE several times, and each time have been more impressed. Booked RENFE from Malaga to Madrid a few days before travelling online and it could not be more simple, purchased a Tarjeta Dorada card a few days earlier which is used for travelers over 60, which cost 6 Euro each, and reduced the fare from 60 Euro to 45 Euro, although not the fastest train, travelled non-stop, just over 400km in a little over 3 hours.The seats were like first class, wide, electrically operated and with plenty of room, all the facilities were excellent, as was the service.As we travelled to Malaga from Fuengirola, enquired about the cost of the tickets, and was told by a most friendly lady, that they were INCLUDED in the main train fare!If you are used to UK levels of service and standards, be prepared to be amazed!Also if you arrive at Madrid’s Atocha station, leave some time to look at the botanical garden within the station, which includes 100’s of turtles of all sizes – on the first time, nearly missed the train watching this fascinating sight!

I have been in Madrid for 3 months and to date with the train service there has been nothing negative to report. There is a point that happens at Chamartin station where every weekend the ticket counters are insufficient to meet the demand for ticket sales, so always arrive 1 hour before your train leaves or buy online and I know you will be sure to use the best service in Europe.

I have just returned from a train trip around Spain. It would certainly not have been possible to have such an enjoyable trip were it not for the professionalism of Renfe - I would like to congratulate the company on its excellent service - professional staff, on-time trains, clean trains, food and beverage services available (buffet car, trolley or vending machines). It's definitely worth using the trains in Spain - not expensive and generally a nice experience. You could do worse than book through Rail Bookers who make a trip run smoothly but Renfe also offers a wide range of tourist routes with different types of trains and discount rates
Fabulous trip and staff were very helpful.If you are over 60dont forget to get Tarjeta Dora to get 40%off journeys (mon-Thursday)

Poor signage for parking at the main station in malaga but eventually found the underground parking and once parked we were in the station in minutes.All luggage was put through X-ray but I do not think passengers were. What is the point.Anyway our reserved seats were waiting and it was a comfortable two hour ride to Seville in better seating than that offered in economy in the UK.

We took the train to Ronda.  Booked our tickets on-line from the UK but could have just as easily bought them at the station.  We took the media distance train out and it was punctual, comfortable and with clear announcements.  We caught the Altaria train back (a  bit like an intercity) which again was punctual and comfy but with less distinctive announcements.
