As our journey back was at night I was glad our destination was the end of the line as it was difficult to see out to see what station you were stopping at.

I purchased RENFE Spain Rail Passes for my wife, adult daughter and myself on line.  I found the purchase to be relatively straight forward.  Reserving seats was a little more difficult but I managed to get through it not too much effort.  Be certain to reserve your seats in the order in which you will be traveling. Example, if you reserve seats on the second and third legs but not the first you will not be able to reserve seats on the first leg later.  I spent two hours in the Ochoa Station reworking our entire itinerary and, thankfully, we were still able to get seats on the trains  we had earlier scheduled and then had to redo them.  The trains are fantastic, not just the AVE high speed trains but the Altria as well.

We needed to get from Madrid to Morocco in the cheapest way possible. And at the same time it was interesting to see the country. The plane cost more than 7 thousand rubles. per person. We decided to look for an alternative option. We found out that there is a ferry to Tangier from Tarifa. But there are no trains to Tarifa. At the central station we were offered to take tickets for RENFE to Algeciras, there is also a crossing there. An adult train ticket costs 75 euros. If there are travel benefits (youth ticket, age over 60 years, disability), then you need to come to the ticket office strictly on weekdays from 10 to 18 hours. Then for 5 euros you buy the right to a discount, and you get a 40% discount on a ticket, so it turns out not 75, but 50 euros. The crossing from Algeciras to Tangier costs 18-25 euros, depending on the carrier. There are two trains - morning and afternoon. We went early in the morning to ensure we were on time for the crossing. We left at 8 am and were in Algeciras at 1 pm. The train is seated, with soft chairs, and small tables in the backs of the seats.  Quite comfortable and fast. Nice clean toilets. There are no lockers for luggage.  There are open shelving at the end of the cars, space for prams, wheelchairs, and bicycles. You need to take food or water with you - we didn’t find a restaurant or buffet on the train. There was no Internet. The route is beautiful, passes through a picturesque area through the mountains. From the station in Algeciras to the ferry it takes no more than 30 minutes. walking through a very pretty city. Ferries to Tarifa depart every 1-2 hours, the last at approximately 22 hours. The journey takes about an hour. We took tickets for 16 o'clock, and at 16 o'clock. We were already at the port in Tangier (in Morocco the time is 1 hour less than in Spain), and at 18:00 we checked into the hotel.
Algeciras, due to its population and its location, deserves a much better station, it is uncomfortable, small...
After the last renovation, it was a very simple station, the surroundings are the worst in Algeciras, it is difficult to park without paying, a positive point is the connection with Madrid.

We took the train to the Basque country again, great. We couldn't buy the ticket at the airport, but we did it at the station, 10% discount when you present copies of international tickets. We took the preferential one, a special waiting room with internet, coffee, soft drinks and very comfortable seats.  I forgot my camera charger, I remembered it on the train and the supervisor very kindly took all my information and sent it to Bilbao on the next train the next day... we returned to the station and the charger was there. We took the train in the afternoon, excellent sunset and landscapes, very good service. clean, comfortable seats, very good music, time to relax..... we loved it, a unique experience., we will return... my husband loved the dessert!!

We arrived in Algeciras by train from Cordoba.The last 90 minutes from Ronda to Algeciras takes you through some wonderfully scenic country.The train doesn't go very fast (averages about 40mph).Apparently RENFE want to close this line.  The train was about 30% full.

The Algeciras to Ronda train journey is a trip through some of the most beautiful countryside in Andalucía. The little three-carriage train winds its way past some of the attractive 'white towns' of the region and through the spectacular scenery of the Los Alcornocales and Grazalema Natural Parks.British engineers built the line when Victoria was on the throne - I have often wondered whether she had some sort of stomach disorder the amount of time she spent there - sorry - I couldn't resist that!  Many of the stations still have the original equipment and furnishings that were shipped out from Britain in the 19th century.La línea de los ingleses - the 'English Railway' - is actually 110 miles long and continues beyond Ronda to the town of Bobadilla. The line is just one section of a large scenic route that stretches eastwards through Granada and on to Almería. Robert Bovington

We bought a Eurorail pass and travelled through Spain and France for 15days of travel in a month. This worked really well if we were able to book far enough ahead. The earlier you book the more choice you have. There are usually three levels of travel - Preferente, Turista Plus and Turista. We did a mixture of TGV and RENFE in the two countries. The only hiccup was that we cold not book any trips that originated in the other country but were fine to book from one country to the other. We also could not book our Barcelona to Paris leg until we were in Barcelona, but now wonder if this was at the discretion of the particular station attendant that we asked. We have very limited Spanish so found it best to have our trips written down clearly so that they knew what to expect. The trains are very fast, usually quite clean, but the toilets leave a lot to be desired. I think it may depend on who has used them, but some were very smelly and paper, soap etc had run out. They were not always flushed either. You do also have to be careful that there is no one sitting in your seat. A show of your ticket and seat number is usually enough to move them on but a passenger from Turista will often just come and find a spare seat in Preferente until moved on. The food available onboard is minimal and does not cater for any particular diets eg. gluten free, so you would need to take something with you. There are luggage racks for large cases at each end of a carriage and I would recommend you put yours in your line of vision. A friend saw his disappearing off the train at a station and had to give chase. It was stashed somewhere and eventually found and they waited at the next station for it to be forwarded on. A bicycle chain with accompanying padlock would be a good item to have to either join bags together or attaching them to a bar on the luggage rack. Having said this, we did not have a problem.

Best train journey ever. And I work on trains for a living!€43 for a 1st class single from Madrid to Alicante. Booked on the RENFE website with no problems. Tickets availableto print at home or collect from vending machine at station.  Luggage is scanned at departure station so allow a bit of extra time.  The journey was amazing. 300km/hr felt smooth as silk, spotless carriage with huge seats and film to watch. I didn't want the trip to end. Point to note, a discounted 1st class ticket "promo fare" doesn't entitle you to use the 1st class lounge at Madrid Atocha, and the beverage/food on board (1050am departure) consisted of a minuscule sandwich, piece of cake and glass of wine.
The area is, let's say, very safe. It's a little run down and there are quite a few drunks. The only good thing is that it is in front of the bus station.

We rode the high speed train from Algeciras to Barcelona with a change about an hour outside of Algeciras.  I appreciated the clean comfortable surroundings.  There is no real competition here aside from airplanes so I guess my comment is that I enjoyed the ride between the two cities.  I should note that if I were on a quick trip, then I would have investigated flying.  The countryside was pretty, but I saw nothing particularly impressive to offset the additional time commitment.  Of course, there are the hassles at the airport which are not experienced by train travelers.....The food car was very nice with tasty options.

We travelled from Madrid on a day trip from atocha renfe to Toledo by booking ticket at station and also did the Madrid to Malaga by booking online. The service is great and fast. I only wish when booking online the options come up in English making it easier to book without referring to google for Spanish translations.

During my trip to Spain, I booked and used RENFE railways several times. The route that satisfied me the most was Seville-Madrid. With Ave we covered this itinerary in around 2.30 hours. Impeccable service, exceptionally clean, spacious, well-soundproofed carriages. We were offered a snack, drinks, newspapers, coffee. Truly exceptional. Booking via internet, easy and fast. I found this solution to go to Madrid, really interesting and cheaper than flying.

We had a fantastic experience of Renfe train travel in Spain. We boarded an overnight trenhotel journey from Granada to Barcelona. We had booked a cama preferente doble familiar which entitled us a bathroom within our compartment. The train compartment was very clean and the bathroom included a sink and shower with toiletries, towel, bottles of water. There is a plug point for charging phones in the bathroom.The restaurant car was also very clean though the food was mostly overpriced packaged snacks at breakfast. The train was very punctual and reached our destination on time. The staff was very warm and helpful.

After our Iberia flight from Madrid to Barcelona was cancelled due to the strike, we decided to book tickets on the AVE.  This was not such a terrible thing considering we actually wanted to take the high speed train instead of the flight - it would give us a chance to see more of the country (however, you should check because flights are actually about half the cost of the train ticket).  We left from Madrid - Puerta de Atocha, destination Barcelona - Sants.  Our train was at 10:30 AM.  We took the metro from our hotel at Plaza de Espana to Atocha Renfe (note, get off at Atocha Renfe station, not Atoche).  The ride (which includes one line transfer) took less than 30 minutes.  It was quick and easy... I love the metro system in Madrid.  Only downside is when you're hauling your luggage... sometimes you feel that every corner you turn in the station you see another set of stairs or broken/opposite direction escalator -- gaaah!  The train boards promptly, are clean and actually quite comfortable.  We sat in a Tourist Class car, Promo+ (which means you can pick your seat).  There's a cafeteria car, but I didn't check it out.  They play a movie, but the tv is so small and the train was so noisy as it was that I didn't even bother to pay attention.  Here's my gripe with Renfe - the website is very challenging to book tickets through, at least from the US.  I suggest you read all the forum advice on how to book directly on Renfe's website (which is the cheapest).  There are a lot of sites that have detailed instructions on how to register and book tickets on Renfe.  Good luck - I was unable to do this.  Other websites easily markup the cost of the ticket by at least double!  If you want my advice - I spoke to Visa customer service rep and was also transfered to a Verified by Visa customer service rep - and they indicated to me that Renfe was aware of issues that customers in the US had with purchasing tickets from their site.  They recommend that you purchase tickets from www.petrabax.com.  And that is precisely what we did.  No issues at all with Petrabax.   Total duration: 2 hours 45 mins (plus quick stop in Zaragoza)Total cost: 2 tickets = $264 Recommend: Definitely, was quick and comfortable.Oh, last piece of advice... board the train sooner rather than later if you have large luggage.  There are limited spaces by the doors and overhead space fills up as you can imagine.

The station is still the same as it was, perhaps less and less. Since it was renovated it has lost a lot of services. It does not have newspaper sales, it does not have a cafeteria, it is not comfortable for waiting. I think that a city like Algeciras deserves more.

It was a very pleasant and relaxing journey lasting one hour and thirty-five minutes. Departure and arrival times perfectly respected both on the outward and return journey. Very clean carriages, comfortable and comfortable seats. Speed ​​achieved 301 per hour. By booking online the WEB rate is very convenient. Nice experience that we will repeat.
It is renovated, but despite everything it is a bit third world, the services are to cry, the staff is friendly and the station itself is central but little to be a terminal and entrance to Spain

I traveled to Spain recently and to visit other cities I used the Renfe High Speed ​​Train. Everything works very well, the train leaves exactly on time and there are no problems with delays. The train's departure and arrival times can be found on the website. The carriages are comfortable, clean and even have a snack car if you want to eat or drink something. This is definitely the best way to get around Spain.

It is very central and very close to the Comes transport bus stop. If you travel by bus, just cross the street and you have the Renfe. The only problem it has is that there is no longer a cafeteria to have a drink, because if you arrive early to travel you have to do it on the train, or at the bus station, but you already run the risk that if you get too distracted you could miss the train.

We caught the overnight train from Barcelona to Granada. In terms of facilities and timeliness, the train is good. However, we ran into some trouble just before boarding. From what we could gather, two of the same tickets had been printed. We were running quite close for time, and having gone through the scanner and handed over our tickets, we were stopped by a woman at the counter who started speaking rapidly in Spanish while brandishing our tickets. We were travelling in a group of seven and half of our number had already gone down the elevator towards the train. We explained that we had limited Spanish, and her response was to speak louder, faster and more aggressively. We tried to find out what was wrong or to ask if anyone could explain but noone was able to explain it to us. Eventually she got a supervisor who was friendlier but who also could not explain. She got visibly frustrated and kept waving the tickets at us and saying "duplicado". We showed her our online booking which showed seven different tickets but she just kept saying the same thing over and over again as it got closer and closer to our train's leaving time. In the end the supervisor waved us on and we got on the train just in time. They checked our tickets again on the train and there were no problems.The service left a sour taste of what was otherwise a good train service - regularly cleaned toilets, bar cart, four person compartments made up of two comfortable bunk beds, free bottles of water, and a basin in the room.

We bought the tickets at the Madrid airport once we arrived, very friendly, and provided all the necessary information, it was the first time we used this service. We show our plane tickets and apply for a fare discount.   There is not much difference between internet prices and office prices. We buy the preferred one. It was worth it. We took the Alvia Madrid - Bilbao at 8 am. Checked in and access to the train, easy, fast without any setbacks. Very good service, a good sunrise, dreamlike landscapes, very good breakfast. Excellent music, we really enjoyed it!

We recently travelled Barcelona (Passeig de Gracia) to Figueres return, also one way Granada Cordoba, Cordoba Ronda and Ronda San Roque (for Gibraltar).  All trips were good except for the outbound Barcelona Figueres, we took an all stops local which pretty much was a stuffy subway car ride for over 2 hours.  Our fault for not doing a better job on choosing our train.  Also Passeig de Gracia station is under construction, platform was very hot and crowded, we probably would have done better boarding at Sants.  The trip back was a semi-express, more comfortable cars and food/bev vending machines.  Toilets were reasonably clean by railroad standards.  All the other trips were on Alteria equipment, comfortable and fast enough, although with stop for gauge adjustment at Antequerra to and from Cordoba.  This seemed to take about 15 minutes.  Scenery was interesting on all routes in Andalucia, especially into Ronda and down to San Roque.  None of the trains were crowded except the outbound Barcelona Figueres.We were Tourist (2nd) class.We waited until arriving in Spain to get our tickets, and bought them (except for Barcelona - we bought those with no trouble at P de G station) at a Travel Agent (Viajes Ecuador) near our hotel in Granada.  Not sure how their pricing compared to the RENFE website but the tickets seemed reasonable enough and it was an easy process.Some differences in Spanish rail travel vs other parts of Europe, in Granada and Cordoba we lined up and were checked in airport style at the gate when boarding started, you then just find your seat and your ticket is not looked at again.  But give yourself some extra time at the station before boarding as I think they shut off check in a few minutes ahead of departure, no last minute dash onto the platform and into the train as it pulls away!  Also in Cordoba they do a luggage x-ray before you check in and go down to the platform but this didn't take long.  Just be aware that at major stations it is a bit like boarding a plane.  Ronda was traditional get on when the train pulls in.  Also we had trouble seeing the car numbers when boarding, they seemed to be a little random, i.e car 10 was next to car 6 on one occasion.  Station stops are very short, be ready to get on and off promptly.Didn't check out food/bev on Andalucian trains, may have also been vending, not many people seemed to be consuming it.  Trains were all on time, stations well marked, staff were helpful and competent, stations (except P de G) were pleasant and clean.  This was a good way for us to get around in Andalucia.

We choice to use the AVE to travel between Madrid and Malaga and were delighted by the experience. The train stations are easy to navigate and travel announcements (audio and visual) made the trip easy. The AVE is the high speed train, ours maxed at 303 KPH (188 MPH) and the ride was pleasant. The seats were comfortable, luggage easy to stow and the environment was clean and quiet. We were amazed at how smooth was the ride. The trains were timely and the on board service pleasant and polite. To our surprise there were movies and free headsets to listen to music or the movie. The train can be as expensive as the plane, but the experience of being able to view the country side far exceeds the benefit of saving money or time. Use Trip Advisor forums to learn how to save money by purchasing on line at RENFE's notoriously difficult web site (the savings are well worth the hassle).

Journeyed from Jimena to Ronda for a day out. Train on time, modern, clean, vending machine on board, not expensive - 12 euros return for an hour long journey through some of Andalucias most stunning countryside.

For two weeks I made a thousand failed attempts to buy 2 Madrid-Cordoba train tickets using the RENFE website. When it came time to pay by card after uploading the correct details and choosing seats, it always said that the card-issuing bank did not authorize the operation. Which was not the case. I tried VIsa, Mastercard and Amex from different banks, but always the same error. The response from Renfe was that the problem was with my banks, that their page works correctly. Which is not true since many people from abroad have the same problem. Moral: I ended up buying the tickets through Barcelo Viajes, which are the ones that charge the least management fees. Thank goodness that with a website you try to save time and provide the customer with better service. Renfe in this aspect is a disaster.

I flew in from Miami to Madrid and needed to go to Malaga in a hurry. The taxi ride from the airport to the train terminal is about 20-25 minutes and costs around 30 euro.Help was ok, I encountered someone who spoke English. Only first class tickets were available and after a long intercontinental flight, that was what I needed. It's still a bit cheaper than buying an Iberia ticket.It was smooth training. Service was better than coming back, though. Plenty of leg room, outlets and drinks. No-one to help you with your luggage though, and they were standing at the door greeting you. No wireless internet as well, which is a bit of a downer, considering a lot of European trains do offer that.It took 2,45 hours to get to Malaga. For the trip back, I tried booking online. It's a bit of a hassle, but eventually it went through.I would do this again and see if I will indeed save money on this trip. Getting rid of the airport hassle in Madrid was pleasant.

While we were in Spain, we took the Renfe from Barcelona to Valencia and return. The trains are extremely clean, lots of leg room and very relaxing. The train route was also spectacular. We followed the coastline of the Mediterranean all the way. On one side of the train you could watch the beautiful blue waters of the Mediterranean and on the other side orange groves, olives and lots of artichokes! Would recommend this mode of transporatation to anyone travelling in Spain. here is also a direct metro route between the Barcelona airport and the main train station.

It is well located and connected. At the exit you have the taxis and crossing a roundabout the bus station. The station itself, despite being remodeled, does not have a cafeteria in operation, although at the exit on the left you will find one where you can have a very good breakfast.

We took the train from Madrid to Malaga (return) and were pleasantly surprised by the experience. I agree with everybody else's assessment of booking tickets online, but after getting over that hurdle, it was smooth sailing. The train stations are state-of-the art, particularly the Malaga one, the staff were helpful and friendly enough, the Bombardier-made cars comfortable. All seats are reserved so there is no arguing over who sits where. We have travelled by train extensively all over Europe and the Spanish rail system compares favourably, indeed.  When in Spain, we will definitely take the train again.

After struggling with the renfe.com website (despite reading the many web blogs that discuss how to wring a ticket out of it), we gave up and booked our trip through travelocity.  That worked like a charm.  The train was as beautiful as we were led to expect -- clearly their huge taxes are going somewhere. The train was smooth, comfortable and on time.Madrid's Atocha station IS huge -- more like an airport than a train station. But we found information booths everywhere and had no difficultly finding our way (we needed to find the luggage lockers, which are fantastic by the way).But we found one amusing indication of how screwed up renfe is regarding on-line booking.  We found a mysterious (I think regional) train that seemed to meet our needs by leaving from Atocha rather than from Chamartin, but couldn't book that on travelocity. So we went to the information desk and the man there found the train and even printed out the schedule and train number for us to take to the ticket window.  When we got there, the ticket seller couldn't find the train and couldn't give us a ticket for it. Apparently they use the same website !  We ended up with a different solution.

I read the Frommers forum regarding Renfe three months prior to our trip to Madrid.  I secured two seats in tourist class on the internet site from Madrid to Cordoba on Renfe's AVE train (fast train) for 27 euro each. (full price at 68 euro).  We chose not to purchase return tickets because we were sleeping over in Cordoba for one night and didn't know what time we would feel like leaving to head back to Madrid the following day.   We spoke with the concierge in Madrid prior to our trip and he assured us that since there are trains every hour heading back we would have no trouble securing tickets.  He was WRONG.    We had the concierge in Cordoba (Hospes Palacio de Baillo) call a travel agent for the following days travel and all the trains in the afternoon were booked in tourist class, except single seats.  We ended up having to purchase preference seats (business) for 127 euros each, plus a 10% fee for the travel agent. While its true you get food service (it looks like a frozen dinner defrosted) we passed on the offering and only accepted drinks.  The menus offering included drink service (wine, beer, beverages: sodas, waters etc), juices, apertifs, brandy and spirits):  they had hors d'oeuvre (gazpacho); starter(smoked salmon salad);main dish(chicken breast w potatoes and spinach);desert (camembert). Also rolls, tomato spread; and finished with coffee, herbal teas, chocolate.   It was a good experience to travel preference service but we think everyone should know the importance of buying tickets ahead. You decide. Knowledge is power.  The ticket sellers at both the Atocha stattion and the Chemartin station do not know (or pretend not to know) how to speak English and they are clearly just out and out unfriendly.   We took the fast train to Toledo and Segovia traveling tourist class.  Every car, whether tourist or preference, has luggage racks at the ends of the car as well as overhead racks for smaller bags.  There is  good leg room and reclining seats.  We watched English movies with Spanish subtitles which was fun (they give you ear buds for free).  Tourist class was perfect for us.Do not be late for your train. Besides  one train to Cordoba which was 30 minutes late on arrival, every other train pulled into the station fifteen minutes before departure and left exactly on the minute of departure.The bathrooms on the train are clean , if small.You get specific seats for travel as well as which coach your seat is in.There is one four seater in each car of tourist class(four seats facing each other) that we think costs less money.  If you don't mind staring at strangers for the time you're on the train, go for it. We preferred not doing that, but the unfriendly ticket seller put us in those seats to Segovia from Madrid. Luckily, the ride was only thirty minutes.We would choose to spend more to have two regular seats, facing the way the train is traveling. But that's just us.  We wish we would have known about this before our travels, which is why I am including this information.The trains are immaculate and a wonderful way to travel through Spain.  Have fun.

Apart from the difficult time getting tickets on line from RENFE's web site (there is a good article about the subject here in TripAdvisor) and one rude RENFE staff at the station in San Sebastian things went well .We traveled in Preferente ( business class) which entitles you to a meal (a good breakfast since it was an A.M train) newspaper & magazine and you get to choose your seat. Preferente also has 3 seats abreast ( 2-1 configuration ) We will be taking the same train this year although this time we were luckier and found a less expensive fare ( about 38 euros less per adult ) . The train (Alvia) is fairly punctual and makes very short stops. Seats are comfy and there is a movie ( for children) .  The ride was fine and we arrived at Chamartin station on time . In a few years ( if they do not cut the funds) the service should be high speed (AVE) . There is also a nice cafe on board were you can purchase sandwiches ,drinks and coffee.No wi-fi yet on this train .Bathrooms are clean and modern ( unlike AMTRAK in USA)
It is located in the center of Algeciras, you have a taxi rank right at the exit. The bad thing is that the cafeteria is not in operation.

I admit that when I first visited the website at www.renfe.es I struggled. However, once the page settings are changed to translate to English, all becomes clear. Their website is easy to navigate with a simple from and to drop down boxes. Along with one way and return options you just choose how many passengers and up come your results. The earlier you book the tickets the cheaper they are. I also think that in summer the prices are slightly higher due to demand. You get to choose between standard and first class. Trust me when I say their version of first class and standard is VERY different from the UK version. I paid €43 per person for a first class ticket and I booked approximately 2 months ahead. The same tickets I had purchased online would have been nearly €100 each of brought at the station. The website can give up to 60% discount for booking online. The price also varies according to whether you are a child/Senior Citizen or hold a Spanish rail card. The website also has an offers section and it is always worth checking this out to see if you can get a deal on the fare you are looking for. The tickets are then emailed to you as a PDF file and you can just print your tickets out when it suits you. Overall the website is easy to navigate around, although the only thing I struggled with was the fact that I couldn’t find a map of the train routes on their website, although one can be found by using Google.There are actually two main stations in Madrid. One is Atocha and the other is Chamartín. Atocha is the biggest station in Madrid and is the primary station serving both commuter and high speed trains. Don’t forget that in Madrid the easiest mode of transport (in my opinion) is the Metro and wherever you stay in Madrid, Atocha will only be a few Metro stops away. The station itself is huge and is more like a cross between a station and a shopping mall. There are also plenty of places to eat and drink. The first time we went to the station it was a little bit daunting as there seemed to be so many different areas to the station depending on where you were going. Luckily for us Renfe have a very large Customer Services area where we enquired and were kindly walked to where we had to board the train. It is almost like a check in desk at the airport where they check your ticket and direct you towards where you depart. Once down the escalators it is simple as there are 4 or 5 similar looking check in desks all positioned just next to a set of escalators which all lead to a specific platform. Be warned though, they only let you on to the platform around 10 minutes before the train pulls into the station. All of the staff we came across were incredibly helpful and we found our way around easily. All of the departure and arrival boards are in clear view (seemingly everywhere), but just ensure you give yourself enough time to work out where you need to go as the station is very big.Unfortunately for my husband I was panicking and insisted that we arrive at the station early. We had therefore been hanging around for over an hour and all we wanted to do was to get settled on the train. Once we showed our tickets we made our way down to the platform expecting to wait a while. No sooner had I set my bag on the floor, the train was pulling in; and a very nice train it was too. I was very unused to the promptness of the train (being a London commuter you expect bad service permanently when it comes to transport), and found myself smiling at the ease of the journey already. None of that boarding in a massive queue where everybody piles on and the stresses of trying to find somewhere to put your bags once you board. The people on the platform all waited very calmly and the Spanish men were very insistent that the 3 or 4 women waiting boarded first. The train has two doors to each carriage making it really easy to board. As we had booked 1st class seats we figured we would be near the front of the train and were grateful that we had boarded in the correct place the first attempt.Once I stepped on the train I had to remind myself that this was a train and not a fancy first class cabin on an aeroplane. The first and second carriages were first class and there were only 12 seats to each carriage. There were 4 single seats to the left one behind the other and then 4 rows of double seats to the right. When I say seat I am not really doing it justice. The seats are almost like armchairs they are so big. We had actually picked seats when we booked our ticket and we had the last two seats at the back on the right. Directly behind our seats were two huge luggage carriers. Once I had placed my weary backside on the seat I almost felt like curling up with a hot cuppa it was so comfortable. The footrest that is on the back of the seat on front was so far I couldn’t reach it. Tall people (and by tall I mean over 6 foot) would have no problems on these trains with regards to leg room. There were only 4 other passengers in our carriage so it was very quiet and before we knew it the train was going. None of that irritating beeping before the doors close, the train just glides away almost as stylish as the city itself. I was almost shocked to realise we were on the move as the ride was as smooth as silk. The train doesn’t take long to build up speed but at no point did it feel like we were going that fast. Around 5 minutes into the journey a man appeared with a trolley. I assumed that you had the opportunity to buy a paper (Spanish of course) but was surprised to realise this was a free service. My husband suddenly decided that he was an expert and claimed that he believed we would be getting food and drink on the journey too. Of course I told him he was a fool and that no one in their right mind could expect a first class seat on a beautiful train AND free food and drink for less than £50.The rest of the train was just as nice and upon our little wander up and down we realised that standard class is lovely too with spacious seats (although a few more per carriage). The train also has a carriage with a buffet type shop where you can buy snacks and drinks. Toilets are situated in every other carriage and there are rakes of luggage compartments. Renfe have sensibly opted to put luggage racks floor to ceiling at one end of the carriage instead of above people’s heads.About ten minutes into the journey two rather dapper looking men walked a trolley into the carriage and starting speaking rapid Spanish to other passengers. When they got to us I glared at the hubby (to convey how wrong he was, clearly these people had paid extra) and he smugly looked back at me as the men seamlessly asked in perfect English, “would you like Tea or Coffee with your food”. They then proceeded to give us tea with our tray of food. The food consisted of a bowl of fresh fruit, a small portion of couscous, some cheese and butter with a cracker and a hot meal. The meal that we had was chicken in almond sauce. Not only was the meal double the size and treble the quality of similar aeroplane food, but we also then received a choice of breads and drinks to finish off with. Never before have I been so surprised that we paid such a great price to receive such a wonderful service. In addition to the food, we received headphones for the television which showed a film en route (Spanish speaking), we also received hot towels after our meal and they had cleaned the cabin within minutes of everybody finishing their meal. When it comes to price and service with rail travel the Spanish are right on the money!After we had eaten we spent nearly an hour looking at the beautiful Spanish countryside. The train ride is smooth nearly the whole way and you never feel like you are on a bumpy railway track. The only time you notice the fact you are on a train is when the train nears the end of the Madrid-Alicante route. On the approach to Alicante the train actually stops at two stations before its final destination. Due to this the train has to slow considerably and you then realise that the journey is a lot smoother the faster you go. The train arrived into Alicante station around 2 minutes early. We grabbed our bags and exited the train as civilly as we had boarded. I couldn’t believe that we had been on the train as long as 3 and a half hours. I got off the train feeling totally relaxed and couldn’t believe that the journey had been as easy as it had been.I can honestly say that I cannot think of any negatives relating to the price, service or journey itself. The only negative was a personal one, which was that my Spanish is not up to scratch and communication is made a lot harder when you can’t speak the language. Having said that the staff that we came across did the best they could and we managed with their broken English and my broken Spanish to get to where we needed to be.Why fly when you can catch a train? Since the Madrid train journey my husband and I have been looking into train travel all the way from London to Southern Spain. Unfortunately Renfe is in Spain only and not all routes are as fast as the one we took and if we were to do the whole thing from London it would be a 24 hour trip. I would have no hesitation in using Renfe again and think that my journey was a lot less stressful than flying. It was fantastic value for money and an enjoyable trip. I cannot recommend this enough, if you are in Spain and want to travel around to different areas check out Renfe, it’s amazing!

The route used to go a few hundred meters further to the ferry port, but now you have to cover this part on foot. Nevertheless, it is no problem at all to switch from train to ferry or vice versa. Train station, only to pick up or take travelers, not even the cafeteria deserves praise. Clean, tidy. Friendly lockers and staff

A mini AVE (TGV in French) which takes you across Andalusia diagonally from Granada to Algeciras, or the other way around, through sumptuous and varied landscapes that the roads do not necessarily offer. Sierras, the vega (fertile plain) of Antequera, gorges (Guadiaro for example), vast and magnificent valleys, a whole range of Andalusian landscapes right up to the seaside. The train offers an automatic distribution service for drinks, sweets and sandwiches (make sure it is not empty). If you make the entire journey, the best is to sleep in one of the 2 arrival towns. If not, you can leave from ANTEQUERA or RONDA, for example, two small towns to visit, or from another place. The leaflet you can take at a station will detail all the stops so you can organize yourself. The journey between the two cities takes 4 hours. Don't sit near the engine so as not to get the smell of diesel when you open the doors. If you like the train, beautiful landscapes and not having to drive for a day or two, this is a very nice excursion to do in whole or in part. A good experience. A foreigner will need their passport to enter the train station. There are no tickets issued, just a reservation done online. All you need to know is train number, date, time. When you get into train station, there is a massive sign board with Chinese and English. Once you find the gate, you will scan passport at gate and will get carriage and seat number. All is well organised and perfectly on time. You can board 15 minutes before train leaves

At the station, your ID will be checked and your baggage will be inspected. It can get quite crowded depending on the time of year, so it's best to arrive early. After completing the baggage inspection, there will be an electronic bulletin board, so you will need to look for the passenger compartment of the train you are boarding. Then, wait for the display to become a check. It's not like you can go to your home anytime like in Japan. If you are a foreign tourist, you will pass through an artificial passageway and present your passport. The ticket gates close a few minutes before departure time.

During our recent trip to Shanghai, which we also took the highspeed train from Shanghai to Yiwu and we came by this station to catch the train.The station was already full of people when we arrived slightly before 7am (we took the metro from People's Park station to here and that took about 30mins). The station was huge, covering several storeys with eateries, convenience stores and fast food restaurants around. As usual, before entering, all passengers needed to have their carrierbags scanned (same as those in the metro stations too). As we have booked our train tickets in advance, we just needed to have our passports scanned, quite convenient.Thereafter, we proceeded to the respective gate to board the train. But there's no use arriving early because the staff would only open the gate about 10~15mins before the train departure time. But passengers started queuing prior to that. Imagine the massive number of passengers queuing and entering the gate via scanning of identity cards or passports, one will need to run after passing the gate to go down to the platform and enter the right compartment of the train. This is important as some train compartments are not "interlinked" (because the train heads are facing each other), so do make sure you enter the right one. Luckily for us, reading Chinese words is a breeze for us and so it's quite straightforward.And the gate closed 3 mins before the train departure (and it leaves on time) and so it's quite a rush kind of thing. But once you sat down at the seat, it's quite ok.It's good to skip the morning/evening peak hours and you should be fine.

very large airport transit place to get lost easily than you must pay attention to the post and keep the ears on any word s of the avouchment

Once through security (quickly). we found a huge waiting room where we waited near our gate. It was opened 20 minutes before our train and we quickly found out seat on the train. It is also well sign-posted in English.

The inside looks just like the Japanese Shinkansen, or rather, it's a complete rip-off. It's a pain to ride. Just follow the signs, don't let the amount of people and size of the station to overwhelm you. arrive with enough time and keep calm. Not all the metro ticket machines accept cash, just look for the one that will take it and click at the top right to change the language to English. American credit cards are not accepted. Keep in mind that in this metro station the ramp may not have the same line in two opposite directions, the same ramp may have two different lines (i.e. line 2 west is not on the same ramp as line 2 east).

I take the high speed train from Shanghai to Beijing.  The trip is about 4 hours and 20 minutes.  Much easier and cheaper than air travel and the Hongqiao station is a great place to start the trip.  Very new, very clean and the staff is very helpful.  I have made the trip several times and I highly recommend it. But you can go almost anywhere in China from this station.  Next to the airport.  And hotels and shopping and other modes of transportation are right there.

This is a new train station, and it is HUGE. It is very cavernous and difficult to find your way to your gate due to the huge number of people crowded and pushing their way thru this station. There is very little assistance, and virtually no one speaks English. We found it challenging. However, taking the bullet train at over 200km/hour was AWESOME!

This station is fantastic, easy to navigate, has places to grab a bite to eat. The high speed train service has become so easy to use that i travel to the interior almost always now by this method. I took customers on this trip from Shanghai to Yiwu and we rode in style and were there in 2 hours.
We went to visit the city of Hangzhou for a couple of days and took the fast train, everything was very well organized
very convenient to go to Suzhou independently. fast, cheap, and easy to remember your passports.

large station People travel a lot. It's big, modern, and the bathrooms are very modern. There is a train connection into the city. Or you can go to the stadium. Outside there is a bus that can go. I feel very comfortable.

I have used Wuxi-Shanghai a few times and it is cheap and fast. Foreigners can board after purchasing a ticket and using their passport, not the ticket, as their boarding pass, and go to the entrance where a staff member is standing to check their passport. (In this case, the line was short, so they were able to get in rather quickly.) At night, six people sit in the sleeper compartment, but there are no chairs, so it is uncomfortable.
with access to long distance buseslots of places to eat herehas automated ticket boothsnear a metro line station

I had a hard time getting a Shinkansen ticket. Foreigners cannot purchase tickets from vending machines, so we first have to find a ticket office. The sales floor was on the first floor of the building across the street from Police Box in Shanghai Station South Square. There were so many people in line that I initially lined up at number 13 (cash), but I was told that foreigners were lined up at number 3. I immediately re-lined and secured a first class seat for the round trip. 120 yuan round trip. It took 30 minutes, but I was able to move comfortably. It was surprisingly quiet. In Suzhou, we strolled around Tiger Hill, Beigan Temple, and Guanqian Street.

I had no trouble finding the railway station which was connected to Line 2, a long (90 minute) but one-line subway ride from Pudong Airport. Once inside, I found the ticket windows easily.  If you are a foreign tourist, you cannot use the automatic ticketing machines.  I didn't see a specific ticket window for English speakers, but I had no problem communicating with the official.  You do need to provide your passport and your visa to buy a ticket.  Once I had my ticket, I found the gate quickly.  It's pretty easy to see where your seat is, even though the ticket doesn't specify "car" and "seat" in English.  Even in this huge station during a holiday period, it took less than an hour from when I got off the subway until I had my seat on the outgoing train.

This is a very large train station with many levels, entrances and concessions. You can easily get lost if you don’t know what level to go to. If you are going to meet someone you should be very specific about where to meet or you may both be at the place you believe is correct but the level is wrong!

Took a while to get in to the Station as they were only letting a few people at a time and then checking them for something by swabbing them. However once in we picked up our pre booked tickets really quickly there were no queues. We were really early incase there were queues so we made out way to get some food and drink. This is all upstairs and there are plenty of options both local and western. There are some shops to look around and many toilets. The Station is clean and modern.
Very well laid out.   Lots of people.   Lots of access to many VFT that all travel over 200kph.   The station was very clean.   We had no trouble accessing our train.

We were there to catch bullet train from Shanghai to Hangzhou. It is a big station with lots of gates. You will need to be there early as it is quite confusing for visitors that are not familiar with how Chinese train station works. It is quite crowded too so its best to be there earlier. Saying how busy the station is, the cleanliness is still maintained very well. Would recommend.
Very far from everywhere, old building and the checking point is like a bad joke they really don't care if you cooperate with the checking just go inside and run for get in your train
For smokers, there are no smoking corners within the zone. Please smoke before entry or you will have to walk 10 mins to the other terminal for a puff.

Been through here many times. This time was during a national holiday so it was pretty busy. Plenty of food options and access to the Hongqiao Airport and shanghai subway lines 2 and 10. Close to several shopping malls and many hotels.  I absolutely love the bullet trains operated by the CRH. Fast and sleek. I wish the USA had such fast trains.

Just a big station... Where to go, which platform - everything is clear... If you took a ticket on the Internet, then you need to exchange it for a paper one at the ticket office. You need a number and a passport.
Very organized for the amount of people coming through there everyday. Lot's of food shops while waiting on train. Special waiting hall for each train and monitors that guide you.
Huge station with thousands of people, organized like an airport. Despite the numbers it is perfectly organised.

I used it for part of the journey from the airport to the city. I believe it cost about 800 yen one way and the ride took about 7 minutes. Although I had covered 300km, it was a surprisingly safe and comfortable ride with almost no shaking. I heard later that it seems to be a German-made vehicle. I agree.
We got the bullet train from Beijing to Shanghai, such a cool way to travel and something a bit different!

I have recently used this train station on my monthly trips into Shanghai. It is connected to the Shanghai Hongqiao International Airport Terminal 2 and it is also connected to the Shanghai Metro Station lines 2 and 10. Line 10 goes to Shanghai Hongqiao International Airport Terminal 1 as well. Line 2 Does not serve the airport terminal 1, but is the primary link from Shanghai Hongqiao International Airport to Shanghai Pudong International Airport (90 metro train ride).
We arrived there from Xi’an by express train (305 km per hour). I think it's great that Hongquiao Airport is right next to it
Huge station, with multiple boarding gates like an airport. You must carry a passport to buy tickets and it is recommended to do so at the windows because the machines are only in Chinese

I used it to go to Suzhou. At Shanghai Hongqiao Station, there was a baggage inspection at the entrance of the station. Apparently there are different entrances for nationals and foreigners, and there was quite a line, so I showed my passport to the person at the front and asked, but he said no, so I didn't have to waste any time. The system is easy to understand, but I had to wait in line for about 30 minutes to get my ticket, so it can be frustrating if it's your first time. Even among Chinese people, if you were in a hurry, you could ask someone in line to let you in first. I was surprised that there was such a compromise.

Big spacious building for departures and arrival trains 🚞 .  Connected to airport and you just walk few hundred meters inside. Decent choices of fast foods or local restaurants. Airport, railway station 🚉 and metro 🚇 are very well connected

A station which has the dimensions of a large airport, lots of travelers especially since it is adjacent to the airport of the same name which discharges internal travelers. Well equipped and above all well organized. We did the Beijing-Shanghai TGV in 4h30, it's a marvel.
We were most impressed by the efficiency and cleanliness of the railway station.  After taking a fast train from Bejing to Shanghi, we appreciated the speed that everything was handled.

The directions to find the departures are not very clear, but given how large the station is, it is easy to get around. Ask the many people who work there for directions. Like every Chinese station, it has metal detector checks at the entrance and then the various gates that lead to the platforms which can only be accessed with a ticket. Excellently connected to the metro of which it is a station.

Visiting the Shanghai Hongqiao railway station is efficient and for the amount of people moving through the area is a wonder in itself!  Subway or fast speed trains Hongqiao will get you to you're destination!
Station perfectly organized and tidy. Trains punctual and cheap. Truly a great experience.

Shanghai's large train stations, which have many high-speed trains, have many VIP lounges. The VIP lounge I used in Guangfa is a little better than the hard seats outside. For a train station, it is pretty good.
Efficiency because you can reach infinite destinations in a short time at low costs. Convenience due to the location, close to the city center and obviously with the subway available.

The Shanghai Hongqiao Railway Station is really big and right next to the Hongqiao Airport. It’s really advanced and has all kinds of trains at all times (slow trains and fast trains). The ticket system is also pretty great because you can either get a ticket there or get it before on wechat and just go there to pick it up. Very convenient for traveling inside China!

This is a massive train station.  It is attached to the Hongqiao Airport as well.  There are plenty of places to eat at the station, and people can even buy food there to take it on the train with them.  It is also big enough to get lost so please make sure to have specific points to meet up if you are travelling in groups like we did.

It is a truly enormous high-speed rail station. Fortunately... I brought my passport with me and was able to enter. I remember that it was difficult to enter Shenzhen without a train ticket. When I said I came here to see off a friend, they let me in after looking at my passport.
Amazing... huge train station. Very clean, very organized. Trains on time like Swiss clockwork. Ok, you shouldn't be afraid of crowds. Ads also in English

It was my first China’s railway station after 10 years and I must admit their development progress all these years to cater the gigantic population. This railway is very big from one end to another. I almost felt I don’t want to walk back after I reach the end of the other side. It is also a very busy station, full of people very time. I am not quite use to the security screen for domestic station, but got to adapt to it. The arrival hall also very busy. They crowd control is doing its best to cater for the gigantic people river. Passenger (me) just need to be more patience. Although they have walk in ticket counters, but majority of the passengers bought their ticket online and print out at the machines there. They are pathway link to the nearest shopping mall.

This is an important transportation hub, and high-speed trains to Hangzhou and Suzhou are also available here. However, it is a bit far from the city center, so you need to allow enough time to get to this station.
Very modern, well thought-out train station. Right next to the airport (T2). You can take the metro to T1.

This train station is run effectively. Train departure times are respected without any delay, despite the large number of people who use this terminal daily.  The spectacular bullet train. You don't even feel it. In 1 hr we arrived at our destination. Highly recommended.

The subway station is located on the underground floor on the west side of Shanghai Hongqiao Station. Passengers can take Shanghai Rail Transit Line 2 and Shanghai Rail Transit Line 10. After arriving at the station, they will reach the B1 floor after exiting the subway station. Take the escalator to the waiting hall on the 2F departure floor to buy tickets and wait. The station waiting hall covers an area of ​​about 11,340 square meters. The waiting hall is a fully open space. After entering the station hall, you can wait in the waiting area, go shopping in shops or visit the sightseeing platform. The ticket gates are mainly arranged on both sides of the waiting hall. The electronic screen above the ticket gate displays the train name and driving time. Passengers can choose the corresponding ticket gate to wait for the nearest train based on the information on the ticket.
Huge railway station with all required amenities. Best part is their food court. Ample veg & non veg restaurants to chose from. Probably one of the best stations so far.

I use the high speed train service very often.This is the largest station I have used in China to date with 30 platforms. However, this does mean that you have to arrive in good time to get through the security checks as they are always busy. And if you need to collect your tickets from the ticket office give yourself an hour before your departure time. Tip: if you need to pick up tickets, go to the special turnstile at the entrance and show your passport. So that you can enter the station to pick up your ticket(s) which you will need your receipt and passport. Hope you find this review helpful. Dominic

All signage (as all of SH transportation) is very clearly labeled - but the place is the size of a village. The first time, come at least 1 hr before departure to file through security scans, passport + ticket control + find your waiting room. The train ticket can be purchased online + sent to your hotel. Short notice bookings can be picked up at a ticket window in (any) train station, Just bring email confirmation # + passport (You need a passport to travel). I waited about 30 min at the only 'English language' ticket window. So come early or pick them up the day before. Hongqiao is in the far west of SH, but you can pick up your ticket at the older, more central train station. Enjoy the ride (up to 350 km/h).

The location is convenient. The place is clean and spacious even though it always has hundreds of people, if not thousands.I like their different choices of cuisines. This is a place you don't feel bored on a trip.

shanghai is a big city has more than one airport and hongqiao is my preference as it is so near to the downtown with a few metro stops only, and also have the train station to reach more place near shanghai

This train station always reminds me of the airport and the hangar - there could easily be room for several A380s next to each other in the waiting hall... don't mess, mess! That's the motto in China! But everything is organized very well and efficiently (like the entire train network in China... except for picking up tickets). I like to go via Hongqiao.

Very big, like an airport and same control before to get it. Is directly connected to the local airport just next to them. The station is connected with metro, and by subway you can easily reach the international airport. Just 7-10¥.

My first experience riding a train was with Hongqiao Railway Station from Shanghai to Beijing on the bullet train.  It is best to buy your tickets in advance because once you're there it is like going through a whirlwind.  It is not necessarily foreign-friendly, so best keep a translator with you or brush up on some Mandarin.  Keep your eye out for the open doors for boarding because it is not announced.  There isn't a clear order of boarding.  Don't be late because the train leaves on time!  Once you're on the train it's smooth sailing.

It was conveniently located for my use. I have never seen so many high speed trains in one area. This place is amazing, beautiful, and Chinese massive. The Chinese build so many things to be the world’s best. This is another example.
Beautiful station! From here you will take the fastest train in the world to go Shanghai-Beijing in 4 1/2 hours for 1300 km. Station and trains are very clean!

I had no idea what to expect until we got here. It is massive and incredibly well designed. There is no getting away from the crowds and crowds of people. But the logistics of the place we incredibly well designed.

I took the train from Shanghai to Suzhou at 20:00. It was a good trip from the airport to Shanghai Station, where I transferred to the Linear and then the subway, but I couldn't find the ticket office for the high-speed rail, so I wasted 30 minutes walking back and forth in front of the station, never realizing it was on the other side of the road. Naturally, I couldn't use Visa or Master cards, so I had to use cash, and since my English was poor, I showed them my destination on my phone and bought it. The station has the image of an airport for domestic flights, the entrance to the station building, security at the ticket gate, and waiting at the gate before going down to the platform. The train was almost full.

More people, more people, more people! Shanghai Hongqiao Station has abundant station and train commerce. In short, in addition to taking a ride here, you can also buy and buy!
Big terminal for trains, fast moving, clean and convenient! One of the best railway station in Asia and the world.

Not exactly a tourist spot. Very functional. Many entrances all leading to security checks like at airports. Connected underneath to the Shanghai Hongqiao Airport so very convenient for interline transfers. Bilingual signage as well as announcements.Very very organized as far as queuing up for your train. Probably close to 30 gates and all paired off and on both sides of the concourse.  Electronic signs above the paired gates list what trains depart from them. There are turnstiles in which you insert your ticket, much like the subway system there, and it comes back out. You take it and the gate opens and off you go up the escalator. Those signs also specify which train cars stop at that or the opposite gate so you will know which way to enter. BTW,make sure you are on the platform in the correct area for your assigned car or be ready to run.Food concourse upstairs from which the overview pic was taken.I paid extra for business class seating since I was on vacation.  Soooo nice. No crowd and the seat was much better than any domestic first class US airline seat. It was about RMB300 to get to my destination. About USD45.

Inbound traffic just to drop off can be a nightmare.  Getting a ticket often takes 15 to 20 minutes at peak times ( and I still have not found off-peak times!)Often crowded, there are still plenty of places to grab a bite or a tea or coffee. China’s rail system is amazing!

Now that you can make reservations online, it has become much more convenient, but foreigners still have to line up at a manned counter to receive their tickets at the station. Chinese people can use automatic ticket machines, but foreign passports are not supported. Even though there are many automatic ticket machines, for some reason many Chinese people line up at the manned counters, so it is always crowded. If you are issuing tickets inside the station, it is safer to allow at least 30 minutes for waiting in line for pick-up. Immediately after online reservations started operating, there was a pick-up counter exclusively for foreigners, but that is no longer the case. You will also need to show your passport when entering the station premises. Again, Chinese people can pass through the automatic machine using their ID, but foreigners have to go through a manned counter. There are agency sales offices located throughout the city. A ticketing fee of 5 yuan per ticket will be charged. Passport must be presented. As online reservations begin, the number of agent sales offices has decreased.

If you are into Railways stations this is a doozy its as huge as it is crowded. Serving both Intercity and Hongqiao International Airport. People travelling everywhere. Be prepared for longish queues for taxi's. They are frequent and there are many of them but the sheer weight of numbers in transit means there will be a reasonably fast moving but long queues
First of all, like the Korean High Speed ​​Rail, the platform is wide and the station layout is the same as the airport lobby. I was surprised that it didn't shake.

We took the bullet train from Shanghai to HangZhou. The train stations were very big and crowded. I would recommend to go earlier in view of the security checks and the long queues at the boarding gates.

We were told to be early and were afraid of getting lost. But if you have your ticket already it‘s super easy.When you arrive there is a passport and security check. Inside all tracks/gates leave from one big hall. All signage in English as well. Only shopping and restaurants are limited (for the biggest train station in asia). A lot of fast food.

China has amazing railway stations as well as amazing trains. The size of the stations are such that you should arrive and yourself (during non peak travel periods) at least half an hour before your train departs so you have time to pass station security and find your platform on the basis you already have your ticket. During peak travel period (CNY etc) allow significantly longer.

To be honest, I don't want to use it too much if possible. I'm tired by the time I get on it. Tickets can now be easily reserved and purchased in Japan, and there are no longer long lines to pick them up at the station at Shanghai Hongqiao on weekday mornings. You don't have to print out your reservation number (there is a screen where you can confirm your reservation number and name); just hand over your phone and passport and the ticket will be issued in about a minute. However, the change/cancellation line is more empty than the same-day ticket line. No matter which counter you use, we will help you, so if there is an empty line, please do not hesitate to line up. Depending on the train, there are trains with more first-class cars and others with mostly second-class cars, and the customer base is quite different. I don't know how to tell the difference yet, but from my experience, I feel that trains with faster travel times and trains departing from/bound from Beijing are mostly high-class cars. Also, since the difference in price is not that big, I recommend taking the first class car.
Pre bought tix ahead and just took conf number to ticket counter! Lot of people in many lines. Pretty easy to navigate.

I booked tickets with ChinaTour.Net which was simple online but don’t waste time looking for Internet Ticket Collection Window as this doesn’t exist, and ticket window will do (see photo). If you are picking up tickets for a return journey there is one ticket for each trip. They speak reasonable English at the counter, but there can be a long wait (30 minutes at 7am). The train number on the big screen will guide you to the correct platform.

China uses trains as a major form of transportation and this station is no exception.  It is busy, crowded and many people are moving in many different directions.  The bullet trains are quite comfortable in first class and the I have been told that the trains are always on time!

I wanted to take the ferry from Hong Kong to Zhuhai, and from Zhuhai to Shenzhen, take the China High Speed ​​Rail to conquer the Pearl River Delta by land, sea, and air, so I researched it and found out that there are two trains a day that go directly to Shenzhen, so I immediately booked business class on Trip.com. On the day of the event, there was a 40 minute queue at the ticket office. It says at the counter that the elderly, people with disabilities, military personnel, and people with business class reservations are given priority, but I was so scared that there was no way I could cross the line, so I reluctantly waited in line for 40 minutes, handed over the ticket slip and passport that I had printed out in advance, and the ticket was issued in just a few seconds. It is a promise of Chinese railways that you can check your baggage as usual, go through ticket gates in advance, and be able to get on the platform more than 10 minutes early. Business class, which takes up about half of one car, is a separate space behind automatic doors. The older sister of the crew doesn't speak English, but if you do your best, she'll bring you something. The alignment may not be very good, but I'm driving intermittently between 200km and 100km, but of course the seat is completely flat, so it's comfortable, and I'm thrilled to be able to lie down on the Shinkansen. On the way, there is a 25-minute stop at Guangzhou South Railway Station, a mega station where bullet trains of various shapes are constantly arriving, reminding me of Andromeda Station on the 999. I thought it was strange that 25 minutes was a very long stop, but then the older sister of the crew slowly asked me to take a seat, so I stood up, and with practiced ease, the train spun around, and from there we headed for Shenzhen via switchbacks. We arrived at Shenzhen North in about an hour from here, and the time flew by. At 6,400 yen including water, sweets, and lunch, it's probably more cost-effective than Super View Odoriko's Green, so be sure to give it a try when touring Hong Kong, Zhuhai, Guangzhou, and Shenzhen.

Railway in china? Always good .. I always go for first class (which is cheaper than business class) so no experience with second class but I’d say never book business class .. you just pay extra and nothing special I’ve tried it once and i actually regret it because tickets are already very expensive and not worth the extra cost

We took a day tour to Nanjing which included transfer from Shanghai by bullet train.  Our guide and driver picked us up at our hotel, drove us to the station, and the guide accompanied us on the train.  When we booked the tour our passport information was required for her to purchase our tickets.  Upon arrival at the station we had to walk to a far end of the station, just to walk back, as there are barriers across the front - to avoid congestion at the doors.  We had to show our passports and clear security, to include putting our bags through X-ray.  Once we located our waiting area we couldn’t find two, much less three, seats together.  There were places to purchase food, as well as restrooms.  When it was time to board it was like a sea of humanity moving forward.  While it was crowded there was no pushing or shoving.  We had reserved seats and were able to find them quickly.  The train was clean, and I saw a lady cleaning the floor after leaving each station.  There were outlets so we could charge our phones during our journey.  The ride was smooth and was a great way to get to/from Nanjing.  Too bad we don’t have this type of transportation in the US!
If possible, we recommend purchasing tickets in advance. They sell out easily, and be sure to go to the station with plenty of time to exchange for a physical ticket.

To say that the fast train network in China is amazing is an under statement.  China is leading the world in so many things. Their high speed adoption of high speed rail is an example to us all. In Australia we have been taking the need for this for at least 20 years. We are still 20 plus years away from even a train between our to major cities  Sydney and Melbourne. Meanwhile China has built more hight speed rail than the rest of the world put together.We had to go to Suzhou by car on arrival in Shanghai, took almost two hours, returning to Shanghai we took the train, we were there in 20mins in comforts and saved up to 1 hour and 40 minutes. Cost is so cheap.

China’s high speed rail is amazing, clean and convenient. The only inconvenience is the purchasing and obtaining of tickets. As business travelers, we had our tickets purchased by our local counterparts. We knew we had to collect our tickets at the station, same as all other local train passengers. What we didn’t know was foreign travelers can’t collect tickets at the machines and only at counters. If you’re leaving Shanghai early in the morning, ie before counters are open at 8.30am, you’ll have to collect your tickets a day before at any of the ticket collection counters, or head to the South Gate on the morning of the departure because the north gate counters are closed.

There are many self-service ticket buying and dispensing machines at the entrance of this train station, but they can only be used by people with mainland residence permits/ID cards. My friend and I only hold hometown return permits and cannot use the self-service ticket machines or self-service gates to enter the station. You can only enter the station by using the staff passage next to the station entrance, where the staff will check your home return permit.
A great train service and clean. Station very large. Unfortunately not much English spoke. So need a translator if you do not speak Chinese to get tickets and find your way around

Oh the trains here are far better than the ones we have in England. Travelled on the bullet train from here to Xian. A total of 7.5 hours. So comfortable with plenty of leg room. Cleaners are constantly spraying and mopping the carriage floor and collect rubbish every half an hour. They are spotlessly clean and no overcrowding. Never seen a train station like this one but then again it is the largest in Asia. It really does put our stations to shame. Large beautifully clean tiled platforms and everywhere just smacks of spaciousness.

this has to be one of if not the most impressive train stations there is, it just huge, with airport checkin stations, baggage areas, goodness know how many restaurants and shops, 100s for sure. this is a train, metro station to be seen, even if you are not using the Metro

You can cover a distance of over 60 minutes by riding a regular train in just 20 minutes :-) One thing to note is that there are some stations where there is no Cao Tier, a high-speed train. Although the Cao Tieh station is small, the platform is simple and easy to board. Hongqiao Station, Shanghai Station, and Suzhou Station are the size of an airport and have over 30 platforms moving around, so they are always crowded and crowded. If you are considering traveling to nearby cities such as Hangzhou or Nanjing, we recommend the high-speed train. It feels like going from Seoul to Cheonan Asan Station or Daejeon.

It takes 1 hour from Wuxi Station to Shanghai Station. Booking second class is cheap at around 1000 yen in Japanese yen. Unreserved seating may be a little difficult for business travelers. I had a Chinese acquaintance ask me for a ticket at the counter, but since the counter didn't understand the language, I wasn't sure if I could do 100% of what I wanted. The inside of the train is almost the same as the Japanese Shinkansen.

Used at Beijing-Shanhaiguan and Beijing-Tianjin. The time is accurate. Ride comfort is also good. The same thing happened when I used Shanghai-Suzhou in 2011. However, on this round trip to Shanhaiguan Station, the front of Shanhaiguan Station was under renovation, and the only entrance on the return trip was the south exit on the other side of the tracks, so I had to take a taxi from the front (north side) to get there. The ticket exchange counter at Beijing Station is on the far right as you face the building.

Hard to buy tickets online so we went a few days before our trip and bought our tickets.  Travelled in first class which is one step up from economy and one step below business class.  Worth the extra few dollars. Leaves on time and you need to get to the station early to get through security etc which is time consuming. you can buy food onboard but we took our own lunch and water as most of the food offered was not to my vegetarian taste. Very efficient, clean and really really fast ! average 350k's per hour.

The station is huge and a little overwhelming so when I’m doubt visit the big round information desks in the middle. Someone there usually speaks English.

Travelled to Hangzhou using this station. As a foreigner, I had to show my passport and ticket to gain entrance to the station. After the baggage security check, I used my train number to find my platform. Struggled to find a seat but that wasn't really an issue. There are also several eateries inside where you can buy food for your journey.
Fabulous integrated hub. High speed trains a great way to travel. Fast, economical and on time. UK take note!!

One of the two major train stations in Shanghai. Since we live in Shanghai, we go there often. The size is gigantic, and the punctuality of the trains in China is unmatched. For those who don't know it, similar to the airport. As a foreigner, you can only enter the train station with a passport and a valid ticket. Of course with security checks. Once inside, you find yourself in a huge hall. You go to the waiting area on the platform, but you can only get on the platform about 10 minutes before the train leaves. Everything well structured.

After you get through security, just look for your departure gate. 1st class is not a lot more than second class (go Business Class for a real treat).Trains are clean, comfortable and very punctual.I was doing speed calculations, and I think we topped out at 193mph.You can order food in advance and it will be delivered to you.When in the station take a look around the little shops. I found the must have fridge magnets at a very reasonable cost.

The only place that trains must pass through is Hongqiao Railway Station, where all kinds of people come and go. You often have to wait for a table in the VIP lounge. There was quite a lot to eat. Alipay and WeChat payment are supported. Transportation is also convenient. Metro lines 2 and 10 are both there. There are also many buses. Close to the Convention and Exhibition Center. The hotel accommodation was also good.

We came by bullet train to Shanghai.  The very modern train station was very clean and very large!  It is worth seeing just to appreciate all that China is doing to make transportation easily accessible.

This train station is the only one I have ever seen. You can go through the security check first and then enter the station before buying the train ticket. This saves you from buying the ticket first and then going through the security check. It is much more convenient. In addition, there are ticket sales and ticket machines for people from Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan. As long as you buy the ticket at 12306, you can get the ticket without manual processing.

Our train booking provider suggested we arrive 3 hours before departure. In off peak times this is quite an over estimate. It took us about 40min to figure out how to enter the station, (without a ticket) collect our ticket and figure out which gate our train was leaving from. We then proceeded up up up the escalators to look down on the huge train terminal with all the tiny people walking below.  There are a few coffee/ food outlets like Costa up the top.When we finally got on the train we loved our business class seats, there is plenty of room for your luggage and the hostess brings you a drink and snack.

Hangzhou is part of our recent 4-city China trip. We wanted to experience China’s popular high speed train as an expeditious way to reach there. For us the best train station is Hongqiao. When booking tickets on line thru Travel China Guide we paid a fee for express delivery of the physical tickets to our hotel in Chengdu. A first class ticket with roomy assigned seat for the 100 plus miles trip cost a reasonable 117 RMB (less than US$20) per person. We flew from Chengdu to Shanghai Hongqiao Airport (SHA) which is connected to the cavernous, crowded Hongqiao train station with good directional signage. The upper floor of the station has many restaurants for food choices (and good places to wait). We found our gate 16B easily (B for train cars 1-4). Passengers started lining up at gate 15 minutes prior to departure time (annoying to see people still just cut in). We found out that our pink-colored tickets had to be handled manually by gate agent (similar to JR pass).  The hour-long ride was pleasant,  spoiled somewhat by some passengers talking loud talking on their cell phones. The train arrived in Hangzhou’s East Station, another huge station. Easy access to orderly taxi queue.
arrived here form beijing in the speed train good service and helpful staff clean and organisedwell kept
