A huge railway station that feels like an airport. Rigorous security check on this occasion three people, we got rid of hair spray, deoderant spray and shaving foam. when it was claimed that the containers were too large to be carried in the luggage. Once out on the clinically clean and polished stone platform, the hugely long express train was boarded which went at 365km/h. Awesome to rush forward at that speed. Felt stable and relaxing with comfortable seats and good service on board with both drinks and food. A pleasant experience that is recommended.

I had made a reservation online in advance, so I presented my passport and reception number at the counter. One of the tickets was defective due to a mistake on my part, but the woman at the counter was furious. I'm just disappointed in that attitude.
We used rail from Fuzhou to Shanghai and the ride was simple and perfect . Get first class tickets for a better experience. Love the massage chairs all over
58 platforms for high speed trains. Everyone is buying their ticket online. Trains are ponctuel despite the crowd. At >275 km/h, the coin can stand itself. Try it at your home train.

China's high-speed railways have been improved and become more convenient. It is easier and more convenient to travel to major cities in southeastern China by high-speed train from Shanghai Hongqiao Railway Station than by connecting planes. However, it is still inconvenient for foreigners to purchase tickets. Should I ask a local friend, buy it through a travel agency, or make a reservation on an online travel site? Either way, you will have to pick it up at a staffed counter, so it will take some time. Passengers with Chinese nationality can use their ID cards to issue tickets at automatic ticket vending machines, so I would like to see some form of arrangement in which foreigners can also receive tickets at automatic ticket vending machines after making online reservations. Additionally, when entering the station, there will be an ID check and a security check, so please arrive at the station with plenty of time to spare.
Awesome terminal. Right next to the airport terminal. Very convenient to go to any part of Shanghai. Transfer available internally. Trolleys too allowed. Very organised and neat.

Compared with Shanghai Railway Station, Hongqiao Railway Station is larger, with newer and better equipment, and more restaurants and shops. The station information is clear and clear, making it easy for passengers to find the correct station entrance.

Station to get a high speed train to go to WaterTowns. It’s better to book your high speed train online and pick up. If purchasing high speed train in this station better get here 1-2 hours ofyour desired train time especially on weekends.

Like other large-scale infrastructure projects in China, Shanghai Hongqiao Railway Station is extremely large. The railway network is also very strong, and you can basically reach all major cities from Hongqiao Station. But the software needs to be improved, both for staff and passengers.

I used it when I went to Guilin on a tour. I took a tour bus from Guangzhou Baiyun Airport for about 1 hour and 30 minutes, then took a high-speed train from Guangzhou South Station to Guilin North Station for 2 hours and 30 minutes. It's a 2nd class car. There were 5 seats per row, 2 seats on the right side and 3 seats on the left side. I think it cost about 2000 yen to ride for such a long time. The speed was about 250km. Along the way, vendors will come to sell drinks and sweets. Everyone other than the tour guests are Chinese people, and it's very lively with people talking on their cell phones, loudly talking to each other, and snoring loudly. Earplugs and eye masks can be helpful. The ride comfort is no different from the Shinkansen. However, just like at the airport, foreigners will need a passport to enter the station, and everyone will undergo a baggage check. The station is very spacious and lively. The toilets are also clean. You can't enter the platform until 10 minutes before the departure, so the campus is packed with people. There was a long line at the ticket gate at that time, but foreigners had a special priority lane and were able to enter easily.

If it's Golden Week in Japan, it's Labor Day in China as well, and there will be a four-day holiday starting May 1st. Public transportation gets crowded every year. You can read the timetables for high-speed trains, but if you search on trip.com, reservations for Labor Day have already started, and the time slots in question are already sold out.
We went to the Venice of China by high-speed train and this station has its reason. 30 high-speed tracks with clean and above all precise trains.

Modern high-tech type of transport. It connects almost the entire territory of China with its network. Speed ​​is 300 km/h. As a rule, it is used by local residents, like our electric trains. Like ours, people move from one city to another every day to and from work. Only the distance is 200 km, and the travel time is less than an hour. We used this type of transport for a trip to Hangzhou

I used it on a business trip to Changzhou city. I took a first class seat (green car in Japan) for about an hour from Shanghai Station to Changzhou Station. The seats are as spacious and comfortable as Japan's Shinkansen trains, and at 120 yuan (about 2,000 yen in Japanese yen), it is cost-effective. Please be careful about baggage inspection before boarding and places where you cannot enter the platform until 10 minutes before departure.

We took high speed train from Beijing to Shanghai and back through this station. The station was huge, right by Hongqiao airport. It was very hard to find exit of this train station. We had to wait in long line for taxi, subway were too crowded to take. Well, it took around 1.5 hour to get to pudong in a taxi. The station is too far away from puxi center and pudong center. Not easy to get to. That is the only complain I had. They have good food places, and gift shops, which is a plus.
Just like airport,  clean and clear. Travel made easy . The system made here handles huge public transportation so easily. Many eateries,  many shopping centers.  Everything managed well.
From there, we take the TGV to Beijing. Go there by metro to avoid traffic jams. Very clean and human-sized station, unlike the other station which serves Suzhou.
The view of the station from the 1st level is impressive, seeing this space with so many people. It's teeming everywhere

Really easy to get to with Line 2 and Line 17 - lots of trains going from here to different parts of China makes it easy for day trips. Lots of small restaurants and shops - inclusive of Starbucks and Family mart perfect for grabbing snacks before your trip.

It is very far. If you want to transfer to the high-speed train from Pudong Airport, it is better to go to Shanghai Railway Station. It is very far from Hongqiao Station, and you need to go around it constantly. It is very big.

One of the largest train stations in Shanghai. All departures are described there and we are also very close to HongCiao airport for domestic flights in the country like Hong Kong. Be careful, lots of ATMs, but not accessible in English, only Chinese. There is, however, a ticket counter inside the station, which is quite huge to navigate on 2 levels, separate departure and arrival.

Hongqiao railway station located approx 50 km of Pudong airport . There is metro line 2 from Pudong airport to Hongqiao railway station which incidentally is also located at Hongqiao airport. Hongqiao station has lot eateries both Chinese & wrstern

Traveling by train in China means getting new impressions and new experiences. The size of train stations is no less than the size of airports. But the navigation in them is not so detailed... Therefore, I recommend arriving at the station 2-3 hours before the train departs. This will help you not be late for the train! Sign language, a ticket in your hands, and the station staff (if you don’t speak Chinese) will help you understand which direction to board. All this requires patience and time...You also need to keep in mind that cutting and piercing objects will be taken away from you. They cannot be taken with you or placed in a suitcase. They will find you and take you away! Boarding the train begins 30-15 minutes before departure. There are a lot of people. Therefore, it is better to immediately choose the correct boarding side (the board will indicate the car numbers). The carriage numbers will also be indicated on the platform. This will help you quickly get into your car. Because trains arrive and depart strictly on schedule and no one will wait for you!  If anything, sit in any carriage of your train. You'll figure it out inside. I wish you a pleasant trip!

Shanghai Hongqiao station is near the airport and allows you to easily get into Shanghai CBD. The station is clean but can get a little busy. If you need some assistance many younger Chinese will speak some English and are almost always happy to assist. The high speed trains are great for long distance travel and there are shops in the station for you to buy food and drinks.

Very modern station. At the metro exit, ticket counters are available to collect tickets reserved online. On the 2nd floor, access to the platforms by very practical Escalator. Restaurant available on the top floors.
We had to use it twice, traveling by train to Beijing, a majestic station, with an impressive crowd and despite everything, perfectly organized.
This station is very modern and efficient signs are in English.  The down side is a lack of seating for the many passengers waiting for their train.
It has several metro lines, connecting with the bus and train lines. Organized, clean and has very good signage.

The train station is easily reached by subway. Feels like arriving at an airport and the train goes fast, almost like flying. We went to Beijing on Thursday with the Fu Xing train, they go at 350 km/h. Went second class one way and first class back. Both were comfortable.

This station is massive and doesn’t except foreign cards making it harder to get around. Alipay and wechat you need Chinese bank accounts to use so cash is the only option. Easy signs but just massive to navigate around.

As everything in China, it is Big place but if you have any sense of orientation should be easy, just follow the signs in Chinese and English.You have to pass security check point with your passport and got to reservation windows, get in line and wait for your turn, have to BE PATIENT, some people will try to rush and push, Don’t take it personal, is their culture and bad matters, just you have to take it, older and middle edge are the worst, get just to the spitting on the floor and the smell, cigarette, alcohol, bad breath or lack of higiene.Try to have your time and destination write in chine or have a translator application on your phone.If you go to the process and got your tickets. Double check the date and time of departure and return, they sold me a same day ticket went I was looking to travel 3 days latter,I got in line again and after 20 minutes they void the tickets and issue new ones, ( the old ones have to be canceled by a higher rank train official ) after that everything went smooth, I suggest to get the Firta class if is available and if you are doing a long way trip, you are getting a big 5 people cabin with a nice seat-Bed, a lot of space if you are bringing some suitcases, and the difference is maybe $5 to $20 more, it is worth it on your return to get some rest if you are doing a one day trip .I Left  the station follows the Exit and signs down to subway station to line number 2 back to downtown Shanghai.
We used this station a couple of times to go to Yiwu and Hanzhou. Always on time!We like the train station very much! Full of stores and restaurants and easy to follow instructions.

The railway station is operated in a similar manner to an airport in that there are security checks to go through. It does take time especially at busy times but it’s worth the peace of mind. The station is very clean with lots of shops and eateries. The bullet train is amazing, clean, modern and fast! Great experience!
Traveling by train in China is much better and easier than by plane. You can buy your ticket on the spot, it doesn't take long to board and the seats are very comfortable and spacious.

Awesome experience, not to be missed. Riding second class is still better than riding an airplane. I thought it was tight as the pictures said but when we got there, the leg room was pretty comfortable and at a cheaper price. No need to ride vip or first class. The people were mot so loud as well. But my mom wanted to ride vip and first class so we did at a higher price. Shanghai to Beijing had newer and faster trains that travels 350kph. Jinjiang to Hangzhou to Shanghai travels at 250kph.Vip tickets and elderly and with small kids are given priority boarding, a few minutes before the regular passengers are allowed to enter. Train stops at the stations are only 2-3 minutes for boarding and alighting. So you have to be quick. We missed our vip train because we didn't know about priority boarding. We took our time going in and failed to look at the clock. So we had to ride the next train on the dining car for 5 hours. My daughter was heart borken. But we had great bonding time with their grandma playing cards with them. So lesson learned, MIND THE TIME, BE QUICK.

I sometimes fly between Beijing and Shanghai. The distance is about the same as between Tokyo and Kagoshima. It will fly at a maximum speed of 350km. The only stop along the way is Nanjing. It's early.

I went to the station for the first time since I always travel by car but really getting to the Hongqiao station from shanghai library station was just perfectly convenient, direct, easy! Get the metro card and have a nice ride.

In China, the process is too complicated for foreigners to buy train tickets, and it takes half a day to go to the site and get the ticket. Ticket issuing machines are not available. After boarding the train, the child watches the smartphone at maximum volume, the grandmother raves about how good it is, and the child's father is loud again on the phone. Hmm~~ It takes a lot of time. To rise to the cultural level

Well...this is probably the best place to come to see that the Chinese peoples are always in such a hurry to get nowhere.  Once you have bought your ticket then you need to wait at the designated gate (there are giant boards indicating departures).  Then, 10 minutes before the train is due to leave, they open the flood barriers and everyone piles forward in a crazed mass to get through...if you are going to be a part of this then you must learn just to push forward (and if you are British or Canadian then don't forget the Chinese don't say 'sorry'...so just barge recklessly whilst looking straight ahead).  This said, everyone has a designated seat anyway, and it only takes about four or five minutes for everyone to get through so feel free to wait until the rush has died down and you can just meander through the gate and get to your seat on the train with a few minutes still to spare.The station itself is organised chaos with a few convenience stores and a coffee shop.  One of my least favourite train stations I've been to around the world, and it isn't very pretty looking from the outside either, but it served its purpose in getting me on the bullet train...and is very central to Shanghai so that is a plus.

Located next to Hong Qiao airport. Make sure you pre-booked train tickets online, and arrive at least an hour and half before to collect the tickets via ticketing counters. Automated ticketing only allow for Chinese citizens to access. Long queue at ticketing countersso be prepared. Boarding only starts 15mins before departure so time well, as waiting areas are packed with people so you might not get a seat. Fast food and restaurants available for quick snack.

Very large modern station. Everything is clearly indicated (the four directions on the ground, the rest on the signs). Metro station: be careful, however, if you arrive in Shanghai, the distance between stations is significant; you might have to drag your suitcase.

This railway station offers very convenient mode of transportation to Shanghai to Beijing high speed train, to Hongqiao Airport as well as Pudong Airport and local Shanghai Subway. We arrived from Beijing to Shanghai using High Speed train and the distance of almost 1350km was covered in exactly 4 hr and 28 minThis railway station offers variety of restaurants as well. Here It is difficult to get good food for vegetarian or vegans though. Vegetarian or vegans should arrange for their food before arriving here.

Not sure why the railway station is mentioned here. It's not a place I would recommend one to visit as a tourist. However, if you're catching a train from here then be prepared to go through security and identification check (foreigners need passport). Also, may be worth your while to have your ticket either delivered to your hotel or have it collected a day or two before departure as the lines at the station can be insanely long - long enough for you to miss your train.There are a couple of Starbucks and a few eating places within the station. You'll need to arrive an hour or so before departure and the station is about 30-45 mins away from the city so don't sign up for a very early train without being aware of the above. PS: A few high speed trains to Beijing depart from the older Shanghai Main stations as well.

It’s a very big train station. Reminds me of Londons British rail stations. It’s the gateway to any destination, easily connects you to metro to and from hotel. Also download China train app so you can see times you will not be able to purchase ticket in advance if a foreigner.No credit cards must have cash. Unless you have Alipay. And must have passport to purchase tickets if a foreigner. Welcome to high speed trains they way to travel in China for long distance to major city to city.  Can get expensive if traveling in business class which is the way to go. For me it’s privacy and place to relax with out all the load phone calls everyone is making.

Shanghai Hongqiao Railway Station is super large and has strong throughput capacity. To take the high-speed train, it is better to prepare VIP cards, Alipay, Longteng, etc., which are all good benefits and make travel more comfortable.

This railway station is bigger than most airports in North America. It takes me approximately 15 min to figure out the gate of my train. A very crowded station and passengers lined up 30 min before gate opened.
I Used the bullet train to travel from danglang to shanghai. Fast, efficient, clean and comfortable ride
A huge station, which looks like a huge airport with a shopping mall and direct access to the metro. Everything is well indicated.

Hongqiao Railway Station is large, spacious and bright, comparable to an airport. Dozens of railway tracks intersect here, providing access to major cities in China. Combined with the airport subway and buses next to it, it is an important transportation hub. Due to the security check and real-name ticket purchase and collection, it takes a long time to wait when there are large crowds. Remember to arrive at the station early to avoid missing the train you want to take.

This station is located well out of the Shanghai city.  It is huge with a connection to the Hongqiao airport next door. Inside there are thousands of people waiting around or lining up for trains.  We booked in advance before entering the country but still had to go to the airport to pick up our tickets which we did the day before so we didn't encounter any hassles and to familiarise ourselves with the airport.  We had no difficulty finding our train gate as signs are in English as well as Chinese.  It also helped that we decided to pay the extra for business class and had dedicated seats and there was a separate lounge.

Shanghai Hongqiao Railway Station is one of Main Railway Stations in Shanghai city, well located not far fron Hongqiao  Airport.  Very easy to find. Could be recommended to all types of Travellers  going  from Shanghai to other cities in China.

I would pay extra money every time to fly out of Hongqiao. The facilities are great the staff Is knowledgable. With access to the train station . The metro is also there . It's closer to the city. The cab drivers are good . Just all around a better experience
Hongqiao is a very, very large train station, an important transportation hub leading to many places. Because it is a hub, there are quite a lot of people. It is recommended that you arrive early.

The Shanghai Hongqiao Railway Station is insanity. It is a massive building, there are thousands of people and hundreds of trains. It is extremely beneficial that signs are in English and are clear because otherwise it would make it much harder than it already is.  Buying tickets for trains is aggressive. There is no formal line so people just attack the ticket counter. Watch your money and belongings. If you are planning a round trip railway itinerary, book BOTH ways at the ticket counter. I booked a one way and had to make my way back to Shanghai without a train (it was a disaster). Book BOTH ways. Finding your train gate is extremely difficult. Ask guards or staff members to help you. Only book a train that you can board 10mins in advance. It is nearly impossible to book a train leaving sooner and make it on time (the sheer size of the terminal alone ensures that). Bottom Line: it is an efficient railway station that has good services. Just be careful and be smart.

We used this railway station several times for day trips to Suzhou, hangzhou and Nanjing while being based for more than a week in Shanghai recently. We bought our tickets on the day and the services were extremely efficient at all levels. The only issue was that we had a hard time looking for the ticket counters when we first arrived at this station. The signage and directions could be improved. There are many nice eateries and small convenient stores within the station, and the subway is easy to locate though.

Was at the train station recently. The place is Big and filled with people everywhere, probably many going back for Lunar New Year. So far, the arrangement was good and boarded the train on time. All went well!

It's useful for business trips, but it's a little inconvenient for foreigners. Even if you make a reservation, you still have to get a ticket from the ticket counter at the station. Train stations in China are usually crowded, so it's best to get there early. Also, be careful here as the entrance will be closed 5 minutes before the departure time!
Although the station is large like an airport, the signs are easy to understand so you won't get lost. But it's so spacious that when my child needed to go to the bathroom, I dashed there (lol).
Taking the train from this station is easy since it is signposted and the people who work there are very friendly.

Thirty years ago you came to China and found mediocrity while in Italy there were good infrastructures. Years later, China has made colossal investments that leave Europeans speechless while we have moved little in recent years. The Shanghai station and the Chinese railway system breathe this projection into the future of a country that knows how to revolutionize itself every few years, of generations that know the meaning of the word future. At the station we observe important infrastructures, cutting-edge information systems, futuristic trains. I won't talk about punctuality then.

Almost everything here in Chinese, but getting your ticket to your next destination is easy. At the station, look for counters with many ppl queuing..these are ticketing counter. Note that the display above the counters show same chinese characters. At the counter, tell them your destination(they will understand your pronountiation)) & preferred travel time(give yourself abt 30mins to get to your boarding gates). On the ticket, there are destination name/boarding gate no/train no/coach no/seat no. Search on any websites on how to read the ticket. Else can always ask the ppl around you.  Chinese ppl are very helpful.
A typical Railway Train station indeed. Nothing bad to complain about, nothing too good to shout about or recommend. Typical Train Station restaurants and fast food, ok chairs.

Always busy, huge amounts of travelers, allow enough time, especially to purchase a ticket or exchange. Many places to eat and get coffee or tea, plenty of seats, very efficient, but a bit stressful when crowded.

The bathroom is very clean, and there is a display in front of the door telling how many people can go. The car was very punctual. There are many restaurants and merchandise stores. The products are very expensive, and most people just look at them without buying them.
Futuristic train station like all those in China. Trains leave from here for Guilin.

I used it for a round trip between Guangzhou South and Guilin North Stations when sightseeing in Guilin. Unlike Japan, there are passport and baggage inspections, so last-minute boarding is not possible. You need to get to the station with plenty of time. Also, like me, there were many passengers with large suitcases coming through the airport, and the suitcases were stacked on top of each other, leaving items scattered about that couldn't be placed. Needless to say, the restroom was filthy, and even though it was full, the locals naturally kept reclining as hard as they could, so it wasn't very comfortable. The good thing was that you could see a spectacular view from the train window around Guilin North Station. Beijing and Shanghai may be different, but I didn't want to use it too actively when going to a tourist city like Guilin.
A lovely modern clean station which I arrived to from Hong Kong on a bullet train.Easy to navigate around plenty of signs in English and easy to get to the subway

High-speed trains leave from Shanghai to other cities through this station. It is simply impressive in its scope, the distances between the metro, ticket offices and exits to the trains.... There are almost always queues at the ticket office, so we started buying tickets in advance through intermediaries with a small commission.... Very good selection of restaurants at reasonable prices, we always try to have a bite to eat in one of them... Exits to the platform on the 2nd floor, security checks like at airports.... in overall a modern station

Extremely clean, busy, organized with precision , signage is very foreigner friendly. Platforms and secure , clean, trains are schedules and managed closely, security and train service employees very helpful.
Extremely well planned setup with the adjoining airport connected. Ease of access, display systems, facilities for travellers, check in to the trains- all classify amongst the best.

We travelled to Hangzhou and Suzhou and in the direction of Moganshan via train and were astonished how efficient this was. The only disadvantage is that you don’t have your own car at the other end, but if you work through a reputable travel agent they will be able to offer both chauffeured car and bus options. The stations, especially the large HongQiao, are all modern and easy to navigate provided that you don’t panic if you cant immediately find signage in English. Usually there is an official who is used to dealing with foreigners in these popular tourist destinations or just look for a young person of post-school age who is professionally dressed and chances are they will have enough English to give you directions. Just remember that even very modern young Chinese will be reticent to approach you as they will lack confidence in their capacity to speak English.

We went to Beijing from Shanghai via Hongqiao station, the station is very big, like an airport and it is also located next to Hongqiao Airport, the distance from Shanghai City to this station is about 30 minutes by taxi and the cost is around RMB 100, Shanghai is a bit congested in the morning or evening, so make sure it takes a long journey from the city/The Bund area to Hongqiao station. Not all officers in the ticket area can speak English, so make sure your internet is always on...
Shangai hongqiao railway station is very latest and classic and airport is very near is so good passengers are very satisfied with services best railway station

Can’t get over how many cleaners there are everywhere especially at the station and on the trains. The station was easy to navigate and had good facilities. Definitely take the train for high speed travel in China!

China is on some other level when it comes to expansion, modernisation and infrastructure. The railway station of Shanghai is one example. This can challenge any airport in the world. In fact to be honest its more accessible, clean, better managed then Airports of many countries if not all.
This train station fascinates with its dimensions. Well organized, clean and clear. When I think of Germany, I feel sad.

Shanghai metro is fast, cheap and reliable. We always use it whenever we can. All the station names are written in both Chinese and English. When you leave the train all the transfer routes are clearly marked. It’s hard to get lost there :)
Nice station, large and safe, full of signs in English that will make your journey easier. Excellently connected to other public transport, it is also full of shops

If train stations in Germany worked half as well as they do in China, I would easily take the train instead of a car/plane in this country. Once you get through security, you feel like you're in the airport. It's huge, absolutely clean and the trains are very punctual. It's advisable to buy tickets in advance or have them bought from the hotel, for example, otherwise you might end up queuing for a long time or, like me, waiting 4 hours at a train station for a train that isn't fully booked to leave.

You have to buy tickets in advance, the trains leave very punctual. Check carefully the number you have on your pass, because the waiting rooms are constantly changing departures because the train leaves very quickly, arrive in time in case you get confused, don't get angry.
The train station in Shanghai is very large and busy. This station connects Shanghai with major cities in China, usually using fast trains.

Was here for a train ride from Beijing. A huge train station and can be confusing. Upon arrival, look for a proper taxi counter as there will be some people offering "taxi" to travel out. This can cost double or triple from the normal taxi ride.

One of the main transportation hub and as expected this is a busy station. Be prepared for the large crowd and checking in can be overwhelming and security is quite tight. But once in the train, it’s another world. Overall it’s another China 🇨🇳 experience to remember.

I've already left there several times... Recently we were looking for a café and so we went one floor higher (from where you can see into the central hall. Just unbelievable... the multitude of people, the hustle and bustle! You have to take a look and be amazed.

The ride quality itself is not that different from Japan's Shinkansen. Perhaps because the tickets are more expensive than regular trains, I feel that many local passengers have good manners. However, everyone is tolerant of noise, so some people talk on their cell phones while sitting in their seats. In China, you are required to present your passport not only on high-speed trains but also on regular trains, so don't forget!
Train is good, food is bad, but toilet is terrible! I would recommend you to pee on the train rather than at the station!

The sheer size of the railroad station is impressive in itself.  Despite the throng that had to go though security, the crowd flowed.  Encountered locals who were very helpful despite the language barrier to assist us in what we were trying to do.

Not a bad train station but if you don’t speak Mandarin and you need help, you’d better have a translate app or really good hand gestures to get assistance.  We had a glitch with our tickets and it literally took one guard, an expat, and Google translate to get our situation undone.  After all that though, we had us some business class seats on the bullet train to Beijing that was epic!  Lots of restaurants and shops.  Station is relatively calm and organized.

If traveling by business or not you need to go to Hongqiao railway station. Incredible. Very organized and functional. Safer and cheaper than flying but time consuming. If you have time take a train. For foreigners please be at the railway station at least 45 minutes before departure. Passport check to get boarding ticket.

Hongqiao station is not in downtown Shanghai, but it's perfectly connected to all of the City via two metro lines and an high number of buses, and obviously taxies.Modern, clean and easy to navigate, it's my favourite station in Shanghai, and trains leaving from it are usually cheaper and quicker than the ones leaving from Shanghai Railway Station :)

Large, cold, uninviting, yet efficient and easy to find ones way.  Many levels and the Subway stops right underneath.  If given a choice between the slow train and the fast train, take the fast one.  Well worth the extra couple of bucks.

We book the tickets online which was straight forward and it was delivered over to our hotel 1 day before we arrived! We took a taxi over to the train station and it was very straightforward that we have no problem finding our ways. Basically, this trip was a challenge for me as I do not understand mandarin or Chinese lettering.We took the train G360 which was heading to Xi’anbei and it only took us 6 hours to reach. We had second class seat but the seating was really comfortable that I snooze with my favourite music. At times, you may want to enjoy the view of the great city of China along the way.

The transportation to Shanghai Hongqiao Railway Station is very convenient. Taking the subway feels a little far on foot. I downloaded a Metropolis APP to use it to take the subway. It is very convenient. The Alipay discount price is available twice a day. From Hangzhou Railway Station, there are about four high-speed trains a day to Hongqiao Railway Station. It takes 1 hour and a few minutes.

I often travel to Shanghai for work. The train is really high speed, that is, 300 km/h. Many trains constantly, many people, get your ticket at least 2 weeks in advance or you will not get tickets. Too many controls to enter, which cause you to be delayed, go early.

Very busy and crowded station. Place to buy the bullet train and fast train. Regular train should go to Shanghai South Station. Planned to go to Yiwu at 12.00 pm but all the fast train tickets are all sold out even the latest train schedule. Suggest to buy online to avoid this. They refer me to the Shanghai South Station for regular trains.

The scale is impressive. Everything is organized clearly. Boarding the train starts 30 minutes before. Officially ends at 10. But latecomers are waited as long as possible before departure. There are counters for printing electronic tickets. There are a lot of catering establishments. An entire floor is given over to restaurants. During the holidays, being at a Chinese railway station is a special experience. The maximum program is to fight your way through the crowds of crowds of crowds to the exit....
A very big and state of the art rail station with many shops and nearby shopping mall that gives travellers an opportunity to shop around and relax. Signage is good and can't get lost.
Very large, bright and very clean station! Punctual and shiny trains! Gigantic and intuitive screens exactly like at the airport.

You will use this station if you are using one of China's high speed trains to travel away from Shanghai. Be ready for crowds. There are two checks - one for ID and then luggage check. But it's all orderly and goes pretty fast. Just go with the flow.

The largest railway station in China.It is clean and well supported by restaurantsTimetable works like a clock, trains leaves and arrives on the dot.However if this is your first visit, like me, I recommend you arrive ahead of time to navigate or prebook your train tickets and collect them at counters

As in China, the subway also has security checkpoints, and the train station is also thorough. It's bigger than the airport, and there are more people. You need a passport or residence card to buy a ticket. English is barely spoken.
I took the high-speed train to go to another area. The station and train facilities were very clean and inexpensive. I used it without any inconvenience and it was very convenient.

Much more like an airport than a station. Worth being aware that you can only go through the barriers from the main waiting area to your platform 15 minutes before departure. The details for your train at the platform entrance will turn green to signify that you can proceed.

Despite the thousands of passengers using it everyday it is still quite comfortable and convenient train station. Large and organized all relevant information is also in English. It is a shame, however, that the number of taxis stopping at the station it is not enough for the needs. in rush hours one may have to wait for more than half an hour to take a taxi...

Hongqiao used to be the outer part of Shanghai but no more. This is one of the key bullet train station for Shanghai. The second airport for Shanghai is right next door. The traffic can be bad but you can easily transit between train and flights
A truly vast station, however it has an excellent information service in English, which is very rare in China
China's bullet train network is magnificent, and the Shanghai train station is very well designed and enormous in size. I recommend riding the trains, as they are spacious and very clean.
Very comfortable, clean train (they pass the floor halfway through the journey!) Trained and attentive staff. YesSilent and very fast. Stations well organized and tidy, clean and safe.

Huge station where tens of thousands of travelers pass each other every day. You can easily live there, dozens of restaurants of all kinds. Plan to arrive a good hour before boarding. Impeccable 1st class service in the 1st! It's worth it. Experience to be had between BEIJING and SGHAI, back and forth.
When I got to this station, at first it seemed to me that I was in an airport instead of a train station. The exits to the platform are very similar to the boarding gates of an airplane.
We visited Shanghai during the National holiday and boy were there a lot of people there! We barley got through to the machine that sells subway tickets

The station is simply extraordinary, it looks like an airport. The logic of its use is simple and the trains are impressive, it is worth traveling by train and thus avoiding the long downtimes that occur at airports.

It’s station is HUGE!!! Don't arrive at the last minute because there are security checks and long waits to collect your tickets even if you have paid in advance! Also very little signage in English and the staff don't speak English very well either. On the other hand, you will have many shops and restaurants while waiting and the trains are comfortable and fast! Warning: very few places accept visa or North American credit cards, so bring cash!

Traveling with family it’s one of the most convenient train stations in Shanghai.Guided in English and Chinese, well organized and so many ways to reach the train station or get to city centre.Many security checks, and as foreigner Make sure to receive time to get your ticket. Metro: line 2&10 about 40 min one wayTaxi: 35-50 min one way - about 80- 100 rmb ( if they ask more use didi to get normal price)Beware of the people who sell you services after exit gate- they are expensive.

My mother and I took a high speed train from Shanghai to Yiwu.We arrived by car and getting to the drop off point was a task in itself. Our driver had to drop us not quite at the kerb and we had to wave our way through. The locals do the same.Then you get your bags through security check and after that you're through to the terminal.On the first level will be the gates for train departures.The second level has many restaurants serving quick eats.One thing I find amazing is that the gate is only opened 10 mins before the train departs. This does not give you much time for you to get your train ticket scanned and making your way down the stairs and finding your carriage. My advice would be to minimize you luggage and be ready to walk briskly.It became quite an ordeal for my poor mum who is 80 years old. Not at this terminal but the one at Hangzhou, when we arrived at the platform, we were at carriage 10. Our seats were in carriage one. The signs on the train are not too clear. After walking for a short while, we realised we were headed in the wrong direction when we found ourselves facing carriage 12!. We had to backtrack and walk the entire length of 12 carriages in 5 mins. It was truly an anxious and excruciating experience then as we were terrified that we would miss our train! But we made it but mum thought she was having a heart attack as she developed a stitch in her side. She did great for an 80 year old!Nevertheless, my experience with taking the train has been good.The high speed trains were fast and efficient and delivered as they promised.

We cabbed from Pudong airport to catch a train to Beijing - it was very confusing and crowded trying to fight our way to the ticket booth to find out they do not accept Visa OR MasterCard (likely wont accept Amex either). This was a surprise to us that such a massive train station in one of the worlds largest financial hub cities, major credit cards are not accepted. We pushed through the crowds to the atms with minimal English options on them to take out cash to purchase our tickets. Then waited our 2 hours until our train. There were no available seats due to the large crowd so we sat on the floor (not a huge deal) although I would not want to experience this place on a weekend. Overall not a good experience.
We came by train from hangzhou..the station is hugh.not easy to find the way you nees.place is clean.

We took the train in coach class from Beijing to Shanghai. The route leads over stilts, so the view of the surrounding area is quite good. Speed ​​up to 350 km/h. You can buy drinks and even pretty decent food on the train. The stations are extremely clean, you can only enter the platforms once the train has arrived. This means you can find your carriage quickly and there is less crowding. The train stations are similar to the gates at the airport, and there are also similar security checks.

The design of Hongqiao Station is relatively reasonable, and it is convenient to take a taxi. Although the elevated section of the business district is more complicated to drive, there is still no problem following the navigation. The security check is efficient, and the supporting catering is also relatively rich.
Even if you weren't catching a train it's worthwhile seeing this huge bustling station. Moving thousands of people.
A huge station close by one of the airports but a long drive downtown. Such a huge station with plenty of platforms and stores. Lots of signs in English but the parking can be difficult.

The Chinese bullet train network is the largest infrastructure project in the world. 50% of the entire bullet train network in the world is in China. For me, it was possible to travel from Shanghai to Taizhou in 3 hours, a journey that previously took 9 hours by car. Hongqiao is one of the main ones in China. Millions of people pass through it every day. Various train options to different cities. The problem is that information in English is still insufficient, although much better than in other cities. In Taizhou, for example, there is almost no information in English yet. Tip: arrive at least 45 minutes before your scheduled time. There is security control, a queue to buy tickets and you will need some time to find your boarding gate.

Big station 3-storey. There is a cafe on the 3rd floor, but you can’t order anything at McDonald’s in the terminal, since it only accepts local cards. I bought tickets online in Russia. With a printout of your reservation, you go to the box office to buy your ticket. There are lines but they move quickly. The main thing is not to go to the ticket office to return and rebook tickets. I don’t know why they write that entry to the station requires a ticket. I calmly entered several times without a ticket or passport. No one asked for a passport at boarding either. And in general, no one ever checked the ticket. At the entrance to the railway station there is a turnstile through which you pass your ticket.  There is also a turnstile at the exit of the destination station. I went to Taizhou.

Always very punctual! You can access the departure platforms 10 minutes from arrival. Fantastic fast trains! Traveling on business is an experience worth trying! Very comfortable seats (you can lie down) - very clean bathroomsRelaxing tripEverything "excellent"😉👍🏻

This place was amazing, bigger than a lot of airports. Wall to wall people,but so very organised. There was a wide choice of eateries and enough seats to cater for the crowd. Great experience if you never done a bullet train and something different than flying.

Unlike Berlin, Hamburg, Munich or frankfurt Central Stations that I went recently, shanghai hongqiao is way too complex. Inconvenient for foreigners where we need to queue.Fantastic job by government planners. Undoubtedly profitable at reportedly RMB60 billion annually.No train passes unlike European cities.See the arrival of The Chinese railway tours.

In September, I traveled on the Hadai High Speed ​​Shinkansen for an 8-day sightseeing tour on the long-awaited Manchuria Railway. I rode for the first time between Harbin and Xinjing (Changchun) and between Xinjing and Mukden (Shenyang), rolling my heavy bag around. It feels just like Japan's Shinkansen. I also had a hard time taking pictures of the outside scenery because I wasn't seated by the window. I took a little bit off at the connecting part.

This train station is next to the old Hongqiao international airport. Organized system at the train station. Station is really huge. We hired "red caps" to help us with our luggage and also to lead us to the correct platform. The boarding time is very close to the departure time so have to hurry a bit sometimes.

Hongqiao Railway Station has something in common with an airport. There are security checks at the entrance to the waiting area. The train station seems very clean and safe. There are a few restaurants in the train station, which are unfortunately difficult to reach for travelers with more than one piece of luggage. In general, I have noticed that with a lot of luggage you can face considerable difficulties in China. Access to the individual platforms is very well signposted, so even long noses should have no problems reaching the train they have booked.

Next to the national airport of Shanghai there is an immense space used for the departure of fast trains for all of inland China. You move as if you were at the airport: Customs at the entrance, check in your luggage and after purchasing your ticket you go to the gate of the train platform which will open only 15 minutes before the train leaves. Just one fact makes you understand the enormity of the site: At the peak of summer departures Malpensa airport allows departures 70,000 passengers per day. Every normal day 220,000 people pass through with peaks of 380,000 passengers

Very convenient and well run. It is modern, well lit and clean. Very clear signage and access to subway.A word of caution when getting pick up from the station. Its carparks are situated at both ends of the stations and they are a good 10 mins walk, so make sure you go to the right one.
Well organized and with lots of food and shopping options. Good access by subway, bit trickier by cab since there is a lot of traffic at the entrance.

The train station and lounge are larger than most overseas airports. And the large number of people is impressive. In China, like Italy, there is a lot of smoking on the train platform, and tickets are checked and entered through the platform entrance line according to the train arrival time.

I took the high-speed train from Hangzhou East Railway Station to Fuzhou East Railway Station, and since it is quiet, spacious, and separated by partitions, it is convenient for traveling while having a meeting. Ticketing locations for high-speed trains are crowded, so if you need to pick up your ticket, it's best to get there early. Also, you cannot get off at the platform until a certain time. I took the first class seat the day before, but the service was the same, and once you were seated, your ticket was checked. Water and snacks after that? services are available. There is also on-board sales, so if you want a different drink, please stop the staff and buy it. Most Shinkansen stations are clean and free of trash. But for some reason, the home is dark.
Very huge, almost like an airport! Very organised and lots of restaurants. Good way to travel around.

You can get to this modern railway station by subway, from where you can leave for Beijing on the high-speed train. They have a food area so that the wait is not so long, since they ask you to be at least one hour before your train leaves. Recommended because they are very punctual when leaving and upon arrival, perhaps it is more convenient than a flight.
Size is the main thing you notice, big. We came in from Beijing on the Bullet Train ....... neat journey. The station was neat, shiny and clean. Nice experience.
China's version of the Shinkansen. The ride comfort is almost the same as the Japanese one. It's very convenient and has quick access to all parts of China. It's cheap and easy to use.

I took the high-speed train from Shanghai to Suzhou. Flights to Suzhou depart from Shanghai and Hongqiao and arrive in Suzhou in about 30 minutes. It is possible to go sightseeing on a day trip, but it is better to be careful about the time you return home. Because we couldn't buy tickets for the time slot we wanted, we had to kill time at Suzhou Station for about an hour. If you have a fixed return time, it is wise to purchase your tickets early. The ride was reasonably comfortable, but unfortunately there was a person sitting in the back with bad manners on the way there and back...LOL This is natural in China, but Japanese manners and common sense don't apply, so I think you can spend a stress-free time by just giving up and trying not to worry about it.

Used by a lot of the High Speed trains and easy enough to find your way around it, only think is on a Friday afternoon the wait for a taxi was over an hour, that’s the only thing that would put me off using it again

Arrived at this station travelling from Beijing on the very fast train.   So we only did a quick transit thru the station to the internal subway line, which happens to be at the other end of this very big station.   Very clean, modern and well organised station as are all the rail systems we used. All the usual facilities, toilets and shops.   I guess the most surprising note is how clean the whole rail transit is, the platforms are like a marble shine its amazing with trains full how clean "spotless" they can keep these area's so clean.Very impressed with the overall  train system, definitely would use again. 🚅🚆🚈
We caught Bullet train to Beijing from here. The station is very crowded, yet very clean. Organised, the directions pretty clear.
Huge station. Bustling with people but well organised. The board with all those boxes is intimidating.

Through security and into the crowded railway station to await the departure of your train. One has to queue and is only let through when the train is waiting at the station. Baggage is a big problem, having to negotiate the escalator to the platform. There are many shops to browse while waiting, as someone minds your spot in the queue.

I used this Railway Station when staying at the Hongqiao Airport Hotel as it is attached to the Airport Concourse by a considerably long walkway.  The Station is unbelievable in size and I believe it has been built to accommodate the Bullet Trains.  The Station is buzzing with crowds from early morning until late at night, both with commuters and travellers visiting all parts of China, on longer distance trains.  The station has its own area of shops and food outlets.  Security is very tight within the railways complex, as I found it to be in all big cities in Shanghai - but easy and very safe to use

would expect nothing more modest or less efficiently organised in Shanghai :) crowded of course, so be prepared and alert where to go. the speed trains are amazing - both (Beijing-Xian, and Shanghai-Guilin) closed the doors a minute before departure time, and left the station a few seconds before the schedule!!! so do not take the schedule too European way ;)
This place is huge. Make sure you know where your going and pay attention.  Trains are quick. Took the high speed train to suzhou.

I have never been to a real, awesome train station, especially that has High Speed Trains. Our first time was great. It is right beside the Hongqiao International Airport so its a great transportation hub for rail, metro and air. There are many runs a day from this station going to various destinations. Its convenient, and ticket pricing are reasonable. My main complaint is the air conditioning is not cold enough. Passport or IDs are a requirement to buy tickets. Buy yours one month in advance if you can. There are many eateries here and the boarding are fast and efficient. Although if you carry more than one large suitcase, you may have issues going to the platform and when you reach your destination because it gets quite crowded and the escalator IS REALLY YOUR ONLY free way out of the station to the arrivals area. They designed this railway station for the available porters to charge you a fee of per piece which we tried really hard to resist them but they are persistent. Look at your tickets carefully and board the correct car by walking along the platform because dragging your luggage through the crowded cars inside is not ideal. Seats are also assigned too. Our speed train took us from Shanghai to Beijing on a G train in 4 hours 50 mins in comfort. Oh I can't wait to take another train in China!
A truly amazing station , high speed rail at its finest .To a Brit used to uk rail system this is the future.

It is a very big station but it is quite well organized. My clear recommendation is that you get your tickets in advance, at least the day before travelling. If not, you can not be able to take your train due to queues. If you have your ticket, unless you are in some peak days, you should be able to do fine with 20-30 minutes (although it is advisable to arrive at least one hour in advance to the station). A lot of signs and panels will help you to find your train. Do not worry about not speaking Chinese.

Shanghai Hongqiao railway station is huge, connected to the airport of the same name and the metro. Located 13 km from the center of Shanghai. Very convenient, the metro line also connects Hongqiao to Pudong Airport. It is quite easy to get your ticket at the ticket counters where the staff speaks a little English. Then it is quite easy thanks to the numbers appearing on the ticket (door, train, car, seat numbers) to find the boarding gates which you can pass through approximately 10 minutes before the train leaves. Good organization.

We took a train to Hangzhou from here. Tickets were easy to purchase from the counter. There were long queues at the ticketing booths but it helps that we can read Chinese cos the longer queues were for change or refund of tickets. There were many boarding gates to board the trains and we find it rather confusing looking for the right one. So don’t be shy to show your tickets to the staff at the boarding gate to check on the right boarding gate. Remember — you need to produce your passports when buying the train tickets. So don’t leave your passports in the hotel safe even though you are only traveling to a neighbouring city

I use it every week for work. Unlike airplanes, there are almost no delays, so I often use it, especially during seasons with bad weather. Recently, new vehicles have been introduced, with a maximum speed of 350km/h, interior Wi-Fi, and improved comfort. Perhaps because there is no problem with land acquisition in China, the ride quality is better than Japan's Shinkansen trains as they are almost straight lines. However, the manners of the passengers are not good, and if you are unlucky, you will find a passenger who loudly uses his cell phone in his seat or listens to music or drama without earphones. Even if you're not next to someone, there's a high chance that there will be one or two people in the car, so we recommend bringing earplugs and a music player.

Take a traveller's tip here, collect your tickets from the station the day before you travel, saves queuing, although the queues here for the bullet train were not nearly as bad as in Beijing South Station (for a trip to Xi'an). Bullet trains are awesome in China!

Shanghai Hongqiao Station is Extremely crowded and huge since this is also a hub for three subway lines and adjacent to the airport. Unfortunately the electronic departure boards for the fast trains are not in English, so a camera-based translator could be useful. You’ll have to go through security to get to the waiting areas but you can find a plethora of restaurants and options for your convenience (without needing to leave the secure area) and in case you want to buy food you want to bring in the train.🕗 BE READY: Tickets validation starts 20 minutes prior to departure time and boarding 10 minutes prior, so the train will depart exactly at the time it’s on the ticket. 🚄 About the FAST TRAIN: Seats in 2nd class are roomy enough for a 6’3” person (1.89 m). There are 18 rows of 5 seats per car with enough room for luggage on top of the seats and in a separate compartment at the end of the car. Each two cars you’ll find 2 restrooms (One oriental, one occidental), a hot water fountain (Not cold though!), a sink to wash your hands and a trash disposal compartment. You can buy food and snacks and the lunch meal (¥60 yuan, about $10 USD), which includes rice, meat, vegetables and other 2 sides, is large enough for two people. BUY COLD WATER if you want to have some during your trip, they might not have any cold drinks! If it’s your first time in the fast train and you’re sensitive, BUY MEDICINE for headaches and nausea.

I bought Qingdao high-speed rail tickets online before, but there are no senior tickets for high-speed rail tickets here. Because I had the experience of going to Beijing on the high-speed rail last time, I was scared by the crowds, so I came early this time and got on the train smoothly. However, most of the people on the train had luggage. After asking the service staff on the train, they put it in the back of the carriage. This time it took seven hours from Shanghai to Qingdao. I ordered their beef bento on the train. The price was $45 and the taste was okay, but it was not comparable to the Taiwan Railway Bento. What is more uncomfortable is that many people start smoking as soon as they get off the bus. The air quality is really bad.

Huge, incomprehensible, absence of indications, kilometers of rooms and corridors... the connection with the airport is worth it. Furthermore, very far from the city and access at the end of the day can take hours. In short, prefer the city center station.

We found it quite easy to find our way. If you pre purchase tickets it’s even easier! U really want to arrive at least 40mins before your scheduled train especially if you have to purchase tickets on arrival. Lots to eat/drink around but not much seating (busy!).

China has the largest high-speed train network in the world at affordable prices. Trains leave from this station to Beijing, Nanjing and many others. You can go by taxi but also by metro (lines 2 and 10). There are trains that make the journey to Beijing in four and a half hours. The trains have three classes: business, first and second. It depends on you but I can say that second gear is great (although you won't be able to avoid the children upstairs and downstairs). If you are going to travel, go early. There are so many people that it takes time to find the right place and get through the checkpoints. I recommend buying the tickets before making the trip and having them already printed on the day of the trip. There are places to eat at the station. Along the way they offer you drinks, ice cream, etc. But it is a good idea to bring what you are going to eat on the trip.

We took the trip to Beijing via high speed rail. The ride was good efficient and on time from departure to arrival. For 1748RmB we had business class in comfortable surrounds.This train terminal has plenty of security and you cannot take shaving cream or aerosol cans on the train but you can take water.Restaurants are on Level 2 but bring cash as not everyone will accept credit card from overseas. There is a McDonald’s, Burger King and KFC there in addition to local restaurants.Seating for eating is a premium with each restaurant having limited seating. Prepare to eat standing up or on the go.

The station is big and huge , we went here to catch the train to Xian. the station is huge hence you have to search the train entrance leaving station. please take sometime in order to catch the train.

If you don't have to take a train, don't.  But sometimes you can't avoid it and at least the Hongqiao RR Station is on the subway Line 10. Try to spend the least amount of time possible in the actual train station, but beware the long lines, insanely sound-reflective floors, walls and ceilings.  Make sure you get to the gate at least 5 minutes before your scheduled departure, as they stop taking tickets 3 minutes before.

A gigantic station building! The queue for taxis was perfectly organized: they arrived when the metro was no longer working, however, the crowd did not rush in disorder, but everyone walked in a neat queue and got into the newly arriving cars. Display boards, shops and eateries at every turn!

This is going to be one of the biggest buildings you will ever have been to. Be sure to know which checkin gaye the train leaves from, because running fun one end to the other takes about 15mins due to the number of people waiting to board trains. Modest fast food offering and some of the usual coffee spots.

The porters help you find your train with a tip, just by showing them the ticket because they don't speak English but it's not necessary, the station is great, the punctuality of the trains is to be applauded! The seats are very comfortable, we bought the tickets in advance online.

I used my passport to book a ticket online, but when I got to the window, I was not given a ticket. They said I had to show my Taiwan Compatriot ID. If I didn’t book with my Taiwan Compatriot ID, I couldn’t get the ticket. It was an inexplicable stipulation. Fortunately, the ticket cutter and the driver all let me get on the bus. It was ridiculous.

On the day we go, there is a typhoon, with winds up to 300 kilometers, and on the day we come, up to 431 kilometers. I got from the hotel to the airport in a total of 45 minutes by subway car. At 80 yuan for a round trip (50 yuan for one way), you can travel quickly at a not that expensive price.
Big and spacious.  Enter via security checking, many retail and food outlet, toilet facilities needs lots of improvement.

Went to station to catch high speed train to Xi’an had already picked up tickets previously. Had to pick up tickets for the other parts of our journey. Staff was helpful. Every sign was in English and Chinese. Very crowded, but found gate easily and boarded without incident.

The Hongqiao Railway station is right adjacent to the International airport and is interconnected. It is quite large/majestic in terms of size and the number of train platforms. Its the place to grab high speed bullet trains to Beijing and other parts of China.

I often use it every time I travel from Shanghai to the outskirts on a business trip. The train station is as big as most airports in the country. The facilities and systems are well-equipped, so there is no inconvenience at all.

This place was amazing.  Plus it was clean, well run, and not scary like some stations.  If you are a foreigner, be ready for the ticket process and have you leave passport ready - they must see it.  There are signs in English but have someone explain your ticket - that can be confusing. But the high speed trains were worth it and I would definitely go back.

My family took the high speed train from Shanghai to Beijing from this station and it is massive. However, despite its size, signs were written in English and Chinese and it made it easy to find where we were going to get our train.

The bus from here to and from Pudong airport is 30 rmb each. It takes about 1 hour but it is better than spending 90 minutes standing of a crowded metro line getting to the airport. Believe me its bliss. I do this all the time.
Good and nothing more to say. Very crouded when you go outside. No clear information when you exit the station for which gate you have to take.

The travel on a speed train in China  is very comfortable, so the trains are full. I was not aware of that and haven't booked my ticket in advance. As the result: 1. I had to stand in the queue for 20 minutes to buy the ticket. 2. My train was in 5 hours due to all earlier trains were full. 3. These 5 hours I spent literally sweating, because there is no air conditioning in the station. Despite that everything was fine: clean building, clear signs, many fast food places. It was an interesting experience for me.

we used this station to catch a train from shanghai to beijing.  The station is massive and it can be confusing to even find the entrance to it.  Once inside, its pretty easy to navigate, the ticket booth speaks only chinese but if you booked online you just show your passport and they print the ticket, so no chinese necessary.lots of fast food restaurants inside, washrooms were not even to scary.

Shanghai Hongqiao Station is the memory of old Shanghainese. No matter where you want to go from Shanghai, you must enter or exit from Hongqiao Station. Heading to Suzhou in the north and Hangzhou in the south, Hongqiao Station is the transportation fortress of Shanghai. Coupled with the transportation connection with Hongqiao Airport, Shanghai has become an important hub of China's first-tier coastal cities.

I use high-speed rail every time. I use this service because I go every month from Shanghai Hongqiao to visit factories in Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province, Shaoxing City, Putian Province, Fujian Province, and Shenzhen Beizan. If the distance between continental cities is around 300-700 km, it is convenient to fly. It doesn't take much time to arrive at your destination, and the fare is around 100 yuan for a 2nd class train for a distance of about 300 km. All tickets can be purchased at the station by presenting your passport. I always buy quickly from elong and ctrip online companies. The inside of the train is kept clean as the crew cleans it with a mop once every hour. All cars are non-smoking, so I have never had any unpleasant experiences. However, there are some rednecks who eat sunflower seeds, scatter them, and leave them full of garbage. The bento boxes sold on the train are reasonably priced for 40-50 yuan.

The signage is very messy, and you must come early. The queues are very long, and the security check is fast, but the traffic lines before boarding the bus are messy. If you are hungry at the station, you can only eat fast food, and there are too many people. It is easy to run out of seats while waiting for the bus.

We went to take one of the fast trains in China to travel from Shanghai to Hangzhou and it was an experience. Lots of people, many kilometers between each point but one of the most impressive trains i ever took.

we took the fast train from Shanghai to Suzhou and it was an amazing journey 25 minutes to cover the 78km stretch, trains were clean and the entire journey was something that is worth a try.The station itself handles thousands of people but its clean and systematic, But remember English is not spoken to much
It's just a very big and very very busy station. So many people! There are plenty of shops and places to get food and drink for your journey.

It's a very busy and most advance railway station that connects all major cities in China.There is a cafeteria with all international brands and food chains and also a shiping area.Toilets are very clean and people are really disciplined.
Accessed by metro line 2, it is next to Hongqiao airport and bus station. Direct access to several shopping centers and commerce such as Paradise and Hub.

Shanghai should have top of the class railway station. The information counter staff are busy chatting on their phones or playing videogame. Hardly anyone speak English and all lounges are expensive serving cookies a business and instant coffee for the price of a buffet meal at Hilton hotel. No lounge hostess speaks English. In the catering floor there is plenty of free space and more seating could be provided.. WC are filthy and mostly out of order and all WC for disabled people are turned into store by the cleaners. Shanghai deserves better facilities because from the tourism point of view the entry and exit doors to a country are the first and last impression a foreigner will have

Easy to reach on the subway and once in the station it is very easy to get to where you need to go. trains are always on time. restaurants are very average as well as teh shops being poor quality and useless for a decent snack to take

We traveled to different places by high-speed train. The first trip left from Shanghai. The train is very comfortable. Even in second grade. I was also the first one. The seat reclines more, more space, footrest, and snack. I don't know if they are all there, but the first train I took in second class only had a bathroom without a toilet. I didn't ask if there was only that one. But it's worth paying attention to.

Wonderful connectivity between the city & the rest of the country. Though if your flight is from Pudong Airport schedule atleast 90-120 minutes as the distances to walk at both the railway station, subway station and airport are quite a bit. But if you are arriving from outside of Shanghai to connect to a flight from Hongqiao Airport- it's the best option. Infact you can just walk from the station to the airport itself and all you have to do is follow the signs. The staff at the information desks are also quite helpful.

It's a train station. Much like any of the hundreds scattered across China. If you can find the DQ or Costa, you'll be fine. The bathrooms are at your own risk (as usual). Make sure you have your own tissue!
Huge train station, but very easy to use even for the unfamiliar. Perfectly connected to both the subway and Shanghai's smallest airport, just one metro stop away.

It is a new station on the outskirts near the airport. Huge and crowded, it serves a lot of very high-speed trains. Buy tickets in advance otherwise you will stand in long queues and risk losing your transport. Remember to always have your passport with you and go through baggage and people checks. We bought the tickets online and the agency had them delivered to the hotel. Convenient, easy, safe. From the city center this station can be reached by metro or taxi - about 30-40 minutes with a lot of traffic, 20 with little.

Arrived via high-speed train, the arrival process was okay, some people were crazy stopping at the bottom of the escalator, luckily there were people there to yell at them, that's very dangerous when the escalator is full... The station was poorly labeled for arrivals, there were sparse toilet signage, the signs over the doors are flush against the wall... We were looking to use Didi and had difficulty finding an appropriate exit. We ended up walking to a nearby hotel to get a car. Next time we'll probably just take a taxi. Beware of people offering rides, they said the taxi queue was going to be a long wait, but appeared to move quickly when we accidentally walked by that exit. The departure signage appears to be well organized and well labeled. Just so many people!! The Beijing South massive station seems comparatively more mellow. We would still use the efficient and good high-speed trains in China though.

Mind you, the express trains, especially to Beijing, are great. But as an international traveler you have trouble finding even a functioning toilet at this train station that isn't just a hole in the ground. With so much international clientele, this would be more than recommended.

I used the high-speed train to go sightseeing in Suzhou from Shanghai. Since it was a Chinese public holiday, I reserved tickets in advance online. As per the advance information, I had booked the tickets in advance and it was indeed the right decision. For overseas travelers, especially those visiting China for the first time, we recommend that you make advance reservations and issue tickets at the station ticket counter the day before. I couldn't find the ticketing counter, so I ended up lining up at the non-reservation counter, wasting time, and many times the tickets were sold out, and it seemed like it took a really long time to get a ticket for those without a reservation. We used online reservations, but we were required to present our passports when reserving tickets, issuing tickets, and entering the venue. Even though I had made a reservation online in advance, I had to enter my passport number at the ticketing counter before they could issue me a ticket, so it took more time than I expected. (If there were 4 people, it would take time to input the number of round-trip tickets for 4 people.) There was a queue at the ticket counter, and then there was a baggage inspection and passport check at the entrance, which was very crowded and took quite a while. I'm glad I took action 30 minutes ago. This time, I used Shanghai Station, and there was plenty of waiting space, and there was space inside to eat snacks and buy souvenirs, so I didn't have to waste time even if I got there early. I tried using first and second class cars on high-speed trains and they were generally comfortable. When I was in the 2nd class train, there was a Chinese person sitting in the seat I reserved, but even though I couldn't speak to him, I showed him my ticket and he let me go right away.

Get there early if you need to buy a ticket, because this place is monster.Without a doubt the biggest train station I have ever seen.Wouldn't be surprised if they had a Great train to Hogwarts from here.Easy(ish) to get to... Taxi, or metro... Or train haha.Plenty of restaurants and amenities here, no problem for food, snacks, drinks.You will have the usual pushing and shoving through security and ticket check, but not as bad as other stations.Train station is also accessable by metro to the airport, but large luggage isn't that easy....Elevators and escalators are probably made in China, but maintained in China they usually ain't.

We went through Hongqiao Station twice during a recent trip to China.  The place is super busy but also super efficient.  We arrived late (flight delay) and so missed ur scheduled train, but the helpful staff were able to rebook us on  new train at no extra cost, all very efficient.  Good choice of food upstairs, fairly reasonably priced.  Easy to get a taxi on the way back.  Very stress-free.

I arrived at this station on a train from Wuhu and found it a little confusing on what exit to take from the platform. Luckily I found a nice woman who spoke very good English and she led the way to the taxi stand.  We seemed to go up multiple  levels. There was a long queue for taxis but it moved pretty fast.

You can plan your trip so that as soon as you leave the airport (after walking a long way from arrival to there because the airport is very big) you can catch the MagLev at the attached station. It is worth it.

I used Guilin → Sanjiang South, Sanjiang South → Yangshuo, Yangshuo → Guilin. I reserved my ticket in advance with Crip. Both were fully booked on that day. For example, the journey from Sanjiang South to Yangshuo took one hour and cost 47 yuan for second class, 75 yen for first class, and 47 yen for standing (same fare as second class). You can make reservations up to two months in advance on ctrip, but I think you need to make reservations early. As the day approaches, it will be "sold out". However, ctrip charges a handling fee of 40 yuan, so the handling fee ends up being more expensive than the ticket price. In addition, baggage inspection on trains in China is strict. I had a paring knife in my suitcase, but it was confiscated because the blade had a maximum length of 5cm. Also, using high-speed trains is very efficient as it saves travel time, but it also has the disadvantage that the tourist spots near high-speed train stations are very popular.

if you plan to take the train for example towards the 3 Gothes dam you will take the Chinese TGV in this station where everything is provided for the comfort of the traveler escalators clear and readable signage easy access to the platforms and all this on the scale of China
Because of the success of their railway infrastructure this station is a madhouse. However it works and we easily caught our train to Hong Kong

This is a very large train station with all the amenities: shops, restaurants, hot water for tea and coffee, even a de-stress room. Many Chinese high-speed trains come through here. I took a train from here to Quanzhou and had no problems, though best to get there early, beat the crowd, and queue up for your train...

Its easy to travel from here, all tickets are best brought on line and seats are strictly allocated. If your not Chinese carry your Passport with you at all times, you will have it examined before you are given your ticket, which you collect at the station
very clean railway station and easy to find your way. Helpful people everywhere. I wish railway stations in Belgium were as clean and nice.
Be sure to choose it. It's 8 minutes from the airport to the city, and it's comfortable and clean. It's really good. I think the price is about 20,000 won round trip, so just take it.

This is absolutely huge in size but once you know how it works, it is easy to follow. All trains run on time and you just need to allow time  to navigate your way through security checks, which are quick, just depends on size of queue, and the distance between entrance and the gate number you need to find.  If you have to pick up a ticket which has been booked prior, you also need to allow time at the ticket window.  The trains which leave here are incredibly, fast, modern, clean and roomy and cannot recommend more highly.
