Very efficient railway station with trains departing to all points North, South, East and West. So many eating options, very easy to navigate and to buy train tickets.

The toilets here a grose! I have no idea how people can use them and how a station like this can allow their toilets to get like that. It is also very confusing for someone who does not speak chinese. Most of shanghai caters to westerners so I thought it very weird that this station does not.

The High Speed ​​Train Station. It has a size of 2 Airport Terminals like EZEIZA (Argentina), you take the Train to Beijing that takes 4 hours and to other destinations, it is Magnificent, it has more than 20 Boarding Gates towards the Platforms. The Green Line 2 Metro links the two Airports and the Train Station
I visit this station in order to buy the Fast train ticket to BeijingNo clear information in English signboardNo Wifi and the Toilet is bad smell

Don't go out if you have nothing to do. There are so many people here. I waited for a taxi in the basement for half an hour and the car couldn't get in because it was blocked outside. It's better to go to the building outside and call for a pick-up.

Impressive how efficient this works. It must be handling a million or more passengers a day. On a normal Friday all goes smooth and on time. There are a few desks for foreigners. You must have a passport to book a ticket. There will be random stranger that can help. The picture is in Hangzhou but the idea is exactly the same.

Of course, each train departs from a fixed platform, and the ticket gates open about 15 minutes before the scheduled departure time. It's like waiting at the airport gate. Also, the doors of the Shinkansen will close two to three minutes before the scheduled time, so please do not get out of the train to take photos. The door closes automatically without ringing the bell. About 40 minutes to Tianjin. The maximum speed was 295km/h, but it was very comfortable in first class. Even a first class car costs around 1,700 Japanese yen.

Big railway station neighbouring with Hongqiao airport in Shanghai. Great 👍 possibility to connect train 🚂 and flight travelling. There is subway under railway station what makes the traveling even easier into the city 🌃. Many choices of restaurant on second floor but the railway station is permanently crowded so very little place to relax
Very functional and efficient. Easy to find your way around.  There is a lack of quality places to eat and comfortable seats to sit on.

A big railway station with clean environment. Usually crowded as you can travel to many different parts of China from this station. I personally feel that it is better equipped (more facilities and shops) than the Pudong International Airport.

The customer service was really terrible. The officer number 03331 was screaming and mad while there was a bit of misunderstanding at the ticket counter.  She also threw passports and tickets without even looking at us while returning it to us. Thanks for treating us so badly.
This is railway station and is also connected to airport. Mainly used for Bullet Train to BEijing and other parts of China

This is the main station for bullet trains in and out of shanghai. If staying at the centre of Shanghai an easy taxi ride will get you there.The station is huge like and airportMake sure u book your train tickets on ctrip or at the ticket office in advance.One must have the ticket and passport at least 30mins before departure due to security and the size of the station. If getting tickets from ticket office come at least 2hrs before hand as there's long queues..U need passport to buy the tickets and need it to to travel. Or u can book line via ctrip and collect at least one he before departure as there's queues.The ticket will say the gate number..When it light up then u can go through the gate..And then the ticket shows the coach number where you should queue up on the platform.

It was a 22hr trip on a sleeper. We had a sleeper just for two which was o.k. Bed was hard like most of the beds in China. The dinner meal was basic but not too bad. If you don't want to use chopsticks take your own knife & fork. We ate breakfast with a worker cleaning his teeth & shaving in the bar area right next to us...quite off putting. We had our own bathroom but no shower.  If you don't expect too much it was a good trip.

A huge station that can be reached by train, taxi, car, metro and located next to the domestic airport. Only regret: this station is far from Pudong airport. (International flights. (Station frequented many times from 2008 to 2012)
This is a very big railway station , very busy and very crowded. Shops and restaurants all over . Near the old airport .

this combines and integrated airport and train station is about 30 minutes fro m the center if there is no traffic.You need a passport to get a train ticket and screnn luggage.If you have a lot of luggage get a porte and he will put the luggage on the train.Tip him 100 rmb -its worth his sweat and not yours with all the people there

Speaking of Hangzhou East Railway Station, you may have a hard time finding a place to buy tickets. When I was heading back from Hangzhou to Shanghai Hongqiao, the purchasing location at the west exit was closed, so I had a hard time asking the staff where I could purchase it. I finally found out that I could buy it at the east exit, so I was confused as to whether I should go there. If you find a place near the east exit where you can buy it, there's only a vending machine. The counter next door is also closed. I couldn't even scan my passport to confirm my identity, so I thought I wouldn't be able to go home today, so I went to the trouble of asking the staff, and it turned out that there was a staffed counter on the next floor up. When I finally made my way to the counter, it was very crowded. I'm sure it wouldn't have been so difficult if I could read Chinese, understand the instructions on the signboards, and have a conversation with the staff. The Shanghai Hongqiao Station I was going to was so spacious that I thought it was an airport terminal, so I kept looking for the station, only to find out that I was already there lol.
Large station, but quite clean and cozy by Chinese standards and also something for people who don't speak Chinese.

We visited via the metro from West Nanjing Road to collect our fast train tickets to Xi’An. We had booked online and the emailed voucher said we could exchange it for tickets at any train station in mainland China. We tried to do this at a metro station but were told we could only collect them from Hongqiao. If you collect your ticket on the day of travel then allow plenty of time. We collected ours a few days early. Once you get into Hongqiao, head straight for 2F. This second floor has ticket booths, shops and the departure lounge. Don’t be too concerned about trying to figure out which ticket counter to go to. The Chinese are very accommodating. To find your train, look at the board. Names of destinations are in Chinese so look for your train number eg G1924 and the departure time. It will tell you which gate to go to eg 16. Go to that area. On one side of the waiting area is 16A and on the other is 16B. At the gate you will see your train number again and then, for example 1-5. This means that if your ticket says you are in car 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5, then 16A is your gate. 16B will be for cars 6, 7 etc. You will be allowed to go through checkin 15 mins before departure. Don’t be late!!! There are sockets for charging on the train plus boiling water and toilets. Take your snacks as choices are limited and staff do not speak English.
It seems that not all trains reach their maximum speed. When I rode in the evening, I covered 431km, but when I rode during the day, it was only 300km.

I rode the bullet train for the first time from Shanghai to Qufu. I reserved the ticket in advance from Japan, and when I arrived, I showed my receipt and ID at the station and picked it up. By the way, this station is two subway stops from Hongqiao Airport Terminal 1. Even if you assume that the travel time after leaving the airport will be crowded and you will get lost, I think you will be fine within 30 minutes. The platform is located on the second floor above the ticket office. An airport? ? It's such a big station. There are many shops inside, so you can enjoy your time while waiting. The platforms are clearly displayed on the bulletin board, so just check the number of the train you are boarding and line up. The Shinkansen itself is very similar to Japan. I think it would be a more comfortable trip if there were quiet people around. I guess the local people are quite tolerant of noise, and the difference from Japan is that they talk normally on their cell phones, and for some reason many people don't wear earphones when listening to music, watching movies, or playing games, and I was surprised at first to hear quite a variety of sounds coming from everywhere. Well, once I got used to it, I was able to read, take a nap, and eat my lunch in comfort!

Hongqiao Railway Station is very large, and it is next to the airport. There are really many entrances and exits. If you don’t ask clearly for the first time, you will really get lost. Because airports, subway stations, and even train stations in China require security checks before entering, the queues are really long when there are many people. The main reason is that the traffic lines are poorly organized and the Chinese people are a bit lazy.

I usually prioritize overnight sleeper trains, which I like, but maybe because of the Labor Day holiday, I didn't have any, so I used them for long distances for the first time in a while. However, I don't mind the price for short distances, so it was expensive for me, but compared to Japan's Shinkansen, it is reasonable and convenient.
On the high-speed train heading from Suzhou to Hongqiao, I first saw a speed display of 306 km/h. I think it's faster than Japan's Shinkansen.

I was in line to get the ticket, a man approached me with a handyman in his hand and an identification saying that he was a terminal operator, he made me skip the line. He asked the person selling the ticket if there was room on the train to my destination, which the other told him no. He personally took me to the bus terminal that is upstairs and wanted to board me on a bus, telling me that it cost 400 rmb, I told him no and they started to lower the fare. It is a sales maneuver, I do not recommend it, after you are in the middle of nowhere they ask you for more money, so be careful.
Comparable to an airport, very clean and well signposted. There are restaurants and lounges. Arrival and departure by taxi is quick and easy.

Station with great connection, next to the Honquiao airport, the only problem is that those who sell the tickets do not understand English. In general, poor disposition of the workers throughout the station. You can enter the platform 15 minutes before the departure of the train and only up to 3 minutes before departure. Without a ticket there is no trip. It is full of fast restaurants at the station.
Especially if you want to grab some food before you leave, there are plenty of options you can choose from.
This station is always crowded, but keeps moving the people on an efficient manner. Security is relatively easy to navigate and there are restaurants in the complex
Like all places in China, the Shanghai Hongqiao Railway Station is massive. It is colocated with Hongqiao Shanghai airport and the metro train lines as well as the intercity high speed rail.

I traveled in a second class train between Shanghai and Wuxi, and the ride itself was comfortable. The seat arrangement and electronic bulletin board must have been copied from Japan, but the noise from another train passing by while I was waiting at the station was no small feat. Japan has not yet caught up with Japanese technology.

The high-speed rail is basically in Hongqiao, so I must come there countless times every year. The management is standardized and orderly. Although the flow of people is very large, it is still a good station. The catering industry is very convenient, mainly fast food

I was very impressed with this rail station as the let you come in to get your tickets. They also offered a really nice variety of food and spas. It was more like an airport. Best rail station that I have been to in China!!!!!

4/22 Beijing-Shanghai High-Speed ​​Railway Shanghai Hongqiao -> Beijing South Railway Station, the filial piety trip is over. Take the Airport Express Line 1 directly to Pudong. The fare is 30RMB and you can pay in cash on the bus. The journey takes about an hour. Although it is a holiday, there are many passengers, the order is maintained well and the traffic is smooth. There are all kinds of food stations in the station (see the attached picture for details), and there is no shortage of various souvenir shops! The only interesting thing is that smoking is allowed on the platform by default, so addicts can relax before getting on the bus! ha!

One of the biggest railway station I have ever seen. Very huge and equally systematic. Very crowded. Mostly for high speed bullet trains. Better to reach 1-1.5 hrs before departure of your train. Very close to Hongqiao Airport.
A huge train station - top organization - we were here just 15 minutes before departure and that wasn't a problem. Security checks at the entrance are also quick. Top!

The round trip takes approximately 4 hours each way from Shanghai Hongqiao. I was in 2nd class on the way there and 1st class on the way back. The seats in 2nd class were quite flat and it was quite painful to sit for a long time, but the seats in 1st class were wide and comfortable. However, on both the round trip, the inside of the car was noisy due to people talking and using cell phones, and there were countless marks on the floor from spilled drinks, so the level of comfort was quite low. It's about 600km one way, and I think 2nd class was around 230 yuan and 1st class was around 310 yuan, so it would be safer to choose 1st class. However, it should not be compared to Japan's Shinkansen.
We were taking the express train to Hangzhou from this station. It’s really easy to navigate and find the platforms. And the express trains are very clean and comfortable.
Huge station but really easy to get to, given public transport in Shanghai, no problem for Western travellers, everything very well signposted in English

I think it was a bit unclear, especially when changing from train to subway or subway to train, which caused everyone to take a long detour. Only there was no smell of smoke inside the train, and the smell of smoke was all there when you got out of the carriage...the air was terrible.
Bullet from Beijing comes here. Grand station like an airport. From here take line two subway to city. Must have more information desks.
It is big, though crowded station. Be prepared for some leadtime if you plan to buy the train tickets at the spot.

The geographical location is close to Hongqiao Airport, where most of Shanghai's high-speed rail lines are located. The transportation is convenient, with direct access to Metro Line 2 and Line 10. There are also many places to eat, which is very convenient.

When you arrive at Hong Kong airport, the train is the best way to get to your hotel. It connects with a bus station that takes you to your hotel or leaves you very close. It is an excellent, comfortable and economical service. It shines for its cleanliness and accessibility.
well organized, and easy to find what you need. Seems like they have everything under control. Maybe it could use some more food vending places.

At this train station it is essential to take care of children, the number of people crowding the station is uncontrollable, it is very easy to get lost here as the train converges with many simultaneous arrivals and departures. At the top of the station is the food area which offers eastern and western services, credit cards are accepted. The ideal is to arrive with enough time to locate the correct exit door to the platform. The porter service is very expensive. Depending on the distance to travel, the time can be very fast since they are trains that go more than 400 km/h according to government regulation (initially they traveled above 500 km/h but have been decreasing to avoid accidents), the time also varies depending on the stops the train makes. It offers very competitive costs compared to a flight. The trains have oriental bathrooms so you will have to be prepared to use the bathroom in a stinking hole and sometimes without toilet paper.
Even for a Traveller with zero Chinese language skill, I didn't have any issues navigating through the massive station.

Despite being a little far from the city, from Shanghai Hongqiao you can connect via high speed to the main cities in China. It is recommended to arrive a little in advance (1 hour), as even when purchasing online, foreigners need to collect a ticket with passport at the counter and sometimes there is a long queue. The station has excellent infrastructure, with local and international restaurants and is connected to the city's metro and Hongqiao airport in the same complex.

Very clean and efficient operation. Trains run on time so allow yourself plenty of time. One needs a google translator or to travel with someone that speaks Chinese as understandably so nothing is in English when buying a ticket. You can also buy online which is helpful. Don’t forget your passport as you cannot travel without it.

The station is huge and has many platforms. The crowds of people who buy tickets can also be objective. You must go through X-ray security inspection when entering the station (whether your luggage is a suitcase, a bag, a leather bag, or a backpack). And buying tickets requires real-name authentication.
Super cheap trains, very clean station with many services inside, shops, restaurants and entertainment, I recommend if you want to save money on transportation that you use this service.
A huge station where you have to go through security before entering. To buy tickets, it's in the building to the right of the station when you face it. Comfortable trains.

Huge stationAll signs and departure boards are in English and Chinese which helps you get on the right train!I can imagine what it must be like at spring festival! Thousands of people everywhere. Good food court upstairs for fast food Chinese style!Gates to platform open minutes before train departure. Get in queue for that in plenty time!

I used the train between Shanghai Hongqiao and Wuxi for work. I took a first class seat on both the round trip. The leg space is wide and good, but the seat is worn out. The seat may not stop reclining midway, or the seat cushion may be flattened. As always, I'm always talking loudly on my cell phone. The good thing is that there is no smoking inside the car and you can move quickly. If you smoke, go down to the platform while the train is stopped at the station and it's time to smoke. Wuxi Station was undergoing expansion work.
Located right next to the airport, you can easily connect there... in my case I took the train to Yiwu

Traveling during Chinese new year, we were cautioned and warned that the trains and train stations would be a total nightmare. But we found this completely untrue.  Shanghai Hongqiao certainly was crowded, but there were many seats to await the trains, some of them quite comfortable.  The big board gives you ample notice which boarding lane your train will be at, and which side your car will be. 15 minutes ahead of time, the light for your train number turns orange and people start queueing up.  Soon you will be standing on your spot and your train car door will pull up to exactly where you are. You then board the bullet train, on time, and zip to your destination, near or far. They have a very efficient system, and even during New Year’s and spring festival, it was smooth sailing. I do recommend that you have a tour agency purchase your tickets for you in advance if you travel during high traffic times.
I went for almost an hour, based on what I had read. However, although the station is quite large, the entire boarding operation is easy.

There are many subways and high-speed trains, and there are buses to Hongqiao Airport Terminal 2 next to it. Now there are many merchants stationed here, and you can buy a lot of food and souvenirs. It is a very convenient transportation hub. The only thing that needs to be improved is that there should be more signs and they should be clearer.
Very busy, but everything is well marked.  I would not hesitate to use the station again.  The bullet train ride is worth it all by itself.

Compared with Beijing station, it is a nice station, even there are many travelers you never have the feeling it is crowded. But the service could be improved. At first more English speaking personal and second a special line for picking up the online bought ticket. It is not convinient to come to early to the station if you always have to expect 1 hour waiting in a line for a booked and payed ticket, but this belongs to all stations.
The place made me wonder the duality of the nature -  Shanghai Hongqiao Railway Station is quite busy and yet very serene.

Don't be over awed by the size and the crowds.The centrally located info booths have English speakers that are extremlly helpful and friendly.That is also the location of the Red Cap luggage porters who will carry your luggage and get to by pass the cues to get to your train for a very small price. I think it was $10.Worth every cent. However, they mostly don't speak English.If you bought business class seat (they are so cheap, why not) you get free use of the 1st class VIP lounges which give you a comfortable, quiet lounge and free baggage storage. Also free food and drinks and the red caps come and pick you up to catch the train.So its a marvelously well run organized station and easy to navigate.Trains at bottom level. Subway 1 floor up. Main floor and gates 1 floor up. Balcony shops and food 1 floor up.Note, you will have to go through security checks to get in. This is normal, but can be a long queue so allow extra time before your train.I went 2 hours early and relaxed in the VIP lounge until the Red Cap came and got me and my luggage, took me the back way to the train avoiding the crowds and I was first on the train. Not bad for $10.The only thing this place doesn't have is a souvineer shop.They seem hard to find in some parts.

The Largest railway  station in Asia, and feels it. Until you see from a height where to go, it can be quite confusing, but looking down  it becomes more understandable what is going on. If you have a pink ticket like we did which was issued by our agent, you show it to the person at the boarding gate, don’t go to the ticket office as you don’t need to, if you have the pink ticket. We were gate 5 which was in the top right corner on the ticket, carriage 10 seat 4F which was printed under our destination. When you arrive at the station, pass through security and there are large blue boards confirming the gate number for your train. After a coffee (upstairs there are a few eateries) we went and waited by our gate 45 minutes before departure. You can go to a or b gate. On the gate sliding door will show which line for which ticket, for us left was pink and the 3 to the right were blue. Above the gate will be the trains leaving from that gate, your train number will turn green when the gate opens for boarding about 15 minutes before, until then they are orange. Find your carriage number and seat and away you go. They announce in English  prior to the next stop. There is a power point on the train for charging. Ps if near holiday time, book your ticket in advance, we almost missed out and we booked 2 days earlier. We used Travel China Guide, they were great, also sent information on approx taxi price to station and info on the station.

We took the high-speed train from Shanghai to Beijing, and arrived at the station pretty early because our morning tour ended earlier than expected. The seats were mostly all taken - and as we witnessed throughout China, people just throw their bags/luggage on as many seats as they want with no concern for people that can't find a seat. We had purchased business class seats on the train (worth every penny in so many ways), so we had read there was a VIP lounge to wait in, but there are no signs, and nobody seems to know where it is! We walked around for quite a while before finally locating it. I even searched through reviews on here, with no info, so here you go! It's behind track gate 9B, near entrance number 4 of the station. It was small but significantly less crowded (maybe because nobody can find it?), and it was air conditioned!!! It felt amazing. They had a few little snacks and a refrigerator with bottled teas and water (downside: refrigerator didn't work, so the beverages were warm). But that air conditioning and quiet space were great. The only bathrooms in the building are Eastern toilets. I know this is China, but most other bathrooms that we used on our trip had both Western and Eastern toilets, especially in high-travel areas. So make sure you have tissues/toilet paper on hand! The bathrooms are also full of people smoking cigarettes, and it hits you hard when you enter. I was in and out quickly, but left with my hair and clothes reeking of cigarette smoke for the rest of the day. There were also employees eating lunch at sink counter in the bathroom. So that was interesting... Besides the bathrooms, the station was fairly clean, and there were tons of options for food. The lines were crazy to board our train, which was to be expected, and in typical Chinese fashion there was lots of pushing and shoving, but overall the boarding process was easy and the gate was easy to find. We would use this station again - with a business class ticket!

It's about twice as expensive as first class, but the fully flat leather chairs are perfect. You can set it to your desired position electrically. The flight attendants who tried their best to speak English that was difficult for Japanese elementary school students to receive a passing grade or higher. Although the journey took time during lunch, a boxed lunch was included. The drink service was similar to that of an airplane and was very comfortable.

The station looks more like an airport. There are a lot of people. You are allowed onto the platform with tickets and only your own. There is a scoreboard in English. In general, the navigation is ok. Trains in China are a very convenient form of transport. Just take tickets with a seat. Sometimes there are no seats and people are standing.

The fast train to Beijing leaves from here. Be in very good time as the place is huge station. It tooks quite fast through security check, but you can't be in hurry when arriving. Took a while to walk from end to end.
As good as any international airport. It has more than 20 odd railway tracks. You can reach there by line 2 & 10 of subway.

During my recent trip to China I used fast trains three times including the routes from Hangzhou to Shanghai and from Shanghai to Suzhou. Efficient and punctual I must say. The Shanghai Hongqiao station is immense, well organized and clean, like the others that welcome fast trains. An interesting alternative for touring the country.
This is one of two major stations in Shanghai with most high-speed trains departing and arriving there. It is well designed and maintained but hardly a tourist attraction all by itself.

This is the easier of the two main Shanghai train stations to get to, get in, and get out of. Most Chinese public transportation hubs are bristling with security stations, and Hongqiao Railway Station is no exception. There can be security at the entrance for the ticket windows, and there is certainly security screening to get into the waiting area. When purchasing tickets, you need to present your passport. I was once successful with my US Passport Card, which I just happened to be carrying, as I had not realized that identification was necessary for purchasing train tickets, but then, this is China...If you are traveling alone, get your snacks before going through the security, because there are no food or beverage vendors in the waiting area. When we were last there, they had arbitrarily divided the rather large waiting hall into two zones, so make sure you go into the correct waiting area for your track of interest. As we were a party of two, I sat in the waiting area guarding the luggage while the wife went to rustle up some snacks, so there is no problem with consuming food and beverages in the waiting area.As far as the trains go, the high speed rail is a lot of fun to ride. We tend to book First Class because it is not that expensive, is very comfortable, and has ample room for the luggage.

The high speed train system in China is wonderful.  As an added benefit, you depart and arrive at brand new, high tech stations.The Shanghai Hongqiao Railway station is modern and easy to navigate.If you are arriving by train, you need to know a few things:1.  The station is HUGE.  You may be walking a long distance to get to taxis or the subway system.2.  The taxi line system is very efficient, but the line can be very long.  You walk down a very long railed channel.  If you are carrying luggage, this can be a little difficult as the channel isn't wide enough to carry one bag on each side of you.  You end up pushing them ahead of you.3.   The taxi system is very efficient.  An endless number of cabs approach.  The attendants fill about nine cabs at a time, then another nine take their places.4.   You want to bring along your hotel address card or a printed address from the hotel website.  Assume your driver reads Chinese only.

This is a major railway station in Shanghai with very frequent scheduled express train to all major cities in China. We booked our tickets at Shanghai Railway Station but took the G-Series express train to Hangzhou from the HongQiao Railway Station. Train will depart on-time - so be early for security clearance, especially during festive season when the queue can be horribly long! We took the EGoBus (RMB$38 per pax) from our Marriott City Centre Hotel to the Railway Station.
This place is always packed and lines to buy tickets are long.You can buy online and then pick up at the station..just look for a window with no line up for pick them up. Will need passport.

Very clean, beautiful, everything works. Elevator, parking, airport, train station, restaurants, there is also a metro station, and even a wonderful hotel inside the airport building.... All in one giant complex.
Easy to get around. Modern. Pretty. Comfortable. 100 recommended. You board up to 7 minutes before the train leaves so be careful.
Took the Shanghai-Nanjing CRH hi speed train from this station. Its  convenient and is just a railway station. Not much to mention really.

Very large and very busy for the unprepared and non Chinese visitor. Go to window eight to change your ticket or ask anyone for help or to just find a window where you can buy a ticket. Getting a taxi from the railway station into the city is quite easy. Do not fall for the hucksters and fake officials who want you to take a private car somewhere instead of getting into a legitimate Taxi. Follow the overhead signs to go to the Taxi Q and just get in line and wait like everyone else it goes pretty fast maximum  I ever waited was about 25 minutes. Most of the time is much shorter.   The taxis in Shanghai that you take from the station for completely legitimate and very reasonably priced and it will cost you about 30 to 40 to get into the city maybe 60 if you have to go all the way to the bund.   Don't worry it's all legitimate.

Clean, bright and HUGE!  Great train station and easy to navigate.  Best way to travel!  There were plenty of food options including Starbucks, Subway etc.  Get there early to go thru security and get into line to wait for boarding.
The station offers connection to almost every place in China, is huge in space and always very busy. Make sure to book trains in advance and always keep a valid ticket with you.
Although there have been accidents before, the China Shinkansen is very convenient. It's comfortable and you can easily make reservations online.

Hongqiao railway station.I have never seen such a large railway station almost as big as an airport. Having arrived at Pudong international airport Shanghai we had to get to Hongqiao railway station to continue our journey to Beijing, as we wanted to experience the Bullet Train. You can do this transfer either by taxi or maglev/metro information on website.You must book your train travel either on line or at the ticket office identification needed. Give your self plenty of time before your journey as you have to queue to go through security to get into the station then again to get tickets. This station is also joined to Hongqiao Airport, there are fast food and shops it is also joined to a Mall. The trains are on time and leave on time they allow you to board the train about 15 minutes before. Your ticket states carriage and seat number tickets need to be shown at gate and on board train.Our journey was about 5 hours seating comfortable toilets clean and food on board.The train travels smoothly at about 200miles an hour with views of the real China. This was a fantastic experience for a couple of pensioners the return journey was just as exciting.

Had to catch the train from here to Beijing. I left my hotel from the Bund at 7:30 am and arrived at 8:15. about an $18 (AUS) fare.The station is near an airport of the same name and appears as big as the airport.However, I was expecting a difficult experience in picking up my ticket. So I was pleasantly surprised to find a clean station, thousands of people going to and thro and bill boards explaining in English where to go and all the train info.I knew how to get my ticket as I was given an Eticket from  China DIY who were excellent in explaining the process.Once I had my ticket I then asked Inquiry to explain the train number and gate number. No problems here.Next found a seat and waited with hundreds of others who were travelling today.Lined up with travellers and found my coach, seat number and was ready to go.Great station, great experience.

It's a great, large terminal with nothing to say about the hardware. There is a profoundness to it that makes you feel that in order to cope with China's 1.4 billion population, we need solid station students. If the people who use it develop a little more, it will become a pleasant station, but do we still need another 20 years?

This new modern railway station is very large, clean, and safe. All the signs are additionally written in English. It was very orderly and the lines were very smooth. It has a good collection of places to eat and Starbucks. I found it very easy to navigate and use for my journey. Give yourself a little extra time to go through security and navigate to your train.

I had no difficulty whatsoever navigating my way to the proper ticket kiosk and my train. My only recommendation is to prebook your travel with TravelChinaGuide.com.  I received excellent service from them that enhanced my travel experience greatly.
Cant even find a place to seat. Most of the time we just seat on the floor while waiting for our train

Although they look similar, the seats are poor quality (even in first class, which is the seat of green cars in Japan), and long distances are difficult. I have no choice but to choose not to stop as much as possible. Buying tickets is far away from the boarding gate, and at large stations there are so many trips that it's really a pain. It's really much better than the old green train, but inside it's just a normal train that's fast.

Very big station, very clean. A lot of shops around the concourse, from eating to shopping.  Very well organised boarding, I was part of a party of around 100 people and we all were directed to our high speed train carriage.

Easy to navigate through the train station. Have to be at the train station early if you need to retrieve the train ticket. The station has plenty of shops and restaurant if you need to grab some food before boarding.

We found it easy enough to navigate except that on arrival we didnt know whether to go upstairs or downstairs to exit. Also there is an elevator which is excellent when yoy have cases.Taxi management was goid and safe

This is the railway station where the high speed train arrives/departs to Beijing. The cheapest and easiest way to access is via the metro which arrives on a different floor. There are a number of floors where you can access or pick up tickets for the fast trains, just be aware not all the ticket outlets are open, but all are signposted and if closed just go up to the departure floor. The signs listing departures are easy to read and just lookup videos on YouTube which show you how if you wish to. There are plenty of places for a coffee and to get something to eat
An expansive but well organised terminus with many food outlets and ticket offices. Paramount to establish the location of the appropriate ticket office for your destination.

Two hours to get a taxi out of here- couldn't find the taxi rank so went through to Hongqiao Hub, thinking surely you can get a taxi from a shopping mall. It too over an hour to get to the outside works and then no taxis would take me where I wanted to go. Never again

It is not a tourist attraction! It is a very large station that looks like an airport and is very well connected to other transportation systems (metro, buses, airport x metro). There are many places where you can eat something simple.
Japan's Shinkansen itself lol Are the vehicles made in China? It was a little scary, but I rode it. When I actually rode it, it was extremely comfortable.

High speed train in China is an experience... big bigger grand... very modern station all in one airport 2017... linked to Hongqioa airport but still more than an hour's drive from PVG airport. A metro connection will be added later.

We arrived at the station early. The tickets had already been purchased and just needed to be printed. There is no English at the terminals for printing tickets, so foreigners just have to queue at the ticket office and print there. We could say we were lucky, the queues were not long. But keep in mind that on holidays and weekends they increase significantly. We stood at the ticket office on floor B1. Trains arrive on this same floor. On the second floor the train boards and departs. There are cafes above the second floor. When you are boarding, look at the carriage number indicated on the ticket and find your exact exit, so that when boarding the train you do not have to go to the correct carriage with all your belongings.
The station is the size of a small town Biggest we have ever saw Once again organised  on time trains and clean not a spec. Of rubbish

We traveled by bullet train from Beijing to Shanghai in less than 5 hours. Train very punctual, clean, everything is extremely efficient and organised. We purchased the tickets in advance by relying on the Chinahighlights agency and having them sent to our hotel in Beijing. Very efficient service that we recommend. The trip was perfect.

This is a massive train station. It moves a gazillion people a day.  I was amazed how smoothly it works. I wouldn't call,this an attraction as much as a transportation hub.  Btw it is right next to the Hongqiao Airport which seems equally massive.One detail, DON'T FORGET YOUR PASSPORT!  It is required to purchase a train ticket if you are not a Chinese National.Oh and Hongqiao has a subway station to line 2!

This train station is huge and very convenient! It can reach Beijing in the upper direction and Zhuhai in the south. There are a lot of people coming in and out! The train schedule and control are very accurate. The station is very big, there are many people, the signs are not clear enough, and the attitude of the service staff can be improved! It is not very convenient for foreigners to buy tickets at automatic ticket machines. It would be better if this could be strengthened!
The place is huge, thousands of people coming and going. But the place is very clean, safe and well signposted.
A lot of people, but that's not going to effect the efficiency of the operations.Beware of touts, especially those taxi guys and be careful when you cross the road, reckless Drivers are plenty

Thousands of people gathered together on sitting areas or lining up in front of the gates to enter the trains. Very efficiently organized, I counted at least 26 gates , from which one there are trains sometimes every 15 min to different destination. Very few shops and expensive. The food court is located on the upper level.
We booked high speed train tickets and had to queue up to get it. The signage was confusing even we knew Chinese.  We therefore queued up twice to complete the task.

We traveled from the station several times and we were pleased how everything is well marked in English and everything is very clear. The organization of boarding the high-speed train is impeccable, without rushes and rushes. Everyone has their own place. The toilets were clean and accessible.

Full of people, even more than many famous airports. Furthermore, everyone is in a hurry because they must carry their suitcases, since there is no luggage check-in. Access to the platform is fluid and opens only about 20 minutes before departure. The building is huge, full of places to eat and some shops. It lacks seats, since since there are many people, they are insufficient.

Much better than Beijing station, modern, easy to get around, no hassle at all. Very well organised. Tip- line up for your train at least 45 minutes a prior if you have luggage to go above your seats because the luggage room above seats runs out quickly.Trains are always on time

There are many dining options and it is convenient, but the price is higher than outside the station. But it's really a bit troublesome to get into the station. All stations in China are like this. There are few entrances because of security checks.
I have often used the Fast Train which connects Chinese cities in a very short time at impressive speeds, the station is very clean and tidy
It is one of the largest train stations in Shanghai, after arriving by taxi at this station, we went by train to work in Taizhou

This was my 1st experience of Chinese transportation and I have to say I was highly impressed. This is a big, busy station but so very well laid out and easy to navigate. You have to go through security just like an airport but it was fast and efficient. Inside the large station is clean and spacious. The gates are well marked and all signs are in Chinese and English. If possible have your tickets purchased in advance and just check for your boarding area, again just like the airport, and just wait for your gate to open and the proceed to your platform and board. There are plenty of shops and food outlets. Arrive approximately 60 mins before departure if possible to give yourself time to get through security etc.
On a par with any of the top-rated airport terminals in the world. Shops, eateries, and comfortable waiting rooms.

Having spent 5 days in Shanghai, we decided to go to the city of Suzhou - eastern Venice. and went by train. Keep in mind that documents are checked when entering the station. so be sure to take at least a copy of your passports with you. We had copies and there were no complaints against us. the trains are clean. the seats are comfortable. there are toilets, of course, buy a ticket with a seat, otherwise you risk standing in a crowd of people
The biggest difficulty, besides the queues to catch a taxi, is getting information in English, even at the information center the attendants did not speak any other language other than Chinese.

Very busy pleace.Air transport, long dist fast / slow trains and subway lines meet here.English and Chinese signage is throughout.Book ticket in advance.We reched 2 hours in advance for fast train ride, and then waited 30 to 40 mintues before then let us on the platform
A busy bustling station. if possible book your ticket in advance. Signs are in English as well as Chinese so not too difficult to navigate.

There are crowds of people, and you have to queue up and pass the security check before entering the station. Non-Chinese passengers can only buy tickets at the manual counter. They start entering the platform about 20 minutes before the train leaves, and they are prohibited from entering the station about ten minutes before the train leaves. People who time it very well can easily miss the train.

I used a regular reserved seat from Guangzhou South Station to Guilin North Station. The seats were thoroughly cleaned, and they were cleaned once during the two and a half hour journey. As for the comfort of the seat, it was very concave due to my weight, and the backrest was lowered even though I didn't lower it, making it shaky. Large suitcases cannot be put up on the shelves, so if you don't mind, there is a space next to the entrance where you can store them. You can place it at the foot of your seat, but you can't move your feet. Also, if the backrests of the front seats are lowered, the space will become even narrower. People who did not have reserved seats filled the aisles between the cars. There are one or two toilets per vehicle. There is also a Western style, but it is horribly dirty. It's better to bring paper with you, even if you don't have it. If you don't line up properly, you will be cut into.

The Shanghai Hongqiao station is massive and bustling with people arriving and departing on the amazing high speed trains. It's a little confusing if you are meeting someone in the station and there are North and South Exits and a number of gates so I would recommend a meeting place of a cafe or restaurant, of which there are plenty in the concourse.Despite the slick marble and high overhead domed ceilings, the toilet facilities were disappointing with long queues for holes in the floor toilets which seemed at odds with the rest of the stations modern style.

Well organised clean and efficient the railway station is a great example of modern china. It can be a bit chaotic getting your ticket and getting in and out of the station but that's normal in China. Just make sure you arrive with plenty of time i.e 45mins before your train
This was easy to get to, easy to get something to eat, easy to get out tickets, and easy find our train.  Signage was good.  It's very crowded, but efficient.
It's a Clean and Crowded public train transportation station. The ticket counter staff are very friendly.

We were very much impressed by the Shanghai Hongqiao Railway Station. It is huge! And very clean, too. You'd be spoilt for choice when it comes to food. Our guide, bless her, brought us to Yang's Dumplings and we loved every sip, every morsel.

This train station is the hub of the fast train network in Shanghai. It is a bustling facility catering for millions of travellers every year. Access is easy and it is co-located (adjacent to) the Shanghai Hongqiao airport. If you are a first timer there are Porters known as "Red hats" that will guide you safely to where you need to be in what is a vast facility. We found it well worth their fee to be led directly to where we needed to wait and then have them come back at the appropriate time to put our bags on the train for us. (We just followed behind like grateful puppies!)My last piece of advice is that there are taxi ranks on all sides of the building but lots of "salesmen" in yellow jackets trying to catch you before you get to them to sell their own cars at very inflated rates. Beware also their warnings of 2 hour waits at the taxi ranks. They are just not true. If you can though, make sure you have your destination written in mandarin before you get to the front of the queue, the taxi drivers don't do English!

We took off from this station to travel to Hangzhou . The station itself is on the NR2 subway line and everything is well indicated - also in English . All in all traveling by Gtrain is child's play . the Chinese are super practical and efficient .

Once you arrive in Shanghai, the idea of ​​visiting China using the train as a means of transport has not been ruled out. Most of the main cities are well connected with high-speed trains that can exceed 400 km per hour. In Shanghai the departure station for the main connections is the Hongqiao Railway Station. Tickets must be purchased well in advance, even online, and my suggestion is to go to the station at least an hour and a half before departure. In Hongqiao Station, which is about 40 minutes by taxi from the city centre, you will find many restaurants, shops as well as a shopping centre. Everything inside is well organized so you will have no problem finding everything you need. The infrastructure is nothing short of colossal and in itself it will be a nice surprise to visit it. Renato

The train station is not impressive because of its beauty or size, but because of its spaciousness and the fact that there are always a lot of people walking around. Big suitcases - or huge plastic bags - are a constant. The stores and neon lights help to make the place urban and high tech.

We took the train from here to Beijing. The station is very large but well organized. Collecting the cards was relatively easy. It is also clearly indicated in English where exactly you need to be for your train.

Security can take a long time at this airport so allow an hour to get through security alone. However unfortunately flights are often delayed due to air congestion. So take a good book. If you're working make sure your computer and phone are fully charged. Power outlets are at a premium.
When I go back to Shanghai, if I go anther city and I usually to take the train from Hongqiao railway station. It is clean and nice.

Traveling by train in China is more like flying in most European countries. You go through security checks (equivalent to those in the subway) and board the plane. But everything worked perfectly and it was tidy and clean. A tip is to remember to bring toilet paper because there is no toilet paper at the station.
Excellent train station with great amenities. All trains run to a split second schedule, are clean and well organised.

An amazing experience and quite daunting.it would have to be the biggest in the world!It is huge but well planned out and with instructions from my agent to purchase the tickets written in English for me then translated to Chinese to show at ticket windows  and help from other travellers we  figured it out quite easily.
Not an attraction, but an excellent station that takes you everywhere. Train station at the airport. Taxi not necessary

Not unlike hundreds of other railway stations in China, this one is large, efficient and accessible to travellers. Tickets are easy to buy, don't mind the queues, and platform information easily understood for non- Mandarin speakers.
It's basically like going to the airport but without the number of security areas to be screened etc. there was only one and it took less than a minute. English friendly signs and easy to navigate.
The station is big. You will need some time to reach your gate. You should arrive earlier than the train as they will close the gate in advance from departure.
Impressive clean and well organized train station with modern amenities. Lots of touts offering transportation with negotiated price which is convenient if you don't want to wait

Amazingly easy to travel on the bullet train. Advice was to arrive one hour before departure to allow for security. We got through in about 5 minutes so had time to look around the station (although in the summer queues may be longer I don't know). It's like an airport with departures and departure gates listed on a big screen. You queue up at your designated gate number and they start to board about 15 minutes before departure. They stop people going through the gate 3 minutes before departure so if you are running late you do have time pretty much up to the departure time. On walking through the gate you hand your ticket to the conductor or put it through automated machines then you go down an escalator where the train is clearly marked with the carriage letter and the train number and destination- it would be pretty impossible to get the wrong train in my view. All signs are in English as well as Chinese. We booked first class tickets and were glad as the second class was very full and seats were smaller. In first class the seat has a foot rest and reclines - very comfortable. Also you have a hostess who gives you a bottle of drink (coke, orange or water) and a small lunch box with a roll, and a couple of snacks in them - not massive but ok. There is also hot water available constantly - the Chinese use it for their tea. But we brought some instant coffee sachets (Nescafé 2+1) which had milk included so we had coffee which was good. As you journey through there is a display showing the next station but they also announce the next station coming up in English and Chinese. Absolutely recommend this way of travelling around China. Easy, smooth and you see some interesting sights too. There is a socket for charging your phone in the seat. The stations and trains are immaculately clean as well.

We came from Beijing by bullet train. And we were shocked because the Beijing Station was nothing compared to how massive Shanghai one is...There you can get trains, busses and metro!!It is a suler organized place, way better than the train stations i have been in Europe. Full of shops and restaurants.

I was very impressed with my rail journey from Beijing to Shanghai on the high speed 'bullet' train. Travelling at an average of 310 kph was no mean feat. Arriving at Shanghai Hongqiao, the pleasant and well designed station offered efficiency, comfort and good directions. I was especially pleased with the signposting and the ease with which I obtained a taxi at the station. Escalators were in good working order and using the station was easy. If all stations were this easy to use.

I don’t know if it’s because I picked up the ticket online, but Hongqiao doesn’t require me to bring my ID card and ticket for real-name authentication at the security check. There are various fast food restaurants outside the waiting hall, but the prices are more expensive than outside. There are also some places selling coffee, light meals, and convenience foods in the waiting hall. There are also some clothing stores, bookstores, and other places where passengers can kill time. You can use second-generation ID cards to check tickets. Basically, ticket checking is done by machine, which is very convenient and fast. The overall infrastructure is first-class.

Unexpectedly, this train station is newer and more beautiful than Shanghai's airport. There are many delicious restaurants inside. It makes you feel like you are at Hong Kong Airport, which is more beautiful than Hangzhou Airport.

Hongqiao Railway Station (only CRH fast trains!) and Hongqiao airport (the old Shanghai airport SHA) together with their metro connections constitute one of the busiest transportation hubs on the planet. In fact the railway station has much of the buzz of an airport in its own right. Via metro lines 2 and 10 there is a good connection with the business and tourist centers of the city. Be warned that a lot of walking may be needed to get from railway to metro and vice-versa, and that lines are usually very long at the ticket counters. Plan accordingly!

most long distance high-speed train leave from that station. There is a METRO station under the station but the distances are long. Plan at least 15 minutes from the METRO to the plat forms. There are not enough ticket counters, so the queues are most times long, 1/2 hour waiting time is necessary. Better is to buy and get the tickets in advance.

I took a ride to Hangzhou to go sightseeing. I was able to purchase tickets without any problems as a Chinese official attended to me, but as I watched the process, I noticed that the process was surprisingly troublesome, as I had to show my passport. The inside of the train was not first class, but it was comfortable.

I took the train from Shanghai to visit a town out in the country.I did not have any trouble getting the ticket, finding the rail or the correct car.  it was very easy to do.got a taxi back to my hotel the next day with no problems.

This train station is the largest in Shanghai and connects other cities with super fast trains such as Beijing. This station is also integrated with Hongqiao airport so that we can connect directly from the train to the airport, especially terminal 2. Apart from that, it is also connected to the subway which goes to downtown Shanghai.

The integrated train and high-speed rail center is a huge train station. It is easy to get lost if you don't have a good sense of direction, and there is a constant flow of people. There are many restaurants inside, so you don’t have to worry about getting hungry while waiting for the bus.

Very bad. Some of the machines for buying subway tickets can only use coins, and some can only use banknotes. There are many people queuing up, which is very inconvenient. Especially the taxis are monopolized. They say that the queue will take an hour and that specific taxis will charge 260 yuan. Exaggeration.
I arrived on a train from nanjing and found the station too busy and chaotic to find the right exit to meet the driver who was waiting for me.

Central train station, from where you can go to almost all cities in China. Although a little chaotic, I advise you to go early. It is essential to go to the different windows to buy tickets with the name of the city where you want to travel written in Chinese.
Fast train and on time but need to add more counter for buy tickets and staffs who can Speak English.

The train station itself is very good, large, clean and orderly, but for me, who lives in Pudong, it is really annoying to travel by high-speed rail. It takes two round trips from Pudong to Hongqiao and Suzhou. There is a strong demand for the opening of the maglev from Longyang Road to Hongqiao Airport and Railway Station. Really, this will not only facilitate travel, but also save a lot of time.

Shanghai's new TGV station in the west of the city, not far from the airport of the same name. The Salle des Pas Perdus is a good kilometer long. The architecture is nothing great, but the space is well occupied by luxury boutiques and the TGV logistics are impeccable.

Had to take the fast train from Shanghai up north on. A good 6 hour journey for the thousand kilometres. With fast trains running over 300 km/h and a well-functioning station network and precise departures, it makes it easy and convenient. Absolutely recommendable.

One of the largest train stations in the world if not the largest. Amazing building, clean, well maintained and air conditioned, unbelievable amounts of people but some how it all works well and smooth. I suggest getting there at least 30 minutes before your train departure time cause it may take you 20 minutes to find the train boarding gates. If you want to buy some food in the multiple stores there it will take 15 to 20 minutes as the place is huge.

If you have not eaten in the city beforehand, it is best to take the subway to Hongqiao Railway Station. This way you can directly visit the underground food street with many choices. Not only are there few choices on the departure floor, but they are also divided into two isolated mezzanines, which is inconvenient.

The station is modern style, they have the lounge or the gate like at the airport.Big display screen to inform the destination status, gate and time to depart.There are restaurant, cafe, coffee bar, fruit store, etc, it's very comportable.
The high speed rail from Beijing connects here... is just next to the airport with the same name. Huge station but extremely well organised. Kudos.

I found it relatively easy to navigate. Went inside through security to buy ticket. I went up to a person as kiosks didn't appear to have language switch option. They weren't able to take Visa credit card so paid cash. A ticket from Shanghai    to Kunshan was 24RMB. You'll need to present your passport for travel. Once I got my ticket,  I found the train on the departure board, it's the A#### (A=letter #### number). Next locate your car number and seat upper right of ticket. There's different boarding sides based on car number. The gate numbers are the same but on opposite sides. There's some luggage storage on the train and power outlets available. The seats are spacious and the train is clean.

This station is one of China's great stations.  Travel from Pudong Airport is easy using subway line 2 - green line for under 10 yuan.  Do your homework and experience Chinese travel like a local.  I bought tickets from Travel China Guide that were delivered to my hotel with instructions to navigate Chinese rail from start to finish.  Give yourself at least an hour at the station to make sure you get to the right gate and have time to enjoy the local travel culture.  Travel from Pudong airport takes a little less than an hour.

Immense and well-serviced station, hub for many destinations with high-speed and long-distance trains. Spread over various floors and equipped with many shops, restaurants and cafes for all tastes and gastronomic cultures. Very clean and organized...a real feather in the cap.

The environment is not bad, but it is connected to the subway station, there are many exits, the venue is too big, and the signs are not clear. I can't always find the correct exit. Unless I don't live in Shanghai and pass by it every day, otherwise we come here occasionally on business trips and often get lost. It's okay if we are not in a hurry, but it will be really fatal if we are in a hurry.

No matter it is off-peak or peak hours, there are always huge crowds of people, but the circulation route is well planned and clearly marked, so there will be no doubts about getting lost, but the large number of people can't help but make people upset ~
Another piece of modern architecture in Shangai, not worthy to visit if you dont have to take a train, you can expend this time on better stuff

Impressive station! It would make you dizzy! A crazy world. We do not go onto the platform until we are invited. In any case, you have to go through a turnstile by swiping your ticket. In fact it looks more like an airport! The information panels are pretty epic.

The Hongqiao Railway Station is a magnificent train station with connections for the high-speed train and local trains. Direct connection to Honggiao airport and bus service to PVG airport. With some shops and restaurants and taxi in the S or N part. For high speed trains, be sure to pre-order seats online for seats. Especially on, before or after holidays.

Used the railway station to get to Hangzhou. Very modern & big. The ticket buying process was easy, the staff spoke English.It was not easy to navigate the station, a few more signs would be helpful.There are many places to eat or drink such as Costa coffee. A few little shops to buy drinks & snacks.However, the station is very modern but the male toilets were awful. The floor was swimming in urine, deeply unpleasant, especially for such a modern station.

I used it to travel from Shanghai Hongqiao Station to Wuxi for work. This time, I took the 2nd class seat. There were no seats available in 1st class. The price is 59.5 yuan. Since 1 yuan = about 17 yen, it is about 1,000 yen in Japanese yen. 1st prize is about 110 yuan. When I used it last March, there was a tremendous amount of talking (like swearing). I took the China High Speed ​​Rail from Shanghai to Beijing. The flight departs from the huge Hongqiao High Speed ​​Rail Station in Shanghai on time at 11 a.m. Business seats are fully flat, with blankets and slippers provided. Immediately after departure, there was a drink service and I ordered coffee. The coffee served with the cookies was a little warm but delicious. Lunch was served around 1pm. You can choose from three types: meat, fish, and noodles. I ordered noodles, so I had slightly spicy beef noodles. We arrived at Beijing South Railway Station at 15:58, 3 minutes behind schedule. It is surprising that it takes about 4 hours from Shanghai to Beijing. It was easier to read the time than the flight between Shanghai and Beijing, which has many delays, and the fully flat seats were very comfortable.

Why in earth someone would like to visit a railway station if not traveling and therefore forced to go? Anyway a review was requested so here it comes. A huge hall with lots of travelers, mostly locals, waiting for their trains. Worth to go? Yes, if you have to.
Easy to get to, very well connected to the main points of interest in Shanghai and easy to understand and find. Very large building but well maintained
This station is unbelievable It's well organised despite the thousands that travel through we caught a bullet train and were well impressed Train was on time and arrived on time what a shocker
Good station and clean. While you are waiting for the train, you also can shopping or eating in some restaurants here.

Like many other railway stations in China, Shanghai is a huge structure, where it is better to arrive in advance so that you have time to figure it out and simply run to the desired platform. If you need to buy or redeem a ticket booked through the website, you should arrive at the station 40 minutes, or better yet, an hour. The queues at the cash registers, when you find them and get to them, can turn out to be like a dry-drying shop during the years of Soviet shortages, especially if there is some Chinese holiday coming up. At the same time, there are a lot of ticket machines at the station! But many Chinese still prefer to wait at the ticket office; apparently they don’t trust the soulless machine... If you have the ticket in your hands, find your platform and wait patiently for boarding. Boarding is only possible from the station building; the turnstiles do not open before boarding and you will not be able to wait on the platform. Boarding happens quickly, and it starts 15 minutes before departure, so there’s no time to mess around. And be careful - the Chinese are on their way out, like the ninth wave in Aivazovsky’s paintings.
Spacious, and lots of eateries outside. Lots of groups too doing their dance exercise. Tickets can be bought by the machines

Everything is good, and there are service staff available for inquiries. The train station is very large, so be aware of the time. If you are not Chinese, you can only book train tickets on site and at the counter.
Excellent and clean railway station next to airport. High speed train runs from here to Beijing. I went to Jinan in 4 hours from Shanghai. Good facility.
A large central station with bus and airport connection. Ticket for the trains better pre-order via cellphone or internet, otherwise can be longer wait to get on the train.

Bring your passport and if you intend to travel, buy the return ticket first. On weekends and forget about finding a seat on trains without prior reservation. The stations are real airports in terms of cleanliness, silence and controls.

Hongqiao railway station is an important departure point for many high speed trains into china. It is very well organised , however due to its sheer size and also security controls it can be difficult to find your way . When you buy a ticket you will need your passport . This is to avoid Chinese buy many tickets for days where there is huge demand , like Chinese New Year , and sell them at the black market for high prices

There are often lines to get tickets. There is a security check from the moment you enter the station. There is a waiting room for each train, and you can only enter the platform just before departure. Once you get on it, it's quite comfortable. As far as I have experienced, there were no problems with company etiquette.

This train station is huge. If it's your first time there make sure to arrive early to catch your train in order to have time to understand where you need to go! It's pretty easy, you just need to queue in front of your door entrance, but so many people is quite impressive. You have a bunch of restaurants (Burger king, ...) The view on the trainstation worth a picture!)

Although I couldn't hide my anxiety, I rode thinking that it would probably be okay, but it wasn't that bad. The linear car also didn't have much of a sense of speed, considering the speed that the numbers were showing, and it was comfortable.

This station is connected to the Shanghai Hongqiao Airport, which gives you the ability to take high spped train all over china and makes it easy to comute from city to city taking the train into this station and going straight to a flight to another city or arriving at the airport and taking the train to another city.

The station is for all high speed train depart from Shanghai. The station is almost on the last stop of line 2 and take almost 1.5hr (9RMB) from Pudong Airport. If you have to catch a train at HQ after landed in Pudong, make sure you have enough time. It is faster to take airport bus line 1 from Pudong to HQ train station (30RMB) if you have less time. The station connected to the mall call Hongqiao Hub and you can walk there if you have long waiting time. Free wifi available at the train station (but you need to have local sim card). Large waiting area and many kind of food available. If you are getting out from the train station by taxi, be prepared as the taxi queue is always super long!

If you are used to European stations you have to take a train here. The noise is deafening. You will find yourself surrounded by thousands of screaming people running aimlessly and without education. Then once you have passed the controls and entered the train platform, everything changes in silence, the order and punctuality of the trains except when the train arrives and you have to get on.....forget your manners....don't think about letting anyone who gets off the train exit the carriage because a mass of people will arrive immediately from behind. people pressing to enter....and thinking that the seats are assigned...but we are in China....unfortunately or fortunately, judge for yourself

You can get to almost anywhere in China from here. It is the termination point for many of the high speed railways in eastern China. Huge, but simple - just one gigantic hall. You go downstairs for the taxi line - which is astoundingly long but moves quickly. You can also leave the station by transit (there is a subway line here), and that is recommended.

is very easy to get to compared to other main stations in Shanghai (metro line 2 or line 10) and is closer to the city center than the other ones as well...20 mins by metro to Jingan Temple.It is joined to Terminal 2 of Hongqiao International Airport and so pretty much has everything you would expect to find, including banks (airport part). All the eating places are near to the arrivals section of train station. There is free wifi in the station as well, which you activate by a sms code.The car park is 60 RMB for 24 hours or 10 RMB an hour. For park and ride purposes as well getting into Shanghai it is excellent.

For those of you travelling from Shanghai on the high speed rail network, it is more than likely that you will be going from or to this station. It is not located in or close to the city centre, but is really easy to get to. Metro lines 2 and 10 serve the station with the city centre and a cab ride is abut 70RMB.The station is really modern with lots of cafes/restaurants on a level above the main concourse. Just head to the gate that your ticket says the train will depart from, take a seat and wait for your displayed train on the digital screen to turn green. You will see a big queue forming by the gate, but they only usually only open the entrance gate to the platform 10 to 20 mins before the train is due to depart.

You can transfer to the long-distance bus station, take Line 2 to Pudong Airport, or go to Hongqiao Airport. There are also Hongqiao transportation hub, Hongqiao complex, and many company headquarters nearby. There is a lot to eat, and the price is a little more expensive than outside.

Hongqiao is a brilliant transport hub between flights, cars, buses, long-distance trains, taxis, buses and subways. You can change quickly. The whole complex is very clean. Shopping is very developed. Only the transport connection to Pudong Airport could be better.
Your typical Chinese railway...people smoking inside can be very annoying, it's also very very dirty at times. Having said this it does make it easy and convenient to get around.

Modern and well organized,hard to get lost. Massive and impressive, like many new buildings and infrastructure in China. You can find English speaking staff available there, there is a metro station and a MAGLEV station available. Try the MAGLEV, riding above ground 450 kmh!

Estivemos nesse terminal duas vezes. Cuidado com o golpe do taxi. There are pirate taxis that charge you absurdly to go to the center. Tente chegar antes das 11 para pegar o metrô. Travel by fast train in China is an experience worth the effort. Its cost effective, fast and convenient. The trains are spotless clean, well maintained; just as the stations are. Shanghai Hongqiao Railway Station is one of the bigger railway stations with a number of high speed trains with a lot of people. However I was impressed by how organized and clean it was. It was easy to figure out but this can be overwhelming for some.

This station, built exclusively for high-speed trains, is in a different category than anything known from Europe. 29 tracks with regular, closely scheduled train services. I travel here weekly. I went back and forth from Beijing to Tianjin. The Chinese Shinkansen is a mixture of Japanese and German technology and is being operated with the claim that it was developed domestically. The Japanese Hayate-type vehicle, which was a hot topic in the past, has left the main route, and now it seems that vehicles similar to the German ICE are taking center stage. With a maximum speed of 285 km/h, it connects Beijing to Tianjin in just over 30 minutes, and the fare is 54.5 yuan, which is quite cheap for Japanese people. The seating arrangement of the regular cars is the same as in Japan's Shinkansen trains, with two-seater and three-seater seating, as well as standing seats. The running intervals are similar to Japan's Shinkansen, but the regular cars on all trains are almost full. There are no on-board sales, but there is a kiosk. I think it's because of PM2.5, but some vehicles are already white and have a very yellow and dirty color. The problem is that the train for which you purchased the ticket an hour in advance suddenly cancels service. What's more, there is no information broadcast, so you have no choice but to check the flight information board. Tickets can be exchanged for free, but I was passed around at the ticket office, which was terrible. I was at a loss because I basically couldn't communicate in English. Also, while around the world you get a discount when you buy a round trip ticket, in China there is a fee. Basically, it seems like you should buy it at the departure and arrival station. Additionally, foreigners cannot use automatic ticket vending machines when purchasing tickets, so it may take a long time to purchase tickets. Just like on a plane, there is a baggage check before boarding (though it's better than on a plane), and there may be quite a line, so it's best to allow yourself plenty of time.

This is a big train station.  You will find your way quite easily. There are a number of good shops and chance to eat is ok - McDonald's and KFC. Being connected to Hongqiao airport is ver convenient.

It's incredibly fast and convenient. Because it was China, I rode without fear of derailment, but it was more pleasant and comfortable than Korea's Ketex.

I was able to book a first class seat from Hongqiao on the outbound flight, and the smell wasn't too bad, but on the way back from Suzhou, I was seated in second class, which had a very fresh smell, so next time I wanted to get a first class seat since there wouldn't be that much of a difference in price.

Hongqiao is a very large train station.  Ticketing is on the top floor so if you arrive by Metro you need to go up 3 long escalators or take the elevator. Go through security!
