The station is beautiful if you like modern architecture. It is a very well built and designed pharaonic space. Despite being prepared for so many people, it can sometimes become overwhelming.

I rode between Shanghai and Suzhou on December 23rd. I had learned how to buy tickets online in advance, so when I checked into the hotel just before 8pm on December 22nd, I asked the guy at the front desk who could speak English fairly well, ``I'm going to go to the station now and buy a round-trip ticket for the high-speed train to Suzhou tomorrow.'' When I asked him, ``Mr., there's no need to go all the way to Shanghai Station now. If you want to buy a high-speed train ticket to Suzhou, you can buy it right here, but there will be a 30 yuan commission for each ticket.'' So, I made an immediate decision and asked them to find out that the next day, the 23rd, was a flight from 10:00 to 11:00 and a return from 17:00 to 18:00, and they told me that I could immediately take a flight to Nanjing South Station at 10:40 and a return flight from Suzhou Station at 17:09. I took a photo of my passport with a scanner and paid in cash for 139 yuan (approximately 2,740 yen) (regular fare: 39.5 yuan/2 flights + 30 yuan commission x 2), but foreigners cannot use vending machines, so I had to go all the way to the station, line up and show my passport, and there was no guarantee that I would be able to get a flight at a convenient time the next day, so I thought it was a good trade. So, I left the hotel at 9:00am, arrived at the station after 9:40am, checked my ID card (passport for foreigners) at the entrance, and then went through my baggage x-ray and metal detector inspection. I waited in the lobby assigned to each scheduled train number displayed on the electronic bulletin board, and an announcement was made about 15 minutes before departure.I went through the automatic ticket gate to the platform and boarded the designated train. However, there were some smart people out there, so I took a window seat, but there were two male passengers in the aisle and middle seats of the third row who had placed their large luggage between them and the seat in front of them and spread it out to the table. When I stood in the aisle and called out, ``Tai Fu Ki,'' the male passenger in the middle slowly tried to move his baggage to the window seat where I was supposed to be sitting, so I instinctively warned him in English, and he gave me an apologetic smile, got up from his seat, and made way for me. The ride took less than 30 minutes, and before we could enjoy the scenery, we arrived at our destination, Suzhou Station. From there, we took the subway one stop to Shantang Street, where we planned to take the photo, then went around Pingjiang Road, and then took the high-speed train back to Shanghai at 5:09 p.m. However, on the return flight, I forgot the name of the station, but it stopped for quite a long time at a station just before Shanghai Station, and I passed several trains, so it took over 40 minutes to arrive. As soon as I realized that traveling to and from China had one thing in common: it was cheap, fast, comfortable, and clean, and it would be an indispensable means of transportation for future trips to China.

It feels like a world away compared to the past. It's really convenient to go to relatively nearby areas. There was a famous accident when it first opened, but now everyone is riding it and I think it's safe.

Shanghai Hongqiao Railway Station is a large transportation hub. Next to it is Hongqiao Airport Terminal 2. The underground is also directly connected to Metro Line 2 and Line 10. I was seated in a standard 2nd class seat, and even though I'm a big person, the seat was comfortable and had enough space for me, and my butt didn't really hurt. There are also outlets for PCs, smartphones, and tablets, so you can charge them. There is space to store suitcases that need to be checked in on the aircraft, so there is no problem even with large luggage. The area where I felt there was room for improvement compared to the Shinkansen was the tilt of the car body to the left and right. I think the structure of the pedestal is inferior to the Shinkansen. If you are not careful, the plastic bottle on the table will tip to the point where it will fall off the table. I accidentally caught it just before it fell, but you need to be careful when placing plastic bottles on the table. I think it depends on where you're going, but I think it would take about the same amount of time to check baggage on an airplane as it does to travel by high speed train, including the time to travel by subway to the city, waiting time at the airport, time to pick up your baggage, time to travel within the airport, and time to wait for baggage inspection. Next time, I would like to prioritize reliability and travel by high speed train between Shanghai and Beijing.
A decent railway station with all the basic facilities, restaurants and coffeeshop. The more impressive part is the train ride, with modern, always on time trains.

Was there with friends while returning from Zhenjiang by high speed train. Its near the International airport.For the taxi queue was very long, about a km, but well disciplined crowed was managed by guards

Hongqiao Railway Station is very convenient. It is right next to Hongqiao Airport. You can walk directly from Hongqiao Airport, less than a kilometer away. There are many fast food restaurants on the ground floor. Although there are many people, the environment is very clean.

Hongqiao Station is close to Hongqiao Airport. Terminal 1 is for international flights and Terminal 2 is for domestic flights. There are 30 platforms in total. AB is actually the same train but with different numbers. There are restaurants such as Yonghe King and Taiwan Snacks, which are convenient for dining and shopping.

I have never seen this big station. There is English signs for tickets so no problems, I got my destination written down but ticket counter understood my English as well. Food court upstairs was a different, I could not order coffee from Maccas without help of locals. Toilets are local smoking rooms and in need of maintenance

Pudong often has long immigration queues and taxi queues.  Just getting from your plane can be a walk that seems like a kilometer before you get to the immigration counters.  There is always a disconnect between the number of staff serving local Chinese and foreigners - many more.   By comparison Hongqiao is a dream.  Short queues, fast service.

The station is huge, but very easy to find your way around, after going through security.  Tickets are purchased in a seperrate building, with long cues.  Make sure you have your passport with you at all times.

This isn't a tourist site, it's the gateway to tourist destinations. It's massive. I recommend arriving TWO hours before departure because it's so big and you'll need time to get through security and find your gate. Do not forget your passport and do not use a printed ticket from the internet once you've made your booking. I did and had real problems being allowed into a train. There's plenty of places to buy food and coffee in the station, and it's generally very clean, except the toilets. Be prepared to push n shove in the queue and take your own loo roll and sanitiser for the train journey.

This is the rail hub for the domestic airport and links to Metro Lines 2 and 10. It has good signage and clean bathrooms. It is usually very crowded. A place I avoid unless having to take a train from here.

Don't look for a toilet. We had to exit the station on the opposite side and then found Asian style ladies in the local square . Trains clean but don't wait your turn to enter. 2 of our friends were left on the station. Be the first to push on.
Huge, very very interesting, had a good look around, lots of building taking place nearby.Then onto the Speed Train.  WOW.
Quite a large station and it can be a headache from one end to the other, otherwise it is a beautiful and technological place, it has several stores for shopping.

I had to travel from Shanghai to Hangzhou on business in Late May 2015.  I took a high speed train from Shanghai to Hangzhou leaving from the Hongqiao rail station.  It is a large and very busy station that was bustling with people.  It is well laid out and there is easy acces to each of the gates.  It was very clean and spacious, even with the large number of people there.  The boarding process was very efficient.  Passengers lined up about 5-10 minutes beforehand.  Then were let through the ticket takes down the stairs to the train platform, The trains ran extremely efficiently.  They arrived exactly in time and spent no more than 5 minutes at the station to completely load and unload passengers (which were numerous). The only detractors I had were (1) it was difficult at times to to find seating near my gate while waiting and (2) the ladies at the information desk were not very attentive.  These were small retractions from an otherwise good experience.

I spend a large amount of time at Hongqiao and thankfully there are Coffee houses to house my early morning visits. It works and is clean (Except Toilets).Very busy and extremely hectic you cannot be late. Allways give yourself time here

We departed from this station for Suzhou. Non-Chinese tickets can only be purchased at the ticket office, which is located to the right of the station - Office tiket. There is a special ticket office, where it says at the top that this is an English-speaking ticket office, you go there; at the other ticket offices they won’t sell you a ticket anyway. Only the Chinese can buy tickets from the vending machines, as to purchase a ticket you must present an ID card to the machine. Be sure to have your passport ready; you buy tickets using your passport and at the entrance to the station they check both your tickets and your passport. There is a large board inside that says where the train is departing from. It is impossible to get lost and confused. And it is advisable to immediately go to the waiting room from where you will board your train. There are cafes inside the station where you can buy takeaway food and drinks. Prices are the same as in the city.

I rode to Hefei with some skepticism, but the time was accurate, there was little shaking, and it was comfortable. The inside of the train is noisy because the passengers are talking loudly, but that's unavoidable. If you can make it this far, that's great.

I took a first class seat round trip from Shanghai to Zhenjiang. I used the high-speed train once about five years ago to go from Zhenjiang to Shanghai, but at that time it wasn't as frequent as it is now, and for some reason there were stops near Shanghai Station to adjust the timing, so I got the strong impression that it wasn't sophisticated. However, after using it this time, my perception has changed drastically. What impressed me most was that there were a lot of them, and that they moved accurately to the diamond. The first class cars were empty both ways, but the second class cars seemed to be quite crowded. In any case, as others have pointed out, the situation seems to have improved considerably from before, but I think it's best to secure tickets in advance.

Enormous and gives a sense of modern China.  Seems like the size of two stadiums but all polished clean floors leading to modern train platforms and trains.  It can be a bit overwhelming it is so larger.  Takes about 45 min from Pudong area.
Impeccable structure, very organized. Pay close attention to the boarding counter as it is large and usually full.
Large and extremely busy, plenty of escalators. Centrally placed , good access to the underground. May be a bit daunting on the first visit and arrival.Close to the bus station.

Place is open and clean.  Bathrooms were a bit of a disaster just like railway stations anywhere else in the world.  If you want a seat, good luck; because there is always a couple thousand people sitting around waiting for an evening train (in the morning.)
It is the fastest way to be in the center of Shanghai, it only takes a few minutes to reach your destination, safe, comfortable, good price, recommended.
Very good  Train station , well connected to Airport and Subway line 2 . All fast trains now from this train station.

Massive, Simply Massive. Many platforms, fantastic trains and signage is in both Chinese and English. Be prepared to line up as gates to each platform do not open until about ten minutes before the train is due for departure.

Railways are state of the art in China. This modern railway station is connected to the local airport and has great highspeed connections.  Only issue is when you get back, especially in the afternoon between 4 and 7, to get a taxi.  I have been in line for an hour. Never get lured in by the clowns trying to sell you one of their "special taxis" - you might find yourself out of 400rmb and walking across the highway to get to that special taxi (I have seen people who tried it).  There is also a direct metro connection, which is great, but potentially very crowded.
Huge stations where mostly the bullet trains come. It was right next to one of the airports of Shanghai. Its quiet difficult to find some one even if the type of exits are told
Immense and impressive, I had to go to take the bullet train to Beijing (Pekin), it is really immense with the same traffic as any major airport in the world, excellent architecture

Before the bridge to Ningbo and the bullet train to Changzhou, transit times for meetings in other areas used to be much longer. What was a 5 hr drive is now a 45 min train ride.  Station is clean with some shops including a Starbucks. Using the signs for your train is not difficult.  What is confusing is which # on the ground to use for your train car#.  Since the train can enter the station either way the train car #'s are written in both directions and do not land in the same spot, you have to ask which way it is going to stand at the proper train car #. You are supposed to have your passport with you to match the name on your ticket but I have never been asked to show it.

I used it for a business trip. I sat in first class (like a green car) and second class (like a Shinkansen), but I recommend first class. I happened to be sitting in a bad seat, but in the second class seats, the seats would come off, and it was so noisy that the voices of people talking on the phone and talking were so loud that I felt uncomfortable. Considering the price, it felt a little expensive, but I felt more comfortable sitting in the first class seat.

China has been very progressive in developing their rail network.  The train stations in major cities, like Shanghai, are very modern structures and designed like modern airports, with individual gates that let you in about 15 minutes before your departure time, and lead you to the platform, much more organized and cleaner than what you find even in other advanced countries.  The stations also have a very large selection of restaurants and shops.  Although you can buy your tickets at the station, you may not be able to get the first class, unless you buy your ticket well in advance.  But, if you travel with the bullet train (G Trains) even the second class seats are very clean and comfortable, and the bullet train travels extremely fast, so your travel time is not very long.

I rode it twice this month. I went to Changzhou and Hangzhou, both of which could be reached in an hour. It's convenient. It is better to buy tickets in advance. The ticket office takes too long on the day of the event.
Although very busy but it was Very smoothly run.  Loads of eating places and cafe.  The rotating TV screens by the sitting areas were extremely cooled.

Best of all, the station is spacious and you can enjoy the feeling of being overseas. A feeling that you can never experience in Japan. . There was a long line to buy tickets, which wasn't too cumbersome, and it was interesting to have to enter my passport and name. Please come and take a look!

Efficient and clean, trains mostly always on time, fast 300 km per hour so it does not take long wherever you are going. Inside the trains you have good interiors toilets are available in most carriages. Have first class and also executive class but second class is good for journeys under 1 hour.

The Hongqiou Railway station is about 45 minutes away from city centre by taxi if it is not rush hour. We took the bullet train twice from this location which is next to the Hongqiao Airport. The station is large, modern and very busy. There are about 32 gates. Ticket offices are at the ends of the station so it can be a lo-o-ng walk if your train leaves from gate 32 and you pick the ticket office at the other end! If you are a visitor, you need your passport to pick up your tickets. Ladies, there are sit down flush toilets with toilet paper in the station. There are escalators and an accessible elevator to reach the platforms. Loading is quick and trains leave on time. Trains are fast (300 km/hr), clean and comfortable with a smooth ride. It is easy to move from car to car so if you running to catch the train, just get on and walk to through to your car. Food service and bottled water is expensive so buy something from a kiosk in the station. Hot water is free so be a local and bring your own cup and tea. Washrooms are like the airlines - very compact - but there are sit down toilets and toilet paper. On arrival, the taxi line can be very long but it moves very quickly. There is dispatcher who directs the cabs. Also ask for a metered rate - should cost between 50 and 70 RMB to city centre depending on traffic. Add 30% for travel after 10 pm.  If you don't have much luggage and know where you are going, consider taking the Metro. If you think you miss your train, call the number on your reservation. There are English speaking people to assist you and you can rebook for the same day. Note that cell phones do not work in China unless you have a national service in your own country with international service agreements in China. If you have an unlocked phone with 4G, consider getting a SIM card from China Mobile or China Unicom.

Very convenient location for travel around the city. Easy to purchase tickets as the machines are not only in Chinese but in English as well. Price is inexpensive for a day long ticket to go anywhere or for a one way ticket for a specific location. Map adorn the walls to you can see where you want to go.

As a regular traveller, I use that station almost every week. I have been to many Railway Station, New Delhi, Kyoto, Beijing, Mumbai, Tokyo, Shin-Osaka. For China, Hongqiao is the BEST. The location is very convenient. Metro Line 2, Airport Terminal 2, Coach Bus Station is all in same area. Resturaunts are also well displayed both arrival and departure hall. No hassle caused, the only problem maybe the queue from their toilet, too many people, not enough :)

You must prepare to wait for an hour to get on to a taxi when you arrive in Hong Qiao Train station. It would be best to take a subway to somewhere before hopping on a taxi. Other than this, I think Hong Qiao do very well as a modern China train station.
I used it when I went to Hangzhou. Unfortunately, the recliner was broken, so it's still not at the level of Japan. The return trip was comfortable. The price is cheap.
very professionally managed hub though getting there from the city was a little difficult by road - on time departures, nice stores

The station is well organized. It almost feels like an airport with “boarding gates” depending on the destination and the car number. There are many food outlets. There is access with 2 or 3 metro lines, including one of the lines to the airport. For those who stay several days, there is an interesting 24-hour metro card whose validity begins from the time of purchase

From Hongqiao to Yiwu, I passed where that train was buried. It was definitely quieter and more comfortable than I expected, but it's a reasonable price. The extra incomprehensible snacks and drinks were not good enough, and on top of that, the CA didn't speak Chinese at all, and to make matters worse, he couldn't even speak English, which was very inconvenient. The worst part was that even though the car was not that old, the seats were floppy and the recline was not good, so the seats would fall down on their own. That's too much for first class (green).
When using this rail or any rail system in China if you are a non Chinese national make sure you take your passport as you can not obtain rail tickets if you do not have.
If you go from Shanghai airport to the city, it is great to take the magnetic train, it takes 8 minutes to travel 34 km. Although it is not the cheapest, the experience is worth it.
It looks like an airport, the station is super organized, I arrived there from Beijing. Also close to Hongqiao airport, there is a subway to the center, bund, pudong, etc.

What's interesting here is that this large train station is built over several levels and Hongqiao Airport is right next door. If someone is interested in railways, I recommend taking a train trip to Suzhou. The route runs at a traveling speed of 300 km/h and is usually around 12-15 meters above the ground on stilts.
Well organized, well appointed. There was a huge taxi line but we still only had to wait about ten minutes. Transfer to Pudong airport to 40 minutes in mid afternoon.

Since this is a station, its official name is Shanghai Hongqiao Railway Station. It opened in July 2010 as a dedicated high-speed rail station. This station is directly connected to Shanghai Subway Lines 2 and 10, making transfers very convenient. There is also a bus terminal and a taxi stand. Shanghai Hongqiao Airport is also nearby and can be reached by subway. When entering the station premises, you must pass through a baggage check and metal detector. There is also a ticket office on the premises, so you will need to undergo this inspection when purchasing tickets. Please note that a passport is required at the time of purchase. If you are boarding on the day, you can get mineral water by showing your ticket at the ``water intake area'', so be sure to get some to take with you on your journey. There are two smoking corners, so if you smoke, please do so here. (Smoking is not allowed on the train) Since it's a station, you won't have any trouble eating or shopping, but prices are higher than in the city, so if possible, buy before entering the station. There is also Starbucks coffee, and the staff can speak English. Train ticket gates generally open 15 minutes before departure. (Ticket gates stop 3 minutes before departure) As per Chugoku Railway's rules, waiting rooms differ for each train, so check the electronic bulletin board before lining up. For those who are riding a train in China for the first time, the station is extremely large. Traveling within the station building also takes quite a bit of time. We recommend that you arrive at least 1 hour before departure to allow plenty of time. I will omit the explanation of the train as it has been written by someone else.

Perfectly reachable by Metro, connected to airport and roads. Orientation within the station has been easy and perfectly logical. Personnel efficient and helpful. Catching a train in Shanghai is as catching a flight: purchase ticket (passport needed), check-in, xray controls, gates, and then the excellent fast trains. It takes no less than 1 hour to do so.At night most food places close earlier than expected.

A huge place that you catch bullet trains. You should get the tickets ahead at ticketing offices located throughout the city. Mine is inside a tiny convienience shop near Oriental Tower in Pudong. If you are fluent in Chinese and willing wait for the availability at the station, you can purchase tickets at the station too.You can also check out the availability of the trains/schedule online before purchasing.Check out www.chinatrainguide.com, orhttp://www.travelchinaguide.com/china-trains/beijing-shanghai-highspeed.htmUnlike the airplane, the most expensive ticket is the business seats, then first class, then the rest.Upon arrival, you need to do a security check.Put your bags for an inspection through a short conveyor belt. You get scanned/patted.Then, you are free till your departing time.Your ticket will show you the gate number and time.Must remember, they can change the gate at any time, and will leave on time no matter what. They do not wait for you. They don't have many seats available to sit nearby the gate.A gate is just an entrance where people check your tickets with ID's(passports for expats). When the boarding time gets near, people line up regardless the class and gets hectic.There are many eateries including Starbucks, McDonald's and other Chinese vendors.They seem to improve on the stores to shop, but not in restrooms.They are few in numbers and not clean. Must carry tissues and wet towels etc., if you have to go.In lower level, there are many eateries and stores, and the subway line 2 and 10.
I guess we shouldn't compare it to Japan, but it's a shame that you can't just buy it and ride it right away. As the network is expanding, we want it to be more convenient.

Visited the Hongqiao to take the speed train to Beijing and we did it in 5 hours. it was easy to navigate and get a ticket and board the train. the actual train which travels at speeds of over 300 kilometers is a pleasant experience too.

First let me say that the china high speed railway system is incredible. The fastest most efficient way of travel I have ever experienced. That being said however there needs to be some upgrades:1: Toilets.  The most disgusting toilets I have ever seen. No toilet paper in stalls, cleaned with water, rampant smoking, and overall feeling of wanting to vomit. 2. Food. Although there are a few good places to check out this could be greatly improved upon. All in all a happy experience but could be a lot better

the loos  OMG did not appreciate not many proper toilets.  Why is this, in this viberant society.  Not happy about the loos at all in most of tourist spots, train stations and airports we visited in China. Dont they have a proper drainage system

I used it between Shanghai and Suzhou. After riding it, I felt it was not that different from the Shinkansen in Japan, but I thought the ride quality was a little more like the Shinkansen of Japan from a while ago. The occupancy rate seemed to be over 100%, and passenger manners seemed to be pretty good. It made me want to ride again.
Clean, roomy, food, shopping and lots of people.  Easy to get there.  Hongqiao Railway makes train travel enjoyable.
A beautiful new station.  It is far from the bund and pudong.  2 was to get into town.  A taxi after a 30 minute wait in line or packed subway.  Feels more like an airport than a train station.

Caught the high speed train from Shanghai to Beijing. Booked tickets online thru China Highlights which were very good and left tickets with our concierge at the hotel. Processing at train station very easy, it was well signed and clean. Great way to see more of China.

it can be achieved by Metro, and the sign about information is understandable ( an English article ), it's a big station is connect to everywhere to a big city in China by TRAIN... so u must try it when you go to China..

I used it for work from Nijibashi to Tokosu Station. I requested a first class round trip ticket from JTB Shanghai, and the return trip was half the price of the outbound trip! Even though the regular price was so cheap that it couldn't be compared to Japan, it was even more of a bargain.

It is a very large and crowded station. Traveling should allow time. Because for people who don't know Chinese, it may be confusing with bus schedules or various entrance and exit doors. But the staff are good at helping foreigners. and understand English more than anywhere else
we took the Gtrain from Guilin to Shanghai. Got off and transferred to the metro, ez to do. Metro takes you to the shopping area & near the Bund, and to the PVG int'l arpt

Very impressive building and services, trains on time ! This train station looks and feels like an airport. Only point is that if you did not book your ticket earlier, (which is difficult from abroad) make sure you arrive early enough as the queues at the counters can take half an hour. Try the business class if you can, it's awesome !

Very new train station that blows away the beaten up old main station. Nice new facilities, excellent selection of food and even some shopping available for last minute gifts.Downside, VERY far from downtown, The Bund, etc., and even farther to Pudong Business area and Pudong Airport. Consequently, expensive taxi ride to any part of the city. There is a subway station that will take you, via the MagLev, directly to Pudong International.The ticket booths on the main floor are always crowded but if you come in by subway, the booths on bottom floor are quite quick.

BUSY - BUSY - BUSY but very efficient.  With the thousands of people that pass through daily it is amazingly clean and can process them quickly.The security scans the bags and the passenger quickly.Lots of excellent food stands throughout.

This place is GIGANTIC!!!!! It is conveniently reached by metro (Line 2 and Line 10) - Line 2 being the fastest way to get there. Once you get off the metro, walk up the stairs, follow the signs and reach the entrance to the railway station. Once you enter the railway station walk 100ft to 150ft or so and to the right you will see the ticket office and ticket machines where you can "pick up" your bought online tickets. The employees at the ticket office do speak some English so you shoudn't have any trouble buying tickets; however, make sure YOU BRING YOUR PASSPORT to buy any ticket, otherwise you won't be able to buy one!!!! Arrive at least 1.5hrs before your train departs in case you experience long lines at the ticket office; find your way upstairs; pass security line; get something to eat; and find your departing door. The first floor of the railway station (where the metro stops) is the ARRIVING floor (Starbucks located here/opens at 7am as well as Costa Cafe opens at 7am as well as other food restaurants), the second floor is the DEPARTURING floor (more restaurants than the first floor - McDonalds; Burger King; Starbucks: Costa Cafe, souvenir shops, newspaper stands, etc.) Walk through the terminal floor to locate what you feel like eating (there are stairways located on the corners of the terminal as well as in the middle terminal), sit down, eat, and wait for your train!!!! Get there early!!!! It has a total area of 1.3 million square meters, it is the largest railway station in Asia!!!!

A model of good organisation , impressive by the size ,the number of desk and its efficiency.I was going to Hungzhao from this railway station ,the train was perfectly on time and I did a perfect trip !

if you are foreigner and need to go to the others chinese cities, go first to the chinatrainguide.com and find your train, safe the number of train and time....then show it at casier. there is some cashiers accepts international cards...(for example .. booth 79 at depurture floor) then vuala you have your ticket. also if you have ticket you can get bottle of water for free))) then find your train and enjoy your journey))

Coming in from Yichang late evening to a huge, but clean train station was nice but that's were the fun ended. Taxi line was routed outside underneath  in a tunnel. After 50 minutes of masses of people smoking, pushing, taxi's  honking and exhaust fumes we felt lightheaded and slightly sick.

◇Safety A few years ago, a car crashed and tried to bury the debris, exposing the world to shame.(Kanichi) But please think about it! Is there any other high-speed railway in Japan that has not caused serious accidents, other than the Shinkansen? Just like France's TGV, Germany's ICE, and Spain's high-speed railway! Accidents that kill or injure dozens of people occur on high-speed trains around the world. China's high-speed rail network is much larger than Japan's. There is no transportation system in this world that is accident-free. So when it comes to traveling, it's just a matter of probability. ◇Differences from regular railways The quality of passengers and facilities are completely different. There is a bigger difference between Japan's conventional lines and the Shinkansen. You can't ride it unless you're wealthy or wealthy. I have never thought that I have bad manners. ◇How to buy tickets Passport required. Since it's an online system, you can buy it at any JNR station. (The trick is to buy during off-peak hours on weekdays in the countryside.) ◇Even a first class car is much cheaper than an ordinary car on Japan's Shinkansen. For reference, compare Shanghai Hongqiao Station to Qufu East Station (fastest time is 3 hours and 9 minutes); 1st class is 584 yuan, 2nd class is 344 yuan. The first class car has the same route and time, but drinks and snacks are provided. ◇The seats in the second class car are a little narrower than those on the Shinkansen. First class cars are similar to green cars. ◇The speed of the D type is about 200 km, and the G type is about 308 km.◇How to get there In Guangzhou and Qufu, including Shanghai, high-speed railway stations are 15 to 20 km away from the city center! Also, please note that the stations are often different from those on conventional lines. ◇Station staff level is not low. Isn't the probability of being able to speak English higher than in Japan? ◇Conclusion Railway networks are increasing mainly in large cities, so it's worth using!

Had to take the train to go to Beijing from this station and I was surprised at how organized it was. Is big and it has a lot of stores in case you need to wait for a long period of time for your train. The bathrooms are relatively clean and there are a lot of sits! I was impressed!

Good train from Beijing to Shanghai over than 1000 km in 4.55hours exactly. Spacious place in First class coach. Many things to buy. Nice Canteen in Cabin 9. Very co operative and beautiful hostess. Seems like airport. No compare with other Asian countries railway station. Loved it. The bad is there is no trolley to carry your baggage. They will charge you Yuan 20 per bag. The same when arrival to Shanghai no trolley alone. Waited almost 1 hour and at last one lady came from far and carry my bags in her trolley half way from up to the South Exit for Yuan 100.Train is perfect. Speed is 305 kph. Only 2 stops in our journey.Highly recommended.

I visited Shanghai Several time & Used Shanghai Hongqiao Railway station .It is one of the best Railway Station I used , it is Clean / Well Design/ Beautiful. It is so huge & all facilities are available .Easy to reach  Metro / Car / Cab etc. & even on arrival Excellent Transportation mode It is Next to Hongqiao Airport , so any one coming out of town or out of country can use it to mostly all places / cities / town near by Shanghai .Only thing I missed is lack of English speaking Counters / English Sign Board at Ticking Counter / area . Now China being an International country with lot of English speaking visitors , should look in to more English Ticking Counter with proper English Sign Boards .
This is one thing that China does really well, I prefer to take rail than fly, trains are always on time.

The Shanghai HongQiao Railway station is modern, well-designed, clean, and beautiful. We took high-speed trains to Hangzhou and Nanjing. They x-rayed our bags and we had to pass metal detector gates for security checks. There are big screens for the train departures. The check-in and check-out processes were fast. The trains were on time. There are shops and restaurants in the station.

The station itself is humongous (probably due to the fact that during high season there's an endless crowd of people taking the trains), but you won't get lost as the signs are easy to follow. The facilities are clean, and there's a few restaurants (McDonald's, dumplings, Yonghe, etc.) and shops. The trains are a good price for an excellent mode of transportation, a pleasant alternative to flying if your destination isn't too far.Unless you are a Chinese citizen you must receive you ticket at certain ticket counters, but they're pretty easy to find. Another thing to note is that you are not allowed to bring live animals onto the high-speed rail, not sure about normal trains.

The station is really cool, very organized, it looks like an airport. Very different from what I'm used to in São Paulo. I used the station to catch a train to a nearby city in the interior. Tudo muito organizado, seguro e tranquilo. Gostei bastante da experiência.
I have been there twice, I like the prices and you can go anywhere in china practicly. It have good facilities and is easy to use, it have the english signals

we are traveling in a group of 4. I was a little intimidated by the thought of finding my way around a train station not knowing the local language.did not have a problem. the ticket windows were easy to find. the train numbers and the  train locations were clearly displayed and there were announcements in English .The train station itself was nothing less than a modern airport with great food and even better shopping.very impressed.

Trains leave every few minutes. With such a huge number of travelers, the station is clean and efficient. You can get water in front of the ticket offices by showing your ticket. Please note that it is easier and faster to buy a ticket in the city than at the station. Tickets are personal and when purchased by someone, they must have a copy of their passport and visa

We departed from this station for the city of Yangzhou. everything is cultured and very comfortable. There are cafes everywhere and places to sit. The main thing is to locate yourself not far from the boarding entrance, because boarding and departure is a very quick procedure. High-speed trains 305 km/h.
Use regularly when on business. Efficient, clean and absolutely HUGE !!Typical Chinese efficiency with easy to find platforms.

A must do if you are in Shanghai. Our guide purchased the tickets for us an then hurried us onto the train. we got up to 441km per hour. When we passed another train going in the opposite direction, it was literally in the blink of an eye.Its comfortable and over in some 10mins or less. Be aware that it does not take you into the centre of the city, so you need to have some arrangements made to go the final leg to your hotel.

The easiest, cheapest and quickest way to commute from Shanghai to Pudong International Terminal 2 Airport.The station is clean, good sign in english and it takes you 8 minutes to be at the airport avoiding all the crazy traffic in Shanghai.You pay only 50 RMB (one way) or 80 (VIP seat) and you get safely and comfortably.Highly recommended.

To take the amazing high speed train, that goes in only 4 hours from Shanghai to Jinan, at a distance of aprox. 1.000 km, even stopping 4 or 5 times on its way, is an incredible futurist experience; but it is not only about the train, but it starts in the station!  Modern architecture, huge halls with plenty of comfortable seats, beautifull stores, clean bathrooms and very well organized system of gates to the trains, with last generations electronic placards.

I think the biggest difference between China and Japan is the toilet. Especially when you think of public restrooms, the first thing that stands out is the lack of toilet paper and how dirty they are, but this one is different. Although it is not comparable to Japan, I am glad that there is paper and that I can wash it. There is hot water, and we also sell lunch boxes and drinks, so it's comfortable.

This massive new station, which now handles most of Shanghai's traffic, is well run.  But it's always very busy and therefore, together with the language barrier, a bit daunting.  Do yourself a favour and make sure you arrive nice and early, and book ahead with C-Trip.  It doesn't let you avoid the queues (you still have to swap your booking for a 'real' ticket), but it does guarantee you a place on the train....

Huge modern railway station. Easy access. Only one counter to take your ticket as you cant use the machines as foreigners. Have some buffer in your schedule as sometimes there is long queue. Food offering is poor. Mc Donald, KFC and some other chinese style shop. High speed train are good, platform easy to find.
I"m told that the Chinese are going to Germany on advice about how to make thier stations, but the stations I have seen here surpasses anything in Germany.Bright modern efficient

A little corny but a nice way to get from one side of the river to the other. Somewhat pricey nonetheless cool. The water taxi is another very reasonable option of crossing over- and only costs 2 RMB.

The high-speed railway itself seemed to be comparable to the Shinkansen. However, getting a ticket is not as easy as it is in Japan. Chinese people can purchase from self-service machines, but foreigners have to line up at specialized counters. A passport is required at this time. The electric bulletin board shows the train number, time, destination, and whether tickets are available for the three-day train, but it is sold out so there are quite a lot of people who ride it. If you want to be sure to ride, I recommend purchasing in advance instead of just going haphazardly like I did.
Not speaking Chinese made it difficult to know which queue to be in etc but once your through wow!  306km/hr and no sensation of speed

Yeah? ? ? When I used it, I didn't feel any danger, and I don't think it was as fast as Japan's Shinkansen. The electronic individual itself is neither good nor bad, but it is China! Very noisy and annoying! Pepe the outer skins of pumpkin seeds and sunflower seeds on the train! Well, it's been a long time!

This train station is the newest one in the Shanghai Metro. Easy to transfer to Pudong Airport via Bus from the train station. Only qualm I have is that if you are a foreigner you can only pick up the ticket at the ticket counter and usually long lines. This has nothing to do with the station but it is the government policy in China. All in all I wish we have high speed trains in America!

Trains have become really convenient. You can now travel from Shanghai to Suzhou, Hangzhou, Ningbo, etc. in no time. The car body is exactly the same as the Japanese Shinkansen. The ride comfort remains the same. However, the price is so low that it feels like a good deal. It's a bit troublesome that you need your passport number when making a reservation, but if you can get through that, I don't think there's any ride that's as easy as this one.

I changed from the D type to the G type, and I think the performance has improved significantly. In the past, Shinkansen trains were not that fast, but the G-type can reach 300km/h, and is quiet and comfortable. The journey from Shanghai to Yiwu, which used to take 2 hours and 40 minutes, has been shortened to 1 hour and 30 minutes. This is a huge improvement compared to the time it took over 5 hours 10 years ago.

Its a train station, so you can only expect so much. The concourse when you pull up is noisy and can feel quite daunting, but ive never felt threatened at all. As a Western face, you do get looked at quite a bit, but just smile, or dont look. Plenty of "restaurants" to use if required. Departures are swift, and the train is always there waiting when you reach the platform.

Deutsche Bahn - do you know the announcement? In Shanghai or China you should definitely take a ride on the speed train. No delays because everything is going perfectly at the station like in Hongquio. And don't worry, everything is announced in English

This Railway station will Give U the Glimpse of Airport..Unlike Normal Railway station anywhere in the world one is not allow to Enter the Platform without their train departure announce..U can catch a Bullet train from here to All Major City of China..nd 200kilometer away city is reachable within 45 Minutes..The OutLook of this Railway station is a Huge..

Economical way to travel. This train station is huge. Security check in place, bags will be scanned before entering. Many shops around, one can easily find some food there while waiting for the train. Highly recommended to buy ticket a day or two before the travel date. Will need to produce passport (for security purposes) when purchasing ticket and during the travel again. So bring along yr ID or passport (for foreigners). High speed train aka bullet train goes really fast (max speed now reduced to 300km/hr). Arrive early and expect big crowd. Toilet Q was long, so was Q for taxi.

This station is the home of the bullet train which can get you from Shanghai to Beijing in under 6 hrs, faster than a plane.  It's modern, efficient, less prone to delays and connected to the metro stations at each stop. Food choices are limited, so bring your own. Convention seems to be extra large suitcases reside in the aisle next to the owner if they don't fit on the overhead rack. Bathrooms, though modern, suffer from a cultural lack of user care, with pee and toilet paper on the floors and seats. With short stops at stations along the route, the restrooms are not serviced so be prepared to check adjacent cars.

April 2014 came here twice in & out going to catch the HST from & then return to Beijingthe High speed train is exactly that it goes around 354KM ph & takes half the time i found the station to be extemely  clean but busy i advise anyone taking a train to arive in plenty of time to assure yourself the right gate

I do like the organization, how the system works on the station, although people didn't speak English I made myself understood. Very clean and modern, highly secure I found. There was no English on the departures/ arrivals boards, but I think things could be figured out. Also showing your ticket says what you want to know. I don't speak Chinese so I was quite happy with the guidance and help I got. Chinese people always there for you!

This train station is quite modern unlike others in China, it is right next to the airport, which makes it wonderful in case you have to connect with other cities and there is also the subway, which allows you to connect wonderfully with all of Shanghai, I arrived from Guangzhou and I wanted to walk and walk from the moment I arrived and it was super easy since the signage is quite clear, something you don't see much in China, I recommend taking the train at least once, it is a nice experience and I really liked the landscapes, enjoy.
This Railway station is actually nicer than the Pudong Airport. Excellent Metro connectivity. China's high speed trains are the best

Very convenient, and located at the side of Hogqiao Airport, with easy access by subway. However, if you need to be there for a long time the seats are very limited, station is always overocupied, not really comfortable to be there for long time.

Shanghai's Hongqiao Railway Station sees a lot of action. There are trains arriving and departing constantly so there's always a ton of activity. Navigating it isn't complicated though, even for someone who only speaks English. There is plenty of clear signage indicating where things are and where you have to go, and it's a manageable size (nothing like Tokyo Station in scope.) There are ticketing windows that have signs indicating English speakers as well if you don't have tickets.I bought mine well in advance, a new thing in China which used to release ticket sales only a few weeks in advance.. you can now purchase tickets sometimes up to 60 days in advance.There are lost of shops and food places, including a few western chains like KFC, in the railways station, even past security. Restrooms aren't bad either.You have to arrive a little early for a train in China, I'd recommend at least 25 minutes, but traveling by rail is convenient and pleasant, even on non-high-speed-rail routes. Prices are good as well.

I think this is the best place when it comes to see how railway station can be turned into beautiful commercial place which is smoothly connected to Airport, Metro and Bus Service. Though it is crowded, place is quite managed and navigation signs are well directed for non-Chinese speaking person to reach the right place.

This is a really massive Railway station. I believe, if you are planning to take the G train (fastest bullet train), this one is the last stop. To go to Pudong Airport, you could get down here and catch a underground tube. There are sign boards every where. But, I would suggest, if you have a smart phone, get all the necessary maps into it to move from one place to another. There are sign boards every where. But, many a times I was confused as there are multiple entrance/exits.

We came from Beijing with the bullet train and stopped there, very spacious and well-structured. It is not close to the center or bund, the transfer took about 30 minutes to the center, but it has a metro

I recommend getting on the train during your stay in China, I really liked the whole experience, the place and the station is very "futuristic" and the train is very modern and has very good views of the city.

I much prefer travel by train in China rather than by air. Domestic flights are rarely on time, often cancelled and very crowded.But with the high-speed trains, I can enjoy much better seating comfort, the trains are ALWAYS on time and I will arrive to my destination's city center rather than an hour outside of the city.The reason why I am making a review of Hongqiao train station is that I do find the station very modern and well working. Also for you that do not speak much Chinese (yet) it is easy to find your way around here.In the opposite, the central Shanghai train station, is old and I dare say, a bit filthy. No one speaks any english. If you dont have a Chinese ID, to pick up a pre-booked ticket can be a bit of a nightmare. It has to be done in a separate building located across the street from the station itself. Allow for time.
Once u understand how to navigate this is one of the best train stations ever.Great facilities and efficient service .

Big and modern and physically attached to the hongqiao airport. Always a big queue for a ticket. You cannot buy over a week in advance for most trains. All queues are the same even if the signs are different. Nice and clean and quite well ordered.

I've never seen a train station like this before, an incredible hustle and bustle of people. Luckily I had a Chinese colleague with me, otherwise I would probably still be there. But everything was really very clean and the Chinese were pushing in a very disciplined manner.
Close to subway train station, buses and taxis not a problem there.Walking is the best too, hotel close to everything

Hongqiao has an airport, station, and bus all in one. Extremely convenient. After getting off the plane, I took a shuttle bus (15 minutes free) and met up with my colleagues at the Shinkansen station. The journey to Nanjing has begun. It lasted just under an hour. I was impressed by how clean and on time the train was. It was a moment where I forgot about my unpleasant job.

I thought uk train stations were big but this place is huge we nearly got lost.  It's nicely laid out so we found our way. Lots of shops and eating places to keep you occupied while waiting for your bullet trains.  We travelled to Beijing it took us 5 hours to cover over 600 miles.
Next to the Hongquiao airport, the combination of both is monstrous. Modernity and tested accuracy are the watchword.
The station is easy to navigate with signs and announcements made in English.  Plenty of places to ship or eat while you wait for the train.

Located adjacent to Hongqiao airport, i have used this station many times for my trains to ningbo but this time i used it for a train to qingdao. despite heavy crowd, they maintain this station very clean, the seat arrangements are extraordinary, i appreciate the railway station management and the staff. right from the security check in to boarding the trains, everything was smooth and the staff are so nice and friendly although they dont speak english. food and newspapers and magazines (99% in chinese) available within the station. free water is given to you based on your ticket. Huge LED screens display all the train info, departure time and the platform numbers etc it is really great to be in this station. you dont need to know chinese, still you will zero problem locating your platform. I salute the CRH for making this station so well and so user friendly. I appreciate everyone behind this success. I recommend other travelers to experience this station to have a first hand pleasure. Announcements are made in chinese as well as in English. I just love CRH.
Wide. From there you can take tickets to go to Hangzhou. Be careful, sometimes thieves or scammers are around.

One of the biggest railroad stations on earth. During the Spring Festival period extremely busy, but as everywhere in this town, extremely well organised, with special tourists' counters where staaf spoke an adequate English.
New and efficient. Love to travel by rail and easy for white monkey to get around. Asians call westerns "white monkeys". I know I am married to one.
Very good information boards but can still take some time to find. Good to be out in good time. Good with security checks. Too few seats.

Perfect hub, well served by Metro line 2 (green), very large, clean and strictly controlled. To purchase the ticket you need a passport, luggage goes through the scanner and people go through a metal detector like at the airport, the gates only open when the train is present. Clean trains, very punctual and pleasant on-board service (we have something to learn...). In the station, the catering and essential general services are normal.
A bit dated and dirty. But the ticket process was easy and I got where I was going. That's the whole point!

This railway station is extremely easy to get to. Just hop on line 10 and hop off. It's relatively clean and has some good places to eat (Starbucks, McDonald's, etc.).  Definitely the preferred train station in Shanghai. The trains usually leave on time, so don't be late and don't forget your passport. The taxi line when you arrive can be really long, but the wait isn't so bad. Only squatter toilets (bring your own tissues)...or wait to use the restroom on the train.
Nice and convenient railway! But you have to be there in a half an hour for sure! The territory is huge! Just to make sure that you can reach the gate you need.

Perfect transport hub. On the left the station and on the right the airport which once, before the birth of Pu Dong, was the only one in Shanghai. Very large station, with many restaurants, shops and services. Fast trains to Beijing leave from here. Well organized and strangely clean. Worth seeing and trying

The company will make ticket reservations for you, but even if you have a reservation, you will need to go to the station and line up at the counter to get your ticket issued, so you need to get there quite early. Chinese people can issue tickets using an automatic machine, but foreigners have to line up at a separate counter, which takes time. As Japanese people know, if you arrive at the last minute, you run the risk of missing your flight. Rather than waiting on the platform, the ticket gates open at a set time before the train arrives. There is a place in the middle of the waiting floor at Nijibashi Station where water is distributed. If you bring your ticket with you and show it to them, they will give you water for each person. There's no problem even if you don't understand Chinese at all, so please try searching.

I took a first class train from Suzhou to Shanghai. It's like a slightly dirty Japanese Shinkansen. What caught my attention was the fact that there was a parent and child in the same car who were constantly moving their seats. Maybe you don't have a ticket? No way, right?

Anthill, both in terms of the number of people and the systematic nature: everything is simple, understandable, convenient. Tickets for "non-Chinese" only at the ticket office (at the machines you need a Chinese ID, which is a magnetic card), which understands English, but for insurance, ask the locals to write down the exact name of the station, type of ticket and train (high-speed or not, etc.)

HUGE and well laid out station. Really like an airport. Connected to the Subway, it's painless to get there and also to the Hongqiao airport. Gates to let you on the tracks at the appointed time. Assigned seats on the high speed trains that go 305 km/hr. It's an amazing transportation system.

great station but don't make the mistake of using one of the porters dressed in red uniform as they overcharge. a polite warning. otherwise great station. first class on the train is good vaue about £13 one way only to Hangzhou. Business class is much more and flat bed. surprising but true........

Easy to get around- announcements are in both Mandarin and English, which was really helpful for us.  Get there a little early to be safe, there are plenty of places to shop or sit and read while you wait for the train.  Also, buy your tickets in advance!  We bought ours a day or 2 ahead of time.

The size of Shanghai Station is impressive. Trains run with minute accuracy; on the board you can track the number of the desired train and the platform exit number, even without knowing Chinese. The staff at the station speaks normal English. However, the windows at the box office are not duplicated on it, so you need to guess where you can buy tickets and where to exchange them. Arrive early so you have time to get your bearings, get/buy tickets and go through security.

This is really a good example of city planning. The Airport and the Railway Station are very close (walking distance). The organisation for travellers is great. I which we can find more of this around the world.
I've ridden on it several times, and I think it's a great vehicle that doesn't feel like China, as it runs on time without having to read the time like on Chinese planes.

My wife and I took the train to Hangzhou out of this station. I found the experience actually went quite well, since neither of us spoke Mandarin. A lady staff member quickly walked us to our platform, by looking at our tickets only, and then refused a quick tip. She left her station for 5min to get us where we needed to be! Security guard then came over, looked at our ticket, and with solid gesturing finger, pointed to say "board here." As another reviewer alluded to, it can be very overwhelming and stressful. It can. But utilize staff and the thousands of travelers around you.
Nice place with shopping and efficient flow. I did not have any issues finding where to go. Buying the tickets was the only slow down in the process.

There are high-speed train services to nearby cities and Beijing from Hongqiao Train Station. It is also possible to fly to the important cities of China at affordable prices from the adjacent airport. You can easily reach the train station and airport from the city center by metro.

We went here with a Chinese speaker which I think must help.  She bought the tickets and found the gate.  We sat in the restaurant car all the way to Ningbo which was about 2 hours. Then you can eat your own food or buy some there. The trip was very smooth.  We went through one town which had lots of chimneys smoking massively and a very think smog over the place. The station was very big and clean
First class cars are the best! Business class is spacious enough to accommodate three people. Drinks and cookies are included in the service. The sofa is fluffy and can recline fully automatically.
If you don't speak or read Chinese stay away!  It's confusing enough for native Chinese!  You will NOT be able to handle this place if you have no Chinese.
Much bigger and cleaner than Shanghai railway station. Unfortunately, ticket vending machines are only for ID card holders and ticketing window only accepts local cards.

A must do when you visit Shanghai is ride on the bullet train. It sits on 300kmh and my empty coffee cup sat on the window sill all the way. Not a bump. The station is big and easy to find your gate. More expensive than flying, but worth the experience. Also hooks up with local metro.
Adjacent to Hongqiao Airport, it is convenient to take the fast train to nearby Hangzhou. Lots of merchandise shops around for last minute shopping.
it is fast train station and in same building with Hongqiao Airport. If you are travelling early in the morning, pl take hotel near by.

It’s impossible to get lost, it’s written where the ticket office is, where the departure hall is, where the taxi, metro, etc.. all the boarding gates are written on huge boards, a large waiting room, everything is clean, there are many toilets, there are many cafes on the lower floors.
Very well connected with Hongqiao Airport, Subway and with city, mainly for those in the Puxi Area. Also this train station has several options for long distance trains in China.

What can one say... This place is amazing... It is total controlled chaos.  I prefer traveling by high speed train and the transportation system in China is becoming the worlds standard.  The signage is clear and getting to the gate is no issue.One caveat:  Get there early because the thousands of people are sure to be there.

The best Railway station in the world, so organized and everything is well thought of so that the hundreds of thousands of travelers can make their journey with ease.Connected to Hongqiao airport and the local Metro. You can make it to any part of Shanghai, China or the world very easily from here.

Very clean and efficient set up.  They even have a Xing ba ke (look it up).  It did help that my daughter speaks Mandarin when we picked up our tickets.  If you do not, it would be better to have your tickets delivered to your hotel.  Easy to navigate and very organized.  LOVE the fact the train attendants are dressed elegantly and the place is spotless.  Took the train to Beijing (there is a subway stop there so skip the cab line and pay the 2 kuai to ride anywhere in Beijing).

Very big place, from there you can get the bullet train to go to Suzhou -the Chinese Venice-, which is a beautiful city to visit.It's a clean and modern station, but if you are not travelling by train, don't bother going there.

Well indicated, massive and clean. runs as you will expect and better, easy to get to as well. China can be a very confusing place but they have some stuff, like their public transport stations to high standards...

I used it when moving from Shanghai to Hangzhou. It's a train similar to Japan's Shinkansen, and it seems to shake a little more than in Japan. I think the price was cheaper than in Japan. My train ran on time.

This building is huge inside! Nothing much to see here: a decent amount of shops but nothing special except for the size of the main hall! This is huge...no columns in the middle to support, so you really feel how tiny you are in this one big room! Impressive...

Man this place is huge and very modern. Never have I ever seen a railway station so big and beautiful! This place is out of the world. I am an Indian so its quiet obvious you can't found such stations in India(lol) but many of my European friends told me that even the railway stations in Ukraine and Germany are awful in front of this station. And the staff over there is most courteous and helpful. They would help you out in any situations. A friend of mine missed his train but the Chinese authorities arranged another train from him without taking in any extra charge and without many hassle.
this station is huge and very convenient to access to different lines of subway in shanghai as well as high speed trains service to other towns.
It is an excellent experience to use this train station, very modern and accessible facilities, tickets are very easy to buy despite the language.

The maximum speed changes depending on the time of day, but you can experience that speed and get to the center in no time, so you can kill two birds with one stone. There are also bundles with round-trip tickets and one-day subway passes, so it's a good idea to research in advance. If you're staying along Subway Line 2, it's definitely worth it.

I took a flight from Beijing South to Shanghai for work. A Chinese colleague was planning to buy a ticket on the day, but is it summer vacation? I couldn't buy a first class seat, but I finally got a business seat, which meant a two-hour wait. Unlike Japan's Shinkansen, the tracks are straight, so you can't compare the ride comfort. However, the seats are wider than the green cars on the Shinkansen, and you can sleep completely flat. I almost overslept. However, when you wake up with an electric recliner, it's broken and you can't go back to normal. There was a problem with other seats as well, so I had to use force to move them. The ticket office only has explanations in Chinese, so if you don't speak Chinese, you won't be able to buy a ticket.
A great experience - modern, clean and efficient.  Took the fast train to Wenzhou and the whole experience was comfortable and seamless.
An incredible train station. Huge, clean and everything perfectly organized. Both the ticket pick-up area and the waiting halls are perfectly organized. Starbucks and McDonald are also available :-)
Located next to airport which is a plus it is basically good except they cannot handle payment by (foreign) credit card is at best problematic!
A 24-hour subway and linear round trip ticket cost 85 yuan. Recommended for those who plan to mainly use the subway for transportation.
This place is huge, but pretty easy to find where you need to go. Remember to leave early or give extra time to travel there, Shanghai traffic can be quite stop-start, not as bad as Beijing though.

This is more like an airport then a train station.  It's so well organised - you're not allowed on the platform until the guards say so, just like at the airport gate.Imagine being here (so organised and clean) then going straight to Delhi's main train station which we did...!

The platform is very open and connected to the outside, so it's very cold. However, it's good because it's quick to get to the airport. However, as with all means of transportation in China, the chairs are a bit dirty, but they are on the clean side.
An immense station that almost looks like an airport. Really comfortable. Well served. Equipped with various catering services.
I was in Hongqiao to take the bullet train to Beijing. The terminal is very modern and can be reached by subway. The punctuality of the trains and access to boarding is very comfortable.

i like this place because it's like an airport. very bug and organized. but since there are a lot of people coming here to go back to provinces especially peak season, i suggest you go here 2 hrs before your suggested trip. the instructions and informations on screen is chinese so you need ample time to ask around. I like the window personnel because they speak and understand english so it's easier to purchase tickets. Maybe because of beijing olympics that these people learned english language
caught the high speed train from here, very nice and clean station, i was with friends who read Chinese, but if I was on my own a couple of more signs in english would have helped.

Incredibly cool station with fast trains that go to all major cities in China. There is also some shopping and restaurants here. Please book tickets in advance as the queues at the ticket offices are long. It is a very modern station with all the amenities you can imagine. Just like an airport. *The easiest way to get here is by metro. If you have to get out of the station at night, you should avoid the usual taxi queue, which can be extremely long. Walk up and out of the station instead, as no metro runs.

This station has everything you could possibly need--more like a Western airport.  Note you cannot buy train tickets from the automatic machines without a Chinese identity card, you must speak with a teller.

I rode expecting to do 500km, but the top speed that day was around 300km. You will need to transfer to the subway or taxi from the station you get off at, so it might be better to take a taxi from the beginning. A taxi from the airport to the city center costs about 200-250 yuan.

We read a review which said to take your own food on the trains, so we got a small takeaway package from our hotel.  However, there are shops galore at this HUGE train station. Even if you can't read Chinese, you will see on your ticket at the top in the middle your train number, the next line is your originating train station and your destination, the next line is the date and time of departure and next to that is the carriage/car number and your seat number.  At the bottom right-hand side is your gate number, e.g. 20B or 18A.  On one side of the station are the "A" gates and the other side are the "B" gates, so you'll know where to wait.  When the sign above the gate is red it is NOT ready to board and when the sign turns green, you can board.  You can only go onto the platform about 10 minutes before the train arrives.If all else fails, there is a customer service desk in the middle.

The design is attractive: simple and clear, circulation and signage are excellent. No hassle or scrum to get on the train. Plenty of food outlets and shops. This is a "sister" station of Beijing Nan and both are EXCELLENT stations. The high-speed rail experience was one of the best rides of our lives could not be better!

Of course it is crowded. It's a railway station and it's in China. However it is very very efficient. Hongqiao is located in the west of the city so please make sure that if you are staying east side ensure that you keep enough time to reach the station. The traffic could get very very difficult and slow.
This station is located in the other SHANGHAI airport, it connects the train station, and metro lines 2 and 10; Despite its size, it is functional.

Although the building is vast, a clear map of the station premises cannot be found on the internet, so when greeting first-time users, it is difficult to identify a designated spot within the station premises and meet them immediately. The last train on the subway also runs earlier than on the high speed railway, running out before 11pm. Therefore, taxis are the main means of transportation, but there are long lines and you need to be prepared to transfer. It is very difficult for a first-time Japanese visitor to buy a same-day ticket in the same way as the Shinkansen in Japan, as passport information is required, there are language barriers, and the train is always crowded. We recommend that you ask a local representative or travel agency in advance. In any case, compared to terminal stations in Japan, Europe, and America, its convenience is not so good.

I have walked from Hongqiao Airport countless times, but this is only the second time to the train station, and the first time to set off. The queue outside to buy tickets was really scary, so I gave up the idea of ​​changing my ticket, so I went in to find a coffee shop to sit for a while. There is actually an Alipay booth in the hall, demonstrating the offline payment function, which is very ambitious.
This station is quitw new and convenient as it is very near the hongqiao airport. If you need to go to suzhou it s the best way

got of a high speed train and though first time through this station the directions were flawless and i was out in a jiffy after meeting up  at the correct exit gate (there are many) with the person who came to receive me.

But we found it eventually and picked up our bullet train tickets for Beijing. Gotta do it the day before just to be sure, finding the right counter 5 minutes and queue was about 15 minutes wait. Need your passport. The station is huge and well resourced with waiting rooms and coffee shops, easy connection to the local network.

If you buy a Shanghai public transportation card at the airport and ride this linear train, you can ride it for 40 yuan. From there, I recommend taking the subway and other forms of transportation, as you don't have to worry about buying tickets. A deposit of 20 yuan is required, but it can be refunded at the same location on your return. It was my first time on a maglev, but it was over 300km long and only took a few minutes. It seems that it has traveled 400 km several times, but even though it has been in operation for several years, it was still at the same level as China. It's so salty that it can't be compared to Japan's Shinkansen. The seats inside the train were dirty, there was a platform where you couldn't enter until the scheduled time, and there wasn't even a KIOSK inside the station. It cannot be compared to the Shinkansen, which travels long distances in Japan's mountainous, valley-filled and tunnel-filled terrain, and has a comfortable and clean interior. I'll probably never ride it again.
point of importance because trains, subway stations, airport, and almost any means of transportation you may need to get around Shanghai connect here.
A station commensurate with the development and power of China. Very functional, organized and clean.

Clean, airy, well organised. Obviously train travellers are well cared for and all very organised in China. Trains are easy to find, queues run smoothly and the trains themselves are very clean, smooth and on time!!All went very smoothly for our fast train trip to Hangzhou.

This place was well organised, it's easy to find taxi, Metro (Lines  2 & 10) and you are connected directly to Hongqiao Airport. To get to the international Airport Pudong takes only short time if taking bus or Metro Check the last train times (around 11pm or so.)

It was my first time to take the high-speed rail. The whole station was full of people. Everyone finally found the entrance according to the instructions on the ticket. When the time came, they entered the waiting room in order. One small drawback was that the entrance sign was not very clear and it was not easy to identify whether it was the entrance.

A gigantic station building with extensive infrastructure. Everything works extremely well, the trains and service are above all praise (every passenger in the carriages is even given a tablet video player). The train speed is about 300 km per hour. I would really like there to be more information in English, otherwise it’s hard to figure out the schedule and there are problems with buying tickets!

Regular seats are basically 50 yuan, but if you show your e-ticket receipt at the counter when purchasing a ticket, the price will be 40 yuan. There is a speed display inside the car, and when I rode it, the maximum speed was 301 km/h, but it seems that it can reach 400 km/h several times a day. It took about 10 minutes to reach the final destination. I got on the train around noon on Thursday, and the occupancy rate was about 30%. If I'm not in a hurry, I don't think there will be a second time.

I will say its very well maintained with so much crowd travelling from here everyday. The train connectivity is very good. Navigating through station is very easy. Buying ticket and catching train is very easy and convenient. Food court is of OK size. Waiting area is sufficient. Only drawback is that it is in one end of city.
well organzied, it's easy to find taxi, Metro and you are connected directly to Hongqiao Airport. To get to the international Airport Pudong takes only short time if taking bus or Metro.

This is a huge station with most of express trains departing from here. Directly connected to Hongqiao airport. Beware that if you arrive you need to know you exit where. Taxi pick up can be a mess. Metro lines 2 and 10 are available but cease operation around 11pm or so.
Great transportation hub.   Very modern and efficient.  Easy to get around and no trouble to communicate.

For work reasons I needed to move from Beijing to Shanghai during the day, but it wasn't possible between flights and I took the train. Positive experience, business class, very comfortable, you can work, use the phones, and sleep, especially to recover from jet lag. Very comfortable and well served.

We arrived on the High-Speed train from Beijing. The signboards and directions are clear and straight forward in Chinese & English. Clean and bright station. The taxi line was orderly and although the line was long it was constantly moving. There were some 'taxi touts' standing alongside selling their services & trying to convince locals and tourists alike not to waste time in the line. I see little sense in that because the long line does move at a good pace from the ever flowing taxis and most importantly the taxis at the end of the line are metered rides.Stay alert as always at train stations around the world. 'Spidey' tingle, on a scale of 1-10 (where 10 means get outta there fast), this station scores a 3.5.

It is easy to get to via taxi or subway and VERY large.  Going through security  can be tricky as people are in a hurry and push in front plus you have to watch your bags.  Mine went through x-ray and the person in front grabbed it, could have been just to move it out of their way but need to be observant.  The train tickets have to be picked up as a specific window (88 I think) which is for people with passports which need to be verified.  However, there are many locals in the line as well which really increases the wait time for the line.  The station is very well organized with no issues determining where to enter to the platforms, clean and with many food and drink options and seating.  Seats are assigned so I generally wait to go through the turn styles as a line forms early.  Make sure you take an official taxi when you are leaving and not to take a ride from someone offering a taxi with no wait time (there will be many offers) so go to the queue area with the chrome plated railings.  If you take the "no wait" taxi, be prepared to pay exhorbinent rates and not to arrive at your destination.   Overall it works like an airport.

Okay make sure you arrive at least an hour before your trip to purchase tickets and get a sense for the environment.  The morning rush can be overwhelming if using for the first time.  The train station is very organized but there is a lot of people buying tickets so be prepared to wait.  The trains are clean and on time.  Take a bullet train to where ever you go for a first class experience like no other.
Despite its scale, it's easy in, easy out. Not sure what else to say about a train station. Impressive architecture, clean. Very modern.

On the way back, I wanted to take the maglev train to the airport, so I took a taxi to Longyang Road Station for 50 yuan. At the hotel, I had to call it a magnet car to get the word out. There is a security check at the ticket gate, similar to an airport. When I got the VIP seat (I think it was 100 yuan), there were only Japanese people there.

We came by bullet train from Wenzhou and were amazed to see how the station was integrated with the domestic airport and bus station. It was nice because it was planned like a big mall with a variety of dining and shopping options.
