We left Shanghai on the bullet train and so found ourselves in Hongqiao station in a Saturday in early November. The station is apparently the largest railway station in the world, and I can see how it can lay claim to that title. It truly is enormous. I had visited a few days before to get our tickets ahead p, rather than worrying about it on the day. There are 8 ticket halls and each one has plenty of travellers queuing up at the window points. I joined the right one with about 20 people in front of me, thinking this was going to take hours to get to the front of the queue. Nothing like it. I had all my tickets for the three journeys we were making in total I my hands in fifteen minutes from joining the queue. UK stations could take note! There are plenty of eateries and coffee shops on the ground floor.On the day of travel, we were able to use the business lounge and this provided coffee etc and also free wifi. Plenty of departure screens, in English too. Two departure gates per platform gets everyone on the train within 1 minutes of opening and this is very impressive. No trouble in finding our coach and our train left exactly on time.Very impressive operation. I would recommend train travel in China.

We needed to leave 4 pieces of luggage at the left luggage office (right hand side as exiting station, not the left luggage office directly in main square.No price list to be seen!!Two ladies (the 'rip off sisters') took our luggage & then asked for 160 PMB which is approx. £16, well over the top. I complained so they immediately began to negotiate we settled on 150RMB mainly as I wanted to leave. See picture to avoid!Noticed after lots of men trying to attract tourists to use the left luggage office, clearly they have worked out they can rip the tourists off!
extraordinary and quite informative, for those of you who want to try the fast train to Beijing you should try going through this station.
The biggest train station ever seen. That's huge and fortunately very well organized. You're linked to all biggest cities in China, Beijing included.

I took a day trip from Shanghai to Hangzhou. It was a comfortable trip. Currently, the most reasonable and hassle-free way to purchase a ticket is to ask Ctrip, Shanghai's largest travel agency, to deliver it to your hotel. Of course, you can also use Japanese credit cards. Applications are accepted from 20 days before the ride, and you will need to register your passport number, but there is no need to send any photos. Some sites seem to ask you to send a passport photo. There is a fee of 40 yuan for the first ticket, and 20 yuan for the second ticket, and if you are traveling round trip, you have to buy them separately, so there is still room for improvement on this site, but you can easily purchase them in Japanese and it is much cheaper than asking HIS in Japan or Shanghai Navi. I chose 1st class, but I was assigned to the panoramic cabin at the front, which had only 2 business seats and 3 first class seats, and I had a very comfortable time there.
Trains are comfortable, depart and arrive on time and save you that extra waiting time in airports. Stations are centrally located and sometimes cost is 1/3 of usual air fares. Try it!

Impressive train station by all global standards in terms of size, technology, efficiency, shopping, connecting transportation, although English speaking staff and overseas ticket reservations could still be a lot improved. China has built the largest high speed rail network within 7 years and will almost double it by 2015! My business travel to our partner factory which took more than 6 hours by car on treacherous roads 6 years ago has been cut down to a mere 3 hours and will be 2 hours next year. The taxi pick-up line which is at times more than half a mile long with 500+ people in front of you dissolves within 15-20 minutes with a continuous flow of 100s of taxis pulling up to the pick-up point to haul you into Town. Both train and taxi rates are still amazingly low. Very impressive!
Crowded as all in China, but with good services, as restaurants, subway access (recommended), taxis and just by the national airport.

An absolutely huge but efficient and modern train station. It will seem familiar in style to Europeans but not Americans who don't know they live in a country with a lesser public train system. When you arrive here by fast train from Beijing etc. make sure you go to the official public taxi line. Do not freak out because of the length of the line and be patient as it will move very quickly. Also do not be misled by a staff member at the station information desk (marked by a ? sign) who tells you about the "private driver" versus "very very long wait" for taxi as if these are two reasonable choices. You stand a 100% chance of being scammed if you do not ignore the many pests inside the station or even running up and down the taxi line offering you a quicker "private taxi" ride to town. If they had a safe real taxi they would be picking up people in the real line !

is the largest train station in Shanghai, connected to the second largest airport. From there you have bullet train options for all of China. For us in Brazil, it's unimaginable, but even for those who know the railway structure in Europe and the United States, they are impressed by the organization, cleanliness and precision of this service in China. Traveling by train in China is an experience that should not be missed.
What a surprise, the sheer size of it, so modern, and efficient.  I was pleasantly surprised, and wished managers of Union station in DC, or Penn in NYC would have a look at this station.

Hongqiao's train station is close to the airport, so it's very convenient to take the high-speed rail or plane to Hongqiao. After leaving the station, you can take the subway directly to the city. A ticket costs just a few yuan, which is much cheaper than the 25 yuan in Beijing. Hongqiao is still closer to the city than Pudong. Next time I go to Shanghai, I will choose Hongqiao.

I used this station for travelling to Danyang after landing in Hongqiao airport. I could pull out some Yoans from the ATM before going directly to the tickets counters which are about 500 meters walking within the facility from the airport arrivals hall. This is not only a railway station but a large size shopping mall incorporating fashion and other regular mall businesses.A short line and we got the tickets for the train departure to Danyang. We booked the 2nd class seats which are ok. A plenty of room for legs and suitcases. This train's final destination is Nanjing while Danyang is just before. As it was Sunday night most of the people were packed with bags getting back from shopping at Shanghai to their home cities. The only downfall (which wasn't in Hongqiao) was the escalators in Danyand which didn't work so we had to drag our lagguage through the stairs.
Huge double building, station and airport, very modern, the exit is a little complicated, be careful because in Chinese stations you enter on one side and exit on the other.

The station is quite big, make me feels like I'm in an airport.. hahaIt is equipped with modern technology and modern convenience...We were here to board the bullet train to Beijing, and it's easy to navigate ourselves here...There's some shops around the boarding gate so you can buy things you need before boarding the train...If you brought a lot of luggage, there's concierge service provided by the station and the price is quite cheap...

There are two ways to purchase tickets: via the Internet or directly at the ticket office at the station. You can make reservations and pay online, but you can only pay with a card issued by a Chinese bank, and you cannot pay with a credit card issued in Japan. Furthermore, after completing the purchase procedure, foreigners must present their passport at the station ticket office to issue and receive their tickets. However, since you can see how crowded it is, it has the advantage of being able to confirm which flight you will board during the purchase process. If you go directly to the ticket office, you only need to show your passport and make the purchase once, but it is not always possible to buy a train that you can board immediately after purchasing, and in some cases you may have to wait several hours at the station. Since the ticket office is in China, there is a high possibility that there will be a lot of people. In the past, I had to wait as long as 2 hours. You need to give yourself plenty of time. The vehicle is a complete Japanese copy. However, the shaking, vibration, and noise cannot match that of the Shinkansen. However, it is cheaper and faster than the Shinkansen.

For a Chinese train station , this is a really good one: nice, clean, all facilities, helpful staff, no way you get lost...just remember this station only handles High Speed Trains and not the overnight trains. We came with a G-train (high speed) and returned with a T-train which leaves from the Shanghai Railway Station. We didn't know there was a difference, so we needed to get asap to the other one. Luckely the Subway system is very efficient so we got to the right station in no time!

In the winter, flights between Shanghai and Tianjin are often canceled or delayed due to heavy fog (smog?), so I use this route several times a year to travel from Shanghai to Tianjin. It's the same as the Tohoku Shinkansen train, so once you get on it, it's pretty comfortable, but remembering the accident in Zhejiang Province and the response that followed makes me feel sick. Also, many Chinese passengers do not sit in their assigned seats, but sit as they please, so it can be frustrating to have to be asked to move out of the way.
You can't tell if it's a station or an airport, it's gigantic, if you don't know where to go you risk getting lost.

We left by train from Hangzhou, the station was quite complicated to say the least, as well as getting on the train since you have access to the platform ten minutes before the time, at which point the train starts moving, the trip was spectacular, fast (more than 230 km) in some routes and comfortable, so when we arrived in Shanghai Hongqiao it was like entering a different and surprising China like all the buildings in this city.

There are a lot of trains from this station to different cities in China. There are ATMs and branches of some banks. The staff speaks English very poorly, so it is better to have the name of the desired city and the train schedule to it written on a piece of paper in Chinese.  PAYMENT FOR TICKETS BY CASH ONLY!!

I live in Hongqiao and use the Shanghai Hongqiao Railway Station a fair amount for travelling in China.  The Station is next to the recently (2012) expanded Terminal 2 of the Honqiao International Airport which should make it convenient, but it is not.The Train Station Terminal is highly functional and build in modern steel and marble design.  There is nothing to commend the railway station building other than that it is airy and has a reasonable amount of seating.  It is noisy.  No, not just a little noisy, the decibel level can be very high even for the vast space (in part because the marble flooring reflects the noise and there is no attempt to reduce the echoing off the ceiling and floor).  The Station has reasonable access to Line 2 of the Shanghai subway station which makes it very easy to access from any part of the city without the uncertainty of Shanghai traffic which has become increasingly terrible over the past 5 years as the number of new cars sold in Shanghai has skyrocketed.Don't expect to buy anything "international" in the Shanghai Subway station kiosks either.  Even the Starbucks is tucked away out of sight so you have to seek it out rather than being convenient.  The selection of vendors in the Station and their placement is very, very hard to understand and really makes you wonder.If you are transiting the Hongqiao Railway Station, I would give yourself 30 minutes (at least) from the arrival time (by subway or car) to locate your gate and prepare to board (generally  starting 10-12 minutes before departure.  Access to train platforms requires the use of a long stairway or escalator (or small elevator).  It is wise to get in line to board if you have luggage to carry as the boarding "window" is fairly short.  If you do not have a ticket in advance (recommended), give yourself at least 50 minutes as the ticket lines can be long depending on the time of day.  Finally, if you don't speak Mandarin be sure to book your ticket in advance through your hotel.  There is almost no English capability at the ticketing office and Chinese passengers waiting to buy tickets are notoriously intrusive and impatient.Using the station once is worth the experience of seeing a huge, modern Chinese rail station.  But there is almost nothing to attract you for another visit except the need to take a train.
Arrive at least 30 minutes before departure as stations are very busy and you will need a passport to buy tickets

This is a Japanese name that is said to have been created to imitate the Japanese Shinkansen. At over 200km/h, it is convenient for day trips to Hangzhou. Leave from Nihonbashi Station. The first class cars are 2+2, with four rows abreast, but the second class cars are sleeper cars that seat three people on each side of the bed.

The Hongqiao Railway station is located quite conveniently if you visit it via metro line 2 or 10, takes only about 35 min from the city center.The station is quite huge and is located directly adjacent to the Hongqiao airport so its convenient to switch from plane to train.The are some fast food style restaurants at the station with average  quality, and some convenient convenience stores where it is possible to buy some basic stuff. The way to the train platforms is actually quite fast, just be there a few min before departure because they close the gates about 5-10 min before departure.

First time taking the bullet train. Went on a day trip with a friend and it was both of ours first trip on the train and the station. Wow, this place was huge! I was expecting a much smaller place. We bought our tickets, the wrong ones, but we got the tickets and realized we had the wrong one. The service at the station was good and we also had a pretty decent lunch while we were there. While on the train the stewardess helped us with correcting the ticket that got us to the correct location, very nice, friendly and professional. The clerk at the station we got off on was not so much. We tried to get our return ticket corrected but he said he could not change it. Finally I realized, after being here in China for 18 months I was asking the wrong question. I asked if he could cancel our returning tickets and give us new ones, no problem!? Anyway the station and train ride was a very good experience, worth trying out. Just buy the correct ticket :-) .

This train station is just massive, and unlike any station in Europe! The station works like an airport with security checks when you enter and departures arranged in numbered gates. Departing is very easy, even if you don't speak Chinese. Arriving on the other hand is not! There is a platform for getting a taxi but it's always very crowded. You may have to wait for a taxi for as long as an hour. Many people may choose to hire a private car, but if you do, expect to pay about double the taxi fare and forget asking for a receipt.

We leave the hotel at 7.15 and take a taxi to Shanghai's Hongqiao station. Incredible influx here too, the very modern station is structured like an airport. You wait in the large room in the center and only a quarter of an hour before departure you enter the actual gate from which the train leaves. Ours is gate 1 from which the Bullet Trains depart for Beijing 533Y. Anyone who imagines a chaotic and timeless station will certainly be disappointed here, everything here is perfect, clean and very modern. The future is now here in the East, cutting-edge structures and impeccable services.

Build for the EXPO 2010 this new railway station is so huge that you can easily get lost even after having traveled through there for several time. The Waiting Hall, in front of all the gates to the tracks, is just something!

The easiest way to navigate in most major Chinees train stations is think like you are in an airport. The ticketing and departures are always the upper levels and the arrivals will be on the lower levels. Hongqiao is no different. The metro line 2 (green line) runs on the lowest level. Next level up (level 1) is the exit for the fast train arrivals, and level two is the ticketing and departures for the fast trains.Dont forget you will need your passport to buy tickets on the intercity trains. The tickets are clearly show the departure gate, on the bottom right of the ticket. The numbers in the top right are the car number follwed by the seat number. Huge screens in the departure lounge show the train number and the gate number and departure time. Entry onto the platform is fifteen minutes before the departure time. The platforms are clearly marked with the car numbers so lining up at the right car is also very easy. For a large railway station it doesn't  get much easier than this. I agree with one reviewer, if you are meeting a driver or friend be very clear about which exit number to meet at. These stations are huge with many exits on different levels and finding the right one can be challenge. Signage within the station is usually pretty good, but trying to find the right exit number and signage outside can be very hit and miss. Two starbucks outlets at Hongqiao makes early starts that much easier!
A city within the city, lots of people, but despite this, order and cleanliness reign supreme, a fantastic experience... definitely worth doing.
This station is impressive, it is a real eye-catcher with its size, its organization, its design! This is a good way to travel!

Love this train station!  Well-organized, many eateries, and very comfortable waiting areas.  There were two queues for our train, directly across from each other.  The front of the train boarded from gate 15A and the back of the train boarded from 15B.  Signs are in Mandarin and English.  Connects to the end of the subway line, which is an easy commute into the city.

imagine a station as big as Orly airport, it's gigantic, wide, clean corridors that are well marked, the "Chinese" still throw a lot of things on the ground, but there are many sweepers who pick them up, so we are amazed at the level of cleanliness, access to the (huge) platforms is 30 minutes before the departure of the "TGV" which is very long.after numerous security checks.a little word on their ''TGV'' (Shangai/Beijing 1380 km in 4h50 at 309 km/h) comfortable, spacious and very very clean even the toilets...

Very modern and clean but hard to find specific exits as signs aren't clear enough.   I always have a driver prearranged but I can never find the right location for the pickup location.  No one speaks English in the station and they are unhelpful.

Railway Station is very big with many platforms. The truth is that it seems a little complicated when you enter and see how many people there are. And like all metro and train stations, the security checks have to go through everything through the cameras. It is easy to get to on the subway.

It is a very modern station, and if we compare it with the one in Guangzhou it is totally different, very large and organized and unlike other stations in China, this one has everything translated into English which makes everything much easier. It is very easy to get there by metro since. The name of the station and it leaves you practically inside the train station. The trains you see at this station are not like the ones you see at other Chinese stations. Here you see mostly high-speed and quite modern trains. It's worth going. I arrived here and had to take the subway to go to Pudong airport, which is at the other end of the city. On the subway, everything goes on the same line. You get on here and go straight to Pudong, although right now they are doing repairs and you have to change trains. I don't remember exactly which station, but it's super easy. It is approximately a 45 minute drive to Pudong.
Nice facility, seems new and quite well organized. Very easy connection to the airport, and the porters standing around are helpful if you get lost.

A great modern station for the high speed train - it's huge so remember which entrance / exit you need It houses a lot if shops and cafés and is on line 2 metro which is great for Shanghai avoiding the traffic jams Don't forget your passport though if you're going on the train
I arrived here by plane and then took the train. Since both buildings are virtually built together, there are relatively short distances when changing trains.

The Shanghai Hongqiao Station was built to relieve the old Shanghai Railway Station, it is very large and very modern, the metro station is next to it and so is the airport. For foreigners it is not that easy to buy tickets, you have to go to the ticket office, try to buy your tickets a few days before your trip, there is usually still enough room and you can choose, the ticket office crew does speak some English. The waiting area is very large and there are dining options. Most trains that depart from here are high-speed trains.

This is my second time visit to Hongqiao and the busy station has still maintained its cleanliness very well. There are fast food restaurants on the second level if you want a quick bite, you could also pack food and eat it on the train. If you take the cab in the afternoon at 3-4pm, it should take less than an hour duration and less than 100 RMB from HongQiao to Jin Mao Tower (Lujiazu area of Pudong). If you don't wish to queue for cab, there are people in the station trying to quote you sky rocket prices. If you are travelling back to shanghai hongqiao, try to avoid coming back in the evening because (based on our first experience) firstly, cab queue is super long and secondly, evening traffic in shanghai can be pretty heavy and you could get stuck in the cab for couple of hours.

Bigger and better than some of the airports I have been to. Busier than fish markets lots of people around be careful of people with big bags rolling over your feet they seem to be on the wrong gate are running to the next playroom gate which is 10 min walk so don't blame them.
Multi-functions within one location providing all passengers with easy access to various services, although the Wi-Fi is not so reliable, which is quite the same accross China.
Excellent station.Almost like an airport,big,clean and with all facilities.The station is next to the Shanghai Hongqiao Airport.The location of the station is quite near the city center.

The size of this very foreigner-friendly station is impressive (screens in English and international restaurants). Be careful here everything works at the stipulated time, consider that it is far from the center. You can exceed the hour by Taxi

The train is fast, so fortunately you don't have to be there long. However the restrooms at the station are squatty potties, and when flushing the restroom on the train (yep, squatty potties even in first class) you actually see train tracks below. At 300 mph. First class was sparse, but thankfully cheap. Our family of four adults cost $500 to travel at highest-speed available from Shanghai to Beijing. All in all, we made it there quickly and safely, but not without a few reminders that China still has a ways to progress.

Spectacular infrastructure, much, much better than many airports we have in Brazil. Everything very organized and well signposted in English. Taking the bullet train from Shanghai to Beijing is a unique experience. You can easily reach Hongqiao Station using the subway from anywhere in Shanghai. The only negative point is that the Chinese don't really like waiting their turn and love "skipping the queue", but apart from this detail, everything else is ok. I recommend.
The structure of this station looks like an airport, boarding and disembarking is very organized and access to the location is easy.

People in China ask me if Japanese trains are that fast. However, they simply answered that there was, but did not provide detailed explanations. If you say it's a copy of Japan, you'll get into an argument. I rode from Hongqiao Station to Shaoxing via Hangzhou. The speed was slower than in the past (before the accident), and I guess they realized that it was dangerous to run at 100 with 100 power. However, when making reservations, shouldn't couples be seated next to each other? Also, my little sister came to me and asked me to change seats, so I gave her a change, but she wasn't sitting by the window. It's a shame.

Very impressive building. Layout is spacious so doesn't feel crowded even during morning rush hour and train being full. Excellent system of regulating the entry of passengers onto the platform 15 minutes before departure of the train. So everyone gets to wait in the spacious station hall. Good clear sign ages.

If you don't go to the station at least one hour before you want to board and buy a ticket, you won't be able to board the train that stops at your desired time and station. Things get even more difficult during the Lunar New Year and National Day seasons. All seats are reserved and there are no standing seats. It's always full. Although the regular cars have only been in business for a few years, they are very dirty and damaged, and the locals are talking loudly, making it a chaotic situation. Be sure to buy a first class ticket. The seats are comfortable and ratty. In terms of Japanese yen, the difference is very small.
If you are travelling by train make sure you give yourself plenty of time.The queues are long but it is very efficiently run.Not many people speak English so you need to be well prepared.

The Hongqiao railway station is quiet amazing. When you walk in, you`ll fell like you entered an airport. Thousands of people, all races rushing in one direction or another. And of course, there are more than enough shops and restaurants there.  To summarize it - Hongqiao feels like the future. :)

I came in here on the bullet train from Beijing and the taxi queue at the South was ridiculously long. However don't bout off because it only took ten minutes as there is a constant stream of taxis coming through to pick up new fares.

As an international crew member for an airline I was pleasantly surprised by this experience. If you purchase the tickets in person you will need cash and your passport. We paid $290 (1748 yuan) for Business Class and it was worth every penny. They provide a meal, blanket, slippers, TV, earplugs, eyeshades and earbuds. It took under 5 hours to get from Beijing to Shanghai and I was more comfortable than if I'd flown First Class from NY to LA. I suggest purchasing the tickets ahead or just allow enough time to familiarize yourself with the train station as it is massive.

Second class seats have less compartment space, which is inconvenient for those carrying large luggage. Even though I have a reserved seat, when I go to my seat, there is always someone else sitting there. It's still better since first class cars are somewhat managed. If you have large luggage, we recommend sitting in a first class seat as there is some space to store your luggage.
You get lost because the environment inside the station is so immense, not to mention the outside. Better to have a guide.
One of the best and well organized train station. Although i am a foreigner it was quite easy to buy tickets and move around the place.
The station is very clean. But if I were alone, I would probably get lost. The trains are insanely fast and quiet.

The first impression is that it is big, very majestic. There were many people getting on and off trains and catching flights. Everyone lined up in an orderly manner and it didn't feel crowded. The design of the train station is very good, and the signage is quite good. You can basically know where to go at a glance. In short, it is a high-end and very comfortable train station.

Taking the High Speed Train G7525 from Shanghai Hongqiao to Hangzhou. The train ride is very smooth and punctual. Inside the train is very clean and nice. The train is usually pack and seldom do have empty seats. They do sell food and drinks inside the train. Toilets are usually clean and sometime dirty depending on the distance but usually it is clean from where you starts. Therefore if you have to use the toilets, please go first before others. The train ride is very smooth even with 300km an hour. You will need your passport to buy the train tickets. It would be better to ask the hotel concierge to do it for you for a small fee.

We took the bullet train from Shanghai to Hangzhou and it was great. The station is seriously HUGE. Think 3 x airplane hangers. Lots and lots of people, but still very efficient. Easy to navigate about. Just do it
We had to go to the Hongqiao Railway station to get the high speed train to Hangzhou. Very efficient and convenient.
Train services in Shanghai are extremely nice and organised.stations are very clean.very convenient to travel through trains.

Take the Beijing-Shanghai high-speed rail from Beijing to Shanghai, the speed is 300KM/H, it feels like flying, and it only takes 6 hours. After getting off the train, I found that Hongqiao Railway Station is really spectacular, with good commercial facilities, food and drink, good guidance signs, and perfect connection with the subway. Love this train station!
absolutly a very well organize hub, both for railway station as for airport. good connection by Tube as by taxi. really easy to reach the city center in less then 20min

It's not as good as the Shinkansen in Japan, but I think it's comfortable enough to enjoy your trip. There's no need to check in hours in advance like you would for a plane; as long as you get your ticket in advance, you can arrive at the station 15 minutes early. If you want to buy tickets on the day, it's safe to buy tickets 3-40 minutes in advance. The first two rows of car 1 seem to be special seats among the soft seats, and are leather-covered first class seats. The lighting is dark and gives a VIP feel. The seat was too big and didn't fit my body very well. It's amazing how a high-speed rail network is being built all over China. There are many Japanese people who feel that it really takes a while, but this is what China Speed ​​is all about.
It was easy to buy a ticket without speaking Chinese, but remember to bring your passport, as they write the passport number in the ticket.

Went there to take the train to Hangzhou. The station was so crowded thus seats were limited. Have a look around if not rushing to take the train. A must to buy train tickets online as the queue was long and if you are foreigner, a must to collect the ticket with passport.
Good food, useful retail, excellent signage, clean toilets, spacious halls. Train, Metro, Air, Taxi, Bus....

Hongqiao Railway Station is ENORMOUS, which can be intimidating, especially to first-time visitors who don't speak any Chinese.  Do yourself a favor, and order your tickets online ahead of your trip.  Pay the extra fee to have these delivered to your hotel on arrival.  This alleviates any chance of standing in (wrong) lines & having to start over in the right one.  Plan to arrive at least an hour before your train departs-earlier, if it's a very busy time (ask the concierge at your hotel about this).Upon entering the station, everyone must pass through security-follow the crowds, and don't be afraid to push to keep your place in line.  This is not considered rude in China-they all just have someplace to go, and don't understand western ideas of queuing.  Once through, take a moment to get oriented to the station.  There is a large information desk in the center of the station, though they don't speak much English there.  Show them your ticket & they will point to the proper loading gate. The gates all list the trains loading there in both English & Chinese: the current train loading is lighted green, the upcoming train is lighted in yellow.  Trains generally load about 15 minutes before departure-don't be late!  While other forms of transportation in China may be lax in their departure records, the trains are scrupulously ON TIME.Food is available on the 2nd floor of the station (American fast food with a twist, or Chinese), as well as on most trains (Chinese only).  Bring cash if you plan to purchase food on the train.  If you ride the high speed train and  can afford it, the Executive Class seats are outstanding!  They are leather, fully reclining, and slippers & a blanket are provided.  The Executive Class cabin also has its own dedicated attendant, nicer restroom, and on longer trips, a full hot meal is included in the ticket price.  We rode 1st class on the way back, and found the seats to be adequate, the restrooms less clean (although a cleaning crew sweeps through at each station stop to tidy up), and meals were extra.  2nd class seats are the cheapest, and have the fewest frills.  Still, the train all arrives at the same time...On our return trip, we decided we were comfortable enough to take the Metro to our destination downtown.  The #2 Metro line goes all the way from Hongqiao Station to Pudong Airport, with multiple stops throughout the city.  The directions are well-marked & easy to follow, and Metro tickets can be purchased at kiosks, with an English option on the touch-screen.  If you take a taxi, use only the regular taxi queue in front of the station to avoid being scammed.  Buses are also available to most locations.  A huge, bustling, but surprisingly well-organized hub!
There you have a train station, extremely modern with many platforms. High-speed trains arrive and depart that link other cities in China.

The price is much cheaper than Japan's Shinkansen, so you can easily use it. I think it's safer to buy tickets in advance, but I've never been in a situation where I couldn't buy a ticket even though there were only soft seats available. (Even soft seats are cheap for Japanese people. The atmosphere inside the train is also very different, so we recommend purchasing soft seats.) Previously, you could use vending machines, but now you have to use your national registration card? Things like these became necessary, and foreigners basically had no choice but to buy them at the counter.

A few years ago, it became a hot topic for covering up a major accident, but if you use it often on a daily basis, it doesn't bother you much. However, the reason cell phones are so noisy in the car is probably because of the country's characteristics...

The new railway station is full of modernity. Shanghai has built Hongqiao Railway Station into a transportation hub. It is very convenient to transfer between trains. The construction of the station venues is also very fashionable and the crowds are well organized. It is really good.

massive, modern, clean station. Has a museum on site for the Meglev (superfast) trainOur tour group went on a round trip to the airport so they could experience the speed of the super fast train and most of them really enjoyed the experience.  There are places to eat and even s supermarket in the complex. A small section of the complex is currently having a massive renovation so some of the restaurants  were closed.
a 2 hour drive was a 20 minute train ride - and super convenient for a driver to pick me up to go to the next business meeting.
The station is ridiculously big and not efficient at all (1) It's quite difficult to buy tickets (2) The inside of the train is dirty (3) It's noisy (4) The service is bad. It's the worst
It looks like an airport, it’s so big, organized and so clean. We can find everything we need at this station which is the only one in Shanghai that has the TGV.
Shinkansen trains in China are very quiet. But it can't reach 300km/h. I've bought lunch in the car, but there was a lot of food!

Although the ride is not as comfortable as Japan's Shinkansen, it is quiet and comfortable. However, getting through the ticket gates and boarding the train at major stations can be a challenge. Unlike the ticket gate system in Japan, it is similar to the boarding system for airplanes, and you cannot use the ticket gate until the time is up. I can't stand it when the platform in front of the ticket gate is crowded with people...

This gigantic trainstation is ,as most things in Shanghai, worldclass. At least when it comes to technolgy and hygiene. Too bad the entire train station is underground and there is not a singel beam of sunlight coming in, even the entrences to the taxi stand are underground. Giving this collosos an unpleasent bunker-like feel.
Efficient, clean & trains punctual you'll also be given a bottle of water for your journey (our guide had to ask though). A lot of security, and it's massive you could easily get lost.

Hongqiao Railway Station links Shanghai and Beijing with the high speed train. The station itself is very easy to get to, we took a cab, however, it was accessible by metro as well. Once there, you'll first notice it's sheer size, seems surreal to be honest. At each of the four corners there are dining/coffee areas on the second level. Grab a coffee and a quick bite to eat and you can sit and watch the thousands and thousands of people milling about in this busy huge train station below. My only qualm was that boarding times and process was not well posted/explained. We purchased business class tickets but we're herded through the turnstiles with the 500 other people travelling, all forcing their way through the two aisles.

This may be the largest inter-model transportation hub I have ever seen. It is huge and complicated. I was able to follow the instructions and found my way around. The signage could be a bit more to direct the passengers. Allow yourself 30 minutes minimum to find your way, you will be fine. But it is a different story if you are to be picked by someone at this station. It will be necessary to go out the exit and call your friend which exit you are at, or they will never find you. There are so many exits which makes me dizzy.

I thought I might not be able to buy a same-day ticket at Hongqiao Station, so I lined up at the reservation counter the day before, prepared my passport, selected my first and second choice flights, wrote down and presented them, and bought the ticket myself. I was overwhelmed by the huge Hongqiao Station, and as expected, it is a representative city of China with 1.3 billion people! I admire you. However, you can't pass through the boarding gates until 15 minutes before the departure of each train, so I felt stressed by the system of having to wait in line. There is also a buffet car where you can sit, which seems to be popular. You can also drink coffee and have light snacks. It feels like the echo of the old Japanese Tokaido Shinkansen. The first class seats were spacious and comfortable with leather seats, but they were mostly empty, probably because of the high fares. It took about an hour to get to Hangzhou, and even the second class seats were reasonably comfortable.
We went by taxi to the station, had a quick lunch at Burger King and found our train easily. This is a very clear, well organized railway station. Not the most beautiful, but very efficient!

To get from the center to this huge station, you need to spend an hour on the metro. Then go through the scanning (as at every station), find your gate, wait in line... the crossing is certainly quite long. The station is huge! But it is very modern and clean, and most of the staff speak basic English

I used it for business. The couple probably bought it at the last minute. The seats weren't lined up, so I was sitting in my seat, and he showed me his ticket and gestured for me to go over there. No matter how different the countries may be, I don't think there is any awareness of reserved seats. Even if you tell the conductor (female), she will just give in to the crowd and apologize to you. I spent an unpleasant hour.

When I lived there before, it was before the Shinkansen line opened, so I think it took about 2 hours and 30 hours to get to Hangzhou by express train. The inside of the car was like a festival and I couldn't sleep. This was the case even in the first class car. This time I was in a second class train on the Shinkansen, but everyone was quiet. One child was watching TV on speakers and it was so noisy. I had reserved seats both last time and this time, but as expected, the non-reserved seats were occupied (lol). However, the person this time seemed to have been planning to get off at Shanghai Station, so I woke him up and explained the situation, and he hurried off to the platform. On the previous express train, there was an argument in Japanese and Chinese, and a Chinese person who could speak English came in and I don't know what he said, but the Chinese person who was taking the seat disappeared, and the Chinese person who was interpreting for me said something like, ``This is the seat for you to sit in (something like that).'' That left an impression on me. Isn't high-speed rail a little more expensive? I recommend it because you don't have to worry too much about riding it, and I think even Japanese people can have a relatively relaxing train journey.

High-speed trains and high-speed trains depart and arrive from this station. It is not far from Hongqiao Airport, and subways run to various places in Shanghai. There are various fast food restaurants after exiting the station, allowing tourists to eat delicious food as soon as they get off the bus.

We went to this huge station to go by train to Beijing... It feels like passing through the airport due to its size, the controls and the frenetic and incessant comings and goings! Excellent organization and cleanliness!!
With many international restaurants. The screens in English and Chinese are all perfect, very easy to travel with. A little far from the city center, 40 minutes approx.

We took a daytrip from Shanghai to Hangzhou. Thank goodness my daughter knew a little Chinese, because the person at the ticket window didn't speak any English. Make sure you have your passport, or they won't issue you a ticket. The waiting area was very nice  -- crowded, but we found seats. There are plenty of places to purchase drinks and food. Getting to the station was very simple and the people at the information desk were quite helpful.

I used it to go from Shanghai to Suzhou. I bought the ticket at Shanghai Station the day before. It was during the Mid-Autumn Festival holiday, but there was no line up and I was able to buy it smoothly with just a note and my passport (although it seemed to be fully booked on that day). On the day of the trip, I entered Shanghai Station 30 minutes early, bought some chimaki from the shops lining the concourse, and relaxed in the huge waiting room. There is also an outlet for mobile phones in the waiting room. The cars are almost the same as the Shinkansen trains in Japan and are very relaxing. I rode in both 50 yuan 1st class and 30 yuan 2nd class, but I think 1st class was more comfortable as the seats were softer.

This is one of the more impressive train station I have been to.  Very big but it works.  The waiting "room" is impressive, especially when viewed from the second level / restaurants are located here.

It is a big facility. Like an airport. Convenient,-- tube station-- next to airport-- a lot of food restaurants-- easy to find a taxiIf it compares to old Shanghai train station, this is surly a "modern" one.

We took the bullet train to Beijing and back.This place is very complex, efficient and impressive. However, it is HUGE and it can be difficult to find your way to the right gate and right platform because instructions in English cannot be found anywhere !! So make sure you give yourself enough time to figure things out, especially WHERE to BUY your ticket.It is also rather chaotic outside at the taxi-drop off point.
Airport, train station, taxi stands, subway, and bus station all connected in one easily maneuverable, monstrous complex.  Very impressive.  Plenty of signage to guide you through.  I use it often.

Although they have a lot of bad reviews, such as being imitations of Japanese products and being buried in case of an accident, they are still convenient. The main route between Shanghai and Beijing has 3 to 4 trains per hour and is always nearly full, indicating that it is a popular destination for Chinese people.
The service at the only counter that answered in English was quite rude. But the explanation by a very interested guard was good. About the very different place where we should catch the train. good.
We went to Wuxi by train and we took the rapid train at the Shanghai Hongquiao Station.  Important...need to bring your passport (copy) with you when planning to travel on Shanghai's trains.

You can basically get to anywhere on the bullet trains. Most of the times, the staff has little or no knowledge on english so if you have a chinese friend or someone who speaks the language, take them with you!

I really enjoyed using the Shanghai Metro. It is clean and very efficient. The stations were very well ventilated considering the outdoor temperature was about 41 C! Great for people watching if nothing else!
A very big station but compared to other Chinese stations this seems a little more organised, we also collected tickets we had reserved for us by China Travel DIY which was quick and easy.

Shanghai Hongqiao railway station is very convenient. You can go almost other province in China by hi-speed train. It's comfortable and easy to sleep ^^. I have experience to Wuxi, Suzhou, Hangzhou from Shanghai.

I believe at least 2 to 3 football ovals would fit into this massive station. The ticketing is  quite well organised cue system, with the obvious "cue" jumper attempts... Don't forget to collect your free water per ticket and the trains ALL LEAVE on TIME....For a great pic opportunity go o either end and at the first level there is area for photos, do this and you will be surprised at the size.....amazing....

Traveled several times using this station. It is easy with bilinual signs helping direct you. Definetly train travel is the safest and best for touring China. Just stay away from the National Holidays as the train will be VERY crowded.
Convenience and access to buses, and airport. The whole Hongqiao transport hub is so well blended together.
Huge, feels like a domestic airport...very professionally run, highly impressed with things are handled here since the train traffic seems huge.
Very easy to find your way around despite being a huge station. Outside of Shanghai, we took a cab there. Only bad thing was the bathrooms, not very clean. No soap or paper.

I used the Chinese version of the Shinkansen at Hongqiao Station. Foreigners are required to present their passports, so they are unable to use the vending machines and have to wait in long lines at the counter. You cannot enter the Shinkansen platform until the time is up. I had a hard time getting on it. The inside of the car was very comfortable. Just like the Shinkansen in Japan, they come to sell food and drinks.

We had the opportunity to enter it, since we had to take the train to Hangzhou and we were truly impressed by the size of this station, but at the same time we were very pleased to see the cleanliness and order that reigned inside. This time the proverbial confusion created by Chinese travelers was not seen.

I was impressed by the size of the station, the convenience of the location, everything was done for people, it was beautiful, bright, lots of signs, a food court on the second floor with an abundance of European fast foods.
This was a very big railway station but didn't have anything special to see or do. Easy to reach via metro lines 2 & 10.

First of all I do not understand why this railway station is catalogued as an "attraction". It is a functional building and nothing touristical.We went Shanghai Hongqiao Railway Station to take the train to Beijing. It took us 35 minutes from the very center (People's Square) by taxi and around 110 RMB, but you can easily get there in 40-45 min by metro (2 RMB).You will find here, besides several thousands of people, some shops, particularly food stalls, luggage, shoes, electronics, etc., and also a food area with McDonalds, KFC, Burger King, etc.Everything we did here was smooth and the train departed on time.Note: just in case you need it, there are no pharmacies in this railway station.
No direct flight to Suzhou, so take high speed rail after taking off the flight. It's definitely within walking distance, unnecessary to waste time waiting for taxi or take a subway

This is a big train station about 45 mins from Peoples square, on the suburbs of town.   Easy to access on the Metro 2 line.  Most things are written in Chinese and English as are most announcements.  There are a few ticket counters that agents speak english.  Allow a lot of time to get your tickets if you weren't savvy enough to get them ahead of time.  (Best bet is to pre buy and have you physical paper ticket before you get there).  Loads of food and drinks available.

If you are catching a bullet or high speed train to shanghai beijing I suggest you go up to 2 hours before train leaves . It is a huge place we counted 29 plateforms which had A and B . You also have to go throu security and check bags and wand over .all the food section is on level 2 so make sure you buy food before hand to take on the train as they only serve chinese food. They do serve coffee but it's not the best . They come throu with trolleys like on the planes.we picked up our tickets 2 days due to crowds and made sure were we had to go. International travellers have to show there passports . You can quite easy get lost as it is massive
Chinese high speed rail --- extremely fast, reliable, comfortable.  And a magnificent train station --- right next to the airport terminal.
It is pretty easy to travel by train from there. Even if you come by plane and you have to go further to Chengdu, it is quite convenient to take the train from there.
A huge railway station situated outside Shanghai centre.  Huge numbers of people but departure point easy to locate.  Lack of seating areas.  Some shops, some coffee stations and 3 eating areas.
It's not the place to be: Dirty Toilets, Old Restaurants and the trains are always late. It really truely sucks.

Myself and a friend arrived via a CRH bullet train from Beijing (4 hours).It's a transport hub including international & domestic airline terminal, CRH train station and Metro lines to city centre. Contains numerous shops and fast food restaurants.Large display boards show train times, although I would recommend a guide to purchase tickets and take to platform. WARNING: When in Shanghai and other cities beware the tea ceremony scam (an individual/group invites you to a tea festival/ceremony, then demands an excessive overpayment - $100's) at tourist locations such as 'People's Square'. Other scams include watches/jewellery/bags (fake and excessively overpriced), unofficial tour guide (excessively overpriced), bar (excessively overpriced) and massage (I dread to think). The scammers are both genders and all ages. Be alert at all times and never follow 'friendly' strangers anywhere!

Wow! The old Shanghai International Airport, Hong Qiao, is just next to it - The railway station, also known as Hong Qiao. Same place, same name. Just different kind of transportation.However, all international flights into China (except from Hong Kong and Macau) goes into Pudong International Airport. Therefore, one would have to take a cab, when you have plenty of luggage, to zip you to Hong Qiao railway station, when you need to go to other cities from Shanghai, like Wuxi, Suzhou, Hangzhou.As usual, this is China.Every where is full of people. This railway station is just as big as the airport next door itself. With little English signboards, you can get lost.. in transit.Getting a train ticket is easy, and you need your identification documents. As foreigner, passport is required to show. Locals need to show their ID card, when purchasing a train ticket.When you know the system and the way around, it is pretty easy. Even for other railway station in other parts of China.Just that there are so many people around that makes you panic. So, one need to calm down, and everything will work out in due time.Coffee shops and restaurants is available at the floor above.
Train station and airport right there and plenty of cabs. But often known for theirs and even violence. Very crowded during holidays. But a nice place with food that is digestible on the 2nd level.

This station is bright and airy as well as so user-friendly.  We have taken the bullet train (Harmony!) to Suzhou and also to Hangzhou.  We don't speak Chinese, so we did have to do a lot of asking and guessing and trial & error to get in the right lines for purchasing and then queueing.   Head for the information desk and then proceed.  If you are prepared for that, you will be fine.  Waiting areas are clean, big and bright.  It is less cumbersome than plane travel and the system is efficient and on-time.  I like this station because it is right on our metro (line 2) and there were very few steps to maneuver with luggage, unlike the other train terminal we used last year.
even though it is crowded always, the entire area is maintained well  spik and spanEven if you do not know local language the English writing or signs will help you to get in to proper trains.

You may get lost at this station. You need to ASK and ASK if you don't read and speak Chinese. The security guards are helpful. The Ticket displays are written in Chinese and at least the signs are in English also.It is a beautiful place and I was surprised China has developed this much. They are very efficient and the station is well planned. Watch your ticket carefully for the seat numbers (with letters) and the gates to use. There are a lot of gates so be careful you don't miss the train. Better still ASK security for guidance.Enjoy Shanghai!

Connecting Shanghai and Hangzhou in two hours, the high-speed train is convenient, time-saving, and affordable. Normally, most people travel from Shanghai to Hangzhou by express bus, but the expressway is so congested that the 2-3 hour journey often becomes 3-4 hours. On the other hand, high-speed trains (China's version of the Shinkansen) are relatively punctual, have frequent trains, and can easily be used for day trips in the same section. If you are visiting Shanghai and planning a trip to Hangzhou, we highly recommend using the high-speed train.
I took the high-speed train from Kunshan to Shanghai Station for about 20 minutes. The passenger cars are comfortable, but I think smoking is allowed in all of them. Is it difficult for non-smokers?

Fast and efficient way to travel.  We took the bullet train to Hangzhou for the day from Shanghai.  First class seats were very comfortable.  Speeds got up to 302 kph.  Shanghai to Hangzhou in 1 hr. 10 min.  That is with three other 5 minute stops along the way.

I have to agree with almost everyone who has put up a posting here about using the high speed service between Beijing and Shanghai. When you add up the time and expense (and exercises in patience...) of having to fly between both cities, using the train is by far the most economical and most rewarding. The best part for me though is that being 1.8 meters tall, I am not eating my knees for the entire journey. The seats fold back, are comfortable, and you can actually have a decent nap during your journey.The only issue that I have is with the dining car. I have now used the train twice and both times I am awestruck by the lack of etiquette on the part of the passengers, and lack of proactive management on the part of the staff. Both times that I have used the train service, I have gone to the dining car to eat and have had to either stand and eat, or on this journey, share a single sized bench on the half-table near the service counter. Meanwhile there are people loitering, eating take away food that was not purchased on the train, or watching four middle aged gentleman pretending to drink from empty cups. The staff needs to be more proactive in getting loiterers away from those tables so that paying customers can enjoy the food that they have purchased.That said, I will continue to use the train service every time I come to Shanghai. It is by far the best way to get around China.

China's version of the Shinkansen is very convenient, but it's always crowded. Reservations are required. Tickets are also sold throughout the city, so we recommend purchasing them in advance even if you are charged a handling fee. Also, a passport is required at the time of purchase. Although it is available for purchase online (you can purchase it from 20 days in advance), it is difficult because it is a Chinese site. If you have friends in China, it would be convenient to ask them to buy it in advance with their credit card. Passport number is required when making a reservation. If you purchase online, you will receive your ticket at the station on the same day. (Tickets can be issued even for tickets departing from other stations)

I had to make my way across town to catch a rush hour train from this station. I knew it was big from the pictures and simply looking at the schedules with dozens of trains every hour. I got the hotel concierge to buy my tickets in advance. The guide book advise 35 minutes travel by taxi without traffic so I allowed 50 minutes given the time of day. It took over an hour to get there and the scary thing as I approached this colossus building with just 8 minutes before my train departure how will I navigate my way to the correct triangle in time. I was concerned. Once inside I was faced with a wall of commuters being fed through airport style security full bay search, search scans and body scans. Very concerned now because I have been in security queues for over an hour in Greece. Fortunately this is not Greece, there was a hub of security personnel processing people at the speed of knots. A guard who spoke little English but could point was engaged by my look of total bewilderment to help me jump the line and he pointed to where I had to run to get the connection. It is a vast place but with luck I got there just as the doors were closing.On the return I decided to use the Metro just to get the experience of joining the queue of 100's of commuters waiting to buy tickets at the high speed and very efficient ticket machines. Brilliant example of public transport at its best

Although the tracks are new and there are only straight lines, the ride is definitely more comfortable than Japan's Shinkansen. Running endlessly at over 300 km/h and covering 1000 km in 4 hours is amazing. The train and track seem to be designed for speeds of 400 km/h, so I guess this is normal. First class is too expensive and I haven't seen many people on board, but both first and second class cars are full. 2nd prize is about 2/3 the price compared to 1st prize. In the past, if you rode in 1st class, you would get a lot of free snacks, but lately I've been getting a lot of snacks for free. With the development of high-speed railways, airplanes are taking up the slack, and there are some routes that no longer fly, and some routes that only have a few flights a week left. This is inconvenient. It would be nice if the high-speed train station was close to the airport, but in most cases this is not the case. Well, in Japan, Narita and Haneda are not directly connected to Shinkansen stations, so it's the same thing. Anyway, try riding without any preconceptions. After that, if you ride the Shinkansen in Japan, you might feel sick.
The station was huge and actually looked like any airport.It has a very modern appearance.Upon arrival, we couldn't find a clean toilet/urinal! The ones available were not kept clean.

This is the largest railway station in the whole of Asia, and it certainly isn't disappointing. Signage is in both Mandarin and English, so it is easy to find out what time and the platform from which your train will be departing. There are a wide variety of shops and eateries, including Relay, Disney Store, Starbucks and KFC. Even though the station is very busy a lot of the time, we didn't find it difficult to find a seat. All in all it was above standard expected of a major railway hub, very impressive station.

There was a major accident in the year I was assigned to China, so I avoided using high-speed trains in China as much as possible, but after a year, I have been using them as needed. Every time I ride a high-speed train, I feel like the safety standards and service are improving little by little. I think 2nd class is sufficient, but the 1st class seats are very comfortable and I have traveled between Shanghai Hongqiao and Nanjing, Xiamen and Fuzhou, Changzhou and Shanghai, and it was comfortable. Although I haven't had the courage to ride for a long time yet, my Chinese friends seem to prefer taking the high-speed train over planes these days when going from Shanghai to Beijing. The grandeur of Nanjing's train station is astounding. The other day, when I took the high-speed train from Jitsugi, I noticed that there was a stylish cafe inside the station, and I felt that the service had improved, as I noticed that the staff were efficient when entering the form. I always get tired of the hassle of having to bring my passport with me to buy tickets in advance, and the amount of people at Hongqiao Station, but I will continue to try to use the minimum necessary amount and enjoy myself as much as possible when I use the station.

It is certainly not a place to "visit" on purpose, but passing through it for work I must say that it has nothing to do with our stations. Large, clean and organized like an airport with the gate opening 15 minutes before the train leaves. Unique.
A very large railway station, well organized with clear signage in English, a hub for long distance trains to other cities in china.

Big railway station with connection to the high speed train, the metro and connection to the airport Hongqiao. Lots of small restaurants and shops, you can spend here at least a few hours to look around

Though this station is far from my side of town, I had to venture over to Hongqiao to pick up a friend who was arriving at this station due to his oversight in picking the correct arrival station in Shanghai.Anyway-- the station was very large, big, clean and easy to find the areas where I needed to go to find my friend.  The station is connected to the subway making it very convienent to get to but -- very hard to get out of due to all the arriving trains and many *millions (*intentional exageration)  of people wanting to get into the city center.It was a nice station in all things I could see, everything was clearly marked even for non-chinese speakers such as myself, and it was large enough that it can accomodate the large numbers of travelers on an average day. I did not go on a holiday when I'm told its packed and bursting at the seems...

very convenient station, clean, understandable and simply beautiful. very understandable also for foreigners - it is usually a little scary to travel on local trains in other countries, since the trains are primarily intended for the local population. and here - everything is like at the airport, boarding gates, buying tickets, signs and signs. very cool) by the way, only high-speed trains leave from this station. There are other stations in Shanghai for regular trains - well, they will be worse... well, just for the local population)
Gigantic and modern express train station next to Hongqiao Airport. Very clean and tidy. The only big problem is that the timetable with train schedules and routes is only in Chinese.
It is an incredible station, very well organized, but like everything you see in the city, full of people.  Incredible!!!!

Shinkansen trains are becoming faster and faster, and they are becoming very convenient. The time is getting more accurate, and of course there have been some serious accidents, but I still think it's a safer vehicle than a car or taxi. Next, when buying tickets, be aware that D (train) 1234 (temporary number) is cheaper and G (high-speed railway) 6789 (temporary number) is more expensive for the same section. If you don't say "D, D" when purchasing a ticket, you will be offered G, even if it takes about the same amount of time. Please do your best with “Unnecessary G Poo Yao Ji”.

We asked our hotel to get us our train tickets to Hangzhou, 35 minutes away - they didn't charge a fee for this service and the tickets were delivered in less than 24 hours. Clean, non-smoking waiting areas, though most seats were taken when we got there midday. Drinks and some snacks are sold at shops in the train station. Platform numbers are posted at different turnstiles ( you don't have to read Chinese) and people get in line to go into the departure area around 15 minutes ahead of departure. You put your  ticket through a slot, retrieve your ticket, then go through a turnstile into the platform area. Cars are marked and you get onto the car specified on your ticket, then find your seat. We found a woman sitting in one of our seats but when we compared tickets, she moved as she was in the wrong train car. Non- smoking cars, air conditioning, snacks sold by a woman wheeling a cart through.Overhead screens show the train's last stop; not all the stops were posted on the screen until the train got close to a stop. Then the stop name was posted on the screen. We had no problem recognizing our stop as it was posted in pinyin (it said "Hangzhou") as well as in Chinese characters. The train was very clean, efficient and on time. We saw that everyone put their small rolling luggage on the shelf above their seats, unless they had larger pieces of luggage which they deposited behind seats at the end of the car. Excellent, and no problem on the return trip back to Shanghai. It helps to know which direction you are going to when you cab it out of the station though - so study a map to see if you need to leave from the north or south entrance- save on the cab fare. Or, take the subway into town.
It looks just like Japan's Shinkansen. A beautiful lady like CA is nice. It seems that many local people do not know that it is a Japanese technology.

Have you noticed that the entrances and exits of Hongqiao Railway Station are not numbered. There are several "West Entrances and Exits" alone, and there are many entrances and exits without names. Moreover, inside the station, the corridors and pillars are very similar, which leads to many people being confused about the direction. I just thought of a few reasons: Are you afraid that the enemy will know the layout of the train station too well? Well, this is not a military base. This is a place where visitors come and go. Is it a pleasure for visitors to get lost? ? Does it look bigger? Come on, be as old as you want. Do you like seeing a bunch of people walking around with their phones? The waitress at the information desk was so tired that she licked her lips, but she still strived to be a service model. . .

An amazing new rail passenger facility easily accessible by bus, taxi or subway from anywhere in Shanghai.  Dozens and dozens of shops and restaurants on both levels as you wait for the train.  Downside for foreign residents is that we can't use the ticket  vending machines, because we must show our passport when purchasing or picking up pre-purchased tickets.  Buy your tickets in advance if at all possible because many of the 2nd and 1st class train tickets can sell out, and the business class seats are nice, but pricey.

I must go here,cause I fly to and from Hangzhou.I thought,I will find a dirty,dark railway station..,but I 1 was very surprised seeing the huge,bright,clean,and integrated station,such as airport...and you can go from and to this railway station easily,direct by metro,or taxi.

I have traveled between Shanghai and Wuxi many times. In terms of Japan's Shinkansen, it's like going from Nagoya to Kyoto. I always take the first class (=green car), and it's cheap at just under 100RMB (≒1,700 yen). There are Japanese E2 type vehicles and German ICE type vehicles, but unfortunately the ICE type has less shaking and is more comfortable to ride. The ICE type seems to be mainly used between Shanghai and Beijing, while the E2 type is mainly used between Shanghai and Nanjing. Shanghai Hongqiao Station is a newly built station for the Shinkansen, and is functional and clean, but compared to Shanghai Station, there are fewer trains, and the traffic around the station seems to be worse, so I prefer to use Shanghai Station. few
We went on a journey on the new fast train. The station was absolutely spotless and every thing was so efficient. a surprisingly interesting experience.

The place is huge and clean, quite easy to find your way inside, right next door to the airport, so you can walk from the train to the plane without getting out.Beware that this place is always crowded, sometime it's ok but it can be a nightmare due to some holidays or worse, the Chinese new year.Electronic ticket vending machine ARE NOT for foreigner so don't waste your time waiting to buy a ticket as people need to scan their chinese ID card in order to buy a ticket, you can't scan your passeport or foreign ID in it.You will have to queue at the counter, note that there is counter downstairs but also upstairs at the departure, after security check so if downstairs is too crowded try upstairs.There is some English speaking counters but expect little english speaking from the staff.I strongly recommend to buy your ticket in advance by coming several day before your departure, either directly at the train station either in many railway ticket shops downtown, however these shops don't sell all the ticket, I don't know why but you may have to go to the train station to buy your ticket in advance.

Purely functional. No art or color of any kind. Food options very limited. Very little English signage, so you have to know where you are going or ask around if you don't speak Mandarin. Buying a train ticket requires waiting on a long line with nothing in English and no assistance. All that said however, the station is fairly efficient when it comes to putting you on your train. The train network is large and the high speed trains get you to your destination relatively quickly. I've used this station more than a dozen times and only once was a train late, and then only by a couple of minutes. Easy access to Shanghai Metro System and Shanghai Hongqiao Airport (for domestic flights only). Many bus connections into Shanghai and beyond. Overall I'd rate this station highly for regular commuters or foreigners who've been living in China for a while, but not for tourists or first-time travelers to China.

It can't be compared to Japan's Shinkansen, but it's punctual and fast, so there's no reason not to use it. The cleaning inside the train is pretty good, and it's not too rough. Passengers had good manners and were quiet.

Easily accessible on the subway. As with everything in China it is very busy. Signs are in Chinese and English, and is very well organised with good seating while you are waiting. Clean and tidy toilets and hot water is available for your noodles.Most impressive.

Pudong may be newer or bigger but the old Hongqiao airport is still my favorite for non-international flights. Conveniant to getting into and out of Shanghai not a very long metro ride with a required change of trains like Podong.The railway station has been modernized and connects the airport, Fast Trains and Shanghai Metro - great for travelrs in China.

Used from Shanghai South to Shaoxing North. In the first place, as a result of researching "Let's go to Shaoxing City!", I boarded the Shinkansen without knowing it was a Shinkansen. The ride comfort is the same as that of Japan's Shinkansen. Moreover, there is a TV in the office, and this one is luxurious? (lol). However, I don't feel like I'm getting much speed. However, I would definitely like to experience riding the Shinkansen while looking at the vastness of China.
Very efficient and very clean train station with well organized train accesses. the gates are activated 15 minutes before the train departs. It feels like being at the airport.

It's more like an airport than a railway station, big and modern and very impressive, and operates the " MAGLEV " train to the airport, which is the fastest land based form of transport, which does the 19 miles in a mere 7 minutes, when useing it's top speed, though we took a slower time ( due to restrictions at rush hour ) which took us 8minutes15 seconds, still pretty good eh !!!

I went to Shanghai Hongqiao Railway Station when I was going from Shanghai to Suzhou. It was really big and comfortable, except the toilet of course. You can directly reach the station via MRT Line 2. It has two kinds of train, the first one will go all the way to East Xujing, and the other one will stop at Songhong Road. Take the one that goes to East Xujing. The Railway Station is exactly one station before East Xujing, and located one station after Shanghai Hongqiao Airport.

I used it from Ningbo to Hangzhou and from Hangzhou to Shanghai Hongqiao. Tickets can be reserved and purchased at the hotel in Ningbo. 96 yuan including handling fee. I only needed a copy of my passport to verify my identity. In Hangzhou, it was not possible to make arrangements at the hotel, so I was told about a nearby sales office and made a pre-order purchase with my passport, which cost 77 yuan, including a 5 yuan handling fee. It is best to check the stations, as the stations for conventional lines and high-speed railways may be different. Hangzhou and Hongqiao are connected by subway. Each location has a baggage inspection and the premises are large, so it's best to allow plenty of time. In particular, Hongqiao is a complex with a subway and a domestic terminal, so we had to walk quite a bit. The high-speed railway itself is almost the same as Japan's Shinkansen, including the system, and is easier to get used to than Europe's TGV. Perhaps because most of the passengers were young and on summer vacation, they were very orderly and didn't rush to get ahead of the others, so I felt that my social skills had improved in line with the hard work.
Very clean, safe and not a bad place to wait for a train.not enough places to eat, and it is often crowded.
This is one of the biggest railway stations in China but quite comfortable. except the toilets. Be prepared for the anti-sanitary. A lot of cafes, shops, but the seats are usually all occupied.
Huge train station with lots of food and shopping. Big screen clearly showing the departure time and gates. No problem for non-chinese speakers. Has escalators and lifts for getting up/down platform.

We had to pick up our previously reserved tickets at the station.  WARNING: do not enter the station until you have the tickets in hand.  We waited in line, went through security and began looking for the ticket office to collect tickets ordered online from an acquaintance in China.  After wandering and finally finding an English speaker, we discovered the ticket office was far outside the station.  After a long walk dragging bags, up and down stairs, and waiting in 2 long lines, we finally found the right line and got our tickets.  Going through the line and security again, we made it to our train with 8 minutes to spare!  The good news is that the big monitor was easy to read telling us which track we were on.
modern , clean , super well organized….staff starts to understand english!!!! good job Shangahi!!!i love to travel from hongqiao , very convenient

From Beijing to Shanghai, fly to Shanghai Hongqiao and then transfer to train. The train station is right next to Hongqiao Airport, which is very convenient. Although there are many people at the train station, it is not crowded, and the shops inside are quite high-end. You don’t have to wait in long lines to buy tickets, it’s a good experience

Took  a high speed train to Beijing from shanghai . You feel as you are in an airport. Excellent facilities at the station . All trains start and end their journey dot on time. Worth going by high speed train .

Riding the train in China is great, everything is punctual and easy to use! I bought the ticket at the hotel, but you can buy it online. I took the metro to the station and got on without any problems.

I went there once when I took a train to Hongqiao. From a distance, the train station was very majestic. When I entered the train station, I found that the facilities inside the station were also very complete. I felt that this train station was quite good and not bad.

to get there you can take the metro that stops directly in the station or take a taxi, as we did! the station is really huge and operates the most train connections in Shanghai. a big variety of shops and its easy to find your way. only stupid thing if you want to buy tickets at the ticket machines you have to be chinese citizen (really stupid) so you have to buy them at the ticket desk

I took the high-speed railway (Hebin) from Nanjing to Shanghai. I had heard in advance that I would need a passport to get the ticket, so I had a Japanese travel agency collect it for me (7,500 yen). Of course, there are fees involved, so whether you see this as cheap or expensive depends on the person. Also, if you make a reservation in Japan, all you will receive is the reservation number and you will have to exchange it for a ticket before boarding, so I asked my Chinese friend to provide this as well. The ticket you receive also includes your name and passport number. Please note that Nanjing has two stations: Nanjing Station (in the middle of the city) and Nanjing South Station (a little further away from the city center). We made this mistake and almost missed the train. I had heard that the ticket gates would close 15 minutes before departure and that you would not be able to board the train after that, but I was able to just get on without waiting. The inside of the train is like a Japanese Shinkansen, and the ride is comfortable. There were only a few passengers, so I was able to put the trunk near the seat, but normally I would have put it far away from the seat (I was afraid it would get stolen, so I even brought a bicycle chain lock with me just in case, but I didn't use it). I had heard that there would be on-board sales, but they didn't come to our car (first class). However, there was a menu with a price list in front of the seat, so there may be some way to get it. I didn't even know where the hot water was. When you arrive at each station, the conductor (older sister) locks the train from the inside to check on the passengers, which is a bit scary as it seems like you won't be able to get out.

This is a very efficiently run train station in Shanghai.  There will be long queues for tickets, passport checks and bag checks, but this is all typical of Chinese train stations.  If you want to avoid the queues buy tickets at one of the many train ticket shops in Shanghai city itself.
