It is a super large transportation hub with clear moving lines and extending in all directions. It is an easy-to-use station. The scale of China's major stations is like an international airport, which is very impressive!

Hongqiao Railway Station is the gateway to Shanghai, reflecting the efficiency of Shanghai as a modern city. It integrates bus stations, train stations, high-speed rail, subways, bus stations, and airports. No matter how you want to transfer, it is very convenient. What's more valuable is that the environment is still very clean despite the large flow of people.

China's high-speed rail is the worst. First of all, buying tickets is a pain. Depending on the route, it is unclear whether seats can be secured. If you purchase on the same day, you will have to wait in a long line. It may be difficult for a foreigner to ride alone.

If you only have 10 minutes before the train departs, be careful, since the first floor is the arrivals + metro entrance, and the departures are on the second floor. Otherwise, in a hurry, we stood in line to enter the metro, thinking that this was the entrance to the departure area, where even the Chinese couldn’t immediately figure out where to go and what the exit was. And the boarding gates are simply numbers and numbers + letters.. a, b.. don’t get confused)))

It's such a big train station, it takes at least 15 minutes to walk from one end to the other. Parking is quite convenient, but the fees are not very generous. I listened for less than 20 minutes and it seemed like 12 yuan was charged. Picking up a bus is a test of intelligence. First, go to the screen to check the platform where the train is located. Note that it is the platform, not the pick-up exit number. It's a bit mind-boggling.

I took the train from Beijing to Shanghai and to get off in this station was quite impressive. The only downside was that it was HUGE and we walked for what felt like 10min just to get to the car. Having said that, it is modern with nice places to eat, sit, etc and for any foreigner, easy to get around so don't be concerned.

The high-speed rail is becoming more and more convenient. I have been to Shanghai Hongqiao Railway Station many times. The transportation hub in China that can integrate the airport, train station and subway is here. The three are easily interconnected, and it is also very convenient to walk from the airport to the high-speed rail station. There are many automatic ticket purchase and collection machines at the train station, and there are also manual windows at the departure level. But even so, there will still be queues. There are many places to eat and drink coffee, which is convenient for people traveling. There are many brand stores in the waiting hall now, but unlike the airport waiting hall, there are no charging sockets and free Wi-Fi at the station.

A giant hub station, incredibly convenient when traveling by train throughout China. Despite its huge size, the journey from the entrance to boarding the train took only 5-7 minutes, which was very useful, since we were late. Everything is very convenient and, most importantly, understandable.

Apart from the fact that it almost looks like an airport, it is very large but clean and with attention to every detail. Considering that Shanghai with almost 26 million inhabitants is the most populated city on the planet it is impressive to think about the number of people who use and pass through this station. I don't think they know what a delay is, there are gates with very kind staff to access the trains complete with boards also in English. We did the Beijing-Hangzhou route with the bullet train where we stopped for 2 days and then Hangzhou-Sgaghhai perfect journeys, excellent trains... and compliments to the organization of the stations which make us understand why these are the first economy in the world. Just like our stations where if a train is on time we even celebrate!!
Very efficient rail system and easy to use.  Te one level station makes it easy to handle luggage .  Very clean .

The Shanghai Hongqiao Railway Station is very impressive. We boarded the bullet train to Beijing from there. Its almost state-of-the-art like an airport. Especially for tourists from India, it certainly doesn't look like our railways stations!

Rail is a convenient, relaatively inexpensive, and overal, excellent way to travel. This Railway station is generally almost perfect. The only thing bad is something they can't contain- smokers at the toilets
Huge modern station. Very convenient, there are signs everywhere. Everything is clear and accessible. Responsive staff.
We traveled by high-speed train from Shanghai to Beijing. It is striking in its size and has a very airy appearance. Well organized landing

High Speed ​​Maglev Train from the Airport. Distance 40 km in about 7 minutes. This is called saving time (though not money, as the ride is more expensive than a taxi). While driving, you can observe on the displays the speed at which the train is moving at a given moment - super speed

Shanghai to Beijing, excellent way to travel, better than any aircraft, plenty of room for your case's, room to walk, good seating,  recommend you bring your own food etc., as there isn’t much on offer to eat on the train, many Chinese take along pot noodles and use hot water that’s provided alongside the cold water tap, a great way to get a feel for the land as it pass’s bye, but there’s always a power station or high rise apartments somewhere near a town, but overall I enjoyed the train, much better than the flight from Beijing to Shanghai on our return journey.

Probably cause  I come from Italy when railway station are at minimum acceptable level ( to be kind) by but this new station is really workable and studied like an airport. There Is the luggage control at entrance, so take enough time before your departure time to pass this, sometimes is very busy. All doors are automatic, you get your ticket with indicate coach and seat and everything works very well

A very convenient transportation hub, just accessible by Line 2. If you haven’t had breakfast, you can solve the problem. If you get up late, you can just change your reservation (my friend is a latecomer). It’s clean and orderly, and it’s definitely a good review.

I like that there is a big Costa and Starbucks with lots of seating upstairs and they have kiosks downstairs for travellers that don't have much time. There are lots of shops if you have money and have to or want to buy overpriced stuff. There is a Subway sandwich store just outside, buy it when you are out of the metro exit (still inside the metro station) before entering the railway station. Make sure you get some food for the trip because train food is usually limited and not very good. There are some (mostly Chinese snacks) and  ice cream though!

Taking the bullet train to travel between cities in China is a must! The platforms are clean and the trains sparkling, the service is great, our trip was around 400 km and the train reached speeds up to 270km........the station works like Swiss clockwork, large screens in various languages and if need be a few staff to help......a great way to start the journey with Thomas the Tank......oh maybe it should Bob the Bullet.......

It was our first excursion in China and nothing could have prepared us for the amazing infrastructure that this station has. We took a Bullet train and reverting about this station - tickets to platforms and the trains - had a wow factor attached. Efficiency at its best.

It was my first time to take a high-speed train at Shanghai Railway Station. Compared to Beijing, Guangzhou, and Shenzhen, this high-speed railway station has the most people. It is not easy to find a seat, but the layout of the bathroom is very reasonable, and there are many vending machines, so buying something to drink is not expensive at all.

This is the biggest railway station that I ever seen, they are including airport to. So, they serve anything you want. The restaurant, shop, convenience store, everything. The departure terminal is in the back side at Third floor, need a couple times to getting there from Exit metro station. Actually I have a long story with this place:We choose the sleeper train to Beijing at 9PM, than we arrive at HongQiao station at 7PM. After dinner we going to departure terminal at 3rd floor, and didn't found our train number at billboard. So, we ask to the information. And the lady said there's no train to Beijing after 5PM with NO English (I can heard a little Mandarin). So, is a men behind us try to explain to us that we must going to Shanghai Train Station in down town and we have 1 hour to catch that train.Oh, Jez. So we run to taxi stop and that a looooong que. Thanks God there is a private taxi who give us solution with 250 Yuan goes to Shanghai Train Station. And, finally we catch the train 4 minutes before leaving. What a journey :))

The terminals in this country are very good because they can connect to various areas that we will visit or transfer to other transportation easily and not far, but because this country has a large population it is always busy never semi and be careful with pickpockets

As you arrive ,you are shocked by the activity around you , but it is well signed .It has plenty of places where you can buy food and bevearage .There are plenty of sitting places .You can pre-book your train seat ,online .Once you go to the platform ,the floor is like a mirror ...super clean .You can go on the 'super fast' train ( 300km/hour) from Shanghai to Beijin .We went first class and it appears as you are sitting inside an aeroplane ( the chairs are exactly the same) .They only offer on board service once ,so even if you are not hungry ,ask for eats and drinks .Otherwise ,there is a hot water dispenser that you can use to make your instant noodles and a bar on the next carriage .But they only accept local currency .

This is where I stopped by to catch the high-speed rail to Hangzhou. It is a place where you can use intercity buses and high-speed rail, boasts a huge size, and seems to have a neat and systematic system. There are many restaurants so it would be nice to fill your stomach while waiting for the bus or train.

Everything runs like clockwork.  Huge railway station with its own shopping district. That said it was the longest taxi queue ever although it did move relatively fast with a steady stream of taxis coming through. Good signage in Chinese and English.

I spent three days traveling from Shanghai Hongqiao to Shaoxing North to Changzhou North to Qufu East to Shanghai Hongqiao for work. It is similar to Japan's Shinkansen. Second class cars have 2nd and 3rd rows of seats. First class cars have two rows and two rows. Before entering the station, you show your passport and ticket and go through the usual random security check (only at Shanghai Hongqiao Station, you buy the ticket on the premises after going through the security check). You will not be allowed to enter the platform until it is close to the departure time. The train will come on time. For Japanese people, I recommend first class cars even if they are more expensive. Second class cars have a lower quality of passengers. There are always Chinese people in second class who are talking loudly on their cell phones. Conversations between Chinese people in the company are also long and noisy. In addition, there is surprisingly nothing around the local high-speed rail station.

The most inconvenient thing about my independent trip in Shanghai was that my WIFI was not connected and I couldn't get information! I took the bus from Shengze, Suzhou back to Shanghai Hongqiao Airport, and the WIFI was not connected. When I was worried about what to do, I went to the subway ticket office and asked the service staff where there was a public phone?? A male waiter in his 40s was willing to lend a helping hand at the right time~~~ He lent me his mobile phone to solve my problem~~~ Thanks to the friendly waiter

You will find this us the starting place for most fast rail trains in southern china you can catch metro to it and it's easy to buy a ticket just follow the signs.Allow an hour for purchase of ticket as it is a very busy place and you will have to wait in line, you can purchase tickets on internet but you still have to wait in line to pick up ticket.Don't forget your passport you cannot purchase tickets with out passport.
Great railway station, well signed and accessible. Plenty of food and drink outlets. Arrive early as it's very busy.

I have traveled back and forth from Shanghai to Zhejiang Province many times for work. The boarding procedure is the same system as for domestic flights. There are many people lining up at train stations in rural areas of Zhejiang Province, but ticketing is smooth. Foreigners need to show their passports, and Chinese people need to show their resident cards. There is no platform, so it's very clean. There is no guidance and the train arrives and departs quietly. There is little vibration and the seat size feels even bigger than on a Shinkansen. The station is located in a place where there is nothing other than the metropolitan station, so you can get there by car or taxi.

I am a frequent traveler to China and when at all possible, will take the high speed train over airplanes, especially during foggy season in Fall.  Air flights are notoriously late in China due to high volume of travellers and military action (unannounced).  The country is connected by high speed railway and tickets can be reserved, seating is clean and comfortable. Best of all, it's always on time!

I came to this Station from Wenzhou, coming from Ruian City.I wasted my flight to Shanghai just to have an experience of this high speed train and i must say it was worth it.Amongst the best in world.
You must take the Megalev, which goes non-stop from Pudong Airport to the city. The cost is cheap and the advantage of saving time is huge.

I heard that the Shinkansen ran from Xi'an to Shenzhen, so I rode the Shinkansen in China for the first time. It was a vehicle that introduced German technology. It didn't shake much even after driving close to 300km. Although it is a relatively new route, it is surprising. I took the special seat in the first car, but it was the last car, and the driver's seat had fogged glass, so I couldn't see the scenery behind me.

A super modern train station, clean controlled and clear, you can reach it with the green metro line no. 2 - we took a fast train from there to Hangzhou - the station has a variety of restaurants and the possibility of shopping, going down to the platforms through gates with clear signage and an electronic ticket like at airports.

This has to be the largest train station we have ever used.  We can only speak about arriving here.  We arrived from Hangzhou and walked what seemed like a gazillion steps before we could find the proper door for taxi queues for where we wanted to go.  The station is so huge that you must know where you want to go since there are taxi lines for different areas of the city.  We had the name of our hotel written in Chinese and asked at the information booth (which we had to find first) and they told us the proper exit. The taxi queue was very long but moved quickly  since there were men directing both taxis and passengers.  Extremely efficient system (wish Penn Station in NYC had such a system!)

A huge train station with a large number (about 20) exits to the platforms. From this station, mainly high-speed and semi-high-speed trains depart to many cities in China (Beijing, Nanjing, Shenzhen, Guangzhou, Hangzhou, etc.). Inside the building there are many cafes and shops: Starbucks, McDonald's, KFS, Costa coffee, bread talk (fresh baked goods). The station itself is very clear and convenient. Boarding the train occurs from both sides, depending on the car number. You can get to Hongqiao Airport on foot via the passage or by metro. As for the metro, there are 2 metro lines approaching the station: 2nd and 10th. Line 2 passes through the city center and main attractions.

Probably the biggest railway station in this part of the country. Easy to find around and accessible from both south and north. Be aware that there are many pickpockets and trick thieves who try to sell rolex watches and other fun by luring you into a corner, but others from the gang take your things without you noticing. The police are not immediately present and really don't care, we had to find out.

I spend a lot of time in Shanghai, and travel by high-speed train from Shanghai Hongqiao Railway Station often. This station is modern and easy to navigate as a non-Chinese speaker traveling alone. Lot's of familiar fast-food restaurants if you want to pick up a quick breakfast or lunch prior to departure.

I used it from Shanghai Hongqiao to Hangzhou East. Both stations were huge in scale and were the most impressive of my trip to Shanghai. The boarding system is almost the same as that of an airplane, but it can be confusing to compare it with the Shinkansen boarding method. Think of it as an airplane. Foreigners can only buy tickets by presenting their passports at manned counters. There are quite a lot of lines, and it takes a long time to provide directions for purposes other than purchasing, how to get there, how to buy, etc., and I think it would be better to wait for 1 to 2 minutes per person to issue a ticket. There was a foreigner counter at Hangzhou East Railway Station. I had made a reservation and payment in advance through Ctrip in Japan, so it was easy as all I had to do was present my passport and reservation confirmation at the counter and have the ticket issued. Japanese railway customs include paying for transit, changing boarding, etc.

A very modern railway station and very big has lots of shops and restaurants .. i took the train for one stop , it was very efficient but make sure to have the name of the  station you are goin to in chinese so that the ticket office sales can understand .

This very modern station is very well organized. It is very easy to find the boarding platform for your train because the organization is closer to that of an airport than that of a European station. Allow between a quarter of an hour and a half hour between arrival at the station because this station is really huge...You can easily reach it by Metro, in particular by line 2 which provides a connection with Pu Dông international airport (allow a little over an hour and a half because you have to change trains once even if it remains the same line) The station is also accessible by metro line 10. This station serves all the major cities in China by high-speed trains (CRH) very comfortable which travel at more than 300 km/h.

Very efficiently run railway station.  Collected the ticket for the G2 train to Beijing and boarded the train with no difficulty.  Extremely helpful staff and fellow passengers. (Though we had been provided with a few translated stock sentences) 5 star service.  Would use it again if ever I visit China.

It's a busy train station but well run. I would advise arriving 30-40 minutes before your train to pick up your tickets, as the queues can often been too long.So why have I rated in 1 starYou cannot order your ticket online with a foreign credit cardBut the primary reason - the taxi queue can be well over an hour long, whatever time of day you arrive  and the taxi drivers can be crazy (be watchful of the illegal taxis, in my experience I have never had any trouble with them but they will charge you a lot more - ensure you negotiate in advance - and then you put your life in your hands as they drive like a bat out of hell)

Very big and crowded station indeed! At the same time it's well organized and clean. Great place to take pictures from is the second floor (close to McDonalds). Try to buy drinks/snacks somewhere beforehand as prices bite (usual thing for railway station though).

When you enter the station, there is a ticket check and a security check, just like at the airport. (The ticket office is outside the station) The ticket gate opens about 10 minutes before your car arrives, and you swipe your ticket over to the platform. (You can't ride the Shinkansen at a time other than the one you booked, and there are no free seats.) After reading the travelogue, it didn't seem like it would be easy to buy at the counter, so we arranged for tickets at the hotel's front desk.
Not many elevators.  Some need assistance to unlock the lift.  The ticket counters are everywhere.  Easy to buy tickets as they can speak basic English.

ShangHai HongQiao Railway Station is one of the most convenient place that I have arrived China and transport to other location and other cities in China. There are plane , Subway and Railway station combined in this place.You can fly to China ShangHai HongQiao airport and then transport to other places.  It is very convenient.

It can also be reached by metro Line 2 from the center of Shanghai. Incredible organization despite scary crowds (see photo). At the ticket offices they are very efficient and try to help foreigners even if with approximate English. Everything is written on the tickets they issue: train number, gate to take, time, carriage number and your assigned seat. Then just follow your train number on the signs and you won't have any problems. This is my new favorite transportation hub. So simple and efficient. Even with crazy crowds you are able to get where you need to be with very little stress.

My advice would be to collect your tickets the day before and to give yourself a chance to familiarise yourself with the layout of the station.  We took a train from here to Beijing.  Each of the ticket halls we visited had pretty large queues so you have to be prepared to queue, which is always interesting in China.  To enter the station you have to pass through airport style security, you don't need a ticket to enter the station.  We followed signs for Beijing fast trains.  When you stand in the queue you have to be prepared for some people trying to jump in we were told by a Chinese lady behind us who spoke English in no uncertain terms to allow anyone to push in.  We did queue for some time, so we were glad we collected our tickets a day early.  We handed over our passports and confirmation details of our tickets and duly were given our tickets.  The station is very large.  Our train started to board about 30 minutes before it was due to leave and it can get a bit chaotic with people pushing to get on.  We had a 2nd class ticket which was perfectly adequate, clean, large seats and comfortable.  The catering car is near 1st class but with limited English it's pretty hard to order anything, best to bring your own snacks.  This is a hot water dispenser.
Get into the queue as early possible and you can stay relaxed post your tickets are issued . Gates will open 30 minutes  before the departure time, think so. Well organised and clean place.
I personally think that the station is quite big and the signage is clear. No worries of getting lost.

The rail stations in China are massive to say the least. They are geared to handle thousands of people every day. The trains are the newest , latest technology- very clean and easy to navigate. Both airports connected. Announcements in English. Much faster than sitting in traffic!
Very decent station. Everything is arranged conveniently and it is unlikely that a foreigner will not be able to figure out what’s what. There are a lot of cafes, catering establishments, etc.
Easy to arrive, line 2  metro , always crowded. Well organized with many food options, good service for foreigners, easy to solve the place.
La estación es enorme y toda diafana. It does not have specific waiting rooms for each train, but rather it is the hall itself that acts as a waiting room.
it's really a huge railway station. many trains there and crowded always. a clean place, and easy to get there - metro line 2.

The station is located in the western part of the city. Shanghai is a very big city and it takes more than 40 minutes to travel directly from the center by metro. The station is huge and you can get lost, since not all the signs are intuitive. It is difficult to find ticket offices with the ability to buy tickets without knowing Chinese. From here there are trains to Hangzhou approximately every half hour.
Easy to use, can be difficult to get to with traffic from Shanghai and especially from Pudong.  Efficient, clean, and easy to use.

This station is quite magnificent and close to the airport. Me and 2 friends spent the night here because we had to catch the earliest train to Beijing. Unfortunately it's not open 24 hours (only 1-2 convenient stores are open) even though many passengers spend the night here. Either waiting for the subway to operate or waiting for departure.

If your flight to Beijing is delayed, take a bullet train. Business class is great. There is no priority boarding and the food on the train is sub standard, but if you stock up at the stations Starbucks, your journey will be much more palatable. Great station.

make sure you get there early like 1 hour ahead. Buy your ticket at least a day ahead and be prepared to stand in line for hours.  Sit near your gate so you don't get distracted and miss the train boarding time which is 20 min before departure. Gates are closed 10 min to leaving time. Watch for where the compartment you are sitting is. Travelling by bullet train is fast and cheap in china.

I made a reservation online from Japan using ctrip. 19:00 Beijing South 20:34 Jinnan 22:48 Nanjing South 23:55 Shanghai Hongqiao I was a solo female traveler with a suitcase-sized suitcase, so I would arrive late at night, but I took this train, which doesn't have a lot of stops, got a first class seat, and the reservation fee was 973 yuan (pay by card). It's a little tight, but the seats were wide enough to put my suitcase in. There were quite a few empty seats in Nanjing South, so I took a vacant seat and spent an hour relaxing. There were no security issues at all (but I think you should carry your valuables with you). However, this is the last train, so please be careful as the lights on the platform will turn off about 5 minutes after you arrive.If you are worried, you should bring a flashlight.

We wanted to take the 'D train' from Shanghai to Yichangdong. When you arrive at Hongqiao Station you immediately notice; this station is huge. it's a huge area, you can choose railway to another area such as jiashanan county or another area.connected with airport area too.the office are very helpful when you ask for guidance.not all the destination, equipped with English language, so you need to ask for support, from officer

You maybe able to swop for an earlier train, they have a fast and efficient service. No English needed.

With the fast train service in China now it is very easy to base your self in Shanghai and then travel to the various cities on your agenda. This station is easy to navigate, clean and efficient. The other big plus is that the trains are just about always on time, not like their airports.

High-speed train station, which connects Shanghai with the rest of China. Well organized and direct access to all major highways. Attached to railway station is Terminal 2 of Hongqiao Airport. Busy hub but most convenient for travelling.

We took several trains around China. The Beijing station was a mad house. In comparison the Shanghai station was orderly & easy to navigate. Still as we had lots of luggage we hired a "red cap" to get us to the train & in our compartment. Cost 100 Yuen but worth it to skip the line ups & get loaded on board. Made everything hassle free.

If you're British or American or German you might expect that a major city's rail hub would be located right downtown. Nope, not this one -- it's about a 40 minute taxi ride from the Bund, and feels more like an airport than a train station. For one, you have to put your bags through security, and though nothing was amiss in my luggage, there was very little info available about what you could bring with you and what you couldn't (for instance, I'd purchased a six-pack of sodas, and was told that liquids weren't permitted, so I left them behind, but don't really know if it would have been a problem to bring them). You also should plan to arrive 1.5 hours ahead of time, which means you'll inevitably wait around. The good news? A fair selection of shops in which to browse, plentiful public seating, and some casual cafes. On the return trip, passengers debark on a different level and are herded to taxi lines that look insane, but actually are pretty efficient. Bottom line: With all the mass of people, the railway station manages to avoid chaos. Westerners could learn from it.

Hongqiao is a travel hub in Shanghai. It has an airport (mostly used for domestic flights), a train station and it is also a subway station. So, in case you are going to downtown, out of the city or flying to domestic stations, this is the place mostly to go to. The railway station is very clean, quite well marked and has a lot of shops and restaurants/ fast food outlets. Make a note of the platform of your train and reach there on time because the trains here do run on schedule.
If there is one thing that the Chinese are good at, it's moving people.  Thousands of people go through here on a daily basis.  It's. Lean, cheap and very efficient

Do your homework before using the station.  Some signs are in English, but many are not, so planning in advance is key.  The station was crowded when I was there and there were few places to sit.  The station offers lots of shops and opportunities to purchase food.  You must pass through security before entering.
Hongqiao station looks more like an airport or a groupie bus station due to the number of people. Extremely punctual trains

Hongqiao railway station is an extensive,modern, well laid-out facility. North and south entrances have security and x-ray facilities upon entering. Only a few minutes wait when we went through, but I imagine it could be quite busy at peak times. Once through security, check the large screens to see if your number train leaves from the South or North side. Then go to that side and find the gate number. All info is posted on large screens several places in the station. If any questions or problems, there are a couple of information desks where someone usually understands basic English. Having  your tickets in hand (blue colored version) before arriving at the train station is best - because all you have to do is get in the appropriate turnstile line - which opens 15 minutes before the scheduled departure time (and not sooner)  and put your ticket in the turnstile entry point to go through the turnstile and follow the signs to the correct  platform, just like the subway or metro. There are lots of restaurants and eating areas, some shops, information desks and in general, excellent signs and directions to the various trains, platforms and tracks were well documented. It might be a little overwhelming when first entering as it is similar to a major US airport!

We utilized the station three times while visiting Shanghai, Suzhou and Hangzhou. Easy to navigate and located next door to the Hongqiao airport. The entrance to the train is clearly marked and unlike the RR in the US, everything is new and modern.

I came to this station 3 times. Since this station is hub for 3 types of transportation; train, air plane, subway; or may be 4 with the bus (I don't sure) so this station is very hectic! As usual, we can reach this station through subway and I like it.

Next to Hongqiao Airport, the location is very convenient, right in the city. It is a big station and there are many people. It was difficult to find a seat to sit down and rest for a while. A place with thousands of people, but extremely organized, respectful people in the queues... admirable

I particularly like Hongqiao Railway station as connected to Hongqiao Airport. Once landed from many destination you can continue your trip by train. Very efficient security control allows you peace of mind. Big tables in two languages will direct you to the correct platform. Boarding performed again in a very efficient way, with no hassle.

Please allow time when you leave - it is always full. When you arrive there is always an endless line of taxis waiting for you.. It is poorly solved here. It's better to take the subway straight away and drive a few stops and look for a taxi there. It really saves a lot of time!!

first thing first, this is a large railway station that takes probably close to 1/2 million people a day! however exceptionally efficient in every way, from the moment you arrive until you board your train.

Modern station, very large and with many security checks, so I advise you to go well in advance. High-speed trains leave from here to Hangzhou.

This Station is really busy so many people. But the systems are in order and in a proper state. Very well planned railway station with good signage, perfect time, good facility for food with international chains, well managed

Order your tickets online and get them delivered to your hotel - well worth the US$15 in additional charges. Plenty of places to eat and platforms open precisely 15 minutes before train departure, but the queue starts early, so it pays to be at the turnstiles waiting.

i think this train station only has high speed railway, the railway station looks more like airport. so huge and so beautiful.

As a German, the experience with what I consider to be the perfect purchase and check-in logistics is recommended for everyone. Tickets are sold and occupied based on the seat. Access and boarding can be carried out 15 minutes before departure, without jostling or stress.

Many trains pass back and forth here, and there are many passengers. They are basically high-speed trains and high-speed trains, which can reach many cities in all directions. The train station is far from the city, but there are subways and buses to choose from, so traveling is still convenient.

We took the metro from here to downtown. The railway station is huge but it's easy to find your way around as everything is very well signposted. The journey to the Financial District takes just under 45 minutes by metro from there.

Shanghai Hongqiao Railway Station is adjacent to Shanghai Hongqiao International Airport. Hongqiao Railway Station is convenient and has various means of transportation for passengers to choose from. Public transportation and taxis are all very convenient.

This station is massive... It feels to me as though everything in China is operating on a different level. When you enter the station, it is overwhelming. The personnel's English is not great but if you show them your ticket they will point you in the right direction. Important: Download Google Translate and Pleco Dictionary to translate between English and Chinese. Also, download the Memrise app to learn basic Chinese phrases. Another hint: I like to plan ahead and be there early enough. Allow yourself ±2 hours of travel to get to the station (which is dependent on how far you stay from the station). There are Western and Chinese restaurants at the station. If your journey is quite long, ensure that you buy a few snacks for the ride. not friendly for the disabled. Took my father who requires wheelchair for long distance travel, they reserve the elevators for transportation of goods but not for people with disabilities. It is a comprehensive transportation hub. It was built not too long ago. It is relatively convenient to transfer to the subway and airplanes. However, there are relatively few seats in the station and not too many shops. It is a bit chaotic.

Very well equipped station for catching High speed as well as normal trains. Almost feels like airport terminal. But beware that lot of walking is required to reach your boarding gate as well as platform. So reach station on time

This place is colossal it will blow you away for its sheer size and number of platforms it's well operated and it's really smoothly run

Arrived from Beijing, glad to see escalators here too - helps with large luggage.  Signage in English as well as Chinese, so navigation is easy.  Watch out for the taxi touts at the exits - go outside and get in line, the queue can be really long but the line moves really fast as taxis are in constant supply.

I used it to go from Shanghai to Hangzhou on August 30th and 31st. If you buy online in advance, you can exchange tickets smoothly. However, if you try to buy it locally, there will be a huge line. Using the Shinkansen = advance purchase This is a golden rule. There are many food stalls at Hongqiao Station, so be sure to check out the stops before relaxing. It's quite spacious, so if you relax at the cafe until the last minute, you'll end up running. There is a queue in front of the Shinkansen ticket gate starting about 30 minutes in advance, but since it is a reserved seat ticket, there is no need to line up. Let's go slowly. Also, there is one important point to be careful about when using this. That is when you return to this station after 11pm. When the subway runs out, it becomes hell waiting for a taxi. Again, if you can use a taxi app, you can solve the problem, but if you are not familiar with Shanghai, please be patient.
Not much to say for a train station. Relatively clean and easy to navigate for an English speaker. The taxi queue was not that bad either.

What an immense station this is. This is a relief for those who travel by train in Europe. Trains run on time. You have a permanent place. It is cheap to travel by train, and it is also very comfortable. Shanhai Hongqiao Station is next to one of Shanghai's airports.

Train travel in China and in particular Shanghai is very well organised.The Railway timetables are accurate and the whole experience is one of a precision well oiled and highly organised operation. Just be mentally prepared for huge numbers of passengers that use the station constantly.Before you get any where near China, arrange your train travel before hand by using the online China based web site ...Ctrip.com.The service provided by Ctrip is outstanding. You can sort out the best train to meet your travel requirements, and both book and purchase your ticket(s) on-line. You print down your booking info which provides a ticket pickup number, You then can present this information plus your passport at any Mainland China Railway Station Ticket office and receive your actual credit card sized train ticket. How do you find the ticket office?...just look for the queues of people standing in line waiting in front of a multi windowed office within the street level arrivals area of the Station. Look after your tickets carefully, because without the ticket you will not be allowed through the boarding gates down to the train platform area.On your train ticket at the top right hand corner is the Gate # through which you will be allowed through to gain access to the train platform at the lower level, 15minutes before the train departs. Also on the ticket, printed on the right hand side immediately underneath the destination station name of the ticket are 2 sets of numbers. The left pair indicates the carriage number e.g. 01  and the other set is your seat number e.g. 04A. On the side of each train carriage is an electronic display panel which has the carriage number and the range of seat numbers... So just take your time, and board onto the correct carriage. The golden rule is to arrive at the station in plenty of time well before the departure time, and kill time just people watching and relaxing. If you choose to take a bus from Shanghai's Pudong Airport allow 2 hours for the journey to the station. The bus often gets caught in traffic jams. If you have limited luggage a better idea is to use Line 2 on the subway, and put up with the multiple stops. The station is very clean, it's well policed, security is high, and it operates just like a huge airport, with the gate numbers, train numbers, and departure times very well displayed.Enjoy the train ride!

You must go to the ticket counters in the station, and ask the customer service desk in the middle of the station if you have trouble finding it. Be sure to bring your passport. They also do not take Visa/Mastercard, only Unionpay for CC so bring cash. Given the crowdedness of the station, you do have to wait a while. The ticket agents are also very blunt and terse :) Welcome to China.The station is very crowded so if you want to buy tickets on the spot, be prepared to wait 1 hour before your train leaves, because many are often sold out, depending on where you are going.

Getting Tickets:Using the rail in China, you need to figure out how best to get your tickets. If you have Chinese friends they can help you with and it is quite easy.I went to this station days ahead of the trip, but I went to a ticket counter (counter 11) and was told I could only buy today's tickets. I went again later to the station, for I was anxious to get a ticket on a particular train, and this time, I found help at one information desk manned by someone with a little more fluent English. There were counters located elsewhere for future train tickets. In this case Counter 4, lower level. Yeah, so as I did not buy a ticket well in advance of my trip from Hongqiao, I ended up having to get a business class ticket, as all the normal tickets were gone.Travelling:I arrived about an hour before the departure, but the signs for where the VIP lounge was were so inconclusive. I eventually found a lounge about 15 minutes to the departure time. And took some time to convince the attendants to allow me some 5 minutes of sitting down. They were anxious that I go to board the train, so that I don't miss it. Rightly so. You should enter the  boarding gates latest 10 minutes before your train departure time. Well, the station is massive, sometimes very crowded. You should arrive early in case there are lot of people at the entrance going through the security checks. (Budget at least 10 minutes).There are lots of places to eat, and shops. And also lots of people waiting. So, go early enjoy the station, enjoy your trip.

We were traveling for the day to Hangzhou, and our hotel concierge wrote out on paper in Mandarin that we wanted 2 tickets (round trip for that day).  The ticket guy did speak a little English, so I think he would've understood.You then have to line up at the gate and show your tickets.  Important.  Hang onto those tickets because you will need it to leave the stations!We went to and from the airport via the subway.  Easy.
You want to take the Chinese TGV towards Hangzou for example, then you will go to this ultra modern, spacious and functional station... just like China today

The station is where you book to go on the Lev train to the airport. There are shops around andit has lots of tourist things around so plenty to see. The train trip was seven minutes and we ended up at over 430 km/hour which was interesting. There is a museum on site about the history of the rail development
We took the Chinese TGV to Beijing from this station, nothing to say perfect, perfect organization, immaculate trains, a service that we should take inspiration from in France.

It was work-related, but I used it for a round trip from Shanghai to Hangzhou. This time, I used business class, which is the highest class of seats out of 3. There are 3 rows of seats, so the space is spacious and the seats recline horizontally, making it very comfortable. It came with a drink (water or orange juice) and a small snack. Blanket service is also available.

There are at least 12 platforms to allow trains to travel to various parts of China. I came to take the high-speed rail to Hangzhou. The platform space is okay, but the waiting room is too small. Many people have to stand and wait for the train to enter the gate. Because there are too few gate machines, they can’t enter after waiting for a long time.

This station is huge. When in China taking a high speed train is a must not only to experience the ride but to see how China is transforming. Hongqiao station is a good starting point. When at the station you must climb to the food court to see the scale of the building.

There was a ticket for 50 yuan that included a one-way high-speed train and unlimited subway rides, so I decided to ride it. I was imagining something like the Shinkansen, but the inside of the train looked a bit tired, perhaps due to age. The ride was like a ``very shaky Shinkansen'', and it felt like we had covered 300km before we arrived. By the way, I used the subway on my way back, but it took about an hour to get to the airport.

We took a bullet train from Shanghai to Beijing South from this station. This place is huge!! Be there early if you want to catch a train to avoid confusion and lost of time trying to figure out where is your platform. Need to go through the scanners for all bags as usual. Take the subway Line 2 or 10 to get here, faster than taking a taxi as traffic jams are quite common in Shanghai.

Arrived into Hongqiao station from Deqing and I had wait for a friend for a couple of hours which normally I would have been annoyed about at a train station but Hongqiao had some amazing places to eat and some averagely priced and varied shops to look at

From the outside it seems we are arriving at an airport, a huge and busy one. Although located in the outskirsts of the city, the station is easily accessible, by metro (Line 2 and Line 10), by bus and by taxi. The station, looks good with open space and the polish granit.Plenty of places to eat that can cater for all types of travellers.One issue is the always present tobacco smell and smokers. In the toilette the tobacco smell was unbearable.All the information boards have information in english but, unfortunatly to travellers that do not speak any of the local languages, english is not understood by the staff. If you try to speak to them they just smile you back...
I was here for a transit to Beijing and it is a very large station, but still very well structured! Almost everything is in Chinese but easy to follow

We got off on this station at the end of our BeiJing - ShangHai bullet train ride. This is a huge railway station. Without our guide, we would have gotten lost finding a way towards the bus parking lot.We saw plenty of restaurants and shops around, tho we did not linger.
Gigantic train station, the largest in Asia. It has many shops and restaurants, but be prepared for typical Chinese chaos.

I used it on a day trip from Shanghai to Suzhou. It's comfortable to ride, but you have to buy a ticket before you get on the train (most people don't speak English, so you have to show them your memo in kanji to buy it), the train may be late but there are no announcements in English, and the bus stop may change all the time, so it depends on your luck. 1st class seats are spacious and clean, and you can tell which station to get off on the electronic bulletin board inside the train, so once you get on, you'll be fine!

Like many train station in China, this is a gigantic station. The facilities within the station is quite good, there's a lot of choice of shops, restaurants and cafes available. However I must warned you that most of the officials working at the station are unhelpful and unfriendly. I experience this when asking for some direction to locate the escalator to go downstairs. When traveling by train in China, I recommend buying your ticket online, I personally have good experience with Ctrip. Buying your ticket online can give your more certainty on your travel schedule, especially during busy travel season. All you need to do to get your ticket at the station is show your booking no, proper ID or passport. This way you can avoid disappointment of encountering a sold out train. Travel by high speed rail in China is highly recommended, it's a very comfortable and efficient way to travel. I much preferred this method over air travel.
Good station near the city airport. Trains going everywhere with a lot of high speed and very high speed options. Obviously very busy but not too badly organized considering

Well laid out train station, airport and metro are a short walking distance away. Very busy. Buy your train tickets as early as you can as trains can get sold out quickly, especially on holiday weekends. Many places to eat, again, with large lines and limited places to sit down and enjoy your food. Very efficient. Security lines can be long as well, but they move quickly. Easy taxi pickup and drop off.

Very clean, enough foreign food outlets to get food from, large and functions like clockwork. Situated to catch the metro or a plane as well. All notice boards for trains in English as well.  A great station.

Ok, the only reason I go here is to catch a train. It can be terribly crowded sometimes but what do you expect, it's a train station. It's clean though and pretty well organized. I find getting in and out to be just fine.

The sheer volume of the station and the thoughtfulness of it are amazing... It’s just a pity that there is not enough information in English. And girls don't talk in information booths. But you can figure it out

Easy to use station, well laid out and efficient.  I often take the high speed trains when traveling within China.  Prefer this over flying.  Very modern system and always on time and hassle free.  If you need to get to any other city within 1000 km of Shanghai, this is the best way to go.  Would not travel any other way between nearby cities in China.
Traveled to Hangzhou from Hongqiao station.Getting tickets can be a nightmare if you don't speak Chinese.Managed tickets on my own.Liked the chinese efficiency.

My hometown is ningbo however I worked in Shanghai in 2015, travelling between these two cities weekly, usually took train from this station to and from. Spacious and not too difficult to find the correct platform, however the staff at the ticket box were not very friendly and effectively, better to use ticket machine
I was very impressed by this station...bigger than any French airport!!! Very modern and airy, it makes it very easy to get to the platform indicated on your ticket...
A very big station a little bit out of Shanghai, near an airport

It's next to hongqiao airport and the railway station is huge, like a airport with many platforms...Equipped well with eateries and convenient shops and you just be very clear on the destinations you are heading to (referring to the main board) so that you won't feel lost in this huge station.

I live in Hangzhou, come to Shanghai for work a lot, and travel through Shanghai several times when traveling abroad, so every time I come to Shanghai, I will definitely go to Shanghai Hongqiao Railway Station. It is relatively large and more convenient, because it is the second station of the subway, so I can usually get a seat. Shanghai Hongqiao Railway Station is large and clean, and the various signs are well made. However, there are a few toilets and there is a long queue every time.
This is an amazing place and it gives you a small idea of how large and populated China really is. I'm pretty sure you can connect to anywhere from here.
I rode the Lujiazui from the airport and saw that it arrived in 7 minutes at 30 km and was convenient, reaching speeds of up to 460 per hour.  It's really amazing.

Very large train station but well laid out.  Buy your tickets on Ctrip before you go and get there one hour before the train leaves. Then take your E ticket number to the window and they will print your tickets. I booked 4 train tickets in advance as I am travelling during May day holiday and it can get crazy. They printed all my tickets at once.

I traveled by train between Shanghai and Beijing (round trip), I loved the train, which was super well organized and very clean. Beautiful and relaxing landscapes. Comfortable during the 5 hour journey. I recommend.

It is busy, extremely busy and you have to get used to the fact that everything is generally in Chinese, but after the initial shock it is of course just like everywhere else. Arrivals and departures are clearly indicated via large signs. Buying tickets is usually done upon reservation and your hotel will usually arrange this for a very small additional cost; I would if you don't speak Chinese and don't want to shuffle along in long lines. The station is located near Hongqiao airport. And please note, domestic but also international flights from, for example, Nanjing (350 km but 1 hour by fast train) and Hangzhou are often much cheaper than from Shanghai itself! There are of course shops and eateries.

The former No. 1 railway station in Asia is currently the top comprehensive transportation hub in China. It is closely adjacent to Hongqiao Airport and has convenient transportation. You can take Line 2 and Line 10 to get here. All high-speed trains from Shanghai to the south depart from here.

Massive station and hub with connection to the metro system. You can get seriously lost in this station. Having said that, the train system is quite organised and contrary to popular belief, queuing is quite civil.The trains are quite cheap and very comfy and clean. You have to issue your passport to get a ticket and also pass security and metal detectors and have your bags screened.There are quite a few shops in the building including a Costa Coffee for the brits there
Very well structured with clear directions to airport style departure areas. Ran like clockwork for our train. Carriage numbers marked on platform.

If you are going to use the train I would advise to use the app CTRIP or the website ctrip.cn to book your train in advance. All trains have a quota of passengers; ctrip shows how many places left per train. Once booked and paid you then collect your tickets from any train station. The queues are massive and you will need your passport to travel. So give plenty of time. I would advise also to book return journey online but you can do this when you collect your tickets. There are English speaking attendants in major stations but not always. All the train boards are in Chinese but numbers are shown and platform also, ticket shows this too so you can get by ok. Hope this helps.

The Station is huge! there are a lot of ticket desks/booths but ques can be long, at both ticket desks and security. There are scanners and bag scans etc , takes a while. Its best to leave extra time to make sure your where you need to be. Try to book tickets in advance. Best if you have the destination, train number and expected price with you, (try Ctrip) , if your not Chinese you can't use the machines to buy tickets, you will need to enter your Chinese ID number (right at the end, very annoying) You will need your passport to buy train tickets. Lots of food/drink/snack options to stock up in the station. Handy and convenient way to get around, also you can take the metro to the train station,

It is one of the Chinese high-speed stations, the first time I saw it, it seemed to me like I was in an airport, access to the platforms is only ten minutes from departure, the wifi and services are also good

My first train experience in China. There were so many people, but everything was very well organized. Announcements in English are sometimes not as frequent as those in Chinese, so check the screens often.

This was my first time riding the China High Speed ​​Rail, and I was surprised at how fast it was. When I rode it, it was up to about 300 km. I don't think I'll use it again, but it was a fun experience.

The subway and the high-speed rail are two railways co-constructed! The second floor is the entrance of the rail transit! The gate opens 7 minutes before departure to allow tourists to enter the No. 10 subway station to Hongqiao Airport Station and continue to Shanghai city! The queue at the high-speed rail ticket counter is long!

It is so easy to travel, take a subway (line 2) from anywhere, you can reach Shanghai Hongqian Railway station, from this station you can go to Wuxi (45 minutes), Nanjing (2 hours)... etc... NOTE: But be alert do not bring any hair  spray or any thing that flammable, or got a flame logo on the bottle, they will confiscate it before you step in the railway station.

Perhaps one of the greatest innovations in expanded transportation options is the great network of high speed trains that criss cross this expansive country.  It can be conveniently reached by car, taxi, bus, and Shanghai's excellent subway system.  It's a must visit simply for a great opportunity of

Be prepared if you are departing from this station. 5000 Chinese travelers and you! Sorry but the Chinese standards of personal space are different from Westerners' opinion. Be patient as English is not spoken or little spoken. The place is big, clean, I would say safe for Western standards. Always lots of law enforcement visible and undercover. Make sure you allow yourself time(2h) unless you have a Chinese speaking tour-guide who knows where to get what.

Not being from China, I found this train station very easy to use and accessible.  I arrived and departed here with the China Bullet Trains, as well as used its accompanying Metro station to get in and around Shanghai.  Everything was very logical, easy to use, and easy to find.  Food, stores, shops, and places to sit were all easily found.  Definitely a staple of modern traveling.  If you don't like flying, utilizing the trains in China is the way to go, and this station makes that extremely easy and comfortable.

Not really sure why I am reviewing a railway  station however here goes.A stations go, it is modern, very spacious and we'll run by Chinese standards.All Chinese railway stations require faff and queuing and Hongqiao is no exception.If you are buying tickets, arrive at least 2 hours before you want to travel.
This is a pretty huge station. It is easy enough to find things, the only issue is the size, be prepared to walk.

It's really hard to ride alone. First class. The seats are wide and quite good. The bento box is okay, but the service is not so good. I think so even if I'm used to China. But I guess it would be better if it was China. I took a flight to Beijing, but I'm thinking of taking a plane from now on. But it's fast and convenient, so it's great for traveling between nearby cities.

From there we took the express train to Beijing. Clear even with the size, what we didn't like was the virtual absence of English when buying tickets and the impossibility of paying by card, I wouldn't blame them for that, it was a problem almost everywhere, but finding an ATM was a punishment, there weren't many of them

Hongqiao Railway Station id linked not only to the Hongqiao airport but also a growing business and shopping centre. Very convenient to the FFC but only limited International flights operate out of this airport these days. The railway station can be chaotic to obtain tickets but otherwise it is reasonably well organised and a great place to catch fast trains across China

Don't underestimate my advice. Arrive about 2 hours in advance at this huge train station to find the counter where you will exchange your travel ticket, after facing a queue with several Chinese people ready to jump the queue if you give up! Mas o trem sai na hora, é tudo organizado, gostei da estação de trem moderna de Shanghai.

I had a lot of concerns before using China's railway, but when I stopped by this station to get to Xitang, the signs were well written and it was convenient to use, probably because there were a lot of travelers. In particular, the high-speed rail was very fast.

I am a train nut...so this was always going to be an enjoyable arrival and departure point for me...BUT even train nuts realise that is all a station has to be. The Chinese are all about efficiency and this place exemplifies that...even for a non speaker it would be I almost impossible to miss your train here...or fail to get here by the various access methods...ARRIVAL please note the Shanghai taxi ranks (double sided) are outside and DOWN their own escalator...giving the opportunity for taxi touts to grap the unsuspecting and tired traveller before they realise their confusion or disorientation.
It's good because you can travel around China easily by riding this. Shanghai-Suzhou is 30 minutes...but the train station feels like an airport.
Lots of security. High-speed trains leave from here punctually. There is an information service in English for tourists. They supported us for the departure to Beijing.
The best way to travel from the airport to the city in a short time. When I used it for the first time, I couldn't help but exclaim.

Unlike Shanghai Railway Station, Hongqiao is clean and tidy with modern design. The surrounding facilities are getting better and better. The transportation is also convenient. It is not far from the city and can be reached by subway. Food is mainly fast food, and now you can choose to eat at Hongqiao Tiandi.

This is a huge, and very new-looking, station. But it was easy to navigate around and find our train. You have to go through airport-style security to get in, which can take a while depending on queues. I'd say arrive about 30 mins before your train, just in case it takes a while. Lots of shops and eateries to look around when you're there.
Go ahead and travel alone without speaking almost Chinese, the stations are quite intuitive, a little shocking at first but you will surely find your car and your train

If you visit there for the first time, this railway station can be a bit intimidating; I had a problem finding the proper counter for my trip to Kunshan. Doesn't seem that too many people are capable of giving directions in English...talking about station personnel.Left my passport in the hotel but they accepted my US drivers license....lucky

The new train and the great seats in business class are absolutely recommended, even if they are very expensive. The care is great and the landscape just flies by at 300 km/h. You get a lot more out of it than when you fly
I loved the security and the incredible cleanliness, we don't have this kind of station in France... too bad everything is clear and clean
The station has nothing special, beyond the incessant and multitudinous movement of people. They may come to it without planning it.

Absolutely huge Railway Terminus that covers the whole Train system for East China. So many platforms .Careful not to get lost.Careful if meeting people to get the correct area.Next to the Domestic airport Terminal T2
This can be said to be an important hub in Shanghai. There are many platforms, subways, and two co-structured shopping streets and food streets. The large modern indoor station is worth exploring.
Huge station but there is no risk of you getting lost because it is perfectly signposted. That’s organization!

The railway station is huge but very well organized with clear signs also in English, so you will certainly find your way. If you plan to buy a train ticket, please remember to carry you passport with you. Without any official ID you will just not get any tickets.
Huge building ! It's bigger than anything I visited before. It lacks a tramway or shuttle... To connect from the last platform to the Airport, it's going to be a hike !

Magnetic levitation is a good expression in Chinese. It floats magnetically and runs smoothly. However, the speed of 400km/h is limited to only one minute, and the entire section is only seven minutes, and if you want to go from the airport to the city, you will end up changing to the subway, so it is not bad to go between the airport and the city by subway.

I paid a $100 Yuan for taxi from the Bund to Hongqiao Rail Station where I picked up my Rail Tickets purchased online in the states. At first the station looked huge and chaotic but once you look around you will find that there is order to all the madness.  My wife pointed out that there was only one window with a running ad to pick up tickets of the many that were opened and all had long lines.  Good thing we arrived an hour earlier as we needed to go to 3 windows before we got our tickets in proper order.  Seems like one number was off on the passport so we had to cancel one ticket and lost 20% plus had to go to another for refund.  She issued the new ticket and although I gave my itinerary, put us on separate trains departing an hour in between.  So we had to go to information and after explaining our dilemma, we were sent to another window at the other end of the station.  after paying an additional fee we had same departure but 6 trains cars apart so we used our phones to communicate and walking back and forth in between cars on our 5 hour journey to Beijing.  Use first class or business class otherwise you will be bunched up 3 on each side of the car and it is full and noisy with locals.  otherwise the ride was fast and smooth.  These trains are amazing and just as comfortable and as fast as the ones you find in Europe.  I would recommend it to anyone who does not mind minor language inconveniences and likes adventures.  I enjoyed seeing the countryside and still amazed at so many tall structures and so many large communities all along the way.

Great experience especially between major citiesFaster than the airline as it saves time for checkin etc.Comfortable journey with scenic views Both English and Chinese announcements In-train services are awesome for a quick grubSometimes neighbors may get noisy however it's a fun if you can crack a conversation with themBeing a foreigner (laowai), you have an advantage of attracting peoples' attention, some of you may want to click pics with you and try to know youChinese people respect all foreign nationals unlike Thai, Filipino, Koreans and Singaporeans who disrespect Asians and only bow down (literally to the ground) to westerners.For the dwellers and travelers who want to move between the cities within China must try the CRH fast train.
Impressive station, everything very well organized, quite close to the city with arrival by metro. Necessary to speak Chinese.

It's very big, and there are many, many, many people... but it's very convenient. All the signs and instructions are very clear. The service attitude at the station is quite good. Some of the restaurants that have settled there need to be improved and are still quite good.

The Hongqiao High Speed ​​Railway Station (Hongqiao) is a new, spacious, convenient, clean station with direct subway access into the city and close to Hongqiao Airport. We traveled from Beijing by high-speed train in 5 hours. There were clear signposts throughout. Both the way to the subway, bus, taxi, clean bathrooms available.

Make sure you arrive well prepared, with as much information as you can: destination, train number, price, etc., preferably written in Chinese, and DO NOT forget to bring your passport if you have not pre-purchased tickets. Allow at least half an hour to purchase tickets and walk to the correct gate, and if you can afford it travel first class.

Its modern, good connection to subway, has food and toilets. What it lacks - good food, a good convenience store, enough seats for passengers to wait, and stopping smokers from smoking in all the corners and toilets etc.All said, better than most train stations.

It is a perfectly organized train station, the trains are incredibly comfortable and affordable, places that used to be a pain to go by road are now very close, I hope our country will have such beautiful stations.
For me one of the best places that chinese ever built to unite flyers and train riders. So convinient!
I have never seen such large train stations. Everything is very well done, there is somewhere to kill time while waiting for a trip. A metro station, boutiques, restaurants.
Super easy to get to via the subway. Only a 37 min. trip from our stop in Pudong each way. The building is impressive as are the G-Trains.

The station is, like Beijing, huge. To enter, you have to have luggage x-rayed - which I very much approve of,. The many shops tend to be rather pricey for the kinds of goods on sale, but there are lots of food outlets to suit all tastes and also for take-aways for the train journey.Everything is clearly signed and there is no problem at all finding your boarding gate. An incredible number of people were there, but all behaved sensibly and queued really well.
Conveniently located close to the airport of same name. Get in pass through and on to your train. Nothing soecial to see except vast size.

About 18km outside of Shanghai at the old airport. Be sure to get there an hour before departure, the queues at the ticket counter are long. Took the bullet train to Beijing. A comfortable journey in First Class (8tung Business Class is more luxurious)

The station itself is a fine example of connectivity with a huge area given over to eating shopping and drinking almost like an airport. Oh wait a moment there's an airport attached - it is a hub!The ticketing and track access is efficient although if you do book ahead make sure you have given the correct passport number, my old one was given and I had to buy an expensive first class ticket and my old ticket was sol on, capitalism eh? Wonder what will happen if the communists ever come back?? 😆

The train station is located right next to Hongqiao Airport. It is very spacious, bright and modern. Orientation is easy for the traveler. You can also travel here without knowing the Chinese language.

I went from Shanghai to Suzhou. At first, I went to the wrong ticket office to buy a ticket, so I had to ask locals and station staff for help in broken English. I was able to buy a ticket with my broken English and a memo with my destination written down. The inside of the train was comfortable and no one was making any noise, so I was able to ride with peace of mind. The time was also surprisingly accurate. I felt that there were more noisy people on Japanese trains. All the locals were kind and very helpful. Thank you!

What a gigantic train station - one really feels temporarily lost in the hustle and bustle. We have to go through security to get in (which is a good sign) and it opens up to this gigantic hall. There are shops all around and so many gates for so many stations. The restaurants tend to be on the second floor. Train gates open 20 minutes beforehand and everyone is standing in neat rows before the door opens. They really seem well tuned into crowd control but even then one thing that stands out is how crowded the place is. This is really impressive

And that's not necessarily a good thing. I'd recommend planning your strategy if you travel through here. Bus connections, airport, taxi, they're all long hikes. If you have large luggage, plan accordingly.If possible, other stations make better departure/arrival points to Shanghai. This place is just too large and easy to get lost.There's a decent mall on the West end with coffee, restaurants, etc...
Imagine a very large airport that you know, as this train station is likely to be larger, look for a departure board and you will be aware of the gigantism of this place.

When you're traveling in China, you quickly notice that a lot of things are automated and therefore tightly organized. In transport, this applies to train travel. The train station is huge but incredibly well organized, allowing even people new to China like me to travel without any problems.

Similar to the NYC subway. If you do not read Chinese you will need an interpreter. It was tough to find a customer service agent, but the train system is solid and easy to use once you understand it.

Give yourself enough time to navigate this station, it is very big.  I took the #2 Subway from the Nanjing East station and arrived about 40 minutes later.  The #10 train is another option.  I had to pick up my ticket and the are ticket areas just inside the station after leaving the subway station and it was a good place to get my tickets as the line was much shorter than the areas in the middle of the station.

When I got to the Shanghai high-speed rail station after 7 p.m., most of the seats were already sold out. It varies depending on the destination, but the last train to my final destination was around 9:30. Fortunately, I was able to return to Hangzhou at night with standing seats. It's fast and convenient, but there are a lot of people using the train, so the line is long. If you use it, get there a little early!

As is often the case in China, this place where high-speed trains stop to get on and off is misleadingly described by the term train station for Europeans. It is more reminiscent of a state-of-the-art airport. Travelers are advised to allow a little more time than in Europe to reach the train. On the one hand, because the security checks (also typical of airports) are occasionally taken very seriously. On the other hand, to allow a little time to marvel.

An excellent experience. The trip took 5 hours and was so smooth. It was ashamed the views were clouded by smog and we were too early for the trees and flowers to bloom.The station was quick to get out of.
Think big! This trainstation is huge! Nevertheless it is easy to find where the trains leave. It is clean and has quite some food outlets (Western and Chinese)

High speed trains are better for trips of 350km or less in eastern China. This railway station is huge compared to Jinan, probably on par with Beijing.  Lots of food outlets are available.  Allow at least 30 minutes via car from the Bund area.

First of all, the toilet is really dirty. The moment I open the bathroom door, it shuts down. The floor is soaked with 〇〇, and the toilet seat is also covered with 〇〇 and mud. If you are in a second class seat, there is a 70% chance that someone will be sitting in your seat first. When I say "My seat!", it moves reluctantly. The first class seats were also dirty with food particles falling on them. There are many people who are looking at their phones or iPads without using earphones, and there are always people who are talking loudly on their phones. It's the worst.
You don't need many minutes to get to know each other and find your way to the trains. And then you have a good part of China within reach. Fly blir bortkastet.

Shanghai Hongqiao Railway Station is very accessible by Metro Line.  It is also connected to the Shanghai Hongqiao Airport.  The station is very huge and clean.  It may be be bigger than some airports in the Third World countries.  The rest rooms are very clean with maintenance personnel taking good care of it.  However, the only drawback is when queueing, the local people seems not disciplined.  Beware of ambulant hawkers selling fake mobile phones and watches.

Railways looks like airport, only in China…Hangzhou and Shanghai HongQiao (Red Bridge) station are the big and modern airport style. But only one need more, i.e. the toilet / lavatory / bathroom / WC. Need more of them within the waiting room.
The railway station has many good outlets. KFC was the saviour for those veggies who survive on fries! It feels more like a mall than a railway station.
