Public transport is easy to get to and you can take line 2 directly to pudong (2 hours max, normally 1 hour and a half). Don't take the fake taxis they are not reliable. The taxi line may seem long but you never wait more than 20 minutes. My only complaint is that there are not enough seats at the station. So no need to arrive more than an hour before your train, even if you need to pick up your tickets, which takes about 20 minutes.

For traveling to Beijing or other cities by high-speed rail From the city, you can reach the train station by metro line 2 or line 10. Passengers who want to board the train must pass baggage inspection first. Inside the train station there are restaurants, shops, and drinks vending machines. and has a bathroom service

The good: This place has trains going to about every city in China. The bad: it is very crowded be prepared to be in long lines...be careful not to get in the wrong lines--I can't help you here--just to say, there are some lines for advanced or on-line tickets. Don't forget your passport or you are not going anywhere. Come here with plenty of time or you could be in for a long wait.

Foreigners can no longer buy tickets from vending machines, which has become inconvenient. You can purchase it online, but you will have to pick it up at the counter. The counter staff are unfriendly at all stations.

I used it when going from Shanghai to Hangzhou. The seating arrangement is 3 seats + 2 seats, similar to the Japanese Shinkansen. Tickets can be purchased on the day of the event, but the counters will be crowded, so it's best to get them the day before.

I love traveling on the fast train network in China.  Regular, safe and affordable travel supported by huge stations. Hongqiao is a good station, great facilities.  For westerners turning up by taxi, be aware that the guys in the red jackets that assist with your bags aren't doing it for free.  There were four of us traveling to Ningbo with quite a few bags, so having a guy manage that lot was useful.  He also assisted with pickup of booked tickets and even tried to negotiate an upgrade for us.  He then settled us in our waiting area seats and took me to the kiosk to pay.  For him to look after our significant baggage and see us through security to the train cost us RMB180.   Not cheap but useful after a long haul flight, so,we went with it.   Good food options on site, but large, noisy station.  Has a good system for security management and ticket checking to get to the platform 10 minutes prior to 'launch'

Shanghai used to have only South Station and North Station. Since the construction of Hongqiao Railway Station, it has shared part of the traveling force. The subway can reach it and the transportation is very convenient. However, special attention should be paid to the two directions of the subway. The facilities here are very new and very spacious. A hub that you must pass through when traveling.
Very easy to get tickets to different places.  We bought tickets to go to Nanjin/Suzhou and Hangzhou during our trip!

I took the bullet train from Shanghai Hongqiao Station to Jiashan South. At the station, there is a baggage inspection just like at an airport. All baggage is placed on a conveyor belt, passed through a gate, and there is also a physical sensor inspection. There are several ticket gates depending on your destination, and you should head to the ticket gate numbered on the top right of your ticket. (15A, etc.) When it's time to board, there will be a long line at the ticket gate. I took a soft seat (first class seat), and the seat was spacious, clean, and comfortable. It takes about 30 minutes to get to Kazen South. There are some restaurants inside the station where you can eat simple meals.
I traveled from here to Beijing by high-speed train. You can get there by metro directly from the city center. Spacious, light, large-scale!

We were SO EXCITED to ride the Maglev train. It was our first time riding a bullet train. However, it was a bit anticlimactic given the ride lasted about 7 mins from Pudong Airport to Longyang Road (30 km). There are two speeds and we were on the faster one going into the city and the slower one going back to the airport.The Maglev line runs to/from Longyang Road station in Pudong to Pudong International Airport. There are other high speed trains in China, but this is ONLY Maglev train in China. We purchased a roundtrip ticket, but in hindsight, we would've chosen only a one-way ticket from Pudong Airport to Longyang Road. On the way back to the airport, we would've taken the train/subway instead of Maglev. The train is much cheaper and it doesn't take that long to get to and from the airport from downtown Shanghai.
luxury and functionality combined under a single majestic roof, almost exaggerated, I would have made it lower

Although it was a short ride, I traveled using business class. It departed from Shanghai Station, and there were very few seats in the waiting room. However, I was 100% satisfied with the trip because it was business class. The price was a bit expensive, but

There are several subways that arrive at Hongqiao Railway Station, but there is one subway that has two terminals, one of which is Hongqiao, and it arrives on a staggered train, which means you may have to wait 10 minutes to catch up, which will be troublesome if you are in a hurry. . That's how I was delayed.

Upon entering the station you must present your ticket and identity document and then pass through the metal detector!!! very large halls, very high and spacious, very efficient and clean bathrooms. Billboards written strictly in Chinese but ... easy to understand, let me explain ... the train number and the platform are easily understood, the gate opens 15 minutes before the departure of the trains and on the platform it is marked where the carriage will stop ... it looks like a station from the other world!!!

I just came back from the Hongqiao Railway Station a few days ago, going to Wuxi and then back. This railway station is HUGE! There is great security there with numerous checking points! Please be aware that when you put your luggage into the security machine, take it out immediately when it comes out! You do not want to loose any luggage or carry-ons! There are many shops in the station as well: there are restaurants upstairs including KFC (etc), there are shops that sell Shanghai Specialties, there are other retail shops (e.g. Disney shops). You are bound to spend time there! Be aware that the Shanghai specialty shops probably put the prices very high so its best if you buy the specialties elsewhere. The railway station is very well connected with the metros and the other public transportation and you can go to many places in China e.g. Wuxi, Beijing e.t.c!

I bought a ticket at Shanghai Station, but there was a line, and if the ticket for the train I wanted was sold out, there was no way to tell me which train was available like in Japan, so it took a long time to buy. We recommend purchasing your tickets the day before, rather than on the same day, with plenty of time to spare.

The car body and interior are exactly the same as the Japanese Shinkansen. However, the running sound and passengers are noisier than the Japanese Shinkansen. Foreigners must present their passport when purchasing tickets, so they can only purchase them at the counter. Just tell them where you're going and show them your passport, and they'll assign you the closest available seat. However, when I purchased tickets for two people at the counter, for some reason they were placed in separate seats in different cars. If you prefer serial numbers, it might be better to tell them properly. If you don't worry too much about the details, I think it's comfortable because it's fast and the ride isn't too bad.
Extremely large building. easy to get to from the subway. lots of people, long lines. Explations in chinese and english. plenty of food options.

Well connected with metros and other public transport ways, this one serves as the hub for major connectivity with beijing and other cities. reach there early if you need to collect the ticket and give some time for security check during rush hours

The railway station has easy connection to the city and airport by two lines of subway, which working hours should be extended to at least midnight.  Weekend nights are hell to find a taxi or use your own car.  We waited in the garage for 1hr before our friend can pass the long line and drive in.

This is a large moddern railway station well laid out and simple to follow with good instructions in English as well as Chinese. Give yourself enough time as security checks  can take time and if you enter the station at the opposite end to your train its a long walk to the platform.
It was a nice reailway station in high standard, well done and efficient in line with European equivalent.

A high-speed railway station in China. I took the high-speed train to Suzhou. The difference with Japan's Shinkansen is that you cannot enter the platform at any time you like. When the departure time for your train approaches, the gates open and you board the train all at once. There is also a simple body check at the station entrance.

Used between Shanghai and Nanjing. I heard that Shanghai Hongqiao Station is newer and easier to use than Shanghai Station, so I used Shanghai Hongqiao Station for both trips. Shanghai Hongqiao Station was large and clean, but we still had to wait in line for several minutes to buy tickets. By the way, since I can't speak Chinese, I wrote down my destination on a piece of paper and handed it to the person at the counter along with my passport, and they told me how much it would cost, so I paid the price and they gave me the ticket and change. Nanjing South Station, which I used on my return trip, was also clean, large, and easy to use. Personally, I was very happy because there was a British coffee shop called COSTA at Nanjing South Station, which has not yet come to Japan.

This train station is huge, but it's easy to navigate. We took the train from Beijing to Shanghai. When you exit out of the station, there's a mall where you can hang around. There's also a taxi stand where you will see very long queue but it's fast flowing. Don't be deceived by people who are offering to get you a taxi because they will definitely charge you 10x more than the metered taxi.

Because I have to go to Beijing frequently for work, I take Line 10 and take the train every time, and then take the Fool subway to Beijing. The whole journey is basically seamless and does not waste time at all. I can’t remember how many times I went there in the morning or in the evening to finish my errands and leave. Having this station is so convenient.

The development of high-speed railways in China is remarkable, and they are especially essential for transportation in the area called the Yangtze River Delta, which is centered on Shanghai, Hangzhou, and Nanjing. When it first opened, it was convenient for foreigners to buy tickets at the automatic ticket machines by inserting their passports, but after that they have to line up at the ticket office to buy tickets. It's a bit of a hassle, but compared to the past, I think it's heaven. The appearance is similar to that of Japanese Shinkansen trains, and the washroom facilities are similar to those of German ICEs, so I can't help but laugh at the fact that they call it completely domestically produced. In any case, thanks to the high-speed railway, I am grateful that my travel time has been significantly shortened.

One of four main train stations, Hongqiao Railway Station is close to the regional airport (Hongqiao) and links to the Metro. I liked the fact that when it is time for your train to depart, only then are you allowed to go down to the correct platform. Only concern was that not enough seats were available for waiting for the trains.

Non chinese ppl may worry about being able to take a train but there is no need. This station is like an airport with boarding gates so it is impossible to go wrong. Simply look for the train number and finding the boarding number. Also of note if you have a valid ticket (eg in email) you can travel in China with just your passport. Simply show your passport and electronic ticket to the guard at the gates. This is especially useful if you booked last minute.
Easy to get yourself around, nice friendly staff to help if you get in trouble. Taxi line was huge, but moved really quickly.
Since it's a new terminal, the equipment is new and the system is easy to understand, so I think it's easy to use. It is accessible by subway lines 2 and 10.
Great Station but an even better railway System. The Shanghai Maglev Train was amazing reaching 431 Kilometers per hour at one stage.  This is a must and much faster tan a taxi in the traffic.
A really nice, clean and well-arranged railway station. Took a trip with the magnet train to Shanghai international airport, you have to try it, it was fast (432km.hour).

the railway station is the only way to travel. Don't be fooled if you think that taking a plane is faster. The trains are on time..the planes are not.  Comfortable seats, nice snacks and a great way to see the countryside of china

The subway goes directly to the station, and the road into the station is much shorter than that of Hangzhou East Railway Station. It once took me 11 minutes to get on the train after getting off the subway. It must have collapsed in Hangzhou, and there are many dining options in the station. There is also a portion, and I usually buy a bag before getting on the train.

Traveled with my son from Shanghai to Beijing via Bullet train. This is a VERY modern station with lots of food and shopping options. Many large boards inside station to help you locate where to board for your train. Signs are in English and Chinese

I used it to go to Hangzhou. Shanghai Station is so large that it can be a struggle to even buy a single ticket. This time it was easier, but I lined up for about 10 minutes with the other people. Since the seats were fixed, I was able to board the train easily without having to fight for a seat with other passengers. Although the seats felt a little cramped, we arrived at our destination in relative comfort. At the on-board sales, you don't even have time to decide whether to buy or not, and it passes by in the blink of an eye. If you want to buy beer, it's sold on the second floor above the ticket office, so please buy it there.

After a couple of successful and alright visits to Hongqiao there are some tips to share. - buy your ticket ahead of time on ctrip only if there are not that many trains to your desire destination, you need to arrive there by a certain time on the day of travel, or its a holiday in which tickets sell out extremely fast. -if you buy your tickets online on ctrip remember the reference number or booking number because youll need it in order to get your actual ticket once in Hongqiao. Just screenshot the confirmation email that you get to be safe- if you bought them online and need to redeem your ticket get to Hongqiao well in advance because there are alwas tons of people; i would say on the safe side is one hour and a half before your train departs- trains are rarely delayed but they often leave a couple of minutes before they are supposed to, anywhete between 3-5 maybe a little bit more, so be at your gate at least 20 minutes before the train is set to depart - once you have a ticket in your hand, you are able to return it as long as the train hasnt left yet for a full price refund (even if its minutes beforehand). I think if you try to return the ticket once the train has left you get a partial refund, though make sure its not an hour after. There are specific service windows for returning tickets- if you are doing a day trip to suzhuo or Hangzhou i would recommend buying the return ticket once you arrive at suzhuo, return tickets to Shanghai tend to go fast. - in my experience foreign credit cards and debit cards are not accepted

This is the gathering point for high-speed rail and train stations. You can reach it directly by Metro No. 2. It undertakes the railway transportation function of Shanghai. The hall is very luxurious. Each line is displayed on an electronic screen, and the instructions for coming and going are very clear.

Anyone who only knows the German train will be impressed by the Chinese train system, somewhat similar to that at the airport (pointless screening, but without all the undressing nonsense). However, the trains are super punctual, you only get to the platform shortly before the train arrives and a ticket includes a reserved seat (that makes sense somehow).
You will be amazed at the size of this place.  Get there early.  Everything is very clean and you have options to buy food.

I like getting off the train at this train station. If there is no car to pick me up, it is also very convenient to take the bus. The location is very reasonable and orderly, and the instructions are very clear.

I rode on the train for work, and my business partner arranged for me to ride in second class. The seats and other facilities are not much different from those in Japan, but they are noisy and there is trash under your feet. However, cleaning staff and garbage collectors come around regularly, so you may find it difficult to get used to the noise and the people around you who are openly interested in you. If you have to travel for a long time, it may not be recommended for people who are not used to living in China.
in front of the station there is a huge square from which you can take the metro, nothing to see in this square and the surrounding shops are not worth it

It is very easy to get around by train/subway in Shanghai. Basically all the places you need to go are covered by the lines. The subway attendants are very friendly and the ticket machines have an English option.

this train station is huge there are ticket counters both on the upper departure area and the lower arrival area.security in the departure area is very stringent so allow plenty of time the trains departure are like clockwork. if you have a first class tickets which i would recommend for long trips you might be able to go to the front of the queue. if you plan to use train travel (i did) in China you should check out the man in seat 61 website it gives you plenty of information about train travel in china

Very clean and quite big. Actual entrance to get to the high speed trains are at the higher levels. escalators can be found at both ends of the station so do not waste time looking for an access at the middle.You have to go through security check to enter. Once you are in, search the big boards for your gates and you are good to go.Lots of shops at the ground floor as well as inside near the gates. Plenty to entertain you as you wait for the trains.

I used it when visiting Hangzhou from Shanghai. It was more convenient as it was connected to the subway station, the facilities were clean, and there were restaurants and cafes scattered throughout, so I could use them while waiting for the train.

If you travel from the airport to the city on the Maglev, you will arrive at this station. The easiest thing is to take the subway on the floors below to go to your destination. You can also ask for an Uber to take you where you need. In my experience it is better to order an Uber because you enter the destination and the driver takes you there even if he does not understand you. If you try to hail a taxi on the street it will be super difficult for them to understand where you are going.

Very comfortable and quick.  I would highly recommend as it is attached to the airport also so its convenient.  Absolutely get business class or even first class as it wasn't expensive and a lot more room.   I would rather take this than go through the airport again for sure and a cab is not the way to do it.

Great station. Very clean and the staff speaks English without any problems. You can get there from Pudong Airport by shuttle, which departs from the ground floor (a comfortable minivan with a TV) costs around 70 yuan, you can take the metro for 7-10 yuan (Shanghai metro is informative, you can easily buy a ticket at the box office or through the terminal. The terminal is in 2 languages, Chinese and English, you press the destination station, it gives the cost, you pay and get your ticket. Save your ticket to the station. arrivals both in the metro and on railway connections.) I flew in for work and got to the city of Wenzhou by train. I registered my ticket electronically through the website. I went to the 11th ticket office (probably it serves electronic tickets), gave my passport, printed out the ticket and went to the train. Boarding begins 15-20 minutes before departure. The train speed is 200-250 km/h (it is better to take first or business class.) The food on the train is disgusting, so if the journey is long, it is better to take something with you.

One of the largest train stations in Shanghai. If you have never set foot in a large train station you will be surprised by the size. It is worthy of a large international airport. The information is well indicated. There are many ATMs and staffed ATMs. Be careful, I had difficulty at the ATMs to withdraw a ticket with my passport. They only recognize Chinese ID cards. The platforms are indicated 30 minutes before boarding. Be careful on busy days, allow time because access to the station is controlled by gates. Like in an airport it can take time with the crowds.
China has come a long way in public transport. We are decades behind here. Hongqiao is one of the most beautiful, but there are similar ones in big cities around Shanghai

we caught the train to Beijing from this station, very clean and safe.recommend purchasing the business class ticket as the seats are bigger and the carriage offers a little better view, or move to the dinning cart and enjoy the food and larger seats.yes the seats a small....

Railway station and the second airport in Shanghai in one place, which is quite convenient, but expensive from the city center. Railway The station is not very convenient, small place and a lot of things are not clear, but you can figure it out if you want.
It was easier and cheaper. You feel safer and our hotel was not far from the station. It is aslo quicker to get to your destination. No traffic. Nice and clean.

Although buying a ticket is a hassle, once you get on the train it's easy. The delays aren't as bad as with planes, so it's more reliable than planes for medium distances. Please note that if you buy your ticket on the same day, you may not get the seat you expected on the train. The next train will not come immediately like in Japan.

Large, impressive railway station with plenty of signs in English.  As we had bought first class tickets, there was a different waiting area for us, and we were also allowed to board early.  There is a smoking room in the station, and quite a few food outlets.  Don't use taxi touts to get to or from the station - there is a queue for registered taxis, which is much cheaper and more reliable.  Security screening to get into the station, but there is security screening everywhere in China.
We booked first class to Hangzhou - amazing - better than an airplane and so well organised.  The train station is great and very clean and plenty of seating.

From Shanghai, I took the Chinese version of the Shinkansen, the Japanese Shinkansen. I took the most expensive seat, and it had more space than the Japanese green car, so I was able to relax and although it was a long journey, it was comfortable. I think the service is better in Japan.
I used it when traveling from Pudong Airport and got a discount if I showed my boarding pass. They say it moves with a magnetic field. Oh, it's really fast and it saves a lot of time.
A must see as it is so big.  Enjoyable to people watch.  Get a train to anywhere in China here.  Even if not traveling by train it is a fun visit.

this experience is also gone: finding yourself in this station the first time you take a train can be disorientating. Upon arrival on subway no. 2 you find yourself in immense spaces that you have to manage to understand where to go without finding yourself wandering uselessly. Furthermore the time tables are all in Chinese!!! Automatic ticket machines are the same... So arm yourself with patience and arrive early enough for your train. It will be fun. The station is very beautiful but you have to know how to move... for expert travellers!

The trains are the most convenient way to get around in China as they are typically on time unlike in country air travel.  Signs are in English and this is a very modern train station with several places to shop.  Once through security, look to your right to show your train ticket and receive a free bottle of water (big sign says "Free Water").  There is a Starbucks on the second floor of the station so buy up as the coffee on the train isn't so good.  Food is available for purchase on the train, but I recommend buying something before you get on board.

Sitting on a train going 431 km/p...awesome. It is not really a train, it doesn't have wheels....you are floating some inches above the "track"....then you pass another Maglev train going the opposite direction. The sound, the actual FEEL you get in your chest as the train shudders...Disneyland for adults. I took a video...but will not post it. Just a blur. My husband and I just took the ride to and from one stop to the next and back again. The whole thing took about 15 minutes. But what an exhilarating 15 minutes.
Very big and easy to get around.  Make sure you are clear which gate you arrange to meet at.  There is more than one.  Escalators for your overweight luggage.  That is what I loved the best.
Very organized and easy to get around, which has no heating or cooling. Large signs indicate where to queue and at the indicated time you can go to the platforms.

This train station could be said to be even better than airports in Indonesia. very sophisticated, neat and nice. lots of trains here and there, on time and regularly, lots of food and drinks selling inside and not too expensive. really like riding trains in China

I took the train from Shanghai to Beijing and allowed myself plenty of time to make sure I got my ticket and was able to find where I needed to be. I really gave myself way too much time as it turns out. This facility is very well designed and easy to navigate, and there are lots of options for eating and shopping while you wait.

Clean, professional transport hub between trains and planes. It is important for Europeans to know that the utmost importance is placed on punctuality and that the trains often leave 1 or 2 minutes before the actual departure time!

The time between Beijing and Shanghai is getting shorter and shorter, and it can be reached in 5 hours by high-speed train. However, whether it is Beijing South Railway Station or Hongqiao Railway Station, there are many people...be careful against theft and crowding...
Like all things in China, its huge. The facilities are good and the station is relatively clean for public standards.

One hour from dowtown if traffic jam. Booked your taxi from your hotel, you will have one taxi with a meter! A modern station where you can find easily the tickets office and get your tickets when you will show your passeport and printed e-mail.
A very large and modern complex consisting of a railway station, an airport and a metro station; the spaces are simply huge and very easy to find your way around.

Big and modern. It shows the "power" of the chinese builders. If you love fast and ultra modern 400 km/h trains - visit the railway station. :) It also offers a lot of places to eat, shop, relax. Everything is easy and understandable for tourists.

No two ways about it, the Hongqiao Train Station is well constructed, clean and mostly runs pretty smoothly. It is a huge modern station. You need to allow plenty of time to travel on foot to get to your departure lounge waiting area. Any be warned, trains all leave exactly on time - you cannot be late! The main reason for my average rating is the poor service encountered when picking up tickets the day before travelling. For travellers not able to speak much Chinese, this can be a problem. The counter clerk we dealt with initially would only give out the return tickets for a trip that had already been pre-purchased and pre-paid online. She would not explain why the departure tickets couldn't be issued and came across as very rude. We were told by a helpful customer behind us that we had to go to another counter upstairs. The counter number we were instructed to go to by the counter clerk turned out to be an auto-ticket machine, which it only accepted local resident ID cards, not foreigners passports... We ended up going to another counter where fortunately the young clerk spoke reasonable English and issued the departure tickets on the spot. The experience was very frustrating with a couple of hours needed, with long queues and unprofessional staff. The plus side was the train itself was on time, new and very quick to board. The business class section was very comfortable. Recommend picking up your tickets with the help of a local to make sure there are no undue delays.

After reading many reviews of how to get to this place from Terminal 2 at Hongqiao I was dismayed.  When i got there I realised how easy it was to get around.  I was alone so the walk from T2 to the train station was a few minutes, at most 5.  The station is well setup and You would need to give yourself some time if you are travelling to another city to pick up tickets as lines can be long.

It was my first experience traveling alone on China's high-speed trains. awesome. Getting there is easy, buying tickets is relatively easy and can be done by phone with an app that works 10 points. The question is about the signs in Chinese!! To my surprise, a security person approached and asked me for the ticket, with simple signs he told me how to get to the door where I had to take the train.

I boarded the train when I returned home with my family.The way I got tickets was so bad that I didn't know where to line up.My wife is Chinese, so I bought one despite complaining.Afterwards, we waited in the waiting area for the Shinkansen to arrive.Until then, we couldn't enter the platform.When the signal to start entering was given, we all headed to the platform in about 30 minutes.All seats were reserved, so there was no confusion and things went well.It's strange. We have experts to carry your luggage, so it will be smooth if you leave it to them.

We took the train in/out of Shanghai. One of the nicest/modern stations I've been in. They have Chinese-brand eateries, as well as western-brand (starbucks, burger king) -- in addition to a small Chinese market where you can buy snacks/drinks to take with you.
To visit only if you have to travel from there. You need to pass security to enter. Arrive early and get in line ready to push hard...

It could be said that Shanghai Hongqiao Railway Station is the most magnificent and cleanest railway station in all of China. Directly attached to Hongqiao international airport, so that those arriving in Shanghai by plane can immediately continue their journey to other cities by train.
We arrived in the evening by train from Guilin. It is a very large station, but the arrival and signage is very clear. Easy to find a taxi to the hotel.

It's much bigger than Japanese stations. A large station in China is an image of an airport in Japan. There is an automatic ticket vending machine, but foreigners have to show their passports at the time of purchase, so we had to buy tickets at the counter. I can't speak English.

It was my first time riding the Shinkansen in China, so I asked a friend for a ticket in advance. You will need to send your scanned passport via email from Japan. Everyone has to wait in line until 3 minutes before departure and board the train all at once. I was saved because my friend guided me to the inside of the car. It is very similar to Japan's Shinkansen, but it is more comfortable with less vibration, and the fares are cheaper than in Japan. We highly recommend riding it at least once. I took the train to Nanjing, but it was only a 30 minute ride.
Took mass transit train from Pudong airport into town. This rail station very modern well run. Puts US stations to shame.

Shanghai's largest high-speed rail station, with taxis, subway stations and arrivals floors at the bottom. The transportation is very convenient, and there are many different styles of food to choose from inside. There are also many departure floors, many departure points, and many food and beverage options. It's just that the store has been renovated a lot internally, which is inconvenient for tourists. Hongqiao Airport is right next door, and the subway is just one stop away, very close. You can also walk. There are also many battery cars that shuttle back and forth on the arrivals floor, costing 10 yuan per person.
We took the express train from here to Beijing. Everyone at the counters speaks English, so you can communicate easily. you can take the metro from here to anywhere in the city

There is a rather cursory examination of luggage and person (think airport TSA in US) before entering the station.  Once inside, it is easy to find  your train and waiting room.  Access is granted to the platform about 15 minutes prior to arrival of train.  Coach numbers are marked next to the track.  Find your coach number on the ticket and proceed to that number on the pavement.  When the train arrives, the door will only be a few feet away.  No climbing of steps to board coach - deck of coach aligns with the platform.  Move quickly as the trains don't wait for you to stumble aboard.  What an example to AMTRAK.
Even if you do not have any knowledge of Chinese, you can easily understand the organization of this railway station. Indications are excellent, and the waiting rooms are extremely comfortable.
There are places to eat on the second floor of the station, including a Starbucks coffee shop. You won’t get lost at the station; you can see from the signs which train is arriving where

I took two fast train trips (320 km/h) leaving and arriving at this huge station. I had guidance from a local guide on the first boarding, and then the guidance was easier. But for those who don't speak Chinese and don't have someone from the city accompanying them, it can be difficult to find the right platform!

This is a huge modern railway station.  It is convenient, efficient and trains run on time.  There is adequate security and the luggage service staff are very helpful.  It takes a little time to understand the system but everything a person needs to know is printed on the ticket.  Finding the gate is straight forward but it can be a long walk.  There is electronic entry to the train exactly 15 min before departure and the train leaves on time. This is a viable alternative to air travel especially to cities which are within a 200-400 km distance.  The high speed "G" trains are superb.  We prefer the train from Shanghai to Beijing versus an airplane.
If you are taking the train anywhere, this is a major hub where you can get the bullet trains.  We used this station often.  It is huge, well signed in English and Mandarin and super easy to use.

We took the Maglev train from the airport to the city center and this was very convenient.  We had a seat in the first car and the door was open so we could get a nice impression on how fast the train was going.At the exit from the train platform taxi drivers were waiting. I'd encourage taking the metro to/from the rail station, as taxi's (especially when departing the station) can be problematic and you may end up waiting hours if you arrive w/ throngs of other travelersI have limited Mandarin skills, but was able to purchase tickets at the walk-up counters (bring your passport!). For tickets purchased in advance, you'll receive a receipt and can claim you ticket at the ticket counters.High speed travel is a great alternative to flights - and for flight of ~3hrs or less - I always opted to take trains.  Security is more manageable.  Departures are nearly always on time (compared to the flights which are often delayed and w/o explanation).I've traveled on 3rd,1st class & business class.  I was pleasantly surprised by 3rd class.  For a trip of ~1hr, 3rd is fine.  But if you're traveling further - and if you intend to use a laptop or conduct work, I'd suggest 1st class.Safe travels!

easy walking distance to the hotel, the road is busy but veryeasy for pulling along a suitcase, and a couple of good coffeecafes right next door....easy walking distance to the Bund,  and also to walk amd mix with the locals

This is an impressive facility that provides well-oiled fast train transport in and out of Shanghai. A very well organised Railway station. Usually very busy in July because of school vacations from 1st of July to 1st of September every year. Book before you travel so you don't have to buy tickets at the station. The Station employees do not speak english. The high speed trains have 3 classes of seating, Economy, First Class and Business Class. Unlike airlines, Business is better than first with full flat reclining seats for sleeping. Best for very long journey like Shanghai to Bejing. First Class is best as the seats are more comfortable and less people in the carriage, it gets quite noisey in Economy with talking. Take your own food, you do get snacks but its Chinese dried fruits and a few other things. Bottled juice and water is supplied. Water dispensers are in each carriage. The Toilets are very good and western type. A little larger than a aircraft toilet. Luggage racks above you seat. Larger bags have space at the end of each carriage. There is a digital display in each carriage so you know the next stop. All announcements are in Chinese mostly. On one trip we had both, so I think they are working on it. They are pre-recorded. The train is very modern, comfortable, air-conditioned but not cold as the Chinese do not like it too cold. All stations are immaculately clean on the hi speed routes. Not all stations have western toilets, so go on the train before you get off if you have a ways to go.

Shanghai Hongqiao Railway Station is a huge modern station.  Trains are excellent, clean, comfortable, and can often be a much better option than going by airplane. Trains are exactly on time and get to their destination exactly on time.  The airport, by contrast, can be a total nightmare, with almost all domestic flights delayed by several hours.  I flew from Shanghai to Beijing and was delayed six hours.  I took the high speed train (it's called "Gao Tie" in Chinese) and it took me 4 and a half hours.  I could chat on my cellphone and work on my computer the whole ride and there were plenty of snacks and drinks.  The tricky part is buying the tickets for the high speed train.  The lines can be very long, there are ticket kiosks but they are for the Chinese nationals and unless you have a "shen fen zhen" (Chinese ID card) you need to go up another floor to where you buy the tickets using your passport or foreign ID and credit card. You have to know exactly which line to line up in according to the signs. Some booths are for that particular day only (no advance sales) -- so make sure you are in the right line or they will kick you out of it.  Also there are some that are for 3 days advance sales.  It is exactly 3 days in advance, not more. If you book longer distances (eg Shanghai to Beijing) they sometimes let you book the return.Other thing that's important is you MUST have your passport or ID card with you.  They won't let you book without it.  Kids need passport or ID too (I think for kids 150 cm and above, if I recall, they are counted as adult and must have their ID or passport for each kid) -- and for babies or little kids under 150 cm, they don't require the passport or ID ticket is half price, but it's still wise to bring them.  They are strict about the height limitation so for instance, if your kid is 11 years old but very tall, they're going to count him as an adult ticket, not as a child. When you get up to the window, you should be prepared to immediately tell them what day you're travelling, what time, what class (yi deng is first class, er deng is second class, shang wu chang is business class -- though business class on the high speed train is definitely much nicer than yi deng first class). Know what you want because the people at the window are quite matter-of-fact, not polite, and are in a hurry.  If you don't speak Chinese, it might be good to have your planned train times and class and cities written out in English and also have it written out in Chinese to save time and frustration. Or have a translator on hand to help.If you need a ticket refund, it is a different window again and you will receive a portion of the ticket price refunded.  You need the credit card that you bought the tickets on and also again, the ID/passport of each person who requires the refund. Amount refunded will go back on the credit card (unless you paid cash). Next is getting to the train and the platform, allow yourselves plenty of time to find the waiting area and platform of your train.  The train pulls up about 15 minutes before departure time, they collect tickets from that time, and departs exactly on time, so don't be late.  In Shanghai, traffic can be hectic so allocate enough time to get yourself there.
Its a big station with lots of food joints KFC, Bread Talk, Starbucks, etc. Very organized with lots of ATMs and the ticket counter is big and spacious.

Great station with all facilities. Just too crowded much like anywhere else in China. Does not help that people smoking in toilets ... Not sure why.. Otherwise clean.. Has a direct connection in subway line 2 taling all the way to Pudong

Since Hangqiao Railway station is right next to the Hangqiao International Airport, I almost felt I am at the airport instead of a Railway station. it was simply unbelievable to have seen this station train station. While this is a physically appealing building, knowing where to queue up in this busy station to purchase tickets is extremely difficult, even for the locals. Difficult to believe as train station as almost trains (G) arrive here and it is fully equipped with many eateries and shopping area. all signs are in English too so one can easily find the way. Some time becomes too crowded near entry gates.
Pretty good train station based on China standards!  There are the usual western food places here along with some shops.
I arrived from Beijing to Shanghai on the Bullet train, the station is huge, it is very easy to get lost, our guide was waiting for us on the platform. The station is large and very clean.

Shanghai Hongqiao Railway Station is a massive and huge building connecting the local trains station.The connecting trains going to almost anywhere in China at high speed.This is very clean and well maintained station.A lot of staffs for security reason, but easy to get. Very clean and ordered. One of the best place I have seen in my trip to Shanghai.

One of the best world class Railway station I had ever seen. I had gone to the station for catching the bullet train to Hangzhou. it's a massive station. not s tourist attraction between t you probable have to visit the station if you are taking the train from shanghai to nearby cities

It is spacious, clean, new, easy to navigate. Also a decent selction of food and drink options. Allow plenty of time before your departure, distances between everything are great.

Massive railway station, more like an airport! Although it is very crowded, there are many ticket offices, so the waits aren't too long. Because of its size, allow plenty of time to get to your platform, its easy to get lost.

Train tickets were printed with which ramp to take to get to your carriage for faster access. This place is vast place but well organised and can be daunting if you do not what you have to do.  Please refer to www.seat61.com and follow links to China Railways which will even break down how to read your ticket that you collect. Good luck.

There are also standing tickets, so if you are seated in the middle of the car, you will have to push through the people to get to your seat. Even when you reach your seat, the racks are often full of luggage. If you have a lot of luggage, it is definitely better to choose 1st class. We got the tickets online, and they were delivered to us at the box office without any problem. You just have to bring the code and passports. However, it is really huge and has many trains. You have to pay close attention and follow the signs carefully.

As a tourist site? I don't understand why anyone would go here. As a train station, nothing special. All high speed train stations look exactly alike in China. They are loud and crowded and have poor food and facilities.
Very modern station. You can figure it out without any problems even without knowing Chinese, everything is very clear and convenient.
Anyone who knows train stations from Germany will be amazed at the Hongqiao Railway Station - in all areas: DimensionCleanliness, Processing and Punctuality

The station is far away from the city, but a taxi is not too expensive and it takes around 40 minutes. We traveled to Beijing in business class. First disappointed was the vip lounge, just a corner at the end on the station separated by panels. The seats were uncomfortable sofas covered with a tacky sofa cover and lace decorations. I was surprised by how dirty was everything, stains on the sofas and carpets and the floor looked like if it wasn't hoovered in 2 days, not the standards you expect for a vip lounge.  You get free tea and coffee and soft drinks, however the soft drink there only one choice, an iced tea drink. And the snacks were just a poor selection of tiny packs of salty biscuits or nuts. No train departure information inside the lounge, you have to go outside to check on the screens. And when it's boarding time it doesn't matter if you're travelling in economy, firs or business: everybody boards at the same time. Then on the train another disappointment with our seats, we were given seats in what they call the viewing carriage. So we had the last 2 seats of the train in a tiny compartment shared with 3 first class seats. The business cabin was 3 carriages away from us, this meant that we were the very last 2 to be served. I went for a wonder to the business carriage and they already had lunch, when we didn't until 1 hour later when they finished the service in the business carriage, also we didn't get the same things as for example coffee and a muffin, even we payed the same fare. If you are thinking about travelling in business make sure you get a seat in the proper business cabin.

I hope it can be more friendly to the people. There are two subway lines connecting to downtown Shanghai and it is very convenient.

For business I use the Hongqiao train station a lot. The place is just huge.It is very easy accesible by metro. Follow the people and the signs to go to the departure hall. You can board the train about 10 mins bebore it leaves.To get an impression how big the station is, take the escalator up to the food outlets and watch the crowds and massive space below. (Saturday mornings are amazing) Despite the amount of people, all is well organised, so no worries to take the train on peakdays.Trains in China are a great option to travel. Very organized, they move people at a very quick pace without fuss or bother.  We were able to transfer trains very smoothly.  Security transitions easy.

Use the station many times since we started living here. Train station, but it's bigger than many airports. Security control to get in. Crowded. Noisy. If you have to wait longer then half an hour you will have headache.

The station is organized like an airport, but registration is not required. Each train is assigned its own exit, which is indicated on the ticket. All information is on the electronic display. Above the exit there is electronic information about the train you are boarding. At each exit there are inspectors checking tickets. Due to the large size of the station, some exits may not be immediately accessible. Not scary. Show your ticket to the station employee and he will tell you which way to go. I read in one of the reviews that tickets are sold to foreigners only at one ticket office with a corresponding sign. I haven’t seen such a sign, I bought a ticket 2 times at different ticket offices, no problems. I printed out the train number, departure date and time, destination station (in Chinese) and carriage class in advance. Please note that you can buy a ticket at the box office no earlier than three days before departure. The station is well organized and things flow in a strict time. Clean, good food options, like KFC, Burger King too..
Like the station,it is convenience location in side the city and a lo of bullet trains stops here, Taxi is not a problem here to anywhere in shanghai.

Tickets can be collected at any station for any seperate departure station. Some other stations - this gets trickier because of the English!Hongqiao itself is very easy to find your way around. just have to see to believe the 35 platforms  - its shiny expanse of floors and 1000s of people its not far from the city by taxi and a great way to catch the fast train to Hongzhou - just 45 mins away Dont get it confused with the airport nearby !!
commitment of the staff and keeping the range of time for destination. But the railway station should have staff who can speak English and written guide specially for foreigners

It is also very convenient to take a taxi. It is not far from the city and is connected to the airport. The station is well organized and well planned.

This airport-train and metro station complex combines incredible size, architectural magnificence, efficiency. In addition to the astonishing dimensions which seem to guarantee adequate functionality even when the passengers will be triple those of today, one cannot fail to be struck by the implementation of a concept that is both brilliant and banal at the same time: combining all possible transport in one place, guaranteeing each a synergistic effect that works as a multiplier for each of them. To leave you speechless.
While i have not been in many train stations, this was by far the largest and it was very crowded.But it amazed me on how organized and on time the train were.

I was taking the subway, and I remembered that I could get free mineral water at Shanghai Station before, so I took my ticket to look for water, but I couldn’t find it. I found that there was no water in Hongqiao, Shanghai, which was on the same level as the shabby train station in my capital city.
I visit Shanghai almost every month. All movements are mainly through this station. Convenient, clear, clean.

From Shanghai to Wenzhou in three and a half hours, stopping at at least 10 stations; maximum speed of 300Km/h and travel comfort superior to the economy class of the plane. There have already been two business trips that I changed by plane for the train; faster, more comfortable and with the possibility of walking and having a drink sitting on chairs with tables. It has little space for large luggage but by walking a little you can find the suitcases.

The Railway Station is easily accessed by subway.  There is some signage in English but all of the ticket information seems to be in Chinese.  Fortunately, we had our Chinese friend to assist us with purchasing tickets.The Station is very large to accommodate the crowds.  It appears very clean and organized with numerous eateries of the fast food variety available.

Taking the train is an experience in China. It looks more like an airport than a train station. If you get there first, take a moment to see how it works, because you first have to go to the right floor, go through security, go to the check-in desk and waiting area. Then through the gates and to the correct platform.
And did 31 km in 7 minutes 😄 the maglev has a top of 500km/hour but because of the short distance we could only get up to 431 🚄👍 we loved it and its worth it

It is a modern station created for the 2010 expo. Going by subway is the best since this station connects with subway line 1 that leads to People's Square (the nerve center of Shanghai). Going by taxi costs about 100RMB but the subway only 5Y. It is very easy to take and it is advisable to have coins and not bills, since the machines accept coins but rarely bills.
This is a railway station, the one did for the 2010 world expo in Shanghai. Very well organized and cleaned.

We travelled from Shanghai to Beijing from this station via the high speed train. It was an excellent experience. The train station is huge and very well organized. The signs are in Chinese obviously but there was plenty of help from the well located and conveniently placed service counters. Now, we are frequent travelers and have taken the Eurorail as well as the trains in the U.S.  This train station is comparable if not better than most other North American and European train stations in larger cities. The train ride itself was very comfortable. It took us from Shanghai to Beijing in just about four hours; it takes two hours by plane and is much more hectic. I highly recommend traveling by the high speed train, if you plan on any domestic travel in China and especially from Shanghai. It is an impressive and well run operation.

Don't think this is an "attraction" per se but this is the rail station where high speed rails (Gao Tie) to Suzhou, Nanjing, Hangzhou, Beijing, etc. You don't necessarily need to buy tickets at the station. You can get tickets at some sale points downtown, just pay RMB 5 per ticket for booking fee.

Excellent train station, super easy to obtain the tickets, the ticket sellers are willing to understand English and make things easier for tourists, something to highlight, that with the ticket they give you a bottle of water...it's great!!, punctuality and security are points to highlight.

Do take the Chinese railway to your domestic destinations.  The organization of the entire station is magnificent & relatively stress-free.  Just be sure you give yourself enough time to get your ticket as to need to show your passport to get your ticket.  The line-ups can be long but again, all is vey efficient & it goes relatively quickly.

Hongqiao railway station is new and clean with large waiting areas and easy lift on/off the platforms with luggage.  Highly recommend using this station, over the older and more crowded /smaller stations in Shanghai.
The station is super well organized, the trains are punctual and leave for the most diverse points in China at the exact minute they are scheduled.

I've used it many times for business. The outside looks exactly like Japan, and the inside is very clean and comfortable. ID is now required when making a purchase. However, when I got on the train right after the accident, the power went out after 300km, and the repair person inside the car ran out of the hallway in a panic, which caused a panic (^^;;It's a good memory (^^;;

Amazing structure, easy access by subway/tube, and wide options of routes. The lines to purchase tickets can get long. If you haven´t purchased your tickets before going to the station, it would be advisable to lease some spare time for the ticket counter lines.

This station is huge! But it is easy to navigate, with plenty of English signage. The taxi line is very long so be prepared...but so well organized. The subway a good alternative if you have carry-on luggage only. Very clean.

Everything is clean, beautiful and tidy. We took the high speed train from Beijing to Shanghai, it was worth it! The view outside the window leaves only positive impressions of China. The train is pleasant and comfortable. Although the cost is the same as on an airplane. The main thing is not to throw away your ticket, you will need them at the exit!

It's a very large station, so it takes quite a while to get to the platform after you buy your ticket (you had to wait in line for about 20 minutes). Although it was a bit noisy with passengers playing games and watching videos, the Shinkansen itself was comfortable and similar to Japanese Shinkansen trains.
